23Lot déem ma vo o yi Zoara dedaane wɛ maŋe de puli mo. 24Baŋa Wɛ laam ma pa se chilibugu na jege mini to nwoŋi wɛyuu ne ko to Sodom de Gomora teene dem baŋa ne nenɛɛne doa na nena tei to. 25Wɛ déem tɔge konto mo o ma chɔge teene dem konto dedaane jei sem maama, ko woli de balo maama na zoore teene dem konto ne to dedaane tega kam wonnu telo maama na nwoŋi ka baŋa ne to. 26Lot kaane déem ma gwi o nii o kwaga ne. O ma ji yɛ-kuŋa kandwɛ o zege da.
27Tega na poore to, Abaraham ma gwoni tega o jwoori o vo o ya na zege mɛ Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to. 28O ma tiiri o nii Sodom de Gomora teene dem seeni. O ta ma nii bwolo kom laŋa kam maama, ye o na nyo-zwona mo na zege jei sem konto ne ka zaŋe ka maa diini wɛyuu ne, ka nye dedaane nyoa kalo na nwoŋi min-vogo wone to mo.
29Wɛ na chɔge teene dem de bwolo kom maama to, o déem guli Abaraham gula ye o vere Lot o ja nwoŋi cham delo na chɔge jei sem konto maama to.
Lot de o bukwa bam taane
30Lot de o bukwa balei bam laam ma nwoŋi Zoara teo kom ne ba vo ba jeini peero tem wone, kokuri o déem kɔre se o zo Zoara ne. Ba maa zoore peo bɔɔne wone. 31Dɛ dedwe mo bukɔ-kwea kam tage de balaŋa kam we, “Debam kwo wom kwe mo, ye baaro nam tera ywo se o peini de debam nenɛɛne logo baŋa nabiina maama na yeini ba ke tei to. 32Konto ŋwaane, yage se dé pa dé kwo wom nyɔ sana o bugi se dé laam peini ded‑o, se dé kwo wom dwi yé kweeli.”
33Dento tete dem ne, ba ma pa ba kwo nyɔ sana o su. Bukɔ-kwea kam ma zo o peini ded‑o. O kwo wom maa wo maane o na zo o peini ded‑o naa o na zaŋe o nwoŋi maŋa kalo to.
34Tega na poore to, bukɔ-kwea kam ma ta de balaŋa kam we, “Amo de dé kwo diim peini daane mo. Yage se zem tete dento dé daa pa se o nyɔ sana o bugi, se nmo de vo n peini ded‑o se ko pa dé tɔge dé kwo baŋa ne dé twoŋi dé dwi dem.” 35Ba ma seene ba pa se ba kwo wom nyɔ sana o su dento tete dem ne. Bukɔ-balaŋa kam de ma vo o peini ded‑o, ye o kwo wom ta wo maane o na zo o peini ded‑o naa o na zaŋe o nwoŋi maŋa kalo to.
36Lot bukwa bam déem ma ja pwi de ba kwo wom. 37Bukɔ-kwea kam ma lo bakeira, ye o pa o yere we ‘Moaba’. Wonto mo ye Moaba tiina bam nabaaro zem dɛ dem ne. 38Bukɔ-balaŋa kam de ma lo bakeira, ye o pa o yere we ‘Ben-Ammi’. Wonto mo ye Amon tiina bam nabaaro zem dɛ dem ne.

english_text:
Abraham and Sarah at Gerar
1Abraham moved to the Southern Desert, where he settled between Kadesh and Shur. Later he went to Gerar, and while there 2 he told everyone that his wife Sarah was his sister. So King Abimelech of Gerar had Sarah brought to him. 3But God came to Abimelech in a dream and said, “You have taken a married woman into your home, and for this you will die!”
4-5Abimelech said to the Lord, “Don't kill me! I haven't slept with Sarah. Didn't they say they were brother and sister? I am completely innocent.”
6Then God continued:
I know you are innocent. That's why I kept you from sleeping with Sarah and doing anything wrong. 7Her husband is a prophet. Let her go back to him, and his prayers will save you from death. But if you don't return her, you and all your people will die.
8Early the next morning Abimelech sent for his officials, and when he told them what had happened, they were frightened. 9Abimelech then called in Abraham and said:
Look what you've done to us! What have I ever done to you? Why did you make me and my nation guilty of such a terrible sin? 10What were you thinking when you did this?
11Abraham answered:
I did it because I didn't think any of you respected God, and I was sure that someone would kill me to get my wife. 12Besides, she is my half sister. We have the same father, but different mothers. 13When God made us leave my father's home and start wandering, I told her, “If you really love me, then tell everyone that I am your brother.”
14After Abimelech had given Abraham some sheep, cattle, and slaves, he sent Sarah back 15and told Abraham he could settle anywhere in his country. 16Then he said to Sarah, “I have given your brother 1,000 pieces of silver as proof to everyone that you have done nothing wrong.”
17-18Meanwhile, God had kept Abimelech's wife and slaves from having children. But Abraham prayed, and God let them start having children again.
translation_text:
Abaraham de Abimeleka taane
1Abaraham ma zaŋe jei sem konto ne o kwei chwoŋa kalo na maa tu kuri seeni to ye o laam vo o zoore Kadese dedaane Sura tetare laŋa ne. Teene dem konto wo tega-kuri kagoa kam ne mo.
Maŋa kadwoŋi ne o ma vo o jeini Gerare ne. 2O na wora to mo Abaraham tage o kaane Sarah taane we, o ye o nakɔ. Gerare teo kom pɛ Abimeleka ma toŋe Sarah kwaga ne ye o jwoŋi‑o se o ma o ke o kaane. 3Tete dedwe ne Baŋa Wɛ ma ba Abimeleka tei dendwɛ wone o ta ded‑o we, “Nmo ye too mo, kaane wom n na kwei to na ye nɔɔno kaane to ŋwaane.”
4Abimeleka ya daa ta wo dwei‑o. Konto to, o laam maa we, “Amo Teiru, a wo ke kolokolo a chɔge. Nmo wó sɛ n chɔge teo kolo na wo ke wo-lɔŋɔ to na? 5Abaraham mo tage de amo we ‘Kaane wom ye a nakɔ mo’, ye kaane wom de ta we ‘O ye a nabɔ’. Amo ke tento de a bochare-laao mo. A jea de ba jege digiru.”
6Wɛ daa ta ma ŋɔɔne ded‑o dendwɛ dem wone we, “Ko ye chega. A yei we n na toŋe tei maama to, n ke dedaane boboŋ-laaro. Konto ŋwaane amo cheiŋi se nmo yé ke wɛleere n chɔge amo yiga mo ye a wo pɛ‑m chwoŋa se n dwei‑o. 7Nɔɔno wom ye amo ni-jwoŋinu mo. Konto ŋwaane, jwoori n pa‑o o kaane wom se o daare o lwoori amo o pa‑m se n ta‑n ŋwe. Ko daare n ná wo ke konto, nmo wó seene n te, de n nɔɔna maama.”
8Tega na poore to, Abimeleka ma gwoni tega o bwoŋi o nɔɔna bam, ye o daare o lwoni kolo maama na ke to o bere-ba. Ba na nigi to, foone ma tiini de ja-ba. 9Abimeleka ma bwoŋi Abaraham pa se o zo ba tei ye o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo nmo ke debam konto? Bɛ lwarem mo a ke‑m ye nmo laam ja chɔgem n ba amo de a teo kom baŋa ne? Nmo na ke n chɔge amo yiga tei to ba lana.” 10O ta ma bwei Abaraham we, “Bɛ mo pɛ se n ke konto?”
11Abaraham laam ma leiri we, “Amo ya boŋe we, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba kɔre Wɛ jei sento ne, ye ba wó wane ba go-ne, a kaane wom ŋwaane. 12O ta ye a nakɔ mo. Dé dae nu daane mo se o ye a kwo wom bukɔ mo, ye o laam ji amo kaane. 13Maŋa kalo Wɛ na pɛ se a nwoŋi a kwo sɔŋɔ kom ne ye a kare a beeri to, mo a tage ded‑o we ‘Sarah, ke tento se n bere we n swoi amo: Mɛ maama debam ná vei de yi, se nmo ta we, a ye n nabɔ mo.’ ”
14Abimeleka laam ma ja peeni de naane dedaane kabɛ, baara de kaana maama, o ja o nwoŋi o pa Abaraham. O ta ma jwoori o kwei Abaraham kaane Sarah o pa‑o. 15Abimeleka maa we, “Amo tega kam mo tento, nmo yiga ne. Ta n zoore jei selo maama ne n na lage to.” 16O ma daare o ta de Sarah we, “Nii, lu-nyenno sabu-dala moro mo a pɛ n nabɔ wom. Ko wó taa ye maana ko pa balo maama na wo n tei ne to se ko bere we n jege bora. Nmo wo ke kolokolo n chɔge.”
17Abaraham laam ma lwoori Wɛ o pa Abimeleka de o kaane dedaane ba ka-nyaana bam, ye Wɛ pa ba na yazura, pa se ba daa wane ba lo bia. 18Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem ya cheiŋi nɔɔna maama de bu-lore mo Abimeleka sɔŋɔ kom ne, Abaraham kaane Sarah ŋwaane.

english_text:
Sarah Has a Son
1The Lord was good to Sarah and kept his promise. 2 Although Abraham was very old, Sarah had a son exactly at the time God had said. 3Abraham named his son Isaac, 4 and when the boy was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, just as God had commanded.
5Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac was born, 6and Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. And now everyone will laugh with me. 7Who would have dared to tell Abraham that someday I would have a child? But in his old age, I have given him a son.”
8The time came when Sarah no longer had to nurse Isaac, and on that day Abraham gave a big feast.
Hagar and Ishmael Are Sent Away
9-10 One day, Sarah noticed Hagar's son Ishmael playing, and she said to Abraham, “Get rid of that Egyptian slave woman and her son! I don't want him to inherit anything. It should all go to my son.”
11Abraham was worried about Ishmael. 12 But God said, “Abraham, don't worry about your slave woman and the boy. Just do what Sarah tells you. Isaac will inherit your family name, 13but the son of the slave woman is also your son, and I will make his descendants into a great nation.”
14Early the next morning Abraham gave Hagar an animal skin full of water and some bread. Then he put the boy on her shoulder and sent them away.
They wandered around in the desert near Beersheba, 15and after they had run out of water, Hagar put her son under a bush. 16Then she sat down a long way off, because she could not bear to watch him die. And she cried bitterly.
17When God heard the boy crying, the angel of God called out to Hagar from heaven and said, “Hagar, why are you worried? Don't be afraid. I have heard your son crying. 18Help him up and hold his hand, because I will make him the father of a great nation.” 19Then God let her see a well. So she went to the well and filled the skin with water, then gave some to her son.
20-21God blessed Ishmael, and as the boy grew older, he became an expert at hunting with his bow and arrows. He lived in the Paran Desert, and his mother chose an Egyptian woman for him to marry.
A Peace Treaty
22 About this time Abimelech and his army commander Phicol said to Abraham, “God blesses everything you do! 23Now I want you to promise in the name of God that you will always be loyal to me and my descendants, just as I have always been loyal to you in this land where you have lived as a foreigner.” 24And so, Abraham promised he would.
25One day, Abraham told Abimelech, “Some of your servants have taken over one of my wells.”
26“This is the first I've heard about it,” Abimelech replied. “Why haven't you said something before? I don't have any idea who did it.” 27Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle, then the two men made a peace treaty.
28Abraham separated seven female lambs from his flock of sheep, 29and Abimelech asked, “Why have you done this?”
30Abraham replied, “I want you to accept these seven lambs as proof that I dug this well.” 31So they called the place Beersheba, because they made a treaty there.
32When the treaty was completed, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol went back to the land of the Philistines. 33Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and worshiped the eternal Lord God. 34Then Abraham lived a long time as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines.
translation_text:
Izaak lora kam taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ déem nii Sarah baŋa ne ye o seene o ke kolo o na tage ded‑o to o pa‑o. 2Sarah déem ma ja puga o lo bakeira o pa Abaraham o kokweero maŋa ne. Ko déem ke ko maŋe de maŋa kalo Wɛ na tage to mo. 3Abaraham ma pa bu wom yere we ‘Izaak’. 4Izaak na yi da nana to mo Abaraham gwoni o peini, nenɛɛne Wɛ na tage we o ke tei to. 5Abaraham déem jege bena bi mo ye ba lo o bu-baaro Izaak ba pa‑o. 6Sarah maa we, “Wɛ jaane mwanno mo o ba o pa amo, ye wolo maama na nigi kolo na ke to, kotu wó da o woli de amo mo se dé mɔne.”
7O daa ta ma woli da o we, “Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ya bá wane o ta de Abaraham we Sarah wó wane o ja bia se ba ŋɔge yele. De konto maama de, amo loge bakeira a pa‑o o kokweero maŋa ne.”
Ba zeili Hagara dedaane Isameli ba yage
8Izaak ma ke nɔɔno ye ba kwori‑o yele. Dɛ dem konto ne, Abaraham ma bwoŋi nɔɔna se ba di kuri kamunu. 9Sarah déem ma na we Ejipti tiina bukɔ Hagara na loge bakeira kalo o pa Abaraham to zege da o ke Izaak o mɔna. 10O na nɛ to, o ma ta de Abaraham we, “Zeili kaane wolo na ye kabaa to de o bu-baaro wom se ba viiri, se kaane wonto bu wom bá tɔge de amo tete bu Izaak o pɔɔre nmo jejegero tem o taa tei.”
11Taane dem ma tiini de daane Abaraham, Isameli na ye o tete bu-baaro to ŋwaane. 12Wɛ ma ta ded‑o we, “Yé ta‑n pae se bakeira kam de n kaba-kana kam taane dem daane‑m. Nam cheigi Sarah na tage tei o bere‑m to, kokuri to, ko lage ko tɔge Izaak baŋa ne mo se nmo dwi dem ba de zege. 13Amo nam ta wó pa se kaba-kana kam bu-baaro wom dwi de puli de ji teo, o de na ye nmo bu to ŋwaane.”
14Tega na poore to zezeŋa ne to, Abaraham ma kwei wodiu o pa Hagara ye o daare o lwo na lɔɔ wone o pa‑o se o daŋe o bakala baŋa ne. O laam ma bane‑o de o bakeira kam o yage-ba chwoŋa ne. Hagara de ma to chwoŋa ne o kare Beeriseba kagoa kam yuu ne o beera. 15Lɔɔ kom wo na bam ma ti. O ma ja bu wom o vo jeini sabara kadwoŋi woro ne. 16O tete laam ma fɔɔre o vo dáa o jei se ko maŋe de nɔɔno na wó ta taŋa se ka yi mɛ to. O ma boŋe we, “Amo ba lage se a na a bu wom toone.” O na jei da to, o ma bobo se o taa keera.
17Wɛ ma ni bakeira kam na keeri to. Wɛ maleka kam maa zege Wɛ telaao ne ka bwoŋi Hagara ka we, “Hagara, bɛ mo kea? Yé ta‑n fona. Wɛ niga bu wom na tigi o keeri to. 18Zaŋe n vo n ja bu wom se o zaŋe, se amo wó pa se o dwi dem ji te-zɔŋɔ.” 19Wɛ laam ma puri o yia pa se o na vole na tigi da. O ma vo o mɔ na o su o lɔɔ kom ni ye o ja vo o pa bu wom se o nyɔ.
20Wɛ déem ma nii bu wom baŋa ne ye o ba o ke nɔɔno. O déem zoore kagoa kam yuu ne mo ye o ji tɔɔno chekke. 21Kagoa kam o na zoore mɛ to yere mo Paran. O na wora to, mo o nu vei o lage kaane Ejipti ne o swo o ba o pa‑o.
Abaraham de Abimeleka ke ni-mɔrɔ daane
22Da yam konto ni ne mo Abimeleka de Fikola na ye o jar-keira yiga tu to déem vei Abaraham tei. Ba ma ta de Abaraham we, “Debam maane we kolo maama nmo ná yeini n ke, Wɛ wo n tei ne mo. 23Konto to, laam du duuri Wɛ yiga ne we nmo bá‑n ke n gane amo kɔtaa, ko ná ye amo naa a bia bam, naa a dwi dem maama. Amo na ke‑m lanyerane to, nmo de wó ke amo lanyerane, ko ná ye amo de teo kolo nmo na ye veiru ko wone to maama.” 24Abaraham maa we, “Amo sɛ se a du duuri dem konto.”
25Abimeleka nɔɔna nam ya vere Abaraham vole dedwoŋi mo. Abaraham ma ŋɔɔne taane dem de Abimeleka. 26Abimeleka ma ta o we, “Amo wo lɔre wolo na ke konto to. Nmo wo tage ko taane n bere-ne, ye zem yerane mo amo laam lɔre ko ni ne.”
27Abaraham laam ma ja peeni, de bone, de naane o ja o nwoŋi o pa Abimeleka, ye banto balei ke ni-sɛɛm daane. 28Abaraham ma daare o le pi-chwa barepɛ o vara bam wone o zege dáa ne. 29Abimeleka ma bwei Abaraham we, “Bɛŋwaane mo nmo pɔɔre pi-chwa yam yarepɛ?” 30O ma leiri we, “Jwoŋi pi-chwa yarepɛ yam amo tei ne se ko taa ye maana we amo mo koge vole dento.” 31Ba déem ma bwoŋi jei sem konto we Beeriseba, kokuri dáane mo nɔɔna banto balei déem dugi duuri.
32Ba na ke ni-sɛɛm dem konto Beeriseba ne ba ti to mo Abimeleka dedaane o jar-keira yiga tu Fikola jwoori ba vo Filisi tiina teo kom. 33Abaraham de ma zege Beeriseba ne o jeiri tio kodwoŋi ko yere na ye ‘Tamarisaka’ to. Dáane mo o bwoŋi Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ yere o zuli‑o, o na ye Wɛ wolo na maŋe o wora taa wuu to. 34Abaraham déem maa zoore Filisi tiina teo kom wone o dáane da.

english_text:
The Lord Tells Abraham To Offer Isaac as a Sacrifice
1 Some years later God decided to test Abraham, so he spoke to him.
Abraham answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
2 The Lord said, “Go get Isaac, your only son, the one you dearly love! Take him to the land of Moriah, and I will show you a mountain where you must sacrifice him to me on the fires of an altar.” 3So Abraham got up early the next morning and chopped wood for the fire. He put a saddle on his donkey and set out with Isaac and two servants for the place where God had told him to go.
4Three days later Abraham looked off in the distance and saw the place. 5He told his servants, “Stay here with the donkey, while my son and I go over there to worship. We will come back.”
6Abraham put the wood on Isaac's shoulder, but he carried the hot coals and the knife. As the two of them walked along, 7-8Isaac said, “Father, we have the coals and the wood, but where is the lamb for the sacrifice?”
“My son,” Abraham answered, “God will provide the lamb.”
The two of them walked on, and 9 when they reached the place that God had told him about, Abraham built an altar and placed the wood on it. Next, he tied up his son and put him on the wood. 10 He then took the knife and got ready to kill his son. 11But the Lord's angel shouted from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!”
“Here I am!” he answered.
12“Don't hurt the boy or harm him in any way!” the angel said. “Now I know that you truly obey God, because you were willing to offer him your only son.”
13Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in the bushes. So he took the ram and sacrificed it instead of his son.
14Abraham named that place “The Lord Will Provide.” And even now people say, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”
15The Lord's angel called out from heaven a second time:
16 You were willing to offer your only son to the Lord, and so he makes you this solemn promise, 17 “I will bless you and give you such a large family, that someday your descendants will be more numerous than the stars in the sky or the grains of sand along the seashore. They will defeat their enemies and take over the cities where their enemies live. 18 You have obeyed me, and so you and your descendants will be a blessing to all nations on earth.”
19Abraham and Isaac went back to the servants who had come with him, and they returned to Abraham's home in Beersheba.
The Children of Nahor
20-23Abraham's brother Nahor had married Milcah, and Abraham was later told that they had eight sons. Uz was their first-born; Buz was next, and then there was Kemuel the father of Aram; their other five sons were: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel the father of Rebekah. 24Nahor also had another wife. Her name was Reumah, and she had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
translation_text:
Wɛ faŋe Abaraham o nii
1Ko na ke fee to, Wɛ ma ke Abaraham o nii. O ma bwoŋi‑o o ta we, “Abaraham!” O ma leiri we, “Nii-ne.” 2Wɛ laam maa we, “Ja n bu-doa Izaak wom n na tiini n swoi to, n vo Moria laŋa kam se n ma‑o n kaane dáane n zwɛ‑o n pa-ne, peero tem dedoa yuu ne a na wó bere‑m to.”
3Tega na poore to, Abaraham ma zaŋe zezeŋa ne o ja o bonaga se o kɛ chwoŋa. O ma ja o tontoŋena balei dedaane o bu-baaro Izaak o woli da. O ma gwoni da-kore selo o na wó ma o zwɛ pɛɛra yam to. O laam ma kwei chwoŋa o maa vei jei selo Wɛ na tage we o véi to. 4Da yatɔ dɛ dem ne mo Abaraham kwoni o yuu wɛɛne o na jei sem yiga ne. 5O ma ta de o tontoŋena bam we, “Abam de bonaga kam maŋe-na ywo se amo dedaane bakeira kam vo dáane. Dé wó vo de zuli Wɛ ye dé daa ta jwoori dé ba abam tei ne.”
6Abaraham na tage konto to, o ma kwei dɛ sem o zeŋe o bu-baaro Izaak. Wonto tete laam maa zei mini dem de seo kom. Banto balei na vei ba maa kɛ to, 7Izaak ma bwoŋi o kwo Abaraham ye o ta o we, “Amo kwo.” O de ma leiri we, “Amo bu, nmo we bɛ mo?” Izaak maa we, “A nɛ mini dem de dɛ sem na wo ywo to, se pipeila kalo dé na lage dé zwɛ kaanem dé pa Wɛ to laam nam bɛ?” 8Abaraham ma leiri we, “Amo bu, Wɛ tete mo wó na pipeila kalo dé na wó zwɛ dé ma ke kaanem dem to o pa debam.”
Banto balei daa ta maa vei yiga. 9Ba na yi jei selo Wɛ na tage o bere Abaraham to, o ma tigisi kandwa o lɔ bimbini dáane ye o tɛɛse dɛ sem de baŋa ne. O laam ma vɔ o bu-baaro Izaak ye o gɔ‑o o daŋe dɛ sem baŋa ne. 10O laam ma tore o jeŋa o le seo kom se o go o bu wom. 11Bedwe baŋa ne mo Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam zege Wɛ telaao ne ka bwoŋi‑o we, “Abaraham! Abaraham!” O de ma sɛ o we, “Nii-ne da.” 12Maleka kam ma ta ka we, “Yé ke n bu wom zonne. Nam yé chɔge‑o. Amo laam maane we nmo seene n kɔre Wɛ, kokuri to nmo wo ve se n kwei n bu-doa kam n pa Baŋa Wɛ.”
13Abaraham ma kwoni o yuu wɛɛne ye o na we pi-bɛa mo zege sabara kadwoŋi wone, ka nyea na gerege ka wone to ŋwaane. O ma fɔɔre o yi pia kam tei o ja-ka o ba o ma o ke kaanem o zwɛ o pa Wɛ o ma o leiri o bu-baaro wom yuu ne. 14Ko déem ma pa se Abaraham bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we ‘Baŋa Wɛ wó pa’. De zem maama de, nɔɔna ta yeini ba tɛ we, “Baŋa Wɛ peo kom yuu ne, pɛɛra wó taa wora.”
15 Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam daa ta ma zege Wɛ telaao ne ka bwoŋi Abaraham ka ke kuni belei 16ye ka we, “Cheigi Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to we, ‘Nmo na ke tento ye n wo ve se n kwei n bu-doa kam n pa amo mo, a dugi a tete ŋwaane mo we, 17amo wó seene a swɛ nmo swolim, ye a pa se nmo dwi dem puli dedɛ de taa daga nenɛɛne wɛyuu chalechwe sem dedaane naneo ni kasol-bia na daga tei to. Nmo dwi dem wó taa jege dam se ba jwoŋi ba dona teene ba taa tei. 18Ko ta lage ko tɔge nmo dwi dem baŋa ne mo se logo baŋa teene maama na zaane ba de baŋa ne, nmo tete na sɛ amo ni to ŋwaane.’ ”
19Abaraham de o bu Izaak laam ma jwoori o tontoŋena bam tei. Ba maama ma kwei Beeriseba chwoŋa kam ba maa kɛa. Ba na yi da to, Abaraham ma maŋe Beeriseba ne.
20Ko na ke fee ko woli da to, Abaraham ma ni we, o choro Nahora kaane Milika de loge bu-baara o pa‑o. 21Bia bam yera mo tento: Yuzi, bu-kwea kam, ko woli de o nyaane Buzi, de Kemweli, o na ye Aram kwo to, 22de Chesed, de Hazo, de Pilidasi, de Jidalafa, dedaane Bɛtuweli.
23Bɛtuweli ma ji Rebeka kwo. Milika déem loge bakeiri nana banto mo o pa Abaraham choro Nahora. 24Nahora déem jege ka-bia, o yere na ye Reuma. Wonto de déem ma lo bakeiri sento o pa‑o: Teba, de Gaham, de Tahasi, dedaane Maaka.

english_text:
Sarah's Death and Burial
1-2When Sarah was 127 years old, she died in Kiriath-Arba, better known as Hebron, in the land of Canaan. After Abraham had mourned for her, 3he went to the Hittites and said, 4 “I live as a foreigner in your land, and I don't own any property where I can bury my wife. Please let me buy a piece of land.”
5-6“Sir,” they answered, “you are an important man. Choose the best place to bury your wife. None of us would refuse you a resting place for your dead.”
7Abraham bowed down 8and replied, “If you are willing to let me bury my wife here, please ask Zohar's son Ephron 9to sell me Machpelah Cave at the end of his field. I'll pay what it's worth, and all of you can be witnesses.”
10Ephron was sitting there near the city gate, when Abraham made this request, and he answered, 11“Sir, the whole field, including the cave, is yours. With my own people as witnesses, I freely give it to you as a burial place for your dead.”
12Once again, Abraham bowed down 13and said to Ephron, “In front of these witnesses, I offer you the full price, so I can bury my wife. Please accept my offer.”
14-15“But sir,” the man replied, “the property is worth only 400 pieces of silver. Why should we haggle over such a small amount? Take the land. It's yours.”
16-18Abraham accepted Ephron's offer and paid him the 400 pieces of silver in front of everyone at the city gate. That's how Abraham came to own Ephron's property east of Mamre, which included the field with all of its trees, as well as Machpelah Cave at the end of the field. 19So Abraham buried his wife Sarah in Machpelah Cave that was in the field 20he had bought from the Hittites.
translation_text:
Sarah toone
1Sarah déem jege bena bi de finlei-yarepɛ (127) mo, 2ye o laam ba o te Kiriaf-Araba ne. Ko ye Kanaan teo mo, ko yere dedwoŋi mo Heboron. Abaraham ma zaŋe o vo se o keeri Sarah ye o ka yi-na o ŋwaane.
3Abaraham kaane wom na tega to, o ma zaŋe o baŋa ne ye o vo se o ŋɔɔne dedaane Hiti tiina bam. O maa we, 4“Amo ye veiru mo a na zoore abam tetare ne. A nam lwoori tega se á pa-ne se ko taa ye mɛ amo na wó suli a too wom da to.”
5Hiti tiina bam ma leiri Abaraham we, 6“Cheigi ywo-seeni. Nmo ye dedɛɛro kamunu mo debam tetare ne. Konto to, kuri debam yibeela yam wone delo na lamma de pa‑m to se n suli n too wom da. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá ve nmo we n yé suli n too wom o yibeeli ne.”
7Abaraham ma zaŋe wɛɛne o tiiri tega ne Hiti tiina bam na ye tega kam tiina to yiga ne. 8O ma ta-ba o we, “Abam nam ná sɛ se amo suli a kaane wom ywo-seeni, se á sɛ se á lwoori Zohare bu Eforon á pa-ne. 9Lwoori‑o á pa-ne se o kwei Machapela peo-bɔɔne dem na wo o kara kam siseini ni ne to o pa-ne. Ko na ye o nyem to, amo wó ŋwe ko sabu kom ni maama a pa‑o. Dé wó ke konto abam maama yiga ne se bɔɔne dem laam ji yibeeli de pa-ne.”
10Hiti tu Eforon de déem jei o nɔɔna bam wone. O ma leiri Abaraham tento pa se Hiti tiina balo maama déem na dɛ ba jeeri teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni ne to de cheigi. 11O maa we, “Amo tu, cheigi ywo-seeni. Amo wó kwei kara kam mo a pa‑m zɛɛra, ye a ta wó pa‑m peo-bɔɔne delo na wo ka laŋa ne to a woli da. Amo nɔɔna bam yiga ne mo a kwei a pa‑m. Véi n suli n kaane wom da.”
12Abaraham daa ma tiiri tega ne teo kom nɔɔna bam yiga ne. 13O ma ta de Eforon pa se ba maama ni ye o we, “Nam cheigi a na tɛ kolo to. Amo wó ŋwe tega kam sabu a pa‑m. Sɛ se n jwoŋi sabu kom se amo de wane a kwei a kaane wom a suli dáane.”
14Eforon ma leiri Abaraham we, 15“Amo tu, cheigi-ne. Tega kam sabu maŋe dedaane lu-nyenno sabu-dala bia yana yerane mo. Konto nam dae kolo debam na wó daane daane ko baŋa ne to. Kwei-ka n ma n suli n kaane wom.”
16Abaraham ma sɛ se o ŋwe tega kam sabu kom ni se ko maŋe de Eforon na bere tei Hiti tiina bam maama yiga ne to. O ma maŋe lu-nyenno sabu-dala bia yana mo o pa‑o se ko maŋe de maŋem delo pipiu-tiina bam déem na jege ba maŋa yaga ne to.
17Ko déem ke konto ye Eforon kara kam na wo Machapela ne ye ka bwola de Mamere to ba ka ji Abaraham nyem. Kara kam konto dedaane peo-bɔɔne delo na wo ka wone to, dedaane teeni delo maama na wo kara kam wone to laam ma ji Abaraham nyem. 18O déem yeigi-ka Hiti tiina balo maama na jeeri teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni ne to tei ne mo ye ba sɛ we ko ye o nyem.
19Ko maama na ti to, mo Abaraham laam suli o kaane Sarah Machapela peo-bɔɔne dem wone. Kara kam bwola de Mamere. Konto ye Kanaan te-balaŋa mo ye ko twɛ Heboron. 20Mo ko na ke tei ye Hiti tiina bam kwei tega kam konto de ka peo-bɔɔne dem ba pa Abaraham se ko taa ye o yibeela jei to.

english_text:
A Wife for Isaac
1Abraham was now a very old man. The Lord had made him rich, and he was successful in everything he did. 2One day, Abraham called in his most trusted servant and said to him, “Solemnly promise me 3in the name of the Lord, who rules heaven and earth, that you won't choose a wife for my son Isaac from the people here in the land of Canaan. 4Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for him from among my relatives.”
5But the servant asked, “What if the young woman I choose refuses to leave home and come here with me? Should I send Isaac there to look for a wife?”
6“No!” Abraham answered. “Don't ever do that, no matter what. 7The Lord who rules heaven brought me here from the land where I was born and promised that he would give this land to my descendants forever. When you go back there, the Lord will send his angel ahead of you to help you find a wife for my son. 8If the woman refuses to come along, you don't have to keep this promise. But don't ever take my son back there.” 9So the servant gave Abraham his word that he would do everything he had been told to do.
10Soon after that, the servant loaded ten of Abraham's camels with valuable gifts. Then he set out for the city in northern Syria, where Abraham's brother Nahor lived.
11When he got there, he let the camels rest near the well outside the city. It was late afternoon, the time when the women came out for water. 12The servant prayed:
You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships. Please keep your promise to him and let me find a wife for Isaac today. 13The young women of the city will soon come to this well for water, 14and I'll ask one of them for a drink. If she gives me a drink and then offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen and that you have kept your promise to my master.
15-16While he was still praying, a beautiful unmarried young woman came by with a water jar on her shoulder. She was Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his wife Milcah. Rebekah walked past Abraham's servant, then went over to the well, and filled her water jar. When she started back, 17Abraham's servant ran to her and said, “Please let me have a drink of water.”
18“I'll be glad to,” she answered. Then she quickly took the jar from her shoulder and held it while he drank. 19-20After he had finished, she said, “Now I'll give your camels all the water they want.” She quickly poured out water for them, and she kept going back for more, until his camels had drunk all they wanted. 21Abraham's servant did not say a word, but he watched everything Rebekah did, because he wanted to know for certain if this was the woman the Lord had chosen.
22The servant had brought along an expensive gold ring and two large gold bracelets. When Rebekah had finished bringing the water, he gave her the ring for her nose and the bracelets for her arms. 23Then he said, “Please tell me who your father is. Does he have room in his house for me and my men to spend the night?”
24She answered, “My father is Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah. 25We have a place where you and your men can stay, and we also have enough straw and feed for your camels.”
26Then the servant bowed his head and prayed, 27“I thank you, Lord God of my master Abraham! You have led me to his relatives and kept your promise to him.”
28Rebekah ran straight home and told her family everything. 29-30Her brother Laban heard her tell what the servant had said, and he saw the ring and the bracelets she was wearing. So Laban ran out to Abraham's servant, who was standing by his camels at the well. 31Then Laban said, “The Lord has brought you safely here. Come home with me. There's no need for you to keep on standing outside. I have a room ready for you in our house, and there's also a place for your camels.”
32Abraham's servant went home with Laban, where Laban's servants unloaded his camels and gave them straw and feed. Then they brought water into the house, so Abraham's servant and his men could wash their feet. 33After that, they brought in food. But the servant said, “Before I eat, I must tell you why I have come.”
“Go ahead and tell us,” Laban answered.
34The servant explained:
I am Abraham's servant. 35The Lord has been good to my master and has made him very rich. He has given him many sheep, goats, cattle, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of silver and gold, and many slaves. 36Sarah, my master's wife, didn't have any children until she was very old. Then she had a son, and my master has given him everything. 37I solemnly promised my master that I would do what he said. And he told me, “Don't choose a wife for my son from the women in this land of Canaan. 38Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for my son from among my relatives.”
39I asked my master, “What if the young woman refuses to come with me?”
40My master answered, “I have always obeyed the Lord, and he will send his angel to help you find my son a wife from among my own relatives. 41But if they refuse to let her come back with you, then you are freed from your promise.”
42When I came to the well today, I silently prayed, “You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships, so please lead me to a wife for his son 43while I am here at the well. When a young woman comes out to get water, I'll ask her to give me a drink. 44If she gives me a drink and offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen.”
45Even before I had finished praying, Rebekah came by with a water jar on her shoulder. When she had filled the jar, I asked her for a drink. 46She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said, “Have a drink. Then I'll get water for your camels.” So I drank, and after that she got some water for my camels. 47I asked her who her father was, and she answered, “My father is Bethuel the son of Nahor and Milcah.” At once I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms. 48Then I bowed my head and gave thanks to the God my master Abraham worships. The Lord had led me straight to my master's relatives, and I had found a wife for his son.
49Now please tell me if you are willing to do the right thing for my master. Will you treat him fairly, or do I have to look for another young woman?
50Laban and Bethuel answered, “The Lord has done this. We have no choice in the matter. 51Take Rebekah with you; she can marry your master's son, just as the Lord has said.” 52Abraham's servant bowed down and thanked the Lord. 53Then he gave clothing, as well as silver and gold jewelry, to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.
54Abraham's servant and the men with him ate and drank, then spent the night there. The next morning they got up, and the servant told Rebekah's mother and brother, “I would like to go back to my master now.”
55“Let Rebekah stay with us for a week or ten days,” they answered. “Then she may go.”
56But he said, “Don't make me stay any longer. The Lord has already helped me find a wife for my master's son. Now let us return.”
57They answered, “Let's ask Rebekah what she wants to do.” 58They called her and asked, “Are you willing to leave with this man at once?”
“Yes,” she answered.
59So they agreed to let Rebekah and an old family servant woman leave immediately with Abraham's servant and his men. 60They gave Rebekah their blessing and said, “We pray that God will give you many children and grandchildren and that he will help them defeat their enemies.” 61Afterwards, Rebekah and the young women who were to travel with her prepared to leave. Then they got on camels and left with Abraham's servant and his men.
62At that time Isaac was living in the southern part of Canaan near a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.” 63-65One evening he was walking out in the fields, when suddenly he saw a group of people approaching on camels. So he started toward them. Rebekah saw him coming; she got down from her camel, and asked, “Who is that man?”
“He is my master Isaac,” the servant answered. Then Rebekah covered her face with her veil.
66The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.
67Isaac took Rebekah into the tent where his mother had lived before she died, and Rebekah became his wife. He loved her and was comforted over the loss of his mother.
translation_text:
Izaak kadiri
1Abaraham déem ma tiini o kwe ye o bena gaale. O chwoŋa maama wone Baŋa Wɛ ma ke zaane o ke o yuu ne. 2O ma bwoŋi o sɔŋɔ tontoŋena bam maama yiga tu wom, wolo na nii o wonnu maama baŋa ne to ye o ta ded‑o we, “Kwei n jeŋa n ke amo chwei kuri ne se n du duuri. 3Nmo jege se n du duuri Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane, o na tei wɛyuu de tega baŋa to. Du duuri n pa-ne we, debam na seene dé zoore Kanaan tiina bam wone to, nmo bá beeri kaane ba bukwa bam wone n pa amo bu Izaak. 4Nmo nam wó jwoori n vo amo nabaara teo kom, de a dwi tiina na wo mɛ to mo n beeri kaane n pa‑o.”
5Tontoŋeno wom ma bwei‑o we, “Se kaane wom ná wo sɛ se o tɔge de amo o jwoori o ba tega kanto ne, a wó ke tɛ mo? A wó ja n bu wom a jwoori a vo mɛ n na nwoŋi n ba ywo to mo na?” 6Abaraham ma leiri o ta we, “Ta‑n yei se n daa‑n yé ja amo bu wom n jwoori dáane. 7Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ wom na tei wɛyuu to mo jaane amo o ja o nwoŋi a kwo sɔŋɔ ne se a yage a dwi tiina tega kam. Wonto mo ŋɔɔne de amo o du duuri we ‘Nmo dwi dem mo a wó seene a pa tega kanto’. Wonto mo lage o toŋe o maleka se ka tɔge nmo yiga ka vo se nmo wane n na kaane dáane n ja n ba n pa amo bu wom. 8Kaane wom nam ná wo sɛ se o tɔge de nmo o ba ywo-seeni, kanto maŋa ne mo duuri dento daa bá taa wo n yuu ne. Nmo yé ja amo bu wom n jwoori n vo dáane.” 9Tontoŋeno wom ma sɛ o kwei o jeŋa o ke o tu Abaraham chwei kuri ne ye o du duuri, taane dem konto ŋwaane.
10Tontoŋeno wom laam ma le kona fuga Abaraham kona yam wone o ma o zeŋe o tu wom wo-laaro dwi maama o ja o woli da o kɛ. O ma kwei chwoŋa se o vo Mesopotamia seeni. O ma vo o yi teo kolo Nahora déem na zoore to. 11O na yi teo kom ni to, o ma pa se o kona yam kuni ya nadwoona ya tigi vole ni ne. Ko déem ye dedaan-ni ne mo, maŋa kalo kaana na nwoŋi ba vei ba mɔɔne na to. 12O ma lwoori Wɛ ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ, amo tu Abaraham Wɛ, nam pa se ko ke lanyerane ko pa-ne zem dɛ dem ne, se n daare n duri amo tu Abaraham ŋwaŋa. 13Nii! Amo zege vole dento ni ne mo, ye teo kom bukwa bam wó ba se ba mɔ na. 14Amo ná tage dedaane busankana kalo we ‘Ja! Zoore n kɔɔro wom n zege se n ke na n pa-ne se a nyɔ,’ ye konto tu wom ná taga we ‘Nyɔ, se n daare se a mɔ na a pa n kona yam se ya de nyɔ,’ pa se wonto taa ye wolo nmo na kuri se n pa Izaak to. Ko nam ná ke konto mo, amo wó lɔre we nmo seene n duri amo tu wom ŋwaŋa.”
15O daa ta na wora o lwoori Wɛ konto to, mo o nɛ Rebeka na vei o beene, ye o zeŋe kɔɔro o bakale baŋa ne. O déem ye Bɛtuweli bukɔ mo. Bɛtuweli de maa ye Abaraham choro Nahora de o kaane Milika bu. 16Busankana kam déem tiini ka lamma. O déem maa ta yeiri baaro. O ma yi vole dem ni, o mɔ na o su o kɔɔro wom ye o jwoori o bɛ.
17Abaraham tontoŋeno wom ma ke lela o jeeri‑o ye o we, “Ja! Twei na n kɔɔro wom ne n pa-ne se a nyɔ.” 18O de maa we, “Amo tu, nam nyɔ”, ye o ke lela o zoore o kɔɔro wom o zeeri o jea ne se o nyɔ. 19O na pɛ se o nyɔ o ti to, busankana kam maa we, “A lage a mɔ na bam mo a pa n kona yam de, se ya maama nyɔ ya su.” 20O laam ma ke lela o lwo na bam o ke vara na nyɔɔm gwoŋo wone, ye o daa jwoori vole dem ne o mɔ na bam o woli da. O ke konto mo taa o mɔ na bam pa se kona yam maama nyɔ ya su. 21Nɔɔno wom de maa wo tage kolokolo, ye o laam fɔge o nii busankana kam lanyerane se o lɔre Baŋa Wɛ seene o pa se o chwoŋa kam veiŋa ke lanyerane naa ko dae konto.
22Kona yam na nyɔge na bam ya ti to, mo nɔɔno wom le sabu-seŋa jafole delo ba déem na ke momwa ne to dedaane jeŋa bɛ selei se o pa Rebeka. Wonnu tem konto déem tiini te jege sabu. 23O laam ma bwei‑o we, “Nmo ye wɔ bukɔ mo? Jei nam wó taa wo abam sɔŋɔ ne se a peini tete dento se tega poore na?” 24Rebeka ma leiri o we, “Amo ye Bɛtuweli bukɔ mo. Wonto maa ye Milika de Nahora bu.” 25O ta ma woli da we, “Debam jege jei se nmo dedaane balo na tɔge‑m to peini da. Vara wodiu dedɛ de wora se á kona yam de di ya su.”
26O na nigi konto to, nɔɔno wom ma chɔɔle tega ne o zuli Baŋa Wɛ, 27ye o we, “Amo wó tei Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye amo tu Abaraham Wɛ to. Kokuri to, o seene o zege o chega kam wone mo ye o swoi amo tu Abaraham. Ko nam ná ye amo, Baŋa Wɛ tɔge amo yiga mo chwoŋa kam maama ne o ja-ne o ja o yi amo tu wom tete nɔɔna wone.”
28Rebeka ma ke lela o duri o vo sɔŋɔ o guli wonnu tento maama de o nu de ba sɔŋɔ tiina bam. 29O déem jege nabɔ o yere na ye Laban. Wonto ma ke lela o duri o vo se o jeeri nɔɔno wom vole dem ni ne. 30O ya maŋe o na jafole dem o nakɔ wom momwɛ ne de bɛ sem na wo o je sem ne to, ye o ta ni taane delo maama nɔɔno wom ya na tage de Rebeka to. Laban ma ke lela o nwoŋi o vo o na nɔɔno wom na zege vole dem ni ne de o kona yam. 31O maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ ke zaane nmo yuu ne mo. Pa se dé vo sɔŋɔ. Bɛŋwaane mo nmo wó ta‑n zege pwola kanto ne? Amo nam maŋe a kwɛ diga nmo ŋwaane, ye kona yam de wó na jei ya taa tiga.”
32Nɔɔno wom laam ma tɔge o vo o zo ba sɔŋɔ kom. Laban ma zoore o kona yam zela yam. O ma beeri vara wodiu o pa kona yam, ye o daare o ke na se Abaraham tontoŋeno wom de balo na tɔge dedaane‑o to zare ba nɛ. 33Ba na jaane wodiu kom ba ba to, mo Abaraham tontoŋeno wom we, “Amo ná wo tage kolo na wo a ni ne to, a bá di wodiu.” Laban maa we, “Nam ta n bere debam.”
34O laam ma tole taane dem o we:
“Amo ye Abaraham tontoŋeno mo. 35Baŋa Wɛ nam mo tiini o ke zaane o ke amo tu wom yuu ne pa se o laam ji jejegero tu. Wɛ pɛ‑o peeni, de bone, de naane, ko woli de lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa, de tontoŋe-baara de tontoŋe-kana, dedaane kona de bonɛ. 36Amo tu kaane Sarah ya loge bakeira o pa‑o mo o kokweero maŋa kam ne. Amo tu wom de kwei woŋo kolo maama o na jege to mo o pa bu wom konto. 37Amo tu wom laam ya ma pa se amo du duuri, ye o ta we ‘N ná wó beeri kaane se n pa a bu wom, yé beeri Kanaan tiina bukwa bam wone, mɛ tento amo na zoore leile to. 38Nam jwoori n vo amo nabaara teo kom n lage kaane amo tete sɔ-yuu kom ne n pa amo bu wom.’ 39Amo de ma bwei a tu wom we ‘Se kaane wom ná ve se o tɔge de amo o jwoori o ba, se a ke tɛ mo?’
40O de ma leiri we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wolo wom a na sɛ o ni to wó toŋe o maleka se o da nmo yiga se nmo chwoŋa kam veiŋa ke lanyerane. Ko wó pa se n na kaane n pa amo bu wom se o nwoŋi amo tete sɔ-yuu kom ne, amo kwo dwi tiina wone. 41Nmo nam ná lwoori n vo amo sɔ-yuu kom ne, ye ba ve‑m ba bukɔ wom, n laam wó sii duuri delo a na pɛ se n du to wone.’
42Amo zem ma na tu a yi vole dem ni to, mo a lwoori Wɛ we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ, na ye amo tu Abaraham Wɛ to, nenɛɛne ko ná su nmo yi, sɛ se a chwoŋa kam veiŋa ke lanyerane. 43Nii! Amo zege vole dem ni ne mo ywo. Bukɔ wolo ná tu ywo se o mɔ na ye a ta ded‑o we, “Ja! Pa-ne n kɔɔro wom wo na fee se a nyɔ,” 44ye kotu ná tage de amo we, “Nyɔ, se a ta wó mɔ na se n kona yam de nyɔ,” sɛ se o taa ye kaane wolo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri se o zo amo tu wom bu-baaro to.’
45Tɔ. Amo bere a maŋe a wo lwoori wɛ-lworo kom a bochare ne a ti dedaane Rebeka na maa beena, de o bakale baŋa kɔɔro. O ma yi vole dem o mɔ na bam, ye amo de ta ded‑o we ‘Ja! Pa-ne na se a nyɔ.’ 46O ma ke lela o zoore o kɔɔro wom ye o we ‘Nyɔ, se a ta wó pa n kona yam de na se ya nyɔ.’ Amo ma nyɔ ye o seene o mɔ na o pa kona yam ye ya nyɔ. 47Amo de ma bwei‑o we ‘Nmo ye wɔ bukɔ mo?’ O ma leiri we ‘Amo ye Bɛtuweli bukɔ mo. Amo kwo wom mo ye wolo Milika na loga o pa Nahora to.’ A na lɔre konto to, mo a laam kwei jafole dem a ke o momwɛ ne a daare a kwei bɛ sem a ke o je sem ne. 48A ma chɔɔle tega ne a tei Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye amo tu Abaraham Wɛ to. Wɛ wom konto mo dɛ amo yiga ye o bere-ne chwo-laao kom se a wane a na amo tu wom choro bukɔ se o taa ye a tu wom bu-kaane.
49Konto to, ko laam wo abam tei ne. Á ná sɛ se á ke amo tu wom lanyerane ye á ke chega á pa‑o, se á ta á bere-ne. Á nam daa ná lage se á lɔ o kwaga ne mo, ta ta-na á bere-ne, se amo laam wó lɔre chwoŋa kalo a na wó tɔge to.”
50Laban de Bɛtuweli ma leiri we, “Tento nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ tei ne mo. Debam bá wane de ta kolokolo dede‑m nenɛɛne dé sɛ naa dé wo sɛ. 51Nii Rebeka da, ja‑o n viiri n vo n pa n tu bu wom se o taa ye o kaane, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na bere tei to.”
52Abaraham tontoŋeno wom na nigi ba na tage tei to, o ma tiiri tega ne o ke Baŋa Wɛ lei. 53O laam ma le zela o tampɔgɔ ne o kwei o pa Rebeka. Pɛɛra yam déem ye sabu-seŋa dedaane lu-nyenno wonnu tedwonna ko woli de gwaaro. O ta ma le pɛɛra yalo na tiini ya ke sabu to o pa Rebeka nabɔ wom de o nu. 54Konto maama kwaga ne, o de nɔɔna balo na tɔge daane to laam ma di ba daare ba nyɔ ye ba peini sɔŋɔ kom ne pa se tega poore.
Tega na poore ye ba zaŋe zezeŋa ne to mo Abaraham tontoŋeno wom tage we, “Yage-na amo chwoŋa ne se a jwoori a vo a tu wom tei ne.” 55Bukɔ wom nabɔ de o nu ma leiri we, “Yage se bukɔ wom maŋe debam tei ne se ko yi nenɛɛne da fuga to, se abam laam viiri.” 56O de ma leiri we, “Baŋa Wɛ na lwoori o pa se amo chwoŋa kam ke lanyerane to, daa yé cheiŋi-na amo. Pa-na pwola se a jwoori amo tu wom tei.” 57Ba maa we, “Yage se dé bwoŋi busankana kam dé bwei‑o dé nii.” 58Ba ma bwoŋi Rebeka ba bwei‑o we, “Nmo wó sɛ n da dedaane nɔɔno wonto n kɛ na?” O ma leiri we, “Amo wó vo.”
59Ba ma sɛ ye ba bane ba nakɔ Rebeka de wolo na wó taa nii o baŋa ne to ba yage chwoŋa ne, ko woli de Abaraham tontoŋeno wom de balo na tɔge ded‑o to. 60Ba ma kwei Wɛ zaane ba ma swɛ Rebeka swolim ye ba ta ded‑o we:
“Debam nakɔ, Wɛ wó pa se nmo dwi puli
de yi morro morro.
Wɛ wó pa se nmo dwi dem taa jege dam
se ba jwoŋi ba dona teene ba taa tei.”
61Rebeka de o ka-nyaana bam ma ti ba yiga ye ba di kona yam ba tɔge de nɔɔno wom ba kɛ. Mo ko na ke tei ye Abaraham tontoŋeno wom ja Rebeka o ja viiri.
62Izaak déem ya zaŋe Beeri Lahayi Royi ne o vo o zoore tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam ne mo. 63Dedaan-ni ne o ma nwoŋi o vo o kara o kare o beera. O ma kwoni o yuu wɛɛne ye o na kona na vei ya beena. 64Rebeka de ma kwoni o yuu o nii ye o na Izaak. O ma zege o kone dem yuu ne o faŋe o chu tega ne. 65Rebeka daa ma bwei Abaraham tontoŋeno wom we, “Wɔ mo tento kara kam ne o na vei o beene se o jeeri debam to?” O ma leiri we, “Amo tu Izaak mo.” O na lɔre konto to, o ma kwei o yu-gare-daŋɔ kom o ma o kwoli o yibia.
66Abaraham tontoŋeno wom laam ma lwoni o bere Izaak o na ke tei maama to. 67Izaak ma ja Rebeka o zo o nu Sarah vwei dem wone. O déem ma di o ma o ke kaane. Izaak maa swoi‑o lanyerane. Izaak wo déem ya chɔge de o nu toone dem ye Rebeka laam pa se o wo jwoori ko zuri.

english_text:
Abraham Marries Keturah
1Abraham married Keturah, 2and they had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. 3Later, Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan, and when Dedan grew up, he had three sons: Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim. 4Midian also had five sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah.
5-6While Abraham was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of Hagar and Keturah. He also sent their sons to live in the east far from his son Isaac, and when Abraham died, he left everything to Isaac.
The Death of Abraham
7-8Abraham died at the ripe old age of 175. 9-10 His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him east of Hebron in Machpelah Cave that was part of the field Abraham had bought from Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite. Abraham was buried there beside his wife Sarah. 11God blessed Isaac after this, and Isaac moved to a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
Ishmael's Descendants
12Ishmael was the son of Abraham and Hagar, the slave woman of Sarah. 13Ishmael had twelve sons, in this order: Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, 14Mishma, Dumah, Massa, 15Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. 16Each of Ishmael's sons was a tribal chief, and a village was named after each of them.
17-18Ishmael had settled in the land east of his brothers, and his sons settled everywhere from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt on the way to Asshur. Ishmael was 137 when he died.
The Birth of Esau and Jacob
19Isaac was the son of Abraham, 20and he was 40 years old when he married Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel. She was also the sister of Laban, the Aramean from northern Syria.
Almost 20 years later, 21Rebekah still had no children. So Isaac asked the Lord to let her have a child, and the Lord answered his prayer.
22Before Rebekah gave birth, she knew she was going to have twins, because she could feel them inside her, fighting each other. She thought, “Why is this happening to me?” Finally, she asked the Lord why her twins were fighting, 23 and he told her:
“Your two sons will become
two separate nations.
The younger of the two
will be stronger,
and the older son
will be his servant.”
24When Rebekah gave birth, 25the first baby was covered with red hair, so he was named Esau. 26The second baby grabbed on to his brother's heel, so they named him Jacob. Isaac was 60 years old when they were born.
Esau Sells His Rights as the First-Born Son
27As Jacob and Esau grew older, Esau liked the outdoors and became a good hunter, while Jacob lived the quiet life of a shepherd. 28Esau would take the meat of wild animals to his father Isaac, so Isaac loved him more, but Jacob was his mother's favorite son.
29One day, when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came home hungry 30and said, “I'm starving to death! Here and now give me some of that red stew!” That's how Esau got the name “Edom.”
31Jacob replied, “Sell me your rights as the first-born son.”
32“I'm about to die,” Esau answered. “What good will those rights do me?”
33 But Jacob said, “Promise me your birthrights, here and now!” And that's what Esau did. 34Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_text:
Abaraham toone
1Abaraham daa ma swo kaane wodwoŋi, o yere na ye Ketura to. 2Wonto de ma lo bia: Zimiran, de Jokisan, de Medan, de Midian, de Isibaka, dedaane Sua. 3Jokisan déem mo ye Seba de Dedan kwo. Dedan dwi dem mo ye Asuri tiina bam, de Letusi tiina bam, de Leyum tiina bam. 4Midian de bu-baara bam mo tento: Efa, de Efere, de Hanoki, de Abida, de Elida. Banto maama déem ye Ketura dwi mo.
5Abaraham ma kwei o na jege woŋo kolo maama to o tiŋi o pa Izaak. 6Ko daare o ka-bi sem bia bam mo o le pɛɛra o pa-ba ye o daa ta ŋwe. O ma daare o pwɛ-ba o pa se ba yɔɔre ba vo wɛ-puli seeni ye ba daare o bu Izaak.
7Abaraham bena yam maama déem yi bi dedaane fuserepɛ-yanu (175), 8ye o laam ba o te. O nɛ momwɛ-dɛɛre mo ye o laam ba o te o kokweero maŋa ne. 9O bia Izaak dedaane Isameli ma kwei‑o ba suli Machapela peo-bɔɔne dem ne, de na bwola de Mamere to. Tega kam déem ya ye Hiti tu Zohare bu Eforon nyem mo, 10ye Abaraham yeigi-ka Hiti tiina bam tei ne. Ba déem ke‑o mɛ ba na suli Sarah to mo. 11Abaraham toone dem kwaga ne, mo Wɛ swɛ Izaak swolim. Ka maŋa ne o déem zoore Beeri Lahayi Royi jei sem ne mo.
Isameli dwi dem taane
12Isameli de o dwi dem yera taane mo tento. Sarah ka-nyaane Hagara na ye Ejipti tu to de Abaraham mo loge Isameli. 13Isameli bu-baara bam yera mo tento, ya popone ya maŋe de ba lora kam na ye tei to mo: Nebayofa mo déem ye o bu-kwea, ko woli de Kedare, de Adibeeli, de Mibisam, 14de Misima, de Duma, de Massa, 15de Hadad, de Tema, de Jetura, de Nafisi dedaane Kedema. 16Isameli bia fuga-balei bam mo konto. Ba dedoa dedoa déem ma ji ba dwi tiina nabaaro. Mo ba yera yam mo konto, nɔɔno maama, de o nawuuri, de o teo.
17Isameli bena yam maama yi bi dedaane fintɔ-yarepɛ (137) ye o laam ba o te. 18O dwi dem ma vo ba jeini tega kalo na zege Havila de Sura tetare laŋa ne to. Jei sem konto yɔɔre ko wo Ejipti siseini ni ne se ko taa vei Asiria seeni to mo. Maŋa maama ba déem jege nankɔɔre mo ba ke de ba chorro tem.
Jakob dedaane Esawu taane
19Abaraham bu Izaak de o dwi dem yera taane mo tento. Abaraham déem mo ye Izaak kwo. 20Izaak déem jege bena finna mo ye o di Bɛtuweli bukɔ Rebeka o ma ke o kaane. Bɛtuweli maa ye Aram tu ye o zoore Mesopotamia ne. Rebeka maa ye Laban nakɔ.
21Rebeka déem na ye kadega to, Izaak ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o kaane wom lo bu. Baŋa Wɛ ma sɛ o wɛ-lworo kom, ye o kaane Rebeka ja puga. 22Bia bam ma yigi daane o puga kam ne. O déem maa we, “Bɛŋwaane mo ko ye tento amo yera yam ne?” Ko ma pa se o vo Baŋa Wɛ yiga o bwei‑o se o lɔre ko kuri. 23Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
“Dwia yalei mo wo nmo puga kam wone.
Nmo wó lo dwi dwi kuni belei,
ye ba wó ba ba pwɛ chwei.
Dwi dedoa wó taa damma de dwoi dedwoŋi dem,
zembaaro wom mo wó taa toŋe o pa o nyaane wom.”
24Maŋa kam ma yi se o lo. O déem ma seene o lo yeywa, bakeiri yerane. 25Wolo na dɛ yiga se o nwoŋi pwooni to maa ye nasoŋo, ye o yera yam maama ye koro yerane. Ko ma pa se ba bwoŋi wonto yere we ‘Esawu’. 26Konto kwaga ne mo o nyaane wom de saŋe o nwoŋi pwooni, ye o jeŋa sɔ Esawu nakila. Ko ma pa se ba pa wonto yere we ‘Jakob’. Izaak déem jege bena fuseredo mo ye Rebeka lo-ba.
27Bia bam déem ma ba ba ke nɔɔna. Esawu ma ji tɔɔno wolo na tiini o wae o tɔɔna. O maa yeini o swoi se o taa wo pwooni ne maŋa maama. Jakob déem maa ye nɔn-cheno. O maa swoi se o taa wo sɔŋɔ ne maŋa maama. 28Izaak déem maa swoi Esawu, Esawu na jaane kago-vara nɔna yam o tui o pa‑o to ŋwaane. Rebeka de déem maa swoi Jakob.
29Dɛ dedwe mo Jakob wora o saŋe o wodiu. Esawu ma zege gaao ne o jwoori sɔŋɔ ye kana tiini ka chɛ‑o. 30O ma ta de Jakob o we, “Ke lela n wɔɔre n dwoa-nasoŋo kom konto n pa-ne se a di! Kokuri, a wora a toa mo de kana!” Dwoa bam na seene to ŋwaane mo ba déem bwoi‑o we ‘Edom’.
31Jakob ma leiri we, “Nam sɛ se n da yiga n yeigi n nakwe nyɔɔre dem n pa-ne, se n laam daare.” 32Esawu ma leiri we, “Nii ywo, amo laam gɛ fee mo se a te! Bɛ lam mo nakwe nyɔɔre dem wó taa jega se de nam pa amo?” 33Jakob ma leiri we, “Nam du amo yiga ne se n daare.” O de ma du duuri o pa‑o, ye o yeigi o nakwe nyɔɔre dem o pa Jakob.
34Jakob laam ma kwei bworobworo dedaane dwoa o pa Esawu. O ma di ye o daare o nyɔ. O laam ma zaŋe wɛɛne o maa kɛa. Ko déem tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo ye Esawu nii o nakwe nyɔɔre dem o gwooni-de to.

english_text:
Isaac and Abimelech
1Once during Abraham's lifetime, the fields had not produced enough grain, and now the same thing happened. So Isaac went to King Abimelech of the Philistines in the land of Gerar, 2because the Lord had appeared to Isaac and said:
Isaac, stay away from Egypt! I will show you where I want you to go. 3 You will live there as a foreigner, but I will be with you and bless you. I will keep my promise to your father Abraham by giving this land to you and your descendants.
4I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth, 5because Abraham did everything I told him to do.
6Isaac moved to Gerar 7 with his beautiful wife Rebekah. He was afraid that someone might kill him to get her, and so he told everyone that Rebekah was his sister. 8After Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah. 9Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?”
“Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
10“Don't you know what you've done?” Abimelech exclaimed. “If someone had slept with her, you would have made our whole nation guilty!” 11Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
12Isaac planted grain and had a good harvest that same year. The Lord blessed him, 13and Isaac was so successful that he became very rich. 14In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned, 15and they stopped up the wells that Abraham's servants had dug before his death. 16Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
17Isaac left and settled in Gerar Valley, 18where he cleaned out those wells that the Philistines had stopped up. Isaac also gave each of the wells the same name that Abraham had given to them. 19While his servants were digging in the valley, they found a spring-fed well. 20But the shepherds of Gerar Valley quarreled with Isaac's shepherds and claimed the water belonged to them. So this well was named “Quarrel,” because they had quarreled with Isaac.
21Isaac's servants dug another well, and the shepherds also quarreled about it. So that well was named “Jealous.” 22Finally, they dug one more well. There was no quarreling this time, and the well was named “Lots of Room,” because the Lord had given them room and would make them very successful.
23Isaac went on to Beersheba, 24where the Lord appeared to him that night and told him, “Don't be afraid! I am the God who was worshiped by your father Abraham, my servant. I will be with you and bless you, and because of Abraham I will give you many descendants.” 25Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the Lord. Then he set up camp, and his servants started digging a well.
26 Meanwhile, Abimelech had left Gerar and was taking his advisor Ahuzzath and his army commander Phicol to see Isaac. 27When they arrived, Isaac asked, “Why are you here? Didn't you send me away because you hated me?”
28They answered, “We now know for certain that the Lord is with you, and we have decided there needs to be a peace treaty between you and us. So let's make a solemn agreement 29not to harm each other. Remember, we have never hurt you, and when we sent you away, we let you go in peace. The Lord has truly blessed you.”
30Isaac gave a big feast for them, and everyone ate and drank. 31Early the next morning Isaac and the others made a solemn agreement, then he let them go in peace.
32Later that same day Isaac's servants came and said, “We've struck water!” 33So Isaac named the well Shibah, and the town is still called Beersheba.
Esau's Foreign Wives
34When Esau was 40 years old, he married Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite. 35But these two women brought a lot of grief to Esau's parents Isaac and Rebekah.
translation_text:
Izaak dedaane Abimeleka taane
1Maŋa kadwoŋi ne kana déem daa ma jwoori ka ba tega baŋa, nenɛɛne ka na maŋe ka ke ye Abaraham ta ŋwe to. Izaak ma zaŋe o vo Filisi tiina pɛ Abimeleka tei Gerare ne. 2Baŋa Wɛ ma ba Izaak tei o we, “Yé zaŋe n vo Ejipti teo kom. Nam ta‑n zoore jei sem ne mɛ amo na wó bere‑m to. 3Maŋe n jeini teo konto ne. Amo wó taa wo nmo tei ne ye a swɛ nmo swolim. Amo wó kwei tega kanto maama a pa nmo de n dwi dem ye a daare a pa se duuri delo a na pwooli de nmo kwo Abaraham to seene de ji chega. 4Amo wó pa se nmo dwi dem puli dedɛ de taa daga nenɛɛne wɛyuu chalechwe sem na daga tei to, ye a pa ba taa tei tega kanto maama. Ko nam ta wó tɔge nmo dwi dem baŋa ne mo se logo baŋa teene dem maama na zaane ba de yuu ne, 5Ko maa ye Abaraham na sɛ amo ni to ŋwaane mo. O sɛ amo ni-kaana yam, de a chullu tem, de chwo-laaro telo a na bere‑o to.”
6Izaak ma seene o vo o zoore Gerare ne. 7Rebeka na tiini o lamma to ŋwaane, Izaak déem kɔre we teo kom nɔɔna wó ja‑o ba go mo o kaane wom ŋwaane. Ba ná bwei o bwia, o maa tɛ we, Rebeka ye o nakɔ mo. O déem kɔre mo se o ta we, o ye o kaane.
8Izaak na zo da o dáane fee to, mo pɛ Abimeleka tɔge o sɔŋɔ takworo ne o na Izaak na wora o di bwoŋa dedaane o kaane Rebeka. 9Abimeleka na nɛ konto to, o laam ma bwoŋi Izaak ye o we, “O seene o ye nmo kaane mo! Ko laam nam ke tɛ mo ye nmo ta n we, o ye n nakɔ mo?” Izaak ma leiri we, “A kɔre we ba wó go-ne a kaane wom ŋwaane mo.” 10Abimeleka laam maa we, “Bɛ mo ye nmo ke debam konto? Baara bam dedoa ya wó wane o peini de n kaane wom, ye konto ya wó pa chaveera ja debam.”
11Abimeleka laam ma pa kwora yi o nɔɔna bam maama we, “Wolo maama na wó bɛɛse nɔɔno wonto naa o kaane wom to, toone mo wó taa ye kotu ŋweero.”
12Izaak déem ma du wo-dwa tega kam baŋa ne. Bene dem konto ne o ma na wodiiru dedɛ, kuni bi, Baŋa Wɛ na swɛ o swolim to ŋwaane. 13O déem ma duni. O duum dem maa tiini de pula, pa se o ji dedɛɛro kamunu. 14O jejegero tem daga te gaale, te maa ye peeni de bone de naane de tontoŋena dedɛ. Filisi tiina bam déem ma zwe kazwe ded‑o. 15Ko ma pa se ba kwei teero ba ma suuri vola yalo maama Abaraham tontoŋena bam déem na koga ye o ta ŋwe to.
16Abimeleka ma ta de Izaak we, “Nwoŋi n viiri, se nmo laam tiini n damma n dwoi debam.” 17Izaak ma fɔɔre o kɛ o vo o pu o vwei Gerare bwolo kom ne ye o zoore da. 18Izaak déem ma jwoori o gwaare vola yam Filisi tiina bam na suuri o kwo Abaraham toone kwaga ne to. O ta ma jwoori o pa-ya yera yalo o kwo déem na mɛ o bwoŋi-ya to.
19Izaak tontoŋena bam déem ma ko vole dedwoŋi bwolo kom ne ba yi na-ŋona. 20Gerare tiina nayera laam ma mage ni-kantɔgɔ de Izaak nayera bam ba we, “Vole dem na bam ye debam nyem mo!” Izaak ma pa vole dem yere we ‘Eseke’, ba na mage ni-kantɔgɔ de baŋa ne to ŋwaane. 21Ba daa ta ma ko vole dedwoŋi, ye ba ta mage ni-kantɔgɔ dento de baŋa ne. O ma pa vole dem konto yere we ‘Sitina’.
22Izaak ma zaŋe o fɔɔre dáane o vo o ko vole dedem, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa wo ke jara dento baŋa ne. O ma pa de yere we ‘Rehobofa’, ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ laam pɛ debam pwola se dé jeini de yazura, ye debam wó yerege tega kam baŋa ne.”
23Izaak ma zaŋe dáane o jwoori o vo o yi Beeriseba. 24O na yi da to, tete dem konto ne Baŋa Wɛ ma ba o tei ne ye o we, “Amo mo ye nmo kwo Abaraham Wɛ wom. Yé ta‑n kɔre foone, se amo wo nmo tei ne. Amo wó swɛ nmo swolim. A nam ta wó pa se n dwi dem kɔgɔ puli, amo tontoŋeno Abaraham ŋwaane.” 25Izaak maa tigisi kandwa o lɔ bimbini dáane ye o bwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ yere o zuli‑o. O ma pu o vwei jei sem konto ne, ye o tontoŋena bam de ko vole.
26Ba na wora konto to, Pɛ Abimeleka zege Gerare ne o ba o tei, wonto de o nakwe Ahuzafa dedaane o jar-keira bam yiga tu Fikola. 27Ba na tu to, Izaak ma bwei-ba o we, “Abam daa maa á beene amo tei se á ke bɛ mo? Ko dae abam déem mo chuli amo, ye á daare á zeili-ne á tei ne na?” 28Ba ma leiri we, “Debam maane we Baŋa Wɛ seene o wo nmo tei ne. Dé laam maa we, ko jege se dé du duuri mo se dé ke ni-mɔrɔ daane. Sɛ se debam ke ni-sɛɛm de nmo 29se nmo yé ke debam lwarem. Debam déem ke nmo lanyerane mo, se ko dae lwarem kɔtaa, ye dé daare dé bane‑m dé pa se n viiri dedaane yazura. Nmo laam maa n ye wolo Baŋa Wɛ na yɔɔre o swɛ nmo swolim to.”
30Izaak ma sɛ ye o ke kuri o pa-ba. Ba ma di wodi-fɔrɔ ba daare ba nyɔ. 31Tega na poore to, zezeŋa ne nɔɔna bam ma du duuri ba ke ni-sɛɛm daane. Izaak ma bane-ba o yage chwoŋa ne, ye ba de viiri de yazura.
32Dento dɛ dem ne Izaak tontoŋena bam ma ba o tei ba ta ded‑o vole delo ba ya na koge to taane. Ba maa we, “Dé koge dé yi na jei sem ne!” 33O ma bwoŋi vole dem konto we, Siba, ye dedaane zem maama teo kom konto yere mo ye Beeriseba.
34Izaak bu Esawu na yi bena finna to mo o di Hiti tiina bukwa balei o ma o ke o kaana. Dedoa déem ye Beeri bukɔ Judif mo, ye wodwoŋi wom ye Elon bukɔ Basemafa. 35Banto déem tiini ba ja wo-chechɔgɔ mo ba ba ba pa Izaak de Rebeka.

english_text:
Isaac Blesses Jacob
1Isaac was old and almost blind, when he called in his first-born son Esau, who asked him, “Father, what can I do for you?”
2Isaac replied, “I am old and might die at any time. 3So go hunting with your bow and arrows and kill a wild animal. 4Cook some of that tasty food that I love so much and bring it to me. I want to eat it once more and give you my blessing before I die.”
5Rebekah had been listening, and as soon as Esau left to go hunting, 6she said to Jacob, “I heard your father tell Esau 7to kill a wild animal and cook some tasty food for him before he dies. Your father said this because he wants to bless your brother with the Lord as his witness. 8Now, my son, listen carefully to what I want you to do. 9Go and kill two of your best young goats and bring them to me. I'll cook the tasty food that your father loves so much. 10Then you can take it to him, so he can eat it and give you his blessing before he dies.”
11“My brother Esau is a hairy man,” Jacob reminded her. “And I am not. 12If my father touches me and realizes I am trying to trick him, he will put a curse on me instead of giving me a blessing.”
13Rebekah insisted, “Let his curse fall on me! Just do what I say and bring me the meat.” 14So Jacob brought the meat to his mother, and she cooked the tasty food that his father liked. 15Then she took Esau's best clothes and put them on Jacob. 16She also covered the smooth part of his hands and neck with goatskins 17and gave him some bread and the tasty food she had cooked.
18Jacob went to his father and said, “Father, here I am.”
“Which one of my sons are you?” his father asked.
19Jacob replied, “I am Esau, your first-born, and I have done what you told me. Please sit up and eat the meat I have brought. Then you can give me your blessing.”
20Isaac asked, “My son, how did you find an animal so quickly?”
“The Lord your God was kind to me,” Jacob answered.
21“My son,” Isaac said, “come closer, where I can touch you and find out if you really are Esau.” 22Jacob went closer. His father touched him and said, “You sound like Jacob, but your hands feel hairy like Esau's.” 23And so Isaac blessed Jacob, thinking he was Esau.
24Isaac asked, “Are you really my son Esau?”
“Yes, I am,” Jacob answered.
25So Isaac told him, “Serve me the wild meat, and I can give you my blessing.”
Jacob gave him some meat, and he ate it. He also gave him some wine, and he drank it. 26Then Isaac said, “Son, come over here and kiss me.” 27 While Jacob was kissing him, Isaac caught the smell of his clothes and said:
“The smell of my son
is like a field
the Lord has blessed.
28God will bless you, my son,
with dew from heaven
and with fertile fields,
rich with grain and grapes.
29 Nations will be your servants
and bow down to you.
You will rule over your brothers,
and they will kneel
at your feet.
Anyone who curses you
will be cursed;
anyone who blesses you
will be blessed.”
30Right after Isaac had given Jacob his blessing and Jacob had gone, Esau came back from hunting. 31He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
32“Who are you?” Isaac asked.
“I am Esau, your first-born son.”
33Isaac started trembling and said, “Then who brought me some wild meat right before you came in? I ate it and gave him a blessing that cannot be taken back.”
34Esau cried out in great distress, “Father, give me a blessing too!”
35Isaac answered, “Your brother tricked me and stole your blessing.”
36 Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
37“My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
38 “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
39 So his father said:
“Your home will be far
from that fertile land,
where dew comes down
from the heavens.
40 You will live by the power
of your sword
and be your brother's slave.
But when you decide to be free,
you will break loose.”
41Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
42 When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you. 43Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran 44and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry 45and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
46Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_text:
Jakob jwoŋi Izaak swolim dem
1Izaak déem ma kwe ye o yia yam dwei. O déem ma bwoŋi o bu-kwea Esawu ye o laam ta ded‑o we, “Amo bu.” O de ma leiri we, “Nii-ne da.” 2Izaak maa we, “Amo laam ye nɔn-kwea mo ye a yeiri amo toone dɛ. 3Konto to, kwei n taŋa kam de ka chena, se n vo gaao n tɔɔne n go kago-varem n pa-ne. 4Laam kwei varem wom n ma n ke wodiu na ywomma ne a na yeini a lage tetei to, se n daare n ja n ba n pa-ne se a di. Nmo ná ke konto, a laam wó kwei Wɛ zaane a ma swɛ nmo swolim, se a daare a te.”
5Izaak déem na wora o ŋɔɔne de Esawu konto to, Rebeka ya zege o cheigi mo. Esawu na zaŋe o nwoŋi o kɛ gaao se o go varem to, 6Rebeka ma ta de Jakob we, “Nii ywo, amo nigi nmo kwo na tage de n zembaaro we, 7‘Véi n go kago-varem n ja n ba n saŋe wodi-laao n pa-ne se a di, se a laam kwei Baŋa Wɛ zaane a ma swɛ n swolim, se a laam daare a te.’ 8A bu, fɔge n cheigi, se n daare n ke kolo maama a na wó bere‑m to. 9Zo vara bam wone n le bebale selei n ja n ba n pa-ne. Amo laam wó ma-te a ma saŋe n kwo wodiu, se ko taa ywomma ne o na swoi-ko tei to. 10Se n laam ja n zo n pa n kwo se o di. Konto wó pa se o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage n yuu ne, ye o laam daare o te.”
11Jakob ma ta de o nu Rebeka we, “Nmo yei we amo zembaaro Esawu ye nɔn-kogo mo, ye amo ye nɔn-siswola. 12Amo kwo ná taane amo o nii, ko wó taa nye nenɛɛne amo wora a gane‑o mo, ye amo ya na beeri se o sɔɔle lam o yage a yuu ne to, a laam wó jwoori a ja lwarem mo a ba a pa a tete.” 13O nu wom maa we, “Amo bu, yage se sɔɔlem dwi maama ba amo baŋa ne. Nmo za n ke amo na we n ke tei to. Véi n ja bone dem n ba n pa-ne.”
14O ma seene o vo o ja-de o ba o pa o nu, ye o de saŋe wodiu kolo na ywomma to, nenɛɛne o kwo wom na lage wodiu kom tei to. 15Rebeka laam ma kwei o bu-kwea Esawu gare-laaro na wo o tei ne to, o zo o bu-balaŋa Jakob. 16O daa ta ma kwei bone dem tankwallo tem o ma o kwoli Jakob je sem dedaane o ba dem mɛ na ye siswolo to. 17O laam ma kwei wodi-ywoŋo kom, de bworobworo kom o na ke to o pa o bu Jakob.
18Jakob ma vo o kwo tei ye o we, “A kwo.” O de ma leiri we, “Amo bu wɔ mo konto?” 19Jakob ma leiri o kwo we, “Amo ye nmo bu-kwea Esawu mo. Amo nam ke nenɛɛne nmo na tage tei de amo to mo. Konto to, zaŋe n jeini n di amo wodiu kom, se n laam daare n sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n yage amo yuu ne.” 20Izaak ma bwei‑o we, “Amo bu, n ke tetɛ mo n na-ko lela tento?” O ma leiri we, “Nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo woli-ne konto.” 21Izaak laam ma ta de Jakob we, “Amo bu, nam fɔɔre n yi amo yera, se a taane‑m a nii nmo seene n ye amo bu-kwea Esawu mo naa n dae.” 22Jakob ma fɔɔre o yi o kwo Izaak tei. O ma taane‑o o nii ye o we, “Kwora kam ye Jakob kwora mo, ye jea yam laam ye Esawu jea.” 23O maa wo lɔre‑o, kokuri o je sem déem jege koro yerane mo, ne Esawu je sem na ye tetei to. O laam ma sɛ se o kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ o bu wom swolim. 24O daa ma bwei‑o we, “Konto to, nmo seene n ye amo bu-kwea Esawu mo na?” O ma leiri we, “Ɛɛ.”
25Izaak laam ma ta we, “Ja n kago-varem nɔna yam n ba n pa-ne se a di, se a laam daare a kwei a swolim dem a pa‑m.” Jakob ma ja o yi o tei o pa‑o ye o di. O ta ma pa‑o sana ye o nyɔ. 26O kwo Izaak laam ma ta ded‑o we, “Amo bu, fɔɔre n yi ywo, se n kukwori-ne.” 27O de ma yi o tei o kukwori‑o. Izaak ma ni o gwaaro tem lwom, ye o daare o o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o we, “Nii mo! Amo bu wom lwom dem nye nenɛɛne pwola kalo Baŋa Wɛ na ke zaane o yage ka baŋa ne to lwom mo.
28Konto ŋwaane, Wɛ wó pa se nyɔnɔ nwoŋi wɛyuu
ko pa se nmo tega kam fɔge ka ke wodiiru dedɛ,
se n mena de n sa-doora gaale.
29Wɛ wó pa se dwi-gɛ tiina taa toŋe ba pae nmo
ye nɔɔna tiiri nmo yiga ne ba pa‑m zula.
Wɛ wó pa se n ta‑n ye n chorro tem yuu tu,
ye nmo nu-bia bam maama wó tiiri nmo yiga ne ba pa‑m zula.
Balo na sɔɔle lwarem ba yage nmo baŋa ne to
de wó jwoori ba na sɔɔlem konto dwoŋi ba baŋa ne.
Balo nam na sɔɔle lam ba yage n yuu ne to
de wó jwoori ba na zaane.”
Esawu lwoori zaane o kwo tei ne
30Izaak na yɔɔre o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o pa Jakob o ti ye Jakob nwoŋi pwooni o daare o kwo wom to, mo o zembaaro Esawu yɔɔre o zege gaao ne o yi. 31Wonto de ma ke wodi-ywoŋo o ja o zo o kwo tei ne. Esawu laam ma ta o kwo we, “A kwo, zaŋe n jeini se n di a kago-varem nɔna yam, se n daare n sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n yage amo yuu ne.” 32O kwo Izaak ma bwei‑o we, “Nmo ye wɔ mo?” O ma leiri we, “Amo ye nmo bu-kwea Esawu mo.” 33Izaak ma ni ye ko sɔɔre o yera pa se ya tiini ya sae. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Se wɔ nam mo jaane kago-varem wom o zo ywo o pa amo to? Amo yɔɔre a di a ti mo konto ye nmo ma n zoore to, ye a maŋe a sɔɔle Wɛ swolim a pa wonto. Wonto nam wó seene o na Wɛ zaane dem konto mo!”
34Esawu na nigi o kwo taane dem konto to, o ma tiini o laare wɛ-wɛ ye o chwoosa o kwo wom tei ne we, “A kwo, a lwoori‑m! Sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n pa amo de!” 35O ma leiri‑o we, “Nmo nyaane wom zo amo tei mo o gane-ne o ma jwoŋi Wɛ swolim delo ya na ye nmo nyem to.”
36Esawu maa we, “O yere na ye Jakob to seene ko ye chega mo! O gane amo tento o ke kuni belei mo. O maŋe o ŋɔ amo bu-kwea nyɔɔre dem, ye leile konto o daa vere Wɛ swolim delo ya na ye a nyem to o woli da!” O laam daa ma bwei o kwo we, “Konto, n daa ta jege Wɛ swolim se n kwei n pa-ne na?” 37Izaak ma leiri Esawu we, “Amo maŋe a pa se wonto ji nmo yuu tu ye a ta pa se o nu-bia maama taa ye wonto kabɛ. A nam ta kwei wodi-fɔrɔ dedaane sa-doora a pa‑o. Konto to, amo bu, bɛ daa mo wó daare se a kwei a pa‑m?”
38Esawu ma fɔge o ta de o kwo o we, “Amo kwo, nmo bere n wo daare Wɛ swolim dedwoŋi na? Nam sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n yage amo de yuu ne! A kwo! A kwo!” Esawu ma to keira ne baŋa baŋa.
39O kwo Izaak ma leiri we:
“Nmo zoorem jei bá taa ye tega kalo na ke wodiiru dedɛ.
Tega kam ta bá na wɛyuu nyɔnɔ kom.
40Nmo wó ta‑n ke jara mo n zoora.
Nmo wó ta‑n toŋe n pae n nyaane wom ne kabaa tei.
Ko laam nam ná zo nmo yera,
nmo wó vere n tete wonto dam kuri ne.”
41Esawu na nigi konto to, o ma done Jakob, ba kwo na kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ wonto swolim to ŋwaane. O ma ta o tete ne we, “Debam kwo bá dáane ye o te. O lua kam ni ná ti, amo laam wó go a nyaane Jakob.”
42Rebeka déem ma ni o bu-kwea Esawu na boŋe tei to. O ma toŋe o bwoŋi o bu-balaŋa Jakob ye o ta ded‑o we, “Nmo zembaaro wom boŋe se o go‑m mo se ko pa o bane zuri. 43Konto to, ke tetei amo na wó bere‑m to: Duri n vo amo nabɔ Laban tei Haran ne. 44Ta‑n zoore wonto sɔŋɔ ne se ko taa nii maŋa kalo nmo zembaaro wom bane dem na wó zuri to. 45O bane dem ná seene de zuri ye o swei nmo na toŋe kolo o yera ne to, amo laam wó pa ni se nmo zege dáane n jwoori ywo. Bɛŋwaane mo amo wó yɔɔre a ga abam balei dɛ dedwe wone?”
46Rebeka laam ma ta de Izaak o we, “Amo yera laam chɛ mo de Hiti bukwa banto Esawu na di to. Jakob de nam daa ná lage o di Hiti tiina bukɔ jei sento ne, amo toone bere de wó taa gare a ŋwea.”

english_text:
Isaac's Instructions to Jacob
1Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said:
Don't marry any of those Canaanite women. 2Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother. 3I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation. 4 May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
5Isaac then sent Jacob to stay with Rebekah's brother Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean.
Esau Marries the Daughter of Ishmael
6Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria 7and that he had obeyed his father and mother. 8Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women. 9So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham.
Jacob's Dream at Bethel
10 Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran. 11At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock. 12 In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
13 The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said:
I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping. 14 Your descendants will spread over the earth in all directions and will become as numerous as the specks of dust. Your family will be a blessing to all people. 15Wherever you go, I will watch over you, then later I will bring you back to this land. I won't leave you—I will do all I have promised.
16Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.” 17Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
18When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God, 19and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
20Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes 21and bring me safely home again, you will be my God. 22This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_text:
1Rebeka déem na tage konto to, Izaak ma toŋe o bwoŋi Jakob. O ma ta ded‑o o we, “Wɛ taa wo nmo tei ne. Yé zaŋe n di Kanaan tiina bukɔ n ma n ke kaane. 2Zaŋe n vo Mesopotamia leile konto, n nu wom kwo Bɛtuweli sɔŋɔ ne, se n di kaane dáane, nmo nu nabɔ Laban bukwa bam wone. 3Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom wó swɛ nmo swolim ye o pa se á ja dwi á daare á puli dedɛ se á ji nɔn-kɔgɔ. 4Wɛ wó swɛ nmo de n dwi maama swolim, nenɛɛne o na maŋe o ke o pa n nabaaro Abaraham tei to mo, se á wane á jwoŋi tega kanto á na zoore da nenɛɛne veira tei to á ta‑á tei, nenɛɛne o na pɛ Abaraham tei to.” 5Izaak ma bane Jakob o yage chwoŋa ne, ye o de ma kɛ Mesopotamia. O déem ma vo o zoore Aram tu Bɛtuweli bu Laban tei ne. Wonto déem ye Jakob de Esawu nu Rebeka nabɔ mo.
Esawu di kaane wodwoŋi
6Esawu ma ni Izaak na ke tei o kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ Jakob swolim ye o toŋe‑o se o vo Mesopotamia o beeri kaane dáane to. O ta ma ni o na pɛ Jakob ni we, o yé di kaane Kanaan tiina bukwa bam wone. 7O ma ni Jakob na sɛ ba kwo dedaane ba nu ni tei ye o seene o vo Mesopotamia to. 8Esawu laam ma lɔre we Kanaan tiina bukwa bam o na di o ma o ke o kaana to wo su o kwo Izaak yi kɔtaa. 9Ko ma pa se o vo o kwo zembaaro Isameli tei o di Mahalafa. Wonto ye Nebayofa nakɔ ye o ta ye Abaraham bu Isameli bukɔ. O ma di‑o o woli kaana balo o na maŋe o jege to wone.
Jakob dwɛ dendwɛ Bɛtel ne
10Jakob déem ma nwoŋi Beeriseba ne o laam maa vei Haran. 11Tega na wora ka yi, ye o yi jei sedwoŋi to mo o maŋe dáane se o peini se tega poore. O déem ma kwei kandwɛ dedoa na wo jei sem konto ne to o yeiri o yuu, ye o tigi o dɔa. 12O ma dwɛ dendwɛ o na nateini de kuri seeni na wo tega ne ye de yuu kom seeni yi Wɛ telaao ne to. Wɛ malese sem laam maa dɔɔle de baŋa ne se diini ye se tu tega ne. 13Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ba o zege da ye o we, “Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, nmo kwo Abaraham Wɛ wom, dedaane Izaak Wɛ wom. Ko ná ye tega kalo baŋa ne nmo laam na tigi tento to, amo wó kwei-ka a pa nmo de n dwi dem. 14Amo wó pa se n dwi dem taa daga dedɛ nenɛɛne tega baŋa kasol-bia na ye tei to mo. Abam wó puli ye á daare á jage á yi logo baŋa jei maama ne, wɛ-zoore seeni dedaane wɛ-puli seeni, se á daare á yi baŋa seeni dedaane tega-kuri seeni. Logo kom baŋa dwi tiina bam maama wó da nmo de n dwi dem baŋa ne mo se ba de na zaane amo tei ne. 15Nii! Amo wó taa wo nmo tei ne ye a taa nii nmo baŋa ne mɛ maama nmo na wó vo to. Amo wó ja‑m a jwoori a ba se n jeini tega kanto baŋa ne. Amo bá fɔge a yage nmo kɔtaa. Amo nam wó seene a ke amo na pwooli se a ke kolo a pa nmo to.”
16Jakob laam ma zaŋe dɔɔm wone. O ma boŋe we, “Baŋa Wɛ seene o wo jei sento ne mo ye amo ya wo lɔre ko ni ne.” 17Foone ma ja‑o ye o we, “Nii jei sento na jege foone tei! Ywo-seeni dae jei yɔɔ yerane, ko ye Wɛ sɔŋɔ kom mo. Mo Wɛ telaao manchwo-peena yam mo tento.”
18Tega na poore zezeŋa ne to, Jakob ma kwei kandwɛ delo o na mɛ o yeiri o yuu kom to, o cheili-de wɛɛne nenɛɛne ywei dwoŋi ye o laam lwo nuga de baŋa ne. 19O ma bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we ‘Bɛtel’, ye ba déem ya bwoi teo kom konto we ‘Luzi’ mo.
20Jakob laam ma du duuri de Baŋa Wɛ we, “Nenɛɛne nmo ná wó taa wo amo tei ne ye n nii amo baŋa ne a chwoŋa kanto maama yuu ne, ye n ná wó pa-ne wodiu se a di dedaane gwaaro se a zo, 21ye amo laam ba a jwoori a kwo sɔŋɔ de yazura, nmo Baŋa Wɛ wó taa ye amo Wɛ. 22Amo wó daare a kwei kandwɛ dento a na chwi nenɛɛne ywei dwoŋi to mo se de taa ye nmo Wɛ sɔŋɔ kom. Woŋo kolo maama nmo na ke amo jeŋa ne to, amo wó le popɔra dedoa wonnu fuga maama wone a pa‑m.”

english_text:
Jacob Arrives at Laban's Home
1As Jacob continued on his way to the east, 2he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock. 3Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
4Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?”
“We're from Haran,” they answered.
5Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?”
“Yes we do,” they replied.
6“How is he?” Jacob asked.
“He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
7Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
8But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
9While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep. 10When Jacob saw her and his uncle's sheep, he rolled the rock away and watered the sheep. 11He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy. 12He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
13As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened. 14Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.”
Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel
After Jacob had been there for a month, 15Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
