Ba maama laam nam tu a tei mo ywo-seeni.’ 32A ta wó pa se o lɔre we á ye nayere-dwi mo, ye á nam jaane á peeni, de á bone, de á naane dedaane á woŋo maama mo á woli da á ba ywo. 33Pɛ wom wó bwoŋi abam se á zo o tei. O ná bwei abam we ‘Abam toŋe bɛ totoŋa mo?’, 34se á fɔge á leiri‑o we ‘Ko na zege debam biini ne to, dé maŋe dé tɔge vara mo. Debam kwoa de déem nam mo maŋe ba ye nayera.’ Konto wó pa se o pa abam pwola se á jeini Gosen laŋa kam ne.” Josɛf déem tage konto kolo ŋwaane Ejipti tiina chuli balo na yere pei to mo.

english_text:
1-2Joseph took five of his brothers to the king and told him, “My father and my brothers have come from Canaan. They have brought their sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else they own to the region of Goshen.”
Then he introduced his brothers to the king, 3who asked them, “What do you do for a living?”
“Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep. 4But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
5The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived. 6I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
7Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing, 8and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
9Jacob answered, “I have lived only 130 years, and I have had to move from place to place. My parents and my grandparents also had to move from place to place. But they lived much longer, and their life was not as hard as mine.” 10Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left. 11Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses. 12Joseph also provided food for their families.
A Famine in Egypt
13The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly. 14So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury. 15But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
16“If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.” 17From then on, they brought him their horses and donkeys and their sheep and goats in exchange for grain.
Within a year Joseph had collected every animal in Egypt. 18Then the people came to him and said:
Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land. 19Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
20The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king 21and made everyone the king's slaves, 22except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land. 23Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant, 24but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
25“Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.” 26Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land.
Jacob Becomes an Old Man
27The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families. 28Jacob himself lived there for 17 years, before dying at the age of 147. 29 When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt. 30Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.”
“I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
31“Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked.
“Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_text:
1Josɛf ma vo o ta de Pa-faro wom o we, “Amo kwo de a chorro jaane ba peeni, de ba bone, de ba naane dedaane ba wonnu maama mo ba ba ywo. Leile konto, ba tu se ba jeini Gosen laŋa kam ne mo.” 2O ta ma kuri o chorro tem wone tenu o ja o zo Pa-faro wom tei se ba ware‑o.
3Pɛ wom ma bwei Josɛf chorro tem o we, “Abam toŋe bɛ totoŋa mo?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Dé ye nayera mo, nenɛɛne debam kwoa bam déem na toŋe totoŋe delo to.” 4Ba déem ta ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Dé tu ywo se dé taa zoore logo konto ne maŋa fenfee mo. Kokuri to, kana kam tiini ka chɛ Kanaan teo kom ne mo, ye dé vara bam daa ba nae gaaro se ba taa di. Konto mo dé to n pwoa ne se, n ná sɛ, se dé taa zoore Gosen laŋa kam ne.”
5Pa-faro wom ma ta de Josɛf o we, “Nmo kwo de n chorro tem tu nmo tei mo. 6Ejipti teo kom ni maama wo n jeŋa ne. Pa se ba jeini tega kam mɛ maama na lamma to. Pa-ba pwola se ba taa zoore Gosen ne. Nmo ma ná maane we ba wolo tiini o yei vara kɔnɔ lanyerane, se n kwei amo tete naane dem n ke kotu jeŋa ne se o taa nii-de o pa-ne.”
7Josɛf laam ma ja o kwo Jakob o zo se o ware Pɛ wom. Jakob déem ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o ke Pa-faro wom yuu ne. Konto na ti to, 8Pɛ wom ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo jege bena yagera mo?” 9Jakob déem ma leiri Pɛ wom o we, “Amo bena a na mɛ a beeri logo baŋa ne to ye bi de fintɔ mo. Bena yam konto nam ba daga ye ya su de cham. Amo bena yam bá twɛ a kwoa déem na mɛ bena yalo ba beeri logo baŋa ne to.” 10Jakob daa ta ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage Pa-faro wom yuu ne ye o laam nwoŋi da o tei ne.
11Josɛf déem ke Pa-faro wom na bere‑o se o ke tei to mo. O ma pa o kwo de o chorro tem jeiŋa jei Ejipti ne se ba taa zoore da. Tega kalo o déem na pɛ-ba to laam jigi ba tete nyem mo ye ka lamma ka dwoi Ejipti tega kam maama. Jei sem konto déem bwola de Ramesesa teo kom na wo Gosen laŋa kam ne to mo. 12Josɛf déem mo ta jege o kwo, de o chorro tem, de ba kwaga kam maama ni-wodiu. Nɔn-kwe de bu-somwa maama déem di wonto jeŋa ne mo.
Josɛf de kana maŋa kam taane
13Wodiu déem tere logo kom maama jei jei ne. Kana kam déem chɛ Ejipti ne dedaane Kanaan ne ye nɔɔna bam maama déem wora ba kwaare ba jei de kana. 14Nɔɔna maama déem maa tui Josɛf tei ba yeigi mena. O de déem ma la sabu kom o ja o vo Pa-faro wom sɔŋɔ. 15Ejipti tiina bam de Kanaan tiina bam ma di ba sabia ba ti ye kana ta wora. Ejipti tiina maama ma vo Josɛf tei ba we, “Pa debam wodiu, se dé yé pu de kana ye n ta zege da! Dé sabu maama ti.”
16Josɛf déem ma ta-ba o we, “Nam ja-na á vara á ba á pa-ne. Abam sabu ná seene ko ti, amo wó yeigi wodiu a pa abam se á vara bam leiri sabu yuu ne.” 17Ba ma ja ba vara bam ba vo Josɛf tei, ye o de pa-ba wodiu o ma o leini ba sisei yuu ne, de ba pei de ba bone yuu ne. O déem ta pɛ-ba wodiu ba naane de ba bonɛ ŋwaane mo. Dento bene dem ne o déem mɛ wodiu kom o leini ba vara bam maama.
18Bene dedwoŋi daa ma yi. Ejipti tiina déem ma vo Josɛf tei ba we, “Debam tu, dé bá wane dé seigi chega kam nmo yiga ne. Debam sabu ti, dé vara maama maa wo nmo jeŋa ne. Kolo yerane laam na daare to mo ye dé kare sem dedaane dé tete yera yam. 19Nam kwaane n woli debam. Ko ná dae konto, dé wó jei mo dedaane dé tega kam maama. Yeigi debam dedaane dé kare sem se n pa debam wodiu. Debam wó ji Pa-faro wom kabɛ ye o ta wó taa tei dé tega kam de, nenɛɛne n ná pɛ debam wodiu se dé jwoŋi dé tete, de wo-dwa se dé tega kam de bá taa tigi kafɛ.”
20Josɛf déem ma yeigi Ejipti tega kam maama pa se ka ji Pa-faro wom nyem. Kana kam na tiini ka chɛ to, Ejipti tiina bam maama déem maa jege ba kare ba yeigi konto. Pa-faro wom ma ba o taa tei tega kam maama. 21Josɛf déem ma pa se nɔɔna bam ji kabɛ mo, ko zege Ejipti daa dedoa ne se ko yi kakam daa ne. 22Ko nam ná ye Ejipti kaanem tiina bam, o déem wo yeigi banto tega, kolo ŋwaane Pa-faro wom déem mo pɔɔre o wodiiru o pae banto se ko yi ba ni. Konto ŋwaane ba déem ba jege se ba kwei ba tega ba yeigi ba pa Josɛf.
23Josɛf ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Á wo nɛ na? Abam dedaane á tega kam maama laam jigi Pa-faro wom nyem mo. Nam jwoŋi-na wo-dwa á vo á du á kare sem ne. 24Wodiu zagem maŋa ne, se á pɔɔre wodiiru tem kuni benu. Á wó kwei popɔra dedoa á ba á pa Pɛ mo, ye á daare popɔra yana á jege á ma á ke á wo-dwa dedaane á ni-wodiu se ko pa abam de á diga tiina.” 25Nɔɔna bam déem ma leiri ba we, “Dé tu, nmo jwoŋi debam mo n yage. Nmo na tiini n ke debam lanyerane konto to, dé wó taa ye Pɛ wom kabɛ.”
26Josɛf déem ma lɛɛre o pa ni se de taa toŋe Ejipti tega maama baŋa ne. De nam wora mo de zem tento. Ko zege mo we wodiiru zagem maŋa ne, se nɔɔna maama pɔɔre-te kuni benu. Popɔra dedoa maa wó taa ye Pa-faro wom nyem. Kaanem tiina bam tega yerane mo déem tɔge ka dae Pɛ wom nyem.
Jakob twɛ se o te
27Isarele tiina bam ma lɛɛre ba zoore Ejipti ne. Ba déem wo Gosen laŋa kam ne mo. Dáane mo ba déem tiini ba duni ye ba dwi ta puli dedɛ.
28Jakob déem jeini Ejipti ne bena fuga-yarepɛ (17) mo. O ŋwea déem jaane bena bi dedaane finna-yarepɛ (147) mo. 29O déem tu o maane we ko daa bá dáane se o te. O ma bwoŋi o bu Josɛf o ta‑o we, “Nenɛɛne nmo yi ná su de amo, se n kwei n jeŋa n ke amo chwei kuri ne se n du duuri. Pwooli n pa-ne we nmo wó duri amo ŋwaŋa se n bere n chega de amo. Sɛ we, a ná tega, n bá‑n ke-ne Ejipti ne. 30Amo ná maa vei a kwoa tei, a lage se á ja-ne mo á nwoŋi Ejipti ne. Á laam maa wó ja-ne á vo á suli mɛ ba déem na suli amo kwoa bam to.” Josɛf ma leiri o we, “Amo wó ke nmo na we a ke tei to.”
31Jakob ma ta‑o se o fɔge o du duuri se o ke konto. Josɛf ma seene o du duuri dem o pa‑o. Jakob ma guni o peini o peiga jei ne ye o ke Wɛ lei.

english_text:
Jacob Blesses Joseph's Two Sons
1Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim. 2When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
3 Jacob told Joseph:
God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing 4and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
5Then Jacob went on to say:
Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine. 6Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh. 7 Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
8-10Jacob was very old and almost blind. He did not recognize the two boys, and so he asked Joseph, “Who are these boys?”
Joseph answered, “They are my sons. God has given them to me here in Egypt.”
“Bring them to me,” Jacob said. “I want to give them my blessing.” Joseph brought the boys to him, and he hugged and kissed them.
11Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.” 12Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
13After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right. 14But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh. 15Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said:
My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life, 16and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
17Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh. 18Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
19But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
20 Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh. 21After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago. 22Meanwhile, I'm giving you the hillside I captured from the Amorites.”
translation_text:
1Ko déem daa wo dáane ye ba ta de Josɛf ba we, “N kwo weele mo.” Josɛf ma ja o bu-baara Manasɛ de Efrayim, o woli da o vo se o daane o kwo jaweo kom. 2Ba na yi da to, mo nɔɔno tage de Jakob o we, “N bu Josɛf tu se o daane n peiga.” Jakob déem ma ke o tete o ke daane o zaŋe o peiga jei ne o jeini. 3O ma ta de Josɛf o we:
“Amo na wo Kanaan teo Luzi ne to, Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom déem veere o tete de amo. O déem ma swɛ amo swolim dáane. 4Wɛ ma daare o ta de amo o we, ‘Amo wó pa se n dwi puli se n na kɔgɔ dedɛ, ye nmo bia ji teene dedɛ. Amo ta wó daare a kwei tega kanto a pa‑m se n de n dwi dem taa tei-ka taa wuu.’
5Tɔ, amo bu, amo nam lage se n ta‑n yei we, n bia balei bam n na loge Ejipti ne ye a déem ta wo tu ywo to wó ji amo bia mo. Efrayim de Manasɛ laam ye amo bia mo, nenɛɛne Ruben de Simeon na maŋe ba ye amo bia tei to. 6Nmo daa‑n ná loge bia badwonna, se ba laam taa ye n tete bia. Ko nam ye Efrayim de Manasɛ yera baŋa ne mo ba de wó jwoŋi ba tega kam popɔra. 7Amo déem na zege Mesopotamia ne a maa jwoori to, a wo déem tiini ko chɔge de n nu Racheli na tege Kanaan teo kom ne to ŋwaane mo. Dé na wo chwoŋa ne dé vei to, o tega ye ba suli‑o chwoŋa kam yuu ne mo, ko bwola de Eferata.” (Eferata ye Bɛtelehem mo).
8Jakob déem ma na Josɛf bu-baara balei bam ye o bwei o we, “Banto ye bera mo?” 9Josɛf ma leiri o kwo we, “Ba ye bia balo Wɛ na pɛ amo ywo to mo.” Jakob ma ta o we, “Pa se ba yi a yera se a sɔɔle Wɛ swolim a ke ba yuu ne.” 10Jakob déem nam tiini o kwe mo, ye o yia déem wora ya dwia. Josɛf ma ja o bia bam o yi o yera. O kwo déem ma kukwori-ba lanyerane. 11Jakob ma ta de Josɛf o we, “Amo déem daa maŋe a ba teene se a na nmo tete yibia. Nam nii! Wɛ laam pɛ se a na n bia bam de a woli da.”
12Josɛf déem ma pa se o bia bam fɔɔre dáa o kwo nɛ baŋa ne. O tete ma tiiri o kwo yiga ne ye o chɔɔle o yibia tega ne. 13Josɛf ma pa se o bia bam zege Jakob sɛ sem ne. Efrayim wo Jakob jagwia ne ye Manasɛ maa wo o jazem ne. 14Jakob déem ma gare o jazem dem o daŋe Efrayim yuu ne, ye wonto mo ye nyaane wom. O ma daare o kwei o jagwia kam o daŋe Manasɛ yuu ne. Wonto nam mo ye bu-kwea kam. 15O ma daare o kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ Josɛf swolim ye o we:
“Wɛ wó ke zaane o ke bia banto yuu ne.
O ye Wɛ wolo amo kwoa Abaraham de Izaak déem na sɛ ba pa‑o to mo.
Wɛ wom konto mo nii amo baŋa ne ne nayero tei
a ŋwea maama wone se ko yi zem.
16Amo cham dwi maama wone,
o maleka kam mo yeini o le-ne de wone.
Wɛ wom konto wó swɛ bakeiri sem swolim.
Wɛ wó pa se nɔɔna taa tɔge bia banto baŋa ne ba guli amo yere,
ko woli de amo kwoa Abaraham de Izaak yera yam.
Wɛ wó pa se ba dwi puli dedɛ logo baŋa ne.”
17Josɛf na nɛ we o kwo jazem dem daŋe Efrayim yuu ne to, mo ko tiini ko daane‑o. O déem ma kwaane se o dɔne o kwo jazem dem Efrayim yuu ne, se o ja o vo o daŋe Manasɛ yuu ne. 18Josɛf ma ta de o kwo we, “A kwo, wonto mo ye bu-kwea kam. Nam kwei n jazem n daŋe wonto yuu ne.” 19O kwo wom ma ve ye o we, “Amo bu, a yei ko ni ne. Wonto dé wó seene o ji nɔn-kɔgɔ. O nyaane wom nam wó taa daga o dwoi‑o, ye o dwi dem mo wó ji teene dedɛ.”
20Dento dɛ dem ne Jakob ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o ke ba yuu ne ye o we, “Isarele tiina ná yeini ba kwei Wɛ zaane ba ma swɛ wolo maama swolim, ba wó taa tɔge á yera yam ŋwaane ye ba we, ‘Wɛ wó pa se n ta‑n ye nenɛɛne Efrayim dedaane Manasɛ na ye tei to.’ ” Ko ke konto mo ye o pa se Efrayim kɛ Manasɛ yiga.
21Jakob déem ma ta de Josɛf o we, “Ko laam yi amo toone. Wɛ nam wó taa wora abam tei ne se o ja abam o jwoori á nabaara tega kam se á ta‑á jei da. 22Ko nam ná ye nmo tete, n dwoi n chorro tem maama. A kwei peero laŋa kalo a na mɛ a se-zɔɔ dedaane a taŋa a vere-ka Amori tiina bam tei ne to mo a pa‑m.”

english_text:
Jacob Blesses His Sons
1Jacob called his sons together and said:
My sons, I am Jacob,
your father Israel.
2Come, gather around,
as I tell your future.
3Reuben, you are my oldest,
born at the peak of my powers;
you were an honored leader.
4Uncontrollable as a flood,
you slept with my wife
and disgraced my bed.
And so you no longer deserve
the place of honor.
5Simeon and Levi,
you are brothers,
each a gruesome sword.
6I never want to take part
in your plans or deeds.
You slaughtered people
in your anger,
and you crippled cattle
for no reason.
7Now I place a curse on you
because of
your fierce anger.
Your descendants
will be scattered
among the tribes of Israel.
8Judah, you will be praised
by your brothers;
they will bow down to you,
as you defeat your enemies.
9 My son, you are a lion
ready to eat your victim!
You are terribly fierce;
no one will bother you.
10You will have power and rule
until nations obey you
and come bringing gifts.
11You will tie your donkey
to a choice grapevine
and wash your clothes
in wine from those grapes.
12Your eyes are darker than wine,
your teeth whiter than milk.
13Zebulun, you will settle
along the seashore
and provide safe harbors
as far north as Sidon.
14Issachar, you are a strong donkey
resting in the meadows.
15You found them so pleasant
that you worked too hard
and became a slave.
16Dan, you are the tribe
that will bring justice
to Israel.
17You are a snake that bites
the heel of a horse,
making its rider fall.
18Our Lord, I am waiting
for you to save us.
19Gad, you will be attacked,
then attack your attackers.
20Asher, you will eat food
fancy enough for a king.
21Naphtali, you are a wild deer
with lovely fawns.
22Joseph, you are a fruitful vine
growing near a stream
and climbing a wall.
23Enemies attacked with arrows,
refusing to show mercy.
24But you stood your ground,
swiftly shooting back
with the help of Jacob's God,
the All-Powerful One—
his name is the Shepherd,
Israel's mighty rock.
25Your help came from the God
your father worshiped,
from God All-Powerful.
God will bless you with rain
and streams from the earth;
he will bless you
with many descendants.
26My son, the blessings I give
are better than the promise
of ancient mountains
or eternal hills.
Joseph, I pray these blessings
will come to you,
because you are the leader
of your brothers.
27Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf,
destroying your enemies
morning and evening.
28These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings.
Jacob's Death
29-31 Jacob told his sons:
Soon I will die, and I want you to bury me in Machpelah Cave. Abraham bought this cave as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite, and it is near the town of Mamre in Canaan. Abraham and Sarah are buried there, and so are Isaac and Rebekah. I buried Leah there too. 32Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
33 When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_text:
Jakob swɛ o bia bam swolim
1Jakob déem ma bwoŋi o bu-baara bam ye o ta-ba o we, “La-na daane amo yiga ne se a maŋe a bere abam kolo jwa na wó ke á yera ne to.
2Jakob bia bam, nam jeeri-na, se á cheigi.
Cheigi-na á kwo Isarele taane dem.
3Ruben, nmo mo ye amo bu-kwea.
N maa n ye a nɔn-doŋo jana bu, ye n bere amo dam.
Nmo dam de n zula tiini ya gaale nɔɔna maama.
4Nmo nam nye nenɛɛne na na chuuri tei to mo,
n ba zege jeiga dedoa.
Konto to, nmo bá‑n kɛ yiga.
Nmo zo n kwo sara wone n chɔge-ka,
n na peini de amo kaane wodwoŋi to ŋwaane.
5Simeon de Levi ye chorro mo.
Ba se-zɔɔro tem jaane vuvuga mo te tui.
6Amo ba lage ba jeiŋa jei kɔtaa!
Dé bá jeeri daane se dé bane bana,
kokuri to, ba tɔge ban-zɔŋɔ baŋa ne ba go nɔɔna
ba daare ba pa se nabɛ gwarege yɔɔ yɔɔ.
7Amo sɔɔle lwarem a yage ba ban-lom dem baŋa ne,
ba na tiini ba ke lɛɛro to ŋwaane.
Ba tiini ba jege puseŋa dedɛ.
A lage a jage ba dwi dem a yage tega kam maama baŋa ne mo,
se ba gwaane de Isarele dwi tiina bam maama.
8Judah, nmo chorro tem wó tei‑m.
N jeŋa wó taa wo n dona bakala ne se n wane-ba.
Nmo kwo bia wó ba ba chɔɔle tega ne ba zuli‑m.
9Amo bu Judah, n nye de nywoŋ-pɔla mo,
N nye de nywoŋ-kana na zi ka wodiu
ye ka laam vwɛ ka jwoori ka vo
ka tigi chemm ka tiga jei ne to mo.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba lage se o daane‑m.
10Judah wó taa zei paare nacheiga kam mo.
O dwi dem nam wó taa di paare mo taa wuu.
Dwi-gɛ tiina wó ja wonnu ba ba ba pa‑o
ye ba chɔɔle ba yibia tega ne ba zuli‑o.
11Wonto yeini o jaane o bonaga o vei o lei tio yera ne,
de ko tio-bia na maŋe ba lamma tei to de.
O kwei tio-bia nyoa mo o ma zare o gwaaro tem.
12O yia laam wó taa seena lanyerane,
nenɛɛne sa-sona balo o na nyɔa to.
O yeila maa wó taa tiini ya peera
ne nayela tei.
13Zebulun wó taa zoore naneo ni ne mo,
nabwooru wó taa tui te zege jei sem konto ne.
O laŋa kam de wó yale ka vo ka yi Sidon jei sem.
14Isakara nye de bonaga mo na tiini ka damma
ye ka tigi ka zela ywollu telei tetare ne ka sii to mo.
15Wonto nɛ we o zoorem jei sem lamma,
dedaane o tega kam maama.
Konto ŋwaane o laam ma sɛ se o zeŋe zela yam
ye o daare o sɛ totoŋ-chɛɛra ne kabaa tei.
16Dan mo wó taa tei o nɔɔna de chega.
O dwi dem wó jeini Isarele tiina bam wone.
17Dan nam wó taa nye de basankwea mo,
ka na tigi chwoŋa ni ne to.
Ka maa wó zaŋe ka done siseiŋa nakila
se ka pa diru wom yale o to o kwaga tetare ne.
18 Baŋa Wɛ, amo cheigi nmo mo se n jwoŋi-ne n yage!
19Ko ná ye Gad, venverena mo wó kwaane se ba vere‑o.
Wonto nam wó pipiri o zeili-ba pa se ba viiri.
20Asere tega kam wó taa ke wodi-laaro dedɛ.
O wó taa jege wodiu kolo na maŋe de pɛ dim to.
21Nafitali nye de feira kalo ba na yage se ka taa vei zɛɛra to mo.
Ka maa lore bu-laaro.
22Josɛf nye de tio kolo na leiri bia dedɛ to mo.
Ko maa zega ko bwola de buga,
ye ko nɛ sem yɔɔre se dɔɔle se ma diini kabira baŋa.
23O dona bam ma ta ba chena de yi-seena
se ba chiŋi‑o ba ja.
24O tete taŋa kam nam yɔɔre ka zege mo chekke.
O je sem maa dana se o taa tae o chena.
Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Jakob dwi tiina Dam maama Tu wom to
mo wó pa Josɛf dam.
Wonto nii o nɔɔna baŋa ne, ne nayero tei mo.
O maa ye Isarele tiina dalem jei, ne peo mo tei.
25Nmo kwo Wɛ wom, wonto mo wó woli‑m.
Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom mo wó swɛ nmo swolim.
Wonto wó pa se doa nwoŋi wɛyuu ka taa nena.
Na de wó buri tega kuri ne.
Wɛ wó pa se n na dwi dedɛ,
ye n vara de taa daga.
26Nmo kwo na sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage n yuu ne tei to
dwoi wo-laaro telo na wo faŋa faŋa peero tem ne to.
Wɛ wó pa se nmo Josɛf na wodiiru de wo-laaro ko ja gaale.
O wó ke zaane o ke nmo yuu ne,
nmo wolo na ye pa-bu nmo chorro tem maama yiga ne to.
27Benjamin nye de wiiru na jaane vara ko tore to mo.
Zezeŋa maama o yeini o di o na jaane kolo to mo.
Se dedaan-ni ná yia,
o daa pɔɔre kolo maama na daare to.”
28Isarele dwia fuga-yalei yam mo konto, dedaane ba kwo déem na tage tei o ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o ke ba yuu ne to. O kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ ba swolim se ko maŋe de ba dedoa dedoa na ye tei to mo.
Jakob toone
29Jakob déem laam ma pa o bia bam kwora kanto ye o we, “Ko laam gɛ fee se amo de te se a vo a nabaara bam tei. Amo ná tega, kwei-na amo á ke peo-bɔɔne delo ne ba déem na ke amo kwoa bam da to. Tega kam déem ya ye Hiti tu Eforon nyem mo. 30Peo-bɔɔne dem konto wo Machapela pwola kam ne mo, ye de bwola de Kanaan teo Mamere. Abaraham déem yeigi-de Eforon tei ne mo, se o taa ke o nɔɔna de wone. 31Dáane mo ba déem suli Abaraham de o kaane Sarah. Ba ma daare ba suli Izaak de o kaane Rebeka de wone. Amo de déem suli a kaane Leah da. 32Abaraham déem nam yeigi bɔɔne dem dedaane pwola kam maama mo Hiti tiina bam tei ne.”
33Jakob déem ma bere o bia bam ba na wó ke tei maama to o ti. O laam ma guni o peini o peiga jei ne, ye o te.

english_text:
1Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
2Joseph gave orders for Jacob's body to be embalmed, 3and it took the usual 40 days.
The Egyptians mourned 70 days for Jacob. 4When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me. 5 Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
6The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
7-9When Joseph left Goshen with his brothers, his relatives, and his father's relatives to bury Jacob, many of the king's highest officials and even his military chariots and cavalry went along. The Israelites left behind only their children, their cattle, and their sheep and goats.
10After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob. 11The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
12So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed. 13 They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
14After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt.
Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
15After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
16So they sent this message to Joseph:
Before our father died, 17he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.”
Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped.
When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
18Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
19But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided. 20You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing. 21Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better.
Joseph's Death
22Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of 110. 23Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family. 24Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. 25 Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
26So Joseph died in Egypt at the age of 110; his body was embalmed and put in a coffin.
translation_text:
1Josɛf déem na maane we o kwo tege to, o ma pare o to o baŋa ne, o maa jege‑o o kukwora ye o keeri lanyerane. 2Josɛf déem ta pɛ ni mo se o tontoŋena kwei terale nuga ba ma turi o kwo yera yam ba kwɛ ba tiŋi se ba laam di o lua. Ba ma seene ba kwɛ‑o ba tiŋi. 3Ba déem mɛ da finna mo ba kwɛ‑o, ne ko na yeini ko ke tei to. Ejipti tiina bam déem ma keeri‑o da fuserepɛ.
4Ba keira maŋa kam na ti to, mo Josɛf déem tage Pa-faro wom nakwa bam o we, “Nenɛɛne abam yi ná su de amo, se á kwei-na kwora kanto á vo á ta de Pa-faro wom we, 5‘A kwo na lage o te to, o pɛ se a du duuri a pa‑o we, a jege se a ke‑o yibeeli delo o na kwɛ o tiŋi o tete ŋwaane Kanaan teo kom ne to mo. Konto to, pa-ne pwola se a vo dáane a suli a kwo wom se a laam jwoori.’ ” 6Pa-faro wom na nigi to, o maa we, “Véi n suli n kwo wom, se ko tɔge o na pɛ se n du we n wó ke tei to.”
7Josɛf déem ma ja o kwo wom o vo se o suli. Pa-faro wom nakwa bam maama déem tɔge‑o mo ba vo. Dedɛɛra balo maama na wo Pɛ sɔŋɔ ne to dedaane Ejipti teo kom dedɛɛra bam maama de déem wora. 8Josɛf diga tiina de o chorro tem dedaane o kwo sɔŋɔ tiina maama déem dɛ‑o mo ba vo se ba suli o kwo wom. Balo yerane na daare Gosen ne to maa ye bu-balɛ sem, dedaane peeni, de bone, ko woli de naane mo. 9Jar-keira de ma tɔge ba vo, ba badwonna jei sisei-torokooro wone ye badwonna de dɔge sisei baŋa ne ba maa via. Ko déem tiini ko ye kɔ-fɔrɔ mo.
10Ba ma vo ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ye ba daare ba yi jeiga kalo Atade na fere o mena da to. Ba ma zege da ba mɔ nagoro wɛɛne. Josɛf ma maŋe da da yarepɛ o keeri o kwo wom ye o di lua kam. 11Kanaan tiina balo na zoore jei sem konto ne to na nɛ ba keira kam Atade jeiga kam ne to, ba maa we, “Ejipti tiina banto na jeeri ywo to wo mo tiini ko chɔge ye ba keeri dedɛ.” Ba déem maa jege jeiga kam ba bwoi we ‘Abel-Mizarim’. Jeiga kam konto maa ye Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ dedem dem seeni.
12Jakob bia bam déem ma ke ba kwo na pɛ-ba ni se ba ke tei to. 13Ba déem zeŋe o yera mo ba vo ba suli Kanaan ne. Ko nam ye peo-bɔɔne dem na wo Machapela pwola kam ne to mo ba déem suli‑o. De bwola de Mamere mo, ye Abaraham yeigi-de Hiti tu Eforon tei ne se o taa ke o nɔɔna de wone. 14Ba déem na ke o kwo wom ba ti to, Josɛf laam ma jwoori Ejipti, wonto de o chorro tem, ko woli de balo maama na dɛ ba vo Jakob lua kam to.
Josɛf jwoori o pa o chorro tem na baare
15Josɛf chorro tem na maane we ba kwo daa tera to, ba ma ke ni daane ba we, “Dé déem na tiini dé ke lwarem dé pa Josɛf to, dɛ delo o bane ta wo debam baŋa ne, ye o boŋe se o jwoori o ŋwe jene dé yera ne.” 16Ba déem ma toŋe kwora ba pa Josɛf ba we, “Nmo kwo daama yage ni dento mo ye o laam daare o te, 17ye o we dé ta taane dento de nmo we ‘A lwoori‑m se n kwei n chorro tem wɛleere de ba na ke wo-lɔŋɔ kolo ba pa se ko yi‑m to n yage n ma n chɛ-ba.’ Debam ye n kwo wom Wɛ tontoŋena mo. Dé lwoori‑m se n kwei lwarem delo dé na ke‑m to n yage n ma n chɛ debam.” Ba kwora kam na to Josɛf zwɛ ne to, o ma ka yi-na.
18O chorro tem de laam ma vo o tei. Ba ma tiiri tega ne o yiga ne ye ba we, “Debam laam ye nmo kabɛ mo.” 19Josɛf déem ma ta-ba o we, “Yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. Amo bá wane a leiri Wɛ yuu ne. 20Abam déem ya boŋe se á ke amo mo lwarem. Wɛ ma pipiri á boboŋe dem pa se de ke lam. Kolo na seene ko ke to ya ná wo ke, nɔɔna dedɛ ŋwea zem ya jei mo. 21Konto ŋwaane, yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. Amo wó taa nii abam de á bia baŋa ne se á na wodiu á di.” O déem ta ŋɔɔne wo-laaro de o chorro tem mo pa se ba jwoori ba na baare.
Josɛf toone
22Josɛf de o kwo sɔŋɔ tiina bam ma lɛɛre ba maŋe Ejipti ne. O bena maama déem maa ye bena bi de fuga (110). 23O déem nɛ Efrayim bia se ko yi dwia yatɔ laŋa ne. Manasɛ bu Makira de bia déem ta jeini Josɛf nɛ baŋa ne ba lora maŋa ne.
24Josɛf déem ma ta de o chorro tem o we, “Ko laam yi amo toone. Wɛ nam mo wó zeini abam. O wó ja abam o ja nwoŋi logo konto ne, ye o daare o ja abam o jwoori á nabaara tega kam se á ta‑á jei da. Tega kam konto o ya seene o yia o du duuri mo se o kwei-ka o pa Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob.” 25Josɛf déem ma pa se Jakob bia bam du duuri ba pa‑o ye o we, “Wɛ wó seene o ba o woli abam se á yage ywo. Abam nam ná maa viira, se á kwei amo kwi sem á woli da á ja kɛ.”
26Josɛf déem jege bena bi de fuga (110) mo ye o te. Ba ma kwei terale nuga ba ma turi o yera yam ba kwɛ ba tiŋi. Ba na ke konto ba ti to, ba déem kwei‑o ba ke dakaa ne mo ba zege Ejipti teo kom ne.

english_text:
The People of Israel Suffer
1-5 When Jacob went to Egypt, his son Joseph was already there. So Jacob took his eleven other sons and their families. They were: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Benjamin, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. Altogether, Jacob had 70 children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren who went with him.
6After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died, 7 the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
8 Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt, 9and he told the Egyptians:
There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are. 10 If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
11The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies. 12But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before 13and made them work so hard 14that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
15Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth. 16He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
17But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to. 18The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
19They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.” 20-21God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own.
The Hebrews kept increasing 22 until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_text:
1Jakob bu-baara balo na tɔge ded‑o ba vo ba zoore Ejipti ne to yera mo tento. Nɔɔno maama de o diga tiina déem mo dɛ ba vo.
2Ruben, de Simeon, de Levi, de Judah.
3Isakara, de Zebulun, de Benjamin.
4Dan, de Nafitali; Gad, de Asere.
5O bu Josɛf déem maŋe o wo Ejipti ne mo. Jakob dwi dem maama déem ye fuserepɛ mo. 6Josɛf de o chorro tem maama dedaane banto yuudwoŋo kom maama ma ba ba te. 7Isarele dwi tiina bam déem nam ta puli mo dedɛ ye ba kɔgɔ daga ko gaale. Ba ma tiini ba ke dam ye teo kom maama su de ba dwi dem yerane.
8Pa-dooro de déem ma jwoŋi Ejipti o tei. Wonto maa yeiri Josɛf ni ne. 9Pɛ wom ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Nii-na Isarele tiina banto na puli dedɛ tei ye ba jege dam ba dwoi debam. 10Pa-na se dé ke swa dé che ba pulim dem, se ko ná dae konto, jara ná to debam dedaane teo kodwoŋi tetare ne, ba wó woli debam dona bam wone ba ke jara dedaane debam ye ba laam duri ba lu debam teo kom ne.”
11Konto ŋwaane Ejipti tiina ma kuri totoŋa yuu tiina se ba taa bɛɛse-ba de totoŋ-dɛɛra. Ba ma pa se Isarele tiina bam lɔ Pitom teo dedaane Ramesesa teo se Ejipti Pɛ wom taa zege o wodiiru da. 12Ba nam na yeini ba tiini ba bɛɛse-ba tei to mo Isarele tiina bam laam fɔge ba pula dedɛ ye ba jage jei maama. Ko ma pa se Ejipti tiina bam tiini ba kɔre foone de Isarele tiina bam. 13Ejipti tiina bam ma pa ko chɛ Isarele tiina bam yera ye ba tiini ba bɛɛse-ba de totoŋa. 14Ba ma pa se ba ŋwea ke cham dedaane bira magem de teero totoŋ-dɛɛra. Ba déem ta fe-ba se ba taa toŋa ba kare de ba kadwi ne. Konto to Ejipti tiina bam déem bɛɛse Isarele tiina bam ye ba ba jege ba ŋwaŋa.
15Kaana balei déem maa wora balo na yeini ba zeini Hiburu kapwi se ba lo bia to. Ba dedoa yere mo Sifira. Wodwoŋi wom de yere maa ye Pua. Ejipti Pɛ wom ma ta de-ba o we, 16“Á ná yeini á woli Hiburu kaana bam se ba lo, ye ba ná loga, se á fɔge á nii. Bu wom ná ye bakeira, se á go‑o. O daa ná ye busankana, se á yage‑o.” 17Kaana balei bam maa kɔre Wɛ, ye ba wo sɛ Ejipti Pɛ wom ni. Ba maa pae se bakeiri sem wora.
18Pɛ wom ma bwoŋi kaana bam ye o bwei-ba o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo á ke konto ye á pae se bakeiri sem ta ŋwe?” 19Ba ma leiri ba we, “Pɛ. Hiburu kaana bam dae nenɛɛne Ejipti kaana bam tei. Banto wara mo. Ba ma yeini ba gare ba lo ba ti mo ye debam laam yi ba tei.” 20Konto ŋwaane Wɛ ma ke kaana balei bam lanyerane. Isarele tiina bam déem puli mo ye ba kɔgɔ tiini ko gaale. 21Kaana balei bam na kɔre Wɛ to ŋwaane, o ma pa ba de lo bia.
22Pa-faro wom laam ma pa o nɔɔna bam maama ni dento we, “Hiburu tiina ná loge bakeira maama, á jege se á dole‑o mo á de Naili buga kam ne. Ko daare ko ná ye busankana, se á yage‑o se o ta ŋwe.”

english_text:
Moses Is Born
1A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe, 2 and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months. 3But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River. 4The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
5About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water. 6When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
7At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
8“Yes,” the king's daughter answered.
So the girl brought the baby's mother, 9and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.”
The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him. 10 And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.”
Moses Escapes from Egypt
11 After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them. 12Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
13When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
14The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?”
This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened. 15 When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian.
One day, when Moses was sitting by a well, 16the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats. 17Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals. 18When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
19They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
20“Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
21Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses. 22And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
23After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help, 24 and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, 25and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_text:
Moses lora taane
1Levi dwi tu dedoa déem ma di o tete dwi tiina bukɔ wodwoŋi o ma ke o kaane. 2Kaane wom ma ja puga o lo bakeira. O ma na we bu wom lamma. O ma da ko ŋwaane o seigi‑o chane setɔ. 3O laam ma maane we o daa bá wane o seigi‑o. O ma kwei tetɔgɔ ba na mɛ sangɛ ba sɔ-ko to, ye o daare o kwei kɔtaale o ma turi-ko se na yé wane ba zo. O déem ma kwei bu wom o ke ko wone ye o daare o ja‑o o vo Naili buga kam ni o seigi‑o nanchan-gullu wone. 4Bu wom nakɔ déem maa zege da ye o tole o nii kolo na wó ke‑o to.
5Ko na ke fee to, Ejipti Pɛ bukɔ déem ma tu buga kam se o swɛ o yera. O ka-nyaana maa vei ba kaare buga kam ni dem ne. O laam ma tole o na tetɔgɔ kom nanchan-gullu tem wone ye o toŋe o kaba-kana se o vo o ja-ko o ja ba. 6O ma puri ko ni ye o na bu-seseŋa na tigi da ye o keera. Bu wom ŋwaŋa ma zo‑o. O ma ta o we, “Hiburu tiina bu-balwa bam dedoa mo tento.”
7Bu wom nakɔ wom ma vo Pɛ bukɔ wom tei o bwei‑o o we, “A véi a beeri Hiburu tiina kaana bam wone a pa‑m se ba dedoa taa pae bu wom ŋɔge yele na?” 8O ma sɛ ye o we, o véi! Busankana kam ma vo o bwoŋi bu wom nu se o ba. 9Pɛ bukɔ wom ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ja bu wonto n vo sɔŋɔ n ta‑n nii o baŋa ne n pa-ne. Amo wó ŋwe‑m ko ŋwaane.” Kaane wom ma seene o ja bu wom o vo sɔŋɔ, o maa jege‑o o kɔna.
10Bu wom déem na bege fee to, o nu wom ma ja‑o o vo o pa Pɛ bukɔ wom se o kwei‑o o ma ji o tete bu. O déem ma pa bu wom yere we ‘Moses’, ye o we ‘A na liiri‑o na wone to ŋwaane.’
Moses duri o vo Midian
11Moses déem na bege baaro o ti to dɛ dedwe o ma zaŋe o nwoŋi o vo o tete Hiburu tiina bam na zoore mɛ to. O ma nii o na ba yera na chɛ de totoŋ-dɛɛra tei to. O ta ma na Ejipti tu wodwoŋi na jege Hiburu tu dedoa o maga. 12O ma dole o yi o nii jei maama ye o wo nɛ nɔɔn-nɔɔno. O ma mage Ejipti tu wom o go, ye o daare o kwei‑o o seigi kasolo wone.
13Tega na poore to, o daa ma nwoŋi ye o na Hiburu tiina balei na jege daane. O ma bwei wolo na tusi to o we, “Bɛ mo ye nmo jege n dwoŋi Hiburu tu n maga?” 14Nɔɔno wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Wɔ mo pɛ nmo ni se n ta‑n ye dedɛɛro debam baŋa ne, se n bore debam bora? Nmo wó go amo n woli Ejipti tu wom n na go to wone mo na?” Moses na nigi konto to, foone ma zo‑o ye o boŋe o tete ne we, “Chega ŋwaane to, a na ke tei to lɔre jaja mo.”
15Ejipti Pɛ wom déem ma ni kolo na ke to. O ma kwaane se o go Moses. Moses ma duri o lu Pɛ wom jeŋa ne ye o vo o zoore Midian teo ne.
O déem ma vo o jei vole dedwoŋi teiŋa ne. 16O na wora to, Midian tiina kaanem tu wodwoŋi bukwa barepɛ ma ba se ba mɔ na ba lwo gwoŋo kolo vara bam na nyɔ na da to wone ba ma nye ba kwo pei de bone. 17Nayera badwonna déem ma ba ba zeili bukwa bam. Moses ma zaŋe o jwoŋi-ba o yage, ye o daare o nye ba vara bam. 18Ko na ke konto to, busankane sem ma jwoori ba vo ba kwo tei, o yere mo Jetero. O déem ma bwei-ba o we, “Abam zem ke tɛ mo á jwoori konto lela?” 19Ba ma leiri ba we, “Ejipti tu wodwoŋi mo jwoŋi debam o yage nayera bam jeŋa ne. Wonto mo lɛɛre o mɔ na o ma nye vara bam o pa debam.” 20O ma bwei o bukwa bam we, “Nɔɔno wom nam wo yeim mo? Abam yage‑o da se bɛ mo? Bwoŋi-o-na se o ba o di wodiu.”
21Moses déem ma sɛ se o taa zoore nɔɔno wom tei ne. Ko na ke fee to, Jetero ma kwei o bukɔ Zipora o pa Moses se o di o ma ke kaane. 22Zipora ma lo bakeira ye Moses pa o yere we ‘Geresom’. Kokuri to, o déem boŋe o tete ne mo we, “Amo ye veiru mo sa-teo ne.”
23Ko na wora ko wora to, Ejipti Pɛ wom déem ma te. Isarele tiina bam maa ŋwaana ba kabɛɛne ŋwaane. Ba déem tiini ba keeri mo ba lwoori wolim. Ba keira kam ma to Wɛ zwa ne, 24ye o sɛ ba ŋwana yam. O ma guli ni delo o déem na gwoni o pa Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob to gula. 25Wɛ ma nii o na Isarele tiina bam na yaare tei to ye o ke o yiga ba wone.

english_text:
God Speaks to Moses
1One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain. 2 There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up. 3“This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
4When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
5God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy. 6I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
7The Lord said:
I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them, 8and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians.
I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live. 9My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them. 10Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
11But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
12God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
13 Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
14-15 God said to Moses:
I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
16Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt, 17and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
18The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.” 19But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to. 20So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
21 After I punish the Egyptians, they will be so afraid of you that they will give you anything you want. You are my people, and I will let you take many things with you when you leave the land of Egypt. 22Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_text:
1Moses déem lɛɛre o jege o tembaaro Jetero bone dem de o pei sem o nii te baŋa ne mo. Jetero déem maa ye Midian tiina kaanem tu. Dɛ dedwe, Moses ma ja vara bam o kɛ kagoa kam kwaga ne, o vo o yi Sinayi peo. Peo kom konto mo ye Wɛ tete jeiga kam. 2Moses na wora to mo Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam veere ka tete ded‑o ne min-vogo tei to. Moses ma na we mini dem jaane sabara kadwoŋi ye de laam ba di sabara kam de zwɛa. 3Moses ma ta o tete ne we, “Amo wó fɔɔre mo a yi a nii wo-kenkagele dento, se a lɔre bɛ mo ke ye sabara kam ba zwɛa to.”
4 Baŋa Wɛ ma maane we o fɔɔre o yi se o nii. Wɛ ma zege sabara kam wone o bwoŋi‑o o we, “Moses! Moses!” Moses ma leiri we, “Nii-ne da.” 5Wɛ ma ta o we, “Yé tiini n twɛ ywo. Le n natera yam, se mɛ n na zege to ye amo tete nyem mo.” 6O daa ta ma ta o we, “Amo ye nmo kwo Wɛ wom mo. A maa kwori a ye nmo nabaara Wɛ wom: Abaraham Wɛ wom, de Izaak Wɛ wom, dedaane Jakob Wɛ wom mo.” Moses déem na nigi konto to mo o seigi o yibia. O déem kɔre se o nii o na Wɛ.
7 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we, “Chega to, amo maane cham delo na yi a nɔɔna bam Ejipti ne to. Ba totoŋa yiga tiina bam na tiini ba bɛɛse-ba pa se ba keeri tei maama to zo amo zwa. A yiga nam wo ba yaara yam wone. 8Konto ŋwaane, amo laam tu ba tei se a jwoŋi-ba mo a yage Ejipti tiina bam jeŋa ne. Amo ta wó pa se ba zaŋe ba nwoŋi ba vo ba jeini tega kalo na lamma ye ka daga to baŋa ne. Tega kam konto ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ. Ko nam ye tega kalo Kanaan tiina bam, de Hiti tiina bam, de Amori tiina bam, de Pɛrizi tiina bam, de Hivi tiina bam, dedaane Jebusi tiina bam maama na zoore to mo. 9Isarele tiina bam keira kam yi-ne, ye a ta kwori a na Ejipti tiina bam na jege-ba ba bɛɛse tei maama to. 10Konto ŋwaane, a laam nam lage a toŋe nmo mo se n vo Ejipti Pɛ wom tei n ja amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam n nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne.”
11Moses ma ta de Wɛ o we, “Amo ye wɔ mo? A muri se a vo Pa-faro wom tei a ja Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne.” 12Wɛ daa ta ma ta o we, “Amo wó taa wora nmo tei ne. Memaŋe dento mo wó bere we amo mo seene a toŋe‑m: Nmo ná jaane a nɔɔna bam n nwoŋi Ejipti ne, abam laam wó ba peo konto yuu ne mo á zuli-ne.”
13Moses ma leiri o we, “Amo nam ná vei Isarele tiina bam tei ye a ta-ba we ‘Abam nabaara Wɛ wom mo toŋe-ne á tei ne,’ ba wó wane ba bwei amo we ‘Wɛ wom konto yere mo bɛ?’ Tetɛ mo amo wó leiri-ba?”
14Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Amo mo ye a na maŋe a ye wolo to. Ta dedaane Isarele tiina bam we, Amo-maŋe-a-wora-taa-wuu mo toŋe‑m ba tei ne.” 15Wɛ ma daare o ta de Moses o we:
“Ta de Isarele tiina bam we, ‘Taa wuu Tu Baŋa Wɛ na ye á nabaara Wɛ wom to, Abaraham Wɛ wom, de Izaak Wɛ wom, de Jakob Wɛ wom mo toŋe-ne á tei ne.’ Amo yere dem mo konto se ko taa vei wuu. Ko ná zege dwi dedwe ne se ko vo ko yi dwi dedwoŋi ne, yere dem konto mo ba wó taa mae ba guli a gula. 16Nam véi n la Isarele nakwa bam n ke daane se n ta-ba we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye abam nabaara Wɛ wom to, Abaraham Wɛ wom, de Izaak Wɛ wom, de Jakob Wɛ wom mo tu amo tei. O nam tage o we: Amo seene a nii á baŋa ne mo, ye a na kolo maama na yi abam Ejipti ne to. 17Amo nam maŋe a pwooli we a lage a ja abam a nwoŋi á yaara yam wone á na nɛ Ejipti ne to. Amo ta wó pa se á zaŋe á vo tega kalo Kanaan tiina bam na zoore da to, de Hiti tiina bam, de Amori tiina bam, de Pɛrizi tiina bam, de Hivi tiina bam, dedaane Jebusi tiina bam. Tega kam konto ywomma mo de varem de kɔnɔ.’
18Nmo ná tage konto dwoŋi, Isarele nakwa bam wó sɛ n taane dem. Nmo laam jege se n ja-ba se á vo Ejipti pɛ wom tei, ye á ta ded‑o we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Hiburu tiina bam Wɛ to mo tu debam tei. Konto, pa debam pwola se dé ma da yatɔ dé kwei chwoŋa dé vo kagoa kam wone dé ke kaanem dáane dé pa dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ 19Amo nam yei we Pɛ wom bá sɛ o pa abam pwola se á vo, ko ná dae we a mɛ dam mo a fe‑o. 20Amo laam wó ma a dam a waare Ejipti tiina bam dedaane wo-kenkagela yalo a na wó ke ba tetare ne to. Ko kwaga ne mo Pɛ wom laam wó pa abam chwoŋa se á viiri.
21Amo nam ta wó pa se á kikia su Ejipti tiina bam yi. Konto wó pa se á bá gwɛ de je-yaara á viiri. 22Abam kaana maama jege se ba vo ba fara balo na ye Ejipti tiina kaana to tei mo, dedaane kaane wolo maama na zoore ba sɔŋɔ ne to tei. Ba laam maa wó lwoori ba na lu-nyenno wonnu, de sabu-seŋa wonnu, dedaane gwaaro telo á bia na wó taa jege ba zoore to. Abam ná ke konto mo, á wó ma swa á ja Ejipti tiina bam jejegero tem á woli da á viiri.”

english_text:
The Lord Gives Great Power to Moses
1Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
2The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?”
“A walking stick,” Moses replied.
3“Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
4“Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
5“Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
6Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
7“Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
8-9Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
10Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
11But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things? 12Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
13Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
14The Lord became angry with Moses and said:
What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again. 15-16Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do. 17Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles.
Moses Returns to Egypt
18Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.”
“All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
19But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.” 20So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
21On the way the Lord said to Moses:
When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go. 22Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son, 23 and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.”
Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
24One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him. 25But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.” 26So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.”
Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
27The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss. 28Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
29Later they brought together the leaders of Israel, 30and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people, 31and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na wó tɔge Moses baŋa o ke memaŋa yalo to
1Moses déem ma leiri Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Dɛ dedwoŋi ne, Isarele tiina bam bá sɛ a taane dem, ba nam bá pa-ne chega. Ba wó wane ba ta nenɛɛne, nmo seene n wo veere n tete de amo.” 2Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo n zei de n jeŋa?” O ma leiri o we, “Nacheiga mo a zia.” 3Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we, “Dole-ka n de tega ne.” Moses ma dole-ka o de tega ne. Ka ma ji basankwea, ye o duri o daare-ka.
4 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we, “Twe n jeŋa n ja-ka ka nabili seeni.” Moses na twe o jeŋa o ja basankwea kam to, ka ma jwoori ka ji nacheiga o jeŋa ne. 5Baŋa Wɛ laam maa we, “Keim dento wó pa se ba sɛ we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo seene a veere a tete de nmo, amo wolo na ye ba nabaara Wɛ wom to: Abaraham Wɛ wom, de Izaak Wɛ wom, de Jakob Wɛ wom to.”
6 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta‑o o we, “Tore n jeŋa n gɔrɔ kom ne se n dwei n nyɔɔne.” O ma ke konto. Moses na jwoori o le o jeŋa kam to, ka pɔpɔ ka peere mo de naywaane jaweo kom. 7Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta o we, “Daa‑n jwoori n tore n jeŋa kam n gɔrɔ kom ne.” Moses ma kwei o jeŋa o tore o gɔrɔ kom ne. O na jwoori o le-ka to, ka pɔpɔ ka ke lanyerane mo, nenɛɛne o yera yam maama na ye tei to. 8Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta o we, “Ba ná wo pɛ‑m chega de boboa wo-memaŋe dem, ba laam wó sɛ memaŋe belei tu wom. 9De konto de, ba ná nɛ wo-memaŋa yalei yanto ye ba ta ve se ba sɛ n taane dem, se n mɔ na Naili buga kam ne n daare n lwo-ba te-kora kam baŋa ne. Na bam konto wó ji jana tega kam baŋa ne.”
10Moses déem ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Amo Teiru, amo ware a ŋɔɔne chekke. Ko zege nmo de amo na ŋɔɔne daane to, a maŋe a ware mo. A nam maŋe a bá lɔre ŋɔŋa. A ni ware se de pipiri lanyerane.”
11 Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Wɔ mo pɛ nabiinu o ni dem? Wɔ mo ke zwa-kwarro de memaaro? Wɔ mo pae nabiinu yia se o taa nae, naa se o taa ye lilwei? Ko dae amo Baŋa Wɛ mo na? 12Laam nam véi, se amo wó woli‑m de ŋɔŋa, ye a daare a bere‑m n na wó ta kolo maama to.”
13Moses maa we, “Amo Teiru, jan ja! Toŋe nɔn-gaa se konto tu vo o toŋe totoŋe dem.”
14Moses taane dem déem ma zaŋe Baŋa Wɛ bane. Wɛ ma ta‑o o we, “Se nmo zembaaro Aron wolo de na ye Levi tu to, wonto wae o ŋɔɔne lanyerane. Nii ywo! O wo chwoŋa ne o beene se o jeeri‑m. O nam ná nɛ‑m, ko wó pa o wo pwoli dedɛ. 15Nmo wó wane n ŋɔɔne n bere‑o nmo taane dem de o na wó ta kolo to. Amo wó woli abam de ŋɔŋa ye a bere abam á na wó ke tei maama to. 16Aron mo wó lwoni n taane dem o ŋɔɔne de nɔɔna bam, nenɛɛne o ye nmo ni mo tei. Nmo tete wó leiri amo yuu ne n ŋɔɔne ded‑o. 17Nam kwei nacheiga kanto nmo na zei n jeŋa ne to n woli da n vo, se n lage n ma-ka n toŋe wo-kenkagela mo.”
Moses jwoori o vo Ejipti
18Moses déem ma jwoori o tembaaro Jetero tei o ta‑o o we, “Amo boŋe se a jwoori a chorro tem tei mo Ejipti ne, se a nii ba ta ŋwe de yazura na.” Jetero ma sɛ ye o we, “Véi, se Wɛ wó pa se n yi lanyerane.”
19Moses déem ta na wo Midian ne to, mo Baŋa Wɛ ya tage‑o o we, “Jwoori n vo Ejipti, se balo maama na beeri‑m se ba go to laam tega.” 20Moses ma ja o kaane de o bu-baara bam o jeini-ba bonaga baŋa ne, ye o laam kwei chwoŋa o tɔge de-ba o maa jwoori Ejipti. O déem maa zei Wɛ nacheiga kam o jeŋa ne. 21Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Nmo ná yi Ejipti teo kom, wo-kenkagela yalo maama amo na pɛ‑m dam se n ke to, se n fɔge n ke-ya Ejipti Pɛ wom yiga ne. Amo nam wó pa se o bochare taa dana mo, ye o bá sɛ se amo nɔɔna bam viiri. 22Ko ná tu konto, se n ta de Pɛ wom we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo tento:
Isarele ye amo bakeiri-kwea mo. 23Amo nam mo tage de nmo se n pa a bakeiri-kwea kam chwoŋa se o viiri o vo o zuli-ne. Nmo nam ve amo ni. Konto ŋwaane, amo de nam wó go nmo bakeiri-kwea kam mo.’ ”
24Moses de o kwaga kam ta na wo chwoŋa ne ye ba vo ba yi jei selo ba na wó peini se tega poore to, Baŋa Wɛ déem ma vo o tei ye o boŋe se o go‑o. 25Moses kaane Zipora ma zaŋe o kwei kandwɛ-fole na jege ni to o ma o gwoni o bu-baaro wom peini. O ta ma dwei o baro wom napera de tɔnɔ kom ye o ta o we, “Nmo yɔɔre n ye amo baro jana bam ŋwaane mo.” 26O na ŋɔɔne tei to tɔge de pein-gwoŋa kam ŋwaane mo. Baŋa Wɛ daa maa wo go Moses.
27 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Aron o we, “Zaŋe n vo kagoa kam yuu se n jeeri Moses.” O ma vo o jeeri‑o Wɛ peo kom ne ye o kukwori‑o. 28Moses déem laam ma lwoni o bere Aron kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe‑o se o ta to. O ma daare o ta wo-kenkagela yam Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑o ni se o ke to taane o bere Aron.
29Moses de Aron déem ma kwei chwoŋa ba vo ba yi Ejipti ye ba la Isarele nakwa bam ba ke daane. 30Aron ma ta kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ déem na tage de Moses to o bere-ba. O de ma ke wo-kenkagela yam maama pa se nɔɔna bam na. 31Nakwa bam déem ma sɛ. Ba ta ma ni Baŋa Wɛ na nɛ ba yaara yam ye o chu o ba se o jwoŋi-ba ya wone tei to. Ba ma chɔɔle tega ne ba zuli Wɛ.

english_text:
Moses and Aaron Go to the King of Egypt
1Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
2“Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
3They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
4-5The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
6That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
7Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can, 8but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God. 9Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
10The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw. 11Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
12The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw. 13But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.” 14The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
15Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this? 16No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
17The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord. 18Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
19The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day. 20After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them. 21Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.”
The Lord's Promise to Moses
22Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here? 23Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_text:
Moses de Aron vei Ejipti Pɛ wom tei
1Ko na ke fee to, Moses de Aron déem ma vo Ejipti Pɛ wom tei ba ta ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina bam Wɛ to ni mo tento: ‘Pa chwoŋa se a nɔɔna bam viiri. Ba jege se ba vo kagoa wone ba ke kuri mo ba zuli amo.’ ” 2Pa-faro wom maa we, “Wɔ mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, pa ko maŋe se a sɛ o ni se Isarele tiina bam viiri? Amo yeiri Baŋa Wɛ wom konto, a nam bá pa chwoŋa se Isarele tiina bam viiri.”
3Ba laam ma leiri‑o ba we, “Hiburu tiina Wɛ wom mo tu debam tei. Konto ŋwaane, dé lwoori nmo tei ne se dé na pwola dé kwei da yatɔ chwoŋa dé vo kagoa kam wone dé ke kaanem dáane dé pa dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Kokuri to, dé ná wo ke konto, o wó waare debam dedaane jawe-chɛɛro dwi dwi mo, naa o pa se dé to jara-keim wone ye dé te.” 4Pɛ wom ma ve ye o ta o we, “Moses de Aron, bɛ mo ye abam pa se nɔɔna bam yage ba totoŋa? Abam maama jwoori-na á vo á totoŋa ni ne!” 5O ta maa we, “Nii-na ywo! Nɔɔna bam laam tiini ba daga Ejipti tega kam ne, ye á dáa lage se á cheiŋi-ba se ba yé toŋe ba totoŋa yam.”
6Dento dɛ ne, Ejipti Pɛ wom ma bwoŋi dedɛɛra balo na fe tontoŋena bam de totoŋ-chɛɛra to de balo na nii totoŋa yam baŋa ne to, ye o pa-ba ni. O déem maa we:
7“Abam daa yé kwei-na ga-korro á pa nɔɔna bam se ba taa mae ba mage bira. Banto tete laam mo jege se ba beeri ga-korro ba ma ba toŋe totoŋa yam. 8Ba bira yam ba na wó mage to ba jege se ya muri, de fenfee de. Ba ye jawɔre-nyena mo! Konto ŋwaane mo ba beeri chwoŋa se ba vo ba ke kaanem ba pa ba Wɛ wom. 9Pa-na se totoŋa yam tiini ya chɛ ba yera. Konto wó pa se ba yé na yiga se ba daa cheigi vwa yam konto.”
10Balo na fe kabɛ sem de totoŋ-chɛɛra to de totoŋa yiga tiina bam déem ma nwoŋi ba vo ba ta de nɔɔna bam ba we, “Pɛ wom tage tento mo: ‘Amo daa bá pa abam ga-korro. 11Abam mo jege se á vo á beeri ga-korro á pa á tete. Nam ta‑á yei-na we á bira yam á na maŋe á yeini á mage to ba jege se ya muri ya ni ne de fenfee de.’ ”
12Ko déem ma pa se nɔɔna bam jage Ejipti tega kam jei maama ne ba beeri ga-korro se ba ma ba toŋe. 13Balo na fe kabɛ sem de totoŋa to, de déem laam tiini ba fe-ba, ye ba tɛ-ba ba we, “Dɛ maama abam totoŋa yam jege se ya yi ko daama na ye tei ye á jwoŋi ga-korro debam tei ne to mo.” 14Pɛ wom nɔɔna balo na fe kabɛ sem de totoŋ-chɛɛra to déem ma bɛɛse Isarele yiga tiina balo na nii totoŋa yam baŋa ne to. Ba maa jege-ba ba maga ye ba we, “Ko ke da yalei ye á nɔɔna bam wo mage bira yam se ya ja ya ni ne, nenɛɛne ko daama na ye tei to. Bɛ mo kea?”
15Isarele totoŋa yiga tiina bam laam ma vo ba lwoori Pa-faro wom ba we, “Dé Tu, bɛ laam mo kea ye nmo jege debam n ke tento? 16Dedɛɛra bam daa ba pae debam ga-korro se dé taa ma dé toŋa, ye ba ta fe debam se dé mage bira yam se ya yé muri. Ba ta maa jege debam ba maga, ye ko ye banto yiga mo.” 17Pɛ wom ma leiri-ba o we, “Nii jawɔre-nyena banto! Abam na vae totoŋa to ŋwaane mo á kare á beeri chwoŋa amo tei ne se á vo á ke kaanem á pa Baŋa Wɛ. 18Lela! Se á jwoori á totoŋa ni ne! Ba bá pa abam ga-korro. Á nam ta jege se á mage bira yam mo se ya ja ya ni.” 19Isarele totoŋa yiga tiina bam ma lɔre we keim dem laam tiini de chamma mo de pa banto de Isarele tiina bam maama. Kokuri to, ba maane we bira yam ba na wó mage dɛ maama to ba jege se ya muri ya ni ne.
20Nɔɔna bam déem na nwoŋi Pɛ wom tei ne to, mo ba jeeri Moses de Aron. Ba de déem nam maŋe ba zege ba cheigi nɔɔna bam mo se ba ba. 21Ba na nɛ-ba to, mo ba poone de Moses de Aron ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó waare abam á na ke kolo to ŋwaane. Abam laam pɛ se debam totoŋa tiini ya lwoi mo Ejipti Pɛ de o dedɛɛra bam momwa ne. Á ta ma á pa-ba pwola se ba go debam.”
22Moses ma pipiri o vo o bwei Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Amo Teiru, bɛ mo ye n tiini n ja cham dento n ba n pa n nɔɔna bam? Nmo boŋe se n ke tento mo ye n toŋe-ne ywo to na? 23Ko zege dɛ delo amo na vei a ŋɔɔne dedaane Pɛ wom nmo yere ŋwaane to, mo o yɔɔre o pae nmo nɔɔna bam cham se ba taa di. Nmo tete nam ba ke kolokolo se n jwoŋi-ba n yage.”

english_text:
1The Lord God told Moses:
Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
2 My name is the Lord. 3But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name. 4I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners. 5Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
6Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery. 7I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians. 8I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
9When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
10Then the Lord told Moses 11to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave. 12But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?” 13But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt.
Family Record of Aaron and Moses
14The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans:
The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
15The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
16 Levi lived to be 137; his sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
17Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
18Kohath lived to be 133; his sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
19Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
20Amram lived to be 137. He married his father's sister Jochebed, and they had two sons, Aaron and Moses.
21Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
22Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
23Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
24Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
25Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
26The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt, 27and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free.
The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
28When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt, 29he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
30But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ toŋe Moses Pa-faro wom tei ne
1 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we, “Amo laam lage a pa se n lɔre amo na wó ke Pa-faro wom tei to mo. Amo wó ma dam mo a fe‑o se o yage a nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri. Amo wó pa se o zeili-ba mo se ba nwoŋi ba daare o teo kom.”
2Wɛ daa ta ma ta de Moses o we, “Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. 3Amo déem veere a tete de Abaraham, de Izaak, dedaane Jakob, se ba lɔre we a ye Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom mo. Amo déem nam wo pɛ se ba lɔre a yere dem na ye Taa Wuu Tu Baŋa Wɛ to. 4Amo déem ma gwoni ni de-ba, ye a pwooli se a pa-ba Kanaan tega kam. Ba déem nam ta ye veira mo ba zoore jei sem konto ne. 5Amo laam nam nigi Isarele tiina bam na ŋwaana tei maama to kolo ŋwaane Ejipti tiina bam tiini ba de-ba kabɛɛne wone. Amo nam wó ke a tɔge de a ni-gwonim dem. 6Nam ta de Isarele tiina bam we ‘Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ! A nam wó ma a dam-fɔrɔ de a totoŋ-kamunnu a ma a waare Ejipti tiina bam, se a daare a jwoŋi abam á totoŋ-dɛɛra wone a yage se á daa yé ta‑á ye kabɛ. 7A maa wó pa se á ta‑á ye amo tete nɔɔna. Amo maa wó taa ye abam Wɛ. Konto to, á wó wane á lɔre we amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ, a na jwoŋi abam a yage Ejipti tiina bam jeŋa ne to ŋwaane. 8A maa wó ja abam a zo tega kalo a déem na gwoni ni se a pa Abaraham, de Izaak, dedaane Jakob to. Amo wó seene a pa abam tega kam konto se ka taa ye abam tete nyem. Amo nam mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.’ ”
9Moses déem ma ta tento maama de Isarele tiina bam. Ba ma ve o taane dem, kokuri to ba vɔna mo dɛ yiga ya pare. Ba yera de déem ma chɛ, ba totoŋ-dɛɛra yam ŋwaane. 10Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we, 11“Jwoori n vo Ejipti Pɛ tei, se n ta ded‑o we o pa Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba nwoŋi da o teo kom ne ba viiri.” 12Moses ma leiri o we, “Nmo yei we amo ni ware de pipiri lanyerane. Nii amo tete nɔɔna bam na wo cheigi amo taane dem to, Pɛ wom laam mo wó sɛ o cheigi-de na?”
13 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa Moses de Aron ni ye o we, “Véi-na Isarele tiina bam de Ejipti Pɛ tei, á ta de-ba we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ abam ni se á ja Isarele tiina bam á nwoŋi da Ejipti teo kom ne.”
Moses de Aron dwi dem taane
14Nɔɔna banto déem mo wo Isarele sɔ-yuni tem maama yiga ne:
Jakob bu-kwea kam mo ye Ruben. Ruben bu-baara bam mo tento:
Hanoki, de Pallu, de Hezeron, de Karimi. Sɔ-yuni tento mo ke daane te ye Ruben dwi dem nabaara.
15Simeon de bu-baara bam mo tento:
Jemweli, de Jamin, de Ohadi, de Jakin, de Zohare, dedaane Sawuli. (Sawuli nu déem ye Kanaan tiina bukɔ mo.) Sɔ-yuni tento mo ke daane te ye Simeon dwi dem nabaara.
16Levi bu-baara bam yera na popone ya tiŋi to mo tento:
Gereson, de Kohafe, de Merari. Levi déem ŋwe mo taa o yi bena bi de fintɔ-yarepɛ (137).
17Gereson bia de ba sɔ-yuni tem déem maa ye Libini de Simeyi.
18Kohafe bia déem mo ye Amiram, de Izehara, de Heboron, dedaane Yuzeli. Kohafe de déem ŋwe mo taa o yi bena bi de fintɔ-yatɔ (133).
19Merari bia déem mo ye Mahili de Musi.
Sɔ-yuni tento mo ke daane te ye Levi dwi dem nabaara.
20Amiram déem ma di o kwo nakɔ Jokebedi o ma o ke kaane. Ba déem ma lo Aron de Moses. Amiram déem ŋwe mo taa o yi bena bi de fintɔ-yarepɛ (137).
21Izehara bia de déem maa ye Kora, de Nefega, dedaane Zikiri.
22Yuzeli bia de déem maa ye Misayeli, de Elizafan, de Sitiri.
23Aron déem ma di Eliseba o ma o ke kaane. Wonto maa ye Aminadabi bukɔ mo, ye o ta ye Naason nakɔ. Ba déem loge bia bana mo: Nadab, de Abihu, de Eleaza, de Itamara.
24Kora bia déem maa ye Asiri, de Elikana, de Abiasafa. Banto de ba sɔ-yuni tem mo ye Kora dwi dem nabaara.
25Aron bu Eleaza déem ma di Puteli bukɔ o ma o ke o kaane, ye ba lo Finehase.
Levi dwi dem taane mo konto. Sɔ-yuni tem konto maama déem ye Levi dwi dem mo.
26Aron de Moses taane na bere tei tento to, banto maa ye balo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ba ni o we, ba véi ba ja Isarele tiina bam de ba kɔgɔ kom maama ba ja nwoŋi da Ejipti ne. 27Banto déem ma seene ba vo Ejipti Pa-faro wom tei ba ta ded‑o se o pa Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba viiri.
Baŋa Wɛ pɛ Moses de Aron ni
28 Baŋa Wɛ déem na ŋɔɔne de Moses Ejipti teo kom ne to, 29o déem tage o we, “Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. Amo ná tage a bere‑m kolo maama, se n lwoni n ta tento de Ejipti Pɛ wom.” 30Moses déem ma ve ye o we, “Nmo yei we a ni ware se de pipiri lanyerane. Konto to, Pɛ wom bá sɛ o cheigi amo taane dem.”

english_text:
1The Lord said:
I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people. 2Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country. 3-4 But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go. 5When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
6Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord 7and spoke to the king. At the time, Moses was 80 years old, and Aaron was 83.
A Stick Turns into a Snake
8-9The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
10Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake. 11Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing— 12they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs. 13The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen.
The Nile River Turns into Blood
14 The Lord said to Moses:
The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go. 15Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king. 16Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
17 “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood. 18The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
19Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
20Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood, 21the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
22But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen. 23Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought. 24The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink.

translation_text:
1 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma leiri Moses o we, “Nii! Amo lage a pa se n ta‑n nye de Wɛ mo Ejipti Pɛ wom yiga ne. Nmo zembaaro Aron wó taa ye nmo ni-jwoŋinu se o taa ŋɔɔne ded‑o. 2Nmo jege se n ta kolo maama a na wó ŋɔɔne dede‑m to n bere n zembaaro Aron. Wonto laam maa wó ta de Pɛ wom se o yage chwoŋa se Isarele tiina bam viiri ba daare o teo kom. 3Amo nam wó pa se Pɛ wom bochare taa damma. Amo wó pa se wo-kenkagela dedɛ ke Ejipti tiina bam tetare ne. 4De konto de, o ta bá sɛ o cheigi abam taane dem. Amo laam wó ma a dam-fɔrɔ a waare Ejipti tiina bam. Ko kwaga ne, amo wó pa se a nɔɔna bam nwoŋi da teo kom konto ne. Isarele tiina bam maama wó nwoŋi kɔgɔ de kɔgɔ. 5Konto maama ná kea, Ejipti tiina bam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, de amo na mɛ dam a waare-ba pa se Isarele tiina bam na chwoŋa ba nwoŋi ba teo kom ne to ŋwaane.”
6Moses de Aron ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na bere-ba to. 7Ba déem na vei se ba ŋɔɔne dedaane Pa-faro wom to, de Moses ye bena funɔnɔ (80) mo. Aron maa ye bena funɔnɔ-yatɔ (83).
Aron nacheiga kam jigi basankwea
8 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Moses de Aron o we, 9“Ejipti Pɛ wom ná tage o we ‘Ke-na wo-kenkagele se a nii’, se n laam ta de Aron se o kwei o nacheiga kam o dole o de tega ne, Pɛ wom yiga ne. O ná kea, ka wó ji basankwea.” 10Moses de Aron déem ma vo ba zo Pa-faro wom tei. Ba ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na bere-ba to. Aron déem kwei o nacheiga kam mo o dole o de tega ne, Pɛ wom dedaane o nakwa yiga ne. Ka ma seene ka ji basankwea. 11Pa-faro wom ma toŋe o bwoŋi o teo kom yi-nara de ko liri-mwa tiina se ba la daane. Liri keira bam na tu to, ba de ma kwei ba liri kikia ba lwoni ba ke wo-kenkagela yanto dwoŋi. 12Ba dedoa dedoa déem ma dole ba nachei sem ba de tega ne, ye se ji basankwe. Ko nam ná ye Aron nacheiga kam, kanto déem ligi ba nachei sem maama mo. 13Ejipti Pɛ wom déem nɛ tento maama, ye o bochare ta dana. O déem wo sɛ se o cheigi ba taane dem. Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o ta we ko wó taa ye konto mo.
Cham kuni fuga
1. Jana
14 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Ejipti Pɛ bochare yɔɔre de dana mo, ye o ve se o pa amo nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri. 15Jwa tetete se n kwei nacheiga kalo na jigi basankwea to n vo Naili buga kam ni se n jeeri Pɛ wom da. O na maa beene maŋa kalo to, se n zege buga kam ni ne n cheigi‑o. 16O ná tua, se n ta ded‑o we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wolo Hiburu tiina bam na zuli‑o to mo toŋe-ne se a ta de nmo se n pa o nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba vo kagoa kam wone ba zuli‑o. Nmo nam ta wo sɛ se n pa ba viiri. 17Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo tento:
Wɛ wó ke keim se nmo wane n lɔre we wonto mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. Nii ywo! Amo lage a kwei nacheiga kanto a na zei to a mage Naili na bam se ba pipiri ba ji jana. 18Ywona yalo na wo Naili buga kam wone to maama wó te. Na bam de maa wó taa lwoi, pa se Ejipti tiina bam de daa bá wane ba nyɔ buga kam na.’ ”
19 Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta de Moses o we, “Ta de Aron se o kwei o nacheiga kam o twe-ka o jeeri Ejipti bwi sem, de nabare sem, de bu-nwaro tem, de chwaro tem. O ná ke konto, na bam maama wó pipiri ba ji jana. Ko ná maŋe ko ye kambi sem de kɔɔra bam wone, Ejipti teo kom jei maama wó su de jana.” 20Moses de Aron ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na bere-ba to.
