19Moses ma ta de-ba o we, “Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé pa se wodiu konto peini o tei ne ko poore tega.” 20Nɔɔna badwonna ma ve se ba sɛ Moses taane dem. Ba déem ma di ba daare pa se ko poore tega. Wodiu kom ma ji kanzwa ye ko laam lwoi. Moses bane ma zaŋe de nɔɔna bam konto. 21Dɛ maama tetete, ba maa yeini ba pɛ tetei na wó maŋe de ba dim to. Wea ná yeini ka di wɛɛne, kolo maama na daare tega ne to wó nyeene mo.
22Da yaredo dɛ dem ne, ba déem pɛ wodiu kom kuni belei mo, bwɛ selei nɔɔno maama ŋwaane. Ba nakwa tiina bam ma vo Moses tei ba ta ba bere‑o ko na ke tei to. 23O ma ta de-ba o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: ‘Baŋa Wɛ mo pɔɔre jwa dɛ dem se de taa ye de yera da maama wone. O nam ke-de se de taa ye siu dɛ mo se á ma á zuli‑o. Konto ŋwaane, wɔ-na woŋo kolo maama na maŋe de wɔɔm to se á saŋe kolo maama na maŋe de saŋem to. Ke-na konto zem se woŋo kolo ná daare, se á tiŋi-ko jwa ŋwaane.’ ” 24Nɔɔna bam ma ke tei Moses na tage to. Ba déem zege wodiu kolo na daare to pa se tega poore. Ko maa wo zo kanzwa, ye ko ba lwoi de.
25Tega na poore to, Moses ma ta o we, “Di-na wodiu kom konto zem, se zem dɛ dem ye siu dɛ mo se á ma á zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Abam zem bá na wodiu jei de jei tega kam baŋa ne. 26Da yaredo mo abam wó ta‑á pɛ wodiu kom. Ko daare da yarepɛ dɛ dem wó taa ye siu dɛ mo ko pae abam. Wodiu bá taa wora se á pɛ-ko.”
27Ko nam na ke tei to, nɔɔna badwonna mo nwoŋi da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne ba beeri wodiu se ba pɛ, ye ba wo nɛ kolokolo. 28Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Abam wó ve se á sɛ amo nia yam de a bera yam taa se á vo á maŋe yei ne mo? 29Á wo nɛ? Baŋa Wɛ tiŋi siu dɛ dem o pa abam. Konto ŋwaane mo da yaredo dɛ dem ne Wɛ wó pa da yalei wodiu se á pɛ. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege se o nwoŋi pwooni da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne. O wó maŋe sɔŋɔ ne mo.” 30Ko ma pa se da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne nɔɔna bam déem sii de ba totoŋa.
31Isarele tiina bam ma bwoŋi wodiu kom yere we ‘Manna.’ Ko déem nye dedaane nyansaŋa bia mo. Ko maa ye napwoŋo, ye ko ywomma nenɛɛne ba mɛ tooro mo ba fɔge maasa tei to. 32Moses ta ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ pɛ o ni dem mo se á kwei Manna yam bɔŋa dedoa á tiŋi jwa ŋwaane. Abam bia jwa wó lɔre wodiu kolo Wɛ na pɛ abam kagoa kam yuu ne, maŋa kalo o na jaane abam o nwoŋi Ejipti ne to.”
33Moses laam ma ta de Aron o we, “Kwei zoŋa n daare n zwɛ Manna n ke ka wone se ka maŋe de bɔŋa dedoa. Laam ja-ka n vo n zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Á bia jwa wó taa nae Manna yam dáane maŋa maama.” 34Aron déem ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na bere Moses to. O kwei Manna yam mo o zege Wɛ ni-gwonim kandwa yalei yam yiga ne se ya taa wo dáane.
35Isarele tiina bam ma di Manna yam bena finna. Ba déem di-ya mo taa se ko taa vei maŋa kalo ba na vei ba yi Kanaan ye ba zoore da to. 36Ba déem na mɛ bɔŋa kalo ba maŋe Manna yam to yere mo ye ‘Omaa’. Omaa kuni fuga mo ye kuriwaa bu dedoa.

english_text:
The Lord Gives Water from a Rock
1 The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
2The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!”
Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
3But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
4Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
5The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River. 6When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
7The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.”
Israel Defeats the Amalekites
8When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites. 9So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
10Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop. 11The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them. 12After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset. 13That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
14 Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
15Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.” 16Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_text:
Na nwoŋi peo yera ne
1Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom déem ma zege Sin kagoa kam ne, ye ba laam kare ba beeri, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na yeini o bere-ba se ba vo mɛ to. Ba ma vo ba yi jei sedwoŋi ba na bwoi we Refidim to ye ba chwi ba vwoa dáane. Jei sem konto ne, na déem tera se nɔɔna bam nyɔ. 2Ba ma bobo se ba taa bwɛ Moses ye ba we, “Pa debam na se dé nyɔ!” Moses ma leiri o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye á bwɛ amo konto? Bɛ mo ye abam lage se á maŋe Baŋa Wɛ á nii?” 3Na-nyɔm dem nam na jege nɔɔna bam to, ba déem ta poone ye ba bwɛ Moses ba we, “Bɛ mo maŋe ko ba n yuu ne ye n ja debam n nwoŋi Ejipti ne n ba ywo-seeni? Nmo lage se na-nyɔm mo go debam dedaane dé bia dedaane dé vara maama na?”
4Moses ma kaase o jare Baŋa Wɛ ye o we, “Amo bere a lage a ke nɔɔna banto tetɛ mo? Ba laam boŋe se ba dole-ne de kandwa mo ba go.” 5Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri Moses o we, “Kuri Isarele nakwa bam badwonna se á da nɔɔna bam yiga á kɛ. Kwei n nacheiga kalo n na mɛ n mage Naili buga kam to n woli da n vo. 6Amo wó zege Sinayi peo kom yuu ne se a jeeri abam. Á ná yi da, nmo laam wó ma n nacheiga kam n mage peo kom. Nmo ná ke konto, na wó nwoŋi ko yera ne se nɔɔna bam nyɔ.” Moses ma ke konto Isarele nakwa bam yiga ne.
7Moses déem pɛ jei sem konto yere we ‘Meriba’, de ‘Massa’. Kokuri to, dáane mo Isarele tiina bam poone ye ba maŋe Baŋa Wɛ se ba nii. Ba déem we, “Baŋa Wɛ wo dé tei ne naa o tera mo?”
Amaleki tiina ke jara de Isarele tiina bam
8Isarele tiina bam na wo Refidim ne to, Amaleki tiina bam ma pɔpɔ ba zaŋe ba baŋa ne se ba ke jara de-ba. 9Moses ma ta de Josua o we, “Kuri nɔɔna bam badwonna se á vo á jeeri Amaleki tiina bam de jara. Jwa ne, amo de wó taa zege peo kom yuu ne, ye a zei Wɛ nacheiga kam.”
10Josua ma ke kolo Moses na bere‑o to. O ma vo o jeeri Amaleki tiina bam se o ke jara de-ba. Se ko ná ye Moses de Aron dedaane Hura, banto déem diini peo kom yuu mo ba zege da. 11Maŋa kalo maama Moses je sem na yeini se wo wɛɛne to, Isarele tiina bam yeini ba dana mo jara yam wone. O je sem nam ná yeini se pare se maa tu tega, Amaleki tiina bam de daa maa dana jara yam yiga ne. 12Moses je sem déem ma bugi. Aron de Hura ma tiŋi kandwɛ, ye ba pa se o jeini de baŋa ne. Ba déem ma teili o je sem pa se lɛɛre se wo wɛɛne. Dedoa zei jazem dem, ye wodwoŋi wom de zei jagwia kam. Ba zei Moses je sem wɛɛne konto mo taa se ko yi wɛ-zoore maŋa. 13Ko dɛ chwoŋa kam konto mo ye Josua de o nɔɔna bam ja jara ba wane Amaleki tiina bam.
14 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we, “Popone keim dento n tiŋi tɔnɔ ne se nɔɔna guli ko gula. Ta popone we, Amo wó ba a pa se Amaleki tiina yere saare logo baŋa ne, se n daare n pa se Josua taa yei ko ni ne.” 15Moses ma lɔ kaanem bimbini jei sem konto ne ye o bwoŋi-de we ‘Baŋa Wɛ mo ye amo Tuta.’ 16O maa we, “Ba zeiŋi je mo wɛɛne se se jeeri Baŋa Wɛ. Baŋa Wɛ wó ja jara dedaane Amaleki tiina bam mo de ba kwaga kam taa wuu.”

english_text:
Jethro Visits Moses
1Jethro was the priest of Midian and the father-in-law of Moses. He heard what the Lord God had done for Moses and his people, after rescuing them from Egypt.
2-4 In the meantime, Moses had sent his wife Zipporah and her two sons to stay with Jethro, and he had welcomed them. Moses was still a foreigner in Midian when his first son was born, and so Moses said, “I'll name him Gershom.”
When his second son was born, Moses said, “I'll name him Eliezer, because the God my father worshiped has saved me from the king of Egypt.”
5-6While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
7When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent, 8where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
9Jethro was so pleased to hear this good news about what the Lord had done, 10that he shouted, “Praise the Lord! He rescued you and the Israelites from the Egyptians and their king. 11 Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.” 12Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship.
Judges Are Appointed
(Deuteronomy 1.9-18)
13The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening. 14Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
15Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do. 16They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
17Jethro replied:
That isn't the best way to do it. 18You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone. 19God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people, 20and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
21You will need to appoint some competent leaders who respect God and are trustworthy and honest. Then put them over groups of 10, 50, 100, and 1,000. 22These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier. 23This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
24Moses followed Jethro's advice. 25He chose some competent leaders from every tribe in Israel and put them over groups of 10, 50, 100, and 1,000. 26They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
27After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_text:
Jetero
1Midian tiina kaanem-tu wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere na ye Jetero. Wonto maa ye Moses tembaaro. O ma ni Wɛ na ke tei maama o pa Moses dedaane Isarele tiina bam, ye o ja-ba o nwoŋi Ejipti ne to. 2-3Moses déem nam ya pɛ se o kaane Zipora de o bia balei bam vo o tembaaro Jetero tei ne mo se ba taa wora. Bia bam dedoa yere mo ye ‘Geresom’. Kokuri to, Moses déem we, “Amo ye veiru mo sa-teo ne.” 4Wodwoŋi wom yere maa ye ‘Eliazera’. Kokuri to, o déem we, “Amo kwo Wɛ wom mo woli-ne. Wonto mo jwoŋi-ne Ejipti Pɛ wom jeŋa ne o yage, pa se o wo go-ne.”
5Moses déem maa chwi o vwoa yam Wɛ peo kom teiŋa ne. O tembaaro Jetero déem ma vo o tei kagoa kam ne. O ma ja Moses kaane wom de o bia balei bam o woli da. 6Jetero ya toŋe ni mo o pa Moses o we, “Amo maa beene nmo tei. N kaane wom de n bia balei bam de maa tɔga.” 7Ba na yi to, Moses ma nwoŋi se o jeeri-ba. O déem ma tiiri o tembaaro wom yiga ne, ye o daare o kukwori‑o. Ba ma bwei da-kwaga, ye ba laam daare ba zo Moses vwei dem wone se ba lare. 8Moses ma lwoni kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe Ejipti Pɛ wom de o nɔɔna bam yerane pa se o vere Isarele tiina bam to o bere Jetero. O ta ma ta ded‑o ba na jeeri cham delo maama chwoŋa kam yuu ne to, de Baŋa Wɛ na ke tei o vere-ba to.
9Jetero na nigi konto to, o wo ma pwoli de Baŋa Wɛ na woli Isarele tiina bam to. 10O ma tei Wɛ ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de teem! O vere abam Ejipti tiina bam de ba Pɛ wom jeŋa ne o yage. 11Amo laam lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ mo daga o dwoi wa yam maama. Kokuri to, o pɛ se o nɔɔna bam lu Ejipti tiina bam dam kuri ne, de ba na bɛɛse-ba tei maama to.” 12Jetero ma ja varem o ba se ba zwɛ ba ma ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ, ye o kwori o ja pɛɛra yadwonna o woli da se o pa‑o. Aron de Isarele nakwa bam maama de ma ba Moses de o tembaaro wom tei, se ba tɔge daane ba di wodiu kom ba ma zuli Wɛ.
13Tega na poore to, Moses ma jeini se o cheigi nɔɔna balo na tu o tei ba saŋe daane to taane. Nɔɔna bam na daga to ŋwaane, ba zege Moses yiga ne mo taa, zezeŋa ne se ko vo ko yi dedaan-ni ne. 14Moses tembaaro Jetero na nɛ konto to mo o bwei‑o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo ye nmo toŋe totoŋe dento n pae nɔɔna bam n yerane? Nii nɔɔna bam na zege ywo-seeni tetete wɛɛne se ko yi dedaan-ni ne, ye nmo yerane mo bore ba taane.” 15Moses ma leiri‑o o we, “Kokuri to, nɔɔna bam yeini ba tui amo tei se ba lɔre Wɛ boboŋa na ye tei ya pa-ba to mo. 16Nɔɔna balo ná jege kantɔgɔ ba tetare ne, ba yeini ba tui amo tei mo se a bere-ba wolo na jege bora to. Amo ta wó daare a bere-ba Wɛ nia yam de o bera yam maama se ba taa ni ya kuri.”
17Jetero ma leiri o we, “Nmo na ke tei to ba tɔge chwoŋa. 18Nmo ná lage n ta‑n ke konto, ko bá dáane de n yera na chɛ. Nɔɔna bam yera de maa wó chɛ. Totoŋe dento daga de dwoi nmo yerane jaanem. 19Cheigi amo kwea yanto a na lage a pa‑m to, se Wɛ wó taa wora nmo tei ne. Nɔɔna bam ná yeini ba jege kantɔgɔ, ko lana se n kwei ba taane dem n ja n vo Wɛ yiga ne mo. 20Nmo ta jege se n bere-ba Wɛ nia yam, dedaane o bera yam na bere kolo to, se ba lɔre ba na wó tɔge chwoŋa kalo to. 21Ko daare, beeri nɔɔna bam maama wone n kuri balo na ye jawale-nyena ye ba kɔre Wɛ to. Banto wó taa ye balo nɔɔna na jege ba chega ye ba ba tɔge sabu-laga chwoŋa to mo. Nmo laam wó tiŋi nɔɔna bam konto se ba taa ye yiga tiina ye ba nii nɔɔna baŋa ne. Badwonna wó taa nii nɔɔna moro baŋa ne, badwonna maa nii bi bi, badwonna maa nii finnu finnu, ye badaara nii nɔɔna fuga fuga baŋa ne. 22Maŋa maama ba wó taa cheigi balo na jege taane to se ba bore ba bora. Ko ná ye wo-chɛɔ, ko ye se ba kwei taane dem ba ja ba nmo yiga ne mo se n bore-de. Ko nam ná ye ta-balaŋa, ba tete mo wó bore. Konto wó pa se totoŋa yam ke mɔle ya pa‑m, yiga tiina bam na tɔge ba zeŋe nmo zele dem to ŋwaane. 23Nmo ná ke konto dwoŋi nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na bere‑m to, ko daa bá ni‑m. Nɔɔna bam de nam wó jwoori ba sam ne dedaane bochare-zuru.”
24Moses déem ma cheigi Jetero bera yam ye o sɛ-ya. 25O ma beeri Isarele tiina bam maama wone o kuri jawale-nyena se ba taa ye yiga tiina ye ba nii nɔɔna moro moro baŋa ne, se badwonna taa nii bi bi, se badwonna nii finnu finnu, ye badaara nii fuga fuga baŋa ne. 26Maŋa maama banto mo yeini ba bore Isarele tiina bam taane. Ko ná ye wo-chɛɔ, ba wó kwei taane dem ba ja vo Moses yiga ne mo se o bore-de. Ko nam ná yeini ko ye ta-balaŋa, ba tete mo wó bore-de.
27Ko kwaga ne mo Moses bane o tembaaro Jetero o yage chwoŋa ne pa se o jwoori o vo o tete teo.

english_text:
At Mount Sinai
1-2The Israelites left Rephidim and arrived at the desert. Then two months after leaving Egypt, they arrived at the desert near Mount Sinai, where they set up camp at the foot of the mountain. This was two months after they had left Egypt.
3Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
4You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young. 5 Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine, 6 but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests.
Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
7After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said, 8and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
9The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
10Once more the Lord spoke to Moses:
Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes 11and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
12 Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death, 13either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
14After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God. 15He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime.
The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
16 On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear. 17Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
18Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook. 19The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
20The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there. 21Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die. 22Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
23Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
24Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
25After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_text:
Sinayi Peo kom
1-2Isarele tiina bam déem zege Refidim ne ba vo ba yi Sinayi kagoa kam. Ba na nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne to, ko ye chane setɔ boboa dɛ ne mo ba yi da. Ba ma chwi ba vwoa yam Sinayi Peo kom teiŋa ne. 3Moses ma di peo kom yuu se o vo Wɛ tei. Baŋa Wɛ ma zege peo kom yuu ne o bwoŋi‑o ye o we, “Ta tento n bere Isarele tiina bam na ye Jakob dwi dem to:
4‘Abam tete yi nɛ amo Baŋa Wɛ na ke kolo se ko zo Ejipti tiina bam yera to. Á ta nɛ amo na kwei abam a daŋe a bakale baŋa ne nenɛɛne kalwoŋo na yeini ko ke tei de ko bia to. A ke abam konto mo a ja a yi amo tei ywo-seeni. 5Tɔ. Logo baŋa maama ye amo nyem mo. Abam nam ná sɛ amo ni se á ta‑á ke kolo maama amo na wó bere abam to, amo wó kuri abam nabiina maama wone se á ta‑á ye amo tete nɔɔna. 6Abam nam wó ta‑á ye amo kaanem tiina, ye á toŋe amo paare yerane ŋwaane mo. Abam dwi dem wó taa ye á yera amo ŋwaane.’ Ta konto maama n bere Isarele tiina bam.”
7Moses ma zege peo kom yuu ne o tu. O ma bwoŋi Isarele nakwa bam ye o daare o tole Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam maama o bere-ba. 8Nɔɔna bam ma sɛ ye ba leiri ba we, “Dé wó ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na tage to.” Moses daa ma ja nɔɔna bam kwora kam o vo o tole o bere Baŋa Wɛ.
9 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Moses o we, “Amo lage a ba nmo tei, ye kunkwon-lilirru mo wó kwoli-ne. Ko wó pa se, amo ná tu a ŋɔɔne de nmo, nɔɔna bam wó ni amo kwora ye ba daare ba ke ba wo-dedoa de nmo maŋa maama.”
Moses daa ma ta nɔɔna bam taane dem maama o bere Baŋa Wɛ. 10Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, “Jwoori n tu nɔɔna bam tei n daare n pa ba kwei zem de jwa dɛ dem ba ma kwɛ ba bochara ba pa amo. Ba jege se ba zare ba gwaaro 11se ba ti ba yiga se, da yatɔ dɛ ná yia, se a laam ba ba tei. Amo Baŋa Wɛ wó tu a ba Sinayi Peo kom yuu ne se nɔɔna bam maama taa nii ba na-ne. 12Nam lɔ siseini n kaare peo kom maama se nɔɔna bam yé lɛɛne-de. Ta de nɔɔna bam we, ba yé diini peo kom yuu naa ba twɛ ko teiŋa kam. Nɔɔno wolo naga ná nɔne peo kom baŋa ne, ba jege se ba go konto tu mo. 13Ba ná lage ba go‑o, ba jeŋa yé dwei‑o. Ba nam wó dole‑o mo de kandwa naa ba ta‑o de chena se o te. Ko ná ye nabiinu naa varem mo ye o naga ná nɔne peo kom, o jege se o te mo. Tɔ. Ba nam ná wugi nabɔna kam, nɔɔna bam laam jege chwoŋa se ba fɔɔre ba yi peo kom.”
14Moses ma zege peo kom yuu ne o tu o vo nɔɔna bam tei. O ma pa ba kwɛ ba bochara ba pa Wɛ ye ba daare ba zare ba gwaaro. 15Moses ma ta de-ba o we, “Ti-na á yiga da yatɔ dɛ dem ŋwaane. Da yam konto ne, nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé peini de kaane.”
16Da yatɔ dɛ dem tetete mo doa tiini ka pepele ye ka bage pina-pina. Kunkwon-liliru ma tu ko ba ko kwoli peo kom yuu. Nabɔna laam ma tiini ka wuuri sɔɔ dedɛ. Nɔɔna bam na nigi sɔɔ kom to, ba yera maa tiini ya sae ye foone zo-ba. 17Moses ma tɔge nɔɔna bam yiga o ja-ba o nwoŋi ba vwoa yam wone se ba vo ba jeeri Wɛ. Ba ma vo ba zege peo kom teiŋa ne. 18Nyoa déem maa kwoli Sinayi peo kom yuu maama. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem chugi ko baŋa ne ye mini gilimi‑o. Nyoa kam ma zaŋe toge-toge ka di wɛyuu, nenɛɛne min-vo-fɔrɔ tei. Peo kom maama ma tiini ko ziziŋi. 19Nabɔna kam kwori laam maa tiini de dana. Moses déem maa ŋɔɔne de Wɛ, ye Wɛ de leiri o taane dem ne doa na bage tei to.
20 Baŋa Wɛ ma tu o ba Sinayi Peo kom yuu ne. O ma bwoŋi Moses se o di o ba peo kom yuu. Moses ma di Wɛ tei. 21Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, “Jwoori n tu tega n kaane nɔɔna bam se ba yé lɛɛne siseini dem. Ba ba jege se ba fe ba di se ba na amo Baŋa Wɛ. Ba ná fe ba ke konto, ba dedɛ lage ba te mo. 22Ko ná maŋe ko ye amo kaanem tiina balo na yeini ba tui amo tei to, ba jege se ba kwɛ ba bochara mo amo ŋwaane. Ko ná dae konto, amo wó chɔge-ba mo.”
23Moses ma ta de Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Nɔɔna bam ba jege chwoŋa se ba di peo kom. Nmo pɛ se amo lɔ siseini mo a tiŋi se nɔɔna bam yé lɛɛne-de, nmo na pwɛ peo kom pa ko ye ko yera to ŋwaane.” 24Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Nam tu tega n ja Aron se á tɔge daane á di ywo-seeni. Se ko ná ye kaanem tiina bam dedaane nɔɔna bam maama, ba ná fe ba lɛɛne se ba twɛ ywo-seeni, amo bane wó zaŋe de-ba mo, ye a chɔge-ba.”
25Moses ma tu o vo nɔɔna bam tei ye o ta de-ba kolo Baŋa Wɛ na tage to.

english_text:
The Ten Commandments
(Deuteronomy 5.1-21)
1God said to the people of Israel:
2I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
3Do not worship any god except me.
4 Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth. 5 Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me, I will punish your families for three or four generations. 6But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
7 Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
8 Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me. 9 You have six days when you can do your work, 10but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns. 11 In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
12 Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
13 Do not murder.
14 Be faithful in marriage.
15 Do not steal.
16 Do not tell lies about others.
17 Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else.
The People Are Afraid
(Deuteronomy 5.23-33)
18 The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off 19and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
20“Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.” 21But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off.
Idols and Altars
22The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel:
With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven. 23So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
24Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you. 25 If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship. 26And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_text:
Wɛ ni-kaana fuga kam
Nia Gulim 5:6-21
1Wɛ déem mo ŋɔɔne taane dento maama:
2“Amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Amo maa ye wolo na jaane abam a ja nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne pa se a vere abam á kabɛɛne dem ne a yage to. 3Daa á yé zuli-na wɛ dedwoŋi á woli amo wone.
4Yé zaŋe-na á mɔ kamɔgɔ se ko taa ye jwoni ko pa abam. Á yé mɔ woŋo se ko lwoni wɛyuu wonnu, naa tega baŋa wonnu, naa tega kuri na bam wo wonnu. 5Abam ba jege se á tiiri te yiga ne naa á zuli-te. Kokuri to, amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Amo yi page abam baŋa ne mo. Ko ná ye balo na ve amo to, a yeini a waare-ba de ba bia maama se ko vo ko yi ba dwi dem kuni betɔ naa bena laŋa ne mo. 6Ko nam ná ye balo na swoi-ne ye ba sɛ a nia yam to, a maa yeini a jege ba swono taa, se ko yi ba dwi dem kuni moro laŋa ne.
7Yé zaŋe-na á bwoŋi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere kafɛ yerane, se Baŋa Wɛ wó waare wolo maama na ke konto to.
8Ta‑á guli-na Wɛ siu dɛ dem se á pɔɔre-de da yam maama wone á pa Wɛ. 9Da yarepɛ maama wone, abam jege da yaredo mo se á ma á toŋe totoŋa dwi maama. 10Ko nam ná ye da yarepɛ dɛ dem, abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ pɔɔre-de mo o pa o tete, se de taa ye siu dɛ. De dɛ ne, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege se o toŋe kolokolo. Ko maa ye abam, de á bia, de á bukwa, de á kabɛ, de á ka-nyaana maama mo bá taa toŋa. Ko woli da, abam vara bam, de veira balo na zoore á teo wone to de bá taa toŋe totoŋa dɛ dem konto ne. 11Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem kwei da yaredo mo o naane wɛyuu de tega baŋa, de naneero tem, dedaane wonnu telo na wo tento maama wone to. O laam ma sii da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne. Baŋa Wɛ ma ke zaane o ke siu dɛ dem baŋa ne o pa de ye de yera.
12Ta‑á nege-na á kwoa de á niina, se ko pa á ta‑á jege momwɛ-dɛɛre maŋa kalo á na wó ta‑á zoore tega kalo abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ na lage o pa abam to wone.
13Yé zaŋe-na á go nɔɔno.
14Yé ke-na kabwoŋa de nɔɔno wodwoŋi kaane.
15Yé ŋɔ-na kolokolo.
16Yé zaŋe-na á bore vwa bora á ma á vane á dwonna.
17Yé kwei-na á boboŋa á daŋe á dwonna sam baŋa ne. Nam yé pa-na se á boboŋa taa wo ba kaana baŋa ne. Yé pa-na se á fera zo ba kabɛ naa ba ka-nyaana wone. Yé pa-na se á yi su á dwonna nabɛ, naa ba bonɛ, naa woŋo kolo maama na ye ba nyem to.”
18Nɔɔna bam maama déem ma na doa kam na tiini ka bage ye ka ta pepele tei maama to. Ba ta ma ni nabɔna kam kwori, ye ba daare ba na peo kom maama na kwoli dedaane nyoa tei maama to. Ba yera maa sae ye foone tiini de jege-ba. Ba déem ma fɔɔre ba kɛ dáa. 19Ba ma ta de Moses ba we, “Jan ja! Nmo ná ŋɔɔne taane n bere debam, dé wó cheigi. Nam yé pa se Wɛ tete ŋɔɔne dedaane debam, se dé wó te.” 20Moses ma leiri nɔɔna bam o we, “Yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. Kokuri to, Wɛ tu abam tei se o faŋe abam mo o nii, se á ta‑á kɔre‑o ye á yé tusi o chwoŋa kam ne.” 21Nɔɔna bam déem zege yiga yiga mo, ye Moses fɔɔre o twɛ kunkwon-liliru kom mɛ Wɛ na wora to.
Chullu tedwonna
22 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Ta tento de Isarele tiina bam:
‘Abam tete yia nɛ we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo zege wɛyuu ne a ŋɔɔne de abam. 23Abam nam ba jege se á zuli wo-gaa á woli amo ne. Á yé zaŋe á kwei sabu-seŋa naa lu-nyenno á ma á ke jwoni.’ ”
24 Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta de Moses o we, “Kwei tega kam teero n ma‑n lɔ kaanem bimbini n pa-ne. Abam ná lage á ke zwɛɛm kaanem naa yazura kaanem, á laam wó yeini á ja á pei, de á bone, dedaane á naane á ba á kaane de baŋa ne á pa-ne. Jei selo maama amo na wó pa se á zuli amo yere konto dwoŋi to, amo tete wó ba abam tei se a swɛ abam swolim. 25Nmo nam ná boŋe se n kwei kandwa se n seene bimbini n pa-ne, se n yé ma kolokolo n ma‑n sare kandwa yam naa n lɔ-ya. Nmo ná ke konto dwoŋi, ko wó pa se bimbini dem ji kafɛ mo amo yiga ne. 26Yé kwei nateini n yeiri bimbini dem yera ne, se n dɔɔle-de n di. Ko dae se nɔɔn-nɔɔno na nmo yera yam bwori, nenɛɛne n ná lage n ke kaanem n pa-ne.”

english_text:
Hebrew Slaves
(Deuteronomy 15.12-18)
1The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
2 If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him. 3If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom. 4If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
5But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them. 6Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
7A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does. 8If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her. 9If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
10If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife. 11If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it.
Murder and Other Violent Crimes
The Lord said:
12 Death is the punishment for murder. 13 But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside. 14If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
15Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
16 Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
17 Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
18Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed, 19and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
20Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves. 21However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
22Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve. 23But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life, 24 eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, 25burn for burn, cut for cut, and bruise for bruise.
26If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free. 27The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
28A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
29Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning. 30However, you may save your own life by paying whatever fine is demanded. 31This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter. 32If the bull kills a slave, you must pay the slave owner 30 pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
33Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property. 34You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
35If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
36If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_text:
1 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta o nia yanto taane o bere Moses se o lwoni o bere Isarele tiina bam:
Isarele tiina de ba kabɛ taane
Nia Gulim 15:12-18
2Wolo ná yeigi Hiburu tu se o ma o ji o kabaa, kabaa kam wó toŋe ka pa‑o bena yaredo mo. Bena yarepɛ bene dem wone, se kotu yage‑o se o viiri zɛɛra, ye kabaa kam bá ŋwe kolokolo. 3Nɔɔno wom ná ye badeim ye o ba o toŋe o pa‑m, ye o ná lage o viiri, ko ye wonto yerane mo wó viiri. O ya nam ná maŋe o jege kaane mo ye o ba n tei, o jege se o ja o kaane wom mo o woli da o viiri. 4O na toŋe o pae wolo to ná pɛ‑o kaane, ye o de kaane wom lo bia daane, nɔɔno wom yerane mo wó viiri. Kaane wom de o bia ye o tu wom nyem mo.
5Kabaa kam nam wó wane o ta we, “Amo swoi a tu wom, ko woli de a kaane de a bia bam. A nam bá viiri a daare-ba.” 6O tu wom maa wó ja‑o o vo Wɛ wara-jei sem ni dem seeni o pa o sale bworo kom. Dáane mo o wó kwei se-lwei o puri kabaa kam zwɛ dedoa. Konto bere we kabaa kam ŋwea maama wone, o ye o tu wom nyem mo.
7Nɔɔno ná kwei o bukɔ o yeigi o pa se o ji kabaa, ko dae se ka maŋa ná yia, se ba yage‑o se o viiri nenɛɛne ba na ke baara bam tei to. 8Kaba-kana kam ná chɔge wolo na yeigi‑o to yiga, o tu wom wó wane o jwoori o yeigi‑o o pa. O nam ba jege chwoŋa se o yeigi‑o o pa dwi-gɛ tiina. O tu wom ná ke konto, ko bere we o lɔge ba ni-sɛɛm dem kwaga ne mo. 9Nɔɔno wom nam ya ná yeigi‑o se o bu mo di o ma o ke kaane, ko jege se o taa nii kabaa kam baŋa ne nenɛɛne ko ye o tete bukɔ mo. 10Nɔɔno wom ná tu o swo kaane wodwoŋi o woli o wone, ko dae se o ve boboa kaane wom o ni-wodiu, naa gwaaro. O nam dae se o ve‑o sare-peiga. 11Nɔɔno wom ná ve se o ke wonnu tento maama o pa kaane wom, kaane wom wó wane o viiri zɛɛra, ye o bá ŋwe kolokolo.
Keim-lwanno telo na maŋe de toone to
12Wolo ná mage o dwoŋi pa se o te, ba wó go kotu de mo. 13Kotu nam ná wo paale o go nɔɔno wom, ye ko ye Wɛ mo jaane o ba, nɔɔno wom konto nam jege se o duri mo o vo jei selo amo na wó kuri to, se o seigi da. 14Ko daare, nɔɔno ná paale o dwoŋi mo o tiŋi, ye o seene o go‑o, ko dae se o lu kɔtaa! O ná maŋe o vo o ja amo kaanem bimbini dem, se á vaŋe‑o á ja á nwoŋi pwooni á go.
15Wolo maama ná mage o kwo naa o nu, se ba go konto tu.
16Wolo ná zi nabiinu o ja se o yeigi, ye kotu ná maŋe o yeigi‑o mo de, naa nɔɔno wom ta ná wo o tei ne ye ba ja‑o, se ba go kotu.
17Wolo maama ná sɔɔle lwarem o yage o kwo naa o nu yuu ne, se ba go kotu de.
18Ni-kantɔgɔ ná tu nɔɔna balei tetare ne, ye ba dedoa ma kwei kandwɛ naa o jaguli o ma o ke wodwoŋi wom zonne ye o wo tege. 19Wolo ba na ke‑o zonne dem to ná wori ye o daare o zaŋe wɛɛne o zi nacheiga o via, ba daa ba jege se ba ke wolo na ke‑o zonne dem to kolokolo. Kotu wó ŋwe nɔɔno wom de o na chɔge o totoŋa to. O ta wó taa nii o baŋa ne mo se o na yazura lanyerane.
20Nɔɔno ná jege kaba-baaro naa kaba-kana, ye o mage‑o pa se o te ko nɛ sem ni ne, se ba waare kotu. 21Kabaa kam nam ná zaŋe ye ka yi da yalei naa yatɔ wɛɛne, ba daa bá ke ka tu wom kolokolo, kabaa kam na ye o nyem to ŋwaane.
22Baara balei jara baŋa ne, ba ná mage kapua pa se o puga kam chɔge, wo-gaa ná wo daane kapua kam, o baro wó gwoni jene mo o pa wolo na pɛ o kaane wom puga kam chɔge to, nenɛɛne nakwa bam na sɛ we ko maŋe tei to. 23Ko nam ná tiini ko chamma ko pa kaane wom, waarem dem de wó taa chamma: ŋwea mo ba wó chɔge ba ma ba leiri ŋwea, 24yi mo ba wó le ba ma leiri yi, yeili mo ba wó guri ba ma leiri yeili, jeŋa mo ba wó le ba ma leiri jeŋa, naa naga mo ba ma leiri naga. 25Kaane wom yera na nɛ zonne delo to, se ba de ke nɔɔno wom konto dwoŋi, ne ko ná ye zwɛɛm naa fufwollu.
26Wolo ná mage o kabaa kam yi pa se de chɔge, se kotu pa kabaa kam chwoŋa se ka viiri zɛɛra ka yi dem chɔgem ŋwaane. 27O nam ná mage kabaa kam yeili mo o guri, se o pa ka viiri zɛɛra, ka yeili dem na guri to ŋwaane.
28Nabea ná chugi nɔɔno ka go, ba jege se ba dole-ka de kandwa ba go mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá done ka nɔna yam. Ka tu wom de nam bá na waarem. 29Nabea kam nam ná maŋe ka kare ka chu nɔɔna mo, se ba kaane ka tu wom se o lei-ka. O ná ve ye ka chu nɔɔno ka go, se ba dole nabea kam de ka tu wom maama ba go. 30Too wom yera nɔɔna nam ná sɛ, nabea kam tu wom wó wane o kwei sabu o leiri o ŋwea kam se ko maŋe de ba na lage tei to. 31Ko nam ta ye bedwe mo de nabea ná chugi nɔɔno wodwoŋi bu-baaro naa o bukɔ de. 32Nɔɔno nabea nam ná go o dwoŋi kabaa, ba wó kwei kandwa ba dole nabea kam ba go mo. Nabea kam tu wó jeeli lu-nyenno sabu-dala fintɔ mo o pa wolo na tei kabaa kam to.
33Nɔɔno maa ná gwaare gwoŋo naa o koge bɔɔne ye o wo jwoori o seere-ko, pa se o dwoŋi nabea naa o bonaga to ko wone ka te, 34gwoŋo kom tu wó ŋwe varem wom jene mo o pa varem wom tu. O ná ŋwe o ti, se o laam taa tei varem wom na tege to.
35Nɔɔno nabea nam ná chugi o dwoŋi nabea ka go, se ba kwei nabea kalo ta na ŋwe to ba yeigi ba daare ba pɔɔre ka sabu kom ba pa daane. Ba ta wó maŋe kalo na tege to nɔna yam mo ba pa daane, se sabu kom de nɔna yam taa mae daane. 36Ko daare nabea kam ná maŋe ka kare ka chu mo ye ka tu wo leigi-ka, ka ná go nɔɔno nabea, ka tu wom jege se o ŋwe nabea kam jene maama mo o pa nɔɔno wom. Nabe-teka kam laam wó taa ye o nyem.

english_text:
Property Laws
The Lord said:
1If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep. 2-4But if you cannot afford to replace the animals, you must be sold as a slave to pay for what you have stolen. If you steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and are caught with it still alive, you must pay the owner double.
If you happen to kill a burglar who breaks into your home after dark, you are not guilty. But if you kill someone who breaks in during the day, you are guilty of murder.
5If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
6If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
7Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double. 8But if the thief isn't caught, some judges will decide if you are the guilty one.
9Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
10Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking. 11If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough. 12But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it. 13If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
14Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it. 15But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it.
Laws for Everyday Life
The Lord said:
16 Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her. 17But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
18 Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
19 Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
20 Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
21 Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
22Do not mistreat widows or orphans. 23If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue. 24In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
25 Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need. 26 Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan, 27because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
28 Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
29Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me.
Dedicate to me your first-born sons 30and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
31 You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
translation_text:
Isarele tiina de ba jejegero
1Nɔɔno ná ŋɔge nabea ye o go-ka naa o kwei-ka o yeigi, ba ná jaane kotu, o wó kwei nabɛ senu mo o jwoori o ŋwe nabea kalo o na ŋɔge to. Ko nam ná ye pia mo o ŋɔga, se o kwei pei sena o ma o ŋwe pia kalo o na ŋɔge to yuu ne.
2-4Ŋweeno jege se o jwoori o ŋwe kolo o na ŋɔge to mo. O daa ná ware o ŋwe, se ba ja‑o ba yeigi se o taa ye kabaa jene dem ŋwaane. Ko daare, ba ná jaane ŋweeno wom ye o ta jege varem wolo o na ŋɔge to, se o ŋwe-ko kuni belei o pa kotu, nenɛɛne ko ná ye nabea naa bonaga naa pia mo de. Ŋweeno ná bwori nɔɔno sɔŋɔ tete ne ye ba ja‑o ba mage ba go, wolo na go‑o to bá te ko ŋwaane. Se ko ná ye wea ne mo ba jaane ŋweeno wom, wolo na go‑o to maŋe se o de te mo.
5Nɔɔno ná pɛ se o vara vere ba zo nɔɔno wodwoŋi kara naa o kaduga wone ba ja o wodiiru tem ba chɔge, vara bam tu wó kwei o tete wodiiru tem o ma o ŋwe wodwoŋi wom wonnu tem na chɔge to mo, nenɛɛne ko ná ye mena naa tio-bia mo de.
6Nɔɔno ná puli mini kuri pa se de di de vo de to o dwoŋi kara wone de chɔge o mena yalo ba na maŋe ba zage naa yalo ba na wo zage to de, o jege se o ŋwe wolo kara na chɔge to mo.
7Nɔɔno ná kwei o sabu naa o jejegero o pa o dwoŋi se o taa nii-te o diga wone o pa‑o, ye ŋweeno ná tu o ŋɔ sɔŋɔ kom, ba ná jaane ŋweeno wom, o jege se o ŋwe kolo o na ŋɔge to kuni belei mo. 8Se ba ná wo jaane ŋweeno wom, wolo ya na jege o dwoŋi wom wonnu tem o nii to wó vo Wɛ wara-jei sem mo se nakwa bam bwei‑o ba lɔre, wonto mo ŋɔge naa ko dae wonto.
9Nɔɔna balei ná mage ni-kantɔgɔ woŋo dedoa ŋwaane, ko ná ye nabea, naa bonaga, naa pia, naa gɔrɔ, naa woŋo kolo maama, se ba vo ba jeeri Wɛ wara-jei sem ne. Nakwa bam laam wó bere wolo na gɛ bora to, se konto tu ŋwe o na to kolo baŋa ne to o pa wodwoŋi wom kuni belei.
10Nɔɔno ná kwei o bonaga, naa o nabea, naa o pia, naa o varem dwi delo maama o pa o dwoŋi se o taa nii o pa‑o, ye varem wom ná tega, naa o ná nɛ zonne, naa o ná jei, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ná tera se o na kolo na ke to, 11wolo ba na kwei varem wom ba ke o jeŋa ne to mo wó vo wara-jei sem o pwooli Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne we wonto wo pɛ se varem wom chɔge. Varem wom tu de nam jege se o sɛ konto mo, se o dwoŋi wom yé ŋwe kolokolo. 12Ko daare, nɔɔna ná ŋɔge varem wom wolo na nii-ko to tei ne, wolo na nii-ko to jege se o ŋwe ko jene dem mo. 13Kago-varem nam ná jaane varem wom o tore tore, se wolo na nii varem wom baŋa ne to ja ko yera yam na tore to o ba o bere varem wom tu. Konto mo ye maana se o yé ŋwe kolokolo.
14Nɔɔno ná jene varem o dwoŋi tei ne, ye varem wom ná tega, naa o ná nɛ zonne, varem wom tu ná tera se o na, wolo na jene varem wom to mo wó jwoori o ŋwe varem wom tu. 15Ko daare varem wom tu ná nɛ kolo na ke to, nɔɔno wolo na jene varem wom to daa bá ŋwe kolokolo. Kokuri to, o na jene varem wom to, o jene dem ti.
Kɔgɔ wo zoorem
16Bukɔ ná yeiri baaro ye nɔɔno ná gane‑o o lage, kotu nam wó yɔɔre o ke bukɔ wom kadiri mo se o daare o taa tei‑o. 17Bukɔ wom kwo nam ná ve se o pa nɔɔno wom o bukɔ se o ji o kaane, wolo na ke‑o puga kam to ta wó ŋwe kolo maama na ye bukwa kwaga wonnu to mo o pa kwo wom.
18Kaane ná ye yi-naro, á jege se á go‑o mo.
19Wolo ná peini de varem, se á go‑o.
20Wolo ná zuli wɛ-gaa ye ko dae Baŋa Wɛ yerane, se á yɔɔre á chɔge kotu.
21Yé daane-na veira, á nam yé bɛɛse-ba. Guli-na we abam de déem ye veira mo Ejipti tega baŋa ne.
22Yé pa-na se ko zo kadeim yera, naa botaro yera. 23Abam ná yaare-ba pa se ba keeri ba jare-ne, amo wó cheigi ba keira kam. 24A bane maa wó zaŋe abam baŋa ne, ye a daare a go abam de se-zɔɔ mo. Konto maa wó pa se á kaana bam ji kadeina, ye á bia bam de ji botara.
25Amo nɔɔna bam wone, nmo ná jene sabu n pa wolo na ye nabwom to, se n yé ke sabu-leinna kikia de kotu. Yé pa se o ŋwe sabu-daŋɔ o pa‑m. 26Nɔɔno nam ná kwei o gɔrɔ o ma tiŋi daare n tei ne, se n yeini n kwei-ko n pa‑o dɛ maama dedaan-ni maŋa ne. 27O ná lage o peini tete ne, gɔrɔ kom konto yerane mo o yeini o jega se o taa mae o kwoli o tete. O nam ná keeri o jare-ne, amo wó cheigi o keira kam. Kokuri to, amo tiini a duri nɔɔna yibwona mo.
28Yé ŋɔɔne Wɛ n ja n chɔge. Nam yé sɔɔle lwarem n yage wolo na ye nakwe tu to yuu ne.
29Kolo na maŋe se n pɔɔre n wodiiru tem wone n pa amo to, ko ná ye mena, naa wo-nyɔɔro tem, se n yé ve se n ke konto.
Nam kwei-na á bakeiri-kwe sem á pa amo. 30Ko ta woli da, wo-kwe selo na nwoŋi á naane dem wone, de á pei sem wone to ye se á pa-ne mo. Vare-kwe selo na ye wo-bɛ to wó maŋe se niina tei ne mo da yarepɛ. Da nana kam dɛ ne, á maa wó pɔɔre-se á pa-ne.
31Abam maŋe se á ji nɔɔna balo na pwɛ ba tete ba pa amo to mo. Mo kokuri, á ba jege se á di nɔna yalo ga-vara na jaane ba tore tore to. Kwei-na nɔna yam konto á pa kukuri.

english_text:
Equal Justice for All
The Lord said:
1 Don't spread harmful rumors or help a criminal by giving false evidence.
2Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice. 3 And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
4 If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
5If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
6 Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court. 7Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
8Don't accept bribes. Judges are blinded and justice is twisted by bribes.
9 Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like.
Laws for the Sabbath
The Lord said:
10 Plant and harvest your crops for six years, 11but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
12 Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
13Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names.
Three Annual Festivals
(Exodus 34.18-26; Deuteronomy 16.1-17)
The Lord said:
14Celebrate three festivals each year in my honor.
15 Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
16 Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
17Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
18Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
19 Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
A Promise and a Warning
The Lord said:
20I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you. 21Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion. 22If you faithfully obey him, I will be a fierce enemy of your enemies. 23My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out. 24Don't worship their gods or follow their customs. Instead, destroy their idols and shatter their stone images.
25Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong. 26Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
27I will terrify those nations and make your enemies so confused that they will run from you. 28I will make the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites panic as you approach. 29But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere. 30Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
31I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land. 32But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods. 33Don't let them stay in your land. They will trap you into sinning against me and worshiping their gods.
translation_text:
Ka-taa-jege-chega taane
1Yé zaŋe n pa vwa taane jage. Nam yé bore vwa bora n woli nɔn-balɔrɔ.
2Yé tɔge kɔgɔ kom se n sɛ keim-lwanno totoŋa. Taane ná wora ye n jege maana, se n yé kweele chega kam, nɔɔna dedɛ ná maŋe ba fɔ vwa tei maama de. 3Yé pa nɔɔno di bora o na ye yiniga tu to ŋwaane.
4Nmo ná beeri n yi n dono nabea, naa o bonaga, se n ja-ka n jwoori n vo n pa ka tu. 5Nmo ná nɛ we n dono bonaga zela dum pane-ka tega ne, yé gaale n kɛ. Woli-ka se ka zaŋe wɛɛne.
6Yiniga tu ná jege taane, se n yé kweele o chega kam. 7Yé zaŋe n fɔ vwa n pa nɔɔno se n ma n de‑o taane dim baŋa ne. Nɔɔno ná jege chega, se n yé go‑o. Nmo ná ke konto dwoŋi, a bá ma a chɛ‑m. 8Yé sɛ se n jwoŋi dim bora borem ŋwaane. Keim dem konto yeini de dwei dedɛɛra yia mo pa se chega ba tɛa. Nɔn-ŋona de maa gugwoli ba ni taane.
9Ko dae se á yaare veira, kolo ŋwaane abam de déem ye veira mo Ejipti teo ne, ye á yei ŋwea kam konto na ye tei to.
Ka-toŋe-ka-daare chullu
Chullu 25:1-7
10Kwei-na bena yaredo maama á du wodiiru á kare ne se á ta‑á zage-te. 11Bene delo maama na wó ke yarepɛ to, se á yage á kare se se taa tigi da kafɛ. Bene dem konto ne, yiniga tiina balo na zoore á tetare ne to laam wó zo se wo ba lare wodiiru tem ba di. Ba ma ná daare kolo, se á yage-na se kago-vara de zo ba di. Ta ke-na konto dwoŋi de kare selo á na jeiri Vini teeni de Olivi teeni se wone to de.
12Abam jege da yaredo mo se á ma á toŋe. Da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, yé toŋe-na kɔtaa! Konto wó pa á na siu, de á nabɛ, de á bonɛ, de á kabɛ, dedaane veira balo na zoore á tetare ne to. Konto wó taa pae á jege dam.
13Yɔɔre á ta‑á ke á tɔge a na bere abam tei maama to. Yé zuli-na wɛ dedwoŋi, ye ko dae amo. Yé bwoŋi-na wɛ dedwoŋi naa jwoni dedwoŋi yere.
Bene maama wo kura yatɔ
14Bene maama wone abam jege se á yeini á di kuri kuni betɔ mo se á ma‑á zuli amo:
15Bene maama Abibi chana kam da yadwonna wone, se á di Bworobworo-memene kuri dem. Kwei-na da yarepɛ á di bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to. Kanto chana kam ne mo á déem nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne. Á na yeini á zuli amo konto to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé ba amo yiga ne ye o ba zei kaanem pɛɛre.
16Mena zagem maŋa nam ná yia, se á di Ga-kwea kuri dem. Kwei-na mena yalo á na dɛ yiga á zage to, á ba á pa-ne.
Ko woli da, abam ná yeini á toŋe á kare totoŋa maama á ti, se á laam di Faao kuri dem.
17Kuni betɔ bene maama wone á baara bam jege se ba jeeri amo wolo na ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom to yiga ne mo konto dwoŋi.
18Abam ná lage á go varem se á ma o jana bam á ke kaanem á pa amo, se á yé woli bworobworo kolo na jege sabɔle ko wone to. Nam lɔre-na se á zwɛ varem wom lara kam maama dɛ dem konto ne. 19Bene maama wone se á ja á kare wodiiru telo na lwoori yiga te ke ye te lamma to á ja á jeeri abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé kwei bebala de ka nu nayela o saŋe mini wone.
Baŋa Wɛ bera
20Nii-na! Amo lage a toŋe amo maleka mo se ka che abam ka ja ka yi jei selo amo na kwɛ se a pa abam to. 21Ta‑á nege-na maleka kam se á daare á sɛ ka taane dem maama. Amo pɛ-ka dam se ka taa toŋe amo totoŋa. Abam wolo ná ve-ka, ka bá yage ka ma chɛ kotu. 22Abam nam ná sɛ ka ni ye á daare á ke a na we á ke tei to chekke, amo laam wó sɛ se abam dona taa ye amo dona, se a daare a chuli balo na zege abam zega to. 23Ko ná ye Amori tiina bam, de Hiti tiina bam, de Pɛrizi tiina bam, de Kanaan tiina bam, de Hivi tiina bam dedaane Jebusi tiina bam, amo maleka kam wó ja abam se á zo ba tega kam á jwoŋi, ye a daare a chɔge-ba pa se ba jei. 24Abam nam ná yi-da, yé tɔge á tiiri teene dem konto jwona yam yiga ne á zuli-ya. Nam yé lwoni-na ba totoŋ-balwaaro tem. Chɔge-na ba jwona yam dedaane kandwa yalo ba na chwi ya ŋwaane to.
25Ta‑á zuli-na amo na ye á Teiru Baŋa Wɛ to yerane. Abam ná ke konto, amo wó ke zaane a yage á wodiu dedaane á na baŋa ne. Amo wó taa cho se jaweero yé ja abam. 26Abam kaana bam de wone, ba wolowolo bá ja puga se ka chɔge. Kadega maa bá taa wora. Á maama ŋwea maa wó tiini ka dáane lanyerane.
27Amo wó pa se foone tiini de ja balo maama abam na wó jeeri to, pa se vuvuga to ba tetare ne. Amo wó pa se á dona maama pipiri ba duri ba daare abam. 28Amo ta wó pa se keilimuni taa tɔge á yiga ye se daare se zeili Hivi tiina bam, de Kanaan tiina bam, de Hiti tiina bam na chege abam chwoŋa to. 29A nam bá zeili ba maama abam yiga ne bene dedoa wone. Amo ná ke konto, tega kam wó ji kagoa yerane mo. Ko wó pa kago-vara tiini ba gaale se ba daane abam. 30A lage a taa zeili-ba fenfee mo se ba nwoŋi abam yiga ne, se ko yi maŋa kalo abam na wó puli á su logo kom maama to. 31Abam tega kam laŋa wó zege Nane-soŋo kom ni ne mo se ka taa vei Mediterania naneo kom seeni. Ka ta maa wó zege kagoa kam seeni ka vo ka yi Yuferata buga kam ne. Ko ná ye balo na zoore jei sem konto ne leile to, amo wó ke-ba abam dam kuri ne. Abam maa wó zeili-ba se ba nwoŋi á yiga ne.
32Yé ke-na ni-sɛɛm de-ba. Nam yé sɛ-na ba jwona yam. 33Bere á yé sɛ se banto taa zoore abam tega kam baŋa ne. Kolo ŋwaane, ba wó soge abam mo se á tusi amo yiga ne, ye ba ja abam se á zuli ba jwona yam.

english_text:
The People Agree To Obey God
1The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and 70 of Israel's leaders. They must worship me at a distance, 2but you are to come near. Don't let anyone else come up.”
3Moses gave the Lord's instructions to the people, and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded!” 4Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said.
The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel. 5He also sent some young men to burn offerings and to sacrifice bulls as special offerings to the Lord. 6Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar. 7Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
8 Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
9Moses and Aaron, together with Nadab and Abihu and the 70 leaders, went up the mountain 10and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something that looked like a pavement made out of sapphire, and it was as bright as the sky.
11Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank.
Moses on Mount Sinai
12The Lord said to Moses, “Come up on the mountain and stay here for a while. I will give you the two flat stones on which I have written the laws that my people must obey.” 13Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
14Moses had told the leaders, “Wait here until we come back. Aaron and Hur will be with you, and they can settle any arguments while we are away.”
15When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it, 16and the bright glory of the Lord came down and stayed there. The cloud covered the mountain for six days, and on the seventh day the Lord told Moses to come into the cloud. 17-18 Moses did so and stayed there 40 days and nights. To the people, the Lord's glory looked like a blazing fire on top of the mountain.
translation_text:
Ba fɔge ba sɛ Wɛ ni-gwonim dem
1 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we:
“Diini peo kom yuu se n ba amo tei. Nam ja Aron, de Nadab, de Abihu dedaane Isarele nakwa fuserepɛ n woli da. Abam ta ná wo yiga yiga, se á tiiri á zuli-ne. 2Nmo yerane mo wó wane n fɔɔre n yi amo yiga. Ko daare Isarele nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama ba jege se ba di peo kom yuu.”
3Moses déem ma tu o maŋe Baŋa Wɛ nia yam de o chullu tem maama o bere nɔɔna bam. Ba maama ma leiri de kwora dedoa ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ na we debam ke kolo maama to, dé wó ke.” 4Moses ma popone Baŋa Wɛ taane dem maama o tiŋi.
Tega na poore to, o ma lɔ kaanem bimbini peo kom teiŋa ne. O déem ta ma kwei kandwa fuga-yalei o chwi, se kandwɛ maama taa zege de pae Isarele dwia fuga-yalei yam. 5O ma toŋe Isarele tiina nɔn-donno tedwonna mo se ba kwei vara ba ma ke kaanem ba zwɛ ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ba ma daare ba kwei nabɛ-pɔle ba ma ke yazura kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. 6Moses déem ma pwori vara bam jana o ke zwe wone. O laam ma kwei jana balo na daare to o miisi o yage kaanem bimbini dem yera ne. 7O ma daare o kwei Wɛ Ni-gwonim tɔnɔ kom o ga o bere nɔɔna bam. Ba maama daa maa leiri ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ na we debam ke kolo maama to, dé wó ke. Dé wó sɛ o ni dem.”
8Moses laam ma kwei jana balo na wo zwe sem wone to, o miisi-ba o yage nɔɔna bam yera ne ye o we, “Jana banto mo bere we, ni-gwonim delo Baŋa Wɛ na ke de abam bera yanto baŋa ne to jege bu.”
9Moses ma ja Aron, de Nadab de Abihu dedaane Isarele nakwa fuserepɛ ye ba di peo kom yuu. 10Dáane mo ba déem nɛ Isarele tiina Wɛ wom. O nɛ sem kuri ne ko nye de pwola mo tiini ka peere ne Safira to, ka ta ye napwon-pwoŋo mo nenɛɛne wɛyuu kom. 11Isarele yiga tiina bam déem nɛ Baŋa Wɛ konto, ye o wo chɔge-ba. Ba ma di ye ba daare ba nyɔ dáane.
12 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Diini n ba amo tei peo kom yuu ne. Nmo wó maŋe ywo-seeni mo se a kwei kandwa-pelɛ selo baŋa ne a na popone a bera yam de a nia yam se a nɔɔna bam taa tɔge to a pa‑m.”
13Moses ma zaŋe dedaane o zeinnu Josua se ba ti ba yiga ba nwoŋi. Moses laam ma di peo kom yuu se o jeeri Baŋa Wɛ. 14O nam ya wuuri o ta de nakwa bam mo o we, “Abam maŋe-na ywo-seeni á ta‑á cheigi debam se dé jwoori dé ba. Aron de Hura wó maŋe á tei ne se wolo maama ná jege ni-kantɔgɔ de o dwoŋi, se ba kwɛ-ko ba pa abam.”
15Moses déem na diini Sinayi peo kom yuu to, kunkwoŋo ma kwoli-ko. 16-17Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kolo na nyeene to ma tu ko jeini peo kom yuu ne. Isarele tiina bam na nii ba na Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom konto to, ko nye de mini mo na di bugi-bugi peo kom yuu ne. Kunkwoŋo kom ma kwoli peo kom da yaredo. Da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma bwoŋi Moses se o ba o tei. 18Moses déem ma seene o di peo kom yuu o zo kunkwoŋo kom wone. O ma maŋe dáane da finna wea de tete maama.

english_text:
The Sacred Tent
(Exodus 35.4-9)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Tell everyone in Israel who wants to give gifts that they must bring them to you. 3Here is a list of what you are to collect: Gold, silver, and bronze; 4blue, purple, and red wool; fine linen; goat hair; 5tanned ram skins; fine leather; acacia wood; 6olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices to mix with the incense and with the oil for dedicating the tent and ordaining the priests; 7and onyx stones and other gems for the sacred vest and the breastpiece. 8I also want them to build a special place where I can live among my people. 9Make it and its furnishings exactly like the pattern I will show you.
The Sacred Chest
(Exodus 37.1-9)
The Lord said to Moses:
10Tell the people to build a chest of acacia wood 110 centimeters long, 66 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 11Cover it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the lid. 12Make four gold rings and attach one of them to each of the four legs of the chest. 13Make two poles of acacia wood. Cover them with gold 14and put them through the rings, so the chest can be carried by the poles. 15Don't ever remove the poles from the rings. 16When I give you the Ten Commandments written on two flat stones, put them inside the chest.
17 Make the lid of the chest out of pure gold. 18-19Then hammer out two winged creatures of pure gold and fasten them to the lid at the ends of the chest. 20The creatures must face each other with their wings spread over the chest. 21Inside it place the two flat stones with the Ten Commandments on them and put the gold lid on top of the chest. 22I will meet you there between the two creatures and tell you what my people must do and what they must not do.
The Table for the Sacred Bread
(Exodus 37.10-16)
The Lord said:
23Make a table of acacia wood 88 centimeters long, 44 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 24-25Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border 75 millimeters thick. 26Make four gold rings and attach one to each of the legs 27-28near the edging. The poles for carrying the table are to be placed through these rings and are to be made of acacia wood covered with gold. 29-30 The table is to be kept in the holy place, and the sacred loaves of bread must always be on it. All bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings are to be made of pure gold and set on this table.
The Lampstand
(Exodus 37.17-24)
The Lord said:
31Make a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered gold 32with three branches on each of its two sides. 33There are to be three decorative almond blossoms on each branch 34and four on the stem. 35There must also be a blossom where each pair of branches comes out from the stem. 36The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold. 37The lamp on the top and those at the end of each of its six branches must be made so as to shine toward the front of the lampstand. 38The tongs and trays for taking care of the lamps are to be made of pure gold. 39The lampstand and its equipment will require 35 kilograms of pure gold, 40 and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
translation_text:
Wɛ wara-vwei dem taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we:
2“Ta n bere Isarele tiina bam se ba ja pɛɛra ba ba ba pa-ne. Nmo nam mo wó jwoŋi-ya se ko tɔge de nɔɔno maama boboŋa na jaane se o pa tei to. 3Nam jwoŋi pɛɛra yanto dwi ba tei ne:
Sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de channa, 4de gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to, de gare-fefale, dedaane boŋo koro, 5de pi-bea twanno telo ba na seini to, de twan-nyenno, de golesaa dɛ, 6de min-zwonnu nuga, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa kalo ba na wó ma ba ke Wɛ swolim nuga kam to, de kalo ba na wó zwɛ wara-vwei dem totoŋa ŋwaane to, 7de Onika kandwa, de kandwa-nyenno ya dwi ya dwi, se ba ke-ya kaanem nakwe tu wom gare-wogo kom ne, ba daare ba ke yadwonna o gare-pale dem yera ne.
8Amo lage se a nɔɔna bam chwi wara-diga mo ba pa-ne, se a taa zoore ba tetare ne. 9Wara-vwei dem á na wó chwi to, dedaane de wo wonnu maama jege se te maŋe de amo na wó bere‑m tei to mo.
Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam
10Pa se nɔɔna bam kwei golesaa dɛ ba ma ke dakaa. Ka wó taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni belei de chichworo mo dedɔrem baŋa ne. Kayɔlɔ baŋa maa wó taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem dedoa de chichworo. Ka baŋa seeni de maa wó taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem dedoa de chichworo. 11Pa ba kwei sabu-seŋa na tiini ka ye chekke to ba ma kwoli ka yiga de ka kwaga maama, se sabu-seŋa tɔge ka nia yam maama. 12Kwei-na sabu-seŋa á ma á mɔ kwana yana se á kwei ya dedoa dedoa á lei dakaa kam nɛ sena maama yera ne. Kwana yalei wó ke dakaa kam saŋa dedoa ne, yalei maa wó ke saŋa kadwoŋi ne. 13Ba ta wó gwoni golesaa dɛ selei ba daare ba kwei sabu-seŋa ba kwoli dɛ sem konto maama. 14Laam pa se ba kwei dɛ sem ba tore dakaa kam kwana yam wone, se ba daare ba ja dɛ sem ba ma zeŋe dakaa kam. 15Maŋa maama dɛ sem konto wó maŋe kwana yam ne mo. Ba ba jege se ba daa le-se.
16Amo ná pɛ‑m amo ni-gwonim kandwa yalei yam, se n kwei-ya n ke dakaa kam wone.
17Kwei-na sabu-seŋa kalo na tiini ka ye chekke to á ma á ke wɛleera saarem ni-pugu se ko pu dakaa kam. Ka dedɔrɔ baŋa nam wó taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem belei de chichworo mo, se kayɔlɔ baŋa taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem dedoa de chichworo. 18-19Nam kwei-na sabu-seŋa á ma á mɔ wonnu telei na nye de malese ye ba bwoi-ba we cherubi to. Pa se cherubi selei sem meeli se taa zege ni-pugu kom dɛ selei sem ne. Kwei-na sabu-seŋa kandwɛ-dale dedwe á mage-de á ke cherubi sem dedaane ni-pugu kom tete. 20Cherubi sem wó jeeri daane mo, ye se yibia chɔɔle tega ne se se taa nii dakaa kam ni-pugu kom seeni. Se vɔna de maa wó yarege wɛɛne, ye se laam kwaare se vɔna yam daane se ma-ya se kwoli ni-pugu kom. 21Laam kwei-na amo ni-gwonim kandwa yalei yam á ke dakaa kam wone, se á daare á kwei ni-pugu kom á pu ka ni. 22Amo wó taa tui ni-gwonim dakaa kam baŋa seeni a jeeri‑m cherubi selei sem tetare laŋa ne. Dáane mo amo wó bere‑m a nia yam maama se Isarele tiina bam taa tɔge-ya.
Tabolo Kom
23Ta kwei-na golesaa dɛ á ma á ke tabolo. Ko dedɔrem baŋa maŋem wó taa ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni belei mo, se kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem dem taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem bedwe. Nam pa-na se tabolo kom wɛ-baŋa seeni maŋem taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem dedoa de chichworo. 24Kwei-na sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to á kwoli ko yiga de ko kwaga maama, se á daare á pa sabu-seŋa kam tɔge ko nia yam. 25Sabu-seŋa kam na wó tɔge tabolo kom nia yam to wó taa ye da-yiga noa maŋem mo. 26Nam mɔ-na sabu-seŋa kwana yana á meeli tabolo kom nɛ sena sem na wo mɛ to. 27Kwana yam wó meeli ya taa bwola de tabolo kom nia yam mo, se dɛ selo ba na wó taa mae ba zeŋe tabolo kom to tore ya wone. 28Ko nam wó taa ye golesaa dɛ mo nmo wó kwoli de sabu-seŋa, se ba taa maa zeŋe-ko. 29Nam ta kwei-na sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to á ma á ke zon-tanlɛ, de zwe dwi dwi, de kabeili, de kambi selo na wó taa toŋe sana-pɛɛra kaanem totoŋa to. 30Tabolo kom wó taa wo amo wara-jei di-yuu kom ne mo maŋa maama, ye bworobworo kolo na ye ko yera ko tigi amo yiga ne to taa wo ko baŋa ne.
Min-zwon-zego kom
31Kwei-na sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to á ma á ke woŋo kolo min-zwonnu na wó taa zege ko baŋa ne to. Ma-na sabu-seŋa kandwɛ-dale dedwe á mage se á mɔ ko kuri, de ko daa kam, de zwe selo min-zwonnu tem na wó zege se wone to. Zwe sem wó taa nye de pun-kogela mo. 32Laam ke nɛ seredo se se nwoŋi daa kam yera ne. Nɛ setɔ wó taa wo jazem baŋa ne se setɔ taa wo jagwia baŋa ne. 33Nenɔŋa punnu tetɔ mo wó taa wo naga maama ne, se te taa nye de Aamonda pun-kogela de te vɔɔro. Nɛ seredo sem maama wó taa ye konto mo. 34Ko daa kam tete wó taa jege nenɔŋa punnu tena mo na nye de Aamonda pun-kogela de te vɔɔro to. 35Pun-kogele dedwe maama na wo daa kam yera ne to wó teili nɛ selei selo maama na jeeri daane ka yera ne to. Konto to, pun-kogela yatɔ mo wó teili nɛ seredo sem. 36Pun-kogela yam, de nɛ seredo sem, de daa kam tete maama ye se ba mage sabu-seŋa kandwɛ-dale dedwe mo ba ma ke-te.
37Nam pa se ba ke min-zwonnu terepɛ se te taa zege nɛ seredo sem yuni ne de daa kam yuu ne. Kwei-na-te á zege se te taa di te pae pwooni min-zwon-zego kom yiga seeni. 38Á ta wó kwei sabu-seŋa kam na ye chekke to á ma á ke wonnu telo na wó fɔge te kwɛ mini dem to, dedaane zon-tanlɛ selo ba na wó taa mae ba pɛ tentwarem dem to. 39Kwei-na sabu-seŋa kalo dunni na maŋe de kilo fintɔ-tenu ye ka ye chekke to á ke min-zwon-zego kom de ko zela yam dwi dwi. 40Nam pa se ba ke woŋo maama se ko maŋe de tetei amo na bere‑m peo kom yuu ne to.”

english_text:
Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.8-19)
The Lord said to Moses:
1The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. 2Make each piece twelve meters long and two meters wide 3and sew them together into two panels with five sections each. 4-6Put 50 loops of blue cloth along one of the wider sides of each panel, then fasten the two panels at the loops with 50 gold hooks.
7-8As the material for protecting the tent, use goat hair to weave eleven sections of cloth 13 meters by 2 meters each. 9Sew five of the sections together to make one panel. Then sew the other six together to make a second panel, and fold the sixth section double over the front of the tent. 10Put 50 loops along one of the wider sides of each panel 11and fasten the two panels at the loops with 50 bronze hooks. 12-13The panel of goat hair will be a meter longer than the tent itself, so fold 50 centimeters of the material behind the tent and on each side as a protective covering. 14Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather.
The Framework for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.20-34)
The Lord said:
15Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent. 16Make each frame 4 meters high and 66 centimeters wide 17with two wooden pegs near the bottom. 18-21Place two silver stands under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so the frames can be joined together. Put 20 of these frames along the south side and 20 more along the north. 22For the back wall along the west side use six frames 23-24with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom. 25Altogether, this back wall will have eight frames with two silver stands under each one.
26-27Make five crossbars for each of the wooden frames, 28with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall. 29Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold and attach gold rings to the frames to run the crossbars through. 30Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain.
The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.35-38)
The Lord said:
31-33 Make a curtain to separate the holy place from the most holy place. Use fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Cover four acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a silver stand. Then fasten gold hooks to the posts and hang the curtain there.
34Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid. 35Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
36For the entrance to the tent, use a piece of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework. 37Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ wara-vwei dem taane
1“Nam pa se ba kwei gare-jale-laaro fuga na nwoŋi gare-fefale delo na ye chekke to ba ma ke wara-vwei dem. Kwei-na gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to á ma‑á sɔ-ya. Á maa wó daare á gɔgere cherubi nyenyero á ke gare-jala yam yera ne. 2Gare-jale dedwe dedɔrem baŋa maŋem wó taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finlei-nana mo. De kayɔlɔ baŋa maa wó taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni bena. Gare-jala fuga kam maama jege se ya taa mae daane mo. 3Laam twoŋi-na gare-jala yanu á ke daane, se ya ji gare-pum dedoa. Ta ke-na konto de gare-jala yanu yadwonna yam. 4Nam kwei-na gare-yi delo nyenyego na ye nazwon-pupwia to á ma‑á ke kuna á lei gare-pum ni-dedɔrɔ kom seeni. Á wó ke konto mo gare-pum dedwoŋi dem ne. 5Kuna finnu mo á wó ke gare-puna yalei nia dedwaaro tem na jeeri daane to yera ne. 6Á ta wó ke sabu-seŋa gwoli finnu mo se se ja gare-puna yalei yam se ke daane. Konto mo wó pa se wara-vwei dem taa ye woŋo dedoo.
7Ta pa se ba kwei boŋo koro ba sɔ gare-jala se ba ma-ya ba pu wara-vwei dem yuu kom seeni. Ya maama wó ke daane se ya taa ye fuga-dedoa mo. 8Ya maama maa wó taa ma daane mo. Maŋe-na ya dedɔrem baŋa ne se ko taa ye nenɛɛne jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fintɔ. Kayɔlɔ baŋa maa wó taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni bena. 9Laam kwei-na gare-jala yanu á twoŋi daane se ya ji gare-pum. Á ta wó kwei gare-jala yaredo yam na daare to mo á twoŋi daane se ya de ji gare-pum. Abam maa wó piri gare-jala yaredo tu wom belei á jeeri wɛɛne se ko maŋe de wara-vwei dem ni seeni. 10Ke-na kuna finnu á lei gare-pum ni-dedɔrɔ kom seeni, se á daare á ke konto gare-pum dedwoŋi dem ne. 11Nam ta kwei-na channa á ma á ke gwoli finnu selo na wó twoŋi gare-puna yalei yam daane se ya ji gɔrɔ dedoa to. 12Abam maa wó yage boŋo koro gare-jale dem se de daa dedoa daare wara-jei sem kwaga ne. 13Boŋo koro gare-jale dem maa wó li wara-vwei dem dedɔrem seeni se ko dwoni gare-jale dedwoŋi dem se ko maŋe de jatwogo de noa ni maŋem bedwe mo. 14Daa‑n ta pa se ba pwoni pi-bɛ tankwallo ba daare ba seini-te nasoŋo se ba maa kwoli wara-vwei dem. Kwei-na twan-nyenno á daŋe boboa twanno tem baŋa ne.
15Pa se ba beeri golesaa ywoa yalo na zege cheppe to, se ba kwei-se ba ke wara-vwei dem. 16Ywei maama dedɔrem baŋa maŋem wó taa ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni fuga mo, se de kayɔlɔ baŋa seeni taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem dedoa de chichworo. 17Abam maa wó sare nwa balei ywei maama yera ne. Konto wó pa se ywei maama wane de twoŋi dedaane dedwoŋi na saŋe-de to. Nam ke-na dɛ sem maama konto. 18Ywoa finlei mo wó zege se ko maŋe de wara-vwei dem tega-kuri seeni saŋa kam. 19Nam kwei-na lu-nyenno á ma á ke wonnu telo dɛ sem na wó zege te baŋa ne to finna. Luuru telei wó taa teili ywei maama. Te wó taa jege chwiim jei selei mo se ywei nwa bam wane ba zege se wone. 20Ke-na konto se ko maŋe de wara-vwei dem baŋa seeni saŋa kam, se ywoa finlei taa zege da. 21Lu-nyenno wonnu finna mo á wó ke se ywoa yam taa zege te baŋa ne. Wonnu telei maa wó taa wora ywei maama ŋwaane. 22Ko ná ye saŋa kalo na wo bira-kwaga ne ye ka jeeri wɛ-zoore seeni to, se á chwi ywoa yaredo dáane. 23Nam ta woli-na ywoa yalei se á chwi-ya vwei dem kwaga saŋa kam gugworru telei tem ne. 24Abam maa wó twoŋi gugworru ywoa yam konto se ya meeli daane. Ko wó zege tega kam ne mo ko meeli se ko taa diini baŋa kam mɛ sabu-seŋa kwane dem na leigi da to. 25Bira-kwaga kam seeni ywoa yam laam maa wó taa ye nana mo, ye ya laam jege lu-nyenno wonnu fuga-teredo telo na wó teili-ya to.
26-27Ta pa se ba kwei golesaa dɛ se ba ma-se ba gare wara-vwei dem sɛ sem maama. Dɛ senu mo wó gare ywoa yam na wo saŋa kalo maama ne to, se ya ja daane chekke. Tega-kuri seeni saŋa kam, de baŋa seeni saŋa kam de bira-kwaga seeni saŋa kam mo konto. 28Ko daare, tetare dagara kam wó tole ka zege saŋa kam daa dedoa ne ka vo ka yi daa kadwoŋi kam ne, ka twoŋi ywoa yam maama ka ke daane. 29Laam kwei-na sabu-seŋa á kwoli ywoa yam, se á daare á ma á ke kwana á meeli ywoa yam yera ne se dagare sem taa tore ya wone. Dagare sem de ye se á taare-se de sabu-seŋa mo.
30Laam pa se ba chwi wara-vwei dem se de zege ne amo na bere‑m tetei peo kom yuu ne to.
Wɛ di-yun-gala gare-jale dem
31-33Abam ta ke-na gare-jale delo na wó lei de pwɛ Wɛ di-yuu kom de di-yun-gala kam daane to se popɔra taa wora. Kwei-na gare-fefale delo na ye chekke to á ma á ke gare-jale dem konto. Abam wó kwei gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to mo á ma‑á sɔ-de. Á maa wó daare á gɔgere cherubi nyenyero á ke gare-jale dem yera ne. Nam kwei-na golesaa dɛ sena á kwoli-se de sabu-seŋa, ye á daare á ke sabu-seŋa gwoli á meeli se yera ne. Laam kwei-na-se á chwi lu-nyenno wonnu tena tem baŋa ne. Abam ná ke konto, se á kwei gare-jale dem á lei gwoli sem yera ne pa se de che de kwoli Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam. 34Nam ta kwei-na wɛleera saarem ni-pugu kom á ma pu ni-gwonim dakaa kam na zege Wɛ di-yun-gala kam ne to. 35Yiga diga kam na ye Wɛ di-yuu kom to mo á wó zege tabolo kom se ko taa wo vwei dem jagwia saŋa kam seeni. Min-zwon-zego kom maa wó taa wo vwei dem jazem saŋa kam seeni.
36Ko nam ná ye vwei dem ni, se á ke tento: Kwei-na gare-fefale selo na ye chekke to de gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to á ma‑á sɔ gare-jale delo na wó lei ni dem ne to. Á ta wó daare á gɔgere nyenyero gare-jale dem yera ne. 37Abam ná sɔge gare-jale dem konto, á laam wó kwei golesaa dɛ senu á taare-se de sabu-seŋa ye á daare á ke sabu-seŋa gwoli á meeli se yera ne. Laam mɔ-na channa wonnu tenu se á chwi dɛ sem te baŋa ne, ye á daare á lei gare-jale dem da.”

english_text:
The Altar for Offering Sacrifices
(Exodus 38.1-7)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Use acacia wood to build an altar 2.25 meters square and 1.34 meters high, 2and make each of the four top corners stick up like the horn of a bull. Then cover the whole altar with bronze, including the four horns. 3All the equipment for the altar must also be made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4-5Halfway up the altar build a ledge around it, and cover the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. Then attach a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners of the altar. 6-7Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar. 8Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 38.9-20)
The Lord said:
9-15Surround the sacred tent with a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. Use 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods.
Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts. 16Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
17-18Make the curtains that surround the courtyard 2.25 meters high and hang them from the bronze posts with silver hooks and rods. 19Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard.
The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place
(Leviticus 24.1-4)
The Lord said to Moses:
