Konto ná kea, Wɛ wó yage o wɛleera o ma chɛ‑o. 29Ni dento zege de pae wolo maama na tusi ye o wo paale o ke to mo, kotu ná ye Isarele tu naa veiru de.
30Wolo maama nam ná zeiŋi o tete ye o paale o ke wɛleere, konto tu ná ye Isarele tu naa veiru mo de, ba jege se ba le‑o se o daa yé tɔge o woli Isarele dwi dem wone, o na yaale Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane. 31O na ke tei to bere we o gwooni Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam ye o ta daare o chɔge o nia yam. O wɛleera yam wó taa wo o yuu ne. Á jege se á yɔɔre á le‑o se o daa yé tɔge o woli a nɔɔna bam wone.”
Siu dɛ chullu tem chɔgem taane
32Isarele tiina bam déem ta na wo kagoa kam wone ba kare ba vei to, mo dɛ dedwe ba jaane nɔɔno na wora o puuri dɛ Wɛ siu dɛ dem ne. 33Ba ma ja‑o ba vo ba yi Moses de Aron de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama tei. 34Ba ma pe‑o se ba cheigi ba nii, ba na yeiri ko na wó maŋe se ba ke‑o tei to ŋwaane. 35Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “O jege se o te mo. Ja-na nɔɔno wom á nwoŋi á vo dáa se Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom dole‑o de kandwa ba go.” 36Ba ma seene ba ja‑o ba vo ba dole‑o ba go, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Moses ni se ba ke tei to.
Ba gwaaro nia yam kuna taane
37 Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta de Moses o we:
38“Ta n bere Isarele tiina bam we: Á wó seere á gare-dwanno tem se zɔla taa wo te nia yana yam maama ne, se á daare á nyaane ŋone selo nyenyego na ye nazwon-pupwia to á ke zɔle maama yera ne. Á jege se á ta‑á ke á gwaaro tem konto dwoŋi mo taa wuu. 39Á wó ta‑á nii á kuna yam konto, ye á guli Baŋa Wɛ nia yam maama se á ta‑á tɔge-ya. Ko ta wó pa se abam bá ywori Wɛ kwaga ne á daare á tɔge wo-yɔɔro telo á fera na zo to. 40Konto to, á wó toŋe á tɔge amo nia yam maama. Á ta wó pɔɔre á tete á pa á Tu Wɛ wom. 41Amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. A nam jaane abam a nwoŋi Ejipti wone, se a taa ye abam Tu Wɛ wom mo. Chega to, amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_text:
Korah, Dathan, and Abiram Lead a Rebellion
1-2 Korah son of Izhar was a Levite from the Kohathite clan. One day he called together Dathan, Abiram, and On from the Reuben tribe, and the four of them decided to rebel against Moses. So they asked 250 respected Israelite leaders for their support, and together they went to Moses 3and Aaron and said, “Why do you think you're so much better than everyone else? We're part of the Lord's holy people, and he's with all of us. What makes you think you're the only ones in charge?”
4When Moses heard this, he knelt down to pray. 5Then he said to Korah and his followers:
Tomorrow morning the Lord will show us the person he has chosen to be his priest, and that man will faithfully serve him.
6-7Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
8-9You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want? 10The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest. 11You and your followers have rebelled against the Lord, not against Aaron.
12Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come! 13It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around! 14You keep promising us rich farmlands with fertile fields and vineyards—but where are they? Stop trying to trick these people. No, we won't come to see you.”
15Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
16Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent. 17Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
18The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent. 19Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders.
When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory 20and said to Moses and Aaron, 21“Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
22But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
23The Lord answered Moses, 24“Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
25Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed. 26Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.” 27So everyone moved away from those tents, except Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and their families.
28Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know: 29If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me. 30But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
31As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up 32-33and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
34The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
35Suddenly the Lord sent a fire that burned up the 250 men who had offered incense to him.
36Then the Lord said to Moses, 37“Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred, 38because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
39Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar, 40just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers.
The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
41The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
42As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent. 43So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent, 44 where the Lord said to them, 45“Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.”
They immediately bowed down and prayed. 46Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
47-48Aaron did exactly what he had been told. He ran over to the crowd of people and stood between the dead bodies and the people who were still alive. He placed the incense on the pan, then offered it to the Lord and asked him to forgive the people's sin. The disease immediately stopped spreading, and no one else died from it. 49But 14,700 Israelites were dead, not counting those who had died with Korah and his followers.
50Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.
translation_text:
Kora de Datan de Abiram chichuŋu
1Izehara bu Kora déem ye Levi dwi tu mo ye o nwoŋi Kohafe sɔ-yuu kom wone. O ma ke ni de Ruben dwi tiina badwonna se ba dwoni de Moses. Nɔɔna bam konto maa ye Eliabi bia balei Datan de Abiram, dedaane Peleti bu Ona mo. 2Ba déem dwoni de Moses, ye Isarele kɔgɔ kom yiga tiina bia yalei de finnu balo nɔɔna na nege to maa zege ba kwaga ne. 3Ba laam ma vo ba jeeri Moses de Aron, ye ba ta de-ba ba we, “Abam zeiŋi á tete á gaale ko na maŋe se á ke tei to. Á boŋe we á gare Isarele tiina bam maama mo na? Dé kɔgɔ kom wone nɔɔno maama ye Wɛ nyem mo. Baŋa Wɛ maa wo nɔɔno maama tei ne. Bɛ nam mo ye á zeiŋi á tete Baŋa Wɛ kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne?”
4Moses na nigi ba taane dem to, mo o vwi o yibia tega ne. 5O laam ma ta o bere Kora de o kwaga kɔgɔ kom o we, “Jwa tetete Baŋa Wɛ tete wó bere debam wolo o na seene o pɔɔre se o taa ye o nyem to. O ta wó pa kotu chwoŋa se o fɔɔre o twɛ o tei. Nɔɔno wolo o na seene o kuri to mo wó zege o yiga ne. 6Kora, nmo de n kɔgɔ kom maama jege se á ke tento mo: kwei-na min-chala zwe 7se á jwa ke min-chala se wone. Á ta wó kwei talwoŋ-ywoŋa á ke á woli da se á daare á vo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Baŋa Wɛ wó kuri wolo o na pɔɔre se o taa ye o nyem to. Abam Levi dwi tiina mo zeiŋi á tete á gaale!”
8Moses ta ma ta de Kora o we, “Nam cheigi-na lanyerane, abam Levi dwi tiina bam! 9Baŋa Wɛ pɔɔre abam Isarele dwi tiina bam maama wone se á ta‑á toŋe á pa‑o o wara-jei sem ne, se á daare á ta‑á zege Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom yiga ne á woli-ba Wɛ zula seeni. O na kwei totoŋe dem konto o pa abam to dae kolokolo abam tei ne na? 10O pɛ chwoŋa se nmo, Kora, de n dwonna Levi tiina badaara bam taa tui o yiga ne. Nmo nam boŋe se n ji Wɛ kaanem tu mo n woli da na? 11Chega ŋwaane to, nmo de n kwaga kɔgɔ kom na zeiŋi á tete tei to, ko ye á chiŋi jara de Baŋa Wɛ mo. Á jege Aron á ŋwaana se bɛ mo?”
12Moses ma toŋe o bwoŋi Eliabi bia, Datan de Abiram. Ba ma toŋe kwora o tei ne ba we, “Dé bá ba nmo tei! 13Nmo jaane debam n nwoŋi Ejipti te-ywoŋa kalo na lana de varem de kɔnɔ to wone n ba ywo-seeni se dé te kagoa kanto wone. Ko nam dae kolokolo nmo tei ne ye n ta boŋe se n di dam dé baŋa ne! 14Nmo ta wo pɛ se dé zo tega kalo na ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ to. N wo pɛ se dé taa tei tega se dé du wonnu ka wone, naa dé jeiri Vini teeni dé gwori de bia. Daa‑n yé boŋe se n gane nɔɔna banto. Dé bere dé ba beena n tei!”
15Moses bane ma tiini de zaŋe ye o ta de Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Yé pa n yiga taa wo nɔɔna banto pɛɛra yam wone. A wo chɔge ba yiga, a nam wo jwoŋi ba bonaga dedoa tete de.”
16Moses laam ma ta de Kora o we, “Jwa ne se nmo de n kwaga kɔgɔ kom ba á zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Abam maama de Aron wó ba á jeeri da. 17Abam nɔɔno maama wó ja o min-chala zoŋa kam de ka wo talwoŋ-ywoŋa mo o ja o jeeri se o zwɛ o pa Baŋa Wɛ. Aron de wó ke konto. Á min-chala zwe sem maama wó taa ye bia yalei de finnu mo.”
18Tega na poore to, nɔɔna bam maama ma seene ba kwei ba zwe de se wo min-chala, ye ba laam daŋe talwoŋ-ywoŋa se wone. Ba ma vo ba jeeri Moses de Aron ye ba maama zege wara-jei sem ni ne. 19Kora déem ya pɛ se Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama ba ba jeeri wara-jei sem ni ne ba zege Moses de Aron yiga ne. Ba maama na tu ba zege da konto to, Baŋa Wɛ ma veere o tete de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom o bere ba maama, 20ye o ta de Moses de Aron o we, 21“Abam balei kɛ-na dáa á daare Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom, se a yɔɔre a lage a ti-ba mo leile konto.” 22Moses de Aron ma vwi ba yibia tega ne ba lwoori Wɛ ba we, “Dé Tu Wɛ, nmo ŋwaane mo nabiina maama ŋwe. Nɔɔno dedoa nam ná ke o tusi, nmo wó da ko ŋwaane n ke bane de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama mo na?”
23 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, 24“Nam ta de kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama se ba ja ba tete ba vo dáa ba daare Kora, de Datan, de Abiram vwoa yam.” 25Moses ma zaŋe o vo Datan de Abiram tei ye Isarele nakwa bam de tɔge o kwaga. 26Moses maa jege nɔn-kɔgɔ kom o kaane ye o we, “Lage-na jei á vo, se á daare puseŋ-nyena banto. Nam yé zaŋe-na á dwei ba kolokolo, se á de tɔge de-ba á te ba wɛleera yam ŋwaane.” 27Nɔɔna bam maama ma seene ba vo dáa ba daare Kora, de Datan, de Abiram vwoa yam. Datan de Abiram déem nwoŋi mo ba zege ba vwoa yam ni ne, ye ba kaana de ba bia de zege ba tei ne.
28Moses laam ma ta o we, “Keim dento baŋa ne mo abam wó ma á sɛ we Baŋa Wɛ mo toŋe-ne, se ko dae a tete boboŋa ŋwaane mo a ke totoŋa yalo a na jege a ke to. 29Nɔɔna banto ná tege ba tete toone, ko bere we Baŋa Wɛ wo toŋe-ne, se a tete mo ke a boboŋa. 30Baŋa Wɛ nam ná ke wo-kenkagele delo ta na wo maŋe de ke to, pa se tega kam bɔke belei ka jwoŋi-ba ka li, ye banto de ba wonnu maama ná zo tega kuri ne ye ba ŋwe, ko wó pa se á lɔre we ba na gwooni Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane mo o ke konto.”
31Moses na yɔɔre o ta konto o ti to, mo tega kam mɛ seeni nɔɔna bam na zege to bɔke belei. 32Ka ma jwoŋi ba de ba di sem tiina ka li. Tega kam déem ta ligi Kora de o kwaga tɔgena bam maama mo, de ba jejegero maama. 33Ba de ba wonnu maama na sirimi ba zo gwoŋo kom wone konto to, mo tega kam jwoori ka kwoni ka tete. Nɔɔna bam konto laam jei, ye ba daa tera Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom wone. 34Isarele tiina bam déem nigi nɔɔna bam na laare bɔge-bɔge tei to. Ba de ma duri se ba lu ye ba laare ba we, “Dé vae se tega kam li debam de!”
35Ko ta ná ye nɔɔna bia yalei de finnu balo na mɛ ba mini zwe sem ba zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa ba pa Baŋa Wɛ to, min-vogo mo pɔpɔ ko nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ tei ne ko chu ba baŋa ne ko go-ba.
36 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, 37“Ta de Aron bu Eleaza se o beeri tentwarem dem wone o twɛ min-chala zwe sem. O ná ke konto, se o laam le min-chala yalo na wo se wone to o dole o yage yiga yiga. Kokuri to, zwe sem laam ye wose mo, 38ba na kwei-se ba ma ke pɛɛra ba pa Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane. Nɔɔna balo na ke konto to laam tege mo ba wɛleera ŋwaane. Mo kokuri, á jege se á kwei zwe sem á mage á ke daane se se chaane se ji channa-pelaga, se á daare á kwei á ma á kwoli kaanem dakaa kam. Konto ná kea, min-chala zwe sem wó ji maana mo se pa Isarele tiina bam.”
39Kaanem tu Eleaza ma seene o twɛ zwe selo nɔɔna bam na jaane ba vo Wɛ yiga ne ye Wɛ go-ba to. O ma pa se ba mage-se ba ke channa-pelaga na chaane to, ye ba kwei-ka ba kwoli kaanem dakaa kam. 40Ko maa ye maana ko pa Isarele tiina bam se ba taa yei we nɔɔn-nɔɔno dae se o zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa o pa Baŋa Wɛ ye o wo nwoŋi Aron dwi dem wone. Nɔn-gaa ná kwaane se o ke konto, kotu wó na chɔgem nenɛɛne Kora de o kwaga tɔgena bam na nɛ tei to mo. Eleaza déem ke nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge Moses baŋa o pa‑o ni se o ke tei to mo.
41Tega na poore to mo Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama vei Moses de Aron tei ye ba poone ba we, “Abam balei mo go Wɛ nɔɔna bam badaara.”
42Nɔɔna bam na yɔɔre ba jeeri ba gilimi-ba to, mo Moses de Aron pipiri se ba nii wara-jei sem seeni, dedaane kunkwoŋo kom tu ko kwoli wara-vwei dem ye Baŋa Wɛ pɔpɔ o veere o tete de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom o bere ba maama. 43Moses de Aron ma vo ba zege wara-vwei dem yiga ne. 44Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, 45“Fɔɔre á zege-na dáa ne de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom se a laam yɔɔre a ti ba maama bedwe baŋa ne.” Ba de ma vwi ba yibia tega ne.
46Moses ma ta de Aron o we, “Zaŋe n kwei n min-chala zoŋa kam n daare n le min-chala kaanem dakaa kam mini wone n ke zoŋa kam wone. Ta kwei talwoŋ-ywoŋa n woli da n vo n zo nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wone se n ma n saare ba wɛleera Wɛ yiga ne. Ke lela! Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe nɔɔna bam baŋa ne mo pa se jawe-chɛɔ maŋe ko to ba wone ko jege-ba ko goe.” 47Aron ma seene o ke kolo Moses na tage to. O kwei o mini zoŋa kam mo o ja o duri o zo nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wone, ye jawe-chɛɔ kom ta jege nɔɔna bam ko goe. O ma zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa kam o pa Baŋa Wɛ se o le ba wɛleera Wɛ yiga ne. 48O ma zege twa bam de nɔɔna balo ta na ŋwe to tetare ne. Aron keim dem konto ma che jaweo kom dam, ye nɔɔna bam daa ba toa. 49De ko de, Isarele tiina balo na tege jaweo kom ŋwaane to déem ye nɔɔna morro fuga-tena de bia yarepɛ (14,700). Twa bam konto déem mo woli de balo na maŋe ba te Kora keim-balɔrɔ kom ŋwaane to.
50Jaweo kom na tu ko yage to, mo Aron jwoori wara-jei sem ni ne o vo o zege Moses tei ne.

english_text:
Aaron's Walking Stick Blooms and Produces Almonds
1The Lord told Moses:
2-3Call together the twelve tribes of Israel and tell the leader of each tribe to write his name on the walking stick he carries as a symbol of his authority. Make sure Aaron's name is written on the one from the Levi tribe, then collect all the sticks.
4Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you. 5I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
6Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe. 7Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
8 The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick. 9Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
10But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.” 11Moses did what he was told.
12The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for 13and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_text:
Aron nacheiga na kwi vɔɔro tei to
1 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, 2“Ta de Isarele tiina bam se n jwoŋi nachei fuga-selei ba tei ne. Ba nabaara sɔ-yuni tem maama yiga tu wom wó kwei o nacheiga kam o pa‑m se n popone kotu yere n ke ka yera ne. 3Ko ná ye Levi dwi dem nacheiga kam, se n popone Aron yere n ke ka yera ne. Konto to, ba sɔ-yuni tem maama yiga tu nacheiga kam wó taa wora. 4Nam kwei nachei sem konto n ja n zo wara-vwei dem wone n tiŋi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne, mɛ seeni a na yeini a jeeri‑m to. 5Ko ná ye nɔɔno wolo amo na kuri se o taa ye a kaanem yiga tu wom to, kotu nacheiga kam wó kwi de vɔɔro. A maa wó tɔge ko baŋa ne se Isarele tiina bam na yɔɔre ba jege‑m ba poona tei to yage.”
6Moses ma ta Wɛ ni dem o bere Isarele tiina bam. Ba yiga tiina bam ma seene ba pa‑o ba nachei fuga-selei, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nacheiga. Aron nacheiga kam de ma woli da Levi dwi dem ŋwaane. 7Moses ma ja se maama o zo wara-vwei dem wone o tiŋi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne.
8Tega na poore to mo Moses jwoori o zo wara-vwei dem wone. O na zo to, mo o nɛ we Aron nacheiga kam, ka na zege ka pae Levi dwi dem to kwi vɔɔro. Ka ta ke punnu de, ye Alimodi tio-bia na bege to leigi ka yera ne. 9Moses ma ja nachei sem maama ya na tigi Baŋa Wɛ dakaa kam yiga ne to o nwoŋi pwooni, se Isarele tiina bam maama na. Yiga tiina bam maama ma lɔre ba nachei ye ba kwei-se.
10 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we, “Ja Aron nacheiga kam n jwoori n zo n tiŋi ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne. Ka ye maana mo ka pa zwabani-nyena bam we, ba ná wo yage ba pompona kam amo ŋwaane, a wó chɔge-ba.” 11Moses ma ke tei Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑o ni se o ke to.
12Isarele tiina bam laam ma ta de Moses ba we, “Debam maama lage dé te mo! Chwoŋa tera se dé jwoŋi dé tete dé yage! 13Dé ná fɔɔre dé twɛ Baŋa Wɛ wara-vwei dem yera, lɛɛro wó yi debam mo se dé te! Debam maama nam wó sɛ se dé te na?”

english_text:
The Duties of the Priests and Levites
1The Lord said to Aaron:
You, your sons, and the other Levites of the Kohath clan, are responsible for what happens at the sacred tent. And you and your sons will be responsible for what the priests do. 2The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent. 3You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die. 4No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it. 5Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
6I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers. 7But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death.
The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord
(Deuteronomy 18.1-8)
8-9The Lord said to Aaron:
I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar. 10Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
11You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things. 12For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts. 13And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
14 Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
15The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me. 16The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards. 17However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased. 18You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
19From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
20You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need.
What the Levites Receive
The Lord said to Aaron:
21 Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent. 22-23They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change.
Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own, 24they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me.
What the Levites Must Give
25The Lord told Moses 26to say to the Levites:
When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me. 27Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive 28as an offering to me. That amount must then be given to Aaron, 29so the best of what you receive will be mine.
30After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me. 31Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent. 32You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me.
The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_text:
Wɛ kaanem tiina de Levi dwi tiina totoŋa yam taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Aron o we:
“Nmo de n bia, ko woli de á chorro Levi dwi tiina bam mo jege se á ta‑á nii se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé chɔge wara-jei chullu tem. Ko nam ná ye Wɛ kaanem tiina bam, nmo de n bia bam mo jege se á ta‑á nii ba baŋa ne, se ba yé ke ba chɔge. 2Nmo dé n bia ná yeini á toŋe wara-vwei dem totoŋa, se á pa se á chorro Levi dwi tiina bam taa tui ba woli abam wone ba taa toŋa. 3Ta‑á nii ba baŋa ne se ba taa toŋe wara-jei sem maama totoŋa yam. Nam yé pa-na se ba yi ba dwei wara-vwei dem wo-zela yam, naa kaanem dakaa kam. Á ná pɛ-ba chwoŋa pa se ba ke konto, abam de banto maama wó te mo. 4Banto mo wó woli abam wone se á ta‑á toŋe wara-jei sem totoŋa yam maama. Ko ná dae banto yerane, nɔn-gaa ba jege chwoŋa se o twɛ abam totoŋa jei sem.
5Nmo de n bia bam wó nii wara-vwei dem tete, de kaanem dakaa kam totoŋa baŋa ne, se amo bane daa yé zaŋe de Isarele tiina bam. 6Amo tete mo kuri Levi dwi dem Isarele dwia yam maama wone se ba taa ye a nyem. A laam ma kwei-ba a pa abam kaanem tiina bam se ba taa zeini abam. 7Nmo de n bia bam yerane mo wó taa toŋe kaanem tiina totoŋa yam. Abam mo jege chwoŋa se á ta‑á ke kaanem á pa-ne dakaa kam baŋa ne, ye á ta daare á gaale á zo wara-vwei gare-jale dem yiga ne. Kaanem totoŋe dem á na wó toŋe to ye pɛɛre mo amo na kwei a pa abam. Nɔn-gaa ná kwaane se o twɛ á totoŋa jei sem, kotu jege se o te mo.”
Wɛ kaanem tiina bam pɛɛra taane
8 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Aron o we:
“Amo kwei pɛɛra yalo maama Isarele tiina bam na yeini ba jaane ba tui ba pa-ne to mo a ke abam jeŋa ne se á ta‑á nii ya kaanem baŋa ne. Amo nam pɔɔre abam nyem mo ya wone se á ta‑á jega taa wuu. 9Ko ná ye pɛɛra yalo na tiini ya ye wose ye nɔɔna jaane ba tui ba pa-ne to, á wó pɔɔre á nyem pɛɛra yalo ba na wo zwɛ kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne to wone mo. Ko ná ye ba wodiu pɛɛra yam, de ba wɛleera saarem pɛɛra yam, de ba wɛleere jene pɛɛra yam, nmo de n bia wó jwoŋi á nyem ya maama wone. 10Á nam jege se á maŋe wara-jei sem wone mo á di wonnu tem konto, te na tiini te ye wose to ŋwaane. Á baara bam maama mo jege chwoŋa se ba di-te. Nam pa-na se te taa ye wose abam tei ne.
11Ko ta ná ye pɛɛra yalo á na wó pɔɔre Isarele tiina pɛɛra yalo á na zeiŋi wɛɛne á yaare-ya amo yiga ne to wone, amo kwei tento se te taa ye nmo de n bia bam nyem mo. Nmo bu-baara de n bukwa jege chwoŋa se ba di-te taa wuu. N diga tiina bam wolo maama ná maŋe de chullu tem, kotu jege chwoŋa se o jwoŋi te wone o di.
12Ko ta ná ye pɛɛra yalo nɔɔna na yeini ba pɔɔre ba nuga wone, de ba Vini sa-sona wone, de ba wodiiru telo maama na yeini te lwoori yiga te ke to wone ba ja ba ba ba pa-ne to, amo kwei tento a pa abam mo. 13Wodiiru telo maama tega kam na yeini te ke ye nɔɔna ja-te ba ba ba pa-ne to wó taa ye abam nyem. N diga tiina bam wolo maama ná maŋe de chullu tem, kotu jege chwoŋa se o jwoŋi te wone o di.
14Woŋo kolo maama Isarele tiina bam na yɔɔre ba kwei ba ke amo jeŋa ne to de wó taa ye abam nyem. 15Isarele tiina bam bakeiri-kwe sem, de ba vare-kwe sem ba na yeini ba ja ba ba se ba pa-ne to maama ye abam nyem mo. Á nam wó pa se ba ŋwe sabu mo se ko leiri ba bakeiri-kwe sem yuu ne. Ko ta ná ye vare-kwe selo na wo maŋe de chullu tem to, ba wó ŋwe sabu se ŋwaane. 16Ba ná lage ba ŋwe sabu ba bakeiri-kwe sem ŋwaane, abam wó jwoŋi sɛkɛle sabu-dala yanu mo bu wolo na yi chana to ŋwaane. Sabu kom konto dunni jege se ko tɔge de wara-jei sem maŋem chekke na ye tei to mo. Sɛkɛle dedoa maa ye gɛra kuni finlei. 17Ko nam ná ye vare-kwea kalo na ye naao, naa pia, naa boŋo, ko dae se á jwoŋi sabu ko ŋwaane. Vara bam konto dwoŋi yɔɔre ba ye amo nyem mo. Á jege se á kwei ba jana á miisi kaanem dakaa kam yera ne mo, ye á daare á zwɛ ba lara kam á ma‑á ke zwɛɛm kaanem á pa-ne, se ka lwom dem taa ywomma de pa-ne. 18Vara bam konto nɔna nam ye abam nyem mo se á di, nenɛɛne á na jege chwoŋa se á di vara nyɔɔna yalo á na zeiŋi wɛɛne amo ŋwaane to, de ba jazem chwoa yam tei to. 19Pɛɛra yalo maama Isarele tiina bam na pɔɔre se ba kwei ba pa-ne to mo amo kwei-ya se ya taa ye nmo de n bia bam nyem, bakeiri de busankane maama. Ya wó taa ye abam nyem taa wuu. Amo ni dem konto wó yɔɔre de taa wora ko pae nmo de n kwaga kam se ko taa vei wuu.”
20 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Aron o we:
“Ba ná lage ba pɔɔre tega kam ba pa Isarele tiina bam, nmo bá‑n tɔge n jwoŋi n popɔra ka wone. Nmo daa bá‑n na n nyɔn-mage nyem, ko ná dae amo yerane. Amo tete nam mo yɔɔre a maŋe a pa‑m.
21Ko ta ná ye Levi dwi tiina bam, amo wó pa ba jwoŋi ba ŋweero totoŋa yalo ba na jege ba toŋe wara-vwei dem wone to baŋa ne. Isarele tiina bam ná yeini ba le popɔra dedoa ba wonnu tem popɔre fuga maama wone se ba pa-ne, amo wó kwei amo popɔra kam konto a pa Levi dwi tiina bam. 22-23Banto yerane mo jege se ba taa nii wara-vwei dem baŋa ne, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé chɔge de chullu tem. Nɔn-gaa daa ba jege chwoŋa se o fɔɔre o yi wara-vwei dem. Wolo ná ke konto, kotu tusim dem wó taa wo o yuu ne ye o jege se o te mo. Levi tiina bam de jege se ba na waarem ko ŋwaane. Ni dento a na pɛ abam to wó taa wora mo taa wuu ko pae abam de á kwaga kam.
Levi tiina bam nam bá tɔge ba jwoŋi ba popɔra tega kam pɔɔrem baŋa ne, ne ba chorro Isarele tiina bam na wó na tei to. 24Ko na ye tei to, amo kwei Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yalo Isarele tiina na jaane ba tui ba pa-ne to a pa-ba se ya taa ye ba popɔra. Konto ŋwaane mo a nam tage Levi tiina bam taane a we, ba bá tɔge ba na ba popɔra Isarele tiina tega kam pɔɔrem baŋa ne.”
25 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we:
26“Ta n bere Levi tiina bam we: Abam ná jwoŋi Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yalo na ye abam nyem to Isarele tiina bam tei ne, se á de le popɔra dedoa fuga maama wone á pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ya wó taa ye abam tete Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra á na le banto Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yam wone to mo. 27Baŋa Wɛ wó jeeli á Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yam konto, nenɛɛne á ya ná kwei á tete mena naa sa-doora á pa‑o to mo. 28Á wó tɔge chwoŋa kam konto á le Isarele tiina bam Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yam maama wone, se á de ke pɛɛra á pa‑o. Á ma‑á wó kwei abam tete Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yam konto á pa Wɛ kaanem tu Aron. 29Á jege se á le wonnu telo na tiini te lana to á pɛɛra yam wone mo se te taa ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem. Pɔɔre-na-te á pa‑o.
30Ta ta de Levi tiina bam we: Abam ná pɔɔre wonnu telo na tiini te lana to á pa Wɛ, o wó jeeli á pɛɛra yam konto, nenɛɛne á ya ná kwei á tete mena naa sa-doora á pa‑o to mo. 31Abam de á diga tiina jege chwoŋa se á kwei kolo na daare á pɛɛra yam wone to á di mɛ seeni á na lage to. Kokuri to, pɛɛra yam konto ye á ŋweero telo á na nɛ wara-vwei dem totoŋa baŋa ne to mo. 32Á ná yɔɔre á le wonnu telo na tiini te lana to se te taa ye á Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra á pa‑o, á bá na chɔgem chullu tem seeni. Pɛɛra yalo Isarele tiina bam na jaane ba tui ba pa-ne to ye wose mo. Ko dae se á kwei-ya á di yɔɔ yɔɔ. Á ná tɔge chwei sem konto, á bá te chullu tem chɔgem ŋwaane.”

english_text:
The Ceremony To Wash Away Sin
1-2The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law:
The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing. 3Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches. 4He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent. 5Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned. 6A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
7After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening. 8The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
9 A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin. 10The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them.
What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body
The Lord said:
11If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days. 12But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean. 13Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
14If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean. 15Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
16If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
17-18Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water. 19If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
20If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel. 21These laws will never change.
The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening. 22When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_text:
Wɛleera saarem chullu tem
1 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Moses de Aron o we:
2“Amo Baŋa Wɛ tiŋi a ni dento mo se á ta‑á tɔge-de. Ta-na á bere Isarele tiina bam we: Ba jege se ba ja na-chwɛ-soŋo kolo na ba jege gɛɛ ko yera ne ye ba ta wo kwei-ko ba ma toŋe to mo ba ba ba pa abam. 3Á wó kwei-ko á pa kaanem tu Eleaza. O de maa wó ja-ko o nwoŋi o vo dáa, pa se ba go-ko ye o zege o nia. 4Eleaza ta wó de o noa na-chwɛ dem jana wone, ye o laam pipiri o jeeri wara-jei sem yiga seeni o miisi jana bam kuni berepɛ. 5Ko daare naao kom tete, de ko tɔnɔ kom, de ko nɔna yam, de ko jana bam, de ko wo-zela yam maama ye se ba zwɛ mo kula ye kaanem tu wom zege o nia. 6Na-chwɛ dem na jege de zwɛ konto to, kaanem tu wom laam wó kwei Sedare daa dedoa, de Husopa tio vɔɔro, de gare-ŋon-seŋa, o dole-te o de mini dem wone. 7Konto kwaga ne se kaanem tu wom swɛ o yera o daare o zare o gwaaro. O laam jege chwoŋa se o jwoori o taa zoore Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom wone. O laam maa wó digiri chullu tem seeni se ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa. 8Nɔɔno wolo de na zwɛ na-chwɛ dem to de wó zare o gwaaro mo ye o daare o swɛ o yera. Wonto de wó digiri chullu tem seeni mo se ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa.
9Wolo na maŋe de chullu tem to maa wó pɛ na-chwɛ dem tentwarem dem, ye o ke-de pwola kalo ba na kwɛ Wɛ ŋwaane to ne. Jeiga kam konto nam wó taa ye dáa dáa mo de á na zoore mɛ to. Ba ta wó yeini ba viiri tentwarem dem na wone se Isarele tiina bam ma ba kwɛ ba tete de chullu tem wɛleera saarem ŋwaane. 10Wolo na pɛ tentwarem dem to de wó zare o gwaaro mo. O de wó digiri chullu tem seeni se ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa mo. Abam Isarele tiina bam de veira balo na zoore á wone to jege se á tɔge ni dento mo se ko taa vei wuu.
11Wolo ná dwei too, konto tu digiri chullu tem seeni mo se ko taa vei da yarepɛ. 12O jege se o kwei chullu kwɛɛm na bam mo o ma o kwɛ o tete de chullu tem. O wó ke konto da yatɔ dɛ dem ne, dedaane da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne mo, se o laam maŋe de chullu tem. O ná wo kwɛ o tete da yam konto ne, o yɔɔre o ta wo maŋe de chullu tem mo. 13Nɔɔno nam ná dwei too, ye o ve se o kwɛ o tete chullu tem ŋwaane, kotu chɔge Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem mo. Ba le‑o se o daa yé woli Isarele tiina bam wone. O ta digiri chullu tem seeni mo, ba na wo kwei chullu kwɛɛm na bam ba miisi o yera ne to ŋwaane.
14Nɔɔno ná wo vwei ne ye o te, chullu tem bere we wolo maama na wora ye kotu te, de wolo na zo da o maŋe de o toone dem to maama digiri mo chullu tem seeni se ko taa vei da yarepɛ. 15Kambia naa kɔɔro naa zoŋa kalo ná wo vwei dem wone ye ka ni wo pugi, ka de wo maŋe de chullu tem.
16Nɔɔno wolo ná wo pwooni yiga ne pa se o dwei too, kotu wó digiri chullu tem seeni se ko taa vei da yarepɛ. Ko ná ye wolo na tega jara-keim baŋa ne to, naa wolo na tege o tete toone to mo kotu dwei, ko ta ye bedwe mo. O ta ná dwei too kua, naa o dwei yibeeli, kotu digiri mo se ko taa vei da yarepɛ maŋa ne.
17Á ná lage á kwɛ wolo na digiri chullu tem seeni to, á wó kwei na-chwɛ delo ba na zwɛ wɛleera saarem ŋwaane to tentwarem mo á ke kikeira wone á daare á lwo na-doora á woli da. 18Nɔɔno na maŋe de chullu tem to laam wó kwei Husopa tio vɔɔro o de na bam wone o daare o miisi vwei dem, de de wo-zela yam, de nɔɔna balo na wo de wone ye nɔɔno wom te to. Ko ta ye bedwe mo de wolo ná dwei too, naa too kua, naa yibeeli. Ba jege se ba miisi kotu de chullu kwɛɛm na bam mo. 19Á wó miisi wolo na digiri to da yatɔ dɛ dem ne, dedaane da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, se o laam maŋe de chullu tem. Nɔɔno wom wó zare o gwaaro mo o daare o swɛ o yera. Dedaan-ni maŋa ná yia, o wó maŋe de chullu tem. 20Nɔɔno ná digiri chullu tem seeni, ye o ve se o kwɛ o tete de chullu tem, ba jege se ba le kotu se o daa yé woli Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom wone mo, o na chɔge Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem to ŋwaane. O ta digiri mo chullu tem seeni, ba na wo kwei chullu kwɛɛm na bam ba miisi o yera ne to ŋwaane. 21Nia yanto nam wó taa wora taa wuu ya pa abam.
Wolo na kwei chullu kwɛɛm na bam o miisi nɔɔna to de jege se o zare o gwaaro mo. Wolo maama de ná dwei na bam konto, kotu wó digiri chullu tem seeni, se ko taa nii dedaan-ni maŋa. 22Wolo na digiri chullu tem seeni to ná dwei woŋo kolo maama, woŋo kom konto de digiri mo. Wolo de nam ná dwei woŋo kom, o de wó digiri o tete se ko taa nii dedaan-ni maŋa mo.”

english_text:
Water from a Rock
1The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
2 The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron 3and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent. 4You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die! 5Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
6Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory 7-8and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
9Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent. 10After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!” 11 He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
12But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
13The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.”
Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
14Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom:
We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us. 15Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us, 16and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land.
Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh. 17Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
18But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
19Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
20But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!”
Then Edom sent out its strongest troops 21to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction.
Aaron Dies
22After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor 23on the Edomite border, the Lord said, 24“Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites. 25Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain. 26Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
27Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor. 28 Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there.
When Moses and Eleazar came down, 29the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for 30 days.
translation_text:
Na nwoŋi peo wone se nɔɔna bam nyɔ
1Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom déem ma beeri ba vo ba yi Zin kagoa kam boboa chana kam ne. Ba ma vo ba chwi ba vwoa Kadese ne ba zoore da. Ba na wora to, Miriam déem ma te ye ba suli‑o da.
2Na déem tera se Isarele tiina bam nyɔ. Ba maama ma la daane ba vo ba yi Moses de Aron tei se ba dwoni de-ba. 3Ba ma bwɛ Moses ye ba we, “Debam de déem ya ná tɔge dedaane dé chorro tem dé te Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem yiga ne, ko ya gare tento. 4Nmo nam yɔɔre n ja debam na ye Baŋa Wɛ kɔgɔ kom to mo n ba n dole n yage kagoa kanto ne, se debam dedaane dé vara maama te. 5Bɛ mo ye n ja debam n nwoŋi Ejipti teo wone se dé ba dé zege kasol-gwiu konto ne? Wodiiru ware se te ke ywo-seeni, kaporro nam tera, Vini teeni de tera, Pomegara teeni de maa tera. Na de nam tera se dé nyɔ!”
6Moses de Aron ma tutwoni ba kɛ ba daare nɔn-kɔgɔ kom ba vo ba zege wara-vwei dem ni ne. Ba ma vwi ba yibia tega ne, ye Baŋa Wɛ pɔpɔ o chu o veere o tete ko tɔge de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom o bere-ba. 7Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, 8“Zaŋe n kwei n nacheiga kam se nmo de n zembaaro Aron vo á la kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama á ke daane. Laam zege ba yiga ne n ŋɔɔne de peo kolo na zege tento to. Na wó ta ba nwoŋi ko yera ne. Chega to, nmo wó pa na taa nwoŋi peo kom wone ba pae nɔn-kɔgɔ kom de ba vara bam se ba taa nyɔa.”
9Moses ma seene o vo o zo Baŋa Wɛ wara-vwei dem wone o kwei o nacheiga kam ne Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ ni se o ke tei to. 10O de Aron ma ja nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama ba vo ba zege peo kom yiga ne. Moses laam ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam zwabani-nyena banto, cheigi-na! Debam mo jege se dé pa se na ta ba nwoŋi peo konto ne se á nyɔ na?” 11O laam ma zeiŋi o jeŋa wɛɛne ye o kwei o nacheiga kam o ma mage peo kom kuni belei. Na-fɔrɔ ma pɔpɔ ba wuura ye ba chuura, pa se nɔɔna bam de ba vara nyɔ.
12Ko daare Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses de Aron o we, “Abam nam wo ke á wo-dedoa de amo se ko pa Isarele tiina bam lɔre we, amo yɔɔre a ye wose. Á wo-dedoa kam na muri to ŋwaane, a daa bá pa abam chwoŋa se á ja amo nɔn-kɔgɔ kom á vo á zo tega kalo a na lage a pa-ba to wone.”
13Ba déem jege jei sem konto ba bwoi we ‘Meriba’ mo. Dáane mo Isarele tiina bam mage kantɔgɔ dedaane Baŋa Wɛ. O de ma bere-ba o wo-pwoŋo kom na ye tei to.
Edom teo pɛ ve se o pa Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba kɛ
14Moses déem ma zege Kadese ne o toŋe kwora o pa Edom teo pɛ o we:
“Debam ye nmo tete chorro Isarele dwi tiina bam mo. Nmo maŋe n yei yaara yalo maama na yi debam to ni ne. 15Dé nabaara déem vei ba zo Ejipti teo wone ba maŋe da bena dedɛ. Ko kwaga ne mo Ejipti tiina bam bɛɛse dé kwoa bam de debam de. 16Dé na keeri dé jare Baŋa Wɛ to, mo o nigi dé wɛ-lworo kom. O ma tɔge o maleka baŋa ne o ja debam o nwoŋi teo kom konto ne. Dé laam nam tu dé jei Kadese ne mo, ko na wo abam teo kom siseini ni ne to. 17Dé maa lwoori nmo mo se n pa debam chwoŋa se dé tɔge n tega kam baŋa dé kɛ. Dé bá tɔge á kare de á kadwi seeni. Dé maŋe dé bá mɔ na á vola yam ne dé nyɔ. Dé nam wó yɔɔre dé tole chwo-fara kam yerane mo taa se dé vo dé bɛ abam laŋa kam. Dé bere dé bá ywori chwoŋa kam ne.”
18Edom pɛ wom ma leiri o we, “Aawo! Debam bá pa abam chwoŋa se á tɔge dé laŋa kam á kɛ. Abam nam ná fe se á tɔge da á kɛ, dé wó nwoŋi dé jeeri abam de jara.”
19Isarele tiina bam ma jwoori ba leiri ba we, “Dé nam wó maŋe chwo-fara kam ni ne mo dé taa via. Debam de dé vara ná nyɔge á na, dé wó ŋwe dé pa abam. Dé na lwoori kolo yerane to mo ye se dé tɔge á laŋa kam ne dé kɛ.”
20Edom pɛ wom ma yɔɔre o ve ye o we, “Dé bá sɛ se á tɔge ywo-seeni á kɛ.”
O ma pa se o jar-keira kɔ-fɔrɔ kom nwoŋi de dam se ba jeeri Isarele tiina bam de jara. 21Konto to, Edom tiina bam wo pɛ Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba tɔge ba laŋa kam ba kɛ. Ko déem pɛ se Isarele tiina bam pipiri mo ba jwoori kwaga se ba kwei chwo-gaa.
Aron toone
22Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama déem ma zege Kadese ne ba vo ba yi Hora peo kom 23na wo Edom laŋa kam siseini ne to. Ba na wora to mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Moses de Aron o we, 24“Aron lage o maŋe ywo-seeni mo o te. O bá zo tega kalo a na lage a pa Isarele tiina bam to wone, abam balei na nwoŋi amo ni dem kwaga ne Meriba jei sem ne to ŋwaane. 25Moses, nam ja Aron de o bu Eleaza se á maama di Hora peo kom yuu. 26Pa se Aron lɔɔre o kaanem gare-laaro tem, se n kwei-te n zo o bu Eleaza. Kokuri to, Aron lage o te peo kom yuu ne mo.”
27Moses maa seene o ke tei Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ ni se o ke to. Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama déem zege ba nia mo ye wonto, de Aron, dedaane Eleaza di Hora peo kom yuu. 28Moses ma lɔɔre Aron kaanem gwaaro tem, ye o daare o kwei-te o zo Eleaza. Aron ma maŋe peo kom yuu ne o te.
Moses de Eleaza ma zege peo kom yuu ne ba maa tu tega. 29Nɔɔna bam na yɔɔre ba lɔre we Aron tege to, mo ba maama keeri o lua kam da fintɔ.

english_text:
Israel Defeats the Canaanites at Hormah
1 The Canaanite king of Arad lived in the Southern Desert of Canaan, and when he heard that the Israelites were on their way to the village of Atharim, he attacked and took some of them hostage.
2The Israelites prayed, “Our Lord, if you will help us defeat these Canaanites, we will completely destroy their towns and everything in them, to show that they belong to you.”
3The Lord answered their prayer and helped them wipe out the Canaanite army and completely destroy their towns. That's why one of the towns is named Hormah, which means “Destroyed Place.”
Moses Makes a Bronze Snake
4 The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient 5 that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
6Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
7Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.”
Moses prayed, 8and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
9 Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes.
Israel's Journey to Moab
10As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth, 11then at Iye-Abarim in the desert east of Moab, 12and then in the Zered Gorge. 13After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites. 14A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River, 15with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
16From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
17That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song:
Let's celebrate!
The well has given us water.
18With their royal scepters,
our leaders pointed out
where to dig the well.
The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah, 19then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth. 20Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite
(Deuteronomy 2.26-37)
21The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
22Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
23But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz. 24Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
25The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages. 26King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge. 27That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon:
Come and rebuild Heshbon,
King Sihon's capital city!
28 His armies marched out
like fiery flames,
burning down the town of Ar
and destroying the hills
along the Arnon River.
29You Moabites are done for!
Your god Chemosh
deserted your people;
they were captured, taken away
by King Sihon the Amorite.
30We completely defeated Moab.
The towns of Heshbon and Dibon,
of Nophah and Medeba
are ruined and gone.
31After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory, 32Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there.
Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan
(Deuteronomy 3.1-11)
33The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
34The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
35So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_text:
Isarele tiina bam wane Kanaan tiina bam
1Arada teo pɛ déem mo wora. O maa ye Kanaan dwi tu ye o zoore tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam ne. O ma ni we Isarele tiina bam wo Atarim chwoŋa kam ne mo ba vei ba beene o jei sem. O ma nwoŋi o jeeri-ba de jara ye o ja ba badaara o pe. 2Isarele tiina bam ma du duuri de Baŋa Wɛ ba we, “Nmo ná woli pa se dé wane nɔɔna banto dé di, debam de gwoni ni se dé yɔɔre dé chɔge ba teene dem maama dé pa nmo.” 3Baŋa Wɛ ma cheigi ba wɛ-lworo kom ye o sɛ o woli-ba pa se ba di Kanaan tiina bam. Ba ma yɔɔre ba chɔge ba teene dem de de nɔn-bia bam. Konto ŋwaane mo ba bwoŋi jei sem yere we Horama.
Channa basankwea kam
4Isarele tiina bam déem na zaŋe Hora peo kom ne to, ko jege se ba kaare ba yage Edom laŋa kam dáa ne mo. Ba ma kwei Nane-soŋo chwoŋa kam ba kɛ. Ba nam na wo chwoŋa ne ba vei to, mo nɔɔna bam daa wo wane ba ja ba tete. 5Ba maa ŋwaane Wɛ de daane Moses ye ba we, “Moses, bɛ mo ye nmo yɔɔre n ja debam n nwoŋi Ejipti wone, se dé ba dé te kagoa kanto wone? Wodi-laao tera ywo-seeni. Na de maa tera se dé nyɔ. Dé yera de laam chɛ de wodi-yɔɔ konto.”
6 Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se basankwe selo ni na chana to to Isarele tiina bam wone, ye se done ba dedɛ se go. 7Nɔɔna bam badwonna ma vo Moses tei ba ta ba we, “Dé na ŋɔɔne dé chɔge Baŋa Wɛ de nmo to, ko ye wɛleere mo dé kea. Nam lwoori Baŋa Wɛ n pa debam, se o pa se basankwe sento viiri se daare debam.” Moses de ma lwoori Wɛ o pa nɔɔna bam.
8 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Nam yɔɔre n mɔ basankwea, se n daare n kwei-ka n lei daa yera ne. Basankwe sem ná done wolo maama, kotu wó kwoni o nii-ka se o ma jwoŋi o ŋwea.” 9Moses ma kwei channa o ma o mɔ basankwea o daare o lei-ka daa yera ne o zege-ka deiki. Wolo maama basankwe sem na done ye o kwoni o nii channa basankwea kam to mo jwoŋi o ŋwea o yage.
Ba kwei chwoŋa ba maa vei Moaba
10Isarele tiina bam daa ma zaŋe ba vo ba yi Obofe teo ba jeini da. 11Ba ma zege Obofe ne, ba zaŋe ba vo ba yi Ye-Abarim ba jeini da. Jei sem konto maa ye Moaba wɛ-puli seeni kagoa kam ne mo. 12Ba daa ma zaŋe dáane ba vo ba jeini Zereda nabara kam ni ne. 13Ba laam ma zaŋe ba vo ba bɛ Aranon buga kam, ye ba vo ba jeini kagoa kalo na wo Amori tiina laŋa kam siseini ni ne to. Aranon buga kam déem mo ye siseini na tigi Moaba tiina bam de Amori tiina bam tetare ne to. 14Konto ŋwaane nam mo tei Baŋa Wɛ Jara-keim Tɔnɔ kom tage jei sem konto taane we:
“Waheba teo na wo Sufa laŋa ne, de ko nabare sem, de Aranon buga kam, 15de nabare sem siswooru tem konto na tigi Moaba siseini ni ne, ye te kɛ te yi Ara teo to.”
16Ba ma zege jei sem konto ne ba vo ba yi Beeri teo. Vole maa wo teo kom konto ne, ye dáane mo Baŋa Wɛ déem tage de Moses o we, “La nɔɔna bam n ke daane se a lage a pa-ba na mo se ba nyɔ.” 17Kanto maŋa ne mo Isarele tiina bam leeni leiŋa kanto ba we:
“Vole dem na buri na
de pa debam to,
debam de wó ke wopwolo
ye dé leeni lei!
18Pwa mo koge vole dem!
Naduna de ma fɔge-de!
Ba kwei ba paare nachei sem mo
ba ko-de!”
Isarele tiina bam déem ma zaŋe kagoa kam ne ba vo ba jeini Matana ne. 19Ba maa zaŋe Matana ne ba vo Nahaleli. Ba daa zege da ba vo ba yi Bamofe. 20Ba ma zege Bamofe ne ba vo ba yi bwolo kodwoŋi na wo Moaba laŋa kam ne to. Ba ma jeini mɛ na twɛ de Pisiga peo kom to. Peo kom yuu maa yɔɔre ko jeeri kagoa kam seeni.
Ba na di Pɛ Sihon de Pɛ Oga tei to
21Isarele tiina bam déem ma toŋe kwora ba pa Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon, ye ba we:
22“Dé lwoori nmo mo se n pa debam chwoŋa se dé tɔge n tega kam baŋa dé kɛ. Dé bá ywori chwoŋa kam ne dé tɔge á kare de á kadwi seeni. Dé maŋe dé bá mɔ na á vola yam ne dé nyɔ. Dé nam wó yɔɔre dé tole chwo-fara kam yerane mo taa se dé vo dé bɛ abam laŋa kam.”
23Pɛ Sihon ma ve se Isarele tiina bam tɔge o laŋa kam ne ba kɛ. O ma bwoŋi o jar-keira bam maama o ke daane, ye ba nwoŋi ba vo kagoa kam wone se ba jeeri Isarele tiina bam. Ba na yi Jahaza seeni to, mo ba déem kwaare jara de-ba. 24Isarele tiina bam déem ma di-ba. Ba ma vere ba tega kam ba tei, ko zege Aranon buga kam ni ne, se ko yi Jaboke buga kam. Ba nam wo bɛ Jaboke buga kam ba kɛ, ko na ye Amon tiina bam siseini dem ye de fɔge de che de dam to ŋwaane. 25Isarele tiina bam déem vere Amori tiina teene dem maama, de ba te-fɔrɔ Hesebon de ko nawuura yam mo. Ba maa lɛɛre ba zoore de wone. 26Hesebon ye teo kolo Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon na jei o di o paare ko wone to mo. O déem nam ya ke jara de Moaba tiina bam pɛ mo, pa se o vere ba tega kam maama se ko vo ko yi Aranon buga kam seeni.
27Konto ŋwaane nam mo tei lein-leena bam yeini ba seini Hesebon teo kom ba we:
“Ba-na á zo Hesebon teo kom wone,
se á jwoori á fɔge á lɔ-ko.
Pa-na se Pɛ Sihon te-fɔrɔ kom
zege de dam!
28Min-fɔrɔ déem nwoŋi Pɛ Sihon teo Hesebon wone
ko jage ko di Moaba teo Ara,
de naduna balo na zoore
Aranon peero tem wone to.
29Moaba tiina bam, lɛɛro yi abam!
Abam balo na zuli á jwoni Chemosi to,
chɔgem to abam baŋa ne!
Á jwoni dem ve abam mo
pa se Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon chwooli abam.
Á baara ma duri ba jage jei maama sae!
O ma zi á bukwa o ja o viiri.
30Debam laam nam yɔɔre
dé wane-ba dé di mo,
ko zege Hesebon ne
se ko yi Dibon seeni.
Dé chɔge-ba mo se ko vo ko yi Nofa,
se ko ta yi Medeba seeni.”
31Isarele tiina bam déem na jeini Amori tiina tega kam ne to, 32mo Moses toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba ŋɔ ba nii Jazera teo kom. Ba na nii-ko to, Isarele tiina bam ma vo ba di teo kom konto de ko nawuura yam. Ba ma zeili Amori tiina bam na zoore jei sem konto ne to.
33Ko kwaga ne mo Isarele tiina bam pipiri ba kwei Basan chwoŋa kam ba via. Basan teo Pɛ Oga ma nwoŋi de o jar-keira bam maama o vo o jeeri-ba Ederi ne se ba kwaare jara.
34 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Moses o we, “Yé ta‑n fona de Pɛ Oga. Amo lage a kwei pɛ wom de o nɔɔna bam maama a ke nmo jeŋa ne, se á jwoŋi ba tega kam á ta‑á tei mo. Abam nam jege se á chɔge pɛ wom konto dedaane o nɔɔna bam mo nenɛɛne á na ke Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon na di paare Hesebon ne tei to.”
35Isarele tiina bam ma yɔɔre ba ti Pɛ Oga, de o bia, de o jar-keira bam maama pa se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa wo daare. Ba maa lɛɛre ba zoore o tega kam ne.

english_text:
1Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho.
King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
2-3When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked. 4They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.”
So King Balak 5 sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said:
I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory. 6They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
7The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
8“Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
9During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
10“They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them 11to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
12But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
13The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
14The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
15Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones. 16They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab, 17I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
18Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God. 19You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
20That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
21So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials.
Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
22Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him. 23When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
24Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side. 25When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
26The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around. 27So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
28When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
29“You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
30“But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?”
“No,” Balaam admitted.
31Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
32The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab. 33If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
34Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
35“It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials.
King Balak Meets Balaam
36When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab. 37Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
38“I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
39They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth, 40where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
41The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_text:
Pɛ Balaki bwoŋi Balaam se o ba o woli‑o
1Isarele tiina bam déem ma gɔ ba vwoa yam ba vo ba yi Moaba laŋa kam te-kampare ba jeini da. Jei sem konto wo Jɔdan buga kam ni ne mo ye Jeriko de wo bubɛ dedwoŋi dem seeni.
2Zipore bu Balaki déem mo ye Moaba teo pɛ. O ma lɔre kolo maama Isarele tiina bam na ke de Amori tiina bam to. 3Foone ma tiini de zo o de o nɔɔna bam, Isarele tiina bam kɔgɔ kom na daga to ŋwaane. Moaba tiina bam nagwola ma te Isarele tiina bam ŋwaane. 4Ba ma ta de Midian tiina nakwa bam ba we, “Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom lage ko ba ko chɔge debam de dé wonnu tem maama, ne nabea na yɔɔre ka gaane gaao pwola ne tei to mo.”
5Moaba Pɛ Balaki déem toŋe kwora o pa Beora bu Balaam se o ba o tei. Balaam déem zoore Amawa teo kodwoŋi ne, ko yere mo Petora. Ko déem wo Yuferata buga kam ni ne mo. Pɛ Balaki maa we:
“Nɔn-dwi dedwoŋi mo zege Ejipti ne ba ba ywo-seeni. Ba yɔɔre ba jage jei maama mo, ye ba laam ba ba jeini amo tega kam ni ne. 6Nɔɔna bam konto dana ba dwoi debam. Nam ba n sɔɔle lwarem n yage ba yera ne, se ko pa dé wane-ba dé zeili se ba viiri ba daare debam. Amo yei lanyerane we nmo ná yeini n sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n yage wolo yera ne, konto tu wó seene o jwoŋi Wɛ swolim mo. N ma‑n ná sɔɔle lwarem n daŋe wolo yuu ne, kotu wó seene o na lɛɛro mo.”
7Moaba de Midian tiina nakwa bam ma zaŋe se ba vo Balaam tei. Ba ma kwei kwora se ba ŋwe‑o o yi-nɛɛre totoŋe dem ŋwaane. Ba na yi da to mo ba pɛ‑o Balaki ni dem.
8Balaam ma leiri-ba o we, “Maŋe-na ywo-seeni á peini, se tega ná poore, se a laam leiri á taane dem, ne Baŋa Wɛ na veere o boboŋa o bere-ne tei to.” Moaba dedɛɛra bam ma maŋe o sɔŋɔ ne ba peini.
9Tete ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma ba Balaam tei ye o we, “Nɔɔna banto ye bera mo ye ba ba nmo sɔŋɔ?” 10Balaam ma leiri o we, “Moaba teo Pɛ Balaki mo toŋe-ba se ba ba ba ta de amo we, 11nɔn-dwi dedwoŋi mo nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba ba ba jage tega kam baŋa maama. O laam maa lage se a vo o tei, se a sɔɔle lwarem a daŋe ba baŋa ne, se o wane-ba o zeili se ba viiri ba daare‑o.”
12Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, “Yé sɛ n tɔge Balaki tontoŋena bam kwaga se á vo o tei. Nam yé sɔɔle lwarem n daŋe nɔn-kɔgɔ kom konto baŋa ne, se amo maŋe a swɛ ba swolim mo.”
13Tega na poore to, Balaam ma yi Balaki tontoŋena bam tei ye o ta de-ba o we, “Jwoori-na á tete teo, se Baŋa Wɛ ve se a da de abam a vo.” 14Moaba tiina dedɛɛra bam ma zaŋe ba jwoori ba vo ba ta de Balaki ba we, “Balaam wo sɛ se o tɔge debam se dé ba nmo tei.”
15Balaki daa ma toŋe o dedɛɛra badwonna se ba vo Balaam tei. Banto tiini ba ye naduna, ye ba daga ba dwoi boboa nɔɔna bam. 16Ba na yi Balaam tei to, mo ba we, “Zipore bu Balaki toŋe ni o we, n yé pa kolokolo che‑m se n ba omo tei. 17N nam ná tua, Balaki wó pa‑m kwora yalo maama n na lage to. O ta wó ke kolo maama n na lage se o ke o pa‑m to. Nam yɔɔre n ba n sɔɔle lwarem n daŋe nɔɔna bam yuu ne n pa‑o.”
18Balaam maa wo sɛ ye o leiri-ba o we, “Pɛ Balaki ná maŋe o lɔ sɔ-fɔrɔ mo, ye o laam su ko ni de sabu-seŋa dedaane lu-nyenno se o kwei o pa-ne de, amo ta bá wane a ve ni delo amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na kwei o pa-ne to. A ba jege chwoŋa se a ke wo-kamunu naa wo-balaŋa de, ye ko dae kolo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ amo ni se a ke to. 19Nam maŋe-na ywo-seeni á peini, nenɛɛne á dwonna bam daama na ke tei to. Amo ta wó nii Baŋa Wɛ jege boboŋe dedwoŋi se o daa veere o bere-ne na?”
20Tete dem konto ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Balaam o we, “Nɔɔna bam na tu se ba bwoŋi‑m se n vo Moaba to, tɔge de-ba n vo. Nmo nam wó ke kolo yerane amo na wó bere‑m se n ke to mo.” 21Tega na poore to, Balaam ma zaŋe o vɔ o bonaga de zela. O na diini-ka to, o ma tɔge de Moaba dedɛɛra bam pa se ba kɛ.
Balaam de o bonaga kam
22 Baŋa Wɛ bane nam ya zaŋe de Balaam mo o na tɔge de-ba o maa vei to ŋwaane. Balaam déem diini o bonaga mo ye ba via. O tontoŋena balei de maa tɔge ba via. Ba na maa vei to, Baŋa Wɛ maleka ma zege ka che Balaam chwoŋa se o yé kɛ. 23Bonaga kam na nɛ we Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam chege ba chwoŋa ye se-zɔɔ wo ka jeŋa ne to, mo ka yage chwoŋa kam ye ka lɔ ka zo gaaro wone. Balaam maa mage-ka ye o ja-ka o jwoori o de chwoŋa kam ne.
24 Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ma vo ka yi chwoŋa kam mɛ na ye memena ye ka tigi kabiri selei laŋa ne to. Kadwi selo Vini teeni na wo se wone to maa tigi chwoŋa kam jazem de jagwia ne. Maleka kam maa zege da ka che chwoŋa kam. 25Bonaga kam daa ma na Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam. Ka ma peene ka tete de kabira kam pa se kabiri kam kweere Balaam napere. O daa ma mage o bonaga kam.
26 Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ta ma fɔɔre ka yi ka zege chwoŋa kam mɛ na tiini ka peene to ne. Laŋa daa tera se bonaga kam tɔge jazem naa jagwia seeni ka kɛ. 27Ka de na nɛ konto to, mo ka to tega ne ka tiga. Balaam daa maa ware o bane o ja. O ma kwei o nacheiga o jege bonaga kam o maga. 28Se nɛ sem ni ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ bonaga kam chwoŋa se ka ŋɔɔne. Ka ma bwei Balaam ka we, “Bɛ mo a ke a chɔge pa se n yɔɔre n mage-ne kuni betɔ tento dwoŋi?” 29Balaam ma leiri-ka o we, “Ko ye nmo na pɛ se a nye de jworo to ŋwaane mo. A ya ná maŋe a jege se-zɔɔ ywo-seeni, a ya wó go‑m lela.”
30Bonaga kam laam maa we, “Amo dae nmo tete bonaga mo ye n jege-ne n diini maŋa maama na? A nam yeini a ke tento dwoŋi nmo yera ne na?” Balaam ma leiri we, “Aawo! N ta wo ke tento dwoŋi.”
31Konto baŋa ne mo Baŋa Wɛ pore Balaam yia, pa se o na Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam na chege chwoŋa kam ka zega ye se-zɔɔ wo ka jeŋa ne to. Balaam na nɛ to, o ma tiiri o vwi o yibia tega ne.
32Maleka kam ma bwei‑o ka we, “Bɛŋwaane mo nmo mage n bonaga kam kuni betɔ konto? Amo nwoŋi se a ba a dwoni de nmo, kokuri to, a nɛ we chwoŋa kalo n na kwei to ba jege kuri. 33Ko ná dae n bonaga kam ŋwaane, tento a ya go‑m. Ka nɛ-ne mo pa se ka ywori chwoŋa kam ne kuni betɔ. Ko ya ná dae konto, a ya wó go‑m ye a daare a yage n bonaga kam pa se ka viiri.”
34Balaam ma leiri maleka kam o we, “Amo ke a tusi. A ya yeiri we nmo chege chwoŋa mo se n dwoni de amo. De ko de, nmo yi ná wo su a veiŋa kam, amo wó jwoori sɔŋɔ.”
35 Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ma ta ded‑o ka we, “Ta tɔge de nɔɔna bam n kɛ. Nam lɔre se n ta kolo yerane amo na wó bere‑m se n ta to.” Balaam laam ma da de Balaki dedɛɛra bam o kɛ.
36Balaki na nigi we Balaam wo chwoŋa ne o beene o tei to, mo o nwoŋi o vo se o jeeri‑o Moaba teo kodwoŋi ne. Ko déem wo Aranon buga kam ni ne mo, se ko maŋe de o laŋa kam siseini. 37O na yi da to, o ma bwei Balaam o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n wo sɛ a kwora kam a na toŋe to? Bɛ mo ye n wo tu lela? Nmo boŋe se a jeŋa muri se a ŋwe‑m mo na?” 38Balaam ma leiri‑o o we, “Ko ná ye tei maama, a laam tua. A nam ba jege chwoŋa se a ta taane se de dwoni tei yerane Wɛ na bere-ne se a ta to.”
39Ba ma tɔge daane ba vo Kiriaf-Huzofa. 40Ba na yi da to, Balaki ma kwei naane de pei o ke kaanem. O ma fɔ nɔna yam wone o kwei o pa Balaam de o teo dedɛɛra balo na tɔge ded‑o to. 41Tega na poore to, Balaki ma zaŋe o ja Balaam o vo Bamofe-Baal. Balaam na zege dáane to, o wae o nii o nae Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom wone nɔɔna bam badaara.

english_text:
Balaam's First Message
1Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
2After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar. 3Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
4When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
5The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak. 6When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
7Balaam said:
“King Balak of Moab brought me
from the hills of Syria
to curse Israel
and announce its doom.
8But I can't go against God!
He did not curse
or condemn Israel.
* 9“From the mountain peaks,
I look down and see Israel,
the obedient people of God.
10They are living alone in peace.
And though they are many,
they don't bother
the other nations.
“I hope to obey God
for as long as I live
and to die in such peace.”
11Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
12Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.”
Balaam's Second Message
13Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.” 14So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
15“Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
16The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak. 17Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings.
Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
18Balaam answered:
“Pay close attention
to my words—
19God is no mere human!
He doesn't tell lies
or change his mind.
God always keeps his promises.
20“My command from God
was to bless these people,
and there's nothing I can do
to change what he has done.
21Israel's king is the Lord God.
He lives there with them
and intends them no harm.
22With the strength of a wild ox,
God led Israel out of Egypt.
23No magic charms can work
against them—
just look what God has done
for his people.
24They are like angry lions
ready to attack;
and they won't rest
until their victim
is gobbled up.”
25Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
26“I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.”
Balaam's Third Message
27Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.” 28So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
29Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
30After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_text:
Balaam boboa taane dem
1Balaam ma ta de Balaki o we, “Pa se ba ke kaanem bimbina yarepɛ jei sem konto ne, se n daare n ja na-bale serepɛ dedaane pi-bɛ serepɛ n ba n pa-ne.” 2Balaki ma seene o ke konto. Ba balei ma kwei na-bala de pi-bea ba ma ke kaanem bimbini maama baŋa ne.
3Balaam laam ma ta de Balaki o we, “Ta‑n zege n zwɛɛm pɛɛra yam teiŋa ne konto. Amo wó fɔɔre a vo dáa se a nii Baŋa Wɛ wó jeeri-ne na? O ná veere kolo maama de amo, amo de wó ba a ta a bere‑m.” O laam ma vo o di peo yuu mɛ teeni na tera to.
4Wɛ ma ba o tei. Balaam ma ta o we, “Amo ke bimbina yarepɛ mo, ye a kaane na-bala de pi-bea bimbini maama baŋa ne.” 5Baŋa Wɛ ma kwei o kwora o pa Balaam ye o ta ded‑o we, “Nam jwoori Balaki tei, se n ta amo kwora kam n bere‑o.”
6Balaam ma jwoori Balaki tei, dedaane o ta zege o zwɛɛm pɛɛra yam teiŋa ne mo. Moaba dedɛɛra bam de maa wo o tei ne. 7Balaam ma bobo se o tole taane dem ye o we:
“Moaba teo pɛ Balaki mo jaane amo
o pa a nwoŋi Aram peero tem na wo wɛ-puli seeni to ne
a ba ywo-seeni.
O maa boŋe se a sɔɔle lwarem
a daŋe Isarele tiina bam yuu ne
se ko chɔge-ba.
8Wɛ nam na wo sɔɔle lwarem o pa Isarele tiina bam to ŋwaane,
amo wó ke tɛ mo a sɔɔle lwarem a daŋe ba yuu ne?
Amo wó na chwoŋa yein-seeni mo se a bwɛ-ba,
ye Baŋa Wɛ wo bwɛ-ba?
9Amo na zege peero tem yuu ne to,
a yɔɔre a na-ba mo.
Isarele dwi tiina ye balo na pɔɔre ba tete
se ba yé tɔge ba taa wo dwi-gɛ tiina bam wone to mo.
10Isarele tiina bam kɔgɔ daga dedɛ
ne kasol-bia na ye tei to mo.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware-ba se o ga o ti.
Amo ná lage a te,
Wɛ wó pa se a toone taa nye de nɔn-ŋona toone na ye tei to mo,
pa se a ŋwea kweeli de bochare-zuru.”
11Balaam na tole taane dem o ti to, mo Balaki tage ded‑o o we, “Bɛ mo konto n jege n ke a yera ne? A bwoŋi‑m se n ba n sɔɔle lwarem mo n yage a dona baŋa ne. Nmo daa‑n ma‑n zege n sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n pa-ba.” 12Balaam ma leiri‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ nam ná we a ta kolo, ko dae se a ta konto yerane mo na?”
Balaam taane belei tu
13Balaki daa ma ta‑o o we, “Ba se dé vo jeiga kadwoŋi. Nmo wó na Isarele tiina bam badwonna da, ye ko dae ba maama. Nmo laam ma‑n wó zege dáane n sɔɔle lwarem n yage ba baŋa ne.” 14O ma ja Balaam o vo o di Pisiga peo kom yuu o zege Zofim te-kampare jei sem ne. Balaam daa ma lɔ kaanem bimbina yarepɛ. O ta ma kwei na-bala de pi-bea o daŋe kaanem bimbini maama baŋa ne. 15Balaam ma ta de Balaki o we, “Ta‑n zege n zwɛɛm pɛɛra yam teiŋa ne konto. Amo wó fɔɔre a vo dáa se a jeeri de Baŋa Wɛ.”
16 Baŋa Wɛ daa maa jeeri‑o, ye o daare o kwei o kwora o pa Balaam ye o we, “Jwoori Balaki tei se n ta amo kwora kam n bere‑o.”
17Balaam ta na jwoori Balaki tei to, dedaane o ta zege o zwɛɛm pɛɛra yam teiŋa ne mo. Moaba dedɛɛra bam ta maa wo o tei ne. Balaki ma bwei Balaam o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wom tage o we bɛ mo?”
18Balaam ma bobo se o tole taane dem ye o we:
“Zipore bu Balaki, ba n cheigi a taane dem!
Fɔge n cheigi se n ni ko kuri chekke.
19Wɛ dae nabiinu,
se o taa kare o fɔe vwa,
naa se o taa jege ni-zɛ ni-zɛ.
O ná yeini o gwoni o ni,
o seene o ke o tɔge o na tage tei to mo.
20Wɛ pɛ-ne ni se a sɔɔle swolim mo
a daŋe nɔɔna banto yuu ne.
Wonto nam ná swɛ wolo swolim,
ko daa ware ko kwane.
21Amo nii a na Isarele tiina bam
na ye tei to.
Cham de wo-chechɔgɔ bá yi-ba.
Ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo wo ba tei ne.
Ba maa zeiŋi o yere we,
o ye ba Pɛ.
22 Baŋa Wɛ mo jaane-ba o nwoŋi Ejipti wone.
O na jaŋe tei o pa-ba to
nye de nabea kalo na ware ka ja to mo.
23Liri tera se na wó wane Isarele dwi tiina bam se chɔge.
Yi-nɛɛre de ba toŋa ba yera ne pa se ko bwei-ba.
Nɔɔna wó taa tɛ Jakob bia bam taane ba we,
‘Nii-na Wɛ na ke kolo o pa-ba to.’
24Nii-na! Ba kɔgɔ kom nye de nywoŋo!
Ko lage ko zaŋe ko zi varem mo ko di.
Ko daa bá peini ko sii,
ye ko wo done nɔna yam maama ko su,
ko daare ko nyɔ vara bam jana ko ti.”
25Balaam na tole taane dem o ti to, mo Balaki bage‑o ye o we, “Yage! Nmo ná ware n sɔɔle lwarem n ke ba yera ne, nam yé sɔɔle lam n ke ba yuu ne!” 26Balaam ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo maŋe a pa se n maane we kolo Baŋa Wɛ na tage de amo to yerane mo a jege se a ta.”
Balaam taane betɔ tu
27Balaki daa ma ta de Balaam o we, “Pa se dé daa leiri jeiga, se dɛ delo Wɛ wó pa‑m chwoŋa dáane se n sɔɔle lwarem n daŋe Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne n pa-ne.” 28O ma ja Balaam o vo o di Peora peo kom yuu ne. Jeiga kam konto tole ka nii kagoa kam mo.
29Balaam ma ta de Balaki o we, “Nam lɔ kaanem bimbina yarepɛ ywo-seeni, se n daare n ja na-bale serepɛ de pi-bɛ serepɛ n ba n pa-ne.” 30Balaki ma ke konto, pa se Balaam kwei na-bala de pi-bea o kaane bimbini maama baŋa ne.

english_text:
1Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert 2and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him, 3and Balaam said:
“I am the son of Beor,
and my words are true,
so listen to my message!
4It comes from the Lord,
the God All-Powerful.
I bowed down to him
and saw a vision of Israel.
5“People of Israel,
your camp is lovely.
6It's like a grove of palm trees
or a garden beside a river.
You are like tall aloe trees
that the Lord has planted,
or like cedars
growing near water.
7You and your descendants
will prosper like an orchard
beside a stream.
Your king will rule with power
and be a greater king
than Agag the Amalekite.
8With the strength of a wild ox,
God led you out of Egypt.
You will defeat your enemies,
shooting them with arrows
and crushing their bones.
9 Like a lion you lie down,
resting after an attack.
Who would dare disturb you?
“Anyone who blesses you
will be blessed;
anyone who curses you
will be cursed.”
10When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times. 11Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
12Balaam answered, “I told your messengers 13that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me. 14So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.”
Balaam's Fourth Message
15Balaam said:
“I am the son of Beor,
and my words are true,
so listen to my message!
16My knowledge comes
from God Most High,
the Lord All-Powerful.
I bowed down to him
and saw a vision of Israel.
17“What I saw in my vision
hasn't happened yet.
But someday, a king of Israel
will appear like a star.
He will wipe out you Moabites
and destroy those tribes
who live in the desert.
18Israel will conquer Edom
and capture the land
of that enemy nation.
19The king of Israel will rule
and destroy the survivors
of every town there.
20“And I saw this vision
about the Amalekites:
Their nation is now great,
but it will someday
disappear forever.
21“And this is what I saw
about the Kenites:
They think they're safe,
living among the rocks,
22but they will be wiped out
when Assyria conquers them.
23“No one can survive
if God plans destruction.
24Ships will come from Cyprus,
bringing people who will invade
the lands of Assyria and Eber.
But finally, Cyprus itself
will be ruined.”
25After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_text:
1Balaam déem yɔɔre o lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ lage se o swɛ Isarele tiina bam swolim mo. Konto ŋwaane, o daa wo nii o tankwa yam wone se o lɔre kolo na wora, nenɛɛne o ya na maŋe o ke tei to. O ma pipiri o yibia o nii kagoa kam seeni. 2O ma kwoni o nii o na Isarele tiina bam na chwi ba vwoa yam dwi de dwi. Se nɛ sem ni ne mo Wɛ Jworo tu o baŋa ne. 3O ma bobo se o tole taane dem o we:
“Amo, Beora bu Balaam taane mo tento.
A yi-nɛɛre dem pae se a lɔre wonnu jaja.
4A maa yeini a ni Wɛ kwora,
pa se a lwoni o taane dem a bere nɔɔna.
A vwi a yibia tega ne ye a ta nae mo,
pa se Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom veere wonnu o bere-ne.
5Isarele tiina bam,
