Dé ná seene dé ke konto, wonto de wó taa nii debam baŋa ne, ye o daare o pa se dé woŋo maama da chwoŋa ko pa debam, nenɛɛne ko na ye tei zem to. 25Dé ná seene dé yia dé tɔge o bera yam konto maama, nenɛɛne o na pɛ debam ni tei to, ko wó pa dé na chega o yiga ne.’ ”

english_text:
Force the Other Nations Out of the Land
(Exodus 34.11-16)
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, the Lord your God will help you take the land of the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. These seven nations have more people and are stronger than Israel, but when you attack them, 2the Lord will force them out of the land. Then you must destroy them without mercy. Don't make any peace treaties with them, 3and don't let your sons and daughters marry any of them. 4If you do, those people will lead your descendants to worship other gods and to turn their backs on the Lord. That will make him very angry, and he will quickly destroy Israel.
5 So when you conquer these nations, tear down the altars where they worship their gods. Break up their sacred stones, cut down the poles that they use in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and throw their idols in the fire.
The Lord's Chosen People
Moses said:
6 Israel, you are the chosen people of the Lord your God. There are many nations on this earth, but he chose only Israel to be his very own. 7You were the weakest of all nations, 8but the Lord chose you because he loves you and because he had made a promise to your ancestors. Then with his mighty arm, he rescued you from the king of Egypt, who had made you his slaves.
9 You know that the Lord your God is the only true God. So love him and obey his commands, and he will faithfully keep his agreement with you and your descendants for a thousand generations. 10But if you turn against the Lord, he will quickly destroy you. 11So be sure to obey his laws and teachings I am giving you today.
The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey
(Deuteronomy 28.1-14; Leviticus 26.3-13)
Moses said to Israel:
12 If you completely obey these laws, the Lord your God will be loyal and keep the agreement he made with you, just as he promised our ancestors. 13The Lord will love you and bless you by giving you many children and plenty of food, wine, and olive oil. Your herds of cattle will have many calves, and your flocks of sheep will have many lambs. 14God will bless you more than any other nation—your families will grow and your livestock increase. 15You will no longer suffer with the same horrible diseases that you sometimes had in Egypt. You will be healthy, but the Lord will make your enemies suffer from those diseases.
Destroy the Nations and Their Gods
Moses said to Israel:
16When the Lord helps you defeat your enemies, you must destroy them without pity! And don't get trapped into worshiping their gods.
17You may be thinking, “How can we destroy these nations? They are more powerful than we are.” 18But stop worrying! Just remember what the Lord your God did to Egypt and its king. 19You saw how the Lord used his tremendous power to work great miracles and bring you out of Egypt. And he will again work miracles for you when you face these enemies you fear so much. 20Some of them may try to survive by hiding from you, but the Lord will make them panic, and soon they will be dead. 21So don't be frightened when you meet them in battle. The Lord your God is great and fearsome, and he will fight at your side.
22As you attack these nations, the Lord will force them out little by little. He won't let you get rid of them all at once—if he did, there wouldn't be enough people living in the land to keep down the number of wild animals. 23-24But when you attack your enemies, the Lord will make them panic, and you will easily destroy them. You will defeat their kings one after another until they are gone, and no one will remember they ever lived.
25After you conquer a nation, burn their idols. Don't get trapped into wanting the silver or gold on an idol. Even the metal on an idol is disgusting to the Lord, 26so destroy it. If you bring it home with you, both you and your house will be destroyed. Stay away from those disgusting idols!
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na tei o nɔɔna bam tei to
1“Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó pa á ta‑á tei tega kalo á na lage á zo leile to. O maa wó pa á na dam se á di dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ ye á zeili-ba tega kam ne: Hiti tiina bam, de Giragasi tiina bam, de Amori tiina bam, de Kanaan tiina bam, de Pɛrizi tiina bam, de Hivi tiina ko woli de Jebusi tiina bam. Dwia konto maama yarepɛ daga dedɛ ye ya ta damma ya dwoi abam. 2Baŋa Wɛ nam wó ke-ba á jeŋa ne se á wane-ba á di. O ná seene o ke konto, se á yɔɔre á chɔge-ba. Abam nam yé ke-na ni-sɛɛm de-ba, naa á duri ba ŋwaŋa de fee de. 3Daa ta lɔre-na se á yé kwei ba bukwa á ma á ji á kaana, naa á kwei-ba á pa á bia. Nam yé zaŋe-na á kwei á tete bukwa á pa-ba se ba di ba ma ba ke ba kaana. 4Abam ná sɛ pa se konto ke, ba wó soge á bia mo pa se ba tusi ba taa zuli wa-yɔɔro ye ba daare ba lɔ Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne. Konto nam wó pa se Baŋa Wɛ bane mo zaŋe abam baŋa ne se o chɔge abam lela.
5Konto ŋwaane, abam ná wane dwi-gɛ tiina bam konto, se á mage ba kaanem bimbina yam á de tega ne. Á ta jege se á lɔ kandwa yalo ba na chwi ba jwona ŋwaane to. Gwoni-na ba Asera nyenyego dɛ sem á de tega ne, se á daare á ke mini á zwɛ ba jwona yam maama. 6Kokuri to, abam ye nɔɔna balo na ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom nyem mo. O déem kuri abam mo logo baŋa dwi maama wone se á ta‑á ye wonto tete lonne jejegero.
7Nam lɔre-na we Baŋa Wɛ na kuri abam konto to, ko dae we á kɔgɔ mo daga ko dwoi dwi-gɛ tiina maama. Chega ŋwaane to, abam déem mo tiini á muri nɔɔna maama wone. 8Ko nam ye o na jege abam swono to ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ kuri abam se á ta‑á ye o nyem. Ko ta maa ye o na pwooli dedaane á nabaara bam se o ke tei to ŋwaane mo. Mo kokuri o déem toŋe de dam o jwoŋi abam Ejipti Pa-faro wom jeŋa ne o yage pa se á nwoŋi teo kolo á ya na ye kabɛ da to wone. 9Ta‑á yei-na we abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yerane mo ye Wɛ chekke. Á wae á sale‑o, ye o bá kwane o ni de ni-gwonim delo o na ke o swono kom ŋwaane to. O ta wó taa swoi balo na swoi‑o ye ba tɔge o nia yam to, ye o bá yage-ba, se ko yi ba dwi dem kuni moro laŋa ne. 10Ko nam ná ye balo na ve‑o to, o wó yɔɔre o waare-ba. O bá dáane ye o chɔge-ba lela. 11Mo kokuri, ta‑á yei-na se á ta‑á toŋe á tɔge Wɛ nia yam, de o bera yam, de o chullu tem, ne amo na pɛ abam zem to.
Wɛ swolim na wó ba ba baŋa tei to
12Abam ná cheigi Wɛ nia yanto ye á daare á toŋe á tɔge-ya de chega, Baŋa Wɛ swono kolo na ba ti to de wó taa wora de abam, ne o na gwoni ni tei de á nabaara bam to. 13O wó taa swoi abam, ye o swɛ abam swolim pa se á kɔgɔ kom puli dedɛ. Á ná zo tega kalo Baŋa Wɛ na pwooli de á nabaara bam se o pa abam to, o zaane wó taa wo á bia baŋa ne, de á wodiiru baŋa ne, ne ko ná ye mena, de sana, de nuga maama. O zaane ta wó taa wo á vara baŋa ne, á naane, de á pei, dedaane de bia maama 14Abam wó na Wɛ swolim á dwoni tega baŋa dwia yam konto maama. Wolo na ba lore to, naa varem wolo na ba lore to daa bá taa wo abam wone. 15Baŋa Wɛ tete mo wó che abam de jaweero dwi maama. O bá pa chwoŋa se jawe-chɛɛro telo dwi na to Ejipti tiina bam yera ne to ba abam baŋa. O nam wó kwei-te o ke á dona yera ne mo. 16Nam chɔge-na dwi-gɛ tiina balo maama Baŋa Wɛ na wó kwei o ke á jeŋa ne se á chɔge to. Yé duri-na ba yibwona, nam yé zuli-na nɔɔna bam konto jwona. Abam ná ke konto, ba wó soge abam se á tusi amo yiga ne.
17Abam wae á boŋe á tete ne we, ‘Debam bá wane teene dento nɔɔna dé zeili, ba na tiini ba dana ba dwoi debam to ŋwaane.’ 18Nam yé ta‑á fona de-ba. Guli-na abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe tei o chɔge Ejipti Pɛ wom de o nɔn-bia bam to. 19Abam tete yi mo nɛ Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge o dam baŋa ne o toŋe wo-kamunnu dedaane wo-kenkagela pa se jawe-chɛɛro ja Ejipti tiina bam ye o daare o vere abam ba jeŋa ne tei to. Guli-na á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom déem na ke tei, se o ta wó ma dam dem konto mo o chɔge nɔɔna banto abam laam na kɔre tento to. 20O maa wó pa se vuvuga to á dona tetare ne, se balo na duri ba lu ba seigi to tete de na chɔgem. 21Mo kokuri, á ba jege se á ta‑á kɔre nɔɔna bam konto. Baŋa Wɛ wora de abam. Wonto nam mo jege dam-fɔrɔ ye o maŋe se nɔɔna taa kɔre‑o. 22Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom tete mo lage o taa zeili dwi-gɛ tiina bam konto o yage fee fee se abam zo ba tega kam wone. Abam bá yɔɔre á zeili-ba bedwe baŋa ne. Ko ná ke konto, kago-vara mo wó puli da ba daane abam. 23Baŋa Wɛ nam wó kwei á dona bam o ke á jeŋa ne. O wó de vuvuga ba tetare ne, se ba na chɔgem ba ti. 24O maa wó kwei ba pwa o ke á jeŋa ne, se á go-ba pa se ba dwi saare logo baŋa ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane abam o che de á na lage á ke kolo to. Abam maa wó chɔge ba maama. 25Zwɛ-na ba jwona yam. Yé pa-na se á fera zo sabu-seŋa, naa lu-nyenno telo na wo jwona yam yera ne to. Nam yé lɔɔne-na-te. Abam ná ke konto, te wó ja abam ne kalanchogo tei. Jwona kaanem ye totoŋ-vɛɛsa mo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. 26Yé ja-na wo-zɔɔna yam konto dwi á zo á sam wone, se konto ná kea abam de wó na chɔgem mo ne wonnu tem konto na maŋe de chɔgem tei to. Yɔɔre á ta‑á chuli-te-na, se te maŋe de chɔgem mo.”

english_text:
The Lord Takes Care of You
Moses said:
1Israel, do you want to go into the land the Lord promised your ancestors? Do you want to capture it, live there, and become a powerful nation? Then be sure to obey every command I am giving you.
2Don't forget how the Lord your God has led you through the desert for the past 40 years. He wanted to find out if you were truly willing to obey him and depend on him, 3 so he made you go hungry. Then he gave you manna, a kind of food that you and your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was teaching you that people need more than food to live—they need every word that the Lord has spoken.
4Over the past 40 years, your clothing hasn't worn out, and your feet haven't swollen. 5 So keep in mind that the Lord has been correcting you, just as parents correct their children. 6Obey the commands the Lord your God has given you and worship him with fear and trembling.
7The Lord your God is bringing you into a good land with streams that flow from springs in the valleys and hills. 8-9You can dig for copper in those hills, and the stones are made of iron ore. And you won't go hungry. Wheat and barley fields are everywhere, and so are vineyards and orchards full of fig, pomegranate, and olive trees, and there is plenty of honey.
Don't Forget the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10After you eat and are full, give praise to the Lord your God for the good land he gave you. 11 Make sure that you never forget the Lord or disobey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. If you always obey them, 12you will have plenty to eat, and you will build good houses to live in. 13You will get more and more cattle, sheep, silver, gold, and other possessions.
14But when all this happens, don't be proud! Don't forget that you were once slaves in Egypt and that it was the Lord who set you free. 15Remember how he led you in that huge and frightening desert where poisonous snakes and scorpions live. There was no water, but the Lord split open a rock, and water poured out so you could drink. 16He also gave you manna, a kind of food your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was testing you to make you trust him, so that later on he could be good to you.
17When you become successful, don't say, “I'm rich, and I've earned it all myself.” 18Instead, remember that the Lord your God gives you the strength to make a living. That's how he keeps the promise he made to your ancestors.
19-20But I'm warning you—if you forget the Lord your God and worship other gods, the Lord will destroy you, just as he destroyed the nations you fought.
translation_text:
Ba yé swei Baŋa Wɛ swia
1“Nam toŋe-na á tɔge Wɛ ni delo maama a na pɛ abam zem tento to de chega, se ko pa á ta‑á ŋwe ye á kɔgɔ kom puli dedɛ. Abam maa wó zo tega kalo Baŋa Wɛ na gwoni ni de á nabaara bam se o pa abam to wo á ta‑á tei. 2Guli-na we abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom déem tɔge abam yiga kagoa chwo-dɔrɔ kom ne bena finna mo. O ma pa se cham dedɛ yi abam se o ma pa á yage kamunni, se o daare o lɔre kolo na wo á bochare ne to mo, se o nii á wó sɛ o ni naa á bá sɛ. 3O na pɛ se á tu á tete tei to, o pɛ se kana mo ni abam, ye o laam pa abam Manna se á di. Konto nam ye wodiu kolo abam de á nabaara ya na yeiri to mo. O nam ke konto se ko pa se abam lɔre we ko dae wodiu yerane mo pae se nabiina ŋwe, se ko ye Baŋa Wɛ ni taane dem maama mo pae nɔɔna ŋwea. 4Bena finna yam konto maama wone abam gwaaro tem wo zareme, ye á napera de wo foose chwoŋa kam cham ŋwaane. 5Nam maane-na á bochare ne we á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom de yɔɔre o korese abam mo, ne kwo na korese o bu tei to.
6Konto to, yɔɔre á sɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ nia yam. Ta‑á tɔge-na o chwei sem, se á daare á ta‑á kɔre‑o. 7Kokuri to, abam Baŋa Wɛ wom jege abam o zoore te-ŋoŋa wone mo. Bu-tole, de chwaro mo wo ka wone, ye buli-yia tae ya nwoŋi ka bwollu de ka peero jei sem ne. 8Tega kam konto ke mena dwi dwi, de Vini teeni, de kaporro, ko ta woli de Pomegara teeni, de Olivi teeni, dedaane tooro. 9Jei sem konto ne wodiiru gaale, ye kolokolo zore bá ja abam. Tega kam peero jege luuru te wone, ye channa-seŋa de wo ka zwonnu tem wone.
10Abam nam ná di ka wodiiru á su, se á tei á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom de te-ŋoŋa kalo o na pɛ abam to. 11Ta‑á yere-na á tete se á yé swei abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Yé swei-na o ni ne, se á ve o nia yam, de o bera yam, de o chullu tem a na pɛ abam zem to. 12Ko ná dae konto, abam ná di tega kam wodiiru á su, ye á ta lɔ sɔ-laaro á zoore te wone, 13ye á vara de ná puli dedɛ, ye á lu-nyenno de á sabu-seŋa daga pa se á jejegero tem puli te pa abam, 14á wó bere á tete, ye á swei á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ni ne. Wonto nam mo ye wolo na jaane abam o ja nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne pa se o vere abam á kabɛɛne dem ne o yage to. 15O ma ja abam o tɔge kagoa kam wone, ka na yala ye ka tiini ka jege foone ka pa abam to. Basankwe selo ni na chamma to wora, ye nwanno de gaale. Jeiga kam konto na koge ye na tera jei jei to, o pɛ se na ta ba nwoŋi pe-liliru wone. 16Kagoa kam wone mo Baŋa Wɛ yɔɔre o kwei Manna o kɔne abam. Ko nam ye wodiu kolo á nabaara na yeiri to mo. O ma pa se cham dedɛ yi abam se o ma pa á tu á tete, se o daare o faŋe abam o nii, se ko kwaga seeni á ŋwea ke lanyerane ka pa abam. 17Konto ŋwaane, abam wolowolo yé fɔge o boŋe o tete ne we, ‘Amo dam de a jeŋa totoŋa mo pɛ-ne a jejegero tem.’ 18Nam guli-na we, ko ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo pae abam dam se á ma á ji naduna. O nam ke konto se ni-gwonim delo o na ke de á nabaara bam to mo su lanyerane, ne ko na ye tei de zem maama tento to.
19Yé swei-na á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ni ne se á pipiri á beeri wa yadwonna se á zuli-ya. Chega ŋwaane to, abam ná ke konto, ko wó bwei abam mo. 20Baŋa Wɛ wó ke abam ne o na lage o ke tei de teene delo na wora ye abam laam lage á zo ba tega kam wone to mo. O wó yɔɔre o chɔge abam mo, á na wo sɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora to ŋwaane.”

english_text:
Why the Lord Will Help Israel
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to me! You will soon cross the Jordan River and go into the land to force out the nations that live there. They are more powerful than you are, and the walls around their cities reach to the sky. 2Some of these nations are descendants of the Anakim. You know how tall and strong they are, and you've heard that no one can defeat them in battle. 3But the Lord your God has promised to go ahead of you, like a raging fire burning everything in its path. So when you attack your enemies, it will be easy for you to destroy them and take their land.
4-6After the Lord helps you wipe out these nations and conquer their land, don't think he did it because you are such good people. You aren't good—you are stubborn! No, the Lord is going to help you, because the nations that live there are evil, and because he wants to keep the promise he made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
When Israel Made an Idol
(Exodus 32)
Moses said to Israel:
7Don't ever forget how you kept rebelling and making the Lord angry the whole time you were in the desert. You rebelled from the day you left Egypt until the day you arrived here.
8At Mount Sinai you made the Lord so angry that he was going to destroy you. 9-11 It happened during those 40 days and nights that I was on the mountain, without anything to eat or drink. He had told me to come up there so he could give me the agreement he made with us. And this agreement was actually the same Ten Commandments he had announced to you when he spoke from the fire on the mountain. The Lord had written them on two flat stones with his own hand. But after giving me the two stones, 12he said:
Moses, hurry down the mountain to those people you led out of Egypt. They have already disobeyed me and committed the terrible sin of making an idol.
13I've been watching the Israelites, and I've seen how stubborn and rebellious they are. 14So don't try to stop me! I am going to wipe them out, and no one on earth will remember they ever lived. Then I will let your descendants become an even bigger and more powerful nation than Israel.
Moses said:
15Fire was raging on the mountaintop as I went back down, carrying the two stones with the commandments on them. 16I saw how quickly you had sinned and disobeyed the Lord your God. There you were, worshiping the metal idol you had made in the shape of a calf. 17So I threw down the two stones and smashed them before your very eyes.
18-20I bowed down at the place of worship and prayed to the Lord, without eating or drinking for 40 days and nights. You had committed a terrible sin by making that idol, and the Lord hated what you had done. He was angry enough to destroy all of you and Aaron as well. So I prayed for you and Aaron as I had done before, and this time the Lord answered my prayers.
21It was a sin for you to make that idol, so I threw it into the fire to melt it down. Then I took the lump of gold, ground it into powder, and threw the powder into the stream flowing down the mountain.
22 You also made the Lord angry when you were staying at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-Hattaavah. 23 Then at Kadesh-Barnea the Lord said, “I am giving you the land, so go ahead and take it!” But since you didn't trust the Lord, you rebelled and disobeyed his command. 24In fact, you've rebelled against the Lord for as long as he has known you.
25After you had made the idol in the shape of a calf, the Lord said he was going to destroy you. So I lay face down in front of the Lord for 40 days and nights 26and prayed:
Our Lord, please don't wipe out your people. You used your great power to rescue them from Egypt and to make them your very own. 27Israel's ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob obeyed you faithfully. Think about them, and not about Israel's stubbornness, evil, and sin. 28If you destroy your people, the Egyptians will say, “The Lord promised to give Israel land, but he wasn't powerful enough to keep his promise. In fact, he hated them so much that he took them into the desert and killed them.” 29But you, our Lord, chose the people of Israel to be your own, and with your mighty power you rescued them from Egypt.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ zeina yam taane
1“Isarele tiina bam, cheigi-na! Abam zem lage á bɛ Jɔdan buga kam mo, se á zeili dwia yalo na daga ye ba ta dana ba dwoi abam to ba tega kam ne. Nɔɔna bam konto zoore te-fwaaro wone, te kabiri sem na diini wɛɛne vili vili se yi wɛyuu to mo. 2Ba maa dɔra ye ba ta dana. Ba ye nɔn-sawaara balo na nwoŋi Anaki dwi dem ne to mo. Abam nam nigi ba na tɛ ba taane we, ‘Wɔ mo wó wane o dwoni de Anaki tiina bam?’ 3Nam lɔre-na we á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom lage o da á yiga o bɛ buga kam, se o chɔge-ba mo. Ko wó taa nye de min-fɔrɔ na di wo-yɔɔro maama kula tei to mo. Maŋa kalo abam na wó vo á zo da to mo o lage o di-ba, se á wane-ba á zeili á daare á chɔge-ba lela ne Baŋa Wɛ na pwooli de abam tei to.
4 Baŋa Wɛ nam ná zeili-ba konto o pa abam, yé ta-na á tete ne we, ‘Debam totoŋ-ŋona ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ kwei tega kanto o pa debam se dé taa tei!’ Aawo! Ko ye tega kam tiina totoŋ-lwanno ŋwaane mo o lage o zeili-ba. 5Ko dae á na ye nɔn-ŋona, ye á kikia tɔge chega to ŋwaane mo abam lage á jwoŋi ba tega kam á ta‑á tei. Ko ye banto wo-zɔɔna kikia ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ wó zeili-ba, se ko ke ne o na pwooli de á nabaara Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob tei to. 6Lɔre-na we abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ba lage o pa abam te-ŋoŋa kanto á na ye nɔn-ŋona to ŋwaane, se abam dae kɔtaa! Abam nam yɔɔre á ye zwabani-nyena mo.
Sabu-seŋa na-mɔra jwoni dem gula
7Guli-na abam déem na wo kagoa kam ne ye á tiini á pa se á Tu Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe tei to. Ko na zege dɛ delo ne abam na nwoŋi Ejipti ne, se ko yi á na zege ywo leile to, abam yɔɔre á lɔ o kwaga ne mo maŋa maama. 8Sinayi peo kom ne mo á tiini á chuchugi o bane pa se o lage se o chɔge abam. 9Amo déem diini peo kom yuu ne mo, se a jwoŋi kandwa-pelɛ selei selo baŋa ne Baŋa Wɛ ni-sɛɛm dem o na ke de abam to na popone de ke da to. A ma maŋe dáane da finna, wea de tete maama, ye a ba di wodiu, a nam ba nyɔ na. 10Baŋa Wɛ ma kwei kandwa yalei yam o na mɛ o tete jeŋa o popone o nia yam maama ya baŋa ne to o pa-ne. Dɛ dem Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama na jeeri peo kom teiŋa ne to, mo Baŋa Wɛ zege peo kom yuu ne o ŋɔɔne min-vogo wone de abam.
11Amo na ke da finna peo kom yuu ne wea de tete maama to, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwei kandwa yalei yam, o na popone ni-sɛɛm dem ya baŋa ne to o pa-ne. 12Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta amo o we, ‘Ke lela n tu tega se n yi nɔɔna balo n na jaane n nwoŋi Ejipti ne to tei. Ba chɔge ba tete mo, ye ba ta ke wɛleere. Ba gare ba yage ni delo a na pɛ-ba se ba taa tɔge to mo, ye ba ma sabu-seŋa ba ke jwoni ba pa ba tete.’
13 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de amo o we, ‘Amo yei nɔɔna banto na ye balo to. Ba yɔɔre ba ye zwabani-nyena mo. 14Nam ta‑n zege dáa ne n nii-ne. A lage a chɔge-ba mo se ba yere saare logo baŋa maama ne. Amo laam maa wó zege nmo baŋa ne, a pa se te-fɔrɔ bobo de nmo kwaga kam. Banto teo kom maa wó taa daga ye ko dana ko dwoi nɔɔna banto na ye tei leile to.’
15Amo ma seene a pipiri a zege peo kom yuu ne a tu tega, ye a zei kandwa-pelɛ selei selo baŋa ne ni-sɛɛm dem na popone de ke da to. Peo kom nam ya ta yɔɔre ko di de min-vogo mo. 16Amo na seene a nii to, a nɛ sabu-seŋa na-mɔra kalo abam na mɔɔne se ka taa ye á jwoni to. A ta nɛ we á ke lela á ywori Baŋa Wɛ chwoŋa wone ye á ke wɛleere o yiga ne. 17A na nɛ konto to, mo a de yɔɔre a zeiŋi ni-sɛɛm kandwa yalo a ya na zei to wɛɛne, ye a feiri-ya tega ne a lɔ. Abam yibia ne mo a ke keim dem konto.
18Amo daa ma vwi a yibia tega ne Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne pa se da finna maama wone a ba di kolokolo, a nam ba nyɔ na, wea de tete maama. A ke konto bɛŋwaane abam ke wɛleere delo Baŋa Wɛ na yɔɔre o chuli to ye á pa se o bane tiini de zaŋe. 19Foone ya tiini de jege-ne mo de Baŋa Wɛ na wó ke abam tei to ŋwaane. O bane déem tiini de zaŋe mo ye o boŋe se o yɔɔre o chɔge abam. De ko de, a na lwoori Wɛ to, o cheigi-ne. 20Baŋa Wɛ bane ya ta zaŋe de Aron de mo ye o boŋe se o chɔge wonto de. A maa na lwoori Wɛ a pa Aron to, Baŋa Wɛ déem sɛ a wɛ-lworo kom konto de. 21A déem ma kwei woŋo kolo na pɛ se á ke wɛleere dem to, sabu-seŋa na-mɔra kam mo konto. A ma nyeene-ka, ye a daare a nɔne-ka mura-mura. A laam ma kwei-ka a dole a yage bu-dura ne pa se na bam zeŋe-ka ba ja ba viiri.
22Abam déem ta na vei á yi Tabera ne, de Massa ne, de Kiberof-Hataava ne to, á pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe mo. 23Abam nam na yi Kadese-Baranea ne to mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ abam ni o we, ‘Zo-na tega kalo a na pɛ abam to á kwei-ka á ta‑á tei.’ Abam ma ve Baŋa Wɛ ni dem konto, ye á wo pɛ‑o chega. 24Chega to, ko zege a na lɔre abam maŋa kalo ne to, á yɔɔre á ye balo na ve Baŋa Wɛ ni to mo.
25Konto ŋwaane nam mo pɛ se amo de to Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, ye a ja o teiŋa da finna, wea de tete maama. Ko maa ye o na ti yiga se o chɔge abam de á na pɛ se o bane zaŋe to ŋwaane mo a ke konto. 26Amo ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ ye a we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, ja! Yé chɔge nmo tete nɔɔna bam. Ba ye nmo nyɔn-mage nɔɔna balo n na kwei n dam-fɔrɔ kom n ma‑n vere-ba n ja n nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne to mo. 27Guli n tontoŋena Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob ni ne, se n yé jeeli nɔɔna banto wo-dɛɔ de ba keim-lwanno, de ba wɛleera yam. 28Nmo nam ná chɔge nɔɔna banto, Ejipti tiina bam wó ta we nmo wo wane n nɔɔna bam se n ja n zo tega kalo n na gwoni ni se n pa-ba to. Ba ta wó ta we, “Baŋa Wɛ na chuli o nɔɔna bam to ŋwaane mo o jaane-ba o vo kagoa kam wone se o go-ba!” 29Nam nii! Nɔɔna banto ye nmo tete nɔɔna balo n na kuri se ba taa ye nmo nyɔn-mage nɔɔna to. N tɔge n dam baŋa ne n toŋe wo-kamunnu n ma‑n ja-ba n nwoŋi Ejipti ne n ba ywo.’ ”

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Exodus 34.1-10)
Moses said to the people:
1The Lord told me to chisel out two flat stones, just like the ones he had given me earlier. He also commanded me to make a wooden chest, then come up the mountain and meet with him. 2He told me that he would write on the new stones the same words he had written on the ones I broke, and that I could put these stones in this sacred chest.
3So I made a chest out of acacia wood, and I chiseled two flat stones like the ones I broke. Then I carried the stones up the mountain, 4where the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them, just as he had done the first time. The commandments were exactly what he had announced from the fire, when you were gathered at the mountain.
After the Lord returned the stones to me, 5I took them down the mountainside and put them in the chest, just as he had commanded. And they are still there.
Aaron Died
(Numbers 20.22-29)
Moses said to Israel:
6 Later we set up camp at the wells belonging to the descendants of Jaakan. Then we moved on and camped at Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar became the priest. 7Next, we camped at Gudgodah and then at Jotbathah, where there are flowing streams.
The Levites Were Appointed To Carry the Chest
Moses said to Israel:
8 After I put the two stones in the sacred chest, the Lord chose the tribe of Levi, not only to carry the chest, but also to serve as his priests at the place of worship and to bless the other tribes in his name. And they still do these things. 9The Lord promised that he would always provide for the tribe of Levi, and that's why he won't give them any land, when he divides it among the other tribes.
The Lord Answered the Prayers of Moses
(Exodus 34.9,10,27-29)
Moses said to Israel:
10 When I had taken the second set of stones up the mountain, I spent 40 days and nights there, just as I had done before. Once again, the Lord answered my prayer and did not destroy you. 11Instead, he told me, “Moses, get ready to lead the people into the land that I promised their ancestors.”
What the Lord Wants
Moses said:
12People of Israel, what does the Lord your God want from you? The Lord wants you to respect and follow him, to love and serve him with all your heart and soul, 13and to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. Do this, and all will go well for you.
14Everything belongs to the Lord your God, not only the earth and everything on it, but also the sky and the highest heavens. 15Yet the Lord loved your ancestors and wanted them to belong to him. So he chose them and their descendants rather than any other nation, and today you are still his people.
16Remember your agreement with the Lord and stop being so stubborn. 17 The Lord your God is more powerful than all other gods and lords, and his tremendous power is to be feared. His decisions are always fair, and you cannot bribe him to change his mind. 18 The Lord defends the rights of orphans and widows. He cares for foreigners and gives them food and clothing. 19And you should also care for them, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
20Respect the Lord your God, be faithful, and serve only him, making promises in his name. 21Offer your praises to him, because you have seen him work such terrifying miracles for you.
22 When your ancestors went to live in Egypt, there were only 70 of them. But the Lord has blessed you, and now there are more of you than there are stars in the sky.
translation_text:
Wɛ jwoori o tiŋi o nia yam o pa Moses
1“Ka maŋa kam ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we, ‘Sare kandwa-pelɛ selei ne boboa nyena yam, n daare n kwei daa n ma‑n ke dakaa, se n laam di peo kom yuu n ba a tei. 2Se a lage a jwoori a popone botare selo a na ke boboa kandwa yam ne ye n lɔ to mo a ke kandwa yanto baŋa ne. Ko kwaga ne, n jege se n kwei-ya mo n tiŋi dakaa kam wone.’
3A ma kwei golesaa dɛ a ma a ke dakaa a daare a sare kandwa-pelɛ selei ne boboa nyena yam. A ma zeeri kandwa yam a ja a di peo kom yuu. 4Baŋa Wɛ ma jwoori o popone o nia fuga kam o tiŋi kandwa yam baŋa ne, nenɛɛne boboa poponem dem dwoŋi. O ya zege min-vogo wone o tɔɔle o nia yam konto se abam ni dɛ dem á déem na gilimi o yiga ne to. O na jwoori o popone-ya to, o laam ma kwei kandwa yam o pa amo. 5A ma zege peo kom yuu ne a tu tega, ye a daare a kwei kandwa yam a tiŋi dakaa kalo a na ke to wone. A ke Baŋa Wɛ na we a ke tei maama to ye ya ta wora de zem maama.
6Isarele tiina bam déem ya zege Jaakan dwi tiina buli sem seeni mo ba vo ba yi Mosera. Ba na yi da to mo Aron tega ye ba suli‑o jei sem konto ne. O bu Eleaza ma leiri o yuu ne o ji Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu. 7Ba ma zege dáane ba vo Gudigoda. Ba daa ma zege Gudigoda ne ba vo ba yi Jotibafa, mɛ bu-nwaro na daga da to.
8Ka maŋa kam ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma pɔɔre Levi dwi dem o pa o tete, se ba taa zeeri dakaa kam, se ba kwori ba taa zege o yiga ne ba toŋe ba pa‑o ye ba kwei Wɛ yere ba ma swɛ Isarele dwi tiina bam maama swolim. Ba ta wora ba ke konto dwoŋi de zem maama. 9Konto ŋwaane mo tei Levi tiina bam ba jege se ba jwoŋi tega nenɛɛne ba chorro tem na nɛ ba nyem tega kam pɔɔrem baŋa ne tei to. Baŋa Wɛ tete mo ye ba nyem, nenɛɛne o na pwooli de-ba tei to.
10Amo nam ta ke da finna mo peo kom yuu ne, wea de tete maama, ne a ya na ke boboa kam ne tei to. Baŋa Wɛ ma sɛ a wɛ-lworo kom pa se o wo chɔge abam. 11O ma ta de amo o we, a zaŋe a da abam yiga se á wane á zo á ta‑á tei tega kam nenɛɛne o na pwooli de á nabaara bam se o ke tei to.
Ta‑á kɔre-na Baŋa Wɛ
12Konto to, Isarele tiina bam, kikia dwi dɔ mo abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom beeri á tei ne? Ko ye se á ta‑á kɔre á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, se á ta‑á tɔge o chwei sem, se á ta‑á swoi‑o lanyerane, se á daare á ta‑á toŋe á pa‑o de á bochare de á boboŋa maama mo, 13ye á toŋe á tɔge o nia de o bera yalo maama amo na pɛ abam zem to. Á ná seene á ke konto dwoŋi, á ŋwea wó ke lanyerane ko pa abam. 14Chega ŋwaane to, abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo tei wɛyuu baŋa kam maama, dedaane logo baŋa de kolo maama na wo ko wone to. 15Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa nam dɛ á nabaara bam se o taa jege ba swono. O ma daare o kuri abam balo na ye ba bia to logo baŋa dwi maama wone, se á ta‑á ye wonto tete nyem, nenɛɛne á ta na ye tei de zem maama to. 16Konto to, kwɛ-na á bochara ne Wɛ na pɛ abam ni se á ke tei to, se á daa yé ke zwabania. 17Kokuri, abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo tei wa maama. O maa ye yuu tiina maama Yuu-tu. O ye Wɛ kamunu ye o tiini o jege foone. Wonto nam ba kuri nɔɔna daane de o na bore ba bora tei to ye o ba jwoŋi dim. 18Ko ná ye botara de kadeina, o yeini o toŋe de chega mo o pa-ba. O ta kwori o swoi veira balo na zoore á wone to, ye o woli-ba de wodiiru de gwaaro. 19Abam de jege se á ta‑á swoi veira mo, á de déem na ye veira Ejipti teo kom ne to ŋwaane. 20Ta‑á kɔre-na á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ye á toŋe á pa‑o. Ta‑á sale-na wonto. Á ná gwoni ni de nɔɔno, se á ma Baŋa Wɛ yere dem yerane á du duuri. 21Wonto mo ye wolo á na jege se á ta‑á tei‑o to. O toŋe wo-kenkagela na jege foone to á yibia ne se o ma jwoŋi abam. 22Á nabaara bam déem zaŋe ba vo Ejipti teo kom ye ba ye nɔɔna fuserepɛ yerane mo. Leile konto abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom pɛ se á kɔgɔ kom puli ko daga ne wɛyuu chalechwe sem na ye tei to.”

english_text:
If You Are Loyal to the Lord, He Will Bless You
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord is your God, so you must always love him and obey his laws and teachings. 2Remember, he corrected you and not your children. You are the ones who saw the Lord use his great power 3 when he worked miracles in Egypt, making terrible things happen to the king and all his people. 4 And when the Egyptian army chased you in their chariots, you saw the Lord drown them and their horses in the Red Sea. Egypt still suffers from that defeat!
5You saw what the Lord did for you while you were in the desert, right up to the time you arrived here. 6 And you saw how the Lord made the ground open up in the middle of our camp underneath the tents of Dathan and Abiram, who were swallowed up along with their families, their animals, and their tents.
7With your own eyes, you saw the Lord's mighty power do all these things.
8Soon you will cross the Jordan River, and if you obey the laws and teachings I'm giving you today, you will be strong enough to conquer the land 9that the Lord promised your ancestors and their descendants. It's rich with milk and honey, and you will live there and enjoy it for a long time. 10It's better land than you had in Egypt, where you had to struggle just to water your crops. 11But the hills and valleys in the promised land are watered by rain from heaven, 12because the Lord your God keeps his eye on this land and takes care of it all year long.
13 The Lord your God commands you to love him and to serve him with all your heart and soul. If you obey him, 14-15he will send rain at the right seasons, so you will have more than enough food, wine, and olive oil, and there will be plenty of grass for your cattle.
16But watch out! You will be tempted to turn your backs on the Lord. And if you worship other gods, 17the Lord will become angry and keep the rain from falling. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will die and disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
18 Memorize these laws and think about them. Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and your foreheads to help you obey them. 19Teach them to your children. Talk about them all the time—whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 20Write them on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates. 21Then you and your descendants will live a long time in the land that the Lord promised your ancestors. Your families will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.
22Love the Lord your God faithfully and obey all the laws and teachings I'm giving you today. If you live the way the Lord wants, 23he will help you take the land. And even though the nations there are more powerful than you, the Lord will force them to leave when you attack. 24 You will capture the land everywhere you go, from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains, and from the Euphrates River west to the Mediterranean Sea. 25No one will be able to stand up to you. The Lord will make everyone terrified of you, just as he promised.
26You have a choice—do you want the Lord to bless you, or do you want him to put a curse on you? 27Today I am giving you his laws, and if you obey him, he will bless you. 28But if you disobey him and worship those gods that have never done anything for you, the Lord will put a curse on you.
29 After the Lord your God helps you take the land, you must have a ceremony where you announce his blessings from Mount Gerizim and his curses from Mount Ebal. 30You know that these two mountains are west of the Jordan River in land now controlled by the Canaanites living in the Jordan River valley. The mountains are west of the road near the sacred trees of Moreh on the other side of Gilgal.
31Soon you will cross the Jordan River to conquer the land that the Lord your God is giving you. And when you have settled there, 32be careful to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ jege dam
1“Konto to á jege se á ta‑á swoi abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo. Ta‑á toŋe á tɔge o nia yam, de o chullu tem, de o bera yam maama. 2Lɔre-na we a zem ŋɔɔne de abam mo ye ko dae á bia balo na wo nɛ Baŋa Wɛ koresem to. Banto tete yi wo nɛ Baŋa Wɛ kamunni dem dedaane o dam delo o na mɛ o vere abam to. 3O déem toŋe wo-kenkagela Ejipti teo kom ne se o ma waare ko Pa-faro wom de o nɔɔna bam maama. 4O ma chɔge ba jar-keira bam de ba sisei de se torokooro tem. Banto na kwaane se ba zeili abam ba ja to, Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se ba misi Nane-soŋo kom ne ba te. Ko dɛ konto mo ye ba na ba chɔgem se ko ba ko yi zem. 5Á bia bam wo nɛ Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe tei o zeini abam maŋa kalo á na beeri taa kagoa kam wone á ba á yi ywo-seeni to. 6Ba wo nɛ Baŋa Wɛ na ke Ruben dwi tu Eliabi bia Datan de Abiram tei to. Wɛ déem pɛ se tega kam puri Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom tetare ne ka li-ba, de ba sɔŋɔ tiina, de ba vwoa yam, dedaane ba jejegero maama. 7Abam tete yia mo nɛ totoŋ-kamunnu telo maama Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe to.
8Konto ŋwaane, sɛ-na Wɛ nia yalo amo na pɛ abam zem to maama, se á jwoŋi dam á wane á bɛ á zo tega kam á ta‑á tei-ka. 9Á laam maa wó ta‑á zoore tega kalo Baŋa Wɛ na pwooli de á nabaara bam se o pa banto de ba bia bam to wone á dáane. Tega kam tiini ka ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ. 10Tega kam á na lage á zo to dae ne Ejipti logo kom, á déem na zoore mɛ to. Jei sem konto ne á yeini á du wonnu mo ye á kwori á yage na da se ko chɛ á yera ne, nenɛɛne nɔɔno na ke gaare tei to. 11Tega kalo á nam na lage á zo to jege zwonnu de bwollu mo, ye doa nena da lanyerane. 12Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yi page tega kam konto baŋa ne mo. O maa nii-ka bene dem maama wone.
13Konto to, á jege se á sɛ Wɛ nia yalo amo na bere abam zem to, se á daare á ta‑á swoi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ye á toŋe á pa‑o de á bochare dedaane á wo maama. 14Á ná ke konto, Baŋa Wɛ we, o laam wó toŋe doa pa se ka ne ka maŋa ne, duum de kwea wɛɛne. Tega kam wó ke wodiiru dedɛ se á na mena, de sana, de nuga maama. 15Á vara de wó na gaao lanyerane se ba di. Wodiiru telo maama á na lage to wó yi abam se á ta‑á di á sui.
16Nam ta‑á yei-na se ba yé soge abam se á ywori Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne á daare á ta‑á zuli wa-yɔɔro ye á toŋe á pa-ya. 17Á ná ke konto, Baŋa Wɛ bane wó zaŋe de abam. O ta wó che doa kam se ka daa yé taa nena. Te-ŋoŋa kalo o na lage o pa abam to daa bá ke wodiiru ka pa abam, pa se á dwi ti lela logo baŋa ne.
18Ta‑á guli-na Wɛ nia yalo a na bere abam to se á ke-ya á bochare ne. Lwoni-na-ya á tiŋi tɔnɔ ne se á daare á vɔ-ya á je ne, dedaane á tira ne, se á ta‑á guli ya gula. 19Pa-na se á bia de lɔre-ya. Ta‑á tɛ-na ya taane maŋa maama, nenɛɛne á ná jei sɔŋɔ ne ye á lara, naa á ná tɔge daane á vei chwoŋa yuu ne, ko ta woli de á ná peini tete ne, naa á ná zaŋe zezeŋa maama ne. 20Popone-na-ya á tiŋi á di sem ni-bworru tem ne, se á daare á ta popone-ya á yage á manchwo-nia dɛ sem ne. 21Ke-na konto se abam de á kwaga kam wane á zo tega kam ne á dáane. Ka maa ye tega kalo Baŋa Wɛ na gwoni ni de á nabaara bam se o pa-ba to, ye á wó ta‑á tei-ka taa wuu, se ko maŋe de wɛyuu de logo baŋa ta na wora maŋa kalo to wone.
22Ta‑á yei-na se á ke á tɔge Wɛ ni dem maama, ne amo zem na bere abam se á ke tei to: Ta‑á swoi-na á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ye á tɔge o chwei sem maama. Nam sale-na o yera ne. 23Á ná seene á ke konto dwoŋi, Baŋa Wɛ wó zeili dwi tiina balo na maŋe ba wo logo kom wone to mo. O ta wó pa abam dam se á wane á jwoŋi teene delo na dana ba dwoi abam to se á ta‑á tei. 24Tega kalo maama á nɛ na wó nɔ ka baŋa ne to wó taa ye abam nyem mo. Abam laŋa kam wó zege kagoa kalo na wo kuri seeni to se ka vo ka yi Lebanon peero tem na wo baŋa seeni to. Ka daa ta wó zege Yuferata bu-zaŋa kam na wo wɛ-puli seeni to se ko yi Mediterania naneo kom na wo wɛ-zoore seeni to. 25Á ná vei mɛ maama logo kom ne, á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó pa se abam foone mo ja jei sem nɔɔna bam, ne o na pwooli se o ke tei to. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá wane abam o cheiŋi.
26Nii-na! Amo zem kwei Wɛ swolim dedaane o sɔɔlem mo a tiŋi abam tetare ne, se á wane á kuri kolo á na lage to. 27Abam ná sɛ á tɔge Wɛ nia yalo amo zem na pɛ abam to, Wɛ wó swɛ abam swolim. 28Á nam ná ve o nia yanto ye á zuli dwi-gɛ tiina wa-yɔɔro tem, Wɛ wó sɔɔle lwarem mo o yage á baŋa ne.
29Ne abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ná jaane abam o zo tega kam se á ta‑á tei, á jege se á zege Gerizim peo kom yuu ne á tɔɔle Wɛ swolim dem, ye á daare á zege Ebal peo kom yuu ne á tɔɔle o sɔɔlem dem. 30Á yei we, peero tem konto wo Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ dedwoŋi ne se ko taa vei wɛ-zoore seeni mɛ Kanaan tiina bam na zoore bwolo kom ne to. Te maa bwola de Giligal teo kom. Morɛ tei-zɔŋɔ kom seeni mo konto.
31Abam laam lage á bɛ Jɔdan buga kam se á zo tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na pɛ abam se á ta‑á tei to mo. Á na tu á ba á jeini da á ti, 32se á tiini á ta‑á yei se á ta‑á toŋa á tɔge Wɛ nia yam de o chullu tem maama ne amo zem na pɛ abam tei to.”

english_text:
Only One Place To Worship the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
1Now I'll tell you the laws and teachings that you have to obey as long as you live. Your ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he is giving you this land. 2But the nations that live there worship other gods. So after you capture the land, you must completely destroy their places of worship—on mountains and hills or in the shade of large trees. 3 Wherever these nations worship their gods, you must tear down their altars, break their sacred stones, burn the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and smash their idols to pieces. Destroy these places of worship so completely that no one will remember they were ever there. 4Don't worship the Lord your God in the way those nations worship their gods.
5-19 Soon you will cross the Jordan, and the Lord will help you conquer your enemies and let you live in peace, there in the land he has given you. But after you are settled, life will be different. You must not offer sacrifices just anywhere you want to. Instead, the Lord will choose a place somewhere in Israel where you must go to worship him. All of your sacrifices and offerings must be taken there, including sacrifices to please the Lord and any gift you promise or voluntarily give him. That's where you must also take one tenth of your grain, wine, and olive oil, as well as the first-born of your cattle, sheep, and goats. You and your family and servants will eat your gifts and sacrifices and celebrate there at the place of worship, because the Lord your God has made you successful in everything you have done. And since Levites will not have any land of their own, you must ask some of them to come along and celebrate with you.
Sometimes you may want to kill an animal for food and not as a sacrifice. If the Lord has blessed you and given you enough cows or sheep or goats, then you can butcher one of them where you live. You can eat it just like the meat from a deer or gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat. But you must not eat the blood of any animal—let the blood drain out on the ground.
20-21The Lord has promised that later on he will give Israel more land, and some of you may not be able to travel all the way from your homes to the place of worship each time you are hungry for meat. But the Lord will give you cattle, sheep, and goats, and you can butcher any of those animals at home and eat as much as you want. 22It is the same as eating the meat from a deer or a gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And in this way, anyone who is unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat.
23-24 But don't eat the blood. It is the life of the animal, so let it drain out on the ground before you eat the meat. 25Do you want the Lord to make you successful? Do you want your children to be successful even after you are gone? Then do what pleases the Lord and don't eat blood.
26-27All sacrifices and offerings to the Lord must be taken to the place where he chooses to be worshiped. If you offer a sacrifice to please the Lord, all of its meat must be burned on the altar. You can eat the meat from certain kinds of sacrifices, but you must always pour out the animal's blood on the altar.
28If you obey these laws, you will be doing what the Lord your God says is right and good. Then he will help you and your descendants be successful.
Worship the Lord in the Right Way
Moses said:
29Israel, as you go into the land and attack the nations that are there, the Lord will get rid of them, and you can have their land.
30But that's when you must be especially careful not to ask, “How did those nations worship their gods? Shouldn't we worship the Lord in the same way?” 31No, you should not! The Lord hates the disgusting way those nations worship their gods, because they even burn their sons and daughters as sacrifices.
32 Obey all the laws and teachings I am giving you. Don't add any, and don't take any away.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ zula jeiga kam
1“Wɛ nia yam de o chullu tem mo tento. Ta‑á yei-na se á ta‑á tɔge-ya maŋa kalo maama á na zoore logo kolo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ abam se á ta‑á tei to wone. Wonto maa ye á nabaara Baŋa Wɛ wom mo.
2Abam ná tu á ba á zeili logo kom dwi tiina bam, se á chɔge jei selo maama ba na yeini ba kaane ba jwona da to. Ko ná ye peero yuu ne, naa zwonnu baŋa ne, naa tangwana baŋa ne, á jege se á yɔɔre á chɔge ba jwona kaanem jei sem maama mo. 3Mage-na ba kaanem bimbina yam á de tega ne, se á daare á lɔ kandwa yalo ba na chwi ba jwona ŋwaane to. Gwoni-na ba Asera nyenyego dɛ sem á de tega ne, se á daare á ke mini á zwɛ-se, ye á chɔge ba jwona yam maama pa se ya yera saare jei sem konto ne.
4Abam nam ná zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, se á yé ke nenɛɛne nɔɔna banto na zuli ba jwona yam tei to. 5Baŋa Wɛ wó kuri jeiga kadwoŋi Isarele dwi tiina bam maama tega kam wone, se ka taa ye o zoorem jei nɔɔna na wó vo ba zuli o yere da to. 6Dáane mo á wó ja á zwɛɛm kaanem vara bam á ja vo á kaane á pa‑o. Ko ta ná ye á kaanem dwi maama, de á Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra, de á jeŋa pɛɛra, de á ni-gwonim pɛɛra, de á wo-ywoŋo pɛɛra maama, ko ta woli de á vara bam na dɛ yiga ba lo bia balo to, á jege se á kwei-ya á vo jei sem konto á pa Baŋa Wɛ. 7Abam dedaane á sɔŋɔ tiina bam wó vo á jeini á Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne á di wodiiru telo á na toŋe te ŋwaane to, ye á kwori á jege wopwolo Baŋa Wɛ na swɛ abam swolim to ŋwaane.
8Maŋa kam ná yia, á daa ba jege se á ta‑á ke nenɛɛne debam zem na yeini dé ke ye dé zuli Wɛ tei to. Leile konto nɔɔno maama yeini o zuli Wɛ ne o na lage tei to mo. 9Bɛŋwaane abam ta wo yi tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á tei to se á daare á na wo-zuru ka wone. 10Á nam ná bɛ Jɔdan buga kam, ye á vo á jeini tega kam konto ne, Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se á dona daa yé daane abam pa se á sii de wo-zuru. 11Maŋa kam konto ne Baŋa Wɛ wó kuri jeiga dedoa se ka taa ye o zoorem jei nɔɔna na wó vo ba zuli o yere da to. Dáane mo á jege se á ja kolo maama amo na bere abam to á ja á vo á ma ke kaanem á pa‑o: vara zwɛɛm kaanem, dedaane á kaanem dwi delo maama, de á Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra, de á jeŋa pɛɛra, de á ni-gwonim pɛ-laaro tem. 12Dáane mo á wo di ywoni á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne, abam de á bia de á tontoŋena bam, baara de kaana maama. Levi dwi tiina balo na zoore abam tei ne to de wó tɔge de abam ba vo da, banto na ba jege ba tete tega se ba taa tei to ŋwaane. 13Ta‑á yei-na se ko dae we á ná yi mɛ maama, se á zwɛ varem á ma á ke kaanem da. 14Ko nam jege se á vo jeiga kalo yerane Baŋa Wɛ na kuri Isarele dwi tiina bam maama tega kam wone to, se á ke kaanem da á pa‑o, ye á daare á ke kolo maama amo na bere abam se á ke to.
15Chwoŋa nam wora se á go á sɔŋɔ-vara bam á di mɛ maama á na zoore to. Á wae á di á sui, ne á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na woli abam de vara balo to. Ko maa nye de á na lage á di woŋa naa feira ye nɔɔna maama jege chwoŋa se ba di, ba ná maŋe ba kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane naa ba wo kwɛ ba tete mo de. 16Ko nam chula se á di vara bam jana mo. Á pa-na se jana bam lwo tega ne, ne á na wó lwo na á yage tei to. 17Ko daare ko ná ye wodiiru telo á na jege se á ma‑á ke kaanem to, ko chula se á di tento tem á sam dem ne. Ko ná ye á Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yalo na ye mena naa sana naa nuga to, de á vara bam na dɛ yiga ba lo bia balo to, de á ni-gwonim pɛɛra, de á wo-ywoŋo pɛɛra dedaane á jeŋa pɛɛra yam maama, 18á jege se á kwei-ya á ja vo jeiga kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wó kuri to ye á daare á di-ya o yiga ne. Abam de á bia de á tontoŋena, baara de kaana maama, dedaane Levi tiina balo na zoore abam tei ne to mo wó vo á di ywoni Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne de kolo maama á na toŋe ko ŋwaane to. 19Ta‑á yei-na se á yé swei Levi dwi tiina bam ni ne maŋa kalo maama á na wó ta‑á zoore á tega kam ne to.
20Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ná tu o ba o pa se á laŋa kam yale nenɛɛne o na pwooli o pa abam tei to, pa se á fera zo nɔna dim, á wae á done á sui. 21Jeiga kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli o yere da to ná tiini ka ye yiga yiga de abam, á wae á le varem vara balo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ abam to wone á goe ye á daare á di á sam ne á sui, ne amo na bere abam tei to. 22Ko maa nye de á na lage á di woŋa naa feira ye nɔɔna maama jege chwoŋa se ba di, ba ná maŋe ba kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane naa ba wo kwɛ ba tete de. 23Ko nam chula se á di vara bam jana mo, kokuri ŋwea kam mo jege kuri jana bam ŋwaane. Ko nam dae se abam di ŋwea kam dedaane nɔna yam. 24Yé kwei-na jana bam á ma á ji wodiu. Nam kwei-na-ba á lwo tega ne, ne á na wó lwo na á yage tei to. 25Á ná seene á ve jana bam dim, ko wó pa se Baŋa Wɛ wo pwoli lanyerane. Á ŋwea maa wó ke lanyerane ka pa abam de á kwaga kam maama.
26Kwei-na á Wɛ kaanem pɛɛra yam de á ni-gwonim pɛɛra yam á ja á vo jeiga kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kuri to. 27Ko ná ye zwɛɛm kaanem, se á zwɛ varem wom Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem baŋa ne, nɔna yam de jana bam maama. Ko nam ná ye kaanem delo á na wó di de nɔna yam to, á jege se á lwo jana bam bimbini dem baŋa ne á yage mo.
28Ta‑á yei-na se á ta‑á sɛ Wɛ nia yalo maama amo na bere abam to, se ko pa á ŋwea ke lanyerane ka pa abam de á kwaga kam maama taa wuu, á kikia na wó taa tɔge chwoŋa ye ya pwoli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wo to ŋwaane.
Ba yé taa zuli jwona
29Abam ná lage á zo dwi-gɛ tiina logo kom, á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó zeili-ba á yiga ne pa se ba daare ba tega kam se á jwoŋi-ka á ta‑á tei. 30Baŋa Wɛ ná tu o ba o chɔge dwi-gɛ tiina bam konto, yé pa-na se ba soge abam se á tɔge ba jwona yam. Yé bwei-na nenɛɛne: ‘Nɔɔna banto yeini ba tɔge chwoŋa kɔ mo ba zuli ba jwona yam? Debam de lage dé ke konto dwoŋi mo.’ 31Abam ba jege se á zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ne banto na zuli ba jwona yam tei to. Kokuri, dwi-gɛ tiina bam konto yeini ba ke totoŋ-zɔɔna yalo maama Baŋa Wɛ na chuli to ba ma zuli ba jwona yam. Ba bere ba zwɛ ba bia mo mini wone ba ma ke kaanem ba pa ba jwona yam.
32Ta‑á yei-na se á ta‑á tɔge Wɛ nia yalo maama amo na bere abam to. Yé zaŋe-na á woli kolokolo ya wone, nam yé le-na kolokolo ya wone á yage.

english_text:
Don't Worship Other Gods
Moses said to Israel:
1-2Someday a prophet may come along who is able to perform miracles or tell what will happen in the future. Then the prophet may say, “Let's start worshiping some new gods—some gods that we know nothing about.” 3If the prophet says this, don't listen! The Lord your God will be watching to find out whether or not you love him with all your heart and soul. 4You must be completely faithful to the Lord. Worship and obey only the Lord and do this with fear and trembling, 5because he rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
If a prophet tells you to disobey the Lord your God and to stop worshiping him, then that prophet is evil and must be put to death.
6-10 Someone else may say to you, “Let's worship other gods.” That person may be your best friend, your brother or sister, your son or daughter, or your own dear wife or husband. But you must not listen to people who say such things. Instead, you must stone them to death. You must be the first to throw the stones, then others from the community will finish the job. Don't show any pity.
The gods worshiped by other nations have never done anything for you or your ancestors. People who ask you to worship other gods are trying to get you to stop worshiping the Lord, who rescued you from slavery in Egypt. So put to death anyone who asks you to worship another god. 11And when the rest of Israel hears about it, they will be afraid, and no one else will ever do such an evil thing again.
12After the Lord your God gives you towns to live in, you may hear a rumor about one of the towns. 13You may hear that some worthless people have talked everyone there into worshiping other gods, even though these gods had never done anything for them. 14You must carefully find out if the rumor is true. Then if the people of that town have actually done such a disgusting thing in your own country, 15you must take your swords and kill every one of them, and their livestock too. 16-17Gather all the possessions of the people who lived there, and pile them up in the marketplace, without keeping anything for yourself. Set the pile and the whole town on fire, and don't ever rebuild the town. The whole town will be a sacrifice to the Lord your God. Then he won't be angry anymore, and he will have mercy on you and make your nation stronger, just as he promised your ancestors. 18That's why you must do what the Lord your God says is right. I am giving you his laws and teachings today, and you must obey them.
translation_text:
1Sampwora naa yi-naro ná zaŋe abam wone ye o wuuri o ta o bere abam wo-kenkagela na lage ya ke tei to, 2ye wo-kenkagela yam ná seene ya ke ne o na tage tei to, o wó wane o soge abam se á zuli dwi-gɛ tiina wa-yɔɔro, ye o ta nenɛɛne: ‘Pa-na dé zaŋe dé tɔge wa yadwonna se dé zuli-ya.’ 3Sampwora naa yi-naro ná tage konto dwoŋi, yé cheigi-na o taane. Ko nam ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo maane abam se o nii, á seene á swoi‑o de á bochare maama de á boboŋa maama naa á ba swoi. 4Ta‑á tɔge-na abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom se á ta‑á kɔre‑o. Sɛ-na o nia yam ye á cheigi o kwora kam, se á ta‑á toŋe á pa‑o ye á sale‑o.
5Ko nam ná ye sampwora naa yi-naro konto dwoŋi, ko jege se á go‑o mo, o na soge abam se á lɔ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwaga ne to ŋwaane. Baŋa Wɛ nam ye wolo na jaane abam o ja nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne pa se o vere abam á kabɛɛne dem ne o yage to mo. O ye nɔn-balɔrɔ mo ye o lage se o pa á ywori Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ abam chwoŋa kalo se á ta‑á tɔge to wone. Konto ŋwaane, á jege se á saare lwarem dem konto mo á tetare ne.
6Ko ta ná ye n nu-puga bu, naa n tete bia, naa n ka-swono, naa n chilwoŋ-zɔŋɔ, kotu wó wane o waase o ta de nmo o we, ‘Pa dé vo dé zuli wa yayam.’ Wa yam konto mo abam de á nabaara bam ya yeiri. 7Ya nam ye wa yalo dwi-gɛ tiina na zuli to, ba ná maŋe ba ye dwia yalo na bwola de abam to, naa ba ná ye yiga yiga de. 8Yé zaŋe n sɛ kotu gana yam. Bere n yé cheigi‑o de. Daa‑n yé duri o ŋwaŋa naa n kwaane n kwoli o kikia yam. 9Ja‑o n go! Nmo tete wó da yiga n dole‑o de kandwa se nɔɔna babam de laam tɔge ba dole. 10Dole-o-na de kandwa á go, o na kwaane se o ja abam o ywori abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwaga ne to ŋwaane. Baŋa Wɛ nam ye wolo na jaane abam o nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne pa se o vere abam á kabɛɛne dem ne o yage to mo. 11Isarele tiina bam maama ná nigi kolo na ke to, foone wó ja-ba, pa se abam wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá toŋe keim-lɔŋɔ konto dwoŋi.
12Ko daa ta ná ye teene delo abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á zoore de wone to, á wae á ni we, 13nɔn-wo-korro tedwonna zaŋe teo kodwoŋi ne ye ba soge ba teo kom nɔɔna pa se ba ywori Baŋa Wɛ chwoŋa wone se ba daare ba zuli wa yayam. Abam nam ya yeiri wa yam konto zula. 14Á ná nigi kanto sawea kam dwoŋi, kwaane-na á tɔge ka nɛ se á lɔre chega kam. Ko ná ye chega mo we totoŋ-lɔŋɔ kom seene ko ke abam tetare ne, 15ko jege se á zaŋe á kwei á se-zɔɔro mo á vo á go teo kom konto nɔɔna bam maama ka, de ba vara bam de, se á yɔɔre á chɔge teo kom konto fase. 16Ta daare-na á la ba jejegero tem maama á ke daane teo kom kapworo ne, se á laam zwɛ teo kom de ko woŋo maama á ma‑á ke kaanem á pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ko jege se ko taa ye di-dwonnu yerane mo se ko taa vei wuu, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa yé jwoori o lɔ teo kom konto. 17Ko ná ye teo kom wonnu telo maama na maŋe de chɔgem Wɛ ŋwaane to, yé pa se á fera zo kolokolo se á kwei. Á ná sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem konto, o bane wó zuri ye o daare o duri abam ŋwaŋa, pa se á kɔgɔ kom puli dedɛ, ne o na pwooli de á nabaara bam se o ke tei to.
18Konto ŋwaane abam jege se á cheigi abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam ye á sɛ o nia yam maama, ne amo zem na bere abam tei to. Ta‑á ke-na kolo na jege chega o yiga ne to.”

english_text:
Don't Mourn like Other Nations
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, you are the Lord's children, so when you mourn for the dead, you must not cut yourselves or shave your forehead. 2 Out of all the nations on this earth, the Lord your God chose you to be his own. You belong to the Lord, so don't behave like those who worship other gods.
Animals That Can Be Eaten
(Leviticus 11.1-47)
3 Don't eat any disgusting animals.
4-5You may eat the meat of cattle, sheep, and goats; wild sheep and goats; and gazelles, antelopes, and all kinds of deer. 6It is all right to eat meat from any animals that have divided hoofs and also chew the cud.
7But don't eat camels, rabbits, and rock badgers. These animals chew the cud but do not have divided hoofs. You must treat them as unclean. 8And don't eat pork, since pigs have divided hoofs, but they do not chew their cud. Don't even touch a dead pig!
9You can eat any fish that has fins and scales. But there are other creatures that live in the water, 10and if they do not have fins and scales, you must not eat them. Treat them as unclean.
11You can eat any clean bird. 12-18But don't eat the meat of any of the following birds: eagles, vultures, falcons, kites, ravens, ostriches, owls, sea gulls, hawks, pelicans, ospreys, cormorants, storks, herons, and hoopoes. You must not eat bats. 19Swarming insects are unclean, so don't eat them. 20However, you are allowed to eat certain kinds of winged insects.
21 You belong to the Lord your God, so if you happen to find a dead animal, don't eat its meat. You may give it to foreigners who live in your town or sell it to foreigners who are visiting your town.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Give the Lord Ten Percent of Your Harvest
Moses said:
22 People of Israel, every year you must set aside ten percent of your grain harvest. 23Also set aside ten percent of your wine and olive oil, and the first-born of every cow, sheep, and goat. Take these to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, and eat them there. This will teach you to always respect the Lord your God.
24But suppose you can't carry that ten percent of your harvest to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. If you live too far away, or if the Lord gives you a big harvest, 25then sell this part and take the money there instead. 26When you and your family arrive, spend the money on food for a big celebration. Buy cattle, sheep, goats, wine, beer, and if there are any other kinds of food that you want, buy those too. 27And since people of the Levi tribe won't own any land for growing crops, remember to ask the Levites to celebrate with you.
28Every third year, instead of using the ten percent of your harvest for a big celebration, bring it into town and put it in a community storehouse. 29The Levites have no land of their own, so you must give them food from the storehouse. You must also give food to the poor who live in your town, including orphans, widows, and foreigners. If they have enough to eat, then the Lord your God will be pleased and make you successful in everything you do.
translation_text:
Wonnu telo na chula to
1“Abam ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna mo. Konto to á ná lage a keeri twa, yé gwe-na á yera yam, nam yé cheeri-na á yuni te tira seeni. 2Abam seene á ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo. Logo baŋa nɔɔna maama wone mo o kuri abam se á ta‑á ye o tete nɔɔna o yi na su to.
Wonnu telo na maŋe de dim to
Chullu 11:1-47
3Yé zaŋe-na á di wo-yɔɔro telo Baŋa Wɛ na chuli te dim to. 4Á wae á di vara banto dwi:
Naao, naa pia, naa boŋo, 5naa woŋa, naa feira, naa siga, naa kagoa wo boŋo, naa nambworo, naa kagoa wo pia.
6Á ta wae á di varem wolo maama napɔɔna na lɔge belei ye ba yeini ba done gaao ba guli ba jwoori ba done to. 7Ko nam dae se á di kone, naa zwoni, naa pe-ware, se vara bam konto done gaao ba guli ye ba napɔɔna laam wo lɔge belei. Konto ŋwaane banto wo maŋe se á di-ba. 8Teira de nam wo maŋe se á di-ya. Ya napɔɔna lɔge belei ye ya laam ba done gaao ya gula ya jwoori ya dona. Konto ŋwaane ko chula se á di ya nɔna. Ya ná tega, bere á yé dwei-ya.
9Ko nam ná ye wonnu telo na zoore na wone to, á wae á di ywona yalo na jege nabili-pelwaro ye ya ta jege poro pa te kwoli ya yera to. 10Ko daare ko ná ye woŋo maama na wo na wone ye ko ba jege nabili-pelwaro dedaane poro na kwoli-ko to, ko chula se á di-ko. Ko wo maŋe de dim.
11Á wae á di zuna balo maama na maŋe de dim to. 12Ko daare á ba jege se á di zuna banto dwi:
Maaro, de duura dwi maama, 13de chilachi, de kalwonnu dwi maama, 14de bachangaaro, 15-17de kunkwooru dwi maama, de lenlane, de naneo zuna, de kawuli dwi maama, de nakelakɔro, de bugacheeni, 18de buga ni zuna, de kabakollo, de pɛbia, de jenjwaano.
19Wo-korro telo na jege vɔna ye te kare te vei tega ne to de chula. Á ba jege se á di-te. 20Á za wae á di wo-korro telo na maŋe de dim to.
21Yé zaŋe-na á di varem wolo na tega o tete ne to. Á wae á kwei á pa veira balo na zoore abam teo kom ne to se ba di, naa á kwei á yeigi á pa sa-teena. Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kuri abam se á ta‑á ye o tete nɔɔna mo.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé kwei bebala de ka nu nayela o saŋe mini wone.
Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra
22Bene maama wone ta‑á yei-na se á le á kare sem wodiiru popɔra dedoa fuga maama wone á pa Wɛ. 23Laam ja-na Wɛ-teiri wodiiru tem konto á ja vo jeiga kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli o yere da to. Ko ná ye á mena yam, de á sa-doora bam, de á nuga kam, de á vara bam na dɛ yiga ba lo bia balo to, se á vo á di Wɛ-teiri dem á Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, se á ta‑á kɔre‑o taa wuu. 24Baŋa Wɛ nam ná yɔɔre o ke zaane abam yuu ne pa se á na wodiiru dedɛ, ye o wara-jei sem ná ye yiga yiga ka pa abam se á ja á wodiiru tem á yi da, se á ke tento: 25Kwei-na á Wɛ-teiri wodiiru tem á yeigi á jwoŋi sabu, se á daare á ja sabu kom á vo Baŋa Wɛ zula jeiga kam. 26Á ná yi da, se á laam ma á yeigi kolo maama á na lage to se á di. Ko ná ye naane, naa pei, naa sana, abam de á sɔŋɔ tiina bam wó di-te á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne de wopwolo.
27Za ta‑á yei-na se á yé swei-na Levi dwi tiina balo na zoore abam tei ne to ni ne, banto na ba jege ba tete tega se ba taa tei to ŋwaane. 28Bena yatɔ bene dem maama ná yeini de yi, se á kwei-na Wɛ-teiri wodiiru tem maama á la-te jeiga dedoa á teo maama wone. 29Wodiiru tem konto wó taa ye Levi dwi tiina bam nyem mo, banto na ba jege ba tete tega to ŋwaane. Abam ta jege se á kwei-te á pa veira, de botara, de kadeina balo na zoore abam wone to mo. Ba maama wó wane ba ba ba jwoŋi wodiu ba di ba su. Ke-na konto se ko pa á Tu Baŋa Wɛ zaane taa wo á baŋa ne de kolo maama á na lage á toŋe to.”

english_text:
Loans
(Leviticus 25.1-7)
Moses said:
1-2Every seven years you must announce, “The Lord says loans do not need to be paid back.” Then if you have loaned money to another Israelite, you can no longer ask for payment. 3This law applies only to loans you have made to other Israelites. Foreigners will still have to pay back what you have loaned them.
4-6No one in Israel should ever be poor. The Lord your God is giving you this land, and he has promised to make you very successful, if you obey his laws and teachings that I'm giving you today. You will lend money to many nations, but you won't have to borrow. You will rule many nations, but they won't rule you.
7 After the Lord your God gives land to each of you, there may be poor Israelites in the town where you live. If there are, then don't be mean and selfish with your money. 8Instead, be kind and lend them what they need. 9Be careful! Don't say to yourself, “Soon it will be the seventh year, and then I won't be able to get my money back.” It would be horrible for you to think that way and to be so selfish that you refuse to help the poor. They are your relatives, and if you don't help them, they may ask the Lord to decide whether you have done wrong. And he will say that you are guilty. 10You should be happy to give the poor what they need, because then the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
11 There will always be some Israelites who are poor and needy. That's why I am commanding you to be generous with them.
Setting Slaves Free
(Exodus 21.1-11)
Moses said to Israel:
12 If any of you buy Israelites as slaves, you must set them free after six years. 13And don't just tell them they are free to leave— 14give them sheep and goats and a good supply of grain and wine. The more the Lord has given you, the more you should give them. 15I am commanding you to obey the Lord as a reminder that you were slaves in Egypt before he set you free. 16But one of your slaves may say, “I love you and your family, and I would be better off staying with you, so please don't make me leave.” 17Take the slave to the door of your house and push a sharp metal rod through one earlobe and into the door. Such slaves will belong to you for life, whether they are men or women.
18Don't complain when you have to set a slave free. After all, you got six years of service at half the cost of hiring someone to do the work.
First-Born Animals
(Leviticus 27.26,27; Numbers 18.15-18)
Moses said to Israel:
19 If the first-born animal of a cow or sheep or goat is a male, it must be given to the Lord. Don't put first-born cattle to work or cut wool from first-born sheep. 20Instead, each year you must take the first-born of these animals to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped. You and your family will sacrifice them to the Lord and then eat them as part of a sacred meal.
21But if the animal is lame or blind or has something else wrong with it, you must not sacrifice it to the Lord your God. 22You can butcher it where you live, and eat it just like the meat of a deer or gazelle that you kill while hunting. Even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some. 23 But you must never eat the blood of an animal—let it drain out on the ground.
translation_text:
Jena chɛɛm taane
Nwoŋim 23:10-11; Chullu 25:1-7
1“Bena yarepɛ bene dem maama ná yeini de yi, se á kwei-na balo na jege á jena to á yage á chɛ-ba. 2Á na wó ke tei to mo tento: Wolo maama na kwei sabu o jene o pa o dwoŋi Isarele tu to jege se o yage jene dem o ma chɛ‑o mo. Kotu daa yé boŋe se o jwoŋi o sabu kom o choro kom tei ne, Baŋa Wɛ na bere we ko ye jena saarem bene to ŋwaane. 3Ko ná ye veiru, n wae n jwoŋi n jene dem o tei ne. Ko daare ko ná ye n tete nɔɔna bam jena yam mo, se n yage n chɛ-ba.
4Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó swɛ abam swolim pa se á na ywoni tega kalo o na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á tei to wone. Konto ŋwaane, yiniga bá ja abam dedoa tete de, 5ne á ná sɛ o ni ye á toŋe á tɔge bera yalo maama amo na bere abam zem tento to. 6Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ abam swolim ne o na pwooli se o ke tei to. Konto to, á wo ta‑á jena á pae dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ ye á ba jege se á di jena ba tei ne. Á wó ta‑á jege dam dwi-gɛ tiina baŋa ne. Teo kodwoŋi nam bá di dam abam baŋa ne.
7Á ná zo tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam to, ye yiniga ná jaane á dwoŋi Isarele tu wolo na zoore á teo wone to, yé ve-na se á woli‑o, á na jege wo-chɛɔ to ŋwaane. 8Á nam jege se á ke wo-ywoŋo mo ded‑o se á jene tei maama o na wó taa laga se o ma ji nɔɔno to. 9Ta‑n yei se n yé pa se boboŋ-lɔŋɔ ba n kana ne ye n ta nenɛɛne: ‘Bena yarepɛ bene dem na ye jena saarem bene to bwola.’ Nmo ná boŋe konto dwoŋi ye n ve se n jene n pa n dwoŋi Isarele tu wolo yiniga na jaane‑o to, ko ye puseŋa keim mo n kea. Nɔɔno wom wó wane o keeri o jare Baŋa Wɛ nmo ŋwaane, ye Wɛ wó pa n to de n bora. 10N jege se n pa yiniga tu zɛɛra mo se n yé ke wo-chɛɔ ded‑o. N Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom laam wó swɛ nmo swolim pa se kolo maama n na jege n toŋe to ke lanyerane ko pa‑m. 11Maŋa maama yiniga na jaane balo to wó taa wo abam wone. Konto to amo pɛ abam ni se á ke wo-ywoŋo á pa Isarele tiina balo cham na jege-ba to.
Bena yarepɛ yarepɛ bene dem taane
Nwoŋim 21:1-11
12Hiburu tu ná kwei o tete o yeigi o pa nmo se o taa ye n kabaa, o ná ye baaro naa kaane, kotu wó toŋe o pa‑m bena yaredo mo. Bena yarepɛ bene dem ná yia, se n yage‑o se o taa tei o tete. 13N nam ná yage‑o, yé pa o viiri de je-yaara. 14Pwoli n wo se n le kolo maama n na jege to wone n pa‑o, ko ná maŋe ko ye n vara bam wone, de n wodiiru tem wone, de n sana bam wone. Nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ na ke zaane n yuu ne o pa‑m wonnu telo to, se nmo de ke n kabaa kam lanyerane konto dwoŋi. 15Guli-na we abam de déem ye kabɛ mo Ejipti ne, ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom laam ba o jwoŋi abam o yage. Mo kokuri a zem tage Wɛ ni dem konto a bere abam.
16N kabaa kam nam wó wane o ta de nmo we o ba lage se o viiri, o na swoi nmo de n sɔŋɔ tiina bam ye n ke‑o lanyerane to ŋwaane. 17O ná tage konto dwoŋi, ko jege se n ja‑o mo n vo n pa se o sale manchwo-peena bworo kom, se n daare n kwei silwei n puri o zwɛ dedoa. Konto bere we o wó taa ye nmo kabaa se ko taa nii o toone. N kabaa kam ná ye kaane, se n ke‑o de konto dwoŋi.
18Nmo ná yage n kabaa se o viiri, se n yé pa ko taa ye wo-chɛɔ ko pa‑m. Kokuri o toŋe o pa‑m bena yaredo mo ye o totoŋa yam daga ya dwoi wolo na toŋe o pa‑m ŋweero ŋwaane to totoŋa kuni belei. N Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom laam wó swɛ nmo swolim pa se kolo maama n na jege n toŋe to ke lanyerane ko pa‑m.
Sɔŋɔ-vara bu-kwe sem
19Le-na wo-bale selo á vara bam na dɛ yiga ba lo to se á kwei á pa á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Yé ma-na naane dem konto á toŋe totoŋe, nam yé fane á pei sem konto koro. 20Bene maama wone abam de á sɔŋɔ tiina tiina bam jege se á vo jeiga kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kuri to ye á di wonnu tem konto o yiga ne. 21Varem wolo nam ná jege gɛɛ o yera ne, ne o ná ye vare-gwana, naa vare-lilwei, naa o jege tusim dwi delo, ko wo maŋe se á kwei wonto dwi á ma‑á ke kaanem á pa Baŋa Wɛ. 22Á nam jege se á kwei vara bam konto dwoŋi á di á sam ne mo. Ko nye de á na lage á di woŋa naa feira ye nɔɔna maama jege chwoŋa se ba di, ba ná maŋe ba kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane naa ba wo kwɛ ba tete mo de. 23Ko nam chula se á di vara bam jana. Pa-na se jana bam lwo tega ne, ne á na wó lwo na á yage tei to.”

english_text:
Passover
(Exodus 12.1-20; Leviticus 23.4-8)
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, you must celebrate Passover in the month of Abib, because one night in that month years ago, the Lord your God rescued you from Egypt. 2The Passover sacrifice must be a cow, a sheep, or a goat, and you must offer it at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. 3-4Eat all of the meat of the Passover sacrifice that same night. But don't serve bread made with yeast at the Passover meal. Serve the same kind of thin bread that you ate when you were slaves suffering in Egypt and when you had to leave Egypt quickly. As long as you live, this thin bread will remind you of the day you left Egypt.
For seven days following Passover, don't make any bread with yeast. In fact, there should be no yeast anywhere in Israel.
5Don't offer the Passover sacrifice in just any town where you happen to live. 6It must be offered at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Kill the sacrifice at sunset, the time of day when you left Egypt. 7Then cook it and eat it there at the place of worship, returning to your tents the next morning.
8Eat thin bread for the next six days. Then on the seventh day, don't do any work. Instead, come together and worship the Lord.
The Harvest Festival
(Exodus 34.22; Leviticus 23.15-21)
Moses said to Israel:
9 Seven weeks after you start your grain harvest, 10-11go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped and celebrate the Harvest Festival in honor of the Lord your God. Bring him an offering as large as you can afford, depending on how big a harvest he has given you. Be sure to take along your sons and daughters and all your servants. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. 12Remember that you used to be slaves in Egypt, so obey these laws.
The Festival of Shelters
(Leviticus 23.33-43; Numbers 29.12-38)
Moses said to Israel:
13-15 After you have finished the grain harvest and the grape harvest, take your sons and daughters and all your servants to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
The Lord will give you big harvests and make you successful in everything you do. You will be completely happy, so celebrate this festival in honor of the Lord your God.
Three Festivals at the Place of Worship
(Exodus 23.14-17)
Moses said:
16Each year there are three festivals when all Israelite men must go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. These are the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters. And don't forget to take along a gift for the Lord. 17The bigger the harvest the Lord gives you, the bigger your gift should be.
Treat Everyone with Justice
Moses said to Israel:
18-19 After you are settled in the towns that you will receive from the Lord your God, the people in each town must appoint judges and other officers. Those of you that become judges must be completely fair when you make legal decisions, even if someone important is involved. Don't take bribes to give unfair decisions. Bribes keep people who are wise from seeing the truth and turn honest people into liars.
20People of Israel, if you want to enjoy a long and successful life, make sure that everyone is treated with justice in the land the Lord is giving you.
Don't Set Up Sacred Poles or Stones
Moses said to Israel:
21 When you build the altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God, don't set up a sacred pole for the worship of the goddess Asherah. 22 And don't set up a sacred stone! The Lord hates these things.
translation_text:
Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem
Nwoŋim 12:1-20
1“Bene maama Abibi chana kam ne, á jege se á di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem á ma á zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, kokuri kanto chana kam dɛ dedoa ne mo o jaane abam tete ne o ja nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne. 2Á ná lage á di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem, véi-na jeiga kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wó kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli o yere da to á ja varem wolo á na le á naane dem wone naa á pei sem naa bone dem wone to á go á ma ke kaanem á pa‑o. 3Á ná jeini á di varem wom nɔna yam, se á yé di bworobworo kolo na jege sabɔle to. Da yarepɛ wone á jege se á di bworobworo kolo sabɔle na wo woli ko wone to nenɛɛne á déem na ke tei ye á lage lela se á nwoŋi Ejipti ne á ya na yaare da to. Á ná yeini á di yaara bworobworo kom konto dwoŋi, á wó guli dɛ delo á na zaŋe á nwoŋi Ejipti ne to gula. 4Da yarepɛ yam maama wone, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege se sabɔle ta wo o sɔŋɔ ne. Varem wolo á na wó go kuri dem boboa dɛ dem dedaan-ni ne to, á jege se á di o nɔna yam maama mo se tega laam poore. 5Abam ná wo teo kolo maama ne á Tu Baŋa Wɛ na lage o pa abam to, se á yé go Atɔgebabaŋa vara bam jei de jei, 6ko ná dae jeiga kalo o na wó kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli o yere da to yerane. Wɛ-zoore maŋa ne mo á wó go vara bam se ko maŋe de maŋa kalo á na yage Ejipti to. 7Saŋe-na nɔna yam á di Wɛ jeiga kam ne, se tega ná poore, á laam zaŋe á jwoori á vwoa ne. 8Da yaredo yalo na saŋe to wone, á wó di bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to mo, se da yarepɛ dɛ dem ná yia, á la daane se á kɔgɔ kom maama zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Á ba jege se á toŋe dɛ dem konto ne.
Ga-kwea kuri dem
Nwoŋim 34:22; Chullu 23:15-21
9Á ná bobo se á zage á wodiiru tem, jeeli-na da yarepɛ yarepɛ kuni berepɛ, 10se á laam di Ga-kwea kuri dem á ma‑á zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Kwei-na á wo-ywoŋo pɛɛra se ko maŋe de Baŋa Wɛ na ke zaane á baŋa ne tei to á ja vo á zuli‑o. 11Á jege se á vo jeiga kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wó kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli o yere da to á di kuri dem de wopwolo o yiga ne. Ko wó taa ye abam, de á bia, de á kabɛ, ko woli de Levi tiina, de veira, de botara, de kadeina balo maama na zoore á tetare ne to mo. 12Guli-na we á déem ye kabɛ mo Ejipti ne, se á ke á yuu ne se á sɛ Wɛ nia yanto maama.
Vwoa chwiim kuri dem
Nwoŋim 23:16; Chullu 23:33-43; Jeelim 29:12-34
13Á ná fere á wodiiru tem maama á ti, ye á ta kwori á ŋoke á Vini tio-bia bam maama á ti, á laam jege se á ke da yarepɛ á di Vwoa chwiim kuri dem mo. 14Tɔge-na de á bia, de á kabɛ, ko woli de Levi tiina, de veira, de botara, de kadeina balo maama na zoore á teene dem ne to, á di kuri dem de wopwolo. 15Á wó vo jeiga kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wó kuri to á ke da yarepɛ á di kuri dem á ma‑á zuli‑o. Á wó ta‑á jege wopwolo lanyerane, Baŋa Wɛ na ke zaane á baŋa ne de á wodiiru de kolo maama á na toŋe to ŋwaane.
16Bene maama wone kuni betɔ mo á baara bam jege se ba vo jeiga kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wó kuri to ba jeeri o yiga ne ba zuli‑o. Ko wó taa ye Bworobworo-memene kuri dem, de Ga-kwea kuri dem, de Vwoa chwiim kuri dem mo. Nɔɔno maama nam jege se o taa zei pɛɛre mo o ja vo o ma zuli Baŋa Wɛ. 17Nɔɔno maama wó kwei pɛɛre se ko maŋe de Baŋa Wɛ na ke zaane o baŋa ne o woli‑o tei to mo o ja jeeri.
Bora borem
18Teo kolo maama á Tu Baŋa Wɛ na lage o pa abam to wone, kuri-na nakwa de yiga tiina se ba wane ba tɔge chega ba di nɔɔna taane. 19Nmo nam ná di nɔɔno taane, n dae se n zege vwa wone, naa n pu nɔɔn-nɔɔno kwaga n bora borem ne. Ko dae se n jwoŋi dim, bɛŋwaane pɛɛra wae ya dwei nɔn-ŋona tete yia ye ya kweele chega taane ya pa se de ji vwa. 20Yɔɔre-na á tɔge chega borem lanyerane se ko pa á wane á zo tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam to wone á dáane.
21Á ná lage á lɔ bimbini á pa á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, ta‑á yei-na se á yé kwei daa á ma‑á sare Asera nyenyego á zege da se á zuli-ko. 22Nam ta yé chwi-na kandwɛ se de taa ye jwoni de pa abam. Baŋa Wɛ chuli wonnu tem konto maama.

english_text:
Sacrifices That Have Something Wrong with Them
Moses said to Israel:
1If an ox or a sheep has something wrong with it, don't offer it as a sacrifice to the Lord your God—he will be disgusted!
Put To Death People Who Worship Idols
Moses said to Israel:
2-3 The Lord your God is giving you towns to live in. But later, a man or a woman in your town may start worshiping other gods, or even the sun, moon, or stars. I have warned you not to worship other gods, because whoever worships them is disobeying the Lord and breaking the agreement he made with you. 4So when you hear that someone in your town is committing this disgusting sin, you must carefully find out if that person really is guilty. 5-7 But you will need two or three witnesses—one witness isn't enough to prove a person guilty.
Get rid of those who are guilty of such evil. Take them outside your town gates and everyone must stone them to death. But the witnesses must be the first to throw stones.
Difficult Cases
Moses said to Israel:
8-12It may be difficult to find out the truth in some legal cases in your town. You may not be able to decide if someone was killed accidentally or murdered. Or you may not be able to tell whether an injury or some property damage was done by accident or on purpose. If the case is too difficult, take it to the court at the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped.
This court will be made up of one judge and several priests who serve at the Lord's altar. They will explain the law to you and give you their decision about the case. Do exactly what they tell you, or you will be put to death. 13When other Israelites hear about it, they will be afraid and obey the decisions of the court.
The King
Moses said:
14 People of Israel, after you capture the land the Lord your God is giving you, and after you settle on it, you will say, “We want a king, just like the nations around us.”
15Go ahead and appoint a king, but make sure that he is an Israelite and that he is the one the Lord has chosen.
16 The king should not have many horses, especially those from Egypt. The Lord has said never to go back there again. 17 And the king must not have a lot of wives—they might tempt him to be unfaithful to the Lord. Finally, the king must not try to get huge amounts of silver and gold.
18The official copy of God's laws will be kept by the priests of the Levi tribe.
