1“Á ná sɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora ye á toŋe á tɔge o nia yam amo na pɛ abam zem tento to, Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se á yere zaŋe de dwoni teene delo maama na wo logo kom baŋa ne to. 2Sɛ-na o ni dem chekke se swolim dento maama taa ye á nyem ye de woli abam maŋa maama:
3Wɛ swolim wó taa wo á teene dem baŋa ne de á kare sem baŋa ne. 4Wɛ swolim wó taa wo á bia baŋa ne, de á wodiiru baŋa ne, de á vara baŋa ne, ne ko ná ye á naane, de á pei, de de bia maama. 5Wɛ swolim wó taa wo á mena tetwaro baŋa ne, de á nwanno tem baŋa ne. 6Wɛ swolim wó taa wo á kikia maama baŋa ne, ne ko ná ye totoŋa yalo á na ke diga ne, de yalo á na ke pwooni ne to maama.
7Á dona ná nwoŋi se ba kwaare jara de abam, Baŋa Wɛ wó wane-ba o pa abam. Ba kɔgɔ kom wó da chwoŋa dedoa ba ba abam baŋa, ye ba laam jage ba da chwei serepɛ ba duri se ba lu abam jeŋa ne.
8 Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ swolim o ke á tuli baŋa ne, de á jeŋa totoŋa maama baŋa ne, pa se á na swolim lanyerane tega kalo o na lage o pa abam to wone.
9Abam ná sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni maama ye á tɔge o chwei sem, o wó fɔge abam pa se á ta‑á ye o tete nɔɔna, ne o na pwooli se o ke tei to. 10Ko maa wó pa se logo baŋa nɔɔna maama lɔre we á ye Baŋa Wɛ wom nyem, se ba ta kɔre abam. 11Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se á ŋwea maama ke lanyerane, se á ta‑á jege bia dedɛ, de vara dedɛ, de wodiiru dedɛ, ne á ná tu á zo tega kalo ne o na pwooli de á nabaara se o pa abam to. 12Baŋa Wɛ wó zege o wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom ne o toŋe doa se ka ne á kare sem ne, pa se wodiiru telo á na dugi to ke lanyerane. O na wó ke zaane á totoŋa maama baŋa ne to wó pa se á ta‑á jene á pae dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ. Abam nam bá jwoŋi jena nɔɔn-nɔɔno tei ne. 13Baŋa Wɛ wó pa á ta‑á wo nɔɔna maama yiga ne mo, ye á bá ta‑á wo ba kuri ne. Chega to, á ná sɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora ye á toŋe á tɔge o nia yam amo na pɛ abam zem tento to, á wó ta‑á vei yiga mo maŋa maama ye á daa bá jwoori kwaga. 14Ko ná ye Wɛ nia yalo a na pɛ abam zem to, yé ywori-na ya wone se á vo jazem naa jagwia seeni. Á nam yé zaŋe á zuli wa-yɔɔro.
Zwabania wó ja sɔɔlem ka ba
Chullu 26:14-46
15Abam ná ve á Tu Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam ye á wo sɛ se á tɔge o nia yam amo na pɛ abam zem to chekke, lwarem dento maama wó ba á baŋa:
16 Baŋa Wɛ wó sɔɔle lwarem o yage á teene dem de á kare baŋa ne. 17Baŋa Wɛ wó sɔɔle lwarem o yage á mena tetwaro baŋa ne, de á nwanno baŋa ne. 18Baŋa Wɛ wó sɔɔle lwarem o yage á bia baŋa ne, de á wodiiru baŋa ne, de á vara baŋa ne, ne ko ná ye á naane, de á pei, de de bia maama. 19Baŋa Wɛ wó sɔɔle lwarem o yage á kikia maama baŋa ne, ne ko ná ye totoŋa yalo á na ke diga ne, de yalo á na ke pwooni ne to maama.
20 Baŋa Wɛ wó ja lɛɛro de cham o ba abam baŋa ne, pa se á boboŋa vugimi de kolo maama á na lage á toŋe to. Chɔgem wó ba de ti abam lela, á na toŋe lwarem totoŋa ye á lɔ Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne to ŋwaane. 21Baŋa Wɛ wó ja jawe-chɛɛro dwi dwi o ba abam baŋa ne, pa se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa yé daare tega kalo á na lage á zo se á ta‑á tei to wone. 22O wó pa sesa-dwonnu, de paa, de yera foosem ba te ja abam. O ta wó toŋe wulim de da-kore de jawe-chɛɛro dwi dwi se te chɔge wodiiru telo á na dugi to. Lɛɛro tento maama wó taa jaane abam se ko ta nii á toone. 23Kunkwonnu bá taa wo wɛyuu ne. Tega kam wó ko mo kaŋ-kaŋ ne luuru tei. 24Á na teene doa, ka bá ba, ye fwogo de kasol-koro yerane mo á wó na. Te wó ba te chɔge abam te ti.
25 Baŋa Wɛ wó kwei abam o ke á dona jeŋa ne. Á kɔgɔ kom wó da chwoŋa dedoa á vo á kwaare jara de-ba, ye á laam jage á da chwei serepɛ á duri se á lu ba jeŋa ne. Logo baŋa dwi tiina maama ná nɛ kolo na wó ba abam baŋa to, ko wó tiini ko so-ba ye foone ja-ba. 26Á ná tega, zuna de kago-vara mo wó ba ba di abam yera ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá daare se o zeili-ba o yage.
27 Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se ŋɔn-pwoni lei abam yera ne, ne o déem na ke tei de Ejipti tiina bam to. O ta wó pa se sankwɛ, de tambwala, de kasili-nabiina to abam yera ne, ye yɔɔrem tera. 28Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se á yuni vuvugi, á yia de wó dwei ye á boboŋa vugimi. 29Wea tetare ne de á wó ta‑á kare á taane mo ne lilwoa tei. Á bá na nyɔɔre á totoŋa baŋa ne. Maŋa maama de, nɔɔna wó taa bɛɛse abam, ye ba vere á wonnu tem. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam bá taa wora se o jwoŋi abam o yage.
30Nɔɔno wolo ná vei o cha kaane se o di, nɔn-gaa wó zi kaane wom. Wolo ná lɔge diga, kotu bá zo ka wone. Wolo ná dugi kara, kotu bá na ka wodiiru o di. 31Ba wó zage á naane ba go á yibia ne, ye á bá na nɔna yam á done. Abam ná zege á nia, ba wó vere á bonɛ ba vaŋe ba ja kɛ, ye ba daa bá jwoori ba pa abam. Ba wó vere á pei sem ba kwei ba ke á dona jeŋa ne ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se o woli abam. 32Ba ta wó ja á bia bam, bakeiri de busankane, ba vo ba ke dwi-gɛ tiina jeŋa ne. Á wó ta‑á zege chwoŋa ni ne taa á nia se á bia bam jwoori ye á ga. Á bá wane kolokolo á ke. 33Sa-teena mo wó ba ba vere wodiiru telo á na koore luluŋu á na to. Á wó yeini á ta‑á nae yaara de bɛɛsem yerane mo. 34Keim-chɛɛre delo á yia na wó na to wó pa se á yu-punnu vugimi. 35Baŋa Wɛ wó waare abam pa se ŋɔn-pwoni jwoŋi á nɛ sem maama. Se wó kwoli á yera yam maama ye se ba jia.
36 Baŋa Wɛ wó zeili abam de pɛ wolo á na wó kuri se o taa tei abam to se á jage á vo sa-teo yiga yiga, teo kolo abam de á nabaara bam ya na yeiri ko ni ne to. Jei sem konto ne á wó ta‑á zuli jwona yalo ba na mɛ dɛ dedaane kandwa ba ma ke-ya to. 37Teene delo wone Baŋa Wɛ na wó jage abam to tiina ná nɛ kolo na wó ke abam to, ko wó so-ba dedɛ. Á wó ji memaŋa de wo-mɔnɔ á pa-ba.
38Á wó du dedɛ á kare ne, ye á ba á zage fenfee, kayere na wó di á wodiu kom to ŋwaane. 39Á wó jeiri Vini teeni á daare á nii de baŋa ne, ye á bá gwori de bia bam naa á ŋoke nyoa bam se á nyɔ, kanzwa na wó chɔge á teeni dem to ŋwaane. 40Olivi teeni wó nwoŋi á tega kam jei maama ne, ye á za bá na de nuga mo, de bia bam maama na wó siiri to ŋwaane. 41Á wó lo bia, bakeiri de busankane, ye á bá ta‑á nii-ba, á dona na wó ja-ba ba ja viiri to ŋwaane. 42Á teeni dedaane á wodiiru maama ye kayere mo wó deilimi se ti.
43 Dwi-gɛ tiina balo na zoore abam teo kom ne to wó fɔge ba taa puli de dam, ye abam tete wó ta‑á jwoori kwaga. 44Banto wó taa jege sabu ba jene ba pae abam. Abam nam bá ta‑á jega se á jene á pa-ba. Ba wó taa ye abam yuu tiina mo, se á ta‑á wo ba dam kuri ne.
45Chega ŋwaane to, abam ná ve á Tu Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam ye á wo sɛ se á tɔge o nia yam de o bera yam maama, lwarem dento dwoŋi wó ba á baŋa de bá yage se ko yi á laam na tu á chɔge á ti to. 46Tento maama mo wó taa ye maana se nɔɔna lɔre we Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ wo abam de á kwaga kam baŋa ne taa wuu.
47Abam wo sɛ se á ta‑á zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom de wopwolo ye á toŋe á pa‑o, de o na maŋe o pa á jeŋa jege wo-laaro dedɛ to. 48Mo kokuri á laam wó ta‑á toŋe á pae á dona balo Baŋa Wɛ na wó toŋe se ba wane abam to. Kana wó ja abam, na-nyɔm de wó ja abam. Zore de wó ja abam woŋo maama wone ye á ta‑á vei kalambwolo. Á wó ji kabɛ ye á na bɛɛsem se ko taa nii á ná tu á chɔge á ti.
49 Baŋa Wɛ wó le dwi delo na wo yiga yiga ye á ba ni ba taane to se ba popo ba ba abam baŋa ne, ne maao na yeini ko chaale ko wodiu tei to. 50Ba maa ye balo na jege wo-dɛɔ ye ba ba duri nɔɔn-nɔɔno ŋwaŋa, nɔn-kwe de bia de to mo. 51Ba wó ba ba vere á vara de á wodiiru maama ye ba daare abam se á pu de kana. Ba bere ba bá daare kolokolo, mena, de sana, de nuga, de naane, de pei, de bone. Ba wó vere te maama ba daare abam se á laam ba á chɔge á ti.
52Á dona wó nwoŋi ba ba tega kalo á Tu baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam to ba kaare á teene dem maama ba pu. Ko ná ye kabiri-dɛɛro telo na dɔra ye á boŋe we te wó che á dona yiga to, tento wó to tega ne buri-buri. 53Á dona na wó peene abam konto to, ko wó pa se á chɔɔre ye á laam di bia balo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na pɛ se á lo to. 54-55Á dona ná kaare á teene dem maama ba pu, nɔn-yero wolo maama na bere o jege yibwona to de lage o di o tete bia mo, o na yaare de kana to ŋwaane. O nam bá sɛ se o chɛ nɔna yam o pa o choro, naa o ka-swono, naa o bia balo ta na daare to. 56Ka-yero wolo de na jege yibwona ye o yeiri yaara to de wó ma o kwaga o ya o baro wolo o na swoi to de o bia maama. 57O wó seigi o di bu-seseŋa kalo o na loge to de ka nyeene, ye o ba ke o chɛ o pa o diga tiina, kana na jege‑o ye wodiu tera to ŋwaane.
58Abam ná wo sɛ se á toŋe á tɔge bera yalo maama na popone ya tiŋi tɔnɔ konto ne to, ye á ná ve se á zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere-kamunu kom, 59o wó waare abam de á bia pa se jawe-chɛɛro lɔgese abam maama ye te bá jei. 60Jaweero telo dwoŋi Ejipti tiina déem na nɛ ye á jege te lwia to wó ba á baŋa ye á bá na te yɔɔrem jei. 61Baŋa Wɛ ta wó pa se jaweero de yaara yalo na maŋe ya wo popone ya tiŋi Wɛ nia tɔnɔ konto ne to ba abam baŋa se te chɔge abam fase. 62Á kɔgɔ kom seene ko puli ne wɛyuu chalechwe sem na daga tei to mo. De ko de, abam fenfee yerane mo wó daare, á na ve á Tu Baŋa Wɛ ni to ŋwaane. 63Ko ya pwoli Baŋa Wɛ wo mo se o ke abam lanyerane pa se á puli dedɛ. Ko laam nam wó pwoli o wo se o chɔge abam pa se á ti. O wó pa se ba vuuri abam ba gɔ tega kalo á na lage á zo to ne.
64 Baŋa Wɛ wó zeili abam pa se á jage á vo á yi logo baŋa teene dem maama. Dáane mo á wó ta‑á zuli jwona yalo ba na mɛ dɛ dedaane kandwa ba ma ba ke to. Abam de á nabaara ya yeiri wa-yɔɔro tem konto ni ne. 65Jei sem konto ne, á bá na kugu jei de bochare-zuru. Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se lwia taa jege abam. Á yia wó ba ya dwei ye á vɔna pare. 66Á bochara wó taa jaana ye foone jege abam wea de tete maama. Á wó ta‑á kɔre foone de toone maŋa maama. 67Á ná zaŋe zezeŋa ne, á wó ta nenɛɛne, ‘Ko ya ná ye dedaan-ni mo tento, ko ya wó taa gara.’ Dedaan-ni ne á maa wó ta we, ‘Ko ya ná ye zezeŋa mo konto, ko wó taa gara.’ Á wó ta‑á tɛ konto dwoŋi de wo-lwanno telo á yia na wó na pa se foone ja abam to. 68Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se á zo nabwooru á jwoori á vo Ejipti, de o na maŋe o pa abam ni se á daa yé da chwoŋa kam konto to. Á ná yi da, á wó kwaane se á yeigi á tete á pa á dona se á ji ba kabɛ, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá sɛ se o yeigi abam.”

english_text:
The Agreement in Moab
1So Moses finished telling the Israelites what they had to do in order to keep the agreement the Lord was making with them in Moab, which was in addition to the one the Lord had made with them at Mount Sinai.
The Third Speech: Israel Must Keep Its Agreement with the Lord
The Lord Is Your God
2-3Moses called the nation of Israel together and told them:
When you were in Egypt, you saw the Lord perform great miracles that caused trouble for the king, his officials, and everyone else in the country. 4-6He has even told you, “For 40 years I, the Lord, led you through the desert, but your clothes and your sandals didn't wear out, and I gave you special food. I did these things so you would realize that I am your God.”
But the Lord must give you a change of heart before you truly understand what you have seen and heard.
7 When we first camped here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan attacked, but we defeated them. 8 Then we captured their land and divided it among the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
Keep the Agreement
Moses said:
9Israel, the Lord has made an agreement with you, and if you keep your part, you will be successful in everything you do. 10-12Today everyone in our nation is standing here in the Lord's presence, including leaders and officials, parents and children, and even those foreigners who cut wood and carry water for us. We are at this place of worship to promise that we will keep our part of the agreement with the Lord our God.
13-15In this agreement, the Lord promised that you would be his people and that he would be your God. He first made this promise to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and today the Lord is making this same promise to you. But it isn't just for you; it is also for your descendants.
16-17When we lived in Egypt, you saw the Egyptians worship disgusting idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold. Then as we traveled through other nations, you saw those people worship other disgusting idols. 18 So make sure that everyone in your tribe remains faithful to the Lord and never starts worshiping gods of other nations.
If even one of you worships idols, you will be like the root of a plant that produces bitter, poisonous fruit. 19You may be an Israelite and know all about the Lord's agreement with us, but he won't bless you if you rebel against him. You may think you can get away with it, but you will cause the rest of Israel to be punished along with you. 20-21The Lord will be furious, and instead of forgiving you, he will separate you from the other tribes. Then he will destroy you, by piling on you all the curses in The Book of God's Law, and you will be forgotten forever.
22The Lord will strike your country with diseases and disasters. Your descendants and foreigners from distant countries will see that your land 23 has become a scorching desert of salt and sulfur, where nothing is planted, nothing sprouts, and nothing grows. It will be as lifeless as the land around the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, after the Lord became angry and destroyed them.
24People from other nations will ask, “Why did the Lord destroy this country? Why was he so furious?”
25And they will be given this answer:
Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, but after he brought them out of Egypt and made an agreement with them, they rejected the agreement 26and decided to worship gods that had never helped them. The Lord had forbidden Israel to worship these gods, 27-28and so he became furious and punished the land with all the curses in The Book of God's Law. Then he pulled up Israel by the roots and tossed them into a foreign country, where they still are today.
29The Lord our God hasn't explained the present or the future, but he has commanded us to obey the laws he gave to us and our descendants.
translation_text:
Ba jwoori ba ke ni-gwonim de Wɛ
1 Baŋa Wɛ déem na lage o gwoni ni de Isarele tiina bam Moaba laŋa ne to, taane delo o na tage de Moses se o lwoni o bere-ba to mo tento. Tento de nam ta lage te tɔge te woli de ni-gwonim delo Baŋa Wɛ na maŋe o ke o pa-ba Sinayi peo yuu ne to mo. 2Moses ma bwoŋi Isarele tiina bam maama ye o ta de ba o we:
“Abam tete maŋe á na Baŋa Wɛ déem na toŋe kolo de Ejipti Pa-faro wom de o nakwa de o teo kom maama to. 3Á yia mo nɛ chana yalo, de wo-kenkagela yalo, de wo-kamunnu telo Baŋa Wɛ na ke o ma faŋe Ejipti tiina bam o nii to. 4De zem maama de, o ta wo pɛ abam yia poore se á wane á ni kolo maama á na nɛ to kuri.
5 Baŋa Wɛ tage o we, ‘Bena fintɔ mo a tɔge abam yiga kagoa kam wone ye dé via. Á gwaaro nam wo zareme, ye á natera de wo chɔge. 6Á na beeri konto to, á wo di bworobworo ye á wo nyɔge sana. De ko de, a woli abam se á wane á lɔre we amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.’
7Dé na yi ywo-seeni to, Hesebon teo Pɛ Sihon de Basan teo Pɛ Oga ma nwoŋi se ba kwaare jara de debam. Dé déem ma wane-ba. 8Dé ma kwei ba tega kam dé pɔɔre dé pa Ruben dwi dem, de Gad dwi dem, de Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom se ba taa tei.
9Ta‑á yei-na se á tɔge kolo maama na popone ko tiŋi ni-gwonim dem konto ŋwaane to, se ko pa kolo maama á na lage á toŋe to taa ke lanyerane ko pa abam. 10Zem dɛ dem ne, abam maama zege á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne mo, de á yuu tiina, de á nakwa, de á dedɛɛra, de Isarele baara bam maama, 11ko ta woli de á kaana, de á bia, de veira balo na zoore de abam ye ba gwoni dɛ ba daare ba mɔɔne na ba zeŋe ba pae abam to maama. 12Á tu se á sɛ ni-gwonim delo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na dugi duuri o ma ke de abam zem to mo. 13Ni-gwonim dem konto bere we á seene á ye o nɔɔna bam se o de taa ye abam Tu Wɛ wom, ne o na maŋe o pwooli tei de abam, de á nabaara Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob to. 14-15Ko dae abam balo zem na zege debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne to yerane mo o lage o du duuri o ma ke ni-gwonim dem konto de-ba, se ko ta ye á kwaga kam de mo o lage o ke o pa-ba.
16Á wó wane á guli dé déem na zoore Ejipti ne ye dé daare dé tɔge teene dedwonna wone dé kɛ dé ba ywo ye ko ke debam tei to. 17Á nɛ dwia yanto tiina na zuli wo-zɔɔna de jwona yalo ba na mɛ dɛ, de kandwa, de lu-nyenno, de sabu-seŋa ba ma ke to. 18Ta‑á yei-na se abam wolowolo yé lɔ dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwaga ne se o daare o vo o zuli dwi-gɛ tiina jwona. Ko ná ye abam balo zem na wora to wone baaro, naa kaane, naa sɔŋɔ kolo, naa dwi delo maama, se á yé zaŋe á ke konto.
Wolo maama ná tɔge jwo-yɔɔro, kotu wó taa nye de tei-kugu kolo na bege se ko laam ba ko lei tio-bi-balwaaro to mo. 19O wae o ni ni-gwonim dento na bere wonnu telo to ye o boŋe o yuu ne we, o ta wó na lanyerane de o na maŋe o jege yi-dɛɛre ye o ba tɔge Wɛ chwoŋa to de. Kotu nam wó ja chɔgem o ba abam maama baŋa ne, nɔn-ŋona de nɔn-balwaaro maama. 20Baŋa Wɛ bá yage nɔɔno wom konto wɛleera o ma chɛ‑o. O ban-zɔŋɔ za mo wó tɔrege kotu baŋa ne, pa se chana yalo maama na popone ya tiŋi tɔnɔ konto wone to ba kotu baŋa ne se ko taa nii o yere ná saare logo baŋa maama ne. 21Baŋa Wɛ wó le‑o Isarele dwia yam maama wone se o tiini o na chɔgem. Sɔɔlem delo maama na popone Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom wone o ni-gwonim dem ŋwaane to maa wó to kotu baŋa ne. 22Abam kwaga kam de sa-teena balo na nwoŋi yiga yiga to jwa wó na chɔgem delo Baŋa Wɛ na wó pa de to tega kam baŋa ne se yaara dedɛ ta wora to. 23Á tega kam maama wó chɔge, yɛ de chilibugu na wó li-ka to ŋwaane. Ba bá wane kolokolo ba du ka wone. Wodiiru de bá ke da, ye gaaro tete bá wane te nwoŋi. Laŋa kam maama wó taa nye de Sodom, de Gomora, de Adema, de Zeboyiim teene dem déem na chɔge tei, Baŋa Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane to. 24Dwi-gɛ tiina maama ná nɛa, ba wó taa bwei nenɛɛne, ‘Bɛ laam mo ke ye Baŋa Wɛ chɔge ba tega kam konto dwoŋi? Bɛŋwaane mo o bane tiini de zaŋe de-ba konto?’
25Nɔɔna wó leiri-ba ba we:
‘Ko wó taa ye we, Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam chɔge ni-gwonim delo o na ke de-ba maŋa kalo o na jaane-ba o nwoŋi Ejipti ne to, de o na ye ba nabaara Wɛ wom to. 26De konto de, ba déem yage‑o ba daare ba zuli wa-yɔɔro mo, te na ye wa yalo ba ya na yeiri, ye Wɛ wo sɛ se ba zuli-ya to. 27Konto laam mo pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe ba baŋa ne, ye o pa se sɔɔlem delo maama na popone tɔnɔ konto ne to ba ba tega kam baŋa ne. 28Baŋa Wɛ ma vuuri-ba o le ba tega kam ne, ye o laam dole-ba o yage sa-teo ne, o ban-lom dem ŋwaane. Dáane mo ba ta wora de zem maama.’
29Wo-siseigiru wora, te na maŋe te wo dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom boboŋa ne, se ko daare bera yalo o na veere o pa debam to, yanto mo ye debam de dé kwaga kam nyem se ko taa vei wuu, se dé wane dé taa tɔge o nia yam maama.”

english_text:
The Lord Will Bring You Back
Moses said to Israel:
1 I have told you everything the Lord your God will do for you, and I've also told you the curses he will put on you if you reject him. He will scatter you in faraway countries, but when you realize that he is punishing you, 2return to him with all your heart and soul and start obeying the commands I have given to you today. 3-4Then he will stop punishing you and treat you with kindness. He may have scattered you to the farthest countries on earth, but he will bring you back 5to the land that had belonged to your ancestors and make you even more successful and powerful than they ever were.
6You and your descendants are stubborn, but the Lord will make you willing to obey him and love him with all your heart and soul, and you will enjoy a long life.
7Then the Lord your God will remove the curses from you and put them on those enemies who hate and attack you.
8You will again obey the laws and teachings of the Lord, 9and he will bless you with many children, large herds and flocks, and abundant crops. The Lord will be happy to do good things for you, just as he did for your ancestors. 10But you must decide once and for all to worship him with all your heart and soul and to obey everything in The Book of God's Law.
Choose Life, Not Death
Moses said to Israel:
11You know God's laws, and it isn't impossible to obey them. 12 His commands aren't in heaven, so you can't excuse yourselves by saying, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are in heaven, and no one can go up to get them, then bring them down and explain them to us.” 13And you can't say, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are across the sea, and someone must go across, then bring them back and explain them to us.” 14No, these commands are nearby and you know them by heart. All you have to do is obey!
15 Today I am giving you a choice. You can choose life and success or death and disaster. 16-18I am commanding you to be loyal to the Lord, to live the way he has told you, and to obey his laws and teachings. You are about to cross the Jordan River and take the land that he is giving you. If you obey him, you will live and become successful and powerful.
On the other hand, you might choose to disobey the Lord and reject him. So I'm warning you that if you bow down and worship other gods, you won't have long to live.
19Now I call the sky and the earth to be witnesses that I am offering you this choice. Will you choose for the Lord to make you prosperous and give you a long life? Or will he put you under a curse and kill you? Choose life! 20 Be completely faithful to the Lord your God, love him, and do whatever he tells you. The Lord is the only one who can give life, and he will let you live a long time in the land that he promised to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_text:
Ba na wó ke tei se Baŋa Wɛ jwoori o ke-ba lanyerane
1“Amo laam nam bere abam Wɛ swolim dem de o sɔɔlem dem na wó taa ye tei to. Wonnu tento maama ná seene te ke abam baŋa ne, ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ná zeili abam o jage se á ta‑á zoore dwi-gɛ tiina tetare ne, á wó guli te gula. 2Abam de á kwaga kam laam ná pipiri á jwoori á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom tei ye á sɛ o ni de á boboŋa maama de á wo maama, ne amo zem na bere abam tei maama to, 3Baŋa Wɛ wó duri á ŋwaŋa ye o jwoori o ke abam lanyerane. O wó pa á zege teene delo wone o na jage abam to se á jwoori ywo. 4Á ná maŋe á jage mo a zo logo kom gugworru yiga yiga de, Baŋa Wɛ wó la abam dáane o ja jwoori ywo. 5O wó pa á jwoori á zo tega kalo á nabaara déem na tei to, se abam tete de taa tei-ka. O ta wó pa se á fɔge á puli á dwoni á nabaara bam déem na ye tei to. 6Baŋa Wɛ wó kwɛ abam de á bia bochara, se á ta‑á wae á swoi‑o de á boboŋa maama, de á wo maama, se á dáane tega kam ne. 7O ta wó pa se lwarem delo o ya na sɔɔle o ke abam baŋa ne to yage abam se de pipiri de ba á dona baŋa ne, de balo maama na chuli abam to. 8Á wó jwoori á sɛ Baŋa Wɛ kwora ye á toŋe á tɔge o nia yam maama amo na pɛ abam zem to. 9Á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó pa se á ŋwea ke lanyerane ye á totoŋa maama taa jege nyɔɔre. O ta wó pa á ta‑á jege bia dedɛ, de vara dedɛ, de wodiiru dedɛ. Ko wó pwoli o wo se o ke abam lanyerane, ne o yi déem na page á nabaara bam baŋa ne tei to mo. 10Abam nam jege se á sɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora ye á toŋe á tɔge o nia de o bera yalo na popone ya tiŋi Wɛ nia tɔnɔ konto ne to mo. Á jege se á pipiri á jwoori o tei mo de á boboŋa maama de á wo maama.
Ŋwea de toone taane
11Wɛ nia yalo amo na pɛ abam zem to ba tiini ya dwoi á jaanem. 12Ko dae we ya tigi wɛyuu ne mo, se á ta‑á bwei da-tei ne we, ‘Wɔ mo wó wane o di o ja-ya o jwoori o ba o pa debam, se dé wane dé ni se de daare dé sɛ?’ 13Ko dae we ya wo naneo kom kakam daa ne, se á ta‑á bwei nenɛɛne, ‘Wɔ mo wó yɛ na o bɛ naneo kom o ja-ya o jwoori o ba o pa debam, se dé wane dé ni ye dé daare de sɛ?’ 14Aawo, ya zege ywo mo ya bwola de abam. Ya maŋe ya wo á ni ne de á bochara ne. Konto to, sɛ-na-ya chekke.
15Amo zem pɛ abam chwoŋa mo se á kuri lanyerane de balɔrɔ tetare ne kolo á na lage to, se á ta kuri ŋwea de toone de tetare ne. 16Amo zem pɛ abam ni se á ta‑á swoi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom se á daare á ta‑á tɔge o chwei sem, ye á sɛ o nia yam de o bera yam de o chullu tem maama. Á ná seene á ke konto, Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ abam swolim pa se á fɔge á puli tega kalo á na lage á zo á jeini ka wone to. 17Ko daare, á ná lɔge o kwaga ne ye a ve o nia yam, ye á fera ná zo wa-yɔɔro se á zuli-te, 18ta‑á yei-na we á wó na chɔgem se á ti lela. Á ná vei á bɛ Jɔdan buga kam se á zo tega kam á ta‑á tei, á bá dáane ka wone ye á te.
19Zem dɛ dento ne a kwei wɛyuu kom de tega kam baŋa maama mo, se te taa ye maana abam de Baŋa Wɛ tetare ne. A pɛ abam chwoŋa se á kuri ŋwea de toone tetare ne, se á ta kuri Wɛ swolim de o sɔɔlem dem tetare ne. Konto to, twori-na ŋwea, se abam de á kwaga kam wane á ta‑á ŋwe, 20se á daare á ta‑á swoi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom á kwori á sɛ o kwora ye á sale‑o. Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na wó pa abam momwɛ-dɛɛre, ne á ná zo tega kalo o na pwooli de á nabaara Abaraham de Izaak de Jakob se o pa-ba to wone.”

english_text:
Final Speeches and the Death of Moses
Joshua Is Appointed the Leader of Israel
1Moses again spoke to the whole nation of Israel:
2 I am 120 years old, and I am no longer able to be your leader. And besides that, the Lord your God has told me that he won't let me cross the Jordan River. 3-5 But he has promised that he and Joshua will lead you across the Jordan to attack the nations that live on the other side. The Lord will destroy those nations just as he destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings. Just remember—whenever you capture a place, kill everyone who lives there.
6Be brave and strong! Don't be afraid of the nations on the other side of the Jordan. The Lord your God will always be at your side, and he will never abandon you.
7Then Moses called Joshua up in front of the crowd and said:
Joshua, be brave and strong as you lead these people into their land. The Lord made a promise long ago to Israel's ancestors that this land would someday belong to Israel. That time has now come, and you must divide up the land among the people. 8 The Lord will lead you into the land. He will always be with you and help you, so don't ever be afraid of your enemies.
Read These Laws
9Moses wrote down all of these laws and teachings and gave them to the priests and the leaders of Israel. The priests were from the Levi tribe, and they carried the sacred chest that belonged to the Lord. 10-11 Moses told these priests and leaders:
Each year the Israelites must come together to celebrate the Festival of Shelters at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. You must read these laws and teachings to the people at the festival every seventh year, the year when loans do not need to be repaid. 12-13Everyone must come—men, women, children, and even the foreigners who live in your towns. And each new generation will listen and learn to worship the Lord their God with fear and trembling and to do exactly what is said in God's Law.
Israel Will Reject the Lord
14The Lord told Moses, “You will soon die, so bring Joshua to the sacred tent, and I will appoint him the leader of Israel.”
Moses and Joshua went to the sacred tent, 15and the Lord appeared in a thick cloud right over the entrance to the tent. 16The Lord said:
Moses, you will soon die. But Israel is going into a land where other gods are worshiped, and Israel will reject me and start worshiping these gods. The people will break the agreement I made with them, 17and I will be so furious that I will abandon them and ignore their prayers. I will send disasters and suffering that will nearly wipe them out. Finally, they will realize that the disasters happened because I abandoned them. 18They will pray to me, but I will ignore them because they were evil and started worshiping other gods.
19Moses and Joshua, I am going to give you the words to a new song. Write them down and teach the song to the Israelites. If they learn it, they will know what I want them to do, and so they will have no excuse for not obeying me. 20I am bringing them into the land that I promised their ancestors. It is a land rich with milk and honey, and the Israelites will have more than enough food to eat. But they will get fat and turn their backs on me and start worshiping other gods. The Israelites will reject me and break the agreement that I made with them.
21When I punish the Israelites and their descendants with suffering and disasters, I will remind them that they know the words to this song, so they have no excuse for not obeying me.
I will give them the land that I promised, but I know the way they are going to live later on.
22Moses at once wrote down the words to the song, and he taught it to the Israelites.
23 The Lord told Joshua, “Be brave and strong! I will help you lead the people of Israel into the land that I have promised them.”
24Moses wrote down all these laws and teachings in a book, 25then he went to the Levites who carried the sacred chest and said:
26This is The Book of God's Law. Keep it beside the sacred chest that holds the agreement the Lord your God made with Israel. This book is proof that you know what the Lord wants you to do. 27I know how stubborn and rebellious you and the rest of the Israelites are. You have rebelled against the Lord while I have been alive, and it will only get worse after I am gone. 28So call together the leaders and officials of the tribes of Israel. I will bring this book and read every word of it to you, and I will call the sky and the earth as witnesses that all of you know what you are supposed to do.
29I am going to die soon, and I know that in the future you will stop caring about what is right and what is wrong, and so you will disobey the Lord and stop living the way I told you to live. The Lord will be angry, and terrible things will happen to you.
The Song of Moses
30Moses called a meeting of all the people of Israel, so he could teach them the words to the song that the Lord had given him. And here are the words:
translation_text:
Josua jeini Moses jeiŋa jei ne
1Moses daa ta ma vo o ta de Isarele tiina bam o we:
2“Amo laam jege bena bi de finlei mo. A daa bá wane a da á yiga. Ko ta woli da, Baŋa Wɛ tage jaja de amo o we, a bá tɔge a bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. 3Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom tete mo lage o da á yiga se á bɛ á vo á chɔge teene delo na wora to, ye á daare á zeili-ba pa se ba daare ba tega kam se á jwoŋi-ka á ta‑á tei. Josua mo wó taa wo á yiga ne ye á bɛ. Ko maama wó ke ne Baŋa Wɛ na bere tei to mo. 4Baŋa Wɛ wó chɔge nɔɔna bam konto ne o déem na ke Amori tiina pwa Sihon de Oga tei ye ba de ba teene dem maama chɔge to. 5Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ wó ke-ba á jeŋa ne se á wane-ba. Ko nam jege se á tɔge nia yalo amo na pɛ abam to se á chɔge-ba á ti. 6Ke-na dam á ke á tete kuri ne se á ta‑á jege baare. Yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone de-ba. Á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wo á tei ne. O bá fɔge o yage abam. O nam bá pa se á to.”
7Moses laam ma bwoŋi Josua o ta tento ded‑o Isarele tiina bam maama yiga ne o we:
“Yɔɔre n ke dam n ke n tete kuri ne, se n daare n ta‑n jege baare. Nmo mo jege se n da amo nɔɔna bam yiga se ba vo ba zo tega kalo ne Baŋa Wɛ na pwooli de ba nabaara se o pa-ba to. Nmo ta wó pɔɔre tega kam n pa-ba se ba taa tei. 8Baŋa Wɛ tete mo wó taa wo n tei ne se á ta‑á via. O bá fɔge o yage‑m. O nam bá pa se n to. Konto to, yé ta‑n lwia. Nam yé pa n vɔna pare.”
Wɛ nia yam garem
9Moses laam ma popone Wɛ nia yam o tiŋi, ye o daare o kwei-ya o pa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam de Isarele nakwa bam. Kaanem tiina bam déem nwoŋi Levi dwi dem wone mo ye ba yeini ba zeeri Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam. 10-11O ma ta de-ba o we:
“Bena yarepɛ bene dem maama ná yia, bene delo á na wó ma‑á chɛ balo na jege á jena to, se á ga Wɛ nia yam konto se Isarele tiina bam maama cheigi. Ko ye maŋa kalo ba na wó vo jeiga kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kuri ye ba jeeri o yiga ne se ba di Vwoa chwiim kuri dem to mo á jege se á ga á de ba zwa ne. 12Á wó bwoŋi nɔɔna bam maama, baara, de kaana, de bia, de veira balo na zoore á tei ne to, se ba maama la daane ba cheigi Wɛ nia yam. Konto wó pa se ba lɔre ba na wó ke tei ba taa kɔre Baŋa Wɛ ye ba toŋe ba tɔge o bera yam maama chekke. 13Ba kwaga kam de jwa wó ba ba cheigi Wɛ nia yam ye ba ya yeiri-ya. Banto de jege se ba lɔre ba na wó ke tei ba taa kɔre á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, maŋa kalo maama á na wó ta‑á zoore tega kalo ne á na lage á bɛ Jɔdan buga kam á jwoŋi se á ta‑á tei to.”
Wɛ na bere Moses tei o kweeli to
14 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we:
“Ko gɛ fee se n te. Bwoŋi Josua se á laam ba á zo wara-vwei dem ne se á tiŋi‑o se o ji á yiga tu.”
Moses de Josua ma vo ba zo vwei dem ne. 15Kunkwoŋo na zege deiki to ma ba ko dɔge vwei dem ni dem ne, ye Baŋa Wɛ zege kunkwoŋo kom wone. 16O ma ta de Moses o we:
“Ko bá dáane se n te. Nmo toone dem kwaga ne nam, nɔɔna banto bam wó zaŋe ba yage amo ba vo se ba taa zuli tega kalo ba na lage ba zo to wa-yɔɔro. Ba wó lɔ amo kwaga ne ye ba daare ba chɔge ni-gwonim delo a na ke de-ba to. 17Ko ná ke konto, a bane wó zaŋe ba baŋa ne lela, pa se a ma a kwaga a ya-ba. Amo yiga bá taa wo ba wone pa se ba na chɔgem. Yaara de chana dedɛ na wó ba ba baŋa ne to, ba wó ta nenɛɛne, ‘Bɛŋwaane mo yaara yanto wo debam baŋa ne? Ko dae debam Tu Wɛ wom na yage debam to ŋwaane mo na?’ 18Dɛ dem konto ne, amo yiga bere ka bá ta wo ba wone, ba na toŋe lwarem delo ye ba pipiri ba vo ba zuli wa-yɔɔro to ŋwaane.
19Konto ŋwaane, popone-na leiŋa kanto, se nmo, Moses, laam kwei-ka n ma‑n zamese Isarele tiina bam se ba wane ba taa leeni-ka. Leiŋa kam wó taa ye maana mo amo de banto laŋa ne we ba tusi. 20Amo lage a kale-ba a ja zo te-ŋoŋa kanto na ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ, ne amo na pwooli de ba nabaara se a ke tei to mo. Ba nam ná zo ba jeini da, ba wó taa nae wodiu ba di ba sui pa se ba nu lanyerane, ye ba daare ba pipiri ba taa zuli wa-yɔɔro. Ba wó ve amo ba daare ba chɔge ni-gwonim delo a na ke de-ba to. 21Yaara de chana dedɛ ná to ba baŋa ne, ba laam wó guli leiŋa kanto gula se ka taa ye maana mo we ba tusi. A maŋe a lɔre kolo ba na boŋe ba kana ne to ye a ta wo jaane-ba a zo tega kalo a na pwooli se a pa-ba to wone.”
22Dɛ dem konto ne, Moses ma popone leiŋa kam ye o kwei-ka o zamese Isarele tiina bam. 23Baŋa Wɛ ma pa Nun bu Josua ni ye o we, “Pa n bochare ke dam se n ta‑n jege baare. Nmo mo lage n tɔge Isarele tiina bam yiga se á vo á zo tega kalo ne a na pwooli se a pa-ba to. Amo nam wó taa wo nmo tei ne.”
24Moses ma popone Wɛ nia yam maama nyɔ o ke tɔnɔ ne. 25O na ti to, o ma ta de Levi tiina balo na zeeri Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam to o we, 26“Jwoŋi-na Wɛ nia tɔnɔ konto á ja vo á tiŋi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ni-gwonim dakaa kam teiŋa ne. Ko wó taa tigi da mo se ko taa ye maana we abam Isarele tiina bam tusi. 27A yei abam maama na jege wo-dɛɔ ye á zwa de ba ni tei to. Nii a ta na ŋwe a wo abam tei ne, ye á maŋe á ve Baŋa Wɛ ni dem, se a ná tega, ko bá dwoni konto na? 28Nam bwoŋi-na á dwia yam maama nakwa de á dedɛɛra se ba la daane se a ŋɔɔne wonnu tento de-ba se ba ni. A lage a kwei wɛyuu kom de tega kam baŋa maama mo, se te taa ye maana banto de Baŋa Wɛ tetare ne. 29A yei we amo toone dem kwaga ne, á wó biini á tete de wo-zɔɔna, ye á daare á ve Wɛ nia yalo a na bere abam to. Jwa seeni á wó toŋe lwarem kikia á chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga ye á zuli wonnu telo á na mɛ á jea á ke to. Baŋa Wɛ bane wó zaŋe pa se chanɛɛre to abam baŋa ne.”
Moses leiŋa kam
30Moses laam ma leeni leiŋa kanto maama o vo o kweeli ye Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama cheigi:

english_text:
1Earth and Sky,
listen to what I say!
2Israel, I will teach you.
My words will be like gentle rain
on tender young plants,
or like dew on the grass.
3Join with me in praising
the wonderful name
of the Lord our God.
4The Lord is a mighty rock,
and he never does wrong.
God can always be trusted
to bring justice.
5But you lie and cheat
and are unfaithful to him.
You have disgraced yourselves
and are no longer worthy
to be his children.
6Israel, the Lord is your Father,
the one who created you,
but you repaid him
by being foolish.
7Think about past generations.
Ask your parents
or any of your elders.
They will tell you
8 that God Most High
gave land to every nation.
He assigned a guardian angel
to each of them,
9but the Lord himself
takes care of Israel.
10Israel, the Lord discovered you
in a barren desert
filled with howling winds.
God became your fortress,
protecting you as though
you were his own eyes.
11The Lord was like an eagle
teaching its young to fly,
always ready to swoop down
and catch them on its back.
12Israel, the Lord led you,
and without the aid
of a foreign god,
13he helped you
capture the land.
Your fields were rich
with grain.
Olive trees grew
in your stony soil,
and honey was found
among the rocks.
14Your flocks and herds
produced milk and yogurt,
and you got choice meat
from your sheep and goats
that grazed in Bashan.
Your wheat was the finest,
and you drank the best wine.
15Israel, you grew fat and rebelled
against God, your Creator
you rejected the Mighty Rock,
your only place of safety.
16You made God jealous and angry
by worshiping disgusting idols
and foreign gods.
17 You offered sacrifices
to demons, those useless gods
that never helped you,
new gods that your ancestors
never worshiped.
18You turned away
from God, your Creator;
you forgot the Mighty Rock,
the source of your life.
19You were the Lord's children,
but you made him angry.
Then he rejected you 20and said,
“You are unfaithful
and can't be trusted.
So I won't answer your prayers;
I'll just watch and see
what happens to you.
21 You worshiped worthless idols,
and made me jealous
and angry!
Now I will send a cruel
and worthless nation
to make you jealous and angry.
22“My people, I will breathe out fire
that sends you down
to the world of the dead.
It will scorch your farmlands
and burn deep down
under the mountains.
23I'll send disaster after disaster
to strike you like arrows.
24You'll be struck by starvation
and deadly diseases,
by the fangs of wild animals
and poisonous snakes.
25Young and old alike
will be killed in the streets
and terrified at home.
26“I wanted to scatter you,
so no one would remember
that you had ever lived.
27But I dreaded the sound
of your enemies saying,
‘We defeated Israel with no help
from the Lord.’ ”
28People of Israel,
that's what the Lord
has said to you.
But you don't have good sense,
and you never listen
to advice.
29If you did, you could see
where you are headed.
30How could one enemy soldier
chase a thousand
of Israel's troops?
Or how could two of theirs
pursue ten thousand of ours?
It can only happen if the Lord
stops protecting Israel
and lets the enemy win.
31Even our enemies know
that only our God
is a Mighty Rock.
32Our enemies are grapevines
rooted in the fields
of Sodom and Gomorrah.
The grapes they produce
are full of bitter poison;
33their wine is more deadly
than cobra venom.
34But the Lord has written
a list of their sins
and locked it in his vault.
35 Soon our enemies will get
what they deserve—
suddenly they will slip,
and total disaster
will quickly follow.
36 When only a few
of the Lord's people remain,
when their strength is gone,
and some of them are slaves,
the Lord will feel sorry for them
and give them justice.
37But first the Lord will say,
“You ran for safety to other gods—
couldn't they help you?
38You offered them wine
and your best sacrifices.
Can't those gods help you now
or give you protection?
39Don't you understand?
I am the only God;
there are no others.
I am the one who takes life
and gives it again.
I punished you with suffering.
But now I will heal you,
and nothing can stop me!
40“I make this solemn promise:
Just as I live forever,
41I will take revenge
on my hateful enemies.
I will sharpen my sword
and let it flash
like lightning.
42My arrows will get drunk
on enemy blood;
my sword will taste the flesh
and the blood of the enemy.
It will kill prisoners,
and cut off the heads
of their leaders.”
43 Tell the heavens to celebrate
and all gods to bow down
to the Lord,
because he will take revenge
on those hateful enemies
who killed his people.
He will forgive the sins of Israel
and purify their land.
44-45Moses spoke the words of the song so that all the Israelites could hear, and Joshua helped him. When Moses had finished, 46he said, “Always remember this song I have taught you today. And let it be a warning that you must teach your children to obey everything written in The Book of God's Law. 47The Law isn't empty words. It can give you a long life in the land that you are going to take.”
Moses Will See the Land
48 Later that day the Lord said to Moses:
49Go up into the Abarim Mountain range here in Moab across the Jordan River valley from Jericho. And when you reach the top of Mount Nebo, you will be able to see the land of Canaan, which I am giving to Israel. 50Then you will die and be buried on the mountaintop, just as your brother Aaron died and was buried on Mount Hor. 51Both of you were unfaithful to me at Meribah Spring near Kadesh in the Zin Desert. I am God, but there in front of the Israelites, you did not treat me with the honor and respect I deserve. 52So I will give the land to the people of Israel, but you will only get to see it from a distance.
translation_text:
1“Tega baŋa, ba n cheigi a taane dem!
Se wɛyuu de, ba n ni kolo a na jege se a ta to!
2Wɛ wó pa a berem dem to á zwa ne
ne kunkwoŋo na siiri tei to mo,
ne nyɔnɔ de na to tega ne tei to.
A botare sem wó taa nye de do-mimina na siiri
men-chena de ga-lɛɛro baŋa ne tei to mo.
3A lage a zeiŋi Baŋa Wɛ yere!
Ba-na dé zuli dé Tu Wɛ wom de o kamunni dem.
4 Baŋa Wɛ maa ye peo mo o pae debam.
O totoŋa maama lana dedɛ,
ye o chwei sem de yɔɔre se jege chega.
Nɔɔna wae ba sale o yera ne,
ye o ba kwane o ni.
Kolo maama o na toŋe to ye chega mo.
5Abam Wɛ nɔɔna bam nam lɔge o kwaga ne.
Á ye chaveera yerane mo,
ye chwoŋa daa tera se á ta‑á ye o nɔɔna,
á na tiini á tusi to ŋwaane.
6Agɛboŋa tiina, mo á na wó ke Baŋa Wɛ tei na?
Á ba jege swa!
Wonto mo ye á Kwo de á Keiru.
O maa ye wolo na pɛ abam kugu jei logo baŋa ne to.
7Guli-na faŋa faŋa da yam de á nabaara bam gula.
Bwei-na á kwoa de nɔn-kwe sem,
se ba ta ba bere abam kolo déem na ke to.
8Yuu-tu Wɛ wom mo pɔɔre logo baŋa dwia maama,
o daare o pa nabiina dwi maama ba tega kam.
O ma pa teo maama taa jege ko siseini,
se ko tɔge wɛyuu kɔgɔ kom na mae tei to.
9Ko daare Jakob de o kwaga kam mo o kuri o pa o tete,
se ba taa ye o tete nyɔn-mage nɔɔna.
10O déem nɛ o nɔɔna bam
ba na kare ba beeri kagoa yuu ne,
mɛ sam na tera ye vio yerane mo zɔre ko yaga to.
O ma cho-ba ye o nii ba baŋa ne,
o yi na page ba baŋa ne to ŋwaane.
11 Baŋa Wɛ ma korese-ba lanyerane,
ne maao na kɔne ko bia
ye ko yarege ko vɔna ko kɔgese-ba lanyerane tei to.
12 Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo yeini o kale o nɔɔna bam,
ye wa-yɔɔro wo dɛ te zeini‑o.
13O ma pa-ba chwoŋa se ba taa tei logo kom zwonnu tem yuu,
ye ba di wodi-twaro.
Ba déem lɔɔne tooro mo peero jei ne,
ba daare ba na nuga kandwa jei ne,
mɛ Olivi teeni na leiri bia lanyerane to.
14Ba naane de ba bone pɛ-ba nayela dedɛ de nayel-pepala.
Ba vara de déem nugi lanyerane,
pei, de bone, de naane maama.
Ba ta ma na men-dala se ba di,
de Vini sa-ywoŋo se ba nyɔ.
15Wɛ nɔn-swonnu tem déem jaane duum,
ye ba laam ji zwabani-nyena.
Ba ma di wodiu ba su pa se ba nu lanyerane.
Ba lɔge ba Keiru Wɛ kwaga ne.
Chega to, o ye ba vereno,
o ta kwori o ye peo o pa-ba,
ye ba ta ve‑o.
16 Baŋa Wɛ bane ma zaŋe ba baŋa ne,
ba na yage‑o ye ba daare ba zuli wa-yɔɔro de wo-zɔɔna to ŋwaane.
Ko déem pɛ se o ke kazwe ba ŋwaane.
17Ba déem kaane ba pa tangwana,
ba ma leiri Wɛ yuu ne.
Ba ya yeiri wa-yɔɔro tem konto.
Te maa ye jwo-doora yalo ba nabaara ya na wo zuli to.
18Ba swei Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom swia,
de o na maŋe o ye wolo na pɛ-ba ŋwea to de.
Ba mɛ ba kwaga ba ya wolo na loge-ba to.
19 Baŋa Wɛ ma na ba na ke tei to,
ye o daare o ve-ba,
ba na ye o bia ye ba ke puseŋa ded‑o to ŋwaane.
20O déem tage o we:
A yiga daa bá taa wo ba wone.
Nam yage se dé nii ko na lage ko ke-ba tei to.
Ba ye a bia ye ba ta ba kɔre amo,
pa se ba tiini ba tusi.
21Ba tɔge jwo-yɔɔro mo
pa se a bane zaŋe,
ye a ke kazwe ba ŋwaane.
Mo kokuri a lage a tɔge dwi-gɛ tiina balo na ye nɔn-yɔɔro to baŋa ne
a ma pa a tete nɔɔna bam bane zaŋe
se ba de ke kazwe.
22Amo bane dem wó zaŋe de tɔrege mo ne mini tei,
se de di logo baŋa de ko wodiiru maama,
de vo de yi tega kam kuri kuri,
dedaane peero tem kura ga kula.
23A ta wó ja cham dedɛ
a ba a yage ba baŋa ne,
pa se ba tiini ba na zonne,
ne a ná tage a che-tɛɛra maama ba baŋa ne a ti tei to.
24Kana, de paa, de jawe-chɛɛro dwi maama wó ja-ba,
se ba yaare ba te.
A ta wó toŋe kago-vara de tega-veila
a yage ba yera ne se te done-ba te go.
25Ba ná nwoŋi pwooni yiga, ba dona wó go-ba.
Ba nam ná maŋe diga ne, foone wó ja-ba.
Nɔn-donno, de busankane, de bu-sese, de nɔn-kwe de bá daare.
Ba maama wó te.
26A ya wó ta we, ‘A lage a chɔge-ba zɔŋ-zɔŋ mo,
se ba yera saare logo baŋa ne
se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé guli ba gula.’
27A nam ba lage se ba dona taa jege fia
ye ba mage ba nyɔɔna ba we,
‘Debam mo wane Isarele tiina bam
se ko dae Baŋa Wɛ mo kea.’
28Isarele tiina nam ba jege swa
ye ba boboŋa tera.
29Ba ya ná jege swa,
ba ya wó wuuri ba lɔre kolo na lage ko ke-ba to.
Ba nam ware se ba ni kokuri.
30Bɛ mo wó pa nɔɔno dedoa wane nɔɔna moro o zeili,
ye nɔɔna balei wane nɔɔna morro kuni fuga?
Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ na yage-ba to ŋwaane mo.
Wolo na ye peo o pa-ba to
mo kwei-ba o ke ba dona jeŋa ne.
31 Baŋa Wɛ na ye debam peo to,
dé dona bam yei we
ba ba jege wɛ delo dam na yi debam Baŋa Wɛ wom dam to.
32Ba nye de Vini teeni na leiri tio-bi-balwaaro to mo.
Ba kugu jei maa wo Sodom de Gomora ne.
33Ba Vini tio-bia pa nyoa na tiini ka chana
ne sana balo ba na mɛ basankwe vea ba ma ke to.
34 Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
‘Amo maŋe a yei a na wó ke Isarele tiina dona bam tei to.
Ko wo a boboŋa ne se ka maŋa ná yia, se a le-de.
35Amo mo wó jwoori a ŋwe ba keim-balwaaro jene,
se ba na kolo na maŋe de-ba to.
Dɛ wó ba ye ba to tega ne,
se lɛɛro laam ba te chɔge-ba
pa se ba daa bá zaŋe wɛɛne.’
36 Baŋa Wɛ wó zaŋe o bore o nɔɔna bam bora.
O ná nɛ we ba dam ti
ye ba wolowolo daa wo daare
tembia dedaane kabɛ de,
o laam wó duri ba yibwona.
37O maa wó bwei o nɔɔna we:
‘Á wa-yɔɔro tem nam bɛ,
ye á ya boŋe se á sale ya yera ne?
38Á kwei á vara bam lara á ma‑á kaane-ya,
se á kwei á sana bam á ma‑á ke pɛɛra á pa-ya.
Ya wó zaŋe ya ba ya zeini abam na?
Ya wó wane ya kwoli abam ya che na?
39Lɔre-na we, amo yerane mo ye Wɛ chekke.
Wɛ dedwoŋi daa tera.
Amo mo pae nabiina momwɛ tia,
ye a daare a pae badwonna jege ŋwea.
A maa ke zonne nɔɔna yera ne,
ye a daare a yɔɔre-ba.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na wó wane o dwoni de amo.
40A lage a zeiŋi a jeŋa wɛɛne se a du duuri we,
Ne amo na jege ŋwea taa wuu to,
41a laam wó dwori a se-zɔɔ,
se ko taa jege ni ye ko nyeena.
A ta wó kwei-ko a taa zia se a zage a dona,
ye a waare balo na chuli-ne to.
42A che-tɛɛra yam nia wó taare de jana.
A se-zɔɔ kom de wó zɔ ba ya-nɔna yam.
Ba jar-keira bam wolowolo bá lu.
Ko ná ye balo na nɛ zonne de balo ba na jaane ba vɔ to,
a wó go ba maama,
ye a gwo ba yiga tiina bam yuni.’
43Logo baŋa dwi tiina maama,
tɔge-na de Wɛ nɔɔna bam
se á ta‑á tei Baŋa Wɛ de wopwolo.
O lage o ŋwe balo na goe o nɔɔna bam to jene,
se o waare o dona bam maama.
Ko nam ná ye o nɔɔna bam,
o wó yage ba wɛleera o ma chɛ-ba,
se o pa ba tega kam fɔge ka kwɛ lanyerane.”
44Moses ma tɔge de Nun bu Josua o vo o leeni leiŋa kanto se Isarele tiina bam wane ba ni. 45O na tole ka botare sem maama o ti to, 46o laam ma ta de-ba o we, “Ta‑á yei-na se á guli taane delo a na pɛ abam zem tento to. Lwoni-na á bere á bia, se ba de wane ba sɛ ba tɔge Wɛ bera yam maama na popone ya tiŋi tento to. 47Bera yanto dae ta-gwoa. Ya jege ŋwea ya pae abam mo konto. Á ná tɔge-ya chekke, á wó wane á dáane tega kalo wone á na lage á bɛ Jɔdan buga kam á zo á ta‑á tei to.”
Moses nii o na Kanaan tega kam
48Dɛ dem konto ne mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Moses o we:
49“Zaŋe n vo Abarim zwonnu laŋa kam na wo Moaba ne to. N ná yi da, diini Nebo peo kom yuu na jeeri Jeriko teo kom to se n nii n na Kanaan tega kam. A lage a kwei tega kam konto a pa Isarele tiina bam se ba taa tei. 50Ko kwaga ne n wó te peo kom yuu ne mo, ne n zembaaro Aron na maŋe o te Hora peo yuu ne tei to. 51Abam balei déem ve amo ni mo Isarele tiina bam yiga ne, maŋa kalo á na beeri Zin kagoa wone á vo á yi Meriba-kadese buli-yi seeni to. Á déem wo pɛ amo zula nɔɔna bam yiga ne. 52Konto ŋwaane, nmo wó zege yiga yiga mo n nii n na tega kam. N za‑n bá‑n na pwola se n zo tega kalo a na lage a pa Isarele tiina bam to wone.”

english_text:
Moses Blesses the Tribes of Israel
1Moses was a prophet, and before he died, he blessed the tribes of Israel by saying:
2The Lord came from Mount Sinai.
From Edom, he gave light
to his people,
and his glory was shining
from Mount Paran.
Thousands of his warriors
were with him, and fire
was at his right hand.
3 The Lord loves the tribes
of Israel,
and he protects his people.
They listen to his words
and worship at his feet.
* 4I called a meeting
of the tribes of Israel
and gave you God's Law.
5Then you and your leaders
made the Lord your king.
6Tribe of Reuben, you will live,
even though your tribe
will always be small.
7The Lord will listen to you,
tribe of Judah, as you beg
to come safely home.
You fought your enemies alone;
now the Lord will help you.
8 At Massah and Meribah Spring,
the Lord tested you,
tribe of Levi.
You were faithful,
and so the priesthood belongs
to the Levi tribe.
9Protecting Israel's agreement
with the Lord
was more important to you
than the life of your father
or mother,
or brothers or sisters,
or your own children.
10You teach God's laws to Israel,
and at the place of worship
you offer sacrifices
and burn incense.
11I pray that the Lord will bless
everything you do,
and make you strong enough
to crush your enemies.
12The Lord Most High loves you,
tribe of Benjamin.
He will live among your hills
and protect you.
13Descendants of Joseph,
the Lord will bless you
with precious water
from deep wells
and with dew from the sky.
14Month by month, your fruit
will ripen in the sunshine.
15You will have a rich harvest
from the slopes
of the ancient hills.
16The Lord who appeared
in the burning bush
wants to give you the best
the land can produce,
and it will be a princely crown
on Joseph's head.
17The armies of Ephraim
and Manasseh
are majestic and fierce
like a bull or a wild ox.
They will run their spears
through faraway nations.
18Be happy, Zebulun,
as your boats set sail;
be happy, Issachar,
in your tents.
19The sea will make you wealthy,
and from the sandy beach
you will get treasure.
So invite the other tribes
to celebrate with you
and offer sacrifices to God.
20Tribe of Gad,
the Lord will bless you
with more land.
So shout his praises!
Your tribe is like a lion
ripping up its victim.
21Your leaders met together
and chose the best land
for your tribe,
but you obeyed the Lord
and helped the other tribes.
22Tribe of Dan,
you are like a lion cub,
startled by a snake.
23The Lord is pleased with you,
people of Naphtali.
He will bless you
and give you the land
to the west and the south.
24The Lord's greatest blessing
is for you, tribe of Asher.
You will be the favorite
of all the other tribes.
You will be rich with olive oil
25and have strong town gates
with bronze and iron bolts.
Your people will be powerful
for as long as they live.
26Israel, no other god
is like ours—
the clouds are his chariot
as he rides across the skies
to come and help us.
27The eternal God
is our hiding place;
he carries us in his arms.
When God tells you
to destroy your enemies,
he will make them run.
28Israel, you will live in safety;
your enemies will be gone.
The dew will fall from the sky,
and you will have plenty
of grain and wine.
29The Lord has rescued you
and given you more blessings
than any other nation.
He protects you like a shield
and is your majestic sword.
Your enemies will bow in fear,
and you will trample
on their backs.
translation_text:
Moses lwoori Wɛ swolim Isarele dwia yam maama ŋwaane
1Wɛ swolim delo o tontoŋeno Moses déem na sɔɔle o ke Isarele tiina bam yuu ne ye o laam te to mo tento:
2“Baŋa Wɛ déem zege Sinayi peo kom ne
o ba o veere o tete o pa o nɔɔna bam.
O ma zaŋe Edom zwonnu tem yuu ne
nenɛɛne wea na puli tei to,
ye o zege Paran peo yuu ne
o nyeene pwooni ba baŋa ne.
Malese kɔgɔ kɔgɔ mo wo o tei ne,
ye mini de wo o jazem seeni de pepela.
3Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ jege o nɔɔna bam swono.
O maa cho balo o na pɔɔre o pa o tete to.
Konto ŋwaane mo ba chɔɔle ba tete o yiga ne
se ba sɛ o bera yam.
4Dé sɛ Wɛ nia yalo Moses na pɛ debam to,
ya na ye debam dwi dem lonne na dwoi maama to.
5Isarele dwi tiina de ba yiga tiina bam maama na lage daane to,
Baŋa Wɛ déem mo jigi pɛ o nɔn-swonnu tem baŋa ne.”
Ruben dwi dem yera taane:
6“Wɛ bá pa se Ruben dwi dem saare,
de ba na maŋe ba ba daga to de.”
7Judah dwi dem yera taane:
“Baŋa Wɛ, cheigi Judah dwi tiina bam,
de ba na lwoori zeinim nmo tei ne to.
Pa se ba jwoori ba fɔge de ba dwia yadwonna yam.
Kwei dam n ke ba jeŋa ne,
se ba dona yé wane-ba.”
8Levi dwi dem yera taane:
“Baŋa Wɛ, kwei n Yurim de Turim kandwa yam
n ke n tontoŋena Levi dwi tiina bam jeŋa ne
se ba ma lɔre n boboŋa.
Ba na wo Massa ne to,
nmo déem faŋe-ba mo n nii.
Ba ta na wo Meriba buli-yi dem seeni to,
n ta jaane de-ba mo.
9Ba nam bere ba chega de nmo,
ye ba toŋe ba tɔge n bera yam de n ni-gwonim dem,
se ko dwoni ba kwoa, de ba niina, de ba chorro, de ba bia.
10Ba yeini ba bere n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam
se ba taa sɛ n bera yam.
Ba ta zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa nmo yiga ne,
ye ba daare ba zwɛ vara n bimbini dem baŋa ne
ba ma ke kaanem ba pa‑m.
11 Baŋa Wɛ, swɛ Levi dwi dem swolim,
se ba taa jege dunni,
se ba kikia de taa pwoli nmo wo.
Chɔge ba dona maama,
se ba daa yé jwoori ba zaŋe.”
12Benjamin dwi dem yera taane:
“Dwi dento mo Baŋa Wɛ tiini o swoi.
O maa cho-ba se kolokolo yé yi-ba.
O maa wo ba tei ne maŋa maama,
pa se ba sii o woro wone.”
13Josɛf dwi dem yera taane:
“Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ ba tega kam swolim,
pa se nyɔnɔ nwoŋi wɛyuu,
se na de taa bura ba nwoŋi tega kuri ne ba pa-ba.
14Wea wó taa pae se ba wodiiru taa bera lanyerane,
ye ba na dedɛ chane sem maama wone.
15Faŋa faŋa zwonnu tem wó faare de teeni-bia,
ye wodiiru de wó ke lanyerane peero tem yuu ne.
16Josɛf dwi tiina wó na wo-laaro telo maama na puli tega baŋa ne to.
Baŋa Wɛ wolo déem na zege sabara kam wone o ŋɔɔne to
wó ke zaane ba yuu ne.
Wɛ wó zeini-ba konto,
Josɛf déem na jigi o chorro tem yiga tu to ŋwaane.
17Josɛf jege dam ne nabea mo tei.
O bia balei, Efrayim de Manasɛ nye de kago-vara nyea yam
na wae ba dona ya chua to mo.
Efrayim jege jar-keira morro kuni fuga,
ye Manasɛ de jege jar-keira morro morro.
Ba wae dwi-gɛ tiina bam ba zeila
ba ja vo ba yi logo baŋa kweelim jei.”
18Zebulun de Isakara dwia yam yera taane:
“Zebulun dwi tiina bam, ta‑á jege-na wopwolo,
de á na nwoŋi á beeri yiga yiga tei to.
Isakara dwi tiina bam, ta‑á jege-na wopwolo,
de á na maŋe sɔŋɔ ne tei to.
19Ba wó bwoŋi dwia yadwonna tiina
se ba ba ba di peo kom yuu
ye ba ke kaanem delo na ye chekke to ba pa Wɛ.
Ba nae ba dunni dem pipiu baŋa ne mo,
ye ba na tɔge naneo kom wo ba beeri to
ba ta guri wonnu telo na seigi kasolo kom wone to de.”
20Gad dwi dem yera taane:
“Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na wó pa Gad laŋa kam taa daga to.
Tei-na o yere!
Gad yɔɔre o pɔe mo ne nywoŋo tei.
O lage o zi varem
se o ja ko jeŋa naa ko yuu o kaare.
21O ma kuri tega kalo na tiini ka lamma to o pa o tete.
Isarele dwia yam yiga tiina bam na gilimi daane
se ba pɔɔre tega kam to,
mo ba le nakwe popɔra ba pa‑o.
O ma toŋe o tɔge Baŋa Wɛ chwoŋa kam chekke,
ye o sɛ Wɛ nia yalo o na pɛ Isarele tiina bam to.”
22Dan dwi dem yera taane:
“Dan nye de nywoŋ-pɔla mo.
O zege Basan ne mo o faŋe o nwoŋi.”
23Nafitali dwi dem yera taane:
“Nafitali dwi tiina totoŋa yam mo su Baŋa Wɛ yi,
ye Wɛ tiini o swɛ ba swolim.
Ba laŋa kam wó tɔge naneo kom
de tega-kuri seeni maama.”
24Asere dwi dem yera taane:
“Wɛ wó swɛ Asere dwi tiina bam swolim,
se ko dwoni dwia yadwonna yam maama.
Ba chorro tem wó taa swoi-ba.
Ba ta wó na Olivi nuga dedɛ ba tega kam ne.
25Ba wó ma luuru de channa mo
ba fɔge ba pe ba teene dem manchwo-nia yam.
Ba ta wó na dam se ko yi ba ŋwea da yam maama.”
26“Baŋa Wɛ nɔn-swonnu tem,
wɛ dedwoŋi daa tera de na nye de Baŋa Wɛ wom.
O jege nenɔŋa mo ye o dɔge kunkwonnu baŋa ne
o kaare wɛyuu maama o duri o ba se o zeini abam.
27Taa-wuu Baŋa Wɛ mo ye abam dalem jei.
O maa teili abam o jea ne ye o ba yaga.
O daa ta zeili á dona á yiga ne
ye o we, ‘Yɔɔre á chɔge-ba-na!’
28Konto to, Isarele dwi tiina bam nɛ pwola
se ba taa zoore de wo-zuru.
Jakob kwaga kam nɛ ba kugu jei.
Wɛyuu nyɔnɔ maa bugi tega kam
ye ka su de mena de sa-ywoŋo.
29Isarele dwi tiina bam, á jege yu-ywoŋo!
Dwi tera de na nye de abam.
Ko ye abam mo Baŋa Wɛ jwoŋi o yage.
O maa kwoli abam
ne jara nantana na kwoli nɔɔno jara wone tei to.
O daa ta nye de se-zɔɔ á jeŋa ne
se o zeini abam jara wone.
O wó pa á wane á dona á di,
pa se ba lwoori yibwona á tei ne.
Á nam wó nɔne-ba á se tega ne.”

english_text:
The Death of Moses
1Sometime later, Moses left the lowlands of Moab. He went up Mount Pisgah to the peak of Mount Nebo, which is across the Jordan River from Jericho. The Lord showed him all the land as far north as Gilead and the town of Dan. 2He let Moses see the territories that would soon belong to the tribes of Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Judah, as far west as the Mediterranean Sea. 3The Lord also showed him the land in the south, from the valley near the town of Jericho, known as The City of Palm Trees, down to the town of Zoar.
4 The Lord said, “Moses, this is the land I was talking about when I solemnly promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that I would give land to their descendants. I have let you see it, but you will not cross the Jordan and go in.”
5And so, Moses the Lord's servant died there in Moab, just as the Lord had said. 6The Lord buried him in a valley near the town of Beth-Peor, but even today no one knows exactly where. 7Moses was 120 years old when he died, yet his eyesight was still good, and his body was strong.
8The people of Israel stayed in the lowlands of Moab, where they mourned and grieved 30 days for Moses, as was their custom.
Joshua Becomes the Leader of Israel
9Before Moses died, he had placed his hands on Joshua, and the Lord had given Joshua wisdom. The Israelites paid attention to what Joshua said and obeyed the commands that the Lord had given Moses.
Moses Was a Great Prophet
10 There has never again been a prophet in Israel like Moses. The Lord spoke face to face with him 11and sent him to perform powerful miracles in the presence of the king of Egypt and his entire nation. 12No one else has ever had the power to do such great things as Moses did for everyone to see.
translation_text:
Moses toone dem
1Moses déem ma zege Moaba pwaro tem ne o vo o yi Nebo peo kom. O ma di Pisiga peo kom yuu na jeeri Jeriko teo kom to. Dáane mo Baŋa Wɛ bere‑o tega kam maama, ko zege Gilead laŋa kam ne se ko vo ko yi Dan laŋa kam. 2Wɛ daa ta bere‑o Nafitali laŋa kam maama, de Efrayim de Manasɛ jei sem, de Judah laŋa kam se ko taa vei wɛ-zoore seeni ko vo ko yi Mediterania naneo kom, 3ko ta woli de tega-kuri kagoa kam, de bwolo tega kalo na tole ka zege Jeriko ne se ko vo ko yi Zoara to. Ba déem jege Jeriko ba bwoi we ‘Konkware teo kom’.
4 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Tega kanto mo amo dugi duuri ka ŋwaane a pwooli de Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob se a kwei-ka a pa ba kwaga kam. A laam nam pɛ se n na-ka de n yia mo, ko daare n bá‑n na chwoŋa se n bɛ n vo n zo ka wone.”
5 Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses ma te dáane, Moaba laŋa kam ne. Ko déem ke nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na wuuri o ta tei to. 6Ba ma suli‑o Moaba bwolo kodwoŋi ne, ko na jeeri Bɛte-Peora to. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam yeiri mɛ chekke ba na ke‑o to de zem maama. 7Moses na tege to, o déem jaane bena bi de finlei mo. O déem ya ta jege dam, ye o yia de dana lanyerane.
8Isarele tiina bam déem ma maŋe Moaba laŋa kam ne ba kwei da fintɔ ba ma keeri Moses lua kam se ba laam ke ba ti.
9Ko nam ná ye Nun bu Josua, Wɛ déem pɛ‑o swa lanyerane, Moses na kuri wonto se o leiri o yuu ne to ŋwaane. Mo kokuri Isarele tiina bam déem sɛ Josua ni ye ba toŋe ba tɔge nia yalo Baŋa Wɛ ya na pɛ Moses to.
10 Baŋa Wɛ déem ŋɔɔne de Moses jaja mo. Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu wodwoŋi daa ta wo zaŋe Isarele tiina bam wone o na nye de Moses 11ye o toŋe wo-kamunnu de wo-kenkagela se ya ta nye de yalo Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe Moses se o toŋe Ejipti Pa-faro wom, de o nakwa, de o teo kom maama yiga ne to dwoŋi. 12Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa tera o na jege dam konto dwoŋi se o wane o ke wo-kamunnu na jege foone se te maŋe de Moses na toŋe tei Isarele tiina bam maama yibia ne to.

english_text:
Joshua Becomes the Leader of Israel
1Moses, the Lord's servant, was dead. So the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, who had been the assistant of Moses. The Lord said:
2My servant Moses is dead. Now you must lead Israel across the Jordan River into the land I'm giving to all of you. 3 Wherever you go, I'll give you that land, as I promised Moses. 4It will reach from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains in the north, and to the northeast as far as the great Euphrates River. It will include the land of the Hittites, and the land from here at the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea on the west. 5 Joshua, I will always be with you and help you as I helped Moses, and no one will ever be able to defeat you.
6-8 Long ago I promised the ancestors of Israel that I would give this land to their descendants. So be strong and brave! Be careful to do everything my servant Moses taught you. Never stop reading The Book of the Law he gave you. Day and night you must think about what it says. If you obey it completely, you and Israel will be able to take this land.
9I've commanded you to be strong and brave. Don't ever be afraid or discouraged! I am the Lord your God, and I will be there to help you wherever you go.
The Eastern Tribes Promise To Help
10Joshua ordered the tribal leaders 11to go through the camp and tell everyone:
In a few days we will cross the Jordan River to take the land that the Lord our God is giving us. So prepare as much food as you'll need for the march into the land.
12 Joshua told the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
13-14The Lord's servant Moses said that the Lord our God has given you land here on the east side of the Jordan River, where you could live in peace. Your wives and children and your animals can stay here in the land Moses gave you. But all of you that can serve in our army must pick up your weapons and lead the men of the other tribes across the Jordan River. They are your relatives, so you must help them 15conquer the land that the Lord is giving them. The Lord will give peace to them as he has given peace to you, and then you can come back and settle here in the land that Moses promised you.
16The men answered:
We'll cross the Jordan River and help our relatives. We'll fight anywhere you send us. 17-18If the Lord our God will help you as he helped Moses, and if you are strong and brave, we will obey you as we obeyed Moses. We'll even put to death anyone who rebels against you or refuses to obey you.
translation_text:
Josua jigi Isarele tiina bam yiga tu
1Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses toone dem kwaga ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma ŋɔɔne dedaane Nun bu Josua. Wonto déem mo yeini o woli Moses. Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
2“Amo tontoŋeno Moses tega. Nmo laam nam zaŋe n to amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam yiga ne se á bɛ Jɔdan buga kam á zo tega kalo amo na wó pa abam to. 3Amo lage a ke kolo a déem na tage dedaane Moses to mo. Abam ná gwɛ á yi jei selo maama, amo wó kwei tega kam a pa abam. 4Abam laŋa kam siseini wó zege kagoa kalo na wo kuri seeni to, ka tole konto ka yi Lebanon peero tem na wo baŋa seeni to. Ka wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem maa wó zege Yuferata bu-zaŋa kam ne ka tɔge Hiti tiina tega kam maama seeni, se ka laam taa vei Mediterania naneo kom na wo wɛ-zoore seeni to. 5Amo wó taa wo nmo tei ne maŋa maama, nenɛɛne a déem na wo Moses tei ne tei to. Amo bá fɔge a yage‑m. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno de nam bá wane o dwoni de nmo.
6Ke dam n ke n tete kuri ne, se n daare n ta‑n jege baare. Kokuri, nmo mo lage n tɔge nɔɔna bam yiga se á zo á jwoŋi tega kalo a na gwoni ni se a pa á nabaara bam to. 7Yɔɔre n ke dam n tete kuri ne, se n daare n tiini n ta‑n jege baare. Nam ta sɛ Wɛ nia yalo amo tontoŋeno Moses na bere‑m to. Yé virigi n kwaga n ya-ya, se yanto mo wó pa‑m yiga-veiŋa. 8Maŋa maama, se n ta‑n zamese Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom, se n daare n zo ya wo n boŋe ya boboŋa. Nmo ma‑n ná sɛ o nia yam na bere tei maama to, nmo wó seene n na yiga-veiŋa chekke. 9Amo nam maŋe a ta dede‑m we n ke dam n ke n tete kuri ne se n ta ta‑n jege baare. Yé ta‑n fona, nam yé pa se n vɔna pare. Kokuri, amo mo ye nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Jei selo maama nmo na wó vo to, amo wó taa wora de nmo.”
10Josua laam ma pa Isarele tiina dedɛɛra bam ni o we, 11“Véi-na nɔɔna bam tiga jei sem ne, se á ta de-ba we, ‘Ti-na á wodiiru yiga se da yatɔ maŋa ne mo á lage á bɛ Jɔdan buga kam se á zo tega kalo abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na gwoni ni se o pa abam to.’ ”
12Josua ta ma ta de Ruben dwi dem, de Gad dwi dem dedaane Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom o we: 13“Guli-na Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses déem na tage tei dedaane abam to. O déem we, ‘Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ lage o pa abam tega kanto mo se á jeini da.’ 14-15Nam pa-na se á kaana, de á bia, dedaane á vara bam maŋe ywo-seeni. Abam nɔɔna balo maama na yei jara keim to maa wó vɔ ba jara zela diŋ-diŋ, ye ba tɔge de á dwonna Isarele tiina bam se á bɛ Jɔdan buga kam á vo á woli banto se ba wane ba jwoŋi tega kalo na wo buga kam bubɛ delo na jeeri wɛ-zoore seeni ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwei o pa-ba to. Wɛ maa ná pɛ Isarele tiina bam maama ba jeiŋa jei, se abam de laam jwoori á tega kam na wo Jɔdan bubɛ delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni ye Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses kwei o pa abam to wone.”
16Ba de ma leiri‑o ba we, “Dé wó sɛ nmo ni dem maama n na pɛ debam to, ye n ná toŋe debam jei selo maama, dé wó vo. 17Debam wó taa sɛ nmo ni maŋa maama mo nenɛɛne dé déem na sɛ Moses ni tei to. Dé nam teene we nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó taa wo n tei ne nenɛɛne o déem na wora de Moses tei to. 18Wolo maama nam ná gwooni‑m ye o ve se o sɛ nmo taane, se ba go‑o. Konto ŋwaane, yɔɔre n ke dam n tete kuri ne, se n daare n ta‑n jege baare de n totoŋa yam.”

english_text:
Rahab Helps the Israelite Spies
1 Joshua chose two men as spies and sent them from their camp at Acacia with these instructions: “Go across the river and find out as much as you can about the whole region, especially about the town of Jericho.”
The two spies left the Israelite camp at Acacia and went to Jericho, where they decided to spend the night at the house of a prostitute named Rahab.
2But someone found out about them and told the king of Jericho, “Some Israelite men came here tonight, and they are spies.” 3-7So the king sent soldiers to Rahab's house to arrest the spies.
Meanwhile, Rahab had taken the men up to the flat roof of her house and had hidden them under some piles of flax plants that she had put there to dry.
The soldiers came to her door and demanded, “Let us have the men who are staying at your house. They are spies.”
She answered, “Some men did come to my house, but I didn't know where they had come from. They left about sunset, just before it was time to close the town gate. I don't know where they were going, but if you hurry, maybe you can catch them.”
The guards at the town gate let the soldiers leave Jericho, but they closed the gate again as soon as the soldiers went through. Then the soldiers headed toward the Jordan River to look for the spies at the place where people cross the river.
8Rahab went back up to her roof. The spies were still awake, so she told them:
9I know that the Lord has given Israel this land. Everyone shakes with fear because of you. 10 We heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea so you could leave Egypt. And we heard how you destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River. 11We know that the Lord your God rules heaven and earth, and we've lost our courage and our will to fight.
12Please promise me in the Lord's name that you will be as kind to my family as I have been to you. Do something to show 13that you won't let your people kill my father and mother and my brothers and sisters and their families.
14“Rahab,” the spies answered, “if you keep quiet about what we're doing, we promise to be kind to you when the Lord gives us this land. We pray that the Lord will kill us if we don't keep our promise!”
15Rahab's house was built into the town wall, and one of the windows in her house faced outside the wall. She gave the spies a rope, showed them the window, and said, “Use this rope to let yourselves down to the ground outside the wall. 16Then hide in the hills. The men who are looking for you won't be able to find you there. They'll give up and come back after a few days, and you can be on your way.”
17-20The spies said:
You made us promise to let you and your family live. We will keep our promise, but you can't tell anyone why we were here. You must tie this red rope on your window when we attack, and your father and mother, your brothers, and everyone else in your family must be here with you. We'll take the blame if anyone who stays in this house gets hurt. But anyone who leaves your house will be killed, and it won't be our fault.
21“I'll do exactly what you said,” Rahab promised. Then she sent them on their way and tied the red rope to the window.
22The spies hid in the hills for three days while the king's soldiers looked for them along the roads. As soon as the soldiers gave up and returned to Jericho, 23the two spies went down into the Jordan valley and crossed the river. They reported to Joshua and told him everything that had happened. 24“We're sure the Lord has given us the whole country,” they said. “The people there shake with fear every time they think of us.”
translation_text:
Rahaba woli Isarele tiina badwonna
1Isarele tiina bam déem maŋe Sitim ne mo ba tei ba vwoa. Ba na wora to mo Josua le nɔɔna balei o toŋe-ba ye o we, “Véi-na á ŋɔ á nii Kanaan tega kam maama, ko fɔge ko dae Jeriko teo kom.” Nɔɔna bam ma seene ba vo ba yi teo kom. Ba ma zo ka-bworo dedoa sɔŋɔ ba peini. Kaane wom yere mo Rahaba.
2Jeriko teo Pɛ wom ma ni soswea we, “Isarele tiina badwonna mo tu debam teo tete dento, se ba ŋɔ-ko ba nii.” 3Pɛ wom ma pa kwora se ba ta de Rahaba we, “Pa se dé jeŋa zo nɔɔna balo na tua ba zo nmo sɔŋɔ kom ne to, bɛŋwaane ba boŋe se ba ŋɔ dé teo kom mo ba nii se ba di dam debam baŋa ne.”
4Rahaba déem nam ya seigi nɔɔna bam mo. O ma jwoori o leiri Pɛ wom kwora kam o we, “Nɔɔna seene ba ba ywo-seeni, amo nam yeiri ba na nwoŋi mɛ to. 5Wɛ ya na jege de zoore ye ko maŋe se ba pe teo kom bworru tem maŋa kalo to, mo ba nwoŋi amo sɔŋɔ ne ba maa viira. Amo nam daa wo lɔre ba na kwei chwoŋa kalo to. Dɛ delo á ná ke lela ye á pɛ ba kwaga á pu, á wó ja-ba chwoŋa ne.” 6O déem nam ya jaane-ba mo o di o sɔŋɔ kom nayuu, ye o kwei-ba o seigi pupwonnu kuri ne. 7Pɛ wom nɔɔna bam ma tɔge chwoŋa kalo na vei jei selo ba na yeini ba tɔge da ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam to. Ba na yɔɔre ba nwoŋi teo kom wone se ba pare-ba to, mo ba pe ko ni dem.
8Tete dem konto ne Rahaba déem daa ma jwoori o di nɔɔna bam tei, ye ba ta ba dɔa. 9O ma ta de-ba o we, “Amo yei we Baŋa Wɛ kwei tega kanto mo o pa abam. Debam maama yera sae mo abam ŋwaane, ye nɔɔna maama ywo-seeni tiini ba fona de abam. 10Debam maŋe dé ni we á déem na maa nwoŋi Ejipti ne to, Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se Nane-soŋo kom pwɛ mo ye abam nɔne te-kora baŋa ne á kɛ. Dé ta yei abam na ke tei ye á yɔɔre á go Sihon de Oga to. Banto mo ye Amori tiina pwa balei bam na zoore Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to. 11Nii-na mo! Debam na nigi wonnu tento maama to, mo dé baare maama jei, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa ba jege dam se o jeeri abam de jara. Chega to, abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ye Wɛ-kamunu mo, ye o tei wɛyuu dedaane tega baŋa maama. 12Konto ŋwaane, kwei-na Baŋa Wɛ yere dem á ma á pwooli de amo we, abam wó ke amo diga tiina bam lanyerane, nenɛɛne amo de na ke abam lanyerane tei to. Ta bere-ne-na memaŋe se a ma a lɔre we, 13abam bá sɛ se á nɔɔna bam chɔge amo, de a kwo, de a nu, de a nabwa, de a chorro maama, de ba de kwaga kam, se ba yé ga ba ŋwea.”
14Nɔɔna bam de ma leiri‑o ba we, “Nmo ná lwoori n wo pɛ debam keim dento nwoŋi pwooni, debam de pwooli we, Baŋa Wɛ ná kwei jei sento o pa debam, dé wó ke‑m lanyerane. Wɛ wó le dé ŋwea nenɛɛne dé ná ve se dé ke dé na tage tei de nmo to.”
15Rahaba sɔŋɔ kom déem ya lɔge teo kom kabira yera ne mo. O ma lei ŋona pa se ka tɔge takworo ni ne se nɔɔna bam dɔɔle-ka ba tu tega. 16O ya maŋe o ta de-ba o we, “Mage-na á yum zwonnu laŋa kam seeni, se balo na pare abam to yé na abam. Maŋe-na da á seigi da yatɔ, se ba ná jwoori ywo-seeni, se á laam viiri.”
17Nɔɔna bam ma ta ba we, “Dé wó nii se kampwola kalo n na pɛ debam pwooli to seene ka toŋe. 18Dé nam ná tu se dé jeeri teo kom de jara, se nmo yage ŋon-naseŋa kanto se ka taa leigi n takworo kom ni ne. Nmo ma‑n wó ja n kwo, de n nu, de n nabwa, de n chorro tem maama n ba ywo-seeni se ba taa wo nmo sɔŋɔ kom wone. 19Nmo yera nɔɔna bam wolo ná nwoŋi nmo sɔŋɔ kom wone o kare teo kom ne o beera ye o te, ko bá taa ye debam yiga. Ko daare dé pwooli we wolo maama ná wo nmo sɔŋɔ wone, ye o ná tega, se lɛɛro taa tɔge debam. 20Nam ta lɔre we, n ná pɛ se dé boboŋe dento nwoŋi pwooni, kampwola kanto dé na pwooli de nmo to daa bá ja debam.”
21Kaane wom ma sɛ ye o leiri-ba o we, “Dé nam jeini abam ni dem kwaga ne.” O ma bane-ba o yage chwoŋa ne, ye o daare o lei ŋon-naseŋa kam takworo kom ni ne o yage da.
22Baara bam ma duri ba vo ba seigi zwonnu laŋa kam seeni. Pɛ wom nɔɔna bam ma pare-ba ba pwoli. Ba maa na nii chwei sem maama ye ba ga ba ŋwa to, mo ba jwoori Jeriko teo kom wone. 23Nɔɔna balei bam ma zege zwonnu tem seeni ba tu tega. Ba laam ma bɛ Jɔdan buga kam, ye ba jwoori ba vo Josua tei. Ba ma ta kolo maama na ke to ba bere‑o. 24Ba ma ta‑o ba we, “Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o kwei tega kam mo o pa debam. Jei sem konto nɔɔna bam maama tiini ba fom mo debam ŋwaane, ye ba yera sae vare-vare.”

english_text:
Israel Crosses the Jordan River
1Early the next morning, Joshua and the Israelites packed up and left Acacia. They went to the Jordan River and camped there that night. 2Two days later their leaders went through the camp, 3-4shouting, “When you see some of the priests carrying the sacred chest, you'll know it is time to cross to the other side. You've never been there before, and you won't know the way, unless you follow the chest. But don't get too close! Stay about a kilometer back.”
5Joshua told the people, “Make yourselves acceptable to worship the Lord, because he is going to do some amazing things for us.”
6Then Joshua turned to the priests and said, “Take the chest and cross the Jordan River ahead of us.” So the priests picked up the chest by its carrying poles and went on ahead.
7The Lord told Joshua, “Beginning today I will show the people that you are their leader, and they will know that I am helping you as I helped Moses. 8Now, tell the priests who are carrying the chest to go a little way into the river and stand there.”
9Joshua spoke to the people:
Come here and listen to what the Lord our God said he will do! 10The Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites control the land on the other side of the river. But the living God will be with you and will force them out of the land when you attack. And now, God is going to prove that he's powerful enough to force them out. 11-13Just watch the sacred chest that belongs to the Lord, the ruler of the whole earth. As soon as the priests carrying the chest step into the Jordan, the water will stop flowing and pile up as if someone had built a dam across the river.
The Lord has also said that each of the twelve tribes should choose one man to represent it.
14The Israelites packed up and left camp. The priests carrying the chest walked in front, 15until they came to the Jordan River. The water in the river had risen over its banks, as it often does in springtime. But as soon as the feet of the priests touched the water, 16-17the river stopped flowing, and the water started piling up at the town of Adam near Zarethan. No water flowed toward the Dead Sea, and the priests stood in the middle of the dry riverbed near Jericho while everyone else crossed over.
translation_text:
Ba na bɛ Jɔdan buga kam tei to
1Ba déem ma maŋe dáane ba peini ye tega poore. Josua dedaane Isarele tiina bam maama ma gwoni tega ba zaŋe Sitim ne ba vo ba yi Jɔdan buga kam. Ba ma tei ba vwoa ye ba laam cheigi maŋa kalo ba na wó bɛ buga kam to. 2Ba déem na ke da yatɔ jei sem konto ne to, mo Isarele dedɛɛra bam tole nɔɔna bam peiga jei ne, 3ye ba tɛ ba we, “Abam ná yɔɔre á na we, Levi dwi dem na ye kaanem tiina to zeŋe Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam, se á nwoŋi á peiga jei sem á pɛ ba kwaga á pu. 4Abam ta na wo tɔge chwoŋa kanto to, Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam mo wó bere abam chwoŋa. Nam ta‑á yei á tete se á yé tiini á yi ka yera. Ta‑á ye dáa dáa se ko maŋe de naba-laara moro laŋa.”
5Josua laam ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Kwɛ-na á tete, se ko maŋe de Wɛ na lage tei to, kokuri Baŋa Wɛ jwa lage o ke wo-kenkagela mo á tetare ne.”
6Josua ta ma ta de kaanem tiina bam o we, “Kwei-na ni-gwonim dakaa kam á zeŋe, se á tɔge dé maama yiga se dé bɛ Jɔdan buga kam.” Ba de ma kwei-ka ba to nɔɔna bam yiga ne.
7Dento dɛ dem ne mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Josua o we, “Ko zege zem se ko taa via, a lage a pa se nmo ji nɔn-yuu mo Isarele tiina maama wone. Leile konto mo ba lage ba lɔre we, amo wo nmo de tei ne, nenɛɛne a déem na wora de Moses tei to. 8Nam ta de kaanem tiina balo na zeŋe amo ni-gwonim dakaa kam to se ba ná yi buga kam ni dem se ba zo na bam wone. Ba laam maa wó vo fee ba maŋe da ba zege.”
9Josua de ma ta dedaane nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Ba-na ywo-seeni se á cheigi abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na jege kolo se o ta de abam to. 10Abam zem wó lɔre we, Wɛ wolo na jege ŋwea to wora de abam. Wonto mo lage o zeili Kanaan tiina bam, de Hiti tiina bam, de Hivi tiina bam, de Pɛrizi tiina bam, de Giragasi tiina bam, de Amori tiina bam, dedaane Jebusi tiina bam maama se ba nwoŋi ba daare tega kam ba pa abam. 11Nii-na mo! Baŋa Wɛ mo tei logo baŋa maama, ye wonto ni-gwonim dakaa kam lage ka da abam yiga ka bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. 12Abam nam jege se á nii Isarele dwia fuga-yalei yam wone mo á le nɔɔno dedoa dedoa dwi maama wone. 13Dakaa kanto ye Baŋa Wɛ wolo na tei logo baŋa maama to nyem mo. Kaanem tiina balo na zeŋe-ka to maa ná nɔne ba nɛ Jɔdan buga kam wone, na balo na duri ba tui to wó kɔ, ye ba tigisi daane nenɛɛne kabira dwoŋi.”
14Isarele tiina bam ma zaŋe ba gɔ ba vwoa yam, ye ba laam vei ba maa kɛa se ba bɛ buga kam. Kaanem tiina bam de ma zeŋe ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba tɔge ba yiga. 15Bene maama wone, ko ná yeini ko yi wodiiru zagem maŋa, Jɔdan buga kam yeini ka su mo ka wɛɛle ka nia yam maama ne. De konto maama de, kaanem tiina balo na zeŋe ni-gwonim dakaa kam to na yɔɔre ba nɔne ba nɛ buga kam wone to, 16mo na-dura bam na tole ba maa tu to koga. Ko na yɔɔre ko maŋe de teo kolo yere na ye Adama to, mo na bam bobo se ba tigisi daane nenɛɛne kabira dwoŋi to. Teo kom konto déem ye yiga yiga mo ye ko bwola dedaane Zarefan. Na déem daa ba duri se ba zo Araba naneo kom wone. (Yɛ naneo kom mo konto.) Buga na bam ma we pa se nɔɔna bam na pwola ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. Jei sem déem nam bwola dedaane Jeriko mo. 17Kaanem tiina bam na zeŋe dakaa kam to de yɔɔre ba zege buga kam tetare ne mo. Ba maa zege te-kora baŋa ne taa, se ko taa nii maŋa kalo Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama na bɛ ba ti to.

english_text:
The People Set Up a Monument
1After Israel had crossed the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua:
2-3Tell one man from each of the twelve tribes to pick up a large rock from where the priests are standing. Then tell the men to set up those rocks as a monument at the place where you camp tonight.
4Joshua chose twelve men; then he called them together 5and said:
Go to the middle of the riverbed where the sacred chest is, and pick up a large rock. Carry it on your shoulder to our camp. There are twelve of you, so there will be one rock for each tribe. 6-7Someday your children will ask, “Why are these rocks here?” Then you can tell them how the water stopped flowing when the chest was being carried across the river. These rocks will always remind our people of what happened here today.
8The men followed the instructions that the Lord had given Joshua. They picked up twelve rocks, one for each tribe, and carried them to the camp, where they put them down.
9Joshua set up a monument next to the place where the priests were standing. This monument was also made of twelve large rocks, and it is still there in the middle of the river.
The People of Israel Set Up Camp at Gilgal
