11-12Geshur and Maacah were part of this region, and so was the whole territory that King Og had ruled, that is, Gilead, Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far east as Salecah. Og had lived in Ashtaroth part of each year, and he had lived in Edrei the rest of the year. Og had been one of the last of the Rephaim, but Moses had defeated Sihon and Og and their people and had forced them to leave their land. 13However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites.
Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
14 Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.”
The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
15Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe. 16Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba. 17-21The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth.
Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. 22The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
23This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border.
The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
24Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe. 25It included the town of Jazer, and in the Gilead region their territory took in the land and towns as far east as the town of Aroer just west of Rabbah. This was about half of the land that had once belonged to the Ammonites. 26The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor. 27Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon. 28These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe.
The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
29Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe. 30-31Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had 60 towns in all.
The Manasseh tribe is sometimes called the Machir tribe, after Manasseh's son Machir.
32That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own. 33 But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_text:
Tega kalo ta na daare se ba di to
1Josua déem na tiini o kwe maŋa kalo to, mo Baŋa Wɛ tage ded‑o o we:
“Nmo laam kwe dedɛ, ye tega kam jei dedɛ ta wora se á vo á jwoŋi á ta‑á tei. 2Jei sento nam mo daare se nɔɔna vo ba jwoŋi: Filisi tiina laŋa kam, ko woli de Gesura tiina laŋa kam maama. 3Ka zege Sihora bu-nɔgɔ kom ne mo, Ejipti siseini dem na wo mɛ to, se ko yi Ekoron siseini dem na wo baŋa seeni to. Jei sem konto maama ye Kanaan tiina laŋa mo. Filisi dedɛɛra banu teene dem maa ye: Gaza, de Asedodi, de Asekelon, de Gafa, dedaane Ekoron. Ko woli de Awa tiina laŋa kalo na wo kuri seeni to, 4dedaane Kanaan tiina tega kalo na zege Sidon tiina teo Ara ne se ka ta vo ka yi Afeka laŋa kam, Amori tiina siseini dem na wo mɛ to. 5Abam ta maa wó jwoŋi Gebale tiina laŋa kam á woli da, dedaane Lebanon tega kam maama na wo wɛ-puli seeni ye ka zege Baal-Gad na wo Heremon Peo kom tega-kuri seeni to, ka vo ka yi Lebo-Hamafa.
6Sidon tiina laŋa kam maama tɔge ka woli da mo. Banto zoore zwonnu jei sem na wo Lebanon peero tem dedaane Miserefofa-Mayim tetare ne to mo. Amo tete nam mo lage a zeili nɔɔna bam konto maama, se abam wane á zo da. Nmo nam yɔɔre n pɔɔre tega kam n pa Isarele tiina bam nenɛɛne a na pɛ nmo ni se n ke tei to. 7Kwei tega kam konto maama n pɔɔre n pa Isarele dwia nogo kolo na daare to, dedaane Manasɛ dwi dem chichworo, se ba taa tei.”
Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni tega kam popɔre sem
8Ko ná ye Manasɛ dwi dem chichworo kodwoŋi kom, ko woli dedaane Ruben dwi dem, de Gad dwi dem, Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses déem maŋe o pa banto ba tega kam popɔra Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni mo. 9Ba laŋa kam yale konto mo ka yi Arowa na wo Aranon bwolo kom ni ne to, de teo kolo na wo bwolo kom tetare ne to, ko woli de te-kampare jei selo maama na zege Medeba ne se ko yi Dibon to. 10Ka ta yi teene delo maama na ye Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon nyem to. Wonto déem nam di paare Hesebon wone mo. Ka ta ma vo ka yi Amon teo siseini dem. 11Ba tega kam déem tɔge Gilead jei sem de Gesura tiina de Maaka tiina laŋa kam maama, dedaane Heremon Peo kom jei sem maama, ko woli de Basan maama, se ka vo ka yi Saleka mo. 12Basan teo Pɛ Oga laŋa kam maama de ye ba nyem mo. Wonto déem di o paare Asetarof dedaane Ederi ne mo. Wonto déem mo kweeli Refayi tiina bam jeŋa ne. Moses déem maa di-ba, ye o zeili-ba o daare tega kam konto. 13Isarele tiina bam déem maa wo zeili Gesura tiina bam de Maaka tiina bam. Nɔɔna bam konto de déem maa tɔge ba zoore de Isarele tiina bam se ko yi zem maama.
14Moses déem na pɔɔre tega kam o pa Isarele tiina bam to, Levi dwi dem yerane mo wo tɔge ba jwoŋi tega kam popɔra. Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o pa Moses ni we, banto popɔra wó nwoŋi pɛɛra yalo Isarele tiina bam na jaane ba tui ba zwɛ Wɛ bimbini dem baŋa ne ba pa ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom to mo.
Ruben dwi dem tega kam
15Moses déem kwei tega kanto mo o pa Ruben dwi dem. O ma pa sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem se ba taa tei.
16Banto laŋa kam yale konto mo ka yi Arowa na wo Aranon bwolo kom ni ne to, de teo kolo na na wo bwolo kom tetare ne to, ko woli de te-kampare jei selo maama na bwola de Medeba to. 17Hesebon de ye ba nyem mo, dedaane teene delo maama na wo te-kampare dem konto maama ne to: Dibon, de Bamofe-Baal, de Bɛte-Baal-Meon, 18de Jahaza, de Kedemofa, de Mefaafa, 19de Kiriafayim, de Sibima, dedaane Zeref-Sahare. Teo konto maa wo zwoŋo kolo na wo bwolo kom ni ne to baŋa ne mo. 20Ko ta woli de Bɛte-Peora, de tega kalo na wo Pisiga peo kom teiŋa ne to, de Bɛte-Jesimofa, 21dedaane teene delo maama na wo te-kampare jei sem ne to. Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon déem na di paare Hesebon wone ye o tei laŋa kalo maama to de maa ye Ruben dwi dem nyem. Moses déem ma di pɛ wom konto de Midian pwa bam maama mo: Evi, de Rekem, de Zura, de Hura, dedaane Reba. Banto déem mo tei tega kam ba pa Pɛ Sihon. 22Isarele tiina bam déem ma go Beora bu Balaam wolo na ye voro to ba woli de nɔɔna babam bam. 23Ruben dwi dem tega kam déem vei ka kweeli Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ baŋa ne mo. Ba déem kwei teene dem konto de de nawuura yam maama ba tei, diga maama de ka nyem.
Gad dwi dem tega kam
24Moses déem ta ma kwei tega kadwoŋi o pa Gad dwi dem. O ma pa sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem se ba taa tei.
25Banto laŋa kam ma kwei Jazera de teene delo maama na wo Gilead laŋa kam ne, ko ta woli de Amon tiina tega kam chichworo, se ko taa vei Arowa na wo Raba wɛ-puli seeni to. 26Ba laŋa kam zege Hesebon ne, se ka vo ka yi Ramaf-Mizipa dedaane Betonim. Ka ta zege Mahanayim ne, se ka yi Debiri laŋa kam. 27Jɔdan bwolo kom seeni to, ba tega kam ma kwei Bɛte-Haram, de Bɛte-Nimira, de Sukofa, dedaane Zafon. Hesebon teo Pɛ Sihon laŋa kalo ya ta na daare to de maa ye ba nyem. Gad dwi dem tega kam déem vei ka kweeli Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ baŋa ne mo, ka ta tɔge buga kam wɛ-puli seeni ka yi Galili naneo kom ni. 28Ba déem kwei teene dem konto de de nawuura yam maama ba tei, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.
Manasɛ dwi dem chichworo tega kam
29Moses déem ta ma kwei tega kadwoŋi o pa Manasɛ sɔ-yuu kom chichworo. O ma pa diga maama de ka nyem se ba taa tei. 30Banto laŋa kam ma kwei Mahanayim, se ko taa vei Basan laŋa kam maama ne, Pɛ Oga déem na di o paare dem mɛ to. Teene fuseredo delo Jayira ya na di ye de wo Basan ne to de ta woli da mo. 31Gilead laŋa kam chichworo de maa woli da, dedaane Pɛ Oga déem na di o paare dem teene delo ne to, Asetarof dedaane Ederi mo konto. Jei sem konto maama déem laam jigi Manasɛ bu Makira sɔ-yuu kom chichworo nyem mo.
32Mo ko na ke tei ye Moses déem wo Moaba bwollu tem laŋa kam ne o pɔɔre tega kalo na wo Jeriko teo de Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to. 33Se ko na daare Levi dwi tiina bam to, Moses déem wo pɔɔre tega kadwoŋi o pa banto ba nyem se ba taa tei. Kokuri to, Isarele Baŋa Wɛ wom mo maŋe o pwooli o pa-ba we, wonto wó taa ye ba jejaano paro.

english_text:
The Land West of the Jordan River
1-5 Nine and a half tribes still did not have any land, although two and a half tribes had already received land east of the Jordan River. Moses had divided that land among them, and he had also said that the Levi tribe would not receive a large region like the other tribes. Instead, the people of Levi would receive towns and the nearby pastures for their sheep, goats, and cattle. And since the descendants of Joseph had become the two tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, there were still nine and a half tribes that needed land. The Lord had told Moses that he would show those tribes how to divide up the land of Canaan.
When the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the leaders of the families and tribes of Israel met to divide up the land of Canaan, the Lord showed them how to do it.
Joshua Gives Hebron to Caleb
6 One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua:
You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me. 7 I was 40 years old at the time Moses sent me from Kadesh-Barnea into Canaan as a spy. When I came back and told him about the land, everything I said was true. 8The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God. 9 The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
10Joshua, it was 45 years ago that the Lord told Moses to make that promise, and now I am 85. Even though Israel has moved from place to place in the desert, the Lord has kept me alive all this time as he said he would. 11I'm just as strong today as I was then, and I can still fight as well in battle.
12So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
13Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants. 14And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
15Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim.
There was peace in the land.
translation_text:
Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-zoore seeni tega kam popɔre sem
1Kanaan tega kam na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-zoore seeni to déem ta daare se ba pɔɔre-ka ba pa Isarele tiina bam. Wɛ kaanem tu Eleaza, ko woli de Nun bu Josua, dedaane Isarele dwi tiina nakwa bam déem laam ma pɔɔre tega kam konto ba pa Isarele tiina bam maama. 2Ba déem tage jɔrɔ mo tega kam ŋwaane ba pɔɔre-ka ba pa Isarele dwia nogo de chichworo kolo na daare to, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na maŋe o pa Moses ni se o ke tei to. 3-4Ko ná ye dwia yalei de chichworo kodwoŋi kom, Moses ya maŋe o pa banto na ba jeiŋa jei. Banto tega kam wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni mo. Moses nam wo pɛ Levi dwi tiina tega kam dwoŋi. O déem za kuri teene de vara pwoli mo o pa-ba, se ba de wane ba taa zoore de wone ye ba ke kɔnɔ. Ko daare Josɛf dwi dem déem pɔɔre kuni belei mo: o bia balei Manasɛ dedaane Efrayim dwia yam mo konto. 5Isarele tiina bam déem na pɔɔre tega kam tei to ke ko maŋe dedaane Baŋa Wɛ ya na bere Moses se ba ke tei to mo.
Kaleb jwoŋi Heboron
6Isarele tiina bam déem ta maa wo Giligal ne. Ba na wora to mo Judah dwi tiina toŋe nɔɔna Josua tei ne. Ba dedoa déem ye Jefunɛ bu Kaleb, o na nwoŋi Kenizi sɔ-yuu kom ne to. Kaleb ma ta de Josua o we, “Yé swei Baŋa Wɛ déem na tage debam balei taane tetei maama o bere o tontoŋeno Moses, ye dé déem ta wo Kadese-Baranea ne to. 7Maŋa kam konto ne amo déem jege bena finna mo. Moses déem zege Kadese-Baranea ne o toŋe ne, se a vo a ŋɔ a nii tega kanto na ye tei to. Amo déem ma ja ta-ŋom a ba a pa‑o, de a wo maama. 8Se ko ná ye amo chorro telo déem na tɔge de amo ba vo se dé ŋɔ dé nii tega kam to, ba déem ke foone mo nɔɔna bam maama kuri ne. Amo déem nam yɔɔre a tɔge a Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo de a wo maama. 9Dento dɛ dem ne mo Moses déem tage o pwooli de amo o we, ‘Nmo na nɔne n naga Kanaan tega kalo ne konto to wó taa ye nmo nyem. Nmo de n bia mo wó taa tei-ka se ko taa vei wuu, n na tɔge Baŋa Wɛ de n wo maama to ŋwaane.’
10Tɔ. Moses na tage Baŋa Wɛ taane dem konto o bere-ne, se ko yi zem to, ko ye bena finna-yanu mo. Maŋa kam konto ne debam Isarele tiina ta wo kagoa yuu ne mo dé via. Nii amo! Amo ta ŋwe nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to, pa se a zem jege bena funɔnɔ yanu mo. 11De zem maama amo nam ta dana, ye a wara mo, nenɛɛne a déem na ye tei dɛ dem Moses na toŋe-ne to. Dam dem ta wora se a ma a ke jara de totoŋa yalo maama a na lage to. 12Konto to, kwei zwonnu laŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ déem na pwooli se ka taa ye amo nyem to n pa-ne. Nmo wó guli we Anaki tiina bam mo wo daane. Ba teene dem ma lɔ de di vili vili. De ko de, Baŋa Wɛ na wo amo tei ne to ŋwaane, a wó wane-ba a zeili, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na tage se a ke tei to.”
13Jefunɛ bu Kaleb na tage konto maama o ti to, Josua ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage o yuu ne. O ma daare o kwei Heboron o pa‑o, se ko taa ye o tete jejegero. 14Ko na zege dɛ dem konto ne se ko yi zem to, Heboron laam lɛɛre ko ji Jefunɛ bu Kaleb dedaane o bia nyem mo. Kokuri, wonto déem tɔge Isarele Baŋa Wɛ wom mo dedaane o wo maama. 15Kanto maŋa ya ta na wo yi to, ba déem jege teo kom mo ba bwoi we Kiriaf-Araba, Araba déem na ye Anaki tiina bam nɔn-sawɔrɔ to ŋwaane.
Tega kam laam ma sii ye jara daa tera.

english_text:
Judah's Land
1The clans of the Judah tribe were given land that went south along the border of Edom, and at its farthest point south it even reached the Zin Desert. 2Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea. 3As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka, 4and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
5Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea.
The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea. 6From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe. 7From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel, 8and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites.
Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley. 9At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
10From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah. 11It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea, 12which was Judah's western border.
The clans of Judah lived within these borders.
Caleb's Land
(Judges 1.12-15)
13 Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
14Caleb attacked Hebron and forced the three Anakim clans of Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai to leave. 15Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher. 16He told his men, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
17Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, and Caleb let him marry Achsah. 18Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
19She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.”
Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
Towns in Judah's Land
20The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
21-32The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following 29 towns with their surrounding villages:
Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur, Kinah, Dimonah, Aradah, Kedesh, Hazor of Ithnan, Ziph, Telem, Bealoth, Hazor-Hadattah, Kerioth-Hezron, which is also called Hazor, Amam, Shema, Moladah, Hazar-Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth-Pelet, Hazar-Shual, Beersheba and its surrounding villages, Baalah, Iim, Ezem, Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah, Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah, Lebaoth, Shilhim, and Enrimmon.
33-36The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following 14 towns with their surrounding villages:
Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
37-41The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following 16 towns with their surrounding villages:
Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
42-44The fourth region was located in the central part of the lower foothills, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages:
Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah.
45-47The fifth region was located along the Mediterranean seacoast, and it had the following towns with their surrounding settlements and villages:
Ekron and the towns between there and the coast, Ashdod and the larger towns nearby, Gaza, the towns from Gaza to the Egyptian Gorge, and the towns along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
48-51The sixth region was in the southwestern part of the hill country, and it had the following eleven towns with their surrounding villages:
Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, Dannah, Kiriath-Sannah, which is now called Debir, Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, and Giloh.
52-54The seventh region was located in the south-central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages:
Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth-Tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath-Arba, which is now called Hebron, and Zior.
55-57The eighth region was located in the southeastern part of the hill country, and it had the following ten towns with their surrounding villages:
Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah.
58-59The ninth region was located in the central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following six towns with their surrounding villages:
Halhul, Beth-Zur, Gedor, Maarath, Beth-Anoth, and Eltekon.
The tenth region was located in the north-central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following eleven towns with their surrounding villages:
Tekoa, Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem, Peor, Etam, Culon, Tatam, Shoresh, Kerem, Gallim, Bether, and Manahath.
60The eleventh region was located in the northern part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following two towns with their surrounding villages:
Rabbah, and Kiriath-Baal, which is also called Kiriath-Jearim.
61-62The twelfth region was located in the desert along the Dead Sea, and it had the following six towns with their surrounding villages:
Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, Salt Town, and En-Gedi.
The Jebusites
63 The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_text:
Judah dwi dem tega kam
1Ba déem na kuri tega kalo ba pa Judah dwi dem to tole ka tu tega-kuri seeni mo ka tɔge Edom siseini dem ka vo ka yi Zin kagoa kam mo.
2Ba tega kam tega-kuri seeni bobo Yɛ naneo kom kuri nabili seeni mo. 3Ka ma vo ka lɛɛne Nɔŋɔ zwonnu chwoŋa kam tega-kuri seeni ka kɛ ka yi Zin kagoa kam ne. Ka ta maa vei Kadese-Baranea kuri seeni konto, ka daare ka yi Hezeron ne. Ka laam ma di Adara ne ka pipiri ka yɔɔre Karaka seeni. 4Ka ma zege dáane ka tɔge Azemon ne, ka tole taa ka yi Ejipti bu-nɔgɔ kom, ye ka laam vo ka kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ni ne mo. Judah dwi dem tega kam tega-kuri seeni siseini mo konto.
5Ko daare ba tega kam wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem wó taa tole Yɛ naneo kom ni dem mo konto, se ka vo ka yi Jɔdan buga kam ni dem ne. Baŋa seeni siseini dem de maa wó bobo jei sem konto ne, Jɔdan buga kam na zo Yɛ naneo kom mɛ to, 6ye ka laam vo ka yi Bɛte-Hogala. Ka ta ma tɔge Bɛte-Araba baŋa seeni ka kɛ ka yi Bohan Kandwɛ dem. Bohan déem ye Ruben bu mo. 7Ka na zege dáane to, ka laam ma kwei Akore bwolo kom, ka yi Debiri ne, ka daare ka pipiri baŋa seeni ka di Giligal ne. Giligal déem yɔɔre Adumim sisworo kom na wo bwolo kom tega-kuri seeni to. Ko na zege dáane to, siseini dem laam ma kɛ de yi En-Semesa buli-yia yam ne mo, se ka yi En-Rogele. 8Siseini dem ta tole de tɔge Ben-Hinom bwolo kom ne mo, se ko taa vei Jebusi tiina teo kom zwoŋo kom tega-kuri seeni. Jerusalem mo konto. De daa ta ma kɛ de di baŋa seeni se ko maŋe de Hinom bwolo kom wɛ-zoore dem seeni, Refayim bwolo kom baŋa seeni na kweeli mɛ to mo. 9Ka zege zwoŋo kom baŋa ne ka vo ka yi Nefatoa buli-yia yam ne mo, se ka yi teene delo na wo Eforon Peo kom teiŋa ne to. Ka daa ma gugwoli ka yɔɔre Baala seeni. (Kiriaf-Jeerim mo konto.) 10Ba tega kam na kwei Baala wɛ-zoore seeni to, ka vo ka tɔge Seyira Peo kom mo, ka vo ka yi Jeerim peo sisworo kom. (Chesalon mo konto.) Ka laam ma tu ka vo Bɛte-Semesa teo kom, ka daare ka tɔge Timina seeni ka kɛ. 11Siseini dem ta kɛ de vo zwoŋo kolo na wo Ekoron baŋa seeni to mo, de pipiri de yɔɔre Sikeron de daare de kɛ de gaale Baala peo kom. De ma yi Jaminia teo kom ne, ye de vo de kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ne.
12Judah dwi dem tega kam wɛ-zoore seeni siseini dem mo déem ye Mediterania naneo kom ni dem. Judah sɔ-yuni tem maama déem zoore siseina yanto wone mo.
13 Baŋa Wɛ déem ya pɛ Josua ni mo se o fɔ Judah laŋa kam wone o pa Jefunɛ bu Kaleb. Josua de ma seene o ke konto. Ba déem kwei Heboron mo ba pa‑o. Teo kom konto ya ye Araba nyem mo. Wonto maa ye Anaki tiina nabaaro. 14Kaleb déem ma zeili Anaki dwia yatɔ yam na wo Heboron ne to, o daare jei sem konto. Banto déem mo ye: Sesayi, Ahiman, dedaane Talimayi. 15Konto kwaga ne to, o vei o ke jara mo dedaane Debiri teo kom tiina. (Boboa ne to, teo kom konto yere déem mo ye Kiriaf-Sefera.) 16Kaleb déem ma ta o we, “Amo wó kwei a bukɔ Akisa a pa nɔɔno wolo maama na wó wane o vo o ke jara dedaane Kiriaf-Sefera tiina bam ye o wane-ba to.” 17Kenazi bu Ofineli déem ma vo o ke jara yam, ye o wane teo kom nɔɔna bam. Kenazi de déem ye Kaleb choro mo. O ma kwei o bukɔ Akisa o pa Ofineli, se o di o ma o ji o kaane.
18Kadiri dem maŋa kam ne mo, o tage de o baro wom se ba beeri tega ba jwoŋi o kwo wom tei ne. O déem ma di bonaga o vo o tu o kwo yiga ne, ye o kwo bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo nmo lage se a ke a pa‑m?” 19Akisa ma leiri‑o o we, “A lwoori se n ke-ne zaane mo. Nmo na pɛ-ne tega kalo to ye kagoa yerane mo. Konto to, a lage mɛ na na buri to mo se n kwei n pa-ne.” Kaleb ma beeri buli-yia jei o pa‑o, baŋa seeni de tega-kuri seeni maama.
20Tega kanto mo ba déem pɛ Judah dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.
21Teene dento déem wo tega-kuri seeni mo, de na ba tware de Edom siseini dem to:
Kabezele, de Edera, de Jagura, 22de Kina, de Dimona, de Adada, 23de Kedesa, de Hazora, de Ifanan, 24de Zifi, de Telem, de Bealofa, 25de Hazora-Hadata, de Keriof-Hezeron (Hazora mo konto), 26de Amam, de Sema, de Molada, 27de Hazara-Gada, de Hesemon, de Bɛte-Peleta, 28de Hazara-Suali, de Beeriseba, de Biziofia, 29de Baala, de Iyim, de Ezem, 30de Eletolada, de Kesila, de Horama, 31de Zikalag, de Madamana, de Sansana, 32de Lebaof, de Silihim, de Ayin, dedaane Rimon.
De déem ye teene finlei-nogo mo de de nawuura yam maama.
33Teene dento de maa wo wɛ-zoore bwollu tem seeni mo:
Esatola, de Zora, de Asena, 34de Zanoa, de En-Ganim, de Tapua, de Enam, 35de Jaremuf, de Adulam, de Sokoo, de Azeka, 36de Saarayim, de Aditayim, de Gedera, dedaane Gederotayim.
De ye teene fuga-dena mo, dedaane de nawuura yam.
37Teene dento de ta woli da mo:
Zenan, de Hadasa, de Migadal-Gad, 38de Dilean, de Mizipa, de Joketeeli, 39de Lakisi, de Bozekafa, de Egilon, 40de Kabon, de Laamasa, de Kitilisi, 41de Gederofa, de Bɛte-Dagon, de Naama, de Makeda.
Teene fuga-deredo mo konto, de de nawuura yam.
42Teene dento de ta wora:
Libina, de Efera, de Asan, 43de Ifata, de Asena, de Neziba, 44de Keila, de Akiziba, dedaane Maresa.
Dento ye teene nogo mo, de de nawuura yam.
45Ekoron dedaane ko te-balwa bam de ko nawuura yam maama.
46Ko na zege Ekoron ne se ko tɔge wɛ-zoore seeni:
teene delo maama na bwola de Asedodi to, 47Asedodi, de Gaza, de de te-balwa, de de nawuura yam maama, se ko ta tu Ejipti bu-nɔgɔ kom, ko vo ko tole Mediterania naneo kom ni.
48Ko na maŋe dedaane zwonnu laŋa kam to, teene dento mo wora:
Samira, de Jatira, de Sokoo, 49de Dana, de Kiriaf-Sana (Debiri mo konto), 50de Anaba, de Esetemoo, de Anim, 51de Gosen, de Holon, de Giloo.
Teene fuga-dedoa mo konto, de de nawuura yam maama.
52Arab, de Duma, de Esan, 53de Janim, de Bɛte-Tapua, de Afeka, 54de Humata, de Heboron, de Ziora.
De ye teene nogo mo, de de nawuura yam.
55Maon, de Kamele, de Zifi, de Juta, 56de Jezerele, de Jokadeam, de Zanoa, 57de Kayin, de Gibea, de Timina.
Dento de ye teene fuga mo, de de nawuura yam.
58Halula, de Bɛte-Zura, de Gedora, 59de Marafa, de Bɛte-Anofa, de Eletekon.
Teene deredo mo konto, de de nawuura yam.
60Kiriaf-Baal (Kiriaf-Jeerim mo konto), dedaane Raba.
De ye teene delei mo, dedaane de nawuura yam.
61Ba laŋa kalo na wo kagoa kam seeni to, teene dento de maa wora:
Bɛte-Araba, de Midin, de Sekaka, 62de Nibisan (konto maa ye ‘Yɛ Teo’ mo), ko woli de En-Gedi.
Dento de maa ye teene deredo, de de nawuura yam.
63Jebusi tiina bam déem zoore Jerusalem ne mo. Judah tiina bam nam wo wane-ba ba zeili. Jebusi tiina bam dedaane Judah tiina bam maa zoore daane de zem maama.

english_text:
Ephraim's Land
1-4Ephraim and Manasseh are the two tribes descended from Joseph, and the following is a description of the land they received. The southern border of their land started at the Jordan River east of the spring at Jericho. From there it went west through the desert up to the hill country around Bethel. From Bethel it went to Luz and then to the border of the Archites in Ataroth. It continued west down to the land that belonged to the Japhlet clan, then went on to Lower Beth-Horon, Gezer, and the Mediterranean Sea.
5The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon 6-8and the Mediterranean Sea. Their northern border started on the east at Janoah, curved a little to the north, then came back south to Michmethath and Tappuah, where it followed the Kanah Gorge west to the Mediterranean Sea.
The eastern border started on the north near Janoah and went between Janoah on the southwest and Taanath-Shiloh on the northeast. Then it went south to Ataroth, Naarah, and on as far as the edge of the land that belonged to Jericho. At that point it turned east and went to the Jordan River. The clans of Ephraim received this region as their tribal land. 9Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
10 Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_text:
Efrayim dwi de Manasɛ dwi taane
1Ba déem na kuri tega kalo ba pa Josɛf dwi dem to bobo Jɔdan buga kam ne, ka na bwola de Jeriko mɛ to mo. Ka zege Jeriko buli-yia yam wɛ-puli seeni mo, ka tɔge kagoa kam ne ka kɛ ka yi Bɛtel teo kom na wo zwonnu laŋa kam ne to. 2Ka na zege Bɛtel ne to, ka tɔge Luzi ye ka tole ka zo Atarofa, Ariki tiina bam na zoore mɛ to mo. 3Ka laam ma tu wɛ-zoore seeni ka yi Jafeleti tiina jei sem, se ko taa vei Bɛte-Horon kuri seeni. Ka daa ta ma kɛ ka vo Gezere, se ka vo ka kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ni ne.
4Ko dɛ konto mo ye Manasɛ de Efrayim jwoŋi ba tega kam pɔɔrem dem. Josɛf bia balei bam mo konto.
Efrayim dwi dem tega kam
5Laŋa kanto mo ba déem pɔɔre ba pa Efrayim dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem:
Ba tega kam na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to zege Atarof-Adara ne mo. Ka laam ma tole konto, ka di Bɛte-Horon baŋa seeni, 6ye ko kɛ ko yi Mediterania naneo kom. Se ko ná ye baŋa seeni siseini dem, tega kam yi Mikimefa mo. Ka laam ma gugwoli wɛ-puli seeni ka kɛ ka yage Tanafa-Siloo, ka gaale dáane ka yi Janoa na wo wɛ-puli seeni to. 7Tega kam daa zege Janoa ne konto ka vo Atarofa de Naara seeni mo. Ka ma daare ka yi Jeriko, ye ka laam vo ka kweeli Jɔdan buga kam ne. 8Ko na zege Tapua ne to, tega kam siseini yale mo de vo wɛ-zoore seeni. De ma tɔge Kana bu-nɔgɔ kom de vo de kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ni ne. Mo tega kalo Efrayim dwi dem déem na jwoŋi se ba taa tei to mo konto, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. 9Efrayim tiina bam déem ta jwoŋi teene dedwonna na wo Manasɛ dwi dem laŋa kam wone mo.
10Kanaan tiina déem ya zoore Gezere teo wone ye Efrayim tiina bam wo zeili-ba. Banto de Efrayim tiina bam maa zoore daane de zem maama. Efrayim tiina bam déem za fe-ba mo, se ba taa toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛra.

english_text:
Manasseh's Land West of the Jordan River
1-6 Manasseh was Joseph's oldest son, and Machir was Manasseh's oldest son. Machir had a son named Gilead, and some of his descendants had already received the regions of Gilead and Bashan because they were good warriors. The other clans of the Manasseh tribe descended from Gilead's sons Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. The following is a description of the land they received.
Hepher's son Zelophehad did not have any sons, but he did have five daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. One day the clans that were descendants of Zelophehad's five daughters went to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the leaders of Israel. The people of these clans said, “The Lord told Moses to give us land just as he gave land to our relatives.”
Joshua followed the Lord's instructions and gave land to these five clans, as he had given land to the five clans that had descended from Hepher's brothers. So Manasseh's land west of the Jordan River was divided into ten parts.
7The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring. 8The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
9-10Then the border went west to the Kanah Gorge and ran along the northern edge of the gorge to the Mediterranean Sea. The land south of the gorge belonged to Ephraim. And even though there were a few towns that belonged to Ephraim north of the gorge, the land north of the gorge belonged to Manasseh.
The western border of Manasseh was the Mediterranean Sea, and the tribe shared a border with the Asher tribe on the northwest and with the Issachar tribe on the northeast.
11Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands:
Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
12 But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them. 13When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave.
Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
14One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
15Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
16“Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
17“Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful, 18so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_text:
Manasɛ dwi dem tega kam
1Ba déem ma ke tega kam jei sedwoŋi ba pa Manasɛ dwi dem. Manasɛ déem ye Josɛf bu-kwea mo, o de bu-kwea ya maa ye Makira. Wonto déem ye bembea mo. O maa ye Gilead tiina kwo. O ya maŋe o jwoŋi Gilead de Basan laŋa kam na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to mo. 2Ko nam ná ye dwia yadwonna na nwoŋi Manasɛ yera ne to, ba déem pɔɔre tega Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-zoore seeni mo ba pa-ba, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. Banto maa ye: Abizeri, de Heleke, de Asireli, de Sɛkɛm, de Hefera, dedaane Semida. Baara balo na ye Josɛf bu Manasɛ bia to mo konto.
3Hefera bu Zelofehada déem loge bukwa banu mo ye o ba jege bakeira. O nabaara maa ye Gilead de Makira. Ba ye Manasɛ dwi dem tiina mo. Zelofehada bukwa bam yera mo ye: Maala, de Noah, de Hogela, de Milika, dedaane Tiraza.
4Kaana bam konto ma zaŋe ba vo Isarele nakwa bam tei, de Eleaza na ye Wɛ kaanem tu to de Josua de tei. Ba ma ta de-ba ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ Moses ni se o ná lage o ke tega o pa dé dwi dem baara bam, se o pɔɔre ka wone o pa debam de.” Josua ma ke o tɔge Baŋa Wɛ ni dem. O ma pa-ba tega se ba taa tei, nenɛɛne o déem na ke tei de ba baara bam to. 5-6Manasɛ dwi dem déem nɛ jei kuni fuga mo tega kam pɔɔrem baŋa ne, se ko woli de ba ya na maŋe ba jege tega kalo Jɔdan bubɛ dedwoŋi dem seeni to. Gilead de Basan laŋa kam mo konto. Ko nam ye Manasɛ dwi delo na ye kaana to de déem na jwoŋi tega nenɛɛne ba baara bam na jwoŋi tei to ŋwaane mo ko ye konto.
7Manasɛ dwi dem laŋa kam ma zege Asere dwi dem siseini ne, se ko taa vei Mikimefa na wo Sɛkɛm wɛ-puli seeni to mo. Siseini dem ta zege Mikimefa ne mo de tu kuri seeni, de yi Tapua tiina na zoore mɛ to. 8Tega kalo na gilimi Tapua teo to nam ye Manasɛ dwi dem nyem mo, ye Tapua teo kom tete ye Efrayim nyem. Ko déem jei Manasɛ siseini baŋa ne mo. 9Ba laŋa siseini dem ta tole tega-kuri seeni mo de yi Kana bu-nɔgɔ kom ne. De ma tɔge bu-nɔgɔ kom baŋa seeni konto ko vo ko zo Mediterania naneo kom wone. Teene dedwonna maa na tɔge bu-nɔgɔ kom kuri seeni to déem ye Efrayim teene mo, ye de wo Manasɛ siseini wone. 10Efrayim tega kam wo bu-nɔgɔ kom kuri seeni mo. Manasɛ tega kam maa wo ko baŋa seeni, ye Mediterania naneo kom jei ko wɛ-zoore seeni. Asere dwi dem tega wo baŋa seeni mo, ye Isakara dwi dem tega wo wɛ-puli seeni.
11Teene dedwonna déem ye Manasɛ dwi dem nyem mo, ye de wo Isakara dedaane Asere dwia yam tega baŋa ne. De maa ye: Bɛte-San, de Ibeleyam, de Dora tiina (Nafofa-Dora mo konto), de Endora, de Taanaka dedaane Megido, ko ta woli de dento nawuura yam de.
12Manasɛ dwi tiina nam wo wane ba zeili balo na zoore teene dem konto ne to. Ko ma pa se Kanaan tiina bam de yɔɔre ba zoore de wone. 13Isarele tiina bam maa na tu ba dana maŋa kalo to, ba ta wo zeili Kanaan tiina bam. Ba déem jege-ba ba pa se ba toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛra mo ba pa-ba.
Josɛf dwi tiina lwoori Josua ba tega kam ŋwaane
14Ko na wora ko wora to, Josɛf dwi tiina ma vo ba lwoori Josua ba we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n pa debam tega kam pɔɔrem dedoa yerane se dé taa tei? Nii Baŋa Wɛ na tiini o ke zaane debam yuu ne pa se dé kɔgɔ kom daga tei!”
15Josua de ma leiri-ba o we, “Abam na daga konto ye á maane we Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam muri se á pɔɔre-ka á pa daane to, nam zo-na Pɛrizi tiina dedaane Refayi tiina kagoa kam wone. Dáane mo abam wó wane á de teeni ye á daare á chɛ gula se tega taa wora ka pa abam.” 16Ba daa ma leiri‑o ba we, “Zwonnu laŋa kam seene ka muri debam dedɛ. Dé ta maa bá wane dé jeeri Kanaan tiina balo na zoore bwollu tem ne to dé zeili. Banto mae luuru mo ba ma ke torokooro ba jege ba ke ba jara, ko ná ye balo na zoore Bɛte-San seeni de balo na wo Jezerele bwollu tem ne to maama de.”
17Josua ma ta de Efrayim dwi dem de Manasɛ dwi dem o we, “Abam seene á ye nɔn-kɔgɔ mo ye á jege dam. Abam nam wó wane á na tega a woli a tega kam ne. 18Zwonnu seeni laŋa kam na ye goa to ye se á kwei á pɔɔre á pa daane mo. Véi-na dáane á zage gula á na lage tei maama to. Ko nam ná ye Kanaan tiina balo na zoore jei sem konto ne ye ba jege dam, pa ba taa jege jara-keim torokooro to maama de, á wó wane-ba á zeili á daare ba tega kam á ta‑á tei.”

english_text:
Joshua Gives Out the Rest of the Land
1After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent. 2There were still seven tribes without any land, 3-7so Joshua told the people:
The Judah tribe has already settled in its land in the south, and the Joseph tribes have settled in their land in the north. The tribes of Gad, Reuben, and East Manasseh already have the land that the Lord's servant Moses gave them east of the Jordan River. And the people of Levi won't receive land like the other tribes. Instead, they will serve the Lord as priests.
But the rest of you haven't done a thing to take over any land. The Lord God who was worshiped by your ancestors has given you the land, and now it's time to go ahead and settle there.
Seven tribes still don't have any land. Each of these tribes should choose three men, and I'll send them to explore the remaining land. They will divide it into seven regions, write a description of each region, and bring these descriptions back to me. I will find out from the Lord our God what region each tribe should get.
8Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
9The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh. 10Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided.
Benjamin's Land
11Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north. 12Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert. 13-14From there it went to Luz, which is now called Bethel. The border ran along the ridge south of Luz, then went to Ataroth-Orech and on as far as the mountain south of Lower Beth-Horon. At that point it turned south and became the western border. It went as far south as Kiriath-Baal, a town in Judah now called Kiriath-Jearim.
15Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring. 16From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
17At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe. 18The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley. 19Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River. 20The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border.
These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
21-24One region of Benjamin's tribal land had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Those towns were Jericho, Beth-Hoglah, Emek-Keziz, Beth-Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Chephar-Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba.
25-28In the other region there were the following 14 towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town.
These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_text:
Ba pɔɔre tega kadwoŋi kam
1Ko na woli fee ye Isarele tiina bam laam jwoŋi Kanaan tega kam maama ba tei to, mo ba kɔgɔ kom maama jeeri Siloo ne. Ba ma chwi Baŋa Wɛ jeerim vwei dem dáane. 2Ba ya ta wo pɔɔre tega ba pa Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom wo dwia yarepɛ se ba taa tei.
3Josua ma bwei Isarele tiina bam o we, “Dɛ dɔ mo abam boŋe se á vo á jwoŋi tega kam á nabaara Baŋa Wɛ wom na maŋe o kwei o pa abam to á ta‑á tei? 4Kuri-na nɔɔna batɔ batɔ se ba nwoŋi Isarele dwi maama wone. Amo wó toŋe-ba se ba vo ba beeri tega kam mɛ de mɛ ba boboŋa na dɛ to ne. Ba ná popone kolo maama ba yi na su to ba tiŋi, se ba jwoori ba ja-te ba ba ba bere-ne. 5Judah dwi dem wó maŋe ba tega kam na wo kuri seeni to ne. Josɛf dwi tiina de maa wó taa wo baŋa seeni de ba tega kam. Dé wó pɔɔre tega kalo na daare to kuni berepɛ mo. 6Abam nam ná popone tega kam popɔra berepɛ kam na nye tei maama to, se á ja ka memaŋa á ba á pa-ne. Amo laam wó ta jɔrɔ a pa abam se Baŋa Wɛ bere tega kam seina. 7Nam yé swei-na we Levi dwi tiina bam bá tɔge ba jwoŋi tega. Banto kaanem totoŋa yam ba na toŋe ba pa Baŋa Wɛ to mo ye kolo Wɛ na pɔɔre o pa-ba to. Ko nam ná ye Gad dwi dem, de Ruben dwi dem dedaane Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom, Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses mo maŋe o pɔɔre tega o pa-ba. Ka nam wo Jɔdan bubɛ delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to mo.”
8Nɔɔna bam na kwei chwoŋa se ba vo ba maŋe tega kam to, Josua ma ta-ba o we, “Véi-na á maane tega kam lanyerane se á popone ka memaŋa na ye tei to. Abam laam maa wó jwoori Siloo ywo-seeni. Amo de wó ta jɔrɔ Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne a pa abam.”
9Nɔɔna bam ma seene ba ke konto. Ba nɔne tega kam ni maama mo ba ja, ye ba ta pɔɔre-ka laŋa de laŋa kuni berepɛ. Ba ma popone ba bere laŋa maama na ye tei to de ka teene. Ba na ti to, mo ba jwoori Josua de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama tei Siloo ne. 10Josua ma ta jɔrɔ se o lɔre Baŋa Wɛ na lage se tega kam pɔɔre ka pa-ba tei to. O laam ma pɔɔre pɔɔre tega kam o pa Isarele dwia yalo na daare to maama.
Benjamin dwi dem tega kam
11Ba na tage jɔrɔ to, Benjamin dwi dem mo bobo se ba na ba tega kam popɔra, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. Ba tega kam déem wo Judah dwi dem de Josɛf dwi dem tega tetare ne mo.
12Ka baŋa seeni siseini dem zege Jɔdan buga kam ne mo de di Jeriko baŋa. Ba tega kam daa ma tɔge wɛ-zoore seeni ka kwei zwonnu laŋa kam ka vo ka yi Bɛte-Aven kagoa kam. 13Siseini dem zege dáane de vo de kɛ Luzi kuri seeni mo. Bɛtel mo konto. Ka ta kɛ ka yi Atarof-Adara mo. Teo kom konto wo peo baŋa ne mo, ko na wo Bɛte-Horon kuri seeni to. 14Ka ma pipiri ka kwei peo kom wɛ-zoore seeni daa kam ka duri ka vo kuri seeni, ka maa vei Kiriaf-Baal. Kiriaf-Jeerim mo konto. Ko maa ye Judah dwi tiina nyem. Benjamin wɛ-zoore seeni siseini dem mo konto.
15Ko nam ná ye ba tega-kuri seeni siseini dem, de déem bobo Kiriaf-Jeerim ni ne mo de vo de yi Nefatoa buli-yia yam seeni. 16Ka ta vo ka yi peo kolo na wo Refayim bwolo kom baŋa seeni ye ko tole ko nii Hinom bwolo kom teiŋa to. Siseini dem ta siseiri de tɔge bwolo kom de tu kuri de kɛ Jebusi tiina teo kom kuri seeni, de yi En-Rogele. 17Ba tega kam zege dáane ka diini baŋa seeni mo ye siseini dem gugwoli de yi En-Semesa, de Gelilofa. Jei sem konto lɛɛne Adumim sisworo kom mo. Siseini dem daa ta ma kɛ de yi Bohan Kandwɛ dem. Bohan déem ye Ruben bu mo. 18Siseini dem ma kɛ Bɛte-Araba sisworo kom baŋa seeni de tu de zo Jɔdan bwolo kom wone. 19Tega kam laam ma tole ka gaale Bɛte-Hogala baŋa seeni sisworo kom, ka vo ka kweeli Yɛ naneo kom baŋa seeni bubɛ dem ne, Jɔdan buga kam na vei ka guri mɛ to mo. Dento nam mo ye Benjamin kuri seeni siseini dem.
20Jɔdan buga kam tete mo ye Benjamin tega kam wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem. Siseina yalo ba déem na pɔɔre se Benjamin dwi dem taa jege to mo konto.
21Benjamin dwi dem déem jwoŋi teene dento mo, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem:
Jeriko, Bɛte-Hogala, Emeki-Kezizi, 22Bɛte-Araba, Zemarayim, Bɛtel, 23Awim, Para, Ofera, 24Kefare-Amoni, Ofini, Geba. De déem ye teene fuga-delei mo dedaane de nawuura yam.
25Ko ta woli de Gibeon, Rama, Beerofa, 26Mizipa, Chefira, Moza, 27Rekem, Irapeela, Tarala, 28Zela, Hayelefa, Jebusi tiina teo Jerusalem, Gibea, Kiriaf-Jeerim.
Dento nam ya ye teene fuga-dena mo dedaane de nawuura yam maama. Tega kam konto mo ba déem pɛ Benjamin dwi dem, pa se sɔ-yuu maama na ko nyem.

english_text:
Simeon's Land
1Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders. 2-6 In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following 13 towns with their surrounding villages:
Beersheba, Shema, Moladah, Hazar-Shual, Balah, Ezem, Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazar-Susah, Beth-Lebaoth, and Sharuhen.
7In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages:
Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
8Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
9Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon.
Zebulun's Land
10-12Zebulun was the third tribe chosen to receive land. The southern border for its clans started in the west at the edge of the gorge near Jokneam. It went east to the edge of the land that belongs to the town of Dabbesheth, and continued on to Maralah and Sarid. It took in the land that belongs to Chislothtabor, then ended at Daberath.
The eastern border went up to Japhia 13and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah 14and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
15Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
16This is the tribal land, and these are the towns and villages of the Zebulun clans.
Issachar's Land
17-23Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following 16 towns with their surrounding villages:
Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh.
Asher's Land
24-26Asher was the fifth tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans included the following towns:
Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph, Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal.
Asher's southern border ran from the Mediterranean Sea southeast along the Shihor-Libnath River at the foot of Mount Carmel, 27then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel, 28Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon. 29-31Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.
Asher had a total of 22 towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob.
Naphtali's Land
32-34Naphtali was the sixth tribe chosen to receive land. The southern border for its clans started in the west, where the tribal lands of Asher and Zebulun meet near Hukkok. From that point it ran east and southeast along the border with Zebulun as far as Aznoth-Tabor. From there the border went east to Heleph, Adami-Nekeb, Jabneel, then to the town called Oak in Zaanannim, and Lakkum. The southern border ended at the Jordan River, at the edge of the town named Jehudah. Naphtali shared a border with Asher on the west.
35-39The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included 19 towns with their surrounding villages. The following towns had walls around them:
Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth, Adamah, Ramah, Hazor, Kedesh, Edrei, Enhazor, Iron, Migdalel, Horem, Beth-Anath, and Beth-Shemesh.
Dan's Land
40-46Dan was the seventh tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans included the following towns:
Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-Shemesh, Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah, Elon, Timnah, Ekron, Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath, Jehud, Azor, Beneberak, Gath-Rimmon, Mejarkon, and Rakkon.
Dan's tribal land went almost as far as Joppa. 47-48 Its clans received this land and these towns with their surrounding villages.
Later, when enemies forced them to leave their tribal land, they went to the town of Leshem. They attacked the town, captured it, and killed the people who lived there. Then they settled there themselves and renamed the town Dan after their ancestor.
Joshua's Land
49-51The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_text:
Simeon dwi dem tega kam
1Simeon dwi dem déem mo saŋe se ba jwoŋi ba popɔra kam. Ba tega kam déem tole ka vo ka gaale Judah tega siseini dem mo. 2Teene dento nam ya wo Simeon tega kam ne mo:
Beeriseba (Seba mo konto), de Molada, 3de Hazara-Suwala, de Bala, de Ezem, 4de Eletolada, de Betula, de Horama, 5de Zikalag, de Bɛte-Marakabota, de Hazara-Susa, 6de Bɛte-Lebayofa, de Saruhen.
Dento ye teene fuga-detɔ mo, dedaane de nawuura yam.
7Ko ta woli de Ayin, de Rimon, de Efera, de Asan. Ba teene dem konto ye dena mo de de nawuura yam maama. 8Te-balwa na gilimi teene dem konto to déem tole kuri seeni mo de yi Baalafe-Beya mo. Rama mo konto.
Tega kam konto mo ba déem pɛ Simeon dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.
9Judah popɔra kam déem daga ka dwoi ba nɔn-bia bam. Konto ŋwaane mo Simeon dwi tiina déem jwoŋi Judah tega kam kadwoŋi ba jega.
Zebulun dwi dem tega kam
10Tega kam popɔra batɔ tu mo ba déem pɛ Zebulun dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem:
Ba tega kam déem tole ka vo ka yi Saridi mo. 11Ka siseini dem tɔge wɛ-zoore seeni ka yi Marala. Ka déem ta ma vo ka dwei Dabesɛfa, se ko laam yi bu-nɔgɔ kolo na wo Jokeneam wɛ-puli seeni to. 12Ko nam ná ye ba tega kam daa kakam kam, ka zege Saridi ne mo ka yɔɔre wɛ-puli seeni ka yi Kisilofa-Tabora siseini, ka daare ka ta yi Daberafa dedaane Jafia. 13Ka ta tole wɛ-puli seeni mo ka yi Gafa-Hefera dedaane Efakazina, ye ka laam pipiri ka da Nea seeni ka vo ka yi Rimon. 14Ka siseini dem baŋa seeni pipiri mo de jeeri Hanafona, se de vo de kweeli Ifitah-Eli bwolo kom ne.
15Zebulun teene déem ye fuga-delei mo dedaane de nawuura yam maama. Ba teene dem dedwonna mo tento:
Katafa, de Nahalali, de Simiron, de Idala, de Bɛtelehem.
16Teene dem konto de de nawuura yam mo ba déem pɛ Zebulun dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.
Isakara dwi dem tega kam
17Ko ná ye tega kam popɔra bana tu wom, ba déem kwei-ka ba pa Isakara dwi dem mo, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. 18Banto laŋa kam ba déem na jwoŋi to mo tento:
Jezerele, de Kesulofa, de Sunem, 19de Hafarayim, de Sion, de Anaharafa, 20de Rabifa, de Kision, de Ebeza, 21de Remefa, de En-Ganim, de En-Hada, de Bɛte-Pazeza. 22Ba siseini dem ta vei de dwei Tabora peo kom, de Sahazuma, dedaane Bɛte-Semesa. Ka laam ma vo ka kweeli Jɔdan buga kam ne.
Isakara dwi dem teene dem nam ye fuga-deredo mo, de de nawuura yam. 23Teene dem konto de de nawuura yam mo ba déem pɛ Isakara dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.
Asere dwi dem tega kam
24Asere dwi dem déem ma jwoŋi tega kam popɔra banu tu, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. 25Ba teene dem nam ya ye:
Helikafa, de Hali, de Beten, de Akasaf, 26de Alam-Mɛlɛka, de Amada, de Misala.
Tega kam wɛ-zoore seeni siseini dem déem yi Kamele peo kom dedaane Sihora-Libinafa. 27Ka ta ma gugwoli ka vo wɛ-puli seeni ka yi Bɛte-Dagon se ka laam vo ka dwei Zebulun dwi dem laŋa kam ka daare ka yi Ifitah-Eli bwolo kom. Ba tega kam ta vei baŋa seeni ka yi Bɛte-Emeke, de Neyeli. Ka ma kɛ ka vo Kabuli, 28de Eboron, de Rehobi, de Hamon, dedaane Kana, se ka kɛ ka vo ka yi Sidon teo kamunu. 29Ba siseini ta ma pipiri de yɔɔre Rama seeni, de tole de yi Tura, de na ye teo kolo na lɔge ko pe de dam to. Siseini dem laam ma gugwoli de vo Hosa seeni, de vo de kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ne. Ba laŋa kam déem ta yi Mahalaba, de Akiziba, 30de Wuma, de Afeka, de Rehobi.
Teene dem déem ye finlei-delei mo, de de nawuura yam maama. 31Teene dem konto de de nawuura yam mo ba déem pɛ Asere dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.
Nafitali dwi dem tega kam
32Nafitali dwi dem mo déem jwoŋi tega kam popɔra baredo tu wom, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.
33Ba siseini dem ma zege Helefa ne de yi tei-zɔŋɔ kolo na zege Zaananim ne to. De ta tole de vo Adami-Nekeba de Jaminia mo se de yi Lakum, ye de laam kweeli Jɔdan buga kam ne. 34De daa ma gugwoli wɛ-zoore seeni de vo Azanof-Tabora, de Hukoka. Ba tega kam kuri seeni déem dwei Zebulun dwi dem laŋa kam mo. Asere laŋa kam ma jeeri ka wɛ-zoore seeni. Jɔdan buga kam de jeeri wɛ-puli seeni.
35Ba teene dento mo lɔge de pe de dam: Zidim, de Zera, de Hammafa, de Rakafa, de Kinerefa, 36de Adama, de Rama, de Hazora, 37de Kedesa, de Ederi, de En-Hazora, 38de Yiron, de Migadal-Eli, de Horem, de Bɛte-Anafa, de Bɛte-Semesa.
De déem ye teene fuga-nogo mo, dedaane de nawuura yam maama. 39Teene dem konto de de nawuura yam mo ba déem pɛ Nafitali dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.
Dan dwi dem tega kam
40Dan dwi dem nam mo jwoŋi tega kam popɔra barepɛ tu wom, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. 41Teene dento wo banto laŋa ne mo:
Zora, de Esatola, de Irasemesa, 42de Saalabin, de Ayijalon, de Ifala, 43de Elon, de Timina, de Ekoron, 44de Eleteke, de Gibefon, de Baalafe, 45de Jehudi, de Beneberaka, de Gafa-Rimon, 46de Mejarekon, de Rakon, de jei selo maama na jeeri Jopa to.
47Dan dwi dem nam ya gɛ ba tega kam mo. Ko ma pa se ba fe ba vo ba jeeri Lesem tiina bam de jara. Ba ma di-ba ye ba jwoŋi ba tega kam ba zoore ka wone. Dan dwi tiina laam maa bwoi tega kam yere we Dan, se ko maŋe de ba nabaaro wom yere dem.
48Teene dem konto de de nawuura yam mo ba déem pɛ Dan dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.
Josua tega kam
49Isarele tiina bam nam ya na pɔɔre tega kam ba pa daane to, ba déem daare laŋa kadwoŋi mo ba pa Nun bu Josua se o taa tei. 50Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o pa-ba ni mo se ba kwei mɛ maama Josua na wó kuri to ba pa‑o. O ma kuri Timinaf-Sera na wo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne to, ye ba kwei-ko ba pa‑o. O ma fɔge o lɔ teo kom konto o zoore ko wone.
51Ko déem na ke tei Wɛ jeerim vwei dem na wo Siloo ne konto to, ko nam ye Wɛ kaanem tu Eleaza, de Josua, de Isarele sɔ-yuni yiga tiina bam mo zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne ba pɔɔre pɔɔre tega kam ba pa daane. Ba ma pɔɔre-ka ba ti, pa se Isarele dwi maama jwoŋi ba tega.

english_text:
The Safe Towns
(Numbers 35.9-15; Deuteronomy 19.1-13)
1 One day the Lord told Joshua:
2When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns. 3-4If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
5One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies. 6The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder.
Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
7The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns:
Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
8The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River:
Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
9These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_text:
Ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi teene dem
Jeelim 35:6-34
1Maŋa kadwoŋi ne mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Josua o we, 2“Laam ta de Isarele tiina bam se ba le teene dedwonna, ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane, nenɛɛne a na maŋe a ta de Moses se o bere‑m tei to. 3Wolo ná wo paale o go nɔɔno, o wó wane o duri o vo o seigi teo kom konto wone se o lu balo na beeri o gom to jeŋa ne. 4O maa ná duri o vo o yi teene dem konto dedoa, o wó vo ko manchwoŋo ni ne o lwoni o taane dem de teo kom nakwa bam mo. Banto maa wó beeri jei ba pa‑o se o zo ba teo kom o taa zoore de-ba. 5Wolo na beeri o gom to nam ná pare‑o o yi da, ko dae se teo kom tiina le‑o ba pa konto tu, kolo ŋwaane o wo paale o go nɔɔno wom. O nam ya ba chuli‑o. 6Teo kom nakwa bam wó di o taane se ba lɔre ko ke ko maŋe mo naa o paale o go o dwoŋi wom mo. O ná wo paale o ke, ba maa wó yage se o taa zoore de-ba se ko yi kaanem yiga tu wom ná tega. Konto mo o laam wó wane o jwoori o tete teo kom.”
7Ko ma pa se ba le Galili teo Kedesa na wo Nafitali zwonnu laŋa kam ne to ba zege ko ŋwaane. Ba ta le Sɛkɛm na wo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne to mo, de Kiriaf-Araba na wo Judah zwonnu laŋa kam ne to. Teo kom konto laam mo ye Heboron. 8Ko daare teene delo na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to mo ba kuri Bezere na wo Ruben dwi dem laŋa kam ne to. Jei sem konto ye te-kampare mo ka yi kagoa kam na wo Jeriko wɛ-puli seeni to. Ba ta ma le Gad dwi dem teo Ramofa na wo Gilead ne to, dedaane Manasɛ dwi dem teo Golan na wo Basan ne to.
9Isarele tiina bam ma kuri teene dem konto ba tiŋi ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane. Ko maa ye se nɔɔno ná wo paale o go nɔɔno, o ná ye Isarele tu naa veiru, se konto tu duri o zo de wone o seigi se wolo o na go to yera nɔɔna yé yi‑o ba go. Ko ta ye se teo kom nakwa bam wane o taane dem mo ba di de chega.

english_text:
Levi's Towns
1-2 While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
3Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi. 4The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive.
The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given 13 towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. 5The other members of the Kohath clans received 10 towns from the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and West Manasseh. 6The clans that were descendants of Gershon were given 13 towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and East Manasseh. 7The clans that were descendants of Merari received 12 towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
8The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did.
Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
9-19The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given 13 towns and the pastureland around them. Nine of these towns were from the tribes of Judah and Simeon and four from Benjamin.
Hebron, Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, Holon, Debir, Ashan, Juttah, and Beth-Shemesh were from Judah and Simeon. Hebron, located in the hill country of Judah, was earlier called Arba's Town. It had been named after Arba, the ancestor of the Anakim. Hebron's pasturelands went along with the town, but its farmlands and the villages around it had been given to Caleb. Hebron was also one of the Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
Gibeon, Geba, Anathoth, and Almon were from Benjamin.
Towns from Ephraim, Dan, West Manasseh
20-26The rest of the Kohath clans of the Levi tribe received ten towns and the pastureland around them. Four of these towns were from the tribe of Ephraim, four from Dan, and two from West Manasseh.
Shechem, Gezer, Kibzaim, and Beth-Horon were from Ephraim. Shechem was located in the hill country, and it was also one of the Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
Elteke, Gibbethon, Aijalon, and Gath-Rimmon were from Dan.
Taanach and Jibleam were from West Manasseh.
Towns from East Manasseh, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali
27-33The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received 13 towns and the pastureland around them. Two of these towns were from the tribe of East Manasseh, four from Issachar, four from Asher, and three from Naphtali.
Golan in Bashan and Beeshterah were from East Manasseh.
Kishion, Daberath, Jarmuth, and En-Gannim were from Issachar.
Mishal, Abdon, Helkath, and Rehob were from Asher.
Kedesh in Galilee, Hammothdor, and Kartan were from Naphtali. Golan in Bashan and Kedesh in Galilee were also Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
Towns from Zebulun, Reuben, Gad
34-40The rest of the Levi clans were descendants of Merari, and they received twelve towns with the pastureland around them. Four towns were from the tribe of Zebulun, four from Reuben, and four from Gad.
Jokneam, Kartah, Rimmonah, and Nahalal were from Zebulun.
Bezer, Jazah, Kedemoth, and Mephaath were from Reuben. Bezer was located in the desert flatlands east of the Jordan River across from Jericho.
Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim, Heshbon, and Jazer were from Gad.
Bezer and Ramoth in Gilead were Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone.
41-42The people of the Levi tribe had a total of 48 towns within Israel, and they had pastures around each one of their towns.
Israel Settles in the Land
43The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it. 44There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win. 45The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_text:
Levi dwi tiina teene dem
1Konto kwaga ne mo balo na wo Levi dwi tiina yiga ne to vei kaanem tu Eleaza, de Nun bu Josua dedaane Isarele dwia yam maama yiga tiina bam tei. 2Maŋa kam kam konto ne de ba ta zoore Kanaan teo Siloo wone mo. Levi yiga tiina bam ma yi ba tei ba ta ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ nam ya maŋe o pa Moses ni mo we, debam jege se dé jwoŋi teene mo dé taa zoore da se dé daare dé taa kɔna.” 3Isarele tiina bam tete déem ma da Baŋa Wɛ ni dem ŋwaane ba le ba dwia yam dedoa dedoa teene dedwonna ba pa-ba se ba taa zoora. Ba ta ma pa-ba vara pwoli se ba taa maa kɔne vara.
Kohafe sɔ-yuu tiina teene dem
4Ba ma ta jɔrɔ se ba lɔre Baŋa Wɛ na lage se teene dem pɔɔre de pa Levi dwi tiina bam tei to. Kohafe tiina bam nam mo dɛ yiga ba na ba teene dem popɔra, diga maama de ka nyem. Banto balo na ye Wɛ kaanem tu Aron diga kam to ma jwoŋi teene fuga-detɔ, ye de maama wo Judah de Simeon dedaane Benjamin dwia yam laŋa wone. 5Ko maa na daare Kohafe tiina balo to, ba de déem nɛ teene fuga mo na wo Efrayim dwi dem, de Dan dwi dem, dedaane Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom laŋa wone. 6Ko nam ná ye Gereson tiina bam, banto déem nɛ teene fuga-detɔ mo na wo Isakara dwi dem, de Asere dwi dem, de Nafitali dwi dem, de Manasɛ dwi chichworo kokom kom laŋa wone. 7Merari tiina bam de ma na teene fuga-delei na wo Ruben dwi dem, de Gad dwi dem, dedaane Zebulun dwi dem laŋa wone, diga maama de ka nyem.
8 Baŋa Wɛ déem na pɛ Moses ni se ba pɔɔre teene dem ba pa Levi tiina bam tei to mo Isarele tiina bam de kea, ko woli dedaane vara pwoli se ba taa kɔne ba vara.
9Ko ná ye Judah dwi dem dedaane Simeon dwi dem laŋa kam, teene dento mo ba déem le se ba pa 10balo na ye Kohafe sɔ-yuu tiina ye ba ye Aron bia to. Ba pɛ-ba teene dem konto kolo ŋwaane jɔrɔ kom kuri banto mo yiga.
11Judah zwonnu laŋa kam ne mo ba le Kiriaf-Araba ba pa-ba, ko woli dedaane ko vara pwoli sem. Ba laam bwoi-ko we Heboron mo. Araba déem ye Anaki kwo mo. 12Se ko ná ye teo kom kare sem dedaane ko nawuura yam, ba ya maŋe ba kwei tento ba pa Jefunɛ bu Kaleb mo se o taa tei. 13Heboron ya ye teo kolo ba na tiŋi ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane to mo. Wɛ kaanem tu Aron bia bam ma jwoŋi-ko. Ba ta ma woli teene dento:
Libina, 14de Jatira, de Esetemoa, 15de Holon, de Debiri, 16de Ayin, de Juta, de Bɛte-Semesa. Teene dento dedaane de vara pwoli sem ye teene nogo mo ya na ye Simeon dedaane Judah laŋa kam nyem. 17Ko daare Benjamin laŋa kam ne mo ba pɛ-ba teene dena mo: Gibeon, de Geba, 18de Anatofe, de Alemon mo ko woli dedaane de vara pwoli sem.
19Konto to, teene fuga-detɔ dedaane de vara pwoli sem mo ba déem kwei ba pa Aron diga tiina bam na ye kaanem tiina to. 20Ko maa ná ye Levi dwi dem na ye Kohafe sɔ-yuu kom ye ba dae Aron bia to, ba le teene dena mo Efrayim dwi dem laŋa kam ne ba pa-ba.
21Sɛkɛm déem ye laŋa kam konto teo mo. Ko maa ye teo kolo ba na tiŋi ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane to mo. Ko maa wo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne. Ba déem kwei-ko ba pa-ba, ba woli de Gezere, 22de Kibizayim, de Bɛte-Horon. Teene dena dem konto dedaane de vara pwoli mo ba pɛ-ba.
23Dan laŋa kam ne mo ba le teene dento ba pa-ba:
Eleteke, de Gibefon, 24de Ayijalon, de Gafa-Rimon. Teene dena dedaane de vara pwoli sem mo konto. 25Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom na wo wɛ-zoore seeni to laŋa ne mo ba ma kwei teene dento ba pa-ba: Taanaka, de Gafa-Rimon. Teene delei dedaane de vara pwoli sem mo konto.
26Ko maa bere we Kohafe sɔ-yuu tiina balo na dae Aron bia to déem jwoŋi teene fuga mo dedaane de vara pwoli sem.
Gereson sɔ-yuu tiina teene dem
27Ko daare ko ná ye Levi dwi tiina balo na ye Gereson sɔ-yuu tiina to, ba déem le teene dento mo ba pa-ba:
Manasɛ dwi chichworo kodwoŋi kom laŋa ne mo ba le: Basan teo Golan dedaane Be-Esetara. Golan ya ye teo kolo ba na tiŋi ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane to mo. Ba nam kwei teene delei dem konto mo dedaane de vara pwoli sem ba pa-ba.
28Ba ma jwoŋi teene dento Isakara dwi dem laŋa ne: Kision, de Daberafa, 29de Jaremuf, de En-Ganim. Teene dena de de vara pwoli mo ba le ba pa-ba.
30Ba déem ta jwoŋi teene dento Asere dwi dem laŋa ne: Misale, de Abedon, 31de Helikafe, de Rehobi. Teene dena de de vara pwoli sem mo ba pɛ-ba.
32Ko na daare Nafitali dwi dem laŋa kam to, ba jwoŋi teene dento mo: Kedesa na wo Galili ne to, de Hamofa-Dora, de Karatan. Kedesa ya ye teo kolo ba na tiŋi ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane to mo. Ba nam kwei teene detɔ dem konto de de vara pwoli sem ba pa-ba.
33Ko maa bere we Gereson sɔ-yuu tiina bam déem jwoŋi teene fuga-detɔ mo dedaane de vara pwoli sem.
Merari sɔ-yuu tiina teene dem
34Merari tiina bam laam mo daare ye ba ta ye Levi dwi dem wone. Ba ma jwoŋi teene dento mo ba pa-ba:
Zebulun dwi dem laŋa kam ne mo ba le teene dento: Jokeneam, de Karata, 35de Dimina, de Nahalali. Teene dena dedaane de vara pwoli sem mo konto.
36Ko na ye Ruben dwi dem laŋa kam to, ba jwoŋi teene dento mo ba pa-ba: Bezere, de Jahaza, 37de Kedemofa, de Mefaafa. De ta maa ye teene dena de de vara pwoli sem.
38Gad dwi dem laŋa ne mo ba ta ma jwoŋi teene dento: Ramofa na wo Gilead ne to, de Mahanayim, 39de Hesebon, de Jazera. Ramofa ya ye teo kolo ba na tiŋi ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane to mo. Ba nam kwei teene dena dem konto de de vara pwoli sem ba pa-ba.
40Ko maa bere we Merari sɔ-yuu tiina bam déem jwoŋi teene fuga-delei mo dedaane de vara pwoli sem.
41Konto to, Isarele dwi tiina tega kam maama wone mo Levi tiina bam déem jwoŋi teene finna-nana dedaane de vara pwoli sem. 42Teo maama maa jege vara pwoli selo na kaare-ko to.
43 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa Isarele tiina bam tega kalo maama o ya na gwoni ni de ba nabaara se o pa-ba to. Ba de ma jaŋe ba di-ka ye ba jeini ka wone. 44Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa ba sii de jara keim, ne o na gwoni ni de ba nabaara bam se o ke tei to. Isarele tiina dona bam wolowolo wo wane-ba ba chɔge, Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ba dam se ba di-ba to ŋwaane. 45Baŋa Wɛ déem na gwoni ni se o ke wo-laaro telo maama o pa Isarele tiina bam to mo o seene o ke o pa-ba. Dedoa tete wo maŋe kwaga ne.

english_text:
The Two and a Half Tribes Return Home
1Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
2-3 You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives. 4The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
5Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
6-9You've become rich from what you've taken from your enemies. You have big herds of cattle, lots of silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and plenty of clothes. Take everything home with you and share with the people of your tribe.
I pray that God will be kind to you. You are now free to go home.
The tribes of Reuben and Gad started back to Gilead, their own land. Moses had given the land of Bashan to the East Manasseh tribe, so they started back along with Reuben and Gad. God had told Moses that these two and a half tribes should conquer Gilead and Bashan, and they had done so.
Joshua had given land west of the Jordan River to the other half of the Manasseh tribe, so they stayed at Shiloh in the land of Canaan with the rest of the Israelites.
10-11The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river.
When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done, 12the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes. 13But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes. 14Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
15Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
16 All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him? 17 Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin. 18Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again.
If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation. 19If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar. 20 Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
21The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh answered:
22The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar, 23and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
24-25We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.”
Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord. 26That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord. 27-29To build another altar for offering sacrifices would be the same as turning our backs on the Lord and rebelling against him. We could never do that! No, we built the altar to remind us and you and the generations to come that we will worship the Lord. And so we will keep bringing our sacrifices to the Lord's altar, there in front of his sacred tent. Now your descendants will never be able to say to our descendants, “You can't worship the Lord.”
But if they do say this, our descendants can answer back, “Look at this altar our ancestors built! It's like the Lord's altar, but it isn't for offering sacrifices. It's here to remind us and you that we belong to the Lord, just as much as you do.”
30-31Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
32Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes. 33The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
34The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_text:
Isarele dwia yadwonna jwoori wɛ-puli seeni
1Josua laam ma toŋe ni se Ruben dwi tiina bam de Gad dwi tiina bam dedaane Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom na wo wɛ-puli seeni to ba se o na-ba. 2O ma ta-ba o we, “Abam ke chega de á na ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses déem na pɛ ni se á ke to. Kolo maama amo de maa na bere se á ke to, á seene á ke-ko. 3Abam peene mo ye á sɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ nia yam, á daare á woli á chorro tem taa se ko yi leile. Á maa wo nwoŋi ba kwaga ne. 4Ko nam yi se á jwoori á sam dem na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni, ye Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses kwei o pa abam to. Kolo ŋwaane, Baŋa Wɛ na gwoni ni se o pa á chorro tem sii de jara keim to, o seene o ke konto mo. 5Nam kwaane-na se á ta‑á ke kolo maama Moses na bere se á ke to. O maŋe o bere abam se á ta‑á swoi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, ye á daare á ta‑á jege chega á pa‑o. Abam ta jege se á zuli‑o mo ye á sɛ o ni dedaane á bochara de á dam maama.”
6-8Josua laam ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o ke ba yuu ne ye o daare o bane-ba o yage chwoŋa ne se ba viiri. O na bane-ba o yage chwoŋa ne konto to, o ma ta o we, “Abam ma‑á jwoori á sam de jejegero dedɛ mo á na vere á dona tei ne. Abam vara daga lanyerane, ye á ta jege lu-nyenno, de sabu-seŋa, de channa, de luuru, de gwaaro dedɛ. Véi-na á chɛ te maama de á chorro. Wɛ wó pa se á yi lanyerane.”
Ko ná ye Manasɛ dwi dem, Moses déem pɔɔre ba chichworo mo o pa-ba tega Basan laŋa kam ne. Josua de ma kwei tega o pa ba chichworo kodwoŋi kom Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-zoore seeni, se ba jeini de Isarele dwia yadwonna yam.
9Ruben dwi tiina bam de Gad dwi tiina bam dedaane Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom maama ma kwei chwoŋa ba maa jwoori ba sam ne. Ba yage Isarele tiina badwonna bam mo Kanaan teo Siloo ne. Ba ma jwoori ba tete tega kam na wo Gilead ne ye Moses kwei o pa-ba se ko tɔge de Baŋa Wɛ ni dem to.
Baŋa Wɛ gula bimbini dem
10Ruben tiina bam, de Gad tiina bam, de Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom ma vo ba yi Gelilofa. Jei sem konto de wo Kanaan laŋa kam ne mo, ye ko wo Jɔdan buga kam ni ne. Ba ta na wo bɛ buga kam to, ba ma zege dáane ba lɔ bimbin-kamunu ba yage da. 11Ko na wora ko wora to mo Isarele dwia yadwonna nigi we Ruben tiina bam, de Gad tiina bam de Manasɛ dwi chichworo kodwoŋi kom mo lɔge kaanem bimbini ba zege Gelilofa ne, ko na maŋe de banto bubɛ dem na wo Jɔdan buga kam ne to. 12Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama ma jeeri Siloo ne, se ba vo ba kwaare jara de ba chorro tem na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to.
13Ba ma toŋe Wɛ kaanem tu Eleaza bu Finehase se o vo o ŋɔɔne de-ba se ko laam daare se ba jeeri-ba de jara. 14Ba ta ma le yiga tiina fuga se ba nwoŋi ba dwia fuga kam maama wone ba tɔge de Finehase ba vo ba tei. Banto maama jege sam mo ba nii de baŋa ne. 15Finehase de nɔɔna fuga bam ma vo Gilead ba jeeri de Ruben tiina bam, de Gad tiina de Manasɛ dwi chichworo kodwoŋi kom, ye ba ta de-ba ba we, 16“Baŋa Wɛ kɔ-fɔrɔ kom mo toŋe debam á tei ne se dé bwei abam dé nii kolo ŋwaane á daa na ba jege chega dedaane Baŋa Wɛ to. Bɛ mo kea ye abam lɔ Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne, ye á daare á lɔ bimbini se á ta‑á ke kaanem de baŋa ne?
