N wo sɛ n tɔge teo kom nɔn-donno tem kwaga, ba ya ze jege wonnu naa ba ná ye zora de. 11A bukɔ, nam yé ta‑n fona. N na lage woŋo kolo to, a wó ke a pa‑m. Teo kom nɔɔna bam maama maane we n ye ka-yero mo. 12Ko ye chega mo we amo ye n yera nɔɔno, se nɔɔno wodwoŋi wora o na wo yiga ne o dwoi amo se o nii n baŋa ne. 13Ta‑n tigi ywo-seeni tete dento maama, se tega ná poore, dé wó bwei dé nii o boboŋa tɔge keim dento naa ya ba tɔga. O ná sɛ se o ke konto, ko lamma. A dugi de Baŋa Wɛ wolo na ŋwe to yere we, o daa ná wo sɛ, amo wó taa nii n baŋa ne. Peini ywo-seeni se ko taa vei te-pora.”
14Ruf ma peini Bowaza nɛ sem seeni. O ma daare o gwoni tega o zaŋe lela se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé na‑o. Kokuri to, Bowaza ba lage se nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre we Ruf tu o tei. 15Bowaza ma ta o we, “Dɔne n gare-vɔɔ kom n lware tega ne.” O ma lware-ko. Bowaza ma lwo chaara bwɛ seredo o ke da o daare o ja o zeŋe‑o. O laam ma jwoori o vo teo kom wo.
16Ruf na yi sɔŋɔ to, o baro-nu Nawomi ma bwei‑o o we, “A bukɔ, n na vei da to, ko ke tɛ mo?” Ruf ma ta o bere‑o woŋo kolo maama Bowaza na ke o pa‑o to, 17ye o we, “O we a yé jwoori de je-kore. O ma pa-ne mena yanto maama.” 18Nawomi laam ma ta de Ruf o we, “Nam zuri n yera se dé nii tento maama na lage ko ke tei to. Bowaza ná wo nɛ taane dem kuri, o bá sii.”

english_text:
Ruth and Boaz Get Married
1In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did. 2Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down, 3he said to the man:
Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech. 4I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line.
The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
5“If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
6The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
7 To make a sale legal in those days, one person would take off a sandal and give it to the other. 8So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
9Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else:
All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon. 10 You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
11 The town leaders and the others standing there said:
We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem. 12 May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
13Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son. 14After his birth, the women said to Naomi:
Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel. 15He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
16Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him. 17The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.”
When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David. 18-22Here is a list of the ancestors of David: Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, and Perez.
translation_text:
Bowaza swo Ruf
1Bowaza ma vo teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni o jeini mɛ nakwa bam déem na jei ba di taane to. Ko na ke fee to, o yera nɔɔno wolo de daa na tiini o bwola ye o ta o taane to ma tɔge da o maa kɛa. Bowaza ma bwoŋi‑o o we, “A choro, ba n jeini ywo.” O ma vo o jeini da. 2Bowaza ma bwoŋi teo kom nakwa fuga o pa ba de jeini ba tei ne. Ba na jeini to, 3o ma ta de o choro kom o we, “Nawomi laam nwoŋi Moaba o jwoori o ba. O maa lage se o kwei debam choro Elimeleka tega kam o yeigi. 4Amo na boŋe tei to, ko maŋe se n ta‑n yei ko ni ne. Nmo ná laga se n yeigi tega kam, se n yeigi-ka nakwa bam de nɔɔna balo maama na jei ywo to yiga ne. N ná lage n jwoŋi-ka, nam jwoŋi! N daa‑n ná ba laga, se n ta se a lɔre. Nmo mo wó da yiga se n yeigi-ka. Nmo nam ná wo yeigi-ka, amo wó wane a yeigi.” Nɔɔno wom ma leiri o we, o wó yeigi-ka.
5Bowaza maa we, “Tɔ. N nam ná yeigi tega kam Nawomi tei ne, ta‑n yei we, nmo wó lɛɛre n swo Ruf na ye kadeim ye o nwoŋi Moaba to n woli da. Konto mo wó pa se tega kam maŋe o bar-dwooru wom dwi jeŋa ne.” 6Nɔɔno wom na nigi konto to, o ma ta o we, “Ko nam ná ye konto, amo daa bá yeigi tega kam. A ná yeigi-ka, a bia jwa bá taa tei-ka. Nmo nam ná wó leiri a yuu ne n yeigi-ka, se n ke konto.”
7Ko déem na yeini ko ke tei Isarele tiina bam tei ne to, nɔɔna ná yeigi wonnu ba pa daane, ba dedoa mo wó le o natere o kwei o pa wodwoŋi wom, se ko bere we ba sɛ pipiu kom. Konto déem bere we keim dem tɔge chwoŋa chekke. 8Konto ŋwaane, Bowaza choro kom na tage o we, Bowaza mo wó yeigi tega kam to, o ma le o natere o pa‑o. 9Bowaza laam ma ta de nakwa bam, de balo maama na wora to o we, “Abam maama zem nɛ we amo yeigi woŋo kolo maama ya na ye Elimeleka nyem to, ko woli de o bia Kilion, de Maalon de wonnu maama Nawomi tei ne. 10Ko ná ye Moaba tiina bukɔ Ruf wolo na ye Maalon kadeim to, amo jwoŋi‑o a woli da pa se o ye a kaane. Konto wó pa se too wom yere taa wo o jejegero baŋa ne, ye o dwi taa twoŋi taa dé teo kom ne. Abam zem maane we ko ye chega.”
11Nakwa bam de balo maama na wo teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni ne to ma sɛ ye ba we, “Debam seene dé na kolo na ke to. Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se kaane wolo n zem na swo to lo bia, nenɛɛne Racheli de Leah déem na loge bia pa se Isarele dwi dem daga to. Wɛ wó pa se nmo tiini n ji nadum Eferata teo ne ye n ta‑n jege yere Bɛtelehem teo ne. 12Baŋa Wɛ wó pa kaane wonto lo bia dedɛ o pa‑m, pa se n dwi dem yere zaŋe nenɛɛne Judah de Tamara déem na loge Pɛreza ye o pa Judah sɔŋɔ kom yale tei to.”
Bowaza dwi dem se ko yi David
13Bowaza ma kwei Ruf o ma ke o kaane. Ba ma peini daane. Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se Ruf ja puga, ye o lo bakeira. 14Teo kom kaana bam laam ma ta de Nawomi ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de tia! Kokuri to, o zem pɛ‑m naa se o taa nii n baŋa ne. Wɛ wó pa se bu wom yere zaŋe Isarele tiina maama tei ne! 15Wonto wó pa se n ŋwea daa taa jege ywoni ye o fɔge o nii nmo baŋa ne n kokweero maŋa ne. N bu-kaane Ruf mo loga. Wonto nam tiini o swoi‑m lanyerane ye o dwoi bu-baara barepɛ n tei ne.”
16Nawomi ma jwoŋi bu wom ye o kwei‑o o feiri o tete bochare ne. O ma lɛɛre o jege‑o o kɔna. 17Kaana balo na zoore ba bwola de-ba to maa we, “Nawomi bu mo tento.” Ba ma pa bu wom yere we Obeda. Wonto déem mo loge Jesse. Jesse de ma ba o lo Pɛ David.
18Pɛreza dwi dem taane mo tento:
Pɛreza déem mo loge Hezeron. 19Hezeron ma lo Ram. Ram de ma lo Aminadabi. 20Aminadabi ma lo Naason. Naason ma lo Salimon. 21Salimon ma lo Bowaza. Bowaza de ma lo Obeda. 22Obeda déem ma lo Jesse. Jesse de ma lo Pɛ David.

english_text:
Hannah Asks the Lord for a Child
1Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
2Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
3Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
4Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters. 5But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
6Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children, 7especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year.
One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat. 8So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
9When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship. 10Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed, 11 “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
12-13Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk. 14“How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
15-16“Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
17Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
18“Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better.
Samuel Is Born
19Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah 20with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him.
Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
21The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord. 22But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
23“You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
24-25When it was the time of year to go to Shiloh again, Hannah and Elkanah took Samuel to the Lord's house. They brought along a three-year-old bull, a sack containing about nine kilograms of flour, and a clay jar full of wine. Hannah and Elkanah offered the bull as a sacrifice, then brought the little boy to Eli.
26“Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord 27to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for. 28Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.”

translation_text:
Samuwel lora de o biini taane
1Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Elikana. O déem nwoŋi Eferata dwi dem wone mo, de Zufa sɔ-yuu kom ne. O kwo yere maa ye Jeroham, ye o nabaara ye Elihu, de Tohu, de Zufa. O déem zoore Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam teo kodwoŋi ne, ko yere mo Rama. 2Elikana kaana déem ye balei mo. Ba dedoa yere mo Hanna, wodwoŋi wom yere maa ye Penina. Penina déem maa jege bia ye Hanna ba jege bu.
3Bene maama ne, Elikana yeini o zege Rama ne o ja o diga kam maama mo o vo wara-jei sem na wo Siloo ne to se o zuli Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ, ye o daare o ke kaanem o pa‑o. Eli bia balei bam, Hofini dedaane Finehase déem mo ye Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam Siloo ne. 4Elikana ná yeini o ke kaanem konto, o yeini o maŋe nɔna yam mo o pa Penina, ye o daare o kwei yadwonna o pa o bia bam de. 5Se ko ná ye Hanna, Elikana yeini o maŋe nɔna yam kuni belei o pa‑o, o na tiini o swoi‑o to ŋwaane mo. Baŋa Wɛ nam wo pɛ pwola se wonto lo bia. 6Konto ŋwaane, Hanna ka-dwoŋi Penina maa yeini o ke‑o o mɔna, ye o daare o pae ko zoore o yera lanyerane. 7Ko maa ye konto mo bene de bene. Ba ná vei Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne, Penina wó tiini o pa ko chɛ Hanna yera mo. O de déem maa yeini o ve se o di wodiu, ye o lɛɛre o da keira yerane taa. 8O baro Elikana laam ma yeini o bwei we, “Hanna, bɛŋwaane mo ye n ve wodiu. Bɛ mo ye n wo tiini ko chɔge konto? Yé ta‑n keera. Amo ba dwoi bia fuga n tei ne na?”
9Maŋa dedoa ne, ba na vei Siloo ye ba di ba ti to, mo Hanna zaŋe o zo wara-jei sem ne, se o ware Baŋa Wɛ. Konto de Wɛ kaanem tu Eli déem ya jei diga kam ni ne, o na yeini o jei mɛ to. 10Hanna yiga ma tiini ka nyɔne, ye o keera. O ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ, 11ye o pwooli o we, “Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo ye nmo tontoŋeno mo. Nii lɛɛro tento a na wo te wone to, se n guli amo gula. Nmo ná wo swei amo swia, ye n ná pɛ-ne bakeira, amo nam lage a jwoori a kwei‑o mo a pa nmo, se o ŋwea maama wone o taa ye nmo nyem. Fan-choa de nam bá fɔge ka tɔge o yuu ka kɛ.”
12Hanna ma tiini o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne o dáane, ye Eli de maa jei o nii‑o. 13Hanna wɛ-lworo kom maama déem ke o bochare ne mo. O ni-vɔɔro tem déem mage daane mo, ye o kwora ba zaŋa. Eli na nɛ konto to, o déem boŋe we kaane wom nyɔge sana mo o su. 14O ma ta de Hanna o we, “Nmo zo ywo se n bere n sa-nyɔre totoŋa mo na? Yage n sa-nyɔre kikia yam konto!”
15Hanna ma leiri‑o o we, “Aawo! Amo wo nyɔge sana kɔtaa! Amo ye kaane wolo na tiini a na daanem to mo. Konto ŋwaane nam mo amo yɔɔre a lwo a wo-chechɔgɔ kom maama a tiŋi Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. 16Yé ta‑n boŋe we amo ga ye ka-yɔɔ mo, se ko ye a wo mo chɔge dedɛ ko ja kɛ jeŋa. Konto mo tei a tiini a lwoori Wɛ.”
17Eli laam ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ko nam ná ye konto, zaŋe n vo de yazura, se Isarele tiina Wɛ wom wó pa‑m n na beeri kolo to.” 18Hanna ma leiri o we, “Amo tu. A ke n lei. Wɛ wó pa a kikia su n yi.” O ma zaŋe o viiri, o vo o di wodiu. O yiga daa maa wo nyɔne.
19Tega na poore tetete to, Elikana diga tiina bam maama daa ma zo wara-jei sem ne ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ, ye ba daare ba jwoori sɔŋɔ Rama ne. Elikana déem ma peini de o kaane Hanna. Baŋa Wɛ ma sɛ Hanna na lwoori kolo o tei ne to. 20Hanna ma ba o ja puga ye o lo bakeira. O ma pa bu wom yere we ‘Samuwel’. Kokuri to, o déem tage mo o we, “Amo lwoori Baŋa Wɛ mo ye a jwoŋi‑o.”
Hanna ke Samuwel Wɛ jeŋa ne
21Bene dedwoŋi déem daa ma yi se Elikana de o diga tiina bam jwoori ba vo Siloo ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ, se Elikana de kwei ni delo o ya na tiŋi o pa Wɛ to. 22Hanna maa wo tɔge de-ba o vo. O déem tage de o baro wom mo o we, “Yage se a ná tu a kwori bu wom yele, a tete wó ja‑o a vo wara-jei sem se a ke‑o Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ne. O maa wó maŋe da se ko vo ko yi o toone.” 23Elikana ma leiri o we, “Nam ke kolo maama na maŋe ko pa‑m to. Maŋe ywo se bu wom waare. Baŋa Wɛ nam wó pa se o ni dem ji chega ko pa‑m.”
Hanna ma maŋe sɔŋɔ ne ye o kɔne o bu wom. 24Bu wom na tu o kwori yele to, mo Hanna jaane‑o o vo Siloo. O ta maa jege bena yatɔ nabea, dedaane muni kuriwaa bu dedoa, ko woli de lɔa wo sana. O déem ma ja Samuwel o vo wara-jei sem, de o ta na maŋe o ye bu-pwola to mo. 25Ba ma go nabea kam, ye ba daare ba ja bu wom ba vo Eli tei. 26Hanna ma ta de Eli o we, “Amo tu. Ko na ye chega to, amo mo ye kaane wolo déem na zege n tei ne ye a lwoori Baŋa Wɛ to. 27Ko ye bu wonto ŋwaane mo a ya lwoori Baŋa Wɛ, ye o pa-ne a na lage kolo to. 28Konto to, a lage o jwoori a kwei‑o mo a pa Baŋa Wɛ. Bu wom ŋwea kam maama wone, o ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo.” O na tage konto to, ba ma kuni nadwoona ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ dáane.

english_text:
1 Hannah prayed:
You make me strong
and happy, Lord.
You rescued me.
Now I can be glad
and laugh at my enemies.
2No other god is like you.
And with you we are safer
than on a high mountain.
3I can tell those proud people,
“Stop your boasting!
Nothing is hidden from the Lord,
and he judges what we do.”
4Our Lord, you break
the bows of warriors,
but you give strength
to everyone who stumbles.
5People who once
had plenty to eat
must now hire themselves out
for only a piece of bread.
But you give the hungry more
than enough to eat.
A woman did not have a child,
and you gave her seven,
but a woman who had many
was left with none.
6 You take away life,
and you give life.
You send people down
to the world of the dead
and bring them back again.
7Our Lord, you are the one
who makes us rich or poor.
You put some in high positions
and bring disgrace on others.
8You lift the poor and homeless
out of the garbage dump
and give them places of honor
in royal palaces.
You set the world on foundations,
and they belong to you.
9You protect your loyal people,
but everyone who is evil
will die in darkness.
We cannot win a victory
by our own strength.
10Our Lord, those who attack you
will be broken in pieces
when you fight back
with thunder from heaven.
You will judge the whole earth
and give power and strength
to your chosen king.
Samuel Stays with Eli
11Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord.
Eli's Sons
12-13Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork. 14The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh. 15Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord.
Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
16Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.”
“No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
17Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry.
Hannah Visits Samuel
18The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment 19and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
20Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
21The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh.
Eli Warns His Sons
22Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel. 23-24“Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people. 25If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!”
But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father.
A Prophet Speaks to Eli
26 Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
27One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord:
When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am. 28-29 Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar.
But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
30I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me. 31The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
32Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young. 33If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death! 34 To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
35I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king. 36But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_text:
Hanna seini Baŋa Wɛ
1Hanna laam ma lwoori Wɛ o we,
“Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ,
nmo pɛ se a wo pwoli dedɛ!
Amo jwoori a na dam Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane mo.
Amo laam wó teere a dona baŋa ne,
kokuri to, a wo mo tiini ko pwoli nmo zeinim ŋwaane.
2 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo ye Wo-pwoŋo Tu ye n dwoŋi tera!
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa tera
o na mae dede‑m.
Peo kodwoŋi daa tera,
ko na jege dam ne debam Wɛ wom!
3 Baŋa Wɛ ye Wɛ wolo na yei totoŋe maama ni ne to mo.
O maa bore nɔɔna bora
ba totoŋa ŋwaane.
Konto ŋwaane, yage-na ni-wɛɛle taane!
Kweele-na á kamunni ŋwɛ selo
á na jege to á yage tega ne.
4Dedɛɛra tɛ sem bwori
ye ba dam maama ti.
Nabwona dam laam za fɔge
de puli mo taa.
5Balo ya na yeini ba di ba sui to
laam wora ba beeri totoŋa
se ba ma na ba ni-wodiu.
Balo kana ya na wɔe to de laam maa di lanyerane ba sui.
Kadega kam loge bia barepɛ mo.
Wolo bia ya na daga to laam tu
o ga o bu-kɔgɔ kom.
6 Baŋa Wɛ mo jaane toone de ŋwea o tui.
O maa pae se nɔɔna tu churu,
ye o ta pae se badwonna zaŋa.
7Wonto mo pae se nɔɔna ye nabwona,
ye o ta pae se badaara ye jejegero tiina.
O wae o pa se dedoa wo tega ne,
ye o daare o zeiŋi wodwoŋi.
8O yeini o liiri yiniga tu mo
bworu wone.
O maa le nabwom o lɛɛro wone.
O laam maa pa ba taa tɔge
ba jei pa-bia tetare ne,
se nɔɔna taa pa-ba zula lanyerane.
Kokuri, tega kam baŋa maama
ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo,
ye wonto mo chwi woŋo maama ko jeiga ne.
9O nii balo na zege de chega ba pa‑o to baŋa ne mo.
Nɔn-balwaaro nam wó tɔge lim wone mo ba jei.
Dam yerane ware de jwoŋi nɔɔno de yage.
10 Baŋa Wɛ mo wó chɔge o dona bam maama.
O lage o zege wɛyuu ne mo o bage o yage ba baŋa ne!
Baŋa Wɛ maa wó di nabiina maama taane.
Ko nam ná ye pɛ wolo o na tiŋi to,
o wó pa‑o dam
se nɔɔna maama taa pa‑o zula.”
11Elikana de Hanna ma jwoori ba sɔŋɔ Rama ne. Samuwel ma maŋe Siloo ne. O déem toŋe o pa Baŋa Wɛ mo, ye kaanem tu Eli nii o baŋa ne.
Eli bia bam taane
12Eli bia balei bam déem ye nɔn-wo-korro mo. Ba yiga maa tera de Baŋa Wɛ. 13Ba ta maa yeini ba chɔge Wɛ kaanem totoŋa chullu tem. Kokuri, nɔɔna ná tu se ba ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ, ye nɔna yam ta na wora ya saŋa maŋa kalo to, mo Wɛ kaanem tu tontoŋeno wom wó da o ba ye o zei da-chɔrɔ na jege nyea yatɔ to. 14Tontoŋeno wom laam wó chu o le nɔna yalo na wora ya saŋe to wone. Ko ná maŋe ko ye kambia ne, naa nakeina ne, naa woŋo kolo maama ne, nɔna yalo maama da-chɔrɔ kom na wó tore ko zɔ to mo wó taa ye Wɛ kaanem tu wom nyem. Ba déem jege kikia yam konto mo ba ke de Isarele tiina balo maama na tu Siloo se ba ke kaanem to.
15Se ko woli da to, ba déem ná yeini ba go varem ye ba ta wo lɔɔne varem wom lara ba zwɛ bimbini dem baŋa ne se ba daare, Wɛ kaanem tu tontoŋeno wom wae o tui o tɛ we, “Pa-ne nɔn-gwei delo kaanem tu wom na wó wɔ to, se o ba lage o jwoŋi nɔn-saŋa n tei ne se o di.” 16Nɔɔno wom ná zege se o ta we, “Yage se dé ná zwɛ lara kam dé daare, se n laam le nɔna yalo n na lage to,” tontoŋeno wom wó leiri mo o we, “Aawo! Pa-ne lela! Ko ná dae konto, a laam wó vere-ya de dam mo.”
17Eli bia bam wɛleere dem déem tiini de gaale mo ye de chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. Kokuri, ba déem pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ kaanem pɛɛra yam ba jege kuri.
18Se ko ná ye Samuwel, wonto déem zege o biini ne mo o toŋe o pa Baŋa Wɛ. O nam ya zo gare-wogo kolo ba na mɛ gare-fefale ba sɔ se ko taa nye de Wɛ kaanem tiina gwaaro tem to mo. 19Bene maama, o nu wom yeini o sɔ gare-bwora balaŋa mo se o pa‑o. O ná tɔge de o baro o ba wara-jei sem se ba ke bene dem kaanem, o yeini o ja gare-bwora kam mo o ja o ba o pa‑o. 20Eli de maa yeini o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o ke Elikana de o kaane Hanna yuu ne o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó pa kaane wonto lo bia o pa‑m, se ba leiri bu wonto yuu ne, o na kwei bu wom o pa Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane.” Ba de laam maa yeini ba jwoori ba sɔŋɔ.
21 Baŋa Wɛ ma seene o ke zaane o ke Hanna yuu ne. O ma lo bakeiri setɔ dedaane busankane selei. Se ko ná ye Samuwel, wonto déem ke nɔɔno mo, ye o toŋe o pa Baŋa Wɛ.
22Eli déem laam tiini o kwe mo. O ma yeini o ni o bia bam na toŋe tei maama Isarele tiina bam yera ne to. O ta ma ni we o bia bam jaane kaana balo na yeini ba la Wɛ wara-vwei dem ni ne ba toŋe to ba gwala. 23Eli ma ta de-ba o we, “Nɔɔna maama tɛ wo-lwanno telo maama abam na jege á ke to taane ba bere-ne. Bɛ mo ye á jege totoŋ-dwoa yam konto á ke? 24Amo bia bam, Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam na jege á taane ba tɛ tei to ba lamma. Nam yage-na kikia yam konto. 25Nɔɔno wolo ná ke o chɔge o dwoŋi nabiinu yiga, Baŋa Wɛ ta wó wane o zege kotu kwaga ne. Nɔɔno nam ná ke o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ tete yiga mo, o lage o ke tɛ mo?” De konto maama de, Eli bia bam ta wo sɛ o taane dem. Kokuri, Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa maŋe ya ja mo se o go-ba.
26Ko daare, Samuwel déem fɔge o ke nɔɔno mo. Baŋa Wɛ dedaane nabiina maama maa lage o taane.
Waarem delo na wó ba Eli sɔŋɔ baŋa ne to
27Wɛ tontoŋeno wodwoŋi déem ma ba Eli tei ye o we:
“Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo tento: Isarele tiina bam déem ta na ye kabɛ Ejipti pa-faro wom jeŋa ne to, amo déem veere a tete dedaane nmo nabaaro Aron. 28Amo ma kuri n nabaaro wom konto Isarele dwia yam maama wone, se o taa ye amo kaanem tu. A maa pae se wonto de o dwi dem toŋe a kaanem bimbini dem totoŋa, ye ba zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa ba pa-ne. Ba maa jege pwola se ba lɛ kaanem gare-wogo ba zo amo tei. A ta ma pa ba dwi dem chwoŋa se ba taa di a diga pɛɛra yam Isarele tiina bam na zwɛ ba kaane ba pa-ne to wone. 29Bɛ nam mo tei ye abam gwooni pɛɛra yalo amo na pɛ ni se á jwoŋi-ya á ma á ke kaanem á pa-ne a diga kam wone to? Nmo nam na ke tei to bere we n tiini n kɔre n bia bam se ko dwoni n na kɔre amo tei to. Kokuri, abam jege amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam wodi-laaro tem mo á di á nu bigila bigila.
30Amo wolo na ye Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom to ni dem mo tento: Amo déem ya pwooli mo we, á sɔ-yuu kom dedaane á dwi dem wó taa ye a kaanem tiina se ko taa vei wuu. Amo laam nam tɛ a we, ko daa bá taa ye konto. Kokuri, amo wó zuli balo dwi maama na zuli-ne to mo, se a daare a nii balo yiga na tere a wone to a chweese. 31Ta‑n yei we maŋa lage ka yi se a pa se n dwi dem ti. Nɔn-kweo daa bá taa wora n kwo dwi dem wone. Nmo diga tiina bam maama wó te ba nɔn-donne maŋa ne mo. 32Nmo wó na lɛɛro na tu amo wara-jei sem baŋa ne tei to. Nmo ta wó na amo na wó ke Isarele tiina bam lanyerane tei to, se ko daare abam dwi dem ne, nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá kwe se o laam te. 33Amo nam za wó pa se n bia bam wo dedoa daare se o taa toŋe a kaanem bimbini dem totoŋa. Wonto yia nam wó dwei pa se wo-chechɔgɔ yerane taa wora. Abam dwi dem na daare to maa wó te ba nɔn-donne maŋa ne.
34Nmo bia bam balei Hofini dedaane Finehase wó da daane mo ba te dɛ dedwe wone. Ko na wó ke-ba tei to ye se n wane n lɔre we kolo maama a na tage to wó ji chega. 35Amo laam wó kuri kaanem tu wodwoŋi na jege chega lanyerane to. Kotu wó taa toŋe ye o ke a boboŋa na lage kolo maama to o pa-ne. A maa wó pa se o dwi tiina fɔge ba puli lanyerane, se ba taa toŋe ba pae pɛ wolo a na wó kuri to. 36Abam dwi dem wone balo na wó daare to laam wó vo kaanem tu wom konto tei ba lwoori sabu dedaane wodiu. Ba wó ta ba we, ‘Popo, pa se debam de da dé toŋe kaanem tiina totoŋa yam, se debam de da dé laŋe wodiu.’ ”

english_text:
The Lord Speaks to Samuel
1-2Samuel served the Lord by helping Eli the priest, who was by that time almost blind. In those days, the Lord hardly ever spoke directly to people, and he did not appear to them in dreams very often. But one night, Eli was asleep in his room, 3and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long 4when the Lord called out Samuel's name.
“Here I am!” Samuel answered. 5Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?”
“I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.”
Samuel went back.
6Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?”
Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
7The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice. 8When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?”
Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel. 9So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ”
Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
10The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!”
“I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
11The Lord said:
Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it! 12I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised. 13He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever. 14I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
15The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said. 16But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!”
“Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
17Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
18Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.”
The Lord Helps Samuel
19As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true. 20From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet. 21The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ veere o tete de Samuwel
1Samuwel déem ta na ye bu konto to, mo o toŋe o pa Baŋa Wɛ ye Eli nii o baŋa ne. Kanto maŋa ne, nɔɔna ba ni Baŋa Wɛ kwora. Wɛ maa ba veere wonnu dedɛ o bere nɔɔna.
2Eli yia yam déem lage ya dwei mo ye o ba nae lanyerane. Tete dedoa, o maa tigi o tiga jei ne o dɔa. 3Samuwel de maa tigi wara-jei sem ne se ko maŋe dedaane Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam o dɔa. Ko déem ye tete-koro mo, ye Wɛ min-zwoŋo kom ya ta wo dwei.
4 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma bwoŋi Samuwel. O de ma leiri o we, “Nii-ne da.” 5O ma zaŋe o duri o zo Eli tei ye o we, “A kwo, nmo na bwoŋi-ne to, nii-ne da.” Eli ma ta ded‑o o we, “Amo wo bwoŋi‑m. Jwoori n vo n peini.” Bu wom ma jwoori o vo o peiga jei o peini.
6 Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma bwoŋi o yere o we, “Samuwel!” Samuwel ma pɛ o zaŋe wɛɛne. O ma duri o vo Eli tei ye o ta ded‑o o we, “A kwo, nii-ne da, n na bwoŋi-ne to.” Eli ta ma leiri o we, “A bu, amo wo bwoŋi‑m. Jwoori n vo n peini.”
7Samuwel déem ya ta wo me de Baŋa Wɛ. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ ya ta wo veere o kwora o bere‑o. 8Baŋa Wɛ ta ma bwoŋi Samuwel o ke kuni betɔ. Bu wom daa ma duri o vo Eli tei o we, “Amo kwo, n na bwoŋi-ne to, nii-ne da.”
Ko laam ma ba Eli yuu ne we, ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo bwoi bu wom. 9O laam ma ta Samuwel o we, “Jwoori n vo n ta‑n tiga, se o daa ná bwoŋi‑m, se n ta we, ‘Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, ta‑n ŋɔɔna, se a ye n tontoŋeno ye a cheigi n taane dem mo.’ ” Samuwel ma seene o vo o peini o peiga jei ne.
10 Baŋa Wɛ ma jwoori o ba o zege da. O ma bwoŋi‑o ne o ya na maŋe o bwoŋi tei to o we, “Samuwel! Samuwel!” Samuwel ma leiri o we, “Amo Tu, ta‑n ŋɔɔna, se a ye n tontoŋeno ye a cheigi n taane dem mo.” 11Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta o we, “Amo ti a yiga mo se a ke wo-kenkagele Isarele tiina bam wone. Balo maama na wó ni ko ŋwa to yera maa wó sɔɔre. 12Maŋa kam ná yia, amo wó toŋe kolo maama a na tage Eli sɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane to. A ná puli totoŋa, a nam wó ja-ya mo a yi ya gurim. 13Kokuri to, a maŋe a wuuri a kaane‑o we, a lage a waare o diga kam taa wuu, o bia bam keim-lwanno tem ŋwaane. Kolo ŋwaane, Eli ya yei o bia bam na tiini ba lwɛ amo dedɛ tei to ni ne, ye o wo de-ba chwoŋa ne. 14Konto ŋwaane mo, amo tage a du de Eli diga tiina bam a we, ‘Kaanem dwi de pɛɛra dwi daa bá taa wora, se ya wane ya saare ba tusim dem maŋa de maŋa.’ ”
15Samuwel na nigi konto to, o ma lɛɛre o tigi da se tega vo ka poore. O laam ma pore Wɛ wara-jei sem manchwo-peena yam. Foone déem maa tiini de jege‑o. O ma ware se o ta kolo Wɛ na veere o bere‑o to de Eli. 16Eli ma bwoŋi‑o we, “Amo bu Samuwel!” Samuwel ma leiri o we, “Nii-ne da.” 17Eli laam ma bwei‑o o we, “O tage bɛ mo de nmo? Yé zaŋe n seigi kolokolo amo yiga ne, se Wɛ wó pa n tiini n na lɛɛro, nenɛɛne n ná wo tage kolo maama o na ŋɔɔne dede‑m to n bere ne.”
18Samuwel ma tole Wɛ kwora kam maama nyɔ o bere‑o, o wo kweele kolokolo tega ne. Eli ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam mo konto. Yage se o ke kolo na wo o boboŋa ne to.”
19Samuwel déem maa wora o ke nɔɔno, ye Baŋa Wɛ wo o tei ne. Ko ma pa se kolo maama Samuwel na tɛ to yeini ko ji chega. 20Isarele tiina bam maama, ko na zege Dan ne se ko yi Beeriseba to, ba maama déem pɛ chega mo we Samuwel seene o ye Baŋa Wɛ sampwora mo chekke. 21Baŋa Wɛ déem ta yeini o veere o tete mo Siloo ne. O maa wó yeini o ba Samuwel tei o ŋɔɔne ded‑o.

english_text:
1Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel.
The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest
One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek. 2The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about 4,000 of them.
3The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
4 The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest.
As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, 5brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook. 6The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?”
When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp, 7they were scared to death and said:
The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before. 8We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
9Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
10The Philistines did fight. They killed 30,000 Israelite soldiers, and all the rest ran off to their homes. 11Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured.
Eli Dies
12That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow. 13He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying.
Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting. 14-15He was 98 years old and blind, but he could hear everyone crying, and he asked, “What's all that noise?”
The soldier hurried over and told Eli, 16“I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.”
“Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
17“Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
18Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for 40 years.
19The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard, 20and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!”
She didn't pay any attention to them. 21-22Instead she kept thinking about losing her husband and her father-in-law. So she said, “My son will be named Ichabod, because the glory of Israel left our country when the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_text:
1Samuwel de déem ma lwoni Baŋa Wɛ kwora pa ka yi Isarele tiina bam maama.
Filisi tiina vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam
Isarele tiina bam déem ma nwoŋi se ba vo ba kwaare jara de Filisi tiina bam. Ba ma vo ba tei ba vwoa Ebeneza seeni, ye Filisi tiina bam vo ba tei ba vwoa Afeka seeni. 2Filisi tiina bam ma ke ba tete daane se ba ja jara yam. Ba ma vo ba yi Isarele tiina bam de jara. Ba ma wane Isarele tiina bam ye ba go ba jar-keira morro tena (4,000). 3Isarele tiina jar-keira balo na daare to ma zege jara kapworo ne ba jwoori ba ya na tigisi daane mɛ seeni to. Ba nakwa bam ma bwei daane ba we, “Bɛ mo ke ye Baŋa Wɛ pa se Filisi tiina bam wane debam zem konto?” Ba ta maa we, “Pa-na se dé toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo Siloo ba ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ba ywo-seeni. Konto wó pa se Baŋa Wɛ taa wo dé tei ne, ye o jwoŋi debam o yage dé dona bam jeŋa ne.”
4Ba ma toŋe nɔɔna Siloo ne, se ba vo ba ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba ba ba tei ne. Ka maa ye jeiga kalo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na di paare cherubi sem tetare laŋa ne to mo. Eli bia balei, Hofini dedaane Finehase mo déem dɛ ba zeŋe dakaa kam ba ja ba ba.
5Ba na jaane Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba yi ba tigisim dem jei ye Isarele tiina bam na-ka to, mo ba déem tiini ba chwoosi wɛ-wɛ pa se tega kam maama ziziŋi. 6Filisi tiina bam ma ni sɔɔ kom. Ba ma bwei daane ba we, “Sɔɔ konto na zaŋe Hiburu tiina bam vwoa yam ne to kuri mo bɛ?” Ba ma maane we ko ye Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam mo tu ka yi Isarele tiina bam na tigisi daane mɛ to. 7Ko ma pa se foone tiini de zo Filisi tiina bam. Ba maa tɛ ba we, “Cham nam yi debam na! Ba wa yam mo tu ya zo ba tetare ne konto! Dé ta wo nɛ konto woŋo dwoŋi! 8Lɛɛro yi debam! Wɔ mo wó wane o jwoŋi debam o yage wa-dɛɛra yanto jeŋa ne? Ko ye wa yam konto mo déem pɛ se chanɛɛre dwi dwi ja Ejipti tiina bam kagoa kam ne ya go. 9Filisi tiina bam, á pa-na dé di baare! Ke-na jara yam ne babɛ tei! Ko ná dae konto, dé lage dé ji Hiburu tiina bam kabɛ mo, nenɛɛne banto de déem na ye debam kabɛ tei to. Konto to, jaŋe-na de baare!”
10Filisi tiina bam déem ma ke jara yam de ba dam maama. Ba ma wane Isarele tiina bam. Isarele tiina bam ma duri ba jwoori ba sam ne. Isarele tiina balo na tege de dɛ dem ne to kɔgɔ déem tiini ko gaale dedɛ, nenɛɛne jar-keira morro fintɔ (30,000). 11Filisi tiina bam ma vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam, ye ba daare ba go Eli bia balei bam, Hofini dedaane Finehase.
Eli toone
12Dento dɛ dem ne mo Benjamin dwi tu dedoa zege jara kapworo kom ne o duri o vo o yi Siloo. Nɔɔno wom ya kaare o gwaaro, ye kasolo taare o yuu maama, o wo na chɔge to ŋwaane. 13Eli boboŋa maama déem nam ya duri ya da Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam kwaga mo, se o lɔre kolo na kea ka baŋa ne to. O ma vo o jei chwoŋa ni ne, se o cheigi o ni jara-keim dem taane. Nɔɔno wom ma ba o zo teo kom wo o ta jara yam laŋa ya na vei tei to. Ba na nigi to, teo kom tiina bam maama maa chwoosa ba yaga bɔge-bɔge.
14Eli na nigi sɔɔ kom ŋwa to, mo o bwei o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye ba chwoosa konto?” Nɔɔno wom ma ke lela o vo o yi Eli tei o ta o bere‑o kolo na ke to. 15Eli bena déem laam ya ye funogo-nana (98) mo, ye o yia yam dwei. 16Nɔɔno wom ma ta o we, “Amo nwoŋi jara kapworo kom ne mo a ma a yi tento. Zem mo a zege dáane a duri a ba.” Eli ma bwei‑o o we, “Amo bu, bɛ mo ke da?” 17Nɔɔno wom ma leiri o we, “Ko ye lɛɛro mo dé nɛa. Isarele jar-keira bam duri Filisi tiina bam yiga ne se ba lu. Ba kɔgɔ dedɛ mo tega. Nmo de bia bam Hofini dedaane Finehase de tɔge ba te mo. Filisi tiina bam ta ma vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba viiri!”
18Nɔɔno wom na yɔɔre o ta kolo na ke Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yera ne to, mo Eli yale o to o kwaga ne. O déem jei teo kom manchwo-peena ni ne mo, ye o to tega ne konto. O na yale o to o kolɔ-bea baŋa ne to, mo o ba bwori pa se o te. Kokuri to, o déem kwe mo dedɛ, ye o ta tiini o nu o gaale. Eli déem ya nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne bena finna mo.
19Eli bu Finehase kaane wom déem jege puga mo, ye ka be ka ti se o lo. O de ma ni we ba vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba viiri, ye o baro wom dedaane o baro kwo wom maama tega. O na nigi to, mo o puga dɛ ka virigi ka lage lora. O maa wo wane o wori. 20O na lage o te o lora kam baŋa ne to, kaana balo na lwori‑o se o lo to ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Nam vɔ wo, se n loge bakeira mo.” O maa wo leiri kolokolo.
21Kaane wom déem ma pa o bu wom yere mo we, ‘Ikaboda’, ye o ta yere dem kuri o we, “Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom jei Isarele tiina bam tei ne!” Ko déem ye Filisi tiina bam na vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam to ŋwaane, de o baro dedaane o baro kwo wom maama de na tege to ŋwaane mo o tage konto. 22O ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom nwoŋi ko daare Isarele teo kom, ba na vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba viiri to ŋwaane.”

english_text:
God Causes Trouble for the Philistines
1The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod. 2They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
3When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged. 4But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway. 5This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
6The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic. 7Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
8The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?”
“Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there, 9the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened, 10so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!”
The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
11The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.”
Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die, 12and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_text:
Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam
1Filisi tiina bam déem na jaane Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba vere Isarele tiina bam jeŋa ne konto to, ba déem zege Ebeneza ne ba ja-ka ba vo ba teo kolo yere na ye Asedodi to mo. 2Ba ma ja-ka ba zo ba jwo-dɛɛre diga kam ye ba daare ba zege-ka jwoni dem kamɔgɔ kom teiŋa ne. Jwoni dem yere mo ye Dagon. 3Tega na poore to, Asedodi tiina bam ma zaŋe ba vo ba zo diga kam. Ba ma na we Dagon to o yibia baŋa ne Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne. Ba déem ma jwoori ba gɔ-de ba chwi de zega jei sem ne. 4Tega daa na poore to, mo ba nɛ we jwoni dem daa ta to Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne. Jwoni dem yuu dedaane de jataala maama bwori mo te tigi diga kam ni ne dáa dáa. De yera yam yerane mo daare. 5Konto mo pɛ se, dedaane zem maama, balo maama na yeini ba zo Dagon diga kam ne to ba sɛ se ba nɔne diga kam ni dem jei sem ba kɛ, ko ná maŋe ko ye balo na tu se ba kaane Dagon to de.
6 Baŋa Wɛ ma pa ko tiini ko zo Asedodi tiina bam yera. Ko ma ni balo na zoore jei sem konto maama ne to ye foone zo-ba. O ma pa se kasili-nabiina ŋone ba yera ne. 7Asedodi tiina bam na maane kolo na jege ko ke to, ba ma laare ba we, “Ko ye Isarele tiina Wɛ dem mo wora o waare debam, dedaane dé wɛ Dagon. Dé yé pa se wonto ni-gwonim dakaa kam maŋe debam tei ne ywo.” 8Ba ma la Filisi tiina dedɛɛra bam ba ke daane se ba jeini ba bane. Ba ma bwei-ba ba we, “Dé laam nam wó ke tɛ mo dedaane Isarele tiina wɛ dem dakaa kam?” Ba ma bwɛ ba ja ye ba we, “Pa-na se nɔɔna kwei-ka ba ja vo Gafa.” Ba ma seene ba ja-ka ba vo ba yi da.
9Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam na yɔɔre ka yi Gafa ka zege da to, mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se ko tiini ko zo teo kom konto tiina bam de yera. Vuvuga ma to teo kom jei maama ne. O ma de kasili-nabiina ba yera ne, nɔn-kweero dedaane bu-balwa maama. 10Ba daa ma pa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam vo Ekoron.
Ba na jaane-ka ba yi teo kom wo to, mo Ekoron tiina bam chwoosi ba yage ba we, “Ba jege Isarele tiina wɛ dem dakaa kam mo ba beene ywo! Nii ba na lage ba go debam de dé dwi dem maama tei!” 11Ba ma toŋe ba la Filisi dedɛɛra bam ba ke daane, ye ba ta ba we, “Toŋe-na Isarele tiina wɛ dem dakaa kam se ka jwoori ka na nwoŋi mɛ to. Se ko ná dae konto, ka wó wane ka go debam dedaane dé dwi dem maama ka ti.” Vuvuga ma to teo kom maama ne, ba na kɔre toone to ŋwaane. Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se ko tiini ko zo ba yera. 12Balo na wo tege to, kasili-nabiina mo ŋone ba yera ne. Nɔɔna bam déem maa kaase bɔge-bɔge.

english_text:
1After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months, 2the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
3“Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
4“What should we send?” the Philistines asked.
The priests and fortunetellers answered:
There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have. 5So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops. 6Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
7Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn. 8Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
9Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
10The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn. 11Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
12The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
13The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
14-15The cows left the road and pulled the cart into a field that belonged to Joshua from Beth-Shemesh, and they stopped beside a huge rock. Some men from the tribe of Levi were there. So they took the chest off the cart and placed it on the rock, and then they did the same thing with the bag of gold rats and sores. A few other people chopped up the cart and made a fire. They killed the cows and burned them as sacrifices to the Lord. After that, they offered more sacrifices.
16When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
17That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron. 18They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened.
The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
19Some of the men of Beth-Shemesh looked inside the sacred chest, and the Lord God killed 70 of them. This made the people of Beth-Shemesh very sad, 20and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
21They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_text:
Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam jwoori Isarele teo
1Filisi tiina bam na vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam Isarele tiina bam jeŋa ne to, ka déem maŋe ba tei ne chane serepɛ mo. 2Ba ma bwoŋi ba kaanem tiina de ba yi-nara, ye ba bwei-ba ba we, “Dé wó ke Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam tetɛ mo? Dé wó tɔge chwoŋa kɔ mo dé toŋe-ka se ka jwoori ka vo ka jeiga?” 3Ba ma leiri ba we, “Abam ná lage á toŋe Isarele tiina Wɛ dem dakaa kam se ka jwoori ka na nwoŋi mɛ to, ko nam ye se á toŋe-ka dedaane pɛɛre mo. Ko dae se dakaa kam jwoori ka vo bwori. Pɛɛre dem konto mo á lage á ma‑á ywoori ba wɛ dem, se de yage á wɛleere dem jene de ma chɛ abam. Konto mo wó pa se á jwoori á na yazura ye á daare á lɔre kolo ŋwaane o na tiini o pa ko zo á yera to.”
4Filisi tiina bam daa ma bwei ba we, “Pɛɛre dwi dɔ mo de nam wó toŋe se dé ma dé ywoori ba Wɛ dem?”
Ba daa ta ma leiri ba we:
“Jawe-chɛɔ kom na to á pwa banu bam de ba teene denu dem maama baŋa ne to, ko jege se á kwei sabu-seŋa mo, á ma á mɔ kasili-nabiina yanu dedaane baywoa yanu kamwaro, 5se te taa nye nenɛɛne telo na jege á teene dem te chɔge to. Konto mo á wó pa Isarele tiina Wɛ dem jwoŋi zula. Dɛ delo, abam ná ke konto, o wó jwoori o dɔne o je-dɛa abam baŋa ne, de á jwona yam, dedaane á tega kam maama baŋa ne, se á daa yé na cham. 6Bɛ mo ye á boŋe se á bochara ke dam yerane, nenɛɛne Ejipti tiina bam de ba Pa-faro wom de déem na ke tei to? Yé swei-na we Baŋa Wɛ ke kolo o boboŋa na lage to o yage ba baŋa ne, pa se ba ga ga ba yage Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba jwoori ba tete teo. 7Konto to, kwei-na dɛ á ke toroko-doŋo. Laam beeri-na naane delei na loga, ye ba ta wo kwei-de se ba ma toŋe to. Ja-na naane dem á lei de toroko kom se de taa vaŋe-ko, se á daare á pwɛ nwa balo naane dem na loge to á pe. 8Laam kwei-na Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam á daŋe toroko kom baŋa ne. Ta beeri-na dakaa kadwoŋi, á ke sabu-seŋa wonnu telo á na mɔɔne se á ma á ywoori‑o to ka wone, se á daare á zege-ka Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam takeiri ne. Abam ná ke konto á ti, se á laam kale naane dem á yage chwoŋa ne se de taa vaŋe toroko kom de via, 9ye á fɔge á nii. Naane dem ná lɛɛne debam siseini dem ye de kwei Bɛte-Semesa chwoŋa kam de maa kɛa, dé wó lɔre we ko ye Isarele tiina Wɛ dem mo seene o toŋe chanɛɛre dento o yage debam yera ne. Se naane dem ná tɔge chwo-gaa, dé wó lɔre we ko ke ko maŋe daane mo, se ko dae wo-lɔŋɔ.”
10Filisi tiina bam ma seene ba ke konto. Ba déem beeri naane delei delo na loge to mo ba lei toroko yera ne. Ko daare ye ba pe de nwa bam sɔŋɔ ne. 11Ba ma kwei Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba daŋe toroko kom baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba zege dakaa kalo sabu-seŋa baywoa de kasili-nabiina kamwaro tem na wo ka wone to ba ke da. 12Naane dem ma yɔɔre de kwei Bɛte-Semesa chwoŋa kam de maa kɛa. De yɔɔre de mage de yuu chwoŋa kam konto ne mo, ye de keeri de via. De daa wo ywori se de vo jazem seeni naa jagwia seeni. Filisi tiina dedɛɛra banu bam ma tɔge de kwaga ba vo ba yi Bɛte-Semesa ni ne.
13Bɛte-Semesa tiina bam déem ya wo ba bwollu tem ne mo ba gwei banina. Ba ma kwoni ba yuni ba nii, ye ba na Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam. Ko ma pa se ba wo tiini ko pwoli dedɛ. 14Toroko kom dɛ konto mo taa ko vo ko yi nɔɔno dedoa kara ko zege da, peo kamunu kodwoŋi teiŋa ne. Nɔɔno wom yere mo Josua. O maa ye Bɛte-Semesa tu. Nɔɔna bam ma yɔɔre ba lɔ toroko kom dɛ sem ba ma dwei mini. Ba ma daare ba go naane dem ba zwɛ ba ma ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. 15Levi dwi tiina bam déem ya gɔge Baŋa Wɛ dakaa kam toroko kom baŋa ne ba ja tu tega. Ba ta ma kwei dakaa kalo sabu-seŋa kamwaro tem na wo ka wone to ba woli da. Ba ma zege tento maama peo kamunu kom baŋa ne. Dɛ dem konto ne Bɛte-Semesa tiina bam ma ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra de pɛɛra yadwonna ba kaane ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. 16Filisi tiina dedɛɛra banu bam déem zege mo ba nii totoŋa yam konto maama. Ba laam ma jwoori ba vo Ekoron dɛ dem konto ne.
17Sabu-seŋa kasili-nabiina kamwaro tenu tem déem zege te pae teene dento mo: Asedodi, de Gaza, de Asekelon, de Gafa, dedaane Ekoron. Filisi tiina bam déem kwei tento mo se ba ma ba ywoori Baŋa Wɛ ba wɛleere dem ŋwaane. 18Ba sabu-seŋa baywoa yanu yam de maa zege ya pae teene denu delo dedɛɛra bam na nii de baŋa ne to. De maa ye te-fwaaro delo na lɔge de pe de dam to, ko woli de te-balwa bam na wo chege to. Peo kamunu kolo baŋa ne ba na zege Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam to daa ta wo Bɛte-Semesa tu Josua bwolo kom ne de zem maama mo, se ko taa ye maana de kolo na ke da to.
19Ko daare, Baŋa Wɛ déem ma go Bɛte-Semesa tiina bam nɔɔna fuserepɛ, ba na leesi ba nii Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam wone to ŋwaane. Teo kom nɔɔna bam ma keeri dedɛ, de Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe tei ba yera ne to. 20Bɛte-Semesa tiina bam ma bwei daane ba we, “Debam wone wɔ mo wó wane Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne o zege? O tiini o ye wose mo. Dé wó pa se o dakaa kam zege ywo ka vo nɔɔno wɔ tei ne mo?”
21Ba ma toŋe kwora Kiriaf-Jeerim tiina tei ne ba we, “Filisi tiina bam jaane Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba jwoori ba ba ba yage ywo-seeni mo. Konto to, ba-na á kwei-ka á ja á vo á tei.”

english_text:
1 The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it, 2and it stayed there for 20 years.
During this time everyone in Israel was very sad and begged the Lord for help.
The People of Israel Turn Back to the Lord
3One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
4The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
5Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
6The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord.
The Philistines Attack Israel
7When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel.
The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming. 8“Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
9-10 Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away. 11The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
12-13The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them.
For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines. 14The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath.
Israel was also at peace with the Amorites.
Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
15Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life. 16Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people. 17Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_text:
1Kiriaf-Jeerim tiina bam ma seene ba ba ba kwei Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam. Ba ma ja-ka ba vo ba zege nɔɔno wodwoŋi sɔŋɔ ne, o yere na ye Abinadaba. O déem zoore peo yuu ne mo. Ba ma kuri wonto bu Eleaza ye ba pwɛ‑o se o taa nii dakaa kam baŋa ne.
Samuwel nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne
2Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam déem maŋe Kiriaf-Jeerim ne ka dáane taa, nenɛɛne bena finlei. Isarele tiina bam maa keeri chekke, ye ba lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o jwoŋi-ba o yage. 3Samuwel déem ma zaŋe o ta de Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama o we, “Abam ná seene á seene yia mo se á jwoori Baŋa Wɛ tei ne, ko nam ye se á le Asetare jwona yam de jwo-yɔɔro tem maama á tetare ne á dole á yage, se á daare á lwei á wo maama á pa Baŋa Wɛ. Abam ná zuli wonto yerane, o wó jwoŋi abam Filisi tiina bam jeŋa ne o yage.” 4Isarele tiina bam ma seene ba dole Baal dedaane Asetare jwona yalo na wo ba tetare ne to ba yage. Ba laam ma sɛ se ba taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ yerane.
5Samuwel ma toŋe ni o pa Isarele tiina bam se ba maama la ba jeeri Mizipa ne, se o de lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o pa-ba. 6Nɔɔna bam ma seene ba vo ba jeeri Mizipa ne. Ba na gilimi ba ti to, ba ma mɔ na ba lwo tega ne ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Dɛ dem konto maama ne, ba ya vɔge ba nia mo ye ba we, “Dé seene dé ke lwarem dé chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga.” Isarele tiina bam déem na wo Mizipa ne konto to, Samuwel mo tu o ji ba yiga tu.
7Filisi tiina bam déem ma ni we Isarele tiina bam jeeri daane Mizipa ne. Ba dedɛɛra banu bam ma la ba jar-keira bam ba ke daane se ba vo ba kwaare jara de Isarele tiina bam. Isarele tiina bam na nigi ko ŋwa to, mo foone tiini de zo-ba. 8Ba ma ta de Samuwel ba we, “Fɔge n ta‑n lwoori dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ! Ta ja o teiŋa debam ŋwaane, se o jwoŋi debam Filisi tiina bam jeŋa ne o yage.” 9Samuwel ma kwei pi-choa o go o zwɛ ka maama puna o ma o kaane o pa Baŋa Wɛ. O laam ma kaase o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ Isarele tiina bam ŋwaane. Baŋa Wɛ de ma sɛ o wɛ-lworo kom.
10Samuwel ta na wora o ke kaanem dem o pa Baŋa Wɛ to, mo Filisi tiina bam fɔɔre ba twɛ se ba ja jara yam ba yi Isarele tiina bam. Ba ma yi da de Baŋa Wɛ zege wɛyuu ne o pa se doa tiini ka bage-ba pina-pina! Foone ma tiini de ja Filisi tiina bam, pa se ba duri Isarele tiina bam yiga ne ba jage jei maama ne! 11Isarele tiina bam ma da ko ŋwaane ba zege Mizipa ne, ba pare Filisi tiina bam taa, ba vo ba yi Bɛte-Kara kuri seeni. Ba maa jege-ba ba goe konto ye ba via.
12Samuwel ma kwei kandwɛ-kamunu o chwi-de Mizipa dedaane Sɛn tetare laŋa ne. O ma pa kandwɛ dem yere we, ‘Ebeneza’, ye o ta o we, “Se ko ba ko yi tento maama to, Baŋa Wɛ mo zeini debam.” 13Ko dɛ konto baŋa ne mo, ye Isarele tiina bam wane Filisi tiina bam. Baŋa Wɛ déem ma che-ba, pa se ba daa wo lɛɛne Isarele laŋa kam ne.
Samuwel ta na ŋwe to, Baŋa Wɛ déem lɔge Filisi tiina bam kwaga ne mo. 14Isarele tiina bam ma jwoori ba jwoŋi teene delo maama na wo Ekoron dedaane Gafa laŋa ne ye Filisi tiina bam ya vere-de ba tei ne to. Isarele tiina bam déem jwoori ba na ba tega kam ni maama mo. Yazura déem maa wora Isarele tiina bam dedaane Amori tiina bam laŋa ne.
15Samuwel déem nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne taa, ko vo ko yi o toone mo. 16Bene maama ne, o déem yeini o vei o kare teene dento mo: Bɛtel, de Giligal, dedaane Mizipa. Jei sento maama ne mo o yeini o kwɛ nɔɔna bam taana o pa-ba. 17O nam ná yeini o ti, o daa yeini o jwoori Rama mo o vo o jeini o tete sɔŋɔ ne. O na wora to, o ta ma nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. O déem ma lɔ kaanem bimbini Rama ne o pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_text:
The People of Israel Want a King
1-2Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba. 3But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
4One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah 5 and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
6Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it. 7The Lord answered:
Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king. 8Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you. 9Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
10Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
11If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot. 12Some of them will be officers in charge of 1,000 soldiers, and others will be in charge of 50. Still others will have to farm the king's land and harvest his crops, or make weapons and parts for his chariots. 13Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
14The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials. 15He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
16The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work. 17He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves, 18and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
19-20The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
21Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said. 22“Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.”
Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_text:
Isarele tiina we ba lage pɛ
1Samuwel déem ma ba o kwe dedɛ. O ma pa o bia bam ni se banto taa nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. 2O bu-kwea kam yere mo ye Joweli. Wolo na saŋe wonto kwaga to yere maa ye Abija. Ba déem yeini ba jeeri Beeriseba ne mo, ye ba nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. 3Samuwel bia bam nam wo tɔge ba kwo wom nɛ-bwora kam. Ba déem tɔge sabu-laga mo. Ba maa sɛ se nɔɔna yeigi-ba de sabu, ye ba daare ba kweele chega kam ba yage tega ne de ba na bore nɔɔna taana tei to.
4Isarele nakwa bam laam ma la ba jeeri daane, ye ba vo Samuwel tei Rama ne. 5Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Leile konto, nmo tiini n kwe mo. N bia bam nam ba tɔge nmo nɛ-bwora. Konto to, tiŋi pɛ n pa debam, se kotu taa nii dé baŋa ne, nenɛɛne teene dedwonna dem na jege pwa tei to.”
6Nakwa bam na tage we ba lage pɛ to déem tiini ko daane Samuwel dedɛ. O ma lwoori Wɛ ko ŋwaane. 7Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Cheigi nɔɔna bam taane dem, se n sɛ n ke kolo maama ba na tage dede‑m to. Kokuri, ko dae nmo mo ba ve, se ko ye amo mo ba we ba daa vae se a taa ye ba pɛ. 8Ba maŋe ba zege ko dɛ ne mo ba ve amo ye ba daare ba tɔge jwona kwaga, ko zege a na jaane-ba a nwoŋi Ejipti ne to, se ko ba ko yi zem dɛ dem. Ba laam maa wora ba ke nmo ne ba na maŋe ba ke amo de tei to. 9Konto to, za n sɛ ba kwora kam, se n daare n kaane-ba dedɛ se ba lɔre ba pɛ wom na wó toŋe tei ba yera ne to.”
10Samuwel laam ma tole Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to maama o bere nɔɔna balo na tu o tei se ba beeri pɛ to, 11ye o we, “Wolo abam na beeri se o di paare á baŋa ne to na wó toŋe kolo á yera ne to mo tento: o lage o fe á bakeiri mo se ba ji o jar-keira. O wó pa ba badwonna taa chwo o jara-keim torokooro, se badaara taa diini sisein-nɔɔna, ye badaara duri torokooro tem yiga ne ba kwɛ chwoŋa kam ba pa‑o. 12O ta lage o kuri á bia bam wone mo se ba taa ye o jar-keira yiga tiina, se badwonna taa nii nɔɔna moro baŋa ne, ye badwonna de taa nii nɔɔna finnu baŋa ne. O ta wó fe á bia bam mo se ba taa toŋe o kare sem ne ba vara ye ba daare ba zage mena. O wó pa ba ke jara zela de torokooro zela dwi maama se o ma kwaare jara. 13Ko ná ye á bukwa bam, o maa wó pa ba taa ke talwoŋ-ywoŋa dwi dwi ba pa‑o. Ba badaara de maa wó saŋe ba pa‑o, se badwonna de taa fɔge bworobworo. 14Pɛ wom lage o vere á kare selo na tiini se lamma to mo, de jei selo á na dugi Vini de Olivi teeni se wone to, se o daare o kwei-se o pa o tontoŋena. 15O ta maa wó jwoŋi á mena de á tio-bia fuga maama wone popɔra dedoa, se o kwei o pa o kwaga nɔɔna de o tontoŋena. 16Ko ta ná ye abam tete tontoŋena, baara de kaana, de á naane, de á bonɛ, o lage o jwoŋi balo maama na lana to mo o taa tei se ba taa toŋe ba pa‑o. 17O ta lage o jwoŋi á vare-mumugu fuga maama wone popɔra dedoa mo. Abam tete de nam wó ji o kabɛ. 18Dɛ dem ná tua ye á jege pɛ, á wó tiini á chwoosi á lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o woli abam, pɛ wom na bɛɛse abam tei to ŋwaane. Dɛ dem konto ne Baŋa Wɛ nam ba lage o cheigi á taane dem.”
19Nɔɔna bam maa wo sɛ Samuwel kwora kam. Ba ma ta‑o ba we, “De konto maama de, debam ta lage pɛ mo se o taa di paare dé baŋa ne. 20Dé lage se dé taa nye nenɛɛne teene dedwonna dem na ye tei to mo. Dé pɛ wom wó taa nii dé baŋa ne, ye o ta wó tɔge dé yiga se dé yeini dé kwaare jara dwi maama!”
21Samuwel ma cheigi nɔɔna bam ni taane dem maama, ye o de vo o lwoni woŋo maama o bere Baŋa Wɛ. 22Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Nam sɛ ba taane dem n daare n tiŋi pɛ n pa-ba.” Samuwel ma sɛ, ye o yage ni o pa Isarele tiina bam se ba maama jwoori ba sam.

english_text:
Saul Meets Samuel
1Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah. 2Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
3Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
4Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys. 5Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
6“Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
7Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
8“I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
9-10“Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets.
Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived. 11As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
12“Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry 13and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
14They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
15The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel, 16“I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
17Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
18Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
19“I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions. 20Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
21“Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.”
Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
22Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining room at the place of worship. About 30 people were there for the dinner, but Samuel gave Saul and his servant the places of honor. 23-24Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.”
The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.”
After Saul and Samuel had finished eating, 25they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house, 26and Saul slept there.
About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.”
Saul got up. He and Samuel left together 27and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.”
