translation_text:
Samuwel kuri Sɔɔl se o ji pɛ
1Benjamin dwi tu wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Kisi. O maa ye nadum. O déem ye Abiyeli bu mo. O kwo-nakwe yere maa ye Zerora ye wonto de kwo yere ye Bekorafa. Banto déem nwoŋi Benjamin dwi tu Afiya sɔ-yuu kom ne mo. 2Kisi bu dedoa déem wora, o yere mo ye Sɔɔl. O maa ye nenɔm ye o dwoŋi tera Isarele tiina bam maama wone. O déem ye nɔn-wagele mo chekke. O maa ye nɔn-doŋo ye o tiini o dɔra o dwoi o yuudwonna bam maama.
3Dɛ dedwe mo Kisi bonɛ sedwonna ywori se jei. O ma ta o bu Sɔɔl o we, “Ja dé tontoŋena bam wone dedoa se á vo á beeri bonɛ sem.” 4Sɔɔl ma seene o ke konto. Wonto de o tontoŋeno wom ma tole Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam maama, de Salisa jei sem maama, ba beeri bonɛ sem ba ga. Ba ma kɛ ba vo ba yi Saalim, ye ba wo nɛ-se dáane de. Ba ma daare ba tɔge Benjamin laŋa kam maama. Ba ta maa wo nɛ bonɛ sem jei sem konto mɛ mɛ.
5Ba laam ma beeri ba vo ba yi Zufa. Sɔɔl ma ta de o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Pa se dé jwoori sɔŋɔ. Tento wɛɛne, amo kwo daa ba nii bonɛ sem, o laam jei o boŋe debam boboŋa mo, dé na daane to ŋwaane.” 6Tontoŋeno wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Nii, Wɛ tontoŋeno dedoa wo teo konto ne. Nɔɔna tiini ba nege‑o, kokuri, kolo maama o na tɛ to yeini ko ke konto mo. Pa se dé beeri o jei dé vo, se dɛ delo wonto wó bere debam chwoŋa kalo de na wó tɔge to.”
7Sɔɔl laam ma bwei‑o o we, “Dé nam ná lage dé vo nɔɔno wom tei, bɛ mo dé wó ja dé vo dé pa‑o ye dé wodiu maama ti tento to? Kolokolo daa tera dé tampɔro tem wone, naa woŋo wora?” 8Tontoŋeno wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Nii mo! Amo jege sabu-dale balaŋa. Amo wó kwei dento mo a pa‑o, se o bere debam chwoŋa kalo dé na wó da to.” 9Faŋa to, Isarele tiina bam déem ná lage se ba vo Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu tei ba bwei woŋo Wɛ tei ne, ba yeini ba ta we, ‘Pa-na se dé vo dé na Yi-naro wom.’ Kokuri, ba déem bwoi Wɛ sampwori sem we, ba ye yi-nara mo. 10Sɔɔl laam ma ta o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Ko nam lamma, dé kɛ.” Ba ma kwei chwoŋa ba maa vei teo kolo Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na zoore da to.
11Ba na wora ba diini zwoŋo se ba vo ba yi teo kom to, mo ba jeeri bukwa na nwoŋi teo kom wone ba maa vei buga se ba mɔ na. Ba ma bwei-ba ba we, “Yi-naro wom zem wo ywo na?” 12Bukwa bam ma leiri ba we, “Ɛɛ! Nam ke-na lela, se o yɔɔre o wo abam yiga ne mo. Zem mo o daa ta tu debam teo. Kokuri, o lage o woli dé nɔɔna bam wone se ba ke kaanem zwoŋo yuu wara-jei bimbini dem baŋa ne. 13Á ná zo teo kom wo, á wó wane á yi‑o ye o ta wo diini o yi mɛ kaanem dem na wó ke to. Nɔɔna bam wó taa jei ba cheigi wonto mo se o ba o lwoori Wɛ swolim o ke kaanem dem baŋa ne, se wonto de nɔɔna bam maama laam wane ba di wodiu. Nam véi-na, se á wó na‑o.”
14Ba ma vo ba zo teo kom wone. Ba na maa zoore to, mo Samuwel de maa beene se o jeeri-ba. O déem wo chwoŋa ne mo, o diini o maa vei kaanem jei sem. 15Dɛ delo tega na wó poore se Sɔɔl ba o yi teo kom to, mo Baŋa Wɛ déem nam ya lwoori yiga o ta de Samuwel o we, 16“Jwa kanto maŋa ne, amo wó toŋe Benjamin dwi tu dedoa se o ba n tei. Ko ye se n lwo swolim nuga mo o yuu ne, se n ma n tiŋi‑o se o taa ye amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam yiga tu. Se wonto mo wó jwoŋi a nɔɔna bam o yage Filisi tiina jeŋa ne. Kokuri, a nii a na a nɔɔna bam cham dem, ye ba keira kam de yi-ne.”
17Samuwel yi na tu de peere Sɔɔl to, mo Baŋa Wɛ tage ded‑o o we, “Nɔɔno wonto mo a tage o taane a bere‑m to. Wonto mo wó taa nii amo nɔɔna bam baŋa ne.” 18Samuwel na wo teo kom manchwo-peena ni ne to mo Sɔɔl fɔɔre o vo o yi o tei. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Ja! Bere debam Yi-naro wom na zoore mɛ to.” 19Samuwel ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo mo ye Yi-naro wom. Nam da-na amo yiga se dé di zwoŋo kom baŋa dé vo kaanem jei sem. Zem mo dé wó tɔge daane dé di kaanem dem wodiu. Jwa zezeŋa ne, a ta wó ta kolo maama na wora to a bere‑m, se a daare a yage‑m chwoŋa ne se n viiri. 20Pa se n boboŋa taa tiga, se ko ná ye bonɛ selo na jei da yatɔ zem tento to, ba jwoori ba na-se. Nam lɔre we, Isarele tiina bam maama yi page nmo de n kwo sɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne mo.”
21Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Amo nam nwoŋi Benjamin dwi dem wone mo. Isarele dwia yam maama wone, Benjamin dwi dem mo tiini de muri. Amo ta na nwoŋi diga kalo ne to mo ye kalo nɔɔn-nɔɔno na yeiri ka ni ne to. Tetɛ mo ye nmo ŋɔɔne taane dento n pa-ne?”
22Samuwel déem ma ja Sɔɔl de o tontoŋeno wom o vo o zo jeerim diga kam wone. O ma pa se ba jeini mɛ yuu tiina na jei to. Balo ba na bwoŋi se ba jeeri da to maa ye nenɛɛne nɔɔna fintɔ. 23Samuwel ma ta de wolo na saŋe ba wodiu kom to o we, “Kwei nɔne delo a ya na pɛ‑m ye a ta dede‑m se n tiŋi de yera to n ja n ba n pa-ne.” 24Wodi-saŋeno wom ma kwei chwei dem de de nɔna yam maama o ja o vo o zege Sɔɔl yiga ne. Samuwel laam ma ta de Sɔɔl o we, “Ko ye nmo nyem mo. Di n na lage tei to, se a maŋe a tiŋi nɔne dento n ŋwaane mo, ye a laam bwoŋi nɔɔna banto maama se dé di daane.”
Dento dɛ dem ne, Sɔɔl dedaane Samuwel ma di wodiu daane. 25Ba na di ba ti to, ba ma zege da ba tu ba jwoori teo kom wone. Samuwel ma ja Sɔɔl o di sɔŋɔ kom nayuu baŋa ye ba lara. 26Tega na jege ka poore to, mo ba gwoni tega ba zaŋe. Samuwel ma ta de Sɔɔl ya na wo nayuu kom ne to o we, “Nam zaŋe n ti n yiga, se a bane‑m a yage chwoŋa ne se n viiri.” Sɔɔl na zaŋe o tu nayuu kom ne to, o de Samuwel ma nwoŋi pwooni ba kwei chwoŋa ba maa kɛa.
27Ba na vei ba yi teo kom ni dem to, Samuwel ma ta de Sɔɔl o we, “Ta de n tontoŋeno wom se o tɔge yiga o taa via.” Sɔɔl tontoŋeno wom na kɛ o ti to, mo Samuwel daa tage o we, “Zege konto, se a ta Wɛ kwora kam a bere‑m.”

english_text:
1Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him:
The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people. 2When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
3Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine. 4After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
5Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
6The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them. 7After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
8Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next.
Saul Goes Back Home
9As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said. 10When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
11Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
12 “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
13After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
14Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?”
Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
15“And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
16Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king.
The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
17Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord. 18When everyone had arrived, Samuel said:
The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
19God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
20Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe. 21Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
22The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?”
“Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
23The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else. 24“Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!”
The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
25Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
26God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him. 27But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_text:
1Ba na zege da konto to, Samuwel laam ma kwei Olivi nuga kabɔɔ. O ma lwo nuga kam Sɔɔl yuu ne ye o daare o kukwori‑o. O ma ta‑o o we:
“Baŋa Wɛ mo kwɛ nmo tento, ye o tiŋi‑m se n ta‑n ye o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam yiga tu. [Nmo wó ta‑n nii ba baŋa ne ye n daare n jwoŋi-ba ba dona maama jeŋa ne n yage. Tento nam mo wó bere‑m we Baŋa Wɛ seene o tiŋi‑m se n ta‑n tei o nɔɔna bam:] 2Zem, nmo ná nwoŋi amo tei ne, ye n ná kɛ n yi Benjamin laŋa siseini dem, Racheli yibeeli dem na wo Zeliza ne to, n wó jeeri baara balei. Banto maa wó ta ba bere‑m we, ba jwoori ba na bonɛ selo n ya na kare n beeri to. Ba ta wó pa n maane we n kwo wom daa ba jege se lwia, se o laam jege lwia mo nmo tete ŋwaane ye o bwei o we, ‘Amo wó ke tɛ mo se a jwoori a na a bu wom?’
3Nmo ná zege dáane ye n vo n yi Tabora tei-zɔŋɔ kom, n ta wó jeeri baara batɔ na maa vei Bɛtel se ba ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ. Ba dedoa wó taa jege bebale setɔ, dedoa maa zei bworobwooru tetɔ, ye batɔ tu wom de jege lɔɔ de ko wo sa-doora bam. 4Ba ná jeeri‑m konto, ba wó ware‑m, ye ba daare ba pa‑m bworobwooru telei. Ko ná ke konto, se n jwoŋi bworobwooru tem ba jeŋa ne.
5N laam ná zege dáane, n wó vo n yi Wɛ zwoŋo kom na wo Gibea seeni to. Dáane mo Filisi tiina jar-keira bam jege tigisim jei. Nmo ná yi teo kom ni, n wó jeeri Wɛ sampwori sedwonna kɔgɔ na zege zwoŋo kom wara-jei sem ne ba maa tua. Ba maa wó taa tae kwanno dwi dwi, ye ba wɔe senyɛ, ba daare ba taa wu wui. Ba maa wó taa via ye ba pworisa. 6Baŋa Wɛ jworo laam wó ba nmo baŋa dedaane dam pa se n de woli ba wone n tɔge n ta‑n pworisa. Konto baŋa ne n lage n leiri mo n ji nɔn-gaa. 7Wo-kenkagela yam konto maama ná seene ya ke nmo yera ne, ko laam ye se n ke kolo maama na wó su n yi to, se Wɛ wora dede‑m.
8Nmo laam ma‑n wó da yiga n vo Giligal, se a laam ba. Amo nam ná tu a jeeri‑m, a laam wó ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra dedaane yazura pɛɛra a ma kaane a pa Wɛ. Nmo jege se n cheigi-ne da yarepɛ mo, se a laam ba a yi‑m Giligal ne. A ná tua, a laam wó bere‑m kolo daa na wora se n ke to.”
Sɔɔl jigi Isarele tiina pɛ
9Sɔɔl déem na pipiri se o kɛ o daare Samuwel to, mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ o bochare leiri de ji bochare-doore. Dɛ dem konto ne woŋo maama seene ko ke ko maŋe dedaane Samuwel na tage tei to mo. 10Sɔɔl dedaane o tontoŋeno wom na dɛ ba yi Gibea to, mo ba nɛ Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ na beene se ba jeeri-ba. Wɛ jworo ma ba Sɔɔl baŋa dedaane dam. O ma to ba wone o tɔge o pworisa. 11Nɔɔna balo déem na yei Sɔɔl faŋa to ma na o na ke tei ye o pworisi to, ye ba bwei daane ba we, “Keitaa! Bɛ mo yi Kisi bu wom tento? Sɔɔl de ga tɔge o wo sampwori sem wone mo na?”
12Jei sem konto nɔɔno dedoa ma ta o we, “Se sampwori sento sem, á yei ba kwoa na?” Ko maama na ke tei to déem ma lɛɛre ko ji sinseira we, “Sɔɔl de laam tɔge o wo sampwori sem wone mo na?” 13Sɔɔl na pworisi o ti to, o laam ma bɛ o di zwoŋo baŋa wara-jei sem.
14Sɔɔl kwo choro wodwoŋi déem ma na Sɔɔl de o tontoŋeno wom ye o bwei-ba o we “Abam ya vei yei ne mo?” Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Dé ya kare dé beeri bonɛ sem mo. Dé nam na wo nɛ-se to, mo dé vei Samuwel tei.” 15O kwo choro kom ma ta o we, “Nam ta n bere-ne Samuwel na tage kolo dede‑m to.” 16Sɔɔl ta ma leiri o we, “O yɔɔre o ta debam mo we dé kɔ jworo, se ba nɛ bonɛ sem.” Ko daare, Sɔɔl wo sɛ se o ta kolo Samuwel na ŋɔɔne ded‑o paare dim ŋwaane to.
17Samuwel déem ma bwoŋi Isarele tiina bam maama se ba ba Mizipa ba jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. 18Ba na lage daane to, o ma ta de-ba o we, “Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora mo tento: Isarele tiina bam, amo mo jaane abam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne a ba ywo-seeni. Amo ta ma vere abam Ejipti tiina jeŋa ne, ye a jwoŋi abam a yage teene delo maama déem na bɛɛse abam to jeŋa ne. 19Abam Tu Wɛ ye wolo na yeini o vere abam á cham de á yaara maama wone to mo. De konto de, abam ta lɔge Wɛ kwaga ne mo ye á we, á lage pɛ se o taa wo á yiga ne. Konto ŋwaane nam ba-na á tigisi á tete Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, dwi de dwi, sɔ-yuu de sɔ-yuu.”
20Samuwel laam ma bwoŋi Isarele dwia yam maama se ba nwoŋi dwi de dwi ba zege o yiga ne. Wɛ ma kuri Benjamin dwi dem ba maama wone. 21Samuwel daa ma pa Benjamin dwi dem tutwoni de yi, sɔ-yuu de sɔ-yuu. Wɛ ma kuri Matiri sɔ-yuu kom ba wone. Se ko kweeli to, Kisi bu Sɔɔl mo Wɛ kuri Matiri sɔ-yuu kom wone. Nɔɔna déem ma vo ba beeri‑o ba ga. 22Ba na wo nɛ‑o to, ba ta ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ ba we, “Wonto ná seene o ye nɔɔno wom, o tu ywo-seeni na?” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Véi-na á nii. O seigi o tete mo zela yam wone.”
23Nɔɔna déem ma duri ba vo ba vaŋe‑o ba ja ba nwoŋi pwola. Sɔɔl na tu o zege nɔɔna bam tetare ne to, ba ma na we o zege wagele wagele mo, ye o dedɔrem dwoi nɔɔna bam maama. 24Samuwel laam ma ta de nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Nii-na, nɔɔno wonto mo Baŋa Wɛ kuri o pa abam. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera debam maama wone se kotu dwoni de wonto.” Nɔɔna bam maama ma kaase de kwor-dɛa ba we, “Wɛ wó pa dé pɛ wom momwɛ-dɛɛre.”
25Samuwel laam ma lwoni o bere nɔɔna bam se ba lɔre paare dim totoŋ-naga na wó taa ye tei maama to. O ta ma popone tento o ke tɔnɔ wone, ye o kwei-ko o tiŋi Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Konto kwaga ne mo o bane nɔɔna bam o pa ba jwoori ba sam. 26Sɔɔl de ma jwoori o vo o sɔŋɔ Gibea ne. Nɔɔna badwonna na ye babɛ to déem ma kwogili‑o ye ba tɔge‑o ba vo. Wɛ déem ya pɛ se banto boboŋa tɔge Sɔɔl mo. 27Nɔn-wo-korro tedwonna ba wo na ba ŋwae to de maa wora, ye ba ŋwaane ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto yi se o jwoŋi debam o yage na?” Ba na gwooni‑o konto to, ba wo sɛ se ba ja pɛɛra ba ba ba pa‑o. Sɔɔl ma chem.

english_text:
Saul Rescues the Town of Jabesh in Gilead
1About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
2Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
3The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
4Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying. 5Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen.
“Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked.
They told him what the men from Jabesh had said. 6Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious. 7Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!”
The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together 8at Bezek. Saul had them organized and counted. There were 300,000 from Israel and 30,000 from Judah.
9Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued.
Everyone was encouraged! 10So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
11The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
12The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
13“No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.”
Saul Is Accepted as King
14“Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
15Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_text:
Sɔɔl wane Amon tiina bam
1Amon tiina pɛ Nahasi déem lage o jar-keira o vo Jabese Gilead, se o li teo kom konto o jwoŋi o taa tei. Teo kom baara bam ma ta de Nahasi ba we, “Nam pa dé gwoni ni daane, se dé wó sɛ se n ta‑n tei debam.” 2O ma leiri-ba o we, “Amo beeri chaveera mo se a ke Isarele tiina bam yera ne. Konto to, á na lage se dé gwoni ni daane, ko nam jege se a chochɔrege a le nɔɔno maama jazem yi mo ywo-seeni, se a daare a gwoni ni de abam.” 3Teo kom nakwa bam ma ta‑o ba we, “Nam pa debam pwola se dé kwei da yarepɛ dé toŋe kwora Isarele tega kam maama ne dé beeri wolim. Dé ná beeri dé pwoli ye jwoŋinu ná wo tu se o vere debam n jeŋa ne o yage, dé laam wó ba dé sɛ‑m.”
4Nɔɔna badwonna ma ja kwora kam konto ba vo ba yi Gibea. Sɔɔl teo kom mo konto. Ba ma ta taane dem ba de Gibea tiina bam zwa ne. Ba de na nigi to, ba ma kaase bɔge-bɔge. 5Konto de Sɔɔl ya zege o kara ne mo o kale o nabɛ o maa jwoori sɔŋɔ. O na nigi sɔɔ kom to, mo o bwei o we, “Bɛ mo ke nɔɔna bam yera ne ye ba kaase konto ŋɔɔ?” Ba ma lwoni kwora kalo na nwoŋi Jabese ka ba to ba bere‑o.
6Sɔɔl na nigi to, Baŋa Wɛ jworo ma chu o baŋa de dam. O wo ma pɛ. 7O ma ja o nabɛ sem selei o go. O ta ma tore tore se nɔna yam mura-mura, ye o pa nɔɔna ja-ya ba jage se ya yi Isarele tiina maama. Nɔɔna bam ná yi jei selo maama, ba wó ta tento mo ba we, “Sɔɔl de Samuwel mo wora ba lae jar-keira ba ke daane. Wolo ná wo sɛ se o nwoŋi o tɔge ba kwaga, ba lage ba ke kotu ne ba na ke tei de nabɛ sento to mo.” Foone ma tiini de zo Isarele tiina bam Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane. Ba maama jilli ma nwoŋi se ba vo ba kwaare jara. 8Sɔɔl ma pa nɔɔna bam maama jeeri Bezeki ne. Ba na jeeli ba ni to, Isarele jar-keira bam déem ye nɔɔna morro bia yatɔ (300,000) mo. Judah jar-keira bam maa ye nɔɔna morro fintɔ (30,000).
9Sɔɔl de o kwaga nɔɔna bam ma toŋe Jabese teo nɔɔna se ba jwoori ba teo kom de kwora kanto: “Jwa we-bere maŋa ne, dé wó ba dé jwoŋi abam dé yage.” Nɔɔna bam na jaane kwora kam ba yi Jabese Gilead ye ba ta to, teo kom tiina wo ma pwoli dedɛ. 10De ko de, ba ta toŋe kwora Amon tiina bam tei ne mo we, “Ko ta wo á tei ne. Dé jwa wo á jeŋa ne, se á ke debam á na boŋe tei to.”
11Tega na lage ka poore to, mo Sɔɔl pɔɔre o jar-keira bam kuni betɔ. O laam ma pa ba nwoŋi ye ba pɔpɔ ba zaŋe Amon tiina kɔgɔ kom baŋa ne. Ba ma wane-ba, ye ba go ba dedɛ se ko vo ko yi wea berem maŋa. Balo fee na lugi to ma duri ba jage jei maama ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa wo tɔge de o dwoŋi.
12Isarele tiina bam ma yi Samuwel tei ba we, “Nɔɔna balo na gwooni Sɔɔl ye ba we, ko ya wo maŋe se o di paare debam baŋa ne to, ba wo yei ne mo? Nam pa debam chwoŋa se dé go-ba!” 13Sɔɔl maa wo sɛ ye o we, “Zem dɛ dento, yé go-na nɔɔn-nɔɔno! Kolo ŋwaane to, ko ye zem dɛ dem mo Baŋa Wɛ jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage.”
14Samuwel laam ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Pa se dé jwoori-na Giligal se dé kwɛ Sɔɔl paare dem se de da chwoŋa nɔɔna maama yia ne.” 15Ba maama ma seene ba vo Giligal. Ba ma fɔge ba tiŋi Sɔɔl paare dem wara-jei sem ne, ye ba daare ba ke yazura pɛɛra ba ma ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Jei sem konto ne mo Sɔɔl de Isarele tiina bam maama déem chake de wopwolo.

english_text:
Samuel's Farewell Speech
1Samuel told the Israelites:
I have given you a king, just as you asked. 2You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
3 Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
4“No,” the Israelites answered. “You've never cheated us in any way!”
5Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.”
“That's true,” they replied.
6 Then Samuel told them:
The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders. 7Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
8 After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land. 9 But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
10 Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
11 The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked. 12 Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
13You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king. 14If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn! 15If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
16Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power. 17Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
18Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel. 19They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
20Samuel answered:
Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart. 21Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble. 22But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
23I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right. 24You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you. 25But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_text:
Samuwel bane Isarele tiina bam
1Samuwel ma ŋɔɔne de Isarele tiina bam o we, “Amo seene a cheigi abam kwora woŋo kolo maama á na tage de amo to baŋa ne. A ma tiŋi pɛ se o taa nii á baŋa ne. 2Ko zege a nɔn-donne maŋa ne mo a wo abam yiga ne se ko ba ko yi zem. Leile konto a tiini a kwe ye a yuu peere. Amo bia laam ye baara mo, ye ba wo á wone. Pɛ wom laam leiri amo yuu ne mo, se o taa nii á baŋa ne. 3Nii-na ne da, a jale a tete mo Baŋa Wɛ dedaane o pɛ wom yiga ne. Ta-na chega: abam wɔ mo amo vere o nabea naa o bonaga? Wɔ mo a nam ke‑o swa a pini? A bɛɛse wɔ mo abam wone? Wɔ mo sugi amo yia de pɛɛre se ko kwoli o keim-balɔrɔ? Amo ná tusi tei kolo maama wone, se á ta á bere-ne, se a jwoori a yiri-te a pa abam.” 4Nɔɔna bam ma leiri‑o ba we, “Kɔtaa! Nmo wo pini debam, n ma‑n wo bɛɛse debam. Nmo ta wo fɔge n jwoŋi vwa pɛɛre nɔɔno tei ne.”
5Samuwel daa ma leiri o we, “Zem dɛ dento ne, Baŋa Wɛ de o pɛ wom zege amo chega kam kwaga ne we abam wo nɛ amo tusim kolokolo baŋa ne.” Nɔɔna bam ma leiri ba we, “Ɛɛ! Baŋa Wɛ zege ye o nia.”
6Samuwel daa ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we:
“Baŋa Wɛ déem mo kuri Moses dedaane Aron ye o tɔge banto baŋa ne o ja abam kwoa bam o nwoŋi Ejipti ne. 7Ta‑á zege konto, se a lage a bwɛ abam mo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, se ko tɔge dedaane Baŋa Wɛ na ke wo-kamunnu telo maama o ma jwoŋi abam de á kwoa bam o yage to. 8Jakob de o dwi tiina déem na jeini Ejipti ne to, mo abam nabaara bam déem keeri ba jare Baŋa Wɛ. Wɛ ma pa Moses de Aron vere-ba ba ja nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba ba ba zoore tega kanto á laam na tei to ne.
9De konto de, á nabaara bam ma ba ba swei ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom swia. Konto ŋwaane mo o ke-ba ba dona jeŋa ne. Ko ma pa se Sisera wolo na ye Hazora teo jar-keira bam yiga tu to, de Filisi tiina bam, dedaane Moaba pɛ wom de o nɔɔna bam wane á nabaara bam ba di jara wone. 10Á kwoa bam déem daa ma keeri ba jare Baŋa Wɛ ye ba we, ‘Debam tusi mo. Dé pipiri dé yage Baŋa Wɛ zula ye dé daare dé zuli Baal dedaane Asetare jwona yam. Nam jwoŋi debam n yage dé dona jeŋa ne, se dé laam wó jwoori dé taa zuli‑m.’ 11Baŋa Wɛ ma kuri Gideon, de Baraki, de Jefeta, dedaane amo, Samuwel o pa abam. Wɛ ma tɔge nɔɔna bam konto baŋa ne o jwoŋi abam o yage á dona bam maama jeŋa ne, se á ta‑á wae á zoore de yazura.
12Abam nam na yɔɔre á na Amon tiina pɛ Nahasi na lage o kwaare jara de abam to, mo á tage de amo á we, ‘Lage pɛ n pa debam, se o taa nii dé baŋa ne.’ Á tage konto ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ya mo maŋe o ye abam pɛ. 13Á nam nii-na á pɛ wom mo tento. O maa ye pɛ wolo á na lwoori Wɛ o ŋwaane ye Baŋa Wɛ kuri‑o o pa abam to. 14Nam seene-na yia á ta‑á kɔre Baŋa Wɛ se á daare á ta‑á zuli‑o ye á tɔge o chwei sem. Yé se-na á zwa á ve o nia yam. Abam maama de á pɛ wom ná tɔge á Tu Baŋa Wɛ konto dwoŋi, ko wó taa lana ko pa abam. 15Ko daare á na pɛ se á zwa se, ye á ve se á sɛ o nia yam, Baŋa Wɛ de wó lɔ abam de á pɛ wom kwaga ne mo.
16Nam ta‑á zege á na zege mɛ konto to, se Baŋa Wɛ wó ke wo-kamunu á yibia ne leile konto. 17Maŋa kanto dae te-pwoŋa mo na? Amo nam wó lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o pa doa ba ka taa baga ka wuura ye ka nena. Abam ná nɛ do-fɔrɔ kom, á wó maane we á tiini á sa chwoŋa ye á chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga mo, de á na tage we á lage pɛ to.”
18Samuwel na seene o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ to, Wɛ ma pa do-fɔrɔ ba ka baga ye ka nena dɛ dem konto ne. Ko ma pa nɔɔna bam maama tiini ba kɔre Baŋa Wɛ dedaane Samuwel. 19Ba ma ta de Samuwel ba we, “Pwopwo, ja n Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom teiŋa n pa debam se dé yé te. Debam laam seene dé lɔre we dé wɛleera yam daga, ye dé ta woli ya wone mo dedaane dé na we dé lage pɛ to.”
20Samuwel laam ma leiri-ba o we, “Chega to, abam seene á ke wo-balɔrɔ. Nam yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. Ko laam nam jege se á ta‑á tɔge Baŋa Wɛ de á wo maama mo, se á daa yé lɔ o kwaga ne. 21Yé zuli-na jwona. Yanto ba jege dam, ya nam bá wane abam ya jwoŋi ya yage cham wone. Ya ye wo-yɔɔro yerane mo. 22Baŋa Wɛ bá sɛ o ve abam balo na ye o nɔɔna bam to, o tete yere-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane. Kokuri to, wonto mo kuri abam se o pa á ta‑á ye o tete nɔɔna. 23Se ko ná ye amo, a ta wó taa lwoori Baŋa Wɛ a pa abam. Ko ya ná dae konto, a ya wó ke wɛleere mo. Amo za wó taa bere abam chwo-laaro telo na maŋe se á tɔge to. 24Ta‑á kɔre-na Baŋa Wɛ se á daare á ta‑á zuli‑o de á bochare maama. Guli-na wo-kamunnu telo maama o na ke o pa abam to. 25Nam ta‑á yei-na we, abam de á pɛ wom ná misi á yuni keim-balwaaro wone, Wɛ wó pa á yera maama saare tega baŋa ne mo.”

english_text:
Saul Disobeys the Lord
1Saul was a young man when he became king, and he ruled Israel for two years. 2Then he chose 3,000 men from Israel to be full-time soldiers and sent everyone else home. Two thousand of these troops stayed with him in the hills around Michmash and Bethel. The other 1,000 were stationed with Jonathan at Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin.
3Jonathan led an attack on the Philistine army camp at Geba. The Philistine camp was destroyed, but the other Philistines heard what had happened. Then Saul told his messengers, “Go to every village in the country. Give a signal with the trumpet, and when the people come together, tell them what has happened.”
4The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
5The Philistines called their army together to fight Israel. They had 3,000 chariots, 6,000 cavalry, and as many foot soldiers as there are grains of sand on the beach. They went to Michmash and set up camp there east of Beth-Aven.
6The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits. 7Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River.
Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear, 8 and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come. 9Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.”
Saul killed one of the animals, 10and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
11“What have you done?” Samuel asked.
Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash, 12and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
13“That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel. 14 But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.” 15Then Samuel left Gilgal.
Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had 600 men. 16Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin.
Jonathan Attacks the Philistines
The Philistine army was camped at Michmash. 17Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual. 18Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
19The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
20-21Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices. 22So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.

Sɔɔl ve Baŋa Wɛ ni dem
1Sɔɔl déem jege bena fintɔ mo ye o bobo se o di paare. O déem nam di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne bena finna-yalei mo.
2Sɔɔl déem ma kuri Isarele tiina bam wone nɔɔna morro tetɔ se ba taa wo o tei ne. Nɔɔna morro telei ma maŋe Mikimasa ne, ko woli de Bɛtel zwonnu laŋa kam ne. Nɔɔna moro de maa wo o bu Jonatan tei ne. Banto ma vo Gibea na wo Benjamin laŋa kam ne to. Sɔɔl ma pa Isarele tiina jar-keira balo maama na daare to jwoori ba sam.
3Jonatan déem ma vo Gibea mɛ Filisi tiina jar-keira kɔgɔ kodwoŋi na gilimi to. O na yi da to, o ma jeeri-ba de jara ye Filisi tiina bam maama ni ko ŋwa. Sɔɔl de ma pa ba wu nabwanno Isarele teo kom maama wone se Hiburu tiina bam nwoŋi jara keim ŋwaane. 4Isarele tiina bam ma ni we Sɔɔl mo wane Filisi tiina jar-keira kɔgɔ kolo na wo Gibea ne to o zeili. Konto nam mo pɛ Isarele tiina bam kikia maama lwoi Filisi tiina bam momwa ne. Isarele tiina jar-keira bam maama ma sɛ Sɔɔl kwora kam ye ba vo ba jeeri‑o Giligal ne.
5Filisi tiina bam de déem ma bwoŋi ba jar-keira bam se ba nwoŋi ba kwaare jara dedaane Isarele tiina bam. Ba jara torokooro déem ye morro tetɔ (3,000) mo. Balo na diini sisein-nɔɔna to maa ye morro teredo (6,000). Ba jar-keira maama ni déem ware de ga de ti. Ba daga dedɛ nenɛɛne naneo ni kasolo mo tei. Ba ma tɔge daane ba vo Mikimasa ba chwi ba vwoa da. Jei sem konto jeeri Bɛte-Aven wɛ-puli seeni mo. 6Isarele tiina bam ma na we ko tiini ko zo ba yera, Filisi tiina bam na jege-ba ba peene to ŋwaane. Ba ma duri ba vo ba seigi peero bɔɔna wone, de punnu wone, de gugworru wone, de gwonnu wone, de vola wone se ba wane ba lu. 7Ba badwonna bere ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ye ba zo Gad dedaane Gilead laŋa kam ne mo.
Sɔɔl ma maŋe Giligal ne. Foone ma ja nɔɔna balo na wo o tei ne to pa se ba yera sae pɔm-pɔm. 8O déem peene mo se o cheigi Samuwel na wó ba maŋa kalo to. O ma cheigi da yarepɛ ne Samuwel na tage tei to. Samuwel yuu na ba nae to, Sɔɔl nɔɔna bam laam ma bobo se ba jage ba daare‑o. 9Sɔɔl ma ga ga o we, “Ja-na zwɛɛm pɛɛra yam dedaane yazura pɛɛra yam á ba á pa-ne.” O na jwoŋi-te nɔɔna bam tei ne to, mo o kwei varem wom o wora o zwɛ o ma o ke kaanem. 10O na yɔɔre o ti kaanem dem to dedaane Samuwel dɛ o yi da. Sɔɔl ma vo se o jeeri‑o o daare o zaane‑o.
11Samuwel ma bwei Sɔɔl o we, “Bɛ mo konto n kea?” Sɔɔl ma leiri‑o o we, “Maŋa kalo nmo na pɛ se n ba to na yia ye n ta wo tu to, amo nɔɔna bam ya wora ba jage ba daare-ne. Filisi tiina jar-keira bam de ma jeeri daane Mikimasa ne se ba kwaare jara dedaane debam. 12Amo ya ta maa jege lwia we ba wó ba Giligal ywo-seeni ba zaŋe a baŋa ne, ye a ta wo lwoori Baŋa Wɛ zeinim jara yam ŋwaane. Konto to amo boŋe we ko fee mo se a ke lela a ke kaanem dem.”
13Samuwel ma ta o we, “Nmo tiini n toŋe jworim dedɛ. Nmo wo tɔge ni delo nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑m se n da to. N ya ná dɛ-de chekke, Baŋa Wɛ ya wó pa nmo de n dwi dem di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne, se ko taa vei wuu. 14Nam nii! N paare dem daa bá taa wora taa. Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o beeri o na nɔɔno wolo kikia na dɛ o wo to, ye o laam wó pa wonto mo taa nii o nɔɔna bam baŋa ne, nmo na wo dɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem to ŋwaane.”
15Samuwel ma zege Giligal ne o kwei o chwoŋa o maa kɛa. Nɔɔna balo ta na wo Sɔɔl tei ne to ma tɔge ded‑o ba vo Gibea na wo Benjamin laŋa kam ne to. Sɔɔl ma jeeli ba ni daane, o na we ba ta yi nɔɔna bia yaredo (600).
16Sɔɔl de o bu Jonatan dedaane ba kɔgɔ kom maama maa maŋe Benjamin teo Gibea ne ba tiga. Filisi tiina bam de maa maŋe Mikimasa ne ba tiga. 17Filisi tiina jar-keira badwonna ma zege ba na gilimi mɛ to ne ba pɔɔre ba tete kuni betɔ. Ba maa yeini ba nwoŋi se ba taa mage ba dona ye ba vere ba wonnu. Popɔra dedoa déem kwei Ofera chwoŋa kam na wo Suwali laŋa kam seeni to mo. 18Ba popɔra kadwoŋi de ma kwei Bɛte-Horon chwoŋa kam, ko daare ye popɔra kalo na daare to de kwei chwoŋa kalo na vei siseini dem laŋa ne, mɛ na maŋe de Zeboyim bwolo kom de kagoa kam to.
19Kanto maŋa kam ne, luru tera Isarele tiina teene dem maama wone. Kokuri to, Filisi tiina bam mo déem ya tage ba we, “Dé yé pa Hiburu tiina bam pwola se ba ke se-zɔɔro dedaane chichwoa ba ma daane debam.” 20Konto ŋwaane ko fee mo se Isarele nɔɔna maama vo Filisi tiina bam tei se ba dwori ba vaane, de ba dwoora, de ba sekware, de ba seene maama. 21Ko ná ye vaane, Filisi tiina bam maa yeini ba pa ba ŋwe sabu-dala yalei se ba dwori-de ba pa-ba. Ko daare ko ná ye dwoora, de pengasa, de chichwoa, ba wó ŋwe sabu-dale dedoa mo.
22Konto ŋwaane, dɛ dem na yi se Isarele tiina bam ke jara yam to, nɔɔno wolo maama na wo Sɔɔl de o bu Jonatan kwaga ne to ba jege se-zɔɔ naa chichwei o jeŋa ne. Sɔɔl de Jonatan yerane mo jege jara zela yam konto.
Jonatan kwaare jara de Filisi tiina
23Filisi tiina bam déem ma pa ba jar-keira kɔgɔ kodwoŋi vo ba che Mikimasa zwonnu chwoŋa kam.

1-3and Saul was in Geba with his 600 men. Saul's own tent was set up under a fruit tree by the threshing place at the edge of town. Ahijah was serving as priest, and one of his jobs was to get answers from the Lord for Saul. Ahijah's father was Ahitub, and his father's brother was Ichabod. Ahijah's grandfather was Phinehas, and his great-grandfather Eli had been the Lord's priest at Shiloh.
One day, Jonathan told the soldier who carried his weapons that he wanted to attack the Philistine camp on the other side of the valley. So they slipped out of the Israelite camp without anyone knowing it. Jonathan didn't even tell his father he was leaving.
4-5Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
6Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
7“Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
8“This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us. 9If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp. 10But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
11-12Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!”
Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
13Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind. 14Before they had gone 30 meters, they had killed about 20 Philistines.
15The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble.
Israel Defeats the Philistines
16Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax. 17Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
18At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.” 19Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
20Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
21There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
22Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
23-24So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day.
Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats
Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat.
By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger. 25-26The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
27Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert. 28Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
29Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert. 30I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
31By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon. 32They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood. 33 Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.”
“You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here. 34Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.”
That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there. 35It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord.
The Army Rescues Jonathan
36Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!”
The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.”
“Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
37Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?”
This time God did not answer. 38Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering. 39I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.”
No one said a word.
40Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.”
Everyone agreed.
41 Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?”
The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army. 42Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.”
The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned. 43“Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!”
“I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
44“Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
45“No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
46Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home.
Saul Fights His Enemies
47-48When Saul became king, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, the Philistines, and the Amalekites had all been robbing the Israelites. Saul fought back against these enemies and stopped them from robbing Israel. He was a brave commander and always won his battles.
Saul's Family
49-51Saul's wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz. They had three sons: Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. They also had two daughters: The older one was Merab, and the younger one was Michal.
Abner, Saul's cousin, was the commander of the army. Saul's father Kish and Abner's father Ner were sons of Abiel.
War with the Philistines
52Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_text:
1Dɛ dedwe mo Sɔɔl bu Jonatan tage de nɔn-doŋo wolo na yeini o zei o jara zela yam to o we, “Pa se dé bɛ dé vo mɛ Filisi tiina jar-keira bam na vei ba tigi to.” O nam wo pɛ se o kwo Sɔɔl lɔre ko ni ne.
2Sɔɔl déem maŋe Gibea teo kom laŋa kam seeni mo. O maa jei Pomegara tio kodwoŋi na wo Migoron ne to kuri ne. Jar-keira balo na daare ba maŋe o tei ne to maa ye nenɛɛne bia yaredo. 3Nɔɔna bam konto wone dedoa déem ye Ahituba bu Ahija. O maa ye Wɛ kaanem tu ye o jege kaanem gare-wogo kom. Ahituba déem ye Ikaboda choro de Finehase bu mo, ye o ta ye Eli naa. Eli déem ya ye Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tu Siloo ne mo. Nɔɔna bam maama nam wo lɔre we Jonatan nwoŋi ba tei ne.
4Chwoŋa kam na wo Mikimasa zwonnu tem ne ye Jonatan jeeli se o tɔge da o kɛ o vo o yi Filisi tiina jar-keira bam tei to, déem tigi pe-kamunnu telei tetare ne mo. Te dedoa yere déem mo ye Bozezi, ye kodwoŋi kom yere ye Senɛ. 5Peo dedoa déem jeeri baŋa seeni daa kam mo, ye ko yɔɔre Mikimasa. Kodwoŋi kom de maa wo tega-kuri seeni daa kam ne, ye ko yɔɔre Geba.
6Jonatan ma ta de nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara zela yam to o we, “Nam pa dé bɛ dé yi nɔn-kafɛ tento na wo mɛ to! Dɛ delo Baŋa Wɛ wó woli debam se dé wane-ba. Baŋa Wɛ ná lage o jwoŋi o nɔɔna bam o yage, kolokolo bá cheiŋi‑o. Dé ná daga naa dé ná muri de, ko maama ye bedwe mo Wɛ tei ne.” 7Nɔn-doŋo wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Ke kolo maama n na boŋe n ja se n ke to, se a zege n kwaga ne de a wo maama.” 8Jonatan maa we, “Nam pa dé fɔɔre dé vo dé bere dé tete Filisi tiina bam. 9Ba ná tage ba bere debam we, ‘Ta‑á zege-na á cheigi debam se dé beene á tei’, de wó maŋe da mo, de bá di dé yi ba tei. 10Ko daare ba ná tage we, ‘Titwoni-na á di peo kom á ba-na ywo-seeni’, dé wó di dé yi-ba mo. Konto wó bere we Baŋa Wɛ mo seene o kwei-ba o ke debam jeŋa ne.”
11Banto balei bam ma vo ba zege mɛ Filisi tiina bam na wó na-ba to. Filisi tiina bam ma ta ba bere daane ba we, “Nii-na! Hiburu tiina bam laam wora ba pi ba nwoŋi bɔɔna yalo ba ya na seigi da to wone mo.” 12Ba laam ma tɔɔle ba ta Jonatan dedaane nɔn-doŋo wom ba we, “Tutwoni á yi-na ywo-seeni, se dé wane dé bere abam woŋo.” Jonatan ma ta o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Ta‑n tɔge a kwaga n diini, se Baŋa Wɛ mo ke nɔɔna bam konto Isarele tiina bam jeŋa ne.”
13Jonatan laam ma gwane o di peo kom, ye o tontoŋeno wom tɔge o kwaga. O ma jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara o mage o de tega ne. O ná mage wolo o de tega ne, nɔn-doŋo wom wó tɔge o kwaga o go kotu. 14Ba na dɛ yiga ba jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara konto to, Jonatan de o tontoŋeno wom déem go nɔɔna finlei mo jeiga dedoa ne, ka wo gaale naba-laara fintɔ.
15Foone ma tiini de ja Filisi tiina jar-keira balo maama déem na wo pwola ne to, de balo na nwoŋi vero ŋwaane to, de balo na yere ba tigisim jei to, de ba teo kom nɔn-bia bam maama. Tega kam ma ziziŋi, kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ mo ke se foone dem konto taa wora.
16Sɔɔl nɔɔna balo na zege Gibea ne ba tole ba nii kolo na wora ko ke to ma na we, Filisi tiina bam jage mo ye ba duri jei maama ne. 17Sɔɔl laam ma ta o nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Jeeli-na dé nɔɔna bam maama ni, se dé lɔre balo na tere ywo-seeni to.” Ba na jeeli ba ti to, mo ba maane we Jonatan de nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara-keim zela yam to mo tera. 18Wɛ kaanem tu Ahija déem na jege kaanem zela yam o tei ne to, Sɔɔl ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ja gare-wogo kom n fɔɔre n yi ywo-seeni se dé bwei Baŋa Wɛ dé nii dé wó ke tɛ mo.” 19O ta na wora o ŋɔɔne de kaanem tu wom konto to, ba ma ni vuvuga sɔɔ na tiini ko zaŋe Filisi tiina bam tigisim jei sem ne. Sɔɔl ma ta‑o we, “Le n jeŋa gare-wogo kom ne. Maŋa daa tera se dé bwei Baŋa Wɛ dé nii.”
20Sɔɔl dedaane o jar-keira bam maama ma ke daane ba yɔɔre Filisi tiina bam jei sem se ba kwaare jara de-ba. Ba ma vo ba na we vuvuga tiini ka to Filisi tiina bam wone ye ba kwaare jara da-baŋa ne. 21Hiburu tiina balo ya na tɔge de Filisi tiina bam ba ke jara yam ba woli-ba to laam ma jwoori ba lɛɛne ba pu Isarele tiina balo na wo Sɔɔl de Jonatan tei ne to. 22Ko daare Isarele tiina balo ya na seigi Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne to de ma ba ba ni we, Filisi tiina bam kwaane ba duri se ba lu Isarele tiina jeŋa ne mo. Ba de ma nwoŋi ba tɔge ba pare-ba de fora. 23Ba déem pɛ Filisi tiina bam konto ba pu mo taa ba vo ba gaale Bɛte-Aven. Mo chwoŋa kalo wone Baŋa Wɛ déem na dɛ o ma o jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage dɛ dem konto ne to.
Jara yam kwaga kikia
24Dɛ dem konto ne mo Isarele tiina bam yera tiini ya bwona, kana na jege-ba to ŋwaane. Kokuri to, Sɔɔl déem ya dugi duuri mo ye o daare o pa ni dento o nɔɔna bam o we, “Wolo maama ná di wodiu zem ko lwoori wɛ-zoore maŋa ye a ta wo yiri a jene a dona bam baŋa ne, se sɔɔlem taa wo kotu yuu ne.” Ko ma pa se dɛ dem konto, o nɔɔna bam wolowolo wo laŋe wodiu o ni ne.
25Sɔɔl jar-keira bam maama ma tɔge gaao wone, mɛ teeni na gaale to ba kɛ. Ba ma na we tooro mo wora jei sem maama. 26Ba na dɛ da ba kɛ ye ba na tooro tem konto to, ba wolowolo wo laŋe-te. Sensɔla kam mo ba déem kɔre. 27Ko daare Jonatan déem wo nigi we o kwo dugi mo o pa nɔɔna bam. O ma kwei o nacheiga kam o twe o ma laŋe to-nuga. O laam ma weeri de o jeŋa o di. O yera ma daŋe, ye o ta wara. 28Nɔɔna bam dedoa ma ta de Jonatan o we, “Nmo kwo nam dugi mo o yage dé jar-keira bam baŋa ne we, ‘Lɛɛro taa wo wolo maama na wó di wodiu zem to baŋa ne.’ Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo dé maama bwona tento ye kana jege debam.” 29Jonatan ma ta o we, “Chega to, a kwo pɛ ko zo á maama yera chekke. Nii a na di tooro tem fenfee ye a jwoori a na dam tei! 30Dé nɔɔna bam ya ná nɛ chwoŋa se ba di wodiu kolo maama ba na vere Filisi tiina bam tei ne to, ko ya bá taa gare na? Tento ba ya wó na dam se ba go Filisi tiina bam dedɛ ba dwoni ba zem na go tei to.”
31Dento dɛ dem ne, Isarele tiina bam zege Mikimasa ne ba pare Filisi tiina bam taa ba vo ba yi Ayijalon. Ba na wane-ba ba ti konto to, dedaane ba yera yam bugi dedɛ kana ŋwaane. 32Ba ma ke lela ba pɛ wonnu telo ba na vere Filisi tiina bam tei ne to se ba na wodiu ba di. Ba ma go pei, de naane, de na-mɔre, ba daare ba jege nɔna yam ba buri ba di gweeni, ye vara bam jana wo lwoori ba lu tega ne.
33Nɔɔna ma ta Sɔɔl ba we, “Nii debam nɔɔna bam na ke wɛleere delo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Ba jege nɔna mo ba done de ya yera jana.” Sɔɔl ma ta o we, “Abam chɔge á chega de Baŋa Wɛ. Bibili-na kandwɛ-kamunu á ja á ba ywo-seeni á pa-ne.” 34O daa ma ta o we, “Véi-na á da nɔɔna bam wone á ta se ba maama ja ba naane dedaane ba pei sem ba ba ywo-seeni. Ba jege se ba go vara bam maama kandwɛ dem baŋa ne ba daare ba di ywo mo. Ko dae se ba done nɔna yam de ya yera jana ba ma ke wɛleere Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.” Tete dem konto ne, nɔɔna bam maama ma ja ba vara ba ba ba go dáane. 35Sɔɔl de ma lɔ kaanem bimbini se o ma o zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Mo bimbini delo o na dɛ yiga o lɔ o pa Baŋa Wɛ to.
36Sɔɔl ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Nam pa-na se dé vo dé pare Filisi tiina bam tete dento wone se ko taa nii te-pora maŋa ne. Dé wó go-ba ye dé daare dé vere ba zela. Dé yé daare nɔɔno dedoa de.” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ke kolo maama n na boŋe n ja se n ke to.” Kaanem yiga tu wom ma ta o we, “Yage-na se dé bwei Baŋa Wɛ se dé lɔre o boboŋa.” 37Sɔɔl ma bwei Wɛ o we, “A ja jara a jeeri Filisi tiina bam se n pa dé di-ba na?” Baŋa Wɛ maa wo leiri‑o dento dɛ dem ne.
38Ko ma pa Sɔɔl ta de Isarele jar-keira yiga tiina bam o we, “Á ba-na ywo se dé lɔre wɛleere dwi dɔ mo dé ke zem. 39A dugi dedaane Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na pae Isarele tiina di ba jara to a we, wolo maama na ke wɛleere dem to wó te mo. Ko ná maŋe ko ye amo bu Jonatan de, o bá lu.” O na tage konto to, ba maama wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo leiri taane.
40Sɔɔl laam ma ta de Isarele jar-keira bam o we, “Abam maama véi-na dáa á zege kɔgɔ dedoa, se amo de a bu Jonatan de zege ywo-seeni.” Nɔɔna bam ma sɛ ye ba we, “Ke kolo nmo na boŋe n ja se n ke to.” 41Sɔɔl ma lwoori Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom o we, “Popo, bere-ne woŋo kolo ŋwaane n na wo leiri debam lworo kom zem to. Ko ná ye amo, naa a bu Jonatan yiga mo, pa se Yurim kandwɛ dem bere. Ko nam ná ye Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom yiga mo, se n pa Tumim kandwɛ dem bere.” Jɔrɔ kom ma ja Jonatan de Sɔɔl, ye ko yage Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom. 42Sɔɔl daa ma ta o we, “Laam pa Wɛ kuri amo de a bu Jonatan tetare ne.” Jɔrɔ kom ma le Jonatan.
43Sɔɔl laam ma bwei o bu wom o we, “Nmo ke bɛ mo n sa chwoŋa?” Jonatan ma ta o we, “Amo mɛ a nacheiga ni mo a laŋe tooro fenfee a di. Konto to, a nam jege se a te mo na?” 44Sɔɔl ma ta o we, “Jonatan, lɛɛro taa wo amo yuu ne nenɛɛne a ná wo pɛ se n te!”
45Isarele jar-keira bam ma ta de Sɔɔl ba we, “Konto bá ke! Ko dae Jonatan mo jaane wɔnɔ-kamunu konto o ba o pa debam Isarele tiina bam na? Debam dugi de ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere dem we Jonatan yu-yua dedoa tete bá gɔ o yuu ne. Ko ye Wɛ mo woli‑o pa o ke kolo maama o na ke zem to!” Ko déem ke konto mo ye Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom jwoŋi Jonatan momwɛ ba yage, ye o daa wo tege.
46Sɔɔl laam ma yage Filisi tiina bam zeilim. Filisi tiina bam ma jwoori ba tete teo.
Sɔɔl na di paare ye o ke kolo to
47Sɔɔl na tu o di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne o ti to, o déem ke jara mo dedaane ba dona bam maama. Banto maa ye Moaba tiina, de Amon tiina, ko woli de Edom dwi tiina bam, de pwa balo na tei Zoba laŋa kam, dedaane Filisi tiina bam. O déem na jeeri balo maama to, o yeini o di-ba mo. 48Ko ta ná ye Amaleki tiina bam, o tiini o ke baare o wane-ba. Ko ma pa se o jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage balo maama déem na jege-ba ba vere to jeŋa ne.
49Sɔɔl déem jege bakeiri setɔ mo: Jonatan, de Isivi, dedaane Maliki-Sua. O bukɔ-kwea yere mo ye Meraba, bukɔ-balaŋa kam yere maa ye Mikaale. 50O kaane wom déem ye Ahimaazi bukɔ mo, o yere ye Ahinoam. Nera bu Abenera déem mo ye Sɔɔl jar-keira bam yiga tu wom. Nera nam ta ye Sɔɔl kwo choro mo. 51Sɔɔl kwo Kisi dedaane Abenera kwo Nera maama kwo mo ye Abiyeli.
52Maŋa kalo maama Sɔɔl na ŋwe to, tigura dedɛ ma ke Isarele tiina bam dedaane Filisi tiina bam laŋa ne. Sɔɔl déem ná maane we nɔɔno wolo dana ye o ta jege baare, o wó pa kotu da o zo o jar-keira kɔgɔ kom wone mo.

english_text:
Saul Disobeys the Lord
1 One day, Samuel told Saul:
The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord: 2 “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
3“Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
4Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were 210,000 troops in all, and 10,000 of these were from Judah. Saul organized them, 5then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack. 6Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.”
The Kenites left, 7and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt. 8Every Amalekite was killed except King Agag. 9Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak.
The Lord Rejects Saul
10The Lord told Samuel, 11“Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.”
Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night. 12Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
13Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
14“Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
15“The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
16“Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.”
“All right,” Saul answered.
17Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel. 18When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites. 19Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
20“But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation. 21All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
22“Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him. 23Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
24“I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead. 25Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
26“No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
27 As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore! 28Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you. 29Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
30Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
31Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord. 32Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!”
Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
33But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
34Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah. 35Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again.
The Lord Chooses David To Be King
The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ pɛ Sɔɔl paare dem ti
1Samuwel déem tage de Sɔɔl o we, “Ko ye amo mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ ni se a tiŋi nmo se n di paare o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. Konto to, cheigi kwora kalo Baŋa Wɛ na jege se o pa‑m to. 2Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ we:
‘A lage a waare Amaleki tiina mo ba déem na toŋe tei de Isarele tiina bam to ŋwaane. Maŋa kalo Isarele tiina bam na nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba maa beene to, Amaleki tiina bam chege ba chwoŋa ye ba jeeri-ba de jara mo. 3Konto to, vei n kwaare jara dedaane Amaleki tiina bam. Yɔɔre n chɔge-ba de ba woŋo maama. Yé ja ba ŋwaŋa. Go-na ba baara, de ba kaana, de ba bia, de ba bu-sese, ko woli de ba naane, de ba pei, de ba kona, de ba bonɛ.’ ”
4Sɔɔl ma bwoŋi o jar-keira bam o ke daane pa ba jeeri Telayim ne. Jar-keira morro fuga (10,000) mo nwoŋi Judah dwi dem ne. Nɔɔna morro bia yalei (200,000) de maa nwoŋi Isarele dwia yadaara yam ne. 5Sɔɔl laam ma da o kɔgɔ kom yiga ye ba vo Amaleki tiina teo kom. Ba ma vwɛ nabara kadwoŋi ne, ye ba cheigi se ba nwoŋi da ba zaŋe Amaleki tiina bam baŋa ne. 6Keni dwi tiina de déem zoore jei sem konto ne. Sɔɔl ma pa-ba kwora o we, “Maŋa kalo Isarele tiina bam na nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba maa kɛ to, abam kwoa déem ke-ba lanyerane. Konto to, zaŋe-na á vo yiga á daare Amaleki tiina bam, se a lage a chɔge ba maama mo. Ko nam dae se abam de da á te.” Keni tiina bam ma seene ba vo dáa ba daare Amaleki tiina bam.
7Sɔɔl laam ma jeeri Amaleki tiina bam de jara ye o di-ba. Jara yam bobo Havila ne mo ya vei taa ya yi Sura na wo Ejipti teo wɛ-puli seeni to. 8O ma ja Amaleki tiina pɛ Agagi ye o ta ŋwe. Se ko ná ye Amaleki teo nɔɔna bam maama, o go-ba mo nyɔ! 9Ko daare, Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam déem wo go pɛ Agagi. Ba ma yage teo kom vare-ŋona bam, naane de pei maama. Ba wo sɛ se ba go-te. Ko daare ko ná ye wo-kokware sem de telo na ba jege kuri to, ba yɔɔre ba chɔge tento maama mo nyɔ!
10 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Samuwel o we, 11“A wo chɔge mo, de a na pɛ Sɔɔl ji pɛ to. O lɔge amo kwaga ne mo, ye o ba sɛ se o ke a ni dem ne.” Samuwel wo ma pɛ, ye o tiini o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ tete dem maama ne o poore tega.
12Samuwel ma gwoni tega o zaŋe se o vo o beeri Sɔɔl jei. Ba ma ta ba bere‑o we, Sɔɔl vei Kamele mo, o nam chwi kandwɛ-kamunu mo o zege da se ko pa o na yere. Ba ta we, o na zege dáane to, o laam vei Giligal mo. 13Samuwel ma vo o yi Sɔɔl tei. Sɔɔl ma ware‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ swolim taa wo n yuu ne. Amo ke a tɔge Baŋa Wɛ ni dem chekke.” 14Samuwel ma bwei‑o we, “Chega? Bɛ nam daa mo ke ye a ni naane dem dedaane pei sem keira konto?” 15Sɔɔl ma leiri‑o o we, “Jar-keira bam mo vere vare-ŋona banto Amaleki tiina jeŋa ne ba ja ba se ba ma ke kaanem ba pa nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Ko daare kolo maama laam na daare to, dé yɔɔre dé chɔge-te mo kula!” 16Samuwel ma bage‑o o we, “Pu n ni konto, se a ta kwora kalo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ne diim tete ne to a bere‑m.” Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “A nam cheiga.”
17Samuwel laam maa we, “Nmo ya maŋe n nii n tete we, n dae kolokolo yiga da. De ko de, Baŋa Wɛ nam mo pɛ n ji Isarele dwi tiina bam maama yiga tu. O ma tiŋi‑m se n ta‑n ye ba pɛ. 18Wonto mo pɛ‑m totoŋe se n toŋe, ye o we n véi n yɔɔre n chɔge Amaleki tiina bam, ba na ye puseŋ-nyena to ŋwaane. O bere‑m se n ke jara yam taa se ko taa nii n na ti ba maama to. 19Bɛ nam mo ye n wo sɛ o ni dem? Bɛ mo ke ye n ke lela n vo n pɛ ba jejegero tem se n ta‑n jega? Nmo toŋe lwarem mo n chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga!”
20Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Ko ná ye chega, amo ke Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo chekke. A dɛ chwoŋa kalo o na toŋe-ne se a da to. A ma yɔɔre a chɔge Amaleki tiina bam, ye a daare a ja ba pɛ Agagi a ba ywo-seeni. 21Dé nam na di-ba to, mo a nɔɔna bam kuri pei selo na lamma to, dedaane naane delo na lamma to, ba le wonnu telo na maŋe de chɔgem to wone. Ba nam jaane-te ba ba Giligal ywo-seeni mo, se ba ma ba ke kaanem mo ba pa nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”
22Samuwel maa we, “Kɔ mo pwoli Baŋa Wɛ wo? N ná sɛ kwora kalo o na pɛ‑m se n ke to mo naa n ná zwɛ vara ye n pae pɛɛra n ma n ke kaanem n pa‑o mo, kɔ mo gara? Nii-ywo! N ná sɛ Wɛ ni, konto gare n ná ke kaanem delo dwi maama n pa‑o. 23N ná lɔge Wɛ kwaga ne, konto de yi-nɛɛre ye bedwe mo. Yi-dɛɛre-nyem dedaane jwo-kaano de maa ba gare daane. Nmo na ve Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam to, o de ve‑m we n daa‑n bá‑n taa ye pɛ.”
24Sɔɔl ma leiri Samuwel o we, “Chega to, amo ke wɛleere. A ve Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam. A wo sɛ nmo na bere-ne se a ke tei to. A nam ya kɔre a nɔɔna bam mo, pa a ke banto na lage tei to. 25A nam lwoori‑m se n yage a wɛleere n ma n chɛ-ne, se n daare n da dedaane amo se dé jwoori sɔŋɔ, se a daa wane a zuli Baŋa Wɛ.” 26Samuwel ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo bá tɔge‑m a jwoori. Kokuri to, nmo ve Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam pa o de ve‑m we, n daa‑n bá‑n taa ye Isarele tiina pɛ.”
27Samuwel laam ma pipiri se o viiri. Sɔɔl ma ja o gɔrɔ kom ni dem seeni ye ko kaare. 28Samuwel ma ta‑o o we, “Nii! Baŋa Wɛ zem jwoori o jwoŋi Isarele tiina paare dem na wo n jeŋa ne to mo o daare‑m. O ma kwei-de o pa n dwoŋi wolo na gare‑m to. 29Isarele tiina Nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ba fɔe vwa, o taane de maa ba gɔe de yaga. Kokuri to, o dae nabiin-zwona, se o taa zae o ni.” 30Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Amo seene a ke wɛleere. De konto maama de, yé pa a na a chaveera Isarele nakwa bam dedaane ba kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne. Nam jwoori n da de amo se a vo a zuli n Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.” 31Samuwel ma sɛ. O ma da de Sɔɔl o jwoori pa Sɔɔl vo o zuli Baŋa Wɛ.
32Samuwel laam ma ta o we, “Ja-na Amaleki tiina pɛ Agagi á ja á ba ywo-seeni.” Agagi ma zaŋe o vo o yi o tei de baare ye o boŋe o wone we, “Cham de toone daa bá yi-ne.” 33Samuwel maa we, “Nmo mɛ n se-zɔɔ mo n pa kaana dedɛ ga ba bia. Konto chwoŋa kam ne mo nmo de nu wó ga o bia.” O ma zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne o kwei o se-zɔɔ kom o cha Agagi mura-mura Giligal ne.
34Samuwel ma jwoori o vo Rama. Sɔɔl de ma jwoori sɔŋɔ o tete teo Gibea ne. 35Samuwel daa wo jwoori o vo o na Sɔɔl se ko yi o toone. Sɔɔl totoŋ-naga déem za pɛ Samuwel yiga nyɔne dedɛ. Baŋa Wɛ de wo déem chɔge mo de o na pɛ Sɔɔl di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne to.

english_text:
1 One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
2Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.”
“Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me, 3then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
4Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
5“Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
6When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
7 But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
8Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
9Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
10One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men. 11 Do you have any other sons?”
“Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.”
“Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
12Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
13Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on.
Samuel returned home to Ramah.
David Plays the Harp for Saul
14The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him. 15“It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him. 16“Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
17“All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
18“A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
19Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
20Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul. 21David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons. 22Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
23 Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_text:
Samuwel le David se o jwa ba o ji pɛ
1Dɛ dedwe mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Samuwel o we, “Amo maŋe a ve Sɔɔl we, o daa bá taa ye Isarele tiina pɛ. N nam wó keeri o ŋwaane taa se n vo n maŋe yei ne mo? Zaŋe n kwei n kwara kam n su-ka de nuga, se n daare n vo Jesse sɔŋɔ Bɛtelehem ne. Kokuri to, amo kuri o bia bam dedoa mo se o ji pɛ.”
2Samuwel maa we, “Amo wó ke tetɛ mo a vo a ke konto? Sɔɔl ná niga, o wó go-ne mo.” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Ja na-chwɛ n woli da, se n laam ta we n tu se n ke kaanem mo n pa Baŋa Wɛ. 3Ta daare n bwoŋi Jesse se o ba o taa wo kaanem dem wone. Amo wó bere‑m n na wó ke kolo ye a pa se n lɔre wolo a na kuri se o ji pɛ to. N ma n ná nɛ kotu mo n jege se n lwo nuga o yuu ne, se n tiŋi‑o paare.”
4Samuwel ma ke kolo Baŋa Wɛ na bere to, ye o vo Bɛtelehem. O na yi da to, teo kom nakwa ma nwoŋi ba jeeri‑o ye ba yera sae. Ba ma bwei‑o ba we, “Ko ye ywoni mo ye n vei n beene na?” 5Samuwel ma leiri-ba o we, “Ɛɛ, a tu de ywoni mo. Amo tu ywo se a ke kaanem mo a pa Baŋa Wɛ. Kwɛ-na á tete, se á ba á gwaane de amo se dé ke kaanem dem.” O ma vo o le Jesse de o bia bam pa ba kwɛ ba tete ye o daare o bwoŋi-ba se ba vo kaanem dem jeiga.
6Jesse dedaane o bia bam na yi da to, Samuwel ma na o bu-kwea Eliabi. O ma ta o wone we, “N nɛ naa n wo nɛ, baaro wonto na zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to mo ye wolo o na kuri se o tiŋi pɛ to.” 7Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Samuwel o we, “Yé jeeli n daŋe baaro wom yibia pwooni na ye tei to baŋa ne, naa o na ye nɔn-wagele to ne. Amo ve wonto mo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ ba nii wonnu o nae-te nenɛɛne nabiina na nae tei to. Nabiina nii ba nae pwooni yiga kam mo, Baŋa Wɛ nam nii o nae bochare-yi dem ne mo.”
8Jesse laam ma bwoŋi o bu Abinadaba o pa o vo Samuwel tei se o na‑o. Samuwel ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wo kuri wonto de.” 9Jesse daa ma toŋe Samma o tei ne. Samuwel ta maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ wo kuri wonto de.” 10Jesse bere o pa o bia barepɛ maama mo vo Samuwel tei ba da o yiga ne ba kɛ, ye Samuwel we, “Baŋa Wɛ wo kuri banto wolowolo.” 11O laam ma ga ga o bwei Jesse o we, “Nmo bia bam maama mo konto na?” Jesse ma ta o we, “Jeŋa-bu wom mo daare. Wonto nam wo pei sem kwaga ne mo o yere-se.” Samuwel maa we, “Toŋe n bwoŋi‑o se o ba. Wonto ná wo tu ywo-seeni, dé bá wane dé ke kaanem dem se dé di.”
12Jesse ma pa ba bwoŋi o jeŋa-bu David ye o ba. O maa ye lanno ye yazura yi‑o lanyerane. O yibia ta maa pwomma. Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Samuwel o we, “Zaŋe n lwo nuga o yuu ne, se wonto mo a kuri.” 13Samuwel ma kwei kwara kam de ka wo nuga o lwo David yuu ne, o chorro tem yibia ne. Sento nɛ sem ni ne mo Baŋa Wɛ Jworo chugi David baŋa ne de dam. Ko maa wo o tei ne taa, ko zege dɛ dem konto ne se ko taa via. Samuwel laam ma jwoori o vo Rama.
David toŋa o pae Pɛ Sɔɔl
14 Baŋa Wɛ Jworo ma nwoŋi ko daare Sɔɔl. Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o kwei jwori-lɔŋɔ o pa ko yeini ko daane‑o. 15Sɔɔl tontoŋena bam ma ta‑o ba we, “Dé maane we Wɛ mo pɛ se jwori-lɔŋɔ ba ko jege‑m ko daana. 16Pɛ, dé ye nmo tontoŋena mo. Konto, yage se dé beeri jei sem maama ne dé nii wolo na wae o tae kɔnɔ chekke to. Baŋa Wɛ ná pɛ se jwori-lɔŋɔ kom ba n baŋa ne ye kotu ná tage o kɔnɔ kom, nmo wo wó to.” 17Sɔɔl ma pa-ba ni o we, “Kwaane-na á beeri nɔɔno wolo na tae kɔnɔ lanyerane to á ja á ba á pa-ne.” 18Sɔɔl tontoŋena bam dedoa ma leiri o we, “Amo nɛ nɔɔno wodwoŋi, o ye Bɛtelehem tu Jesse bu mo. O yei kɔnɔ tam lanyerane. Nɔɔno wom ye babea ye o yei jara keim. O ni taane de ywomma, ye o yibia pwomma. Baŋa Wɛ maa wo o tei ne.”
19Sɔɔl ma toŋe kwora Jesse tei ne ye o we, “Nmo bu David wolo na yere n pei sem to mo a laga. Pa o ba a tei.” 20Jesse ma ja bonaga o daare o kwei bworobworo, dedaane lɔɔ de ko wo sana, de bo-chwɛ o daŋe ka baŋa ne. O ma toŋe o bu David se o ja o vo o pa Sɔɔl.
21Ko ke konto mo ye David da o zo Sɔɔl tontoŋena bam wone. Sɔɔl déem maa tiini o swoi David. O ma le‑o se o taa ye wolo na wó taa zei o jara zela yam to. 22Sɔɔl ma toŋe kwora o pa Jesse o we, “Amo wo tiini ko pwoli de n bu David. Konto to, yage se o maŋe a tei ne o taa toŋa o pa-ne.”
23Maŋa kalo maama Wɛ ná yeini o pa jwori-lɔŋɔ kom zo Sɔɔl, David wó ta o kɔnɔ kom mo. Konto ná yeini ko ke, Sɔɔl wo wó to mo, ye ko gara ko pa‑o. Jwori-lɔŋɔ kom maa yeini ko viiri ko daare‑o.

english_text:
Goliath Challenges Israel's Army
1The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah. 2-3King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
4The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall. 5-6He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about 57 kilograms. He carried a bronze sword strapped on his back, 7and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
8Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel:
Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me! 9If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves. 10Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
11Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing.
David Decides To Challenge Goliath
12David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons: 13-14the oldest was Eliab, the next was Abinadab, and Shammah was the third. The three of them had gone off to fight in Saul's army.
David was Jesse's youngest son. 15 He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
16Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for 40 days.
17One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp. 18And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right. 19They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
20David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry. 21The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
22David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well. 23While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
24When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off. 25They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
26David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
27The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
28David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
29“Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?” 30Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
31Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came. 32“Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
33“You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
34But David told him:
Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear, 35I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
36Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God! 37The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine.
“All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
38Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear. 39David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things.
“I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.”
David took off the armor 40and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath.
David Kills Goliath
41Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield. 42When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him. 43 “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods 44and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
45David answered:
You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
46Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God. 47Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
48When Goliath started forward, David ran toward him. 49He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps.
