When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground. 50 David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
51 David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head.
When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away. 52But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
53When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp. 54David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent.
David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
55After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?”
“Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
56“Then find out!” Saul told him.
57When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head.
Abner took David to Saul, 58and Saul asked, “Who are you?”
“I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_text:
Goliafe dwoni de Isarele jar-keira bam
1Filisi tiina bam déem ma la ba jar-keira bam ba ke daane. Ba ma vo Judah teo kolo yere na ye Sokoo to se ba kwaare jara da. Ba déem chwi ba vwoa Efese-Damima ne mo. Jei sem konto wo Sokoo dedaane Azeka tetare laŋa ne mo. 2Sɔɔl dedaane Isarele jar-keira kɔgɔ kom de déem ma vo ba chwi ba vwoa Ela bwolo kom ne ba tigi da. Ba maa wora ba ti ba yiga se ba jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara. 3Filisi tiina bam déem tigisi daane mo, ba zege zwoŋo dedoa yuu ne. Isarele tiina bam de maa zege zwoŋo kodwoŋi yuu ne, ye bwolo laam tigi ba maama tetare ne ko pɔɔre-ba daane.
4Filisi tiina bam déem nam ya jege ba babea kadwoŋi na nwoŋi Gafa to. O yere mo ye Goliafe. O ma nwoŋi ba tigisim jeiga kam se o dwoni de Isarele tiina bam. O dedɔrem déem dwoi jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni beredo mo. 5Channa yu-gwoŋo mo o déem yeini o ma o pu o yuu. Channa de mo ba déem mɛ ba sɔ o jara-keim gɔrɔ, ye ko dunni de déem tiini de gaale nenɛɛne kilo fuseredo (60) tei. 6Channa kam mo o mɛ o kwoli o nachere sem seeni. O ta jege channa se-zɔɔ mo o na peili o kwaga ne. 7Chichwei delo o déem na zei o jeŋa ne to tiini de duna de dwoi gare-yi sɔɔna da-kwolo na mae tei to. De yuu dedaane de ni-chechwaga kam tete dunni dem ye nenɛɛne kilo terepɛ (7). Nɔn-doŋo maa tɔge o yiga o zei o jara-keim nantana kam o via.
8Goliafe ma zaŋe o zege o bage Isarele tiina jar-keira bam o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo á maama wora á tigisi se á ke jara? Amo ye Filisi tiina bam babea mo. Abam de ye Sɔɔl jar-keira mo naa á dae? Le-na á wone nɔɔno dedoa, se kotu jeeri amo de jara. 9Nɔɔno wom konto ná wane amo o go, debam Filisi tiina maama wó ji abam kabɛ. Amo de daa ná wane kotu a go, abam de mo wó taa ye debam kabɛ ye á toŋe á pae debam. 10Amo nii Isarele jar-keira bam mo a gwooni. Le-na nɔɔno á pa-ne se dé jeeri daane de jara.” 11Sɔɔl dedaane o nɔɔna bam na nigi Filisi tu wom taane dem to, ba bochare ma di ye foone tiini de zo-ba.
David vei jara jei sem
12David kwo déem maa ye Eferata tu Jesse. Jesse déem nwoŋi Judah teo Bɛtelehem ne mo. O maa jege bakeiri nana. Sɔɔl paare dem maŋa kam ne to de Jesse kwe dedɛ mo. 13Jesse bu-kwe setɔ sem déem ya tɔge ba vo se ba woli Sɔɔl mo jara-keim baŋa ne. Eliabi mo ye ba maama nakwe, Abinadaba ma saŋe, ye Samma ye batɔ tu wom. 14David déem nam mo ye ba maama nyaane. O zembaara batɔ na vei ba wora ba woli Sɔɔl to, 15mo David yeini o vei sɔŋɔ Bɛtelehem ne ye o jwoora, se o taa nii o kwo pei sem baŋa ne.
16Goliafe lɛɛre o dole kandwona konto mo taa Isarele tiina bam yiga ne da finna, zezeŋa ne de dedaan-ni ne maama.
17Yanto da yam ne, mo Jesse tage de o bu David o we, “Kwei men-wɔa ywolo konto na maŋe de kuriwaa bu dedoa to, de bworobwooru fuga kanto, se n ke lela n ja n vo n pa n chorro tem na wo jara kapworo ne to. 18Nam ta kwei nayel-pepala banto fuga n woli da n vo n pa ba jar-keira yiga tu wom. Nmo laam ma‑n wó lɔre ko na ye tei n chorro tem yera ne, se n daare n ja taane n nwoŋi ba tei ne n ba se ko pa a kɔ jworo. 19Nmo chorro tem dedaane Isarele jar-keira bam maama nam wo Ela bwolo kom ne mo. Ba wora ba woli Sɔɔl mo se ba ke jara dedaane Filisi tiina bam.”
20David ma gwoni tega o zaŋe te-pora ni ne. O ma lage nɔɔno wodwoŋi o kwei pei sem o ke o jeŋa ne. O ta ma vɔ o zela yam o ke daane. O ma kwei chwoŋa o maa kɛa, nenɛɛne o kwo Jesse na maŋe tei o bere‑o to. O na dɛ dɛ o yi jara jei sem to, dedaane jar-keira bam de nwoŋi mo ba maa vei se ba chichei ba zege jara ŋwaane. Ba déem maa mage tiguri-kaasa. 21Isarele jar-keira bam dedaane Filisi jar-keira bam ma tigisi tigisi, ye ba yibia laam jeeri daane. 22David ma yage o wodiiru tem o pa wolo na nii jar-keira bam zela yam baŋa ne to. O laam ma duri o vo o yi jara yam yiga kam ne, ye o bwei o chorro tem kwaga. 23David déem ta zege o ŋɔɔne de o chorro tem mo, ye Goliafe na ye Filisi tiina bam babea to pi o nwoŋi. Wonto déem nwoŋi Gafa ne mo. O ma fɔɔre o nwoŋi dáa ne, ye o chichei o fɔge o zege. O daa ma bobo o toro tem. David ma ni o na twe Isarele tiina bam tei to. 24Isarele tiina bam na nɛ Goliafe konto to, ba duri mo o yiga ne, foone na tiini de ja-ba to ŋwaane.
25Isarele tiina bam déem maa ŋɔɔne da-tei ne ba we, “Nii-na nɔɔno wonto na yɔɔre o nwoŋi dɛ dɛ o gwooni debam tei! Pɛ Sɔɔl gwoni ni mo we, wolo maama ná go nɔɔno wonto, o wó pa kotu ŋweero dedɛ. O ta wó pa kotu mo o bukɔ se o ma o ke o kaane. Kotu sɔŋɔ tiina de daa bá taa ŋwe lampwoo.”
26David ma bwei balo na zege o tei ne konto to o we, “Nɔɔno ná zaŋe o go Filisi tu wonto, se chaveera yalo o na jege o ke de Isarele tiina bam to ti, bɛ nyɔɔre mo kotu wó na? Filisi tu wonto ye nɔn-kafɛ mo. O za ye wɔ mo se o taa zege o dwoni de Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ jar-keira bam?” 27Jar-keira bam ma tole taane dem ye ba ta kolo maama pɛ wom na wó ke o pa wolo na wó go Goliafe to ba bere David.
28David zemba-kwea Eliabi ma ni o na zege de nɔɔna bam o lare tei maama to. O bane ma tiini de zaŋe de David ye o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo tu ywo-seeni se n ke bɛ mo? Pei sem fenfee n na yage kagoa ne to, n pɛ wɔ mo nii-se? A lɔre n kamunni dem ni ne. Nmo paale n ba se n nii jara yam keim dem mo!” 29David ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo amo ke a ja a chɔge? Konto a yé bwei bwia de na?” 30O ma tutwoni o vo o jwoori o bwei nɔn-gɛ taane dem konto. Ba de ta ma pa‑o boboa nɔɔna bam leira yam.
31Nɔɔna badwonna ma ni David na ŋɔɔne tei to, ye ba vo ba lwoni ba bere Sɔɔl. Sɔɔl ma pa ba bwoŋi David. 32David na yi o tei ne to, o ma ta Sɔɔl o we, “Pɛ, ko ba jege se nɔɔn-nɔɔno taa kɔre foone de Filisi tu wonto. Amo ye n tontoŋeno mo. A wó vo a jeeri‑o de jara.” 33Sɔɔl ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo bá‑n wane n jeeri nɔɔno wom se á ke jara. Ta‑n yei we n ye bu mo. Filisi tu wonto nam maŋe o seŋe o nɔn-donne maŋa ne mo, o lɔre jara keim.”
34Ko ma pa David leiri o we, “A kwo, amo yeini a jege a kwo pei mo a nia. Nywoŋo naa kago-vara dwi maama ná yeini ko ba ko ja a vara bam dedoa, 35a yeini a duri a vo a yi-ko, a daare a mage-ko mo se a vere a varem wom ko ni ne. Nywoŋo kom konto laam ná yeini ko pipiri se ko ja amo, a yeini a to a gorege ko ba ne mo, ye a laam daare a go-ko. 36Amo go nywonnu dedaane kago-vara badwonna konto dwoŋi a na. Filisi tu wom de dae kolokolo. A wó go‑o de. Ko ya wo maŋe se o gwooni Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ jar-keira bam. 37Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na jwoŋi amo o yage nywonnu dedaane kago-vara babam jeŋa ne to mo. O ta wora se o jwoŋi-ne o yage Filisi tu wom jeŋa ne.” Sɔɔl laam ma ta de David o we, “Tɔ! Nam véi se Baŋa Wɛ wó taa wo n tei ne.”
38Sɔɔl déem kwei wonto tete jara gwaaro tem o zo David mo. O ma kwei channa yu-gwoŋo o ma pu o yuu kom, ye o ta kwei luu jara-keim gɔrɔ o ma kwoli o nyɔɔne dem. 39David ma kwei Sɔɔl se-zɔɔ kom o vɔ jara-keim gwaaro tem yera ne, ye o laam kwaane se o vo o nii. O na wo zo gwaaro tento dwoŋi o me to, veiŋa maa chamma ka pa‑o. O ma ta de Sɔɔl o we, “Jara zela yanto bá jwoŋi-ne, kokuri to amo wo toŋe de-te a na.” O ma lɔɔre te maama o tiŋi. 40O ma kwei o nayera da-lɔŋɔ kom, o daare o vo nabara ni ne o kuri kandwa-siswollu tenu. O ma de kandwa yam konto o nayera tampɔgɔ ne, ye o daare o kwei o napana, o laam maa vei se o jeeri Filisi tu wom.
41Filisi tu wom maa fofɔ o vei mɛmɛ o twɛ David. Nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara-keim nantana kam maa wo o yiga ne o via. 42Goliafe na yɔɔre o nii o na David to, o maane we o ye bu mo. O ma gwooni‑o de o na ye bu-pwola na ye lanno to ŋwaane. 43O ma bwei David o we, “N boŋe we a ye kukura mo na, ye n jege da-lɔŋɔ n beene amo baŋa ne konto?” O ma kwei o teo kom jwo-dɛɛra yam yera o ma o sɔɔle lwarem o yage David yuu ne. 44O ta ma ta o we, “Fɔɔre n yi ywo-seeni, se a ná wo kwei n ya-nɔna yam a pa zuna dedaane kago-vara se ba di.”
45David ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo jege se-zɔɔ de chichwei de kalaŋa mo n beene se n ma n jeeri amo de jara. Amo nam jege Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yere mo a beene n baŋa ne. O maa ye wolo na tei Isarele jar-keira bam maama to. Ko nam ye wonto yere mo n jege n gwoona. 46Zem dɛ dento, Baŋa Wɛ wó ke‑m a jeŋa ne. A wó mage‑m a de tega ne, ye a gwoni n yuu. Zem, a ta lage a kwei Filisi jar-keira ya-nɔna yam mo a pa wɛyuu zuna de kago-vara se ba di. Tega baŋa nɔɔna maama laam wó sɛ de chega we, Wɛ wora o na tei Isarele tiina bam. 47Nɔn-kɔgɔ kolo maama na jeeri ywo-seeni to wó lɔre we, Baŋa Wɛ ná lage o jwoŋi nɔɔna o yage, ko dae se-zɔɔ naa chichwei mo o mae o jwoŋi-ba o yaga. Jara yam ye Baŋa Wɛ mo tei-ya. Wonto nam wó wane abam maama o ke debam jeŋa ne.”
48Filisi tu Goliafe daa ta maa fofɔ o beene David tei ne. David ma duri o yɔɔre jara jei sem ne se o vo o jeeri‑o. 49O laam ma tore o le kandwɛ o tampɔgɔ kom wone. O ma kwei kandwɛ dem o ke o napana kam ne, ye o vuvugi-ka o dole o yage. Kandwɛ dem ma yɔɔre de vo de lɔ Goliafe tiri, de moore de zo da. Goliafe ma to tega ne, ye o yibia vwi tega ne.
50Mo ko na tu tei, David déem mɛ napana dedaane kandwɛ mo o ma o di Goliafe. O ma mage‑o o go ye ko dae se-zɔɔ mo o mɛ o go‑o. 51David ma duri o yi o zege Goliafe baŋa ne. O ta ma le Goliafe tete se-zɔɔ ko pwolo ne, o ma go‑o o daare o gwoni o yuu.
Filisi tiina bam na maane we ba babea kam tege to, mo ba maama pipiri ba duri se ba lu. 52Isarele jar-keira bam dedaane Judah jar-keira bam ma laare de tiguri-kaasa, ye ba daare ba pɛ Filisi tiina bam kwaga ba pu. Ba ma pare-ba konto taa ba vo ba kwaare Gafa ni ne dedaane Ekoron manchwo-peena ne. Filisi tiina dedɛ twa maa maŋe Saarayim chwoŋa kam yuu ne ba tigi tigi konto, se ko vo ko yi Gafa dedaane Ekoron ne. 53Isarele jar-keira bam na zeili Filisi tiina bam ba ti ye ba jwoori to, ba ma lu kolo maama na wo ba tiga jei sem ne to ba ja ba viiri. 54David ma ja Goliafe yuu kom o ja o vo Jerusalem, se ko daare Goliafe jara-keim zela yam mo o jaane yanto o zo o tiŋi o tete vwei wone.
55Maŋa kalo David ya na maa vei se o jeeri Goliafe to, mo Sɔɔl ŋɔɔne o taane de o jar-keira yiga tu wom, Abenera mo konto. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Nɔn-doŋo kom ye wɔ bu mo?” Abenera ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, ko na ye chega to, amo yeiri o kwo na ye wolo to.” 56Sɔɔl ma ta o we, “Nam véi n bwei se dé lɔre o na ye wolo bu to.”
57David na go Goliafe ye o zege jara pwola ne o jwoori o ba to, mo Abenera jaane‑o o ja o zo Sɔɔl tei ne. David ta jege Goliafe yuu kom mo o jeŋa ne. 58Sɔɔl ma bwei‑o o we, “A bu, n kwo ye wɔ mo?” David ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, amo ye Bɛtelehem tu Jesse bu mo.”

english_text:
1David and Saul finished talking, and soon David and Jonathan became best friends. Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself. 2From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
3Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends. 4Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
5David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers.
Saul Becomes David's Enemy
6David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps. 7 They sang:
Saul has killed
a thousand enemies;
David has killed
ten thousand!
8This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.” 9Saul never again trusted David.
10The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand. 11Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
12Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him. 13Saul put David in charge of 1,000 soldiers and sent him out to fight. 14The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles. 15This made Saul even more afraid of David. 16But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
17One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
18David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
19But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
20Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy, 21and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
22-23Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?”
“I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
24The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said. 25Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed 100 Philistines!” 26The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess.
King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out, 27David and his men left and killed 200 Philistines. David brought back the proof that Saul had demanded and showed it to him, so he could marry Michal. Saul agreed to let David marry Michal. 28King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David. 29But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
30The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_text:
David de Jonatan badwoŋo kom
1Sɔɔl dedaane David ma ti ba lara yam. Sɔɔl bu Jonatan bochare dedaane David bochare déem ma ba ya meeli daane. Jonatan maa jege David swono ne o na swoi o tete tei to. 2Ko déem zege dɛ dem konto ne, Sɔɔl lɛɛre o cheiŋi David mo pa o toŋe o pa‑o. David daa wo jwoori o kwo wom sɔŋɔ. 3Jonatan na swoi David ne o na swoi o tete tei to ŋwaane, o pɛ se ba gwoni ni mo daane. 4Jonatan ma lɔɔre o gare-bwora kam, ye o kwei-ka o pa David. O ta ma le o jara gwaaro tem o kwei o pa‑o, ko woli de o se-zɔɔ kom, de o taŋa kam, dedaane o tankila kam de.
5Sɔɔl déem ná toŋe David jei selo maama ne, ko yeini ko vei yiga lanyerane mo. Konto ŋwaane Sɔɔl ma pa‑o dam o jar-keira bam tetare ne. Sɔɔl keim dem konto ma pwoli nɔɔna bam maama wo, ye ko ta pwoli o nakwa bam de wo.
6David déem na go Filisi tu wom ye jar-keira bam maa jwoori sɔŋɔ to, mo kaana nwoŋi Isarele teene dem maama wone ba ba se ba jeeri Pɛ Sɔɔl. Ba maa leeni de wopwolo, ya ba sae. Ba maa jege senyɛ ba wɔe ye ba tae kwanno. 7Ba ma di ywoni ye ba leeni ba pa daane ba we:
“Sɔɔl go o dona bam
moro de moro mo.
Se ko ná ye David,
wonto ma go o dona bam
morro fuga de fuga.”
8Sɔɔl na nigi ba leiŋa kam to, o wo déem wo dɛ ka taane dem. O bane ma zaŋe. O ma jeeli o wone o we, “Ta‑n nii tei! Ba pɛ se David go nɔɔna morro fuga fuga mo, ye ko daare amo, a go moro moro yerane mo. Ko laam nam daare paare dem mo se ba jwoŋi ba pa wonto.” 9Ko na zege dɛ dem konto ne ko maa vei to, Sɔɔl déem daa ba jege David chega. O wo ta ma gweene de David keim maama.
10Tega déem na poore to, Wɛ ma pa jwori-lɔŋɔ ba ko jwoŋi Sɔɔl de dam. O maa wo o tete diga kam ne o kare o yirisa. David maa jege o kɔnɔ kom o tae ne o na yeini o ke tei to. Sɔɔl de maa zei chichwei o jeŋa ne. 11O ma boŋe o ja we, “A lage a dole‑o mo a tane de kabira kam.” O ma dole‑o kuni belei, ye David de liisi kuni belei wom maama.
12Sɔɔl déem ma kɔre David, kolo ŋwaane Baŋa Wɛ wo David tei ne mo ye o lɔ wonto kwaga ne. 13Sɔɔl ma le jar-keira moro o ke David kwaga ne ye o pa o nwoŋi da o tei ne. David de maa yeini o to o nɔɔna bam yiga ne ye ba vo jara-keim ne. 14O ná ke woŋo kolo maama, ko vei yiga mo lanyerane, Baŋa Wɛ na wo o tei ne to ŋwaane. 15Sɔɔl ma maane we David yɔɔre o di wɔnɔ o dona maama baŋa ne. Ko ma pa o tiini o kɔre David dedɛ. 16Se ko ná ye Isarele tiina bam dedaane Judah tiina bam, banto maama swoi David mo, o na tɔge ba yiga pa se ba di ba dona to ŋwaane.
David swo Sɔɔl bukɔ o ma ke o kaane
17Dɛ dedwe mo Sɔɔl tage de David o we, “Nii a bukɔ-kwea kam Meraba. Nmo ná jaŋe Baŋa Wɛ jara yam dedaane baare, ye n jege chega n pa-ne, amo de wó pa‑m Meraba, se n ma n ke n kaane.” Sɔɔl déem tage konto ye o boŋe o tete ne o we, “Amo bá ma a tete jeŋa a ma a go David. A nam wó pa Filisi tiina bam chwoŋa se ba go‑o.”
18David ma leiri Sɔɔl o we, “Amo ye wɔ mo ye a kwo dwi dem de ye bɛ mo Isarele dwia yam wone se a wane a ji pɛ bukɔ baro?” 19Maŋa kam ma ba ka yi se ba kwei Sɔɔl bukɔ Meraba ba pa David. Ba ma jwoori ba kwei‑o ba pa Mehola tu wodwoŋi, o yere na ye Adireli.
20Sɔɔl déem ta jege bukɔ wodwoŋi, o yere na ye Mikaale. O maa lage David ni taane. Sɔɔl na lɔre ko ni ne to, o wo ma pwoli. 21Sɔɔl daa ma boŋe o tete yera ne o we, “A ná kwei Mikaale a pa David se o ma o ke o kaane, a wó wane a tɔge o ŋwaane a gane David, se Filisi tiina bam na chwoŋa se ba go‑o.” O ma ta de David o we, “Pwola ta wora se n di amo bukɔ wodwoŋi.”
22Sɔɔl ma pa o nakwa bam ni se ba soge David boboŋa ye ba we, “N kikia yam su Pɛ wom yi mo. O nakwa bam boboŋa de dɛ‑m. Konto to, sɛ se n swo o bukɔ Mikaale n ma n ke n kaane.” 23Ba ma seene ba ta botare sem konto ba bere David, ye o leiri o we, “Abam ná wo lɔre! Á boŋe we ko ye mɔle mo se nɔɔno wane o ji pɛ bukɔ baro na? Amo dae kolokolo yiga da, ye a ta ye yiniga tu.”
24Sɔɔl nakwa bam ma lwoni kolo maama David na tage to ba bere‑o. 25Sɔɔl ma jwoori o ta-ba o we, “Ta-na á bere David we, ‘Filisi tiina bam na yaare pɛ dedɛ to, o ma lage se o ŋwe jene ba baŋa ne. Konto, pɛɛre delo yerane pɛ na lage se n pa‑o o bukɔ wom ŋwaane to mo ye Filisi tiina bi fwoli-twanno.’ ” Sɔɔl déem tage konto ye o boŋe se o ja Filisi tiina bam je mo o ma o go David.
26Pɛ nakwa bam ma jwoori ba ja pɛ kwora kam ba vo David tei. David na nigi to, o wo ma pwoli de taane dem, o na wó ji pɛ wom bukɔ baro to ŋwaane. Kadiri dɛ dem na lage de yi to, 27dedaane David lwoori o zaŋe de o nɔɔna bam ye ba vo ba go Filisi tiina bia yalei. O ma ja Filisi tiina fwoli-twanno tem o ba o jeeli te ni ne o bere Sɔɔl, se o wane o ji Pɛ tembaaro. Sɔɔl ma ga ga o kwei o bukɔ Mikaale o pa David se o ma o ke o kaane.
28Sɔɔl ma lɔre jaja we Baŋa Wɛ mo wo David tei ne. O ta ma maane we o bukɔ Mikaale seene o swoi David. 29Ko laam ma fɔge ko pa o tiini o kɔre‑o. Sɔɔl ma lɛɛre o done David taa, se ko yi o toone.
30Filisi jar-keira bam déem yeini ba tui ba ke jara mo de Isarele tiina bam ba ba yaga. Sɔɔl jar-keira yiga tiina bam maama wone David mo di Filisi tiina bam se ko dwoni ba maama. Ko ma pa David yere jage jei maama ne.

english_text:
Saul Tries To Have David Killed
1One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends, 2-3and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
4-5The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
6Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
7Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
8The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat.
Michal Helps David Escape
9-10One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
11 Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning.
Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!” 12She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off, 13Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
14The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
15Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
16When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
17“Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!”
She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!”
Samuel Helps David Escape
18Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
19Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
20Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
21When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them. 22Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?”
“At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
23Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village, 24 he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_text:
Sɔɔl na chuli David tei to
1Sɔɔl déem zaŋe dɛ dedwe mo o ta Jonatan dedaane o nakwa bam maama we, ba kwaane ba go David. Jonatan yiga déem nam maa tiini ka wo David wone. 2O ma vo o ta de David o we, “Amo kwo boŋe se o go‑m mo. Konto to, ta‑n jege n tete. Jwa zezeŋa ne, se n vo n seigi pwola ne n ta‑n wora. 3Amo wó da de a kwo se dé ba nmo na seigi mɛ to dé taa zega. A laam wó taa tɛ nmo taane ded‑o, se a nii o na wó leiri kolo to se a laam ba a ta a bere‑m.”
4Tega na poore to, Jonatan ma tei David o kwo Sɔɔl yiga ne. O ma ta de Sɔɔl o we, “Jan ja! Yé zaŋe n ke David n ja n chɔge, se o wo ke‑m lwarem. Chega to, kolo maama o na ke to ye se ko zeini nmo mo. 5Yé swei we o déem na vei se o go Goliafe to, ko ye o tete ŋwea mo o dole o yage. Baŋa Wɛ ma da wonto baŋa ne o di wɔnɔ o pa Isarele tiina bam maama. Nmo na nɛ konto to, n wo pwoli mo. Bɛ nam daa mo kea ye nmo lage se n ja nɔɔno wolo na wo ke kolokolo to n chɔge? Nmo ná go David, ko bá taa jege kuri.”
6Jonatan taane dem tiini de dwei Sɔɔl bochare. O ma du duuri o we, “Amo tɛ chega de ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere we, David daa bá te.” 7Jonatan laam ma bwoŋi David ye o ta kolo maama na ke o de o kwo laŋa ne to, o bere‑o. O déem ta jaane‑o mo o vo Sɔɔl tei, pa o toŋe o pa Sɔɔl nenɛɛne boboa kam ne o ya na maŋe o toŋe o pa‑o tei to.
8Ko kwaga ne, jara daa jwoori ya chu Isarele tiina de Filisi tiina tetare ne. David déem ma di-ba ye o fe-ba pa se ba duri o yiga ne.
9Dɛ dedwe mo Sɔɔl wo o sɔŋɔ ne, ye o zei chichwei o jeŋa ne. David maa wo o tei ne o jege kɔnɔ o tae. Baŋa Wɛ ma pa jwori-lɔŋɔ ba ko jwoŋi Sɔɔl. 10O ma kwaane se o dole David de o chichwei dem o tane kabira yera ne. David ma liisi pa se chichwei dem moore de maŋe kabira kam yera ne. Tete dem konto ne David ma duri o lu.
11Sɔɔl ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba gilimi David sɔŋɔ ba yere-ko tete dem konto, se tega ná poore, se ba go‑o. David kaane Mikaale ma kaane‑o o we, “Nmo ná wo ke lela n lage jei n vo, jwa ne n lage n te mo.” 12O ma ja David o pa o tɔge takworo ne o chu, ye o duri o lu. 13Mikaale ma daare o kwei jwoni o tiŋi David sara ne. O ma kwei boŋo koro o kwɛ kwɛ o ke yuu kom seeni, ye o laam kwei gare-jale o ma kwoli ko maama. 14Sɔɔl tontoŋena bam na zo sɔŋɔ kom se ba ja David to, Mikaale ma ta de-ba o we, David weele mo. 15De konto maama de, Sɔɔl toŋe-ba mo se ba jwoori ba vo ba na David yera. O maa we, “Ja-o-na á ba ywo-seeni de o sara kam maama, se a go‑o.”
16Nɔɔna bam na jwoori ba vo ba na to, ba maane we jwoni yerane mo tigi sara kam ne, ye boŋo koro mo wo jwoni dem yuu seeni. 17Sɔɔl na lɔre kolo na ke to mo o bwei Mikaale o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n gane-ne, ye n pa a dono wom chwoŋa se o duri o lu?” Mikaale ma leiri‑o o we, “David tage o we, a ná wo yage chwoŋa a pa‑o se o lu, o wó go-ne mo.”
18David déem na duri o lu konto to, o ma vo Samuwel tei Rama ne. O ma tole kolo maama Sɔɔl na ke‑o to o bere Samuwel. Ba laam ma da daane ba vo Nayofi ba zoore da. 19Nɔɔna ma vo ba ta de Sɔɔl ba we, “David wo Rama teo kodwoŋi ne mo, ko yere ye Nayofi.” 20Sɔɔl na nigi konto to, o ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba ja David. Ba na yi da to, ba ma na Wɛ sampwori sedwonna na zege ba pworisa, ye Samuwel wo ba yiga ne. Baŋa Wɛ jworo ma chu Sɔɔl nɔɔna bam maama baŋa ne. Ba de ma da ba to pworisim ne. 21Ba ma ta ba bere Sɔɔl kolo na ke to. O daa ma toŋe nɔɔna badwonna. Ba na yi da to, ba de bobo se ba taa pworisa mo. O daa ta ma toŋe nɔɔna o ke kuni betɔ, ye ba de to pworisim ne.
22Sɔɔl tete laam ma zaŋe o kwei Rama chwoŋa, se o da ba kwaga. O na vei o yi vole-kamunu kom na wo Seku ne to, mo o bwei nɔɔna o we, “Samuwel dedaane David wo yein-seeni mo?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ba wo Rama teo Nayofi ne mo.”
23Sɔɔl ta na wo chwoŋa ne o maa vei Nayofi to, Wɛ jworo ma chu o de baŋa ne. O maa pworisi o via konto taa o vo o yi Nayofi. 24O na yi Samuwel tei to, mo o lɔɔre o gwaaro, ye o ta wora o pworisa dɛ dem maama wone. O ma tigi da tete dem konto maama ne, se tega ba ka poore. Ko déem ke konto mo ye ba seeri sinseira kam ba we, “Sɔɔl de tɔge o wo sampwori sem wone mo na?”

english_text:
Jonathan Helps David Escape
1David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
2“My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
3“Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
4Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
5 David answered:
Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day. 6If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
7If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me. 8Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
9“Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
10“How will you do that?” David asked.
11“Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered.
When they got there, 12Jonathan said:
I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you. 13But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise.
I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father. 14-15 Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
16Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
17Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend. 18After this Jonathan said:
Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty. 19By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock. 20I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock, 21and send my servant to find the arrows.
You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!” 22But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go. 23But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
24So David hid there in the field.
During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat 25by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty. 26Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
27The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
28-29Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
30Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born. 31You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
32“Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
33Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David. 34Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
35In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along 36and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.”
The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him. 37When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?” 38Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!”
The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan, 39but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew. 40Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
41After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder. 42Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.”
David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_text:
Jonatan na woli David tei to
1David déem ma zege Rama teo Nayofi ne o duri se o lu Sɔɔl, ye o daare o vo Jonatan tei. O ma bwei Jonatan o we, “Amo bere a ke bɛ mo a chɔge ye n kwo kwaane se o go-ne? Bɛ lwarem mo a ke‑o?” 2Jonatan ma leiri‑o o we, “Wɛ bá sɛ se ko ke konto. Nmo bá‑n te. Amo kwo bá ke woŋo ye o wo tage o pa a maane ko ni ne. Ko ná maŋe ko ye wo-balaŋa naa wo-kamunu, o yeini o ba seigi-ne. Ko bá wane ko ke konto!”
3David ma ta o du ye o we, “Jonatan, ko seene ko ye chega mo we n kwo beeri se o go-ne mo. O nam yei we nmo yiga tiini ka wo amo wone. Mo kokuri o wo pɛ se n lɔre o boboŋa, o na ba lage se o chɔge nmo wo to ŋwaane. Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane, de nmo tete yere ŋwaane we, amo tiini a bwola de toone.” 4Jonatan maa we, “Nmo na lage se a ke kolo maama to, a wó ke a pa‑m.”
5David ma leiri o we, “Nmo yei we jwa ne mo chan-doŋa kuri dem di. Ko maa jege se a taa tɔge a wo balo na jeini dedaane pɛ ba di wodiu to mo. Nam sɛ se a vo pwola a seigi da se ko vo ko yi jwa yiga dedaan-ni ne. 6Nmo kwo ná maane we a tera ye o bwei a bwia, se n ta we, ‘David ya lwoori chwoŋa mo a tei ne se o ke lela o vo Bɛtelehem o woli de o diga tiina se ba tɔge daane ba ke kaanem, nenɛɛne ba na yeini ba ke bene maama wone o sɔ-yuu kom maama ŋwaane to.’ 7Tɔ. Nmo ná tage konto, ye n kwo ná we, ‘Ko lamma’, ta‑n yei we kolokolo bá yi-ne. Se n taane dem baŋa ne, o bane ná zaŋe, lɔre se o boboŋa jaane se o go-ne mo. 8Ja! Nam ke woŋo konto n pa-ne, debam na ke ni-sɛɛm daane Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to ŋwaane. Nmo nam daa‑n ná maane we a seene a ke lwarem mo, se nmo tete go-ne. Yé ja-ne n vo n pa n kwo.”
9Jonatan ma leiri o we, “Wɛ bá sɛ se ko ke konto. Amo ya ná maane we a kwo boboŋa jaane se o go‑m mo, a ya bá ta a bere‑m na?” 10David ma bwei‑o o we, “Konto to, n kwo ná leiri nmo de ban-zɔŋɔ, wɔ mo wó pa se a lɔre ko ni ne?” 11Jonatan maa we, “Pa se dé nwoŋi dé vo pwola kam wone.” Ba ma tɔge daane ba kɛ.
12Ba na zege da konto to, Jonatan ma ta de David o we, “Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom taa ye maana tu debam balei laŋa ne we, ko ná ke da yalei, amo wó bwei a kwo a lɔre o boboŋa na ye tei de nmo to. O boboŋa yam ná lamma, a wó pa n maane. 13O boboŋa nam ná jaane se o chɔge‑m, a ta wó pa‑m kwora, ye a daare a yage chwoŋa a pa‑m se n duri n lu. Baŋa Wɛ nam wó pa se ko tiini ko ni amo, nenɛɛne a ná wo ke kolo a na we a wó ke to. Amo ta lwoori Baŋa Wɛ mo a pa‑m, se o taa wora dede‑m nenɛɛne o déem na wo amo kwo tei ne tei to. 14Amo de lwoori‑m se n yé swei a swia. Amo ta ná ŋwe, ta ta‑n jege amo swono kom, ne Baŋa Wɛ na jege debam swono tei to. Amo nam ná tege de, 15se n ta ta‑n jege amo bia bam swono se ko taa vei wuu. Baŋa Wɛ ná tu o ba o chɔge nmo dona bam maama pa se ba yera saare logo baŋa ne, se n yé yage swono kom konto de a dwi dem.”
16Jonatan déem tɔge konto mo o ma o fɔge o ke ni-sɛɛm dedaane David de o dwi dem. O ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se David dona bam maama bere‑o chega.” 17Jonatan ta ma pa David tɔge o swono kom baŋa ne o du duuri ba ni-sɛɛm dem ŋwaane. Kokuri to, o déem tiini o swoi David mo nenɛɛne o na swoi o tete tei to.
18Ko kwaga ne, Jonatan ma ta de David o we, “Jwa dɛ dem mo ye chan-doŋa kuri dem. Nɔɔna bam wó lɔre we nmo tera, nmo jeiŋa jei sem na wó taa zege kafɛ to ŋwaane. 19Tega daa na wó poore to, se n zaŋe n kɛ yiga yiga n vo mɛ n na seigi boboa kam ne to, se ko maŋe dedaane Ezeli kandwɛ dem teiŋa ne. Laam ta‑n cheigi-ne dáane. 20Amo ná tua, a wó kwei a taŋa a ke nenɛɛne a lage a ta chena mo a jeeri kandwɛ dem konto. Chena yatɔ mo a wó ma a ta. 21A maa wó pa bu wolo na wo a tei ne to vo o beeri che-tɛɛra yam. Amo ná tage de bu wom a we, ‘Nii mo! Chena yam wo n saŋa kanto ne mo ya twɛ ywo-seeni. Kwei-ya n ja n ba.’ Se n ta‑n yei we ko ye yazura mo. Konto, n wó wane n nwoŋi n na seigi mɛ to n ba. Kokuri to, ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane kolokolo bá ke‑m. 22A nam daa ná tage de bu wom a we, ‘Chena yam wo nmo yiga ne mo ya kɛ ya gaale‑m,’ se n lage jei n duri n viiri. Konto ye se n lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ‑m chwoŋa se n viiri. 23Nam yé swei debam balei ni-sɛɛm dem swia! Baŋa Wɛ mo ye maana tu debam laŋa ne taa wuu, se dé wane dé ke dé su ni-sɛɛm dem.”
24David déem ma vo o seigi pwola kam ne. Chan-doŋa kuri dɛ dem na yi to, pɛ Sɔɔl ma jeini de o dedɛɛra bam se o di kuri dem wodiu. 25O ma jeini o na maŋe o yeini o jei mɛ to ye o sale kabira. Jonatan ma jeini o jeeri‑o. Abenera de ma jeini Sɔɔl takeiri ne. Ko daare ye David jeiŋa jei sem mo tigi kafɛ. 26Sɔɔl ma na, ye o wo tage kolokolo dɛ dem konto ne. Kokuri to o ya boŋe we, “Dɛ delo woŋo mo chege David yiga pa se o wo tu. Tento o lage o kwɛ o tete se ko maŋe de chullu tem mo, se o laam ba o di kuri dem.” 27Tega daa na poore chan-doŋa da yalei dɛ dem ne to, Sɔɔl ma maane we David daa ta tera. O ma ga ga o bwei o bu Jonatan o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye Jesse bu wom wo tu se o di kuri dem wodiu diim dedaane zem maama?”
28Jonatan ma leiri‑o o we, “David seene o lwoori chwoŋa mo amo tei ne se o liisi fee o vo Bɛtelehem. 29O tage de amo we, ‘Ja! Debam diga kam mo jege kaanem se dé ke dé ma di kuri dé teo kom ne. Amo zembaaro ma toŋe o bwoŋi-ne. Nam sɛ dé badwoŋo kom ŋwaane, se n pa a vo se a jwoori.’ Konto ŋwaane nam mo pɛ se David zem tere ywo-seeni se o di wodiu nmo tei ne.”
30Sɔɔl na nigi Jonatan na tage kolo to, o bane ma zaŋe o baŋa ne ye o we, “Nmo dae amo bu chekke! N jege yi-dɛɛre ne n nu mo tei! A maane we n lɔge amo kwaga ne, ye n daare n tɔge Jesse bu David kwaga mo. Nmo na ke tei to ye n tete de n nu wom chaveera mo. 31Ta‑n yei we Jesse bu wom ta ná ŋwe, nmo bá wane n di ywoni. N bá‑n na chwoŋa se n di paare dem. Ke lela n toŋe nɔɔna se ba ja‑o ba ba ywo-seeni, se o jege se o te mo!” 32Jonatan ma leiri o kwo o bwei o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo o jege se o te? O ke kɔ mo o ja o chɔge?” 33Konto baŋa ne mo Sɔɔl kwei o chichwei o dole Jonatan se o kwaane o go. Jonatan laam ma maane we Sɔɔl seene yia mo se o go David. 34Jonatan ma pɛ o zaŋe wodiu kom baŋa ne de ban-zɔŋɔ, ye o daa wo di kolokolo chan-doŋa da yalei dɛ dem ne. O wo déem ma tiini ko chɔge de o kwo na jege kolo o toŋe David yera ne to.
35Tega na poore to, Jonatan ma zaŋe o da dedaane bu o vo pwola kalo David na seigi to, ne ba na maŋe ba bane ba tiŋi tei to. 36O ma ta de bu wom o we, “Duri n vo n twɛ che-tɛɛra yalo a na wó ta tento to n ja n ba n pa-ne.” Bu wom na bobo se o duri to, mo Jonatan vaŋe taŋa o ta chene o pa de gaale‑o de kɛ yiga ne. 37Bu wom na yi chene dem na to jei selo ne to, Jonatan ma tɔɔle o ta‑o o we, “Ta‑n via! Chene dem kɛ de wo n yiga ne mo.” 38O ta ma tɔɔle o we, “Ke lela! Yé ta‑n zega! Ta‑n via!” Bu wom ma twɛ chene dem ye o jwoori o pa o tu wom. 39Bu wom nam wo lɔre keim dem konto kuri. Jonatan dedaane David yerane mo yei kolo na wora to. 40Jonatan laam ma kwei taŋa kam de ka chena yam o pa bu wom. O ma ta‑o se o ja-ya o jwoori teo kom wone.
41Bu wom na kɛ o daare to, David ma zaŋe kandwa yalo kwaga ne o ya na seigi to, o nwoŋi o vo o yi Jonatan tei ye o daare o vwi o yibia tega ne kuni betɔ. O de Jonatan ma kukwori daane ye ba keera. David nam mo tiini o keeri o dwoni Jonatan. 42Jonatan laam ma ta de David o we, “Wɛ taa wo n tei ne! Za n yé swei we dé ke ni-sɛɛm mo daane Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane we, Baŋa Wɛ ye maana tu debam balei laŋa ne, dedaane dé dwia yam laŋa ne se ko taa vei wuu.” Ba na ŋɔɔne ba ti to, David ma zaŋe o kɛ. Jonatan de ma jwoori o vo teo kom wo.

english_text:
Ahimelech Helps David
1 David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
2“I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else. 3Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
4“The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
5“Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
6 The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
7It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
8David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
9 The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.”
“It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!”
David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
10David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish. 11 The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing,
‘Saul has killed
a thousand enemies;
David has killed
ten thousand’?”
12 David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish. 13 So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
14“Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me? 15I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_text:
Sɔɔl na tɔge David nɛ tei to
1David déem ma vo Nobi. Wɛ kaanem tu maa wora, o yere mo Ahimeleka. David na tu o tei to, Ahimeleka ma nwoŋi se o jeeri‑o ye o yera sae. O ma bwei David o we, “Bɛ mo ye n vei n yerane ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba tɔge dede‑m?” 2David ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ mo toŋe-ne. O nam we a yé pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre ni delo o na pɛ-ne to. Ko ná ye a nɔɔna bam, a tage de-ba se ba taa cheigi-ne jei sedwoŋi ne mo. 3N jege wodiu n tei ne na? Lage bworobwooru tenu naa woŋo kolo maama dwi n na jege to n pa-ne.”
4Kaanem tu wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Bworobworo kolo yerane na wo amo tei ne to ye kolo na yeini ko tigi da Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane to mo. Nmo de n nɔɔna bam nam ná wo peini de kaana da yanto ne, á wó wane á kwei-ko á di.” 5David maa we, “Chega to, debam de kaana wo yi daane. Amo nɔɔna bam ná maŋe ba yeini ba beeri yɔɔ yerane mo de, ba wó taa cho ba tete de kaana Wɛ ŋwaane. Konto laam na ye wo-chɛɔ to, ko tiini ko ke dwono mo!”
6Kaanem tu Ahimeleka ma kwei bworobworo kolo ya na tigi da Wɛ ŋwaane to o pa David. Bworobworo kom konto nam yeini ko wo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne mo. Ba maa yeini ba jwoori ba kwei-ko ye ba daare ba leiri ba tiŋi bworobworo-loŋo da. Konto to, bworobworo kolo ba na jwoori ba kwei Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to yerane mo wo kaanem tu wom tei ne. 7Sɔɔl tontoŋeno dedoa déem maa wora, o yere na ye Doegi. O maa ye Edom tu ye o kwori o ye Sɔɔl nayera bam yiga tu. Dɛ dem konto ne wonto déem wo Ahimeleka tei ne, o na jege se o kwɛ o tete Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to ŋwaane.
8David ta ma bwei Ahimeleka o we, “Nmo wó ta‑n jege chichwei naa se-zɔɔ n tei ne na? Pɛ wom tontoŋa kam tiini ka lomma mo pa se a wo nɛ pwola se a kwei a se-zɔɔ kom. A maa ba jege jara zele de zele.” 9Ahimeleka ma leiri o we, “Se-zɔɔ kodwoŋi wora. Ko ye Filisi tu Goliafe wolo nmo déem na go Ela bwolo kom ne to nyem mo. Ko nam kukuli de gɔrɔ ko tigi a gare-wogo kom kwaga ne. N ná lage-ko se n kwei. Se-zɔɔ kodwoŋi daa tera.” David ma leiri o we, “Se-zɔɔ tera ko na dwoi-ko. Amo wó jwoŋi-ko.”
10Dɛ dem konto ne David déem ma zaŋe o duri se o lu Sɔɔl yiga ne. O ma vo o yi Gafa teo pɛ Akisi tei. 11Pɛ Akisi dedɛɛra bam na nɛ David to, ba ma ta de Akisi ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto ye David mo, ba teo pɛ wom. Ko dae konto na? O teo kom nɔɔna bam yeini ba sae ye ba leeni ba seini‑o mo ba we:
‘Sɔɔl go o dona bam
moro de moro.
Se ko ná ye David,
wonto ma go o dona bam
morro fuga de fuga.’ ”
12David na nigi konto to, o ma jeeli nɔɔna bam taane dem maama, ye ko pa foone tiini de ja‑o de Gafa teo pɛ Akisi. 13Konto ŋwaane, David na yeini o wo ba tei ne to, o maa ke nenɛɛne o yirisi mo. O déem kare o ke yuu-vuvuga kikia mo, ye o jege ba teo kom manchwoŋo ni bworru o kwɛɛra yɔɔ yɔɔ ye o beiri te yera ne. O ta maa yage o twana yam pa se o lileeru nwoŋi te bɔɔre ya maama. 14Pɛ Akisi ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam wo nɛ we nɔɔno wonto ye chichwoo mo na? Bɛŋwaane mo á nam jaane‑o á ba amo tei? 15Amo gɛ chichwooru mo ye á ja‑o á ba amo tei na? A ba lage se wonto taa wo a sɔŋɔ ne o jege-ne o daana!”

english_text:
People Join David
1 When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there. 2A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of 400 men.
3David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.” 4So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
5One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest.
Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
6Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him. 7He told them:
Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done. 8But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
9 Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub. 10Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
11Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came, 12Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.”
“Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
13Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
14“Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him. 15This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
16“Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
17Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!”
But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
18Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!”
On that same day, Doeg killed 85 priests. 19Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep.
Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
20Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David 21and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
22David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me. 23Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_text:
David seigi o tete Sɔɔl tei ne
1David déem ma zege Gafa teo kom ne, o duri o vo o seigi peo kodwoŋi bɔɔne wone. Jei sem konto bwola dedaane Adulam teo mo. O chorro de o sɔŋɔ tiina bam maama na nigi we o wo dáane to, ba ma vo o tei. 2Ko ta woli da, nɔɔna balo maama na wo cham wone to, de balo na jege nɔɔna jena to, ko woli dedaane balo maama ŋwea na ba ywomma to maama ma la ba vo David tei ne. Ba maama kɔgɔ déem ye bia yana mo. David ma ji banto maama yiga tu.
3David déem ma zege dáane o vo Moaba teo Mizipa. O ma ta de Moaba pɛ wom o we, “A lwoori‑m mo se n pa a kwo dedaane a nu taa wo nmo tei ne, se ko taa nii a na tu a lɔre Wɛ na jege kolo se o ke o pa-ne to.” 4David ma ja-ba o vo o yage Moaba pɛ wom sɔŋɔ ne. Ba maa wo pɛ wom tei ne maŋa kalo maama David déem na kare o seigi o tete jei sem konto ne to.
5Dɛ dedwe Wɛ sampwora Gaadi ma ba o ta de David o we, “Daa‑n yé maŋe gugworo kom ne ywo-seeni! Zaŋe n nwoŋi n vo Judah.” David ma pɛ o zaŋe o vo o zoore Herefa kagoa kam wone.
Sɔɔl pɛ ba go Nobi teo kaanem tiina
6Sɔɔl déem maa wo Gibea teo zwoŋo kodwoŋi yuu ne. O maa jei sana kuri ne, ye o zei chichwei o jeŋa ne. O dedɛɛra bam maama maa kaare‑o ba zega. Sɔɔl laam ma ba o lɔre we ba nigi David ŋwa mo. 7O ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam, Benjamin tiina bam, á boŋe we Jesse bu David ná di paare, o ta wó taa yei á ni ne, se o pa abam kare de kadwi ye o daare o pa á taa wo o jar-keira bam yiga ne na? 8Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo á ke ni daane se á lɔ amo kwaga ne na? Amo tete bu Jonatan mo ke ni dedaane Jesse bu wom se ba chɔge-ne, ye abam wolowolo wo pɛ se a lɔre ko ni ne. Abam bere we á yiga tere amo wone. Amo bu wom maŋe o soge a tontoŋeno pa se o kwaane o na pwola o go-ne, ye á wo tage á bere-ne!”
9Edom tu Doegi de déem tɔge o wo Sɔɔl nɔɔna bam tei ne. O na nigi Sɔɔl na tage kolo to, o maa we, “Maŋa kam a na wo Nobi ne to, mo a nɛ Jesse bu wom na tu Ahituba bu Ahimeleka tei. 10Ahimeleka ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ se o lɔre David yiga na ye tei to. O ta pɛ David wodiiru, ye o daare o kwei Filisi tu Goliafe se-zɔɔ kom o woli da o pa‑o.”
11Sɔɔl na nigi konto to, o ma toŋe o bwoŋi Ahimeleka dedaane o sɔŋɔ tiina maama se ba ba o tei. Banto déem ye Wɛ kaanem tiina mo Nobi teo ne. Ba maama na yi Sɔɔl tei to, 12o ma ta o we, “Ahituba bu, cheigi ywo!” O de ma leiri o we, “Pɛ, a cheiga.” 13Sɔɔl ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye nmo sɔ ni dedaane Jesse bu wom, se á ke á chɔge-ne? Nmo pɛ‑o wodiu, de se-zɔɔ, ye n ta ma‑n sɔɔle Wɛ n kwɛ o chwoŋa. Konto ma pa se o lɔ amo kwaga ne, ye o zem tɔge amo nɛ tento se o go-ne!”
14Ahimeleka ma leiri pɛ wom o we, “Pɛ, nɔɔn-nɔɔno tere nmo tontoŋena bam wone ye o jege chega o pa‑m nenɛɛne David na jege nmo chega tei to. O ta maa ye n bukɔ baro. Babɛ selo na yere nmo to maama wone, o wo ba yiga ne mo. O ta maa jege yere nmo sɔŋɔ kom maama wone. 15Chega to, ko dae dento dɛ ne mo a bobo se a sɔɔle Wɛ a pa‑o. A nam ke a chɔge mo na? Yé ja taane dento n jeeri amo de a sɔŋɔ tiina bam, se amo yeiri taane dem kolokolo ni ne.”
16Sɔɔl ta maa we, “Ahimeleka, nmo dedaane n dwi dem maama jege se á te mo.” 17O ma ta de balo na zege ba yere‑o to o we, “Zaŋe-na á go Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam! Kokuri to, ba sɔge ni dedaane David se ba chɔge-ne. Ba maane we David maa duri se o lu amo mo, ye ba wo tage ba bere-ne.” Pɛ dedɛɛra bam maa wo sɛ se ba ma ba je ba dwei Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam.
18Sɔɔl ma pipiri o ta de Edom tu Doegi o we, “Nmo nam zaŋe n go Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam!” Doegi ma seene o mage-ba o go. Wɛ kaanem tiina funɔnɔ banu mo tege de dɛ dem konto ne, ye ba maama zoore kaanem gare-wogo kom mo. 19Sɔɔl ma vo Nobi teo kom, mɛ kaanem tiina bam na zoore da to. O ma go teo kom nɔɔna bam maama. O pɛ ba go baara, de kaana, de ba bia, ko bere ko woli bu-sese de mo. Ba ta ma go ba naane, de ba bonɛ, ko woli de ba pei maama.
20Wolo yerane déem na lugi to mo ye Abiatara. O maa ye Ahimeleka bu mo, ye o kwo-nakwe ye Ahituba. O ma duri o vo o woli David kɔgɔ kom wone. 21O ma lwoni o bere‑o Sɔɔl na go Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam tei to. 22David ma leiri‑o o we, “Dento dɛ dem a na maŋe a na Doegi na wora to, a maane we o wó vo o ta o bere Sɔɔl o na nɛ kolo to. Abam sɔŋɔ kom maama na tege to, ko ye amo yiga mo. 23Konto ŋwaane, ta‑n wo amo tei ne. Yé ta‑n kɔre foone. A yei we Sɔɔl beeri debam balei mo se o go. Nmo nam ná wo amo tei ne, cham bá yi‑m.”

english_text:
David Rescues the Town of Keilah
1One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
2David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?”
“Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
3But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
4David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
5David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
6-8Meanwhile, Saul heard that David was in Keilah. “God has let me catch David,” Saul said. “David is trapped inside a walled town where the gates can be locked.” Saul decided to go there and surround the town, in order to trap David and his men. He sent messengers who told the towns and villages, “Send men to serve in Saul's army!”
By this time, Abiathar had joined David in Keilah and had brought along everything he needed to get answers from God.
9David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
10David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me. 11Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.”
“Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
12David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?”
“Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
13David and his 600 men got out of there fast and started moving from place to place. Saul heard that David had left Keilah, and he decided not to go after him.
Jonathan Says David Will Be King
14David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
15One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him. 16But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David. 17“Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
18 They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh.
David Escapes from Saul
19 Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon. 20If you come, we will help you catch him.”
21Saul told them:
You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you. 22Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky. 23Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
24The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert. 25Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert.
Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him. 26Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men, 27when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
28Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
29David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_text:
David jwoŋi Keila teo kom o yage
1Dɛ dedwe mo ba tage ba bere David ba we, “Filisi tiina bam mo vei se ba ke jara de Keila tiina. Ba nam vere ba mena ye ba ta wora ba fere-ya mo.” 2David ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A véi a jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara na?” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Zaŋe n vo n jeeri-ba se n jwoŋi Keila teo ba jeŋa ne n yage.”
3David nɔɔna bam ma ta‑o ba we, “Nii dé na maŋe dé wo Judah laŋa kam ne mo ywo-seeni, ye dé fona de Filisi tiina bam. Se dé laam nam ná lage dé jeeri-ba Keila ne, ko bá taa ye lɛɛro ko pa debam na?” 4David daa ma vo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se o bwei o lɔre o na wó ke tei to. Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Nam véi Keila leile konto, se amo wó ke Filisi tiina bam nmo jeŋa ne se n di-ba.”
5David de o nɔɔna bam ma zaŋe ba vo Keila ba jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara. Ba ma wane-ba ye ba vere ba vara ba ja ba viiri. Ba ma go Filisi tiina bam dedɛ, ye ba daare ba jwoŋi Keila tiina bam ba yage. 6Ahimeleka bu Abiatara déem ya na duri o vo David tei Keila ne to, o ya kwei Wɛ kaanem gare-wogo kom mo o woli da.
7Sɔɔl déem ma ni we David vei Keila mo o wora. O ma ta o we, “Wɛ laam mo kwei David o ke amo jeŋa ne, kokuri to o vei o pe o tete mo teo kolo ba na yeini ba ma bworru kamuna ba pe ko nia yam to wone.” 8Sɔɔl ma bwoŋi o jar-keira bam se ba la daane, ba vo ba gilimi teo kom ba ke tetare ne, se ba daare ba ja David de o nɔɔna bam.
9David na nigi we Sɔɔl boboŋa jaane mo se o ba o ja‑o to, o ma ta de Wɛ kaanem tu Abiatara o we, “Kwei kaanem gare-wogo kom n ja n ba, se dé ma dé lɔre Wɛ boboŋa na ye tei to.” 10David laam ma lwoori Wɛ o we, “Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom, amo nigi we Sɔɔl lage o ba ywo-seeni mo o chɔge teo kom amo ŋwaane. 11A lage a bwei a nii, Sɔɔl wó seene o ba ywo, ne amo na nigi tei to na? Keila tiina bam wó ja amo ba kwei ba ke o jeŋa ne na? Popo a lwoori‑m se n pa a lɔre ko na wó ke tei to.” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Sɔɔl wó ba.” 12David daa ma bwei o we, “Se Keila tiina bam, ba wó kwei amo de a nɔɔna bam ba ke Sɔɔl jeŋa ne na?” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Ɛɛ, ba wó kwei abam ba pa‑o.”
13David na nigi konto to, o dedaane o nɔɔna bam ma ke lela ba duri ba nwoŋi Keila ne. Ba maa kare ba vei jei selo maama ba na wó wane ba vo to. Sɔɔl na nigi we David daa tere Keila ne to, o ma leiri o boboŋa ye o wo vei da.
David lugi Sɔɔl jeŋa ne
14David déem maa wo Zifi kagoa kam ne o seigi zwonnu laŋa kam gugworru tem wone. Sɔɔl de ma yɔɔre o beeri‑o mo se o wane‑o o ja. Wɛ maa wo pɛ se Sɔɔl na o jei.
15David déem wo Zifi kagoa kam jei sedwoŋi ne, Horesi ne mo. O na wora to, o ma maane we Sɔɔl nwoŋi o ba se o go‑o. 16Sɔɔl bu Jonatan de nam ya vei Horesi. O ma vo David tei, o daare o pa o na baare Baŋa Wɛ dam ŋwaane. 17Jonatan ma ta‑o o we, “Yé ta‑n fona, se a kwo Sɔɔl bá yi‑m o ja. O maŋe o yei we, nmo mo lage n ta‑n ye Isarele tiina Pɛ, se amo laam saŋe n kwaga a taa wo n takeiri ne.” 18Banto balei daa ma ke ni-sɛɛm Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se ba taa jege chega ba pa daane. Konto kwaga ne mo Jonatan jwoori o vo sɔŋɔ. David maa maŋe Horesi ne.
19Zifi tiina badwonna ma zaŋe ba vo Sɔɔl tei Gibea ne. Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Pɛ, David tu o seigi debam laŋa kam Horesi zwonnu tem ne. O wo Hakila peo kom na wo Jesimon tega-kuri seeni to yuu ne mo. 20Nmo na kwaane n beeri‑o se n ja to, nam lage dɛ se n ba dé teo kom, se dé ja‑o dé ke nmo jeŋa ne.”
21Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Á ke chega. Baŋa Wɛ swolim taa wo á yuu ne, de á na lage a lanyerane to! 22Nam ta kwaane-na á woli-ne fee. Jwoori-na á vo á lɔre o na wo mɛ chekke to, dedaane nɔɔna balo na nɛ‑o dáane to. Amo nigi we o tiini o wae o peperega. 23Véi-na á fɔge á beeri á lɔre o seigim jei sem maama, se á laam ba á ta á bere-ne jaja. Ko kwaga ne, a laam wó da de abam a vo. O ta ná wo laŋa kam konto ne, a wó beeri a na o jeiga. Ko ná maŋe ko ye se a beeri Judah sɔ-yuni tem maama wone mo de, a ta wó ja‑o.”
24Nɔɔna bam ma ke lela ba lwoori Sɔɔl ba vo Zifi, ye Sɔɔl laam saŋe kwaga o yi da. David de o nɔɔna bam déem ya seigi Maon kagoa kam ne mo. Ba maa wo Araba bwolo kom na wo Jesimon tega-kuri seeni to ne mo. 25Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam ma nwoŋi se ba beeri David jei. David de ma ni Sɔɔl ŋwa. O de o nɔɔna bam ma vo peo-kamunu kodwoŋi na wo Maon kagoa kam ne to ba seigi da. Sɔɔl ma lɔre David na wo mɛ to. O ma vo Maon kagoa kam ne o pu o kwaga vira-vira. 26Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam maa wo peo kom daa dedoa ne mo ba via. David de o nɔɔna bam de maa wo ko daa kadwoŋi ne ba kwaane se ba lu Sɔɔl jeŋa ne. Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam ma daare fee se ba yi David de o nɔɔna bam tei se ba li-ba. 27Ko nɛ ni ne mo nɔɔno duri o vo o yi Sɔɔl tei ye o we, “Ke-na lela á ba! Filisi tiina bam mo chugi ba puri debam teo kom baŋa ne!”
28Sɔɔl ma ga ga o yage David zeilim. O ma jwoori o pipiri se o vo o jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara. Konto ŋwaane mo ba jege jei sem konto yere ba bwoi we ‘Popɔra Peo’. 29David déem ma zege dáane o vo En-Gedi o seigi jei sem konto ne.

english_text:
David Lets Saul Live
1When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi. 2Saul led 3,000 of Israel's best soldiers out to look for David and his men near Wild Goat Rocks at En-Gedi. 3 There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself.
David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave. 4They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.”
David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing. 5Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that, 6-7 and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.”
Saul left the cave and started down the road. 8Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance.
Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low 9and said:
Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you? 10You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!” 11Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
12I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you. 13An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
14 Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea. 15I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
16“David, my son—is that you?” Saul asked. Then he started crying 17and said:
David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you. 18You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance. 19If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
20I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that. 21Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
22So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_text:
David yage Sɔɔl o pa o lu
1Jara yalo déem na wo Sɔɔl dedaane Filisi tiina bam tetare ne to ma ti. Sɔɔl na jwoori sɔŋɔ to mo o nigi we David wo En-Gedi kagoa kam seeni. 2O ma kuri jar-keira morro tetɔ Isarele tiina bam wone, balo na yei jara laŋa chekke to. O ma ke-ba o kwaga ne ye ba nwoŋi ba vo se ba beeri David de o nɔɔna bam jei. Ba ma vo ba yi peero tedwonna seeni ba na bwoi-te we ‘Kagoa wo bone peero’ to.
3Ba na wo chwoŋa ne to, mo ba yi jei selo nayera na yeini ba pe ba pei da to. Peo bɔɔne maa wora de na bwola de chwoŋa kam ni. Sɔɔl ma ywori o zo bɔɔne dem wone se o fo fea. Peo bɔɔne dem konto ne mo David de o nɔɔna bam de déem seigi. Banto nam jwoori ba wo yiga ne mo dáa dáa. 4David nɔɔna bam na nɛ Sɔɔl to ba ma ta de David ba we, “Nii pwola na tigi jaja ka pa‑m tei! Zem dɛ dento mo ye dɛ delo Baŋa Wɛ na tage de taane, de o na taga we, o wó kwei n dono wom o ke n jeŋa ne se nmo ke‑o n na lage tei to.” David ma vwɛ konto mɛmɛ o vo o ja Sɔɔl gɔrɔ kom kuri seeni o gwoni, ye Sɔɔl yeiri ko ni ne.
5Ko kwaga ne mo David boboŋa daane‑o dedɛ de kolo o na ke to. 6O ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó che se amo kwei a jeŋa a ma a ke wolo na tei amo to zonne. Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo kuri‑o. Wɛ wó che se a chɔge a tu wom, kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ swolim nuga mo wo o yuu ne.” 7Taane dem konto mo David mɛ o kuni o nɔɔna teiŋa, ye ko che pa se ba wo ke Sɔɔl kolokolo. Sɔɔl ma zaŋe peo bɔɔne dem wone o nwoŋi se o kɛ.
8David de laam ma pi o nwoŋi peo bɔɔne dem wone ye o zege dáa ne o bwoŋi Sɔɔl o we, “Pɛ! Amo tu, denlei!” Sɔɔl ma pipiri se o nii. David ma vwi o yibia tega ne o pa‑o zula, 9ye o ta o we:
“Amo kwo, bɛŋwaane mo n kare n cheigi balo na tɛ ba we amo kwaane se a chɔge‑m to taane? 10Nmo zem nɛ we, n na zo peo bɔɔne dem wone to, Baŋa Wɛ kwei nmo o ke amo jeŋa ne mo. A nɔɔna bam badwonna ya we dé go‑m mo, ye amo wo pɛ-ba chwoŋa. Amo ma ta-ba a we, ‘A bá sɛ a ke a tu wom zonne, o na ye wolo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to ŋwaane.’ 11A kwo, fɔge n nii gare-zenzware dento a zei a jeŋa ne to! De nwoŋi nmo gɔrɔ kom kuri seeni mo. Amo na yi n yera to, a ya wó wane‑m a go. A na gwoni n gɔrɔ kom, ye a daare n tete a yage to, laam nam lɔre we a ba jege nmo lwarem puga a jei. A bere a wo lɔge nmo kwaga ne. Nmo laam ma‑n pu amo kwaga se n le a momwɛ, ye a wo ke‑m kolokolo a chɔge. 12Baŋa Wɛ nam mo wó bere debam balei wone wolo na jege bora to. Baŋa Wɛ mo wó ŋwe amo jene nmo yuu ne, dedaane n na jege amo n ke tei maama to. Se ko ná ye amo, a bá kwei a jeŋa a ma a dwei‑m de fee de. 13Faŋa tiina maa we, ‘Keim tɔge de tu mo.’ Konto to, amo bá ke nmo lwarem.
14Amo nam ye wɔ mo ye Isarele tiina pɛ pare-ne se o go? Amo ye kukuri-teka, naa yeenu mo nmo jege n zeila? Ko ba jege kuri. 15Baŋa Wɛ mo wó zo taane dento wone se o di-de debam balei laŋa ne. Wonto mo wó zege amo kwaga ne o woli-ne. O ta wó pa a na bora ye a lu nmo jeŋa ne.”
16David na tage konto maama o ti to, mo Sɔɔl bwei‑o o we, “Amo bu David, nmo kwora mo konto na?” Sɔɔl laam ma keeri baŋa baŋa. 17O ta ma ta o we, “Yage, se n jege chega, amo mo toŋe vwa. Nmo nam ke amo lanyerane, ye amo lage nmo chɔgem. 18Nmo zem pɛ se a lɔre we n lage a ni taane. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ ya pɛ‑m pwola se n go-ne, ye n wo sɛ se n go-ne. 19Nɔɔno ná jeeri o dono ye o ja‑o, o daa wó yage‑o se o kɛ mɔle mɔle mo na? Nmo zem na ke-ne lanyerane to, Baŋa Wɛ mo wó ke zaane n yuu ne. 20Amo laam lɔre we nmo mo wó seene n ji Isarele tiina Pɛ, ye n paare dem wó zege chekke. 21A nam lwoori‑m mo se n ta n du de Baŋa Wɛ yere we, n ná tu n di paare, n bá‑n chɔge a dwi dem se de ti maama. Yé pa se a yere dem jei a kwo sɔŋɔ kom wone.”
22David ma seene o ta o du konto Sɔɔl yiga ne. Sɔɔl ma zaŋe o jwoori sɔŋɔ. David de o nɔɔna bam de ma jwoori ba vo ba seigim jei sem ne.

english_text:
Samuel Dies
1Samuel died, and people from all over Israel gathered to mourn for him when he was buried at his home in Ramah. Meanwhile, David moved his camp to Paran Desert.
Abigail Keeps David from Killing Innocent People
2-3Nabal was a very rich man who lived in Maon. He owned 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats, which he kept at Carmel. His wife Abigail was sensible and beautiful, but he was from the Caleb clan and was rough and mean.
4One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it. 5-6So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal:
I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you. 7I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep.
When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them. 8Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing.
My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
9David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
10This is what he said:
Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days. 11What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
12The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
13“Everybody get your swords!” David ordered.
They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other 400 followed David.
14-16Meanwhile, one of Nabal's servants told Abigail:
David's men were often nearby while we were taking care of the sheep in the fields. They were very good to us, they never hurt us, and nothing was ever stolen from us while they were nearby. With them around day or night, we were as safe as we would have been inside a walled city.
David sent some messengers from the desert to wish our master well, but he shouted insults at them. 17He's a bully who won't listen to anyone.
Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
18Abigail quickly got together 200 loaves of bread, two large clay jars of wine, the meat from five sheep, a large sack of roasted grain, 100 handfuls of raisins, and 200 handfuls of dried figs. She loaded all the food on donkeys 19and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
20Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
21David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults. 22I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
23Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David. 24Then she said:
Sir, please let me explain! 25Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him!
I didn't see the men you sent, 26-27but please take this gift of food that I've brought and share it with your followers. The Lord has kept you from taking revenge and from killing innocent people. But I hope your enemies and anyone else who wants to harm you will end up like Nabal. I swear this by the living Lord and by your life.
28Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live. 29The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
30The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you, 31and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people.
When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
32David told her:
I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today. 33And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people. 34If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
35David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
36Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night. 37But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone. 38Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
39-40David heard that Nabal had died. “I praise the Lord!” David said. “He has judged Nabal guilty for insulting me. The Lord kept me from doing anything wrong, and he made sure that Nabal hurt only himself with his own evil.”
David and Abigail Are Married
Abigail was still at Carmel. So David sent messengers to ask her if she would marry him.
41She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
42Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
43David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives. 44 Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_text:
David de Abigali taane dem
1Samuwel déem ma ba o te. Isarele tiina bam maama ma jeeri o teo kom ne, se ba di o lua. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o tete teo Rama ne.
Ko kwaga ne, mo David vei o wo Paran kagoa kam wone. 2-3Kaleb dwi tu wodwoŋi déem zoore Maon teo kom ne, o yere mo Nabale. O déem ye nadum chekke. O maa jege pei morro tetɔ, ye o bone de ye moro. O maa jege tega Kamele seeni o nii o vara baŋa ne. O kaane yere déem mo ye Abigali. O maa ye boboŋa tu ye o yibia tiini ya lamma. Ko daare Nabale tete, wonto wo lona dedɛ ye o ta jege ban-jworo. Ko ma maŋe dedaane Nabale de o nɔɔna bam wo Kamele ne ba wora ba fane o vara bam koro.
4David déem na wo kagoa kam ne konto to, mo o nigi we Nabale tu se o fane o vara bam koro. 5O ma le o nɔn-donno tem fuga, o toŋe-ba Nabale tei ne ye o we, “Véi-na Nabale tei Kamele ne á da amo ŋwaane á ware‑o. 6Ta-na ded‑o we: ‘Wɛ wó pa nmo de n sɔŋɔ tiina maama yazura de momwɛ-dɛɛre! Wɛ wó pa se n jeŋa wonnu maama ke lanyerane! 7Amo nam nigi we nmo wora n pa ba fane n vara bam koro mo. A maa lage se n maane we, nmo nayera bam ya na wo debam tei ne to, dé wo daane-ba. Maŋa kalo maama ba na wo Kamele seeni to, ba kolokolo wo jei. 8Nam bwei n tontoŋena bam n nii, se ba wó ta konto mo. Zem na ye kuri dim dɛ to mo a lwoori‑m se n ke a nɔn-donno tem lanyerane, dé badwoŋo kom ŋwaane. Pa debam zeina yalo maama n na jege n jeŋa ne to.’ ”
9David nɔɔna bam ma ja o kwora kam ba vo ba pa Nabale. Ba laam ma zege se ba jwoŋi leira. 10Nabale ma leiri-ba o we, “David mo ye wɔ? Amo yeiri‑o. Jesse bu wonto nɛ o tete na? Leile konto, tontoŋeno wolo maama ná jeini o boŋe ga, o wó zaŋe mo o lɔ o tu kwaga ne se o taa tei o tete. 11Amo bá sɛ se a kwei a wodiu dedaane a na a pa nɔn-yɔɔro telo a na yeiri mɛ ba na nwoŋi to. A bá kwei vara balo a na go se a tontoŋena di to a pa abam.”
12David nɔɔna bam ma jwoori ba vo David tei, ye ba ta kolo maama Nabale na tage to ba bere‑o. 13David ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Nɔɔno maama kwei o se-zɔɔ o vɔ o teiŋa ne diŋ-diŋ!” Ba ma kwei ba se-zɔɔro tem ba vɔ. David tete de ma vɔ o se-zɔɔ kom o teiŋa ne. O maa tɔge nɔɔna bia yana yiga o maa vei Nabale baŋa. Nɔɔna bia yalei ma daare, se banto taa yere ba zela yam.
14Nabale tontoŋeno wodwoŋi ma ta de Nabale kaane Abigali o we, “David mo zege kagoa kam ne o toŋe nɔɔna debam tu Nabale tei ne se ba ware‑o, ye o twe-ba lanyerane. 15Chega ŋwaane nam, nɔɔna banto ya yɔɔre ba ke debam lanyerane mo. Ba wo daane debam. Maŋa kalo maama dé na wo ba tei ne dé beeri gaao kom wone to, dé kolokolo wo jei. 16Dé na jege dé pei sem dé yere gaao kom wone to, David nɔɔna bam mo kwoli debam, wea dedaane tete maama wone. 17Konto to, fɔge n jeeli se n nii n na wó ke kolo n woli dé maama to. Kokuri lɛɛro mo lage te yi dé tu wom de o sɔŋɔ kom maama, de o na tiini o ye puseŋ-nyeno, ye o ba sɛ o jwoŋi bera to ŋwaane.”
18Abigali ma ke lela o ke woŋo maama daane. O maa jege bworobwooru bia yalei (200), de sana lɔɔro telei, de pei senu ba ya na wɔge-se to, de men-wɔa ywolo-kamunu, de kekan-wogila bwɛ bi (100), de kapere-kora maasa bia yalei (200). O ma kwei wonnu tem konto maama o vɔ bonɛ baŋa ne. 19O ma ta de o tontoŋena bam o we, “Ja-na wonnu tento á ta‑á wo yiga ne se amo de wó saŋe á kwaga a ba.” Konto maama to, o wo pɛ o baro wom maane ko ni ne.
20Abigali ma di o bonaga baŋa ne o kwei chwoŋa o maa via. O wo chwoŋa kam ne mo, se ko maŋe dedaane mɛ na gugwoli ko kaare peo kom to. David de o nɔɔna bam maa tu peo kom yuu ne ba beena. Ba ma jeeri daane. 21David ya boŋe o ja we, “A yɔɔre a yaare a tete mo kafɛ ye a déem wora a yere Nabale jea wonnu kagoa kam wone. Amo ke‑o lanyerane pa se o kolokolo wo jei.
