Laam nam nii o na mɛ balɔrɔ mo o jwoori o leini lanyerane delo a na ke‑o to. 22Amo nam dugi de Wɛ se o pa lɛɛro yi amo, nenɛɛne tega daa ná poore ye a wo go baara balo maama na ye o dwi tiina to pa se ba wolowolo wo daare de dedoa de.”
23Abigali na yɔɔre o na David to, mo o zege o bonaga kam yuu ne o faŋe o chu. O laam ma chɔɔle o yibia tega ne o ware David. 24O ma ja David nadwooni ye o we:
“Amo tu, pa-ne pwola se a ŋɔɔne fee dede‑m. Ja! Sɛ se ko maama taa ye amo yiga, se n daare n cheigi a taane. 25Amo tu, yé pa se Nabale na ke tei to daane‑m, se o ye puseŋ-nyem mo. O yere na ye Nabale to, de kuri mo ye ‘nɔn-jworo’. Chega to, o ma seene o toŋe jworim. Se ko ná ye amo, a wo nɛ nɔɔna balo nmo na toŋe a baro tei ne to.
26Amo tu, a nɛ we ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo chege nmo, se n yé ma lwarem n ma n ŋwe n dona. O ma che‑m se n yé ma n jeŋa n go-ba. Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane, de nmo tete yere ŋwaane we, nmo dona maama de balo dwi maama na boŋe balɔrɔ ba pa‑m to wó guri nenɛɛne Nabale na lage o guri tei to mo. 27Amo nam lwoori‑m mo se n jwoŋi pɛɛra yanto n tontoŋ-kana jeŋa ne, a na jaane a ba to, n pɔɔre-ya n pa n nɔɔna bam. 28Amo tu, a nam lwoori‑m mo se n ma n chɛ-ne de a ná ke kolo a ja a chɔge. Amo yei we Baŋa Wɛ wó pa n paare dem fɔge de zege taa, nmo na ye wolo na jaŋe Baŋa Wɛ jara n pa‑o to ŋwaane. Wɛ bá sɛ se n ke lwarem n ŋwea maama wone. 29Nɔɔno ná pare nmo se o go‑m, n Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo wó taa kwoli‑m se cham yé yi n ŋwea. Ko nam ná ye n dona bam, o ta maa wó pa se ba ŋwea yɔɔre ka jei, nenɛɛne nɔɔno na kwei kandwɛ o ke napana wone, ye o laam dole-ka pa kandwɛ dem jei tei to. 30A yei we Baŋa Wɛ wó seene o ke wo-laaro telo maama o na gwoni ni se o ke o pa‑m to. O ta wó pa se n ji Isarele tiina pɛ. 31Ko maama ná kea, nmo boboŋa daa bá chɔge, nenɛɛne n ya ná go nɔɔna kafɛ yerane. Nmo boboŋa bá daane‑m de n na mɛ n tete jeŋa n ŋwe n jene nɔn-gwia baŋa ne to. Amo tu, Baŋa Wɛ ná tu o ke‑m lanyerane konto, se n guli amo de gula.”
32David ma ta Abigali o we:
“Amo wó seini Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom mo, kokuri to, wonto mo toŋe‑m se n ba n jeeri-ne zem dɛ dento. 33A nam ta ke Wɛ lei nmo de ŋwaane. N ye boboŋa tu. Swa taane delo n na tage to ŋwaane, amo ta wo mɛ a jeŋa a go nɔɔna se a ŋwe a jene ba baŋa ne. 34Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ mo chege amo chwoŋa se a yé chɔge abam. Nmo ya ná wo ke lela n ba n jeeri debam, tento n baro wom de o nɔɔna maama na ye baara naa bakeiri to ya tega. Dé ya wó go baaro dwi maama na wo o sɔŋɔ kom ne to, se tega daa ba ka poore. Amo dugi de Isarele tiina Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo we a tɛ chega mo konto.”
35David ma jwoŋi Abigali pɛɛra yam ye o daare o ta‑o o we, “Jwoori n vo sɔŋɔ, se n daare n pa n wo taa tiga. Amo wó ke n na tage tei n bere-ne to.”
36Abigali ma jwoori o vo sɔŋɔ. O na nɛ o baro Nabale to, o ma maane we o ke wodi-fɔrɔ nenɛɛne pɛ na wó ke tei to mo. O ke kuri mo o pa nɔɔna se ba tɔge ba di. O ma di ywoni o ba o bugi de sana. Konto ŋwaane Abigali wo tage kolokolo de o baro wom dento tete dem ne. 37Tega laam na poore ye sana bam nwoŋi Nabale yia ne to, mo o kaane wom tole kolo maama na ke to o bere‑o. Nabale na nigi to, o bochare ma tiini de baane, ye o yera yam maama bobo se ya taa toa. 38Da fuga na ke ya woli da to mo Baŋa Wɛ fere Nabale pa o te.
39David na nigi we Nabale tege to, o ma seini Wɛ ye o we, “Amo wó ke Baŋa Wɛ lei, kokuri to, o bere we a jege chega Nabale yiga ne dedaane o na twe-ne to. O ta ma che a jeŋa pa se a wo toŋe lwarem, ye o daare o pa se Nabale keim-balɔrɔ kom jwoori ko to o tete yuu ne.” David laam ma toŋe kwora o pa Abigali we, o lage‑o mo se o ma o ke o kaane.
40David nɔɔna bam ma vo Kamele ba ta de Abigali ba we, “David mo toŋe debam n tei ne se dé ja‑m dé ba se n ta‑n ye o kaane.” 41O ma chɔɔle o yibia tega ne ye o leiri-ba o we, “Amo ye David tontoŋ-kana mo. A maa wó sɛ se a zare o tontoŋena bam nɛ.” 42Abigali ma ke lela o zaŋe o di bonaga, ye o pa o ka-nyaana banu tɔge‑o ba vo. Ba ma pɛ David nɔɔna bam kwaga ba pu ba vo ba yi David tei, pa se o ji o kaane.
43David nam ya maŋe o di Jezerele teo bukɔ Ahinoam mo o ma o ke o kaane. Abigali laam ma woli da o ye o kaane. 44Se ko ná ye o ka-kwea kam na ye Sɔɔl bukɔ Mikaale to, Sɔɔl déem ya kwei‑o mo o pa o zo Layisi bu Paliteli. Nɔɔno wom konto déem nwoŋi Galim mo.

english_text:
David Again Lets Saul Live
1 Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
2Saul took 3,000 of Israel's best soldiers and went to look for David there in Ziph Desert. 3Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert.
When David heard that Saul was following him, 4he sent some spies to find out if it was true. 5Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them. 6David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?”
“I will!” Abishai answered.
7That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
8Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
9“Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king. 10As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle. 11 But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
12David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep. 13David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance. 14“Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?”
Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
15“Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight. 16You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
17Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?”
“Yes it is, Your Majesty. 18Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime? 19Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods. 20Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
21“David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
22“Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it. 23The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right. 24I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
25“David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!”
David in Philistia
Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_text:
David daa ta yage Sɔɔl o pa o lu
1Ziifi tiina badwonna déem ma zaŋe ba vo Gibea ye ba ta de Sɔɔl ba we, “David tu o seigi Hakila peo kom yuu ne, jei selo na jeeri Jesimon kagoa kam ne to mo.”
2Sɔɔl na nigi konto to, o ma la Isarele tiina jar-keira morro tetɔ balo na yei jara laŋa chekke to, ye ba vo Zifi kagoa kam se ba beeri David jei. 3Ba na yi chwoŋa kalo na wo Hakila peo kom teiŋa ne to ba ma zege ba chwi ba vwoa jei selo na jeeri Jesimon to ne. David ma maŋe kagoa kam wone. O ma ba o ni we Sɔɔl tu se o beeri o jei. 4O ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba ŋɔ ba nii Sɔɔl na wo mɛ to, ye ba lɔre we o seene o yi kagoa kam seeni.
5David na lɔre to, o laam ma zaŋe o vo o yi mɛ Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam na tigi to. O ma maane Sɔɔl de o jar-keira yiga tu Abenera na tigi mɛ chekke to. Abenera maa ye Nera bu. Sɔɔl maa tigi o dɔa ye jar-keira bam maama laam maa gilimi‑o ba ke tetare ne. 6Hiti tu Ahimeleka dedaane Joaba nyaane Abisayi mo zege David tei ne. Abisayi nu maa ye Zeruya. David ma bwei-ba o we, “Abam wɔ mo wó tɔge de amo, se dé vo dé yi Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam na tigi mɛ to?” Abisayi ma leiri o we, “Amo wó tɔge‑m se dé vo.”
7Dɛ dem konto tete ne David dedaane Abisayi ma lɔɔre ba vo Sɔɔl de o jar-keira bam tiga jei sem. Ba na yi da to, dedaane Sɔɔl tigi o jar-keira bam tetare ne mo o dɔa. O chichwei ma moore tega ne de maŋe de o yuu kom seeni. Abenera dedaane jar-keira bam maama maa gilimi‑o ba ke tetare ne, ye ba de dɔa. 8Abisayi ma ta de David o we, “Nii Baŋa Wɛ zem na kwei n dono wom o ke n jeŋa ne tei! Nmo ná sɛ, amo wó vaŋe o chichwei dem mo a le a jwoori a zɔ‑o a moore a yage tega ne. A maa wó zɔ‑o bedwe mo ye o te, a bá zɔ belei.”
9David ma leiri‑o o we, “Yé ke zonne o yera ne! Nɔɔno ná mage pɛ wolo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to, kotu tusim wó taa wo o yuu ne. 10Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane, wonto mo wó mage Sɔɔl o go. Wɛ wae o pae se o toa o tete toone, naa o te jara-keim baŋa ne. 11Baŋa Wɛ nam wó che amo se a ma a jeŋa a go wolo Baŋa Wɛ swolim nuga na wo o yuu ne to. Nam pa se dé kwei o chichwei dem, de na moore o yuu seeni to, dedaane o na-kunkwolo kom dé ja dé viiri.” 12David ma gɔ Sɔɔl chichwei dem ye o daare o kwei o na-kunkwolo kom te na zege te maŋe o yuu seeni to, ye ba kɛ. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam wo nɛ-ba. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno de wo lɔre kolo na ke to. Ba maama maa tigi ba dɔa ye ba wo zaŋe, Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ ba tiini ba dɔ ba lusi to ŋwaane.
13David dedaane Abisayi ma jwoori ba tɔge bwolo kom ba bɛ daa kadwoŋi kam ne. Ba ma vo ba di peo kodwoŋi yuu ba zege da, ye pwola daga banto de Sɔɔl nɔɔna bam tetare laŋa ne. 14David laam ma nii Sɔɔl jar-keira bam seeni ye o tɔɔle o bwoŋi Abenera o we, “Abenera, nmo wora na? Zaŋe n leiri-ne!” Abenera de ma tɔɔle o leiri o we, “Nmo ye wɔ mo ye n ke sɔɔ konto n bwoŋi pɛ wom?” 15David ma jwoori o leiri‑o o we, “Abenera, nmo dae babea n dwoi Isarele jar-keira bam maama mo na? Bɛ mo ke ye n ware n pɛ wom se n ta‑n yera? Ba ya tu mo se ba go n tu wom. 16Nmo na ke tei tento to ba lana. Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane, nmo dedaane n kwaga nɔɔna bam maama maŋe se á te mo, kolo ŋwaane á wo fɔge á yere a tu wom Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to. Laam nam fɔge-na á nii! Pɛ wom chichwei dem ya na wo o yuu seeni to wo yei ne mo? Se o na-kunkwolo kom de bɛ?”
17Sɔɔl ma lɔre David kwora kam ye o bwei‑o o we, “Amo bu David, nmo mo konto na?” David ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, amo mo konto.” 18O ta ma ta o we, “Amo na ye n tontoŋeno to, bɛ laam nam mo ke pa se nmo yɔɔre n pare amo konto se n zeili n ja? A ke bɛ mo a tusi? 19Amo tu, a lwoori‑m mo se n cheigi a taane dento. Ko ya ná ye Baŋa Wɛ mo na pɛ se n pare amo tento, a teene we o wó jwoŋi pɛɛre a jeŋa ne ye o leiri o boboŋa yam. Se ko ná ye nabiina mo kwei amo yuu ba mage de nmo nyem, Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se ba na lɛɛro. Kokuri to, ba fe-ne ba le a nabaara tega kam ne, Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ se ka taa ye amo nyem to, ye ba daare ba pa se a kare a zoore jwo-kaana teene ne. Ba laam maa we, a taa kaane jwona. 20Nam yé pa se a jana lu ka ke sa-teena tega ne, yiga yiga dedaane tega kalo na ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem to. Amo bere a ye wɔ mo? Yeenu dento, mo Isarele tiina pɛ tɔge-ne o para? Naa a ye luga mo ye n jege-ne n choa peero tem ne?”
21Sɔɔl ma ta David o we, “Amo bu David, jwoori n ba amo tei! Amo mo ke lwarem. Amo nam daa ba boŋe se a ke‑m zonne. Kokuri to, n zem bere we a jege lonne nmo yibia ne, ye n wo go-ne. Chega to, amo toŋe jworim. A tiini a tusi mo.” 22David daa ta maa we, “Pɛ, nii n chichwei dem mo tento. Toŋe n nɔn-donno tem dedoa se o ba o jwoŋi o ja o ba o pa‑m. 23Baŋa Wɛ mo yeini o bore o pa nɔɔno maama de o na jege chega de wo-dedoa tei to. Baŋa Wɛ ya pɛ-ne pwola se a go‑m zem, ye a wo ke konto, nmo na ye pɛ wolo o na kuri to ŋwaane. 24Amo zem na pɛ se n ŋwea kam jege kuri amo yibia ne to, a lwoori Wɛ mo se amo de ŋwea kam taa jege kuri o yibia ne se o taa cho-ne cham dwi maama wone.”
25Sɔɔl laam ma ta David o we, “Amo bu, Baŋa Wɛ swolim taa wo n tei ne. Nmo ná ke kolo maama, ko wó ke lam ko pa‑m.”
David ma kwei o chwoŋa o maa kɛa. Sɔɔl de ma jwoori o vo sɔŋɔ.

english_text:
1but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
2-3David and his 600 men went across the border to stay in Gath with King Achish the son of Maoch. His men brought their families with them. David brought his wife Ahinoam whose hometown was Jezreel, and he also brought his wife Abigail who had been married to Nabal from Carmel. 4When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
5One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
6Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
7David was in Philistia for a year and four months. 8The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns. 9Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there.
After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish, 10who would ask, “Where did you attack today?”
David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.” 11That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.”
David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia. 12But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_text:
David vei o seigi Filisi tiina teo ne
1Dɛ dedwe mo David déem jeini o boŋe o tete ne o we, “Ko laam bwola se Sɔɔl ja-ne o go. A ná duri a vo a seigi Filisi tiina bam tetare ne, ko wó taa gara. A daa ná tera Isarele tiina teo kom maama ne, Sɔɔl wó beeri-ne o ga. Konto maa wó pa se a lu o jeŋa ne.”
2Ko ma pa se David dedaane o nɔɔna bia yaredo yam duri ba vo Maoka bu Akisi tei ne. Wonto déem ye Gafa teo pɛ mo. 3David de o nɔɔna bam ma vo ba maŋe Akisi tei ne ba zoore Gafa teo kom ne, nɔɔno maama de o diga tiina. David kaana balei bam déem maa tɔge ba wo o tei ne: Ahinoam na nwoŋi Jezerele to, dedaane Nabale kadeim Abigali na nwoŋi Kamele to. 4Sɔɔl ma ni we David duri o vo o wo Gafa ne. O ma yage David beira kam.
5Dɛ dedwe David ma ta de Akisi o we, “Pɛ, nmo yi ná seene de su de amo totoŋa yam, se n le n teene dem wone te-balaŋa dedoa se amo de a nɔɔna bam taa zoore da. Ko dae se amo de taa tɔge a zoore n tei ne te-fɔrɔ konto wone.” 6Akisi ma sɛ ye o kwei Zikalag dento dɛ dem ne o pa David. Ko na zege kanto maŋa ne se ko yi zem maama to, Zikalag lɛɛre ko ye Judah pwa bam mo tei-ko. 7David déem ma zo Filisi tiina bam tetare ne bene dedaane chane sena.
8Maŋa kam konto ne, David de o nɔɔna bam ma yeini ba kwaare jara de Gesura tiina, de Girizi tiina, ko woli de Amaleki tiina bam. Ko zege faŋa faŋa to, teene dem konto tiina déem zoore jei sem konto ne se ko vo ko yi Sura seeni de Ejipti seeni maama mo. 9David de o nɔɔna bam ná jeeri teo kolo maama, ba yeini ba chɔge ko maama mo. Ba ma go ko nɔɔna bam, baara de kaana maama, ye ba daare ba vere ba pei sem, de ba naane dem, de ba bonɛ, dedaane ba kona yam, ko woli de ba gwaaro maama. O laam ma yeini o jwoori o vo Akisi tei. 10Akisi de ma yeini o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo zem vei teo kɔ mo n chɔge-ko ye n daare n vere ba wonnu?” David de ma yeini o leiri o we, “Dé vei Judah teo kodwoŋi kagoa kam wone mo dé vere nɔɔna bam,” naa o wae o tɛ we, “Dé vei kagoa kam seeni mɛ Jerameeli tiina na wora to mo dé vere-ba,” naa o we, “Dé vei kagoa kam seeni mɛ Keni tiina na wora to mo dé vere-ba.” 11Konto ŋwaane mo David ná jeeri teo kolo de jara, o wó kwaane o go ko nɔɔna bam maama, baara de kaana. O ma yeini o we, “A ná wo go-ba, ba wó wane ba vo Gafa ba ta ba bere Akisi amo na yeini a ke kolo maama to mo.”
Maŋa kalo maama David na tu o wo Filisi tiina tetare ne to, o déem yeini o ke konto mo. 12Se ko ná ye Akisi, wonto déem ma kwei o chega maama o pa David. O ma jeeli o we, “David na tiini o ke o chɔge o tete nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam tei to, o kikia maama laam lwoi ba momwa ne mo. Leile konto se ko taa vei wuu, o laam wó taa toŋe o pa amo mo.”

english_text:
Saul Asks To Talk with Samuel's Ghost
1-3 Samuel had died some time earlier, and people from all over Israel had attended his funeral in his hometown of Ramah.
Meanwhile, Saul had been trying to get rid of everyone who spoke with the spirits of the dead. But one day the Philistines brought their soldiers together to attack Israel.
Achish told David, “Of course, you know that you and your men must fight as part of our Philistine army.”
David answered, “That will give you a chance to see for yourself just how well we can fight!”
“In that case,” Achish said, “you and your men will always be my bodyguards.”
4The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa. 5Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear. 6 So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet. 7Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.”
His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
8That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
9The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
10Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
11 “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked.
“Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
12When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
13“Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.”
She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
14“What does it look like?”
“It looks like an old man wearing a robe.”
Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
15“Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked.
“I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
16Samuel said:
If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do. 17 I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing! 18 When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you. 19Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
20At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
21The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked. 22Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
23“No, I won't eat!”
But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed. 24At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread. 25Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_text:
1Ko na wora ko wora to, mo Filisi tiina bam déem lage ba jar-keira ba ke daane se ba kwaare jara dedaane Isarele tiina bam. Akisi ma ta de David o we, “Ko jege se n ta‑n yei we, nmo de n nɔɔna bam wó woli amo kɔgɔ kom wone mo, se dé vo dé ke jara yam.” 2David ma leiri‑o o we, “Dáane mo nmo wó wane n lɔre a na wó toŋe tei a pa‑m to.” Akisi ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo na sɛ amo konto to, amo wó pa se n ta‑n yere-ne taa wuu.”
Sɔɔl vei o vo chichiri voro
3Samuwel déem nam ya maŋe o te, ye Isarele tiina bam maama di o lua. Ba ma daare ba kwei‑o ba suli o tete teo Rama ne. Sɔɔl nam lwoori yiga mo o zeili chichiri vora de yi-nara maama Isarele tega kam ne.
4Filisi jar-keira bam ma vo Sunem ba gilimi daane. Sɔɔl ma bwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o ke daane pa se ba jeeri Giliboa ne. 5Sɔɔl na yɔɔre o dole o yi o na Filisi jar-keira bam to, mo foone zo‑o, o bochare de ma di kwaa. 6O ma kwaane o bwei Baŋa Wɛ se o nii o na wó ke kolo to. Baŋa Wɛ nam wo sɛ o leiri‑o. Ko ná ye dendwea, naa Yurim de Tumim kandwa yam, naa sampwori, Baŋa Wɛ wo tɔge se baŋa ne o pa‑o leira de fenfee de. 7Sɔɔl laam ma ta de o nakwa bam o we, “Véi-na á beeri kaane wolo na wae o bwei chira se o lɔre kolo na wora to á pa-ne. Ko jege se a vo kotu tei ne mo a nii a yiga.” O nakwa bam ma ta‑o ba we, “Kaane wodwoŋi mo wo Endora ne, o na nae chekke.”
8Sɔɔl laam ma zaŋe tete ne o kwei gwaaro telo na dae o nyem to o zo. O na leini o tete konto to, o ma tɔge dedaane o nɔɔna balei ye ba nwoŋi se ba vo kaane wom tei. Ba na yi da to, Sɔɔl ma ta de kaane wom o we, “Kwei n voro zela yam se n bwoŋi chiru wodwoŋi n pa-ne. Pa chiru wolo a na wó bwoŋi o yere to nwoŋi o ba amo tei.”
9Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “Nmo nam yei Sɔɔl na ke kolo ye o zeili chichiri vora de yi-nara maama pa se ba nwoŋi Isarele tega ne to. Bɛ mo ye n lage n kwei kalanchogo n ma n ja amo? Nmo laam ma n lage se ba go amo de!” 10Sɔɔl ma ta o du o we, “Amo dugi de Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere we, n ná toŋe a totoŋe dem n pa-ne, n bá‑n na waarem ko ŋwaane.” 11Kaane wom ma bwei‑o o we, “Wɔ mo n lage se a bwoŋi se o nwoŋi o ba?” Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Bwoŋi Samuwel chiru n pa-ne.”
12Kaane wom na yɔɔre o na Samuwel to, mo o laare cheppe! O ma pipiri o ta de Sɔɔl o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n gane-ne konto? Nmo mo ye Pɛ Sɔɔl!” 13Sɔɔl ma leiri‑o o we, “Yé ta‑n fona, za n ta kolo n na nɛ to n bere-ne.” Kaane wom ma ta o we, “A nɛ chiru mo na nwoŋi tega ne, ye o zaŋe o beene.” 14Pɛ wom ma bwei o we, “O nyenyego ye tetɛ mo?” Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “O ye nɔn-kwea mo na beene ye o zo gare-dedɔrɔ.”
Sɔɔl ma maane we ko seene ko ye Samuwel mo. O ma vwi o yibia tega ne se o pa‑o zula. 15Samuwel ma bwei Sɔɔl o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n daane-ne konto? N jaane-ne n jwoori n ba ywo-seeni se a ke bɛ mo?” Sɔɔl ma ta o we, “A wo mo dia, ye a yeiri a na wó ke kolo to. Kokuri to, Filisi tiina bam jeeri-ne mo de jara. Baŋa Wɛ nam lɔge amo kwaga ne mo. O daa ba tɔge sampwori baŋa ne, naa dendwea baŋa ne se o leiri-ne. Konto ŋwaane nam mo tei a bwoŋi‑m se a lɔre a na wó ke tei to.”
16Samuwel ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ nam na lɔge nmo kwaga ne pa se o ji n dono to, bɛ mo ye n daa‑n bwoŋi-ne se n bwei n nii n na wó ke tei? 17Baŋa Wɛ na ke kolo de nmo to ye kolo a na wuuri a ta a bere‑m to mo. O jwoŋi paare dem nmo jeŋa ne mo, ye o kwei-de o pa n dwoŋi. David mo konto! 18Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ‑m ni se n chɔge Amaleki tiina bam de ba wonnu tem maama, o bane na zaŋe de-ba to ŋwaane. Nmo nam wo sɛ n ke o ni dem konto chekke. Konto nam mo pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ zem ke‑m tento. 19Ko na wó ke tei to, Baŋa Wɛ lage o kwei nmo de Isarele tiina bam o ke Filisi tiina bam jeŋa ne mo. Jwa dɛ dem ne, nmo de n bia bam de wó te ye á ba churu ywo-seeni á woli amo wone. Ko ná ye Isarele jar-keira bam maama, Baŋa Wɛ wó ke-ba Filisi tiina bam jeŋa ne mo.”
20Sɔɔl na nigi taane dem konto maama to, mo o to tega ne o tigi da konto yirr. Samuwel taane dem ma tiini de pa foone zo‑o. O yera maa bwomma, o na wo di wodiu dɛ dem konto ne wea de tete maama to ŋwaane. 21Kaane wom ma fɔɔre o yi Sɔɔl yera, ye o maane we o bochare tiini de fwei. O ma ta‑o o we, “Ja, amo tu! Amo na sɛ nmo ni to, a yɔɔre a ve a ŋwea mo, ye a ke nmo na lage tei to a pa‑m. 22Konto to, a lwoori‑m mo se n sɛ amo na wó ta kolo to. Yage se a ke wodiu fee se n di. Konto wó pa n na dam se n wane n jwoori n viiri.”
23Sɔɔl ma ve ye o we, “Amo bá di wodiu.” O nɔɔna bam ma tɔge de kaane wom ba lwoori‑o. O laam ma sɛ. O ma kwaane o zaŋe wɛɛne, ye o daare o jeini gadwogo baŋa ne. 24Kaane wom ya jege na-paale o sɔŋɔ ne o na jege-de o kɔne to. Sento nɛ sem ni ne o ma ja-de o go. O ta ma kwei muni o ma fɔge bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to. 25O na ti wodiu kom yiga to, o ma kwei-ko o pa Sɔɔl dedaane o nɔɔna bam. Ba ma di ye ba daare ba gwoni tega ba zaŋe ba viiri.

english_text:
The Philistines Send David Back
1The Philistines had brought their whole army to Aphek, while Israel's army was camping near Jezreel Spring. 2-3The Philistine rulers and their troops were marching past the Philistine army commanders in groups of 100 and 1,000. When David and his men marched by at the end with Achish, the commanders said, “What are these worthless Israelites doing here?”
“They are David's men,” Achish answered. “David used to be one of Saul's officers, but he left Saul and joined my army a long time ago. I've never had even one complaint about him.”
4The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted:
Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers. 5 The Israelites even dance and sing,
“Saul has killed
a thousand enemies;
David has killed
ten thousand!”
6Achish called David over and said:
I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along. 7Go on back home and try not to upset them.
8“But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
9Achish said:
I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle. 10You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
11David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_text:
Filisi tiina bam wo sɛ se ba woli David
1Filisi tiina bam déem ma la ba jar-keira bam ba ke daane, ye ba jeeri Afeka ne. Ko daare Isarele tiina bam de ma vo ba jeeri Jezerele buli-yi dem seeni. 2Filisi tiina jar-keira bam déem maa pɔɔre bi bi dedaane moro moro. Ba pwa banu bam ma gwɛ ba yiga ne ba via. David de o nɔɔna bam maa maŋe kwaga ne ba tɔge de Akisi ba de gwɛ ba via.
3Filisi jara dedɛɛra bam ma bwei ba we, “Hiburu tiina banto tɔge de debam se ba ke bɛ mo?” Akisi ma leiri-ba o we, “David de o nɔɔna bam mo konto. O déem ye Isarele tiina pɛ Sɔɔl babea mo. O nam nwoŋi Sɔɔl kwaga ne mo ye o daare o ba o me de amo. Dé na toŋe daane to, ko dwoi bene. Dɛ dem o na tu amo tei ne to se ko yi zem, a ta wo nɛ o wo-lɔŋɔ de fenfee de.”
4Filisi dedɛɛra bam bane ma zaŋe dedaane Akisi ye ba we, “Pa se nɔɔno wom jwoori o viiri! Pa o jwoori o vo teo kolo nmo na pɛ‑o se o taa zoore da to. Yé pa o tɔge debam se dé kwaare jara yam. Ta‑n yei we o wó wane o lɔ debam kwaga ne, ye o pipiri o go dé jar-keira badwonna. Konto wó pa se o de Sɔɔl jwoori ba ke daane. 5Yé swei we ko ye David wom konto taane mo Isarele tiina bam sae ye ba leeni ba seini‑o ba we:
‘Sɔɔl go o dona bam
moro de moro.
Se ko ná ye David,
wonto go o dona bam
morro fuga de fuga mo.’ ”
6Akisi ma bwoŋi David ye o ta‑o o we, “Amo dugi de ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ we a seene a jege n chega mo. Ko zege nmo na tu n me dedaane amo to se ko yi zem maama, amo wo nɛ n wo-lɔŋɔ. Ko ya ná ye amo tei ne, a ya lage se n da dedaane amo mo se dé vo dé ke jara yam. Pwa babam bam nam wo pɛ‑m chega. 7Konto to, jwoori n vo sɔŋɔ chemm. Yé zaŋe n ke kolo na wó daane pwa bam to.”
8David ma leiri Akisi o we, “A ke bɛ mo a tusi? Nenɛɛne ko ná ye chega mo we n wo nɛ amo wo-lɔŋɔ de fenfee de, bɛ nam mo wó che se a yé tɔge a vo a ke jara a woli nmo wolo na ye a pɛ to, se dé di n dona bam?” 9Akisi ma jwoori o leiri o we, “Chega to, n totoŋa yam su amo yi. Amo maa nii nmo nenɛɛne a na nii Wɛ maleka tei to mo. De konto de, Filisi pwa badwonna bam nam mo ve, ye ba tɛ ba we, nmo bá‑n tɔge n vo n ke jara yanto. 10Konto to, jwa zezeŋa ne se á gwoni tega á zaŋe, nmo de nɔɔna balo maama na dɛ dede‑m ba ba amo tei to. Tega ná poore, pa se á kɔgɔ kom zaŋe á jwoori á viiri.”
11Tega na seene ka poore to, David de o nɔɔna bam ma gwoni tega ba zaŋe ba kwei Filisi teo chwoŋa ba maa jwoora. Filisi tiina bam de ma kɛ ba vo Jezerele.

english_text:
David Rescues His Soldiers' Families
1It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground, 2and had taken away the women and children. 3When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive. 4They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more. 5 David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
6David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength, 7 and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.”
Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David. 8Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?”
“Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
9-10David led his 600 men to Besor Gorge, but 200 of them were too tired to go across. So they stayed behind, while David and the other 400 men crossed the gorge.
11Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water, 12some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
13“Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?”
“I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick. 14We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
15“Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked.
“Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
16He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah. 17David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
18David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag. 19No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen, 20including their livestock.
David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
21On the way back, David went to the 200 men he had left at Besor Gorge, because they had been too tired to keep up with him. They came toward David and the people who were with him. When David was close enough, he greeted the 200 men and asked how they were doing.
22Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
23But David said:
My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked. 24Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
25David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
26David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
27-31This is a list of the towns where David sent gifts: Bethel, Ramoth in the Southern Desert, Jattir, Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa, Racal, the towns belonging to the Jerahmeelites and the Kenites, Hormah, Bor-Ashan, Athach, and Hebron. He also sent gifts to the other towns where he and his men had traveled.
translation_text:
David chɔge Amaleki tiina bam
1David de o nɔɔna bam na zege jara kapworo ne to, da yatɔ dɛ ne mo ba vei ba yi Zikalag. Ba ma maane we Amaleki tiina bam mo tu ba di Judah tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam maama. Ba ya tu ba ja jara dedaane Zikalag teo kom, ye ba daare ba zwɛ-ko. 2Ko ná ye teo kom kaana bam de bia bam maama, Amaleki tiina bam wo go-ba. Ba pɛ-ba mo ba ja viiri, ko woli dedaane balo maama na zoore teo kom wone to.
3David de o nɔɔna bam na jwoori to, ba ma na we ba teo kom maama zwɛ ko daare di-dwonnu mo ko zege. Ba ta ma na we dona mo tu ba pɛ ba kaana bam de ba bia, bakeiri sem de busankane sem, ba ja ba kɛ. 4David de o kwaga kɔgɔ kom ma tiini ba kaase ŋɔɔ! Ba ma keeri taa ye dam daa tere ba tei ne se ba keeri. 5Ba dona bam nam ya jaane David kaana balei bam de mo ba woli da ba ja ba kɛ. Banto ye Jezerele tiina bukɔ Ahinoam, dedaane Nabale kadeim Abigali mo. 6David boboŋa maama ma jei. Kokuri to, nɔɔna bam maama wo déem pɛ mo de ba na gɛ ba bia bam to. Ba ma ke bana se ba dole David de kandwa ba go. David ma sale Baŋa Wɛ yera ne pa se o na baare.
7David laam ma ta dedaane Wɛ kaanem tu Abiatara o we, “Kwei kaanem gare-wogo kom n ja n ba, se dé ma dé bwei Wɛ dé nii dé wó ke tetɛ mo.” Abiatara ma ja gare-wogo kom o ba o pa‑o. 8David ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A zaŋe a pare dé dona banto na? A ná pɛ ba kwaga a pu, a wó yi-ba a ja na?” Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, véi-na á zeili-ba, se á wó yi-ba. Abam nam ta wó jwoŋi á nɔɔna bam á yage.”
9David ma ja o nɔɔna bia yaredo yam se ba vo ba ja ba dona bam. Ba ma vo ba yi Besora nabara kam, ye o nɔɔna bam badwonna maŋe dáane. 10Nɔɔna bia yalei mo ware se ba bɛ ba daa vo yiga, ba na tiini ba bugi to ŋwaane. Ko daare David dedaane nɔɔna bia yana yam na daare to ma bɛ nabara kam ba maa kɛa.
11Ba na maa vei to, David nɔɔna bam badwonna ma vo ba na Ejipti tu wodwoŋi na beeri gaao kom wone. Ba ma ja‑o ba vo David tei, ye ba daare ba pa‑o wodiu se o di dedaane na se o nyɔ. 12Kapere-kora dedaane kekan-wogila bwɛ selei mo ba pɛ‑o ye o di. O na di o ti to mo o dam jwoori, kokuri to, da yatɔ maama mo o wo di wodiu ye o wo nyɔge na, wea dedaane tete maama.
13David ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo ye wɔ nɔɔno mo? N nam nwoŋi yei mo?” Nɔn-doŋo kom ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo nwoŋi Ejipti mo, ye a laam ye Amaleki tu kabaa. Da yatɔ na kɛ to, mo a tu wom dole-ne o yage, a na weele to ŋwaane. 14Dé ya vei dé ja jara de teene delo na wo kagoa kam seeni ye Cherete tiina bam zoore da to mo, de Judah laŋa kam tega-kuri seeni, ye dé ta yi kagoa kalo Kaleb dwi tiina na wora to. Dé ma zwɛ Zikalag teo kom dé woli da.” 15David ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nmo wó wane n ja-ne n yi mɛ venverena banto na wora to na?” O ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, a wó sɛ a ja‑m se dé vo ba na wo mɛ to. Nam du de Wɛ yere we, n bá‑n go-ne, n nam bá‑n jwoori n kwei-ne n ke a tu wom jeŋa ne.”
16Ejipti tu wom ma ja-ba o ja o vo o yi Amaleki tiina bam na wo mɛ to. Ba déem laam jage jei sem maama ne mo. Ba maa di ba boboŋa ba daare ba nyɔ sana ye ba kwɛɛre yɔɔ. Kokuri to, wonnu telo ba na vere Filisi tiina bam de Judah tiina bam tei ne to tiini te gaale. 17Tega na lage ka yi to, David ma zaŋe ba baŋa ne. O ma lɛɛre o jeeri-ba de jara taa se ko vo ko yi tega na poore to wɛ-zoore maŋa ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo lugi, ko ná dae nɔn-donno bia yana yerane. Banto déem kwei kona mo ba di ye ba duri ba viiri. 18David ma jwoori o jwoŋi nɔɔna balo maama Amaleki tiina bam na jaane ba vere to, de ba jejegero tem maama. O ma jwoŋi o kaana balei bam de o woli da. 19Kolokolo déem wo jei. Nɔn-donno tem, de nɔn-kwe sem, de bakeiri de busankane sem maama, ko ta woli de ba jejegero tem maama, kolokolo wo daare ko maŋe ba dona bam tei ne. David déem jwoori o jwoŋi te maama. 20David ma ja vara bam maama pa se o nɔɔna bam kale-ba ba ke ba kɔgɔ kom yiga ne. Ba maa via ye ba we, “Wonnu tento maama ye David nyem mo jara yam ŋwaane.”
21David ma jwoori o vo o yi nɔɔna bia balei balo ya na bwona ye ba maŋe Besora nabara kam ni ne to tei. Banto ya ba jege dam se ba tɔge ba vo ba ja jara yam. Ba ma nwoŋi se ba jeeri David de o kwaga kam. David de ma tutwoni o yi-ba ye o daare o ware-ba dedaane wopwolo. 22Puseŋ-nyena de nɔn-yɔɔro déem maa wo David kwaga nɔɔna bam wone. Ba ma ta ba we, “Nɔɔna banto wo wane ba tɔge de debam ba vo ba ke jara yam. Konto ŋwaane, dé bá sɛ se dé pɔɔre wonnu telo dé na vere dé dona bam tei ne to dé pa-ba. Dé wó pa nɔɔno maama kwei o kaane de o bia bam yerane mo o ja o viiri!”
23David ma ta o we, “Amo nɔɔna bam, yé ke-na wo-loŋo dedaane woŋo kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ debam to. Wonto mo kwoli debam, ye o daare o pa dé di dé dona balo ya na tu ba vere debam to. 24Abam taane dem tera. Nɔɔna bam maama wó chɛ kolo Wɛ na pɛ debam to, se ko taa mae daane. Balo na vei jara jei to, de balo na maŋe kwaga ne ba nii zela yam baŋa ne to maama wó jwoŋi ko mae daane mo.” 25Ko na zege dɛ dem konto ne to se ko ba ko yi zem, David lɛɛre o pa Isarele tiina bam tɔge ni dem konto mo.
26David ma ja kolo maama o na vere Amaleki tiina bam tei ne to, o ja o jwoori Zikalag. O ma pa ba le wonnu tem tedwonna ba ja ba vo ba pa Judah nakwa bam na ye o yuudwonna to, ye ba ta-ba ba we, “Nii-na, dé vere wonnu tento Baŋa Wɛ dona bam jeŋa ne mo. Abam de jwoŋi-na pɛɛre á ta‑á jega.” 27O déem le pɛɛra yam konto dwoŋi mo o toŋe o pa Bɛtel tiina bam, de tega-kuri kagoa kam teo Ramofa tiina bam, de Jatira tiina bam, 28ko ta woli de Arowa tiina bam, de Sifimofa tiina bam, dedaane Esetemoa tiina bam, 29de Rakali tiina bam. O ta ma toŋe pɛɛra o pa balo na zoore Jerameeli teene dem de Keni teene dem wone to, 30dedaane Horama tiina bam, de Borasan tiina bam, de Atachi tiina bam, 31ko ta woli de Heboron tiina bam. David déem toŋe pɛɛra yam se ya yi teene delo maama o de o nɔɔna bam na kare da ba kɛa ba beira kam wone to mo.

english_text:
Saul and His Sons Die
1Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed. 2The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua. 3The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
4Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him.
Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it. 5When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
6Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day. 7The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
8The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa. 9-10The Philistines cut off Saul's head and pulled off his armor. Then they put his armor in the temple of the goddess Astarte, and they nailed his body to the city wall of Beth-Shan. They also sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the good news in the temples of their idols and among their people.
11The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body. 12So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them. 13They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_text:
Sɔɔl na gɛ o ŋwea tei to
1 Tigisim 10:1-14
1Konto maama na jege ko ke to, dedaane Filisi tiina bam kwaare jara mo dedaane Isarele tiina bam. Isarele jar-keira bam ma jage sae ye Filisi tiina bam pare-ba. Ba ma go Isarele tiina bam dedɛ Giliboa peo kom yuu ne. 2Sɔɔl de o bia bam ma duri, ye Filisi tiina bam pɛ ba kwaga ba pu. Ba ma go Sɔɔl bia Jonatan, de Abinadaba, de Maliki-Sua. 3Jara yam ma tiini ya peene Sɔɔl dedɛ. O dona bam ma na‑o ye ba ta ba chena ba tɔ‑o pa ko tiini ko ke‑o zonne.
4Sɔɔl ma ta de nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara zela yam to o we, “Le n se-zɔɔ kom n ma n zɔ-ne n go. Amo ba lage se Filisi nɔn-yɔɔro tento yi amo yera ba de zɔ-ne se ba mɔne-ne ba ke chaveera” Nɔn-doŋo kom maa wo sɛ se o go‑o, foone na tiini de jege‑o to ŋwaane. Konto baŋa ne to, Sɔɔl ma vaŋe o tete se-zɔɔ o le. O ma kwei-ko o moore o puga ne, ye o daare o to ko baŋa ne o te. 5Nɔn-doŋo kom na maane we Sɔɔl tege to, o de ma le o se-zɔɔ kom o to ko baŋa ne ye o de te o tigi o tu wom takeiri ne. 6Ko déem ke konto mo ye Sɔɔl de o bia batɔ bam maama tɔge daane ba te, ko woli de nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara zela yam to, de o kwaga nɔɔna bam maama. Ba maama déem tega dɛ dem konto ne mo.
7Isarele tiina balo déem na zoore Jezerele bwolo kom seeni to, de balo na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to ma lɔre we Sɔɔl de o bia bam tege mo, ye Isarele jar-keira bam maama duri ba jage. Ba na nigi konto to mo ba duri ba lage jei ba daare ba teene dem. Filisi tiina bam ma vo ba zoore de wone.
8Tega na poore to, Filisi tiina bam ma jwoori jara kapworo kom ne se ba zane ba le jejegero twa bam yera ne. Ba ma na we Sɔɔl de o bia batɔ bam tege mo ba tigi Giliboa peo kom yuu ne. 9Ba na nɛ to, ba ma gwoni Sɔɔl yuu ba le. Ba ma daare ba lɔɔre o jara zela yam na wo o yera ne to. Ba laam ma toŋe kwora se ka yi Filisi tiina teene dem maama we ba di Sɔɔl. Ba ma tɔɔle taane dem ba jwona di sem wone, de ba dwi tiina bam na wo mɛ to. 10Ko ná ye Sɔɔl jara zela yam, ba kwei-ya ba ja zo ba tiŋi ba jwoni Asetare diga kam ne mo. Ba ma daare ba kwei o yera yam ba vo ba pale Bɛte-San teo kabira kam yera ne.
11Nɔɔna balo déem na zoore Jabese Gilead ne to ma ni Filisi tiina bam na ke Sɔɔl tei maama to. 12Balo na tiini ba ye bembɛ ba wone to ma zaŋe tete ne ba vo ba yi Bɛte-San se tega laam poore. Ba ma pare Sɔɔl de o bia bam yera yam teo kom kabira yera ne. Ba laam ma ja-ya ba jwoori Jabese, ye ba daare ba zwɛ-ya. 13Ko kwaga ne mo ba lage ba kwi sem ba ke daane, ye ba kwei-se ba suli sana kadwoŋi kuri ne, Jabese teo wone. Ba ta ma di ba lwi ye ba vɔ ba nia da yarepɛ.

english_text:
David Finds Out about Saul's Death
1Saul was dead.
Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag. 2Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
3David asked, “Where did you come from?”
The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
4“Who won the battle?” David asked.
The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
5David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
6 The young man replied:
I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him. 7When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
8Saul asked me, “Who are you?”
“An Amalekite,” I answered.
9Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
10So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
11At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow. 12They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
13David asked the young man, “Where is your home?”
The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
14-16David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!”
Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!”
David Sings in Memory of Saul
17David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan, 18 and he ordered his men to teach the song to everyone in Judah. He called it “The Song of the Bow,” and it can be found in The Book of Jashar. This is the song:
19Israel, your famous hero
lies dead on the hills,
and your mighty warriors
have fallen!
20Don't tell it in Gath
or spread the news
on the streets of Ashkelon.
The godless Philistine women
will be happy
and jump for joy.
21Don't let dew or rain fall
on the hills of Gilboa.
Don't let its fields
grow offerings for God.
There the warriors' shields
were smeared with mud,
and Saul's own shield
was left unpolished.
22The arrows of Jonathan struck,
and warriors died.
The sword of Saul cut
the enemy apart.
23It was easy to love Saul
and Jonathan.
Together in life,
together in death,
they were faster than eagles
and stronger than lions.
24Women of Israel, cry for Saul.
He brought you fine red cloth
and jewelry made of gold.
25Our warriors have fallen
in the heat of battle,
and Jonathan lies dead
on the hills of Gilboa.
26Jonathan, I miss you most!
I loved you
like a brother.
You were truly loyal to me,
more faithful than a wife
to her husband.
27Our warriors have fallen,
and their weapons
are destroyed.
translation_text:
David nigi Sɔɔl na tege tei to.
1David déem di Amaleki tiina bam mo ye o daare o jwoori Zikalag. O maa maŋe da o ke da yalei dedaane Sɔɔl maŋe o te. 2David na jwoori ye ko ke da yatɔ to nɔɔno ma nwoŋi Sɔɔl jar-keira bam wone o ba o tei. Nɔɔno wom déem ya kaare o gwaaro mo, ye o daare o kwei kasolo o ma o taare o yuu o wo-chechɔgɔ kom ŋwaane. O ma yi David tei, ye o vwi o yibia tega ne o zuli‑o.
3David ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo nwoŋi yei ne mo?” O de ma leiri o we, “Amo ya tɔge a wo Isarele jar-keira bam wone mo, ye a duri a lu jara yam wone a ba ywo-seeni.”
4David daa ma ta‑o o we, “Ta kolo maama na ke to n bere-ne.” Nɔɔno wom ma leiri o we, “Isarele jar-keira bam duri mo ba jage se ba lu. Ba dedɛ nɛ zonne mo, ba badwonna de ma te. Sɔɔl de o bu Jonatan de ma tɔge ba te.”
5David daa ma bwei nɔɔno wom o we, “N ke tɛ mo n lɔre we Sɔɔl de Jonatan seene ba te?”
6Nɔn-doŋo kom ma leiri o we, “Amo yɔɔre a zege Giliboa peo kom yuu ne mo ye a na Sɔɔl na sale o chichwei dem yera ne o zega. Ko ma maŋe dedaane dé dona bam diini ba sisein-nɔɔna de ba torokooro tem ba duri ba ma yi o tei. 7O ma pipiri o na amo ye o bwoŋi-ne se a vo a woli‑o. A ma sɛ ye a we, ‘Pɛ, nii-ne da!’ 8O ma bwei amo o we, ‘N ye wɔ mo?’. Amo ma leiri‑o a we ‘A ye Amaleki tu mo.’ 9O laam ma lwoori amo o we, ‘Fɔge n zege konto se n go-ne, se a dam maama ti, ye a toone dem bwola mo.’ 10O na tage konto to, a ma lɛɛre a go‑o, bɛŋwaane a lɔre we ko tiini ko ni‑o ye o daa bá wori. A laam ma dɔne paare yipuga kam na wo o yuu ne to, ye a daare a le o jeŋa baŋa kam, se a ja a ba a pa‑m. Amo tu, nii-te da.”
11David na nigi konto to, o wo déem ma chɔge. O ma ja o na zo gwaaro telo to o vaŋe o kaare. O nɔɔna bam maama de ma ke konto. 12Ba ma lɛɛre ba keeri taa ye ba vɔ ni se ko vo ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa. Ba wo déem chɔge dedɛ Sɔɔl de o bu Jonatan toone dem ŋwaane, dedaane Baŋa Wɛ tete nɔɔna bam maama ŋwaane, de Isarele tiina bam dedɛ na tege jara yam wone to ŋwaane.
13David daa ma bwei nɔn-doŋo kolo na jaane kwora kam o ba o pa‑o to o we, “Nmo nwoŋi yei ne mo?” O de ma leiri o we, “A ye Amaleki tu mo, ye a laam zoore Isarele tega kam ne.”
14David laam ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo tu n yuu ne pa se n ma n jeŋa n go Baŋa Wɛ na kuri wolo se o taa ye Pɛ to? Foone ba jege‑m na?” 15O ma bwoŋi o nɔɔna bam dedoa o pa‑o ni o we, “Zɔ‑o n go!” O de ma seene o vo o zɔ Amaleki tu wom o go. 16David nam ya tage de Amaleki tu wom mo o we, “Nmo toone dem ye n tete yiga mo. N mɛ n ni mo n ŋɔɔne n ve n tete bora, de n na we, nmo mo go Pɛ wolo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to.”
David keeri Sɔɔl de Jonatan toone
17David déem laam ma leeni luseim leiŋa se o ma o guli Sɔɔl de Jonatan gula. 18O ta ma pa ni se ba kwei-ka ba bere Judah tiina maama. O ma bwoŋi leiŋa kam we ‘Taŋa Baŋa Leiŋa.’ Leiŋa kam konto popone ka tiŋi Jasare tɔnɔ kom wone mo. O maa we:
19“Isarele tiina bam,
dé bembɛ sem to dé peero tem yuu ne ba te.
Nii-na dé jar-keira dedɛɛra bam na tiini ba to tei!
20Yé ta-na taane dento se Gafa tiina ni.
Yé tɔɔle-na-de Asekelon teo kom pwooni ne.
Filisi tiina kaana ná nigi-de,
ba wó taa chake mo de wopwolo.
Balo na yeiri Wɛ to wó taa mɔna.
21Giliboa peero tem,
Wɛ bá sɛ se nyɔnɔ daa to á yuu ne.
Doa de nam daa bá ne.
Abam kare sem daa bá ke wodiiru.
Kokuri to, dáane mo babɛ sem jara zela yam maŋe teero wone.
Ba daa ba lage ba lwo nuga
ba ma taare Sɔɔl jara-keim nantana kam.
22Jonatan déem ná tage o taŋa,
o dona wó siiri mo bare-bare,
ba ze ná maŋe ba ye babɛ tei de.
Sɔɔl de ná le o se-zɔɔ,
wonto wó mage o dona mo o de,
ye ko bá jwoori kafɛ.
23Sɔɔl de Jonatan,
nɔɔna déem jege ba swono dedɛ!
Ba ŋwea wone, ba ye daane mo,
ba ta ma tɔge daane ba te.
Ba tiini ba wara ba dwoi maaro,
ye ba ta dana ba dwoi nywonnu.
24Isarele tiina kaana bam,
ta‑á keeri-na Sɔɔl toone dem ŋwaane!
Se o déem pɛ se á zo gare-laaro telo na ke sabu dedɛ to mo.
O ta ma kwɛ á gwaaro tem dedaane sabu-seŋa wonnu.
25Nii-na jar-keira bembɛ sem na to jara tetare ne tei!
Jonatan ma te o tigi peero tem yuu ne.
26Amo choro Jonatan,
a wo tiini ko chɔge nmo ŋwaane.
Nmo tiini n jege lonne n pa-ne!
Swono kolo nmo na jege n pa amo to
dwoi nɔɔno de o kaane swono na ye tei to.
27Nii-na jar-keira bembɛ sem na to jara wone tei!
Ba jara zela yam daa ba jege kuri!”

english_text:
David Becomes King of Judah
1Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?”
The Lord answered, “Yes.”
David asked, “Which town should I go to?”
“Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
2 David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel. 3David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
4 The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
5David sent messengers to tell them:
The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler, 6and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done. 7Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage.
Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
8Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim 9and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin. 10Ishbosheth was 40 years old at the time, and he ruled for two years. But the tribe of Judah made David their king, 11and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years.
The War between David and Ishbosheth
12One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon. 13Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side. 14Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!”
Joab agreed, 15and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men. 16They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.” 17Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
18Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field, 19and he ran straight after Abner, without looking to the right or to the left.
20When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?”
Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
21Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.”
But Asahel refused to stop.
22Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
23But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still. 24But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert. 25Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
26Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
27Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!” 28Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
29Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
30As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were 19 missing besides Asahel. 31But David's soldiers had killed 360 of Abner's men from the tribe of Benjamin. 32Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_text:
David jigi Judah tiina pɛ
1Konto kwaga ne, David ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A jwoori Judah laŋa kam se a vo a taa zoore ba teene dem dedoa ne na?” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we “Ɛɛ, véi.”
David daa ma bwei‑o o we, “Teo kɔ mo a nam wó vo?” Baŋa Wɛ maa we, “Véi Heboron.”
2David ma zaŋe o vo Heboron se o taa zoore da, o de o kaana balei bam, Ahinoam dedaane Abigali. Ahinoam nam ya nwoŋi Jezerele ne mo, Abigali maa ye Kamele tu Nabale kadeim wom. 3David nɔɔna bam de ba sɔŋɔ tiina maama de déem ma tɔge ded‑o ba vo ba zoore Heboron teo kom de ko nawuura yam wone. 4Judah tiina nakwa bam ma vo Heboron ne, ye ba lwo nuga David yuu ne ba tiŋi‑o se o taa ye Judah tiina pɛ.
David ma ni we Jabese Gilead tiina mo kwei Sɔɔl ba suli. 5David ma toŋe nɔɔna ba tei ne de kwora kanto ye o we:
“Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ abam swolim, de á na bere á pɛ wom chega á kwei‑o á suli to. 6Amo nam sɔɔle Baŋa Wɛ mo a pa abam se o de bere abam chega, o daare o ke abam lanyerane. Á keim-laao konto ŋwaane amo de wó ke abam lanyerane. 7Sɔɔl na tege to, nam ta jege-na baare, se á daare á ta‑á dana! Lɔre-na we Judah tiina bam tiŋi-ne mo se a taa ye ba pɛ.”
David sɔŋɔ kom dedaane Sɔɔl sɔŋɔ kom tetare jara yam taane
8Nera bu Abenera déem mo ye Sɔɔl jar-keira bam yiga tu. Sɔɔl na tege to, Abenera ma ja Sɔɔl bu Isi-Bosefa o bɛ Jɔdan buga kam o lu o vo Mahanayim. 9Abenera ma pa se Isi-Bosefa di paare Gilead teene dem baŋa ne, de Asuri tiina baŋa ne, de Jezerele jei sem baŋa ne, ko ta woli de Efrayim dwi tiina bam, de Benjamin dwi tiina bam, dedaane Isarele tiina badaara bam maama baŋa ne. 10Isi-Bosefa déem jege bena finna mo ye o bobo se o di paare. O ma jeini paare dem wone bena yalei.
Ko daare Judah dwi tiina bam ma pa David chega se o taa ye ba pɛ. 11David ma maŋe Heboron ne o di paare Judah tiina bam baŋa ne bena yarepɛ de chichworo.
12Dɛ dedwe Abenera de Isi-Bosefa dedɛɛra bam ma zege Mahanayim ne ba vo Gibeon. 13Zeruya bu Joaba de déem ma ja David dedɛɛra bam o vo o jeeri Abenera de o nɔɔna bam Gibeon bula kam ne. Nɔɔno maama de o jar-keira maa wo bula kam bubɛ ne, kɔgɔ dedoa wo bula kam daa kadwoŋi ne ye kɔgɔ kodwoŋi wo ka daa kakam kam ne pa se ba jeini ba jeeri daane. 14Abenera ma ta de Joaba o we, “Le n jar-keira bam wone nɔɔno dedoa dedoa se amo de le dedoa dedoa. Banto maa wó jeeri daane ba jaŋe balei balei se dé nii.” Joaba ma sɛ.
15Ba ma le Benjamin dwi dem nɔɔna fuga-balei na ye Isi-Bosefa kwaga nɔɔna to se ba nwoŋi ba jeeri David nɔɔna fuga-balei dedaane jara. 16Ba balei balei na wo jara yam wone to, ba maama ma ja da yu-ywei. Ba laam ma kwei se-zɔɔro ba moore da sɛ ne, ye ba go daane. Ko dɛ konto mo ye nɔɔna finlei-bana bam maama te. Ba ma pa jei sem konto yere we, ‘Se-zɔɔro Kapworo’. 17Ko na tu ko chɛ to, nɔɔna bam maama ma lɛɛre ba zo jara wone. David jar-keira bam ma di Abenera de Isarele jar-keira bam.
18Zeruya bia batɔ bam, Joaba, de Abisayi, de Asaheli déem tɔge ba wo jara yam wone. Ko ná ye Asaheli, wonto déem wara o dwoi feira. 19O ma zaŋe o yɔɔre o pare Abenera se o ja. O maa wo sɛ se o tɔge wo-gaa. 20Abenera ma pipiri o na‑o ye o we, “Asaheli, nmo mo pare-ne konto na?” O de ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ! Amo mo pare‑m.”
21Abenera daa ma ta‑o o we, “Nam yage amo se n vo n beeri nɔn-doŋo kodwoŋi n pare. N ná jaane kotu, se n jwoŋi o jara zela yam n ta‑n tei.” Asaheli ma ve se o yage Abenera zeilim.
22Abenera daa ta ma kaane‑o ye o we, “Yé ta‑n pare-ne se n ja! Amo ba lage se a fere‑m a de tega ne a go. Nmo ná fe-ne se a go‑m, a daa bá wane n zembaaro Joaba yibia a nii.” 23Asaheli nam wo sɛ se o jwoori kwaga. Abenera ma kwei o chichwei dem nabili seeni o tɔ Asaheli puga ne de dam pa se de moore da ye de kɛ de nwoŋi o kwaga ne. Asaheli ma to tega ne o te. Wolo maama na tu o yi mɛ Asaheli na tege o tigi to, kotu wó maŋe dáane mo o zege.
24Joaba de Abisayi laam ma zeili Abenera se ba ja. Wɛ-zoore maŋa ne mo ba yi Amma zwoŋo kom seeni. Jei sem konto wo Gibeon kagoa kam chwoŋa ne mo, mɛ na bwola de Gia to. 25Abenera ma la Benjamin jar-keira bam o ke daane zwoŋo kodwoŋi yuu ne. Ba ti ba yiga mo se ba ke jara. 26Abenera ma tɔɔle o bwoŋi Joaba o we, “Dé lage dé ja jara taa dé go daane dé vo dé yi yei ne mo? N bá‑n pa dé yage konto na? N wo maane we ko kweelim jei wó taa ye wo-chechɔgɔ yerane mo na? Debam maama na ye chorro daane to, nmo bá‑n ke lela n ta de n nɔɔna bam se ba daa yé zeili debam na?”
27Joaba ma sɛ ye o we, “Amo dugi Ŋwea Tu Wɛ wom yere ŋwaane, nmo ya ná wo tage tento, a nɔɔna bam ya wó kwei tete dem maama ba ma zeili abam ba ja mo.” 28Joaba ma le o nabɔnɔ kom o wu pa se o nɔɔna bam maama zege. Ba ma yage Isarele tiina bam parem. Ba daa wo mage jara dedaane-ba.
29Tete dem konto maama Abenera de o jar-keira bam ma vo ba tɔge Jɔdan bwolo kom ne ba kɛ. Ba ma vo ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. Tega na poore to, ba ta maa vei taa, ba vo ba yi Mahanayim.
30Joaba na yage Abenera zeilim to, o ma zaŋe se o jwoori sɔŋɔ. O ma jeeli o nɔɔna bam ni ye o maane we ba fuga-nogo mo woli Asaheli wone ye ba tera. 31David jar-keira bam nam ya go Abenera nɔɔna bam bia yatɔ dedaane fuseredo mo na ye Benjamin dwi dem tiina. 32Joaba de o nɔɔna bam ma ja Asaheli yera yam ba vo Bɛtelehem. Ba ma suli‑o o kwo yibeeli dem wone. Konto kwaga ne, mo ba vei konto taa tete dem maama wone. Te-pora ni ne ba ma yi Heboron.

english_text:
1This battle was the beginning of a long war between the followers of Saul and the followers of David. Saul's power grew weaker, but David's grew stronger.
David's Sons Born in Hebron
(1 Chronicles 3.1-4)
2-5Several of David's sons were born while he was living in Hebron. His oldest son was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel. David's second son was Chileab, whose mother was Abigail, who had been married to Nabal from Carmel. Absalom was the third. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of King Talmai of Geshur. The fourth was Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith. The fifth was Shephatiah, whose mother was Abital. The sixth was Ithream, whose mother was Eglah, another one of David's wives.
Abner Decides To Help David
6As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family. 7He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
8Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth:
Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
9I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him! 10 God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
11Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
12Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
13David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
14 David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed 100 Philistines so I could marry her.”
15Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish. 16Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
17Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now. 18So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
19Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do. 20Abner took 20 soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
21After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.”
David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble.
Joab Kills Abner
22Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village. 23Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
24Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone! 25You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
26Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it. 27When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel.
Abner's Funeral
28David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death! 29Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
30Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
31David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!”
David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried. 32Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly. 33Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner:
Abner, why should you
have died like an outlaw?
34No one tied your hands
or chained your feet,
yet you died as a victim
of murderers.
Everyone started crying again. 35Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
36Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did. 37Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
38David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died? 39I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_text:
1Tigura déem ma lɛɛre ka peini Sɔɔl diga kam de David diga kam tetare ne ka dáane. David diga kam ma yɔɔre ka nae dam dɛ maama ka woli da, ko daare ye Sɔɔl diga tiina bam bwom dɛ maama.
2David ta na wo Heboron ne to, mo o loge o bia baredo banto:
O bu-kwea kam mo ye Aminon. Wonto nu maa ye Jezerele tiina bukɔ Ahinoam.
3Chileabi ma saŋe. O nu ye Abigali mo, o na ye Kamele tu Nabale kadeim wom to.
Abisalom maa ye o bia batɔ tu. O nu déem ye Gesura teo pɛ Talimayi bukɔ Maaka mo.
4Adonija maa ye o bia bana tu. O nu ye Hagifa.
Sefatia maa ye bia banu tu. O nu ye Abitali.
5David bia baredo tu maa ye Ifream. O de nu déem ye Egela mo.
Mo bia balo David na loge Heboron ne to.
Abenera gɔge o zo David kɔgɔ kom wone
6Maŋa kalo tigura kam na tigi Sɔɔl diga kam de David diga kam tetare ne to, Abenera ma ba o jege dam dedɛ Sɔɔl kwaga nɔɔna bam maama wone. 7Sɔɔl nam ya jege o ka-bia wodwoŋi, o yere na ye Rizapa. Wonto maa ye Aya bukɔ. Dɛ dedwe Sɔɔl bu Isi-Bosefa ma ta de Abenera o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n vo n peini de a kwo ka-bia kam?”
8Isi-Bosefa taane dem ma fuli Abenera wo dedɛ. O ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo pɛ chega we amo ye bebare nyem mo na? Amo wó yeigi Sɔɔl kwaga nɔɔna bam a ke Judah tiina jeŋa ne na? De zem maama, a tiini a kwei a chega maama mo a pa n kwo Sɔɔl, de o diga tiina dedaane o badwonna maama. Amo nam mo chege David pa se o ta wo di nmo, ye n laam kwei kaane wonto taane n ja n jeeri-ne. 9-10Baŋa Wɛ déem gwoni ni o tiŋi de David o we, o wó jwoŋi paare dem Sɔɔl dwi dem tei ne o pa David. Wɛ nam wó pa se a na a lɛɛro, nenɛɛne a ná wo pɛ se ni-gwonim dem konto ji chega. Amo laam wó woli David se o di paare Judah tiina de Isarele tiina bam maama baŋa ne, ko na zege Dan laŋa kam seeni se ko yi Beeriseba to.” 11Isi-Bosefa ma ga ni se o puri de Abenera, o na tiini o kɔre‑o to ŋwaane.
12Abenera ma toŋe nɔɔna David tei ne o we, “Teo kom maama ye wɔ nyem mo, ye ko dae nmo? Nam sɛ se nmo de amo ke ni-sɛɛm daane, se a ja Isarele tiina bam maama a ba a ke n kwaga ne.” 13David ma jwoori o leiri‑o o we, “Nmo taane dem lamma. N nam ná lage se dé fɔge dé ke ni-sɛɛm daane, se n ná beene, se n ja Sɔɔl bukɔ Mikaale n jwoori n ja n ba n pa-ne.”
14David ma daare o toŋe nɔɔna Isi-Bosefa tei ne o we, “Jwoori n pa-ne a kaane Mikaale. A déem go Filisi tiina bi mo se a wane‑o a di a ma ke a kaane.”
15Mikaale déem nam ya zo Layisi bu Paliteli mo. Isi-Bosefa ma pa ba vo ba jwoŋi Mikaale o tei ne. 16Ba na maa kɛ to, Paliteli ma tɔge Mikaale kwaga ye o keeri taa o vo o yi Bahurim teo kom. Abenera ma bage‑o o we, o jwoori sɔŋɔ! O ma pipiri o jwoori.
17Abenera ma vo Isarele nakwa bam tei o ta de-ba o we, “Maŋa kalo abam na boŋe se David taa ye á pɛ to, ko dae zem. 18Chwoŋa laam tiga se á ke á boboŋa na lage tei to. Nam yé swei-na we Baŋa Wɛ ya maŋe o gwoni ni se o tɔge o tontoŋeno David baŋa ne o jwoŋi o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam o yage Filisi tiina bam de dé dona maama jeŋa ne mo.”
19Abenera tete ma vo o ŋɔɔne de Benjamin dwi tiina bam. O laam ma daare o vo Heboron se o lwoni kolo na ke to o bere David, se o taa yei Isarele tiina de Benjamin tiina bam maama na boŋe se ba ke tei to. 20Abenera ma ja nɔɔna finlei o ke o kwaga ne ye ba vo Heboron. Ba na yi da to, mo David pɛ se ba ke kuri kamunu ba pa-ba. 21Ko kwaga ne mo Abenera déem tage de David o we, “Pɛ, pa-ne chwoŋa se a vo a la Isarele tiina bam a ke daane se ba jeeri‑m. Ba laam maa wó ke ni-sɛɛm dede‑m se n ta‑n ye ba pɛ, n di paare tega kam maama ne, ne n boboŋa na lage tei to.” David ma bane Abenera o yage chwoŋa ne, pa o jwoori o viiri de o yazura.
22Joaba de David jar-keira bam déem ya vei jara keim ne mo. Ba ma vere jejegero dedɛ ba dona tei ne ba ja jwoori sɔŋɔ. Ba na yi Heboron to dedaane Abenera daa tera. O de David ŋɔɔne ba ti mo, ye pɛ wom pa se o viiri de o yazura. 23Joaba dedaane o kwaga kam na yɔɔre ba yi to, mo nɔɔno tage‑o o we, “Nera bu Abenera ya tu ywo-seeni o na Pɛ, ye o pa o jwoori o viiri de o yazura.”
24Joaba ma vo o zo David tei ye o we, “Abenera na tu nmo tei to, bɛ mo ye n yage‑o pa se o jwoori o viiri mɔle mɔle? 25Nmo maŋe n yei Abenera na ye wolo. O tu se o ŋɔ n swa mo o nii, se o lɔre n na-veili dedaane kolo maama n na jege n ke to.”
26Joaba ma nwoŋi da David tei ne, ye o vo o toŋe nɔɔna Abenera kwaga ne se ba ja‑o ba jwoori. Ba ma beeri‑o ba na Sira vole dem seeni. Ba ma ja‑o ba jwoori, ye David yeiri ko ni ne. 27Abenera na jwoori o vo o yi Heboron to, mo Joaba jaane‑o o fɔɔre o vo gugworo kodwoŋi ne, teo kom manchwo-peo ni ne. O ma ke nenɛɛne o lage se ba bwɛ woŋo mo daane. Dáane mo o zɔge‑o o puga ne o go, se ko ŋwe Abenera na go wonto choro Asaheli to jene.
28David déem na tu o lɔre we Joaba go Abenera to, o maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó zege amo kwaga ne we amo de a nɔn-bia bam maama yiga tera Abenera toone dem wone. 29Abenera toone dem jene wo Joaba de o sɔŋɔ tiina baŋa ne. Wɛ wó pa se Joaba dwi dem maama wone, jaweero dwi dwi yé fɔge te ti se ko taa vei wuu. Ŋɔn-pwoni wó le ba badwonna yera ne. Ba badwonna wó taa ye naywanno, de gwaaro. Ba badwonna wó te jara keim wone. Ba badaara wó ga wodiu se ba di.”
30Ko déem dɛ konto mo ye Joaba de o nyaane Abisayi paale ba go Abenera. Ko nam ye o de déem na go ba choro Asaheli Gibeon jara yam ne to ŋwaane mo ba ke konto.
31David ma ta de Joaba de o nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Á maama kaare-na á gwaaro, se á daare á zo gare-nyenyaaro wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. Dé jege se dé di Abenera lua mo.” David tete ma pɛ Abenera na wo gandwa yalo baŋa ne to kwaga o pu. 32Ba ma kwei Abenera ba suli Heboron wone. David ma maŋe o yibeeli dem ne o keeri dedɛ. Nɔɔna bam maama de ma tiini ba keeri. 33David déem dɛ ko ŋwaane o leeni luseim leiŋa kanto Abenera baŋa ne o we:
“Abenera ye nɔn-jworo mo,
pa se o te toone dento dwi na?
34Abenera, ba wo vɔge n je sem.
Ba nam wo mɛ chaponno ba vɔ n nɛ de.
Nmo yɔɔre n te nɔn-gora jeŋa ne mo!”
David na leeni leiŋa kam konto to, nɔɔna bam maama daa ma to keira ne. 35Ba ma kwaane se ba kwoori David se o jwoori o di wodiu dɛ dem konto ne. O ma ve ye o du duuri o we, “Amo ná di wodiu ye wɛ wo zo, se Wɛ pa lɛɛro yi-ne!”
36Nɔɔna bam na maane David na ke tei konto to, ba ma sɛ de wopwolo. Ba wo yeini ko da kolo maama pɛ wom na ke to mo. 37Dento dɛ dem ne, Judah tiina bam de Isarele tiina bam maama ma lɔre we, Abenera na tege to, ko dae David yiga.
38David déem ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam wo maane we Isarele tiina nɔn-kamunu zem mo tege na? 39Amo zem ye Pɛ wolo Wɛ na kuri to mo. De konto de, a nam tiini a bwona mo lage-lage. Zeruya bia balei bam konto tiini ba dana se a wane-ba a che. Baŋa Wɛ nam mo wó waare-ba se ko maŋe de ba totoŋ-lwanno tem!”

english_text:
Ishbosheth Is Killed
1Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
2Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. 3The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
4 Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
5One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting 6-7in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them.
Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long. 8Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
9David answered:
I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble! 10 When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
11You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
12Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_text:
Ba na go Isi-Bosefa tei to
1Sɔɔl bu Isi-Bosefa déem ma ni we ba go Abenera Heboron wone. O vɔna ma pare, ye foone de zo Isarele tiina bam maama ko ŋwaane. 2Isi-Bosefa déem jege jar-keira yiga tiina balei na ye Beerofa tu Rimon bia. Ba yera maa ye Baana de Rekabi. Ba ye Benjamin dwi tiina mo. Ba déem jeeli Beerofa teo kom ba ke Benjamin laŋa kam wone mo. 3Kokuri to, balo déem ya na zoore Beerofa ne to duri mo ba vo ba zoore Gitayim teo ne. Ba nam ye veira mo teo kom konto ne de zem maama.
4Sɔɔl bu Jonatan déem jege bu o yere na ye Mefibosɛfi. O maa ye gɔrɔ. Maŋa kalo o na jege bena yanu to, mo ba jaane Sɔɔl de Jonatan lua taane ba nwoŋi Jezerele teo wone ba ba. Ba na nigi to mo kaane wolo na jege Mefibosɛfi o nii to kwei‑o se o ja o duri o lu. O na tiini o lage lela to, bu wom ma vere o jeŋa ne o kwori o to tega ne pa se o ji gɔrɔ.
5Dɛ dedwe wea kam na tiini ka dana to, mo Isi-Bosefa tigi o diga ne o sia. Rimon bia Rekabi de Baana ma vo ba yi o sɔŋɔ kom. 6-7Ba ma zo sɔŋɔ kom wone ba ke nenɛɛne ba lage ba beeri muni mo. Ba ma zo o diga kam wo de o tigi o dɔ mo o gadwogo baŋa ne. Ba ma kwei seo ba zɔ o puga ne ba go. Ba ma gwoni o yuu, ye ba ja-ko ba jwoori ba liisi ba viiri. Tete dem konto ne, ba ma yɔɔre ba kwei Jɔdan bwolo chwoŋa kam ba vo taa ba poore tega. 8Ba ma ja Isi-Bosefa yuu kom ba vo Heboron. Ba ma zo Pɛ David tei ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Nii, nmo dono Sɔɔl bu Isi-Bosefa yuu mo tento. Sɔɔl déem kwaane se o go nmo mo, ye zem dɛ dento Baŋa Wɛ ŋwe n jene Sɔɔl de o dwi dem maama baŋa ne o pa‑m.”
9David ma leiri Rekabi de o nyaane Baana o we, “Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na jwoŋi amo o yage cham maama wone to mo. Amo nam dugi wonto yere ŋwaane we, á maŋe se á te mo! 10Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem tu o ta de amo we Sɔɔl tega. Kotu ya boŋe we ta-laao mo o tage o bere-ne se o jwoŋi ŋweero de ŋwaane. A ma pa se ba ja‑o ba go Zikalag ne se ko taa ye o ŋweero! 11Abam nam zo nɔn-ŋom diga á go‑o o peiga jei ne ye o dɔa. Á na toŋe puseŋa kikia yalo to, ko wó taa ye tɛ mo á yera ne? Amo dugi we amo de wó go abam mo se ko leiri nɔɔno wom toone dem yuu ne, pa se á yera jei logo baŋa ne.”
12David ma pa o nɔɔna bam ni se ba go-ba. Ba ma go-ba ye ba daare ba gwoni ba je de ba nɛ. Ba ma kwei ba yera yam ba vo ba pale ba yage Heboron buga kam ni ne. Ba ma daare ba kwei Isi-Bosefa yuu kom ba ja ba vo ba suli Abenera yibeeli dem na wo Heboron ne to wone.

english_text:
David Becomes King of Israel
(1 Chronicles 11.1-3)
1Israel's leaders met with David at Hebron and said, “We are your relatives. 2Even when Saul was king, you led our nation in battle. And the Lord promised that someday you would rule Israel and take care of us like a shepherd.”
3During the meeting, David made an agreement with the leaders and asked the Lord to be their witness. Then the leaders poured olive oil on David's head to show that he was now the king of Israel.
4 David was 30 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 40 years. 5He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for 33 years.
How David Captured Jerusalem
(1 Chronicles 11.4-9; 14.1,2)
6 The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
7-9David told his troops, “You will have to go up through the water tunnel to get those Jebusites. I hate people like them who can't walk or see.”
That's why there is still a rule that says, “Only people who can walk and see are allowed in the temple.”
David captured the fortress on Mount Zion, then he moved there and named it David's City. He had the city rebuilt, starting with the landfill to the east. 10David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
11King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
