12David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people.
David's Sons Born in Jerusalem
(1 Chronicles 14.3-7)
13After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children. 14His sons who were born there were Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, 15Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, 16Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
David Fights the Philistines
(1 Chronicles 14.8-17)
17The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress. 18So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
19David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?”
The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
20David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.” 21David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
22Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley. 23David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered:
Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees. 24Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
25David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_text:
David jigi Isarele tiina bam maama pɛ
1Isarele dwi tiina bam maama déem vei Heboron mo. Ba ma ta de David ba we, “Nii mo. Debam maama dedaane nmo ye yera dedoa de jana dedoa mo. 2Faŋa ye Sɔɔl ta ye debam maama pɛ to, nmo mo ye wolo na tɔge dé yiga pa se dé vei dé ke jara de dé dona to. Baŋa Wɛ nam ya maŋe o ta de nmo o we, ‘Nmo mo wó ji a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam yuu tu ye n nii ba baŋa ne ne nayero tei.’ ”
3Konto to, Isarele nakwa bam maama déem jeeri Pɛ David tei ne Heboron ne mo. Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne mo David ke ni-sɛɛm de-ba. Ba laam ma lwo nuga o yuu ne se o taa ye Isarele tiina bam maama pɛ.
4David déem jege bena fintɔ mo ye ba tiŋi‑o se o ji pɛ. O ma di paare dem bena finna. 5O ya jeini Heboron ne o di paare Judah dwi tiina baŋa ne bena yarepɛ de chichworo mo, ye o daare o vo o jeini Jerusalem ne o di Isarele tiina dedaane Judah tiina maama paare bena fintɔ-yatɔ.
David na di Jerusalem tei to
1 Tigisim 11:4-9
6Jebusi tiina déem mo zoore Jerusalem teo kom ne. David dedaane o jar-keira bam ma zaŋe ba vo Jerusalem se ba ke jara de Jebusi tiina bam. Nɔɔna bam konto maa wo jeeli we David wó wane o di ba teo kom. Mo kokuri ba déem mɔne‑o ye ba ta ba we, “Lilwoa de gwane tete wó wane ba che abam se á yé zo ywo-seeni.” 7De konto de, David wane Zion o di. Ko déem ye teo kom dam jeiga mo. Nɔɔna laam maa jege jei sem konto ba bwoi we, ‘David teo’.
8Dɛ dem konto ne David déem tage de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Nɔɔno ná boŋe se o wane Jebusi tiina bam, konto tu wó tɔge peo bɔɔne na-chwoŋa kam mo o zo teo kom o yi-ba. Amo tiini a chuli-ba, de ba na maŋe ba ye gwane de lilwoa to!” Konto ŋwaane nam mo ba tɛ ba taane ba we, ‘Lilwoa dedaane gwane bá na chwoŋa se ba zo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wo.’
9David na di teo kom dam jeiga kam to, mo o lɛɛre o maŋe da o zoore ko wone. O ma bwoŋi ko yere we ‘David teo’. O ma zege mɛ tega kam na suuri ka maŋe daane to o jwoori o lɔ teo kom o zege o kaage jeiga kam maama. 10David dam dem déem ma fɔge de puli de ke da, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wo o tei ne to ŋwaane.
11Tura teo Pɛ Hiram déem ma toŋe nɔɔna David tei ne se ba ke pipiu daane. O ma pa se ba ja Sedare da-kwollu ba vo ba pa‑o. O ta ma pa se gwaro, de kandwa-cherena tɔge ba vo, pa se ba lɔ pɛ sɔŋɔ ba pa David. 12David ma lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ mo seene o pa se o di Isarele teo paare, ye o ta daare o pa se o paare dem fɔge de puli lanyerane Wɛ tete nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam ŋwaane.
13David na zege Heboron ne o vo o zoore Jerusalem ne to, mo o daa ta swo ka-bi dedɛ o woli o kaana bam wone. Ba ma lo bia dedɛ, bakeiri de busankane, ba pa‑o. 14Bia balo David na loge Jerusalem ne to yera mo tento:
Sammua, de Sobabi, de Natan, de Solomon, 15de Ibihara, de Elisua, de Nefega, de Jafia, 16de Elisama, de Eliada, dedaane Elifeleti.
David di Filisi tiina bam
17Filisi tiina bam déem ma ni we ba tiŋi David se o taa ye Isarele tiina pɛ. Ba ma la ba jar-keira bam maama ba ke daane ba vo ba beeri o jeiga se ba ja. David ma lɔre ko ni ne ye o nwoŋi teo kom ne o vo o seigi dalem jei sem ne. 18Filisi tiina bam ma ba ba yi Refayim bwolo kom. Ba ma maŋe da ba faare jei sem maama. 19David ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A véi a jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara, se nmo wó ke-ba a jeŋa ne na?” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Ɛɛ, zaŋe n vo n jeeri-ba, se amo wó seene a ke-ba n jeŋa ne.”
20David ma vo o yi Baal Perazim o jeeri Filisi tiina bam. O ma wane-ba o di. O laam ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ mage o pore a dona bam baŋa ne mo o zeili-ba, nenɛɛne na na mage ba pore tei to.” Ba ma lɛɛre ba jege jei sem konto ba bwoi we ‘Baal Perazim’. 21Dáane mo Filisi tiina bam duri ba daare ba jwona yam ba yage. David de o nɔɔna bam ma pɛ-ya ba ja ba viiri.
22Ko na ke da fenfee to, Filisi jar-keira bam daa ta ma jwoori ba ba ba faare Refayim bwolo kom maama. 23David daa ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ se o lɔre o na wo ke tei to. Wɛ ma ta o we, “Nmo ná jeeri-ba, se n yé yɔɔre ba yiga vekke. Nam kaare n tɔge Balesam teeni dem n kekare dáa kadwoŋi kam ne n yi ba kwaga seeni. 24Ta‑n nii teeni dem yuu ne. Nmo ná tu n ni ko dɔna de baŋa ne, se n laam zaŋe n jeeri-ba. Ko bere we amo Baŋa Wɛ tete mo dɛ á yiga se a jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara se a di-ba.”
25David ma seene o ke kolo Baŋa Wɛ na bere‑o se o ke to. Ko ma pa se o wane Filisi tiina bam o di. O ma zege Gibeon ne o pare-ba o vo o yi Gezere.

english_text:
David Brings the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
(1 Chronicles 13.1-14; 15.1—16.3,43)
1David brought together 30,000 of Israel's best soldiers and 2 led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
3 They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart, 4with Ahio walking in front of it. 5Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
6But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest. 7The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
8David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
9David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?” 10He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
11-12 The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.”
At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating. 13The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow. 14He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth. 15He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
16Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
17They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar, 18then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. 19 He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home.
Michal Talks to David
20David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
21David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him. 22I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
23Michal never had any children.
translation_text:
Ba jaane Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba vo Jerusalem
1David déem kuri Isarele jar-keira balo na yei jara laŋa chekke to morro fintɔ mo se ba la daane. 2O ma da ba yiga se ba vo Judah teo Baala, se ba daare ba ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba jwoori Jerusalem. Dakaa kam konto nam wora Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane mo. Wonto di paare cherubi sem tetare laŋa ne, se na zege dakaa kam baŋa ne to. 3Dakaa kam nam ya wo Abinadaba sɔŋɔ ne mo. O sɔŋɔ kom de déem maa wo zwoŋo yuu ne. Ba ma vo ba kwei-ka ba daŋe nabɛ toroko-doŋo baŋa ne. Ba laam ma siseiri ba tu zwoŋo kom kuri ne. Abinadaba bia balei Yuza de Ahio maa tɔge toroko kom ye ba yere-ko. 4Ahio maa wo ko yiga ne o via. 5David de Isarele dwi tiina bam maama ma leeni lei ba seini Baŋa Wɛ de ba dam maama. Ba ta maa jege kwanno, de senyɛ, de gungwei, dedaane kwɛɛra zela dwi dwi ba kwɛɛre ye ba daare ba sae ba tɔge kwaga.
6Ba ma vo ba yi Nakon na yeini o fere o mena mɛ to. Nabɛ sem ma gare se tete se lage se to. Yuza ma zi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam se o pa ka fɔge ka zege. 7Baŋa Wɛ bane ma tiini de zaŋe Yuza baŋa ne, o na wo sɛ se o tɔge dakaa kam chullu tem to ŋwaane. Nɛ sem konto ni ne, o ma mage Yuza dakaa kam teiŋa ne o go. 8David wo ma fuli dedɛ de Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge o ban-zɔŋɔ kom baŋa o go Yuza to ŋwaane. Konto ma pa o bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we, ‘Pɛrezi Yuza.’ Mo jei sem yere de zem maama.
9Keim dem konto ma pa se David kɔre Baŋa Wɛ. O ma bwɛ o we, “Amo wó ke tɛ mo a na chwoŋa se a wane a ja Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam a ba a tei?” 10O daa maa wo sɛ se o ja-ka o ja o vo o zo Jerusalem teo wone. O ma lɛɛre o pa se ba ywori ba ja-ka ba vo Gafa tu Obed-Edom sɔŋɔ. 11Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ma maŋe Obed-Edom sɔŋɔ ne chane setɔ. Ka na wo dáane to, Baŋa Wɛ ma swɛ wonto de o sɔŋɔ tiina maama swolim.
12Nɔɔna ma ta ba bere Pɛ David ba we, “Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam na wo Obed-Edom sɔŋɔ ne to, Baŋa Wɛ swɛ o swolim lanyerane. O wonnu maama de ma vo yiga.” David laam ma vo Obed-Edom sɔŋɔ o vo o ja dakaa kam o ja o ba Jerusalem teo wone de wopwolo dedɛ. 13Nɔɔna balo na zeŋe dakaa kam to na gɔge naba-laara yaredo to, David ma pa ba zege. O ma go nabea dedaane na-paale o ke kaanem o zuli Baŋa Wɛ. 14David nam ya zo gare-wogo kolo ba na mɛ gare-fefale ba sɔ to mo. O maa tiini o sae de o dam maama se o zuli Baŋa Wɛ. 15Wonto de Isarele tiina bam maama ma ja Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba jege ba zoore Jerusalem wone. Ba na tiini ba jege wopwolo to, ba maama ma ke sɔɔ ye ba wui nabwanno.
16Ba na yɔɔre ba jege Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba zoore Jerusalem teo wone tei to mo, Sɔɔl bukɔ Mikaale tɔge o takworo seeni o nii o na kɔgɔ kom. O maa na nɛ Pɛ David na faŋe ye o sae o zuli Baŋa Wɛ tei to, o ma chweese‑o o bochare ne.
17David déem ya maŋe o chwi vwei dedwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ dakaa kam ŋwaane. Ba laam ma kwei dakaa kam ba zege vwei dem wone. David ma go vara o ke kaanem o zwɛ o pa Baŋa Wɛ, ye o daare o ja yazura pɛɛra o ba se o ma o zuli‑o. 18O na ke kaanem dem o ti to, o laam ma kwei Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere dem o ma o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o ke nɔɔna bam yuu ne. 19O ta ma pa se ba chɛ wodiiru tem ba pa Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama, baara de kaana. Nɔɔno maama ma jwoŋi bworobworo dedoa, de nɔn-wɔa, de kekan-wogila bɔŋa dedoa. Ba laam ma jage ba vo ba sam.
20Konto maama na ti to, David ma jwoori o tete sɔŋɔ se o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage o sɔŋɔ tiina bam yuu ne. Sɔɔl bukɔ Mikaale ma jeeri‑o chwoŋa ne ye o we, “Nmo wolo na ye Isarele tiina Pɛ wom to zem yage n tete chekke! Nmo tiini n toŋe jworim dedɛ, de n na jale n tete pa se n tontoŋena bam busankan-bia na n chaveera to!”
21David ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo zem sage se a zuli Baŋa Wɛ mo. Wonto mo yage nmo kwo de n kwo sɔŋɔ tiina o daare o kuri amo se a taa nii o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. A nam ta wó fɔge a bere a wopwolo de do. 22Amo nam ta lage a yaale a tete a dwoni a na ke tei to mo. Amo nii a tete se a ta dae kolokolo mo, se ko ná ye busankan-bia balo n na tɛ ba taane to, banto wó yɔɔre ba tiini ba zuli-ne mo.”
23Sɔɔl bukɔ Mikaale déem nam wo fɔge o lo bu se o vo o te.

english_text:
The Lord's Message to David
(1 Chronicles 17.1-15)
1King David moved into his new palace, and the Lord let his kingdom be at peace. 2Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
3Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
4That night, the Lord told Nathan 5to go to David and give him this message:
David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me? 6I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them. 7I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
8 David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people. 9Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
10I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did 11when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you.
Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings. 12 I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler, 13and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me. 14 I will be his father, and he will be my son.
When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents. 15But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you. 16 I will make sure that one of your descendants will always be king.
17Nathan told David exactly what he had heard in the vision.
David Gives Thanks to the Lord
(1 Chronicles 17.16-27)
18David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed:
Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us, 19and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people? 20I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say. 21You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
22 Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true. 23 And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here. 24You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
25And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants. 26Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.” 27After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
28 Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise. 29Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ gwoni ni dedaane David
1Pɛ David déem laam zoore o sɔ-fɔrɔ kom ne mo de yazura. Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se o dona maama daa ba daane‑o. 2Dɛ dedwe David ma ta de Wɛ sampwora Natan o we, “Nii amo mo tento! A zoore sɔ-fɔrɔ kolo ba na kwei Sedare da-ŋonno ba ma lɔ-ko to, ko daare ye Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam laam wo vwei kuri ne.” 3Natan ma leiri o we, “Ke n boboŋa na jaane tei maama to, se Baŋa Wɛ wo n tei ne.”
4Dɛ dem konto tete ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma ŋɔɔne dedaane Natan o we:
5“Véi n ta de amo tontoŋeno David we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: N boŋe we nmo mo wó lɔ sɔŋɔ n pa-ne se a taa zoore da na? 6Ko nam na ye tei to, ko na zege maŋa kalo a na jaane Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne to, se ko ba ko yi zem, amo ta wo fɔge a zo sɔŋɔ wone. Mɛ maama a ná jaane-ba a ja a vo, a yeini a zoore vwei wone mo. 7Jei selo maama amo dedaane Isarele tiina bam na beeri dé vo to, amo ta wo fɔge a ta de yiga tiina balo a na kuri se ba taa nii a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam to we, “Bɛ mo ke ye á wo kwei Sedare da-ŋonno á ma á lɔ sɔŋɔ á pa-ne?” ’
8Konto to, ta de a tontoŋeno David we, ‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo na le nmo to, dedaane n déem ye nayero mo gaao ne n nii pei baŋa ne. A ma daare a pa se n di paare amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. 9Mɛ maama nmo na yeini n vei to, a déem tɔge n kwaga konto mo, ye a pa se n dona dwi maama saare tega baŋa ne. Leile konto, amo wó pa n yere tiini de zaŋe, se n ta‑n tɔge n ye logo baŋa nɔn-kamuna bam wone dedoa. 10Amo laam nam kwei tega kalo a nɔɔna bam na wó taa zoore ka wone to mo a pa-ba. Ko lage ko taa ye ba tete kugu jei nɔɔn-nɔɔno na bá wane o daane-ba ka wone to mo. Nankɔ-nyena daa bá bɛɛse-ba nenɛɛne ko déem na ke tei, 11ko zege maŋa kalo a na pɛ se yiga tiina nii a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne to. Amo ta lage a pa se á sii mo á dona maama daanem baŋa ne.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam tɛ we, amo tete wó pa n dwi dem puli mo pa se n sɔŋɔ kom jeini de dam. 12Nmo ŋwea kam ná ba ka ti ye ba kwei‑m ba suli mɛ ba déem na suli nmo kwoa bam to, a ta wó pa n dwi dem wone nɔɔno dedoa zaŋe se wonto leiri nmo yuu ne o ji pɛ. A maa wó pa se o paare dem jeini de dam. 13Ko ye wonto mo wó lɔ sɔŋɔ amo yere dem zulim ŋwaane. Amo ta wó pa se wonto dwi dem taa di paare dem taa wuu. 14Amo wó taa ye o kwo, se o de taa ye amo bu. O ná ke o sa chwoŋa, a lage a ma da-lɔŋɔ mo a ma a de‑o chwoŋa ne, ye a korese‑o nenɛɛne nabiina na ke ba bia tei to. 15Amo nam bá fɔge a dɔne a swono kom o baŋa ne, nenɛɛne a déem na ke tei dedaane Sɔɔl ye a le‑o paare dem wone se nmo laam ji pɛ to. 16Amo wó pa se n paare dem taa wora taa. Ko daa bá jei amo yiga ne. Maŋa maama se ko taa vei wuu, nmo sɔŋɔ kom wó na dwi se n paare dem fɔge de ja dam.’ ”
17Natan ma ta kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na le o bere‑o to de David.
David na ware Wɛ tei to
18David ma vo o zo Baŋa Wɛ wara-vwei dem o jeini da, ye o ware Wɛ o we:
“Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo ye wɔ mo, amo dwi dem de ye bɛ mo, ye n zeini amo tento se ko yi zem? 19De konto maama de, n ta boŋe se n ke-ne lanyerane n woli da! Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo laam nam tiŋi ni mo a jwa dwi dem ŋwaane. Ko maa ye wo-kenkagele ko pa-ne! 20Amo nam daa jege bɛ mo se a ta? Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo ye n tontoŋeno mo ye n yei a maama n tia. 21Ko ye nmo tete ni-gwonim dem ŋwaane de n boboŋa yam ŋwaane mo n ke wo-kamunnu tento maama, ye n daare n le-te n bere-ne.
22Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, konto ŋwaane mo nmo tiini n ye kamunu! Nmo dwoŋi tera! Nmo yerane mo ye Wɛ. Dé yɔɔre dé yei konto mo chekke. 23Debam Isarele tiina bam mo ye dwi dedwe logo baŋa ne. Dwi dedwoŋi tera de na ma de Isarele tiina bam. Nmo déem jwoŋi-ba kabɛɛne wone mo pa se ba ji nmo tete nɔɔna, se n daare n pa n yere zaŋe wɛɛne. Nmo na vere-ba Ejipti tiina jeŋa ne to, n déem ke wo-kenkagela na jege foone to mo ba tetare ne. Ko ta ná ye dwi tiina balo na kwaane se ba che-ba to, n zeili banto mo de ba wa maama. 24Nmo ma‑n kuri Isarele dwi tiina bam se ba taa ye nmo tete nɔɔna se ko taa vei wuu. Ko daare nmo Baŋa Wɛ de ma ji banto Wɛ wom.
25Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, laam pa se n ni-gwonim dem, n na ke amo de a dwi dem ŋwaane to taa jege kuri se ko taa vei wuu. Seene n ke kolo nmo na tage to, 26se n yere dem taa ye kamunu taa wuu. Nɔɔna laam wó taa tɛ ba we, ‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne.’ Ko ta wó pa se amo wolo na ye n tontoŋeno David to sɔŋɔ kom na dwi se ko taa vei wuu.
27Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo ye Isarele dwi tiina Wɛ wom. Nmo nam le wonnu tento maama n bere-ne we a dwi dem wó puli pa se a sɔŋɔ kom jeini de dam. Konto ŋwaane mo pɛ se a na baare a lwoori‑m konto dwoŋi. 28Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo seene n ye Baŋa Wɛ chekke mo! Nmo ni taane dem ye chega mo. Nmo nam pwooli wo-laaro tento n pa amo wolo na ye n tontoŋeno to mo. 29Amo lwoori‑m se n swɛ a kwaga kam swolim mo, se n ta‑n ke-ba zaane taa wuu. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo na gwoni n ni konto to, n swolim wó yɔɔre de taa tɔge a dwi dem mo se ko taa vei wuu!”

english_text:
A List of David's Victories in War
(1 Chronicles 18.1-13)
1Later, David attacked and badly defeated the Philistines. Israel was now free from their control.
2David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
3David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob. 4In the battle, David captured 1,700 cavalry and 20,000 foot soldiers. He also captured war chariots, but he destroyed all but 100 of them. 5When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed 22,000 of them. 6He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
7Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem. 8He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
9-10King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze. 11David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from 12Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, Amalek, and from King Hadadezer of Zobah.
13 David fought the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed 18,000 of their soldiers. When he returned, he built a monument. 14David left soldiers all through Edom, and the people of Edom had to accept him as their ruler.
Wherever David went, the Lord helped him.
A List of David's Officials
(1 Chronicles 18.14-17)
15David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
16Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army.
Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
17Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests.
Seraiah was the secretary.
18Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard.
David's sons were priests.
translation_text:
David na di jara yalo maama to
1Konto kwaga ne, David déem ma vo o jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara. O ma di-ba pa se ba na ba chaveera. O ma chɔge ba dam ba teo kom maama wone.
2David déem ma kwaare jara o di Moaba tiina bam de. O ma pa se ba peini tega ne ba twoŋi daane, ye o laam kwei ŋona o maŋe-ba kuni betɔ betɔ o vo o ti. Ŋona kam dedɔrem kuni belei ná yi mɛ, ba wó go nɔɔna bam konto mo. Ka dedɔrem yi dedoa ná daare ka yi mɛ, ba wó yage se banto taa ŋwe mo. Moaba tiina bam déem ma lɛɛre ba zo David dam kuri ne, ye ba tui ba ŋwe lampwoo ba pa‑o.
3Rehobi bu Hadadezere déem ye Zoba teo pɛ mo. O nam ya maa vei se o jwoori o jwoŋi Yuferata buga laŋa kam teene dem mo o taa tei. David ma jeeri Hadadezere de jara o di. 4David de o nɔɔna bam ma ja Hadadezere jar-keira balo na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna yuu ne to moro de bia yarepɛ (1,700), ko woli de o jar-keira balo na vei tega ne to morro finlei (20,000). David ma le ba sisein-nɔɔna bi (100) se o taa jege o vaŋa o jara-keim torokooro, ye o daare o bwori selo na daare to nɛ pa se gwarege.
5Aram tiina balo déem na zoore Damasika laŋa kam ne to ma nwoŋi ba vo se ba woli Hadadezere. David ma jeeri-ba de jara ye o go ba nɔɔna morro finlei-telei (22,000). 6David ma daare o ja o jar-keira badwonna o vo che Aram tiina bam laŋa kam maama. Damasika ne mo konto. Aram tiina bam déem ma zo David dam kuri ne, ye ba ŋwe lampwoo ba pa‑o. Mɛ maama David ná via, Baŋa Wɛ yeini o pa se o di o dona mo jara wone. 7David ma vere sabu-seŋa jara zela yalo Hadadezere dedɛɛra bam ya na jege to o ja o jwoori o vo Jerusalem. 8Ko ta ná ye Teba dedaane Berotayi teene dem Hadadezere na tei to, Pɛ David ma zo de wone o vere channa wonnu dedɛ o ja o viiri.
9Hamafa teo Pɛ Toyi déem ma ni we David di Hadadezere jar-keira bam maama. 10Toyi tete déem ya ke jara kuni dedɛ mo de Hadadezere. O ma toŋe o bu Joram se o vo o jɔɔne David o ke‑o yu-ywoŋo lei de o na wane Hadadezere o di to ŋwaane. Joram ma ja lu-nyenno pɛɛra, de sabu-seŋa pɛɛra, de channa pɛɛra o vo o pa David. 11David ma kwei pɛɛra yam konto o pa se ba taa mae ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. O déem ya maŋe o ke konto dwoŋi de lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa wonnu telo o na vere o dona bam tei ne to mo. 12O dona balo o na di to teene dem maa ye: Edom, de Moaba, de Amon, de Filisi, de Amaleki. O ta ma kwei jejegero telo o na vere Zoba teo Pɛ Hadadezere tei ne to o pa Baŋa Wɛ.
13David déem ma vo Yɛ bwolo kom o kwaare jara de Edom tiina bam o go ba nɔɔna morro fuga-nana (18,000). O na jwoori jara yam wone to, o yere déem ma tiini de zaŋe. 14O ma ja o jar-keira bam o vo o che Edom laŋa kam maama. Edom tiina bam maama laam ma zo David dam kuri ne. Mɛ maama David ná via, Baŋa Wɛ yeini o pa se o di o dona mo jara maama wone.
15David déem ma di paare Isarele tiina bam maama baŋa ne. O ma tɔge chwoŋa de o na ke o nɔɔna bam tei to, se ko taa lana ko pa-ba. 16Zeruya bu Joaba mo ye David jar-keira bam yiga tu. Ahiluda bu Jehosafate de ma nii woŋo maama se o popone-te o tiŋi. 17Ahituba bu Zadoki dedaane Abiatara bu Ahimeleka déem ye Wɛ kaanem tiina mo. Seraya maa ye David tɔn-poponno. 18Jehoyada bu Benaya mo nii Cherete tiina bam dedaane Peleti tiina bam. David bia bam ma toŋe kaanem tiina totoŋa ba pa‑o.

english_text:
David Is Kind to Mephibosheth
1 One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.” 2David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.”
“Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
3 David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.”
Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
4“Where is he?” David asked.
Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
5-6David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down.
David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?”
“Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
7David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
8Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
9David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family. 10You and your 15 sons and 20 servants will work for Mephibosheth. You will farm his land and bring in his crops, so that Saul's family and servants will have food. But Mephibosheth will always eat with me at my table.”
11-13Ziba replied, “Your Majesty, I will do exactly what you tell me to do.” So Ziba's family and servants worked for Mephibosheth.
Mephibosheth was lame, but he lived in Jerusalem and ate at David's table, just like one of David's own sons. And he had a young son of his own, named Mica.
translation_text:
Pɛ David dedaane Mefibosɛfi taane
1Dɛ dedwe mo David bwei o we, “Sɔɔl dwi dem nɔɔno wo daare se amo da Jonatan ŋwaane a ke kotu lanyerane na?”
2Sɔɔl diga kam déem nam jege ba tontoŋeno dedoa o yere na ye Ziba. Ba ma bwoŋi‑o ba pa David. O na yi pɛ wom tei to, mo David bwei‑o o we, “Nmo mo ye Ziba to na?” O de ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, amo ye n tontoŋeno Ziba mo.”
3Pɛ David ma bwei‑o o we, “Sɔɔl dwi dem nɔɔno daa wo daare se a ke kotu lanyerane Wɛ zaane dem ŋwaane na?” Ziba ma leiri o we, “Jonatan ta daare bu dedoa. O nam gwarege mo o nɛ sem maama ne o jei.”
4Pɛ David daa ma bwei o we, “O nam wo yei ne mo?” Ziba ma leiri o we, “O wo Lo-Debara ne mo, Ameli bu Makira sɔŋɔ ne.”
5Pɛ David ma toŋe pa se ba vo Lo-Debara ba ja‑o ba ba o tei. 6Jonatan bu wom konto yere mo ye Mefibosɛfi. O kwo-nakwe maa ye Sɔɔl. O na tu o yi David tei to, o ma vwi o yibia tega ne o jɔɔne‑o. David ma bwoŋi‑o o we, “Mefibosɛfi!” O de ma leiri o we, “Amo wolo na ye n tontoŋeno to mo tento.”
7David ma ta‑o o we, “Yé ta‑n fona. Amo boboŋa maŋe ya ja se a ke‑m lanyerane mo n kwo Jonatan ŋwaane. A wó kwei tega kalo maama ya na ye n kwo-nakwe Sɔɔl nyem to a jwoori a pa‑m. A ta pɛ‑m chwoŋa se n ta‑n zoore amo sɔŋɔ kom ne n di wodiu kolo amo na wó di to.” 8Mefibosɛfi daa ma vwi o yibia tega ne ye o we, “Amo ye n tontoŋeno mo, a de kukuri-teka ba gare daane. Bɛŋwaane mo ye n boŋe se n ke-ne lanyerane konto?”
9Pɛ David ma bwoŋi Sɔɔl tontoŋeno Ziba o ta ded‑o o we, “Amo kwei woŋo kolo maama ya na ye nmo tu Sɔɔl de o diga kam nyem to mo a jwoori a pa o naa Mefibosɛfi. 10Nmo dedaane n bia, de n tontoŋena bam maama jege se á ta‑á vare kare sem mo á pa Mefibosɛfi. Se ná ke wodiu, á wó ja á ba á pa o diga kam se ba yé ga. Ko nam ná ye Mefibosɛfi, wonto lage o taa di wodiu kolo amo na wó di a sɔŋɔ kom ne to mo.”
Ziba déem nam jege bakeiri fuga-banu de tontoŋena finlei mo. 11O ma leiri Pɛ David o we, “A ye n tontoŋeno mo. A nam wó ke tei maama n na bere se a ke to.”
Mefibosɛfi laam ma lɛɛre o tɔge o di kolo maama David na yeini o di to, nenɛɛne pɛ bia bam na di tei to. 12O maa jege bakeiri-pwola mo o yere na ye Mika. Ziba sɔŋɔ tiina bam maama déem ma ji Mefibosɛfi tontoŋena. 13Mefibosɛfi na gwarege o nɛ sem maama ne to laam ma ba o zoore Jerusalem ne. Maŋa maama o maa tɔge o di kolo maama Pɛ wom na yeini o di to.

english_text:
Israel Fights Ammon
(1 Chronicles 19.1-19)
1Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king. 2David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
3But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.” 4Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away. 5They were terribly ashamed.
When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
6The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah, 1,000 were from the king of Maacah, and 12,000 were from the region of Tob. 7David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
8The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
9Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans. 10He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites. 11Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you. 12Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
13Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them. 14When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
15The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again. 16Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
17David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them. 18The Arameans attacked, but then they ran from Israel. David killed 700 chariot drivers and 40,000 cavalry. He also killed Shobach, their commander.
19When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_text:
David di Amon tiina bam
1Konto kwaga ne, Amon tiina pɛ Nahasi ma te. O bu Hanun ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ. 2David ma ta o we, “Amo lage a ke Nahasi bu Hanun lanyerane mo nenɛɛne o kwo de déem na ke amo lanyerane tei to.” O ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba ke Hanun lei de o kwo lua kam.
David nɔɔna bam na yi Amon tiina laŋa kam to, 3Amon tiina dedɛɛra bam ma ta de ba pɛ Hanun ba we, “Nmo pɛ chega we David boŋe lanyerane mo ye o toŋe nɔɔna se ba ba ba ke n kwo lua kam lei na? Lɔre we o toŋe-ba se ba ŋɔ ba nii dé teo kom mo, se o wane o ba o di debam.” 4Hanun ma pa se ba ja David tontoŋena bam ba cheeri ba twana yam ba daare chichwo-chwooru. Ba ta ma ja ba gwaaro tem tetare ne ba gwoni ba yage se ko yi ba takeira seeni. Ba laam ma yage-ba se ba viiri de kuri-nɔrɔ. 5David tontoŋena bam ma kɔre se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ, chaveera na jege-ba to ŋwaane. David na nigi ko na ke-ba tei to, o ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba jeeri-ba chwoŋa ne. O ma pa-ba kwora o we, “Maŋe-na Jeriko ne se á twana yam ná nwoŋi maama se á laam jwoori sɔŋɔ.”
6Amon tiina bam ma maane we ba kikia maama laam lwoi David momwa ne. Ba ma vo ba sɔ ni de Aram tiina balo na wo Bɛte-Rehoba ne, de Zoba ne to, ba jwoŋi ba jar-keira morro finlei (20,000). Ba ta ma jwoŋi jar-keira moro (1,000) Maaka teo pɛ tei ne, ye ba daare ba jwoŋi jar-keira morro fuga-balei (12,000) Toba tiina tei ne.
7David na lɔre ko ni ne to, o ma toŋe Joaba se o ja o babɛ sem kɔgɔ kom maama o vo o jeeri-ba de jara. 8Amon tiina bam ma gwɛ ba nwoŋi ba chichei ba zege ba te-fɔrɔ kom manchwoŋo ni ne se ba ke jara yam. Ko daare Aram tiina balo na nwoŋi Zoba de Rehobi to, de Toba tiina bam, dedaane Maaka tiina bam de laam ma chichei ba zege teo kom pwola ne ye ba cheiga.
9Joaba ma lɔre we ba dona bam lage ba jeeri-ba yiga de kwaga maama mo. O ma kuri Isarele jar-keira bam wone balo na tiini ba yei jara laŋa chekke to, se banto yɔɔre ba jeeri Aram tiina bam. 10Jar-keira balo na daare to, o ma ke-ba o nyaane Abisayi jeŋa ne se banto maama vo ba jeeri Amon tiina bam. 11Joaba laam ma ta Abisayi o we, “Nmo ná nɛ we Aram tiina bam tiini ba dana ba dwoi amo, se n ba n woli-ne. Amon tiina bam de nam ná dana ba dwoi nmo, amo de wó ba a woli‑m. 12Ke dam n tete kuri ne se n ta ta‑n jege baare! Pa-na dé jaŋe dé pa dé nɔɔna bam dedaane dé Tu Wɛ wom teene dem ŋwaane. Baŋa Wɛ wó ke kolo na su o yi to!”
13Joaba de o jar-keira bam ma ja jara yam ba jeeri Aram tiina bam, ye ba duri ba jage. 14Amon tiina bam na nɛ we Aram tiina bam duri ba jage to, mo ba de duri ba jwoori ba zo ba teo kom wone, ye ba daare Abisayi de o jar-keira kɔgɔ kom. Jara yam ma ti pa se Joaba jwoori o vo Jerusalem.
15Aram tiina bam na maane we Isarele tiina bam wane-ba ba di to, mo ba jwoori ba la ba jar-keira bam ba ke daane. 16Zoba teo Pɛ Hadadezere ma bwoŋi Aram tiina balo na wo Yuferata buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to se ba vo ba jeeri Helam ne. Hadadezere jar-keira yiga tu Sobaka déem wo ba yiga ne mo. 17David ma maane ba na ke tei to. O de ma la Isarele jar-keira bam maama o ke daane. Ba ma vo ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ba lɛɛne ba vo ba yi Helam. Aram tiina bam ma chichei ba fɔge ba zege ye ba jeeri David de jara. 18Isarele tiina bam ma fe Aram tiina bam ba zeili pa se ba duri ba jage. David de o nɔɔna bam ma go ba dona balo na dɔge sisei-torokooro yuu to bia yarepɛ (700). Ba ta ma go balo na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna to morro finna (40,000). Ko ná ye ba jar-keira bam yiga tu Sobaka, ba ma tiini ba ke zonne o yera ne, pa se o te jara kaporo kom ne. 19Hadadezere kwaga pwa bam maama ma maane we Isarele tiina bam yɔɔre ba di-ba mo jara wone. Ba ma lwoori yibwona Isarele tiina bam tei ne ye ba daare ba sɛ ba pa-ba.
Aram tiina bam laam ma kɔre se ba daa woli Amori tiina bam jara keim baŋa ne.

english_text:
David and Bathsheba
(1 Chronicles 20.1a)
1 It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
2-4Late one afternoon, David got up from a nap and was walking around on the flat roof of his palace. A beautiful young woman was down below in her courtyard, bathing as her religion required. David happened to see her, and he sent one of his servants to find out who she was.
The servant came back and told David, “Her name is Bathsheba. She is the daughter of Eliam, and she is the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”
David sent some messengers to bring her to his palace. She came to him, and he slept with her. Then she returned home. 5But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
6David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.”
Joab sent Uriah 7to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?” 8Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house. 9But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
10Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
11Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
12Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.”
Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day, 13David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards. 14Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab. 15The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
16Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers. 17When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
18Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war. 19He gave the messenger these orders:
When you finish telling the king everything that has happened, 20he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall? 21 Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?”
Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
22The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him. 23He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate. 24Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
25David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
26When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him. 27Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son.

translation_text:
David dedaane Bafeseba taane
1Ko déem ma yi teeni punnu keim maŋa. Ko maa ye maŋa kalo pwa na yeini ba nwoŋi se ba ke jara to mo. David ma toŋe Joaba de o dedɛɛra badwonna, dedaane Isarele jar-keira bam maama, se ba vo ba kwaare jara de Amon tiina bam. Ba ma chɔge-ba ye ba daare ba li Raba teo kom se ba ja. Ko daare David tete ma maŋe Jerusalem ne.
2Dɛ dedwe, David ma peini wea tetare ne o dɔ. O na pɛ o zaŋe dedaan-ni maŋa ne to, mo o kare o sɔŋɔ kom nayuu ne o kekara. O ma dole o yia o na kaane na wo o sɔŋɔ ne o swɛ yera. Kaane wom déem tiini o lamma dedɛ. 3David ma toŋe nɔɔno se o vo o bwei o lɔre kaane wom laŋa maama. Nɔɔno wom ma ta o we, “Ko wó taa ye Bafeseba mo. O ye Eliam bukɔ mo. O baro maa ye Hiti tu Yuria.”
4David ma toŋe nɔɔna pa se ba vo ba ja kaane wom ba ba. Kaane wom na tu to, o ma peini ded‑o. Yanto da yam ne kaane wom ya ke o wo zarem mo, ye o daare o kwɛ o tete se ko maŋe de chullu tem. O ma zaŋe o jwoori o sɔŋɔ. 5Bafeseba ma ja puga, ye o toŋe o ta de David o we, “Amo jege puga mo.”
6David na lɔre konto to, o ma toŋe kwora o pa Joaba o we, “Ta de Hiti tu Yuria se o ba amo tei ywo-seeni.” Joaba ma toŋe Yuria David tei ne. 7Yuria na yi David tei to, mo David bwei o kwaga se o lɔre Joaba, de jar-keira bam laŋa na ye tei to. O ta ma bwei se o lɔre jara yam na vei tei to. 8O laam ma ta de Yuria o we, “Nam véi sɔŋɔ n sii fee.”
Yuria na nwoŋi Pɛ sɔŋɔ ne to, mo David toŋe nɔɔna se ba ja pɛɛre ba saŋe o kwaga ba vo ba pa‑o sɔŋɔ ne. 9Yuria nam wo vei o tete sɔŋɔ. O ma maŋe de pɛ tontoŋena bam, o peini pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo kom ni ne. 10David ma maane we Yuria wo vei sɔŋɔ, ye o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo nwoŋi chwo-dɔrɔ n ba n yi ywo-seeni. Bɛ mo tei ye n wo vei sɔŋɔ?” 11Yuria ma leiri‑o o we, “Isarele tiina de Judah tiina bam maama nwoŋi mo se ba ke jara. Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam de wo ba tei ne. Amo yiga tu Joaba de o dedɛɛra bam maama de tigi pwola ne. Ko laam nam wó ke tɛ mo se a vo sɔŋɔ a taa di ye a nyɔa, se a daare a peini de a kaane? Pɛ, a dugi n ŋwea kam ŋwaane de n tete yere dem ŋwaane we, a bá fɔge a ke konto!” 12David ma ta‑o o we, “Nam peini ywo zem, se jwa ne a laam wó yage‑m se n jwoori jara jei sem ne.”
Dɛ dem konto ne, Yuria ma maŋe Jerusalem ne o peini o poore tega. 13David ma bwoŋi‑o pa se ba di daane. O ma pa se ba nye Yuria dedaane sana, ye o tiini o bugi. De konto maama de, Yuria wo vei sɔŋɔ se o peini. O maŋe pɛ sɔŋɔ ni ne de pɛ tontoŋena bam mo o peini o sara kam ne.
14Tega na poore tetete to, David ma popone tɔnɔ o toŋe Yuria se o ja o vo o pa Joaba. 15Tɔnɔ kom popone ko we, “Kwei Yuria n zege jar-keira bam yiga ne, mɛ jara yam na tiini ya chana to, se á daare á tutwoni á jwoori kwaga á daare‑o o yerane se dé dona bam go‑o.”
16Joaba déem li Raba teo kom mo ye o nii ko maama. O ma kwei Yuria o zege jei selo ba dona bam babɛ sem na daga to. 17Teo kom nɔɔna ma nwoŋi ba jeeri Joaba jar-keira bam de jara. Ba ma go David nɔɔna bam badwonna ko woli de Yuria tete.
18Joaba ma toŋe kwora David tei ne se o bere‑o jara yam na ke tei to. 19O ma ta tontoŋeno wom o we, “Nmo ná tole jara yam na ke tei maama to n pa pɛ wom n ti, 20o bane wó wane de zaŋe ye o ta we, ‘Bɛ mo ye á tiini á yi teo kom se á ke jara de-ba? Abam ya yeiri we nɔɔna bam wó dale ba teo kabiri sem ne ba ta che-tɛɛra na? 21Á swei Gideon bu Abimeleka swia na? Ko déem ye kaane mo zege Tebeza teo kom kabira yuu ne o dole nɔŋɔ namim o de o yuu ne o go. Abam tiini á yi ba kabira kam teiŋa wo bɛ mo?’ Tɔ. Pɛ wom ná bwei‑m konto, se n ta ded‑o we, ‘Nmo tontoŋeno Yuria de tɔge o te mo.’ ”
22Tontoŋeno wom ma seene o vo o yi David tei, ye o tole kolo maama Joaba na bere‑o se o ta to. 23O ma woli da o we, “Dé dona bam ya tiini ba dana ba dwoi debam mo. Ba ma nwoŋi ba teo kom ba jeeri debam de jara pwola kam ne. Dé ma kwaane dé zeili-ba dé jwoori ba teo kom ni ne. 24Dáane mo ba che-tara bam zege ba teo kabiri sem yuu ne ba ta debam. Nmo nɔɔna bam badwonna tega, ye n tontoŋeno Yuria na ye Hiti tu to de tɔge o te mo.”
25David ma ta de tontoŋeno wom o we, “Nmo ná jwoori, se n ta de Joaba we, ‘Yé pa n wo chɔge de kolo na ke to. Wolo maama na lwoori o vo jara wone to wae o toa. Fɔge n ja baare. Tiini á kwaare-na jara yam de-ba se á di teo kom.’ ”
26Bafeseba na nigi we o baro wom tega jara yam ne to, o ma keeri dedɛ o ŋwaane. 27Lua kam ni na kɛ to, mo David toŋe o pa ba vo ba ja‑o ba ba pɛ sɔŋɔ pa se o ji o kaane. O déem ma lo bakeira o pa David.
Kolo David nam na ke to déem chɔge Baŋa Wɛ wo mo.

english_text:
1 and he sent Nathan the prophet to tell this story to David:
A rich man and a poor man lived in the same town. 2The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle, 3but the poor man had only one little lamb that he had bought and raised. The lamb became a pet for him and his children. He even let it eat from his plate and drink from his cup and sleep on his lap. The lamb was like one of his own children.
4One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
5David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die! 6And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
7Then Nathan told David:
You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul 8and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more. 9Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
10“Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace. 11 Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on. 12What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
13-14David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.”
“Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.” 15Then Nathan went back home.
David's Young Son Dies
The Lord made David's young son very sick.
16So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor. 17His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
18After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
19David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants.
“Yes, he did,” they answered.
20David got up off the floor; he took a bath, combed his hair, and dressed. He went into the Lord's tent and worshiped, then he went back home. David asked for something to eat, and when his servants brought him some food, he ate it.
21His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
22David answered:
While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.” 23But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me.
Solomon Is Born
24David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon 25and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.”
The End of the War with Ammon
(1 Chronicles 20.1b-3)
26Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress 27and sent a messenger to tell David:
I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply. 28Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
29David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city 30and took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about 35 kilograms of gold, and there was a valuable jewel on it. David put the jewel on his own crown. He also carried off everything else of value. 31David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities.
David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_text:
Natan na bwɛ David tei to
1 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma toŋe Natan David tei ne. Natan ma ta o we:
“Nɔɔna balei mo zoore teo dedoa wone. Ba dedoa ye nadum, wodwoŋi wom maa ye yiniga tu. 2Nadum wom vara bam gaale dedɛ, naane de pei de bone. 3Yiniga tu wom nam ba jege kolokolo, ko ná dae pi-chwɛ dedoa yerane mo o na yeigi. O ma kɔne-ka, ye ka be de o bia. O maa yeini o pae-ka o tete wodiu pa ka di, ye ka nyɔ o tete na. Pia kam maŋe ka tigi o nɛ baŋa ne mo. Chega to, o pia kam yɔɔre ka nye de o tete bukɔ mo. 4Dɛ dedwe mo veiru tu nadum wom sɔŋɔ. Nadum wom maa wo sɛ se o le o vara bam wone se ba ma ba ke na ba pa o veiru wom. O ma vo o vere yiniga tu wom pia kam se ba ma ba ke o veiru wom na bam.”
5David na nigi sensɔla kam to, o bane ma tiini de zaŋe dedaane nadum wom ye o ta de Natan o we, “Amo dugi de Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ we nɔɔno wom konto jege se o te mo! 6O ta wó ŋwe kolo o na vere yiniga tu wom tei ne to kuni bena mo o pa‑o, o na ba jege o ŋwaŋa to ŋwaane.”
7Natan laam ma ta de David o we, “Nmo mo ye nɔɔno wom konto! Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora mo tento:
Amo mo kuri‑m se n ta‑n ye Isarele tiina pɛ, ye a jwoŋi‑m a yage Sɔɔl jeŋa ne. 8A ma kwei Sɔɔl paare dem a pa‑m, ye a ta pa se o kaana bam ji nmo nyem. A ma pa se n di paare Isarele de Judah tiina bam maama baŋa ne. Konto ya ná ba daga mo de, a ya ta wó wane a woli ko wone kuni belei a pa‑m. 9Bɛŋwaane mo nmo nam tiini n gwooni amo Baŋa Wɛ taane dem, ye n daare n ke wo-balɔrɔ konto? Nmo pɛ se Amon tiina go Hiti tu Yuria jara ne. Nmo na go‑o to, n laam ma‑n daare n di o kaane! 10Nam lɔre we n diga tiina laam wó taa tɔge jara baŋa ne mo ba toa. Kokuri to, n ve amo mo ye n vere Yuria kaane se o ji nmo nyem.
11Chega ŋwaane to, a lage a pa se n tete yera nɔɔno mo ke‑m se ko yi. Nmo wó ta‑n nia se a kwei n kaana a pa nɔn-gaa se kotu peini de-ba pwooni yiga ne. 12Nmo na ke wɛleere to, n seigi mo n ke. Amo nam wó pa se keim dento ke pwooni yiga ne se Isarele tiina bam maama na.”
13David ma leiri Natan o we, “Amo tiini a ke wɛleere a chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga.” Natan ma leiri‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ kwei n wɛleere dem o ma o chɛ‑m. N daa‑n bá‑n te. 14Ko nam na ye tei to, n na tiini n nii Baŋa Wɛ n gwooni de n keim dem to ŋwaane, n bu wom mo wó te.”
15Konto kwaga ne, Natan laam ma viiri.
David bu wom toone
Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa se bu wolo Yuria kaane Bafeseba de David na loge daane to weele ye ko tiini ko chɛ. 16David ma lwoori Wɛ o pa bu wom se o na yazura, ye o vɔ ni. Tete maama ne, o ná yeini o zo diga se o peini, o ta tigi tega ne mo. 17O sɔŋɔ kom nakwa bam ma vo o tei ba kwaane ba lwoori‑o se o zaŋe tega kam ne ye ba ga. O ma ve se o da de-ba o di wodiu.
18Bu wom weele da yarepɛ mo ye o te. David dedɛɛra bam ma kɔre se ba pa o lɔre ko ni ne. Ba déem bwɛ ba tete ne mo ba we, “Bu wom ya ta na ŋwe ye dé ŋɔɔne taane de David to, o ve se o leiri dé taane dem. Bu wom laam nam na tege tento to, de wó ke tɛ mo dé ta dé bere‑o? Dé ná wo lɔre, o wó wane o ke zonne o tete yera ne!”
19David na tole o na we o tontoŋena bam jege woŋo mo ba waase ba bere daane to, o ma maane we bu wom mo tega. O ma bwei-ba o we, “Bu wom tege mo na?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ɛɛ, Wɛ jwoŋi‑o mo o daare debam.”
20David na nigi konto to, o ma pɛ o zaŋe tega kam ne. O ma vo o swɛ o yera, o daare o turi nuga. O ma leiri o gwaaro o zo, ye o laam vo o zo Wɛ wara-jei sem ne o zuli Baŋa Wɛ. O na zuli Wɛ o ti to, mo o jwoori o tete sɔŋɔ ye o we, ba ke wodiu ba pa‑o. O ma jwoŋi wodiu kom o di. 21O dedɛɛra bam ma bwei‑o ba we, “Nmo keim dem ke debam yaau dedɛ. Bu wom ta na ŋwe to, nmo keeri mo o ŋwaane, ye n vɔ ni. O laam nam na tege to, n zaŋe mo n wora n di wodiu. Bɛ mo konto?”
22David ma leiri-ba o we, “Bu wom ya ta na ŋwe to, amo ya vɔ ni mo ye a keera. A ya boŋe we Baŋa Wɛ wó wane o duri amo yibwona mo ye o pa bu wom wori. 23Amo nam gɛ‑o. Bɛŋwaane mo a daa wó taa vɔ ni? Amo wó wane a pa bu wom jwoori o taa ŋwe na? Dɛ wora amo na wó vo bu wom tei, se wonto daa ba lage o jwoori o ba amo tei.”
24David déem ma gane o kaane Bafeseba se o pa o bochare peini tega ne. Ba daa ma peini daane ye o ja puga o lo bakeira. Ba ma pa bu wom konto yere we ‘Solomon’. Baŋa Wɛ ma swoi bu wom. 25Ko ma pa se o toŋe o ni-jwoŋinu Natan se o vo o pa bu wom yere we ‘Jedidia’, Baŋa Wɛ na swoi‑o to ŋwaane.
David di Raba teo kom
26Ko daare Joaba déem daa ta jeeri Amon tiina balo na zoore Raba teo wone to de jara. O ma di teo kom paare jei sem. 27O laam ma toŋe kwora o pa David ye o we, “Amo ke jara de Raba teo kom ye a wane mɛ ba teo kom na bam na zege da ba tui to a ja. 28Nam kwaane n la dé jar-keira balo na daare to n ke daane, se n ba n jeeri teo kom de jara n daare n di-ba. Nmo ná wo ke konto, ye amo tete ná di teo kom, amo laam wó jwoŋi yere nmo yiga ne.”
29David ma seene o la o jar-keira bam o ke daane o vo o jeeri Raba tiina bam de jara. O ma wane teo kom o jwoŋi o tei. 30David ma dɔne sabu-seŋa paare yipuga kam ba pɛ wom yuu ne. Ka dunni daga dedɛ, nenɛɛne kilo fintɔ-tenu (35), ye kandwɛ-nyeno mo meeli ka yera ne. Ba ma kwei kandwɛ dem ba ke David yipuga kam ne. O de o nɔɔna bam déem ta ma pɛ teo kom jejegero dedɛ ba ja ba viiri. 31Ko nam ná ye teo kom nɔn-bia bam, o déem kwei-ba mo o de totoŋ-dɛɛra wone. O ma pa se ba yeini ba taa mae pengasa, de dwoora, de seene ba toŋa, se ba badaara de taa mage wara. David déem ke Amon tiina teene dem maama konto dwoŋi mo.
Konto kwaga ne, David dedaane o jar-keira bam maama ma jwoori ba vo Jerusalem.

english_text:
Amnon Disgraces Tamar
1David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her. 2But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
3Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted, 4and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.”
Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
5Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
6So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
7David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.” 8When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched. 9Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it.
Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone, 10he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.”
Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom. 11But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
12She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting! 13Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
14But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her. 15Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
16She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.”
But Amnon would not listen. 17He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
18The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her.
The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves. 19Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away.
Absalom Kills Amnon
20Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.”
Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely. 21When David heard what had happened to Tamar, he was very angry. But Amnon was his oldest son and also his favorite, and David would not do anything to make Amnon unhappy.
22Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
23Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there. 24Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
25David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
26Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.”
David asked, “Why should he go with you?” 27But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom.
Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king. 28But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
29Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
30While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.” 31David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
32Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him. 33Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead, 34and Absalom has run away.”
One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
35Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
36No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly. 37-38 David was sad for a long time because Amnon was dead.
David Lets Absalom Come Home
Absalom had run away to Geshur, where he stayed for three years with King Talmai the son of Ammihud. 39David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_text:
Aminon dedaane Tamara taane
1David bu Abisalom déem jege nakɔ, o yere mo Tamara. O maa ye ka-laao. David bu wodwoŋi de maa wora, o yere na ye Aminon. Wonto fera maa tiini ya wo o nakɔ Tamara wone. 2Tamara ya ta yeiri baaro. Konto to, Aminon ma lɔre we ko wó taa chamma se o yi o nakɔ wom yuu. O ma da ko ŋwaane o weele, boboŋe dem na tiini de daane‑o to ŋwaane.
3Aminon déem jege yuudwoŋi, o yere mo Jonadabi. O maa ye David zembaaro Simea bu. Jonadabi déem jege swa-goa mo ko ja gaale. 4Dɛ dedwe o ma bwei Aminon o we, “Bɛ mo daane‑m? Nmo ye pa-bu mo ye ko dae se dɛ maama n ta‑n jei de wo-chechɔgɔ. Nam ta n bere-ne kolo na jege‑m to.”
Aminon ma ta o we, “A fera mo tiini ya zo a nyaane Abisalom nakɔ Tamara.” 5Jonadabi ma leiri‑o o we, “Zo n ta‑n tigi n sara baŋa ne, n paale n ke nenɛɛne n weele mo tei. Nmo kwo ná tu se o daane n jaweo kom, se n ta ded‑o we, ‘A kwo, pa a nakɔ Tamara ba amo tei ywo-seeni o ke wodiu o pa-ne. Amo lage se o saŋe wodiu kom a yiga ne se a taa nae, se a taa di-ko o jeŋa ne.’ ”
6Aminon ma seene o zo o tigi sara wone o ke nenɛɛne o weele mo tei. Pɛ David na tu se o daane o jaweo kom to, mo o tage‑o o we, “Popo, amo lage se a nakɔ Tamara mo ba ywo-seeni o fɔge maasa fenfee o pa-ne, se a di o jeŋa ne.” 7David ma sɛ. O ma toŋe kwora o sɔŋɔ kom ne o ta de Tamara o we, “Zaŋe n vo n nabɔ Aminon sɔŋɔ n ke wodiu n pa‑o se o di.” 8Tamara na yi da to, dedaane Aminon tigi sara baŋa ne mo. O ma zwɛ muni o viiri Aminon yibia ne. O ta ma fɔge maasa ye o tigi o nia. 9Bukɔ wom laam ma le wodiu kom o ke zoŋa ne o pa‑o se o di. Aminon ma ve ye o we, “Nɔɔno maama nwoŋi pwooni ne se á daare-ne na!” Nɔɔna bam maama ma seene ba nwoŋi.
10Aminon laam ma ta de Tamara o we, “Nam kwei wodiu kom n ja n zo diga kam wone amo na tigi mɛ to, se a jwoŋi wodiu kom n jeŋa ne a di.” Tamara ma seene o ja wodiu kom o zo o na tigi diga kalo wone to. 11O na jege wodiu kom o ma yi o yera to mo Aminon zi‑o ye o we, “Amo nakɔ, sɛ se dé peini daane!” 12O de ma leiri‑o o we, “A nabɔ, yé fe-ne se dé toŋe totoŋ-zɔɔne dento! Keim-balɔrɔ konto dae se ko ke Isarele tega baŋa ne. 13Nmo ná zi amo, a chaveera yam bá na kwolim jei. Ko ta wó pa se a kwei tetɔ-goro mo a kwoli a yuu! Ko nam ná ye nmo, nɔɔna maama Isarele ne wó ta we, n ye wo-koro mo. Nam ja n tete, se n ŋɔɔne dedaane pɛ wom, se o bá ve se o kwei-ne o pa‑m se n ma-ne n ke n kaane.” 14Aminon maa wo sɛ se o cheigi o taane dem. O na dana o dwoi bukɔ wom to o ma wane o zi‑o o lage.
15Aminon na ke konto o ti to, o daa maa ba lage se o yi na Tamara. O maa tiini o chuli‑o se ko dwoni o fera ya na zo o wone tei to. O ma ta ded‑o o we, “Zaŋe n nwoŋi daa a yiga ne!” 16Tamara ma leiri o we, “Chwoŋa tera se n zeili-ne! Nmo ná ke konto, ko maŋe ko wó taa ye lɛɛro ko dwoi n na chɔge-ne tento to.”
Aminon maa wo sɛ o taane dem. 17O ma bwoŋi o tontoŋeno ye o ta‑o o we, “Vaŋe kaane wonto n ja n nwoŋi n yage pwooni ne, se n daare n pe a bworo kom.” 18O tontoŋeno wom ma seene o vaŋe Tamara o ja o nwoŋi ye o daare o fɔge o pe bworo kom.
Tamara nam ya zo gare-dedɔrɔ na tiini ko jege nenɔŋa to mo. Tento mo ye gwaaro telo dwi pɛ bukɔ-pwoli na yeini ba zoora to. 19Tamara laam ma pɛ tentwarem o chaare o yage o yuu maama, ye o daare o ja o gare-dedɔrɔ kom o kaare kaare. O ta ma kwei o je o daŋe o yuu ne, ye o chwoosa o maa vei sɔŋɔ.
20O nabɔ Abisalom ma na‑o ye o bwei‑o o we, “N nabɔ Aminon mo ke lɛɛro tento nmo yera ne na? O nam na ye n nabɔ to, yé ke sɔɔ se nɔɔna maane ko ni ne. A nakɔ, nam ta yé pa se ko taa wɔe‑m.” Tamara ma vo Abisalom sɔŋɔ ne o zoore da. O maa yɔɔre o jei de wo-chechɔgɔ yerane.
21David déem ma ni kolo maama Aminon na ke to. O bane ma tiini de zaŋe. 22Se ko ná ye Abisalom, o wo sɛ se o ŋɔɔne de Aminon, ko ná maŋe ko ye ta-laao naa ta-balɔrɔ de. O déem nam tiini o chuli‑o mo, o na chɔge o nakɔ to ŋwaane.
Abisalom go Aminon
23Konto kwaga ne bena yalei maa kɛ. Abisalom tontoŋena maa wo Baal-Hazora ne se ba fane o pei sem koro. Jei sem konto wo Efrayim teo kom seeni mo. Abisalom ma bwoŋi pɛ bia bam maama se ba da ba jeeri da. 24O ma vo o ta de Pɛ David o we, “Pɛ, amo tontoŋena bam mo wora ba fane a pei sem koro. Nmo dedaane n nakwa ya ná sɛ se á ba da, ko wó taa lamma.” 25David ma leiri‑o o we, “A bu, ko bá wane ko ke konto. Dé maama ná lage dé ba, nmo wó chɔge n jeŋa mo.”
Abisalom ta ma kwaane se o nii David wó sɛ o vo na, ye o wo sɛ. David ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o pa Abisalom. 26Abisalom laam ma ta o we, “Nmo nam ná bá wane n vo, yage se a zembaaro Aminon tɔge de debam o vo.”
Pɛ David ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo ye n lage se wonto tɔge o vo?” 27Abisalom ma tiini o gigili David yia pa se o ga ga o yage o pa Aminon tɔge dedaane pa-bia badwonna bam se ba vo Abisalom pei sem koro fanem ne.
28Ba na ti kuri dem yiga to, Abisalom ma pa o tontoŋena bam ni o we, “Fɔge á ta‑á yere-na Aminon. O ná nyɔge sana o bugi, amo wó ke woŋo se ko bere we chwoŋa tiga se á go‑o. Konto ná kea, se á zaŋe o baŋa ne á go‑o. Yé ta‑á fona, se ko ye amo mo pɛ abam ni dem konto. Ke-na dam á tete kuri ne, se á daare á ta‑á jege baare.” 29Abisalom tontoŋena bam ma seene ba ke kolo o na bere-ba se ba ke to. Ba go Aminon mo. Pɛ wom bia badaara bam maama na nɛ konto to, ba ma di ba bona-sisei ba duri ba viiri.
30Ba ta na wo chwoŋa ne ba maa kɛ to, kwora ya maŋe ka yi David ka we, “Abisalom zaŋe o go n bia bam maama. Dedoa daa wo daare.” 31Pɛ David na nigi konto to, o ma kaare o gwaaro o wo-chechɔgɔ kom ŋwaane, ye o daare o dole o tete tega ne o tiga. O tontoŋena bam maama de maa zege o tei ne ye ba kaare ba gwaaro.
32David zembaaro Simea bu Jonadabi ma yi o tei o ta o we, “Pɛ, ko dae we ba go n bia bam maama. Aminon yerane mo tega. Abisalom nam maŋe o ja boboŋa se o go‑o ko zege maŋa kam Aminon na chɔge o nakɔ Tamara to mo. 33Nam yé sɛ we n bia bam maama tega, se Aminon yerane mo ba goa.”
34Ko daare Abisalom, wonto déem duri mo o jei.
Nɔn-doŋo wolo ba na le se o taa zege o yere teo kom to laam ma tole o na nɔn-kɔgɔ na wo Horon chwoŋa ne ba tɔge zwoŋo yuu ne ba siseiri ba beena. O ma vo o ta pɛ wom o we, “Amo nɛ nɔɔna na zege Horon seeni ba beena.” 35Jonadabi ma ta de David o we, “Nmo bia bam mo konto ba maa beene, nenɛɛne a na maŋe a ta tei to.”
36O ni dem maŋe de wo to tega ne, dedaane David bia bam na yi da. Ba maama ma to keira ne ye ba chwoosa baŋa baŋa. David dedaane o nakwa bam de ma tiini ba keeri dedɛ.
37-38Abisalom déem nam ya duri o vo o seigi o nu nakwe Talimayi tei ne mo o wora. Wonto maa ye Amihuda bu ye o ta ye Gesura teo pɛ. Abisalom déem maŋe Gesura ne o ke bena yatɔ mo.
Ko daare David ma keeri o bu Aminon lua kam o dáane. 39O wo laam ma ba ko to de Aminon toone dem. O boboŋa ma jwoori ya vo Abisalom wone se ba ke daane.

english_text:
1Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom, 2-3and he sent someone to bring in the wise woman who lived in Tekoa. Joab told her, “Put on funeral clothes and don't use any makeup. Go to the king and pretend you have spent a long time mourning the death of a loved one.” Then he told her what to say.
4The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
5David asked, “What's the matter?”
She replied:
My husband is dead, and I'm a widow. 6I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other. 7Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land.
Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
8“Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
9The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
10He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
11“Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!”
He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
12Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?”
“Yes,” he answered.
13The woman said:
Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back. 14We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
15Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help. 16In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
17 I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
18Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!”
The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
19David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?”
The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say, 20but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
21David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
22Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
23Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem, 24David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father.
Absalom Was Handsome
25No one in all Israel was as handsome and well-built as Absalom. 26His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
27Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful.
Absalom Finally Sees David
28Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father. 29He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused. 30Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
31Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
32Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
33Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_text:
Abisalom nɛ chwoŋa se o jwoori Jerusalem
1Zeruya bu Joaba déem ma maane we David boboŋa tigi Abisalom wone mo dɛ maama. 2O ma toŋe nɔɔno Tekoa teo ne se o bwoŋi kaane wodwoŋi o na tiini o jege swa to. O na tu to, Joaba ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ke nenɛɛne n keeri nɔɔno lua mo tei. Kwei lua gwaaro n zo, se n daare n yage n yuu yɔɔ yerane, n yé kwɛ n tete de terale nuga. Pa se ko taa nye nenɛɛne n keeri lua mo n dáane. 3Nmo laam ma‑n wó vo pɛ wom tei n ta kolo amo na wó bere‑m to.” Joaba laam ma bere kaane wom kolo maama o na wó ta de pɛ to.
4Tekoa tiina kaane wom ma vo o yi pɛ wom yiga o vwi o yibia tega ne o zuli‑o, ye o ta o we, “Pɛ, jan ja! Woli-ne!”
5Pɛ wom ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo n laga?” O de ma leiri o we, “Dé kwo, amo baro tega o daare-ne kadeim mo. 6A nam ya jege bakeiri selei mo. Dɛ dedwe mo ba vei kara ye jara to ba tetare ne dáane. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno na tera se o lwɛ-ba to, mo ba dedoa mage wodwoŋi wom o go. 7Dé sɔ-yuu kom maama laam nam zege amo baŋa ne se a ja a bu wom a ja a ba a pa-ba se ba go, o na go o choro kom to ŋwaane. Ba maa lage se ba pa a dwi dem ti mo. Wonto yerane laam mo ye a yi na daare. Ba ná go‑o, amo gɛ mo konto, a baro de daa maa ba taa jege bu se ko jwa bwoŋi o yere.”
8Pɛ wom ma ta de kaane wom o we, “Jwoori n vo sɔŋɔ, se a wó nii n taane dem baŋa ne se de kwɛ.” 9Tekoa tiina kaane wom ta maa we, “Pɛ, keim dem konto wo amo de a dwi dem yuu ne mo. Se ko ná ye nmo dedaane paare dem n na jege n di to, daanem dae se de yi‑m.”
10Pɛ wom laam ma ta o we, “Wolo maama ná ŋɔɔne taane dedaane‑m, se n ja kotu n ba amo yiga ne, se o daa bá na chwoŋa o daane‑m.” 11Kaane wom ta ma ta o we, “Konto to, nam kwei n Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere dem n du we, wolo na lage se o jwoori o jwoŋi a bu wolo na tege to jene dem to daa yé na chwoŋa se o go a bu wonto de o woli da.” Pɛ David maa we, “Amo dugi dedaane Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere we, n bu wom yu-yua dedoa tete bá gɔ ka to tega ne.”
12Kaane wom laam maa we, “Jan ja! Pɛ, pa-ne chwoŋa se a ta taane dedoa yerane a woli da.” Pɛ David ma leiri o we, “Ta‑n tɛa.” 13O laam ma ta Pɛ wom o we:
“Dé kwo, lɔre we n wo tɔge chwoŋa de n na jege Wɛ nɔɔna bam n ke keim delo to. Nmo tete bu wo sa-teo ne mo ye n wo pɛ‑o chwoŋa se o jwoori sɔŋɔ. Nmo nam na ŋɔɔne tei de amo to, n de n tete mo konto. 14Nɔɔno maama jege se o te mo. Toone nye de na balo na lwogi tega ne to mo, ba daa ware-ba se ba jwoori ba pɛ ba ke jeiga dedoa ne. Wɛ nam ba beeri nɔɔna toone, se ko ná ye balo na ba ŋwae to, o yeini o pore chwoŋa se ba wane ba jwoori o tei.
15Pɛ, amo na jaane taane dem a ba nmo tei to, ko ye nɔɔna bam na pɛ foone di amo to ŋwaane mo. A ye nmo tontoŋ-kana mo. A ma boŋe a tete ne we, a ná tu a ta de nmo, n wó wane-ne n woli. 16Pɛ, a nam jege chega we nmo wó seene n jwoŋi amo de a bu wom se wolo na kwaane se o chɔge debam to yé yi dé yuu. Wonto lage se dé ga dé tega kam popɔra Wɛ na pɛ debam to mo.
17Amo laam nam tɛ a tete ne mo we, ‘Amo wo laam tiga mo de kolo pɛ na gwoni ni se o ke to. Kokuri to, dé kwo, nmo nye nenɛɛne Wɛ maleka mo, n wae n kuri lanyerane dedaane balɔrɔ n pɔɔre daane. N Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó taa wora dede‑m.’ ”
18Pɛ wom ma ta de kaane wom o we, “Amo de lage a bwei‑m woŋo mo, nam yé seigi kolokolo de amo.” Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “A kwo, bwei n bwia yam.”
19Pɛ David ma bwei‑o o we, “Joaba yiga tɔge ka wo keim dento wone na?” Kaane wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, amo dugi nmo ŋwea kam ŋwaane we nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane se o fo chega kam nmo yiga ne. Nmo dedɛɛro Joaba mo seene o bere-ne kolo maama a na wó ke to, dedaane kolo maama a na jege se a ta to. 20O nam ke konto maama se ko pa keim dem mo pipiri de kwɛ. Dé kwo, nmo nam maŋe n jege swa mo, ne Wɛ maleka tei, n ma‑n yei kolo maama na ke dé tega kam baŋa ne to.”
21David laam ma bwoŋi Joaba ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Tɔ. A lage a ke n boboŋa yam mo. Zaŋe n vo n ja a bu Abisalom n jwoori n ba ywo-seeni.” 22Joaba ma vwi o yibia tega ne David yiga ne o zuli‑o. O ma daare o ta‑o o we, “Pɛ, a ke nmo lei. Amo laam nam lɔre we n yiga wo amo wone, dedaane n na sɛ n ke a na lage tei to.”
23Joaba déem ma zaŋe o vo Gesura o ja Abisalom o jwoori o ba Jerusalem. 24David nam ya maŋe o pa ni mo o we, “Abisalom maŋe se o vo o tete sɔŋɔ kom mo o taa wora. A bá sɛ se o ba amo tei.” Abisalom ma seene o vo o zoore o tete sɔŋɔ kom ne ye o wo nɛ pɛ wom yibia.
25Nɔɔn-nɔɔno déem tere Isarele tega kam maama ne ye ba tɛ o lam taane se ko maŋe dedaane Abisalom. Ko na zege o yuu ne se ko tu ko kwaare o napera seeni to, o mɛ mɛ ba jege gɛɛ. 26O déem yeini o pa se ba fa o yuu bedwe mo bene maama wone, o yu-ywei sem na tiini se dɔra ye se duna to ŋwaane. Ba ná yeini ba gwoni-se, se dunni wó taa maŋe de kilo telei mo. 27O déem jege bakeiri setɔ de busankana dedoa mo. Busankana kam yere maa ye Tamara. O na tu o ke nɔɔno to, o tiini o lana dedɛ.
28Abisalom déem zo Jerusalem ne bena yalei mo, ye o wo wane pɛ wom yibia o na. 29O ma toŋe o ta se Joaba ba o tei se o daare o ja taane dem o vo Pɛ David tei o pa‑o. Joaba ma ve se o vo Abisalom tei. Abisalom ta ma toŋe Joaba kwaga ne kuni balei maama ye o daa ta wo sɛ se o ba. 30Abisalom laam ma ta de o tontoŋena bam o we, “Nii-na, Joaba kara mo yeiri de amo kara kam. Ka wo mena nam wora ya ke lanyerane. Véi-na á de mini ka wone á zwɛ-ka.” Ba ma seene ba vo ba de mini Joaba kara kam ne.
31Joaba laam ma zaŋe o vo Abisalom sɔŋɔ o bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n pa n tontoŋena vo ba zwɛ a kara kam?” 32Abisalom ma leiri o we, “Amo toŋe n kwaga ne se n ba amo tei ye n wo sɛ. A ya lage se n vo pɛ wom tei n bwei‑o mo we, ‘Bɛŋwaane mo amo bere a zege Gesura ne a ba ywo-seeni? Ko nye de a ya ná maŋe dáane mo a zoora, ko ya wó taa gara ko pa-ne.’ Tɔ. Amo nam ta lage se a na pɛ wom mo. O nam ná yei we a keim wo maŋe, se o go-ne.”
33Joaba ma vo Pɛ David tei o tole kolo maama Abisalom na tage to o bere‑o. David ma pa ba bwoŋi Abisalom se o ba. O na yi da to, mo o vwi o yibia tega ne o ware‑o. Pɛ wom ma sɛ o peiga ye o ja‑o o kukwori.

english_text:
Absalom Rebels against David
1Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had 50 men run in front. 2He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?”
