mo o jwoori o ŋwe-ne konto dwoŋi.
22Amo yɔɔre a tɔge Baŋa Wɛ chwei sem mo.
A wo ywori a Tu Wɛ kwaga ne
se a daare a toŋe lwarem.
23O nia yam maama mo amo tɔga.
A maa wo ve chullu telo o na pɛ to.
24A jege chega mo o yiga ne,
a na cho a tete dedaane lwarem to ŋwaane.
25Ko ma pa se o jwoori o ke-ne lanyerane,
de a na tɔge chega chwoŋa
ye a kwori a toŋe chekke to ŋwaane.
26Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ!
Nmo yeini n jege chega mo
de balo na jege chega ba pa‑m to.
Balo na jege bora n yiga ne to mo,
nmo yɔɔre n toŋe lanyerane n pa-ba.
27Ko ná ye balo na jege wo-pwoŋo to,
nmo de ye wo-pwoŋo tu mo n pa-ba.
Ko daare balo na toŋe tusim kikia to,
n ke swa mo pa ko chɛ ba yera ne.
28Nmo yeini n jwoŋi nabwona mo n yaga.
Ko daare ye n pa kamun-nyena jwoori ba tu tega.
29 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo ye amo pwooni.
Chega to, n pae se lim delo na li amo to
jwoori de ji pwooni mo.
30Amo Tu Wɛ, nmo mo yeini n pa amo dam,
se a wane a zeili a dona bam kɔgɔ maama.
N dam dem konto ta ma woli-ne,
se a wane a faŋe a gaale a dona bam teo kabira,
ye a daare a di-ba.
31Amo Tu Wɛ chwoŋa kam lamma fase mo!
O ni taane dem yɔɔre de ye chega mo.
O wae o cho balo na seigi o woro kom wone to,
ne jara nantana na kwoli nɔɔna jara wone tei to.
32Wɛ dedwoŋi daa tera ko ná dae Baŋa Wɛ.
Wonto yerane mo ye peo kolo na ye dé dalem jei to.
33O maa jege dam ye o kwoli-ne.
O ma pa se a chwoŋa tigi jase se a taa vei ka wone.
34O ma pa se a nɛ kwaare tega,
nenɛɛne woŋa nɛ na ye tei to.
O maa cho-ne se a yé to peero tem yuu ne.
35Wonto ta bere-ne jara keim laŋa mo,
se a taa wae a saŋe taŋa kalo na vaŋe de dam to a tae.
36 Baŋa Wɛ,
nmo pɛ-ne jara-keim nantana se ka taa kwoli-ne,
ye n jwoŋi-ne n yage cham wone.
Nmo na sɛ se n woli-ne tei to pɛ se a ji babea.
37Nmo kwɛ chwoŋa kalo na yala to mo
n tiŋi amo yiga ne,
se a yé seeri a to tega ne.
38Amo pare a dona bam mo a ja.
A ma yɔɔre a mage ba maama a go,
se ba wolowolo yé daare.
39A chochoge-ba mo a de tega ne
pa se ba daa ware ba zaŋe wɛɛne,
a na nɔne-ba de a naga to ŋwaane.
40 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo pa-ne dam se a taa ma a ke jara.
N pae se a dona bam ba ba kuni dwoona amo yiga ne.
41N ta pae se foone ja a dona bam maama
ye ba pipiri mo ba duri ba daare-ne.
Amo ma yɔɔre a chɔge balo na chuli-ne to.
42Ba maa beeri wolim.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera se o jwoŋi-ba o yage.
Ba ma keeri ba jare Baŋa Wɛ,
ye o wo sɛ ba wara yam.
43Amo maa cho-ba a mumugi
se ba ji ne tega fwogo tei.
A ta maa nɔne-ba ye a chochoge-ba
nenɛɛne ba ye chwoŋa ni bworu mo tei.
44Ko ná ye pawe-nyena na wo a dwi tiina bam wone to,
nmo vere-ne n yage ba jeŋa ne mo.
Nmo ta ma‑n pa se a di paare teene dedɛ baŋa ne,
se a taa tei dwi tiina balo a ya na yeiri to.
45 Dwi-gɛ tiina mo tui ba gwane amo yiga ne de foone.
Ba ná yɔɔre ba ni a taane,
ba yeini ba sɛ a ni mo.
46Veira bam konto vɔna yeini ya da ya pare mo.
Ba ma zaŋe ba nwoŋi ba dalem jei sem wone,
ye ba yera sae de foone.
47 Baŋa Wɛ seene o ŋwe!
O maa ye peo kolo na ye amo dalem jei to.
Ko maŋe mo se dé taa tei‑o.
Pa-na dé tei Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Baŋa Wɛ!
Wonto nam mo jwoŋi amo o yage!
48Wonto mo jwoori o ŋwe jene a dona baŋa ne.
O maa ke dwi-gɛ tiina amo dam kuri ne.
49O ta vere-ne mo a dona jeŋa ne o yage.
Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ!
Nmo mo pa-ne dam se a di balo na chuli-ne to.
N ta ma‑n jwoŋi-ne nankɔ-nyena jeŋa ne.
50Konto ŋwaane nam mo, amo wó tei nmo yere,
se dwi-gɛ tiina taa yei n ni ne.
Chega ŋwaane to, Baŋa Wɛ,
amo wó leeni a tei nmo yere.
51 Baŋa Wɛ yeini o pa se o pɛ wom di wɔnɔ mo maŋa maama.
O maa tɔge o swono kom baŋa
o ke wolo o na kuri to lanyerane se ko taa vei wuu.
Ko maa ye amo David de a dwi dem mo konto.

english_text:
David's Last Words
1These are the last words of David the son of Jesse.
The God of Jacob chose David
and made him a great king.
The Mighty God of Israel
loved him.
When God told him to speak,
David said:
2The Spirit of the Lord
has told me what to say.
3Our Mighty Rock,
the God of Jacob, told me,
“A ruler who obeys God
and does right
4is like the sunrise
on a cloudless day,
or like rain that sparkles
on the grass.”
5I have ruled this way,
and God will never break
his promise to me.
God's promise is complete
and unchanging;
he will always help me
and give me what I hope for.
6But evil people are pulled up
like thornbushes.
They are not dug up by hand,
7but with a sharp spear
and are burned on the spot.
The Three Warriors
(1 Chronicles 11.10-19)
8These are the names of David's warriors:
Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed 800 men with his spear.
9The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran, 10except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
11Next was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. One time the Philistines brought their army together to destroy a crop of peas growing in a field near Lehi. The rest of Israel's soldiers ran away from the Philistines, 12but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
13One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley 14and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress, 15and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
16The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice 17and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.”
The Three Warriors did these brave deeds.
The Thirty Warriors
(1 Chronicles 11.20-47)
18Joab's brother Abishai was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and in one battle he killed 300 men with his spear. He was as famous as the Three Warriors 19and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
20Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion. 21Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it. 22-23Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
24-39Some of the Thirty Warriors were:
Asahel the brother of Joab
Elhanan the son of Dodo from Bethlehem
Shammah from Harod
Elika from Harod
Helez the Paltite
Ira the son of Ikkesh from Tekoa
Abiezer from Anathoth
Mebunnai the Hushathite
Zalmon the Ahohite
Maharai from Netophah
Heleb the son of Baanah from Netophah
Ittai the son of Ribai from Gibeah of the tribe of Benjamin
Benaiah from Pirathon
Hiddai from the streams on Mount Gaash
Abialbon from Beth-Arabah
Azmaveth from Bahurim
Eliahba from Shaalbon
Jashen
Jonathan the son of Shammah the Hararite
Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite
Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai from Maacah
Eliam the son of Ahithophel from Gilo
Hezro from Carmel
Paarai the Arbite
Igal the son of Nathan from Zobah
Bani the Gadite
Zelek from Ammon
Naharai from Beeroth, who carried the weapons of Joab the son of Zeruiah
Ira the Ithrite
Gareb the Ithrite
Uriah the Hittite
There were 37 in all.
translation_text:
David kweelim botare
1David botare selo o na popone o kweeli to mo tento:
“Cheigi-na Jesse bu David kwora.
Jakob Tu Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se o jwoŋi yere,
o daare o kuri‑o se o di paare.
O maa ye lein-leenu wolo Isarele tiina na swoi to.
2 Baŋa Wɛ Jworo mo bere-ne kolo a na wó ta to.
Chega ŋwaane to, o tɔge amo ni baŋa ne mo o ŋɔɔne.
3Isarele tiina Wɛ wom tete mo ŋɔɔne,
Wɛ wolo na ye Isarele tiina dalem jei to
ma ta de amo o we:
‘Pɛ wolo ná tɔge chega o tei o nɔɔna
ye o kɔre Wɛ,
4kotu nye de wɛ mo puli te-pora ne
ye kunkwonnu tere wɛɛne tei.
O ta maa nye de wea na pa se gaaro nyeene
doa nenem kwaga ne tei to.’
5Wɛ nam wó seene o ke zaane amo dwi dem baŋa ne konto dwoŋi mo.
Wonto gwoni ni de amo se o zeini-ne.
Ni-gwonim dem konto wó taa wora taa wuu.
Maŋa maama de bá fɔge de leiri,
de nam daa bá gɔ.
Baŋa Wɛ lage o yɔɔre o jwoŋi-ne mo o yage.
Kolo maama amo boboŋa na lage to mo,
Wɛ wó seene o ke o pa-ne.
6Ko nam ná ye nɔn-wo-korro maama,
banto nye de sabare selo nɔɔna na dole ba yage to mo.
N bá‑n wane n ma n jeŋa n ja sabare sento dwoŋi.
7Wolo ná lage o dwei sabare sem konto,
kotu jege se o kwei luu,
naa chichwei mo o ma o toŋe,
ye o laam daare o zwɛ-se kula!”
Bembɛ selo na woli David to
1 Tigisim 11:10-41
8Bembɛ selo déem na wo David tei ne ba woli‑o de jara-keim to yera mo tento:
Joseba-Basebɛfa déem mo ye ‘Bembɛ setɔ sem’ yiga tu wom. Wonto nwoŋi Tachemon mo. O déem jeeri nɔɔna bia nana (800) mo de jara. O ma kwei o chichwei o ma go ba maama jara-keim dedoa baŋa ne.
9Wolo na saŋe wonto kwaga bembɛ setɔ sem wone to déem ye Dodo bu Eleaza mo. Ba maa ye Ahohi sɔ-yuu tiina. Dɛ dedwe Filisi tiina bam na gilimi jara ŋwaane to, wonto de David ma yiŋi-ba de jara. Isarele jar-keira bam maama ma tutwoni ba jwoori kwaga, 10se ko daare Eleaza, wonto pɛ o zaŋe mo o jeeri Filisi tiina bam. O ma kwei o se-zɔɔ o jege-ba o zɔ o goe taa ye o daa ware se o de-ko tega ne o yera na chɛ to ŋwaane. Dento dɛ dem ne Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa se Isarele tiina bam di wɔnɔ dedɛ. Ko kwaga ne Isarele tiina bam ma jwoori ba ba ba pu Eleaza kwaga. Kolo yerane na daare se ba ke to maa ye se ba buŋi twa bam yera ba nii se ba daare ba vere ba zela yam.
11Wolo na saŋe o ke batɔ tu to ye Agee bu Samma mo. Ba maa ye Harara sɔ-yuu tiina. Filisi tiina bam déem tu ba gilimi Lehi ne mo mɛ swoona kara na wora to. Isarele tiina bam ma duri se ba lu Filisi tiina bam jeŋa ne. 12Samma ma zege swoona kara kam tetare ne o kwaane o ke jara yam ka ŋwaane. O ma go Filisi tiina bam dedɛ. Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa se Isarele tiina bam di wɔnɔ dedɛ.
13Bene dedwe, ko na maŋe de mena zagem to, mo bembɛ fintɔ sem wone setɔ déem vei David tei, o na seigi Adulam peo bɔɔne wone to. Filisi tiina jar-keira kɔgɔ kodwoŋi ya tu ba tigisi Refayim bwolo kom ne. 14Ba kɔgɔ kodwoŋi de ya jwoŋi Bɛtelehem teo kom mo ba wora. Konto maama dedaane David ya wo o peo kom dalem jei sem ne mo. 15David boboŋa ma tiini ya ja o tete teo kom ye o ta o we, “Wɔ mo wó zaŋe o vo Bɛtelehem se o mɔ na vole delo na tigi teo kom manchwoŋo ni ne to wone o ja o ba o pa-ne se a nyɔ?” 16Bembɛ setɔ sem konto ma lɔɔre ba tɔge Filisi tiina kɔgɔ kom wone ba vo ba yi vole dem ba mɔ na bam, ye ba jwoori ba ja-ba ba ba ba pa David. Ba na jwoori to, o ma ve se o nyɔ na bam konto. O ma lwo-ba o yage tega ne se ba taa ye pɛɛre ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. 17O ma ta o we, “Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo bá wane a nyɔ na banto! A ná nyɔge-ba, ko nye de a nyɔge nɔɔna banto jana mo, ba na sɛ se ba ga ba ŋwea se ba ma ba mɔ na banto to ŋwaane.” O ma ve se o nyɔ-ba.
Bembɛ setɔ sento déem na toŋe tei to mo konto.
18Abisayi de déem mo ye ‘Bembɛ kɔgɔ kom’ wone jar-keiru dedoa. O maa ye Joaba nyaane ye ba nu ye Zeruya. O ma kwei o chichwei o jeeri nɔɔna bia yatɔ (300) jara wone o go. Konto ŋwaane o ma na yere bembɛ setɔ sem yiga ne. 19Wonto déem mo nɛ yere o dwoni bembɛ fintɔ sem maama, ye o ji ba yiga tu. O nam wo woli bembɛ setɔ sem wone.
20Jehoyada bu Benaya de déem ye jar-keiru mo na ye bembea. O nwoŋi Kabezele mo, ye o toŋe baare dedɛ. Benaya déem go Moaba bembɛ selei. O ta ma tu gwoŋo wone o go nywoŋo dɛ dedwe do-kandwa na toe ye waaro tiini te wora to. 21Benaya ta go Ejipti nɔn-wagele dedwoŋi mo. Nɔɔno wom déem zei chichwei mo. Ko daare ye Benaya jege da-lɔŋɔ. O ma vo o vere chichwei dem Ejipti tu wom jeŋa ne, o jwoori o ma-de o zɔ‑o o go. 22Jehoyada bu Benaya déem na toŋe tei to mo konto. O de ma na yere nenɛɛne bembɛ setɔ sem tei. 23O ma tiini o na yere bembɛ fintɔ sem wone, se o wo tɔge o woli bembɛ setɔ sem wone mo. David ma pa se Benaya ji balo na yere‑o to yiga tu.
24Balo de na tɔge ba wo ‘Bembɛ fintɔ sem’ wone to mo tento:
Joaba nyaane Asaheli.
Dodo bu Elihanan, na nwoŋi Bɛtelehem to.
25Samma de Elika, na ye Haroda tiina to.
26Paliti tu Heleza.
Ikesa bu Yira, na nwoŋi Tekoa to.
27Anatofe tu Abizeri.
Husaa tu Mebunayi.
28Ahohi tu Zalemon.
Netofa tu Maharayi.
29Baana bu Helebi, de na ye Netofa tu to.
Ribayi bu Itayi, na nwoŋi Gibea teo Benjamin laŋa kam ne to.
30Pirafon tu Benaya.
Hidayi, na nwoŋi Gaasa bu-nwaro tem seeni to.
31Arabafa tu Abi-Alebon.
Baharum tu Azimavefa.
32Saalebon tu Eliaba.
Jasen bia bam.
Jonatan 33na ye Harara tu Samma bu to.
Sarare bu Ahiyam, de na ye Harara tu to.
34Ahasabayi bu Elifeleti, na ye Maaka tu to.
Ahitofeli bu Eliam, na ye Giloo tu to.
35Kamele tu Hezero.
Aribi tu Parayi.
36Natan bu Igale, na nwoŋi Zoba to.
Gad tu Bani.
37Amon tu Zeleki.
Beerofa tu Naharayi. Wonto déem zei Zeruya bu Joaba jara zela yam mo.
38Ifiri tu Yira.
Ifiri tu Gareba.
39Hiti tu Yuria.
Bembɛ sem maama déem ke daane se ye fintɔ-serepɛ (37) mo.

english_text:
David Counts the People
(1 Chronicles 21.1-6)
1The Lord was angry with Israel again, and he made David think it would be a good idea to count the people in Israel and Judah. 2So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
3Joab answered, “I hope the Lord your God will give you 100 times more soldiers than you already have. I hope you will live to see that day! But why do you want to do a thing like this?”
4But when David refused to change his mind, Joab and the army officers went out and started counting the people. 5They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer. 6They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon. 7They came to the fortress of Tyre, then went through every town of the Hivites and the Canaanites. Finally, they went to Beersheba in the Southern Desert of Judah. 8After they had gone through the whole land, they went back to Jerusalem. It had taken them 9 months and 20 days.
9Joab came and told David, “In Israel there are 800,000 who can serve in the army, and in Judah there are 500,000.”
The Lord Punishes David
(1 Chronicles 21.7-17)
10After everyone had been counted, David realized he had done wrong. He told the Lord, “What I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Lord, please forgive me.”
11Before David even got up the next morning, the Lord had told David's prophet Gad 12-13to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him:
You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? Or will your enemies chase you and make you run from them for three months? Or will there be three days of horrible disease in your land? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God, who sent me.
14David was really frightened and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
15-16So that morning, the Lord sent an angel to spread a horrible disease everywhere in Israel, from Dan to Beersheba. And before it was over, 70,000 people had died.
When the angel was about to destroy Jerusalem, the Lord felt sorry for all the suffering he had caused and told the angel, “That's enough! Don't touch them.” This happened at the threshing place that belonged to Araunah the Jebusite.
17David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!”
David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place
(1 Chronicles 21.18—22.1)
18-19That same day the prophet Gad came and told David, “Go to the threshing place that belongs to Araunah and build an altar there for the Lord.”
So David went.
20Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low, 21and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?”
David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
22Araunah said, “Take whatever you want and offer your sacrifice. Here are some oxen for the sacrifice. You can use the threshing-boards and the wooden yokes for the fire. 23Take them—they're yours! I hope the Lord your God will be pleased with you.”
24But David answered, “No! I have to pay you what they're worth. I can't offer the Lord my God a sacrifice that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing place and the oxen for 50 pieces of silver. 25Then he built an altar for the Lord. He offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings.
The Lord answered the prayers of the people, and no one else died from the terrible disease.
translation_text:
David jeeli o jar-keira bam ni
1 Baŋa Wɛ bane déem daa ma jwoori de zaŋe de Isarele tiina bam. O ma tɔge David baŋa o pa ba na chɔgem. O ma ta David se o vo o jeeli Isarele dedaane Judah baara bam ni se o lɔre ba na mae tei to. 2Pɛ David laam ma pa o jar-keira yiga tu Joaba ni o we, “Véi n kaare Isarele dwia yam maama wone, ko na zege Dan laŋa kam seeni se ko yi Beeriseba to. Pa ba jeeli baara balo na yi se ba woli a jar-keira bam wone to ni.”
3Joaba ma leiri David o we, “Pɛ, amo lwoori nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom se o pa Isarele kɔgɔ kom puli kuni bi se ko dwoni ba zem na ye tei tento to, se nmo daare n ma n yia n na konto maama. Se bɛ ŋwaane mo nmo laam nam boŋe se n jeeli ba ni konto dwoŋi?”
4De ko de Pɛ David wo to o pa Joaba dedaane o jar-keira yiga tiina bam. Ba ma zaŋe ba nwoŋi se ba vo ba jeeli Isarele baara bam ni. 5Ba ma vo ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. Ba ma zege Arowa ne, dedaane teo kolo na wo bwolo kom tetare ne to, ba bobo se ba taa jeeli nɔɔna bam. Ba ma zege dáane ba tole Gad laŋa kam maama ba vo ba yi Jazera. 6Ba ma daare ba vo Gilead, ba kɛ ba vo ba yi Kadese na wo Hiti tiina laŋa kam ne to. Ba daa ma zaŋe ba vo Dan, ba daare ba zege Dan ne ba gugwoli ba vo Sidon. 7Ba na zege dáane to, ba ma kɛ ba yɔɔre Tura teo kom na lɔge ko pe de dam to seeni. Ba ma daare ba tole Hivi tiina teene dem, de Kanaan tiina teene dem maama, ba vo ba kweeli Beeriseba ne. Teo kom konto maa wo Judah tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam ne.
8Ba déem kwei chane nogo de da finlei mo ba ma kaare teo kom ni maama ba pu. Ba laam ma jwoori ba vo Jerusalem. 9Joaba ma lwoni o bere pɛ wom Isarele baara balo na yi jara keim ye ba jeeli-ba to ni na mae tei to. Isarele dwia yam wone, ba déem ye baara morro bia nana (800,000) mo. Ko daare ye Judah dwi dem wone ba ye baara morro bia yanu (500,000).
10David na jeeli nɔɔna bam ni o ti to, mo o boboŋa daane‑o. O ma ta de Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Amo tiini a ke wɛleere de a keim dento. Baŋa Wɛ, popo a lwoori‑m se n yage n ma n chɛ-ne. Kokuri to, a tiini a toŋe jworim dedɛ.”
11Tega na jege ka poore ye David zaŋe to dedaane Baŋa Wɛ kwora ya tu o sampwora Gaadi tei. Wonto maa ye Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu wolo na toŋe o pa David to. 12-13Baŋa Wɛ ma pa‑o ni se o vo o ta de David o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: N jege se n kuri wonnu tento tetɔ wone dedoa se a ke-ko n yera ne. Kɔ mo nmo nam wó kuri? N lage se kana mo zo n teo kom bena yatɔ, naa se á dona mo taa jege abam ba zeila ye á duri ba yiga ne chane setɔ, naa se jawe-chɛɔ to n teo kom wone da yatɔ? Nam boŋe lanyerane, se n laam kuri te wone n ta n bere-ne, se amo de jwoori a vo a ta de wolo na toŋe-ne n tei ne to.”
Gaadi na tage Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam de David o ti to, 14David ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo bochare tiini de di mo. A wó kuri kɔ se a daare kɔ? Amo ba lage se nabiina taa jege debam ba dam kuri ne. Baŋa Wɛ tete nam ná waare debam, ko gara, wonto na tiini o duri nɔɔna yibwona to ŋwaane.”
15 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma pa se jawe-chɛɔ ba ko to Isarele teo kom ne. Jaweo kom ma bobo zezeŋa kam konto ko goe nɔɔna taa se ko yi maŋa kam na yi se ko kweeli to. Ko nam na zege Dan laŋa kam seeni se ko yi Beeriseba to, nɔɔna morro fuserepɛ (70,000) déem mo tega. 16Wɛ maleka kam na yi Jerusalem teo kom se ka go ko nɔn-bia to, mo Baŋa Wɛ leiri o boboŋa de lɛɛro telo o na toŋe ba baŋa ne to. O ma ta de maleka kam o we, “Ko maŋe! Dɔne n jeŋa teo kom baŋa ne se n yé chɔge-ko!” Konto de Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ya zege ka maŋe de Jebusi tu Arawuna mena ferem jei sem ne mo.
17David na nɛ maleka kam na jege nɔɔna bam ka goe to, o ma ta de Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Nɔɔna banto ye amo kwaga nɔɔna mo. Ba tete nam ke bɛ mo ye ba na lɛɛro tento? Ko ye amo mo tiini a ke wɛleere. Amo tusi dedɛ. Nam ma n jeŋa n waare amo de a sɔŋɔ tiina bam n daare banto.”
David lɔge bimbini se o ma o zuli Wɛ
18Dɛ dem konto ne nɔɔ mo Gaadi de vei David tei o ta ded‑o o we, “Zaŋe n vo n lɔ kaanem bimbini Arawuna mena ferem jei sem ne se n ma n zuli Baŋa Wɛ.” 19David ma sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem o na pɛ Gaadi se o ta ded‑o to, ye o zaŋe o maa vei jei sem. 20Arawuna na kwoni o nii o na we pɛ de o dedɛɛra mo vei ba beene o tei to, mo o nwoŋi o vo pɛ wom tei o vwi o yibia tega ne o zuli‑o.
21O ma bwei‑o o we, “Pɛ, bɛ mo jege nmo ko beene amo tei ywo-seeni?” David ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo tu se a lwoori‑m mo se n yeigi n mena ferem jei sem n pa-ne. A lage se a lɔ kaanem bimbini dáane mo a zuli Baŋa Wɛ se ko pa jawe-chɛɔ kom ti dé teo kom ne.” 22Arawuna ma ta o we, “Pɛ, nam kwei-ka zɛɛra n ma n ke kaanem delo maama n na lage to. Nii amo nabɛ mo tento se n wane n ja n zwɛ n ma n ke kaanem dem. Mena ferem dɛ sem de nabɛ zela yam de maa wora se n kwei-ya n ma n tɔre mini n zwɛ vara bam. 23Pɛ, amo kwei tento maama a pa nmo zɛɛra.”
Arawuna ma daare o ta‑o o we, “Nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó sɛ o jwoŋi n pɛɛra yam.” 24David ma ve se o jwoŋi-te zɛɛra ye o ta de Arawuna o we, “Amo wó ŋwe te maama jene mo a pa‑m. Kokuri to, a ba lage se a kwei pɛɛra yalo a na jwoŋi zɛɛra to a zwɛ a ke kaanem a pa a Tu Baŋa Wɛ.”
David ma jeeli lu-nyenno sabu-dala finnu o pa Arawuna o ma yeigi o mena ferem jei sem de o nabɛ sem. 25O ma lɛɛre o lɔ bimbini da se o ma ke kaanem o zuli Baŋa Wɛ. O ma daare o ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de yazura pɛɛra o ma kaane Baŋa Wɛ. Baŋa Wɛ ma sɛ o wɛ-lworo kom, ye o daare o pa se jawe-chɛɔ kom yage Isarele teo kom maama.

english_text:
David in His Old Age
1King David was now an old man, and he always felt cold, even under a lot of blankets. 2His officials said, “Your Majesty, we will look for a young woman to take care of you. She can lie down beside you and keep you warm.” 3-4They looked everywhere in Israel until they found a very beautiful young woman named Abishag, who lived in the town of Shunem. They brought her to David, and she took care of him. But David did not have sex with her.
Adonijah Tries To Become King
5-6 Adonijah was the son of David and Haggith. He was Absalom's younger brother and was very handsome. One day, Adonijah started bragging, “I'm going to make myself king!” So he got some chariots and horses, and he hired 50 men as bodyguards. David did not want to hurt his feelings, so he never asked Adonijah why he was doing these things.
7Adonijah met with Joab the son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest and asked them if they would help him become king. Both of them agreed to help. 8But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's bodyguards all refused.
9Adonijah invited his brothers and David's officials from Judah to go with him to Crawling Rock near Rogel Spring, where he sacrificed some sheep, cattle, and fat calves. 10But he did not invite Nathan, Benaiah, David's bodyguards, or his own brother Solomon.
11 When Nathan heard what had happened, he asked Bathsheba, Solomon's mother:
Have you heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has made himself king? But David doesn't know a thing about it. 12You and your son Solomon will be killed, unless you do what I tell you. 13Go say to David, “You promised me that Solomon would be the next king. So why is Adonijah now king?”
14While you are still talking to David, I'll come in and tell him that everything you said is true.
15Meanwhile, David was in his bedroom where Abishag was taking care of him because he was so old. Bathsheba went in 16and bowed down.
“What can I do for you?” David asked.
17Bathsheba answered:
Your Majesty, you promised me in the name of the Lord your God that my son Solomon would be the next king. 18But Adonijah has already been made king, and you didn't know anything about it. 19He sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. And he invited Abiathar the priest, Joab your army commander, and all your sons to be there, except Solomon, your loyal servant.
20Your Majesty, everyone in Israel is waiting for you to announce who will be the next king. 21If you don't, they will say that Solomon and I have rebelled. They will treat us like criminals and kill us as soon as you die.
22Just then, Nathan the prophet arrived. 23Someone told David that he was there, and Nathan came in. He bowed with his face to the ground 24and said:
Your Majesty, did you say that Adonijah would be king? 25Earlier today, he sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. He invited the army commanders, Abiathar, and all your sons to be there. They are already eating and drinking and shouting, “Long live King Adonijah!” 26But he didn't invite me or Zadok the priest or Benaiah or Solomon. 27Did you say they could do this without telling the rest of us who would be the next king?
Solomon Becomes King
28David said, “Tell Bathsheba to come here.” She came and stood in front of him. 29-30Then he said, “The living Lord God of Israel has kept me safe. And so today, I will keep the promise I made to you in his name: Solomon will be the next king!”
31Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and said, “Your Majesty, I pray that you will live a long time!”
32Then David said, “Tell Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to come here.”
When they arrived, 33he told them:
Take along some of my officials and let Solomon ride my own mule to Gihon Spring. 34When you get there, Zadok and Nathan will pour olive oil over Solomon's head to show that he is the new king of Israel. Then order someone to blow a trumpet and tell everyone to shout, “Long live King Solomon!” 35Bring him back here, and he will take my place as king. He is the one I have chosen to rule Israel and Judah.
36Benaiah answered, “We will do it, Your Majesty. I pray that the Lord your God will let it happen. 37The Lord has always watched over you, and I pray that he will now watch over Solomon. May the Lord help Solomon to be an even greater king than you.”
38Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah left and took along the two groups of David's special bodyguards. Solomon rode on David's mule as they led him to Gihon Spring. 39Zadok the priest brought some olive oil from the sacred tent and poured it on Solomon's head to show that he was now king. A trumpet was blown and everyone shouted, “Long live King Solomon!” 40Then they played flutes and celebrated as they followed Solomon back to Jerusalem. They made so much noise that the ground shook.
41Adonijah and his guests had almost finished eating when they heard the noise. Joab also heard the trumpet and asked, “What's all that noise about in the city?”
42Just then, Jonathan son of Abiathar came running up. “Come in,” Adonijah said. “An important man like you must have some good news.”
43Jonathan answered:
No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king. 44-45Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city. 46Solomon is now king.
47And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!”
David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed 48and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
49Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could. 50Adonijah himself was afraid of what Solomon might do to him, so he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
51Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
52Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.” 53Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah.
After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_text:
David kokweero maŋa kam taane
1Pɛ David déem tiini o kwe ye o bena gaale. O ná maŋe o zo gwaaro tei maama, o ware waaro tem. 2O tontoŋena bam ma ta ba we, “Dé tu, pa se dé beeri busankan-pwola se o taa wo n tei ne o nii nmo baŋa ne. Wonto wó taa kukwori‑m se waaro daa yé taa zoore‑m.”
3Ba ma buŋi Isarele teo kom maama wone ba na bukɔ-laao, o yere na ye Abisage ye o zoore Sunem teo ne. Ba ma ja‑o ba vo ba pa pɛ wom. 4Bukɔ wom yibia déem tiini ya lana ye o sɛ se o taa wo pɛ wom tei ne o woli‑o. Pɛ wom de nam wo ke sare-peiga ded‑o.
5Adonija wolo nu na ye Hagifa to déem ma zaŋe o bere o tete kamunim ye o we, “A lage a ji pɛ mo.” O ma kwei torokooro de sisein-nɔɔna de se dira bam, ye o daare o kwei baara finnu se ba duri ba da o yiga. 6Wonto déem mo ye Abisalom nyaane. O maa ye nenɔŋ-chɔrɔ mo. Ko na zege o biini ne to, o kwo David wo korese‑o naa o fɔge o bwei‑o taane we, “Bɛŋwaane mo n ke keim dem konto?”
7Adonija ma bane de Joaba wolo kwo na ye Zeruya to, dedaane Wɛ kaanem tu Abiatara. Ba ma sɛ se ba da ba woli‑o. 8Ko nam ná ye Wɛ kaanem tu Zadoki, de Benaya wolo kwo na ye Jehoyada to, de Natan wolo na ye Wɛ sampwora to, de Simeyi, de Reyi, dedaane David babɛ sem, banto maama wo tɔge Adonija kwaga.
9Adonija ma kwei pei, de nabɛ, de na-paala o ja o vo se o ma ke kaanem Zohelete pelɔrɔ kom baŋa ne. Jei sem konto bwola de En-Rogele. O déem ma bwoŋi pɛ wom bia bam maama na ye o chorro to, de pɛ sɔŋɔ dedɛɛra balo na nwoŋi Judah dwi dem wone to. 10Se ko ná ye Wɛ sampwora Natan, de Benaya, de pɛ wom babɛ sem, de o nyaane Solomon, o wo bwoŋi-ba.
11Natan ma zaŋe o vo o ta de Solomon nu Bafeseba o we, “Nmo wo nigi we Hagifa bu Adonija laam jigi pɛ mo, ye debam tu David yeiri ko ni ne na? 12Konto ŋwaane amo lage a bere‑m n na wó ke tei se n jwoŋi n tete ŋwea de n bu Solomon ŋwea to mo. 13Ke lela n zo Pɛ David tei n ta we, ‘Pɛ, nmo ya wo dugi duuri de amo we, amo bu Solomon mo wó saŋe n kwaga o ji pɛ na? Bɛŋwaane nam mo Adonija jigi pɛ?’ 14Tɔ. N ta ná wora n ŋɔɔna de pɛ wom, amo laam wó ba a zo, ye a zege n taane dem kwaga ne we ko ye chega mo.”
15Bafeseba ma sɛ ye o vo o zo Pɛ David tei. O déem tiini o kwe mo ye Sunem tu Abisage de wora o nii o baŋa ne. 16Bafeseba ma tiiri tega ne o zuli pɛ wom. Pɛ wom ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo n laga?”
17O ma leiri o we, “Pɛ, nmo tete mo dugi duuri n Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane n pa amo we, amo bu Solomon mo wó saŋe n kwaga o ji pɛ. 18Adonija nam maŋe o ji pɛ mo, ye n yeiri ko ni ne. 19O kwei nabɛ dedɛ, de na-paala, de pei mo o ma o ke kaanem. O ma bwoŋi pɛ wom bia bam de Wɛ kaanem tu Abiatara, ko ta woli de Joaba wolo na ye nmo jar-keira yiga tu to. O nam wo bwoŋi n bu Solomon wolo na kwei o chega o pa nmo to o woli da. 20Pɛ, Isarele tiina bam maama kwoni ba nii nmo mo, se ba ni nmo ni ne se ba lɔre nmo na lage se wolo leiri nmo yuu ne o di paare dem to. 21Nmo nam ná wo ke konto, ye n momwɛ ná ti ko daare amo de Solomon yerane, ba wó ma debam ba ji paweero mo.”
22Bafeseba ta na wora o ŋɔɔna de pɛ wom konto to, mo Natan yi o zo. 23Ba ma ta ba bere pɛ wom we, “Nii Wɛ sampwora Natan da.” O ma vo o tiiri pɛ wom yiga ne o zuli‑o.
24Natan ma ta o we, “Pɛ, nmo mo pɛ chwoŋa se Adonija saŋe nmo kwaga o ji pɛ na? 25Zem dɛ dento o jaane nabɛ dedɛ, de na-paala, de pei mo o ma o ke kaanem. O bwoŋi pɛ wom bia bam maama, de n jar-keira yiga tiina bam, de Wɛ kaanem tu Abiatara se ba ba. Leile konto ba jei ba nyɔ ye ba di ded‑o mo. Ba laam maa zuli‑o ye ba tɛ ba we, ‘Wɛ wó pa Pɛ Adonija taa jege momwɛ-dɛɛre!’ 26Ko daare amo wolo na ye n tontoŋeno to, de Wɛ kaanem tu Zadoki, de Benaya wolo kwo na ye Jehoyada to, de nmo bu Solomon, o wo bwoŋi debam. 27Pɛ, nmo mo pɛ chwoŋa se tento maama ke ye n wo pɛ se debam balo na ye n tontoŋena to lɔre wolo na lage o leiri nmo yuu ne o di paare to na?”
David pɛ ni we Solomon wó ji pɛ
28Pɛ David maa we, “Bwoŋi-na Bafeseba á pa-ne”. Ba ma seene ba bwoŋi‑o pa se o ba o zege Pɛ David yiga ne. 29Pɛ wom ma du duuri Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane ye o we, “Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora ye o vere-ne chanɛɛre dedɛ wone to, 30amo na maŋe a pwooli Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom yere ŋwaane se a ke a pa‑m to, amo wó seene a ke. Nmo bu Solomon wó saŋe amo kwaga o ji pɛ.”
31Bafeseba ma kuni dwoona Pɛ David yiga ne ye o we, “Wɛ wó pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre.”
32Pɛ David maa we, “Bwoŋi-na Wɛ kaanem tu Zadoki, de Wɛ sampwora Natan, de Jehoyada bu Benaya á pa-ne.” Ba na tu ba zege pɛ wom yiga ne konto to, 33o ma ta-ba o we, “Ja-na Solomon á jeini amo tete bona-siseiŋa kam baŋa ne se á ja a dedɛɛra bam á woli da á vo Gihon buli-yi dem seeni. 34Á na yi da, se á pa Wɛ kaanem tu Zadoki, de Wɛ sampwora Natan lwo nuga o yuu ne se o ji Isarele tiina pɛ. Wu-na nabɔnɔ á daare á ta de kwor-dɛa we, ‘Wɛ wó pa Pɛ Solomon momwɛ-dɛɛre’. 35Laam tɔge ded‑o á jwoori á ba ywo, se o laam ba o leiri amo yuu ne o ji pɛ. Amo mo kuri‑o se o di paare Isarele de Judah tiina maama baŋa ne.” 36Benaya ma leiri o we, “Ameena! Pɛ, nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó pa ko ke. 37Ne Baŋa Wɛ na maŋe o wora de nmo to, o ta wó taa wora de Solomon, pa se o paare dem fɔge de ke dam se ko dwoni nmo David paare dem.”
38Zadoki, de Natan, de Benaya, de Cherete tiina bam, de Peleti tiina bam maama ma ja Solomon ba jeini Pɛ David bona-siseiŋa baŋa ne ba ja‑o ba vo ba yi Gihon. 39Wɛ kaanem tu Zadoki ma kwei kwara de ka wo nuga wara-vwei dem wone o nwoŋi o vo o lwo-ka Solomon yuu ne. Ba ma wu nabɔnɔ kom ba daare ba bage de kwor-dɛa ye ba we, “Wɛ wó pa Pɛ Solomon momwɛ-dɛɛre.” 40Nɔɔna bam maama ma tɔge o kwaga ba ja‑o ba jwoori Jerusalem teo wo. Ba na maa vei to, ba ma wui wi ye ba jege wopwolo dedɛ pa se tega ziziŋi.
41Adonija de o veira bam maa na twɛ se ba di ba ti to mo ba nigi sɔɔ kom. Joaba na nigi nabɔnɔ kom kwori to, o ma bwei o we, “Sɔɔ konto na ke teo wone to kuri mo bɛ?”
42O na wora o ŋɔɔne konto to mo Wɛ kaanem tu Abiatara bu Jonatan tu o yi. Adonija maa we, “Ba n zo. Nmo na ye nɔn-ŋom to, ko wó taa ye kwor-ywoŋa mo n jaane n ba.”
43Jonatan ma leiri we, “Aawo, ko dae konto. Debam Pɛ David mo tiŋi Solomon se o ji pɛ. 44O ta ma pa se Zadoki, de Natan, de Benaya, de Cherete tiina bam, de Peleti tiina bam ja‑o ba vo Gihon. O ta pɛ se ba ja‑o ba jeini pɛ wom bona-siseiŋa baŋa ne mo. 45Wɛ kaanem tu Zadoki, de Wɛ sampwora Natan ma lwo nuga o yuu ne Gihon ne se o taa ye pɛ. Ba nam zege dáane mo ba beene teo kom wo de wopwolo. Konto ŋwaane mo sɔɔ kom ke konto. 46Ko woli da, Solomon laam mo jei paare yituŋu kom baŋa ne. 47Pɛ wom tontoŋena de ma ba ba ke debam Pɛ David yu-ywoŋo lei ye ba we, ‘Nmo Tu Wɛ wom wó pa se Solomon yere zaŋe de gaale, ye o paare taa daga de dwoi nmo paare dem.’ Pɛ wom ma maŋe o gadwogo yuu ne o ke o yuu tega ne o zuli Baŋa Wɛ, 48ye o we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to maŋe de tia. Wonto mo kuri nɔɔno se o leiri a yuu ne o di paare, ye a na keim dento.’ ”
49Adonija veira bam na nigi konto to, foone ma zo-ba. Ba ma zaŋe wodiu kom baŋa ne ye ba duri ba jage. 50Adonija na kɔre foone de Solomon to ŋwaane, o ma duri o vo o zo wara-vwei dem o zi bimbini dem nyea yam. 51Ba ma ta ba bere Solomon we, “Nii mo! Adonija kɔre foone de nmo. O ma vo o zi bimbini dem nyea yam ye o lwoori we, ‘Pa Pɛ Solomon du duuri we o bá kwei se-zɔɔ o go-ne. Ko ná dae konto, a bá nwoŋi pwooni.’ ” 52Solomon ma leiri o we, “O ná bere we o lage o ke o chega de amo, o bá na zonne de fenfee de. O nam ná jege puseŋa, o wó te mo.” 53O ma toŋe nɔɔna ye ba vo ba bwoŋi Adonija ba ja ba ba pa‑o. Adonija ma tiiri Pɛ Solomon yiga ne o zuli‑o. Solomon maa we, “Adonija, zaŋe n vo sɔŋɔ!”

english_text:
David's Instructions to Solomon
1Not long before David died, he told Solomon:
2My son, I will soon die, as everyone must. But I want you to be strong and brave. 3Do what the Lord your God commands and follow his teachings. Obey everything written in the Law of Moses. Then you will be a success, no matter what you do or where you go. 4You and your descendants must always faithfully obey the Lord. If you do, he will keep the solemn promise he made to me that someone from our family will always be king of Israel.
5 Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him 6in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
7 The sons of Barzillai from Gilead helped me when I was running from your brother Absalom. Be kind to them and let them eat at your table.
8 Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him. 9Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed.
David Dies
10-11 David was king of Israel 40 years. He ruled 7 years from Hebron and 33 years from Jerusalem. Then he died and was buried in Jerusalem. 12 His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom.
Adonijah Is Killed
13One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
“Yes. 14I just want to talk with you.”
“All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
15“You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed. 16Would you do me a favor?”
“What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
17 “Please ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag. He won't say no to you.”
18“All right,” she said. “I'll ask him.”
19When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side. 20Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?”
Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
21“Allow your brother Adonijah to marry Abishag,” she answered.
22Solomon said:
What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
23I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me. 24The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
25“Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died.
Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
26 Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said:
Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father. 27 But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore.
And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true.
Joab Is Killed
28Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection. 29When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?”
Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.”
Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
30Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!”
“No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.”
Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
31-32Solomon replied:
Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders. 33Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
34Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
35Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest.
Shimei Is Killed
36Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city! 37If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
38“That's fair, Your Majesty,” Shimei answered. “I'll do that.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem from then on.
39About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were, 40he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
41Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back. 42Solomon sent for him and said:
Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you? 43You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
44I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did. 45But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
46“Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died.
Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_text:
David na pɛ Solomon bera yalo to
1Ko na yi se David te to, mo o bwoŋi o bu Solomon ye o ta o bere‑o we:
2“Ko bá dáane se amo te, ne nabiina maama na jege se ba te tei to. Nam ke dam n ke n tete kuri ne se n bere we n ye babea mo. 3Ta‑n yei n Tu Baŋa Wɛ na lage se n toŋe totoŋe delo to. Ta‑n tɔge chwei selo o na wó bere‑m to, se n toŋe n tɔge o nia yam, de o chullu tem, de o bera yam maama, nenɛɛne ya na popone ya tiŋi Moses twanno tem wone to. Nmo ná ke konto, ko wó pa‑m yiga-veiŋa woŋo maama wone de jeiga kalo maama nmo na wó vo to. 4Ko ta wó pa se Baŋa Wɛ déem na pwooli tetei de amo to ji chega we ‘Nmo dwi dem jege se ba taa cho ba tete de ba na jege ba ŋwea ba ŋwe tei to. Ba ná seene ba kwei ba chega ba pa-ne ye ba tɔge amo chwei sem de ba wo maama, nmo dwi dem bá ga nɔɔno se o di paare Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne.’
5Nam yé swei Zeruya bu Joaba déem na ke amo tei to. O go Nera bu Abenera, de Jefere bu Amasa. Banto maa ye Isarele jar-keira yiga tiina balei bam mo. Maŋa kalo tigura na tera dé logo kom wone to mo o go-ba ne ba wo jara wone mo tei. Jana bam konto wo o yuu ne, ne ba na kwei-ba ba taare o teiŋ-kila de o natera maama tei to mo. 6Nam ke‑o ne n boboŋa na lage tei to. Yé yage‑o se o te o tete toone. 7Ko nam ná ye Bazilayi wolo na nwoŋi Gilead to bia bam, ke banto lanyerane se n pa-ba ba ni-wodiu. Bɛŋwaane banto déem nii amo baŋa ne maŋa kalo a na duri se a lu nmo zembaaro Abisalom jeŋa ne to mo.
8Nam guli Simeyi wolo kwo na ye Gera ye o nwoŋi Bahurim na wo Benjamin kateiri dem ne to. Dɛ dem a na maa vei Mahanayim to mo o tiini o sɔɔle lwarem o yage a yuu ne. O maa na jeeri-ne Jɔdan buga kam ni ne to mo a pwooli Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane we amo bá zɔ‑o a go. 9Nmo nam yé ke‑o nenɛɛne o jege bora. Nmo na jege swa lanyerane to, ta‑n yei n na wó ke‑o tei se o te jana wone, de o yuu na maŋe ko peere tei maama to de.”
10Konto kwaga ne, David ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma suli‑o David teo kom wone. 11O nɛ bena finna mo Isarele teo paare dem wone. Bena finna yam wone, o ke bena yarepɛ mo Heboron ne, o daare o ke bena fintɔ-yatɔ Jerusalem ne. 12David bu Solomon ma leiri o di o kwo paare dem. O paare dem déem tiini de jeini lanyerane.
Solomon paare dem yɔɔre de jeini
13Dɛ dedwe, Adonija wolo nu na ye Hagifa to ma zaŋe o vo Bafeseba wolo na ye Solomon nu to tei. Bafeseba ma bwei Adonija o we, “N tu de wo-zuru mo na?” O ma leiri we, “Ɛɛ, a tu de wo-zuru mo.” 14O ta maa we, “A jege taane mo se a ta a bere‑m.” Bafeseba ma leiri o we, “Nam ta.”
15Adonija ma tole o taane dem o we, “Nmo maŋe n yei we, teo kom ya ye amo nyem mo. Isarele tiina maama maa teena se amo mo taa ye pɛ wolo na wó leiri David yuu ne to. Baŋa Wɛ nam mo laga ye o kwei paare dem o pa a choro kom. 16Tɔ, amo lage a lwoori woŋo dedoa mo n tei ne. Popo, nam yé ve-ne.” Bafeseba ma leiri o we, “Nam ta.” 17Adonija ma leiri o we, “A lage se n lwoori Pɛ Solomon se o kwei Abisage wolo na ye Sunem tu to o pa-ne se a ma a ji a kaane. Pɛ wom wó sɛ nmo na wó lwoori‑o kolo to.” 18Bafeseba ma leiri o we, “Ko lana. Amo wó seene a vo a ŋɔɔne de Pɛ Solomon a pa‑m.”
19Bafeseba na vei o yi da to, mo Pɛ Solomon zaŋe o jeeri‑o ye o daare o tiiri o yiga ne. O ma jwoori o vo o jeini tega ne ye o pa ba ja yituŋu ba ba ba pa o nu Bafeseba se o jeini o jazem seeni. 20Bafeseba ma ta o we, “A lage a lwoori wo-balaŋa mo n tei ne. Nam yé ve-ne.” Solomon ma leiri o we, “A nu, lwoori nmo na lage kolo to, se amo wó ke a pa‑m.”
21Bafeseba maa we, “Sɛ se n zembaaro Adonija kwei bukɔ wolo na nwoŋi Sunem ye o yere ye Abisage to o ma o ji o kaane.” 22Pɛ Solomon ma leiri o we, “Bɛ mo ye n lage se a pa se Abisage zo Adonija? Nam lɛɛre n yage se a pa‑o paare dem a woli da, o na ye amo zembaaro to ŋwaane. Nam ta ŋɔɔne n pa Wɛ kaanem tu Abiatara, de Zeruya bu Joaba de!”
23Pɛ Solomon ma du duuri Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane o we, “A ná wo pɛ se Adonija ma o ŋwea o leiri woŋo kolo o na lwoori amo tei ne to yuu ne, se Wɛ go-ne. 24Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo tiŋi-ne se a leiri a kwo David yuu ne a di paare dem. O ma pwooli we Isarele tiina pwa wó nwoŋi a dwi dem ne. Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, Adonija jege se o te mo zem dɛ dem wone.” 25Pɛ Solomon ma toŋe Jehoyada bu Benaya se o vo o mage Adonija o go. Adonija ma seene o te.
26Pɛ wom ma ta o bere Wɛ kaanem tu Abiatara o we, “Jwoori n vo n tete teo Anatofe. Nmo maŋe se n te mo. A nam bá go‑m leile, bɛŋwaane nmo ya mo zeŋe Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam n pa a kwo David. N ma‑n tiini n tɔge ded‑o n na yaara dedɛ.” 27Solomon laam ma le Abiatara Baŋa Wɛ kaanem totoŋe dem wone. O keim dem konto ma pa se Baŋa Wɛ na tage taane delo Siloo ne ye de vo Eli dwi dem seeni to ji chega.
28Joaba déem ye wolo na ke ni de Adonija se o ji pɛ to mo. O nam ya wo woli Abisalom. O na nigi we ba go Adonija to, o ma duri o vo o zo Baŋa Wɛ wara-vwei dem wone o ja kaanem bimbini dem nyea yam. 29Ba ma ta ba bere Pɛ Solomon we Joaba duri o zo Baŋa Wɛ wara-vwei dem o sale bimbini dem yera ne. Solomon ma ta de Jehoyada bu Benaya o we, “Véi n mage‑o n go.”
30Benaya ma vo o zo Wɛ wara-vwei dem wone o ta o bere Joaba o we, “Pɛ wom we, n nwoŋi n ba pwooni yiga.” Joaba ma leiri o we, “Aawo, a bá nwoŋi. Ywo mo a lage a te.” Benaya ma jwoori o vo o ta o bere Solomon Joaba na tage tei to. 31Solomon ma leiri Benaya o we, “Nam ke o na taga tei to. Mage‑o n go n daare n kwei‑o n suli. Konto mo wó bere we o déem na go nɔɔna balo to jana jene daa tere amo de a kwo dwi tiina bam yuu ne. 32O déem mɛ o se-zɔɔ o go Nera bu Abenera wolo na ye Isarele jar-keira bam yiga tu to, de Jefere bu Amasa wolo de na ye Judah jar-keira bam yiga tu to, ye a kwo ya yeiri ko ni ne. Banto balei nam ya ye nɔn-laaro ba gare Joaba. Baŋa Wɛ nam mo wó pa se o na o nɔn-gora kam ŋweo. 33Ba jana bam jene laam wó jwoori Joaba yuu ne, de o dwi tiina bam yuu ne taa wuu. Baŋa Wɛ nam wó fɔge o pa se David de o dwi tiina bam taa nae yazura, se wo-zuru taa wo o paare dem baŋa ne.”
34Pɛ Solomon na tage konto to, Benaya ma jwoori o vo Wɛ wara-vwei dem o mage Joaba o go. Ba ma kwei o yera yam ba vo o tete teo ba suli‑o kagoa kam wone. 35Solomon ma pa se Benaya leiri Joaba yuu ne o ji jar-keira bam yiga tu. O ma daare o pa Zadoki de leiri Abiatara yuu ne o ji Wɛ kaanem tu.
36Solomon ma toŋe o bwoŋi Simeyi ye o ta we, “Maŋe Jerusalem teo wone ywo se n lɔ sɔŋɔ n ta‑n zoore da. Nam yé lɔgese teo n vo jei jei. 37Dɛ dem n na wó nwoŋi Jerusalem n bɛ Kidoron nabara kam to, ba wó go‑m mo. Konto nam ná kea, ko ye nmo tete yiga mo.”
38Simeyi ma leiri Solomon o we, “Kolo nmo na taga to ye lanyerane mo. Amo wó ke kolo maama a Pɛ wom na taga to.” Simeyi ma zo Jerusalem ne o dáane.
39Bena yatɔ na kɛ to mo Simeyi kabɛ selei duri ba nwoŋi ba vo Gafa teo Pɛ Akisi wolo kwo na ye Maaka to tei. Simeyi na lɔre we ba wo Gafa ne to, 40o ma zaŋe o di o bonaga kam o vo Pɛ Akisi tei se o beeri o kabɛ sem. O ma na-ba ye o daare o ja-ba o jwoori sɔŋɔ.
41Solomon na maane we Simeyi zege Jerusalem ne o vo Gafa o jwoori to, 42o ma bwoŋi‑o ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Amo déem pɛ nmo pwooli Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane we n yé nwoŋi Jerusalem teo wone. A ma daare a kaane‑m we, ‘Dɛ dem n na wó lɔgese teo to, nmo wó te mo.’ Nmo nam leiri amo we, kolo a na taga to lana, se nmo wó sɛ. Ko dae konto na? 43Bɛŋwaane mo n yiri ni delo n na pwooli de Baŋa Wɛ to, ye n daare n ve amo de ni dem?” 44Solomon daa ma ta de Simeyi o we, “N tete yɔɔre n yei puseŋa kikia yalo n na ke a kwo David baŋa ne to. Nam ta yei we Baŋa Wɛ mo wó waare‑m ko maŋe de zonne delo maama n na ke to. 45Se ko ná ye amo Pɛ Solomon, Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ amo swolim, ye o ta pa se David dwi paare dem fɔge de jeini lanyerane taa wuu.” 46Solomon laam ma pa Jehoyada bu Benaya ni pa se o vo o mage Simeyi o go.
Konto baŋa ne mo Solomon déem nɛ dam se o paare dem wane de jeini chekke.

english_text:
The Lord Makes Solomon Wise
(2 Chronicles 1.1-13)
1Solomon signed a treaty with the king of Egypt and married his daughter. She lived in the older part of Jerusalem until the palace, the Lord's temple, and the wall around Jerusalem were completed.
2At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines. 3Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
4 The most important shrine was in Gibeon, and Solomon had offered more than 1,000 sacrifices on that altar.
5One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
6Solomon answered:
My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king. 7Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader. 8And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
9Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
10-11God said:
Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions. 12So I'll make you wiser than anyone who has ever lived or ever will live.
13I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king. 14If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
15Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials.
Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
16One day two women came to King Solomon, 17and one of them said:
Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home, 18and three days later her baby was born. Nobody else was there with us.
19One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died. 20Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
21In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
22“No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!”
“The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!”
They argued back and forth in front of Solomon, 23until finally he said, “Both of you say this live baby is yours. 24Someone bring me a sword.”
A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered, 25“Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
26“Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.”
The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
27Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
28Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_text:
Solomon lwoori swa Baŋa Wɛ tei ne
1Solomon déem ke ni mo de Ejipti teo Pa-faro wom. O ma di Ejipti pɛ wom bukɔ o ma o ke kaane. O ma ja bukɔ wom o jwoori David teo kom se ko taa nii maŋa kalo o na wó lɔ o sɔŋɔ kom, de Baŋa Wɛ diga kam, de kabira kalo na kaare Jerusalem o ti to. 2Kanto maŋa kam ne, nɔɔna daa ta ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ mo wara-jei bimbina dwi dwi baŋa ne, bɛŋwaane ba ya ta wo lɔge diga Baŋa Wɛ yere dem zula ŋwaane.
3Solomon déem swoi Baŋa Wɛ ye o sɛ se o tɔge o kwo David bera yam. De ko de Solomon ta yeini o ke kaanem de zwɛɛm pɛɛra o pa Wɛ wara-jei bimbina yam baŋa ne mo. 4Wara-jei selo na jege kuri chekke se dwoi maama to déem wo Gibeon teo ne mo. Pɛ Solomon ma vo da o ke zwɛɛm kaanem kuni moro bimbini dem baŋa ne. 5O na wora to mo Baŋa Wɛ veere o tete ded‑o dendwea wone tete ne, ye o we, “Solomon, lwoori kolo maama n na lage to amo tei ne, se amo wó ke-ko a pa‑m.”
6Solomon ma leiri o we, “Nmo déem jege a kwo David swono lanyerane, o na ye nɔn-laao na jege nmo chega ye o yɔɔre o tɔge chwoŋa to ŋwaane. N ta ma‑n ke chega n pa‑o de n na pɛ o lo bakeira se wonto leiri o yuu ne o di paare dem se ko ba ko yi zem to. 7Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo laam pɛ amo wolo na ye nmo tontoŋeno to leiri a kwo David yuu ne a ji pɛ mo. Amo nam ta ye bu mo ye a yeiri a yiga de a kwaga, se a taa wo a nɔɔna bam yiga ne. 8Nmo nam le amo mo se a taa nii nɔɔna balo n na kuri to baŋa ne. Ba nam tiini ba ye kɔ-fɔrɔ kolo ni na ware de jeeli to. 9Nam pa-ne boboŋ-laaro se a wane a nii n nɔɔna bam baŋa ne lanyerane, se a daare a ta wae a pɔɔre lam de lwarem daane. Kokuri to, wɔ mo wó wane nmo kɔ-fɔrɔ konto o nii o tete ne?”
10Baŋa Wɛ wo ma pwoli de Solomon na lwoori kolo to. 11O ma leiri‑o o we, “Ko lana de nmo na kwaane n lwoori se a pa‑m boboŋ-laaro se n wane n ja a nɔɔna bam de chega to. N wo lwoori se a pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre, de jejegero, naa se a pa n dona bam na chɔgem. Nmo nam na lwoori swa se n wane n lɔre chega kam to ŋwaane, 12amo wó seene a pa‑m kolo nmo na lwoori amo tei ne to, pa se n na swa de boboŋ-laaro. Nmo swa yam wó dwoni nɔɔna balo maama na lwoori‑m ba ŋwe to, de balo maama na wó saŋe nmo kwaga se ba taa ŋwe to de. 13Kolo nmo ta na wo lwoori amo tei ne to mo a lage a kwei a pa‑m a woli da. Amo wó pa n na jejegero, de zula n ŋwea maama wone, ye pɛ wodwoŋi tera o na wó taa nye de nmo. 14Nmo ná sɛ n tɔge a chwei sem ye n sɛ a nia yam nenɛɛne n kwo David na ke tei to, amo wó seene a pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre”.
15Solomon ma puri o yia dɔɔne wone ye o maane we ko ye dendwea wone mo Wɛ ŋɔɔne ded‑o. O ma jwoori o vo Jerusalem o zege Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne o ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra de yazura pɛɛra o kaane o pa Wɛ. O laam ma bwoŋi o tontoŋena bam maama pa ba jeeri ba di wodi-fɔrɔ.
Ka-bworru telei taane
16Dɛ dedwe mo ka-bworru telei tu Pɛ Solomon tei se ba kwɛ ba taane. 17Ba dedoa maa we, “Pɛ, amo de kaane wonto mo zoore sɔŋɔ dedoa wone. O wora mo ye amo lo a bu. 18Ko na ke da yalei to, mo o de loga. Debam balei yerane nam ya mo zoora ye nɔn-gaa tera. 19Tete dedwe mo kaane wonto pane o bu wom o go dɔɔne wone. 20O ma zaŋe tete-koro ne o kwei a bu wom a takeiri ne o tiŋi‑o o nyɔɔne baŋa ne, ye a tigi a dɔa. O daare o kwei o bu wolo na tege to o tiŋi a takeiri ne. 21Tega na poore se a kwei a bu wom se o ŋɔge yele to, mo a nɛ we o tege mo. Ka na poore jagesage ye a na bu wom yibia to, a maane we o dae bu wolo a na loge to.”
22Kaane wodwoŋi wom de ma ta we, “Aawo! Bu wolo na ŋwe to ye amo bu mo. Wolo na tege to maa ye nmo nyem.” Da-yiga kaane wom de maa we, “Aawo! Bu wolo na tege to mo ye nmo bu, se wolo na ŋwe to ye amo bu mo.” Ba ma mage ni-kantɔgɔ konto dwoŋi Solomon yiga ne.
23Pɛ Solomon laam maa we, “Abam maama tɛ we bu wolo na ŋwe to mo ye á bu, se bu-too wom ye á dwoŋi nyem mo.” 24O ma toŋe nɔɔno se o vo o ja se-zɔɔ o ba o pa‑o. Ba na kwei ba pa‑o to, 25o ma pa ni we, “Zage-na bu wonto na ŋwe to belei, se á pɔɔre chichworru tem telei á pa kaana balei banto.”
26Ko ná ye bu wolo na ŋwe to nu wom, o maa tiini o jege o bu wom ŋwaŋa. O ma lwoori Solomon we, “Pɛ! Kwei bu wom n pa kaane wom. Yé go‑o.” Kaane wodwoŋi wom maa we, “Zage‑o belei! Amo ná gɛa, se o de ga” 27Solomon laam ma ta we, “Yé go bu wom. Kwei‑o n pa da-yiga kaane wom, se ko ye bu wom nu mo konto chekke.”
28Isarele tiina bam maama na nigi Solomon na bore kaana bam taane dem tei to, ko ma ke-ba yaau, ba na maane we Wɛ mo pɛ‑o swa se o taa ma o bore nɔɔna bora chekke to ŋwaane.

english_text:
Solomon's Officials
1-6Here is a list of Solomon's highest officials while he was king of Israel:
Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah sons of Shisha were the secretaries;
Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the government records;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the army commander;
Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the regional officers;
Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and the king's advisor;
Ahishar was the prime minister;
Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the forced labor.
7Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year. 8These were the twelve officers:
The son of Hur was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim.
9The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
10The son of Hesed was in charge of the towns of Arubboth and Socoh, and the region of Hepher.
11The son of Abinadab was in charge of Naphath-Dor and was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath.
12Baana son of Ahilud was in charge of the towns of Taanach and Megiddo. He was also in charge of the whole region of Beth-Shan near the town of Zarethan, south of Jezreel from Beth-Shan to Abel-Meholah to the other side of Jokmeam.
13The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had 60 walled towns with bronze bars on their gates.
14Ahinadab son of Iddo was in charge of the territory of Mahanaim.
15Ahimaaz was in charge of the territory of Naphtali and was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath.
16Baana son of Hushai was in charge of the territory of Asher and the town of Bealoth.
17Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in charge of the territory of Issachar.
18Shimei son of Ela was in charge of the territory of Benjamin.
19Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived.
And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah.
The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
20There were so many people living in Judah and Israel while Solomon was king that they seemed like grains of sand on a beach. Everyone had enough to eat and drink, and they were happy.
21 Solomon ruled every kingdom between the Euphrates River and the land of the Philistines down to Egypt. These kingdoms paid him taxes as long as he lived.
22Every day, Solomon needed 5,000 liters of fine flour, 10,000 liters of coarsely-ground flour, 2310 grain-fed cattle, 20 pasture-fed cattle, 100 sheep, as well as deer, gazelles, and geese.
24Solomon ruled the whole region west of the Euphrates River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, and he was at peace with all of the countries around him. 25Everyone living in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, was safe as long as Solomon lived. Each family sat undisturbed beneath its own grape vines and fig trees.
26 Solomon had 40,000 stalls of chariot horses and 12,000 chariot soldiers.
27Each of the twelve regional officers brought food to Solomon and his household for one month of the year. They provided everything he needed, 28as well as barley and straw for the horses.
Solomon's Wisdom
29Solomon was brilliant. God had blessed him with insight and understanding. 30-31 He was wiser than anyone else in the world, including the wisest people of the east and of Egypt. He was even wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Mahol's three sons, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Solomon became famous in every country around Judah and Israel. 32 Solomon wrote 3,000 wise sayings and composed more than 1,000 songs. 33He could talk about all kinds of plants, from large trees to small bushes, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish. 34Kings all over the world heard about Solomon's wisdom and sent people to listen to him teach.
translation_text:
Solomon tontoŋena bam taane
1Solomon déem tu o ji Isarele tiina bam maama pɛ. 2O dedɛɛra bam mo tento:
Zadoki bu Azaria mo ye Wɛ kaanem tu. 3Elihorefa de Ahija na ye Sisa bia to maa ye pɛ tɔn-poponna bam. Ahiluda bu Jehosafate maa ye wolo na tiŋi teo kom lonne twanno tem to. 4Jehoyada bu Benaya ye jar-keira bam yiga tu mo. Zadoki de Abiatara de maa ye kaanem tiina. 5Natan bu Azaria ye wolo na nii kateira yiga tiina bam baŋa ne to mo. Natan bu Zabudi maa ye kaanem tu ye o ta woli pɛ wom boboŋa kurim baŋa ne. 6Ahisara ye wolo na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom totoŋa baŋa ne to mo. Abeda bu Adoniram maa nii balo na toŋe totoŋ-dɛɛra to baŋa ne.
7Solomon déem tiŋi nɔɔna fuga-balei mo se ba taa nii Isarele kateira yam baŋa ne. Banto totoŋa maa ye se ba ja wodiu ba ba ba pa pɛ de o diga tiina chana dedoa bene maama wone. 8Yiga tiina bam de ba kateira yam mo tento:
Ben-Huri déem mo nii Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam. 9Ben-Dekere maa nii Makaza, de Saalibim, de Bɛte-Semesa, de Elon-Bɛte-Hanan teene dem baŋa ne. 10Ben-Heseda maa nii Arubota, de Sokoo, de Hefera laŋa kam ni maama. 11Ben-Abinadab maa nii Dora kateiri dem maama baŋa ne. Wonto déem di Solomon bukɔ wolo yere na ye Tafata to
12Ahiluda bu Baana maa nii Taanaka, de Megido, de Bɛte-San jei selo maama na bwola de Zarefan na wo Jezerele teo tega-kuri seeni to. Jei sem konto zege Bɛte-San ne se tole konto se yi Abel-Mehola de Jokemeam teene dem maama.
13Ben-Gebere maa nii Ramofa-Gilead kateiri dem baŋa ne, ko ta woli de Gilead teene delo na ye Manasɛ tu Jayira dwi dem nyem to, dedaane Aragobi kateiri dem na wo Basan ne to, de de teene fuseredo dem ba na lɔge kabira ba kaare-de ye ba ma lu-nyenno ba gare de manchwo-nia yam to.
14Yido bu Ahinadaba maa nii Mahanayim kateiri dem. 15Ahimaazi maa nii Nafitali laŋa kam baŋa ne. Wonto de déem di Solomon bukɔ wodwoŋi yere na ye Basemafa to mo. 16Husayi bu Baana maa nii Asere laŋa kam, ko woli de Bealofa teo. 17Parua bu Jehosafate maa nii Isakara laŋa kam. 18Ela bu Simeyi maa nii Benjamin laŋa kam.
19Yuri bu Gebera maa nii Gilead kateiri dem. Ko maa ye jei selo Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon de Basan teo Pɛ Oga ya na di paare se baŋa ne to mo.
Ko ta woli da to, yiga tu dedoa déem mo jege logo kom maama o nia.
Solomon paare dim na vei yiga tei to
20Judah de Isarele tiina bam kɔgɔ déem daga dedɛ nenɛɛne buga ni kasolo na mae tei to mo. Ba di ba ni ye ba nyɔ ba sui. Ba maa jege wopwolo. 21Solomon di o paare dem teene dem maama baŋa ne se ko zege Yuferata buga kam ni ne, ko tole konto ko yi Filisi tiina tega kam ni, se ko daare ko vo ko yi Ejipti teo kom siseini dem. Solomon ta na ŋwe to, teene dento maama ŋwe ba lampwoo ye ba toŋe ba pa‑o mo.
22Wodiu kolo ba na lage dɛ maama wone se Solomon de o nɔɔna bam taa di to mo tento: mun-bwei ywollu fuseredo (60), dedaane muni ywollu bi de finlei (120), 23de naane fuga delo na nugi bigila-bigila to, de naane finlei delo na beeri gaao wone de di to, de pei bi, ko ta woli de wei, de feiri, de si, de cheeni to.
24Solomon déem tei teene delo maama na wo Yuferata buga kam wɛ-zoore seeni to de ba pwa bam mo. Laŋa kam konto zege Tipisa ne ka tole taa ka yi Gaza teo kom. Wo-zuru maa wo jei sem maama ne. 25Solomon déem ta na ŋwe maŋa kalo maama ne to lwia ba jege nɔɔna balo maama na zoore Judah de Isarele teo ne to, ko na zege Dan laŋa kam seeni se ko yi Beeriseba to. Sɔŋɔ maama ko ni twoo jege ba kare mo ba vara. 26Solomon déem chege najere morro finna (40,000) mo o zege se o sisei selo na vaŋe jara-keim torokooro to taa zege da. O ta maa jege sisein-nɔɔna morro fuga-selei (12,000).
27Chana maama wone kateiri yiga tiina fuga-balei bam dedoa dedoa jege se o ja wodiu mo o ba o pa Solomon de balo maama na di wodiu o tei ne to. Ba kwaane mo ba nii se o yé ga kolokolo. 28Ba ta jaane mena de ga-korro ba tui ba tiŋi ba pa sisein-nɔɔna selo na wae se duri lela to de sisei sesem sem maama. Ba maama déem ke ne ko na maŋe se ba taa ke tei to.
Pɛ Solomon swa na gaale tei to
29Wɛ na pɛ Solomon boboŋa de swa yalo to tiini ya daga dedɛ. O yi-poro kom de gaale nenɛɛne buga ni kasolo na mae tei to mo. 30O swa yam déem dana ya dwoi yi-pore-nyena balo maama na nwoŋi wɛ-puli seeni jei sem de Ejipti teo to. 31O déem jege swa o dwoi nabiina maama, ko ná maŋe ko ye Ezera dwi tu Etan, de Mahole bia batɔ Heman, de Kalekole, de Dareda mo de. O yere ma zaŋe teene delo maama na bwola da to ne. 32Solomon déem lage memaŋa morro tetɔ (3,000) mo o ke daane. O ma puli lei moro dedoa de senu (1,005) o tiŋi. 33O maa ŋɔɔne teeni de punnu dwi dwi taane, ko ná ye Lebanon Sedare teeni-kamunnu tem taane de Husopa punnu telo na puli kabiri yera ne to. O ta maa ŋɔɔne vara, de zuna, de tega-veila, de ywona dwi dwi taane. 34Logo baŋa teene pwa maama na nigi Solomon swa yam ŋwa to, mo ba toŋe ba nɔɔna se ba vo ba cheigi o ni taane.

english_text:
Solomon Asks Hiram To Help Build the Temple
(2 Chronicles 2.1-16)
1King Hiram of Tyre had always been friends with Solomon's father David. When Hiram learned that Solomon was king, he sent some of his officials to meet with Solomon.
2Solomon sent a message back to Hiram:
3Remember how my father David wanted to build a temple where the Lord his God could be worshiped? But enemies kept attacking my father's kingdom, and he never had the chance. 4Now, thanks to the Lord God, there is peace in my kingdom and no trouble or threat of war anywhere.
5 The Lord God promised my father that when his son became king, he would build a temple for worshiping the Lord. So I've decided to do that.
6I'd like you to send your workers to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. I will pay them whatever you say and will even have my workers help them. We both know that your workers are more experienced than anyone else at cutting lumber.
7Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!” 8Then he sent back his answer:
I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need. 9My workers will carry them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea. They will tie the logs together and float them along the coast to wherever you want them. Then they will untie the logs, and your workers can take them from there.
To pay for the logs, you can provide the grain I need for my household.
10Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar and pine logs he needed. 11In return, Solomon gave Hiram over 2,000 tons of wheat and almost 4,000 liters of pure olive oil each year.
12The Lord kept his promise and made Solomon wise. Hiram and Solomon signed a treaty and never went to war against each other.
Solomon's Workers
13Solomon ordered 30,000 people from all over Israel to cut logs for the temple, 14 and he put Adoniram in charge of these workers. Solomon divided them into three groups of 10,000. Each group worked one month in Lebanon and had two months off at home.
15He also had 80,000 workers to cut stone in the hill country of Israel, 70,000 workers to carry the stones, 16and over 3,000 assistants to keep track of the work and to supervise the workers. 17He ordered the workers to cut and shape large blocks of good stone for the foundation of the temple.
18Solomon's and Hiram's men worked with men from the city of Gebal, and together they got the stones and logs ready for the temple.
translation_text:
Solomon ti o yiga se o lɔ Jerusalem Wɛ diga kam
1Tura teo pɛ Hiram déem nigi we ba tiŋi Solomon mo se o leiri o kwo David yuu ne o ji Isarele teo pɛ. O ma toŋe o tontoŋena se ba vo Solomon tei ba ke o yu-ywoŋo lei, Hiram ni déem na ywomma de David to ŋwaane. 2Solomon de ma toŋe kwora kanto o pa Hiram ye o we:
3“Nmo maŋe n yei we a kwo David ya lage se o lɔ Wɛ diga mo se nɔɔna taa zuli o Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom da. O dona bam nam na yeini ba kwaare jara ded‑o to, o wo nɛ chwoŋa se o ke konto, se Baŋa Wɛ ná pɛ o wane-ba o di o ti, se o ke. 4Ko nam ná ye leile konto, a Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom pɛ se dé jei de wo-zuru mo jei maama ne. Dé dona daa tera ba na wó pa lɛɛro yi debam. 5Konto ŋwaane a boŋe a ja se a lɔ Wɛ diga kam se ko pa a Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere dem na zula. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem pwooli de a kwo David o we, ‘Ta‑n yei se n bu wolo na wó leiri n yuu ne o ji pɛ to mo lage o lɔ a diga kam se ko pa a na zula.’
6Konto to, toŋe n nɔɔna bam se ba vo Lebanon ba gwoni Sedare dɛ sem ba pa-ne. Amo nɔɔna bam wó gwaane de-ba ba toŋe. Nmo na lage se a ŋwe n tontoŋena bam tei maama to, amo wó ŋwe-ba. Nmo yei we nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera debam tei ne o na yei dɛ gwonim se ko yi abam balo na nwoŋi Sidon seeni to.”
7Pɛ Hiram na nigi Solomon kwora kam to o wo ma tiini ko pwoli, ye o ta o we, “Zem dɛ dem ne a ke Baŋa Wɛ lei de o na pɛ David jege bu wolo na ye swa tu to, se wonto leiri o yuu ne o taa tei Isarele na ye te-fɔrɔ to.” 8Hiram ma toŋe kwora kanto o pa Solomon ye o we:
“A jwoŋi nmo kwora kam. A nam wó ke tei maama n na taga to. Amo wó pa ba gwoni Sedare teeni de tei-ŋonno tedwonna da-kwollu ba pa‑m. 9Amo nɔɔna bam wó ja dɛ sem ba zege Lebanon zwonnu tem yuu ne ba tu ba vo Mediterania naneo kom ni. Ba maa wó vɔ-se ba ke daane se se puki na bam baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba dɔge se baŋa ne ba ja ba yi mɛ maama nmo na laga to. A nɔɔna maa wó bwoli-se, se nmo nɔɔna bam laam ja-se ba kɛ. Nmo nam wó woli-ne de wodiiru se a sɔŋɔ kom taa di.”
10Hiram déem ma seene o pa Solomon Sedare teeni de tei-ŋonno tedwonna da-kwollu telo maama o na laga to. 11Bene maama wone Solomon de ma pa Hiram chaara ywollu morro fuseredo (60,000) de Olivi nuga kuriwaa bia morro finlei (20,000) se o sɔŋɔ tiina bam taa di.
12 Baŋa Wɛ déem seene o pa Solomon jege swa ne o na pwooli we o wó ke tei to mo. Hiram de Solomon ma di badwoŋo da-tei ne. Ba ma fɔge ba gwoni ni se ba yé lɔ da-kwaga ne.
13Pɛ Solomon déem kuri baara morro fintɔ (30,000) mo na nwoŋi Isarele jei maama ne. O ma fe-ba se ba taa gwoni dɛ ba pa‑o. 14O ma pa se Adoniram nii tontoŋena bam konto baŋa ne. O nam ya pɔɔre kɔgɔ kom kuni betɔ mo ye popɔra maama jege baara morro fuga (10,000). Popɔra dedoa maama ke chana dedoa mo Lebanon ne ye ba jwoori sɔŋɔ ba sii chane selei. 15Solomon déem ta kuri baara morro funɔnɔ (80,000) mo se ba vo Isarele zwonnu laŋa kam se ba lɔ kandwa-zana peero jei sem ne. O ma daare o le baara morro fuserepɛ (70,000) se ba taa zeŋe kandwa yam. 16O ta ma kuri baara morro tetɔ de bia yatɔ (3,300) se banto taa nii tontoŋena bam de ba totoŋ-dɛɛra yam baŋa ne. 17O déem pɛ se ba yare kandwa yalo na dana ye ya ye kamuna to peo yera ne mo se ba ma ba tiŋi Wɛ diga kam kuri. 18Solomon dedaane Hiram tontoŋena bam, ko woli de Gebale tiina badwonna mo ke daane ba gwoni dɛ sem ba daare ba lɔ kandwa yam, ye ba daare ba fɔge ba kwɛ-ya se ba ma ba lɔ Wɛ diga kam.

english_text:
The Outside of the Temple Is Completed
1Solomon's workers started building the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year. It had been 4 years since Solomon became king of Israel, and 480 years since the people of Israel left Egypt.
2The inside of the Lord's temple was 27 meters long, 9 meters wide, and 13.5 meters high. 3A four-and-a-half-meter porch went all the way across the front of the temple. 4The windows were narrow on the outside but wide on the inside.
5-6Along the sides and back of the temple, there were three levels of storage rooms. The rooms on the bottom level were just over two meters wide, the rooms on the middle level were over two and a half meters wide, and those on the top level were just over three meters wide. There were ledges on the outside of the temple that supported the beams of the storage rooms, so that nothing was built into the temple walls.
7Solomon did not want the noise of hammers and axes to be heard at the place where the temple was being built. So he gave orders for the workers to shape the blocks of stone at the quarry.
8The entrance to the bottom storage rooms was on the south side of the building, and stairs to the other rooms were also there. 9The roof of the temple was made out of beams and cedar boards.
The workers finished building the outside of the temple. 10Storage rooms just over two meters high were all around the temple, and they were attached to the temple by cedar beams.
11The Lord told Solomon:
12-13If you obey my commands and do what I say, I will keep the promise I made to your father David. I will live among my people Israel in this temple you are building, and I will not desert them.
14So Solomon's workers finished building the temple.
The Inside of the Temple Is Furnished
(2 Chronicles 3.8-14)
15The floor of the temple was made out of pine, and the walls were lined with cedar from floor to ceiling.
16 The most holy place was in the back of the temple, and it was nine meters square. Cedar boards standing from floor to ceiling separated it from the rest of the temple. 17The temple's main room was 18 meters long, and it was in front of the most holy place.
18The inside walls were lined with cedar to hide the stones, and the cedar was decorated with carvings of gourds and flowers.
19The sacred chest was kept in the most holy place. 20-22 This room was nine meters long, nine meters wide, and nine meters high, and it was lined with pure gold. There were also gold chains across the front of the most holy place. The inside of the temple, as well as the cedar altar in the most holy place, was covered with gold.
23 Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made from olive wood to put in the most holy place. Each creature was four and a half meters tall 24-26and four and a half meters across. They had two wings, and the wings were just over two meters long. 27Solomon put them next to each other in the most holy place. Their wings were spread out and reached across the room. 28The creatures were also covered with gold.
29The walls of the two rooms were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures. 30Even the floor was covered with gold.
31-32The two doors to the most holy place were made out of olive wood and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures. The doors and the carvings were covered with gold. The door frame came to a point at the top.
33-34The two doors to the main room of the temple were made out of pine, and each one had two sections so they could fold open. The door frame was shaped like a rectangle and was made out of olive wood. 35The doors were covered with gold and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
36The inner courtyard of the temple had walls made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams.
37Work began on the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year, four years after Solomon became king of Israel. 38Seven years later the workers finished building it during Bul, the eighth month of the year. It was built exactly as it had been planned.
translation_text:
Solomon na lɔge Wɛ diga kam tei to
2 Tigisim 3:1-14
1Solomon déem zaŋe o bobo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam lɔɔm. Ko déem ya ke bena bia yana de funɔnɔ (480) mo ye Isarele tiina bam yage Ejipti teo. Ko maa ye Solomon paare dim bena yana bene dem chane selei chana kam yere na ye Zivi to wone mo.
2Diga kalo Solomon na lɔge o pa Baŋa Wɛ to maŋem na ye tei to mo tento: Ka dedɔrem seeni ye naba-laara fintɔ mo. Ka kaywalem baŋa maŋem maa ye naba-laara fuga. Ka wɛ-baŋa maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fintɔ. 3Diga kam napɔrɔ kaywalem maŋem déem ye naba-laara fuga mo se ko maŋe de diga kam tete. Ko dedɔrem maa ye naba-laara yanu. 4O ma kwei dɛ o ma o ke takwor-balwa Wɛ diga kabira kam yera ne. 5Diga kam sɛ setɔ seeni o ta ma lɔ di-balwa o kaare kabira kam pwooni yiga seeni. 6Di sem lɔge se daŋe da-baŋa mo kuni betɔ. Kuri seeni diga kam kaywalem maŋem ye naba-laara yalei de chichworo mo. Tetare diga kam de kaywalem maŋem maa ye naba-laara yatɔ, ye baŋa seeni diga kam kaywalem maŋem ye naba-laara yatɔ de chichworo. Ba déem na lɔge di-kamunu kom kabira kam to, ba pɔɔre mɛ di-balwa bei sem na wó peini da to. Ba ke konto se ba daa yé lu bɔɔna kabira kam yera ne ba lɔ mo.
7Ba déem vei peero jei mo ba sare kandwa yalo ba na wó ma ba lɔ Wɛ diga kam to pa ya maŋe daane. Ba laam ma zeiŋi-ya ba ja ba diga kam lɔɔm jei, se sɔɔ yé taa ke ka lɔɔm maŋa ne, ko ná maŋe ko ye dwooru naa luuru telo maama sɔɔ de.
8Ni delo na zoore di-balwa bam tega di sem to jeeri Wɛ diga kam tega-kuri seeni saŋa kam mo. Nateina maa zege dáane ya dɔɔle ya diini tetare di sem, de wɛyuu di sem.
9Solomon déem ma pa ba lɔ Wɛ diga kam ba ti. O ma daŋe bei kabira kam baŋa ne ye o daare o ma Sedare da-pelwaro o lware se baŋa ne o ma pu diga kam. 10Di-balwa balo o na lɔge o kaare Wɛ diga kam to dedoa maama wɛ-baŋa maŋem déem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu mo. Ba déem mɛ Sedare bei mo ba twoŋi di sem konto de Wɛ diga kam daane.
11 Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ Solomon ni o we, 12“Ko ná ye Wɛ diga kanto kam nmo na lage n lɔ n pa-ne to, nmo ná seene n sɛ a nia yam, de a chullu tem, ye n tɔge a bera yam, amo wó tɔge nmo baŋa a ke a su ni delo a na pwooli de n kwo David to. 13Amo wó taa zoore a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam tetare ne taa. Amo daa bá viiri a daare-ba.”
14Solomon déem ma pa ba lɔ Wɛ diga kam ba ti. 15O ma kwei Sedare da-pelwaro mo o kwoli ka wo kabira kam, ko zege ka tega kam seeni se ko yi mɛ ba na ne to. O laam ma lware ka tega kam dedaane da-ŋonno. 16O ma zege diga kam wo kwaga kam seeni o maŋe naba-laara fuga se o lɔ kabira o ma che Wɛ di-yun-gala kam se ka tiini ka taa ye wose Wɛ ŋwaane.
