O laam ma kwei Sedare da-pelwaro o ma kwoli kabira kam konto ko zege ka tega kam seeni se ko yi mɛ ba na ne to. 17Wɛ di-yuu kom tete ma daare naba-laara finlei ye ka wo di-yun-gala kam yiga ne. 18Ba ma gɔgere kunkwollu de ga-punnu nyenyero ba ke Sedare dɛ sem yera ne. Diga kam wo kandwa daa ba nae, ba na mɛ Sedare dɛ ba kwoli ko maama to ŋwaane. 19O ma kwɛ di-yun-gala kam se ba laam kwei Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ba ba zege da. 20Diga kam konto dedɔrem baŋa maŋem déem ye naba-laara fuga. Ka kaywalem baŋa maŋem de maa ye naba-laara fuga, ye ka wɛ-baŋa maŋem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finlei. O ma taare ka wo kom maama de sabu-seŋa. O ta ma kwei Sedare dɛ o ma ke kaanem bimbini ye o daare o ma sabu-seŋa o kwoli-de. 21Solomon ma yɔɔre o kwei sabu-seŋa o ma kwoli Wɛ diga kam maama o daare o kwei sabu-seŋa chegero o ma che Wɛ di-yun-gala kam ni dem. 22Konto dwoŋi mo Solomon déem pɛ ba kwei sabu-seŋa ba ma ba kwoli Wɛ diga kam maama ba vo ba ti. Ko ta ná ye kaanem bimbini delo na ye Wɛ di-yuu kom nyem to, o ma taare-de de sabu-seŋa.
23Solomon déem ma pa ba kwei Olivi dɛ ba gɔgere cherubi nyenyero telei se ba kwei-te ba zege Wɛ di-yun-gala kam wone. Se dedoa maama wɛ-baŋa maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga. 24-26Ya maama jege vɔna yalei yalei mo. Vɔŋɔ dedoa maama dedɔrem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu. Ko na zege cherubi dedoa vɔŋɔ kweelim jei ne se ko yi ko dwoŋi kom vɔŋɔ na kweeli mɛ to ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga mo. Cherubi nyenyero telei tem maama mae daane mo.
27Solomon ma kwei cherubi selei sem o zege Wɛ wara-jei di-yun-gala kam wone. Se vɔna yam yarege pa se cherubi dedoa vɔŋɔ dwei kabira kam daa dedoa, ye kadwoŋi kam vɔŋɔ de dwei daa kadwoŋi kam. Se wo vɔna yam de ma dwei daane. 28O ma daare o kwei sabu-seŋa o ma taare cherubi selei sem. 29O ma pa ba gɔgere cherubi, de konkware, de ga-punnu nyenyero ba ke di-yun-gala kam de di-yuu kom maama wo kabiri sem yera ne. 30O ta ma kwei sabu-seŋa o ma kwoli di selei sem maama tega.
31-32Wɛ di-yun-gala kam ni dem jege bworru telei mo ba na mɛ Olivi dɛ ba ke. Solomon ma pa ba gɔgere cherubi, de konkware, de ga-punnu nyenyero ba ke te yera ne. Ba laam ma kwei sabu-seŋa ba ma taare bworru tem maama. Ba kwei dɛ mo ba ke ni dem ne pa se de jege sɛ senu.
33Ni delo na zoore Wɛ diga kam tete wone to, ba ma kwei Olivi dɛ ba ma ke ni dem sɛ sena. 34Ba ma kwei da-ŋonno ba ma ke bworru telei ba kwaare ni dem ne. Bworo maama maa wae ko pira. 35Solomon ma pa ba gɔgere cherubi, de konkware, de ga-punnu nyenyero ba ke te yera ne. Ba ma kwei sabu-seŋa ba taare te maama pa ko mara ko mara. 36Ba ma lɔ kabira Wɛ diga kam yera ne ba che ka tetare konkɔlɔ kom. Ba ma lware kandwa kuni betɔ ba daŋe da-baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba daŋe Sedare da-kwollu kandwa yam baŋa ne, ye ba lɔ konto ba di.
37Solomon paare dim bena yana bene dem wone mo, ba déem chwi Baŋa Wɛ diga kam kuri. Ko ye Zivi chana kam wone mo konto. 38Ka ma guri o paare dim bena fuga-dedoa bene dem wone. Ko maa ye chane nana chana kam yere na ye Bula to mo konto. Wɛ diga kam de ka yera wonnu maama ma lɔ fase, ne Solomon na jaane o boboŋa se o ke tei to. Ba déem kwei bena yarepɛ mo ba lɔ ka maama ba guri.

english_text:
Solomon's Palace Is Built
1Solomon's palace took 13 years to build.
2-3Forest Hall was the largest room in the palace. It was 44 meters long, 22 meters wide, and 13.5 meters high, and was lined with cedar from Lebanon. It had 4 rows of cedar pillars, 15 in a row, and they held up 45 cedar beams. The ceiling was covered with cedar. 4Three rows of windows on each side faced each other, 5and there were three doors on each side near the front of the hall.
6Pillar Hall was 22 meters long and 13.5 meters wide. A covered porch supported by pillars went all the way across the front of the hall.
7Solomon's throne was in Justice Hall, where he judged cases. This hall was completely lined with cedar.
8 The section of the palace where Solomon lived was behind Justice Hall and looked exactly like it. He had a similar place built for his wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt.
9From the foundation all the way to the top, these buildings and the courtyard were made out of the best stones carefully cut to size, then smoothed on every side with saws. 10The foundation stones were huge, good stones—some of them four and a half meters long and others three and a half meters long. 11The cedar beams and other stones that had been cut to size were on top of these foundation stones. 12The walls around the palace courtyard were made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams, just like the front porch and the inner courtyard of the temple.
Hiram Makes the Bronze Furnishings
(2 Chronicles 3.15-17; 4.1-10)
13-14Hiram was a skilled bronze worker from the city of Tyre. His father was now dead, but he also had been a bronze worker from Tyre, and his mother was from the tribe of Naphtali.
King Solomon asked Hiram to come to Jerusalem and make the bronze furnishings to use for worship in the Lord's temple, and he agreed to do it.
15Hiram made two bronze columns eight meters tall and almost two meters across. 16For the top of each column, he also made a bronze cap just over two meters high. 17The caps were decorated with seven rows of designs that looked like chains, 18with two rows of designs that looked like pomegranates.
19The caps for the columns of the porch were almost two meters high and were shaped like lilies.
20The chain designs on the caps were right above the rounded tops of the two columns, and there were 200 pomegranates in rows around each cap. 21Hiram placed the two columns on each side of the main door of the temple. The column on the south side was called Jachin, and the one on the north was called Boaz.
22The lily-shaped caps were on top of the columns.
This completed the work on the columns.
23Hiram also made a large bowl called the Sea. It was just over two meters deep, about 4.5 meters across, and 13.5 meters around. 24Two rows of bronze gourds were around the outer edge of the bowl, ten gourds to every 45 centimeters. 25The bowl itself sat on top of twelve bronze bulls with three bulls facing outward in each of four directions. 26The sides of the bowl were 75 millimeters thick, and its rim was like a cup that curved outward like flower petals. The bowl held about 40,000 liters.
27Hiram made ten movable bronze stands, each one over a meter high, almost two meters long, and almost two meters wide. 28-29The sides were made with panels attached to frames decorated with flower designs. The panels themselves were decorated with figures of lions, bulls, and winged creatures. 30-31Each stand had four bronze wheels and axles and a round frame 68 centimeters across, held up by four supports 45 centimeters high. A small bowl rested in the frame. The supports were decorated with flower designs, and the frame with carvings.
The side panels of the stands were square, 32and the wheels and axles were underneath them. The wheels were about 68 centimeters high 33and looked like chariot wheels. The axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were made out of bronze.
34-35Around the top of each stand was a 22-centimeter strip, and there were four braces attached to the corners of each stand. The panels and the supports were attached to the stands, 36and the stands were decorated with flower designs and figures of lions, palm trees, and winged creatures. 37Hiram made the ten bronze stands from the same mold, so they were exactly the same size and shape.
38 Hiram also made ten small bronze bowls, one for each stand. The bowls were almost two meters across and could hold about 800 liters.
39He put five stands on the south side of the temple, five stands on the north side, and the large bowl at the southeast corner of the temple.
40Hiram made pans for hot ashes, and also shovels and sprinkling bowls.
A List of Everything inside the Temple
(2 Chronicles 4.11—5.1)
This is a list of the bronze items that Hiram made for the Lord's temple: 41two columns; two bowl-shaped caps for the tops of the columns; two chain designs on the caps; 42400 pomegranates for the chain designs; 43ten movable stands; ten small bowls for the stands; 44a large bowl; twelve bulls that held up the bowl; 45pans for hot ashes, and also shovels and sprinkling bowls.
Hiram made these bronze things for Solomon 46near the Jordan River between Succoth and Zarethan by pouring melted bronze into clay molds.
47There were so many bronze things that Solomon never bothered to weigh them, and no one ever knew how much bronze was used.
48 Solomon gave orders to make the following temple furnishings out of gold: the altar; the table that held the sacred loaves of bread; 49 ten lampstands that went in front of the most holy place; flower designs; lamps and tongs; 50cups, lamp snuffers, and small sprinkling bowls; dishes for incense; fire pans; and the hinges for the doors to the most holy place and the main room of the temple.
51 After the Lord's temple was finished, Solomon put into its storage rooms everything that his father David had dedicated to the Lord, including the gold and the silver.
translation_text:
Solomon na lɔge o sɔ-fɔrɔ kom tei to
1Solomon déem kwei bena fuga-yatɔ (13) mo o ma o lɔ o tete sɔ-fɔrɔ kom o ti. 2O ma lɔ di-kamunu kolo yere na ye ‘Lebanon Goa Diga Kam’ to. Diga kam konto déem ye naba-laara finnu (50) mo dedɔrem baŋa ne. Ka kaywalem baŋa maŋem maa ye naba-laara finlei-yanu (25). Ka maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fintɔ (30) wɛ-baŋa seeni. Ba déem kwei Sedare bei mo ba daŋe Sedare ywoa baŋa ne. Ywoa yam jege gene sena mo. 3Danno telo ba na mɛ ba kwoli diga kam yuu to de déem ye Sedare dɛ mo. Bei sem déem ye finna-senu (45) mo. Bei fuga-senu (15) maa zege gena maama ŋwaane. 4Takworru gene setɔ mo ba ke pa te jeeri daane kuni betɔ. 5Diga kam nia yam mo jeeri daane yatɔ yatɔ ya maŋe diga kam yiga seeni. Ni dem maama sɛ sena sem maa ma daane.
6Solomon ta ma lɔ diga kalo ba na bwoi we ‘Ywoa Diga Kam’ to. Ka dedɔrem baŋa maŋem ye naba-laara finlei-yanu (25) mo. Ka kaywalem baŋa maŋem maa ye naba-laara fuga-yanu (15). O ta ma chwi ywoa o zege o ma ke pwola o tiŋi diga kam yiga ne. O laam ma kwoli ywoa yam o ma o ji pwoŋa.
7O déem ta ma lɔ diga kadwoŋi se o paare yituŋu kom taa zege da. Ba déem bwoŋi ka yere we, ‘Taane Dim Diga Kam’. Dáane mo Solomon déem jei o di nɔɔna taane. O pɛ ba kwei Sedare da-pelwaro mo ba ma kwoli-ka, ko zege ka tega kam ne se ko yi ka yuu kom seeni.
8O ma lɔ di selo o tete na zoore to pa se nye de di sesem sem. Jeiga kam konto déem zege konkɔlɔ kodwoŋi ne ye ka wo ‘Taane Dim Diga Kam’ kwaga ne. O ta ma lɔ sɔŋɔ kodwoŋi de o pa Ejipti Pa-faro bukɔ wolo o na di o ma o ke o kaane to. Ko di sem de maa nye de di sesem sem o na lɔge to.
9Ba déem kwei kandwa-ŋona yalo ba na sare pa ya sɛ sem maama maŋe daane to mo ba lɔ sɔ-fwaaro tento maama. Ba ma kwei-ya ba lɔ di sem ko zege se biri-beiri sem ne se ko yi se nayuni tem maama. Ba déem mɛ kandwa-ŋona yam ba lɔ di sem maama, ko zege bira-kwaga kam se ko vo ko yi konkɔlɔ-kamunu kom maama mo. 10Ba mɛ kandwa-zana mo ba beiri di sem maama. Kandwa yadwonna dedɔrem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni nana mo. Yadwonna dedɔrem de maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga. 11Ba ta ma kwei kandwa-ŋona yalo na sare ya maŋe daane to, ko woli de Sedare dɛ ba lɔ ba daŋe biri-beira kam baŋa ne. 12Ko ná ye pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ-kamunu kom, ba kwei kandwa-ŋona yalo ba na sare to mo ba lɔ kabira ba che-ko. Ba ma lware kandwa kuni betɔ ba daŋe da-baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba daŋe Sedare da-kwollu kandwa yam baŋa ne, ye ba lɔ konto ba di. Ko ye bedwe mo de ba na lɔge Baŋa Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom de ko napɔrɔ kom tei to.
Wɛ diga kam yera zela
13Pɛ Solomon ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo Tura ba bwoŋi Huram se o ba. 14Huram nu déem ye kadeim mo ye o nwoŋi Nafitali dwi dem wone. O kwo maa ye Tura tu na yeini o kwei channa o gɔgere wonnu to mo. Huram tete jege swa lanyerane. O maa ye gɔgɔ kolo na wae o kwei channa o ma o ke wonnu dwi dwi to mo. O ma ba Pɛ Solomon tei ye o ke totoŋe delo maama o na kwei o pa‑o to.
15Huram déem ma mɔ channa ywoa yalei o chwi. Ya dedoa wɛ-baŋa seeni dedɔrem déem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga-nana mo. Ya yera kikilu maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga-belei. [Ba déem mɔɔne-ya se ya taa ye wogo mo. Channa kam liliru maa ye nwe sena maŋem mo.] Ywoa yalei yam déem ye bedwe mo. 16O ma kwei channa o ma o mɔ wonnu o sugili ywei maama yuu ne se te wane te teili diga kam yuu kom seeni. Kolo na sugili da to maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu wɛ-baŋa seeni ywei maama ŋwaane. 17O ma gɔgere channa kam o lɛɛne daane ne chegero tei ye o kwei-ka o lei ywoa yalei wo-sugila yam yera ne. O ke konto mo kuni berepɛ wo-sugila yalei yam maama yera ne. 18O ta ma kwei channa kam o gɔgere Pomegara nyenyero o ke gene selei wo-sugila yalei yam yera ne. 19O ke wo-sugila yam pa se ya nye de kantɔgela na ye tei to mo. Ya wɛ-baŋa maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni bena. 20Ywei maama yuu maa jege wo-gigilu na wo chegero nyenyero tem teiŋa ne to. Wo-sugili dem daŋe ko baŋa ne mo, ye Pomegara nyenyero bia yalei tigisi te kaare-de gene selei.
21Huram ma kwei ywoa yam o chwi Wɛ diga kam napɔrɔ kom ni ne. O déem ma pa ba bwoi ywei delo na zege ni dem jazem seeni to we, ‘Jakim’. Delo maa na wo jagwia seeni to maa ye ‘Bowaza’. 22Wo-sugila yam maa wo ywoa yam yuni ne, ye ya nye de kantɔgela na ye tei to. Konto ma guri ywoa yam totoŋa.
23Huram laam ma kwei channa o mɔ ware-zon-zɔŋɔ ye o bwoŋi ko yere we, ‘Naneo kom’. Ko na zege ni dedoa se ko vo ni dedwoŋi to ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga mo. Ka wɛ-baŋa maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni benu. N ná kwei ŋona n maŋe-ka gigilu baŋa ne, ko ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni fintɔ mo ko kaare. 24Ba ma kwei channa ba gɔgere wonnu na nye de kunkwollu to ba ke zon-zɔŋɔ kom nia yam seeni ba kaare-ka gene selei. Jatwogo de noa ni maŋem maama jege kunkwollu fuga mo. Ba déem mɔɔne zon-zɔŋɔ kom de ko kunkwollu nyenyero tem daane mo. 25O ta ma kwei channa o mɔ nabɛ fuga-selei pa se ware-zon-zɔŋɔ kom daŋe se baŋa ne. Nabɛ sem maama ma kwei se kwɛ se pa daane mo. Nabɛ setɔ déem jeeri baŋa seeni mo. Se setɔ de jeeri wɛ-zoore seeni. Setɔ maa jeeri tega-kuri seeni ye setɔ jeeri wɛ-puli seeni. 26Zoŋa kam déem lira se ko maŋe de da-yiga noa maŋem mo. Ka ni dem maa nye de na-zoŋa ni na ye tei to, ye ka laam ta ka nwoŋi ne kantɔgela na ye tei to. Ka wó wane ka jwoŋi kuriwaa bia morro telei na mo.
27Huram ma kwei channa o ma o ke ware-zwe zegem torokooro fuga. Toroko maama dedɔrem maŋem ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni bena mo. Ko kaywalem baŋa maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem bena. Ko wɛ-baŋa de maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem betɔ. 28O na ke torokooro tem tei to mo tento: 29O kwei channa o ke woŋo na lwoni dakaa to mo o zege. O ma kwoli ka sɛ sena sem de channa. O ma mɔ nywonnu, de nabɛ, ko woli de cherubi nyenyero o yage ka sɛ sem yera ne, ye o daare o gɔgere tio-vɔɔ nyenyero o yage nywonnu de nabɛ nyenyero tem baŋa de te kuri seeni. 30Toroko maama déem jege weela nɛ sena de se bei. Te maama ye ba mɛ channa mo ba ke-te. Torokooro tem maa jege nyea yana se ya teili na-zoŋa kam. Ba ma gɔgere tio-vɔɔ nyenyero ba ke nyea yam sɛ sem ne. 31Ba ma ke wo-zego na ye gigilu to dakaa kam baŋa seeni. Wo-gigilu kom luuna se ko maŋe de jatwogo de noa ni maŋem dedoa mo. Ko kaywalem baŋa maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem dedoa de chichworo. Ba gɔgere wonnu mo ba kaare dakaa kam ni dem seeni. Ko ná ye toroko kom tete, ko sɛ sem maama mae daane mo, se se dae gigilu. 32Ko nɛ sem maa zege ko sɛ sena sem kuri ne. Se bei sem de ma meeli ko yera ne. Weela yam kaywalem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem dedoa de chichworo. 33Ba ke-ya nenɛɛne ya ye jara-keim toroko weela mo. Ba kwei channa mo ba ke bei sem, de weela yam, de ya yera wonnu tem maama. 34Ba ma meeli gwonnu tena dakaa kam sɛ sena sem yera ne se ba taa maa jaane-ka. 35Ba ma ke baŋa ba daŋe dakaa kam baŋa ne. Ka na luuna tei to maŋe de jatwogo de noa ni maŋem chichworo mo. Baŋa kam de wonnu telo na vɔge-ka to maama meeli dakaa kam yera ne mo. 36Huram ma gɔgere cherubi, de nywonnu, de konkwara o ke dakaa kam yera maama ne ko maŋe de pwola kalo maama na wora to. O ta ma gɔgere tio-vɔɔ nyenyero o kaare ka maama. 37O déem tɔge konto dwoŋi mo o ke torokooro fuga kam maama. Te maama maa mae daane ye te nye daane.
38Huram ma kwei channa o ma mɔ ware-zwe fuga se dedoa maama zege ko pa toroko dedoa. Ware-zoŋa maama déem jwoŋi garewɛ finna. Ko zege ka ni dedoa ne se ko yi dedwoŋi dem ye jatwogo de noa maŋem kuni bena. 39O ma kwei torokooro tem tenu o zege Wɛ diga kam tega-kuri saŋa kam seeni. O ta ma kwei tetem tenu o zege baŋa saŋa kam seeni. O ma kwei ware-zon-zɔŋɔ kom o zege Wɛ diga kam kuri saŋa kam seeni se ko maŋe de ka gugworo kolo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to.
40Huram ta ma mɔ zwe selo ba na wó taa mae ba pɛ tentwarem to, de sɛbullu, de na-zwe. O déem ma toŋe Baŋa Wɛ diga kam totoŋa yalo maama Pɛ Solomon na pɛ‑o to o ti. 41Ko maa ye channa ywoa yalei yam, de wo-sugila yalei yam na wo ywoa yalei yam yuu ne to, de channa kam na lɛɛne daane ka kwoli wo-sugila yam to, 42dedaane Pomegara bia yana nyenyero telo o na gɔgere o yage channa kalo na lɛɛne daane to ne. Pomegera nyenyero tem maa ye gene selei na kwoli wo-sugili dedoa maama. 43O déem ta mɔɔne torokooro fuga, de te ware-zwe fuga, 44dedaane ware-zon-zɔŋɔ dedoa, de ka kuri channa nabɛ nyenyero fuga-selei mo.
45Ko ná ye zwe selo ba na wó taa mae ba pɛ tentwarem to, de sɛbullu tem, de na-zwe sem, Huram kwei channa kalo na kwɛ to mo o ke te maama o pa Pɛ Solomon se ba taa mae ba toŋa Baŋa Wɛ diga kam totoŋa. 46Pɛ wom déem pɛ ba mɔ tento maama kamɔ-mɔra jeiga kalo na wo Jɔdan bwolo kom ne se ko maŋe de Sukofa de Zarefan tetare laŋa ne to mo. 47Solomon maŋe o wo pɛ ba maŋe channa wonnu tem konto dunni ba nii, te na tiini te daga to ŋwaane. Mo kokuri ba ta wo lɔre te dunni na mae tei to.
48Solomon déem ta pɛ ba ke Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wo zela yam maama. Ko maa ye sabu-seŋa kaanem bimbini dem, de sabu-seŋa tabolo kolo baŋa ne ba na tiŋi bworobworo na zege Wɛ yiga ne to. 49O ta pɛ ba kwei sabu-seŋa kalo na ye chekke to mo ba ke min-zwon-zegero. Te maa zege Wɛ di-yuu kom wone mɛ na ye di-yun-gala kam yiga ne to, pae tenu wo jazem seeni, ye tenu wo jagwia seeni. O ma pa ba gɔgere sabu-seŋa punnu nyenyero, ye ba kwei sabu-seŋa ba ke min-zwonnu, de wonnu telo na dwei mini dem to. 50O ma pa ba kwei sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to ba ke na-zwe, de wonnu telo na fɔge te kwɛ mini dem to, de ware-zwe, de zon-tanlɛ selo ba na ma ba zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa to, dedaane min-chala zwe. O ta ma pa ba kwei sabu-seŋa ba taare Wɛ di-yun-gala kam ni-bworru tem, dedaane bworru telo na zoore Wɛ diga kam tete to.
51Ko déem dɛ konto mo ye Pɛ Solomon pɛ ba toŋe Baŋa Wɛ diga kam totoŋa maama ba ti. O laam ma ja wonnu telo maama o kwo David déem na pɔɔre o zege Wɛ ŋwaane to o ja zo ka wo. Ko maa ye lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa wonnu tem de diga kam wo zela yam maama mo o kwei o zege Baŋa Wɛ diga kam lonne wonnu tiŋim jei sem ne.

english_text:
Solomon Brings the Sacred Chest to the Temple
(2 Chronicles 5.2—6.2)
1-2 The sacred chest had been kept on Mount Zion, also known as the city of David. But Solomon decided to have the chest moved to the temple while everyone was in Jerusalem, celebrating the Festival of Shelters during Ethanim, the seventh month of the year.
Solomon called together the important leaders of Israel. 3-4Then the priests and the Levites carried to the temple the sacred chest, the sacred tent, and the objects used for worship. 5Solomon and a crowd of people stood in front of the chest and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted.
6The priests carried the chest into the most holy place and put it under the winged creatures, 7whose wings covered both the chest and the poles used for carrying it. 8The poles were so long that they could be seen from right outside the most holy place, but not from anywhere else. And they stayed there from then on.
9 The only things kept in the chest were the two flat stones Moses had put there when the Lord made his agreement with the people of Israel at Mount Sinai, after bringing them out of Egypt.
10 Suddenly a cloud filled the temple as the priests were leaving the most holy place. 11The Lord's glory was in the cloud, and the light from it was so bright that the priests could not stay inside to do their work. 12 Then Solomon prayed:
“Our Lord, you said that you
would live in a dark cloud.
13Now I have built a glorious temple
where you can live forever.”
Solomon Speaks to the People
(2 Chronicles 6.3-11)
14Solomon turned toward the people standing there. Then he blessed them 15-16 and said:
Praise the Lord God of Israel! Long ago he brought his people out of Egypt. He did not choose a city from any tribe in Israel where his temple would be built, but he kept his promise to make my father David the king of Israel.
17 So when David wanted to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel, 18the Lord said, “It's good that you want to build a temple where I can be worshiped. 19 But you're not the one to do it. Your son will build a temple to honor me.”
20The Lord has done what he promised. I am the king of Israel like my father, and I've built a temple for the Lord our God. 21I've also made a place in the temple for the sacred chest. And in that chest are the two flat stones on which is written the solemn agreement the Lord made with our ancestors when he led them out of Egypt.
Solomon Prays at the Temple
(2 Chronicles 6.12-42)
22Solomon stood facing the altar with everyone standing behind him. Then he lifted his arms toward heaven 23and prayed:
Lord God of Israel, no other god in heaven or on earth is like you!
You never forget the agreement you made with your people, and you are loyal to anyone who faithfully obeys your teachings. 24My father David was your servant, and today you have kept every promise you made to him.
25 Lord God of Israel, you promised my father that someone from his family would always be king of Israel, if they do their best to obey you, just as he did. 26Please keep this promise you made to your servant David.
27 There's not enough room in all of heaven for you, Lord God. How could you possibly live on earth in this temple I have built? 28But I ask you to answer my prayer. 29 This is the temple where you have chosen to be worshiped. Please watch over it day and night and listen when I turn toward it and pray. 30I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you. So whenever any of us look toward this temple and pray, answer from your home in heaven and forgive our sins.
31Suppose someone accuses a person of a crime, and the accused has to stand in front of the altar in your temple and say, “I swear I am innocent!” 32Listen from heaven and decide who is right. Then punish the guilty person and let the innocent one go free.
33 Suppose your people Israel sin against you, and then an enemy defeats them. If they come to this temple and beg for forgiveness, 34listen from your home in heaven. Forgive them and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors.
35Suppose your people sin against you, and you punish them by holding back the rain. If they turn toward this temple and pray in your name and stop sinning, 36listen from your home in heaven and forgive them. The people of Israel are your servants, so teach them to live right. And please send rain on the land you gave them to be theirs forever.
37Sometimes the crops may dry up or rot or be eaten by locusts or grasshoppers, and your people will be starving. Sometimes enemies may surround their towns, or your people will become sick with deadly diseases. 38Listen when anyone in Israel truly feels sorry and sincerely prays with arms lifted toward your temple. 39You know what is in everyone's heart. So from your home in heaven answer their prayers, according to the way they live and what is in their hearts. 40Then your people will worship and obey you for as long as they live in the land you gave their ancestors.
41-42Foreigners will hear about you and your mighty power, and some of them will come to live among your people Israel. If any of them pray toward this temple, 43listen from your home in heaven and answer their prayers. Then everyone on earth will worship you, just like your people Israel, and they will know that I have built this temple to honor you.
44Our Lord, sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you. 45Answer their prayers from heaven and give them victory.
46Everyone sins. But when your people sin against you, suppose you get angry enough to let their enemies drag them away to foreign countries. 47-49Later, they may feel sorry for what they did and ask your forgiveness. Answer them when they pray toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, here in this land you gave their ancestors. From your home in heaven, listen to their sincere prayers and do what they ask. 50Forgive your people no matter how much they have sinned against you. Make the enemies who defeated them be kind to them. 51Remember, they are the people you chose and rescued from Egypt that was like a blazing fire to them.
52I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you. So listen when any of us pray and cry out for your help. 53When you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, you told your servant Moses to say to them, “From all people on earth, the Lord God has chosen you to be his very own.”
Solomon Blesses the People
54When Solomon finished his prayer at the altar, he was kneeling with his arms lifted toward heaven. He stood up, 55turned toward the people, blessed them, and said loudly:
56 Praise the Lord! He has kept his promise and given us peace. Every good thing he promised to his servant Moses has happened.
57The Lord our God was with our ancestors to help them, and I pray that he will be with us and never abandon us. 58May the Lord help us obey him and follow all the laws and teachings he gave our ancestors.
59I pray that the Lord our God will remember my prayer day and night. May he help everyone in Israel each day, in whatever way we need it. 60Then every nation will know that the Lord is the only true God.
61Obey the Lord our God and follow his commands with all your heart, just as you are doing today.
Solomon Dedicates the Temple
(2 Chronicles 7.4-10)
62-63Solomon and the people dedicated the temple to the Lord by offering 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing. 64On that day, Solomon dedicated the courtyard in front of the temple and made it acceptable for worship. He offered the sacrifices there because the bronze altar in front of the temple was too small.
65Solomon and the huge crowd celebrated the Festival of Shelters at the temple for seven days. There were people from as far away as the Egyptian Gorge in the south and Lebo-Hamath in the north. 66Then on the eighth day, he sent everyone home. They said goodbye and left, very happy, because of all the good things the Lord had done for his servant David and his people Israel.
translation_text:
Ba jaane Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba zo Wɛ diga kam
1Pɛ Solomon déem pɛ ni mo yi Isarele dwi tiina nakwa bam maama se ba ba o tei Jerusalem ne. Ko ye ba pwa bam de ba sɔ-yuni tem yiga tiina bam maama mo konto. O déem ma bwoŋi-ba se ba ke daane ba ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam na wo David teo Zion ne to ba ja ba zo Wɛ diga kam. 2Ba maama ma ke daane ba yi pɛ Solomon tei kuri delo na ke chane serepɛ chana kam ba na bwoi we Etanim to maŋa ne.
3Isarele tiina nakwa bam maama na jeeri konto to, Wɛ kaanem tiina bam ma zeiŋi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam wɛɛne 4se ba ja ba vo Wɛ diga kam. Levi tiina bam de kaanem tiina bam de ma zeŋe Wɛ wara-vwei dem de de yera zela yam maama ba ja ba kɛ. 5Pɛ Solomon de Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama ma vo ba gilimi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne. Ba ma kwei pei de naane dedɛ ba ma ba ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ. Vara bam tiini ba daga dedɛ pa se nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware ba ni o ga.
6Wɛ kaanem tiina bam ma zeŋe Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba zo Wɛ diga kam wone ba zege-ka di-yun-gala kam na tiini ka ye wose Wɛ ŋwaane to wone. Ba déem zege dakaa kam cherubi vɔna yam kuri ne mo. 7Cherubi selei sem vɔna yam twe mo wɛɛne ya kwoli dakaa kam de ka dɛ selo ba na mae ba zeŋe-ka to. 8Dɛ sem konto tiini se dɔra dedɛ. Ko ma pa se nɔɔno ná zo Wɛ diga kam o zege ka ni ne, o wae o tole o nae dɛ sem. Ko nam ná ye pwooni dem ne mo o zega, o ba nae-se. Se ta zege da de zem maama. 9Woŋo kolo yerane déem na wo Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam wone to mo ye kandwa-pelɛ selei selo Moses déem na kwei o ke-da Sinayi peo kom baŋa ne to. Dáane mo Baŋa Wɛ déem gwoni ni de Isarele tiina bam maŋa kalo ba na nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne ba kɛ to.
10Wɛ kaanem tiina bam na nwoŋi Wɛ di-yuu kom ne to mo kunkwoŋo pɔpɔ ko zo ko kwoli Baŋa Wɛ diga kam maama. 11Wɛ kaanem tiina bam ware ba jwoori ba zo da ba toŋe ba totoŋa, kunkwoŋo kom na wora ye Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom pwooni yɔɔre de su jei sem maama to ŋwaane.
12Pɛ Solomon ma ware Wɛ o we, “Baŋa Wɛ, nmo maŋe n ta n we, nmo wó ta‑n zoore kunkwon-lilirru wone mo. 13Amo nam lɔge sɔ-fɔrɔ mo a pa‑m, se n ta‑n zoore ka wone taa wuu.”
Solomon ŋɔɔne de nɔɔna bam
14Isarele nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama na zege da konto to mo Solomon pipiri o jeeri-ba. O ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage ba baŋa ne. 15O maa we:
“Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to maŋe de tia! O yɔɔre o ke o su ni delo o na pwooli de a kwo David to mo. Wɛ déem tage o we, 16‘Ko na zege maŋa kalo a na jaane a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi Ejipti teo wone to, a ya ta wo kuri teo Isarele dwia yam tega maama wone se ba lɔ wara-jei ba ma ba zuli a yere da. A laam nam mo kuri David se o taa nii a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne.’ ”
17Solomon ta ma ta o we:
“Amo kwo David ya maŋe o boŋe o ja mo se o lɔ Wɛ diga se ba taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to yere da. 18Baŋa Wɛ nam tage ded‑o o we, ‘Nmo ke chega de n na jaane boboŋa se n lɔ Wɛ diga se ba taa zuli a yere da to. 19Ko nam dae nmo mo jege se n lɔ diga kam n pa-ne. Se ko ye nmo tete bu mo wó lɔ diga amo yere zula ŋwaane.’ 20Leile konto Baŋa Wɛ ke o su tei maama o na pwooli we o wó ke to mo. Amo laam mo leiri a kwo David yuu ne a ji Isarele teo pɛ. A ta ma sɛ a lɔ Wɛ diga kam se Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to yere na zula da. 21A ta ma ke jeiga Wɛ diga kam wone se ba taa zege Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam da. Dakaa kam konto wone mo kandwa-pelɛ selo Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dem na popone se baŋa ne to maa wora. O déem gwoni ni dem konto de dé nabaara bam maŋa kalo o na jaane-ba o nwoŋi Ejipti teo wone to mo.”
Solomon na lwoori Wɛ tei to
2 Tigisim 6:12-42
22Solomon ma vo o zege o jeeri Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem ye Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama zege ba nia. O ma zeiŋi o je sem wɛyuu ne 23ye o lwoori Wɛ o we:
“Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to, wɛ dedwoŋi tera wɛyuu ne naa tega baŋa ne de na nye de nmo. Nmo yɔɔre n swoi balo na tɔge n chwei sem de ba wo maama to de n na yeini n ke n sui ni delo n na gwoni de-ba se n ke to. 24Ko ná ye amo kwo David na ye nmo tontoŋeno to, nmo na tiŋi ni ded‑o se n ke tei to mo n seene n ke te maama se ko ba ko yi zem. 25Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom, a laam lwoori‑m se n ke tei n na pwooli de a kwo David ye n we o dwi dem bá ga nɔɔno se o di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne, ne ba ná kwaane ba tɔge nmo chwei sem ne David tete na ke tei to. 26Isarele tiina Wɛ wom, nam sɛ se kolo nmo na pwooli de a kwo David na ye n tontoŋeno to seene ko ji chega.
27Amo Tu Wɛ, nmo wó seene n ta‑n zoore tega baŋa ne na? Wɛyuu de wɛ-baŋa jei sem maama ne, pwola tera ka na maŋe de nmo. Tetɛ mo diga kanto a na lɔge to wó wane ko yi n zoorem? 28Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, a ye nmo tontoŋeno mo. Nam pa n yiga taa wo a wɛ-lworo kom wone. Cheigi a keira kam se n daare n sɛ a zem na lwoori‑m woŋo kolo to. 29Popo, pa se n yia taa page diga kanto baŋa ne maŋa maama, tete de wea ne. Nmo maŋe n ta we ka zege n yere dem zula ŋwaane mo. Maŋa kalo maama ne a ná zege a jeeri diga kanto a lwoori‑m, se n cheigi a wɛ-lworo kom. 30Ko ná ye amo de n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam, dé ná zege dé jeeri nmo diga kam se dé lwoori‑m, se n jeini n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom ne n cheigi dé wɛ-lworo n daare n yage n chɛ debam.
31Nɔɔno ná ke o chɔge o dwoŋi yiga ye ba ja‑o ba zo nmo diga kam wone se o zege nmo kaanem bimbini dem yiga ne se o du duuri we o wo ke o chɔge, 32jeini telaao ne n cheigi o taane dem se n daare n ke kolo na maŋe to. Pɔɔre chega n tontoŋena bam tetare ne. Pa se puseŋ-nyeno wom na waarem delo na maŋe de o kikia to, se n daare n pa wolo na jege chega to na o bora.
33Nmo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam wɛleera ná pɛ se ba dona di-ba jara wone, ye ba laam ná pipiri ba jwoori nmo tei ba zo nmo diga kanto wone ba ma n yere dem ba lwoori‑m se n duri ba yibwona se n daare n yage n chɛ-ba, 34jeini Wɛ telaao ne n cheigi ba keira kam konto. Seene n yage ba wɛleera yam n ma‑n chɛ-ba, n daare n ja-ba n jwoori tega kalo nmo na kwei n pa ba nabaara bam to.
35Nmo nɔɔna bam wɛleera ná pɛ se n ja kunkwoŋo kom pa se doa ba nena, ye ba laam ná leiri ba wo ye ba zege ba jeeri n diga kam ba ma n yere dem ba lwoori wolim nmo tei ne de n na waare-ba tei to, 36jeini Wɛ telaao ne n cheigi ba keira kam. Yage n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam wɛleera n chɛ-ba, se n daare n bere-ba chwo-laao se ba taa tɔga. Pa se doa jwoori ka ne tega kanto n na kwei n pa n nɔɔna se ba taa tei to baŋa ne.
37Da-kore de jawe-chɛɛro ná tu te yi ba tega kam, ye jaweero naa kayere dwi dwi ná chɔge ba kara wodiiru tem, ye ba dona ná zaŋe ba teo kolo maama baŋa ne, naa ko ná ye lɛɛro telo maama mo yi n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam, 38cheigi ba keira kam. Ba wolo maama ná zeiŋi o jea o jeeri n diga kanto ye o lwoori‑m naa o keeri o jare‑m, o wo na tiini ko chɔge to ŋwaane, 39se n jeini n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom ne n cheigi o keira kam konto. Yage ba maama wɛleera n chɛ-ba se n daare n woli-ba. Ke de ba dedoa dedoa se ko maŋe de ba kikia na ye tei to, nmo yerane mo na yei nabiinu boboŋa na ye tei to ŋwaane. 40Konto wó pa se n nɔɔna bam taa kɔre‑m da yalo maama ba na wó taa ŋwe ye ba zoore tega kalo nmo na kwei n pa dé nabaara bam to wone.
41Ko ta ná ye veira balo na dae n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam dwi to, banto wae ba zege sa-teo ne ba tui ywo-seeni, ba na nigi n yere dem ŋwa to ŋwaane. 42Ko ye n yere na zaŋe de n na mɛ n dam n toŋe totoŋ-kamuna to ŋwaane mo banto yeini ba tui ywo. Ba wolo ná tu o zege o jeeri n diga kanto o lwoori‑m, 43se n jeini n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom ne n cheigi o wɛ-lworo kom konto. Ke n su kolo maama o na lwoori n tei ne to, se logo baŋa nɔɔna maama da ko ŋwaane ba ni nmo yere dem ŋwa, ye ba taa kɔre‑m nenɛɛne nmo tete nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam na ke tei to. Ba maa wó lɔre we diga kanto a na lɔge to seene ka ye nmo yere dem zula ŋwaane mo.
44Nmo nɔɔna bam ná nwoŋi se ba vo mɛ maama n na toŋe-ba se ba kwaare jara de ba dona, ye ba ná zege ba jeeri teo konto n na kuri to, de Wɛ diga kanto a na lɔga nmo yere dem zula ŋwaane to ba lwoori wolim nmo Baŋa Wɛ tei ne, 45se n jeini Wɛ telaao ne n cheigi ba wɛ-lworo kom, de ba na ŋɔne tei n yiga ne to, se n daare n ke chega n pa-ba.
46Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na ba ke wɛleera. Nmo nɔɔna bam nam ná ke wɛleera pa se nmo bane zaŋe de-ba, n wae n yage se ba dona di-ba pa se ba ji peena sa-teo ne yiga yiga naa bwola bwola de. 47Jei sem konto ne ba boboŋa ná jwoori ye ba leiri ba wo Wɛ ŋwaane, se n cheigi ba wɛ-lworo. Ba ná zege ba dona bam teo ne ba lwoori‑m ye ba we, ‘Dé seene dé tusi mo ye dé ke lwarem de puseŋa kikia’, 48ye ba ná pipiri ba jwoori n tei de ba wo maama, nam sɛ se n cheigi ba wɛ-lworo kom. Ba ná maŋe sa-teo ne ba zege ba jeeri tega kanto n na pɛ ba nabaara bam to, de teo kolo nmo na kuri n pa n tete to, de a na lɔge diga kalo nmo yere dem zula ŋwaane to, 49se n jeini n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom ne n cheigi ba wɛ-lworo kom de ba keira kam n daare n ke chega n pa-ba. 50Nam kwei n nɔɔna bam na ke kolo maama ba chɔge n yiga to n yage n chɛ-ba, de ba na nwoŋi n kwaga ne tei to. Nam pa se ba dona balo na di-ba to taa duri ba yibwona. 51Kokuri to, ba ye balo n na kuri n pa n tete se ba taa ye n nyɔn-mage nɔɔna to mo. N ma‑n ja-ba n nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne mɛ ba na nɛ yaara dedɛ ne min-vogo to.
52Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, ta‑n nii amo wolo na ye n tontoŋeno to baŋa ne, de n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne, se n cheigi dé wɛ-lworo maŋa kalo maama dé na lwoori wolim n tei ne to. 53Kokuri to, ko ye nmo tete mo pɔɔre debam logo baŋa dwi maama wone se dé taa ye nmo tete nyɔn-mage nɔɔna bam, ko maŋe de nmo déem na tage tei n bere n tontoŋeno Moses maŋa kalo nmo na le dé nabaara bam n ja n nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne to.”
54Solomon na ware Baŋa Wɛ ye o lwoori wolim o tei ne o ti konto to, o ma zaŋe wɛɛne o zege Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem yiga ne, mɛ o ya na kuni dwoona de teiŋa ne o zeiŋi o jea wɛɛne o lwoori to. 55O ma zege o yɔɔre Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom ye o kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ ba maama swolim. O ma ta de kwor-dɛa o we:
56“Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de tia mo, o na pɛ se o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam laam na siu ne o na maŋe o pwooli we o wó ke tei to. O na tiŋi ni de o tontoŋeno Moses we o wó ke wo-laaro telo maama to, de dedoa tete wo dɛ na. 57Debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó taa wora debam tei ne, nenɛɛne o déem na wora de dé nabaara bam tei to. O bá yage debam naa o ve debam. 58O nam wó virigi dé bochara se dé taa tɔge o chwei sem, ye dé daare dé sɛ o nia yam, de o bera yam, de o chullu tem maama, ne o na pɛ dé nabaara bam se ba taa tɔge to. 59Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se o yiga taa wo a taane dento a na lwoori o yiga ne to wone maŋa maama, wea de tete. Debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ ta wó woli amo wolo na ye o tontoŋeno to de o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam se ko maŋe de ba na lage tei dɛ wone to. 60Konto wó pa se logo baŋa dwi maama lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo ye Wɛ chekke ye o dwoŋi daa tera. 61Abam balo na ye debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna to, ta‑á yei-na se á ta‑á tɔge o bera yam á daare á sɛ o nia yam maama, ne á na maŋe á ke tei zem to.”
Ba di kuri Wɛ diga kam ŋwaane
62Pɛ Solomon dedaane Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama déem ma kwei pɛɛra ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. 63Solomon déem kwei naane morro finlei-telei (22,000) mo, de pei de bone morro bi de finlei (120,000) mo o pa se ba ma ba ke yazura pɛɛra ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. O de Isarele tiina bam maama ke konto mo ba ma pore Baŋa Wɛ diga kam o yere zula ŋwaane. 64Dɛ dem konto ne pɛ wom kwɛ konkɔlɔ kom na wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam yiga ne to mo se ko taa ye ko yera Wɛ ŋwaane. O ma zege konkɔlɔ kom tetare dem seeni o kwei zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de wodiu pɛɛra, de vara lara kalo na wora yazura pɛɛra ŋwaane to o ke kaanem dem. Kokuri to, channa kaanem bimbini dem na zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to muri se kaanem dem maama wane de ke de baŋa ne.
65Solomon de Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom na wo o tei ne to kwei da yarepɛ mo se ba di kuri dem. Ba kɔgɔ kom déem daga mo ye ba nwoŋi Isarele jei maama ne, ko zege Lebo-Hamafa teo ne se ko yi Ejipti bu-nɔgɔ kom seeni, ba ba ba tɔge ba di kuri dem ba ma zuli Baŋa Wɛ. 66Tega na poore to, Solomon ma bane nɔɔna bam se ba jwoori ba sam. Nɔɔna bam ma ke pɛ wom lei. Ba na maa jwoori sɔŋɔ to, ba déem jege wopwolo dedɛ de Baŋa Wɛ na ke wo-laaro telo maama o pa o tontoŋeno David de o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam to.

english_text:
The Lord Appears to Solomon Again
(2 Chronicles 7.11-22)
1The Lord's temple and Solomon's palace were now finished, and Solomon had built everything he wanted. 2 Some time later the Lord appeared to him again in a dream, just as he had done at Gibeon. 3 The Lord said:
I heard your prayer and what you asked me to do. This temple you have built is where I will be worshiped forever. It belongs to me, and I will never stop watching over it.
4You must obey me, as your father David did, and be honest and fair. Obey my laws and teachings, 5 and I will keep my promise to David that someone from your family will always be king of Israel.
6But if you or any of your descendants disobey my commands or start worshiping foreign gods, 7I will no longer let my people Israel live in this land I gave them. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped. Then people everywhere will think this nation is only a joke and will make fun of it. 8 This temple will become a pile of rocks! Everyone who walks by will be shocked, and they will ask, “Why did the Lord do such a terrible thing to his people and to this temple?” 9Then they will answer, “We know why the Lord did this. The people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.”
Other Things Solomon Did
(2 Chronicles 8.1-18)
10It took 20 years for the Lord's temple and Solomon's palace to be built. 11Later, Solomon gave King Hiram of Tyre 20 towns in the region of Galilee to repay him for the cedar, pine, and gold he had given Solomon.
12When Hiram went to see the towns, he did not like them. 13He said, “Solomon, my friend, are these the kind of towns you want to give me?” So Hiram called the region Cabul because he thought it was worthless. 14He sent Solomon only five tons of gold in return.
15After Solomon's workers had finished the temple and the palace, he ordered them to fill in the land on the east side of Jerusalem, to build a wall around the city, and to rebuild the towns of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
16Earlier, the king of Egypt had captured the town of Gezer; he burned it to the ground and killed the Canaanite people living there. Then he gave it to his daughter as a wedding present when she married Solomon. 17So Solomon had the town rebuilt.
Solomon ordered his workers to rebuild Lower Beth-Horon, 18Baalath, and Tamar in the desert of Judah. 19They also built towns where he could keep his supplies and his chariots and horses. Solomon ordered them to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere in his kingdom.
20-22Solomon did not force the Israelites to do his work. They were his soldiers, officials, leaders, commanders, chariot captains, and chariot drivers. But he did make slaves of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who were living in Israel. These were the descendants of those foreigners the Israelites could not destroy, and they remained Israel's slaves.
23Solomon appointed 550 officers to be in charge of his workers and to watch over his building projects.
24Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the older part of Jerusalem to her new palace. Then Solomon had the land on the east side of Jerusalem filled in.
25 Three times a year, Solomon burned incense and offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built.
Solomon had now finished building the Lord's temple.
26He also had a lot of ships at Ezion-Geber, a town in Edom near Eloth on the Red Sea. 27-28King Hiram let some of his experienced sailors go to the country of Ophir with Solomon's own sailors, and they brought back about 14 tons of gold for Solomon.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ daa veere o tete de Solomon
1Pɛ Solomon déem na lɔge Baŋa Wɛ diga kam, de o tete sɔŋɔ kom, de woŋo kolo maama o ya na lage se o lɔ o ti to, 2Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ba o veere o tete ded‑o o ke belei, ne o ya na maŋe o ke tei Gibeon ne to. 3Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we:
“Amo nigi nmo na lwoori a tei ne se a ke woŋo kolo a pa‑m to. Diga kam n na lɔga amo ŋwaane to, a seene a pɔɔre-ka se ka taa ye wose mo, se a yere dem taa wora taa wuu. Amo yi page ka baŋa ne ye a boboŋa de wó taa wo ka wone maŋa maama. 4Ko nam ná ye nmo, n ná jege chega n ŋwea ne, ne n kwo David déem na ke tei ye o yɔɔre o tɔge chwoŋa de boboŋ-laaro to, ye n ná sɛ n tɔge a nia yam, de a bera yam, de a chullu tem, 5amo laam wó pa se n dwi dem taa di Isarele teo paare taa wuu. A na pwooli tei de nmo kwo David we, o dwi dem bá ga nɔɔno se o di paare Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne to wó seene ko ji chega.
6Nmo dedaane dwi delo na wó saŋe nmo kwaga to nam ná ywori amo chwoŋa kam ne ye á ve a nia yam de a bera yam, á daare á pipiri á zuli wa yadwonna, 7amo laam wó zeili abam Isarele tiina bam se á daa yé ta‑á zoore tega kanto a na kwei a pa abam to baŋa ne. A maa wó ve diga kanto a ya na sɛ se ka taa ye wose a yere zula ŋwaane to de. Konto ná kea, dwi-gɛ tiina laam wó taa jege Isarele tiina bam mo ba mɔna ye ba gwooni-ba. 8Diga kanto maa wó yɔɔre ka to ka saare ka taa ye di-dwoŋo. Nɔɔna maama maa ná dɛ da se ba kɛ, ko wó ke-ba yaau mo, pa se ba taa chweesa ye ba tɛ we, ‘Bɛ mo ye Baŋa Wɛ pa se lɛɛro tento yi ba tega kam de ba Wɛ diga kam?’ 9Nɔɔna maa wó leiri we, ‘Ba tete mo mɛ ba kwaga ba ya ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Wonto nam ya mo jaane ba nabaara bam o nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne. Ba nam na pipiri ba tɔge wa yadwonna ye ba zuli-ya to ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se lɛɛro tento yi-ba.’ ”
Pɛ Solomon totoŋa yadwonna
10Pɛ Solomon déem kwei bena finlei mo o ma o lɔ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam de o tete sɔŋɔ kom maama. 11Solomon ma kwei teene finlei na wo Galili laŋa kam ne to o pa Tura teo pɛ Hiram, kokuri to wonto déem woli‑o de Sedare dɛ, de da-ŋonno tedwonna, de sabu-seŋa, ne o na laga tei maama se o ma o lɔ Wɛ diga kam to. 12Pɛ Hiram na zege Tura ne o vo o na teene delo Solomon na pɛ‑o to, o yi maa wo su-de. 13O ma ta de Solomon o we, “A badwoŋi, teene dento dwi mo nmo kwei n pa-ne?” O ma pa de laŋa kam yere we ‘Kabul’. Yere dem konto mo wora de zem maama. 14Hiram ya pɛ Solomon sabu-seŋa kalo dunni na yi kilo morro tena (4,000) to mo.
15Tontoŋena balo Solomon déem na pɛ se ba toŋe totoŋ-dɛɛra ba pa‑o to taane mo tento. O déem pɛ se ba lɔ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam, de o tete sɔŋɔ kom, de Millo jeiga kam, ye ba daare ba lɔ Jerusalem teo kabira kam, de Hazora teo kom, de Megido teo kom, de Gezere teo kom.
16Ko ye Ejipti Pa-faro wom déem mo maŋe o ke jara o di Gezere teo kom. O de mini mo ko wone ye o daare o go Kanaan tiina bam na zoore da to. O ma daare o kwei-ka o pa o bukɔ se o ma o zo Solomon. 17Solomon ma pa ba jwoori ba lɔ Gezere teo kom.
Solomon déem ma pa o tontoŋena bam lɔ Bɛte-Horon teo kom na wo kuri seeni to, 18de Baalafe, de Tamara na wo Judah kagoa kam ne to. 19O ta pɛ se ba lɔ teene delo o na wó taa zege wodiiru, de jara-keim torokooro, de sisein-nɔɔna da to. O ta pɛ se ba lɔ o boboŋa na jaane kolo maama se o lɔ to mo Jerusalem ne, de Lebanon ne, de jei selo maama o na di paare da to.
20-21Solomon na fe nɔɔna balo se ba taa toŋe totoŋ-dɛɛra ba pa‑o to déem ye Amori tiina, de Hiti tiina, de Pɛrizi tiina, de Hivi tiina, de Jebusi tiina mo. Banto dae Isarele dwi tiina ye ba ya ta daare Isarele tega kam ne. Banto nam ye dwia yalo Isarele tiina bam déem na wo yɔɔre ba chɔge to bia mo. Ba ta ye kabɛ mo de zem maama. 22Ko nam ná ye Isarele tiina bam tete, Solomon déem wo pɛ se banto ji o kabɛ. O nam pɛ se ba ji o jar-keira, de o dedɛɛra, de o jar-keira yiga tiina, de o jara-keim torokooro dira, dedaane o sisein-dira yiga tiina mo.
23Dedɛɛra balo na nii tontoŋena bam baŋa ne ba pa Solomon to déem ye nɔɔna bia yanu de finnu (550) mo. Ba déem maa nii o totoŋa yam maama baŋa ne.
24Pɛ Solomon kaane wolo na ye Ejipti Pa-faro wom bukɔ to déem zege David teo kom ne o vo sɔŋɔ kolo Solomon na lɔge o pa‑o to. Solomon ma lɔ Millo jeiga kam o woli da.
25Kuni betɔ bene maama wone mo Solomon yeini o ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra de yazura pɛɛra bimbini delo o na lɔga o pa Baŋa Wɛ to baŋa ne. O ta ma zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa o pa Baŋa Wɛ. Konto baŋa ne mo o déem pɛ se Wɛ diga kam zege ka ti.
26Pɛ Solomon déem pɛ se ba ke nabwor-kamunnu dedɛ Ezion-gebera ne ba pa‑o. Teo kom konto bwola de Elofe na wo Nane-soŋo kom ni ne Edom tega baŋa ne to mo. 27Pɛ Hiram ma toŋe o nɔɔna balo na yei nabwooru yuŋim to badaara se ba vo ba gwaane de Solomon nɔɔna bam ba toŋe. 28Ba ma yuŋi nabwooru tem ba vo ba yi Ofiri ye ba na sabu-seŋa dedɛ dáane. Ba ma ja sabu-seŋa kilo morro fuga-tena (14,000) ba jwoori ba vo ba pa Pɛ Solomon.

english_text:
The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon
(2 Chronicles 9.1-12)
1 The Queen of Sheba heard how famous Solomon was, so she went to Jerusalem to test him with difficult questions. 2She took along several of her officials, and she loaded her camels with gifts of spices, jewels, and gold. When she arrived, she and Solomon talked about everything she could think of. 3He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
4-5The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, his servants in their uniforms, the people who served his food, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple. 6She said:
Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done. 7But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are wiser and richer than I was told. 8Your wives and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
9I praise the Lord your God. He is pleased with you and has made you king of Israel. The Lord has always loved Israel, so he has given them a king who will rule fairly and honestly.
10The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, many jewels, and more spices than anyone had ever brought into Israel.
11-13In return, Solomon gave her the gifts he would have given any other ruler, but he also gave her everything else she wanted. Then she and her officials went back to their own country.
Solomon's Wealth
(2 Chronicles 9.13-28)
King Hiram's ships brought gold, juniper wood, and jewels from the country of Ophir. Solomon used the wood to make steps for the temple and palace, and harps and other stringed instruments for the musicians. It was the best juniper wood anyone in Israel had ever seen.
14Solomon received almost 23 tons of gold a year. 15The merchants and traders, as well as the kings of Arabia and rulers from Israel, also gave him gold.
16Solomon made 200 gold shields and used almost seven kilograms of gold for each one. 17He also made 300 smaller gold shields, using almost two kilograms for each one, and he put the shields in his palace in Forest Hall.
18His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold. 19-20The back of the throne was rounded at the top, and it had armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on both sides of the throne, and there was a statue of a lion at both ends of each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
21Since silver was almost worthless in those days, everything was made of gold, even the cups and dishes used in Forest Hall.
22Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
23He was the richest and wisest king in the world. 24People from every nation wanted to hear the wisdom God had given him. 25Year after year people came and brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, or mules.
26 Solomon had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses that he kept in Jerusalem and other towns.
27 While he was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
28-29 Solomon's merchants bought his horses and chariots in the regions of Musri and Kue. They paid 600 pieces of silver for a chariot and 150 pieces of silver for a horse. They also sold horses and chariots to the Hittite and Syrian kings.
translation_text:
Seba ka-pɛ wom yera taane
1Seba teo ka-pɛ wom déem nigi Pɛ Solomon yere na zaŋe jei maama ne de o na zuli Baŋa Wɛ tei to. O ma zaŋe o vo Jerusalem se o faŋe‑o de bwia yalo na dana to o nii. 2O déem pɛ se o tontoŋena dedɛ tɔge ded‑o ba vo, dedaane kona yalo na zeŋe talwoŋ-ywei dwi dwi, de sabu-seŋa, de kandwa-nyenno dedɛ to. O na yi Solomon tei to mo o bwei‑o bwia yalo maama o boboŋa na jaane se o bwei to. 3Pɛ Solomon de ma leiri o bwia yam maama. Ya ná maŋe ya chana tei de, o wane o leiri ya maama. 4Seba teo ka-pɛ wom ma maane Solomon swa yam maama na ye tei to. O ta ma na pɛ sɔŋɔ kolo o na lɔge to, 5de wodiiru telo o na yeini o di to, de o na kwɛ o tontoŋena bam jeiŋa jei tei, de balo na zeŋe o wodiu de wo-nyɔɔro ba pa‑o to na zo gare-nyenno telo to, dedaane pɛɛra yalo o na yeini o zwɛ o ma o ke kaanem Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ne to. O na maane tento maama to, ko ma pa o ni yɛ.
6O ma ta de pɛ wom o we, “A ta na wo a tete teo ne ye a ni n yera seina yalo maama to seene ko ye chega mo. 7Ko ná dae amo tete mo na tu a na tento maama to, a ya wó ta we ko ye vwa mo. A nam na nigi wonnu telo to wo yi tei maama a yi dento zem na nɛ to chichworo. Nmo swa yam de n jejegero tem daga te dwoi ba na taga tei ba bere-ne to. 8Nmo nɔɔna bam de n tontoŋena bam tiini ba jege yu-ywoŋo, ba na wo n tei ne dɛ maama ba cheigi nmo swa taana yam to ŋwaane. 9N Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom maŋe de tia, de o wo na dɛ nmo ye o kuri‑m se n di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne to. Baŋa Wɛ na swoi Isarele dwi tiina taa wuu to ŋwaane mo o kuri‑m se n ji ba pɛ, se n daare n tɔge chwoŋa n ta‑n bora chega bora n pa-ba.”
10Ka-pɛ wom déem ma kwei sabu-seŋa na dwoi kilo morro tena (4,000) to o pa Solomon, ko woli de talwoŋ-ywei, de kandwa-nyenno dedɛ. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam ta wo fɔge o ja talwoŋ-ywei selo na daga se yi selo Seba ka-pɛ wom na kwei o ja o ba o pa Pɛ Solomon to.
11Pɛ Hiram nabwooru telo déem na zege Ofiri ne te ja sabu-seŋa te ba te pa Pɛ Solomon to ta ma ja da-ŋonno de kandwa-nyenno dedɛ na nwoŋi da to te ba te pa‑o. 12Pɛ wom ma kwei dɛ sem o ma ke nateina se ya woli Wɛ diga kam ne, de pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne. O ma daare o ma dɛ sem o ke kwanno dwi dwi o pa balo na leeni to. Da-ŋonno tem konto tiini te lana te dwoi telo maama na tu te yi Isarele teo de zem maama to.
13Pɛ Solomon déem kwei kolo maama Seba ka-pɛ wom na laga to o pa‑o mo. Ko dae wonnu telo o boboŋa na jaane se o pa‑o to yerane, se ko ye ka-pɛ wom na lwoori kolo maama o tei ne to mo o pɛ‑o o woli da. Ka-pɛ wom de o kwaga kam laam ma jwoori ba teo.
Solomon jejegero na daga tei to
14Bene maama wone Solomon déem yeini o jwoŋi sabu-seŋa kilo morro finlei-tetɔ (23,000) mo, 15ko woli de lampwoo kolo o na jwoŋi bimbeera, de pipim-piina, de Arabia pwa bam maama, de Isarele teo kateira yiga tiina bam tei ne to.
16Pɛ Solomon déem kwei sabu-seŋa o ma mɔ nantan-kamuna bia yalei (200) mo. O déem kwei sabu-seŋa na yi kilo terepɛ to mo o ma turi se dedoa dedoa. 17O ta ma ke nantan-balwa bia yatɔ (300), ye o kwei sabu-seŋa na yi kilo telei to o ma turi se dedoa dedoa. O ma kwei-se o ke diga kalo ba na bwoi we ‘Lebanon Goa’ to wone.
18Pɛ wom ta ma pa se ba kwei tuu yeila ba ma ke paare yituŋ-zɔŋɔ ba pa‑o. Ba ma daare ba ma sabu-seŋa kalo na ye chekke to ba turi ko yera. 19Nateini delo na jege natein-yia yaredo to mo diini de yi paare yituŋu kom. Ko kwaga kam maa ye kukulu ko baŋa seeni. Ko je selei sem maama maa jege nywoŋo nyenyego se takeiri ne. 20Nateini dem natein-yi maama de maa jege nywoŋo nyenyero telei de baŋa ne, jazem de jagwia seeni, se ko ke nywoŋo nyenyero fuga-telei. Logo baŋa teene maama ne paare yituŋu tera ko na nye de Pɛ Solomon nyem kom.
21Ko ná ye Pɛ Solomon na-zwe sem maama, ko woli de o zela yalo maama na wo ‘Lebanon Goa’ diga kam ne to, ba mɛ sabu-seŋa mo ba ke te maama. Ba wo mɛ lu-nyenno ba ke te kolokolo, te na ba jege yuu Solomon paare maŋa kam ne to ŋwaane. 22Pɛ wom déem jege nabwor-kamunnu dedɛ te na woli de Pɛ Hiram nabwooru tem te beeri pipiu ŋwaane to. Bena yatɔ maama wone o nabwooru tem wó zeŋe sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de tuu yeila, de kali-faaro, de kali dwi dwi mo te ba te pa‑o.
23Pɛ Solomon déem mo ye nadum de swa tu o dwoi pwa maama logo baŋa ne. 24Logo baŋa nɔɔna dwi maama maa swoi se ba taa tui o tei ba cheigi yi-poro taane delo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑o to. 25Ba nam ná yeini ba tui, ba dedoa dedoa maa wó ja o pɛɛre o ba o pa Solomon. Bene maama wone ba déem jaane lu-nyenno wonnu, de sabu-seŋa wonnu, de gwaaro, de terale nuga, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa dwi dwi, de sisein-nɔɔna, de bona-sisei ba tui ba pa‑o.
26Solomon déem ma la jara-keim torokooro moro de bia yana (1,400), dedaane sisein-nɔɔna morro fuga-telei (12,000). O déem pɔɔre se sedwonna o yage teene delo o na kuri se ŋwaane to ne. Sedaara maa wo Jerusalem ne mɛ o na zoore to. 27O paare dim maŋa ne, lu-nyenno tiini te daga Jerusalem ne ne kandwa tei. Sedare da-ŋonno de maa ba jege zore nenɛɛne kaporro na daga tei wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne to. 28Nɔɔna déem vei Ejipti de Silisia teene dem mo ba kwei sabu ba yeigi sisei ba pa Solomon. Ko maa ye o pipim-piina mo yeini ba yeigi-se Silisia teo ne, ye ba ŋwe kolo na maŋe to. 29Ko ná ye jara-keim toroko, ba yeini ba yeigi-ko Ejipti ne de lu-nyenno sabu-dala bia yaredo (600) mo. Siseiŋa maa yeigi de lu-nyenno sabu-dala bi de finnu (150). Pɛ wom pipim-piina bam déem yeini ba kwei torokooro de sisein-nɔɔna dedɛ ba yeigi ba pa Hiti tiina pwa bam de Aram tiina pwa mo.

english_text:
Solomon Disobeys the Lord
1-2 The Lord did not want the Israelites to worship foreign gods, so he had warned them not to marry anyone who was not from Israel.
Solomon loved his wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt. But he also loved some women from Moab, Ammon, and Edom, and others from Sidon and the land of the Hittites. 3-4Seven hundred of his wives were daughters of kings, but he also married 300 other women.
As Solomon got older, some of his wives led him to worship their gods. He wasn't like his father David, who had worshiped only the Lord God. 5Solomon also worshiped Astarte the goddess of Sidon, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon. 6Solomon's father had obeyed the Lord with all his heart, but Solomon disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
7Solomon built shrines on a hill east of Jerusalem to worship Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Molech the disgusting god of Ammon. 8In fact, he built a shrine for each of his foreign wives, so all of them could burn incense and offer sacrifices to their own gods.
9-10The Lord God of Israel had appeared to Solomon two times and warned him not to worship foreign gods. But Solomon disobeyed and did it anyway. This made the Lord very angry, 11and he said to Solomon:
You did what you wanted and not what I told you to do. Now I'm going to take your kingdom from you and give it to one of your officials. 12But because David was your father, you will remain king as long as you live. I will wait until your son becomes king, then I will take the kingdom from him. 13When I do, I will still let him rule one tribe, because I have not forgotten that David was my servant and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
Hadad Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
14Hadad was from the royal family of Edom, and here is how the Lord made him Solomon's enemy:
15-16Some time earlier, when David conquered the nation of Edom, Joab his army commander went there to bury those who had died in battle. Joab and his soldiers stayed in Edom six months, and during that time they killed every man and boy who lived there.
17-19Hadad was a boy at the time, but he escaped to Midian with some of his father's officials. At Paran some other men joined them, and they went to the king of Egypt. The king liked Hadad and gave him food, some land, and a house, and even let him marry the sister of Queen Tahpenes. 20Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, and the queen let the boy grow up in the palace with her own children.
21When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he said to the king, “Your Majesty, please let me go back to my own country.”
22“Why?” asked the king. “Do you want something I haven't given you?”
“No, I just want to go home.”
Rezon Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
23Here is how God made Rezon son of Eliada an enemy of Solomon:
Rezon had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah. 24-25He formed his own small army and became its leader after David had defeated Hadadezer's troops. Then Rezon and his army went to Damascus, where he became the ruler of Syria and an enemy of Israel.
Both Hadad and Rezon were enemies of Israel while Solomon was king, and they caused him a lot of trouble.
The Lord Makes a Promise to Jeroboam
26Jeroboam was from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His father Nebat had died, but his mother Zeruah was still alive. Jeroboam was one of Solomon's officials, but even he rebelled against Solomon. 27Here is how it happened:
While Solomon's workers were filling in the land on the east side of Jerusalem and repairing the city walls, 28Solomon noticed that Jeroboam was a hard worker. So he put Jeroboam in charge of the work force from Manasseh and Ephraim.
29-30One day when Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, he met Ahijah, a prophet from Shiloh. No one else was anywhere around. Suddenly, Ahijah took off his new coat and ripped it into twelve pieces. 31Then he said:
Jeroboam, take ten pieces of this coat and listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you. “Jeroboam, I am the Lord God, and I am about to take Solomon's kingdom from him and give you ten tribes to rule. 32But Solomon will still rule one tribe, since he is the son of David my servant, and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
33“Solomon and the Israelites are not like their ancestor David. They will not listen to me, obey me, or do what is right. They have turned from me to worship Astarte the goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of Ammon.
34“Solomon is David's son, and David was my chosen leader, who did what I commanded. So I will let Solomon be king until he dies. 35Then I will give you ten tribes to rule, 36but Solomon's son will still rule one tribe. This way, my servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to be worshiped.
37“You will be king of Israel and will rule every nation you want. 38I'll help you if you obey me. And if you do what I say, as my servant David did, I will always let someone from your family rule in Israel, just as someone from David's family will always rule in Judah. The nation of Israel will be yours.
39“I will punish the descendants of David, but not forever.”
40When Solomon learned what the Lord had told Jeroboam, Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam. But he escaped to King Shishak of Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died.
Solomon Dies
(2 Chronicles 9.29-31)
41Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the book about him and his wisdom. 42After he had ruled 40 years from Jerusalem, 43he died and was buried there in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_text:
Solomon kaana bam taane
1Pɛ Solomon déem swoi se o taa lage kaana dedɛ na ye veira to mo o woli o kaane wolo na ye Ejipti Pa-faro bukɔ wom to ne. O kaana bam konto nwoŋi Moaba tiina, de Amon tiina, de Edom tiina, de Sidon tiina, de Hiti tiina bam wone mo. 2Se ko lwoori o na di kaana bam konto to, Baŋa Wɛ ya maŋe o kaane Isarele dwi tiina bam we, ba yé zaŋe ba di bukwa balo na nwoŋi teene dem konto ne to, naa ba sɛ se ba bukwa zo banto de baara. Baŋa Wɛ tage o we, “Á ná ke konto, banto wó soge á bia bam boboŋa se ba taa zuli ba jwona yam mo.” De konto maama, Solomon déem ta lage teene dem konto bukwa mo. 3Solomon déem di kaana na ye pwa bukwa to bia yarepɛ (700) mo. O maa jege ka-bi bia yatɔ (300) o woli da. Kaana bam konto ma pa se Solomon ywori Wɛ chwoŋa wone. 4Solomon na yi o kokweero maŋa to, mo o kaana bam pɛ se o zuli ba wa-yɔɔro tem. Konto ma pa se o daa ba jege chega de o Tu Baŋa Wɛ se ko yi o kwo David ya na yɔɔre o ke o chega de Wɛ tei to. 5O déem zuli Asetare jwoni dem Sidon tiina na zuli to, de Moleka jwoni dem na ye wo-zɔɔne delo Amon tiina na zuli to mo. 6Solomon déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. O maa wo kwei o bochare maama o ma o tɔge Baŋa Wɛ nenɛɛne o kwo David na ke tei to.
7Solomon déem lɔge wara-jei bimbini mo peo kolo na wo Jerusalem wɛ-puli seeni to yuu ne, se o taa zuli Chemosi na ye Moaba tiina jwoni to, de Moleka na ye Amon tiina jwoni to da. 8O daa ta ke konto dwoŋi mo o pa o kaana bam maama, se ba de taa zwɛ wonnu ba daare ba taa ke kaanem ba pa ba tete wa-yɔɔro tem.
9 Baŋa Wɛ bane déem zaŋe Solomon baŋa ne, de o na ywori o chwoŋa kam wone to. Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to déem ya veere o tete o bere Solomon kuni belei mo. 10O ma yɔɔre o kaane‑o se o yé zuli wa-yɔɔro. Solomon ma ve Wɛ ni dem. 11Mo kokuri Baŋa Wɛ tage de Solomon o we, “Nmo na paale n ke n boboŋa na laga tei, ye n ve a ni dem, de a bera yam to ŋwaane, a laam lage a jwoŋi paare dem nmo jeŋa ne mo a kwei a pa nmo tontoŋena bam dedoa se o taa tei. 12David nam na ye nmo kwo to ŋwaane, amo bá ke konto nmo ŋwea maŋa ne. Nmo bu nam ná leiri n yuu ne, a laam wó jwoŋi paare dem wonto jeŋa ne mo. 13De konto maama, a bá jwoŋi paare dem maama o jeŋa ne. A nam wó pa se dwi dedoa daare se o di paare banto baŋa ne, a tontoŋeno Pɛ David ŋwaane, dedaane a tete teo Jerusalem ŋwaane.”
Solomon dono Hadad taane
14 Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ se dono wodwoŋi mo zaŋe o ke chichuŋu de Solomon. Wonto ye Edom tu Hadad na ye Edom pɛ sɔŋɔ bu to mo. 15Faŋa faŋa mo David déem ya vei o kwaare jara de Edom teo tiina ye o wane-ba. Joaba wolo na ye o jar-keira bam yiga tu to ma tɔge o vo teo kom konto se o kwei twa bam o ke. O na wora to mo o go Edom tiina baara bam maama. 16O de Isarele jar-keira bam maama déem ma maŋe Edom teo kom ne ba ke chane seredo, ye ba go baara bam maama ba ti. 17Hadad ta na ye bu to, o ma tɔge de o kwo wom tontoŋena balo ya na ye Edom tiina to se ba duri ba lu ba vo Ejipti teo. 18Ba déem zege Midian ne mo ba vo Paran. Ba ta ma zege Paran ne ba kwei nɔɔna ba woli da ba vo Ejipti. Ba na yi da to, Ejipti Pa-faro wom ma kwei sɔŋɔ, de tega, de ba dɛ wone ni-wodiu o pa Hadad. 19Pɛ wom yi na su Hadad kikia to, o ma kwei o tete kaane nyaane o pa Hadad se o di o ma o ke kaane. Pɛ kaane Tapenesi nyaane wom mo konto. 20Wonto ma lo bakeira o pa Hadad, ye ba pa o yere we Genubafe. Tapenesi maa jege‑o o kɔna pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne. Bu wom de Pa-faro wom bia bam maama maa me daane.
21Hadad déem nigi we David de o jar-keira bam yiga tu Joaba mo tega. O ma ta de Ejipti Pa-faro wom o we, “Pɛ, ja! Pa-ne chwoŋa se a jwoori a kwo sɔŋɔ.” 22Pɛ wom ma leiri o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo? Nmo laga woŋo mo ye n ga amo tei ne na?” Hadad ma leiri o we, “Ko dae konto. Nam yage se a jwoori sɔŋɔ.” O ma seene o jwoori o tete teo.
Solomon dono Rezon taane
23Wɛ ta ma pa se dono wodwoŋi ke chichuŋu de Solomon. Wonto maa ye Eliada bu Rezon. Rezon déem duri mo o yage o tu Hadadezere na ye Zoba teo pɛ to. 24David na wane Hadadezere jar-keira bam to, konto kwaga ne mo Rezon kuri baara balo na ye pawe-nyena to o ke daane ye o ji ba yiga tu. Ba ma vo Damasika ba zoore da. Ba na wora to mo ba pɛ Rezon di paare Damasika ne. 25Rezon déem ye Isarele tiina dono mo maŋa kalo maama Solomon ta na wo o ŋwea wone to. O pɛ se lɛɛro yi Isarele tiina bam, ne Hadad de na ke tei to mo. O déem di paare Siria tiina maama baŋa ne ye o chuli Isarele tiina bam.
Solomon dono Jeroboam taane
26Nɔɔno wolo de daa na zaŋe o ke chichuŋu de Pɛ Solomon to ye o tontoŋena bam dedoa, o yere na ye Jeroboam to mo. Wonto déem ye Efrayim tu Nebat bu mo, ye o nwoŋi Zereda. O nu mo ye Zerua. O maa ye kadeim. 27Ko na ke tei ye o chuli Solomon to mo tento: Solomon ya pɛ se ba fɔge ba lɔ Millo jeiga kam Jerusalem teo ne. O ta ma pa ba kwɛ teo kom kabira kam. 28Jeroboam déem jege baare ye Solomon maane we o seene o yia totoŋa yam baŋa ne mo. Mo kokuri o pɛ se Jeroboam nii Josɛf dwi tiina balo na toŋe totoŋa yam to baŋa ne.
29Dɛ dedwe mo Jeroboam nwoŋi Jerusalem ne o maa vei chwoŋa. Wɛ sampwora Ahija na ye Siloo tu to ma jeeri‑o chwoŋa yuu ne. Ba balei bam maa wo pwooni ne ba yerane, ye Ahija zo gare-daŋɔ kolo na ye nadoŋo to. 30O ma le o gare-daŋɔ kom, o ja o tore tore se ko ji gare-bia fuga-telei. 31O ma ta de Jeroboam o we, “Kwei gare-bia fuga n ta‑n jega, bɛŋwaane Baŋa Wɛ wolo na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to mo we, ‘A lage a ja paare dem mo a jwoŋi Solomon jeŋa ne, a daare a kwei dwia fuga a pa‑m se n ta‑n tei. 32A nam wó pa se Solomon ta taa tei dwi dedoa mo, a tontoŋeno David ŋwaane, dedaane Jerusalem teo kolo a na kuri Isarele dwia yam maama wone se ko taa ye amo tete nyem to ŋwaane. 33Solomon de o dwi dem ve amo ye ba zuli Asetare jwoni dem Sidon tiina na zuli to, de Chemosi jwoni na ye Moaba tiina wɛ to, de Moleka na ye Amon tiina wɛ to. Ba maa wo tɔge amo chwei sem se ba taa ke kolo na pwoli a wo to. Ba nam ve a chullu tem de a bera yam mo. Ba maa wo tɔge chwoŋa kalo Solomon kwo David na tɔge to. 34De ko de, a bá le paare dem maama Solomon jeŋa ne. O ta ná ŋwe, o daa ta wó di paare dem, a tontoŋeno David ŋwaane, de wonto na toŋe o tɔge a bera yam de a nia yam to ŋwaane. 35Solomon bu nam ná leiri o yuu ne, a laam wó jwoŋi paare dem o tei ne, ye a daare a kwei Isarele dwia fuga a pa‑m se n ta‑n tei. 36A nam wó pa se Solomon bu wom taa tei dwi dedoa mo. Konto mo wó pa se Pɛ David dwi dem nɔɔno ta taa di paare Jerusalem teo kolo wone amo na kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli-ne da to. 37Ko daare, ko ná ye nmo Jeroboam, amo wó tiŋi‑m se n ta‑n tei Isarele tega kam mɛ maama n boboŋa na lage to. N laam wó di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne. 38N nam jege se n ke kolo maama a na wó pa‑m ni se n ke to, ye n tɔge a chwei sem n ke kolo na wó pwoli a wo to. Nmo ná toŋe n tɔge a bera yam de a ni-kaana yam, nenɛɛne a tontoŋeno David déem na ke tei to, amo wó taa wora n tei ne. A ta wó pa se n dwi dem taa wora taa, nenɛɛne a na pɛ se David dwi dem ke tei to. N wó ta‑n nii Isarele dwi tiina bam baŋa ne. 39Solomon wɛleera yam ŋwaane, a lage a waare David kwaga kam mo. Ko nam bá taa ye taa wuu.’ ”
40Konto ŋwaane Solomon déem beeri chwoŋa se o go Jeroboam. Jeroboam ma duri o lu o vo Ejipti. O ma maŋe Ejipti teo Pɛ Sisake tei ne se ko taa nii maŋa kalo Solomon na tege to.
Solomon toone
41Solomon déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam, de o yi-poro kom maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Solomon Kikia Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 42Solomon jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare Isarele teo maama ne o ke bena finna mo. 43O laam ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwo David teo kom ne. O bu Rehoboam ma leiri o yuu ne o di paare.

english_text:
Some of the People Rebel against Rehoboam
(2 Chronicles 10.1-19)
1Rehoboam went to Shechem where everyone was waiting to crown him king.
2Jeroboam son of Nebat heard what was happening, and he stayed in Egypt, where he had gone to hide from Solomon. 3But the people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said, 4“Your father Solomon forced us to work very hard. But if you make our work easier, we will serve you and do whatever you ask.”
5“Give me three days to think about it,” Rehoboam replied, “then come back for my answer.” So the people left.
6Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
7They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should do what they ask today. Tell them you will make their work easier.”
8But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials. 9He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
10His younger advisors said:
Here's what we think you should say to them: “Compared to me, my father was weak. 11He made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
12Three days later, Jeroboam and the others came back. 13Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors. 14He spoke bluntly and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
15-19 When the people realized that Rehoboam would not listen to them, they shouted: “We don't have to be loyal to David's family. We can do what we want. Come on, people of Israel, let's go home! Rehoboam can rule his own people.”
Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor, and Rehoboam sent him to talk to the people. But they stoned him to death. Then Rehoboam ran to his chariot and hurried back to Jerusalem.
So the people from the northern tribes of Israel went home, leaving Rehoboam to rule only the people from the towns in Judah. Ever since that day, the people of Israel have opposed David's family in Judah. All of this happened just as the Lord's prophet Ahijah had told Jeroboam.
20When the Israelites heard that Jeroboam was back, they called everyone together. Then they sent for Jeroboam and made him king of Israel. Only the people from the tribe of Judah remained loyal to David's family.
Shemaiah Warns Rehoboam
(2 Chronicles 11.1-4)
21After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and take control of the whole country. So he called together 180,000 soldiers from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.
22Meanwhile, God told Shemaiah the prophet 23to give Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin this warning: 24“Don't go to war against the people from Israel—they are your relatives. Go home! I am the Lord, and I made these things happen.”
Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord and went home.
Jeroboam Makes Religious Changes
25Jeroboam rebuilt Shechem in Ephraim and made it a stronger town, then he moved there. He also fortified the town of Penuel.
26-27One day, Jeroboam started thinking, “Everyone in Israel still goes to the temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord. What if they become loyal to David's family again? They will kill me and accept Rehoboam as their king.”
28 Jeroboam asked for advice and then made two gold statues of calves. He showed them to the people and said, “Listen everyone! You won't have to go to Jerusalem to worship anymore. Here are your gods who rescued you from Egypt.” 29Then he put one of the gold calves in the town of Bethel and the other in the town of Dan. 30The people sinned because they started going to these places to worship.
31Jeroboam built small places of worship at the shrines and appointed men who were not from the tribe of Levi to serve as priests. 32-33 He also decided to start a new festival for the Israelites on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, just like the one in Judah. On that day, Jeroboam went to Bethel and offered sacrifices on the altar to the gold calf he had put there. Then he assigned the priests their duties.
translation_text:
Isarele tiina ve Rehoboam
1Rehoboam déem ma vo Sɛkɛm, Isarele tiina bam maama na jeeri da se ba tiŋi‑o pɛ to ŋwaane. 2Nebat bu Jeroboam déem ya duri o vo Ejipti mo se o lu Pɛ Solomon jeŋa ne. O ta na wo dáane to mo o nigi Solomon toone ŋwa. O ma jwoori sɔŋɔ. 3Ba ma toŋe ba bwoŋi Jeroboam se o de Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama tɔge daane ba vo Rehoboam tei. Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, 4“Nmo kwo Solomon déem tiini o yaare debam de totoŋ-chɛɛra. Konto to, nam kwaane se n pa ko taa bwona ko pa debam, se dé wane dé sii dé yaara yam wone. N ná ke konto, dé wó sɛ dé pa‑m.” 5Rehoboam ma leiri-ba o we, “Nam véi-na se da yatɔ kwaga ne á laam jwoori á ba se dé nii.” Nɔɔna bam ma viiri.
6Pɛ Rehoboam ma bwɛ taane dem de nɔn-kwe selo déem ya na ye o kwo Solomon nakwa to. O ma bwei-ba o we, “Bɛ boboŋa mo abam jega se á ma á woli-ne se a leiri a pa nɔɔna banto?” 7Nakwa bam ma leiri ba we, “Nmo ná tu n tete se n sɛ nɔɔna bam zem na lwoori kolo to, ye n to n pa-ba, ba de wó yɔɔre ba sɛ ba pa‑m wuu.”
8Rehoboam ma ve nɔn-kwe sem boboŋe dem ye o daare o vo o bane de nɔn-donno telo na ye o yuudwonna pa ba wo o tei ne to. 9O ma bwei-ba o we, “Nɔɔna banto na we, a kwo wom na yaare-ba dedɛ to, a laam pa se ba sii de ba yaara yam to, bɛ boboŋa mo abam jega se á ma á woli-ne se a ma a leiri a pa-ba?” 10Nɔn-donno tem na ye o yuudwonna to ma leiri ba we, “Ko ná ye balo na lwoori‑m konto to, ta n bere-ba we, ‘Amo noa kam tete kula ka dwoi a kwo wom teiŋa! 11A kwo keim déem seene ko chana á baŋa ne. Ko nam ná ye amo, ko wó dwoni dáane. A kwo wom déem mɛ kafene mo o fere abam. Amo nam laga a ma kafene selo nia na chana ne nɔŋɔ donem to mo a ma a fere abam.’ ”
12Da yatɔ yam dɛ ne mo Jeroboam de nɔɔna bam maama daa jwoori ba vo Pɛ Rehoboam tei, ne o na maŋe o ta se ba ke tei to. 13Ba na tu to, Pɛ Rehoboam ma zage-ba ni-chɛɛre, o na dole nɔn-kwe sem taane dem o yage to ŋwaane. 14O nam yɔɔre o ke o tɔge nɔn-donno tem boboŋa yam mo. O ma ta o we, “A kwo keim déem seene ko chana á baŋa ne. Ko nam ná ye amo, ko wó dwoni dáane. A kwo wom déem mɛ kafene mo o fere abam. Amo nam lage a ma kafene selo nia na chana ne nɔŋɔ donem to mo a ma a fere abam.”
15Pɛ Rehoboam na wo sɛ nɔɔna bam taane dem to déem tɔge Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa na jaane tei to mo. Ko pɛ Baŋa Wɛ na dɛ o sampwora Ahija baŋa o ta tei de Nebat bu Jeroboam to mo ji chega.
16Isarele tiina bam maama na maane we pɛ wom ve se o ke o tɔge ba boboŋa yam to, ba ma chɛ sɔɔ ye ba leiri‑o ba we, “Isarele tiina bam, debam dedaane Jesse bu David dae daane. Dé yiga tera o dwi dem paare wone! Pa-na dé jwoori-na sam. David dwi tu, ta‑n nii n tete sɔ-yuu kom baŋa ne!” Ba maama ma seene ba jwoori ba sam. 17Ko nam ná ye Isarele dwi tiina balo na zoore Judah teene dem ne to yerane, Pɛ Rehoboam déem ta mo di paare ba baŋa ne.
18Pɛ Rehoboam ma toŋe Adoniram wolo na nii totoŋ-chɛɛra yam baŋa ne to se o vo Isarele dwia yalo na wo baŋa seeni to tei o kwɛ taane dem. O na yi da to, nɔɔna bam maama ma dole‑o de kandwa ba go. Konto baŋa ne Pɛ Rehoboam ma faŋe o lei o toroko o duri o lu o vo Jerusalem. 19De zem maama Isarele tiina na wo baŋa seeni to ve mo se David dwi dem taa di paare ba baŋa ne.
20Isarele tiina bam na maane we Jeroboam tu o wora to, ba ma toŋe ba bwoŋi‑o se o ba ba kɔgɔ kom na gilimi mɛ to. Ba ma pa se o ji Isarele tiina pɛ. Judah dwi dem yerane mo sɛ ba pa David diga kam.
Semaya na pworisi tei to
21Rehoboam na yi Jerusalem to mo o bwoŋi Judah de Benjamin dwia yam nɔɔna balo na yei jara keim chekke to. Ba déem ye jar-keira morro bi de funɔnɔ (180,000) mo. O ma boŋe se o kwaare jara de Isarele dwi tiina badaara bam, se o wane o pa ba maama jwoori ba ke daane se o taa tei-ba, o na ye Solomon bu to ŋwaane. 22Wɛ ma pa o tontoŋeno Semaya ni ye o we, 23“Nam pa amo taane dento yi Judah teo Pɛ Solomon bu Rehoboam, de Judah dwi tiina bam maama, de Benjamin dwi tiina bam, de nɔɔna badaara bam maama we, 24‘Baŋa Wɛ kwora mo tento: Yé zaŋe-na á ke jara de á chorro Isarele tiina bam. Á maama véi-na sɔŋɔ, se amo mo pɛ se konto maama ke.’ ” Ba maama ma sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem ye ba jwoori ba sam.
Jeroboam nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne
25Jeroboam ma fɔge o lɔ Sɛkɛm teo na wo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne to o zoore da. O ma zaŋe dáane o vo o lɔ Peneli teo. 26Dɛ dedwe o ma boŋe o tete ne o we, “Keim dem na ye tei to, paare dem wó wane de jwoori David diga kam. 27Amo nɔɔna bam ta ná lage ba taa vei Jerusalem Wɛ diga kam ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ, ba laam wó jwoori ba sɛ ba pa ba tu Rehoboam wolo na ye Judah teo pɛ to mo. Ko maa ná ke konto, ba wó go-ne mo se ba laam taa zuli wonto.”
28O na boŋe de wone o ti to, o ma kwei sabu-seŋa o mɔ na-mɔre selei o daare o ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Isarele tiina bam, á daa yé daane á tete de á na vei Jerusalem yiga yiga á zuli Wɛ tei to. Nii-na! Wa yalo déem na jaane abam ya ja nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne to mo tento.” 29O ma kwei kamɔgɔ kom dedoa o zege Bɛtel ne, o daare dedoa o zege Dan ne. 30Keim dem konto ma pa se Isarele tiina bam ke wɛleere, ba na yeini ba vei Bɛtel de Dan ba zuli kamwaro tem to ŋwaane. 31Jeroboam déem ta lɔge wara-jei bimbina zwonnu tem yuu ne, ye o daare o kuri kaanem tiina balo na wo nwoŋi Levi dwi dem wone to se ba taa ke kaanem jei sem konto ne.
32Jeroboam ta ma zege chulu se nɔɔna bam taa vei ba kaane kamwaro tem chane nana chana kam da fuga-yanu dɛ ne, ne ba déem na yeini ba ke kuri tei Judah teo ne to. Jeroboam maa yeini o vei Bɛtel o ke kaanem o pa na-mɔre kamwaro telo o na mɔɔne to. O déem pɛ se kaanem tiina bam zoore Bɛtel ne, se ba taa nii wara-jei selo o na lɔge to baŋa ne mo.
Wɛ sampwora na tu Bɛtel ye o ta taane delo to
33Chane nana chana kam da fuga-yanu dɛ dem na yi to, Jeroboam ma vo Bɛtel o ke kaanem bimbini delo o na mɔɔne to baŋa ne, se o di kuri delo o na dɛ o tete boboŋa ŋwaane o tiŋi o pa Isarele tiina bam to.

english_text:
A Prophet Condemns the Altar at Bethel
1-2 One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. Suddenly one of God's prophets arrived from Judah and shouted:
