The Lord sent me with a message about this altar. A child named Josiah will be born into David's family. He will sacrifice on this altar the priests who make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on it.
3You will know that the Lord has said these things when the altar splits in half, and the ashes on it fall to the ground.
4Jeroboam pointed at the prophet and shouted, “Grab him!” But at once, Jeroboam's hand became stiff, and he could not move it. 5The altar split in half, and the ashes fell to the ground, just as the prophet had warned.
6“Please pray to the Lord your God and ask him to heal my hand,” Jeroboam begged.
The prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed.
7“Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”
8“No, I wouldn't go with you, even if you offered me half of your kingdom. I won't eat or drink here either. 9The Lord said I can't eat or drink anything and that I can't go home the same way I came.” 10Then he started home down a different road.
An Old Prophet from Bethel
11At that time an old prophet lived in Bethel, and one of his sons told him what the prophet from Judah had said and done.
12“Show me which way he went,” the old prophet said, and his sons pointed out the road. 13“Put a saddle on my donkey,” he told them. After they did, he got on the donkey 14and rode off to look for the prophet from Judah.
The old prophet found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the prophet from Judah?”
“Yes, I am.”
15“Come home with me,” the old prophet said, “and have something to eat.”
16“I can't go back with you,” the prophet replied, “and I can't eat or drink anything with you. 17The Lord warned me not to eat or drink or to go home the same way I came.”
18The old prophet said, “I'm a prophet too. One of the Lord's angels told me to take you to my house and give you something to eat and drink.”
The prophet from Judah did not know that the old prophet was lying, 19so he went home with him and ate and drank.
20During the meal the Lord gave the old prophet 21a message for the prophet from Judah:
Listen to the Lord's message. You have disobeyed the Lord your God. 22He told you not to eat or drink anything here, but you came home and ate with me. And so, when you die, your body won't be buried in your family tomb.
23After the meal the old prophet got a donkey ready, 24and the prophet from Judah left. Along the way, a lion attacked and killed him, and the donkey and the lion stood there beside his dead body.
25Some people walked by and saw the body with the lion standing there. They ran into Bethel, telling everyone what they had seen.
26When the old prophet heard the news, he said, “That must be the prophet from Judah. The Lord warned him, but he disobeyed. So the Lord sent a lion to kill him.”
27The old prophet told his sons to saddle his donkey, and when it was ready, 28he left. He found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and lion standing there. The lion had not eaten the body or attacked the donkey. 29The old prophet picked up the body, put it on his own donkey, and took it back to Bethel, so he could bury it and mourn for the prophet from Judah.
30He buried the body in his own family tomb and cried for the prophet. 31He said to his sons, “When I die, bury my body next to this prophet. 32I'm sure that everything he said about the altar in Bethel and the shrines in Samaria will happen.”
33But Jeroboam kept on doing evil things. He appointed men to be priests at the local shrines, even if they were not Levites. In fact, anyone who wanted to be a priest could be one. 34This sinful thing led to the downfall of his kingdom.
translation_text:
1Jeroboam ta na zege bimbini dem teiŋa ne se o ke kaanem to mo Wɛ tontoŋeno wodwoŋi tu o yi da. Baŋa Wɛ ya toŋe kotu se o zege Judah teo ne mo o vo Bɛtel. 2O ma ta kaanem bimbini dem taane, ne Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑o ni se o ke tei to. O ma bage de kwor-dɛa ye o we, “Bimbini, bimbini, nam cheigi! Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Ba wó lo bakeira kalo na nwoŋi David dwi dem wone o yere na ye Josia to. Nmo baŋa ne mo o lage o go kaanem tiina balo na ke kaanem ywo-seeni to. O maa wó zwɛ nabiina kwi nmo baŋa ne.”
3Dɛ dem konto ne, Wɛ tontoŋeno wom ta ma maŋe taane dem ye o we, “Bimbini dem wó bɔke belei ye tentwarem na wo de baŋa ne to wó jage. Konto baŋa ne mo á wó lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ mo seene o tɔge amo baŋa ne o ŋɔɔne.”
4Pɛ Jeroboam na nigi Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na tage tei o chɔge Bɛtel bimbini dem to, o ma twe o jeŋa o jeeri‑o, ye o bage de kwor-dɛa o we, “Ja-o-na”. Pɛ wom na tage konto to mo bedwe baŋa ne o jeŋa kam koge ka maŋe wɛɛne. O ma ware o de-ka tega ne. 5Bimbini dem de ma bɔke belei pa se tentwarem dem jage jei maama, ko maŋe de Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na tage Baŋa Wɛ kwora tei to.
6Pɛ Jeroboam ma ta de nɔɔno wom o we, “Lwoori n Tu Baŋa Wɛ tei ne se o duri a yibwona o daare o yɔɔre a jeŋa kam.” Wɛ tontoŋeno wom ma seene o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ pa se pɛ wom jeŋa kam jwoori ka lana, ne ka ya na ye tei to. 7Pɛ wom ma ta de Wɛ tontoŋeno wom o we, “Nam pa se dé vo a sɔŋɔ se n di wodiu. A nam ta jege pɛɛre se a woli da a pa‑m.” 8Nɔɔno wom ma leiri pɛ wom o we, “Nmo ná maŋe n kwei n jejegero tem chichworo mo se n pa-ne, a bá sɛ a vo n sɔŋɔ. A ta ná wo ywo-seeni, a bá di wodiu naa a nyɔ na. 9Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ pɛ-ne o ni dento mo o we, ‘Yé di kolokolo naa n nyɔ na. Nam yé tɔge chwoŋa kalo nmo ya na tɔge to n jwoori Judah teo.’ ” 10Wɛ tontoŋeno wom ma zege Bɛtel ne o tɔge chwo-gaa o viiri.
Wɛ sampwora kadwoŋi na tusi tei to
11Maŋa kam konto ne, Wɛ sampwora kadwoŋi ya zoore Bɛtel ne ye o tiini o kwe. O bia bam ma pa se o maane Wɛ tontoŋeno wolo na nwoŋi Judah teo to na ke tei maama Bɛtel ne to. Ba ta ma ta o na tage taane delo o bere pɛ wom to. 12Bia bam kwo ma bwei-ba o we, “O dɛ yei ne mo o viiri?” Ba ma bere‑o Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na dɛ chwoŋa kalo o viiri to. 13Nɔn-kwea kam ma ta de o bia bam o we, “Ke-na lela á ti bonaga kam yiga á pa-ne.” Ba na ti ka yiga to, o ma faŋe o lei-ka 14ye o duri se o yi Wɛ tontoŋeno wom. O ma vo o na o na jei tei-zɔŋɔ kuri ne ye o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo mo ye Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na nwoŋi Judah teo n ba to na?” O ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, ko ye amo mo.”
15Sampwora kalo na nwoŋi Bɛtel to ma ta‑o o we, “Pa dé vo sɔŋɔ se n di wodiu.”
16Wɛ tontoŋeno wom ma leiri o we, “A bá wane a da de nmo a jwoori. A maa bá wane a zo n diga, naa a di wodiu, naa a nyɔ na de nmo. 17Baŋa Wɛ pɛ-ne ni o we, a yé di wodiu naa a nyɔ na ywo-seeni. A nam yé tɔge chwoŋa kalo a na dɛ to a jwoori Judah teo.”
18Nɔn-kwea kam ma leiri o we, “Amo de ye nmo dwoŋi sampwora mo. Wɛ maleka nam mo tage Baŋa Wɛ kwora de amo o we, a ja‑m a jwoori a sɔŋɔ se n di wodiu n daare n nyɔ na.” Tento maama nam ye vwa yerane mo o fɔga. 19Wɛ tontoŋeno wom ma seene o da de Wɛ sampwora kam o vo o di wodiu ye o nyɔ na o sɔŋɔ ne.
20Maŋa kalo ba na jei ba di to mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora tu o sampwora kalo na kwe ye o ja wodwoŋi wom o jwoori o sɔŋɔ to tei. 21O ma bage Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na nwoŋi Judah to de kwor-dɛa o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: N ve ni delo n Tu Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑m se n tɔge to. 22N nam sɛ se n jwoori n ba n di wodiu mɛ o na taga o we n yé di to. Konto ŋwaane, ba bá suli‑m n kwoa yibeeli dem ne.”
23Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na di o ti to, nɔn-kwea kalo na jaane‑o o jwoori to ma ti o bonaga yiga o pa‑o se o viiri. 24Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na maa viiri to mo nywoŋo jeeri‑o chwoŋa ne ko go. O yera yam na tigi chwoŋa ni ne to, nywoŋo kom de bonaga kam ma daare te maŋe ya baŋa ne te zega. 25Nɔɔna balo na dɛ chwoŋa kam konto ba maa kɛa to ma na o na tiga ye nywoŋo kom maŋe o baŋa ne ko zega. Ba ma duri ba vo Bɛtel teo mɛ nɔn-kwea kam na zoore to ba ta kolo na ke to ba bere nɔɔna.
26Wɛ sampwora kalo na chege‑o o ja o jwoori to na nigi to, o ma ta o we, “Wɛ tontoŋeno wom tete mo tento! O ve Baŋa Wɛ ni dem o na pɛ‑o se o tɔge to. Baŋa Wɛ ma kwei‑o o pa nywoŋo kom se ko kaare‑o ko go, se ko pa o na tage tei to ji chega.” 27O ma ta de o bia bam o we, “Ti-na bonaga kam yiga á pa-ne.” Ba ma seene ba ke konto. 28O ma nwoŋi o vo o na Wɛ sampwora kam na tigi chwoŋa kam ni ne ye bonaga kam de nywoŋo kom maŋe o baŋa ne te zega. Nywoŋo kom ya wo di‑o. Ko maa wo daane bonaga kam de. 29Nɔn-kwea kam ma kwei Wɛ tontoŋeno wom yera yam o daŋe o bonaga kam baŋa ne o ja o jwoori o tete teo. O ma keeri o lua o daare o suli‑o. 30O déem suli‑o o tete yibeeli wone mo. O de o bia bam ma keeri ba we, “Woo, a choro ywoo.”
31O na kwei‑o o suli o ti to, o ma ta de o bia bam o we, “Amo tete ná tega, kwei-na amo á suli Wɛ tontoŋeno wonto yibeeli dem wone. Pɛ-na a kwi sem á tiŋi o kwi sem teiŋa ne. 32Kokuri to, wonto na tage Wɛ kwora kalo o ma o chɔge bimbini dem na wo Bɛtel ne to, dedaane wara-jei selo na wo Samaria teene dem wone to wó seene ko ji chega.”
33Tento maama kwaga ne, Jeroboam déem ta wo sɛ se o yage o keim-balwaaro tem. O ta yeini o le wolo de wolo maama o na yi to mo se ba taa ke kaanem wara-jei sem ne. Wolo maama ná lage se o ji kaanem tu, o yeini o sɛ kotu mo se o ke konto. 34Jeroboam de o dwi dem na ke wɛleera yanto dwoŋi to mo pɛ se o dwi dem maama saare logo baŋa ne.

english_text:
Jeroboam's Son Dies
1About the same time, Abijah son of Jeroboam got sick. 2-3Jeroboam told his wife:
Disguise yourself so no one will know you're my wife, then go to Shiloh, where the prophet Ahijah lives. Take him ten loaves of bread, some small cakes, and honey, and ask him what will happen to our son. He can tell you, because he's the one who told me I would become king.
4She got ready and left for Ahijah's house in Shiloh.
Ahijah was now old and blind, 5but the Lord told him, “Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask about her son. I will tell you what to say to her.”
Jeroboam's wife came to Ahijah's house, pretending to be someone else. 6But when Ahijah heard her walking up to the door, he said:
Come in! I know you're Jeroboam's wife—why are you pretending to be someone else? I have some bad news for you. 7Give your husband this message from the Lord God of Israel: “Jeroboam, you know that I, the Lord, chose you over anyone else to be the leader of my people Israel. 8I even took David's kingdom away from his family and gave it to you. But you are not like my servant David. He always obeyed me and did what was right.
9“You have made me very angry by rejecting me and making idols out of gold. Jeroboam, you have done more evil things than any king before you.
10 “Because of this, I will destroy your family by killing every man and boy in it, whether slave or free. I will wipe out your family, just as fire burns up trash. 11Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind!”
12That's the Lord's message to your husband. As for you, go back home, and right after you get there, your son will die. 13Everyone in Israel will mourn at his funeral. But he will be the last one from Jeroboam's family to receive a proper burial, because he's the only one the Lord God of Israel is pleased with.
14The Lord will soon choose a new king of Israel, who will destroy Jeroboam's family. And I mean very soon. 15The people of Israel have made the Lord angry by setting up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. So the Lord will punish them until they shake like grass in a stream. He will take them out of the land he gave to their ancestors, then scatter them as far away as the Euphrates River. 16Jeroboam sinned and caused the Israelites to sin. Now the Lord will desert Israel.
17Jeroboam's wife left and went back home to the town of Tirzah. As soon as she set foot in her house, her son died. 18Everyone in Israel came and mourned at his funeral, just as the Lord's servant Ahijah had said.
Jeroboam Dies
19Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including the battles he won, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 20He was king of Israel for 22 years, then he died, and his son Nadab became king.
King Rehoboam of Judah
(2 Chronicles 11.5—12.16)
21Rehoboam son of Solomon was 41 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 17 years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon.
22The people of Judah disobeyed the Lord and made him even angrier than their ancestors had. 23 They also built their own local shrines and stone images of foreign gods, and they set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah on every hill and in the shade of large trees. 24 Even worse, they allowed prostitutes at the shrines, and followed the disgusting customs of the foreign nations that the Lord had forced out of Canaan.
25 After Rehoboam had been king for four years, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem. 26 He took everything of value from the temple and the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
27Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe. 28Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he was finished.
29Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 30He and Jeroboam were constantly at war. 31Rehoboam's mother Naamah was from Ammon, but when Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Abijam then became king.
translation_text:
Ahija pworisi o chɔge Jeroboam
1Maŋa kam konto ne Jeroboam bu Abija weela ko chana. 2Pɛ Jeroboam ma ta de o kaane o we, “Paale n leiri n tete se ba yé lɔre we n ye a kaane, se n zaŋe n vo Siloo. Wɛ sampwora Ahija wo dáane. Wonto ya mo taga a taane we amo wó ji pɛ to. 3Nam kwei bworobwooru fuga, de maasa, de tooro kunkwolo dedoa n ja n vo n pa‑o n daare n bwei‑o n nii kolo na lage ko ke bakeira kam to. O laam wó ta o bere‑m.”
4Jeroboam kaane wom ma sɛ. O ma zaŋe o vo Siloo ye o kɛ o yi Ahija sɔŋɔ. Kanto maŋa ne to, Ahija yia mo dwei, o na tiini o kwe to ŋwaane. 5Baŋa Wɛ nam tage de Ahija o we, “Jeroboam kaane wó ba n tei ye o bwei o bakeira kam jaweo kom bwia, o na tiini o weele to ŋwaane. A lage a bere‑m n na jege se n leiri‑o tei de tei to. O nam wó ke nenɛɛne o dae pɛ kaane mo tei.”
6Ahija na nigi kaane wom napera dɔnne o diga ni ne to, o ma ta o we, “Zo n ba, se a yei we nmo mo ye Jeroboam kaane wom. Bɛŋwaane mo n paale n ke se ba yé lɔre‑m? A nam jege ta-lɔŋɔ mo se a ta a bere‑m. 7Jwoori sɔŋɔ n ta taane dento n bere n baro Jeroboam we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo mo le nmo a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam wone se n ji ba yiga tu. 8A déem mo jaane paare dem a jwoŋi David dwi dem jeŋa ne a kwei a pa‑m. De ko de, n wo ke ne a tontoŋeno David na toŋe tei to. Wonto déem sɛ a nia yam ye o tɔge a chwei sem de o wo maama pa se o kikia pwoli a wo. Nmo nam wo ke konto. 9N tiini n toŋe lwarem n dwoni balo maama ya na dɛ yiga ba ba to. Nmo tiini n zaŋe a bane mo de n na mɔɔne wa-yɔɔro n pa n tete to. Ya maa ye jwona yalo ba na mɛ sabu-seŋa ba mɔ to. Konto to n mɛ n kwaga n ya amo. 10Keim dem konto ŋwaane a lage a pa se lɛɛro yi Jeroboam sɔ-yuu kom mo. A nam wó go n dwi bakeiri sem maama Isarele teo ne, ko ná ye balo ta na wo ba kwo sɔŋɔ ne to, de balo na tei ba tete to de. Amo wó yɔɔre a chɔge Jeroboam dwi dem, ne mini na di na-beinnu kula tei to. 11Nmo dwi dem nɔɔno wolo maama na wó te teo kolo wone to wó ji kukuri ni-wodiu mo. Wolo na wó te pwola ne to maa wó taa ye duura ni-wodiu. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.’ ”
12Ahija ta ma ta de Pɛ Jeroboam kaane wom o we, “Nam jwoori sɔŋɔ. N ná yɔɔre n nɔne n naga teo kom wone, n bu wom wó te. 13Isarele tiina maama maa wó keeri o lua ye ba kwei‑o ba suli. Jeroboam dwi dem maama wone, ko ye bu wom konto yerane mo ba wó kwei ba suli. Kokuri to, Jeroboam dwi dem maama wone wonto yerane kikia mo su Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to yi. 14Baŋa Wɛ tete mo lage o tiŋi pɛ wolo na wó di paare Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne, se wonto saare Jeroboam kwaga kam maama. Ko bá dáane ye ko ke. 15Baŋa Wɛ wó waare Isarele tiina bam nenɛɛne vo-dɛɔ na fuli nanchan-gullu ye te vuvugi tei to. O ta wó gɔ Isarele tiina bam te-ywoŋa kanto o na kwei o pa ba nabaara bam to ne, o daare o pa se ba jage ba kɛ yiga yiga ba gaale Yuferata buga kam. Kokuri to, ba pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe de-ba, ba na zuli Asera nyenyego dɛ sem to ŋwaane. 16Wɛ wó ve Isarele tiina bam, Jeroboam na ke wɛleera o daare o pa se banto de lwoni ba ke-ya to ŋwaane.”
17Jeroboam kaane wom ma zaŋe o jwoori Tiraza teo. O na yɔɔre o nɔne o naga o diga ni ne to mo bu wom tega. 18Isarele tiina maama ma keeri o lua ye ba kwei‑o ba suli, ne Wɛ sampwora Ahija na maŋe o ta Wɛ kwora we ko wó ke tei to.
Pɛ Jeroboam toone
19Jeroboam déem na di paare ye o toŋe wonnu telo maama to ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone, ne ko ná ye o tigura keim de o na tei o nɔɔna tei to. 20Jeroboam di paare Isarele teo ne bena finlei-yalei (22) mo ye o daare o te. O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Nadab ma leiri o ji pɛ.
Judah teo Pɛ Rehoboam taane
21Solomon bu Rehoboam déem jege bena finna-dedwe (41) mo ye o ji Judah teo pɛ. O ma di paare bena fuga-yarepɛ (17) Jerusalem ne, mɛ Baŋa Wɛ tete na kuri Isarele teene maama wone se ba taa zuli o yere da to. O nu yere mo ye Naama. O maa ye Amon tu.
22Judah tiina bam déem tiini ba toŋe lwarem ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. Ba na tiini ba ke wɛleera tei to chuchugi Wɛ bane ko dwoni ba nabaara bam na ke tei to. 23Ba déem lɔge bimbina mo se ba taa kaane ba jwona zwonnu maama baŋa ne, de teeni maama kuri ne. Ba ta ma chwi kandwa de Asera nyenyego dɛ ba zege se ba taa zuli-ya. 24Baara déem ta bwoori mo jei sem konto ne. Konto to Judah tiina bam ke ba lwoni wo-zɔɔna yalo dwi-gɛ tiina na yeini ba ke ye Wɛ zeili-ba tega kam ne o daare o pa Isarele tiina bam jeini to mo.
25Pɛ Rehoboam paare dim bena yanu maŋa ne mo Ejipti Pɛ Sisake déem tu o kwaare jara de Jerusalem teo kom. 26O ma wane o vere jejegero telo maama na wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone to, de telo maama na wo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wone to, ko woli de jara-keim nantane selo Solomon déem na mɛ sabu-seŋa o ke to. 27Pɛ Rehoboam ma kwei channa o ma o jwoori o ke nantane sedwonna o zege da. O ma kwei-se o ke babɛ selo na yere pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo ni dem to jeŋa ne. 28Maŋa kalo maama pɛ wom na wó zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone to, babɛ sem mo jege se ba zeŋe nantane sem ba tɔge o kwaga. Ba daa ná ti, banto ta mo wó zeŋe-se ba jwoori ba tiŋi pɛ sɔŋɔ yerena diga kam ne.
29Rehoboam déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 30Maŋa kam konto maama ne tigura déem mo tigi Pɛ Rehoboam de Pɛ Jeroboam tetare ne. 31Rehoboam ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa bam yibeeli ne David teo Jerusalem ne. O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Abija ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.

english_text:
King Abijam of Judah
(2 Chronicles 13.1-22)
1Abijam became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel, 2and he ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
3Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam. 4-5 David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
6-7 The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king.
Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 8Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king.
King Asa of Judah
(2 Chronicles 15.16—16.6,11-13)
9Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel, 10and he ruled 41 years from Jerusalem. His grandmother was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
11Asa obeyed the Lord, as David had done. 12 He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made. 13His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
14As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines. 15He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
16Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel. 17One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
18When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria: 19“Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
20Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali. 21When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
22Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
23Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease. 24Asa died and was buried in the tomb of his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jehoshaphat then became king.
King Nadab of Israel
25Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years. 26Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
27-28Baasha son of Ahijah was from the tribe of Issachar, and he made plans to kill Nadab. When Nadab and his army went to attack the town of Gibbethon in Philistia, Baasha killed Nadab there. So in the third year of Asa's rule, Baasha became king of Israel.
29 The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family, 30because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
31Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
32King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war.
King Baasha of Israel
33Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled 24 years from Tirzah. 34Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_text:
Judah teo Pɛ Abija taane
1Isarele teo pɛ Jeroboam paare dim bena fuga-nana bene dem wone mo Abija déem di Judah teo paare. 2O déem jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem bena yatɔ mo. O nu yere mo ye Maaka wolo na ye Abisalom bukɔ to.
3Abija déem ke wɛleera yalo maama o kwo Rehoboam na ke to mo. O maa wo sɛ o Tu Baŋa Wɛ de o bochare maama nenɛɛne o nabaaro David déem na sɛ tei to. 4De ko de, David ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ duri o yibwona. O ma pa se Abija lo bakeira se wonto leiri o yuu ne o twoŋi paare dem Jerusalem ne. 5Baŋa Wɛ ke konto bɛŋwaane David kikia déem su o yi lanyerane, de o na sɛ o nia yam o ŋwea maama wone tei to, ko ná dae o na ke o chɔge Hiti tu Yuria seeni to yerane.
6Abija ŋwea maama maŋa ne to, tigura kalo ya na maŋe ka tigi Rehoboam de Jeroboam tetare ne to wo fɔge ka kwori. 7Abija déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 8Abija ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli David teo Jerusalem ne. O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Asa ma leiri o di paare.
Judah teo Pɛ Asa taane
9Isarele teo pɛ Jeroboam paare dim bena finlei bene dem wone mo Asa déem di Judah teo paare. 10O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem bena finna-dedwe (41). O nu nakwe yere déem mo ye Maaka wolo na ye Abisalom bukɔ to.
11Asa totoŋa déem su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane ne o nabaaro David na ke tei to. 12O zeili baara balo na bwoori wara-jei sem ne to. O ta ma daare o chɔge jwona yalo o nabaara bam na mɔɔne ba jege ba zuli to. 13O nu nakwe Maaka ya chwi Asera nyenyego daa pa ba jege ba kaana. Asa ma gwoni-de o de tega ne o daare o kwei-de o zwɛ Kidoron nabara kam ne. O ta ma le Maaka se o daa yé taa jege dam pɛ sɔŋɔ ne. 14Asa déem wo wane o chɔge wara-jei bimbina yalo ba na ke kaanem da to. De ko de, o ŋwea maama wone o yɔɔre o kwei o chega o pa Baŋa Wɛ mo. 15O déem ta ma kwei pɛɛra yalo o de o kwo wom na kwei ba pa Baŋa Wɛ to o ja o vo o tiŋi Wɛ diga kam wone. Pɛɛra yam déem ye lu-nyenno wonnu, de sabu-seŋa wonnu, de zela dwi dwi mo.
16Tigura déem mo wo Judah teo pɛ Asa de Isarele teo pɛ Baasa tetare ne maŋa kalo maama ba na jege ba paara yam ba di to. 17Dɛ dedwe Pɛ Baasa ma nwoŋi o vo o kwaare jara de Judah tiina bam. O ma wane o jwoŋi Rama teo o daare o fɔge o lɔ-ko o che. O ma yere jei sem se nɔɔna yé wane ba lɛɛne ba vo Asa laŋa kam naa ba nwoŋi da ba kɛ.
18Asa déem ma kwei lu-nyenno wonnu de sabu-seŋa wonnu telo ta na wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone to, dedaane jejegero telo na wo o tete sɔŋɔ ne to o ke o tontoŋena jeŋa ne. O ma toŋe-ba se ba ja kwora ba vo Siria pɛ Ben-hadadi tei Damasika ne. Ben-hadadi mo ye Tabirimon bu. O ta maa ye Hezion naa. 19O kwora kam mo tento: “Pa se dé gwoni ni daane, nenɛɛne ko déem na ye tei nmo kwo de amo kwo laŋa ne to. Nii mo, a jege pɛɛra na ye lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa to mo se a pa‑m. Nam sɛ se n yiri ni delo n déem na ke de Isarele teo pɛ Baasa to, se ko pa o viiri o daare a laŋa kam.”
20Ben-hadadi ma sɛ Pɛ Asa na tage tei to. O ma toŋe o jar-keira de ba yiga tiina se ba vo ba kwaare jara de Isarele tiina. Jara yam wone, ba ma wane ba jwoŋi Yijon, de Dan, de Abel Bɛte-Maaka, de Galili jei sem, dedaane Nafitali laŋa kam maama. 21Isarele teo pɛ Baasa na yɔɔre o ni konto to, o ma yage Rama teo lɔɔm o daare o tutwoni o jwoori Tiraza se o taa zoore da. 22O na viiri to, Pɛ Asa ma pa ni yi Judah tiina maama se ba zeŋe kandwa yam, de da-kwollu tem Baasa nɔɔna bam ya na jege ba lɔ teo kom to ba ja ba kɛ. Pɛ Asa déem kwei wonnu tento mo o ma o lɔ Geba na wo Benjamin laŋa kam ne to, de Mizipa.
23Asa déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o bembɛɛne dem, de o totoŋa yam maama, de o na fɔge o lɔ teene delo to maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. O kokweero maŋa ne mo jaweo to o nɛ ne pa se o gwarege. 24Pɛ Asa ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o nabaara yibeeli ne o kwo nakwe David teo wone. O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Jehosafate ma leiri o ji pɛ.
Isarele teo Pɛ Nadab taane
25Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena yalei bene dem ne mo Jeroboam bu Nadab di Isarele teo paare. O ma di paare dem Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne bena yalei. 26Nadab déem ke lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga nenɛɛne o kwo Jeroboam déem na ke tei pa se Isarele tiina bam de tusi to.
27Baasa wolo kwo na ye Ahija ye o nwoŋi Isakara dwi dem wone to déem ma ke chichuŋu de Nadab. Maŋa kalo Nadab de Isarele tiina bam na gilimi Gibefon teo ba pu se ba wane teo kom ba jwoŋi Filisi tiina jeŋa ne to, mo Baasa zaŋe o baŋa ne o go‑o. 28Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena yatɔ maŋa ne mo Baasa déem go Nadab o daare o leiri o yuu ne o di Isarele teo paare dem. 29O na yɔɔre o jeini paare dem baŋa ne to mo o go Jeroboam dwi tiina bam maama nyɔ, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo daare. Konto nam pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ kwora kalo o na pɛ o sampwora Ahija na nwoŋi Siloo to mo ji chega. 30Ko déem ke konto, bɛŋwaane Jeroboam ke wɛleera o daare o pa se Isarele tiina de lwoni ba ke-ya. O ta ma chuchugi ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom bane lanyerane.
31Nadab déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 32Tigura déem mo wo Judah teo pɛ Asa de Isarele teo pɛ Baasa tetare ne maŋa kalo maama ba na di ba paara yam to.
Isarele teo Pɛ Baasa taane
33Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena yatɔ maŋa ne mo Ahija bu Baasa di Isarele teo paare Tiraza ne. O ma di paare dem bena finlei-yana (24). 34O déem ke lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga, ne Pɛ Jeroboam ya na ke tei ye o pa se Isarele tiina de tusi to.

english_text:
1The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
2Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry 3that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam. 4Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
5-7Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family!
Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king.
King Elah of Israel
8Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for 25 years, and he ruled from Tirzah for two years.
9Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah.
One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister, 10when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
11As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed. 12Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned. 13Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
14Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Zimri of Israel
15-16Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah.
Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day. 17At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked. 18When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire. 19Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
20Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Omri of Israel
21After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri. 22Omri's followers were stronger than Tibni's, so Tibni was killed, and Omri became king of Israel 23in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah.
Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah, 24then he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for 6,000 pieces of silver. He built a town there and named it Samaria, after Shemer who had owned the hill.
25Omri did more evil things than any king before him. 26He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
27Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 28Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king.
King Ahab of Israel
29Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled 22 years from Samaria.
30Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him. 31He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal. 32Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria 33and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
34 While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo o chɔge Pɛ Baasa to
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora déem yi o sampwora Jehu wolo kwo na ye Hanani to we o ta taane dento o bere Pɛ Baasa we, 2“N déem na ye nabwom to, mo a liiri‑m bworu wone se n ji amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam yuu tu. Nmo nam jwoori n kwei Jeroboam totoŋ-naga kam mo n jege keim-balwaaro n toŋa, ye n daare n pa se Isarele tiina de ke wɛleera pa se a bane zaŋe. 3Nii mo! A lage a chɔge nmo de n dwi dem maama mo, ne a na ke Nebat bu Jeroboam de o dwi dem tei to. 4Nmo dwi dem nɔɔno wolo maama na wó te teo kolo wone to wó ji kukuri ni-wodiu mo. Wolo maa na wó te pwola ne to wó taa ye duura ni-wodiu.”
5Baasa déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam, de o bembɛɛne dem maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 6Baasa ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli Tiraza teo ne. O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Ela ma leiri o ji pɛ.
7 Baŋa Wɛ déem mo tɔge o sampwora Jehu baŋa ne o pa o kwora kam konto yi Baasa de o dwi tiina bam, Baasa na tiini o toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga pa se o totoŋa yam chuchugi Wɛ bane dedɛ to ŋwaane. O daa wo daare Jeroboam totoŋ-naga kam. O ta ma kwori o chɔge Jeroboam dwi dem maama nyɔ.
Isarele teo Pɛ Ela taane
8Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena finlei-yaredo (26) bene dem wone mo Baasa bu Ela di Isarele teo paare Tiraza ne. O ma di paare dem bena yalei. 9Pɛ Ela déem jege o tontoŋeno wolo yere na ye Zimiri ye o nii pɛ sɔŋɔ torokooro tem chichworo baŋa ne to. O ma ke chichuŋu de pɛ wom. Dɛ dedwe mo Ela wo Areza sɔŋɔ ne. Wonto déem nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom Tiraza ne mo. Ela ma nyɔ sana o wora o buga. 10Zimiri ma zo sɔŋɔ kom o mage Ela o de tega ne o go. Keim dento kea Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena finlei-yarepɛ (27) bene dem wone mo. Zimiri ma daare o leiri o ji Isarele teo pɛ.
11O na yɔɔre o jeini paare dem baŋa ne to mo o go Baasa dwi tiina bam maama nyɔ, ye o chorro de o yuudwonna maama bakeira de dedoa de wo daare. 12Zimiri déem na chɔge Baasa dwi dem maama to pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ kwora kalo o na tɔge o sampwora Jehu baŋa ne o pa Baasa to ji chega. 13Keim dento maama zege Baasa de o bu Ela na ke wɛleera ye ba pa se Isarele tiina bam de ke wɛleera yalo to baŋa ne mo. Ba déem chuchugi Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to bane de ba na zuli jwona tei to mo.
14Ela déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone.
Isarele teo Pɛ Zimiri taane
15Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena finlei-yarepɛ (27) bene dem wone mo Zimiri di Isarele teo paare Tiraza ne da yarepɛ yerane. Kanto maŋa kam ne Isarele jar-keira bam ya tigisi daane mo ba gilimi Filisi teo Gibefon. 16Omiri déem mo ye jar-keira bam yiga tu. Ba ma ni we Zimiri zaŋe ba pɛ wom baŋa ne o go‑o. Ba ma lɛɛre ba zege ba jara keim jei sem ne ba kuri Omiri se o leiri o ji Isarele teo pɛ dɛ dem konto ne. 17Omiri ma zege Gibefon teo ne o ja Isarele jar-keira bam maama o vo Tiraza pa se ba gilimi teo kom ba pu. 18Zimiri na nɛ we ba tu ba cheiŋi teo kom to, o ma zo pɛ sɔŋɔ dam jei sem wone, ye o daare o de mini diga kam wone. Mini dem ma zwɛ‑o de go. 19Lɛɛro tento yi Zimiri o na ke lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga ye o wo yage Pɛ Jeroboam totoŋ-naga kam to ŋwaane mo. O déem yɔɔre o ke wɛleera o daare o pa se Isarele tiina de lwoni ba ke-ya mo.
20Zimiri déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o na zaŋe Ela baŋa ne tei to maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone.
Isarele teo Pɛ Omiri taane
21Kanto maŋa kam ne kampɔra déem mo zo Isarele tiina bam wone. Ba chichworo mo zege Ginafi bu Tibini kwaga ne se ba tiŋi‑o pɛ. Badaara bam maa zege Omiri kwaga ne. 22Omiri kwaga nɔɔna bam déem dana ba dwoi Tibini kwaga nɔɔna bam. Konto ŋwaane Tibini ma te ye Omiri jeini Isarele paare dem baŋa ne.
23Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena fintɔ-dedwe (31) bene dem wone mo Omiri di Isarele teo paare. O ma kwei bena fuga-yalei (12) o di paare dem. O dɛ yiga o ke bena yaredo mo Tiraza ne. 24Pɛ Omiri déem kwei lu-nyenno dunni na yi kilo fuserepɛ (70) to mo o ma o yeigi tega kalo ba na bwoi we Samaria zwoŋo to. O ma yeigi-ka nɔɔno wodwoŋi tei ne, o yere mo Semera. O ma daare o lɔ sɔ-fwaaro zwoŋo kom yuu ne, ye o bwoŋi teo kom yere we Samaria, Semera yere zula ŋwaane.
25Pɛ Omiri déem tiini o toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga se ko dwoni balo na dɛ yiga ba jeini paare dem wone to. 26O yɔɔre o kwei Nebat bu Jeroboam totoŋ-naga kam maama mo. O ma yɔɔre o ke wɛleera ye o pa se Isarele tiina bam de lwoni ba ke-ya. Ba déem chuchugi Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to bane de ba na zuli jwona tei to. 27Omiri déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o bembɛɛne dem maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 28Pɛ Omiri ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli Samaria teo ne. O bu Ahab ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.
Isarele teo Pɛ Ahab taane
29Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena fintɔ-nana (38) bene dem wone mo Omiri bu Ahab di Isarele teo paare. O ma jeini Samaria ne o di paare bena finlei-yalei (22). 30Omiri bu Ahab déem tiini o toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga se ko dwoni balo maama na dɛ yiga ba jeini paare dem wone to. 31O déem paale o kwei Nebat bu Jeroboam totoŋ-naga kam mo. Kolo maa na dwoi to mo ye o kwei Sidon pɛ Efebaal bukɔ Jezebele mo o ma o ji o kaane. O déem tɔge o zuli Baal jwoni dem mo. 32O lɔge diga mo Samaria ne Baal zula ŋwaane o daare o zege kaanem bimbini ka wone. 33Ahab ta ma chwi Asera nyenyego daa. O ma tiini o chuchugi Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to bane se ko dwoni pwa balo na dɛ yiga ba ba to.
34Pɛ Ahab paare dim maŋa ne to mo Hiyeli na nwoŋi Bɛtel to fɔge o lɔ Jeriko teo. O na bobo o chwi teo kom biri-beira to mo o bu-kwea Abiram tega. O maa na kwaare ko manchwoŋo ni bworru tem to mo o bu Segubi de tega. Ko na ke tei konto to pɛ se Wɛ kwora kalo Nun bu Josua na tage faŋa faŋa to ji chega.

english_text:
Elijah Stops the Rain
1 Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
2Later, the Lord said to Elijah, 3“Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek. 4You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
5Elijah obeyed the Lord and went to live near Cherith Creek. 6Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek. 7But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain.
Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
8The Lord told Elijah, 9 “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
10When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked. 11As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
12The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
13Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me. 14The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
15The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time. 16The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil.
Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
17Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
18The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
19“Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed 20and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.” 21 Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
22The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again. 23Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
24“You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na ke tei o pa Elija o ni-wodiu to
1Wɛ sampwora kadwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Elija. O déem nwoŋi Gilead teo Tisibi mo. Dɛ dedwe o ma vo o ta de Pɛ Ahab o we, “Amo toŋe a pa Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to mo. Wonto na ye Ŋwea Tu chekke to, a ná wo jwoori a ta taane, nyɔnɔ daa bá to, doa de nam daa bá ne tega kanto baŋa ne, se ko taa nii bena yalei naa yatɔ wɛɛne.”
2 Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi Elija we, 3“Zaŋe n yɔɔre wɛ-puli seeni n vo n seigi n tete Kerifi nabara kam na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to ni ne. 4Nabara kam konto na mo n jege se n ta‑n nyɔa. A nam pɛ bachangaaro ni se te taa tui te pa‑m wodiu dáane.”
5Elija ma ke kolo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑o ni se o ke to. O ma seene o vo Kerifi nabara kam na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to o maŋe da o zoora. 6Bachangaaro tem ma jaane bworobworo de nɔna te tui te pa‑o tetete de dedaan-ni maama. O ma nyɔ nabara kam na bam.
Elija de kadeim wodwoŋi taane
7Ko na wora ko wora to, nabara kam ma we, doa daa na ba nena tega kam maama ne to ŋwaane. 8Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Elija o we, 9“Zaŋe lela n vo Zarefate na wo Sidon teo kom seeni to n ta‑n zoore da. A nam maŋe a ta de kadeim wodwoŋi se o pa‑m n ni-wodiu.”
10Elija ma zaŋe o vo Zarefate. O na yi teo kom manchwoŋo ni dem to mo o nɛ kadeim na wora o beeri o da-dwa. O ma bwoŋi kadeim wom o lwoori‑o o we, “Jan ja! Mɔ na n pa-ne se a nyɔ.” 11Kadeim wom na maa vei se o ja na bam o ba o pa‑o to mo Elija daa we, “Jan ja! Kwei bworobworo fee n woli da n ja n ba.” 12Kadeim wom ma leiri o we, “Nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ na ye Ŋwea Tu chekke to, a dugi o yere ŋwaane we, a ba jege bworobworo. Muni fee yerane mo a jega mun-duru wone, a daare a jege nuga de fee kabɔɔ wone. A zege a puuri da-dwa balei se a jwoori sɔŋɔ a ma a saŋe wodiu mo, se a de a bu wom di dé kweeli se dé laam te.”
13Elija ma ta de kadeim wom o we, “Yé ta‑n kɔre foone. Véi sɔŋɔ n ke n na taga tei to. Da yiga n kwei muni delo n na jege to fee n ma n fɔge maase n pa-ne. Se n kwei kolo na daare to n ma n ke wodiu se n de n bu wom di. 14Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: ‘Mun-duru kom bá fɔge ko kwɛ muni. Kabɔɔ kom de maa bá kwɛ nuga se ko taa nii maŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó pa se doa jwoori ka ne tega kam baŋa ne to.’ ”
15Kadeim wom ma seene o jwoori sɔŋɔ o ke kolo maama Elija na taga to. Ko ma seene ko ke we, Elija tete, de kadeim wom, de o bu wom wolowolo wo gɛ wodiu se ba di da dedɛ wone. 16Ba déem ná maŋe ba kwoori nuga kam de muni dem tei maama, ko ba tia, ne Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge Elija baŋa o ta we ko wó ke tei to.
17Konto kwaga ne mo kadeim wom bu-baaro wom weele. Jaweo kom ma tiini ko zo‑o ye o momwɛ ti. 18Kadeim wom ma ta de Elija o we, “Wɛ tontoŋeno, bɛ mo ye n ke amo tento? N tu amo tei se n pa a wɛleera lɔre ja, se n daare n pa a bu wom te mo na?” 19Elija ma leiri‑o o we, “Ja n bu wom n ba n pa-ne.” O ma jwoŋi bu wom kaane wom jeŋa ne o ja‑o o di nayuu diga kalo o na zoore da to. O ma tiŋi bu wom o kadwogo baŋa ne. 20O ma keeri o jare Baŋa Wɛ de kwor-dɛa o we, “A Tu Baŋa Wɛ, bɛ mo ye n pa se lɛɛro tento yi kadeim wom pa se o bu wom te, ye wonto mo jwoŋi-ne o sɔŋɔ ne?” 21O ma twe o tete bu wom baŋa ne kuni betɔ o keeri o jare Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nam pa se bakeira kam jwoori ka na ŋwea.” 22Baŋa Wɛ ma sɛ Elija lworo kom ye bu wom jwoori o na ŋwea. 23O na wori to, Elija ma kwei‑o o tu konkɔlɔ kom ne o pa o nu. O maa we, “Nii, n bu wom jwoori o ŋwe.” 24Kadeim wom ma ta de Elija o we, “Leile konto a laam tu a lɔre chekke we n ye Wɛ tontoŋeno. N ma‑n na tage kolo to seene ko ye Baŋa Wɛ kwora chekke mo.”

english_text:
Elijah Proves He Is the Lord's Prophet
1-2For three years no rain fell in Samaria, and there was almost nothing to eat anywhere. The Lord said to Elijah, “Go and meet with King Ahab. I will soon make it rain.” So Elijah went to see Ahab.
3-4At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid 100 of them in two caves and gave them food and water.
Ahab sent for Obadiah 5and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass. 6You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
7As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
8“Yes. Go tell Ahab I'm here.”
9Obadiah replied:
King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong. 10I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country. 11Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
12What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me.
I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy. 13I even hid 100 of the Lord's prophets in caves when Jezebel was trying to kill them. I also gave them food and water. 14Do you really want me to tell Ahab you're here? He will kill me!
15Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
16Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah.
Ahab went to meet Elijah, 17and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
18Elijah answered:
You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
19Call together everyone from Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. Be sure to bring along the 450 prophets of Baal and the 400 prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table.
20Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel. 21Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!”
The people did not say a word.
22Then Elijah continued:
I am the Lord's only prophet, but Baal has 450 prophets.
23Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
24The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God.
“That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
25Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
26They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
27At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
28The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped, 29and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
30Elijah told everyone to gather around him while he repaired the Lord's altar. 31-32 Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about 14 liters. 33He placed the wood on the altar, then they cut the bull into pieces and laid the meat on the wood.
He told the people, “Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the meat and the wood.” After they did this, 34he told them to do it two more times. They did exactly as he said 35until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
36When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed:
Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command. 37Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
38The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch. 39When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
40Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.”
So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them.
It Starts To Rain
41Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
42 Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground 43and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.”
The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
44After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.”
Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
45-46A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.
translation_text:
Elija de Ahab taane
1Da-kore sem déem zege ko yi bena yatɔ mo. Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Elija o we, “Zaŋe n vo Pɛ Ahab tei se o na‑m, se a lage a pa doa jwoori ka ne tega kam ne mo.” 2Elija ma seene o vo se o jeeri Ahab.
Kana déem tiini ka chana Samaria teo ne. 3Pɛ Ahab ma bwoŋi o tontoŋeno Obadia. Wonto déem mo nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne. O maa yɔɔre o kɔre Baŋa Wɛ lanyerane. 4Jezebele déem na wora o goe Baŋa Wɛ sampwori sem to mo Obadia kwei sampwori sem bi o seigi peo bɔɔna yalei wone. O seigi-ba bɔɔna yalei wone, nɔɔna finnu bɔɔne maama wone. O maa jaane wodiu de na o vei o pa-ba. 5Pɛ Ahab tage de Obadia o we, “Véi n beeri buli-yia yam de nabare sem ni maama dé tega kam baŋa ne se dé nii, dé wó na ga-zuru dé pa sisei sem de bona-sisei sem se se di na. Konto wó woli se dé yé go-se.” 6Ba ma pɔɔre tega kam ba pa daane se ba beeri ga-zuru jei. Ahab ma kwei tega kam daa dedoa, ye Obadia de kwei daa kadwoŋi kam, ye ba to beira ne.
7Obadia na wo veiŋa ne konto to mo o jeeri Elija chwoŋa ne. O na lɔre we ko ye Elija to, o ma tiiri o zuli‑o ye o we, “Amo tu Elija, ko ye nmo mo konto na?” 8Elija ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ! Ko ye amo mo. Nam véi n ta n bere n yuu tu wom we Elija mo wo ywo-seeni.”
9Obadia ma bwei‑o o we, “A tu, a ke bɛ tete mo a chɔge n yiga pa se n boŋe se a ke keim delo na wó pa Ahab ti a ŋwea to? 10N Tu Baŋa Wɛ na ye Ŋwea Tu chekke to, ko yɔɔre ko ye chega mo we, teo de ko teo tera ye pɛ wom wo toŋe nɔɔna da se ba beeri nmo jeiga. Teo kolo nɔɔna ná we, n tere ba tei ne, Ahab yeini o pa se ba du duuri mo we ba wo nɛ‑m. 11De konto maama, n laam nam boŋe se a vo a ta a bere a tu Ahab mo we, Elija wo ywo-seeni na? 12A ná yage‑m ye a viiri leile konto, a yeiri Baŋa Wɛ Jworo daa na wó kwei‑m o ja o vo mɛ. A nam ná vei a ta a bere Ahab ye o wo nɛ‑m, o laam wó go-ne mo. Ko nam na maŋe ko zege amo biini ne to mo a kɔre Baŋa Wɛ. 13A tu, nmo wo nigi a déem na ke tei maŋa kalo Jezebele na wora o goe Baŋa Wɛ sampwori sem to na? Amo déem mo kwei Wɛ sampwori sem nɔɔna bi a pɔɔre-ba finnu finnu a seigi peo bɔɔna yalei wone. A ma daare a jaane wodiu a vei a pa-ba. 14Bɛŋwaane mo n laga se a vo a ta de a tu wom we, Elija wo ywo-seeni? Nmo yɔɔre n lage a momwɛ-tiu mo!”
15Elija ma leiri o we, “Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ye Ŋwea Tu mo chekke, ye a toŋe a pa‑o. A nam dugi wonto yere ŋwaane we, a zem wó ja a tete a vo a bere Ahab.”
16Obadia ma seene o jwoori Pɛ Ahab tei o ta o bere‑o we Elija wora. Pɛ wom ma vo o jeeri Elija. 17O na nɛ Elija to mo o we, “Nmo wolo na pae Isarele teo kom na ko lɛɛro to mo konto na?” 18Elija ma leiri o we, “Ko dae amo mo pɛ se lɛɛro yi Isarele tiina bam. Ko nam ye nmo de n kwo dwi dem mo ke konto, abam na ve Baŋa Wɛ nia yam ye á daare á zuli Baal jwona yam to ŋwaane. 19Nam ta n bere Isarele tiina bam maama se ba ba ba jeeri-ne Kamele peo kom yuu ne. Ko ta ná ye Baal sampwori bia yana de finnu (450) bam, de Asera sampwori bia yana (400) bam, balo Jezebele na yeini o pa-ba ba ni-wodiu to, bwoŋi-ba se ba de da ba jeeri.”
Elija na ke tei Kamele peo kom yuu ne to
20Pɛ Ahab ma pa ni yi Isarele tiina bam maama pa se ba de sampwori sem maama jeeri Kamele peo kom yuu ne. 21Elija ma fɔɔre o zege ba kɔgɔ kom yiga ne o ta o we, “Á ta wó ta‑á jege boboŋa yalei taa se á vo á maŋe yei ne mo? Nam kuri-na á na wó ke tei. Baŋa Wɛ mo ná seene o ye Wɛ, ta‑á zuli-na wonto. Á nam daa ná we Baal mo ye wɛ chekke, se á ta‑á zuli wonto.” Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maa wo leiri kolokolo.
22Elija ta ma ta o we, “Amo yerane mo daare a na ye Baŋa Wɛ sampwora. Ko nam ná ye Baal, wonto jege sampwori bia yana de finnu (450) mo. 23Ja-na nabɛ selei á ba á pa debam. Baal sampwori sem wó kuri nabɛ sem dedoa se ba ma ba ke kaanem. Ba laam wó go-ka ba cha ka nɔna yam yera yera ba kwei ba daŋe dɛ sem baŋa ne. Ba nam ba jege se ba de mini da. Amo de maa wó cha nabea kadwoŋi kam a daŋe dɛ sem baŋa ne, ye a bá de mini da. 24Abam laam wó bwoŋi á wɛ dem yere, se amo de bwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ wom yere. Wɛ delo na wó leiri ye o de mini kaanem dem ne to mo wó seene o taa ye Wɛ chekke.”
Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama ma sɛ ye ba we, “N na tage kolo to jege kuri.” 25Elija daa ta ma ta de Baal sampwori sem o we, “Abam kɔgɔ kom na daga to, da-na yiga á kuri nabea dedoa á go se á ti ka nɔna yiga. Á ná ti, se á laam lwoori á wɛ dem se de de mini da, ye ko dae abam mo wó de mini da.” 26Ba ma ja nabea kalo ba na pɛ-ba to ba go ba ti ka nɔna yiga. Ba ma bwoŋi Baal yere dem taa, ko zege tetete se ko yi we-bere maŋa. Ba ma sa ba kaare bimbini delo ba na lɔge to ye ba bage de kwor-dɛa ba we, “Baal, zaŋe n cheigi dé lworo kom!” Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa wo leiri-ba de fenfee de. Ko maa ye yirititi.
27We-bere maŋa ne Elija ma zaŋe o jege Baal sampwori sem o mɔna ye o we, “Tiini á bage de kwor-dɛa, se Baal ye wɛ mo! O ga wo boboŋa wone mo, naa o nwoŋi mo, naa o vei chwoŋa mo. Dɛ delo o tigi o dɔa mo, ye ko maŋe se á pa o zaŋe.” 28Baal sampwori sem ma tiini ba keeri wɛ-wɛ, ye ba daare ba ma ba fane de se-zɔɔro ba gwoni ba yera pa se ba jana lwo ba ke ba yera ne, ne ba chullu tem na bere se ba ke tei to. 29Ba zege wea ne ba bore Baal yiga ne konto mo taa se ko taa nii dedaan-ni kaanem dem maŋa. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa wo leiri kolokolo ye ko ye yirititi.
30Elija déem ma ta de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama o we, “Fɔɔre-na á ba amo tei ywo-seeni.” Ba ma zaŋe ba yi o tei. O ma fɔge o kwɛ Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem ya na chɔge to. 31O ma daare o kwei kandwa-pelɛ fuga-yalei se ya taa zege ya pae Jakob dwia fuga-yalei yam. Ko ye wonto mo Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ o yere leiri de ji Isarele to. 32O ma kwei kandwa yam konto o ma o lɔ bimbini Baŋa Wɛ yere zula ŋwaane. O ta ma daare o ko gwoŋo o kaare bimbini dem. Kuriwa-zwanno telei wo-dwa mo wó wane ba zo gwoŋo kom. 33O na ke konto o ti to, o ma tigisi dɛ sem bimbini dem baŋa ne o daare o cha nabea kam nɔna yam muga-muga o daŋe dɛ sem baŋa. O ma ta o we, “Véi-na á mɔ na á su kɔɔra bana á ja á ba á lwo zwɛɛm kaanem dem de dɛ sem baŋa ne.”
34Ba na ke konto ba ti to, Elija ta ma ta o we, “Jwoori-na á mɔ á lwo-da.” Ba ma seene ba ke konto. O ta ma ta-ba o we, “Jwoori á mɔ á lwo-da á ke betɔ.” Ba ma seene ba lwo ba ke kuni betɔ. 35Na bam tagele bimbini dem maama mo ba tu ba su gwoŋo kom de.
36Ko na yi dedaan-ni kaanem maŋa to, Wɛ sampwora Elija ma fɔɔre o yi bimbini dem o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo ye dé nabaaro Abaraham Wɛ, de Izaak Wɛ, dedaane Isarele Wɛ. Nam toŋe zem se ko bere jaja we nmo mo ye Isarele teo kom maama Wɛ wom, se n daare n pa se nɔɔna bam lɔre we a ye n tontoŋeno mo ye n pa-ne ni se a ke tento maama. 37Baŋa Wɛ, leiri a wɛ-lworo kom! Yɔɔre n leiri-ne se nɔɔna banto lɔre we nmo Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo ye Wɛ chekke, ye n daare n pa se ba boboŋa jwoori se ba tɔge nmo.”
38Elija na ŋɔɔne o ti to mo Baŋa Wɛ toŋe mini pa se de zege wɛyuu ne de ba de zwɛ kaanem dem nɔna yam, de dɛ sem, de kandwa yam, de teero tem maama. Mini dem ta ma deilimi na bam maama wegesege. 39Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom na nɛ kolo na ke to, ba maama ma vwi ba yibia tega ne ye ba laare ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ seene o ye Wɛ mo! Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo ye Wɛ!”
40Elija ma pa ni o we, “Ja-na Baal sampwori sem maama! Yé pa-na se ba dedoa lu.” Ba ma seene ba ja ba maama. Elija ma pa se ba ja-ba ba tu Kison nabara kam ni ne ba gwoni ba maama ba go.
Doa jwoori ka ne
41Elija déem ma ta de Pɛ Ahab o we, “Nam véi sɔŋɔ n lage wodiu n di, se a nigi do-fɔrɔ na mumuna se ka ne.” 42Ahab ma seene o kwei chwoŋa se o jwoori sɔŋɔ o lage wodiu o di. Elija ma vo o di Kamele peo kom yuu o tiiri tega ne pa se o yuu maŋe de o nadwoona. 43O ma ta de o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Véi n zege n leesi n nii naneo kom seeni.” Tontoŋeno wom ma seene o vo o jwoori o ba o we, “A wo nɛ kolokolo.” Kuni berepɛ maama mo Elija toŋe tontoŋeno wom pa o vei o nia ye o jwoora.
44Tontoŋeno wom na vei o ke kuni berepɛ kom to, o ma ta o we, “Amo nɛ kunkwoŋ-balaŋa na mae de nɔɔno jataale to mo zege naneo kom baŋa ne ko beene.” Elija ma ta ded‑o o we, “Véi Pɛ Ahab tei n ta n bere‑o we, o ke lela o di o toroko kom o duri o vo sɔŋɔ, se doa kam lage ka li‑o mo.”
45Ko wo dáane mo kunkwoŋo kom tene ligi-ligi pa se do-vio de zaŋe. Doa ma bobo se ka tiini ka ne chaa-chaa. Ahab ma ke lela o kwei chwoŋa o maa kɛ Jezerele. 46Baŋa Wɛ dam dem ma ba Elija baŋa. O ma fɔge o vɔ o gare-kura kiri-kiri, ye o duri o lwoori Ahab yiga taa o vo o yi Jezerele.

english_text:
Elijah Runs Away from Ahab and Jezebel
1Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets. 2She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
3Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there, 4 then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.” 5Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep.
Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.” 6Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
7Soon the Lord's angel woke him again and said, “Get up and eat, or else you'll get too tired to travel.” 8So Elijah sat up and ate and drank.
The food and water made him strong enough to walk 40 more days. At last, he reached Mount Sinai, the mountain of God, 9and he spent the night there in a cave.
The Lord Appears to Elijah
While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
10 He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
11“Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.”
All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake. 12Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire.
Finally, there was a gentle breeze, 13and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave.
A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
14Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
15 The Lord said:
Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria. 16 Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
17Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
18 But 7,000 Israelites have refused to worship Baal, and they will live.
Elisha Becomes Elijah's Assistant
19Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
20Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said.
“You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
21Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_text:
Elija duri o vo Sinayi peo
1Pɛ Ahab déem ma ta Elija kikia yam de o na mɛ o se-zɔɔ o go Baal sampwori sem tei to maama o bere o kaane Jezebele. 2Jezebele ma toŋe kwora se ka yi Elija we, “A dugi we, jwa kanto maŋa ná yia ye a wo go nmo ne n na go Baal sampwori sem tei to, se wa yam go amo de.”
3Elija na nigi konto to, foone ma zo‑o. O ma duri se o jwoŋi o tete Jezebele jeŋa ne. O ma vo o yi Beeriseba teo na wo Judah ne to o yage o tontoŋeno wom dáane. 4Elija tete ma zaŋe o kwei dɛ dem maama o kɛ o zo kagoa kam wone. O ma yi o jeini vɔkɔŋɔ kuri ne ye o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o yage se o te. O maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ, a na nɛ cham delo to, ko daga. Nam ti a ŋwea se a ba gare balo na tege to.” 5Elija ma lɛɛre o maŋe vɔkɔŋɔ kom kuri ne o peini o dɔ. O na tigi o dɔ konto to mo Wɛ maleka pɔpɔ ka ba ka dwei‑o ye ka we, “Zaŋe wɛɛne se n di wodiu.” 6O ma nii o na bworobworo kolo ba na wɔge to na zege o yuu seeni. Kunkwolo de ko wo na de maa zege da. O ma di ye o daare o nyɔ na bam. O laam ma jwoori o guni o peini.
7 Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ma jwoori o tei ne ka dwei‑o, ye ka we, “Zaŋe wɛɛne n di wodiu n woli da, se n chwoŋa ta dɔra.” 8Elija ma seene o zaŋe o di wodiu o daare o nyɔ na. O na di o na dam-doore konto to, mo o kwei da finna, tete de wea maama, o vo o yi Sinayi peo kom na ye Baŋa Wɛ tete jeiga to.
Baŋa Wɛ na veere o tete de Elija tei to
9Elija ma vo o zo peo bɔɔne wone o peini o poore tega. Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma pɔpɔ ka ba o tei we, “Elija, bɛŋwaane mo n tu ywo-seeni?” 10Elija ma leiri o we, “Amo tiini a seene a yia se a taa toŋa a pae nmo Baŋa Wɛ na ye Paŋwa to mo. Isarele tiina bam nam ve n na gwoni ni delo de-ba to, ba daare ba chochoge n kaanem bimbina yam. Ba ta mɛ ba se-zɔɔro ba go n sampwori sem, ye amo yerane mo daare. Ba nam boŋe se ba go amo de ba woli da mo.” 11Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nwoŋi n vo n di peo kom yuu se n zege a yiga ne, se amo Baŋa Wɛ lage a ba a tɔge dáane mo a kɛ.”
Vo-dɛɔ ma pɔpɔ ko zaŋe Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne ko lɔ peo kom belei ko daare ko mumugi kandwa yam. Ko na ke konto to, Baŋa Wɛ tera vio kom wone. Konto kwaga ne tega kam de ma tiini ka ziziŋi, ye Baŋa Wɛ tɔge o tera. 12Tega kam ziziŋim dem kwaga ne min-vogo de ma ba ko kɛ, ye Baŋa Wɛ tera mini dem wone. Konto kwaga ne mo kwor-memena zaŋa ne waasa tei to. 13Elija na nigi to, o ma ja o gɔrɔ o kwoli o yibia ye o daare o vo o maŋe bɔɔne dem ni ne o zega. O ma ni kwora na ŋɔɔne ded‑o ka we, “Elija, bɛŋwaane mo n tu ywo-seeni?” 14Elija ma leiri o we, “Amo tiini a seene a yia se a taa toŋa a pae nmo Baŋa Wɛ na ye Paŋwa to mo. Isarele tiina bam nam ve n na gwoni ni delo de-ba to, ba daare ba chochoge n kaanem bimbina yam. Ba ta mɛ ba se-zɔɔro ba go n sampwori sem, ye amo yerane mo daare. Ba nam boŋe se ba go amo de ba woli da mo.”
15 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, “N na tɔge chwoŋa kalo n ba ywo-seeni to, jwoori n da konto n vo Damasika kagoa kam. N ná vei n yi da, se n lwo nuga Hazayeli yuu ne n ma‑n tiŋi‑o Siria teo pɛ. 16Nam ta ke konto dwoŋi n tiŋi Nimisi bu Jehu se o taa ye Isarele teo pɛ, se n daare n tiŋi Elisa wolo na ye Abel-Mehola tu Safate bu to se o leiri n yuu ne o ji a sampwora. 17Jehu wó go balo maama na duri ba lu Hazayeli jeŋa ne to. Elisa de maa wó go balo maama na duri ba lu Jehu jeŋa ne to. 18A nam tiŋi nɔɔna morro terepɛ (7,000) mo Isarele laŋa kam ne. Banto wo fɔge ba kuni dwoona ba zuli Baal jwoni dem. Ba nam wo mɛ ba ni-vɔɔro ba duuri-de.”
Elisa na saŋe Elija kwaga tei to
19Elija ma yage jei sem konto o vo o beeri Safate bu Elisa jei. O ma na‑o ye o jege nabɛ selei selei kuni fuga-belei o vara. Elisa tete mo kale nabɛ selei sem na wo kwaga ne to o jege o vara. Elija ma fɔɔre o yi o tei ye o le o gare-daŋɔ kom o daŋe Elisa bakale ne. 20Elisa ma yage nabɛ sem ye o daare o duri o tɔge Elija kwaga. O maa we, “Yage se a vo a bane a kwo de a nu, se a laam ba a taa tɔge‑m.” Elija ma leiri o we, “Tɔ. Jwoori sɔŋɔ. Nam yé swei a na ke tei n yera ne to.”
21Elisa ma pipiri o viiri o daare Elija. O ma vo o ja o nabɛ selei sem o go o ma ke kaanem. O ma kwei se yera zela yam o ma o dwei mini o saŋe nɔna yam. O laam ma pɔɔre-ya o pa o nɔɔna bam ye ba di. O na bane-ba to mo o lɛɛre o vo o tɔge Elija kwaga o woli‑o totoŋa baŋa ne.

english_text:
Syria Attacks Israel
1King Benhadad of Syria called his army together. He was joined by 32 other kings with their horses and chariots, and together they marched to Samaria and attacked. 2Benhadad sent a messenger to tell King Ahab of Israel, 3“Ahab, give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your strongest sons!”
4“Your Majesty,” Ahab replied, “everything I have is yours, including me.”
5Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children. 6But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
7Ahab called a meeting with the leaders of Israel and said, “Benhadad is causing real trouble. He told me to give him my wives and children, as well as my silver and gold. And I agreed.”
8“Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
9So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.”
When Benhadad got his answer, 10he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
11Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
12Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
13At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
14“Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked.
The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.”
“But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked.
“You will!” the prophet replied.
15So Ahab called together the 232 young soldiers and the 7,000 troops in Israel's army, and he got them ready to fight the Syrians.
Israel Defeats the Syrians
16-17At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front.
King Benhadad of Syria and the 32 kings with him were drunk when the scouts he had sent out ran up to his tent, shouting, “We just now saw soldiers marching out of Samaria!”
18“Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
19The young soldiers led Israel's troops into battle, 20and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses, 21but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots.
Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
22Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.”
Syria Attacks Israel Again
23Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained:
Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
24Here's what you should do. First, get rid of those 32 kings and put army commanders in their places. 25Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out.
Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
26In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel. 27The Israelites also prepared to fight. They marched out to meet the Syrians, and the two armies camped across from each other. The Syrians covered the whole area, but the Israelites looked like two little flocks of goats.
28The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
29For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed 100,000 Syrian troops. 30The rest of the Syrian army ran back to Aphek, but the town wall fell and crushed 27,000 of them.
Benhadad also escaped to Aphek and hid in the back room of a house. 31His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
32They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.”
“Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
33Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.”
“Go get him,” Ahab said.
When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
34Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.”
Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go.
A Prophet Condemns Ahab
35About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused, 36 and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
37The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
38The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
39When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay 3,000 pieces of silver. 40But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.”
Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
41The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets. 42The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
43Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_text:
Ben-hadadi ke jara de Samaria tiina
1Siria teo pɛ Ben-hadadi déem bwoŋi o jar-keira bam mo o ke daane. Pwa fintɔ-balei de ba sisein-nɔɔna de ba torokooro ma tɔge ded‑o ba vo Samaria teo se ba kwaare jara de ko nɔn-bia bam. 2Ben-hadadi ma toŋe o tontoŋena se ba vo ba zo teo kom ba ta ba bere Isarele tiina pɛ Ahab we, “Ben-hadadi kwora mo tento: 3‘Ahab, amo mo laam tei n lu-nyenno tem de n sabu-seŋa kam, ko woli de n ka-yorro tem de n bu-swonnu tem maama.’ ” 4Pɛ Ahab ma leiri o we, “A tu, n tage chega. Amo tete de kolo maama a na seene a jege to ye nmo nyem mo.”
5Ben-hadadi daa ma toŋe o tontoŋena bam ye ba jwoori ba ba ba ta de Ahab ba we, “Ben-hadadi we, ‘A ya pɛ kwora yi‑m we, n jege se n kwei n lu-nyenno tem, de n sabu-seŋa kam, de n kaana bam, de n bia bam mo n ja n ba n pa-ne. 6Nam ta‑n yei we, jwa kanto maŋa ne a wó toŋe a dedɛɛra se ba ba ba buŋi nmo sɔŋɔ kom de n dedɛɛra bam de di sem maama. Ba laam wó kwei woŋo kolo maama na jege lonne ko pa‑m to ba ja ba ba ba pa-ne.’ ”
7Ahab ma bwoŋi Isarele nakwa bam maama o ke daane ye o ta de-ba o we, “Á wo nɛ na? Ben-hadadi laam lage cham mo o pae debam! O ya na taga o we o lage o jwoŋi a kaana bam, de a bia bam, de a lu-nyenno tem, de a sabu-seŋa kam to, a yɔɔre a sɛ mo.” 8Nakwa bam de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama ma leiri‑o ba we, “Yé cheigi Ben-hadadi taane. Nam yé sɛ n ke kolo o na taga to.”
9Ahab laam ma leiri Ben-hadadi tontoŋena bam o we, “Véi-na á kwei a kwora kanto á pa á pɛ wom we, ‘Amo tu, ko ná ye n na dɛ yiga n ta we n lage n jwoŋi wonnu telo a tei ne to, a sɛ. Se ko ná ye wonnu telo n ta na lage se n vere n woli da to, a bá sɛ konto kɔtaa.’ ” Ba ma seene ba ja kwora kam ba vo ba pa Ben-hadadi.
10Ben-hadadi daa ma toŋe kwora o pa Ahab ye o we, “A dugi we, a ná wo pɛ se a jar-keira bam chɔge Samaria teo zɔŋ-zɔŋ, se wa yam laam yɔɔre ya chɔge-ne ya woli da. Á teo kom fwogo daa bá daare se a kwaga nɔɔna bam dedoa dedoa wane ba pɛ jaguli-yi.” 11Isarele teo pɛ Ahab ma toŋe kwora o leiri o we, “Ta-na á bere Ben-hadadi we, ‘Nɔɔno ba gare o zeiŋi o vɔna o tɛ we o wane, ye jara ta wo bobo. Cheigi se n nii, n wó lu jara yam wone na.’ ” 12Kwora kam na yi Ben-hadadi maŋa kalo to, o de pwa badwonna bam déem jei ba nyɔ sana ba vwoa yam wone mo. O ma ta de o jar-keira bam o we, “Nwoŋi-na á ti á yiga se á vo á ke jara de Samaria tiina bam.” Ba ma seene ba ke konto.
Baŋa Wɛ jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam
13Sento nɛ sem ni ne mo Wɛ sampwora kadwoŋi vei o ta de Isarele teo pɛ Ahab o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: N nɛ Ben-hadadi jar-keira bam kɔgɔ na daga tei to na? Amo zem lage a pa se n di-ba mo. Konto wó pa se n lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.” 14Ahab ma bwei o we, “Wɛ wó tɔge wɔ baŋa ne mo o ke konto?” Sampwora kam ma leiri ka we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Nɔn-donno telo na toŋe ba pae kateira yam dedɛɛra bam to mo wó ke jara yam.” Ahab ta ma bwei o we, “Wɔ mo wó da ba yiga o ke jara yam?” Sampwora kam de ma leiri ka we, “Ko ye nmo mo wó ke konto.”
15Ahab ma bwoŋi nɔn-donno telo na toŋe ba pae kateira yam dedɛɛra bam to o ke daane. Ba maa ye jar-keira bia yalei de fintɔ-balei (232). O ma daare o bwoŋi Isarele jar-keira balo na daare to maama o ke daane. Banto maa ye nɔɔna morro terepɛ (7,000). 16Ba maama ma zaŋe wea tetare ne ba nwoŋi se ba ke jara yam, de Ben-hadadi na jei o nyɔ sana de pwa fintɔ-balei bam ba vwoa wone pa se ba bugi to. 17Isarele nɔn-donno tem ma da yiga ba vo se ba kwaare jara yam. Ben-hadadi ya toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba yere jei sem. Ba ma jwoori ba ta de Ben-hadadi ba we, “Jar-keira badwonna mo zege Samaria teo ne ba beena”. 18Ben-hadadi ma leiri-ba o we, “Ba ná tu se ba lwoori yibwona amo tei ne, naa ba ná tu se ba ke jara mo, ko maama ye bedwe mo. Ja-na-ba se á nam yé go-ba.”
19Isarele nɔn-donno tem déem ma gwɛ ba nwoŋi teo kom wone ye jar-keira nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama wo ba kwaga ne. 20Jar-keiru maama ma mage Siria tu dedoa o go. Siria tiina balo na daare to duri se ba lu jara yam wone, ye Isarele tiina bam pare-ba mo. Siria teo pɛ Ben-hadadi ma di sisein-nɔɔno o duri o kɛ. O nɔɔna badwonna de wane ba di sisein-nɔɔna ba duri ba lu. 21Isarele teo pɛ Ahab de o jar-keira bam ta ma duri ba yi Siria jar-keira bam, de ba sisei sem, de ba torokooro tem. Ba ma zaŋe ba baŋa ne ba go ba dedɛ.
22Konto kwaga ne mo Wɛ sampwora kam fɔɔre o yi Isarele teo pɛ Ahab tei ye o we, “Fɔge n ke baare n ke n nɔɔna bam kuri ne, se n boŋe n nii n na wó ke tei. Kokuri to, ben-doore ná yia, Siria teo pɛ wom daa ta wó nwoŋi se o ke jara de abam.”
23Ko nam ná ye Siria teo pɛ dedɛɛra bam, banto mo tage ded‑o ba we, “Isarele tiina wa yam jege dam peero jei sem ne mo. Konto ŋwaane mo Isarele tiina bam wane debam ba di. Dé nam ná jwoori dé kwaare jara de-ba te-kampare sem ne, dé wó seene de wane-ba. 24N nam na wó ke tei to, le pwa fintɔ-balei bam n yage, n daare n pa se jar-keira yiga tiina leiri ba yuu ne ba taa nii jara yam baŋa ne. 25Nam ta jwoori n la jar-keira badwonna se ba taa mae de balo n ya na gɛ jara yam wone to. Ta kwaleme sisein-nɔɔna de torokooro se te ni taa mae de telo n ya na jege to. Dé laam wó wane dé vo dé kwaare jara de Isarele tiina bam te-kampare sem ne. De ná ke konto, de wó yɔɔre dé wane-ba.” Siria teo pɛ ma sɛ o ke o dedɛɛra bam na tage kolo to.
26Ben-doore na jwoori de yi to, Siria teo pɛ Ben-hadadi ma la o jar-keira bam o ke daane, ye ba vo Afeka se ba ke jara de Isarele tiina bam. 27Isarele jar-keira bam de ma ti ba yiga de ba jara zela. Ba ma nwoŋi ba vo se ba kwaare jara de-ba. Ba na jeeri daane konto to, Isarele tiina bam déem nye de bobom-bia kɔgɔ de kɔgɔ kuni belei mo. Siria tiina kɔgɔ kom nam faare tega kam maama mo.
28Wɛ tontoŋeno wom ma vo o ta de Isarele teo pɛ Ahab o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Siria tiina bam na boŋe we amo Baŋa Wɛ jege dam peero jei sem ne mo se ko dae te-kampare ne to, a lage a pa se n wane ba jar-keira kɔgɔ konto maama n di mo. Konto wó pa se abam maama lɔre we amo mo seene a ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.”
29Jar-keira kɔgɔ kuni belei bam kwei da yarepɛ mo ba tigisi kɔgɔ de kɔgɔ ba chichei ba zege ye ba yiga jeeri daane. Da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne jara yam ma bobo.
