Isarele tiina bam ma go Siria tiina jar-keira balo na vei tega ne to morro bi (100,000) dɛ dem konto wone. 30Ba badaara bam ma duri ba zo Afeka teo wone se ba lu. Teo kom kabira kam ma bwori ka to tega ne buri-buri ka pane ba morro finlei-terepɛ (27,000) ka go. Pɛ Ben-hadadi de ma duri o zo teo kom wo o seigi o tete di-yuu wone.
31Ben-hadadi dedɛɛra bam ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Nii mo. Dé nigi we Isarele dwi dem pwa yeini ba jege nɔɔna yibwona. Nam pa se dé tu dé tete dé zo gare-nyenyaaro, se dé daare de vɔ ŋone dé yuni ne dé vo de lwoori Isarele tiina pɛ wom. Dɛ delo o laam wó yage‑m se n ta‑n ŋwe.” 32Ba ma seene ba zo ba gare-nyenyaaro tem ye ba daare ba vɔ ŋone ba yuni ne. Ba ma vo Isarele tiina pɛ tei ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Pɛ, n tontoŋeno Ben-hadadi lwoori‑m we, ‘Jan ja! Yage se a taa ŋwe.’ ” Pɛ Ahab ma leiri o we, “Ben-hadadi ta ŋwe mo na? Dé nam ye da-yuudwonna mo.”
33Ben-hadadi dedɛɛra bam maa wo pɛ se Ahab ni to tega ne ye ba sɛ o taane dem ba we, “Ben-hadadi seene o ye n yuudwoŋi chekke mo.” Ahab ma ta de-ba o we, “Véi-na á ja‑o á ba.” Ben-hadadi na tu to, Ahab ma pa se o di o jeini o toroko kom baŋa ne. 34Ben-hadadi déem ma ta o we, “Amo wó jwoori a kwei teene delo a kwo déem na tɔge jara baŋa ne o vere n kwo jeŋa ne to a pa‑m. A ta wó pa‑m chwoŋa se n tiŋi ya-fwaaro Damasika ne, nenɛɛne a kwo déem na maŋe o ke tei Samaria ne to.” Pɛ Ahab ma leiri o we, “Ni delo n na tage konto to ŋwaane a wó yage‑m se n viiri.” O déem ma gwoni ni ded‑o ye o daare o yage‑o pa se o viiri.
Wɛ sampwora na tage kolo o chɔge Pɛ Ahab to
35 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa o sampwori sem kɔgɔ wone nɔɔno dedoa ni ye o vo o ta de o dwoŋi sampwora o we, “Popo, mage-ne n ke zonne.” O dwoŋi wom ma ve se o ke konto. 36Sampwora kam ma ta ded‑o o we, “N na ve Baŋa Wɛ ni dem konto to, ta‑n yei we, n ná yɔɔre n yage-ne n ma‑n viira, nywoŋo mo lage ko go‑m chwoŋa yuu ne.” O na maa viiri to mo bedwe baŋa ne nywoŋo seene ko jeeri‑o ko go.
37Sampwora kam daa ma vo o na nɔɔno wodwoŋi ye o ta‑o we, “Mage-ne n ke zonne!” Nɔɔno wom ma tiini o mage‑o o fuuli o yera. 38Sampwora kam ma kwei gare-yi o vɔ o yibia ne se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé lɔre‑o. O ma vo o zege chwoŋa ni ne o cheigi Pɛ Ahab se o tɔge da o kɛ. 39Pɛ wom na maa kɛ to mo sampwora kam bwoŋi‑o o we, “Pɛ, amo ya wo jara wone mo ko chana. Nɔɔno ma ja peeno o ba o ke a jeŋa ye o daare o kaane-ne o we, ‘Fɔge n yere nɔɔno wonto lanyerane. O nam ná vere n jeŋa ne o lu, n jege se n te mo. Ko ná dae konto, n wó ŋwe lu-nyenno dunni na yi kilo fintɔ-tena (34) to.’ 40A nam ya kwei a yiga mo a ke dáa ne a wora a nii totoŋa yadwonna baŋa ne pa se peeno wom duri o lu.” Pɛ wom ma leiri o we, “Nmo na fereme n tete de n beinnu tem to, ko ye n tete yiga.”
41Sampwora kam ma ke lela o le gɔrɔ kom o yibia ne. Pɛ wom ma lɔre lela we, o ye sampwori sem wone dedoa mo. 42O ma ta de pɛ wom o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Ko nam ná ye nɔɔno wolo a ya na we, n jege se n yɔɔre n chɔge‑o to, nmo yage kotu pa se o viiri. Konto ŋwaane nmo nam mo jege se n leiri kotu yuu ne n te. N nɔɔna bam de maa wó leiri kotu nɔɔna bam yuni ne ba na lɛɛro.” 43Isarele teo pɛ Ahab na nigi konto to, o ma jwoori o vo Samaria teo ye o wo pɛ.

english_text:
Jezebel Has Naboth Killed
1Naboth owned a vineyard in Jezreel near King Ahab's palace.
2One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
3Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
4So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
5Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
6“I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
7“Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
8-10Jezebel wrote a letter to each of the leaders of the town where Naboth lived. In the letters she said:
Call everyone together and tell them to go without eating today. When they come together, give Naboth a seat at the front. Get two liars to sit facing him and swear that Naboth has cursed God and the king. Then take Naboth outside and stone him to death!
She signed Ahab's name to the letters and sealed them with his seal. Then she sent them to the town leaders.
11After receiving her letters, they did exactly what she had asked. 12They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front. 13The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
14The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
15As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.” 16Ahab got up and went to take over the vineyard.
Elijah Condemns Ahab
17The Lord said to Elijah the prophet, 18“King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over. 19Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ”
When Elijah found him, 20Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.”
Elijah answered:
Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates. 21Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free. 22Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
23 And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel. 24Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
25-29When Ahab heard this, he tore his clothes in sorrow and wore sackcloth day and night. He was depressed and refused to eat.
Some time later, the Lord said, “Elijah, do you see how sorry Ahab is for what he did? I won't punish his family while he is still alive. I'll wait until his son is king.”
No one was more determined than Ahab to disobey the Lord. And Jezebel encouraged him. Worst of all, he had worshiped idols, just as the Amorites had done before the Lord forced them out of the land and gave it to Israel.
translation_text:
Nabofi kaduga kam
1Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Nabofi ye o nwoŋi Jezerele. O maa jege Vini teeni kaduga Jezerele ne, ye ka bwola de Samaria teo pɛ Ahab sɔŋɔ kom. 2Dɛ dedwe mo Ahab taga de Nabofi o we, “Sɛ se n kwei n kaduga kam n yeigi n pa-ne se a taa mae a du a dwoa da, ka na wo a sɔŋɔ takeiri ne to ŋwaane. A jege kaduga kadwoŋi na dwoi kanto kam se a ma a leiri ka yuu ne a pa‑m. N ya ze ná laga, a wó ŋwe ka kwora a pa‑m.” 3Nabofi ma leiri o we, “Baŋa Wɛ taa choa se a kwei a nabaara na daare tega kalo ba pa-ne to a pa‑m.”
4Pɛ Ahab ma jwoori sɔŋɔ ye o wo pɛ de Jezerele tu Nabofi na taga kolo to. O ma yɔɔre o peini o kadwogo baŋa ne o pa o yibia jeeri kabira kam ye o daare o ve se o di wodiu, Nabofi na ve se o kwei o kaduga kam o pa‑o to ŋwaane.
5Pɛ Ahab kaane Jezebele ma zo o bwei‑o o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo n wo chɔge pa se n ba lage wodiu?” 6Ahab ma leiri o we, “A vei a ta de Nabofi mo a we, o kwei o Vini teeni kaduga kam o yeigi o pa-ne. O nam daa ná laga, se a leiri ka yuu ne a pa‑o kaduga kadwoŋi. O ma ve se o kwei kaduga kam o pa-ne.” 7Jezebele ma leiri o we, “N dae Isarele teo pɛ mo na? Nam zaŋe wɛɛne se n di wodiu. Ta‑n sii n wonnu, se amo mo lage a pa se n jeŋa zo Jezerele tu Nabofi tega kam.”
8Jezebele ma popone twanno Ahab yere ŋwaane, o daare o kwei Ahab dam nyenyego kom o nye twanno tem baŋa ne. O ma toŋe-te o pa nakwa de dedɛɛra balo na jeini de Nabofi ba nii Jezerele teo kom to. 9O na popone kolo o ke twanno tem wone to mo tento: “La-na á teo kom nɔɔna bam á ke daane se á maama tu á tete Wɛ yiga ne ye á vɔ ni. Ta daare-na á pa se Nabofi jeini dedɛɛra bam jeiŋa jei ne. 10Ta pa-na se nɔn-kayɛ selei jeini ba jeeri Nabofi yiga ne. Banto laam wó ta we o tusi de o na sɔɔle lwarem o ke Wɛ yera ne, de pɛ wom yera ne to. Konto ná kea se á laam ja‑o á nwoŋi pwooni á dole‑o de kandwa á go.”
11Jezerele teo nakwa bam de dedɛɛra bam ma seene ba ke kolo Jezebele na pɛ-ba ni twanno tem wone se ba ke to. 12Ba ma seene ba la nɔɔna bam ba ke daane pa se ba maama vɔ ni. Ba ma daare ba pa se Nabofi jeini dedɛɛra jeiŋa jei ne. 13Nɔn-kayɛ selei sem de ma ba ba jeini Nabofi yiga ne. Ba laam ma ta ba bere nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama we Nabofi ke o chɔge de o na sɔɔle lwarem o ke Wɛ de pɛ wom yera ne to. Ba ma vaŋe‑o ba ja ba nwoŋi teo kom pwooni ba dole‑o de kandwa ba go. 14Ba ma toŋe kwora ba pa Jezebele we, “Ba dole Nabofi de kandwa ba go.”
15Jezebele na yɔɔre o ni we Nabofi seene o te to, o ma ta de Ahab o we, “Jezerele tu Nabofi tega. O daa ba ŋwe. Konto to, véi n kwei tega kam o na ve se o yeigi o pa‑m to n ta‑n tei.” 16Ahab na nigi Nabofi toone dem ŋwa konto to mo o pɛ o zaŋe bedwe baŋa ne o vo Nabofi Vini teeni kaduga kam se o kwei-ka o taa jega.
17 Baŋa Wɛ kwora déem ma yi Tisibi tu Elija we, 18“Zaŋe n vo n jeeri Isarele teo pɛ Ahab na di o paare Samaria ne to. O vei Jezerele o jwoŋi Vini kaduga kalo ya na ye Nabofi nyem to mo o tei. 19Ta n bere‑o we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Nmo go nɔɔno, ye n daare n vere o tega mo n woli da! Ko dae chega na?’ Ta daare n ta de Ahab we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Ta‑n yei we kukuri jwa wó deilimi nmo tete jana jeiga kalo ne se zem na deilimi Nabofi jana to.’ ”
20Elija na vei o jeeri Ahab to, Ahab ma ta ded‑o o we, “Konto to, a dono, nmo nɛ amo jeiga na?” Elija ma leiri o we, “A tu a na‑m se a ta a bere‑m we, n yɔɔre n yage n tete se n ke lwarem n chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga mo. 21Baŋa Wɛ nam tage o we, ‘Nii mo! Amo wó pa se lɛɛro yi‑m. A ta wó yɔɔre a chɔge dwi delo na wó saŋe n kwaga to maama kula. Nmo tete de n dwi dem bakeiri sem maama wó saare Isarele teo ne, ko ná ye balo ta na wo ba kwo sɔŋɔ ne to, de balo na tei ba tete to de. 22Amo wó pa se n sɔ-yuu kom ji nenɛɛne Nebat bu Jeroboam sɔ-yuu kom, de Ahija bu Baasa sɔ-yuu kom na ye tei to, n na chuchugi a bane ye n ta pa se Isarele tiina ke wɛleera yalo to ŋwaane.’ 23Ko nam ná ye Jezebele, Baŋa Wɛ tage o taane o we, ‘Kukuri mo lage se di‑o Jezerele teo kabira teiŋa ne.’ 24N dwi dem nɔɔno wolo maama na wó te teo kolo wone to wó ji kukuri ni-wodiu mo. Wolo na wó te pwola ne to maa wó taa ye duura ni-wodiu.”
25Nɔɔn-nɔɔno déem tera o na yɔɔre o yage o tete se o ke lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga ko ma de Ahab. Ko déem ye o kaane Jezebele mo soge‑o se o ke konto. 26Ahab déem tiini o ke lwarem jwona kaanem baŋa ne mo, nenɛɛne Amori tiina bam ya na ke tei to. Baŋa Wɛ déem zeili banto mo tega kam baŋa ne ye Isarele tiina bam laam ba ba jeini da.
27Ahab déem nam na nigi taane dem konto Elija tei ne to, o ma kaare o gwaaro o yage, o daare o zo gare-nyenyaaro ye o vɔ ni wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. O lɛɛre o tigi de gare-nyenyaaro tem mo ye o nyɔne o yiga o via.
28 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ta ma yi Tisibi tu Elija we, 29“N nɛ Ahab na gwooni o tete a yiga ne tei to na? O na tu o tete konto to, a daa bá pa se lɛɛro tem yi‑o ye o ta ŋwe. A nam wó pa te ba o kwaga kam baŋa ne mo maŋa kalo o bu wom na wó ba o di paare to.”

english_text:
Micaiah Warns Ahab about Disaster
(2 Chronicles 18.2-27)
1For the next three years there was peace between Israel and Syria. 2During the third year King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to visit King Ahab of Israel.
3Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.” 4Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?”
“Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command. 5But first, let's ask the Lord.”
6Ahab sent for about 400 prophets and asked, “Should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?”
“Yes!” the prophets answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
7But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
8“We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.”
“Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied. 9Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
10All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
11Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
12All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth, and they promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
13Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
14“I'll say whatever the living Lord tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
15Then Micaiah went to Ahab, and Ahab asked, “Micaiah, should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?”
“Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
16“Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth!” Ahab shouted. “What does the Lord really say?”
17 He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
18Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring bad news!”
19 Micaiah replied:
Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him. 20The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?”
They talked about it for a while, 21then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.”
“How?” the Lord asked.
22“I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.”
“Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it.”
23This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
24Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
25Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
26Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria. 27Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
28Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!”
Ahab Dies at Ramoth
(2 Chronicles 18.28-34)
29Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead. 30Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Then Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
31The king of Syria had ordered his 32 chariot commanders to attack only Ahab. 32So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them, 33they realized he wasn't Ahab, and they left him alone.
34However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
35The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He bled so much that the bottom of the chariot was covered with blood, and by evening he was dead.
36As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
37Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there. 38Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
39Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 40Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah became king.
King Jehoshaphat of Judah
(2 Chronicles 20.31—21.1)
41Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in Ahab's fourth year as king of Israel. 42Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
43-46Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done, and during his rule he was at peace with the king of Israel.
He got rid of the rest of the prostitutes from the local shrines, but he did not destroy the shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king, including his brave deeds and military victories, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
47The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.
48Jehoshaphat had seagoing ships built to sail to Ophir for gold. But they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber and never sailed. 49Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.
50Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.
King Ahaziah of Israel
51Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
52Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin. 53Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_text:
Wɛ sampwora Mikaya na kaane Pɛ Ahab tei to
1Jara déem daa wo chugi Siria de Isarele laŋa ne ko vei bena yatɔ mo. 2Bene dem na wó ke bena yatɔ to wone mo Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate zaŋe o vo Isarele teo pɛ Ahab tei. 3Ahab déem ma ta de o dedɛɛra bam o we, “Abam swei we Ramofa-Gilead jeiga kam ye debam nyem mo na? Bɛ mo ye dé chem? Dé nam jege se dé zaŋe mo se dé wane dé jwoŋi dé teo kom Siria teo pɛ wom jeŋa ne.”
4Ahab ma bwei Jehosafate o we, “Nmo wó sɛ se n da de amo se dé vo Ramofa-Gilead dé ke jara de-ba na?” Jehosafate ma leiri o we, “Dé ye chorro mo daane. Ta‑n yei we debam jar-keira de dé sisein-nɔɔna maama ye nmo tete nyem mo.” 5Jehosafate ta ma ta Isarele teo pɛ Ahab o we, “Nam pa se dé da yiga dé bwei dé nii Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to se dé laam daare dé vo.”
6Ahab ma bwoŋi Wɛ sampwori sem o ke daane. Ba maa ye nenɛɛne nɔɔna bia yana (400). O ma bwei-ba o we, “Chwoŋa wora se a vo Ramofa-Gilead a ke jara de-ba, naa a yé vei?” Sampwori sem ma leiri ba we, “Pɛ, nam véi n gware-ba, se dé Teiru Wɛ wó kwei-ba o ke n jeŋa ne.” 7De ko de, Jehosafate ta bwei mo o we, “Baŋa Wɛ sampwora wodwoŋi daa wora ywo-seeni se dé bwei o de dé nii na?” 8Pɛ Ahab ma leiri‑o o we, “Nɔɔno wodwoŋi ta daare, o yere mo Mikaya ye o ye Imila bu. Dé wó wane dé da wonto ŋwaane dé lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa. Ko nam na ye tei to, o ba swoi se o taa pworisi wo-laaro o pa-ne, se ko ye lɛɛro yerane mo. Konto ŋwaane mo a ba laga o ni taane kɔtaa.” Jehosafate ma leiri‑o o we, “Ko nam dae se n ta konto dwoŋi.” 9Ahab ma bwoŋi o dedɛɛra bam dedoa ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Ke lela n vo n ja Imila bu Mikaya n ba ywo-seeni.”
10Isarele teo pɛ Ahab dedaane Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate déem zo ba paare gwaaro mo ba jeini ba paare yitunnu baŋa ne ko maŋe de Samaria teo manchwoŋo ni dem. Jeiga kam déem ye mena ferem jeiga. Sampwori sem maama maa zege ba yiga ne ba pworisa. 11Ba dedoa yere na ye Zedekia ye o ye Chenaana bu to ma mage luu o ma o ji nyea. O ma ta de Ahab o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Nyea yanto bere we n jege dam mo se n ma n chu Siria tiina bam n go zɔŋ-zɔŋ.” 12Sampwori sem maama de déem pworisi konto mo ye ba we, “Pɛ, zaŋe n vo Ramofa-Gilead n ke jara n wane-ba. Baŋa Wɛ lage o kwei teo kom o ke n jeŋa ne mo.”
13Dedɛɛro wolo na vei se o bwoŋi Mikaya to ma ba o ta de Mikaya o we, “Nii mo! Sampwori sedwonna sem jege ni dedwe ba pworisi wo-laaro mo ba pa pɛ wom. Nmo de nam jege se n pworisi zaane taane mo ne banto na ke tei to.” 14Mikaya ma leiri‑o o we, “Ne Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we, Baŋa Wɛ na wó pa-ne ni se a ta kolo to yerane mo a wó ta a bere pɛ wom.”
15Mikaya na vei o yi Ahab tei to, Ahab ma bwei‑o o we, “Mikaya, chwoŋa wora se dé vo Ramofa-Gilead dé ke jara de-ba, naa dé yé véi?” Mikaya ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, zaŋe n vo n ke jara yam n wane-ba, se Baŋa Wɛ mo lage o kwei teo kom o ke n jeŋa ne.” 16Ahab ma yɔɔre o ta Mikaya o we, “A maŋe a ta de nmo kuni dedɛ we, n jege se n du we n wó ta chega taane yerane mo n bere-ne maŋa kalo maama n na yeini n pworisi Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane to.” 17Mikaya laam ma ta o we, “A nɛ Isarele jar-keira bam maama na jage peero tem baŋa ne ye ba beeri yɔɔ yɔɔ nenɛɛne pei selo na ba jege nayero to. Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we, ‘Nɔɔna banto ba jege yuu tu. Yage-na se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ chemm de yazura.’ ”
18Isarele teo pɛ Ahab ma ta de Jehosafate o we, “A ya maŋe a ta de nmo we, o bá sɛ o pworisi wo-laaro o pa-ne, se lɛɛro yerane mo.”
19Mikaya daa ma ta o bere Ahab o we, “Nam cheigi Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ne kwora kalo to. A nɛ Baŋa Wɛ na jei o paare yituŋu baŋa ne ye Wɛ telaao kɔgɔ kom maama zege ba gilimi‑o, o jazem de jagwia seeni. 20Baŋa Wɛ maa we, ‘Wɔ mo wó sɛ o vo o gane Ahab se o vo Ramofa-Gilead o ke jara de-ba se o laam ga o ŋwea?’ Kɔgɔ kom maama dedoa dedoa ma ta o boboŋa. 21Ko kwola ne to, chichira kadwoŋi ma nwoŋi ka zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne ye ka ta ka we, ‘Amo wó wane a vo a gane Ahab’. 22Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei-ka o we, ‘N lage n ke tɛ mo n wane n ke konto?’ Chichira kam ma leiri ka we, ‘A lage a vo a pa se Ahab sampwori sem pworisi vwa pworisim mo.’ Baŋa Wɛ maa we, ‘Nmo wó na chwoŋa se n soge‑o. Nam véi n ke konto.’ 23Tɔ. Nam lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ seene o pa se n sampwori sem maama fɔ vwa ba pa‑m mo. Chega ŋwaane to, Baŋa Wɛ yɔɔre o tiŋi lɛɛro mo se te ba n baŋa.”
24Konto na ke to mo Chenaana bu Zedekia zaŋe o vo o mage Mikaya yibia ne ye o bwei‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ jworo ke tɛ mo ko yage amo ye ko ba nmo tei ko ŋɔɔne dede‑m?” 25Mikaya ma leiri o we, “Nii mo. Nmo wó lɔre debam wone wɔ mo tage chega dɛ dem n na wó zo di-yuu wone n seigi n tete to mo.”
26Isarele teo pɛ Ahab ma pa ni se ba ja Mikaya ye o we, “Ja-o-na á ja á vo teo kom dedɛɛro Amon tei, dedaane amo bu Joasa tei. 27Ta-na de-ba we, ‘Pɛ wom na tage kolo to mo tento: Ja-na nɔɔno wom á ke peena diga ne. Ta‑á pa‑o bworobworo fenfee de na yerane se ko taa nii maŋa kam a na wó zege jara yam wone a jwoori de yazura to.’ ”
28Mikaya ma leiri pɛ wom o we, “N ná seene n zege jara yam wone n jwoori de yazura, ko nam dae Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ-ne kwora kam.” Mikaya ta ma ta de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom o we, “Á maama yé swei-na a na taga taane delo to.”
Pɛ Ahab toone
29Isarele teo pɛ Ahab de Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate déem ma zaŋe ba vo Ramofa-Gilead se ba ke jara de-ba. 30Ahab ma ta Jehosafate o we, “De ná zo jara yam wone, a laam wó leiri a yibia se ba yé lɔre-ne. Ko daare nmo wó zo n paare gwaaro tem.” Ahab ma seene o ke ne o na taga tei to, ye ba maama vo se ba ke jara yam.
31Siria tiina pɛ wom déem ya maŋe o bwoŋi o jara-keim toroko-dira dedɛɛra fintɔ-balei bam mo ye o pa-ba ni we, “Kwaare-na jara yam de Isarele teo pɛ wom yerane, se ko dae jar-keira badaara bam, ba ná maŋe ba ye dedɛɛra tei de.” 32Siria jara-keim dedɛɛra bam na nɛ Jehosafate ye o zo o paare gwaaro tem to, ba ma boŋe ye ba we, “Nii-na Isarele teo pɛ wom da!” Ba ma fɔɔre ba yi se ba ke jara ded‑o. Jehosafate na nɛ-ba to, o ma laare de kwor-dɛa. 33Siria jar-keira dedɛɛra bam ma maane we ko dae Isarele teo pɛ wom. Ba ma yage‑o ye ba kɛ.
34Siria jar-keiru wodwoŋi déem saŋe o taŋa mo o ta chene yɔɔ yerane. Chene dem ma vo de zɔ Isarele teo pɛ Ahab o nyɔɔne seeni mɛ o jara zela yam na wo kwoli‑o to. Ahab ma ta de o toroko-diru wom o we, “Pa se dé ke lela dé pipiri dé vo dáa yiga yiga jara yam wone, se a nɛ zonne mo.” 35Jara yam déem kea dɛ dem maama wone mo. Pɛ Ahab ma maŋe o toroko kom wone o sale o jeeri Siria tiina bam. O fufwollu tem jana ma lwo ba duri ba tagele toroko kom wo. Dɛ dem konto dedaan-ni ne mo o tega. 36Wea na maa zoore maŋa kalo to mo Isarele jar-keira bam keeri bɔge-bɔge ba we, “Ko ti ywoo! Pa-na se nɔɔno maama jwoori o tete teo!”
37Isarele teo pɛ Ahab na tege konto to, ba ma kwei o yera yam ba ja ba vo Samaria ba suli‑o da. 38Ba ma zare o toroko kom Samaria buga kam ni ne mɛ ka-tole na yeini se swɛ se yera da to. Dáane mo kukuri tu se deilimi Ahab jana bam. Konto déem ma pa se Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo faŋa to ji chega.
39Ahab déem na di paare ye o toŋe wonnu telo maama to ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone, ne ko ná ye o na lɔge pɛ sɔŋɔ o fɔge-ko de tuu yeili to, de o ta na lɔge teene delo maama to. 40O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Ahazia ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.
Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate taane
41Isarele teo pɛ Ahab paare dim bena yana bene dem ne mo Asa bu Jehosafate bobo se o di Judah teo paare. 42Jehosafate déem jege bena fintɔ-yanu mo ye o di paare dem. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena finlei-yanu. O nu déem mo ye Silihi bukɔ Azuba. 43Jehosafate déem yɔɔre o kwei o kwo Asa totoŋ-naga kam maama mo, o wo ywori ka wone kɔtaa, pa se o totoŋa su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane. O déem nam wo wane o chɔge wara-jei selo ba na ke kaanem da to. Nɔɔna daa ta ke kaanem de zwɛɛm pɛɛra jei sem konto ne mo. 44Kolo na woli da to mo ye Jehosafate pɛ se o de Isarele teo pɛ mo ke ni daane.
45Jehosafate déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o baare kikia yam, de o tigura keim maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 46O déem zeili baara balo ta na daare ye ba bwoori wara-jei sem ne to. Banto maa ye balo o kwo Asa ya na zeili o ga ye ba ta toŋe Judah laŋa kam ne to.
47Jehosafate paare maŋa kam ne Edom teo déem ba jege pɛ. Jehosafate mo le nɔɔno se o taa nii teo kom o pa‑o.
48Jehosafate déem ke nabwooru se te yeini te tɔge naneo te beeri pipiu ŋwaane. O ma boŋe se o toŋe-te Ofiri seeni se te zeŋe sabu-seŋa te ja ba. Nabwooru tem konto nam chɔge mo Ezion-gebera ne te maŋe da. Te daa ware te vo jei jei. 49Ahab bu Ahazia déem tage de Jehosafate o we, “Sɛ se nmo nɔɔna bam de amo de nɔɔna bam ke daane ba taa diini n nabwooru tem.” Jehosafate ma ve.
50Jehosafate ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa bam yibeeli ne o nabaaro David teo Jerusalem ne. O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Jehoram ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.
Isarele teo pɛ Ahazia taane
51Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate paare dim bena fuga-yarepɛ bene dem ne mo Ahab bu Ahazia jeini Samaria ne o di Isarele teo paare. O ma di paare dem bena yalei. 52O déem ke lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga nenɛɛne o kwo, de o nu, de Nebat bu Jeroboam déem na ke tei ye ba pa se Isarele tiina bam de tusi to. 53Ahazia déem zuli Baal jwoni dem mo. Ko ma pa se o chuchugi Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to bane ko maŋe de o kwo de déem na ke tei to maama.

english_text:
The Lord Condemns Ahaziah
1-2Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah.
One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
3About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury. 4Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
5When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
6“A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
7“What did the man look like?” Ahaziah asked.
8 “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered.
“It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah. 9So at once he sent an army officer and 50 soldiers to meet Elijah.
Elijah was sitting on top of a hill at the time. The officer went up to him and said, “Man of God, the king orders you to come down and talk with him.”
10 “If I am a man of God,” Elijah answered, “God will send down fire on you and your 50 soldiers.” Fire immediately came down from heaven and burned up the officer and his men.
11Ahaziah sent another officer and 50 more soldiers to Elijah. The officer said, “Man of God, the king orders you to come see him at once.”
12“If I am a man of God,” Elijah answered, “fire will destroy you and your 50 soldiers.” And God sent down fire from heaven on the officer and his men.
13Ahaziah sent a third army officer and 50 more soldiers. This officer went up to Elijah, then he got down on his knees and begged, “Man of God, please be kind to me and these 50 servants of yours. Let us live! 14Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
15The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
16When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
17Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah. 18Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_text:
Elija vei o jeeri Pɛ Ahazia
1Pɛ Ahab déem na tege to, mo Moaba tiina ve se ba taa wo Isarele tiina dam kuri ne.
2Dɛ dedwe mo Samaria teo pɛ Ahazia zege o nayuu ne o tɔge nayaa kam ne o chɔɔle o to tega ne pa se o tiini o fuuli. O ma toŋe o tontoŋena se ba vo ba bwei Ekoron tiina jwoni Baal-Zebubi ba nii, o wó jwoori o zaŋe naa o daa bá zaŋe.
3 Baŋa Wɛ maleka ma vo o ta de Wɛ sampwora Elija na ye Tisibi tu to ka we, “Zaŋe n vo n jeeri Pɛ Ahazia tontoŋena bam n bwei-ba we, ‘Aawo, bɛŋwaane mo abam maa vei se á bwei Ekoron tiina jwoni Baal-Zebubi se á nii? Wɛ nam tera Isarele teo wone mo na? 4Nam véi-na á ta de pɛ wom we o bere o bá zaŋe sara kalo o na tigi ka wone to. O jege se o te mo. Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.’ ” Elija ma seene o vo o ke konto.
5Tontoŋena bam ma jwoori ba vo pɛ Ahazia tei. O ma bwei-ba o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo abam jwoori á ba ywo?” 6Ba ma leiri ba we, “Nɔɔno mo jeeri debam o ta o we, dé jwoori dé ba dé ta de bere‑m we Baŋa Wɛ mo tage de nmo o we, ‘Bɛŋwaane mo n toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba bwei Ekoron tiina jwoni Baal-Zebubi ba nii? Wɛ tera Isarele teo wone mo pa se n ke konto na? Nmo keim dem konto ŋwaane n bá‑n yage sara kalo n na tigi ka wone to. Nmo jege se n te mo.’ ”
7Ahazia ma bwei-ba o we, “Nɔɔno wom na jeeri abam ye o ta konto dwoŋi to nye tetɛ mo?”
8Tontoŋena bam ma leiri‑o ba we, “Nɔɔno wom zo gɔrɔ kolo na jege varem koro to mo. O ma vɔ tankila o teiŋa ne.” Ahazia maa we, “Tisibi tu Elija mo konto.”
9Pɛ wom ma le jar-keira finnu de ba yiga tu o toŋe-ba Elija tei ne. Jar-keira yiga tu wom ma vo o na Elija na jei peo kodwoŋi yuu ne. O ma ta ded‑o o we, “Wɛ tontoŋeno, pɛ wom we n tu n ba o tei.” 10Elija ma leiri jar-keira yiga tu wom o we, “Amo ná seene a ye Wɛ tontoŋeno, se o pa min-vogo zege wɛyuu ne de ba de di nmo de n nɔɔna finnu bam maama kula.” O na tage konto o ti to, mo mini dem seene de nwoŋi wɛyuu ne de ba de zwɛ ba maama.
11Konto na ke to, pɛ wom ma jwoori o toŋe jar-keira finnu de ba yiga tu ye ba vo Elija tei. Yiga tu wom ma ta de Elija o we, “Wɛ tontoŋeno, pɛ wom we n ke lela n tu n ba o tei.” 12Elija ma leiri o we, “Amo ná seene a ye Wɛ tontoŋeno, se o pa min-vogo zege wɛyuu ne de ba de di nmo de n nɔɔna finnu bam maama kula.” Wɛ min-vogo kom ma seene ko nwoŋi wɛyuu ne ko ba ko zwɛ ba maama kula.
13Konto na ke to, pɛ wom daa ma jwoori o toŋe jar-keira finnu de ba yiga tu se ba vo Elija tei o ke yiga tiina batɔ tu. Jar-keira yiga tu wom ma vo o kuni dwoona Elija yiga ne ye o lwoori‑o o we, “Wɛ tontoŋeno, duri amo de a kwaga nɔɔna bam ŋwaŋa, se n yage se dé taa ŋwe. 14Ko ná ye jar-keira yiga tiina balei bam de ba kwaga nɔɔna bam, dé maane min-vogo kom na zege wɛyuu ne ko ba ko di ba maama tei to. Ko nam ná ye amo, duri a ŋwaŋa se n yage se a yé te.”
15 Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ma ta de Elija ka we, “Zaŋe n tɔge ded‑o se á tu á vo pɛ wom tei. Nam yé ta‑n kɔre foone.” Elija ma seene o tu pa se ba tɔge daane ba vo ba yi pɛ wom tei. 16Elija ma ta de pɛ wom o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Nmo na toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba bwei Ekoron tiina jwoni Baal-Zebubi ba nii to, ko ye Wɛ na tera Isarele teo wone se n bwei‑o n nii to ŋwaane mo na? Keim dem konto ŋwaane, nmo daa bá‑n yage sara kalo n na tigi ka wone to se n zaŋe wɛɛne. N jege se n te mo.”
17Pɛ Ahazia ma seene o te, se ko maŋe de Wɛ sampwora Elija na wuuri o ta o taane tei to. Ahazia déem ba jege bakeira. Konto ŋwaane o nyaane Joram ma leiri o yuu ne o ji Isarele teo pɛ. Ko déem ke maŋa kalo Jehosafate bu Jehoram na di paare Judah teo ne o ke bena yalei to mo. 18Ahazia déem na di paare ye o toŋe wonnu telo maama to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone.

english_text:
The Lord Takes Elijah Away
1Not long before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a strong wind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal. 2Elijah said to Elisha, “The Lord wants me to go to Bethel, but you must stay here.”
Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Bethel.
3A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?”
“Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
4Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.”
Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
5A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?”
“Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
6Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.”
Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
7Fifty prophets followed Elijah and Elisha from Jericho, then stood at a distance and watched as the two men walked toward the river. 8When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
9 After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?”
Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
10“It won't be easy,” Elijah answered. “It can happen only if you see me as I am being taken away.”
11Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven. 12 Elisha saw this and shouted, “Israel's cavalry and chariots have taken my master away!” After Elijah had gone, Elisha tore his clothes in sorrow.
13Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River. 14He struck the water with the coat and wondered, “Will the Lord perform miracles for me as he did for Elijah?” As soon as Elisha did this, a dry path opened up through the water, and he walked across.
15When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.”
They walked over to him, bowed down, 16and said, “There are 50 strong men here with us. Please let them go look for your master. Maybe the Spirit of the Lord carried him off to some mountain or valley.”
“No,” Elisha replied, “they won't find him.”
17They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him. 18They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.”
Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
19One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
20He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.”
They brought him the bowl of salt, 21and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
22The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said.
Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
23Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
24Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces 42 of the boys.
25Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ kwei Elija o ja o vo telaao
1Maŋa kam déem yi se Baŋa Wɛ tɔge vo-kekara baŋa o kwei Elija o ja o vo telaao. Elija de Elisa déem ma zege Giligal ne ba maa kɛa. 2Elija ma ta de Elisa o we, “Nam maŋe ywo-seeni, se Baŋa Wɛ toŋe-ne mo se a vo Bɛtel.” Elisa ma ve ye o we, “Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane, de nmo tete ŋwea ŋwaane we, amo bá yage n yera.” O na tage konto to, ba maama ma tɔge daane ba vo Bɛtel.
3Ba na yi da to, Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kolo na zoore Bɛtel ne to ma vo Elisa tei ba bwei‑o ba we, “Nmo yei we Baŋa Wɛ zem lage o kwei nmo yuu tu wom mo o ja o viiri na?” Elisa ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, amo seene a yei ko ni ne. Nam yé pa-na se dé lare ko lara.”
4Elija laam ma ta de Elisa o we, “Nam maŋe ywo-seeni, se Baŋa Wɛ mo toŋe-ne se a vo Jeriko.” Elisa daa ta ma leiri o we, “Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane, de nmo tete ŋwea ŋwaane we, amo bá yage n yera.” Ba maama ma tɔge daane ba vo ba yi Jeriko.
5Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kolo na zoore Jeriko ne to ma vo Elisa tei ba bwei‑o ba we, “Nmo yei we Baŋa Wɛ zem lage o kwei nmo yuu tu wom mo o ja o viiri na?” Elisa ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, amo seene a yei ko ni ne. Nam yé pa-na se dé lare ko lara.”
6Elija daa ta ma ta de Elisa o we, “Maŋe ywo-seeni, se Baŋa Wɛ mo toŋe-ne se a vo Jɔdan buga kam ni seeni.” Elisa de daa ma leiri o we, “Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane, de nmo tete ŋwea ŋwaane we, amo bá yage n yera.” Ba maama ma tɔge daane ba maa kɛa.
7Banto balei na vei ba zege Jɔdan buga kam ni ne to, mo Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kom wo nɔɔna finnu ma tɔge ba vo ba zege dáa ne ye ba nia. 8Elija ma le o gɔrɔ o kukuli-ko o ma o mage Jɔdan buga na bam. Na bam ma pɔɔre ba peini jazem de jagwia pa se ba balei bam tɔge te-kora baŋa ne ba bɛ.
9Ba na bɛ buga kam konto to, mo Elija tage de Elisa o we, “Ta n bere-ne nmo na laga se a ke woŋo kolo a pa‑m to, se Baŋa Wɛ laam ba o ja-ne o viiri.” Elisa ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, a lage se a jwoŋi n dam delo n na jege n toŋe to kuni belei mo.”
10Elija ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo na lwoori woŋo kolo to tiini ko dana ko gaale. Nmo nam ná nɛ-ne maŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kwei-ne o ja o viiri to, n jeŋa wó zo n na beeri kolo to. Ko nam ná dae konto, n bá na-ko.”
11Elija de Elisa na tɔge daane ba via ye ba lara konto to, mo torokooro na jege min-vogo to de te sisein-nɔɔna de na jege mini to pɔpɔ te zaŋe ba baŋa ne kulululu te pwɛ-ba daane. Elija ma da de vo-kekara o kɛ Wɛ telaao. 12Elisa na nɛ konto to, mo o laare o we, “Amo kwo! Amo kwo! Isarele jar-keira torokooro tem de te sisein-dira bam laam wó ke tɛ mo?” O daa maa wo nɛ Elija yera.
Elija na kɛ konto to, Elisa wo ma chɔge ye o ja o tete gɔrɔ o kaare belei. 13O ma kwei Elija gɔrɔ kolo ya na lwei to o jwoori o vo o zege Jɔdan buga kam ni ne. 14O ma kwei Elija gɔrɔ kom o mage na bam baŋa ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Elija Wɛ to nam bɛ?” O na mage na bam konto to, ba ma pɔɔre belei ba daare te-kora. O laam ma tɔge da o bɛ Jɔdan buga kam.
15Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kolo déem na nwoŋi Jeriko to ma tole ba na Elisa na ke kolo to, ye ba we, “Elisa mo leiri Elija yuu ne o jege o dam dem.” Ba ma fɔɔre ba yi o tei ye ba tiiri o yiga ne ba zuli‑o. 16Ba maa we, “Nii mo. Dé jege babɛ finnu mo dé tei ne. Debam tu, nam pa se dé toŋe-ba se ba vo ba beeri nmo yuu tu wom jei. Dɛ delo Baŋa Wɛ Jworo ga jaane‑o o vo o yage peo kodwoŋi yuu ne mo, naa bwolo kodwoŋi kuri ne.” Elisa ma leiri-ba o we, “Yé toŋe-na-ba.”
17Ba ma tiini ba kwoori‑o pa se Elisa ga ba ŋwa. O ma ta-ba o we, “Nam toŋe-na-ba se ba vo.” Ba ma seene ba toŋe nɔɔna finnu ye ba vo ba kwei da yatɔ ba beeri jei maama ye ba wo nɛ Elija. 18Elisa déem maŋe Jeriko teo wone mo. Ba na jwoori ba ba o tei to, o ma ta-ba o we, “A ya maŋe a wo tage a bere abam we, á yé vei na?”
Elisa na ke wo-kenkagela yalo to
19Jeriko teo nɔn-bia badwonna déem ma vo Elisa tei ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Debam tu, nii dé teo kom zega na tiini ko lana tei. Ko nam na ye tei to, na bam mo ba lana. Tega kam de maa ba ke wodiiru lanyerane.”
20Elisa ma ta o we, “Kwei-na yɛ á ke zon-doŋa wone á ja á ba á pa-ne.” Ba na ke konto to, 21o ma kwei yɛ dem o vo o lwo teo kom buli-yi dem ne ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo kwɛ na banto pa ba ji na-ŋona. Wolo ná nyɔge-ba, kotu bá te. Tega kam de nam bá ji kafɛ.” 22Konto na ke to, na bam ma lɛɛre ba ji na-ŋona se ko ba ko yi zem, nenɛɛne Elisa na tage tei to.
23Elisa déem ma zege Jeriko ne o maa vei Bɛtel. O na wo chwoŋa ne konto to, mo bu-donno tedwonna nwoŋi teo kom wone ba ba ba jege‑o ba mɔna ye ba bage‑o ba we, “Yu-kapworo tu, ta‑n kɛa! Lage jei!” 24Elisa ma pipiri o nii ba seeni ye o daare o sɔɔle lwarem o yage ba yuu ne Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane. O na yɔɔre o ta konto to, mo kago-vara balei nwoŋi gaao kom wone ba ja bu-donno tem finna-balei ba tore yera-yera. 25Elisa ma zege jeiga kam konto ne o vo Kamele peo kom seeni. Ko kwaga ne o ma jwoori Samaria.

english_text:
King Joram of Israel
1Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria 2and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents. 3But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do.
The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
4For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and the wool from 100,000 rams. 5But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
6One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army. 7He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?”
“Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command. 8But which way should we go?”
“We will march through Edom Desert,” Joram replied.
9So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals. 10Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
11Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.”
One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
12Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.”
The three kings went over to Elisha, 13and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.”
“No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
14Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.” 15Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.”
The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
16The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water. 17You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
18That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army. 19You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
20The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
21Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle. 22When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look 23and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
24But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack. 25The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks.
Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it. 26King Mesha of Moab saw that he was about to be defeated. So he took along 700 soldiers with swords and tried to break through the front line where the Edomite troops were positioned. But he failed. 27He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_text:
Tigura chugi Isarele de Moaba laŋa ne
1Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate paare dim bena fuga-nana bene dem wone mo Ahab bu Joram déem di Isarele teo paare Samaria ne. O ma jeini Samaria ne o di paare dem bena fuga-yalei. 2Joram déem toŋe lwarem mo o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. O lwarem kikia yam nam wo yi o kwo de nu ya na ke yalo to. O wane o chɔge kandwɛ delo o kwo déem na chwi Baal zula ŋwaane to. 3De konto de, o paale o ke wɛleera dwi delo Nebat bu Jeroboam déem na ke pa se Isarele tiina de da ba ke to mo. O wo sɛ se o yage.
4Moaba teo pɛ Mesa déem kɔne pei mo. O ma yeini o jege se o ja pipeili morro bi (100,000) o woli de pi-bɛ morro bi (100,000) korro mo o vo o pa Isarele teo pɛ bene maama wone. 5Isarele teo pɛ Ahab nam na tege to mo Moaba teo pɛ ve se o to o pa Isarele teo pɛ wom. 6Pɛ Joram ma zaŋe Samaria ne o la Isarele jar-keira bam maama o ke daane se ba nwoŋi ba ke jara. 7O ma toŋe ni o pa Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate ye o we, “Moaba pɛ wom ve se o to o pa-ne. Nmo nam wó sɛ se n da de amo se dé vo dé ke jara de Moaba tiina bam na?” Jehosafate ma leiri o we, “A wó sɛ se a woli‑m. Dé ye chorro mo daane. Ta‑n nii debam jar-keira de dé sisein-nɔɔna bam we ba ye nmo tete nyem mo.” 8Jehosafate ta ma bwei o we, “Dé nam wó tɔge chwoŋa kɔ mo dé vo dé bobo jara yam?” Joram ma leiri o we, “Dé wó tɔge Edom kagoa chwoŋa kam mo dé vo dé yi-ba.”
9Isarele pɛ Joram, de Judah pɛ wom, ko woli de Edom pɛ wom ma zaŋe ba kɛ de ba nɔɔna bam. Ba maama ma kwei da yarepɛ ba kaare kagoa kam wone pa se na daa tera se ba de ba vara bam nyɔ.
10Pɛ Joram ma laare o we, “Lɛɛro yi debam! Baŋa Wɛ lage o kwei debam pwa batɔ banto mo o ke Moaba tiina bam jeŋa ne se ba di debam!” 11Pɛ Jehosafate ma bwei o we, “Baŋa Wɛ sampwora wora ywo-seeni se dé bwei‑o dé lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa na?” Pɛ Joram tontoŋeno wodwoŋi ma leiri o we, “Safate bu Elisa mo wora. Wonto déem mo yeini o bwola de Elija ye o woli‑o.” 12Pɛ Jehosafate ma ta o we, “Ko ná ye konto, Baŋa Wɛ kwora yeini ka yi wonto mo chekke”. Pwa batɔ bam maama ma zaŋe ba vo Elisa tei.
13Elisa ma ta de Isarele pɛ Joram o we, “Debam jege bɛ mo se dé ke daane? Véi n bwei n kwo de n nu sampwori sem se ba woli‑m.” Joram ma leiri o we, “Aawo! Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo kwei debam pwa batɔ banto o ke daane se o daare o kwei debam o ke Moaba tiina bam jeŋa ne.” 14Elisa ma leiri o we, “Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o ŋwe ye a ye o tontoŋeno to, amo dugi o yere ŋwaane we, ko ná dae a na nege Judah Pɛ Jehosafate, amo ya ba lage a nii n seeni kɔtaa. 15Nam bwoŋi-na wolo na yei kɔnɔ tam to á pa-ne.” Kokuri to, nɔɔno déem ná yeini o ta kɔnɔ mo Baŋa Wɛ dam dem wó ba Elisa baŋa ne. 16Elisa ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: ‘Ko-na gwonnu á tiŋi nabare-kora kanto ne. 17Kokuri to, amo na wó ke tei to, abam bá na doa, ye vio de bá dole. Ko daare na wó ba ba su bwolo konto se abam de á nɔɔna bam maama de á vara bam taa nyɔa.’ 18Keim dento ye mɔle mo Baŋa Wɛ tei ne. O daa ta wó kwei Moaba tiina bam o ke abam jeŋa ne. 19Abam wó vo á wane ba dam jei sem maama de ba te-fwaaro tem. Á ta wó gwoni ba tei-ŋonno tem á de tega ne ye á daare á se ba buli-yia yam de. Á ta maa wó lwo kandwa á chɔge ba tega kalo maama na lana to.”
20Tega na poore se ko maŋe de zezeŋa kaanem dem to mo na seene ba zege Edom laŋa kam seeni ba ba ba tagele tega kam maama.
21Moaba tiina bam na nigi we pwa batɔ bam mo ke ba jar-keira daane ba ba se ba kwaare jara de-ba to, ba ma bwoŋi balo maama na yei jara keim to, nɔn-donno de nɔn-kweero de, pa se ba vo ba laŋa kam siseini ba zege da. 22Tega na poore tetete ye Moaba tiina bam zaŋe to, ba ma tole ba na na bam na tigi bwolo kom ne tei to. Wea maa nyeene na bam baŋa ne pa se ko nye de jana mo to. 23Ba ma laare ba we, “Jana mo tento! Ko wó taa ye pwa bam de ba jar-keira bam mo jaŋe ba go daane. Nam pa-na se dé laam vo dé vere ba wonnu maama dé taa tei.”
24Moaba tiina bam na yɔɔre ba yi Isarele jar-keira bam na tigisi daane mɛ to, mo Isarele jar-keira bam nwoŋi ba kwaare jara de-ba. Ba ma zeili-ba pa se ba duri ba jwoori ba teo. Ba ma pare-ba taa ye ba go Moaba tiina dedɛ. 25Ba déem chɔge ba teene dem mo. Isarele nɔɔna bam dedoa dedoa ma dole kandwa ba faare Moaba te-ywoŋa kam maama ba chɔge. Ba ma se ba buli-yia yam maama ba daare ba gwoni ba tei-ŋonno tem maama ba de tega ne. Kiri-Heresi teo kom yerane ya mo daare ko zege puna. Isarele jar-keira laam ma vo ba gilimi-ko ye ba daare ba ma napane ba dole kandwa ba ma ba chɔge-ko.
26Moaba teo pɛ na maane we o lage o to jara yam wone to, o ma ja balo na yei se-zɔɔ jara keim to nɔɔna bia yarepɛ o vo se ba wane ba mage ba dona bam ba kɛ ba yi Edom pɛ wom na wo mɛ to ye ba ga. 27O laam ma ja o bu-kwea kalo ya na wó leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ to o ma o ke zwɛɛm kaanem teo kom kabira kam baŋa ne. Keim dento déem ma tiini de daane Isarele tiina bam pa se ba pipiri ba jwoori ba tete teo ba daare Moaba teo pɛ de o nɔɔna bam.

english_text:
Elisha Helps a Poor Widow
1One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
2“Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?”
“Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
3Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can, 4go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.” 5The woman left.
Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
6At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.”
“We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
7After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.”
Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
8Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
9Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God. 10Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
11The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest. 12-13He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?”
The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
14“Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi.
Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
15“Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
16 Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.”
“You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
17But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
18One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops. 19Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!”
“Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant. 20The servant picked up the boy and carried him to his mother. The boy lay on her lap all morning, and by noon he was dead. 21She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
22The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
23“Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.”
“That's all right,” she answered. 24She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.” 25She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha.
When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem. 26Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.”
“Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi. 27But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet.
Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
28The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
29“Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
30But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
31Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
32Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed. 33He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord. 34 Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm. 35Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
36Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
37She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left.
Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
38Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed.
One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
39One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
40The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
41“Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine.
Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
42A man from the town of Baal-Shalishah brought Elisha some freshly cut grain and 20 loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
43“There's not enough here for 100 people,” his servant said.
“Just give it to them,” Elisha replied. “The Lord has promised there will be more than enough.”
44So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_text:
Elisa na woli kadeim wodwoŋi tei to
1Kaane wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o na ye Wɛ sampwori sem dedoa kaane. Dɛ dedwe o ma zaŋe o vo Elisa tei o ŋwane o we, “Amo tu, a baro wom tega ye o ya tɔge nmo kwaga. Nmo maŋe n yei o na yeini o kɔre Baŋa Wɛ tei to. O ya na di jene nɔɔno wolo tei ne to nam mo tu se o jwoŋi a bakeiri sem selei o vo o ma o ji o kabɛ se o ma o yiri jene dem.” 2Elisa ma bwei‑o o we, “Woŋo wora amo na wó wane a ke a woli‑m na? Nam ta n bere-ne, bɛ mo n daare n yage sɔŋɔ ne?” Kadeim wom ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, kolokolo tera ko ná dae kabɔɔ de ka wo nuga fenfee yerane.”
3Elisa ma ta de kadeim wom o we, “Tole sane delo na bwola de nmo to se n jene kunkwollu ba tei ne. Pa se te taa daga dedɛ. 4Kwei kunkwollu telo n na nɛ to n zo diga n pe ka ni, se nmo de n bia balei bam taa wora. Nmo ma‑n wó pwori nuga kam n ke kunkwollu tem wone. Kunkwolo kolo ná sua, se n zege-ko dáane.”
5Kadeim wom ma jwoori sɔŋɔ o pe o ni diga wone, o de o bia bam. Ba maa jaane kunkwollu tem ba vei ba pa‑o ye o lɛɛre nuga kam te wone. 6Kunkwollu tem maama na su to, o ma ta bia bam se ba ja tedwonna ba ba ba pa‑o. Ba dedoa ma leiri o we, “Mo te maama.” O na tage konto to mo kabɔɔ kam wo nuga kam ti. 7Kadeim wom ma vo o ta ko na ke tei to o bere Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa. Elisa ma ta ded‑o o we, “Véi n kwei nuga kam n yeigi n ma n ŋwe jene dem. Sabu ta ná daare, ko wó woli nmo de n bia bam se á na á ni-wodiu.”
Sunem tiina kaane wodwoŋi taane
8Dɛ dedwe mo Elisa déem vei Sunem. Kaane wodwoŋi maa zoore da ye o ye nadum. O ma bwoŋi Elisa o sɔŋɔ ne se o di wodiu. Ko na zege dɛ dem konto ne to, maŋa kalo maama Elisa ná vei Sunem, o yeini o di kaane wom konto sɔŋɔ ne mo. 9Kaane wom ma ta de o baro o we, “Nii mo. Amo maane we nɔɔno wonto na yeini o tui debam tei to ye Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno mo chekke. 10Nam pa se dé lɔ di-balaŋa nayuu kom ne se dé daare dé zege kadwogo, de tabolo, de yituŋu, de min-zwoŋo da. Konto wó woli Wɛ tontoŋeno wom se, o ná yeini o ba, se o na peiga jei.”
11Dɛ dedwe mo Elisa jwoori Sunem. O ma di o zo nayuu diga kam se o peini. 12O ma ta de o tontoŋeno Gehazi o we, “Véi n bwoŋi kaane wom n pa-ne.” Gehazi ma seene o bwoŋi kaane wom pa se o ba o zege Elisa yiga ne. 13Elisa ma ta de Gehazi se o lwoni o ta kaane wom we, “Nii nmo na pɛ n yera chɛ se n ma‑n woli debam tei! Debam nam wó ke bɛ mo dé ma dé zeini nmo? Dɛ delo amo wó wane a ta n lanyerane a bere pɛ wom naa jar-keira yiga tu wom.” Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “Yé daane n tete, amo na zoore de a sɔŋɔ tiina to ŋwaane.”
14Elisa laam ma bwei Gehazi o we, “Bɛ nam mo maŋe se a ke a pa kaane wom?” Gehazi ma leiri o we, “Kaane wom ta wo loge bu. O baro de ma tiini o kwe lanyerane.”
15Elisa ma ta de Gehazi o we, “Bwoŋi kaane wom se o jwoori o ba.” Kaane wom ma ba o zege diga kam ni ne. 16Elisa ma ta de kaane wom o we, “Bene tento wɛɛne nmo wó lo bakeira.” Kaane wom maa wo sɛ ye o we, “Amo tu, yé gane-ne, se n ye Wɛ tontoŋeno mo.”
17Bene na jwoori de yi to, kaane wom ma seene o ja puga o lo bakeira. Ko déem ke ne Elisa na wuuri o ta tei ded‑o to mo.
18Bu wom na ke nɔɔno fee to mo dɛ dedwe o zaŋe o vo o kwo tei kara ne maŋa kalo o kwo wom de tontoŋena badwonna na wora ba zage mena to. 19Bu wom ma pɔpɔ o laare bedwe baŋa ne de o kwo o we, “A yuu wɔe ywoo! A yuu wɔe ywoo!” O kwo ma ta de o tontoŋeno wodwoŋi o we, “Ja bu wom n vo o nu tei.” 20Tontoŋeno wom ma teili bu wom o ja o vo o ke o nu wom jeŋa ne. Bu wom ma maŋe o nu nɛ baŋa ne o jeini. Wea na yi yupare baŋa maŋa kalo to mo bu wom tega. 21Kaane wom ma ja o bu wom o di nayuu kom o zo Elisa diga o tiŋi‑o kadwogo kom baŋa ne. O ma nwoŋi o ja diga kam ni o pe o yage bu wom da. 22Kaane wom ma bwoŋi o baro o ta ded‑o o we, “Ja, pa se n tontoŋena bam dedoa ja bonaga o ba, se dé da daane dé vo Wɛ tontoŋeno wom tei, se dé jwoori lela.”
23O baro wom ma ta‑o o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n lage se n vo zem? Chan-doŋa ta wo nwoŋi. Ko maa dae siu dɛ.” Kaane wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Ko ye yazura mo.” 24O ma ti bonaga kam yiga ye o daare o ta de tontoŋeno wom o we, “Pa dé kɛ. Ta‑n pae bonaga kam zaara. Nam yé pa se dé taa vei mɛmɛ ko ná dae we a tage‑m se n ke konto.” 25Kaane wom ma vo o yi Kamele peo kom mɛ Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa na wora to. Elisa ma tole o na‑o yiga yiga ye o ta de o tontoŋeno Gehazi o we, “Nii Sunem tiina kaane wom na maa beene. 26Ke lela n duri n jeeri‑o n bwei‑o n nii, yazura mo o vei na? Bwei‑o n nii o baro de o bu yazura na ye tei to.” Kaane wom ma leiri Gehazi o we, ko ye yazura mo.
27Kaane wom na yi Elisa tei Kamele peo kom yuu ne to mo o to o yiga ne o ja o naga. Gehazi ma fɔɔre o yi se o vaŋe‑o o yage dáane. Elisa ma ta o we, “Yage o yera! O wo tiini ko chɔge mo ye o ba. Baŋa Wɛ nam wo tage kolo na daane‑o to o bere-ne.”
28Kaane wom ma ŋwane Elisa yiga ne o we, “Amo tu, a wo tage we n pa-ne bu. Konto mo a ya taga a we n yé gane-ne to.”
29Elisa ma ta de Gehazi o we, “Fɔge n vɔ n gare-kura kiri-kiri n daare n kwei a nacheiga kam n duri lela n kɛ. Nam yé ware nɔɔn-nɔɔno chwoŋa yuu ne. Nɔɔno ná ware‑m, se n yé leiri‑o. N ná yi da se n kwei a nacheiga kam n daŋe bu wom yibia ne.” 30Kaane wom ma ta de Elisa o we, “Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane, de nmo tete ŋwea ŋwaane we, amo bere a bá yage‑m.” Elisa ma zaŋe se ba tɔge daane ba kɛ.
31Gehazi ma lwoori yiga o vo o yi da ye o daare o kwei nacheiga kam o daŋe bu wom yibia ne ye bu wom wo gigiri o tete. O ma jwoori o vo Elisa tei o ta ded‑o o we, “Bu wom ta wo zaŋe.”
32Elisa na yi sɔŋɔ kom o zo o diga kam to mo o nɛ bu wom na tege o tigi o kadwogo baŋa ne. 33O ma pe diga kam ni ye o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o yerane. 34Elisa ta ma zaŋe o yi kadwogo kom baŋa, o peini bu wom baŋa ne pa se o ni dem yɔɔre bu wom ni, ye o yia yɔɔre o yia. O ma daare o lware o jea pa ya yɔɔre o jea. O na lware o tete o peini bu wom baŋa ne konto to mo bu wom yera lone. 35Elisa ma zaŋe o kekare diga kam wone ye o daa jwoori o vo o lware o tete o peini bu wom baŋa ne. Bu wom ma te kuni berepɛ ye o daare o puri o yia. 36Elisa ma bwoŋi Gehazi ye o ta ded‑o se o bwoŋi Sunem tiina kaane wom o pa‑o. O na bwoŋi nu wom pa se o yi to, Elisa ma ta ded‑o o we, “Jwoŋi n bu.” 37Kaane wom ma zo o to Elisa nɛ baŋa ne ye o vwi o yibia tega ne. O ma seene o jwoŋi o bu o viiri.
Wo-kenkagela yalei taane
38Elisa ma jwoori o vo Giligal. Da-kore déem maa zege jei sem konto ne. Dɛ dedwe o de Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kom ma jeeri daane se ba zamese. O ma ta de o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Kwei kambi-zaŋa n teini mini ne n saŋe dwoa n pa nɔɔna bam.”
39Ba kɔgɔ kom wo nɔɔno dedoa ma zo gaao se o gwoni dwo-vɔɔro. O ma na kunkwol-chɛɛra o pɛ o su o gɔrɔ ni o jwoori. O ma gwoni te maama o woli dwoa balo na wo kambia kam wone to, ye o wo lɔre te na ye wonnu telo. 40Ba laam ma kwei dwoa bam ba maŋe ba pa daane. Nɔɔna bam na yɔɔre ba laŋe wodiu kom to, ba ma laare ba we, “Keitaa! Dé tu, Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno, chɔŋɔ mo ba ke wodiu kom wone!” Ba maa wo ware-ko ba di.
41Elisa ma ta o we, ba ja muni ba ba ba pa‑o. O ma kwei-de o ke kambia kam wone ye o we, “Jwoori n ke wodiu kom n pa nɔɔna bam se ba di.” Ba ma seene ba di ye ko daa wo bwei-ba.
42Dɛ dedwe mo nɔɔno wodwoŋi zege Baal-Salisa ne o ja o wodiiru telo na lwoori yiga te ke to o ba o pa Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa. Bworobwooru finlei, de men-zwaro telo o na ke ywolo wone to mo konto. Elisa ma ta de o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Kwei n pa nɔɔna bam se ba di.” 43Tontoŋeno wom ma leiri o we, “Ba ye nɔɔna bi mo. Wodiu konto wó wane ko yi-ba na?” Elisa ma jwoori o ta o we, “Kwei n pa-ba se ba di. Kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ mo taga o we, ba wó di ba su ba daare.” 44Tontoŋeno wom déem ma seene o kwei wodiu kom o pa-ba pa ba di ba daare, ne Baŋa Wɛ na maŋe o ta tei to.

english_text:
Elisha Heals Naaman
1 Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
2One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife. 3Some time later the girl said, “If your husband Naaman would go to the prophet in Samaria, he would be cured of his leprosy.”
4When Naaman told the king what the girl had said, 5the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.”
Naaman left and took along 30,000 pieces of silver, 6,000 pieces of gold, and 10 new outfits. 6He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
7When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
8As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
9Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house. 10Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
11But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me. 12What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
13His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
14Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
15Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
16“I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.”
Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing. 17Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord. 18But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
19“Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left.
Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi
After Naaman had gone only a short distance, 20Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.” 21So he hurried after Naaman.
When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
22“Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them 3,000 pieces of silver and some new clothes?”
23“Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
24When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone, 25Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?”
“Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
26Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants. 27Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!”
Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_text:
Naaman jaweo kom na jei tei to
1Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Naaman. O maa ye Siria tiina pɛ wom jar-keira yiga tu. O ye dedɛɛro mo ye o kikia su pɛ wom yi lanyerane, Baŋa Wɛ na dɛ o baŋa o woli Siria tiina pa se ba di ba dona jara wone to ŋwaane. Konto to, o ye babea na yei jara keim chekke to mo. De ko de, o déem ye nayɔŋɔ mo.
2Siria teo kom jar-keira déem yeini ba zo Isarele laŋa kam ba ke jara ba vere wonnu ye ba jwoori sɔŋɔ. Ba déem ma vo ba ja Isarele tiina busankana kadwoŋi. Ba ma ja‑o ba vo ba pa Naaman kaane se o taa ye o ka-nyaane. 3Dɛ dedwe, busankana kam ma ta de Naaman kaane o we, “A nu, nmo baro wom ya ná wae o vei Wɛ sampwora kalo na zoore Samaria ne to tei, wonto ya wó pa o na yazura de naywaane jaweo kom.” 4Naaman na nigi konto to, o ma vo o ta kolo Isarele tiina busankana kam na tage to o bere o tu wom. 5Siria tiina pɛ wom ma leiri o we, “Tɔ. Véi se n na nɔɔno wom konto. Amo wó popone tɔnɔ nmo ŋwaane se n ja n vo n pa Isarele teo pɛ wom.”
Naaman ma la lu-nyenno kilo bia yatɔ de finna (340), de sabu-seŋa kilo fuserepɛ (70), ko woli de gare-bia fuga. O laam ma zaŋe o ja-te o kɛ. 6O ma kwei tɔnɔ kom o vo o pa Isarele teo pɛ wom. Kolo na popone ko wone to mo tento: “Tɔnɔ konto ye se ko bere we amo mo toŋe a tontoŋeno Naaman se o ba nmo tei, se n yɔɔre o naywaane jaweo kom n pa‑o.”
7Isarele teo pɛ wom na gage tɔnɔ kom o ti to, mo o jaane o gɔrɔ o kaare ye o we, “Amo ye Wɛ mo se a wane a pa nɔɔno momwɛ ti, ye a daare a pa wodwoŋi na ŋwea na? Bɛ mo ye Siria teo pɛ toŋe nɔɔno wonto se o ba amo tei se a yɔɔre‑o? Nii-na o na beeri woŋo se o da ko baŋa o ja jara de amo tei!”
8Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa na nigi kolo na ke ye Isarele tiina pɛ wom kaare o gɔrɔ to, o ma toŋe ni dento o pa‑o ye o we, “Bɛ mo pɛ se n ja n gwaaro n kaare? Toŋe nɔɔno wom se o ba amo tei se a pa o lɔre we, Wɛ sampwora seene o wo Isarele teo ne.” 9Naaman laam ma ja o sisei sem de se torokooro tem o vo o zege Elisa diga ni ne. 10Elisa ma toŋe o tontoŋeno se o vo ta de Naaman we, “Nam véi n swɛ n yera kuni berepɛ Jɔdan buga kam wone, se n ya-nɔna yam laam wó kwɛ ye n jaweo kom jei.”
11Naaman na nigi konto to, o bane ma zaŋe dedɛ. O ma varege ye o we, “Nii mo! A ya boŋe we Elisa tete mo wó nwoŋi o ba o zege amo yiga ne o bwoŋi o Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yere, se o daare o yeese o jea a ŋɔna yam baŋa ne o yɔɔre amo. 12Abana de Farepa bwi sem na wo Damasika ne to ba gare Isarele bwi sem maama na? A ya wae a swɛ a yera bwi sento wone ye a ya-nɔna kwɛ.” 13Naaman tontoŋena ma fɔɔre ba yi o tei. Ba dedoa ma ta ded‑o o we, “A kwo, sampwora kam ya ná we n toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛre, nmo bá‑n ke na? O nam na tage kolo to dae mɔle ko pa‑m na? O we n swɛ n yera se ya kwɛ. Ko dae konto mo na?” 14Naaman laam ma seene o tu o misi o tete Jɔdan buga kam wone kuni berepɛ, ne Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na taga tei to. O ya-nɔna yam ma jwoori ya kwɛ lanyerane nenɛɛne bakeiri-pwola yera na ye tei to, ye o jaweo kom jei.
15Naaman de o nɔɔna bam maama ma jwoori ba vo Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa tei ba zege o yiga ne. Naaman ma ta de Elisa o we, “Amo zem laam tu a lɔre we Isarele tiina Wɛ wom yerane mo ye wɛ chekke logo baŋa maama wone. Jan ja, amo tu! Sɛ se n jwoŋi a pɛɛra yam.” 16Elisa ma leiri o we, “Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora ye a toŋe a pa‑o to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane we, amo bá jwoŋi kolokolo nmo tei ne.” Naaman ta ma lwoori Elisa o ga se o jwoŋi pɛɛra yam o tei ne. 17Naaman ma ta o we, “Amo tu, nmo na tage we n bá‑n sɛ se n jwoŋi kolokolo a jeŋa ne to, nam pa-ne chwoŋa se a pɛ teero ywo-seeni se te yi bona-sisei selei na wó wane se zeŋe tei to, se a ja a viiri. Kokuri to, ko zege zem se ko taa via, amo daa bá ke kaanem naa zwɛɛm pɛɛra a pa wɛ dedwoŋi, ko ná dae Baŋa Wɛ yerane. 18Amo nam lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o duri a yibwona keim dento ŋwaane: amo ná dɛ de a tu Siria teo pɛ a zo Rimon jwoni diga kam se o zuli-de, ye pɛ wom ná sale a yera ne, ye amo de da a tiiri tega ne ded‑o, se Baŋa Wɛ yage o chɛ-ne.” 19Elisa ma leiri o we, “Nam véi, se Wɛ wó pa‑m yazura.” Naaman ma viiri.
Naaman na vei o yi yiga fee to, 20mo Elisa tontoŋeno Gehazi taga o tete ne we, “Ta‑n nii tei. Amo tu Elisa yage Siria tu wom mo se o viiri konto mɔle mɔle, ye o wo jwoŋi pɛɛra yam o jeŋa ne de fenfee de. Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, a dugi wonto yere ŋwaane we amo tete mo wó pare Naaman a jwoŋi woŋo o tei ne.” 21Gehazi ma ke lela se o vo o yi‑o. Naaman na tole o na nɔɔno na duri o beene o tei to, o ma zege o toroko kom baŋa o faŋe o chu tega ne o vo o jeeri‑o. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Yazura mo n vei na?” 22Gehazi ma leiri Naaman o we, “Ko dae wo-lɔŋɔ. Ko ye amo tu Elisa mo toŋe-ne se a ta dede‑m we, Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kom nɔn-donno telei mo zege Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne ba yɔɔre ba yi o sɔŋɔ leile konto. O nam lage se n kwei lu-nyenno kilo fintɔ-tenu (35), ko woli de gare-bia balei mo n pa-ba.”
23Naaman ma leiri o we, “Amo tei ne, a lage a pa‑m lu-nyenno kilo fuserepɛ (70) mo.” O ma kwoori Gehazi pa se o jwoŋi. O ma kwei lu-nyenno tem o ke ywollu telei wone o vɔ. O ta ma kwei gare-bia balei bam o woli da. O laam ma toŋe o tontoŋena balei se ba zeŋe zela yam ba tɔge Gehazi yiga ba taa via. 24Ba na yi peo kom yuu mɛ seeni Elisa na zoore to, Gehazi ma jwoŋi zela yam ba jeŋa ne o seigi o tete diga ne, o daare o bane Naaman tontoŋena balei bam pa se ba jwoori ba viiri.
25Gehazi ma zo o zege Elisa tei ne. Elisa ma bwei‑o o we, “Gehazi, nmo ya vei yei ne mo?” Gehazi ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, a wo vei jei jei.” 26Elisa ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nmo wo lɔre we maŋa kalo Naaman na zege o toroko kom baŋa ne o chu o jeeri‑m to, amo jworo ya wora mo na? Kanto dae maŋa se n jwoŋi sabu, de gwaaro, de Olivi teeni kare, de Vini teeni kadwi, de pei, de nabɛ, de tontoŋena, de ka-nyaana. 27Nmo nam na ke konto to, ta‑n yei we Naaman naywaane jaweo kom wó ba nmo tete, de n bia, de dwi delo na wó saŋe n kwaga to baŋa se ko taa vei wuu.” Gehazi na nwoŋi pwooni yiga to mo o jigi nayɔŋɔ. O yera ma peere cha ne lɔŋɔ dwoŋi to.

english_text:
Elisha Makes an Ax Head Float
1One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small. 2Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.”
“That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
3“Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked.
“Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered, 4and he left with them.
They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees. 5While one of the prophets was working, his ax head fell off and dropped into the water. “Oh!” he shouted. “Sir, I borrowed this ax.”
6“Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
7“Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it.
Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
8Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
9Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.” 10So the king would warn the Israelite troops in that place to be on guard.
11The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
12“None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
13“Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.”
They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king. 14He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
15When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
16“Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.” 17Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
18As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
19Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
20When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
21The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
22“No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
23The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go.
For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory.
King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
