Jehoasa ta ma daare o vo Jerusalem o bwori teo kom kabira kalo na zege Efrayim Ni dem ne se ka vo ka yi Gugworo Ni dem to. Ka laŋa kam déem ye naba-laara bia yalei mo. 14O ma vo o zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam o vere ka sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno wonnu, de ka lonne zela yam maama. O ta ma pɛ jejegero telo na tigi pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne to. O ma ja te maama o jwoori Samaria. O ta ma ja teo kom nɔɔna o ja viiri se ko fe Judah teo pɛ se o sɛ o ni.
15Jehoasa déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam, de o na kwaare jara de Judah teo pɛ Amazia tei to maama, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 16Jehoasa ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli mɛ ba na suli Isarele tiina pwa badwonna bam Samaria ne to. O bu Jeroboam ma leiri o yuu ne o di paare.
17Isarele teo pɛ Jehoasa toone dem kwaga seeni, Judah teo pɛ Amazia déem ta nɛ bena fuga-yanu mo ye o laam te. 18Amazia déem na di paare ye o toŋe wonnu telo maama to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone.
19Jerusalem dedɛɛra badwonna déem ke ni daane mo se ba go Pɛ Amazia. O ma duri o vo Lakisi. O dona bam ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba pare‑o. Ba ma yi‑o ba go Lakisi ne. 20Ba ma kwei Amazia yera yam ba daŋe sisein-nɔɔno baŋa ne ba ja jwoori Jerusalem. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa bam yibeeli ne David teo ne.
21Judah tiina bam maama ma kuri Azaria se o leiri o kwo Amazia yuu ne o ji pɛ. Ba na tiŋi‑o paare konto to, Azaria déem jege bena fuga-yaredo mo. 22O kwo Amazia toone dem kwaga seeni mo Azaria fɔge o lɔ Elafa teo pa se Judah tiina bam tei-ko.
Isarele teo pɛ Jeroboam II taane
23Judah teo pɛ Joasa bu Amazia paare dim bena fuga-yanu bene dem wone mo Jehoasa bu Jeroboam déem di Isarele teo paare. O ma jeini Samaria ne o di paare dem o ke bena finna-dedwe. 24O déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga mo. O wo sɛ se o yage wɛleera dwi delo Nebat bu Jeroboam déem na ke pa se Isarele tiina de da ba ke to. 25Jeroboam déem mo jwoori o jwoŋi tega kalo na zege Lebo-Hamafa ne ka tole ka yi Yɛ naneo kom to o pa Isarele tiina bam. Keim dem konto tɔge kwora kalo Isarele tiina Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wuuri o pa Amitayi bu Jonah to. Wonto déem ye Wɛ sampwora kalo na nwoŋi Gafa-Hefera to.
26 Baŋa Wɛ déem ya maane Isarele tiina bam maama na nɛ cham tei to. Ba maama tiini ba yaare dedɛ, ko ná ye balo na ye kabɛ, de balo na tei ba tete to maama de. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno déem tera se o woli-ba. 27Baŋa Wɛ nam tɔge Jehoasa bu Jeroboam baŋa ne mo se o jwoŋi-ba o yage. Kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ wo tage we, o wó saare Isarele tiina bam yere logo baŋa maama ne.
28Jeroboam déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam, de o bembɛɛne dem, ko woli de o na jwoori o jwoŋi Damasika de Hamafa teene dem o ke Isarele tiina bam jeŋa ne tei to maama, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 29Jeroboam ma te ye ba kwei‑o ba suli mɛ ba na suli Isarele tiina pwa badwonna bam to. O bu Zekaria ma leiri o ji pɛ.

english_text:
King Azariah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 26.1-23)
1Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah in Jeroboam's twenty-seventh year as king of Israel. 2He was only 16 years old when he became king, and he ruled 52 years from Jerusalem, which was also the hometown of his mother Jecoliah.
3Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done. 4But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
5The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
6Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 7 Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king.
King Zechariah of Israel
8Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria. 9Like his ancestors, Zechariah disobeyed the Lord by following the evil ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
10Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king. 11-12 So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family.
Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Shallum of Israel
13Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king, 14-16Menahem son of Gadi came to Samaria from Tirzah and killed him. Menahem then became king. The town of Tiphsah would not surrender to him, so he destroyed it and all the surrounding towns as far as Tirzah. He killed everyone living in Tiphsah, and with his sword he even ripped open pregnant women.
Everything else Shallum did while he was king, including his plot against Zechariah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Menahem of Israel
17Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria. 18He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
19During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over 34 tons of silver. 20So Menahem ordered every rich person in Israel to give him at least 50 pieces of silver, and he gave it all to Tiglath Pileser, who stopped his attack and left Israel.
21Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 22Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king.
King Pekahiah of Israel
23Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria. 24He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
25Pekah son of Remaliah was Pekahiah's chief officer, but he made plans to kill the king. So he and 50 men from Gilead broke into the strongest part of the palace in Samaria and murdered Pekahiah, together with Argob and Arieh. Pekah then became king.
26Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Pekah of Israel
27Pekah son of Remaliah became king of Israel in Azariah's fifty-second year as king of Judah, and he ruled 20 years from Samaria. 28He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
29During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
30In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
31Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Jotham of Judah
(2 Chronicles 27.1-9)
32Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel. 33Jotham was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled 16 years from Jerusalem. His mother Jerusha was the daughter of Zadok.
34Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right. 35It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
36Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 37During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah. 38Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_text:
Judah teo pɛ Azaria taane
2 Tigisim 26:1-23
1Isarele teo pɛ Jeroboam paare dim bena finlei-yarepɛ bene dem wone mo Amazia bu Azaria déem di Judah teo paare. 2Azaria déem jege bena fuga-yaredo mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena finnu-yalei. O nu wom yere mo Jekolia ye o nwoŋi Jerusalem. 3O totoŋa déem su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane, nenɛɛne o kwo Amazia na ke tei to. 4De ko de, o wo wane o chɔge wara-jei selo ba na ke kaanem da to. Nɔɔna déem yeini ba ke kaanem de zwɛɛm pɛɛra jei sem konto ne ye ba wo yage.
5 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa se naywaane jaweo kom lɔgese Pɛ Azaria. O dɛ de jaweo kom konto mo o vo o te. O déem zoore sɔŋɔ kolo na ye dáa dáa to wone mo. O bu Jotam ma leiri o nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom de teo kom nɔn-bia baŋa ne o pa‑o.
6Azaria déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o totoŋa yam maama, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 7Azaria ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa bam yibeeli seeni David teo Jerusalem ne. O bu Jotam ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.
Isarele teo pɛ Zekaria taane
8Judah teo pɛ Azaria paare dim bena fintɔ-nana bene dem wone mo Jeroboam bu Zekaria déem di Isarele teo paare. O jeini Samaria ne mo o di paare dem chane seredo. 9O déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga mo nenɛɛne o kwoa bam de na ke tei to. O ma yɔɔre o ke wɛleera dwi delo Nebat bu Jeroboam déem na ke pa se Isarele tiina de da ba ke to.
10Jabese bu Salum déem ke chichuŋu de Zekaria. O ma vo o li‑o Ibeleyam ne de jara o go. O ma daare o leiri o di paare dem. 11Zekaria déem na di paare ye o toŋe wonnu telo maama, to ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 12O toone dem konto ma pa se Baŋa Wɛ kwora kalo o na pɛ Jehu to ji chega, de o na tage o we, “Nmo dwi delo na wó saŋe n kwaga to wó di Isarele teo paare dem se ko taa vei dwia yana wɛɛne.”
Isarele teo pɛ Salum taane
13Judah teo pɛ Yuzia paare dim bena fintɔ-nogo bene dem wone mo Jabese bu Salum déem di Isarele teo paare. O jeini Samaria ne mo o di paare dem chana dedoa yerane. 14Gadi bu Menahem déem zaŋe Tiraza teo ne o vo Samaria. O na yi da to, o ma li Salum de jara o go o daare o leiri o ji pɛ.
15Salum déem na di paare ye o toŋe wonnu telo maama to, de chichuŋu kolo o na ke de Zekaria to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone.
16Menahem déem zege Tiraza ne o vo Tipisa o chɔge teo kom de ko nawuura yam maama, ko nɔn-bia bam na ve se ba sɛ ba pa‑o to ŋwaane. O ta ma lɔ ba kapwi sem ba pwi seeni o go.
Isarele teo pɛ Menahem taane
17Judah teo pɛ Azaria paare dim bena fintɔ-nogo bene dem wone mo Gadi bu Menahem déem di Isarele teo paare. O jeini Samaria ne mo o di paare dem o ke bena fuga. 18O déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. O paare dim maŋa kam maama wone o yɔɔre o ke wɛleera dwi delo Nebat bu Jeroboam déem na ke pa se Isarele tiina de da ba ke to mo.
19Asiria teo pɛ Pulu déem cheiŋi Isarele tega kam mo. Pɛ Menahem ma kwei lu-nyenno na yi ywollu moro dedoa (1,000) to o pa Pɛ Pulu se o ma o kwoori‑o se Pulu woli‑o se o wane o fɔge o di dam Isarele teo kom ne. 20Menahem déem gwoni jene mo o pa Isarele naduna bam maama. O ma fe ba dedoa dedoa se ba ŋwe lu-nyenno sabu-dala finnu. O ma kwei sabu kom o pa Pɛ Pulu pa se o pipiri o viiri o daare Isarele tiina tega kam.
21Menahem déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o totoŋa yam maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 22Menahem ma te ye ba kwei‑o ba suli. O bu Pekahia ma leiri o di paare dem.
Isarele teo pɛ Pekahia taane
23Judah teo pɛ Azaria paare dim bena finnu bene dem wone mo Menahem bu Pekahia déem di Isarele teo paare. O jeini Samaria ne mo o di paare dem bena yalei. 24Pekahia déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. O ma yɔɔre o ke wɛleera dwi delo Nebat bu Jeroboam déem na ke pa se Isarele tiina de da ba ke to. 25Remalia bu Peka déem mo ye Pekahia jar-keira yiga tu wom. O ma kwei Gilead tiina baara finnu o ja o vo Samaria teo o li Pekahia pɛ sɔŋɔ dam jei sem wone de jara o go. O ta ma go Aragobi de Ariyɛ o woli da. O ma daare o leiri o di paare dem.
26Pekahia déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o totoŋa yam maama, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone.
Isarele teo pɛ Peka taane
27Judah teo pɛ Azaria paare dim bena finnu-yalei bene dem wone mo Remalia bu Peka déem di Isarele teo paare. O jeini Samaria ne mo o di paare dem bena finlei. 28O déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. O ma yɔɔre o ke wɛleera dwi delo Nebat bu Jeroboam déem na ke pa se Isarele tiina de da ba ke to.
29Maŋa kalo Peka déem na ye Isarele teo pɛ to, mo Asiria teo pɛ Tigilaf-Pilesa tu o zo tega kam o wane Isarele teene dedwonna o jwoŋi o tei. Teene dem konto déem ye: Yijon, de Abel Bɛte-Maaka, de Janoa, de Kedesa, de Hazora. O déem ta wane Gilead, de Galili, de Nafitali laŋa kam maama. O ma daare o ja jei sem konto nɔn-bia bam o vo o yage Asiria teo ne. 30Konto na ke to, Ela bu Hosea ma vo o ke chichuŋu de Remalia bu Peka. O ma li‑o de jara o go o daare o leiri o di paare dem. Yuzia bu Jotam paare dim bena finlei bene dem wone mo konto.
31Peka déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o totoŋa yam maama, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone.
Judah teo pɛ Jotam taane
32Isarele teo pɛ Peka wolo na ye Remalia bu to paare dim bena yalei bene dem wone mo Yuzia bu Jotam déem di Judah teo paare. 33Jotam déem jege bena finlei-yanu mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem bena fuga-yaredo. O nu wom déem mo ye Zadoki bukɔ Jerusa. 34O totoŋa ma su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane, nenɛɛne o kwo Yuzia déem na ke tei to. 35De ko de, o wo wane o chɔge wara-jei selo ba na ke kaanem da to. Nɔɔna bam déem yeini ba ke kaanem de zwɛɛm pɛɛra jei sem konto ne. Ko ye Jotam mo fɔge o lɔ Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ni delo na wo baŋa seeni to.
36Jotam déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o totoŋa yam maama, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 37Ko ye o paare dim maŋa kam ne mo Baŋa Wɛ bobo se o toŋe Siria teo pɛ Rezin, de Remalia bu Peka se ba li Judah teo de jara. 38Jotam ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa yibeeli ne o nabaaro David teo Jerusalem ne. O bu Ahaz ma leiri o di paare.

english_text:
King Ahaz of Judah
(2 Chronicles 28.1-27)
1Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel. 2He was 20 years old at the time, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years.
Ahaz wasn't like his ancestor David. Instead, he disobeyed the Lord 3 and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 4Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
5-6 While Ahaz was ruling Judah, the king of Edom recaptured the town of Elath from Judah and forced out the people of Judah. Edomites then moved into Elath, and they still live there.
About the same time, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel marched to Jerusalem and attacked, but they could not capture it.
7Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.” 8Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
9As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
10Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one. 11Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
12When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar 13and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings. 14 After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple. 15He told Uriah the priest:
From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
16Uriah did everything Ahaz told him.
17 Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone. 18He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
19Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 20 Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_text:
Judah teo pɛ Ahaz taane
1Remalia bu Peka paare dim bena fuga-yarepɛ bene dem wone mo Jotam bu Ahaz déem di Judah teo paare. 2Ahaz déem jege bena finlei mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena fuga-yaredo. O nam wo toŋe o pwoli o Tu Baŋa Wɛ wo nenɛɛne o nabaaro David na ke tei to. 3O déem tusi de o na kwei Isarele teo pwa bam totoŋ-naga tei to. O ma ja o tete bu o zwɛ o ma o ke kaanem. O keim dem konto bere we o lwoni totoŋ-zɔɔna yalo dwi-gɛ tiina na ke ye Wɛ zeili-ba tega kam ne o daare o pa Isarele tiina bam jeini to mo. 4Ko ná ye wara-jei bimbina yam baŋa ne, de zwonnu tem baŋa ne, de teeni maama kuri ne, o déem yeini o ke kaanem de zwɛɛm pɛɛra mo jei sem konto maama ne.
5Siria teo pɛ Rezin de Isarele teo pɛ Peka déem ma zaŋe ba vo Jerusalem se ba kwaare jara de Judah tiina bam. Ba ma gilimi teo kom ba pu, ye ba wo wane Ahaz ba di. 6Kanto maŋa kam ne mo Siria teo pɛ Rezin déem zeili Judah tiina balo na zoore Elafa ne to o jwoori o ke teo kom o tete nɔɔna jeŋa ne. Edom tiina laam ma vo ba zoore Elafa ne ye ba ta wora de zem maama.
7Pɛ Ahaz ma toŋe o tontoŋena se ba vo ba ta de Asiria teo pɛ Tigilaf-Pilesa we, “Amo ye nmo tontoŋeno mo ye a yɔɔre a sɛ a pa‑m. A nam lwoori‑m se n ba n jwoŋi-ne n yage Siria tiina de Isarele tiina bam jeŋa ne, ba na tu ba li amo de jara to ŋwaane.” 8Ahaz ta ma kwei lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa wonnu telo na wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ne to dedaane telo na wo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wone to o toŋe o pa Asiria pɛ wom. 9Asiria teo pɛ ma sɛ. O ma vo o kwaare jara de Damasika o wane-ko. O ma ja ko nɔn-bia bam o vo o yage Kiri teo ne o daare o go Pɛ Rezin.
10Pɛ Ahaz déem ma vo Damasika se o ware Asiria teo pɛ Tigilaf-Pilesa. O na wo teo kom wone konto to mo o nɛ kaanem bimbini ba na lɔge ba zege da. O ma kwei bimbini dem nyenyego o toŋe o pa Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu Yuria se o wane o lɔre ko na ye tei to chekke. 11Yuria de ma lɔ bimbini dem dwoŋi se de yɔɔre de maŋe de nyenyego kom. O ma lɔ-de o ti ye Ahaz laam zege Damasika ne o jwoori. 12Ahaz na jwoori o ba ye o na bimbini dem to, o ma yi de yera o ke kaanem de baŋa ne. 13O déem ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de wodiu pɛɛra kaanem mo. O ma lwo wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛra o ke da ye o daare o kwei yazura kaanem jana bam o miisi bimbini dem yera ne. 14Ahaz ma le channa kaanem bimbini dem na zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to o ja o nwoŋi Wɛ diga kam ni dem ne. De déem ya zege diga kam ni dem de bimbin-doore dem tetare ne mo. O ma kwei-de o zege bimbin-doore dem baŋa kam seeni. 15O ma ta de Wɛ kaanem tu Yuria o we, “Ko ná ye bimbin-kamunu kolo dé laam na lɔge to, ta‑n ke zezeŋa maama zwɛɛm kaanem, de dedaan-ni maŋa maama wodiu pɛɛra yam de baŋa ne. Ta ke pɛ wom tete zwɛɛm kaanem dem, de o wodiu pɛɛra yam, ko woli de nɔɔna bam maama zwɛɛm kaanem, de ba wodiu pɛɛra, de ba wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛra yam maama bimbin-doore dem baŋa ne. Ta daare n kwei kaanem dem maama jana bam n miisi bimbini dem yera ne. Ko nam ná ye channa bimbini dem, amo wó taa mae dento a fɔge a yiga.” 16Yuria ma seene o ke ne Pɛ Ahaz na tage tei to.
17Pɛ Ahaz déem ma le channa wonnu telo na meeli ware-zwe zegem torokooro tem sɛ sem ne to. O ta ma le ware-zwe sem tete. Ko ná ye channa ware-zon-zɔŋɔ kolo ba na bwoi we ‘Naneo kom’ to, o ta ma zoore-ka ka na zege channa nabɛ selo baŋa ne to. O ma daare o kwei-ka o zege kandwɛ-polɔgɔ baŋa ne. 18Ahaz ta ma gɔ vwei delo ba ya na pugi wara-jei sem ne siu dɛ ŋwaane to. O ta ma daare o se manchwoŋo ni delo ba ya na pore se pɛ wom taa tɔge da o zoore Wɛ diga kam wone to. Ahaz déem ke konto maama se ko pwoli Asiria teo pɛ wom wo mo.
19Ahaz déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o totoŋa yam maama, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 20Ahaz ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa bam yibeeli ne David teo Jerusalem ne. O bu Hezekia ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.

english_text:
King Hoshea of Israel
1Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria. 2Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
3During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes. 4But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison.
Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
5Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years, 6before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
7All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods, 8followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings. 9Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities. 10 They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree. 11They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
12Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway. 13So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
14But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God. 15They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
16 The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal. 17 They used magic and witchcraft and even sacrificed their own children. The Israelites were determined to do whatever the Lord hated. 18The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners.
Only the people living in Judah were left, 19but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites. 20So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
21Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord. 22The people kept on sinning like Jeroboam, 23until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets.
That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained.
Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
24The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
25At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them. 26A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
27The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.” 28One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
29But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines. 30The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima; 31those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech. 32-33They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines. 34 Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel. 35 At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them:
Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice. 36 Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices. 37Never worship any other god, always obey my laws and teachings, 38and remember the solemn agreement between us.
I will say it again: Do not worship any god 39except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
40But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs. 41They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_text:
Isarele teo pɛ Hosea taane
1Judah teo pɛ Ahaz paare dim bena fuga-yalei bene dem wone mo Ela bu Hosea déem di Isarele teo paare. O jeini Samaria ne mo o di paare dem bena nogo. 2Hosea déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. O totoŋ-lwanno tem nam daa wo yi Isarele pwa balo na dɛ yiga ba di paare dem to.
3Asiria teo pɛ Salemanesa déem ma vo o kwaare jara de Isarele teo pɛ Hosea. Konto ŋwaane mo Hosea déem wo o dam kuri ne ye Isarele tiina bam yeini ba ŋwe lampwoo ba pa‑o bene maama wone. 4Asiria pɛ wom déem nam maane we Hosea lɔge o kwaga ne mo de o na toŋe nɔɔna Ejipti teo pɛ Soo tei ne se ba sɔ ni daane to. Hosea ma daare o ve se o daa taa ŋwe lampwoo o pa Asiria pɛ wom, ne o ya na ke tei bene maama wone to. Konto ŋwaane Pɛ Salemanesa ma ja‑o o vo o pe peena diga ne. 5O laam ma vo o li Isarele laŋa kam maama de jara. O ma vo o kaare Samaria teo kom o pu se ko yi bena yatɔ.
6Hosea paare dim bena nogo bene dem wone mo Salemanesa wane o di Samaria teo kom. O ma ja Isarele tiina bam o vo o yage Asiria ne. O jaane ba badwonna o vo o yage Hala ne, de Gozan jei selo na wo Habora buga kam ni ne to. O ta ma ja ba badaara o vo o yage teene delo Media tiina na zoore da to.
Ko na ke tei ye Isarele tiina bam na chɔgem to
7Tento maama déem kea Isarele tiina bam na ke wɛleera ba chɔge ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga to ŋwaane mo. Ko nam ye Baŋa Wɛ mo jaane-ba o nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne mɛ ba ya na wo ko Pa-faro dam kuri ne to. Ba ma yeini ba zuli wa-yɔɔro mo, 8ba daare ba lwoni chullu telo dwi-gɛ tiina na yeini ba ke ye Wɛ zeili-ba tega kam ne o daare o pa Isarele tiina bam jeini to. Ba daa ta ma tɔge keim-balwaaro telo Isarele pwa bam déem na jege ba ke to. 9Isarele tiina bam déem seigi mo ba toŋe lwarem ba chɔge ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga. Ba lɔge wara-jei mo se ba taa maa ke kaanem ba teene maama wone, ko ná maŋe ko ye teo balaŋa de teo kamunu maama wone de. 10Ba déem ta chwi kandwa de Asera nyenyego dɛ ba zege zwonnu maama yuu ne de teeni maama kuri ne se ba taa zuli-te. 11Ba ta ma ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra ba zuli jwona yam, nenɛɛne dwi-gɛ tiina ya na ke tei ye Wɛ zeili-ba tega kam ne o daare o pa Isarele tiina bam jeini to. Konto to, ba déem ke wo-zɔɔna yalo na chuchugi Baŋa Wɛ bane to mo. 12Baŋa Wɛ nam ya pɛ-ba ni o we, ba yé taa zuli jwona. De ko de, ba ta ke konto mo. 13Kuni dedɛ mo Baŋa Wɛ déem tɔge o sampwori de o yi-nara baŋa ne o kaane Isarele tiina bam de Judah tiina bam o we, “Nam yage-na á keim-balwaaro tem, se á daare á sɛ amo ni-kaana yam de a bera yam. Yanto maama ye nia yalo amo déem na pɛ á nabaara bam se ba taa tɔge to mo. A ma daare a tɔge a tontoŋena bam baŋa ne a bere abam de.”
14De ko de, Isarele tiina bam wo sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem. Ba bochara digili mo, ne ba nabaara bam déem na ke tei ye ba ve ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ to. 15Ba déem ve se ba taa tɔge o nia yam, de ni-gwonim delo o na ke de ba nabaara bam to. Ba ma daare ba ve o ni-kaana yam de. Ba ma zuli jwo-yɔɔro pa se ba de ji nɔn-kayɛ. Ba ma lwoni dwi-gɛ tiina balo na gilimi-ba to kikia. Baŋa Wɛ ya maŋe o kaane-ba se ba yé lwoni banto kikia.
16Ba yiga déem tera de ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ nia yam. Ba ma kwei luu ba ma ba mɔ na-mɔre selei kamwaro, ba daare ba ke Asera nyenyego daa se ba zuli-te. Ba ta ma kuni dwoona ba zuli chalechwe sem de Baal jwoni dem. 17Ba déem kwei ba tete bia, bakeiri de bukwa, ba zwɛ ba ma ke kaanem. Ba ta maa yeini ba vei vora de yi-nara tei se ba nii ba yiga ba pa-ba. Ba ma yɔɔre ba yage ba tete se ba taa ke lwarem ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga pa se ba chuchugi o bane.
18 Baŋa Wɛ bane na tiini de zaŋe Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne konto to, o ma zeili-ba o yiga ne. Judah dwi tiina bam yerane mo daare. 19Judah tiina bam de déem wo sɛ ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ nia yam. Ba ma kwei Isarele tiina bam totoŋ-naga ye ba ke lwarem. 20Konto ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ déem mɛ o kwaga o ya Isarele dwi dem maama, ye o daare o pa cham ba ba baŋa ne de ba dona na jege-ba ba bɛɛse tei to. Ko ke konto mo taa ye Baŋa Wɛ laam zeili-ba o yiga ne.
21 Baŋa Wɛ déem na pɔɔre Isarele dwi dem o ja nwoŋi Pɛ David dwi dem jeŋa ne to mo Isarele tiina bam kwei Nebat bu Jeroboam ba tiŋi‑o paare. Jeroboam ma soge Isarele tiina bam pa se ba ywori Baŋa Wɛ chwoŋa kam ne, ye ba fɔge ba zo wɛleera dedɛ wone. 22Ko kwaga ne Isarele tiina yɔɔre ba tɔge wɛleera dwi delo maama Jeroboam na ke to mo. Ba bere ba wo sɛ se ba yage-ya. 23Ba ke konto mo taa ye Baŋa Wɛ laam zeili-ba o yiga ne. O déem maŋe o tɔge o sampwori sem baŋa ne o kaane-ba we, o wó ke konto mo. Mo kokuri Isarele tiina dona bam jaane-ba ba nwoŋi ba tete tega kam ne ba vo Asiria. Dáane mo ba ta wora de zem maama.
Asiria tiina na nɛ jeiŋa jei Samaria ne
24Asiria teo pɛ déem ma ja nɔɔna badwonna ya na zoore Babilon ne, de Kufa ne, de Awa ne, de Hamafa ne, dedaane Sefavayim ne to o ba o yage Samaria ne se banto leiri Isarele tiina bam yuu ne ba taa zoore da. Nɔɔna bam konto ma lɛɛre ba tei Samaria laŋa kam ye ba zoore ka teene dem wone. 25Ba na bobo se ba taa zoore da to, ba wo kɔre Baŋa Wɛ. Baŋa Wɛ ma pa nywonnu zo ba wone pa se te go ba badwonna. 26Nɔɔna ma ta ba bere Asiria teo pɛ ba we, “Nɔɔna bam nmo na jaane n ba n jeini Samaria teene dem wone to yeiri tega kam konto wɛ dem chullu tem. Konto ŋwaane mo wɛ dem konto pɛ se nywonnu zo ba wone ye te go ba badwonna.”
27Asiria pɛ wom ma pa ni dento o we, “Le-na nɔɔno dedoa Samaria kaanem tiina balo dé na jaane dé ba ywo to wone á daare á pa se o jwoori o vo o taa zoore o tete tega kam ne. Kotu laam wó wane o bere nɔɔna bam se ba lɔre tega kam wɛ dem chullu tem na ye tei to.” 28Ba ma seene ba pa Samaria kaanem tiina dedoa jwoori o vo o zoore Bɛtel ne. O ma bere nɔɔna bam ba na wó taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ tei to.
29De ko de, nɔɔna balo na nwoŋi ba teene dwi dwi ba ba Samaria to daa ta mɔɔne ba tete wa kamwaro mo. Ba déem ma kwei-te ba zege wara-jei selo Samaria tiina bam ya na lɔge ba tete jwona yam ŋwaane to. Nɔɔna bam dwi dwi ke konto teo kolo maama ba na zoore da to mo. 30Babilon tiina bam na mɔɔne jwoni delo to yere mo Sukof-Benofi. Kufa tiina bam jwoni dem yere maa ye Nɛgale. Hamafa tiina bam de maa kaane Asima. 31Awa tiina bam maa kaane Nibaza de Tataka jwona yam. Sefavayim tiina bam maa yeini ba zwɛ ba bia ba ma kaane ba jwona Aderamɛlɛka de Anamɛlɛka. 32Nɔɔna bam konto déem kɔre Baŋa Wɛ mo ba woli da. De ko de, ba yeini ba le ba tete dwi wone nɔɔno de nɔɔno mo se ba taa yeini ba ke kaanem wara-jei sem maama ne. 33Konto to, ba déem zuli Baŋa Wɛ ye ba ta vei ba zuli ba tete teene dem jwona, ne ba tete dwi tiina na yeini ba tɔge chullu telo to mo.
34De zem maama, nɔɔna bam ta wo yage ba faŋa chullu tem. Ba ba yɔɔre ba kɔre Baŋa Wɛ. Ba maa ba sɛ Baŋa Wɛ bera yam, de o chullu tem, de o nia yam, ne o déem na kwei o pa Jakob dwi tiina bam se ba taa tɔge to. Jakob yere dem konto mo Baŋa Wɛ déem leiri pa de ji Isarele. 35Baŋa Wɛ déem gwoni ni de Isarele dwi tiina bam, ye o kaane-ba we, “Abam daa á yé zuli-na wa yadwonna á woli amo wone. Á ba jege se á tiiri jwona yiga ne, naa á zuli-ya, naa á kaane-ya. 36Abam nam jege se á ta‑á kɔre Baŋa Wɛ mo, o na tɔge o dam-fɔrɔ baŋa ne o toŋe wo-kamunnu o ma o ja abam o nwoŋi Ejipti wone to ŋwaane. Wonto yerane mo abam wó tiiri o yiga ne á zuli‑o, á daare á ke kaanem á pa‑o. 37Á ta‑á yei se á sɛ o bera yam, de o chullu tem, de o ni-kaana yam, ne o na popone nia yalo o tiŋi o pa abam to. Á ye zaŋe-na á zuli wa-yɔɔro. 38Á nam yé swei a na gwoni ni delo de abam to. Yé kɔre-na wa yadwonna á woli amo wone. 39Á nam jege se á kɔre á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yerane mo. Ko ye wonto mo wó vere abam á dona maama jea ne o yage.”
40Nɔɔna bam nam wo sɛ Wɛ ni dem konto, ye ba ta ke ne ba na maŋe ba ke tei faŋa to. 41Dwi-gɛ tiina bam konto déem yeini ba kɔre Baŋa Wɛ ye ba ta zuli ba jwona kamwaro tem de mo. De zem maama ba dwi dem ta ke konto mo, ne ba nabaara bam de ya na ke tei to.

english_text:
King Hezekiah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 29.1,2; 31.1)
1Hezekiah son of Ahaz became king of Judah in the third year of Hoshea's rule in Israel. 2Hezekiah was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem. His mother Abi was the daughter of Zechariah.
3Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done. 4 He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
5Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him. 6He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people. 7The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant. 8Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
9During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked 10and captured it three years later, in the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule and the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. 11The king of Assyria took the Israelites away as prisoners; he forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived. 12All of that happened because the people of Israel had not obeyed the Lord their God. They rejected the solemn agreement he had made with them, and they ignored everything that the Lord's servant Moses had told them.
King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah
(2 Chronicles 32.1-19; Isaiah 36.1-22)
13 In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem. 14Hezekiah sent this message to Sennacherib, who was in the town of Lachish: “I know I am guilty of rebellion. But I will pay you whatever you want, if you stop your attack.”
Sennacherib told Hezekiah to pay ten tons of silver and one ton of gold. 15So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury. 16He even stripped the gold that he had used to cover the doors and doorposts in the temple. He gave it all to Sennacherib.
17The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool. 18They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
19One of the Assyrian commanders told them:
I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself. 20Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria? 21Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
22Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
23The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people. He will give you 2,000 horses, if you have enough troops to ride them. 24How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry? 25Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
26Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
27The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you.”
28Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew:
Listen to what the great king of Assyria says! 29Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you. 30Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria. 31Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns 32for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there.
Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him. 33Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria? 34What happened to the gods of Hamath and Arpad? What about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces? 35None of these gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord your God can do any better?
36-37Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_text:
Judah teo pɛ Hezekia taane
1Isarele teo pɛ Ela bu Hosea paare dim bena yatɔ bene dem wone mo Ahaz bu Hezekia déem di Judah teo paare. 2Hezekia déem jege bena finlei-yanu mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena finlei-nogo. O nu wom déem ye Zekaria bukɔ Abija mo. 3O totoŋa ma su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane, nenɛɛne o nabaaro David déem na ke tei to. 4O déem yɔɔre o chɔge wara-jei bimbina yam mo o dole o yage. O ta ma guri kandwa yalo ba ya na chugi ba jege ba kaane to o chochoge, o daare o gwoni Asera nyenyego dɛ sem o de tega ne. Ko ta ná ye channa basankwea kalo Moses déem na mɔɔne o zege to, o ma chochoge-ka bɛŋwaane Isarele tiina bam yeini ba ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra mo ba ma kaane-ka. Ba déem pɛ ko yere we ‘Nehusitan’ mo.
5Hezekia déem pɛ Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to chega. Judah teo pwa balo maama ya na dɛ yiga ba ba to, de balo na saŋe o kwaga ba ba to maama wone, pɛ tera o na nye de wonto. 6O ma yɔɔre o sale Baŋa Wɛ yera ne, ye o wo ywori o chwei sem ne. O déem tɔge Baŋa Wɛ nia yalo o na pɛ Moses to chekke. 7Baŋa Wɛ de maa wo Hezekia tei ne, pa se o na yiga-veiŋa o totoŋa maama wone. O ma lɔ Asiria teo pɛ kwaga ne, ye o wo sɛ o pa‑o. 8O déem wane Filisi tiina bam o di. O wane ba teene dem, ko ná maŋe ko ye teo balaŋa de teo kamunu maama de, o kɛ o vo yiga yiga o yi Gaza de ko kateira yam.
9Hezekia paare dim bena yana bene dem wone mo Asiria teo pɛ Salemanesa de o jar-keira vei ba li Samaria teo kom ba ba pu de jara. Isarele teo pɛ Ela bu Hosea paare dim bena yarepɛ bene dem wone mo konto. 10Bena yatɔ na kɛ to, Asiria jar-keira bam ma lɛɛre ba jwoŋi teo kom ba tei. Hezekia paare dim bena yaredo bene dem wone mo konto, ye ko ta ye Isarele teo pɛ Hosea paare dim bena nogo bene dem wone. 11Asiria teo pɛ ma le Isarele tiina bam o ja o vo o yage Hala ne, de Gozan jei selo na wo Habora buga kam ni ne to, dedaane teene delo Media tiina na zoore da to. 12Tento maama déem ke Isarele tiina bam, ba na wo sɛ ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam to ŋwaane mo. Ba ma chɔge ni delo o na gwoni de-ba to. Ba maa wo sɛ nia yalo Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses déem na kwei o pa-ba to. Ba bere ba wo cheigi-ya. Ba maa wo sɛ se ba tɔge-ya de.
Asiria teo pɛ ke chichuŋu de Judah tiina
13Pɛ Hezekia paare dim bena fuga-yana bene dem wone mo Asiria teo pɛ Senakeribi tu o li Judah te-kamunnu telo na fɔge te pe to maama de jara. O ma wane-ba o di. 14Judah teo pɛ Hezekia ma toŋe kwora o pa Asiria pɛ wom Lakisi teo ne ye o we, “Amo toŋe a tusi nmo yiga ne. Konto ŋwaane amo wó ŋwe lampwoo kolo maama nmo na boŋe we ko maŋe to a pa‑m. Nam yage jara yam n daare n viiri.” Asiria pɛ wom ma ta se Hezekia ŋwe lu-nyenno dunni na yi kilo morro fuga (10,000) to, de sabu-seŋa kilo moro dedoa (1,000) o pa‑o. 15Hezekia ma la lu-nyenno wonnu telo maama na wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ne to, ko woli de telo ba ya na tiŋi pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wone to o kwei o pa Asiria pɛ wom.
16Kanto maŋa kam ne, Hezekia ta ma le sabu-seŋa kalo o ya na mɛ o taare Baŋa Wɛ diga kam bworru tem de ka ywoa yam to o kwei ka maama o pa Asiria pɛ wom. 17Asiria pɛ wom ma toŋe o jar-keira yuu tu de o dedɛɛra balei se ba zege Lakisi ne ba nwoŋi de jar-keira kɔgɔ dedɛ ba vo Jerusalem ba gware Hezekia. Ba na yi da to, ba ma vo ba zege na-fera kalo na zoore baŋa seeni chɔgɔ kom to ni ne. Jeiga kam konto bwola de chwoŋa kalo ba na zare gwaaro ka ni ne to mo. 18Dedɛɛra bam ma toŋe ba bwoŋi Pɛ Hezekia. Pɛ wom de ma toŋe Hilikia bu Eliakim na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom totoŋa baŋa ne to, dedaane Sebena na ye tɔn-poponno to, ko woli de Asaf bu Joa na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom yera seina twanno baŋa ne to, se ba nwoŋi teo kom wone ba vo ba jeeri-ba.
19Ba na jeeri to mo Asiria teo pɛ dedɛɛra yiga tu wom taga de-ba se ba ja Asiria pɛ wom kwora ba vo ba ta de Pɛ Hezekia. O maa we:
“Asiria Pa-faro wom we: Bɛ mo bere ko pa se n jege n tete chega konto? 20Nmo boŋe we ni-wɛɛle wae jara de ke mo na? Wɔ baŋa ne mo n teege ye n lɔ amo kwaga ne? 21Nmo teena wo Ejipti teo ne mo na? Konto nam nye de nɔɔno na kwei kasogo o ji o nacheiga to mo. Kasogo kom wó seere mo ka zɔ wolo maama na zei-ka to jeŋa. Konto mo wó ke wolo maama na sale Ejipti Pa-faro wom yera ne to. 22Nmo nam ta ná we, ‘Dé wó sale debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ yera ne mo,’ ko dae Wɛ dem konto wara-jei de kaanem bimbina mo Hezekia guri o yage o daare o pa ni se Jerusalem de Judah nɔɔna maama taa tui bimbini dem na wo Jerusalem ne ywo-seeni to yerane ba zuli‑o na?
23Amo lage a ma a tu wom yere mo a ke ni dedaane nmo Hezekia. Amo wó pa‑m sisein-nɔɔna morro telei, ne nmo ná wó wane n na se dira bam n ke da. 24Nii amo wolo na ye a pɛ wom nabwom to na jege dam delo to. Nmo wó wane-ne n ve n daare n ke n teena de Ejipti tiina mo we ba wó woli‑m de ba jara-keim torokooro de ba sisein-dira na? 25Ko dae Baŋa Wɛ mo toŋe-ne se a ba ywo a wane n teo kom na? Ko seene ko ye Baŋa Wɛ tete mo pɛ-ne ni se a li teo kom de jara a daare chɔge-ko.”
26Eliakim, de Sebena, dedaane Joa maama ma ta de Asiria teo dedɛɛra yiga tu wom ba we, “Popo ŋɔɔne Aram tiina taane de debam, se dé wó ni. Nmo ná ŋɔɔne de Judah tiina taane dem, balo na dɔge kabira kam yuu ne ba cheigi to wó da ba ni n na tɛ kolo to mo.” 27Asiria teo yiga tu wom ma leiri-ba o we, “Á boŋe we amo tu kwora kam wora ka pa abam de á pɛ wom yerane mo na? Ko ye balo maama na dɔge kabira kam baŋa ne to de nyem mo. Banto de wó da ba di ba beinnu ba daare ba nyɔ ba fea ne abam na jege se á ke tei to mo.”
28Asiria yiga tu wom ma tɔɔle o yage de Judah tiina taane dem o we:
“Abam maama cheigi-na Asiria teo pa-faro wom kwora kam. 29Pɛ wom we: Yé sɛ-na se Hezekia taa jege abam o gana, se o bá wane abam o jwoŋi o yage amo jeŋa ne. 30Nam yé pa-na se á pɛ wom gane abam se á ke á wo-dedoa de Baŋa Wɛ. O ná tage de abam we, Baŋa Wɛ wó jwoŋi abam o yage ye o che se Asiria teo pɛ yé di á teo kom, nam yé sɛ-na. 31Yé cheigi-na Hezekia taane kɔtaa. Asiria pɛ wom nam na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Abam maama jege se á nwoŋi á teo kom wone se á daare á to á pa-ne. Á ná ke konto, á wó na chwoŋa se á ta‑á jei yɔlɔ-lɔ-lɔ ye á di á tete Vini teeni de á kaporro tem nyɔɔre. Á ta maa wó nyɔ á vola na bam á ni ywoni. 32Konto kwaga ne, amo ta wó ja abam a vo a yage tega kalo na nye de abam tete tega kam to baŋa ne. Dáane Vini teeni wora se á na sana á nyɔ, de mena se á ma á ke bworobworo. Olivi teeni nuga, dedaane tooro dedɛ de maa wo dáane. Kuri-na ŋwea á leiri toone yuu ne! Yé cheigi-na pɛ Hezekia taane dem, de o na gane abam ye o we, Baŋa Wɛ wó jwoŋi abam o yage to. 33Teo kɔ tete jwona mo dana pa se ya wane ya jwoŋi ya teene ya yage Asiria pa-faro wom jeŋa ne? 34Hamafa, de Arapade jwona yam bɛ? Sefavayim, de Hena, dedaane Ivaa jwona yam de nam wo yei ne mo? Ya wane ya vere Samaria tiina ya yage a dam kuri ne na? 35Teene dem maama jwona yam wone, jwoni dɔ mo wane de jwoŋi de teo de yage amo jeŋa ne? Baŋa Wɛ de nam bá wane o vere Jerusalem o yage amo jeŋa ne.’ ”
36Jerusalem teo nɔɔna bam ma maŋe da chemm, ba wo leiri o taane dem, kokuri to, Pɛ Hezekia ya pɛ-ba ni mo o we, “Yé leiri-o-na.” 37Hilikia bu Eliakim na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom totoŋa baŋa ne to, de Sebena na ye tɔn-poponno to, dedaane Asaf bu Joa na tiŋi pɛ sɔŋɔ kom yera seina twanno tem to maama ma ja ba gwaaro ba kaare wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane, ye ba ja kwora kalo Asiria teo dedɛɛra yiga tu wom na taga to ba vo ba ta de Pɛ Hezekia.

english_text:
Hezekiah Asks Isaiah the Prophet for Advice
(Isaiah 37.1-13)
1As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord. 2He told Prime Minister Eliakim, Assistant Prime Minister Shebna, and the senior priests to dress in sackcloth and tell the prophet Isaiah:
3These are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born. 4Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
5When these leaders went to Isaiah, 6he told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah:
I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria. 7I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
8Meanwhile, the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
9About this same time the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
10Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me. 11You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe? 12The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them? 13The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared.
Hezekiah Prays
(Isaiah 37.14-20)
14After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see. 15 He prayed:
Lord God of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world. 16But just look how Sennacherib has insulted you, the living God.
17It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts. 18They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped. 19But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only God.
The Lord's Answer to Hezekiah
(Isaiah 37.21-35)
20Isaiah went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said:
Hezekiah, I heard your prayer about King Sennacherib of Assyria. 21Now this is what I say to that king:
The people of Jerusalem
hate and make fun of you;
they laugh
behind your back.
22Sennacherib, you cursed,
shouted, and sneered at me,
the holy God of Israel.
23You let your officials
insult me, the Lord.
And this is how you
bragged about yourself:
“I led my chariots
to the highest heights
of Lebanon's mountains.
I went deep into its forest,
cutting down the best cedar
and cypress trees.
24I dried up every stream
in the land of Egypt,
and I drank water
from wells I had dug.”
25Sennacherib, now listen
to me, the Lord.
I planned all this long ago.
And you don't even realize
that I alone am the one
who decided that you
would do these things.
I let you make ruins
of fortified cities.
26Their people became weak,
terribly confused.
They were like wild flowers
or tender young grass
growing on a flat roof,
scorched before it matures.
27I know all about you,
even how fiercely angry
you are with me.
28I have seen your pride
and the tremendous hatred
you have for me.
Now I will put a hook
in your nose,
a bit in your mouth,
then I will send you back
to where you came from.
29Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest. 30Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit. 31I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
32I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack. 33As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem. 34I will protect it for myself and for my servant David.
The Death of King Sennacherib
(Isaiah 37.36-38)
35 That same night the Lord sent an angel to the camp of the Assyrians, and he killed 185,000 of them. And so the next morning, the camp was full of dead bodies. 36After this King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh. 37One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_text:
Hezekia lwoori wolim Baŋa Wɛ tei ne
Izaya 37:1-7
1Pɛ Hezekia déem na nigi kwora kam to, o wo ma tiini ko chɔge ye o kaare o gwaaro. O ma daare o kwei gare-nyenyaaro o zo ye o vo o zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam. 2O ma toŋe Eliakim na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom totoŋa baŋa ne to, de Sebena na ye tɔn-poponno to, dedaane Wɛ kaanem yiga tiina bam se ba zo gare-nyenyaaro ba vo Amozi bu Izaya na ye Wɛ sampwora to tei. 3Ba ma vo ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Hezekia na tage tei to mo tento: Dé zem jege lɛɛro de chaveera mo dé di. Ko tiini ko ye kuri-nɔrɔ mo de yera ne. Dé nye de kaane na virigi puga se o lo ye dam tere o yera ne se o lo bu wom to mo. 4Asiria teo pɛ wom mo toŋe o dedɛɛra yiga tu se o ba o twe Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Dɛ delo tento nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ nigi toro tem konto maama, ye o nam wó bwɛ dedɛɛro wom de o ta-balɔrɔ kom. Nam lwoori Wɛ n pa debam balo fee na daare de maŋe teo kom ne to.”
5Hezekia tontoŋena bam na pɛ Izaya kwora kam ba ti to, 6mo Izaya de kwei kwora o pa-ba o we, “Jwoori-na á vo á ta de Pɛ Hezekia we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Yé ta‑n kɔre foone de taane delo Asiria pɛ na tɔge o tontoŋena bam baŋa ne o ma o twe-ne to. 7Nii mo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se Asiria pɛ wom boboŋa vugimi pa se o ni sawea ye o da ka ŋwaane o jwoori o tete teo. Dáane mo ba wó zɔ‑o de se-zɔɔ ba go.’ ”
Asiria pɛ Senakeribi chichuŋu belei tu
8Asiria teo dedɛɛra yiga tu wom déem nigi we ba pɛ wom yage Lakisi teo ye o vo se o kwaare jara de Libina teo tiina. O de ma kɛ o vo dáane. 9Maŋa kam konto ne de, Asiria teo Pɛ Senakeribi ta nigi kwora we Tirahaka na ye Kusi teo pɛ to mo beene se o jeeri‑o de jara. O ma toŋe nɔɔna Hezekia tei ne de kwora kanto o we:
10“Ta-na de Judah teo pɛ Hezekia we, ‘Yé pa wɛ delo n na pɛ-de chega to taa jege‑m de gane we, Jerusalem teo bá fɔge ko zo Asiria teo pɛ jeŋa ne. 11Nmo maŋe n ni Asiria teo pwa bam na toŋe tei de logo baŋa teene maama to. Ba yɔɔre ba chɔge de maama mo. Nmo nam boŋe tetɛ mo ye n teene se n lu? 12Teene dedwonna dem jwona wane-de ya jwoŋi ya yage amo nabaara bam jeŋa ne na? A nabaara bam nam chɔge Gozan, de Haran, de Rezefe, de Eden tiina balo déem na zoore Telasara ne to ba ti. 13Ko ta ná ye Hamafa, de Arapade, de Sefavayim, de Hena, de Ivaa, teene dento pwa bam de wora na?’ ”
Hezekia wɛ-lworo kom
14Hezekia ma jwoŋi tɔnɔ kom Asiria teo pɛ tontoŋena bam tei ne, ye o ga-ko. O ma ja-ko o zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone o kwei o jare Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. 15Hezekia ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to, nmo paare di cherubi sem tetare laŋa ne mo. Nmo yerane mo ye Wɛ, ye n tei tega baŋa paare dim jei maama. Nmo nam mo naane wɛyuu de tega baŋa. 16Baŋa Wɛ, nam pore n zwa se n cheigi! Ta puri n yia se n nii n na kolo na ke debam to. Cheigi ta-kwogila yalo Senakeribi na toŋe o ma o twe nmo Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ to. 17Baŋa Wɛ, ko ye chega mo we Asiria teo pwa déem seene ba chɔge teene de de nɔn-bia dedɛ, pa se de ji di-dwonnu yerane. 18Ba ma dole teene dem konto jwona ba de mini wone ba zwɛ-ya. Kokuri to, ba wa yam dae wa chekke. Nabiina mo boŋe ba ja ye ba kwei dɛ de kandwa ba ke-ya. Konto ŋwaane mo ya nɛ chɔgem. 19Konto to, dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ, yɔɔre n jwoŋi debam n yage Asiria teo pɛ jeŋa ne se logo baŋa teene dem maama lɔre we nmo Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo ye Wɛ.”
Izaya na leiri pɛ wom tei to
Izaya 37:21-28
20Amozi bu Izaya ma toŋe kwora Pɛ Hezekia tei ne ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: Nmo na lwoori amo tei se ko vo Asiria teo pɛ Senakeribi seeni to, a sɛ n wɛ-lworo kom. 21Kwora kanto mo Baŋa Wɛ jege se o pa‑o:
Zion tiina bam yɔɔre ba neese nmo mo.
Jerusalem teo tiina bam jege‑m mo ba mɔna.
22Wɔ mo nmo twe
ye n daare n lwɛ konto?
Wɔ yiga ne mo n zege n nye baare
ye n daare n bere n tete konto dwoŋi?
Ko ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom mo.
23Nmo tɔge n tontoŋena baŋa ne mo n twe amo.
Nmo ta ma‑n bere n tete n we,
‘Amo pɛ se a sisei-torokooro dedɛ
mo di peero tem yuu
te yi Lebanon peero tem yuu chekke.
A ta ma gwoni ba tei-dedwaaro tem a de tega ne,
de ba tei-ŋonno tem maama.
A ma vo a yi yiga yiga
a zo ba goa mɛ na lini to wone.
24Amo ta ma vo a ko vola
sa-teene ne yiga yiga,
ye a nyɔ na ya wone.
A jar-keira bam ma nɔne
Ejipti bwi sem de ba napera pa se we.’
25Nmo wo nigi we amo maŋe
a boŋe boboŋe dem faŋa faŋa mo na?,
A na boŋe tei faŋa faŋa konto to
mo amo laam pɛ se ko seene ko ke.
A boboŋa déem jaane
se nmo zaŋe n chɔge teene
delo ya na lɔge de pe to
se de ji kandwa na dogele da-baŋa ne ya tigi to mo.
26A ta pɛ se teene dem konto
nɔn-bia bam dam ti,
ye ba di ba chaveera nmo ŋwaane.
Banto jigi ne ga-punnu
de ga-lɛɛro nmo yiga ne.
Ba maa nye de gaao na wora
ko tae ko nwoŋi to mo,
ye wea laam mage-ko
pa se ko te lela.
27Amo nam yei nmo kuri maama.
A ta yei n na-veili maama ni ne,
de ni-wɛɛle delo n na jege n ke de amo to ni ne.
28Amo laam lage a waare‑m mo
n na jege ni-wɛɛle delo
n ke de amo to ŋwaane.
N yi-dɛɛre kikia yam to amo zwa ne.
Mo kokuri amo wó lei gwola
n momwɛ ne,
ye a daare a ke gara n ni ne.
A laam maa wó vaŋe‑m se n tɔge
chwoŋa kalo n na tɔge da n ba to
n jwoori n tete teo.”
29Izaya laam ma ta de Hezekia o we:
“Keim dento mo wó ke de pa‑m: Dɔɔm bene dem ne, á wó di wodiiru telo na ke te tete ne to. Bene delo na saŋe-de to ne, á wó di kolo na tage ko nwoŋi boboa nyem kom yera ne to. Ko daare bena yatɔ bene dem ne, abam wó du wodiiru ye á pe-te. Á ta wó jeiri Vini teeni ye á daare á di de wo-bia bam. 30Judah dwi tiina balo ta na daare to laam wó taa ye ne tio bonno na jaane tega ye ko nɛ sem leiri bia to mo. 31Kokuri to, Jerusalem teo tiina ta wó daare. Chega to, balo na zoore Zion peo kom baŋa ne to badaara wó lu toone wone. Baŋa Wɛ tete nam wó pa se wonnu tento maama ke, o na seene yia o nii o nɔɔna baŋa ne to ŋwaane.”
32Izaya ta ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage Asiria teo pɛ yera taane tei to mo tento:
O bá na chwoŋa se o zo teo konto wone. O jar-keira bam bá ta che-tɛɛre ywo-seeni, de dedoa de! Ba bá kwei ba jara nantana ba nwoŋi se ba ke chichuŋu de teo kom, naa ba lɔ taara ba yeiri teo kom kabiri sem teiŋa ne. 33Asiria pɛ na tɔge chwoŋa kalo o ba to mo o wó tɔge da o jwoori, se o bá zo teo konto wone. 34Amo tete yere dem zula ŋwaane, de a tontoŋeno David ŋwaane, a wó taa kwoli teo konto se kolokolo yé wane-ko ko chɔge. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.”
Pɛ Senakeribi toone
35Tete dem konto ne Baŋa Wɛ maleka déem ma zaŋe ka vo Asiria jar-keira bam na tigisi mɛ to. Ka ma go Asiria tiina morro bi de funɔnɔ-banu (185,000). Tega na poore to, ba ma na we ba jei sem su de twa yerane mo. 36Konto baŋa ne mo Senakeribi pɛ o jar-keira bam yage jara yam keim, ye o jwoori o kɛ o vo o tete teo. O laam ma vo o zoore Ninevɛ teo ne.
37Dɛ dedwe, o déem ma zo o jwoni Nisiroka diga kam se o zuli-de. O bia balei Aderamɛlɛka, de Sarezera ma zo ba zage‑o ba go de se-zɔɔro. Ba ma duri ba vo Ararati laŋa kam ba zoore da. Senakeribi bu Esara-hadon déem ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.

english_text:
Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies
(2 Chronicles 32.24-26; Isaiah 38.1-8,21,22)
1About this time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. Isaiah the prophet went in and told him, “The Lord says you won't ever get well. You are going to die, so you had better start doing what needs to be done.”
2Hezekiah turned toward the wall and prayed, 3“Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried bitterly.
4Before Isaiah got to the middle court of the palace, 5the Lord sent him back to Hezekiah with this message:
Hezekiah, you are the ruler of my people, and I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will heal you, so that three days from now you will be able to worship in my temple. 6I will let you live 15 years more, while I protect you and your city from the king of Assyria. I will defend this city as an honor to me and to my servant David.
7Then Isaiah said to the king's servants, “Bring some mashed figs and place them on the king's open sore. He will then get well.”
8Hezekiah asked Isaiah, “Can you prove that the Lord will heal me, so that I can worship in his temple in three days?”
9Isaiah replied, “The Lord will prove to you that he will keep his promise. Will the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?”
10“It's normal for the sun to go forward,” Hezekiah answered. “But how can it go back?”
11Isaiah prayed, and the Lord made the shadow go back ten steps on the stairway built for King Ahaz.
The Lord Is Still with Hezekiah
(Isaiah 39.1-8)
12Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah had been sick, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him. 13Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
14Isaiah asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?”
“They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
15“What did you show them?” Isaiah asked.
Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
16Then Isaiah told Hezekiah:
I have a message for you from the Lord. 17 One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left. 18 Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
19Hezekiah thought, “At least our nation will be at peace for a while.” So he told Isaiah, “The message you brought me from the Lord is good.”
Hezekiah Dies
(2 Chronicles 32.32,33)
20Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he made the upper pool and tunnel bring water into Jerusalem, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 21Hezekiah died, and his son Manasseh became king.
translation_text:
Hezekia weele ye o jwoori o zaŋe
Izaya 38:1-8, 21-22; 2 Tigisim 32:24-26
1Da yam konto ne, Hezekia déem yɔɔre o weele mo ye o bwola de toone. Wɛ sampwora Izaya na ye Amozi bu to ma vo o tei ye o ta‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Bere n sɔŋɔ tiina bam ba na wó ke tei ne n ná tera. Kokuri to, n lage n te mo, n bá‑n wori de n jaweo kom.”
2Hezekia na nigi konto to, mo o pipiri o yibia o jeeri kabira kam ye o lwoori Wɛ o we, 3“Baŋa Wɛ, guli we amo yeini a tɔge‑m de a chega maama dedaane a wo maama mo. A ma yɔɔre a ke kolo nmo na laga se a ke to.” Hezekia ma tiini o keeri dedɛ.
4Se Izaya laam yage pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom to mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi‑o we:
5“Jwoori n vo n ta de a nɔɔna bam yuu tu Hezekia we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye n kwo David Wɛ to mo tage o we: A nigi n wɛ-lworo kom, ye a ta na n na kane yi-na tei to. Amo wó pa‑m yazura. Da yatɔ dɛ ne nmo wó vo Baŋa Wɛ sɔŋɔ kom n zuli-ne. 6A nam lage a woli bena fuga-yanu mo n bena yam wone. A ta wó jwoŋi nmo de Jerusalem teo konto a yage Asiria teo pɛ wom jeŋa ne, se a daare a taa kwoli teo konto amo tete yere de David yere zula ŋwaane.’ ”
7Izaya ma ta de Hezekia o we, “Zɔ mɔɔro se n kwei-te n taare n ŋɔn-pwona kam, se n wó na yazura.”
8Hezekia ma ta de Izaya o we, “Keim dɔ mo wó ke se ko bere we Baŋa Wɛ wó seene o pa-ne yazura se a wane a vo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam a zuli‑o da yatɔ dɛ ne?” 9Izaya ma leiri o we, “Keim dento nam mo wó pa n lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ wó seene o ke o na gwoni ni se o ke tei to. Nmo laga se luluŋu kom fɔɔre ko vo yiga naba-laara yia fuga mo naa n laga se ko fɔɔre ko jwoori kwaga kuni fuga mo?”
10Hezekia ma leiri o we, “Ko ye mɔle se luluŋu kom fɔɔre ko vo yiga naba-laara yia fuga. Laam nam pa se ko jwoori kwaga naba-laara yia fuga.” 11Izaya ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o ke konto. Wɛ ma seene o pa se nateini dem luluŋu kom jwoori kwaga naba-laara yia fuga.
Ba zege Babilon ne ba toŋe nɔɔna
Izaya 39:1-8
12Ko maŋe de maŋa kam konto ne, Merodaki-Baladan laam mo jigi Babilon teo pɛ. O na nigi we Hezekia ya weele to, mo o toŋe nɔɔna o tei ne, de twanno, de pɛɛra. 13Hezekia déem ma jeeri nɔɔna bam de wopwolo. O ma ja-ba o zo o jejegero tem na tigi mɛ to. O laam ma bere-ba o lu-nyenno tem maama, de o sabu-seŋa, de o talwoŋ-ywei sem, de o nu-ŋoŋa kam, de o jara zela yam, de kolo maama ba na tiŋi jejegero di sem wone to. Pɛ Hezekia déem wo daare kolokolo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne, naa o paare dim jei sem maama ne ye o wo kwei o bere-ba.
14Wɛ sampwora Izaya déem ma vo Hezekia tei ye o bwei‑o o we, “Nɔɔna banto nwoŋi yein-seeni mo ba ba nmo tei? Ba nam tage bɛ mo de nmo?” Hezekia ma leiri o we, “Ba nwoŋi Babilon teo yiga yiga mo ba ba.” 15Izaya daa ma bwei o we, “Bɛ mo ba nii ba na n sɔŋɔ kom wone?” Hezekia ma leiri o we, “Amo bere-ba wonnu telo maama na tigi a jejegero di sem wone to mo. Kolokolo wo daare ye a wo bere-ba.”
16Izaya de ma ta de Pɛ Hezekia o we, “Nam cheigi Baŋa Wɛ na jege kwora kalo se o pa‑m to: 17Ta‑n yei we maŋa lage ka yi se Babilon teo tiina ba ba pɛ jejegero telo maama na tigi n sɔŋɔ kom wone to, de telo n nabaara bam na yaare ba la ba tiŋi to ba ja ba vo ba tete teo kom. Kolokolo daa bá daare ko pa abam. Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo konto. 18Nmo tete dwi dem de wó tɔge ba woli da. Ba nam ná jaane-ba ba yi da, ba wó lwe n bia bam mo se ba taa toŋe Babilon teo pɛ sɔŋɔ ne.”
19Hezekia na nigi konto to mo o tage de Izaya o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑m kwora kalo se n pa-ne to lana.” Kokuri to o boŋe o tete ne o we, “Ko ná ke konto, cham bá yi debam amo paare dim maŋa kam ne, ye a nɔɔna wó taa zoore de bochare-zuru.”
Hezekia toone
20Hezekia déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o totoŋ-kamuna yam maama, ko woli de o na koge chɔgɔ ye o ke na-fera pa teo kom nɔɔna wae ba mɔɔne na to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 21Hezekia ma te ye o bu Manasɛ leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.

english_text:
King Manasseh of Judah
(2 Chronicles 33.1-20)
1Manasseh was 12 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 55 years from Jerusalem. His mother was Hephzibah. 2 Manasseh disobeyed the Lord by following the disgusting customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 3He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah, just as King Ahab of Israel had done. And he faithfully worshiped the stars in heaven.
4 In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods 5and the stars. He placed these altars in both courts of the temple, 6-7 and even set up the pole for Asherah there. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own son. He did many sinful things and made the Lord very angry.
Years ago the Lord had told David and his son Solomon:
Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there I will be worshiped forever. 8If my people will faithfully obey all the commands in the Law of my servant Moses, I will never make them leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
9But the people of Judah disobeyed the Lord. They listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
10One day the Lord said to some of his prophets:
11King Manasseh has done more disgusting things than the Amorites, and he has led my people to sin by forcing them to worship his idols. 12Now I, the Lord God of Israel, will destroy both Jerusalem and Judah! People will hear about it but won't believe it. 13Jerusalem is as sinful as Ahab and the people of Samaria were. So I will wipe out Jerusalem and be done with it, just as someone wipes water off a plate and turns it over to dry.
14I will even get rid of my people who survive. They will be defeated and robbed by their enemies. 15My people have done what I hate and have not stopped making me angry since their ancestors left Egypt.
16Manasseh was guilty of causing the people of Judah to sin and disobey the Lord. He also refused to protect innocent people—he even let so many of them be killed that their blood filled the streets of Jerusalem.
17Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his terrible sins, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 18He died and was buried in Uzza Garden near his palace, and his son Amon became king.
King Amon of Judah
(2 Chronicles 33.21-25)
19Amon was 22 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 2 years. His mother Meshullemeth was the daughter of Haruz from Jotbah. 20Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done. 21Amon worshiped the idols Manasseh had made and 22refused to be faithful to the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
23Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace. 24-26He was buried in Uzza Garden. Soon after that, the people of Judah killed the murderers of Amon, then they made his son Josiah king.
Everything else Amon did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_text:
Judah teo Pɛ Manasɛ taane
1Manasɛ déem jege bena fuga-yalei mo ye o di paare dem. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare o ke bena finnu-yanu. O nu yere mo Hefiziba. 2Manasɛ déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga de o na lwoni totoŋ-zɔɔna yalo dwi-gɛ tiina na yeini ba ke ye Wɛ zeili-ba tega kam ne o daare o pa Isarele tiina bam jeini to. 3O jwoori o lɔ jwona kaanem jei selo o kwo Hezekia déem na chochoge o yage to mo o zege. O ma lɔ bimbina o zege Baal jwoni zula ŋwaane o daare o chwi Asera nyenyego daa nenɛɛne Isarele teo pɛ Ahab déem na ke tei to. O ma tiiri o zuli chalechwe sem de. 4O déem ta lɔge jwona kaanem bimbina mo o zege Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ne. Baŋa Wɛ ya tage jeiga kam konto taane mo we, “Jerusalem ye teo kolo wone nɔɔna na wó taa zuli a yere da to mo.” 5O ta lɔge bimbina mo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam konkwallo telei tem wone se nɔɔna taa mae ba zuli chalechwe sem. 6O ma ja o tete bu o zwɛ mini wone o ma o ke kaanem. O ma ke vora, de yi-nara totoŋa, o ta tɔge chichiri vora, de liri-mwa tiina kwaga. O déem tiini o toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga pa se Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe ded‑o.
7Manasɛ déem pɛ ba sare Asera nyenyego daa mo ye o kwei-ka o zege Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne o jege o kaana. Baŋa Wɛ déem taga jei sem konto taane de David, de o bu Solomon o we, “Diga kanto na zege Jerusalem ne to mo ye jeiga kalo amo na kuri Isarele dwia yam maama wone se nɔɔna taa zuli amo yere da se ko taa vei wuu. 8Isarele tiina bam ná yɔɔre ba tɔge bera yalo a na pɛ-ba to, ye ba sɛ nia yalo a na tɔge Moses baŋa a pa-ba to maama, amo bá pa chwoŋa se nɔɔna zeili-ba se ba nwoŋi da tega kalo amo na pɛ ba nabaara bam to.” 9Judah dwi tiina bam nam wo sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem. Manasɛ ma ja-ba o vo o de tusim wone. Ba ma tiini ba toŋe lwarem se ko dwoni lwarem delo dwi-gɛ tiina na yeini ba ke ye Wɛ chɔge-ba o daare o kwei ba tega kam o pa Isarele tiina bam to.
10 Baŋa Wɛ ma tɔge o sampwori sem baŋa o ta o we, 11“Judah pɛ Manasɛ tiini o toŋe totoŋ-zɔɔna ko ja gaale. O ma toŋe lwarem se ko dwoni Amori tiina balo déem na maŋe ba wora ye Isarele tiina bam laam ba to na ke tei to. O ma pa se Judah tiina bam de tusi de ba na tɔge ba kaane o jwona yam to. 12Konto ŋwaane Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to taga tento mo we, ‘Amo wó pa se lɛɛro yi Jerusalem teo nɔn-bia bam de Judah tiina bam maama se ko ke balo na wó ni ko ŋwa to yaau. 13Amo wó waare Jerusalem tiina bam se ko maŋe de a déem na ke tei de Samaria tiina bam de ba pɛ Ahab dwi dem to. Amo wó saare Jerusalem tiina bam a yage, ne ba na zare zoŋa ba guguni ka wo ye ba pipiri ka ni ba pu tega ne tei to mo. 14Amo nam ta wó ve a nɔɔna balo ta na daare to ye a kwei-ba a ke ba dona jeŋa ne se ba di-ba ba daare ba vere ba jejegero. 15Amo wó ke konto bɛŋwaane ba tiini ba toŋe lwarem ba chɔge a yiga ye ba chuchugi a bane. Ko zege maŋa kalo ba nabaara bam na nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne to ba maŋe ba ke konto mo se ko ba ko yi zem.’ ”
16Manasɛ déem ta pɛ se nɔn-laaro dedɛ ga ba ŋwea pa se ba jana taare Jerusalem teo kom ni maama. O ke lwarem dem konto mo o woli de o ya na maŋe o ke tei o pa Judah tiina bam tusi ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga to.
17Manasɛ déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o totoŋa yam maama, ko woli de o na ke wɛleera yalo to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 18Manasɛ ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o sɔŋɔ kaduga kam ne. Ko déem ye Yuza kaduga mo. O bu Amon ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.
Judah teo Pɛ Amon taane
19Amon déem jege bena finlei-yalei mo ye o di paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena yalei. O nu yere mo Mesulemef wolo na ye Haruzi bukɔ ye o nwoŋi Jotiba to. 20Amon déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga mo ne o kwo Manasɛ na ke tei to. 21O kwo totoŋ-naga kam mo o yɔɔre o kwei. O déem kaane jwona yalo o kwo déem na kaane to ye o tiiri o zuli-ya mo. 22Amon mɛ o kwaga mo o ya Baŋa Wɛ wom o nabaara na zuli to. O ma ve se o tɔge Baŋa Wɛ chwoŋa kam.
23Amon tete tontoŋena bam ma lɔ o kwaga ne ba ke ni daane ye ba go‑o pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne. 24Judah teo nɔn-bia bam de ma zaŋe ba go balo maama na lɔge Amon kwaga ne to. Ba ma tiŋi Amon bu Josia pa o leiri Amon yuu ne o di paare.
25Amon déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 26Ba ma kwei Amon yera yam ba suli o yibeeli ne Yuza kaduga kam ne. O bu Josia ma leiri o yuu ne o di paare dem.

english_text:
King Josiah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 34.1,2)
1 Josiah was 8 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 31 years from Jerusalem. His mother Jedidah was the daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath. 2Josiah always obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
Hilkiah Finds The Book of God's Law
(2 Chronicles 34.8-28)
3After Josiah had been king for 18 years, he told Shaphan, one of his highest officials:
Go to the Lord's temple 4and ask Hilkiah the high priest to collect from the guards all the money that the people have donated. 5Tell Hilkiah to give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. They can use some of the money to pay 6the workers, and with the rest of it they can buy wood and stone for the repair work. 7 They are honest, so we won't ask them to keep track of the money.
8While Shaphan was at the temple, Hilkiah handed him a book and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.”
Shaphan read it, 9then went back to Josiah and reported, “Your officials collected the money in the temple and gave it to the men supervising the repairs. 10But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it out loud.
11When Josiah heard what was in The Book of God's Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow. 12At once he called together Hilkiah, Shaphan, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, and his own servant Asaiah. He said, 13“The Lord must be furious with me and everyone else in Judah, because our ancestors did not obey the laws written in this book. Go find out what the Lord wants us to do.”
14The five men left at once and went to talk with Huldah the prophet. Her husband was Shallum, who was in charge of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in the northern part of Jerusalem, and when they met in her home, 15she said:
You were sent here by King Josiah, and this is what the Lord God of Israel says to him: 16“Josiah, I am the Lord! And I will see to it that this country and everyone living in it will be destroyed. It will happen just as this book says. 17The people of Judah have rejected me. They have offered sacrifices to foreign gods and have worshiped their own idols. I cannot stand it any longer. I am furious.
18“Josiah, listen to what I am going to do. 19I noticed how sad you were when you read that this country and its people would be completely wiped out. You even tore your clothes in sorrow, and I heard you cry. 20So I will let you die in peace, before I destroy this place.”
The men left and took Huldah's answer back to Josiah.
translation_text:
Judah teo Pɛ Josia taane
1Josia déem jege bena nana mo ye o di paare dem. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena fintɔ-dedwe. O nu yere mo Jedida wolo na ye Adaya bukɔ ye o nwoŋi Bozekafa to. 2Josia totoŋa déem su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane. O yɔɔre o kwei chwei selo o nabaaro David déem na tɔge to mo, ye o wo ywori se wone.
3Pɛ Josia paare dim bena fuga-nana bene dem ne mo o toŋe Azalia bu Safan na ye Mesulam naa to se o vo Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne. Safan déem ye pɛ sɔŋɔ tɔn-poponno mo. Josia ma ta de Safan o we, 4“Zaŋe n vo kaanem nakwe tu Hilikia tei n ta ded‑o se o jeeli sabu kolo Wɛ diga ni-yerena bam na jwoŋi nɔɔna bam tei ne ba tiŋi to ni. 5O laam wó kwei-ko o pa balo na nii Baŋa Wɛ diga kam kwɛɛm totoŋa baŋa ne to se banto jwoŋi ba ma ŋwe tontoŋena balo na wora ba fɔge ba kwɛ diga kam to. 6Tontoŋena bam konto maa ye gwaro, de lɔra, de kandwa-cherena mo. Ba jege se ba ma sabu kom ba yeigi dɛ, de kandwa yalo ba na yare peo yera ne to se ba ma ba fɔge ba kwɛ Wɛ diga kam. 7Ko ná ye balo ba na wó pa-ba sabu kom to, ko dae se ba jeeli sabu kom ba bere jaja, banto na yɔɔre ba toŋe de chega to ŋwaane.”
Hilikia nɛ Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom
8Safan na pɛ Hilikia pɛ kwora kam to, mo Hilikia tage ded‑o o we, “Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom mo tento a na nɛa Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone.” O ma kwei-ko o pa‑o. Safan ma jwoŋi o ga. 9O ma jwoori o vo ta de pɛ Josia o we, “Pɛ, nmo dedɛɛra bam kwei sabu kolo ya na tigi Wɛ diga kam ne to ba pa balo na nii Baŋa Wɛ diga kam kwɛɛm totoŋa baŋa ne to.” 10Safan ta ma ta de pɛ wom o we, “Kaanem tu Hilikia mo kwei tɔnɔ konto o pa-ne.” O ma ga tɔnɔ kom o bere pɛ wom.
11Pɛ Josia na nigi Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom seina to mo o wo chɔge dedɛ. O ma ja o gwaaro o kaare. 12O ma daare o ta de kaanem tu Hilikia, de Safan bu Ahikam, de Mikaya bu Akebora, de o tɔn-poponno Safan, ko woli de Asaya na ye pɛ wom yera tontoŋeno to o we, 13“Véi-na Wɛ diga kam á lwoori Baŋa Wɛ kolo na popone tɔnɔ konto wone to ŋwaane, se dé wane dé lɔre o boboŋa. Ke-na konto á pa amo, de Judah tiina bam maama. Baŋa Wɛ bane mo yɔɔre de wiira debam baŋa ne, bɛŋwaane dé nabaara bam wo toŋe ba tɔge nia yalo na popone debam ŋwaane tɔnɔ konto wone to.”
14Hilikia, de Ahikam, de Akebora, de Safan, ko woli de Asaya maama ma zaŋe ba vo Jerusalem jei-doŋa laŋa kam ne se ba na de Wɛ sampwori-kana kalo yere na ye Hulida to. O maa ye Tikiva bu Salum kaane mo. Tikiva de déem ye Hahase wolo na nii pɛ wom gwaaro baŋa ne to bu mo. Nɔɔna bam ma ŋɔɔne de Hulida. 15O de ma leiri-ba o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to kwora mo tento: Véi-na a ta de nɔɔno wolo na toŋe abam amo tei ne to we, 16‘Baŋa Wɛ kwora mo tento: Amo wó pa se lɛɛro yi n teo kom de ko nɔn-bia bam maama, se ko maŋe de kolo maama na popone tɔnɔ konto wone ye Judah teo pɛ wom ga to. 17Kokuri to, Judah tiina bam ve amo mo ye ba daare ba kaane wa-yɔɔro. Ba ma chuchugi a bane de ba jea na ke jwona yalo to. Konto ŋwaane a ban-lom dem wó to teo konto baŋa ne.
