Hakimoni bu Jeheli mo bere pɛ wom bia bam.
33Ahitofeli déem mo woli pɛ wom de kwea.
Ariki tu Husayi maa ye pɛ wom badwoŋ-swono.
34Benaya bu Jehoyada, ko woli de Abiatara maama déem mo leiri Ahitofeli yuu ne.
Joaba déem maa ye pɛ wom jar-keira bam yiga tu.

english_text:
David Gives Solomon the Plans for the Temple
1David called a meeting in Jerusalem for all of Israel's leaders, including the tribal leaders, the government officials, the army commanders, the officials in charge of the royal property and livestock, the palace officials, and the brave warriors.
2 After everyone was there, David stood up and said:
Listen to me, my people. I wanted to build a place where the sacred chest would be kept, so we could go there and worship the Lord our God. I have prepared all the supplies for building a temple, 3but the Lord has refused to let me build it, because he said I have killed too many people in battle.
4The Lord God chose Judah to be the leading tribe in Israel. Then from Judah, he chose my father's family, and from that family, he chose me to be the king of Israel, and he promised that my descendants will also rule as kings. 5The Lord has blessed me with many sons, but he chose my son Solomon to be the next king of Israel. 6The Lord said to me, “Your son Solomon will build my temple, and it will honor me. Solomon will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. 7If he continues to obey my laws and commands, his kingdom will never end.”
8My friends, you are the Lord's people. And now, with God as your witness, I want you to promise that you will do your best to obey everything the Lord God has commanded us. Then this land will always belong to you and your descendants.
9Solomon, my son, worship God and obey him with all your heart and mind, just as I have done. He knows all your thoughts and your reasons for doing things, and so if you turn to him, he will hear your prayers. But if you ignore him, he will reject you forever. 10The Lord has chosen you to build a temple for worshiping him. Be confident and do the work you have been assigned.
11After David finished speaking, he gave Solomon the plans for building the main rooms of the temple, including the porch, the storerooms, the rooms upstairs and downstairs, as well as the most holy place. 12He gave Solomon his plans for the courtyards and the open areas around the temple, and for the rooms to store the temple treasures and gifts that had been dedicated to God.
13David also gave Solomon his plans for dividing the priests and the Levites into groups, as well as for the work that needed to be done at the temple and for taking care of the objects used for worship. 14He told Solomon how much gold and silver was to be used in making the sacred objects, 15including the lampstands and lamps, 16the gold table which held the sacred loaves of bread, the tables made of silver, 17the meat forks, the bowls and cups, 18the gold incense altar, and the gold statue of a chariot for the winged creatures which were on the lid of the sacred chest.
19David then said to Solomon:
The Lord showed me how his temple is to be built. 20But you must see that everything is done according to these plans. Be confident, and never be afraid of anything or get discouraged. The Lord my God will help you do everything needed to finish the temple, so it can be used for worshiping him. 21The priests and Levites have been assigned their duties, and all the skilled workers are prepared to do their work. The people and their leaders will do anything you tell them.
translation_text:
Wɛ diga kam
1Pɛ David déem ma bwoŋi Isarele dedɛɛra bam maama se ba jeeri Jerusalem ne. Banto maa ye Isarele dwia yam nakwa bam, de teo kom dedɛɛra balo na toŋe ba pa pɛ wom to, de balo na tei jar-keira moro moro to, de balo na tei jar-keira bi bi to, de dedɛɛra balo na nii pɛ wom de o bia zela yam de ba vara baŋa ne to, de pɛ sɔŋɔ kom tontoŋena bam, ko woli de balo maama na ye nɔn-yerro de bembɛ to. 2Ba na jeeri daane konto to, Pɛ David ma zege wɛɛne o ta o we:
“A nu-bia bam, a déem jaane boboŋa mo se a lɔ diga se ba taa zege Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam da, se dé Tu Wɛ wom na jeiga kalo o na wó chwi o nɛ da to. A nam bobo se a ti ka lɔɔm dem yiga. 3Baŋa Wɛ nam ve mo ye o we, ‘Nmo bá‑n lɔ diga amo yere zula ŋwaane, nmo na ye bembea ye n pwori nɔɔna dedɛ jana to ŋwaane.’
4Ko nam ye Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to mo le amo a kwo sɔŋɔ kom maama wone se a taa di Isarele teo paare taa wuu. O déem kuri Judah dwi dem mo se ba di yiga Isarele dwia yam maama wone. O ta ma kuri a kwo diga kam Judah dwi dem wone, ye o daare o zo a kwo bia bam wone o kuri amo se a taa ye Isarele teo maama pɛ, o yi na su amo kikia to ŋwaane. 5Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se a lo bakeiri dedɛ. O ma nii ba maama wone o kuri Solomon se o leiri amo yuu ne o di paare Baŋa Wɛ tete nɔɔna Isarele tiina baŋa ne. 6Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo we, ‘Nmo bu Solomon mo ye wolo na wó lɔ a diga kam de ka konkwallo tem to. Kokuri to, a kuri wonto mo se o taa ye a bu, se amo de taa ye o kwo. 7Amo wó pa se o paare dem fɔge de jeini lanyerane taa wuu, ne o ná yɔɔre o sɛ se o toŋe o tɔge amo nia yam de a bera yam, ne ko zem na ye tei to.’
8Konto ŋwaane, amo na zege abam Isarele tiina na ye Baŋa Wɛ kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne, ye dé Tu Wɛ wom wora o maane dé keina yam to, amo zem kaane abam we, abam jege se á ta‑á toŋe a tɔge á Tu Baŋa Wɛ nia yam maama mo. Konto mo wó pa se á wane á jwoŋi te-ywoŋa kanto á ta‑á tei, ye á daare á kwei-ka á ta‑á pae á bia se ko taa vei wuu.
9Ko nam ná ye nmo Solomon na ye amo bu to, kwaane se n sɛ n pa n kwo Wɛ wom, se n ta‑n zuli‑o de n bochare maama, de n boboŋa maama. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ yeini o buŋi nɔɔna bochara wone ye o lɔre ba boboŋa maama na ye tei to mo. Nmo ná beeri o jei, o wó pa‑m chwoŋa se n na‑o. Nmo nam daa ná ve‑o, o de wó ve‑m se ko taa vei wuu. 10Nam ta‑n yei n tete ni ne, kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ kuri nmo mo se n lɔ diga kalo na wó taa ye o wara-jei sem to n pa‑o. Konto to, ke dam n ke n tete kuri ne, se n kwaane n toŋe.”
11David na ŋɔɔne konto o ti to, o ma kwei twanno telo na bere Wɛ diga kam zega to o pa o bu Solomon. Te bere ba na wó lɔ-ka tei maama to mo: ka napɔrɔ kom, de ka di-balwa bam, de ka zela di sem, de ka wɛyuu di sem, de ka wo di sem, ko woli de wɛleera saarem jeiga kam maama. 12David déem ma bere‑o o boboŋa na jaane se o lɔ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam konkwallo tem tei to, de ka pwooni yiga di sem, de ka lonne wonnu tiŋim di sem, de di selo ba na wó zege Wɛ pɛɛra da to. 13O ta ma bere‑o kaanem tiina bam de Levi dwi tiina bam totoŋa na jege se ya pɔɔre tei to, dedaane ba na wó taa toŋe tei maama Wɛ diga kam wone to, de zela yalo ba na wó taa mae ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ to. 14O ta ma bere Solomon sabu-seŋa dunni, de lu-nyenno dunni na jege se te taa mae tei to se ba ma ba ke zwe selo ba na wó taa ma-se ba toŋe totoŋa dwi dwi Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone to. 15O ta bere‑o sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno dunni na jege se te taa mae tei se ba ma ba ke min-zwon-zegero tem de min-zwonnu tem tete, se ko tɔge te maama totoŋe na ye tei to. 16O ta ma bere‑o sabu-seŋa dunni ba na wó ma ba ke tabolo kolo ba na tigisi bworobworo da Wɛ ŋwaane to, ko ta woli de lu-nyenno dunni ba na wó ma ba ke tabollo tedwonna to. 17O ta bere‑o sabu-seŋa dunni na wó taa mae tei se o ma o ke wonnu telo ba na wó taa ma-te ba zɔ nɔna te le to, de zwe sem, de kambi sem maama. O ma daare o bere‑o sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno dunni na jege se te taa mae tei se ba ma ba ke zwe sedwonna to. 18O ta ma bere‑o ba na wó kwei sabu-seŋa dunni delo to ba ma ba ke talwoŋ-ywoŋa zwɛɛm bimbini dem. O ta ma daare o bere‑o ba na wó ma sabu-seŋa ba mɔ cherubi nyenyero tem de te jeiŋa jei tei to. Tento lware te vɔna mo te kwoli Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam.
19Pɛ David ma ta o we, “Tento maama a popone a tiŋi tɔnɔ wone, ne Baŋa Wɛ tete na bere-ne tei maama to. O ma pa a lɔre diga kam lɔɔm de ka totoŋa maama na jege se ya taa ye tei to.”
20David ta ma ta de o bu Solomon o we, “Yɔɔre n ke dam n tete kuri ne, se n daare n ta‑n jege baare ye n kwaane n toŋe. Yé ta‑n fona, nam yé pa se n vɔna pare. Kokuri to, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na ya amo Tu Wɛ to wó taa wo n tei ne. O wó yɔɔre o woli‑m ye o bá yage‑m, se n wane n toŋe Baŋa Wɛ diga kam lɔɔm totoŋe dem maama n ti. 21Nii mo! Wɛ kaanem tiina bam de Levi dwi tiina bam maŋe ba lɔre ba na wó taa toŋe Wɛ diga kam totoŋa dwi dwi tei to. Gwaro tem maama de yei ba totoŋa chekke, ye ba ti ba yiga se ba woli‑m totoŋa yam maama wone. Dedɛɛra bam de nɔɔna bam maama de maa wó sɛ ni delo maama n na wó pa-ba to.”

english_text:
Gifts for Building the Temple
1 David told the crowd:
God chose my son Solomon to build the temple, but Solomon is young and has no experience. This is not just any building—this is the temple for the Lord God! 2That's why I have done my best to get everything Solomon will need to build it—gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, onyx, turquoise, colored gems, all kinds of precious stones, and marble.
3Besides doing all that, I have promised to give part of my own gold and silver as a way of showing my love for God's temple. 4More than 100 tons of my finest gold and almost 240 tons of my silver will be used to decorate its walls 5and to make the gold and silver objects. Now, who else will show their dedication to the Lord by giving gifts for building his temple?
6After David finished speaking, the family leaders, the tribal leaders, the army commanders, and the government officials voluntarily gave gifts 7for the temple. These gifts included more than 170 tons of gold, over 340 tons of silver, 620 tons of bronze, and more than 3,400 tons of iron. 8Everyone who owned precious stones also donated them to the temple treasury, where Jehiel from the Levite clan of Gershon guarded them.
9David and the people were very happy that so much had been given to the Lord, and they all celebrated.
David Praises the Lord
10Then, in front of everyone, David sang praises to the Lord:
I praise you forever, Lord! You are the God our ancestor Jacob worshiped. 11 Your power is great, and your glory is seen everywhere in heaven and on earth. You are king of the entire world, 12and you rule with strength and power. You make people rich and powerful and famous. 13We thank you, our God, and praise you.
14But why should we be happy that we have given you these gifts? They belong to you, and we have only given back what is already yours. 15We are only foreigners living here on earth for a while, just as our ancestors were. And we will soon be gone, like a shadow that suddenly disappears.
16Our Lord God, we have brought all these things for building a temple to honor you. They belong to you, and you gave them to us. 17But we are happy, because everyone has voluntarily given you these things. You know what is in everyone's heart, and you are pleased when people are honest. 18Always make us eager to give, and help us be faithful to you, just as our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob faithfully worshiped you. 19And give Solomon the desire to completely obey your laws and teachings, and the desire to build the temple for which I have provided these gifts.
20David then said to the people, “Now it's your turn to praise the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped!” So everyone praised the Lord, and they bowed down to honor him and David their king.
Solomon Is Crowned King
21The next day, the Israelites slaughtered 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, and 1,000 lambs, and they offered them as sacrifices to please the Lord, along with offerings of wine. 22The people were very happy, and they ate and drank there at the Lord's altar.
That same day, Solomon was again crowned king. The people celebrated and poured olive oil on Solomon's head to show that he would be their next king. They also poured oil on Zadok's head to show that he was their priest.
23 So Solomon became king after David his father. Solomon was successful, and everyone in Israel obeyed him. 24Every official and every soldier, as well as all of David's other sons, were loyal to him. 25The Lord made Solomon a great king, and the whole nation was amazed at how famous he was. In fact, no other king of Israel was as great as Solomon.
David Dies
26David the son of Jesse was king of Israel 27 for 40 years. He ruled from Hebron for 7 years and from Jerusalem for 33 years. 28David was rich and respected and lived to be an old man. Then he died, and his son Solomon became king.
29Everything David did while he was king is included in the history written by the prophets Samuel, Nathan, and Gad. 30They wrote about his powerful rule and about the things that happened not only to him, but also to Israel and the other nations.
translation_text:
Pɛɛra yalo na woli Wɛ diga kam lɔɔm to
1Pɛ David déem ma ta de kɔgɔ kom maama o we:
“Baŋa Wɛ kuri amo bu Solomon mo se o lɔ o diga kam. Solomon nam ye nɔn-doŋo mo ye o ta bwona. Totoŋe dem nam ye totoŋ-kamunu mo, bɛŋwaane ko dae nabiinu diga mo o lage o lɔ, se ko ye Baŋa Wɛ diga mo. 2Konto ŋwaane mo amo tiini a kwaane a beeri zela yalo maama na maŋe de amo Tu Wɛ diga kam lɔɔm to a ke da-yiga ne. Zela yanto ye sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de channa, de luuru tete, de dɛ sedwonna, ko woli de Onika kandwa, de kandwa-nyenno dwi dwi se ba taa mae ba gɔgere wonnu, ko woli de pe-siswollu dwi dwi. Amo nam tiini a la tento maama dedɛ mo a tiŋi. 3Konto maama kwaga ne amo jege a tete sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno wonnu se a pa se ba ma ba lɔ amo Tu Wɛ diga kam, a na sae yera ka lɔɔm dem ŋwaane to. Amo tete ta na wó woli kolo da to mo tento: 4Sabu-seŋa kalo na ye chekke ye ka nwoŋi Ofiri to dunni ye kilo morro bi (100,000) mo. Lu-nyenno telo ba na wó ma ba taare kabiri sem to dunni maa ye kilo morro bia yalei de finna (240,000). 5Gwaro tem ta wó ma sabu-seŋa kam de lu-nyenno tem konto ba ma ba gɔgere Wɛ diga kam wonnu dwi dwi. Tɔ. Abam wɔ tete mo wó sɛ se o de kwei o wonnu o pa Baŋa Wɛ zem dɛ dento ne?”
6David na tage konto o ti to, sɔ-yuni nakwa bam, de Isarele dwia yam nakwa bam, de dedɛɛra balo na tei jar-keira moro moro to, de balo na tei jar-keira bi bi to, ko woli de dedɛɛra balo na nii pɛ wom totoŋa baŋa ne to maama ma sɛ ba pa pɛɛra de ba wo maama Wɛ diga kam lɔɔm ŋwaane. 7Ba déem pɛ sabu-seŋa dunni na yi kilo morro bi de fuserepɛ (170,000) to, de lu-nyenno dunni na yi kilo morro bia yatɔ de finna (340,000) to, de channa dunni na yi kilo morro bia yaredo (600,000) to, de luuru telo dunni na yi kilo moro kuni morro tetɔ de bia yana (3,400,000) to mo. 8Balo maama de déem na jege kandwa-nyenno to de ma kwei-ya ba ja ba vo ba tiŋi lonne wonnu diga kam wone, ye Gereson tu Jeheli nii te baŋa ne. 9Nɔɔna bam wo ma tiini ko pwoli de ba na pɛ wonnu dedɛ de ba wo maama ba ma ke pɛɛra ba pa Baŋa Wɛ to. Ba maama de Pɛ David tete maa tiini ba chaka.
David wɛ-lworo
10David ma zege kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne o seini Baŋa Wɛ ye o we:
“Pa-na se dé tei Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom
debam nabaaro Isarele de déem na zuli to.
Baŋa Wɛ, nmo maŋe se n jwoŋi zula
se ko taa vei wuu.
11Nmo kamunim, de dam,
de nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ, de paare daga dedɛ,
nmo na tei logo baŋa de wɛyuu wonnu maama to ŋwaane.
12Jejegero de dunni maama
nwoŋi nmo tei ne mo,
nmo na di paare nabiina maama baŋa ne to ŋwaane.
Nmo yeini n kwei n dam-fɔrɔ mo
n pa nɔɔna
pa se ba jiri naduna de nɔn-yerro.
13Debam Tu Wɛ, dé ke nmo lei,
ye dé daare dé tei
n yere-kamunu kom mo.
14Amo de a nɔɔna bam nam ya muri se dé wane dé pa pɛɛra yanto de dé wo maama, jejegero maama na nwoŋi nmo tei ne to ŋwaane. Kolo na ye nmo nyem to mo dé jwoori dé kwei dé pa‑m. 15Debam ye veira mo dé zoore logo konto wone, ne dé nabaara bam de déem na ye tei to. Dé ba jege kugu jei logo baŋa ne. Dé nam wó jei lela nenɛɛne luluŋu na pɔpɔ ko duri ko jei tei to mo.
16Debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ, ko ná ye pɛɛra yanto maama dé na jaane dé ba se dé ma dé lɔ diga kalo na wó taa zege nmo yere-kamunu kom zula ŋwaane to, ya maama maŋe ya ye nmo nyem mo. 17Amo Tu Wɛ, a yei we n yeini n maŋe nɔɔno bochare mo n nii, ye n wo pwoli de balo kikia na tɔge chega to. A kwei wonnu tento a pa‑m de a wo maama, de a boboŋ-laaro mo. A ta ma maane we nmo nɔɔna balo na jeeri ywo-seeni to de kwei ba wonnu ba ke nmo jeŋa ne de wopwolo, de ba chega maama. 18Yuu-Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye dé nabaara Abaraham, de Izaak, de Isarele Wɛ to, nam pa n nɔɔna bam taa jege pempanno taa, se ba taa jege nmo chega se ko taa vei wuu. 19Ta pa se amo bu Solomon yɔɔre o taa toŋe o tɔge n nia yam, de n chullu tem, de n bera yam maama. Woli‑o se o seene o yia o lɔ nmo diga kam a na maŋe a la ka yera zela yam a tiŋi se ba ma ba lɔ to.”
20David laam ma ta de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama o we, “Tei-na abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ!” Ba maama ma tei Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye ba nabaara Wɛ to. Ba maa tiiri ba vwi ba yibia tega ne ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ, ba daare ba zuli Pɛ David tete de.
Solomon leiri David yuu ne o ji pɛ
21Tega na poore to, Isarele tiina bam déem ma go vara dedɛ ba ma ke zwɛɛm kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ba déem go na-bale moro dedoa, de pi-bɛ moro dedoa, de pipeili moro dedoa mo. Ba ta ma ke wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛra dedaane pɛɛra dwi dwi ba woli da, Isarele tiina bam maama ŋwaane. 22Dɛ dem konto ne nɔɔna bam wo déem pwoli se ko gaale. Ba ma di wodi-fɔrɔ kuri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Ba ma jwoori ba tiŋi Solomon paare dem se ko ke belei tu, se o wane o leiri o kwo David yuu ne o di paare dem. Ba ma kwei Wɛ swolim nuga ba lwo o yuu ne. Ba ta ma lwo nuga kam Zadoki yuu ne se o ji Wɛ kaanem tu. 23Solomon ma leiri o kwo David yuu ne o di paare Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane. Wonnu maama déem ma ke lanyerane te pa Solomon. Isarele tiina bam maama maa sɛ o ni. 24Teo kom dedɛɛra bam maama, de nɔn-yerro tem maama, ko woli de David bia bam maama déem ma sɛ se ba to ba pa Solomon.
25 Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ Solomon tiini o na zula Isarele tiina bam maama tei ne. O ta ma pa se o paare dem jege nenɔŋa dedɛ se ko dwoni Isarele teo pwa balo na lwoori wonto na nɛ nenɔŋa kalo to.
David paare dem seina
26Jesse bu David déem mo di paare Isarele teo maama ne. 27O nɛ bena finna mo Isarele teo paare dem baŋa ne. Bena finna yam wone o ke bena yarepɛ mo Heboron ne, o daare o ke bena fintɔ-yatɔ Jerusalem ne. 28David déem jege jejegero dedɛ ye nɔɔna nege‑o. O kwe o yi o maŋa mo ye o te. O bu Solomon ma leiri o yuu ne o di paare dem.
29David déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, ko zege o paare dem boboa ne se ko yi de na kweeli maŋa kalo to, ba popone te maama ba tiŋi Wɛ ni-jwoŋina Samuwel, de Natan, de Gaadi yera seina twanno tem wone. 30Ba déem popone ko tɔge o dam dem de o paare dem, de wonnu telo na yi o de Isarele tiina bam to, ko woli de wonnu telo na yi dwi-gɛ tiina de ba teene dem to mo ba tiŋi.

english_text:
The Lord Makes Solomon Wise
(1 Kings 3.1-15)
1King Solomon, the son of David, was now in complete control of his kingdom, because the Lord God had blessed him and made him a powerful king.
2-5 At that time, the sacred tent that Moses the servant of the Lord had made in the desert was still kept at Gibeon, and in front of the tent was the bronze altar that Bezalel had made.
One day, Solomon told the people of Israel, the army commanders, the officials, and the family leaders, to go with him to the place of worship at Gibeon, even though his father King David had already moved the sacred chest from Kiriath-Jearim to the tent that he had set up for it in Jerusalem. Solomon and the others went to Gibeon to worship the Lord, 6and there at the bronze altar, Solomon offered a thousand animals as sacrifices to please the Lord.
7God appeared to Solomon that night in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
8Solomon answered:
Lord God, you were always loyal to my father David, and now you have made me king of Israel. 9 I am supposed to rule these people, but there are as many of them as there are specks of dust on the ground. So keep the promise you made to my father 10and make me wise. Give me the knowledge I'll need to be the king of this great nation of yours.
11God replied:
Solomon, you could have asked me to make you rich or famous or to let you live a long time. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom and knowledge to rule my people. 12So I will make you wise and intelligent. But I will also make you richer and more famous than any king before or after you.
13Solomon then left Gibeon and returned to Jerusalem, the capital city of Israel.
Solomon's Wealth
(1 Kings 10.26-29)
14 Solomon had a force of 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses that he kept in Jerusalem and other towns.
15While Solomon was king of Israel, there was silver and gold everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
16-17 Solomon's merchants bought his horses and chariots in the regions of Musri and Kue. They paid 600 pieces of silver for a chariot and 150 pieces of silver for a horse. They also sold horses and chariots to the Hittite and Syrian kings.
translation_text:
Pɛ Solomon lwoori swa Wɛ tei ne
1 Pwa 3:1-15
1David bu Solomon déem yɔɔre o jege o paare o di teo kom maama ne mo, ye o kuri ja tega. Kokuri to, o Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo wo o tei ne, pa se o yere tiini de zaŋe.
2Solomon déem ma bwoŋi Isarele tiina bam maama se ba jeeri daane. Banto maa ye balo na tei jar-keira moro moro to, de balo na tei jar-keira bi bi to, de Isarele teo dedɛɛra bam, de ba nakwa bam, de ba sɔ-yuni yiga tiina bam maama. 3Ba na gilimi daane to, Pɛ Solomon de Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama ma vo Gibeon. Wara-jei déem wo dáane, vwei delo o tontoŋeno Moses déem na ke o zege kagoa kam wone to na wora to ŋwaane. 4David déem ya lwoori yiga mo o ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam o zege Kiriaf-Jeerim ne o vo Jerusalem, mɛ o na chwi vwei se o zege-ka de wone to. 5Ko nam ná ye channa kaanem dakaa kalo Yuri wolo na ye Hura bu to bu Bezaleli déem na ke to, ka déem zege Gibeon ne mo ye ka wo Baŋa Wɛ wara-vwei dem yiga ne. Mo kokuri Solomon de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama vei dáane se ba ware Baŋa Wɛ. 6Ba na zege wara-vwei dem yiga ne konto to, mo Solomon fɔɔre o yi channa kaanem dakaa kam, ye o ke zwɛɛm kaanem kuni moro bimbini dem baŋa ne o pa Baŋa Wɛ.
7Tete dem konto mo Wɛ veere o tete ded‑o, ye o we, “Solomon, lwoori n na lage kolo maama to, se amo wó pa‑m”. 8Solomon ma leiri o we, “Nmo déem jege a kwo David swono lanyerane, ye n daare n pa se a leiri o yuu ne a di paare dem. 9Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, laam pa se ni delo nmo na gwoni de amo kwo to ji chega. Kokuri to, nmo pɛ se amo mo ji pɛ se a taa tei kɔ-fɔrɔ kolo ni na daga dedɛ ne tega kasolo tei to. 10Nam pa-ne swa chekke de yeino, se a taa mae a nii nɔɔna banto baŋa ne. Kokuri to, wɔ mo wó wane nmo kɔ-fɔrɔ konto o nii o tete ne?”
11Wɛ ma leiri Solomon o we, “Nmo boboŋa yam lana dedɛ. Kokuri to, nmo wo lwoori-ne se n jwoŋi jejegero, naa nadunni, naa zula amo tei ne. Nmo ta ma‑n ba beeri toone se n pa n dona, naa se n jwoŋi momwɛ-dɛɛre n pa n tete. Ko nam ye swa de yeino mo n laga se n ta‑n mae n tei amo nɔɔna balo a na kwei a pa‑m se n ta‑n ye ba pɛ to. 12Konto ŋwaane amo wó seene a pa‑m swa de yeino. A nam ta wó pa‑m jejegero, de nadunni, de zula, se pɛ wodwoŋi yé kɛ nmo yiga ne, ko ná ye balo na lwoori nmo to, naa balo na wó saŋe nmo kwaga ba di paare to de.”
13Solomon laam ma zege Gibeon wara-jei sem ne Wɛ wara-vwei dem na wo mɛ to o jwoori Jerusalem teo kom wo. O ma lɛɛre o jege Isarele teo paare dem o di.
14Solomon déem ma la jara-keim torokooro moro de bia yana (1,400), dedaane sisein-nɔɔna morro fuga-telei (12,000). O déem pɔɔre se sedwonna o yage teene delo o na kuri se ŋwaane to ne. Sedaara maa wo Jerusalem ne mɛ o na zoore to. 15O paare dim maŋa ne, lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa tiini te daga Jerusalem ne, ne kandwa mo tei. Sedare da-ŋonno de maa ba jege zore nenɛɛne kaporro na daga tei wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne to. 16Nɔɔna déem vei Ejipti de Silisia teene dem mo ba kwei sabu ba yeigi sisei ba pa Solomon. Ko maa ye o pipim-piina mo yeini ba yeigi-se Silisia teo ne, ye ba ŋwe kolo na maŋe to. 17Ko ná ye jara-keim toroko, ba yeini ba yeigi-ko Ejipti ne de lu-nyenno sabu-dala bia yaredo (600) mo. Siseiŋa maa yeigi de lu-nyenno sabu-dala bi de finnu (150). Pɛ wom pipim-piina bam déem yeini ba kwei torokooro de sisein-nɔɔna dedɛ ba yeigi ba pa Hiti tiina pwa bam de Aram tiina pwa mo.

english_text:
Solomon Asks Hiram To Help Build the Temple
(1 Kings 5.1-12)
1Solomon decided to build a temple where the Lord would be worshiped, and also to build a palace for himself. 2He assigned 70,000 men to carry building supplies and 80,000 to cut stone from the hills. And he chose 3,600 men to supervise these workers.
3Solomon sent the following message to King Hiram of Tyre:
Years ago, when my father David was building his palace, you supplied him with cedar logs. Now will you send me supplies? 4I am building a temple where the Lord my God will be worshiped. Sweet-smelling incense will be burned there, and sacred bread will be offered to him. Worshipers will offer sacrifices to the Lord every morning and evening, every Sabbath, and on the first day of each month, as well as during all our religious festivals. These things will be done for all time, just as the Lord has commanded.
5This will be a great temple, because our God is greater than all other gods. 6 No one can ever build a temple large enough for God—even the heavens are too small a place for him to live in! All I can do is build a place where we can offer sacrifices to him.
7Send me a worker who can not only carve, but who can work with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, as well as make brightly colored cloth. The person you send will work here in Judah and Jerusalem with the skilled workers that my father has already hired.
8I know that you have workers who are experts at cutting lumber in Lebanon. So would you please send me some cedar, pine, and juniper logs? My workers will be there to help them, 9because I'll need a lot of lumber to build such a large and glorious temple. 10I will pay your woodcutters 2,000 tons of wheat, the same amount of barley, 400,000 liters of wine, and that same amount of olive oil.
11Hiram sent his answer back to Solomon:
I know that the Lord must love his people, because he has chosen you to be their king. 12Praise the Lord God of Israel who made heaven and earth! He has given David a son who isn't only wise and smart, but who has the knowledge to build a temple for the Lord and a palace for himself.
13I am sending Huram Abi to you. He is wise and very skillful. 14His mother was from the Israelite tribe of Dan, and his father was from Tyre. Not only is Huram an expert at working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, but he can also make colored cloth and fine linen. And he can carve anything if you give him a pattern to follow. He can help your workers and those hired by your father King David.
15Go ahead and send the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine you promised to pay my workers. 16I will tell them to start cutting down trees in Lebanon. They will cut as many as you need, then tie them together into rafts, and float them down along the coast to Joppa. Your workers can take them to Jerusalem from there.
Solomon's Work Force
17Solomon counted all the foreigners who were living in Israel, just as his father David had done when he was king, and the total was 153,600. 18He assigned 70,000 of them to carry building supplies and 80,000 of them to cut stone from the hills. He chose 3,600 others to supervise the workers and to make sure the work was completed.
translation_text:
Wɛ diga kam lɔɔm taane
1Solomon boboŋa déem nam ya jaane se o lɔ diga mo Baŋa Wɛ yere zula ŋwaane, se o daare o lɔ paare sɔ-fɔrɔ o pa o tete. 2O ma pa ba beeri nɔɔna morro fuserepɛ (70,000) balo na wó taa zeŋe zela to ba pa‑o. O ta pɛ ba beeri nɔɔna morro funɔnɔ (80,000) mo, se ba yeini ba di peero yuu ba yare kandwa-zana ba pa‑o. O ma beeri nɔɔna morro tetɔ de bia yaredo (3,600) o woli da se ba taa nii tontoŋena bam maama baŋa ne.
3Solomon laam ma toŋe kwora kanto o pa Tura pɛ Hiram we:
“Nmo déem kwei Sedare da-kwollu mo n toŋe n pa amo kwo David pa se o lɔ sɔ-fɔrɔ o zoore ko wone. Nam kwaane n woli amo konto dwoŋi. 4Amo ti a yiga mo se a lɔ diga a Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere zula ŋwaane. Ba laam maa wó pɔɔre-ka ba zege se ba yeini ba taa zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa da, se ba ta daare ba taa tigisi bworobworo kolo na tigi Wɛ yiga ne to ka wone maŋa de maŋa. Dáane mo ba ta wó yeini ba zwɛ kaanem pɛɛra tetete maama, de dedaan-ni maama, ko woli de Wɛ siu da yam ne, de chan-doŋa kura yam ne, de kura yalo maama na wora se dé taa mae dé zuli dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom to. Mo o na pɛ debam Isarele tiina bam ni delo se dé taa ke taa wuu to.
5Diga kalo amo na lage a lɔ to wó taa tiini ka ye kamunu mo, debam Tu Wɛ wom na dwoi wa yadwonna yam maama to ŋwaane. 6Wɔ nam mo yi se o lɔ diga o pa Baŋa Wɛ? Wɛyuu baŋa tete ne, pwola tera ka na maŋe ded‑o! Amo ye wɔ mo se a lɔ diga a pa‑o? Diga kam nam wó taa ye mɛ ba na wó taa zwɛ kaanem da ba pa‑o to mo.
7Nam toŋe gɔgɔ na wae o kwei sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de channa, de luuru o toŋe totoŋa chekke to n pa-ne. Kotu ta wó kwei gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ, de nazwon-pupwia to o ma o toŋe. O ta jege se o taa yei sarem totoŋa na ye tei to. Wonto de gwaro telo amo kwo David déem na kuri to wó woli daane ba toŋe Jerusalem ne de Judah teene dedwonna wone.
8Nam ta toŋe Lebanon teo Sedare da-kwollu, de teeni dedwonna da-ŋonno n pa-ne. Amo maane we, n nɔɔna bam tiini ba yei dɛ gwonim totoŋa abam jei sem ne. Amo nɔɔna wó woli de nmo nɔɔna bam, 9se ba lage da-ŋonno se te taa daga. Kokuri to, diga kalo a na boŋe se a lɔ to jege se ka taa daga mo, ye ka jege nenɔŋa lanyerane. 10Ko ná ye nmo tontoŋena balo na wó gwoni dɛ sem to, amo wó kwei banina ywollu morro fuseredo (60,000), de chaara ywollu morro fuseredo (60,000). A ta wó pa-ba sana kuriwaa bia morro finlei (20,000), de nuga kuriwaa bia morro finlei (20,000) mo.”
11Pɛ Hiram na lage o leiri Solomon to, o popone tɔnɔ mo o pa‑o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na swoi o nɔɔna bam to ŋwaane mo o pɛ se nmo ji ba pɛ.”
12Hiram ta ma ta o we:
“Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina bam Wɛ to mo maŋe de tia. Wonto mo naane wɛyuu de tega baŋa maama. O nam pɛ bu wolo Pɛ David na loge to jege swa chekke, dedaane yi-poro, de boboŋ-laaro. O maa wó lɔ diga o pa Baŋa Wɛ, ye o ta lɔ sɔ-fɔrɔ o pa o tete.
13Amo nam lage a toŋe Huram-Abi mo n tei ne, o na ye gɔgɔ chekke ye o jege yi-poro to ŋwaane. 14O nu maa ye Dan dwi dem bukɔ mo, ye o kwo de ye Tura teo tu. O yei ba na kwei sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de channa, de luuru, de kandwa, de dɛ ba gɔgere wonnu tei to. O nam ta wó wane o ma gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nasoŋ-pupwia, de nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to, dedaane gare-fefale o ma o toŋe. O wae o sare nyenyego dwi maama, ne ba na wó bere‑o se o ke tei to. Wonto wó toŋe o woli nmo tete gwaro tem, de balo nmo kwo Pɛ David déem na kuri to.
15Pɛ Solomon, ko ná ye amo tei ne, nam toŋe banina kam, de chaara yam, de nuga kam, de sana bam, n pa a tontoŋena bam, ne n na gwoni ni se n ke tei to. 16Debam de wó gwoni Lebanon teo da-ŋonno se ko maŋe de nmo na lage tei maama to. Ba laam maa wó vɔ da-kwollu tem ba ke daane, ye ba daare ba de-te naneo kom ne ba yɛ ba vo ba yi Jopa. Nmo nɔɔna bam de laam maa wó jeeri da se ba kwei-te ba ja ba vo Jerusalem.”
17Solomon déem ma pa ba jeeli veira balo na wo Isarele teo wone to ni, ne o kwo David de déem na ke tei to. O ma na we ba ye nɔɔna morro bi de finnu-batɔ dedaane bia yaredo (153,600) mo. 18O ma le ba wone nɔɔna morro fuserepɛ (70,000) se ba taa zeŋe zela, se ba nɔɔna morro funɔnɔ (80,000) taa yare kandwa-zana peero jei sem ne, ye ba wo morro tetɔ de bia yaredo (3,600) de taa nii tontoŋena bam konto baŋa ne.

english_text:
The Temple Is Built
(1 Kings 6.1-38)
1-2 Solomon's workers began building the temple in Jerusalem on the second day of the second month, four years after Solomon had become king of Israel. It was built on Mount Moriah where the Lord had appeared to David at the threshing place that had belonged to Araunah from Jebus.
3The inside of the temple was 27 meters long and 9 meters wide, according to the older standards. 4Across the front of the temple was a porch 9 meters wide and 9 meters high. The inside walls of the porch were covered with pure gold.
5Solomon had the inside walls of the temple's main room paneled first with pine and then with a layer of gold, and he had them decorated with carvings of palm trees and designs that looked like chains. 6He used precious stones to decorate the temple, and he used gold imported from Parvaim 7to decorate the ceiling beams, the doors, the door frames, and the walls. Solomon also told the workers to carve designs of winged creatures into the walls.
8 The most holy place was nine meters square, and its walls were covered with over 20 tons of fine gold. 9Five hundred and seventy grams of gold was used to cover the heads of the nails. The walls of the small storage rooms were also covered with gold.
10 Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made to put in the most holy place, and he covered them with gold. 11-13Each creature had two wings and was four and a half meters from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other wing. Solomon set them next to each other in the most holy place, facing the doorway. Their wings were spread out and reached all the way across the nine-meter room.
14 A curtain was made of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with designs of winged creatures.
The Two Columns
(1 Kings 7.15-22)
15Two columns were made for the entrance to the temple. Each one was 16 meters tall and had a cap on top that was over 2 meters high. 16The top of each column was decorated with designs that looked like chains and with 100 carvings of pomegranates. 17Solomon had one of the columns placed on the south side of the temple's entrance; it was called Jachin. The other one was placed on the north side of the entrance; it was called Boaz.
translation_text:
Solomon na lɔge Wɛ diga kam tei to
1 Pwa 6:1-29
1Solomon déem pɛ se ba bobo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam lɔɔm Jerusalem teo ne. Ko ye Moria peo kom yuu ne mo. Baŋa Wɛ ya maŋe o veere o tete de Solomon kwo David dáane mo, mɛ seeni Jebusi tu Arawuna déem na yeini o vei o fere o mena to. David maŋe o kuri jei sem konto mo se ba lɔ Wɛ diga kam da. 2Solomon paare dim bena yana bene dem, chane selei chana kam da yalei dɛ dem ne mo ba bobo se ba lɔ-ka.
3Solomon déem na tiŋi Wɛ diga kam biri-beira tei to ye naba-laara fintɔ mo ka dedɔrem maŋem baŋa ne. Ka kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem de maa ye naba-laara fuga. Ko nam ye ba faŋa maŋem dem mo ba kwei ba maŋe-ka. 4Wɛ diga kam jege napɔrɔ mo ka yiga kam seeni, ko kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem na ye naba-laara fuga, ye ko wɛ-baŋa seeni maŋem de ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni finlei. Ko ná ye napɔrɔ kom wo kom seeni, ba déem kwei sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to mo ba taare ko maama.
5Ko ná ye Wɛ diga kam tete, o déem pɛ se ba kwei da-pelwaro mo ba kwoli ka wo kabiri sem. O ta ma pa se ba kwei sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to ba taare se maama, ye ba daare ba gɔgere konkwara nyenyero, de nyenyero na lwoni chegero to ba ke da. 6O déem ta kwei kandwa-nyenno mo o ma o kwɛ Wɛ diga kam yera maama. Ba maa na mɛ sabu-seŋa kalo ba toŋe ka totoŋa to maa nwoŋi Paravayim ne. 7Ko ná ye da-kwollu telo ba na kwei ba ne Wɛ diga kam to, de ka manchwo-peo dɛ sem, de ka kabiri sem, de bworru tem, ko déem ye sabu-seŋa mo o mɛ o taare-te. O laam ma daare o pa ba gɔgere cherubi nyenyero o ke kabiri sem yera ne.
8Solomon ta ma lɔ Wɛ di-yun-gala kam na tiini ka ye wose Wɛ ŋwaane to. Ka dedɔrem maŋem de ka kayɔlɔ maŋem maama ye naba-laara fuga fuga mo, pa se ka maŋe de Wɛ diga kam tete. O laam ma kwei sabu-seŋa dunni na yi kilo morro finlei (20,000) to o taare ka wo maama. 9Sabu-seŋa chena yalo ba na kwei ba ke da to dunni maa ma de sabu-dala finnu na ye tei to. Ba ta ma kwei sabu-seŋa ba taare di selo na lɔge se di to kabiri sem.
10Ko ná ye Wɛ di-yun-gala kam, Solomon pɛ se ba kwei dɛ mo ba sare cherubi selei nyenyero ba zege ka wone, ye ba taare-te de sabu-seŋa. 11Cherubi sem ná yarege se vɔna pa ko zege diga kam saŋa dedoa ne ko vo ko yi kadwoŋi kam ne, ko ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finlei mo. Cherubi dedoa vɔŋɔ dedɔrem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu mo, ye o yarege-ko o dwei diga kam kabira kam. Ko vɔŋɔ kodwoŋi kom de maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu, ye ko yi ko dwei cherubi kadwoŋi kam vɔŋɔ. 12Cherubi kanto kam de yarege ka vɔŋɔ kodwoŋi kom ka dwei diga kam saŋa kadwoŋi kam. Ka de vɔŋɔ dedɔrem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu mo. 13Cherubi selei sem konto vɔna ná yarege ye ya dwei daane, ya maama ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finlei mo. Se nam zege se nɛ baŋa ne mo, ye se jeeri Wɛ diga kam ni dem.
14Ko ná ye gare-jale delo na wó lei de che Wɛ di-yun-gala kam to, Solomon ma pa ba kwei gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to ba ma ba sɔ gare-fefale, ye ba daare ba gɔgere cherubi nyenyero ba ke se yera ne.
15O laam ma daare o pa ba mɔ ywoa yalei pa ya zege Wɛ diga kam yiga ne. Ywoa yalei yam ná twoŋi daane, ya maama dedɔrem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fintɔ-benu mo. Ba ma ke wo-sugila yalo dedɔrem na ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu to ba meeli ywoa yam yuu kom seeni. 16O ta ke chegero mo ye o milimi-te daane. O laam ma kwei-te o ke ywoa yam yuu ne. O ta ma mɔ Pomegara bi nyenyero ye o kwei-te o meeli chegero tem yera ne. 17O ma kwei ywoa yam o chwi Wɛ diga kam yiga ne, ka jazem seeni de ka jagwia seeni. O ma pa ba bwoi ywei delo na zege ka jazem seeni to we, ‘Jakim’. Delo maa na zege jagwia seeni to maa ye ‘Bowaza’.

english_text:
The Furnishings for the Temple
(1 Kings 7.23-51)
1 Solomon had a bronze altar made that was nine meters square and four and a half meters high. 2He also gave orders to make a large metal bowl called the Sea. It was 4.5 meters across, just over two meters deep, and 13.5 meters around. 3Its outer edge was decorated with two rows of carvings of bulls, ten bulls to about every 45 centimeters, all made from the same piece of metal as the bowl. 4The bowl itself sat on top of twelve bronze bulls, with three bulls facing outward in each of four directions. 5The sides of the bowl were 75 millimeters thick, and its rim was in the shape of a cup that curved outward like flower petals. The bowl held about 60,000 liters.
6 He also made ten small bowls and put five on each side of the large bowl. The small bowls were used to wash the animals that were burned on the altar as sacrifices, and the priests used the water in the large bowl to wash their hands.
7 Ten gold lampstands were also made according to the plans. Solomon placed these lampstands inside the temple, five on each side of the main room. 8 He also made ten tables and placed them in the main room, five on each side. And he made 100 small gold sprinkling bowls.
9Solomon gave orders to build two courtyards: a smaller one that only priests could use and a larger one. The doors to these courtyards were covered with bronze. 10The large bowl called the Sea was placed near the southeast corner of the temple.
11Huram made shovels, sprinkling bowls, and pans for hot ashes. Here is a list of the other furnishings he made for God's temple: 12two columns, two bowl-shaped caps for the tops of these columns, two chain designs on the caps, 13400 pomegranates in two rows for the chain designs, 14the stands and the small bowls, 15the large bowl and the twelve bulls that held it up, 16pans for hot ashes, as well as shovels and meat forks.
Huram made all these things out of polished bronze 17by pouring melted bronze into the clay molds he had set up near the Jordan River, between Succoth and Zeredah.
18There were so many bronze furnishings that no one ever knew how much bronze it took to make them.
19Solomon also gave orders to make the following temple furnishings out of gold: the altar, the tables that held the sacred loaves of bread, 20the lampstands and the lamps that burned in front of the most holy place, 21flower designs, lamps and tongs, 22lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, ladles, fire pans, and the doors to the most holy place and the main room of the temple.
translation_text:
Wɛ diga kam zela
1Solomon déem ma pa ba kwei channa ba ma ba mɔ kaanem bimbini, pa de maŋem ye naba-laara fuga dedɔrem baŋa ne, dedaane de kayɔlɔ seeni. De maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga wɛ-baŋa seeni. 2O laam ma kwei channa o mɔ ware-zon-zɔŋɔ ye o bwoŋi ko yere we, ‘Naneo Kom’. Ko na zege ni dedoa se ko vo ni dedwoŋi to ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga mo. Ka wɛ-baŋa maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni benu. N ná kwei ŋona n maŋe-ka gigilu baŋa ne, ko ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni fintɔ mo ko kaare. 3Ba ma kwei channa ba gɔgere wonnu na nye de nabɛ to ba ke zon-zɔŋɔ kom nia yam seeni ba kaare-ka gene selei. Jatwogo de noa ni maŋem maama jege nabɛ nyenyero fuga mo. Ba déem mɔɔne zon-zɔŋɔ kom de ko nyenyero tem daane mo. 4O ta ma kwei channa o mɔ nabɛ fuga-selei pa se ware-zon-zɔŋɔ kom daŋe se baŋa ne. Nabɛ sem maama ma kwei se kwɛ se jeeri daane mo. Nabɛ setɔ déem jeeri baŋa seeni mo. Se setɔ de jeeri wɛ-zoore seeni. Se setɔ maa jeeri tega-kuri seeni ye setɔ jeeri wɛ-puli seeni. 5Zoŋa kam déem lira se ko maŋe de da-yiga noa maŋem mo. Ka ni dem maa nye de na-zoŋa ni na ye tei to, ye ka laam ta ka nwoŋi ne kantɔgela na ye tei to. Ka wó wane ka jwoŋi garewɛ morro tetɔ na mo.
6O ta ma ke ware-zwe fuga, ye o zege senu diga kam jazem seeni, ye o daare o zege senu ka jagwia seeni. Ba déem jege vara balo ba na wó kwei ba ke zwɛɛm kaanem to mo ba zare zwe sem konto na bam wone. Ko daare, kaanem tiina bam de maa yeini ba sane ba je ware-zon-zɔŋɔ kom wo na bam wone.
7Solomon daa ma pa ba kwei sabu-seŋa ba ma ba mɔ min-zwon-zegero fuga se ko maŋe de ba na jeeli diga kam kikia se ya taa ye tei to, ye o daare o kwei-te o zege Wɛ diga kam wone. Te tenu mo o déem kwei o zege jazem seeni, ye o daare o kwei tenu o zege jagwia seeni.
8O ta ma ke tabollo fuga. O ma kwei tento de o zege Wɛ diga kam wone. Tenu déem zege jazem seeni mo, ye tenu de wo jagwia seeni. O ta ma ke sabu-seŋa zwe bi se ba taa jege-se ba zezage na.
9O ma lɔ konkɔlɔ kolo na wora kaanem tiina bam ŋwaane to, dedaane konkɔlɔ-kamunu kom, de ko ni-bworru tem. O laam ma kwei channa o taare ko bworru tem maama. 10O ma kwei ware-zon-zɔŋɔ kom o zege Wɛ diga kam tega-kuri saŋa kam seeni se ko maŋe de ka gugworo kolo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to.
11Huram ta ma mɔ zwe selo ba na wó taa mae ba pɛ tentwarem to, de sɛbullu, de na-zwe. O déem ma toŋe Wɛ diga kam totoŋa yalo Pɛ Solomon na pɛ‑o to o ti. 12Ko maa ye:
Channa ywoa yalei yam, de wo-sugila yalei yam na wo ya yuu ne to, de channa kam na lɛɛne daane ka kwoli wo-sugila yam to, 13dedaane Pomegara bia yana nyenyero telo o na gɔgere o yage channa kalo na lɛɛne daane to ne. Pomegera nyenyero tem maa ye gene selei na kwoli wo-sugili dedoa maama to.
14O déem ta mɔɔne torokooro tem, de te ware-zwe sem, 15dedaane ware-zon-zɔŋɔ kom, de ko kuri channa nabɛ nyenyero fuga-selei sem, 16ko ta woli de zwe selo ba na wó taa mae ba pɛ tentwarem to, de sɛbullu tem, de wonnu telo ba na wó taa mae ba chu nɔna ba le to.
Ko ná ye Wɛ diga yera zela yam maama, Huram-Abi déem kwei channa kalo na kwɛ to mo o ke te maama o pa Pɛ Solomon se ba taa mae ba toŋa Baŋa Wɛ diga kam totoŋa. 17Pɛ wom déem pɛ ba mɔ tento maama kamɔ-mɔra jeiga kalo na wo Jɔdan bwolo kom ne se ko maŋe de Sukofa de Zereda tetare laŋa ne to mo. 18Solomon déem pɛ ba ke wonnu tento dedɛ mo. Mo kokuri ba wo lɔre te channa kam dunni na mae tei to.
19Solomon déem pɛ ba ke Wɛ diga kam wo zela yam maama. Ko maa ye:
Sabu-seŋa bimbini dem, de tabollo telo baŋa ne ba na tiŋi bworobwooru tem na zege Wɛ yiga ne to mo.
20O ta pɛ ba kwei sabu-seŋa kalo na ye chekke to mo ba ke min-zwon-zegero kom, de te min-zwonnu tem. Te maa zege Wɛ di-yuu kom wone te pae pwooni, ne ko na maŋe tei to.
21O ma pa ba gɔgere sabu-seŋa punnu nyenyero, ye ba kwei sabu-seŋa ba ke min-zwonnu, de wonnu telo na dwei mini dem to. 22O ma pa ba kwei sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to ba ke wonnu telo na fɔge te kwɛ mini dem to, de ware-zwe, de zon-tanlɛ selo ba na mae ba zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa to, dedaane min-chala zwe. O ta ma pa ba kwei sabu-seŋa ba taare Wɛ di-yun-gala kam ni-bworru tem, dedaane bworru telo na zoore Wɛ diga kam tete to.

english_text:
1 After the Lord's temple was finished, Solomon put in its storage rooms everything that his father David had dedicated to the Lord, including the gold and silver, and the objects used in worship.
Solomon Brings the Sacred Chest to the Temple
(1 Kings 8.1-13)
2-3 The sacred chest had been kept on Mount Zion, also known as the city of David. But Solomon decided to have the chest moved to the temple while everyone was in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Shelters during the seventh month.
Solomon called together all the important leaders of Israel. 4-5Then the priests and the Levites picked up the sacred chest, the sacred tent, and the objects used for worship, and they carried them to the temple. 6Solomon and a crowd of people stood in front of the chest and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted.
7The priests carried the chest into the most holy place and put it under the winged creatures, 8whose wings covered both the chest and the poles used for carrying it. 9The poles were so long that they could be seen from just outside the most holy place, but not from anywhere else. And they stayed there from then on.
10 The only things kept in the chest were the two flat stones Moses had put there when the Lord made his agreement with the people of Israel at Mount Sinai, after bringing them out of Egypt.
11-13 The priests of every group had gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable to the Lord. The Levite musicians, including Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives, were wearing robes of fine linen. They were standing on the east side of the altar, playing cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments. One hundred and twenty priests were with these musicians, and they were blowing trumpets.
They were praising the Lord by playing music and singing:
“The Lord is good,
and his love never ends.”
Suddenly a cloud filled the temple as the priests were leaving the holy place. 14The Lord's glory was in that cloud, and the light from it was so bright that the priests could not stay inside to do their work.
translation_text:
1Ko déem dɛ konto mo ye Solomon pa ba toŋe Baŋa Wɛ diga kam totoŋa maama ba ti. O laam ma ja wonnu telo maama o kwo David déem na pɔɔre o zege Wɛ ŋwaane to o ja o zo ka wo. Ko maa ye lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa wonnu tem de diga kam wo zela yam maama mo o kwei o zege Wɛ diga kam lonne tiŋim jei sem ne.
Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam
2Solomon déem pɛ ni mo yi Isarele dwi tiina nakwa bam maama se ba ba Jerusalem. Ko ye ba pwa bam de ba sɔ-yuni tem yiga tiina bam maama mo konto. O déem bwoŋi-ba se ba ke daane ba ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam na wo David teo Zion ne to ba ja ba zo Wɛ diga kam. 3Ba maama ma ke daane ba yi Pɛ Solomon tei kuri delo na ke chane serepɛ chana kam ne to maŋa ne. 4Isarele tiina nakwa bam maama na jeeri konto to, Levi dwi tiina badwonna ma zeiŋi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam wɛɛne 5se ba ja ba zo Wɛ diga kam. Levi tiina bam de kaanem tiina bam de ma zeŋe Wɛ wara-vwei dem dedaane de yera zela yam maama ba ja ba kɛ. 6Pɛ Solomon de Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama ma vo ba gilimi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne. Ba ma kwei pei de naane dedɛ ba ma ba ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ. Vara bam tiini ba daga dedɛ pa se nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware ba ni o ga.
7Wɛ kaanem tiina bam ma zeŋe Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba zo Wɛ diga kam wone ba zege-ka di-yun-gala kam na tiini ka ye wose Wɛ ŋwaane to wone. Ba déem zege dakaa kam cherubi vɔna yam kuri ne mo. 8Cherubi selei sem vɔna yam twe mo wɛɛne ya kwoli dakaa kam de ka dɛ selo ba na mae ba zeŋe-ka to. 9Dɛ sem konto tiini se dɔra dedɛ. Ko ma pa se nɔɔno ná zo Wɛ diga kam o zege ka ni ne, o wae o tole o nae dɛ sem. Ko nam ná ye pwooni dem ne mo o zega, o ba nae-se. Se ta zege da de zem maama. 10Woŋo kolo yerane déem na wo Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam wone to mo ye kandwa-pelɛ selei selo Moses déem na kwei o ke-da Sinayi peo kom baŋa ne to. Dáane mo Baŋa Wɛ déem gwoni ni de Isarele tiina bam maŋa kalo ba na nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba kɛ to.
11Kaanem tiina bam na nwoŋi sɔ-yuu kolo ye ba wo dáane to maama nam ya kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane mo. Ba ma nwoŋi Wɛ di-yuu kom wone ba vo dáa. 12Levi tiina balo na ye lein-leena to ma vo ba zege kaanem bimbini dem wɛ-puli saŋa kam seeni. Banto maa ye Asaf, de Heman, de Jedutuna, ko woli de ba bia, de ba chorro tem maama. Ba déem zo gare-fefale mo, ye ba laam zei zwe, de kwanno dwi dwi, ba jege-te ba ke kwɛɛra. Kaanem tiina bi de finlei (120) de ma ba ba woli lein-leena bam konto wone, ye ba wui nabwanno. 13Nabɔn-wura bam, de lein-leena bam kwɛɛra zela sɔɔ kom maŋe daane lanyerane pa kwora dedoa zaŋe wɛɛne ka seini Baŋa Wɛ. Ba ma leeni ba tei Baŋa Wɛ ye ba we:
“O tiini o lamma,
ye o swono kom wora taa wuu.”
Kunkwoŋo ma pɔpɔ ko zo ko su Baŋa Wɛ diga kam maama. 14Wɛ kaanem tiina bam ware ba jwoori ba zo da ba toŋe ba totoŋa, kunkwoŋo kom na wora ye Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom pwooni yɔɔre de pe jei sem maama to ŋwaane.

english_text:
1Solomon prayed:
“Our Lord, you said that you
would live in a dark cloud.
2Now I've built a glorious temple
where you can live forever.”
Solomon Speaks to the People
(1 Kings 8.14-21)
3Solomon turned toward the people standing there. Then he blessed them 4-6 and said:
Praise the Lord God of Israel! He brought his people out of Egypt long ago and later kept his promise to make my father David the king of Israel. The Lord also promised him that Jerusalem would be the city where his temple will be built, and now that promise has come true.
7When my father wanted to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel, 8the Lord said, “It's good that you want to build a temple where I can be worshiped. 9But you're not the one to do it. Your son will build the temple to honor me.”
10The Lord has done what he promised. I am now the king of Israel, and I've built a temple for the Lord our God. 11I've also put the sacred chest in the temple. And in that chest are the two flat stones on which is written the solemn agreement the Lord made with our ancestors when he rescued them from Egypt.
Solomon Prays at the Temple
(1 Kings 8.22-53)
12-13Earlier, Solomon had a bronze platform made that was about two meters square and over a meter high, and he put it in the center of the outer courtyard near the altar. Solomon stood on the platform facing the altar with everyone standing behind him. Then he lifted his arms toward heaven; he knelt down 14and prayed:
Lord God of Israel, no other god in heaven or on earth is like you!
You never forget the agreement you made with your people, and you are loyal to anyone who faithfully obeys your teachings. 15My father David was your servant, and today you have kept every promise you made to him.
16 You promised that someone from his family would always be king of Israel, if they do their best to obey you, just as he did. 17Please keep this promise you made to your servant David. 18 There's not enough room in all of heaven for you, Lord God. How could you possibly live on earth in this temple I have built? 19But I ask you to answer my prayer. 20 This is the temple where you have chosen to be worshiped. Please watch over it day and night and listen when I turn toward it and pray. 21I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you, and so whenever any of us look toward this temple and pray, answer from your home in heaven and forgive our sins.
22Suppose someone accuses a person of a crime, and the accused has to stand in front of the altar in your temple and say, “I swear I am innocent!” 23Listen from heaven and decide who is right. Then punish the guilty person and let the innocent one go free.
24Suppose your people Israel sin against you, and then an enemy defeats them. If they come to this temple and beg for forgiveness, 25listen from your home in heaven. Forgive them and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors.
26Suppose your people sin against you, and you punish them by holding back the rain. If they stop sinning and turn toward this temple to pray in your name, 27listen from your home in heaven and forgive them. The people of Israel are your servants, so teach them to live right. And send rain on the land you promised them forever.
28Sometimes the crops may dry up or rot or be eaten by locusts or grasshoppers, and your people will be starving. Sometimes enemies may surround their towns, or your people will become sick with deadly diseases. 29Please listen when anyone in Israel truly feels sorry and sincerely prays with arms lifted toward your temple. 30You know what is in everyone's heart. So from your home in heaven answer their prayers, according to what they do and what is in their hearts. 31Then your people will worship you and obey you for as long as they live in the land you gave their ancestors.
32Foreigners will hear about you and your mighty power, and some of them will come to live among your people Israel. If any of them pray toward this temple, 33listen from your home in heaven and answer their prayers. Then everyone on earth will worship you, just as your own people Israel do, and they will know that I have built this temple in your honor.
34Sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you. 35Answer their prayers from heaven and give them victory.
36Everyone sins. But when your people sin against you, suppose you get angry enough to let their enemies drag them away to foreign countries. 37-39Later, they may feel sorry for what they did and ask your forgiveness. Answer them when they pray toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, here in this land you gave their ancestors. From your home in heaven, listen to their sincere prayers and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
40 Lord God, hear us when we pray in this temple. 41 Come to your new home, where we have already placed the sacred chest, which is the symbol of your strength. I pray that when the priests announce your power to save people, those who are faithful to you will celebrate what you've done for them. 42Always remember the love you had for your servant David, so that you will not reject your chosen kings.
translation_text:
1Pɛ Solomon ma ware Wɛ o we, “Baŋa Wɛ, nmo maŋe n ta n we, nmo wó ta‑n zoore kunkwon-lilirru wone mo. 2Amo nam lɔge sɔ-fɔrɔ mo a pa‑m, se n ta‑n zoore ko wone taa wuu.” 3Isarele nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama na zege da konto to mo Solomon pipiri o jeeri-ba. O ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage ba baŋa ne. 4O maa we:
“Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to maŋe de tia! O yɔɔre o ke o su ni delo o na pwooli de a kwo David to mo. Wɛ déem tage o we, 5‘Ko na zege maŋa kalo a na jaane a nɔɔna bam a nwoŋi Ejipti to, a ya ta wo kuri teo Isarele dwia yam wone se ba lɔ diga ba ma zuli a yere da. A nam wo kuri nɔɔn-nɔɔno se kotu taa nii a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. 6Ko laam nam na ye tei to, amo mo kuri Jerusalem se ko taa ye teo kolo wone ba na wó taa zuli-ne to, ye a daare a kuri David se o taa di paare a nɔɔna bam baŋa ne.’ ”
7Solomon ta ma ta o we:
“Amo kwo David ya maŋe o boŋe o ja se o lɔ Wɛ diga se ba taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to yere da mo. 8Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, ‘Nmo ke chega de n na jaane boboŋa se n lɔ diga amo yere zula ŋwaane to. 9Ko nam dae nmo mo jege se n lɔ diga kam n pa-ne. Se ko ye nmo tete bu mo wó lɔ diga kam amo yere zula ŋwaane.’
10Leile konto Baŋa Wɛ ke o su tei maama o na pwooli we, o wó ke to mo. Amo laam mo leiri a kwo David yuu ne a ji Isarele teo pɛ. A ma sɛ a lɔ Wɛ diga kam se Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to yere na zula da. 11A ta ma kwei Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam a zege ka wone. Baŋa Wɛ ni delo o na gwoni de Isarele tiina bam to na popone kandwa-pelɛ selo baŋa ne to maa wo ka wone.”
Solomon wɛ-lworo kom
12Solomon ma vo o zege o jeeri Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem ye Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama zege ba nia. O ma zeiŋi o je sem wɛɛne se o ware Wɛ. 13O nam ya pɛ ba ke channa bimbini mo ba kwei ba zege Wɛ diga kam pwooni yiga konkɔlɔ kom tetare dem ne. De dedɔrem baŋa maŋem dedaane de kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem déem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu mo. De wɛ-baŋa maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni betɔ. Solomon ma vo o zege bimbini dem konto baŋa ne o kuni nadwoona, ye o daare o zeiŋi o je sem wɛyuu ne. 14O ma lwoori Wɛ o we:
“Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to, wɛ dedwoŋi tera wɛyuu ne naa tega baŋa ne de na nye de nmo. Nmo yɔɔre n swoi balo na tɔge n chwei sem de ba wo maama to, de n na yeini n ke n sui ni delo n na gwoni de-ba se n ke to. 15Ko ná ye amo kwo David na ye nmo tontoŋeno to, nmo na tiŋi ni ded‑o se n ke tei to, mo n seene n ke te maama se ko ba ko yi zem.
16Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom, a laam lwoori‑m se n ke tei n na pwooli de a kwo David ye n we, o dwi dem bá ga nɔɔno se o di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne, ne ba ná kwaane ba sɛ nmo nia yam ne David tete na ke tei to. 17Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to, nam sɛ se kolo nmo na pwooli de n tontoŋeno David to seene ko ji chega. 18Amo Tu Wɛ, nmo wó seene n ta‑n zoore de nabiina tega baŋa ne na? Wɛyuu de wɛ-baŋa jei sem maama ne, pwola tera ka na maŋe de nmo. Tetɛ mo diga kanto a na lɔge to wó wane ka yi n zoorem? 19Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, a ye nmo tontoŋeno mo. Nam pa n yiga taa wo a wɛ-lworo kom wone. Cheigi a keira kam se n daare n sɛ a na lwoori‑m woŋo kolo to. 20Popo, pa se n yia taa page diga kanto baŋa ne maŋa maama, tete de wea. Nmo maŋe n ta we ka zege n yere dem zula ŋwaane mo. Maŋa kalo maama ne a ná zege a jeeri diga kanto a lwoori‑m, se n cheigi a wɛ-lworo kom. 21Ko ná ye amo de n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam, dé ná zege dé jeeri nmo diga kam se dé lwoori‑m, se n jeini n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom wone n cheigi dé wɛ-lworo n daare n yage n chɛ debam.
22Nɔɔno ná ke o chɔge o dwoŋi yiga ye ba ja‑o ba zo nmo diga kam wone se o zege nmo kaanem bimbini dem yiga ne o du duuri we, o wo ke o chɔge, 23jeini telaao ne n cheigi o taane dem se n daare n ke kolo na maŋe to. Pɔɔre chega n tontoŋena bam tetare ne. Pa se puseŋ-nyeno wom na waarem delo na maŋe de o kikia to, se n daare n pa wolo na jege chega to na o bora.
24Nmo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam wɛleera ná pɛ se ba dona di-ba jara wone, ye ba laam ná pipiri ba jwoori nmo tei ba zo nmo diga kam wone ba ma n yere dem ba lwoori‑m se n duri ba yibwona n daare n yage n chɛ-ba, 25jeini telaao ne n cheigi ba keira kam konto. Seene n yage ba wɛleera yam n ma‑n chɛ-ba, n daare n ja-ba n jwoori tega kalo nmo na kwei n pa ba de ba nabaara bam to.
26Nmo nɔɔna bam wɛleera ná pɛ se n ja kunkwoŋo kom pa se doa ba nena, ye ba laam ná leiri ba wo ba zege ba jeeri n diga kam ba ma n yere dem ba lwoori wolim nmo tei ne de n na waare-ba tei to, 27nam jeini Wɛ telaao ne n cheigi ba keira kam. Yage n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam wɛleera n chɛ-ba, se n daare n bere-ba chwo-laao se ba taa tɔga. Pa se doa jwoori ka ne tega kanto n na kwei n pa n nɔɔna se ba taa tei to baŋa ne.
28Da-kore de jawe-chɛɛro ná tu te yi ba tega kam, ye jaweero naa kayere dwi dwi ná chɔge ba kara wodiiru tem, ye ba dona ná zaŋe ba teo kolo maama baŋa ne, naa ko ná ye lɛɛro telo maama mo yi n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam, 29cheigi ba keira kam. Ba wolo maama ná zeiŋi o jea o jeeri n diga kanto ye o lwoori‑m naa o keeri o jare‑m, o wo na tiini ko chɔge to ŋwaane, 30se n jeini n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom ne n cheigi o keira kam konto. Yage ba maama wɛleera n chɛ-ba se n daare n woli-ba. Ke de ba dedoa dedoa se ko maŋe de ba kikia na ye tei to, nmo yerane mo na yei nabiinu boboŋa na ye tei to ŋwaane. 31Konto wó pa se n nɔɔna bam taa kɔre‑m, ye ba taa tɔge n chwei sem da yalo maama ba na wó taa ŋwe ye ba zoore tega kalo nmo na kwei n pa dé nabaara bam to wone.
32Ko nam ná ye veira balo na dae n nɔɔna Isarele tiina to, banto wae ba zege sa-teo ne ba tui ywo-seeni, ba na nigi n ŋwa to ŋwaane. Ko ye n yere na zaŋe de n na mɛ n dam n toŋe totoŋ-kamuna to ŋwaane mo banto yeini ba tui ywo. Banto ná tu ba zege ba jeeri n diga kanto ba lwoori‑m, 33se n jeini n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom ne n cheigi ba wɛ-lworo kom konto. Ke n su kolo maama ba na lwoori n tei ne to, se logo baŋa nɔɔna maama da ko ŋwaane ba ni nmo yere dem ŋwa, ye ba taa kɔre‑m, nenɛɛne nmo tete nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam na ke tei to. Ba maa wó lɔre we, diga kanto a na lɔge to seene ka ye nmo yere dem zula ŋwaane mo.
34Nmo nɔɔna bam ná nwoŋi se ba vo mɛ maama n na toŋe-ba se ba kwaare jara de ba dona, ye ba ná zege ba jeeri teo konto n na kuri to, de Wɛ diga kanto a na lɔga nmo yere dem zula ŋwaane to ba lwoori wolim nmo tei ne, 35se n jeini Wɛ telaao ne n cheigi ba wɛ-lworo kom de ba na ŋwane tei n yiga ne to, se n daare n ke chega n pa-ba.
36Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na ba ke wɛleera. Nmo nɔɔna bam nam ná ke wɛleera pa se nmo bane zaŋe de-ba, n wae n yage se ba dona di-ba pa se ba ji peena sa-teo ne yiga yiga naa bwola bwola de. 37Jei sem konto ne ba boboŋa ná jwoori ye ba leiri ba wo Wɛ ŋwaane, se n cheigi ba wɛ-lworo. Ba ná zege ba dona bam teo ne ba lwoori‑m ye ba we, ‘Dé seene dé tusi mo ye dé ke lwarem de puseŋa kikia’, 38ba maa ná pipiri ba jwoori n tei de ba wo maama, nam sɛ se n cheigi ba wɛ-lworo kom. Ba ná maŋe sa-teo ne ba zege ba jeeri tega kanto n na pɛ ba nabaara bam to, de teo kolo nmo na kuri n pa n tete to, de a na lɔge diga kalo nmo yere dem zula ŋwaane to, 39se n jeini n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom ne, n cheigi ba wɛ-lworo kom de ba keira kam, se n daare n ke chega n pa-ba. Nam kwei n nɔɔna na ke kolo maama ba chɔge n yiga to n yage n chɛ-ba.
40Amo Tu Wɛ, nam yɔɔre n pa se n yi taa page diga kanto baŋa ne, ye n pore n zwa se n ta‑n cheigi wara yalo maama ba na yeini ba lwoori‑m ka wone to.
41Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nam zaŋe
n ba n zo n jeiŋa jei sem ne!
Tɔge de n ni-gwonim dakaa kam n ba n ta‑n zoore da,
se n dam dem bere jaja!
Pa se n zaane taa wo kaanem tiina bam baŋa ne,
ne ba zo gare-laaro mo to.
Pa se n tete nɔɔna bam taa jege wopwolo,
n na yeini n ke-ba lanyerane to ŋwaane.
42Yé fɔge n ve wolo n laam na tiŋi
se o di paare n nɔɔna baŋa ne to.
Nam guli Pɛ David gula,
de nmo na gwoni ni ded‑o
n swono kom ŋwaane to.”

english_text:
Solomon Dedicates the Temple
(1 Kings 8.62-66)
1 As soon as Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and burned up the offerings. The Lord's dazzling glory then filled the temple, 2and the priests could not go in.
3 When the crowd of people saw the fire and the Lord's glory, they knelt down and worshiped the Lord. They prayed:
“The Lord is good,
and his love never ends.”
4-5Solomon and the people dedicated the temple to the Lord by sacrificing 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep. 6Everybody stood up during the ceremony. The priests were in their assigned places, blowing their trumpets. And the Levites faced them, playing the musical instruments that David had made for them to use when they praised the Lord for his never-ending love.
7On that same day, Solomon dedicated the courtyard in front of the temple and got it ready to be used for worship. The bronze altar he had made was too small, so he used the courtyard to offer sacrifices to please the Lord and grain sacrifices, and also to send up in smoke the fat from the other offerings.
8For 7 days, Solomon and the crowd celebrated the Festival of Shelters, and people came from as far away as the Egyptian Gorge in the south and Lebo-Hamath in the north. 9Then on the next day, everyone came together for worship. They had celebrated a total of 14 days, 7 days for the dedication of the altar and 7 more days for the festival. 10Then on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent everyone home. They left very happy because of all the good things the Lord had done for David and Solomon, and for his people Israel.
The Lord Appears to Solomon Again
(1 Kings 9.1-9)
11The Lord's temple and Solomon's palace were now finished. In fact, everything Solomon had planned to do was completed.
12Some time later, the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream and said:
I heard your prayer, and I have chosen this temple as the place where sacrifices will be offered to me.
13Suppose I hold back the rain or send locusts to eat the crops or make my people suffer with deadly diseases. 14If my own people will humbly pray and turn back to me and stop sinning, then I will answer them from heaven. I will forgive them and make their land fertile once again. 15I will hear the prayers made in this temple, 16because it belongs to me, and this is where I will be worshiped forever. I will never stop watching over it.
17Your father David obeyed me, and now, Solomon, you must do the same. Obey my laws and teachings, 18 and I will keep my solemn promise to him that someone from your family will always be king of Israel.
19But if you or any of the people of Israel disobey my laws or start worshiping foreign gods, 20I will pull you out of this land I gave you. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped, so that people everywhere will think it is only a joke and will make fun of it. 21This temple is now magnificent. But when these things happen, everyone who walks by it will be shocked and will ask, “Why did the Lord do such a terrible thing to his people and to this temple?” 22Then they will answer, “It was because the people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.”
translation_text:
Wɛ diga kam kwɛɛm
1 Pwa 8:62-66
1Solomon na yɔɔre o ware Wɛ o ti to, mo mini zege wɛyuu ne de chu de di zwɛɛm pɛɛre dem, de kaanem yadwonna yam kula. Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom pwooni ma yɔɔre ko li Wɛ diga kam maama. 2Kaanem tiina bam maa wo wane Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wo se ba zo, Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom pwooni na li-ka to ŋwaane. 3Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama na nɛ we, mini nwoŋi wɛyuu ne de ba tega, ye Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom de jwoŋi Wɛ diga kam to mo ba vwi ba yibia tega ne ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Ba ma ke o lei ba we:
“O tiini o lamma,
ye o swono kom wora taa wuu.”
4Pɛ Solomon dedaane nɔɔna bam maama ma kwei pɛɛra ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. 5Pɛ wom déem kwei naane morro finlei-telei (22,000), ko woli de pei de bone morro bi de finlei (120,000) mo o pa se ba ma ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. O de nɔɔna bam maama ma ke konto ba pore Wɛ diga kam o yere zula ŋwaane. 6Kaanem tiina bam déem ma vo ba zege ba zega jei ne ye ba jege ba nabwanno ba wui. Levi tiina bam de ma zege ba jeeri-ba ye ba zei kwɛɛra zela ba kwɛɛre ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Pɛ David nam ya ke-ya mo o pa-ba, se ba taa mae ba tei Baŋa Wɛ o swono kom na wora taa wuu to ŋwaane. Konto maama na jege ko ke to, de Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama zege wɛɛne mo.
7Solomon ma pore konkɔlɔ kom na wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam yiga ne to se ko taa ye wose Wɛ ŋwaane. O ma zege konkɔlɔ kom tetare dem seeni o kwei zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de wodiu pɛɛra, de vara lara kalo na wora yazura pɛɛra ŋwaane to o ke kaanem dem. Kokuri to, channa kaanem bimbini delo o déem na pɛ ba lɔ to muri se kaanem dem konto maama wane de ke de baŋa ne.
8Solomon de Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom na wo o tei ne to kwei da yarepɛ mo se ba di kuri dem. Ba kɔgɔ kom déem daga dedɛ ye ba nwoŋi Isarele jei maama ne, ko zege Lebo-Hamafa teo ne se ko yi Ejipti bu-nɔgɔ kom seeni. 9Tega na poore ye ko ke da nana to, nɔɔna bam daa ma jeeri daane se ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Kokuri to ba maŋe ba kwei da yarepɛ mo kaanem bimbini dem kwɛɛm totoŋa ŋwaane, ye ba daare ba jeeri da yarepɛ ba woli da ba ma ba di kuri dem. 10Chane serepɛ chana kam da finlei-yatɔ dɛ dem ne, Solomon ma bane nɔɔna bam se ba jwoori ba sam. Ba na maa jwoori sɔŋɔ to, ba déem jege wopwolo dedɛ de Baŋa Wɛ na ke wo-laaro telo o pa David, de Solomon, de o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam to.
Baŋa Wɛ daa veere o tete de Solomon
11Pɛ Solomon déem na lɔge Baŋa Wɛ diga kam, de o tete sɔŋɔ kom o ti, ye o daare o ke o boboŋa na jaane se o ke tei maama tento baŋa ne to, 12mo Baŋa Wɛ veere o tete ded‑o tete ne o we:
“Nmo na lwoori kolo maama amo tei ne to, a niga. A ta ma pɔɔre jeiga kanto a pa a tete, se nɔɔna taa ke kaanem da ba pa-ne.
13Ne amo ná jaane kunkwoŋo kom mo pa se doa ba nena, naa a ná yage ni se kayere yo se deilimi á wodiiru maama, naa jawe-chɛɛro mo a ná de amo nɔɔna tetare ne, 14pa se nɔɔna balo na ye amo nyem to ná gwooni ba tete, ye ba lwoori-ne ba daare ba bwei se ba lɔre amo boboŋa, ye ba ta ná pipiri ba yage ba puseŋa kikia yam, amo de nam wó zege Wɛ telaao ne a cheigi ba wara yam. A maa wó kwei ba wɛleera yam a chɛ-ba, ye a daare a yɔɔre a kwɛ ba tega kam a pa-ba. 15Amo yi nam wó taa page diga kanto baŋa ne, ye a pore a zwa se a taa cheigi wara yalo maama á na yeini á lwoori-ne ka wone to. 16Kokuri to, amo pɔɔre diga kanto mo se ka taa ye wose, se a yere taa wora taa wuu. Amo yi page ka baŋa ne mo, ye a boboŋa de wó taa wo ka wone maŋa maama.
17Ko nam ná ye nmo, n ná yɔɔre n tɔge a chwei sem, ne n kwo David déem na ke tei to, ye n ná sɛ n tɔge a nia yam, de a bera yam, de a chullu tem, 18amo laam wó pa se n dwi dem taa di paare taa wuu. A na gwoni ni tei de nmo kwo David we, o dwi dem bá ga nɔɔno se o di Isarele teo kom paare to wó seene ko ji chega.
19Abam nam ná ywori amo chwoŋa kam ne ye á ve a nia yam de a bera yam, á daare á pipiri á zuli wa yadwonna, 20amo laam wó zeili abam se á daa yé ta‑á zoore tega kanto a na kwei a pa abam to baŋa ne. A maa wó ve diga kanto a ya na sɛ se ka taa ye wose a yere zula ŋwaane to de. Konto ná kea, dwi-gɛ tiina maama laam wó taa jege diga kam mo ba mɔna ye ba gwoona. 21Diga kanto zem na jege yere to, nɔɔna maama laam ná dɛ da se ba kɛ, ko wó ke-ba yaau mo ye ba we, ‘Bɛ mo ye Baŋa Wɛ pa se lɛɛro tento yi ba tega kam de ba Wɛ diga kam?’ 22Nɔɔna maa wó leiri we, ‘Ba tete mo mɛ ba kwaga ba ya Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye ba nabaara bam Wɛ to. Wonto nam ya mo jaane-ba o nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne. Ba nam na pipiri ba tɔge wa yadwonna ye ba zuli-ya to ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se lɛɛro tento yi-ba.’ ”

english_text:
Other Things Solomon Did
(1 Kings 9.10-28)
1It took 20 years for the Lord's temple and Solomon's palace to be built. 2After that, Solomon had his workers rebuild the towns that Hiram had given him. Then Solomon sent Israelites to live in those towns.
3Solomon attacked and captured the town of Hamath-Zobah. 4He ordered his workers to build the town of Tadmor in the desert and some towns in Hamath where he could keep his supplies. 5He strengthened Upper Beth-Horon and Lower Beth-Horon by adding walls and gates that could be locked. 6He did the same thing to the town of Baalath and to the cities where he kept supplies, chariots, and horses. Solomon ordered his workers to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere else in his kingdom.
7-9Solomon did not force the Israelites to do his work. Instead, they were his soldiers, officers, army commanders, and cavalry troops. But he did make slaves of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who were living in Israel. These were the descendants of those foreigners the Israelites did not destroy, and they remained Israel's slaves.
10Solomon appointed 250 officers to be in charge of his workers.
11Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the part of Jerusalem called David's City to her new palace that Solomon had built. The sacred chest had been kept in David's City, which made his palace sacred, and so Solomon's wife could no longer live there.
12Solomon offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built in front of the temple porch. 13 He followed the requirements that Moses had given for sacrifices offered on the Sabbath, on the first day of each month, the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters.
14Solomon then assigned the priests and the Levites their duties at the temple, and he followed the instructions that his father, the man of God, had given him. Some of the Levites were to lead music and help the priests in their duties, and others were to guard the temple gates 15and the storage rooms. The priests and Levites followed these instructions exactly.
16Everything Solomon had planned to do was now finished—from the laying of the temple's foundation to its completion.
17Solomon went to Ezion-Geber and Eloth, two Edomite towns on the Red Sea. 18Hiram sent him ships and some of his experienced sailors. They went with Solomon's own sailors to the country of Ophir and brought back more than 15 tons of gold for Solomon.
translation_text:
Solomon totoŋa yadwonna
1Pɛ Solomon déem kwei bena finlei mo o ma o lɔ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam de o tete sɔŋɔ kom maama. 2Solomon ma pa ba jwoori ba fɔge ba lɔ teene delo Hiram na kwei o pa‑o to, ye o daare o pa Isarele tiina bam vo ba zoore de wone. 3Solomon ma vo o jeeri Hamafa-Zoba teo de jara, ye o wane-ko o di. 4O ta ma pa ba fɔge ba lɔ Tademora ba zege kagoa kam ne, de teene dedwonna na wo Hamafa kateiri dem wone, ye o lɔ-de se ba taa tiŋi zela de wone to. 5O daa ta pɛ se ba fɔge ba lɔ Bɛte-Horon teo kom na wo baŋa seeni to, de Bɛte-Horon teo kom na wo kuri seeni to mo o pe o zege de dam. De maa jege kabiri-lilirru, ye de ni-bworru tem maa jege luuru. 6O ta ma fɔge o lɔ Baalafe, de teene delo o na wó taa tiŋi zela dwi dwi, de jara-keim torokooro, de sisein-nɔɔna da to. O ta pɛ se ba lɔ o boboŋa na jaane kolo maama se o lɔ to mo Jerusalem ne, de Lebanon ne, de jei selo maama o na di paare da to.
7-8Solomon na fe nɔɔna balo se ba taa toŋe totoŋ-dɛɛra to déem ye Hiti tiina, de Amori tiina, de Pɛrizi tiina, de Hivi tiina, de Jebusi tiina mo. Banto dae Isarele dwi tiina ye ba badaara ta zoore Isarele tega kam ne. Ba maa ye dwia yalo Isarele tiina bam ya na wo yɔɔre ba chɔge to bia mo. Ba ta ye kabɛ mo de zem maama. 9Ko nam ná ye Isarele tiina bam tete, Solomon déem wo pɛ se banto ji o kabɛ se ba taa toŋe totoŋ-dɛɛra ba pa‑o. O nam pɛ se ba ji o jar-keira, de ba dedɛɛra, de o jara-keim torokooro dira, dedaane o sisein-dira yiga tiina mo. 10Dedɛɛra balo na nii tontoŋena bam baŋa ne ba pa Solomon to déem ye nɔɔna bia yalei de finnu (250) mo.
11Pɛ Solomon déem ma pa se o kaane wolo na ye Ejipti Pa-faro wom bukɔ to zege David teo kom ne o vo sɔŋɔ kolo o na lɔge o pa‑o to. O nam tage o we, “Ko ná ye Isarele teo pɛ David sɔŋɔ kom, ko wo maŋe se a kaane taa zoore ko wone, ko na ye wose to ŋwaane. Kokuri to, jeiga kalo maama Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ya na zege ka wone to ye wose mo.”
12Solomon laam ma zwɛ vara kaanem bimbini delo o na lɔga o zege Wɛ diga napɔrɔ kom yiga ne to baŋa ne o ke kaanem o pa Baŋa Wɛ. 13O déem ke dɛ wone kaanem delo na maŋe de Moses nia yam na bere tei to mo, ne ko ná ye Wɛ siu da yam, de chan-doŋa kura yam, ko ta woli de bene bene kura yatɔ yam. Kura yanto maa ye Bworobworo-memene kuri dem, de Ga-kwea kuri dem, de Vwoa chwiim kuri dem. 14Solomon déem yɔɔre o ke o tɔge o kwo David bera yam mo, ye o kuri Wɛ kaanem tiina bam popɔra de popɔra se ba taa toŋe ba totoŋa. O ta ma pɔɔre Levi tiina bam de se ba taa leeni ba seini Baŋa Wɛ, ye ba toŋe ba woli Wɛ kaanem tiini bam, ne ko na maŋe de dɛ maama wone totoŋa tei to. O ma kuri Wɛ wara-jei sem ni-yerena bam popɔra de popɔra, se ba taa yere manchwo-peena yam maama. Wɛ tontoŋeno David déem nam maŋe o pa ni se ba ke konto mo. 15David déem na pɛ ni delo maama kaanem tiina bam, de Levi dwi tiina bam totoŋa yam ŋwaane to mo, ba yɔɔre ba ke ba tɔge-de, ne ko ná ye lonne zela tiŋim di sem totoŋa yam de.
16Solomon na pɛ ni se ba toŋe totoŋa yalo to maama déem ke ya ti mo, ko na zege dɛ delo ba na chwi Baŋa Wɛ diga kam kuri to, se ko vo ko yi dɛ delo ba na lɔge-ka ba ti to. Baŋa Wɛ diga kam maama lɔge ka zege ka ti mo konto.
17Pɛ Solomon déem ma vo Ezion-gebera de Elofe. Teene dem konto maa wo Edom laŋa kam ne, ye de wo naneo kom ni ne. 18Pɛ Hiram ma toŋe nabwor-kamunnu o pa Solomon. Hiram nɔɔna balo na yei nabwooru yuŋim to déem mo nii te baŋa ne. Banto ma gwaane de Solomon nɔɔna bam ba yuŋi nabwooru tem ba vo ba yi Ofiri pa ba na sabu-seŋa dedɛ dáane. Ba ma ja sabu-seŋa kilo morro fuga-tenu (15,000) ba jwoori ba vo ba pa Pɛ Solomon.

english_text:
The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon
(1 Kings 10.1-13)
1 The Queen of Sheba heard how famous Solomon was, so she went to Jerusalem to test him with difficult questions. She took along several of her officials, and she loaded her camels with gifts of spices, jewels, and gold. When she arrived, she and Solomon talked about everything she could think of. 2He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
3-4The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, all his servants in their uniforms, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple. 5She said:
Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done. 6But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are greater than I was told. 7Your people and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
8I praise the Lord your God. He is pleased with you and has made you king of Israel. God loves the people of this country and will never desert them, so he has given them a king who will rule fairly and honestly.
9The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, a large amount of jewels, and the best spices anyone had ever seen.
10-12In return, Solomon gave her everything she wanted—even more than she had given him. Then she and her officials went back to their own country.
Solomon's Wealth
(1 Kings 10.14-29)
Hiram's and Solomon's sailors brought gold, juniper wood, and jewels from the country of Ophir. Solomon used the wood to make steps for the temple and palace, and harps and other stringed instruments for the musicians. Nothing like these had ever been made in Judah.
13Solomon received almost 23 tons of gold each year, 14not counting what the merchants and traders brought him. The kings of Arabia and the leaders of Israel also gave him gold and silver.
15Solomon made 200 gold shields that weighed over three kilograms each. 16He also made 300 smaller gold shields that weighed almost two kilograms, and he put these shields in his palace in Forest Hall.
17His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold. 18It had a gold footstool attached to it and armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on each side of the throne, 19and there were two lion statues on each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
20Solomon's cups and dishes in Forest Hall were made of pure gold, because silver was almost worthless in those days.
21Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
22Solomon was the richest and wisest king in the world. 23-24Year after year, other kings came to hear the wisdom God had given him. And they brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
25 Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his horses and chariots, and he owned 12,000 horses that he kept in Jerusalem and other towns.
26 He ruled all the nations from the Euphrates River in the north to the land of Philistia in the south, as far as the border of Egypt.
27While Solomon was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as the sycamore trees in the western foothills. 28 Solomon's horses were brought in from other countries, including Musri.
Solomon Dies
(1 Kings 11.41-43)
29Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the records of Nathan the prophet, Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh, and Iddo the prophet who wrote about Jeroboam son of Nebat. 30After Solomon had ruled 40 years from Jerusalem, 31he died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_text:
Seba ka-pɛ wom taane
1Seba teo ka-pɛ wom déem nigi Pɛ Solomon yere na zaŋe jei maama ne tei to. O ma zaŋe o vo Jerusalem se o faŋe‑o de bwia yalo na dana to o nii. O déem pɛ se o tontoŋena dedɛ tɔge ded‑o ba vo, dedaane kona yalo na zeŋe talwoŋ-ywei dwi dwi, de sabu-seŋa, de kandwa-nyenno dedɛ to.
