O na yi Solomon tei to mo o bwei‑o bwia yalo maama o boboŋa na jaane se o bwei to. 2Solomon de ma leiri o bwia yam maama. Ya ná maŋe ya chana tei de, o wane o leiri ya maama. 3Seba teo ka-pɛ wom ma maane Solomon swa yam na ye tei to. O ta ma na pɛ sɔŋɔ kolo o na lɔge to, 4de wodiiru telo o na yeini o di to, de o na kwɛ o tontoŋena bam jeiŋa jei tei, de balo na zeŋe o wodiu de wo-nyɔɔro ba pa‑o to na zo gare-nyenno telo to, dedaane pɛɛra yalo o na yeini o zwɛ o ma o ke kaanem Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ne to. O na maane tento maama to, ko ma pa o ni yɛ.
5O ma ta de pɛ wom o we, “A ta na wo a tete teo ne ye a ni n ni taane de n swa yam taane to maama seene ko ye chega mo. 6Ko ná dae amo tete mo na tu a na tento maama, a ya wó ta we, ko ye vwa mo. A nam na nigi wonnu telo to wo yi tei maama a yi dento zem na nɛ to chichworo. Nmo swa yam daga ya dwoi ba na taga tei ba bere-ne to. 7Nmo nɔɔna bam de n tontoŋena bam tiini ba jege yu-ywoŋo, ba na wo n tei ne dɛ maama ba cheigi nmo swa taana yam to ŋwaane. 8N Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom maŋe de tia, de o wo na dɛ nmo ye o kuri‑m se n di paare o yere dem ŋwaane to. Baŋa Wɛ na swoi Isarele dwi tiina bam ye o pa ba jeini taa wuu to ŋwaane mo o kuri‑m se n ji ba pɛ, se n daare n tɔge chwoŋa n ta‑n bora chega bora n pa-ba.”
9Ka-pɛ wom déem ma kwei sabu-seŋa na dwoi kilo morro tena (4,000) to o pa Solomon, ko woli de talwoŋ-ywei, de kandwa-nyenno dedɛ. Talwoŋ-ywei nam tera se na jege kuri se yi selo Seba ka-pɛ wom na kwei o pa Pɛ Solomon to.
10Pɛ Hiram tontoŋena de Pɛ Solomon tontoŋena déem na zege Ofiri ne ba ja sabu-seŋa ba ba ba pa Pɛ Solomon to, ba ta jaane da-ŋonno, de kandwa-nyenno na nwoŋi da to mo ba ba ba pa‑o. 11Pɛ wom ma kwei dɛ sem o ma ke nateina se ya taa wo Wɛ diga kam ne de pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne. O ma daare o ma dɛ sem o ke kwanno dwi dwi o pa balo na leeni to. Te tiini te lana te dwoi telo maama nɔɔna na maŋe ba na Judah teo ne to.
12Pɛ Solomon déem kwei kolo maama Seba ka-pɛ wom na laga to o pa‑o mo. Ka-pɛ wom na lwoori kolo maama o tei ne to mo o pɛ‑o, pa se ko dwoni pɛɛra yalo ka-pɛ wom na jaane o ba o pa‑o to. Ka-pɛ wom de o kwaga kam laam ma jwoori ba teo.
Solomon yere na zaŋe tei to
13Bene maama wone Solomon déem yeini o jwoŋi sabu-seŋa kilo morro finlei-tetɔ (23,000) mo, 14ko woli de lampwoo kolo o na jwoŋi bimbeera, de pipim-piina tei ne to. Arabia pwa bam maama, de Isarele teo kateira yiga tiina bam de déem yeini ba ja sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno ba ba ba pa‑o.
15Pɛ Solomon déem kwei sabu-seŋa o ma ke jara nantan-kamuna bia yalei (200) mo. O déem kwei sabu-seŋa na yi kilo serepɛ to mo o ma turi se dedoa dedoa. 16O ta ma ke nantan-balwa bia yatɔ (300), ye o kwei sabu-seŋa na maŋe de kilo setɔ (3) to o ma turi se dedoa dedoa. O ma kwei-se o ke diga kalo ba na bwoi we ‘Lebanon Goa’ to wone.
17Pɛ wom ta ma pa se ba kwei tuu yeila ba ma ke paare yituŋ-zɔŋɔ ba pa‑o. Ba ma daare ba ma sabu-seŋa kalo na ye chekke to ba turi ko yera. 18Nateini delo na jege na-baara yaredo to mo diini de yi paare yituŋu kom. Ko maa jege sabu-seŋa yituŋ-balaŋa se pɛ wom wane o chwi o nɛ da. Ko je selei sem maama maa jege nywoŋo nyenyego se takeiri ne. 19Nateini dem na-baare maama de maa jege nywoŋo nyenyero telei de baŋa ne, jazem de jagwia seeni, se ko ke nywoŋo nyenyero fuga-telei. Logo baŋa teene maama ne paare yituŋu tera ko na nye de Pɛ Solomon nyem kom. 20Ko ná ye Pɛ Solomon na-zwe sem maama, ko woli de o zela yalo maama na wo ‘Lebanon Goa’ diga kam ne to, ba mɛ sabu-seŋa mo ba ke te maama. Ba wo mɛ lu-nyenno ba ke te kolokolo, te na ba jege yuu Solomon paare maŋa kam ne to ŋwaane. 21Pɛ wom déem jege nabwor-kamunnu dedɛ Pɛ Hiram tontoŋena na yuŋi ye te beeri pipiu ŋwaane to. Bena yatɔ maama wone o nabwooru tem wó zeŋe sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de tuu yeila, de kali-faaro, de kali dwi dwi mo te ba te pa‑o.
22Pɛ Solomon déem mo ye nadum de swa tu o dwoi pwa maama logo baŋa ne. 23Logo baŋa teene maama pwa maa swoi se ba taa tui o tei ba cheigi yi-poro taane delo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑o to. 24Ba nam ná yeini ba tui, ba dedoa dedoa wó ja pɛɛra mo o ba o pa Solomon. Bene maama wone ba déem jaane lu-nyenno wonnu, de sabu-seŋa wonnu, de gwaaro, de terale nuga, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa dwi dwi, de sisein-nɔɔna, de bona-sisei ba tui ba pa‑o.
25Solomon déem chege najere morro tena (4,000) mo o zege se o sisei selo na vaŋe jara-keim torokooro to taa zege da. O ta maa jege sisein-nɔɔna morro fuga-telei (12,000). O déem pɔɔre se sedwonna o yage teene delo o na kuri se ŋwaane to ne. Se sedaara maa wo Jerusalem ne mɛ o na zoore to. 26O déem maa jege dam o di teene delo na wo Yuferata buga kam seeni to, se ko kɛ ko yi Filisi tiina laŋa kam, dedaane Ejipti siseini dem maama. 27O paare dim maŋa ne, lu-nyenno tiini te daga Jerusalem ne, ne kandwa mo tei. Sedare da-ŋonno de maa ba jege zore nenɛɛne kaporro na daga tei wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne to. 28Solomon déem ma pa o nɔɔna vei Ejipti dedaane teene maama se ba taa yeigi sisein-nɔɔna ba jaane ba tui ba pa‑o.
Solomon toone
29Solomon déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, ko zege o paare dem boboa ne se ko yi de na kweeli maŋa kalo to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Wɛ sampwora Natan tɔnɔ kom wone, de Siloo tu Ahija na pworisi wonnu telo to tɔnɔ kom wone, dedaane Yi-naro Ido veera yam tɔnɔ kom wone. Veera yalo o déem na nɛ se ko vo Nebat bu Jeroboam seeni to mo konto. 30Solomon jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare Isarele teo maama ne o ke bena finna mo. 31O laam ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwo David teo Jerusalem ne. O bu Rehoboam ma leiri o yuu ne o di paare.

english_text:
Some of the People Rebel against Rehoboam
(1 Kings 12.1-20)
1Rehoboam went to Shechem where everyone was waiting to crown him king.
2Jeroboam son of Nebat heard what was happening, and he returned from Egypt, where he had gone to hide from Solomon. 3The people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said, 4“Your father Solomon forced us to work very hard. But if you make our work easier, we will serve you and do whatever you ask.”
5Rehoboam replied, “Come back in three days for my answer.” So the people left.
6Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
7They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should be kind and promise to make their work easier.”
8But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials. 9He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
10His younger advisors said:
Here's what we think you should say to them: “Compared to me, my father was weak. 11He made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
12Three days later, Jeroboam and the others came back. 13Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors. He spoke bluntly 14and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested. He said: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
15-19 When the people realized that Rehoboam would not listen to them, they shouted: “We don't have to be loyal to David's family. We can do what we want. Come on, people of Israel, let's go home! Rehoboam can rule his own people.”
Adoniram was in charge of the work force, and Rehoboam sent him to talk to the people. But they stoned him to death. Then Rehoboam ran to his chariot and hurried back to Jerusalem.
Everyone from Israel's northern tribes went home, leaving Rehoboam to rule only the people from Judah. And since that day, the people of Israel have been opposed to David's descendants in Judah. All of this happened just as Ahijah the Lord's prophet from Shiloh had told Jeroboam.
translation_text:
Isarele tiina ve Rehoboam
1Rehoboam déem ma vo Sɛkɛm, Isarele tiina bam maama na jeeri da se ba tiŋi‑o pɛ to ŋwaane. 2Nebat bu Jeroboam déem ya duri o vo Ejipti mo se o lu Pɛ Solomon jeŋa ne. O maa na nigi Solomon toone ŋwa konto to, o ma jwoori sɔŋɔ. 3Ba ma toŋe ba bwoŋi Jeroboam se o tɔge de Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama se ba vo Rehoboam tei. Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, 4“Nmo kwo Solomon déem tiini o yaare debam de totoŋ-chɛɛra. Konto to, nam kwaane se n pa ko taa bwona ko pa debam, se dé wane dé sii dé yaara yam wone. N ná ke konto, dé wó sɛ dé pa‑m.” 5Rehoboam ma leiri-ba o we, “Nam véi-na se da yatɔ kwaga ne se á laam jwoori á ba se dé nii.” Nɔɔna bam ma viiri. 6Pɛ Rehoboam ma bwɛ taane dem de nɔn-kwe selo déem ya na ye o kwo Solomon nakwa to. O ma bwei-ba o we, “Bɛ boboŋa mo abam jega se á ma á woli-ne se a leiri a pa nɔɔna banto?” 7Nakwa bam ma leiri ba we, “Nmo ná tu n tete se n sɛ nɔɔna bam zem na lwoori‑m kolo to, ye n duri ba yibwona, ba laam wó sɛ ba pa‑m.”
8Rehoboam ma ve nɔn-kwe sem boboŋe dem ye o daare o vo o bane de nɔn-donno telo na ye o yuudwonna pa ba wo o tei ne to. 9O ma bwei-ba o we, “Nɔɔna banto na we, a kwo wom na yaare-ba dedɛ to, a laam pa se ba sii de ba yaara yam to, bɛ boboŋa mo abam jega se á ma á woli-ne se a ma a leiri a pa-ba?”
10Nɔn-donno tem na ye o yuudwonna to ma leiri ba we, “Ko ná ye balo na lwoori‑m konto to, ta n bere-ba we, ‘Amo noa kam tete kula ka dwoi a kwo wom teiŋa! 11A kwo keim déem seene ko chana á baŋa ne. Ko nam ná ye amo, ko wó dwoni dáane. A kwo wom déem mɛ kafena mo o fere abam. Amo nam laga a kwei kafene selo nia na chana ne nɔŋɔ donem to mo a ma a fere abam.’ ”
12Da yatɔ yam dɛ dem ne mo Jeroboam de nɔɔna bam maama daa jwoori ba vo Pɛ Rehoboam tei, ne o na maŋe o ta o tiŋi tei to. 13Ba na tu to, Pɛ Rehoboam ma zage-ba de ni-chɛɛre, o na dole nɔn-kwe sem taane dem o yage to ŋwaane. 14O nam yɔɔre o ke o tɔge nɔn-donno tem boboŋa yam mo. O ma ta o we, “A kwo keim déem seene ko chana á baŋa ne. Ko nam ná ye amo, ko wó dwoni dáane. A kwo wom déem mɛ kafena mo o fere abam. Amo nam lage a kwei kafene selo nia na chana ne nɔŋɔ donem to mo a ma a fere abam.” 15Pɛ Rehoboam na wo sɛ nɔɔna bam taane dem to déem tɔge Wɛ boboŋa na jaane tei to mo. Ko pɛ Baŋa Wɛ na dɛ o sampwora Ahija baŋa o ta tei de Nebat bu Jeroboam to mo ji chega. 16Isarele tiina bam maama na maane we pɛ wom ve se o ke o tɔge ba boboŋa yam to, ba ma chɛ sɔɔ ye ba leiri‑o ba we, “Isarele tiina bam, debam dedaane Jesse bu David dae daane. Dé yiga tera o dwi dem paare wone! Pa-na dé maama jwoori-na sam. David dwi tu, ta‑n nii n tete sɔ-yuu kom baŋa ne!” Ba maama ma seene ba jwoori ba sam. 17Ko nam ná ye Isarele dwi tiina balo na zoore Judah teene dem ne to yerane, Pɛ Rehoboam déem ta mo di paare ba baŋa ne.
18Pɛ Rehoboam ma toŋe Adoniram wolo na nii totoŋ-chɛɛra yam baŋa ne to se o vo Isarele dwia yalo na wo baŋa seeni to tei. O na yi da to, nɔɔna bam ma dole‑o de kandwa ba go. Konto baŋa ne Pɛ Rehoboam ma faŋe o lei o toroko o duri o lu o vo Jerusalem. 19De zem maama Isarele dwi tiina na wo baŋa seeni to ve mo se David dwi dem taa di paare ba baŋa ne.

english_text:
Shemaiah the Prophet Warns Rehoboam
(1 Kings 12.21-24)
1After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and regain control of the whole country. So he called together 180,000 soldiers from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.
2Meanwhile, the Lord had told Shemaiah the prophet 3to tell Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin, 4“The Lord warns you not to go to war against the people from the northern tribes—they are your relatives. Go home! The Lord is the one who made these things happen.”
Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord's message and did not attack Jeroboam and his troops.
Rehoboam Fortifies Cities in Judah
5Rehoboam ruled from Jerusalem, and he had several cities in Judah turned into fortresses so he could use them to defend his country. These cities included 6Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa, 7Beth-Zur, Soco, Adullam, 8Gath, Mareshah, Ziph, 9Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah, 10Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. After he had fortified these cities in the territories of Judah and Benjamin, 11he assigned an army commander to each of them and stocked them with supplies of food, olive oil, and wine, 12as well as with shields and spears. He used these fortified cities to keep control of Judah and Benjamin.
The Priests and the Levites Support Rehoboam
13The priests and Levites from the northern tribes of Israel gave their support to King Rehoboam. 14And since Jeroboam and the kings of Israel that followed him would not allow any Levites to serve as priests, most Levites left their towns and pasturelands in Israel and moved to Jerusalem and other towns in Judah. 15 Jeroboam chose his own priests to serve at the local shrines in Israel and at the places of worship where he had set up statues of goat-demons and of calves.
16But some of the people from Israel wanted to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done. So they followed the priests and Levites to Jerusalem, where they could offer sacrifices to the Lord. 17For the next three years, they lived in Judah and were loyal to Rehoboam and his kingdom, just as they had been loyal to David and Solomon.
Rehoboam's Family
18Rehoboam married Mahalath, whose father was Jerimoth son of David, and whose mother was Abihail the daughter of Eliab and granddaughter of Jesse. 19Rehoboam and Mahalath had three sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham. 20Then Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom. Their sons were Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
21Rehoboam had 18 wives, but he also married 60 other women, and he was the father of 28 sons and 60 daughters. Rehoboam loved his wife Maacah the most, 22so he chose their oldest son Abijah to be the next king. 23Rehoboam was wise enough to put one of his sons in charge of each fortified city in his kingdom. He gave them all the supplies they needed and found wives for every one of them.
translation_text:
1Rehoboam na yi Jerusalem to mo o bwoŋi Judah de Benjamin dwia yam nɔɔna balo na yei jara keim chekke to. Ba déem ye jar-keira morro bi de funɔnɔ (180,000) mo. O ma ja boboŋa se o kwaare jara de Isarele dwi tiina badaara bam, se o wane o pa ba maama jwoori ba ke daane se o taa tei-ba. 2Baŋa Wɛ ma pa o tontoŋeno Semaya ni ye o we, 3“Nam pa amo taane dento yi Judah teo Pɛ Solomon bu Rehoboam, de Isarele tiina balo na nwoŋi Judah de Benjamin dwia yam wone to we, 4‘Baŋa Wɛ kwora mo tento: Yé zaŋe-na á ke jara de á chorro. Á maama véi-na sɔŋɔ, se amo mo pɛ se konto maama ke.’ ” Ba maama ma sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem ye ba jwoori ba sam. Ba daa wo kwaare jara de Jeroboam nɔɔna bam.
Rehoboam na lɔge teene delo o pe to
5Rehoboam déem ma maŋe Jerusalem ne o zoora, ye o fɔge o lɔ Judah teene dedɛ o pe se de taa ye dalem jei de pa‑o. 6De nam ye: Bɛtelehem, de Etam, de Tekoa, 7de Bɛte-Zura, de Sokoo, de Adulam, 8de Gafa, de Maresa, de Zifi 9de Adorayim, de Lakisi, de Azeka, 10de Zora, de Ayijalon, de Heboron. Teene dem konto maama mo o déem pɛ de ji dalem jei Judah de Benjamin kateira yam wone. 11O ma fɔge o lɔ-de o pe, pa de dana chekke, ye o tiŋi dedɛɛra de maama wone. O ta ma lɛɛre o pa teene dem konto wo su de wodiiru, de nuga, de sana. 12O ta ma yage jara-keim nantane de chichwoa teene dem konto wone se ko pa de taa dana.
Konto baŋa ne Rehoboam déem di paare Judah de Benjamin dwia yam baŋa ne. 13Wɛ kaanem tiina bam de Levi dwi tiina bam na zoore Isarele laŋa kam jei selo maama ne to de ma sɛ ba pa‑o. 14Levi tiina bam ma varege ba yage ba te sem, de ba sam ba ya na zoore teene delo maama ne to, ye ba vo ba zoore Judah kateiri dem de Jerusalem teo kom ne. Ba nam ke konto bɛŋwaane Pɛ Jeroboam de o kwaga kam ya le-ba Baŋa Wɛ kaanem totoŋe dem ne mo. 15O laam ma kuri o tete kaanem tiina se ba taa ke kaanem wara-jei sem bimbina yam baŋa ne ba pa jwona yalo o na ke o zege ye ya ye bone de naane nyenyero to. 16Nɔɔna balo na nwoŋi Isarele dwi delo maama wone ye ba boboŋa ja se ba yɔɔre ba taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to déem ma tɔge de Levi tiina bam ba vo Jerusalem se ba taa ke kaanem dáane ba pae Baŋa Wɛ na ye ba nabaara bam Wɛ to. 17Konto ma pa Judah paare dem kuri ja tega. Bena yatɔ wone mo ba déem yɔɔre ba sɛ ba pa Solomon bu Rehoboam. Bena yatɔ yam konto wone ba tɔge David de Solomon nia yam na bere tei to mo.
Rehoboam diga tiina taane
18Rehoboam nam ya di Mahalafa mo o ma o ke o kaane. Wonto déem ye David bu Jerimofa bukɔ mo. O nu yere maa ye Abihali na ye Jesse bu Eliabi bukɔ to. 19Mahalafa ma lo bakeiri setɔ o pa Rehoboam. Ba yera maa ye Jewusi, de Semaria, de Zaham. 20Pɛ wom daa ma di Abisalom bukɔ Maaka ye ba lo Abija, de Atayi, de Ziza, de Selomifa. 21Rehoboam déem nam yɔɔre o swoi Abisalom bukɔ Maaka mo o dwoi o kaana bam de o ka-bi sem maama. O déem jege kaana fuga-nana mo, de ka-bi fuseredo. O bu-baara déem ye finlei-nana mo, ye o bukwa ye fuseredo.
22Rehoboam déem nam kuri Maaka bu Abija mo se o taa wo o bia bam maama yiga ne, kokuri to, o boboŋa jaane se wonto mo ba o leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ. 23O déem tɔge swa baŋa ne mo o le o bu-baara bam wone o pa ba jage ba vo Judah de Benjamin kateira yam maama, se ba taa zoore teene delo na lɔge de pe to wone. O ma la wodiiru dedɛ o pa-ba, ye o daare o beeri bukwa dedɛ se ba di-ba ba ma ba ke ba kaana.

english_text:
King Shishak of Egypt Invades Judah
(1 Kings 14.25-28)
1Soon after Rehoboam had control of his kingdom, he and everyone in Judah stopped obeying the Lord. 2So in the fifth year of Rehoboam's rule, the Lord punished them for their unfaithfulness and allowed King Shishak of Egypt to invade Judah. 3Shishak attacked with his army of 1,200 chariots and 60,000 cavalry troops, as well as countless Egyptian soldiers from Libya, Sukkoth, and Ethiopia. 4He captured every one of the fortified cities in Judah and then marched to Jerusalem.
5Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah had gone to Jerusalem to escape Shishak's invasion. And while they were there, Shemaiah the prophet told them, “The Lord says that because you have disobeyed him, he has now abandoned you. The Lord will not help you against Shishak!”
6Rehoboam and the leaders were sorry for what they had done and admitted, “The Lord is right. We have deserted him.”
7When the Lord heard this, he told Shemaiah:
The people of Judah are truly sorry for their sins, and so I won't let Shishak completely destroy them. But because I am still angry, 8he will conquer and rule them.
Then my people will know what it's like to serve a foreign king instead of serving me.
9 Shishak attacked Jerusalem and took all the valuable things from the temple and from the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
10Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe. 11Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he had finished worshiping.
12Rehoboam turned back to the Lord, and so the Lord did not let Judah be completely destroyed, and Judah was prosperous again.
Rehoboam's Rule in Judah
(1 Kings 14.21,29-31)
13Rehoboam was 41 years old when he became king, and he ruled 17 years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon. Rehoboam was a powerful king, 14but he still did wrong and refused to obey the Lord.
15Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king, including a history of his family, is written in the records of the two prophets, Shemaiah and Iddo. During Rehoboam's rule, he and King Jeroboam of Israel were constantly at war. 16When Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Abijah became king.
translation_text:
Sisake kwaare jara de Jerusalem tiina
1Pɛ Rehoboam déem jwoŋi dam mo ye o paare dem kuri ja tega. Ko kwaga ne o de o teo nɔɔna bam maama ma lɔ Baŋa Wɛ nia yam kwaga ne. 2O paare dim bena yanu maŋa ne mo Ejipti Pɛ Sisake tu o kwaare jara de Jerusalem teo kom, ba na ve Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane. 3Sisake déem zege Ejipti ne o ja o jara-keim torokooro moro de bia yalei (1,200), de jar-keira morro fuseredo (60,000) balo na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne to, de jar-keira balo na vei tega ne ye ba kɔgɔ ware ko ga ko ti to o ba o kwaare jara yam. Jar-keira bam konto badaara déem ye Libia tiina, de Suki tiina, de Kusi tiina mo. 4O de o jar-keira bam ma wane Judah kateiri teene delo maama na lɔge de pe to ba di, ye ba laam vo ba yi Jerusalem.
5Rehoboam de Judah teo dedɛɛra bam ya vei Jerusalem se ba duri ba lu Sisake jeŋa ne mo. Wɛ sampwora Semaya ma vo ba tei ye o ta de-ba o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Abam na nwoŋi amo kwaga ne to ŋwaane mo amo de nwoŋi abam kwaga ne ye a ke abam Sisake jeŋa ne.”
6Pɛ Rehoboam de o dedɛɛra bam ma gwooni ba tete Wɛ yiga ne ye ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ seene o jege chega de kolo o na ke to.”
7 Baŋa Wɛ na nɛ ba na gwooni ba tete tei to, o daa ma pa o kwora yi Semaya we, “Nɔɔna bam na gwooni ba tete konto to, amo bá chɔge-ba fase. Ko ná ke fee, a daa ta wó jwoŋi-ba. A bá tɔge Sisake baŋa ne a waare Jerusalem. 8A nam wó pa chwoŋa se Sisake ja-ba o ke o dam kuri ne. Konto wó pa ba lɔre kɔ mo gara, ne ba ná toŋe ba pa amo, naa ba ná toŋe ba pa dwi-gɛ tiina pwa bam mo.”
9Ejipti teo Pɛ Sisake ma seene o kwaare jara de Jerusalem. O ma vere jejegero telo maama na wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone to, de telo maama na wo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wone to, ko woli de jara-keim nantane selo Solomon déem na mɛ sabu-seŋa o ke to o ja o viiri. 10Pɛ Rehoboam ma kwei channa o ma o jwoori o ke nantane sedwonna o zege da. O ma kwei-se o ke babɛ selo na yere pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo ni dem to jeŋa ne. 11Maŋa kalo maama pɛ wom na wó vo Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem to, babɛ sem mo jege se ba zeŋe nantane sem ba tɔge o kwaga. Ba daa ná ti, banto ta mo wó zeŋe-se ba jwoori ba tiŋi pɛ sɔŋɔ yerena diga kam ne.
12Rehoboam na gwooni o tete Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne konto to, Baŋa Wɛ ma de o bane na wone, ye o daa wo yɔɔre o chɔge‑o fase. Wonnu déem nam ke lanyerane te pa Judah laŋa kam.
13Rehoboam déem ma fɔge o jeini Jerusalem wone o di paare bena fuga-yarepɛ. O déem jege bena finna-dedoa mo ye o di paare dem, ye o paare dem ba de nu chekke. Baŋa Wɛ nam ya kuri Jerusalem mo Isarele dwia yam maama wone se o nɔɔna taa vei da ba zuli o yere dem. Rehoboam nu déem ye Amon tiina bukɔ Naama mo. 14O déem nam toŋe lwarem kikia, o na wo jaane boboŋa se o taa tɔge Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane.
15Rehoboam déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, ko zege o paare dem boboa ne se ko yi de na kweeli maŋa kalo to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Wɛ sampwora Semaya tɔnɔ kom wone, de Yi-naro Ido veera yam tɔnɔ kom wone. O kwoa nakwa yera natɔga de popone ya tiŋi da. Maŋa kam konto maama ne tigura déem mo tigi Pɛ Rehoboam de Pɛ Jeroboam tetare ne. 16Rehoboam ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa bam yibeeli ne David teo Jerusalem ne. O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Abija ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.

english_text:
King Abijah of Judah
(1 Kings 15.1-8)
1Abijah became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel, 2and he ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah.
Some time later, Abijah and King Jeroboam of Israel went to war against each other. 3Abijah's army had 400,000 troops, and Jeroboam met him in battle with 800,000 troops.
4Abijah went to the top of Mount Zemaraim in the hills of Ephraim and shouted:
Listen, Jeroboam and all you Israelites! 5The Lord God of Israel has made a solemn promise that every king of Israel will be from David's family. 6But Jeroboam, you were King Solomon's official, and you rebelled. 7Then right after Rehoboam became king, you and your bunch of worthless followers challenged Rehoboam, who was too young to know how to stop you.
8Now you and your powerful army think you can stand up to the kingdom that the Lord has given to David's descendants. The only gods you have are those gold statues of calves that Jeroboam made for you. 9You don't even have descendants of Aaron on your side, because you forced out the Lord's priests and Levites. In their place, you appoint ordinary people to be priests, just as the foreign nations do. In fact, anyone who brings a bull and seven rams to the altar can become a priest of your so-called gods.
10But we have not turned our backs on the Lord God! Aaron's own descendants serve as our priests, and the Levites are their assistants. 11Two times every day they offer sacrifices and burn incense to the Lord. They set out the sacred loaves of bread on a table that has been purified, and they light the lamps in the gold lampstand every day at sunset. We follow the commands of the Lord our God—you have rejected him! 12That's why God is on our side and will lead us into battle when the priests sound the signal on the trumpets. It's no use, Israelites. You might as well give up. There's no way you can defeat the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped.
13But while Abijah was talking, Jeroboam had sent some of his troops to attack Judah's army from behind, while the rest attacked from the front. 14Judah's army realized they were trapped, and so they prayed to the Lord. The priests blew the signal on the trumpet, 15and the troops let out a battle cry. Then with Abijah leading them into battle, God defeated Jeroboam and Israel's army. 16The Israelites ran away, and God helped Judah's soldiers slaughter 17500,000 enemy troops. 18Judah's army won because they had trusted the Lord God of their ancestors.
19Abijah kept up his attack on Jeroboam's army and captured the Israelite towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, as well as the villages around them.
20Jeroboam never regained his power during the rest of Abijah's rule. The Lord punished Jeroboam, and he died, but Abijah became more powerful.
21Abijah had a total of 14 wives, 22 sons, and 16 daughters. 22Everything Abijah said and did while he was king is written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
translation_text:
Judah teo Pɛ Abija taane
1Isarele teo pɛ Jeroboam paare dim bena fuga-nana bene dem wone mo Abija déem di Judah teo paare. 2O déem jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem bena yatɔ mo. O nu yere mo ye Maaka wolo na ye Gibea tu Yureli bukɔ to.
Jara déem ma to Abija de Jeroboam tetare laŋa ne. 3Abija ma la nɔɔna balo na yei jara keim chekke to morro bia yana (400,000) o ke daane se o jeeri Jeroboam de jara. Jeroboam ma jeeri‑o de o jar-keira morro bia funɔnɔ (800,000) balo de na ye babɛ to.
4Abija déem ma vo o zege Zemarayim peo kom yuu ne. Peo kom konto wo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne mo. O ma tɔɔle baŋa baŋa o we:
“Jeroboam, de Isarele tiina bam maama, cheigi-na a taane dem. 5Abam yɔɔre á yei we, Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to maŋe o gwoni ni de David we, o wó kwei Isarele teo paare dem o pa wonto de o dwi dem se ko taa vei wuu. 6Ko nam na ye tei to, Nebat bu Jeroboam ya na ye David bu Solomon tontoŋeno to mo nwoŋi o tu wom kwaga ne. 7O ma beeri nɔn-wo-korro o de o kwaga ne pa ba vo ba dwoni de Solomon bu Rehoboam. Ka maŋa ne de Rehoboam ta ware se o kuri o tete boboŋa o tɔge-ya. O maa bwona se o wane ba yiga o che.
8Abam de nam kwaane se á ve paare delo Baŋa Wɛ na tiŋi o pa David dwi dem to mo. Á kɔgɔ kom seene ko daga lanyerane. Abam ta maa jege Jeroboam na kwei sabu-seŋa o mɔ na-mɔre kamwaro telo se á ta‑á zuli to á tei ne. 9Nam yé swei-na we á zeili Aron bia bam na ye Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina to, de Levi dwi tiina bam mo. Abam laam ma lwoni teene dedwonna kikia de á na kuri á tete kaanem tiina to. Wolo maama maa ná wane o ja na-bala, de pi-bale serepɛ o ba o ma o ke pɛɛra, konto tu wae o kwɛ o tete se o ji kaanem tu o kaane abam wa-yɔɔro tem.
10Debam nam ta zuli dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo, ye dé wo yage‑o. Aron dwi dem nɔɔna mo ye Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina debam tei ne, ye Levi dwi tiina bam yeini ba toŋe ba woli-ba. 11Tetete maama de dedaan-ni maama ne, ba yeini ba ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra mo, ye ba zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ba ta yeini ba kwei bworobworo mo ba tiŋi tabolo kolo ba na kwɛ Wɛ ŋwaane to baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba tɔre min-zwonnu tem na zege sabu-seŋa min-zwon-zego kom baŋa ne to dedaan-ni maama ne. Konto to, debam yɔɔre dé ke tei dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ na bere se dé taa ke to mo. Ko nam ná ye abam, á nwoŋi o kwaga ne mo. 12Ta‑á yei-na we, Wɛ seene o wo debam tei ne. Wonto mo ye debam yiga tu. O kaanem tiina bam mo ti ba yiga se ba wu nabwanno se dé laam kwaare jara de abam. Isarele tiina bam, yé dwoni-na de Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye á nabaara bam Wɛ to, bɛŋwaane á bá na ko kuri.”
13Abija ta na zege da o ŋɔɔne konto to, mo Jeroboam toŋe o jar-keira badwonna se ba dale ba tɔge Judah jar-keira bam kwaga seeni ba zaŋe ba baŋa ne de jara. Balo na daare to de maa wo Judah tiina bam yiga seeni. 14Judah tiina bam ma maane we ba dona bam li-ba mo yiga seeni, de kwaga kam seeni. Ba ma keeri ba jare Baŋa Wɛ se o woli-ba. Kaanem tiina bam ma wu ba nabwanno tem, 15ye Judah tiina bam maama kaase tiguri-kaasa. Jeroboam de Isarele jar-keira bam na nigi sɔɔ kom to, Wɛ ma pa ba duri se ba lu Abija de Judah tiina bam jeŋa ne. 16Isarele tiina bam déem na duri konto to mo Wɛ pɛ Judah tiina bam wane-ba ba di. 17Abija de o nɔɔna bam ma yɔɔre ba go Isarele tiina bam dedɛ. Isarele jar-keira balo na tege to ye morro bia yanu (500,000) mo. 18Ko déem nam ye Judah dwi tiina bam na ke ba chega de Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye ba nabaara bam Wɛ to ŋwaane mo ba wane Isarele tiina bam ba di dɛ dem konto ne.
19Abija de o nɔɔna bam ma pare Jeroboam taa. Ba ma vere teene dedwonna o tei ne ba tei. Teene dem konto nam ye Bɛtel, de Jesana, de Eforon, ko woli de de nawuura yam maama. 20Abija paare dim maŋa kam maama wone, Jeroboam daa wo jwoori o na dam. Baŋa Wɛ ma waare Jeroboam pa o te.
21Ko daare, Abija dam dem ke de woli da mo. O kaana déem ye fuga-bana mo. O bu-baara maa ye finlei-balei, ye o bukwa ye fuga-baredo.
22Abija déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama na daare to, kolo maama o na kea, de taana yalo o na taga to, ba popone ba tiŋi Wɛ Sampwora Ido memaŋa yam tɔnɔ kom wone.

english_text:
King Asa of Judah
1Abijah died and was buried in Jerusalem. Then his son Asa became king, and Judah had ten years of peace.
2Asa obeyed the Lord his God and did right. 3He destroyed the local shrines and the altars to foreign gods. He smashed the stone images of gods and cut down the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah. 4Then he told everyone in Judah to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done, and to obey his laws and teachings. 5He destroyed every local shrine and incense altar in Judah.
6The Lord blessed Judah with peace while Asa was king, and so during that time, Asa fortified many of the towns. 7He said to the people, “Let's build walls and defense towers for these towns, and put in gates that can be locked with bars. This land still belongs to us, because we have obeyed the Lord our God. He has given us peace from all our enemies.” The people did everything Asa had suggested.
8Asa had a large army of brave soldiers: 300,000 of them were from the tribe of Judah and were armed with shields and spears; 280,000 were from Benjamin and were armed with shields and bows.
Judah Defeats Ethiopia's Army
9Zerah from Ethiopia led an army of 1,000,000 soldiers and 300 chariots to the town of Mareshah in Judah. 10Asa met him there, and the two armies prepared for battle in Zephathah Valley.
11Asa prayed:
Lord God, only you can help a powerless army defeat a stronger one. So we depend on you to help us. We will fight against this powerful army to honor your name, and we know that you won't be defeated. You are the Lord our God.
12The Lord helped Asa and his army defeat the Ethiopians. The enemy soldiers ran away, 13but Asa and his troops chased them as far as Gerar. It was a total defeat—the Ethiopians could not even fight back!
The soldiers from Judah took everything that had belonged to the Ethiopians. 14The people who lived in the villages around Gerar learned what had happened and were afraid of the Lord. So Judah's army easily defeated them and carried off everything of value that they wanted from these towns. 15They also attacked the camps where the shepherds lived and took a lot of sheep, goats, and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_text:
1Abija ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli David teo Jerusalem ne. O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Asa ma leiri o di paare. Asa paare dim maŋa kam ne ba teo kom sii de jara bena fuga mo.
Judah teo Pɛ Asa taane
2Asa déem ke wo-laaro mo, ye o totoŋa su o Tu Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane. 3O ma ja bimbin-yɔɔro tem, de zwonnu yuu wara-jei sem o chɔge. O ta ma lɔ kandwa yalo ba na jege ba zuli to, ye o daare o chochoge Asera nyenyego dɛ sem o yage. 4O laam ma pa Judah dwi tiina bam ni we, ba taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye ba nabaara bam Wɛ to, se ba daare ba taa sɛ o nia yam de o bera yam. 5Judah teene dem maama wone mo o déem pɛ ba chɔge wara-jei bimbina yam, de yalo ba na zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa ya baŋa ne to. Ko maa pa se Asa paare dim maŋa kam ne, yazura yɔɔre ka wo Judah laŋa kam ne mo. 6Asa déem fɔge o lɔ Judah teene delo maama na pe de dam to mo, ba laŋa kam na wo nɛ daanem to ŋwaane. Bena yam konto maama ne, nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo kwaare jara ded‑o, kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ déem mo pɛ se o zoore tega kam ne de bochare-zuru.
7O déem ma ta de Judah tiina bam o we, “Pa-na se dé fɔge dé pe teene dem dé zege de dam, se de taa jege kabiri-lilirru, de ni-bworru telo na jege luuru to. Tega kam ta ye debam nyem mo, dé na ke dé tɔge dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa to ŋwaane. Wonto mo chege debam dé dona jeŋa ne pa ba ba daane debam.”
Ba ma seene ba lɔ ba teene dem ba pe, ye wonnu ke lanyerane te pa-ba.
8Asa déem jege jar-keira morro bia yatɔ (300,000) mo na nwoŋi Judah dwi dem ne. Ba maama maa zei jara-keim nantan-kamuna, de chichwoa. O ta maa jege jar-keira morro bia yalei de funɔnɔ (280,000) na nwoŋi Benjamin dwi dem ne, ye ba de zei jara-keim nantan-balwa, dedaane tɛ, de chena. Jar-keira bam maama déem ye bembɛ mo.
9Dɛ dedwe Kusi tu wolo yere na ye Zera to ma nwoŋi de jar-keira kɔ-fɔrɔ, de jara-keim torokooro bia yatɔ o vo o yi Maresa se o jeeri Judah tiina bam de jara. 10Asa de ma nwoŋi de o o jar-keira bam o jeeri‑o dáane, Zefata bwolo jei sem ne. Ba maama ma fɔge ba tigisi ba jar-keira bam se ba ke jara yam.
11Asa déem ma lwoori o Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom o we, “Baŋa Wɛ, nmo yerane mo wae nabwona n jwoŋi n yaga dedɛɛra kɔgɔ jeŋa ne. Debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ, dé teege nmo baŋa ne mo se n woli debam. Ko nam ye nmo yere dem ŋwaane mo debam nwoŋi se dé jeeri kɔ-fɔrɔ konto de jara. Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo ye debam Wɛ wom. Nam yé sɛ se nɔɔn-nɔɔno dwoni de nmo o di.”
12 Baŋa Wɛ ma chɔge Kusi tiina bam pa se ba duri se ba lu Asa de Judah jar-keira bam jeŋa ne. 13Asa de o nɔɔna bam ma pare-ba taa ba vo ba yi Gerare seeni. Kusi tiina bam dedɛ ma te pa ba kɔgɔ kom daa ware jara yam se ba ke. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ de o jar-keira bam déem yɔɔre ba wane-ba mo. Judah tiina bam ma pɛ ba dona bam jejegero dedɛ ba ja ba viiri. 14Ba déem ta ma chɔge te-balwa balo na gilimi Gerare teo kom to, Baŋa Wɛ foone na tiini de jege jei sem konto nɔn-bia bam to ŋwaane. Judah tiina bam ma lɛɛre ba pɛ teene dem konto maama jejegero ba ja ba viiri, te na tiini te daga to ŋwaane. 15Ba ta ma vo ba li napɔra balo na yere vara bam to, ye ba kale pei, de bone, de kona dedɛ ba ja ba kɛ. Ba laam ma jwoori ba vo Jerusalem.

english_text:
Asa Destroys the Idols in Judah
1Some time later, God spoke to Azariah son of Oded. 2At once, Azariah went to Asa and said:
Listen to me, King Asa and you people of Judah and Benjamin. The Lord will be with you and help you, as long as you obey and worship him. But if you disobey him, he will desert you.
3For a long time, the people of Israel did not worship the true God or listen to priests who could teach them about God. They refused to obey God's Law. 4But whenever trouble came, Israel turned back to the Lord their God and worshiped him.
5There was so much confusion in those days that it wasn't safe to go anywhere in Israel. 6Nations were destroying each other, and cities were wiping out other cities, because God was causing trouble and unrest everywhere.
7So you must be brave. Don't give up! God will honor you for obeying him.
8As soon as Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he gave orders for all the idols in Judah and Benjamin to be destroyed, including those in the towns he had captured in the territory of Ephraim. He also repaired the Lord's altar that was in front of the temple porch.
9Asa called together the people from Judah and Benjamin, as well as the people from the territories of Ephraim, West Manasseh, and Simeon who were living in Judah. Many of these people were now loyal to Asa, because they had seen that the Lord was with him.
10In the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule, they all met in Jerusalem. 11That same day, they took 700 bulls and 7,000 sheep and goats from what they had brought back from Gerar and sacrificed them as offerings to the Lord. 12They made a solemn promise to faithfully worship the Lord God their ancestors had worshiped, 13and to put to death anyone who refused to obey him. 14The crowd solemnly agreed to keep their promise to the Lord, then they celebrated by shouting and blowing trumpets and horns. 15Everyone was happy because they had made this solemn promise, and in return, the Lord blessed them with peace from all their enemies.
16Asa's grandmother Maacah had made a disgusting idol of the goddess Asherah, so he cut it down, crushed it, and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother. 17As long as Asa lived, he was faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines in Israel. 18He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to God.
19There was peace in Judah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
translation_text:
Pɛ Asa na toŋe wo-laaro telo to
1Wɛ Jworo déem tu Odeda bu Azaria baŋa. 2O ma nwoŋi o vo Asa tei o ta ded‑o o we:
“Pɛ Asa, de Judah tiina bam, de Benjamin tiina bam maama, cheigi-na a taane dento: Baŋa Wɛ wó taa wo abam tei ne, ne á ná yɔɔre á me ded‑o. Á ná beeri o jei, o wó pa abam chwoŋa se á na‑o. Abam nam ná nwoŋi o kwaga ne, o de wó dole abam mo o yage. 3Bena dedɛ wone Isarele tiina bam wo sɛ se ba tɔge Wɛ dem chekke, ye ba ba jege kaanem tu se kotu taa bere-ba. Ba maa wo lɔre Wɛ nia yam. 4Cham nam ná yeini de yi-ba, ba yeini ba pipiri se ba jwoori Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to tei mo. Ba ma yeini ba beeri o jei, ye o pa-ba chwoŋa se ba na‑o. 5Maŋa kam konto ne, nɔɔna déem ba beeri yɔɔ yɔɔ, vuvuga na to teene dem maama de de nɔn-bia baŋa ne to ŋwaane. 6Dwi dedwe yɔɔre de zaŋe de chɔge dedwoŋi dwi yɔɔ yɔɔ mo, ye teo dedoa nɔɔna de zaŋe teo kodwoŋi nɔɔna baŋa ne. Ko nam ye Baŋa Wɛ mo jaane lɛɛro dwi maama o tui ba baŋa. 7Ko nam ná ye abam, ke-na dam á ke á tete kuri ne, se á yé pa se á vɔna bugi. Kokuri to, abam wó na á totoŋa yam nyɔɔre.”
8Asa na nigi Wɛ sampwora Azaria na pworisi taane delo maama to mo o nɛ baare. O ma le jwo-yɔɔro telo na wo Judah de Benjamin kateira yam maama wone to o dole o yage. Ko ta ná ye teene delo na wo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne ye o vere-de o tei to, o dole ba jwona yam de o yage. O laam ma pa ba fɔge ba kwɛ Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem na zege Wɛ diga kam napɔrɔ kom yiga ne to.
9Asa déem ma bwoŋi Judah dwi tiina, de Benjamin dwi tiina bam se ba la daane. O ta ma bwoŋi nɔɔna balo na nwoŋi Efrayim, de Manasɛ, de Simeon dwia yam wone ye ba laam ba ba zoore Judah laŋa kam ne to. Kokuri to, Isarele tiina dedɛ ya tu ba sɛ ba pa Asa, ba na maane we o Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo wo o tei ne to ŋwaane.
10Ba maama déem nam jeeri Jerusalem ne Asa paare dim bena fuga-yanu chane setɔ chana kam wone mo. 11Dɛ dem konto ne ba ma kwei na-bale bia yarepɛ (700), de pei de bone morro terepɛ (7,000) ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Vara bam konto nam ye ba na vere balo ba dona bam jeŋa ne to mo. 12Ba laam ma ke ni-sɛɛm se ba yɔɔre ba taa tɔge Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye ba nabaara Wɛ to de ba bochara maama, ko woli de ba dam maama. 13Ba ta sɛ we, wolo maama ná ve se o tɔge Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to, ba wó go konto tu, nabwom naa dedɛɛro mo ywoo, baaro naa kaane mo de. 14Ba laam ma du duuri Baŋa Wɛ yere dem ŋwaane ba vɔ ba tete. Ba nam yɔɔre ba kwei sɔɔ kolo na zaŋe baŋa baŋa to, de nabwanno wum, de namunnu wum mo ba du duuri dem de kwor-dɛa. 15Judah tiina bam maama wo déem ma pwoli de ba na ke kampwola se ko yɔɔre ko nwoŋi ba bochara ne to. Ba ma beeri Baŋa Wɛ jei de ba wo maama, ye o de pa-ba chwoŋa se ba na‑o. O déem chege-ba ba dona jeŋa ne pa ba daa ba daane-ba.
16Asa nu nakwe Maaka ya chwi Asera nyenyego daa pa nɔɔna jege-ka ba kaana. O ma vo o gwoni-ka o de tega ne o daare o kwei-ka o zwɛ Kidoron nabara kam ni ne. O ta ma le Maaka se o daa yé taa jege dam pɛ sɔŋɔ ne. 17Asa déem wo wane o chɔge wara-jei bimbini selo na wo Isarele laŋa kam maama wone to. De ko de, o ŋwea maama wone o yɔɔre o kwei o chega o pa Baŋa Wɛ mo. 18O déem ta ma kwei pɛɛra yalo o de o kwo wom na kwei ba pa Baŋa Wɛ to o ja o vo o tiŋi Wɛ diga kam wone. Pɛɛra yam déem ye lu-nyenno wonnu, de sabu-seŋa wonnu, de zela dwi dwi mo.
19Jara déem daa wo ke Judah teo kom ne se ko taa nii bene delo Asa na di paare o ke bena fintɔ-yanu to wone.

english_text:
King Baasha of Israel Invades Judah
(1 Kings 15.16-22)
1In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's rule, King Baasha of Israel invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, and he put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
2When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. Then he sent it to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria: 3“I think we should sign a peace treaty, just as our fathers did. This silver and gold is a present for you. Would you please break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel and force him to leave my country?”
4Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept. 5When Baasha heard about it, he stopped his work on the town of Ramah.
6Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to fortify Ramah. Then he fortified the towns of Geba and Mizpah with these same stones and wood.
Hanani the Prophet Condemns Asa
7Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said:
You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army. 8Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them. 9The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
10When Asa heard this, he was so angry that he put Hanani in prison. Asa was also cruel to some of his people.
Asa Dies
(1 Kings 15.23,24)
11Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 12In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help. 13He died two years later.
14Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
translation_text:
Asa na ti tei to
1Judah teo pɛ Asa na di paare o ke bena fintɔ-yaredo to mo Isarele teo pɛ Baasa nwoŋi o vo o kwaare jara de Judah tiina bam. O ma wane o jwoŋi Rama teo o daare o fɔge o lɔ-ko o che. O maa yere jei sem se nɔɔna yé wane ba lɛɛne ba vo Asa laŋa kam naa ba nwoŋi da ba kɛ.
2Asa déem ma kwei lu-nyenno wonnu de sabu-seŋa wonnu telo na wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam de o tete sɔŋɔ wone to o pa se nɔɔna ja-te ba vo Siria teo pɛ Ben-hadadi tei Damasika ne. 3O ma toŋe kwora o we, “Pa se dé gwoni ni daane, nenɛɛne ko déem na ye tei nmo kwo de amo kwo tetare laŋa ne to. Nii mo, a jege lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa mo se a pa‑m. Nam sɛ se n yiri ni delo n déem na ke de Isarele teo pɛ Baasa to, se ko pa o viiri o daare a laŋa kam.”
4Ben-hadadi ma sɛ Pɛ Asa na tage tei to. O ma toŋe o jar-keira de ba yiga tiina se ba vo ba kwaare jara de Isarele tiina bam. Jara yam wone, ba ma wane ba jwoŋi Yijon, de Dan, de Abel-Mayim, dedaane Nafitali teene delo ba na yeini ba kwei ba zela ba tiŋi de wone to maama. 5Isarele teo pɛ Baasa na yɔɔre o ni konto to, o ma yage Rama teo kom lɔɔm de o totoŋe dwi maama. 6O na viiri to, Pɛ Asa ma pa se Judah tiina maama vo ba zeŋe kandwa yam, de da-kwollu tem Baasa nɔɔna bam ya na jege ba lɔ teo kom to ba ja ba kɛ. Pɛ Asa déem kwei wonnu tem konto mo o ma o lɔ Geba de Mizipa teene dem.
7Konto na ke ko kɛ to, mo Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu Hanani vei Judah teo pɛ Asa tei ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Nmo na ve se n kwei n teena n daŋe n Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom baŋa ne, ye n pa n teena wo Siria pɛ wom wone to ŋwaane, nam ta‑n yei we Siria pɛ wom de o jar-keira bam yɔɔre ba lu n jeŋa ne mo. 8Kusi tiina bam, de Libia tiina bam déem jege jar-keira kɔ-fɔrɔ, de jara torokooro dedɛ, dedaane sisein-dira dedɛ. De ko maama de, Baŋa Wɛ déem kwei-ba o ke n dam kuri ne, n teena na daŋe o baŋa ne to ŋwaane. 9Baŋa Wɛ yia yam nam dole ya kaare tega baŋa ni maama se o nii balo na yɔɔre ba ke ba teena o wone to baŋa ne se o daare o pa-ba dam. Nmo nam toŋe jworim mo de n na ke tei to. Konto ŋwaane, ko zege zem se ko taa via, nmo laam wó ta‑n zoore jara-keim wone mo taa.”
10Asa na nigi Hanani taane dem to, o bane ma tiini de zaŋe pa o ja Hanani o pe peena diga ne. O déem ta yɔɔre o jege o nɔɔna bam badaara mo o bɛɛsa.
11Asa déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, ko zege o paare dem boboa ne se ko yi de na kweeli maŋa kalo to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa de Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 12O na di paare o ke bena fintɔ-nogo maŋa kalo ne to mo jaweo to o nɛ ne pa se o gwarege. O jaweo kom na tu ko chɛ to, o wo lwoori wolim Baŋa Wɛ tei ne, ye o tɔge liri-keira se ba nii o baŋa ne. 13Asa na di paare o ke bena finna-dedoa to, mo o tega. 14Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli yibeeli delo o ya na bɔɔre o tiŋi David teo Jerusalem wone to. Ba ma daŋe‑o gandwa baŋa ne, ye ba kwei talwoŋ-ywei de terale nwi dwi dwi ba ke da. Ba ta ma tɔrege min-vo-zɔŋɔ se ba zuli o yere.

english_text:
King Jehoshaphat of Judah
1Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king and strengthened his defenses against Israel. 2He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
3-4When Jehoshaphat's father had first become king of Judah, he was faithful to the Lord and refused to worship the god Baal as the kings of Israel did. Jehoshaphat followed his father's example and obeyed and worshiped the Lord. And so the Lord blessed Jehoshaphat 5and helped him keep firm control of his kingdom. The people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, but even after he became very rich and respected, 6he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
7In the third year of Jehoshaphat's rule, he chose five officials and gave them orders to teach the Lord's Law in every city and town in Judah. They were Benhail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah. 8Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along. 9They carried with them a copy of the Lord's Law wherever they went and taught the people from it.
10The nations around Judah were afraid of the Lord's power, so none of them attacked Jehoshaphat. 11Philistines brought him silver and other gifts to keep peace. Some of the Arab people brought him 7,700 rams and the same number of goats.
12As Jehoshaphat became more powerful, he built fortresses and cities 13where he stored supplies. He also kept in Jerusalem some experienced soldiers 14from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans.
Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had 300,000 soldiers under his command. 15Jehohanan was second in command, with 280,000 soldiers under him. 16Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with 200,000 soldiers under him.
17Eliada was a brave warrior who commanded the troops from Benjamin. He had 200,000 soldiers under his command, all of them armed with bows and shields. 18Jehozabad was second in command, with 180,000 soldiers under him. 19These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
translation_text:
Judah teo Pɛ Jehosafate taane
1Asa bu Jehosafate ma leiri o kwo wom yuu ne o ji pɛ. O déem fɔge Judah kateiri dem de dam se ba wane Isarele tiina bam ba jeeri de jara. 2O ma kwei jar-keira o zege teene delo na lɔge de pe to maama wone o che-de. O ta ma pa jar-keira badwonna zege ba che Judah teene dedwonna, dedaane Efrayim teene delo o kwo Asa ya na wane o di jara baŋa ne to.
3 Baŋa Wɛ déem nam wo Jehosafate tei ne mo, kokuri to, o nɔn-donne maŋa ne o yɔɔre o ke ne o nabaaro David déem na ke tei to mo. O déem ve se o kaane Baal jwona yam mo. 4O nam sɛ se o taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ wom o kwo de déem na zuli to, ye o ke o tɔge Wɛ nia yam. O wo lwoni Isarele tiina kikia yam. 5Baŋa Wɛ de ma woli Jehosafate se o taa tei o teo kom de dam. Judah tiina bam maama maa jaane pɛɛra ba tui ba pa Jehosafate, pa se o jejegero tiini te puli, ye o yere de zaŋe. 6O déem yɔɔre o tɔge Baŋa Wɛ chwei sem de o wo maama mo. O ma ja wara-jei bimbina yam o chɔge o yage, ye o daare o chochoge Asera nyenyego dɛ sem se Judah tiina daa yé taa zuli-te.
7Jehosafate na di paare o ke bena yatɔ to, mo o toŋe o dedɛɛra banu se ba taa tole Judah teene dem wone ba bere nɔɔna Wɛ nia yam. Nɔɔna bam déem ye Ben-Hayili, de Obadia, de Zekaria, de Netaneli, de Mikaya mo. 8Levi tiina badwonna de maa tɔge ba wo ba wone. Ba maa ye Semaya, de Netania, de Zebadia, de Asaheli, de Semiramofa, de Jehonatan, de Adonija, de Tobija, dedaane Tobi-Adonija. Wɛ kaanem tiina balei de maa wo ba wone, ba yera na ye Elisama de Jehoram to. 9Ba déem jege Baŋa Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom mo ba beeri Judah teene dem maama wone. Jei selo maama ba maa ná via, ba yeini ba kwei Wɛ nia yam mo ba bere nɔɔna bam.
10 Baŋa Wɛ foone déem ma ja teene delo maama na gilimi de kaare Judah to. Ba daa wo sɛ se ba kwaare jara de Pɛ Jehosafate. 11Filisi tiina badaara ma ja lu-nyenno de pɛɛra yadwonna ba ba ba pa Jehosafate se ba sɛ ba pa‑o. Arabi tiina de ma ja pei de bone ba ba pa‑o. Te maa ye pi-bale morro terepɛ de bia yarepɛ (7,700), dedaane bone morro terepɛ de bia yarepɛ (7,700).
12Jehosafate déem yɔɔre o na dam mo maŋa maama wone. O ma lɔ dalem jei, de teene dedwonna Judah kateiri dem ne, se o taa tiŋi o wonnu de wone. 13O maa jege zela dedɛ o na tiŋi-ya Judah teene dem wone to. O déem ta yage jar-keira balo na tiini ba yei jara laŋa to mo Jerusalem teo kom wone. 14Ba kɔgɔ déem na ye tei ko tɔge de ba sɔ-yuni tem to mo tento:
Judah dwi tiina bam wone, Adina déem mo ye jar-keira bam yiga tu. O kwaga nɔɔna déem ye jar-keira morro bia yatɔ (300,000) mo.
15Jehohanan mo saŋe wonto kwaga. O de kwaga nɔɔna maa ye jar-keira morro bia yalei de funɔnɔ (280,000).
16Dedɛɛro wolo na ke batɔ tu to déem ye Zikiri bu Amasia mo. Wonto déem yɔɔre o nwoŋi mo o tete ne Baŋa Wɛ totoŋa yam ŋwaane. O kwaga nɔɔna maa ye jar-keira morro bia yalei (200,000).
17Benjamin dwi tiina bam wone, Eliada déem mo ye bembea kalo na nii ba jar-keira morro bia yalei (200,000) to. Banto déem zei tɛ dedaane jara-keim nantane mo.
18Wolo de daa na saŋe wonto kwaga to maa ye Jehozabadi. O déem jege jar-keira morro bi de funɔnɔ (180,000) balo na zei ba jara zela to mo.
19Jar-keira balo déem na maŋe Jerusalem ne ba toŋe ba pa pɛ wom to mo konto. Jar-keira badaara maa yere teene delo na lɔge de pe ye de jage de wo Judah ni maama ne to.

english_text:
Micaiah Warns King Ahab of Israel
(1 Kings 22.1-28)
1Jehoshaphat was now very rich and famous. He signed a treaty with King Ahab of Israel by arranging the marriage of his son and Ahab's daughter.
2One day, Jehoshaphat went to visit Ahab in his capital city of Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle and prepared a big feast to honor Jehoshaphat and the officials with him. Ahab talked about attacking the city of Ramoth in Gilead, 3and finally asked, “Jehoshaphat, would you go with me to attack Ramoth?”
“Yes,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army is at your command. 4But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
5Ahab sent for 400 prophets and asked, “Should I attack the city of Ramoth?”
“Yes!” the prophets answered. “God will help you capture the city.”
6But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
7“We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.”
“Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied. 8Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
9All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
10Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
11All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth and promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
12Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
13“I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
14Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?”
“Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
15Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
16 Micaiah answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers wandering around, lost in the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These troops have no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
17Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
18Micaiah replied:
I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him. 19The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?”
They talked about it for a while, 20then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.”
“How?” the Lord asked.
21“I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.”
“Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
22Ahab, this is exactly what has happened. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
23Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
24Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
25Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria. 26Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
27Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!”
Ahab Dies at Ramoth
(1 Kings 22.29-35)
28Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead. 29Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
30The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders to attack only Ahab. 31So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop. 32And when they realized he wasn't Ahab, they left him alone.
33However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
34The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_text:
Wɛ sampwora Mikaya taane
1Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate déem tiini o jege jejegero mo, ye o yere de zaŋe jei maama ne. O déem ma tɔge kadiri baŋa ne o ke ni-sɛɛm de Isarele teo pɛ Ahab. 2Ko na ke bena fenfee to mo Jehosafate zaŋe o vo Samaria se o na Ahab. Ahab ma pa ba go pei de naane dedɛ se o ma o zuli Jehosafate de o dedɛɛra. O laam ma bwɛ ded‑o se ba vo ba kwaare jara ba li Ramofa-Gilead. 3Ahab ma bwei Jehosafate o we, “Nmo wó sɛ se n da de amo se dé vo Ramofa-Gilead dé ke jara de-ba na?”
Jehosafate ma leiri o we, “Dé ye chorro mo daane. Ta‑n yei we debam jar-keira ye nmo tete nyem mo. Dé zege n kwaga ne.” 4Jehosafate ta ma ta de Ahab o we, “Nam pa se dé da yiga dé bwei dé nii Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa na ye tei to se dé laam daare dé vo.”
5Ahab ma bwoŋi Wɛ sampwori sem o ke daane. Ba maa ye nɔɔna bia yana (400). O ma bwei-ba o we, “Chwoŋa wora se a vo Ramofa-Gilead a ke jara de-ba, naa a yé vei?” Sampwori sem ma leiri ba we, “Pɛ, nam véi n gware-ba, se Wɛ wó kwei-ba o ke n jeŋa ne.”
6De ko de, Jehosafate ta ma bwei o we, “Baŋa Wɛ sampwora wodwoŋi ta wora ywo-seeni se dé bwei o de dé nii na?”
7Pɛ Ahab ma leiri‑o o we, “Nɔɔno wodwoŋi ta daare, o yere mo Mikaya ye o ye Imila bu. Dé wó wane dé da wonto baŋa dé lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa. Ko nam na ye tei to, o ba swoi se o taa pworisi wo-laaro o pa-ne, lɛɛro yerane mo o tɛa. Konto ŋwaane mo a ba laga o ni taane fase.” Jehosafate ma leiri o we, “Ko nam dae se n ta konto dwoŋi.”
8Ahab ma bwoŋi o dedɛɛra bam dedoa ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Ke lela n vo n ja Imila bu Mikaya n ba ywo-seeni.”
9Isarele teo pɛ Ahab dedaane Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate déem zo ba paare gwaaro mo ba jeini ba paare yitunnu baŋa ne ko maŋe de Samaria teo manchwoŋo ni dem. Jeiga kam déem ye mena ferem jeiga mo. Sampwori sem maama maa zege ba yiga ne ba pworisa. 10Ba dedoa yere na ye Zedekia ye o ye Chenaana bu to ma mage luu o ma o ji nyea. O ma ta de Ahab o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Nyea yanto bere we, n jege dam mo se n ma n chu Siria tiina bam n go.”
11Sampwori sem maama de déem pworisi konto mo ye ba we, “Pɛ, zaŋe n vo Ramofa-Gilead n ke jara n wane-ba. Baŋa Wɛ lage o kwei teo kom o ke n jeŋa ne mo.”
12Dedɛɛro wolo na vei se o bwoŋi Mikaya to ma ba o ta de Mikaya o we, “Nii mo! Sampwori sedwonna sem jege ni dedwe mo ba pworisi wo-laaro ba pa pɛ wom. Nmo de nam jege se n pworisi zaane taane mo ne banto na ke tei to.”
13Mikaya ma leiri‑o o we, “Ne Baŋa Wɛ na ye ŋwea tu to, ko ye chega mo we, amo Tu Wɛ na wó pa ni se a ta kolo to yerane mo a wó ta a bere pɛ wom.”
14Mikaya na vei o yi Ahab tei to, Ahab ma bwei‑o o we, “Mikaya, chwoŋa wora se dé vo Ramofa-Gilead dé ke jara de-ba, naa dé yé véi?” Mikaya ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, zaŋe n vo n ke jara yam n wane-ba, se Wɛ mo lage o kwei teo kom o ke n jeŋa ne.”
15Ahab ma yɔɔre o ta Mikaya o we, “A maŋe a ta de nmo kuni dedɛ we, n jege se n du we n wó ta chega taane yerane mo n bere-ne maŋa kalo maama n na yeini n pworisi Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane to.”
16Mikaya laam ma ta o we, “A nɛ Isarele jar-keira bam maama na jage peero tem baŋa ne ye ba beeri yɔɔ yerane, nenɛɛne pei selo na ba jege nayero to. Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we, ‘Nɔɔna banto ba jege yuu tu. Yage-na se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ chemm de yazura.’ ”
17Isarele teo pɛ Ahab ma ta de Jehosafate o we, “A ya maŋe a ta de nmo we, o bá sɛ o pworisi wo-laaro o pa-ne, se lɛɛro yerane mo o tɛa.”
18Mikaya daa ma ta o bere Ahab o we, “Nam cheigi Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ne kwora kalo to. A nɛ Baŋa Wɛ na jei o paare yituŋu baŋa ne ye Wɛ telaao kɔgɔ kom maama zege ba gilimi‑o, o jazem de jagwia seeni. 19Baŋa Wɛ maa we, ‘Wɔ mo wó sɛ o vo o gane Isarele teo pɛ Ahab se o vo Ramofa-Gilead o ke jara de-ba se o ga o ŋwea?’ Kɔgɔ kom maama dedoa dedoa ma ta o boboŋa. 20Ko kwola ne to, chichira kadwoŋi ma nwoŋi ka zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne ye ka ta ka we, ‘Amo wó wane a vo a gane Ahab’. Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei-ka o we, ‘N lage n ke tɛ mo n wane n ke konto?’ 21Chichira kam ma leiri ka we, ‘A lage a vo a pa se Ahab sampwori sem pworisi vwa pworisim mo.’ Baŋa Wɛ maa we, ‘Nmo wó na chwoŋa se n soge‑o. Nam véi n ke konto.’ 22Nam lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ seene o pa se n sampwori sem fɔe vwa mo ba pa‑m. Chega ŋwaane to, Baŋa Wɛ yɔɔre o tiŋi lɛɛro mo se te ba n baŋa.”
23Konto na ke to mo Chenaana bu Zedekia zaŋe o vo o mage Mikaya o yibia ne, ye o bwei‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ jworo ke tɛ mo ko yage amo ye ko ba nmo tei ko ŋɔɔne dede‑m?”
24Mikaya ma leiri o we, “Nii mo. Dɛ dem n na wó zo di-yuu wone n seigi n tete to, nmo wó lɔre debam wone wolo na tage chega to mo.”
25Isarele teo pɛ Ahab ma pa ni se ba ja Mikaya ye o we, “Ja-o-na á ja á vo teo kom dedɛɛro Amon tei, dedaane amo bu Joasa tei. 26Ta-na de-ba we, ‘Pɛ wom na tage kolo to mo tento: Ke-na nɔɔno wonto peena diga ne. Ta‑á pa‑o bworobworo fenfee de na yerane se ko taa nii maŋa kam a na wó zege jara yam wone a jwoori de yazura to.’ ”
27Mikaya ma leiri pɛ wom o we, “N ná seene n zege jara yam wone n jwoori de yazura, ko nam dae Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ-ne kwora kam.” Mikaya ta ma ta de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom o we, “Á maama yé swei-na a na taga taane delo to.”
Pɛ Ahab toone
28Isarele teo pɛ Ahab de Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate déem ma zaŋe ba vo Ramofa-Gilead se ba ke jara de-ba. 29Ahab ma ta de Jehosafate o we, “De ná zo jara yam wone, a laam wó leiri a yibia se ba yé lɔre-ne. Ko daare nmo wó zo n paare gwaaro tem.” Ahab ma seene o ke ne o na taga tei to, ye ba maama vo se ba ke jara yam.
30Siria tiina pɛ wom déem ya maŋe o bwoŋi o jara-keim toroko-dira dedɛɛra bam mo ye o pa-ba ni we, “Kwaare-na jara yam de Isarele teo pɛ wom yerane, se ko dae de jar-keira badaara bam, ba ná maŋe ba ye dedɛɛra tei de.” 31Siria jara-keim dedɛɛra bam na nɛ Jehosafate ye o zo o paare gwaaro tem to, ba maa boŋe we, ko ye Isarele teo pɛ wom mo. Ba ma fɔɔre ba yi se ba ke jara ded‑o. Jehosafate na nɛ-ba to, o ma laare de kwor-dɛa pa Baŋa Wɛ woli‑o. Wɛ ma che Siria jar-keira bam ye ba wo wane ba yi o yera. 32Ba ma maane we ko dae Isarele teo pɛ wom. Ba ma yage o yera ye ba kɛ.
33Siria jar-keiru wodwoŋi déem saŋe o taŋa mo o ta chene yɔɔ yerane. Chene dem ma vo de zɔ Isarele teo pɛ Ahab o nyɔɔne seeni mɛ o jara zela yam na wo kwoli‑o to. Ahab ma ta de o toroko-diru wom o we, “Pa se dé ke lela dé pipiri dé vo dáa dáa jara yam wone, se a nɛ zonne mo.” 34Jara yam déem kea dɛ dem maama wone mo. Pɛ Ahab ma maŋe o toroko kom wone o sale-ko o jeeri Siria tiina bam. Dɛ dem konto wɛ na maa zoore maŋa kalo to mo o tega.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem. 2But the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and said:
By helping that wicked Ahab, you have made friends with someone who hates the Lord. Now the Lord God is angry with you! 3But not everything about you is bad. You destroyed the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah—that shows you have tried to obey the Lord.
Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges To Settle Cases
4Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
5He assigned judges to each of the fortified cities in Judah 6and told them:
Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide. 7So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
8Jehoshaphat also chose some Levites, some priests, and some of the family leaders, and he appointed them to serve as judges in Jerusalem. 9He told them:
Faithfully serve the Lord! 10The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
11Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_text:
1Pɛ Jehosafate ma zege jara yam ne o jwoori Jerusalem de yazura. 2Hanani bu Jehu na ye Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu to ma vo se o jeeri‑o. O ma ta pɛ wom o we, “Ko ye ko chwoŋa ne se nmo vo n woli puseŋ-nyena, ye n ta me de balo na chuli Baŋa Wɛ to na? Nmo keim dem konto pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom zaŋe n baŋa ne mo. 3De ko de, nmo ke wo-laaro tedwonna n ŋwea ne, de nmo na jaane Asera nyenyego dɛ selo nɔɔna na zuli n tega kam ne to n chochoge n yage, ye n ta ja boboŋa se n ta‑n tɔge Wɛ to.”
Jehosafate yiga tiina taane
4Jehosafate déem zoore Jerusalem teo kom wone mo. O ma yeini o kwei maŋa o tole o paare laŋa kam ni maama, ko zege Beeriseba ne se ko yi Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam. O ma yeini o kaane-ba se ba pipiri ba jwoori ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye ba nabaara Wɛ to. 5Judah laŋa kam maama ne mo o kuri yiga tiina o yage teene delo na lɔge de pe to wone. 6O ma ta de-ba o we, “Fɔge-na á ta‑á yei á tete. Kolo ŋwaane, abam ná bore nɔɔna bora, ko ye se ko tɔge de Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa mo, se ko dae de nabiina na lage tei to. Wonto nam wó taa wo á tei ne se á ta‑á yeini á bore nɔɔna taane á pa-ba. 7Nam yɔɔre á ta‑á kɔre Baŋa Wɛ, se á ta‑á di nɔɔna taana ko chwoŋa ne. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ ba lage kampina de kalipera totoŋa. O nam ba sɛ se á ta‑á kuri nɔɔna da-wone.”
8Jehosafate déem ta kuri Levi dwi tiina, de kaanem tiina badwonna, de Isarele sɔ-yuni yiga tiina badaara mo se ba taa tɔge Baŋa Wɛ nia yam ŋwaane ba kwɛ nɔɔna taana ba pa-ba. Banto maa zoore Jerusalem teo wone. 9O ma pa-ba ni dento:
“Ta‑á kɔre-na Baŋa Wɛ de á na toŋe de boboŋ-laaro de á wo maama tei to. 10Abam chorro ná nwoŋi Judah teo de teo maama ne ba jaane taane delo ba ba á tei, se á nii de baŋa ne á pa-ba. Ko ná ye nɔn-gora taane mo, naa ko ná ye ba sage Wɛ nia yam wone, naa ba ke ba chɔge o bera yam, naa o chullu tem de, abam wó kaane-ba mo se ba daa yé taa ke wɛleera ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. Konto de maa wó che abam de á chorro tem se Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom dem yé ba á baŋa. Ke-na konto se wɛleera daa yé taa wo á yuu ne.
11Ko ná ye Baŋa Wɛ chwoŋa kam taane maama, kaanem nakwe tu Amaria nam mo wó taa wo á yiga ne. Ko ta ná ye paare dem taana yadaara yam, Judah dwi tiina nakwe Zebadia na ye Isameli bu to de maa wó taa wo á yiga ne. Levi dwi tiina bam de maa wó taa toŋe ba woli abam. Vɔ-na á wo se á ta‑á toŋa, kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ toŋe o woli balo na toŋe de chega to mo.”

english_text:
Moab and Ammon Are Defeated
1Some time later, the armies of Moab and Ammon, together with the Meunites, went to war against Jehoshaphat. 2Messengers told Jehoshaphat, “A large army from Edom east of the Dead Sea has invaded our country. They have already reached En-Gedi.”
3Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow. 4They immediately left for Jerusalem to ask for the Lord's help.
5After everyone from Judah and Jerusalem had come together at the Lord's temple, Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard 6and prayed:
You, Lord, are the God our ancestors worshiped, and from heaven you rule every nation in the world. You are so powerful that no one can defeat you. 7 Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever. 8Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you. 9They believed that whenever this land is struck by war or disease or famine, your people can pray to you at the temple, and you will hear their prayer and save them.
10 You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed. 11Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us. 12Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
13While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple, 14the Lord's Spirit suddenly spoke to Jahaziel, a Levite from the Asaph clan. 15 Then Jahaziel said:
Your Majesty and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem, the Lord says that you don't need to be afraid or let this powerful army discourage you. God will fight on your side! 16So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley. 17 You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
18Jehoshaphat bowed low to the ground and everyone worshiped the Lord. 19Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
20Early the next morning, as everyone got ready to leave for the desert near Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Listen my friends, if we trust the Lord God and believe what these prophets have told us, the Lord will help us, and we will be successful.” 21Then he explained his plan and appointed men to march in front of the army and praise the Lord for his holy power by singing:
“Praise the Lord!
His love never ends.”
22As soon as they began singing, the Lord confused the enemy camp, 23so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
24When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground. 25So Jehoshaphat and his troops went into the camp to carry away everything of value. They found a large herd of livestock, a lot of equipment, clothes, and other valuable things. It took them three days to carry it all away, and there was still some left over.
26Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
27-28Jehoshaphat led the crowd back to Jerusalem. And as they marched, they played harps and blew trumpets. They were very happy because the Lord had given them victory over their enemies, so when they reached the city, they went straight to the temple.
29When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid 30to invade Judah. The Lord let Jehoshaphat's kingdom be at peace.
Jehoshaphat Dies
(1 Kings 22.41-50)
31Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi. 32Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done, 33but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
34Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
35While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel. 36They agreed to build several seagoing ships at Ezion-Geber. 37But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_text:
Jehosafate wane o dona jara wone
1Ko kwaga seeni mo Moaba tiina bam, de Amon tiina bam, de Meyunim tiina badaara tu se ba kwaare jara de Jehosafate.
2Nɔɔna badwonna ma vo ba ta de Jehosafate ba we, “Kɔ-fɔrɔ mo zege Edom seeni, ko na maŋe de Yɛ naneo kom bubɛ dedwoŋi dem ne to, ba beene‑m de jara. Ba nam maŋe ba yi Hazazon-Tamare.” (En-gedi mo konto.) 3Foone ma zo Jehosafate, ye o seene o yia o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o lɔre o na wó ke tei to. O ta ma pa ni se balo maama na zoore Judah ne to vɔ ni. 4Judah tiina bam ma jeeri daane Jerusalem ne se ba lwoori wolim Baŋa Wɛ tei ne. Judah teene dem maama wone, nɔɔna bam wo nwoŋi ba kwɛɛre.
5Jehosafate laam ma zaŋe o zege Judah tiina bam, de Jerusalem tiina bam kɔ-fɔrɔ kom yiga ne. Ba maa wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam konkɔl-doŋo kom yiga ne. 6O maa we:
“Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo ye dé nabaara bam Wɛ. Nmo wo Wɛ telaao ne mo, ye n jege paare n di tega baŋa teene dem maama ne. Nmo tiini n dana mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware nmo yiga o choa. 7Debam Tu Wɛ, nmo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam déem na tu ywo-seeni to, n zeili balo ya na zoore tega kanto wone to mo, ye n daare n kwei-ka n pa n badwoŋi Abaraham dwi dem we, ba taa tei-ka se ko taa vei wuu. 8Ba de nam na zoore tega kam wone to, ba lɔge wara-diga mo n yere dem zula ŋwaane. Ba maa we, 9‘Ne cham dwi delo maama mo ná yi debam tega kanto wone, ko ná ye jara mo, naa waarem, naa jawe-chɛɛro, naa kana mo de, dé wó ba dé zege diga kanto na ye n yere dem zula ŋwaane to yiga ne dé lwoori wolim nmo tei ne. Nmo de maa wó cheigi dé wɛ-lworo kom n daare n jwoŋi debam n yage.’
10Nam fɔge n nii kolo na yi debam leile. Dé dona nwoŋi Amon, de Moaba, de Edom peero laŋa kam ne mo ba ba se ba jeeri debam de jara. Dé nabaara bam déem na nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba ba ywo-seeni to, teene dem konto nam ye delo n na tage de-ba we, ba yé chɔge-de to mo. Ba ma seene ba pipiri ba yage teene dem konto, ba wo chɔge-de. 11Ba laam na lage ba jwoori ba ŋwe debam tei to mo tento: ba boŋe se ba zeili debam mo tega kalo nmo tete na kwei n pa debam se dé taa tei to wone. 12Dé Tu Wɛ, nmo nam bá‑n waare-ba na? Debam ba jege dam se dé jeeri kɔ-fɔrɔ konto na beene se ba kwaare jara de debam to. Debam yɔɔre dé ye boremaa mo keim dento wone. Dé teena nam za daŋe nmo baŋa ne mo.”
13Judah dwi tiina maama déem zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, ko woli de ba kaana, de ba bia, de ba bu-sese mo. 14Levi dwi tu Jahazeli déem tɔge o wo kɔgɔ kom wone. O maa ye Zekaria bu mo. O déem ye Asaf sɔ-yuu kom nɔɔno mo, ye o nwoŋi Matania, de Jeyeli, de Benaya dwi dem wone. Baŋa Wɛ Jworo déem chugi o baŋa ne mo, 15ye o we:
“Jehosafate, nmo de balo maama na zoore Judah, de Jerusalem wone to, cheigi-na a taane dento. Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei de abam to mo tento: Yé ta‑á fona, nam yé pa-na se á vɔna pare kɔ-fɔrɔ konto ŋwaane. Ko dae abam mo tei jara yam, se ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo tei-ya. 16Jwa ne nam nwoŋi-na se á jeeri á dona bam de jara. Ba wó taa diini Ziza zwoŋo kom chwoŋa kam pa se á jeeri-ba bwolo kolo na wo Jeruweli kagoa kam wɛ-puli seeni to ni ne. 17Abam maŋe á ba lage á ke jara yam kɔtaa! Nam véi-na á fɔge á chichei á zege á zega jei sem ne, se á nii á na Baŋa Wɛ na lage o tɔge chwoŋa kalo o jwoŋi abam o yage to. Konto ŋwaane, Judah de Jerusalem tiina bam, yé ta‑á fona-na. Nam yé pa-na se á vɔna pare. Jwa véi-na á jeeri-ba de jara, se Baŋa Wɛ wo á tei ne.”
18Jehosafate na nigi konto to, o ma tiiri o vwi o yibia tega ne o zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Judah de Jerusalem tiina bam maama de ma ke konto. 19Levi tiina bam badaara na nwoŋi Kohafe de Kora sɔ-yuni tem ne to de ma zaŋe wɛɛne ba bage tia lei ba yaga, se ba ma zuli Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to.
20Tega na poore tetete to, nɔɔna bam ma zaŋe se ba nwoŋi ba vo Tekoa kagoa kam seeni. Jehosafate ma zege ba yiga ne o ta we, “Judah de Jerusalem tiina bam, cheigi-na a taane dento. Ke-na á wo-dedoa de á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, se wonto wó pa á na dam. Kwei-na á chega á ke o sampwori sem de wone, se á wó na yiga-veiŋa.” 21Pɛ wom laam ma bwɛ de o nɔɔna bam, ye o daare o kuri balo na wó taa leeni ba seini Baŋa Wɛ ye ba tei‑o o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom ŋwaane to. O ma pa ba to jar-keira bam yiga ne ba leeni ba we:
“Ke-na Baŋa Wɛ lei,
o swono kom na wora taa wuu to ŋwaane.”
22Ba na yɔɔre ba bobo se ba taa leeni konto to, mo Baŋa Wɛ pɔpɔ o zaŋe Judah tiina dona bam baŋa ne. 23Amon tiina bam de Moaba tiina bam ma li Edom jar-keira bam ba yɔɔre ba go ba maama. Konto kwaga ne mo ba tete daa pipiri ba go daane.
24Judah tiina bam na gwɛ ba vo ba yi jeiga kalo na jeeri kagoa kam to, mo ba zege da ba tole ba na we, ba dona kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama laam yɔɔre ba ye twa mo ba tigi tega kam maama ne, ye ba wolowolo wo lugi. 25Jehosafate de o jar-keira bam ma yɔɔre ba vo ba pɛ wo-kuri dwi maama se ba ja-te ba viiri. Ba déem wane ba kwaleme jara zela dedɛ, de gwaaro, de wo-kura yadwonna mo. Ba déem kwei da yatɔ mo ba kwaleme wonnu tem konto, ye ba ga tedaara ŋwa ba yage-te da. 26Da yana dɛ dem ne, ba ma jeeri daane Beraka bwolo kom ne se ba tei Baŋa Wɛ. De zem maama, ba ta jege bwolo kom konto yere ba bwoi we ‘Tia Bwolo’ mo.
27Jehosafate laam ma to Judah de Jerusalem tiina bam maama yiga ne pa ba leeni de wopwolo ba maa jwoori Jerusalem. Ba ke konto kolo ŋwaane Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ ba di ywoni ba dona bam chɔgem ŋwaane. 28Ba na yi Jerusalem to, mo ba yɔɔre Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ba zo ka wo, ye ba daa ta mage ba kwanno, de kwɛɛra zela dwi dwi, ye ba wu nabwanno.
29Teene delo na gilimi da to nɔɔna na nigi Baŋa Wɛ na jaŋe tei o wane Isarele tiina dona o pa-ba to, mo foone tiini de ja-ba Wɛ dam dem ŋwaane. 30Konto de ma pa yazura wo Jehosafate paare laŋa kam wone. Kokuri to, o Tu Wɛ wom déem chege-ba ba dona maama jeŋa ne pa ba daa ba daane-ba.
Jehosafate paare na kweeli tei to
31Jehosafate déem jege bena fintɔ-yanu mo ye o bobo se o di Judah teo paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena finlei-yanu. O nu déem ye Silihi bukɔ Azuba mo. 32Jehosafate déem yɔɔre o kwei o kwo Asa totoŋ-naga kam mo, o wo ywori ka wone kɔtaa, pa se o totoŋa su Baŋa Wɛ yi. 33O déem nam wo wane o chɔge wara-jei bimbina yam. Nɔɔna ya ta wo ke ba boboŋa ne se ba taa zuli ba nabaara Wɛ wom.
34Jehosafate déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, ko zege o paare dem boboa ne se ko yi de na kweeli maŋa kalo to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Hanani bu Jehu memaŋa tɔnɔ kom wone, ye te ta wo Isarele teo pwa tɔnɔ kom wone.
35Jehosafate ta na ye Judah pɛ to, mo o ke ni-sɛɛm de Isarele pɛ Ahazia. Ahazia nam tiini o toŋe puseŋa mo. 36Jehosafate ma ke ni ded‑o pa ba ke nabwooru se ba taa ma ba pipia. Ba déem zege Ezion-gebera ne mo ba ke-te. 37Eliazera na ye Dodavahu bu ye o nwoŋi Maresa teo ne to ma pworisi taane o vane Jehosafate o we, “Nmo na vei n ke ni-sɛɛm de Ahazia to ŋwaane, Baŋa Wɛ lage o ja nabwooru telo n na ke to mo o chɔge o yage.” Nabwooru tem ma seene te chochoge ye te daa wo wane te tɔge naneo kom baŋa te ke pipiu.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.
King Jehoram of Judah
(2 Kings 8.16-24)
2King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. 3Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
4After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders. 5He was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled eight years from Jerusalem.
6Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong, 7 but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
8 While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king. 9Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night, 10but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time.
