Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped. 11Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
12One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said:
I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather. 13Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
14Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own. 15You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
16The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram. 17They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
18After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease. 19About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
20Jehoram was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled 8 years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_text:
1Jehosafate ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa bam yibeeli wone David teo Jerusalem ne. O toone dem kwaga ne o bu Jehoram ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ. 2Jehosafate déem ta jege bia badwonna. Ba yera maa ye Azaria, de Jeheli, de Zekaria, de Azariahu, de Mikayeli, de Sefatia. Banto maama ye Jehoram nyaana mo. 3Ba kwo déem kwei lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa zela yalo na jege kuri to mo o pa ba maama. O ta ma pa-ba teene delo na wo Judah ne ye de lɔ de pe to. Ko nam ná ye paare dem, o kwei-de o pa Jehoram mo, o na ye o bu-kwea to ŋwaane.
Judah teo pɛ Jehoram taane
4Jehoram na yɔɔre o jeini o kwo paare dem ne o ti to, mo o go o nyaana bam maama, ko woli de Isarele teo dedɛɛra badaara. 5O déem jege bena fintɔ-yalei mo ye o laam ji pɛ. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena nana. 6Jehoram déem kwei Isarele pwa bam totoŋ-naga mo, ne Pɛ Ahab de o dwi dem na ke tei to, kokuri to o di Ahab bukɔ mo. Konto to, o déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. 7Baŋa Wɛ nam wo sɛ se o chɔge Pɛ David dwi dem, bɛŋwaane o maŋe o gwoni ni ded‑o we, o diga kam wó taa tei paare dem taa wuu.
8Jehoram paare dim maŋa ne mo Edom dwi dem ve se ba taa wo Judah pɛ wom dam kuri ne. Ba ma lɛɛre ba tiŋi ba tete pɛ. 9Jehoram ma ja o jar-keira, de ba dedɛɛra bam, de ba torokooro tem maama o vo se o ke jara de Edom tiina. Edom tiina bam ma ba ba gilimi o de o nɔɔna bam ba ke tetare ne. Tete ne mo Jehoram de o jar-keira bam wane ba lu ba jeŋa ne ba jwoori sɔŋɔ. 10De zem maama Edom tiina ta ve mo se ba taa wo Judah tiina dam kuri ne. Libina teo tiina de déem ke konto dwoŋi mo. Ko ye Jehoram na mɛ o kwaga o ya Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye o nabaara Wɛ to ŋwaane mo ko déem ke konto. 11O déem ta lɔge wara-jei bimbina Judah zwonnu tem yuu ne mo. Konto ma pa Jerusalem de Judah tiina bam tusi mo de ba na dɛ ba zuli jwona ba daare Baŋa Wɛ to.
12Dɛ dedwe mo Jehoram jwoŋi tɔnɔ Wɛ sampwora Elija jeŋa ne ye ko popone we:
“Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye n kwo David Wɛ to mo taga o we: Nmo wo sɛ se n kwei n kwo Jehosafate totoŋ-naga kam, naa n kwo-nakwe Asa totoŋ-naga kam de. 13Nmo nam na ke tei to, n kwei Isarele pwa totoŋ-naga kam mo n tɔga. N ma‑n da ko ŋwaane n pa Judah tiina de Jerusalem tiina bam yage Baŋa Wɛ, ba daa ba zuli‑o, nenɛɛne Ahab de o kwaga kam de na ke tei to. Ko woli da, n ta yɔɔre n go n nyaana balo na ye n tete kwo bia to. Banto nam ya gare‑m. 14Baŋa Wɛ de laam nam yɔɔre o ti o yiga mo se o dole n nɔɔna bam jaguli-zane, ko woli de n bia, de n kaana, de n n na jege kolo maama to. 15Nmo tete nam lage n na jawe-chɛɔ mo pa se ko tiini ko ja n wo loro tem taa, ye te laam pi te nwoŋi te to tega ne.”
16Ko kwaga seeni mo Baŋa Wɛ chiŋi Filisi tiina bam, de Arabi tiina balo déem na zoore ba twɛ de Kusi tiina bam to o yage Jehoram yera ne. 17Ba ma vo ba kwaare jara de Judah laŋa kam ba di-ka. Ba ma zo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ba pɛ zela yalo maama na wora to ba ja ba viiri. Ba ta ma kale Jehoram kaana, de o bia bam ba ja ba woli da ba kɛ. Ahazia yerane mo ba déem yage‑o da. Wonto mo ye balaŋa Jehoram bakeiri sem maama wone.
18Wonnu tento maama kwaga ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma pa jawe-chɛɔ ja Jehoram o wo loro tem ne, ye ko yɔɔrem tera. 19Bena yalei na kɛ to mo o wo loro tem tage te nwoŋi, pa o na zonne dedɛ ye o te. O nɔɔna bam déem maa wo tɔrege min-vo-zɔŋɔ se ba ma zuli o yere, ne ba na yeini ba ke tei o nabaara bam toone baŋa ne to.
20Jehoram déem jege bena fintɔ-yalei mo ye o ji pɛ. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare o ke bena nana. O toone dem wo daane nɔɔn-nɔɔno. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli David teo Jerusalem ne, se ko dae pwa yibeela yam wone mo ba suli‑o.

english_text:
King Ahaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 8.25-29; 9.21,27,28)
1Earlier, when the Arabs led a raid against Judah, they killed all of Jehoram's sons, except Ahaziah, the youngest one. So the people of Jerusalem crowned him their king. 2He was 22 years old at the time, and he ruled only one year from Jerusalem.
Ahaziah's mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel, 3and she encouraged her son to sin against the Lord. He followed the evil example of King Ahab and his descendants. 4In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors.
Their advice led to his downfall. 5He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle, 6and he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. And Ahaziah later went there to visit him. 7It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death.
When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family, 8and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah. Jehu killed them on the spot, 9then gave orders to find Ahaziah. Jehu's officers found him hiding in Samaria. They brought Ahaziah to Jehu, who immediately put him to death. They buried Ahaziah only because they respected Jehoshaphat his grandfather, who had done his best to obey the Lord.
There was no one from Ahaziah's family left to become king of Judah.
Queen Athaliah of Judah
(2 Kings 11.1-3)
10As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that, 11but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah. 12Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_text:
Judah teo pɛ Ahazia taane
1Jerusalem teo tiina bam ma pa Jehoram bu Ahazia ji pɛ o leiri o kwo yuu ne, Arabi tiina venverena bam na wuuri ba go Jehoram bakeiri-kwe sem ba daare Ahazia yerane to ŋwaane. Konto to, Ahazia na ye Jehoram bu-balaŋa kam to ma bobo se o di Judah teo paare. 2O déem jege bena finlei-yalei mo ye o laam ji pɛ. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bene dedwe. O nu déem mo ye Atalia wolo na ye Isarele teo pɛ Omiri naa to.
3Ahazia déem kwei pɛ Ahab de o dwi dem totoŋ-naga kam mo, o nu na soge‑o o de puseŋa kikia wone to ŋwaane. 4O tiini o toŋe lwarem o ma o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga, ne Ahab dwi dem na ke tei to. Kokuri to, o kwo toone kwaga ne, banto mo yeini ba bere‑o pa o tusa. 5O ma sɛ ba bera yam pa se o da de Isarele teo pɛ Ahab bu Joram o vo Ramofa-Gilead se ba kwaare jara de Siria teo pɛ Hazayeli. Siria tiina bam ma ke Joram zonne jara yam wone. 6Mo kokuri o jwoori o vo Jezerele teo se ba teibi o fufwollu tem ba pa‑o. O na wo Jezerele ne to, Judah teo pɛ Ahazia ma vo o tei se o ware‑o de o zonne dem.
7Ahazia na vei se o daane Joram jaweo kom to, Wɛ déem tɔge o keim dem konto baŋa ne mo se o pa o paare dem ti. O ta na wo Joram tei ne to mo ba tɔge daane ba vo se ba na Nimisi bu Jehu. Baŋa Wɛ nam ya maŋe o kuri Jehu mo se o pa Ahab dwi dem yere saare. 8Jehu na yɔɔre o wora o chɔge Ahab dwi dem konto to, mo o nɛ Judah teo nakwa badaara, de Ahazia zembaara bam bia badwonna. Ahazia na vei se o daane Joram jaweo kom to, banto ya tɔge o kwaga mo. Jehu ma go ba maama. 9Konto kwaga ne, mo o toŋe o nɔɔna se ba beeri Ahazia jei. Ba ma na we, o vei o seigi o tete Samaria ne mo. Ba ma zi‑o ba ja ba vo Jehu tei ye o de go‑o.
Ba ma da o kwo-nakwe Jehosafate yere ŋwaane ba kwei Ahazia ba suli. Kokuri to, ba déem tage ba tete ne mo ba we, “Jehosafate déem zuli Baŋa Wɛ de o bochare maama, ye Ahazia de ye o naa mo.” Nɔɔn-nɔɔno déem daa maa wo daare Ahazia dwi dem wone se kotu wane o di Judah paare dem.
Atalia de Joasa taane
10Pɛ Ahazia nu Atalia na maane we o bu wom tega to, o ma zaŋe se o pa ba go Judah pa-diga kam nɔn-bia maama. 11Ba na tu se ba go pɛ wom bia bam to, Pɛ Jehoram bukɔ Jehoseba ma ŋɔ Ahazia bu-seseŋa kam yere na ye Joasa to o seigi. O ma kwei bu wom de kaane wolo na jege‑o o kɔna to o vo o seigi o peiga jei ne se Atalia yé na‑o. Jehoseba déem ye Ahazia nakɔ ye o kwori o ye Wɛ kaanem tu Jehoyada kaane. Ko ma pa se o seigi Joasa pa se Atalia wo nɛ chwoŋa se o go‑o. 12Joasa déem maŋe ba tei ne bena yaredo mo, ye ba seigi‑o Wɛ wara-jei sem diga kadwoŋi wone. Maŋa kam konto ne Atalia ma nii Judah teo paare dem baŋa ne.

english_text:
Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah
(2 Kings 11.4-21)
1After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri. 2These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem 3 and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash.
Jehoiada said to them:
Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king. 4Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple, 5one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards. 6Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded. 7You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
8The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty. 9Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders. 10They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
11Jehoiada and his sons brought Joash outside, where they placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of the instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, and the crowd cheered and shouted, “Long live the king!”
12As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple. 13There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
14At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!” 15She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
16Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed, 17then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
18Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing. 19Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
20Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah. 21Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_text:
1Bena yarepɛ na kɛ to mo Wɛ kaanem tu Jehoyada déem jaane baare se o ke keim. O ma ke ni-sɛɛm de dedɛɛra balo na tei jar-keira bi bi to badwonna. Banto maa ye Jeroham bu Azaria, de Jehohanan bu Isameli, de Obeda bu Azaria, de Adaya bu Maaseya, de Zikiri bu Elisafate. 2Dedɛɛra bam konto ma tole Judah teene dem maama wone ba la Levi tiina bam, de Isarele sɔ-yuni yiga tiina bam ba ke daane. Ba maama laam ma vo Jerusalem 3ba zo Wɛ diga kam wone. Ba ma jeeri Joasa yiga ne, ye ba daare ba gwoni ni ded‑o. Jehoyada ma ta de ba maama o we:
“Pɛ wom bu Joasa mo tento o zege á yiga ne. O nam jege se o jeini o di o kwo David paare dem, ne Baŋa Wɛ na maŋe o gwoni ni se ko taa ye tei David dwi dem seeni to mo. 4Abam na jege se á ke tei to mo tento: Abam balo na ye Wɛ kaanem tiina de Levi dwi tiina ye á pɔɔre kuni betɔ to, á kɔgɔ kolo na tui totoŋa siu dɛ ne to chichworo wó taa yere Wɛ diga kam nia yam. 5Abam chicheiro de wó taa nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom, se chicheiro kodwoŋi kom de taa nii Biri-beira ni dem. Abam balo na daare to laam wó taa zege á yere Baŋa Wɛ diga kam konkwallo tem. 6Nɔɔn-nɔɔno dae se o zo Wɛ diga kam, ko ná dae kaanem tiina de Levi tiina balo na jege totoŋa se ba toŋe ka wone to yerane. Banto jege chwoŋa se ba zo, bɛŋwaane ba kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane mo. Balo maama na daare to jege se ba taa nii totoŋe delo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ba se ba taa ke to baŋa ne mo. 7Levi tiina bam jege se ba fɔge ba zege ba gilimi pɛ wom mo ba ke tetare ne, ye ba zei ba jara zela. Nɔɔno wolo ná zo diga kam, se á yɔɔre á go kotu. Pɛ wom nam na wó vo mɛ maama to, se abam de ta‑á wo o tei ne.”
8Levi tiina bam, de Judah tiina bam maama ma seene ba tɔge ni delo maama Wɛ kaanem tu Jehoyada na taga to. Ba dedoa dedoa ma ja ba nɔɔna ba ba Jehoyada tei, ne ko ná ye balo na tui totoŋa siu dɛ ne to, de balo na ti ba totoŋa siu dɛ ne to de. Kokuri to, Jehoyada wo pɛ ba popɔre maama chwoŋa se ba yage ba totoŋa. 9Jehoyada ma kwei chichwoa de jara-keim nantane selo déem na ye David nyem ye te tigi Wɛ wara-jei sem ne to o pa jar-keira dedɛɛra bam. 10O ma pa se nɔɔna bam maama vo ba zege ba gilimi pɛ wom ba ke tetare ne, ye ba zei ba jara zela. Ba déem tigisi ba tete Wɛ diga kam jei maama ne, jagwia seeni de jazem seeni, ko zege kaanem bimbini dem takeiri ne de diga kam tete yiga ne. 11Jehoyada de o bia bam déem ma ja pɛ wom bu Joasa ba ja ba nwoŋi. Ba ma kwei paare yipuga kam ba pu o yuu ne, ye ba daare ba kwei paare tiŋim seina tɔnɔ kom ba ke o jeŋa ne. Ba ma lwo nuga o yuu ne ba ma ba tiŋi‑o paare. Nɔɔna bam ma tɔɔle ba we, “Wɛ wó pa pɛ wom momwɛ-dɛɛre!”
12Atalia na nigi nɔɔna bam na ke sɔɔ ye ba tei pɛ wom to, o ma ke lela o nwoŋi o vo Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem o daare o na nɔn-kɔgɔ kom. 13O ma na pɛ wom na zege ywei delo na wo Wɛ diga kam ni ne to teiŋa ne, ne ba na yeini ba ke tei ba tiŋi pɛ to. Dedɛɛra bam de balo na wui nabwanno to maa zege pɛ wom takeiri ne. Teo kom nɔn-bia bam maama maa chaka de wopwolo ye ba badwonna wui nabwanno. Lein-leena bam de maa zege da de ba kwɛɛra zela ba mɔɔne lei ba seini pɛ wom. Atalia na nɛ konto to, o ma ja o gwaaro tem o vaŋe o kaare ye o we, “Bebare-nyena mo zaŋe a baŋa ne!”
14Jehoyada ma ta de jar-keira dedɛɛra bam o we, “Ja-na Atalia á nwoŋi Wɛ diga kam wone á ke‑o babɛ sem gena tetare ne. Nɔɔno ná kwaane se o woli‑o, se á kwei se-zɔɔ á go kotu.” Kokuri to, Jehoyada ya maŋe o ta we, ba yé go Atalia Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone. 15Ba ma zi Atalia ba ja ba nwoŋi ba vo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom. Ba ma pa o tɔge manchwoŋo ni mɛ sisei na tɔge da se zoore nabwoo kom to, ye ba daare ba go‑o jei sem konto ne.
16Wɛ kaanem tu Jehoyada ma pa se o de pɛ wom de nɔɔna bam maama gwoni ni de Baŋa Wɛ we, ba wó taa ye Baŋa Wɛ tete nɔɔna. 17Nɔɔna bam maama déem ma vo ba zo Baal jwoni diga kam ba yigi ka maama ba de tega ne, ba daare ba chochoge kaanem bimbina yam de jwoni kamwaro tem maama. Ko ta ná ye Baal kaanem tu Matan, ba jaane‑o bimbina yam takeiri ne mo ba go.
18Jehoyada ta ma kuri balo na ye kaanem tiina de Levi dwi tiina to se ba taa nii Baŋa Wɛ diga kam totoŋa yam baŋa ne, ne Pɛ David déem na pɔɔre ba totoŋa yam tei to. Banto ye se ba taa zwɛ vara ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ, ba daare ba taa leeni lei de wopwolo, ne Moses nia yam de David bera yam déem na ye tei to. 19O ta ma kwei nɔɔna o zege Baŋa Wɛ diga kam manchwo-peena yam ne, se ba taa cho se nɔɔna balo maama na wo kwɛ ba tete de chullu tem to yé zo ka wone.
20O laam ma tɔge de jar-keira dedɛɛra bam, de nakwa bam, de yiga tiina bam, ko ta woli de teo kom nɔn-bia bam maama, se ba vo ba ja pɛ Joasa ba ja ba nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone. Ba ma ja‑o ba vo ba tɔge ka ni delo na wo baŋa seeni to ba vo ba zo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom. Ba ma ja Joasa ba pa o jeini paare yituŋu kom baŋa ne. 21Nɔn-bia bam maama maa chaka de wopwolo. Ko kwaga ne teo kom maama ma ke ziim, ba na go Atalia to ŋwaane.

english_text:
King Joash of Judah
(2 Kings 12.1-16)
1Joash was only 7 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 40 years from Jerusalem. His mother Zibiah was from the town of Beersheba.
2While Jehoiada the priest was alive, Joash obeyed the Lord by doing right. 3Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
4Some time later, Joash decided it was time to repair the temple. 5He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.”
But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders. 6 So he sent for Jehoiada the high priest and asked, “Why didn't you send the Levites to collect the taxes? The Lord's servant Moses and the people agreed long ago that this tax would be collected and used to pay for the upkeep of the sacred tent. 7And now we need it to repair the temple because the sons of that evil woman Athaliah came in and wrecked it. They even used some of the sacred objects to worship the god Baal.”
8Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple. 9He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
10The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box. 11Each day, after the Levites took the box into the temple, the king's secretary and the high priest's assistant would dump out the money and count it. Then the empty box would be taken back outside.
This happened day after day, and soon a large amount of money was collected. 12Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
13These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new. 14They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple.
Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived. 15He died at the ripe old age of 130 years, 16and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple.
Joash Turns Away from the Lord
17After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted. 18The people of Judah soon stopped worshiping in the temple of the Lord God and started worshiping idols and the symbols of the goddess Asherah. These sinful things made the Lord God angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, 19but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
20 God's Spirit spoke to Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and Zechariah told everyone that God was saying: “Why are you disobeying me and my laws? This will only bring punishment! You have deserted me, so now I will desert you.”
21-22King Joash forgot that Zechariah's father had always been a loyal friend. So when the people of Judah plotted to kill Zechariah, Joash joined them and gave orders for them to stone him to death in the courtyard of the temple. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “I pray that the Lord will see this and punish all of you.”
Joash Is Killed
23In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus. 24The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
25-26Joash was severely wounded during the battle, and as soon as the Syrians left Judah, two of his officials, Zabad and Jehozabad, decided to revenge the death of Zechariah. They plotted and killed Joash while he was in bed, recovering from his wounds. Joash was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. 27The History of the Kings also tells more about the sons of Joash, what the prophets said about him, and how he repaired the temple. Amaziah son of Joash became king after his father's death.
translation_text:
Joasa na kwɛ Wɛ diga kam tei to
2 Pwa 12:1-16
1Joasa déem jege bena yarepɛ mo ye o di Judah teo paare dem. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare bena finna. O nu yere mo Zibia, o na nwoŋi Beeriseba to. 2Wɛ kaanem tu Jehoyada ta na wo o ŋwea wone maŋa kalo to, Joasa totoŋa su Baŋa Wɛ yi mo. 3Jehoyada ma kuri kaana balei o pa Joasa se o di o ma o ke o kaana. Ba de ma lo bia ded‑o, bakeiri de busankane.
4Ko na wora ko wora to, Joasa boboŋa ma ja se o fɔge o kwɛ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam. 5O ma la kaanem tiina bam, de Levi tiina bam o ke daane ye o ta de-ba o we, “Véi-na á tole Judah teene dem maama wone á jwoŋi bene dem wone lampwoo kom nɔɔna bam maama tei ne, se dé ma dé fɔge dé kwɛ Wɛ diga kam. Nam yé dáane-na de totoŋe dem.” Levi tiina bam nam wo ke ba yiga totoŋe dem wone.
6Pɛ wom ma da ko ŋwaane o toŋe o bwoŋi kaanem nakwe tu Jehoyada ye o bwei‑o o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo nmo wo nii ko baŋa ne se Levi tiina bam kaare ba vo Jerusalem de Judah teene dem maama wone ba jwoŋi lampwoo kolo na ye Wɛ ni-gwonim vwei dem ŋwaane to? Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses déem tiŋi ni dem konto mo o pa Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom ye ba de sɛ.”
7Puseŋ-nyem Atalia bia bam nam ya ŋɔge ba zo Wɛ diga kam wone mo ba chɔge-ka. Ba ta bere ba vere wonnu telo na ye wose Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane to mo ba ja ba nwoŋi ba ma ba zuli Baal jwona yam.
8Pɛ wom ma pa ni ye ba kwei dɛ ba mage dakaa ba daare ba zege-ka pwooni yiga ne, se ko maŋe de Baŋa Wɛ diga kam manchwo-peena yam. 9Ba ma toŋe kwora Jerusalem de Judah teene dem maama wone se nɔɔna bam ja lampwoo ba ba ba pa Baŋa Wɛ, ne Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses déem na pɛ Isarele tiina bam ke tei kagoa yuu ne to. 10Dedɛɛra bam de nɔɔna bam maama ma ja ba sabia ba ba Jerusalem de wopwolo. Ba ma kwei ba pɛɛra yam ba de dakaa kam wone pa ka ba ka su. 11Dɛ maama wone, Levi tiina bam ná kwei dakaa kam ba ja ba vo pɛ wom dedɛɛra bam tei, ye ba ná nɛ we sabia bam daga, pɛ wom tɔn-poponno wom, de kaanem nakwe tu zeinnu wom yeini ba lwo ka wo sabu kom mo ba tiŋi, ye ba jwoori ba ja dakaa kam ba vo ba zege ka ya na zege mɛ to. Ba yɔɔre ba ke konto mo dɛ maama pa ba ba ba la sabu zanzam. 12Pɛ wom de Jehoyada ma kwei sabu kom ba ke nɔɔna balo na wó taa nii Baŋa Wɛ diga kam totoŋa baŋa ne to jeŋa ne. Banto de ma beeri lɔra, de gwaro, ye ba ŋwe-ba se ba taa toŋa ba kwɛ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam. Ba déem ta beeri balo na yei luuru de channa totoŋa to mo se ba de taa kwɛ wonnu.
13Tontoŋena bam maa ye jawale-nyena, pa totoŋa yam yɔɔre ya vei yiga. Ba ma fɔge ba kwɛ Wɛ diga kam ba ti pa se ka tɔge chwoŋa ye ka tiini ka dana. 14Ba na toŋe ba ti konto to, ba ma ja sabu kolo ta na daare to ba vo ba pa Pɛ Joasa de Jehoyada. Ba de ma kwei-ko ba pa nɔɔna se ba ma ba ke sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno zwe de zela yadwonna Baŋa Wɛ diga totoŋa yam de zwɛɛm pɛɛra kaanem dem ŋwaane. Maŋa kalo Jehoyada ta na wo o ŋwea wone to mo nɔɔna déem yeini ba kwei zwɛɛm pɛɛra ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ o wara-jei sem ne.
15Jehoyada déem nam ya tiini o kwe mo se ko maŋe de bena bi de fintɔ ye o laam te. 16Ba ma ja‑o ba vo ba suli David teo Jerusalem ne mɛ ba na yeini ba suli pwa to. Ba ke konto o na toŋe wo-laaro Isarele teo kom ne o pa Wɛ, de Wɛ diga kam to ŋwaane mo.
Joasa puseŋa kikia yam
17Ko daare, Jehoyada toone kwaga ne, mo Judah teo dedɛɛra bam vei Joasa tei ba jɔɔne‑o. Ba na lwori ba nia daane to, pɛ wom ma sɛ se o ke ba boboŋa yam ne. 18Konto baŋa ne mo Judah tiina bam swei Wɛ diga kam swia. Ba ma da ba zuli Asera nyenyego dɛ, de jwona yadwonna, ba daare ba yage ba nabaara Wɛ wom zula. Ba na sage chwoŋa de ba wɛleera kikia yam konto to, Baŋa Wɛ bane ma zaŋe de Judah tiina bam, de Jerusalem tiina bam. 19De ko de, Baŋa Wɛ ta toŋe o sampwori mo se ba kaane nɔɔna bam se ba pipiri ba jwoori o tei. Nɔɔna bam ma ve se ba cheigi sampwori sem taane dem.
20 Baŋa Wɛ Jworo déem ma chu kaanem tu Jehoyada bu Zekaria baŋa ne. O ma zege nɔɔna bam yiga ne o ta o we, “Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Bɛŋwaane mo abam yeini á ve Baŋa Wɛ nia yam? Abam yɔɔre á beeri cham mo á pa á tete. Abam na nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne to ŋwaane, o de dole abam mo o yage.”
21Nɔɔna bam ma ke bana se ba go Zekaria. Pɛ Joasa ma pa ni pa ba dole‑o de kandwa ba go Baŋa Wɛ diga kam konkɔlɔ kom wone. 22Pɛ wom swei Jehoyada ya na ke‑o lanyerane tei to mo pa se o go o bu Zekaria. Zekaria na wora o to to, mo o taga o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó nii o na kolo á na jege á ke to se o yiri jene o pa-ne.”
23Bene dem konto maa na yɔɔre de wora de ti to, mo Siria tiina jar-keira tu ba kwaare jara de Joasa. Jara yam ma yi Jerusalem de Judah teene dem maama. Siria jar-keira bam ma yɔɔre ba go Judah yiga tiina bam maama, ye ba daare ba pɛ ba jejegero tem maama ba ja ba jwoori Damasika se ba ke-te ba pɛ wom jeŋa ne. 24Siria jar-keira bam déem seene ba ye fenfee yerane mo. De ko de, Baŋa Wɛ yage chwoŋa mo pa ba wane Joasa jar-keira kɔ-fɔrɔ kom ba di. Judah tiina bam déem na lɔge Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye ba nabaara Wɛ kwaga ne to ŋwaane mo o waare Joasa. 25Jara yam na ke ya ti ye Siria jar-keira bam maa viiri to, de Joasa tiini o na zonne mo. O tete dedɛɛra ma bwɛ daane se ba go‑o, o na go kaanem tu Jehoyada bu Zekaria to ŋwaane. Ba ma li‑o ba go ye o tigi o peiga jei ne. Joasa na tege to, ba ma suli‑o Jerusalem ne, ye ko dae yibeela yalo ba na yeini ba ke pwa ya wone to ne.
26Ko déem ye Zabadi wolo nu na ye Amon tiina bukɔ Simeafi to, de Jehozabadi wolo nu na ye Moaba tiina bukɔ Simirifa to mo ke bana ba vo ba go Joasa. 27Ko nam ná ye Joasa bia bam yera taane, de Wɛ sampwori sem na pworisi wonnu telo ko vo o tete seeni to, de o na fɔge o kwɛ Wɛ diga kam tei to memaŋa, te maama popone te tigi Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. Joasa bu Amazia ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.

english_text:
King Amaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 14.1-6)
1Amaziah was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem, the hometown of his mother Jehoaddin.
2Even though Amaziah obeyed the Lord by doing right, he refused to be completely faithful. 3For example, as soon as he had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father. 4 But the children of those officers were not killed; the Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished.
Edom Is Defeated
(2 Kings 14.7)
5Amaziah sent a message to the tribes of Judah and Benjamin and called together all the men who were 20 years old and older. Three hundred thousand men went to Jerusalem, all of them ready for battle and able to fight with spears and shields. Amaziah grouped these soldiers according to their clans and put them under the command of his army officers. 6Amaziah also paid about 3.4 tons of silver to hire 100,000 soldiers from Israel.
7One of God's prophets said, “Your Majesty, don't let these Israelite soldiers march into battle with you. The Lord has refused to help anyone from the northern kingdom of Israel, 8and so he will let your enemies defeat you, even if you fight hard. He is the one who brings both victory and defeat.”
9Amaziah replied, “What am I supposed to do about all the silver I paid those troops?”
“The Lord will give you back even more than you paid,” the prophet answered.
10Amaziah ordered the troops from Israel to go home, but when they left, they were furious with the people of Judah.
11After Amaziah got his courage back, he led his troops to Salt Valley, where he killed 10,000 Edomite soldiers in battle. 12He captured 10,000 more soldiers and dragged them to the top of a high cliff. Then he pushed them over the side, and they all were killed on the rocks below.
13Meanwhile, the Israelite troops that Amaziah had sent home, raided the towns in Judah between Samaria and Beth-Horon. They killed 3,000 people and carried off their possessions.
14After Amaziah had defeated the Edomite army, he returned to Jerusalem. He took with him the idols of the Edomite gods and set them up. Then he bowed down and offered them sacrifices. 15This made the Lord very angry, and he sent a prophet to ask Amaziah, “Why would you worship these foreign gods that couldn't even save their own people from your attack?”
16But before the prophet finished speaking, Amaziah interrupted and said, “You're not one of my advisors! Don't say another word, or I'll have you killed.”
The prophet stopped. But then he added, “First you sinned and now you've ignored my warning. It's clear that God has decided to punish you!”
Israel Defeats Judah
(2 Kings 14.8-14)
17King Amaziah of Judah talked with his officials, then sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
18Jehoash sent back a reply that said:
Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon arranged the marriage between his son and the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
19Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. But stay at home and do your celebrating. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
20God made Amaziah stubborn because he was planning to punish him for worshiping the Edomite gods. Amaziah refused to listen to Jehoash's warning, 21so Jehoash led his army to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops. 22During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home, 23and Jehoash captured Amaziah.
Jehoash took Amaziah with him when he went to attack Jerusalem. Jehoash broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly 200 meters long. 24He carried away the gold, the silver, and all the valuable furnishings from God's temple where the descendants of Obed-Edom stood guard. He robbed the king's treasury, took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
Amaziah Is Killed
(2 Kings 14.15-20)
25Amaziah lived 15 years after Jehoash died. 26Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
27As soon as Amaziah started disobeying the Lord, some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there. 28His body was taken to Jerusalem on horseback and buried beside his ancestors.
translation_text:
Judah teo pɛ Amazia taane
1Amazia déem jege bena finlei-yanu mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena finlei-nogo. O nu yere mo Jehoadin ye o nwoŋi Jerusalem. 2O totoŋa déem su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane, se ko nam dae de o wo maama mo o toŋe. 3O na yɔɔre o jeini paare dem baŋa ne to, o ma go nɔɔna balo déem na jaane o kwo ba go to. 4O nam wo pɛ ba go nɔn-gora bam konto bia bam. O déem sɛ ni delo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Moses to. Ni dem konto bere we, “Kwoa ba jege se ba te ba bia kikia ŋwaane. Bia de nam ba jege se ba te ba kwoa kikia ŋwaane. Nɔɔno ná maŋe se o te, ko wó taa ye o tete yuu lwarem ŋwaane mo.”
5Amazia déem ma la Judah dwi tiina de Benjamin dwi tiina bam. O ma pɔɔre-ba pa ba ye jar-keira kɔgɔ de kɔgɔ se ko tɔge ba sɔ-yuni tem na ye tei to. O ma pɔɔre-ba nɔɔna moro moro, de nɔɔna bi bi mo, ye o daare o kuri dedɛɛra se ba taa nii kɔgɔ maama baŋa ne. O ma jeeli balo na yi bena finlei ba daŋe ye ba yei jara keim to ni. Ba déem ye baara morro bia yatɔ (300,000) mo, ba na maŋe se ba zeeri chichwoa, de jara-keim nantane to. 6Amazia ta ma kwei lu-nyenno kilo morro tetɔ de bia yana (3,400) o ŋwe jar-keira morro bi (100,000) na nwoŋi Isarele laŋa kam to se ba ba ba woli o tete jar-keira bam wone.
7Wɛ sampwora kadwoŋi nam yɔɔre o ba o tei o ta ded‑o o we, “Pɛ, yé pa Isarele tiina jar-keira bam konto tɔge de nmo nɔɔna bam ba vo ba ke jara yam. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ dole Isarele tiina bam o yage mo. O yɔɔre o ve Efrayim dwi tiina bam maama mo. 8Nmo ná maŋe n vɔ pu-dɛa tei maama n vo n ke jara yam, nam lɔre we Wɛ wó pa n dona bam chwoŋa se ba wane‑m. Wonto mo jege dam se o pa nɔɔna di yiga jara wone, ye o ta wae o pa ba toe de.”
9Amazia ma bwei Wɛ sampwora kam o we, “Se ko ná ye lu-nyenno tem a na ŋwe Isarele jar-keira bam ŋwaane to, a nam wó ke tɛ mo?” Wɛ tontoŋeno wom ma leiri o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó wane o pa‑m nyɔɔre delo na tiini de dwoi konto to.”
10Amazia ma pa jar-keira balo na nwoŋi Efrayim laŋa kam ne ba ba to ni we, ba jwoori ba sam. Keim dem konto ma pa ba bane tiini de wiira de Judah tiina bam, ye ba jwoori ba viiri de ban-lom.
11Amazia ma yɔɔre o vɔ pu-dɛa o ja o jar-keira bam o vo Yɛ bwolo kom. Dáane mo o ke jara de Edom tiina, ye o go ba jar-keira morro fuga (10,000). 12Judah tiina bam ta wane ba zi Edom jar-keira morro fuga (10,000) badwonna ye ba ta ŋwe. Ba ma kale-ba ba ja ba di pe-dedɔrɔ yuu. Ba laam ma zege peo kom yuu ne ba yigi-ba ba de tega ne pa ba maama to ba te.
13Ko daare ko ná ye Isarele jar-keira balo Amazia na pɛ se ba jwoori ba sam pa ba wo tɔge ba ke jara yam to, banto vei ba li ba chɔge Judah teene dedwonna mo. Ba zege Samaria seeni mo ba chɔge teene dedɛ ba vo ba yi Bɛte-Horon. Ba ma go nɔɔna morro tetɔ (3,000) ye ba daare ba vere wonnu dedɛ ba ja ba viiri.
14Amazia na wane Edom tiina bam ye o maa jwoori Jerusalem to, o jaane ba jwona mo o woli da o ba. O déem ma chwi-ya o zege ye o tiiri ya yiga ne, o daare o ke kaanem o pa-ya. 15Baŋa Wɛ bane ma tiini de fuli Amazia baŋa ne. O ma toŋe o sampwora Amazia tei ne de kwora o bwei o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo nmo jege wa-yɔɔro tento n zula, ye ya maŋe ya wo wane ya tete nɔɔna ya jwoŋi n jeŋa ne ya yage?”
16Wɛ sampwora kam na jege taane dem o ŋɔɔne to, mo pɛ wom gwoni o zo taane dem wone o we, “Ei! Dé kuri nmo mo se n ta‑n tui pɛ wom yiga n bere‑o wonnu na? Nmo ná wo yage taane dem, a wó pa ba go‑m.” Wɛ sampwora kam ma seene o yage taane delo o ya na jege o ŋɔɔne to, ye o ta o we, “Amo nam lɔre jaja we Wɛ jaane boboŋa mo se o chɔge‑m n totoŋ-balɔrɔ kom ŋwaane. N ta ma ve se n cheigi a taane dem.”
17Dɛ dedwe mo Judah teo pɛ Amazia bane de o nɔɔna bam ye o daare o toŋe o tontoŋena se ba vo ba gware Isarele teo pɛ Jehoasa na ye Jehohaza bu ye o ta ye Jehu naa to. Amazia ma ta ded‑o we, “Ba n jeeri-ne se dé ke kayiŋu.” 18Pɛ Jehoasa ma jwoori o toŋe kwora o pa Judah teo pɛ Amazia o we, “Sabara kadwoŋi mo zege Lebanon ne ka toŋe kwora ka pa Sedare tei-zɔŋɔ Lebanon ne ka we, ‘Kwei n bukɔ wom n pa a bu se o di o ma o ke kaane.’ Konto nɛ sem ni ne mo ga-varem zege Lebanon ne ka nɔne sabara kam ka chɔge. 19Nmo bere n tete we, n wane n di Edom tiina bam mo pa se n cho n vɔna konto. Nam ya maŋe n sɔŋɔ ne se n jwoŋi zula. Bɛ mo ye n boŋe se n vaare lɛɛro n yage nmo tete yuu ne, de Judah tiina de yuu ne?”
20Amazia ma se o zwa de taane dem konto. Kokuri to, ko ye Wɛ boboŋa mo se o tɔge dáane o waare Amazia de o na lɛɛne o zuli Edom tiina jwona yam to. 21Ko kwaga ne Isarele teo pɛ Jehoasa ma la o jar-keira o ke daane ye ba vo Judah teo Bɛte-Semesa ba kwaare jara de Amazia. 22Isarele jar-keira bam ma wane ba di Amazia de o nɔɔna bam pa se ba maama duri ba jwoori ba sam. 23Pɛ Jehoasa ma zi Amazia Bɛte-Semesa ne. O ma ja‑o o vo Jerusalem. Dáane mo o bwori teo kom kabira kalo na zege Efrayim Ni dem ne se ka vo ka yi Gugworo Ni dem to. Ka laŋa kam déem ye naba-laara bia yalei mo. 24O ma vo o zo Wɛ diga kam o vere ka sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno wonnu maama, de ka lonne zela yalo Obed-Edom dwi dem na yere to. O ta ma pɛ jejegero telo na tigi pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne to. O ma ja te maama o jwoori Samaria. O ta ma ja teo kom nɔɔna o ja viiri se ko fe Judah teo pɛ se o sɛ o ni.
25Isarele teo pɛ Jehoasa toone dem kwaga seeni, Judah teo pɛ Amazia déem ta nɛ bena fuga-yanu mo ye o laam te. 26Amazia déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, ko zege o paare dem boboa ne se ko yi de na kweeli maŋa kalo to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah de Isarele Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 27Ko déem na zege maŋa kalo Amazia na mɛ o kwaga o ya Baŋa Wɛ to, Jerusalem dedɛɛra badwonna ke ni daane mo se ba go‑o. O ma duri o vo Lakisi. O dona bam ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba pare‑o. Ba ma yi‑o ba go Lakisi ne. 28Ba ma kwei Amazia yera yam ba daŋe sisein-nɔɔno baŋa ne ba ja ba jwoori Jerusalem. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa bam yibeeli ne.

english_text:
King Uzziah of Judah
(2 Kings 14.21,22; 15.1-7)
1-3After the death of King Amaziah, the people of Judah crowned his son Uzziah king, even though he was only 16 at the time. Uzziah ruled 52 years from Jerusalem, the hometown of his mother Jecoliah. During his rule, he recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath.
4He obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done. 5Zechariah was Uzziah's advisor and taught him to obey God. And so, as long as Zechariah was alive, Uzziah was faithful to God, and God made him successful.
6While Uzziah was king, he started a war against the Philistines. He smashed the walls of the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, then rebuilt towns around Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia. 7God helped him defeat the Philistines, the Arabs living in Gur-Baal, and the Meunites. 8Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
9In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward. 10He also built defense towers out in the desert.
He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
11Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials. 12-13There were 307,500 trained soldiers, all under the command of 2,600 clan leaders. These powerful troops protected the king against any enemy. 14Uzziah supplied his army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones used for slinging. 15Some of his skilled workers invented machines that could shoot arrows and sling large stones. Uzziah set these up in Jerusalem at his defense towers and at the corners of the city wall.
God helped Uzziah become more and more powerful, and he was famous all over the world.
Uzziah Becomes Too Proud
16Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall.
One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him. 17Azariah the priest and 80 other brave priests followed Uzziah into the temple 18 and said, “Your Majesty, this isn't right! You are not allowed to burn incense to the Lord. That must be done only by priests who are descendants of Aaron. You will have to leave! You have sinned against the Lord, and so he will no longer bless you.”
19Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead! 20Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
21Uzziah had leprosy the rest of his life. He was no longer allowed in the temple or in his own palace. That's why his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
22Everything else Uzziah did while he was king is in the records written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. 23 Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_text:
Judah teo pɛ Yuzia taane
2 Pwa 15:1-7
1Judah tiina bam maama ma kuri Yuzia se o leiri o kwo Amazia yuu ne o ji pɛ, de o na jege bena fuga-yaredo to de. 2Yuzia kwo toone kwaga ne, o déem ma jwoori o jwoŋi Elofe teo kom o woli Judah kateiri dem wone, ye o fɔge o lɔ-ko.
3Yuzia déem jege bena fuga-yaredo mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena finnu-yalei. O nu wom yere mo Jekolia ye o nwoŋi Jerusalem. 4O totoŋa déem su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane, nenɛɛne o kwo Amazia na ke tei to. 5Zekaria déem mo yeini o bere‑o Wɛ chwoŋa na ye tei to. Zekaria ta na ŋwe to, Yuzia yɔɔre o zuli Baŋa Wɛ mo. O maa na zuli Wɛ konto to, Wɛ de pɛ o wonnu ke lanyerane mo te pa‑o.
6Yuzia ma vo o kwaare jara de Filisi tiina bam. O ma vo o li Gafa, de Jabenɛ, de Asedodi teene dem o yigi de kabiri sem o de tega ne. O laam ma lɔ teene pa de bwola de Asedodi, dedaane Filisi tiina bam na zoore jei sedaara ne to. 7Wɛ ma woli‑o pa se o wane Filisi tiina, de Meyunim tiina, de Arabi tiina balo na zoore Guri-Baal seeni to maama. 8Amon tiina bam de maa jaane pɛɛra ba tui ba pae Yuzia se ba sɛ ba pa‑o. O yere déem tiini de zaŋe jei maama ne se ko vo ko yi Ejipti teo siseini, o na tiini o jege dam to ŋwaane.
9Yuzia déem lɔge di-dedwaaro Jerusalem teo kabira kam ne mo o zege pa teo kom dana. O ke konto Gugworo Ni dem teiŋa ne, de Bwolo Ni dem teiŋa ne, dedaane mɛ seeni kabira kam na gugwoli to ne. 10O ta ma pa ba lɔ di-dedwaaro ba zege kagoa kam ne, ye ba daare ba ko vola dedɛ, o na jege vara dedɛ wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne, de te-kampare jei sem ne to ŋwaane. Zwonnu laŋa kam ne, de te-ywoŋa jei sem ne o tontoŋena maa vare tega kam ba pa‑o ye ba jeiri Vini teeni, o na swoi varem de kɔnɔ totoŋa to ŋwaane.
11Yuzia déem ta jege jar-keira balo na yei jara keim laŋa chekke to. Ba maa ye siri se ba nwoŋi kɔgɔ de kɔgɔ ba ke jara. Tɔn-poponno Jeyeli de o kwaga nɔɔno Maaseya mo yeini ba tigisi-ba ba ke daane ne ba na jeeli ba ni dem se ko maŋe tei to. Pɛ sɔŋɔ dedɛɛro Hanania déem nii jar-keira kɔgɔ kom maama baŋa ne mo. 12Sɔ-yuni yiga tiina balo na tei jar-keira bam kɔgɔ de kɔgɔ to déem ye nɔɔna morro telei de bia yaredo (2,600) mo. 13Ba nam na jege nɔɔna balo ba nii to maama ye jar-keira morro bia yatɔ de yarepɛ dedaane bia yanu (307,500) mo. Banto maama yɔɔre ba yei jara-keim laŋa chekke, pa se ba wae ba cho pɛ wom se o dona yé wane‑o. 14Yuzia ma kwei jara-keim nantane, de chichwoa, de yu-gwonnu, de jara-keim gwaaro, de tɛ, de napana kandwa o pa-ba. 15O ma pa o tontoŋena badwonna ke wonnu telo na wae te tae chena, ye te dole kandwa-zana te yaga ba dona baŋa ne to. O ma zege wonnu tem konto Jerusalem kabira di-dedwaaro tem ne, de kabira gugworru tem ne. Yuzia yere dem déem tiini de zaŋe jei maama ne, Wɛ na tiini o zeini‑o pa o na dam dedɛ to ŋwaane.
16O nam na tu o na dam to, mo o bere o tete kamunim. Konto nam mo yɔɔre ko pa o to tega ne. Dɛ dedwe, o ma tusi o chɔge o Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga ye o zo Wɛ diga kam wone se o zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa ka bimbini dem baŋa ne. 17Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tu Azaria ma tɔge de kaanem tiina funɔnɔ ba na jege pu-dɛa to, pa ba zo o tei. 18Ba ma yɔɔre ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Pɛ Yuzia, ko dae ko chwoŋa ne se n zo ywo n zwɛ talwoŋa n pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ko ye Aron dwi dem mo Baŋa Wɛ pɔɔre o zege se ba taa ye kaanem tiina ba zwɛ talwoŋa kam ba pa‑o. Nwoŋi da o diga kanto ne. Nmo sage chwoŋa mo, pa Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ daa bá ke‑m lanyerane.”
19Yuzia nam ya zei min-chala zoŋa mo o ti o yiga se o zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa kam. O bane ma zaŋe. O ma zege Baŋa Wɛ diga talwoŋa zwɛɛm bimbini dem yiga ne o bage kaanem tiina bam. O na jege-ba o bage to, mo naywaane jaweo kom bobo ko zaŋe o tiri seeni. 20Kaanem nakwe Azaria de kaanem tiina badaara bam ma maane we naywaane mo to pɛ wom yera ne. Ba na nɛ konto to, ba ma zeili‑o pa o nwoŋi lela. O tete de ma ke lela se o nwoŋi da, Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ se lɛɛro yi‑o to ŋwaane.
21Naywaane jaweo kom déem wo yage Yuzia yera kɔtaa. O dɛ de jaweo kom konto mo o vo o te. O déem zoore sɔŋɔ kolo na ye dáa dáa to wone mo, jawe-chɛɔ na wae ko lɔgese nɔɔna to na jege‑o to ŋwaane. O maa ba jege chwoŋa se o zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ne. O bu Jotam ma leiri o nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom de teo kom nɔn-bia baŋa ne o pa‑o.
22Yuzia déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, ko zege o paare dem boboa ne se ko yi de na kweeli maŋa kalo to, mo Wɛ sampwora Izaya na ye Amozi bu to popone-te o tiŋi. 23Yuzia ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli pwola kalo na ye pwa bam nyem to wone. Ba nam wo ke‑o o kwoa yibeeli wone, kokuri to, ba déem tage mo ba we, “Naywaane jaweo kom mo jege‑o.” O bu Jotam ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.

english_text:
King Jotham of Judah
(2 Kings 15.32-38)
1Jotham was 25 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years. Jerushah his mother was the daughter of Zadok.
2Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
3Jotham rebuilt the Upper Gate of the temple and did a lot of work to repair the wall near Mount Ophel. 4He built towns in the mountains of Judah and built fortresses and defense towers in the forests.
5During his rule he attacked and defeated the Ammonites. Then every year for the next three years, he forced them to pay 3.4 tons of silver, 1,000 tons of wheat, and 1,000 tons of barley.
6Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
7Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah. 8After he had ruled Judah 16 years, he died at the age of 41. 9He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_text:
Judah teo pɛ Jotam taane
1Jotam déem jege bena finlei-yanu mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem bena fuga-yaredo. O nu wom déem mo ye Zadoki bukɔ Jerusa. 2O totoŋa ma su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane, nenɛɛne o kwo Yuzia déem na ke tei to. O nam wo zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam o chɔge ka chullu tem ne o kwo déem na ke tei to. Nɔɔna bam maa ke totoŋ-zɔɔna ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. 3Jotam ma fɔge o lɔ Wɛ wara-jei sem ni delo na wo baŋa seeni to, ye o ta tiini o kwɛ teo kom kabira kalo na bwola de Ofeli peo kom to. 4O déem ta lɔge teene mo Judah zwonnu laŋa kam ne o zege, ye o daare o lɔ dam jei dedɛ o yage kagwe sem jei ne.
5Jotam déem vei o ke jara de Amon tiina pɛ de o nɔɔna mo ye o di-ba. O déem ma kwei bena yatɔ o fe Amon tiina bam pa bene maama wone ba jege se ba taa jaane lu-nyenno kilo morro tetɔ de bia yana (3,400), de banina ywollu morro fintɔ (30,000), de chaara ywollu morro fintɔ (30,000) ba tui ba pa‑o.
6Jotam déem tiini o na dam mo, o na seene o yia o tɔge o Tu Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa yam to ŋwaane. 7Jotam déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o na kwaare jara de teene delo to, ko woli de chwei selo o na tɔge to maama, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele de Judah Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 8Jotam déem jege bena finlei-yanu mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem bena fuga-yaredo. 9Jotam ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli David teo Jerusalem ne. O bu Ahaz ma leiri o di paare.

english_text:
King Ahaz of Judah
(2 Kings 16.1-4)
1Ahaz was 20 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years.
Ahaz was nothing like his ancestor David. Ahaz disobeyed the Lord 2and was as sinful as the kings of Israel. He made idols of the god Baal, 3and he offered sacrifices in Hinnom Valley. Worst of all, Ahaz sacrificed his own sons, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 4Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
Syria and Israel Attack Judah
(2 Kings 16.5,6)
5-6 Ahaz and the people of Judah sinned and turned away from the Lord, the God their ancestors had worshiped. So the Lord punished them by letting their enemies defeat them.
The king of Syria attacked Judah and took many of its people to Damascus as prisoners. King Pekah of Israel later defeated Judah and killed 120,000 of its bravest soldiers in one day. 7During that battle, an Israelite soldier named Zichri killed three men from Judah: Maaseiah the king's son; Azrikam, the official in charge of the palace; and Elkanah, the king's second in command. 8The Israelite troops captured 200,000 women and children and took them back to their capital city of Samaria, along with a large amount of their possessions. They did these things even though the people of Judah were their own relatives.
Oded the Prophet Condemns Israel
9Oded lived in Samaria and was one of the Lord's prophets. He met Israel's army on their way back from Judah and said to them:
The Lord God of your ancestors let you defeat Judah's army only because he was angry with them. But you should not have been so cruel! 10If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
11Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
12About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong, 13and they said:
If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
14So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah. 15The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria.
Ahaz Asks the King of Assyria for Help
(2 Kings 16.7-9)
16-18Some time later, the Edomites attacked the eastern part of Judah again and carried away prisoners. And at the same time, the Philistines raided towns in the western foothills and in the Southern Desert. They conquered the towns of Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, including the villages around them. Then some of the Philistines went to live in these places.
Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria and begged for help. 19But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning. 20So Tiglath Pileser came to Judah, but instead of helping, he made things worse. 21Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz.
The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
22Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before. 23He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
24Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem. 25In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
26Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 27 Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_text:
Judah teo pɛ Ahaz taane
1Ahaz déem jege bena finlei mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena fuga-yaredo. O nam wo toŋe o pwoli Baŋa Wɛ wo, nenɛɛne o nabaaro David na ke tei to. 2-3O déem tusi de o na kwei Isarele teo pwa bam totoŋ-naga to mo. O ma mɔ kamwaro o lwoni Baal jwona yam o zege, ye o daare o ke kaanem Ben-Hinom bwolo kom ne. O ma zwɛ o tete bia o ma o ke kaanem o pa jwona yam. O keim dem konto bere we o lwoni totoŋ-zɔɔna yalo dwi-gɛ tiina bam na ke ye Wɛ zeili-ba tega kam ne o daare o pa Isarele tiina bam jeini to mo. 4Ko ná ye wara-jei sem ne, de zwonnu tem baŋa ne, de teeni maama kuri ne, o déem yeini o ke kaanem de zwɛɛm pɛɛra mo jei sem konto maama ne.
5 Baŋa Wɛ ma da ko ŋwaane o pa o to Siria teo pɛ dam kuri ne. Siria tiina bam ma wane‑o jara wone. Ba ma kale o nɔɔna bam dedɛ ba ja ba vo Damasika pa ba ji peena da.
Konto kwaga ne, Wɛ ta pɛ Isarele teo pɛ mo na chwoŋa o wane Ahaz de o nɔɔna bam, pa ko zo ba yera lanyerane. 6Remalia bu Peka ma zaŋe o go Judah bembɛ morro bi de finlei (120,000) dɛ dedwe wone. Ko ye Judah tiina bam na mɛ ba kwaga ba ya Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye ba nabaara Wɛ to ŋwaane mo lɛɛro tento maama yi-ba. 7Efrayim tu Zikiri na yɔɔre o ye babea to ma go Judah pɛ wom bu Maaseya, de Azerikam wolo na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne to, de Elikana wolo wom dam na saŋe pɛ wom kwaga to. 8Isarele tiina bam ta fe ba chorro Judah tiina kaana de ba bia morro bia yalei (200,000) mo ba kale ba ja ba vo Samaria. Ba déem ta ma vere ba jejegero dedɛ ba woli da ba zeŋe ba viiri.
9Wɛ sampwora déem mo wora, o yere mo Odeda. O maa zoore Samaria teo kom wone. Isarele jar-keira bam na jwoori ba maa zoore Samaria teo to, mo o nwoŋi se o jeeri-ba. O ma ta de-ba o we:
“Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye á nabaara Wɛ to bane na zaŋe de Judah tiina bam to ŋwaane mo o pɛ abam na chwoŋa á wane-ba. Abam nam tiini á go-ba ye ŋwaŋa tera, pa ko yɔɔre ko daane‑o. 10Abam laam na boŋe se á pa ba baara bam de ba kaana bam ji á kabɛ konto to, á wo lɔre we abam de tete ke wɛleera á chɔge á Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga mo na? 11Nam cheigi-na a taane dem, se á pa ba jwoori ba teo. Ba ye abam tete chorro mo. Á ná ve se á ke konto, Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom wó to á baŋa ne mo.”
12Efrayim teo dedɛɛra bam bana de déem ma zaŋe ba vo ba bwɛ jar-keira balo na nwoŋi jara yam wone ba jwoori ba ba to. Banto maa ye Jehohanan bu Azaria mo, de Mesilemofa bu Berekia, de Salum bu Jehizekia, de Hadelayi bu Amasa. 13Ba ma ta ba we, “Yé ja-na peena bam konto á zo Samaria teo wo. Dé na maŋe dé ke wɛleera yalo to pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe debam Isarele tiina baŋa ne mo. Yé pa-na se wɛleera yadwonna taa wo debam yuu ne ya woli da.”
14Jar-keira bam ma lɛɛre ba zege dedɛɛra bam de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom yiga ne ba kwei peena bam de jejegero telo ba na vere to ba yage. 15Dedɛɛra bana bam ma bwoli peena bam ba daare ba le gwaaro jejegero tem wone ba ma ba kwoli peena balo na zege da kalambwolo to. Ba ta ma kwei gwaaro, de natera, de wodiiru ba pa peena bam maama, ye ba daare ba kwei nuga ba ma ba lɛ ba fufwollu. Peena balo ta na bwomma to, ba ma kwei-ba ba daŋe bonɛ baŋa ne. Ba laam ma ja peena bam ba jwoori ba dwi tiina tei Jeriko ne, teo kolo ba na bwoi we ‘Konkware teo kom’ to. Dedɛɛra bam laam ma jwoori Samaria.
16Pɛ Ahaz ma toŋe o tontoŋena se ba vo Asiria teo pɛ tei ba lwoori‑o se o toŋe jar-keira se ba ba ba woli‑o. 17Kokuri to, Edom tiina bam ya daa tu ba kwaare jara de Judah tiina bam mo ba di-ba, ye ba daare ba zi nɔɔna ba ja ba viiri. 18Filisi tiina bam de ma vo Judah wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem, de kagoa kalo na wo tega-kuri seeni to ba li teene dedwonna da. Teene delo ba na vere to maa ye Bɛte-Semesa, de Ayijalon, de Gederofa, de Sokoo, de Timina, de Gimizo, dedaane de nawuura yam maama. Ba ma lɛɛre ba zoore de wone. 19Baŋa Wɛ nam yɔɔre o pa Judah dwi tiina bam tu tega mo Pɛ Ahaz kikia yam ŋwaane. Kokuri to, wonto mo pɛ chwoŋa se wɛleere puli Judah teo kom maama ne, ye o wo ke o chega dedaane Baŋa Wɛ. 20Asiria teo pɛ Tigilaf-Pilesa ma ba Ahaz tei. O nam wo tu se o woli‑o. O ma jwoori o pa ko tiini ko chɛ Ahaz yera. 21Ahaz ta ma kwei lonne wonnu telo na wo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ne to dedaane telo na wo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wone, de teo kom nakwa sam dem ne to o toŋe o pa Asiria pɛ wom. Konto nam ta wo wane‑o ko zeini.
22Cham na tu Pɛ Ahaz baŋa konto to, o yɔɔre o toŋe o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga se ko dwoni o ya na ke tei to mo. 23O ke kaanem mo o pa Siria teo Damasika jwona yam, o na boŋe we ya jege dam ya pa Siria tiina se ba wane‑o ba di to ŋwaane. O ya boŋe o tete ne mo we, “Ko ye Siria tiina jwona yam mo woli-ba. Amo de nam wó zuli-ya mo se ya zeini-ne.” O keim dem konto nam pɛ se lɛɛro ba o baŋa, dedaane o teo kom maama baŋa mo.
24Ahaz déem ta zo Wɛ diga kam wone mo o la ka zela yam o ja o nwoŋi. O ma chochoge-ya o yage. O ma fɔge o pe Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ni, ye o daare o chwi kaanem bimbina Jerusalem teo ni maama ne. 25Judah teene dem maama wone de, o ta lɔge wara-jei bimbina mo, se ba taa vei da ba kaane wa-yɔɔro. Kikia yam konto ŋwaane o ma chiŋi Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye o nabaara Wɛ to bane o yage.
26Ahaz déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo to, de o totoŋa yam maama, ko zege o paare dem boboa ne se ko yi de na kweeli maŋa kalo to, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah de Isarele Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. 27Ahaz ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli Jerusalem teo wone, se ko za dae pwa yibeela yam wone mo ba suli‑o. O bu Hezekia ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.

english_text:
King Hezekiah of Judah
(2 Kings 18.1-3)
1Hezekiah was 25 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem. His mother was Abijah daughter of Zechariah. 2Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done.
The Temple Is Purified
3In the first month of the first year of Hezekiah's rule, he unlocked the doors to the Lord's temple and had them repaired. 4Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple 5and said:
It's time to purify the temple of the Lord God of our ancestors. You Levites must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean, then go into the temple and bring out everything that is unclean and unacceptable to the Lord. 6Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple. 7They locked the doors, then let the lamps go out and stopped burning incense and offering sacrifices to him. 8The Lord became terribly angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and everyone was shocked and horrified at what he did to punish them. Not only were 9our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
10So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us. 11Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
12-14When Hezekiah finished talking, the following Levite leaders went to work:
Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the Kohath clan; Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel from the Merari clan; Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah from the Gershon clan; Shimri and Jeuel from the Elizaphan clan; Zechariah and Mattaniah from the Asaph clan; Jehuel and Shimei from the Heman clan; Shemaiah and Uzziel from the Jeduthun clan.
15These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.
16The priests went into the temple and carried out everything that was unclean. They put these things in the courtyard, and from there, the Levites carried them outside the city to Kidron Valley.
17The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month 18they went back to Hezekiah and said:
Your Majesty, we have finished our work. The entire temple is now pure again, and so is the altar and its utensils, as well as the table for the sacred loaves of bread and its utensils. 19And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar.
Worship in the Temple
20At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple. 21They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
22The priests killed the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, then splattered the blood on the altar. 23They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals. 24The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
25Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan. 26 The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
27As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments, 28and everyone worshiped the Lord. This continued until the last animal was sacrificed.
29After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord. 30Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.
31Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.”
The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices. 32Seventy bulls, 100 rams, and 200 lambs were brought as sacrifices to please the Lord; 33600 bulls and 3,000 sheep were brought as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing. 34There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned. 35Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar.
So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord. 36Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
translation_text:
Pɛ Hezekia na kwɛ Wɛ diga kam tei to
1Hezekia déem jege bena finlei-yanu mo ye ba tiŋi‑o paare. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena finlei-nogo. O nu wom déem ye Zekaria bukɔ Abija mo. 2O totoŋa ma su Baŋa Wɛ yi lanyerane, nenɛɛne o nabaaro David déem na ke tei to.
3Bene delo wone Hezekia na jigi pɛ to boboa chana kam wone mo o jwoori o pore Baŋa Wɛ diga kam nia yam. O ma pa ba fɔge ba kwɛ bworru tem ba zege. 4O ma bwoŋi Wɛ kaanem tiina bam, de Levi dwi tiina bam o ke daane se ba jeeri Wɛ diga kam konkɔlɔ kolo na yɔɔre wɛ-puli seeni to. 5O laam ma ta de-ba o we:
“Abam Levi tiina bam, cheigi-na a taane dento! Kwɛ-na á tete se á maŋe de chullu tem, se á ta daare á fɔge á kwɛ Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye á nabaara Wɛ to diga kam. Le-na wonnu telo maama na wora ye te pae ka jege digiru to ka wone. 6Debam kwoa bam nam wo jaane chega de dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Ba ma ve‑o, pa se ba toŋe lwarem ba ma ba chɔge o yiga. Ba déem mɛ ba kwaga ba ya Baŋa Wɛ de o wara-jei sem maama mo. 7Ba ma yɔɔre ba pe Wɛ diga napɔrɔ kom nia yam, ye ba yage pa min-zwonnu tem dwei. Ba ma ve se ba zwɛ talwoŋa, naa se ba ke zwɛɛm kaanem Isarele tiina Wɛ wom wara-jei sem ne. 8Ko ma pa se Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom dem to Jerusalem de Judah teo kom maama baŋa ne. O na ke tei o ma o waare-ba to ma so nɔɔna maama pa foone jege-ba, ye ba ta jege Judah tiina bam ba yaala, ne abam na nɛa ko na ye tei tento to. 9Konto ŋwaane mo debam dona go dé kwoa bam jara wone, ye ba daare ba pɛ dé bia de dé kaana ba ja ba viiri. 10Amo boboŋa nam jaane se dé jwoori dé ke ni-sɛɛm mo de Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to. Konto mo wó che se o ban-lom daa yé taa wo debam baŋa ne. 11Konto ŋwaane, a bia bam, daa yé ja-na á jeini. Kokuri to, abam mo Baŋa Wɛ kuri se á ta‑á zege o yiga ne á toŋa ye á kaane á pa‑o.”
12Levi tiina banto ma zaŋe ba nwoŋi se ba toŋe.
Kohafe sɔ-yuu nɔɔna bam wone:
Amasayi bu Mahafe, de Azaria bu Joweli.
Merari sɔ-yuu nɔɔna bam wone:
Abidi bu Kisi, de Jehaleli bu Azaria.
Gereson sɔ-yuu nɔɔna bam wone:
Zimma bu Joa, de Joa bu Eden.
13Elizafan dwi dem wone:
Simiri, de Jeyeli.
Asaf dwi dem wone:
Zekaria, de Matania.
14Heman dwi dem wone:
Jeheli, de Simeyi.
Jedutuna dwi dem wone:
Semaya, de Yuzeli.
15Nɔɔna bam konto de ma vo ba la ba chorro tem ba ke daane. Ba maama ma vo ba kwɛ ba tete de chullu tem, ye ba daare ba fɔge ba kwɛ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam, se ba pa ka maŋe de o chullu tem na bere tei to, nenɛɛne Pɛ Hezekia na pɛ-ba ni se ba ke tei to. 16Kaanem tiina bam ma zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam tete wo se ba kwɛ-ka. Ba ma zeŋe wonnu telo maama ba déem na nɛ ka wone ye te biini-ka to ba ja ba nwoŋi pwooni ba vo ba zege Wɛ diga kam konkɔlɔ kom wone. Levi tiina bam de ma zeŋe-te ba ja ba nwoŋi teo kom dáa dáa, ye ba dole-te ba yage Kidoron bwolo kom ne. 17Ba déem bobo ba kwɛɛm totoŋa yam konto boboa chana kam boboa dɛ dem ne mo. Ba na toŋe ba ke da nana to, de ba kwɛ pwooni yiga jei sem ba vo ba yi Baŋa Wɛ diga napɔrɔ kom. Ba daa ma kwei da nana ba kwɛ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam tete ba woli da. Ko ye boboa chana kam da fuga-yaredo dɛ dem ne mo ba déem kwɛ Wɛ diga kam maama ba ti.
18Ba ma vo Pɛ Hezekia tei ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Debam wane Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem maama dé kwɛ dé ti. Ko ná ye zwɛɛm pɛɛre bimbini dem de de yera zela yam maama, ko woli de tabolo kolo ba na yeini ba tiŋi bworobworo ko baŋa ne Wɛ ŋwaane to de ko yera wonnu tem maama, dé fɔge dé kwɛ te maama mo. 19Ko ta ná ye wonnu telo Pɛ Ahaz na yage o chega de Wɛ ye o le-te Wɛ diga kam wone o paare dim maŋa ne to, dé ta beeri tento maama dé na, ye dé daare dé kwɛ-te chullu tem seeni. Leile konto te maama laam zege Baŋa Wɛ bimbini dem yiga ne.”
20Tega na poore tetete to, Hezekia ma la teo kom dedɛɛra bam o ke daane ye ba vo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam. 21Ba maa jege pɛɛra se ba ma ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem pɛ sɔŋɔ kom tiina ŋwaane, de Wɛ wara-jei sem ŋwaane, de Judah tiina bam maama ŋwaane. Ba pɛɛra yam déem ye na-bale serepɛ, de pi-bale serepɛ, de pipeili serepɛ, de bo-bale serepɛ mo. Pɛ wom ma pa kaanem tiina bam na ye Aron dwi dem to ni se ba kwei vara bam ba ma ba ke kaanem Baŋa Wɛ bimbini dem baŋa ne. 22Kaanem tiina bam ma go na-bale sem ba ma ba ke kaanem, ye ba daare ba kwei se jana bam ba miisi ba yage bimbini dem yera ne. Ba ta ke konto dwoŋi mo de pi-bale sem, de pipeili sem de. 23Ko ná ye bone delo na wora wɛleere saarem ŋwaane to, ba jaane-de ba nwoŋi Pɛ Hezekia de kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama yiga ne mo. Ba de ma kwei ba je ba daŋe bone dem baŋa ne. 24Kaanem tiina bam laam ma go-de, ye ba daare ba kwei de jana bam ba lwo bimbini dem baŋa ne se ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem ba ma ba le Isarele tiina bam maama lwarem Wɛ yiga ne. Kokuri to, Pɛ wom ya pɛ ni mo se ba ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de wɛleere saarem pɛɛra Isarele tiina bam maama ŋwaane.
25Hezekia laam ma kwei Levi tiina o zege ba zega jei ne Wɛ diga kam wone. O ma pa-ba zwe, de kwanno, de kwɛɛra zela dwi dwi, ne Pɛ David, de Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu Gad, de o sampwora Natan déem na bere we ba taa ke tei to. Baŋa Wɛ déem tɔge o sampwori sem baŋa mo o pa-ba o ni dem konto. 26Levi tiina bam ma yɔɔre ba ke siri de David kwɛɛra zela yam, ye kaanem tiina bam de zege de ba nabwanno se ba wu-te.
27Hezekia déem ma pa ni se ba ke zwɛɛm kaanem Wɛ diga kam bimbini dem baŋa ne. Ba na wora ba ke kaanem dem to, nɔɔna bam maa leeni lei, ye ba jege Isarele teo Pɛ David kwɛɛra zela yam, dedaane nabwanno tem ba ma ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. 28Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama ma tiiri ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ, ye lein-leena bam de leeni ba lei sem, ye nɔɔna de wui ba nabwanno tem. Ba yɔɔre ba ke konto mo taa se zwɛɛm kaanem dem maama vo de ti.
29Ba na ke kaanem dem ba ti to mo Pɛ Hezekia de o kwaga nɔɔna bam maama tiiri tega ne ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. 30Pɛ wom de o nakwa bam ma ta de Levi tiina bam se ba kwei seinim lei selo David de Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu Asaf déem na puli to ba ma ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Ba maama ma seene ba leeni lei sem de ywoni zanzam ye ba tiiri tega ne ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ.
31Hezekia ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam laam na seene á kwɛ á tete Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to ŋwaane, nam ja-na kaanem de lei-keim pɛɛra á ba á zo Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne.” Ba ma seene ba ke konto. Ba badaara ta ma ja zwɛɛm pɛɛra ba woli da, se ko tɔge de ba boboŋa na jaane tei to.
32Nɔɔna bam déem jaane nabɛ fuserepɛ (70) mo, de pi-bale bi (100), de pipeili bia yalei (200) mo ba ma ba ke zwɛɛm kaanem dem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. 33Ba ta ma ja naane bia yaredo (600), de pei morro tetɔ (3,000) se ba kwei-te ba ke Wɛ jeŋa ne. 34Kaanem tiina bam kɔgɔ ni déem nam ya muri se ba wane vara bam konto maama ba pwoni ba daare ba zwɛ. Mo kokuri ba chorro Levi dwi tiina bam woli-ba pa ba toŋe totoŋe dem ba vo ba guri, ye ko maŋe de kaanem tiina badwonna de laam kwɛ ba tete pa ba maŋe de chullu tem. Kokuri to, Levi tiina bam boboŋa déem jaane se ba kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane, se ko dwoni kaanem tiina bam na ke tei to. 35Vara balo nɔɔna bam na jaane ba ba se ba ke zwɛɛm kaanem to déem daga dedɛ. Ba ta maa jege lara kalo na ye yazura pɛɛra yam nyem to, dedaane wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛra yalo na woli zwɛɛm pɛɛra yam wone to.
Konto baŋa ne mo ba déem daa jwoori ba bobo ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ o diga kam wone. 36Hezekia de nɔɔna bam maama ma di ywoni de Wɛ na ke kolo o pa o nɔɔna bam to. Kokuri to, ba totoŋa yam maama yɔɔre ya ti lela mo.

english_text:
Hezekiah Prepares To Celebrate Passover
1-4 Passover wasn't celebrated in the first month, which was the usual time, because many of the priests were still unclean and unacceptable to serve, and because not everyone in Judah had come to Jerusalem for the festival. So Hezekiah, his officials, and the people agreed to celebrate Passover in the second month.
Hezekiah sent a message to everyone in Israel and Judah, including those in the territories of Ephraim and West Manasseh, inviting them to the temple in Jerusalem for the celebration of Passover in honor of the Lord God of Israel. 5Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
6Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter:
People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. If you do this, he will stop being angry. 7Don't follow the example of your ancestors and your Israelite relatives in the north. They were unfaithful to the Lord, and he punished them horribly. 8Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry, 9and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
10The messengers went to every town in Ephraim and West Manasseh as far north as the territory of Zebulun, but people laughed and insulted them. 11Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem. 12God also made everyone in Judah eager to do what Hezekiah and his officials had commanded.
Passover Is Celebrated
13In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread. 14They took all the foreign altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and threw them into Kidron Valley.
15-17Then, on the fourteenth day of that same month, the Levites began killing the lambs for Passover, because many of the worshipers were unclean and were not allowed to kill their own lambs. Meanwhile, some of the priests and Levites felt ashamed because they had not gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean. They immediately went through that ceremony and went to the temple, where they offered sacrifices to please the Lord. Then the priests and Levites took their positions, according to the Law of Moses, the servant of God.
As the Levites killed the lambs, they handed some of the blood to the priests, who splattered it on the altar.
18-19Most of the people that came from Ephraim, West Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not made themselves clean, but they ignored God's Law and ate the Passover lambs anyway. Hezekiah found out what they had done and prayed, “Lord God, these people are unclean according to the laws of holiness. But they are worshiping you, just as their ancestors did. So, please be kind and forgive them.” 20The Lord answered Hezekiah's prayer and did not punish them.
21The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments. 22Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration.
The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors. 23Everyone was so excited that they agreed to celebrate seven more days.
24So Hezekiah gave the people 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep to be offered as sacrifices and to be used as food for the sacred meals. His officials gave 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep, and many more priests agreed to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. 25Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel. 26It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David. 27The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
translation_text:
Hezekia di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem
1Hezekia déem toŋe kwora mo o pa Isarele de Judah dwia yam maama. O ta ma popone twanno se te yi Efrayim de Manasɛ dwi tiina bam. O déem dɛ konto baŋa ne mo o bwoŋi ba maama se ba jeeri Baŋa Wɛ diga kam na wo Jerusalem ne to ba di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem ba ma zuli Baŋa Wɛ na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to. 2Pɛ wom, de o nakwa bam, de Jerusalem teo kɔgɔ kom nam ya jaane boboŋa mo se ba di kuri dem chane selei chana kam ne. 3Ba wo wane kuri dem ba di boboa chana kam ne, ne ba na yeini ba di-de bene maama wone tei to, Wɛ kaanem tiina bam dedɛ ta na wo kwɛ ba tete de chullu tem to ŋwaane. Nɔɔna bam dedɛ de ya ta maa wo tu ba jeeri Jerusalem ne. 4Pɛ wom de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama boboŋe dem na jaane de tiŋi konto to ma pa se ba wo pwoli. 5Ba laam ma toŋe kwora pa se ka yi Isarele jei sem maama, ko na zege Beeriseba ne, se ko yi Dan laŋa kam seeni to. Ba ma bwoŋi nɔɔna bam se ba jeeri daane Jerusalem ne ba di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem ba ma zuli Baŋa Wɛ na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to. Kokuri to, nɔɔna bam ba yeini ba tui dedɛ dedɛ, ne Wɛ nia yam na bere se ba taa ke tei to.
6Pɛ wom ma pa ni se nɔɔna kwei o kwora kam ba ja ba jage ba yi Isarele teo kom de Judah teo kom ni maama. Pɛ wom de o nakwa bam kwora na popone ka tiŋi ye ka bere kolo to mo tento:
“Abam Isarele tiina bam, jwoori-na Baŋa Wɛ na ye á nabaara Abaraham, de Izaak, de Isarele Wɛ to tei. Abam ná ke konto, o de wó pipiri o jeeri abam balo ta na daare ye á lu Asiria pwa bam jeŋa ne to. 7Nam yé lwoni-na á nabaara bam kikia, de á chorro tem kikia, de ba na nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne to. Abam nam nɛ we ba keim dem konto ŋwaane, Wɛ pɛ se lɛɛro ba ba baŋa mo. 8Nam yé pa se á bochara digili, ne á kwoa bam déem na ke tei to. Sɛ-na á pa Baŋa Wɛ, se á daare á ta‑á jeeri o wara-jei sem wone. Kokuri to, o pɔɔre jeiga kam konto se ka taa ye wose mo se ko taa vei wuu. Ta‑á zuli-na á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, se o de dɔne o ban-lom dem á baŋa ne. 9Abam nam ná jwoori Baŋa Wɛ tei, balo na kale á chorro de á bia ba ja ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga to wó duri ba ŋwaŋa ye ba daare ba yage-ba se ba jwoori tega kanto ne. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ tiini o jege yibwona de ŋwaŋa. Abam maa ná jwoori á ba o tei, o daa bá ma o kwaga o ya abam.”
10Pɛ wom tontoŋena déem ma ja twanno tem ba jage ba kaare Efrayim de Manasɛ laŋa kam maama ne, ba vo ba yi Zebulun laŋa kam de. Ba nam na tole teo de teo konto to, nɔɔna bam maama jege-ba mo ba yaala ye ba mɔna. 11Ko nam na ye tei to, Asere dwi dem wone, de Manasɛ dwi dem wone, de Zebulun dwi dem wone nɔɔna badaara déem gwooni ba tete mo ye ba vo Jerusalem. 12Ko woli da, Wɛ déem pɛ se Judah tiina bam jege boboŋe dedwe mo we, ba wó taa ke ba tɔge kolo maama Pɛ Hezekia de o nakwa bam na toŋe kwora se ba ke to, ne Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ banto ni tei to.
