23Benjamin de Hasubi ma lɔ mɛ na bwola de ba sam to ba twoŋi da.
Maaseya bu Azaria wolo ta na ye Anania naa to de ma lɔ kabira kam o twoŋi mɛ na bwola de o sɔŋɔ to.
24Henadadi bu Binnui de ma lɔ o twoŋi da se ko zege Azaria sɔŋɔ ne se ko yi mɛ kabira kam na gugwoli ye gugworo wora to.
25-26Yuzayi bu Palale de daa ma lɔ kabira kam o zege gugworo kom yiga ne, baŋa seeni pɛ sɔŋɔ di-dedɔrɔ kom na wo mɛ ye ko bwola de pa-tara bam konkɔlɔ to.
Parose bu Pedaya de daa ma lɔ o twoŋi da se ko taa vei wɛ-puli seeni. O lɔge o vo o yi Na Ni dem seeni dedaane di-dedɔrɔ kolo na zege da to mo. Ofeli jei sem ne mo konto, Wɛ diga tontoŋena bam déem na zoore mɛ to.
27Tekoa teo tiina bam de daa ma lɔ ba twoŋi da. Banto toŋe di-dedɔrɔ-kamunu kom na zege mɛ to seeni, ye ba lɔ ba vo ba yi kabira kam na bwola de Ofeli to.
28Kaanem tiina badwonna de daa ma lɔ kabira kam ba twoŋi da. Ba zege Sisein-nɔɔno Ni dem ne mo ba lɔa ba vei baŋa kam seeni. Nɔɔno maama déem zege o tete sɔŋɔ ne mo o lɔa.
29Yimera bu Zadoki de ma lɔ o twoŋi kabira kam jei selo na zege o sɔŋɔ kom yiga ne to.
Sekania bu Semaya wolo na ye Wɛ-puli seeni Ni yereno wom to ma lɔ o twoŋi da.
30Selemia bu Hanania, de Hanun na ye Zalafe bia baredo tu wom to, de daa maa lɔ ba twoŋi da.
Berekia bu Mesulam de ma zege o di sem yiga ne o lɔ kabira kam o twoŋi da.
31Malakija na ye sabu-seŋa gɔgɔ to mo lɔge kabira kam o twoŋi da. O ma vo o yi sɔŋɔ kolo Wɛ diga tontoŋena de pipim-piina na zoore to. Jei sem konto déem bwola de Yerem Ni dem mo. O ta lɔge o yi mɛ kabira kam na jege gugworo ye wɛyuu diga wo ka yera ne to mo.
32Sabu-seŋa gwaro tem de pipim-piina bam de laam ma zege gugworo kom diga kam na wo mɛ to ba lɔ kabira kam ba vo ba yi Pei Ni dem seeni.

english_text:
Nehemiah's Enemies
1When Sanballat, the governor of Samaria, heard that we were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, he became angry and started insulting our people. 2In front of his friends and the Samaritan army he said, “What is this feeble bunch of Jews trying to do? Are they going to rebuild the wall and offer sacrifices all in one day? Do they think they can make something out of this pile of scorched stones?”
3Tobiah from Ammon was standing beside Sanballat and said, “Look at the wall they are building! Why, even a fox could knock over this pile of stones.”
4But I prayed, “Our God, these people hate us and have wished horrible things for us. Please answer our prayers and make their insults fall on them! Let them be the ones to be dragged away as prisoners of war. 5Don't forgive the mean and evil way they have insulted the builders.”
6The people worked hard, and we built the walls of Jerusalem halfway up again. 7But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people from the city of Ashdod saw the walls going up and the holes being repaired. So they became angry 8and decided to stir up trouble, and to fight against the people of Jerusalem. 9But we kept on praying to our God, and we also stationed guards day and night.
10Meanwhile, the people of Judah were singing a sorrowful song:
“So much rubble for us to haul!
Worn out and weary,
will we ever finish this wall?”
11Our enemies were saying, “Before those Jews know what has happened, we will sneak up and kill them and put an end to their work.”
12On at least ten different occasions, the Jews living near our enemies warned us against attacks from every side, 13and so I sent people to guard the wall at its lowest places and where there were still holes in it. I placed them according to families, and they stood guard with swords and spears and with bows and arrows. 14Then I looked things over and told the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don't be afraid of your enemies! The Lord is great and fearsome. So think of him and fight for your relatives and children, your wives and homes!”
15Our enemies found out that we knew about their plot against us, but God kept them from doing what they had planned. So we went back to work on the wall.
16From then on, I let half of the young men work while the other half stood guard. They wore armor and had spears and shields, as well as bows and arrows. The leaders helped the workers 17who were rebuilding the wall. Everyone who hauled building materials kept one hand free to carry a weapon. 18Even the workers who were rebuilding the wall strapped on a sword. The worker who was to blow the signal trumpet stayed with me.
19I told the people and their officials and leaders, “Our work is so spread out, that we are a long way from one another. 20If you hear the sound of the trumpet, come quickly and gather around me. Our God will help us fight.”
21Every day from dawn to dark, half of the workers rebuilt the walls, while the rest stood guard with their spears.
22I asked the men in charge and their workers to stay inside Jerusalem and stand guard at night. So they guarded the city at night and worked during the day. 23I even slept in my work clothes at night; my relatives, the workers, and the guards slept in theirs as well. And we always kept our weapons close by.
translation_text:
Veira kwaane se ba chɔge totoŋa yam
1Sanbalati na yɔɔre o ni we debam Juu tiina bam wora dé fɔge dé lɔ Jerusalem kabiri sem to, mo ko tiini ko fuli o wo. O laam ma bobo se o taa ke debam o mɔna. 2O déem zege o yuudwonna yiga ne, dedaane Samaria jar-keira bam yiga ne mo ye o ta o we, “Juu tiina nabwona banto boŋe we ba wora ba ke bɛ mo? Ba boŋe se ba jwoori ba lɔ ba teo kom ba pe mo na? Ba teene we dɛ dedwe kaanem wó wane de gare de ti ba totoŋa yam mo na? Ba nam wó wane ba na kandwa se ya nwoŋi weero tento wone ye mini chɔge-ya to na?”
3Amon tu Tobia déem zege o tei ne mo. O de ma leiri o taane dem o we, “Nii kabira kalo ba na wora ba lɔa to! Yiru tete ná diini ka baŋa ne, o wó yigi-ka mo o de tega ne!”
4Amo de ma lwoori Wɛ a we, “Debam Wɛ, nii ba na gwooni debam tei! Cheigi mwanno telo dwi ba na mɔne debam to! Nam pipiri ba mwanno tem se te jwoori ba tete yuu ne. Pa se nɔɔna vere ba jejegero maama, se ba daare ba zeŋe-ba ba ja ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga. 5Yé kwei ba keim-balwaaro tem n ma n chɛ-ba! Yé saare ba wɛleera! Kokuri to, ba tiini ba twe debam balo na wora dé lɔ to mo.”
6Dé ma se zwa ye dé toŋa. Ko wo dáane ye kabira kam di ka yi ka chichworo jei, nɔɔna bam maama boboŋa déem na jaane se ba toŋe to ŋwaane.
7Ko daare Sanbalati, de Tobia, de Arabi tiina bam, de Amon tiina bam, de Asedodi tiina bam maama na nigi we dé lɔge kabira kam pa se ka vo yiga, ye pwoli sem maama se to, mo ba bane tiini de zaŋe. 8Banto maama ma sɔ ni se ba jeeri Jerusalem teo kom de jara. Ba ta ma boŋe se ba pa se vuvuga taa wora jei maama wone. 9Debam de ma yɔɔre dé ware Wɛ, ye dé daare dé pa se nɔɔna yere teo kom wea de tete maama dé dona bam ŋwaane.
10Judah tiina bam déem yeini ba leeni mo ye ba toŋa. Ba maa we,
“Debam tontoŋena bam zeŋe zela dé bugi!
Nii teero de weero na daga tei!
Dé zem wó ke tetɛ mo dé lɔ kabira kam?”
11Dé dona de maa tɛ ba we, “Dé wó pɔpɔ dé ba ba baŋa ne! Ba bá wuuri ba lɔre ko ni ne. Dé laam maa wó go-ba se totoŋa yam kwori.” 12Ko nam na ke tei to, Juu tiina balo na zoore ba twɛ de dé dona bam to ma yeini ba ba kuni dedɛ wone, ba ta dé dona bam boboŋa yam ba bere debam. 13Ko ma pa se a le nɔɔna badwonna ye ba zege kabira kam jei teiri teiri wone. Ba déem zege da dedaane se-zɔɔro, de chichwoa, de chena mo. A déem kuri-ba diga de diga mo se ba zege mɛ maama ta na wo lɔge ko di to.
14Amo ma na we keim dem maama daane nɔɔna bam mo. A ma ta de nɔɔna bam, de ba yiga tiina, de ba nakwa bam a we, “Yé ta‑á kɔre-na dé dona bam. Nam guli-na we dé Teiru Wɛ wom ye kamunu, ye o totoŋa yɛ ni. Konto mo wó pa se á jaŋe á dwonna Isarele tiina bam, de á bia, de á kaana, de á sam dem ŋwaane.”
15Dé dona bam ma maane we dé lɔre ba na sɔge ni se ba ke tei to. Wɛ de ma pa se ba boboŋa yam ji kafɛ. Ba na ke ye ba ga dé ŋwa to ŋwaane, dé maama dedoa dedoa ma jwoori dé lɔɔm jei. 16-17Ko na zege dento dɛ ne to, a tontoŋena bam chichworo mo toŋe kabira kam totoŋa, ye chichworo de vɔ jara zela ba zei chichwoa, de jara nantane, de chena ba zega. Ko ná ye Judah dwi tiina balo maama na toŋe kabira kam lɔɔm totoŋa to, ba nakwa bam de déem ma zege ba kwaga ne. Tontoŋena balo na zeŋe lɔɔm zela to de maa zei jara zela de jeŋa dedoa, ye ba daare ba toŋe de kadwoŋi kam. 18Lɔra bam tete kwei se-zɔɔro mo ba vɔ ba tei ne ye ba lɔa. Ko daare wolo wom na yeini o wui nabɔnɔ kom to yerane mo zege amo tei ne.
19Amo laam ma ta de dedɛɛra bam, de nakwa bam, dedaane nɔɔna bam maama a we, “Totoŋa yam laŋa yala, ye ya jage ya yi kabira kam ni maama pa se dé ba nae daane. 20Abam nam ná wo mɛ maama ye á ni nabɔnɔ kom kwori, se á ba debam tei ywo-seeni. Dé Wɛ wom mo lage o jaŋe o pa debam.”
21Dɛ maama wone, tega na jege ka poore to, mo dé chichworo yeini dé bobo kabira kam totoŋa. Dé chichworo kodwoŋi kom de maa zei jara zela ba yere lɔra bam. Dé yɔɔre dé ke konto mo taa, se ko yi tete ne, chalechwe na bobo se se nwoŋi maŋa kalo to. 22Ko na ye konto to mo a déem tage nɔɔna bam we, “Nɔɔno maama de o wolinu jege se ba maŋe Jerusalem ne mo ba peini. Konto mo wó pa se ba taa yere dé teo kom tete ne, se wea ne ba wane ba taa toŋa.” 23Ko nam ná ye amo tete, de a chorro tem, de a tontoŋena bam, de balo na yere-ne to maama, debam wolowolo yeini dé ware se dé le dé gwaaro dé tiŋi wea ne, naa tete ne. Dé maama yɔɔre dé yeini dé vɔ dé jara zela mo kiri kiri dé zega.

english_text:
Nehemiah's Concern for the Poor
1Some of the men and their wives complained about the Jews in power 2and said, “We have large families, and it takes a lot of grain merely to keep us alive.”
3Others said, “During the famine we even had to mortgage our fields, vineyards, and homes to them in order to buy grain.”
4Then others said, “We had to borrow money from those in power to pay the government tax on our fields and vineyards. 5We are Jews just as they are, and our children are as good as theirs. But we still have to sell our children as slaves, and some of our daughters have already been raped. We are completely helpless; our fields and vineyards have even been taken from us.”
6When I heard their complaints and their charges, I became very angry. 7 So I thought it over and said to the leaders and officials, “How can you charge your own people interest?”
Then I called a public meeting and accused the leaders 8by saying, “We have tried to buy back all of our people who were sold into exile. But here you are, selling more of them for us to buy back!” The officials and leaders did not say a word, because they knew this was true.
9I continued, “What you have done is wrong! We must honor our God by the way we live, so the Gentiles can't find fault with us. 10My relatives, my friends, and I are also lending money and grain, but we must no longer demand payment in return. 11Now give back the fields, vineyards, olive orchards, and houses you have taken and also the interest you have been paid.”
12The leaders answered, “We will do whatever you say and return their property, without asking to be repaid.”
So I made the leaders promise in front of the priests to give back the property. 13Then I emptied my pockets and said, “If you don't keep your promise, that's what God will do to you. He will empty out everything you own, even taking away your houses.”
The people answered, “We will keep our promise.” Then they praised the Lord and did as they had promised.
Nehemiah Is Generous
14I was governor of Judah from the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king until the thirty-second year. And during these entire twelve years, my relatives and I refused to accept the food that I was allowed. 15Each governor before me had been a burden to the people by making them pay for his food and wine and by demanding forty silver coins a day. Even their officials had been a burden to the people. But I respected God, and I didn't think it was right to be so hard on them. 16I spent all my time getting the wall rebuilt and did not buy any property. Everyone working for me did the same thing. 17I usually fed 150 of our own Jewish people and their leaders, as well as foreign visitors from surrounding lands. 18Each day one ox, six of the best sheep, and lots of chickens were prepared. Then every ten days, a large supply of wine was brought in. I knew what a heavy burden this would have been for the people, and so I did not ask for my food allowance as governor.
19I pray that God will bless me for everything I have done for my people.
translation_text:
Nehemia na woli nabwona tei to
1Ko déem na woli fee to, mo nɔɔna dedɛ, kaana de baara maama bobo se ba taa tiini ba poona ba dwonna Juu tiina bam. 2Nɔɔna dedɛ déem mo tɛ ba we, “Dé bia tiini ba daga mo, dé nam ná wo nɛ wodiu se dé di, debam dedaane dé bia wó te mo.” 3Badwonna maa tɛ ba we, “Debam kwei dé te sem, de dé kare, dedaane dé sam mo dé tiŋi daare ye dé jwoŋi wodiiru se dé di sem tiina wori.” 4Badaara daa ta maa we, “Debam jene sabia mo se dé ma dé ŋwe Pɛ wom lampwoo kom o na tiŋi dé kare dedaane dé kadwi ŋwaane to. 5Nam nii! Debam de dé dwonna Juu tiina bam ye woŋo dedoa mo, dé ye yera de jana daane. Debam bia de banto bia ba gare daane, ye dé laam kwei debam bia bam dé yeigi dé pa-ba se ba taa ye kabɛ. Ba fe debam se dé yeigi dé bukwa dé pa-ba. Ba ta ma vere debam kare, de dé kadwi pa se dé daa ware kolokolo se dé ke.”
6Amo na nigi ba ŋwaana yam to mo a bane yɔɔre de zaŋe. 7A boboŋa ma ja se a woli-ba. A ma bwɛ Isarele yiga tiina de ba nakwa bam a we, “Abam ba kwaana de á na boŋe se á zi á tete chorro Juu tiina baŋa ne, se á zaŋe to. Abam yeini á fe á chorro se ba ŋwe sabu dedɛ ba jena ŋwaane.” A ta ma bwoŋi kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama se dé nii taane dem konto baŋa ne, 8ye a we, “Dé ya kwaane se dé jwoori dé yeigi Juu tiina balo ba na yeigi-ba ba pa veira to mo. Abam tete daa ma fe á chorro Juu tiina se ba yeigi ba tete ba pa abam se ba taa ye á kabɛ. Ko lana na?” Ba yiga tiina bam ma maŋe da chemm, ba na gɛ taane se ba leiri to ŋwaane.
9Amo ma ta de-ba a we, “Abam na jege kolo á ke to ba lana. Abam maŋe se á kɔre Wɛ mo, se á daare á ta‑á ke lanyerane. Á ná ke konto, dwi-gɛ tiina balo na ye dé dona to bá na chwoŋa se ba mɔne debam. 10Amo sɛ se nɔɔna bam ba a tei ba jene sabu de wodiu, ye balo na toŋe ba pa-ne to de ke a na ke tei to. Nam pa-na se dé daa yé taa pini dé chorro tem. 11Kwei-na ba kadwi, de ba kare, de ba sam á jwoori á pa-ba leile. Nam ta yage-na jena yalo ba na jege to á chɛ-ba, ko ná ye mena, naa sana, naa nuga, naa sabia mo.” 12Ba de ma leiri ba we, “Dé wó seene dé ke nmo na tage tei to. Dé wó pa-ba ba wonnu maama, ye dé daa bá taa pini-ba.”
Amo laam ma bwoŋi kaanem tiina bam ye a pa se nakwa bam du duuri ba yiga ne se ba ke ba tɔge ba na tage tei to. 13Amo ma bwoli gɔrɔ kolo na vɔge a teiŋa ne to, ye a zezage-ko pa se wonnu telo ya na wo ka yera ne to siiri tega ne. A ma ta-ba a we, “Wolo maama ná ve se o toŋe o tɔge o ni dem, Wɛ wó zezage kotu tento dwoŋi mo se o ga o sɔŋɔ de o wonnu maama, ye o laam ta ye bwori.” Kɔgɔ kom maama ma sɛ ye ba we, “Ameena!” Ba ma tei Baŋa Wɛ ye ba daare ba ke ba tɔge ba ni dem.
14Bena fuga-yalei yam maama wone a déem na tei Judah laŋa kam to, amo de a chorro maama wo sɛ se dé kwei wodiiru telo teo kom dedɛɛro wom na jege chwoŋa se o jwoŋi o di to se dé di-te. Ko maa ye Pɛ Atazeregese paare dim bena finlei bene dem ne mo o tiŋi-ne se a ji dedɛɛro wom, se ko taa nii o paare dim bena fintɔ-yalei bene dem ne. 15Dedɛɛra balo déem na lwoori yiga ba nii Judah laŋa kam to yeini ba fe nɔɔna bam ba jwoŋi ba lu-nyenno sabu-dala finna mo, ye ba wodiiru de sana ta zega. Ba tontoŋena de maa bɛɛse nɔɔna bam. Amo nam wo ke konto, a na kɔre Wɛ to ŋwaane. 16Amo ma yɔɔre a kwei a dam de a boboŋa maama a ke kabira kam lɔɔm baŋa ne. Amo wo boŋe se a beeri tega a pa a tete. Amo tontoŋena bam maama de seene ba yia se ba taa toŋe totoŋa yam.
17Ko ta woli da, Juu tiina de ba yiga tiina bi de finnu déem mo tui a tei, ye a pae-ba ba ni-wodiu maŋa maama. Nɔɔna ta ma zege teene dedwonna ne ba tui ye a woli-ba. 18Dɛ maama wone, a déem yeini a go nabea mo, de pi-kamuna yaredo dedaane cheeni dedɛ. Da fuga maama wone, a maa yeini a pae se ba yeigi sana dedɛ se nɔɔna bam taa nyɔa. A nam na yei we ko tiini ko chamma ko pae nɔɔna bam to ŋwaane mo amo wo tage we ba pa-ne kolo a na ye ba dedɛɛro ye a maŋe se a jwoŋi to.
19Amo Tu Wɛ, a nam lwoori‑m se n guli amo gula se n ke-ne lanyerane, a na ke kolo maama a pa nɔɔna banto to ŋwaane.

english_text:
Plots against Nehemiah
1Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and our other enemies learned that I had completely rebuilt the wall. All I lacked was hanging the doors in the gates. 2Then Sanballat and Geshem sent a message, asking me to meet with them in one of the villages in Ono Valley. I knew they were planning to harm me in some way. 3So I sent messengers to tell them, “My work is too important to stop now and go there. I can't afford to slow down the work just to visit with you.” 4They invited me four times, but each time I refused to go.
5Finally, Sanballat sent an official to me with an unsealed letter, 6which said:
A rumor is going around among the nations that you and the other Jews are rebuilding the wall and planning to rebel, because you want to be their king. And Geshem says it's true! 7You even have prophets in Jerusalem, claiming you are now the king of Judah. You know the Persian king will hear about this, so let's get together and talk it over.
8I sent a message back to Sanballat, saying, “None of this is true! You are making it all up.”
9Our enemies were trying to frighten us and to keep us from our work. But I asked God to give me strength.
10One day I went to visit Shemaiah. He wasn't supposed to leave his house, but he said, “Let's hurry to the holy place of the temple and hide there. We will lock the temple doors, because your enemies are planning to kill you tonight.”
11I answered, “Why should someone like me have to run and hide in the temple to save my life? I won't go!”
12Suddenly I realized that God had not given Shemaiah this message. But Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him to trick me 13and to frighten me into doing something wrong, because they wanted to ruin my good name.
14Then I asked God to punish Tobiah and Sanballat for what they had done. I prayed that God would punish the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who, together with her, had tried to frighten me.
The Work Is Finished
15On the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, the wall was completely rebuilt. It had taken 52 days. 16When our enemies in the surrounding nations learned that the work was finished, they felt helpless, because they knew that our God had helped us rebuild the wall.
17All this time the Jewish leaders and Tobiah had been writing letters back and forth. 18Many people in Judah were loyal to Tobiah for two reasons: Shecaniah son of Arah was his father-in-law, and Tobiah's son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah. 19The people would always tell me about the good things Tobiah had done, and then they would tell Tobiah everything I had said. So Tobiah kept sending letters, trying to frighten me.
translation_text:
Veira bam ta kwaane se ba chɔge totoŋa yam
1Sanbalati, de Tobia, de Arabi tu Gɛsem, dedaane dé dona bam maama ma ni kwora we dé lɔge kabira kam dé ti, pa se pwoli daa tere ka wone. Kolo yerane na muri to, dé ya ta wo kwei ka bworru tem dé ke di-nia yam ne. 2Sanbalati de Gɛsem ma toŋe kwora ba pa-ne, se a jeeri-ba Ono te-kampare teo kodwoŋi ne se dé na daane. Ba nam ya boŋe se ba ke-ne lwarem mo. 3Amo ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba ta-ba we, “Amo jege totoŋ-kuri mo a toŋa pa se a bá wane a jeeri da. Amo nam bá da we abam lage se a na-ne ŋwaane se a yage a totoŋa yanto.” 4Ba beeri dem nam ya ye kwora dedoa mo kuni bena. Kuni bena wom maama ne, a de ma leiri-ba nenɛɛne a na maŋe a ta tei to.
5Sanbalati laam ma toŋe o tete tontoŋena bam dedoa de kwora, se o pa-ne tɔnɔ kolo ni na puri to. 6Ba ma popone ko wone we:
“Gɛsem mo pɛ se a lɔre we sawea mo kare jei sem maama ka ŋɔɔne we nmo de Juu tiina bam maama boŋe se á nwoŋi pa-faro wom kwaga ne mo. Konto nam mo pɛ se á yɔɔre á seene á yia de á kabira kam lɔɔm. Ba ta we nmo kwaane se n tiŋi n tete mo se n ta‑n ye ba pɛ. 7Ba we n maŋe n beeri n sampwori selo na wó zege Jerusalem ne ba ta we, ‘Ba tiŋi pɛ Judah ne!’ to. Pa-faro Atazeregese nam na wó ni taane dento to ŋwaane, nmo jege se n ba mo se dé ke dé yuni daane dé nii dé wó ke tɛ mo.”
8Amo ma leiri-ba a we, “Ko dae chega! Sawea bere ka tere jei jei ne ka kare ka ŋɔɔna. Abam tete mo loge wonnu tem konto a pa debam.”
9Ba déem yɔɔre ba kwaane se ba fugi debam mo ye ba boŋe we, “Ba je sem ná bugi, totoŋa yam daa bá toŋe.” Amo de ma ware Wɛ ye a we, “Amo Tu Wɛ, pa-ne dam.”
10Dɛ dedwe mo a vei Delaya bu Semaya sɔŋɔ se a ware‑o. O déem ta ye Mehetabeli naa mo. Semaya nam ya pe o tete mo o wo o sɔŋɔ ne. O ma ta de amo o we, “Nɔɔna mo boŋe se ba zaŋe n baŋa ne tete dedwe ba go‑m. Nam pa se dé duri dé vo dé zo Wɛ wara-jei sem di-yuu kom wone. Dé laam maa wó pe ka ni dé seigi dáane se ba yé yi‑m ba go.”
11A ma leiri‑o a we, “Amo dae balo na duri ba seigi se cham yé yi-ba to. Bɛŋwaane mo amo wó duri a zo Wɛ diga wone se a lu toone? Amo bere a bá ke konto.” 12A na boŋe ko wone to mo a maane we ko ya dae Wɛ mo ŋɔɔne ded‑o, se ko ye Tobia de Sanbalati mo vei ba pa‑o sabu se o ta taane dem konto de amo. 13Ba nam soge‑o se o pa foone zo-ne mo, se a daare a ke wɛleere. A ná chɔge a yere konto, ba ya wó ke-ne chaveera.
14“Amo Tu Wɛ, guli Tobia de Sanbalati na ke-ne tei to. Nam yé swei we sampwori-kana Noadia, de sampwori sesem sem maama ya kwaane mo se ba fugi-ne.”
Ba na ti ba totoŋa yam tetei to
15Ba déem kwei da finnu-yalei mo ba lɔ kabira kam ba ti. Ko maa ye Eluli chana kam da finlei-yanu dɛ ne mo konto. 16Debam dona bam dedaane teene delo na gilimi debam to na nigi konto to, mo ba baare maama ti, ye foone tiini de ja-ba. Kokuri to, ba maama lɔre we Wɛ mo woli debam pa se dé ke tento maama.
17Konto maama to, de Judah yiga tiina bam badaara me de Tobia mo. Ba ma yeini ba toŋe kwori ba pa daane. 18Judah tiina dedɛ de déem maa sɔ ni ded‑o, kolo ŋwaane Ara bu Sekania ye Tobia tembaaro mo. Ko ta woli da o bu Jehohanan de ya vei o di Berekia bu Mesulam bukɔ mo. 19Nɔɔna maa yeini ba tui ba tɛ de amo Tobia keim na lana tei to. Ba ta ma jaane kolo maama amo na wó ta to ba vo ba lwei ba tiŋi o yiga ne. O de maa yeini o popone twanno o pa-ne se o fugi-ne.

english_text:
1After the wall had been rebuilt and the gates hung, then the temple guards, the singers, and the other Levites were assigned their work. 2I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, along with Hananiah, the commander of the fortress, because Hananiah could be trusted, and he respected God more than most people did. 3I said to them, “Don't let the gates to the city be opened until the sun has been up for a while. And make sure that they are closed and barred before the guards go off duty at sunset. Choose people from Jerusalem to stand guard at different places around the wall and others to stand guard near their own houses.”
A List of Exiles Who Returned
(Ezra 2.1-70)
4Although Jerusalem covered a large area, not many people lived there, and no new houses had been built. 5-6So God gave me the idea to bring together the people, their leaders, and officials and to check the family records of those who had returned from captivity in Babylonia, after having been taken there by King Nebuchadnezzar. About this same time, I found records of those who had been the first to return to Jerusalem from Babylon Province. By reading these records, I learned that they settled in their own hometowns, 7and that they had come with Zerubbabel, Joshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah.
8-25This is a list of how many returned from each family group: 2,172 from Parosh; 372 from Shephatiah; 652 from Arah; 2,818 from Pahath Moab, who were all descendants of Jeshua and Joab; 1,254 from Elam; 845 from Zattu; 760 from Zaccai; 648 from Binnui; 628 from Bebai; 2,322 from Azgad; 667 from Adonikam; 2,067 from Bigvai; 655 from Adin; 98 from Ater, also known as Hezekiah; 328 from Hashum; 324 from Bezai; 112 from Hariph; and 95 from Gibeon.
26-38This is a list of how many returned whose ancestors had come from the following towns: 188 from Bethlehem and Netophah; 128 from Anathoth; 42 from Beth-Azmaveth; 743 from Kiriath-Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth; 621 from Ramah and Geba; 122 from Michmas; 123 from Bethel and Ai; 52 from Nebo; 1,254 from Elam; 320 from Harim; 345 from Jericho; 721 from Lod, Hadid, and Ono; and 3,930 from Senaah.
39-42This is a list of how many returned from each family of priests: 973 descendants of Jeshua from Jedaiah; 1,052 from Immer; 1,247 from Pashhur; and 1,017 from Harim.
43-45This is a list of how many returned from the families of Levites: 74 descendants of Hodevah from the families of Jeshua and Kadmiel; 148 descendants of Asaph from the temple musicians; and 138 descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai from the temple guards.
46-56These are the names of the families of temple workers whose descendants returned: Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth, Keros, Sia, Padon, Lebana, Hagaba, Shalmai, Hanan, Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah, Besai, Meunim, Nephushesim, Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur, Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha, Barkos, Sisera, Temah, Neziah, and Hatipha.
57-59Here are the names of Solomon's servants whose descendants returned: Sotai, Sophereth, Perida, Jaala, Darkon, Giddel, Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, and Amon.
60A total of 392 descendants of temple workers and of Solomon's servants returned.
61-62There were 642 who returned from the families of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, though they could not prove they were Israelites. They had lived in the Babylonian towns of Tel-Melah, Tel-Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer.
63-64The families of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai could not prove they were priests. The ancestor of the family of Barzillai had married the daughter of Barzillai from Gilead and had taken his wife's family name. But the records of these three families could not be found, and none of them were allowed to serve as priests. 65 In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until he lets us know if you really are priests.”
66-69There were 42,360 who returned, in addition to 7,337 servants and 245 musicians, counting both men and women. Altogether, they brought with them 736 horses, 245 mules, 435 camels, and 6,720 donkeys.
70-72Many people gave gifts to help pay for the materials to rebuild the temple. The governor himself gave 8 kilograms of gold, 50 bowls to be used in the temple, and 530 robes for the priests. Family leaders gave 153 kilograms of gold and 1,458 kilograms of silver. The rest of the people gave 153 kilograms of gold, 1,325 kilograms of silver, and 67 robes for the priests.
73 And so, by the seventh month, priests, Levites, temple guards, musicians, workers, and many of the ordinary people had settled in the towns of Judah.

1Dé na ti kabira kam maama, ye dé ta kwei bworru tem maama dé kwaare nia yam ne te na maŋe se te taa wo mɛ maama to, a laam ma kuri nɔɔna badwonna se ba taa ye nia yam yerena. A ta ma le badwonna se ba taa ye lein-leena, ye Levi tiina badaara de maa toŋe ba totoŋa. 2A daa ta kwei Jerusalem teo kom a ke a choro Hanani de Hanania je ne mo, se ba taa nii-ko ba pa-ne. Hanania déem nam ye teo kom dalem jei sem yiga tu mo. O ma kɔre Wɛ ye o jege chega lanyerane. 3A ma pa-ba ni we, “Yé pa-na se ba pore Jerusalem teo ni-bworru tem ko ná dae wea ná bega. Nam pe-na bworru tem se ni-yerena bam laam zaŋe wɛ-zoore maŋa ne ba jwoori sɔŋɔ. Ta kwei-na luuru á ma á fɔge á che-te. Á laam maa wó kuri Jerusalem nɔɔna badwonna se ba taa yere teo kom, nɔɔno maama de o yerem jei, se badwonna de taa kare ba sam ni ne.”
Balo na jwoori sɔŋɔ to yera yam
4Jerusalem teo kom ni déem daga lanyerane, ye nɔɔna balo na zoore ko wone to ba daga. Ko woli da, ba déem ta wo lɔge sam dedɛ. 5Wɛ ma kwei boboŋe o pa-ne se a la dedɛɛra bam, de yiga tiina bam, de nɔɔna bam maama, se a tole nɔɔno maama dwi natɔga kam na ye tei to. Amo ma na tɔnɔ kolo na bere balo na dɛ yiga ba jwoori to yera. A déem nɛ tento mo:
6Nɔɔna balo déem na zege Babilonia kateiri dem ne ba jwoori Jerusalem de Judah teene dedwonna wone to yera mo tento. Nɔɔno maama déem ma jwoori o vo o tete teo. Babilonia Pa-faro Nebukadeneza ya jaane-ba mo o vo o pe o tete teo kom ne. 7Ba ma tɔge de Zerubabel, de Jesua, de Nehemia, de Azaria, de Raamia, de Nahamani, de Modekayi, de Bilisan, de Mispare, de Bigavayi, de Nehum, dedaane Baana mo ba jwoori ba sam.

63Twanno déem tera se te bere kaanem tiina banto nabaara na ye balo to: Hobaya bia, de Hakoza bia, de Bazilayi bia bam. (Bazilayi ya vei Gilead mo o swo Bazilayi dwi dem kaane wodwoŋi. Ba ma lɛɛre ba kwei o tembaaro yere ba mae ba bwoi‑o.) 64Ba na beeri ba nabaara natɔga twanno tem ba ga to, mo ba déem chege-ba se ba yé tɔge ba taa ye Wɛ kaanem tiina. 65Teo kom dedɛɛro wom ma pa-ba ni we ba yé tɔge ba di wodiu kolo na ye ko yera Wɛ ŋwaane to, ko ná dae kaanem tu ná tua ye o wae o kwei Yurim de Tumim memaŋa kandwa o ma o kuri Wɛ boboŋa o pa nɔɔna bam.
66Nɔɔna balo déem na jwoori to maama ni dem ye 42,360 mo.
67Ba kabɛ, baara de kaana maama maa ye 7,337.
Ba lein-leena, baara de kaana maama maa ye 245.
68Ba sisein-nɔɔna déem ye 736 mo.
Ba sisei-bonɛ maa ye 245.
69Ba kona maa ye 435.
Ba bonɛ sem maa ye 6,720.
70Sam yiga tiina dedɛ déem ma tɔge ba woli se Wɛ diga kam jwoori ka ke lam. Teo kom dedɛɛro wom de ma pa sabu-seŋa kilo nana (8), de zwe finnu (50), dedaane gwaaro bia yanu de fintɔ (530) se kaanem tiina bam taa zoora. 71Sam yiga tiina badaara ma la sabu-seŋa kilo bi de fuserepɛ (170), de lu-nyenno kilo moro de bia yalei (1,200) ba pa totoŋa yam ŋwaane. 72Nɔɔna balo maama na daare to de ma pa sabu-seŋa kilo bi de fuserepɛ (170), de lu-nyenno kilo moro de bi (1,100), ko woli de gwaaro fuseredo-terepɛ (67) se kaanem tiina bam taa zoora.
73Kaanem tiina bam, de Levi dwi tiina bam, de Wɛ diga ni-yerena bam, de lein-leena bam, ko ta woli de Wɛ diga tontoŋena bam, de Isarele dwi tiina badaara bam maama laam ma vo ba jeini ba tete teene dem ne.
Ezera gage Wɛ Tɔnɔ kom o bere nɔɔna bam
Ko déem ke chane serepɛ de Isarele tiina bam na jwoori ba jeini ba tete teene dem ne to.

english_text:
Ezra Reads God's Law to the People
1-2On the first day of the seventh month, the people came together in the open area in front of the Water Gate. Then they asked Ezra, who was a teacher of the Law of Moses, to read to them from this Law that the Lord had given his people. Ezra the priest came with the Law and stood before the crowd of men, women, and the children who were old enough to understand. 3From early morning till noon, he read the Law of Moses to them, and they listened carefully. 4Ezra stood on a high wooden platform that had been built for this occasion. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah were standing to his right, while Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash Baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam were standing to his left.
5Ezra was up on the high platform, where he could be seen by everyone, and when he opened the book, all the people stood up. 6Ezra praised the great Lord God, and they lifted their hands, shouting “Amen! Amen!” Then they bowed with their faces to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
7-8After this, the Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah went among the people, explaining the meaning of what Ezra had read.
9The people started crying when God's Law was read to them. Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who had been teaching the people all said, “This is a special day for the Lord your God. So don't be sad and don't cry!”
10Nehemiah told the people, “Enjoy your good food and wine and share some with those who didn't have anything to bring. Don't be sad! This is a special day for the Lord, and he will make you happy and strong.”
11The Levites encouraged the people by saying, “This is a sacred day, so don't worry or mourn!” 12When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them.
Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
13On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law 14 that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year. 15They also learned that they were to go into the woods and gather branches of leafy trees such as olives, myrtles, and palms for making these shelters.
16So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate. 17Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun. 18On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
translation_text:
1Isarele tiina bam maama déem ma jeeri kapworo ne, se ko maŋe de Na Ni dem. Ezera déem nam ye Wɛ nia zamesem tu mo ye o kwori o ye Wɛ kaanem tu. Ba ma toŋe ba bwoŋi‑o se o ja Moses nia tɔnɔ kom Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Isarele tiina bam to, o ba o ga se ba cheigi. 2Chane serepɛ boboa dɛ dem ne, mo Ezera jaane Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom o ba o zege nɔn-kɔgɔ kom yiga ne. Baara, de kaana, de balo maama na bege ba yi se ba ni taane kuri to déem mo wora. 3Dɛ dem konto ne mo Ezera maŋe kapworo kom ne o ga Wɛ nia yam ko zege tetete se ko yi wea tetare maŋa ne. Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom de yɔɔre ba maŋe da mo ba cheigi taane dem.
4Ba ya kwei dɛ mo ba ke bimbini tigisim dem ŋwaane. Ezera ma di o dɔge de baŋa ne ye o ŋɔɔne de nɔɔna bam. Matitia, de Sema, de Anaya, de Yuria, de Hilikia, de Maaseya déem wo o jazem ne mo. Pedaya, de Misayeli, de Malakija, de Hasum, de Hasabadana, de Zekaria, dedaane Mesulam maa zege o jagwia ne.
5Ezera déem zege bimbini dem yuu ne mo pa se nɔɔna bam maama kwoni ba nii ba na‑o. O na yɔɔre o puri tɔnɔ kom to, mo ba maama zaŋe ba zege wɛɛne. 6Ezera ma ta o we, “Á pa-na se dé tei Baŋa Wɛ, se o ye Wɛ kamunu!”
Nɔɔna bam maama ma zeiŋi ba je wɛɛne, ye ba daare ba ta we, “Ameena! Ameena!” Ba ta ma tiiri ye ba yibia vwi tega ne se ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ.
7Nɔɔna bam na zege ba ni Wɛ nia yam to, mo Levi tiina badwonna woli-ba se ba wane ba ni ko kuri. Banto maa ye Jesua, de Bani, de Serebia, de Jamin, de Akuba, de Sabetayi, de Hodia, de Maaseya, de Kelita, de Azaria, de Jozabadi, de Hanan, dedaane Pelaya. 8Ba ma ga Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom ye ba maŋe ko kuri lanyerane, se nɔɔna bam wane ba ni ko kuri chekke.
9Ba déem na nigi Wɛ nia taane konto to mo ba yɔɔre ba keeri bɔge-bɔge. Teo kom dedɛɛro Nehemia, de Ezera na ye Wɛ nia zamesem tu de Wɛ kaanem tu to, de Levi tiina balo na jege nɔɔna bam ba zamese to laam ma ta de nɔɔna bam maama ba we, “Zem dɛ dem ye de yera mo de pae abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Konto ŋwaane, yé pa-na se á wo chɔge, nam yé ta‑á keera.”
10Nehemia ma ta-ba o we, “Jwoori-na á sam, se á di wodi-ywonnu, á daare á nyɔ sa-sona. Ta chɛ-na á wo-laaro tem de balo na ba jege to se ba de di ba su. Zem dɛ dem na ye de yera de pae Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane, yé pa-na se á wo chɔge. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ wopwolo kom o na pae abam to mo wó ji abam dam.”
11Levi tiina bam de ma zi nɔɔna bam bochwanno ye ba we, “Zuri-na á bochara. Zem dɛ dem ye de yera de pae Baŋa Wɛ. Yé pa-na se á wo chɔge.”
12Nɔɔna bam maama ma jwoori ba sam, ba vo ba di ba su de wopwolo. Ba ma chɛ ba wonnu de balo na gɛ to. Kokuri to, ba déem nigi Wɛ botara kalo ba na gage ba bere-ba to kuri lanyerane.
Vwoa chwiim kuri
13Ko na ke da yalei to, mo sɔ-yuni tem yiga tiina, de Wɛ kaanem tiina, dedaane Levi tiina bam jwoori ba gilimi Ezera tei ne se ba yɛ taane delo na nwoŋi Wɛ nia yam wone to. 14Ba ma maane we ko maŋe ko popone ko tiŋi Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Moses to wone, we Baŋa Wɛ ya pɛ Isarele tiina bam ni se ba chwi vwoa. Ba wó ma-ya ba di kuri bene maama chane serepɛ chana kam wone se ba taa zoore ya wone maŋa fenfee. 15Ba ta ma lɔre we ba jege se ba tɔɔle kwora Jerusalem ne de ba teene dedwonna ne ba bere nɔɔna bam maama we, “Diini-na zwonnu laŋa kam ne á gwoni Olivi teeni nɛ de se vɔɔro, de konkwara nɛ de se vɔɔro, de teeni dwi dwi nɛ selo na jege vɔɔro to. Laam ja-na tento maama á jwoori á ba á ma-te á chwi vwoa nenɛɛne Wɛ nia yam na bere tei to.”
16Nɔɔna bam ma seene ba beeri teeni nɛ de se vɔɔro ba ja ba jwoori ba sam. Ba laam ma tei pwei ba sam nayuni ne de ba konkwallo ne. Ba ma daare ba tei-se Wɛ diga kam konkɔlɔ kom ne, de kapworo kolo na maŋe de Na Ni dem to seeni, de kolo na maŋe de Efrayim Ni dem to seeni. 17Balo maama déem na nwoŋi kabɛɛne ne ba jwoori to mo tei pwei sem ye ba zo se wone. Ko na zege Nun bu Josua maŋa ne se ko yi maŋa kam konto to, Isarele tiina bam déem daa wo di kuri dem konto. Nɔɔna bam maama wo ma pwoli dedɛ.
18Ba déem kwei da yarepɛ mo ba di kuri dem. Dɛ maama wone, Ezera maa yeini o ga Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom wone o bere-ba. Da nana dɛ dem ne ba kɔgɔ kom maama ma gilimi daane Wɛ ŋwaane, nenɛɛne Wɛ ni dem na bere tei to.

english_text:
The People Confess Their Sins
1On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, the people of Israel went without eating, and they dressed in sackcloth and threw dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. 2They refused to let foreigners join them, as they met to confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors. 3For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
4Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God. 5Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said:
“Stand and shout praises
to your Lord,
the eternal God!
Praise his wonderful name,
though he is greater
than words can express.”
The People Pray
6You alone are the Lord,
Creator of the heavens
and all the stars,
Creator of the earth
and those who live on it,
Creator of the ocean
and all its creatures.
You are the source of life,
praised by the stars
that fill the heavens.
7 You are the Lord our God,
the one who chose Abram—
you brought him from Ur
in Babylonia
and named him Abraham.
8 Because he was faithful,
you made an agreement
to give his descendants
the land of the Canaanites
and Hittites,
of the Amorites and Perizzites,
and of the Jebusites
and Girgashites.
Now you have kept your promise,
just as you always do.
9 When our ancestors
were in Egypt,
you saw their suffering;
when they were at the Red Sea,
you heard their cry for help.
10 You knew that the King of Egypt
and his officials and his nation
had mistreated your people.
So you worked fearsome miracles
against the Egyptians
and earned a reputation
that still remains.
11 You divided the deep sea,
and your people walked through
on dry land.
But you tossed their enemies in,
and they sank down
like a heavy stone.
12 Each day you led your people
with a thick cloud,
and at night you showed the way
with a flaming fire.
13 At Sinai you came down
from heaven,
and you gave your people
good laws and teachings
that are fair and honest.
14You commanded them to respect
your holy Sabbath,
and you instructed
your servant Moses
to teach them your laws.
15 When they were hungry,
you sent bread from heaven,
and when they were thirsty,
you let water flow
from a rock.
Then you commanded them
to capture the land
that you had solemnly promised.
* 16 Our stubborn ancestors
refused to obey—
they forgot about the miracles
you had worked for them,
and they were determined
to return to Egypt
and become slaves again.
17 But, our God, you are merciful
and quick to forgive;
you are loving, kind,
and very patient.
So you never turned away
from them—
18 not even when they made
an idol shaped like a calf
and insulted you by claiming,
“This is the god who rescued us
from Egypt.”
19 Because of your great mercy,
you never abandoned them
in the desert.
And you always guided them
with a cloud by day
and a fire at night.
20Your gentle Spirit
instructed them,
and you gave them manna to eat
and water to drink.
21You took good care of them,
and for forty years
they never lacked a thing.
Their clothes didn't wear out,
and their feet were never swollen.
22 You let them conquer kings
and take their land,
including King Sihon of Heshbon
and King Og of Bashan.
23 You brought them into the land
that you had promised
their ancestors,
and you blessed their nation
with people that outnumbered
the stars in the sky.
24 Then their descendants
conquered the land.
You helped them defeat
the kings and nations
and treat their enemies
however they wished.
25 They captured strong cities
and rich farmland;
they took furnished houses,
as well as cisterns,
vineyards, olive orchards,
and numerous fruit trees.
They ate till they were satisfied,
and they celebrated
your abundant blessings.
26 In spite of this, they rebelled
and disobeyed your laws.
They killed your prophets,
who warned them
to turn back to you,
and they cursed your name.
27So you handed them over
to their enemies,
who treated them terribly.
But in their sufferings,
they begged you to help.
From heaven you listened
to their prayers
and because of your great mercy,
you sent leaders to rescue them.
28 But when they were at peace,
they would turn against you,
and you would hand them over
to their enemies.
Then they would beg for help,
and because you are merciful,
you rescued them
over and over again.
29 You warned them to turn back
and discover true life
by obeying your laws.
But they stubbornly refused
and continued to sin.
30 For years, you were patient,
and your Spirit warned them
with messages spoken
by your prophets.
Still they refused to listen,
and you handed them over
to their enemies.
31But you are merciful and kind,
and so you never forgot them
or let them be destroyed.
32 Our God, you are powerful,
fearsome, and faithful,
always true to your word.
So please keep in mind
the terrible sufferings
of our people, kings, leaders,
priests, and prophets,
from the time Assyria ruled
until this very day.
33You have always been fair
when you punished us
for our sins.
34Our kings and leaders,
our priests and ancestors
have never obeyed your commands
or heeded your warnings.
35You blessed them with a kingdom
and with an abundance
of rich, fertile land,
but they refused to worship you
or turn from their evil.
36Now we are slaves
in this fruitful land
you gave to our ancestors.
37Its plentiful harvest is taken
by kings you placed over us
because of our sins.
Our suffering is unbearable,
because they do as they wish
to us and our livestock.
The People Make an Agreement
38And so, a firm agreement was made that had the official approval of the leaders, the Levites, and priests.
translation_text:
Ba tɛ ba bere ba wɛleera jaja
1Chana kam konto da finlei-yana dɛ dem ne, mo Isarele tiina bam maama jeeri se ba vɔ ni. Ba déem zo gare-nyenyaaro mo, ye ba daare ba ke teero ba taare ba yuni se ko bere we ba wo chɔge. 2Isarele dwi tiina bam nam ya maŋe ba pwɛ ba tete de veira dwi maama mo. Ba maa zege wɛɛne ye ba tɛ jaja wɛleera yalo ba de ba nabaara na ke to. 3Ba ma zege da konto, ye ba ga Baŋa Wɛ nia yam tɔnɔ kom wone taa, nenɛɛne awa batɔ. Ba ma daare ba ke awa batɔ ba yɔɔre ba tɛ ba wɛleera jaja, ye ba zuli ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. 4Bimbini de de nateini déem zege da Levi tiina ŋwaane. Jesua, de Bani, de Kadimeli, de Sebania, de Bunni, de Serebia, de Bani wodwoŋi wom, dedaane Kenani na ye Levi tiina to ma zege de baŋa ne ba ware ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom de kwor-dɛa. 5Levi tiina badwonna ma pa nɔɔna bam maama baare se ba zuli Wɛ. Ko déem ye Jesua, de Kadimeli, de Bani, de Hasabenia, de Serebia, de Hodia, de Sebania, dedaane Petahia mo. Ba ma ta ba we:
“Zaŋe-na wɛɛne se dé tei dé Baŋa Wɛ wom! Wonto mo wora taa wuu!
Baŋa Wɛ, nmo yere dem tiini de jege nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ, pa se nɔɔna maama tei-de. Nɔɔna wó zeiŋi-de mo se ko dwoni woŋo maama.
6Dé Tu Wɛ, nmo yerane mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. N ma n ke wɛyuu dwi maama, de wɛ-baŋa chalechwe sem maama. Nmo mo ta ke tega baŋa, de naneero, de wonnu telo maama na wo te wone to. Nmo ma n pa nabiina de wonnu maama jege ŋwea. Wɛyuu maama wó tiiri ba zuli‑m mo.
7Nmo Baŋa Wɛ déem mo kuri dé nabaaro Abaram. N ma-n ja‑o n nwoŋi Babilonia tiina teo Uri ne, ye n daare n leiri o yere dem se de taa ye Abaraham. 8Nmo na nɛ we o jege chega de nmo to mo n gwoni ni ded‑o we, nmo wó pa‑o Kanaan tiina tega kam, de Hiti tiina tega, de Amori tiina tega, de Pɛrizi tiina tega, de Jebusi tiina tega, de Giragasi tiina te sem maama, se o dwi tiina taa zoore da. N ke n su n ni-gwonim dem konto, n na ye chega tu to ŋwaane.
9Nmo nam nɛ dé nabaara bam déem na yaare tei Ejipti wone, ye n daare n ni ba na keeri ba jare‑m tei Nane-soŋo kom ni ne to. 10N déem yɔɔre n ke wo-kenkagela mo ye n tɔge ya baŋa n pa se ko chɛ Ejipti Pa-faro wom yera, de o dedɛɛra de o teo kom tiina maama yera, n na yei ba na bɛɛse n nɔɔna bam tei to ŋwaane. Ko ta ma pa se nmo da ko ŋwaane n na yere kamunu, ye de ta wora de zem maama mo.
11Nmo déem tiŋi chwoŋa mo naneo kom tetare ne n pa n nɔɔna bam, pa se ba nɔne te-kora baŋa ne ba bɛ. Balo na pare-ba to maŋe naneo kom wone mo, nenɛɛne kandwa mo to ya maŋe na-luŋa wone tei.
12Nmo déem yeini n tɔge ba yiga mo ye á via. Wea ne n nye de kunkwoŋo na zege deiki to mo, ye tete ne n nye de mini se ba taa nae chwoŋa ba via. 13N nɔɔna bam déem na yi Sinayi peo kom to, mo n tu n yi ba tei, ye n daare n zege wɛyuu ne n ŋɔɔne de-ba. Nmo ma-n bere-ba chwei selo na lana to, ye n pa-ba nia yalo na jege chega to se ba taa tɔge-ya se ba ŋwea ke lam. 14N ma-n bere-ba se ba pɔɔre n siu dɛ dem ba pa‑m, se de taa ye de yera da yadwonna yam wone mo.
Nmo ta dɛ n tontoŋeno Moses baŋa mo, n pa-ba n nia yam. 15Kana déem na jege-ba to, n pɛ se wodiiru nwoŋi telaao ne pa ba di. N ta ma n pa se na nwoŋi peo wone, se ba nyɔ ba zuri ba na-nyɔm. Nmo ma n daare n pa-ba ni, se ba zo tega kalo n na gwoni ni se n pa-ba to wone, se ba taa tei-ka.
16Dé nabaara bam zwa déem nam kwareme mo, ye ba ta bere ba tete kamunim. Ba ma yɔɔre ba ve se ba sɛ nmo nia yam. 17Ba déem swei wo-kenkagela yalo n na ke ba tetare ne to mo ni ne, ye ba wo cheigi n taane dem. Ba wo-dɛɔ kom baŋa ne mo, ba déem kuri ba yiga tu se kotu ja-ba o jwoori Ejipti wone, se ba daa taa ye kabɛ da.
Nmo nam ye Wɛ wolo na kwei nɔɔna lwarem n yage n chɛ-ba to mo. N ma-n ye yibwon-dura tu, ye n swono gaale. N ma‑n yeini n peene n bane. N ŋwaŋa na daga to ŋwaane, n déem wo mɛ n kwaga n ya-ba.
18Ba déem tiini ba twe‑m. Ba mɔɔne jwoni mo na nye de na-mɔra to, ye ba we dento mo vere-ba de ja nwoŋi Ejipti wone. 19Ba déem nam na wo kagoa kam wone to, n wo yage ba yera, n ŋwaŋa kam na daga to ŋwaane. Wea ne mo n kunkwoŋo kom zege deiki ba yiga ne se ko bere-ba chwoŋa. Tete maama ne n mini dem maa yeini de pa-ba pwooni.
20Nmo ta pɛ-ba n Jwori-laao mo pa se ba yia poore. N ma n pa-ba Manna yam se ba di, ye n ta pa-ba na se ba zuri ba na-nyɔm. 21Bena finna yam ba na ke kagoa kam wone to, n zeini-ba pa se ba wo gɛ kolokolo. Ba gwaaro tem wo zareme, ye ba nɛ de wo foose chwoŋa kam cham ŋwaane.
22Nmo déem pɛ se ba di teene de pwa dedɛ. Ba tega siseini dem ma tole de yi yiga yiga. Ko ná ye Hesebon teo pɛ Sihon de Basan teo Pɛ Oga, ba jwoŋi banto tega kam maama ba tei.
23Nmo ta mo pɛ dé nabaara bam dwi dem puli dedɛ, nenɛɛne wɛyuu chalechwe sem na daga tei to. Nmo pɛ se ba bia bam di tega kalo n na gwoni ni de ba kwoa bam we ba jege se ba jwoŋi-ka ye ba laam zoore da to mo.
24N wane Kanaan tiina bam n zeili ba yiga ne pa se nmo nɔɔna bam zo ba tega kam ba tei. Nmo laam ma n pa n nɔɔna bam dam, se ba ke Kanaan tiina bam de ba pwa ba na lage tei to. 25Ba déem di teene delo na lɔge de pe to, de te-ywoŋa na ke wodiiru lanyerane to, de sam delo na su de wo-laaro dwi dwi to mo.
Ba yi da ba na vola yalo na koge ya tigi da to mo, de Vina teeni, de Olivi teeni, de teeni dwi dwi na leiri bia to, dedaane teeni kare. Ba ma yɔɔre ba di wodi-laaro ba su, pa se ba nu bigila bigila. Ba wo ma pwoli nmo lanyerane dem ŋwaane.
26De ko de, n nɔɔna bam se ba zwa mo ye ba lɔ n kwaga ne. Ba ma virigi ba kwaga ba ya n nia yam. Ba déem go n sampwori selo na kaane-ba se ba jwoori ba ba nmo tei ne to mo. Ba maa tiini ba twe‑m kuni dedɛ.
27Konto ŋwaane n ma n pa ba dona chwoŋa se ba di-ba ye ba daare ba bɛɛse-ba. Nmo nɔɔna bam nam na keeri ba jare‑m ba cham dem ŋwaane to, n zege wɛyuu ne mo n cheigi ba keira kam.
Nmo yibwon-dura kam ŋwaane mo n toŋe jwoŋina se ba jwoŋi-ba ba dona jeŋa ne ba yage. 28Ba wo maa na yeini ko to to, mo ba daa jwoori ba ke wɛleera, ye n daa‑n pa se ba dona bam di-ba. Ba de na chuli ba wɛleera yam, ye ba lwoori‑m ba cham dem ŋwaane to, nmo ta zege wɛyuu ne mo n cheigi-ba.
N déem jwoŋi-ba n yage kuni dedɛ wone, n yibwon-dura kam na gaale to ŋwaane. 29Nmo déem yeini n kaane-ba mo se ba taa yei n nia yam ni ne. Ba nam na bere ba tete kamunim to ŋwaane, mo ba ve nmo ni-kaana yam. Ba ma se ba zwa ye ba ve-ya, de ya na maŋe ya jege ŋwea ya pa wolo na tɔge-ya to de.
30Bene maama wone, nmo ta zuri n yera mo de-ba. N ma n pa n jworo tɔge n sampwori sem baŋa se ba ŋɔɔne de n nɔɔna bam ye ba kaane-ba. Ba nam na se ba zwa ye ba ve se ba cheigi to, nmo pɛ teene dedwonna tiina chwoŋa se ba di-ba. 31De ko maama de, nmo wo chɔge-ba naa n yage ba yera, nmo yibwon-dura na tiini ya daga to ŋwaane. Chega to, nmo tiini n jege nɔɔna ŋwaŋa dedɛ!
32Dé Tu Wɛ, nmo ye Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ kamunu, ye n kikia jege foone! Nmo tiini n jege chega mo se n yé yage n ni-gwonim de n swono kom. Nam yé swei dé yaara yam maama swia! Ko ná ye debam, de dé pwa, de dé yiga tiina, de dé kaanem tiina, de dé sampwori sem, ko ta woli de dé nabaara bam de n nɔɔna bam maama, debam maama tiini dé yaare mo, ko zege Asiria pwa bam na bɛɛse debam maŋa kalo ne to, se ko yi zem.
33Nmo nam yɔɔre n ke chega mo de n na ke debam tei to. Nmo wo n chega wone, se ko ye debam mo toŋe lwarem. 34Debam nabaara, de dé pwa bam, de dé yiga tiina bam, de dé kaanem tiina bam maama, ba toŋe ba tɔga n nia yam. Ba wolowolo wo cheigi n ni-kaana yam, naa ba sɛ nmo berem dem.
35Maŋa kalo ba déem na tei ba tete te-ywoŋa kalo n na pɛ-ba to wone, ye n nii ba baŋa ne lanyerane to, ba ta ve se ba yage wɛleera kikia, se ba daare ba zuli‑m.
36Laam nam nii! Dé ye kabɛ mo tega kanto n déem na kwei n pa dé nabaara bam to wone. Ka nam ya ye te-ywoŋa mo ka na pae debam wodi-laaro. 37Dé tega kam wo-laaro tem maama laam vei pwa balo n na pɛ chwoŋa se ba taa tei debam to tei ne mo. Debam na ke wɛleera to ŋwaane mo konto kea. Pwa bam konto maa jege debam tete, de dé vara, ba ke ba na lage tei to. Konto ma pa se dé cham dem laam kɛ jeŋa.”
Nɔɔna bam ke ni-sɛɛm
38“Tento maama na ke to ŋwaane mo debam Isarele dwi tiina bam maama sɛ se dé du duuri. Dé nam popone-de mo dé tiŋi, se dé yiga tiina zi ba je sem da. Dé Levi tiina bam, de dé kaanem tiina bam de je wó tɔge se zi da.”

english_text:
1As governor, I signed the agreement together with Zedekiah and the following priests: 2-8Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah, Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch, Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah.
9The Levites who signed were: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the clan of Henadad, Kadmiel, 10Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan, 11Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah, 12Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah, 13Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
14The leaders who signed were: Parosh, Pahath Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani, 15Bunni, Azgad, Bebai, 16Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin, 17Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur, 18Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai, 19Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai, 20Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir, 21Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua, 22Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah, 23Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub, 24Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek, 25Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah, 26Ahiah, Hanan, Anan, 27Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.
The Agreement
28-29All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
30 We won't let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
31 We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners.
Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
32 Once a year we will each donate a small amount of silver to the temple of our God. 33This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
34We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
35 Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
36 We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
37 To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil.
We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns. 38 A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom, 39which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers.
Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room.
We will not neglect the temple of our God.

de dé kaana bam,
de dé bia balo maama na jege yi-poro to.
29Debam maama mo tɔge de dé yiga tiina se dé gwoni ni dento dem:
Dé nam dugi we, dé wó sɛ Wɛ nia yalo o na dɛ o tontoŋeno Moses baŋa o pa debam to. Dé sɛ se dé tɔge debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ chwei sem de chullu telo maama o na bere debam to. Lɛɛro taa wo dé baŋa ne nenɛɛne dé ná wo ke konto.
30Dé pwooli we debam bu-baara bá kwei tega kanto bukwa ba ma ji ba kaana, debam de nam bá pa-ba dé bukwa se ba di ba ma ke ba kaana.
31Ko ná ye Wɛ siu dɛ dem, naa dé kura da yam ne, veira ná jaane ba zela ba ba se ba yeigi ba pa debam, dé bá ke pipiu de-ba.
Bena yarepɛ maama wone, bene dedoa mo dé wó yɔɔre dé yage dé kare se se peini se sii. Dé ta maa wó kwei dé chɛ balo na jege dé jena to.
32Dé nam wó fe dé tete se dé la sabu se dé kwei dé kwɛ Wɛ diga kam. Nɔɔno maama wó ŋwe sabu se ko maŋe dedaane sɛkɛle chichworo mo. 33Konto wó pa se zela yalo maama na maŋe de Wɛ diga kam totoŋa to taa wora maŋa maama: ko maa ye bworobworo kolo ba na tigisi Wɛ ŋwaane to mo, dedaane dɛ maama wone wodiu pɛɛra yam, de vara zwɛɛm pɛɛra yam, de Wɛ siu dɛ pɛɛra yam, de chan-doŋa pɛɛra yam, de kura yadwonna pɛɛra yam, de Isarele tiina wɛleera saarem pɛɛra yam, de pɛɛra yalo maama ba na wó ma ba zuli Wɛ to.
34Bene maama wone debam Isarele tiina bam, de dé kaanem tiina bam, de Levi tiina bam wó ta jɔrɔ se dé lɔre maŋa kalo sɔ-yuu de sɔ-yuu kolo na wó taa jaane dɛ ba tui Wɛ diga kam wone to. Ba wó yeini ba kwei dɛ sem konto ba ma zwɛ wonnu mo ba ke kaanem de Tu Baŋa Wɛ bimbini dem baŋa ne, nenɛɛne Wɛ nia yam na bere tei to.
35Dé ta gwoni ni we, bene maama wone dé wó yeini dé kuri dé kare wodiiru de dé teeni-bia balo na dɛ yiga ba ke to wone dé ja dé ba Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone. 36Dé ta wó ke Wɛ nia yam na bere tei to ye dé ja dé bu-kwe selo na ye baara to dé ba Wɛ diga kam wone se kaanem tiina balo na toŋe da to pɔɔre-ba Wɛ ŋwaane, se dé daare dé ja dé vare wo-bɛ kwe sem de dé ba dé pa Baŋa Wɛ. 37Debam ta wó ja dé kare wodiiru telo maama na bobo se te be to dé ba Wɛ diga kam wone. Ko ná ye muni, de mena, de teeni-bia, de Vini sa-doora, de Olivi tio nuga, dé wó kwei-te dé pa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam. Wodiiru telo maama dé na nɛ to, dé nam wó pɔɔre te fuga wone popɔra kam dé pa Levi tiina bam na wo dé teene dem wone to. Kokuri to, popɔra kam wora banto ŋwaane mo. 38Levi tiina ná yeini ba lage ba jwoŋi wodiiru popɔra kam konto, se Aron dwi dem kaanem tiina bam wone dedoa taa zege da o nia. Levi tiina bam laam wó le te fuga wone popɔra dedoa ba ja vo Jerusalem Wɛ diga kam ne ba tiŋi-te da. 39Konto to, Isarele tiina de Levi tiina bam ná yeini ba ja ba wodiiru pɛɛra, de ba Vini sa-doora pɛɛra, de ba Olivi nuga pɛɛra yam ba vo Wɛ diga kam ne, ba wó zege-te ka di sem wone mo, mɛ Wɛ diga totoŋa zela yam na wora to. Ko maa ye jei selo Wɛ kaanem tiina balo totoŋa maŋa na yi to, de Wɛ diga ni-yerena bam, de lein-leena bam na zoore to mo.
Dé bore we dé yiga wó taa wo Wɛ diga kam wone ye dé bá yage-ka.

english_text:
People Who Settled in Jerusalem
1The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there. 2Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
3 Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families.
The Judah Tribe
4-6From the Judah tribe, two leaders settled in Jerusalem with their relatives. One of them was Athaiah son of Uzziah. His ancestors were Zechariah, Amariah, Shephatiah, Mahalalel, and Perez, the son of Judah. From the descendants of Perez, 468 of the best men lived in Jerusalem.
The other leader from Judah was Maaseiah the son of Baruch. His ancestors were Colhozeh, Hazaiah, Adaiah, Joiarib, Zechariah, and Shelah, the son of Judah.
The Benjamin Tribe
7-8From the Benjamin tribe, three leaders settled in Jerusalem. The first was Sallu son of Meshullam, and the others were Gabbai and Sallai. Sallu's ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah. Altogether, there were 928 men of the Benjamin tribe living in Jerusalem. 9Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command.
Priests
10Four priests settled in Jerusalem. The first was Jedaiah; he was the son of Joiarib and the uncle of Jachin.
11The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest. 12Altogether, there were 822 from his clan who served in the temple.
The third priest to settle there was Adaiah son of Jeroham. His ancestors were Pelaliah, Amzi, Zechariah, Pashhur, and Malchijah. 13Altogether, there were 242 clan leaders among his relatives.
The fourth priest to settle there was Amashsai son of Azarel. His ancestors were Ahzai, Meshillemoth, and Immer. 14Altogether, there were 128 brave warriors from their clans, and their leader was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
Levites
15Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
16Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
17Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant.
Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
18Altogether, 284 Levites settled in the holy city.
Temple Guards and Others
19One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
20The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah. 21But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
22Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services, 23though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
24The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe.
The People in the Other Towns and Villages
25Some of the people of Judah lived in the following towns near their farms: Kiriath-Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel, 26Jeshua, Moladah, Beth-Pelet, 27Hazar-Shual, Beersheba, 28Ziklag, Meconah, 29Enrimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth, 30Zanoah, Adullam, Lachish, and Azekah. In fact, they settled the towns from Beersheba in the south to Hinnom Valley in the north.
31The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages, 32Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah, 33Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim, 34Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat, 35Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley. 36Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
translation_text:
Nɔɔna balo na tu ba taa zoore Jerusalem wone to
1Isarele yiga tiina bam déem ma ba ba zoore Jerusalem teo wone. Nɔɔna balo na daare to ma ta jɔrɔ se ba kuri balo de na wó vo ba taa zoore da to. Sam fuga maama wone ba ma le sɔŋɔ dedoa se ko nɔɔna bam vo ba taa zoore Jerusalem wone, se balo na daare to taa wo ba tete teene wone. 2Nɔɔna badaara bam wo ma da balo maama na sɛ se ba vo Jerusalem ba taa zoore da to.
3Judah kateiri dem yiga tiina balo na tu ba zoore Jerusalem wone to mo tento. Isarele tiina badaara déem maa zoore ba tete tega ne de ba teene dem wone, ko ná ye kaanem tiina, de Levi tiina, de Wɛ diga tontoŋena, de Solomon tontoŋena bia bam, 4se badaara na nwoŋi Judah dwi dem wone de Benjamin dwi dem wone to taa zoore Jerusalem wone.
Judah dwi dem yiga tiina balo na zoore Jerusalem wone to mo tento:
Yuzia bu Ataya.
O déem ta ye Zekaria naa mo, ye o nabaara bam ye Amaria, de Sefatia, de Mahalaleli. Nɔɔna bam konto maama déem ye Judah bu Pɛreza naaro mo.
5Baruki bu Maaseya.
O déem ta ye Kola-Hozɛ naa mo, ye o nabaara bam ye Hazaya, de Adaya, de Joyariba, dedaane Zekaria. Nɔɔna bam konto maama maa ye Judah bu Sela naaro.
6Pɛreza dwi tiina balo déem na zoore Jerusalem wone to ye baara bia yana de fuseredo-nana (468) mo. Ba maa ye babɛ.
7Benjamin dwi tiina bam mo tento:
Mesulam bu Saalu.
O déem ta ye Joyedi naa mo, ye o nabaara bam ye Pedaya, de Kolaya, de Maaseya, de Iteli, dedaane Jesaya.
8Saalu chorro Gabayi de Salayi.
Benjamin dwi tiina balo na zoore Jerusalem wone to maama déem ye baara bia nogo de finlei-nana (928) mo. 9Zikiri bu Joweli déem mo ye ba yiga tu, ye Hasenua bu Judah saŋe o tei ba teo jei sem.
10Kaanem tiina bam mo tento:
Joyariba bu Jedaya, de Jakin.
11Hilikia bu Seraya.
O déem ye Mesulam naa mo, ye o nabaara bam ye Zadoki, de Merayofa, dedaane kaanem yiga tu Ahituba.
12Banto de ba tontoŋena dwonna balo na toŋe Wɛ diga kam totoŋa to déem ye baara bia nana de finlei-balei (822) mo.
Jeroham bu Adaya.
O déem ta ye Pelalia naa mo, ye o nabaara bam ye Amezi, de Zekaria, de Pasura, dedaane Malakija.
13Adaya dedaane o chorro tem déem ye baara bia yalei de finna-balei (242) mo.
Azareli bu Amasesayi.
O déem ye Ahazayi naa mo, ye o nabaara bam ye Mesilemofa, dedaane Yimera.
14Amasesayi de o chorro tem maa ye baara bi de finlei-nana (128). Ba maa ye babɛ na yei jara-keim chekke to. Ba yiga tu déem mo ye Hagedolim bu Zabideli.
15Levi tiina bam mo tento:
Hasubi bu Semaya.
O déem ta ye Azerikam naa mo, ye o nabaara bam ye Hasabia de Bunni.
16Sabetayi, de Jozabadi.
Banto déem ye Levi tiina bam yiga tiina mo ye ba nii Wɛ diga kam pwooni yiga totoŋa baŋa ne.
17Mika bu Matania.
O déem ta ye Zabidi naa mo. O nabaaro maa ye Asaf. Matania déem mo tɔge Wɛ diga lein-leena bam yiga pa se ba leeni lei-keim lei de wɛ-lworo lei.
Bakabukia.
Wonto déem saŋe Matania kwaga mo o dwonna bam wone.
Sammua bu Abeda.
O ta ye Galale naa mo, ye o nabaaro ye Jedutuna.
18Levi tiina balo maama déem na vei ba zoore Jerusalem wone to ye baara bia yalei de funɔnɔ-bana (284) mo.
19Wɛ diga ni-yerena bam mo tento:
Akuba, de Talemon.
Ba de ba tontoŋena dwonna bam déem ye baara bi de fuserepɛ-balei (172) mo.
20Ko nam ná ye Isarele tiina, de ba kaanem tiina, de ba Levi tiina balo na daare to, banto déem zoore Judah teene dem maama wone mo, ba tete nabaara tega kam baŋa ne.
21Wɛ diga tontoŋena bam déem maa zoore Jerusalem kateiri delo yere na ye Ofeli to ne mo. Ziha dedaane Gisepa maa ye ba yiga tiina.
22Levi tiina bam yiga tu wolo déem na tɔge o zoore Jerusalem wone to mo ye Bani bu Yuzi. O déem ta ye Hasabia naa mo, ye o nabaara bam ye Matania, de Mika. Yuzi nwoŋi Asaf sɔ-yuu kom ne mo. Banto nam mo jege se ba taa leeni Wɛ diga kam lei maama. 23Pɛ wom nam ya pɛ lein-leena bam ni mo, se de taa bere-ba ba dɛ maama totoŋa na wó taa ye tei to.
24Mesezabela bu Petahia maa wo pɛ wom tei ne se o pa Isarele tiina bam ba wonnu maama. O ye Judah bu Zera dwi dem nɔɔno mo.
Teene delo na kaare Jerusalem to
25Nɔɔna bam badaara déem maa zoore teene dedwonna wone, ye ba kare bwola da. Judah dwi tiina badwonna déem maa zoore Kiriaf-Araba ne, de Dibon ne, de Jekabazeeli ne, dedaane de nawuura yam wone. 26Ba ta maa zoore Jesua ne, de Molada ne, de Bɛte-Peleta ne, 27de Hazara-Suwala ne, de Beeriseba de ko nawuura yam wone. 28Ba badwonna ta zoore Zikalag ne, de Mekona de ko nawuura yam wone, 29de En-Rimon ne, de Zora ne, de Jaremuf ne, 30de Zanoa ne, de Adulam ne, de teene dem konto nawuura yam wone. Ba ta maa zoore Lakisi ne, de kare selo na bwola da to wone. Badwonna maa zoore Azeka de ko nawuura yam wone. Ko maa bere we Judah tiina bam déem zoore laŋa kalo na tigi Beeriseba ne, se ko taa vei Hinom bwolo kom seeni to mo.
31Ko ná ye Benjamin dwi tiina bam, ba déem zoore Geba teo ne, de Mikimasa ne, de Ayija ne, de Bɛtel de ko nawuura yam wone, 32de Anatofe ne, de Nobi ne, de Anania ne, 33de Hazora ne, de Rama ne, de Gitayim ne, 34de Hadida ne, de Zeboyim ne, de Nebalate ne, 35de Loda ne, de Ono ne, dedaane Gwaro bwolo kom ne mo.
36Ba déem ma pa se Levi dwi dem sɔ-yuni tedwonna ya na zoore Judah kateiri dem ne to vo ba zoore de Benjamin tiina bam.

english_text:
A List of Priests and Levites
1Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, 2Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, 3Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth, 4Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah, 5Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah, 6Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah, 7Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
8The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise, 9while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses.
Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
10Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada. 11Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua.
Leaders of the Priestly Clans
12When Joiakim was high priest, the following priests were leaders of their clans: Meraiah of the Seraiah clan, Hananiah of Jeremiah, 13Meshullam of Ezra, Jehohanan of Amariah, 14Jonathan of Malluchi, Joseph of Shebaniah, 15Adna of Harim, Helkai of Meraioth, 16Zechariah of Iddo, Meshullam of Ginnethon, 17Zichri of Abijah, Piltai of Moadiah, 18Shammua of Bilgah, Jehonathan of Shemaiah, 19Mattenai of Joiarib, Uzzi of Jedaiah, 20Kallai of Sallai, Eber of Amok, 21Hashabiah of Hilkiah, and Nethanel of Jedaiah.
The Priestly and Levite Families
22During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families. 23However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
24Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
25Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
26All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest.
Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
27When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments. 28-29The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth. 30The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
31I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate. 32Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them. 33Then came the priests Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, 34Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah, 35all of them blowing trumpets. Next, there was Zechariah of the Asaph clan 36and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law. 37When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
38The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall, 39Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard, 40where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders, 41as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets. 42Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers. 43God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem.
Preparation for Worship
44On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites.
Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites, 45 when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon. 46In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship. 47During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_text:
Kaanem tiina de Levi tiina bam yera
1Kaanem tiina de Levi tiina balo na tɔge de Selateli bu Zerubabel, dedaane kaanem yiga tu Jesua ba jwoori Judah kateiri dem ne to mo tento:
Wɛ Kaanem tiina:
Seraya, de Jeremia, de Ezera, 2de Amaria, de Maluki, de Hatusi, 3de Sekania, de Rehum, de Meremofa, 4de Ido, de Ginetoni, de Abija, 5de Mijamina, de Mowadia, de Biliga, 6de Semaya, de Joyariba, de Jedaya, 7de Saalu, de Amoki, de Hilikia, dedaane Jedaya.
Jesua maŋa kam ne, nɔɔna bam konto déem mo ye ba dwonna kaanem tiina bam yiga tiina.
Levi tiina:
8Jesua, de Binnui, de Kadimeli, de Serebia, de Judah, dedaane Matania. Matania de o dwonna déem mo tei se ba taa nii lei-keim lei sem baŋa ne.
9Ko daare Bakabukia de Yunni de ba dwonna mo sɛ lei sem.
10Jesua déem mo ye Joyakim kwo, Joyakim maa ye Eliasibi kwo, Eliasibi maa ye Joyada kwo, 11Joyada maa ye Jonatan kwo, Jonatan maa ye Jadua kwo. 12Joyakim maŋa kam ne, nɔɔna banto déem mo nii kaanem tiina bam sɔ-yuni tem baŋa ne:
Meraya déem mo nii Seraya di sem.
Hanania ma nii Jeremia di sem.
13Mesulam ma nii Ezera di sem.
Jehohanan ma nii Amaria di sem.
14Jonatan ma nii Maluki di sem.
Josefa ma nii Sekania di sem.
15Adana ma nii Harim di sem.
Helikayi nii Meremofa di sem.
16Zekaria ma nii Ido di sem.
Mesulam ma nii Ginetoni di sem.
17Zikiri ma nii Abija di sem.
Pilitayi ma nii Minamina di sem de Mowadia di sem.
18Sammua ma nii Biliga di sem.
Jehonatan ma nii Semaya di sem.
19Matenayi ma nii Joyariba di sem.
Yuzi ma nii Jedaya di sem.
20Kalayi ma nii Salayi di sem.
Ebera ma nii Amoki di sem.
21Hasabia ma nii Hilikia di sem.
Netaneli ma nii Jedaya di sem.
22Maŋa kalo ne Eliasibi, de Joyada, de Johanan, dedaane Jadua na jigi kaanem yiga tiina ba leiri daane to, mo ba pɛ se ba popone kaanem tiina de ba di sem yera wonnu ba tiŋi twanno wone. Ba déem ke konto se ko taa vei Darusi na tu o ji Peresia teo pa-faro to mo. 23Ko daare ko ná ye Levi tiina bam de ba di sem yera wonnu, ba popone tento ba tiŋi ba teo kom lonne twanno wone se ko taa vei Eliasibi bu Johanan maŋa ne mo.
Wɛ diga kam totoŋa na pɔɔre tei to
24Levi tiina bam yiga tiina déem ye Hasabia, de Serebia, de Jesua, de Binnui de Kadimeli mo. Banto ma nii Wɛ tia de lei-keim lei sem baŋa ne ye ba dwonna bam zege ba jeeri-ba se ba taa leeni ba sɛ-se, nenɛɛne Wɛ tontoŋeno David déem na bere-ba se ba taa ke tei to.
25Wɛ diga ni-yerena bam déem ye Matania, de Bakabukia, de Obadia, de Mesulam, de Talemon, dedaane Akuba mo. Banto totoŋe mo ye se ba taa yere zela di sem na wo Wɛ diga kam bworru tem seeni to.
26Levi tiina bam konto déem toŋe Wɛ diga kam totoŋa Joyakim na ye Jesua bu de Jozadaki naa to maŋa ne mo. Ba ta toŋe maŋa kalo ne Nehemia na ye teo kom dedɛɛro, ye Ezera ye Wɛ kaanem tu, ye o ta ye Wɛ nia zamesem tu to mo.
Ba kwei Jerusalem kabira kam ba pa Wɛ
27Ba déem na ti yiga se ba kwei Jerusalem kabira kam ba ke Wɛ jeŋa ne to, mo ba toŋe ba bwoŋi Levi tiina bam se ba zege ba na wo mɛ maama ne to ba ba. Ba ma kwei zwe, de kwanno dwi dwi mo ba tɔge ba di ywoni dem, ye ba leeni Wɛ lei-keim lei. 28-29Levi tiina lein-leena bam déem zoore Jerusalem nawuura yam wone, de Netofa teo kom seeni, de Bɛte-Giligal ne, de Geba ne, de Azimavefa ne mo. Ba de ma zege ba ya na zoore mɛ maama ne to ba ba Jerusalem. 30Kaanem tiina bam, de Levi tiina bam déem ma toŋe kolo na wó kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane, ye ba daare ba kwɛ nɔɔna bam, de teo kom bworru, de ko kabiri sem maama.
31Amo laam ma pa ni se Judah kateiri yiga tiina bam di ba zege kabira kam yuu ne. A ta ma beeri lein-leena dedɛ a pɔɔre-ba kuni belei, se ba taa vei ba kaare teo kom mo ye ba leeni ba ke Wɛ lei. Ba kɔgɔ dedoa ma tɔge kabira kam jazem seeni ba vo Tampuuri Ni dem seeni. 32Hosaya dedaane Judah yiga tiina bam chichworo kom ma tɔge lein-leena bam kwaga. 33Azaria, de Ezera, de Mesulam, 34de Judah, de Benjamin, de Semaya, de Jeremia, de maa tɔge da. 35Kaanem tiina badwonna de na zei nabwanno to ma saŋe banto de kwaga. Jonatan bu Zekaria de daa ma saŋe. Wonto déem ye Semaya naa mo, ye o nabaara déem ye Matania, de Mikaya, de Zakura, de Asaf. 36Zekaria chorro telo na tɔge ded‑o to mo tento: Semaya, de Azareli, de Milalayi, de Gilalayi, de Maayi, de Netaneli, de Judah, dedaane Hanani. Banto maama déem zei kwɛɛra zela yalo maama Wɛ tontoŋeno David déem na pɛ ni se ba taa ma-ya ba zuli Wɛ to mo. Wɛ nia zamesem tu Ezera déem ma tɔge kɔgɔ kom maama yiga. 37Ba déem ma vo ba yi Buli-yi Ni dem, ye ba yɔɔre ba vo ba dɔɔle ba di David teo kom ne. Ba ta ma vo ba gaale David sɔ-fɔrɔ kom na zege mɛ to, ye ba laam tole ba vo ba yi teo kom wɛ-puli seeni mɛ kabira kam na vei ka tɔ de Na Ni dem to.
38Lein-leena kɔgɔ kodwoŋi kom ma tɔge kabira kam jagwia seeni ba via. Amo de ma tɔge ba kwaga, dedaane nɔɔna bam chichworo. Dé ma vo dé gaale Jugu di-dedɔrɔ kom dé vo dé yi Kabiri-kayɔlɔ kom seeni. 39Dé zege dáane dé vo dé gaale Efrayim Ni dem mo, de Jesana Ni dem, de Ywona Ni dem, de Hananeli di-dedɔrɔ kom, de Wonnu Bi di-dedɔrɔ kom, dé ta vo dé yi Pei Ni dem. Dé laam ma vo dé yi Wɛ diga Yerena ni dem dé zege da.
40Lein-leena popɔre selei sem laam ma vo ba zege Wɛ diga kam wone. Amo dedaane yiga tiina bam chichworo de ma vo dé zege da. 41Kaanem tiina banto de déem nam mo tɔge ba zege de amo, ye ba jege nabwanno ba wui:
Eliakim, de Maaseya, de Minamina, de Mikaya, de Elio-enayi, de Zekaria, dedaane Hanania.
42Nɔɔna banto de déem mo tɔge ba wora:
Maaseya, de Semaya, de Eleaza, de Yuzi, de Jehohanan, de Malakija, de Elam, dedaane Ezere.
Ko déem ye Jezerahia mo to lein-leena bam yiga pa se ba leeni de kwor-dɛa ba ke Wɛ lei. 43Dɛ dem konto ne, ba ma ke kaanem dedɛ ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Nɔɔna bam de ma tiini ba di ywoni se ko gaale, Wɛ na pɛ se ba wo pwoli to ŋwaane. Kaana bam de ba bia maama de ma nwoŋi ba tɔge ba di ywoni dem, pa se de sɔɔ kom zaŋe wɛɛne ko yi yiga yiga.
Wɛ tontoŋena bam ni-wodiu taane
44Dɛ dem konto ne ba déem ma kuri nɔɔna se ba taa nii Wɛ diga zela di sem de se wonnu tem baŋa ne. Ba déem yeini ba kwaleme Wɛ teiri dem, de da-yiga mena yam, de da-yiga tio-bia pɛɛra yam, de pɛɛra yalo maama nɔɔna na pɛ Wɛ diga totoŋa yam ŋwaane to mo. Ba maa wó vo Isarele tiina kare sem na wo ba teene dem maama wone to ba jwoŋi wodiiru telo Wɛ nia yam na pɛ chwoŋa se kaanem tiina de Levi tiina bam jwoŋi to. Judah tiina bam maama wo déem tɔge de kaanem tiina bam de Levi tiina bam kikia mo. 45Kolo ŋwaane, banto déem seene yia mo ba toŋe chullu de kwɛɛm totoŋa yam Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ba se ba ke to. Lein-leena bam, de Wɛ diga ni-yerena bam de ma toŋe ba totoŋa se ko tɔge de nia yalo Pɛ David de o bu Solomon na bere-ba se ba taa ke to. 46Ko nam na zege Pɛ David dedaane Asaf maŋa kam ne to, mo ba le nɔɔna se ba yeini ba tɔge lein-leena bam yiga se ba taa leeni ba tei Wɛ, ye ba daare ba ke o lei. 47Ko daa ta na yi Zerubabel maŋa kam ne dedaane Nehemia maŋa kam ne to, Isarele tiina bam maa yeini ba kuri ba wodiiru tem wone ba pae lein-leena bam de Wɛ diga ni-yerena bam dɛ maama se ko woli-ba ba totoŋa baŋa ne. Ba ta maa yeini ba le popɔra kalo na maŋe de Levi tiina badaara bam to mo ba pa-ba. Levi tiina de laam maa yeini ba le popɔra kalo na ye kaanem tiina bam nyem to ba pa-ba.

english_text:
Foreigners Are Sent Away
1 On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God. 2 This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them.
