However, our God turned the curse into a blessing. 3Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors.
Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
4The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms. 5So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
6This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king 7to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple. 8It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture. 9Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
10 I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest. 11I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs. 12 After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom. 13Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
14I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there.
The Sabbath
15 I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath. 16People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath. 17I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath! 18Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
19I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath. 20Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods. 21But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath. 22I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy.
God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this.
Mixed Marriages
23 I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. 24About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language. 25So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise:
In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners. 26 God dearly loved King Solomon of Israel and made him the greatest king on earth, but Solomon's foreign wives led him into sin. 27So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
28 Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
29I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
30Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites. 31I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple.
I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_text:
Ba na sɛ ba tɔge Wɛ nia yam tei to
1Dɛ dem konto ne mo ba gage Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom Moses na popone to. Ba na cheigi taane dem to mo ba maane we ko chula se Amon tu, de Moaba tu tɔge ba zo Wɛ nɔɔna kɔgɔ kom wone. 2Kokuri to, maŋa kalo Isarele tiina bam déem na nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba beeri jeiŋa jei to, Amon tiina de Moaba tiina bam wo jeeri-ba chwoŋa ne ba pa-ba na se ba nyɔ. Ba ma jwoori ba pa Balaam sabu, se o wane o sɔɔle lwarem o yage Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. Dé Tu Wɛ wom ma pipiri o sensɔla kam pa se ko ke debam lam. 3Isarele tiina bam na nigi Wɛ ni dem konto to, mo ba le nɔn-gongwaaga ba wone, se ba daa yé taa zoore de-ba.
Nehemia kwɛ nɔɔna bam de ba totoŋa
4Konto maama de Wɛ kaanem tu Eliasibi déem mo nii Wɛ diga zela di sem baŋa ne. O maa me de Amon tu Tobia. 5O ma da ko ŋwaane o kwei Wɛ diga zela di-kamunu o pa Tobia. Ba nam ya yeini ba kwei wodiu pɛɛra, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa, de Wɛ diga zela yam, de Wɛ teiri delo na ye mena, de sana, de Olivi nuga to mo ba zege da. Pɛɛra yam konto maama ye se ba taa kwei-ya ba pae Levi tiina bam, de Wɛ diga lein-leena dedaane ni-yerena bam mo, ko woli de pɛɛra yalo na ye kaanem tiina bam nyem to.
6Konto maama déem na ke to, dedaane amo daa tere Jerusalem wone. A ya jwoori a vo Babilonia se a lwoni kolo na ke to mo a bere Pɛ Atazeregese. Ko maa ye o paare dim bena fintɔ-yalei bene dem ne mo a via. Ko nam na ke fee to mo a daa lwoori chwoŋa o tei ne, 7se a jwoori a vo Jerusalem. A na yi da to, a nɛ we Eliasibi toŋe wo-balɔrɔ ye o yage chwoŋa o pa Tobia se o taa zoore Wɛ diga di sem dedoa wone. 8Keim dem na tiini de fuli a wo to, mo a zo da a kwaleme Tobia zela yam a dole a yage pwooni ne. 9A ma daare a pa ni se ba jwoori ba kwɛ di sem se ko tɔge dé chullu tem, ye a pa ba jwoori ba kwei Wɛ diga zela yam ba ba ba zege se wone. A ta ma pa ni se ba taa jaane mena pɛɛra yam, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa kam ba tui ba zege diga kam wone.
10A ta ma lɔre we ba wo pɛ Levi tiina bam wodiiru tem popɔra kalo na ye ba nyem to. Ko déem pɛ se Wɛ diga lein-leena bam, de Levi tiina badaara bam nwoŋi da Jerusalem teo kom ne, ye ba jwoori ba vo ba wo ba kare totoŋa ne. 11Amo ma bwɛ yiga tiina bam lanyerane ye a bwei-ba a we, “Bɛ mo ye á dole Wɛ diga kam totoŋa yam á yage?” A ma pa se Wɛ diga tontoŋena bam jwoori ba toŋe ba totoŋa yam.
12Judah tiina bam daa ma jwoori ba jaane ba Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra maama ba tui ba zege Wɛ diga wone, ko ná ye ba mena popɔra, de ba sana popɔra, de ba nuga popɔra kam. 13Amo laam ma kwei Wɛ diga zela di sem de se totoŋa yam a ke nɔɔna banto jeŋa ne. Ko maa ye Wɛ kaanem tu Selemia, de Wɛ nia zamesem tu Zadoki, de Levi tu Pedaya. A ta le Zakura bu Hanan mo se o taa woli-ba. Nɔɔna maa pae we nɔɔna bam konto jege chega. Ba totoŋa maa ye se ba taa chɛ wodiiru tem ba pa ba dwonna bam.
14Amo Tu Wɛ, nam guli se n ke-ne lanyerane, a na ke wonnu tento maama to ŋwaane. Yé swei amo na tɔge chega a kwɛ nmo diga kam se ka taa jege zula tei to ni ne.
15Kanto maŋa ne mo a ta maane we Judah tiina badwonna yeini ba toŋe ba totoŋa Wɛ siu dɛ dem wone. Nɔɔna maa kare ba ŋoke Vini tio-bia nyoa. Badwonna maa zeŋe ba bonɛ de wodiiru zela, de teeni bia dwi dwi ba jaane ba zoore Jerusalem teo wo se ba yeiga. Amo ma kaane-ba se ba yé taa di yaga Wɛ siu dɛ dem ne. 16Tura tiina badwonna na tu ba zoore Jerusalem teo ne to de ma jaane ywona dedaane zela dwi dwi ba tui ba yeigi ba pae Judah tiina bam Wɛ siu dɛ dem ne. 17A ma bwɛ Judah yiga tiina bam lanyerane ye a we, “Nii-na á na tiini á toŋe lwarem tei! Abam yɔɔre á chɔge Wɛ siu dɛ dem mo pa se de ye kafɛ. 18Á nabaara bam déem maŋe ba ke konto mo, pa se Wɛ ja chɔgem o ba dé teo konto baŋa ne. Abam daa ta ma‑á yɔɔre á ke kolo na wó pa se Wɛ bane zaŋe debam Isarele tiina baŋa ne de woli da to mo, de á na jege o siu dɛ dem á chɔge to.”
19A ma pa ni we wɛ-zoore maŋa ne se ba yeini ba pe teo kom ni bworru tem, se ko maŋe de siu dɛ dem boboa maŋa. A ma ta-ba se ba yé pore-te ba yage ko ná dae siu dɛ dem na ti maŋa kalo to. A déem ta pɛ se a tontoŋena mo zege teo kom bworru ni ne ba yere, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé ja o zela o ba teo kom Wɛ siu dɛ dem ne se o yeigi. 20Ko ná yeini ko wora ko wora, pipim-piina badaara yeini ba vei tete ne ba tigi teo bworru tem kwaga ne mo, ye ba cheiga se siu dɛ dem yi. 21Amo de maa kaane-ba a we, “Bɛ mo ye á ke konto dwoŋi? Abam ná jwoori á ba ywo-seeni á tigi se tega ba ka poore, amo wó ja abam de dam mo.” Ko na zege dɛ dem a na tage-ba konto to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa wo tu se o ke pipiu Wɛ siu dɛ dem ne. 22A laam ma pa Levi tiina bam ni se ba kwɛ ba tete, se ba daare ba vo ba taa zege ba yere teo bworru tem. A ke konto se ko pa se Wɛ siu dɛ dem seene de taa ye de yera mo.
A Tu Wɛ, guli amo gula keim dento de ŋwaane. Tɔge nmo swono kom baŋa n duri amo yibwona.
23Ka maŋa ne mo a ta maane we Judah tiina baara bam dedɛ vei ba di Asedodi tiina bukwa, de Amon tiina bukwa, de Moaba tiina bukwa mo ba ke ba kaana. 24Ko ma pa se bia balo ba na loge to chichworo jege Asedodi taane ba ŋɔɔna, ye badwonna jege ta-gɛ ba ŋɔɔna. Ba maa ware se ba ŋɔɔne debam Judah tiina taane dem. 25A ma tiini a bwɛ baara bam konto, ye a daare a sɔɔle lwarem a yage ba yuu ne. A ta mage-ba ye a ja ba yu-ywei mo a vaŋe a vuuri. A ma daare a pa se ba ma Wɛ yere ba du duuri ye a we, “Abam daa yé kwei-na á bukwa á pa dwi-gɛ tiina. Nam yé lage-na dwi-gɛ tiina bukwa á pa á tete naa á bia bam se á di. 26Dwi-gɛ tiina kaana déem mo pɛ se Pɛ Solomon ke wɛleere. Pɛ déem nam tere teene dedwonna ne o na mae dedaane wonto. Wɛ tete déem yɔɔre o swoi‑o mo pa se o ji Isarele tiina bam maama pɛ. De konto maama de, dwi-gɛ tiina kaana bam pɛ se o tusi Wɛ yiga ne. 27Abam nam ta lage se dé maama da á keim-balɔrɔ kom baŋa ne dé vo dé swo dwi-gɛ tiina bukwa se ba taa ye dé kaana mo na? Dé bá sɛ se dé ve Wɛ ni dem konto!”
28Joyada déem ye Wɛ kaanem yiga tu Eliasibi bu mo, ye wonto de bu dedoa laam vo o di Horon tu Sanbalati bukɔ o ma ke o kaane. Amo déem ma zeili‑o se o daa yé taa zoore Jerusalem teo wone.
29Amo Tu Wɛ, guli nɔɔna banto gula de ba na yɔɔre ba jege kaanem totoŋe dem yuu ba yaala tei to. Ba ma daare ba chɔge ni-gwonim delo nmo déem na ke dedaane kaanem tiina de Levi tiina bam to.
30Amo déem kwɛ nɔɔna bam mo, pa se ba pwɛ ba tete dedaane wo-yɔɔro dwi maama. A ta ke nia mo a tiŋi se kaanem tiina de Levi tiina bam maama taa yei ba totoŋa na ye tei to, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé lɛɛne wodwoŋi totoŋa. 31Amo ma pa se nɔɔna jaane dɛ ba tui ba tiŋi Wɛ diga kam wone, nenɛɛne maŋa kam ná yeini ka yi se ba ke konto. A ta ma pa se ba jaane da-yiga wodiiru telo na bege to ba tui ba ke da.
Amo Tu Wɛ, nam guli amo gula, se n ke-ne lanyerane.

english_text:
Queen Vashti Disobeys King Xerxes
1-2 King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. 3During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came. 4For 180 days he showed off his wealth and spent a lot of money to impress his guests with the greatness of his kingdom.
5At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens. 6The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
7The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous 8and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
9While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
10By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas, 11to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was. 12The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
13-14The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
15The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
16Then Memucan told the king and the officials:
Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
17The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?” 18Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
19Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
20When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
21King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said, 22and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_text:
Ka-pɛ Vasiti gɛ o paare
1Wonnu tento maama déem ke te maŋe de Pɛ Zeregese na di paare to mo. Pɛ wom konto laŋa kam pɔɔre kuni bi de finlei-berepɛ (127) mo, ka zege India ne se ka yi Etiopia. 2Ka te-fɔrɔ kom maa ye Susa, pɛ wom na di o paare dem ko dam jei sem ne to. 3O paare dim bena yatɔ maŋa ne mo Zeregese déem ke kuri-fɔrɔ o pa o nakwa, de o teo kom naduna maama. O ta ma bwoŋi Peresia de Media jar-keira babɛ sem, dedaane dedɛɛra balo na nii o laŋa kam popɔre sem to, se ba maama da ba jeeri kuri dem ne. 4Balo o déem na bwoŋi to o kwei chane seredo mo o ma o bere o paare dem na tiini de jege nenɔŋa tei, de o sɔŋɔ kom jejegero na daga tei to. 5Konto kwaga ne mo Pɛ Zeregese ta kwei da yarepɛ o ke kuri-fɔrɔ o pa nɔɔna balo maama na zoore Susa dam jei sem wone to. O ma bwoŋi naduna de nabwona se ba maama jeeri pɛ sɔŋɔ kapworo kom ne, teeni na wora to. 6Ba déem kwɛ kapworo kom mo dedaane gare-fefale selo nyenyero na ye napwonnu de nazwon-pupwia to. Ywoa yalo ba na mɛ pe-siswollu ba ke to maa wora. Ba laam ma kwei gare-ŋon-nyenno dwi dwi ba ma vɔ gwaaro tem de lu-nyenno kwana se te lei ywoa yam yera ne. Ba ta ma kwei kandwa-nyenno dwi dwi ba ma kwɛ kapworo kom tega kam, ye ba daare ba kwei sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno ba ma fɔge ba kwɛ yitunnu ba tiŋi jei sem ne se nɔɔna jeini te baŋa ne. 7Ba déem jege sabu-seŋa zwe na ye yera yera to mo ba nyɔ sana se wone. Pɛ wom wo-ywoŋo kom ŋwaane o déem pɛ se sana bam daga ba yi nɔɔna bam maama. 8O ma pa o tontoŋena bam ni se ba taa pae sana se ko tɔge nɔɔno maama na lage tei to.
9Pɛ Zeregese na ke tei de baara bam konto to, o kaane Vasiti de ya jege kuri mo pɛ sɔŋɔ jei sedwonna ne o ke o pae kaana bam. 10Kuri dem da yarepɛ dim dɛ ne, mo pɛ wom wo tiini ko pwoli de sa-nyɔre. O ma bwoŋi o dedɛɛra barepɛ balo na toŋe ba pa‑o to se ba ba o tei. Banto maa ye: Mehuman, de Bizefa, de Harebona, de Bigeta, de Abagata, de Zetare, ko woli de Kakase. 11O ma pa-ba ni se ba vo ba ta o kaane Vasiti we, o kwei o ka-pɛ yipuga kam o pu, se ba laam ja‑o ba ba o tei. Vasiti na ye ka-laao to ŋwaane, pɛ wom ya lage se o nakwa de o nɔɔna bam maama na we o lam tiini de gaale. 12Pɛ wom tontoŋena bam na vei de o ni dem to, Vasiti ma ve se o vo o tei. Pɛ wom bane ma tiini de zaŋe ye o ware o tete se o ja.
13Keim dem konto dwoŋi ná kea, Pɛ wom yeini o bwoŋi swa tiina balo na yei chega to, se o lɔre ba teo chullu tem na bere o na wó ke tei se lanyerane taa wora to. 14O déem ma ja taane dem o yi swa tiina balo na tiini ba me ded‑o to. Karesena mo konto, de Sefare, de Ademata, de Tarasisi, de Meresi, de Masena, dedaane Memukan. Nɔɔna barepɛ bam konto déem mo ye naduna Peresia dedaane Media laŋa kam ne ba dwoi nɔɔna maama.
15O ma bwei-ba o we, “Amo toŋe a bwoŋi ka-pɛ Vasiti mo ye o ve se o ba. Dé teo chullu tem nam bere se a ke‑o tetɛ mo?”
16Memukan ma leiri Pɛ wom o we, “Ka-pɛ Vasiti na ke o chɔge tei to, o wo ke o ma o twe Pɛ wom yerane. Ko ye debam balo na ye nmo nakwa bam to mo o gwooni, ko woli de balo maama na zoore nmo paare jei sem ni maama ne to. 17O keim dem ná to kaana bam maama zwa ne, ba de daa bá taa nege ba banna ye ba wó ta de-ba we, ‘Pɛ Zeregese tete toŋe o bwoŋi o kaane Vasiti mo ye o ve se o vo o tei.’ 18Zem tento, Peresia tiina dedaane Media tiina nakwa bam kaana nigi Vasiti keim dem ŋwa. Ba maa wó bobo se ba taa leiri ba banna yɔɔ yerane. Banegero maa na wó gaale to, ba banna bam bane wó taa zaŋe de-ba mo.
19Pɛ, nmo wo ná dɛ tento, se n pa ni we n daa‑n ba lage se Vasiti yi n yera maŋa de maŋa, se ba daare ba popone-de ba tiŋi Peresia de Media chullu twanno tem ne, se ko yé taa ye kolo na wó leiri maŋa de maŋa to. N ma‑n ta wó ta se wolo na gare‑o to leiri wonto yuu ne o ji nmo ka-pɛ. 20Nmo ni dento ná lwoori yiga de yi nmo paare laŋa kam ni maama, kaane maama laam wó lɔre se o taa nege o baro, de kotu ná ye nadum naa nabwom de.”
21Pɛ Zeregese dedaane o nakwa bam maama wo déem ma pwoli dedaane Memukan taane dem, ye o ke se ko tɔge taane dem na bere tei to. 22O ma popone twanno o toŋe o pa teene delo maama na wo wonto dam kuri ne to se te bere o ni we, baaro maama taa jege dam o di o diga tiina baŋa ne. Teo maama tɔnɔ kom popone de ba dwi taane, nenɛɛne ba na yeini ba popone-de tei to.

english_text:
Esther Becomes Queen
1After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her. 2Then the king's personal servants said:
Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women. 3You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments. 4Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen.
King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
5At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin. 6 Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
7Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died. 8When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them.
Hegai was put in charge of all the women, 9and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
10Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him. 11He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
12The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes. 13When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters. 14In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
15-16Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
17Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti. 18In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts.
Mordecai Saves the King's Life
19When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official. 20He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
21Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him. 22Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out. 23King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_text:
Ɛseta jigi ka-pɛ
1Ko na wora ko wora to, Pɛ Zeregese bane ma to. O laam ma yɔɔre o boŋe Vasiti na ke tei, dedaane ni delo o na pɛ we, o daa yé taa ye ka-pɛ to. 2Pɛ wom nakwa balo na me ded‑o to ma bwɛ ded‑o ba we, “Nmo ná pɛ chwoŋa, dé wó pa se ba beeri bukɔ-pwoli selo na lana ye ba yeiri baara to. 3Kuri dedɛɛra n paare dim laŋa kam jei maama ne, se n pa-ba ni we ba ja bukɔ-pwoli sento ba ba Susa ne ywo-seeni. Ba maa wó pa se bukwa bam konto zo pɛ sɔŋɔ di selo ba na jege pɛ kaana ŋwaane to, se ba maŋe da. Nmo dedɛɛro Hegayi wolo na nii n kaana to wó taa nii-ba, ye o pa se ba kwei terale nuga ba kwɛ-ba se ba taa lana. 4Nmo laam ma‑n wó nii bukɔ-laaro tem konto wone, n le wolo na tiini o su n yi to se o ji ka-pɛ o leiri Vasiti yuu ne.”
Pɛ wom na maane we boboŋe dem lana to, o ma sɛ-de.
5Juu tu dedoa de déem tɔge o zoore Susa dam jei sem ne. O yere ye Modekayi mo. O maa ye Jayira bu, ye o nwoŋi Benjamin dwi dem wone. Kisi dedaane Simeyi de déem ye o nabaara mo. 6Maŋa kalo Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza déem na di Judah teo pɛ Jehoyachin, ye o chwooli o de o nɔɔna o le Jerusalem ne o ja vo o tete teo to, Modekayi de déem tɔge o wo ba wone mo. 7O nam ya jege o choro yere na ye Ɛseta. Wonto Hiburu yere déem ye Hadasa mo. O nam ya ye bukɔ-pwola kalo na lana chekke to mo, ye o ya-tega de lana. Ɛseta kwo de o nu déem na tege to, mo Modekayi lɛɛre o kwei‑o o ji o tete bukɔ, o jege‑o o kɔna.
8Pɛ wom ni-doore dem ŋwaane, ba déem ma ja bukwa dedɛ ba vo Susa dam jei sem, ye Ɛseta de déem wo ba wone. Ba déem kwei o de ba ke pɛ sɔŋɔ di selo wone Hegayi na nii ba maama baŋa ne to mo. 9Ɛseta kikia ma su Hegayi yi, pa o lage o ni taane. Hegayi ma pa se ba taa mae nuga ba turi Ɛseta yera, ye o daare o pa‑o wodi-laao se o di. Hegayi ta kwei‑o o ke sɔ-fɔrɔ kom mɛ na jege zula chekke to ne mo, ye o daare o kuri pɛ sɔŋɔ ka-nyaana barepɛ se ba taa nii o baŋa ne.
10Modekayi nam ya maŋe o ta de Ɛseta se o yé pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre we o ye Juu tu, naa ba lɔre o na nwoŋi sɔŋɔ kolo wone to. 11Dɛ maama wone, Modekayi déem yeini o kare pɛ kaana di sem konkɔlɔ ni ne mo o kekara. O nam ke konto se o taa yei ko na ye tei Ɛseta yera ne to, dedaane kolo na wó yi‑o to mo.
12Bukwa bam lam kwɛɛm yeini de kwei bene mo. Ba mae Mura nuga mo ba wei ba yera yam chane seredo, se ba daa kwei terale nuga ba turi-ba chane seredo. Konto kwaga ne, ba laam wó ja ka-bwona bam mo dedoa dedoa ba zo Pɛ Zeregese tei. 13Ka-bwom wolo ná ye se o nwoŋi kaana bam di sem ne o vo pɛ tete diga kam, kotu wó wane o taa zoore gwaaro telo maama o na lage to. 14Ba nam jege se ba ja ka-bwom wom konto ba vo ba zo pɛ tei mo dedaan-ni maŋa ne. Tega maa ná poore, ba wó ja‑o ba daa vo di sedwonna sem mɛ pɛ kaana badwonna bam na zoore da to mo. Saasegaza nam mo ye dedɛɛro wolo na nii pɛ ka-bi sem konto to. Pɛ wom ná wo mɛ ka-bwom wolo yere o jwoori o bwoŋi‑o, ko bere we o yi wo su kotu. O maa daa bá jwoori pɛ tei.
15Ko ma yi se Abihali bukɔ Ɛseta de zo pɛ wom tei. Wonto ye Modekayi choro mo, ye Modekayi ya kwei‑o o ji o tete bukɔ. Nɔɔna maama maa lage Ɛseta ni taane. Ɛseta na lage o zo pɛ wom tei to, o zo gwaaro telo yerane pɛ dedɛɛro Hegayi na bere‑o se o zo to mo. O wo kwei kolokolo o woli da. 16Ko ye Zeregese paare dim bena yarepɛ bene dem wone chane fuga kam ne, mo ba déem jaane Ɛseta ba zo pɛ-sɔŋɔ kom ne se o zo Pɛ Zeregese tei. Chana kam konto yere ye ‘Tebefa’ chana mo. 17Pɛ wom boboŋa maa tɔge Ɛseta se ko dwoni ka-bwona babam bam de o kaana bam maama. Ɛseta keim de ma su pɛ wom yi, ye pɛ wom ke‑o zaane. O ma kwei ka-pɛ yipuga kam mo o pu o yuu ne, se o taa ye ka-pɛ o leiri Vasiti yuu ne. 18Ko kwaga ne mo pɛ wom dɛ Ɛseta ŋwaane o ke kuri-fɔrɔ. O ma bwoŋi o teo nakwa, de o dedɛɛra maama se ba jeeri ba di kuri dem. O ta ma pa ni we de dɛ dem ye kuri siu dɛ mo, ye o daare o kwei pɛɛra na maŋe de pɛ to o pa o nɔɔna bam.
Modekayi chege pɛ wom toone
19Ka-bwona bam daa na jeeri daane to, dedaane Modekayi yeini o jei pɛ-sɔŋɔ ni ne o toŋe o pa pɛ wom mo. 20Ko daare, Ɛseta wo pɛ se nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre sɔŋɔ kolo o na nwoŋi to naa ba lɔre we o ye Juu tu, ne Modekayi na maŋe o bere‑o se o seigi o dwi dem tei to mo. O na sɛ o ni dem konto to tɔge o déem na maŋe o ke tei ye Modekayi kɔne‑o to mo.
21Modekayi déem na wo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ni ne o toŋe o totoŋa to, mo dɛ dedwe Bigetana, de Terese bwɛ se ba go pɛ wom, ba na done‑o to ŋwaane. Ba maa ye pɛ sɔŋɔ dedɛɛra balo na yere o di sem to mo. 22Modekayi ma ni ko ŋwa ye o vo o ta de Ɛseta. Wonto de ma pa se pɛ wom lɔre Modekayi na tage kolo o bere‑o to. 23Ba ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba yɛ taane dem wone ye ba daare ba maane we ko ye chega mo. Ba ma kuuni nɔɔna balei bam konto de ŋone ba go. Pɛ wom ma pa se ba popone keina yam konto ba tiŋi ba teo pwa yera seina twanno tem wone.

english_text:
Haman Plans To Destroy the Jews
1Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag, 2and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai. 3When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command, 4he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
5Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him. 6And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
7It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
8 Then Haman went to the king and said:
Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them! 9Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
10The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him, 11“Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
12On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
13The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
14-15King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_text:
Haman boŋe se o ti Juu tiina bam
1Ko na ke fee to, mo Pɛ Zeregese zeiŋi Haman se o ji wolo na saŋe pɛ kwaga o taa nii teo kom to. Haman nam ye Hamedata bu mo, ye o nwoŋi Agagi dwi dem wone. 2Pɛ wom ma pa o dedɛɛra balo na toŋe o sɔŋɔ kom ne to maama ni se ba tiiri tega ne ba ma zuli Haman. Ba maama ma sɛ ba ke konto, ye Modekayi yerane ve se o tiiri o zuli‑o. 3Pɛ dedɛɛra badwonna bam maa yeini ba bwei‑o ba we, “Bɛŋwaane mo n ve pɛ wom ni dem?” 4Dɛ maama wone, ba maa jege‑o ba nyenyɔna se o de sɛ o tiiri, ye o ba sɛa. O laam ma ta o bere-ba o we, o ye Juu tu mo, ko nam wo maŋe se o tiiri konto dwoŋi. Ba ma vo ba ta o taane dem de Haman, se ba lɔre wonto wó ja keim dem tetɛ. 5Haman na lɔre we Modekayi ve se o tiiri o pa‑o to, mo o bane zaŋe. 6O ta na lɔre we Modekayi ye Juu tu to, o ma jeeli we o ná go Modekayi yerane, ko bá zuri o bane. O ma ke o boboŋa ne se o chɔge Juu tiina balo maama na zoore Pɛ Zeregese paare dim laŋa kam ne to.
7Pɛ Zeregese paare dim bena fuga-yalei bene dem wone, de boboa chana kam, ka yere na ye Nisan to wone mo Haman pɛ se ba ta jɔrɔ se o lɔre chana kalo de dɛ delo chekke o na wó wane o ke o boboŋa yam to. Jɔrɔ kom yere mo ‘Pura’. Ko ma le chane fuga-selei chana kam ka yere na ye Adare to mo. 8Haman na lɔre konto to, o laam ma yi pɛ wom tei ye o we, “Nɔɔna badwonna mo jage ba yi nmo paare dim laŋa kam ni maama. Ba dwi dem zoore kateira maama ne mo. Ba chullu nam ye te yera mo de nɔɔna maama chullu. Ko kwaga ne, ba ba tɔge nia yalo debam na pɛ dé teo nɔɔna bam se ba taa tɔge to. Konto ŋwaane, yé sɛ se debam de-ba taa zoore daane. 9Pɛ, nmo nam ná sɛ a boboŋe dem, se n pa ni we ba jege se ba te mo. Konto ná kea, amo wó kwei lu-nyenno dunni na wó yi kilo morro bia yatɔ de finna (340,000) to a pa balo na nii teo kom totoŋa baŋa ne to, se ba tiŋi-te nmo paare dem ŋwaane.”
10Pɛ wom ma sɛ ye o daare o le o jeŋa jafole delo na bere o dam to, o pa Haman. Wonto maa ye Agagi tu Hamedata bu ye o chuli Juu tiina bam. 11Pɛ wom ma ta de Haman o we, “Ta‑n jege n sabu kom. Nɔɔna bam de nam wo n jeŋa ne, se n ke-ba n na lage tei to.”
12Ko ma pa se Haman bwoŋi pɛ wom tɔn-poponna, ye o pa ba popone twanno pɛ wom yere ŋwaane. O ta pɛ se ba popone o ni dem de teo maama dwi taane, nenɛɛne ba na yeini ba popone-de tei to. O laam ma kwei Pɛ Zeregese jafole dem o nye te baŋa ne, ye o we ba ja-te ba vo o paare laŋa kam ni maama ne ba pa pɛ wom yiga tiina, de kateira yam dedɛɛra, de dwi tiina maama nakwa. Haman déem ke konto boboa chana kam da fuga-yatɔ dɛ dem ne mo. 13Balo na ye se ba pa taane dem jage to ma ja ni dem konto ba vo Pɛ Zeregese paare dim laŋa kateira yam maama ne. Ni dem bere we chwoŋa tiga se chane fuga-selei chana kam, ka yere na ye Adare to, da fuga-yatɔ dɛ ne, se ba chɔge Juu tiina maama ba ti dɛ dedwe wone. Ko ná ye ba nɔn-donno, naa nɔn-kwe, naa kaana, naa bu-somwa de, se ba go ba maama, ye ba daare ba vere ba jejegero ba ja ba viiri. 14Ba déem ma pa se kateiri de kateiri maama taa jege de tɔnɔ, se nɔɔna maama wane ba lɔre ni dem jaja, ye ba daare ba ti yiga se dɛ dem laam yi.
15Pɛ wom ni dem ma pa se balo na pae taane dem jage to duri lela ba vo ba yi jei maama. Ba ta ma tɔɔle taane dem Susa dam jei sem wone. Pɛ wom dedaane Haman maa jei ba jege sana ba nyɔa. Susa teo kom nɔɔna maama boboŋa nam vugimi.

english_text:
Mordecai Asks for Esther's Help
1When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping. 2But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace. 3 In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
4When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
5Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
6Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate, 7and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
8Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
9Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said. 10She answered, “Tell Mordecai 11there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
12When Mordecai was told what Esther had said, 13he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace. 14If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
15Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying, 16“Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
17Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_text:
Modekayi beeri wolim Ɛseta tei ne
1Modekayi na maane kolo maama na ke to, o ma kaare o gwaaro, o wo na chɔge to ŋwaane. O ma zo gare-nyenyaaro, ye o daare o puki o yuu maama dedaane tentwarem. O ma nwoŋi o kare teo kom maama wone o via ye o laare de kwor-dɛa baŋa baŋa. 2O ke konto mo o vo o yi Pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo ni dem, ye o wo zo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wone, ko na chula se nɔɔna zo gare-nyenyaaro ba zo dáane to ŋwaane. 3Pɛ wom ni dem na yi mɛ de mɛ o paare laŋa kateira yam maama wone to, Juu tiina bam yɔɔre ba laare bugi-bugi mo. Ba maa vɔ ni, ye ba keera, ye ba ta chwoosa. Ba dedɛ ma zo gare-nyenyaaro, ye ba daare ba jei tentwarem wone.
4Ka-nyaana dedaane tontoŋena balo na nii Ɛseta to ma na Modekayi na ke kolo to, ye ba ta ba bere Ɛseta. Ko ma tiini ko daane‑o. O ma toŋe gwaaro o pa Modekayi se o leiri o gare-nyenyaaro tem se o daare o zo-te. O maa wo sɛ. 5Tontoŋena balo pɛ wom na le se ba taa nii Ɛseta to dedoa yere ye Hatake mo. Ɛseta laam ma toŋe‑o Modekayi tei ne se o bwei o lɔre kolo na daane‑o to. 6Hatake ma nwoŋi o vo Modekayi tei, ye o wo teo kom kapworo kom ne, ko na jeeri de pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo to. 7Modekayi de ma ta o bere‑o kolo maama na yi‑o to, dedaane Haman na gwoni ni se o tiŋi sabu-fɔrɔ teo kom kwɛɛm ŋwaane, ne o ná nɛ chwoŋa se o pa Juu tiina maama na chɔgem. 8O laam ma daare o kwei tɔnɔ kolo na pɛ nɔɔna ni se ba chɔge Juu tiina bam ye ba tɔɔle ko taane Susa ne to o bere Hatake. O ma kwei ko dwoŋi o pa‑o se o ja o vo o pa Ɛseta. O ta tage‑o mo se o maŋe tɔnɔ kom wo wonnu tem o bere Ɛseta, se o daare o ta‑o we, o véi pɛ wom tei o lwoori‑o se o duri Juu tiina bam yibwona.
9Hatake ma seene o vo Ɛseta tei o bere‑o kolo Modekayi na tage to. 10Ɛseta ma leiri‑o o we:
“Nam véi n ta de Modekayi we, 11ko zege pɛ nakwa ne, se ko yi nɔn-bia bam na wo kateira yam maama wone to, nɔɔno maama yei we chwoŋa tera se nɔɔno zo pɛ wom tei ye o wo bwoŋi‑o. Ba ta yei we wolo ná zo da ye pɛ wo bwoŋi‑o, ba jege se ba go konto tu mo. Debam teo kom wadaa mo konto. Ko nam ye pɛ ná zeiŋi o sabu-seŋa nacheiga kam o jeeri kotu, mo ba bá go‑o. Chana mo tento nam, pɛ na wo toŋe o bwoŋi-ne.”
12Modekayi na nigi Ɛseta kwora kam to, 13o ma toŋe o ta‑o o we:
“Yé ta‑n boŋe we, n na wo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wone to ŋwaane, nmo yerane wó ta‑n ye Juu tu se n lu. 14Nmo ná maŋe da chemm maŋa kanto, nam lɔre se wolim wó nwoŋi jei sedwonna ne de ba Juu tiina bam ŋwaane, se ba na verem. Nmo nam wó te, ye n kwo sɔŋɔ kom de ti. Dé nam yeiri dé tia. Dɛ dedwoŋi ne ko zege ko ye maŋa kanto kikia yam ŋwaane mo n tu n ji ka-pɛ!”
15Ɛseta laam ma leiri Modekayi o we:
16“Véi n la Juu tiina bam maama na wo Susa ne to n ke daane. Vɔ-na ni se á lwoori Wɛ á pa-ne. Yé di-na wodiu, nam yé nyɔ-na na da yatɔ, wea dedaane tete maama. Amo de a ka-nyaana bam de wó ke konto. Dé ná ti, amo laam wó zo pɛ wom tei, de ko na maŋe ko chula to de. Ko ná ye se a te ko ŋwaane, a sɛ se a te!”
17Modekayi laam ma viiri o vo o ke kolo maama Ɛseta na bere se o ke to.

english_text:
Esther Invites the King and Haman to a Dinner
1Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway. 2He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her.
When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter, 3the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
4Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
5The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.”
The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner, 6and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
7-8Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.”
Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
9Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry, 10but he did not say a thing.
When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh 11and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him. 12Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow. 13But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
14Haman's wife and friends said to him, “Have a gallows built about 22 meters high, and tomorrow morning ask the king to hang Mordecai there. Then later, you can have dinner with the king and enjoy yourself.”
This seemed like a good idea to Haman, and he had the gallows built.
translation_text:
Ɛseta na vei pɛ wom tei ye o ta kolo to
1Ɛseta ni-vɔre dem da yatɔ dɛ dem ne, mo o zo o paare gwaaro tem o laam vo o zo pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne o zege da. Jei sem konto jeeri de paare diga kam. Pɛ Zeregese déem jei o paare yituŋu kom baŋa ne mo o nii diga kam ni dem seeni. 2O ma na we Ɛseta zege konkɔlɔ kom ne. O wo ma pwoli ded‑o ye o tei o sabu-seŋa nacheiga kam o jeeri‑o se o ma zaane‑o. O de ma fɔɔre o yi o tei, ye o dwei ka nabili dem seeni. 3Pɛ wom ma bwei‑o o we, “Ɛseta, bɛ mo daane‑m? Ta n bere-ne kolo n na lage to, se ko ná maŋe ko ye a paare dim laŋa kam chichworo de, amo wó kwei-ka a pa‑m.” 4Ɛseta ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, laŋa ná daare, se nmo dedaane Haman ba amo tei zem se dé di daane. A lage a vo a ti wodi-fɔrɔ yiga abam ŋwaane mo.”
5Pɛ wom ma pa ni se ba ke lela ba bwoŋi Haman se ba vo Ɛseta tei ba di, ne o na tage tei to. Ba ma seene ba vo. 6Ba na di ba ti ye ba nyɔ sana to, pɛ wom ma bwei Ɛseta o we, “Ta n bere-ne n na lage se a ke kolo to, se amo wó ke a pa‑m, ko ná maŋe ko ye a laŋa kam chichworo de.”
7Ɛseta ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, amo na wó lwoori kolo nmo tei ne to mo tento: 8Nmo yi ná sui a kikia yam ye n wo ná dɛ se n ke kolo a na lage to, se nmo de Haman jwa daa jwoori ywo-seeni. Amo ta wó ke wodi-fɔrɔ se abam ba á di. Kanto maŋa ne, a laam wó ta kolo a na lage to a bere‑m.”
Haman bane zaŋe de Modekayi
9Dɛ dem konto ne, Haman na nwoŋi ka-pɛ Ɛseta tei ye o maa viiri to, o wo yɔɔre ko tiini ko pwoli mo. Ko daare, o na nwoŋi pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo kom ni ne o maa kɛ to, mo o nɛ Modekayi. Wonto maa wo zaŋe wɛɛne, o nam wo kɔre foone de Haman. Konto ŋwaane Haman bane tiini de zaŋe o baŋa ne. 10De ko de, o déem peene o bane mo ye o viiri. O na yi sɔŋɔ to, o ma bwoŋi o badwonna se ba ba o sɔŋɔ, ye o bwoŋi o kaane Zerese o woli da. 11O laam ma ŋɔɔne o bere o tete de o jejegero, de o bu-baara na daga tei, de pɛ na zeiŋi wonto se o saŋe o kwaga pa se teo kom nakwa de naduna maama jege se ba taa kɔre‑o tei to. 12Haman laam ma ta o woli da o we, “Kolo na tiini ko dwoi maama to mo ye ka-pɛ Ɛseta na ke wodi-fɔrɔ se pɛ wom ba o di to, amo yerane mo o bwoŋi se a da a vo. O daa ma ta o we dé ta jwoori jwa ne se dé daa di daane. 13Amo nam ná nɛ tento maama, ye a jwoori a na Juu tu Modekayi na jei pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo ni ne tei to, tento maama ye kafɛ mo.”
14O kaane Zerese de o badwonna bam maama maa bwɛ ded‑o ba we, “Ko nam ná ye konto, pa se ba chwi da-kwollu na dɔra te yi jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finnu to. Laam lei ŋone te yera ne se jwa tetete, n vo pɛ tei n jwoŋi chwoŋa se n kuuni Modekayi te baŋa ne n go. Ko kwaga ne, n laam wó tɔge de pɛ wom n vo n di dedaane wopwolo.”
Haman ma kwei ba boboŋe dem o ke o yuu ne, ye o pa se ba chwi da-kwoli-dedwaaro se ba wane ba kuuni Modekayi te baŋa ne.

english_text:
The King Honors Mordecai
1That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king. 2 When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king, 3the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?”
“Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
4About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
5The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.”
“Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
6When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?”
Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor. 7So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man, 8get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress. 9Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
10The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
11Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
12Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame. 13Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.” 14They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_text:
Pɛ wom pɛ se ba zuli Modekayi
1Tete dem konto ne, dɔɔm ba tui pɛ wom yia ne. O ma pa ni se ba ja ba teo pwa yera seina twanno tem ba na yeini ba popone o paare dim kikia ba tiŋi da to ba ja ba ba ba ga se o cheigi. 2Ba na jege tɔnɔ kom ba gare to, ba ma vo ba di mɛ ko na popone we Bigetana de Terese ya boŋe se ba go pɛ wom to baŋa. Banto déem ye pɛ sɔŋɔ dedɛɛra balo na yere o di sem to, ye Modekayi pa se pɛ wom lɔre ba bana yam ni ne.
3Pɛ wom ma bwei o tontoŋena bam o we, “Modekayi na ke keim-laao konto to, dé zuli‑o tetɛ seeni mo ko ŋwaane?” Ba ma leiri ba we, “Ba wo ke kolokolo ba pa‑o.” 4Pɛ Zeregese daa ma bwei-ba o we, “Amo nakwa bam wone wɔ mo wo ywo-seeni?”
Ko yɔɔre ko ke ko maŋe dedaane Haman yi pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo kom. O déem ya tu pɛ wom tei se o lwoori chwoŋa mo se ba kuuni Modekayi de ŋone selo o na leigi da-kwollu tem yera ne to. 5Pɛ tontoŋena bam ma leiri ba we, “Haman wo konkɔlɔ kom ne, ye o beeri chwoŋa se o na‑m.” Pɛ wom ma ta o we, “Pa-na chwoŋa se o zo amo tei ne.”
6Haman na zo pɛ wom tei to, mo Zeregese bwei‑o o we, “Amo boŋe se a ke zula mo a pa nɔɔno wodwoŋi, a yi na su o kikia to ŋwaane. Nmo boŋe tɛ mo se a ke a pa konto tu?”
Haman ma boŋe o tete ne we, “Wɔ mo pɛ daa wó taa lage se o ke‑o zula ko ná dae amo yerane?” 7O ma leiri pɛ wom o we, “Pɛ. Nmo yi ná su nɔɔno kikia ye n boŋe se n ke‑o zula, 8se n pa ba kwei n paare gwaaro telo n tete na zoore to, se ba daare ba ja nmo paare sisein-nɔɔno wom ba ba, ye paare yipuga wo ka yuu ne. 9Nmo laam ma‑n beeri n nakwa bam dedoa na ye nɔn-yuu chekke to, se o kwei gwaaro tem konto o zo nɔɔno wom ye o daare o pa se wolo n na lage n ke‑o zula to dɔge n sisein-nɔɔno wom baŋa ne. O maa wó taa jege kotu o kaare teo kom pwooni ne o tɔɔle o we, ‘Nii-na! Pɛ ná boŋe se o ke nɔɔno zula, o wó ke tento mo o pa kotu.’ ”
10Pɛ wom ma ta Haman o we, “Nmo taane dem lana. Nam ke lela n ti a gwaaro tem yiga dedaane a sisein-nɔɔno wom yiga, se n tete ke n na bere tei maama to se dé ma dé zuli Modekayi na ye Juu tu ye o jei pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo ni ne to. Yé swei se n ke kolo maama n na tage to n pa‑o!”
11Haman ma vo o jwoŋi paare nenɔŋa gwaaro tem dedaane sisein-nɔɔno wom. O ma pa se Modekayi zo gwaaro tem. Modekayi na diini siseiŋa kam baŋa ne to, Haman laam maa tɔge o yiga o jege‑o o beeri o kaare teo kom pwooni maama. O na vei to, o maa tɔɔle o we, “Nii-na! Pɛ ná boŋe se o ke nɔɔno zula, o wó ke tento mo o pa kotu.”
12Ba na kaare teo kom ba ti to, Modekayi ma jwoori o vo o wo pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo ni ne o toŋa. Haman ma gwoori o tiri ye o ke lela o jwoori sɔŋɔ de chaveera. 13O ma ta o bere o kaane Zerese de o badwonna maama kolo na yi‑o to. O kaane de o badwonna balo na jege swa to ma ta‑o ba we, “Nmo wo maane we n bobo se n ta‑n toe n pae Modekayi mo na? O ye Juu tu mo, ye n ware‑o. O nam wó de‑m tega ne.”
14Ba ya daa ta wo ba lara yam wone mo, ye pɛ sɔŋɔ dedɛɛra bam ba se ba ja Haman ba ke lela ba vo se o di wodi-fɔrɔ kolo Ɛseta na ke to.

english_text:
Haman Is Punished
1The king and Haman were dining with Esther 2and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
3Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want, 4because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
5“Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
6Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!”
Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
7The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden.
Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
8Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!”
As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head. 9Then Harbona, one of the king's personal servants, said, “Your Majesty, Haman built a gallows 22 meters high beside his house, so he could hang Mordecai on it. And Mordecai is the very one who spoke up and saved your life.”
“Hang Haman from his own gallows!” the king commanded. 10At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_text:
Haman na to tei to
1Pɛ Zeregese de Haman ma vo ba zo ka-pɛ Ɛseta tei ne se ba di daane. 2Ba na di ded‑o belei tu baŋa ne ba ti ye ba nyɔ sana to, mo pɛ wom daa bwei Ɛseta o we, “Laam ta n bere-ne n ya na lage se a ke kolo to, se amo wó ke a pa‑m, ko ná maŋe ko ye a paare laŋa kam chichworo de.”
3Ɛseta ma leiri o we, “Pɛ, a keim ná sui n yi, ye ko ná pwoli n wo, se n ke a na wó bwei‑m kolo to n pa-ne. Ko ye se n jwoŋi amo ŋwea se n daare n yage a dwi tiina bam maama se ba taa ŋwe. 4Ko na ye tei to, ba maŋe ba yeigi amo de a dwi tiina bam mo se dé maama na chɔgem dé ti. Ko ya ná ye ba lage se dé ji kabɛ mo, amo ya wó taa chem mo, ko na wo yi se a daane‑m to ŋwaane. Ba boboŋe dem nam ye se debam dwi dem jei tega baŋa ne lela!”
5Pɛ Zeregese ma bwei ka-pɛ wom o we, “Wɔ mo boŋe se o ke wo-balɔrɔ kom konto? O wo yei ne mo?” 6Ɛseta ma leiri o we, “Debam dono wom, o na beeri dé toone to mo ye nɔn-balɔrɔ konto, Haman.”
Haman ma lɛɛre o jei o nii pɛ wom de ka-pɛ wom ferebaa, ye foone tiini de zo‑o. 7Pɛ wom ma zaŋe wɛɛne de bane o nwoŋi pwooni ye o yage sana bam nyɔɔm. O ma vo o zege pɛ sɔŋɔ kapworo ne mɛ teeni na wora to. Haman ma maane we pɛ wom boboŋa jaane se o waare‑o o kikia yam ŋwaane. O ma maŋe diga kam ne se o lwoori Ɛseta se o ja pɛ wom naga se o yé te. 8O ma yɔɔre o vo o to gadwogo kolo ne Ɛseta na tigi da to se o lwoori‑o, de pɛ wom de zege pɛ sɔŋɔ kapworo kom ne o zo diga kam. Pɛ wom na nɛ konto to, mo o we, “Nɔɔno wonto laam boŋe se o zi ka-pɛ wom mo a tete sɔŋɔ ne na?”
O taane dem maŋe de wo to tega ne dedaane pɛ sɔŋɔ tontoŋena na tu ba kwoli Haman yibia. 9Pɛ tontoŋena bam dedoa o yere na ye Harebona to ma ta o we, “Haman maŋe o chwi da-kwollu mo o sɔŋɔ ne, te na dɔra te yi jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finnu to, ye o lei ŋone se yera ne se o ma kuuni Modekayi o go. Wonto déem nam mo ye wolo na jwoŋi nmo o yage to.”
Pɛ wom ma pa ni ye o we, “Véi-na á kwei Haman á lei dáane á go.” 10Ba déem ma kwei Haman ba jwoori ba kuuni de ŋone selo o ya na leigi da-kwollu tem yera ne se o ma o kuuni Modekayi o go to. Pɛ wom wo laam ma to.

english_text:
A Happy Ending for the Jews
1Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials 2and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
3Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!” 4King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther, 5and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed, 6and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
7King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews. 8 I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
9On the twenty-third day of Sivan, the third month, the king's secretaries wrote the law. They obeyed Mordecai and wrote to the Jews, the rulers, the governors, and the officials of all 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. The letters were written in every language used in the kingdom, including the Jewish language. 10They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
11-13In these letters the king said:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies.
A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
14-15Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth.
After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered, 16and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
17In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_text:
Ba pɛ Juu tiina chwoŋa se ba jaŋe ba jwoŋi ba ŋwea
1Dɛ dem konto ne mo Pɛ Zeregese kwei Juu tiina bam dono Haman jejegero maama o pa Ɛseta. Wonto de ma ta de pɛ wom we Modekayi ye o choro mo. Modekayi laam ma na chwoŋa se o zo pɛ wom tei. 2Pɛ wom nam ya maŋe o le o dam jafole dem mo Haman jeŋa ne. O laam ma kwei-de o ke Modekayi noa ne. Ko na zege dɛ dem konto ne to, Ɛseta ma pa se Modekayi lɛɛre o nii kolo maama Haman ya na jege to.
3Ɛseta daa ta ma zo pɛ wom tei se o lwoori‑o o dwi tiina bam ŋwaane. O déem to o pwoa ne mo ye o keera. O ma lwoori‑o se o che boboŋ-balɔrɔ kolo Agagi dwi tu Haman ya na ke se o ma o chɔge Juu tiina bam to. 4Pɛ wom ma tei o sabu-seŋa nacheiga kam o jeeri Ɛseta, ye o zaŋe wɛɛne o fɔɔre o yi pɛ wom tei. 5Ɛseta daa maa we, “Pɛ, nmo wo ná dɛa, ye ko maŋe dede‑m, nmo yi maa ná sui a kikia yam ye n yiga ná wo amo wone, se n pa kwora kalo na wó che Haman ni dem se de daa yé toŋe. Ko ye ni delo Agagi dwi tu Hamedeta bu Haman na pɛ we ba chɔge Juu tiina bam nmo paare dim laŋa kam jei maama ne to taane mo a tɛa. 6Amo nam bá wane a yage se lɛɛro tento ba a dwi tiina bam baŋa. A bá wane a peene a tete ye ba jege a tete chorro ba goe.”
7Pɛ Zeregese ma ta de ka-pɛ Ɛseta de Juu tu Modekayi o we, “Nii-na amo na ke tei Juu tiina bam ŋwaane. A pɛ se ba kuuni Haman mo de o na boŋe lwarem se o ti Juu tiina bam to, a ta ma kwei o jejegero tem a pa Ɛseta. 8Amo nam wó pa abam chwoŋa se á kwei amo yere á popone á na lage kolo maama to á ke twanno wone se ko woli Juu tiina bam ba cham wone. Á ná popone taane dem á ti, se á kwei a dam jafole dem á ma nye twanno tem baŋa ne. Ko nam ná ye ni delo ba na kwei pɛ yere ba popone-de, ye ba daare ba ma o jafole dem ba nye tɔnɔ kom to, dento bá wane de kwane.”
9Ba déem ma bwoŋi pɛ wom tɔn-poponna bam se ba ba. Modekayi ma ta kolo ba na wó popone to, se o kwei o ni dem o pa Juu tiina bam, de pɛ wom yiga tiina, de dedɛɛra, de nakwa balo na wo kateira bi de finlei-barepɛ (127) yam maama wone to, se ko zege India ne se ko yi Etiopia. Ko maa ye chane setɔ chana kam da finlei-yatɔ dɛ ne mo tento maama kea. Chane kam yere mo ‘Sivan’. Ba déem popone twanno tem de teo maama dwi taane, nenɛɛne ba na yeini ba popone-de tei to mo. Juu tiina bam de ma jwoŋi ba twanno de ba tete taane, dedaane ba poponem na ye tei to. 10Modekayi déem mɛ Pɛ Zeregese yere mo o popone twanno tem, ye o daare o kwei pɛ dam jafole dem o nye te baŋa ne. O ma daare o kwei-te o pa pɛ tontoŋena balo na diini pɛ wom tete sisein-nɔɔna balo na wae ba duri lela to.
11Twanno tem déem bere pɛ wom ni we Juu tiina na zoore teo kolo maama wone to jege chwoŋa se ba la daane se ba jaŋe ba jwoŋi ba tete ba yage. Ko ta we, jar-keira ná nwoŋi dwi delo maama wone, naa teo kolo maama wone, ye ba kwaare jara de Juu tiina bam, banto wó wane ba chɔge balo maama na done-ba to ba ti, ko ná maŋe ko ye ba kaana de ba bia de. Ba ta wó wane ba kwei ba dona bam jejegero ba taa tei. 12Dɛ dem Juu tiina bam na jege chwoŋa se ba jaŋe ba jwoŋi ba tete Pɛ Zeregese paare dim laŋa kam maama wone konto to maa ye chane fuga-selei chana kam, ka yere na ye Adare to, da fuga-yatɔ dɛ dem ne. 13Ba déem pɛ se kateiri de kateiri maama taa jege de tɔnɔ kom, se dwi maama tiina wane ba lɔre ni dem jaja. Ba ke se de dɛ dem ná yia, se Juu tiina bam ti yiga se ba jaŋe de ba dona mo. 14Pɛ wom ni dem ma pa se o sisein-dira bam duri lela ba ja twanno tem ba vo ba yi jei maama. Ba ta ma tɔɔle taane dem Susa dam jei sem wone.
15Modekayi ma nwoŋi pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne o maa viira, de o zo paare gwaaro mo telo nyenyero na ye napwonnu de nazwon-pupwia to. O ta ma daŋe gare-fefala kalo nyenyego na ye nasoŋ-pupwia to o ke da, ye sabu-seŋa yipuga wo o yuu ne. Susa teo kom dam jei sem laam ma su dedaane sɔɔ, nɔɔna bam na jege wopwolo to ŋwaane. 16Juu tiina bam wo déem ma pwoli de kolo maama na ke to. Nɔɔna maama ma pa-ba zula jei maama ne. 17Ba déem na tɔɔle pɛ wom ni dem teo maama de kateira maama wone to, ko pɛ se Juu tiina bam ke kuri mo ba di wodiiru, ye ba kwɛɛre, ba na tiini ba jege wopwolo to ŋwaane. Dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ de bere ba pipiri ba ji Juu tiina, ba na tu ba kɔre foone de Juu tiina bam to ŋwaane.

english_text:
The Jews Destroy Their Enemies
1The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around, 2and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
3The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews. 4Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
5The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy. 6-10They killed 500 people in Susa, but they did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Haman had been one of the worst enemies of the Jews, and ten of his sons were among those who were killed. Their names were Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.
11Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa. 12Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
13Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
14King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa. 15Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed 300 more people. But they still did not take anything that belonged to their enemies.
16-17On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed 75,000 of their enemies, but the Jews did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Then on the fourteenth day of the month the Jews celebrated with a feast.
18 On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth. 19This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other.
The Festival of Purim
20Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces 21and told them:
Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar, 22the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
23They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration.
The Reason for the Festival of Purim
24 Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
25Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged. 26Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast. 27Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do. 28From now on, all Jewish families must remember to celebrate Purim on these two days each year.
29Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast. 30Copies of this letter were sent to Jews in the 127 provinces of King Xerxes. In the letter they said:
We pray that all of you will live in peace and safety.
31You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
32These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_text:
Juu tiina bam di dam ba dona baŋa ne
1Adare chana kam da fuga-yatɔ dɛ dem ma seene de yi. Dɛ dem konto mo pɛ wom ni dem jege se de toŋe. Juu tiina dona bam déem ya teene se ba wane-ba mo, ye banto jwoori ba wane ba dona bam ba di. 2Pɛ Zeregese paare dim laŋa kam ne Juu tiina na zoore mɛ maama to, ba ma la daane se ba jeeri balo na boŋe se ba chɔge-ba to de jara. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa ware se o dwoni de-ba, dwi maama tiina na kɔre foone de-ba to ŋwaane. 3Teo maama nakwa, dedaane pɛ wom dedɛɛra, de o yiga tiina, de o tontoŋena maama déem tɔge ba woli Juu tiina bam mo, ba na kɔre Modekayi to ŋwaane. 4Peresia kateira yam maama wone nɔɔna laam tu ba maane we Modekayi mo tiini o jege dam pɛ sɔŋɔ ne. O dam dem déem ke de woli da mo dɛ maama.
5Dɛ dem na yi to, Juu tiina bam déem chɔge ba dona bam ba na lage tei to. Ba ma kwei se-zɔɔro ba jeeri balo na chuli-ba to ye ba go-ba. 6Susa dam jei sem wone, ba déem go nɔɔna bia yanu. 7-10Ba ma go Hamedata bu Haman bu-baara fuga. Wonto déem ye Juu tiina bam dono mo. O bia bam mo tento: Pasandata, de Dalefon, de Asepata, de Porata, de Adalia, de Aridata, de Paramaseta, de Arisayi, de Aridayi, dedaane Vayizata. Ba ma go nɔɔna bam konto maama, ye ba laam wo vere ba jejegero.
11Dɛ dem konto ne ba ma ta ba bere pɛ wom ba na go nɔɔna balo Susa dam jei sem ne to ni na mae tei. 12O de ma guli de ka-pɛ Ɛseta o we, “Susa dam jei sem yerane wone Juu tiina bam go nɔɔna bia yanu mo, ye Haman bia fuga kam tɔge ba wo twa bam wone. Se ko ná ye kateira yadwonna yam wone, ko laam wó taa ye tetɛ mo? Nam ta n bere-ne kolo nmo daa‑n na lage se a ke to, se amo wó ke a pa‑m. Nmo wó lwoori bɛ mo amo tei ne?”
13Ɛseta ma leiri o we, “Pɛ, ko ná dɛ de n wo, se n jwa daa‑n pa Juu tiina bam chwoŋa se ba ke ba na ke tei zem tento to dwoŋi. Ta pa ni se ba kwei Haman bia bam yera ba lei da-kwoli-dedwaaro tem yera ne.”
14Pɛ wom ma pa ni Susa teo wone se ba ke tei ka-pɛ wom na tage to. Ba ma kwei Haman bia bam yera yam ba lei da-kwollu tem yera ne. 15Adare chana kam da fuga-yana dɛ dem ne Juu tiina balo na zoore Susa wone to daa ma ke daane ba go nɔɔna bia yatɔ, ye ba ta wo vere ba jejegero.
16Juu tiina balo na wo kateira yayam yam wone to de ma ke daane se ba jaŋe ba jwoŋi ba tete, ye ba wane ba dona ba di. Ba ma go ba dona morro fuserepɛ-tenu (75,000). Ba de maa wo vere ba dona bam jejegero. 17Ko déem ye Adare chana kam da fuga-yatɔ dɛ dem ne mo ba go-ba. Se ko ná ye da fuga-yana dɛ dem ne, ba sii mo de jara. Ba pɛ se de ji wopwolo dɛ mo ye ba di kuri. 18Ko daare, Juu tiina balo na zoore Susa wone to, mo pɛ se chana kam da fuga-yanu dɛ dem ye wopwolo dɛ ye ba di kuri. Kokuri to, ba mɛ da fuga-yatɔ dɛ dem de da fuga-yana dɛ dem mo ba go ba dona ye ba laam sii de jara yam. 19Konto ma pa se Juu tiina balo na zoore te-balwa wone to kwei Adare chana kam da fuga-yana dɛ dem se de ji ba wopwolo dɛ. Ko ná yeini ko yi dɛ dem konto, ba maa yeini ba ke kuri ye ba daare ba toŋe wodiiru ba pae daane.
Purim kuri dem dim
20Modekayi déem pɛ se ba popone wonnu tento maama mo ba tiŋi, ye o daare o toŋe twanno o pa Juu tiina balo na zoore Pɛ Zeregese paare dim laŋa kam jei maama ne, ba ná maŋe ba ye bwola bwola naa yiga yiga de. 21O ma ta-ba se bene maama wone, ko ná yeini ko kaare ko yi Adare chana kam da fuga-yana dɛ dem de ka da fuga-yanu dɛ dem, se ba taa ke wopwolo kuri, 22ko na ye da yam konto wone mo Juu tiina bam déem vere ba tete ba dona jeŋa ne to ŋwaane. Ko ta ye chana kalo wone ba wo-chechɔgɔ déem na pipiri ko ji wopwolo ye ba cham de ji ywoni to mo. Modekayi ma bere-ba se ba kwei da yam konto ba di kuri ye ba kwɛɛra, se ba taa ke wodiiru pɛɛra ba pa daane, ye ba ta woli yiniga tiina de pɛɛra. 23Juu tiina bam ma sɛ Modekayi ni dem ye ba pa se keim dem konto lɛɛre de ji bene maama kikia, ne ba na bobo se ba ke tei to.
24Ko na ye tei to, Agagi dwi tu Hamedata bu Haman, o ya na ye Juu tiina maama dono to, déem mo boŋe se o chɔge Juu tiina bam o ti. O ma ta jɔrɔ se o lɔre dɛ delo o na wó pa se ba dwi dem saare tega baŋa ne to. Jɔrɔ kom yere mo ‘Pura’. 25Ɛseta ma pa se pɛ wom lɔre Haman boboŋa yam ni ne. Pɛ wom na nigi to, o ma popone o ni o ke tɔnɔ wone, pa se Haman ya na boŋe se o ke Juu tiina bam lwarem delo to pipiri de jwoori o tete yuu ne. Pɛ wom ta ma pa se ba kuuni Haman de o bia da-kwollu yera ne. 26Haman ya na tage ‘Pura’ jɔrɔ kom to ŋwaane, ba laam ma lɛɛre ba jege kuri dem konto da yam ba bwoi we ‘Purim’. Juu tiina bam déem sɛ kolo Modekayi tɔnɔ kom na bere-ba se ba taa ke to se ba taa gula kolo maama na yi-ba to. 27Konto ŋwaane ba ma lɛɛre ba sɛ se da yam konto yalei taa zege ya pa-ba, se ba de ba bia, dedaane wolo maama na wó ba o woli ba wone to taa di ywoni. Ba ta ma sɛ se ba tɔge Modekayi ni dem se ba yɔɔre ba di kuri dem bene maama ne, nenɛɛne ko ná yeini ko yi ka maŋa kam. 28Juu tiina bam maama jege se ba jwa jwa taa yei da yalei yam konto ni ne, se ba di Purim kuri dem sɔŋɔ maama ne, de teo de kateiri maama wone, se ba de ba dwi dem yé swei ya ni ne se ko taa vei wuu.
29Ka-pɛ Ɛseta na ye Abihali bu to ma zege Juu tu Modekayi kwaga ne, ye o daare o popone tɔnɔ se ko pa ni delo Modekayi na popone Purim kuri dem ŋwaane to taa jege kuri. 30Ba déem ma pa se twanno yi Juu tiina balo maama na zoore Pɛ Zeregese paare dim laŋa kam kateira bi de finlei-yarepɛ (127) maama wone to. Twanno tem maa tɛ yazura de chega zegem taane mo. 31Te ta ma bere Juu tiina de ba dwi dem se ba tiŋi da yam konto ba di Purim kuri dem nenɛɛne ka maŋa ná yeini ka yi bene maama wone. Ba wó taa ke nenɛɛne Juu tu Modekayi de ka-pɛ Ɛseta na pɛ-ba ni se ba ke tei to, se ko tɔge ba na maŋe ba ke tei ye ba yeini ba vɔ ni wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane tei to.
32Ɛseta ni dem konto déem pɛ se Purim kuri dim chullu tem zege. Ba popone-de mo ba ke tɔnɔ wone.

english_text:
The Greatness of Xerxes and Mordecai
1King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea. 2All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai. 3Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_text:
Pɛ Zeregese dedaane Modekayi na ye nɔn-yum tei to
1Pɛ Zeregese déem fe nɔɔna balo maama na zoore o paare dim laŋa kam wone to se ba taa ŋwe lampwoo ba pa‑o, ko ná maŋe ko ye balo na zoore naneo ni yiga yiga seeni to de. 2Pɛ wom déem nam na mɛ o dam o ke wo-kamuna yalo maama to, ko woli de o déem na zeiŋi Modekayi wɛɛne pa se o di dam baŋa tei to, mo ba popone te maama ba ke Media de Peresia pwa yera seina twanno tem wone. 3Modekayi déem ye Juu tu mo. O déem nam jege dam o saŋe Pɛ Zeregese yerane kwaga mo. O maa jege yere o dwoi Juu tiina bam maama. O dwonna Juu tiina bam déem maa tiini ba nege‑o, o na toŋe o woli-ba, ye o daare o beeri ba de ba dwi dem yazura to ŋwaane.

english_text:
Job and His Family
1Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
2Job had 7 sons and 3 daughters. 3He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pair of oxen, 500 donkeys, and a large number of servants. He was the richest person in the East.
4Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking. 5After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God.
Angels, the Lord, and Satan
6 One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them, 7the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
8Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
9 “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked. 10“You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere. 11Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
12The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.”
Then Satan left.
Job Loses Everything
13Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son, 14when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass, 15a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
16That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
17Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
18That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son, 19when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
20When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God 21 and said:
“We bring nothing at birth;
we take nothing
with us at death.
The Lord alone gives and takes.
Praise the name of the Lord!”
22In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_text:
Setaana pɛ na maŋe Job tei to
1Nɔɔno déem mo wora, o yere mo Job. O maa zoore Yuzi teo kom wone. O kikia déem tɔge chwoŋa mo, ye tusim tera. O maa kɔre Wɛ, pa se o yɔɔre o cho o tete de lwarem. 2O déem jege bakeiri serepɛ de bukwa batɔ mo. 3O maa jege pei morro terepɛ (7,000), de kona morro tetɔ (3,000), de nabɛ moro (1,000), de bonɛ bia yanu (500). O ta maa jege tontoŋena dedɛ pa ba toŋe ba pa‑o. Chega to, wonto déem mo ye nadum o dwoi wɛ-puli jei sem nɔɔna maama.
4Job bakeiri sem déem yeini ba ke kuri-fɔrɔ mo ba leira ba pa daane. Ba ma yeini ba bwoŋi daane se ba maama jeeri ba di wodiu ba daare ba nyɔ sana ba dedoa sɔŋɔ ne, ye ba ta ba nakwa batɔ bam se ba de da ba jeeri. 5Job bia bam ná yeini ba di kuri ba ti, o laam wó bwoŋi-ba mo se o kwɛ-ba de chullu tem. O ma yeini o zaŋe tetete o kwei vara o ke zwɛɛm kaanem bu maama ŋwaane. Maŋa maama o yeini o ke konto dwoŋi, bɛŋwaane o yeini o boŋe o tete ne mo o we, “Dɛ delo a bia bam tusi mo ye ba lwɛ Wɛ ba bochwanno wone.”
6Dɛ dedwe mo wɛyuu nɔn-kɔgɔ kom tu ba jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Setaana pɛ de ma da o zo ba wone. 7Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo zege yei ne mo n ba ywo?”
Setaana pɛ de ma leiri Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A yɔɔre a kare tega kam baŋa ne mo a kekara.”
8 Baŋa Wɛ daa maa we, “N nam maane n nii a tontoŋeno Job na ye tei to na? Tega baŋa nɔɔna maama wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na ye nɔn-ŋom ne wonto na ye tei to. O yɔɔre o tɔge chwoŋa mo, ye o ba jege tusim. O maa kɔre Wɛ, pa se o cho o tete de lwarem kikia.”
9Setaana pɛ ma leiri Wɛ o we, “Job nam na kɔre Wɛ tei to ye kafɛ ŋwaane mo na? 10Nmo yeini n kwoli‑o mo se kolokolo yé yi‑o. N ta kwoli o diga tiina de o jejegero maama de mo, ye n daare n pa se kolo maama o na ke to yeini ko ke lanyerane ko pa‑o. Nii o na jege vara dedɛ pa ba su teo kom ni maama tei! 11N nam ná twe n jeŋa pa se kolo maama o na jege to ti ko daare‑o, o laam wó yɔɔre o lwɛ nmo jaja.”
12 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Setaana pɛ o we, “Tɔ! A kwei o jeŋa woŋo maama a ke nmo dam kuri ne. Nam yé ke o tete yera yam kolokolo.”
Setaana pɛ ma yage Baŋa Wɛ tei ye o viiri.
13Dɛ dedwe mo Job bia bam maama déem jei o bakeiri-kwea kam sɔŋɔ ne ba di kuri-fɔrɔ, ye ba daare ba nyɔ sana. 14Nɔɔno ma duri o vo o yi Job tei o we, “Dé ya jege n nabɛ sem dé vare mo, ye n bonɛ sem de zege se bwola dáane se di gaao. 15Seba tiina badwonna ma pɔpɔ ba zaŋe dé baŋa ne, ye ba kale te maama ba ja ba viiri. Ba ta ma go n tontoŋena bam maama. Amo yerane mo wane a lu se a ba a ta kolo na ke to a bere‑m.”
16O ta na wora o tɛ taane dem o bere‑o to mo nɔɔno wodwoŋi de yia. O de ma ta de Job o we, “Doa mo nwoŋi wɛyuu ne ka ba ka bage n pei sem de n tontoŋena bam maama ka go. Amo yerane mo wane a lu se a ba a ta kolo na ke to a bere‑m.”
17O ta na wora o tɛ taane dem to mo nɔɔno wodwoŋi de yia. O de ma ta de Job o we, “Chaladea tiina bam jar-keira chɛ ba tete kuni betɔ mo, ye ba pɔpɔ ba zo n kona yam wone ba kale ya maama ba ja ba viiri. Ba ta ma go n tontoŋena bam maama. Amo yerane mo wane a lu se a ba a ta kolo na ke to a bere‑m.”
18O ta na wora o tɛ taane dem to mo nɔɔno wodwoŋi de yia. O de ma ta de Job o we, “N bia bam ya wo n bu-kwea kam sɔŋɔ ne mo ba di kuri-fɔrɔ, ye ba nyɔ sana. 19Vo-fɔrɔ ma pɔpɔ ko nwoŋi kagoa kam seeni ko ba de dam, ye ko mage sɔŋɔ kom sɛ sem maama pa ko to ko pane ba maama ko go. Amo yerane mo wane a lu se a ba a ta kolo na ke to a bere‑m.”
20Job na nigi konto maama to, o ma zaŋe o zege wɛɛne o ja o gɔrɔ o kaare wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. O ma cheeri o yuu ye o daare o vwi o yibia tega ne o zuli Wɛ. 21O maa we:
“A na nwoŋi a nu puga ne a beene logo baŋa to, a tu bwori mo. A nam ná lage a yage logo kom, a ta wó viiri bwori mo. Baŋa Wɛ ya mo pɛ-ne a wonnu tem maama, ye o daa jwoori o jwoŋi-te. Baŋa Wɛ yere dem nam ta maŋe de tia.”
22De kolo maama na ke to de, Job wo ke wɛleere. O nam wo poone Wɛ we o tusi.

english_text:
Job Loses His Health
1When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them, 2and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
3Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
4Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive. 5Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
6“All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.” 7Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
8Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery, 9his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
10Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God.
Job's Three Friends
11Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him. 12When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly. 13For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_text:
Setaana pɛ daa ta na maŋe Job tei to
1Maŋa daa ma yi se wɛyuu nɔɔna bam jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Setaana pɛ de ma da o zo ba wone o zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. 2Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei Setaana pɛ o we, “Nmo zege yei ne mo n ba ywo?”
Setaana pɛ de ma leiri Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A yɔɔre a kare tega kam baŋa ne mo a kekara.”
3 Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta o we, “N nam maane n nii a tontoŋeno Job na ye tei to na? Tega baŋa nɔɔna maama wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na ye nɔn-ŋom ne wonto na ye tei to. O kikia tɔge chwoŋa mo, ye o ba jege tusim. O maa kɔre Wɛ, pa se o yɔɔre o cho o tete de lwarem. Nmo nam soge-ne pa a yage chwoŋa se o na chɔgem kafɛ ŋwaane. De ko de, Job ta zege de o chega mo, ne o na maŋe o ye tei to.”
4Setaana pɛ ma leiri o we, “Nɔɔno ya-nɔna jege kuri ya pa‑o! Konto tu wó kwei o woŋo maama o dole o yage se o wane o jwoŋi o ŋwea. 5N nam ná twe n jeŋa n pa o na zonne o yera yam wone, o laam wó yɔɔre o lwɛ‑m jaja.”
6 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de Setaana pɛ o we, “Tɔ! A kwei o maama a ke n dam kuri ne. Nam yé le o ŋwea kam.”
7Setaana pɛ ma yage Baŋa Wɛ tei. O ma vo o kwei ŋɔn-zana o ke Job yera yam maama ne, ko zege o napera yam ne se ko vo ko yi o yuu kom maama. 8Job maa jei tampuuri teiŋa ne wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. O ma kwei kanchua o jege o zae o yera yam.
