9O kaane ma yi o tei ye o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo ta zege de n chega mo na? Nam yɔɔre n lwɛ Wɛ, se n ná wó te se n te.”
10Job ma leiri‑o o we, “Ja n jworim dem n lage jei! Wɛ ná pɛ debam wo-laaro, dé bá tei je selei mo dé jwoŋi-te na? Bɛŋwaane mo o ná toŋe lɛɛro o pa debam, se dé ve?”
De Job na zo cham dem maama wone to de, o wo ke wɛleere o ni taane baŋa ne.
Job badwonna batɔ bam yera taane
11Job déem jege badwonna batɔ, ba na ye Teman tu Elifaza, de Suuhi tu Bilidad, de Naamatia tu Zofara. Ba ma ni lɛɛro telo na yi Job to ni ne. Ba ma zaŋe ba sam ne ba tɔge daane de ni dedwe se ba vo ba ŋwane ba pa Job, se ba daare ba zuri o bochare. 12Ba ta na vei ba beene o tei ye ba tole ba na‑o to, ba wo lɔre‑o lela. Ba laam ma bobo se ba laare de kwor-dɛa. Ba ma kaare ba gwaaro tem, ye ba daare ba kwei kasolo ba taare ba yuni tem, ba wo na tiini ko chɔge to ŋwaane. 13Ba ma fɔɔre ba yi o yera ba jeini tega ne, da yarepɛ wea de tete maama. Ba wolowolo wo wane se o ta taane ded‑o, ba na nɛ o na tiini o yaare to ŋwaane.

english_text:
Job's First Speech
Blot Out the Day of My Birth
1 Finally, Job cursed the day
of his birth
2by saying to God:
3Blot out the day of my birth
and the night when my parents
created a son.
4Forget about that day,
cover it with darkness,
5and send thick, gloomy shadows
to fill it with dread.
6Erase that night from the calendar
and conceal it with darkness.
7Don't let children be created
or joyful shouts be heard
ever again in that night.
8Let those with magic powers
place a curse on that day.
9Darken its morning stars
and remove all hope of light,
10because it let me be born
into a world of trouble.
Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
11Why didn't I die at birth?
12Why was I accepted
and allowed to nurse
at my mother's breast?
13Now I would be at peace
in the silent world below
14with kings and their advisors
whose palaces lie in ruins,
15and with rulers once rich
with silver and gold.
16I wish I had been born dead
and then buried, never to see
the light of day.
17In the world of the dead,
the wicked and the weary rest
without a worry.
* 18Everyone is there—
19where captives and slaves
are free at last.
Why Does God Let Me Live?
20Why does God let me live
when life is miserable
and so bitter?
21 I keep longing for death
more than I would seek
a valuable treasure.
22Nothing could make me happier
than to be in the grave.
23Why do I go on living
when God has me surrounded,
and I can't see the road?
24Moaning and groaning
are my food and drink,
25and my worst fears
have all come true.
26I have no peace or rest—
only troubles and worries.
translation_text:
Job tɛ o yaara yam taane
1Ko na ke fee to, Job ma ga ga o puri o ni ye o poone o lora dɛ dem pompona. 2O ma ta o we,
3“A lora dɛ dem ya na jigi kafɛ,
ko gara.
Tete delo wone ba na tage we
ba loge bakeira to,
de taa ye kafɛ!
4Ko maŋe se dɛ dem konto
wea kam pipiri ka ji lim mo.
Wɛ na wo wɛyuu ne to daa yé guli
dɛ dem konto gula kɔtaa.
Pwooni de nam yé nye de wone.
5Pa se lim yɔɔre de kwoli
dɛ dem konto liira liira,
ye kunkwoŋo li tega kam maama,
pa se jei maama yɔɔre se zwori tim-tim.
6Ta pa se tete dem konto maama
taa ye yibiri yerane.
De dae se de tɔge de gwaane
bene dem da wone,
se ba yé jeeli-de chane de chane da yam wone.
7Yé sɛ se kaane daa ja puga
tete dem konto ne.
Ko dae se nɔɔna bage wopwolo sɔɔ ko wone.
8Pa balo na toŋe jira totoŋa to
sɔɔle lwarem ba yage
a lora dɛ dem baŋa ne.
Banto wae ba pa naneo wo juru
Leviatan zaŋe mo.
9Naŋɔgɔ ya ba jege se ko fuŋi
a lora dɛ dem ne,
se tega yé ba ka poore,
de tete dem ná maŋe de dáane tei maama de.
10Kokuri to, dɛ dem konto wo pɛ
se a nu puga kam kwaale-ne
ka yage da.
Konto ya wó pa se a yé taa nii
a nae cham dento.
11Bɛŋwaane mo ye a wo tege
a lora maŋa ne,
se a ya yɔɔre a maŋe jana wone?
12Bɛ mo kea ye a nu tei o jwoŋi-ne
o tiŋi o nɛ baŋa ne,
ye o daare o ja yele o ke a ni ne
se a taa ŋɔga?
13A ya ná tega a lora maŋa ne mo tento,
a zem ya ba tigi churu ne a sii na?
14Amo ya wó taa jei de tega baŋa pwa de ba nakwa mo.
Banto ya lɔge sɔ-fwaaro
ye te laam ba te chɔge.
15Tento a ya tigi a sii de naduna
balo sabu-seŋa déem na daga
ye ba sam dem de su
de lu-nyenno wonnu dedɛ to mo.
16Ko déem ná ke ne ba loge-ne
ba de bu-too mo, ko gara.
Ba ya wó suli-ne tega ne,
ne bu-seseŋa kalo na wo nɛ
logo pwooni to dwoŋi.
17Churu ne, puseŋ-nyena yeini
ba sii de ba lwia yam.
Balo yera ya na chɛ to
de laam sii mo falalala.
18Peena tete de jei daane
de bochare-zuru mo,
balo ya na fe-ba to daa na ba bage-ba to ŋwaane.
19Nɔɔna maama wo dáane mo,
nabwona de naduna.
Kabɛ de yɔɔre se tei se tete mo
jei sem konto ne.
20Ko ná ye wolo cham na jege‑o to,
bɛ mo ye Wɛ yeini o pa kotu na wea pwooni?
Bɛŋwaane mo Wɛ pae balo teena na ti to daa taa ŋwe?
21Nɔɔna banto dwoŋi yɔɔre ba chare toone mo se de ba de ja-ba,
ye de ve se de ba.
Ba ma kwaane ba beeri toone ba ga,
ne nɔɔno na wó ko bɔɔne
o beeri jejegero na seigi tega ne tei to.
22Ba ŋwea nam ná tu ka ti
pa se ba suli-ba tega kuri ne,
ba laam wó di ywoni lanyerane mo.
23Ko ná ye nɔɔno wolo Wɛ na chege o chwoŋa
pa se o yeiri o na wó vo mɛ to,
bɛ mo ye Wɛ pa se kotu daa taa jege ŋwea?
24Sisigim mo leiri a ni-wodiu yuu ne.
A ta yɔɔre a suuri mo,
ne na na chuuri ba nwoŋa
a ni ne tei to.
25Amo ya na kɔre we kolo wó yi-ne to mo tu amo baŋa.
A maa na jege lwia de woŋo kolo to mo yɔɔre ko yi-ne.
26A bere a ba nae a tete.
A wo de nam ba tiga.
A bá wane a sii.
Lwia yerane mo yɔɔre ya jege-ne taa.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's First Speech
Please Be Patient and Listen
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2Please be patient and listen
to what I have to say.
* 3Remember how your words
4have guided and encouraged
many in need.
5But now you feel discouraged
when struck by trouble.
6You respect God and live right,
so don't lose hope!
7No truly innocent person
has ever died young.
8In my experience, only those
who plant seeds of evil
harvest trouble,
9and then they are swept away
by the angry breath of God.
10They may roar and growl
like powerful lions.
But when God breaks their teeth,
11they starve, and their children
are scattered.
A Secret Was Told to Me
12A secret was told to me
in a faint whisper—
13 I was overcome by sleep,
but disturbed by dreams;
14I trembled with fear,
15and my hair stood on end,
as a wind blew past my face.
16It stopped and stood still.
Then a form appeared—
a shapeless form.
And from the silence,
I heard a voice say,
17“No humans are innocent
in the eyes of God
their Creator.
18He finds fault with his servants
and even with his angels.
19Humans are formed from clay
and are fragile as moths,
so what chance do you have?
20Born after daybreak,
you die before nightfall
and disappear forever.
21Your tent pegs are pulled up,
and you leave this life,
having gained no wisdom.”
translation_text:
Elifaza na bobo o ta kolo to
1Teman tu Elifaza ma leiri Job o we:
2“Nɔɔno ná tage taane dede‑m,
n bá‑n zuri n yera na?
Amo nam daa ware se a taa ye chemm.
3Jeeli n nii nmo daama na bere nɔɔna dedɛ tei to.
N ta pɛ se balo vɔna na pare to na dam.
4N ni taane woli balo ya na saare ba toe to mo,
pa ba jwoori ba zege deiki.
Balo nagwola na tege to de ma na baare.
5Cham laam na yi nmo tete baŋa to,
n dɛ ko baŋa ne mo ye n vɔna pare.
Ko na zoore n yera to, n nagwola tege mo.
6Nmo nam na kɔre Wɛ tei to mo
bá pa‑m baare na?
N ma‑n na ba jege tusim
Wɛ chwoŋa wone to mo
bá pa se n teena taa wo o wone na?
7Nam fɔge n jeeli n nii:
Wɔ mo seene o jege bora
pa o pɔpɔ o te lela?
Yein-seeni mo nmo wó na we
chɔgem yi balo na yɔɔre ba tɔge chwoŋa to?
8Amo na maane tei to,
balo na dugi lwarem naa cham to
wó zage-te mo.
9Wɛ ná sii o yage ba yera ne,
ba wó chɔge ba ti mo.
10Nywonnu mo yeini te suuri
ye te ŋuuri de dam.
De ko de, Wɛ mo pae nywon-kamuna yeila gura.
11Konto to, nywoŋo ná gɛ varem se ko ja ko di,
ko wó te mo, ye ko bia de jage.
Mo ko na wó ke puseŋ-nyena tei to.
12Ba daane ba waase taane
ba bere-ne,
pa se a wo nigi-de a ti.
13Dɔɔne ya tiini de jege-ne tete ne,
ye a dwɛ dendwa yalo
na daane-ne to.
14Foone ma yɔɔre de ja-ne,
ye a yera sae pa se a nagwola mage daane.
15Ko ke ne vio mo dole
a yibia seeni,
pa se waaro da te zo-ne
foone ŋwaane.
16Ko laam ma zege da chemm.
A maa wo lɔre ko na ye woŋo kolo to.
Ko nyenyego wo a yiga ne mo,
ye a ni kwora na waase ka we:
17‘Nabiinu wó wane o yɔɔre o taa jege chega Wɛ tei ne na?
O ta wó wane o taa ye wose
o Keiru wom yiga ne na?
18Ko ná maŋe ko ye Wɛ malese tete,
o ba ke o teena se wone,
o na nɛ we se ke se sa se chwoŋa to ŋwaane.
19Nabiina nam ye dɔgɔ mo Wɛ mɛ
o ke ba yera yam,
ye ba kuri nwoŋi teero wone.
Banto yɔɔre ba bwona
ba dwoi tóa na ye tei to mo.
20Tega ná yeini ka poore,
nabiinu ŋwe mo,
ye tega na beene se ka yi to,
de kotu nɛ chɔgem.
O laam yeini o jei mo
ye nɔɔna daa ba guli o gula.
21Ba maa vaŋe kotu wonnu maama
ba le ba daare‑o.
O laam ma ba o te
ye o wo nɛ yi-poro.’ ”

english_text:
Eliphaz Continues
Call Out for Help
1Job, call out for help
and see if an angel comes!
2Envy and jealousy
will kill a stupid fool.
3I have seen fools take root.
But God sends a curse,
suddenly uprooting them
4and leaving their children
helpless in court.
5Then hungry and greedy people
gobble up their crops
and grab their wealth.
6Our suffering isn't caused
by the failure of crops;
7it's all part of life,
like sparks shooting skyward.
8Job, if I were you,
I would ask God for help.
9 His miracles are marvelous,
more than we can count.
10God sends showers on earth
and waters the fields.
11He protects the sorrowful
and lifts up those
who have been disgraced.
* 12God swiftly traps the wicked
13 in their own evil schemes,
and their wisdom fails.
14Darkness is their only companion,
hiding their path at noon.
15God rescues the needy
from the words of the wicked
and the fist of the mighty.
16The poor are filled with hope,
and injustice is silenced.
Consider Yourself Fortunate
17 Consider yourself fortunate
if God All-Powerful
chooses to correct you.
18 He may cause injury and pain,
but he will bandage and heal
your cuts and bruises.
19God will protect you from harm,
no matter how often
trouble may strike.
20In times of war and famine,
God will keep you safe.
21You will be sheltered,
without fear of hurtful words
or any other weapon.
22You will laugh at the threat
of destruction and famine.
And you won't be afraid
of wild animals—
23they will no longer be fierce,
and your rocky fields
will become friendly.
24Your home will be secure,
and your sheep will be safe.
25You will have more descendants
than there are blades of grass
on the face of the earth.
26You will live a very long life,
and your body will be strong
until the day you die.
27Our experience has proven
these things to be true,
so listen and learn.
translation_text:
Elifaza ta ma ta de Job o we:
1“Chwoosi n bwoŋi n nii
nɔɔno wó ba na?
Malese sem wone wɔ mo wó ba
o woli‑m?
2Ban-wira goe jworru mo lela,
ye kazwe de chɔge nayeiri-nyena.
3Amo yi nɛ jworru kugu
na jaane tega chekke,
ye lɛɛro laam yi-ba lela,
de ba sɔŋɔ kom maama.
4Ba bia daa ba jege woro
se ba jeini ko kuri ne.
Ba maa wó vane banto bora,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na wó zege ba kwaga ne.
5Kana na jege balo to laam wó di
banto kara wodiiru faao ni ne mo,
ko ná maŋe ko ye telo na chege
sabare wone to de.
Na-nyɔm na jege balo to fera
wó zo ba jejegero tem.
6Kokuri to, cham ba ke tega ne,
nenɛɛne wodiiru na ke tega ne tei to.
Yaara de nam ba tae
ya nwoŋi tega kam ne.
7De ko de, ba lore nabiina
ba de cham wone mo,
ne min-cheŋo na parese
ko jaane wɛɛne tei to.
8Ko ya ná ye amo mo tento,
a wó ja Wɛ teiŋa mo,
ye a kwei a taane dem
a tiŋi o yiga ne.
9O yeini o ke wo-kamuna
ye dé ba ni ya kura dé tia.
Dé maa bá wane wo-kenkagela
yalo o na ke to dé ga dé ti.
10Wonto mo pa se doa nene
tega baŋa ne,
se na wane ba bugi pwola ni maama.
11Wɛ mo pae balo na zoore ba tete tega ne to
jwoori ba diini baŋa.
Balo de na jei ba keeri to mo
o pa ba nae dalem jei.
12O maa vugimi balo na yei tega to boboŋa yam,
pa se ba na jeeli kikia yalo to
ba toŋa.
13O ta maa vugimi swa tiina swa yam
pa ya jwoori ya ja-ba.
Ba boboŋa yam maama jigi vio
ya jei.
14Lim mo kwoli-ba wea tetare ne,
ye ba kare we-bere maŋa ne
ba taana ne lilwoa to.
15Wɛ jwoŋi nabwona mo o yaga
de dedɛɛra ta-balwaaro tem
na chɔge-ba tei to.
O maa vere-ba o jaane o nwoŋa
balo na bɛɛse-ba to jeŋa ne.
16Ko maa pae yiniga tiina jege teena,
ye balo na kweele chega kam to
laam pu ba nia.
17Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom na korese wolo to jege yu-ywoŋo.
Konto ŋwaane yé gwooni
o koresem dem.
18Kokuri, o yeini o ke zonne
nɔɔna yera ne.
O nam wó vɔ ba fufwollu tem.
O maa ná de cham nɔɔno wolo yera ne,
o je sem ta wó yɔɔre kotu.
19Lɛɛro ná yi nmo kuni beredo,
Wɛ wó taa kwoli‑m.
Cham ná maŋe de ye tei maama
de daŋe da-baŋa ne,
de bá di‑m.
20Da-kore maŋa ne
o ta wó jwoŋi‑m o yage,
se kana yé go‑m.
Jara de ná to logo kom ne de,
se-zɔɔ bá di nmo.
21Nɔɔna ná jege‑m ba twea,
Wɛ wó kwoli‑m
se ba ta-balwaaro tem yé wane‑m kolokolo te ke.
Chɔgem de maa ná lage de ba,
nmo bá‑n ta‑n kɔre foone.
22Chega to, chɔgem de kana ná yia,
nmo wó ta‑n jege-te n gwoona mo.
Ko ta ná ye kago-vara de,
ko dae se n ta‑n kɔre foone de-ba.
23Ko na ye tei to, nmo wó ke
ni-mɔrɔ dedaane kandwa
yalo na tigi n kara kam wone to.
Kago-vara de nam bá taa daane‑m.
24Nmo wó ta‑n yei lanyerane we
n kugu jei sem tigi falalala mo.
N ta ná jeeli n vara bam n nii,
ba dedoa tete de bá jei.
25Nmo wó lɔre we n bia kɔgɔ lage ko gaale,
ye n naaro de puli mo,
ne tega baŋa gaaro tem na ye tei to.
26Nmo ŋwea maa wó dáane
tega baŋa ne.
N ta wó ta‑n dana mo se n vo n te,
ne mena na yeini ya be
ye ba laam zage-ya tei to.
27Dé boŋe wonnu tento maama boboŋa mo
ye dé yei we te ye chega.
Konto ŋwaane,
cheigi dé na tage kolo to,
se n daare n ma-ko n toŋe.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
It's Impossible
1Job said:
2It's impossible to weigh
my misery and grief!
3They outweigh the sand
along the beach,
and that's why I have spoken
without thinking first.
4The fearsome arrows
of God All-Powerful
have filled my soul
with their poison.
5Do oxen and wild donkeys
cry out in distress
unless they are hungry?
6What is food without salt?
What is more tasteless
than the white of an egg?
7That's how my food tastes,
and my appetite is gone.
* 8How I wish that God
would answer my prayer
9and do away with me.
10Then I would be comforted,
knowing that in all of my pain
I have never disobeyed God.
11Why should I patiently hope
when my strength is gone?
12I am not strong as stone
or bronze,
13and I have finally reached
the end of my rope.
My Friends, I Am Desperate
14My friends, I am desperate,
and you should help me,
even if I no longer respect
God All-Powerful.
* 15But you are treacherous
16like streams that swell
with melting snow,
17then suddenly disappear
in the summer heat.
18I am like a caravan,
lost in the desert
while searching for water.
19Caravans from Tema and Sheba
20thought they would find water.
But they were disappointed,
21just as I am with you.
Only one look at my suffering,
and you run away scared.
What Have I Done Wrong?
22Have I ever asked any of you
to give me a gift
23or to purchase my freedom
from brutal enemies?
24What have I done wrong?
Show me,
and I will keep quiet.
25The truth is always painful,
but your arguments
prove nothing.
26Here I am desperate,
and you consider my words
as worthless as wind.
27Why, you would sell an orphan
or your own neighbor!
28Look me straight in the eye;
I won't lie to you.
29Stop accusing me falsely;
my reputation is at stake.
30I know right from wrong,
and I am not telling lies.
translation_text:
Job daa na leiri tei to
1Job ma leiri o we:
2“Ko ná ye amo ban-wira kam,
de a wo-chechɔgɔ kom,
ba ya ná wae-te ba kwei
ba maŋe te dunni,
3te ya wó dwoni naneo ni kasolo kom maama na mae tei to.
Konto ŋwaane mo nam pɛ se
a lɔgere a ŋɔɔne yɔɔ yɔɔ.
4Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom mo kwei
che-tɛɛra o zɔ-ne,
pa se ya vea kam yɔɔre
ka zoore a yera.
Wɛ jeeri amo mo de o chanɛɛra yam pa ya fugi-ne.
5Ko ná ye bonɛ selo na ware se ja to,
se ná nɛ ga-lɛɛro se se di,
se ta wó taa kare se keeri mo na?
Naane de ná nɛ wodiu,
de wó taa ye chemm mo.
6Wodiu kolo na ba jege yɛ to
zoore ni na?
Chechare napwoŋo jei sem ywoni
nam wo yein-seeni mo?
7Wodiu ná ye konto dwoŋi
a ware-ko se a di.
Ko yɔɔre ko lwoi a momwa ne mo.
8Ko ya ná wae se Wɛ ke amo na lwoori‑o kolo to o pa-ne na!
Konto mo ya wó pa a na jei
a teene kolo to seene ko ke.
9O ya ná sɛ se o yɔɔre o meere-ne,
pa se a ŋwea guri, ko gara.
10Konto mo ya wó pa a wo taa tiga.
A ya wó di ywoni,
de a ná maŋe a na zonne dedɛ
a yera ne tei maama de.
Kokuri, a cham dem maama wone,
a wo ve Wo-pwoŋo Tu
Wɛ wom ni kɔtaa!
11Amo dam daa wo yein-seeni mo,
se a ta taa jege teena?
Bɛ nyɔɔre daa mo wora se amo na,
pa ko maŋe se a taa peena
a bane to?
12Amo bere a jege peo dam dwoŋi mo na?
A yera yam nam ye channa mo
ba mɛ ba ke-ya na?
13A dam ti ye a daa ware a tete
se a jwoŋi a yage.
A ya na teege mɛ maama to
kɛ ko daare-ne.
14Nɔɔno teena ná ti,
o badwonna ta maŋe
se ba ta taa swoi‑o mo,
de o ná maŋe o yage
Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ kɔrɔ kom de.
15Amo yuudwonna bam bochwanno
nam ba ŋwae dedɛ.
Ba nye de nabare selo
na ba dáane se we to mo.
Se wó su se pɛɛle
ye se na bam laam duri ba kɛ.
16Yadɛ ne se maa yeini se su,
ye kunu de kwoli-se.
17Se na bam nam we mo te-pwoŋa ne.
Wulim maŋa ne se bu-nwaro tem de maa ga na.
18Pipim-piina na kare kagoa yuu ne
ba vei to mo wó ywori
ba chwoŋa kam ne se ba beeri na.
Ba maa beeri na bam ba ga
ye ba jei kagoa kam wone.
19Tema teo pipiu tiina bam kare
ba beeri na mo.
Seba teo bein-beera bam
de jege na teena mo.
20Ba boboŋa ya jaane we
ba wó na na mo.
Ba nam na yi da to,
mo ba kɔge teena yam konto jworo,
ye lwia tiini ya ja-ba.
21Nam nii-na!
Abam de maŋe á ba sii zore.
Á na yɔɔre á na chanɛɛre delo
na yi amo to,
mo foone tiini de ja abam.
22Amo nam wo fɔge a ta de abam we,
‘Kwei-na woŋo á pa-ne,
se á le á jejegero wone á ma
á tiŋi daare amo ŋwaane.’
23A ta wo tage a we, á jwoŋi-ne-na
á yage a dona jeŋa ne,
naa á ŋwe-na sabu se á vere-ne
á ja á nwoŋi nankɔ-nyena jeŋa ne.
24Nam ta-na á bere-ne
mɛ seeni a na tusi to,
se a pu a ni ye a daa bá ta taane.
25Chega jei ye ŋɔn-zane mo,
se á bwɛa yam nam lage ya woli tetɛ seeni mo?
26Á boŋe se á yaale-ne a ni taane dem ŋwaane mo na?
Amo teena maama jei mo,
ye á gwooni amo ni taane we
ko ye vio yerane.
27Chega to, abam wó wane á ta jɔrɔ
se á ma á yeigi botara.
Á ta wó kwei á badwonna á pa
se á ma-ba á jwoŋi wo-gɛ.
28Nam pipiri-na á nii amo seeni!
Kokuri, amo bá gane abam.
29Yage-na á bwɛa yam!
Yé kweele-na a chega kam
á se tega ne.
Ko nam maŋe se a na a bora mo.
30Vwa mo a jege a fɔe na?
Lɛɛro yi-ne ye a wo wane-te a lɔre na?”

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Is Life So Hard?
1Why is life so hard?
Why do we suffer?
2We are slaves in search of shade;
we are laborers longing
for our wages.
3God has made my days drag on
and my nights miserable.
4I pray for night to end,
but it stretches out
while I toss and turn.
5My parched skin is covered
with worms, dirt, and sores,
6and my days are running out
quicker than the thread
of a fast-moving needle.
Don't Forget!
7I beg you, God, don't forget!
My life is just a breath,
and trouble lies ahead.
8I will vanish from sight,
and no one, including you,
will ever see me again.
9 I will disappear in the grave
or vanish from sight
like a passing cloud.
10Never will I return home;
soon I will be forgotten.
11And so, I cry out to you
in agony and distress.
12Am I the sea or a sea monster?
Is that why you imprison me?
13I go to bed, hoping for rest,
14but you torture me
with terrible dreams.
* 15I'd rather choke to death
than live in this body.
16Leave me alone and let me die;
my life has no meaning.
17 What makes you so concerned
about us humans?
18Why do you test us
from sunrise to sunset?
19Won't you look away
just long enough
for me to swallow?
20Why do you watch us so closely?
What's it to you, if I sin?
Why am I your target
and such a heavy burden?
21Why do you refuse to forgive?
Soon you won't find me,
because I'll be dead.
translation_text:
Job ta ma ta o we:
1“Nabiinu yeini o toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛra mo
o logo baŋa ŋwea maama wone.
O yera ma chɛ dɛ maama wone,
nenɛɛne ba na jene nɔɔno wolo
se o taa toŋe to.
2Kabaa yɔɔre o teena
se wɛ dem guni ye tega yi.
Tontoŋeno de maa jei o teena
se o jwoŋi o ŋweero.
3Konto mo amo de toŋe kafɛ ŋwaane chana maama wone.
Ŋweero telo a na yeini a jwoŋi to
ye wo-chechɔgɔ yerane mo
tete maama ne.
4Tete ne a tigi a sara ne
ye a boŋe mo a we,
‘Tega wó poore lela se a zaŋe na?’
Tega de ma ve se ka poore,
pa se a tigi a sara kam ne
a pipira taa.
5Amo yera maama nwoŋi kanzwa mo,
ye ya su de ŋɔna yalo na kuuri to.
Mwara de maa nwoŋa.
6Amo ŋwea da yam wora ya ti mo lela,
ne gare-yi doleno na dole
o gare-yi tei lela lela to.
Ya maa wó yi ya kweelim jei
ye teena tera ya pa-ne.
7Amo Tu Wɛ, popo guli
amo ŋwea kam gula
ne ka na lage ka jei lela
ne vio tei to.
Amo maa da bá fɔge a na
ŋwea ywoni.
8Chega to, yia yalo zem na nae amo to daa bá na-ne.
Nmo tete de wó beeri amo jei n ga mo,
a na tera to ŋwaane.
9Ko nye de kunkwoŋo na wora
pa ko pɔpɔ ko jage ko jei tei to mo.
Wolo maama ná tega ye o zo tega kuri,
kotu daa bá jwoori tega baŋa.
10O daa bá wane o sɔŋɔ se o jwoori.
Nɔɔna ma swei o ni ne,
nenɛɛne o ya ga maŋe o tera mo to.
11Konto ŋwaane nam mo pɛ se
a bá taa chem.
Amo nam wó tole a yaara yam taane jaja,
a bochare na tiini de di to ŋwaane.
A maa wó ŋwane Wɛ yiga ne,
a bane na wɔe to ŋwaane.
12Bɛ mo ke ye n yɔɔre n yere-ne konto se a yé lu?
Nmo pae se amo ye naneo tete mo
naa ko wo juru mo,
pa se n yɔɔre n pe-ne konto dwoŋi?
13Amo nam yeini a teena we,
a ná zo se a peini a sara ne,
ko wó gare ko pa-ne.
14Nmo nam yeini n kwei dendwa-yɔɔro mo n ma n fugi-ne,
ye n daare n le wonnu telo
na jege foone to n bere-ne.
15Konto ŋwaane mo a boŋe we,
nɔɔno ná tu o peene a momwa se a te,
ko gare a ta ná jege ŋwea kanto dwoŋi a ŋwe.
16A ŋwea kam ye wo-yɔɔ mo
amo tei ne.
A ba lage se a taa ŋwe taa wuu.
Nam dɔne n jeŋa a baŋa ne,
se a ŋwea kam daa ba jege kuri
ka pa-ne.
17Nabiina bere ba ye bɛ mo
pa se n yiga wo ba wone?
Bɛ mo ye n yɔɔre n nii
ba kikia yam konto?
18Tetete maama ne,
nmo yeini n maane
ba na jege kolo ba ke to mo.
Ba ŋwea maŋa maama wone
n ma‑n jege-ba n faŋe n nia.
19N nam bá‑n dɔne n yia n daare-ne
maŋa fenfee wone de na?
N bere n bá‑n pa-ne pwola
se a fi a momwa de?
20Nmo wolo na yere nabiina to,
amo ná maŋe a ke wɛleere mo de,
konto lage ko ke‑m bɛ mo?
Bɛŋwaane mo n yɔɔre n jeeri amo
se n zɔ-ne konto?
Amo nam jigi zele-zane delo
na daane‑m to mo na?
21A ná seene a tusi, bɛ mo ke
pa nmo ware a wɛleera yam
se n yage n ma n chɛ-ne?
Ko nam bá dáane se a te
ye a daare a zo tega.
Nmo ma‑n wó yɔɔre n beeri a jei
n ga, a na tera to ŋwaane.”

english_text:
Bildad's First Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk
and keep saying nothing?
3Does God All-Powerful
stand in the way of justice?
4He made your children pay
for their sins.
5So why don't you turn to him
6and start living right?
Then he will decide
to rescue and restore you
to your place of honor.
7Your future will be brighter
by far than your past.
Our Ancestors Were Wise
8 Our ancestors were wise,
so learn from them.
9Our own time has been short,
like a fading shadow,
and we know very little.
10But they will instruct you
with great understanding.
11Papyrus reeds grow healthy
only in a swamp,
12and if the water dries up,
they die sooner than grass.
13Such is the hopeless future
of all who turn from God
14and trust in something as frail
as a spider's web—
15they take hold and fall
because it's so flimsy.
16Sinful people are like plants
with spreading roots and plenty
of sun and water.
17They wrap their roots tightly
around rocks.
18But once they are pulled up,
they have no more place;
19their life slips away,
and other plants grow there.
20We know God doesn't reject
an innocent person
or help a sinner.
21And so, he will make you happy
and give you something
to smile about.
22But your evil enemies
will be put to shame
and disappear forever.
translation_text:
Bilidad na bobo o ta kolo to
1Suuhi tu Bilidad ma leiri o we:
2“Nmo bere n lage n ŋɔɔne
ta-gwoa yanto
n vo n maŋe yein-seeni mo?
Nmo ni botare sem nye de vio
na fufugi tei to mo.
3Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom wó sɛ
o ja chega kam o ju na?
Wɛ wó wane o kweele chega kam
o se tega ne na?
4Nmo bia bam na ke ba chɔge o yiga to,
konto ŋwaane mo o pɛ se ba na ba wɛleera yam ŋweero.
5Nam ja n tete n kwoni n nii
Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom,
se n daare n ŋwane o yiga ne
se o duri n ŋwaŋa.
6Nmo ná ke konto,
ye n ná yɔɔre n ke n tɔge chwoŋa,
Wɛ wó zaŋe se o jaŋe o pa‑m,
ye o pa n sɔŋɔ kom jwoori
ko zege de chega.
7Nmo jwa wó ba n duni dedɛ,
se ko dwoni n faŋa kam na ye tei to.
8Boŋe n nii ko na ye tei
faŋa kam ne to,
se n lɔre swa yalo
dé nabaara déem na nɛ to.
9Debam ŋwea ye kukua mo
ye dé yeiri kolokolo.
Dé ŋwea da yam ba dáane ye ya jia,
ne lunluŋu na ye tei to.
10Ko nam ná ye faŋa tiina bam,
banto wó wane ba bere‑m yeino,
ye ba ta taana ko nwoŋi
ba yi-poro wone.
11Ko ná dae bwolo tega ne
mɛ na na wora to,
sangɛ ba zaŋa se ke dedwaaro,
nanchan-gullu de nam ba fɔge
te bera.
12Na ná tera, te wó kwaare lela mo
ye te ta wo bege,
se ko dwoni ga-lɛɛro na wó kwaare tei to.
13Wolo maama na swei Wɛ swia to
wó guri konto mo,
pa se o teena yam ti,
o na ve Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem to ŋwaane.
14Kotu na kwei o teena o daŋe mɛ to tiini ko bwona,
ne o na boŋe se o sale
zwollu yera ne tei to mo.
15O ná sale o sɔŋɔ kom yera ne,
ko wó to ko daare‑o mo.
O maa ná zei o jejegero,
te wó jei lela.
16Balo na ve Wɛ to nye de ga-lɛɛro
telo na nɛ na dedɛ
ye wea nye te baŋa ne to mo.
Te ma be lanyerane
ye te jage te yi gaare dem ni maama.
17Te bonno ma zo kandwa-pwoa
te milimi-ya,
pa se te na kugu jei ya tetare ne.
18Ba nam ná vaŋe-te te kuru seeni
ba gɔ ba yage,
jeiga kam konto wó ve-te mo
ye ka ta de-te we,
ka ya maŋe ka wo fɔge ka lɔre-te.
19Gaaro tem konto maa wó ko te te,
se gaaro tedwonna de daa puli tega kam konto ne.
20Wɛ bá fɔge o ve chega tu wolo
na ba jege tusim to.
O nam bá ja nɔn-balɔrɔ jeŋa
se o woli‑o.
21O daa wó pa se n ni su de mwanno,
se n di ywoni
ye n bage wopwolo sɔɔ.
22Ko nam ná ye balo na chuli‑m to,
chaveera mo lage ya di-ba.
Puseŋ-nyena sam dem de wó to
de saare.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
What You Say Is True
1Job said:
2 What you say is true.
No human is innocent
in the sight of God.
3Not once in a thousand times
could we win our case
if we took him to court.
4God is wise and powerful—
who could possibly
oppose him and win?
5When God becomes angry,
he can move mountains
before they even know it.
6God can shake the earth loose
from its foundations
7 or command the sun and stars
to hold back their light.
8God alone stretched out the sky,
stepped on the sea,
9 and set the stars in place—
the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and the stars
in the southern sky.
10Of all the miracles God works,
we cannot understand a one.
11God walks right past me,
without making a sound.
12And if he grabs something,
who can stop him
or raise a question?
13When God showed his anger,
the servants of the sea monster
fell at his feet.
14How, then, could I possibly
argue my case with God?
Though I Am Innocent
15Even though I am innocent,
I can only beg for mercy.
16And if God came into court
when I called him,
he would not hear my case.
17He would strike me with a storm
and increase my injuries
for no reason at all.
18Before I could get my breath,
my miseries would multiply.
19God is much stronger than I am,
and who would call me into court
to give me justice?
20Even if I were innocent,
God would prove me wrong.
21I am not guilty,
but I no longer care
what happens to me.
22What difference does it make?
God destroys the innocent
along with the guilty.
23When a good person dies
a sudden death,
God sits back and laughs.
24And who else but God
blindfolds the judges,
then lets the wicked
take over the earth?
My Life Is Speeding By
25My life is speeding by,
without a hope of happiness.
26Each day passes swifter
than a sailing ship
or an eagle swooping down.
27Sometimes I try to be cheerful
and to stop complaining,
28but my sufferings frighten me,
because I know that God
still considers me guilty.
29So what's the use of trying
to prove my innocence?
30Even if I washed myself
with the strongest soap,
31God would throw me into a pit
of stinking slime, leaving me
disgusting to my clothes.
32God isn't a mere human like me.
I can't put him on trial.
33Who could possibly judge
between the two of us?
34Can someone snatch away
the stick God carries
to frighten me?
35Then I could speak up
without fear of him,
but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_text:
Job na leiri tei to
1Job ma leiri o we:
2“Chega ŋwaane to,
nmo na tage kolo to
ba jege digiru.
Nabiinu nam wó ke tetɛ mo
se o na chega Wɛ yiga ne?
3Nabiinu ná boŋe se o saŋe Wɛ,
Wɛ wó wane o bwei‑o
kuni moro mo,
se kotu yé wane o leiri‑o
kuni dedoa tete de.
4Wonto swa yam mo gaale,
ye o dam dem ba tia!
Wɔ mo wó wane o dwoni de Wɛ
ye o bá to?
5Wɛ yeini o pɔpɔ o guri peero!
O ma daare o tɔge o bane baŋa ne
o vuvugi-te o dole o yage.
6O ta wae o ziziŋi tega kam baŋa maama
pa ka na chwi mɛ to de bibigi.
7O wó bage wea kam
pa se ka daa ba nye,
ye o ta pa chalechwe sem
yé taa nye se pae pwooni.
8Wɛ yerane nam ta mo lware wɛyuu kom
pa se ko tigi palalala.
O ta maa nɔne naneo na-ŋone sem baŋa ne o via.
9O ma ke chalechwe sem yera yera
o tigisi wɛyuu kom ne.
O ta ma pa se tega-kuri seeni chalechwe sem wora.
10O ta toŋe wo-kamunnu telo
dé na ba ni te kuri to,
de wo-kenkagela yalo dé na ware
ya ni dé ga dé ti to mo.
11Wɛ tɔge a jei seeni mo o via
ye a ta ba na‑o.
O na maa kɛ to, amo wo lɔre we
wonto mo maa kɛa.
12O ná chaale woŋo kolo o ja kɛ,
wɔ mo wó wane‑o o gwi?
Wɔ nam mo jege chwoŋa
se o bwei‑o we,
‘Bɛ mo n wora n ke?’
13Wɛ bane ná zaŋe, de ba gwia.
Naneo wo juru Rahaba de ko kwaga kɔgɔ kom maama mo
o chochoge o nɛ kuri ne.
14Konto to, amo nam wó wane
a leiri Wɛ taane dem na?
Amo lage a kuri botare bia tetɛ mo se a leiri‑o?
15Amo ná maŋe a jege bora
tei maama de,
a bá jwoori a leiri o taane dem.
Amo na jege kolo yerane se a wane a ke to maa ye
se a lwoori yibwona o tei ne,
o na ye wolo na di a taane to ŋwaane.
16Amo ná wae Wɛ a saŋe mo,
ye o ná sɛ se o jeeri de,
a ba boŋe we
o wó cheigi taane delo
a na jege a saŋe‑o de baŋa ne to.
17O nam wó kwei vo-fɔrɔ o ma
o mage-ne o chochoge,
ye o pa se a fufwollu tem
de puli kafɛ ŋwaane.
18Se a taa tɛ we a daa wae a sii
a yi a tete to,
de o daa pɛ se a yiga tiini ka nyɔne.
19Ko ná ye dam taane mo dé tɛa,
Wɛ dam ba tia.
Ko nam ná ye ka-di-bora taane mo,
wɔ mo wó wane o saŋe Wɛ?
20Amo ná maŋe a jege chega
tei maama de,
a ni taane mo lage de pa
se a to bora dim baŋa ne.
A nam ná ba jege tusim de,
a ni botare-bia wó de-ne tega ne.
21Amo seene a wo tusi o yiga ne.
A yiga nam tera de kolo
na wó yi-ne to.
A ŋwea kam ye wo-yɔɔ mo
ko pa-ne.
22Chwei sem maama ba gare daane.
Mo amo na tɛ tei to.
Ko ná ye balo na yɔɔre chwoŋa to,
de puseŋ-nyena bam,
Wɛ ba pɔɔre-ba daane
de o na chɔge-ba tei to.
23Lɛɛro ná yi nɔɔna pa se ba pɔpɔ ba te,
Wɛ jei o nii balo na jege chega to mo ye o mɔne-ba.
24Puseŋ-nyena mo vere tega baŋa
ba jege ba tei.
Wɛ laam ma yeini o kwoli balo
na jege taana ba di to yia
pa ba kweele chega kam.
Ko ná dae Wɛ mo ke konto,
wɔ mo kea?
25Amo ŋwea da yam wora ya ti mo lela,
ne nɔɔno na duri lela lela tei to.
Ya maa ke lela ya jei
ye wopwolo tera a tei ne.
26Dɛ maama duri de kɛ mo,
ne ba na yɛ nabwooru na wone
ba vei tei to.
Ya maa wuura ya tia,
ne maaro na foore tei te chui
se te ja te ni-wodiu to.
27Amo nam ná boŋe a tete ne we,
‘Yage se a swei a cham dem swia,
se a pa a yi-nyɔna leiri ya ji wopwolo,’
28a yaara yam daa ta pa-ne foone mo,
kokuri amo yei we n bá‑n ta we,
a jege bora.
29Wolo na to o tigi tega ne to
daa ba kɔre ba de wɔ.
Bɛŋwaane mo a daa wó pa
ko chɛ a yera kafɛ ŋwaane?
30A ná maŋe a kwei chanfene de sea
se a ma a swɛ a yera ye a sane a je,
31n ta wó kwei-ne mo
n de gwoŋo kolo na su de digiru to wone.
A yera digiru tem wó pa se a tete yera gwaaro tem chɛɛse-ne mo.
32Wɛ nam dae nabiinu
ne amo tete na ye tei to.
Tento amo de wonto ya diini
daa baŋa
se dé ŋɔɔne dé leiri dé pa daane.
33Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o ná wó wane o zo
amo de Wɛ taane dem wone,
se o tɔge o dam ŋwaane
o bore bora debam laŋa ne.
34Kotu ya wó wane o pa se
Wɛ dɔne o je o daare-ne,
se o daa yé waare-ne,
naa o fugi-ne de o chana yam.
35Amo ya wó na chwoŋa
se a ŋɔɔne jaja ye foone tera.
Ko nam na ye tei to,
a bá wane konto a ke.”

english_text:
Job Complains to God
I Am Sick of Life!
1I am sick of life!
And from my deep despair,
I complain to you, my God.
2Don't just condemn me!
Point out my sin.
3Why do you take such delight
in destroying those you created
and in smiling on sinners?
4Do you look at things
the way we humans do?
5Is your life as short as ours?
6Is that why you are so quick
to find fault with me?
7 You know I am innocent,
but who can defend me
against you?
8Will you now destroy
someone you created?
9Remember that you molded me
like a piece of clay.
So don't turn me back
into dust once again.
10 As cheese is made from milk,
you created my body
from a tiny drop.
11Then you tied my bones together
with muscles and covered them
with flesh and skin.
12You, the source of my life,
showered me with kindness
and watched over me.
You Have Not Explained
13You have not explained
all of your mysteries,
14but you catch and punish me
each time I sin.
15Guilty or innocent,
I am condemned and ashamed
because of my troubles.
16No matter how hard I try,
you keep hunting me down
like a powerful lion.
17You never stop accusing me;
you become furious and attack
over and over again.
18Why did you let me be born?
I would rather have died
before birth
19and been carried to the grave
without ever breathing.
20I have only a few days left.
Why don't you leave me alone?
Let me find some relief,
* 21before I travel to the land
22of darkness and despair,
the place of no return.
translation_text:
Job ta ma ta o we:
1“Amo chuli ŋwea kalo
a na jege a ŋwe to.
Konto ŋwaane mo a wó taa poona jaja,
ye a yɔɔre a tɛ kolo na daane-ne to.
2A nam wó ta de Wɛ mo we:
Yé di bora n vane-ne lela!
Nam ta n bere-ne se a lɔre
a na ke kolo a chɔge
pa se taane wora debam laŋa ne to.
3A ye wolo n tete je na mɔɔne to mo.
N wo nam tigi
de n na jege-ne n bɛɛsa
ye n ta dole-ne n yage tei to mo na?
Ko nam ná ye puseŋ-nyena bam,
n yi yeini de su ba totoŋa yam mo.
4N yeini n nii n nae wonnu
ne nabiina na nae-te tei to mo na?
5Nmo ŋwea de ye ne nabiina ŋwea
na ye tei,
pa ka ba dáana ye ka ti to mo na?
6Konto ma pa se n buŋi jei maama ne
se n na a na tusi mɛ seeni,
ye n lɔre a wɛleera yam maama
na ye tei to.
7Nmo nam yei we a jege bora.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera
o na wó wane o jwoŋi-ne
o yage nmo jeŋa ne.
8Nmo tete mo mɛ n je
n fɔge n naane-ne.
N daa wó pipiri se n ja-ne
n chɔge mo na?
9Guli we n naane-ne ne dɔgɔ mo tei.
Nmo nam lage n pa se a jwoori
a ji teero mo na?
10N lwogi-ne n ke a nu puga ne,
ne ba na lwoi nayela tei to mo.
N ta ma pa se a tigisi a ke daane
ne nayel-pepala to.
11Nmo laam ma‑n kwei ya-tana
de ya-nɔna n daŋe da,
ye n pa se ŋwanno de kwi
twoŋi daane a yera yam ne.
12Konto baŋa ne mo n pɛ se a na ŋwea,
ye n ta duri a yibwona.
N ma‑n yɔɔre n yere-ne
se a ŋwea ke dam.
13Amo laam tu a lɔre kolo nmo ya na seigi n boboŋa ne to.
N na jaane boboŋa se n ke-ne
tei to mo tento:
14Nmo boŋe se n yɔɔre n nii amo,
se a ná tusi, se n waare-ne
a wɛleera yam ŋwaane.
15A ná toŋe puseŋa,
lɛɛro lage te yi-ne!
A ná wo ke a chɔge mo de,
wo-chechɔgɔ de chaveera
ta wó ja-ne,
de chanɛɛre delo maama
na daane-ne to.
16A nam ná kwaane se a jwoori a zaŋe,
nmo yɔɔre n pare-ne mo se n ja,
ne nywoŋo na pare varem
se ko ja ko di tei to.
Konto dwoŋi mo n ke wo-kenkagela
n ma n chɔge-ne.
17N yeini n pa se yaara tui
ya chɔge a yiga,
ye n bane fɔge de zaŋa a baŋa ne.
Ko nye ne n toŋe jar-keira mo
se ba taa jeeri-ne de jara taa taa.
18Bɛŋwaane mo n pɛ chwoŋa
se a nu lo-ne?
A ya ná tege lela ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo nɛ-ne,
konto ya bere ko gara.
19Amo ya ná maŋe a wo nɛ ŋwea mo,
naa ba ná jaane-ne a lora dɛ ne
ba yɔɔre yibeela ba suli,
konto gara.
20A ŋwea da yam daa ba daga.
Ja, yage a yera se a wane
a sii fenfee de wopwolo,
21ye a laam daare a vo
mɛ na ye lim yerane to
se a daa yé jwoori.
22Lim maa kwoli jei sem konto liira liira.
Vuvuga de yibiri maa wora biramm.
Dáane mo wea pwooni
ye lim yerane.”

english_text:
Zophar's First Speech
So Much Foolish Talk
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2So much foolish talk
cannot go unanswered.
3Your words have silenced others
and made them ashamed;
now it is only right for you
to be put to shame.
4You claim to be innocent
and argue that your beliefs
are acceptable to God.
5But I wish God would speak
6and let you know that wisdom
has many different sides.
You would then discover
that God has punished you
less than you deserve.
7Can you understand the mysteries
surrounding God All-Powerful?
8They are higher than the heavens
and deeper than the grave.
So what can you do
when you know so little,
9and these mysteries outreach
the earth and the ocean?
10If God puts you in prison
or drags you to court,
what can you do?
11God has the wisdom to know
when someone is worthless
and sinful,
12but it's easier to tame
a wild donkey
than to make a fool wise.
Surrender Your Heart to God
13Surrender your heart to God,
turn to him in prayer,
14and give up your sins—
even those you do in secret.
15Then you won't be ashamed;
you will be confident
and fearless.
16Your troubles will go away
like water beneath a bridge,
17and your darkest night
will be brighter than noon.
18You will rest safe and secure,
filled with hope
and emptied of worry.
19You will sleep without fear
and be greatly respected.
20But those who are evil
will go blind and lose their way.
Their only escape is death!
translation_text:
Zofara na bobo o ta kolo to
1Naamatia tu Zofara de ma leiri o we:
2“Dé bá leiri nɔɔno wom ta-fara yam konto mo na?
O ni-wɛɛle dem bere we
o jege bora na?
3Job, nmo boŋe we ta-yɔɔro telo
n na jege n ŋɔɔne to
wó pa dé pu dé nia mo na?
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá zaŋe o bwɛ‑m,
de n na jege nɔɔna n mɔna tei to na?
4N tage we, n bera yam lana fase mo,
ye n tete de kikia tɔge chwoŋa Wɛ yiga ne.
5Amo nam ya lage se Wɛ puri o ni mo
o ta taane de nmo.
6O ya wó bere‑m yi-poro
kolo na seigi n tei ne to.
Kokuri swa yalo na ye chekke to
chwei sem ye yera yera mo.
Nam lɔre we Wɛ wo waare‑m
se ko maŋe de n wɛleera yam ni
na mae tei to.
7Nmo wó wane n yɛ se n lɔre
Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ boboŋ-lilirru tem na ye tei to na?
N ta wó wane n lɔre
o swa yam kweelim jei
na wo mɛ to na?
8Ya diini wɛ-baŋa se ko dwoni
wɛyuu kom na ye tei to.
Nmo nam wó ke bɛ mo ko wone?
Ya ta luuna se ko dwoni
churu na luuna tei to.
Nmo wó ke tetɛ mo se n lɔre-ya?
9Wɛ boboŋa yam dɔra
ya dwoi tega baŋa kam ni dedɔrem.
Ya ta maa yala ya dwoi
naneo kom na ye tei to.
10O nam ná tu se o ja wolo o pe,
naa se o saŋe wolo taane dim baŋa ne,
wɔ mo wó wane o yiga o che?
11O wae o lɔre balo na ye nɔn-yɔɔro to.
O ná nɛ lwarem kikia,
o bá maane ya ni ne na?
12Kagoa wo bonaga wó wane
ka lo nabiinu,
ye nɔn-jworo ta wo wane o ja swa.
13Nam sɛ se n kwei n bochare maama n pa Wɛ,
se n daare n twe n je
n jeeri‑o wɛ-lworo baŋa ne.
14N je sem ná toŋe lwarem,
se n dole-de n yage.
Ta yé pa puseŋa kikia chwoŋa
se ya taa zoore n sɔŋɔ ne.
15Nmo ná leiri n boboŋa konto dwoŋi,
chaveera daa bá ja‑m.
N ma‑n wó jwoori n kwoni
n yuu wɛɛne.
N ta wó taa zege de baare
ye n ba kɔre foone.
16Nmo wó swei n yaara yam swia.
Ya gula maa wó jei lela,
ne na na duri ba kɛ tei to.
17Konto wó pa n ŋwea taa pera
ne wea tetare pwooni na ye tei to.
Lim ná tu de kwoli‑m,
de wó pipiri de ji te-pora.
18Nmo wó ta‑n jege baare,
n teena na wó taa daga to ŋwaane.
Kolokolo bá daane‑m.
N ma‑n wó sii ye lwia tera.
19Nmo wó ta‑n tigi n sara ne mo,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera
o na wó pa foone ja‑m.
Nɔɔna dedɛ nam wó ja n naga
se n woli-ba mo.
20Ko nam ná ye puseŋ-nyena bam,
ba yia wó dwei mo
ye ba bá na chwoŋa se ba lu.
Ba teena maa wó taa wo toone wone se de ja-ba.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
You Think You Are So Great
* 1Job said to his friends:
2You think you are so great,
with all the answers.
3But I know as much as you do,
and so does everyone else.
4I have always lived right,
and God answered my prayers;
now friends make fun of me.
5It's easy to condemn
those who are suffering,
when you have no troubles.
6Robbers and other godless people
live safely at home and say,
“God is in our hands!”
If You Want To Learn
7If you want to learn,
then go and ask
the wild animals and the birds,
8the flowers and the fish.
9Any of them can tell you
what the Lord has done.
10Every living creature
is in the hands of God.
11We hear with our ears,
taste with our tongues,
12and gain some wisdom from those
who have lived a long time.
13But God is the real source
of wisdom and strength.
14No one can rebuild
what he destroys, or release
those he has imprisoned.
15God can hold back the rain
or send a flood,
16just as he rules over liars
and those they lie to.
17God shames counselors,
turns judges into fools,
18and makes slaves of kings.
19God removes priests and others
who have great power—
20he confuses wise,
experienced advisors,
21puts mighty kings to shame,
and takes away their power.
22God turns darkness to light;
23he makes nations strong,
then shatters their strength.
24God strikes their rulers senseless,
then leaves them to roam
through barren deserts,
25lost in the dark, staggering
like someone drunk.
translation_text:
Job na leiri o badwonna bam tei to
1Job daa ta ma leiri o we:
2“Abam boŋe we
á dwoi nɔɔna maama mo,
ye á ná tega, yeino wó tɔge
de abam ko te mo!
3Nam ta‑á yei-na we,
amo de jege boboŋa,
ne abam na jege tei to mo.
Abam de amo ba gare daane.
Abam na tage wonnu telo maama to,
wɔ nam mo yeiri te ni ne?
4Amo badwonna de laam jege-ne mo ba mɔna,
de a na yeini a lwoori Wɛ
pa o de leiri a wɛ-lworo tei maama to.
Ba yɔɔre ba mɔne-ne mo,
de a na jege chega ye tusim tera to.
5Nɔɔna balo kolokolo na ba daane-ba to
yeini ba gwooni chanɛɛre na jege balo to mo.
Ba maa yeini ba yigi
balo na seeri se ba to tega ne to.
6Ko nam ná ye venverena,
ba sam yɔɔre de zega de dam mo.
Kolokolo ba yi balo na dwoni de Wɛ to de.
Ba nam teena we
ba tete dam mo ye ba wɛ.
7Nam bwei-na vara bam,
de wɛyuu zuna bam,
se ba wó ta chega ba bere abam.
8Abam ta ná laga,
bwei-na tega baŋa wonnu,
naa naneo wo ywona yam,
se te bere abam yeino taane.
9Wonnu tem konto maama yei we,
ko ye Baŋa Wɛ dam dem mo ke konto.
10Wonnu telo maama na wo
tega baŋa ne to
wo Wɛ dam dem kuri ne mo.
Nabiina maama ŋwea
de maa wo wonto jeŋa ne.
11Nabiina zwa cheigi taana
se ba lɔre mo,
ne ba dindeilima na yeini
ya laŋe wodiiru tei to.
12Kokweero pae nɔɔna jaane swa mo.
Momwɛ-dɛɛre de jaane yi-poro mo
de tui.
13Swa dedaane dam ye Wɛ mo tei-te.
O maa bere kwea,
de yi-poro maama de.
14Wonto ná yigi woŋo kolo
o de tega ne,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware-ko
se o jwoori o lɔ o zege.
O nam ná jaane wolo o pe,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware kotu
se o pore o yage.
15O ná yeini o che doa se ka yé nene,
da-kore mo wó zege.
O maa ná yeini o pa chwoŋa
se ka tiini ka ne,
ka de yɔɔre ka chɔge tega baŋa wonnu dedɛ mo.
16Dam-fɔrɔ de wɔnɔ ye Wɛ mo tei-te.
Balo na tusi to, de balo na soge ba dwonna pa se ba tusi to
maama wo o jeŋa ne mo.
17O maa kale dedɛɛra de kuri-nɔrɔ
o ja viiri,
ye o daare o pae balo na jege taana ba di to de yirisi.
18O yeini o puri pwa yipwi o tiŋa,
pa ba gae ba paare dem,
ye o daare o pae ba jiri kabɛ.
19O ta kale kaanem tiina
de kuri-nɔrɔ o ja viiri,
ye o daare o pae se naduna
jiri nabwona.
20O maa pae balo nɔɔna na jege ba chega to nia pui,
ye o pae nakwa boboŋa vugima.
21O pae nɔn-yum di ba chaveera mo,
ye o vere babɛ dam o daare-ba
o zege bwori.
22O yeini o le wonnu telo na seigi
lim wone to mo o bere nɔɔna.
O maa pae pwooni nye yibiri jei ne.
23O yeini o pa teene dedwonna yere zaŋe wɛɛne,
ye o daa ta chɔge dedwonna de.
O maa ná pɛ de yale de ke kamunnu,
o laam yeini o jage-de mo
o yage jei maama ne.
24O pae tega baŋa teene dem
yuu tiina toŋe jworim mo,
o daare o pa ba kare kagoa yuu ne
ba beeri yɔɔ yerane.
25Ba kare ba taane lim wone mo
ye pwooni tera ba tei ne.
O ta ma pa ba kare ba yuŋi
jei maama,
ne sa-nyɔra na yeini ba vei tei to.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Know and Understand
1I know and understand
every bit of this.
2None of you are smarter
than I am;
there's nothing you know
that I don't.
3But I prefer to argue my case
with God All-Powerful—
4you are merely useless doctors,
who treat me with lies.
5The wisest thing you can do
is to keep quiet 6and listen
to my argument.
7Are you telling lies for God
8and not telling the whole truth
when you argue his case?
9If he took you to court,
could you fool him,
just as you fool others?
10If you were secretly unfair,
he would correct you,
11and his glorious splendor
would make you terrified.
12Your wisdom and arguments
will blow away like dust.
Be Quiet While I Speak
13Be quiet while I speak,
and we'll see what happens.
14I will be responsible
for what happens to me.
15God may kill me, but still
I will trust him
and offer my defense.
16This may be what saves me,
because no guilty person
would come to his court.
17Listen carefully to my words!
18I have prepared my case well,
and I am certain to win.
19If you can prove me guilty,
I will give up and die.
Job Prays
I Ask Only Two Things
20I ask only two things
of you, my God,
and I will no longer
hide from you—
21stop punishing
and terrifying me!
22Then speak, and I will reply;
or else let me speak,
and you reply.
23Please point out my sins,
so I will know them.
24Why have you turned your back
and count me your enemy?
25Do you really enjoy
frightening a fallen leaf?
26Why do you accuse me
of horrible crimes
and make me pay for sins
I did in my youth?
27 You have tied my feet down
and keep me surrounded;
28I am rotting away like cloth
eaten by worms.
translation_text:
Job ta ma ta o we:
1“Amo yia mo yɔɔre
ya na tento maama.
A zwa de ma ni-te, ye a ni te kuri.
2Abam de amo ba gare daane.
Abam maa na yei wonnu telo to,
amo de yei-te mo.
3A nam lage se a ŋɔɔne
de Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom mo.
A wó yi o tei mo
se a tole a taane dem.
4Abam nam yeini á fɔ vwa-dɛɛra mo
á daŋe amo yuu ne.
Á nye de liri-keira balo na ware
nɔɔn-nɔɔno se ba yɔɔre to mo.
5Abam ná pugi á nia, ko wó taa gara!
Konto ya wó bere we,
á jege swa chekke.
6Nam cheigi-na taane delo
a na jege se a ta to.
Cheigi-na amo ni na ŋɔɔne kolo to.
7Abam boŋe se á tɔge tusim baŋa ne
á jwoŋi Wɛ taane á ta á pa‑o mo na?
Á wó fɔ vwa á ma á jwoŋi o taane
á ta na?
8Abam wó sɛ se á zege á pa Wɛ mo,
se á jwoŋi o taane saŋa baŋa ne
á ŋɔɔne na?
9O nam ná jwoori o bwei abam,
á wó lu taane ne na?
Á wó wane Wɛ á gane,
ne á na jege nabiina á gane
tei to na?
10Chega ná tere abam taane dem wone,
á yeiri we o wó bwɛ abam
ko ŋwaane na?
11O nenɔŋa kam bá fugi abam,
pa se o foone taa jege abam na?
12Memaŋa yalo abam na jege
á maŋe to ba jege kuri,
ne tentwarem na ye tei to mo.
Á swa yam ware abam ya che
kantɔgɔ wone,
ne dɔgɔ na yare lela tei to mo.
13Nam pu-na á nia
se ko pa-ne chwoŋa se a ŋɔɔne.
Pa-na se dé nii bɛ mo lage ko ba
amo baŋa.
14Yage-na se kolo ná wó yi-ne,
se ko yi.
Amo dole a ŋwea mo a yage.
15Wɛ ná laga de, o wó go-ne,
se a teena nam tigi wonto wone mo.
Amo wó zege o yiga ne
a tole a taane dem,
se a wane a na a bora.
16Konto baŋa ne mo Wɛ wó wane
o jwoŋi-ne o yage.
Kokuri, wolo na ve Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem to bá na chwoŋa
se o zege Wɛ yiga ne.
17Fɔge á cheigi-na taane delo
a na jege se a ta to.
Pa-na se kolo a na tɛ to to á zwa ne.
18Nii-na! A yɔɔre a jeeli taane delo
a na wó ta to mo.
A nam yei lanyerane we
a wó di bora.
19Wɔ mo wora se o saŋe-ne we a chɔge?
A nam ná seene a tusi,
amo wó taa chem mo se a laam te.
20Amo Tu Wɛ, wonnu telei yerane mo
a lage a lwoori n tei ne
se n ke n pa-ne.
Konto ná kea, amo daa bá taa kare a seigi nmo yiga ne.
21Dɔne n je n daare-ne.
Daa yé ta‑n jege-ne n fuga
de n chana yam.
22Nam bwoŋi-ne, se a wane
a leiri n taane dem,
naa pa-ne chwoŋa se a ŋɔɔne,
se nmo de leiri a taane dem.
23A tiini a ke wɛleera a chɔge n yiga
se ko vo ko maŋe yei ne mo?
Ta a wɛleera yam de a tusim dem
n bere-ne se a lɔre-ya.
24Bɛŋwaane mo n yiga tere amo wone?
Bɛ mo ye n yɔɔre n done-ne?
25Vɔɔ ye bɛ mo ye n lage se n fugi-ko?
Bɛ mo ye n zeili-ne,
ne vio na kale swanno
ko ja jei tei to?
26N nam popone wo-chɛɛro
n tiŋi tɔnɔ ne
we te ye amo yiga.
Ko ta ná ye wɛleera yalo a na ke
a nɔn-donne maŋa ne to,
n laam ma‑n pa se ya jene
wo a yuu ne.
27Nmo kwei chegero mo
n vɔ a nɛ ne diŋ-diŋ.
N yeini n yere a na-veili maama,
ye n lɔ siseini n pa-ne
se a yé gaale-de.
28Konto to, a wora a jei mo,
ne woŋo na yɔɔre ko pɔe tei to.
A ŋwea tiini ka chɔge,
ne gɔrɔ kolo tóa na mugi to.”

english_text:
Job Continues His Prayer
Life Is Short and Sorrowful
1 Life is short and sorrowful
for every living soul.
2We are flowers that fade
and shadows that vanish.
3And so, I ask you, God,
why pick on me?
4There's no way a human
can be completely pure.
5Our time on earth is brief;
the number of our days
is already decided by you.
6Why don't you leave us alone
and let us find some happiness
while we toil and labor?
When a Tree Is Chopped Down
7When a tree is chopped down,
there is always the hope
that it will sprout again.
8Its roots and stump may rot,
9but at the touch of water,
it sprouts once again.
10Humans are different—
we die, and that's the end.
11We are like streams and lakes
after the water has gone;
12we fall into the sleep of death,
never to rise again,
until the sky disappears.
13Please hide me, God,
deep in the ground—
and when you are angry no more,
remember to rescue me.
Will We Humans Live Again?
14Will we humans live again?
I would gladly suffer
and wait for my time.
15My Creator, you would want me;
you would call out,
and I would answer.
16You would take care of me,
but not count my sins—
17you would put them in a bag,
tie it tight,
and toss them away.
18But in the real world,
mountains tumble,
and rocks crumble;
19streams wear away stones
and wash away soil.
And you destroy our hopes!
20You change the way we look,
then send us away,
wiped out forever.
21We never live to know
if our children are praised
or disgraced.
22We feel no pain but our own,
and when we mourn,
it's only for ourselves.
translation_text:
Job daa ta ma ta o we:
1“Kaane ná loge nabiinu wolo maama,
kotu ŋwea ye kukua mo
ye ka su de cham yerane.
2O maa nye de ga-puŋu kolo na puli
ye ko laam daare ko kwaare
lela to mo.
O ta ye ne lunluŋu na ye tei to mo.
O ba dáana ye o jia.
3Wɛ, nabiina na bwona konto to,
bɛ mo tei ye n ke n yiga ba wone?
Bɛŋwaane mo n lage n saŋe amo
se n daare n di a taane?
4Nɔn-diku wó wane o lo nɔn-laao na?
Ko bá wane ko ke.
5Nmo wuuri n jeeli nabiina ŋwea da yam mo,
pa se ya ba ya kweeli ya maŋa ne.
Nɔɔna ware se ba gaale
ba maŋa kam chekke.
6Konto ŋwaane nam yage ba yera,
se ba wane ba toŋe
ye ba daare ba sii,
ne ba na jene nɔɔna balo
se ba taa toŋe to.
7Ba ná gwoni tio ba de tega ne,
teena ta wora we
ko wó jwoori ko kwi,
se ko nɛ-donno tem daa yé te.
8Ko bonno tem wae te pɔe
tega kuri ne,
pa se da-buŋa kalo na daare to de te.
9Se na fenfee ná yɔɔre ba dwei
tio kom yera,
ko wó jwoori ko kwi nɛ-donno
de vɔɔro mo.
10Ko nam ná ye nabiina,
ba ná yɔɔre ba te,
ba dam wó ti mo.
Ba momwɛ nam ná tu de ti,
ba laam wó vo yei ne mo?
11Buga wo ná yeini ba we
ba daare-ka,
pa se ka tigi te-kora yerane mo,
12konto dwoŋi mo, nɔɔno ná tega,
o daa ware se o zaŋe.
Wɛyuu kom maama wó ba ko jei
ye kotu ta wo zaŋe.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o peese‑o
se o zaŋe dɔɔne ne.
13Ja! Amo Tu Wɛ, kwei-ne
n seigi churu ne,
se kolokolo yé yi-ne,
ko taa nii dɛ dem
n bane na zuri to.
Nam kuri dɛ se n laam jwoori
n guli amo gula.
14Nɔɔno ná tega, o daa wó jwoori
o na ŋwea na?
Amo logo baŋa totoŋ-chɛɛra
maŋa kanto maama wone,
a wó taa toŋa ye a teena
a verem maŋa kam mo.
15Nmo ná bwoŋi a yere,
a wó leiri‑m.
Nmo boboŋa maa wó taa tigi
amo wolo n tete je na mɔɔne to wone.
16Nmo laam wó ta‑n yere
a na-veili maama,
ye n nam bá‑n jeeli
a wɛleera yam na ye tei to.
17Nmo ma‑n wó kwoli a wɛleera yam,
ne nɔɔno na seigi wonnu
tampɔgɔ wone tei to.
18-19Ko nam na ye tei to,
nmo jaane nabiina teena yam mo
n chɔge n yaga.
Ko maa nye ne peero na wae
te sirimi te toe tei,
ye kandwa-zana de guri
ya na tigi mɛ to mo.
Na-fɔrɔ de wó wane kandwa
ba chochoge,
ye ba chuuri ba chwooli
tega kasolo ba ja ba kɛ.
Konto mo nmo de chɔge
nabiinu ŋwea.
20N yeini n ma n dam mo
n dwoni ded‑o,
pa o yɔɔre o jei wuu.
O yibia wó leiri mo,
ye n laam daare n zeili‑o se o viiri.
21Kotu kwaga kam ná nɛ zula
tega baŋa ne, o yeiri ko ni ne.
Ba nam ná jege chaveera mo
ba di de,
o bá wane o lɔre ko na ke-ba tei to.
22Kolo yerane o na yei to mo ye
o tete yera na nɛ zonne tei to.
O maa wó taa keeri o tete keira.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Second Speech
If You Had Any Sense
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
* 2Job, if you had any sense,
3you would stop spreading
all of this hot air.
4Your words are enough
to make others turn from God
and lead them to doubt.
5And your sinful, scheming mind
is the source of all you say.
6I am not here as your judge;
your own words are witnesses
against you.
7Were you the first human?
Are you older than the hills?
8Have you ever been present
when God's council meets?
Do you alone have wisdom?
9Do you know and understand
something we don't?
10We have the benefit of wisdom
older than your father.
11And you have been offered
comforting words from God.
Isn't this enough?
12Your emotions are out of control,
making you look fierce;
13that's why you attack God
with everything you say.
14 No human is pure and innocent,
15and neither are angels—
not in the sight of God.
If God doesn't trust his angels,
16what chance do humans have?
We are so terribly evil
that we thirst for sin.
Just Listen to What I Know
17Just listen to what I know,
and you will learn
18wisdom known by others
since ancient times.
19Those who gained such insights
also gained the land,
and they were not influenced
by foreign teachings.
20But suffering is in store
each day for those who sin.
21Even in times of success,
they constantly hear
the threat of doom.
22Darkness, despair, and death
are their destiny.
23They scrounge around for food,
all the while dreading
the approaching darkness.
24They are overcome with despair,
like frightened soldiers facing
a fearsome king in battle.
25This is because they rebelled
against God All-Powerful
26and have attacked him
with their weapons.
27They may be rich and fat,
28but they will live in the ruins
of deserted towns.
29Their property and wealth
will shrink and disappear.
30They won't escape the darkness,
and the blazing breath of God
will set their future aflame.
* 31They have put their trust
in something worthless;
now they will become worthless
32like a date palm tree
without a leaf.
33Or like vineyards or orchards
whose blossoms and unripe fruit
drop to the ground.
34Yes, the godless and the greedy
will have nothing but flames
feasting on their homes,
35because they are the parents
of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_text:
Elifaza na tage kolo o ke belei to
1Teman tu Elifaza daa ma leiri Job o we:
2“Vio yerane mo nwoŋi n ni ne!
Boboŋa tu nam ba ŋɔɔne ta-yɔɔro.
3Swa tu ba kare o ŋɔɔne wo-korro,
de taane delo na ba jege kuri to,
ne nmo na ke tei to.
4Nii mo! N boŋe se n dole Wɛ kɔrɔ
n yage mo.
N ta ma‑n lage n che se nɔɔna
yé taa boŋe Wɛ boboŋa chekke.
5N wɛleere kikia yam
de n pipiri totoŋa yam,
mo pa se n jege ni se n ŋɔɔne
n chɔge Wɛ yere.
6Ko dae amo mo ŋɔɔne
a vane nmo bora.
Se n tete ni taane mo le‑m
de zege dáa ne.
7Nmo mo puli nabiina maama kuri na?
Naa n koe logo baŋa peero tem mo?
8Wɛ kɔgɔ kom ná yeini
ba jeeri daane wɛyuu ne,
nmo de wó tɔge n gwaane
ba wone na?
Nmo boŋe we nmo yerane yi mo poore na?
9N yei wonnu ye debam yeiri-te na?
Naa n ni wonnu kuri mo
ye debam ware-te se dé lɔre?
10Balo yuni na peere to mo
zege dé kwaga ne.
Ba maa ye nɔn-kwe
selo na koe nmo kwo to.
11Wɛ kwei bochare-zuru taane mo
o ta dede‑m.
O na zuri o yera de nmo konto to,
ko ba jege kuri ko pa‑m na?
12Bɛŋwaane mo nmo ware n bane
se n ja pa se n yibia leiri?
13Nmo nam pɛ se n bane zaŋe de Wɛ,
ye ta-yɔɔro yerane tɔge n ni ne
ya nwoŋa.
14Nabiinu wó wane o taa ye wose na?
Kaana na loge balo maama to wone
wɔ mo jege chega Wɛ yiga ne?
15Ko ná maŋe ko ye
Wɛ malese-laaro tete de,
o ba ke o teena se wone.
O maa wo sɛ we wɛyuu baŋa
jei sem ye wose o yiga ne.
16Nabiina laam wó taa ye tetɛ mo
o tei ne?
Ba boboŋa tiini ya pɔ mo,
ye ba toŋe lwarem
ne na mo ba jege ba nyɔ to.
17Jeini konto chemm se a maŋe wonnu se n ni te kuri.
Yage se a ta a yi na nɛ kolo to
a bere‑m.
18Ko nam ye swa tiina na nɛ kolo faŋa
ye ba ta ko taane jaja to mo.
Ba kwoa de déem ma bere-ba
swa yam konto.
19Banto yerane mo jwoŋi tega kam
Wɛ tei ne.
Sa-teena maa ba jege chwoŋa
se ba gane-ba.
20Puseŋ-nyena de nankɔ-nyena
wó na yaara mo taa,
se ba ŋwea bena yam maama
ba ya ti.
21Ba ni kwori mo ba zwa wone
pa se foone zo-ba.
Yazura ná yi-ba de,
venverena mo beene ba baŋa.
22Ba maa ba jege teena
se ba lu lim wone,
se-zɔɔro na jaane chɔgem
te ba ba baŋa to ŋwaane.
23Duura mo wó taa kare ba jaane
jei maama ne
se ba di nɔɔna bam konto ya-nɔna.
Ba maa yei we ba ba jege jwa,
se lim yerane mo lage
de kwoli-ba.
24Lwia dedɛ jege-ba,
pa se ba tiini ba kɔre foone.
Foone maa wó wane-ba de di,
ne pɛ wolo na kwaare jara
de o dona to.
25Puseŋ-nyena bam liligi ba nwa
Wɛ yiga ne,
ye ba dwoni de Dam-fɔrɔ Tu
Wɛ wom mo.
26Ba maa jege de Wɛ
ne jar-keira balo na duri
se ba ja jara yam ba yi‑o tei to.
27Puseŋ-nyena bam yɔɔre ba nu mo
bigila bigila, ye ba yera duna.
28Ba nam zoore teene delo na jigi di-dwonnu to wone mo,
mɛ seeni na wo maŋe se nɔɔn-nɔɔno taa zoore da to.
Ba sam dem lage de to tega ne
de ji weero yerane mo.
29Ba daa bá taa ye naduna.
Ba jejegero tem de maa bá dáane
ye te jei.
Ba wonnu tem bá puli
se te yi tega kam ni maama.
30Ba bá na chwoŋa se ba lu
lim dem wone.
Ba nam wó taa ye ne teeni delo nɛ
na jaane mini to mo.
Wɛ ná sii o yage ba yera ne,
ba wó yɔɔre ba jei mo.
31Puseŋ-nyeno nam yé gane o tete
se o kwei o teena o daŋe wo-yɔɔro baŋa ne.
Kokuri o na wó na nyɔɔre delo to
ye wo-korro yerane mo.
32O bá yi o maŋa de o na kwaare,
ne konkwara kalo daa
na bá kwi vɔɔro to.
33Kotu ta wó taa ye ne Vini tio
na yage ko bi-kanywaano
ko de tega ne tei to mo,
de Olivi tio punnu na kwori
te toe tega ne tei to.
34Ko ná ye balo na ve Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem to,
ba kɔgɔ kom bá daare dwi
tega kam baŋa ne.
Mini mo wó zwɛ ba sam dem maama,
ba na lɔge-de kalipera baŋa ne to ŋwaane.
35Ba yeini ba ja chanɛɛre puga mo,
ye ba puga kam virigi lwarem.
Bu wolo ba na wó lo to
maa ye gengana.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
I Have Often Heard This
1Job said:
2I have often heard this,
and it offers no comfort.
3So why don't you keep quiet?
What's bothering you?
4If I were in your place,
it would be easy to criticize
or to give advice.
5But I would offer hope
and comfort instead.
6If I speak, or if I don't,
I hurt all the same.
My torment continues.
7God has worn me down
and destroyed my family;
8my shriveled up skin proves
that I am his prisoner.
9God is my hateful enemy,
glaring at me and attacking
with his sharp teeth.
10Everyone is against me;
they sneer and slap my face.
11And God is the one
who handed me over
to this merciless mob.
Everything Was Going Well
12Everything was going well,
until God grabbed my neck
and shook me to pieces.
God set me up as the target
13for his arrows,
and without showing mercy,
he slashed my stomach open,
spilling out my insides.
14God never stops attacking,
15and so, in my sorrow
I dress in sackcloth
and sit in the dust.
16My face is red with tears,
and dark shadows
circle my eyes,
17though I am not violent,
and my prayers are sincere.
18If I should die,
I beg the earth not to cover
my cry for justice.
19 Even now, God in heaven
is both my witness
and my protector.
20My friends have rejected me,
but God is the one I beg
21to show that I am right,
just as a friend should.
22Because in only a few years,
I will be dead and gone.
translation_text:
Job na leiri tei to
1Job ma leiri o we:
2“Amo maŋe a ni ta-dwoa
yalo abam na tɛ de amo to dedɛ.
Á taana yam nam ba zuri
amo bochare kɔtaa!
3Abam na tiini á ŋɔɔne ta-yɔɔro
telo to bá kweeli na?
Bɛ mo daane abam
pa á ba yage te ŋɔŋa?
4Abam ya ná nɛ cham
ne amo na nɛ tei to,
a ya wó wane a ŋɔɔne
ne abam na ke de amo tei to.
A ya wó ma ta-fare a bwɛ abam,
ye a dole a yuu abam yiga ne.
5Amo ni taane nam ya wó ke dam
de ke á kuri ne mo,
se á bochara zuri a ŋɔŋa kam ŋwaane.
6Ko nam na ye tei to,
amo ná puri a ni a ŋɔɔne,
a ba sii de zonne delo na jege-ne to.
A ya ze ná chem de,
amo cham dem yɔɔre
de wora mo taa wuu.
7Chega to, Wɛ yɔɔre o pa
a yera chɛ mo,
ye o daare o chɔge
amo sɔŋɔ tiina maama.
8O ma ja-ne o vɔ
pa ko zo a yera dedɛ.
Amo na tiini a bugi tei to mo pae
nɔɔna tɛ ba we, a ba jege chega.
9Wɛ ma yɔɔre o chuli-ne
ye o tɔge o ban-lom baŋa ne
o ja-ne o tore,
ne ga-varem na ke tei to.
O nii-ne de yi-soŋo se o chɔge-ne mo.
10Nɔɔna kare ba jege-ne ba mɔna mo,
ye ba daare ba lɔe a popwaano.
Ba maa ke ni daane
se ba dwoni de amo.
11Wɛ yɔɔre o kwei amo o ke
nɔn-balwaaro jeŋa ne mo,
pa a to puseŋ-nyena jeŋa ne.
12Amo déem jei de bochare-zuru,
ye o laam ba o chɔge-ne.
O ma sɔ a ba ne ye o daare
o dole-ne o de tega ne.
Wɛ bole amo mo.
13O taŋa chena foore
ya tui amo baŋa.
O ma ta-ne o zɔ
a tapwale-bia bam seeni,
ye yibwona tera.
A wo loro tete tage te nwoŋi
te to tega ne mo.
14O yɔɔre o zaŋe amo baŋa ne mo
kuni dedɛ,
ne babea na zo jara wone tei to.
O ma pi o nwoŋi se o jeeri-ne de jara.
15Amo tiini a wo keira ne mo,
ye a daare a zo gare-nyenyaaro
a jei.
A kwei a dam maama
a suli tega kuri ne.
16A yɔɔre a keeri mo taa
pa a yia ba ya seene.
A yibia maama foose mo
a keira kam ŋwaane.
17De ko maama de,
amo wo ke nankɔɔre
a ma a chɔge nɔɔn-nɔɔno yiga.
A maa ná lwoori Wɛ,
a wo chɔge o yiga.
18Ko wo maŋe se a jana bam ba
ba suli tega ne,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo lɔre ko ni ne.
A keira kam ba jege se ka seigi.
19Wolo na zege amo kwaga ne to
nam maŋe o wo Wɛ telaao ne.
Wonto mo wó ŋɔɔne o pa-ne.
20Amo badwonna bam gwooni-ne mo.
Amo nam keeri dedɛ
a kane yi-na a lwoori Wɛ,
21se nɔɔno mo zo nabiinu de Wɛ
tetare laŋa ne,
se o kwɛ debam daane,
ne nabiinu na ŋɔɔne
o pa o dwoŋi tei to.
22Kokuri bena fenfee yerane mo daare,
se amo laam kwei chwoŋa
a vo mɛ nɔɔna na vei
ye ba daa ba jwoori to.”

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?
translation_text:
Job ta ma ta o we:
1“A daa ba jege ŋwea teena.
Amo da yam bwola se ya ti.
Ba laam maa wó ke-ne
yibeeli wone.
2Nɔɔna dedɛ mo jege-ne ba mɔna,
pa se a yɔɔre a na
ba na chuchugi-ne tei to.
3Wɛ, nmo yerane mo a nia
se n zege daare n pa-ne.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa tera
se kotu zege a kwaga ne.
4N pɛ se a badwonna bam boboŋa se mo
pa ba ba lɔre lɔra.
Konto ŋwaane yé pa
se ba wane amo ba di.
5Wolo ná nwoŋi o badwonna bam kwaga ne
se o ma o na nyɔɔre,
kotu bia yia wó dwei mo.
6Wɛ pɛ se amo ji wo-mɔnɔ
nɔɔna tei ne mo.
Ba maa twe lileeru
ba yage a yera ne.
7A yia yam yɔɔre ya dwei,
a wo na tiini ko chɔge to ŋwaane.
A yera maama ma yɔɔre ya ti.
8Nɔn-ŋona ye yaau mo
de kolo na yi amo to.
Ba bane maa wɔe balo na ve
Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem to ŋwaane.
9Balo na wo ba chega wone to
nam yɔɔre ba tɔge ba chwoŋa.
Ba dam dem fɔge de ke de ke da mo,
ba na ba jege tusim to ŋwaane.
10Abam maama nam jwoori-na á ba
se á kwaane á korese-ne!
A nam ta bá na yi-pore-nyem á wone.
11Amo ŋwea da yam gɛ fenfee
se ya ti mo.
A boboŋa ya na jaane se a ke
wonnu telo to daa bá ke.
A teena maama de ma ti.
12A badwonna bam pae se lim
pipiri de ji te-pora.
A maa wo lim wone ye ba tɛ we,
‘Wea pwooni bwola mo.’
13Amo laam na jei a cheigi
se a zo sɔŋɔ kolo wone to mo
ye a yibeeli dem.
A wó vo churu a taa tigi lim wone.
14A maa wó ware gwoŋo kom we,
‘A kwo,’
ye a daare a ta de tóa we,
‘A nu, de a nakɔ, de á lei.’
15Amo teena yam nam daŋe
bɛ baŋa ne mo?
Wɔ mo wó wane o lɔre
a ná jege jwa?
16Teena yam konto wó da ya vo churu
se dé tɔge daane dé vo
dé taa tigi da na?”

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
Bilidad na leiri tei to
1Suuhi tu Bilidad ma leiri o we:
2“Nmo lage n ŋɔɔne tento
n vo n maŋe yein-seeni mo?
Ja swa se dé laam taa ŋɔɔne daane.
3Nmo boŋe we debam ye vara mo
n yiga ne na?
N pae dé ye nɔn-jworru mo na?
4N tɔge n ban-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane mo
n fere n tete n ke zonne.
N nam boŋe we tega baŋa kam
wó da nmo ŋwaane se ka pa
nabiina viiri ba daare-ka na?
Kandwa-zana de maa wó guri
ya na tigi mɛ to,
se ya vo ya to jei-gaa ne na?
5Ko ná ye puseŋ-nyena bam,
ba ŋwea pwooni dem
wó pɔpɔ de dwei mo.
Ba min-vogo pwooni daa bá zaŋe wɛɛne.
6Ba vwoa yam wo pwooni
yeini de ji lim mo,
ye ba min-zwoŋo kom de dwei.
7Ba daane ba nɔne ba na-baara yam
bwom yerane mo.
Ba kwea yam mo de-ba tega ne.
8Ba nɛ sem yeini se ja-ba se vo
se de gwoŋo wone,
pa se ba maŋe da.
9Kalanchogo mo yɔɔre
ko sɔ ba nagwola,
pa se ba ware ba tete se ba vere.
10Ŋona de ka kaleiro mo
ba seigi tega kam ne,
se ka ja-ba ba chwoŋa kam ne.
11Lɛɛro dwi dwi mo fugi-ba
jei maama ne,
pa se foone tiini de jege-ba.
12Ba dam maa lage de jei,
kana na jege-ba to ŋwaane.
Ba ná tiri ba to tega ne,
lɛɛro mo wó ba ba baŋa.
13Jawe-chɛɔ wó di ba yera yam
daa kadwoŋi,
pa se ba ya-nɔna yam moore,
ye toone de ja-ba.
14Ba yɔɔre ba fe-ba mo
pa ba nwoŋi ba vwoa ne,
mɛ ba ya na jei de yazura to,
se ba vo ba te dam toone.
15Nɔn-gɛ maa zoore
ba vwoa yam wone,
ye chilibugu mo ba kwei ba lwo da.
16Puseŋ-nyena bam nye de
teeni delo kuru de de nɛ sem
na kwaare to mo.
17Ba yere yɔɔre de saare mo
logo baŋa ne,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa ba guli ba gula.
18Ba zeili-ba mo
pa ba nwoŋi pwooni wone,
ye ba zo lim wone.
Ba yɔɔre ba le-ba logo kom wone mo.
19Ba maa wo daare dwi ba teo kom ne,
se ko jwa bwoŋi ba yere.
20Nabiina maama ye yaau mo
de kolo na yi puseŋ-nyena bam to,
ko ná ye balo na zoore
wɛ-zoore seeni to
de balo na zoore
wɛ-puli seeni to de.
21Chega ŋwaane to,
wɛleere-keira na wó guri tei to
mo konto.
Ba sam dem wó chɔge mo,
ba na yeiri Wɛ to ŋwaane.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
Job na leiri tei to
1Job ma leiri o we:
2“Abam lage se á tɔge
á botare bia bam ŋwaane
á pa ko zo a yera
á vo á maŋe yein-seeni mo?
3Chaveera ta ba jege abam
de á na bwɛ-ne kuni fuga tento to na?
4Ko nam ná seene ko ye chega we
amo tusi mo,
ko wó taa ye amo yu-wɔrɔ mo,
se ko dae abam yiga.
5Abam boŋe se á bere á tete mo
amo baŋa ne.
Á ta maa pae ko ye amo tusim ŋwaane mo a nɛ a chaveera.
6Nam lɔre-na we ko ye Wɛ yiga mo
pa yaara yanto maama ba a baŋa.
Wonto mo chege kalanchogo
se o ma o ja-ne.
7Amo ná laare mo we,
‘Vuvuga tu a baŋa!’
nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba leiri-ne.
A nam ná beeri wolim,
ba ba pae a jege chega.
8Wɛ chege a yiga mo se a yé na chwoŋa a tɔge da a kɛ.
O ma daare o pa lim kwoli
a chwei sem maama.
9O jaane a zula maama mo o jwoŋi
o daare-ne o zege bwori,
se a daa yé taa jege paare a di.
10O maa yɔɔre o mage-ne o de tega ne,
pa se a jei.
Ko ta ná ye teena yalo a ya na jege to,
o vaŋe-ya o gɔ o yage mo,
ne ba na ke tei de tio kolo
ya na jeiri ko zege to.
11O ban-lom dem wo amo baŋa ne mo,
ye o jeeli amo o ke balo
na ye o dona to wone.
12O jar-keira bam gwɛ de dam mo
ba beena.
Ba yɔɔre ba kwɛ chwoŋa mo
ba tiŋi se ba yi amo,
ye ba chwi ba vwoa
ba gilimi-ne ba ke tetare ne.
13Wɛ ta ke se amo de a chorro tem
taa ware daane mo,
se a badwonna de a fara
de nwoŋi a kwaga ne.
14A chorro maama duri ba daare-ne mo.
A badwonna de ma swei a swia.
15Amo sɔŋɔ veira de a tontoŋ-kana bam maama laam nii-ne
se a taa ye sa-teeno mo a pa-ba.
16Amo ná bwoŋi a tontoŋeno wolo,
kotu bá sɛ se o leiri-ne,
de a na tiini a lwoori‑o
se o duri a ŋwaŋa tei to de.
17A ná sii a yera vio,
ko lwoi a kaane momwa ne mo.
A diga tiina maama de neese-ne
pa ba duri ba daare-ne mo.
18Bu-balwa tete lɔŋe-ne mo.
A maa ná zaŋe wɛɛne,
ba jege-ne ba ke ba mɔna.
19A badwoŋ-swonnu maama de
daa vae a ni taane,
ye ba duri ba daare-ne.
20Amo yɔɔre a di maama mo a ti
a daare kwi yerane.
A momwa ta na sii to mo
se ko daa dae ŋwea mo amo jega.
21Amo badwonna bam, ja!
Kwaane-na se á duri a ŋwaŋa,
se Wɛ yɔɔre o mage-ne
o de tega ne mo.
22Bɛŋwaane mo abam de pare-ne
se á ja nenɛɛne Wɛ na ke tei to?
Ko na tiini ko chɛ amo yera ne tei to ta wo su abam yi na?
23Nɔɔno ya ná wó wane a ni taane
dento o popone o tiŋi tɔnɔ wone,
ko ya wó taa lana dedɛ.
24Ba ná kwei luu ba sare-de
ba ke peo yera ne,
a botare bia bam ya wó taa wora
taa wuu.
25Amo nam yei we wolo na bore
o pa-ne to ŋwe.
Wonto maa wó zaŋe o ŋɔɔne
o pa-ne se ko kweeli.
26Jaweo nam ná di a ya-nɔna yam mo ko ti de,
amo ta wó na Wɛ
ko tɔge a yera yanto wone.
27Chega to, amo tete mo lage a na‑o
de a yia, se ko dae we nɔn-gaa.
A nam yɔɔre a jei a teena
se a na‑o mo.
28Abam tɛ á tete ne we:
‘Pa-na dé yɔɔre dé pare‑o dé ja.
O tete mo jaane cham dento
o ba o pa o tete.’
29Nam kɔre-na foone
de Wɛ na lage o waare abam tei to!
Wɛ wó tɔge o ban-lom dem baŋa
o kwei o se-zɔɔ,
pa se á lɔre we
o seene o di nabiina taane.”

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
Zofara ni taane
1Naamatia tu Zofara ma ta o we:
2“Nmo taane dem yɔɔre
de vevele a wo mo,
ye ko maŋe se a daa ta taane
a woli da,
a boboŋa na daane-ne to ŋwaane.
3Nmo ni taane dem ye toro mo
de pa-ne.
Amo de nam wó da yi-poro ŋwaane
a ta a ni a leiri‑m mo.
4Nmo nam yei ko na maŋe
ko ye tei faŋa faŋa,
ye ba bobo ba ke nabiina
ba yage tega kam baŋa ne to.
5Wopwolo kolo puseŋ-nyena
na yeini ba nae to mo ti lela.
Wɛ-lwɛɛna de na di ywoni delo to
maa ba dáana.
6Ba wae ba zeiŋi ba vɔna
se ya di wɛ-baŋa,
naa ba kwoni ba yuni wɛɛne
se te dwei wɛyuu kom de.
7De ko de, ba lage ba ba
ba ji teero mo ba jei wuu,
se balo ya na yei-ba to taa bwei we,
‘Ba wo yein-seeni mo?’
8Ko wó ke-ba ne nɔɔno na dwɛ dendwɛ
ye de kɛ lela tei to mo.
Ba lage ba jei mo,
nenɛɛne tete wo dendwa
na ye tei to.
9Ba fara de ba sɔŋɔ tiina daa bá na-ba,
ba daa na tera to ŋwaane.
10Puseŋ-nyena bam bia mo jege
se ba jwoori ba yiri jena yalo
ba kwoa na vere yiniga tiina tei ne to.
11Chega ŋwaane, ba ta ná wo
ba nɔn-donne maŋa ne,
ba wó ba ba te mo
de ba dam maama.
12Lwarem kikia sona ya pae
puseŋ-nyeno mo,
pa o yɔɔre o jege-ya o tɔna.
13O maa vae se ya ti o ni ne,
ye o laam liri-de fee fee.
14O wodiu kom konto nam ná yi o wo,
ko wó pipiri ko ji wo-gaa mo.
Ko maa wó ji basankwea vea
o puga ne.
15Ko ta ná ye jejegero telo
kotu na ligi puseŋa baŋa ne to,
Wɛ nam wó pa o tɔne-te o yage.
16O wó mu kapaa vea mo.
Basankwea maa wó done‑o ka go.
17Kotu bá di ywoni tega baŋa
wo-laaro tem baŋa ne,
ne te ná ye tooro de nayel-pepala
na tigi yɔɔ ne bu-dura to de.
18O nam ta wó ga wonnu telo maama
o na yaare te ŋwaane
ye o wo di te ywoni to mo.
O maa bá na o totoŋa yam nyɔɔre.
19Kokuri to, o tiini o bɛɛse yiniga tiina
ye o daare-ba o zege bwori.
O ma vere sam delo o na wo lɔge to,
se o taa zoore de wone.
20O nam bá toŋe o su o fera pa se o sii.
O maa yeini o puuri wonnu telo maama o yi na su to.
21O ná di o ti, kolokolo daa ba daara.
Mo kokuri, o wonnu bá dáane
ye te jei.
22O ná maŋe o na kolo maama
o ya na beeri to,
lwia ta wó taa jege‑o.
Wo-chechɔgɔ de maa wó tiini
ko ja‑o.
23Puseŋ-nyeno wom ná wora o di
o su o fera,
Wɛ ban-lom dem wó ba o baŋa,
pa se ko tiini ko chɛ o yera.
24Kotu ná kwaane se o duri
o daare luuru jara zela,
channa chichwei mo wó zɔ‑o.
25De na moore de maŋe
o yera ne to mo o vaŋe-de
o le o wo loro ne,
ye de ni dem nyeena.
Foone ma tiini de zo‑o.
26Lim wó yɔɔre de kwoli
o lonne wonnu tem maama.
Mini delo nabiina na wo ke to
nam mo wó di‑o,
ye de daare de zwɛ o jejegero
telo maama na daare to kula.
27Wɛyuu kom wó bere o tusim dem mo jaja.
Tega kam baŋa de maa wó pa maana we, o ke o chɔge.
28Na-fwaaro mo lage te chuuri
te chwooli o sɔŋɔ kom te ja te jei
Wɛ ban-lom dɛ dem ne.
29Puseŋ-nyeno wom na wó ba
o guri tei to mo konto.
Wɛ mo maŋe o sɛ we
konto taa tiga kotu ŋwaane.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.
translation_text:
Job ni taane
1Job ma leiri o we:
2“Fɔge á cheigi-na taane delo a na jege se a ta to,
se ko pa amo bochare zuri.
3Zuri-na á yera se á cheigi a taane dem.
Ko kwaga seeni, á laam wae
á daa ta‑á jege-ne á mɔna.
4Amo de nabiina mo jege
ni-kantɔgɔ daane na?
A na ware a tete se a ja to,
ko dae ko chwoŋa ne na?
5Yɔɔre á nii-na amo,
se á daare á ja á nia,
ye á ta ta‑á teili á popwaano.
6Amo ná boŋe kolo na yi-ne to boboŋa,
a nagwola wó te mo.
A yera maa sae pɔm-pɔm de foone.
7Bɛ mo tei pa puseŋ-nyena taa ŋwe
ba dáana tega baŋa ne,
ye ba fɔge ba nae dam
pa de puli de pa-ba?
8Ba jei mo ye ba nae ba bia nɔn-keiri,
pa ba dwi dem puli de pa-ba.
9Kolokolo ba daane-ba ba sam wone.
Wɛ bane de nam ba zaŋe de-ba
se o waare-ba.
10Ba naane tete de puli dedɛ mo
de pa-ba,
ye de dedoa de bá chaare
ko puga ko yage.
11Ba maa pae ba bia kare ba kwɛɛre mo
ne pei-kɔgɔ dwoŋi tei to.
Ba bu-balwa bam sae mo
ye kolokolo ba daane-ba.
12Ba maa jege senyɛ de kwanno
ba leeni lei.
Ba ta wui wi mo ba ke sɔɔ
ba ma di ywoni.
13Puseŋ-nyena bam ŋwea maama wone,
ba yɔɔre ba jege wo-laaro mo ba di,
