5Jerusalem, nenɛɛne amo na wó swei nmo ni ne,
Wɛ de nam wó pa se a jazem dem swei ka totoŋa yam keim.
6Amo ná ba yeini a guli
Jerusalem gula,
Wɛ wó pa se a ni dem
laam meeri mo.
Amo ná ba pae Jerusalem ye
amo wopwolo maama,
Wɛ wó waare-ne konto dwoŋi mo.
7 Baŋa Wɛ, guli Edom tiina bam
na ke tei maama Jerusalem teo
chɔgem dɛ dem ne to,
se n daare n waare-ba.
Banto déem zege dé dona bam
kwaga ne ye ba we:
“Chɔge-na teo kom fase!
Yé daare-na sɔŋɔ dedoa de!”
8Babilon tiina bam, á nam yɔɔre
á maŋe de chɔgem!
Balo na wó jwoori ba ke abam
se ko maŋe de á na ke debam tei to,
Wɛ wó pa se banto taa jege yu-ywoŋo.
9Chega to, balo ná maŋe ba kwei
á bu-sese ba feiri peero yera ne,
Wɛ wó pa se banto de
taa jege yu-ywoŋo.

english_text:
(By David.)
Praise the Lord with All Your Heart
1With all my heart
I praise you, Lord.
In the presence of angels
I sing your praises.
2I worship at your holy temple
and praise you for your love
and your faithfulness.
You were true to your word
and made yourself more famous
than ever before.
3When I asked for your help,
you answered my prayer
and gave me courage.
4All kings on this earth
have heard your promises, Lord,
and they will praise you.
5You are so famous
that they will sing about
the things you have done.
6Though you are above us all,
you care for humble people,
and you keep a close watch
on everyone who is proud.
7I am surrounded by trouble,
but you protect me
against my angry enemies.
With your own powerful arm
you keep me safe.
8You, Lord, will always
treat me with kindness.
Your love never fails.
You have made us what we are.
Don't give up on us now!
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ lei keim
David déem pane leiŋa kanto.
1 Baŋa Wɛ, amo kwei a bochare maama mo
a ma a ke nmo lei.
A maa wó zege
wa yadwonna yam yiga ne
a leeni a seini nmo yere dem.
2Amo wó pipiri a jeeri
n wara-jei selo na ye wose to
ye a laam chɔɔle tega ne a tei‑m.
Kokuri to, n swono kom wora mo
taa wuu,
ye n ta yɔɔre n zege
n chega wone.
N ma‑n pa se n yere dem
zaŋe wɛɛne,
ye ni delo n na tiŋi to
tiini de jege kuri.
3A na keeri a jare nmo to,
nmo leiri a wɛ-lworo kom lela.
Nmo ma‑n pa se a na baare
de dam.
4 Baŋa Wɛ, logo baŋa pwa bam maama wó tei nmo mo,
ne ba ná nigi kwora kalo
na nwoŋi n ni ne to.
5Ba wó leeni mo ba ta
Baŋa Wɛ totoŋa yam taane,
o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom na tiini
ko gaale to ŋwaane.
6 Baŋa Wɛ, n seene n wo wɛ-wɛ mo,
ye n yiga ta wo nabwona wone.
Ko nam ná ye balo
na bere ba tete to,
o zege dáane mo
ye o yei ba chwei sem.
7Cham dedɛ ná maŋe de wo
amo yuu ne,
n ta wó pa a ŋwea jwoori
ka ke dam.
A dona bam bane ná zaŋe
amo baŋa ne,
nmo wó dole-ba jaguli-zane mo.
N ta wó kwei n dam-fɔrɔ kom
n ma n jwoŋi-ne n yage.
8 Baŋa Wɛ zege amo kwaga ne
pae a na bora.
O swono kom wora mo taa wuu.
Baŋa Wɛ, yé kwei debam balo
nmo na ke to
n dole n yage.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
The Lord Is Always Near
1You have looked deep
into my heart, Lord,
and you know all about me.
2You know when I am resting
or when I am working,
and from heaven
you discover my thoughts.
3You notice everything I do
and everywhere I go.
4Before I even speak a word,
you know what I will say,
5and with your powerful arm
you protect me
from every side.
6I can't understand all of this!
Such wonderful knowledge
is far above me.
7Where could I go to escape
from your Spirit
or from your sight?
8If I were to climb up
to the highest heavens,
you would be there.
If I were to dig down
to the world of the dead
you would also be there.
9Suppose I had wings
like the dawning day
and flew across the ocean.
10Even then your powerful arm
would guide and protect me.
11Or suppose I said, “I'll hide
in the dark until night comes
to cover me over.”
12But you see in the dark
because daylight and dark
are all the same to you.
13You are the one
who put me together
inside my mother's body,
14and I praise you because of
the wonderful way
you created me.
Everything you do is marvelous!
Of this I have no doubt.
15Nothing about me
is hidden from you!
I was secretly woven together
out of human sight,
16but with your own eyes you saw
my body being formed.
Even before I was born,
you had written in your book
everything about me.
17 Your thoughts are far beyond
my understanding,
much more than I
could ever imagine.
18I try to count your thoughts,
but they outnumber the grains
of sand on the beach.
And when I awake,
I will find you nearby.
19How I wish that you would kill
all cruel and heartless people
and protect me from them!
20They are always rebelling
and speaking evil of you.
21You know I hate anyone
who hates you, Lord,
and refuses to obey.
22They are my enemies too,
and I truly hate them.
23Look deep into my heart, God,
and find out everything
I am thinking.
24Don't let me follow evil ways,
but lead me in the way
that time has proven true.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ yei wonnu maama ni ne
David déem pane leiŋa kanto.
1Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ,
nmo yɔɔre n buŋi
a maama mo,
pa se n lɔre amo na ye tei maama to.
2Amo ná jeini tega ne
naa a ná zaŋe wɛɛne,
nmo maŋe n yei ko ni ne.
Nmo ná maŋe n ye yiga yiga
tei maama de,
n ta lɔre a boboŋa yam.
3Ko ná ye amo chwoŋa veiŋa maama
dedaane a siu kom maama,
ko ye nmo mo yei a na-veili
de a keina maama.
4 Baŋa Wɛ, amo ná boŋe se a ŋɔɔne
ye a ta wo puri a ni,
nmo maŋe n yei a ŋɔŋa kam maama ni ne.
5Nmo yɔɔre n gilimi amo mo
n ke tetare ne.
Nmo daŋe n jeŋa a baŋa ne
se n zeini-ne.
6Nmo yeino kom na gaale tei to
mo pae se a ye yaau.
Amo boboŋa ware se ya yi
nmo yeino kom na tiini
ko yala tei to.
7Jeiga wora amo na wó vo
se a wane a lu
nmo Jworo kom yiga ne na?
Amo bere a lage a duri
a vo yei ne mo ye nmo tera?
8Amo ná kwaane a di wɛyuu
baŋa baŋa mo
nmo maŋe n wo dáane.
Amo nam ná koge gwoŋo mo
luŋu luŋu
se a vo a yi churu kuri kuri,
nmo daa‑n ta wo dáane de!
9Amo ná jaane wɛɛne ne zuŋa tei
a vo a yi wɛ-puli seeni,
naa a ná vei a gaale naneo kom
yiga yiga a vo a zoore
wɛ-zoore seeni,
10nmo ta wo dáane de,
se n kwei n jeŋa n ma
n bere-ne chwoŋa se a taa via,
se n daare n ma n jazem dem
n ta‑n teili-ne.
11Amo wó ta nenɛɛne,
“A lage a vo a seigi lim wone mo,
pa se de kwoli-ne.
Wea kam wó ji lim pa se
nɔɔna yia daa ba nae.”
12Amo ya ná tage konto dwoŋi,
lim dem nam bá wane nmo yia de che.
Nmo tei ne,
tete dem maa jege pwooni
ko maŋe de wea kam na ye tei to.
Lim dedaane pwooni ye bedwe mo
te pa‑m.
13Nmo mo naane a yera yam maama.
Amo ta na wo a nu puga ne to,
mo n kwei-ya n meeli n ke daane.
14A ke nmo lei dedɛ,
de n na tɔge chwo-kenkagela
n naane-ne se a taa kɔre‑m tei to.
Nmo totoŋa yam maama
maa ye wo-kenkagela,
ye ko ba jege bobwea.
15Amo yera yam kolokolo
wo seigi nmo tei ne
maŋa kalo nmo na naane-ne
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno yeiri ko ni ne to.
Maŋa kalo n na gɔgere amo maama n ke daane
tega kuri gwoŋ-chanluŋu wone to mo konto.
16Maŋa kam konto ne
nmo maŋe n na-ne,
ye a ta wo bege a ti se ba lo-ne.
Ba ta na wo loge-ne se a na
wea pwooni to mo,
nmo maŋe n jeeli da yalo maama
amo na wó taa ŋwe to
n tiŋi n tɔnɔ kom wone.
17Amo Tu Wɛ, nmo boboŋa yam gaale
ya dwoi se a lɔre-ya.
Nɔɔno ware ya ni se o jeeli o ja.
18Amo ná maŋe a kwaane mo
se a ga ya ni,
a ga ga mo a vo a pwoli,
ya na daga ya dwoi buga ni
kasol-bia bam to ŋwaane.
Amo ta ná dɔ a zaŋe,
nmo ta wora amo tei ne.
19Amo Tu Wɛ, nam zaŋe
n go puseŋ-nyena bam!
Abam nɔn-gora bam,
lage-na jei da amo yiga ne!
20Banto kare ba ŋɔɔne wo-balwaaro mo ba pa‑m.
Nmo dona bam fɔ vwa yerane mo.
21 Baŋa Wɛ, amo yɔɔre a chuli
balo na chuli nmo to.
Ko na ye balo na lɔge
nmo kwaga ne to,
amo tiini a neese-ba mo.
22Amo tiini a chuli-ba mo chekke,
ba na jigi a dona to ŋwaane.
23Amo Tu Wɛ, yɔɔre n buŋi
a maama n ja,
se n lɔre amo bochare dem
na ye tei to.
Faŋe a maama n nii,
se n lɔre a boboŋa yam chekke.
24Kwaane se n nii,
tusim chwoŋa wora
amo na tɔge-ka na?
Laam ta‑n tɔge amo yiga,
se a kwei chwoŋa kalo na maŋe ka wora taa wuu to.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
A Prayer for the Lord's Help
1Rescue me from cruel
and violent enemies, Lord!
2They think up evil plans
and always cause trouble.
3 Their words bite deep
like the poisonous fangs
of a snake.
4Protect me, Lord, from cruel
and brutal enemies,
who want to destroy me.
5Those proud people have hidden
traps and nets
to catch me as I walk.
6You, Lord, are my God!
Please listen to my prayer.
7You have the power to save me,
and you keep me safe
in every battle.
8Don't let the wicked succeed
in doing what they want,
or else they might never
stop planning evil.
9They have me surrounded,
but make them the victims
of their own vicious lies.
10Dump flaming coals on them
and throw them into pits
where they can't climb out.
11Chase those cruel liars away!
Let trouble hunt them down.
12Our Lord, I know that you
defend the homeless
and see that the poor
are given justice.
13Your people will praise you
and will live with you
because they do right.
translation_text:
David wɛ-lworo zeinim ŋwaane
1 Baŋa Wɛ, jwoŋi-ne nɔn-balwaaro jeŋa ne n yage!
Kwoli-ne se nankɔ-nyena
yé wane ba ke-ne zonne.
2Banto yeini ba boŋe se ba ke lwarem dwi maama mo.
Ba maa lage se ba taa jaane
ni-kantɔgɔ ba tui.
3Ba nia yam zage mo nya-nya
ne basankwe nia na done tei to.
Ba ni taane maa goe nɔɔna,
ne kapaa vea kam na ke tei to.
4 Baŋa Wɛ, jan ja! Ta‑n kwoli-ne
se puseŋ-nyena yé ma ba dam
ba chɔge-ne.
Ta‑n cho-ne de nankɔ-nyena,
de ba na lage se a to tega ne tei to.
5Boyere-nyena tiŋi kalanchogo mo
se ba ja-ne.
Ba ma che bora amo chwoŋa ne
se a to ka wone.
6Amo lage a ta de Baŋa Wɛ mo a we,
“Nmo mo ye amo Tu Wɛ wom.”
Baŋa Wɛ, nam cheigi
a na ŋwane n yiga ne tei to.
7Amo Teiru Baŋa Wɛ,
n jege dam se n vere-ne n yage.
Jara ná yi amo dɛ delo wone,
n yeini n kwoli a yuu.
8 Baŋa Wɛ, yé sɛ se puseŋ-nyena bam
na wonnu telo
ba fera na zoore to.
Ba ná zaŋe amo baŋa ne,
yé pa ba na pwola
ba toŋe ba lwarem dem.
9Ko ná ye balo na gilimi-ne
se ba ke-ne zonne to,
pa se cham delo ba na boŋe
se ba ke amo yera ne to
jwoori de ba ba tete yuu ne.
10Lwo min-chala n yage ba yuu ne,
se n daare n dole-ba n yage
min-lɔŋɔ wone.
Pa se ba to gwon-chanlunnu wone
se ba daa yé wane ba nwoŋi
te wone.
11Yé pa pwola se bebare-nyena
na jeiŋa jei dé tega kam wone.
Nam pa se lɛɛro pare nankɔ-nyena
te ja lela.
12Amo yei we Baŋa Wɛ mo yeini
o zege o pa yiniga tiina,
pa se nabwona wane
ba na ba chega.
13Chega ŋwaane to,
nɔn-ŋona wó tei n yere dem.
Balo na vei chwo-laao wone to
wó taa zoore n woro kom wone.

english_text:
(A psalm by David.)
A Prayer for the Lord's Protection
1I pray to you, Lord!
Please listen when I pray
and hurry to help me.
2 Think of my prayer
as sweet-smelling incense,
and think of my lifted hands
as an evening sacrifice.
3Help me to guard my words
whenever I say something.
4Don't let me want to do evil
or waste my time doing wrong
with wicked people.
Don't let me even taste
the good things they offer.
5Let your faithful people
correct and punish me.
My prayers condemn the deeds
of those who do wrong,
so don't let me be friends
with any of them.
6Everyone will admit
that I was right
when their rulers are thrown
down a rocky cliff,
7and their bones lie scattered
like crushed rocks
on top of a grave.
8You are my Lord and God,
and I look to you for safety.
Don't let me be harmed.
9Protect me from the traps
of those violent people,
10and make them fall
into their own traps
while you help me escape.
translation_text:
David wɛ-lworo
1 Baŋa Wɛ,
amo keeri a jare nmo mo.
Ja, ke lela n ba n woli-ne.
Pore n zwa se n cheigi
amo wɛ-lworo kom.
2Amo ná yeini a ware nmo,
pa se ko taa nye de talwoŋ-ywoŋa
a na zwɛ a pa‑m to.
A ná zeiŋi a je sem wɛɛne
se a lwoori‑m,
pa se ko taa nye nenɛɛne
dedaan-ni seeni kaanem dem.
3 Baŋa Wɛ, fɔge n yere
amo ni taane dem,
se n che se ta-balɔrɔ
yé nwoŋi a ni ne.
4Ta‑n cho-ne se a fera
yé zo totoŋ-lwanno.
A ba lage se a tɔge a woli
de nɔn-balwaaro
ba puseŋa kikia yam wone,
ne ko ná maŋe ko ywomma tei de.
5Yage se nɔn-ŋom mage-ne.
Keim dem konto dwoŋi
ye lanyerane mo ko pa-ne.
Pa kotu chwoŋa se o korese-ne,
se ko taa nye de nuga mo
o mɛ o turi-ne.
Amo bá ve se o lwo-ka a yuu ne.
Amo nam na lwoori‑m tei to
ye se n che nɔn-balwaaro totoŋ-lwanno tem mo.
6Ba dedɛɛra bam wó pa
ba to de bora
pa se ba zege peero yuu ne
ba to tega ne vim.
Ba laam maa wó sɛ we amo ni taane dem ya jege ywoni.
7Ko wó ke nenɛɛne valo
na chɛ swoori, ye o guri tega
pa ka jage jei maama ne tei to.
Konto dwoŋi mo ba kwi
de lage se jage
se tiŋi churu ni dem ne.
8Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo nam kwoni
a nii nmo mo.
A lage a seigi a tete
nmo woro kom wone.
Yé pa chwoŋa se lɛɛro yi-ne!
9Ko nam ná ye kalanchorro telo
ba na tiŋi se ba ja-ne to,
ta‑n cho a ŋwea se a yé to te wone.
Yé sɛ se wo-lwan-keira na che ba bora kalo amo ŋwaane to ja-ne.
10Nam pa se puseŋ-nyena bam
jwoori ba to ba tete kalanchorro tem wone,
se amo tete laam wane a lu
ba jeŋa ne.

english_text:
(A special psalm and a prayer by David when he was in the cave.)
A Prayer for Help
1 I pray to you, Lord.
I beg for mercy.
2I tell you all my worries
and my troubles,
3and whenever I feel low,
you are there to guide me.
A trap has been hidden
along my pathway.
4Even if you look,
you won't see anyone
who cares enough
to walk beside me.
There is no place to hide,
and no one who really cares.
5I pray to you, Lord!
You are my place of safety,
and you are my choice
in the land of the living.
Please answer my prayer.
I am completely helpless.
6Help! They are chasing me,
and they are too strong.
7Rescue me from this prison,
so I can praise your name.
And when your people notice
your wonderful kindness to me,
they will rush to my side.
translation_text:
Wɛ-lworo zeinim ŋwaane
David déem pane leiŋa kanto maŋa kalo o na seigi peo bɔɔne wone to.
1A keeri mo a jare
Baŋa Wɛ de kwor-dɛa.
A maa lwoori Baŋa Wɛ
se o duri a yibwona.
2A ta yeini a ŋwane o yiga ne,
ye a lwoni a yaara yam maama
a bere‑o.
3Amo vɔna ná yeini ya pare,
nmo yerane mo yei
chwoŋa kalo a na wó tɔge to.
Amo na wó pipiri a vo mɛ maama to
mo a dona bam tiŋi
ba kalanchorro ba seigi
se a to te wone.
4Kwaane n nii amo jazem seeni,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera
se kotu zeini-ne.
A wo nɛ wolowolo
se a sale o yera ne.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yiga tera a wone.
5 Baŋa Wɛ, amo keeri a jare nmo mo.
A maa tɛ a we,
“Nmo mo ye amo dalem jei.
A ta na ŋwe tega baŋa ne to,
nmo mo ye wolo na maŋe
de amo to.”
6Ja, cheigi amo wɛ-lworo kom,
se amo wo mo tiini ko chɔɔre.
Jwoŋi-ne n yage balo na pare-ne
se ba ja to jeŋa ne,
ba na dana ba dwoi amo to ŋwaane.
7Pore-ne n ja n nwoŋi
peena diga kanto wone,
se a laam wó tei nmo yere dem.
N nɔn-ŋona bam wó ba
ba gilimi daane amo ŋwaane,
dedaane n na ke-ne lanyerane
tei to.

english_text:
(A psalm by David.)
A Prayer in Time of Danger
1Listen, Lord, as I pray!
You are faithful and honest
and will answer my prayer.
2 I am your servant.
Don't try me in your court,
because no one is innocent
by your standards.
3My enemies are chasing me,
crushing me in the ground.
I am in total darkness,
like someone long dead.
4I have given up hope,
and I feel numb all over.
5I remember to think about
the many things you did
in years gone by.
6Then I lift my hands in prayer,
because my soul is a desert,
thirsty for water from you.
7Please hurry, Lord,
and answer my prayer.
I feel hopeless.
Don't turn away
and leave me here to die.
8Each morning let me learn
more about your love
because I trust you.
I come to you in prayer,
asking for your guidance.
9Please rescue me
from my enemies, Lord!
I come to you for safety.
10You are my God. Show me
what you want me to do,
and let your gentle Spirit
lead me in the right path.
11Be true to your name, Lord,
and keep my life safe.
Use your saving power
to protect me from trouble.
12I am your servant.
Show how much you love me
by destroying my enemies.
translation_text:
David wɛ-lworo
1 Baŋa Wɛ,
cheigi a wɛ-lworo kom.
Pore n zwa se n ni
a na ŋwane n yiga ne tei to.
N na yɔɔre n zege n chega wone to,
da n nɔn-ŋonne dem ŋwaane
n leiri n pa-ne.
2Yé ja-ne n ba n saŋe n tete yiga ne,
se a ye nmo tontoŋeno mo.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na ŋwe
ye o yɔɔre o jege bora nmo yiga ne.
3Amo dona bam kwaane mo
ba pare-ne
se ba mage-ne ba de tega ne.
Ba ma fe-ne ba ke lim jei ne
nenɛɛne balo na tega ba dáane
na ye tei to.
4Konto ŋwaane,
a vɔna tiini ya pare mo,
ye a wo de chɔɔre dedɛ.
5A ma guli faŋa kam
déem na ye tei to.
A maa boŋe nmo keina yam maama boboŋa,
ye a daare a jeeli n na mɛ n jea
n ke kolo to.
6A maa zeiŋi a je sem wɛɛne
a ware‑m.
A maa tiini a lage‑m
de a wo maama,
ne te-kora na tigi ye na tera tei to.
7 Baŋa Wɛ, ke lela n ba n leiri-ne,
se a vɔna yam laam pare mo.
Yé seigi n yibia amo tei ne,
se a laam wó taa nye de
balo na maa vei churu to.
8Amo ná yeini a zaŋe
zezeŋa maama ne,
pa se a taa guli
nmo swono kom gula.
Kokuri to,
a ke a wo-dedoa dedaane‑m.
Nam pa se a lɔre chwoŋa kalo
a na wó tɔge to,
a na kwei a tete a pa‑m to ŋwaane.
9 Baŋa Wɛ, jwoŋi-ne n yage
a dona bam jeŋa ne .
A duri mo a ba se a seigi
n woro kom wone.
10Bere-ne a na wó ke tei
se a taa ke nmo boboŋa yam,
nmo na ye amo Tu Wɛ wom to ŋwaane.
Sɛ se n Jwori-laao kom
tɔge amo yiga
se a taa vei tega kalo
na maŋe daane to baŋa ne.
11 Baŋa Wɛ, da n yere dem ŋwaane
se n pa a ŋwea jwoori ka ke dam.
Tɔge n nɔn-ŋonne dem baŋa ne
n le-ne yaara wone.
12Nmo na jege a swono taa wuu to,
yɔɔre n chɔge a dona bam n ti!
Ko ná ye balo maama
na beeri amo gom to,
saare-ba tega baŋa ne se ba jei.
Kokuri to,
amo ye nmo tontoŋeno mo.

english_text:
(By David.)
A Prayer for the Nation
1I praise you, Lord!
You are my mighty rock,
and you teach me
how to fight my battles.
2You are my friend, my fortress,
where I am safe.
You are my shield,
and you made me the ruler
of our people.
3 Why do we humans mean anything
to you, our Lord?
Why do you care about us?
4We disappear like a breath;
we last no longer
than a faint shadow.
5Open the heavens like a curtain
and come down, Lord.
Touch the mountains
and make them send up smoke.
6Use your lightning as arrows
to scatter my enemies
and make them run away.
7Reach down from heaven
and set me free.
Save me from the mighty flood
8of those lying foreigners
who never tell the truth.
9In praise of you, our God,
I will sing a new song,
while playing my harp.
10By your power, kings win wars,
and your servant David is saved
from deadly swords.
11Won't you keep me safe
from those lying foreigners
who never tell the truth?
12Let's pray that our young sons
will grow like strong plants
and that our daughters
will be as lovely as columns
in the corner of a palace.
13May our barns be filled
with all kinds of crops.
May our fields be covered
with sheep by the thousands,
14and every cow have calves.
Don't let our city be captured
or any of us be taken away,
and don't let cries of sorrow
be heard in our streets.
15Our Lord and our God,
you give these blessings
to all who worship you.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de teem
David déem pane leiŋa kanto.
1 Baŋa Wɛ maŋe dedaane tia,
se wonto nye de peo kolo
amo na dale da to mo.
O maa bere-ne
se a taa yei jara keim laŋa.
2A Tu Wɛ wom jege a swono mo
taa wuu.
O maa ye amo dam jei,
de a dalem jei, de a jwoŋinu.
O maa yeini o cho-ne,
ne jara nantana na kwoli nɔɔna
jara wone tei to,
ye a seigi a tete o woro kom wone.
O maa jaane dwi-gɛ tiina o tui
o ke amo dam kuri ne.
3 Baŋa Wɛ, bɛ mo ke
ye n yiga wo nabiina wone?
Bɛŋwaane mo n jege nabiin-bia boboŋa konto?
4Nabiina maama momwɛ
ye vio yerane mo.
O ŋwea da yam yeini ya ti lela
nenɛɛne lunluŋu na ye tei to mo.
5 Baŋa Wɛ, kɔɔre wɛyuu kom
nenɛɛne diga ni gɔrɔ,
se n daare n tu tega kam baŋa.
Twe n jeŋa n dwei peero tem,
se te tɔre min-vogo
ye nyoa zaŋe gulululu.
6Kwei doa pepelem
n ma n bage n dona bam
pa se ba jage jei maama ne.
Kwei n che-tɛɛra yam n ta-ba
pa se ba duri ba jei.
7Zege wɛyuu baŋa kam ne
n twe n jeŋa n ja-ne,
se n jwoŋi-ne n yage.
Liiri-ne n ja n nwoŋi
na-fwaaro tem wone,
se dwi-gɛ tiina yé taa jege dam
a baŋa ne.
8Banto nia yam yɔɔre ya su mo
dedaane vwa.
Ba na yeini ba pwooli se ba ke kolo to maa ye gana yerane mo.
9Amo Tu Wɛ,
a lage a leeni leiŋ-doŋa mo
a ma a seini‑m.
A ta wó kwei kɔnɔ a ta,
se a ma a zuli‑m.
10Kokuri to, nmo mo zeini pwa
se ba wane ba dona ba di.
N ta ma jwoŋi n tontoŋeno David
n yage,
se o dona yé go‑o jara wone.
11Vere-ne dwi-gɛ tiina jeŋa ne
n yage.
Banto nia yam yɔɔre ya su mo
dedaane vwa.
Ba na yeini ba pwooli
se ba ke kolo to
maa ye gana yerane mo.
12Sɛ se dé bia bam
ke nɔɔna lanyerane,
nenɛɛne teeni na jege
de bere lela tei to.
Dé bukwa de wó taa jege lam,
nenɛɛne ywoa yalo
na teili pɛ di-kamunu
ye ba gɔgere-ya lanyerane tei to.
13Nam ta pa dé tuli sem taa sui
de wodiiru dwi dwi,
se dé pei sem de taa lore bia zanzam, moro moro laŋa ne,
pa se se faare tega kam maama.
14Pa se dé naane dem yɔɔre
de taa lore bia dɛ dɛ.
Yé pa dé dona chwoŋa
se ba wane dé teo kom ba zo,
se ba kale debam ba ja viiri.
Che se nɔɔna yé taa chwoosa
dé teo kom chwei sem ne.
15Wɛ ná ke konto dwoŋi
o zeini teo kolo
yu-ywoŋo wo ko nɔn-bia bam
tei ne!
Ko ta ná ye nɔɔna balo
na sɛ Baŋa Wɛ
se o taa ye ba Teiru to,
yu-ywoŋo wo ba tei ne!

english_text:
(By David for praise.)
The Lord Is Kind and Merciful
1I will praise you,
my God and King,
and always honor your name.
2I will praise you each day
and always honor your name.
3You are wonderful, Lord,
and you deserve all praise,
because you are much greater
than anyone can understand.
4Each generation will announce
to the next your wonderful
and powerful deeds.
5I will keep thinking about
your marvelous glory
and your mighty miracles.
6Everyone will talk about
your fearsome deeds,
and I will tell all nations
how great you are.
7They will celebrate and sing
about your matchless mercy
and your power to save.
8You are merciful, Lord!
You are kind and patient
and always loving.
9You are good to everyone,
and you take care
of all your creation.
10All creation will thank you,
and your loyal people
will praise you.
11They will tell about
your marvelous kingdom
and your power.
12Then everyone will know about
the mighty things you do
and your glorious kingdom.
13Your kingdom will never end,
and you will rule forever.
Our Lord, you keep your word
and do everything you say.
14When someone stumbles or falls,
you give a helping hand.
15Everyone depends on you,
and when the time is right,
you provide them with food.
16By your own hand you satisfy
the desires of all who live.
17Our Lord, everything you do
is kind and thoughtful,
18and you are near to everyone
whose prayers are sincere.
19You satisfy the desires
of all your worshipers,
and you come to save them
when they ask for help.
20You take care of everyone
who loves you,
but you destroy the wicked.
21I will praise you, Lord,
and everyone will respect
your holy name forever.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ lamma
David déem pane leiŋa kanto se o ma tei Wɛ.
1Amo Tu Wɛ,
nmo ye a Pɛ.
Amo wó taa tei‑m,
ye a zuli nmo yere dem mo.
2Dɛ maama wone a lage
a taa seini‑m,
ye a daare a taa zeiŋi
n yere dem taa wuu mo.
3 Baŋa Wɛ jege kamunni mo!
O maa seene o maŋe dedaane tia.
O kamunni dem daga de dwoi
se dé wane dé lɔre de kuri maama.
4Kwoa wó lwoni nmo totoŋ-zana yam ba bere ba bia
se ba taa seini nmo.
5Ba lage ba ŋɔɔne nmo paare dem
nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ taane mo
ba bere nɔɔna.
Amo de maa wó taa boŋe
nmo totoŋ-kenkagela yam boboŋa.
6Nɔɔna wó taa tɔɔle nmo na tɔge
n dam dem baŋa ne
n ke totoŋ-zana tei to.
Amo de maa wó taa ŋɔɔne
nmo kamunni dem taane.
7Ba ta wó tɔɔle nmo na jege yere
nmo lanyerane dem ŋwaane tei to,
ye ba daare ba leeni de wopwolo
ba seini nmo
n bora borem ŋwaane.
8 Baŋa Wɛ tiini o jege yibwona
dedaane zaane o maa zeini nɔɔna.
O yeini o peene o bane mo.
O swono kom maa tiini ko daga.
9 Baŋa Wɛ yeini o ke nɔɔna maama lanyerane.
Ko ná ye woŋo kolo maama
o na ke to,
o maa duri ba maama yibwona.
10 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo na naane
woŋo kolo maama to
wó taa ke nmo lei dedɛ.
Balo na ke ba chega de nmo to
maa wó taa tei‑m.
11Ba ta wó taa tɛ nmo paare dem
na jege nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ tei to,
de nmo dam dem na daga tei to.
12Ko laam maa wó pa se
nabiina maama lɔre totoŋ-zana
yalo nmo na toŋe to ni ne.
Ba ta wó lɔre nmo paare dem
na tiini de jege nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ tei to.
13Paare delo nmo na di to
wó taa wora mo ga taa wuu.
Dwi dedwe ná kɛ
se dedwoŋi laam saŋe de ba,
nmo wó taa tei nɔɔna
se ko taa vei wuu.
[Baŋa Wɛ yeini o zege
o chega wone mo
de o na tage kolo maama to.
O ta maa yeini o jege
nɔɔna yibwona
de totoŋa yalo maama o na ke to.]
14Ko ná ye balo na lage ba to to,
Baŋa Wɛ yeini o teili-ba mo o zege.
O maa zeini balo vɔna na pare to
se ba wane ba zege de dam.
15Nɔɔna maama jege nmo teena mo.
Nmo mo pa-ba ba ni-wodiu
ko maŋa ne chekke.
16Nmo ma‑n puri n jataala yam
n kwei wo-laaro dedɛ n pa
balo maama n na naane to
pa se ba di ba su.
17 Baŋa Wɛ yɔɔre o tɔge chwoŋa
de kolo maama o na ke to mo.
Maŋa maama o jege
nɔɔna ŋwaŋa.
18 Baŋa Wɛ yeini o zeini balo maama
na lwoori‑o to,
nenɛɛne ba ná lwoori‑o
de ba wo maama.
19O toŋe o tɔge balo na kɔre‑o to boboŋa mo.
Ba ná keeri ba jare‑o,
o ta wó cheigi ba wɛ-lworo kom,
ye o daare o jwoŋi-ba o yage.
20 Baŋa Wɛ cho balo na swoi‑o to mo.
Ko nam ná ye puseŋ-nyena bam,
o lage o chɔge ba maama mo fase.
21Amo wó ma a ni mo a tei Baŋa Wɛ.
Ko maŋe se nabiina maama
taa zuli‑o taa wuu,
o yere dem na ye wose to ŋwaane.

english_text:
Shout Praises to the Lord
1Shout praises to the Lord!
With all that I am,
I will shout his praises.
2I will sing and praise
the Lord God
as long as I live.
3You can't depend on anyone,
not even a great leader.
4Once they die and are buried,
that will be the end
of all their plans.
5The Lord God of Jacob blesses
everyone who trusts him
and depends on him.
6 God made heaven and earth;
he created the sea
and everything else.
God always keeps his word.
7He gives justice to the poor
and food to the hungry.
The Lord sets prisoners free
8and heals blind eyes.
He gives a helping hand
to everyone who falls.
The Lord loves good people
9and looks after strangers.
He defends the rights
of orphans and widows,
but destroys the wicked.
10The Lord God of Zion
will rule forever!
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Wɛ lei keim
1Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!
Amo tɛ a tete wone mo we,
“Tei Baŋa Wɛ!”
2Amo wó yɔɔre a tei a Tu
Baŋa Wɛ wom
a ŋwea maama wone.
A wó taa leeni a seini‑o
se ko taa nii a ŋwea kam kweelim.
3Yé kwei-na á teena á daŋe dedɛɛra
naa nabiina wolowolo baŋa ne,
se ba bá wane abam
ba jwoŋi ba yage.
4Kokuri to, ba siu kom ná kɔga,
ba yeini ba jwoori tega kuri ne mo.
Dɛ dem konto nɔɔ mo
ba ya na jege boboŋa yalo maama to wó jei.
5Wolo nam ná sɛ we
Jakob Wɛ wom ye o zeinnu,
yu-ywoŋo wo kotu tei ne,
o teena maama na wo
o Tu Baŋa Wɛ yera ne to ŋwaane.
6 Baŋa Wɛ mo naane wɛyuu kom,
de tega kam,
de naneo kom, dedaane kolo maama na wo te wone to.
O maa yeini o zege o chega wone
taa wuu.
7O maa pae se balo nɔɔna na
jege-ba ba bɛɛse to na ba bora,
ye o daare o pae kana
na jege balo to ba ni-wodiu.
Baŋa Wɛ vere balo na wo
peena diga ne to o yage
pa ba nwoŋi da.
8O ta maa puri lilwoa yia pa ba nae.
Ko ná ye balo vɔna na pare to,
Baŋa Wɛ pae se ba wane
ba zege de dam.
O maa swoi balo na jege chega
o yiga ne to.
9 Baŋa Wɛ nii balo na ye veira
sa-teo wone to baŋa ne.
O maa zeini botara de kadeina.
Ko nam ná ye puseŋ-nyena,
o yeini o che ba yiga.
10 Baŋa Wɛ wó taa di paare mo
taa wuu.
Zion tiina bam,
abam Tu Wɛ wom mo konto,
maŋa maama se ko taa vei wuu.
Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!

english_text:
Sing and Praise the Lord
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Our God is kind,
and it is right and good
to sing praises to him.
2The Lord rebuilds Jerusalem
and brings the people of Israel
back home again.
3He renews our hopes
and heals our bodies.
4He decided how many stars
there would be in the sky
and gave each one a name.
5Our Lord is great and powerful!
He understands everything.
6The Lord helps the oppressed,
but he smears the wicked
in the dirt.
7Celebrate and sing!
Play your harps
for the Lord our God.
8He fills the sky with clouds
and sends rain to the earth,
so that the hills
will be green with grass.
9He provides food for cattle
and for the young ravens,
when they cry out.
10The Lord doesn't care about
the strength of horses
or powerful armies.
11The Lord is pleased only
with those who worship him
and trust his love.
12Everyone in Jerusalem,
come and praise
the Lord your God!
13He makes your city gates strong
and blesses your people.
14God lets you live in peace,
and he gives you
the very best wheat.
15As soon as God speaks,
the earth obeys.
16He covers the ground with snow
like a blanket of wool,
and he scatters frost
like ashes on the ground.
17God sends down hailstones
like chips of rocks.
Who can stand the cold?
18At his command the ice melts,
the wind blows,
and streams begin to flow.
19God gave his laws and teachings
to the descendants of Jacob,
the nation of Israel.
20But he has not given his laws
to any other nation.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Wɛ zeini debam cham maŋa ne
1Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!
Ko lamma mo se dé leeni
dé seini dé Tu Wɛ wom,
ko na pae ywoni
ye ko tɔge chwoŋa to ŋwaane.
2 Baŋa Wɛ lage o fɔge o lɔ
Jerusalem teo kom.
O maa lae Isarele tiina balo
ya na jage jei maama ne to
o ke daane se ba jwoori
ba tete teo kom.
3O maa zuri balo wo na pɛ to bochara,
ye o vɔ ba fufwollu tem pa te jei.
4O jeeli chalechwe sem ni mo o ja,
ye o daare o bwoŋi se maama
dedoa dedoa de ka yere.
5Dé Teiru wom yɔɔre
o jege kamunim mo,
ye o dam dem gaale.
Dé ware se dé lɔre o yeino kom
dé ti.
6 Baŋa Wɛ yeini o zeiŋi balo
na tu ba tete to mo wɛɛne.
Ko nam ná ye puseŋ-nyena bam,
o lage o meere-ba mo o de tega ne.
7Leeni-na á tei Baŋa Wɛ
ye á ke o lei.
Kwei-na kwanno á ta
á ma á zuli‑o.
8Wɛ yeini o pae se kunkwonnu kwoli wɛyuu kom maama.
O ta maa pae se doa nene
tega kam baŋa ne,
se gaaro de nwoŋi
te faare zwonnu tem.
9Wonto mo pae vara ba ni-wodiu,
ko ta woli de bachangaaro de,
ne te ná keera wodiu ŋwaane.
10Wɛ ba jege wopwolo de
sisein-nɔɔna na dana tei to.
O yiga maa tera jar-keira
de ba baare dem wone.
11 Baŋa Wɛ wo nam pwoli
de balo na kɔre‑o to,
ba na kwei ba teena ba daŋe
o swono kom baŋa ne to ŋwaane.
12Jerusalem teo nɔn-bia bam,
zeiŋi-na Baŋa Wɛ yere dem.
Zion tiina bam,
tei-na á Tu Wɛ wom.
13Kokuri to, wonto fɔge o kwɛ
á teo kom ni-bworru tem,
pa se te damma.
O ma daare o swɛ abam balo
na zoore ko wone to swolim.
14O maa pae se yazura taa wo
á tega kam ni maama ne,
ye á na men-dala dedɛ
se á ta‑á di á sui.
15Wɛ yeini o toŋe o kwora mo
se ka yi logo baŋa ni maama.
Ka maa ke lela ka vei
jei maama ne.
16O ma pa se kunu ba
ko kwoli tega kam
ye ka peere cha
ne lɔŋɔ na ye tei to.
Ko ta ná ye nyɔnɔ,
o yeini o pa se ko jage lela mo
ne tentwarem tei to.
17O maa dole do-kandwa
o yage tega baŋa ne.
O waaro tem ná bobo se te zuri,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o zege
te yiga ne.
18O laam ma toŋe o kwora
se o pa tento maama nyeene.
O ta ma pa se vio kom zaŋe
ko taa dola,
pa se bwi sem na bam
jwoori ba taa dura.
19Wɛ toŋe o kwora mo
se Jakob dwi tiina bam lɔre-ka.
O ma kwei o bera yam
de o nia yam
o pa Isarele tiina bam
se ba taa tɔge-ya.
20 Dwi-gɛ tiina nam tera
Wɛ na ke konto dwoŋi o pa-ba.
Banto maŋe ba yeiri
o bera yam ni ne.
Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!

english_text:
Come Praise the Lord
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Shout the Lord's praises
in the highest heavens.
2All of you angels,
and all who serve him above,
come and offer praise.
3Sun and moon,
and all of you bright stars,
come and offer praise.
4Highest heavens, and the water
above the highest heavens,
come and offer praise.
5Let all things praise
the name of the Lord,
because they were created
at his command.
6He made them to last forever,
and nothing can change
what he has done.
7All creatures on earth,
you obey his commands,
so come praise the Lord!
8Sea monsters and the deep sea,
fire and hail, snow and frost,
and every stormy wind,
come praise the Lord!
9All mountains and hills,
fruit trees and cedars,
10every wild and tame animal,
all reptiles and birds,
come praise the Lord!
11Every king and every ruler,
all nations on earth,
12every man and every woman,
young people and old,
come praise the Lord!
13All creation, come praise
the name of the Lord.
Praise his name alone.
The glory of God is greater
than heaven and earth.
14Like a bull with mighty horns,
the Lord protects
his faithful nation Israel,
because they belong to him.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de teem
1Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!
Abam balo na wo wɛyuu kom ne to
tei-na Baŋa Wɛ!
Tei-o-na wɛ-wɛ baŋa jei sem maama ne!
2Abam balo na ye o malese
ye á wo o kwaga kɔgɔ kom wone to, tei-o-na!
3Wea kam de chana kam,
ko maŋe se abam de taa tei‑o!
Se abam chalechwe sem
na pepele to de tei‑o!
4Wonnu maama na wo wɛyuu kom baŋa ne to, tei-o-na!
Ko ta woli de na balo na tigisi wɛyuu kom baŋa ne to,
ba-na á tei‑o!
5Ko maŋe se woŋo maama mo
taa tei‑o,
kokuri to, wonto mo dɛ o ni dem ŋwaane o naane-te.
6O déem pɛ se te zege
te zega jei ne taa wuu,
ye kolokolo daa ware o ni dem konto ko chɔge.
7Abam balo na wo
tega kam baŋa ne to
tei-na Baŋa Wɛ!
Naneo wo vare-kamuna bam,
de wonnu telo maama na zoore naneo kom kuri kuri ne to,
tei-o-na!
8Ko ná ye doa pepelem,
de do-kandwa, de kunu, de nyɔnɔ,
ko woli de vo-dɛɔ dwi maama
na sɛ o ni dem to,
tei-o-na!
9Peero de zwonnu tem maama,
de kagoa wo teeni,
dedaane teeni delo
nɔɔna na jeiri ba kare ne to,
ba-na á tei‑o!
10Ko ta woli de kago-vara,
de sɔŋɔ-vara,
dedaane tega-veila,
de zuna dwi maama,
tei-o-na!
11Tega baŋa pwa bam,
de dwi tiina maama,
dedaane nakwa,
de dedɛɛra maama,
12ko woli de nɔn-donno, de bukwa,
de nɔn-kwe, de bu-balwa,
á maama tei-o-na!
13Pa-na se wonnu maama tei Baŋa Wɛ,
o yere dem na tiini de daga
de gaale to ŋwaane!
O nenɔŋa kam de daga ka dwoi
woŋo kolo maama na wo
tega baŋa ne
dedaane wɛyuu maama ne to.
14O zeiŋi o tete nɔɔna bam mo
pa se ba na dam de zula.
O ke konto o pa o nɔn-swonnu
Isarele tiina bam mo.
Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!

english_text:
A New Song of Praise
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Sing him a new song of praise
when his loyal people meet.
2People of Israel, rejoice
because of your Creator.
People of Zion, celebrate
because of your King.
3Praise his name by dancing
and playing music on harps
and tambourines.
4The Lord is pleased
with his people,
and he gives victory
to those who are humble.
5All of you faithful people,
praise our glorious Lord!
Celebrate and worship.
6 Praise God with songs
on your lips
and a sword in your hand.
7Take revenge and punish
the nations.
8Put chains of iron
on their kings and rulers.
9Punish them as they deserve;
this is the privilege
of God's faithful people.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Leiŋ-doŋa
1Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!
Leeni-na leiŋ-doŋa
á ma‑á tei Baŋa Wɛ.
Jeeri-na de o nɔn-ŋona kɔgɔ kom
á tei‑o.
2Pa-na se Isarele dwi tiina bam
di ywoni ba Keiru wom ŋwaane,
se Zion tiina bam taa chaka
de wopwolo ba Pɛ wom ŋwaane.
3Pa-na se ba taa sae Wɛ yiga ne
ba maa seini o yere dem.
Ba ta wó taa wɔe senyɛ
ye ba mage kwanno ba zuli‑o.
4Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ wo pwoli
de o nɔɔna bam kikia.
O jwoŋi balo na tu ba tete to o yaga,
pa se ba na nenɔŋa nɔɔna yiga ne.
5Pa-na se balo na kɔre Wɛ to taa chaka
dedaane zula yalo o na pɛ-ba to.
Pa-na se ba taa leeni de ywoni,
ne ba ná tigi ba sare wone tei to.
6Ko maŋe se tia lei taa wo ba ni ne,
ye ba ta zei jara se-zɔɔro ba jea ne.
7Ba maa wó jwoori ba ŋwe ba jene
dwi-gɛ tiina bam baŋa ne,
ye ba tiini ba waare-ba.
8Ba maa wó kwei chegero
ba vɔ teene dedwonna pwa bam,
ye ba daare ba ma luuru
ba lei ba dedɛɛra bam nɛ sem ne.
9Ba keim dem konto wó ŋwe jene
delo ya na tigi ba dona bam
baŋa ne to mo.
Konto to, balo maama na kɔre Wɛ to wó na zula.
Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!

english_text:
The Lord Is Good to His People
1Shout praises to the Lord!
Praise God in his temple.
Praise him in heaven,
his mighty fortress.
2Praise our God!
His deeds are wonderful,
too marvelous to describe.
3Praise God with trumpets
and all kinds of harps.
4Praise him with tambourines
and dancing,
with stringed instruments
and woodwinds.
5Praise God with cymbals,
with clashing cymbals.
6Let every living creature
praise the Lord.
Shout praises to the Lord!
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de teem!
1Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!
Pa-na o jwoŋi o tia
o wara-jei sem ne!
Pa-na o jwoŋi o tia wɛyuu ne
mɛ na ye o dam jei sem to!
2Tei-o-na o totoŋ-zana yam ŋwaane,
de o na daga o dwoi kamunim dwi maama to ŋwaane.
3Wu-na nabwanno á ma‑á tei‑o,
se á daare á ta kwanno á tei‑o.
4Kwei-na senyɛ á ma‑á tei‑o,
se á kwɛɛre á sa.
Ta ta-na kwanno dwi dwi
ye á wu wi se á ta‑á tei‑o!
5Mage-na zwe, de konkwanno
na wó ke sɔɔ baŋa baŋa to
á ma á tei‑o!
6Ko maŋe se woŋo kolo maama
na wae ko sii vio to
mo tei Baŋa Wɛ.
Pa-na dé tei Baŋa Wɛ!

english_text:
How Proverbs Can Be Used
1 These are the proverbs
of King Solomon of Israel,
the son of David.
2Proverbs will teach you
wisdom and self-control
and how to understand
sayings with deep meanings.
3You will learn what is right
and honest and fair.
4From these, an ordinary person
can learn to be smart,
and young people can gain
knowledge and good sense.
5If you are already wise,
you will become even wiser.
And if you are smart,
you will learn to understand
6proverbs and sayings,
as well as words of wisdom,
and all kinds of riddles.
7 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of knowledge.
Only a fool rejects wisdom
and good advice.
Warnings against Bad Friends
8My child, obey the teachings
of your parents,
9and wear their teachings
as you would a pretty hat
or a lovely necklace.
10Don't be tempted by sinners
or listen 11when they say,
“Come on! Let's gang up
and kill somebody,
just for the fun of it!
12They're well and healthy now,
but we'll finish them off
once and for all.
13We'll take their valuables
and fill our homes
with stolen goods.
14If you join our gang,
you'll get your share.”
15Don't follow anyone like that
or do what they do.
16They are in a big hurry
to commit some crime,
perhaps even murder.
17They are like a bird
that sees the bait,
but ignores the trap.
18They gang up to murder someone,
but they are the victims.
19The wealth you get from crime
robs you of your life.
Wisdom Speaks
20 Wisdom shouts in the streets
wherever crowds gather.
21She shouts in the marketplaces
and near the city gates
as she says to the people,
22“How much longer
will you enjoy
being stupid fools?
Won't you ever stop sneering
and laughing at knowledge?
23Listen as I correct you
and tell you what I think.
24You completely ignored me
and refused to listen;
25you rejected my advice
and paid no attention
when I warned you.
26“So when you are struck
by some terrible disaster,
27or when trouble and distress
surround you like a whirlwind,
I will laugh and make fun.
28You will ask for my help,
but I won't listen;
you will search,
but you won't find me.
29No, you would not learn,
and you refused
to respect the Lord.
30You rejected my advice
and paid no attention
when I warned you.
31“Now you will eat the fruit
of what you have done,
until you are stuffed full
with your own schemes.
32Sin and self-satisfaction
bring destruction and death
to stupid fools.
33But if you listen to me,
you will be safe and secure
without fear of disaster.”
translation_text:
1Isarele teo pɛ Solomon na ye David bu to memaŋa mo tento.
2Memaŋa yanto nam ye se ya bere nɔɔna swa se ya daare ya korese-ba. Ya wó woli nɔɔna se ba taa ni yi-poro taane kuri, ye ba pɔɔre taana daane. 3Ya ta wó kaane nɔɔna se ba kwei yi-poro ba ma ja ba tete, se ba kikia taa tɔge chwoŋa, ne ko na maŋe de chega kam tei to. 4Memaŋa yam wae ya pae nayeiri-nyena ja boboŋ-ŋona. Ya ta wae ya pae nɔn-donno na yeino de yi-poro. 5Yi-pore-nyena de ná cheigi-ya, ba wó zamese ba woli ba swa wone. Boboŋ-boŋena de wó fɔge ba lɔre chwoŋa ba taa tɔge-ka. 6Ko maa wó pa se nɔɔna lɔre memaŋa yam kuri, ko woli de sinseiri, de dende selo maama swa tiina na yeini ba ŋɔɔne to.
7Nabiina na kɔre Baŋa Wɛ mɛ to,
yeino de puli dáane mo.
Ko daare jworru yerane mo
wó gwooni swa taane
de koresem.
Yé pa ba soge‑m ba wane
8Amo bu, sɛ se n jwoŋi n kwo koresem.
Nam yé swei n nu na bere‑m tei to.
9Pa ba bera yam taa tigi n bochare ne,
ne nenɔŋa zambili mo n de
n ba ne to.
10Amo bu, ne wɛleere-keira ná jege‑m ba soga,
se n yé sɛ ba taane dem.
11Ba wó wane ba ta de nmo we,
“Pa dé ke daane,
se dé vo dé vwɛ chwoŋa ni ne,
dé daare dé nwoŋi dé ja nɔɔna
dé go,
ye ba nam wo ke kolokolo ba chɔge.
12Dé wó ti-ba lela nenɛɛne dé ná nɛ-ba,
de ba ná maŋe ba jege yazura
tei maama de.
Dé wó li-ba ne ba ga zo tega kuri mo tei.
13Pa-na dé tɔge daane dé vere
ba wo-laaro tem dé taa tei,
pa se dé sam su de ba jejegero tem.
14Konto to, ba n woli debam wone,
se dé ná pɛ wonnu tem,
dé wó pɔɔre te wone dé pa‑m.”
15Amo bu, ba ná tage konto dwoŋi,
yé da n woli ba wone.
Nam ja n tete se n lɔŋe
ba na wo mɛ to.
16Kokuri, nɔn-balwaaro tem konto
gare ba toŋe lwarem,
ye ba lage lela de nɔn-gora totoŋa.
17Wolo ná boŋe se o ja zuŋa,
kotu bá pa ka na kalanchogo
kolo o na chege ka ŋwaane to.
18Venverena bam konto nam na vwɛ
se ba go nɔɔna to,
ko ye ba tete dwi mo ba lage ba ja.
19Wolo maama ná boŋe se o duni
kampina baŋa ne,
kotu wó guri konto mo.
Jejegero telo o na vere to mo
wó ba te chɔge‑o.
Ba maŋe yi-poro de bukɔ daane
20Yi-poro mo zege teo kom chwei sem de ko yaga kam ni ne ko tɔɔla ko yaga. 21Teo kom pwooni mɛ nɔɔna na jeeri ba ke sɔɔ to, de ko manchwo-nia yam ne mo ko zege da ko ŋɔɔne baŋa baŋa ko we:
22“Nayeiri-nyena, dɛ dɔ mo
á wó yage á jworim dem?
Nɔn-lwɛɛna, á de wó ta‑á lwɛ
á dwonna taa,
se á vo á maŋe yei ne mo?
Nɔn-jworru, á wó yage ka-taa-chuli-yeino maŋa kɔ mo?
23Á ya ná sɛ a bwɛa yam,
amo de ya wó kwei a bochare maama a pa abam,
ye a pa á lɔre kolo na tigi
a boboŋa ne to.
24Abam nam ve amo beeri dem,
pa se a twe a je a jeeri abam
ye á wo ke-ne á ke da.
25Abam ta maa wo pɛ se a kwea yam jege kuri ya pae abam,
ye á daare á wo ke á yiga
de bwɛa yalo a na pɛ to.
26Konto ŋwaane amo de wó ke abam mo a mɔne,
de á na lage á na cham tei to.
27Foone maa wó ja abam
nenɛɛne vo-dɛɔ dwoŋi,
ye lɛɛro de ba á baŋa se te li abam
ne vo-kekara na ke tei to.
28Ba laam wó lwoori wolim amo tei ne,
ye a ve se a leiri-ba.
Ba maa ná beeri a jei tei de,
ba bá na-ne.
29Kokuri, ba yɔɔre ba chuli yeino mo,
ye ba ve we,
ba bá taa kɔre Baŋa Wɛ.
30Ba maa wo sɛ amo kwea yam,
ye ba ta kwareme ba zwa
de a bwɛa yam.
31Konto ŋwaane ba wó su de yaara
ba chwoori-ya,
ba boboŋ-lwanno tem
de ba kikia yam ŋwaane.
32Kokuri, nayeiri-nyena ve bera mo
pa ba lage ba te lela.
Nɔn-jworru yiga maa tera de kolokolo
pa ba wó na chɔgem.
33Ko daare, wolo maama ná sɛ
a bera yam,
ko wó ke lam ko pa kotu.
O bochare bá taa zaga de kolokolo,
ye kolokolo foone de bá taa jege‑o.”

english_text:
Wisdom and Bad Friends
1My child, you must follow
and treasure my teachings
and my instructions.
2Keep in tune with wisdom
and think what it means
to have common sense.
3Beg as loud as you can
for good common sense.
4Search for wisdom
as you would search for silver
or hidden treasure.
5Then you will understand
what it means to respect
and to know the Lord God.
6 All wisdom comes from the Lord,
and so do common sense
and understanding.
7God gives helpful advice
to everyone who obeys him
and protects those
who live as they should.
8God sees that justice is done,
and he watches over everyone
who is faithful to him.
9With wisdom you will learn
what is right
and honest and fair.
10Wisdom will control your mind,
and you will be pleased
with knowledge.
11Sound judgment and good sense
will watch over you.
12Wisdom will protect you
from evil schemes
and from those liars
13who turned from doing good
to live in the darkness.
14Most of all they enjoy
being mean and deceitful.
15They are dishonest themselves,
and so are all their deeds.
Wisdom and Sexual Purity
16Wisdom will protect you
from the smooth talk
of a sinful woman,
17who breaks her wedding vows
and leaves the man she married
when she was young.
18The road to her house leads
down
to the dark world
of the dead.
19Visit her, and you will never
find the road to life again.
20Follow the example
of good people
and live an honest life.
21If you are honest and innocent,
you will keep your land;
22if you do wrong
and can never be trusted,
you will be rooted out.
translation_text:
1Amo bu, sɛ se n jwoŋi a bera yam.
Kwei nia yalo a na pɛ‑m to
n ke n bochare ne.
2Pore n zwa se n ja swa,
n daare n kwei n boboŋa maama
n pa yi-poro.
3Yɔɔre n beeri yi-poro,
se n daare n lwoori yeino
de kwor-dɛa.
4Chɛ se n beeri swa,
ne ya ye lu-nyenno
telo na seigi to mo.
5N ná ke konto, n wó lɔre Baŋa Wɛ kɔrɔ na ye tei chekke,
ye n daare n me ded‑o.
6Kokuri Baŋa Wɛ mo kwei swa
o pae nabiina.
O ta maa woli-ba de yeino de yi-poro.
7O maa jege swa chekke
se o kwei o pa nɔn-ŋona.
Ko ta ná ye balo na yɔɔre
ba tɔge chwoŋa to,
o kwoli-ba ne jara nantana mo tei.
8O nii ko baŋa ne mo
se chega taa toŋa,
ye o che balo na jege o chega to,
se cham yé yi-ba.
9Nmo ná sɛ se n jwoŋi swa,
n laam wó ba n lɔre kolo na lana
ye ko tɔge chwoŋa to.
N ta wó lɔre kolo na maŋe keim to,
se n wane n tɔge chwo-laao.
10N boboŋa maa wó ja swa,
ye yeino de pa n na wopwolo lanyerane.
11Nmo na lɔre lɔra tei to mo
wó taa kwoli‑m.
N boboŋ-ŋona maa wó taa yere‑m.
12Konto to, n bá‑n ta‑n tɔge
puseŋ-nyena chwei sem,
naa n to pipiri-nyena chwoŋa ne.
13Banto maŋe ba ywori chega chwoŋa kam ne mo,
ye ba vei lim wone.
14Ba ta swoi se ba taa toŋe lwarem mo,
ye ba wo de tiga de puseŋa kikia.
15Ba ye nɔn-ŋollo mo
ye ba kikia ba tɔge chwoŋa.
16Swa chekke wó che‑m de ka-tola,
de o ná maŋe o ŋɔɔne ni-som ŋɔŋa
se o ma soge‑m tei de.
17Kotu yage o baro wolo o na zo
o donne maŋa ne to,
pa se o yiri ni delo o na gwoni
Wɛ yiga ne to.
18Chwoŋa kalo na vei o sɔŋɔ kom ne to guri de toone mo.
Balo na tɔge da to maa zoore churu.
19Wolo maama ná vei o tei,
kotu daa ba jwoora.
O nam daa bá to
ŋwea chwoŋa kam wone.
20Nmo nam ná jwoŋi swa,
n laam wó ta‑n tɔge
nɔn-ŋona nɛ-bwora mo,
ye n vei chega tiina chwoŋa ne.
21Kokuri to, balo na yɔɔre
ba tɔge chwo-laao to mo
wó taa zoore dé tega kam wone.
22Ko daare puseŋ-nyena bam yere
wó saare tega kam baŋa ne.
Nɔn-ŋollo de maa wó jei ka wone.

english_text:
Trust God
1My child, remember
my teachings and instructions
and obey them completely.
2They will help you live
a long and prosperous life.
3Let love and loyalty
always show like a necklace,
and write them in your mind.
4 God and people will like you
and hold you in high esteem.
5With all your heart
you must trust the Lord
and not your own judgment.
6Always let him lead you,
and he will clear the road
for you to follow.
7 Don't ever think that you
are wise enough,
but respect the Lord
and stay away from evil.
8This will make you healthy,
and you will feel strong.
9Honor the Lord by giving him
your money and the first part
of all your crops.
10Then you will have
more grain and grapes
than you will ever need.
11 My child, don't turn away
or become bitter
when the Lord corrects you.
12 The Lord corrects
everyone he loves,
just as parents correct
a child they dearly love.
The Value of Wisdom
13God blesses everyone
who has wisdom
and common sense.
14Wisdom is worth more
than silver;
it makes you much richer
than gold.
15Wisdom is more valuable
than precious jewels;
nothing you want
compares with her.
16In her right hand
Wisdom holds a long life,
and in her left hand
are wealth and honor.
17Wisdom makes life pleasant
and leads us safely along.
18Wisdom is a life-giving tree,
the source of happiness
for all who hold on to her.
19By his wisdom and knowledge
the Lord created
heaven and earth.
20By his understanding
he let the ocean break loose
and clouds release the rain.
21My child, use common sense
and sound judgment!
Always keep them in mind.
22They will help you to live
a long and beautiful life.
23You will walk safely
and never stumble;
24you will rest without a worry
and sleep soundly.
25So don't be afraid
of sudden disasters
or storms that strike
those who are evil.
26You can be sure that the Lord
will protect you from harm.
27 Do all you can for everyone
who deserves your help.
28Don't tell your neighbor
to come back tomorrow,
if you can help today.
29Don't try to be mean
to neighbors who trust you.
30Don't argue just to be arguing,
when you haven't been hurt.
31Don't be jealous
of cruel people
or follow their example.
32The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is dishonest,
but he lets good people
be his friends.
33He places a curse on the home
of everyone who is evil,
but he blesses the home
of every good person.
34 The Lord sneers at those
who sneer at him,
but he is kind to everyone
who is humble.
35You will be praised
if you are wise,
but you will be disgraced
if you are a stubborn fool.
translation_text:
Pa Wɛ n chega
1Amo bu, yé swei wonnu telo
a na jege a bere‑m to.
Nam yɔɔre n pa a nia yam
taa tigi n boboŋa wone.
2Kokuri, n ná tɔge-ya,
n wó na momwɛ-dɛɛre,
ye wonnu da chwoŋa te pa‑m.
3Fɔge n ta‑n jege chega de swono,
se n yé yage-te.
Pa tento taa nye de zambili
n na kwei n de n ba ne to.
Pa te taa tigi n boboŋa ne wuu,
ne n na popone-te n tiŋi
kandwa-pelɛ yera ne tei to.
4Konto baŋa ne mo Wɛ de nabiina
wó taa lage n ni taane,
ye n na yere-ŋom.
5Kwei n chega maama
n daŋe Baŋa Wɛ baŋa ne.
Nam yé teege nmo tete boboŋa baŋa ne.
6Totoŋe delo maama n na wó ke to,
ta‑n yei Baŋa Wɛ ni ne.
Konto mo o wó pa wonnu maama kwei te chwoŋa te pa‑m.
7Yé fɔge n jeeli n yuu ne we
nmo mo yei n tia.
Nam ta‑n kɔre Baŋa Wɛ
ye n duri lwarem kikia.
8Konto mo wó pa n na yazura,
ye n dam dem wó jwoori n tete ne.
9Kwei n jejaano tem
n ma n zuli Baŋa Wɛ,
se n daare n kwei n da-yiga wodiiru pɛɛra n pa‑o.
10Konto baŋa ne mo n tuli wó su
de wodiiru,
ye sa-doora de taa daga ba gaale,
pa n yeiri n na wó ke-te mɛ.
11Amo bu, ne Baŋa Wɛ ná jege‑m
o koresa, se n sɛ koresem.
O maa ná bwɛ‑m,
se n yé pa n yiga nyɔne.
12Kokuri, Baŋa Wɛ korese
balo o na swoi to mo,
ne kwo na ke tei de o bu-swono to.
Swa na lana tei to
13Wolo maama ná lɔre swa
ye o jege yi-poro,
kotu yuu ywomma.
14Swa tiini ya jege kuri
ya dwoi lu-nyenno.
Ya maa jege nyɔɔre
ya dwoi sabu-seŋa de.
15Ya ta maa jege lonne
ya dwoi kandwa-nyenno.
Nmo fera ná zo woŋo kolo maama,
ko bá yi swa na ye tei to.
16Swa zei momwɛ-dɛɛre mo o jazem ne.
Jejegero de yere-kamunu maa wo
pɛɛra yalo o na zei o jagwia ne to.
17Swa chwei sem jege ywoni mo.
Se tɔgem maa pae nɔɔna bochara zura.
18Swa nye de tio kolo bia
na pae ŋwea to mo,
balo na beeri-ya se ba jwoŋi to
tei ne.
Ya ma yeini ya ja yu-ywoŋo ya ba
ya pa balo na puuri-ya ba ja to.
19 Baŋa Wɛ dɛ o swa ŋwaane mo
o chwi tega baŋa kam kuri.
O ma tɔge o yi-poro baŋa ne
o pa se wɛyuu kom de wora.
20O mɛ o yeino mo o pɔɔre
naneero tem yera yera,
ye o daare o pa doa taa zege
kunkwonnu wone ka nena.
21Amo bu, ta‑n mae swa chekke
de boboŋ-laaro n toŋa.
Yé pa se te vere n jeŋa ne
te daare‑m.
22Tento mo wó pa n ŋwea
taa jege kuri lanyerane,
ye ka taa jege lam ka pa‑m,
ne zambili mo n de n ba ne to.
23Te ta wó pa n veiŋa tɔge chwoŋa,
se n yé seeri n to tega ne.
24N ma‑n ná tigi n sia,
foone bá taa jege‑m.
Nmo nam ná peini se n dɔ mo de,
n wó dɔ mo yɔlɔ-lɔ-lɔ.
25Foone bá ja‑m,
ne lɛɛro ná pɔpɔ te ba n baŋa,
naa chɔgem ná to puseŋ-nyena yuu ne.
26Kokuri, Baŋa Wɛ mo wó pa
n wo taa tiga.
Wonto wó taa cho‑m cham wone,
se kolokolo yé ja‑m pa n to.
27N dwoŋi ná maŋe se n woli‑o,
ye nmo ná jege kolo
na wó woli‑o to,
se n yé vane‑o.
28Nmo ná wae n dwoŋi n wola leile,
nam yé ta ded‑o we,
“Vei se n jwa jwoori n ba
se a woli‑m.”
29Ko ná ye n faro wolo
na pɛ nmo o chega to,
yé boŋe lwarem se n ma n chɔge‑o.
30Yé mage kantɔgɔ de nɔɔno
yɔɔ yerane,
ne kotu ná wo chɔge n yiga
kolokolo baŋa ne.
31Yé pa se n boboŋa zo
nankɔ-nyena kikia wone.
Nam yé lwoni ba totoŋ-naga kam.
32Kokuri, Baŋa Wɛ chuli nɔn-ŋollo mo.
Ko nam ná ye nɔn-ŋona,
o lɔge o wo o bere banto mo.
33 Baŋa Wɛ sɔɔle lwarem mo o yage
puseŋ-nyem sɔŋɔ ne.
Ko daare nɔn-ŋom sɔŋɔ su
de o zaane mo.
34Ko ná ye nɔn-lwɛɛna,
Wɛ nii-ba kafɛ mo.
Ko daare ye o zaane wo balo na tu ba tete to yuu ne.
35Swa tu yere wó zaŋe mo.
Nɔn-jworo maa wó di o chaveera.

english_text:
Advice to Young People
1My child, listen closely
to my teachings
and learn common sense.
2My advice is useful,
so don't turn away.
3When I was still very young
and my mother's favorite child,
my father 4said to me:
“If you follow my teachings
and keep them in mind,
you will live.
5Be wise and learn good sense;
remember my teachings
and do what I say.
6“If you love Wisdom
and don't reject her,
she will watch over you.
7The best thing about Wisdom
is Wisdom herself;
good sense is more important
than anything else.
8If you value Wisdom
and hold tightly to her,
great honors will be yours.
9It will be like wearing
a glorious crown
of beautiful flowers.”
The Right Way and the Wrong Way
10My child, if you listen
and obey my teachings,
you will live a long time.
11I have shown you the way
that makes sense;
I have guided you
along the right path.
12Your road won't be blocked,
and you won't stumble
when you run.
13Hold firmly to my teaching
and never let go.
It will mean life for you.
14Don't follow the bad example
of cruel and evil people.
15Turn aside and keep going.
Stay away from them.
16They can't sleep or rest
until they do wrong or harm
some innocent victim.
17Their food and drink
are cruelty and wickedness.
18The lifestyle of good people
is like sunlight at dawn
that keeps getting brighter
until broad daylight.
19The lifestyle of the wicked
is like total darkness,
and they will never know
what makes them stumble.
20My child, listen carefully
to everything I say.
21Don't forget a single word,
but think about it all.
22Knowing these teachings
will mean true life
and good health for you.
23Carefully guard your thoughts
because they are the source
of true life.
24Never tell lies or be deceitful
in what you say.
25Keep looking straight ahead,
without turning aside.
26 Know where you are headed,
and you will stay
on solid ground.
27Don't make a mistake by turning
to the right or the left.
translation_text:
Bera yadwonna
1A bia bam, cheigi-na á kwo bera. Ke-na á zwa keo se á wane á lɔre lɔra. 2A kwea yam jege kuri mo. Konto to, yé ve-na a bera yam. 3Amo biini maŋa ne ye a ta ye bu-pwola to mo a nu déem swoi-ne, ne a na ye o bu-doa to. A kwo de ma jeini-ne tega ne 4o bere-ne o we:
“Ta‑n jege a botare sem n boboŋa ne,
ye n daare n ta‑n ke n tɔge a nia yam,
se n wó na momwɛ-dɛɛre.
5Beeri swa dedaane yi-poro.
Yé swei a bera yam ni ne, nam yé ve-ya.
6Yé ma n kwaga n ya yi-poro,
se o wó taa kwoli‑m.
Nam yɔɔre n ta‑n swoi‑o
se o taa nii n baŋa ne.
7Yi-poro mo jege kuri
ko dwoi wonnu maama.
Konto to, kwaane n beeri swa jei.
N ná maŋe n beeri kolo maama
se n ta‑n tei,
ta chɛ se n lɔre lɔra.
8Pa yi-poro taa jege lonne o pa‑m,
se o wó pa n na yere-zɔŋɔ.
N ma‑n ná kukwori‑o,
o wó pa n na zula.
9O wó ke zaane o ke n yuu ne,
ne o milimi ga-punnu daane mo
o sɔ-te o ke da to.
O ta wó pa n na nenɔŋa,
ne o kwei paare yipuga mo
o pu n yuu ne to.”
10Amo bu, sɛ se n ke n tɔge
amo bera yam,
se ko pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre.
11Amo kwei nmo mo a de
swa chwoŋa kam ne,
se n ta‑n tɔge chega chwei sem.
12Nmo ma‑n ná via,
kolokolo bá che n yiga.
N nam ná duri lela,
n bá‑n tiri n to tega ne.
13Zamese bera n ke n boboŋa ne,
se n yé yage-ya.
Fɔge n nii ya baŋa ne,
kokuri yanto mo wó pa
n ni ŋwea ywoni.
14Yé lwoni puseŋ-nyena kikia yam,
naa n tɔge nɔn-balwaaro nɛ-bwora.
15Nam lɔŋe banto dwi chwei sem,
se n ja n tete de ba totoŋ-naga kam.
Pipiri se n daare n ta‑n vei
n veiŋa.
16Kokuri, ba ná wo toŋe lwarem,
ba bá peini ba dɔ.
Dɔɔne ba tui ba yia,
ne ba ná wo pɛ se nɔɔno to tega ne.
17Puseŋa kikia de vuvuga totoŋa mo ye ba ni-wodiu.
18Nɔn-ŋona na jege ŋwea kalo to
nye de te-pora ni pwooni dem mo.
Pwooni dem konto lɔɔre de ke da mo
se ko vo ko yi wea tetare maŋa.
19Ko nam ná ye puseŋ-nyena bam,
ba ŋwea maama yɔɔre
ka ye ligi-ligi mo.
Ba maa yeiri wonnu telo na pae ba tiri ba toe tega ne to.
20Amo bu, ke n zwa keo se n cheigi
kolo a na jege se a ta de nmo to.
21Yé swei a bera yam swia,
de fenfee de.
Nam yɔɔre n pa ya taa tigi
n boboŋa ne.
22Kokuri, balo na lɔre-ya to
wó na ŋwea ya baŋa ne.
Ya ta maa pae nɔɔna jege yazura chekke.
23Kolo na dwoi maama to,
fɔge n ta‑n yei n boboŋa yam ni ne.
Kokuri to, n ŋwea totoŋe maama puli dáane mo.
24Yé ta‑n jege ni-zɛ ni-zɛ.
Nam yé ta‑n kare n ŋɔɔne ta-yɔɔro.
25Kwaare n yuu n yiga ne,
se n yé bare n nii jei jei.
26Ta‑n yei n tete na-veili ni ne,
se n tɔge chwoŋa kalo
na ye chekke to.
27Yé lɔ chwoŋa n vo jazem seeni,
naa jagwia seeni.
Nam yɔɔre n ta‑n cho n tete
de lwarem kikia.

english_text:
Be Faithful to Your Wife
1My son, if you listen closely
to my wisdom and good sense,
2you will have sound judgment,
and you will always know
the right thing to say.
3The words of an immoral woman
may be as sweet as honey
and as smooth as olive oil.
4But all that you really get
from being with her
is bitter poison and pain.
5If you follow her,
she will lead you down
to the world of the dead.
6She has missed the path
that leads to life
and doesn't even know it.
7My son, listen to me
and do everything I say.
8Stay away from a bad woman!
Don't even go near the door
of her house.
9You will lose your self-respect
and end up in debt
to some cruel person
for the rest of your life.
10Strangers will get your money
and everything else
you have worked for.
11When it's all over,
your body will waste away,
as you groan 12and shout,
“I hated advice and correction!
13I paid no attention
to my teachers,
14and now I am disgraced
in front of everyone.”
15You should be faithful
to your wife,
just as you take water
from your own well.
16And don't be like a stream
from which just any woman
may take a drink.
17Save yourself for your wife
and don't have sex
with other women.
18Be happy with the wife
you married
when you were young.
19She is beautiful and graceful,
just like a deer;
you should be attracted to her
and stay deeply in love.
20Don't go crazy over a woman
who is unfaithful
to her own husband!
21The Lord sees everything,
and he watches us closely.
22Sinners are trapped and caught
by their own evil deeds.
23They get lost and die
because of their foolishness
and lack of self-control.
translation_text:
1Amo bu, ke n zwa keo
se n cheigi swa de yi-poro taane
delo a na jege se a ta de nmo to.
2Ko wó pa n lɔre kolo na maŋe keim,
ye yeino taane wó taa wo n ni ne.
3Kokuri, ka-tola ke ni-som de nɔɔna,
ne to-nuga na lura tei to mo.
O ni taane maa yɔɔre de swola
ne nuga na ye tei to.
4Se ko kweeli to, o kikia maama wó pa
n na chanɛɛre de zonne yerane mo.
5O nɛ-bwora guri de toone mo.
Balo na tɔge‑o to maa vei churu.
6O yiga tera de chwoŋa kalo
na pae ŋwea to.
O ma tusi chwoŋa kam,
ye o daa yeiri woŋo kolo
o na jege o ke to.
7Konto to, amo bu,
cheigi a taane dem.
Yé se n zwa de a na jege kolo
a tɛ to.
8Nam lɔŋe ka-dwi dem konto chwoŋa kam.
Maŋe n yé twɛ o sɔŋɔ seeni.
9Yé dole n zula n yage.
Ko ná dae konto,
nankɔ-nyem wó ja‑m o go.
10Veira maa wó ba ba ba jwoŋi
n jejegero ba taa tei,
pa se nmo na yaare n na kolo to
laam kweeli nɔn-gaa sɔŋɔ ne.
11Se ko ba ti maama to,
n yera maama wó bugi ya jei mo,
pa se n ŋwana 12ye n we:
“Bɛ mo ye a déem chuli koresem?
A déem wo sɛ bwɛa se bɛ mo?
13A nam ve a berena bam taane,
ye a daare a se a zwa
de ba bera yam.
14Amo laam nam zege
se a na a lɛɛro mo,
pa se a na a chaveera
nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne.”
Ta‑n jege chega n pa n kaane wom
15Ta‑n jege swono lara
de n kaane yerane,
nenɛɛne nɔɔno na wó nyɔ
o tete lɔɔ wone na tei to.
16Ko dae se n pa n lɔɔ wo na bam
taa tigi zɛɛra,
se wolo maama ná yia,
se o twei o nyɔ.
17Yé pa nɔn-gaa tɔge o nyɔ-ba,
se nmo yerane mo wó taa nyɔ
ko wone.
18Ta‑n pae n yi sui de n tete lɔɔ wo na bam maŋa maama.
Ta‑n di ywoni taa de kaane wolo
n na maŋe n di
n nɔn-donne maŋa ne to.
19Pa o taa jege lam n yibia ne,
ne woŋa dwoŋi to,
se o yela yam taa jege fera
ya pa‑m taa wuu,
ye o swono kom de taa pae
n su de wopwolo.
20Amo bu, nmo wó pa ka-tola ja‑m
o ke o ja-bɔŋɔ ne se bɛ mo?
Bɛ mo wó pa n vo n kukwori nɔɔno wodwoŋi kaane?
21Kokuri, nabiinu kikia maama
ye jase mo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.
O maa yei dé na-veili maama ni ne.
22Puseŋ-nyeno tete wɛleera mo
jwoori ya jaane‑o.
Ya nye de ŋone mo
ya vɔge‑o ya tiŋi.
23Kotu na ware o tete o peene to
pa o lage o te lela.
O wó ba o tusi ye o jei mo,
o na tiini o toŋe jworim to ŋwaane.

english_text:
Don't Be Foolish
1 My child, suppose you agree
to pay the debt of someone,
who cannot repay a loan.
2Then you are trapped
by your own words,
3and you are now in the power
of someone else.
Here is what you should do:
Go and beg for permission
to call off the agreement.
4Do this before you fall asleep
or even get sleepy.
5Save yourself, just as a deer
or a bird tries to escape
from a hunter.
6You lazy people can learn
by watching an anthill.
7Ants don't have leaders,
8but they store up food
during harvest season.
9How long will you lie there
doing nothing at all?
When are you going to get up
and stop sleeping?
10 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
11Suddenly, everything is gone,
as though it had been taken
by an armed robber.
12Worthless liars go around
13 winking and giving signals
to deceive others.
14They are always thinking up
something cruel and evil,
and they stir up trouble.
15But they will be struck
by sudden disaster
and left without a hope.
16There are six or seven
kinds of people
the Lord doesn't like:
17Those who are too proud
or tell lies or murder,
18those who make evil plans
or are quick to do wrong,
19those who tell lies in court
or stir up trouble
in a family.
20Obey the teaching
of your parents—
21always keep it in mind
and never forget it.
22Their teaching will guide you
when you walk,
protect you when you sleep,
and talk to you
when you are awake.
23The Law of the Lord is a lamp,
and its teachings
shine brightly.
Correction and self-control
will lead you through life.
24They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
25Don't let yourself be attracted
by the charm and lovely eyes
of someone like that.
26A woman who sells her love
can be bought for as little
as the price of a meal.
But making love
to another man's wife
will cost you everything.
27If you carry burning coals,
you burn your clothes;
28if you step on hot coals,
you burn your feet.
29And if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you pay the price.
30We don't put up with thieves,
not even with one who steals
for something to eat.
31And thieves who get caught
must pay back
seven times what was stolen
and lose everything.
32But if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you will destroy yourself
by your own stupidity.
33You will be beaten
and forever disgraced,
34because a jealous husband
can be furious and merciless
when he takes revenge.
35He won't let you pay him off,
no matter what you offer.
translation_text:
Ni-kaana yadwonna
1Amo bu, nmo ná kwei n tete
n zege daare ŋwaane
se n ŋwe n dwoŋi jene n pa‑o,
ko ná fɔge ko dae nɔn-veira,
2ko bere we nmo tete ni taane mo
lage de ja‑m ne kalanchogo tei.
3Amo bu, ko nam ye se n ke tento mo,
se n wane n jwoŋi n tete,
nmo je na wo n dwoŋi wom
ni ne to ŋwaane.
Nam véi n tu n tete o yiga ne,
se n daare n lwoori‑o
se o ma o chɛ‑m.
4Ke lela n vo o tei,
ye n ta wo sii de fenfee de.
5Nam ke nmo na wó ke tei maama
se n wane n lu to,
nenɛɛne feira naa zuŋa
na kwaane ka lu
ka jaro jeŋa ne tei to.
6Nmo wolo na ye jawɔre-nyem to,
véi n nii memela na chɛ
de totoŋa tei to,
se n daare n jwoŋi swa ba tei ne.
7Banto ba jege ba yiga tu naa pɛ.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba nii ba baŋa ne.
8De ko maama de, ba yeini ba pɛ ba wodiiru te maŋa ne,
ye ba daare ba tiŋi-te
cham maŋa ŋwaane.
9Nmo wolo na ye jawɔre-nyem to,
nmo wó ta‑n tigi n dɔa taa
se n vo n maŋe yei ne mo?
Nmo ba lage n zaŋe
n tiga jei sem ne na?
10Tɔ. Daa ta‑n dɔ fenfee n woli da.
Kwogili n yia se n sii.
Ta‑n tigi n peiga jei sem ne ziim.
11Yiniga wó vɔɔre ka zi‑m,
ne venvereno na zaŋe
nɔɔno baŋa ne tei to mo.
Gɛɛre de maa wó pɔpɔ de ja‑m lanyerane.
12Nɔn-wo-koro na toŋe lwarem tei to,
o kare fɔ vwa mo.
13O ta yeini o go yi mo ye o yeese o jea
se o gane o dwonna.
14Kotu jeeli lwarem mo se o ke,
o boboŋa na ywori to ŋwaane.
O ná vei mɛ maama,
nankɔɔre mo zaŋe dáane.
15Konto ŋwaane mo lɛɛro wó pɔpɔ
te ba o baŋa.
O maa wó yɔɔre o na chɔgem
ye o bá lu de wone.
16Wonnu teredo mo Baŋa Wɛ chula.
Chega to, wonnu terepɛ maa ye
wo-zɔɔna o tei ne.
17Te maa ye:
Wolo na bere o tete kamunim to,
de wolo na jege ni-zɛ ni-zɛ to,
de nɔn-goro,
18de wolo na jei o boŋe lwarem
o pae o dwonna to,
de wolo na yɔɔre o wuuri
de lwarem keim to,
19de wolo na fɔ vwa
taane dim baŋa ne to,
dedaane wolo na pae vuvuga tui
o dwonna tetare ne to.
Gwalem taane
20Amo bu, ta‑n ke n tɔge ni delo n kwo na pɛ‑m to.
Nam yé swei n nu
na bere‑m kolo to ni ne.
21Pa ba bera yam taa tigi n boboŋa ne,
se ya taa nye de zambili
n na kwei n de n ba ne to.
22Nmo ná vei mɛ maama,
ya wó taa wo n yiga ne
ya bere‑m chwoŋa.
Nmo ná tigi n dɔa de,
ya wó taa yere‑m.
Nmo daa ná zaŋe,
ya wó pa‑m kwea.
23Kokuri, ba bera yam nye de
min-zwoŋo mo.
Ya maa ye pwooni ya pa‑m
se n ta‑n via.
Ba koresem dem de maa wó pa
n ni ŋwea ywoni.
24Taana yam konto wó che‑m
de ka-balɔrɔ,
ko fɔge ko dae ka-tola
na wó kwei ni-som
se o soge‑m tei to.
25Yé ke n fera o ya-tega lam dem wone.
Nam yé sɛ se o go o yia
o ma-ya o ja‑m.
26Nɔɔna ŋwe woŋo fee mo
ba pae ka-bworo
ye ba peini ded‑o.
Nmo ta ná peini de nɔɔno wodwoŋi kaane,
o laam wó sɔ‑m mo wuu.
27Nmo ná seigi min-chala
n gare-fɛɛle ne,
n gɔrɔ kom bá ja mini na?
28Nmo nam ná nɔne min-chala
baŋa ne,
n nɛ bá pwogili na?
29Ko nam ta ye bedwe mo de wolo
na wó vo o peini
de nɔɔno wodwoŋi kaane to.
Wolo maama ná ke konto,
ko wó tiini ko zo kotu yera.
30Ba ba ŋwane ba pae ŋweeno we,
kana jege‑o ka ni pa o ŋɔ
se o zuri o kana.
31Ba nam ná jaane‑o,
kotu wó ŋwe o na ŋɔge kolo to
kuni berepɛ,
pa se o ga o sɔŋɔ jejegero maama.
32Agɛboŋa yerane mo wó ke bwoŋa
de nɔn-gaa kaane.
Kotu yɔɔre o beeri chɔgem mo
o pa o tete.
33O maŋe de waarem mo,
ye ba wó kwei tetɔ-goro
ba pu o yuu ne.
O chaveera yam de maa bá fɔge
ya ti.
34Kokuri, kazwe wiiri kan-baro bane mo ko ke da.
O ná lage o yiri o jena,
o bá ja ŋwaŋa kɔtaa.
35Ba ná maŋe ba ja kolo maama
ba ba se ba ja o naga,
o wo ta bá zuri.
Ba nam ná pɛ‑o dim
se ko taa mae tei de,
o bá sɛ se o jwoŋi-de.

english_text:
The Foolishness of Unfaithfulness
1My son, pay close attention
and don't forget
what I tell you to do.
2Obey me, and you will live!
Let my instructions be
your greatest treasure.
3Keep them at your fingertips
and write them
in your mind.
4Let wisdom be your sister
and make common sense
your closest friend.
5They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
6From the window of my house,
I once happened to see
7some foolish young men.
8It was late in the evening,
sometime after dark.
9One of these young men
turned the corner
and was walking by the house
of an unfaithful wife.
10She was dressed fancy
like a woman of the street
with only one thing in mind.
11She was one of those women
who are loud and restless
and never stay at home,
12who walk street after street,
waiting to trap a man.
13She grabbed him and kissed him,
and with no sense of shame,
she said:
14“I had to offer a sacrifice,
and there is enough meat
left over for a feast.
15So I came looking for you,
and here you are!
16The sheets on my bed
are bright-colored cloth
from Egypt.
17And I have covered it
with perfume made of myrrh,
aloes, and cinnamon.
18“Let's go there
and make love all night.
19My husband is traveling,
and he's far away.
20He took a lot of money along,
and he won't be back home
before the middle
of the month.”
21And so, she tricked him
with all of her sweet talk
and her flattery.
22At once he followed her
like an ox on the way
to be slaughtered,
or like a fool on the way
to be punished
23and killed with arrows.
He was no more than a bird
rushing into a trap,
without knowing
it would cost him his life.
24My son, pay close attention
to what I have said.
25Don't even think about
that kind of woman
or let yourself be misled
by someone like her.
26Such a woman has caused
the downfall and destruction
of a lot of men.
27Her house is a one-way street
leading straight down
to the world of the dead.
translation_text:
Nɔn-doŋo de ka-bworo taane
1Amo bu, sɛ se n jwoŋi a bera yam. Kwei nia yalo a na pɛ‑m to n ke n yuu ne. 2Ta‑n ke n tɔge a nia yam, se n wó na momwɛ-dɛɛre. Ta‑n ni a bera yam nenɛɛne ya ye n tete yi-chele-bu mo to. 3Ta‑n guli ya gula maŋa maama. Pa ya taa tigi n boboŋa ne wuu, ne n na popone-ya n tiŋi kandwa-pelɛ yera ne tei to. 4Sɛ se swa chekke taa nye de n nakɔ mo, se yi-poro de taa ye n badwoŋ-swono. 5Banto ná wo n tei ne, ko wó che‑m de ka-bworo kom. Nmo ma‑n wó lu ka-tola kalo na mae ni-som o soge nɔɔna to jeŋa ne.
6Amo yɔɔre a zege a sɔŋɔ takworo ni ne mo, ye a leesi a nii 7a na nɔn-donno na vei chwoŋa ne tei to. Nayeiri-nyem maa wo ba wone, ye a maane we o tiini o ga boboŋa. 8O maa tɔge chwoŋa kalo na vei ka-tola sɔŋɔ kom seeni to, ye o vo o yi ko jeiga kam. 9Ko déem ye wɛ-zwora maŋa mo, ye je-gwonnu ba nii te nae. 10Kaane wom de maa yɔɔre o pi o nwoŋi se o jeeri‑o. O yɔɔre o zo ka-bworo gwaaro mo ye o laam jege o boboŋa o seiga. 11Kaane wom tiini o pepera mo ye o ba kɔre nɔɔno yi. O nam ware jeiga dedoa se o jeini da. 12O yɔɔre o kare teo kom chwei sem ni ne, de ko yaga kam ni ne mo o seigi o nii o na wó yi wolo to. 13O laam ma yɔɔre o vaŋe nɔn-doŋo konto o kukwori‑o ye o mu o ni, o daare o ta o bere‑o de baare we: 14“Yazura pɛɛre nɔna ta daare a sɔŋɔ kom ne mo. A zem nam ke a su a ni-gwonim dem mo. 15Konto ŋwaane mo a nwoŋi se a jeeri‑m. A ya yɔɔre a beeri nmo jei mo, wɛ-ywom nam nii‑m da! 16Amo kwei gare-laaro mo a ma a lware a kwoli a gadwogo kom maama. Te maa ye gare-fefale selo na nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne ye se nyenyero ye dwi dwi to. 17A ta ma kwei talwoŋ-ywoŋa dwi dwi a zezage a yage ko maama ne, se na ye Mura, de Alwo, de Kinamon to mo 18Laam nam ba se dé zo dé lare dé yi dé tete se tega laam ba ka poore. Dé yɔɔre dé lage dé di dé swono kom ywoni mo. 19Amo baro beeri o kɛ yiga yiga mo. O tera sɔŋɔ ne. 20O nam kwei sabu na daga mo o ke o yera ne o ja o kɛ. Chana kam wó peere ka ti mo se o laam jwoori sɔŋɔ.”
21Ka-tola kam tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo o ja nɔn-doŋo kom o ywori. O nam yɔɔre o kwei ni-som mo o soge‑o o wane. 22Bedwe baŋa ne mo o pɛ o kwaga o pu, ne na-bala mo ba jege ba vei se ba go to. O ta nye de woŋa kalo kalanchogo na jaane 23ye ko laam daare se che-tɛɛre moore o bochɔŋɔ ne to mo. Ne zuŋa kalo na zo kalanchogo wone to, o nam yeiri we o seene o to cham wone se o ga o ŋwea.
24Konto ŋwaane amo bia bam, nam cheigi-na a taane dem. Ke-na á zwa keo se á ke a bera yam á boboŋa ne. 25Yé pa-na kaane wom konto dwoŋi chwoŋa se o soge abam o wane. Nam yé sɛ-na se o ja abam o ywori á chwoŋa kam ne. 26O pɛ baara dedɛ mo to tega ne, pa se nɔn-kɔgɔ dole ba ŋwea ba yage. 27Balo na zo o sɔŋɔ kom ne to laam to chwo-fara kalo na vei churu to ne. Chwoŋa kam konto wó ba ka guri de toone mo.

english_text:
In Praise of Wisdom
1 With great understanding,
Wisdom is calling out
2as she stands at the crossroads
and on every hill.
3She stands by the city gate
where everyone enters the city,
and she shouts:
4“I am calling out
to each one of you!
5Good sense and sound judgment
can be yours.
6Listen, because what I say
is worthwhile and right.
7I always speak the truth
and refuse to tell a lie.
8Every word I speak is honest,
not one is misleading
or deceptive.
9“If you have understanding,
you will see that my words
are just what you need.
10Let instruction and knowledge
mean more to you than silver
or the finest gold.
11 Wisdom is worth much more
than precious jewels
or anything else you desire.”
Wisdom Speaks
12I am Wisdom—Common Sense
is my closest friend;
I possess knowledge
and sound judgment.
13If you respect the Lord,
you will hate evil.
I hate pride and conceit
and deceitful lies.
14I am strong, and I offer
sensible advice
and sound judgment.
15By my power kings govern,
and rulers make laws
that are fair.
16Every honest leader rules
with help from me.
17I love everyone who loves me,
and I will be found by all
who honestly search.
18I can make you rich and famous,
important and successful.
19What you receive from me
is more valuable
than even the finest gold
or the purest silver.
20I always do what is right,
21and I give great riches
to everyone who loves me.
22 From the beginning,
I was with the Lord.
I was there before he began
23to create the earth.
At the very first,
the Lord gave life to me.
24When I was born,
there were no oceans
or springs of water.
25My birth was before
mountains were formed
or hills were put in place.
26It happened long before God
had made the earth
or any of its fields
or even the dust.
27 I was there when the Lord
put the heavens in place
and stretched the sky
over the surface of the sea.
28I was with him when he placed
the clouds in the sky
and created the springs
that fill the ocean.
29I was there when he set
boundaries for the sea
to make it obey him,
and when he laid foundations
to support the earth.
30I was right beside the Lord,
helping him plan and build.
I made him happy each day,
and I was happy at his side.
31I was pleased with his world
and pleased with its people.
32 Pay attention, my children!
Follow my advice,
and you will be happy.
33Listen carefully
to my instructions,
and you will be wise.
34Come to my home each day
and listen to me.
You will find happiness.
35By finding me, you find life,
and the Lord will be pleased
with you.
36But if you don't find me,
you hurt only yourself,
and if you hate me,
you are in love with death.
translation_text:
Yi-poro na pae wolim delo to
1Cheigi-na! Swa chekke nye de bukɔ na tɔɔla o yaga.
Yi-poro mo zeiŋi o kwora wɛɛne
se nɔɔna ni o ŋwa.
2O yeini o di zwonnu yuu mo
o vo o zege mɛ seeni chwei sem
na lɛɛne daane to.
3O ta zege o maŋe de teo kom manchwo-nia,
mɛ seeni ba na tɔge
ba zoore ko wo to,
o tɔɔla we:
4“Amo tɔɔle a bwoi abam,
se logo baŋa nabiina maama mo ni.
5Abam balo na ye nayeiri-nyena to,
ja-na boboŋ-ŋona.
Abam nɔn-jworru tem,
ja-na yi-poro.
6Cheigi-na, se a jege wo-kura mo
se a ta.
Amo ná puri a ni,
a wó ta wonnu telo
na ye chega to mo.
7Amo ni taane yɔɔre de ye chega,
a na chuli vwa to ŋwaane.
8Amo ni-botare sem maama
yɔɔre se tɔge chwoŋa mo.
A ba jege ni-zɛ kolokolo baŋa ne.
9Yi-pore-nyena nae a bera yam we,
ya yɔɔre ya ye chekke mo.
Balo na jege yeino to maa nae we,
ya ba jege tusim.
10Pa-na a koresem dem
taa jege lonne abam tei ne,
se de dwoi lu-nyenno.
Nam kuri-na yeino
se á daare sabu-seŋa,
ne ka ná maŋe ka ye chekke tei de.
11Kokuri swa chekke jege kuri
ya dwoi kandwa-nyenno.
Woŋo kolo maama á fera na wó zo to bá maŋe de-ya.
12Amo ye swa chekke mo.
Amo dedaane boboŋ-ŋona mo
vei daane.
A maa beeri yeino
dedaane yi-poro jei
se a kwei-te a pa nɔɔna.
13Wolo ná kɔre Wɛ,
kotu lɔŋe lwarem mo.
A yɔɔre a chuli ka-bere-ka-tete,
de boyerem, de totoŋ-zɔɔna,
de ni-zɛ ni-zɛ kikia mo.
14Boboŋ-ŋona de swa chekke
wo amo tei ne mo.
A maa jege yi-poro de dam.
15Pwa tɔge amo baŋa ne mo
ba di paare.
Ko ta ye amo ŋwaane mo ba kuri
wadɛ selo na maŋe to
ba pae ba nɔɔna.
16Ko ná ye nakwa, de nɔn-yum,
de dedɛɛra balo na jege chega to,
ba maama tɔge amo ŋwaane
ba na dam.
17Balo maama na swoi amo to,
amo de swoi-ba mo.
Ko ná ye balo na seene ba yia
ba beeri amo jei to,
banto wó ba ba yi amo tei.
18Jejegero de yere-kamunu
maa wo a jeŋa ne,
se a kwei a pa nɔɔna.
A maa pae nɔɔna duna,
ye ba tɔge chwoŋa chekke.
19Nyɔɔre delo nɔɔna na wó na
amo tei ne to gare sabu-seŋa,
ka ná maŋe ka tiini ka lana tei de.
Pɛɛra yalo ba na wó jwoŋi
amo jeŋa ne to
gare lu-nyenno chekke.
20Amo veiŋa maama ye chekke.
A maa tɔge chwei selo na yɔɔre to.
21A maa kwei jejegero a pae balo
dwi maama na swoi-ne to,
pa se ba sam sui de wo-laaro.
22Se Baŋa Wɛ laam ke
wonnu maama to,
o naane amo mo yiga
o jeŋa totoŋa maama wone.
23Faŋa faŋa ye Baŋa Wɛ ta wo naane logo kom to,
o maŋe o kuri-ne boboa kam ne mo.
24Ba na loge-ne to,
de naneero tem ta tera,
de buli-yia de tera se ya taa tae.
25Ba loge-ne mo ba daare,
ye Wɛ laam chwi peero tem
de zwonnu tem te jei ne.
26Konto maama kea ye o laam mɔ
tega kam, de ka pwoli sem,
de logo baŋa kasolo kom.
27A tu a wora mo ye o kwei wɛyuu kom o ke ko jeiga ne,
ye o daare o lɔ siseini delo
na kaare naneo kom maama to.
28A déem maa wora ye o kwei kunkwonnu tem o ke wɛyuu ne,
ye o daare o fɔge buli-yia
se ya pa na su naneo kom.
29A wo o tei ne mo ye o lɔ pempala
o ma che naneo kom,
se ko wo na-fwaaro yé ve o ni
ba gaale mɛ o na pɛ-ba to.
O ta na fɔge o chwi tega kam kuri to mo a wora.
30A yɔɔre a wo o tei ne mo
a woli‑o ne gɔgɔ tei.
O déem di ywoni amo ŋwaane mo,
ye a de wo pwoli o yiga ne.
31A maa jege wopwolo
de logo kolo o na ke to,
de ko nɔn-bia bam.
32Amo bia bam, cheigi-na a taane dem.
Balo na sɛ ba tɔge amo nia yam to
mo jege yu-ywoŋo.
33Cheigi-na a bera yam se á ja swa.
Yé dole-ya á yage.
34Wolo ná cheigi amo taane,
kotu jege yu-ywoŋo.
Dɛ maama wone,
o swoi se o taa tui a sɔŋɔ mo,
ye o cheiga se a ŋɔɔne ded‑o.
35Wolo maama ná tu o lɔre amo,
kotu nɛ ŋwea mo.
O nam ta wó na zaane
Baŋa Wɛ tei ne.
36Ko daare, wolo maama na gɛ amo to
beeri yaara mo o pa o tete.
Balo na chuli amo to
lage ba tete toone mo.”

english_text:
Wisdom Gives a Feast
1Wisdom has built her house
with its seven columns.
2She has prepared the meat
and set out the wine.
Her feast is ready.
3She has sent her servant women
to announce her invitation
from the highest hills:
4“Everyone who is ignorant
or foolish is invited!
5All of you are welcome
to my meat and wine.
6If you want to live,
give up your foolishness
and let understanding
guide your steps.”
True Wisdom
7Correct a worthless bragger,
and all you will get
are insults and injuries.
8Any bragger you correct
will only hate you.
But if you correct someone
who has common sense,
you will be loved.
9If you have good sense,
instruction will help you
to have even better sense.
And if you live right,
education will help you
to know even more.
10 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of wisdom.
To have understanding,
you must know the Holy God.
11I am Wisdom. If you follow me,
you will live a long time.
12Good sense is good for you,
but if you brag,
you hurt yourself.
A Foolish Invitation
13Stupidity is reckless,
senseless, and foolish.
14She sits in front of her house
and on the highest hills
in the town.
15She shouts to everyone
who passes by,
16“If you are stupid,
come on inside!”
And to every fool she says,
17“Stolen water tastes best,
and the food you eat in secret
tastes best of all.”
18None who listen to Stupidity
understand that her guests
are as good as dead.
translation_text:
Swa de jworim taane
1Swa chekke mo lɔge o sɔŋɔ.
O ma chwi ywoa yarepɛ
o teili-ko o zege.
2O go vara mo se o ke wodi-fɔrɔ,
ye o daare o ke sa-sona o woli da.
O ma ti ko maama yiga.
3O laam ma toŋe o ka-nyaana
se ba kwei o kwora ba vo
ba zege teo kom zwonnu yuu ne
ba taa tɔɔla ba yaga.
4O maa tɛ de balo na gɛ boboŋa to
o we:
“Abam nayeiri-nyena bam,
ba-na á zo amo sɔŋɔ ywo!
5Ba á di-na wodiu kolo a na ke
a zege abam,
de sana balo a na ke á ŋwaane to.
6Yage-na jworim kikia,
se á wó ni ŋwea ywoni.
Nam tɔge-na yi-poro chwoŋa kam.”
7Nmo ná kwaane se n de
nɔn-lwɛɛno chwoŋa ne,
o wó jwoori o twe‑m.
N ta ná bwɛ puseŋ-nyeno,
o de wó pa ko zo n yera mo.
8Yé zaŋe n bwɛ nɔn-lwɛɛno,
se o wó taa chuli‑m ko ŋwaane.
Nmo nam ná bwɛ yi-pore-nyem,
o wó taa swoi‑m ko ŋwaane.
9Nmo ná woli boboŋa tu,
o laam wó na swa o woli da.
N ná bere nɔn-ŋom,
o wó fɔge o lɔre wonnu.
10Nabiina na kɔre Baŋa Wɛ mɛ to,
yi-poro de puli dáane mo.
Nmo ná me de
Wo-pwoŋo Tu Wɛ wom,
nmo wó lɔre wonnu.
11N ná jege swa chekke,
n laam wó na momwɛ-dɛɛre mo.
N bena yam wó gaale logo baŋa ne.
12Yi-pore-nyem swa yam jaane
nyɔɔre mo ya tui ya pa‑o.
Wolo nam ná ye nɔn-lwɛɛno,
kotu yerane mo wó yaare
ko ŋwaane.
13Ajworo yɔɔre o ye ka-pwogo mo.
O maa ba jege boboŋa
ye o ye pere-pere.
14O jei o sɔŋɔ manchwo-ni dem seeni mo
de teo kom zwonnu yuu ne.
15O maa tɔɔle o yaga o bwoi
balo na wo chwoŋa ne
ba maa kɛa to.
16O maa tɛ de balo na gɛ boboŋa to
o we:
“Abam balo maama
na ye nayeiri-nyena to
ba-na á zo amo sɔŋɔ ywo!
17Nɔn-gaa lɔɔ wo na bam
tiini ba ywomma.
Wodiu kolo n na wó seigi n di to
de dim ywoni mo dwoi!”
18Nayeiri-nyena nam yeiri we
balo maama na lɛɛne ba zo
Ajworo sɔŋɔ to jege se ba te mo.
Churu nam yɔɔre ko su
de o sɔŋɔ veira mo.

english_text:
Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some proverbs
of Solomon:
Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
make them sad.
2What you gain by doing evil
won't help you at all.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
3If you obey the Lord,
you won't go hungry;
if you are wicked,
God won't let you have
what you want.
4Laziness leads to poverty;
