hard work makes you rich.
5At harvest season
it's smart to work hard,
but stupid to sleep.
6Everyone praises good people,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
7Good people are remembered
long after they are gone,
but the wicked
are soon forgotten.
8If you have good sense,
you will listen and obey;
if all you do is talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
9You will be safe,
if you always do right,
but you will get caught,
if you are dishonest.
10Deceit causes trouble,
and foolish talk
will bring you to ruin.
11The words of good people
are a source of life,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
12 Hatred stirs up trouble;
love overlooks the wrongs
that others do.
13If you have good sense,
it will show when you speak.
But if you are stupid,
you will be beaten
with a stick.
14If you have good sense,
you will learn all you can,
but foolish talk
will soon destroy you.
15Great wealth can be a fortress,
but poverty
is no protection at all.
16If you live right,
the reward is a good life;
if you are evil,
all you have is sin.
17Accept correction,
and you will find life;
reject correction,
and you will miss the road.
18You can hide your hatred
by telling lies,
but you are a fool
to spread lies.
19You will say the wrong thing
if you talk too much—
so be sensible and watch
what you say.
20The words of a good person
are like pure silver,
but the thoughts
of an evil person
are almost worthless.
21Many are helped
by useful instruction,
but fools are killed
by their own stupidity.
22When the Lord blesses you
with riches,
you have nothing to regret.
23Fools enjoy doing wrong,
but anyone with good sense
enjoys acting wisely.
24What evil people dread most
will happen to them,
but good people will get
what they want most.
25Those crooks will disappear
when a storm strikes,
but God will keep safe
all who obey him.
26Having a lazy person on the job
is like a mouth full of vinegar
or smoke in your eyes.
27If you respect the Lord,
you will live longer;
if you keep doing wrong,
your life will be cut short.
28If you obey the Lord,
you will be happy,
but there is no future
for the wicked.
29The Lord protects everyone
who lives right,
but he destroys anyone
who does wrong.
30Good people will stand firm,
but the wicked will disappear
from the land.
31Honest people speak sensibly,
but deceitful liars
will be silenced.
32If you obey the Lord,
you will always know
the right thing to say.
But no one will trust you
if you tell lies.
translation_text:
Pɛ Solomon memaŋa
1Pɛ Solomon memaŋa yam mo tento:
Bu wolo na jege boboŋ-laaro to
pae o kwo wo pwola.
Se ko ná ye bu-jworo,
wonto pae se o nu wo chɔge mo.
2Nɔɔno ná dɛ lwarem baŋa o ma o na jejegero,
o bá na nyɔɔre te baŋa ne.
Chwo-laaro tɔgem nam wó jwoŋi nɔɔno toone jeŋa ne.
3 Baŋa Wɛ bá sɛ se kana ja nɔn-ŋona.
Ko daare ko ná ye puseŋ-nyena,
Wɛ wó che-ba de kolo maama ba fera na zoore to.
4Jawɔrɔ jaane yiniga mo ko tui ko pae nɔɔna.
Ko daare jawale-nyem jeŋa yi o ni mo.
5Wolo na nwoŋi o ja faao o zo diga ko maŋa ne to cho o tete mo.
Wolo nam na dɔ faao ni ne to jaane chaveera yerane mo o ba.
6Wɛ swolim wó taa wo nɔn-ŋona yuni ne.
Puseŋ-nyeno ni taane nam pae nankɔɔre zaŋe mo.
7Nmo ná guli nɔn-ŋom gula,
ko ke‑m ywoni mo.
Ko daare puseŋ-nyeno yere wó saare mo.
8Boboŋa tu jwoŋi bera mo.
Wolo na ŋɔɔne yɔɔ yerane to wó na chɔgem.
9Wolo ná vei chega chwoŋa ne,
kotu nɛ jaane tega mo.
Ko daare pipiri-nyena wó seeri ba to.
10Wolo ná kweele chega,
kotu beeri jara mo.
Wolo na ŋɔɔne yɔɔ yerane to wó na chɔgem.
11Nɔn-ŋom ni taane nye de buli-yi
delo na na pae ŋwea to mo.
Puseŋ-nyeno ni taane nam pae nankɔɔre zaŋe mo.
12Dono wiiri kantɔgɔ mo.
Swono maa kwoli wɛleera dwi maama.
13Yi-pore-nyem ni taane bere swa chekke.
Agɛboŋa nam maŋe se o na waarem mo.
14Swa tu mo tiŋi yeino o yuu ne.
Nɔn-jworo ŋɔŋa nam jaane lɛɛro mo ka tui.
15Nadum jejegero tem wae te che‑o de cham.
Yini-gwia nam wó chɔge yiniga tiina.
16Nɔn-ŋona nyɔɔre ye ŋwea chekke.
Puseŋ-nyena ŋweero nam wó taa ye waarem mo
ba wɛleera ŋwaane.
17Wolo maama ná sɛ bera,
kotu wo ŋwea chwoŋa ne mo o via.
Wolo nam ná ve koresem,
kotu wó pa se o dwonna de tusi.
18N ná mɔne de nɔɔno ye n wo ba ŋwae,
n ye vwa-fɔro mo.
N ná ye bebare nyem, n ye nɔn-jworo mo.
19Ta-fara jaane tusim mo ya tui.
Swa tu wó pu o ni mo chemm.
20Nɔn-ŋom ni taane jege nyɔɔre mo,
ne lu-nyenno to.
Puseŋ-nyem boboŋa maa ye weero yerane.
21Nɔn-ŋona bera jege nyɔɔre
ya pae nɔɔna dedɛ.
Ko daare jworru jworim dem mo jege-ba de goe.
22 Baŋa Wɛ swolim mo pae ko gare nɔɔno yera ne.
Kolokolo bá baare kotu kwaga.
23Nɔn-jworo mae lwarem kikia o jiri kwɛɛra mo.
Boboŋa tu wo nam pwoli keim-laaro ŋwaane.
24Puseŋ-nyena na duri kolo to mo wó yi-ba.
Ko daare nɔn-ŋona wó na ba na beeri kolo to mo.
25Vo-dɛɔ ná zaŋe, puseŋ-nyena ba jege zega jei.
Ko nam ná ye nɔn-ŋona,
banto fɔge ba zege mo cheppe taa wuu.
26Yé kwei n totoŋa n ke jawɔre-nyem jeŋa ne.
Ko wó taa ye ne mia ná ŋaare yeila,
naa nyoa na wiiri yia tei to mo.
27Nɔɔno ná kɔre Baŋa Wɛ,
kotu wó na momwɛ-dɛɛre.
Puseŋ-nyeno nam ba yi o dɛ.
28Nɔn-ŋona teena guri de ywoni mo.
Ko daare puseŋ-nyena teena wó chɔge lela mo.
29 Baŋa Wɛ mo pae chega tiina na dalem jei.
O ta maa pae puseŋ-nyena na chɔgem.
30Nɔn-ŋona kuri ba gɔe.
Puseŋ-nyena nam bá dáane tega kam baŋa ne.
31Nɔn-ŋom ni taane bere swa mo.
Vwa-fɔro ni nam maŋe se ba pu-de mo.
32Nɔn-laaro ni taane ywomma puga ne.
Ko daare ye puseŋ-nyena mo ŋɔɔne ta-yɔɔro yerane.

english_text:
Watch What You Say and Do
1The Lord hates anyone
who cheats,
but he likes everyone
who is honest.
2Too much pride
can put you to shame.
It's wiser to be humble.
3If you do the right thing,
honesty will be your guide.
But if you are crooked,
you will be trapped
by your own dishonesty.
4When God is angry,
money won't help you.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
5If you are truly good,
you will do right;
if you are wicked,
you will be destroyed
by your own sin.
6Honesty can keep you safe,
but if you can't be trusted,
you trap yourself.
7When the wicked die,
their hopes die with them.
8Trouble goes right past
the Lord's people
and strikes the wicked.
9Dishonest people use gossip
to destroy their neighbors;
good people are protected
by their own good sense.
10When honest people prosper
and the wicked disappear,
the whole city celebrates.
11Good people bring prosperity
to their city,
but deceitful liars
can destroy a city.
12It's stupid to say bad things
about your neighbors.
If you are sensible,
you will keep quiet.
13A gossip tells everything,
but a true friend
will keep a secret.
14 A city without wise leaders
will end up in ruin;
a city with many wise leaders
will be kept safe.
15It's a dangerous thing
to guarantee payment
for someone's debts.
Don't do it!
16A gracious woman
will be respected,
but a ruthless man
will only get rich.
17Kindness is rewarded—
but if you are cruel,
you hurt yourself.
18Meanness gets you nowhere,
but goodness is rewarded.
19Always do the right thing,
and you will live;
keep on doing wrong,
and you will die.
20The Lord hates sneaky people,
but he likes everyone
who lives right.
21You can be sure of this:
All crooks will be punished,
but God's people won't.
22A beautiful woman
who acts foolishly
is like a gold ring
on the snout of a pig.
23Good people want what is best,
but troublemakers
hope to stir up trouble.
24Sometimes you can become rich
by being generous
or poor by being greedy.
25Generosity will be rewarded:
Give a cup of water,
and you will receive
a cup of water in return.
26Charge too much for grain,
and you will be cursed;
sell it at a fair price,
and you will be praised.
27Try hard to do right,
and you will win friends;
go looking for trouble,
and you will find it.
28Trust in your wealth,
and you will be a failure,
but God's people will prosper
like healthy plants.
29Fools who cause trouble
in the family
won't inherit a thing.
They will end up as slaves
of someone with good sense.
30Live right, and you will eat
from the life-giving tree.
And if you act wisely,
others will follow.
31 If good people are rewarded
here on this earth,
all who are cruel and mean
will surely be punished.
translation_text:
1 Baŋa Wɛ vae kampin-nyena ni taane.
Ko daare balo na jege bwɛ chekke ba toŋe to mo pwoli o wo.
2Bere n tete de chaveera vei daane mo,
ne tu-n-tete de yi-poro na ye tei to.
3Nɔn-ŋom chega kam yere‑o
pa o ŋwea lana mo.
Nɔn-ŋolo vwa yam maa pipiri ya jaane‑o.
4Wɛ ná wora o waare‑m,
n jejegero daa ba jege kuri.
N nɔn-ŋonne nam wó che‑m de toone.
5Nɔn-laaro nɔn-ŋonne dem tiŋi chwoŋa jaja mo pa ba via.
Ko daare puseŋ-nyena puseŋa kam pae ba saare ba toe mo.
6Chega tiina nɔn-ŋonne dem mo jwoŋi-ba de yaga.
Nɔn-ŋollo fera maa jaane-ba.
7Puseŋ-nyem ná tega, o teena yam maama dɛ ded‑o mo ya te.
O boboŋa yalo maama o na jege to daa bá toŋe.
8Nɔn-ŋona wó lu cham wone,
se de jwoori de to puseŋ-nyena baŋa ne.
9Wɛ-lwɛɛno yeini o chɔge o dwonna de ni-chworu mo.
Nɔn-ŋona nam mae yeino mo ba jwoŋi ba tete.
10Nɔn-ŋona chwoŋa ná pore,
ba teo kom nɔɔna jege ywoni mo ba di.
Puseŋ-nyena nam ná tu ba na chɔgem,
nɔɔna wó taa mɔne ba chaka mo.
11Nɔn-laaro ná ke zaane ba ke ba teo kom yuu ne,
teo kom konto wó na yere mo.
Ko daare puseŋ-nyena wó ma ba ni taane mo
ba chɔge ba teo kom.
12Wolo maama ná gwooni o dwoŋi,
kotu boboŋa mo muri.
Boboŋa tu wó pu o ni mo chemm.
13Wolo na kare o ba bebara to
yeini o bere wo-siseigiru jaja mo.
Nɔn-yero nam mo wó pu o ni,
se ya yé nwoŋi pwooni.
14Nakwa ná tera se ba woli pɛ de kwea,
o teo kom bá zege.
Nakwa dedɛ nam ná wora,
teo kom wó ke lam.
15Wolo ná sɛ se o zege daare nɔn-veiru jene ŋwaane,
kotu wó na cham.
Kotu nam ná ve se o zege daare dem,
ko wó che‑o cham wone.
16Ka-yero na nɛ yere delo to
gare nankɔ-nyena na nae jejegero telo to.
17Ŋwaŋa tu kikia yam kwɛ o tete mo.
Ko daare keim-chɛ-nyeno jaane yaara mo
o tui o tete baŋa.
18Puseŋ-nyeno ŋweero nye de lunluŋu mo te pa‑o.
Wolo nam na toŋe chega to wó yɔɔre o na o totoŋa yam nyɔɔre.
19Wolo ná seene o yia de nɔn-ŋonne totoŋa,
kotu wó ni ŋwea ywoni.
Wolo maa na seene yia de lwarem kikia to wó te mo.
20 Baŋa Wɛ chuli balo boboŋa na ywori to mo.
Ko nam ná ye balo na yɔɔre ba tɔge chwoŋa to,
ba kikia yam su o yi mo.
21Taane dento bá kwane:
Nankɔ-nyena yɔɔre ba lage ba na waarem mo.
Ko nam ná ye nɔn-ŋona dwi dem,
ba wó taa tei ba tete.
22Kaane ná lana ye o ye ka-pwogo,
ko nye de sabu-seŋa kwane na leigi teiri momwɛ ne to mo.
23Nɔn-ŋona fera na tɔge wonnu telo to wó guri lanyerane mo.
Puseŋ-nyena teena nam guri de ban-zɔŋɔ mo.
24Wo-ywoŋo tu pae mo ye o jwoori o nae o woli da.
Wo-chɛ-nyem maa ve pɛɛre
ye o ba o guri de yiniga.
25Wo-ywoŋo tu wó na zaane nɔɔna tei ne.
Wolo na twei na o pa nɔɔna to,
ba wó twei na ba pa o de.
26Nɔɔna sɔɔle lwarem ba pae balo na jege wodiiru ba seiga to mo.
Ba maa tei balo na pae te nwoŋa se ba yeigi-te to.
27Nmo ná toŋe n totoŋa de boboŋ-ŋona,
nɔɔna wó pu n kwaga.
Nmo nam ná kare n beeri lwarem jei, n wó na-de.
28Wolo maama teena ná tigi o jejegero wone,
kotu wó to mo,
se nɔn-ŋom yera zura mo,
ne vɔ-lɛɔ na kwi tio yera ne tei to.
29Wolo ná jaane daanem o tui
o diga tiina baŋa,
kotu bá fɔge o ni o diga kam ywoni.
Nɔn-jworo maa wó taa toŋe
o pae swa tu.
30Nɔn-ŋom nye de tio kolo na pae nɔɔna ŋwea to mo.
Wolo maa na jwoŋi o dwonna o yage to mo seene o jege swa.
31Nɔn-ŋona ná lage ba na ba totoŋa nyɔɔre tega baŋa ne,
se wɛle-keira laam ná niga?

english_text:
You Can't Hide behind Evil
1 To accept correction is wise,
to reject it is stupid.
2The Lord likes everyone
who lives right,
but he punishes everyone
who makes evil plans.
3Sin cannot offer security!
But if you live right,
you will be as secure
as a tree with deep roots.
4A helpful wife is a jewel
for her husband,
but a shameless wife
will make his bones rot.
5Good people have kind thoughts,
but you should never trust
the advice of someone evil.
6Bad advice is a deadly trap,
but good advice
is like a shield.
7Once the wicked are defeated,
they are gone forever,
but no one who obeys God
will ever be thrown down.
8Good sense is worthy of praise,
but stupidity is a curse.
9It's better to be ordinary
and have only one servant
than to think you are somebody
and starve to death.
10Good people are kind
to their animals,
but a mean person is cruel.
11Hard working farmers have more
than enough food;
daydreamers are nothing more
than stupid fools.
12An evil person tries to hide
behind evil;
good people are like trees
with deep roots.
13We trap ourselves
by telling lies,
but we stay out of trouble
by living right.
14We are rewarded or punished
for what we say and do.
15Fools think they know
what is best,
but a sensible person
listens to advice.
16Losing your temper is foolish;
ignoring an insult is smart.
17An honest person
tells the truth in court,
but a dishonest person
tells nothing but lies.
18Sharp words cut like a sword,
but words of wisdom heal.
19Truth will last forever;
lies are soon found out.
20An evil mind is deceitful,
but gentle thoughts
bring happiness.
21Good people never have trouble,
but troublemakers
have more than enough.
22The Lord hates every liar,
but he is the friend of all
who can be trusted.
23Be sensible and don't tell
everything you know—
only fools spread
foolishness everywhere.
24Work hard, and you
will be a leader;
be lazy, and you
will end up a slave.
25Worry is a heavy burden,
but a kind word
always brings cheer.
26You are better off to do right,
than to lose your way
by doing wrong.
27Anyone too lazy to cook
will starve,
but a hard worker
is a valuable treasure.
28Living right is a pathway
that leads to life
and away from death.
translation_text:
1Wolo na sɛ se ba de‑o chwoŋa ne to lɔre lɔra chekke.
Ko daare wolo na chuli bwɛa to boboŋa muri mo.
2 Baŋa Wɛ zaane wo nɔn-ŋona yuu ne mo,
se ko ná ye balo na boŋe lwarem ba pa ba dwonna to,
Wɛ wó vane ba bora mo.

7Wɛ yeini o vuvugi puseŋ-nyena mo o de tega ne

Nɔn-ŋom sɔŋɔ nam zege mo cheppe.
8Yi-pore-nyem ye ba tei‑o mo o boboŋa ŋwaane.

16Nɔn-jworo mo gare o bere o ban-lom jaja.

18N ná wo boŋe n yi, n wó ta taane pa de daane n dwoŋi,

20Wolo na boŋe lwarem o pa o dwoŋi to bochare su de gana.

24Jawale-nyem jei paare baŋa ne mo.

25Boboŋ-fara ye zele-dunni mo ya daane nɔɔna.

26Nɔn-ŋom yeini o woli o badwoŋi mo
se o to chwoŋa ne.
Puseŋ-nyena maa na kwei chwoŋa kalo to jaane-ba ka jia.
27Jawɔre-nyem ba wɔa nɔna yalo o na jaane to.
Jawale-nyem wó di o su o daare o yeigi o nɔna mo.
28N kikia na tɔge chwoŋa,
n wó na ŋwea chekke.

english_text:
Wise Friends Make You Wise
1Children with good sense
accept correction
from their parents,
but stubborn children
ignore it completely.
2You will be well rewarded
for saying something kind,
but all some people think about
is how to be cruel and mean.
3 Keep what you know to yourself,
and you will be safe;
talk too much,
and you are done for.
4No matter how much you want,
laziness won't help a bit,
but hard work will reward you
with more than enough.
5A good person hates deceit,
but those who are evil
cause shame and disgrace.
6Live right, and you are safe!
But sin will destroy you.
7Some who have nothing
may pretend to be rich,
and some who have everything
may pretend to be poor.
8The rich may have
to pay a ransom,
but the poor don't have
that problem.
9The lamp of a good person
keeps on shining;
the lamp of an evil person
soon goes out.
10Too much pride causes trouble.
Be sensible and take advice.
11Money wrongly gained
will disappear bit by bit;
money earned little by little
will grow and grow.
12Not getting what you want
can break your heart,
but a wish that comes true
is a life-giving tree.
13If you reject God's teaching,
you will pay the price;
if you obey his commands,
you will be rewarded.
14Sensible instruction
is a life-giving fountain
that helps you escape
all deadly traps.
15Sound judgment is praised,
but people without good sense
are on the way to disaster.
16If you have good sense,
you will act sensibly,
but fools act like fools.
17Whoever delivers your message
can make things better
or worse for you.
18All who refuse correction
will be poor and disgraced;
all who accept correction
will be praised.
19It's a good feeling
to get what you want,
but only a stupid fool
hates to turn from evil.
20 Wise friends make you wise,
but you hurt yourself
by going around with fools.
21You are in for trouble
if you sin,
but you will be rewarded
if you live right.
22If you obey God,
you will have something
to leave your grandchildren.
If you don't obey God,
those who live right
will get what you leave.
23Even when the land of the poor
produces good crops,
they get cheated
out of what they grow.
24If you love your children,
you will correct them;
if you don't love them,
you won't correct them.
25If you live right,
you will have plenty to eat;
if you don't live right,
you will go away empty.

2Nɔɔna wó taa di ba sui ba ni taane ŋwaane mo.
Nɔn-ŋollo nam yɔɔre ba beeri nankɔɔre jei mo.
3N ná boŋe ye n tɛ taane,
n ŋwea wó dáane.
N nam ná kare n yaga,
chɔgem wó ba n baŋa mo.

Ko daare wolo ná chɛ de totoŋa,
o wó taa di o sui mo.
5Nɔn-ŋona chuli vwa mo.
Puseŋ-nyena nam swoi chaveera kikia mo.
6Chega tu totoŋ-ŋona jege‑o ya kwoli mo.
Puseŋ-nyena wɛleera yam maa chɔge-ba.

ye ba ba yi ba teiŋa jɔgɔ.

11Nmo ná lɔgere se n na sabu,
ko wó jei lela n jea ne.

n beeri-ko fenfee,
ko wó puli ko pa‑m.
12N ná ware n teena yam n yi,
ko bwori nɛ.
Ko daare n boboŋa yam ná toŋe ya pa‑m,
wopwolo gaale mo.

17Wolo n na toŋe to ná ba jege chega,

18Wolo maama ná ve se o jwoŋi koresem,
yiniga de chaveera wó ja kotu.
Wolo nam na sɛ bera to wó na zula.
19Nabiinu ná ke o su o fera, ko ywomma ko pa‑o mo.
Jworru nam ware se ba yage wɛleera kikia.
20Wolo na me de swa tiina to de wó ja swa mo.
Ko nam ná ye wolo na tɔge de jworru to,
ko wó tiini ko zo kotu yera mo.
21Cham zeili wɛle-keiru mo se de ja.
Ko nam ná ye nɔn-ŋom,
o nyɔɔre ye wo-laaro mo o wó na.
22Nɔn-laao wó daare jejegero se o bia leini ba taa di.
Wɛle-keiru maa lae o jejegero o tiŋa,
se te ba te kweeli nɔn-ŋona jeŋa ne.
23Wodiiru ya ba jege totoŋe yiniga tu kara ne.
Chega nam jei pa ba vere-te ba daare‑o.
24Wolo na nii o bu de yi to ba lage‑o.
N ná swoi n bu,
n wó korese‑o mo se o da chwoŋa.
25Nɔn-ŋona di ba sui ba pwi.
Ko daare puseŋ-nyena vei de kan-koro mo.

english_text:
Wisdom Makes Good Sense
1A woman's family
is held together
by her wisdom,
but it can be destroyed
by her foolishness.
2By living right, you show
that you respect the Lord;
by being deceitful, you show
that you despise him.
3Proud fools are punished
for their stupid talk,
but sensible talk
can save your life.
4Without the help of an ox
there can be no crop,
but with a strong ox
a big crop is possible.
5An honest witness
tells the truth;
a dishonest witness
tells nothing but lies.
6Make fun of wisdom,
and you will never find it.
But if you have understanding,
knowledge comes easily.
7Stay away from fools,
or you won't learn a thing.
8Wise people have enough sense
to find their way,
but stupid fools get lost.
9Fools don't care
if they are wrong,
but God is pleased
when people do right.
10No one else can really know
how sad or happy you are.
11The tent of a good person
stands longer than the house
of someone evil.
12 You may think you are
on the right road
and still end up dead.
13Sorrow may hide
behind laughter,
and happiness may end
in sorrow.
14You harvest what you plant,
whether good or bad.
15Don't be stupid
and believe all you hear;
be smart and know
where you are headed.
16Only a stupid fool
is never cautious—
so be extra careful
and stay out of trouble.
17Fools have quick tempers,
and no one likes you
if you can't be trusted.
18Stupidity leads to foolishness;
be smart and learn.
19The wicked will come crawling
to those who obey God.
20You have no friends
if you are poor,
but you have lots of friends
if you are rich.
21It's wrong to hate others,
but God blesses everyone
who is kind to the poor.
22It's a mistake
to make evil plans,
but you will have loyal friends
if you want to do right.
23Hard work is worthwhile,
but empty talk
will make you poor.
24Wisdom can make you rich,
but foolishness leads
to more foolishness.
25An honest witness
can save your life,
but liars can't be trusted.
26If you respect the Lord,
you and your children
have a strong fortress
27and a life-giving fountain
that keeps you safe
from deadly traps.
28Rulers of powerful nations
are held in honor;
rulers of weak nations
are nothing at all.
29It's smart to be patient,
but it's stupid
to lose your temper.
30It's healthy to be content,
but envy can eat you up.
31If you mistreat the poor,
you insult your Creator;
if you are kind to them,
you show him respect.
32In times of trouble
the wicked are destroyed,
but even at death
the innocent have faith.
33Wisdom is found in the minds
of people with good sense,
but fools don't know it.
34Doing right brings honor
to a nation,
but sin brings disgrace.
35Kings reward servants
who act wisely,
but they punish those
who act foolishly.
translation_text:
1Ka-yero kale o diga o ke da mo.
Ka-pwogo maa jage-ka o yaga.
2Chega tu kikia bere we
o kɔre Baŋa Wɛ lanyerane.
Ko daare nɔn-ŋolo kikia bere we
o yiga tera de Wɛ.
3Nɔn-jworo ni taane mo beeri waarem de pa‑o.
Yi-pore-nyem ni botare nam mo jwoŋi‑o se yaga.
4N ná ba jege nabɛ-vala se n ma n toŋe,
n tula wó ji tuli-kora mo.
N nabɛ nam ná toŋe de dam,
n wodiu wó gaale.
5Wolo na pae chega maana to ba fɔ vwa.
Wolo na fɔe vwa taane dim baŋa ne to
nam yɔɔre o gaane vwa mo o tiŋa.
6Nɔn-lwɛɛno ná beeri yi-poro jei,
o bá na-ko.
Ko daare boboŋa tu ni wonnu kuri mɔle mɔle mo.
7Pwɛ n tete de nɔn-jworo,
kokuri, n bá‑n zamese kolokolo o tei ne.
8Boboŋa tu yeino pa o boŋe o yi mo ye o ke keim.
Nɔn-jworo jworim dem maa jege‑o de gana.
9Nɔn-jworru ba pae wɛleera saarem jege kuri.
Wɛ zaane nam wo nɔn-ŋona yuu ne mo.
10Choa tu mo yei ka peiga.
Nɔn-gaa ware se o lɔre n cham de n ywoni.
11Puseŋ-nyena sam wó ji di-dwonnu.
Nɔn-ŋona di sem nam wó ke lanyerane mo.
12Nmo wae n boŋe we n na vei chwoŋa kalo ne to lana.
Ka nam wae ka tu ka guri de toone.
13Nɔɔna wae ba mɔna ye ba yiga nyɔne.
Ywoni dim nam wae de guri de wo-chechɔgɔ.
14Balo boboŋa na ywori to wó na ba totoŋa ŋweero.
Nɔn-ŋona de maa wó na ba totoŋa nyɔɔre.
15Nayeiri-nyem sɛ kolo maama na to o zwa ne to mo.
Ko daare boboŋa tu jeeli kolo o na jege o ke to mo.
16Swa tu zuri o yera mo se o lɔŋe lɛɛro.
Nɔn-jworo nam lɔgere mo ye o kare o toŋe yɔɔ.
17Ban-lom tu swoi se o taa toŋe jworim mo.
Ba maa chuli wolo na ke swa
de o dwonna to.
18Wolo boboŋa na muri to vei o kweeli de jworim mo.
Ko nam ná ye swa tu,
o na lɔre kolo to mo wó pa‑o zula.
19Nɔn-balwaaro wó chɔɔle nɔn-laaro yiga ne.
Ba wó lwoori nɔn-ŋona se ba ke-ba zaane.
20Yiniga tiina fara tete yeini ba lɔŋe-ba mo.
Ko nam ná ye naduna, ba badwonna gaale mo.
21Wolo na yeini o neese o dwonna to ke wɛleere mo.
Ko nam ná ye wolo na ke nabwona lanyerane to,
Wɛ zaane wó taa wo kotu yuu ne.
22Balo na jeeli lwarem kikia to tusi chwoŋa ba jei mo.
Balo nam na jeeli lanyerane to
bere swono kolo na ye chekke to mo.
23Totoŋ-chɛɛra dwi maama jege nyɔɔre.
Ni taane yerane nam jaane
yini-gwia mo de tui.
24Jejegero ye zula mo te pae swa tiina.
Jworru maa kare ba toŋe jworim yerane.
25Nɔɔno ná pɛ maana chekke,
wonto wó jwoŋi o dwoŋi ŋwea o yage mo.
Balo nam na fɔe vwa taane dim baŋa ne to
jege ba dwonna ba chɔga.
26Nɔɔno wolo ná kɔre Baŋa Wɛ,
kotu boboŋa wó ke dam.
O bia de wó na dalem jei.
27Nmo ná kɔre Baŋa Wɛ,
ko nye de buli-yi delo na na pae ŋwea to mo.
Ko lage ko che nmo mo se toone yé ja‑m.
28Pɛ wolo teo na jege nɔn-bia dedɛ to wó na zula lanyerane.
Pɛ wolo nɔn-kɔgɔ na muri to ba jege paare o di.
29Wolo na wae o bochare o jaane to bere we o poore mo.
Wolo na bere o ban-lom to maa bere jworim yerane.
30Nɔɔno wo ná tiga, kotu yera wó zuri.
Kazwe nam ye jaweo mo ko goe.
31Wolo ná pɛ ko zo yiniga tu yera,
kotu twe o Keiru wom mo.
Wolo nam ná ke nabwona lanyerane,
kotu zuli Wɛ mo.
32Lɛɛro ná tua, puseŋ-nyena bá wane ba zege.
Nɔn-ŋona nam wó na dalem jei,
de toone maŋa ne de.
33Swa chekke mo wo yi-pore-nyena boboŋa ne.
Ya nam ba lɔra jworru tetare ne.
34Keim-laaro na su teo kolo to,
ko yere zaŋe wɛɛne mo.
Ko daare keim-lwanno jaane chaveera mo te tui
te pae nɔɔna.
35Pɛ wo wó pwoli de o tontoŋeno wolo na toŋe de swa to.
Se ko ná ye wolo na toŋe jworim to,
o bane wó zaŋe kotu baŋa ne mo.

english_text:
The Lord Sees Everything
1A kind answer
soothes angry feelings,
but harsh words
stir them up.
2Words of wisdom
come from the wise,
but fools speak foolishness.
3The Lord sees everything,
whether good or bad.
4Kind words are good medicine,
but deceitful words
can really hurt.
5Don't be a fool
and disobey your parents.
Be smart! Accept correction.
6Good people become wealthy,
but those who are evil
will lose what they have.
7Words of wisdom
make good sense;
the thoughts of a fool
make no sense at all.
8The Lord is disgusted
by gifts from the wicked,
but it makes him happy
when his people pray.
9The Lord is disgusted
with all who do wrong,
but he loves everyone
who does right.
10If you turn from the right way,
you will be punished;
if you refuse correction,
you will die.
11If the Lord can see everything
in the world of the dead,
he can see in our hearts.
12Those who sneer at others
don't like to be corrected,
and they won't ask help
from someone with sense.
13Happiness makes you smile;
sorrow can crush you.
14Anyone with good sense
is eager to learn more,
but fools are hungry
for foolishness.
15The poor have a hard life,
but being content is as good
as an endless feast.
16It's better to obey the Lord
and have only a little,
than to be very rich
and terribly anxious.
17A simple meal with love
is better than a feast
where there is hatred.
18Losing your temper
causes a lot of trouble,
but staying calm
settles arguments.
19A lazy person refuses
to clear a thorny path,
but everyone who does right
walks on a smooth road.
20Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
despise them.
21Stupidity brings happiness
to senseless fools,
but everyone with good sense
follows the straight path.
22Without good advice
everything goes wrong—
it takes careful planning
for things to go right.
23Giving the right answer
at the right time
makes everyone happy.
24All who are wise follow a road
that leads upward to life
and away from death.
25The Lord destroys the homes
of those who are proud,
but he protects the property
of widows.
26The Lord hates evil thoughts,
but kind words please him.
27Being greedy causes trouble
for your family,
but you protect yourself
by refusing bribes.
28Good people think
before they answer,
but the wicked speak evil
without ever thinking.
29The Lord never even hears
the prayers of the wicked,
but he answers the prayers
of all who obey him.
30A friendly smile
makes you happy,
and good news
makes you feel strong.
31Healthy correction is good,
and if you accept it,
you will be wise.
32You hurt only yourself
by rejecting instruction,
but it makes good sense
to accept it.
33Showing respect to the Lord
will make you wise,
and being humble
will bring honor to you.
translation_text:
1Nmo ná leiri taane de ni-bwom, ko gwi bane mo.
Ko daare, kare-yɔgɔ fɔge
ko wiiri-de ko ke da mo.
2Yi-pore-nyena pae yeino jege kuri mo.
Ko daare nɔn-jworo ni ná puri,
jworim yerane mo nwoŋa.
3 Baŋa Wɛ dole o yia o nii jei maama mo.
O yei puseŋ-nyena de nɔn-laaro na jege kolo ba ke to.
4Taane ná zura puga ne, ko nye de tio kolo na pae ŋwea to mo.
Ko daare, nɔn-ŋolo ni taane to nagwola mo.
5Nɔn-jworo ba jwoŋi o kwo bera.
Boboŋa tu sɛ koresem mo.
6Nɔn-ŋona sam su de jejegero mo.
Puseŋ-nyena maa lae wonnu ba tiŋi
ye cham ba de ja-ba.
7Yi-pore-nyena jege yeino ba jage mo.
Jworru nam ware konto ba ke.
8 Baŋa Wɛ chuli puseŋ-nyena na kwei pɛɛra yalo ba pa‑o to.
Ko daare o boboŋa tɔge wɛ-lworo kolo nɔn-ŋona na ke to mo.
9 Baŋa Wɛ chuli puseŋ-nyena kikia yam mo.
Ko nam ná ye balo na tɔge nɔn-ŋonne kikia to,
o swoi banto mo.
10Wolo ná ywori chega chwoŋa kam,
ba wó waare‑o mo,
Wolo de ná kɔre se ba bwɛ‑o, o wó te mo.
11Toone de churu tete ye jase mo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.
Nabiina bochara mo o laam bá taa yei na?
12Boyere nyem ba lage koresem.
O maa pwɛ o tete de swa tiina.
13Nɔɔno wo ná pwoli, ko bere o yibia ne mo.
Ko daare wolo wo na pɛ to nagwola wó te mo.
14Yi-pore-nyem beeri se o lɔre chega mo.
Nɔn-jworo nam yɔɔre o puuri jworim mo o su o puga.
15Yiniga tu ŋwea yɔɔre ka ye yaara yerane mo.
Ko nam ná ye wolo wo na pwoli to,
dɛ maama nye de kuri-fɔrɔ mo o jege o di.
16N jeŋa ná ba gara
ye n kɔre Baŋa Wɛ
gare n jejegero ná gaale
ye n wo cham wone.
17Swono na wo mɛ
ye ba di dwo-vɔɔro yerane to
gare sebaŋa ná wora
ye ba done nɔna ba sui.
18Ban-lom tu fɔge o wiiri kantɔgɔ mo o ke da.
Ban-peno tu maa zuri jara.
19Jawɔre-nyem ŋwea nye de sabare na vere kara tei to mo.
Nɔn-ŋom chwei nam ye jase mo ne chwo-fara to.
20Bu wolo na jege boboŋ-laaro to pae o kwo wo pwola mo.
Ko nam ná ye nɔn-jworo,
wonto bere o ba nege o nu.
21Wolo boboŋa na muri to jege wopwolo de jwor-kikia mo.
Boboŋa tu kikia maa tɔge chwoŋa lanyerane.
22Kwea na tere mɛ to wonnu ba tɔge chwoŋa.
Berena nam ná daga, ko kwɛ wonnu mo.
23Ta-ywom ná nwoŋi de maŋa ne chekke,
ko pae nɔɔna yɔɔre ba chake mo.
24Yi-pore-nyem kikia wó pa o na momwɛ-dɛɛre,
se ko che‑o de toone.
25 Baŋa Wɛ wó yigi boyere-nyem sɔŋɔ o de tega ne.
O maa yere kadeina tega siseini dem.
26 Baŋa Wɛ chuli puseŋ-nyena boboŋa yam mo,
se ko ná ye ta-ŋona,
o yi sui yanto mo.
27Wolo na boŋe se o duni kampina baŋa ne to
wó pa cham yi o diga tiina mo.
Ko daare wolo na chuli kalipera to wó dáane.
28Nɔn-ŋom wó sigi belei mo se o ta taane.
Puseŋ-nyeno ni nam ná puri,
lwarem taane yerane mo nwoŋa.
29 Baŋa Wɛ se o zwa de puseŋ-nyena keira.
Ko daare, o yeini o cheigi nɔn-ŋona wɛ-lworo mo.
30Nɔɔno ná bwoli o yibia o jeeri‑m,
ko pae wopwolo mo.
Ta-ŋona maa pae nɔɔna wo tiga.
31Wolo ná sɛ bera yalo na jege jwa,
kotu de swa tiina wó taa vei daane.
32N ná chuli se ba bwɛ‑m,
n jege n tete mo n ni.
Wolo maa na sɛ bera to yi wó poore.
33Nɔɔno ná kɔre Baŋa Wɛ, ko pa‑o yi-poro mo.
Ka-gwooni-ka-tete de maa tɔge zula yiga.

english_text:
The Lord Has the Final Word
1We humans make plans,
but the Lord
has the final word.
2We may think we know
what is right,
but the Lord is the judge
of our motives.
3Share your plans with the Lord,
and you will succeed.
4The Lord has a reason
for everything he does,
and he lets evil people live
only to be punished.
5The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is conceited—
you can be sure
they will be punished.
6 If we truly love God,
our sins will be forgiven;
if we show him respect,
we will keep away from sin.
7When we please the Lord,
even our enemies
make friends with us.
8 It's better to be honest
and poor
than to be dishonest
and rich.
9We make our own plans,
but the Lord decides
where we will go.
10Rulers speak with authority
and are never wrong.
11The Lord watches to see
if we are fair
or if we cheat others.
12Justice makes rulers powerful.
They should hate evil
13and like honesty and truth.
14An angry ruler
can put you to death.
So be wise!
Don't make one angry.
15When a ruler is happy
and pleased with you,
it's like refreshing rain,
and you will live.
16It's much better to be wise
and sensible
than to be rich.
17God's people avoid evil ways,
and they protect themselves
by watching where they go.
18Too much pride
will destroy you.
19You are better off
to be humble and poor
than to get rich
from what you take by force.
20If you know what you're doing,
you will prosper.
God blesses everyone
who trusts him.
21Good judgment proves
that you are wise,
and if you speak kindly,
you can teach others.
22Good sense is a fountain
that gives life,
but fools are punished
by their foolishness.
23You can persuade others
if you are wise
and speak sensibly.
24Kind words are like honey—
they cheer you up
and make you feel strong.
25 Sometimes what seems right
is really a road to death.
26The hungrier you are,
the harder you work.
27Worthless people plan trouble.
Even their words burn
like a flaming fire.
28 Gossip is no good!
It causes hard feelings
and comes between friends.
29Don't trust violent people.
They will mislead you
to do the wrong thing.
30When someone winks
or grins behind your back,
trouble is on the way.
31Gray hair is a glorious crown
worn by those
who have lived right.
32Controlling your temper
is better than being a hero
who captures a city.
33We make our own decisions,
but the Lord alone
determines what happens.
translation_text:
1Nabiina wae ba boŋe ba jaane ba na wó ke kolo jwa seeni.
Baŋa Wɛ nam mo jege ni se o ta o guri.
2Nabiina boŋe we ba kikia maama yɔɔre ya tɔge chwoŋa mo.
Baŋa Wɛ nam yeini o maŋe ba bochara mo
o lɔre ya na ye tei to.
3Ke Baŋa Wɛ yiga da
n totoŋe maama wone,
se n na boŋe n ja kolo to
toŋe ko pa‑m.
4Ko kuri mo wora ye Baŋa Wɛ ke wonnu tem maama.
Puseŋ-nyena de jege ba dɛ se o chɔge-ba.
5 Baŋa Wɛ vae balo maama na bere ba kamunim to ni taane.
Ko tigi ko nae we ba wó na ba waarem.
6Nɔɔna ná jege swono de chega o pa Wɛ,
Wɛ wó yage ba wɛleera o chɛ-ba mo.
Nɔɔna ná kɔre Baŋa Wɛ,
ko cho-ba de lwarem mo.
7Nɔɔno kikia ná tɔge de Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa,
Wɛ pae o de balo ya na ware daane to me daane mo.
8N ná ye yiniga tu
ye n tɔge chega
gare n ná ye nadum
ye n wo vwa wone.
9Nabiinu wae o jeeli o tete ne
o na wó ke kolo jwa seeni.
Baŋa Wɛ nam mo wó bere chwoŋa se o taa tɔga.
10Pɛ wó da Wɛ chega kam ŋwaane o ŋɔɔne de dam.
O ná di taane, o ni taane dem bá tusi.
11 Baŋa Wɛ lage se nɔɔna maŋe wonnu chekke mo ba pa daane.
O maa nii o nae ba na jege bwɛ selo ba maa toŋe to.
12Pwa chuli lwarem kikia.
Paare nam zega chega ŋwaane mo.
13Pɛ yi wó su balo na tɛ chega to ni taane.
O maa swoi balo na ŋɔɔne chega taane ba bere‑o to.
14Pɛ bane ná zaŋe de wolo,
kotu wó wane o te lela.
Swa tu wó pa pɛ bane dem to mo.
15Pɛ lanyerane dem ná kwoli wolo,
kotu wó na ŋwea.
O wo ná dɛ nɔɔno wolo kikia,
ko nye de doa na nene duum maŋa ne to mo.
16Nɔɔno ná jege yi-poro de yeino
gare o ná jege sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno.
17Nɔn-ŋona chwoŋa yɔɔre mo ye ba lɔŋe lwarem.
Wolo maa na yei o na-veili ni ne to wó jwoŋi o tete o yage.
18Zeiŋi-n-tete ba chɔge nɔɔno belei.
Wolo na bere o tete to wó to mo.
19Nmo ná tu n tete
ye n jei de yiniga tiina
gare n ná jei de boyere-nyena
se ba pɔɔre wonnu telo ba na vere to wone ba pa‑m.
20Wolo na ke o woŋo maama de yi-seena to vei yiga mo.
Wolo nam na ke wo-dedoa de Baŋa Wɛ to jege yu-ywoŋo.
21Wolo na wae o maase wonnu to bere we o yi poore.
Wolo taane na ywomma puga ne to,
nɔɔna wó jwoŋi o bera.
22Yi-poro nye de buli-yi delo na
na pae ŋwea to mo
balo na jege-ko to tei ne.
Ko daare jworru jworim dem mo wó waare-ba.
23Swa tu boboŋa mo pae se o ni taane jege kuri.
Nɔɔna maa cheigi ye ba sɛ-de.
24Botare-ŋona ywomma ne tooro to mo.
Se maa pae bochare-zuru de yazura.
25Nmo wae n boŋe we n na vei chwoŋa kalo ne to lana.
Ka nam wae ka tu ka guri de toone.
26Nɔɔno kana mo yigi‑o ka de totoŋ-dɛɛra wone.
O ni-wodiu ŋwaane mo o toŋa.
27Nabiin-wo-korro mo boŋe lwarem ba pae ba dwonna.
Ba ni botare tete di ne min-vogo mo tei.
28Boyere nyem swoi kantɔgɔ mo.
Bebare nyem maa jage badwoŋo.
29Nankɔ-nyem soge o dwonna mo se ba tusi.
O laam ma de-ba chwo-balɔrɔ ne.
30Wolo yibia na nyɔne kiri-kiri to boŋe lwarem boboŋa mo.
O maa ná merege o ni dem,
o zege se o toŋe cham mo.
31Yu-pwei ye nenɔŋa yipuga mo.
Nɔn-ŋona nam mo wae-se ba yi.
32Ban-peno tu gare babea.
Wolo ná wae o tete o jaana,
kotu gare wolo na wae teo maama o di to.
33Nabiina wó ta jɔrɔ mo.
Ko nam ye Baŋa Wɛ mo
wó bere kolo na wora to.

english_text:
Our Thoughts Are Tested by the Lord
1A dry crust of bread eaten
in peace and quiet
is better than a feast eaten
where everyone argues.
2A wise slave
will be placed in charge
of a no-good child,
and that slave will be given
the same inheritance
that each child receives.
3Silver and gold are tested
by flames of fire;
our thoughts are tested
by the Lord.
4Troublemakers listen
to troublemakers,
and liars listen to liars.
5By insulting the poor,
you insult your Creator.
You will be punished
if you make fun
of someone in trouble.
6Grandparents are proud
of their grandchildren,
and children should be proud
of their parents.
7It sounds strange for a fool
to talk sensibly,
but it's even worse
for a ruler to tell lies.
8A bribe works miracles
like a magic charm
that brings good luck.
9You will keep your friends
if you forgive them,
but you will lose your friends
if you keep talking about
what they did wrong.
10A sensible person
accepts correction,
but you can't beat sense
into a fool.
11Cruel people want to rebel,
and so vicious attackers
will be sent against them.
12A bear robbed of her cubs
is far less dangerous
than a stubborn fool.
13You will always have trouble
if you are mean to those
who are good to you.
14The start of an argument
is like a water leak—
so stop it before
real trouble breaks out.
15The Lord doesn't like those
who defend the guilty
or condemn the innocent.
16Why should fools have money
for an education
when they refuse to learn?
17 A friend is there to help,
in any situation,
and relatives are born
to share our troubles.
18It's stupid to guarantee
someone else's loan.
19The wicked and the proud
love trouble and keep begging
to be hurt.
20Dishonesty does you no good,
and telling lies
will get you in trouble.
21It's never pleasant
to be the parent of a fool
and have nothing but pain.
22If you are cheerful,
you feel good;
if you are sad,
you hurt all over.
23Crooks accept secret bribes
to keep justice
from being done.
24Anyone with wisdom knows
what makes good sense,
but fools can never
make up their minds.
25Foolish children bring sorrow
and pain to their parents.
26It isn't fair
to punish the innocent
and those who do right.
27It makes a lot of sense
to be a person of few words
and to stay calm.
28 Even fools seem smart
when they are quiet.
translation_text:
1Nmo ná di gole-kateiga de ni-mɔrɔ,
ko gare balo na di ba sui
ye ni-kantɔgɔ wo ba sɔŋɔ ne to.
2Kabaa yi ná poore, o wó di dam sɔŋɔ tu bu-kayaa baŋa ne.
Ba ná lage ba pɔɔre sɔŋɔ tu wom jejegero,
ba wó ga‑o ba woli sɔŋɔ kom bia wone se o na o nyem.
3Min-vogo pae ba yei lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa lam mo.
Ko daare Baŋa Wɛ mo wae o bere nabiinu bochare nyenyego.
4Puseŋ-nyeno zwɛ ye keo mo se o cheigi ta-balwaaro.
Vwa-fɔro de maa cheigi ba na gaane vwa ba tiŋi tei to.
5N ná mɔne yiniga tu, n twe wolo na naane‑o to mo.
N ma‑n ná chake de n dwoŋi cham, waarem wó yi‑m.
6Nankwe nae zula ba naaro ŋwaane mo.
Bia de maa wó taa jege teera ba kwoa de ba niina ŋwaane.
7Ta-ŋom wo maŋe de nɔn-wo-koro.
Vwa fɔm tiini ko wo maŋe de Pa-bu.
8Nɔɔno wolo ná jaane dim
o vo o pa o dwoŋi,
kotu boŋe we o jege wo-kuri mo
se o maa na woŋo kolo maama
o na lage to.
9Nmo ná kwei n dwonna keim-lwanno n chɛ-ba,
n bere swono mo.
Ko daare botare-gula chɔge sɔŋɔ mo.
10N ná bwɛ boboŋa tu bedwe,
ko wó woli‑o,
ko dwoni n ná kwei kafena
n fere nɔn-jworo kuni bi.
11Nɔn-balwaaro mo ba sɛ
ba pae ba yiga tiina.
Keim-chɛ-nyeno nam mo wó ba
o pa ko zo ba yera.
12N ná vei n jeeri nywoŋ-kura kalo ba na vere ka bia ba daare-ka,
gare n ná jeeri nɔn-jworo na wora o toŋe jworim.
13N ná kwei lwarem se n ma n ŋwe lanyerane keim,
lwarem bá fɔge de nwoŋi n sɔŋɔ ne.
14Jara ná bobo, ya yagem chamma,
ne buga na pore pa ka na wuuri yɔɔ tei to mo.
N ná chege da-lɔŋɔ ko yiga ne gara.
15 Baŋa Wɛ chuli se nɔɔno pa puseŋ-nyeno bora,
naa se nɔɔno vane chega tu o bora.
16N ná chɔge sabu nɔn-jworo baŋa ne se o beeri swa,
ko ye kafɛ mo.
Kokuri, o bá fɔge o ja swa.
17Badwoŋ-ŋom zege n kwaga ne mo maŋa maama.
Chorro wora se ba woli‑m cham maŋa ne mo.
18Wolo ná le o yuu o zege se o dwoŋi jwoŋi jene,
kotu boboŋa muri mo.
19Wolo na lage kantɔgɔ to lage lwarem keim mo.
Zeiŋi-n-tete tu maa beeri chɔgem.
20Wolo boboŋa na ywori to kolokolo ba yɔɔre chwoŋa.
Ni-zɛ ni-zɛ tu maa zoore cham wone.
21N bu ná ye jworo, bane mo wó go‑m.
Nɔn-jworo kwo wo maa ba fɔge ko tiga.
22Wolo wo ná pwola maŋa maama,
kotu jege yazura mo,
Yi-nyɔna nam ye jaweo mo ko goe lela.
23Puseŋ-nyem seigi o jwoŋi dim mo
se o ma kweele chega kam.
24Wo-pore-nyem jaŋa se o yi poore mo.
Nɔn-jworo boboŋa nam kare ya beeri mo yɔɔ yerane.
25N bu ná ye jworo, bane mo wó go‑m.
Bu dwi dem konto jege zonne mo o ke o tiina.
26Ko dae ko chwoŋa ne se n waare
wolo na yeiri woŋo ni ne to,
naa se n fere nɔn-yuu de o chega.
27Wolo ni taane na ba daga to mo bere we o lɔre chekke.
Wolo maa na ba wuuri de o taane to mo seene o yei.
28Nɔn-jworo ná ye chemm de o ni ŋɔŋa kam,
ba we o yi poore mo.
O ná wae o ni o pui,
ba we o wae wonnu o kuri da-wone.

english_text:
It's Wrong To Favor the Guilty
1It's selfish and stupid
to think only of yourself
and to sneer at people
who have sense.
2Fools have no desire to learn,
instead they would rather
give their own opinion.
3Wrongdoing leads to shame
and disgrace.
4Words of wisdom
are a stream that flows
from a deep fountain.
5It's wrong to favor the guilty
and keep the innocent
from getting justice.
6Foolish talk will get you
into a lot of trouble.
7Saying foolish things
is like setting a trap
to destroy yourself.
8There's nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
9Being lazy is no different
from being a troublemaker.
10The Lord is a mighty tower
where his people can run
for safety—
11the rich think their money
is a wall of protection.
12Pride leads to destruction;
humility leads to honor.
13 It's stupid and embarrassing
to give an answer
before you listen.
14Being cheerful helps
when you are sick,
but nothing helps
when you give up.
15Everyone with good sense
wants to learn.
16A gift will get you in
to see anyone.
17You may think you have won
your case in court,
until your opponent speaks.
18Drawing straws is one way
to settle a difficult case.
19Making up with a friend
you have offended
is harder than breaking
through a city wall.
20Make your words good—
you will be glad you did.
21Words can bring death or life!
Talk too much, and you will eat
everything you say.
22 A man's greatest treasure
is his wife—
she is a gift from the Lord.
23The poor must beg for help,
but the rich can give
a harsh reply.
24Some friends don't help,
but a true friend is closer
than your own family.
translation_text:
1Wolo na ba ye de nɔɔna to nii o tete yerane mo.
O ba nege yi-pore-nyem boboŋa.
2Jworru yiga tera se ba zamese swa,
Banto yɔɔre ba nii se ba ta ba boboŋa mo.
3Puseŋa kikia vei de chaveera mo.
Totoŋ-vɛɛsa nam ba yaale nɔɔno belei.
4Nabiinu ni-botare luuna ne naneo wo na-luŋa dwoŋi mo.
Swa taane nam nye de bu-dura na zege buli-yi ne ka vei to mo.
5Ko dae ko chwoŋa ne se n woli puseŋ-nyem se o lu taane wone,
ye n daare n che wolo na yeiri woŋo ni ne to se o yé na bora.
6Nɔn-jworo ni taane jaane jara mo de tui.
O ŋɔŋa kam ŋwaane o wó su magero mo.
7Nɔn-jworo ni taane mo jwoori de chɔge‑o.
O tete taane yeini de de‑o mo.
8Bebare nyem ni taane nye de
wodi-ywoŋo na duri solololo
ko tu nabiinu kana ne to mo.
9N ná kɔre jawɔrɔ de n totoŋa,
n de wo-chɔgeno ba gare daane.
10 Baŋa Wɛ yere dem ye dalem jei chekke mo.
Nɔn-ŋona maa duri ba zoore da ye ba nae siu.
11Nadum jejegero tem wae te che‑o de cham.
O boŋe we te kwoli‑o ne teo kabira na kwoli-ko tei to mo.
12Ka-zeiŋi-ka-tete mo yeini ko lwoori chɔgem.
Ka-gwooni-ka-tete de maa tɔge zula yiga.
13Nmo ná gare n leiri taane n ti,
ye n ta wo cheigi se n lɔre de kuri,
ko tɛ n kuri we n jworim dem kɛ jeŋa mo.
14N boboŋa ná ba sɛ ya pae n jaweo,
ko wó woli‑m mo se n na dam.
Ko daare n teena ná ti de n jaweo kom,
n daa‑n bá wane n ja n tete.
15Yi-pore-nyem seene o yia
se o zamese swa mo,
Swa tiina maa cheigi bera.
16Pɛɛre wó pore chwei dedɛ de pa‑m
se nɔɔna maama cheigi n taane,
de nɔn-kamuna de.
17Pa-bu dedoa ni ye solololo mo.
18Dedɛɛra balei ná mage ni-kantɔgɔ,
ko maŋe se ba ta jɔrɔ mo
se ba lɔre wɔ mo jege chega.
19Ni-kantɔgɔ pwɛ nɔɔna daane mo.
Ne ko na chana se nɔɔno bwori peena diga o zo tei to,
n ná pɛ n choro wo chɔge,
ko tiini ko chana se á kwɛ daane.
20Ni-wodiu sui kana mo.
Ni taane maa zuri bochare.
21Balo na swoi ŋɔn-fara to wó na ka ŋweero,
kokuri nabiinu ni taane mo jege toone de ŋwea dam.
22N ná di kaane, n nɛ wo-laao.
Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo ke‑m zaane.
23Yiniga tu ŋwane se o na yibwona mo.
Nadum maa kare nɔɔna o yaga.
24Yuudwoŋo wae ko chɔge nɔɔno.
Ko daare chilwoŋ-zɔŋɔ wora
o na gare nu-puga bu.

english_text:
It's Wise To Be Patient
1It's better to be poor
and live right
than to be a stupid liar.
2Willingness and stupidity
don't go well together.
If you are too eager,
you will miss the road.
3We are ruined
by our own stupidity,
though we blame the Lord.
4The rich have many friends;
the poor have none.
5Dishonest witnesses and liars
won't escape punishment.
6Everyone tries to be friends
of those who can help them.
7If you are poor,
your own relatives reject you,
and your friends are worse.
When you really need them,
they are not there.
8Do yourself a favor
by having good sense—
you will be glad you did.
9Dishonest witnesses and liars
will be destroyed.
10It isn't right for a fool
to live in luxury
or for a slave to rule
in place of a king.
11It's wise to be patient
and show what you are like
by forgiving others.
12An angry king roars
like a lion,
but when a king is pleased,
it's like dew on the crops.
13Foolish children bring disgrace
to their fathers.
A nagging wife goes on and on
like the drip, drip, drip
of the rain.
14You may inherit all you own
from your parents,
but a sensible wife
is a gift from the Lord.
15If you are lazy
and sleep your time away,
you will starve.
16Obey the Lord's teachings
and you will live—
disobey and you will die.
17Caring for the poor
is lending to the Lord,
and you will be well repaid.
18Correct your children
before it's too late;
if you don't punish them,
trouble will come their way.
19People with bad tempers
are always in trouble,
and they need help
over and over again.
20Pay attention to advice
and accept correction,
so you can live sensibly.
21We may make a lot of plans,
but the Lord will do
what he has decided.
22What matters most is loyalty.
It's better to be poor
than to be a liar.
23Showing respect to the Lord
brings true life—
if you do it, you can relax
without fear of danger.
24Some people are too lazy
to lift a hand
to feed themselves.
25Stupid fools learn good sense
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being corrected.
26Disgraceful children
rob their father
and chase their mother away.
27If you stop learning,
you will forget
what you already know.
28A lying witness makes fun
of the court system,
and criminals think crime
is really delicious.
29A stupid fool should expect
to be punished.
translation_text:
1Yiniga tu ná jei de o chega
gare nɔn-jworo ná jege ni-zɛ ni-zɛ.
2N ná lage keim ye n laam yeiri-ka,
ko ba lana.
Kokuri, lela lela kɔe bu-kaane nyeene.
3Nabiina tete jworim mo jege-ba de chɔga,
ye ba jwoori ba jege de Baŋa Wɛ.
4Jejegero tu wó na badwonna dedɛ.
Yiniga tu badwonna nam duri ba daare‑o mo.
5Wolo ná fɔe vwa taane dim baŋa ne,
kotu wó na waarem.
Wolo maa ná gaane vwa o tiŋi, o de bá lu.
6Nɔɔna dedɛ beeri se nadum mo taa lage ba taane.
Nɔɔna maama maa lage wo-ywoŋo tu ni taane.
7Yiniga tu chorro tete lɔŋe‑o mo.
O badwonna de nam bá duri ba daare‑o na?
O ná kwaane o tɔge-ba o lwoori tei de,
o bá na-ba.
8N ná jege yeino,
n wó nii n tete baŋa ne.
Yi-poro maa wó pa‑m yiga-veiŋa.
9Wolo ná fɔe vwa taane dim baŋa ne,
kotu wó na waarem.
Wolo maa ná gaane vwa o tiŋi, o yere wó jei.
10Nɔn-jworo wo maŋe se o taa di o ni.
Ko laam nam wó ke tɛ mo
se kabaa di dam pa-bia baŋa ne?
11Yi-pore-nyem peene o bane mo.
Ba ná maŋe ba chɔge o yiga,
o ke ne o ba nae mo to.
12Pɛ bane ná zaŋe,
ko nye de nywoŋo mo laara.
O nam ná ke wolo zaane,
ko nye de nyɔnɔ mo to ga-lɛɛro baŋa ne.
13Bu-jworo yɔɔre o pae ko jege o kwo mo ko ni.
Ka-wam ná swoi jara,
ko nye de doa na nene ka ba waara to mo.
14Kwoa kwei jejegero mo ba pae ba bia,
se ko ná ye ka-yero, Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo pae.
15N yera ná duna,
n wó ta‑n dɔ dedɛ mo.
N ma‑n ná ba sɛ totoŋa,
kana mo wó ni‑m.
16Wolo na sɛ bera to wó jwoŋi o tete o yage.
Ko daare, n ná jege Wɛ nia yam n gwoona,
n wó te mo.
17Wolo ná jege wo-ywoŋo de yiniga tiina,
kotu jene o pa Baŋa Wɛ mo.
Wɛ nam wó jwoori o yiri kotu jene o pa‑o.
18De n bia chwoŋa ne ye pwola ta tigi ka pa‑m.
Yé woli-ba se ba jwa na chɔgem.
19Ban-lom tu bane dem mo pae o nae cham.
O dae ba woli,
kokuri o ta wó to de wone.
20N ná cheigi kwea ye n jwoŋi bera,
n jwa wó ji yi-pore-nyem mo.
21Nabiinu na boŋe se o ke kolo to ba lɔre ko tia,
Ko nam ye Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa yam mo wó zege.
22Kolo na ye wo-chɛɔ to mo ye se nɔɔna bere swono daane.
Yiniga tu maa gare vwa-fɔro.
23Nɔɔno ná kɔre Baŋa Wɛ,
o wó na ŋwea.
O ta wó sii mo chɔnɔ,
ye chɔgem bá yi‑o.
24Jawɔre-nyem ware o pa o jeŋa vo o ni.
25N ná mage nɔn-lwɛɛno,
nayeiri-nyem wó tɔge da o zamese swa.
N ma‑n ná bwɛ yi-pore-nyem, o wó lɔre o yi mo.
26Wolo ná ke pa ko yi o kwo,
naa o ná zeili o nu o yage pwola ne,
kotu beeri chaveera de yu-yɔlɔ mo o pae o tete.
27Amo bu, n ná yɔɔre n ve bera,
n nam ywori lɔra chwoŋa kam ne mo konto.
28Nɔn-wo-koro yeini o yaale taane dim mo de o maana.
Puseŋ-nyena maa pae lwarem kikia jiri wodiu pa ba di.
29Nɔn-lwɛɛna maŋe de waarem mo,
ye jworru maŋe de magero.

english_text:
Words of Wisdom Are Better than Gold
1It isn't smart to get drunk!
Drinking makes a fool of you
and leads to fights.
2An angry ruler
is like a roaring lion—
make either one angry,
and you are dead.
3It makes you look good
when you avoid a fight—
only fools love to quarrel.
4If you are too lazy to plow,
don't expect a harvest.
5Someone's thoughts may be
as deep as the ocean,
but if you are smart,
you will discover them.
6There are many who say,
“You can trust me!”
But can they be trusted?
7Good people live right,
and God blesses the children
who follow their example.
8When rulers decide cases,
they weigh the evidence.
9Can any of us really say,
“My thoughts are pure,
and my sins are gone”?
10Two things the Lord hates
are dishonest scales
and dishonest measures.
11The good or bad
that children do
shows what they are like.
12Hearing and seeing
are gifts from the Lord.
13If you sleep all the time,
you will starve;
if you get up and work,
you will have enough food.
14Everyone likes to brag
about getting a bargain.
15Sensible words are better
than gold or jewels.
16You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
17The food you get by cheating
may taste delicious,
but it turns to gravel.
18Be sure you have sound advice
before making plans
or starting a war.
19Stay away from gossips—
they tell everything.
20Children who curse their parents
will go to the land of darkness
long before their time.
21Getting rich quick
may turn out to be a curse.
22Don't try to get even.
Trust the Lord,
and he will help you.
23The Lord hates dishonest scales
and dishonest weights.
So don't cheat!
24How can we know
what will happen to us
when the Lord alone decides?
25Don't fall into the trap
of making promises to God
before you think!
26A wise ruler severely punishes
every criminal.
27Our inner thoughts are a lamp
from the Lord,
and they search our hearts.
28Rulers are protected
by God's mercy and loyalty,
but they must be merciful
for their kingdoms to last.
29Young people take pride
in their strength,
but the gray hairs of wisdom
are even more beautiful.
30A severe beating can knock all
of the evil out of you!
translation_text:
1Sa-nyɔre pae nɔɔno toŋe jworim mo.
Sa-dɛɛra maa pae nɔɔno swoi jara.
Sana na gane wolo maama to ba jege swa.
2Pɛ bane ná zaŋe, ko nye de nywoŋo mo laara.
Wolo ná gɔre‑o, kotu wó ga o ŋwea.
3Wolo na lɔŋe jara to wó na yere.
Ko daare nɔn-jworo beeri jara jei mo se o ke.
4Jawɔre-nyem na kɔre varem to,
ba wó taa toŋe faao ye o jei o nii mo.
5Nabiinu boboŋa luuna ne naneo wo na-luŋa dwoŋi mo.
Boboŋa tu nam mo wae-ya o vaŋe o lea.
6Dedɛ tɛ de ni-vɔɔ we, ba ye chega tiina.
Chega tu nam ba yi.
7Nɔn-ŋom ŋwe o ŋwea pa ka tɔge chwoŋa mo.
O kwaga kam maama wó taa jege yu-ywoŋo.
8Pɛ ná jeini se o di nɔɔna taane,
o maane taane dwi maama mo o nia,
se o le lwarem o yage.
9Wɔ mo wó wane o ta we,
o boboŋa maama yɔɔre ya ye chekke,
ye biin tera o ŋwea wone?
10Ko ná ye kampin-nyena na kwei bwɛ selo na dae chekke ba maa toŋe to,
Baŋa Wɛ vae banto ni taane.
11Ba lɔre bia ba kikia baŋa ne mo.
Dáane mo n wó lɔre ba tɔge chwoŋa na.
12Zwa na cheiga ye yia de nii to, Baŋa Wɛ mo ke-te.
13Yé ta‑n dɔ dedɛ, se yiniga wó ja‑m.
Nam poore n yera se n ta‑n di n sui.
14Yeillu maama tɛ we wonnu yeiga dana mo.
O nam ná yeigi o ti, o we o pugi mɔle.
15Sabu-seŋa de kandwa-nyenno wae te daga te gaale.
Ko nam ná ye yeino taane,
ko tiini ko jege lonne.
16Nɔɔno ná sɛ se o zege
se veiru di jene nmo tei ne,
ko maŋe se n jwoŋi kotu gare-bwora mo n woli da.
17Kampini wonnu dim ywomma.
Te nam wó ba te ja n ba.
18Bwɛ de n dwonna se n daare
n tigisi n boboŋa jeiga dedoa.
Nam yé vei jara ne ye n wo jwoŋi kwea.
19Ta‑n yei bebare nyem ni ne,
se o ware o peene taane.
Ta‑n lɔŋe balo na ware ba nia ba pu to.
20Wolo ná jege o kwo naa o nu yere o chɔga,
o momwɛ wó pɔpɔ de ti,
ne mini na pɔpɔ de dwei
tete ne tei to mo.
21N kwo ná tega o daare jejegero o pa‑m ye n muri,
te bá kwɛ‑m n nɔn-keiri maŋa ne.
22Yé boŋe n tete ne we,
“Amo wó yiri lwarem kikia jene mo.”
Ta‑n cheigi se Baŋa Wɛ jaŋe o pa‑m.
23 Baŋa Wɛ vae kampin-nyena ni taane.
Bwɛ selo na dae chekke to ba lana o tei ne.
24 Baŋa Wɛ mo tiŋi chwoŋa o pa debam se dé taa via.
Nabiinu nam wó ke tɛ mo o lɔre kolo na wo yiga ne to?
25N ná wuuri n ta we,
“A pɛ woŋo konto Wɛ mo,”
pa n boŋe se n kwane n ni-gwonim dem,
n kwei kalanchogo mo n ja n tete konto.
26Pɛ ná nii o nɔɔna baŋa ne de swa,
o yeini o le puseŋ-nyena bam mo se o fere-ba.
27Wɛ kwei boboŋa o ke nabiinu maama wone mo.
Ya nye de min-mɔɔla mo ya bere dé wo kom chekke.
28Pɛ ná dɛ chega ŋwaane o swoi nɔɔna,
konto mo wó kwoli‑o.
Ko ye o swono kom mo pae
se o paare dem zega.
29Nɔn-donno teere ba dam baŋa ne mo.
Nɔn-kwe nam wó mage nenɔŋa de ba yu-pwei mo.
30Ba ná ke‑m zonne pa ko chɛ n yera,
n wó yage lwarem kikia mo.
Magero dedɛ korese‑m mo se n leiri n wo.

english_text:
The Lord Is In Charge
1 The Lord controls rulers,
just as he determines
the course of rivers.
2We may think we are doing
the right thing,
but the Lord always knows
what is in our hearts.
3Doing what is right and fair
pleases the Lord
more than an offering.
4Evil people are proud
and arrogant,
but sin is the only crop
they produce.
5If you plan and work hard,
you will have plenty;
if you hurry to get rich,
you will end up poor.
6Cheating to get rich
is a foolish dream
and no less than suicide.
7You destroy yourself
by being cruel and violent
and refusing to live right.
8All crooks are liars,
but anyone who is innocent
will do right.
9 It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
10Evil people want to do wrong,
even to their friends.
11An ignorant fool learns
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being instructed.
12God is always fair!
He knows what the wicked do
and will punish them.
13If you won't help the poor,
don't expect to be heard
when you cry out for help.
14A secret bribe will save you
from someone's fierce anger.
15When justice is done,
good citizens are glad
and crooks are terrified.
16If you stop using good sense,
you will find yourself
in the grave.
17Heavy drinkers and others
who live only for pleasure
will lose all they have.
18God's people will escape,
but all who are wicked
will pay the price.
19It's better out in the desert
than at home with a nagging,
complaining wife.
20Be sensible and store up
precious treasures—
don't waste them
like a fool.
21If you try to be kind and good,
you will be blessed with life
and goodness and honor.
22One wise person can defeat
a city full of soldiers
and capture their fortress.
23Watching what you say
can save you
a lot of trouble.
24If you are proud and conceited,
everyone will say,
“You're a snob!”
25If you want too much
and are too lazy to work,
it could be fatal.
26But people who obey God
are always generous.
27 The Lord despises the offerings
of wicked people
with evil motives.
28If you tell lies in court,
you are done for;
only a reliable witness
can do the job.
29Wicked people bluff their way,
but God's people think
before they take a step.
30No matter how much you know
or what plans you make,
you can't defeat the Lord.
31Even if your army has horses
ready for battle,
the Lord will always win.
translation_text:
1 Baŋa Wɛ mo tei pɛ wom boboŋa.
O ma pa ya tɔge
o na lage tei to,
ne o na bere bu-dura
ka na wó tole tei to.
2Nɔɔna yeini ba boŋe we
ba kikia maama tɔge chwoŋa mo.
Baŋa Wɛ nam yeini o maŋe
ba boboŋa yam mo
o lɔre ya na ye tei to.
3Nmo ná toŋe ko lɔɔre
ye n tɔge chega,
gare n ná zwɛ vara
n ke kaanem n pa Baŋa Wɛ.
4Puseŋ-nyem na-veili
ye wɛleere yerane mo,
de o na pae o dwoi maama
ye o bere o tete to ŋwaane.
5Boboŋa tu ná chɛ de totoŋa,
o wó vo yiga.
Yiniga maa wó ja wolo na wuuri se o duni to.
6Jejegero telo nɔɔna na fɔe vwa ba nae to ba dáana.
Te nye de nyoa na maa jei to mo.
Te maa wó ja‑o te go.
7Puseŋ-nyena nankɔɔre kikia yam
wó jwoori ya chɔge-ba mo,
ba na ve se ba ke chega to ŋwaane.
8Wolo na wo vwa wone to totoŋa ba tɔge chwoŋa.
Chega tiina kikia nam yɔɔre ya ye chekke mo.
9Nɔɔno ná beeri gugworo o nayuu ne o tigi da
gare o ná zoore de ka-wam.
10Puseŋ-nyeno jege lwarem puga mo o jei.
Wonto ba duri o fara yibwona kɔtaa!
11N ná mage nɔn-lwɛɛno,
nayeiri-nyem wó tɔge da
o zamese swa.
N ma‑n ná bere boboŋa tu,
o wó lɔre lɔra mo.
12Chega Tu wom yei kolo na jege ko ke puseŋ-nyena sam ne to.
O maa pae chɔgem tui ba baŋa.
13Nabwona ná lwoori wolim
ye n ve se n cheigi,
nmo de ná lage zeinim,
ba bá leiri.
14Pɛɛre ná seigi de pa,
de goe bane.
Dim delo na kwoli de pa to
de zuri ban-lom mo.
15Chega ná jege ka toŋe jei selo ne,
nɔn-ŋona chaka mo,
ye nankɔ-nyena fona.
16Wolo na ba boŋe o yi
ye o ke keim to,
wó kweeli yibeeli wone mo.
17Yiniga mo wó ja wolo na swoi kajaŋa keim to.
Wolo na swoi sa-nyɔre de wodi-fɔrɔ to bá duni.
18Puseŋ-nyena yeini ba jwoŋi nɔn-ŋona cham ba zeŋe mo,
ye nɔn-ŋollo leiri ba jwoŋi chega tiina lɛɛro tem.
19Nɔɔno ná duri o vo kagoa yuu o zoora,
gara o ná zoore de ka-wam wolo na jege nyenyɔna to.
20Yi-pore-nyem lae wo-laaro dwi dwi de nuga mo o zege o sɔŋɔ wone.
Nɔn-jworo nam ba di o daare o zega.
21Nɔɔno ná beeri lam de swono jei,
kotu wó na momwɛ-dɛɛre,
de duni, de zula mo.
22Yi-pore-nyem wó wane teo
kolo na su de babɛ to.
O maa wó vaare mɛ ba na dale to o de tega ne.
23Ke gara n ni ne,
se n che n tete de cham.
24Ba bwoi boyere nyem we,
“Nɔn-tweeno” mo.
Kotu ba fe nɔɔna o nae bu da.
25Wolo fera ná zo wonnu dedɛ
ye o jawɔrɔ gaale,
kotu beeri toone o pa o tete mo.
26Kotu jei o teene se o na wonnu o woli da mo.
Nɔn-ŋona nam yɔɔre ba pae ba wonnu mo
ye kolokolo bá che ba yiga.
27 Baŋa Wɛ chuli puseŋ-nyena
na goe vara ba kaane‑o tei to,
ko fɔge ko dae lwarem boboŋa yam
ba jege ye ba ke-de to.
28Wolo ná fɔe vwa taane dim baŋa ne,
kotu taane wó maŋe tega ne mo.
Wolo nam ná boŋe o yi,
ba bá che kotu maana yam.
29Puseŋ-nyem pa o ye mo
ye o bere o dae da.
Nɔn-ŋom nam boŋe mo
ye o ke keim.
30N ná yei tega tei de,
de n ná jeeli n tiŋi mɛ de mɛ de,
n bá‑n dwoni de Wɛ se n di.
31Nabiinu wó wane o kwɛ o sisein-nɔɔno o ti
se o vo jara wone.
Baŋa Wɛ nam mo lage o di jara yam.

english_text:
The Value of a Good Reputation
1A good reputation and respect
are worth much more
than silver and gold.
2The rich and the poor
are all created
by the Lord.
3When you see trouble coming,
don't be stupid
and walk right into it—
be smart and hide.
4Respect and serve the Lord!
Your reward will be wealth,
a long life, and honor.
5Crooks walk down a road
full of thorny traps.
Stay away from there!
6 Teach your children
right from wrong,
and when they are grown
they will still do right.
7The poor are ruled by the rich,
and those who borrow
are slaves of moneylenders.
8Troublemakers get in trouble,
and their terrible anger
will get them nowhere.
9The Lord blesses everyone
who freely gives food
to the poor.
10Arguments and fights
will come to an end,
if you chase away those
who insult others.
11The king is the friend of all
who are sincere
and speak with kindness.
12The Lord watches over everyone
who shows good sense,
but he frustrates the plans
of deceitful liars.
13Don't be so lazy that you say,
“If I go to work,
a lion will eat me!”
14The words of a bad woman
are like a deep pit;
if you make the Lord angry,
you will fall right in.
15All children are foolish,
but firm correction
will make them change.
16Cheat the poor to make profit
or give gifts to the rich—
either way you lose.
Thirty Wise Sayings
17Here are some sayings
of people with wisdom,
so listen carefully
as I teach.
18You will be glad
that you know these sayings
and can recite them.
19I am teaching them today,
so that you
may trust the Lord.
20I have written thirty sayings
filled with sound advice.
21You can trust them completely
to give you the right words
for those in charge of you.
–1–
22Don't take advantage
of the poor
or cheat them in court.
23The Lord is their defender,
and what you do to them,
he will do to you.
–2–
24Don't make friends with anyone
who has a bad temper.
25You might turn out like them
and get caught in a trap.
–3–
26Don't guarantee to pay
someone else's debt.
27If you don't have the money,
you might lose your bed.
–4–
28Don't move a boundary marker
set up by your ancestors.
–5–
29If you do your job well,
you will work for a ruler
and never be a slave.
translation_text:
1Yere-ŋom gare jejegero dedɛ.
Nɔɔna ná nege‑m gare n ná jege lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa dedɛ.
2 Baŋa Wɛ mo naane nabiina maama,
ko ná maŋe ko ye naduna de nabwona de.
3Boboŋa tu duri o seigi cham mo se de yé yi‑o.
Nayeiri-nyem nam wó duri o zo de wone mo ye o yaare.
4Nmo ná tu n tete
ye n kɔre Baŋa Wɛ,
nmo wó na jejegero,
de zula, de momwɛ-dɛɛre.
5Sabare de kalanchorro mo tigi
te cheigi nankɔ-nyem,
Wolo maa na jege o tete to mo wó lɔŋe-te.
6Korese n bu se o da chwoŋa.
O ná ke nɔɔno,
o bá ywori ka wone.
7Naduna di dam mo nabwona baŋa ne.
Je-diru maa ye kabaa jene tu tei ne.
8Wolo na du puseŋa to wó zage cham mo.
O ban-jworo kom bá toŋe ko pa‑o.
9Wɛ swolim wo wo-ywoŋo tu baŋa ne mo,
kokuri, kotu yei we
yiniga tiina de ni di.
10Le-na nɔn-tweeno á wone se kantɔgɔ jei.
Toro de jara maama de maa wó ti.
11Wo-pwoŋo tu ni taane ná bwona,
kotu de pɛ wó di badwoŋo mo.
12 Baŋa Wɛ yɔɔre o yere boboŋa tiina mo,
se ko na ye nɔn-ŋollo,
o jage ba boboŋa mo o yaga.
13Jawɔre-nyem maŋe diga ne ye o we,
“A ná nwoŋi pwooni ne,
nywoŋo wó ja-ne!”
14Ka-tola ni taane ye kalanchogo mo.
Ko maa jaane balo Baŋa Wɛ bane na zaŋe de-ba to.
15Bia boboŋa yɔɔre ya su
de busɔɔne kikia mo.
Nmo nam ná yɔɔre n korese-ba,
ba wó to chwoŋa ne.
16Wolo na bɛɛse nabwona
se o ma o na nyɔɔre to,
de wolo na woli naduna de pɛɛra to,
yiniga wó ja ba maama.
Faŋa tu bera yam
17Fɔge n cheigi faŋa tu bera yam,
se n daare n tɔge kolo a na bere‑m to.
18Kokuri to, ya ná tigi n bochare ne,
ye n wae-ya n lwoni n bere nɔɔna,
n wó di ywoni ya baŋa ne.
19Ko ná ye nmo,
a zem pɛ n lɔre wonnu tento maama,
se ko pa n teena taa wo Baŋa Wɛ tei ne.
20Amo nam popone ta-kura fintɔ mo
a tiŋi se a bere‑m.
Ya maa ye yalo na kwei nɔɔno kwea
ye ya daare ya pa o lɔre lɔra to.
21Memaŋa yam wó pa n lɔre taane
delo na yɔɔre de jege chega to,
se n wane n ta chega kam
de balo na toŋe‑m to.
1
22Yé zaŋe n vere nabwom wonnu
o na bwona to ŋwaane.
Nam yé vane yiniga tiina bora.
23 Baŋa Wɛ mo wó ŋɔɔne o pa-ba,
ye o pa ko zo balo na jege-ba ba bɛɛse to.
2
24Yé di badwoŋo dedaane ban-lom nyem.
Nam lɔŋe wonto dwi dem.
25N ná wo lɔre zega,
n de wó ji kodwoŋi nɔɔno,
pa se n ŋwea kam chɔge.
3
26Yé le n yuu n zege
se n ŋwe nɔn-gaa jene.
27Nmo ná wo wane n ŋwe,
ba wó ba ba kwei n sara ba daare‑m.
4
28Yé fɔɔre siseini delo dé nabaara bam na lɔge ba tiŋi ba pa daane to.
5
29Nɔɔno jeŋa totoŋa ná tɔge chwoŋa,
kotu wó toŋe o pa pwa
ye ko dae nɔn-yɔɔro.

english_text:
–6–
1When you are invited
to eat with a king,
use your best manners.
2Don't go and stuff yourself!
That would be just the same
as cutting your throat.
3Don't be greedy for all
of that fancy food!
It may not be so tasty.
–7–
4Give up trying so hard
to get rich.
5Your money flies away
before you know it,
just like an eagle
suddenly taking off.
–8–
6Don't accept an invitation
to eat a selfish person's food,
no matter how good it is.
7People like that take note
of how much you eat.
They say, “Take all you want!”
But they don't mean it.
8Each bite will come back up,
and all your kind words
will be wasted.
–9–
9Don't talk to fools—
they will make fun of you.
–10–
10Don't move a boundary marker
or take the land
that belongs to orphans.
11God All-Powerful is there
to defend them against you.
–11–
12Listen to instruction
and do your best to learn.
–12–
13Don't fail to correct
your children.
You won't kill them
by being firm,
14and it may even
save their lives.
–13–
15My children,
if you show good sense,
I will be happy,
16and if you are truthful,
I will really be glad.
–14–
17Don't be jealous of sinners,
but always honor the Lord.
18Then you will truly have hope
for the future.
–15–
19Listen to me, my children!
Be wise and have enough sense
to follow the right path.
20Don't be a heavy drinker
or stuff yourself with food.
21It will make you feel drowsy,
and you will end up poor
with only rags to wear.
–16–
22Pay attention to your father,
and don't neglect your mother
when she grows old.
23Invest in truth and wisdom,
discipline and good sense,
and don't part with them.
24Make your father truly happy
by living right and showing
sound judgment.
25Make your parents proud,
especially your mother.
–17–
26My son, pay close attention,
and gladly follow
my example.
27Bad women and unfaithful wives
are like a deep pit—
28they are waiting to attack you
like a gang of robbers
with victim after victim.
–18–
29Who is always in trouble?
Who argues and fights?
Who has cuts and bruises?
Whose eyes are red?
30Everyone who stays up late,
having just one more drink.
31Don't even look
at that colorful stuff
bubbling up in the glass!
It goes down so easily,
32but later it bites
like a poisonous snake.
33You will see weird things,
and your mind
will play tricks on you.
34You will feel tossed about
like someone trying to sleep
on a ship in a storm.
35You will be bruised all over,
without even remembering
how it all happened.
And you will lie awake asking,
“When will morning come,
so I can drink some more?”
translation_text:
6
1Dedɛɛro ná bwoŋi‑m
se á di wodiu daane,
ta‑n yei se n ja n tete lanyerane.
2Peene n fera yam,
se n yé di n ni.
3Yé sa yera de wodiu kom na totoge ni tei to,
kokuri, ko tigi da gana ŋwaane mo.
7
4Yé go n tete se n ma‑n duni.
Nam boŋe lanyerane
se n zuri n yera.
5N ná yɔɔre n da n na sabu,
ko nam jei mo konto,
ne ko puli vɔna mo
ko jaane wɛɛne ko jei to.
8
6Yé vei n jeini de wo-loŋ-nyem
n di wodiu,
ne ko ná maŋe ko ywomma tei de.
7Nɔɔno wom konto dwi yeini o jeeli nmo na di tei to mo.
O wae o tɛ de nmo we,
“Di nmo na lage tei!”
Ko nam wo yi o wo.
8Nmo ná maŋe n di fee de,
n wó tɔne-ko n yage.
Nmo ya na seini‑o tei to maa wó ji kafɛ.
9
9Yé ja swa taane n yi nɔn-jworo,
se o bá nege-de.
10
10Yé fɔɔre siseini delo dé nabaara bam na lɔge ba pa daane to.
Nam yé di n zo botaro kara,
o na bwona to ŋwaane.
11Baŋa Wɛ nam ye kotu yera nɔɔno na zege o kwaga ne to.
O maa wó ŋɔɔne o pa‑o.
11
12Yɔɔre n seene n yia n zamese,
se n wane n lɔre lɔra dedɛ.
12
13Yé ve se n korese n bu.
N ná waare‑o, o bá te.
14N nam ta wó che‑o de toone.
13
15Amo bu, nmo yi ná poore mo,
amo wo wó pwoli.
16Amo wó yɔɔre a taa chaka mo,
ne nmo ni ná ŋɔɔne chega taane yerane.
14
17Yé pa n boboŋa zo wɛle-keira wone.
Nam seene n yia se n ta‑n kɔre Baŋa Wɛ dɛ maama wone.
18Teena wora jwa seeni ya pa‑m,
ya nam bá ji kafɛ.
15
19Amo bu, cheigi a taane se n ja swa.
Pa n kikia taa tɔge chwoŋa lanyerane.
20Yé ta‑n vei de balo na misi ba tete sa-nyɔre wone to,
naa nɔn-kwollu telo na lage dim-fɔrɔ to.
21Yiniga mo wó ja sa-nyɔra de nɔn-kwollu.
Ba jawɔre kikia yam wó pa ba ji nɔn-kayɛ.
16
22N dɛ n kwo baŋa mo
n ba logo baŋa.
Ta‑n cheigi o taane.
Nam yé ve n nu bera
o kokweero baŋa ne.
23Kwaane se n ja chega yera.
N nam ná jaane-ka,
yé kwei-ka n yeigi.
Ta beeri se n na yi-poro,
de boboŋ-ŋona, de lɔra.
24Bu yi ná poore,
o kwo jege wopwolo mo,
ye o teere de o bu wom.
25Pa n kwo de n nu yuni
taa wo wɛɛne.
Ta ke kolo na wó pa n nu wopwolo to.
17
26Amo bu, fɔge n cheigi a taane. Zamese a ŋwea na ye tei to, se n lɔre veiŋa. 27Ta‑n yei we ka-bworo ye gwoŋ-chanluŋu mo. Ka-tola kam ye vole delo ni na ye voloa to mo. 28Ba vwɛ mo nenɛɛne venverena, se ba vere baara ba kaana tei ne.
18
29Wɔ mo wo lɛɛro wone tento? Wɔ mo tiini o jege ŋwaŋa tento? Wɔ mo swoi jara? Wɔ pompona mo gaale? Wɔ fufwollu mo dwoi o tete? Wɔ yia mo seene ne jana tento? 30Ko ye balo na kwei ba tete ba pa sana to mo. Ba maa vei ba jwoŋi sa-laŋa. 31Yé pa n fera zo sana bam ba lam ŋwaane, ne ba ná maŋe ba fufugi tei maama zom-bia wone, naa ba ná duri ba tu puga wone solololo de. 32Ka ná jaane wolo, ka zaga ne basankwea mo ye ka vea de nye de anakɔbayi vea. 33N yia wó taa kare ya nii mo liira liira ye n boboŋa maama vugimi wo-yɔɔro baŋa ne. 34Nmo dɔɔm wone tega kam nye de ka gigili mo. N laam ma‑n pipira ye n ye bele-bele n sara wone. 35Nmo laam maa wó ta nenɛɛne, “Wɔ mo jege-ne o yiga ye a ba na‑o? Sana banto bá lwoori a yia ne se a daa vo a jwoŋi sa-laŋa na?”

english_text:
–19–
1Don't be jealous of crooks
or want to be their friends.
2All they think about
and talk about
is violence and cruelty.
–20–
3Use wisdom and understanding
to establish your home;
4let good sense fill the rooms
with priceless treasures.
–21–
5Wisdom brings strength,
and knowledge gives power.
6Battles are won
by listening to advice
and making a lot of plans.
–22–
7Wisdom is too much for fools!
Their advice is no good.
–23–
8No one but troublemakers
think up trouble.
9Everyone hates senseless fools
who think up ways to sin.
–24–
10Don't give up and be helpless
in times of trouble.
–25–
11Don't fail to rescue those
who are doomed to die.
12Don't say, “I didn't know it!”
God can read your mind.
He watches each of us
and knows our thoughts.
And God will pay us back
for what we do.
–26–
13Honey is good for you,
my children,
and it tastes sweet.
14Wisdom is like honey
for your life—
if you find it,
your future is bright.
–27–
15Don't be a cruel person
who attacks good people
and hurts their families.
16Even if good people
fall seven times,
they will get back up.
But when trouble strikes
the wicked,
that's the end of them.
–28–
17Don't be happy
to see your enemies trip
and fall down.
18The Lord will find out
and be unhappy.
Then he will stop
being angry with them.
–29–
19Don't let evil people
worry you
or make you jealous.
20They will soon be gone
like the flame of a lamp
that burns out.
–30–
21My children, you must respect
the Lord and the king,
and you must not make friends
with anyone who rebels
against either of them.
22Who knows what sudden disaster
the Lord or a ruler
might bring?
More Sayings That Make Good Sense
23Here are some more sayings
that make good sense:
When you judge,
you must be fair.
24If you let the guilty
go free,
people of all nations
will hate and curse you.
25But if you punish the guilty,
things will go well for you,
and you will prosper.
26Giving an honest answer
is a sign
of true friendship.
27Get your fields ready
and plant your crops
before starting a home.
28Don't accuse anyone
who isn't guilty.
Don't ever tell a lie
29or say to someone,
“I'll get even with you!”
30I once walked by the field
and the vineyard
of a lazy fool.
31Thorns and weeds
were everywhere,
and the stone wall
had fallen down.
32When I saw this,
it taught me a lesson:
33 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
34Suddenly poverty hits you
and everything is gone!
translation_text:
19
1Yé pa n boboŋa zo puseŋ-nyena wone.
Nam yé di badwoŋo de-ba.
2Kokuri ba yeini ba jeeli nankɔɔre kikia mo ba yuu ne,
ye ba ná puri ba nia
ko ye se ba chɔge nɔɔno mo.
20
3Swa lɔ sam mo ya zega.
Yi-poro pae de fɔge de chwi lanyerane de dam mo.
4Yeino maa pae sam sui
de wo-laaro dwi maama.
21
5Swa tu jege dam
o dwoi nɔn-sawɔrɔ.
Wolo na zamese o yi to ma gare babea.
6Wolo na sɛ bera to mo ke jara o di wɔnɔ,
Wolo maa na bwɛ wonnu de nɔɔna dedɛ to bá to jara wone.
22
7Botare dende tiini se dana
se dwoi nɔn-jworo jaanem.
Nakwa ná jeeri manchwoŋo ni ne,
o ba jege ni se o puri.
23
8Ba wó bwoŋi balo na swoi se ba taa boŋe lwarem ba pae ba dwonna to we nankɔ-nyena.
9Nɔn-jworo jeeli o woŋo maama
o vei o guri de wɛleere mo.
Nɔɔna maa yɔɔre ba chuli nɔn-lwɛɛno.
24
10Nmo vɔna ná pare cham maŋa ne mɔle-mɔle,
ko nam bere we n tiini n bwona mo lage-lage.
25
11Ba ná vaŋe wolo ba vei se ba go vwa chwoŋa ne,
se n jwoŋi kotu n yage.
12Nmo nam ná we,
“Ka wo nɛ amo, a yeiri nɔɔno wom,”
nam lɔre we Wɛ yei nɔɔna maama bochara na ye tei to.
Wonto mo zei n ŋwea
ye o yei n kikia maama ni ne.
N boŋe we o bá ŋwe nɔɔno maama
ko tɔge de o kikia na?
26
13Amo bu, n ná nɛ tooro,
di-te n boboŋa, te na lana to ŋwaane.
To-nuga maa sona
ye ka duri ka tu n kwora chwoŋa.
14Nam lɔre we yi-poro de ye konto mo ko pa‑m.
N ná nɛ-ko, nmo wó ta‑n jege jwa lanyerane,
ye n teena yam bá fɔge ya ti.
27
15Yé ji wolo o teo tiina na mage gulu ba le‑o,
pa o beeri nɔn-ŋom de o sɔŋɔ tiina se o de chɔge to.
16Kokuri, nɔn-ŋom ná to kuni berepɛ de,
o ta wó pɛ o zaŋe o zege cheppe.
Se ko ná ye puseŋ-nyem,
lira tera ka na wó jwoŋi‑o ka yage.
28
17Yé ta‑n chaka de n dono na to tega ne to.
O na tiri se o to,
yé ta‑n jege wopwolo.
18Kokuri, Wɛ wó na n kikia
se o wo chɔge dede‑m.
O laam maa wó pa o bane daa yé zaŋe de n dono wom.
29
19Yé pa se n boboŋa vugimi
nɔn-balwaaro ŋwaane.
Ta yé ta‑n lage se n ta‑n nye de puseŋ-nyena.
20Kokuri, nɔn-balɔrɔ ba jege jwa.
O ŋwea pwooni dem wó pɔpɔ de dwei mo.
30
21Amo bu, ta‑n kɔre Baŋa Wɛ de pɛ.
Nam yé ta‑n ye de balo na ba nege banto to.
22Kokuri to, Wɛ de pɛ jege dam
se ba chɔge nɔn-dwoa bam konto mɔle mɔle.
Faŋa tu memaŋa yadwonna
23Boboŋa tu taana yadwonna mo tento:
Ko dae ko chwoŋa ne
se n ta‑n kuri nɔɔna da-wone.
24Wolo ná tage de Agɛbora we,
“Nmo jege chega,”
nɔɔna wó sɔɔle lwarem ba pa kotu,
ye teene maama de ve‑o.
25Wolo nam ná waare balo na toŋe vwa to,
wonnu maama wó da chwoŋa te pa kotu,
ye Wɛ zaane de taa wo o yuu ne.
26Wolo na wó ta n yera chega to mo seene o ye n badwoŋi chekke.
27N ná ti n pwooni yiga totoŋa maama,
ye n daare n lwei n lweeru maama,
se n laam ta‑n yei n sɔŋɔ lɔɔm ni ne.
28Yé pa maana n chɔge n dwoŋi
ye n yeiri chega kam n tia.
Nam yé ma n ni n gane nɔɔna.
29Yé ta n tete ne we,
“O na zage a suŋu to,
a de wó zage o sɔŋɔ mo.”
30Amo nɛ pwola mo a tɔge jawɔre-nyem kara seeni a kɛ. 31A ma na we bombɔŋɔ mo jwoŋi jei sem maama. Ga-cheiŋo de ma lware tega kam maama. O na mɛ kandwa yalo o che-ka to de jage sae!
32A ma boŋe kolo a na nɛ to wone zii, ye a zamese woŋo ko wone a lɔre we:
33Ta‑n swoi dɔɔne,
ye n lage se n ta‑n tigi n sia.
Vɔ n je daane se n sii n ja n tete,
34se yiniga ná wo vɔɔre ka ba‑m ne venvereno to.
Gɛɛre de maa wó zi‑m ne ŋween-bembea dwoŋi to.

english_text:
More of Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some more
of Solomon's proverbs.
They were copied by the officials
of King Hezekiah of Judah.
2God is praised
for being mysterious;
rulers are praised
for explaining mysteries.
3Who can fully understand
the thoughts of a ruler?
They reach beyond the sky
and go deep in the earth.
4Silver must be purified
before it can be used
to make something of value.
5Evil people must be removed
before anyone can rule
with justice.
6 Don't try to seem important
in the court of a ruler.
7It's better for the ruler
to give you a high position
than for you to be embarrassed
in front of royal officials.
Be sure you are right
8before you sue someone,
or you might lose your case
and be embarrassed.
9When you and someone else
can't get along,
don't gossip about it.
10Others will find out,
and your reputation
will then be ruined.
11The right word
at the right time
is like precious gold
set in silver.
12Listening to good advice
is worth much more
than jewelry made of gold.
13A messenger you can trust
is just as refreshing
as cool water in summer.
14Broken promises
are worse than rain clouds
that don't bring rain.
15Patience and gentle talk
can convince a ruler
and overcome any problem.
16Eating too much honey
can make you sick.
17Don't visit friends too often,
or they will get tired of it
and start hating you.
18Telling lies about friends
is like attacking them
with clubs and swords
and sharp arrows.
19A friend you can't trust
in times of trouble
is like having a toothache
or a sore foot.
20Singing to someone
in deep sorrow
is like pouring vinegar
in an open cut.
21 If your enemies are hungry,
give them something to eat.
And if they are thirsty,
give them something
to drink.
22This will be the same
as piling burning coals
on their heads.
And the Lord
will reward you.
23As surely as rain blows in
from the north,
anger is caused
by cruel words.
24It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
25Good news from far away
refreshes like cold water
when you are thirsty.
26When a good person gives in
to the wicked,
it's like dumping garbage
in a stream of clear water.
27Don't eat too much honey
or always want praise.
28Losing self-control
leaves you as helpless
as a city without a wall.
translation_text:
Solomon dende sem sedwonna
1Solomon memaŋa yam yadaara mo tento. Judah teo pɛ Hezekia nam mo pɛ ba jwoori ba lwoni-se ba popone ba tiŋi.
2Wɛ jege dam se o seigi wonnu mo.
Pɛ maa jege dam o yɛ wonnu.
3Ba ba lɔre pɛ boboŋa ba tia.
Ya diini wɛɛne ya dwoni wɛ baŋa kam,
ye ya ta tu tega kam kuri kuri.
4Lura ná le digiru lu-nyenno yera ne,
lu-nyenno tem wó ke wo-kura.
5Pwa ná zeili nakwa-balwaaro ba daare,
ba paare wó jeini nɔn-ŋonne baŋa ne.
6Yé zeiŋi n tete pɛ yiga ne.
Nam yé ja n tete n vo n maŋe de nɔn-kamuna.
7Pɛ ná tage de nmo o we,
“Ba n jeini ywo,”
gare o ná gwooni‑m nɔn-yerro yiga ne.
Nmo yi ná nɛ n dwoŋi wo-keeru,
8yé wuuri n ja‑o n vo taane dim jei.
Kokuri to, ko kwaga ne nmo wó maane we,
chave-kukua gare chave-dedɔrɔ.
9Pa nmo de n faro wom jeini á kwɛ daane.
Se yé ta‑n jege‑o n chwo n bere nɔɔna.
10Ko ná dae konto, nɔɔna wó ta we
n ye bebare nyem.
Nmo laam ma‑n wó te de n chaveera.
11Ta-kuri nye de sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno na gɔgere te ke daane tei to mo.
12Yi-pore-nyem ná kwoni‑m o zege de swa taane,
ko jege kuri ko dwoi ba ná kwei sabu-seŋa zambili ba de‑m.
13Wolo ba na toŋe to ná jege chega,
o zuri balo na toŋe‑o to bochara mo,
ne na-zura na zuri na-nyɔm faao-ni maŋa ne tei to.
14N ná pwooli we n wó pa n dwoŋi woŋo ye n wo pɛ‑o,
n nye de kunkwonnu de vio na ware te ja doa te ba tei to mo.
15N ná peene n bane,
dedɛɛro wó cheigi n taane.
Wolo ni taane na bwona to
wae o kwɛ wonnu.
16Tooro tete maŋe se n ná nɛ-te,
se n di-te n maŋe mo.
Te dedɛ wó pa n tɔne mo.
17Yé pa n nɛ taa lona
de n faro sɔŋɔ.
O fera ná nwoŋi‑m,
o laam wó taa lɔŋe‑m mo.
18Wolo ná fɔge vwa
se o ma o chɔge o dwoŋi,
kotu nye de o kwei da-lɔŋɔ,
naa se-zɔɔ, naa che-tɛɛre delo na sele to mo o chɔge‑o.
19Ne yeili-bɔɔ de nachara na pae nɔɔno yeiri o tete jei to,
konto mo nɔn-ŋolo jege o ke
de o dwoŋi cham maŋa ne.
20Nmo ná jege wopwolo lei n leeni
wolo wo na chɔge to yiga ne,
ko nye de n lɔɔre o gɔrɔ mo
n daare‑o n zege waaro yiga ne,
naa n lwogi yɛ mo
n yage o ŋɔne wone.
21Nmo dono kana ná wɔe,
pa‑o wodiu se o di.
Na-nyɔm ná jege‑o,
pa‑o na se o nyɔ.
22Kikia yam konto wó pa se chaveera tiini ya ja‑o,
ne Wɛ zeiŋi mini mo o yuu ne to.
Baŋa Wɛ maa wó zuli‑m ko ŋwaane.
23Ne baŋa seeni vio kom na tui de doa tei to,
mo ban-zɔŋɔ na tɔge de bebara ko tui tei.
24Nɔɔno ná beeri gugworo o nayuu ne o tigi da
gare o ná zoore de ka-wam.
25Kwor-ywoŋa ná nwoŋi yiga yiga ka ba,
ka pae bochara tigi mo,
ne na-zura na zuri bochare tei to.
26Vole mo su de weero
pa na daa ware se ba bu.
Nɔn-ŋom de nam ná sɛ o pa puseŋ-nyem,
ko ye konto mo.
27Ne tooro dedɛ na ba woli nɔɔno tei to,
konto mo wolo ná beeri o tete seinim, ko ba woli‑o.
28Nɔɔno ná ware o bane o ja,
o nye de teo kolo kabiri na sirimi se to se daare-ko to mo.

english_text:
Don't Be a Fool
1Expecting snow in summer
and rain in the dry season
makes more sense
than honoring a fool.
2A curse you don't deserve
will take wings and fly away
like a sparrow or a swallow.
3Horses and donkeys
must be beaten and bridled—
and so must fools.
4Don't make a fool of yourself
by answering a fool.
