5But if you answer any fools,
show how foolish they are,
so they won't feel smart.
6Sending a message by a fool
is like chopping off your foot
just to spite yourself.
7A fool with words of wisdom
is like an athlete
with legs that can't move.
8Are you going to honor a fool?
Why not shoot a slingshot
with the rock tied tight?
9A thornbush waved around
in the hand of a drunkard
is no worse than a proverb
in the mouth of a fool.
10It's no smarter to shoot arrows
at every passerby
than it is to hire a bunch
of worthless nobodies.
11 Dogs return to eat their vomit,
just as fools repeat
their foolishness.
12There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who says,
“I'm really smart!”
13Don't be lazy and keep saying,
“There's a lion outside!”
14A door turns on its hinges,
but a lazy person
just turns over in bed.
15Some of us are so lazy
that we won't lift a hand
to feed ourselves.
16A lazy person says,
“I am smarter
than everyone else.”
17It's better to take hold
of a mad dog by the ears
than to take part
in someone else's argument.
18It's no crazier to shoot
sharp and flaming arrows
19than to cheat someone and say,
“I was only fooling!”
20Where there is no fuel
a fire goes out;
where there is no gossip
arguments come to an end.
21Troublemakers start trouble,
just as sparks and fuel
start a fire.
22There is nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
23Hiding hateful thoughts
behind smooth talk
is like coating a clay pot
with a cheap glaze.
24The pleasant talk
of an enemy
hides more evil plans
25than can be counted—
so don't believe a word!
26Everyone will see through
those evil plans.
27 If you dig a pit,
you will fall in;
if you start a stone rolling,
it will roll back on you.
28Watch out for anyone
who tells lies and flatters—
they are out to get you.
translation_text:
1Ne doa na ba nena, ye nyɔnɔ de ba toe te-pwoŋa ne tei to,
konto mo nɔn-jworo de wo maŋe se n zuli‑o.
2Ne kawɛbidwoori na ba jege tega jeiŋa tei to,
mo sensɔla kalo na wo tɔge chwoŋa to na ye tei.
Ka bá jeini n yuu ne.
3Fere sisein-nɔɔno de fena,
se n de ŋona bonaga ba ne n vaŋe-ka.
Ko nam ná ye nɔn-jworo,
mage‑o se ko yi.
4Nɔn-jworo ná tage taane pa n leiri-de,
nmo ded‑o ba gare daane.
5Leiri nɔn-jworo de o jworim dem.
Ko ná dae konto,
o wó boŋe we o yɔɔre o yei mo.
6Nmo ná kwei kwora n ke nɔn-jworo jeŋa ne se o vo o pa nɔɔna,
nye de n na zage n tete naga n gwoni,
naa n na beeri cham n pa tete tei to mo.
7Ne gɔrɔ nɛ na ware se vo tei to,
konto mo nɔn-jworo de ware o lɔre dende kuri.
8Nmo ná vɔge kandwɛ napana wone
se n vuvugi n yage,
nye de n na kwaane se n zuli Agɛboŋa tei to.
9Ne sa-nyɔro na yeiri sabara jaanem tei to,
konto mo nɔn-jworo de yeiri dende kuri.
10N ná kwei totoŋe n ke Agɛboŋa jeŋa ne,
n mage bwogo mo.
11Ne kukura na jwoori ka di ka tetwanno tei to,
nɔn-jworo de kare o toŋe jworim konto mo.
12Nɔn-jworo jege teena se o lɔre,
se ko dwoi wolo na pa o yei to.
13Jawɔre-nyem tigi mo ye o we,
“Nywoŋo kare pwooni ne ko beera!”
14Ne diga ni bworo na pore
ye ko pe tei to,
konto mo yezona tu
de kare o pipiri o sara ne.
15Nɔɔna badaara jawɔrɔ ye ko yera.
Ba ná tore jeŋa zoŋa ne ba fɔ gole,
ba ware ba lu dwoa
se ba ja-de ba vo ba ni.
16Jawɔre-nyem pa o yei o dwoi yi-pore-nyena barepɛ na yeini ba leiri taane de swa tei to mo.
17Nɔɔno ná jwoŋi o dwoŋi jara o ja,
kotu wó na na-gare chene mo.
18Ne chichwoo na tae chena yɔɔ yɔɔ tei to,
19mo wolo de na gane o dwoŋi ye o we,
“A ke a kwɛɛra mo” de na ye tei.
20Dɛ ná ti, mini wó dwei mo.
Bebara ná tera, ni-kantɔgɔ jei mo.
21Min-chala nyeeri mini mo,
nankɔ-nyem de maa nyeeri jara.
22Bebare nyem ni taane nye de wodi-ywoŋo na duri solololo ko tu nabiinu kana ne to mo.
23Wolo ná tage taane
ye o wo ba tɔge o taane dem,
kotu nye de ba na kwei lu-nyenno
ba taare dɔgɔ kamɔgɔ tei to mo.
24Pipiri-nyem kwei ni-som mo
o seigi o boboŋa.
O laam maa tɔge dáane
o chɔge nɔɔna.
25O taane dem ná ywomma tei maama de,
yé sɛ-de, se o boboŋa yɔɔre ya su de lwarem mo.
26O ná seigi o boboŋ-lwanno tem tei maama de,
te wó nwoŋi pwooni
se nɔɔna na-te jaja.
27N ná chege kalanchogo,
ko wó ja n tete.
N nam ná bibili kandwɛ-zane
n ja n di peo yuu n yage-de,
de wó bibili de to de pane‑m mo.
28Vwa-nyem chuli o dona mo.
Ni-som nyem maa jaane chɔgem o tui.

english_text:
Don't Brag about Tomorrow
1 Don't brag about tomorrow!
Each day brings
its own surprises.
2Don't brag about yourself—
let others praise you.
3Stones and sand are heavy,
but trouble caused by a fool
is a much heavier load.
4An angry person is dangerous,
but a jealous person
is even worse.
5A truly good friend
will openly correct you.
6You can trust a friend
who corrects you,
but kisses from an enemy
are nothing but lies.
7If you have had enough to eat,
honey doesn't taste good,
but if you are really hungry,
you will eat anything.
8When you are far from home,
you feel like a bird
without a nest.
9The sweet smell of incense
can make you feel good,
but true friendship
is better still.
10Don't desert an old friend
of your family
or visit your relatives
when you are in trouble.
A friend nearby is better
than relatives far away.
11My child, show good sense!
Then I will be happy
and able to answer anyone
who criticizes me.
12Be cautious and hide
when you see danger—
don't be stupid and walk
right into trouble.
13You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
14A loud greeting
early in the morning
is the same as a curse.
15The steady dripping of rain
and the nagging of a wife
are one and the same.
16It's easier to catch the wind
or hold olive oil in your hand
than to stop a nagging wife.
17Just as iron sharpens iron,
friends sharpen the minds
of each other.
18Take care of a tree,
and you will eat its fruit;
look after your master,
and you will be praised.
19You see your face in a mirror
and your thoughts
in the minds of others.
20Death and the grave
are never satisfied,
and neither are humans.
21Gold and silver are tested
in a red-hot furnace,
but we are tested by praise.
22No matter how hard
you beat a fool,
you can't pound out
the foolishness.
23You should take good care
of your sheep and goats,
24because wealth and honor
don't last forever.
25After the hay is cut
and the new growth appears
and the harvest is over,
26you can sell lambs and goats
to buy clothes and land.
27From the milk of the goats,
you can make enough cheese
to feed your family
and all your servants.
translation_text:
1Yé tiini n ŋɔɔne jwa taane n su n ni,
se n yeiri tega ná poore,
ko na wó taa ye tei n yera ne.
2Yage se nɔn-gɛ tei‑m,
se nmo tete yé ta n su n ni.
3Kandwa-zana dumma,
ye kasolo dunni de gaale.
Nɔn-jworo nam ná toŋe jworim nmo yera ne,
ko cham dem duna
de dwoi tento maama.
4Ban-lom tu keim chana
ye o ware o ja.
Wolo kazwe na gaale to nam dwoi kotu.
5Wolo ná wo kɔre n yi se o ta n chega jei,
kotu gare wolo na jege n chega o seigi dede‑m to.
6Nmo badwoŋi ná tage n chega jei,
ko jege kuri ko pa‑m.
Ko daare n dono mɔne dede‑m mo,
se ko dae swono.
7N ná di n su,
tooro tete lwoi n momwa ne mo.
Kana nɔɔno nam yeiri ko chana.
8Wolo na duri o daare o sɔŋɔ to
nye de zuŋa kalo na nwoŋi
ka daare ka pwogo to mo.
9Terale nuga de talwoŋ-ywoŋa pae nɔɔna wopwolo mo.
Badwoŋ-ywoŋo bera nam gare tento.
10Ta‑n yei n badwonna de n kwo badwonna ni ne.
Cham ná yi‑m,
n fara bam konto wó woli‑m
ba dwoni n chorro telo na ba bwola to.
11Amo bu, kwaane n ja swa
se a wo pwoli ko ŋwaane.
Konto wó pa-ne chwoŋa
se a puri a ni a leiri
balo na jege-ne ba lwɛ to.
12Boboŋa tu duri o seigi cham mo se de yé yi‑o.
Nayeiri-nyem nam wó duri o zo de wone mo ye o na yaara.
13Nɔɔno ná sɛ se o zege
se veiru di jene nmo tei ne,
ko maŋe se n jwoŋi kotu gare-bwora mo n woli da.
14Wolo na gwoni tega
o tɔɔle o ware o dwonna to
nye de o sɔɔle lwarem mo o pa-ba.
15Ka-wam wolo na jege nyenyɔna to
nye de doa na nene
ye na luri n diga ne tei to mo.
16Wolo ná kwaane se o ja ka-dwi dem konto,
kotu wó ke o ga mo.
Ko nye de n na zeili vio se n ja-ko,
naa n mɔ nuga de n ja-bɔŋɔ tei to mo.
17Seene na kekarege daane se de ja ni tei to,
konto mo nabiina de zamese da-tei ne.
18Wolo na fɔge o kwɛ teeni to wó di ko bia mo.
Wolo de maa na toŋe o pae o tu de chega to wó jwoŋi zula.
19Niu bere nabiinu yibia mo.
Ko daare o bochare maa bere o na ye wolo to.
20Twa ná maŋe ba daga tei,
churu ba sui.
Nabiina yia de ba nii ya sui.
21Min-vogo pae ba yei lu-nyenno
de sabu-seŋa lam mo.
Ko nam ná ye nabiinu,
ba wó lɔre o wo de o na nɛ yere tei to mo.
22Kwei nɔn-jworo n ke kazɔgɔ ne
n woli de mena n zɔ n na lage tei.
O jworim dem ta bá ti.
23Ta‑n yei n vara bam ni ne,
se n daare n ta‑n nii ba baŋa ne lanyerane.
24Kokuri jejegero bá taa wora taa taa.
Dwi dedoa nam wó wane
de taa tei paare wuu na?
25Ba ná gaane gaao pa ko jwoori ko kwi,
ye ba tigisi ga-korro telo ba na gaane to ba ke daane,
26mo nmo wó kwei n pei koro n sɔ gwaaro n ta‑n zoora.
N ta wó kwei n bone n yeigi
n jwoori n ma‑n yeigi tega.
27N ma‑n wó kwei n vara nayela
n kɔne n diga kam,
de n ka-nyaana bam.

english_text:
The Law of God Makes Sense
1Wicked people run away
when no one chases them,
but those who live right
are as brave as lions.
2In time of civil war
there are many leaders,
but a sensible leader
restores law and order.
3When someone poor takes over
and mistreats the poor,
it's like a heavy rain
destroying the crops.
4Lawbreakers praise criminals,
but law-abiding citizens
always oppose them.
5Criminals don't know
what justice means,
but all who respect the Lord
understand it completely.
6It's better to be poor
and live right,
than to be rich
and dishonest.
7It makes good sense
to obey the Law of God,
but you disgrace your parents
if you make friends
with worthless nobodies.
8If you make money by charging
high interest rates,
you will lose it all to someone
who cares for the poor.
9God cannot stand the prayers
of anyone who disobeys
his Law.
10By leading good people to sin,
you dig a pit for yourself,
but all who live right
will have a bright future.
11The rich think highly
of themselves,
but anyone poor and sensible
sees right through them.
12When an honest person wins,
it's time to celebrate;
when crooks are in control,
it's best to hide.
13If you don't confess your sins,
you will be a failure.
But God will be merciful
if you confess your sins
and give them up.
14The Lord blesses everyone
who is afraid to do evil,
but if you are cruel,
you will end up in trouble.
15A ruler who mistreats the poor
is like a roaring lion
or a bear hunting for food.
16A heartless leader is a fool,
but anyone who refuses
to get rich by cheating others
will live a long time.
17Don't give help to murderers!
Make them stay on the run
for as long as they live.
18Honesty will keep you safe,
but everyone who is crooked
will suddenly fall.
19Work hard, and you will have
a lot of food;
waste time, and you will have
a lot of trouble.
20God blesses his loyal people,
but punishes all who want
to get rich quick.
21It isn't right to be unfair,
but some people can be bribed
with only a piece of bread.
22Don't be selfish
and eager to get rich—
you will end up worse off
than you can imagine.
23Honest correction
is appreciated
more than flattery.
24If you cheat your parents
and don't think it's wrong,
you are a common thief.
25Selfish people cause trouble,
but you will live a full life
if you trust the Lord.
26Only fools would trust
what they alone think,
but if you live by wisdom,
you will do all right.
27Giving to the poor
will keep you from poverty,
but if you close your eyes
to their needs,
everyone will curse you.
28When crooks are in control,
everyone tries to hide,
but when they lose power,
good people are everywhere.
translation_text:
1Puseŋ-nyena duri se ba lu mo
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba pare-ba.
Nɔn-ŋona nam jege baare mo ne nywoŋo to.
2Teo ná su de zwabani-nyena,
ba leiri balo na nii-ko to yɔɔ yɔɔ mo.
Boboŋa tu nam wó kwei yeino mo o ja o teo o dáane.
3Yiniga tu ná pɛ ko zo o dwonna yiniga tiina yera,
o de do-jworo na chuura ka chɔge wodiiru to ba gare daane.
4Balo na ve Wɛ nia yam to bere we ba seini puseŋ-nyena mo.
Balo maa na sɛ-ya to bere we ba dwoni de-ba mo.
5Nɔn-balwaaro bá wane ba ni chega kam kuri.
Ko nam ná ye balo na kɔre Baŋa Wɛ to,
ba yɔɔre ba ni ka kuri mo lanyerane.
6Yiniga tu ná jei de o chega
gare nadum ná ye nɔn-ŋolo.
7Wolo na ke o tɔge Wɛ nia yam to
bere we o yi poore mo.
Wolo nam ná vei de nɔn-kwollu,
kotu yaale o kwo mo.
8Wolo ná dɔne nyɔɔre dedɛ jena baŋa ne se o ma o duni,
kotu wó ga o jejegero,
ye wolo na jege yiniga tiina ŋwaŋa to laam na-te.
9Nɔɔno ná paale o se o zwa de Wɛ nia yam,
o wɛ-lworo tete lwoi mo Wɛ momwa ne.
10Nmo ná soge nɔn-ŋom n de lwarem ne,
n tete wó to n gwoŋo wone mo.
Ko nam ná ye balo na ba tusi to,
banto jege jwa.
11Nadum yeini o boŋe we
o yei o ti mo.
Yiniga tu wolo yi na poore to
nam yɔɔre o yei nadum wo maama mo.
12Nɔn-ŋona ná diini dam baŋa,
nɔɔno maama chake mo.
Puseŋ-nyena nam ná jege dam ba di,
nɔɔna duri ba seigi mo.
13Wolo na jege o wɛleera o seigi to ba vei yiga.
Wolo nam ná pɛ ya nwoŋi pwooni ye o chuli-ya,
Wɛ wó duri kotu ŋwaŋa.
14Wolo na yɔɔre o kɔre Baŋa Wɛ to jege yu-ywoŋo.
Zwabani-nyem nam zoore cham wone mo.
15Pɛ ná tɔge puseŋa baŋa o yaare nabwona,
o nye de nywoŋo na ŋuuri se ko zi nɔne to mo.
16Pɛ keim ná chamma,
o boboŋa mo muri.
Wolo nam na chuli kampina to wó dáane.
17Nɔn-goro boboŋa wó daane‑o mo
se ko yi o toone maŋa.
O dae ba woli.
18Chega tu kikia cho‑o mo.
Ko daare nɔn-ŋolo wó pɔpɔ o na chɔgem.
19Wolo na sɛ varem to jeŋa yi o ni.
Yini-gwia nam wó ja wolo na kare o toŋe wo-yɔɔro to.
20Chega tu wó na Wɛ zaane se ko gaale.
Wolo yera nam ná sae se o beeri jejegero,
kotu wó yɔɔre o na waarem.
21Ko dae ko chwoŋa ne
se n ta‑n kuri nɔɔna da-wone.
Dim ŋwaane nam,
nɔɔna jege konto mo ba ke.
22Wo-loŋ-nyem lɔgere mo se o duni.
O nam yeiri we yiniga wó yi‑o.
23Nmo ná bwɛ nɔɔno de chega,
kwaga seeni n kikia wó su kotu yi,
ko dwoni n ya ná ke ni-som ded‑o.
24Wolo ná pini o kwo de o nu
ye o boŋe we konto dae kolokolo,
kotu de nɔn-goro ba gare daane.
25Wo-loŋ-nyem pae nankɔɔre mo zaŋa.
Ko daare wolo na ke o wo-dedoa de Baŋa Wɛ to wó di ywoni.
26Wolo na teege o tete yeino baŋa ne to ye jworo mo.
Wolo nam ná ke woŋo maama de swa,
kotu wó lu cham wone.
27N ná yei yiniga tiina ni ne,
n bá‑n fɔge n ga.
N nam ná se n zwa de nabwona keira,
ba wó sɔɔle lwarem ba pa‑m mo.
28Puseŋ-nyena ná jege dam ba di,
nɔɔna duri ba seigi mo.
Ba dam maa ná ti,
nɔn-ŋona daa wó pi ba nwoŋi mo.

english_text:
Use Good Sense
1If you keep being stubborn
after many warnings,
you will suddenly discover
you have gone too far.
2When justice rules a nation,
everyone is glad;
when injustice rules,
everyone groans.
3If you love wisdom
your parents will be glad,
but chasing after bad women
will cost you everything.
4An honest ruler
makes the nation strong;
a ruler who takes bribes
will bring it to ruin.
5Flattery is nothing less
than setting a trap.
6Your sins will catch you,
but everyone who lives right
will sing and celebrate.
7The wicked don't care
about the rights of the poor,
but good people do.
8Sneering at others is a spark
that sets a city on fire;
using good sense can put out
the flames of anger.
9Be wise and don't sue a fool.
You won't get satisfaction,
because all the fool will do
is sneer and shout.
10A murderer hates everyone
who is honest
and lives right.
11Don't be a fool
and quickly lose your temper—
be sensible and patient.
12A ruler who listens to lies
will have corrupt officials.
13The poor and all who abuse them
must each depend on God
for light.
14Kings who are fair to the poor
will rule a long time.
15Correct your children,
and they will be wise;
children out of control
disgrace their mothers.
16Crime increases
when crooks are in power,
but law-abiding citizens
will see them fall.
17If you correct your children,
they will bring you peace
and happiness.
18Without guidance from God
law and order disappear,
but God blesses everyone
who obeys his Law.
19 Even when servants are smart,
it takes more than words
to make them obey.
20There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who speaks
without thinking.
21Slaves that you treat kindly
from their childhood
will cause you sorrow.
22A person with a quick temper
stirs up arguments
and commits a lot of sins.
23Too much pride brings disgrace;
humility leads to honor.
24If you take part in a crime
you are your worst enemy,
because even under oath
you can't tell the truth.
25Don't fall into the trap
of being a coward—
trust the Lord,
and you will be safe.
26Many try to make friends
with a ruler,
but justice comes
from the Lord.
27Good people and criminals
can't stand each other.
translation_text:
1Ba ná kaane bere-gɛɔ tu kuni dedɛ baŋa ne ba ga,
o wó pɔpɔ o na chɔgem mo ye o bá lu de wone.
2Nɔn-ŋona ná diini paare baŋa,
nɔɔna jege wopwolo.
Puseŋ-nyena nam ná jege paare ba di,
nɔɔna laare mo.
3Wolo na beeri swa to kwo wo pwoli mo.
Wolo na tɔge ka-bworru kwaga to ma chɔge o kwo wonnu.
4Pɛ ná nii o nɔɔna de chega,
teo kom ywomma mo.
Kalipera tu yigi teo kom o de tega ne mo.
5Ni-som nyem nye de o chege kalanchogo mo o tiŋi.
6Nɔn-balɔrɔ wɛleera jigi da-bunnu mo ya gare‑o pa o to.
Chega tu lei nam jaana mo ye o wo tiga.
7Nɔn-ŋom jege yiniga tiina ŋwaŋa
ye o pae-ba ba chega.
Konto kolokolo nam dae puseŋ-nyem yiga.
8Nɔn-lwɛɛna wiiri jara mo
ba yage teo wone.
Swa tiina maa lwɛ jara.
9Swa tu ba saŋe nɔn-jworo pɛ sɔŋɔ ne,
kokuri, jworo kom wó da mwanno, de sɔɔ yerane mo
pa á bá na taane dem kuri.
10Nɔn-goro yɔɔre o chuli chega tu mo,
ye o beeri chwoŋa se o ti o momwɛ.
11Nɔn-jworo mo bere o ban-lom jaja.
Swa tu maa jaane o bane.
12Pɛ ná mae bebare taana o toŋa,
o nakwa maama wó taa ke puseŋa mo.
13 Baŋa Wɛ mo pae nabiina maama pwooni pa ba nae,
ko ná maŋe ko ye yiniga tu
de wolo na bɛɛse‑o to de.
14Pɛ ná bore chega o pa yiniga tiina,
o paare wó dáane mo.
15Kafena de bwɛa korese bu
pa o jaane swa mo.
Bu wolo ba na yage ywori to
wó yaale o nu mo.
16Puseŋ-nyena ná jei dam ne,
wɛleere puli mo.
Ba nam wó to ye nɔn-ŋona zege ba nii mo.
17Korese n bia, se ba wó pa‑m bochare-zuru de wopwolo.
18Wɛ kwora ná tera se ka bere nɔɔna,
ba ke ba na lage tei mo.
Balo maa na sɛ Wɛ nia yam to jege yu-ywoŋo.
19Ni taane yerane ba de kabɛ chwoŋa ne.
O ná maŋe o yei n na lage
se o ke tei to, o bá ke.
20Nɔn-jworo jege teena se o lɔre,
se ko dwoi wolo na tɛ taane
ye o ba boŋe to.
21Nmo ná maŋe n pa n kabaa ywooli o biini maŋa ne,
o jwa wó ba o de‑m jaguli-zane mo.
22Bane tu wiiri kantɔgɔ mo o ke da.
Ban-lom tu kikia maa jege daanem.
23Zeiŋi-n-tete pae nɔɔna toe ba yaale lela mo.
Wolo nam na tu o tete to wó na zula.
24Wolo na woli ŋweeno pa o ŋɔ to
jege o tete mo o waara.
O ná maŋe o chem taane dim baŋa ne, o ta wo sii.
25N ná kɔre n dwonna nabiina,
ko bá woli‑m.
N nam ná ke n chega de Baŋa Wɛ,
mo n sii.
26Wɛ ná pɛ nɔɔno na chega
gare o ná lage se pɛ taa yei o ni ne.
27Chega tiina kɔre nɔn-balwaaro na wo mɛ to mo.
Puseŋ-nyena de ma chuli nɔn-ŋona bam jei.

english_text:
The Sayings of Agur
1These are the sayings
and the message
of Agur son of Jakeh.
Someone cries out to God,
“I am completely worn out!
How can I last?
2I am far too stupid
to be considered human.
3I never was wise,
and I don't understand
what God is like.”
4 Has anyone gone up to heaven
and come back down?
Has anyone grabbed hold
of the wind?
Has anyone wrapped up the sea
or marked out boundaries
for the earth?
If you know of any
who have done such things,
then tell me their names
and their children's names.
5Everything God says is true—
and it's a shield for all
who come to him for safety.
6Don't change what God has said!
He will correct you and show
that you are a liar.
7There are two things, Lord,
I want you to do for me
before I die:
8Make me absolutely honest
and don't let me be too poor
or too rich.
Give me just what I need.
9If I have too much to eat,
I might forget about you;
if I don't have enough,
I might steal
and disgrace your name.
10Don't tell a slave owner
something bad about one
of the slaves.
That slave will curse you,
and you will be in trouble.
11Some people curse their father
and even their mother;
12others think they are perfect,
but they are stained by sin.
13Some people are stuck-up
and act like snobs;
14others are so greedy
that they gobble up
the poor and homeless.
15Greed has twins,
each named “Give me!”
There are three or four things
that are never satisfied:
16The world of the dead
and a childless wife,
the thirsty earth
and a flaming fire.
17Don't make fun of your father
or disobey your mother—
crows will peck out your eyes,
and buzzards will eat
the rest of you.
18There are three or four things
I cannot understand:
19 How eagles fly so high
or snakes crawl on rocks,
how ships sail the ocean
or people fall in love.
20An unfaithful wife says,
“Sleeping with another man
is as natural as eating.”
21There are three or four things
that make the earth tremble
and are unbearable:
22A slave who becomes king,
a fool who eats too much,
23a hateful woman
who finds a husband,
and a slave who takes the place
of the woman who owns her.
24On this earth four things
are small but very wise:
25Ants, who seem to be feeble,
but store up food
all summer long;
26badgers, who seem to be weak,
but live among the rocks;
27locusts, who have no king,
but march like an army;
28lizards, which can be caught
in your hand,
but sneak into palaces.
29Three or four creatures
really strut around:
30Those fearless lions
who rule the jungle,
31those proud roosters,
those mountain goats,
and those rulers
who have no enemies.
32If you are foolishly bragging
or planning something evil,
then stop it now!
33If you churn milk
you get butter;
if you pound on your nose,
you get blood—
and if you stay angry,
you get in trouble.
translation_text:
Aguri memaŋa yadwonna
1Jakɛ bu Aguri memaŋa mo tento. Ya maa ye Wɛ kwora. Nɔɔno maa we, “A yera maama chɛ mo! Wɛ, a yera chɛ mo. A daa bá wane a zege!”
2Amo yeiri kolokolo.
A yi maa wo poore nenɛɛne a dwonna nabiina bam tetei.
3A maa wo fɔge a zamese swa,
ye a yeiri Wo-pwoŋo Tu Baŋa Wɛ.
4Nabiinu wɔ mo diini Wɛ telaao
ye o jwoori o ba?
Wɔ mo jaane vio
o ke o jaguli ne?
Wɔ mo pɛ naneo kom
o kukuli o gɔrɔ ne?
Wɔ mo lɔge logo kom baŋa maama siseini o tiŋi?
Abam yei o de o bu wom yere na?
Á ná yei, se á ta á bere-ne.
5Wɛ taane dem maama yɔɔre de zege de chega mo.
O wae o cho balo na tui ba zoore o woro ne to.
6Ta‑n yei se n yé woli kolokolo Wɛ taane dem wone,
se Wɛ wó bwɛ‑m se ko bere we n ye vwa-fɔro mo.
7Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ,
a beeri wonnu telei mo
se n ke n pa-ne, se a laam te.
8Yé pa a taa ye vwa-nyem.
Ta yé pa zore ja-ne.
Nam yé pa-ne dunni dedɛ.
Pa-ne kolo yerane na maŋe
a jaanem to.
9Ko ná dae konto, a ná jege ko gaale,
a daa bá teege nmo yera ne,
ye a ta we “Wɔ mo ye Baŋa Wɛ?”
Yiniga nam ná tiini ka ja-ne,
a wae a ŋɔna
pa se a yaale amo Tu Wɛ yere.
10Yé chwo kabaa kwaga ka tu yiga ne,
se o laam wó sɔɔle lwarem
o ke n yuu ne.
11Nɔɔna badwonna swoi
se ba taa chɔge ba kwoa yere,
ye ba ta yɔɔre ba pae
ba niina ba jege yuu.
12Badwonna de maa boŋe we
ba kikia yɔɔre ya tɔge chwoŋa mo,
ye ba wo laam ye ligi-ligi.
13Badwonna maa bere ba kamunim mo
ye ba ta gwooni ba dwonna.
14Badaara ke wo-goo mo de nɔɔna
ye ba ni-yeila nye de se-zɔɔro.
Ba maa lage se nabwona yere saare tega baŋa ne.
15Kasandiu jege bukwa balei mo.
Ba maama maa tɛ ba we, “Tei n pa-ne.”
Wonnu tetɔ wora te na ba fɔge te sui.
Tena mo ba tɛ we “Ko maŋe!”
16Te maa ye:
churu chwoŋa,
de kadega puga,
de tega na ba fɔge ka sui na to,
de min-vogo na di bileim-bileim to.
17Wolo ná mɔne o kwo,
naa o ná ke o nu kachaare,
bachangaaro wó zɔge o yia te le,
ye duura de di o ya-nɔna yam.
18Wonnu tetɔ wora te na tiini te so-ne.
A maa ba ni wonnu tena kuri.
19Te maa ye:
Maao na jaane tei wɛyuu kom ne,
de basankwea na yei ka chwoŋa tei peero yuu ne,
de nabworo na yɛ naneo kom wone tei to,
de baaro de kaane swono laŋa na ye tei to.
20Ka-tola keim ye de yera.
O wó peini de nɔn-gaa
ye o ta jwoori o ta we,
“Amo wo ke kolokolo a chɔge.”
21Wonnu tetɔ mo pae tega baŋa kam ziziŋi.
Tena maa dwoi nabiina jaanem.
22Te maa ye:
Kabaa ná jigi pɛ,
de nɔn-jworo ná di ko su,
23de bukɔ wolo yuu na chana to ná pɔpɔ o zo baro,
de ka-nyaane ná zeili o tu o daare o vere baro wom o tei.
24Wonnu tena kamɔgɔ mo tiini ko muri tega baŋa ne,
ye te yi-poro ba jege dwoŋi.
25Memela tiini ba muri de dam.
De ko de, ba lae wodiiru
ba tiŋi cham maŋa ŋwaane.
26Pe-ware dam tiini de muri.
De ko de, ya zoore peo gugworru ne mo.
27Kayere ba jege pɛ se o bere ba na wó ke tei.
Se nam ná yo, dedoa tete ba ywori ka chwoŋa ne.
28Nɔɔno wae baleiga o jaane de o jeŋa.
Se nam ba kɔre pwa sam, se su da mo.
29Wonnu tetɔ mo yeini te vei nenɔŋa veiŋa.
Te tena gwɛɛm dem maa tiini de lana:
30Nywoŋo ye dedɛɛro mo ga-vara maama wone.
Ko maa ba ywori ko daare chwoŋa ko pae kolokolo.
31Chebɛɔ na kwoni ko yuu ko keeri to,
de bo-bala,
de pɛ wolo jar-keira na wo o tei ne to.
32N ná ke jworim de n na bere n kamunim tei to,
naa n ná jeeli lwarem kikia se n ke,
se n pu n ni chemm.
33Kokuri to, n ná mage nuga,
ka wó peere mo.
N ná chugi nɔɔno momwɛ,
jana mo wó nwoŋi.
N nam ná gware nɔɔno bane,
jara mo wó zaŋe.

english_text:
What King Lemuel's Mother Taught Him
1These are the sayings
that King Lemuel of Massa
was taught by his mother.
2My son Lemuel, you were born
in answer to my prayers,
so listen carefully.
3Don't waste your life
chasing after women!
This has ruined many kings.
4Kings and leaders
should not get drunk
or even want to drink.
5Drinking makes you forget
your responsibilities,
and you mistreat the poor.
6Beer and wine are only
for the dying or for those
who have lost all hope.
7Let them drink and forget
how poor and miserable
they feel.
8But you must defend
those who are helpless
and have no hope.
9Be fair and give justice
to the poor and homeless.
In Praise of a Good Wife
10A truly good wife
is the most precious treasure
a man can find!
11Her husband depends on her,
and she never
lets him down.
12She is good to him
every day of her life,
13and with her own hands
she gladly makes clothes.
14She is like a sailing ship
that brings food
from across the sea.
15She gets up before daylight
to prepare food for her family
and for her servants.
16She knows how to buy land
and how to plant a vineyard,
17and she always works hard.
18She knows when to buy or sell,
and she stays busy
until late at night.
19She spins her own cloth,
20and she helps the poor
and the needy.
21Her family has warm clothing,
and so she doesn't worry
when it snows.
22She does her own sewing,
and everything she wears
is beautiful.
23Her husband is a well-known
and respected leader
in the city.
24She makes clothes to sell
to the shop owners.
25She is strong and graceful,
as well as cheerful
about the future.
26Her words are sensible,
and her advice
is thoughtful.
27She takes good care
of her family
and is never lazy.
28Her children praise her,
and with great pride
her husband says,
29“There are many good women,
but you are the best!”
30Charm can be deceiving,
and beauty fades away,
but a woman
who honors the Lord
deserves to be praised.
31Show her respect—
praise her in public
for what she has done.
translation_text:
Pɛ Lemuweli memaŋa
1Pɛ Lemuweli memaŋa mo tento. Ya maa ye Wɛ kwora kalo o nu na bere‑o to.
2Nii mo! Nmo ye amo tete puga bu mo.
Nmo lora kam nam tɔge wɛ-lworo baŋa ne mo.
Konto to, pore n zwa se n cheigi.
3Yé da kaana ŋwaane n chɔge n dam,
se banto dwi yeini ba pa
se pwa dedɛ na ba chaveera mo.
4A bu Lemuweli, pwa dae se ba nyɔ sana.
Ba nam dae se ba ke fera de sa-dɛɛra.
5Sa-nyɔre wó pa ba swei
Wɛ nia yam na bere tei mo,
ye ba ja chega kam ba ju
nabwona yiga ne.
6Sa-dɛɛra maŋe de balo na jei
ba cheigi ba toone to mo,
ba teena maama na ti to ŋwaane.
7Ba ná bugi, ba wó swei ba yiniga de ba cham dem ni ne.
8Jiri nabwona ni
se n ŋɔɔne n pa-ba.
Pa balo na ba jege nɔɔna se ba nii-ba to na ba chega.
9Zaŋe n ŋɔɔne jaja
ye n bore chega bora.
Zege nabwona de yiniga tiina kwaga ne se ba na ba chega.
Ka-yero taane
10Ka-yero yuu yim chana dedɛ.
O dwi jege lonne de dwoi kandwa-nyenno dwi dwi.
11O baro ba jege lwia de kolokolo.
O maa bá ga nyɔɔre de fenfee de.
12Ka-yero ke o baro lanyerane mo maŋa maama,
ye o ba pae o nae zonne.
13O yeini o sɔ gwaaro mo
waaro de wulim maŋa ŋwaane,
ye o toŋe o totoŋa de wopwolo.
14O nye de nabwooru telo na zeŋe pipiu zela te tui to mo.
O maa vei yiga yiga o jaane wodiiru o tui o pae o diga tiina.
15Tega ba poore‑o sara ne,
de o na zaŋe o saŋe wodiu
o pa o diga tiina,
se o ka-nyaana bam de na ba nyem.
16O yeini o beeri tega mo o yeigi.
O ta ma kwei o na lage o jeŋa kalo o tiŋi to
o ma o jeiri Vini teeni.
17O ba sɛ o pae jawɔrɔ,
ye o tete chɛ de totoŋ-dɛɛra.
18O yɔɔre o yei pipiu laŋa mo
pa o ba toe,
ye tega ba poore‑o sara ne.
19O tete mo dole gare-yi
ye o sɔ gwaaro o pae o diga tiina.
20O ye wo-ywoŋo tu mo, naa
ye o yeini o zeini nabwona de yiniga tiina.
21Waaro maŋa ne o bá taa lwia
o diga tiina ŋwaane,
kokuri to, ba maama jege gare-ŋonno
se ba ma ba kwoli ba tete.
22O yeini o nyaane gwaaro mo
se o ma kwɛ o peiga jei,
ye kolo o na ke o yera ne to
yeini ko jwoŋi‑o chekke.
23O baro ná yeini o jeeri teo kom kapworo ne,
nɔɔna maama pa‑o zula mo,
ye ba gare‑o ba ke ko nakwa wone.
24O sɔ gare-fefale de se vovwe mo
o yeigi o pa pipiu tiina.
25O ye nɔn-dɛɔ mo
ye nɔɔna nege‑o.
O maa ba lwia de kolo na wó ke jwa seeni to.
26O yeini o kuri o ni botare-bia mo o ŋɔɔne de swa.
O ni taane bere lanyerane keim na ye tei mo.
27O yɔɔre o chɛ de totoŋa mo,
ye o nii o diga tiina baŋa ne lanyerane.
28O bia wó ke daane ba sɛ we o jege yu-ywoŋo.
O baro de maa wó seini‑o o we:
29“Kaana dedɛ ke wo-kura.
Nmo nam mo di yiga
ba maama wone.”
30Ya-tega wae ka gana,
lam de nam wae de tia.
Ko nam ná ye kaane wolo na kɔre Baŋa Wɛ to,
kotu maŋe de zula mo.
31Tei‑o se ko maŋe de
o totoŋa na ye tei to.
Ja‑o n yi teo kom kapworo,
se n pa o na zula nɔɔna yiga ne.

english_text:
Nothing Makes Sense
1When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
2Nothing makes sense!
Everything is nonsense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense!
3What is there to show
for all of our hard work
here on this earth?
4 People come, and people go,
but still the world
never changes.
5The sun comes up,
the sun goes down;
it hurries right back
to where it started from.
6The wind blows south,
the wind blows north;
round and round it blows
over and over again.
7All rivers empty into the sea,
but it never spills over;
one by one the rivers return
to their source.
8All of life is far more boring
than words could ever say.
Our eyes and our ears
are never satisfied
with what we see and hear.
9Everything that happens
has happened before;
nothing is new,
nothing under the sun.
10Someone might say,
“Here is something new!”
But it happened before,
long before we were born.
11No one who lived in the past
is remembered anymore,
and everyone yet to be born
will be forgotten too.
It Is Senseless To Be Wise
12I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel. 13With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do. 14I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
15If something is crooked,
it can't be made straight;
if something isn't there,
it can't be counted.
16 I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.” 17Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
18The more you know,
the more you hurt;
the more you understand,
the more you suffer.
translation_text:
1Wolo na ye Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno to kwora mo tento. Wonto mo ye Pɛ David bu, o na di paare Jerusalem teo kom ne to.
Dé yeiri wonnu kuri
2Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno mo we:
Dé bá wane dé ni wonnu tento maama kuri.
Te kuri nim tiini de chana de gaale se dé lɔre.
3Nabiina yaare de totoŋ-chɛɛra mo tega baŋa ne.
Bɛ nyɔɔre mo ba nam nae ya baŋa ne?
4Nabiina tui logo kom baŋa mo,
ye badwonna de leiri ba toa.
Logo kom nam yɔɔre ko ye ko na maŋe ko ye tei to mo.
5Wɛ dem yeini de puli mo,
ye de laam vo de zo.
De nam ta wó ke lela mo
se de jwoori de tole de veiŋa kam.
6Vio yeini ko dole ko vei kuri seeni,
ye ko ta dole ko vei baŋa seeni.
Vio kom nam ta vei yiga de kwaga mo
ko kare ko vei konto mo taa.
7Bu-tole sem maama duri se vei
se lwoi se na bam naneo kom wone mo,
ye naneo kom ba fɔge ko sui ko wɛɛla.
Na bam daa maa yeini ba jwoori mo,
ba vei bu-tole sem na buri mɛ to.
8Woŋo maama yeini ko ke konto dwoŋi mo
ye kweelim tera.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o ta ko kuri o ti.
Nabiinu yia bá wane woŋo maama ya nii ya su.
O zwa de nam bá wane ya cheigi wonnu maama ya su.
9Wo-doŋo tera logo baŋa ne.
Kolo na maŋe ko wora to mo ta wó taa wora taa.
Kikia yalo déem na ke to mo ta wó jwoori ya ke.
10Woŋo kolo nɔɔna ná tɛ ko taane we,
“Nii-na, wo-doŋo mo tento!”
konto woŋo kom maŋe ko wora mo faŋa faŋa,
ye ba wo loge debam.
11Dé daa ba gula balo ya na wora faŋa kam ne to gula.
Ko nam ná ye balo ba jwa na wó lo to,
balo na tu banto kwaga ne to wó swei ba de swia.
Amo na lɔre chega kalo to
12Amo wolo na ye Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno to déem di Isarele tiina paare Jerusalem ne. 13Amo seene a yia mo se a tɔge swa chwoŋa a ma zamese a daare a buŋi wonnu telo maama na jege te ke logo baŋa ne to, se a wane te kuri a lɔre. Amo nɛ we totoŋa yalo Wɛ na pɛ nabiina se ba taa toŋe to tiini ko chana ko pa-ba. 14Amo nam maane wonnu telo maama na jege te ke logo baŋa ne to. Nii-na! Te maama chana se dé lɔre te kuri mo. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja-ko tei to mo.
15Woŋo kolo ná gugwoli,
ko tweem chamma mo.
Wonnu telo maa na tera to
ware se nɔɔno jeeli te ni.
16Amo nam ya tage a tete ne a we, “Nii mo! Amo tiini a jege yi-poro a dwoi balo na maŋe ba di paare Jerusalem ne to maama. A ma jwoŋi swa de yeino dedɛ.” 17Amo seene a yia mo se a lɔre swa, se a ta lɔre jworim de chichwooru na ye tei to. A tu a maane we konto maama de nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja-ko tei to mo.
18Nɔɔno yi-poro na mae tei to,
o lwia de mae konto mo.
O yeino ná daga tei,
o wo-chechɔgɔ de wó taa daga konto dwoŋi mo.

english_text:
It Is Senseless To Be Selfish
1I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense. 2Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do? 3I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
4 I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards. 5I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees. 6And I had pools where I could get water for the trees. 7 I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem. 8 Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
9 I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise. 10I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work. 11Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble.
Wisdom Comes from God
12I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity. 13And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness. 14Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
15Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense. 16Wise or foolish, we all die and are soon forgotten.” 17This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
18Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all. 19Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
20I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed. 21When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong. 22What do we really gain from all of our hard work? 23 Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
24 The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us, 25and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do. 26 If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Wo-loŋo jege nyɔɔre na?
1Amo laam ma ta a tete ne we, “Amo wó ke kwɛɛra yɔɔ se a maŋe-te a nii, te seene te lana na?” Tɔ. A ma na we konto ba jege kuri. 2A ta maane we mwanno ye jworim mo. Kwɛɛra de ba jege nyɔɔre. 3A laam ma zo sa-nyɔre wone se a nyɔ a su a na wopwolo. A maa lage se a tɔge swa ŋwaane a boŋe a nii chwoŋa kɔ mo jege nyɔɔre se nɔɔna taa tɔge-ka ba logo baŋa ŋwea wone.
4Amo déem ke totoŋ-zana yadwonna a pa a tete. A lɔge sam, ye a jeiri Vini teeni de. 5A ta ma che gaara ye a jeiri dwo-vɔɔro, de ga-punnu, de teeni delo na leiri bia dwi dwi to ya wone. 6A ma ko buli se ba taa mɔɔne na da ba yage teeni dem se de be lanyerane. 7Amo nam ta yeigi kabɛ, baara de kaana, ye ba de lo ba bia a sɔŋɔ wone pa se ba ji amo nyem. A ta ma na naane, de pei, de bone kɔgɔ kɔgɔ se a taa tei. Ko ná ye balo maama na lwoori yiga ba zoore Jerusalem ne ba daare amo to, a vara bam daga ba dwoi banto nyem. 8A ma na lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa dedɛ a pa a tete. A déem jwoŋi jejegero teene delo de kateira yalo a na tei to pwa bam tei ne. A déem pɛ se baara de kaana taa wo a tei ne ba leeni lei se ko taa ywomma ko pa-ne. Ko maa ná ye kaana, amo yɔɔre a jege-ba mo ne ko na wó pa nabiina di ywoni dedɛ tei to. 9Ko ná ye balo dwi maama na lwoori yiga ba zoore Jerusalem wone ba daare amo to, ba wolowolo wo yi amo kamunni dem. De konto maama de, a ta tɔge swa chwoŋa kam mo.
10Kolo maama amo yi na page
ko baŋa ne to mo
a yeini a jwoŋi se a nii
ko na ye tei to.
A boboŋa ná jaane se a beeri
ywoni delo maama,
amo yeini a tɔge de kwaga mo.
Amo yi ma su a na toŋe
a na kolo maama to,
pa se a na nyɔɔre
a totoŋa yam baŋa ne.
11A laam ma jeini a jeeli
a kikia maama,
dedaane a totoŋ-chɛɛra
na pɛ-ne kolo maama to.
A ma na we te ba jege kuri.
Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri
o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo.
A totoŋa yam maama ba jege nyɔɔre
tega kam baŋa ne.
Swa de jworim taane
12Amo ta ma jeeli se a nii swa na ye tei to chekke, se a daare a lɔre jworim de yiyiri kikia na ye tei to. Kokuri to, wolo na tu o di paare to jege se o tɔge pwa balo na lwoori‑o to chwoŋa kam mo. 13Amo nam tu a maane we swa jege nyɔɔre ya dwoi jworim, se ko maŋe de pwooni na gare lim tei to. 14Chega to,
Swa tu yia wae ya na chwoŋa.
Jworo maa wo lim wone o via.
De ko maama de, a maane we swa tiina de jworru lage ba guri bedwe mo. 15Amo laam ma ta a tete ne we, “Toone na wó ja jworo to, de lage de ba amo de baŋa mo. Bɛ nyɔɔre mo a nam nɛ a swa yam baŋa ne?” A ma leiri a tete ne we, “Amo bá wane a lɔre ko kuri”.
16Swa tu dedaane jworo maama jege se ba te mo. Ba ná tega, nɔɔna daa bá taa guli ba gula taa. Jwa seeni ba wó swei debam maama swia. 17Konto pɛ se a ŋwea kam ji wo-chɛɔ ka pa-ne. Chanɛɛre yerane mo tu a baŋa de kolo maama na yeini ko ke tega baŋa ne to. Ko maama ba jege kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo.
Totoŋ-chɛɛra taane
18A na tu a maane we a jege se a yage kolo maama a na toŋe a na to a pa wolo na wó saŋe amo kwaga to, ko ma pa se totoŋ-chɛɛra yalo maama a na toŋe tega baŋa ne to ji wo-chɛɔ ya pa-ne. 19A nam ware se a lɔre konto tu wó taa ye swa tu mo naa jworo mo. O laam maa wó ba o jwoŋi kolo maama a totoŋ-chɛɛra de a swa na jaane te ba te pa-ne to, o taa tei. Ko maama ba jege kuri. 20Amo na jeini a jeeli a totoŋ-chɛɛra yam maama na wó pa-ne nyɔɔre delo to, a wo pɛ ya ŋwaane. 21Kokuri to, dé wó kwei dé swa, de dé yeino, de dé boboŋa maama, dé toŋe taa se dé na wonnu. Bɛ laam nam mo tei se dé yage-te dé pa wolo na wo yaare te ŋwaane to? Ko maama ba jege kuri, se ko ye lɛɛro yerane mo. 22Logo baŋa ŋwea wone, nabiinu wó toŋe taa, ye o jei de lwia mo. O nam lage o na bɛ nyɔɔre mo ko baŋa ne? 23Dɛ maama wone, dé totoŋa yeini ya ni debam ye lwia daane debam ya ŋwaane. Tete ne de, dé boboŋa maa kare ya beera. Ko maama ba jege kuri.
24Kolo na tiini ko lamma ko pae nɔɔno to mo ye se o taa di wodiu, ye o nyɔa, se o daare o di ywoni o totoŋa yam baŋa ne. Amo nam maane we tento maama nwoŋi Wɛ tei ne mo. 25Kokuri to, Wɛ ná wo woli, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware o na wodiu naa ywoni se o di. 26Ko ná ye nɔɔno wolo na ke o sui Wɛ yi to, Wɛ pae kotu swa, de yeino, de wopwolo mo. Ko daare, wɛleere-keira toŋe ba tiŋi se ba laam kwei ba pa balo kikia na sui Wɛ yi to mo. Konto de ba jege kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo.

english_text:
Everything Has Its Time
1Everything on earth
has its own time
and its own season.
2There is a time
for birth and death,
planting and reaping,
3for killing and healing,
destroying and building,
4for crying and laughing,
weeping and dancing,
5for throwing stones
and gathering stones,
embracing and parting.
6There is a time
for finding and losing,
keeping and giving,
7for tearing and sewing,
listening and speaking.
8There is also a time
for love and hate,
for war and peace.
What God Has Given Us To Do
9What do we gain by all our hard work? 10I have seen what difficult things God demands of us. 11God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future. 12I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life, 13because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do. 14Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
15Everything that happens
has happened before,
and all that will be
has already been—
God does everything
over and over again.
The Future Is Known Only to God
16Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice. 17So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good. 18I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals. 19Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense. 20All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth. 21Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth? 22We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.
translation_text:
Woŋo maama jege ko maŋa
1Woŋo maama logo baŋa ne
jege ko maŋa mo.
Maŋa tigi mo se dé toŋe
totoŋe dwi maama.
2Maŋa wora ba na wó lo nɔɔno,
ye maŋa de wora kotu na wó te.
Jeirim maŋa maa wora
ye ka-gɔ-ka-yage maŋa de wora.
3Maŋa wora se ba go nɔɔna,
ye maŋa wora se ba yɔɔre nɔɔna.
Ka-ja-ka-chɔge maŋa maa wora,
ye ka-lɔ-ka-zege maŋa de wora.
4Wo-chechɔgɔ maŋa mo wora,
ye mwanno maŋa de wora.
Maŋa tigi mo keira ŋwaane,
ye kadwoŋi de tiga wopwolo kwɛɛra ŋwaane.
5Maŋa wora mo se ba dole kandwa ba jage ba yage.
Maŋa de maa wora se ba tigisi-ya ba ke daane.
Maŋa nam mo wora se nɔɔna kukwori daane,
ye maŋa de wora se ba taa lɔŋe daane.
6Maŋa mo wora se nɔɔno beeri o na woŋo.
Maŋa ta maa wora se o ga kolo o na jege to.
Maŋa wora se dé kwaleme wonnu,
ye maŋa de wora se dé dole kolo dé na jege to dé yage.
7Maŋa wora se dé kaare gwaaro dé yage,
ye maŋa de wora se dé nyaane-te dé ke daane.
Maŋa wora ka pa nɔɔno se o taa ye chemm,
ye maŋa wora se kotu ŋɔɔne.
8Maŋa ta wora mo se nɔɔna taa swoi daane,
ye kadwoŋi de wora se ba taa chuli daane.
Jara-keim maŋa maa wora,
ye bochare-zuru maŋa de wora.
9Nɔɔna ná tiini ba toŋe tei, bɛ nyɔɔre mo ba nam nae ko baŋa ne?
Bɛ nyɔɔre mo dé wó na dé ŋwea wone?
10Amo maane Wɛ na kwei totoŋa yalo o pa nabiina se ba taa toŋe to. 11Wɛ maa pae se wonnu maama ke lanyerane te maŋa ne chekke. O ma kwei boboŋa yalo na vei taa wuu seeni to o ke nabiina yuu ne. Konto maama wone nam, dé bá wane dé lɔre o na jege kolo o ke to maama dé ti. 12Amo ma maane we kolo na lamma ko pae nɔɔna to ye se ba taa jege wopwolo ye ba tɔge chwo-laaro ba ŋwea wone mo. 13Ko maŋe se ba taa di wodiu, ye ba nyɔa, se ba daare ba di ywoni ba totoŋa yam baŋa ne. Konto maama ye Wɛ pɛɛre mo.
14Amo maane we Wɛ na ke wonnu telo maama to wora mo taa. Dé bá wane dé woli kolokolo o kikia yam wone, naa dé le kolokolo ya wone dé yage. O pɛ se ko taa ye konto mo se dé taa kɔre‑o. 15Kolo zem na wora to maŋe ko ke maŋa kadwoŋi ne. Kolo na lage ko ke jwa ne to de maŋe ko wora mo. Wɛ maa beeri wonnu telo na maŋe te ke te kɛ to se o pa te jwoori te ke.
Nabiina de vara ye bedwe mo na?
16Kolo na woli da to, amo maane ko na ye tei tega baŋa ne to we, chega borem na jege se de taa wo mɛ to, lwarem mo wo dáane. Chwo-balwaaro mo leiri chwo-laaro yuu ne. 17Amo ma ta a tete ne we, “Maŋa ná yia, Wɛ wó di nɔn-ŋona dedaane puseŋ-nyena maama taane, o na maŋe o tiŋi dɛ mo se wonnu maama de kikia maama ke te maŋa ne to ŋwaane.” 18A ta ma ta nabiina taane a tete ne we, “Wɛ yeini o faŋe debam mo o nii, se o pa dé lɔre we debam de vara bam ba gare daane. 19Kokuri to, debam nabiina de vara maama guri bedwe mo. Toone yeini de tui de jaane dé maama. Nabiina de vara siu ye bedwe mo. Konto to, nabiina ba gare vara. Chega to, ko maama ba jege kuri. 20Wonnu maama ŋwe ye te guri bedwe mo. Kolo maama na ŋwe to nwoŋi tega kam teero wone mo, ye te maama nam wó jwoori te zo teero wone. 21Wɔ mo wane o lɔre chekke we nabiina ná tega, ba diini wɛɛne mo, ko daare ye vara ná tega ba zoore tega kam kuri ne?”
22Konto maama wone amo maane we kolo na tiini ko lana se dé ke to ye se dé di ywoni mo dé totoŋa baŋa ne. Mo nyɔɔre delo Wɛ na pae debam to. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na wó pa dé lɔre kolo na wora jwa seeni to.

english_text:
1I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful. 2I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living. 3But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
4Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
5Fools will fold their hands
and starve to death.
6Yet a very little food
eaten in peace
is better than twice as much
earned from overwork
and chasing the wind.
7Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense. 8For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life!
It Is Better To Have a Friend
9You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn. 10If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble. 11If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night. 12Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
13You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice. 14Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king. 15I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone. 16His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Bɛɛsem de yaara taane
1Amo daa ta ma maane nabwona na tiini ba nae bɛɛsem logo baŋa jei maama ne tei to. Ba maa keeri bugi-bugi ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na wó wane o woli-ba pa se ba wo to. Balo na jege-ba ba bɛɛse to tiini ba dana lanyerane mo. Konto ŋwaane nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se o pa nabwona bam bochare zuri. 2Amo laam maa boŋe we, balo na tega ye ba daa tera to gare balo ta na ŋwe ye ba yaare to. 3Ko nam ná ye chega, balo ba ta na wo loge to yuu mo ywomma ba dwoi maama, kolo ŋwaane banto ta wo nɛ lwarem kikia yalo na kare ya ke logo baŋa ne to.
4Amo ta maane we nɔɔna na yeini ba ma dam de yeino ba toŋe tei to maama ye ba dwoni daane mo. Ko maama ba jege kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo.
5Ko ná ye jworru,
ba yeini ba vɔ ba jea totoŋa baŋa ne mo.
Kana nam mo wó go-ba.
6Nɔɔno nam ná nɛ o wodiu bɔŋa dedoa
ye o bochare zuri,
konto gare o ná yaare de totoŋ-chɛɛra
se o na bwɛ selei.
Konto maama nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo.
Badwoŋo taane
7Amo daa ta ma maane woŋo kodwoŋi logo baŋa ne ko na ba jege kuri. 8Amo nɛ we nɔɔno wodwoŋi wora o na ba jege fara, naa chorro, naa bia, ye o laam toŋe taa o ba jeini tega ne. O toŋe mo se o na jejegero ye o yi ba sui-te. Wonto nam jege se o bwei o tete we, “Wɔ mo lage o na nyɔɔre a totoŋ-chɛɛra yam baŋa ne? Amo ba di ywoni ya ŋwaane.” Konto maama de ba jege kuri. Cham yerane mo wora kotu ŋwea wone.
9Balei gare dedoa.
Kokuri, ba wó na nyɔɔre da-tei ne
ba totoŋa yam baŋa ne.
10Ba wone dedoa ná toa,
wodwoŋi wom wó ja‑o
se o zaŋe wɛɛne.
Se ko ná ye nɔɔno dedoa o yerane ye o to,
lɛɛro mo wó yi kotu,
o dwoŋi na tera se o woli‑o
se o zaŋe to ŋwaane.
11Ko ta woli da, nɔɔna balei ná kukwori daane,
ba yera wulim wó mage daane
se waaro yé yi-ba.
Nɔɔno nam ná ye o yerane,
o lage o ke tɛ mo o che o waaro?
12Nɔɔno dedoa wae o mage
o dwoŋi wolo na zaŋe
o baŋa ne to o di.
Ko nam ná ye nɔɔna balei mo
jaŋe ded‑o,
o yerane bá wane o mage-ba o di.
Ŋona kalo na ŋoge kuni betɔ to ba kɔe mɔle-mɔle.
Swa de paare taane
13Nɔn-doŋo ná ye yiniga tu ye o jege swa, wonto gare pa-dwooru wolo na ve se nɔɔna bere‑o to. 14Nɔn-doŋo kom wae o nwoŋi peena diga ne ye o laam ba o di paare, naa ba loge‑o yiniga wone o paare laŋa kam ne ye o daare o ji pɛ. 15Amo ta ma maane nɔɔna balo maama na ŋwe logo baŋa ne to na kare ba ke tei ye ba pɛ nɔn-doŋo wodwoŋi kwaga ba pu. Wonto lage o ba o jeini pa-dwooru wom jeiŋa jei ne mo. 16Nɔn-kɔgɔ kolo na tɔge wonto kwaga to tiini ko daga ko gaale. Ba kwaga kam nam ná tua, ba wolowolo bá nege‑o. Ko maama de ba jege kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo.

english_text:
Be Careful How You Worship
1Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship. 2Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much. 3If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
4 God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God. 5It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it. 6Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
7Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
8Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do. 9And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
10If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense. 11The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you. 12If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
13I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good. 14Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children. 15 They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work. 16That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind. 17Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
18What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do. 19Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you. 20God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_text:
Ta‑n yei n na zuli Wɛ tei to
1Nmo ná yeini n ma‑n zoore Wɛ diga se n zuli‑o, se n ja n tete. Fɔɔre n yi Wɛ tei se n cheigi o taane, se konto wó taa gare kaanem delo jworru na ke ye ba yeiri we ba tusi to. 2Boŋe n yi se n laam ŋɔɔne n ni taane. Yé gwoni ni de Wɛ yɔɔ yɔɔ ye n wo fɔge n boŋe de wone. Lɔre lanyerane we Wɛ wo telaao ne mo ye nmo zoore tega kam baŋa ne. Konto ŋwaane nam pa se n ni taane dem taa ye fenfee yerane. 3Boboŋ-fara pae se nɔɔno dwɛ dendwea ye ya daane‑o mo. Konto dwoŋi mo ta-fare dedɛ pae se nɔɔno tɛ wo-jworru.
4Nmo nam ná gwoni ni de Wɛ, se n ke lela n kwei-de. Wɛ ba lage jworru ni taane. Konto ŋwaane, yɔɔre n kwei ni delo n na gwoni to. 5Nmo ná wo gwoni ni se n ke woŋo, konto gare n ná tiŋi ni ye n laam kwane-de. 6Yé pa se n ni taane ja‑m de zo wɛleere wone. Ta‑n cho n tete se n yé ta de Wɛ tontoŋeno we, “Amo wo maane mo ye a ta tento.” Kokuri to, Wɛ bane wae de zaŋe nmo baŋa ne n ŋɔŋa kam ŋwaane ye o daare o saare n totoŋa yam maama.
7Dendwea dwi dwi wora. Boboŋ-yɔɔro de taana daga dedɛ. Nmo nam jege se n ta‑n kɔre Wɛ mo.
Bɛɛsem taane
8Nmo ná nɛ we chega ti teo kolo wone, ye ko dedɛɛra jege nabwona ba bɛɛsa pa se ba ware ba tete se ba jwoŋi, se n yé pa se ko so‑m. Ko nam na ye tei to, dedɛɛro maama jege o yiga tu na nii‑o to. Ko daare ye yiga tu maama de jege o yuu tu. 9Ko ya maŋe se nɔɔno maama na nyɔɔre tega kam baŋa ne. Pɛ wom tete jege se o nii kare sem baŋa ne.
Jejegero taane
10Nɔɔno ná tiini o lage sabu, kotu yi ba fɔge de sui de o na jege kolo to. Nɔɔno fera ná zo jejegero wone, o ŋweero ba yi‑o. Ko maama ba jege kuri. 11Nɔɔno jejegero na mae tei to, balo na jwoŋi te wone se ba di to de gaale konto mo. Kotu na nɛ nyɔɔre delo o jejegero baŋa ne to mo ye o yi na nɛ-te to yerane. 12Tontoŋena ná toŋe taa ba ti, ye ba ná di wodi-fɔrɔ naa fenfee yerane, ba laam wae ba dɔ lanyerane tete ne. Ko nam ná ye naduna, ba ba yeini ba dɔ, ba jejegero tem boboŋa na daane-ba to ŋwaane.
13Amo nam ta maane wo-chɛɔ kodwoŋi mo logo baŋa ne. Nadum mo ke o jejegero o ke daane pa se te wae te che‑o cham wone. 14O jejegero tem laam ma jei wo-chɛɔ baŋa ne. O na loge bu wolo to daa ta wo nɛ woŋo se o taa tei. 15Ba ná loge bu wolo maama, kotu nwoŋi o nu wone bwori mo. O ŋwea ná tu ka kweeli, o daa ta wó yage logo baŋa bwori mo. O ná maŋe o toŋe tei maama, o bá ja kolokolo o woli da o kɛ. 16Tento maama yɔɔre te ye wo-chɛɔ mo! Nɔɔno na tu logo baŋa wone tei to, konto mo o jege se o yage-ko. Bɛ nyɔɔre mo o lage o na o totoŋa maama baŋa ne, de o na toŋe se o jwoŋi vio yerane to ŋwaane? 17O ŋwea maama wone, lim dedaane wo-chechɔgɔ mo tɔge‑o. O maa yɔɔre o nae ban-zɔŋɔ, de jaweero, dedaane ni-kantɔgɔ yerane.
Ywoni dim taane
18Amo nam maane we ko lamma se dé taa di wodiu, ye dé nyɔa, se dé daare dé di ywoni dé totoŋ-chɛɛra yam dé na ke dé logo baŋa ŋwea kam wone to baŋa ne. Mo nyɔɔre delo Wɛ na pae debam to. 19Ko ta ná ye Wɛ na pae balo dum de jejegero to, o ta pa-ba pwola se ba di ywoni te baŋa ne, se ba jwoŋi ba ŋweero tem konto ye ba toŋe ba totoŋ-chɛɛra yam de wopwolo. Konto maama ye Wɛ pɛɛre mo. 20Nɔɔno nam ba jege se o fɔge o jeeli o ŋwea da yam na ye tei to, Wɛ na pae o yɔɔre o na wopwolo o totoŋa yam baŋa ne to ŋwaane.

english_text:
Don't Depend on Wealth
1There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth. 2God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
3You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial. 4-5That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you, 6even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
7We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied. 8We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right. 9It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
10Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us. 11The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk? 12Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_text:
Jejegero pae ywoni na?
1Amo nam ta maane wo-chɛɔ kodwoŋi mo logo baŋa ne, ye ko daane nabiina jei maama ne. 2Wɛ wae o pa nɔɔno dum, de jejegero, de zula, pa se kotu jege kolo maama na jege o fera to, ye o wae o vane kotu chwoŋa se o yé di-te. Nɔn-gaa mo wó ba o di te ywoni. Konto maama tiini ko ye wo-chɛɔ. A bá wane a lɔre ko kuri.
3Nenɛɛne nɔɔno ná kwe o ja gaale ye o lo bia bi, kotu ná maŋe o ŋwe taa, ye o ná wo di ywoni o jejegero tem baŋa ne, bu-too wolo ba na loge zem to ta gare‑o. 4Kokuri to, ba ná loge bu-too, dé bá wane dé lɔre ko kuri. O tua ye o daare o jwoori lela. O yere maŋe de wo bwoŋi. 5Bu wom konto ta wo fɔge o na wea pwooni. O nam wo lɔre ŋwea na ye tei to. De konto de, o ta nɛ siu o dwoni nadum wom konto, 6ko fɔge ko dae nɔɔno wom ŋwea ná yi bena morro telei ye o wo di ka ywoni. Ba maama kweelim ye bedwe mo. Ko dae konto na?
7Nabiina totoŋa maama yɔɔre ya ye ba ni-wodiu ŋwaane mo. Ba nam ba fɔge ba nae se ko yi-ba. 8Swa tu wó na nyɔɔre o dwoni jworo na? Nabwom de ná yei o na wó taa jaane o tete nɔɔna yia ne tei to, bɛ nyɔɔre mo o jega?
9“Nɔɔno yi ná su de kolo maama
o na jege to,
konto gare o ná pɛ se o fera
zo wo-gaa wone.”
Konto de chana se dé lɔre ko kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja-ko tei to mo.
10Kolo maama zem na wora to mo, Wɛ maŋe o tigisi-ko se ko taa jege ko yere. Nabiinu de yei o ŋwea chwoŋa na ye tei to. O bá wane o dwoni de wolo na dana o dwoi‑o to. 11Kolo ŋwaane, nɔɔno ná tiini o ŋɔɔne dedɛ, vuvuga wó tiini ka tɔge da mo. Bɛ nyɔɔre mo o lage o na o ŋɔŋa kam baŋa ne? 12Kokuri to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno yeiri kolo na wó taa lana ko pa nabiina ba ŋwea wone, ba ŋwea kam na ye kukua tei to ŋwaane. Ka ta nye de nɔɔno lunluŋu mo na bá dáane ye ka jei to. Dé bá wane dé lɔre ka kuri. Chega to, wɔ mo wó wane o bere debam kolo na wó ke dé toone kwaga ne to?

english_text:
The Best in Life
1 A good reputation
at the time of death
is better than loving care
at the time of birth.
2It's better to go to a funeral
than to attend a feast;
funerals remind us
that we all must die.
3Choose sorrow over laughter
because a sad face
may hide a happy heart.
4A sensible person mourns,
but fools always laugh.
5Correction from someone wise
is better by far
than praise from fools.
6Foolish laughter is stupid.
It sounds like thorns
crackling in a fire.
7Corruption makes fools
of sensible people,
and bribes can ruin you.
8Something completed is better
than something just begun;
patience is better
than too much pride.
9 Only fools get angry quickly
and hold a grudge.
10It isn't wise to ask,
“Why is everything worse
than it used to be?”
11Having wisdom is better
than an inheritance.
12Wisdom will protect you
just like money;
knowledge with good sense
will lead you to life.
13Think of what God has done!
If God makes something crooked,
can you make it straight?
14When times are good,
you should be cheerful;
when times are bad,
think about what it means.
God makes them both
to keep us from knowing
what will happen next.
Some of Life's Questions
15I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper. 16So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart! 17Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool. 18Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
19Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
20No one in this world always does right.
21Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you. 22Haven't you cursed many others?
23I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me. 24The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep. 25So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
26Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for. 27With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together, 28but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman. 29I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_text:
Bɛ mo lana ko pae nabiina?
1Nɔɔno ná beeri yere-ŋom,
konto lana ko pa‑o
ko gare terale nuga na tiini ka lana to.
Nabiinu toone dɛ maa gare
o lora dɛ dem.
2Nmo nam ná vei lua sɔŋɔ,
konto lana ko pa‑m
ko gare n ná vei sɔŋɔ kolo wone
ba na di kuri to.
Toone maa ye nɔɔno maama gurim jei.
Ko maŋe se balo ta na ŋwe to
yé swei toone ni ne.
3Nmo wo ná chɔge,
konto gare n ná su de mwanno.
Kokuri to, yi-nyɔna wae ya pae
n bochare mo fɔge lanyerane.
4Swa tu yeini o boŋe lua boboŋa mo.
Jworo fera nam zoore jei selo
mwanno na wo mɛ to wone mo.
5Nmo ná sɛ swa tu na bwɛ nmo tei to,
konto lana ko pa‑m
ko gare nɔn-jworru na wo n tei ne,
ye ba leeni ba seini nmo.
6Jworo ná puri mwanno,
ko nye de sabare na to mini wone
ye se parese yɔɔ tei to mo.
Konto de ba jege kuri.
7Swa tu ná jigi kampin-nyeno,
o de laam ye jworo mo.
Nɔɔno wolo maa ná jwoŋi dim,
kotu keim dem wó chɔge o boboŋa mo.
8Totoŋe gurim mo gare
de pulim jei.
Nɔɔno ná wae o jaane o tete bochare,
konto gare o ná bere o tete kamunim.
9Kwaane se n ta‑n wae
n bane n jaana.
Balo na pae se ba ban-lom dáane to
ye nɔn-jworru mo.
10Yé zaŋe n bwei nenɛɛne,
“Bɛ mo ke ye faŋa kam gare leile?”
Bwia yam konto nam ba tɔge
swa boboŋa!
11Swa mo lana ya pae nɔɔno,
nenɛɛne o kwo na tiŋi jejegero telo se o pa‑o to.
Swa jege nyɔɔre ya pae
balo maama na ŋwe to.
12Swa wó pa n na woro mo
se kolokolo yé yi‑m,
nenɛɛne sabu de na kwoli nɔɔno kuri tei to.
Nmo nam ná lɔre swa,
ko tiini ko jege nyɔɔre mo ko pa‑m,
nmo na wó fɔge n na ŋwea
ko baŋa ne to ŋwaane.
13Nam maane Wɛ na ke tei maama to n nii!
Wɛ ná pɛ se woŋo kolo gugwoli,
wɔ mo wó wane o twe-ko?
14Wonnu ná tɔge chwo-laao te pa‑m,
se n ta‑n jege wopwolo.
Te nam daa ná vei gweeni,
se n maane we Wɛ mo pae
se lanyerane de cham tui,
pa se nabiina yeiri kolo jwa
na wó ke ko pa-ba to.
Amo bá wane a lɔre wonnu kuri a ti
15Amo maane wonnu dwi dwi dedɛ a ŋwea wone, ye a lɔre te kuri a ga. Nɔn-ŋom wora ye o wuuri o te de o na maŋe o tɔge chega tei to. Nɔn-balɔrɔ de maa wora o na yɔɔre o kwe o ja gaale ye o ta toŋe lwarem. 16Yé tiini n bere n tete we n ye nɔn-ŋom, naa n bere n swa de. Nmo boŋe se n chɔge n tete mo na? 17Nmo ta yé yɔɔre n ta‑n ke lwarem, naa se n ta‑n toŋe jworim. Nmo boŋe se n wuuri n te mo na? 18Ko nam lana se n tɔge chwei selei sem konto. Kokuri to, nmo ná kɔre Wɛ n wonnu wó kwɛ mo se maama wone.
19Swa tu yeini o nae dam o swa ŋwaane, se ko dwoni dedɛɛra fuga na nii ba teo baŋa ne.
20Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera logo baŋa jei maama ne o na yɔɔre o ke chega, ye o ba fɔge o tusa.
21Yé yɔɔre n sɛ kolo maama nɔɔna na wó ta to. N wae n ni we n tontoŋeno mo jege‑m o twea. 22Kokuri to, nmo tete yei we n maŋe n twi n dwonna kuni dedɛ mo.
23Amo ma kwaane se a tɔge swa ŋwaane a lɔre wonnu tem konto maama na ye tei to. A boboŋa ma ja se a jwoŋi swa. Amo nam maane we ko kuri chana ko dwoi se a lɔre. 24Woŋo kolo maama na wora to kuri nim tiini ko chana mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o lɔre te kuri.
25Amo boboŋa laam ma ja se a zamese yeino ye a buŋi wonnu wone a nii se a ja swa, se a wane a lɔre wonnu na ye tei to. Amo ta maa lage se a lɔre bɛŋwaane mo lwarem kikia ye jworim yerane, ye jworim kikia de jege yiyirim. 26Amo nam ta maane we, kaane wolo na lage o ja‑m ne o ye kalanchogo to mo chana o dwoi toone. O maa kwaane o kukwori‑m ne o na kwei chegero o ma vɔ‑m tei to. Balo nam na ke ba sui Wɛ yi to wó lu o jeŋa ne. O nam wó yɔɔre o ja wɛleere-keira mo.
27Amo wolo na ye Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno to we, “Nii-na amo na buŋi wonnu wone mo fee fee se a laam ba a lɔre wonnu na ye tei to. 28A nam na kwaane a beeri maama to, a gɛ ko ŋwa mo. Amo na beeri baara moro tetare ne to, mo a nɛ baaro dedoa na tɔge chega. Ko daare a wo nɛ kaane banto maama wone, de dedoa de! 29Woŋo kolo yerane amo na tu a lɔre mo tento: Wɛ ke nabiina pa se ba yɔɔre ba tɔge chwoŋa mo. Ba laam nam mo pɛ se vuvuga tui.”

english_text:
1Who is smart enough
to explain everything?
Wisdom makes you cheerful
and gives you a smile.
Obey the King
2If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise. 3Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind. 4The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?” 5If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it. 6Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything, 7though no one can tell the future. 8We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil. 9I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another?
Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
10I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense. 11When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime. 12They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying:
Everyone who lives right
and respects God
will prosper,
13but no one who sins
and rejects God
will prosper or live very long.
14There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens. 15So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
16Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world. 17I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_text:
Sɛ pɛ wom ni taane
1Wɔ mo seene o ye swa tu chekke?
Wɔ mo wae wonnu kuri o lɔra?
Swa pae se nɔɔno yiga pwoli mo,
ye yi-nyɔna daa ba jege‑o.
2Ta‑n yei se n sɛ Pɛ wom ni, nmo na gwoni ni Wɛ yiga ne mo we, n wó ke konto to ŋwaane. 3Yé wuuri n nwoŋi da Pɛ wom tei ne. Yé tɔge de balo na boŋe se ba nwoŋi o kwaga ne to, Pɛ wom na wae o ke kolo maama o na lage to ŋwaane. 4Kokuri to, Pɛ wom ni taane tiini de jege dam mo ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware se o bwei‑o we, “Bɛ mo ye n ke konto?” 5Wolo nam ná toŋe o tɔge Pɛ wom ni, konto tu bá zo cham wone. Swa tu yeini o lɔre maŋa kalo na maŋe keim, dedaane chwoŋa kalo keim dem na wó tɔge to mo.
6Kokuri to, woŋo maama
jege ko maŋa mo,
ye ko de jege ko chwoŋa mo
se ko toŋe.
Lɛɛro nam yeini te tui nabiina baŋa.
7Dé bá wane dé lɔre kolo
na wó ke to chekke,
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa tera se o ta
jwa na wó taa ye tei to
o bere debam.
8Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware vio se o ja.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware o toone dɛ dem se o che.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware se o le o tete jara keim wone.
Nmo ná toŋe lwarem kikia,
ya bá wane ya jwoŋi‑m ya yage.
9Amo na seene a yia a zamese wonnu tem konto maama to, mo a maane kolo maama na jege ko ke logo baŋa ne to. A ma na we maŋa de maŋa nɔɔno wae o tei o dwonna de dam pa se ba maama yaare.
Dé ware dé lɔre Wɛ chwei sem
10A ta nɛ puseŋ-nyena na tege ye ba suli-ba de zula to. Banto ya yeini ba vei Wɛ wara-jei sem, ye nɔɔna tei-ba teo kolo wone ba na ke ba puseŋa kikia da to. Ko maama ba jege kuri. 11Nɔɔna nam ná yeini ba ke lwarem ye ba wo waare-ba lela, konto pa se nabiina yɔɔre ba lage se ba de taa toŋe lwarem kikia mo. 12Chega to, wɛleere-keira wó wane ba toŋe lwarem kuni bi mo ye ba ta yɔɔre ba kwe ba ja gaale. Amo nam yei we, “Nmo ná kɔre Wɛ, wonnu wó yɔɔre chwoŋa te pa‑m, nmo na zuli‑o to ŋwaane.” 13Amo ta yei we, “Puseŋ-nyena wonnu bá da chwoŋa. Ba ŋwea nye de nɔɔno lunluŋu na bá dáane ye ko jei to mo. Banto bá kwe ba kɛ, ba na ba kɔre Wɛ to ŋwaane.”
14Woŋo kodwoŋi maa wora logo baŋa ne ye a bá wane a lɔre ko kuri. A maane we nɔn-ŋona wora ye ko ke-ba nenɛɛne ba ga ye nɔn-balwaaro mo tei. Ko ta daare ye ko ke nɔn-balwaaro nenɛɛne ko ya na maŋe se nɔn-ŋona na tei to mo. Amo tei ne, konto maama ba jege kuri.
Ywoni dim taane
15Amo nam wó ta we, dé jege se dé di ywoni mo dé ŋwea kanto wone. Kolokolo daa tera logo baŋa ne ko na lana ko pae nabiina to, ko ná dae dé na wó taa di wodiu, ye dé nyɔa, ye dé di ywoni to yerane. Nɔɔno ná ke konto mo ye o toŋe o totoŋa, ko wó woli‑o o ŋwea wone, ne Wɛ na pɛ se o taa ye tei logo baŋa ne to.
16Amo seene a yia mo se a lɔre swa chekke na ye tei to, se a daare a maane totoŋe delo maama na jege de ke logo baŋa ne to. Dɔɔm maa ba tui a yia ne, wea dedaane tete maama ne. 17Amo laam ma maane Wɛ na ke tei to maama. Nɔɔno ná maŋe o kwaane tei maama se o ni ko kuri, o bá lɔre kolo maama na ke logo baŋa ne to kuri. O ná maŋe o ye swa tu ye o bere we o yei ko kuri, o nam ta yeiri.

english_text:
One Day at a Time
1I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad. 2But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
3It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die. 4As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion. 5We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten. 6Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
7So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do. 8Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best. 9Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth. 10Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
11Here is something else I have learned:
The fastest runners
and the greatest heroes
don't always win races
and battles.
Wisdom, intelligence, and skill
don't always make you healthy,
rich, or popular.
We each have our own share
of misfortune.
12None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap.
Better To Be Wise than Foolish
13Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me. 14It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls. 15But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten. 16So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
17Words of wisdom spoken softly
make much more sense
than the shouts of a ruler
to a crowd of fools.
18Wisdom is more powerful
than weapons,
yet one mistake can destroy
all the good you have done.
translation_text:
Nɔɔno maama gurim jei ye bedwe
1Amo nam seene yia a boŋe wonnu tento maama wone se a lɔre te na ye tei to. A ma lɔre we nɔn-ŋona de swa tiina de ba kikia maama wo Wɛ jeŋa ne mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam yeiri kolo na wo yiga ne to, ne ko ná wó taa jege swono naa ko wó taa jege dono ko pa‑o. 2Ko wó taa ye bedwe ko pa nɔɔno maama. Nabiina maama lage ba guri bedwe mo, ne ko ná ye nɔn-ŋona de puseŋ-nyena, naa balo na maŋe de Wɛ chullu tem to de balo na wo maŋe to, naa balo na ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ to de balo na ba ke-de to maama. Nɔn-laaro de wɛleere-keira gurim ye bedwe mo, ko ta woli de balo na gwoni ni de Wɛ to, de balo na ve se ba ke konto to. 3Ko na ke tei logo baŋa ne konto to ye wo-chɛɔ mo, de nɔɔna maama gurim na ye bedwe tei to. Nabiina bochara nam ye lwarem yerane mo. Ba ta na ŋwe to, vuvuga mo su ba boboŋa. Ko kwaga ne ba laam ma te.
4Wolo nam ta ná ŋwe logo baŋa ne, teena wo kotu tei ne mo. “Kukura kalo na ŋwe to gare nywoŋo kolo na tege to.” 5Chega ŋwaane to, balo ta na ŋwe to yei we ba wó ba ba te. Ko nam ná ye twa bam, ba yeiri kolokolo ni ne. Nyɔɔre daa tera se ba jwoŋi, ye nɔɔna maŋe ba swei ba swia mo. 6Ba na swoi wonnu tei to, de ba na chuli-te tei to, de ba fera na wo wonnu baŋa ne tei to laam jei mo fase. Ba daa ba jege totoŋe logo baŋa ne se ba tɔge ba ke.
Ywoni dim taane
7Nam ta‑n jege ywoni n di wodiu, se n daare n nyɔ sa-doora de wopwolo. Kokuri to, Wɛ yi maŋe de su n kikia yam konto. 8Kwɛ n tete se n yeini n zo gare-pwonnu, se n daare n turi n yuu de nuga. 9Ta‑n swoi n kaane se á ta‑á di ywoni daane n ŋwea da yam na ye kukua to maama wone. Mo pɛɛre delo Wɛ na pɛ‑m logo baŋa ne, se n wane n di ywoni n totoŋ-chɛɛra yam baŋa ne to. 10Totoŋe delo maama n ná jege n toŋa, se n toŋe-de de n dam maama. Kokuri to, churu ne ba ba toŋa, ba nam ba boŋe boboŋa naa ba jege yeino, ye ba ta ba beeri swa dáane. Nmo nam lage n vo dáane mo.
N bá‑n wane n che n tete de cham
11Amo daa ta tu a maane tento mo logo baŋa ne:
Ko dae we balo na duri lela lela to mo wó di yiga durim kayuŋu kom ne.
Ko dae we babɛ mo wó di jara yam.
Ko nam dae swa tiina mo nae ba ni-wodiu.
Ko ta dae yi-pore-nyena mo ye naduna,
ye ko dae nɔn-yum mo na yiga-veiŋa.
Ko nam na ye tei ko pae ba maama to, keim maama wó ke ko maŋa ne mo. 12Kokuri to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno yeiri maŋa kalo toone na wó ja‑o to. Ko nye de ba na kwei bora ba ma ja ywona tei to, naa ba na jaane zuna kalanchogo wone tei to mo. Toone de yeini de pɔpɔ de yi nabiina mo maŋa kalo na wo maŋe to wone.
Swa gare dam
13Amo ta ma maane woŋo kodwoŋi logo baŋa ne na yɔɔre ko bere-ne swa na ye tei to.
14Te-balaŋa déem mo wora ye ko nɔn-bia ye fenfee yerane. Pa-kamunu ma la o jar-keira o vo se o kwaare jara de-ba. Pɛ wom ma pa se ba kaare teo kom ba pu, se ba daare ba lɔ taara ba sale ko kabiri sem teiŋa se ba wane ba zo ko wone. 15Yiniga tu maa wora teo kom wone o na jege swa. Wonto ma tɔge o swa yam baŋa ne o jwoŋi-ko o yage. Ko kwaga seeni nam nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo guli yiniga tu wom gula. 16Konto mo pɛ a lɔre we, swa lana ya gare dam. Nɔɔno nam ná ye yiniga tu ye o jege swa, nɔɔna wó gwooni o swa yam mo. Ba ba yeini ba sɛ kotu ni taane.
Swa de jworim taane
17Swa tu ná ŋɔɔne tega tega
ye n cheigi o ni taane,
konto jege kuri ko gare
pɛ ná bage de kwor-dɛa
o bere nɔn-jworru.
18Swa lana ya dwoi jara zela.
Wɛleere-keiru dedoa nam wae
o chɔge wo-laaro dedɛ
na maŋe te tigi to.

english_text:
1A few dead flies in perfume
make all of it stink,
and a little foolishness
outweighs a lot of wisdom.
2Sensible thoughts lead you
to do right;
foolish thoughts lead you
to do wrong.
3Fools show their stupidity
by the way they live;
it's easy to see
they have no sense.
4Don't give up your job
when your boss gets angry.
If you stay calm,
you'll be forgiven.
5Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair: 6They honor fools, but dishonor the rich; 7they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
8 If you dig a pit,
you might fall in;
if you break down a wall,
a snake might bite you.
9You could even get hurt
by chiseling a stone
or chopping a log.
10If you don't sharpen your ax,
it will be harder to use;
if you are wise,
you'll know what to do.
11The power to charm a snake
does you no good
if it bites you anyway.
12If you talk sensibly,
you will have friends;
if you talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
13Fools begin with nonsense,
and their stupid chatter
ends with disaster.
14They never tire of talking,
but none of us really know
what the future will bring.
15Fools wear themselves out—
they don't know enough
to find their way home.
16A country is in for trouble
when its ruler is childish,
and its leaders
party all day long.
17But a nation will prosper
when its ruler is mature,
and its leaders
don't party too much.
18Some people are too lazy
to fix a leaky roof—
then the house collapses.
19Eating and drinking
make you feel happy,
and money can buy
everything you need.
20Don't let yourself think about
cursing the king;
don't curse the rich,
not even in secret.
A little bird might hear
and tell everything.
translation_text:
1Nanjo-too ná to talwoŋ-ywoŋa nuga ne,
ka wó pɔ mo ka lwoi.
Konto dwoŋi mo nɔɔno jworim fenfee wó chɔge swa dedɛ.
2Swa tu boboŋa pae
o yɔɔre chwoŋa mo.
Jworo boboŋa nam pae
o toŋe gweeni mo.
3O ná kwei chwoŋa o maa via,
o bere o tete jaja we
o ye jworo mo,
o na tiini o ga boboŋa to ŋwaane.
4Pɛ wom bane ná zaŋe nmo baŋa ne, yé zaŋe n nwoŋi o tei ne. Nmo ná jaane n wo, ko laam wó pa se o ban-lom dem zuri.
5Amo nam maane wo-chɛɔ kodwoŋi mo logo baŋa ne, ne pɛ na ke o tusi tei to. 6Jworru mo yeini te jiri yiga tiina. Naduna de maa wo kwaga kwaga. 7Amo ta ma na kabɛ na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne tei to, ko daare ye nakwa vei tega ne.
8Wolo ná koge gwoŋo,
kotu wó wane o jwoori
o to ko wone.
Wolo nam ná yare kabira
o de tega ne,
basankwea wó wane ka tɔge dáane ka done‑o.
9Wolo ná yare kandwa peo yera ne,
kotu wó wane o na zonne
ya baŋa ne.
Nɔɔno wolo nam ná lɔe da-kwollu,
o de wae o nae zonne te baŋa ne.
10Tontoŋeno dwooru ná ba jege ni,
ye o ná wo dwori‑o,
o totoŋa wó taa chamma mo.
Swa nam wó pa nɔɔno totoŋa
taa ke lanyerane.
11Nɔɔno ná jege liri se o ma
o ja basankwea,
ye ka ná wuuri ka done‑o,
bɛ nyɔɔre mo liri tu wom wó na ko baŋa ne?
12Swa tu ni taane wó pa‑o zula mo.
Jworo ni taane nam wó chɔge‑o mo zɔŋ-zɔŋ.
13Kotu ná puri o ni,
jworim yerane mo o ŋɔɔna.
O ni taane dem yeini de kweeli
de vuvuga yerane.
14Jworo yeini o ŋɔɔne ta-fara mo
o ba kwora.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam yeiri kolo
