jwa na wó ke to.
Wɔ mo wó wane o bere debam
kolo na wó ke dé toone
kwaga ne to?
15Jworo totoŋ-chɛɛra pae
o yera chɛ mo.
O nam maŋe o yeiri chwoŋa kalo
o na wó tɔge
se o vo o yi teo kom wo to.
16Lɛɛro wó yi teo kolo pɛ na ye nɔn-doŋo ye o wo lɔre swa,
ye ko nakwa yɔɔre ba di wodi-fɔrɔ zezeŋa maama ne to mo.
17Ko daare yu-ywoŋo mo wó yi teo kolo pɛ ba na loge naduna dwi wone,
ye ko nakwa jaane ba tete se ba di wodiu ko maŋa ne to.
Ba yazura ŋwaane mo ba di wodiu,
ye ba ba nyɔ sana ba sui.
18Nɔɔno jawɔrɔ mo pae se
o diga to ka vwi.
O ná wo kwoni o diga lulua,
ka wó taa lura mo taa.
19Dé yeini dé saŋe wodiu se ko pa ywoni taa wora.
Sana de maa pae dé jege wopwolo dé ŋwea wone.
Sabu nam ná tere nɔɔno tei ne,
tento maama ware te ke.
20Yé zaŋe n sɔɔle lwarem n daŋe
pɛ wom yuu ne,
ko ná maŋe ko ye n tete boboŋa wone mo de.
Ta yé sɔɔle lwarem n pa naduna,
ko ná maŋe ko ye n tete diga ne mo n tage ba taane de.
Nmo ná ke konto,
zuŋa wó ja n taane dem
ka vo ka ta ka bere-ba jaja.

english_text:
It Pays To Work Hard
1Be generous, and someday
you will be rewarded.
2Share what you have
with seven or eight others,
because you never know
when disaster may strike.
3Rain clouds always bring rain;
trees always stay
wherever they fall.
4If you worry about the weather
and don't plant seeds,
you won't harvest a crop.
5No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
6Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce.
Youth and Old Age
7Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun. 8Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
9Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
10Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_text:
Dé bá wane wonnu maama dé lɔre dé ti
1“Kwei n wonnu n dole n yage
se te tɔge naneo kom baŋa
te jage te yi jei maama.
Ko ná ke da yalei,
nmo wó jwoori n na-te.”
2“Pɔɔre n jejegero n pa
nɔɔna barepɛ naa nɔɔna nana,
se n yeiri cham delo na
wó yi‑m logo baŋa ne to.”
3“Kunkwonnu ná tigisi liira-liira,
dé yei we doa lage ka ne mo.
Tio nam ná to ko jeeri mɛ maama,
ko wó taa tigi konto mo taa.”
4“Wolo ná fɔge o nii tega yibia
se o lɔre duum maŋa,
kotu bá zaŋe o du duum.
Wolo de ná nii kunkwonnu
na tigisi tei to,
kotu bá zage wodiu o ja o zo diga.”
5Nmo nam bá wane n lɔre chwoŋa kalo vio na tɔge da ko dole to. N ta bá wane n lɔre bu na ke tei o ŋwe o nu puga ne to. Konto dwoŋi mo n bá‑n wane n lɔre Wɛ kikia yam kuri n ti, de o na ye wolo na ke wonnu maama to. 6Zezeŋa ne se n nwoŋi n vo n bobo duum. Daa ta ta‑n toŋe n kara ne se tega laam ba ka yi. Kokuri to, n bá‑n wane n lɔre totoŋe delo na wó ke lanyerane to. Dɛ delo n totoŋa yam maama wó pa n na nyɔɔre.
Ywoni taane
7Tega baŋa pwooni mo jege ywoni. Nɔɔno yia ná nae wea kam pwooni, konto tiini ko lana mo ko pa‑o. 8Nɔɔno ná maŋe o kwe de bena dedɛ, ko maŋe mo se kotu di o ŋwea da yam maama ywoni. O nam yé swei we o lage o taa wo lim wone mo taa. Ko ná ye kolo maama jwa na wó ba ko ke to, dé bá wane dé lɔre ko kuri.
Nɔn-donne taane
9Nmo wolo na ye nɔn-doŋo to, nmo ta ná wo kwe, se n di n ŋwea kam ywoni. Ta‑n jege wopwolo n nɔn-donne maŋa ne. Pa se n boboŋa de n yia taa bere‑m chwoŋa kalo n na wo tɔge to. Nam ta‑n yei we, nmo ná tɔge chwoŋa kalo maama, Wɛ wó di n taane ko baŋa ne. 10Yé sɛ se lwia zo n boboŋa, se kolokolo de yé pa n yera chɛ. Kokuri to, dé nɔn-donne maŋa kam ba dáane ye ka tia.

english_text:
1Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
2Someday the light of the sun
and the moon and the stars
will all seem dim to you.
Rain clouds will remain
over your head.
3Your body will grow feeble,
your teeth will decay,
and your eyesight fail.
4The noisy grinding of grain
and the voices of singers
will be shut out
by your deaf ears,
but even the song of a bird
will keep you awake.
5You will be afraid
to climb up a hill
or walk down a road.
Your hair will turn as white
as almond blossoms.
You will feel lifeless
and drag along
like an old grasshopper.
We each go to our eternal home,
and the streets here are filled
with those who mourn.
6The silver cord snaps,
the golden bowl breaks;
the water pitcher is smashed,
and the pulley at the well
is shattered.
7So our bodies return
to the earth,
and the life-giving breath
returns to God.
8Nothing makes sense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense.
Respect and Obey God
9I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied. 10Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
11Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together. 12My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these.
There is no end to books,
and too much study
will wear you out.
13Everything you were taught can be put into a few words:
Respect and obey God!
This is what life
is all about.
14God will judge
everything we do,
even what is done in secret,
whether good or bad.
translation_text:
1Ta‑n guli wolo na naane‑m to gula nmo nɔn-donne maŋa ne. Ke konto ye cham maŋa ta wo yi‑m, se n laam ta nenɛɛne, “Amo daa ba ni ŋwea ywoni.” 2Maŋa kam konto ne wea kam, de chana kam, de chalechwe sem pwooni daa bá taa nae te pa‑m, ye woŋo maama ye lim mo. Do-kunkwonnu de maa wó jwoori te li tega kam. 3Maŋa kam konto ne, balo na yere sɔŋɔ kom to yera laam wó taa sae mo. Babea vɔna de maa wó pare. Kaana balo na cho muni to maa yage muna chom, ba na muri to ŋwaane. Balo de na nii diga takworru tem seeni to yia laam dwei mo. 4Maŋa kam konto ne, ba wó che manchwoŋo ni dem. Nɔŋɔ kom sɔɔ daa bá taa ni teo wone. Zuŋa dedoa tete ná keeri tete ne, nmo wó zaŋe dɔɔm wone lela. Lenlɛ kwori nam daa bá to n zwa wone. 5Ka maŋa ne, nmo wó ta‑n kɔre foone de wɛyuu diinim. Lwia maa wó taa jege‑m n veiŋa wone. Alimodi tio kom maa wó kwi punnu na peere to cha. Manchwanno de wó gwane tega ne mɛmɛ. Nmo fera maama wó ti. Kokuri to, ko gɛ fee se n vo n yi n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom. Ba laam maa wó taa keeri lua bugi-bugi jei maama ne. 6Nam guli n Keiro wom gula ye lu-nyenno chaponno tem ta wo kɔge, ye sabu-seŋa na-zoŋa kam de wo lɔge. Ke konto ye gwoŋo kom ta wo chɔge vole dem seeni se ko pae ba daa yé wane na ba mɔ. 7Dé ye-daa kam laam maa wó jwoori tega kam ka ji teero, se jworo kolo na pae ŋwea to jwoori ko vo Wɛ wolo na kwei-ko o pa debam to tei.
8Amo wolo na ye Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno to mo we:
Dé bá wane dé ni wonnu tento maama kuri.
Te kuri nim tiini de chana
de gaale se dé lɔre.
Kweelim taane
9Kolo na woli da to mo ye: Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno déem jege swa chekke ye o ta yeini o bere nɔɔna pa se ba yia poore. O ma zamese memaŋa se o wane o lɔre ya kuri, ye o daare o tigisi-ya o ke daane. 10Kwor-tɛɛno wom ma seene o yia o lage botare-bia balo na maŋe to, ye o tɔge chega baŋa o popone taane delo na ye chekke to.
11Swa tu ni taane nye de gwoli mo nayero na jege o yere o vara. Kotu bera yam nye de chena yalo na fɔge ya chwi daa yera ne to mo. Ya maama nwoŋi nayero dedoa tei ne mo.
12Amo bu, kolo ta na woli da to mo ye se n ta‑n yei n tete de wonnu tento: nmo ná kwaane n popone swa taana n tiŋi, n totoŋa yam bá ti. Nmo ná tiini n zamese wonnu dedɛ, ko wó bogese‑m mo.
13Dé laam na nigi wonnu maama to, taane dem gurim jei mo tento: Ta‑n kɔre Wɛ, se n daare n ta‑n toŋe n tɔge o nia yam. Konto yerane ŋwaane mo nabiina wora. 14Wɛ nam wó di dé taane dé kikia maama baŋa ne, ko ná ye keim-laaro, de keim-balwaaro, de yalo dé na seigi dé ke to de maama.

english_text:
Love Is Better than Wine
1 This is Solomon's
most beautiful song.
She Speaks:
2Kiss me tenderly!
Your love is better than wine,
3and you smell so sweet.
All the young women adore you;
the very mention of your name
is like spreading perfume.
* 4Hurry, my king! Let's hurry.
Take me to your home.
The Young Women Speak:
We are happy for you!
And we praise your love
even more than wine.
She Speaks:
Young women of Jerusalem,
it is only right
that you should adore him.
5My skin is dark and beautiful,
like a tent in the desert
or like Solomon's curtains.
6Don't stare at me
just because the sun
has darkened my skin.
My brothers were angry with me;
they made me work in the vineyard,
and so I neglected
my complexion.
7My darling, I love you!
Where do you feed your sheep
and let them rest at noon?
Don't let the other shepherds
think badly of me.
I'm not one of those women
who shamelessly follow
after shepherds.
He Speaks:
8My dearest, if you don't know,
just follow the path
of the sheep.
Then feed your young goats
near the shepherds' tents.
9You move as gracefully
as the pony that leads
the chariot of the king.
10Earrings add to your beauty,
and you wear a necklace
of precious stones.
11Let's make you some jewelry
of gold, woven with silver.
She Speaks:
12My king, while you
were on your couch,
my aroma was a magic charm.
13My darling, you are perfume
between my breasts;
14you are flower blossoms
from the gardens of En-Gedi.
He Speaks:
15My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
your eyes are those of a dove.
She Speaks:
16My love, you are handsome,
truly handsome—
the fresh green grass
will be our wedding bed
17in the shade of cedar
and cypress trees.
translation_text:
1Solomon yera leiŋa kalo na ywomma ka dwoi lei maama to.
Leiŋa 1
Bukɔ wom:
2Ba n kwaare n ni de a ni,
se n mu-de.
Kokuri, nmo swono kom ywomma ko pa-ne
ko dwoi sa-sona ywoni.
3Nmo yera terale nuga kam lwom mo tiini ko ywomma.
N yere dem ywomma
ne ba na lwogi talwoŋ-ywoŋa
pa se ka lwom jage jei maama ne tei to.
Konto ŋwaane mo bukwa maama wó taa swoi‑m.
4Nam ja-ne se dé ke lela dé lage jei dé vo!
Pɛ, nam ja-ne n zo n diga kam wone.
Jerusalem bukwa bam:
Dé wó taa chaka mo de wopwolo nmo ŋwaane.
Dé wó tei n swono kom we,
ko ywoni lana ko dwoi sana ywoni.
Bukɔ wom:
Chega ŋwaane to, ko maŋe se bukwa bam taa swoi‑m.
5Abam Jerusalem bukwa bam,
maane-na we amo seene a zwora mo
ye a yibia ta yɔɔre ka lana.
A maa zwora ne Kedare tiina vwoa yam na ye tei to,
de gare-laaro telo Solomon na kwei
o che o di sem nia to.
6Nam yé ta‑á lwoi yia a baŋa ne
de a na zwora tei to.
Ko ye wea kam mo tiini ka mage a yera yam
pa se ya zwori konto.
Amo nu-bia bane mo zaŋe de amo.
Ba pɛ se a toŋe Vini teeni kadwi sem ne mo taa,
ye a wo nɛ pwola se a nii a tete kaduga kam baŋa ne.
7Amo bochɔŋɔ, ta n bere-ne mɛ seeni
n na yeini n kale n vara bam n vei to,
de jei selo nmo na pae ba sii wea tetare ne to.
Ko dae se a taa tole a beera
nayero de nayero pei-kɔgɔ maama wone.
Nɔn-doŋo kom:
8Nmo wolo na lana n dwoi kaana maama to,
n seene n yeiri amo na wo mɛ to na?
Nam tɔge chwoŋa kalo pei sem na nɔne da to,
se n vo n yi nayera bam vwoa yam seeni,
ye n daare n na gaao n pa n bobone sem.
9Amo bochɔŋɔ, nmo nye de sisein-nɔɔno
wolo ba na kwɛ ka yera
se ka vaŋe Ejipti pa-faro wom toroko to mo.
10Zwanno telo na wo n yuu ne to
pɛ n keila yam lam nwoŋi mo chekke.
Kandwa-nyenno telo na ye zambili n ba ne to
de woli pa n lam dem nwoŋi lanyerane.
11Nam pa se dé ke sabu-seŋa zwa-kwana mo dé pa‑m,
ye dé kwei lu-nyenno dé ma dé gɔgere ya maama.
Bukɔ wom:
12Maŋa kalo amo pɛ wom na tigi o jaŋgɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne to,
mo talwoŋ-ywoŋa kalo a na ke a yera ne to
lwom jage jei maama ne.
13A bɔɔlo wom nye de Mura terale mo a tei ne,
de na wo ganlɔgere wone
ye de tigi amo yela yam tetare laŋa ne to.
14O ta nye de ga-pun-laaro telo lwom na ywomma
ye ba gwoni-te En-gedi Vini kare sem ne to.
Nɔn-doŋo kom:
15Amo bochɔŋɔ, nii n na tiini n lana tei!
N yibia tiini ka lana dedɛ!
N yia lam jege fera ne kunkwona mo tei.
Bukɔ wom:
16A bɔɔlo, nmo yɔɔre n ye lanno mo!
Amo bere a ba nii‑m a sui.
Dé na tigi ywo-seeni to
ga-zuru mo pugi dé vwei dem.
17Sedare da-kwollu mo ye dé diga bei,
Danno telo na ne-ka to maa ye Pini teeni dɛ.

english_text:
Love Makes Everything Beautiful
She Speaks:
1I am merely a rose
from the land of Sharon,
a lily from the valley.
He Speaks:
2My darling, when compared
with other young women,
you are a lily among thorns.
She Speaks:
3And you, my love,
are an apple tree
among trees of the forest.
Your shade brought me pleasure;
your fruit was sweet.
4You led me to your banquet room
and showered me with love.
5Refresh and strengthen me
with raisins and apples.
I am hungry for love!
6Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
7Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Winter Is Past
She Speaks:
8I hear the voice
of the one I love,
as he comes leaping
over mountains and hills
9like a deer or a gazelle.
Now he stands outside our wall,
looking through the window
10and speaking to me.
He Speaks:
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
11Winter is past,
the rain has stopped;
12flowers cover the earth,
it's time to sing.
The cooing of doves
is heard in our land.
13Fig trees are bearing fruit,
while blossoms on grapevines
fill the air with perfume.
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
14You are my dove
hiding among the rocks
on the side of a cliff.
Let me see how lovely you are!
Let me hear the sound
of your melodious voice.
15Our vineyards are in blossom;
we must catch the little foxes
that destroy the vineyards.
She Speaks:
16My darling, I am yours,
and you are mine,
as you feed your sheep
among the lilies.
17Pretend to be a young deer
dancing on mountain slopes
until daylight comes
and shadows fade away.
translation_text:
Bukɔ wom:
1Amo nye de ga-puŋu kolo na puli Saron jei sem ne to mo,
de kantɔgele delo na puli bwolo tega ne to.
Nɔn-doŋo kom:
2Amo bochɔŋɔ ná wo o yuudwonna wone,
o ye nenɛɛne kantɔgele mo na puli ye sabare gilimi-de to.
Bukɔ wom:
3Amo bɔɔlo wom de ná zege
de o yuudwonna bam,
o nye de kaligwoŋo tio na zege goa wo teeni tetare ne to mo.
A ke a boboŋa ne se a taa jei o woro kom kuri ne mo.
A ma tiini a ni tio-bia balo o na pɛ-ne pa a di to ywoni.
4O jaane-ne o zo diga kalo wone ba na di ywoni da to.
O ma yɔɔre o kwoli-ne de o swono.
5A yera maama tege mo
a fera na wo n swono kom wone to ŋwaane.
Nam kwei kekan-wogila
de kaligwoŋo tio-bia n pa-ne se a di,
se n ma‑n teibi-ne se a wori.
6O ma kwei o jagwia kam o teili a yuu,
se o daare o ma o jazem dem o kukwori-ne.
7Jerusalem teo bukwa bam,
da-na wei dedaane feiri dam ŋwaane
á du-na duuri we
abam bá gigili debam yia
de dé swono kom.
Nam pa-na debam chwoŋa se dé toŋe dé fera.
Leiŋa 2
Bukɔ wom:
8Amo nigi a bɔɔlo wom kwora.
Nii o na beene tei!
O yɔɔre o nɔne peero de zwonnu tem yuu ne mo
o faŋe o beene.
9A bɔɔlo wom nye de feira
naa woŋ-pɔla mo.
Nii o na zege bira-kwaga ne,
ye o tɔge takworo ne o leesi
o nii diga wone tei.
10O laam maa ŋɔɔne de amo o we:
“Amo bochɔŋɔ, nmo wolo yibia
na lana amo yiga ne to,
ba se dé tɔge daane dé kɛ.
11Nii mo! Waaro maŋa kam kɛ,
doa kam de maa kɔ nenem.
12Ga-punnu laam mo faare tega kam jei maama.
Ko laam ye maŋa mo se dé leeni lei.
Kunkwona keira laam mo zaŋe
dé tega kam jei maama ne.
13Kaporro tem bobo se te taa ke mɔɔro.
Vini teeni dem de maa kwi punnu
ye te lwom zaŋe jei maama ne.
Konto ŋwaane, a bɔɔl-swono,
pa dé lage jei dé vo.”
Nɔn-doŋo kom:
14Nmo wolo na ye amo kunkwoŋa kam
ye n seigi peero gugworru wone to,
nam nwoŋi se a na n yibia,
se a daare a ni n kwora.
Kokuri, nmo yibia kam tiini ka lana mo,
ye n kwora kam de ywomma lanyerane.
Bukɔ wom:
15Popo ja nywoŋ-kuri sem n pa debam,
kokuri vare-balwa bam konto
jege dé Vini teeni dem mo
ba chɔga ba yaga.
Dé Vini teeni dem nam wora
de kwi punnu mo,
se de daare de lei bia.
16A bɔɔlo wom ye amo nyem mo,
ye amo maama de ye wonto nyem.
O laam maa yɛ kantɔgela yam wone.
17Ta ta‑n wora se ko taa nii tega ná poore,
ye tetete vo-zuru kom dole.
A bɔɔlo, laam nam jwoori n kɛ!
Duri-na ne woŋa tei to,
de feira na nɔne peero telo na pɔɔre belei to baŋa ne.

english_text:
Beautiful Dreams
She Speaks:
1While in bed at night,
I reached for the one I love
with heart and soul.
I looked for him,
but he wasn't there.
2So I searched through the town
for the one I love.
I looked on every street,
but he wasn't there.
3I even asked the guards
patrolling the town,
“Have you seen the one
I love so much?”
4Right after that, I found him.
I held him and would not let go
until I had taken him
to the home of my mother.
5Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles,
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
The Groom and the Wedding Party
Their Friends Speak:
6What do we see approaching
from the desert
like a cloud of smoke?
With it comes the sweet smell
of spices, including myrrh
and frankincense.
7It is King Solomon
carried on a throne,
surrounded by sixty
of Israel's best soldiers.
8Each of them wears a sword.
They are experts at fighting,
even in the dark.
9The throne is made of trees
from Lebanon.
10Its posts are silver,
the back is gold,
and the seat is covered
with purple cloth.
You women of Jerusalem
have taken great care
to furnish the inside.
11Now come and see the crown
given to Solomon by his mother
on his happy wedding day.
translation_text:
Bukɔ wom:
1Tete maama ne mo a tigi a sara ne
ye a boŋe a na swoi wolo to boboŋa taa.
A maa beeri o jei ye a wo nɛ‑o.
2“Amo nam wó zaŋe leile mo
a zo teo kom wone.
A maa wó taa kare teo kom chwei sem yuni ne,
de ko kapworru tem maama ne
se a beeri a na swoi wolo to jeiga.”
A nam na beeri‑o a vo mɛ maama to,
a wo nɛ‑o.
3Balo na yere teo kom tete ne to
de maa kare ba via.
Ba ma na-ne, ye a bwei-ba we:
“Amo beeri a na swoi wolo to mo.
Abam nɛ‑o na?”
4A na yɔɔre a fere-ba a kɛ fee to,
mo a nɛ wolo wom a na swoi to.
A ma yɔɔre a to a gorege‑o mɔpe.
A maa wo sɛ se a yage‑o
se ko taa nii a ná jaane‑o a vo sɔŋɔ
ye dé zo diga kalo wone
a nu na loge-ne to.
5Jerusalem teo bukwa bam,
da-na wei dedaane feiri dam ŋwaane
á du-na duuri we,
abam bá gigili debam yia
de dé swono kom.
Nam pa-na debam chwoŋa
se dé toŋe dé fera.
Leiŋa 3
6Bɛ mo zege kagoa seeni ko zaŋe kulululu ko beena,
ne nyoa na zaŋe kulululu ka maa diini wɛyuu tei to?
Ko maa nye de ba zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa mo,
pa se ka lwom zaŋe wɛɛne de jage jei maama.
Ko ke nenɛɛne Mura de Faraniki talwoŋ-ywoŋa mo ba zwɛ,
dedaane talwei dwi dwi selo pipim-piina na jege to.
7Nii mo! Ko ye Pɛ Solomon mo ba zeŋe ba via,
ye Isarele jar-keira babɛ sem fuseredo laam gilimi‑o.
8Ba maama jege se-zɔɔro mo,
ye ba yei jara keim laŋa chekke.
Nɔɔno maama se-zɔɔ leigi o teiŋa ne,
se ko ná maŋe ko ye tete ne de,
se kotu ke jara.
9Ba déem kwei Lebanon teo
da-ŋonno mo
ba ma ba ke yituŋu kom ba pa Pɛ Solomon
se ba taa maa zeŋe‑o ba via.
10Ba kwei lu-nyenno mo ba kwoli dɛ selo na teili yituŋu kom to,
ye ba ma sabu-seŋa ba ke ko kuri dem seeni.
Ko ná ye jeiŋa jei sem tete,
ba kwei gare-nasoŋ-pupwia mo
ba gɔgere ba kwoli da.
Jerusalem teo bukwa mo zuri ba yera
ba kwɛ ko wo kom maama.
11Abam Zion teo bukwa bam,
nwoŋi-na pwooni,
se á nii á na Pɛ Solomon na pugi
o paare yipuga kam o yuu ne to.
Ka ye paare yipuga kalo
o nu na kwei o pu‑o
dɛ delo wone o na di o kaane to mo.
Ko maa ye dɛ dem konto ne mo
o wo tiini ko pwoli.

english_text:
What a Beautiful Bride
He Speaks:
1My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
as you look through your veil,
your eyes are those of a dove.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
2Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
3Your lips are crimson cords,
your mouth is shapely;
behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
4Your neck is more graceful
than the tower of David,
decorated with thousands
of warriors' shields.
5Your breasts are perfect;
they are twin deer
feeding among lilies.
6I will hasten to those hills
sprinkled with sweet perfume
and stay there till sunrise.
7My darling, you are lovely
in every way.
8My bride, together
we will leave Lebanon!
We will say goodbye
to the peaks of Mount Amana,
Senir, and Hermon,
where lions and leopards
live in the caves.
9My bride, my very own,
you have stolen my heart!
With one glance from your eyes
and the glow of your necklace,
you have stolen my heart.
10Your love is sweeter than wine;
the smell of your perfume
is more fragrant than spices.
11Your lips are a honeycomb;
milk and honey
flow from your tongue.
Your dress has the aroma
of cedar trees from Lebanon.
12My bride, my very own,
you are a garden, a fountain
closed off to all others.
13Your arms are vines,
covered with delicious fruits
and all sorts of spices—
henna, nard, 14saffron,
calamus, cinnamon,
frankincense, myrrh, and aloes
—all the finest spices.
15You are a spring in the garden,
a fountain of pure water,
and a refreshing stream
from Mount Lebanon.
She Speaks:
16Let the north wind blow,
the south wind too!
Let them spread the aroma
of my garden,
so the one I love
may enter and taste
its delicious fruits.
translation_text:
Nɔn-doŋo kom:
1Nii nmo na tiini n lana tei,
amo bochɔŋɔ!
Nmo yibia lana dedɛ ka pa-ne!
Nmo ná mɛ gare-fefala n kwoli n yibia,
n yia yam lana ne kunkwona to mo.
Nmo yu-ywei sem zwora lanyerane
nenɛɛne bone na zege Gilead peero tem yuu ne
de faŋe de maa tu tega tei to mo.
2Nmo yeila yam maa peere cha,
ne pei-kɔgɔ ba na gwoni se koro,
ye ba swɛ-se pa se peere tei to mo.
Ya maama maŋe daane mo,
ye dedoa tete wo sage de chwoŋa.
3Nmo ni-vɔɔro tem nye de
gare-ŋon-seŋa mo.
N ni dem nyenyego de lana dedɛ.
N ná kwoli n yibia de gare-fefala,
n keila yam lam ta nae mo jaja,
ye ya nye de Pomegara tio-bu
na chɛ belei tei to.
4Nmo ba dem yɔɔre de dɔra
nenɛɛne di-dedɔrɔ kolo
Pɛ David na lɔge o zege to mo.
Nmo zambili nye de bembɛ mo kwei ba jara nantane moro
ba pale di-dedɔrɔ kom yera ne.
5Nmo yela yɔɔre ya maŋe daane mo chekke,
nenɛɛne feiri selei na vei daane
ye se zege kantɔgela tetare ne se di gaao tei to.
6Tega ta ná wo poore,
se tetete vo-zuru kom dole,
amo nam wó vo a maŋe
nmo peero telei tem seeni,
mɛ ba na zezage Mura terale
de talwoŋ-ywoŋa
pa se se lwom zaŋe lanyerane to mo.
7Amo bochɔŋɔ, n yɔɔre n lana mo
se ko gaale,
ye gɛɛ tera de fenfee de.
8Amo katɔgɔ, pa dé yage Lebanon peero jei sem!
Zege dáane yiga yiga n ba amo tei.
Zege Amana peo kom yuu ne,
de Senira peo kom,
de Heremon peo kom yuu ne,
n tu n ba.
Yage jei sem konto

but I could not find him—
there was no answer.

patrolling the town
and guarding the wall.
They beat me up
and stripped off my robe.

if you find the one I love,
please say to him,

why is the one you love
more special than others?

to tell him how you feel?

among ten thousand.

bathing in a stream
flowing with milk.

covered with jewels;

decorated with sapphires.

on feet of gold.

like Mount Lebanon
and its choice cedar trees.

he is my lover and friend.

Their Friends Speak:
1Most beautiful of women,
tell us where he has gone.
Let us help you find him.
She Speaks:
2My darling has gone down
to his garden of spices,
where he will feed his sheep
and gather lilies.
3I am his, and he is mine,
as he feeds his sheep
among the lilies.
He Speaks:
4My dearest, the cities of Tirzah
and Jerusalem
are not as lovely as you.
Your charms are more powerful
than all of the stars
in the heavens.
5Turn away your eyes—
they make me melt.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.

than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.

beautiful rosy cheeks.

sixty queens, eighty wives,
and thousands of others!

my flawless dove,
the favorite child
of your mother.
The young women, the queens,
and all the others
tell how excited you are
as they sing your praises:

as the morning sky—
glorious as the moon—
blinding as the sun!
Your charms are more powerful
than all the stars above.”
She Speaks:
11I went down to see if blossoms
were on the walnut trees,
grapevines, and fruit trees.
12But in my imagination
I was suddenly riding
on a glorious chariot.

Beautiful woman from Shulam,
let us see you dance!

Why do you want to see
this woman from Shulam
dancing with the others?

1Nmo wolo na lana

Nmo yɔɔre n jege nenɔŋa dedɛ,

se n yé ta‑n nii amo seeni,

Nmo yu-ywei sem zwora lanyerane
nenɛɛne bone na zege
Gilead peero tem yuu ne

7N ná kwoli n yibia de gare-fefala,

dedaane ka-bi funɔnɔ,
ye busankan-pwoli moro ná wo
o tei ne de,

wopwolo ŋwaane.
Ko ke-ne nenɛɛne a jei
pa-bu saŋa ne mo,

de torokooro se via.
13Sulam tiina bukɔ,
jwoori n ba ywo-seeni!
Ba ywo se dé wane dé taa nii nmo!
Bukɔ wom:
Bɛ mo ye á lage á nii
wolo na ba jege gɛɛ to,
ne o na tɔge kɔgɔ kuni belei
tetare ne o sae to?

english_text:
The Wedding Dance
He Speaks:
1You are a princess,
and your feet are graceful
in their sandals.
Your thighs are works of art,
each one a jewel;
2your navel is a wine glass
filled to overflowing.
Your body is full and slender
like a bundle of wheat
bound together by lilies.
3Your breasts are like twins
of a deer.
4Your neck is like ivory,
and your eyes sparkle
like the pools of Heshbon
by the gate of Bath-Rabbim.
Your nose is beautiful
like Mount Lebanon
above the city of Damascus.
5Your head is held high
like Mount Carmel;
your hair is so lovely
it holds a king prisoner.
6You are very beautiful,
so desirable!
7You are tall and slender
like a palm tree,
and your breasts are full.
8I will climb that tree
and cling to its branches.
I will discover that your breasts
are clusters of grapes,
and that your breath
is the aroma of apples.
9Kissing you is more delicious
than drinking the finest wine.
How wonderful and tasty!
She Speaks:
10My darling, I am yours,
and you desire me.
11Let's stroll through the fields
and sleep in the villages.
12At dawn let's slip out and see
if grapevines and fruit trees
are covered with blossoms.
When we are there,
I will give you my love.
13Perfume from the magic flower
fills the air, my darling.
Right at our doorstep
I have stored up for you
all kinds of tasty fruits.

nenɛɛne di-dedɔrɔ ba na mɛ tuu yeila ba ke to mo.

Hesebon chwaro tem na tigi

english_text:
If Only You and I …
She Speaks:
1If you were my brother,
I could kiss you
whenever we happen to meet,
and no one would say
I did wrong.
2I could take you to the home
of my mother,
who taught me all I know.
I would give you delicious wine
and fruit juice as well.
3Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
4Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Their Friends Speak:
5Who is this young woman
coming in from the desert
and leaning on the shoulder
of the one she loves?
She Speaks:
I stirred up your passions
under the apple tree
where you were born.
6Always keep me in your heart
and wear this bracelet
to remember me by.
The passion of love
bursting into flame
is more powerful than death,
stronger than the grave.
7Love cannot be drowned
by oceans or floods.
It cannot be bought—
any offer would be scorned
no matter how great.
Their Friends Speak:
8We have a little sister
whose breasts
are not yet formed.
If someone asks to marry her,
what should we do?
9She isn't a wall
that we can defend
behind a silver shield.
Neither is she a room
that we can protect
behind a wooden door.
She Speaks:
10I am a wall around a city,
my breasts are towers,
and just looking at me
brings him great pleasure.
11Solomon has a vineyard
at Baal-Hamon,
which he rents to others
for a thousand pieces
of silver each.
12My vineyard is mine alone!
Solomon can keep his silver
and the others can keep
their share of the profits.
He Speaks:
13You are in the garden
with friends all around.
Let me hear your voice!
She Speaks:
14Hurry to me, my darling!
Run faster than a deer
to mountains of spices.
translation_text:
Bukɔ wom:
1Ne n ya ná ye a nabɔ
wolo na ŋɔge a tete nu yele to,
ye dé ná jeeri daane jei selo maama ne,
a ya wó mu n ni mo,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá ta we
a ke a chɔge.
2A ya wó ja‑m se dé tɔge daane
dé vo sɔŋɔ,
ye dé zo diga kalo wone
a nu na kɔne-ne to.
A laam wó kwei sa-sona
de amo Pomegara tio-bia nyoa bam
se n nyɔ n su.
3O ma kwei o jagwia kam o teili a yuu,
se o daare o ma o jazem dem
o kukwori-ne.
4Jerusalem teo bukwa bam,
du-na duuri we
abam bá gigili debam yia
de dé swono kom.
Nam pa-na debam chwoŋa
se dé toŋe dé fera mo.
Kweelim taane
Jerusalem teo bukwa bam:
5Busankana kɔ mo tento
o zege kagoa seeni o beene,
ye o sale o bɔɔlo wom yera ne?
Bukɔ wom:
Kaligwoŋo tio kom kuri ne,
mo a pepage‑m se n zaŋe.
Ko ye dáane mo n nu déem jaane n puga.
Jei sento ne mo o ta virigi n puga
ye o lo‑m.
6Pa se amo yerane taa tigi
n bochɔŋɔ ne,
se ko taa ye ne a ye zɔŋɔ mo n ba ne,
naa baŋa mo n jeŋa ne to.
Kokuri swono vɔɔre ko tui
nɔɔna baŋa mo,
ne toone na ke tei to.
Fera de maa zi nɔɔna
ne yibeela na li-ba tei to.
Ko ta nye de min-vo-fɔrɔ kolo
na yɔɔre ko zwɛ wonnu to mo.
7Na-fɔrɔ ná daga tei maama de,
ko ware ko dwei swono mini dem.
Buga ná maŋe ka su ka wɛɛle tei de,
ka ware ka zɔre swono pa ko jei.
Nɔɔno ná maŋe o ve o sɔŋɔ jejegero maama
se o wane o yeigi swono,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá jwoŋi-te o tei ne.
Bukɔ wom nabwa:
8Dé jege dé nakɔ balaŋa,
o ta na wo yi se o mage yela.
Ne nɔɔno ná tu o we o lage‑o
se o di o ke kaane,
dé laam wó ke tɛ mo?
9O ya ná ye kabira,
dé wó kwei lu-nyenno mo
dé ma dé lɔ dé daŋe o baŋa ne.
O nam ya ná ye diga ni bworo,
dé wó kwei Sedare da-ŋonno mo
dé ma dé kwoli o yera se ya kwɛ.
Bukɔ wom:
10Amo seene a ye kabira mo.
A yela yam nam nye de
di-dedwaaro na zege choraam to mo.
Konto ŋwaane mo a kikia laam su
a bɔɔlo wom yi.
11Solomon déem jege Vini teeni gaare Baal-hamon ne.
O ma kwei-de o jene o pa nɔɔna
se ba dedoa dedoa yeini ba taa pa‑o
lu-nyenno sabu-dala moro
de tio-bia bam ŋwaane.
12Ko nam ná ye amo tete Vini teeni gaare dem,
de ye amo nyem mo
se a taa nii de baŋa ne.
Ko ná ye sabu-dala moro kom,
ko ye nmo Pɛ Solomon nyem mo.
Balo na nii de tio-bia baŋa ne to,
ba de wó jwoŋi sabu-dala bia yalei mo.
Nɔn-doŋo kom:
13Nmo wolo na kare n beeri
gaare dem wone
ye n yuudwonna wo n tei ne
ba cheigi nmo kwora to,
pa se amo de ni n kwora!
Bukɔ wom:
14Amo bɔɔlo, ke lela n ba amo tei!
Duri nenɛɛne feira naa woŋ-pɔla mo na duri lela tei
se ka vo ka yi peero telo na su de talwoŋ-ywoŋa to.

english_text:
1 I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz.
And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah:
A Guilty Nation
2The Lord has said,
“Listen, heaven and earth!
The children I raised
have turned against me.
3Oxen and donkeys know
who owns and feeds them,
but my people won't ever learn.”
4Israel, you are a sinful nation
loaded down with guilt.
You are wicked and corrupt
and have turned from the Lord,
the holy God of Israel.
5Why be punished more?
Why not give up your sin?
Your head is badly bruised,
and you are weak all over.
6From your head to your toes
there isn't a healthy spot.
Bruises, cuts, and open sores
go without care
or oil to ease the pain.
A Country in Ruins
7Your country lies in ruins;
your towns are in ashes.
Foreigners and strangers
take and destroy your land
while you watch.
8Enemies surround Jerusalem,
alone like a hut
in a vineyard
or in a cucumber field.
9 Zion would have disappeared
like Sodom and Gomorrah,
if the Lord All-Powerful
had not let a few
of its people survive.
Justice, Not Sacrifices
10You are no better
than the leaders and people
of Sodom and Gomorrah!
So listen to the Lord God:
11 “Your sacrifices
mean nothing to me.
I am sick of your offerings
of rams and choice cattle;
I don't like the blood
of bulls or lambs or goats.
12“Who asked you to bring all this
when you come to worship me?
Stay out of my temple!
13Your sacrifices are worthless,
and your incense disgusting.
I can't stand the evil you do
on your New Moon Festivals
or on your Sabbaths
and other times of worship.
14I hate your New Moon Festivals
and all others as well.
They are a heavy burden
I am tired of carrying.
15“No matter how much you pray,
I won't listen.
You are too violent.
16Wash yourselves clean!
I hate your filthy deeds.
Stop doing wrong
17and learn to live right.
See that justice is done.
Defend widows and orphans
and help the oppressed.”
An Invitation from the Lord
18I, the Lord, invite you
to come and talk it over.
Your sins are scarlet red,
but they will be whiter
than snow or wool.
19If you willingly obey me,
the best crops in the land
will be yours.
20But if you turn against me,
your enemies will kill you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
21Jerusalem, you are like
an unfaithful wife.
Once your judges were honest
and your people lived right;
now you are a city
full of murderers.
22Your silver is fake,
and your wine
is watered down.
23Your leaders have rejected me
to become friends of crooks;
your rulers are looking
for gifts and bribes.
Widows and orphans
never get a fair trial.
24I am the Lord All-Powerful,
the mighty ruler of Israel,
and I make you a promise:
You are now my enemy,
and I will show my anger
by taking revenge on you.
25I will punish you terribly
and burn away everything
that makes you unfit
to worship me.
26Jerusalem, I will choose
judges and advisors
like those you had before.
Your new name will be
“Justice and Faithfulness.”
The Lord Will Save Jerusalem
27Jerusalem, you will be saved
by showing justice;
Zion's people who turn to me
will be saved
by doing right.
28But those rebellious sinners
who turn against me, the Lord,
will all disappear.
29You will be made ashamed
of those groves of trees
where you worshiped idols.
30You will be like a grove of trees
dying in a drought.
31Your strongest leaders
will be like dry wood
set on fire by their idols.
No one will be able to help,
as they all go up in flames.
translation_text:
1 Baŋa Wɛ déem veere wonnu tento na tɛ Judah de Jerusalem taane to o bere Amozi bu Izaya mo. Ko nam ye maŋa kalo Yuzia, de Jotam, de Ahaz, de Hezekia na di Judah teo paare ba saŋe da-kwaga to mo.
Baŋa Wɛ vaŋe o nɔɔna bam zwa
2Wɛyuu cheigi! Tega baŋa de cheigi!
Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo kɔne a bia mo, ye a nii ba baŋa ne.
Ba nam nwoŋi a kwaga ne.
3Nabea yei ka tu.
Bonaga de yei ka tu, de ka tu na pae-ka wodiu mɛ to.
Amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam nam yeiri-ne.
Ba ba ni amo na jege kolo a ke to kuri.”
4Woo, nii teo konto na swoi wɛleera keim tei!
Ba ye balo boboŋa na ywori to mo.
Ba ta ye nɔn-balwaaro dwi mo,
de bia balo totoŋa na ba tɔge chwoŋa to!
Ba ve Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom to mo.
Ba ma pipiri ba kwaga ba ya‑o.
5Bɛ mo ye á ta yɔɔre á ke zwabania kikia?
Á ba kɔre se Wɛ waare abam na?
Abam yuni su de fufwollu mo,
ye á bochara yam wone de, yazura tera.
6Ko na zege á yuni ne se ko taa tu á napera kuri ne to,
yazura tera á yera yam wone.
Fufwollu, de kalwanno,
de ŋɔn-zana yerane mo wora.
Abam nam ba zare á ŋɔna yam, se á vɔ-ya.
Á ma á ba ke liri ya wone
se ya jei ya pa abam.
7Abam tega kam yɔɔre ka tigi mo yɔɔ yerane.
Mini ma zwɛ á teene dem maama.
Veira mo tu ba zage á kare wodiiru maama nyɔ,
ye abam zege á nia.
Sa-teena bam konto ma chɔge á tega kam maama
pa se kolokolo wo daare.
8Zion teo ye ko yerane mo ko zega,
ne pwoŋa na chwi ka zega gaare ne tei to.
Ko ta nye de vwei mo na zege gaane kara tetare ne.
Ko maa ye nenɛɛne teo kolo ba na li-ko
se ba ke jara ba di to.
9Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom
ya ná wo daare debam badaara se dé wori,
debam de ya wó chɔge dé ti,
ne ko déem na ke Sodom teo tiina tei to mo.
Dé ya ta maa wó ji ne Gomora teo déem na ye tei to.
10Nam cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ taane dem,
abam balo na ba gare Sodom teo dedɛɛra bam to.
Abam balo maa na nye de Gomora tiina bam to,
cheigi-na Wɛ nia yam!
11 Baŋa Wɛ tage o we:
“Abam na yeini á ja vara kɔgɔ kɔgɔ
á ke kaanem dedɛ tei to,
á boŋe we amo yiga wo ya wone mo na?
Amo yera chɛ mo de abam na kwei pi-bale,
de na-paala lara,
á ma á ke zwɛɛm kaanem á pa-ne tei to.
Amo yi nam wo su
á na-bale, de pipeili, de bo-bwaalo jana balo
á na kwei á pa-ne to.
12Á na yeini á tui á ware-ne to,
wɔ mo pɛ se á kare á kekare amo wara-jei sem ne
de á vara bam konto?
13Daa yé ta‑á jaane pɛɛra á tui ywo se á kwei-ya á pa-ne,
kokuri ya daa ba jege kuri!
Talwoŋa kalo á na kwei á zwɛ á pa-ne to
ye wo-zɔɔne mo amo tei ne.
Abam na yeini á di kura chan-doŋa ŋwaane,
naa siu dɛ ŋwaane, naa á kɔgɔ tigisim ŋwaane to,
amo yera wiiri mo de á na toŋe lwarem á woli da tei to.
14A jworo mo yɔɔre ko nwoŋi á chan-doŋa kura yam,
de wodi-fɔrɔ kura yam.
A ba veele de-ya mo ne a ga zeŋe zele mo to,
ye a yera chɛ ya ŋwaane.
15Abam ná twe á je á jeeri-ne wɛ-lworo baŋa ne,
amo wó pipiri a kwaga mo a ma a ya abam.
Abam nam ná tiini á ware-ne á dáane tei maama de,
a bá cheigi á wɛ-lworo kom.
Kokuri to, á je sem maama taare de jana mo.
16Nam sane-na á je sem,
se á daare á fɔge á kwɛ á tete.
Ja-na á totoŋ-lwanno tem
á vo dáa á daare-ne.
Yage-na lwarem totoŋa yalo á na jege á ke to,
17se á laam zamese lanyerane keim!
Beeri-na se chega kam taa toŋa,
se á daare á che balo na bɛɛse ba dwonna to.
Ta pa-na se botara na ba bora,
ye á ŋɔɔne á pa kadeina de.”
18 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Ba-na se dé bwɛ wonnu daane.
Abam wɛleera yam ná maŋe ya pa se á biini tei maama de,
amo wó saare ya digiru tem,
se á ta‑á jege wo-pwoŋo fase.
Kolo na biini abam to ná tiini ko seene chwɛ-chwɛ mo de,
amo wó pa se á ŋwea kam peere cha,
ne lɔŋɔ na ye tei to.
19Abam wo ná dɛa, pa se á jege ni-sɛɛm á pa-ne,
mo á wó di tega kam wo-laaro tem á su.
20Abam nam ná ve, pa se á nwoŋi amo kwaga ne,
á dona mo wó go abam jara wone.”
Baŋa Wɛ tete ni taane mo konto o taga o tiŋi.
21Nii mo! Teo konto déem jege amo chega.
Leile, ko laam nam yage-ne mo ne ka-tola tei!
Teo kom déem su de chega mo,
ye nɔn-ŋona de ya zoore ko wone.
Nɔn-gora laam nam mo wora.
22Abam déem jege lam ne lu-nyenno mo.
Á laam nam jigi wo-yɔɔro.
Boboa ne to, á déem ye sa-ŋona mo.
Na laam nam mo gwaane ba wone.
23Abam nakwa bam ye paweero mo,
ye ba me de ŋweena.
Ba maama swoi kalipera kikia mo,
ye ba duri ba tɔge pɛɛra kwaga.
Ba yeini ba kweele chega botara tei ne.
Ba nam ba di taane ba bore ba pae kadeina.
24Konto ŋwaane mo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom
na ye Isarele tiina Dam Tu wom to tage jase o we:
“Amo bane wó zaŋe abam balo na jigi a dona to baŋa ne,
se á daa yé ja cham á ba á pa-ne.
25Amo wó pa ko chɛ abam yera ne,
se a wane a le á yera digiru tem maama,
ne luru na kwɛ lu-nyenno se o le te digiru tei to.
26A maa wó pa abam dedɛɛra de yi-pore-nyena
se ba taa nii á baŋa ne lanyerane,
ne ko déem na ye tei faŋa kam ne to.
Konto kwaga ne nɔɔna laam wó bwoŋi abam yere we,
‘Teo kolo na tɔge chega yerane to’,
de ‘Teo kolo na ke ba chega de Wɛ to.’ ”
27 Baŋa Wɛ wó da o chega kam ŋwaane
o jwoŋi Jerusalem tiina bam o yage.
Balo na pipiri ba jwoori o tei to wó na verem.
28Ko nam ná ye wɛleere keira,
de balo na ve Baŋa Wɛ to maama,
o wó meere-ba mo pa se ba jei.
29Chaveera wó ja abam,
de á na kwei á teena á daŋe tangwana baŋa ne,
ye á daare á zuli jwona liri-mwa tiina kara wone to.
30Abam wó ji ne tei-zɔŋɔ kolo vɔɔro na kwaare to,
de gaare delo na gɛ na se ba ma ba yage-de to mo.
31Dedɛɛra wó ji ne lɔŋɔ mo tei,
ye ba totoŋ-balwaaro de ji ne min-cheŋo de zwɛ-ko,
Nɔɔna bam tete de ba kikia maama maa wó chɔge lela
ne mini na zwɛ wonnu tei to.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o jwoŋi-ba o yage.

english_text:
Peace That Lasts Forever
1This is the message I was given about Judah and Jerusalem:
2In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills;
every nation will rush to it.
3Many people will come and say,
“Let's go to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
4 He will settle arguments
between nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never make war
or attack one another.
5People of Israel, let's live
by the light of the Lord.
Following Sinful Customs
6Our Lord, you have deserted
your people, Israel,
because they follow customs
of nations from the east.
They worship Philistine gods
and are close friends
of foreigners.
7They have endless treasures
of silver and gold;
they have countless horses
and war chariots.
8Everywhere in the country
they worship the idols
they have made.
9And so, all of them
will be ashamed and disgraced.
Don't forgive them!
A Day of Judgment
10 Every one of you,
go hide among the rocks
and in the ground,
because the Lord is fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious.
11When the Lord comes,
everyone who is proud
will be made humble,
and the Lord alone
will be honored.
12The Lord All-Powerful
has chosen a day
when those who are proud
and conceited
will be put down.
13The tall and towering
cedars of Lebanon
will be destroyed.
So will the oak trees of Bashan,
14all high mountains and hills,
15every strong fortress,
16all the seagoing ships,
and every beautiful boat.
17When that day comes,
everyone who is proud
will be put down.
Only the Lord will be honored.
18Idols will be gone for good.
19You had better hide
in caves and holes—
the Lord will be fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious
when he comes to terrify
people on earth.
20On that day everyone will throw
to the moles and bats
their idols of silver and gold
they made to worship.
21The Lord will be fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious
when he comes to terrify
people on earth—
they will hide in caves
and in the hills.
22Stop trusting the power
of humans.
They are all going to die,
so how can they help?
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋa wó bere jaja
1 Baŋa Wɛ déem na le wonnu telo na tɛ Judah de Jerusalem taane o bere Amozi bu Izaya to mo tento:
2Maŋa wó ba ye Baŋa Wɛ diga kam na zege peo kolo yuu ne to na yere ko dwoni logo baŋa jei maama. Ko wó taa zege wɛɛne vili-vili se ko dwoni peero tem maama. Dwi maama tiina wó taa nwoŋi ba teene dem ne ba twoŋi daane taa ba yɔɔre da.
3Dwia yera yera maa wó ba da ye ba ta ba bere daane we,
“Pa-na se dé vo dé di Baŋa Wɛ peo kom yuu
se dé zuli Jakob Wɛ wom o diga kam ne.
Wonto wó bere debam o chwei sem,
se debam de wane dé taa tɔge-se.”
Kokuri to, da yam konto ne Wɛ bera yam wó zege Zion ne mo
ya jage jei maama ne.
Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam maa wó nwoŋi Jerusalem ne
ka yi nɔɔna maama.
4Logo baŋa dwi tiina balo maama ná jege daane,
Wɛ wó fɔge-ba o ke daane ye o lwɛ ba jara yam.
Ba maa wó kwei ba jara-keim se-zɔɔro ba ma lu vaane,
se ba chichwoa yam de pipiri ya ji lare ya pa-ba.
Teo daa bá kwaare jara de ko dwoŋi.
Nɔɔna de daa bá zamese jara keim.
5Jakob dwi tiina bam, nam ba-na!
Pa-na se dé taa vei pwooni delo Baŋa Wɛ na tiŋi o pa debam to wone.
Baŋa Wɛ dɛ-kamunu kom taane
6 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo yɔɔre n dole n nɔɔna Jakob dwi tiina bam n yage mo.
Ba yeini ba tɔge wɛ-puli seeni liri-mwa tiina kikia,
ye ba beeri yi-nara ne Filisi tiina bam na ke tei to mo.
Ba maa me de dwi-gɛ tiina de ba chullu tem.
7Ba teo kom maama su de lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa mo.
Ba jejegero tem ware te jeeli te ti.
Ba tega kam ta su de sisein-nɔɔna mo,
ye ba ware ba sisei-torokooro tem ni se ba ga ba ti.
8Ba tega kam maama su de jwo-yɔɔro mo.
Ba maa tiiri ba zuli wonnu telo ba tete je sem na ke to.
9Nɔɔna gwooni ba tete ya yiga ne,
ye ba daare ba vwi ba yibia tega ne ba pa-ya.
Konto ŋwaane, yé kwei ba wɛleera yam n chɛ-ba.
10Nam véi-na peero tem gugworru ne,
se á seigi tega kam wone.
Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ kom jege foone mo
ye o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom de tiini ko nye.
11Dɛ dem konto ná yia,
nabiina balo na gwooni ba dwonna to wó to tega ne.
Balo na bere ba tete kamunim to de wó jwoori ba ba tega.
Baŋa Wɛ yere dem yerane mo wó zaŋe wɛɛne.
12Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ le dɛ mo o tiŋi dáa ne,
se o waare balo na jege fia ye ba bere we ba fuŋi to.
Dɛ dem konto ne banto maama wó to tega ne.
13O ta wó gwoni Lebanon tei-dedwaaro tem,
de tei-zwanno tem na wo Basan laŋa kam ne to o de tega ne.
14O maa wó pa pe-dedwaaro tem
de zwonnu telo na wo wɛɛne to jwoori tega,
15ye di-dedwaaro dwi maama
de teo kabiri-lilirru dwi maama de to tega ne.
16Ko ta ná ye nabwooru telo na beeri pipiu ŋwaane to,
de telo dwi na lana to,
te maama de wó chɔge dɛ dem konto ne.
17Nabiina kamunim kikia maama wó ti mo
pa se ba fia kam ji kafɛ.
Baŋa Wɛ yere dem yerane mo wó zaŋe wɛɛne.
18Jwona yam nam lage ya pɔpɔ ya jei mo.
19Nɔɔna wó duri mo ba vo ba seigi peero gugworru wone,
dedaane tega kuri bɔɔna wone,
maŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó zaŋe o fugi-ba to.
Kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ jege foone o pa-ba,
ye o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom de tiini ko nye mo.
20Dɛ dem konto nam ná yia, nɔɔna wó kwei ba jwona
yalo ba na mɛ sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno ba mɔ se ba taa zuli to mo
ba dole ba yage,
se twarro de jenjwaano taa kare te kekare ya baŋa ne.
21Ba laam wó vo ba seigi ba tete peero bɔɔna wone,
de gugworru wone,
se ba wane ba lu Baŋa Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom.
Konto wó ke maŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó zaŋe o fugi nabiina to mo.
22Yé ta‑á jege-na nabiina chega.
Ba yɔɔre ba bwona mo lage-lage ne siu tei.
Dam dɔ mo ba jega se á sale ba yera ne?

english_text:
Judgment on Jerusalem and Judah
1The mighty Lord All-Powerful
is going to take away
from Jerusalem and Judah
everything you need—
your bread and water,
* 2soldiers and heroes,
judges and prophets,
leaders and army officers,
3officials and advisors,
fortunetellers and others
who tell the future.
4He will let children and babies
become your rulers.
5You will each be cruel
to friends and neighbors.
Young people will insult
their elders;
no one will show respect
to those who deserve it.
6Some of you will grab hold
of a relative and say,
“You still have a coat.
Be our leader and rule
this pile of ruins.”
7But the answer will be,
“I can't do you any good.
Don't make me your leader.
There's no food or clothing
left in my house.”
8Jerusalem and Judah,
you rebelled against
your glorious Lord—
your words and your actions,
made you stumble and fall.
9The look on your faces shows
that you are sinful as Sodom,
and you don't try to hide it.
You are in for trouble,
and you have brought it all
on yourselves.
The Wrong Kind of Leaders
10Tell those who obey God,
“You're very fortunate—
you will be rewarded
for what you have done.”
11Tell those who disobey,
“You're in big trouble—
what you did to others
will come back to you.”
12Though you are God's people,
you are ruled and abused
by women and children.
You are confused by leaders
who guide you
down the wrong path.
13The Lord is ready to accuse
and judge all nations.
14He will even judge
you rulers and leaders
of his own nation.
You destroyed his vineyard
and filled your houses
by robbing the poor.
15The Lord All-Powerful says,
“You have crushed my people
and rubbed in the dirt
the faces of the poor.”
The Women of Jerusalem
16The Lord says:
The women of Jerusalem
are proud and strut around,
winking shamelessly.
They wear anklets that jingle
and call attention
to the way they walk.
17But I, the Lord, will cover
their heads with sores,
and I will uncover
their private parts.
18-23When that day comes, I will take away from those women all the fine jewelry they wear on their ankles, heads, necks, ears, arms, noses, fingers, and on their clothes. I will remove their veils, their belts, their perfume, their magic charms, their royal robes, and all their fancy dresses, hats, and purses.
24In place of perfume,
there will be a stink;
in place of belts,
there will be ropes;
in place of fancy hairdos,
they will have bald heads.
Instead of expensive clothes,
they will wear sackcloth;
instead of beauty,
they will have ugly scars.
25The fighting men of Jerusalem
will be killed in battle.
26The city will mourn
and sit in the dirt,
emptied of its people.
translation_text:
Lɛɛro wó ba Judah tiina baŋa
1Nii-na ywo!
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Paŋwa to ti o yiga mo
se o le Jerusalem tiina bam de Judah tiina bam
ya na teege wonnu telo maama baŋa ne to.
Ko maa ye ba wodiiru de ba na bam mo konto.
2O ta wó le ba bembɛ sem, de ba jar-keira bam,
de ba dedɛɛra bam, de ba sampwori sem de.
O maa wó le vora bam, de nakwa bam ba wone.
3O daa ta wó le ba jar-keira yiga tiina, de ba nɔn-yerro tem,
de ba swa tiina bam, de ba gwaro tem, de ba liri-mwa tiina bam de.
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
4“A lage a kuri busɔ-nyena mo se ba taa ye teo kom dedɛɛra,
se ba kwei boboŋ-yɔɔro ba taa maa nii teo kom.
5Nɔɔna wó da ko ŋwaane se ba taa bɛɛse daane mo.
Baaro wó nwoŋi o dwoŋi kwaga ne,
ye fara de nwoŋi da-kwaga ne.
Bia daa bá taa nege nɔn-kwe.
Nɔn-yɔɔro de maa wó dwoni de nɔn-yum.
6Kanto maŋa ne nɔɔno wó vo o kwo sɔŋɔ
o kuri o dwi nɔɔno dedoa ye o ta ded‑o o we,
‘Nmo na jege gɔrɔ n zoore to ŋwaane,
ta‑n ye dé yiga tu se n le debam lɛɛro tento wone.’
7Konto tu de maa wó leiri o ta jaja we,
‘Amo bá wane abam a jwoŋi a yage.
A ba jege wodiu, naa gwaaro a sɔŋɔ ne.
Konto ŋwaane, yé le-ne-na se a ji nɔɔna bam yiga tu.’ ”
8Nii-na! Jerusalem teo kom yɔɔre ko titirigi mo se ko to!
Judah kateiri dem maama wora de toe mo!
Ba ni taane de ba kikia maama ba tɔge Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa.
Ba maa mae ba kwaga ba ya wonto de o paare dem.
9Ba yibia maama bere we ba ba lage Baŋa Wɛ ni taane.
Ba maa yɔɔre ba ke wɛleera jaja,
ne Sodom tiina déem na ke tei to.
Lɛɛro mo wó yi-ba!
Ko maa wó zege ba tete yera ne.
10Ko nam ná ye balo na zege de chega to,
ta de-ba we, wonnu wó tɔge chwoŋa te pa-ba.
Ba wó na ba totoŋa yam nyɔɔre.
11Lɛɛro taa wo puseŋ-nyena bam baŋa ne!
Cham mo lage de yi-ba!
Ba lage ba na ba totoŋ-balwaaro tem ŋweero mo.
12Busɔ-nyena mo jege a nɔɔna bam ba bɛɛsa.
Kaana de maa jege-ba ba nia.
Amo nɔɔna bam, á yiga tiina bam mo jaane abam ba ywori.
Ba maa pae se á tusi chwoŋa kam.
13 Baŋa Wɛ tete nam mo tu se o saŋe nɔɔna bam.
O jege taane mo de-ba.
14 Baŋa Wɛ lage o di o nɔɔna nakwa bam,
de ba dedɛɛra bam taane, ye o ta de-ba we:
“Abam mo jaane amo Vini teeni kara kam á chɔge.
Á ta daare á vere wonnu nabwona tei ne
á ja á zo á tete sam wone á tiŋi da.
15Wɔ mo pɛ abam chwoŋa
se á ta‑á yɔɔre á peene a nɔɔna bam?
Á ta maa jege yiniga tiina jana á nyɔa.”
Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.
16 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we:
“Jerusalem teo kaana bam tiini ba bere ba tete mo.
Ba maa kare ba via,
ye ba ba nii ba nae nɔɔn-nɔɔno.
Ba maa jege ba yia ba soge baara se ba da ba kwaga.
Ba maa na vei to, ba jege ba kura mo ba dole ba bere nɔɔna.
Ba maa kare ba vei ye ba na-jullu tem dɔne de sɔɔ.
17Konto ŋwaane, a nam wó pa se ŋɔn-daala jeini ba yuni tem ne,
ye a daare-ba a zege de kuri-nɔrɔ yerane.”
18Maŋa kam konto ná yia, Baŋa Wɛ wó le Jerusalem kaana bam yera zela yalo na pae-ba lam to, se o daare-ba o zege kafɛ. Ko maa ye ba na-jullu tem, de ba zambila yam, de ba yum lu-nyenno tem, 19de ba zwa-kwana yam, de ba je bɛ sem, de ba gare-fefale selo na kwoli ba yibia to. 20O ta wó le ba yu-kwale sem, de ba ban-jullu tem, de ba vovwe sem, de ba talwoŋ-ywei sem, de ba swa-gungwollu tem, 21de ba jafola yam, de ba momwa kwana yam. 22Ko nam ta ná ye ba gare-nyenno, de ba gare-dedwaaro, de ba gare-danno tem, de ba tampɔro tem, 23de ba niiru tem, de ba gare-fefale sem, de ba yuu gare-yia yam, de ba gare-woru tem, Wɛ wó le wonnu tento maama mo kaana bam tei ne.
24Ba wó taa teene se lwom na ywona to mo zaŋe,
ye ba yera lwom nam mo wó chɛ nɔɔna momwa ne.
Ba ya ná teene teiŋa vovwe,
ba wó na ŋone yerane mo.
Ba ya ná teene se ba yu-ywei taa lana,
ba yuni tem wó fe te daare yu-kapwooru mo.
Ba ya ná boŋe se ba zo gare-nyenno,
ba wó zo gare-nyenyaaro mo.
Ba lam dem wó leiri de ji wo-yɔɔro tento dwoŋi mo.
25Á teo kom baara bam wó te jara-keim baŋa ne mo.
Á bembɛ sem de wó tɔge jara baŋa ne mo ba te.
26Jerusalem teo manchwo-peo kom tete wó taa keeri mo ga ŋɔɔ,
teo kom na yɔɔre ko chɔge ye nɔɔna daa tera ko wone to ŋwaane.
Ko maa wó taa nye de kaane na jei tega ne bwori
ye o wo yɔɔre ko chɔge to.

english_text:
1When this happens, seven women will grab the same man, and each of them will say, “I'll buy my own food and clothes! Just marry me and take away my disgrace.”
The Lord Will Bless His People Who Survive
2The time is coming when the Lord will make his land fruitful and glorious again, and the people of Israel who survive will take great pride in what the land produces. 3Everyone who is left alive in Jerusalem will be called special, 4after the Lord sends a fiery judgment to clean the city and its people of their violent deeds.
5 Then the Lord will cover the whole city and its meeting places with a thick cloud each day and with a flaming fire each night. God's own glory will be like a huge tent that covers everything. 6It will provide shade from the heat of the sun and a place of shelter and protection from storms and rain.
translation_text:
1Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia,
kaana barepɛ mo lage ba to
ba gorege baaro dedoa,
ye ba ta ded‑o we,
“Dé wó taa jege dé tete ni-wodiu,
ye dé daare dé beeri dé tete yera gwaaro.
Nam sɛ se dé kwei n yere dé ke dé yera ne,
se ba taa mae-de ba bwoi debam,
se ba yé ke debam chaveera we dé wo zo banna ŋwaane.”
Baŋa Wɛ wó kwɛ teo kom
2Maŋa kam konto ne Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se tega kam teeni de gaaro dwi maama puli dedɛ se ka lam de ka nenɔŋa tiini ko gaale. Tega kam wó ke wodiiru dedɛ ka pa Isarele tiina balo ta na daare to, se ba taa jege wopwolo de teera ka ŋwaane. 3Ba wó taa bwoi Zion teo tiina ta na daare ye ba wo Jerusalem ne to we, “Wose tiina.” Banto yera mo popone ya tiŋi we, ba wó wori chɔgem dem baŋa ne. 4Kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ mo lage o zare Zion kaana bam digiru tem o yage. O lage o toŋe waarem ba wone ne mini mo tei, o ma o zare jana balo na taare Jerusalem teo kom to. 5Baŋa Wɛ laam maa wó pa woro ba ko kwoli Zion peo kom de nɔn-kɔgɔ kolo maama na jeeri da to. Wea ne nyoa wó taa nye de kunkwoŋo mo ko kwoli jei sem. Tete ne min-vogo de maa wó taa wora ko nyeena. Ko wó taa ye ne teo kom de ko lam maama wo pwoŋa kuri ne mo. 6Tento maa wó taa kwoli-ba pa se ba na woro wea funyogo maŋa ne, ye ba daare ba na dalem jei vo-dɛɔ de doa maŋa ne.

english_text:
A Song about a Vineyard
The Lord said:
1 I will sing a song
about my friend's vineyard
that was on the side
of a fertile hill.
2My friend dug the ground,
removed the stones,
and planted the best vines.
He built a watchtower
and dug a pit in rocky ground
for pressing the grapes.
He hoped they would be sweet,
but bitter grapes
were all it produced.
3Listen, people of Jerusalem
and of Judah!
You be the judge of me
and my vineyard.
4What more could I have done
for my vineyard?
I hoped for sweet grapes,
but bitter grapes
were all that grew.
5Now I will let you know
what I am going to do.
I will cut down the hedge
and tear down the wall.
My vineyard will be trampled
and left in ruins.
6It will turn into a desert,
neither pruned nor hoed;
it will be covered
with thorns and briars.
I will command the clouds
not to send rain.
7I am the Lord All-Powerful!
Israel is the vineyard,
and Judah is the garden
I tended with care.
I had hoped for honesty
and for justice,
but dishonesty
and cries for mercy
were all I found.
Isaiah Condemns Social Injustice
8You are in for trouble! You take over house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone else in all the land. 9But the Lord All-Powerful has made this promise to me:
Those large and beautiful homes will be left empty, with no one to take care of them. 10Four hectares of grapevines will produce only 27 liters of juice, and 180 liters of seed will produce merely 18 liters of grain.
11 You are in for trouble! You get up early to start drinking, and you keep it up late into the night. 12At your drinking parties you have the music of stringed instruments, tambourines, and flutes. But you never even think about all the Lord has done, 13and so his people know nothing about him. That's why many of you will be dragged off to foreign lands. Your leaders will starve to death, and everyone else will suffer from thirst.
14The world of the dead has opened its mouth wide and is eagerly waiting for the leaders of Jerusalem and for its noisy crowds, especially for those who take pride in that city. 15Its citizens have been put down, and its proud people have been brought to shame. 16But the holy Lord God All-Powerful is praised, because he has shown who he is by bringing justice. 17His people will be like sheep grazing in their own pasture, and they will take off what was left by others.
18You are in for trouble! The lies you tell are like ropes by which you drag along sin and evil. 19And you say, “Let the holy God of Israel hurry up and do what he has promised, so we can see it for ourselves.” 20You are headed for trouble! You say wrong is right, darkness is light, and bitter is sweet.
21You think you are clever and smart. 22And you are great at drinking and mixing drinks. But you are in for trouble. 23You accept bribes to let the guilty go free, and you cheat the innocent out of a fair trial.
24You will go up in flames like straw and hay! You have rejected the teaching of the holy Lord God All-Powerful of Israel. Now your roots will rot, and your blossoms will turn to dust.
25You are the Lord's people, but you made him terribly angry, and he struck you with his mighty arm. Mountains shook, and dead bodies covered the streets like garbage. The Lord is still angry, and he is ready to strike you again.
Foreign Nations Will Attack
26The Lord has signaled for the foreign nations to come and attack you. He has already whistled, and they are coming as fast as they can. 27None of them are tired. They don't sleep or get drowsy, and they run without stumbling. Their belts don't come loose; their sandal straps don't break. 28Their arrows are sharp, and their bows are ready. The hoofs of their horses are hard as flint; the wheels of their war chariots turn as fast as a whirlwind.
29They roar and growl like fierce young lions as they grab their victims and drag them off where no one can rescue them. 30On the day they attack, they will roar like the ocean. And across the land you will see nothing but darkness and trouble, because the light of day will be covered by thick clouds.
translation_text:
Vini teeni kara kam leiŋa
1Amo wó leeni leiŋa a pa a na swoi wolo to,
ka na bere o Vini teeni kara yera taane to ŋwaane:
Wolo a na swoi to ya jege o teeni kara mo,
o na jeiri-ka zwoŋo kolo tega na lana to baŋa ne.
2O ma va tega kam konto maama lanyerane,
ye o le kandwa yalo na wo ka wone to.
O ta ma jeiri Vini teeni na lana to ka wone.
O ma pu vwei se o taa maa yere-ka.
O ta ma lu gwoŋo se ba taa ŋoke Vini tio-bia nyoa ko wone.
O laam maa jei o cheiga se tio-bia bam be wo-ŋona.
De ko de, ba jigi wo-kanywaano mo.
3“Abam balo nam na zoore Jerusalem teo
de Judah kateiri dem maama ne to,
Zo-na amo de a kara kam tetare á bore bora.
4Bɛ mo a ya daa wó ke de a kara kam
se ka ke lanyerane, ye a wo ke?
A nam ya na beeri wo-ŋona to,
bɛŋwaane mo a kara kam leigi wo-kanywaano yerane?
5Nam nii a na boŋe se a ke tei
de a teeni kara kam to.
A lage a le wonnu telo ya na chege-ka to mo,
se a daare se kara kam chɔge.
A maa wó bwori ka kabira kam a de tega ne,
se vara wane ba zo ka wone ba nɔne teeni dem.
6A ta wó pa se gaaro yerane jwoŋi kara kam.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá gwoni teeni dem nɛ se o kwɛ-de,
naa o va tega kam.
Ga-cheiŋo de sabare mo wó su kara kam maama.
Amo laam maa wó pa kunkwonnu tem ni
se te yé pa doa ne ka wone.”
7Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ teeni kara kam
mo ye Isarele dwi dem.
Judah dwi tiina bam maa ye gaare delo o yi na su to.
O nam ya na beeri se nɔn-ŋonne taa wora to,
nɔn-gora yerane mo o nɛa.
O maa na lage se chega taa toŋe to,
chɔgem mo o nɛa.
Lɛɛro de waarem taane
8Lɛɛro wó yi abam balo na lɔ sam dedɛ
á woli da-baŋa ne to.
Á ta ma beeri kare á jwoŋa á daŋe da-baŋa ne.
Ko ná woli fee, abam daa bá daare jei á tiŋi,
ye á yerane laam mo wó ta‑á zoore tega kam ne.
9Amo nigi Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage o we:
“Abam sɔ-fwaaro tento dedɛ wó ji sɔ-korro mo,
se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé taa zoore de wone.
10Nɔɔno ná jeiri Vini teeni dedɛ kara kamunu wone,
tio-bia bam bá lɛɛre sana ba su kunkwolo dedoa.
Nɔɔno maa ná kwei wo-dwa bwɛ fuga o du tega kam ne,
o wó na wodiu bɔŋa dedoa yerane mo ko baŋa ne.”
11Lɛɛro wó yi balo na yeini ba zaŋe tetete
ba yɔɔre ba wowole ba beeri sana jei to.
Ba maa maŋe sana nyɔɔm ne taa se ko yi tete-koro maŋa,
ye sana bam jwoŋi ba boboŋa maama.
12Ba ná jege kuri ba di, ba jege kwanno mo ba maga.
Ba ta maa jege senseŋa, de wui ba ke sɔɔ,
ye ba nyɔ sana.
Se ko ná ye Baŋa Wɛ, ba yiga tera de o na jege totoŋa yalo
o ke ba tetare ne to.
Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa totoŋa yam ba sae ba yera kɔtaa!
13Mo kokuri ba lage ba kale Wɛ nɔɔna bam
ba ja vo sa-teo yiga yiga,
ba na ba ni o taane kuri to ŋwaane.
Kana wó go ba teo nɔn-yum tem mo,
ye na-nyɔm de ja ba nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama.
14Konto ŋwaane mo churu ke ko fera ko ke daane,
pa se ko yale ko tete ko ke da,
se ko li nɔɔna bam maama.
Toone wó ja teo kom dedɛɛra, de nabwona,
de sa-nyɔra balo na ke sɔɔ bɔge-bɔge to.
15Nɔɔna bam wó ba tega ne mo.
Boyere-nyena de wó di ba chaveera.
16Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere dem mo wó zaŋe wɛɛne,
o chega borem dem na wó bere jaja to ŋwaane.
Wo-pwoŋo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó tɔge o chega kam baŋa ne mo
se o bere we o seene o ye wose.
17Pei laam maa wó taa kare se di wodiu teo kom wone,
ne ko ye se tete pwola mo to.
Veira de wó ba ba zege naduna bam di-dwonnu wone
ba taa di ba sui.
18Lɛɛro wó yi balo na me de ba wɛleera yam
ye ba ware-ya ba yage to.
Ba maa jaane-ya ba vei jei maama,
nenɛɛne nɔɔno na vaŋe toroko de ŋone tei to.
19Ba ta maa tɛ ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ nam ke lela
o toŋe kolo o na we o wó ke to,
se dé yɔɔre dé na.
O boboŋa na jaane se o ke kolo to
o nam jege se o seene o ke mo
se dé lɔre ko ni ne.
Kokuri to, o bere we o ye Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom
na zeini o nɔɔna Isarele tiina to mo.”
20Lɛɛro wó yi balo na pipiri lwarem se de taa ye wo-laao,
ye ba daare ba kwei wo-laaro pa te ye lwarem to.
Banto dwi yeini ba kwei lim mo ba ma ji pwooni,
ye ba daare ba pa pwooni dem ji lim.
Ba ta maa pae se wo-chɛɛro ye telo na sona to,
ye wo-sonno jwoori te ye wo-chɛɛro.
21Lɛɛro wó yi balo na boŋe ba tete ne we
banto swa mo dwoi nɔɔna maama to.
Banto pae se ba tete swa mo jege-ba ya gana.
22Lɛɛro wó yi balo na ye bembɛ sa-nyɔre baŋa ne,
ye ba tiini ba yei sana keim ba dwoi nɔɔna maama to.
23Taane dim baŋa ne ba swoi se ba taa jwoŋi dim mo
ye ba yage balo na gɛ bora to pa ba viiri zɛɛra.
Ba ta ma da ko ŋwaane ba vane nɔn-ŋona ba bora.
24Konto ŋwaane, banto kugu jei mo wó ŋɔɔle,
ne mini na di ga-korro kula
pa se te jei lela tei to.
Ba punnu tem de wó jage te jei,
ne vio na yeini ko jage fwogo tei to.
Kokuri to, ba ve Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom
na ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu to nia yam mo.
Ba ta ma nii o taane dem ba gwooni.
25Konto nam mo pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ bane tiini de fuli de o nɔɔna bam.
O yɔɔre o zeiŋi o jeŋa mo se o mage-ba o de tega ne.
Peero tem wó ziziŋi,
ye twa de faare teo kom chwei yuu ne, ne weero tei to.
De konto maama de nam, Baŋa Wɛ bane dem ta bá zuri.
O ta wó twe o jeŋa kam mo se o waare-ba.
26 Baŋa Wɛ wó zeiŋi tuta mo
se o pa dwi-gɛ tiina balo na wo yiga yiga to
zaŋe ba ba ba kwaare jara de o nɔɔna bam.
O ma fwooli o bwoŋi-ba se ba ba.
Nii ba na ke lela ba wuuri tei ba beene!
27Ba nɔɔna bam wolowolo ba buga.
Ba nam ba tiri ba toe tega ne.
Dɔɔne ba tui ba wolowolo yibia ne.
Ba wolowolo kila wo bwoli o teiŋa ne.
Ba natera yam de nam wo bwoli ba nɛ sem ne.
28Ba che-tɛɛra yam nia yɔɔre ya di mo bileim-bileim.
Ba tɛ sem tete de ma saŋe se ti se se ta.
Ba sisein-nɔɔna bam napɔɔna dana
ne kandwa na ye tei to mo.
Ba torokooro tem nɛ de ye ne vo-kekara na ye tei to mo.
29Ba tiguri-kaasa nye ne nywoŋo na laare tei to mo.
Ba maa yɔɔre ba laare ne nywon-pɔle na ŋuuri tei to.
Ba suuri mo ye ba toe ba gorege ba nɔna yam.
Ba nam na jege-ya ba maa kɛ to,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se kotu jwoŋi-ya o yage.
30Maŋa kam konto ná yia
ye ba suuri balo ba na jaane to baŋa ne,
ko wó taa nye de naneo kom na wuuri tei to mo.
Nɔɔno maa ná bare se o nii tega kam na ye tei to,
kotu wó na we lim mo jwoŋi jei sem maama
ye wo-chechɔgɔ de gaale.
Kunkwonnu mo wó kwoli pwooni delo na maŋe de wora to,
pa se de ji lim yerane.

english_text:
A Vision of the Lord in the Temple
1 In the year that King Uzziah died, I had a vision of the Lord. He was on his throne high above, and his robe filled the temple. 2Flaming creatures with six wings each were flying over him. They covered their faces with two of their wings and their bodies with two more. They used the other two wings for flying, 3 as they shouted,
“Holy, holy, holy,
Lord All-Powerful!
The earth is filled
with your glory.”
4 As they shouted, the doorposts of the temple shook, and the temple was filled with smoke. 5Then I cried out, “I'm doomed! Everything I say is sinful, and so are the words of everyone around me. Yet I have seen the King, the Lord All-Powerful.”
6One of the flaming creatures flew over to me with a burning coal that it had taken from the altar with a pair of metal tongs. 7It touched my lips with the hot coal and said, “This has touched your lips. Your sins are forgiven, and you are no longer guilty.”
8After this, I heard the Lord ask, “Is there anyone I can send? Will someone speak for us?”
“I'll go,” I answered. “Send me!”
9 Then the Lord told me to go and speak this message to the people:
“You will listen and listen,
but never understand.
You will look and look,
but never see.”
The Lord also said,
10“Make these people stubborn!
Make them stop up
their ears,
cover their eyes,
and fail to understand.
Don't let them turn to me
and be healed.”
11Then I asked the Lord, “How long will this last?”
The Lord answered:
Until their towns are destroyed and their houses are deserted, until their fields are empty, 12and I have sent them far away, leaving their land in ruins. 13If only a tenth of the people are left, even they will be destroyed. But just as stumps remain after trees have been cut down, some of my chosen ones will be left.
translation_text:
Wɛ toŋe Izaya
1Bene delo wone Pɛ Yuzia na tege to, mo a nɛ a Teiru Wɛ wom. O déem jei paare yituŋu kolo na tiini ko ye wɛ-wɛ to yuu ne mo. O gare-dedɔrɔ kom nabili maa su Wɛ diga kam maama. 2Serafi tiina déem mo zege o baŋa ne. Ba maama déem jege vɔna yaredo yaredo mo. Ba jege vɔna yalei mo ba maa kwoli ba yibia, yalei de maa kwoli ba nɛ, ye ba daare yalei ba jege ba jaana. 3Ba laam maa mɔɔne leiŋa ba bere daane, ye ba daare ba sɛ-ka ba we:
“Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ye wo-pwoŋo tu mo.
O maa yɔɔre o ye wose ye o dwoŋi tera.
O nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom mo su tega baŋa ni maama.”
4Ba kwori sem sɔɔ ma pa se Wɛ diga kam ziziŋi ka yi ka kuri na jaane mɛ to, ye nyoa yɔɔre ka pe ka wo kom maama.
5A na nɛ konto to, mo a tage a we, “Lɛɛro yi amo! A tege a ti! Kokuri to, a ye wolo ni taane na digiri to mo. A maa zoore de balo ni taane de na digiri to. De ko de, amo ta nɛ Pɛ wom na ye Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ to.”
6Serafi tiina bam dedoa ma jaane o yi a tei, ye o zei min-chale o déem na mɛ tasɔɔne mo o le-de bimbini dem baŋa ne to o ja o ba. 7O laam ma kwei-de o dwei a ni, ye o ta de amo o we, “Nii ywo! Min-chale dento na dwei n ni-vɔɔro to, n tusim dem saare de yage, ye n wɛleera yam daa tere n yuu ne.”
8Amo laam ma ni a Teiru wom kwora, o na bwei o we, “Wɔ mo amo wó toŋe se o ja debam kwora o vo a nɔɔna bam tei?” Amo de ma leiri a we, “Nii amo da! Toŋe-ne!”
9O laam maa we:
“Véi n ta de nɔɔna banto we:
‘Abam ná maŋe á cheigi tei maama de,
á bá ni wonnu kuri.
Abam nam ná kwaane á nii tei maama de,
á bá lɔre kolokolo.’
10Yage nɔɔna bam se ba boboŋa jei,
ye ba zwa yam de kwareme.
Nam ta pa se ba yia yam dwei.
Ko ná dae konto, ba wó ma ba yia ba nii ba na wonnu,
ba daare ba ni de ba zwa yam,
ye ba ma ba boboŋa ba lɔre wonnu kuri,
se ba pipiri ba jwoori amo tei,
ye ba daare ba na fɔgem.”
11Amo de ma bwei‑o a we,
“Amo Teiru, wonnu tento wó taa ke taa
se te vo te maŋe yei ne mo?”
O ma leiri-ne o we,
“Ko jege se ko vo ko yi maŋa kalo ba teene dem na wó ji di-dwonnu
pa se nɔɔna ware de wone se ba taa zoora to.
Nɔɔna wó duri ba daare ba sam,
ye ba tega kam maama de wó chɔge ka ti.
12 Baŋa Wɛ wó zeili o nɔɔna bam
o ja vo o yage teo kodwoŋi ne yiga yiga.
O ta wó daare ba tega kam pa ka taa tigi yɔɔ yerane.
13Nɔɔna fuga maama wone dedoa tete mo ná daare da,
tega kam daa ta wó na chɔgem mo.
Ko nam wó taa ye nenɛɛne ba na gwoni tei-zɔŋɔ,
ye ko kugu kom ta daare tega kam ne tei to mo.
Kugu kom daa wó jwoori ko kwi
se Isarele dwi dem taa ye wose.”

english_text:
Isaiah Offers Hope to King Ahaz
1 Ahaz, the son of Jotham and the grandson of Uzziah, was king of Judah when King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah son of Remaliah of Israel went to attack Jerusalem. But they were not able to do what they had planned. 2When news reached the royal palace that Syria had joined forces with Israel, King Ahaz and everyone in Judah were so terrified that they shook like trees in a windstorm.
3Then the Lord said to me:
Take your son Shearjashub and go see King Ahaz. You will find him on the road near the cloth makers' shops at the end of the canal that brings water from the upper pool. 4Tell Ahaz to stop worrying. There's no need for him to be afraid of King Rezin and King Pekah. They are very angry, but they are nothing more than a dying fire. Ahaz doesn't need to fear 5their evil threats 6to invade and defeat Judah and Jerusalem and to let the son of Tabeel be king in his place.
7I, the Lord, promise that this will never happen. 8-9Damascus is just the capital of Syria, and King Rezin rules only in Damascus. Samaria is just the capital of Israel, and King Pekah rules only in Samaria. But in less than 65 years, Israel will be destroyed. And if Ahaz and his officials don't trust me, they will be defeated.
A Son Named Immanuel
10Once again the Lord God spoke to King Ahaz. This time he said, 11“Ask me for proof that my promise will come true. Ask for something to happen deep in the world of the dead or high in the heavens above.”
12“No, Lord,” Ahaz answered. “I won't test you!”
13Then I said:
Listen, every one of you in the royal family of David. You have already tried my patience. Now you are trying God's patience by refusing to ask for proof. 14 But the Lord will still give you proof. A virgin is pregnant; she will have a son and will name him Immanuel. 15-16Even before the boy is old enough to know how to choose between right and wrong, he will eat yogurt and honey, and the countries of the two kings you fear will be destroyed. 17But the Lord will make more trouble for your people and your kingdom than any of you have known since Israel broke away from Judah. He will even bring the king of Assyria to attack you.
The Threat of an Invasion
18When that time comes, the Lord will whistle, and armies will come from Egypt like flies and from Assyria like bees. 19They will settle everywhere—in the deep valleys and between the rocks, on every thornbush and all over the pastureland.
20The Lord will pay the king of Assyria to bring a razor from across the Euphrates River and shave your head and every hair on your body, including your beard.
21Anyone who is able to save only one young cow and two sheep, 22will have enough milk to make yogurt. In fact, everyone left in the land will eat yogurt and honey.
23Vineyards that had 1,000 vines and were worth 1,000 pieces of silver will turn into thorn patches. 24You will go there to hunt with your bow and arrows, because the whole country will be covered with thornbushes. 25The hills where you once planted crops will be overgrown with thorns and thistles. You will be afraid to go there, and your cattle, sheep, and goats will be turned loose on those hills.
translation_text:
Imanuwel memaŋe dem
1Jotam bu Ahaz na ye Yuzia naa to déem di Judah teo paare. Maŋa kam konto ne mo Siria teo pɛ Rezin, de Isarele teo pɛ Peka na ye Remalia bu to ke daane se ba jeeri Jerusalem teo kom de jara. Ba nam wo wane teo kom ba di.
2Kwora ma yi pɛ sɔŋɔ kom tiina we, “Siria tiina sɔge ni de Efrayim dwi tiina mo se ba ke jara de debam!” Taane dem ma pa se Ahaz de o nɔɔna bam yera yɔɔre ya sae, ne vo-fɔrɔ na mage teeni ye de zuuli tei to.
3 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Izaya o we, “Nwoŋi de n bu Sear-Jasubi se á vo á jeeri Pɛ Ahaz. Abam wó na‑o na-fera kalo na zoore baŋa seeni chɔgɔ kom to ni ne, se ko maŋe de chwoŋa kam mɛ ba na sɔ gwaaro to. 4Ta ded‑o we:
Ta‑n yei n tete. Pa n bochare taa tiga se n yé ta‑n kɔre foone. Siria teo pɛ Rezin, de o nɔɔna bam, dedaane Remalia bu Peka daa ba jege dam. Banto balei nye ne mini na dwei de daare da-toora yalei tei to mo. Konto ŋwaane, yé pa se n vɔna pare ba bane na zaŋe dede‑m to ŋwaane. 5Chega ŋwaane, Siria teo pɛ, de Isarele teo pɛ, de Efrayim tiina bam ke ni daane se ba ke abam zonne. Ba maa tɛ ba we, 6‘Dé wó vo dé li Judah teo kom mo dé fugi ko nɔɔna bam ye dé daare dé jwoŋi-ko dé taa tei. Dé laam maa wó tiŋi Tabeeli bu wom se o ji ba pɛ.’ 7Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam tage tento mo o we:
‘Chega ŋwaane, ko bá toŋe.
Ba bá ba ba jwoŋi teo konto ba taa tei!
8Kokuri to, Siria ba dana ko dwoi ko te-fɔrɔ Damasika.
Damasika teo kom de nam ba dana ko dwoi ko pɛ Rezin.
Se ko ná ye Efrayim tiina bam,
bena fuseredo-yanu mo daare se ba na chɔgem,
ye ba dwi dem jei.
9Efrayim tiina bam ba dana ba dwoi ba te-fɔrɔ Samaria.
Samaria teo kom de nam ba dana ko dwoi Remalia bu Peka.
Abam ná wo ke á chega de amo,
á bá wane á fɔge á zege de pu-dɛa.’ ”
10Izaya na tage Wɛ kwora kam konto o bere Pɛ Ahaz to mo Baŋa Wɛ daa ta tage de pɛ wom o we, 11“Nam lwoori amo wolo na ye n Tu Baŋa Wɛ to, se a wó ke wo-memaŋe a bere‑m, se n lɔre we a tage chega. Amo wó ke wo-memaŋe ne nmo na lage tei to, ko ná maŋe ko ye tega kuri ne naa wɛyuu ne yiga yiga de.”
12Ahaz ma leiri o we, “Aawo, amo bá sɛ se a maŋe Baŋa Wɛ a nii.”
13Izaya laam ma ta o we, “Cheigi-na, abam balo na nwoŋi Pɛ David dwi dem wone to. Á yeini á daane Wɛ tontoŋena bam mo. Á laam boŋe se á daane Wɛ wolo amo na toŋe a pa‑o to tete mo na? 14Ko nam na ye tei to, Baŋa Wɛ tete mo lage o ke wo-memaŋe o bere abam. Nii-na! Busankan-pwola kam wó ba o ja puga o lo bakeira. O maa wó bwoŋi bu wom yere we ‘Imanuwel’. 15Bu wom ná ke nɔɔno o yi se o taa kuri lam ye o ve lwarem, nayel-pepala de tooro yerane mo wó taa wora se o di. 16Kokuri to, bu wom ta ná wo yi se o pɔɔre lam de lwarem daane, de pwa balei bam nmo zem na kɔre foone de-ba to teene dem jigi di-dwonnu. 17Baŋa Wɛ nam lage o pa ko tiini ko ni nmo, de n nɔɔna bam, de n kwo dwi dem maama mo. Ko zege maŋa kalo Efrayim tiina bam na pwɛ ba tete de Judah teo se ko yi zem to, cham dento dwoŋi wo yi abam. Asiria teo pɛ mo wó ba á baŋa.”
18Maŋa kam konto ná yia, Baŋa Wɛ wó fwooli se o pa Ejipti jar-keira nwoŋi ba ba, ne nanjwɛ mo nwoŋi Ejipti bu-nwaro tem ne yiga yiga to. O ta wó bwoŋi Asiria jar-keira se ba de ba, ne ba na chiŋi twe ba yage tei to. 19Banto wó nwoŋi de kɔgɔ mo ba ba ba faare tega kam maama. Ba wó vo ba jeini bwol-fwaaro ne, de peero gugworru wone, de mɛ na jege sabare to ne, ko woli de vara pwoli sem ne.
20Maŋa kam ná yia, Baŋa Wɛ wó bwoŋi Asiria teo pɛ se o nwoŋi Yuferata buga kam seeni o ba o chɔge abam pa se á di á chaveera, ne o na kwei fana o ma o cheeri á yu-ywei maama, ye o fane á twana, se o daare o kwooni á yera koro tem maama tei to. 21Maŋa kam konto ne, valo wae o pɔɔre na-mɔra dedoa de bone delei yerane se o taa jega. 22De ko de, kotu ta wó na nayela dedɛ se o taa di nayel-pepala. Balo ta na daare tega kam ne to wó di nayel-pepala de tooro mo. 23Maŋa kam konto ne, mɛ maama ba ya na jeiri Vini teeni moro ye de jeelim yi sabu-dala moro to, ga-cheiŋo de sabare yerane laam mo wó taa nwoŋi da. 24Nɔɔna laam maa wó taa vei dáane ba tɔɔna, ga-cheiŋo de sabare na wó jwoŋi jei sem konto maama to ŋwaane. 25Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá vo zwonnu tem jei sem ne se o va. Kokuri to, ga-cheiŋo de sabare yerane mo wó su jei sem maama. Dáane mo ba nam wó kale naane ba yage da se de di gaao, ye pei de wó taa nɔne jei sem konto ne.

english_text:
A Warning and a Hope
1The Lord said, “Isaiah, get something to write on. Then write in big clear letters the name, MAHER-SHALAL-HASH-BAZ. 2I will tell Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah to serve as witnesses to this.”
3Sometime later, my wife and I had a son, and the Lord said, “Name him Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz. 4Because before he can say ‘Mommy’ or ‘Daddy,’ the king of Assyria will attack and take everything of value from Damascus and Samaria.”
5The Lord spoke to me again and said:
6These people have refused the gentle waters of Shiloah and have gladly gone over to the side of King Rezin and King Pekah. 7Now I will send the king of Assyria against them with his powerful army, which will attack like the mighty Euphrates River overflowing its banks. 8Enemy soldiers will cover Judah like a flood reaching up to your neck.
But God is with us.
He will spread his wings
and protect our land.
9All of you foreign nations,
go ahead and prepare for war,
but you will be crushed.
10Get together and make plans,
but you will fail
because God is with us.
11The Lord took hold of me with his powerful hand and said:
I'm warning you! Don't act like these people. 12 Don't call something a rebellious plot, just because they do, and don't be afraid of something, just because they are. 13I am the one you should fear and respect. I am the holy God, the Lord All-Powerful! 14-15 Run to me for protection. I am a rock that will make both Judah and Israel stumble and break their bones. I am a trap that will catch the people of Jerusalem—they will be captured and dragged away.
Isaiah and His Followers
16My message and my teachings are to be sealed and given to my followers. 17 Meanwhile, I patiently trust the Lord, even though he is no longer pleased with Israel. 18 My children and I are warning signs to Israel from the Lord All-Powerful, who lives on Mount Zion.
19Someone may say to you, “Go to the fortunetellers who make soft chirping sounds or ask the spirits of the dead. After all, a nation ought to be able to ask its own gods 20what it should do.”
None of those who talk like that will live to see the light of day! 21They will go around in great pain and will become so hungry that they will angrily curse their king and their gods. And when they try to find help in heaven 22and on earth, they will find only trouble and darkness, terrible trouble and deepest darkness.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ wó ma Asiria teo pɛ o toŋe
1 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we, “Beeri tɔn-kamunu se n popone botare-bia ko wone se nɔɔna taa wae ba gara jaja. Popone tento: Mahere-Salal-Hasa-Bazi. 2Amo nam wó bwoŋi Wɛ kaanem tu Yuria, de Jeberekia bu Zekaria, se ba ba ba ji maana tiina chekke ba pa-ne.”
3Amo déem ma peini de a kaane, ye o ja puga o lo bakeira. Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we, “Bwoŋi o yere we Mahere-Salal-Hasa-Bazi. 4Bu wom ta ná wo yi se o taa wae o ni o pura o tɛ we, ‘A nu’ naa ‘A kwo’, Asiria pɛ wom wó ba o vere Damasika jejegero tem, de Samaria wonnu tem maama o ja o viiri.”
5 Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta de amo o we:
6“Judah tiina bam yɔɔre ba ve Siloa bu-nɔgɔ kom na duri mɛmɛ to mo, ye ba sɛ ba pa Rezin, de Remalia bu Peka. 7Konto ŋwaane amo lage a bwoŋi Asiria teo pɛ de o jar-keira bam maama mo se ba ba ba jeeri abam de jara. Ko wó taa nye ne Yuferata buga kam na su ka pɛɛle, ye ka ta nwoŋi ka su ka bu-nwaro tem maama, ka ta kɛ ka kwoli ka buburi-bɛa yam baŋa maama tei to. 8Na bam ta wó chuuri ba kɛ ba yi Judah laŋa kam ba tagele jei sem, ye ba daare ba lini tega kam de nɔɔna bam maama. Imanuwel, Wɛ nam wó kwoli nmo tega kam maama, ne zuŋa na yarege ka vɔna ka bia baŋa ne tei to.”
9Abam dwi-gɛ tiina bam, bage-na tiguri-kaasa,
se á wó na chɔgem!
Cheigi-na, abam teene delo na ye yiga yiga to.
Kwei-na á jara zela se á ke jara!
Á nam wó na chɔgem!
Á ná ti yiga se á ke jara tei de,
á ta wó na chɔgem mo zɔŋ-zɔŋ!
10Abam ná jaane boboŋa se á ke tei maama de,
ya lage ya vugimi mo.
Á ná le á boboŋa yam chwei á tiŋi tei de,
ya bá wane ya zege.
Kokuri to, Wɛ wora dé tei ne.
Kɔre-na Baŋa Wɛ
11 Baŋa Wɛ yɔɔre o tɔge o dam dem baŋa ne mo o kaane-ne se a de yé kwei chwoŋa kalo nɔɔna banto na tɔge da to. O maa we:
12“Banto ná jeeli kolo we, ba ke ni se ba baare nɔɔno kwaga, abam yé jeeli-ko konto. Nam yé ta‑á kɔre-na wonnu telo banto na kɔre to. Yé ta‑á fona-na. 13Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo á wó ta‑á nii we o ye wo-pwoŋo tu. Ko maa ye wonto mo á jege se á ta‑á kɔre, ye á fona ded‑o. 14Baŋa Wɛ tete wó taa ye dalem jei o pa abam. Ko ná ye Isarele dwi tiina di selei sem, o nam wó taa ye kandwɛ delo na cheili pa nɔɔna gare-de ba chɔɔle ba to tega ne to mo. Chega to, o wó taa ye kalanchogo mo se o ja Jerusalem teo nɔn-bia bam de. 15Ba dedɛ mo lage ba tiri ba to ba chochoge ba tete. Ba dona maa wó che-ba de kalanchorro ba ja ba viiri.”
Ke n teena Baŋa Wɛ wone
