16Kwei-na nia yalo maama Wɛ na pɛ debam to á ke daane. Fɔge á tiŋi o bera yam, ye á daare á ke-ya amo tɔgena bam jeŋa ne. 17De Baŋa Wɛ na jege o tete o seigi Jakob dwi tiina bam yiga ne to de, amo ta wó taa cheigi‑o mo, amo teena yam na tigi wonto baŋa ne to ŋwaane.
18Nii-na amo de bia balo Baŋa Wɛ na ke amo jeŋa ne to mo tento dé zega. Dé ye wo-memaŋe mo dé pa Isarele tiina bam se ba wane ba lɔre kolo Wɛ na lage o ke to. Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na zoore Zion peo kom yuu ne to nam mo pɛ dé ye konto.
19Nɔɔna nam wó ta de abam se á beeri vora, de yi-nara, de balo na yeini ba seini ba vogo to mo, ye ba we, “Nɔɔna maŋe se ba vo ba wa yam yiga ne ba beeri ba yiga mo. Ba wó bwɛ de twa se ba lɔre kolo ná wó yi balo na ŋwe to.” 20Nam kwei-na ba taane dem konto á maŋe de Wɛ nia de o bera yam. Ba na tage kolo to bere we, chega seene ka tere ba taane dem wone. 21Amo nɔɔna bam wó taa kaare tega kam maama wone ba beera, se wo-chechɔgɔ de kana taa jege-ba. Ba bane wó zaŋe ba kana kam ŋwaane. Ba maa wó kwoni ba yuni wɛɛne ba lwɛ ba pɛ wom de ba Wɛ dem. 22Ba ta wó tiiri se ba nii tega kam jei maama ne, ye ba na cham, de yibiri, de wo-chechɔgɔ yerane mo. Ba laam maa wó vo ba to lim dem wone.

english_text:
1 But those who have suffered will no longer be in pain. The territories of Zebulun and Naphtali in Galilee were once hated. But this land of the Gentiles across the Jordan River and along the Mediterranean Sea will be greatly respected.
War Is Over
2 Those who walked in the dark
have seen a bright light.
And it shines upon everyone
who lives in the land
of darkest shadows.
3Our Lord, you have made
your nation stronger.
Because of you, its people
are glad and celebrate
like workers at harvest time
or like soldiers dividing up
what they have taken.
4You have broken the power
of those who abused
and enslaved your people.
You have rescued them
just as you saved your people
from Midian.
5The boots of marching warriors
and the blood-stained uniforms
have been fed to flames
and eaten by fire.
A Child Has Been Born
6A child has been born for us.
We have been given a son
who will be our ruler.
His names will be
Wonderful Advisor
and Mighty God,
Eternal Father
and Prince of Peace.
7 His power will never end;
peace will last forever.
He will rule David's kingdom
and make it grow strong.
He will always rule
with honesty and justice.
The Lord All-Powerful
will make certain
that all of this is done.
God Will Punish Israel
8The Lord had warned the people of Israel, 9and all of them knew it, including everyone in the capital city of Samaria. But they were proud and stubborn and said,
10“Houses of brick and sycamore
have fallen to the ground,
but we will build houses
with stones and cedar.”
11The Lord made their enemies attack them. 12He sent the Arameans from the east and the Philistines from the west, and they swallowed up Israel. But even this did not stop him from being angry, so he kept on punishing them. 13The people of Israel still did not turn back to the Lord All-Powerful and worship him.
14In one day he cut off their head and tail, their leaves and branches. 15Their rulers and leaders were the head, and the lying prophets were the tail. 16They had led the nation down the wrong path, and the people were confused. 17The Lord was angry with his people and kept punishing them, because they had turned against him. They were evil and spoke foolishly. That's why he did not have pity on their young people or on their widows and orphans.
18Evil had spread like a raging forest fire sending thornbushes up in smoke. 19The Lord All-Powerful was angry and used the people as fuel for a fire that scorched the land. They turned against each other 20like wild animals attacking and eating everyone around them, even their own relatives. But still they were not satisfied. 21The tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh turned against each other, then joined forces to attack Judah. But the Lord was still angry and ready to punish the nation even more.
translation_text:
1Ko nam na ye tei to, lwia ya na jege nɔɔna balo to wó nwoŋi ba cham dem wone. Faŋa kam to, nɔɔna déem jege Zebulun dwi tiina laŋa kam de Nafitali tiina laŋa kam ba gwoona. Maŋa nam na beene to, Wɛ wó pa jei sem konto na zula lanyerane. Ko maa ye jei selo na wo naneo kom seeni to, de jei selo na wo Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ dedwoŋi dem kwaga ne to, de Galili laŋa kam dwi-gɛ tiina na zoore mɛ to.
2Nɔɔna balo déem na beeri lim wone to
mo pwooni laam yi-ba lanyerane.
Balo ya na zoore yibiri jei ne ye toone tei-ba to,
wea laam maa nye ba baŋa ne.
3Nmo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se teo kom nɔn-bia bam puli dedɛ,
pa se ba wopwolo kom de puli lanyerane.
Ba maa jege ywoni ba di nmo yiga ne,
ne vala na jege wopwolo wodiiru zagem maŋa ne tei to.
Ko ta nye de jar-keira na di ywoni,
de ba na wane ba dona,
ye ba pɔɔre ba jejegero ba pa daane tei to mo.
4Kokuri to, n jaane zele-zana yalo ba ya na zeŋe to,
de da-lwanno telo ya na mage-ba to
n ja n bwori n yage.
Konto to, n chɔge dam delo ba dona na kwei
ba ma ba bɛɛse-ba to mo,
ne nmo déem na ke tei n chɔge Midian tiina bam dam to.
5Ba maa wó kwei ba jara zela yam maama
ba ma ba tɔre mini.
Bembɛ natere-kogela yam,
de gɔrɔ kolo maama na fereme de jana to
wo ba te chɔge zɔŋ-zɔŋ.
6Ba loge bu ba pa debam.
Ba ma pa debam bakeira.
Ko nam ye wonto yuu zele mo se o taa tei o nɔɔna.
Ba maa wó taa jege‑o ba bwoi we:
Swa Bereno na ye kenkagele,
de Wɛ-kamunu kom,
de Taa Wuu Tu Kwo wom,
de Bochare-zuru Tu dedɛɛro wom.
7O na tei o nɔɔna bam tei to
wó taa fɔge ko vei yiga mo,
pa se yazura jage ya yi jei maama.
O lage o jeini Pɛ David paare yituŋu kom baŋa ne mo
o di David dwi dem paare.
O ta wó da chega de nɔn-ŋonne ŋwaane mo
o ma o fɔge o paare dem se de zege de dam,
ko zege zem se ko taa vei wuu.
Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tete nam wó pa se wonnu tento maama ke,
o na seene yia se te ji chega to ŋwaane.
Wɛ wó waare Isarele tiina bam
8Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o toŋe o kwora
se o ma o kaane Jakob dwi dem mo.
Isarele tiina bam wó seene ba na waarem.
9Nɔɔna bam maama wó lɔre ko ni ne,
ko ná maŋe ko ye Efrayim dwi tiina bam,
de balo maama na zoore Samaria teo ne to.
Banto yeini ba bere ba tete kamunim
ye ba ta de nyɔn-mage ba we,
10“Dé bira yam to tega ne.
Dé nam wó sare kandwa
dé fɔge dé lɔ dé di sem.
Ba gwoni dé kaporro tem de ba de tega ne.
De ko de, dé wó jwoori dé jeiri Sedare teeni mo
se dento leiri te yuu ne.”
11 Baŋa Wɛ nam lage o chiŋi Pɛ Rezin dona bam mo
se ba jeeri-ba de jara.
O ta wó pa se Isarele tiina dona bam maama zaŋe
ba ba ba baŋa ne.
12Siria tiina bam wó nwoŋi wɛ-puli seeni
se Filisi tiina bam de zege wɛ-zoore seeni ba ba.
Banto maama laam maa wó kaŋe ba nia
ba li Isarele tiina bam.
13De Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na pɛ se ko zo ba yera to maama de,
nɔɔna bam ta wo pipiri se ba jwoori o tei.
14Konto ŋwaane, Baŋa Wɛ wó chɔge Isarele dwi dem maama,
ne o na gwoni ba yuu kom de ba nabili dem dɛ dedwe wone tei to mo.
Dɛ dedwe wone mo o lage o bwori konkwara vɔɔ de sangaa.
15Ba nakwa de ba nɔn-yum tem mo ye yuu kom.
Ba sampwori selo na kare ba fɔe vwa to maa ye nabili dem.
16Balo na wo nɔɔna banto yiga ne to mo pae ba tusa.
Ko maa pae se balo ba na jege ba bere chwoŋa to na chɔgem.
17Konto ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ yi ba sui ba nɔn-donno tem kikia.
O nam ba duri botara bam de kadeina bam de ŋwaŋa.
Kokuri to, nɔɔna bam maama ve Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem mo
ye ba toŋe puseŋa yerane.
Ba nia maa yɔɔre ya ŋɔɔne wo-popwanno.
De konto maama de nam, Baŋa Wɛ bane dem ta bá zuri.
O ta wó twe o jeŋa kam mo se o waare-ba.
18Nɔɔna bam puseŋa totoŋa yam nye ne mini mo,
de na jege punnu de sabare de di.
De ta ma di gwe sem bileim-bileim,
se nyoa yɔɔre ka tiini ka taa zaŋe wɛɛne.
19Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom dem ŋwaane,
tega kam maama wó di mini mo ye ka zwɛ maama.
Nɔɔna bam wó ji ne dɛ mo se ba kwei-ba ba ma ba tɔre mini,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá ŋwane o pa o dwoŋi.
20Jazem seeni de jagwia seeni maama
ba kare ba beeri wodiu mo se ba di.
Ba nam ta ba di ba sui.
Ba ma kwaane ba di ba tete dwi dem ya-nɔna.
21Manasɛ dwi tiina ke chichuŋu de Efrayim dwi tiina mo,
ye Efrayim dwi tiina bam de ke chichuŋu de Manasɛ dwi tiina bam.
Banto balei laam ma ke daane
ba ke chichuŋu de Judah dwi tiina bam.
De konto maama de nam, Baŋa Wɛ bane dem ta bá zuri.
O ta wó twe o jeŋa kam mo se o waare-ba.

english_text:
1You people are in for trouble! You have made cruel and unfair laws 2that let you cheat the poor and needy and rob widows and orphans. 3But what will you do when you are fiercely attacked and punished by foreigners? Where will you run for help? Where will you hide your valuables? 4How will you escape being captured or killed? The Lord is still angry, and he isn't through with you yet!
The Lord's Purpose and the King of Assyria
5 The Lord says:
I am furious! And I will use the king of Assyria as a club 6to beat down you godless people. I am angry with you, and I will send him to attack you. He will take what he wants and walk on you like mud in the streets. 7He has even bigger plans in mind, because he wants to destroy many nations.
8The king of Assyria says:
My army commanders are kings! 9They have already captured the cities of Calno, Carchemish, Hamath, Arpad, Samaria, and Damascus. 10-11 The gods of Jerusalem and Samaria are weaker than the gods of those powerful nations. And I will destroy Jerusalem, together with its gods and idols, just as I did Samaria.
12The Lord will do what he has planned against Jerusalem and Mount Zion. Then he will punish the proud and boastful king of Assyria, 13who says:
I did these things by my own power because I am smart and clever. I attacked kings like a wild bull, and I took the land and the treasures of their nations. 14I have conquered the whole world! And it was easier than taking eggs from an unguarded nest. No one even flapped a wing or made a peep.
15King of Assyria, can an ax or a saw overpower the one who uses it? Can a wooden pole lift whoever holds it? 16The mighty Lord All-Powerful will send a terrible disease to strike down your army, and you will burn with fever under your royal robes. 17The holy God, who is the light of Israel, will turn into a fire, and in one day you will go up in flames, just like a thornbush. 18The Lord will make your beautiful forests and fertile fields slowly rot. 19There will be so few trees that even a young child can count them.
Only a Few Will Come Back
20A time is coming when the survivors from Israel and Judah will completely depend on the holy Lord of Israel, instead of the nation that defeated them. 21-22 There were as many people as there are grains of sand along the seashore, but only a few will survive to come back to Israel's mighty God. This is because he has threatened to destroy their nation, just as they deserve. 23The Lord All-Powerful has promised that everyone on this earth will be punished.
24Now the Lord God All-Powerful says to his people in Jerusalem:
The Assyrians will beat you with sticks and abuse you, just as the Egyptians did. But don't be afraid of them. 25Soon I will stop being angry with you, and I will punish them for their crimes. 26I will beat the Assyrians with a whip, as I did the people of Midian near the rock at Oreb. And I will show the same mighty power that I used when I made a path through the sea in Egypt. 27Then they will no longer rule your nation. All will go well for you, and your burden will be lifted.
28Enemy troops have reached the town of Aiath. They have gone through Migron, and they stored their supplies at Michmash, 29before crossing the valley and spending the night at Geba. The people of Ramah are terrified; everyone in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, has run away. 30Loud crying can be heard in the towns of Gallim, Laishah, and sorrowful Anathoth. 31No one is left in Madmenah or Gebim. 32Today the enemy will camp at Nob and shake a threatening fist at Mount Zion in Jerusalem.
33But the Lord All-Powerful
will use his fearsome might
to bring down the tallest trees
and chop off every branch.
34With an ax, the glorious Lord
will destroy every tree
in the forests of Lebanon.
translation_text:
1Lɛɛro wó yi abam balo na chwi vwa nia á tiŋi á pa á nɔɔna to,
ya na ye se ya pa nɔɔna bam na bɛɛsem to ŋwaane.
2Á tɔge tento baŋa ne mo á cho nabwona chwoŋa,
pa se balo na ye yiniga tiina a nɔɔna bam wone to
ware se ba na ba bora.
Á yeini á ke konto dwoŋi mo á vere kadeina de botara wonnu tem.
3Bora borem dɛ dem nam ná yia,
abam lage á ke tetɛ mo?
Lɛɛro wó zege yiga yiga ne te ba te to á baŋa ne.
Abam laam wó duri á vo bera tei mo se ba woli abam?
Á lage á vo á seigi á jejegero tem yei ne mo?
4Abam bá wane á lu cham dem wone.
Á nam lage á tɔge de á dwonna bam mo
á kuni dwoona á dona bam yiga ne.
Ko ná dae konto, á wó to jara yam wone
á maŋe tega ne de twa badwonna bam maama.
De konto maama de nam, Baŋa Wɛ bane dem ta bá zuri.
O ta wó twe o jeŋa kam mo se o waare abam.
Wɛ wó waare Asiria tiina
5Lɛɛro wó yi Asiria teo kom!
Ko nam ye da-lɔŋɔ kolo amo na mae a waare nɔɔna
a ban-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane to mo.
A kwei a dam dem a ke ba jeŋa ne,
se ba ma-de ba toŋe a waarem dem.
6Amo wó toŋe-ba se ba vo ba ke chichuŋu
de dwi tiina balo na ve Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem
ye ba chuchugi a bane to.
Asiria tiina bam maa wó vere nɔɔna bam konto jejegero
ba ja ba viiri.
Ba ta wó pa ko yi-ba ne teero mo ba jege ba nɔne to.
7Ko nam dae konto mo Asiria pɛ wom ya boŋa.
Ko dae konto mo o jege o jeela o yuu ne.
Wonto ya yɔɔre o lage se o chɔge teene dedɛ mo,
se o pa de yere saare tega baŋa ne.
8O maa tɛ o we,
“A dedɛɛra bam maama jege dam ba dwoi pwa!
9Kalino teo de Karekemisi teo ye bedwe mo.
Hamafa teo de Arapade teo de maa ye bedwe,
ko ta woli de Samaria teo de Damasika teo kom.
Debam déem wane de maama dé di.
10A ma ja teene delo na kaane jwo-dɛɛra to
a ke a jeŋa ne.
Banto jwona yam dana ya dwoi
yalo na wo Jerusalem ne de Samaria ne to.
11Ne a na maŋe a chɔge Samaria teo kom de ko jwona tei to,
mo a ta na wó ke tei de Jerusalem de ko jwona yam.”
12Baŋa Wɛ nam ná ke o na lage tei to Zion peo kom de Jerusalem teo kom yera ne, o laam wó waare Asiria teo pɛ wom mo, de o na bere o tete kamunim, ye o ta jege teera to. 13Kokuri to, wonto tɛ o we:
“Amo tete dam mo pɛ se a ke tento maama.
A nam ta ke-ko ko tɔge a swa de a yi-poro baŋa ne mo.
A ma gɔ teene dem siseina,
ye a daare a vere ba jejegero a jega.
A maa jege dam ne nabea tei to
pa se a chɔge pwa dam.
14A ma pa a jeŋa zo logo baŋa teene dem wone
ne a ga tore-ka zuna pwogo wone mo tei.
A ma vere ba jejegero tem a ke daane
ne a yɔɔre a la chechara a pɛ mo tei.
Zuna bam dedoa tete nam wo pipeigi ka vɔna.
Ka nam wo puri ka ni ka keeri.”
15Dwooru wó wane o dwoni de wolo na jege‑o o toŋe to na?
Seo de wó taa jege kuri ko dwoi wolo na zei-ko to na?
Gwoli ba zeiŋi nabiinu.
Ko ye nabiinu mo wó zeiŋi gwoli.
16Asiria teo pɛ na bere o tete kamunim konto to ŋwaane mo
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Paŋwa to
wó pa jaweo to o bembɛ sem baŋa ne
se ko di ba yera ko ti.
Wɛ wó chɔge Asiria pɛ wom nenɔŋa kam maama,
ne o na tɔre mini delo na di bileim-bileim tei to mo.
17Baŋa Wɛ wom na pae Isarele tiina pwooni to
laam wó ji mini mo o pa-ba.
Ba Wo-pwoŋo Tu Wɛ wom mo wó ji min-vogo,
se o zwɛ Asiria pɛ wonnu tem dɛ dedwe wone.
O lage o zwɛ-te ne ba na zwɛ sabare de ga-cheiŋo tei to mo.
18Ko ná ye pɛ wom goa na lini to,
naa o te-ywoŋa kam mo,
te maama wó yɔɔre te na chɔgem.
Ko wó taa nye de jaweo na jaane nɔɔno
ye ko yɔɔre ko di‑o ko ti tei to mo.
19Goa wone teeni dem wó mɔ mo de daare fee yerane,
pa se bu-balaŋa de wó wane de ni o jeeli o ja.
Isarele tiina wó jwoori ba tete teo
20Maŋa kam konto ná yia, balo ta na daare Isarele tiina bam wone to daa bá kwei ba teena ba daŋe wolo ya na bɛɛse-ba to baŋa ne. Ba nam wó kwei ba chega de ba teena maama mo ba ke Jakob dwi tiina Wo-pwoŋo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wone. 21Jakob dwi tiina ta wó daare fee se ba jwoori. Ba badaara maa wó jwoori Wɛ-kamunu kom tei ne. 22Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom seene ko daga, ne naneo ni kasolo bia na ye tei to mo. De ko de, ba fenfee yerane mo wó jwoori Wɛ tei. Wɛ boboŋa maŋe ya ja ya ti se o chɔge-ba mo. Chɔgem dem nam wó tɔge o chega bora kam baŋa ne mo chekke. 23Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó yɔɔre o ke-ba ne o na tage tei to o ti, pa se tega kam maama na chɔgem mo.
24Konto ŋwaane, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam tage tento mo ye o we:
“Amo nɔɔna balo na zoore Zion ne to, yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone de Asiria tiina bam, de ba na jege da-lwanno de gwola ba mage abam, ne Ejipti tiina bam de déem na ke abam tei to. 25Kokuri to, ko ná ke fee, amo bane delo ya na zaŋe de abam to wó zuri. A laam maa wó pa se a bane pipiri de zaŋe banto baŋa ne se a chɔge-ba.
26Amo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tete nam wó fere Asiria tiina bam se ko zo ba yera, ne a déem na ke Midian tiina tei Orebi peo kom teiŋa ne to mo. Amo ta wó waare-ba, ne Moses déem na twe o nacheiga kam naneo baŋa ne ye a waare Ejipti tiina bam tei to. 27Maŋa kam konto ná yia, amo wó dɔne zele delo banto na kwei ba daŋe á bakale baŋa ne to. A ta wó bwori yɔgese delo na wo á ba ne to. Abam na wó nu á dwoni-de to ŋwaane mo de wó bwori.”
28Á dona bam tu ba li Ayate teo!
Ba tɔge Migoron ne mo ba kɛ.
Ba ma kwei ba zela ba tiŋi Mikimasa ne.
29Ba kwei peero yuu chwoŋa mo ba vei ye ba tɛ we,
“Dé wó vo dé yi Geba teo mo dé peini da.”
Rama teo nɔɔna bam yera maa sae.
Sɔɔl teo Gibea tiina de duri mo se ba lu.
30Abam Galim teo tiina bam, tiini á ta‑á chwoosa!
Abam de cheigi-na, Layisa teo tiina bam!
Anatofe teo tiina bam, lwia jege abam!
31Mademena teo tiina yɔɔre ba duri mo sae.
Gebim teo nɔɔna de maa duri ba beeri seigim jei.
32Dɛ dento ne nɔɔ mo á dona bam yi Nobi teo
ba maŋe da se ba sii.
Ba maa yɔɔre ba jege ba jagula ba dola
se ba fugi Zion nɔn-bia bam.
Ba gwooni balo na zoore Jerusalem zwoŋo kom yuu ne to mo.
33Nam nii-na! Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Paŋwa to
seene o lage o ma o dam-fɔrɔ kom mo
o gwoni tei-kamunnu nɛ sem.
Tei-zwanno tem mo o lage o gwoni o de tega ne.
Telo maa na dɔra to de wó ba tega.
34Goa kalo na tiini ka lini to mo
o lage o kwei dwooru o ma o gwoni ka teeni o de tega ne.
Wɛ-kamunu kom mo wó pa se Lebanon teo to tega ne.

english_text:
Peace at Last
1 Like a branch that sprouts
from a stump,
someone from David's family
will someday be king.
2The Spirit of the Lord
will be with him
to give him understanding,
wisdom, and insight.
He will be powerful,
and he will know
and honor the Lord.
3His greatest joy will be
to obey the Lord.
This king won't judge
by appearances
or listen to rumors.
4The poor and the needy
will be treated with fairness
and with justice.
His word will be law
everywhere in the land,
and criminals
will be put to death.
5 Honesty and fairness
will be his royal robes.
6 Leopards will lie down
with young goats,
and wolves will rest
with lambs.
Calves and lions
will eat together
and be cared for
by little children.
7Cows and bears will share
the same pasture;
their young will rest
side by side.
Lions and oxen
will both eat straw.
8Little children will play
near snake holes.
They will stick their hands
into dens of poisonous snakes
and never be hurt.
9 Nothing harmful will take place
on the Lord's holy mountain.
Just as water fills the sea,
the land will be filled
with people who know
and honor the Lord.
God's People Will Come Back Home
10 The time is coming when one of David's descendants will be the signal for the people of all nations to come together. They will follow his advice, and his own nation will become famous.
11When that day comes, the Lord will again reach out his mighty arm and bring home his people who have survived in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Ethiopia, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the land along the coast. 12He will give a signal to the nations, and he will bring together the refugees from Judah and Israel, who have been scattered all over the earth. 13Israel will stop being jealous of Judah, and Judah will no longer be the enemy of Israel. 14Instead, they will get together and attack the Philistines in the west. Then they will defeat the Edomites, the Moabites, and the Ammonites in the east. They will rule those people and take from them whatever they want.
15 The Lord will dry up the arm of the Red Sea near Egypt, and he will send a scorching wind to divide the Euphrates River into seven streams that anyone can step across. 16Then for his people who survive, there will be a good road from Assyria, just as there was a good road for their ancestors when they left Egypt.
translation_text:
Pɛ David dwi dem taane
1Jesse dwi dem da-buŋa kalo ta na daare to
wó jwoori ka ta naga.
Naga kalo na wó nwoŋi da to mo wó ke bia.
2 Baŋa Wɛ Jworo maa wó taa wo kotu baŋa ne.
Jworo kom wó pa o taa jege swa de yi-poro,
se o taa wae o bere nɔɔna chega.
Jworo kom ta wó pa o taa jege dam de yeino,
se o taa kɔre Baŋa Wɛ.
3O ywoni maama wó taa wo Baŋa Wɛ kɔrɔ kom wone mo.
O bá kwei o yia na nɛ nɔɔna yibia na ye tei to
se o ma o di ba taane.
O ta bá tɔge sawea baŋa ne se o bore bora o pa nɔɔna.
4O nam wó tɔge nɔn-ŋonne baŋa ne mo
o di yiniga tiina taane.
O maa wó bore chega bora
o pa nabwona balo maama na zoore tega kam ne to.
O ni-vio kom maa wó taa jege dam tega kam jei maama ne,
se ko pa puseŋ-nyena na chɔgem.
5Nɔn-ŋonne mo o lage o vɔ o teiŋa ne,
se o zege o chega wone o nii o nɔɔna bam.
6Wiira de pipeili wó taa zoore daane.
Gweera de bebale de maa wó taa tigi jeiga dedoa ne.
Na-mɔre de nywon-pɔle wó taa tɔge de na-paala mo se ba me daane.
Bu-balwa maa wó taa jege-se ba nia.
7Naane de kago-vara wó zege daane ba di.
Ba bia bam de maa wó taa tigi da-tei ne.
Nywonnu de wó di ga-korro ne nabɛ na di tei to.
8Bu-sese wó taa jei kapɛ bɔɔna ni ne ba kwɛɛra.
Bu-balɛ de wó kwei ba je ba tore anakɔbayi peiga jei ne.
Kolokolo zonne nam bá yi-ba.
9Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá ke o dwoŋi zonne,
naa o chɔge kolokolo
amo Baŋa Wɛ peo kom jei maama ne.
Kokuri to, tega baŋa maama wó su de
nɔɔna balo na yɔɔre ba me de Baŋa Wɛ to,
ne na na yɔɔre ba su naneo kom wo maama tei to mo.
10Maŋa kam konto ná yia, logo baŋa dwi maama wó ba Jesse dwi tu wom tei, o yere dem na wo wɛ-wɛ to ŋwaane. O maa na zoore mɛ to wó na zula lanyerane. 11Maŋa kam konto ne, Baŋa Wɛ daa ta wó tɔge o dam dem baŋa ne se o ja o nɔɔna balo ta na daare ye ba wo teene dedɛ wone to o jwoori sɔŋɔ. Teene dem konto maa ye Asiria, de Ejipti, de Paforosi, de Kusi, de Elam, de Babilonia, de Hamafa, de jei selo na wo naneo kom ni ne to.
12Wonto mo lage o zeiŋi tuta se teene dem maama na,
se o daare o la Isarele tiina de Judah tiina
balo na jage to o ke daane.
Banto wó zege tega baŋa ni maama ne mo ba jwoori.
13Efrayim dwi tiina maa wó yage ba kazwe sem,
se Judah dwi tiina daa yé taa ke dono de-ba.
Efrayim tiina bam daa bá taa jege kazwe
ba di de Judah tiina bam.
Judah tiina bam de nam bá chuli Efrayim tiina bam.
14Ba nam wó tɔge daane mo ba siseiri ba tu
Filisi teo na wo wɛ-zoore seeni to.
Ba maa wó ke daane
se ba vere nɔɔna balo na zoore wɛ-puli seeni to jejegero.
Ba ta wó wane Edom teo, de Moaba teo se ba taa tei-de,
ye Amon teo tiina wó ba ba zo banto dam kuri ne.
15 Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se te-kora peini
Ejipti naneo kom wone.
O maa wó twe o jeŋa o pa se vo-loŋo zaŋe
Yuferata buga kam baŋa ne.
Buga kam laam wó chɛ ka ji nabare serepɛ,
se wolo maama ná vei de napera,
se kotu wane o bɛ-ka.
16Chwo-fara wó taa tigi ka pae Isarele tiina balo ta na daare
ye ba zege Asiria teo ne ba jwoori sɔŋɔ to.
Ko maa wó taa nye de Isarele tiina bam
déem na nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne ye ko ye tei to mo.

english_text:
A Song of Praise
1At that time you will say,
“I thank you, Lord!
You were angry with me,
but you stopped being angry
and gave me comfort.
2 I trust you to save me,
Lord God,
and I won't be afraid.
My power and my strength
come from you,
and you have saved me.”
3With great joy, you people
will get water
from the well of victory.
4At that time you will say,
“Our Lord, we are thankful,
and we worship only you.
We will tell the nations
how glorious you are
and what you have done.
5Because of your wonderful deeds
we will sing your praises
everywhere on earth.”
6Sing, people of Zion!
Celebrate the greatness
of the holy Lord of Israel.
God is here to help you.
translation_text:
Seinim lei
1Maŋa kam konto ná yia, nmo wó ta we:
“Baŋa Wɛ, amo wó ke nmo lei.
Kokuri to, n bane ya zaŋe de amo mo.
De laam nam toa,
ye n jwoori n ke dam n ke amo kuri ne.
2Chega to, Wɛ mo ye wolo na vere-ne o yage to.
Amo wó ke a wo-dedoa ded‑o mo
se foone yé taa jege-ne.
Baŋa Wɛ mo ye wolo na pa-ne dam to,
ye wonto ŋwaane mo a leena.
O ma bere o tete we o ye amo vereno wom mo.”
3Abam na wó na verem tei to wó pa á di ywoni dedɛ,
ne á na mɔɔne na-ŋona vole wone á nyɔ tei to.
4Maŋa kam konto ne, abam wó taa tɛ we:
“Ke-na Baŋa Wɛ lei,
se á daare á tei o yere!
Pa-na se logo baŋa dwi tiina lɔre
o na toŋe kolo maama to.
Pa-na se o yere dem tiini de zaŋe wɛɛne.
5Leeni á seini-na Baŋa Wɛ,
wo-kenkagela yalo o na ke to ŋwaane!
Pa-na se logo baŋa dwi tiina lɔre
o na toŋe kolo maama to.
6Abam Zion teo tiina bam, ta‑á bage-na á yaga,
ye á leena de wopwolo.
Kokuri to, Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom
mo wo abam tetare ne, ye o tiini o dana.”

english_text:
Babylon Will Be Punished
1 This is the message that I was given about Babylon:
2From high on a barren hill
give a signal, shout the orders,
and point the way
to enter the gates
of Babylon's proud rulers.
3The Lord has commanded
his very best warriors
and his proud heroes
to show how angry he is.
4Listen to the noisy crowds
on the mountains!
Kingdoms and nations
are joining forces.
The Lord All-Powerful
is bringing together
an army for battle.
5From a distant land
the Lord is coming
fierce and furious—
he brings his weapons
to destroy the whole earth.
6 Cry and weep!
The day is coming
when the mighty Lord
will bring destruction.
* 7All people will be terrified.
Hands will grow limp;
courage will melt away.
8Everyone will tremble with pain
like a woman giving birth;
they will stare at each other
with horror on their faces.
There Will Be No Mercy
9I, the Lord,
will show no mercy or pity
when that time comes.
In my anger I will destroy
the earth and every sinner
who lives on it.
10 Light will disappear
from the stars in the sky;
the dawning sun will turn dark,
and the moon
will lose its brightness.
11I will punish this evil world
and its people
because of their sins.
I will crush the horrible pride
of those who are cruel.
12Survivors will be harder to find
than the purest gold.
13I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am terribly angry—
I will make the sky tremble
and the earth shake loose.
14Everyone will run
to their homelands,
just as hunted deer run,
and sheep scatter
when they have no shepherd.
15Those men who are captured
will be killed by a sword.
16They will see their children
beaten against rocks,
their homes robbed,
and their wives abused.
17The Medes can't be bought off
with silver or gold,
and I'm sending them
to attack Babylonia.
18Their arrows will slaughter
the young men;
no pity will be shown
to babies and children.
The Lord Will Destroy Babylon
19 The city of Babylon
is glorious and powerful,
the pride of the nation.
But it will be like the cities
of Sodom and Gomorrah
after I, the Lord,
destroyed them.
20No one will live in Babylon.
Even nomads won't camp nearby,
and shepherds won't let
their sheep rest there.
21 Only desert creatures,
hoot owls, and ostriches
will live in its ruins,
and goats will leap about.
22Hyenas and wolves will howl
from Babylon's fortresses
and beautiful palaces.
Its time is almost up!
translation_text:
Babilon tiina taane
1Wɛ kwora kalo Wɛ na kwei o pa Amozi bu Izaya se ka vo Babilon tiina seeni to mo tento:
2Zege-na zwoŋo yuu ne á zeiŋi tuta wɛɛne,
se nɔɔna wane ba na jaja.
Tɔɔle-na kwora se ka yi-ba,
se á daare á yeese á jea á pa ba vo ba ke chichuŋu
de naduna balo na zoore sɔ-fwaaro wone to.
3Amo mo bwoŋi babɛ selo a na kuri to
ye a daare a pa-ba chwoŋa se ba vo
ba waare balo a bane na zaŋe ba baŋa ne to.
Babɛ sem nam di ywoni mo a dam dem ŋwaane.
4Cheigi-na, se á wó ni sɔɔ na ke peero jei sem ne.
Ko nam ye ne kɔ-fɔrɔ mo jeeri daane.
Cheigi-na, se á wó ni logo baŋa dwi tiina bam na bage tiguri-kaasa,
ye ba maama yɔɔre ba lae ba ke daane.
Ko nam ye Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo lae
o jar-keira o ke daane se ba nwoŋi jara ŋwaane.
5Ba nwoŋi jei na ye yiga yiga logo baŋa ni maama ne to mo
ye ba ba ba jeeri daane.
Ba nam ye Baŋa Wɛ jara zela mo,
o na wó tɔge ba baŋa
o chɔge tega kam ni maama
o ban-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane.
6Nam ta‑á chwoosi-na á yaga,
kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ dɛ-kamunu kom bwola.
De ná yia, ko wó taa ye Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom mo pɛ se chɔgem ba.
7Konto ŋwaane nɔɔna maama vɔna wó pare.
Ba maama wo maa wó leegi.
8Foone wó ja ba maama
ye ba yera chɛ yaara ŋwaane.
Ba yera maa wó taa sae,
ne kaane wolo na wowole se o lo bu to.
Ba wó taa nii daane mo, ye ba jaane ba nia.
Ba yibia maa wó bere jaja we,
ko tiini ko chɛ ba yera ne.
9Nii-na, Baŋa Wɛ dɛ-kamunu kom beene.
De nam wó ja lɛɛro mo de ba,
ye Wɛ ban-lom dem wó tiini de zaŋe de wone.
Konto maa wó pa se tega kam jei maama ji kagoa,
ye wɛleere-keira maama saare ka wone.
10Nɔɔna daa bá wane ba na wɛyuu chalechwe sem maama pwooni.
Wɛ nam ná jege de pula, ko wó taa ye lim mo.
Chana kam de bá taa nyea de pwooni.
11Amo nam wó pa se lɛɛro yi logo baŋa,
nabiina totoŋ-lwanno ŋwaane.
A ta wó waare puseŋ-nyena ba wɛleera ŋwaane.
A maa wó pa se boyere-nyena kamunim dem ti,
ye a daare a chɔge nankɔ-nyena dam dem de.
12A waarem dem konto ná ti,
nabiina fenfee yerane ta wó daare.
Balo na daare to maa wó taa jege lonne
ba dwoi sabu-seŋa kalo na lana ye ka nwoŋi Ofiri to.
13Amo nam lage a pa se wɛyuu kom jei maama taa dɔne mo,
ye tega baŋa jei maama de maa wó taa ziziŋa,
amo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ bane na zaŋe to ŋwaane.
Amo wo wó tiini ko fuli mo dɛ dem konto ne.
14Nɔɔna maama wó kwaane ba duri se ba lu,
ne feiri selo tɔɔna na zeili se ba ja to mo,
naa pei selo na ba jege nayero to.
Ba maa wó duri se ba jwoori ba tete teo de ba tete sam.
15Balo nam na wo nɛ chwoŋa se ba lu to,
nɔɔna wó ja-ba ba zɔ de se-zɔɔ ba go.
16Nɔɔna wó yigi ba bu-sese ba de tega ne ba go mo
ye ba zege ba nia.
Ba ta wó zo ba sam wone ba vere ba wonnu
ba daare ba zi ba kaana.
17A lage a chuchugi Media tiina mo se ba nwoŋi
ba vo ba jeeri Babilon teo de jara.
Banto yiga tera de lu-nyenno naa sabu-seŋa.
18Ba wó kwei ba chena mo ba tɔ nɔn-donno ba go.
Ba bá duri bu-sese yibwona,
ba nam bá duri bu-somwa de ŋwaŋa.
19Babilon mo jege nenɔŋa ko dwoi teene maama.
Babilon tiina bam maa jege fia ba teo kamunu kom ŋwaane.
Wɛ nam wó chɔge-ko mo,
ne o déem na ke tei o chɔge Sodom de Gomora to.
20Nɔɔna daa bá jwoori ba taa zoore teo kom konto wone maŋa de maŋa.
Arabi tiina bá chwi ba vwoa dáane.
Nayera de nam bá ja ba vara ba vo da se ba peini ba sii.
21Kago-vara yerane mo wó taa kare da ba beera.
Nywoŋ-kuri maa wó su ba di-dwonnu tem.
Dáane mo kunkwooru de wó taa zoora,
ye tɔro de taa kare de faŋe jei maama.
22Wiira mo wó zege teo kom dam jei sem ne ba ke sɔɔ,
Nywoŋ-kuri de maa wó zege ko sɔ-fwaaro tem wone se wei.
Kokuri to, Babilon teo kom maŋa yi ka ti,
ye ba daa bá twoŋi dɛ dedwe ko maŋa kam wone.

english_text:
The Lord's People Will Come Home
1The Lord will have mercy on Israel and will let them be his chosen people once again. He will bring them back to their own land, and foreigners will join them as part of Israel. 2Other nations will lead them home, and Israel will make slaves of them in the land that belongs to the Lord. Israel will rule over those who once governed and mistreated them.
Death to the King of Babylonia!
3The Lord will set you free from your sorrow, suffering, and slavery. 4Then you will make fun of the King of Babylonia by singing this song:
That cruel monster is done for!
He won't attack us again.
5The Lord has crushed the power
of those evil kings,
6who were furious
and never stopped abusing
the people of other nations.
7Now all the world is at peace;
its people are celebrating
with joyful songs.
8King of Babylonia,
even the cypress trees
and the cedars of Lebanon
celebrate and say,
“Since you were put down,
no one comes along
to chop us down.”
9The world of the dead
eagerly waits for you.
With great excitement,
the spirits of ancient rulers
hear about your coming.
10Each one of them will say,
“Now you are just as weak
as any of us!
11Your pride and your music
have ended here
in the world of the dead.
Worms are your blanket,
maggots are your bed.”
12 You, the bright morning star,
have fallen from the sky!
You brought down other nations;
now you are brought down.
13 You said to yourself,
“I'll climb to heaven
and place my throne
above the highest stars.
I'll sit there with the gods
far away in the north.
14I'll be above the clouds,
just like God Most High.”
15But now you are deep
in the world of the dead.
16Those who see you will stare
and wonder, “Is this the man
who made the world tremble
and shook up kingdoms?
17Did he capture every city
and make earth a desert?
Is he the one who refused
to let prisoners go home?”
18When kings die, they are buried
in glorious tombs.
19But you will be left unburied,
just another dead body
lying underfoot
like a broken branch.
You will be one of many
killed in battle and gone down
to the deep rocky pit.
20You won't be buried with kings;
you ruined your country
and murdered your people.
You evil monster!
We hope that your family
will be forgotten forever.
21We will slaughter your sons
to make them pay for the crimes
of their ancestors.
They won't take over the world
or build cities
anywhere on this earth.
22The Lord All-Powerful has promised to attack Babylonia and destroy everyone there, so that none of them will ever be remembered again. 23The Lord will sweep out the people, and the land will become a swamp for wild animals.
Assyria Will Be Punished
24 The Lord All-Powerful
has made this promise:
Everything I have planned
will happen just as I said.
25I will wipe out every Assyrian
in my country,
and I will crush those
on my mountains.
I will free my people
from slavery
to the Assyrians.
26I have planned this
for the whole world,
and my mighty arm
controls every nation.
27I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have made these plans.
No one can stop me now!
The Philistines Will Be Punished
28 This message came from the Lord in the year King Ahaz died:
29 Philistines, don't be happy
just because the rod
that punished you
is broken.
That rod will become
a poisonous snake, and then
a flying fiery dragon.
30The poor and needy will find
pastures for their sheep
and will live in safety.
But I will starve some of you,
and others will be killed.
31Cry and weep in the gates
of your towns,
you Philistines!
Smoke blows in from the north,
and every soldier is ready.
32If a messenger comes
from a distant nation,
you must say:
“The Lord built Zion.
Even the poorest of his people
will find safety there.”
translation_text:
Judah tiina wó jwoori ba di ywoni
1 Baŋa Wɛ lage o jwoori o duri Jakob dwi dem yibwona mo. O maa wó fɔge o kuri Isarele tiina bam se ba taa ye o tete nyem. O nam wó ja-ba o jwoori ba tete teo kom wone ye o pa ba jeini da. Veira laam maa wó ba ba gwaane ba wone, se ba de Jakob dwi tiina bam taa ye bedwe. 2Teene dedɛ nɔɔna mo lage ba woli Wɛ nɔɔna bam se ba jwoori ba tete teo kom ne. Isarele tiina bam maa ná tu ba jeini Baŋa Wɛ tega kam ne, ba laam wó wane dwi-gɛ tiina bam konto ba taa tei, se dwi-gɛ tiina bam ji ba kabɛ, baara de kaana maama. Konto to, ba lage ba di dam balo ya na jaane-ba ba pe to baŋa ne mo, se ba taa tei balo ya na jege-ba ba bɛɛse to.
Babilon teo pɛ taane
3Isarele tiina bam, Baŋa Wɛ wó seene o pa se á ba á sii de chanɛɛre, de yaara, de totoŋ-dɛɛra yalo á dona na fe abam ba de ya wone to. Dɛ dem konto ná yia, 4abam laam wó ta‑á ke Babilon teo pɛ mo á mɔna ye á we:
Kachɛa kam tete dam ti!
O daa bá yaare debam!
5 Baŋa Wɛ bwori puseŋ-nyena da-lwanno tem,
ye o daare o nɔne pwa dam o se tega ne.
6Ba ya jege ba dam dem konto mo
ba bɛɛse nɔɔna taa ba ba yaga.
Ba ma kwei ba bane ba fe teene pa se de toe de pa-ba,
ye ba laam yɔɔre ba jege-ba ba yaare taa.
7Tega baŋa jei maama laam nɛ bochare-zuru de yazura,
ye ba maama jege wopwolo lei ba leena.
8Lebanon teo Sedare teeni dem tete,
dedaane tei-ŋonno tedaara tem
de jege wopwolo mo de kolo na yi nmo to ye ba tɛ ba we:
“Nmo laam na to n tigi tega ne tei to ŋwaane,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá ba ywo
se kotu gwoni debam o de tega ne.”
9Babilon teo pɛ wom,
churu yɔɔre ko ti yiga mo se ko jeeri‑m.
Ko ma chiŋi chira dwi maama se ba zaŋe ba jeeri‑m.
Ko ná ye balo déem na di paare logo baŋa teene dem wone to,
churu ta pɛ se ba zaŋe ba paare yitunnu baŋa ne mo.
10Banto maama laam maa wó leiri n taane
se ba ta dede‑m we,
“Nmo de laam bwona mo ne debam na ye tei to.
Nmo de yɔɔre n ye ne debam na ye tei to mo.”
11Nmo nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom maama laam tu ko ti churu ne mo,
ye n ya ye wolo ba na mage kwanno mo
ba jege ba tei nmo yere to.
Nam nii! Kanzwa yerane laam nam mo lulugi n kuri ne,
ye kaloro de kwoli n yera yam maama.
12Nmo ya nye de naŋɔgɔ na tiini ko nyeene to mo.
Nam nii nmo laam na zege wɛɛne n to tega ne tei!
Nmo déem mo yigi logo baŋa teene maama n de tega ne,
ye nmo tete laam to n tigi n kwaga tetare ne.
13Nmo ya ke n boboŋa ne mo n we,
“Amo wó di wɛɛne mo baŋa baŋa,
se a zege a paare yituŋu kom wɛ-wɛ,
wɛyuu chalechwe sem na lɛɛne jei selo ne to.
A laam maa wó taa jei baŋa seeni peo kom ne yiga yiga,
mɛ seeni wa yam na yeini ya jeeri to.
14A ta wó di wɛɛne a gaale kunkwonnu tem mo,
se a taa ye ne Yuu-tu Wɛ wom na ye tei to.”
15Ko nam na ke tei to, ba jwoori ba dole‑m mo
ba de gwoŋ-chanluŋu wone.
Nmo laam ma‑n tu n zo churu kuri kuri.
16Balo na wo churu ne to maa wó fɔge ba nii‑m zii,
ye ko so-ba de kolo na yi‑m to.
Ba laam maa wó bwei ba ta we,
“Wolo déem na sugi tega baŋa
ye o pa logo baŋa teene dem ziziŋi to mo tento na?
17Wolo déem na pɛ se logo kom maama ji kagoa,
ye o yɔɔre o chɔge tega baŋa teene maama to mo tento na?
O ma daare o ve se o pa balo o na jaane jara wone to chwoŋa
se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ.”
18Logo baŋa teene dem pwa maama tega
ba tiga de ba nenɔŋa zela mo.
Ba dedoa dedoa maa tigi o tete yibeeli wone.
19Ko nam ná ye nmo, Babilon teo pɛ,
ba le‑m n yibeeli dem ne mo,
ne ba na gwoni tio naga ba yage tei to.
Nmo yera yam wó gwaane de balo ba na go jara wone
ye ba te ba tiga laŋa ne to mo.
Ba laam maa wó tuuri á yera yam maama ba vo ba de gwoŋo wone,
mɛ na ye kandwa jei.
Ko laam maa wó pa se ba nɔne n yera yam ba se tega ne.
20Nmo na maŋe n chɔge n teo kom
ye n go n nɔɔna bam to ŋwaane,
ba bá ke n yera yam tega ne
ne ba na ke pwa badwonna bam tei to.
Puseŋ-nyena dwi dem yera maama nam wó saare mo
se ko taa vei wuu.
21Ti-na yiga se á go pɛ wom bia,
ba nabaara wɛleera yam ŋwaane.
Yé pa-ba chwoŋa se ba wane logo baŋa maama ba di,
se ba fɔge ba lɔ teene jei maama ne ba zege.
22Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo tete nam mo lage a ke chichuŋu de Babilon tiina bam. A maa wó pa se Babilon teo kom yere saare, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa yé daare ko wone. Ba bia de ba dwi dem maama maa wó ti.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
23“Amo wó pa se ba teo kom ji kunkworru zoorem jei mɛ buli na daga to. A maa wó chɔge ko jei sem maama, ne a kwei zwɛ mo a yɔɔre a zɔre ko wonnu maama a yage.”
Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
Asiria teo taane
24Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam yɔɔre o du duuri mo o we:
“Amo na jaane boboŋa se a ke tei to wó seene ko ke mo.
A nam na ti a yiga se a toŋe kolo to jege se ko zege mo.
25A lage a yɔɔre a chochoge Asiria tiina
balo na wo amo tega kam ne to mo.
A ta wó nɔne ba balo na wo amo peero tem yuu ne to
a se tega ne.
Ko ná ye yɔgese delo Asiria tiina bam na de a nɔɔna bam ba ne to,
amo wó le-de a yage.
A maa wó dɔne ba zela yam ba bakale baŋa ne a yage.
26Amo na jege boboŋe delo tega baŋa maama ŋwaane to mo konto.
Amo nam mo twe a jeŋa
se a mage logo baŋa dwi tiina bam.”
27Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa nam na jaane se o ke tei to mo konto.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o che o chwoŋa.
O maŋe o twe o jeŋa se o toŋe.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o gwi o yiga.
Filisi tiina taane
28Wɛ déem pɛ se kwora kanto yi amo tei bene delo Pɛ Ahaz na tege to wone mo.
29Filisi tiina bam, abam maama yé ta‑á chaka we,
da-lɔŋɔ kolo ya na jege abam ko mage to laam bwori.
Lɔre-na we basankwea done ye ka bu nii mo.
Basankwea kam konto bu wom vea nam wó dwoni ka tete vea kam.
30Yini-gwia na jege balo to wó na ba ni-wodiu.
Nabwona de wó sii de ba yaara yam.
Ko daare abam Filisi tiina bam wó te mo de kana.
Abam kɔgɔ kom nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wori.
31Á teo kom nakwa bam, ta‑á chwoosa!
Á teo kom nɔn-bia bam de taa keera!
Abam Filisi tiina bam maama,
kɔre-na foone se á wo maama chɔɔre!
Kokuri to, jar-keira nwoŋi baŋa seeni
ba beene se ba jeeri abam de jara.
Kafooro tere ba kɔgɔ kom wone.
32 Dwi-gɛ tiina ná toŋe nɔɔna debam tei ne,
dé nam wó ta bɛ mo dé bere-ba?
Dé wó ta de-ba mo we,
“Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o chwi Zion teo mo o zege.
Ko nam ye dáane mo o nɔɔna balo na yaare to
wó zo ba na dalem jei.”

english_text:
Moab Will Be Punished
1 This is a message about Moab:
The towns of Ar and Kir
were destroyed in a night.
Moab is left in ruins!
2Everyone in Dibon has gone up
to the temple and the shrines
to cry and weep.
All of Moab is crying.
Heads and beards are shaved
because of what happened
at Nebo and Medeba.
3In the towns and at home,
everyone wears sackcloth
and cries loud and long.
4From Heshbon and Elealeh,
weeping is heard in Jahaz;
Moab's warriors scream
while trembling with fear.
Pity Moab
5I pity Moab!
Its people are running to Zoar
and to Eglath-Shelishiyah.
They cry on their way up
to the town of Luhith;
on the road to Horonaim
they tell of disasters.
6The streams of Nimrim
and the grasslands
have dried up.
Every plant is parched.
7The people of Moab are leaving,
crossing over Willow Creek,
taking everything they own
and have worked for.
8In the towns of Eglaim
and of Beerelim
and everywhere else in Moab
mournful cries are heard.
9The streams near Dimon
are flowing with blood.
But the Lord will bring
even worse trouble to Dimon,
because all in Moab who escape
will be attacked by lions.
translation_text:
Moaba tiina taane
1Kwora kanto mo wora Moaba tiina ŋwaane:
Ara teo na wo Moaba laŋa kam ne to chɔge.
Ko nam ye tete dedoa ne mo ko yɔɔre ko chɔge!
Kira teo de na wo Moaba ne to chɔge.
Ko nam ye tete dedoa ne mo ko chɔge konto!
2Dibon teo tiina diini ba teo jwoni diga kam,
dedaane de wara-jei bimbini dem mo,
se ba keeri wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane.
Moaba tiina yɔɔre ba keeri mo
Nebo de Medeba teene dem na chɔge to ŋwaane.
Ba cheeri ba yuni mo ye ba daare ba fane ba twana
ba wo na chɔge to ŋwaane.
3Ba ma zo gare-nyenyaaro
ye ba kare teo kom chwei sem yuu ne ba via.
Ba ta yɔɔre ba diini ba sam nayuni mo,
ye ba jeeri ba jeerim jei maama ne
ba kare ba chwoosa.
Ba maama ma vwi ba yibia tega ne
ye ba kane yi-na taa.
4Hesebon teo tiina de Elealɛ teo tiina de yɔɔre ba keeri mo.
Ba keira kam sɔɔ kɛ ko ni Jahaza teo ne de.
Moaba teo jar-keira tete vɔna pare mo,
ye ba chwoosa, ba baare maama na ti to ŋwaane.
5A yɔɔre a ŋwane a pae Moaba tiina bam mo.
Teo kom nɔɔna duri mo se ba kwaane ba yi Zoara.
Badaara de ma duri se ba vo ba yi Egalate-Selisiya.
Ba badwonna de kwaana se ba di ba yi Luhifi.
Ba nam yɔɔre ba keeri mo ye ba via.
Balo na to Horon teo chwoŋa ne ba maa kɛ to
de laare mo de ba teo kom na chɔge to.
6Nimirim bu-nɔgɔ kom we maama,
ye gaao kolo na wo dáane to de kwaare.
Ga-zuru de teeni maama jei mo.
7Moaba tiina na nɛ jejegero telo ba tiŋi to mo ba laga ba ke daane,
ye ba ja-te ba vo ba bɛ ‘Buga ni teeni’ nabara kam.
8Ba yini-keira kam kɛ ka yi Moaba laŋa kam siseini.
Ba na laare tei to yi Egelayim seeni,
ye ba ŋwana yam de vo ya yi Beeri-Elim teo kom.
9Dibon teo buga kam su de jana mo.
De ko de, amo Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se ba cham dem dwoni konto.
Ko nam ná ye balo na nɛ chwoŋa se ba lu
ye ba ta daare Moaba laŋa kam ne to,
nywoŋo mo wó zaŋe ba baŋa ne ko go-ba.

english_text:
More Troubles for Moab
1Send lambs as gifts
to the ruler of the land.
Send them across the desert
from Sela to Mount Zion.
2The women of Moab
crossing the Arnon River
are like a flock of birds
scattered from their nests.
3Moab's messengers say
to the people of Judah,
“Be kind and help us!
Shade us from the heat
of the noonday sun.
Hide our refugees!
Don't turn them away.
4Let our people live
in your country
and find safety here.”
Moab, your cruel enemies
will disappear;
they will no longer attack
and destroy your land.
5Then a kingdom of love
will be set up,
and someone from David's family
will rule with fairness.
He will do what is right
and quickly bring justice.
Moab's Pride Is Destroyed
6We have heard of Moab's pride.
Its people strut and boast,
but without reason.
7Tell everyone in Moab
to mourn for their nation.
Tell them to cry and weep
for those fancy raisins
of Kir-Hareseth.
8Vineyards near Heshbon
and Sibmah
have turned brown.
The rulers of nations
used to get drunk
on wine from those vineyards
that spread to Jazer,
then across the desert
and beyond the sea.
9Now I mourn like Jazer
for the vineyards
of Sibmah.
I shed tears for Heshbon
and for Elealeh.
There will be no more
harvest celebrations
10or joyful and happy times,
while bringing in the crops.
Singing and shouting are gone
from the vineyards.
There are no joyful shouts
where grapes were pressed.
God has silenced them all.
11Deep in my heart I hurt
for Moab and Kir-Heres.
12It's useless for Moab's people
to wear themselves out
by going to their altars
to worship and pray.
13The Lord has already said all of this about Moab. 14Now he says, “The contract of a hired worker is good for three years, but Moab's glory and greatness won't last any longer than that. Only a few of its people will survive, and they will be left helpless.”
translation_text:
1Pa-na se dé kwei pei dé ŋwe dé pa
wolo na nii tega kam baŋa ne to.
Dé wó zege Sela teo ne mo dé toŋe-se
se se tɔge kagoa kam yuu
se vo se yi Zion peo kom.
2Moaba teo kaana bam yɔɔre ba zege Aranon buga kam bubɛ ne mo
ye ba lage se ba bɛ-ka.
Ba nam nye ne zuna balo nɔɔna na chiŋi ba pworu ne
pa ba pipeigi ba vɔna to mo.
3Ba maa tɛ ba we, “Bere-na debam dé na wó ke tei to.
Kuri-na boboŋe á pa debam.
Kwei-na á lunluŋu á kwoli debam wea tetare ne,
ne woro na wora tei tete ne to.
Pa-na debam dalem jei,
dé daa na ba jege sɔŋɔ to ŋwaane.
Yé pa-na se balo na pare debam se ba ja to wane ba lɔre dé jei.
4Yage-na se debam balo ba na zeili Moaba teo ne to
na chwoŋa se dé ba dé jeini abam tetare ne.
Pa-na se dé na dalem jei abam tei ne,
se dé dona bam yé wane debam ba chɔge.”
Wolo na bɛɛse nɔɔna to nam wó jei.
Chɔgem dem de maa wó ti
ye nankɔ-nyena bam de saare tega kam baŋa ne.
5Ba wó tɔge swono baŋa ba pa paare dedwoŋi taa zega,
se nɔɔno tɔge chega kikia baŋa ne o di paare dem konto.
Wolo nam na wó di-de to ye David dwi tu mo.
Wonto wó bore nɔɔna bora de chega mo,
se o daare o nii se nɔn-ŋonne taa toŋa.
6Debam nigi Moaba teo tiina bam na jege fia tei to ni ne.
Ba yɔɔre ba bere ba tete kamunim mo de ba dagem,
ye ba toŋe yi-dɛɛre kikia.
Ba boyerem kikia yam nam ba jege kuri.
7Moaba tiina bam nam jege se ba taa chwoosi mo,
lɛɛro telo na yi ba teo kom to ŋwaane.
Ba maama wó taa keeri mo wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane.
Ta‑á keera, de ko na chɛ á yera
pa á daa ba nae Kiri-Heresi kekan-wogila á di to.
8Kare selo na wo Hesebon ne to,
de Sibima teo Vini teeni kare sem maama kwaare mo.
Tio-bia bam konto nyoa déem mo pɛ
teene dedɛ dedɛɛra nyɔ sana ba bugi.
Vini teeni dem ma ta nɛ se yi Jazera
ye de ta jage se yi kagoa kam seeni.
De nɛ sem ta kɛ se yi
naneo kom ni na wo mɛ to.
9Amo nam wó keeri mo ne Jazera tiina na keeri tei to,
Sibima Vini teeni dem na chɔge to ŋwaane.
A yi-na nwoŋi mo bare-bare,
Hesebon de Elealɛ teene ŋwaane!
Kokuri to, abam daa bá taa bage de wopwolo,
á kare wodiiru keim baŋa ne, de á teeni na ke bia tei to.
10Wopwolo de ywoni dim daa tera abam kare sem ne.
Vini teeni kare sem ne, nɔɔna ware se ba leeni lei da.
Ba maa ware se ba bage sɔɔ ba yage wɛɛne.
Ba daa ware Vini tio-bia bam se ba ŋoke ba nyoa,
kokuri to, amo pɛ se wopwolo sɔɔ keim ti ba tei ne.
11A bochare yɔɔre de zage mo Moaba teo ŋwaane,
pa se a suuri ne ba na tae kɔnɔ ye ko ye tei to.
A wo de ma tiini ko chɔge Kiri-Heresi ŋwaane.
12Moaba tiina ta ná kare ba vei ba jwona yiga ne,
ye ba ná yaare ba tete ya wara-jei sem ne,
se ba lwoori wolim ya tei ne tei maama de,
ya bá wane-ba ya jwoŋi ya yage.
13Kwora kam konto mo Baŋa Wɛ déem ya maŋe o pa Moaba teo kom ŋwaane. 14Baŋa Wɛ ta na tage tei to mo tento: “Bena yatɔ ná yia, ne tontoŋeno na jeeli o totoŋa da yam chekke tei to, Moaba teo jejegero tem na pa-ba zula to daa bá taa jege kuri. Ko nɔn-bia bam na maŋe ba daga tei to de, ba fenfee yerane mo wó daare, ye ba de nam wó taa tiini ba bwona mo.”

english_text:
Damascus Will Be Punished
1 This is a message about Damascus:
Damascus is doomed!
It will end up in ruins.
2The villages around Aroer
will be deserted,
with only sheep living there
and no one to bother them.
3Israel will lose its fortresses.
The kingdom of Damascus
will be destroyed;
its survivors will suffer
the same fate as Israel.
The Lord All-Powerful
has promised this.
Sin and Suffering
4When that time comes,
the glorious nation of Israel
will be brought down;
its prosperous people
will be skin and bones.
5Israel will be like wheat fields
in Rephaim Valley
picked clean of grain.
6It will be like an olive tree
beaten with a stick,
leaving two or three olives
or maybe four or five
on the highest
or most fruitful branches.
The Lord God of Israel
has promised this.
7At that time the people will turn and trust their Creator, the holy God of Israel. 8They have built altars and places for burning incense to their goddess Asherah, and they have set up sacred poles for her. But they will stop worshiping at these places.
9Israel captured powerful cities and chased out the people who lived there. But these cities will lie in ruins, covered over with weeds and underbrush.
10Israel, you have forgotten
the God who saves you,
the one who is the mighty rock
where you find protection.
You plant the finest flowers
to honor a foreign god.
11The plants may sprout
and blossom
that very same morning,
but it will do you no good,
because you will suffer
endless agony.
God Defends His People
12The nations are a noisy,
thunderous sea.
13But even if they roar
like a fearsome flood,
God will give the command
to turn them back.
They will be like dust,
or like a tumbleweed
blowing across the hills
in a windstorm.
14In the evening
their attack is fierce,
but by morning
they are destroyed.
This is what happens to those
who raid and rob us.
translation_text:
Damasika teo taane
1Kwora kalo na wora Damasika teo kom ŋwaane to mo tento:
“Nii mo! Damasika teo kom daa bá taa ye te-fɔrɔ!
Ko lage ko taa ye di-dwonnu yerane mo ko zega.
2Ba wó duri ba daare Arowa teene dem
se vare-mwa yerane taa tigi de wone,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane-ba se o zeili.
3Efrayim teene dem ya na lɔge de pe de dam to wó chɔge.
Damasika teo paare dam dem de maa wó ti.
Siria tiina balo fenfee na daare to wó yaale mo,
ne Isarele tiina déem na daga ye ba laam yaale tei to.”
Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.
4“Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia,
Jakob dwi tiina nenɔŋa kam wó ba tega.
Teo kom jejegero maa wó jei,
ne kana na jege nadum pa se o zwale tei to.
5Ko na wó ke-ba tei to wó taa nye ne
men-zagena na zage mena ba ke daane tei to mo.
Ko ta wó taa nye ne ba na lare mena Refayim bwolo kom ne tei to.
6Men-lara yadaara nam ta wó daare da.
Ko wó ke ne ba na pore Olivi tio tei,
ye ba daare ko tio-bia balei, naa batɔ,
tio kom nɛ selo na tiini se wo wɛ-wɛ to yera ne.
Tio-bi-laaro tena, naa tenu mo wó daare
ko nɛ sem maama ne.”
Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to mo tage konto.
7Maŋa kam konto maa ná yia,
nɔɔna wó kwoni ba nii ba Keiru wom se o zeini-ba.
Ba wó kwei ba teena mo
ba daŋe Isarele tiina Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom wone.
8Ba yiga daa bá taa wo bimbina yalo
ba na ke de ba je to wone.
Ko ná ye jwona yalo ba na mɔɔne to,
ba teena bá taa wo ya wone,
ne ko ná ye Asera nyenyego dɛ sem
naa talwoŋa zwɛɛm bimbina yam de.
9Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia, nɔɔna wó duri ba daare teene delo na lɔge de pe de dam ye Isarele tiina bam zeili-ba de wone to. Ga-cheiŋo de punnu yerane mo wó taa wora. Jei sem maama maa wó taa tigi yɔɔ yerane.
10Abam nam swei á Wɛ wom na ye á Vereno to ni ne mo.
Á daa maa ba guli Wɛ na ye á peo de á dalem jei to gula.
Konto ŋwaane, abam ná maŋe á jeiri teeni delo na tiini de lana to,
de delo á na zeŋe á ja á nwoŋi dwi-gɛ tiina teene wone á ba to,
11abam nam ná nii de baŋa ne pa se de puli de nwoŋi lela,
ye de be de ke punnu tetete delo wone á na jeiri-de to de,
á bá na kolokolo á zage.
Á nam wó na wo-chechɔgɔ de zonne delo na ba ti to yerane mo.
12Nii dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ jar-keira na ke sɔɔ tei!
Ba yɔɔre ba wuuri mo ne naneo kom na wuuri tei to!
Nii ba nɔn-kɔgɔ sɔɔ na zaŋe tei!
Ko nye ne na-fɔrɔ na wuuri ba beene tei to mo!
13Nɔɔna bam konto kwora ná maŋe ka zaŋe,
ne na-fɔrɔ na wuuri ko ke sɔɔ tei to de,
Baŋa Wɛ nam ná puri o ni o bwɛ-ba,
ba maama wó lage jei mo ba vo.
Ko wó taa nye de vio na kale swanno zwonnu yuu ne
ko ja jei tei to mo,
naa vo-kekara na pɛ weeru ko ja kɛ tei to mo.
14Dedaan-ni maŋa ne, foone tiini de jege debam,
dé dona na yi debam to ŋwaane.
Tega nam na jege ka poore to, de ba viiri mo!
Kolo na wó yi balo na tu se ba ke chichuŋu de debam
ye ba vere dé wonnu ba ja viiri to mo konto.

english_text:
Ethiopia Will Be Punished
1 Downstream from Ethiopia
lies the country of Egypt,
swarming with insects.
2Egypt sends messengers
up the Nile River
on ships made of reeds.
Send them fast to Ethiopia,
whose people are tall
and have smooth skin.
Their land is divided by rivers;
they are strong and brutal,
feared all over the world.
3Everyone on this earth,
listen with care!
A signal will be given
on the mountains,
and you will hear a trumpet.
4The Lord said to me,
“I will calmly look down
from my home above—
as calmly as the sun at noon
or clouds in the heat
of harvest season.”
5Before the blossoms
can turn into grapes,
God will cut off the sprouts
and hack off the branches.
6Ethiopians will be food
for mountain vultures
during the summer
and for wild animals
during the winter.
7Those Ethiopians are tall and their skin is smooth. They are feared all over the world, because they are strong and brutal. But at that time they will come from their land divided by rivers, and they will bring gifts to the Lord All-Powerful, who is worshiped on Mount Zion.
translation_text:
Kusi tiina taane
1Lɛɛro wó yi teo kolo sɔɔ na zaŋa
ne kayere mo wuuri se beene to!
Teo kom konto nam lɛɛne ko wo Kusi bwi sem jei ne mo.
2Ko yeini ko toŋe ko nɔɔna de kwora mo
se ba tɔge Naili buga kam baŋa ne ba vo jei sedwonna ba pa.
Ba kwei sangɛ mo ba ma ba ke nabwooru telo ba na mae ba yɛ na to.
Nam toŋe-ba se ba ke lela ba jwoori ba tete teo.
Ko ye teo kolo nɔɔna na dɔra ye ba yera de swola to.
Nɔɔna jei maama ne kɔre ko nɔn-bia mo,
ba keim na chana
ye ba chɔge balo na dwoni de-ba to ŋwaane.
Ba tega kam nam ye bwi mo pɔɔre-ka se ke tetare ne.
3Abam logo baŋa nabiina maama,
ba ná zeiŋi tuta peero tem yuu ne, fɔge-na á nii!
Ba maa ná wugi nabɔnɔ, fɔge-na á cheigi!
4 Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei de amo to mo tento:
“Amo wó zege a na zoore mɛ to ne mo
se a taa ye chemm ye a nia.
Amo wó toŋe mɛmɛ ne wulim na zaŋe wea maŋa ne tei to,
naa nyɔnɔ na toe wodiu zagem maŋa ne tei to mo.”
5Kokuri to, Vini teeni ná gɛ fee se de lei de bia,
maŋa kalo punnu tem na yɔɔre te wora te bere se te ke bia to,
Wɛ lage o kwei lara mo o pere teeni dem nɛ o de tega ne,
ne se ná ye balɛ naa se ye selo na jage se maa kɛ yiga to de.
6Ba yera yam wó maŋe tega ne mo,
se ya ji wodiiru ya pa peero yuu zuna de kago-vara.
Kwea maŋa ne mo zuna bam wó di-ya,
se kago-vara bam de di-ya waaro maŋa ne.
7Maŋa kam konto ne nɔɔna wó ja pɛɛra ba ba ba pa Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Balo na wó ja pɛɛra yam ba ba ba pa‑o to mo
nwoŋi teo kolo nɔɔna na dɔra ye ba yera de swola to.
Nɔɔna jei maama ne kɔre ko nɔn-bia mo,
ba keim na chana
ye ba chɔge balo na dwoni de-ba to ŋwaane.
Ba tega kam nam ye bwi mo pɔɔre-ka se ke tetare ne.
Banto wó ja ba pɛɛra ba ba Zion peo kom, jeiga kalo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli o yere da to mo.

english_text:
Egypt Will Be Punished
1 This is a message about Egypt:
The Lord comes to Egypt,
riding swiftly on a cloud.
The people are weak from fear.
Their idols tremble
as he approaches and says,
2“I will punish Egypt
with civil war—
neighbors, cities, and kingdoms
will fight each other.
3“Egypt will be discouraged
when I confuse their plans.
They will try to get advice
from their idols,
from the spirits of the dead,
and from fortunetellers.
4I will put the Egyptians
under the power of a cruel,
heartless king.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have promised this.”
Trouble along the Nile
5The Nile River will dry up
and become parched land.
6Its streams will stink,
Egypt will have no water,
and the reeds and tall grass
will dry up.
7Fields along the Nile
will be completely barren;
every plant will disappear.
8Those who fish in the Nile
will be discouraged
and mourn.
9None of the cloth makers
will know what to do,
and they will turn pale.
10Weavers will be confused;
paid workers will cry and mourn.
Egypt's Helpless Leaders
11The king's officials in Zoan
are foolish themselves
and give stupid advice.
How can they say to him,
“We are very wise,
and our families go back
to kings of long ago?”
12Where are those wise men now?
If they can, let them say
what the Lord All-Powerful
intends for Egypt.
13The royal officials in Zoan
and in Memphis
are foolish and deceived.
The leaders in every state
have given bad advice
to the nation.
14The Lord has confused Egypt;
its leaders have made it stagger
and vomit like a drunkard.
15No one in Egypt can do a thing,
no matter who they are.
16When the Lord All-Powerful punishes Egypt with his mighty arm, the Egyptians will become terribly weak and will tremble with fear. 17They will be so terrified of Judah that they will be frightened by the very mention of its name. This will happen because of what the Lord All-Powerful is planning against Egypt.
The Lord Will Bless Egypt, Assyria, and Israel
18The time is coming when Hebrew will be spoken in five Egyptian cities, and their people will become followers of the Lord. One of these cities will be called City of the Sun.
19In the heart of Egypt an altar will be set up for the Lord; at its border a shrine will be built to honor him. 20These will remind the Egyptians that the Lord All-Powerful is with them. And when they are in trouble and ask for help, he will send someone to rescue them from their enemies. 21The Lord will show the Egyptians who he is, and they will know and worship the Lord. They will bring him sacrifices and offerings, and they will keep their promises to him. 22After the Lord has punished Egypt, the people will turn to him. Then he will answer their prayers, and the Egyptians will be healed.
23At that time a good road will run from Egypt to Assyria. The Egyptians and the Assyrians will travel back and forth from Egypt to Assyria, and they will worship together. 24Israel will join with these two countries. They will be a blessing to everyone on earth, 25then the Lord All-Powerful will bless them by saying,
“The Egyptians are my people.
I created the Assyrians
and chose the Israelites.”
translation_text:
Ejipti teo taane
1Wɛ kwora kalo na vei Ejipti teo seeni to mo tento:
Nii-na! Baŋa Wɛ dɔge kunkwoŋo kolo na wurigi to baŋa ne
o maa beene Ejipti.
Ejipti teo jwona yam yera sae mo o yiga ne.
Ko maa ná ye Ejipti tiina bam tete,
ba wo maama chɔɔre mo.
2“A lage a pa Ejipti tiina bam zaŋe da-baŋa ne mo ba ke jara.
Nɔɔno mo wó ke jara de o choro,
ye nɔɔno de o faro de dwoni daane.
Teo wó chiŋi ko dwoŋi teo se jara zaŋe,
ye pɛ de ke chichuŋu de o dwoŋi pɛ.
3Ejipti tiina bam nagwola lage ya te mo,
amo na wó pa ba boboŋa yam ji kafɛ to ŋwaane.
Ba wó nwoŋi beira se ba lɔre ba jwona yam de ba chira boboŋa.
Ba maa wó vo chichiri vora de yi-nara tei.
4Amo nam lage a kwei Ejipti tiina bam mo
a ke pɛ-balɔrɔ jeŋa ne.
Wonto wó tɔge keim-chɛɛre baŋa ne o taa tei-ba.”
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Paŋwa to mo tage konto.
5Naili buga na bam wó we ba ti,
pa se te-kora yerane daare.
6Bu-nwaro tem wó taa lwoi mo,
ye nabare sem de na ba ba we maama.
Buga ni gaaro, de nanchan-gullu tem de maama wó kwaare.
7Ko woli da, wodiiru telo ba na dugi
Naili buga kam ni ne to maama wó ko mo.
Ko nam ná ye kare selo ba na dugi buga kam ni ne to,
se maama wó ko mo, ye vio kale ko ja jei,
se kare daa yé daare dáane.
8Ywon-jara wó taa vuvuni mo ye ba keera.
Kokuri to, balo na de ba gwoli-dole Naili buga kam wone to,
de balo na dole ba ŋwe ba de ka wone to
wó taa toŋa yɔɔ yerane mo.
9Balo na toŋe gare-nyenno totoŋa to vɔna wó pare mo.
Balo de na dole gare-yia to teena wó ti.
10Ko ná ye balo na sɔ gwaaro to,
ba wo wó chɔɔre mo.
Balo maama na toŋe ŋweero ŋwaane to wo maa wó chɔge.
11Zoan teo dedɛɛra bam yɔɔre ba ye jworru yerane mo.
Ejipti Pa-faro wom na jege nakwa balo to ba bere‑o swa.
Abam lage á tɔge chwoŋa kɔ ne mo se á ta ded‑o we,
“Amo de tɔge a ye swa tiina dwi dem wo nɔɔno mo.
Ko na zege faŋa to mo
dé nabaara bam jwoŋi swa pwa tei ne”?
12Nmo swa tiina nam daa wo yein-seeni mo?
Bwoŋi-ba se ba ba ba ta ba bere‑m
kolo maama Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ
na boŋe se o ke de Ejipti teo kom to.
13Zoan teo dedɛɛra bam seene ba ji jworru mo.
Ko ta ná ye Memfisi teo yiga tiina bam,
nɔɔna jege-ba ba gana mo.
Balo na ye Ejipti sɔ-yuni tem yiga tiina to
jaane ba nɔɔna bam ba ywori.
14 Baŋa Wɛ nam na ke tei to,
o vugimi nakwa bam boboŋa mo,
pa se Ejipti tiina kare ba tusi chwoŋa.
Ba maa nye de sa-nyɔro na bugi
ye o vei chwoŋa yuu de gaao wone tei to.
15Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera Ejipti teo ne
se kotu wane o jwoŋi-ba o yage.
O ná ye nɔn-yero naa nɔn-kafɛ mo de,
naa nadum naa nabwom mo,
kotu bá wane o woli-ba.
16Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia, Ejipti teo tiina maama wó na Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na twe o jeŋa tei se o waare-ba to. Konto maa wó pa ba taa fona ne kaana na jege foone tei to. 17Judah teo tiina nam mo lage ba pa foone tiini de ja Ejipti teo nɔɔna bam. Ba maa ná yɔɔre ba bwoŋi Judah teo kom yere ba bere wolo, kotu wó fom mo, de Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na boŋe se o ke-ba tei to.
18Maŋa kam konto ná yia, Ejipti teene denu mo lage de taa jege Hiburu taane dem ba ŋɔɔna, ne ba na ŋɔɔne Kanaan ne tei to. Ba laam maa wó du duuri ba sɛ ba pa Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Ba wó taa bwoi teene dem konto dedoa yere we, “Wea Teo kom.”
19Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia, ba wó lɔ bimbini Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane Ejipti teo kom tetare ne. Ba ta maa wó chwi kandwɛ nenɛɛne ywei dwoŋi Ejipti siseini dem ne ba pa‑o. 20Wonnu tem konto wó taa ye memaŋe se te guli Ejipti tiina bam mo we Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ yɔɔre o jege dam. Ba dona ná jege-ba ba bɛɛsa, ye ba ná keeri ba jare‑o, o de wó toŋe dedɛɛro se o ba o jwoŋi-ba o yage. 21Baŋa Wɛ laam wó pa Ejipti tiina bam lɔre o na ye wolo to chekke, ye ba de sɛ ba pa‑o. Ba maa wó taa jaane pɛɛra ba tui ba ke kaanem ba pa‑o, se ba ma ba zuli‑o. Ba ta wó taa gwoni ba nia ded‑o, ba daare ba tɔge-ya. 22Baŋa Wɛ tete mo wó waare Ejipti tiina bam, ye wonto nam ta mo lage o pa-ba yazura. Ba maa ná pipiri ba jwoori o tei, o de wó sɛ ba wɛ-lworo kom ye o daare o yɔɔre-ba.
23Maŋa kam konto ná yia, chwo-fara wó taa tigi yala-yala Ejipti de Asiria teene dem tetare ne. Teene dem konto delei nɔɔna wó taa kare ba vei da-teene dem wone. Ba ta wó yeini ba ke daane ba zuli Wɛ. 24Maŋa kam konto ne, Isarele teo kom wó woli Ejipti de Asiria wone, se teene detɔ dem konto taa ye daane. Ba maa wó ja Wɛ swolim ba ba ba pa tega baŋa maama nabiina. 25Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ laam maa wó swɛ banto maama swolim ye o ta we, “Ejipti tiina bam ye amo nɔɔna mo. Asiria tiina bam maa ye amo tete jeŋa totoŋa. Se ko ná ye Isarele tiina bam, amo mo kuri-ba se ba taa ye amo tete nyɔn-mage nɔɔna. Konto ŋwaane, amo wó swɛ ba maama swolim.”

english_text:
Isaiah Acts Out the Defeat of Egypt and Ethiopia
1King Sargon of Assyria gave orders for his army commander to capture the city of Ashdod. 2About this same time the Lord had told me, “Isaiah, take off everything, including your sandals!” I did this and went around naked and barefoot 3for three years.
Then the Lord said:
What Isaiah has done is a warning to Egypt and Ethiopia. 4Everyone in these two countries will be led away naked and barefoot by the king of Assyria. Young or old, they will be taken prisoner, and Egypt will be disgraced. 5They will be confused and frustrated, because they depended on Ethiopia and bragged about Egypt. 6When this happens, the people who live along the coast will say, “Look what happened to them! We ran to them for safety, hoping they would protect us from the king of Assyria. But now, there is no escape for us.”
translation_text:
Ejipti de Kusi taane
1Asiria teo pɛ Saregon déem toŋe o jar-keira yuu tu pa o vo o jeeri Asedodi teo de jara, se o wane-ko o di. 2Bene dem konto wone mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Amozi bu Izaya o we, “Lɔɔre gare-nyenyaaro telo na wo n yera ne to, se n daare n le natera yalo n na zo to.” O ma seene o ke konto, ye o kare jei sem maama o beera bwori de o napera yerane.
3 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta o we, “Ne amo tontoŋeno Izaya na kare o vei bwori o napera baŋa ne bena yatɔ tei to, keim dem konto wó ji maana mo se ko bere kolo na wó yi Ejipti teo de Kusi teo to. 4Asiria teo pɛ lage o ba o kale Ejipti de Kusi tiina balo o na wane to mo o ja o kɛ, ye ba wó taa vei bwori de napera mo ba maa kɛa. Ko nam wó taa ye ba nɔn-donno de ba nɔn-kwe mo, ye ba maama kura nae chaveera yerane. 5Balo ya na kwei ba teena ba daŋe Kusi teo baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba ke ba chega de Ejipti teo to laam maa wó taa kɔre foone, ye chaveera jege-ba. 6Maŋa kam konto ná yia, balo na zoore naneo kom ni seeni to laam maa wó ta we, ‘Debam ya sale banto yera ne ye dé duri dé vo ba tei se ba jwoŋi debam mo ba yage Asiria pɛ wom jeŋa ne. Nam nii kolo na yi-ba to! Debam laam nam wó tɔge yein-seeni mo se dé lu?’ ”

english_text:
The Fall of Babylonia
1This is a message about a desert beside the sea:
Enemies from a hostile nation
attack like a whirlwind
from the Southern Desert.
2What a horrible vision
was shown to me—
a vision of betrayal
and destruction.
Tell Elam and Media
to surround and attack
the Babylonians.
The Lord has sworn to end
the suffering they caused.
3I'm in terrible pain
like a woman giving birth.
I'm shocked and hurt so much
that I can't hear or see.
4My head spins; I'm horrified!
Early evening, my favorite time,
has become a nightmare.
5In Babylon the high officials
were having a feast.
They were eating and drinking,
when someone shouted,
“Officers, take your places!
Grab your shields.”
6The Lord said to me,
“Send guards
to find out
what's going on.
7When they see cavalry troops
and columns of soldiers
on donkeys and camels,
tell them to be ready!”
8Then a guard said,
“I have stood day and night
on this watchtower, Lord.
9 Now I see column after column
of cavalry troops.”
At once someone shouted,
“Babylon has fallen!
Every idol in the city
lies broken on the ground.”
10Then I said, “My people,
you have suffered terribly,
but I have a message for you
from the Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel.”
How Much Longer?
11This is a message about Dumah:
From the country of Seir,
someone shouts to me,
“Guard, how much longer
before daylight?”
12From my guard post, I answered,
“Morning will soon be here,
but night will return.
If you want to know more,
come back later.”
13This is a message for Arabs who live in the barren desert in the region of Dedan:
You must order your caravans
14to bring water for those
who are thirsty.
You people of Tema
must bring food
for the hungry refugees.
15They are worn out and weary
from being chased by enemies
with swords and arrows.
16The Lord said to me:
A year from now the glory of the people of Kedar will all come to an end, just as a worker's contract ends after a year. 17Only a few of their warriors will be left with bows and arrows. This is a promise that I, the Lord God of Israel, have made.
translation_text:
Babilon teo taane
1Kwora kanto wora kagoa kalo na tigi naneo kom ni ne to ŋwaane mo:
Ne vo-kekara na yɔɔre ka dole tega-kuri seeni jei sem ne tei to,
konto mo lɛɛro lage te nwoŋi kagoa kam seeni
mɛ foone na daga to te ba abam baŋa.
2Amo nii a na chanɛɛre mo Wɛ na le o bere-ne:
Jei maama ne nɔɔno wó nwoŋi o dwoŋi kwaga ne.
Venverena de wó zo ba vere wonnu.
Elam jar-keira bam,
ja-na jara yam á jeeri-ba!
Abam Media tiina bam,
á de kaare-na ba teo kom maama á pu!
Amo lage a pa yaara yalo banto na ke nɔɔna yera ne to ti.
3A na nɛ wonnu telo Wɛ na le o bere-ne to,
mo a yera maama yɔɔre ya wiira.
A maa yɔɔre a wowola,
ne kapua na virigi puga se o lo bu tei to.
A yera chɛ de kolo a na nigi to.
A boboŋa maa vugimi de kolo a na nɛ to.
4A yia maama yɔɔre ya gigili mo.
Foone ŋwaane a yera maama maa sae.
A ya na beeri se wɛ-toore yi lela to,
de nam jwoori de ja foone mo de ba de pa-ne.
5Nii-na! Ba ti wodiu yiga mo se ba jeini ba di kuri,
ye ba lware gare-jala se nɔɔna jeini te baŋa ne ba di.
Ba laam maa jei ba di, ye ba daare ba nyɔ sana.
Abam dedɛɛra bam, nam zaŋe wɛɛne!
Kwɛ-na á jara nantane sem se á nwoŋi á vo á ke jara!
6Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de amo o we:
“Véi n kwei nɔɔno n zege se o taa yere teo kom.
Ta ded‑o se o taa tɛ kolo o na nɛ to o bere nɔɔna.
7Kotu nam ná nɛ jara-keim torokooro
ye sisein-nɔɔna vaŋe-te,
ye o ta ná nɛ nɔɔna na dɔge bonɛ baŋa ne
naa ba dɔge kona baŋa ne,
ko bere we o jege se o taa fɔge
o yere o tete mo lanyerane.”
8Teo yereno wom laam ma tɔɔle o ta o we,
“Amo tu, dɛ maama wone mo
amo yɔɔre a zege a zega jei sem ne.
Tete maama ne de, a ta wora mo ye a yere jei sem.
9Nam nii! Nɔɔno mo beene
o na dɔge jara-keim toroko baŋa ne,
ye sisein-nɔɔna vaŋe-ko.”
Nɔɔno wom mo baga o yaga we:
“Babilon teo kom chɔge ywoo!
Ko yɔɔre ko chɔge mo!
Ba teo jwona yam nyenyero maama chochoge mo,
ye ya tigi tega kam jei maama ne.”
10A nɔɔna bam, ba pɛ ko zo á yera mo
ne kaane na zɔge mena kazɔgɔ ne tei to.
Amo nam jwoŋi kwora mo
ye ka nwoŋi Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom
na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to tei ne.
Kwora kam konto mo a laam nam tage a bere abam.
Edom teo taane
11Kwora kanto wora Duma teo kom ŋwaane mo:
Nɔɔno mo zege Seyira ne o bwei o we,
“Maŋa kɔ mo tega kam wó poore?
Ta n bere-ne maŋa kalo tega na wó poore to.”
12Teo yereno wom ma leiri o we,
“Ko bá dáane se tega poore.
Ka nam ta wó jwoori ka yi.
Nmo nam ná lage se n daa‑n bwei woŋo n woli da,
se n jwoori n ba n bwei se n lɔre.”
Arabia jei sem taane
13Kwora kalo na wora Arabia ŋwaane to mo tento:
Abam Dedan pipim-piina bam ná yeini á tɔge daane
á beeri Arabia te-kora kam ne,
á wó peini teeni woro ne mo se tega laam poore.
14Beeri-na na á pa na-nyɔm na jege balo to!
Abam balo de na zoore Tema teo ne to,
ja-na wodiiru á ba
á pa balo na duri se ba lu cham wone to.
15Kokuri to, banto maŋe ba duri mo
se ba lu jara wone.
Ba maa kwaane se ba lu se-zɔɔro de chena tam wone,
jar-keira na lage se ba go-ba to ŋwaane.
16Amo Teiru Wɛ nam na tage tei de amo to mo tento: “Bene dedoa maŋa ne, ne tontoŋeno na jeeli o totoŋa da yam chekke tei to, de Kedare teo nenɔŋa kam ti. 17Kedare che-tara bam mo ye bembɛ ba nɔɔna bam maama wone. Ba nam lage ba daare fenfee yerane mo.”
Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to mo tage konto.

english_text:
Trouble in Vision Valley
1This is a message about Vision Valley:
Why are you celebrating
on the flat roofs
of your houses?
2Your city is filled
with noisy shouts.
Those who lie drunk
in your streets
were not killed in battle.
3Your leaders ran away,
but they were captured
without a fight.
No matter how far they ran,
they were found and caught.
4Then I said, “Leave me alone!
Let me cry bitter tears.
My people have been destroyed,
so don't try to comfort me.”
5The Lord All-Powerful
had chosen a time
for noisy shouts and confusion
to fill Vision Valley,
and for everyone to beg
the mountains for help.
6The people of Elam and Kir
attacked with chariots
and carried shields.
7Your most beautiful valleys
were covered with chariots;
your cities were surrounded
by cavalry troops.
8Judah was left defenseless.
At that time you trusted in the weapons you had stored in Forest Palace. 9You saw the holes in the outer wall of Jerusalem, and you brought water from the lower pool. 10You counted the houses in Jerusalem and tore down some of them, so you could get stones to repair the city wall. 11Then you built a large tank between the walls to store the water. But you refused to trust the God who planned this long ago and made it happen.
A Time To Weep
12When all of this happened,
the Lord All-Powerful told you
to weep and mourn,
to shave your heads,
and wear sackcloth.
13 But instead, you celebrated
by feasting on beef and lamb
and by drinking wine,
because you said,
“Let's eat and drink today!
Tomorrow we may die.”
14The Lord All-Powerful
has spoken to me
this solemn promise:
“I won't forgive them for this,
not as long as they live.”
Selfish Officials Are Doomed
15The Lord All-Powerful is sending me with this message for Shebna, the prime minister:
16Shebna, what gives you the right to have a tomb carved out of rock in this burial place of royalty? None of your relatives are buried here. 17You may be powerful, but the Lord is about to snatch you up and throw you away. 18He will roll you into a ball and throw you into a wide open country, where you will die and your chariots will be destroyed. You're a disgrace to those you serve.
19The Lord is going to take away your job! 20-21He will give your official robes and your authority to his servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
Eliakim will be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the royal family of Judah. 22 The Lord will put him in charge of the key that belongs to King David's family. No one will be able to unlock what he locks, and no one will be able to lock what he unlocks. 23The Lord will make him as firm in his position as a tent peg hammered in the ground, and Eliakim will bring honor to his family.
24His children and relatives will be supported by him, like pans hanging from a peg on the wall. 25That peg is fastened firmly now, but someday it will be shaken loose and fall down. Then everything that was hanging on it will be destroyed. This is what the Lord All-Powerful has promised.
translation_text:
Jerusalem teo taane
1Kwora kanto mo wora teo kolo yere na ye ‘Veerem Bwolo’ to ŋwaane:
Bɛ mo jege ko ke á teo kom ne,
pa nɔɔna bam maama di ba sam nayuni?
2Bɛ mo ke ye ba sɔɔ zaŋe teo kom jei maama ne,
ye ba bage ba yaga de wopwolo?
Balo na tege abam teo kom wone to
wo tɔge jara-keim baŋa ne mo ba te.
3Abam teo yiga tiina bam maama duri mo
se ba lu jara yam wone.
Ba yɔɔre ba sɛ bwom ba pa ba dona bam mo
ye jara yam ta wo yi-ba.
Abam wone balo maama ya na kwaane
se ba liisi ba dona yiga ne to,
ba ta nɛ-ba mo ye ba ja ba maama nywa!
4Konto ŋwaane amo de laam maa we,
“Yage-ne konto chemm,
se a keeri lanyerane a nɔɔna bam ŋwaane.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé gwi-ne de a keira kam,
kokuri to, chɔgem mo yɔɔre de yi a nɔɔna bam.”
5Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom le dɛ mo o tiŋi
de na jege sɔɔ, de vuvuga, de cham,
se o pa de yi Veerem Bwolo kom.
De maa ye dɛ delo ne ba na wó kuusi teo kom kabiri mo,
se ko nɔn-bia bam keira sɔɔ zaŋe ko yi peero jei sem to.
6Elam teo tiina ma kwei ba che-kɔro tem
ba nwoŋi de ba jara-keim torokooro,
de ba sisein-dira maama.
Kiri teo tiina de ti ba jara nantane sem yiga mo.
7Ko ná ye abam bwollu telo ya na ke wodiiru lanyerane to,
jara sisei-torokooro laam mo su te maama se jara ke.
Balo maa na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna yuu ne to
de ma vo ba cheiŋi teo kom manchwo-peo ni.
8Judah teo da ba jege dalem jei se ba ma che ba tete.
Maŋa kam konto ne,
abam boŋe se á le jara zela yalo
ya na tigi ‘Goa’ diga kam ne to mo.
9Abam nɛ we David teo kabiri sem
su de lolwe dedɛ.
Á ma la na á zege kuri seeni chɔgɔ kom ne,
se á daare á mɔ-ba.
10Á ma jeeli Jerusalem teo sam dem ni
ye á daare á yigi de dedwonna á de tega ne,
se á ma á fɔge á lɔ teo kabiri sem se se taa dana.
11Á ta koge gwoŋo mo á yage kabiri selei sem tetare ne
se á ta‑á ke na balo na nwoŋi chɔ-dwoŋo kom wone to dáane.
De ko de, abam yiga nam tera de wolo na pɛ se wonnu tento ke to.
Á maa wo nege wolo na boŋe te boboŋa faŋa faŋa to.
12Maŋa kam konto ne,
Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom nam ya tage de abam mo
se á ka yi-na
ye á ta keeri wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane,
se á daare á cheeri á yuni,
ye á kwei gare-nyenyaaro á zo.
13Nam nii abam na ke wopwolo ye á chake tei!
Á kare á goe naane de pei mo se á ma á di kuri.
Á maa jege nɔna dedɛ á dona,
ye á daare á nyɔ sana!
Abam laam maa tɛ we, “Pa-na se dé taa di dé ni ne,
kokuri to dé yeiri dé jwa wó te na.”
14Amo nigi Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage o we, “Amo bere a bá kwei ba wɛleere dento a chɛ-ba se ko maŋe ko yi ba toone de.” Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.
15Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tage tento mo o we:
“Vei Sebena tei, wolo na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom kikia maama baŋa ne to, se n ta ded‑o we: 16Nmo bere n pa n ye wɔ mo? Ba suli n nabaara badwonna ywo, se n vo n lage n tete yibeeli pɛ-sɔŋɔ yibeela jei sem ne n tiŋi mo na? Bɛ mo ye n vo n bɔɔre bɔɔne peo kom ne wɛ-wɛ, ye n sare siu jei n tete ŋwaane.
17A nɔɔno, nam ta‑n yei we, Baŋa Wɛ mo lage se o ja‑m o vuvugi o dole o yage de dam. 18O wó ja‑m o kukuli o ke daane ne geili dwoŋi to, ye o laam dole‑m o yage tega kalo na tiini ka yala to wone. Nmo ma‑n wó te dáane, ye n sisei-torokooro telo na pɛ‑m zula to de maŋe da. Nmo nam ye wolo na tiini n yaale n tu wom sɔŋɔ kom to mo.
19Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam lage a le‑m mo n totoŋe dem baŋa ne, se n ga zula yalo ya na tɔge de totoŋe dem to. 20Maŋa kam ná yia, amo wó bwoŋi a tontoŋeno Hilikia bu Eliakim. 21A maa wó pa‑o chwoŋa se o taa zoore nmo gwaaro tem, ye o daare o vɔ nmo vovoa kam o teiŋa ne, ye a kwei n dam dem a pa‑o. O laam maa wó ji Jerusalem nɔn-bia bam, de Judah dwi tiina bam maama kwo. 22A lage a kwei David paare dem bwor-bu mo a ke o jeŋa ne. O maa ná jaane boboŋa se kolo ke, nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o gwi o boboŋe dem. O nam ná we kolo bá ke, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware se o pa ko ke. 23A nam ta wó pa o kuri ja tega mo, ne ba na page paare delo tega ne to. Konto to Eliakim mo wó ja zula o ba o pa o kwo sɔŋɔ kom maama. 24O diga tiina nam wó kwei ba chana maama ba gwori wonto mo. Ba wó taa pale ba tete o yera ne mo, ne ba na page chene kabira yera ne ye ba pale kambi de kabeili de baŋa ne tei to.”
25Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we, “Maŋa kam nam ná yia, chene dem wó kore de to tega ne. Wonnu telo maama ya na leigi de yera ne to maa wó pare te to tega ne.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_text:
The City of Tyre Will Be Punished
1 This is a message from distant islands about the city of Tyre:
Cry, you seagoing ships!
Tyre and its houses
lie in ruins.
2Mourn in silence,
you shop owners of Sidon,
you people on the coast.
Your sailors crossed oceans,
making your city rich.
3Your merchants sailed the seas,
making you wealthy by trading
with nation after nation.
They brought back grain
that grew along the Nile.
4Sidon, you are a mighty fortress
built along the sea.
But you will be disgraced
like a married woman
who never had children.
5When Egypt hears about Tyre,
it will tremble.
6All of you along the coast
had better cry and sail
far across the ocean.
7Can this be the happy city
that has stood for centuries?
Its people have spread
to distant lands;
8its merchants were kings
honored all over the world.
Who planned to destroy Tyre?
9The Lord All-Powerful planned it
to bring shame and disgrace
to those who are honored
by everyone on earth.
10People of Tyre,
your harbor is destroyed!
You will have to become farmers
just like the Egyptians.
Tyre Will Be Forgotten
11The Lord's hand has reached
across the sea,
upsetting the nations.
He has given a command
to destroy fortresses
in the land of Canaan.
12The Lord has said
to the people of Sidon,
“Your celebrating is over—
you are crushed.
Even if you escape to Cyprus,
you won't find peace.”
13Look what the Assyrians have done to Babylonia! They have attacked, destroying every palace in the land. Now wild animals live among the ruins. 14Not a fortress will be left standing, so tell all the seagoing ships to mourn.
15The city of Tyre will be forgotten for 70 years, which is the lifetime of a king. Then Tyre will be like that evil woman in the song:
16You're gone and forgotten,
you evil woman!
So strut through the town,
singing and playing
your favorite tune
to be remembered again.
17At the end of those 70 years, the Lord will let Tyre get back into business. The city will be like a woman who sells her body to everyone of every nation on earth, 18but none of what is earned will be kept in the city.
