That money will belong to the Lord, and it will be used to buy more than enough food and good clothes for those who worship the Lord.
translation_text:
Tura teo taane
1Kwora kanto wora Tura teo kom ŋwaane mo:
Ta‑á keeri-na, nabworo yuŋina balo na nwoŋi Tarasisi
ye á beeri pipiu ŋwaane to!
Kokuri to, Tura teo kom chɔge mo.
Ko sam dem maama chɔge.
Jei daa tera se nabwooru tem zo te zege da.
Ko ye Kitim ne mo ba nigi kwora kam konto.
2Ta‑á ye chemm, abam balo na zoore naneo kom ni ne to.
Abam Sidon teo pipim-piina bam mo toŋe nɔɔna
se ba tɔge naneo kom baŋa ba ke pipiu pa se á duni.
3Ba ma beeri na-fwaaro tem baŋa ne
ba ke pipiu de teene delo na ye yiga yiga to.
Ba ma vo ba yi Sihora de Naili bwi sem
ba yeigi wodiiru telo na ke dáane to
ba ja ba jwoori sɔŋɔ.
4Sidon teo tiina bam, á laam wó na á chaveera!
Kokuri to, nmo Sidon teo nɛ dam naneo kom ŋwaane,
ye naneo kom laam nam ve‑m ye ko we,
“Ko nye de amo ta wo virigi puga se a lo bia.
Amo nam wo kɔne bia se ba ke nɔɔna,
ko ná ye bakeiri naa busankane de.”
5Ejipti tiina ná nigi kolo na yi Tura teo tiina to,
ba yera wó sɔɔre dedɛ.
6Kwaane-na se á bɛ á yi Tarasisi se á nii.
Keeri-na á wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane,
abam balo na zoore naneo kom ni ne to.
7Bɛ mo ke teo konto ba na chwi faŋa faŋa to?
Ko déem pɛ á na ywoni lanyerane,
ye ko nɔɔna jage ba vo yiga yiga
ba zoore teene dedwonna ne.
8Wɔ mo jeini o boŋe lwarem kikia yanto
se o ma o chɔge Tura teo kom?
Ko ya ye teo kolo na pɛ nɔɔna di paare mo.
Balo déem na pipi ko wone to ye dedɛɛra mo,
ye logo baŋa nɔɔna maama nege-ba.
9Ko nam ye Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo boŋe se o chɔge-ba.
O ma ke konto se o zoore-ba tega ne de ba nenɔŋa kam,
se ko pa nɔn-yum dwi maama tu ba tete tega ne.
10Abam Tarasisi tiina bam,
laam ta‑á vare-na á tega kam
ne ba na ke tei Naili buga kam ni ne to.
Kokuri to, abam daa ba jege jei selo
á na wó ke pipiu da to.
11 Baŋa Wɛ tete mo twe o jeŋa naneo kom baŋa ne,
pa se logo baŋa teene dem ziziŋi.
O pɛ ni se ko vo Kanaan laŋa kam seeni,
ye o we ba chɔge banto dam jei sem maama.
12O ma ta de Sidon tiina bam o we,
“Abam ywoni dim dem ti mo,
ba na chɔge abam lam to ŋwaane.
Abam ná maŋe á bɛ á vo Kitim,
á ta bá na siu da.”
13Fɔge-na á nii Babilon teo kom. Ko nɔɔna bam daa ba jege yuu! Asiria tiina bam pɛ se ko ji kago-vara zoorem jei mo. Ba ya lɔge taara mo ba yeiri teo kom kabira yera ne, ye ba daare ba tɔge da ba zo ba vaare ko sɔ-fwaaro tem ba de tega ne. Ba ma pa ko ji di-dwonnu yerane ko tiga.
14Ta‑á keeri-na, abam nabwoor-yuŋina balo na nwoŋi Tarasisi
ye á beeri pipiu ŋwaane to,
á dam jei sem maama na chɔge to ŋwaane.
15Maŋa kam konto ná yia, ba wó kwei bena fuserepɛ ba ma swei Tura teo kom swia. Bena yam konto wone mo pɛ wom maŋe se o di paare. Maŋa kam konto nam ná ti, ko lage ko ke Tura teo kom ne ka-tola kalo ba na tɛ o taane leiŋa wone ba we:
16“Ka-tola kalo ba na swei n swia to,
nam kwei kɔnɔ se n ta‑n kare teo kom wone n via.
Kwaane se n ta kɔnɔ kom lanyerane,
se n ta‑n leeni lein-ywei.
Konto mo wó pa se nɔɔna daa guli n gula.”
17Bena fuserepɛ yam ná ti, Baŋa Wɛ yiga daa wó jwoori ka taa wo Tura teo kom ne. Ko nɔn-bia bam daa wó na nyɔɔre ba totoŋa baŋa ne. Ba ta wó kwei ba tete ba yeigi ba pa logo baŋa teene dem maama, ne ka-tola na ke tei de baara to. 18De ko de, nyɔɔre delo ba na wó na ba pipiu kom baŋa ne to, ba wó kwei ba pa Baŋa Wɛ mo. Ba bá kwei ba jejegero tem ba seigi, naa ba tiŋi-te jwa ŋwaane. Te nam wó woli se balo na zuli Baŋa Wɛ to na wodiiru dedɛ, de gare-laaro.

english_text:
The Earth Will Be Punished
1The Lord is going to twist the earth out of shape and turn it into a desert. Everyone will be scattered, 2including ordinary people and priests, slaves and slave owners, buyers and sellers, lenders and borrowers, the rich and the poor. 3The earth will be stripped bare and left that way. This is what the Lord has promised.
4The earth wilts away;
its mighty leaders melt
to nothing.
5The earth is polluted
because its people
disobeyed the laws of God,
breaking their agreement
that was to last forever.
6The earth is under a curse;
its people are dying out
because of their sins.
7Grapevines have dried up:
wine is almost gone—
mournful sounds are heard
instead of joyful shouts.
8No one plays tambourines
or stringed instruments;
all noisy celebrating
has come to an end.
9They no longer sing
as they drink their wine,
and it tastes sour.
10Towns are crushed and in chaos;
houses are locked tight.
11Happy times have disappeared
from the earth,
and people shout in the streets,
“We're out of wine!”
12Cities are destroyed;
their gates are torn down.
13Nations will be stripped bare,
like olive trees or vineyards
after the harvest season.
Praise the God of Justice
14People in the west shout;
they joyfully praise
the majesty of the Lord.
15And so, everyone in the east
and those on the islands
should praise the Lord,
the God of Israel.
16From all over the world
songs of praise are heard
for the God of justice.
But I feel awful,
terribly miserable.
Can anyone be trusted?
So many are treacherous!
There's No Escape
17Terror, traps, and pits
are waiting for everyone.
18If you are terrified and run,
you will fall into a pit;
if you crawl out of the pit,
you will get caught in a trap.
The sky has split apart
like a window thrown open.
The foundations of the earth
have been shaken;
19the earth is shattered,
ripped to pieces.
20It staggers and shakes
like a drunkard
or a hut in a windstorm.
It is burdened down with sin;
the earth will fall,
never again to get up.
21On that day the Lord
will punish the powers
in the heavens
and the kings of the earth.
22He will put them in a pit
and keep them prisoner.
Then later on,
he will punish them.
23Both the moon and sun will
be embarrassed and ashamed.
The Lord All-Powerful will rule
on Mount Zion in Jerusalem,
where he will show its rulers
his wonderful glory.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ wó waare logo baŋa
1Nii-na! Baŋa Wɛ mo lage
o chɔge tega baŋa maama
pa se ka ji di-dwonnu yerane.
O maa wó ja ka ni maama o jujugi,
ye o daare o jage ka nɔn-bia bam
o yage jei maama ne.
2Cham dedwe mo lage de yi ba maama.
Kaanem tu bá taa gare nɔn-kɔgɔ kom.
Sɔŋɔ tu nam bá taa gare o kabaa.
Kaane de o ka-nyaane bá taa gare daane.
Wolo na jege wonnu o yeigi to bá taa gare o na yeigi-te se o pa wolo to.
Je-diru bá taa gare o na jene wonnu wolo tei ne to.
Nadum de bá taa gare nabwom.
3Ba lage ba kɔgese tega kam maama mo
ba daare-ka ba tiŋi yɔɔ yerane.
Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.
4Tega kam koge mo ye gaaro tem maama kwaare.
Logo kom baŋa maama bwona mo.
Balo ya na ye dedɛɛra tega kam maama ne to dam ti.
5Ko ye balo na zoore tega kam baŋa ne to mo chɔge-ka.
Kokuri to, ba yɔɔre ba chɔge Wɛ nia yam mo,
ye ba ve o bera yam.
Ba ma daare ba chɔge ni-gwonim delo Wɛ na ke de-ba
ye de wora taa wuu to.
6Konto ŋwaane mo Wɛ sɔɔle lwarem o yage tega kam ne.
Balo na zoore ka baŋa ne to wó yaare ba wɛleera ŋwaane.
Wɛ ma yɔɔre o waare-ba,
pa se nabiina fee yerane laam daare logo baŋa ne.
7Vini teeni dem maama kwaare
pa sa-doora ji gweeru jana.
Balo ya na di ywoni sana nyɔɔm baŋa ne to laam kare ba ŋwane mo.
8Senyɛ sem daa ba wɔe.
Kwɛn-kwɛɛra wopwolo sɔɔ de nam daa ba ni.
Ko nam ná ye kwanno, ba yage tento tam.
9Nɔɔna daa ba nyɔ ba sana ye ba leena.
Sana de daa maŋe ba ba ywona ba nia ne.
10Teo kolo na chɔge to laam tigi yɔɔ yerane mo.
Ko sam dem maama ma fɔge de pe
se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé zo de wone.
11Nɔɔna kare teo kom chwei sem yuu ne mo
ba laare ba beeri sana se ba nyɔ.
Ba ywoni dem maama leiri de ji wo-chechɔgɔ.
Wopwolo yɔɔre ko jei mo tega kam baŋa ne.
12Teo kom laam daare di-dwonnu yerane mo.
Ko manchwo-peo kom ma chochoge muga-muga.
13Ko lage ko ke konto dwoŋi mo
logo baŋa teene dem maama ne.
Ko wó taa nye de teeni bia gworim maŋa na yeini ka yi,
pa se ba pore tio kolo ba ja tega tei to mo.
Ba laam maa wó lare tio-bia fenfee balo na daare da to.
14Balo na wo wɛ-zoore seeni to wó leeni de wopwolo.
Ba wó bage de kwor-dɛa ba tei Baŋa Wɛ.
15Konto ŋwaane abam balo na zoore wɛ-puli seeni to
zuli-na Baŋa Wɛ.
Abam balo maama na zoore naneo kom ni ne to
de zeiŋi-na Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to yere.
16Dɔŋɔ ni maama ne mo dé nigi ba na leena
ba we, “Chega Tu wom maŋe de zula.”
Amo nam ma ta a we, “A wo yɔɔre ko chɔɔre mo!
Lɛɛro yi-ne ywoo!
Nɔɔna nwoŋi ba dwonna kwaga ne mo.
Ba bebare-kikia yam de maa fɔge ya vei yiga.”
17Lɛɛro, de gwonnu, de kalanchorro mo tigi
se te ja abam balo na zoore tega baŋa ne to.
18Wolo ná kwaane o lu vuvuga kam wone,
kotu wó vo o to gwoŋo wone mo.
Wolo maa ná wane o bɛ gwoŋo kom wone,
kalanchogo mo wó ja kotu.
Kokuri to, chɔgem dedɛ wó nwoŋi wɛyuu ne.
Tega kam kugu jei de maa wó ziziŋi.
19Loloa wó bage tega kam yera ne
pa se ka yare belei.
Ka ta wó tiini ka ziziŋi de dam.
20Tega kam nam kare ka yuŋi jei maama ne mo,
ne sa-nyɔro na beiri tei to.
Ka maa zuuli jei maama ne ne vio na jege vwei
ko mage ye ko ye tei to.
Nɔɔna bam wɛleera yɔɔre ya chɔge tega kam mo,
pa se ka to buru-tu-tu,
ye ka daa bá zaŋe wɛɛne.
21Maŋa kam konto ná yia,
Baŋa Wɛ lage o waare dedɛɛra balo na wo wɛyuu ne ba toŋe to mo.
Ko nam ná ye tega baŋa ne,
o lage o waare pwa balo na jege dam ba di da to mo.
22O ta wó ja ba maama o kale o ke daane mo
ye o daare o pe-ba peena diga ne.
Ba ná maŋe da ba dáane fee,
o laam wó yɔɔre o waare-ba.
23Wɛ wó kwoli chana kam pwooni.
Wea kam de wó pipiri ka ji lim.
Kokuri to, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo wó jeini Zion peo kom yuu ne
o di paare Jerusalem teo kom wone.
Teo kom nakwa bam maa wó na o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom.

english_text:
A Prayer of Thanks to God
1You, Lord, are my God!
I will praise you
for doing the wonderful things
you had planned and promised
since ancient times.
2You have destroyed the fortress
of our enemies,
leaving their city in ruins.
Nothing in that foreign city
will ever be rebuilt.
3Now strong and cruel nations
will fear and honor you.
4You have been a place of safety
for the poor and needy
in times of trouble.
Brutal enemies pounded us
like a heavy rain
or the heat of the sun at noon,
but you were our shelter.
5Those wild foreigners struck
like scorching desert heat.
But you were like a cloud,
protecting us from the sun.
You kept our enemies from singing
songs of victory.
The Lord Has Saved Us
6On this mountain
the Lord All-Powerful
will prepare for all nations
a feast of the finest foods.
Choice wines and the best meats
will be served.
7Here the Lord will strip away
the burial clothes
that cover the nations.
8 The Lord All-Powerful
will destroy the power of death
and wipe away all tears.
No longer will his people
be insulted everywhere.
The Lord has spoken!
9At that time, people will say,
“The Lord has saved us!
Let's celebrate.
We waited and hoped—
now our God is here.”
10 The powerful arm of the Lord
will protect this mountain.
The Moabites will be put down
and trampled on like straw
in a pit of manure.
11They will struggle to get out,
but God will humiliate them
no matter how hard they try.
12The walls of their fortresses
will be knocked down
and scattered in the dirt.
translation_text:
Wɛ lei keim
1Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo ye amo Wɛ.
A zeiŋi n yere dem wɛɛne mo,
ye a daare a tei nmo.
Kokuri to, n yɔɔre n tɔge chega baŋa ne mo
n boŋe n ja faŋa faŋa se n ke wo-kenkagela
ye n seene n jege-ya n ke.
2Nmo pɛ se te-fɔrɔ kom laam ji kandwa-pwoa mo.
Teo kolo ya na lɔge ko pe de dam to laam ma ji di-dwonnu.
Sa-fwaaro telo sa-teena na lɔge to daa tera,
ye ba daa bá wane-te ba fɔge ba lɔ ba zege.
3Konto nam mo tei pa dwia yalo nɔɔna na dana to jege se ba zuli‑m.
Teene delo nɔɔna na ye nankɔ-nyena to maa wó taa kɔre‑m.
4Yiniga tiina yeini ba seigi n woro kuri ne mo.
N ma‑n ye dalem jei n pa nabwona ba cham maŋa ne.
Nmo ye woro mo chekke vo-dɛɔ maŋa ne.
N ta ma‑n ye pwoŋa n kwoli nɔɔna se wea yé yi-ba.
Chega to, nankɔ-nyena yɔɔre ba pare debam mo vera-vera
ne vo-fɔrɔ na tiini ko mage kabira ye ko ye tei to.
5Ba keim dem ta nye ne kagoa yuu wulim na ye tei to mo.
Nmo ma‑n che dé dona bam tiguri-kaasa pa ka ba ni,
ko nye de kunkwoŋo na kwoli wea dam pa zurim wora tei to mo.
Nankɔ-nyena bam daa maa ware ba lei sem se ba leeni.
6Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam lage o ke kuri-fɔrɔ mo
peo konto yuu ne,
o pa logo baŋa dwi tiina bam maama.
Sana de wodiiru wó bugi kuri dem wone,
se ba di wodi-laaro dwi dwi, ye ba nyɔ sa-ŋona.
7O nam lage o zege peo konto yuu ne mo
se o dɔne ni-pugu kolo na kwoli dwi-gɛ tiina bam maama to.
O ta wó lɔɔre gɔrɔ kolo na kaare ko pu teene dem to
o yage dáane.
8O maa wó yɔɔre o chɔge toone dam
se ko taa vei wuu.
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ ta wó weeri nɔɔna bam maama yi-na
se ba daa yé taa jege yi-nɔna.
O maa wó pa se chaveera yalo o nɔɔna bam na nɛ
logo baŋa jei maama ne to jei.
Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.
9Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia, ba laam wó taa tɛ ba we:
“Chega ŋwaane, debam Wɛ mo tento.
Dé ma kwei dé chega maama dé pa‑o,
ye o jwoŋi debam o yage.
Baŋa Wɛ wom mo tento.
Dé kwei dé chega dé seene dé pa‑o mo.
Nam pa-na se dé taa jege wopwolo
ye dé di ywoni o verem dem ŋwaane.”
10 Baŋa Wɛ yi page peo konto baŋa ne mo
se o taa yere ko nɔɔna bam.
Ko daare ko ná ye Moaba tiina bam,
o lage o nɔne-ba mo o se tega ne,
ne ba na nɔne ga-korro ba se bulu wone tei to.
11Moaba tiina wó taa yaare de ba je mo ba korege se ba bɛ,
ne nɔɔno na ligi na ye o korege se o bɛ buga tei to.
Wɛ nam wó pa se ba fia kam ji kafɛ,
de ba ná maŋe ba ke swa de ba jea tei maama de.
12O ta wó pa se ba dam jei kabiri sem to tega ne buri-buri!
Se maama wó ja tega mo,
ye ba daare ba nɔne-se ywale-ywale
se se ji fwogo yerane.

english_text:
A Song of Victory
1The time is coming when the people of Judah will sing this song:
“Our city is protected.
The Lord is our fortress,
and he gives us victory.
2Open the city gates
for a law-abiding nation
that is faithful to God.
3The Lord gives perfect peace
to those whose faith is firm.
4So always trust the Lord
because he is forever
our mighty rock.
5God has put down our enemies
in their mountain city
and rubbed it in the dirt.
6Now the poor and abused
trample all over that city.”
The Lord Can Be Trusted
7Our Lord, you always do right,
and you make the path smooth
for those who obey you.
8You are the one we trust
to bring about justice;
above all else we want
your name to be honored.
9Throughout the night,
my heart searches for you,
because your decisions
show everyone on this earth
how to live right.
10Even when the wicked
are treated with mercy
in this land of justice,
they do wrong and are blind
to your glory, our Lord.
11 Your hand is raised and ready
to punish them,
but they don't see it.
Put them to shame!
Show how much you care for us
and throw them into the fire
intended for your enemies.
12You will give us peace, Lord,
because everything we have done
was by your power.
13Others have ruled over us
besides you, our Lord God,
but we obey only you.
14Those enemies are now dead
and can never live again.
You have punished them—
they are destroyed,
completely forgotten.
15Our nation has grown
because of you, our Lord.
We have more land than before,
and you are honored.
The Lord Gives Life to the Dead
16When you punished our people,
they turned and prayed
to you, our Lord.
17Because of what you did to us,
we suffered like a woman
about to give birth.
18But instead of having a child,
our terrible pain
produced only wind.
We have won no victories,
and we have no descendants
to take over the earth.
19Your people will rise to life!
Tell them to leave their graves
and celebrate with shouts.
You refresh the earth
like morning dew;
you give life to the dead.
20Go inside and lock the doors,
my people.
Hide there for a little while,
until the Lord
is no longer angry.
The Earth and the Sea Will Be Punished
21The Lord will come out
to punish everyone on earth
for their sins.
And when he does,
those who did violent crimes
will be known and punished.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ seinim leiŋa
1Maŋa kam konto ne, ba wó taa leeni leiŋa kanto mo Judah teo kom wone:
Debam teo kom tiini ko dana mo.
Baŋa Wɛ mo vere teo kom cham wone o yage,
ne ko ye kabiri de taara mo chege-ko to.
2Pore-na teo kom nia yam,
se dwi delo nɔɔna na ye nɔn-ŋona to zo ko wone.
Ba ye balo na yɔɔre ba jege chega to mo.
3 Baŋa Wɛ, wolo ná ke o wo-dedoa de nmo,
ye o boboŋa zege cheppe,
nmo wó pa se kotu taa jege bochare-zuru chekke.
4Kwei-na á wo-dedoa á pa Baŋa Wɛ,
se ko taa vei wuu.
Kokuri, Baŋa Wɛ mo ye peo kolo debam na wó dale to.
5Ko ná ye balo na zoore baŋa baŋa jei sem ne to,
o lage o zoore-ba tega ne mo.
O ma pa ba te-fɔrɔ kom to tega ne buri-buri,
ye o daare o nɔne-ko ywale-ywale
pa ko ji fwogo.
6Nɔɔna mo jege-ko ba nɔna ba se tega ne.
Banto maa ye yiniga tiina,
de balo na nɛ yaara to.
7 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo yeini n pa nɔn-ŋona chwoŋa tigi mo jase.
N ma‑n yere-ba de ba veiŋa
se ba yé tiri ba to tega ne.
8 Baŋa Wɛ, debam tɔge nmo bera yam mo
ye dé teena maama wo nmo wone.
Woŋo kolo na jege dé fera to
ye se nmo yere dem taa jege zula mo.
9Amo fera yɔɔre ya wo nmo wone mo tete dem maama ne.
Tega de nam ná jege ka poore de,
a ta wó taa boŋe nmo boboŋa mo.
Nmo bera yam ná jwoŋi logo baŋa ni maama,
nabiina wó lɔre chwei selo na tɔge chega to.
10Nmo yɔɔre n ke zaane mo n ke puseŋ-nyena yuu ne.
De ko de, ba ba zamese chega tɔgem.
Ba ná maŋe ba zoore nɔn-laaro teo wone de,
ba ta swoi se ba taa ke lwarem mo,
ye ba ba nege Baŋa Wɛ paare dem.
11 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo twe n jeŋa se n waare-ba mo.
De ko de, ba ta ba nae ko na ye tei to.
Nam pa se ba lɔre we n yi page n nɔɔna bam baŋa ne,
se chaveera ja-ba.
Ta pa se n ban-lom dem to ba baŋa ne,
ne ko na maŋe se n dona na waarem delo to.
12 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo wó pa se dé jeini de yazura.
Kokuri, totoŋa yalo maama dé na ke to
ye nmo mo ke n pa debam.
13Dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ, dedɛɛra badwonna de ya seene ba ba ba tei debam.
Dé nam yɔɔre dé teege nmo yere dem yerane baŋa ne mo.
14Dedɛɛra bam konto tega,
ye ba daa bá jwoori ba bi.
Ba chira daa bá zaŋe wɛɛne.
Kokuri to, nmo mo waare-ba, pa se ba yɔɔre ba na chɔgem.
N ma‑n pa se ba yere saare nabiina yiga ne.
15 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo pɛ se debam teo kom yale mo ko ke yiga ne.
N yale dé tega kam mo jei maama wone,
pa se n yere dem na zula dedɛ.
16 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo nɔɔna bam lwoori wolim mo n tei ne,
ko na zo ba yera to ŋwaane.
Nmo na korese-ba de cham to,
mo ba pipiri ba ba n tei de wɛ-lworo.
17 Baŋa Wɛ, ko ke ne kaane na virigi puga se o lo
ye o yɔɔre o wowole de cham tei to mo.
Mo debam na yaare tei n yiga ne.
18Chega to, dé jaane puga
ye dé ye bele-bele mo se dé lo.
Ko nam nye de vio yerane mo dé jwoori dé lo.
Debam wo wane dé vere dé teo kom dé yage.
Dé wo daare kwaga se ba jwa jwoŋi tega kam ba taa tei.
19Abam twa bam nam wó jwoori ba bi.
Ba yera yam daa wó zaŋe ya na ŋwea.
Balo na tigi tega kuri ne to wó jwoori ba zaŋe
ba taa chaka de wopwolo.
Ne nyɔnɔ na yeini ko pa tega na zurim zezeŋa ne tei to,
chira daa ta wó zaŋe tega kam ne,
ba jwoori ba na ŋwea.
20Amo nɔɔna bam, zo-na á di sem wone.
Pe-na se ni á maŋe da á seigi maŋa fenfee wone,
se ko taa nii Wɛ ban-lom dem ná zuri.
21Nii-na! Baŋa Wɛ nwoŋi o jeiga kam ne mo o beena.
O nam lage o waare logo baŋa nɔɔna bam mo
ba wɛleera ŋwaane.
Tega kam laam wó pa se nɔn-gora na lwogi jana balo ka baŋa ne to lɔre jaja.
Ka daa bá seigi balo ba na go to ka kuri ne.

english_text:
1 On that day, Leviathan,
the sea monster,
will squirm and try to escape,
but the Lord will kill him
with a cruel, sharp sword.
Protection and Forgiveness
The Lord said:
2At that time you must sing
about a fruitful vineyard.
3I, the Lord, will protect it
and always keep it watered.
I will guard it day and night
to keep it from harm.
4I am no longer angry.
But if it produces thorns,
I will go to war against it
and burn it to the ground.
5Yet if the vineyard depends
on me for protection,
it will become my friend
and be at peace with me.
6Someday Israel will take root
like a vine.
It will blossom and bear fruit
that covers the earth.
7I, the Lord, didn't punish and kill
the people of Israel
as fiercely as I punished
and killed their enemies.
8I carefully measured out
Israel's punishment
and sent the scorching heat
to chase them far away.
9There's only one way
that Israel's sin and guilt
can be completely forgiven:
They must crush the stones
of every pagan altar
and place of worship.
The Lord Will Bring His People Together
10Fortress cities are left
like a desert
where no one lives.
Cattle walk through the ruins,
stripping the trees bare.
11When broken branches
fall to the ground,
women pick them up
to feed the fire.
But these people are so stupid
that the God who created them
will show them no mercy.
12The time is coming when the Lord will shake the land between the Euphrates River and the border of Egypt, and one by one he will bring all of his people together. 13A loud trumpet will be heard. Then the people of Israel who were dragged away to Assyria and Egypt will return to worship the Lord on his holy mountain in Jerusalem.
translation_text:
Wɛ wó jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage
1Maŋa kam konto ná yia, Baŋa Wɛ lage o kwei o se-zɔɔ kom, ko nia na di fileim-fileim de foone to mo. O maa wó waare basankwe-kenkagele dem yere na ye Leviatan ye ka tiini ka duri ye ka pipiri to. O laam maa wó go naneo wo juru kom konto.
2Dɛ dem konto ná yia,
dé wó leeni dé ta Vini teeni kara kalo na lana to taane we:
3Amo Baŋa Wɛ tete mo nii ka baŋa ne.
A maa pae na yi-ka maŋa de maŋa.
A yɔɔre a yere-ka mo wea de tete maama
se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé wane-ka o ja o chɔge.
4A bane wo zaŋe ka ŋwaane.
Nɔɔno nam ya ná pɛ se ga-cheiŋo de sabare li-ka,
amo ya wó nwoŋi se a jeeri kotu de jara,
ye a zwɛ te maama nyɔ!
5Nɔɔno nam daa ná lage se o ba o to amo pwoa ne,
o jege se o ke ni-mɔrɔ de amo.
Chega to, o jege se o ba se dé ke ni-mɔrɔ mo daane.
6Maŋa nam beene se Jakob dwi dem kugu ja tega.
Isarele tiina bam maa wó kwi vɔɔro ye ba lei leira.
Tio-bia balo banto na wó lei to
mo wó jage ba yi logo baŋa jei maama.
7 Baŋa Wɛ pɛ ko zo Isarele tiina bam yera
ne o na ke tei de balo ya na jege-ba ba bɛɛse to mo na?
O nam wo go Isarele tiina bam
se ko yi o na ke tei de balo ya na jege-ba ba goe to.
8O nam na waare Isarele tiina bam tei to,
o zeili-ba pa ba vo sa-teo mo yiga yiga.
Ko yɔɔre ko nye ne wɛ-puli seeni vo-dɛɔ mo
o kwei o maa kale-ba o yage da.
9Ko na wó ke tei ye Wɛ kwei Jakob dwi tiina bam wɛleera
o ma chɛ-ba se ba tusim dem maama saare to mo tento:
Ba jege se ba lɔ ba kandwa yam
ba na mɛ ba ji kaanem bimbina to mo,
ba daare ba cho-ya muga-muga.
Ba nam ta dae se ba yage Asera nyenyego dɛ sem
se se taa zege se zega jei ne.
10Teo kolo ya na lɔge ko pe de dam to
laam jigi di-dwonnu mo.
Ko nɔn-bia bam ma nwoŋi ba daare-ko ba zege
ne kagoa mo to.
Naane laam kare de di gaao jei sem konto ne
ye de daare de tigi da de sia.
De ma yɔɔre de di ko teeni vɔɔro tem maama nyelamm.
11Teeni dem nɛ jigi da-dwa mo
ye se bwori se to tega ne.
Kaana maa vei da ba twɛ-se se ba ma dwei mini.
Ko na ye tei to, nɔɔna bam konto swa muri.
Mo kokuri ba Keiru wom bá duri ba yibwona.
O ta bá ke zaane o yage ba yuu ne,
de o na maŋe o naane-ba to de.
12Maŋa kam ná yia, Baŋa Wɛ wó zege Yuferata buga kam ni ne mo o waare o nɔɔna bam ne o na fere mena tei to, se o vo o yi Ejipti bu-nɔgɔ kom seeni. O laam maa wó la abam Isarele tiina bam dedoa dedoa o ke daane. 13Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia, ba wó wu nabɔnɔ wɛ-wɛ, se ba bwoŋi Isarele tiina balo maama ba ya na kale ba vo ba yage Asiria de Ejipti teene dem wone ye ba dáane da to. Banto maa wó ba ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ peo kolo o na pɔɔre o pa o tete Jerusalem teo kom wone to.

english_text:
Samaria Will Be Punished
1The city of Samaria
above a fertile valley
is in for trouble!
Its leaders are drunkards,
who stuff themselves
with food and wine.
But they will be like flowers
that dry up and wilt.
2Only the Lord is strong
and powerful!
His mighty hand
will strike them down
with the force of a hailstorm
or a mighty whirlwind
or an overwhelming flood.
3Every drunkard in Ephraim
takes pride in Samaria,
but it will be crushed.
4Samaria above a fertile valley
will quickly lose its glory.
It will be gobbled up
like the first ripe fig
at harvest season.
5When this time comes,
the Lord All-Powerful
will be a glorious crown
for his people who survive.
6He will see that justice rules
and that his people are able
to defend their cities.
Corrupt Leaders Will Be Punished
7Priests and prophets stumble
because they are drunk.
Their minds are too confused
to receive God's messages
or give honest decisions.
8Their tables are covered,
completely covered,
with their stinking vomit.
9You drunken leaders
are like babies!
How can you possibly understand
or teach the Lord's message?
10You don't even listen—
all you hear is senseless sound
after senseless sound.
11 So, the Lord will speak
to his people
in strange sounds
and foreign languages.
12He promised you
perfect peace and rest,
but you refused to listen.
13Now his message to you
will be senseless sound
after senseless sound.
Then you will fall backwards,
injured and trapped.
False Security Is Fatal
14You rulers of Jerusalem
do nothing but sneer;
now you must listen
to what the Lord says.
15 Do you think you have
an agreement with death
and the world of the dead?
Why do you trust in your lies
to keep you safe from danger
and the mighty flood?
16 And so the Lord says,
“I'm laying a firm foundation
for the city of Zion.
It's a valuable cornerstone
proven to be trustworthy;
no one who trusts it
will ever be disappointed.
17Justice and fairness
will be the measuring lines
that help me build.”
Hailstones and floods
will destroy and wash away
your shelter of lies.
18Your agreement with death
and the world of the dead
will be broken.
Then angry, roaring waves
will sweep over you.
19Morning, noon, and night
an overwhelming flood
will wash you away.
The terrible things that happen
will teach you this lesson:
20Your bed is too short,
your blanket too skimpy.
21 The Lord will fiercely attack
as he did at Mount Perazim
and in Gibeon Valley.
But this time the Lord
will do something surprising,
not what you expect.
22So you had better stop sneering
or you will be in worse shape
than ever before.
I heard the Lord All-Powerful
threaten the whole country
with destruction.
All Wisdom Comes from the Lord
23Pay close attention
to what I am saying.
24Farmers don't just plow
and break up the ground.
25When a field is ready,
they scatter the seeds
of dill and cumin;
they plant the seeds
of wheat and barley
in the proper places
and sow other grains
around the edges.
26They learn this from their God.
27After dill and cumin
have been harvested,
the stalks are pounded,
not run over with a wagon.
28Wheat and barley are pounded,
but not beaten to pulp;
they are run over with a wagon,
but not ground to dust.
29This wonderful knowledge comes
from the Lord All-Powerful,
who has such great wisdom.
translation_text:
Lɛɛro wó yi Efrayim dwi tiina bam
1Lɛɛro wó yi Efrayim dwi tiina teo kamunu kom,
de ko sa-nyɔra bam na jege fia ko ŋwaane tei to.
Ko maa nye ne punnu telo nenɔŋa na lage ka ti to mo.
Ko lam dem wó jei lela.
Teo kom zege te-ywoŋa bwolo baŋa seeni mo.
Ko nɔɔna bam maa nyɔ sana ba buga,
ye ba jege teera ba teo kom ŋwaane.
2Nii-na dé Teiru Wɛ wom nam lage o toŋe dedɛɛro
na tiini o jege dam to mo se o ba ba baŋa.
Kotu wó mage-ba o de tega ne,
ne do-kandwa naa vo-fɔrɔ na tui ko chɔge wonnu tei to.
Ko ta wó ke ne na-fɔrɔ na chuuri
ye ko chwooli wonnu ko viira tei to mo.
3Efrayim teo sa-nyɔra bam na jege teera de kolo to mo,
ba lage ba nɔne-ko ba se tega ne.
4Ba teo kom seene ko zege te-ywoŋa bwolo baŋa ne.
De ko de, ko lam dem, de ko nenɔŋa kam maama laam wó jei mo.
Ko wó taa nye ne mɔɔro na bege te ti
ye te maŋe se ba su-te ba de tega ne to mo.
Nɔɔno ná nɛ-te ye o gwori de o jeŋa,
o wó yɔɔre o kwei-te o mage o ni ne mo.
5Maŋa kam konto ná yia, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tete
mo wó pa o nɔɔna balo ta na daare to
taa jege nenɔŋa de lam lanyerane.
Ko wó taa nye de wonto mo ye ba paare yipuga.
6O maa wó kwei chega boboŋa o pa balo na di nɔɔna taane to,
se ba ma-ya ba bore chega bora ba pa nɔɔna.
Ko ta ná ye balo na zege teo kom manchwo-nia yam ne
ba cho se ba dona yé zo to,
Wɛ wó pa banto de taa jege baare.
7Balo na kare ba zuuli jei maama sana nyɔɔm ŋwaane to mo tento:
Wɛ kaanem tiina de sampwori sem tete mo ke konto.
Ba ma yeiri ba tete jei ye ba beiri,
ba na bugi de sana to ŋwaane.
Konto ŋwaane ba ware ba lɔre wonnu telo
Wɛ na le o bere-ba to lanyerane.
Ba nam ná wora ba di nɔɔna taane,
ba ba zege boboŋe dedwe baŋa ne.
8Ba yɔɔre ba tɔne mo ba chɔge ba jeiŋa jei sem maama.
Jeiga dedoa tete wo daare ye ba wo digiri-ka.
9Ba ta tɛ mo ba we, “O kwaane se o bere nɔɔno wɔ mo?
Wɔ mo o wora o maŋe wonnu se kotu ni te kuri?
O pa dé ye bu-sese selo ba na kwori yele leile to mo na?
10O yɔɔre o pae dé jwoori dé tɛ botare-bia bam mo dé tulisa.
Dé maa tɛ botare sem gena de gena,
ye dé ta tɛ-se bedwe bedwe se dé lɔre.”
11Ko nam na ye tei to, Wɛ lage o tɔge dwi-gɛ tiina baŋa ne
se o ma ta-veiri mo o ŋɔɔne de o nɔɔna bam.
12O ya tage de-ba mo o we,
“Abam wó sii jeiga kam konto ne mo.
Balo na bugi to wó ba ba jeini ba sii”.
O ta ma ta o we, “Abam siu jei mo tento.”
De ko de, ba wo sɛ o ni dem konto.
13Konto ŋwaane nam mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa wó yi-ba,
se ba jwoori ba taa tɛ botare-bia bam ba tulisa.
Ba wó taa tɛ botare sem gena de gena,
ye ba ta tɛ-se bedwe bedwe se ba lɔre.
Konto to, ba ná boŋe se ba vo yiga,
ba laam wó to ba kwaga ne jambayala.
Konto baŋa ne mo ba wó na zonne,
ye kalanchorro de ja-ba, pa se ba to ba dona jeŋa ne.
Jerusalem teo taane
14Abam nɔn-lwɛɛna balo na nii Jerusalem tiina baŋa ne to,
cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ na jege kwora kalo se o ta de abam to.
15Abam yɔɔre á teere mo we,
“Debam gwoni ni mo de toone,
ye dé daare dé ke ni-sɛɛm de churu.
Konto ŋwaane, lɛɛro ná yɔɔre te yi dé teo kom,
ne na-fɔrɔ na chuuri ko chwooli wonnu tei to de,
te bá wane debam te ke kolokolo.
Kokuri to, debam seigi vwa woro kuri ne mo,
ye ka-gane-nɔɔna ji dé dalem jei.”
16Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Nii-na, amo lage a chwi kabiri-beira mo Zion ne.
Ka maa ye kandwɛ delo na ye chekke ye de kwaare tega ne to.
De tiini de jege kuri, pa se diga kam dana.
Wolo maama nam ná sale de yera ne,
kotu ba lwia de kolokolo.
17Amo na wó chwi diga kam kuri tei to,
amo wó kwei chega de nɔn-ŋonne mo a ma maŋe-ka
ne te ye lɔra ŋone mo tei.
Do-kandwa mo wó ba ya chwooli á vwa yam ya ja ya jei,
ye na-fɔrɔ de ba ko lini á na seigi mɛ to.
18Ni-gwonim delo á na ke de toone de churu to
daa bá taa jege kuri.
Lɛɛro tem ná tu á baŋa, ne na-fɔrɔ na chwooli wonnu tei to,
te lage te yɔɔre te chɔge abam mo.
19Lɛɛro tem nam lage te taa tui titwon-twono mo
se te ja abam te jei.
Ko wó taa ke abam konto mo zezeŋa maama ne,
de wea de tete maama ne.”
Abam ná nigi Wɛ kwora kam konto kuri,
ko wó pa foone mo tiini de zo abam.
20Á bá na siu, ne nɔɔno sara kam na tiini ka ye kukua
se o peini da tei to,
naa o gare-jale dem de na tiini de ye memena
se o ma-de o kukwori o tete tei to.
21 Baŋa Wɛ nam daa wó pɔpɔ o nwoŋi,
ne o déem na ke tei Perazim peo yuu ne to.
O bane daa ta wó zaŋe,
ne ko déem na ke tei Gibeon bwolo kom tega ne to.
O nam na lage o ke tei to wó taa ye wo-kenkagele.
O lage o ke totoŋ-veira mo á tetare ne.
22Konto ŋwaane, daa yé ta‑á jege-ne á lwɛa.
Ko ná dae konto, á cham dem wó puli dedɛ.
Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom nam maŋe o pa-ne kwora o we,
o ti o yiga mo se o chɔge á tega kam maama.
23Nam fɔge-na á cheigi se á ni amo kwora kam.
Ta‑á yei-na se á wane á ni a na tɛ kolo to.
24Valo ná yɔɔre o chɛ swoori,
o bá taa vare taa ye o wo dugi kolokolo.
25O nam ná guri tega kam ye bwogili peini da,
o laam wó dole o wo-dwa bia bam mo ka baŋa ne.
O ta wó du mena dwi dwi da,
se ko maŋe de tega kam na ye tei to,
ye o daare o du wodiiru tedwonna o kara kam nia ne.
26Ko nam yeini ko ye Wɛ mo bere valo wom
pa se o yei o na wó taa ke tei to.
27Ko ná ye wo-sworru mo o pɛ,
o bá kwei luu-zɔŋɔ o tuuri te baŋa ne
naa o mage-te de da-lɔŋɔ.
O nam wó ma da-memena mo o fere-te
se o le te wo-bia bam.
28Ko nam ná ye mena, ba wó fere-ya lanyerane.
Ba nam bá ke konto taa
se ya cho yɔle-yɔle ne muni na ye te to.
Ba ná tuuri luu-zɔŋɔ ya baŋa ne,
ba nam bá mumugi-ya.
29Valo yeino kom konto maama nwoŋi Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tei ne mo.
Wɛ maa jege swa chekke,
ye o bere nabiina kolo na maŋe se ba taa ke to.

english_text:
Jerusalem Will Suffer
The Lord said:
1Jerusalem, city of David,
the place of my altar,
you are in for trouble!
Celebrate your festivals
year after year.
2I will still make you suffer,
and your people will cry
when I make an altar of you.
3I will surround you and prepare
to attack from all sides.
4From deep in the earth,
you will call out for help
with only a faint whisper.
5Then your cruel enemies
will suddenly be swept away
like dust in a windstorm.
6I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will come to your rescue
with a thundering earthquake
and a fiery whirlwind.
7Every brutal nation
that attacks Jerusalem
and makes it suffer
will disappear like a dream
when night is over.
8Those nations that attack
Mount Zion
will suffer from hunger
and thirst.
They will dream of food and drink
but wake up weary and hungry
and thirsty as ever.
Prophets Who Fool Themselves
9Be shocked and stunned,
you prophets!
Refuse to see.
Get drunk and stagger,
but not from wine.
10 The Lord has made you drowsy;
he put you into a deep sleep
and covered your head.
11Now his message is like a sealed letter to you. Some of you say, “We can't read it, because it's sealed.” 12Others say, “We can't read it, because we don't know how to read.”
13 The Lord has said:
“These people praise me
with their words,
but they never really
think about me.
They worship me by repeating
rules made up by humans.
14 So once again I will do things
that shock and amaze them,
and I will destroy the wisdom
of those who claim to know
and understand.”
15You are in for trouble,
if you try to hide your plans
from the Lord!
Or if you think what you do
in the dark can't be seen.
16 You have it all backwards.
A clay dish doesn't say
to the potter,
“You didn't make me.
You don't even know how.”
Hope for the Future
17Soon the forest of Lebanon
will become a field with crops,
thick as a forest.
18The deaf will be able to hear
whatever is read to them;
the blind will be freed
from a life of darkness.
19The poor and the needy
will celebrate and shout
because of the Lord,
the holy God of Israel.
20All who are cruel and arrogant
will be gone forever.
Those who live by crime
will disappear,
21together with everyone
who tells lies in court
and keeps innocent people
from getting a fair trial.
22The Lord who rescued Abraham
has this to say
about Jacob's descendants:
“They will no longer
be ashamed and disgraced.
23When they see how great
I have made their nation,
they will praise and honor me,
the holy God of Israel.
24Everyone who is confused
will understand,
and all who have complained
will obey my teaching.”
translation_text:
David teo Jerusalem taane
1Areli, nmo mo ye teo kolo wone David déem na zoore to,
Lɛɛro nam wó yi teo kom konto nɔɔna bam!
Abam ná laga,
ta‑á di-na á kura yam bene maama.
2Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam lage a ke chichuŋu de Areli tiina bam mo.
Ba wó taa keeri mo, ye ba ŋwana.
Amo wó pa se teo kom ji ne bimbini delo ba na zwɛ wonnu
ba ma ke kaanem da to mo.
3Amo tete mo lage a jeeri teo kom de jara.
A maa wó kaare ko maama a pu,
ye a daare a lɔ taara a yeiri ko yera ne se a di-ko.
4Abam wó ba tega mo
ye á ta‑á tigi da á ŋɔɔna.
Á ŋɔŋa kam wó nwoŋi teero wone se ka zaŋe fenfee.
Á wó ta‑á waase tega-tega ne chira na ŋɔɔne tei to.
5Abam dona kɔgɔ kom wó taa daga ne fwogo mo tei.
Ba nam wó ji ne swanno, vio na kale-te ko ja jei to.
Bedwe baŋa ne mo
6Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam lage o pɔpɔ o ba.
O maa wó tɔge de doa bagem, de tega ziziŋim, de sɔɔ dedɛ o ba.
O ta wó ba de vo-fɔrɔ de ko fufugim,
de mini na di wonnu bileim-bileim tei to mo.
7Ko ná ye dwi-gɛ tiina jar-keira balo na tu se ba kwaare jara de Areli,
ye ba kaare teo kom de ko dam jei sem maama ba pu to,
banto wó jei lela, ne nɔɔno na zaŋe dɔɔne wone
ye o dendwɛ jei tei to mo.
8Ko wó ke ne kana ná chɛ nɔɔno
pa kotu dwɛ we, o jege wodiu mo o di.
O maa na dɔ o zaŋe to, o kana kam ta wɔe.
Ko ta nye ne na-nyɔm ná jege nɔɔno wolo
ye kotu dwɛ we o jege na mo o nyɔa.
O maa ná zaŋe dɔɔm ne,
o yɔɔre o lage o beiri mo de na-nyɔm.
Ko nam wó ke konto dwoŋi mo
de dwi-gɛ tiina jar-keira balo na tu
ba kwaare jara de Zion peo kom tiina to.
9Nam yage-na se ko so abam, se á ta‑á zege yaau.
Pa-na se á yia dwei, se á yé ta‑á nae.
Ta‑á beiri-na, ye ko dae á na bugi sana to ŋwaane.
Ta á véi-na chwoŋa yuu de gaao,
ye ko dae ne ko tɔge sa-dɛɛra baŋa ne mo.
10 Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se á tiini á dɔ á kɛ mo.
O ta ma ja á sampwori sem yia yam o kwoni.
O ma pa ba kwoli abam yi-nara bam de yuni.
11Ko na ye tei to, Wɛ na veere taane delo o bere abam to nye de ba na popone botare selo ba ke tɔnɔ wone, ye ba daare ba kwoni ko ni to mo. Nmo ná kwei-ko n pa tɔnɔ tu ye n ta de kotu n we, “Ja! Ga tɔnɔ konto se a cheigi,” kotu wó leiri mo we, “Amo ba wane-ko a ga, ko ni na kwoni to ŋwaane.” 12N nam ná kwei-ko n pa wolo na yeiri tɔnɔ to, ye n ta ded‑o we, “Ja! Ga tɔnɔ konto se a cheigi,” kotu wó leiri mo we, “Amo yeiri tɔnɔ garem.”
13Baŋa Wɛ nam taga o we:
“Nɔɔna banto zuli amo de ba ni mo,
ye ba yeini ba ta we, ba sɛ amo ni.
Ba boboŋa nam tera amo tei ne.
Ba na pae amo zula tei to maama ye kafɛ mo,
ko na tɔge nabiina boboŋa chullu to ŋwaane.
14Konto ŋwaane mo a daa wó jwoori
a ke wo-kenkagela a saŋe daane se ko so-ba dedɛ.
Swa tiina bam boboŋa maama wó jei mo,
se yi-pore-nyena bam de yi-poro kom ji kafɛ.”
15Lɛɛro wó yi balo na ko tega ba zoore
se ba seigi ba boboŋa Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to.
Banto toŋe ba totoŋa lim ne mo ye ba boŋe ba we,
“Wɔ mo nae debam?
Wɔ mo yei dé na jege kolo dé ke to ni ne?”
16Abam nam kwaane se á pa na mo duri tuntula.
Kamɔgɔ de ko mɔro, wɔ mo dwoi?
Kamɔgɔ wó wane ko ta de kamɔ-mɔro wom we,
“Ko dae nmo mo ke ne” na?
Kambia de nam wó wane o ta wolo na mɔɔne-ka to taane we,
“Wolo na ke-ne to yeiri kolokolo” na?
17Ko daa bá dáane se Lebanon goa kam na lini de teeni to
pipiri ka ji kara.
Kara kalo maa na lana de varem to
de wó pipiri ka ji goa.
18Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia,
zwa-kwarro wó ni tɔnɔ kom wo taane dem.
Lilwoa na jei yibiri wone to yia wó puri
se ba na kolo na jege ko ke to.
19Nabwona laam maa wó jwoori ba di ywoni Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane.
Yiniga tiina de maa wó ke wopwolo
Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom ŋwaane.
20Nankɔ-nyena wó jei.
Boyere-nyena de daa maa bá taa wora.
Balo maama na jege puseŋa kikia puga ba jei to de dwi wó saare.
21Banto maa jege ba dwonna ba soga.
Ba maa jaane chega ba jua se chega bora yé taa toŋa,
ye ba fɔ vwa pa se chega tiina ba nae ba bora.
22 Baŋa Wɛ mo ye wolo na jwoŋi Abaraham o yage to. O nam tɛ tento mo de Jakob dwi tiina bam:
“Chaveera daa bá ja Jakob dwi tiina bam,
se ba yuni taa veela.
23Ba ná nii ba nae ba bia bam na daga tei ba tetare ne,
ye ba ye balo amo mo na kwei a pa-ba to,
ba laam wó zuli amo yere dem.
Ba wó taa nege amo wolo na ye Jakob dwi tiina Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom to.
Ba maa wó da ko ŋwaane ba taa kɔre amo wolo na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ wom to.
24Balo na tusi ba boboŋa ne to laam maa wó na yi-poro.
Balo de na swoi pompona to wó sɛ se ba jwoŋi bera.”

english_text:
Don't Expect Help from Egypt
1This is the Lord's message for his rebellious people:
“You follow your own plans
instead of mine;
you make treaties
without asking me,
and you keep on sinning.
2You trust Egypt for protection.
So you refuse my advice
and send messengers to Egypt
to beg their king for help.
3“You will be disappointed,
completely disgraced
for trusting Egypt.
4The king's power reaches
from the city of Zoan
as far south as Hanes.
5But Egypt can't protect you,
and to trust that nation
is useless and foolish.”
6This is a message
about the animals
of the Southern Desert:
“You people carry treasures
on donkeys and camels.
You travel to a feeble nation
through a troublesome desert
filled with lions
and flying fiery dragons.
7Egypt can't help you!
That's why I call that nation
a helpless monster.”
Israel Refuses To Listen
8The Lord told me to write down his message for his people, so that it would be there forever. 9They have turned against the Lord and can't be trusted. They have refused his teaching 10and have said to his messengers and prophets:
Don't tell us what God has shown you and don't preach the truth. Just say what we want to hear, even if it's false. 11Stop telling us what God has said! We don't want to hear any more about the holy One of Israel.
12Now this is the answer
of the holy One of Israel:
“You rejected my message,
and you trust in violence
and lies.
13This sin is like a crack
that makes a high wall
quickly crumble 14and shatter
like a crushed bowl.
There's not a piece left
big enough to carry hot coals
or to dip out water.”
Trust the Lord
15The holy Lord God of Israel
had told all of you,
“I will keep you safe
if you turn back to me
and calm down.
I will make you strong
if you quietly trust me.”
Then you stubbornly 16said,
“No! We will safely escape
on speedy horses.”
But those who chase you
will be even faster.
17As few as five of them,
or even one, will be enough
to chase a thousand of you.
Finally, all that will be left
will be a few survivors
as lonely as a flag pole
on a barren hill.
The Lord Will Show Mercy
18The Lord God is waiting
to show how kind he is
and to have pity on you.
The Lord always does right;
he blesses those who trust him.
19People of Jerusalem, you don't need to cry anymore. The Lord is kind, and as soon as he hears your cries for help, he will come. 20The Lord has given you trouble and sorrow as your food and drink. But now you will again see the Lord, your teacher, and he will guide you. 21Whether you turn to the right or to the left, you will hear a voice saying, “This is the road! Now follow it.” 22Then you will treat your idols of silver and gold like garbage; you will throw them away like filthy rags.
23The Lord will send rain to water the seeds you have planted—your fields will produce more crops than you need, and your cattle will graze in open pastures. 24Even the oxen and donkeys that plow your fields will be fed the finest grain.
25On that day people will be slaughtered and towers destroyed, but streams of water will flow from high hills and towering mountains. 26Then the Lord will bandage his people's injuries and heal the wounds he has caused. The moon will shine as bright as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter than usual. It will be like the light of seven days all at once.
Assyria Will Be Punished
27The Lord is coming
from far away
with his fiery anger
and thick clouds of smoke.
His angry words flame up
like a destructive fire;
28he breathes out a flood
that comes up to the neck.
He sifts the nations
and destroys them.
Then he puts a bridle
in every foreigner's mouth
and leads them to doom.
29The Lord's people will sing as they do when they celebrate a religious festival at night. The Lord is Israel's mighty rock, and his people will be as happy as they are when they follow the sound of flutes to the mountain where he is worshiped.
30The Lord will get furious. His fearsome voice will be heard, his arm will be seen ready to strike, and his anger will be like a destructive fire, followed by thunderstorms and hailstones. 31When the Assyrians hear the Lord's voice and see him striking with his iron rod, they will be terrified. 32He will attack them in battle, and each time he strikes them, it will be to the music of tambourines and harps.
33Long ago the Lord got a place ready for burning the body of the dead king. The place for the fire is deep and wide, the wood is piled high, and the Lord will start the fire by breathing out flaming sulfur.
translation_text:
Ba yé ke ba teena Ejipti wone
1 Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento:
“Lɛɛro wo abam baŋa ne
de á na ye yi-dɛ-nyena to.
Boboŋa yalo abam na jege á ma á toŋe to dae amo boboŋa.
Abam ta maa vei á ke ni-sɛɛm de teene dedwonna,
ye amo wo pɛ chwoŋa se á ke konto.
Á kikia yam konto maa pae se á yɔɔre á ke wɛleera
á daŋe da-baŋa ne.
2Abam duri á vo Ejipti teo ne mo
ye á maŋe á wo bwei-ne se á lɔre a boboŋa.
Abam ya teene we Ejipti teo pa-faro wom wó taa jege abam
o kwola o woro wone mo.
3Ejipti pɛ wom na wó kwoli abam tei to wó ta á kuri mo.
Á na boŋe se á seigi o woro wone tei to
maa wó pa á na á chaveera.
4Á dedɛɛra badwonna maŋe ba wo Zoan ne,
ye á toŋe badwonna se ba vo ba yi Hanesi.
5De ko de, chaveera mo lage ya di Judah tiina bam maama,
de ba na kwei ba teena ba daŋe te-kafɛ baŋa ne to.
Teo kom konto ba jege wolim se ko pa-ba.
Kuri-nɔrɔ de chaveera yerane mo
ko lage ko pa ba na.”
6Wɛ kwora mo tento se ko tɔge vara balo na wo tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam wone to:
Tega kam konto seene ka chana ye daanem dedɛ wora.
Nywonnu maa wo jei sem maama ne,
ko woli de basankwe dedaane kapɛ.
De ko de, dedɛɛra kwei ba jejegero mo
ba daŋe bonɛ de kona baŋa ne ba tɔge da
se ba ja ba vo ba pa teo kom konto nɔɔna.
Ko maa ye teo kolo na ba jege nyɔɔre ko pa-ba to mo.
7Ejipti teo bá wane abam ko woli de fenfee de.
Konto ŋwaane mo amo kwei baseim a pa-ko,
se ba taa bwoi we, ‘Rahaba na jei chemm to’.
Nɔɔna balo na nwoŋi Wɛ kwaga ne to taane
8Popone wonnu tento maama
n tiŋi n pa nɔɔna bam.
Ke-te tɔnɔ wone se te taa tigi da jwa seeni ŋwaane,
se ko taa ye maana ko pa-ba taa wuu.
9Ba yɔɔre ba ye zwabani-nyena mo,
ye ba swoi vwa totoŋa.
Ba maa wo sɛ bera yalo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ba to.
10Ba maa tɛ de yi-nara bam ba we,
“Daa yé ta‑á nii á nae veera!”
Ba ta maa tɛ de Wɛ sampwori sem ba we,
“Daa yé ta-na chega á bere debam!
Nam ta-na wonnu telo na ywona puga ne to,
se á ma á gane debam.
11Ywori-na chwoŋa kam wone,
se á daa yé che dé yiga.
Yage-na ka-taa-kare-ka-tɛ
Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom taane á bere debam.”
12Mo kokuri, Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom nam tage tento:
“Abam seene á ve amo kwora kanto mo,
ye á daare á sɛ vuvuga totoŋa
se á ta‑á ma á gane nɔɔna.
Á na tɔge kikia yam konto dwoŋi to ŋwaane,
13á wó yɔɔre á to de á bora mo.
Abam wó to tega ne ne kabira na dɔra
ye ka jege lolo-kayɔlɔ ka yera ne to mo.
Kabira kam lage ka pɔpɔ ka to mo buri-buri bedwe baŋa ne.
14Abam ta lage á to á chochoge
ne kambia kalo ba na feiri tega ne
pa se ka ji kanchwi muga-muga yerane to mo.
Kanchua daa bá daare
se ba wane min-chale ba kwei ba ke ka wone,
naa se ba dane na ba ke kɔɔro wone.”
15Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu to na tage tei to mo tento:
“Abam ya ná leiri á boboŋa
pa se á jwoori amo tei,
á ya wó na á verem, ye á ta sii.
Á ya ná ye chemm mo,
ye á daare á sale amo yera ne,
á ya wó na á dam dem.
Abam nam ba sɛ se á ke konto.
16Abam nam boŋe á tete ne mo á we,
‘Debam wó kwei dé sisein-nɔɔna
dé duri dé dona yiga ne se dé lu!’
Chega to, á wó seene á duri se á lu!
Á ta tɛ mo we, ‘Dé sisein-nɔɔna bam wara,
dé wó di-se mo dé lu.’
Chega to, á dona bam nam wara ba dwoi abam.
17Á dona bam wone nɔɔno dedoa ná bage tiguri-kaasa,
á nɔɔna moro mo wó duri ba daare‑o.
Ko laam ná ye á dona bam banu,
ba yi se ba fugi abam maama se á duri á daare-ba.
Se ko kweeli to, á wó duri á daare á nɔɔna fenfee.
Ba wó taa ye ba yera,
ne daa na zege geili-geili
ka zeiŋi tuta peo yuu ne tei to.”
Baŋa Wɛ wó duri o nɔɔna yibwona
18Ko nam na ye tei to,
Baŋa Wɛ ta jei se o ke abam zaane mo.
O ma yɔɔre o ti o yiga se o duri abam yibwona.
Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ yeini o bore chega bora mo.
Balo na ke ba teena ded‑o to tiini ba jege yu-ywoŋo.
19Nɔɔna daa wó taa zoore Zion ne. Abam daa yé ta‑á keeri-na Jerusalem teo ne. Baŋa Wɛ wó duri á ŋwaŋa ne á ná keeri á jare‑o. O ná yɔɔre o ni á keira kam, o wó leiri abam lworo. 20Baŋa Wɛ seene o kwei yaara de cham mo o pa abam, se te ji á ni-wodiu, de á na se á nyɔ. Wolo na jege Wɛ bera yam o zamese abam to daa bá seigi o tete. Á yia wó yɔɔre ya na‑o. 21Abam ná ywori chwoŋa ye á vo jazem seeni, naa jagwia seeni de, á wó ni kwora na zege á kwaga ne ka ŋɔɔne de abam ka we, “Chwoŋa kam mo tento á yiga ne. Véi-na ka wone.” 22Ko ná ye á jwona yalo ba na kwei lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa ba gɔgere-ya to, abam laam maa wó taa nii-ya ne ya ye weero mo á yiga ne. Á wó dole-ya á yage, ne á na ke tei de wo-zɔɔna to mo, ye a ta de-ya we, “Lage-na jei dé yiga ne.”
23Abam ná dugi á wo-dwa, Baŋa Wɛ wó pa do-ŋwe ne se á wodiiru ke lanyerane, se á zage wodiiru zanzam. Maŋa kam konto ná yia, á vara de wó na pwola yala-yala se ba taa di ga-zuru da. 24Nabɛ de bonɛ selo na toŋe á kare sem ne to tete wó taa di mena yalo ba na chaare men-swanno tem lanyerane ba yage ba daare-ya to mo. 25Maŋa kam konto ne á wó yɔɔre á di á dona se ba dalem jei sem vaare se to tega ne. Na maa wó taa bura peero de zwonnu maama yuu ne ba duri ba tu tega ne bare-bare. 26Chana kam wó peere pa se ka pwooni de wea pwooni taa mae daane. Wea kam de wó tiini ka nye ka woli da kuni berepɛ, ne da yarepɛ pwooni na lage de ke daane tei to. Konto maama wó ke ne Baŋa Wɛ ná tu o twoŋi o nɔɔna kwi selo na bwori to, ye o daare o pa se ba fufwollu tem fɔge te kwɛ.
27Nii-na! Baŋa Wɛ zege yiga yiga mo o beene,
ye o yere dem nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ nii ko nae jaja.
O wo tiini ko fuli mo ye nyoa zaŋa guli-guli.
Ban-lom taane delo na nwoŋi o ni ne to
ye ne min-vogo na di wonnu bugi-bugi tei to mo.
28O ná sii o momwa vio,
ko nye de na-fɔrɔ na fufugi
ba di ba maŋe nɔɔno ba seeni to mo.
O maa jege dwi-gɛ tiina bam o chɔga
ne o zɛ-ba yɔlɔ ne mo tei.
O ta maa ke-ba ne o na kwei gara o ke ba nia ne,
se o pa ba ywori ba chwoŋa wone tei to mo.
29Wɛ nɔɔna bam, abam nam wó di ywoni, ne á na yeini á di kuri á ma‑á zuli Wɛ ye á leeni lei tete ne tei to. Á wó ke wopwolo se ko nwoŋi á bochara ne, ne á na mage kɔgɔ á diini Baŋa Wɛ peo kom to mo, se á vo á zuli wolo na ye Isarele tiina peo to, ye nɔɔna wui wi ba tɔge á yiga ba via. 30Baŋa Wɛ maa wó bage de kwor-dɛa, pa se nɔɔna lɔre o na jege nenɔŋa de dam tei to. O ta wó twe o jeŋa se o waare nɔɔna o ban-lom dem ŋwaane. O maa wó fugi-ba de min-vogo na di bugi-bugi to, de vo-fɔrɔ, de doa bagem, de do-kandwa. 31Baŋa Wɛ kwora ná zaŋe konto, foone wó tiini de ja Asiria tiina bam. O lage o kwei da-lɔŋɔ mo o mage-ba o de tega ne. 32Ko na wó ke tei to, Baŋa Wɛ wó taa tiini o dole-ba jaguli-zana mo se o ke chichuŋu de-ba. O ná kwei o da-lɔŋɔ kom se o ma o waare-ba maŋa de maŋa, nɔɔna wó taa wɔe senyɛ ye ba tae kwanno wopwolo ŋwaane. 33Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o kwɛ jeiga ba na wó zwɛ twa da to. Ba ti yiga se ba zwɛ Asiria teo pɛ wolo na tege to yera dáane. Mini jei sem konto luuna, ye se ta yala de. Ba ma dogele dɛ dedɛ ba ke da se mini taa di bileim-bileim. Baŋa Wɛ nam ná sii o momwa vio, ko nye de chilibugu mo nyeene ye ko duri ne buga to. Ko laam maa wó taa jege‑o ko di bugi-bugi!

english_text:
Don't Trust the Power of Egypt
1You are in for trouble
if you go to Egypt for help,
or if you depend on
an army of chariots
or a powerful cavalry.
Instead you should depend on
and trust the holy Lord God
of Israel.
2The Lord isn't stupid!
He does what he promises,
and he can bring doom.
If you are cruel yourself,
or help those who are evil,
you will be destroyed.
3The Egyptians are mere humans.
They aren't God.
Their horses are made of flesh;
they can't live forever.
When the Lord shows his power,
he will destroy the Egyptians
and all who depend on them.
Together they will fall.
4The Lord All-Powerful
said to me,
“I will roar and attack
like a fearless lion
not frightened by the shouts
of shepherds trying to protect
their sheep.
That's how I will come down
and fight on Mount Zion.
5I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will protect Jerusalem
like a mother bird circling
over her nest.”
Come Back to the Lord
6People of Israel, come back!
You have completely turned
from the Lord.
7The time is coming
when you will throw away
your idols of silver and gold,
made by your sinful hands.
8The Assyrians will be killed,
but not by the swords
of humans.
Their young men will try
to escape,
but they will be captured
and forced into slavery.
9Their fortress will fall
when terror strikes;
their army officers
will be frightened
and run from the battle.
This is what the Lord has said,
the Lord whose fiery furnace
is built on Mount Zion.
translation_text:
Lɛɛro wó yi balo na sale Ejipti yera ne to
1Lɛɛro wó yi balo na kare ba vei Ejipti teo se ba beeri wolim,
ye ba daare ba teege sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne to.
Banto teena daŋe ba sisei-torokooro baŋa ne mo
te na daga to ŋwaane.
Ba teena ta daŋe ba sisein-dira baŋa ne,
ba na jege baare to ŋwaane.
Ba yiga nam tere Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom wone.
Ba ba lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o zeini-ba.
2 Baŋa Wɛ nam jege swa!
O wae o pae lɛɛro yi nɔɔna.
O maa ba jwoori o ni dem kwaga ne.
Ko ná ye nɔɔna balo dwi maama na toŋe lwarem to,
ko woli de balo na zege ba kwaga ne to,
o lage o zaŋe ba baŋa ne mo o waare-ba.
3Ejipti tiina bam nam ye nabiina mo se ba dae Wɛ.
Ba sisein-nɔɔna maa jege ye-daa,
se se dae jworru telo toone na ware de ja to.
Baŋa Wɛ nam ná twe o jeŋa se o waare-ba,
teo kolo nɔɔna ya na jege dam to wó tiri ba to tega ne mo.
Balo de na beeri wolim ba tei ne to de maa wó to,
pa se ba maama laam tɔge daane ba jei.
4 Baŋa Wɛ de ma ta tento de amo o we:
“Amo Baŋa Wɛ wó ke ne nywoŋo mo suura,
naa nywoŋ-pɔla na nɛ nɔne ye ka laare tei to.
Nayere-kɔgɔ ná gilimi daane se ba zeili-ko
ye ba kaase tei maama de,
ko bá fom.
Ba sɔɔ kom bá pa se ko yera taa sae.
Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ de wó foore o chu konto dwoŋi mo,
se o ke jara Zion peo kom yuu ne.
5Ne zuna na kare wɛyuu kom ne ba jaane tei to,
konto mo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ de lage
o taa kwoli Jerusalem.
O wó che teo kom se cham yé yi-ko,
ye o daare o jwoŋi-ko o yage,
O maa wó tɔge ko baŋa ne o kɛ
se o vere ko nɔɔna bam o yage.”
6Isarele tiina bam, pipiri-na á jwoori Baŋa Wɛ tei, de á ya na yɔɔre á kwei a kwaga á ya‑o tei de. 7Maŋa kam konto ná yia, abam dedoa dedoa wó ve jwona yalo á na tusi á ma á tete je á kwei lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa á ke-ya to.
8“Asiria tiina bam wó te jara wone.
Ko nam dae nabiina se-zɔɔro mo lage te go-ba.
Ko ye Wɛ se-zɔɔ kom mo lage ko go-ba.
Ba jar-keira bam wó kwaane se ba duri ba lu.
Wolo na wane-ba to wó fe ba nɔn-donno tem
o de totoŋ-chɛɛra wone.
9Ba wó duri ba daare ba dam jei sem,
foone na jaane-ba to ŋwaane.
Ba dedɛɛra bam ná nɛ jara-keim tuta na zeiŋi wɛɛne to,
ba boboŋa wó vugimi mo ye foone zo-ba.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
O maa ye wolo na tɔre mini Zion peo yuu ne,
ye o dwei mini-fɔrɔ Jerusalem teo kom wone to.

english_text:
Justice Will Rule
1A king and his leaders
will rule with justice.
2They will be a place of safety
from stormy winds,
a stream in the desert,
and a rock that gives shade
from the heat of the sun.
3Then everyone who has eyes
will open them and see,
and those who have ears
will pay attention.
4All who are impatient
will take time to think;
everyone who stutters
will talk clearly.
5Fools will no longer
be highly respected,
and crooks won't be given
positions of honor.
6Fools talk foolishness.
They always make plans
to do sinful things,
to lie about the Lord,
to let the hungry starve,
and to keep water from those
who are thirsty.
7Cruel people tell lies—
they do evil things,
and make cruel plans
to destroy the poor and needy,
even when they beg
for justice.
8But helpful people
can always be trusted
to make helpful plans.
Punishment for the Women of Jerusalem
9Listen to what I say,
you women who are carefree
and careless!
10You may not have worries now,
but in about a year,
the grape harvest will fail,
and you will tremble.
11Shake and shudder,
you women without a care!
Strip off your clothes—
put on sackcloth.
12Slap your breasts in sorrow
because of what happened
to the fruitful fields
and vineyards,
13and to the happy homes
in Jerusalem.
The land of my people
is covered with thorns.
14The palace will be deserted,
the crowded city empty.
Fortresses and towers
will forever become
playgrounds for wild donkeys
and pastures for sheep.
God's Spirit Makes the Difference
15When the Spirit is given to us
from heaven,
deserts will become orchards
thick as fertile forests.
16Honesty and justice
will prosper there,
17and justice will produce
lasting peace and security.
18You, the Lord's people,
will live in peace,
calm and secure,
19even if hailstones flatten
forests and cities.
20You will have God's blessing,
as you plant your crops
beside streams,
while your donkeys and cattle
roam freely about.
translation_text:
Paare delo na wó tɔge chega to
1Nii-na! Pɛ wodwoŋi wó ba o di o paare de chega.
Teo kom dedɛɛra de wó taa bore chega bora ba pa nɔɔna.
2Ba dedoa dedoa wó taa ye dalem jei,
ne woro mo kwoli nɔɔna se vo-fɔrɔ yé ja-ba.
Ba wó taa nye de na-dura mo kagoa yuu ne
de peo kolo woro na jwoŋi nɔɔna se wea yé di-ba to.
3Balo na nii ba nae to maa wó taa nae jaja.
Balo zwa de na ni to wó taa fɔge ba cheiga.
4Balo na ye wole-wole to wó boŋe ba yi de yi-poro.
Balo de na ŋɔɔne ba bibeigi to wó taa ŋɔɔne jase.
5Nɔɔna daa bá taa tɛ jworo we, o ye nɔn-yero.
Ba bá taa pae nankɔ-nyena zula.
6Kokuri to, jworo ŋɔɔne ko jworim mo.
O boboŋa de maa jeeli lwarem kikia yerane.
O ba lage se o taa tɔge Wɛ chwoŋa,
ye o ni taane nye de o twe Baŋa Wɛ mo.
O maa yage balo kana na jege-ba to se ka ni-ba.
Ko ta ná ye na-nyɔm na jege balo to,
o pae de chɛ-ba mo.
7Nankɔ-nyem kikia yɔɔre ya ye puseŋa yerane mo.
O yeini o jei o boŋe lwarem mo,
se o ma vwa o chɔge nabwona,
de ba ná maŋe ba beeri se ba na ba chega de.
8Ko nam ná ye nɔn-yero, o boŋe boboŋ-ŋona mo.
O maa yeini o zege o totoŋ-ŋona yam kwaga ne.
Jerusalem teo kaana bam taane
9Kaana bam na jei de zurim falalala to,
zaŋe-na se á cheigi a taane dem!
Teo kom bukwa na ba jege lwia to,
cheigi-na amo na lage a ta kolo to!
10Zem mo kolokolo ba daane abam.
Nam lɔre-na we,
bene ko mae tento to abam wó fom,
ye á yera taa sae.
Kokuri to, á teeni dem bá lei bia.
Wodiiru bá ke se á zage á ja á zo diga.
11Kaana bam, yage-na á na jei fae to se á yera taa sae.
Bukwa balo na ba jege lwia to,
kɔre-na foone.
Lɔɔre-na á gwaaro tem,
se á daare á leiri á vɔ gare-nyenyaaro á tei sem ne.
12Daŋe-na á je á nyɔɔna ne wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane
de á kare sem na chɔge
ye á Vini teeni ba leiri bia to ŋwaane.
13Nam keeri-na amo nɔɔna tega kam ŋwaane,
sabare yerane laam na jege-ka.
Ywoni déem mo wo teo kom jei maama ne,
ye nɔɔna chaka ko sam dem wone.
Laam nam ta‑á keera teo kom ŋwaane.
14Nɔɔna wó duri ba daare pɛ sɔ-fɔrɔ kom.
Teo kom konto ya na su de sɔɔ to,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá taa zoore ko wone.
Ko dam jei sem de mɛ ba na zege da ba yere-ko to maama chɔge.
Kagoa wo bonɛ de vare-mwa yerane laam mo jeeri da ba di gaao.
15Ko wó taa ye konto mo se Wɛ laam pa o Jworo nwoŋi wɛyuu ne
ko ba dé baŋa.
Maŋa kam konto ne, kagoa kam wó ji te-ywoŋa,
ye te-ywoŋa kam de laam ji goa mɛ na lini de teeni to.
16Jei maama ne nɔɔna wó taa tɔge chega kikia,
kagoa yuu de te-ywoŋa ne de.
17Ba nɔn-ŋonne kikia wó pa zurim mo taa wora.
Ba ta wó taa jei de yazura taa wuu
ba chega totoŋa yam ŋwaane.
18Amo nɔɔna bam wó taa zoore jei selo ne
yazura na wora to mo.
Daanem de lwia bá yi-ba ba sam dem wone.
19Do-kandwa ná maŋe ya chɔge goa kam,
ye teo kom maama ba tega tei maama de,
20abam ta wó taa jege yu-ywoŋo.
Á wó vo á du á wo-dwa bu-dura maama ni ne.
Á ta wó yage á naane de á bonɛ sem,
se de taa kare de beeri yɔɔ de di gaao.

english_text:
Jerusalem Will Be Safe
1You defeated my people.
Now you're in for trouble!
You've never been destroyed,
but you will be destroyed;
you've never been betrayed,
but you will be betrayed.
When you have finished
destroying and betraying,
you will be destroyed
and betrayed in return.
2Please, Lord, be kind to us!
We depend on you.
Make us strong each morning,
and come to save us
when we are in trouble.
3Nations scatter when you roar
and show your greatness.
4We attack our enemies
like swarms of locusts;
we take everything
that belongs to them.
5You, Lord, are above all others,
and you live in the heavens.
You have brought justice
and fairness to Jerusalem;
6you are the foundation
on which we stand today.
You always save us and give
true wisdom and knowledge.
Nothing means more to us
than obeying you.
The Lord Will Do Something
7Listen! Our bravest soldiers
are running through the streets,
screaming for help.
Our messengers hoped for peace,
but came home crying.
8No one travels anymore;
every road is empty.
Treaties are broken,
and no respect is shown
to any who keep promises.
9Fields are dry and barren;
Mount Lebanon wilts
with shame.
Sharon Valley is a desert;
the forests of Bashan and Carmel
have lost their leaves.
10But the Lord says,
“Now I will do something
and be greatly praised.
11Your deeds are straw
that will be set on fire
by your very own breath.
12You will be burned to ashes
like thorns in a fire.
13Everyone, both far and near,
come look at what I have done.
See my mighty power!”
Punishment and Rewards
14Those terrible sinners
on Mount Zion tremble
as they ask in fear,
“How can we possibly live
where a raging fire
never stops burning?”
15But there will be rewards
for those who live right
and tell the truth,
for those who refuse
to take money by force
or accept bribes,
for all who hate murder
and violent crimes.
16They will live in a fortress
high on a rocky cliff,
where they will have food
and plenty of water.
The Lord Is Our King
17With your own eyes
you will see the glorious King;
you will see his kingdom
reaching far and wide.
18Then you will ask yourself,
“Where are those officials
who terrified us and forced us
to pay such heavy taxes?”
19You will never again have to see
the proud people who spoke
a strange and foreign language
you could not understand.
20Look to Mount Zion
where we celebrate
our religious festivals.
You will see Jerusalem,
secure as a tent with pegs
that cannot be pulled up
and fastened with ropes
that can never be broken.
21Our wonderful Lord
will be with us!
There will be deep rivers
and wide streams
safe from enemy ships.
The Lord Is Our Judge
22The Lord is our judge
and our ruler;
the Lord is our king
and will keep us safe.
23But your nation is a ship
with its rigging loose,
its mast shaky,
and its sail not spread.
Someday even you that are lame
will take everything you want
from your enemies.
24The Lord will forgive your sins,
and none of you will say,
“I feel sick.”
translation_text:
Lɛɛro de wolim taane
1Lɛɛro lage te yi abam balo na kare á chɔge amo nɔɔna bam to mo.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ta wo chɔge abam!
Lɛɛro wó yi abam de á na baare nɔɔna kwaga ne to.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ya ta wo baare abam kwaga!
Abam nam ná chɔge teene dedwonna á ti,
mo ba laam wó chɔge abam de.
Abam bebara kam na ti maŋa kalo ne to
mo ba laam lage ba baare á de kwaga.
2Dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ, pa n zaane dem ba dé baŋa,
se dé teena wo nmo wone mo.
Zezeŋa maama ne pa debam dam.
Ta pa se dé na verem cham maŋa ne.
3Nmo ná pɛ se tiguri-kaasa zaŋe,
teene maama nɔɔna wó duri mo se ba lu.
N ma‑n ná zaŋe wɛɛne,
dwi-gɛ tiina wó jage sae mo.
4Dé dona bam,
ne kayere na yeini se deilimi kara se ja tega tei to,
konto mo nɔɔna wó pɛ á jejegero ba ja viiri,
se kolokolo daa yé daare.
5 Baŋa Wɛ yere dem mo zaŋe wɛɛne.
O maa zoore wɛyuu kom baŋa jei sem ne.
O nam wó pa se Zion tiina bam taa tɔge chega de nɔn-ŋonne kikia yerane.
6Woŋo kolo maama ná ke abam,
Baŋa Wɛ mo wó zege á kwaga ne de dam.
O ta wó vere abam cham wone o yage,
se á ta‑á tiini á jege swa de yeino lanyerane.
Balo na kɔre Baŋa Wɛ to,
wo-laaro tento mo wó taa ye ba lonne wonnu.
7Nii-na! Dé bembɛ sem tete chwoosi
dé teo kom chwei sem yuu ne mo.
Dé na toŋe balo se ba kwɛ wonnu to
de keeri mo de wo-chechɔgɔ.
8Nɔɔna duri ba daare chwo-fare sem mo.
Chwo-veila daa ba tɔge pempala yam ne ba via.
Nɔɔno ná ke ni-sɛɛm de o dwoŋi,
o wó chɔge-de mo.
Ba ta gwooni balo na pae maana taane dim baŋa ne mo.
Ba daa maa ba nege nɔɔn-nɔɔno de.
9Tega kam maama koge mo ye ka ta leere.
Lebanon teeni dem de kwaare mo
ye chaveera di teo kom.
Saron te-ywoŋa kam de jigi kagoa mo.
Basan de Kamele jei sem teeni vɔɔro ma siiri.
10 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Maŋa laam nam yi se a zaŋe a toŋe.
Ko yi se a pa a yere dem zaŋe wɛɛne,
se a jwoŋi zula nɔɔna tei ne.
11Abam ná jaane swanno puga,
ga-korro mo wó ji bu wolo á na wó lo to.
Momwa vio kolo á na sii á yage to
maa wó ji mini de zwɛ abam.
12Ko wó pa á teo tiina bam zwɛ kula mo,
ne sabare na zwɛ ye se ji tentwarem tei to.
13Abam balo teene na wo yiga yiga to,
lɔre-na totoŋ-kamunnu telo amo na ke to.
Abam balo de na bwola to,
ta‑á yei-na we, a dam dem daga dedɛ!”
14Wɛleere-keira balo na wo Zion ne to
wora ba to de foone mo.
Balo na ve Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem to yera maa sae pɔm-pɔm,
ye ba tɛ ba we:
“Debam wone wɔ mo wó wane o taa zoore
jeiga kalo mini na wora de di de chɔge to?
Wɔ mo wó wane o zege
mini delo na bá dwei maŋa de maŋa to yiga ne?”
15Ko nam ye wolo na tɔge chwo-laao
ye o yɔɔre o tɛ chega to mo.
Kotu ba sɛ se o pini nɔɔna se o ma o duni,
ye o ba sɛ o jwoŋi wonnu kalipera baŋa ne.
O ba gwaane de balo na ke bana se ba go nɔɔna to.
O nam bere o ba sɛ se o toŋe lwarem.
16Nɔɔno ná ye konto dwoŋi,
konto tu jei mo ye lwia ba jege‑o.
Ko nye de o dale peo mo.
Maŋa maama wone, wonto ba gae o ni-wodiu,
na-nyɔm de nam bá ja‑o.
17Abam wó nii á na pɛ wom na jei de nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ,
ye o paare laŋa kam jage ka yi jei maama.
18Á laam ma‑á wó boŋe wonnu telo ya na pɛ abam foone to boboŋa
se á ta we, “Dedɛɛra yiga tu wom bɛ?
Wolo na fe o jwoŋi lampwoo dé tei ne to wo yein-seeni mo?
Dedɛɛro wolo na zege o yere teo kom to de bɛ?”
19Abam nam daa bá na boyere-nyena bam konto maŋa de maŋa.
Ba ye balo taane na ye de yera ye á ba ni de kuri to mo.
Ba na ŋɔɔne tei to nye de ba bibeigi mo.
20Nii-na Zion teo kom!
Ko ye mɛ dé na di dé kura yam da to mo.
Abam ná nii á na Jerusalem teo kom,
á wó na we ko zege cheppe mo,
ne vwei delo na ba bebege to.
Ba bá wane ba gɔ vwei dem konto paara.
De yera ŋone de nam bá kɔ se de chɔge.
21Dáane mo Baŋa Wɛ laam wó taa ye dé Dam Tu.
Bu-fara de nabare wó taa duri se kɛa
jei sem konto ne mo.
Pwola nam bá taa wora se dé dona bam ja ba nabwooru
ba ba dáane ba yɛ ba kɛ.
Nabwor-kamunnu bá wane te tɔge da te kɛ.
22Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ mo wó jwoŋi debam o yage.
O ye wolo na bore debam bora to mo.
O maa pae debam o nia yam se dé taa tɔga.
Wonto mo ye dé pɛ.
23Ko ná ye abam nabworo kom,
ko gare-yi ŋone sem daa wo vɔge diŋ-diŋ,
ye ko tetare beiŋa kam daa ba zege deiki.
Konto to, vio daa ware ko yigi gare-yi dem
se nabworo kom taa yɛ na ko via.
Abam nam wó ba á vere á dona bam jejegero á chɛ á pa daane.
Gwaaro de wó na ba popɔra,
jejegero tem na wó taa daga dedɛ to ŋwaane.
24Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá taa zoore Zion teo ne
se kotu ta we, “A weele mo.”
Balo na zoore da to,
Wɛ wó kwei ba wɛleera o yage o chɛ-ba.

english_text:
The Nations Will Be Judged
1Everyone of every nation,
the entire earth,
and all its creatures,
come here and listen!
2The Lord is terribly angry
with the nations;
he has condemned them
to be slaughtered.
3Their dead bodies will be left
to rot and stink;
their blood will flow
down the mountains.
4 Each star will disappear—
the sky will roll up
like a scroll.
Everything in the sky
will dry up and wilt
like leaves on a vine
or fruit on a tree.
Trouble for Edom
5 After the sword of the Lord
has done what it wants
to the skies above,
it will come down on Edom,
the nation that the Lord
has doomed for destruction.
6The sword of the Lord
is covered with blood
from lambs and goats,
together with fat
from kidneys of rams.
This is because the Lord
will slaughter many people
and make a sacrifice of them
in the city of Bozrah
and everywhere else
in Edom.
7Edom's leaders are wild oxen.
They are powerful bulls,
but they will die
with the others.
Their country will be soaked
with their own blood,
and its soil made fertile
with their own fat.
8The Lord has chosen
the year and the day,
when he will take revenge
and come to Zion's defense.
9Edom's streams will turn into tar
and its soil into sulfur—
then the whole country
will go up in flames.
10 It will burn night and day
and never stop smoking.
Edom will be a desert,
generation after generation;
no one will ever travel
through that land.
11Owls, hawks, and wild animals
will make it their home.
God will leave it in ruins,
merely a pile of rocks.
The End of Edom
12Edom will be called
“Kingdom of Nothing.”
Its rulers will also be nothing.
13Its palaces and fortresses
will be covered with thorns;
only wolves and ostriches
will make their home there.
14Wildcats and hyenas
will hunt together,
demons will scream to demons,
and creatures of the night
will live among the ruins.
15Owls will nest there
to raise their young
among its shadows,
while families of vultures
circle around.
16In The Book of the Lord
you can search and find
where it is written,
“The Lord brought together
all of his creatures
by the power of his Spirit.
Not one is missing.”
17The Lord has decided
where they each should live;
they will be there forever,
generation after generation.
translation_text:
Logo baŋa dwi tiina taane
1Abam dwi-gɛ tiina, fɔɔre-na á yi se á cheigi.
Nɔɔna na wo jei maama to pore-na á zwa.
Tega kam baŋa maama
de balo na zoore ka wone to jege se ba cheigi,
ko woli de logo baŋa wonnu dwi maama.
2 Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe de dwi-gɛ tiina bam maama mo.
O wo ma fuli de ba jar-keira bam.
O yɔɔre o pɔɔre-ba o zege dáa ne se ba na chɔgem mo.
O maa wó pa se ba dona go-ba ba ti.
3Ba maa wó kwei ba twa bam ba dole ba yage,
se ba yera yam lwom zaŋe tage-tage.
Ba jana de maa wó faare peero jei sem maama.
4Wɛyuu chalechwe sem maama wó jei,
ye ba piri wɛyuu kom tete ne sara mo ba piri.
Chalechwe sem maama wó taa toe tega ne mo,
ne Vini tio vɔɔro naa kaporo vɔɔro na kwaare
ye te siiri te toe tega ne tei to.
5 Baŋa Wɛ maa we,
“A se-zɔɔ kom maŋe ko toŋe ko fera ko su wɛyuu ne.
Nii-na! A laam wó kwei-ko a ma a waare Edom tiina bam mo.
Banto ye balo a na pɔɔre a zege dáa ne
se ba yɔɔre ba na chɔgem to mo.”
6 Baŋa Wɛ se-zɔɔ kom maama yɔɔre ko ye jana yerane mo.
Vara lara de maa taare ko maama.
Ko nye de pei de bone jana,
ko woli de pi-bale tapwale-bia bam lara mo taare-ko.
Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ lage o ke kaanem mo Bozera teo ne.
O maa wó go nɔɔna dedɛ Edom laŋa kam ne.
7Ba dedɛɛra bam wó yɔɔre ba te,
de ba na nye de na-bale selo na ware se ja to mo.
Ba babɛ sem na dana ne nabɛ tei to de wó tɔge ba te.
Ba jana mo wó bugi ba tega kam maama.
Ba yera lara de maa wó ji popɔnɔ ka pɔɔne-ka.
8Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ le dɛ mo
se o ba o zeini Zion tiina bam.
Bene dem konto wone o lage o yiri jene
ba dona bam baŋa ne mo.
9Edom bu-nwaro tem wó ji kɔtaale mo.
Ba teo kasolo de maa wó ji chilibugu.
Mini maa wó ja ba tega kam maama,
ne mini na jege kɔtaale de di tei to.
10Wea de tete maama wone, teo kom mini bá dwei.
De nyoa kam de wó taa zaŋe wɛɛne mo wuu.
Ba tega kam wó taa tigi yɔɔ yerane mo,
ko zege dwi dedoa ne se ko yi dwi dedwoŋi maŋa ne.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá tɔge ba tega kam ne o kɛ.
11Kunkworru, de bachangaaro, de vara dwi dwi
mo wó taa tei jei sem konto.
Baŋa Wɛ lage o twe o jeŋa Edom tega kam baŋa ne,
se o maŋe-ka ye o daare o jeeli ka chɔgem dem.
O maa wó pa se tega kam taa tigi yɔɔ yerane.
12Edom teo yiga tiina bam daa bá na pɛ
se kotu taa nii ko baŋa ne.
Ba nakwa bam maama wó jei mo.
13Sabare mo wó jwoŋi ba sa-fwaaro tem.
Bombwaano de ga-cheiŋo de maa wó cheiŋi ba dam jei sem maama.
Teo kom laam maa wó taa ye mɛ
nywoŋ-kuri de kunkworru na zoore to.
14Ga-kukuri de wiira mo wó taa tɔge daane ba beeri wodiiru.
Tɔro maa wó taa kare da te keera,
ye tete wo-korro laam taa tigi di-dwonnu tem gugworru wone.
15Kunkworru wó sɔ te pworu da
ye te de te chechara.
Te chechara yam maa wó lwei
se te taa jege te bia te nii da.
Kalwonnu de wó taa jeeri jei sem konto ne,
wo-bɛ de wo-kana maama.
16Nii-na Baŋa Wɛ tɔnɔ kom wone
se á wó na ko na popone we:
Wonnu tento dedoa bá lage kodwoŋi ko ga.
Wo-bɛa bá ga wo-kana se te taa wo daane.
Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ ni dem konto,
ye wonto Jworo kom mo lage ko la-te ko ja jeeri daane.
17 Baŋa Wɛ mo pɔɔre tega kam o pa-te.
O ma maŋe jei selo te maama na wó taa zoore to.
Ko nam na zege dwi dedwe ne se ko yi dwi dedwoŋi to,
te wó lɛɛre te taa zoore dáane mo taa wuu.

english_text:
God's Splendor Will Be Seen
1Thirsty deserts will be glad;
barren lands will celebrate
and blossom with flowers.
2Deserts will bloom everywhere
and sing joyful songs.
They will be as majestic
as Mount Lebanon,
as glorious as Mount Carmel
or Sharon Valley.
Everyone will see
the wonderful splendor
of the Lord our God.
God Changes Everything
* 3 Here is a message for all
who are weak, trembling,
and worried:
4“Cheer up! Don't be afraid.
Your God is coming
to punish your enemies.
God will take revenge on them
and rescue you.”
5 The blind will see,
and the ears of the deaf
will be healed.
6 Those who were lame
will leap around like deer;
tongues once silent
will shout for joy.
Water will rush
through the desert.
7Scorching sand
will turn into a lake,
and thirsty ground
will flow with fountains.
Grass will grow in deserts,
where packs of wild dogs
once made their home.
God's Sacred Highway
8A good road will be there,
and it will be named
“God's Sacred Highway.”
It will be for God's people;
no one unfit to worship God
will walk on that road.
And no fools can travel
on that highway.
9No lions or other wild animals
will come near that road;
only those the Lord has saved
will travel there.
10The people the Lord has rescued
will come back singing
as they enter Zion.
Happiness will be a crown
everyone will always wear.
They will celebrate and shout
because all sorrows and worries
will be gone far away.
translation_text:
Wɛ nɔɔna bam wó di ywoni
1Wopwolo wó yi kagoa jei sem mɛ na na tera to.
Te-kora kam wó di ywoni,
ga-punnu na wó kwi te nwoŋi da de zurim to ŋwaane.
2Jei sem konto wó tiini se ke punnu dedɛ,
pa se se taa chaka de wopwolo.
Tega kam wó ke lam,
ne Lebanon peero tem na ye tei to.
Ka nenɔŋa de wó nwoŋi jaja,
ne Kamele de Saron jei sem na ye tei to mo.
Nɔɔna laam maa wó na Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom,
de o paare dem na ye tei to.
3Nam pa balo vɔna na bugi to
jwoori ba na dam,
se balo nagwola na tege to
daa jwoori ba na baare.
4Ta de balo wo na leegi to we,
“Ja-na baare se á yé ta‑á fona.
Se á Tu Wɛ wom lage o ba
se o bere o ban-zɔŋɔ mo,
ye o daare o yiri jene á dona baŋa ne.
O nam wó ke konto mo se o vere abam o yage.”
5Lilwoa yia laam maa wó puri
ye zwa-kwarro de zwa yam pore.
6Gwaaro de wó faŋe wɛɛne,
ne woŋa dwoŋi to,
ye memaaro de taa bage sɔɔ ba yage de wopwolo.
Na de wó taa buri ba bugi kagoa yuu,
ye nabare de taa wo te-kora kam ne se dura.
7Kasolo kolo wea kam ya na yɔɔre ka jege ka mage to
laam wó ji buga mo ko taa tiga.
Te-kora kam ne, buli-yia wó taa tae
ya nwoŋi jei maama ne.
Jei selo maama nywoŋ-kuri ya na tigi da to,
ga-zuru, de nanchan-gullu, de sangɛ mo laam wó taa wora.
8Chwo-fara wó peini se nɔɔna taa tɔge da ba via.
Ba wó taa bwoi-ka we, “Wose Chwoŋa” mo.
Balo na jege digiru Wɛ chullu tem seeni to
bá wane ba tɔge ka wone.
Kokuri to, balo na tɔge Wɛ chwoŋa to yerane mo vei ka wone.
Jworru bá na chwoŋa se ba beeri ka wone.
9Nywonnu bá taa wo chwoŋa kam konto ne.
Kago-vara balo na jaane nɔɔna to de bá tɔge da.
Tento maama maŋe te bá twɛ da.
Wɛ na vere balo o ja nwoŋi cham wone to
mo wó tɔge da ba taa via.
10 Baŋa Wɛ na jwoŋi balo o yage to
wó tɔge da ba jwoori sɔŋɔ.
Ba maa wó jwoori ba zo Zion teo kom wo
ye ba leeni de wopwolo.
Ywoni delo na ba ti to mo wó taa ye ba nyem.
Ba wopwolo kom wó tiini ko gaale,
ye ba wo-chechɔgɔ de ba keira kam wó jei.

english_text:
The Assyrians Surround Jerusalem
(2 Kings 18.13-27; 2 Chronicles 32.1-19)
1Hezekiah had been king of Judah for 14 years when King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city 2except Jerusalem. The Assyrian king ordered his army commander to leave the city of Lachish and to take a large army to Jerusalem.
The commander went there and stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool. 3Three of the king's highest officials came out of Jerusalem to meet him. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
4The Assyrian commander told them:
I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself. 5Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria? 6 Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
7Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord, your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
8The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people! He will give you 2,000 horses, if you have enough troops to ride them. 9How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry? 10Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
11Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
12The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you!”
13Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted out in Hebrew:
Listen to what the great king of Assyria says! 14Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you. 15Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria. 16Stop listening to Hezekiah. Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns 17for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards and raise your own grain.
18Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him. Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria? 19What happened to the gods of Hamath, Arpad, and Sepharvaim? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces? 20None of those gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord, your God, can do any better?
21-22Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_text:
Asiria teo pɛ ke chichuŋu de Judah tiina
2 Pwa 18:13-27; 2 Tigisim 32:1-19
1Pɛ Hezekia paare dim bena fuga-yana bene dem wone mo Asiria teo pɛ Senakeribi tu o li Judah te-kamunnu telo na lɔge chekke, ye te ta fɔge te pe to maama de jara. O ma wane-ba o di. 2Asiria pɛ wom ma toŋe o dedɛɛra bam yiga tu se o zege Lakisi ne o nwoŋi de jar-keira kɔgɔ dedɛ o vo Jerusalem o gware Hezekia. Dedɛɛro wom ma vo o zege na-fera kalo na zoore baŋa seeni chɔgɔ kom to ni ne, se ko maŋe de chwoŋa kam mɛ ba na sɔ gwaaro to. 3Pɛ wom ma toŋe Hilikia bu Eliakim na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom totoŋa baŋa ne to, dedaane Sebena na ye tɔn-poponno to, ko woli de Asafe bu Joa na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom yera seina twanno baŋa ne to, se ba nwoŋi teo kom wone ba vo ba jeeri‑o.
4Ba na jeeri to mo Asiria teo dedɛɛra yiga tu wom tage de-ba se ba ja Asiria pɛ wom kwora ba vo ba ta de Pɛ Hezekia. O maa we:
“Asiria teo Pa-faro wom we: Bɛ mo bere ko pa se n jege n tete chega konto? 5Nmo boŋe we ni-wɛɛle wae jara de ke mo na? Wɔ baŋa ne mo n teege ye n lɔ amo kwaga ne? 6Nmo teena wo Ejipti teo ne mo na? Konto nam nye de nɔɔno na kwei kasogo o ji o nacheiga to mo. Kasogo kom wó seere mo ko zɔ wolo maama na zei-ko to jeŋa. Konto mo wó ke de wolo maama na sale Ejipti Pa-faro wom yera ne to. 7Nmo nam ta ná we, ‘Dé wó sale debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ yera ne mo,’ ko dae Wɛ dem konto wara-jei, de de kaanem bimbina mo Hezekia guri o yage o daare o pa ni se Jerusalem de Judah nɔɔna maama taa tui bimbini dem na wo ywo-seeni to yerane ba zuli‑o na?
8Amo lage a ma a tu wom yere mo a ke ni dedaane nmo Hezekia. Amo wó pa‑m sisei morro telei, ne nmo ná wó wane n na se dira bam n ke da. 9Nii amo wolo na ye a pɛ wom nabwom to na jege dam delo to. Nmo wó wane amo n ve, ye n daare n ke n teena de Ejipti tiina se ba woli‑m de ba jara-keim torokooro de ba sisein-dira na? 10Ko dae Baŋa Wɛ mo toŋe-ne se a ba ywo a wane n teo kom na? Ko seene ko ye Baŋa Wɛ tete mo pɛ-ne ni se a li teo kom de jara a daare a chɔge-ko.”
11Eliakim, de Sebena, dedaane Joa maama ma ta de Asiria teo dedɛɛra yiga tu wom ba we, “Popo ŋɔɔne Aram tiina taane de debam, se dé wó ni.
