Nmo ná ŋɔɔne de Judah tiina taane dem, balo na dɔge kabira kam yuu ne ba cheigi to wó da ba ni n na tɛ kolo to mo.” 12Asiria teo dedɛɛro wom ma leiri o we, “Á boŋe we amo tu wom kwora kam ye abam de á pɛ wom yerane nyem mo na? Ka ta wora balo maama na dɔge kabira kam baŋa ne to ŋwaane mo. Banto de wó da ba di ba beinnu ba daare ba nyɔ ba fea, ne abam na jege se á ke tei to mo.”
13Dedɛɛro wom ma tɔɔle o yage de Judah tiina taane dem o we:
“Abam maama cheigi-na Asiria teo pa-faro wom kwora kam. 14Pɛ wom we: Yé sɛ-na se Hezekia taa jege abam o gana, se o bá wane abam o jwoŋi o yage! 15Yé pa-na se á pɛ wom gane abam se á ke á wo-dedoa de Baŋa Wɛ. O ná tage de abam we, Baŋa Wɛ wó jwoŋi abam o yage, ye o che se Asiria teo pɛ yé di á teo kom, nam yé sɛ-na.
16Yé cheigi-na Hezekia taane kɔtaa. Asiria pɛ wom nam na tage tei to mo tento: Abam maama jege se á nwoŋi á teo kom wone mo se á ba á to á pa-ne. Á ná ke konto, á wó na chwoŋa se á ta‑á jei yɔlɔ-lɔ-lɔ ye á di á tete Vini teeni de á kaporro tem nyɔɔre. Á ta maa wó nyɔ á vola na bam á ni ywoni. 17Konto kwaga ne, amo ta wó ja abam a vo a yage tega kalo na nye de abam tete tega kam to baŋa ne. Dáane Vini teeni wora se á na sana á nyɔ, de mena se á ma á ke bworobworo.
18Yé cheigi-na pɛ Hezekia taane dem, de o na gane abam ye o we, Baŋa Wɛ wó jwoŋi abam o yage to. Teo kɔ jwona mo dana pa se ya wane ya jwoŋi ya teene dem Asiria pa-faro wom jeŋa ne ya yage? 19Hamafa, de Arapade, de Sefavayim jwona yam bɛ? Ya wane ya vere Samaria tiina ya yage a dam kuri ne na? 20Teene dem maama jwona yam wone, jwoni dɔ mo wane de jwoŋi de teo de yage amo jeŋa ne? Baŋa Wɛ de nam bá wane o vere Jerusalem o yage amo jeŋa ne.”
21Jerusalem teo nɔɔna bam ma maŋe da chemm, ba wo leiri o taane dem, kokuri to, Pɛ Hezekia ya pɛ-ba ni mo o we, “Yé leiri-o-na.”
22Hilikia bu Eliakim na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom totoŋa baŋa ne to, de Sebena na ye tɔn-poponno to, dedaane Asafe bu Joa na tiŋi pɛ sɔŋɔ kom yera seina twanno tem to maama ma ja ba gwaaro ba kaare wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane, ye ba ja kwora kalo Asiria teo dedɛɛra yiga tu wom na taga to ba vo ba ta de Pɛ Hezekia.

english_text:
Hezekiah Asks Isaiah for Advice
(2 Kings 19.1-13)
1As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord. 2He told Prime Minister Eliakim, Assistant Prime Minister Shebna, and the senior priests to dress in sackcloth and tell me:
3Isaiah, these are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born. 4Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
5When these leaders came to me, 6I told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah:
I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria. 7I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
8Meanwhile the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
9About this same time, the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
10Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me. 11You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe? 12The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them? 13The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared.
Hezekiah Prays
(2 Kings 19.14-19)
14After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see. 15Then he prayed:
16 Lord God All-Powerful of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world. 17Just look and see how Sennacherib has insulted you, the living God.
18It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts. 19They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped. 20But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only Lord.
Isaiah Gives the Lord's Answer to Hezekiah
(2 Kings 19.20-34)
21-22I went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said:
Hezekiah, you prayed to me about King Sennacherib of Assyria. Now this is what I say to that king:
The people of Jerusalem
hate and make fun of you;
they laugh behind your back.
23Sennacherib, you cursed,
shouted and sneered at me,
the holy One of Israel.
24You let your officials
insult me, the Lord.
And here is what you
have said about yourself,
“I led my chariots
to the highest heights
of Lebanon's mountains.
I went deep into its forest,
cutting down the best cedar
and cypress trees.
25I dried up every stream
in the land of Egypt,
and I drank water
from wells I had dug.”
26Sennacherib, now listen
to me, the Lord.
I planned all of this long ago.
And you don't even know
that I alone am the one
who decided that you
would do these things.
I let you make ruins
of fortified cities.
27Their people became weak,
terribly confused.
They were like wild flowers
or like tender young grass
growing on a flat roof
or like a field of grain
before it matures.
28I know all about you,
even how fiercely angry
you are with me.
29I have seen your pride
and the tremendous hatred
you have for me.
Now I will put a hook
in your nose,
a bit in your mouth,
then I will send you back
to where you came from.
30Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year, you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest. 31Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit. 32I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
33I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack. 34As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem. 35I will protect it for the sake of my own honor and because of the promise I made to my servant David.
The Death of King Sennacherib
(2 Kings 19.35-37)
36The Lord sent an angel to the camp of the Assyrians, and he killed 185,000 of them all in one night. The next morning, the camp was full of dead bodies. 37After this, King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh. 38One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_text:
Hezekia lwoori wolim Baŋa Wɛ tei ne
2 Pwa 19:1-7
1Pɛ Hezekia déem na nigi kwora kam to, o wo ma tiini ko chɔge ye o kaare o gwaaro. O ma daare o kwei gare-nyenyaaro o zo, ye o vo o zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam. 2O ma toŋe Eliakim na nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom totoŋa baŋa ne to, de Sebena na ye tɔn-poponno to, dedaane Wɛ kaanem yiga tiina bam se ba zo gare-nyenyaaro ba vo Amozi bu Izaya na ye Wɛ sampwora to tei. 3Ba ma vo ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Hezekia na tage tei to mo tento: Dé zem jege lɛɛro de chaveera mo dé di. Ko tiini ko ye kuri-nɔrɔ mo de yera ne. Dé nye de kaane na virigi puga se o lo, ye dam tere o yera ne se o lo bu wom to mo. 4Asiria teo pɛ wom mo toŋe o dedɛɛra yiga tu se o ba o twe Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Dɛ delo tento nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ nigi toro tem konto maama, ye o nam wó bwɛ dedɛɛro wom de o ta-balɔrɔ kom. Nam lwoori Wɛ n pa debam balo fee na daare pa de maŋe teo kom ne to.”
5Hezekia tontoŋena bam na pɛ Izaya kwora kam ba ti to, 6mo Izaya de kwei kwora o pa-ba o we, “Jwoori-na á vo á ta de Pɛ Hezekia we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Yé ta‑n kɔre foone de taane delo Asiria pɛ na tɔge o nɔn-donno tem baŋa ne o ma o twe-ne to. 7Nii mo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se Asiria pɛ wom boboŋa vugimi pa se o ni sawea, ye o da ka ŋwaane o jwoori o tete teo. Dáane mo ba wó zɔ‑o de se-zɔɔ ba go.’ ”
Asiria pɛ Senakeribi chichuŋu belei tu taane
8Asiria teo dedɛɛra yiga tu wom déem nigi we, ba pɛ wom yage Lakisi teo ye o vo se o kwaare jara de Libina teo tiina. O de ma vo dáane.
9Maŋa kam konto ne de, Asiria teo pɛ Senakeribi ta nigi kwora we, Tirahaka na ye Kusi teo pɛ to mo beene se o jeeri‑o de jara. O ma toŋe nɔɔna Hezekia tei ne de kwora kanto o we:
10“Ta-na de Judah teo pɛ Hezekia we, ‘Yé pa wɛ delo n na pɛ-de chega to taa jege‑m de gane we, Jerusalem teo bá fɔge ko zo Asiria teo pɛ jeŋa ne. 11Nmo maŋe n ni Asiria teo pwa bam na toŋe tei de logo baŋa teene maama to. Ba yɔɔre ba chɔge de maama mo. Nmo nam boŋe tetɛ mo ye n teene se n lu? 12Teene dedwonna dem jwo-dɛɛra wane-de ya jwoŋi ya yage amo nabaara bam jeŋa ne na? Gozam teo wɛ, de Haran teo wɛ, de Rezepa teo wɛ, de Eden tiina balo déem na zoore Tɛl-Asara ne to wɛ wo wane ba wolowolo ya jwoŋi ya yage. 13Ko ta ná ye Hamafa, de Arapade, de Sefavayim, de Hena, de Ivaa, teene dem konto pwa bam de wo yein-seeni mo?’ ”
Hezekia wɛ-lworo kom
14Hezekia ma jwoŋi tɔnɔ kom Asiria teo pɛ tontoŋena bam tei ne, ye o ga-ko. O ma ja-ko o zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam. O ma jare-ko Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. 15Hezekia ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ ye o we, 16“Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to, nmo paare di cherubi sem tetare laŋa ne mo. Nmo yerane mo ye Wɛ, ye n tei tega baŋa paare dim jei maama. Nmo nam mo naane wɛyuu de tega baŋa. 17Baŋa Wɛ, nam pore n zwa se n cheigi! Ta puri n yia se n nii n na kolo na jege ko ke debam tento to. Cheigi ta-kwogila yalo maama Senakeribi na toŋe o ma o twe nmo Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ to. 18Baŋa Wɛ, ko ye chega mo we Asiria teo pwa déem seene ba chɔge teene maama de de nɔn-bia dedɛ, pa se de ji di-dwonnu yerane. 19Ba ma dole teene dem konto jwona ba de mini wone ba zwɛ-ya. Kokuri to, ba wa yam dae wa chekke. Nabiina mo boŋe ba ja ye ba kwei dɛ de kandwa ba ke-ya. Konto ŋwaane mo ba de ba jwona nɛ chɔgem. 20Konto to, dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ, yɔɔre n jwoŋi debam n yage Asiria teo pɛ jeŋa ne se logo baŋa teene dem maama lɔre we nmo yerane mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.”
Baŋa Wɛ leiri pɛ wom
2 Pwa 19:20-37
21Amozi bu Izaya ma toŋe kwora Pɛ Hezekia tei ne ye o we:
“Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: Nmo na lwoori amo tei se ko vo Asiria teo pɛ Senakeribi seeni to, 22kwora kanto mo Baŋa Wɛ jege se o pa‑o:
Zion tiina bam yɔɔre ba neese nmo mo.
Jerusalem teo tiina bam jege‑m mo ba mɔna.
23Wɔ mo nmo twe ye n daare n lwɛ konto?
Wɔ yiga ne mo n zege n nye baare
ye n daare n bere n tete konto dwoŋi?
Ko ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom mo.
24Nmo tɔge n tontoŋena baŋa ne mo
n twe amo Baŋa Wɛ.
Nmo ta ma n bere n tete n we,
‘Amo pɛ se a sisei-torokooro dedɛ mo di peero tem yuu
te yi Lebanon peero tem yuu chekke.
A ta ma gwoni ba tei-dedwaaro dem a de tega ne,
de ba tei-ŋonno tem maama.
A ma vo a yi yiga yiga a di ba peero tem yuu,
ye a zo ba goa mɛ na lini to wone.
25Amo ta ma vo a ko vola sa-teene ne yiga yiga,
ye a nyɔ na ya wone.
A jar-keira bam ma nɔne Ejipti bwi sem
de ba napera pa se we.’
26Nmo wo nigi we amo maŋe
a boŋe boboŋe dem faŋa faŋa mo na?,
A na boŋe tei faŋa faŋa konto to
mo amo laam pɛ se ko seene ko ke.
A boboŋa déem jaane
se nmo zaŋe n chɔge teene delo ya na lɔge de pe to,
se de ji kandwa na dogele da-baŋa ne ya tigi to mo.
27A ta pɛ se teene dem konto nɔn-bia bam dam ti,
ye ba di ba chaveera nmo ŋwaane.
Banto jigi ne ga-punnu de ga-lɛɛro mo nmo yiga ne.
Ba maa nye de gaao na wora ko tae ko nwoŋi tei to,
ye wea laam mage-ko pa se ko te lela.
28Amo nam yei nmo kuri maama.
A ta yei n na-veili maama ni ne,
de ni-wɛɛle delo n na jege n ke de amo to ni ne.
29Amo laam lage a waare‑m mo
n na jege ni-wɛɛle delo n ke de amo to ŋwaane.
N yi-dɛɛre kikia yam to amo zwa ne.
Mo kokuri amo wó lei gwola n momwɛ ne,
ye a daare a ke gara n ni ne.
A laam maa wó vaŋe‑m se n tɔge
chwoŋa kalo n na tɔge da n ba to
n jwoori n tete teo.”
30Izaya laam ma ta de Hezekia o we:
“Keim dento mo wó ke se ko taa ye maana ko pa‑m: Dɔɔm bene dem ne, á wó di wodiiru telo na ke te tete ne to. Bene delo na saŋe-de to ne, á wó di kolo na tage ko nwoŋi boboa nyem kom yera ne to. Ko daare bena yatɔ bene dem ne, abam wó du wodiiru ye á pe-te. Á ta wó jeiri Vini teeni ye á daare á di de wo-bia bam. 31Judah dwi tiina balo ta na daare to laam wó taa ye ne tio bonno na jaane tega ye ko nɛ sem leiri bia to mo. 32Kokuri to, Jerusalem teo tiina ta wó daare. Chega to, balo na zoore Zion peo kom baŋa ne to badaara wó lu toone wone. Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tete nam wó pa se wonnu tento maama ke, o na seene yia o nii o nɔɔna baŋa ne to ŋwaane.
33 Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage Asiria teo pɛ yera taane tei to mo tento: O bá na chwoŋa se o zo teo konto wone. O jar-keira bam bá ta chene kɔtaa da! Ba bá kwei ba jara nantane ba nwoŋi se ba ke chichuŋu de teo kom, naa ba lɔ taara ba yeiri teo kom kabiri sem teiŋa ne. 34Asiria pɛ na tɔge chwoŋa kalo o ba to, mo o wó tɔge da o jwoori, se o bá zo teo konto wone. 35Amo tete yere dem zula ŋwaane, de a tontoŋeno David ŋwaane, a wó taa kwoli teo konto se kolokolo yé wane-ko ko chɔge. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.”
36 Baŋa Wɛ maleka déem ma zaŋe ka vo Asiria jar-keira bam na tigisi mɛ to. Ka ma go Asiria tiina morro bi de funɔnɔ-banu (185, 000). Tega na poore to, ba ma na we ba jei sem su de twa yerane mo. 37Konto baŋa ne mo Senakeribi pɛ o jar-keira bam yage jara yam keim, ye o jwoori o kɛ o vo o tete teo. O laam ma vo o zoore Ninevɛ teo ne.
38Dɛ dedwe, o déem ma zo o jwoni Nisiroka diga kam se o zuli-de. O bia balei Aderamɛlɛka, de Sarezera ma zo ba zage‑o ba go de se-zɔɔro. Ba ma duri ba vo Ararati laŋa kam ba zoore da. Senakeribi bu Esara-hadon déem ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ.

english_text:
Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies
(2 Kings 20.1-11; 2 Chronicles 32.24-26)
1About this time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. So I went in and told him, “The Lord says you won't ever get well. You are going to die, and so you had better start doing what needs to be done.”
2Hezekiah turned toward the wall and prayed, 3“Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried hard.
4Then the Lord sent me 5with this message for Hezekiah:
I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will let you live 15 more years, 6while I protect you and your city from the king of Assyria.
7Now I will prove to you that I will keep my promise. 8Do you see the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway built for King Ahaz? I will make the shadow go back ten steps.
Then the shadow went back ten steps.
King Hezekiah's Song of Praise
9This is what Hezekiah wrote after he got well:
10I thought I would die
during my best years
and stay as a prisoner forever
in the world of the dead.
11I thought I would never again
see you, my Lord,
or any of the people
who live on this earth.
12My life was taken from me
like the tent that a shepherd
pulls up and moves.
You cut me off like thread
from a weaver's loom;
you make a wreck of me
day and night.
13Until morning came, I thought
you would crush my bones
just like a hungry lion;
both night and day
you make a wreck of me.
14I cry like a swallow;
I mourn like a dove.
My eyes are red
from looking to you, Lord.
I am in terrible trouble.
Please come and help me.
15There's nothing I can say
in answer to you,
since you are the one
who has done this to me.
My life has turned sour;
I will limp until I die.
16Your words and your deeds
bring life to everyone,
including me.
Please make me healthy
and strong again.
17It was for my own good
that I had such hard times.
But your love protected me
from doom in the deep pit,
and you turned your eyes
away from my sins.
18 No one in the world of the dead
can thank you or praise you;
none of those in the deep pit
can hope for you
to show them
how faithful you are.
19Only the living can thank you,
as I am doing today.
Each generation tells the next
about your faithfulness.
20You, Lord, will save me,
and every day that we live
we will sing in your temple
to the music
of stringed instruments.
Isaiah's Advice to Hezekiah
21I had told King Hezekiah's servants to put some mashed figs on the king's open sore, and he would get well. 22Then Hezekiah asked for proof that he would again worship in the Lord's temple.
translation_text:
Hezekia weele ye o jwoori o zaŋe
2 Pwa 20:1-11; 2 Tigisim 32:24-26
1Da yam konto ne, Hezekia déem yɔɔre o weele mo ye o bwola de toone. Wɛ sampwora Izaya na ye Amozi bu to ma vo o tei ye o ta‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Bere n sɔŋɔ tiina bam ba na wó ke tei ne n ná tera. Kokuri to, n lage n te mo. N bá‑n wori de n jaweo kom.”
2Hezekia na nigi konto to, mo o pipiri o yibia o jeeri kabira kam ye o lwoori Wɛ o we, 3“Baŋa Wɛ, guli we amo yeini a tɔge‑m de a chega maama, dedaane a wo maama mo. A ma yɔɔre a ke kolo nmo na lage se a ke to.” Hezekia ma tiini o keeri dedɛ.
4 Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi Izaya we:
5“Véi n ta de Hezekia we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye n kwo David Wɛ to mo tage o we: A nigi n wɛ-lworo kom, ye a ta na n na kane yi-na tei to. A nam lage a woli bena fuga-yanu mo n bena yam wone. 6A ta wó jwoŋi nmo de Jerusalem teo konto a yage Asiria teo pɛ wom jeŋa ne, se a daare a taa kwoli teo konto.
7Keim dento nam mo wó pa n lɔre we, Baŋa Wɛ wó seene o ke o na gwoni ni se o ke tei to: 8Nii se n wó na wɛ dem na jege de zoora ye de ke luluŋu kolo Ahaz nateini dem yera ne to. Baŋa Wɛ lage o pa lunluŋu kom fɔɔre ko jwoori kwaga naba-laara yia kuni fuga mo.’ ”
Wɛ dem na ke lunluŋu kolo to ma seene ko jwoori kwaga naba-laara yia kuni fuga.
9Hezekia déem na zaŋe o jaweo kom baŋa ne ye o na yazura to, mo o pane leiŋa kanto:
10Amo ya boŋe a tete ne mo we,
“A lage a te a nɔn-donne maŋa ne mo,
se a zo churu ye a maŋe dáane taa wuu.
11A ma boŋe we, a daa bá taa ŋwe logo baŋa ne
se a na Baŋa Wɛ dáane.
A ta maa bá na nabiina balo na ŋwe to de.
A nam bá taa zoore ba tetare ne.
12Amo ŋwea kam pɔpɔ ka ti mo.
Ko nye de nayero na pɔpɔ o gɔ o vwei tei to mo.
Ko ta nye de gare-yi delo
gare-yi sɔɔno na pɔpɔ o vaŋe ŋona
o kɔ de yera ne to mo.
Nmo wora n pa a momwɛ ti lela,
ne wea na pɔpɔ ka ji lim tei to mo.
13A yɔɔre a keeri mo taa pa se tega ba ka poore.
Ko nye de nywoŋo ya mo jege a kwi sem ko yara.
Nmo wora n pa a momwɛ ti lela,
ne wea na pɔpɔ ka ji lim tei to mo.
14A keeri ne kawɛbidwoori
naa koŋwaa na keeri tei to mo.
A nam ta keeri ne kunkwoŋa mo.
Amo na kwoni a yuu wɛɛne taa to,
a yia seene mo de keira.
Amo Teiru Wɛ, a cham dem gaale.
Nam ba lela n jwoŋi-ne n yage.”
15Bɛ mo amo nam jege se a ta
wonnu tento maama baŋa ne?
Wɛ maŋe o ta taane o bere-ne,
ye o seene o ke o boboŋa na jaane tei to.
Amo wó gwooni a tete mo a ŋwea maama wone,
a wo na tiini ko chɔge to ŋwaane.
16Amo Teiru Wɛ, nmo kikia mo pae nɔɔna jege ŋwea.
Amo de maa tɔge ya ŋwaane a jege ŋwea.
Nam pa se yazura yi-ne
se a jwoori a na a ŋwea.
17Nii mo. A na nɛ yaara yalo to
jege nyɔɔre ya pa-ne.
N na swoi-ne to ŋwaane,
n wo sɛ se a to gwoŋo kolo na wó chɔge-ne to wone.
N ta daare n yage a wɛleera yam maama n chɛ-ne.
18Kokuri, balo na wo churu wone to ware se ba tei‑m.
Twa ware ba leeni ba seini‑m.
Balo de nam na zo tega kuri ne to,
ware se ba lɔre nmo na toŋe chega tei to.
19Ko ná ye chega, ko ye balo na ŋwe to yerane mo wae‑m ba tia,
ne amo na wora a ke tei zem to.
Kwoa wó ta ba bere ba bia
nmo na yɔɔre n jege chega tei to.
20 Baŋa Wɛ nam lage o jwoŋi-ne o yage mo.
Dé wó taa jege gwa kwɛɛra wonnu ye dé leeni dé zuli‑o.
Dé nam wó zuli‑o taa mo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone,
se ko yi dé ŋwea siseini.
21Izaya déem ya tage de Pɛ Hezekia mo o we, “Pa se ba zɔ mɔɔro se ba kwei-te ba taare n ŋɔn-pwona kam, se n wó na yazura.”
22Hezekia de ma bwei we, “Keim dɔ mo wó ke se ko bere we, amo daa wó na chwoŋa se a zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wo a zuli‑o?”

english_text:
Isaiah Speaks the Lord's Message to Hezekiah
(2 Kings 20.12-19)
1Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah was well, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him. 2Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
3I asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?”
“They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
4“What did you show them?” I asked.
Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
5Then I told Hezekiah:
I have a message for you from the Lord All-Powerful. 6One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left. 7 Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
8Hezekiah thought, “At least our nation will be at peace for a while.” So he told me, “The message you brought from the Lord is good.”
translation_text:
Ba toŋe nɔɔna pa ba zege Babilon ne ba ba
2 Pwa 20:12-19
1Ko maŋe de maŋa kam konto ne, Merodaki-Baladan laam mo jigi Babilon teo pɛ. O na nigi we Hezekia weele o zaŋe to, mo o toŋe nɔɔna o tei ne de twanno de pɛɛra. 2Hezekia déem ma jeeri nɔɔna bam de wopwolo. O ma ja-ba o zo o jejegero tem na tigi mɛ to. O laam ma bere-ba o lu-nyenno tem maama, de o sabu-seŋa, de o talwoŋ-ywei sem, de o nu-ŋoŋa kam, de o jara zela yam maama, de kolo maama ba na tiŋi jejegero di sem wone to. Pɛ Hezekia déem wo daare kolokolo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne, naa o paare dim jei sem maama ne ye o wo kwei o bere-ba.
3Wɛ sampwora Izaya déem ma vo Hezekia tei o bwei‑o o we, “Nɔɔna banto nwoŋi yein-seeni mo ba ba nmo tei? Ba nam tage bɛ mo de nmo?” Hezekia ma leiri o we, “Ba nwoŋi Babilon teo yiga yiga mo ba ba amo tei.” 4Izaya daa ma bwei o we, “Bɛ mo ba nii ba na n sɔŋɔ kom wone?” Hezekia ma leiri o we, “Amo bere-ba wonnu telo maama na tigi a jejegero di sem wone to mo. Kolokolo wo daare ye a wo bere-ba.”
5Izaya daa ta ma ta de Pɛ Hezekia o we, “Nam cheigi Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege kwora kalo se o pa‑m to: 6Ta‑n yei we, maŋa lage ka yi se Babilon teo tiina ba ba pɛ jejegero telo maama na tigi n sɔŋɔ kom wone to, de telo n nabaara bam na yaare ba la ba tiŋi to ba ja ba vo ba tete teo kom. Kolokolo daa bá daare ko pa abam. Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo konto. 7Nmo tete dwi dem de wó tɔge ba woli da ba vo. Ba nam ná jaane-ba ba yi da, ba wó lwe n bia bam mo se ba taa toŋe Babilon teo pɛ sɔŋɔ ne.”
8Hezekia na nigi konto to, mo o tage de Izaya o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑m kwora kalo se n pa-ne to lana.” Kokuri to, o boŋe o tete ne o we, “Ko ná ke konto, cham bá yi debam amo paare dim maŋa kam ne, ye a nɔɔna wó taa zoore de bochare-zuru.”

english_text:
Encourage God's People
1Our God has said:
“Encourage my people!
Give them comfort.
2Speak kindly to Jerusalem
and announce:
Your slavery is past;
your punishment is over.
I, the Lord, made you pay
double for your sins.”
3 Someone is shouting:
“Clear a path in the desert!
Make a straight road
for the Lord our God.
4Fill in the valleys;
flatten every hill
and mountain.
Level the rough
and rugged ground.
5Then the glory of the Lord
will appear for all to see.
The Lord has promised this!”
6 Someone told me to shout,
and I asked,
“What should I shout?”
We humans are merely grass,
and we last no longer
than wild flowers.
7At the Lord's command,
flowers and grass disappear,
and so do we.
8Flowers and grass fade away,
but what our God has said
will never change.
Your God Is Here!
9There is good news
for the city of Zion.
Shout it as loud as you can
from the highest mountain.
Don't be afraid to shout
to the towns of Judah:
“Your God is here!”
10 Look! The powerful Lord God
is coming to rule
with his mighty arm.
He brings with him
what he has taken in war,
and he rewards his people.
11 The Lord cares for his nation,
just as shepherds care
for their flocks.
He carries the lambs
in his arms,
while gently leading
the mother sheep.
Who Compares with God?
12Did any of you measure
the ocean by yourself
or stretch out the sky
with your own hands?
Did you put the soil
of the earth in a bucket
or weigh the hills and mountains
on balance scales?
13 Has anyone told the Lord
what he must do
or given him advice?
14Did the Lord ask anyone
to teach him wisdom
and justice?
Who gave him knowledge
and understanding?
15 To the Lord, all nations
are merely a drop in a bucket
or dust on balance scales;
all of the islands
are but a handful of sand.
16The cattle on the mountains
of Lebanon
would not be enough to offer
as a sacrifice to God,
and the trees would not
be enough for the fire.
17God thinks of the nations
as far less than nothing.
18 Who compares with God?
Is anything like him?
19Is an idol at all like God?
It is made of bronze
with a thin layer of gold,
and decorated with silver.
20 Or special wood may be chosen
because it doesn't rot—
then skilled hands
take care to make an idol
that won't fall on its face.
God Rules the Whole Earth
21Don't you know?
Haven't you heard?
Hasn't it been clear
since the time of creation?
22God is the one who rules
the whole earth,
and we that live here
are merely insects.
He spread out the heavens
like a curtain or an open tent.
23God brings down rulers
and turns them into nothing.
24They are like flowers
freshly sprung up
and starting to grow.
But when God blows on them,
they wilt and are carried off
like straw in a storm.
25The holy God asks,
“Who compares with me?
Is anyone my equal?”
26 Look at the evening sky!
Who created the stars?
Who gave them each a name?
Who leads them like an army?
The Lord is so powerful
that none of the stars
are ever missing.
The Lord Gives Strength
27You people of Israel say,
“God pays no attention to us!
He doesn't care if we
are treated unjustly.”
But how can you say that?
28Don't you know?
Haven't you heard?
The Lord is the eternal God,
Creator of the earth.
He never gets weary or tired;
his wisdom cannot be measured.
29The Lord gives strength
to those who are weary.
30Even young people get tired,
then stumble and fall.
31But those who trust the Lord
will find new strength.
They will be strong like eagles
soaring upward on wings;
they will walk and run
without getting tired.
translation_text:
Wɛ nɔɔna bam wó jwoori ba na dam
1Abam Tu Wɛ wom na tage tei to mo tento:
“Pa se a nɔɔna bam bochara taa tiga.
2Ŋɔɔne-na bochare-zuru taane de Jerusalem tiina bam,
se á ta de-ba we, ba totoŋ-chɛɛra maŋa kam ti.
Bere-ba we, Baŋa Wɛ kwei ba wɛleera mo
o yage o chɛ-ba.
O maŋe o waare-ba mo
se ko ma ko ŋwe ba jene dem kuni belei ko pa‑o.”
3Nɔɔno kwora mo tɔɔla ka we:
“Kagoa yuu ne mo á wó zaŋe á kwɛ chwoŋa kam
á pa dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ.
Nam pa-na se chwei selo o na wó tɔge te-kora jei ne to
fɔge se yɔɔre lanyerane.
4Jei selo maama na jege gwonnu to
jege se te suuri mo.
Jei selo maama na jege zwonnu de peero to
de maa wó guri te daare chwoŋa kam.
Tega kam mɛ na ba mae daane to
de maa wó palese ka maŋe daane.
5Konto mo wó pa Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom taa nae jaja,
se nabiina maama na-ko bedwe baŋa ne.
Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ ni delo to mo konto.”
6Nɔɔno mo tage o we, “Ta‑n tɔɔle n yaga!”
Amo de ma bwei a we, “A bwooli a ta we bɛ?”
Ta we: “Ko ná ye nabiina,
ba maama nye de gaaro mo.
Ba lam de ye ne punnu na nwoŋi gaao wone to mo.
Ba bere ba ba dáana ye ba toa.
7Gaaro tem wó kwaare mo
ye punnu tem de siiri,
Baŋa Wɛ na wó sii vio o yage te yera ne to ŋwaane.
Chega to, nabiina mo nam nye de gaaro tem konto.
8Gaaro tem wó seene te kwaare,
ye punnu tem de siiri.
Ko nam ná ye Wɛ kwora kam,
kanto wó taa wora mo ga wuu.”
9Zion, nmo jege kwor-ywoŋa se n tɔɔle!
Nam diini peo na tiini ko dɔra to yuu.
Jerusalem, kwei kwor-ywoŋa kam
n ta‑n bwooli n yaga wɛ-wɛ!
Ta‑n tɔɔle n yaga ye n ba fona.
Ta de Judah teene dedwonna dem we,
“Nii-na. Abam Tu Wɛ wom wora!”
10Nii-na! Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom maa beene de baare.
O nam tei nɔɔna de dam-fɔrɔ mo.
Nii-na. O jege o ŋweero mo o beena.
Nyɔɔre delo o na nɛ to ma to o yiga ne pa ba via.
11Dento nam mo ye nɔɔna balo o na kuri to.
O maa yere-ba ne nayero na nii o pei tei to.
O ta bukki pipeili sem mo o ja-kukworo ne,
ye o ja-se o ba o feiri o bochare ne.
Ko ta ná ye pi-ni selo na jege bia to,
o yeini o kale-se o vei mɛmɛ mo.
12Wɔ mo wane naneo na-fwaaro tem
o maŋe o ke o jaguli ne?
Wɔ mo wane o kwei o jeŋa
o maŋe wɛyuu kom maama o ti?
Wɔ nam mo wane tega kasolo kom maama
o la o ke tetɔgɔ wone,
ye o daare o kwei peero tem de zwonnu tem
o maŋe te dunni se o lɔre?
13Wɔ mo yi se o wane o lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa,
naa se kotu bere‑o o na wó ke tei?
14 Baŋa Wɛ jeini de wɔ mo se ba bane daane,
se kotu pa Baŋa Wɛ yi poore,
ye o daare o bere‑o chwoŋa kalo na ye chekke to?
Wɔ mo wane o pa Baŋa Wɛ yeino,
ye o daare o bere‑o se o taa ni wonnu kuri?
15 Baŋa Wɛ nii logo baŋa dwi tiina bam
ne ba ye na mo na lugi fee ba ke ware-zoŋa wone to.
Ba ta nye de kasolo bia mo
ba maŋe ba ke bɔŋa ne ye ka muri.
O ma maŋe teene delo na wo naneo kom ni ne to
ne de ye fwogo mo to.
16Lebanon vara bam muri
se ba kwei-ba ba ma ke zwɛɛm kaanem.
Ko teeni dem de ma muri se ba ma de dɛ sem
ba tɔre mini ba ma zwɛ kaanem dem konto.
17 Dwi-gɛ tiina bam maama ye kafɛ mo o yiga ne.
O nii ba maama we ba ye yɔɔ yerane mo,
ye ba ta ba jege kuri de fenfee de.
18Wɔ mo abam nam wó kwei á maŋe de Wɛ?
Bɛ nyenyego mo abam wó kwei á maŋe ded‑o?
19Ko ná ye jwoni, gɔgɔ mo wó mɔ-de,
ye luru de kwei sabu-seŋa o taare-de,
ye o daare o ma lu-nyenno o gɔgere de maama.
20Yiniga tu ná ware lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa o yi,
o wó beeri da-ŋoŋa kalo na ba pɔe to mo.
O maa wó ta de gɔgɔ
se kotu ke jwoni delo na ba toe tega ne to o pa‑o.
21Abam yeiri tento na?
Abam wo nigi ko ŋwa na?
Ba wo zege ko dɛ ne se ba ta de abam na?
Ko na zege logo boboa ne to,
abam wo nigi ko kuri na?
22 Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na jei mɛ na gaale tega kam baŋa
de wɛyuu kom to mo.
O maa nii nabiina ne ba ye manchwanno mo to.
O yɔɔre o lware wɛyuu kom ne gare-jale mo,
naa vwei delo o na zoore de wone to.
23Wonto mo wae o pae logo baŋa dedɛɛra jia,
ye pwa de yɔɔre ba jiri kafɛ.
24Ba nye de teeni delo ba na yɔɔre ba jeiri to mo.
Ba ná chwi-de tega kam ne,
ye de bonno ná wora te jaane tega,
mo Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se vio ba ko fuli-de
pa se de kwaare lela.
Ba ta nye de swanno mo
vo-kekara na kale ko ja viiri.
25Wo-pwoŋo Tu Wɛ wom mo bwei o we,
“Wɔ mo abam wó kwei á maŋe de amo?
Wɔ de amo mo wó taa mae daane?”
26Kwoni-na á yia á nii wɛɛne se á ta‑á bere-ne,
wɔ mo naane wonnu tem konto maama?
Ko ye Wɛ mo jaane chalechwe sem kɔgɔ kom dedoa dedoa o nwoŋa,
ye o bwoŋi chalechoa maama de ka yere.
Se dedoa tete wo fɔge ka jei,
o dam-fɔrɔ kom na dwoi woŋo maama to ŋwaane.
27Isarele tiina bam na ye Jakob dwi tiina to,
bɛ mo ye abam poona á we,
“Baŋa Wɛ yeiri kolo na ke debam to.”
Á ta ma‑á we,
“Baŋa Wɛ yiga tera debam wone.”
28Abam yeiri tento na?
Á wo nigi ko ŋwa na?
Baŋa Wɛ ye Wɛ wolo na wora taa wuu to mo.
Wonto mo naane logo baŋa de ko ni maama.
O ba buga.
O yera de nam ba chɛa.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba lɔre o yeino kom o tia.
29Ko ná ye balo yera na chɛ to,
o yeini o nyaare ba yera yam mo.
O ta maa pae balo na bugi to dam dem puli de ke da.
30Bu-donno tete wae ba buga ye ba yera chɛa.
Nɔn-donno de maa wae ba tiri ba toe tega ne.
31Ko nam ná ye balo teena na wo Baŋa Wɛ wone to,
ba dam dem yeini de jwoori de jiri dam-doore mo.
Ba wó zaŋe wɛɛne toge-toge,
ne maaro na yaare te vɔna tei to mo.
Ba ná duri tei maama de, ba yera bá chɛ.
Ba maa ná vei taa tei de, ba ba beira.

english_text:
The Lord Controls Human Events
1Be silent and listen,
every island in the sea.
Have courage and come near,
every one of you nations.
Let's settle this matter!
2Who appointed this ruler
from the east?
Who puts nations and kings
in his power?
His sword and his arrows
turn them to dust
blown by the wind.
3He goes after them so quickly
that his feet
barely touch the ground—
he doesn't even get hurt.
4Who makes these things happen?
Who controls human events?
I do! I am the Lord.
I was there at the beginning;
I will be there at the end.
5Islands and foreign nations
saw what I did and trembled
as they came near.
What Can Idols Do?
6Worshipers of idols
comfort each other,
saying, “Don't worry!”
7Woodcarvers, goldsmiths,
and other workers
encourage one another and say,
“We've done a great job!”
Then they nail the idol down,
so it won't fall over.
The Lord's Chosen Servant
8 Israel, you are my servant.
I chose you, the family
of my friend Abraham.
9From far across the earth
I brought you here and said,
“You are my chosen servant.
I haven't forgotten you.”
10Don't be afraid. I am with you.
Don't tremble with fear.
I am your God.
I will make you strong,
as I protect you with my arm
and give you victories.
11Everyone who hates you
will be terribly disgraced;
those who attack
will vanish into thin air.
12You will look around
for those brutal enemies,
but you won't find them—
they will be gone.
13I am the Lord your God.
I am holding your hand,
so don't be afraid.
I am here to help you.
14People of Israel, don't worry,
though others may say,
“Israel is only a worm!”
I am the holy God of Israel,
who saves and protects you.
15I will let you be like a log
covered with sharp spikes.
You will grind and crush
every mountain and hill
until they turn to dust.
16A strong wind will scatter them
in all directions.
Then you will celebrate
and praise me, your Lord,
the holy God of Israel.
The Lord Helps the Poor
17When the poor and needy
are dying of thirst
and cannot find water,
I, the Lord God of Israel,
will come to their rescue.
I won't forget them.
18I will make rivers flow
on mountain peaks.
I will send streams
to fill the valleys.
Dry and barren land
will flow with springs
and become a lake.
19I will fill the desert
with all kinds of trees—
cedars, acacias, and myrtles;
olive and cypress trees;
fir trees and pines.
20Everyone will see this
and know that I,
the holy Lord God of Israel,
created it all.
Idols Are Useless
21I am the Lord,
the King of Israel!
Come argue your case with me.
Present your evidence.
22Come near me, you idols.
Tell us about the past,
and we will think about it.
Tell us about the future,
so we will know
what is going to happen.
23Prove that you are gods
by making your predictions
come true.
Do something good or evil,
so we can be amazed
and terrified.
24You idols are nothing,
and you are powerless.
To worship you
would be disgusting.
25I, the Lord, appointed a ruler
in the north;
now he comes from the east
to honor my name.
He tramples kings like mud,
as potters trample clay.
26Did any of you idols predict
what would happen?
Did any of you get it right?
None of you told about this
or even spoke a word.
27I was the first to tell
the people of Jerusalem,
“Look, it's happening!”
I was the one who announced
this good news to Zion.
28None of these idols
are able to give advice
or answer questions.
29They are nothing,
and they can do nothing—
they are merely
a passing breeze.
translation_text:
Wɛ mo ye Isarele tiina bam zeinnu
1Teene delo na wo naneo kom ni ne to,
ta‑á ye chemm se á cheigi a taane!
Pa-na se tega baŋa dwi tiina bam beeri dam-doore
ba ke ba tete kuri ne,
se ba fɔɔre ba yi amo tei se dé ŋɔɔne taane.
Pa-na dé jeeri daane
se dé lɔre wolo na jege bora.
2Wɔ mo chiŋi wɛ-puli seeni pɛ wom,
ye o pa se o toŋe chega ŋwaane?
Kotu ma kwei teene o ke pɛ wom konto dam kuri ne,
pa se o nɔne ba pwa bam o se tega ne.
O ma kwei o se-zɔɔ o zeili-ba
pa ba jage ne kasolo mo jage,
ye o chena de kale-ba ya ja jei,
ne vio na ke weero tei to.
3O na pare-ba lela tei to
nye de o nɛ sem ba dwei tega mo tei.
O maa kɛ yiga, ye o tete wo nɛ zonne.
4Wɔ mo pɛ se wonnu tento maama ke,
ne o boboŋa na jaane se o ke tei to?
Wɔ mo tei dwi dedwe wora,
ye dedwoŋi saŋe de kwaga?
Ko ye amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tei konto maama.
Amo déem mo maŋe a wora boboa ne,
ye a ta wó taa wora kweelim maŋa ne.
5Naneo ni teene dem nɛ a na ke kolo to,
pa se foone ja-ba.
Logo baŋa jei maama nɔɔna yera tiini ya sae mo.
Ba ma ke daane ba fɔɔre ba ba.
6Ba maama woli daane mo,
ye nɔɔno maama tɛ de o faro we,
“Ke n tete n ke daane!”
7Gɔgɔ kolo na sare dɛ to wó woli
wolo na jege sabu-seŋa o gɔgere wonnu to,
se ba na dam ye ba ke jwoni ba zege.
Wolo de na kwei swoli o ma o kwɛ-de to
wó woli luru wom se ba na baare.
Ba maama wó ta ba bere daane we, “Dé kwaane.”
Ba laam maa wó kwei chena ba kwaare jwoni dem,
se de yé vwi de to tega ne.
8Abam Isarele tiina bam na ye Jakob dwi dem to,
á ye amo tontoŋena balo a na kuri a pa a tete to mo.
Abam maa ye amo badwoŋi Abaraham bia.
9A liiri abam a ja a nwoŋi tega baŋa gugworru tem ne mo.
A ma bwoŋi abam se á zege logo baŋa ni maama ne á ba.
A laam ma ta de nmo Jakob dwi dem we,
“Nmo ye amo tontoŋeno mo.
A nam na kuri nmo to, a wo ve‑m.”
10Nam yé ta‑n fona, se a wo n tei ne.
Yé ta‑n jage lwia, kokuri to, amo mo ye n Tu Wɛ wom.
Amo wó ke dam a ke n kuri ne,
ye a ta woli‑m.
A maa wó kwei a dam dem a toŋe de chega
se a ma a zeini‑m.
11Nii mo! Balo wo na wiiri de nmo to
wó na ba lɛɛro mo ye chaveera ja-ba.
Balo de nam na dwoni de nmo to wó jei mo.
12Nmo wó beeri balo na chiŋi nmo to
ye n bá‑n na-ba.
Balo ná done nmo,
banto yere mo lage de saare logo baŋa ne.
13Kokuri to, amo wolo na ye nmo Isarele dwi dem Tu Baŋa Wɛ to
mo yɔɔre a jege n jazem,
ye a tɛ de nmo we,
“Yé ta‑n fona, se amo wó woli‑m.”
14Jakob dwi dem, n seene n bwona
ne kanzwɛ na ye tei to mo.
Isarele tiina bam, nam yé ta‑á fona.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tɛ a we,
“A lage a woli abam mo.”
Amo wolo na ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom to mo ye á Jwoŋinu.
15Jakob dwi dem, a lage a pa se nmo ji ne
ferem luu-zɔŋɔ ba na tuuri mena baŋa ne to dwoŋi mo,
Ko maa ye wo-doŋo, ye ko jege chen-chechwɛ dedɛ.
Nmo laam ma‑n wó mage peero tem n chochoge,
ye n ta pa se zwonnu tem ji ne swanno dwoŋi.
16Abam wó dole-te á yage wɛɛne,
se vio kale ko ja jei.
Vo-dɛɔ mo lage ko pɛ-ba ko ja jage jei maama ne.
Nmo tete nam wó taa chaka de wopwolo Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane,
ye n ta ta‑n teera o baŋa ne,
o na ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom to ŋwaane.
17Yiniga tiina de nabwona beeri na mo ba ga se ba nyɔ.
Ba dindeilima ma ko na-nyɔm ŋwaane.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam wó leiri ba wɛ-lworo kom.
Amo mo ye Isarele tiina Wɛ wom,
ye a bá ve-ba a yage.
18Amo wó pa se bwi taa tole peero yuu ne se tua,
se buli-yia de taa tae ya nwoŋi bwollu tem ne.
A ta wó pa se kagoa pipiri ka ji jei selo bwi na daga da to,
se te-kora kam leiri ka taa ye mɛ buli-yia na gaale.
19Amo wó pa se Sedare teeni ke kagoa yuu ne,
se golesaa, de Motele, de Olivi teeni de nwoŋi dáane.
Tei-ŋonno de punnu dwi dwi mo wó nwoŋi
se te li te-kora kam maama.
20Nɔɔna laam maa wó na ko maama
ye ba lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ wom
na ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom to mo ke tento maama.
Ba ta wó jeeli ko maama ba nii
pa se ba ni ko kuri lanyerane.
21 Baŋa Wɛ na ye Jakob dwi dem pɛ wom to tɛ o we:
“Nam ja-na á taane á ba, se dé nii.
Ta-na á ni se dé cheigi.
22Pa se á jwona yam ba ya ta
ya bere debam kolo na lage ko ke to.
Ya jege se ya ta wonnu telo na ke te kɛ to
ya bere debam se dé lɔre ko ni ne,
ye dé daare dé lɔre te na lage te guri tei to.
Ya nam wó ta ya bere debam wonnu telo jwa na wó ke to.
23Konto mo wó pa dé wane dé sɛ we,
ya seene ya ye wa chekke.
Ke-na woŋo, ko ná ye lam naa balɔrɔ de,
se konto wó pa foone yɔɔre de ja debam.
24Abam nam ba jege nyɔɔre kolokolo baŋa ne,
ye á na ke wonnu telo to ye totoŋ-yɔɔro mo.
Balo na kuri se ba zuli abam to ye wo-zɔɔna mo!
25Amo nam chiŋi nɔɔno mo se o nwoŋi baŋa seeni
o ba o kwaare jara.
Wonto yeini o bwoi amo yere o zuli-ne mo.
O laam lage o zege wɛ-puli seeni mo o ba.
O maa wó chɔge teene dedɛɛra
ne nɔɔno na nɔne teero tei to.
O ta maa wó ke de-ba
ne kamɔ-mɔro na viiri o dɔgɔ tei to.
26Wɔ mo zege boboa kam ne o ta wonto taane,
se dé wane dé lɔre ko ni ne?
Wɔ mo wuuri o ta debam
se dé wane dé ta we, ‘O wo o chega wone’?
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo tage ko taane.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo pworisi-ko se dé ni.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo nigi taane abam ni ne.
27Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo lwoori yiga
se a ta de Zion tiina bam we, ‘Nii-ba-na!’
A ma toŋe ni-jwoŋinu se o vo Jerusalem
o bere-ba kwor-ywoŋa.
28A nam na nii jwona yam wone to,
a wo nɛ ya dedoa se de wane de bere swa.
Ya dedoa tete tera se de sɛ a beeri dem.
29Ya maama ye wo-yɔɔro mo!
Ya kikia ye kafɛ yerane ŋwaane mo.
Ya nyenyero de maa ba jege wolim kɔtaa,
ko yɔɔre ko nye de momwɛ vio mo to.”

english_text:
The Lord's Servant
1 Here is my servant!
I have made him strong.
He is my chosen one;
I am pleased with him.
I have given him my Spirit,
and he will bring justice
to the nations.
2He won't shout or yell
or call out in the streets.
3He won't break off a bent reed
or put out a dying flame,
but he will make sure
that justice is done.
4He won't quit or give up
until he brings justice
everywhere on earth,
and people in foreign nations
long for his teaching.
5 I am the Lord God.
I created the heavens
like an open tent above.
I made the earth and everything
that grows on it.
I am the source of life
for all who live on this earth,
so listen to what I say.
6 I chose you to bring justice,
and I am here at your side.
I selected you and sent you
to bring light
and my promise of hope
to the nations.
7You will give sight
to the blind;
you will set prisoners free
from dark dungeons.
8My name is the Lord!
I won't let idols or humans
share my glory and praise.
9Everything has happened
just as I said it would;
now I will announce
what will happen next.
Sing Praises to the Lord
10Tell the whole world to sing
a new song to the Lord!
Tell those who sail the ocean
and those who live far away
to join in the praise.
11Tell the tribes of the desert
and everyone in the mountains
to celebrate and sing.
12Let them announce
his praises everywhere.
13The Lord is marching out
like an angry soldier,
shouting with all his might
while attacking his enemies.
The Lord Will Help His People
14For a long time, I, the Lord,
have held my temper;
now I will cry out and groan
like a woman giving birth.
15I will destroy the mountains
and what grows on them;
I will dry up rivers and ponds.
16I will lead the blind on roads
they have never known;
I will guide them on paths
they have never traveled.
Their road is dark and rough,
but I will give light
to keep them from stumbling.
This is my solemn promise.
17Everyone who worships idols
as though they were gods
will be terribly ashamed.
God's People Won't Obey
18You people are deaf and blind,
but the Lord commands you
to listen and to see.
19No one is as blind or deaf
as his messenger,
his chosen servant,
20who sees and hears so much,
but pays no attention.
21The Lord always does right,
and so he wanted his Law
to be greatly praised.
22But his people were trapped
and imprisoned in holes
with no one to rescue them.
All they owned had been taken,
and no one was willing
to give it back.
23Why won't his people
ever learn to listen?
24Israel sinned and refused
to obey the Lord
or follow his instructions.
So the Lord let us be robbed
of everything we owned.
25He was furious with us
and punished our nation
with the fires of war.
Still we paid no attention.
We didn't even care
when we were surrounded
and scorched by flames.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno wom taane
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
1“Nii-na, amo tontoŋeno wolo a na teili to mo tento.
Wonto mo amo kuri, ye o kikia su a yi.
A nam kwei a Jworo mo a ke o wone.
O maa wó toŋe chega o pa logo baŋa dwi tiina maama.
2Wonto bá dɔne o kwora se o ke sɔɔ.
O bá taa pae o kwora zaŋa teo pwooni ne.
3Ko ná ye nanchan-gaa kalo na bwona to de,
o bere o bá bwori-ka.
O nam bá ja min-zwoŋo kolo nuga na ti to mini o dwei o yage.
O maa wó pa chega yi nɔɔna maama,
o tete na ye chega tu to ŋwaane.
4O bá ywori o chwoŋa kalo o na tɔge to wone,
naa o pa se o vɔna pare,
se ko yi o na pɛ se chega jwoŋi logo baŋa jei maama tei to.
Teene delo na wo naneo kom ni ne to
wó ke ba teena wonto bera yam wone mo.”
5Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ déem naane wɛyuu kom
ye o lware-ko pa ko tigi palalala.
O ta mo jare tega kam ni maama,
de wonnu telo na ŋwe te wo ka baŋa ne to.
O pae ka nabiina bam jege siu,
se ba taa jege ŋwea ba vei ka wone.
Wonto na tage kolo to mo tento:
6“Amo Baŋa Wɛ bwoŋi‑m mo se n pa chega taa toŋa.
Amo mo lage a ja n jeŋa se a taa teili‑m.
A ta wó tɔge nmo baŋa a ke ni-gwonim de nabiina,
ye a pa n ji pwooni n nye dwi-gɛ tiina bam baŋa ne.
7Nmo ma‑n wó puri lilwoa yia,
se n daare n pore peena diga
se balo ya na jei lim wone to nwoŋi pwooni.
8Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. A yere dem mo konto!
A nam bá sɛ se nɔɔn-nɔɔno tɔge o jwoŋi amo zula yam.
Jwona de nam bá na amo tia yam dwi.
9Nii-na! Wonnu telo a na wuuri a ta te taane to seene te ke.
Amo laam wó ŋɔɔne wo-donno taane mo.
Wonnu tento ta ná wo bobo se te ke mo,
a nam wó pa se á lɔre te ni ne.”
Leeni-na á seini Baŋa Wɛ
10Leeni-na leiŋ-doŋa se á ma‑á tei Baŋa Wɛ.
Zege-na logo baŋa ni maama ne á tei‑o.
Abam balo na zoore nabwooru wone á lɛɛne teene to,
de wonnu telo maama na wo naneo kom wone to,
ko woli de abam balo na zoore naneo ni teene dem ne to,
ta‑á zuli-na Baŋa Wɛ.
11Kagoa kam de ka teene dem maama wó tei‑o de kwor-dɛa mo,
ko woli de Kedare tiina na zoore jei selo ne to.
Balo na zoore Sela teo ne to wó taa chaka de wopwolo,
ye ba di peero yuu se ba taa bwooli ba yaga de ywoni.
12Sa-teena balo na zoore naneo kom ni ne to
wó taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ ye ba zeiŋi o yere wɛɛne.
13Ko ná ye Baŋa Wɛ, o yeini o nwoŋi mo
se o ke jara ne bembea na ke tei to.
O nam ná chichei se o zege,
o yera yɔɔre ya pepere mo se o ke jara yam.
O lage o kaase tiguri-kaasa mo,
ye o daare o di dam o dona baŋa ne.
Baŋa Wɛ tage o we:
14“A na peene a bane tei to tiini ko dáane.
A ya ta ye chemm mo taa.
A laam nam ti a yiga mo se a taa chwoosi a yage jei maama,
ne kaane wolo na wowole se o lo bu ye o keeri tei to.
15Amo lage a chɔge zwonnu de peero mo,
ye a daare a pa se gaaro de teeni maama kwaare te te.
A maa wó pa se bwi sem ji te-kore selo na na gilimi-se to,
ye a daare a pa se chwaro tem na bam we.
16Amo lage a vaŋe lilwoa bam mo
a pa ba tɔge chwei selo ba na maŋe ba yeiri to.
A maa wó pa se lim delo ba na vei de wone to
ji pwooni de pa-ba.
Chwei selo ya na tigi de gwonnu to
a wó pa se palese mo se pa-ba.
Amo wó yɔɔre a ke wonnu tento mo a pa-ba,
ye a bá dole-ba a yage.
17Ko nam ná ye balo na sale jwona yera ne to,
ba wó jwoori kwaga mo ye ba na ba chaveera.
Nɔɔna banto dwoŋi yeini ba tɛ de kamwaro telo na ye ba jwona to we,
‘Abam mo ye dé wa.’ ”
Isarele tiina bam ye zɔ-kɔro
18“Abam zɔ-kɔro tem, pore-na á zwa se á cheigi!
Abam lilwoa bam de taa fɔge á nii á nae!
19Lilwei nam daa ba dwoi amo tontoŋeno wom.
Zɔ-kɔgɔ de nam daa ba dwoi wolo amo na toŋe de a kwora to.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yia wo tiini ya dwei
ya dwoni wolo na sɛ amo to yia yam.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno wom yia yɔɔre ya dwei mo ko ja gaale.
20Isarele tiina bam, abam nɛ wonnu dedɛ,
ye á wo kwei-te á ke a yuni ne.
Abam ma‑á pore á zwa,
á nam wo nigi kolokolo.”
21 Baŋa Wɛ na zege o chega wone to,
o ya lage se o nia yam taa jege yuu de nenɔŋa nɔɔna tei ne.
22O nɔɔna bam dona nam mo wane-ba,
ye ba daare ba vere ba wonnu ba ja viiri.
Ba ma li ba maama ba yage gwon-chanlunnu
dedaane peena di wone.
Ba na jaane-ba konto to,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa tera se kotu jwoŋi-ba o yage.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se kotu ta we,
“Pa chwoŋa se ba jwoori.”
23Abam wɔ mo wó cheigi a taane dento?
Ko zege leile se ko taa via,
wɔ mo laam wó fɔge o cheigi?
24Wɔ mo yeigi Jakob dwi dem o pa nɔɔna
se ba wane-ba ba vere?
Isarele tiina bam seene ba to venverena jeŋa ne mo.
Ko nam ye Baŋa Wɛ tete mo ke konto.
Dé tusi dé chɔge wonto yiga mo.
O nɔɔna bam wo sɛ se ba tɔge o chwei sem
naa se ba ke o nia yam na bere tei to.
25Konto ŋwaane mo o bane tiini de fuli de-ba,
ye o pa se ba na chɔgem jara baŋa ne.
O bane dem jigi mini-vogo mo de li-ba,
ye ba ta wo nigi ko kuri.
De yɔɔre de zwɛ-ba mo,
ye ba wo zamese keim dem konto baŋa ne,
se ba kwei-ko ba ke ba boboŋa ne.

english_text:
The Lord Has Rescued His People
1Descendants of Jacob,
I, the Lord, created you
and formed your nation.
Israel, don't be afraid.
I have rescued you.
I have called you by name;
now you belong to me.
2When you cross deep rivers,
I will be with you,
and you won't drown.
When you walk through fire,
you won't be burned
or scorched by the flames.
3I am the Lord, your God,
the Holy One of Israel,
the God who saves you.
I gave up Egypt, Ethiopia,
and the region of Seba
in exchange for you.
4To me, you are very dear,
and I love you.
That's why I gave up nations
and people to rescue you.
5Don't be afraid! I am with you.
From both east and west
I will bring you together.
6I will say to the north
and to the south,
“Free my sons and daughters!
Let them return
from distant lands.
7They are my people—
I created each of them
to bring honor to me.”
The Lord Alone Is God
The Lord said:
8Bring my people together.
They have eyes and ears,
but they can't see or hear.
9Tell everyone of every nation
to gather around.
None of them can honestly say,
“We told you so!”
If someone heard them say this,
then tell us about it now.
10My people, you are my witnesses
and my chosen servant.
I want you to know me,
to trust me, and understand
that I alone am God.
I have always been God;
there can be no others.
11I alone am the Lord;
only I can rescue you.
12I promised to save you,
and I kept my promise.
You are my witnesses
that no other god did this.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
13I am God now and forever.
No one can snatch you from me
or stand in my way.
The Lord Will Prepare the Way
14I, the Lord, will rescue you!
I am Israel's holy God,
and this is my promise:
For your sake, I will send
an army against Babylon
to drag its people away,
crying as they go.
15I am the Lord, your holy God,
Israel's Creator and King.
16I am the one who cut a path
through the mighty ocean.
17I sent an army to chase you
with chariots and horses;
now they lie dead,
unable to move.
They are like an oil lamp
with the flame snuffed out.
Forget the Past
The Lord said:
18Forget what happened long ago!
Don't think about the past.
19I am creating something new.
There it is! Do you see it?
I have put roads in deserts,
streams in thirsty lands.
20Every wild animal honors me,
even jackals and owls.
I provide water in deserts—
streams in thirsty lands
for my chosen people.
21I made them my own nation,
so they would praise me.
22I, the Lord, said to Israel:
You have become weary of me,
but not from worshiping me.
23You have not honored me
by sacrificing sheep
or other animals.
And I have not burdened you
with demands for sacrifices
or sweet-smelling incense.
24You have not brought
delicious spices for me
or given me the best part
of your sacrificed animals.
Instead, you burden me down
with your terrible sins.
25But I wipe away your sins
because of who I am.
And so, I will forget
the wrongs you have done.
26Meet me in court!
State your case and prove
that you are right.
27Your earliest ancestor
and all your leaders
rebelled against me.
28That's why I don't allow
your priests to serve me;
I let Israel be destroyed
and your people disgraced.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ wó jwoŋi o nɔɔna o yage
1Jakob dwi dem na ye Isarele tiina to,
Baŋa Wɛ mo naane abam pa se á wora.
O nam na tage tei to mo tento:
“Yé ta‑á fona, se a jwoŋi abam mo a pa a tete.
A ma bwoŋi abam dedoa dedoa de á yera.
Konto ŋwaane, á ye amo nyem mo.
2Abam ná tɔge na-luŋa wone mo se á bɛ,
amo wó taa wo á tei ne.
Á nam ná tɔge bwi wone se á bɛ mo de,
se na bam bá lini abam.
Ko nam ná ye mini wone mo á tɔge da á vei de,
de bá zwɛ abam.
De nam bá zaŋe bugi-bugi se de di abam.
3Kokuri to, amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.
A maa ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom na ye á Jwoŋinu to.
Amo mo kwei Ejipti teo a pa
se abam wane á ta‑á tei á tete.
A nam ta kwei Kusi de Sebaa teene dem de a pa
se a jwoŋi abam a yage.
4Amo wó ga teene dedɛ de nabiina dwi maama
se ko pa a vere abam se á ta‑á jege á ŋwea.
Kokuri to, abam tiini á jege kuri á pa-ne,
ye a tiini a swoi abam mo.
5Nam yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone, se amo wo á tei ne.
A maa wó ja á bia bam á zege wɛ-puli seeni a ba,
ye a daare a la abam badwonna
a ja a nwoŋi wɛ-zoore seeni se a ke abam daane.
6Amo wó ta de baŋa seeni teene dem we,
‘Yage a nɔɔna bam se ba viiri!’
A ta wó ta de tega-kuri seeni teene dem we,
‘Yé che-na ba yiga.’
Pa-na se a bia bam nwoŋi yiga yiga teene dem ne ba ba.
Ta pa-na se a bukwa bam de zege tega baŋa ni maama ne ba ba.
7Banto ye amo nɔɔna balo a na mae a yere mo a bwoi-ba.
A na naane-ba to, a kuri se a tɔge ba baŋa mo
a ma na nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ.”
8Nam ja nɔɔna balo na jege yia ye ya ba nae,
ye ba ta jege zwa yalo na ba ni to,
n pa ba zege amo yiga ne.
9Ta de dwi maama tiina se ba jeeri daane,
se tega baŋa nɔɔna bam la ba ke da-yiga ne.
Banto wone wɔ mo lwoori yiga o ta wonnu tento taane
se te laam ba te ke?
Ba nam ba de ba maana-para se ko bere we ba jege chega,
se nɔɔna badaara de sɛ ye ba ta we, “Chega mo ba tɛa.”
10 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Nmo Isarele dwi dem nam mo wó zege amo chega kam kwaga ne.
N ma‑n ye a tontoŋeno wolo a na kuri to.
Konto mo wó pa se n lɔre we amo mo ye kotu,
se ko pa n ke n wo-dedoa de amo.
Nmo ma‑n wó ni ko kuri we
amo mo ye Wɛ chekke.
Wɛ dedwoŋi ya maŋe de tera,
se amo laam taa wora.
Wɛ nam tera de na wó saŋe amo kwaga se de taa wora.
11Amo yerane mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.
Amo yiga ná le, jwoŋinu nam daa tera.
12Amo mo ya gwoni ni de abam se a jwoŋi abam a yage,
ye a seene a ke a su a ni-gwonim dem.
Ko ye amo tete mo,
se ko dae wɛ-gaa mo wo á tetare ne.
Á maa ye balo na wó zege a chega kam kwaga ne we,
a seene a ye Wɛ chekke to mo.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
13“Chega to, ko na maŋe ko nwoŋi faŋa to
de amo ye Wɛ mo chekke.
Amo ná jege wolo de a jeŋa,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware kotu se o jwoŋi o yage.
A nam ná chwi kolo,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware se o gɔ-ko o yage.”
Wɛ wó duri Isarele tiina yibwona
14 Baŋa Wɛ mo ye abam Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom de á Jwoŋinu. O nam na tage tei to mo tento:
“Abam ŋwaane mo a lage a toŋe jar-keira se ba li Babilon teo,
se ba daare ba ja ko nɔɔna bam ba kale ba ja viiri.
Babilon tiina bam wopwolo sɔɔ
laam wó leiri ko ji wo-chechɔgɔ keira mo.
15Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye abam Wo-pwoŋo Tu to.
A maa ye wolo na naane abam Isarele tiina bam,
ye a ta ye á Pɛ.”
16 Baŋa Wɛ mo ye wolo na pɛ se
chwoŋa peini naneo kom wone,
ka na tigi na-fwaaro tem tetare ne to.
17O ma soge jar-keira dedɛ kɔgɔ,
de ba jara-keim torokooro, de ba sisein-nɔɔna,
pa se ba maama tu ba maŋe na bam wone.
Ba yɔɔre ba to mo, se ba daa yé zaŋe wɛɛne.
Ba maama jilli jei mo,
ne ba na fuli min-zwoŋo mini ba dwei tei to.
Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
18“Swei-na faŋa wonnu telo na ke te kɛ to swia.
Yé ta‑á guli-na wo-dwonnu gula.
19Nii-na, amo lage a ke wo-doŋo mo!
Keim dem nam bobo mo de wora de ke.
Abam ba lɔre ko ni ne na?
A lage a pa se chwoŋa mo peini kagoa yuu ne,
se bu-nwaro de peini te-kora jei sem ne.
20Kago-vara bam maama wó zuli-ne,
ko woli de nywoŋ-kuri, de kunkworru.
Kokuri to, amo wó pa se na taa bura kagoa kam yuu ne,
ye bu-nwaro de taa tigi da,
se amo nɔɔna balo a na kuri to nyɔ ba su.
21Banto mo ye balo a na naane a pa a tete
se ba taa leeni ba seini amo to.
22Jakob dwi dem na ye Isarele tiina to,
abam nam wo bwoŋi a yere se a woli abam.
Á ta wo sɛ se ko chɛ á yera amo ŋwaane.
23Abam wo jaane á pei á ba
se á ma á ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra á pa-ne.
Á maa wo ke kaanem se á ma á zuli amo.
Amo wo fe abam se á ja wodiu pɛɛra á ba á pa-ne,
naa se á zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa á ma á zuli-ne.
24Á wo kwei á sabia á yeigi nu-ywoŋa
se á ma á zuli-ne.
Á ta wo kwei á vara lara kam á pa-ne
se ko pa a di ywoni ko ŋwaane.
Abam nam pɛ se a yera chɛ de á wɛleera yam mo,
ye á ta pa se a yia gigili de á tusim kikia yam.
25De konto maama de, amo Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo
ye wolo na saare á wɛleera yam a yage to.
Ko nam ye amo tete ŋwaane mo a ke konto.
A nam daa bá guli á wɛleera yam gula.
26Pa-na se dé jeeri dé ŋɔɔne se dé maŋe daane.
Pa-na se a guli kolo na ke ko kɛ to gula.
Tole-na taane dem se dé lɔre
á seene á wo á chega wone na?
27Boboa ne to, á nabaaro wom déem wo wɛleera wone mo.
Á yiga tiina bam de ma nwoŋi amo kwaga ne.
28Konto ŋwaane mo a lage a pa á kaanem tiina
balo na kweere de ba totoŋa to di ba chaveera.
A ta wó yɔɔre a chɔge Isarele dwi tiina bam,
se nɔɔna maama taa jege-ba ba yaala.”

english_text:
The Lord's Promise to Israel
1People of Israel,
I have chosen you
as my servant.
2I am your Creator.
You were in my care
even before you were born.
Israel, don't be terrified!
You are my chosen servant,
my very favorite.
3I will bless the thirsty land
by sending streams of water;
I will bless your descendants
by giving them my Spirit.
4They will spring up like grass
or like willow trees
near flowing streams.
5They will worship me
and become my people.
They will write my name
on the back of their hands.
6 I am the Lord All-Powerful,
the first and the last,
the one and only God.
Israel, I have rescued you!
I am your King.
7Can anyone compare with me?
If so, let them speak up
and tell me now.
Let them say what has happened
since I made my nation
long ago,
and let them tell
what is going to happen.
8Don't tremble with fear!
Didn't I tell you long ago?
Didn't you hear me?
I alone am God—
no one else is a mighty rock.
Idols Can't Do a Thing
The Lord said:
9Those people who make idols
are nothing themselves,
and the idols they treasure
are just as worthless.
Worshipers of idols are blind,
stupid, and foolish.
10Why make an idol or an image
that can't do a thing?
11Everyone who makes idols
and all who worship them
are mere humans,
who will end up
sadly disappointed.
Let them face me in court
and be terrified.
Idols and Firewood
12A metalworker shapes an idol
by using a hammer
and heat from the fire.
In his powerful hand
he holds a hammer,
as he pounds the metal
into the proper shape.
But he gets hungry and thirsty
and loses his strength.
13Some woodcarver measures
a piece of wood,
then draws an outline.
The idol is carefully carved
with each detail exact.
At last it looks like a person
and is placed in a temple.
14Either cedar, cypress, oak,
or any tree from the forest
may be chosen.
Or even a pine tree planted
by the woodcarver
and watered by the rain.
15 Some of the wood is used
to make a fire for heating
or for cooking.
One piece is made into an idol,
then the woodcarver bows down
and worships it.
16He enjoys the warm fire
and the meat that was roasted
over the burning coals.
17Afterwards, he bows down
to worship the wooden idol.
“Protect me!” he says.
“You are my god.”
18Those who worship idols are stupid and blind! 19They don't have enough sense to say to themselves, “I made a fire with half of the wood and cooked my bread and meat on it. Then I made something worthless with the other half. Why worship a block of wood?”
20How can anyone be stupid enough to trust something that can be burned to ashes? No one can save themselves like that. Don't they realize that the idols they hold in their hands are not really gods?
The Lord Won't Forget His People
21People of Israel,
you are my servant,
so remember all of this.
Israel, I created you,
and you are my servant.
I won't forget you.
22Turn back to me!
I have rescued you
and swept away your sins
as though they were clouds.
Sing Praises to the Lord
23Tell the heavens and the earth
to start singing!
Tell the mountains
and every tree in the forest
to join in the song!
The Lord has rescued his people;
now they will worship him.
The Lord Created Everything
24Israel, I am your Lord,
the source of your life,
and I have rescued you.
I created everything
from the sky above
to the earth below.
25 I make liars of false prophets
and fools of fortunetellers.
I take human wisdom
and turn it into nonsense.
26I will make the message
of my prophets come true.
They are saying, “Jerusalem
will be filled with people,
and the Lord will rebuild
the towns of Judah.”
27I am the one who commands
the sea and its streams
to run dry.
28 I am also the one who says,
“Cyrus will lead my people
and obey my orders.
Jerusalem and the temple
will be rebuilt.”
translation_text:
Isarele tiina ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem
1“Jakob dwi dem a na kuri a pa a tete to, nam cheigi.
Isarele dwi dem, nmo mo ye a tontoŋeno.
2Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo naane‑m a ke n nu puga ne,
ye a ta wó woli‑m.
Amo nam na tage tei to mo tento:
Amo tontoŋeno Jakob, yé ta‑n fona.
Kokuri to, a kuri Isarele tiina bam
se á ta‑á ye a nɔn-swonnu mo.
3Amo wó lwo na dedɛ te-kora baŋa ne,
pa se bu-nwaro taa duri jei sem konto ne.
A maa wó pa se a Jworo ba á bia baŋa ne,
ye a daare a swɛ ba swolim.
4Banto wó puli ne ga-lɛɛro na puli tei to mo,
de teeni delo na zege bwi ni ne to.
5Ba wone nɔɔno dedoa wó ta we,
‘Baŋa Wɛ mo tei amo’.
Wodwoŋi de wó taa jege Jakob yere dem,
o ma o bwoi o tete.
Wodwoŋi de maa wó popone o jeŋa ne we,
‘Baŋa Wɛ nyem,’
ye o daare o ta we, o nwoŋi Isarele dwi dem wone mo.”
Jwona ba jege kuri, se Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo
6Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ye Isarele dwi tiina bam Pɛ mo de ba Jwoŋinu. O nam na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo mo ye boboa kam de gurim tu.
Amo yiga ná le, wɛ nam daa tera.
7Wɔ mo wó kwei o tete o maŋe de amo?
O ná wora, se o bwooli taane dem.
Kotu nam ba o zege a yiga ne o ta se dé cheigi.
Ko zege faŋa kam ne a na kuri dwi delo se ba taa ye a nɔɔna to,
o nam jege se o ta kolo na maŋe ko ke to
ko woli de kolo na wó ke jwa seeni to se dé lɔre.
Ɛɛ, pa se kotu ta wonnu telo na beene to.
8A nɔɔna bam, yé ta‑á pa se á yera sae.
Nam yé ta‑á fona-na.
A wo wuuri a ta wonnu tem konto taane
a bere abam mo na?
Abam nam mo wó zege amo chega kam kwaga ne.
Wɛ dedwoŋi nam daa mo wora
ye ko dae amo na?
Aawo! Peo kodwoŋi daa tera se nɔɔna dale da.
Amo yeiri dedoa tete ni ne.”
9Balo maama na gɔgere jwona to ba jege kuri. Jwona yalo ba na pa-ya chega to de ye wo-yɔɔro mo. Balo na zege ya kwaga ne to ye lilwoa mo, ye ba yeiri kolo wone ba na wora to. Konto ŋwaane ba wó na ba chaveera.
10Wɔ mo boŋe se o mɔ jwoni o pa de ji o wɛ? De bere de bá pa o na nyɔɔre. 11Nii-na! Nɔɔno wom konto de o dwi maama wó di ba chaveera. Gwaro telo na ke jwona to maa ye nabiina yerane. Ba nam jege se ba ba ba zege amo yiga ne se dé ŋɔɔne. Foone yerane mo wó ja-ba ye ba ta di ba chaveera.
12Luru mo yeini o kwei o yɔrɔ kom zela o ma o gɔgere luu mini wone. O ma kwei swoli mo o mage luu kom de o dam, se ko ji jwoni nyenyego na ye tei to. O kana laam maa wae ye na-nyɔm jege‑o pa se o bugi ye o dam de ti.
13Gɔgɔ kolo na sare dɛ to de ma yeini o maŋe daa. O ma bei bibeira daa kam yera ne se ko bere jwoni nyenyego. O laam maa wó kwei o totoŋa zela o ma o sare daa kam, ye o daare o swolisi. O ma ke ka nyenyego kom pa ko lwoni nabiinu nyenyego, ye ko jege nabiinu lam dem. O laam wó kwei-ka o vo o zege ka diga wone.
14Gɔgɔ kom wae o kuri dɛ dwi dwi wone se o ma o ke jwoni dem. O wó wane o zo goa wone o gwoni Sedare tio o de tega ne, naa loa, naa kantɔŋɔ, naa tei-zɔŋɔ kolo maama. Ko ná dae konto, o tete mo wó jeiri tio, ye doa laam ne ko baŋa ne pa ko be kamunu. 15Kotu ná gwoni daa kanto dwoŋi, o laam wó kwei ka chichworo mo o ma o wiiri mini, ye o daare o kwei ka chichworo o ke jwoni. Konto to, o tɔge ka chichworo baŋa ne o weeri mini, naa o ma o wɔ bworobworo. O ta ma kwei ka chichworo kom o gɔgere jwoni se o taa zula. 16O yeini o twori dɛ sem wone o dwéi mini, ye o daare o ma mini dem o wɔ nɔna, pa se o done o su. O ta ma yeini o weeri mini de dɛ sem ye o we, “Aha! Nii mini dem na lana tei! A yera ye ŋwamm!” 17Dɛ selo na daare to mo o wó ma o ke jwoni. O laam ma yeini o tiiri de yiga ne o zuli-de. O ma lwoori wolim de tei ne ye o we, “Jwoŋi-ne n yage, se nmo mo ye amo wɛ.”
18Nɔɔna banto dwoŋi nam yeiri kolokolo. Ba bere ba ba ni wonnu kuri. Ba yia yam kwoni mo pa se ya ba nae kolokolo. Ba boboŋa de kwaale mo de chega kam. 19Ba ba fɔge ba jeeli wonnu. Ba wone wolowolo ba boŋe o yi se o ta we, “A kwei da kam chichworo mo a ma a dwéi mini. A ma wɔ bworobworo mini dem wulim wone. A ta wɔge nɔna wulim dem wone a done. A nam wó wane a kwei ka chichworo kolo na daare to a ma a ke jwo-yɔɔ na? Amo wó tiiri a zuli da-kwolo mo na?”
20Nɔn-jworo konto dwoŋi boboŋa gane‑o mo. Ko nye de o ni-wodiu ye tentwarem mo. O maa ware o tete o jwoŋi. O bá ta de o tete we, “Nii woŋo kolo a na zei a jazem ne to. Ko ba jege-ne ko gana mo na?”
Baŋa Wɛ jwoŋi o nɔɔna o yage
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
21“Abam Isarele tiina bam nam guli-na wonnu tento gula.
Kokuri to, nmo Jakob dwi dem ye amo tontoŋeno mo.
Amo mo naane‑m pa se n ye a tontoŋeno.
Isarele tiina bam, amo bá swei abam swia.
22A kale á wɛleera yam a pa ya jei
ne kunkwonnu na duri te kɛ tei to mo,
naa tetete nyɔnɔ na jei tei to.
Jwoori-na á ba amo tei,
se amo mo vere abam a pa a tete.”
23Wɛyuu jei sem maama,
bage-na á yage de wopwolo!
Tega kuri gugworru tem de,
ta‑á bwoola á yage jei maama ne.
Peero tem, de teeni delo maama na wo goa wone to,
ta‑á chake-na de ywoni.
Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ mo vere Jakob dwi dem o pa o tete,
se o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom taa nae jaja Isarele tiina bam tetare ne.
24 Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na vere nmo mo o pa o tete.
Wonto nam mo naane‑m o ke n nu puga ne.
O na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom na ke wonnu maama to.
Amo mo lware wɛyuu kom a tete ne
pa se ko tigi palalala.
A daa ta ma jare tega kam ni maama a tiŋi a tete ne.
25Amo mo pae vora ni taane jiri kafɛ,
ye daare a pae yi-nara jworim dem bere jaja.
A yeini a pa swa tiina jwoori kwaga mo,
se ba yeino maama taa ba jege kuri.
26Ko daare, ko ná ye amo tete tontoŋena,
a yeini a pa se ba taane jege kuri mo.
A ta maa ke a sui a tontoŋena na bere wonnu telo to.
Amo nam mo tɛ Jerusalem teo taane we,
‘Nɔɔna wó taa zoore ko wone.’
Ko ta ná ye Judah teene dedwonna dem,
a maa we, ‘Ba wó fɔge ba lɔ-de mo ba zege,
pa se de di-dwonnu jwoori te ji sɔ-ŋonno.’
27A maa tɛ de naneero tem we, te na bam we,
se bu-nwaro tem de we.
28Ko ta ná ye Pɛ Sarusi, a maa tɛ o taane we,
‘O ye nayero mo o toŋe o pa-ne.
O jege se o ke o su amo boboŋa na dɛ se o ke tei to mo.’
Wonto laam maa wó pa ni we,
‘Fɔge á lɔ-na Jerusalem teo kom á zege.’
O nam wó ta Wɛ diga kam taane we,
‘Chwi-na ka kabiri-beira kam.’ ”

english_text:
Cyrus Obeys the Lord's Commands
1The Lord said to Cyrus, his chosen one:
I have taken hold
of your right hand
to help you capture nations
and remove kings from power.
City gates will open for you;
not one will stay closed.
2As I lead you,
I will level mountains
and break the iron bars
on bronze gates of cities.
3I will give you treasures
hidden in dark
and secret places.
Then you will know that I,
the Lord God of Israel,
have called you by name.
4Cyrus, you don't even know me!
But I have called you by name
and highly honored you
because of Israel,
my chosen servant.
5Only I am the Lord!
There are no other gods.
I have made you strong,
though you don't know me.
6Now everyone from east to west
will learn that I am the Lord.
No other gods are real.
7I create light and darkness,
happiness and sorrow.
I, the Lord, do all this.
8Tell the heavens
to send down justice
like showers of rain.
Prepare the earth
for my saving power
to sprout and produce justice
that I, the Lord, create.
The Lord's Mighty Power
The Lord said:
9 Israel, you have no right
to argue with your Creator.
You are merely a clay pot
shaped by a potter.
The clay doesn't ask,
“Why did you make me this way?
Where are the handles?”
10Children don't have the right
to demand of their parents,
“What have you done
to make us what we are?”
11I am the Lord, the Creator,
the holy God of Israel.
Do you dare question me
about my own nation
or about what I have done?
12I created the world
and covered it with people;
I stretched out the sky
and filled it with stars.
13I have done the right thing
by placing Cyrus in power,
and I will make the roads easy
for him to follow.
I am the Lord All-Powerful!
Cyrus will rebuild my city
and set my people free
without being paid a thing.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Alone Can Save
14My people, I, the Lord, promise
that the riches of Egypt
and the treasures of Ethiopia
will belong to you.
You will force into slavery
those tall people of Seba.
They will bow down and say,
“The only true God is with you;
there are no other gods.”
15People of Israel,
your God is a mystery,
though he alone can save.
16Anyone who makes idols
will be confused
and terribly disgraced.
17But Israel, I, the Lord,
will always keep you safe
and free from shame.
Everyone Is Invited
18The Lord alone is God!
He created the heavens
and made a world
where people can live,
instead of creating
an empty desert.
The Lord alone is God;
there are no others.
19The Lord did not speak
in a dark secret place
or command Jacob's descendants
to search for him in vain.
The Lord speaks the truth,
and this is what he says
20to every survivor
from every nation:
“Gather around me!
Learn how senseless it is
to worship wooden idols
or pray to helpless gods.
21“Why don't you get together
and meet me in court?
Didn't I tell you long ago
what would happen?
I am the only God!
There are no others.
I bring about justice,
and have the power to save.
22“I invite the whole world
to turn to me and be saved.
I alone am God!
No others are real.
23 I have made a solemn promise,
one that won't be broken:
Everyone will bow down
and worship me.
24They will admit that I alone
can bring about justice.
Everyone who is angry with me
will be terribly ashamed
and will turn to me.
25I, the Lord, will give
victory and great honor
to the people of Israel.”
translation_text:
Peresia teo pɛ Sarusi taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei de o dam tu Sarusi wolo o na kuri to mo tento:
“Amo mo jaane n jazem se a woli‑m
se n wane n di teene dedɛ,
se n daare n vere ba pwa bam jara zela.
A ta wó pa‑m dam se n pore teene ni-bworru
se n wane de wo n zo,
ye ba daa ware ba che n chwoŋa.
2A nam wó to nmo yiga ne,
ye a palese peero a tiŋi a pa‑m.
Amo wó bwori channa ni-bworru tem se n zo,
ye a daare a gwoni te luuru tem a de tega ne.
3A ta wó kwei jejegero telo ya na tigi lim wone to a le a pa nmo.
Wonnu telo nɔɔna na tiŋi gugworru wone jwa ŋwaane to mo konto.
Konto mo wó pa se n lɔre we,
amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina bam Wɛ to.
A ma bwoŋi‑m de n yere.
4Ko ye a tontoŋeno Jakob dwi dem
na ye Isarele tiina bam a na kuri to ŋwaane mo,
a yɔɔre a bwoŋi nmo yere.
N nam ta wo sɛ n pa amo.
De konto de a kwei yere-kamunu mo a pa‑m.
5Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ,
ye wɛ dedwoŋi wo woli amo wone.
Amo yiga ná le, wɛ nam daa tera.
Amo wó taa pa‑m dam,
de n na wo lɔre amo to de.
6Ko na zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko vo ko yi wɛ-zoore seeni to,
nɔɔna wó lɔre we, wɛ dedwoŋi daa tera ko ná dae amo yerane.
Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ,
ye wɛ dedwoŋi wo woli amo wone.
7Amo mo ke pwooni ye a ta pa lim wora.
A maa pae nɔɔna yazura ye a jaane chanɛɛre de a tui.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam mo pae wonnu tem konto maama ke.
8Wɛyuu kom maama, pa se doa taa nena.
Se chega taa toŋe tega baŋa ne,
ne kunkwonnu tem na siiri de doa tei to.
Nam pa se tega baŋa ni maama de pore dedɛ,
se verem de nɔn-ŋonne ta te nwoŋi ka wone,
ye te yɔɔre te be tega kam baŋa ne.
Ko ye amo Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ ko ke konto.
9Lɛɛro wó yi wolo na mage kantɔgɔ de o keiru to.
Kotu nye de kanchua mo na gwaane de kanchwi sedwonna
ye se maama tigi tega ne to.
Dɔgɔ ba jege chwoŋa se ko bwei kamɔ-mɔro we,
‘Bɛ mo ye n ke-ne tento?’
Ko bá ta ded‑o we,
‘N totoŋa yam ba lana.’
10Lɛɛro wó yi bu wolo na wó ta de o kwo we,
‘Bu dwi dɔ mo tento n loga?’
naa wolo na wó ta de o nu we,
‘N virigi puga se n lo bɛ woŋo mo tento?’”
11 Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom
ye o ta ye ba Keiru to na tage tei mo tento:
“Ko ná ye wonnu telo na wó ke jwa seeni to,
bɛ mo ye á bwei amo se ko tɔge a bia bam seeni?
Bɛ mo ye á bere amo a na jege se a ke kolo
de balo a tete je na ke to?
12Amo mo ke logo baŋa
ye a daare a naane nabiina a ke da.
Amo tete mo kwei a je a lware wɛyuu kom
pa se ko tigi palalala.
A laam ma tigisi chalechwe sem de se kɔgɔ kom maama.
13Ko ta ná ye Sarusi, a lage a chiŋi‑o mo se o ke keim,
pa se chega taa toŋa.
A maa wó to o yiga ne se a pa o totoŋa ke mɔle ya pa‑o.
O wó fɔge o lɔ amo tete teo Jerusalem,
ye o daare o vere a nɔɔna balo ya na wo sa-teo ne to
pa se ba taa tei ba tete,
De ko de, o ba lage o toŋe ŋweero ŋwaane.”
Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
Isarele tiina taane
14 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Ko ná ye Ejipti tiina bam, de Kusi tiina bam,
de Sabea tiina bam na ye nɔn-dedwaaro to,
banto maama wó ba ba to ba pa abam.
Ba nam ta wó ja ba pipiu zela de ba jejegero
ba ba ba pa te ji á nyem.
Ba wó ba ba tɔge á kwaga de ba nɛ chegero,
ye ba ke ba tete á jeŋa ne.
Ba maama wó tiiri abam yiga ne,
ye ba lwoori abam we,
‘Wɛ mo seene o wora abam tei ne,
se wɛ dedwoŋi nam daa tera.’ ”
15Isarele tiina Wɛ wom na ye dé Vereno to,
nmo seene n ye Wɛ wolo na yeini o seigi o tete to mo.
16Ko ná ye balo maama na ke jwona ba zege to,
chaveera wó di-ba mo, ye nɔɔna de yaale-ba.
Ba maama lage ba tɔge daane ba na ba lɛɛro mo.
17Ko nam ná ye Isarele tiina bam,
Baŋa Wɛ tete nam mo lage o jwoŋi-ba o yage.
Á verem dem wó taa ye verem chekke na wora taa wuu to.
Abam daa bá na á chaveera, ye ba nam bá yaale abam,
se ko taa vei maŋa na ba ti to.
18Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na naane wɛyuu maama to mo.
Wonto mo ye Wɛ chekke.
O ma jeeli logo kom na wó taa ye tei to ye o ke-ko.
O ta ma chwi ko kuri.
O na naane-ko konto to,
o wo ke-ko se ko taa ye yɔɔ yerane.
O nam ke se nɔɔna mo taa zoore ko wone.
Wonto na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.
Wɛ dedwoŋi daa wo woli amo wone.
19A wo tage taane a seigi.
A nam wo ke na a ni ne se a ta taane.
A wo tage de Jakob dwi dem we,
‘Beeri-na amo kafɛ ŋwaane.’
Amo Baŋa Wɛ wom, a ŋɔɔne chega taane mo.
A maa ná pɛ a ni, de ye chega mo.
20Nam la-na daane se á ba amo tei.
Abam dwi-gɛ tiina balo na wane á lu jara yam wone to
ba-na á jeeri daane.
Ko ná ye jwona yalo nɔɔna na mɛ dɛ ba ke to,
balo na zeŋe-ya ba kare ba beeri to boboŋa tera.
Kokuri to, ba zuli wa yalo na ware nɔɔna
se ya jwoŋi ya yage to mo.
21Ba-na á tole taane dem se dé nii kolo na wora to.
Pa-na se ba bane daane ba nii ba na wó ta kolo to.
Wɔ mo wuuri o ta tento faŋa faŋa o pa ko nwoŋi pwooni.
Wɔ déem mo bwooli-ko o yage?
Ko dae amo Baŋa Wɛ mo na?
Wɛ dedwoŋi wo woli amo wone,
de na jege chega ye de ta ye jwoŋinu.
Amo yiga ná le, wɛ nam daa tera.
22Logo baŋa jei sem maama nɔɔna,
pipiri-na á ba amo tei,
se a jwoŋi abam a yage.
Kokuri to, amo mo ye Wɛ chekke,
se wɛ dedwoŋi daa tera.
23Amo nam dugi de a tete yere mo.
A ni ma puri de da a chega kam ŋwaane
de ta kwora kalo daa na ba kwana to we:
Nabiina maama wó ba ba kuni nadwoona amo yiga ne.
Ba maama wó puri ba nia ba sɛ ba pa amo mo.
24Ba maa wó ta amo taane we,
‘Baŋa Wɛ yerane wone mo
chega de dam maama wora.’ ”
Balo maama nam na chuli Wɛ to
wó ba o yiga ne ba di ba chaveera.
25 Baŋa Wɛ nam wó pa se Isarele dwi tiina maama na ba bora,
ye ba de wó taa jege teera Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_text:
Babylonia's Gods Are Helpless
The Lord said:
1The gods Bel and Nebo
are down on their knees,
as wooden images of them
are carried away
on weary animals.
2They are down on their knees
to rescue the heavy load,
but the images are still taken
to a foreign country.
3You survivors in Israel,
listen to me, the Lord.
Since the day you were born,
I have carried you along.
4I will still be the same
when you are old and gray,
and I will take care of you.
I created you. I will carry you
and always keep you safe.
5Can anyone compare with me?
Is anyone my equal?
6Some people hire a goldsmith
and give silver and gold
to be formed into an idol
for them to worship.
7They carry the idol
on their shoulders,
then put it on a stand,
but it cannot move.
They call out to the idol
when they are in trouble,
but it doesn't answer,
and it cannot help.
8Now keep this in mind,
you sinful people.
And don't ever forget it.
The Lord Alone Is God
9I alone am God!
There are no other gods;
no one is like me.
Think about what happened
many years ago.
10From the very beginning,
I told what would happen
long before it took place.
I kept my word 11and brought
someone from a distant land
to do what I wanted.
He attacked from the east,
like a hawk swooping down.
Now I will keep my promise
and do what I planned.
12You people are stubborn
and far from being safe,
so listen to me.
13I will soon come to save you.
I am not far away
and will waste no time;
I take pride in Israel
and will save Jerusalem.
translation_text:
Babilon teo jwona yam taane
1Babilon teo wa yam Bel de Nebo dam ti,
ya nadwoona jege tega mo.
Ya nyenyero tem laam nam ye zela mo
bonɛ na zeŋe-ya se via.
Ya maa ye zele-zana yalo na duna to mo,
pa se vara balo na zeŋe-ya to tiini ba bugi.
2Jwona yam konto de balo na zeŋe-ya to
nam dɛ daane mo ba tiiri tega ne.
Wa yam ware se ya jwoŋi ya tete nyenyero tem ya yage.
Ya maama ye se nɔɔna ja-ya mo
ba ja ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga.
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
3“Abam Jakob dwi tiina bam, cheigi-na a taane dem.
Abam Isarele dwi tiina balo maama ta na daare to,
a yɔɔre a teili abam mo,
ko zege maŋa kalo á nu na kwei á puga to.
Ko zege ba na loge abam maŋa kalo to
a ta yɔɔre a jege abam a peila mo.
4Abam na kwe maŋa kalo
ye á yum tem su de yu-pwei to,
ko ta ye amo mo jege abam a nia.
Amo mo naane abam, ye a wó taa nii á baŋa ne taa.
Amo wó taa teili abam, ye a jwoŋi abam a yaga.
5Wɔ mo abam wó kwei á maŋe de amo?
Wɔ mo á wó ta we, dé ye da-yuudwonna?
6Nɔɔna badwonna yeini ba lwo ba tampɔro wo sabu-seŋa mo ba tiŋi tega ne,
ye ba daare ba maŋe ba lu-nyenno tem dunni.
Ba laam maa wó kwei sabu kom ba pa luru
se o pipiri-ka se ka ji ba jwoni.
Ba laam maa wó tiiri de yiga ne,
ye ba jege-de ba zula.
7Ba ta wó kwei-de mo ba daŋe ba bakale baŋa ne,
ye ba jege-de ba via.
Ba ná yɔɔre ba chwi-de mɛ,
de lɛɛre de zege da mo,
de daa ware se de gɔ naga de tete ne.
Nɔɔno ná laare tei o jare-de se de woli‑o,
de ware se de leiri kolokolo.
De nam ware se de jwoŋi kotu o cham wone de yage.
8Abam balo na swoi se á ta‑á ve amo to,
guli-na tento se á wane á ke dam á ke á kuri ne.
Kwei-ko á ke á yuu ne.
9Guli-na wo-dwonnu telo na ke faŋa faŋa to.
Amo mo ye Wɛ, ye wɛ dedwoŋi daa tera.
Amo mo ye Wɛ, ye kolokolo tera ko na mae de amo.
10Boboa kam ne mo amo maŋe a ta kolo na wó ke ko guri to.
Ko na nwoŋi faŋa to mo a tage kolo jwa na wó ba to.
A maa we: Amo boboŋa yam mo wó yɔɔre ya toŋe.
A nam wó ke kolo maama na su a yi to mo.
11A lage a bwoŋi nɔɔno mo
se o zege wɛ-puli seeni o ba.
O nam wó foore o ba mo
ne kalwoŋo na foore chibia baŋa ne tei to.
Kotu wó nwoŋi teo yiga yiga o ba
o ke tei maama amo na boŋe se o ke to.
Amo na jeeli a ja tei ye a ta kolo taane to mo
a lage a seene a ke.
12Abam zwabani-nyena bam cheigi-na a taane dem.
Á swoi se á ta‑á pɔɔre á tete de a chega kam mo.
13Amo nam lage a vaŋe a chega kam mo se ka yi abam.
Ka daa dae yiga yiga de abam.
Ko bá dáane se a ma a jwoŋi abam a yage.
Amo wó pa se Zion tiina bam na verem,
se Isarele tiina bam taa jege nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ amo ŋwaane.”

english_text:
Babylon Will Fall
The Lord said:
1 City of Babylon,
You are delicate
and untouched,
but that will change.
Surrender your royal power
and sit in the dirt.
2Start grinding grain!
Take off your veil.
Strip off your fancy clothes
and wade across rivers.
3You will suffer the shame
of going naked,
because I will take revenge,
and no one can escape.
4I am the Lord All-Powerful,
the holy God of Israel.
I am their Savior.
5Babylon, be silent!
Sit in the dark.
No longer will nations
accept you as their queen.
6I was angry with my people.
So I let you take their land
and bring disgrace on them.
You showed them no mercy,
but were especially cruel
to those who were old.
7You thought that you
would be queen forever.
You didn't care what you did;
it never entered your mind
that you might get caught.
8 You think that you alone
are all-powerful,
that you won't be a widow
or lose your children.
All you care about is pleasure,
but listen to what I say.
9Your magic powers and charms
will suddenly fail,
then you will be a widow
and lose your children.
10You hid behind evil
like a shield and said,
“No one can see me!”
You were fooled by your wisdom
and your knowledge;
you felt sure that you alone
were in full control.
11But without warning,
disaster will strike—
and your magic charms
won't help at all.
