Ejipti teo Pa-faro wom, de o nakwa, de o dedɛɛra, de o nɔn-bia bam, 20dedaane veira balo maama na zoore ba tetare ne to.
Yuzi laŋa pwa bam maama.
Filisi tiina pwa bam maama. Banto maa ye Asekelon teo pɛ, de Gaza teo pɛ, de Ekoron teo pɛ, de balo ta na daare Asedodi teo wone to.
21Edom tiina bam, de Moaba tiina bam, de Amon tiina bam.
22Tura de Sidon teene pwa bam maama, ko ta woli de pwa balo na zoore naneo ni kateira yam ne to.
23Dedan tiina bam, de Tema tiina bam, de Buzi tiina bam, dedaane balo na cheeri ba yuni ye ba zoore kagoa yuu ne to.
24Arabia laŋa pwa bam, de dwi-gɛ tiina balo na zoore kagoa kam wone to pwa bam.
25Zimiri pwa bam, de Elam pwa bam, de Media pwa bam.
26Pwa balo na zoore baŋa seeni teene dem ne to, ko ná ye delo na bwola daane to, dedaane delo na ye yiga yiga to de.
A vei logo baŋa maama teene dem mo a pa se ba nyɔ na-zoŋa kam wo sana bam. Se ko kweeli to, Babilon teo pɛ wom de maa wó nyɔ ka wone.
27 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we, “Nam ta nɔɔna bam we, ‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to mo we: Nyɔ-na na-zoŋa kam wone sana á bugi, se á tɔne tetwanno. Ta‑á pare á toe tega ne, se á daa yé zaŋe wɛɛne, jara yalo amo na wó pa se ya to á tetare ne to ŋwaane.’ 28Ba nam ná ve se ba nyɔ na-zoŋa kam n na tei na pa-ba to wone, se n ta de-ba we, ‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tage tento mo: Á jege se á nyɔ mo! 29Nii-na! Ko ná ye teo kolo na ye a tete nyem to, amo bobo banto baŋa ne mo se a pa ba na chɔgem. Abam nam boŋe we a laam wó yage abam mo na? Abam de bá lu waarem dem wone! A yɔɔre a lage a pa se jara mo to logo baŋa teene dem maama wone. Amo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto!’
30Jeremia, nam tɔɔle taane dento maama n bere-ba we:
‘Baŋa Wɛ kwora mo lage ka zaŋe wɛyuu ne ka mumuni.
O kwor-dɛa maa wó bage ka zege o telaao sɔŋɔ kom wone.
O sɔɔ wó zaŋe o tega kam maama baŋa ne.
O kwora kam wó zaŋe baŋa baŋa,
ne nɔɔno na nɔne Vini tio-bia ye o ke sɔɔ o yage tei to.
Logo baŋa nɔɔna maama wó ni Baŋa Wɛ na bage-ba tei to.
31Sɔɔ kom konto wó jage ko yi logo baŋa jei maama.
Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ jege taane de dwi yam maama mo.
O nam lage o di nabiina maama taane mo,
se se-zɔɔro ti puseŋ-nyena dwi dem.’
Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.”
32Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam tage tento mo o we:
“Nii mo! Lɛɛro lage te jage
te yi logo baŋa teene maama.
Jara zaŋe ne vo-dɛɔ mo tei.
Ya ma nwoŋi logo baŋa jei selo na wo yiga yiga to ne ya beene.”
33Jara yam ná yia, nɔɔna balo Baŋa Wɛ na go to wó faare tega baŋa jei maama ne mo. Ba bá na nɔɔna se ba keeri ba lwi naa ba suli-ba. Ba yera wó taa tigi tega baŋa jei maama ne pare-pare, ne popɔnɔ mo tei.
34Abam yiga tiina bam, keeri-na á sisigi.
To-na tega ne á ta‑á bibila,
abam balo na yere Wɛ nɔɔna bam to.
Kokuri to, ko laam yi maŋa se ba go abam.
Á lage á yɔɔre á to tega ne mo á chochoge,
ne kabeila na to ka chochoge tei to.
35Yiga tiina bam bá na chwoŋa se ba duri ba lu.
Balo na yere Wɛ nɔɔna bam to bá na seigim jei.
36Cheigi-na se á wó ni
yiga tiina bam na keeri bɔge-bɔge tei to.
Balo na yere Wɛ nɔɔna bam to
de ma laare ba yage jei maama ne.
Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ mo lage o chɔge tega kam
ba na kale o nɔɔna bam ba vo mɛ to.
37Pwoli selo ya na jege ga-zuru lanyerane to
lage se yɔɔre se chɔge mo,
Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom dem na zaŋe to ŋwaane.
38 Baŋa Wɛ viiri o daare o tega kam
ne nywoŋo na yage ko tiga jei tei to mo.
Tega kalo Wɛ nɔɔna bam na zoore da to yɔɔre ka chɔge mo.
Kokuri to, ba dona bam tiini ba kwaare jara de-ba,
Baŋa Wɛ bane na tiini de zaŋe ba baŋa ne to ŋwaane.

english_text:
Jeremiah's Message in the Temple
(Jeremiah 7.1-15)
1 Soon after Jehoiakim became king of Judah, the Lord said:
2Jeremiah, I have a message for everyone who comes from the towns of Judah to worship in my temple. Go to the temple courtyard and speak every word that I tell you. 3Maybe the people will listen this time. And if they stop doing wrong, I will change my mind and not punish them for their sins. 4Tell them that I have said:
You have refused to listen to me and to obey my laws and teachings. 5Again and again I have sent my servants the prophets to preach to you, but you ignored them as well. Now I am warning you that if you don't start obeying me at once, 6 I will destroy this temple, just as I destroyed the town of Shiloh. Then everyone on earth will use the name “Jerusalem” as a curse word.
Jeremiah on Trial
7The priests, the prophets, and everyone else in the temple heard what I said, 8-9and as soon as I finished, they all crowded around me and started shouting, “Why did you preach that the Lord will destroy this temple, just as he destroyed Shiloh? Why did you say that Jerusalem will be empty and lie in ruins? You ought to be put to death for saying such things in the Lord's name!” Then they had me arrested.
10The royal officers heard what had happened, and they came from the palace to the new gate of the temple to be the judges at my trial. 11While they listened, the priests and the prophets said to the crowd, “All of you have heard Jeremiah prophesy that Jerusalem will be destroyed. He deserves the death penalty.”
12-13Then I told the judges and everyone else:
The Lord himself sent me to tell you about the terrible things he will do to you, to Jerusalem, and to the temple. But if you change your ways and start obeying the Lord, he will change his mind.
14You must decide what to do with me. Just do whatever you think is right. 15But if you put me to death, you and everyone else in Jerusalem will be guilty of murdering an innocent man, because everything I preached came from the Lord.
16The judges and the other people told the priests and prophets, “Since Jeremiah only told us what the Lord our God had said, we don't think he deserves to die.”
17Then some of the leaders from other towns stepped forward. They told the crowd that 18 years ago when Hezekiah was king of Judah, a prophet named Micah from the town of Moresheth had said:
“I, the Lord All-Powerful, say
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple
now stands.”
19Then the leaders continued:
No one put Micah to death for saying that. Instead, King Hezekiah prayed to the Lord with fear and trembling and asked him to have mercy. Then the Lord decided not to destroy Jerusalem, even though he had already said he would.
People of Judah, if Jeremiah is killed, we will bring a terrible disaster on ourselves.
20-24After these leaders finished speaking, an important man named Ahikam son of Shaphan spoke up for me as well. And so, I wasn't handed over to the crowd to be killed.
Uriah the Prophet
While Jehoiakim was still king of Judah, a man named Uriah son of Shemaiah left his hometown of Kiriath-Jearim and came to Jerusalem. Uriah was one of the Lord's prophets, and he was saying the same things about Judah and Jerusalem that I had been saying. And when Jehoiakim and his officials and military officers heard what Uriah said, they tried to arrest him, but he escaped to Egypt. So Jehoiakim sent Elnathan son of Achbor and some other men after Uriah, and they brought him back. Then Jehoiakim had Uriah killed and his body dumped in a common burial pit.
translation_text:
Ba na di Jeremia taane tei to
1Josia bu Jehoyakim déem na bobo se o di Judah teo paare to, mo kwora kanto tu Jeremia tei. 2Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we,
“Véi n zege Wɛ diga konkɔlɔ kom ne. Nɔɔna bam laam maa ná nwoŋi Judah teene dem maama wone ba ba ba zo da se ba zuli amo Baŋa Wɛ, se n ta kwora kanto maama n bere-ba. Yé seigi kolokolo ba yiga ne. 3Dɛ delo nɔɔna bam wó cheigi amo kwora kam ye ba daare ba yage ba lwarem kikia yam. Ba ná sɛ ba ke konto, amo wó wane a leiri a boboŋa de lɛɛro telo a ya na jeeli se a ke ba baŋa ne ba wɛleera yam ŋwaane to.
4Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam nam jege se á cheigi amo taane, se á daare á sɛ nia yalo a na pɛ abam to mo. 5A yeini a toŋe a sampwori sem á tei ne titwon-twono se ba tɔɔle a kwora kam ba bere abam. Ko ya maŋe se á sɛ ba ni-kaana yam, á nam ba sɛa. 6Abam daa ta ná wo sɛ a taane dem, amo de nam wó chɔge Wɛ diga kanto mo, ne a déem na ke tei Siloo baŋa ne to. A laam maa wó pa se Jerusalem ji teo kolo logo baŋa dwi maama na wó ma ko yere ba sɔɔle lwarem ba pa daane to.’ ”
7Kaanem tiina bam, de sampwori sem, de nɔɔna bam maama déem ma zege Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne ye ba ni Jeremia na tage tei maama to. 8O maa na tɔɔle Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam maama o ti to, mo kaanem tiina bam, de sampwori sem, dedaane nɔɔna bam maama ke lela ba zaŋe o baŋa ne ba zi‑o ye ba we, “N maŋe se n te mo! 9Wɔ mo pɛ‑m chwoŋa se n pworisi de Baŋa Wɛ yere we, Wɛ diga kanto de lage ka chɔge mo, ne ko déem na ke tei Siloo baŋa ne to? Bɛ mo ye n ta ta we teo konto wó ji di-dwonnu se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa yé taa zoore ko wone?” Ba déem ma ta konto Wɛ wara-jei sem ne ye ba peene Jeremia ba ke‑o ba tetare ne.
10Judah teo nakwa bam na nigi kolo na ke to, mo ba de ke lela ba zege pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne ba vo Wɛ wara-jei sem ne. Ba ma vo Wɛ diga konkɔlɔ kom ni delo yere na ye ‘Ni-doore dem’ to ba jeini da se ba nii taane dem baŋa ne. 11Kaanem tiina bam, de sampwori sem laam ma ta de teo nakwa bam, de nɔn-bia bam maama ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto maŋe se o te mo. Kokuri to, o ŋɔɔne taane delo na yaale dé teo kom to mo. O na tage tei maama to to abam tete zwa wone.”
12Jeremia ma ta de nakwa bam de nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ-ne ni se a pworisi taane a chɔge Wɛ diga kanto de teo konto maama, ne á na nigi tei maama to. 13Nam leiri-na á kikia yam se á ta‑á tɔge chwo-laaro. Pipiri-na á sɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ ni dem. Konto mo wó pa se o leiri o boboŋa de lɛɛro telo o ya na jeeli se o pa te yi abam to. 14Ko nam ná ye amo, a wo á je ne mo, se á ke kolo maama á na boŋe we ko tɔge chwoŋa to. 15Nam lɔre-na we, abam ná go-ne, á go wolo na wo ke kolokolo o chɔge to mo. Á wɛleere dem konto wó taa wo á yuu ne, dedaane teo konto de ko nɔn-bia bam maama yuu ne. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ mo seene o toŋe-ne se a ta kolo maama á na nigi to.”
16Teo kom nakwa bam, de nɔɔna bam maama na nigi konto to, ba ma ta de kaanem tiina bam, de sampwori sem ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto wo ke kolo na maŋe se o te to. Ko ye o tɔge Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane mo o ŋɔɔne de debam.”
17Ba taane dem kwaga ne mo nakwa badwonna zege ba ta de nɔɔna balo maama na jeeri da to ba we, 18“Hezekia déem na ye Judah teo pɛ to mo Moresɛf teo tu Mika pworisi o bere Judah tiina bam maama ye o we:
‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Wɛ tete teo Jerusalem wó to ko saare
ko ji di-dwonnu yerane.
Nɔɔna wó ba ba va Zion tega kam konto ba tiŋi.
Teeni maa wó li zwoŋo kolo Wɛ diga kam ya na zege da to.’
19Pɛ Hezekia de Judah tiina bam déem nam go Mika mo na? Aawo. Pɛ wom kɔre Baŋa Wɛ ye o lwoori‑o se o duri ba ŋwaŋa. Baŋa Wɛ de ma leiri o boboŋa de lɛɛro telo o ya na jeeli se o pa te yi-ba to. Debam nam ná go nɔɔno wonto, lɛɛro lage te ba dé baŋa ne lela mo!”
20Nɔɔno wodwoŋi de déem wora. O ye Semaya bu Yuria mo. O maa nwoŋi Kiriaf-Jeerim. O de déem tɔge Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane mo o pworisi o ta Jerusalem de Judah tiina bam taane, ne Jeremia na tage tei to. 21Pɛ Jehoyakim, de o babɛ sem, de o nakwa bam ma ni ko ŋwa. Pɛ wom ma beeri o gom. Yuria ma maane ko ni ne, pa o duri o vo Ejipti o seigi da, o na kɔre foone to ŋwaane. 22Jehoyakim ta ma toŋe Akebora bu Elinatan de nɔɔna badwonna se ba vo Ejipti ba ja‑o ba ba. 23Ba ma vo ba ja Yuria ba jwoori ba vo ba ke Pɛ Jehoyakim jeŋa ne. Pɛ wom ma pa ba go‑o, ye ba dole o yera yam ba yage ba teo yibeela yam jei ne.
24Ko nam ná ye Jeremia, Safan bu Ahikam déem ŋɔɔne o pa‑o. Mo kokuri ba wo jaane‑o ba ke nɔɔna bam jeŋa ne se ba go.

english_text:
Slaves of Nebuchadnezzar
1-2 Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me:
Jeremiah, make a wooden yoke with leather straps, and place it on your neck. 3Then send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Some officials from these countries are in Jerusalem, meeting with Zedekiah. 4So have them tell their kings that I have said:
I am the All-Powerful Lord God of Israel, 5and with my power I created the earth, its people, and all animals. I decide who will rule the earth, 6-7 and I have chosen my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to rule all nations, including yours. I will even let him rule the wild animals. All nations will be slaves of Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his grandson. Then many nations will join together, and their kings will make slaves of the Babylonians.
8This yoke stands for the power of King Nebuchadnezzar, and I will destroy any nation that refuses to obey him. Nebuchadnezzar will attack, and many will die in battle or from hunger and disease. 9You might have people in your kingdom who claim they can tell the future by magic or by talking with the dead or by dreams or messages from a god. But don't pay attention if any of them tell you not to obey Nebuchadnezzar. 10If you listen to such lies, I will have you dragged far from your country and killed. 11But if you and your nation are willing to obey Nebuchadnezzar, I will let you stay in your country, and your people will continue to live and work on their farms.
12After I had spoken to the officials from the nearby kingdoms, I went to King Zedekiah and told him the same thing. Then I said:
Zedekiah, if you and the people of Judah want to stay alive, you must obey Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians. 13But if you refuse, then you and your people will die from war, hunger, and disease, just as the Lord has warned. 14Your prophets have told you that you don't need to obey Nebuchadnezzar, but don't listen to their lies. 15Those prophets claim to be speaking for the Lord, but he didn't send them. They are lying! If you do what they say, he will have both you and them dragged off to another country and killed. The Lord has spoken.
16When I finished talking to the king, I told the priests and everyone else that the Lord had said:
Don't listen to the prophets when they say that very soon the Babylonians will return the things they took from my temple. Those prophets are lying! 17If you choose to obey the king of Babylonia, you will live. But if you listen to those prophets, this whole city will be nothing but a pile of rubble.
18If I really had spoken to those prophets, they would know what I am going to do. Then they would be begging me not to let everything else be taken from the temple and the king's palace and the rest of Jerusalem. 19-21After all, when Nebuchadnezzar took King Jehoiachin to Babylonia as a prisoner, he didn't take everything of value from Jerusalem. He left the bronze pillars, the huge bronze bowl called the Sea, and the movable bronze stands in the temple, and he left a lot of other valuable things in the palace and in the rest of Jerusalem.
But now I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, say that all these things 22will be taken to Babylonia, where they will remain until I decide to bring them back to Jerusalem. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Judah tiina wó sɛ ba pa Nebukadeneza
1Josia bu Zedekia déem na bobo o di Judah paare to, mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ Jeremia kwora se o ta. 2Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo de amo to mo tento:
“Kwei tankɔlɔ n seere-ko, se n ma sesere sem konto n vɔ daa yera ne n ke nabɛ yɔgese se n daare n kwei-ka n de n ba ne. 3Nmo laam wó toŋe kwora se ka yi Edom teo pɛ, de Moaba teo pɛ, de Amon teo pɛ, de Tura teo pɛ, ko woli de Sidon teo pɛ. Ko nam ye ba dedɛɛra balo na tu Jerusalem se ba ware Pɛ Zedekia to mo wó ja n kwora kam ba vo ba pa pwa bam konto. 4Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to nam tage de amo se a pa-ba kwora kanto, se ba de ta ba bere ba pwa bam we:
5‘Amo tɔge a dam baŋa ne a toŋe wo-kamunnu a ma a naane tega baŋa, de ka nɔn-bia, de vara balo na kare ba vei da to. A nam yeini a kwei tento maama a pae wolo a yi na su to mo. 6Amo yɔɔre a kwei teene dento maama mo a ke Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza jeŋa ne. Wonto ye amo tontoŋeno mo. Amo ma bere a pa kago-vara ni se ba sɛ ba pa‑o. 7Teene maama nɔɔna wó taa toŋe ba pa‑o mo. Ba ta wó toŋe ba pa o bu, de o naa. Ko wó taa ye konto mo se ko yi maŋa kalo ba de teo kom na yi se a pa nɔɔna taa tei-ba to. Wonto de o teo tiina laam maa wó toŋe ba pa pa-kamuna de ba nɔɔna.
8Teo kolo nɔɔna nam ná ve se ba ke ba tete Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza jeŋa ne se o taa tei-ba, amo wó pa se banto te jara wone mo, se jaweero de kana de ja-ba te go. Amo wó tɔge Pɛ Nebukadeneza baŋa ne mo a chɔge-ba konto se ba ba ba ti fase. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto. 9Mo kokuri, á ba jege se á cheigi á sampwori, de á yi-nara, de á dendwea tɛɛna, de á chichiri vora, de á liri-mwa tiina taane. Banto yeini ba ta de abam ba we, á bá taa wo Babilon teo pɛ dam kuri ne. 10Ko ye vwa mo ba jege ba pworisa. Ba na gane abam tei to wó pa se á vo sa-teo yiga yiga á daare á tega kam. Amo wó zeili abam a dole a yage da, se á maŋe dáane á te. 11Teo kolo nɔɔna nam ná sɛ se ba ke ba tete Babilon teo pɛ wom jeŋa ne se o taa tei-ba, amo de wó pa nɔɔna bam konto chwoŋa se ba maŋe ba tete tega wone, se ba taa zoore ka wone ye ba vara.’ ”
12Amo déem ma daare a ja kwora kam konto a vo Judah pɛ Zedekia tei, ye a lwoni-ka a bere‑o. A ma ta ded‑o a we, “Ke n tete Babilon teo pɛ wom jeŋa ne se o taa tei á teo kom. Á ná sɛ á pa wonto de o nɔɔna, á wó jwoŋi á tete á yage. 13Baŋa Wɛ tage o we teo kolo nɔɔna ná wo sɛ Babilon teo pɛ wom, banto wó te jara wone mo, se jaweero de kana de ja-ba te go. Bɛ mo wó ke se nmo de n nɔɔna bam ta‑á lage toone? 14Nam yé cheigi-na sampwori selo na tɛ de abam ba we, á bá taa wo Babilon teo pɛ dam kuri ne to. Banto jege vwa mo ba pworisi de abam.
15 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
‘Amo wo toŋe sampwori sem konto. Ba jege vwa mo ba pworisi amo yere ŋwaane. Konto ŋwaane mo amo lage a zeili abam se á viiri. Abam de á sampwori sem konto maama wó te mo.’ ”
16Amo laam ma ta de kaanem tiina bam, de nɔɔna bam maama a we:
“Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Yé cheigi-na sampwori selo na tɛ de abam ba we, Babilon tiina bam wó jwoori ba ja Wɛ diga zela yalo ba ya na jaane ba viiri to ba ba ba pa debam. Ko ye vwa mo ba jege ba pworisa. 17Nam yé cheigi-na ba taane. Sɛ-na á pa Babilon teo pɛ wom, se á jwoŋi á tete á yage. Á lage á pa se teo konto ji di-dwonnu se bɛ mo?’
18Ba nam ná seene ba ye sampwori selo na jege Baŋa Wɛ kwora se ba ta to, se ba lwoori Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ se o yé pa chwoŋa se ba vere Wɛ diga kam zela yalo ta na daare Jerusalem ne to, de pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wo jejegero tem ba ja vo Babilon. 19Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam tage tento mo se ko vo Wɛ diga kam zela yalo ta na wora to seeni. Yanto maa ye channa ywoa yalei yam, de channa na-zon-zaŋa kalo ba na bwoi we ‘Naneo kom’ to, de ware-zwe zegem torokooro tem, de zela dwi dwi yalo ta na daare to. 20Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza déem na tu o kale Judah teo pɛ Jehoyakim bu Jehoyachin, de Jerusalem de Judah laŋa kam naduna maama o ja o vo Babilon to, o yage Wɛ diga zela yam konto ya jei ne mo. 21Chega to, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to tage Wɛ diga kam zela yalo ta na daare Jerusalem ne to, de pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wo jejegero tem taane o we:
22‘Nɔɔna wó vere jejegero tem konto maama ba vo Babilon mo. Te wó maŋe dáane, se ko yi maŋa kalo amo boboŋa daa na wó vo te seeni to. Amo laam maa wó jwoori a ja-te a ba a zege jei sento ne.’
Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Accuses Hananiah of Being a False Prophet
1 Later that same year, in the fifth month of the fourth year that Zedekiah was king, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur from Gibeon came up to me in the temple. And while the priests and others in the temple were listening, 2he told me that the Lord had said:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I will smash the yoke that Nebuchadnezzar put on the necks of the nations to make them his slaves. 3And within two years, I will bring back to Jerusalem everything that he took from my temple and carried off to Babylonia. 4King Jehoiachin and the other people who were taken from Judah to Babylonia will be allowed to come back here as well. All this will happen because I will smash the power of the king of Babylonia!
5The priests and the others were still standing there, so I said:
6Hananiah, I hope the Lord will do exactly what you said. I hope he does bring back everything the Babylonians took from the temple, and that our people who were taken to Babylonia will be allowed to return home. 7But let me remind you and everyone else 8that long before we were born, prophets were saying powerful kingdoms would be struck by war, disaster, and disease. 9Now you are saying we will have peace. We will just have to wait and see if that is really what the Lord has said.
10Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke from my neck and smashed it. 11Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.”
I left the temple, 12and a little while later, the Lord told me 13-14to go back and say to Hananiah:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You smashed a wooden yoke, but I will replace it with one made of iron. I will put iron yokes on all the nations, and they will have to do what King Nebuchadnezzar commands. I will even let him rule the wild animals.
15-16Hananiah, I have never sent you to speak for me. And yet you have talked my people into believing your lies and rebelling against me. So now I will send you—I'll send you right off the face of the earth! You will die before this year is over.
17Two months later, Hananiah died.
translation_text:
Hanania na dwoni de Jeremia tei to
1Bene dem konto chane senu chana kam wone mo Azura bu Hanania déem zege Wɛ diga kam wone o ŋɔɔne de amo. Pɛ Zedekia paare dim bena yana bene dem ne mo konto. Hanania maa ye sampwora ye o nwoŋi Gibeon teo ne. O ma zege kaanem tiina bam, de nɔɔna bam maama yiga ne o ta de amo o we:
2“Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Amo lage a chɔge Babilon teo pɛ wom dam delo o na jege o di abam baŋa ne nenɛɛne á jege nabɛ yɔgese mo á ba ne tei to. 3Bena yalei laŋa ne amo wó jwoori a ja Wɛ diga kam zela yalo Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza na vere o ja o vo Babilon to a ba a yage ywo. 4A nam ta wó ja Jehoyakim bu Jehoyachin na ye Judah teo pɛ to a jwoori ywo. Wonto de balo maama ba na kale ba ja vo Babilon ne to mo a lage a ja a jwoori ywo. Kokuri to, a lage a chɔge dam delo Babilon teo pɛ na jege o di abam baŋa ne to mo.’ Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”
5Wɛ sampwora Jeremia de ma zege Baŋa Wɛ diga kam wone o leiri Hanania, ye kaanem tiina bam de nɔɔna bam maama de zege da ba cheiga. 6O ma ta o we, “Ameena. Baŋa Wɛ wó pa ko seene ko ke! A teene we n na pworisi tei to wó ji chega, se Baŋa Wɛ pa se jejegero telo Babilon tiina bam na vere Wɛ diga kam ne ba ja ba viiri to, de nɔɔna balo ba na kale ba ja ba viiri to jwoori ywo. 7Nam cheigi taane delo a na jege se a pa nmo de nɔɔna banto maama to. 8Ko ná ye Wɛ sampwori selo na lwoori yiga se ba faŋa faŋa ye nmo de amo ta wo tu to, banto yeini ba pworisi ba bere we jara-keim, de kana, de lɛɛro dwi dwi wó ba teene dedɛ baŋa ne, de ná maŋe de ye te-kamunnu mo de. 9Ko daare, sampwora kalo ná pworisi yazura taane, kotu na pworisi tei to ná seene ko ke, ko bere we wonto mo ye wolo Baŋa Wɛ na seene o toŋe to.”
10Hanania laam ma vaŋe nabɛ yɔgese delo na wo Jeremia ba ne to o le, ye o daare o bwori-de. 11O ta ma zege nɔɔna bam maama yiga ne, ye o ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Tento dwoŋi mo a lage a chɔge dam delo pɛ Nebukadeneza na jege o di dwi tiina maama baŋa ne to. Bena yalei laŋa ne mo amo wó ke konto.’ ”
O na tage konto o ti to, Jeremia ma kɛ o daare-ba.
12Hanania déem na le nabɛ yɔgese Jeremia ba ne ye o daare o bwori-de ye ko ke fee to, mo Baŋa Wɛ daa kwei kwora kadwoŋi o pa Jeremia. O ma ta ded‑o o we, 13“Zaŋe n vo n ta de Hanania we, Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Nmo seene n wane yɔgese delo amo na mɛ daa a ke to n bwori n yage. Nmo nam lage n leiri yɔgese dem konto pa se de ji luuru nyem mo. 14Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a kwei luuru yɔgese mo a de teene dem konto maama ba ne, se ko fe-ba se ba sɛ ba pa Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza. Ba wó taa toŋe ba pa‑o. A ta maa wó pa kago-vara de ni se ba sɛ ba pa‑o.’ ”
15Jeremia ta ma ta de Hanania o we, “Cheigi-ne! Baŋa Wɛ bere o wo toŋe nmo. De ko de, n ta pɛ se nɔɔna banto sɛ n vwa yam. 16Konto ŋwaane, Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: A lage a le nmo se n jei tega baŋa ne. Bene dento ne mo n lage n te, n na bere nɔɔna bam se ba lɔ amo Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne to ŋwaane.”
17Bene dem konto chane serepɛ chana kam ne nɔɔ mo Hanania seene o te.

english_text:
Jeremiah's Letter to the People of Judah in Babylonia
1-2 I had been left in Jerusalem when King Nebuchadnezzar took many of the people of Jerusalem and Judah to Babylonia as prisoners, including King Jehoiachin, his mother, his officials, and the metal workers and others in Jerusalem who were skilled in making things. So I wrote a letter to the priests, the prophets, the leaders, and the rest of our people in Babylonia. 3I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote 4that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. Now I tell you 5to settle there and build houses. Plant gardens and eat what you grow in them. 6Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
7Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
8-9Some of your people there in Babylonia are fortunetellers, and you have asked them to tell you what will happen in the future. But they will only lead you astray with their dreams. And don't let the prophets fool you, either. They speak in my name, but they are liars. I have not spoken to them.
10 After Babylonia has been the strongest nation for 70 years, I will be kind and bring you back to Jerusalem, just as I have promised. 11I will bless you with a future filled with hope—a future of success, not of suffering. 12You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers. 13 You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you 14and accept your worship. Then I will gather you from all the nations where I scattered you, and you will return to Jerusalem.
15You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
16-19But I have been sending prophets to the people of Judah for a long time, and the king from David's family and the people who are left in Jerusalem and Judah still don't obey me. So I, the Lord All-Powerful, will keep attacking them with war and hunger and disease, until they are as useless as rotten figs. I will force them to leave the land, and all nations will be disgusted and shocked at what happens to them. The nations will sneer and make fun of them and use the names “Judah” and “Jerusalem” as curse words.
And you have not obeyed me, even though 20I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now. 21-23You think Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah are prophets because they claim to speak for me. But they are lying! I haven't told them anything. They are also committing other horrible sins in your community, such as sleeping with the wives of their friends. So I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will put them to death while the rest of you watch. And in the future, when you want to put a curse on someone, you will say, “I pray that the Lord will kill you in the same way the king of Babylonia burned Zedekiah and Ahab to death!”
A Message for Shemaiah
24-25The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
26After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars. 27Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him? 28He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
29When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me. 30Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter 31to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said:
I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name. 32He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jeremia popone tɔnɔ o pa balo ba na kale ba ja vo Babilon to
1Jeremia déem zege Jerusalem ne mo o popone tɔnɔ o toŋe o pa Isarele nakwa balo ba na jaane ba vo Babilon ye ba ta wora to, de kaanem tiina bam, de sampwori sem, de balo maama Pɛ Nebukadeneza na jaane Jerusalem ne o kale o vo Babilon to. 2Ko nam ye ba déem na maŋe ba kale Pɛ Jehoyachin, de o nu, de pɛ sɔŋɔ dedɛɛra bam, de yiga tiina balo na nii Jerusalem de Judah kateira yam baŋa ne to, de ba teo kom gwaro, de ba lura ba ja ba viiri to kwaga ne mo. 3Jeremia déem kwei tɔnɔ kom o ke Safan bu Elasa, de Hilikia bu Gemaria jeŋa ne mo. Judah teo pɛ Zedekia déem toŋe banto mo se ba vo Babilon ba zege ba pa‑o Pɛ Nebukadeneza tei ne. Tɔnɔ kom popone we:
4Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na jege kolo se o ta de balo o na pɛ se Nebukadeneza kale o nwoŋi Jerusalem ne o vo Babilon to mo tento:
5“Lɔ-na sam dáane se á lɛɛre á jeini ba teo kom wone. Jeiri-na gaara, se á ta‑á di ya tio-bia bam. 6Swo-na kaana, se á lo bia de-ba. Di-na kaana á pa á bakeiri sem, se á daare á kwei á bukwa á yei á pa banna. Konto wó pa se ba na naaro ba pa abam. Puli-na de kɔgɔ. Yé mɔ-na á kɔgɔ kom ni. 7Ta‑á toŋe-na se teo kolo a na kale abam a vo a yage da to taa jege yazura, se wonnu taa ke lanyerane te pa-ba. Nam ta lwoori-na Baŋa Wɛ á pa-ba, kokuri to ko ná ke lanyerane ko pae banto, abam de wó na á yiga-veiŋa.”
8Chega ŋwaane to, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to tage tento mo:
“Yé pa-na se sampwori selo, de yi-nara balo na wo abam tetare ne to gane abam. Á nam yé ke á boboŋa ba dendwea yam wone. 9Se ko ye vwa mo ba jege ba pworisa ba pae abam amo yere ŋwaane. Amo bere a wo toŋe-ba.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
10 Baŋa Wɛ nam ta tage tento mo o we:
“Abam nam ná ke á bena fuserepɛ yam Babilon ne á ti, á laam wó jwoori á tete teo kom. Amo yiga daa wó taa wo abam wone se a ke wo-laaro telo a na gwoni ni se a ke a pa abam to. 11Kokuri to, amo boboŋa maŋe ya ja de a na wó ke abam tei to mo. Amo jeeli se a pa á na yiga-veiŋa mo, se ko dae lɛɛro. A jeeli se á ta‑á jege teena de jwa mo. 12Abam laam maa wó ba amo yiga ne se á ware-ne. Amo de maa wó cheigi á wɛ-lworo kom. 13Abam maa wó beeri-ne, ye á na-ne. Chega to, á ná beeri-ne de á bochara maama, 14a maa wó pa abam chwoŋa se á lɔre-ne.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
“Amo de wó pa se á jwoori á ta‑á jege yu-ywoŋo. Amo wó la abam a ja a nwoŋi jei selo maama ne a ya na zeili abam a yage se wone to, se á jwoori á ba á jeini á tete teo kom wone.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
15Abam nam wae á tɛ nenɛɛne, “Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o kuri sampwori o pa debam Babilon teo ne.” 16Ko nam ná ye á pɛ wolo zem na jei Pɛ David paare yituŋu kom baŋa ne o di paare Jerusalem ne to, de á chorro telo maama na wo tɔge de abam ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga ye ba ta daare teo kom ne to, Baŋa Wɛ na tage banto taane tei to mo tento:
17“Amo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ lage a pa se jara mo to ba wone, se kana, de jaweero de ja-ba, pa se ba ji ne mɔɔro telo na pɔga ye te ware te di to. 18Chega ŋwaane to, amo lage a tɔge jara-keim, de kana, de jaweero baŋa a zeili-ba mo, pa se ba ji wo-zɔɔna logo baŋa teene maama yia ne. A nam ná pɛ se ba jage ba yi mɛ maama, nɔɔna wó dole ba yuni ba ŋwaane ye ba ma ba yere ba sɔɔle lwarem ba pa daane. Nɔɔna wó taa jege-ba ba yaala, ye ba mɔne-ba. 19Kokuri to, ba wo cheigi amo kwora kalo a tontoŋena bam na pworisi de-ba titwon-twono to.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
“Abam balo na wo sa-teo wone to de wo cheigi a taane dem. 20Abam balo maama a na zeili Jerusalem ne a kale a ja a vo Babilon teo to, nam cheigi-na amo Baŋa Wɛ taane dem.”
21Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to nam na tage tei se ko vo Kolaya bu Ahab, de Maaseya bu Zedekia seeni to mo tento:
“Banto jege vwa mo ba pworisa amo yere ŋwaane. A nam wó kwei-ba a ke Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza jeŋa ne, se o go-ba ye á zege á nia. 22Judah tiina balo maama ba na jaane ba vo Babilon to wolo ná boŋe se o sɔɔle lwarem o pa o dwoŋi, kotu wó tɔge banto ŋwaane o ta we: ‘Baŋa Wɛ wó ke‑m ne Babilon teo pɛ na ke tei de Zedekia, de Ahab, ye o zwɛ-ba mini wone to.’ 23Kokuri to, banto tiini ba toŋe wo-zɔɔna mo a nɔɔna bam tetare ne. Ba ke kabwoŋa de ba dwonna kaana. Ba ma ŋɔɔne vwa amo yere ŋwaane, ye amo wo pɛ-ba a kwora. Amo nam maane ko maama ni ne.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.
Semaya na popone tɔnɔ kolo to
24 Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Jeremia o we, “Nam ta de Nehelam tu Semaya we: 25Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage tei to mo tento: Nmo tɔge n tete yere ŋwaane mo n popone tɔnɔ n toŋe n pa Jerusalem tiina bam maama. N ma‑n pa ko yi Maaseya bu Zefania na ye kaanem tu to, de kaanem tiina badaara bam maama. N ma‑n ta de Zefania we:
26‘Baŋa Wɛ mo tiŋi‑m se n leiri Jehoyada yuu ne n ta‑n ye kaanem tu o wara-jei sem ne, ye n nii Wɛ diga kam baŋa ne. Nmo ná nɛ we chichwoo mo wora o na bere o tete we o ye Wɛ sampwora to, n jege se n ja kotu n vɔ o nɛ mo, se n daare n lei luu o ba ne. 27Bɛ nam mo ye n wo ke Anatofe tu Jeremia kolokolo? Wonto yeini o pworisi mo o pa abam. 28Ko maŋe se n che‑o mo, kokuri to o popone tɔnɔ o toŋe o pa debam balo na wo Babilon ne to ye o we, dé wó dáane ywo bena dedɛ. O we, dé lɔ sam se dé lɛɛre dé jeini ywo, ye dé daare dé jeiri gaara se dé taa di ya tio-bia.’ ”
29Zefania na jwoŋi tɔnɔ kom to, mo o gage-ko o bere Jeremia. 30Baŋa Wɛ de laam ma kwei kwora kanto o pa Jeremia ye o we, 31“Pa kwora kanto yi balo maama ba na kale ba ja vo Babilon to: Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei se ko vo Nehelam tu Semaya seeni to mo tento: ‘Semaya yeini o pworisi mo o bere abam, ye amo wo toŋe‑o. O ma gane abam ye á sɛ o vwa yam. 32Konto ŋwaane amo Baŋa Wɛ lage a waare Nehelam tu Semaya de o dwi dem mo. O dwi dem wolowolo bá na wo-laaro telo a na boŋe se a ke a pa a nɔɔna bam to, o na bere nɔɔna bam se ba lɔ amo kwaga ne to ŋwaane.’ Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_text:
The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
1-2The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you. 3Someday I will let my people from both Israel and Judah return to the land I gave their ancestors.”
4-5Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah:
Screams of terror are heard,
with no word of peace.
6Can men give birth?
Then why do I see them
looking so pale
and clutching their stomachs
like women in labor?
7My people, soon you will suffer
worse than ever before,
but I will save you.
8Now you are slaves
of other nations,
but I will break the chains
and smash the yokes
that keep you in slavery.
9Then you will be my servants,
and I will choose a king for you
from the family of David.
* 10 Israel, you belong to me,
so don't be afraid.
You deserved to be punished;
that's why I scattered you
in distant nations.
But I am with you,
and someday I will destroy
those nations.
11Then I will bring you
and your descendants
back to your land,
where I will protect you
and give you peace.
Then your fears will be gone.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
12The Lord said:
My people, you are wounded
and near death.
13You are accused of a crime
with no one to defend you,
and you are covered with sores
that no medicine can cure.
* 14Your friends have forgotten you;
they don't care anymore.
Even I have acted like an enemy.
And because your sins
are horrible and countless,
I will be cruel
as I punish you.
15So don't bother to cry out
for relief from your pain.
16But if your enemies try to rob
or destroy you,
I will rob and destroy them,
and they will be led as captives
to foreign lands.
17No one wants you as a friend
or cares what happens to you.
But I will heal your injuries,
and you will get well.
The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
18The Lord said:
Israel, I will be kind to you
and let you come home.
Jerusalem now lies in ruins,
but you will rebuild it,
complete with a new palace.
19Other nations will respect
and honor you.
Your homes will be filled
with children,
and you will celebrate,
singing praises to me.
20It will be just like old times.
Your nation will worship me,
and I will punish anyone
who abuses you.
21One of your own people
will become your ruler.
And when I invite him
to come near me
at the place of worship,
he will do so.
No one would dare to come near
without being invited.
22You will be my people,
and I will be your God.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
23I am furious!
And like a violent storm
I will strike those
who do wrong.
24I won't calm down
until I have finished
what I have decided to do.
Someday, you will understand
what I mean.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ wó woli o nɔɔna se ba jwoori ba tete teo
30:1–33:26
Baŋa Wɛ na gwoni ni de o nɔɔna tei to
1 Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Jeremia ni delo to mo tento:
2Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom na tage tei to mo tento: “Popone wonnu telo maama a na tage a bere‑m to n ke tɔnɔ wone se te taa tiga. 3Kokuri to, maŋa kam beene se a pa a nɔɔna bam jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo. Isarele tiina bam de Judah tiina bam mo konto. Amo wó pa se ba jwoori ba jeini tega kalo ne a déem na pɛ ba nabaara bam to. Ba laam maa wó taa tei-ka.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
4Kwora kanto mo Baŋa Wɛ nam pɛ se ka vo Isarele tiina de Judah tiina bam seeni:
5O na tage kolo to mo tento:
“A nigi nɔɔna bam na keeri tei to.
Ko nam ye foone keira mo,
vuvuga na to ba wone to ŋwaane.
Yazura maa tera jei jei.
6Fɔge-na á jeeli taane dento á nii:
Baara de jaane pwi ye ba lore bia na?
Bɛ nam mo ke ye a nae baara na ye bele-bele,
ne kaane puga na virigi se o lo to?
Ba je sem ma teili ba pwi,
ye ba yibia nyɔne kiri-kiri.
7Lɛɛro wó tiini te ba maŋa kam konto ne,
se ko dwoni maŋa maama.
Kokuri to, a nɔɔna Jakob dwi tiina bam wó zo cham dedɛ wone.
Ba nam wó na verem de wone de.”
8Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we, “Amo wó ja nabɛ yɔgese delo na wo a nɔɔna bam ba ne to a bwori a yage, ye a daare a kɔ ba chegero tem, se veira daa yé taa jege dam ba di ba baŋa ne. 9Ba laam wó ke ba tete amo wolo na ye ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom to dam kuri ne mo. Ba ta wó zuli pɛ wolo a na wó kuri a pa-ba ye o ye David dwi tu to mo.”
10 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo tontoŋena, Jakob dwi tiina bam,
yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone.
Isarele tiina bam, nam yé ta‑á lwia.
Ko ná ye balo na peene abam yiga yiga teo wone to,
a lage a jwoŋi abam de á dwi dem mo banto jeŋa ne a yage.
Jakob dwi tiina bam wó jwoori ba tete teo de yazura,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá ke se foone zo-ba.
11Kokuri to, amo Baŋa Wɛ wo abam tei ne
se a jwoŋi abam a yage.
Amo wó yɔɔre a chɔge teene delo maama
a ya na jage abam a yage de wone to.
Se ko ná ye abam, a bá chɔge abam fase.
A nam yeini a wae a korese abam.
Amo ná waare abam maŋa de maŋa,
ko nam wó taa tɔge chega chwoŋa mo.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
12 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Abam na nɛ zonne delo to,
á bá na de yɔɔrem jei.
Á fufwollu tem bá wane te jei.
13Nɔɔno tera se kotu nii á taane dem baŋa ne.
Wolim nam tera á zonne dem ŋwaane,
ye yɔɔrem de tera de pae abam.
14Á fara bam maama swei á swea,
ye ba yiga daa tere á wone.
A tiini a de jaguli-zane mo á yera ne,
ne amo ye á dono mo tei.
A na tiini a waare abam tei to,
a wo duri á ŋwaŋa de fenfee de.
Ko nam ye á na tiini á tusi tei,
de á wɛleera yam na kɛ jeŋa to ŋwaane mo.
15Bɛŋwaane mo ye á keera
á zonne dem na ba jege yɔɔrem jei to ŋwaane?
A na pɛ ko tiini ko zo á yera tei to,
ko ye á na tiini á tusi tei,
de á wɛleera yam na kɛ jeŋa to ŋwaane mo.
16Ko nam na wó taa ye tei to,
amo wó chɔge balo zem na jege abam ba chɔge to.
Amo wó ja á dona maama
a vo a yage teene dedwonna wone.
Ko ná ye balo na vere á jejegero ba ja viiri to,
a lage pa nɔɔna vere banto de jejegero mo.
A ta wó pa se balo zem na bɛɛse abam to
jwoori ba na bɛɛsem.
17A laam maa wó jwoori a pa abam á yazura,
ye a daare a yɔɔre á fufwollu tem.
Kokuri to, ba ya jege abam Zion tiina bam
ba bwoi we, nɔn-yɔɔro telo Wɛ na zeili to,
ye ba we, nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera kotu yiga na wo á wone.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
18 Baŋa Wɛ nam tage tento mo o we:
“Amo wó jwoori a ja Jakob dwi dem
a jwoori ba tete teo,
pa se sɔ-yuu maama taa zoore de yazura.
Ba wó jwoori ba chwi Jerusalem teo kom
ko di-dwonnu baŋa ne mo.
Pɛ sɔ-fɔrɔ kom de wó jwoori ko zege
ko jeiga kam ne.
19Ba wó leeni lei-keim lei jei sem konto ne,
ye ba daare ba ke ywoni dim sɔɔ.
A maa wó pa se ba kɔgɔ puli dedɛ,
se ba daa yé muri.
A ta wó pa se ba jwoŋi zula,
pa se nɔɔna daa yé gwooni-ba.
20Ba nɔn-bia bam wó jwoori ba na dam,
ne ba déem na ye tei faŋa faŋa to.
Ba nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wó fɔge ba zege amo tei ne.
A maa wó waare balo maama na wó bɛɛse-ba to.
21Ba tete dwi tu laam mo wó di paare ba baŋa ne.
Wolo na wó taa tei-ba to
wó nwoŋi ba tete dwi dem wone.
Amo laam maa wó pa kotu chwoŋa
se o fɔɔre o ba o twɛ-ne.
Wɔ mo nam wó sɛ o yi amo tei,
ye amo wo bwoŋi kotu?
22Abam laam wó taa ye amo nɔɔna mo,
se amo de taa ye abam Wɛ wom.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
23Nii-na! Baŋa Wɛ bane wó zaŋe lela,
ne vo-dɛɔ na zaŋe tei to mo.
Ko nam wó taa nye de vo-kekara
na chugi nɔn-balwaaro yuu ne tei to mo.
24 Baŋa Wɛ bane nam ná zaŋe de-ba,
ko ná dae we o ke o su o boboŋa yam,
o bochare dem bá zuri.
Maŋa kam nam ná yia,
abam laam wó ni ko kuri lanyerane.

english_text:
Israel Will Return to God
1The Lord said:
Israel, I promise
that someday all your tribes
will again be my people,
and I will be your God.
2In the desert I was kind
to those who escaped death.
I gave them peace,
and when the time is right,
I'll do the same for you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Rebuild Israel
3Some time ago, the Lord appeared to me and told me to say:
Israel, I will always love you;
that's why I've been so patient
and kind.
4You are precious to me,
and so I will rebuild
your nation.
Once again you will dance for joy
and play your tambourines.
5You will plant vineyards
on the hills of Samaria
and enjoy the grapes.
6Someday those who guard
the hill country of Ephraim
will shout, “Let's go to Zion
and worship the Lord our God.”
Israel Will Return to Its Own Land
7The Lord says:
Celebrate and sing for Israel,
the greatest of nations.
Offer praises and shout,
“Come and rescue
your people, Lord!
Save what's left of Israel.”
8I, the Lord, will bring
my people back from Babylonia
and everywhere else on earth.
The blind and the lame
will be there.
Expectant mothers
and women about to give birth
will come and be part
of that great crowd.
9They will weep and pray
as I bring them home.
I will lead them
to streams of water.
They will walk on a level road
and not stumble.
I am a father to Israel,
my favorite children.
10Listen to me, you nations
nearby or across the sea.
I scattered the people of Israel,
but I will gather them again.
I will protect them like a shepherd
guarding a flock;
11I will rescue them from enemies
who could overpower them.
12My people will come
to Mount Zion
and celebrate;
their faces will glow
because of my blessings.
I'll give them grain, grapes,
and olive oil,
as well as sheep and cattle.
Israel will be prosperous
and grow like a garden
with plenty of water.
13Young women and young men,
together with the elderly,
will celebrate and dance,
because I will comfort them
and turn their sorrow
into happiness.
14I will bless my people
with more food
than they need,
and the priests will enjoy
the choice cuts of meat.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Offers Hope
15 In Ramah a voice is heard,
crying and weeping loudly.
Rachel mourns for her children
and refuses to be comforted,
because they are dead.
* 16But I, the Lord, say
to dry your tears.
Someday your children
will come home
from the enemy's land.
Then all you have done for them
will be greatly rewarded.
17So don't lose hope.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
18The people of Israel moan
and say to me,
“We were like wild bulls,
but you, Lord, broke us,
and we learned to obey.
You are our God—
please let us come home.
19When we were young,
we strayed and sinned,
but then we realized
what we had done.
We are ashamed and disgraced
and want to return to you.”
20People of Israel,
you are my own dear children.
Don't I love you best of all?
Though I often make threats,
I want you to be near me,
so I will have mercy on you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
21With rock piles and signposts,
mark the road well,
my dear people.
The road by which you left
by will now lead you home.
22Will you ever decide
to be faithful?
I will make sure that someday
things will be different,
as different as a woman
protecting a man.
The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
23The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said:
I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say,
“We pray that the Lord
will bless his home,
the sacred hill in Jerusalem
where his temple stands.”
24The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds. 25Those who feel tired and worn out will find new life and energy, 26and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
27Someday, Israel and Judah will be my field where my people and their livestock will grow. 28In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow. 29 No longer will anyone go around saying,
“Sour grapes eaten by parents
leave a sour taste in the mouths
of their children.”
30When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death.
The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
31 The Lord said:
The time will surely come when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah. 32It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
33 Here is the new agreement that I, the Lord, will make with the people of Israel:
“I will write my laws
on their hearts and minds.
I will be their God,
and they will be my people.
34 “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
35I am the Lord All-Powerful.
I command the sun
to give light each day,
the moon and stars
to shine at night,
and ocean waves to roar.
36I will never forget
to give those commands,
and I will never let Israel
stop being a nation.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
37Can you measure the heavens?
Can you explore
the depths of the earth?
That's how hard it would be
for me to reject Israel forever,
even though they have sinned.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
38The Lord said:
Someday, Jerusalem will truly belong to me. It will be rebuilt with a boundary line running from Hananel Tower to Corner Gate. 39From there, the boundary will go in a straight line to Gareb Hill, then turn toward Goah. 40Even that disgusting Hinnom Valley will be sacred to me, and so will the eastern slopes that go down from Horse Gate into Kidron Valley. Jerusalem will never again be destroyed.
translation_text:
Isarele tiina wó jwoori ba tete teo
1 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we, “Maŋa kam konto ná yia, amo wó taa ye Isarele sɔ-yuni maama Wɛ wom, se ba de taa ye amo nɔɔna.”
2 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Ko ná ye balo na lugi toone jara wone,
ye ba kare ba vei kagoa wone to,
banto nɛ wolim lanyerane.
Isarele tiina bam na beeri siu konto to,
3amo Baŋa Wɛ mo veere a tete de-ba
jei selo na ye yiga yiga to ne.
Isarele tiina bam,
ko na zege faŋa faŋa ne to mo a tiini a swoi abam.
Amo ta maa swoi abam de zem maama.
4Isarele tiina, á ye a nɔn-swonnu tem mo.
Amo wó pa se á jwoori á fɔge á zege de dam.
Á wó yɔɔre á fɔge á zege lanyerane.
Á daa ta wó kwei á senyɛ sem
á nwoŋi pwooni á tɔge de sara bam
á ta‑á sae de wopwolo.
5Abam daa ta wó jeiri á Vini teeni
Samaria zwonnu tem yuu ne.
Balo maama na jeiri ba Vini teeni dem to,
banto tete wó di de bia bam.
6Maŋa beene se balo na yeini ba nii Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam to zaŋe
ye ba tɔɔle ba ta we,
‘Ba-na se dé vo Jerusalem,
se dé zuli dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ Zion ne.’ ”
7 Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento:
“Leeni-na lei de wopwolo Jakob dwi dem ŋwaane,
de ba na wo dwi maama tiina yiga ne to ŋwaane.
Pa-na se á tia taa zaŋa,
se á ta we,
‘Baŋa Wɛ, nam zaŋe n jwoŋi n nɔɔna bam n yage!
Jwoŋi balo ta na daare Isarele tiina bam wone to n yage.’
8Nii mo! A lage a ja-ba a nwoŋi baŋa seeni teo kom ne a ba ywo,
se a daare a la ba maama a nwoŋi logo baŋa jei selo na wo yiga yiga ne to.
Lilwoa, de gwane wó taa wo ba kɔgɔ kom wone.
Kapwi de balo na virigi puga se ba lo to de wó taa wora.
Chega to, kɔ-fɔrɔ mo lage ko jwoori.
9Ba ná maa jwoora, ba wó taa keeri mo de wo-chechɔgɔ.
Amo na to ba yiga ne ye dé jwoori to,
Wɛ-lworo wó taa wo ba nia ne mo.
Amo wó kale-ba se ba tɔge na-zura na duri ba tole mɛ to.
Ba wó taa vei chwoŋa kalo na mae daane to ne mo
se ba daa yé to.
Kokuri to, amo mo ye Isarele dwi tiina bam kwo.
Efrayim maa ye amo bu-kwea.”
10Logo baŋa teene dem maama,
cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ taane.
Tɔɔle-na o kwora kam
se ka yi balo na zoore naneo ni ne to we:
“Baŋa Wɛ ya mo jage Isarele dwi tiina bam o yage.
O nam wó jwoori o la-ba o ke daane.
O maa wó taa yere-ba
ne nayero na nii o pei-kɔgɔ baŋa ne tei to.”
11Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ mo lage o jwoŋi Jakob dwi tiina o yage.
O wó vere-ba o ja o nwoŋi
balo na dana ba dwoi-ba to jeŋa ne.
12Ba laam maa wó jwoori ba ba
ba zege Zion peo kom yuu ne,
ye ba leeni de kwor-dɛa.
Ba wó taa di ywoni mo
Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ba wo-laaro telo to ŋwaane.
Tento maa ye mena, de sa-doora, de nuga,
de vare-mɔra.
Ba ta wó taa nye de gaare delo na na yage da ye de zura to mo.
Ba vɔna daa bá pare maŋa de maŋa.
13 Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento:
“Bukɔ-pwoli sem wó taa sae de wopwolo.
Baara bam de nam bá maŋe kwaga ne,
nɔn-donno, de nɔn-kwe de.
Amo wó pa se ba keira kam pipiri ka ji mwanno.
A ta wó fɔge-ba de wopwolo,
se ko leiri ba wo-chechɔgɔ kom yuu ne mo.
14Amo wó pa se kaanem tiina bam ŋwea su de ywoni,
se a daare a pa a nɔɔna bam wo-laaro telo maama ba na lage to.”
15 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Sɔɔ mo zaŋe Rama teo wone.
Nɔɔna mo wora ba keera,
ye ba chwoosa dedɛ.
Racheli mo tiini o keeri o bia bam ŋwaane.
O maa ba sɛ se nɔɔn-nɔɔno ja‑o,
ba daa na tera to ŋwaane.”
16 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we:
“Daa‑n yé ta‑n keera.
Nam weeri n yi-na bam,
se nmo wó na n totoŋa yam nyɔɔre.
Amo wó jwoŋi n bia bam n dona bam jeŋa ne
a pa ba jwoori ba tete teo ne.
17Teena wora ko pae á kwaga kam.
Abam bia bam wó jwoori ba tete teo kom ne
se ba taa zoore da.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.
18“Amo nigi Efrayim tiina wo na chɔge ye ba we,
‘Nmo Baŋa Wɛ waare debam
ye dé sɛ nmo koresem dem.
Dé déem nye de na-bala kalo ta na wo toŋe to mo.
Nam pa debam chwoŋa
se dé jwoori dé ba n tei.
Dé maa wó seene dé ba,
bɛŋwaane nmo mo ye debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ.
19Dé ya ywori chwoŋa mo.
Dé nam chuli dé wɛleera yam.
Dé boboŋa laam na jwoori to,
mo dé mage dé takeira wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane.
Chaveera ma di debam, ye dé yuu yaale,
wo-zɔɔna yalo dé na ke dé nɔn-donne maŋa ne to ŋwaane.’
20Efrayim ye amo bu-swono
kolo na jei amo bochare ne to mo.
A yeini a ŋɔɔne ta-balwaaro a pa‑o.
De ko de, a nam ta yɔɔre a swoi‑o mo.
Amo boboŋa vei o seeni maŋa maama mo,
ye a tiini a jege o ŋwaŋa,”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.
21“Tiŋi-na memaŋa chwei sem nia ne,
se ko pa á yé tusi chwoŋa kam ne.
Fɔge á lɔre chwo-fara kalo á déem na tɔge da
ye á kɛ to.
A nɔn-swonnu Isarele tiina bam,
nam jwoori-na se á zo á teene dem wone.
22Á nwoŋi amo kwaga ne,
ne bukɔ wolo na ve o kwo to.
Á wó ta‑á jege boboŋa yalei taa se á vo á maŋe yei ne mo
se á laam kwei chwoŋa á jwoori amo tei?
Baŋa Wɛ nam lage o ke wo-doŋo logo baŋa ne,
nenɛɛne kaana na cho baara cham wone tei to mo.”
Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna wó na yazura
23Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo ná jaane a nɔɔna bam se ba jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo, Judah tiina bam daa wó ta ba teene dem maama ne we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ swolim taa wo Jerusalem baŋa ne! Wɛ wó ke zaane o di-laao kom de o tete peo kolo na ye wose to baŋa ne!’
24Nɔɔna bam wó taa zoore daane Judah laŋa kam de ka teene dem maama ne, ko ta woli de vala, de nayera. 25Ko ná ye balo na bugi to, amo wó pa se ba yera zuri. Ko ta ná ye balo na beiri to, a wó pa ba di ba su. 26Mo kokuri ba wó ta we, ‘Amo na zaŋe dɔɔm wone ye a nii a kaare a maama to, a dɔɔm dem ke-ne ywoni.’ ”
27 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Nii-na! Maŋa kaage ka yi se amo pa Isarele dwi tiina de Judah dwi tiina puli. Nabiina de vara wó taa daga ba tega kam ne. 28Amo déem mo pɛ se ba wonnu gɔ te yage, se te maama dole te yage kafɛ ye te chɔge. A ta ma ja cham de lɛɛro a ba a pa-ba. De konto maama de, a nam ta wó jwoori a jeiri-ba te-ywoŋa jei ne, ye a daare a fɔge a lɔ-ba a zege lanyerane. 29Maŋa kam konto ná yia, nɔɔna daa bá taa tɛ ba we:
‘Kwoa mo ke ba wonnu,
pa te zem laam gwori ba bia.’
30Ko nam na wó taa ye tei to, nɔɔno maama wɛleera wó taa wo ba tete yuu ne, pa se ba te ya ŋwaane. Konto to, wolo ná done Vini tio bi-kanywaano tem, kotu tete yeila mo wó taa ŋaara.”
31 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Chega to, maŋa lage ka yi se amo jwoori a gwoni ni de Isarele dwi tiina bam de Judah dwi tiina bam, se ko taa ye amo ni-doore. 32Dento nam bá taa ye bedwe de ni delo a déem na gwoni de ba nabaara bam maŋa kalo a déem na mɛ a jeŋa a ja-ba a nwoŋi Ejipti ne to. Kokuri to, ba déem chɔge a ni-gwonim dem konto mo, de amo na maŋe a swoi-ba dedɛ, ne baaro na jege o kaane swono tei to.”
Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we:
33“Maŋa kam ná yia, ni delo amo na wó gwoni de Isarele dwi tiina bam to mo tento:
Amo wó kwei a nia yam a tiŋi ba boboŋa ne mo,
ye a daare a popone-ya a yage ba bochara wone.
Amo laam maa wó taa ye ba Wɛ,
se ba de taa ye amo nɔɔna.
34Ko daa bá taa ye fefeo se ba wolowolo bere o dwonna, naa se o ta de o chorro we, ba lɔre-na Baŋa Wɛ. Kolo ŋwaane, nɔɔna maama wó taa yei amo, ko ná maŋe ko ye nabwona de dedɛɛra de. Amo laam maa wó kwei ba keim-lwanno tem a ma chɛ-ba. A daa bá guli ba wɛleera yam gula.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.
35 Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na yeini o pa wea nye
pa pwooni wora dɛ dem wone to mo.
O ma daare o pa chana kam de chalechwe sem nye,
se se taa pae pwooni tete ne.
O ná yeini o yuŋi naneo kom,
ko pae se na-ŋone sem wuuri mo.
O yere nam mo ye Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ.
36Wonto ma ta o we:
“Amo wó sɛ se wonnu tento maama taa toŋa dɛ dɛ.
Te ta ná wora, Isarele dwi dem wó taa ye teo kolo na zega,
pa se ko nɔn-bia bam taa ye amo nɔɔna.
37Ne ba na ware wɛyuu kom se ba maŋe ko ni ba ti to,
ye nɔɔna ta yeiri tega kuri ni na mae tei to,
konto nam mo amo de bá ve Isarele dwi tiina bam
ba totoŋ-balwaaro ŋwaane.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
38 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we:
“Maŋa lage ka yi ba na wó fɔge ba lɔ Jerusalem teo kom ba pa-ne. Ba nam wó zege Hananeli di-dedɔrɔ kom ne mo, ba lɔ ba yi Gugworo Ni dem. 39Teo kom siseini dem wó zege dáane mo de yɔɔre de vo de yi Gareba zwoŋo kom, se de laam gugwoli de vo de yi Goa. 40Jei sem maama wó taa ye wose mo amo Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane, ko ná maŋe ko ye bwolo kom ba na suli twa ye ba lwoi tentwarem da to, de pwoli selo na vei Kidoron nabara kam seeni to, se ko taa vei wɛ-puli seeni ko yi Sisein-nɔɔno Ni dem gugworo kom. Ba daa bá gɔ teo kom konto ba de tega ne, ba nam bá chɔge-ko.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Buys a Field
1 The Lord spoke to me in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia. 2At that time, the Babylonian army had surrounded Jerusalem, and I was in the prison at the courtyard of the palace guards. 3Zedekiah had ordered me to be held there because I told everyone that the Lord had said:
I am the Lord, and I am about to let the king of Babylonia conquer Jerusalem. 4King Zedekiah will be captured and taken to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will speak with him face to face. 5Then Zedekiah will be led away to Babylonia, where he will stay until I am finished with him. So, if you people of Judah fight against the Babylonians, you will lose. I, the Lord, have spoken.
6Later, when I was in prison, the Lord said:
7Jeremiah, your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, will visit you. He must sell his field near the town of Anathoth, and because you are his nearest relative, you have the right and the responsibility to buy it and keep it in the family.
8Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.”
The Lord had told me to buy it 9from Hanamel, and so I did. The price was 17 pieces of silver, and I weighed out the full amount on a scale. 10-11I had two copies of the bill of sale written out: an official copy containing the details of our agreement and another copy, without the details. Some witnesses and I signed the official copy, which was folded and tied, before being sealed shut with hot wax. Then I gave Hanamel the silver. 12And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
13-14I told Baruch that the Lord had said:
Take both copies of this bill of sale, one sealed shut and the other open, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time. 15I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country.
Jeremiah Questions the Lord
16Then I prayed:
17 Lord God, you stretched out your mighty arm and made the sky and the earth. You can do anything. 18You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful. 19With great wisdom you make plans, and with your great power you do all the mighty things you planned. Nothing we do is hidden from your eyes, and you reward or punish us as we deserve.
20You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well. 21You terrified the Egyptians with your miracles, and you reached out your mighty arm and rescued your people Israel from Egypt. 22Then you gave Israel this land rich with milk and honey, just as you had promised our ancestors.
23But when our ancestors took over the land, they did not obey you. And now you have punished Israel with disaster. 24Jerusalem is under attack, and we suffer from hunger and disease. The Babylonians have already built dirt ramps up to the walls of our city, and you can see that Jerusalem will be captured just as you said.
25So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians?
The Lord Explains about the Field
26The Lord explained:
27Jeremiah, I am the Lord God. I rule the world, and I can do anything!
28 It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem. 29The Babylonian army is already attacking, and they will capture the city and set it on fire. The people of Jerusalem have made me angry by going up to the flat roofs of their houses and burning incense to Baal and offering wine sacrifices to other gods. Now these houses will be burned to the ground!
30-33The kings and the officials, the priests and the prophets, and everyone else in Israel and Judah have turned from me and made me angry by worshiping idols. Again and again I have tried to teach my people to obey me, but they refuse to be corrected.
I am going to get rid of Jerusalem, because its people have done nothing but evil. 34 They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me. 35 And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
36Jeremiah, what you said is true. The people of Jerusalem are suffering from hunger and disease, and so the king of Babylonia will be able to capture Jerusalem.
37I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety. 38They will be my people, and I will be their God. 39-41I will make their thoughts and desires pure. Then they will realize that, for their own good and the good of their children, they must worship only me. They will even be afraid to turn away from me. I will make an agreement with them that will never end, and I won't ever stop doing good things for them. With all my heart I promise that they will be planted in this land once again. 42Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
43Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals. 44But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jeremia na yeigi tega tei to
1 Baŋa Wɛ daa na pɛ Jeremia ni delo to mo tento. Ko déem ke ko maŋe de Judah teo pɛ Zedekia na jege bena fuga o paare dim wone to mo. Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza paare dim bena fuga-nana bene dem wone mo konto.
2Maŋa kam konto ne, Babilon teo pɛ jar-keira bam mo tu ba kaare Jerusalem teo kom ba pu, de ba déem jaane Wɛ sampwora Jeremia ba pe Judah pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne. 3Judah teo pɛ Zedekia mo pe‑o da, Jeremia déem na pworisi wonnu telo Jerusalem seeni to ŋwaane. Zedekia déem ya bwɛ Jeremia o we, “Bɛ mo ye n bere we n jwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ kwora we, o lage o kwei teo kom o ke Babilon teo pɛ jeŋa ne mo se o di-ko?” 4Jeremia ta tage Baŋa Wɛ kwora we, “Pɛ Zedekia bá lu Babilon tiina bam jeŋa ne. Ba wó ja‑o ba vo ba pa Babilon teo pɛ mo se ba ŋɔɔne daane. 5Ba laam wó ja Zedekia ba vo Babilon. O nam wó taa wo dáane mo se amo laam ba a waare‑o. Abam ná kwaane á jaŋe de Babilon teo tiina bam, á lage á to mo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.”
6Konto maama kwaga ne, Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta de Jeremia o we, 7“Nmo kwo choro Salum bu Hanameli wó ba n tei o ta dede‑m we, ‘Amo boŋe se a kwei a kara kalo na wo Anatofe ne to mo a yeigi a pa‑m. Nmo maŋe se n yeigi-ka, nmo na ye amo yera nɔɔno to ŋwaane.’ ”
8Ko na ke da yalei to, amo choro Hanameli ma seene o ba a tei mɛ ba na pe-ne pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne to, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na wuuri o ta o bere-ne tei to. O ma ta de amo o we, “Amo boŋe se a kwei a kara kam na wo Anatofe ne, Benjamin kateiri dem ne to mo a yeigi a pa‑m. Nmo maŋe se n yeigi-ka se ka taa ye nmo nyem. Nam yeigi-ka n ta‑n tei.”
Ko na ke konto to, amo ma lɔre we ko ye Baŋa Wɛ kwora chekke mo a niga. 9A ma yeigi a choro kara kam na wo Anatofe ne to o tei ne, ye a jeeli lu-nyenno sabu-dala fuga-yarepɛ se a pa‑o ka ŋwaane. 10A ta ma popone a yere tega kam tɔnɔ wone, ye a daare a zi a jeŋa ko baŋa ne. Nɔɔna badwonna ma nii ye ba sɛ a na ke tei to. Amo ma maŋe tega kam sabu se ko taa ye chekke. 11Amo laam ma kwei tɔnɔ kolo a na zi ye tega kam yera seina wo te wone to, dedaane tɔnɔ kodwoŋi na lwoni-ko ye ko ta puri to 12a pa Neria bu Baruki. O déem ye Maseya naa mo. A na pɛ‑o twanno telei tem konto to, mo a choro Hanameli nɛa, ko ta woli de nɔɔna balo na maane a keim dem ye ba popone ba yera tɔnɔ kom wone to, de Judah tiina balo maama na wo pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne to. 13Banto maama na zege da ye ba cheigi to mo a pɛ Baruki ni ye a we: 14“Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: ‘Kwei twanno tento dé na popone tega kam yeilo ŋwaane to, se n laam ke-te kambia wone se te maŋe da bena dedɛ. Ke konto de tɔnɔ kolo ba na zi ba je ko baŋa ne to, de ko dwoŋi kom ta na puri to.’ 15Kokuri to, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: ‘Maŋa wó ba se nɔɔna daa jwoori ba yeigi sam, de kare, de Vini kare teo konto wone.’ ”
Jeremia wɛ-lworo
16A na kwei twanno tem a pa Neria bu Baruki a ti to, mo a lwoori Baŋa Wɛ a we:
17“Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo dɛ n dam-fɔrɔ kom baŋa ne n toŋe wo-kamunnu mo n ke wɛyuu kom, de tega baŋa maama. Kolokolo nam tera ko na tiini ko chamma ko dwoi nmo keim. 18Nmo yɔɔre n jege swono mo n pae nɔɔna morro dedɛ. N nam ta pae bia yaare ba kwoa wɛleera ŋwaane. N ye Wɛ-kamunu mo ye n dam de gaale. N yere dem mo ye Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ. 19N yeini n tɔge yeino dwi maama baŋa ne mo n ke totoŋ-kamunnu. Nmo yei nabiina maama kikia na ye tei to. N ma‑n ŋwe-ba se ko maŋe de chwei selo ba na tɔge to de kikia yalo ba na toŋe to. 20Nmo déem ke totoŋ-kamunnu de wo-kenkagela Ejipti wone. Totoŋa yanto dwoŋi mo n ta jege n ke de zem maama Isarele tiina de dwi-gɛ tiina maama tei ne. Mo kokuri n yere zaŋe jei maama ne de zem. 21Nmo tɔge n dam baŋa ne n toŋe wo-kamunnu dedaane wo-kenkagela se n ma‑n fugi Ejipti tiina bam ye n daare n vere n nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam ba jeŋa ne n yage. 22N ma‑n kwei tega kanto n déem na gwoni ni ka ŋwaane de ba nabaara bam to n pa-ba. Ka maa ye tega kalo na ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ to. 23Ba de na tu ba jwoŋi-ka to, ba wo sɛ nmo nia yam. Ba bere ba wo tɔge chwei selo n na bere-ba to. Ko ná ye wonnu telo n na pɛ-ba ni se ba taa ke to, ba wo ke te kolokolo. Konto ŋwaane nam mo tei n pɛ lɛɛro tento maama ba ba baŋa ne.
24Nii-na! Babilon tiina bam lɔge taare kamuna ba yeiri dé teo kom kabiri sem yera ne mo se ba tɔge-ya ba zo teo kom ba di debam. Jara-keim, de kana, de jawe-chɛɛro wó chɔge debam. Dé teo kom laam wo Babilon jar-keira bam jeŋa ne mo se ba wane debam. Nmo Baŋa Wɛ na tage we kolo wó yi debam to laam mo to dé baŋa ne, ye nmo tete nɛ-ko. 25Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo yei we ko bá dáane se Babilon tiina bam di dam dé teo kom baŋa ne. N nam ta pɛ amo ni se a kwei lu-nyenno a ma yeigi kara kam, se nɔɔna de maane a keim dem konto ye ba zi ba je ko ŋwaane.”
26 Baŋa Wɛ daa na pɛ Jeremia ni delo to mo tento:
27“Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom. A nam ye nabiina bam maama Wɛ mo. Woŋo wora ko na tiini ko chamma ko dwoi amo keim na? 28Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: A lage a kwei teo konto mo a ke Pɛ Nebukadeneza de o jar-keira bam jeŋa ne se ba di-ko. 29Jar-keira balo na tu se ba kwaare jara de teo kom to wó zo teo kom wone ye ba daare ba zwɛ-ko. Ba maa wó pa se mini di sam delo nɔɔna na diini de nayuni baŋa ne ye ba zwɛ wonnu ba ma ke kaanem ba pa Baal jwoni dem ba daare ba kwei sana pɛɛra ba pa wa yadwonna to. Ba totoŋa yam konto pɛ se a bane zaŋe ba baŋa ne mo.
30Judah dwi tiina de Isarele dwi tiina bam yɔɔre ba toŋe lwarem kikia amo yiga ne mo ko zege ba nɔn-donne maŋa ne se ko yi zem maama. Ba je na ke wonnu telo to yeini te chuchugi amo bane mo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto. 31Ba na maŋe ba chwi teo kom kuri to mo ko nɔn-bia bam bobo se ba taa ke kolo na wó zaŋe a bane to. Ko laam nam yi se a chɔge-ko, pa se ko jei a yiga ne. 32Isarele tiina bam de Judah tiina bam pae a bane mo yɔɔre de zaŋa de ba lwarem kikia yam. Ko maa ye ba pwa, de ba nakwa, de ba kaanem tiina, de ba sampwori sem, de balo maama na zoore Jerusalem teo kom de Judah laŋa kam maama ne to mo chuchugi a bane. 33Ba mɛ ba kwaga ba ya amo, ye ba yiga tera a wone. Amo yɔɔre a bere-ba maŋa maama mo. Ba nam wo cheigi a taane dem. Ba maa wo sɛ se a korese-ba. 34Ba kwei wo-zɔɔna yalo ba na zuli to ba zege diga kalo na wora a yere zula ŋwaane to wone, ye ba da ko ŋwaane ba chɔge-ka. 35Ba ta ma lɔ bimbina Ben-Hinom bwolo kom ne, ye ba zuli Baal jwoni dem ya baŋa ne. Ba maa yeini ba kwei ba bia ba zwɛ mini wone ba ke kaanem ba pa Moleka jwoni dem. Amo nam wo fɔge a pa-ba ni se ba ke konto. Keim-lɔŋɔ kom konto dwoŋi maŋe ko wo tu a boboŋa ne. Ba nam jege konto mo ba ke, pa se Judah tiina bam maama tiini ba tusi.
36Abam yeini á tɛ teo konto taane á we, ‘Jara-keim, de kana, de jawe-chɛɛro mo lage te chɔge teo kom pa se ko taa wo Babilon teo pɛ jeŋa ne se o wane-ko.’ Amo Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom nam na tage tei to mo tento: 37Ko ná ye jei selo maama a na wó zeili a nɔɔna bam a yage da a ban-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane to, a daa ta wó la-ba a zege da a ja a jwoori ba teo kom, se ba taa zoore ywo de yazura. 38Ba maa wó taa ye a nɔɔna, se amo de taa ye ba Tu Wɛ wom. 39A maa wó pa ba taa jege boboŋe dedwe ba ŋwea wone, pa se ba taa kɔre amo taa wuu. Ba wó ke konto se ko taa lana ko pae ba tete de ba kwaga kam. 40A ta wó ke ni-gwonim delo na wó taa wora taa wuu to de-ba. Amo wó pwooli se a taa ke-ba lanyerane taa wuu. A maa wó pa se ba taa kɔre amo de ba wo maama, se ba daa yé nwoŋi a kwaga ne. 41Ko wó ke amo ywoni se a taa ke-ba lanyerane. A maa wó fɔge a jeiri-ba tega kanto ne de a wo maama.
42Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo seene a ja lɛɛro tento maama a ba a de nɔɔna bam wone. De konto maama a nam wó pa-ba yu-ywoŋo ne a na gwoni ni we a wó pa-ba tei to. 43Abam yeini á ta jei sento taane mo á we, ‘Babilon jar-keira bam tu se ba chɔge tega kam. Ka lage ka ji di-dwonnu yerane, mɛ nabiina de vara na tera ka wone to.’ De ko de, nɔɔna daa wó yeigi tega ywo-seeni. 44Chega to, nɔɔna wó kwei lu-nyenno ba ma yeigi tega jei sento wone. Ba ta wó popone tega kam twanno, ye ba daare ba zi ba je te baŋa ne. Nɔɔna badaara wó maane ba keim dem ye ba de zi ba je ko ŋwaane. Ko nam wó ke konto mo Benjamin kateiri dem ne, de Jerusalem nawuura yam ne, de Judah teene dem ne, ko ta woli de zwonnu laŋa kam seeni, de wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne, de tega-kuri kagoa kam seeni maama. Kokuri to, amo wó jwoori a pa se a nɔɔna bam jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.”

english_text:
The Lord Promises To Give the Land Back to His People
1-2I was still being held prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guards when the Lord told me:
I am the Lord, and I created the whole world. 3Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
4-5Many of the houses in Jerusalem and some of the buildings at the royal palace have been torn down to be used in repairing the walls to keep out the Babylonian attackers. Now there are empty spaces where the buildings once stood. But I am furious, and these spaces will be filled with the bodies of the people I kill. The people of Jerusalem will cry out to me for help, but they are evil, and I will ignore their prayers.
6Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace. 7I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before. 8They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt. 9When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
10Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear 11 happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say:
“We praise you,
Lord All-Powerful!
You are good to us,
and your love never fails.”
The land will once again be productive. 12-13Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord's Wonderful Promise
14 The Lord said:
I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
15I promise that the time will come
when I will appoint a king
from the family of David,
a king who will be honest
and rule with justice.
16In those days,
Judah will be safe;
Jerusalem will have peace
and will be named,
“The Lord Gives Justice.”
17 The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants, 18 and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
19Then the Lord told me:
20I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them, 21and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel, 22and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
23The Lord also said:
24You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
25Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands. 26In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_text:
Wɛ wó pa o nɔɔna jwoori ba na yazura
1Ba déem ta na pe Jeremia ba yage pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne to, mo Baŋa Wɛ daa pɛ‑o o kwora o ke kuni belei ye o we: 2Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na naane tega baŋa maama to. O ma fɔge o mɔ-ka o daare o chwi-ka o zege cheppe. Wonto yere mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. O nam tage tento mo o we:
3“Bwoŋi-na amo yere, se a wó leiri abam. A ta wó bere abam wo-kamunnu telo ya na seigi ye á yeiri te ni ne to.”
4Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom daa tage Jerusalem teo kom sam de Judah pɛ sɔ-fwaaro tem taane mo ye o we:
“Ba yigi sam dem ba de tega ne, se ba ma ba kwɛ teo kom kabira kam, se ba wane ba che Babilon jar-keira bam se ba yé zo teo kom wone. 5Á nam ná ke jara de-ba, á teo kom wó su de twa ye á suli-ba di-dwonnu tem wone. Kokuri to, amo jaane boboŋa se á yɔɔre a chɔge-ba mo, a bane na zaŋe de-ba to ŋwaane. Amo yiga daa bá taa wo teo kom nɔn-bia bam wone, ba lwarem kikia yam ŋwaane.
6Nii-na! Dɛ nam ta wora se amo jwoori a fɔge a kwɛ teo kom. Amo wó yɔɔre a nɔɔna bam pa se ba taa zoore de yazura zurim wone. 7Amo wó pa se Judah tiina bam de Isarele tiina bam jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo, ye a pa ba fɔge ba zege de dam ne ba déem na ye tei to. 8Wɛleera yalo maama ba na ke ba chɔge a yiga to, a lage a saare-ya a yage mo. Ba na nwoŋi amo kwaga ne to, a nam ta wó kwei ba tusim dem konto a ma a chɛ-ba. 9Maŋa kam konto ne, Jerusalem teo kom wó pa a na yere logo baŋa teene maama wone. Amo wó na wopwolo, de zula, de nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ mo teo kom konto ŋwaane. Dwi tiina maama wó lɔre wo-laaro telo a na wó kwei a pa a nɔɔna bam to ni ne. Banto ná nɛ a na fɔge teo kom de yazura tei to, ko wó so-ba ye ba yera de taa sae.”
10 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Abam kare á tɛ we, ‘Teo konto yɔɔre ko ji di-dwonnu yerane mo pa se nabiina de vara maama jei ka wone.’ Chega to, Jerusalem teo chwei sem ne de Judah teene dem maama wone, nabiina de vara seene ba tera. Ko nam na wó taa ye tei to, jei sem konto ne mo abam daa lage á ni 11wopwolo de mwanno sɔɔ na zaŋe. Kadiri ywoni de daa wó taa wora. Ba maa wó ja lei-keim pɛɛra ba ba Baŋa Wɛ ware-jei sem ne, ye ba leeni we:
‘Pa-na se dé ke Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ lei,
se Baŋa Wɛ lamma!
O swono kom de maa wora taa wuu.’
Kokuri to, amo wó jwoori a pa se tega kanto na yu-ywoŋo, ne ka déem na jege tei to.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.
12Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Tega kam laam seene ka daare di-dwonnu yerane mo ka tiga, pa se nabiina de vara daa tere ka wone. Ka nam wó jwoori ka kwi de ga-lɛɛro se nayera ja ba vara ba vo da ba kɔne. 13Ko ná ye zwonnu laŋa kam ne, de wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne, de tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam ne, de Benjamin laŋa kam ne, dedaane Jerusalem nawuura yam de Judah laŋa kam maama ne, jei sem konto teene maama wone mo vara bam wó puli lanyerane ye nayera bam jeeli ba ni.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
14 Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta o we:
“Maŋa lage ka yi se amo ke a su ni delo a déem na gwoni de Isarele dwi tiina dedaane Judah dwi tiina bam we a wó zeini-ba to.
15Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia,
amo wó pa David dwi dem puli naga dedoa
ye kotu wó taa ye nɔn-ŋom mo.
O ta wó taa tɔge chega de o na ke tei de nɔɔna to mo
tega kam maama baŋa ne.
16O paare dim maŋa ne, Judah tiina wó na verem,
ye Jerusalem tiina de taa zoore de yazura.
Nɔɔna maa wó taa bwoi teo kom yere we,
‘Baŋa Wɛ mo bore debam bora de chega.’
17Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: David dwi dem daa bá ga nɔɔno se kotu yeini o jeini o di Isarele teo paare. 18Kaanem tiina bam na nwoŋi Levi dwi dem ne to de wó taa wora maŋa maama mo, se ba taa ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de wodiu pɛɛra, de kaanem dwi dwi ba pa-ne.”
19 Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma pa Jeremia ni ye o we:
20“Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo gwoni ni de wea kam de tete dem, se tento taa tui dɛ maama te maŋa ne. Abam wó wane á chɔge ni-gwonim dem konto na? 21Á ya ná wane á chɔge-de, á ya wó wane ni-gwonim delo a na ke de a tontoŋeno David to dedaane delo a na ke de Levi tiina bam to á chɔge. Ko nam na ye tei to, maŋa maama nɔɔno wó taa wora o na wó nwoŋi Pɛ David dwi dem wone se o di paare. Levi tiina de wó taa wora se ba taa ye kaanem tiina ba pa-ne. 22Ko ná ye a tontoŋeno David dwi dem, de Levi dwi dem na kaane ba pa-ne to, a lage a pa ba puli mo ne wɛyuu chalechwe sem na daga tei to. Ba ni bá wane de ga de ti, ne naneo ni kasolo bia na ye tei to.”
23 Baŋa Wɛ daa ma pa Jeremia ni ye o we:
24“N wo nɛ na? Nɔɔna badwonna jege a nɔɔna bam ba twe ye ba we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ laam virigi o kwaga o ya dwia yalei yam o ya na kuri to.’ Ba yeini ba ta konto dwoŋi, ye ba boŋe we a nɔɔna bam daa ba jege kuri mo. 25Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Ni-gwonim delo a na ke de wea kam, de tete dem to yɔɔre de zege mo chekke. A ta ma pa se wɛyuu de tega baŋa taa tɔge chwei selo na yɔɔre se maŋe de-te to. 26Ko ta ye bedwe mo, amo bá ve Jakob dwi dem kɔtaa. A bá swei se a kuri nɔɔno a tontoŋeno David dwi tiina bam wone, se kotu di paare a nɔɔna bam baŋa ne. Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob dwi tiina bam mo konto. A wó jwoori a pa se a nɔɔna bam taa jege yu-ywoŋo. A maa wó duri ba yibwona.”

english_text:
Jeremiah Warns Zedekiah
1 King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me 2to say to King Zedekiah:
I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down. 3You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
