People of Judah Taken Prisoner
28-30Here is a list of the number of the people of Judah that Nebuchadnezzar took to Babylonia as prisoners:
In his seventh year as king, he took 3,023 people.
In his eighteenth year as king, he took 832 from Jerusalem.
In his twenty-third year as king, his officer Nebuzaradan took 745 people.
So, Nebuchadnezzar took a total of 4,600 people from Judah to Babylonia.
Jehoiachin Is Set Free
(2 Kings 25.27-30)
31Jehoiachin was a prisoner in Babylon for 37 years. Then Evil Merodach became king of Babylonia, and in the first year of his rule, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, he let Jehoiachin out of prison. 32Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there. 33Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day. 34As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_text:
Jerusalem teo na to tei to
2 Pwa 24:18–25:7
1Zedekia déem jege bena finlei-dedwe mo ye o ji Judah teo pɛ. O ma jeini Jerusalem ne o di paare dem o ke bena fuga-dedwe. O nu yere mo Hamutali. Wonto maa ye Jeremia wolo na nwoŋi Libina to bukɔ mo. 2Pɛ Zedekia déem toŋe lwarem mo o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga, ne Pɛ Jehoyakim de ya na ke tei to. 3Lɛɛro telo maama na ke Jerusalem de Judah tiina bam maama yera ne to tɔge Baŋa Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane mo. O ma yɔɔre o zeili-ba o yiga ne, ba kikia yam ŋwaane.
Pɛ Zedekia déem ma zaŋe o nwoŋi Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza kwaga ne. 4O paare dim bena nogo bene dem chane fuga chana kam wone, ka da fuga dɛ dem ne mo Nebukadeneza déem tu o li Jerusalem de o jar-keira bam maama. Ba ma kaare ba pu teo kom ye ba daare ba lɔ taare-kamuna ba yeiri ko kabiri sem yera ne. 5Ko na yi Zedekia paare dim bena fuga-dedoa bene dem to, mo Babilon tiina bam déem wane Jerusalem teo kom ba di.
6Ko na yi bene dem konto chane sena chana kam da nogo dɛ dem to, kana déem tiini ka chɛ mo pa se Jerusalem nɔn-bia bam daa ba jege wodiu se ba taa di. 7Babilon tiina bam ma bwori teo kom kabiri sem ba de tega ne, ye ba tɔge pwoli sem ne ba zo ko wo. Zedekia de o jar-keira bam maama déem duri se ba lu tete ne mo. Ba ma kwei pɛ gaare chwoŋa kam, ba vo ba tɔge ni dem na wo teo kabiri selei sem tetare ne to, ye ba laam duri ba tu Jɔdan bwolo kom seeni. 8De ko de, Babilon tiina jar-keira bam déem pare-ba mo. Ba ma vo ba yi Zedekia se ko maŋe de Jeriko te-kampare sem seeni. O jar-keira bam ma pwɛ da yiga ne, ye ba jage ba daare‑o.
9Ba ma zi Zedekia ba ja ba vo Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza tei. O déem wo Ribila teo ne mo, Hamafa kateiri dem ne. Nebukadeneza ma di taane o vane Zedekia dáane. 10O ma pa ba go Zedekia bia bam Ribila ne, ye o zege da o nia. O ta ma pa ba go Judah teo dedɛɛra bam maama. 11Ko kwaga ne o pɛ se ba kokɔrege Zedekia yia yam mo ba le, ye ba daare ba kwei channa chegero ba ma ba vɔ‑o ba vaŋe ba ja ba vo Babilon. O na yi da to, ba ma ke‑o peena diga ne se o maŋe da o te.
12Nebukadeneza déem na di Babilon teo paare o ke bena fuga-nogo bene delo ne to, chane senu chana kam da fuga dɛ dem ne mo o kwaga-saŋeno Nebuzaradan zo Jerusalem teo kom wone. Wonto maa ye Babilon teo babɛ sem yiga tu. 13O déem ma pa ba zwɛ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam, de pɛ sɔŋɔ kom, de Jerusalem sam dem maama. Ba déem zwɛ sɔ-laao dwi maama mo Jerusalem teo wone. 14Nebuzaradan ma pa ni pa o jar-keira bam yɔɔre ba yigi Jerusalem teo kabiri sem maama ba de tega ne. 15O ma kale yiniga tiina badwonna, de balo ta na daare teo kom wone to, ko ta woli de gwaro ta na daare to, de balo na duri ba zo Babilon tiina kɔgɔ kom wone to o ja o vo Babilon. 16Ko nam ná ye teo kom yiniga tiina badaara bam, Nebuzaradan ma yage-ba Judah laŋa kam ne. O ma pa-ba tega se ba va, de Vini teeni kare, se ba taa nii se baŋa ne.
17Babilon tiina bam ma zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ba bwori channa zela yam maama. Yanto maa ye ywoa yalei yam, de ware-zon-zɔŋɔ kolo ba na bwoi we ‘Naneo kom’ to, de ware-zwe zegem torokooro tem. Ba ma daare ba kwei te channa kam ba zeŋe ba ja ba vo Babilon. 18Ba ta ma kwei zwe selo ba na wó taa mae ba pɛ tentwarem to, de sɛbullu, de wonnu telo na wó fɔge te kwɛ mini dem to, de zwe selo na jege se lwori jana to, de selo ba na zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa se wone to, de channa wonnu telo maama na jege te fɔge Wɛ diga chullu tem to ba woli da. 19Nebuzaradan ta ma pa ba kwei Wɛ diga zela yalo maama ba na mɛ sabu-seŋa, naa lu-nyenno ba ke-ya to. Tento maa ye zon-balɛ, de min-chala zwe, de zwe selo ba na wó ma ba zezage na bimbini dem baŋa ne to, de kambi, de min-zwon-zegero, de zom-bi, de zwe selo ba na mae ba lwoi wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛra to.
20Ko ná ye ywoa yalei yam, de ware-zon-zɔŋɔ kom, de ko nabɛ nyenyero fuga-telei telo na zeŋe-ko to, dedaane ware-zwe zegem torokooro tem, Pɛ Solomon déem ya pɛ ba mɔ wonnu tem konto maama Baŋa Wɛ diga chullu tem ŋwaane mo. Te yera channa kam déem tiini ka dumma ka dwoi maŋem. 21Ywoa yalei yam dedoa wɛ-baŋa seeni dedɔrem déem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga-nana mo. Ya yera kikilu maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga belei. Ba déem mɔɔne-ya se ya taa ye wogo mo. Channa kam liliru maa ye nwe sena maŋem. 22Ywei maama yuu ne ba meeli channa wo-sugili mo da se de wane de teili diga kam yuu kom seeni. Wo-sugila yam dedoa dedoa dedɔrem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu mo. Ba mɛ channa mo ba sɔ ba lɛɛne daane ba ke da, ye ba gɔgere Pomegara tio-bia ba kaare wo-sugila yam. Ywoa yalei yam wo-sugila yam maama ye bedwe mo. 23Ywei maama yera ne, ba gɔgere Pomegara tio-bia bi mo, se nɔɔno ná zege tega ne ye kotu kwoni se o nii de sɛ sem, o nae funogo yaredo yerane mo.
24Nebuzaradan déem ta jaane Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu Seraya, de o kwaga-saŋeno Zefania, de Wɛ diga kam ni-yerena batɔ bam mo o ja o viiri. 25Ko ná ye balo ya ta na daare Jerusalem teo kom wone to, o ma kale ba jar-keira yiga tu wom, de nɔɔna barepɛ balo ya na bwola de pɛ wom to, de dedɛɛro wolo na le nɔɔna se o woli-ba jar-keira kɔgɔ kom wone to, de nɔɔna fuseredo balo ta na wora to o woli da o ja o viiri. 26Nebuzaradan déem jaane banto maama mo o vo Babilon teo pɛ wom tei. O déem wo Hamafa kateiri dem teo Ribila ne mo. 27Dáane mo Babilon teo pɛ déem pɛ se ba go nɔɔna bam konto maama.
Ko déem ke konto mo ye ba kale Judah dwi tiina bam ba ja ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga. 28Pɛ Nebukadeneza na kale balo maama o ja o vo Babilon teo to mo tento:
O paare dim bena yarepɛ bene dem ne
o kale Judah dwi tiina morro tetɔ de finlei-batɔ (3,023) o vo da.
29O paare dim bena fuga-nana bene dem ne
o ma kale Jerusalem tiina bia nana de fintɔ-balei (832) o vo da.
30O paare dim bena finlei-yatɔ bene dem ne
o babɛ sem yiga tu Nebuzaradan ma ja Judah dwi tiina bia yarepɛ de finna-banu (745) o vo da.
Nɔɔna balo ba na kale ba vo Babilon to ná ke daane,
ba ye morro tena de bia yaredo (4,600) mo.
Ba pore Jehoyachin ba yage
31Ba déem na kale Judah teo Pɛ Jehoyachin ba ja ba vo Babilon ye o daare o ke bena fintɔ-yarepɛ Babilon ne to, bene dem konto chane fuga-selei chana kam da finlei-yanu dɛ dem ne mo Babilon teo Pɛ Evil-merodaki ke Pɛ Jehoyachin zaane, ye o pore‑o peena diga ne o yage. Ko maa ye bene delo Evil-merodaki na bobo o di Babilon teo paare to mo o ke konto. 32O ma ke Pɛ Jehoyachin lanyerane, ye o pa‑o jeiŋa jei na tiini se jege zula se dwoi jei selo pwa babam bam na wo Babilon ne na nɛ to. 33Jehoyachin ma lɔɔre o peena diga gwaaro tem o tiŋi. O ŋwea kam dɛ maama wone o ma lɛɛre o di wodiu Babilon teo pɛ tei ne. 34Babilon teo pɛ ta ma kwei kolo maama Jehoyachin na wó ke o yera ne to o pa‑o dɛ maama, se ko vo ko yi o toone maŋa.

english_text:
Lonely Jerusalem
The Prophet Speaks:
1 Jerusalem, once so crowded,
lies deserted and lonely.
This city that was known
all over the world
is now like a widow.
This queen of the nations
has been made a slave.
2Each night, bitter tears
flood her cheeks.
None of her former lovers
are there to offer comfort;
her friends have betrayed her
and are now her enemies.
3The people of Judah are slaves,
suffering in a foreign land,
with no rest from sorrow.
Their enemies captured them
and were terribly cruel.
4The roads to Zion mourn
because no one travels there
to celebrate the festivals.
The city gates are deserted;
priests are weeping.
Young women are raped;
Zion is in sorrow!
5Enemies now rule the city
and live as they please.
The Lord has punished Jerusalem
because of her awful sins;
he has let her people
be dragged away.
6Zion's glory has disappeared.
Her leaders are like deer
that cannot find pasture;
they are hunted down
till their strength is gone.
7Her people recall the good life
that once was theirs;
now they suffer
and are scattered.
No one was there to protect them
from their enemies who sneered
when their city was taken.
8Jerusalem's horrible sins
have made the city a joke.
Those who once admired her
now hate her instead—
she has been disgraced;
she groans and turns away.
9Her sins had made her filthy,
but she wasn't worried
about what could happen.
And when Jerusalem fell,
it was so tragic.
No one gave her comfort
when she cried out,
“Help! I'm in trouble, Lord!
The enemy has won.”
10Zion's treasures were stolen.
Jerusalem saw foreigners
enter her place of worship,
though the Lord
had forbidden them
to belong to his people.
11Everyone in the city groans
while searching for food;
they trade their valuables
for barely enough scraps
to stay alive.
Jerusalem Speaks:
Jerusalem shouts to the Lord,
“Please look and see
how miserable I am!”
12No passerby even cares.
Why doesn't someone notice
my terrible sufferings?
You were fiercely angry, Lord,
and you punished me
worst of all.
13From heaven you sent a fire
that burned in my bones;
you set a trap for my feet
and made me turn back.
All day long you leave me
in shock from constant pain.
14You have tied my sins
around my neck,
and they weigh so heavily
that my strength is gone.
You have put me in the power
of enemies too strong for me.
15You, Lord, have turned back
my warriors and crushed
my young heroes.
Judah was a woman untouched,
but you let her be trampled
like grapes in a wine pit.
16Because of this, I mourn,
and tears flood my eyes.
No one is here to comfort
or to encourage me;
we have lost the war—
my people are suffering.
The Prophet Speaks:
17Zion reaches out her hands,
but no one offers comfort.
The Lord has turned
the neighboring nations
against Jacob's descendants.
Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag
to her neighbors.
Jerusalem Speaks:
18The Lord was right,
but I refused to obey him.
Now I ask all of you to look
at my sufferings—
even my young people
have been dragged away.
19I called out to my lovers,
but they betrayed me.
My priests and my leaders died
while searching the city
for scraps of food.
20Won't you look and see
how upset I am, our Lord?
My stomach is in knots,
and my heart is broken
because I betrayed you.
In the streets and at home,
my people are slaughtered.
21Everyone heard my groaning,
but no one offered comfort.
My enemies know of the trouble
that you have brought on me,
and it makes them glad.
Hurry and punish them,
as you have promised.
22Don't let their evil deeds
escape your sight.
Punish them as much
as you have punished me
because of my sins.
I never stop groaning—
I've lost all hope!
translation_text:
Wo-chechɔgɔ na yi Jerusalem tiina tei to
1Nii teo konto laam na tigi tei
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tere ko wone.
Ko déem nam su de nɔɔna mo!
Ko déem ye te-fɔrɔ mo logo baŋa teene dem wone.
Nii ko laam na ye ne kadeim tei!
Ko ya ye teene dem maama dedɛɛro mo,
ye ko laam to kabɛɛne wone.
2Teo kom nye de kaane wolo na yɔɔre o keeri mo.
Yi-na ma bɔɔre o keila yam tete dem maama wone.
O bɔɔla bam wolowolo nam tera
se kotu zuri o bochare.
O badwonna maama de ma baare o kwaga ne,
ye banto ji o dona.
3Judah tiina yaara yam de ba totoŋ-dɛɛra yam kwaga ne,
ba ta kale-ba mo ba ja ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga.
Ba laam maa zoore dwi-gɛ tiina tetare ne.
Ba daa ba jege mɛ ba na wó jeini se ba sii to.
Ba dona maama pare-ba ba ja mo.
Jeiga daa tera se ba duri ba vo ba jwoŋi ba tete.
4Nɔɔna daa ba tui ba zoore teo kom wone
se ba di kura Wɛ diga kam wone.
Konto ŋwaane chwei selo na vei se zoore Zion wone to de keeri mo.
Teo kom ni maama wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera.
Wɛ kaanem tiina yɔɔre ba vuvuni mo.
Ko bukwa bam wo ma chɔge,
kokuri to, teo kom cham dem kɛ jeŋa mo.
5Balo na ye Jerusalem dona to laam mo jigi ko yuu tiina.
Ba nam ba lwei de kolokolo.
Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ se cham dento yi teo kom,
ko wɛleera yam na tiini ya gaale to ŋwaane.
Ko dona bam yɔɔre ba di ko nɔn-bia bam mo jara wone,
ye ba daare ba pɛ-ba ba ja ba viiri.
6Zion nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom maama laam ti mo.
Teo kom dedɛɛra tiini ba bwona
ne wei na beeri gaao se ga se se di tei to.
Ba ma kwaane se ba duri ba dona yiga ne,
ye ba ware.
7Jerusalem na wo cham wone
ye o kare o beeri maŋa kalo to,
mo o guli o déem na jege ywoni delo o di to.
Ko ye o dendéem gula mo o guli.
O laam nam to o dona jeŋa ne mo,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se kotu woli‑o.
O dona bam maa nii,
ye ba jege‑o ba mɔna
de o na nɛ chɔgem to ŋwaane.
8Jerusalem yɔɔre o ke o tusi dedɛ mo,
pa se o ji wo-zɔɔne nɔɔna yiga ne.
Balo déem na nege‑o to laam gwooni‑o mo,
ba na nɛ o kuri to ŋwaane.
Wonto tete de laam yɔɔre o vuvuni mo,
ye o daare o jege o yibia o seiga
chaveera na jege‑o to ŋwaane.
9O chɔge o tete mo de wo-zɔɔna kikia.
O nam wo boŋe se o lɔre ko jwa na wó ke‑o tei to.
O laam na to tei to mo tiini ko jege lɛɛro.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera se kotu zuri o bochare.
O maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ,
nii ko na zoore a yera tei!
A dona bam mo di dam a baŋa ne!”
10O dona bam nɛ chwoŋa se ba zo
ba pɛ o jejegero maama ba ja ba viiri.
O zege o nii mo ye dwi-gɛ tiina zo Wɛ wara-jei sem wone.
Baŋa Wɛ tete nam ya maŋe o ta we,
ko chula se banto zo o diga kam wo.
11Teo kom nɔn-bia bam maama yɔɔre ba vuvuni mo
ye ba beeri wodiu se ba di.
Ba laam ma kwei ba jejegero ba yeigi,
se tento leiri wodiu yuu ne se ba ma wori.
Ba maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ, nii dé seeni,
se ba tiini ba gwooni debam dedɛ.”
12“Abam balo na wo chwoŋa yuu ne á kɛ to,
á yiga tera na?
Nam pipiri-na á nii kolo na yi amo to.
Nɔɔno tera kotu yaara na yi amo nyem dem.
Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo kwei cham dem konto o ke amo yera ne,
maŋa kalo o ban-lom na zaŋe de amo to.
13O pɛ se mini mo nwoŋi wɛyuu ne de ba amo baŋa.
De ma zo a yera ne, ye de zwɛ a kwi sem.
O chege kalanchogo mo se ko ja-ne,
pa se a pipiri a jwoori kwaga.
O yage amo a yerane mo,
pa se a yera chɛ dɛ dem maama wone.
14Ko nye de o kwei a wɛleera yam mo o ke daane,
ne nɔɔno na vɔge ŋone daane tei to.
O ta kwei-ya o lei a ba ne
pa se a dam maama jei mo.
Baŋa Wɛ na kwei-ne o ke a dona jeŋa ne to,
a ware se a zege de-ba.
15Baŋa Wɛ tete mo maŋe o ve
a na teere de babɛ selo to.
O ma bwoŋi nɔn-kɔgɔ se ba ba amo baŋa,
ye ba daare ba meere a nɔn-donno tem.
Wɛ tete mo nɔne Judah dwi tiina bam o le,
ne nɔɔno na nɔne sɛɛro o le swa wone tei to.
16Wonnu tento ŋwaane nam mo pa se a yɔɔre a keera.
A yia yi-na de maa chuuri bare-bare.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera
se kotu zuri a bochare.
Nɔɔno tera se o woli-ne
se a jwoori a tete ne.
Amo bia bam daa ba jege jwa,
kokuri to, dé dona bam wane debam mo.”
17Jerusalem yɔɔre o lwoori wolim mo nɔɔna tei ne.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera se kotu zi o bochare.
Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o ta Jakob dwi tiina yera taane o we,
ba fara wó ji ba dona.
Jerusalem seene o ji wo-zɔɔne mo banto yiga ne,
pa se ba chuli‑o.
18O maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ ye chega Tu mo,
se ko ye amo mo nwoŋi o ni dem kwaga ne.
Cheigi-na, abam dwia yalo na zoore jei selo maama ne to.
Nii-na a na yaare
ye ko zoore a yera tei!
Ba jaane a nɔn-donno tem de a bukwa bam mo
ba kale ba ja vo sa-teo yiga yiga.
19A bwoŋi a bɔɔla mo se ba ba ba woli-ne.
Ba nam koge a kuri mo ba pa a dona.
Kana ma go a kaanem tiina bam, de a nakwa bam,
teo kom wone.
Ba kare jei maama mo ba beeri wodiu
se ba di ba wori ye ba ga.
20 Baŋa Wɛ, nii ko na tiini ko yi-ne tei!
Ko jege-ne mo ko ni.
A wo kom tete de ma di,
a na nwoŋi n ni dem kwaga ne to ŋwaane.
Teo kom chwei sem ne,
nɔɔna toa jara wone mo.
Sɔŋɔ ne de, toone ta maa wora.
21Nɔɔna nigi a na vuvuni tei to,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se kotu zi a bochare.
A dona bam maama na nigi kolo na yi-ne to,
ba yɔɔre ba chake mo de nmo na ke tei a yera ne to.
Ja! Nam pa se banto de dɛ yi,
ne n na gwoni ni se n ke-ba tei to,
se ba de na yaara
ne ko na ye tei amo yera ne to.
22Pa se ba lwarem kikia maama taa tigi n yiga ne,
se n pa ko zo ba de yera,
ne n na pɛ ko zo amo yera tei
a wɛleera yam maama ŋwaane to.
A tiini a vuvuni dedɛ.
A wo de ma jei.”

english_text:
The Lord Was Like an Enemy
The Prophet Speaks:
1The Lord was angry!
So he disgraced Zion
though it was Israel's pride
and his own place of rest.
In his anger he threw Zion down
from heaven to earth.
2The Lord had no mercy!
He destroyed the homes
of Jacob's descendants.
In his anger he tore down
every walled city in Judah;
he toppled the nation
together with its leaders,
leaving them in shame.
3The Lord was so furiously angry
that he wiped out
the whole army of Israel
by not supporting them
when the enemy attacked.
He was like a raging fire
that swallowed up
the descendants of Jacob.
4He attacked like an enemy
with a bow and arrows,
killing our loved ones.
He has burned to the ground
the homes on Mount Zion.
5The Lord was like an enemy!
He left Israel in ruins
with its palaces
and fortresses destroyed,
and with everyone in Judah
moaning and weeping.
6He shattered his temple
like a hut in a garden;
he completely wiped out
his meeting place,
and did away with festivals
and Sabbaths
in the city of Zion.
In his fierce anger he rejected
our king and priests.
7The Lord abandoned his altar
and his temple;
he let Zion's enemies
capture her fortresses.
Noisy shouts were heard
from the temple,
as if it were a time
of celebration.
8The Lord had decided
to tear down the walls of Zion
stone by stone.
So he started destroying
and did not stop
until walls and fortresses
mourned and trembled.
9Zion's gates have fallen
facedown on the ground;
the bars that locked the gates
are smashed to pieces.
Her king and royal family
are prisoners
in foreign lands.
Her priests don't teach,
and her prophets don't have
a message from the Lord.
10Zion's leaders are silent.
They just sit on the ground,
tossing dirt on their heads
and wearing sackcloth.
Her young women can do nothing
but stare at the ground.
11My eyes are red from crying,
my stomach is in knots,
and I feel sick all over.
My people are being wiped out,
and children lie helpless
in the streets of the city.
12A child begs its mother
for food and drink,
then blacks out
like a wounded soldier
lying in the street.
The child slowly dies
in its mother's arms.
13Zion, how can I comfort you?
How great is your pain?
Lovely city of Jerusalem,
how can I heal your wounds,
gaping as wide as the sea?
14Your prophets deceived you
with false visions
and lying messages—
they should have warned you
to leave your sins
and be saved from disaster.
15Those who pass by
shake their heads and sneer
as they make fun and shout,
“What a lovely city you were,
the happiest on earth,
but look at you now!”
16Zion, your enemies curse you
and snarl like wild animals,
while shouting,
“This is the day
we've waited for!
At last, we've got you!”
17The Lord has done everything
that he had planned
and threatened long ago.
He destroyed you without mercy
and let your enemies boast
about their powerful forces.
18Zion, deep in your heart
you cried out to the Lord.
Now let your tears overflow
your walls day and night.
Don't ever lose hope
or let your tears stop.
19Get up and pray for help
all through the night.
Pour out your feelings
to the Lord,
as you would pour water
out of a jug.
Beg him to save your people,
who are starving to death
at every street crossing.
Jerusalem Speaks:
20Think about it, Lord!
Have you ever been this cruel
to anyone before?
Is it right for mothers
to eat their children,
or for priests and prophets
to be killed in your temple?
21My people, both young and old,
lie dead in the streets.
Because you were angry,
my young men and women
were brutally slaughtered.
22When you were angry, Lord,
you invited my enemies
like guests for a party.
No one survived that day;
enemies killed my children,
my own little ones.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na waare Jerusalem tei to
1Nii Baŋa Wɛ bane na zaŋe Zion teo kom baŋa ne tei!
O ban-lom li-ba mo
ne kunkwon-liliru tei.
Wɛ ma pa se Isarele tiina bam lonne jejegero ji kafɛ.
O ma zege wɛyuu ne o de-te tega ne.
Maŋa kalo o bane na zaŋe de Jerusalem to,
o daa maŋe o wo sɛ se o wara-jei sem taa wora.
2Baŋa Wɛ chɔge teene delo maama
Jakob dwi tiina na zoore de wone to mo.
O wo kom na fuli to ŋwaane,
o vaŋe Judah tiina dam jei sem maama o de tega ne mo.
O ma chɔge ba teene dem de ba pwa bam de,
pa se ba zula maama ti.
3O ma pa se Isarele jar-keira bam maama dam ti
o ban-lom dem ŋwaane.
Ba dona na beene ba baŋa ne to,
o ma dɔne o jeŋa o daare-ba.
Wonto tete jigi ne min-vogo na ye tei to mo,
ye o yɔɔre o zwɛ Jakob dwi tiina bam kula!
4Wɛ mo saŋe o taŋa,
ne o ye ba dono mo tei.
O laam ma yɔɔre ba baŋa se o ta.
O ma go ba nɔn-donno telo maama
kikia ya na su o yi to.
O pɛ se o bane dem to Jerusalem tiina baŋa ne mo,
ne mini na di bileim-bileim tei to.
5Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ jigi Isarele tiina bam dono mo.
O ma yɔɔre o chɔge-ba.
O mage ba sɔ-fwaaro tem pa te ji di-dwonnu mo.
O nam ta chɔge ba dam jei sem de.
O ma pa se Judah tiina keira kam puli dedɛ,
ye ka ba tia.
6Wɛ ta yigi o diga kam o de tega ne,
ne ka ga ye kara wo vwei mo.
O ma pa se o nɔɔna bam de swei
se ba yeini ba di kura yam,
ye ba ta swei o siu dɛ dem swia.
Ko ná ye pɛ wom de kaanem tiina bam maama,
Wɛ nwoŋi ba kwaga ne o ban-lom dem ŋwaane.
7Baŋa Wɛ tage o kaanem bimbini dem mo o yage.
O ma viiri o daare o tete diga kam.
O ma kwei Jerusalem sɔ-fwaaro tem o ke ko dona bam jeŋa ne
pa ba yigi te kabiri sem ba de tega ne.
Banto laam ma zege Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ne ba bage tiguri-kaasa,
ne ba di kuri Wɛ ŋwaane mo tei.
8 Baŋa Wɛ jaane o boboŋa mo
se o yigi Zion kabiri sem o de tega ne.
O ma maŋe se dedɔrem baŋa chekke,
ye o daare o chɔge se maama fase.
Kabiri selo ya na kaare teo kom se che to maama
laam maa tigi tega ne buri-buri.
9Jerusalem teo ni-bworru tem moore tega ne mo.
Wɛ ma yɔɔre o bwori te luuru tem.
Ko ná ye teo kom pɛ de pa-bia bam,
o kale-ba o ja o vo o de teene dedwonna wone mo.
Nɔɔna daa ba mae Wɛ bera yam ba toŋa.
Wɛ sampwori sem daa ware
se ba lɔre Baŋa Wɛ kwora na ye tei to.
10Zion nakwa bam laam jei tega ne mo chemm.
Ba wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane mo ba taare ba yuni de kasolo,
ye ba ta yɔɔre ba zo gare-nyenyaaro ba jei.
Jerusalem teo bukwa bam de gwoori ba tira tega ne mo de chaveera.
11A keeri a yia yi-na maama a ti.
A wo kom de ma yɔɔre ko pɛ.
Amo jworo nye de ko lwogi mo ko tigi tega ne,
kokuri to, ba jege a nɔɔna bam ba chɔge mo.
Bia de bu-sese yɔɔre ba tigi teo kom chwei sem ne mo.
12Bia bam maa tɛ de ba niina ba we
“Dé lage wodiu mo se dé di.”
Ba ma to teo kom chwei sem ne,
ne ko na tiini ko zo babɛ tei jara-keim ne to.
Ba ŋwea ma ti
ba niina bam ja-kukworru wone.
13Jerusalem tiina bam, amo wó ta abam yera taane we bɛ mo?
Amo lage a kwei bɛ mo se a maŋe de abam?
Zion tiina bam, amo wó ke tɛ mo
se a wane a pa se á bochare zuri?
Á yaara yam daga mo ne naneo na yala tei to.
Wɔ mo wó wane o woli abam se á na yazura?
14Abam sampwori sem na nɛ kolo ye ba bere abam to
ya ye vwa mo.
Ba ma gane abam.
Ba wo pɛ se á lɔre á na tiini á tusi tei to,
se á wane á jwoori á ta‑á tɔge chwoŋa.
Ba nam tage vwa taana mo ba bere abam,
pa se á ywori chega chwoŋa kam wone.
15Balo maama na tɔge abam seeni ba kɛ to
laam jege abam mo ba yeera.
Ba ta chweese mo, ye ba daare ba dole ba yuni,
Jerusalem teo kom na nɛ chɔgem to ŋwaane.
Ba maa mɔna ye ba tɛ ba we,
“Teo kolo na lana ko gaale to mo tento na?
Nabiina maama daa jege wopwolo de-ko na?”
16Abam dona maama jege abam mo ba twea.
Ba maa chweese abam.
Ba maa nyɔne ba yibia de abam ye ba we,
“Dé laam wane-ba dé chɔge dé yage.
Dé ya jei dé cheigi dɛ dento mo,
dé yi nam nɛ-de!”
17Ko nam ye Baŋa Wɛ mo laam ke
o na ke o boboŋa ne se o ke tei to.
O yɔɔre o ke o su ni delo o na tiŋi faŋa faŋa to mo.
O dole teo kom o de ye o wo jaane á ŋwaŋa.
O ta pɛ se á dona jege wopwolo á chɔgem ŋwaane.
O ma pa ba tiini ba dana ba dwoi abam.
18Zion teo kom, keeri-na de kwor-dɛa
á lwoori Baŋa Wɛ.
Pa-na á yi-na taa chuuri bare-bare
wea de tete maama ne.
Yé sɛ-na se á sii.
Á yia de nam yé kɔ keira.
19Zaŋe-na dɔɔm ne se á keeri á jare Baŋa Wɛ.
Lwoori-o-na titwon-twono tete dem maama wone.
Lwo-na á wo-chechɔgɔ kom maama á tiŋi Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne,
ne nɔɔna na lwogi na ba tiŋi tega ne tei to.
Zeiŋi-na á je Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se á lwoori‑o,
se o duri á bia bam ŋwaŋa se ba yé te.
Kokuri to, kana wora ka go-ba
teo kom chwei sem maama ne.
20“Baŋa Wɛ, nii debam seeni,
se n duri dé ŋwaŋa.
Ko ye n tete nɔɔna mo n jege n yaara!
N lage se kaana kwei ba tete bia
balo ba na jege ba kɔne to mo
ba di na?
N ta lage se ba go n kaanem tiina bam de n sampwori sem
n tete diga kam ne mo na?
21Nɔn-donno de nɔn-kwe maama mo tega
ba tigi teo kom chwei sem ne.
Nɔn-donno de bukɔ-pwoli de ma yɔɔre ba te jara wone.
Nmo bane na zaŋe de-ba to pɛ se n go-ba.
N yɔɔre n gwoni-ba n tiŋi mo
ye n wo jaane ba ŋwaŋa.
22Nmo bwoŋi a dona mo se ba ba ba di kuri,
ye ba fugi-ne jei maama ne.
Nmo Baŋa Wɛ bane na zaŋe maŋa kalo ne to,
nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo wane se o lu.
Bia balo amo ya na jege a kɔna, ye a nii ba baŋa ne to
mo a dono wom yɔɔre o go nyɔ!”

english_text:
There Is Still Hope
The Prophet Speaks:
1I have suffered much
because God was angry.
2He chased me into a dark place,
where no light could enter.
3I am the only one he punishes
over and over again,
without ever stopping.
4God caused my skin and flesh
to waste away,
and he crushed my bones.
5He attacked and surrounded me
with hardships and trouble;
6he forced me to sit in the dark
like someone long dead.
7God built a fence around me
that I cannot climb over,
and he chained me down.
8Even when I shouted
and prayed for help,
he refused to listen.
9God put big rocks in my way
and made me follow
a crooked path.
10God was like a bear or a lion
waiting in ambush for me;
11he dragged me from the road,
then tore me to shreds.
12God took careful aim
and shot his arrows
13straight through my heart.
14I am a joke to everyone—
no one ever stops
making fun of me.
15God has turned my life sour.
16He made me eat gravel
and rubbed me in the dirt.
17I cannot find peace
or remember happiness.
18I tell myself, “I am finished!
I can't count on the Lord
to do anything for me.”
19Just thinking of my troubles
and my lonely wandering
makes me miserable.
20That's all I ever think about,
and I am depressed.
21Then I remember something
that fills me with hope.
22The Lord's kindness never fails!
If he had not been merciful,
we would have been destroyed.
23The Lord can always be trusted
to show mercy each morning.
24Deep in my heart I say,
“The Lord is all I need;
I can depend on him!”
25The Lord is kind to everyone
who trusts and obeys him.
26It is good to wait patiently
for the Lord to save us.
27When we are young,
it is good to struggle hard
28and to sit silently alone,
if this is what
the Lord intends.
29Being rubbed in the dirt
can teach us a lesson;
30we can also learn from insults
and hard knocks.
31The Lord won't always reject us!
32He causes a lot of suffering,
but he also has pity
because of his great love.
33The Lord doesn't enjoy
sending grief or pain.
34Don't trample prisoners
under your feet
35or cheat anyone out of
what is rightfully theirs.
God Most High sees everything,
36and he knows when you refuse
to give someone a fair trial.
37No one can do anything
without the Lord's approval.
38Good and bad each happen
at the command
of God Most High.
39We're still alive!
We shouldn't complain
when we are being punished
for our sins.
40Instead, we should think
about the way we are living,
and turn back to the Lord.
41When we lift our hands
in prayer to God in heaven,
we should offer him our hearts
and say, 42“We've sinned!
We've rebelled against you,
and you haven't forgiven us!
43Anger is written all over you,
as you pursue and slaughter us
without showing pity.
44You are behind a wall of clouds
that blocks out our prayers.
45You allowed nations
to treat us like garbage;
46our enemies curse us.
47We are terrified and trapped,
caught and crushed.”
48My people are destroyed!
Tears flood my eyes,
49and they won't stop
50until the Lord looks down
from heaven and helps.
51I am horrified when I see
what enemies have done
to the young women of our city.
52No one had reason to hate me,
but I was hunted down
like a bird.
53Then they tried to kill me
by tossing me into a pit
and throwing stones at me.
54Water covered my head—
I thought I was gone.
55From the bottom of the pit,
I prayed to you, Lord.
56I begged you to listen.
“Help!” I shouted. “Save me!”
You answered my prayer
57and came when I was in need.
You told me, “Don't worry!”
58You rescued me
and saved my life.
59You saw them abuse me, Lord,
so make things right.
60You know every plot
they have made against me.
61Yes, you know their insults
and their evil plans.
62All day long they attack
with words and whispers.
63No matter what they are doing,
they keep on mocking me.
64Pay them back for everything
they have done, Lord!
65Put your curse on them
and make them suffer.
66Get angry and go after them
until not a trace is left
under the heavens.
translation_text:
Teena wora Baŋa Wɛ swono kom ŋwaane
1Amo ye wolo na nɛ cham,
ne Baŋa Wɛ na waare-ne o ban-lom dem ŋwaane tei to mo.
2O yɔɔre o kale-ne mo se a taa vei lim wone,
ye pwooni daa tera kɔtaa!
3O nam yɔɔre o jege-ne o maga mo taa.
O ma dole o jaguli-zane a yera ne dɛ maama wone.
4O ma pa a ya-nɔna yam kwe lela,
ye o daare o ja a kwi sem o bwori.
5O yɔɔre o zaŋe a baŋa ne mo o peene-ne,
pa se a maama ye cham de wo-chechɔgɔ yerane.
6O ma zeili-ne pa se a jei yibiri wone,
ne balo na tege ba dáane to.
7Ko nye de o pe-ne mo o yage diga ne,
ye o ta vɔ-ne de chegero se a yé lu.
8Amo ná maŋe a keeri a jare‑o tei maama de,
o yeini o ve se o cheigi-ne mo.
9O mɛ kandwa mo o lɔ kabiri o che a chwoŋa.
Chwoŋa daa tera se a wane a tɔge da a kɛ.
10O seigi jei ne mo o tiga, ne kago-varem tei.
O maa lage se o zi-ne, ne nywoŋo na ke tei to.
11O ma tuuri-ne o le chwoŋa yuu ne ye o tore-ne.
O laam ma yage-ne pa a wo a yerane ye wolim tera.
12O yɔɔre o saŋe o taŋa mo,
ye o laam jege-ne o tae de chena.
13O jeeri amo mo o ta o chena yam.
Ya ma yɔɔre ya moore ya yi a bochare-yi.
14Amo nɔɔna bam laam jege-ne mo ba mɔna.
Dɛ maama ba leeni lei mo ba ma twe-ne.
15O pɛ se a ŋwea maama su de wo-chɛɛro mo.
Ko ta nye nenɛɛne o kwei wo-chechɔgɔ mo
o ke na-zoŋa ne o pa-ne se a nyɔ.
16O pɛ se a done kandwa mo ye ya guri a yeila.
O ta ma nɔne amo o se tega ne
pa se a yera taare de kasolo.
17Yazura daa tera amo tei ne.
Amo swei wopwolo na ye tei to.
18Amo laam ma ta a we,
“A dam dem jei.
Teena yalo amo ya na jege Baŋa Wɛ tei ne to de ti.”
19A guli a chanɛɛre dem,
de a na kare a beeri yɔɔ yerane tei to gula.
A ŋwea yɔɔre ka su de wo-chɛɛro mo.
20A maa ná yeini a guli konto maama,
a wo wó chɔge mo.
21De ko de, a daa ná yeini a guli tento,
a teena daa ta wó jwoori a tei ne mo.
22 Baŋa Wɛ na yɔɔre o jege o swono tei to bá fɔge ko ti.
O na yeini o duri debam yibwona tei to de nam ba tia.
23Tega ná poore dɛ maama,
tento yeini te jwoori te wora mo.
Chega to, nmo zaane dem tiini de daga.
24Amo wó ta a tete ne mo we,
“Baŋa Wɛ wo amo tei ne.
O nam maŋe amo.
Wonto yera ne mo a teena maama tiga.”
25 Baŋa Wɛ lana mo o pa balo na sale‑o to.
O maa zeini balo na tui o tei to.
26Ko lana mo se nɔɔna taa cheigi chemm
ba nii se Baŋa Wɛ jwoŋi-ba o yage.
27Nɔn-donno ná lɔre se ba peene ba tete,
ko wó taa lana ko pa-ba.
28 Baŋa Wɛ ná korese nɔɔno wolo,
ko maŋe se kotu zuri o yera mo o pa‑o.
29O nam ná tu o tete konto dwoŋi
teena daa wó jwoori ya ba o tei ne.
30Nɔɔna ná lage ba mage‑o, se o yage se ba lɔ o popɔŋɔ.
Ba ná jege‑o ba twea, ko maŋe se o sɛ ba toro tem mo.
31Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ ba yɔɔre o ve nɔɔna
o yage-ba taa wuu.
32O ná maŋe o chɔge ba wo tei de,
o ta wó duri ba ŋwaŋa,
o swono kom na tiini ko daga to ŋwaane.
33Wonto ba swoi se o ja yaara naa cham
o ba o de nabiina baŋa ne.
34Nɔɔno ná nɔne peena balo maama na wo tega kam baŋa ne to
o se o nɛ kuri ne, ko lana na?
35Kotu ná ve Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ni,
ye o che nɔɔna de ba chega,
ko lana na?
36Kotu ná ve nɔɔno bora taane dim baŋa ne,
Baŋa Wɛ ba nae ko maama na?
37Wɔ mo wó wane o ŋɔɔne se wonnu toŋe,
ye ko dae Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ chwoŋa se te ke?
38Ko ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora mo pae
se cham de ywoni tui nabiina baŋa.
39Wɛ nam ná waare nabiina ba wɛleera ŋwaane,
ba wolo ná poone ko baŋa ne, ko jege kuri na?
40Nam pa-na se dé fɔge dé maane dé ŋwea na ye tei to,
se dé laam daare dé jwoori Baŋa Wɛ tei.
41Pa-na se dé pore dé bochara,
ye dé zeiŋi dé je wɛɛne
dé jeeri Baŋa Wɛ se dé ta we:
42“Baŋa Wɛ, debam tusi ye dé ta nwoŋi n kwaga ne.
Nmo wo yage dé wɛleera n chɛ debam.
43Nmo mɛ n bane dem mo n pɛ debam kwaga n pu.
N ma‑n daare n go debam,
ye n wo duri dé ŋwaŋa.
44Nmo yɔɔre n kwei kunkwoŋo mo n che n tete,
pa wɛ-lworo tera dé na wó ke se ko yi‑m.
45Nmo dole debam n yage
ne dé ye weero mo to.
Dé ma ji wo-yɔɔro dwi-gɛ tiina bam tetare ne.
46Debam dona bam maama maa jege debam ba twea.
47Cham de chɔgem dedɛ mo tu debam baŋa.
Foone maa jege debam.”
48A yi-na mo yɔɔre ba chuuri bare-bare,
kokuri to, ba jege a nɔɔna bam ba chɔge mo.
49A yia yi-na wó yɔɔre ba ta nwoŋi mo taa,
ye ba ba kwora,
50se ko yi Baŋa Wɛ ná zege wɛyuu ne,
ye o tiiri o nii o na-ne.
51A wo tiini ko chɔge, a yia na nae wonnu telo to ŋwaane,
de a na nɛ a teo kom bukwa bam na yaare tei to.
52Ko ná ye balo na chuli-ne ba tete boboŋa ŋwaane to,
ba jege-ne ba para ne nɔɔno na zeili zuŋa se o ja tei to mo.
53Ba ma ja-ne ba vo ba dole ba yage gwoŋ-chanluŋu wone,
ye ba daare ba dole-ne de kandwa se ba go.
54Na ma bibili a baŋa ne ba kɛa.
A ma boŋe we a ŋwea ti mo.
55 Baŋa Wɛ, amo de ma zege gwoŋo kom wone
a bwoŋi n yere se n ba n zeini-ne.
56Nmo ma‑n cheigi a na lwoori‑m tei a we,
“Yé se n zwa. Nam cheigi a wɛ-lworo kom.”
57Amo na bwoŋi‑m konto to mo n fɔɔre n yi a tei.
N ma‑n ta de amo n we,
“Yé ta‑n fona.”
58Amo Teiru Wɛ, nmo mo jwoŋi a taane dem n ŋɔɔne n pa-ne.
Nmo ta mo jwoŋi a ŋwea n yage.
59 Baŋa Wɛ, n yei ba na ke ba chɔge a yiga tei to.
Nam di a taane se a na bora.
60Nmo nɛ a dona na tiini ba chuli-ne tei to.
Ba jeini ba ke ni daane mo se ba chɔge-ne.
61 Baŋa Wɛ, nmo ta nigi ba na jege-ne ba twe tei to.
Ba jeini ba ke ni daane mo se ba chɔge-ne.
62Nmo ta nigi ba na waase tei,
de ba na yɔɔre ba bane daane
se ba chɔge-ne tei to.
63Nii-ba mo! Ba kikia maama wone,
ba jege-ne mo ba mɔne de ba lei sem.
64 Baŋa Wɛ, yiri jene ba baŋa ne,
se ko maŋe de kolo maama ba na ke to.
65Pa se ba bochara taa tiini ya dana,
se n daare n sɔɔle lwarem
n yage ba yuu ne.
66Tɔge n ban-lom dem baŋa
n zeili-ba n ja,
se n daare n ti-ba
se ba yere saare tega baŋa ne.

english_text:
The Punishment of Jerusalem
The Prophet Speaks:
1The purest gold is ruined
and has lost its shine;
jewels from the temple
lie scattered in the streets.
2These are Zion's people,
worth more than purest gold;
yet they are counted worthless
like dishes of clay.
3Even jackals nurse their young,
but my people are like ostriches
that abandon their own.
4Babies are so thirsty
that their tongues are stuck
to the roof of the mouth.
Children go begging for food,
but no one gives them any.
5All who ate expensive foods
lie starving in the streets;
those who grew up in luxury
now sit on trash heaps.
6 My nation was punished worse
than the people of Sodom,
whose city was destroyed
in a flash without the help
of human hands.
7The leaders of Jerusalem
were purer than snow
and whiter than milk;
their bodies were healthy
and glowed like jewels.
8Now they are blacker than tar,
and no one recognizes them;
their skin clings to their bones
and is drier than firewood.
9Being killed with a sword
is better than slowly
starving to death.
10 Life in the city is so bad
that loving mothers have boiled
and eaten their own children.
11The Lord was so fiercely angry
that he burned the city of Zion
to the ground.
12Not a king on this earth
or the people of any nation
believed enemies could break
through her gates.
13Jerusalem was punished because
her prophets and her priests
had sinned and caused the death
of innocent victims.
14Yes, her prophets and priests
were covered with blood;
no one would come near them,
as they wandered
from street to street.
15Instead, everyone shouted,
“Go away! Don't touch us!
You're filthy and unfit
to belong to God's people!”
So they had to leave
and become refugees.
But foreign nations told them,
“You can't stay here!”
16The Lord is the one
who sent them scattering,
and he has forgotten them.
No respect or kindness
will be shown
to the priests or leaders.
17Our eyes became weary,
hopelessly looking
for help from a nation
that could not save us.
18Enemies hunted us down
on every public street.
Our time was up;
our doom was near.
19They swooped down faster
than eagles from the sky.
They hunted for us in the hills
and set traps to catch us
out in the desert.
20The Lord's chosen leader
was our hope for survival!
We thought he would keep us safe
somewhere among the nations,
but even he was caught
in one of their traps.
21You people of Edom
can celebrate now!
But your time will come
to suffer and stagger
around naked.
22The people of Zion
have paid for their sins,
and the Lord will soon
let them return home.
But, people of Edom,
you will be punished,
and your sins exposed.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na waare Jerusalem o ti tei to
1Nii sabu-seŋa kam na gɛ ka lam dem tei!
Sabu-seŋ-laao kom daa ba jege yuu.
Kandwa-nyenno tem laam jage,
pa te tigi teo kom chwei sem maama ne.
2Zion teo nɔɔna bam déem tiini ba jege dunni,
ne sabu-seŋa na ye tei to mo.
Leile konto ba laam nam nye de kambi selo
kamɔ-mɔro na mɔɔne to mo.
3Ko ná ye ga-kukuri, se yeini se kwei yele
se ma kɔne se bia.
Amo nɔɔna bam nam ve ba bia mo,
ne nakelakɔro na ke te bia tei kagoa yuu ne to.
4Na-nyɔm mo lage de go bia bam.
Ba nia de ma ko ya peere.
Ba yɔɔre ba lwoori wodiu mo,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba sɛ o ke o pa-ba.
5Balo déem na jege wodi-laaro ba di ne pwa tei to,
kana laam wora ka go-ba teo kom chwei sem ne mo.
Balo nam ya na jege ywoni ba di to,
laam mo tigi tampuura baŋa ne.
6A nɔɔna bam na nɛ waarem delo to daga
de dwoi delo Sodom tiina na nɛ to.
Banto déem nɛ chɔgem bedwe baŋa ne mo,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se o woli-ba.
7Jerusalem dedɛɛra bam déem tiini ba lana dedɛ.
Ba maa ye nɔn-pwonnu.
Ba ta ma kwɛ ba yera pa se ya nyeena ne kandwa-nyenno tei.
Ba maa jege dam de yazura lanyerane.
8Ba yibia laam ye ligi-ligi ka dwoi sambinnu mo.
Ba ná nwoŋi pwooni, nɔɔna ware se ba lɔre-ba.
Ba yera yam ma kwaare ya tane ba kwi ne.
Ba ya-nɔna yam ma ko, ne dɛ na koge tei to.
9Balo na tege jara wone to toone dem
maŋe de gare kana na go balo to.
Kokuri to, kana kam jege-ba ka goe fee fee mo se ba ba ti,
kare sem na wo ke wodiiru to ŋwaane.
10Kaana balo na ye pu-bwon-nyena to
mo mɛ ba tete je ba go ba bia ba di.
Ba saŋe ba bia mo ba di,
se ba wori teo kom chɔgem baŋa ne.
11 Baŋa Wɛ nam yɔɔre o pa se o bane tiini de zaŋe mo.
O ma pa se o ban-lom dem to debam baŋa ne.
Wonto mo dwei mini se de di Zion wone.
De ma zwɛ teo kom kabiri-beira kam tete kula.
12Logo baŋa pwa bam de nabiina jei maama ne
ya ba boŋe we,
debam dona wó na chwoŋa
se ba zo Jerusalem wone ba chɔge teo kom.
13Konto nam seene ko ke.
Ko maa ye teo kom sampwori
de ba kaanem tiina wɛleera yam ŋwaane mo.
Kokuri to, banto jege nɔn-ŋona mo teo kom wone
ba goe kafɛ ŋwaane.
14Ba laam nam kare teo kom chwei sem yuu ne mo
ba taana ba beeri chwoŋa, ne lilwoa na ke tei to.
Ba na tiini ba biini ba tete de nɔɔna jana tei to,
pɛ se nɔɔna kɔre se ba dwei ba yera,
ba na wo maŋe de chullu tem to ŋwaane.
15Nɔɔna tɔɔle ba de ba zwa ne mo ba we,
“Lage-na jei dé tei ne,
se á biini á tete dedɛ!
Yé dwei-na debam!”
Ba nam na kare teene dedwonna ne ba beeri jeiŋa jei to,
dwi-gɛ tiina tɛ ba taane ba we,
“Dé bá sɛ se ba taa zoore debam tetare ne.”
16Ko nam ye Baŋa Wɛ tete mo jage-ba o yage.
O yiga daa tera de-ba.
Nɔɔna daa ba nege kaanem tiina bam.
Nakwa bam de maa ba nae zula nɔɔna tei ne.
17Debam nam ya nii chwoŋa ne mo,
se dé fara ná wó ba ba woli debam, ye dé ga.
Dé maa zege dé teo kom nayuni ne dé yɔɔre dé nia,
ye teo kolo dé na beeri ko wolim to wo tu.
18Dé dona bam yɔɔre ba yere dé na-veili maama mo.
Dé daa ware dé teo kom chwei sem yuu ne se dé taa via.
Maŋa kam yia se dé teo kom chɔge.
Dé na wó na dé lɛɛro maŋa kalo to yia!
19Balo na zeili debam se ba ja to
nye de maaro na nwoŋi wɛyuu ne te tu te zi wonnu tei to mo.
Dé na duri dé di peero yuu to,
mo ba pɛ debam kwaga ba pu.
Dé na yɔɔre dé zo kagoa kam wone to,
ba ta li debam da.
20Ba ma che kalanchorro ba ja Baŋa Wɛ na tiŋi pɛ wolo o pa debam to,
ye wonto ya mo pɛ debam pempanno.
Dé nam ya teene we, dé na zoore o woro kom wone to,
teene delo na gilimi debam to bá wane debam de di.
21Abam Edom dwi tiina bam,
á wó ta‑á jege wopwolo na?
Abam balo na zoore Yuzi tega kam ne to wó ta‑á chaka na?
Nam lɔre-na we Wɛ bane wó zaŋe abam de baŋa ne.
Á wó nyɔ o ban-lom dem á su
ye á daare á na á chaveera,
ne debam na nɛ tei tento to.
22Abam Zion tiina bam,
waarem delo á na nɛ á tusim ŋwaane to wó kɛ.
Wɛ bá yage abam sa-teo ne yiga yiga se ko dáane.
Ko daare, ko ná ye abam Edom tiina bam,
o lage o waare abam mo á wɛleera ŋwaane,
se nɔɔna lɔre we á puseŋa kikia gaale.

english_text:
A Prayer for Mercy
The People of Jerusalem Pray:
1Our Lord, don't forget
how we have suffered
and been disgraced.
2Foreigners and strangers
have taken our land
and our homes.
3We are like children
whose mothers are widows.
4The water we drink
and the wood we burn
cost far too much.
5We are terribly mistreated;
we are worn out
and can find no rest.
6We had to surrender
to Egypt and Assyria
because we were hungry.
7Our ancestors sinned,
but they are dead,
and we are left to pay
for their sins.
8Slaves are now our rulers,
and there is no one
to set us free.
9We are in danger
from brutal desert tribes;
we must risk our lives
just to bring in our crops.
10Our skin is scorched
from fever and hunger.
11On Zion and everywhere in Judah
our wives and daughters
are being raped.
12Our rulers are strung up
by their arms,
and our nation's advisors
are treated shamefully.
13Young men are forced
to do the work of slaves;
boys must carry
heavy loads of wood.
14Our leaders are not allowed
to decide cases in court,
and young people
no longer play music.
15Our hearts are sad;
instead of dancing,
we mourn.
16Zion's glory has disappeared!
And we are doomed
because of our sins.
17We feel sick all over
and can't even see straight;
18our city is in ruins,
overrun by wild dogs.
19You will rule forever, Lord!
You are King for all time.
20Why have you forgotten us
for so long?
21Bring us back to you!
Give us a fresh start.
22Or do you despise us so much
that you don't want us?
translation_text:
Jerusalem tiina wɛ-lworo kom
1Dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ,
guli kolo na yi debam to.
Nii n na dé yuu na tiini ko yaale tei to!
2Veira laam mo jwoŋi debam tega kam ba tei.
Dé sam dem laam ma ji sa-teena nyem.
3Dé kwoa daa tera ye ba daare debam botara.
Dé niina de laam ma ji kadeina.
4Dé jege se dé yeigi na balo dé na nyɔ to de sabu mo.
Ko maa ná ye dé dɛ sem de,
dé wó le sabu dedɛ mo se dé ma na-se.
5Dé dona mo pɛ dé kwaga ba pu.
Dé yɔɔre dé bugi mo,
ye siu tera ko pae debam.
6Dé laam to dé pa Ejipti de Asiria tiina mo,
se ba pa debam wodiu se dé ma dé wori.
7Dé kwoa mo tusi, ba nam daa tera.
Wɛ ma waare debam banto wɛleera ŋwaane.
8Dé dona bam kabɛ laam mo tei debam.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera se o jwoŋi debam ba jeŋa ne o yage.
9Dé yeini dé dole dé ŋwea mo
dé yage se dé na wodiu.
Kokuri to, nɔn-gora mo kare ba zi nɔɔna kagoa kam ne.
10Dé yera yam maama maa lone bakke.
Dé kana kam laam jigi paa ka daane debam.
11Baara yeini ba zi dé kaana bam Zion teo kom ne.
Ba maa fe dé busankan-pwoli sem Judah teene dem maama ne ba laga.
12Ba jaane dé teo kom dedɛɛra mo
ba kuuni de ŋone ba go.
Ba maa wo nege dé nakwa bam kɔtaa!
13Ba jege dé nɔn-donno tem mo
ba cho muni.
Bakeiri bia de jege se ba zeŋe dɛ
selo na duna se dwoi-ba to mo.
14Dé teo kom nakwa daa ware
teo kom manchwoŋo ni ne se ba jeini.
Nɔn-donno tem maa ba mage gungwei.
15Wopwolo kikia maama jei debam tei ne.
Dé jɔŋɔ magem maama laam leiri
ko ji keira mo.
16Dé nenɔŋa kam maama jei.
Lɛɛro ma yi debam,
dé wɛleera yam ŋwaane.
17Mo kokuri dé wo maama jei.
Dé daa ba nae chekke,
dé yia na suli de yi-na to ŋwaane.
18Kokuri to, Zion peo kom laam tigi
de di-dwonnu yerane mo.
Ga-kukuri de laam maa kare te wone se beera.
19Dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ,
nmo ye pɛ mo taa wuu.
N paare dem bá taa jege kweelim
se ko taa vei wuu.
20Bɛŋwaane mo nmo yɔɔre n swei dé swia?
Bɛ mo ye n yage debam dé yerane
bena dedɛ wone konto?
21Dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nam pa dé pipiri
dé jwoori nmo tei.
Pa se dé jwoori dé na dé faŋa kam.
22Ko ná dae konto, ko bere we
n yɔɔre n ve debam mo,
ye n ban-lom dem wo dé baŋa ne
se ko kɛ jeŋa.

english_text:
Ezekiel Sees the Lord's Glory
1-3 I am Ezekiel—a priest and the son of Buzi.
Five years after King Jehoiachin of Judah had been led away as a prisoner to Babylonia, I was living near the Chebar River among those who had been taken there with him. Then on the fifth day of the fourth month of the thirtieth year, the heavens suddenly opened. The Lord placed his hand upon me and showed me some visions.
4I saw a windstorm blowing in from the north. Lightning flashed from a huge cloud and lit up the whole sky with a dazzling brightness. The fiery center of the cloud was as shiny as polished metal, 5 and in that center I saw what looked like four living creatures. They were somewhat like humans, 6except that each one had four faces and four wings. 7Their legs were straight, but their feet looked like the hoofs of calves and sparkled like bronze. 8Under each of their wings, these creatures had a human hand. 9The four creatures were standing back to back with the tips of their wings touching. They moved together in every direction, without turning their bodies.
10 Each creature had the face of a human in front, the face of a lion on the right side, the face of a bull on the left, and the face of an eagle in back. 11Two wings of each creature were spread out and touched the wings of the creatures on either side. The other two wings of each creature were folded against its body.
12The four living creatures went wherever the Spirit led them, and they moved together without turning their bodies, because each creature faced straight ahead. 13 The creatures were glowing like hot coals, and I saw something like a flaming torch moving back and forth among them. Lightning flashed from the torch every time its flame blazed up. 14The creatures themselves moved as quickly as sparks jumping from a fire.
15 I then noticed that on the ground beside each of the four living creatures was a wheel, 16shining like chrysolite. Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it, 17so that they could move in any direction without turning. 18 The rims of the wheels were large and frightening, and they had eyes all the way around them. 19-21The creatures controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the four creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels were beside them.
22-23 Above the living creatures, I saw something that was sparkling like ice, and it reminded me of a dome. Each creature had two of its wings stretched out toward the creatures on either side, with the other two wings folded against its body. 24 Whenever the creatures flew, their wings roared like an ocean or a large army or even the voice of God All-Powerful. And whenever the creatures stopped, they folded their wings against their bodies.
25When the creatures stopped flapping their wings, I heard a sound coming from above the dome. 26 I then saw what looked like a throne made of sapphire, and sitting on the throne was a figure in the shape of a human. 27 From the waist up, it was glowing like metal in a hot furnace, and from the waist down it looked like the flames of a fire. The figure was surrounded by a bright light, 28as colorful as a rainbow that appears after a storm.
I realized I was seeing the brightness of the Lord's glory! So I bowed with my face to the ground, and just then I heard a voice speaking to me.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na le kolo o bere Ezekeli to
1Ko déem na yi bena fintɔ bene dem chane sena chana kam da yanu dɛ dem ne to mo amo Ezekeli zege Chebara buga kam ni ne. A maa wora de Judah tiina balo ba na kale jara-keim baŋa ne ba ja vo Babilon to. Amo déem na wora konto to, mo a nɛ wɛyuu kom na pore pa se Wɛ veere o tete o bere-ne. 2Bene dem konto ye ba déem na jaane Judah pɛ Jehoyachin ba kale ba vo jei sem konto ye bena yanu kɛ to mo. Chana kam da yanu dɛ dem ne 3Baŋa Wɛ kwora déem yi amo ye a zege Chebara buga kam ni ne mo Babilon teo wone. A ma maane we Baŋa Wɛ dam dem tu amo wolo na ye Buzi bu Ezekeli ye a ye Wɛ kaanem tu to baŋa.
4Amo déem kwoni a yuu a nii a na vo-dɛɔ na nwoŋi baŋa seeni ko foore ko beena. Kunkwoŋ-zɔŋɔ ma da ko baŋa ko ba ye ko pepele jei maama de dam. Pwooni delo na tiini de pera to maa gilimi ko maama. Kunkwoŋo kom tetare mini dem yɔɔre de seene mo ne channa na tiini ka nyeene tei to. 5A ma nii a na wo-kenkagela yana na ŋwe to mini dem tetare ne. Ya déem nye de nabiina mo, 6ye wo-kenkagele maama laam jege yibi sena, de vɔna yana se de taa maa jaana. 7Ya nɛ sem nam yɔɔre se twe mo, ye ya napera seeni maa nye de na-mɔra napɔɔna yalo na nyeene ne channa na nyeene tei to. 8Wo-kenkagela sɛ sena sem maama maa jege nabiina jea ya vɔna yam kuri ne mo. Ya yana yam maama maa jege yibia de vɔna tento dwoŋi: 9Ya ma kwei ya vɔna ya dwei daane. Wo-kenkagele maama yɔɔre de vei de yiga na jeeri mɛ to mo, pa se de vei ye de ba pipira.
10Ya maama jege yibi sena sena mo na ye se yera: Dedoa maama jege nabiinu yibia de yiga seeni. Nywoŋo yibia maa wo de jazem seeni. Nabea yibia maa wo de jagwia seeni. Maao yibia de maa wo de kwaga kam seeni. 11Wo-kenkagele maama vɔna zeiŋi wɛɛne mo, ye ya yalei yarege ya dwei wo-kenkagela yalo na zege ya yeiri de yera ne to vɔna yam jazem de jagwia seeni. Ko na daare vɔna yalei yadwonna yam to, de laam ma kwei yanto de kwoli de yera yam. 12Wo-kenkagele maama mo yɔɔre de vei yiga ye de ba pipira. Ya maa vei ya jworo kom na bere se ya vo mɛ to. 13Wo-kenkagela yam nye de min-mɔɔla naa min-zwonnu mo wo ya tetare ne. Mini dem maa zaŋa ya tetare ne ye de vei yiga de kwaga. De tiini de nyeene dedɛ mo ye de pepela. 14Wo-kenkagela yam tete maa yɔɔre ya vei yiga de kwaga lela ne doa pepelem to.
15A na zege da a nii wo-kenkagela yam konto to, mo a nɛ wo-gigilu na tigi tega ne ya maama dedoa dedoa teiŋa ne. 16Wo-gigillu tena tem nye daane mo, ye te nyeena ne kandwa-nyenno. Wo-gigilu maama maa nye de ko jege wo-gigilu kodwoŋi na wo ko wone ko gare-ko to. 17Wo-gigillu tem maa ná vei mɛ maama, te wó taa yɔɔre te vei wo-kenkagela yam yiga dedoa na yɔɔre mɛ to, ye te ba pipira. 18Wo-gigillu tem nia déem dɔra mo ye ya tiini ya jege foone. Yia mo yɔɔre ya faare nia yam jei maama.
19Wo-kenkagela yam ná zaŋe ya maa via, wo-gigillu tem de tɔge de-ya te vei mo. Wo-kenkagela yam maa ná jaane ya maa diini wɛɛne, wo-gigillu tem de wó jaane te di wɛɛne mo. 20Wo-kenkagela yam jworo déem wo wo-gigillu tem wone mo. Mo kokuri, jworo kom maa ná laga se ya vo mɛ maama, ya jege se ya vo dáane mo, ye wo-gigillu tem de wó zaŋe te tɔge te maa via. 21Ko na ye tei to, wo-kenkagela yam ná yeini ya via, wo-gigillu tem de tɔge de-ya te vei mo. Ya nam ná maŋe mɛ ya zege, wo-gigillu tem de wó taa zege mo. Ya daa ná zaŋe ya jaane wɛɛne, wo-gigillu tem de maa tɔge-ya te jaana. Kokuri to, wo-kenkagela yam jworo wo wo-gigillu tem wone mo.
22A ma nii wo-kenkagela yam yuni tem baŋa kam seeni a na woŋo na nye de wɛyuu pwola to na tigi da. Ka yɔɔre ka jege nenɔŋa ye ka nyeene jei maama mo ne gelaase na ye tei to. 23Pwola kam kuri seeni, wo-kenkagele maama yarege de vɔna mo pa ya dwei dedwoŋi vɔna. Wo-kenkagele maama ta ma kwei vɔna yalei de ma kwoli de yera yam. 24Wo-kenkagela yam ná yeini ya jaana, a ni ya vɔna yam na wuuri tei to mo. Ya sɔɔ kom nye de na-fwaaro na chuuri tei to mo. Ko ta maa nye de Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom tete kwora, naa jar-keira kɔgɔ sɔɔ na ye tei to. Ko daare ya ná jaane ya ti, ya yeini ya yage ya vɔna yam mo.
25Wo-kenkagela yam na zege da konto ye ya vɔna yam wo tega ne to, a ma ni kwora na nwoŋi pwola kalo na wo ya yuni tem baŋa seeni to. 26Pwola kam wɛyuu baŋa seeni woŋo maa wora, ko na nye de paare yituŋu, ye Safira mo ba mɛ ba ke-ko. Woŋo kodwoŋi de maa wo wɛyuu baŋa seeni, ko na jei yituŋu kom baŋa ne ye ko nye de nabiinu na ye tei to. 27A ma nii a na nenɛɛne ko na zege ko teiŋa seeni se ko taa diini to, ko yɔɔre ko nyeene ne channa na wo mini wone tei to mo. Ko ta na zege ko teiŋa ne se ko taa tua to, ko nye de ko ye mini mo. Pwooni delo na tiini de pera to de ma gilimi ko maama. 28Ko lam dem ye nenɛɛne doa ná nege ka waare ye manlaataŋa yeini ka gare wɛɛne tei to mo.
Nyenyego kom konto bere-ne Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom na ye tei to mo. A na nɛ konto to, mo a vwi a yibia tega ne, ye a ni nɔɔno kwora na ŋɔɔne de amo.

english_text:
The Lord Chooses Ezekiel
1The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, I want you to stand up and listen.” 2After he said this, his Spirit took control of me and lifted me to my feet. Then the Lord said:
3Ezekiel, I am sending you to the people of Israel. They are just like their ancestors who rebelled against me and refused to stop. 4They are stubborn and hardheaded. But I, the Lord God, have chosen you to tell them what I say. 5Those rebels may not even listen, but at least they will know that a prophet has come to them.
6Don't be afraid of them or of anything they say. You may think you're in the middle of a thorn patch or a bunch of scorpions. But be brave 7and preach my message to them, whether they choose to listen or not. 8Ezekiel, don't rebel against me, as they have done. Instead, listen to everything I tell you.
And now, Ezekiel, open your mouth and eat what I am going to give you.
9 Just then, I saw a hand stretched out toward me. And in it was a scroll. 10The hand opened the scroll, and both sides of it were filled with words of sadness, mourning, and grief.
translation_text:
Wɛ na bwoŋi Ezekeli tei to
1O ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu, zaŋe n zege wɛɛne se a ŋɔɔne dede‑m.” 2O na yɔɔre o wora o ŋɔɔne konto to, mo vio fuli ko zo-ne, ye ko gɔ-ne ko zege wɛɛne. Amo ma cheigi o na ŋɔɔne kolo de amo to.
3O ma ta o we, “Nabiinu, a lage a toŋe‑m Isarele tiina bam tei ne mo. Ba nam ye dwi delo nankɔɔre na daga to mo. Ba de ba nabaara bam nwoŋi amo kwaga ne, ye ba ta ve-ne de zem maama. 4Amo na toŋe‑m balo tei ne to yi dana ye ba zwa de ba ni taane. Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Taane dento ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage-de!’ 5Ba ná sɛ n taane dem, naa ba ná ve-de, ko ba fea. Ba maŋe ba ye zwabani-nyena mo. Ko laam wó pa ba lɔre we Wɛ sampwora tu o wo ba tetare ne. 6Nabiinu, ko nam ná ye nmo, yé ta‑n kɔre foone de-ba. Nam yé ta‑n fona de wonnu telo ba na tɛ ba pa‑m to. Ba ŋwɛ sem nye de sabare-mangwoli de kali-chena mo na gilimi‑m ya ke tetare ne, ye ba ni taane ta nye de nɔŋɔ na done nɔɔno tei to. De ko de, yé pa n yera taa sae ba ŋwɛ sem naa ba toro tem ŋwaane. Ta‑n yei we ba dwi dem ye nankɔ-nyena mo. 7Nam yɔɔre n ta amo taane dem n bere-ba, ba ze ná ti yiga se ba cheigi, naa ba ná ve mo de. Kokuri to, ba zwabania kam kɛ jeŋa mo. 8Se ko ná ye nmo nabiinu, fɔge n cheigi a na jege kolo se a ta dede‑m to. Yé lwoni nankɔ-nyena dwi dem konto kikia yam dwoŋi. Puri n ni se n di kolo maama a na lage a pa‑m to.”
9A laam ma nii a na jeŋa na twe ka jeeri amo, ye ka wo jege tɔnɔ na piri ko tigi da. 10O ma bwoli-ko o tiŋi a yiga ne. A ma na we ko yiga de ko kwaga maama ne, ba popone botare-bia ba ke da. Botare-bia bam bere luseim, de wo-chechɔgɔ, de lɛɛro taane yerane mo.

english_text:
1 The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, after you eat this scroll, go speak to the people of Israel.”
2-3He handed me the scroll and said, “Eat this and fill up on it.” So I ate the scroll, and it tasted sweet as honey.
4The Lord said:
Ezekiel, I am sending you to your own people. 5-6They are Israelites, not some strangers who speak a foreign language you can't understand. If I were to send you to foreign nations, they would listen to you. 7But the people of Israel will refuse to listen, because they have refused to listen to me. All of them are stubborn and hardheaded, 8so I will make you as stubborn as they are. 9You will be so determined to speak my message that nothing will stop you. I will make you hard like a diamond, and you'll have no reason to be afraid of those arrogant rebels.
10Listen carefully to everything I say and then think about it. 11Then go to the people who were brought here to Babylonia with you and tell them you have a message from me, the Lord God. Do this, whether they listen to you or not.
12The Spirit lifted me up, and as the glory of the Lord started to leave, I heard a loud, thundering noise behind me. 13It was the sound made by the creatures' wings as they brushed against each other, and by the rumble of the wheels beside them. 14Then the Spirit carried me away.
The Lord's power had taken complete control of me, and I was both annoyed and angry.
15When I was back with the others living at Abib Hill near the Chebar River, I sat among them for seven days, shocked at what had happened to me.
The Lord Appoints Ezekiel To Stand Watch
(Ezekiel 33.1-9)
16Seven days after I had seen the brightness of the Lord's glory, the Lord said:
17Ezekiel, son of man, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me. 18When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways so they won't be punished. If you refuse, you are responsible for their death. 19However, if you do warn them, and they keep on sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent.
20Now suppose faithful people start sinning, and I decide to put stumbling blocks in their paths to make them fall. They deserve to die because of their sins. So if you refuse to warn them, I will forget about the times they were faithful, and I will hold you responsible for their death. 21But if you do warn them, and they listen to you and stop sinning, I will let them live. And you will be innocent.
Ezekiel Cannot Talk
22The Lord took control of me and said, “Stand up! Go into the valley, and I will talk with you there.”
23I immediately went to the valley, where I saw the brightness of the Lord's glory, just as I had seen it near the Chebar River, and I bowed with my face to the ground. 24His Spirit took control of me and lifted me to my feet. Then the Lord said:
Go back and lock yourself in your house! 25You will be tied up to keep you inside, 26and I will make you unable to talk or to warn those who have rebelled against me. 27But the time will come, when I will tell you what to say, and you will again be able to speak my message. Some of them will listen; others will be stubborn and refuse to listen.
translation_text:
1O ta ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu, di kolo na tigi n yiga ne to. Done tɔnɔ kom se n daare n vo n ŋɔɔne de Isarele dwi tiina bam.” 2A de ma puri a ni ye o pa-ne tɔnɔ kom pa a done-ko.
3O daa ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu, done tɔnɔ konto a na kwei a pa‑m to maama n li n su n puga.” A ma seene a done-ko a li. Ko yɔɔre ko sona a ni ne mo, ne tooro na ye tei to.
4O ma ta de amo o we, “Ja amo kwora kam n vo n pa Isarele dwi tiina bam se ba ni a taane dem. 5A na toŋe‑m se n vo balo tei ne to dae nɔn-gɛ selo taane na ye de yera, ye de kuri nim chana to. Ko nam ye Isarele tiina bam mo a we n véi ba tei, 6se ko dae sa-teene delo taane na ye de yera, ye de chana se n wane n ni de kuri to. Ko ya ná ye banto tei ne mo a toŋe‑m, ba ya wó cheigi taane dem. 7Ko nam na ye tei to, Isarele dwi tiina bam bá sɛ se ba cheigi n taane dem, ba na vae se ba ni amo tete kwora to ŋwaane. Kokuri to, ba yɔɔre ba ye zwabani-nyena mo ye ba jege yi-dɛɛre. 8Nii mo! A lage a pa se nmo de taa jege wo-dɛɔ de yi-dɛɛre mo ne banto na ye tei to. 9Chega to, a lage a pa se n wo taa tiini ko dana ko gaale, ne peo na dana tei to. Konto ŋwaane, yé ta‑n kɔre foone de-ba. Yé pa n vɔna pare ba ŋwaane, de ba na maŋe ba ye nankɔ-nyena tei maama to de.”
10O ta maa we, “Nabiinu, fɔge n cheigi a taane dem lanyerane, se n daare n kwei kolo maama a na wó ta a bere‑m to n ke n yuu ne. 11Nmo laam ma‑n wó vo n dwi tiina balo ba na jaane-ba jara-keim baŋa ne ba kale ba vo Babilon teo ne to tei, se n ŋɔɔne de-ba. Ta de-ba we, ‘Taane dento ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage-de!’ Ba ná sɛ ba cheigi n taane dem, naa ba ná maŋe ba ve de, se n ta de-ba konto dwoŋi.”
12Vio laam ma fuli ko gɔ-ne ko zege wɛɛne. A ma ni sɔɔ na nwoŋi a kwaga ne ye ko tiini ko mumuna. Ko ye wo-kenkagela na bere Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom to mo zaŋe ya jeiga kam ne. 13A ma ni wo-kenkagela yam vɔna na mage daane ye ya sɔɔ kom zaŋe tei to, ko woli de wo-gigillu tem de na wo ya teiŋa ne to sɔɔ kom. Ko yɔɔre ko mumuni dedɛ. 14Vio kom daa ta ma gɔ-ne ko ja ko viiri. A maa yɔɔre a vei ye a wo pɛ. A bane de ma tiini de zaŋe. Baŋa Wɛ dam dem nam ya tiini de daga a baŋa ne mo. 15A ma vo a yi balo ba na jaane jara-keim baŋa ne ba kale ba ba ye ba laam zoore Tɛl-Abibi ne to tei. Jei sem konto bwola de Chebara buga kam. A ma maŋe ba na zoore mɛ to da yarepɛ. A na jeini ba tetare ne konto to, a yera sɔɔre mo.
Wɛ na kaane Isarele tiina tei to
16Da yarepɛ yam konto kwaga ne mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora tu amo tei ye o we:
17“Nabiinu, a le nmo mo a zege se n ta‑n yere Isarele dwi tiina bam n pa-ne. Nmo nam ye se n cheigi a kwora kam n daare n lwoni-ka n ma‑n kaane-ba mo n pa-ne. 18Amo ná pɛ puseŋ-nyeno kwora we, ‘N jege se n te mo,’ ye nmo wo vei n kaane‑o, kotu wó seene o te o tusim kikia ŋwaane. Nmo ná wo maŋe ko kuri n bere‑o se o yage o keim-lwanno tem se o wane o ŋwea o jwoŋi, o jege se o te mo. A nam wó bwei nmo mo o toone dem baŋa ne. 19Nmo nam ná vei n kaane kotu, ye o ná ve se o za o puseŋa kikia yam de o totoŋ-lwanno tem, o ta wó te mo o tusim kikia yam ŋwaane. Nmo tete nam wó fwoli n ba ŋona.
20Nɔn-ŋom ná yage totoŋ-laaro kikia ye o bobo se o taa toŋe lwarem, ye amo ná chege o chwoŋa, kotu de jege se o te mo. Nmo ná wo kaane‑o, o wó seene o te o wɛleera yam ŋwaane. Amo yiga bá taa wo o keim-laaro tem wone, ye a nam wó bwei‑m o toone dem baŋa ne. 21Nmo nam ná kaane kotu we o daa yé ke wɛleere pa o seene o wo ke-de, o daa bá te, o na sɛ kaanem dem to ŋwaane. Nmo de maa wó fwoli n ba ŋona.”
22Dáane mo Baŋa Wɛ dam dem wo amo baŋa ne. O ma ta de amo o we, “Zaŋe n nwoŋi n vo te-kampare laŋa kam seeni, se a lage a ŋɔɔne dede‑m dáane mo.” 23A ma seene a vo te-kampare sem. A ma na we Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom wo jei sem konto ne. Ko nye de a ya na nɛ-ko tei ye a wo Chebara buga kam ni ne to mo. A ma to a vwi a yibia tega ne.
24Vio ma fuli ko zo-ne pa a zaŋe a zege wɛɛne. Baŋa Wɛ ma ŋɔɔne de amo o we, “Jwoori n vo sɔŋɔ, se n pe n tete n yage diga ne. 25Nabiinu, nam ta lɔre we ba wó kwei ŋone mo ba vɔ‑m se n daa yé wane n nwoŋi n zo kɔgɔ wo. 26A maa wó pa n ni meeri pa se n jeini da chemm. N bá‑n wane n kaane-ba, de ba na yɔɔre ba ye zwabani-nyena tei to de. 27Maŋa nam ná yia se a ŋɔɔne dede‑m, a laam wó puri n ni se n daare n ta de-ba we, ‘Taane dento ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage-de.’ Balo na wó cheigi taane dem to wó yɔɔre ba sɛ-de. Balo de na wó ve-de to jege se ba taa ye konto. Kokuri to, ba dwi dem ye zwabani-nyena mo.”

english_text:
Ezekiel Acts Out an Attack on Jerusalem
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, son of man, find a brick and sketch a picture of Jerusalem on it. 2Then prepare to attack the brick as if it were a real city. Build a dirt mound and a ramp up to the top and surround the brick with enemy camps. On every side put large wooden poles as though you were going to break down the gate to the city. 3Set up an iron pan like a wall between you and the brick. All this will be a warning for the people of Israel.
4-5After that, lie down on your left side and stay there for 390 days as a sign of Israel's punishment—one day for each year of its suffering. 6Then turn over and lie on your right side 40 more days. That will be a sign of Judah's punishment—one day for each year of its suffering.
7The brick stands for Jerusalem, so attack it! Stare at it and shout angry warnings. 8I will tie you up, so you can't leave until your attack has ended.
9Get a large bowl. Then mix together wheat, barley, beans, lentils, and millet, and make some bread. This is what you will eat for the 390 days you are lying down. 10Eat only a small loaf of bread each day 11and drink only two large cups of water. 12Use dried human waste to start a fire, then bake the bread on the coals where everyone can watch you. 13When I scatter the people of Israel among the nations, they will also have to eat food that is unclean, just as you must do.
14I said, “Lord God, please don't make me do that! Never in my life have I eaten food that would make me unacceptable to you. I've never eaten anything that died a natural death or was killed by a wild animal or that you said was unclean.”
15The Lord replied, “Instead of human waste, I will let you bake your bread on a fire made from cow manure. 16Ezekiel, the people of Jerusalem will starve. They will have so little food and water that they will be afraid and hopeless. 17Everyone will be shocked at what is happening, and, because of their sins, they will die a slow death.”
translation_text:
Jerusalem nyenyego kom
1“Nabiinu, kwei biri n tiŋi n yiga ne, se n daare n la bibeiri de yera ne se se lwoni Jerusalem teo kom na ye tei to. 2Laam ke se ko bere we jar-keira kaare teo kom mo ba pu. Dogele kandwa, de teero n ja n di teo kom kabira kam yuu, se n daare n chwi vwoa se jar-keira bam taa zoore ya wone. Ta tiŋi da-kwollu telo ba na wó kwei ba ma mage kabira kam ba bwori to n kaare teo kom. 3N laam wó lage luu zon-tanlaŋa mo se ka ji kabira ka che nmo de teo kom kabira kam daane. Pipiri n yibia n jeeri teo kom nenɛɛne n tete mo li-ko n pu de jara. Keim dem konto ye se ko kaane Isarele dwi tiina bam mo.
4Nmo laam wó peini n jagwia saŋa ne, se ko bere we n zeŋe Isarele dwi tiina bam wɛleera mo. Da yalo wone nmo na wó peini da to ye maŋa kalo ba wɛleera jene na wó taa wo n yuu ne to mo. 5Nmo wó ta‑n tigi da da bia yatɔ de funogo (390) se ko bere bena yalo wone Isarele tiina bam na ke wɛleera to, se dɛ maama zege de pa bene. Da yam konto wone mo Isarele dwi tiina bam wɛleera jene wó taa wo n yuu ne.
6Da yam konto ná tu ya ti, se n pipiri n peini n jazem saŋa kam ne da finna (40), se ko bere we n zeŋe Judah dwi tiina bam wɛleera. Da yam konto de wó zege ya pa bena yalo Judah tiina de na yaare ba wɛleera ŋwaane to mo. 7Pipiri n jeeri Jerusalem teo de ko jara yam nyenyego kom, se n pu n jagula ko baŋa ne n pworisi n chɔge-ko. 8Amo lage a kwei ŋone mo a vɔ‑m a tiŋi da. N bá‑n wane n pipiri n peini saŋa kadwoŋi ne, ko ná dae we n kwaare jara yam de teo kom n ti.
9La banina, de chaara, de swoona, de sia, de mena, de kadaga n ke-te kambi-zɔŋɔ wone, se n daare n ma-te n wɔ bworobworo n ta‑n jege n di. Wodiu kom konto mo nmo wó ta‑n di da bia yatɔ de funogo (390) yalo nmo na wó ta‑n tigi n saŋa baŋa ne to. 10Nmo wó maŋe wodiu kom ja-bwanno nana mo se n ta‑n jege n di ko maŋa ko maŋa dɛ maama wone. 11Nam ta twei na se ba maŋe de kunkwolo-yi chicheiro, se n ta‑n jege-ba n nyɔ ko maŋa ko maŋa dɛ maama wone. 12Nii wodiu kom ne ko ye maasa mo n jege n di. Nam kwei nabiina beinnu n ji dɛ selo n na wó ma n wɔ bworobworo kom, ye n wɔ-ko mɛ nɔɔna bam maama na wó taa zege ye ba nii to.”
13 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta o we, “Tento bere Isarele tiina bam na wó ke tei ye ba di wodiiru telo na wo maŋe de chullu tem to dwi-gɛ tiina bam tetare ne, mɛ amo na wó zeili-ba se ba taa zoore to.”
14Amo ma ta a we, “Jan ja! Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, yé pa se a ke konto dwoŋi. Ko na zege a biini ne se ko yi leile, amo ta wo biini a tete de wodiiru telo na wo maŋe de chullu tem to. A bere a wo di wo-teko, naa woŋo kolo kago-vara na jaane ba go to.”
15Wɛ laam ma leiri o we, “Tɔ. A nam pɛ‑m chwoŋa se n kwei na-beinnu n ma n wɔ n bworobworo kom, se n daa‑n yé ma nabiinu beinnu n wɔ-ko.”
16O ta ma ta o we, “Nabiinu, a lage a pa Jerusalem teo kom ga wodiu mo. Ko nɔn-bia bam wó taa lare wodiiru ba di fenfee ye lwia jege-ba. Ba ta wó taa twei na fenfee ba nyɔ de wo-chechɔgɔ. 17Kokuri to, wodiiru de na wó tiini te taa jege zore. Teo kom nɔɔna bam ná nii daane, ba yera wó sɔɔre mo. Ba maa wó bugi ba jei ba wɛleera yam ŋwaane.”

english_text:
Jerusalem's Coming Destruction
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, son of man, get a sharp sword and use it to cut off your hair and beard. Weigh the hair and divide it into three equal piles. 2After you attack the brick that stands for Jerusalem, burn one pile of your hair on the brick. Chop up the second pile and let the small pieces of hair fall around the brick. Throw the third pile into the wind, and I will strike it with my own sword.
3Keep a few of the hairs and wrap them in the hem of your clothes. 4Then pull out a few of those hairs and throw them in the fire, so they will also burn. This fire will spread, destroying everyone in Israel.
5I am the Lord God, and I have made Jerusalem the most important place in the world, and all other nations admire it. 6But the people of Jerusalem rebelled and refuse to obey me. They ignored my laws and have become even more sinful than the nations around them.
7So tell the people of Jerusalem:
I am the Lord God! You have refused to obey my laws and teachings, and instead you have obeyed the laws of the surrounding nations. You have become more rebellious than any of them! 8Now all those nations will watch as I turn against you and punish you 9for your sins. Your punishment will be more horrible than anything I've ever done or will ever do again. 10 Parents will be so desperate for food that they will eat their own children, and children will eat their parents. Those who survive this horror will be scattered in every direction.
11Your sins have disgusted me and made my temple unfit as a place to worship me. So I swear by my own life that I will cut you down and show you no pity. 12A third of you will die here in Jerusalem from disease or starvation. Another third will be killed in war. And I will scatter the last third of you in every direction, then track you down and kill you.
13You will feel my fierce anger until I have finished taking revenge. Then you will know that I, the Lord, was furious because of your disobedience. 14Every passerby will laugh at your destruction. Foreign nations 15will insult you and make fun of you, but they will also be shocked and terrified at what I did in my anger. 16I will destroy your crops until you starve to death, and disasters will strike you like arrows. 17 Starvation and wild animals will kill your children. I'll punish you with horrible diseases, and your enemies will strike you down with their swords. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jerusalem teo na wó chɔge tei to
1“Nabiinu, kwei se-zɔɔ kolo ni na di lanyerane to n ma n fane n twana yam de n yu-ywei sem. Maŋe-te se n lɔre te dunni na mae tei to, se n daare n pɔɔre-te kuni betɔ. 2Nmo ná kwaare jara de Jerusalem teo nyenyego kom n ti, se n kwei n twana yam, de n yu-ywei sem popɔra betɔ wone dedoa n zwɛ teo nyenyego kom wone. N ta wó kwei se popɔra betɔ wone dedoa n ja n nwoŋi teo kom dáa ne n zage n gwo de se-zɔɔ. Ta daare n kwei se popɔra betɔ wone dedoa n dole n yage se vio ja-se ko jage. Amo laam wó kwei a se-zɔɔ mo a ma a pare-se. 3Nam daare yu-ywei fenfee se n kwei-se n vɔ n gɔrɔ ni ne. 4N daa‑n wó le yu-ywei sem konto wone mo, se n dole-se n de mini dem wone se se zwɛ. Mini dem konto mo lage de di de jage de yi Isarele dwi tiina bam maama.
5Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Konto lage ko bere Jerusalem teo kom na ye tei to mo. A ya kwei-ko a zege dwi-gɛ tiina tetare ne mo, ye ba teene dem gilimi-ko de ke tetare ne. 6Ko nɔn-bia bam nam nwoŋi a kwaga ne mo, ye ba toŋe puseŋa kikia yerane se ko dwoni dwi tiina balo na gilimi-ba to kikia na ye tei to. Ba yɔɔre ba ve a nia yam de a bera yam mo.
7Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Abam zwabania kikia maŋe ya dwoi teene delo na gilimi abam de ke tetare ne to, ye á ba tɔge a bera yam. Á nam ba sɛ a nia yam. Ko ná maŋe ko ye dwi tiina balo na gilimi abam to chullu tem, á wo kwaane á ke tento na bere tei to.
8Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Jerusalem tiina bam, amo tete nam wó pipiri a ji á dono. A lage a waare abam mo se dwi-gɛ tiina bam taa zege ba nia. 9A nam wó tiini a waare abam, á na zuli wo-zɔɔna to ŋwaane. A na wó ke abam tei to dae kolo a na maŋe a ke to, ye a nam daa bá fɔge a waare nɔɔna konto dwoŋi de. 10Kwoa wó tɔge ko baŋa ne ba di ba bia, ye bia de di ba kwoa, kana na jege-ba to ŋwaane. Amo wó waare abam á wɛleera ŋwaane. A ta wó jage abam wone balo na daare to a yage tega baŋa jei maama ne. 11Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ tage tento mo we: Ne amo na jege ŋwea tei to, ko yɔɔre ko ye chega mo we a jaane boboŋa se a ti abam mo, á na biini amo wara-jei sem de wo-zɔɔna, de totoŋ-vɛɛsa dwi maama to ŋwaane. A bá ŋɔne a pa abam naa a duri á yibwona kɔtaa! 12Abam teo nɔɔna bam popɔra betɔ wone dedoa mo lage ba maŋe teo kom wone ba te jawe-chɛɛro, de kana ŋwaane. Popɔra betɔ wone dedoa maa wó nwoŋi ye á dona bam go-ba jara baŋa ne. Á popɔra betɔ wone dedoa kalo na daare to, a maa wó jage-ba jei maama ne, ye a ta kwei a se-zɔɔ a pare-ba se a go.
13Amo ná ke konto ba yera ne a ti, a bane dem laam wó zuri, a na waare-ba se ko maŋe de ba wɛleera yam to ŋwaane. Amo ban-lom dem ná to ba baŋa ne konto, ba laam wó lɔre we ko ye amo Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ se ko ke-ba konto dwoŋi amo na chana ba baŋa ne to ŋwaane.
14Amo wó pa se á teo kom ji di-dwonnu se dwi-gɛ tiina balo na gilimi abam to na á chaveera, ye ba de balo maama na tɔge da ba maa kɛ to taa jege abam ba gwoona. 15Abam ná nɛ á lɛɛro tento, dwi-gɛ tiina bam wó taa jege abam ba twea ye ba mɔna. Ba nam ta wó kɔre foone de amo na yɔɔre a chɔge abam tei a ban-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane to. Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto. 16Kana lage ka ji chene delo vea na chana to mo, ye amo wó kwei-ka a ma a chɔge abam a ti. Amo wó pa kana taa jaane abam taa, á teo kom na wó ga wodiu dwi maama to ŋwaane. 17Amo wó pa se kana de kago-vara ba á baŋa de dam. Te nam wó ti á bia maama se á daa yé ta‑á jege bia. Jawe-chɛɛro, de tigura, de jara-keim wó to á tetare ne se te go abam. Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.”

english_text:
Israel Is Doomed
1The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, face the hills of Israel and tell them:
3Listen, you mountains and hills, and every valley and gorge! I, the Lord, am about to turn against you and crush all the places where foreign gods are worshiped. 4Every altar will be smashed, and in front of the idols I will put to death the people who worship them. 5Dead bodies and bones will be lying around the idols and the altars. 6Every town in Israel will be destroyed to make sure that each shrine, idol, and altar is smashed—everything the Israelites made will be a pile of ruins. 7All over the country, your people will die. And those who survive will know that I, the Lord, did these things. 8I will let some of the people live through this punishment, but I will scatter them among the nations, 9where they will be prisoners. And when they think of me, they will realize that they disgraced me by rebelling and by worshiping idols. They will hate themselves for the evil things they did, 10and they will know that I am the Lord and that my warnings must be taken seriously.
11The Lord God then said:
Ezekiel, beat your fists together and stomp your feet in despair! Moan in sorrow, because the people of Israel have done disgusting things and now will be killed by enemy troops, or they will die from starvation and disease. 12Those who live far away will be struck with deadly diseases. Those who live nearby will be killed in war. And the ones who are left will starve to death. I will let loose my anger on them! 13These people used to offer incense to idols at altars built on hills and mountaintops and in the shade of large oak trees. But when they see dead bodies lying around those altars, they will know that I am the Lord. 14I will make their country a barren wasteland, from the Southern Desert to the town of Diblah in the north. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Lɛɛro telo na wó yi Isarele tiina to
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora tu ka yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, pa n yibia jeeri Isarele peero tem seeni se n daare n pworisi taane n chɔge-te 3we, ‘Isarele peero tem, cheigi-na Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ kwora. Tento mo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ tage de peero tem, de zwonnu tem, de gugworru tem, de bwollu tem: A lage a pa jara mo zaŋe á jei sem maama ne, se a chɔge mɛ nɔɔna bam na diini ba zuli jwona da to. 4Amo wó yigi ba kaanem bimbina yam a de tega ne, ye a daare a chochoge bimbina yalo ba na zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa ya baŋa ne to. Nɔɔna bam ná zege ba jwona yam yiga ne ba zuli-ya, amo wó go-ba dáane mo. 5A laam wó yage abam Isarele tiina twa bam yera se ya taa tigi á jwona yam yiga ne. A maa wó pa á kwi sem jage se kaare á bimbina yam. 6Teene delo maama á na zoore de wone to wó chɔge mo, se wara-jei selo á na zuli jwona da to de chochoge. Á jwona kaanem bimbina yam wó ba ya chɔge zɔŋ-zɔŋ, ko ta woli de jwona yam tete. Bimbina yalo baŋa ne á na zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa to de wó chochoge. Woŋo kolo maama á na ke to jege se ko saare ko jei mo. 7Twa wó taa tigi jei maama abam tetare ne. Konto maama baŋa ne mo á wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.
8A nam wó pa abam badwonna chwoŋa se ba lu toone. Banto bá te jara wone, ba na jage ba zo teene dedwonna wone to ŋwaane. 9Ba dona maa ná kale-ba ba ja vo sa-teene wone se ba taa zoore da, ba laam wó guli amo gula. Ba maa wó lɔre we a wo tiini ko chɔge de ba na nwoŋi amo kwaga ne tei to. Kokuri to, ba mɛ ba kwaga ba ya amo mo, ye ba daare ba seene ba yia de jwona kaanem. Ba fera nam wó nwoŋi ba tete, lwarem de totoŋ-vɛɛsa yalo maama ba na ke to ŋwaane. 10Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. A na tage we a lage a pa lɛɛro telo yi-ba to, ko dae we a tɛ de a ni yerane mo.’ ”
11Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Mage n je sem daane, se n ta‑n nɔne n nɛ tega ne de dam, ye n daare n laare de wo-chechɔgɔ we, ‘Lɛɛro na!’ Ke konto Isarele dwi tiina bam totoŋ-lwanno, de ba wo-zɔɔna kikia yam ŋwaane. Ba nam lage ba te jara, de kana, de jawe-chɛɛro baŋa ne mo. 12Wolo na wo sa-teo wone to, jawe-chɛɔ mo wó go‑o. Wolo na bwola to de maa wó te jara wone. Wolo na daare ye o lu toone to de maa wó te de kana. A lage a tiini a waare-ba konto dwoŋi mo a ban-lom dem ŋwaane. 13Konto baŋa ne ba wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. Ko nam wó ke ne ba ná nɛ we ba tete tiina twa tigi ba faare tega baŋa jei maama. Ko wó taa ye ba jwona yam tetare ne, de ba kaanem bimbina yam teiŋa ne, de zwonnu tem de peero tem maama yuni ne, de tei-kamunnu kura ne mɛ ba ya na kwei talwoŋ-ywoŋa ba kaane ba pa ba jwona yam maama to mo. 14Amo wó zeiŋi a jeŋa mo se a waare-ba se a daare a chɔge ba tega kam se ka ji di-dwonnu yerane, ko zege kagoa kam ne se ko yi Dibila. Amo wó chɔge jei selo maama ba na zoore to. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_text:
Disaster Is Near
1The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that I am saying:
Israel will soon come to an end! Your whole country is about to be destroyed 3as punishment for your disgusting sins. I, the Lord, am so angry 4that I will show no pity. I will punish you for the evil you've done, and you will know that I am the Lord.
5There's never been anything like the coming disaster. 6And when it comes, your life will be over. 7You people of Israel are doomed! Soon there will be panic on the mountaintops instead of celebration. 8I will let loose my anger and punish you for the evil things you've done. You'll get what you deserve. 9Your sins are so terrible, that you'll get no mercy from me. Then you will know that I, the Lord, have punished you.
10Disaster is near! Injustice and arrogance are everywhere, 11and violent criminals run free.
