O ma toŋe nɔɔna Ejipti teo ne se ba ja jar-keira de sisein-nɔɔna dedɛ ba ba ba pa‑o. Nɔɔno wonto nam wó wane o lu Babilon teo pɛ wom jeŋa ne na? O na lɔge ba ni-gwonim dem kwaga ne to, o wó jwoŋi o tete o yage na?
16Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we kotu lage o te Babilon teo ne mo, se o bá lu. Ko ye Babilon teo pɛ mo tiŋi‑o paare, ye o nam chɔge duuri delo o na dugi to pa se o nwoŋi ni-sɛɛm delo ba na ke daane to kwaga ne. Babilon teo kom wone mo o lage o te! 17Ejipti teo pa-faro wom de o jar-keira bam seene ba ye babɛ. Ba nam bá wane ba jwoŋi Judah pɛ wom ba yage, de ba kɔgɔ kom na maŋe ko daga tei to de. Babilon jar-keira bam wó ba ba kaare Jerusalem teo kom ba pu ye ba daare ba dogele kandwa, de teero ba ja ba di teo kom kabira kam yuu, se ba wane ba go teo kom nɔn-bia dedɛ. 18Judah pɛ wom ve o duuri dem de o na lɔge ba ni-gwonim dem kwaga ne tei to mo. Chega ŋwaane to, o ya ke kampwola mo, ye o ta ke wonnu tem konto maama o ma o chɔge-ka. Konto ŋwaane, o bere o bá lu.
19Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Ne amo na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a lage a waare‑o mo. Ko ye amo yere ŋwaane mo o dugi duuri ye o ta ve-de. O na chɔge ni-gwonim delo to de maa ye amo nyem. O keina yam konto jene wó taa wo o yuu ne. 20A lage a che kalanchogo mo se ko ja‑o. A laam wó ja‑o a vo Babilon, ye a di o taane dáane, o na nwoŋi a kwaga ne to ŋwaane. 21O jar-keira babɛ sem maama wó te jara wone. A ta wó jage balo na wó daare to a yage tega baŋa jei maama ne. Konto baŋa ne mo á wó lɔre we ko ye amo Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ kwora kam konto.
22Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo tete mo lage a ja Sedare tei-dedɔrɔ kodwoŋi na-gela, ye a daare a bwori na-bobɔla dedoa na wo ko yuu ne to. Amo tete laam wó ja-ka á vo a jeiri peo kodwoŋi yuu ne wɛ-wɛ. 23Isarele peero tem yuu ne mo a lage a jeiri-ka. Tio kom wó be lanyerane ye ko ta nɛ, ko daare ko ke bia. Ko maa wó ji Sedare tei-laao. Zuna dwi dwi wó ba da ba sɔ ba pworu ko nɛ sem ne, ye ba sii ko woro kom ne. 24Teeni dem maama na wo goa wone to wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. A maa wae a pa se tei-dedwaaro toe, ye a daare a pa teeni delo na wo tega ne to zaŋe wɛɛne. A ta wae a pa se teeni delo na jege vɔ-lɛɛro to kwaara, ye a daare a pa delo na kwaare to yera zuri.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto. A nam wó seene a ke kolo a na tage to.’ ”

english_text:
Those Who Sin Will Die
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying,
“Sour grapes eaten by parents
leave a sour taste in the mouths
of their children.”
3Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel. 4The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
5Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right. 6He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period. 7He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor 8and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone 9 and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
10But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins 11his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife, 12cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things, 13and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
14But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him. 15He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife. 16He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor 17and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father. 18It is his father who will die for cheating and robbing and doing evil.
19You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws. 20 Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
21Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death. 22All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right. 23I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
24But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
25You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are! 26If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned. 27And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 28They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death. 29But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
30I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished. 31Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins? 32 I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_text:
Wolo na ke wɛleere to mo jege se o te
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ta ma yi amo we:
2“Bɛ mo ye abam jege memaŋe dento na vei Isarele tega kam seeni to ye á tɛ á we:
‘Kwoa mo ke ba wonnu,
pa te zem laam gwori ba bia’?
3Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we abam daa bá maŋe memaŋe dem konto Isarele laŋa kam ne. 4Nii-na! Amo mo jege nabiina maama dam, ne ko ná ye kwo, naa o bu de. Ko ye wolo na ke wɛleera to mo jege se o te.
5Nɔɔno wolo ná seene o ye nɔn-ŋom chekke,
kotu wae o ke totoŋ-ŋona ye o tɔge chwoŋa.
6O maa ba diini peero tem yuu se o di jwona wodiiru,
ye o yiga tera de Isarele dwi tiina jwona yam.
O ba ke tolo de o dwonna bam kaana.
O maa ba peini de kaane wolo na jege o chana zarem o ke to.
7O nam ba bɛɛse nɔɔn-nɔɔno.
O na jwoŋi wonnu telo nɔɔno tei ne jene ŋwaane to
mo o wó jwoori o pa kotu.
O maa ba vere nɔɔna.
O ta yeini o pa wodiu yi balo kana na jege-ba to,
o daare o kwei gwaaro o kwoli yiniga tiina chaveera.
8Konto tu ba jene wonnu o pae
ye o daŋe nyɔɔre dedɛ jene dem baŋa ne.
O maa cho o tete de wo-lwanno kikia
ye o bore nɔɔna taane de chega.
9O maa toŋe o tɔge a bera yam,
ye o ke o chega de a nia yam.
Nɔɔno wolo ná seene o ke konto dwoŋi,
konto tu ye chega tu mo,
ye o wó seene o taa ŋwe.”
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
10“Nɔɔno wom konto nam ná loge bu, ye bu wom ná ye nankɔ-nyem na ye nɔn-goro, ye o daare o ke wonnu tem konto dwoŋi, bu wom jege se o te mo, 11ye o kwo ya wo ke te kolokolo.
O kare o di jwona wodiiru peero yuu bimbina yam ne.
O ta maa swoi se o taa tigi de o dwoŋi kaane.
12O maa jege nabwona de yiniga tiina o bɛɛsa,
ye o kare o vere nɔɔna.
O yeini o cheiŋi kolo ba na pɛ‑o ba ma tiŋi daare to.
O yiga maa wo jwona wone,
ye o daare o tɔge wo-zɔɔna kikia.
13O ta yeini o jene wonnu o pa nɔɔna,
ye o beeri nyɔɔre dedɛ mo se o dɔne.
Nɔɔno ná ke konto dwoŋi, o wó jwoŋi o ŋwea o yage mo na? Kɔtaa! O bá na o ŋwea! Wo-zɔɔna yalo maama o na ke to ŋwaane, o wó te mo ye ko wó taa ye o tete yiga.
14Ko daare, bu wom konto de ná loge bu, ye o bu wom ná nɛ wɛleera yalo o kwo na jege o ke to, ye o ná ve se o ke ne o kwo na ke wo-zɔɔna yalo to, o bá te o kwo wɛleera yam ŋwaane.
15O ba diini peero tem yuu se o di jwona wodiiru,
ye o yiga tera de Isarele dwi tiina jwona yam.
O maa ba ke tolo de o dwonna kaana.
16O ba bɛɛse nɔɔn-nɔɔno.
O ba jwoŋi woŋo nɔɔno tei ne
se o laam jene jene o pa kotu.
O ba vere nɔɔna
O ta yeini o pa wodiu yi balo kana na jege-ba to,
o daare o kwei gwaaro o kwoli yiniga tiina chaveera.
17O maa cho o tete de totoŋ-balwaaro,
ye o ba beeri nyɔɔre dedɛ se o dɔne jena baŋa ne.
O maa toŋe o tɔge a nia yam de a bera yam.
Bu wom konto bá te o kwo wɛleera ŋwaane. O wó taa ŋwe mo. 18O kwo nam wó te o tete wɛleera ŋwaane mo, de o na pini nɔɔna, ye o vere o chorro, ye o daare o toŋe lwarem o tete nɔɔna tetare ne tei to.
19Abam nam bwei we, ‘Bɛ mo ye bu wom konto bá tɔge o yaare o kwo tusim dem ŋwaane?’ Ko na ye tei to, bu wom na jege chega ye o ke kolo na maŋe to, o daare o toŋe o tɔge a bera yam to ŋwaane, o wó seene o taa ŋwe mo. 20Wolo ná ke wɛleere, konto tu mo jege se o te. Nɔɔno kwo wɛleera jene bá taa wo kotu yuu ne. Bu de wɛleera nam bá taa tɔge o kwo. Nɔn-ŋona wó na ba totoŋ-laaro tem nyɔɔre mo, se nɔn-balwaaro na waarem delo na maŋe de ba totoŋ-lwanno tem to.
21Puseŋ-nyeno wolo nam ná pipiri o yage wɛleera keim, kotu bá te. O nam ná toŋe o tɔge a bera yam maama, ye o ke o chega de kikia yalo na maŋe to, kotu wó taa ŋwe mo, o daa bá te. 22Ko ná ye wɛleera yalo o ya na maŋe o ke to, amo bá ke tento a boboŋa ne. O nam wó taa ŋwe mo, o na lɛɛre o ke totoŋ-ŋona yalo to ŋwaane. 23Á nam boŋe we puseŋ-nyena toone mo pae amo wo pwoli na? Ko nam na ye tei to, puseŋ-nyena ná pipiri ba yage ba chwei sem, se ko pa ba na ŋwea, konto wó pa a wo pwoli. Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
24Ko daare, nɔn-ŋom ná yage totoŋ-ŋona keim, ye o bobo se o taa ke wo-zɔɔna yalo dwoŋi puseŋ-nyena bam na kare ba ke to, á boŋe we o wó taa ŋwe mo na? Kɔtaa! Amo bá ke wo-laaro telo o ya na ke to a boboŋa ne. O de jege se o te mo, o na ke wɛleera yalo o ma o chɔge amo yiga to ŋwaane.
25Abam maa yeini á tɛ we, ‘Chega tera Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge chwei selo to wone.’ Isarele dwi tiina bam, á pa-na dé taa tɛ chega. Ko ye amo mo ba toŋe ko chwoŋa ne na? Ko dae abam za mo toŋe á tusi na? 26Nɔn-ŋom ná pipiri o yage totoŋ-ŋona keim, ye o lɛɛre o ke wɛleera, o jege se o te mo o wɛleera kikia ŋwaane. 27Puseŋ-nyeno nam ná yage puseŋa kikia yalo o ya na ke to, ye o daare o toŋe chega kam de kikia yalo na maŋe to, o wó jwoŋi o ŋwea o yage mo. 28Kolo na wó jwoŋi‑o to ye o na jeeli o totoŋ-lwanno tem ni o ja, ye o daare o pipiri o yage-te to. O daa bá te, o wó taa ŋwe mo. 29Isarele dwi tiina bam nam ta maa tɛ ba we, ‘Chega tera Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge chwei selo to wone.’ Chega seene ka tera se wone na? Isarele dwi tiina bam, ko dae abam za mo toŋe á tusi na?
30Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Konto ŋwaane, Isarele dwi tiina bam, amo lage a di abam dedoa dedoa taane mo se ko maŋe de á na ke tei to. Nam pipiri-na á yage á tusim kikia yam maama, se á yé na waarem. Ko ná dae konto, á wɛleera yam wó pa á tiri á to tega ne. 31Dole-na wɛleera yalo maama á na yeini á ke to á yage, se á daare á beeri bochare-doore de boboŋ-doora á pa á tete. Isarele dwi tiina bam, bɛ mo ye á beeri toone á pa á tete? 32Nɔɔn-nɔɔno toone nam ba pae a wo pwola. Konto ŋwaane, pipiri-na á yage wɛleera kikia se á daare á na ŋwea. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Israel's Leaders
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
2Your mother was a brave lioness
who raised her cubs
among lions.
3She taught one of them to hunt,
and he learned to eat people.
4When the nations heard of him,
they trapped him in a pit,
then they used hooks
to drag him to Egypt.
5His mother waited
for him to return.
But soon she lost all hope
and raised another cub,
who also became fierce.
6He hunted with other lions
and learned to eat people.
7He destroyed fortresses
and ruined towns;
his mighty roar
terrified everyone.
8Nations plotted to kill him,
and people came from all over
to spread out a net
and catch him in a trap.
9They put him in a cage
and took him to Babylonia.
The lion was locked away,
so that his mighty roar
would never again be heard
on Israel's hills.
10Your mother was a vine like you,
growing near a stream.
There was plenty of water,
so she was filled with branches
and with lots of fruit.
11Her strong branches
became symbols of authority,
and she was taller
than all other trees—
everyone could see how strong
and healthy she was.
12But in anger, I pulled her up
by the roots
and threw her to the ground,
where the scorching desert wind
dried out her fruit.
Her strong branches wilted
and burned up.
13Then she was planted
in a hot, dry desert,
14where her stem caught fire,
and flames burned
her branches and fruit.
Not one strong branch is left;
she is stripped bare.
This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_text:
Isarele dedɛɛra bam luseim leiŋa
Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we:
1“Mɔ luseim leiŋa n pa Isarele teo dedɛɛra bam 2se n ta we:
‘Á nu wom ye tetɛ mo?
O nam nye de nywoŋ-kana na jege yuu
nywonnu tem maama tetare ne to mo!
Ko maa tigi nywon-pɔle sem tetare ne ko kɔne ko bia.
3Ko ma korese ko bia bam wone dedoa
pa ko ji nywoŋ-doŋo na dana to.
Ko de ma lɔre nɔna jaanem,
ye ko bobo se ko taa di nabiina.
4 Dwi-gɛ tiina laam ma ni ko ŋwa,
ye ba daare ba ko gwoŋo ko ŋwaane pa ko to da.
Ba ma kwei gwoli ba lei ko ba ne
ye ba ja-ko ba vo Ejipti teo.
5Nywoŋ-kana kam na maane we ka teena yam wo ke,
ye ka boboŋa yam de wo toŋe to,
ka daa ma le ka bia bam wone dedoa
ka korese-ko pa ko de ji nywoŋo na dana to.
6Ko de na bege ko ti to, ko ma kare de nywonnu tedwonna
ko beeri nɔna.
Ko de ma ba ko lɔre nɔna jaanem
ye ko bobo se ko taa di nabiina.
7Nywoŋo kom konto yeini ko chɔge nɔɔna bam dam jei sem mo,
ye ko gwɛɛne ba teene dem de.
Teo kom de ko nɔɔna bam ná yeini ba ni ko na suuri tei to,
foone mo yɔɔre de jaane-ba.
8Teene delo maama na gilimi da to maa ba
ba ke ni daane se ba ja-ko.
Ba ma tiŋi ŋwe-choa se ba ja-ko,
ye ko to ba gwoŋo wone.
9Ba laam ma kwei gwoli ba lei ko ba ne,
ye ba vaŋe-ko ba vo ba ke chefeɔ wone.
Ba ma ja-ko ba vo ba pa Babilon teo pɛ wom.
Ba ma pe nywoŋo kom konto,
pa se ko ŋuurim dem daa yé taa ni Isarele peero tem yuni ne.
10Abam nu wom nam ya ta nye de Vini tio
kolo ba na jeiri á Vini kara ne to mo
pa ko wo buga teiŋa ne.
Ko ma leiri bia dedɛ, ye ko nɛ sem de ke zwase,
na na daga ko jeiga kam ne to ŋwaane.
11Ko nɛ sem ma fɔge se ke dam,
ye se maŋe se ba kwei-se ba ke pɛ nacheiga to.
Vini tio kom ke dedɔrem
se ko dwoni teeni delo maama na gilimi-ko to mo.
Nɔɔna maama maa nii ba nae ko na zege deiki tei to,
ko nɛ sem na daga to ŋwaane.
12Ba nam dɛ bane baŋa ne mo ba vaŋe-ko ba vuuri,
ye ba daare ba dole-ko ba de tega ne.
Vio ma zaŋe wɛ-puli seeni ko dole ko mage-ko,
pa se ko tio-bia bam ko.
Ko na-dɛɛro tem de ma bwori pa se te kwaare
ye mini di-te.
13Ba laam nam jaane Vini tio kom konto
ba vo ba jeiri kagoa yuu ne mo,
mɛ tega kam na koge ye na tera to.
14Mini ma zege ko teiŋa ne de jage de yi
ko nɛ sem de ko bia bam maama ko di kula.
Na-dɛa daa wo daare
se ka maŋe de pɛ nacheiga se o taa zeera.’
Leiŋa kanto mo ye luseim leiŋa, ye ba jege se ba taa jege-ka ba mɔɔne luseim mo.”

english_text:
Israel Keeps On Rebelling
1Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord. 2Just then, the Lord God said:
3Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
4Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
5 Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants. 6I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all. 7I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God, 8but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods.
In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt. 9But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt. 10So I brought them out and led them into the desert. 11 I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right. 12 And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me. 13But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day.
Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all. 14But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt. 15 Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised. 16I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
17Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert. 18So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols. 19I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings. 20I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God. 21But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day.
I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert. 22But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt. 23 So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations, 24because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made. 25I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life, 26and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
27Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me 28by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them! 29I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
30Then ask the Israelites why they are following the example of their wicked ancestors 31by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer. 32They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen!
The Lord Promises To Restore Israel
The Lord said to the people of Israel:
33As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger 34and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered 35and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you 36and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt. 37I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement. 38I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
39Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me! 40When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices. 41When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy, 42and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors. 43Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me, 44so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God.
Fire from the South
45The Lord said, 46“Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests 47that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path. 48Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
49But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_text:
Isarele tiina zwabania kam
1Bena yarepɛ bene dem chane senu chana kam da fuga dɛ dem ne, mo Isarele teo nakwa bam badwonna tu amo tei se ba bwei ba lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa na ye tei to. Ba ma ba ba jeini a yiga ne. 2Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:
3“Nabiinu, ŋɔɔne de Isarele teo nakwa bam se n ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam tu se á lɔre amo boboŋa na ye tei to mo na? Ne amo na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a bá pa abam chwoŋa se á lɔre a boboŋa. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.’
4Nabiinu, nmo nam bá bore taane n vane-ba na? Tole ba kwoa bam wo-zɔɔna kikia yam taane se ba taa yei ya ni ne. 5Ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Maŋa kalo a déem na kuri Isarele tiina bam se ba taa ye a nyem to, a tu a veere a tete de Jakob dwi tiina bam Ejipti teo ne. A ma daare a du yi-seena duuri de-ba a we, “Amo mo ye abam Teiru Baŋa Wɛ wom.” 6Amo ta ma du duuri maŋa kam konto ne a ta de-ba we, a wó ja-ba a nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne a vo tega kalo a ya na kuri a pa-ba to. Tega kam konto nam ye te-ŋoŋa kalo na lana ka dwoi jei maama, ye ka ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ to. 7A ma ta de-ba a we, “Abam maama nam dole-na wo-zɔɔna nyenyero telo á na zuli to á yage, se á daa yé ta‑á biini á tete de Ejipti tiina jwo-yɔɔro tem kaanem. Amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”
8Ba nam lɔge amo kwaga ne mo, pa ba ve se ba cheigi a taane dem. Ba wolowolo wo dole wo-zɔɔna yalo ba na zuli to de Ejipti tiina jwona yam ba yage. Konto ŋwaane amo boboŋa ma ja se a lwo a ban-lom dem ba baŋa ne, se a pa ba yaare Ejipti teo kom wone. 9Amo déem nam ba lage se dwi-gɛ tiina bam taa jege amo yere ba yaala. A yere dem ŋwaane a tage we a wó ja Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne, pa se a veere a tete a pa-ba ye dwi tiina balo ba na zoore ba wone to de zege ba nia.
10Konto ŋwaane mo a seene a ja-ba a nwoŋi Ejipti ne, ye a ja-ba a zo kagoa kam wo. 11A ma kwei a bera yam de a nia yam a pa-ba. Kokuri to, nɔɔno wolo ná toŋe o tɔge-ya, kotu wó na ŋwea ya baŋa ne. 12A ta ma tiŋi a siu da yam a pa-ba, se ya taa ye maana na tigi amo de banto tetare ne we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo kuri-ba se ba taa ye amo nyem. 13De ko maama de, Isarele dwi tiina bam nwoŋi amo kwaga ne mo kagoa kam yuu ne. Ba maa wo sɛ se ba ke ba tɔge a bera yam, ye ba daare ba ve a nia yam. Ko nam ye wolo maama ná tɔge yanto mo kotu wó na ŋwea ya baŋa ne. Ba ta ma yɔɔre ba yaale a siu da yam. Ko ma pa se a ja boboŋa se a lwo a ban-lom dem ba baŋa ne se a yɔɔre a chɔge-ba kagoa kam wone. 14Amo nam ba lage se dwi-gɛ tiina bam taa jege amo yere ba yaala, de banto na nii ye a ja Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi dáane to. 15Ko kwaga ne to, a déem dugi duuri a pa-ba kagoa kam ne mo we, a daa bá ja-ba a zo tega kalo a ya na kuri se a pa-ba to. Tega kanto nam mo ye te-ŋoŋa kalo na lana ka dwoi jei maama, ye ka ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ to. 16Amo déem vane-ba konto, ba na ve a nia yam de a bera yam, ye ba ta yaale a siu da yam to ŋwaane mo. Ba fera nam tiini ya wo ba jwona kaanem wone mo. 17De ko de a duri ba ŋwaŋa mo, pa se a wo yɔɔre a chɔge-ba kagoa kam wone.
18A déem ma kaane ba bia bam kagoa yuu ne a we, “Abam de daa yé tɔge-na á kwoa bam chwei sem de ba chullu tem. Nam yé biini-na á tete de ba jwona yam kaanem. 19Amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Ta‑á sɛ-na amo bera yam, se á daare á ta‑á ke á tɔge a nia yam. 20Ta‑á jege-na a siu da yam se ya taa ye ya yera, se yanto taa ye maana amo de abam tetare ne. Konto mo abam wó lɔre we amo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”
21Ba dwi dem de nam lɔge amo kwaga ne mo. Ba wo sɛ ba tɔge a bera yam. Ba yiga de maa tere a nia yam wone. Wolo maama nam ná tɔge yanto, kotu wó na ŋwea ya baŋa ne. Ba ta yɔɔre ba yaale a siu da yam mo. Konto ŋwaane amo boboŋa ma ja se a lwo a ban-lom dem ba baŋa ne, se a pa ba yaare kagoa kam yuu ne. 22De ko de, a yɔɔre a ja a bane dem mo, se dwi-gɛ tiina bam yé taa jege amo yere ba yaala, de banto na nii ye a ja Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne to. 23A nam ta dugi duuri mo a pa-ba kagoa kam ne we a lage a jage-ba pa ba vo yiga yiga se a yage-ba logo baŋa teene dem jei maama wone. 24Ko nam ye ba na wo sɛ ba tɔge amo nia yam, ye ba ve a bera yam to ŋwaane mo a ke-ba konto. Ba ta ma yaale amo siu da yam, ye ba daare ba pa ba fera zo ba kwoa jwona yam ne. 25Amo ta ma pa ba sɛ bera yalo na ba lana to, de chullu telo nɔɔna na bá na ŋwea te baŋa ne to. 26A ma pa ba biini ba tete de pɛɛra yalo ba na kwei ba pa-ne to. Ba bere ba yeini ba kwei ba bu-kwe sem maama mo ba ke kaanem. A ke konto maama ba yera ne se foone mo zo-ba, ye ba daare ba lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.’
27Nabiinu, konto ŋwaane nam ta de Isarele tiina bam we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam kwoa bam de déem maŋe ba twe-ne mo de ba na nwoŋi amo kwaga ne tei to. 28Amo na yɔɔre a ja-ba a yi tega kalo a na dugi duuri we a wó kwei a pa-ba to, mo ba ná nɛ peero telo maama na zeiŋi wɛɛne to, de teeni delo maama na pae woro to, ba yeini ba ke kaanem da. Ba pɛɛra yam konto chuchugi a bane mo. Ba maa zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa ba daare ba lwo wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛra jei sem konto ne. 29Amo déem bwei-ba a we, “Jeiga kɔ mo á yeini á diini wɛ-wɛ se á ke kaanem da to?” ’ Mo kokuri ba bwoi jei sem yere we ‘Wɛ-wɛ Jeiga’ de zem maama.
30Nam ta de Isarele dwi tiina bam we: ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam de boŋe se á biini á tete ne á kwoa bam déem na ke tei to mo, se á de pa á fera taa wo wo-zɔɔna kaanem ne na? 31Abam na kwei á pɛɛra yam á pa jwona, ye á kwei mini á zwɛ á bia se ko taa ye kaanem to, á jege á tete mo á biini de á jwona yam de zem maama. Isarele dwi tiina bam, á nam boŋe we amo wó pa chwoŋa se á ta‑á tui á beeri a boboŋa mo na? Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we amo bá sɛ se á bwei á lɔre a boboŋa yam.
32Abam maa tɛ we, “Debam nam lage se dé taa nye de dwi-gɛ tiina bam na zoore logo baŋa teene dedwonna dem ne ye ba zuli wa yalo ba na mɛ dɛ de kandwa ba ke to mo.” Abam boboŋe dem nam bá fɔge de jeini. 33Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we, amo wó taa ye abam pɛ, pa se a kwei a je-dɛa, de a dam maama, de a ban-lom dem a taa nii abam baŋa ne. 34A maa wó ja abam a nwoŋi teene delo maama a ya na jage abam a yage de wone to de je-dɛa, de dam, dedaane a ban-lom dem. 35Amo laam wó ja abam mo a vo a zege kagoa kam wone mɛ dwi-gɛ tiina na gilimi to. Dáane mo a wó jeeri abam yibia de yibia, ye a di á taane se á to. 36Amo déem na di á kwoa bam taane tei Ejipti teo kagoa kam ne to, konto dwoŋi mo a ta wó di abam de taane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto. 37A ta wó korese abam pa se á ke ne dé ni-gwonim dem na bere se á ke tei to. 38A maa wó le zwabani-nyena balo na wo á wone to, de balo maama na ve-ne to. A nam wó ja-ba a nwoŋi sa-teene delo ba na zoore de wone to. Ba nam bá na chwoŋa se ba tɔge ba zo Isarele tega kam wone. Konto baŋa ne abam de wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.
39Ko nam ná ye abam, Isarele dwi tiina bam, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Á maama véi-na á zuli á jwona yam, ne á na jege boboŋa yalo to. Á ná lage á ve amo ni dem, daa ta‑á ke-na konto dwoŋi taa. Nam lɔre-na we, a bá sɛ se á ta‑á jege amo yere dem na ye wose to á yaala, de pɛɛra yalo á na kwei á pae á jwona yam to. 40Kokuri to, maŋa wó ba ye Isarele dwi dem maama taa zuli-ne ba tega kam ne. Ba maa wó zuli-ne Isarele peo-kamunu kolo a na pɔɔre a pa a tete to yuu ne, ye amo de wó sɛ se ba taa ye a nɔɔna. Dáane mo amo wó beeri á pɛɛra yam, dedaane wo-laaro telo á na wó pɔɔre se á kwei-ya á ma á ke kaanem á pa-ne to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto. 41Amo ná jaane abam a nwoŋi sa-teene delo ne a na jage abam pa á zo dwi-gɛ tiina bam wone to, a laam wó sɛ a jwoŋi abam nenɛɛne á ye talwoŋ-ywoŋa mo ba zwɛ ba pa-ne. A ta ná wo abam tetare ne, a wó bere jaja we a ye wose mo, se dwi-gɛ tiina bam taa zege ba nia. 42Amo laam maa ná jaane abam a ja a jwoori Isarele tega kalo a déem na dugi duuri we a wó kwei-ka a pa á kwoa bam to, á wó seene á lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom. 43Maŋa kam konto ne, abam wó guli wo-zɔɔna kikia yalo á ya na ke pa se á biini á tete to. Konto wó pa á yaale á tete de wo-lwanno telo a ya na ke to. 44Isarele dwi tiina bam, abam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom, ne a ná tɔge a yere dem ŋwaane a duri abam ŋwaŋa, ye a wo waare abam se ko maŋe de á totoŋ-lwanno tem de á wo-zɔɔna kikia yam na ye tei to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ”
Tega-kuri seeni taane
45 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ta ma yi amo we:
46“Nabiinu, pipiri n yibia n jeeri tega-kuri seeni jei sem. Tɔɔle kwora n chɔge kuri seeni tiina bam, se n daare n pworisi taane n chɔge kuri seeni goa kam. 47Nam ta de kuri seeni goa kam we: ‘Cheigi Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam! Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: A yɔɔre a ti a yiga mo se a zwɛ nmo de mini. De nam lage de di n teeni dem maama mo kula! Tei-lɛɛro de delo na koge to maama wó zwɛ mo. Min-lɔŋɔ kom konto nam bá di ko dwei kɔtaa. De maa wó zwɛ kolo maama na tigi de yiga ne ko zege tega-kuri seeni se ko taa diini baŋa seeni to mo. 48Nɔɔna maama wó lɔre we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tɔre mini dem konto, ye de nam bá di de dwei kɔtaa.’ ”
49Amo de laam ma ta a we, “Ja! Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, ko wó ja lɛɛro mo ko ba amo yuu ne! Ba nam maŋe ba jege amo taane mo ba tɛ we, ‘O taana yam yeini ya ye dende mo.’ ”

english_text:
The Lord Will Punish Jerusalem
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel 3that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil. 4From south to north, people will die, 5knowing that my sword will never be put away.
6Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you. 7When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise!
A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
8The Lord said:
9-10Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem:
I have sharpened my sword
to slaughter you;
it is shiny and will flash
like lightning!
Don't celebrate—
punishment is coming,
because everyone has ignored
my warnings.
11My sword has been polished;
it's sharp and ready to kill.
12Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel;
the sword is drawn against
my people and their leaders.
They will die!
So give up all hope.
13I am testing my people,
and they can do nothing
to stop me.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
14Ezekiel, warn my people,
then celebrate my victory
by clapping your hands.
My vicious sword will attack
again and again,
killing my people
with every stroke.
15They will lose all courage
and stumble with fear.
My slaughtering sword
is waiting at every gate,
flashing and ready to kill.
16It will slash right and left,
wherever the blade is pointed.
17Then I will stop being angry,
and I will clap my hands
in victory.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The King of Babylonia and His Sword
18The Lord said:
19Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions. 20Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah. 21When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal. 22His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people. 23Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
24Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
25And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here. 26I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies. 27I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city.
Judgment against Ammon
28 The Lord God said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying:
A sword is drawn,
ready to slaughter;
it is polished and prepared
to kill as fast as lightning.
29You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
30Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth. 31My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing. 32You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ se-zɔɔ kom taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ta ma yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, pipiri n yibia n jeeri Jerusalem teo kom. Tɔɔle kwora n chɔge ko wara-jei sem, se n daare n pworisi taane n chɔge Isarele tega kam. 3Ta de-ba we: ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a vaŋe a se-zɔɔ mo a le ko pwolo kom ne, se a ma-ko a go nɔn-ŋona de puseŋ-nyena de. 4Amo na wó yɔɔre a ke konto to ŋwaane, a se-zɔɔ kom wó zege tega-kuri seeni mo ko taa gwoni nɔɔna maama ko de se ko vo ko yi baŋa seeni. 5Nabiina maama laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. A nam na le a se-zɔɔ kom ko pwolo ne konto to, a daa bá pa ko jwoori ko zo da.’
6Konto ŋwaane, nabiinu, ta‑n vuvuna wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. Pa se nɔɔna bam na nmo wo na pɛ ye n tiini n vuvuni tei to. 7Ba nam ná bwei‑m se ba lɔre kolo ŋwaane n na vuvuni to, se n ta de-ba we, ‘Kwora kalo na beene se ka pa nɔɔna dedɛ nagwola te to ŋwaane mo amo vuvuna. Ba nadwoona wó taa mage daane mo de foone, ye ba vɔna de pare.’ Wonnu tento nam lage te seene te ke mo. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”
8 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ma yi amo we:
9“Nabiinu, pworisi n ta de-ba we: ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Nii-na se-zɔɔ!
Ba nam dwori-ko mo!
Ko maa tiini ko jege ni mo ye ko nyeena.
10Ko ni tiini ko dwori ko ti
se ko gwoni ko de tega ne.
Ko nam ta liligi jei maama ne mo
ne doa na pepele tei to!
Dé wó taa chaka Judah paare dem ŋwaane na?
Se-zɔɔ kom yiga nam tera paare maama wone!
11Amo kuri se-zɔɔ kom a tiŋi
se ba dwori-ko pa ko tiini ko jege ni mo.
Ba laam wó kwei-ko ba ke nɔn-goro wom jeŋa ne.
12Nabiinu, nam ta‑n keera ye n chwoosi n yaga,
lɛɛro telo na wó yi a nɔɔna bam to ŋwaane.
Isarele teo yiga tiina bam de wó na lɛɛro tem konto.
Ba maama wó te jara wone mo,
ba de a nɔɔna bam maama.
Konto ŋwaane, mage n takeiri wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane.
13Ko lage ko faŋe a nɔɔna bam mo ko nii. Judah paare dem ná ti, se-zɔɔ kom yiga na tere de wone to ŋwaane, bɛ mo daa wó ke? Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’
14Konto ŋwaane, nabiinu, pworisi taane
se n daare n mage n jea.
Pa se-zɔɔ kom zage kuni belei naa betɔ.
Kokuri to, ko ye se-zɔɔ kolo na goe to mo.
Ko nam wó kaare nɔɔna bam ko pu
se ko yɔɔre ko go-ba.
15Konto wó pa se ba vɔna pare,
ye ba dedɛ da ko ŋwaane ba to.
Amo pɛ se se-zɔɔ mo che ba teo kom ni maama.
Ko nam yɔɔre ko liligi jei maama ne
ne doa na pepele tei to mo,
ye ko ke siri se ko gwoni ko de tega ne.
16Se-zɔɔ, yɔɔre n ta‑n zage jazem seeni,
se n daare n pipiri jagwia seeni n zage n woli da.
Nmo ni dem ná jeeri mɛ seeni,
se n ta‑n gwoni nɔɔna n de tega ne.
17Amo de maa wó mage a jea daane
ye a bane de laam zuri.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.”
18 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ma yi amo we:
19“Nabiinu, bei bibeiri selei se se bere chwei selo Babilon teo pɛ se-zɔɔ kom na wó tɔge da ko ba to. Chwei sem nam wó nwoŋi teo kodoo ne mo se ba. Laam chwi daa mɛ seeni chwei sem na wó pwɛ to, se ka bere chwoŋa maama yiga na yɔɔre teo kolo seeni to. 20Ta pa se se-zɔɔ kom tɔge chwoŋa dedoa ko vo Amon tiina te-fɔrɔ Raba seeni, se chwoŋa kadwoŋi kam de vo Jerusalem teo na wo Judah laŋa kam ne to seeni. 21Kokuri to, Babilon teo pɛ wom lage o vo o zege chwei sem na pwɛ belei mɛ to, ye o daare o tɔge yi-nɛɛre baŋa se o lɔre chwoŋa kalo o na wó tɔge to. O maa zuzugi taŋa chena, o daare o bwei chwoŋa o teo jwona tei ne, ye o kwei chulu varem chwɛ o nii, se o lɔre o na wó ke tei to. 22O jazem ne mo o wó taa zei chene delo baŋa ne ba na popone Jerusalem teo yere to. O maa wó vo da o tiŋi da-kwollu telo ba na wó kwei ba mage teo kom ni-bworru tem ba bwori, se o laam pa o jar-keira bam ni se ba go ko nɔn-bia bam. Ba maa wó bage tiguri-kaasa, ye ba lɔ taara ba sale teo kom kabira kam teiŋa ne ba ja di ka yuu. 23Jerusalem tiina bam nam bá sɛ we Babilon teo pɛ yi-nɛɛre dem wó ji chega, ba na maŋe ba du duuri ba pa‑o to ŋwaane. Pɛ wom nam wó guli-ba ba tusim dem na ye tei to, ye o daare o ja-ba.
24Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ tage tento mo o we: ‘Abam pɛ se á tusim dem nwoŋi pwooni, ye á wɛleera yam maa yɔɔre ya nae jaja. Á kikia yam maama maa bere we á ba jege chega. Konto ŋwaane mo á dona wó ba ba ja abam de dam.
25Ko ta ná ye nmo Isarele tiina yiga tu wom, n lwarem kikia de n puseŋa gaale. Maŋa kam yi ka ti se n yɔɔre n na waarem. 26Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Dɔne n yuu gare-yi dem, de n paare yipuga kam n yuu ne. Ko daa bá taa ye ne ko ya na ye tei faŋa to. Nabwona jege se ba zaŋe de zula, se balo ya na jege paare ba di to ga ba paare. 27Chɔgem beena! Chɔgem beena! Teo kom paare dem wó ti! Konto nam bá ke, ye ko dae we wolo a na kuri se o waare teo kom to tua. A laam maa wó kwei-ko a ke o jeŋa ne.’
28Nabiinu, ko nam ná ye nmo, pworisi taane we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei Amon tiina bam de ba toro tem seeni to mo tento:
Nii-na se-zɔɔ!
Ba laam zei-ko mo se ba ma ba go nɔɔna.
Ba kwɛ-ko pa ko liligi mo ne doa na pepele tei to,
se ko yɔɔre ko taa chɔge nɔɔna.
29Á veera yalo na vei jara yam seeni to nam gane abam mo,
ye á yi-nɛɛre taana ye vwa yerane.
Se-zɔɔ kom wó ba abam baŋa
pa se puseŋ-nyena bam na maŋe de toone to te.
Dɛ dem banto na wó na chɔgem to yia,
pa se ba yɔɔre ba na waarem.
30Laam nam kwei se-zɔɔ kom
n jwoori n ke ko pwolo wone.
Jwoori n vo jei selo ba na naane‑m to.
Kokuri to, amo wó di n taane
teo kolo na ye n kugu jei to ne.
31A yɔɔre a lage a lwo a ban-lom dem mo n baŋa ne,
se n lɔre we a wo tiini ko fuli dede‑m.
A ta wó kwei‑m a ke nankɔ-nyena
balo na me de nɔn-gora kikia to jeŋa ne.
32Nmo wó ji ne da-kora
kalo ba na kwei ba de mini wone to.
N tete teo kom wone mo
n jana wó lwo tega ne.
N yere dem laam maa wó saare logo baŋa ne.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.’ ”

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Condemned
1Some time later, the Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins 3and tell them I am saying:
Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished! 4Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks, 5and people far and near will make fun of your misery.
6Your own leaders use their power to murder. 7 None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows. 8 You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day. 9Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things. 10 Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period 11or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister. 12 Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
13I will shake my fist in anger at your violent crimes. 14When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind. 15I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways. 16You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
Jerusalem Must Be Purified
17The Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified. 19So I am going to bring them together in Jerusalem. 20-21I will be like a metalworker who collects that metal from the furnace and melts it down. I will collect the Israelites and blow on them with my fiery anger. They will melt inside the city of Jerusalem 22like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger.
Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
23The Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious! 25Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.
26 The priests of Israel ignore my Law! Not only do they refuse to respect any of my sacred things, but they don't even teach the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary or between what is clean and what is unclean. They treat my Sabbath like any other day, and so my own people no longer honor me.
27Israel's officials are like ferocious wolves, ripping their victims apart. They make a dishonest living by injuring and killing people.
28And then the prophets in Israel cover up these sins by giving false visions. I have never spoken to them, but they lie and say they have a message from me. 29The people themselves cheat and rob; they abuse the poor and take advantage of foreigners.
30I looked for someone to defend the city and to protect it from my anger, as well as to stop me from destroying it. But I found no one. 31So in my fierce anger, I will punish the Israelites for what they have done, and they will know that I am furious. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jerusalem tiina bam na tusi tei to
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:
2“Ko ta ná ye nmo, nabiinu, n nam bá bore taane n vane teo konto nɔn-bia bam, de ba na swoi nɔn-gora kikia tei to na? Tole ba wo-zɔɔna kikia yam taane se ba taa yei ya ni ne. 3Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Jerusalem teo, n lage n ja chɔgem mo n ba n pa n tete. Kokuri, n nɔn-bia bam yeini ba go ba dwonna dedɛ n wone, ye ba ta mɔ jwona se ba zuli-ya, pa se ba biini ba tete. 4Abam Jerusalem tiina nɔn-gora kikia yam pɛ se á to de á bora. Á na mɔɔne jwona á pa á tete to de ma pa se á digiri á tete. Jerusalem, nmo waarem maŋa kam bwola. N bena yam lage ya ti mo. Amo lage a pa se dwi-gɛ tiina bam taa jege‑m ba yaale mo, se logo baŋa teene dem de taa twe‑m. 5Teene delo na bwola de nmo to, de delo na ye yiga yiga to maama wó taa mɔne‑m mo, nmo yere na chɔge ye n su de vuvuga to ŋwaane.
6Nii mo! Isarele teo yiga tu wolo maama na wo n wone to jege o dam dem o goe nɔɔna mo. 7Nmo nɔn-bia bam yɔɔre ba gwooni ba kwoa de ba niina mo. Ba ta maa jege veira, de botara, dedaane kadeina ba bɛɛsa. 8Ba bere ba ba nege wonnu telo na ye wose te pa amo to, ye ba daare ba jege amo siu da yam ba yaala. 9Nmo wone nɔɔna kare ba ba bebara se ba wane ba dwonna ba go mo. Nɔɔna badwonna de maa diini peero tem yuu ba di jwona wodiiru, ye badaara de swoi kabwoŋa kikia. 10Nmo wone baara badwonna de maa tigi de ba kwoa kaana, ye babam de fe mo se ba peini de kaana balo na jege ba chana zarem ba ke to. 11Nɔɔna ta wo n wone ye ba lage ba dwonna kaana se ba ke bwoŋa de-ba. Badaara maa jege ba bu-kaana ba laga, ye babam de yeini ba peini de ba nakwa ba na ye kwoa daane to. 12Nmo wone de, nɔɔna jwoŋi dim mo se ba wane ba go ba dwonna. Badwonna de maa jene wonnu ba pae ye ba dɔne nyɔɔre dedɛ jene dem baŋa ne. Ba laam maa tɔge kampina baŋa ne ba duni. Nmo nɔn-bia bam maa swei amo swia. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
13Amo wó dole abam jaguli-zane mo, abam na pini á ma‑á duni, ye á daare á go á dwonna á teo kom wone to ŋwaane. 14Amo nam ná tu a toŋe de abam ne ko na maŋe tei to, á ta wó ta‑á jege baare na? Á ta wó ta‑á dana maŋa kam konto ne na? Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto. A nam wó seene a ke kolo a na tage to. 15A lage a jage abam mo pa á vo yiga yiga se á ta‑á zoore logo baŋa teene dem jei maama wone. Konto to, a laam wó le á digiru tem maama a yage. 16Abam ná pɛ se dwi-gɛ tiina bam jege abam ba yaala, á laam wó ba á lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ”
17 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ta ma yi amo we:
18“Nabiinu, amo nii a nae Isarele dwi tiina bam we ba ye weeru mo. Ko nye de luru na kwɛ lu-nyenno mini wone se o le channa, de luuru tedwonna o daare lu-nyenno chekke to mo. Banto nam nye de weeru tem konto mo amo yiga ne. 19Konto ŋwaane Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Amo de wó la abam mo a ke daane Jerusalem teo kom wone, á laam na jigi weeru dwoŋi to ŋwaane. 20Ne luru na yeini o la lu-nyenno, de channa, de luuru tedwonna o de min-vogo wone se o fuli mini dem pa te nyeene tei to, konto mo amo de lage a ke abam. A maa wó tɔge a ban-lom dem ŋwaane a la abam a ke daane teo kom wone, ye a daare a waare abam, se á de nyeene, a wo na fuli dedɛ to ŋwaane. 21Chega ŋwaane to, a lage a la abam a ke daane teo kom wone mo, se a laam fuli a ban-lom dem a yage á yera ne. 22Ne lu-nyenno na nyeene tei min-vogo wone to, konto mo abam de lage á yaare teo kom wone. Abam laam maa wó lɔre we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo lwogi a ban-lom dem a yage á baŋa ne.’ ”
23 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ma yi amo we:
24“Nabiinu, ta de Isarele tiina tega kam we, ‘Nmo ye tega kalo doa na ba nena n baŋa ne se ka kwɛ to mo, a bane na zaŋe n baŋa ne to ŋwaane.’ 25Teo kom yiga tiina bam ke ni daane mo ne nywonnu na laare tei se te ja nɔna te kaare to. Ba maa kare ba goe nɔɔna, ye ba daare ba vere ba jejegero de ba lonne wonnu tem, pa se ba daare kadeina dedɛ ba yage teo kom wone. 26Teo kom kaanem tiina bam yiga tere amo nia yam wone. Ba maa yaale wonnu telo na ye wose te pae amo to. Ba nam ba pɔɔre wonnu telo na ye wose amo ŋwaane to, de telo na wora dɛ dɛ totoŋa yam ŋwaane to daane. Ba maa bere we wonnu telo na maŋe de Wɛ chullu tem to, de telo na jege digiru chullu tem seeni to maama ye bedwe mo. Ko ta ná ye amo siu da yam, ba yiga tere ya wone. Ba na ke tei konto to maa pae se nɔɔna jege amo yere dem ba yaala. 27Teo kom nakwa bam nye de wiira mo na nɛ vara se ba zi ba kaare to. Ba maa ke nɔɔna zonne ye ba jege-ba ba goe se ba tete ma ba duni. 28Teo kom sampwori sem de ye ja chɔge. Ba yɔɔre ba peeri nɔɔna bam kikia mo, de ba veera yam na gane nɔɔna, ye ba yi-nɛɛre taana ye vwa tei to. Ba maa tɛ ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ tage o we tento mo,’ ye Baŋa Wɛ nam bere o wo puri o ni de-ba de. 29Teo kom nɔɔna bam yɔɔre ba me de kampina mo, ye ba ta swoi se ba taa vere nɔɔna. Ba maa yɔɔre ba jege yiniga tiina de nabwona ba bɛɛsa. Ba ta maa jege veira de ba yaara, ye ba vane banto bora taane dim baŋa ne.
30A nam beeri se a na nɔɔno mo ba wone, se kotu fɔge o lɔ teo kom kabira kam o zege. Kotu ya wó zege o che se lulua kalo na tigi amo de teo kom laŋa ne to kwoni, se a daa yé chɔge teo kom. A ma beeri a ga. 31Konto ŋwaane mo a nam lage a yɔɔre a lwo a ban-lom dem ba baŋa ne, se a zwɛ-ba kula, a wo na tiini ko fuli de-ba to ŋwaane. A maa wó jwoori a ŋwe ba keim-lwanno tem maama jene. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_text:
Two Sinful Sisters
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, listen to this story about two sisters. 3While they were young and living in Egypt, they became prostitutes. 4The older one was named Oholah, which stands for Samaria; the younger one was Oholibah, which stands for Jerusalem. They became my wives and gave birth to my children.
5Even though Oholah was my wife, she continued to be a prostitute and chased after Assyrian lovers. 6She offered herself to soldiers in purple uniforms: handsome, high-ranking officers and cavalry troops. 7She had sex with all the important Assyrian officials and even worshiped their disgusting idols. 8Once she started doing these things in Egypt, she never stopped. Men slept with her, and she was always ready for sex.
9So I gave Oholah to the Assyrian lovers she wanted so badly. 10They ripped off her clothes, then captured her children and killed her. Women everywhere talked about what had happened to Oholah.
11Oholibah saw all this, but she was more sinful and wanted sex more than her sister Oholah ever did. 12Oholibah also chased after good-looking Assyrian officers, uniformed soldiers, and cavalry troops. 13Just like her sister, she did vulgar things.
14But Oholibah behaved worse than her sister. Oholibah saw images of Babylonian men carved into walls and painted red. 15They had belts around their waists and large turbans on their heads, and they reminded her of Babylonian cavalry officers. 16As soon as she looked at them, she wanted to have sex with them. And so, she sent messengers to bring them to her. 17Men from Babylonia came and had sex with her so many times that she got disgusted with them. 18She let everyone see her naked body and didn't care if they knew she was a prostitute. That's why I turned my back on her, just as I had done with her older sister.
19Oholibah didn't stop there, but became even more immoral and acted as she had back in Egypt. 20She eagerly wanted to go to bed with Egyptian men, who were famous for their sexual powers. 21And she longed for the days when she was a young prostitute, when men enjoyed caressing her body.
The Lord Will Punish Oholibah
22The Lord God said:
Oholibah, though you no longer want to be around your lovers, they will surround you like enemies, when I turn them against you. 23I will gather all the handsome young officials and the high-ranking cavalry officers from Babylonia and Assyria, as well as from the Chaldean tribes of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa. 24Their large armies will come from the north with chariots and wagons carrying weapons. They will wear shields and helmets and will surround you, and I will let them judge and sentence you according to their own laws. 25I am angry with you, so I will let them be very cruel. They will cut off your nose and ears; they will kill your children and burn alive anyone in your family who survives. 26Your clothes and jewelry will be torn off. 27I will stop your wickedness and the prostitution you started back in Egypt. You will never want to think about those days again.
28I, the Lord God, am ready to hand you over to those hateful enemies that you find so disgusting. 29They will cruelly take away everything you have worked for and strip you naked. Then everyone will see you for the prostitute you really are. Your own vulgar sins 30have led to this. You were the one determined to have sex with men from other nations and to worship their idols. 31You have turned out no better than your older sister, and now you must drink from the cup filled with my anger.
32I, the Lord God, gave your sister a large, deep cup filled with my anger. And when you drink from that cup, you will be mocked and insulted. 33You will end up drunk and devastated, because that cup is filled with horror and ruin. 34But you must drink every drop! Then smash the cup and chew on its broken pieces. Use them to cut your breasts in sorrow. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
35You have completely rejected me, and so I promise that you will be punished for the disgusting things you did as a prostitute.
The Two Sisters Are Condemned
36The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, it's time for you to tell Oholah and Oholibah that they are guilty. Remind them of their evil ways! 37They have been unfaithful by worshiping idols, and they have committed murder by sacrificing my own children as offerings to idols. 38-39They came into my temple that same day, and that made it unfit as a place to worship me. They have even stopped respecting the Sabbath.
40They sent messengers to attract men from far away. When those men arrived, the two sisters bathed themselves and put on eye shadow and jewelry. 41They sat on a fancy couch, and in front of them was a table for the olive oil and incense that had belonged to me. 42Their room was always filled with a noisy crowd of drunkards brought in from the desert. These men gave the women bracelets and beautiful crowns, 43and I noticed that the men were eager to have sex with these women, though they were exhausted from being prostitutes. 44In fact, the men had sex over and over with Oholah and Oholibah, the two sinful sisters. 45But honest judges will someday accuse those two of murder and of being unfaithful, because they are certainly guilty.
46So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters:
I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you. 47They will stone you to death and cut you to pieces; they will kill your children and burn down your houses. 48I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have. 49You will be punished for becoming prostitutes and for worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_text:
Kaana balei memaŋe
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, kaana balei déem mo wora, ba na ye nu dedoa. 3Ba ta na ye bukwa-donno ye ba zoore Ejipti teo wone to mo ba jigi ka-bworru. Dáane mo baara déem jege ba yela ba teiŋa, ye ba ta jege ba pwoa yam seeni ba peera. 4Zembaaro wom yere mo ye Ohola. O nyaane wom yere maa ye Oholiba. Ba ma ji amo kaana, ye ba lo bakeiri de bukwa ba pa-ne. Ohola mo ye Samaria teo. Oholiba maa ye Jerusalem teo kom.
5Ohola ya ta na wo amo tei ne to mo o zo kabwoŋa kikia wone. O ma kare o lage bɔɔla, ne o fera na zo-ba tei to. Asiria tiina bam mo konto. Ba badwonna maa ye jar-keira 6ye ba zo gwaaro telo nyenyego na ye nazwon-pupwiu to. Ba badaara nam ye dedɛɛra, de yiga tiina, de balo na diini sisein-nɔɔna to mo. Ba maama maa ye nɔn-donno telo na jege lam to. 7O ma yɔɔre o kwei o tete o pa Asiria teo nɔn-yum tem maama kabworim ŋwaane. O ta ma chɔge o tete de o na zuli balo maama fera na wo o wone to jwona yam. 8O nam wo sɛ se o yage o kabworim kikia yam, ne o na maŋe o ke tei Ejipti ne ye o ta ye bukɔ-pwola to. Maŋa kam konto ne baara déem taane o pwoa ye ba daare ba toŋe ba fera na lage tei to mo ded-o. 9Amo nam yɔɔre a yage‑o mo a pa o bɔɔla Asiria tiina bam. Kokuri to, o fera maŋe ya wo ba wone. 10Ba de ma lɔɔre o yera zela ba daare‑o ba zege bwori. Ba ta kale o bakeiri de o bukwa bam mo ba ja ba viiri, ye ba daare ba kwei se-zɔɔ ba ma ba go o tete. Kaana laam maa jege o yera taane ba ŋɔɔna, o na nɛ waarem delo to ŋwaane.
11O nyaane Oholiba déem nɛ tento maama, ye wonto nam ta ke o chɔge se ko dwoni o zembaaro wom kabworim totoŋa, o na ware o fera yam o ja to ŋwaane. 12O ma yɔɔre o lage Asiria tiina bam, ba na ye dedɛɛra, de yiga tiina, de jar-keira na zo gare-laaro to, de balo na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne to. Ba maama maa ye nɔn-donno telo na jege lam to. 13A ma maane we wonto de ke ne o zembaaro wom ya na ke tei to mo, pa se o biini o tete.
14Ko nam ná ye Oholiba, wonto ke kabworim se ko dwoni o zembaaro wom kikia yam. O déem nɛ ba na gɔgere Babilon tiina nyenyero telo ba yage kabira yera ne pa te lana nason-sonno tei to. 15Ba maa jege vovwe selo na bage ba teiŋa ne to, dedaane yuu gare-yia yalo na vɔge ba yuni ne to. Nyenyero tem maama maa yɔɔre te nye de Babilon teo dedɛɛra balo na nwoŋi Chaladea to. 16O na bobo o na ba nyenyero tem konto to, mo o fera zo ba wone, pa o toŋe nɔɔna ba teo kom ne se ba bwoŋi-ba ba pa‑o. 17Babilon tiina bam de ma ba o tei ba peini ded‑o. Ba ma tiini ba chɔge‑o de ba sare-peiga kikia, pa se o yera ba ya chɛ ye o ma o kwaga o ya-ba. 18O yɔɔre o ja o kabworim kikia yam o nwoŋi pwooni mo pa nɔɔna maama na o kuri. A laam ma ma a kwaga a ya‑o, ne a déem na yage o zembaaro tei to. 19De ko de, o ta wo sɛ se o yage o tolo kom. O nam guli o ya na ye nɔn-doŋo Ejipti teo ne ye o tɔge kabworim kikia yalo to gula mo, pa se o tiini o ke konto dwoŋi se ko gaale. 20O ta yɔɔre o swoi se o taa tigi de o bɔɔla bam mo, ba na dana de sare-peiga ne bonɛ de sisein-nɔɔna na ye tei to ŋwaane. 21Oholiba, nmo na guli n na ke wo-zɔɔna yalo n nɔn-donne maŋa ne ye Ejipti baara bam peeri n pwoa ye ba teiŋi n yela to, n ta lage se n ta‑n ye konto mo.
22Konto ŋwaane Oholiba, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Ko ná ye n bɔɔla balo n na mɛ n kwaga n ya-ba to, a lage a pa ba zaŋe jei maama ne ba ke chichuŋu de nmo mo. 23A nam wó la nɔn-donno telo na jege lam ye ba nwoŋi Babilon, de Chaladea, de Pekoda, de Soa, de Koa to, ko ta woli de Asiria tiina bam maama a ke daane. Ba ye ba teo dedɛɛra, de ba yiga tiina, de jar-keira, de babɛ, ye ba maama dɔge sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne mo. 24Ba maa wó ba de jar-keira kɔgɔ kamunu de ba torokooro ba jeeri‑m de jara, ye ba zei jara zela dwi dwi. Ba wó taa jege jara nantane ba ma ba kwoli ba tete, ye ba pu jara yu-gwonnu mo. Ba maa wó ba ba gilimi nmo ba ke tetare ne ye ba daare ba waare‑m. Amo mo wó pa-ba chwoŋa se ba di n taane, ye ba daare ba waare‑m se ko tɔge de banto wadɛ sem. 25A lage a da a ban-lom dem baŋa ne mo a pa se ba seene ba yia ba waare‑m. Ba maa wó dɔɔre n momwɛ de n zwa ba yage. Balo ta na wó daare n wone to wó te jara wone. Ko ta ná ye n bia bam de, ba lage ba ja-ba mo, ye ba daare ba zwɛ n nɔn-bia balo na daare to mini wone. 26Ba ta wó lɔɔre n gwaaro tem maama, de n wo-nyenno zela yam. 27Amo nam wó pa se wo-zɔɔna de kabworim kikia yalo nmo déem na bobo n ke Ejipti ne to ti. Nmo daa bá‑n ta‑n jege kikia yanto dwoŋi fera, naa n guli Ejipti teo gula kɔtaa!
28Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Oholiba, a lage a kwei‑m a ke balo n na chuli to jeŋa ne mo. Ko ye banto mo n déem mɛ n kwaga n ya-ba. 29Ba de wó kwei sebaŋa mo ba toŋe se ko yi abam lanyerane. Ba ta wó vere wonnu telo n na yaare n na to ba ja viiri. Ba maa wó kɛ ba daare‑m, se n ta‑n zege de kuri-nɔrɔ. N kabworim kikia yam wó taa nae jaja pa se chaveera yɔɔre ya ja‑m. Ko ye n wo-zɔɔna de n tolo kikia yam mo 30pɛ se daanem dento ba n baŋa, n na kare n lage dwi-gɛ tiina bam ye n biini n tete ba jwona yam kaanem baŋa ne to ŋwaane. 31Nmo yɔɔre n kwei n zembaaro totoŋ-naga kam mo. Konto ŋwaane, amo de wó kwei na-zoŋa kalo a na pɛ‑o pa o nyɔ ka wo cham to mo a pa‑m se n de nyɔ.
32Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento:
Nmo de lage n nyɔ n zembaaro wom na-zoŋa kam wone mo.
Ka wo nam tiini ko luuna.
Nɔɔna wó taa jege‑m ba mɔna ye ba ta yaale‑m,
na-zoŋa kam konto na jege n yera wonnu dedɛ ka wone to ŋwaane.
33Nmo wó nyɔ ka wo wonnu tem n bugi
ye n ta‑n jei de wo-chechɔgɔ.
Ka nam ye na-zoŋa kalo na wó ja chɔgem de lɛɛro ka ba
ye n zembaaro Samaria de nyɔ ka wone to mo.
34Nmo nam wó nyɔ ka wo wonnu tem mo n ti maama nyɔ!
Nmo laam ma‑n wó feiri-ka tega ne n lɔ muga-muga,
ye n daare n bɛ bɛ n yela wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane.
Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.
35Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Nmo na swei amo swia ye n ta-ne n yage kwaga kwaga to, nmo nam jege se n na waarem mo se ko maŋe de n wo-zɔɔna de n tolo kikia yam.”
36 Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta de amo o we:
“Nabiinu, nmo nam bá bore taane n vane Ohola de Oholiba na? Tole ba totoŋ-vɛɛsa yam taane se ba taa yei ya ni ne. 37Kokuri to, ba tiini ba ke tolo dedɛ, ye ba nɔn-gora kikia de kɛ jeŋa. Ba nwoŋi amo kwaga ne ye ba daare ba zuli ba jwona yam. Ba maŋe ba kwei bia balo amo de-ba na loge daane to mo ba ke kaanem ba pa ba jwona yam konto. 38De ko de, ba ta ke tento mo ba ma chɔge amo yiga: Ba yɔɔre ba jege a wara-jei sem ba biini mo, ye ba yaale a siu da yam. 39Dɛ delo wone ba na kwei ba bia bam ba ke kaanem ba pa ba jwona yam to, mo ba zo amo wara-jei sem wone pa se ba chɔge se chullu tem. Ba seene ba ke konto dwoŋi mo amo tete diga kam wone.
40Ba maa yeini ba toŋe se ba vo yiga yiga ba bwoŋi nɔɔna se ba ba. Nɔɔna bam konto maa ná nwoŋi sa-teene wone ba yi, nmo Oholiba wó swɛ n yera mo, n daare n kwɛ n yibia ye n fɔge n yera de wo-nyenno dwi dwi. 41Nmo laam ma‑n wó vo n jeini jaŋgɔŋɔ kolo na jege nenɔŋa to baŋa ne, ye n pa ba kwei yituŋu ba zege n yiga ne. N ma‑n wó kwei talwoŋ-ywoŋa, de nuga kalo ya na ye amo zula ŋwaane to n tiŋi ko baŋa ne.
42Nɔn-kɔgɔ kolo na tiini ba di ywoni to mo gilimi‑o ba bage sɔɔ ba yaga. Ba nam nwoŋi kagoa kam seeni mo ba ba. Nɔɔna bam maa ye dwia yadwonna, ko woli de sa-nyɔra balo ba na jaane ba nwoŋi kagoa wone to. Nɔɔna bam konto ma kwei jeŋa bɛ ba ke kaana balei bam je ne, ye ba daare ba kwei nenɔŋa yipwi ba pu ba yuni ne. 43A laam ma ta kaane wolo yera na chɛ de kabwoŋa kikia to yera taane a we, ‘Ba ta wó taa tigi ded‑o mo ne ba na ke tei de ka-tole to.’ 44Ba ma seene ba ke sare-peiga ded‑o, ne nɔɔna na tigi de ka-bworru tei to. Ba ke totoŋ-vɛɛsa konto dwoŋi mo de Ohola dedaane Oholiba, ba na ye ka-tole to ŋwaane. 45Nɔn-ŋona nam wó di banto taane ba vane-ba, pa se ba na waarem delo na maŋe de ba kabworim de ba nɔn-gora kikia to mo, ba na seene ba ye ka-tole ye nɔn-gora jana wo ba yuni ne to ŋwaane.
46Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Pa se jar-keira kɔgɔ ba ba ke chichuŋu de-ba, pa se lɛɛro de foone yi-ba. 47Kɔ-fɔrɔ kom konto wó dole-ba de kandwa mo, ye ba daare ba kwei ba se-zɔɔro ba gwoni-ba ba de tega ne. Ba ta wó go ba bu-baara de ba bukwa, ye ba daare ba zwɛ ba sam dem.
48Amo wó tɔge konto baŋa ne mo a pa se wo-zɔɔna kikia yanto dwoŋi ti tega kam jei maama ne. Kaana bam maama wó na ko na ke banto tei to pa se ba daa bá lwoni ba kikia yam. 49Ko nam ná ye abam, Ohola de Oholiba, á wó yaare mo á kabworim kikia yam á na ke to ŋwaane. Á wɛleera yam á na ke de á na kaane jwona tei to jene mo wó taa wo abam yuu ne. Abam laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_text:
A Cooking Pot
1Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem. 3Then tell my rebellious people:
“Pour water in a cooking pot
and set it over a fire.
* 4Throw in the legs and shoulders
of your finest sheep
and put in the juicy bones.
5Pile wood underneath the pot,
and let the meat and bones
boil until they are done.”
6These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it. 7The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground. 8But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
9I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood, 10so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch. 11Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust. 12I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
13Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it. 14That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Ezekiel's Wife Dies
15The Lord said, 16“Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry. 17Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
18One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me, 19and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
20I answered:
The Lord God says 21he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed. 22Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat. 23You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
24I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
25The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well. 26On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened. 27Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Kambi-zaŋa memaŋe
1Bena nogo bene dem chane fuga chana kam da fuga dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora tu ka yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, popone dɛ dento n tiŋi tɔnɔ wone, kokuri, ko ye dɛ dem konto ne nɔɔ mo Babilon teo pɛ tu o kaare Jerusalem teo kom o pu. 3Véi zwabani-nyena banto tei n maŋe memaŋe de-ba we: ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Kwei kambia n teini mini ne,
se n daare n lwo na ka wone.
4-5Nam nii n vara bam wone n kuri vare-ŋom.
Kwei ko nɔn-dɛ sem maama n ke kambia kam wone,
ko chwei dem de ko vɔŋɔ kom mo konto.
Ta kuri ko kwi-laaro tem n ke da,
n su kambia kam ni maama.
Laam tigisi da-dwa dedɛ ka kuri ne,
n pa se na bam chore lanyerane
ye kwi sem de saŋe se be.
6Kokuri to, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Lɛɛro wo teo konto na su de nɔn-gora to yuu ne! Ko yɔɔre ko nye de kambi-dwoŋa mo na tiini ka digiri ye ka ba zare ka gɔe to. Nam ta le ka wo nɔna yam dedoa dedoa ye á wo kuri ya wone á daare. 7Teo kom nɔn-bia bam kare ba go nɔɔna pa se ba jana bam taare tega kam maama mo. Ba ma lwo jana bam pelwaaro baŋa ne jaja, ye ko dae tega ne mɛ fwogo na wó kwoli-ba to. 8Amo de nam yage jana bam pa ba tigi pelwaaro tem baŋa ne konto mo, se nɔn-gora bam daa yé seigi-ba. Konto wó pa se a bane zaŋe ye a jwoori a ŋwe jana bam jene ba yuu ne.
9Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Lɛɛro wo teo konto na su de nɔn-gora to yuu ne! Amo tete mo wó tigisi da-dwa a dogele da-baŋa ne. 10Konto ŋwaane, dogele dɛ sem se se di baŋa, se n daare n dwei mini se kuri ne. Saŋe nɔna yam se ya be lanyerane, se n woli diira ya wone. Nam ta pa se kwi sem fuli. 11Laam kwei kambi-kora kam n saŋe min-chala yam baŋa ne se n pa ka tiini ka lone ye ka channa kam nyeene. Konto mo wó pa se digiru telo na wo ka yera ne to maama nyeene te ti, se mini dem zwɛ wonnu telo ya na pɛ ka chɔge to pa te jei. 12Amo yera nam chɛ de a na kwaane se a kwɛ-ka tei to mo. Digiru telo na daga ka wone to ta wo jei. Dole-ka n yage mini dem wone, de ka digiru tem maama!
13Abam nam biini á tete de á wo-zɔɔna kikia yam mo. Amo yɔɔre a kwɛ abam a ga mo. Á wo sɛ se a le á digiru tem. Abam nam daa bá wane á kwɛ á digiru tem, ko ná dae we amo lwogi a ban-lom dem á baŋa ne mo a ti pa se a wo laam zuri.
14Amo Baŋa Wɛ wom mo tage konto maama. Maŋa kam yi se a ke tei a na tage to. A bá yiri a ni dem konto. A bá leiri a boboŋa, ye a ta bá duri á yibwona. Amo nam lage a waare abam mo se ko maŋe de á totoŋa yam na ye tei to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ”
Ezekeli kaane wom na tege tei to
15 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ma yi amo we:
16“Nabiinu, amo lage a pɔpɔ a ke keim mo na wó zwɛ‑m lanyerane. A wó jwoŋi wolo na tiini o tigi n bochare ne to a daare‑m. De ko de, yé keeri o ŋwaane. Yé kane yi-na naa n pa n yiga nyɔne. 17N jege chwoŋa se n suuri fenfee n wone. Nam yé pa n kwora zaŋe. Yé keeri o lua kam. Kwei n yuu vovoa n ba n yuu ne, se n daare n zo n natera yam. Yé kwoli n yibia ne balo na keeri ba twa na ke tei to, naa se n di wodiu kolo lua tiina na jege ba di to.”
18Dɛ dem konto tetete mo a ŋɔɔne de nɔɔna bam. Ko na yi dedaan-ni maŋa to, mo a kaane wom tega. Tega na poore to, amo de ma ke ne Wɛ na pɛ-ne ni se a ke tei to. 19Nɔɔna bam ma bwei-ne ba we, “N kaane na tega ye n ke konto dwoŋi to, n bá pa dé lɔre ko kuri na ye tei ko pa debam to mo na?”
20Amo de ma ta de-ba a we, “Baŋa Wɛ kwora mo tu ka yi amo we: 21Ta de Isarele dwi tiina bam we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a pa a tete wara-jei sem ji wo-zɔɔne mo. Ko ye kolo á na teere ko baŋa ne to mo. Abam ba nii-ko á sui, ye ko ye jeiga kalo á bochara na tigi da to mo. Abam bia balo á nam na daare kwaga ne to de lage ba te jara wone mo. 22Konto maama nam ná kea, abam de wó ke ne amo na ke tei to mo. Abam bá kwoli á yibia ne balo na keeri ba twa na ke tei to, naa á di wodiu kolo lua tiina na jege ba di to. 23Abam wó yage á yuu vovwe mo se se ba á yuni ne, ye á daare á yage á natera se ya taa wo á nɛ ne. Á bá keeri keim dem ŋwaane. Á nam bá pa á yiga nyɔne de. Abam wó yɔɔre á ta‑á bugi á jei mo á wɛleera yam ŋwaane, ye á daare á suuri á bere daane. 24Ezekeli nam ye memaŋe mo o pa abam se á lɔre ko na wó taa ye tei to á yera ne. Abam de wó ke tei wonto na ke to mo. Konto maama ná yi abam, á wó lɔre we amo mo ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.’
25Ko ta ná ye nmo, nabiinu, dɛ dem wó yi a na wó chɔge dam jei selo ba na teere ko baŋa ne to. Ko maa ye woŋo kolo ba na di ywoni ko ŋwaane ye ba swoi se ba taa nii-ko ba ba sui to mo. Ba bochara maa tigi ko baŋa ne. A ta wó ja ba bia bam mo a woli da a ja a kɛ. 26Dɛ dem konto ne mo nɔɔno wó duri o lu jara wone o ja kwora o ba o pa‑m se n lɔre kolo na ke to. 27Maŋa kam konto ne mo chwoŋa wó pore ka pa‑m se n ni puri se n ŋɔɔne ded‑o. Nmo daa bá ta‑n ye chemm. Konto baŋa ne mo nmo lage n ji memaŋe n pa-ba, se ba de wane ba lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_text:
Judgment on Ammon
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon 3and tell them:
You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners. 4Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk. 5Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
6You hated Israel so much that you clapped and shouted and celebrated. 7And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
Judgment on Moab
8 The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation. 9So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim. 10The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever, 11Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.”
Judgment on Edom
12 The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah. 13So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan. 14I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.”
Judgment on Philistia
15 The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them. 16Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast. 17In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Amon teo taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, pipiri n yibia se ka jeeri Amon tiina bam se n pworisi taane n chɔge-ba. 3Ta de-ba we, ‘Cheigi-na Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ taane dem. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam ya yɔɔre á chake mo de ba na jaane amo wara-jei sem ba chɔge to. Ba na wane Isarele tega kam ba chɔge, ye ba daare ba kale Judah dwi tiina bam ba ja vo sa-teo yiga yiga to, mo á déem jege a nɔɔna bam á mɔna. 4Konto ŋwaane, ta‑á yei-na we a lage a ja abam a ke dwia yalo na zoore wɛ-puli seeni to jeŋa ne mo. Ba wó ba ba chwi ba vwoa se ba taa zoore abam tetare ne. Ba maa wó jwoŋi á tio-bia bam ba di, ye ba ta vere á nayela de ba nyɔ ba daare abam. 5Amo ta wó pa se Raba pipiri ko ji mɛ kona na vei ya di gaao to, se Amon de taa ye jei selo ba na kɔne pei da to. Abam laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom. 6Kokuri, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ tage tento mo o we: Abam mage á jea de wopwolo, ye á tɔ sankena, á ma‑á daare á chake de wo-gworo kolo na yi Isarele teo kom to. 7Mo kokuri nam lɔre-na we amo de lage a twi a jeŋa mo á baŋa ne, se a kwei abam a ke dwia yadwonna jeŋa ne se ba vere á wonnu tem. Amo lage a le abam mo dwi-gɛ tiina bam wone, se a daare a saare abam se á daa yé gwaane logo baŋa teene dem wone. A ná yɔɔre a gwoni abam a de tega ne konto dwoŋi, mo á wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ”
Moaba teo taane
8“Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Moaba teo de Seyira teo déem tage ba we, ‘Judah dwi tiina bam de laam yɔɔre ba nye de dwia yadwonna yam mo.’ 9Konto ŋwaane amo de wó pa se nɔɔna ke chichuŋu de Moaba teene delo na chege ba siseini dem to. Ko nam ye ba teene delo na jege nenɔŋa to, Bɛte-Jesimofa, de Baal-Meon, de Kiriafayim mo konto. 10A nam lage a kwei Moaba teo kom de Amon tiina bam mo a ke dwia yalo na zoore wɛ-puli seeni to jeŋa ne se ba taa tei. Konto to, Amon tiina yere dem wó saare logo baŋa teene dem wone. 11A laam maa wó waare Moaba tiina bam se ba lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.”
Edom teo taane
12“Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Edom tiina bam sage chwoŋa de ba na yiri jene Judah dwi tiina bam baŋa ne to. Tusim dem konto jene yɔɔre de wo ba yuu ne mo. 13Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo nam wó twi a jeŋa mo Edom teo baŋa ne, se a go ko nɔn-bia de ko vara maama. A maa wó pa ko ji di-dwonnu yerane. Ko na wó zege Teman ne se ko yi Dedan to, se-zɔɔro mo wó ti ba maama. 14A maa wó tɔge a tete nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa a yiri jene Edom teo kom baŋa ne. A wó pa-ba chwoŋa se ba waare Edom tiina bam ne a ban-lom dem na lage se ba ke tei to. Konto baŋa ne mo ba wó lɔre a ban-zɔŋɔ kom na ye tei to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.”
Filisi teo taane
15“Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Filisi tiina bam jege nabaara sebaŋa mo ba di de Judah tiina bam. Ba ma kwaane se ba yiri jene ba baŋa ne kuni dedɛ, ba daare ba chɔge-ba. Ba maa wo duri ba ŋwaŋa de fenfee de. 16Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a twi a jeŋa mo Filisi tiina bam baŋa ne. A maa wó pa se Cherete tiina bam dwi jei tega baŋa ne, ye a daare a chɔge Filisi tiina balo ta na daare ye ba zoore naneo kom ni ne to. 17Amo wó tɔge a ban-lom dem ŋwaane a yiri jene ba baŋa ne. A maa ná yiri jene ba baŋa ne ye a waare-ba a ti, ba de wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_text:
Judgment on the City of Tyre
1 Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing,
“Jerusalem has fallen!
It used to be powerful,
a center of trade.
Now the city is shattered,
and we will take its place.”
3Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore. 4They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock, 5where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed 6and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
7King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops. 8First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you. 9He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers. 10He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city. 11His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground. 12The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea. 13 You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps, 14because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
15The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death. 16 The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear 17and sing this funeral song:
“The great city beside the sea
is destroyed!
Its people once ruled the coast
and terrified everyone there.
18But now Tyre is in ruins,
and the people on the coast
stare at it in horror
and tremble in fear.”
