19I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you 20and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people. 21 You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Tura teo taane
1Bena fuga-dedoa bene dem chana kam boboa dɛ dem wone, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, Tura tiina bam ya yɔɔre ba chake mo de Jerusalem totoore dem ye ba we, ‘Jerusalem teo laam to ywoo! Ko laam nam jigi di-dwonnu mo ko tiga. Chwoŋa laam pore se dé tɔge da dé ke pipiu de teene dedwonna. Debam mo wó leiri ba yuu ne dé duni.’ 3Konto ŋwaane Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam Tura teo tiina bam, amo dwoni de abam mo. A lage a pa dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ mo ba ba ke chichuŋu de abam, ne naneo na-ŋone sem na zaŋe wɛɛne tei to. 4Banto nam lage ba vaare teo kom kabiri de ko dalem jei sem mo ba de tega ne. A ta wó pa ba chwooli ko teero tem maama ba ja jei, se kolo yerane na wó daare da to taa ye peo ko tiga. 5Tura teo wó taa zege naneo kom tetare ne mo, se ywon-jara yeini ba jare ba ŋwe da. Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto. Dwia yadwonna tiina mo wó ba ba vere ba wonnu. 6Ba maa wó yɔɔre ba go Tura tiina balo na zoore naneo ni te-kampare sem ne to. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.
7Kokuri, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a pa Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza mo zege baŋa seeni o ba o jeeri Tura teo kom de jara. Wonto ye pa-faro mo pwa maama wone. O maa jege sisein-nɔɔna de jara torokooro dedɛ. O ta jege balo na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne to, de jar-keira kɔ-fɔrɔ na daga to. 8O lage o yɔɔre o chɔge á teene delo maama na wo naneo ni te-kampare sem ne to mo jara-keim baŋa ne. O jar-keira bam maa wó kaare á teo kamunu kom ba pu. Ba wó lɔ taara ye ba dogele teero ba sale á kabira kam teiŋa ne ba ja di ka yuu, ye ba daare ba geene jara-keim nantane ba ma jeeri abam de jara. 9O ta wó pa ba kwei da-kwollu ba ma mage á kabiri sem ba bwori, ye ba daare ba ma ba luuru ba bwori á dalem jei sem ba de tega ne. 10O sisein-nɔɔna bam fwogo wó pe á teo kom, se na daga to ŋwaane. O sisei sem ná guri tega, ye o jara torokooro tem de duri te kɛa, á teo kom kabiri wó taa ziziŋi mo. Ba maa wó tɔge á teo kom manchwo-peena yam ba zo ko wo, ne nɔɔna na mage teo kabira ba yare se ba zo tei to. 11Ba sisein-nɔɔna napɔɔna wó taa dɔna á teo kom chwei sem maama ne mo. Ba maa wó taa jege ba se-zɔɔro ba yɔɔre ba goe nɔɔna. Ywoa yalo á na chwi ye ya dana to maa wó to tega ne buru-tu-tu. 12Jar-keira bam wó vere á jejegero tem, de á pipiu zela maama mo. Ba maa wó yigi á kabiri sem ba de tega ne, ye ba daare ba chɔge á sɔ-ŋonno tem. Ko ná ye á sam dem kandwa yam, de dɛ sem, dedaane teero telo na daare to, ba wó dole tento maama ba yage naneo kom wone mo. 13Amo wó che se á lei sem sɔɔ daa yé taa zaŋa. Abam nam daa bá ta‑á tae á kwanno tem se te kwori zo nɔɔna zwa. 14Amo nam lage a pa se á teo kom ji peo kolo ywon-jara na wó yeini ba jare ba ŋwe da to mo. Ba daa bá jwoori ba lɔ teo kom ba zege. Kokuri, amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.
15Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage taane delo o bere Tura teo to mo tento: Teene delo maama na wo naneo kom ni ne to ná nigi nmo na to tega ne buri-buri ye n nɔn-bia bam nɛ zonne pa ba vuvuna tei to, ba yera bá taa sae mo na? 16Naneo ni teene dem pwa laam wó zaŋe ba daare ba paare yitunnu ye ba le ba paare nenɔŋa gwaaro, ba daare ba lɔɔre ba gare-nyenno tem. Foone wó yɔɔre de ja-ba pa ba jeini tega ne, ye ba yera sɔɔre de kolo na yi á teo kom to. 17Ba laam maa wó mɔ luseim leiŋa nmo ŋwaane ba ta we:
‘Nmo ye teo kolo yere ya na zaŋe
ye n nɔn-bia bam nwoŋi naneero tem baŋa ne to.
Nmo laam nam yɔɔre n chɔge mo n tiga!
Nmo de n nɔn-bia bam déem jege dam mo
naneero tem maama wone,
pa se balo maama na zoore naneo kom ni ne to
tiini ba kɔre foone abam ŋwaane.
18Dɛ dem nmo nam na lage n to konto to,
naneo ni teene dem maama yera wó sɔɔre mo,
de nmo dam dem na ti tei to.’
19Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Amo ná pɛ se n ji di-dwonnu yerane, ne teo kolo nɔɔna daa na ba zoore ko wone to, ye a ta ná pɛ se naneo kom wo na-fwaaro tem pɛɛle te ba te kwoli‑m, 20a laam wó pa se nmo de n nɔn-bia bam tu á zo churu, pa se á woli de faŋa faŋa nɔɔna balo na vei da to. Nmo laam wó ta‑n zoore tega kuri ne mɛ faŋa faŋa di-dwonnu na maŋe te tigi to. Ko laam maa wó pa se n maŋe dáane taa wuu, ye n daa bá‑n ta‑n ye teo kolo nɔn-ŋwena na zoore ko wone to. 21Amo wó pa se lɛɛro ba n baŋa ye n laam guri. Nɔɔna wó beeri n jei ye ba daa bá na‑m. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Tyre
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre, 3the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me:
Tyre, you brag about
your perfect beauty,
4and your control of the sea.
You are a ship
built to perfection.
5Builders used cypress trees
from Mount Hermon
to make your planks
and a cedar tree from Lebanon
for your tall mast.
6Oak trees from Bashan
were shaped into oars;
pine trees from Cyprus
were cut for your deck,
which was then decorated
with strips of ivory.
7The builders used fancy linen
from Egypt for your sails,
so everyone could see you.
Blue and purple cloth
from Cyprus was used
to shade your deck.
8Men from Sidon and Arvad
did the rowing,
and your own skilled workers
were the captains.
9Experienced men from Byblos
repaired any damages.
Sailors from all over
shopped at the stores
in your port.
10Brave soldiers from Persia,
Lydia, and Libya
served in your navy,
protecting you with shields
and helmets,
and making you famous.
11Your guards came from
Arvad and Cilicia,
and men from Gamad
stood watch in your towers.
With their weapons
hung on your walls,
your beauty was complete.
12Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products. 13The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze, 14and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules. 15You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods. 16Edom traded emeralds, purple cloth, embroidery, fine linen, coral, and rubies. 17Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise. 18The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar. 19Vedan and Javan near Uzal traded you iron and spices. 20The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets, 21while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats. 22Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products. 23You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad, 24and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope. 25 Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go.
You were like a ship
loaded with heavy cargo
26and sailing across the sea,
but you were wrecked
by strong eastern winds.
27Everything on board was lost—
your valuable cargo,
your sailors and carpenters,
merchants and soldiers.
28The shouts of your drowning crew
were heard on the shore.
29Every ship is deserted;
rowers and sailors and captains
all stand on shore,
30mourning for you.
They show their sorrow
by putting dust on their heads
and rolling in ashes;
31they shave their heads
and dress in sackcloth
as they cry in despair.
32In their grief they sing
a funeral song for you:
“Tyre, you were greater
than all other cities.
But now you lie in silence
at the bottom of the sea.
33“Nations that received
your merchandise
were always pleased;
kings everywhere got rich
from your costly goods.
34But now you are wrecked
in the deep sea,
with your cargo and crew
scattered everywhere.
35People living along the coast
are shocked at the news.
Their rulers are horrified,
and terror is written
across their faces.
36The merchants of the world
can't believe what happened.
Your death was gruesome,
and you are gone forever.”
translation_text:
Tura teo luseim leiŋa
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, mɔ luseim leiŋa n pa Tura teo kom. 3Tura teo kom lɔge ko zege naneo kom ni ne, ye ko nɔn-bia bam ke pipiu de naneo ni teene dedɛ. Nam ta de teo kom konto we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Tura teo, nmo bere n tete we,
“Amo jege lam mo chekke.”
4N siseina yam yɔɔre ya wo naneo kom tetare ne mo.
N lɔra bam ma pa se n lam dem nwoŋi chekke.
5Nmo nye de nabworo kolo da-kwollu
na ye Senira tei-dedwaaro mo ba gwoni ba ma ke to.
Ba ta ma kwei Sedare tio na nwoŋi Lebanon ne to
ba ma ba ke n tetare beiŋa kam.
6Basan tei-zwanno mo ba kwei
ba ma ba sare n yuŋina bam naywi sem.
Ko ta ná ye n wo kom tega kam seeni,
ba mɛ Koperese dɛ selo na nwoŋi Kitim ne to mo ba ke-ko,
ye ba ma tuu yeila ba gɔgere dɛ sem konto.
7Ba ta ma kwei gare-fefale selo na gɔgere ye se nwoŋi Ejipti ne to
ba pale wɛɛne se vio taa dole ko mage-se.
Gwaaro tem konto nam ta mo ye nmo tuta de.
Ba ta ma kwei gwaaro telo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwiu de nasoŋ-pupwiu ye te nwoŋi Elisa jei sem ne to
ba ma ba pu vwoa ba ke da.
8Sidon tiina, de Aravadi tiina mo ye n yuŋina bam.
Nmo tete Tura nɔɔna balo na jege yi-poro to
nam mo nii nabworo yuŋim baŋa ne.
9Gebale teo nakwa balo na ye gwaro to
mo fɔge ba kwɛ nabworo kom ne ko ná chɔge.
Balo maama na tɔge naneo kom baŋa ba beeri to
mo yeini ba tui se ba ke pipiu n teo kom wone.
10Peresia tiina, de Ludi tiina, de Puti tiina
de tɔge ba ye nmo jar-keira mo.
Ba ma kwei ba jara nantane de ba jara yu-gwonnu
ba pale n kabiri sem yera ne,
pa se ko ja nenɔŋa ko ba ko pa‑m.
11Aravadi tiina, de Heleki tiina
mo zege n kabiri sem baŋa ne ba yere jei sem maama.
Gamade tiina de maa wo n di-dedwaaro tem ne.
Banto de kwei ba jara nantane sem
ba pale n kabiri sem maama yera ne.
Konto ma pa se n lam dem tiini de nwoŋi.
12Tura teo, Tarasisi tiina mo tu ba ke pipiu dede‑m, nmo na tiini n duni de jejegero dedɛ to ŋwaane. Ba maa yeini ba kwei lu-nyenno, de luuru tedwonna ba ma ba yeigi n zela yam.
13Girisi, de Tubal, de Meseka tiina de yeini ba ke ba pipiu de nmo mo. Ba maa yeini ba kwei kabɛ, de channa wonnu ba pa‑m se ba daare ba jwoŋi n zela yam.
14Bɛte-Togarama teo nɔɔna de maa yeini ba kwei sisein-nɔɔna, de jara-keim sisei, de bona-sisei ba pa‑m ye ba daare ba jwoŋi n zela yam.
15Rodan tiina de maa yeini ba ke pipiu dede‑m. Teene delo na wo naneo ni ne to nɔɔna dedɛ mo tu se á ke pipiu daane. Ba ma kwei tuu yeila de kakɔnɔ dɛ ba maa yeigi n zela yam.
16Aram tiina de maa yeini ba ke pipiu dede‑m, n zela yam na daga to ŋwaane. Ba kwei kandwa-nyenno dwi dwi, de gare-nyenno, de gwaaro telo ba na gɔgere to, de gare-fefale, de Korale kandwa-ŋona mo ba ma ba leiri n zela yam.
17Judah de Isarele dwi tiina de pipi de nmo mo. Ba kwei banina kalo na nwoŋi Minifa to, de mɔɔro, de tooro, de nuga, de terale nuga mo ba leiri n wo-yeillo tem.
18Damasika tiina ke pipiu dede‑m, n na jege zela dedɛ de jejegero dwi dwi to ŋwaane. Ba ma ja sana balo na nwoŋi Helebon to, de pei koro telo na nwoŋi Zahara to, 19de kɔɔra de ba wo sana balo na nwoŋi Yuzali ne to ba ba ba ma ba yeigi n wonnu. Luuru, de Kasia tio poro, de feil-kasoro maa wo n zela yam wone.
20Dedan tiina ma kwei gwaaro telo n na wó kwei n daŋe n bonaga baŋa ne to ba ma ba leiri nmo zela yam.
21Ko nam ná ye Arabia tiina, de Kedare teo dedɛɛra bam, ba kwei pipeili, de pi-bale, de bone mo ba ke pipiu de nmo, ye ba ma-te ba leiri n zela yam.
22Seba de Raama tiina bam de ke pipiu de nmo mo. Ba kwei dwoa-bia, de kandwa-nyenno, de sabu-seŋa mo ba ma leiri n zela yam.
23N ta ke pipiu de Haran tiina, de Kanɛ tiina, de Eden tiina, ko ta woli de Seba, de Asuri, de Chilamada pipim-piina bam. 24Banto yeini ba pipi n yɛ sem ne mo ye ba kwei gare-laaro dwi dwi ba ma leiri n zela yam. Gwaaro tem tedwonna nyenyero ye nazwon-pupwiu mo, ye ba ta gɔgere te tedwonna lanyerane. Gwaaro tedwonna na ye sare to ye ba mɛ gare-ŋone na ye nyenyero dwi dwi to mo ba sɔ-se pa se jujugi ye ba daare ba fɔge ba sɔ se nia yam. 25Tarasisi nabwooru tem mo yeini te zeŋe n zela yam te ja vo jei sedwonna pipiu ŋwaane.
Tura teo, nmo déem nye de nabworo kolo zela na duna
ye ko wo naneo kom tetare ne ko vei to mo.
26Balo na yuŋi nmo to mo jaane‑m
ba zoore na-luŋa jei sem ne.
Nmo na wo naneo kom tetare ne konto to,
vio mo zaŋe wɛ-puli seeni ko ba ko vuvugi‑m
pa se n chɔge zɔŋ-zɔŋ.
27Ko ná ye n jejegero tem, de n zela yam,
de n pipiu wonnu tem maama,
de n yuŋina bam, de balo na nii yuŋim dem baŋa ne to,
de balo na fɔge ba kwɛ nabworo kom to,
de n pipim-piina bam,
de n jar-keira bam,
de balo maama na wo n wone to,
banto maama wó maŋe naneo kom tetare wone mo ba te.
Konto maama wó ke dɛ dem lɛɛro na tu n baŋa to mo.
28Naneo ni buburi-bɛ maama wó ziziŋi mo,
de n nɔɔna bam na tiini ba laare tei to.
29Yuŋina bam maama wó nwoŋi ba nabwooru tem wone mo
ba daare-te.
Balo maama ya na wó zo te wone ba yɛ na ba bɛ to
laam maa wó bɛ ba zege buburi-bɛ dem ne.
30Ba maa wó laare baŋa baŋa de wo-chechɔgɔ nmo ŋwaane.
Ba ta maa wó kwei kasolo ba taare ba yuni
ye ba ta bibili tentwarem wone.
31Ba ta wó cheeri ba yuni de kolo na yi nmo to,
se ba daare ba kwei gare-nyenyaaro ba zo.
Ba wó tiini ba keeri de wo-chechɔgɔ ba pa‑m,
ba wo na wó tiini ko pɛ to ŋwaane.
32Ba ná laare konto dwoŋi á ŋwaane,
ba wó taa leeni luseim lei ba we:
“Tura teo jege dwoŋi mo na?
Ko ni nam tu de meeri
ye naneo kom yɔɔre ko li-ko kula!”
33Teene dedɛ yeini de jwoŋi nmo wonnu tem
pa ba toŋe ba fera abam yera ne mo.
Nmo jejegero tem de n zela yam
mo pɛ se tega baŋa teene dem pwa duni.
34Leile nam, naneo kom yɔɔre ko chɔge nmo mo,
pa se n maŋe na-luŋa kuri ne.
N zela yam de balo maama na toŋe n wone to
tɔge dede‑m ba jei naneo kom wone.
35Nɔɔna balo maama na zoore naneo ni teene dem ne to
yera sɔɔre de kolo na yi nmo to.
Ba pwa yera sae mo de foone,
ye ba yiga tiini ka nyɔne.
36Balo na ke pipiu logo baŋa teene dem wone to
pwɛ ba tete de nmo mo.
Lɛɛro telo na yi nmo to kɛ jeŋa,
pa se n dwi ti taa wuu.’ ”

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Tyre
1The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying:
You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human. 3You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
4Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver. 5You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
6You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God, 7will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get. 8Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
9When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human. 10Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
11The Lord said:
12Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying:
At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking. 13You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born. 14I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
15You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things. 16You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
17It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you. 18You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood, 19and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever.
Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
20 The Lord said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon 22and tell its people:
I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy. 23I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
24When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
A Blessing for Israel
25The Lord God said:
Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob. 26They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_text:
Tura teo pɛ yera taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, ta de Tura teo yuu tu wom we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Nmo yeini n bere n tete kamunim mo
ye n tɛ n tete ne we, “Amo ye wɛ mo.
Tura teo kom ne mo a jei a di paare,
ne wɛ dedwoŋi na di paare
naneo kom tetare ne tei to.”
Nmo nam ye nabiinu mo se n dae wɛ,
de nmo na boŋe we n jege wɛ boboŋa to de.
3Nmo bere n tete we n jege swa n dwoi Danyeli mo na?
N ta boŋe we kolokolo wo seigi n yiga ne mo na?
4Nmo kwei swa mo, de yi-poro,
ye n tɔge tento baŋa ne n beeri jejegero n pa n tete.
N ma‑n la sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno dedɛ
n tiŋi n di sem wone.
5Nmo tiini n yei pipiu laŋa
ye n tɔge ko baŋa ne n tiini n duni.
Nmo jejegero tem ŋwaane,
n laam ma n bere n tete.
6Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Nmo boŋe we n jege swa,
pa n yei wonnu ne wɛ dwoŋi to.
7Mo kokuri, amo lage a pa se veira ba
ba ke chichuŋu de n teo kom.
Ba nam ye teene delo nɔɔna na ye nankɔ-nyena
ba dwoi nɔɔna maama to mo.
Nii mo! Ba wó jeeri nmo nɔɔna bam de jara,
se ba chɔge wo-laaro telo n na nɛ n swa baŋa ne to ba yage,
ye ba daare ba chɔge n nenɔŋa kam.
8Nmo dona bam konto wó pa se n te dam toone mo,
pa se n maŋe tega kuri ne,
mɛ na ye naneo kom tetare to.
9Nmo nam ná zege balo na lage ba go‑m to yiga ne,
n laam wó ta we, n ye wɛ mo na?
Ne n ná to n gora bam jeŋa ne,
n laam wó lɔre we n ye nabiinu mo,
se n dae wɛ.
10Nɔn-yɔɔro mo lage ba go‑m,
se n te balo na yeiri Wɛ to toone.
Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ”
11 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ta ma yi amo we:
12“Nabiinu, yɔɔre n mɔ luseim leiŋa n pa Tura teo pɛ wom ye n ta ded‑o we: ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Nmo déem ye nɔɔno mo chekke.
N swa gaale ye n ta ye nenɔm.
13Wɛ na ke kara kalo Eden jei sem ne to
nmo ya n zoora.
N ma‑n kwei kandwa-nyenno dwi maama
n ma n fɔge n yera.
Te maa ye: Rubi, de Topazi, de Emeraleda,
de Kirisola, de Onika, de Jasipa,
de Safira, de Tukwazi, de Berili.
Ba ta ma gɔgere sabu-seŋa wonnu ba tiŋi,
se te cheigi dɛ delo ne ba na wó lo nmo to.
14Amo ma le cherubi yuu tu se o taa yere‑m.
N déem wo amo Wɛ peo kolo na ye wose to baŋa ne mo.
N ma‑n beeri kandwa yalo na di de mini to tetare ne.
15Nmo totoŋa maama déem ba jege tusim
ko zege dɛ delo ne ba na naane‑m to.
Ko laam ma yi yiga ye n bobo se n ta‑n ke lwarem.
16Nmo na tiini n ke pipiu tei to
mo pɛ se n nankɔɔre kikia de n wɛleera laam gaale.
Amo de ma zeili‑m pa se n yage Wɛ peo kom
de n chaveera.
Cherubi tu wolo ya na yere‑m to
de laam ma le‑m kandwa yalo na di de mini to tetare ne.
17N déem bere n tete kamunim mo
n na ye nenɔm to ŋwaane.
N nenɔŋa kam ma li n swa yam.
Konto ŋwaane mo a vuvugi‑m a dole a de tega ne,
pa se n ji wo-mɔnɔ pwa badwonna yiga ne.
18N tiini n tusi dedɛ,
ye n daare n pini nɔɔna pipiu baŋa ne.
Ko ma pa se n chɔge wara-jei selo n ya na zuli-ne da to.
A ma da ko ŋwaane a pa se mini to n teo kom ne,
se de zwɛ ko maama kula!
Teo kom laam jigi tentwarem mo,
ye balo maama na nɛ nmo to zege ba nia.
19Ko ná ye dwi tiina balo ya na yei n na ye wolo to,
ba nia laam yɛ mo de kolo na yi‑m to.
Lɛɛro telo na yi nmo to kɛ jeŋa,
pa se n dwi ti taa wuu.’ ”
Sidon teo taane
20 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ma yi amo we:
21“Nabiinu, pa n yibia jeeri Sidon teo kom seeni se n daare n pworisi taane n chɔge-ko. 22Ta we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Sidon teo, amo dwoni dede‑m.
A nam wó pa se a nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom taa nae jaja n wone.
Nɔɔna wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom,
ne a ná yɔɔre a waare n nɔn-bia bam a ti,
ye ba sɛ we amo mo ye wo-pwoŋo tu.
23Amo wó pa se jawe-chɛɛro to ba teo kom ne
ko go ba dedɛ.
A ta wó pa se jar-keira zaŋe jei maama ne
ba kwaare jara de teo kom
pa se twa faare ko wo maama.
Ba laam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.
24Isarele tiina bam daa bá taa jege dona balo na nye de sabare de sabare-mangwoli to se ba taa jege-ba ba zɔa ye ba yaale-ba. Ba maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.
25Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo ná lage Isarele tiina bam a ja a nwoŋi teene delo a ya na yage-ba de wone to, a laam wó pa dwi-gɛ tiina bam lɔre we amo mo ye wo-pwoŋo tu de a na ke a nɔɔna bam tei to. Isarele tiina bam laam maa wó jwoori ba vo ba taa zoore ba tete tega kalo a déem na kwei a pa a tontoŋeno Jakob to wone. 26Ba maa wó taa zoore da de yazura ye ba lɔ sane ba daare ba jeiri Vini teeni. Kolokolo daa bá daane-ba, amo na wó waare ba dona balo ya na jege-ba ba yaale to ŋwaane. Konto mo ba wó lɔre we amo mo ye ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ”

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Egypt
1 Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people 3that I am saying:
King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy! 4I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body. 5I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh. 6 Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord.
You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick. 7When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
8So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock, 9until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things.
You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it. 10Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia. 11No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for 40 years. 12It will be the most barren place on earth. Every city in Egypt will lie in ruins during those 40 years, and I will scatter your people throughout the nations of the world.
13Then after those 40 years have passed, I will bring your people back from the places where I scattered them. 14They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom 15and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past. 16My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
17Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
18King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city. 19So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops. 20Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
21Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Ejipti teo taane
1Bena fuga bene dem chane fuga chana kam da fuga-yalei dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, pipiri n jeeri Ejipti teo kom seeni, se n pworisi taane n chɔge ba pa-faro wom, de o teo kom maama. 3Ta o yera taane we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Ejipti teo pɛ, amo dwoni de nmo mo.
Nmo nye de naneo wo juru
kolo na tigi n teo kom bwi sem ne to mo.
Nmo ma‑n bere n tete we, “Amo mo tei Naili buga kam.
A nam ke-ka se a pa a tete mo.”
4A nam lage a kwei gwoli mo a ja‑m n peyaa seeni.
A ta wó pa se ywona yalo na su n bwi sem to
meeli n yera yam.
A nam lage a vaŋe‑m mo a ja a nwoŋi n bwi sem ne,
ye ywona yam maama ta yɔɔre ya meeli n yera yam.
5A nam lage a dole nmo tete
de n bwi sem wo ywona yam mo
a yage kagoa yuu ne.
Abam laam wó taa tigi pwola ne mo,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá wane o la abam o ke daane.
A lage a pa se á ji wodiu mo
á pa tega baŋa vara bam,
de wɛyuu zuna bam.
6Balo maama na zoore Ejipti teo wone to laam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.
Nmo déem nye de kasogo kolo Isarele dwi tiina bam na kwei ba ji ba nacheiga to mo. 7Ba na twe ba je se ba zii nmo ba zaŋe to, n seere mo pa se ba vɔna kaare. Ba maa na sale nmo yera ne to, mo n bwori n daare-ba pa ba nɛ sem te.
8Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a pa se jara mo to n teo kom wone, se nabiina de ba vara bam maama te. 9Ejipti teo kom wó ji di-dwonnu yerane, se ba laam lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.
Kokuri to, nmo tage n we, “Amo mo tei Naili buga kam. Amo mo ke-ka.” 10Konto ŋwaane amo dwoni de nmo, de n bwi sem maama mo. Amo wó pa se Ejipti teo kom chɔge, ye ko ji di-dwonnu yerane, se ko zege Migidola ne ko vo ko yi Sayene se ko kɛ ko yi Kusi siseini dem seeni. 11Nabiina de vara daa bá de ba nɛ tega kam konto ne se ba tɔge da ba kɛ. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno de nam bá taa zoore ka wone se ko yi bena finna. 12A lage a pa Ejipti mo yɔɔre ko ji kagoa teene delo maama na chɔge to wone. Ko teene dem maama wó taa ye di-dwonnu yerane mo, ye di-dwonnu de gilimi-de. Ko wó taa ye konto mo bena finna. A maa wó jage Ejipti tiina bam pa ba vo yiga yiga, se a yage-ba logo baŋa teene dem jei maama wone.
13De ko de, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Bena finna yam ni ná dia, amo wó la Ejipti tiina bam se ba nwoŋi teene delo maama ba ya na jage ba zoore de wone to mo. 14A laam maa wó pa se ba jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo. Ba wó zege sa-teo ne ba jwoori ba ba Paforosi seeni, mɛ na ye ba kugu jei to. Dáane mo ba wó maŋe ba taa ye te-balaŋa. 15Ko maa wó tiini ko taa ye te-balaŋa teene dem maama wone. Ko daa bá wane ko zeiŋi ko tete teene dedwonna baŋa ne. Ko bá di dam dwi-gɛ tiina baŋa ne, amo na wó pa ko taa bwona to ŋwaane. 16Ejipti daa bá taa ye teo kolo Isarele dwi tiina bam na ke ba teena ko wone to. Ba nam wó guli ba na tusi ye ba beeri wolim ko wone to mo. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ”
17Bena finlei-yarepɛ bene dem boboa chana kam boboa dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:
18“Nabiinu, Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza déem pɛ o jar-keira bam tiini ba kwaare jara de Tura teo kom. O ma fe-ba jara yam ŋwaane pa ba yuni fe, ye ba vɔna de dɔre ŋɔna. Nebukadeneza de o jar-keira bam nam wo wane Tura teo kom se ba di nyɔɔre ko baŋa ne, de ba na toŋe tei maama de to. 19Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a kwei Ejipti teo kom mo a pa Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza se o taa tei. Wonto wó zeŋe ba jejegero o ja o viiri, ye o daare o vere ba wonnu o pa o jar-keira bam se ba jwoŋi ba ŋweero. 20A nam kwei Ejipti teo kom a pa‑o se ko taa ye o totoŋa yam ŋweero mo, o de o jar-keira bam na ke kolo maama ba pa amo to ŋwaane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
21Maŋa kam konto ná yia, amo wó pa Isarele dwi tiina bam jwoori ba na dam. Ko daare nmo Ezekeli, a maa wó pa n ni puri se n ŋɔɔne de-ba. Ba maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_text:
Egypt Will Be a Barren Desert
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying:
Cry out in despair,
3because you will soon
be punished!
That will be a time
of darkness and doom
for all nations.
4Your own nation of Egypt
will be attacked,
and Ethiopia will suffer.
You will be killed in battle,
and your land will be robbed
and left in ruins.
5Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle. 6All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
7Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin. 8I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
9On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
10Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army. 11He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
12I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken.
Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins
The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
13All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land. 14The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed! 15The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
16I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear. 17The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner. 18You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity. 19When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord.
Egypt's King Is Powerless
20Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword. 22So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever, 23and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
24-25I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord. 26I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_text:
Ejipti teo luseim leiŋa
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we, 2“Nabiinu, pworisi se n ta we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Chwoosi-na se á ta we,
“Lɛɛro naa!”
3Kokuri to, dɛ dem yi de ti.
Baŋa Wɛ dɛ-kamunu kom mo konto.
Kunkwon-lilirru wó kwoli tega kam
ye lɛɛro yi logo baŋa teene dem
maŋa kam konto ne.
4Jara mo lage ya to Ejipti teo wone.
Cham de maa wó yi Kusi tiina bam.
Ejipti tiina dedɛ wó te jara wone.
Ba dona wó zeŋe ba jejegero tem ba ja ba viiri,
ba daare ba chɔge teo kom
se ko taa zege di-dwonnu yerane.
5Ko ta ná ye Kusi, de Puti, de Ludi, de Arabia tiina maama, de Libia tiina, de balo na nwoŋi amo ni-gwonim tega kam ne to, ba maama wó da de Ejipti tiina bam mo ba te jara wone.
6 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Balo na zege Ejipti teo kwaga ne to lage ba to tega ne mo.
Dam delo Ejipti tiina bam na teere de baŋa ne to maa wó jei.
Ko na zege Migidola ne, se ko yi Sayene to,
ba maama lage ba te jara yalo na wó yi Ejipti to wone mo.
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
7Ba jei sem wó yɔɔre se ji kagoa
teene delo maama na chɔge to wone.
Ba teene dem wó taa ye di-dwonnu yerane mo,
ye di-dwonnu de gilimi-de.
8Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom,
ne a na wó pa se Ejipti teo kom ja mini,
ye a daare a nɔne ko fara maama a meere to.
9Dɛ dem konto ná yia, a ta lage a toŋe nɔɔna nabwooru wone se ba ja a kwora ba vo ba pa Kusi teo tiina, de ba na jei de yazura tei to de. Lwia nam wó pɔpɔ ya ja-ba Ejipti teo chɔgem maŋa kam ne, ko na wó seene ko ke to ŋwaane.
10Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento:
Amo lage a tɔge Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza baŋa ne mo
se a chɔge Ejipti jar-keira bam dam.
11Wonto de o jar-keira bam keim tiini de chana
de dwoi tega baŋa nɔɔna maama na ye tei to.
Ba lage ba jeeri Ejipti teo kom de jara mo,
se ba daare ba chɔge ba tega kam.
Ba maa wó pa twa faare Ejipti tega kam maama.
12Amo wó pa se Naili buga kam we,
ye a kwei ba tega kam a pa nɔn-balwaaro.
A yɔɔre a lage a tɔge veira baŋa ne mo
a chɔge ba tega kam de kolo maama na wo ka wone to.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.
13Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ ta na tage tei to mo tento:
A lage a chɔge ba jwona yam mo,
ye a pa se ya nyenyero telo na wo Memfisi ne to jei.
Ejipti teo kom daa bá taa jege pwa.
A maa wó pa foone zo ko nɔɔna bam maama.
14Amo wó pa se Paforosi taa ye yɔɔ yerane,
ye a pa se mini zwɛ Zoan teo kom.
A nam ta wó waare Tebesi de.
15A yɔɔre a lage a lwo a ban-lom dem Pelusi baŋa ne mo,
ko na ye Ejipti dam jei sem to ŋwaane.
A ta wó go Tebesi jar-keira bam maama.
16A lage a pa mini mo ja Ejipti teo kom,
ye Pelusi tiina bam wó taa wowole de cham.
Tebesi teo kabiri sem lage se chɔge mo.
Foone maa wó tiini de ja Memfisi tiina dɛ maama wone.
17Ona, de Pi-besefa nɔn-donno maama wó te jara wone.
Ba maa wó ja teene dem konto nɔɔna bam ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga.
18Wea maŋa ne Tapanahesi teo kom wó ji lim yerane,
ne a ná jaane Ejipti teo dam dem a ja a chɔge a yage.
Ba ya maa na teere kolo baŋa ne to maama wó ti.
Kunkwon-lilirru mo wó kwoli ba tega kam.
Ko ta ná ye Ejipti teene dem maama,
ba lage ba ja de nɔn-bia bam
ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga mo.
19Amo laam maa ná waare Ejipti teo kom a ti,
ba wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ”
20Bena fuga-dedoa bene dem boboa chana kam da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:
21“Nabiinu, amo jaane Ejipti pa-faro wom jeŋa mo a bwori. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam wo vɔge gare-zɔŋɔ se o kwei-ka o de ko wone. Ko laam ma pa se o jeŋa kam wo twoŋi se ka taa dana se ka wane se-zɔɔ ka zeeri. 22Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Amo dwoni de Ejipti teo pa-faro wom mo. A yɔɔre a lage a bwori o je sem maama mo, ne ko ná ye o je-laao kom de je-bubwora kam maama. Konto to, o se-zɔɔ kom wó lwei ko to tega ne. 23A nam ta lage a pa Ejipti tiina bam mo jage ba vo yiga yiga se a yage-ba logo baŋa teene dem maama wone. 24A maa wó pa Babilon teo pɛ na dam ye a kwei a se-zɔɔ a ke o jeŋa ne. A laam maa wó bwori Ejipti pa-faro wom vɔna, se o taa vuvuni de cham Babilon pɛ wom yiga ne, ne wolo na nɛ zonne ye o lage o te to. 25Chega to, a wó pa Babilon teo pɛ je sem na dam. Se ko ná ye Ejipti pa-faro wom, o vɔna lage ya to tega ne mo vareba. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, ne a ná kwei a se-zɔɔ kom a ke Babilon pɛ wom jeŋa ne, se o de kwei-ko o ma o fugi Ejipti tiina bam. 26A nam wó seene a jage Ejipti tiina bam pa ba vo yiga yiga se a yage-ba logo baŋa teene dem maama wone. Konto baŋa ne ba wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_text:
Egypt's King Will Be Chopped Down like a Cedar Tree
1Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying:
You are more powerful
than anyone on earth.
Now listen to this.
3There was once a cedar tree
in Lebanon
with large, strong branches
reaching to the sky.
4This tree had plenty of water
to help it grow tall,
and nearby streams watered
the other trees
in the forest.
5But this tree towered over
those other trees,
and its branches
grew long and thick.
6Birds built nests
in its branches,
and animals were born
beneath it.
People from all nations
lived in the shade
of this strong tree.
7It had beautiful,
long branches,
and its roots found water
deep in the soil.
8 None of the cedar trees
in my garden of Eden
were as beautiful
as this tree;
no tree of any kind
had such long branches.
9I, the Lord, gave this tree
its beauty,
and I helped the branches
grow strong.
All other trees in Eden
wanted to be just like it.
10King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree:
The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant. 11So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness. 12Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else. 13Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
14Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
15On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither. 16This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble.
The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls. 17Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
18King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Ejipti Pa-faro wom taane
1Bena fuga-dedoa bene dem chane setɔ chana kam boboa dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, ta n bere Ejipti pa-faro wom de o nɔn-kɔgɔ kom we:
‘Wɔ kamunni mo ma de nmo?
3Nam boŋe n nii Asiria teo na guri tei to.
Ko déem nye de Sedare tei-zɔŋɔ mo
na wo Lebanon teo kom ne.
Ko nɛ sem déem tage mo lanyerane
ye se ke vɔɔro pa woro wora goa kam ne.
Ko ma tiini ko ke dedɔrɔ
ko kɛ ko di wɛyuu baŋa baŋa.
4Na maa daga da se tio kom taa nyɔa.
Buli-yia yalo na nwoŋi tega kuri ne to
pɛ se ko be lanyerane.
Bu-nwaro maa wora jeiga kalo ko na jeiri to,
ye te na bam duri ba vo ba yi
teeni delo maama de na wo goa kam ne to.
5Tio kom konto ma tiini ko ke dedɔrɔ
ko dwoni goa kam wo teeni dedwonna dem maama.
Ko ma yɔɔre ko ta nɛ dedɛ,
ye se tiini se dɔra.
Ko nɛ sem nam na yarege konto to,
ko ye na bam na daga da to ŋwaane mo.
6Zuna dwi dwi ma ba
ba sɔ ba pworu ko nɛ sem yera ne.
Ko daare ye ga-vara de ba
ba maŋe ko nɛ sem kuri ne ba lo ba bia.
Logo baŋa dwi tiina balo maama na dana to de ma ba
ba jeini ko woro kuri ne.
7Ko déem yɔɔre ko jege lam de kamunni mo,
ye ko nɛ sem yarege se yi jei maama.
Kokuri to, ko bonno tem zo te kwaare tega ne mo,
pa se te yi na dedɛ tega kuri ne.
8Wɛ tete kara Sedare teeni dem
bá wane de maŋe de tio kom konto.
Ko ta ná ye Koperese de Pileeni tei-dedwaaro tem de,
te nɛ sem bá maŋe de konto nɛ sem na ye tei to.
Tio dwi déem maŋe ko tere Wɛ teeni kara kam ne,
se dé kwei dé ma dé maŋe de tio kom konto lam.
9Ko ye amo mo pɛ ko lana konto
pa ko jege nɛ selo na tiini se daga to,
ye Eden wo teeni dem maama
déem tiini de jege kazwe de di de tio kom konto.
10Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Tio kom tiini ko ke dedɔrɔ ko kɛ ko di wɛyuu kom, pa se ko bere ko tete. 11Mo kokuri, a kwei-ko a ke pɛ wolo na jege dam logo baŋa teene dem baŋa ne to jeŋa ne. Wonto laam ma yɔɔre o waare-ko se ko maŋe de ko keim-lwanno na mae tei to. Amo mo dole-ko a yage dáa ne. 12Konto ma pa se dwi-gɛ tiina balo na tiini ba ye nankɔ-nyena to ba ba gwoni-ko ba de tega ne, ba daare ba yage-ko pa ko tiga ko na to mɛ seeni to. Ko nɛ sem to mo se tigi peero yuni ne, de bwollu maama tega ne. Ko da-dwa de ma bwori ye se tigi tega kam gugworru maama wone. Teene delo nɔɔna ya na tigi ko woro kuri ne to ma duri ba daare-ko. 13Zuna bam laam ma ba ba jeini tio kom da-buŋa kalo na daare ka tigi to baŋa ne. Ga-vara bam de ma ba ba nɔne ko nɛ selo na to tega ne to baŋa ne. 14Ko nam na ye tei to, tio kolo maama na nae na ko nyɔ to daa bá fɔge ko ke dedɔrɔ ko di wɛyuu kom, ne tio konto ya na ye tei to. Na ná maŋe ba yi teeni dem tei maama de, de bá wane de taa dɔra konto dwoŋi. De jege se de te mo tega baŋa ne, ne ko na ye tei nabiina tei ne to. De maa jege se de maŋe nabiina tetare ne, ne banto na toa ye ba vei tega kuri ne tei to.
15Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Dɛ delo ne tio kom konto na to ko te ye ko tu ko zo churu to, amo ma pa buli-yia yam ni se ya keeri tio kom lua. A ma che bwi sem pa se na-fwaaro tem daa ba dura. A ma pa Lebanon tega kam maama ye lim, tio kom na to to ŋwaane. Teeni dem maama de ma kwaare de zega. 16Tio kom na to buru-tu-tu ye dwi-gɛ tiina bam ni to, a ma pa se ba yera sae, ko na tɔge de balo na vei tega kuri ne ko vo ko zo churu to ŋwaane. Eden kara kam wo teeni dem maama, de Lebanon tei-laaro tem, ko woli de teeni delo maama na na yi-de chekke to maama wo laam ma zuri. 17Logo baŋa dwi tiina balo maama ya na yeini ba jei tei-zɔŋɔ kom woro ne ye ba ye ko fara to de ma tɔge de-ko ba zo churu, ba woli de balo na maŋe ba te jara wone to.
18Eden kara wo teeni dem maama wone, tio kɔ kamunni de ko nenɔŋa mo ma de nmo? De ko de, ba lage ba gwoni nmo ba de tega ne, se nmo de woli Eden kara wo teeni dem mo n zo tega kuri. Dáane mo n lage n ta‑n tigi de balo na yeiri Wɛ to, dedaane balo maama na tega jara wone to.
Memaŋe dento bere ko na wó ke Ejipti teo pa-faro wom de o nɔn-kɔgɔ kom tei to mo. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ”

english_text:
A Funeral Song for the King of Egypt
1Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying:
You act like a lion
roaming the earth;
but you are nothing more than
a crocodile in a river,
churning up muddy water
with your feet.
3King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore. 4I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh. 5I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys, 6and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams. 7 I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining. 8The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
9Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you. 10They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
11The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt! 12Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed. 13I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water. 14The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
15Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
16This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
A Sad Ending for Egypt
17On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations. 19Say to them:
You may be more beautiful
than the people
of other nations,
but you will also die
and join the godless
in the world below.
20You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you. 21Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
22-23The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
24-25The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
26The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle. 27They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
28You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
29The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
30The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
31The Lord God says:
When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering. 32I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Ejipti Pa-faro wom luseim leiŋa
1Bena fuga-yalei bene dem chane fuga-selei chana kam boboa dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora tu ka yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, mɔ luseim leiŋa n pa Ejipti teo pa-faro wom n ta ded‑o we:
‘Nmo ya bere n tete we n ye nywoŋo mo
ye n jege dam logo baŋa teene dem maama wone.
Ko nam na ye tei to, n yɔɔre n ye naneo wo juru mo.
Nmo ma‑n tigi n teo kom bwi sem ne
n jege na bam n pɔgele de n nɛ,
pa se na bam maama ji bworu yerane.
3Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento:
Amo wó la nɔn-kɔgɔ dedɛ mo
ye a daare a dole a bora se a ma a ja‑m.
Nɔɔna bam laam maa wó vaŋe‑m
ba ja ba nwoŋi buga kam ne.
4A maa wó dole‑m a yage te-kora baŋa ne,
se n ta‑n tigi pwola ne.
Amo ta wó pa se wɛyuu zuna bam maama ba
ba jeini nmo baŋa ne,
se ga-vara bam maama de ba ba di n yera yam ba su.
5A ta lage a kwei n ya-nɔna yam
a jare peero tem yuu ne mo.
Nmo yera yalo na daare ye ya pɔ to
maa wó faare bwollu tem maama.
6N jana wó duri ba taa tole tega kam jei maama ne mo
ba kɛ ba yi peero jei sem,
ye ba su gugworru tem de.
7Amo ná yɔɔre a chɔge‑m a ti,
a lage a li wɛyuu kom mo
se chalechwe sem yé ta se nwoŋi.
A ta wó pa se kunkwoŋo mo kwoli wea kam.
Chana kam de daa bá nye ka pwooni dem.
8Wɛyuu pwooni dwi maama wó ji lim ko pa‑m,
pa se n teo kom jei maama taa ye lim yerane.
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
9Logo baŋa teene dem ná nɛ nmo na yɔɔre n chɔge tei to,
a laam wó pa se lwia tiini ya ja-ba,
ko ná maŋe ko ye dwi-gɛ tiina
balo nmo ya na yeiri ba ni ne to de.
10A ta wó pa se nɔɔna dedɛ yera sɔɔre nmo ŋwaane.
Ba pwa bam wó fom mo ye ba yera taa sae,
a na wó kwei a se-zɔɔ kom
a liligi ba yiga ne to ŋwaane.
Nmo totoore dɛ dem ne mo foone wó ja ba maama,
ye lwia taa jege-ba maŋa maama
de ba ŋwea na lage ka ti tei to.
11Kokuri, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
Babilon teo pɛ wom mo lage o ba
o jeeri n teo kom de jara.
12A nam lage a tɔge babɛ se-zɔɔro baŋa ne mo,
se a go n jar-keira bam maama.
Babɛ sem konto jege nankɔɔre mo
ba dwoi logo baŋa teene dem maama.
Ba lage ba chɔge Ejipti kamunim maama mo,
ye ba daare ba meere ba jar-keira kɔgɔ kom maama.
13Ko ta ná ye n teo kom naane delo na beeri bwi sem ni ne to,
a lage a chɔge de maama mo.
Nabiina daa bá de ba nɛ bwi sem na wone se ba pɔgele-ba.
Naane de napɔɔna de daa bá nɔne na bam wone
se ba pa ba pɔgele.
14Kwaga seeni mo a laam wó pa se
n teo kom bwi sem wo na bam tigisi,
se bu-nwaro tem na de taa duri ba kɛa ne nuga na ke tei to.
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
15Amo wó seene a pa Ejipti teo kom ji di-dwonnu yerane,
se kolokolo daa yé daare tega kam baŋa ne.
A ta wó mage balo maama na zoore ko wone to pa ba to tega ne.
Maŋa kam konto ne mo ba laam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.’
16Luseim leiŋa kanto mo ba lage ba leeni ba pa‑o. Ko nam ye dwi-gɛ tiina bam bukwa mo lage ba mɔ luseim leiŋa kam konto ba pa Ejipti teo de ko nɔn-bia bam maama. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”
17Bena fuga-yalei bene dem chane fuga-selei chana kam da fuga-yanu dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:
18“Nabiinu, yɔɔre n ta‑n keeri Ejipti teo nɔn-bia bam ŋwaane. Banto jege se ba tɔge de te-kamunnu dedwonna nɔɔna mo se ba maama te ba daare ba tu tega kuri jei sem ne. 19Ta de-ba we, ‘Abam boŋe we á jege lam á dwoi dwia yadwonna mo na? Á nam jege se á tu tega kuri ne á ta‑á tigi de balo na yeiri Wɛ to mo.’ 20Ba nam wó tɔge de balo na to jara wone to mo ba te. Se-zɔɔro lage te ba te go-ba mo lela! Ejipti teo kom de ko nɔn-bia bam maama ye se ba dona bam mo zi-ba ba ja ba viiri. 21Bembɛ selo na maŋe ba wo churu wone to wó ta Ejipti teo de ko fara bam taane ba we, ‘Ba laam tu debam tei se ba taa tigi de balo na yeiri Wɛ to, dedaane balo na tege jara wone to.’
22Asiria teo de ko jar-keira bam maama maa wora. Banto tege jara wone ye ba yibeela tigi da. 23Ba déem na ŋwe tega baŋa ne to, ba tiini ba fugi nɔɔna dedɛ. Ba maama ma te jara wone, ye ba yibeela yam wo tega kuri gwoŋo kom gugworru wone.
24Elam teo de maa wora de ko nɔn-bia bam maama ba tigi ba yibeela wone. Ba maama déem tege jara wone mo. Balo maama ya na ŋwe ye ba tiini ba fugi nɔɔna dedɛ to laam mo zo churu ye ba ta yeiri Wɛ. Ba ma tɔge de balo maama na zo tega kuri gwoŋo kom wone to mo ba na ba chaveera. 25Ba ma kwɛ jeiga ba pa Elam teo churu ne se ko taa tigi o jar-keira bam maama tetare ne. Banto maama yeiri Wɛ ye ba laam ba ba te jara wone. Ba ma tɔge de balo maama na zoore churu wone to ba na ba chaveera, ba ya ta na ŋwe ye ba fugi nɔɔna dedɛ to ŋwaane. Ba laam maa tigi balo na tege jara wone to tetare ne.
26Meseka de Tubal de maa wora, ba woli de ba nɔn-bia bam maama ye ba tigi ba yibeela wone. Ba maama nam yeiri Wɛ ye ba te jara wone, ba ya ta na ŋwe ye ba tiini ba fugi nɔɔna dedɛ to ŋwaane. 27Ba nam wo suli-ba de zula ne ba na ke tei de faŋa faŋa bembɛ selo na tege jara wone to mo. Banto déem zo churu wone ye ba jege ba se-zɔɔro ba ma ba yeiri ba yuni, ba daare ba jege ba jara nantane ba kwoli ba yera. Bembɛ sem konto ya ta na ŋwe to, ba ya tiini ba fugi nɔɔna dedɛ.
28Ejipti teo pɛ, ko nam ná ye nmo, nmo de lage n te mo, se n tɔge n taa wo balo na yeiri Wɛ ye ba go-ba jara ne to wone.
29Edom teo, de ko pwa, de ko dedɛɛra bam de maa tɔge ba wo churu wone. Ba tu ba tɔge de balo na tege jara wone to, de ba na maŋe ba jege dam tei maama to de. Ba laam maa tigi de balo ya na yeiri Wɛ ye ba zo tega kuri gwoŋo kom wone to.
30Baŋa seeni teene dem dedɛɛra dedaane Sidon teo tiina bam maama maa wora. Ba ma tɔge de balo na tege jara wone to ba na ba chaveera ye ba te, de ba ya na maŋe ba da ba dam-fɔrɔ ŋwaane ba fugi nɔɔna tei to de. Ba laam maa tigi ba yibeela wone ye ba ta yeiri Wɛ. Ba de di ba chaveera ne balo maama na zo tega kuri gwoŋo kom wone to mo.
31Ejipti teo pa-faro wom wó na kolo na yi teene dem konto maama de de nɔn-bia bam to. O wo laam wó zuri de o tete jar-keira bam na tege jara wone tei to. Mo ko na wó ke Ejipti pa-faro wom de o jar-keira bam maama tei to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. 32Amo ya mo seene a pa‑o dam se o fugi tega baŋa nabiina bam. Wonto de o nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama nam tɔge de balo maama na tege jara wone to mo ba tigi balo na yeiri Wɛ to tetare ne. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_text:
The Lord Appoints Ezekiel To Stand Watch
(Ezekiel 3.16-21)
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying:
Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch 3and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming. 4-5If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
6But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
7Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me. 8When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death. 9If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent.
The Lord Is Always Fair
(Ezekiel 18.21-30)
10The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me. 11Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
12Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
13Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
14Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right. 15For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live. 16Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
17Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair. 18If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned. 19And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 20But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done.
The News of Jerusalem's Fall
21 Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
22The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak.
What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
23Then the Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
25So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying:
How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder 26and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
27As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases. 28I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them. 29I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
The People Listen, but Don't Change
The Lord said:
30Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.” 31So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money. 32They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
33Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_text:
Ezekeli na jigi teo yereno tei to
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ta ma yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, ta de nmo dwi tiina bam we: ‘Amo ná pɛ chwoŋa se jara ba teo kodwoŋi baŋa, ye ko nɔɔna bam kuri ba wone dedoa se o taa yere ba teo kom, 3kotu ná nɛ we jar-keira mo beene teo kom baŋa pa o wu nabɔnɔ se o ma o kaane teo kom nɔɔna, 4wolo maama ná nigi nabɔnɔ kom kwori ye o ke ne o yiga mo tera, nɔɔno wom konto ná tege jara yam wone, ko ye o tete yiga mo. 5Kokuri, kotu nigi nabɔnɔ kom kwori mo ye o ke ne o yiga tera pa o te. O ya ná ke o tɔge nabɔnɔ kom kwori na bere tei to, o ya wó jwoŋi o ŋwea. O toone tɔge de o tete mo. 6Ko daare, wolo na zege o yere teo kom to ná nɛ we jar-keira mo maa beene se ba jeeri-ba de jara, ye o ná ve se o wu nabɔnɔ kom o kaane nɔɔna bam pa ba badwonna te jara yam baŋa ne, ko ye ba nɛ waarem ba tusim kikia ŋwaane mo. Amo nam wó bwei nɔɔna bam konto jana bam jene wolo na zege o yere teo kom to tei ne mo.’
7Nabiinu, a kuri nmo mo se n ji wolo na zege n yere Isarele dwi tiina bam to. Nmo totoŋe mo ye se n cheigi taane delo a na tɛ to, se n laam vo n kaane-ba n pa-ne. 8Amo ná tage puseŋ-nyeno yera taane we o jege se o te mo, ye nmo ná ve se n ŋɔɔne jaja n kaane‑o se o yage o keim-balwaaro tem, puseŋ-nyeno wom konto wó seene o te o tusim kikia yam ŋwaane. A nam wó bwei kotu jana bam jene nmo tei ne mo. 9Ko daare, nmo ná kaane puseŋ-nyeno wom se o yage o keim-balwaaro tem ye o ná ve n ni-kaana yam, o wó seene o te o tusim kikia ŋwaane, ye nmo nam wó jwoŋi n tete n yage.
10Nabiinu, ta de Isarele dwi tiina bam we, ‘Abam na kare á tɛ tei to mo tento: Cham delo debam na nɛ dé zwabania kikia dedaane dé wɛleera yam ŋwaane to tiini de daga de dwoi dé jaanem. Dé wora dé bugi dé jia ya ŋwaane. Debam wó ke tetɛ mo se dé jwoŋi dé ŋwea?’ 11Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we, puseŋ-nyeno toone bá pwoli amo wo. A nam swoi se puseŋ-nyena pipiri ba yage ba totoŋ-nɛ sem, se ba daare ba na ŋwea mo. Isarele dwi tiina bam, nam pipiri-na á yage á lwarem kikia yam. Á wó kuri toone se bɛ mo?’
12Nabiinu, nam ta de n dwi tiina bam we, ‘Nɔn-ŋom ná tusi o chwoŋa, o nɔn-ŋonne kikia bá jwoŋi‑o ya yage. Puseŋ-nyeno nam ná yage o puseŋa kikia yam, o de bá to o puseŋa kikia yalo o ya na ke to ŋwaane. Nɔn-ŋom ná bobo se o taa ke wɛleera, o faŋa nɔn-ŋonne dem bá wane‑o de jwoŋi de yage se o na ŋwea.’ 13Amo nam ná tage de nɔn-ŋom we o wó na ŋwea, pa se o laam kwei o teena o daŋe o nɔn-ŋonne dem baŋa ne se de jwoŋi‑o de yage, ye o bobo se o taa ke totoŋ-lwanno, amo daa bá jeeli wo-laaro telo o ya na ke to de dedoa de. O nam wó te mo o lwarem kikia yam ŋwaane. 14A nam ná tage de puseŋ-nyeno a we, ‘N jege se n te mo,’ ye kotu ná pipiri o yage o wɛleera yam, ye o daare o toŋe chega kam, de kikia yalo na maŋe to, o wó jwoŋi o tete. 15Puseŋ-nyeno ná kwei wonnu telo nɔɔna na pɛ‑o ba ma tiŋi daare to, de wonnu telo o na vere nɔɔna tei ne to o jwoori o pa-ba, ye o ná ke o tɔge a bera yam na pae ŋwea to, ye o daa ba ke wo-lwanno, kotu wó na ŋwea ye o daa bá te. 16Amo daa bá jeeli wɛleera yalo maama o ya na ke to se a ma a chɔge‑o. O laam toŋe chega mo ye o ke kolo na maŋe to. O wó seene o na ŋwea.
17Nmo dwi tiina bam nam jege ni mo ba tɛ ba we, ‘Chega tera Baŋa Wɛ na ke tei to wone.’ Ko nam ye banto mo ba jege chega de kolo ba na jege ba ke to. 18Nɔn-ŋom ná pipiri o yage o nɔn-ŋonne kikia, ye o bobo se o taa toŋe lwarem, o wó te mo ko ŋwaane. 19Puseŋ-nyeno nam ná yage o puseŋa kikia yam, ye o bobo se o taa ke chega kam de kolo na maŋe to, o wó na ŋwea mo o keina yam baŋa ne. 20De ko de, Isarele dwi tiina bam, abam ta kare á tɛ mo á we, ‘Chega tera Baŋa Wɛ na ke tei to wone.’ Amo nam wó bore abam dedoa dedoa taane se ko maŋe de o kikia na ye tei to mo.”
Jerusalem teo totoore dem taane
21Ba na kale debam ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga ye bena fuga-yalei kɛ to, bene dem konto chane fuga kam da yanu dɛ dem ne mo nɔɔno wodwoŋi nwoŋi Jerusalem teo kom ne o duri o lu, ye o ba o ta de amo o we, “Jerusalem teo kom yɔɔre ko to mo jara baŋa ne!” 22Dɛ delo tega na wó poore se nɔɔno wom laam ja kwora kam o ba o pa-ne to, dedaan-ni maŋa ne mo Baŋa Wɛ dam yɔɔre de ba amo baŋa. O ma pa se a ni puri pa a wae a ŋɔɔna se ko lwoori nɔɔno wom tutuuri dem.
23 Baŋa Wɛ kwora laam ma yi amo we:
24“Nabiinu, nɔɔna balo ta na maŋe Isarele teo kom di-dwonnu wone to yeini ba tɛ ba we, ‘Abaraham déem ye o yerane dedoa mo, ye o wane tega kam maama o jwoŋi. Debam nam ye kɔgɔ mo. Dé jege se dé jwoŋi tega kanto mo se ka taa ye debam nyem.’ 25Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam ta swoi se á ta‑á di nɔna yalo yera jana na wo ya wone to mo, ye á daare á kaane jwona, ye á goe nɔɔna. Konto to, ko maŋe se á ta‑á tei tega kam na? 26Abam teege á se-zɔɔro tem baŋa ne mo, ye á kare á ke wo-zɔɔna dwi maama. Nɔɔno maama maa beeri chwoŋa se kotu chɔge o dwoŋi kaane. Abam boŋe we konto maama kwaga ne ko maŋe se á ta‑á tei tega kam mo na?’
27Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: ne amo na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we balo na daare ba zoore di-dwonnu tem wone to wó te jara wone mo. Ko ta ná ye balo de na wo pwola ne to, a lage a pa kago-vara mo go-ba. Ko nam ná ye balo na vei ba dale dam jei de gugworru wone to, jawe-chɛɛro mo wó go-ba. 28Amo nam wó pa se ba teo kom maama taa tigi di-dwonnu yerane, se ba dam dem ba na teere de baŋa ne to ji kafɛ. Isarele teo peero jei sem wó ji kagoa ka taa tiga, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o tɔge dáane o kɛ. 29Konto baŋa ne ba wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom, ne a ná pɛ se ba teo kom ji di-dwonnu, wo-zɔɔna yalo ba na jege ba ke to ŋwaane.’
30Ko daare nmo nabiinu, nmo dwi tiina bam yeini ba jeeri daane mo á teo kabiri sem teiŋa ne, de ba sam manchwo-nia ne, ba waase ba bere daane ba we, ‘Pa-na se dé vo Ezekeli tei, se dé ni Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam o na jege se o pa debam to.’ 31Ba maa yeini ba tui nmo tei de kɔgɔ, ye ba cheigi n taane dem, ne ko na maŋe de a nɔɔna bam na ke tei to. Ba nam ba lage se ba toŋe ba tɔge a taane dem na bere tei to. Swono taane wo ba nia ne. Ba fera nam wo wonnu telo na wó pa ba duni to wone mo. 32Ta‑n yei we banto pae n ye gɔgɔ kolo na leeni lei selo na bere swono taane to mo. Ba maa sɛ we n jege kwor-ywoŋa, ye n yei kɔnɔ tam lanyerane. Ba swoi se ba taa cheigi n kwora kam. Ba nam ba toŋe ba tɔge ka na bere tei to. 33Wonnu telo a na tage to nam wó seene te ke. Maŋa kam konto ne mo ba wó lɔre we Wɛ sampwora ya wo ba tetare ne.”

english_text:
Israel's Leaders Are Worthless Shepherds
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them:
I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep. 3You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock! 4You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep. 5 They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals. 6So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
7-8Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep. 9-10So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
11The Lord God then said:
I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself, 12just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them 13and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields. 14They will be safe as they feed on grassy meadows and green hills. 15I promise to take care of them and keep them safe, 16to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right.
Judgment on the Strong Sheep
17The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel:
I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak. 18Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy. 19That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
20So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak. 21You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak, 22but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
23 After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you. 24 He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep
The Lord God said:
25The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid. 26They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain 27to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord. 28Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear. 29I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners. 30Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise. 31They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
translation_text:
Nayera de ba pei taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma pa-ne o kwora o we:
2“Nabiinu, pworisi taane n chɔge Isarele teo yiga tiina balo na nii a nɔɔna bam baŋa ne to. Nam ta de-ba we: ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Lɛɛro taa wo á baŋa ne! Nayera jege se ba taa nii ba pei sem baŋa ne mo. Ko dae konto na? Abam nam nii á tete baŋa ne mo. 3Á swoi se á ta-á di á pei lara kam, ye á kwei se koro tem á sɔ gwaaro á ma á kwoli á tete. Á ma daare á kuri vare-laaro tem á go á pa á tete, ye á yiga laam tere pei sem wone. 4Á wo nii ko baŋa ne se á ta‑á cho pei selo na bwona to se se na dam. Á ta maa wo yɔɔre vare-jaweena bam, se á daare á vɔ balo na nɛ zonne to ŋɔna yam. Abam chem mo ye á pei sem ywori se maa jia. Selo maa na jei to, á wo beeri-se se á ja á jwoori. Abam nam bɛɛse pei-kɔgɔ kom de je-chɛa mo. 5Ko maa pa se se jage jei maama, se na ba jege nayero se kotu taa nii se baŋa ne to ŋwaane. Se na jage konto to, se laam ma ji kago-vara dwi maama ni-wodiu. 6Amo pei sem yɔɔre se jage mo se yi tega baŋa ni maama. Se maa kare zwonnu de peero maama yuni ne se kekara, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo ke o yiga se wone se kotu beeri se jei.
7Konto ŋwaane, abam balo na nii a nɔɔna bam baŋa ne ne nayera na ke tei to, cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam: 8Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a dwoni de abam mo. Kokuri to, a pei-kɔgɔ kom gɛ nayero pa kago-vara jege-se ba tore ba di. A nayera bam nam wo beeri amo pei selo na tusi chwoŋa to jei, ye ba yɔɔre ba nii ba tete mo, pa ba yiga tere amo pei sem wone. 9Konto ŋwaane, abam nayera bam, nam cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam. 10Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo dwoni de nayera bam mo. A maa wó bwei-ba de ba na ke a pei sem tei to. Amo wó jwoŋi a pei sem a daare-ba se ba daa yé taa nii-se. Nayera bam daa bá na chwoŋa se ba kɔne pei sem, naa se ba taa kɔne ba tete pei sem baŋa ne. Ba daa bá done pei sem nɔna.
11Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo tete mo lage a nwoŋi a beeri a pei sem jei se a taa nii se baŋa ne. 12Ne nayero na beeri o pei selo na jage pwola ne tei to, konto mo amo de wó taa nii a pei sem baŋa ne. Amo pei sem déem yɔɔre se jage mo dɛ delo ne kunkwon-lilirru na tu te li tega kam maama to. A nam wó beeri se jei ye a jwoŋi-se a yage. 13Amo wó ja-ba a nwoŋi teene dedwonna dem ne se a la-ba a ke daane, ye a pa ba jwoori ba tete tega kam ne. Amo laam maa wó kale-se se se na gaaro se di Isarele peero jei sem ne, de bwollu tem ne, de jei selo maama nɔɔna na zoore da to. 14A lage a taa yere-se se se taa di ga-zuru mo Isarele peero tem yuni ne. Se wó taa tigi ga-zuru jei ne mo, ye se taa di se boboŋa Isarele teo peero tem ne. 15Amo tete nam mo lage a taa nii a pei sem baŋa ne, ye a daare a pa se taa tigi tega ne de bochare-zuru. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. 16Amo ta wó beeri pei selo na jei to mo, se a daare a kale selo na ywori chwoŋa to a ja a jwoori. A maa wó vɔ pei selo na nɛ fufwollu to ŋwana se ya jei, se a daare a taa cho selo na bwona to se se na dam. Ko daare, ko ná ye pei selo na nugi bigila bigila ye se dana to, a lage a go-se mo. Amo wó taa kɔne a pei sem ko chwoŋa kam ne mo.
17Ko nam ná ye abam na ye amo pei sem to, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Ta‑á yei-na we amo lage a bore taane pia de ka dwoŋi tetare ne, ye a daare a pɔɔre pi-bale de bo-bale daane mo. 18Abam na nɛ ga-zuru se á ta‑á di to, ko ta wo maŋe ko pa abam na? Bɛŋwaane mo á yɔɔre á titirigi gaao kom ne, ye á jege-ko á nɔne á chɔga? Abam wo ba tigi de na-zura balo á na jege á nyɔ to mo pa se á jege na bam á pɔgele na? 19Amo pei sesem sem daa bá na ga-zuru se di, ko ná dae gaao kolo abam na nɔne á chɔge to. Se maa jege se se nyɔ na balo abam á pɔgele pa ba ji bworu yerane to mo.
20Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei de pei sem to mo tento: Amo tete mo lage a bore pei selo na nugi to de selo na kwaare to daane. 21Abam kwei á vɔna mo á yigi pei selo na bwona to, ye á daare á chu-se de á nyea se á zeili-se pa se jage se kɛ se wo dáa dáa. 22Konto ŋwaane amo wó jwoŋi a pei sem a yage, se se daa yé na bɛɛsem. A ta wó bore pia de ka dwoŋi taane. 23A laam maa wó le nɔɔno dedoa se wonto ji a nɔɔna bam maama nayero. A tontoŋeno David mo konto. O maa wó kɔne-ba ye o ta nii ba baŋa ne. 24Amo Baŋa Wɛ tete wó taa ye ba Tu Wɛ wom. A tontoŋeno David maa wó taa ye ba maama dedɛɛro. Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.
25Amo wó gwoni ni de-ba bochare-zuru ŋwaane, ye a daare a zeili kago-vara dwi maama ba tega kam ne. Konto maa wó pa-ba pwola se ba taa zoore gaao ne, naa ba peini goa wone, ye foone bá taa jege-ba. 26Amo nam wó swɛ ba swolim, se de yi jei selo maama na kaare amo tete peo kom to. A maa wó pa se do-mimina taa nena ka maŋa ne chekke. Do-mimina kam konto mo wó ja swolim ka pa-ba. 27Konto mo wó pa ba teeni dem lei bia lanyerane, ye tega kam de ke wodiiru dedɛ ka pa-ba. Nɔɔna bam maama wó taa jei ba teo kom ne ye kolokolo ba daane-ba. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, ne a ná jaane nabɛ yɔgese delo ba dona na de ba ba ne to a bwori a yage pa ba nwoŋi ba kabɛɛne ne. 28Dwi-gɛ tiina daa bá ba ba vere-ba. Kago-vara de nam daa bá ja-ba ba tore ba di. Ba wó taa jei ba teo ne de yazura mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá fugi-ba. 29A maa wó pa-ba te-ywoŋa se ba jeini ka baŋa ne ba va. Konto wó pa se kana daa yé ja-ba, se dwi-gɛ tiina bam taa jege-ba ba yaala. 30Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo wolo na ye ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom to wo ba tei ne, ye banto Isarele dwi tiina bam de maa ye amo nɔɔna. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. 31A maa yeini a nii abam baŋa ne, ne nayero na nii o pei-kɔgɔ tei to, ye á ye nabiina. Á ye amo nɔɔna mo, ye amo de ye abam Wɛ. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ”

english_text:
Edom Will Be a Wasteland
1 The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom 3and say to them:
I, the Lord God,
am now your enemy!
And I will turn your nation
into an empty wasteland,
4leaving your towns in ruins.
Your land will be a desert,
and then you will know
that I am the Lord.
5People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins. 6And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death. 7I will destroy your nation and kill anyone who travels through it. 8Dead bodies will cover your mountains and fill up your valleys, 9and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
10You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God, 11and as surely as I live, I will punish you for treating my people with anger and hatred. Then they will know that I, the Lord, am punishing you! 12And you will finally realize that I heard you laugh at their destruction and say their land was yours to take. 13You even insulted me, but I heard it all.
14Everyone on earth will celebrate when I destroy you, 15just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
translation_text:
Edom teo taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ma yi amo we:
2“Nabiinu, pipiri n yibia n jeeri Seyira peo kom se n pworisi n chɔge-ko 3n ta we, ‘Seyira peo, amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ dwoni dede‑m mo. A nam wó twe a jeŋa a jeeri‑m se n ji kagoa n ta‑n tiga. 4A lage a pa se nmo teene dem maama mo ji di-dwonnu de taa zega, se n laŋa kam ji kagoa. Nmo laam ma‑n wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.
5Ko zege faŋa kam ne mo abam jege sebaŋa á ke de Isarele tiina bam. Á ma da ko ŋwaane á dole-ba á yage se ba te jara wone, maŋa kalo ne lɛɛro na tiini te yi-ba ye ba yɔɔre ba na waarem ba ti to. 6Konto ŋwaane, ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a lage a pa chwoŋa mo se nɔɔna yɔɔre ba go abam. Abam bá lu de á ŋwea, á na maŋe á swoi nɔn-gora kikia to ŋwaane. 7Amo wó pa Seyira peero jei sem ji kagoa ka taa tiga, ye a daare a go balo maama na tɔge jei sem konto ne ba kɛ to. 8Twa yerane mo lage ba faare abam peero tem yuu. Balo na tege jara wone to wó taa tigi a zwonnu baŋa ne, de á bwollu tem, de á gugworru tem tega ne. 9A lage a pa á teo kom ji kagoa mo se ko taa vei wuu. Nɔɔna daa bá taa zoore á teene dem wone. Abam laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.
10Abam nam tage á tete ne we, “Debam mo wó jwoŋi Judah teo de Isarele teo, de ba tega kam maama dé taa tei.” Á tage konto dwoŋi ye amo Baŋa Wɛ nam wo ba tei ne. 11Konto ŋwaane, ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a lage a waare abam mo se ko maŋe de á na tiini á ke bane de puseŋa tei amo nɔɔna bam baŋa ne, ye á ta done-ba tei to. Amo laam maa wó veere a tete de-ba, ne a ná waare abam a ti. 12Abam de maa wó lɔre we amo Baŋa Wɛ nigi á ta-yɔɔro tem, de abam na yaale Isarele peero tem tei to. Abam maŋe á ta te taane we, “Jei sem konto jigi kagoa mo, pa se dé na chwoŋa se dé wane-ba dé di.” 13Á bere á tete kamunim mo amo yiga ne, ye á daare á ŋɔɔne ta-balwaaro dedɛ á ma á chɔge-ne. Amo nam nigi te maama. 14Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: A lage a pa á teo kom maama chɔge mo, se logo baŋa nɔɔna maama taa chaka. 15Ne nmo de déem na chake maŋa kalo ne Isarele dwi tiina bam de ba tega kam maama na nɛ chɔgem to, konto mo amo de lage a ke abam. Seyira peero jei sem de Edom laŋa kam maama lage te chɔge te ji di-dwonnu yerane mo. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.’ ”

english_text:
A Message for Israel's Mountains
1The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel 2that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them. 3They ruined and crushed you from every side, and foreign nations captured and made fun of you. 4So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you. 5But in my fierce anger, I will turn against those nations, and especially the Edomites, because they laughed at you the loudest and took over your pasturelands. 6You have suffered long enough, and, I, the Lord God, am very angry! Nations have insulted you, 7so I will now insult and disgrace them. That is my solemn promise.
