Amo laam maa wó sɛ se á ta‑á ye a nɔɔna bam. Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_text:
The East Gate Must Remain Closed
1The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed. 2The Lord said:
I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it. 3The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate.
People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
4Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
5The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not. 6Tell those rebellious people of Israel:
I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways! 7My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement. 8Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
9And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel.
The Levites Are Punished
The Lord said:
10Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished! 11They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers. 12But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning, 13and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins. 14They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple.
Rules for Priests
The Lord said:
15The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices. 16They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
17 When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple. 18Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work. 19 And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
20 Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long. 21 They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
22 A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
23 Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean. 24They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
25 Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister. 26If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later, 27he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
28 I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own. 29 Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me. 30The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
31 Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_text:
Wɛ diga kam chullu tedwonna
1Nɔɔno wom daa ma ja-ne pa dé vo dé yi Wɛ diga kam konkɔlɔ ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to. De nam ya pe mo. 2Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we, “Ni dento wó yɔɔre de pe mo de taa zega. Ba daa bá pore-de. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá tɔge da o zo wara-jei sem wone, kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to mo tɔge ni dem konto o zo da. Konto ŋwaane mo de wó pe de taa zega taa wuu. 3Isarele teo dedɛɛro wom yerane mo jege chwoŋa se o vo o jeini ni dem diga dedoa ne o di wodiu amo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. O nam jege se o tɔge ni dem napɔrɔ kom ne mo o zo da, ye o daare o tɔge chwoŋa kam konto o nwoŋi.”
4Nɔɔno wom ma ja-ne pa dé tɔge baŋa seeni ni dem ne dé vo dé zaŋe Wɛ diga kam yiga ne. Amo ma nii a na Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom na su Wɛ diga kam ni maama tei to. A ma to a vwi a yibia tega ne.
5 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu, fɔge n nii lanyerane, se n cheigi kolo maama a na lage a bere‑m Baŋa Wɛ diga kam chullu tem seeni to se n kwei-te n ke n yuu ne. Ta maane ka nia yam na ye tei to de balo na jege chwoŋa se ba taa tɔge-ya ba zoore wara-jei sem ba daare ba nwoŋi to. 6Nam ta de Isarele dwi zwabani-nyena bam we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam Isarele dwi tiina bam, yage-na á totoŋ-vɛɛsa yam! 7Abam jaane sa-teena balo na yɔɔre ba yeiri amo ye ba boboŋa kwaale to mo á ja á zo amo wara-jei sem ne, ne á ná yeini á kwei wodiu pɛɛra, de vara lara, de ba jana á ma á ke kaanem á pa amo. Á ma da ko ŋwaane á biini amo Wɛ diga kam, ye á chɔge ni delo amo na gwoni de abam to. Á yeini á ke konto dwoŋi mo á woli á totoŋ-vɛɛsa yadwonna yam wone. 8Ko ná ye pɛɛra yalo na ye wose amo ŋwaane to, abam wo fɔge á nii ya baŋa ne. Á nam kwei sa-teena mo á pa ba jege amo wara-jei sem totoŋa ba toŋa ba pa abam. 9Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Sa-teena balo na yeiri amo to ba jege chwoŋa se ba zo amo wara-jei sem ne, de balo na zoore Isarele tiina bam tetare ne to de.
10Levi dwi tiina bam badwonna déem yage amo. Ba ma gwaane Isarele tiina badaara bam wone pa ba ywori chwoŋa ba daare amo ye ba zuli jwona. Ba wɛleera yam konto wó taa wo ba yuu ne se ba na waarem. 11Amo nam wó pa-ba chwoŋa se ba taa toŋe amo wara-jei sem ne. Ba wó taa yere Wɛ diga kam nia yam. Ba ta wó taa goe vara balo nɔɔna na jaane ba tui se ba maa ke zwɛɛm kaanem de kaanem dwi maama to, ye ba daare ba taa zege nɔɔna bam yiga ne ba woli-ba Wɛ zula seeni. 12Ba nam na toŋe ba pa Isarele dwi tiina bam jwona kaanem baŋa ne mo ye ba pa ba tusi to ŋwaane, amo nam dugi de a tete yere we a wó waare-ba ba wɛleera yam ŋwaane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. 13A nam bá pa-ba chwoŋa se ba fɔɔre ba twɛ amo se ba taa toŋa kaanem tiina totoŋa ba pa-ne. Ba ta yé twɛ wonnu telo a na pɔɔre-te se te taa ye wose amo ŋwaane to. Ba nam wó di ba chaveera mo totoŋ-zɔɔna yalo ba na ke to ŋwaane. 14De ko de, a lage a kwei Wɛ diga kam totoŋa dwi maama mo a ke banto jeŋa ne se ba taa nii ya baŋa ne.
15Ko daare Levi dwi tiina balo na ye kaanem tiina ye ba nwoŋi Zadoki diga kam ne to, banto mo yɔɔre ba nii amo wara-jei sem totoŋa baŋa ne ba pa-ne maŋa kalo Isarele tiina badaara bam na ywori ba chwoŋa ne to. Banto mo wó fɔɔre ba twɛ amo se ba taa toŋe a kaanem totoŋa yam, ye ba yeini ba kwei vara lara, de jana ba ke kaanem ba pa-ne. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. 16Banto ta wó wane ba zo amo diga kam wone, se ba ke kaanem amo bimbini dem baŋa ne, ye ba toŋe ba pa-ne. Banto nam mo wó ke amo boboŋa yam na lage tei to.
17Ba ná yeini ba zo Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone, ba jege se ba kwei gare-fefale mo ba zo. Ko dae se ba zo pei koro gwaaro se ba ma-te ba toŋe wara-jei konkɔlɔ kom wone, naa Wɛ diga kam tete wone. 18Ba jege se ba yeini ba kwei gare-fefale mo ba ba ba yuni tem, ye ba daare ba vɔ gare-kuri-kukwi ba tei ne. Ko nam dae se ba vɔ ba tete de gwaaro telo na wó pa ba taa chuuri de luluŋu to. 19Ba nam ná nwoŋi wara-jei sem ne se ba vo ba yi da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom mɛ nɔɔna bam na gilimi to, ba wó lɔɔre gwaaro telo ba na zo ba maa toŋe Wɛ diga kam totoŋa to mo ba tiŋi di selo na pɔɔre Wɛ ŋwaane to wone, se ba laam jwoori ba kwei gwaaro tedwonna ba zo. Ba ná ke konto, nɔɔna bam bá wane ba dwei ba gwaaro tem se ko pa ba de ji wose.
20Wɛ kaanem tiina bam nam dae se ba cheeri ba yuni, naa se ba yage ba yu-ywei se se ke dedwaaro. Ba nam wó wane ba dɔɔre ba yu-ywei sem ba yage. 21Ba wolowolo nam yé nyɔ sana ye o daare o zo Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone. 22Ba dae se ba di kadeina ba ma ke ba kaana, naa kaana balo de ba banna na yage daane to. Banto nam jege se ba di Isarele tiina bukwa balo na yeiri baara to yerane mo, naa kaanem tiina badwonna kadeina. 23Banto totoŋe mo ye se ba bere a nɔɔna bam se ba taa wae ba pɔɔre wonnu telo na ye wose to, de telo na wora dɛ dɛ totoŋa ŋwaane to daane. Ba ta wó pa ba taa wae ba pɔɔre wonnu telo na maŋe de Wɛ chullu tem to, de telo na jege digiru chullu tem seeni to daane.
24Taane ná wo amo nɔɔna bam laŋa ne, ko ye kaanem tiina bam mo wó kwei amo nia yam ba ma bore chega ba tetare ne. Ba ta wó nii se a nia yam na bere se nɔɔna bam taa di kura yalo to seene ya taa toŋa. Ba ta wó taa nege a siu da yam, se nɔɔna taa pae ya ye ya yera.
25Kaanem tu dae se o twɛ too yera, kokuri, o ná dwei too yera, ko wó pa o digiri o tete chullu tem seeni mo. Ko nam ná ye o kwo naa o nu mo tega, naa o bia wone dedoa, naa o zembaaro, naa o nyaane, naa o nakɔ ta na wo zo baro mo ná tega, o jege chwoŋa se o dwei kotu yera yam. 26O nam ná dwei too yera, o laam wó kwɛ o tete se o jwoori o maŋe de chullu tem. O ná ke konto o ti, se o daare o pa da yarepɛ kɛ. 27O laam jege chwoŋa se o zo Wɛ diga kam tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone se o toŋe wara-jei sem ne. Dɛ dem konto ne o wó ke wɛleera saarem kaanem o tete ŋwaane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
28Yé pɔɔre-na Isarele tega kam wone á pa kaanem tiina bam. Amo Baŋa Wɛ tete yerane mo wó taa ye ba nyɔn-mage nyem. Amo tete mo yɔɔre a maŋe a pa-ba. 29Ko na ye tei to, wodiu pɛɛra, de wɛleere saarem pɛɛra, de wɛleere jene pɛɛra, de wonnu telo maama Isarele tiina bam na jaane ba tui ba ke amo jeŋa ne to ye banto nyem mo. 30Abam wodiiru telo na lwoori yiga te ke ye te lamma to, dedaane á Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra dwi dwi wó taa ye kaanem tiina bam nyem mo. Á ta wó kwei mun-bwei delo á na bobo á pɔɔre se á ma á fɔge bworobworo to á pa kaanem tiina bam, se Wɛ swolim taa wo á sam dem baŋa ne. 31Kaanem tiina ba jege chwoŋa se ba di woŋo kolo na tege ko tete toone, naa vara na jaane-ko ba tore to. Ko ná maŋe ko ye zuŋa mo, naa varem mo de, ba yé di-te.

english_text:
The Lord's Sacred Land
The Lord said:
1When the land of Israel is divided among the twelve tribes, you must set aside an area that will belong to me. This sacred area will be 12.5 kilometers long and 10 kilometers wide. 2The temple will be on a piece of land 255 meters square, and the temple will be completely surrounded by an open space 25 meters wide.
3-4I will give half of my sacred land, a section 12.5 kilometers long and 5 kilometers wide, to the priests who serve in the temple. Their houses will be in this half, as well as my temple, which is the most sacred place of all.
5I will give the other half of my land to the Levites who work in my temple, and the towns where they will live will be there.
6Next to my sacred land will be an area 12.5 kilometers long and 3 kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem.
Land for Israel's Ruler
The Lord said:
7-8The regions west and east of my sacred land and the city of Jerusalem will belong to the ruler of Israel. He will be given the region between the western edge of my land and the Mediterranean Sea, and between the eastern edge of my land and the Jordan River. This will mean that the length of his property will be the same as the sections of land given to the tribes.
This property will belong to every ruler of Israel, so they will always be fair to my people and will let them live peacefully in the land given to their tribes.
Israel's Rulers Must Be Honest
9The Lord God said:
You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
10 So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures. 11The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
12The standard unit of weight will be the shekel. One shekel will equal 20 gerahs, and 60 shekels will equal one mina.
13Leaders of Israel, the people must bring you one sixtieth of their grain harvests as offerings to me. 14They will also bring one percent of their olive oil. These things will be measured according to the bath, and ten baths is the same as one homer or one cor. 15Finally, they must bring one sheep out of every 200 from their flocks.
These offerings will be used as grain sacrifices, as well as sacrifices to please me and those to ask my blessing. I, the Lord, will be pleased with these sacrifices and will forgive the sins of my people.
16The people of Israel will bring you these offerings. 17But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people.
The Festivals
(Exodus 12.1-20; Leviticus 23.33-43)
18The Lord God said:
On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple. 19The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
20The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
21 Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast. 22On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people. 23Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them. 24He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
25 The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
translation_text:
Ba na wó pɔɔre tega kam tei to
1Abam ná lage á pɔɔre tega kam á pa Isarele dwia yam se ba taa tei, á jege se á le pwola se ka taa ye ka yera amo Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane. Ka wó taa ye naba-laara 12,500 mo dedɔrem baŋa ne, de naba-laara 10,000 ka kayɔlɔ baŋa ne. Pwola kam maama wó taa ye wose mo amo ŋwaane. 2Pwola kam konto ne á wó pɔɔre naba-laara 250 mo dedɔrem baŋa ne de kayɔlɔ baŋa ne se á ma á lɔ Wɛ diga kam da. Kapworo wó taa tigi ko kaare-ka, ye ko kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem ye naba-laara finlei-benu (25). 3Ta pɔɔre-na pwola kalo na ye ka yera to belei, se á maŋe naba-laara 12,500 dedɔrem baŋa ne, de naba-laara 5,000 kayɔlɔ baŋa ne. Jei sem konto á na wó maŋe to mo á wó ke Wɛ diga kam na tiini ka ye wose Wɛ ŋwaane to da. 4Pwola kam chicheiro kom konto wó taa ye tega kalo na pɔɔre amo ŋwaane to. Dáane mo kaanem tiina bam wó taa tei, de ba na toŋe Wɛ diga totoŋa yam ye ba fɔɔre ba twɛ Baŋa Wɛ tei se ba toŋe ba pa‑o to. Ba wó lɔ ba sam dem dáane mo, ye dáane mo Wɛ tete diga kam de maa wó taa wora. 5Pwola kam chicheiro kolo na daare to de wó taa ye naba-laara 12,500 dedɔrem baŋa ne, de naba-laara 5,000 kayɔlɔ baŋa ne. Tega kam konto wó taa ye Levi dwi tiina bam nyem mo, ba na toŋe Wɛ wara-jei sem wone to ŋwaane. Ba wó taa tei-ka pa se teene taa wora se ba taa zoore de wone.
6Ko ta ná ye tega kalo abam na wó lɔ teo kom tete ka baŋa ne to, á wó maŋe laŋa kalo na ye naba-laara 2,500 kayɔlɔ baŋa ne de naba-laara 12,500 dedɔrem baŋa ne to, pa se ka saŋe pwola kalo na ye ka yera amo ŋwaane to. Laŋa kam konto wó taa ye Isarele tiina bam maama nyem mo.
7Isarele teo dedɛɛro wom nam mo wó taa tei tega kadwoŋi, ka na twoŋi de pwola kalo na ye ka yera amo ŋwaane to, ye ka ta twoŋi de tega kalo na ye teo kom nyem to. O laŋa kam maa wó zege amo pwola kam wɛ-zoore seeni ka vo ka yi tega kam maama wɛ-zoore seeni siseini dem, ye ka zege amo pwola kam wɛ-puli seeni ka vo ka yi tega kam maama wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem. Ko maa bere we o tega kam wó taa dɔra ka mae de Isarele dwia yadwonna yam tega na mae tei to mo. 8Tega kam konto maa wó lɛɛre ka taa ye dedɛɛro wom nyem mo Isarele teo kom ne. Konto to, a dedɛɛra bam daa bá taa jege a nɔɔna bam ba bɛɛsa. Ba nam wó yage Isarele tiina bam mo se dwi maama jwoŋi de tega de taa tei.
9Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam Isarele teo dedɛɛra bam, á tiini á pini amo nɔɔna bam, ye á daare á bɛɛse-ba se ko dáane. Nam yage-na vuvuga totoŋa, se á daare á toŋe kolo na ye chega ye ko tɔge chwoŋa to. Á daa yé vere tega amo nɔɔna bam tei ne se á daare-ba á zege bwori. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. 10Abam ná lage á maŋe wonnu á pa daane, se á kwei bwɛ selo na ye chekke to á maŋe-te. 11Kuriwɛ selo á na wó ta‑á mae á maŋe wonnu to jege se se taa ye chekke mo, ne ko ná ye muni mo á jege á maŋa, naa ko ná ye na mo de. Kuriwaa bia fuga mo wó yi homaa dedoa. 12Á nam ná maŋe wonnu se á lɔre te dunni na ye tei to, se á maŋe gɛra kuni finlei se te taa ye sɛkɛle dedoa. Sɛkɛla fuseredo (60) de maa wó taa ye mina dedoa.
Wɛ pɛɛra de kura taane
13Pɛɛra yalo á na jege se á kwei á pa Wɛ to mo tento: Maŋe-na á mena bwɛ fuseredo maama wone se á le dedoa. 14Á ta wó ma kuriwaa mo á maŋe á nuga kam, se á le bwɛ selei kuriwaa bia fuga maama wone. Kuriwaa bia fuga ye bedwe mo de homaa dedoa 15Ko ta ná ye abam pei sem na di gaao Isarele te-ywoŋa kam ne to, á wó le pia dedoa mo se bia yalei maama wone. Ba maa wó kwei pɛɛra yam konto ba ma ba ke wodiu pɛɛra, de zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de nu-biu pɛɛra kaanem, se ba tɔge ya ŋwaane ba le nɔɔna bam wɛleera Wɛ yiga ne. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. 16Isarele tiina bam maama nam mo wó ja pɛɛra yam konto ba ba ba ke ba teo kom dedɛɛro wom jeŋa ne. 17Dedɛɛro wom nam jege se o beeri vara balo ba na wó kwei ba ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de wodiu pɛɛra, de wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛra, ne nɔɔna bam ná lage ba di ba kura dwi dwi. Ko ná ye ba chan-doŋa kura, de ba siu da yam, dedaane kura yalo maama Isarele dwi tiina bam na jege se ba di to, wonto mo wó beeri wɛleere saarem kaanem vara bam, de wodiu pɛɛra yam, de pɛɛra yalo ba na wó zwɛ ba pa Wɛ to, de nu-biu pɛɛra yam se ba kwei ba maa ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ se ba le nɔɔna bam lwarem o yiga ne.
18Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Boboa chana kam boboa dɛ dem ne, se á kwei na-bala kalo na ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to á ma á kwɛ wara-jei sem. 19Kaanem tu wom maa wó pwori wɛleere saarem kaanem varem wom jana wone o ja o vo o taare Wɛ diga kam manchwo-nia sɛ sem ne. O ta wó kwei-ba o ke bimbini dem tetare seeni nia yana yam ne, de Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom ni-kaywallo tem ne. 20Ko ta ná yeini ko yi chana kam da yarepɛ dɛ dem, nmo nam ta wó ke konto dwoŋi mo se n ma n kwɛ wolo maama na tusi ye o wo paale o ke wɛleere, naa o wo lɔre ko ni ne to. Konto maa wó pa se n fɔge n kwɛ Wɛ diga kam chullu tem seeni.
21Boboa chana kam da fuga-yana dɛ dem ne, se á di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem. Kwei-na da yarepɛ á di-de, se da yam konto ne á ta‑á di bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to. 22Kuri dem boboa dɛ dem ne, á teo dedɛɛro wom wó beeri na-bala mo se ba kwei-ka ba ma ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem o tete ŋwaane, de teo kom nɔɔna bam maama ŋwaane. 23Da yarepɛ yam dɛ maama wone o nam ta wó beeri na-bale serepɛ, de pi-bɛ serepɛ, te maama na ba jege gɛɛ te yera ne to mo, se ba kwei-te ba ke zwɛɛm kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. O ta maa wó beeri bo-bala se ba kwei-ka ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem. 24O nam ta wó taa jege muni mo o woli da se ba ma ba ke wodiu pɛɛre kaanem. Ko wó taa ye muni kuriwaa bu dedoa na-bala maama ŋwaane, de kuriwaa bu dedoa pi-bɛ maama ŋwaane. Nuga bwɛ sena nam mo wó woli de muni kuriwaa maama.
25Ko ta ná ye kuri delo na bobo chane serepɛ chana kam da fuga-yanu dɛ dem ne to, kuri dento da yarepɛ yam dɛ maama wone o daa wó beeri pɛɛra mo se ba ma-ya ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem, de zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem, de wodiu pɛɛre kaanem, se nuga de woli te wone.

english_text:
Various Laws for the Ruler and the People
1The Lord said:
The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened. 2Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
3Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me. 4On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals. 5With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
6The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals. 7With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain. 8The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
9When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate. 10Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
11At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
12If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
13Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me. 14Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change— 15the lamb, the flour, and the olive oil will be offered to me every morning for all time.
Laws about the Ruler's Land
16The Lord God said:
If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property. 17 But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
18The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him.
The Sacred Kitchens
19The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard 20and said, “These are the kitchens where the priests must boil the meat to be offered as sacrifices to make things right and as sacrifices for sin. They will also bake the grain for sacrifices in these kitchens. That way, these sacred offerings won't have to be carried through the outer courtyard, where someone could accidentally touch them and be harmed.”
21We went back to the outer courtyard and walked past the four corners. 22At each corner I saw a smaller courtyard, 20 meters long and 15 meters wide. 23Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires. 24The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_text:
1Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to ye se á pe-de mo á totoŋa da yaredo maama wone. Ko maa ná yi siu dɛ dem, dedaane chan-doŋa dɛ dem ne, se á laam pore-de á yage. 2Teo kom dedɛɛro wom maa wó zege da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom ne o vo o zo ni dem konto napɔrɔ kom wone se o taa zege manchwoŋo ni dem ne. Kaanem tiina bam maa wó kwei o zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de o yazura pɛɛra ba ma ba ke kaanem. Dedɛɛro wom ta ná zege manchwoŋo ni dem ne, o wó chɔɔle o yibia tega ne se o zuli-ne, ye o daare o nwoŋi da o viiri. Ba nam bá pe ni dem, se tega ná tu ka yi, se ba laam pe-de. 3Siu da yam de chan-doŋa da yam maama ne, teo kom nɔɔna bam nam jege se ba gilimi daane ni dem konto yiga ne mo, se ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. 4Dedɛɛro wom na jege se o ja zwɛɛm pɛɛre delo siu dɛ maama ne o ba o ke o pa Baŋa Wɛ to nam wó taa ye pi-bale seredo, de pi-bea dedoa mo. Tento maama nam bá taa jege gɛɛ te yera ne. 5Wodiu pɛɛre delo o na woli pi-bea kam wone se o ma o ke kaanem dem to wó taa ye kuriwaa bu dedoa mo. Muni delo o na wó kwei o woli pi-bale sem ne to nam wó maŋe de o na lage tei to mo. O nam wó woli nuga bwɛ sena mo muni kuriwaa maama ŋwaane. 6Chan-doŋa dɛ dem ne dedɛɛro wom ta wó kwei na-bala dedoa, de pi-bale seredo, de pi-bea dedoa se o ma o ke kaanem, te maama na ba jege gɛɛ te yera ne to. 7O ta wó ja wodiu pɛɛre kuriwaa bu dedoa na-bala kam ŋwaane, de wodiu pɛɛre kuriwaa bu dedoa pi-bea kam ŋwaane. Ko nam ná ye pi-bale sem, o wó woli wodiu pɛɛre se ko maŋe de o na lage tei to mo. O ta wó woli nuga bwɛ sena mo kuriwaa maama ŋwaane. 8Dedɛɛro wom ná yeini o zo manchwoŋo ni dem, o wó tɔge napɔrɔ kom ne mo o zo da. O ta ná lage o nwoŋi, ko ye se o jwoori o tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo.
9Teo kom nɔɔna ná yeini ba jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se ba di ba kura yam, se ba na tɔge ni delo ba zo to, ba da ni dedwoŋi ne ba nwoŋi wara-jei sem wone. Ba wolo ná dɛ baŋa seeni ni dem o zo, kotu wó tɔge tega-kuri seeni ni dem ne mo o nwoŋi. Wolo nam na tɔge tega-kuri seeni ni dem o zo, kotu de wó da baŋa seeni ni dem ne mo o nwoŋi. 10Ba ná yeini ba zo da, dedɛɛro wom de maa wó gwaane ba wone, ye o ta tɔge de-ba o nwoŋi.
11Ba ná yeini ba jege ba kura yam dwi maama ba di, wodiu pɛɛre dem wó taa ye muni kuriwaa bu dedoa mo na-bala maama ŋwaane, de kuriwaa bu dedoa pi-bea maama ŋwaane. Ko daare ko ná ye pi-bale sem, wodiu pɛɛre dem na woli da to wó maŋe de nɔɔno boboŋa na lage tei to mo. Ba ta wó woli nuga bwɛ sena mo kuriwaa maama ŋwaane. 12Dedɛɛro wom ná boŋe se o ke wo-ywoŋo pɛɛre o pa Baŋa Wɛ, ne ko ná ye zwɛɛm pɛɛre naa nu-biu pɛɛre mo, se ba pore ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to ba pa‑o. O maa wó ke o zwɛɛm pɛɛre dem, naa o nu-biu pɛɛre dem, ne ko na maŋe ko ke tei siu dɛ dem ne to mo. Ko kwaga seeni o ná nwoŋi se o viiri, ba laam wó wane ni dem ba pe.
13Dɛ maama wone nmo jege se n beeri pi-bala na yi bene ye ka ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to se n ma-ka n ke zwɛɛm pɛɛre n pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ko nam ye zezeŋa maama mo nmo wó ta‑n ke konto. 14Zezeŋa maama se n yeini n ke wodiu pɛɛre n woli da. Pɛɛre dem n na wó ke n pa Baŋa Wɛ to ye muni bwɛ setɔ mo, ye n guuri nuga bɔŋa dedoa de wone. Ni dento ba jege se de leiri maŋa de maŋa. 15Ko maa na ye tei to, pi-bala kam, de wodiu pɛɛre dem, de nuga kalo na woli de wone to ye se á ta‑á beeri-te mo zezeŋa maama se á yeini á ma-te á ke zwɛɛm kaanem maŋa maama ne.
16Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Teo dedɛɛro wom ná pɔɔre ba dwi tega kam wone se ko ji pɛɛre ko pa o bu, ka laam wó lɛɛre ka taa ye bu wom de o de kwaga nyem mo. 17Ko daare, o ná kwei-ka o ji pɛɛre mo o pa o tontoŋeno wolo, o tontoŋeno wom wó taa jege-ka o toŋe mo se ko taa nii wonnu yirim bene dem. Maŋa kam konto ná yia, se o tontoŋeno wom jwoori o kwei tega kam o pa dedɛɛro wom, dedɛɛro wom dwi dem mo na tei tega kam to ŋwaane. Ko ye wonto bia yerane mo jege chwoŋa se ba taa tei o tega se ka ji ba nyem. 18Teo dedɛɛro wom nam ba jege chwoŋa se o zeili nɔɔna ba tega ne se o daare-ba o zege bwori. O nam wó nii o tete tega wone o pɔɔre o pa o bia, se ba de ba dwi dem taa tei. Ko dae se a nɔɔna bam tega nwoŋi ba jeŋa ne ka daare-ba.’ ”
Kaanem tiina bam kaligwoŋo
19Nɔɔno wom daa ma ja-ne pa dé tɔge Wɛ diga konkɔlɔ manchwo-ni dem dé vo dé yi di selo na pɔɔre se zega Wɛ kaanem tiina bam ŋwaane ye se jeeri baŋa seeni to. O ma bere-ne jei selo na yeiri di sem konto wɛ-zoore seeni to. 20O laam ma ta de amo o we, “Jei sento ye kaligwoŋo mo ko pa kaanem tiina bam. Dáane mo ba wó yeini ba taa saŋa wɛleere jene kaanem dem, de wɛleere saarem kaanem dem, ye ba daare ba wɔ wodiu pɛɛra yam, se ba yé ja-ya ba zo da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom wone. Ba ya ná ke konto, ko wó wane nɔɔna bam de mo ko pwɛ Wɛ ŋwaane.”
21O daa ma ja-ne o nwoŋi pa dé zo da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom wone, ye o ja-ne o kaare ko gugworru tena tem. A ma na we gugworo maama jege ko konkɔlɔ mo. 22Da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom gugworru tena tem maa jege konkwallo telo maama na mae daane ye kabiri che-te to. Te maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem finna dedɔrem baŋa ne, de jatwogo de noa ni maŋem fintɔ kayɔlɔ baŋa ne. 23Ba déem kwei kandwa mo ba lɔ taara ba kaare konkwallo tem konto, ye ba lɔ mini kura kabiri sem tega kuri seeni. 24O ma ta de amo o we, “Kaligwonnu tento wone mo balo na yeini ba toŋe Wɛ diga kam totoŋa to wó taa saŋe nɔna yalo nɔɔna bam na yeini ba ja ba ba se ba maa ke kaanem to.”

english_text:
The Stream Flowing from the Temple
1 The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
2We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
3The man walked east, then took out his measuring stick and measured 500 meters downstream. He told me to wade through the stream there, and the water came up to my ankles. 4Then he measured another 500 meters downstream, and told me to wade through it there. The water came up to my knees. Another 500 meters downstream the water came up to my waist. 5Another 500 meters downstream, the stream had become a river that could be crossed only by swimming. 6The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.”
We walked to the riverbank, 7where I saw dozens of trees on each side. 8The man said:
This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water. 9Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea. 10From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea. 11But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
12 Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people.
The Borders of the Land
13-14The Lord God said to the people of Israel:
When the land is divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, the Joseph tribe will receive two shares. Divide the land equally, because I promised your ancestors that this land would someday belong to their descendants. These are the borders of the land:
15The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad, 16Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran. 17So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
18The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
19The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
20The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
21That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel. 22It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive 23a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Bu-tola na zege Wɛ diga kam ne ka duri ka vei tei to
1Nɔɔno wom daa ma ja-ne o jwoori Wɛ diga kam ni seeni. A ma nii a na na na bura ni dem kuri ne ba dura ba vei wɛ-puli seeni ba kɛa. Wɛ diga kam yiga déem jeeri wɛ-puli seeni mo. Na bam nwoŋi Wɛ diga kam manchwo-peo tega-kuri seeni mo, ye ba duri ba tɔge kaanem bimbini dem tega-kuri seeni. 2O ta ma pa dé tɔge baŋa seeni ni dem ne, dé bebare dé da pwooni yiga dé vo dé yi ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to. A ma na we na bam maa tae fenfee ba nwoŋi ni dem tega-kuri seeni ba duri ba kɛa.
3Nɔɔno wom ma ja-ne o yɔɔre wɛ-puli seeni ye o zei lɔra ŋona. O ma kwei-ka o maŋe jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni moro. Dé na vei dé yi da to, o ma tɔge a yiga pa dé vei na bam wone se dé bɛ. Ba déem maŋe nakila ne mo. 4O daa ma maŋe se dé vo dé yi jatwogo de noa ni kuni moro kodwoŋi, ye o daa tɔge a yiga pa dé vei na bam wone. Ba laam ma maŋe nadwoona ne. O ta ma jwoori o maŋe se dé vo jatwogo de noa ni kuni moro dé woli da. O daa ma pa dé vei na bam wone, de ba laam maŋe teiŋa ne mo. 5O daa ta maŋe se dé vo dé yi jatwogo de noa ni kuni moro mo, de ba laam jigi bu-fara mo pa a ware se a vo na bam wone a bɛ. Buga kam déem tiini ka luuna mo pa wolo na boŋe se o bɛ-ka to jege se o pugi na bam mo se o wane o bɛ bubɛ dedwoŋi dem ne. 6O ma bwei amo o we, “Nabiinu, nmo nɛ konto na?”
O ma pa dé jwoori buga kam buburi-bɛ dem ne. 7Dé na yi da to, mo amo nɛ teeni dedɛ na zege de maŋe de buga kam bubɛ maama. 8Nɔɔno wom ma ta de amo o we, “Bu-tola kanto duri ka yɔɔre wɛ-puli seeni mo, se ka tɔge bwolo kolo na tigi Jɔdan buga kam seeni to, ye ka laam vo ka kweeli Yɛ naneo kom wone. Ka na bam ná zo dáane, naneo kom na bam wó ji na-ŋona mo. 9Bu-tola kanto maa ná duri ka yi mɛ maama, wonnu dwi dwi, de ywona dedɛ mo wó taa wora. Kokuri, naneo kom wo na bam laam kwɛ ba ji na-doora mo ye ba pae ŋwea. 10Ywon-jara wó yeini ba zege naneo kom ni ne ba taa jaane ywona. Ko na zege En-gedi ne, se ko yi En-egalayim to, ba wó taa zege naneo kom ni ne mo ba dole ba chworu tem. Ba maa wó taa jaane ywona dwi maama, se ko maŋe de yalo na wo Mediterania naneo kom ne tei to. 11Ko nam ná ye chwaro de bwollu telo na bwola de naneo kom ni to, te na bam bá yɔɔre ba ji na-doora. Nɔɔna ta wó taa nae yɛ te wone. 12Teeni delo na ke bia se nɔɔna taa di to dwi maama de wó nwoŋi de taa zege bu-tola kam bubɛ maama ne. Teeni dem vɔɔro bá kwaare, ye de bá lei bia de ga. Teeni dem wó taa ke bia mo chana maama wone. Kokuri to, na balo na nwoŋi Wɛ diga kam ne to mo duri ba yi-de pa de nyɔ-ba de sui. De bia bam wó taa ye wodiu mo te pae nɔɔna, ye de vɔɔro tem de pa-ba zurim.”
Tega kam siseini na maŋe mɛ to
13Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Abam ná tu á pɔɔre tega kam, siseina yalo á na wó tiŋi á pa á tete to wó taa ye tento mo. Á wó pɔɔre-ka á pa Isarele dwia fuga-yalei yam se ba taa tei. Á nam wó kwei popɔre selei á pa Josɛf dwi dem. 14Pɔɔre-na tega kam á pa á dwia yam maama se ko taa mae daane. Kokuri, amo déem dugi duuri we a lage a kwei-ka a pa á nabaara bam mo. Tega kam nam wó taa ye abam nyem mo se á ta‑á tei-ka.
15Tega kam siseini na wó taa ye tei mo tento:
Baŋa seeni siseini dem wó bobo Mediterania naneo kom ni ne mo de tole de vo Hetelon seeni, se de laam tɔge Lebo-Hamafa, ye de daare de bɛ de kɛ Zedadi, 16de Berota, de Siberayim. Jei sem konto wo Damasika de Hamafa tetare laŋa ne mo. Siseini dem ta wó kɛ de yi Hazera Hatikon, de na wo Hawuran siseini dem ne to. 17Konto to, siseini dem wó zege naneo kom ni ne ko vo ko kweeli Hazara Enan ne. De maa wó tɔge Damasika baŋa seeni siseini dem mo, ye Hamafa teo siseini dem de wo baŋa seeni. Tega kam baŋa seeni siseini dem na wó taa ye tei to mo konto.
18Wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem wó taa tigi Hawuran de Damasika tetare laŋa ne mo. De wó tole Jɔdan buga kam, ye de wo Gilead de Isarele tega kam tetare ne to. Ka maa wó vo ka yi Yɛ naneo kom, Tamara teo na zege mɛ to. Tega kam wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem na wó taa ye tei to mo konto.
19Tega-kuri seeni siseini dem wó zege Tamara ne mo de tole de yi Meriba-kadese buli-yi dem seeni. De daa ta wó tɔge Ejipti nabara kam ne de tole de vo de kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ni ne. Tega kam tega-kuri seeni siseini dem na wó taa ye tei to mo konto.
20Wɛ-zoore seeni siseini dem wó tɔge Mediterania naneo kom ni mo de tole de vo de yi jei selo na maŋe de Lebo-Hamafa to. Tega kam wɛ-zoore seeni siseini dem na wó taa ye tei to mo konto.
21Nam pɔɔre-na tega kam á pa daane se Isarele dwia yam maama wane ba na ba de nyem ka wone. 22Abam nam ná lage á pɔɔre tega kam, á wó kwei-ka á pa á tete dedaane veira balo na tu ba zoore de abam ye ba jege bia to. Abam na wó ke tei á pa Isarele tembia to, se á ke konto de veira bam de. Ba de jege chwoŋa se ba tɔge de Isarele dwi tiina bam ba jwoŋi ba tega. 23Isarele tiina dwi delo wone veiru ná zoore da, kotu wó jwoŋi tega dáane mo se o taa tei.”
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_text:
The Division of Land among Tribes in the North
The Lord said:
1-7Each tribe will receive a section of land that runs from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. The northern border of Israel will run along the towns of Hethlon and Lebo-Hamath, and will end at Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between the kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The tribes will receive their share of land in the following order, from north to south: Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben, and Judah.
The Special Section of Land
The Lord said:
8South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
9An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
10I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle. 11Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning. 12The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
13I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, 14and they must never sell or trade any of this land—it is the best land and belongs to me.
15South of my sacred land will be a section twelve and a half kilometers long and three kilometers wide. It will not be sacred, but will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem, together with its houses and pastureland. 16The city will be a square: Each side will be two kilometers long, 17and an open area 125 meters wide will surround the city. 18The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide. 19People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
20And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
21The regions east and west of this square of land will belong to the ruler of Israel. His property will run east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea. In the very center of his property will be my sacred land, as well as the temple, 22together with the share belonging to the Levites and the city of Jerusalem. The northern border of the ruler's property will be the land that belongs to Judah, and the southern border will be the land that belongs to Benjamin.
The Division of Land among Tribes in the South
The Lord God said:
23-27South of this special section will be the land that belongs to the rest of Israel's tribes. Each tribe will receive a section of land that runs from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. The tribes will receive their share of land in the following order, from north to south: Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad.
28Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
29That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
The Gates of Jerusalem
The Lord said:
30-34 The city of Jerusalem will have twelve gates, three on each of the four sides of the city wall. These gates will be named after the twelve tribes of Israel. The gates of Reuben, Judah, and Levi will be in the north; Joseph, Benjamin, and Dan will be in the east; Simeon, Issachar, and Zebulun will be in the south; Gad, Asher, and Naphtali will be in the west. Each side of the city wall will be two kilometers long, 35and so the total length of the wall will be ten kilometers. The new name of the city will be “The-Lord-Is-Here!”
translation_text:
Tega kam popɔre sem
1“Isarele dwia yam de tega kalo ba maama na wó jwoŋi to mo tento:
Ko na zege tega kam maama baŋa seeni siseini dem ne to, Dan dwi dem wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ka baŋa seeni siseini dem wó tole de vo Hetelon seeni, se de laam yi Lebo-Hamafa. De maa wó vo de kweeli Hazara-enan ne. Damasika baŋa seeni siseini dem na yeiri Hamafa to mo konto. Dan dwi dem siseini mo konto, ko na zege Isarele tega kam wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni to.
2Asere dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Dan dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko kɛ ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
3Nafitali dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Asere dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
4Manasɛ dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Nafitali dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
5Efrayim dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Manasɛ dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
6Ruben dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Efrayim dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko kɛ ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
7Judah dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Ruben dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko kɛ ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
8Nam pɔɔre-na tega kalo na wó taa ye ka yera to. Tega kam konto wó lɔ siseini de Judah dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko kɛ ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni. Maŋe-na jei sem konto se ko taa ye naba-laara kuni 12,500 kayɔlɔ baŋa ne. Ka dedɔrem dem nam wó zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi wɛ-zoore seeni se ko taa mae de dwia yadwonna yam tega ni na wó taa ye tei to. Wɛ tete diga kam nam wó zege tega kam konto tetare ne mo.
9Pwola kalo abam na wó pɔɔre se ka taa ye Baŋa Wɛ tete nyem to ye se á maŋe-ka naba-laara kuni 12,500 dedɔrem baŋa ne. Ka kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem de wó taa ye naba-laara kuni 5,000. 10Tega kam konto wó taa ye ka yera ka pae kaanem tiina bam mo. Ka baŋa seeni siseini maŋem wó taa ye naba-laara 12,500 mo. Ka kayɔlɔ seeni maŋem maa wó taa ye naba-laara 5,000 ka wɛ-zoore seeni, de ka wɛ-puli seeni. Tega-kuri seeni siseini dem maa wó taa ye naba-laara 12,500 dedɔrem baŋa ne. Baŋa Wɛ diga kam maa wó taa zege pwola kam konto tetare dem ne. 11Ka wó taa ye Zadoki tiina bam na ye kaanem tiina to nyem mo. Banto yɔɔre ba nii amo totoŋa baŋa ne mo ye ba wo yage. Ba wo sɛ se ba tɔge de Isarele tiina bam ba ywori ba chwoŋa, ne Levi dwi tiina badaara bam na ke tei to. 12Abam ná pɔɔre tega kam, pwola kam konto wó taa ye ka yera ka pa-ba. Ka wó tiini ka taa ye wose mo. Ka maa wó yeiri de Levi dwi tiina bam tega kam.
13Ko na yeiri kaanem tiina bam tega kam konto to, Levi dwi tiina bam wó taa jege ba de popɔra. Ka wó taa ye naba-laara 12,500 mo dedɔrem baŋa ne. Ka kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem maa wó taa ye naba-laara 5,000. Ba tega kam ni maama wó taa ye naba-laara 12,500 mo dedɔrem baŋa ne, de naba-laara 5,000 kayɔlɔ baŋa ne. 14Ko dae se ba kwei tega kam ba yeigi ba pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno, naa se ba kwei-ka ba ma ba leiri woŋo kodwoŋi, ka na ye wose ka pa Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane.
15Pwola kam tega kalo ta na daare to wó yi naba-laara 2,500 ka kayɔlɔ baŋa ne, de naba-laara 12,500 ka dedɔrem baŋa ne. Kanto dae ka yera Wɛ ŋwaane, ye Jerusalem teo tiina wó wane ba taa jege-ka ba toŋa. Ba wae ba lɔ ba sam ye ba kɔne ba vara jei sem konto ne. Ba nam wó lɔ teo kom tete tega kam tetare ne mo. 16Ko sɛ sena sem maama wó taa mae daane mo: naba-laara 2,250 ko baŋa seeni, de tega-kuri seeni, de wɛ-puli seeni, dedaane wɛ-zoore seeni. 17Pwola maa wó taa tigi teo kom sɛ sena sem maama ne, ka kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem na ye naba-laara 125 ka baŋa seeni, de tega-kuri seeni, de wɛ-puli seeni, dedaane wɛ-zoore seeni to. 18Tega kalo ta na daare ye ka yeiri pwola kalo na ye wose to ne mo ba wae ba kwei-ka ba du wodiu se Jerusalem teo nɔn-bia bam taa di. Tega kam kadwoŋi wó yi naba-laara 5,000 teo kom wɛ-puli seeni, ye ka kadwoŋi yi naba-laara 5,000 teo kom wɛ-zoore seeni. 19Teo kom nɔn-bia balo na nwoŋi Isarele dwia yam maama wone to mo wó taa vare tega kam konto. 20Ko na ye tei to, tega kalo maama na pɔɔre se ka taa ye ka yera to sɛ sem maama mae daane mo. Ka maŋem dem maa ye naba-laara 12,500 saŋa maama ne. Tega kalo na ye wose Wɛ ŋwaane to ná woli de Jerusalem teo laŋa kam, ko maama wó maŋe konto mo.
21Tega kalo ta na daare pwola kam konto wɛ-puli seeni dedaane ka wɛ-zoore seeni to wó taa ye teo dedɛɛro wom nyem mo. Ka kayɔlɔ maŋem maa wó taa ye naba-laara 12,500. O tega kam wó tole wɛ-puli seeni ka yi Jɔdan buga kam, ye ka daare ka tole wɛ-zoore seeni ka yi Mediterania naneo kom. Tega kalo ba na wó pɔɔre ba pa-ne to, de amo wara-jei sem na wó taa wo ka wone to laam maa wó taa tigi dedɛɛro wom tega kam tetare ne. 22Konto to, Levi dwi tiina tega kam, de kalo na wora teo kom ŋwaane to maama wó taa tigi dedɛɛro wom te selei sem tetare laŋa ne mo. O tega kam de maa wó lɔ siseini de Judah dwi tega kam na wo baŋa seeni to. Ka ta wó lɔ siseini de Benjamin dwi tega kam na wo tega-kuri seeni to.
23Ko ta ná daare dwia yalo na daare to:
Benjamin dwi dem wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam nam wó zege Isarele tega kam wɛ-puli seeni mo ka tole ka yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
24Simeon dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Benjamin dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
25Isakara dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Simeon dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
26Zebulun dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Isakara dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
27Gad dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Zebulun dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.
28Gad dwi dem tega-kuri seeni siseini maa wó zege Tamara ne mo de tole de taa vei de yi Meriba-kadese buli-yia yam ne. De daa ta wó tɔge Ejipti nabara kam ne de tole de vo de kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ni ne.
29Tega kam konto mo nmo wó pɔɔre n pa Isarele dwia yam maama se ba taa tei. Dwi de dwi maama popɔra na wó taa ye tei to mo konto. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
Teo kom manchwo-peo nia taane
30Nia yanto mo nɔɔna wó yeini ba tɔge da ba nwoŋi teo kom wone: Teo kom baŋa seeni kabira maŋem wó taa ye naba-laara 2,250 mo. 31Ba maa wó pore nia yatɔ baŋa seeni kabira kam ne, ya yera na ye Ruben ni dem, de Judah ni dem, de Levi ni dem to. Ba wó taa jege Isarele dwia yam yera mo ba bwoi teo kom nia yam.
32Wɛ-puli seeni kabira kam maŋem de wó taa ye naba-laara 2,250, ye ka de jege nia yatɔ. Ko maa ye Josɛf ni dem, de Benjamin ni dem, de Dan ni dem.
33Tega-kuri seeni kabira kam maŋem de wó taa ye naba-laara 2,250, ye ka de jege nia yatɔ. Ko maa ye Simeon ni dem, de Isakara ni dem, de Zebulun ni dem.
34Wɛ-zoore seeni kabira kam maŋem de wó taa ye naba-laara 2,250, ye ka de jege nia yatɔ. Ko maa ye Gad ni dem, de Asere ni dem, de Nafitali ni dem.
35Konto to, laŋa kalo na tigi ka kaare teo kom sɛ sena sem maama to ye naba-laara 9,000 mo. Ko nam na zege maŋa kam konto ne se ko taa vei to, ba wó taa bwoi teo kom yere we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wo ko wone.’ ”

english_text:
Daniel and His Friends
1 In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia attacked Jerusalem. 2 The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim and take away some of the things used in God's temple. And when the king returned to Babylonia, he put these things in the temple of his own god.
3One day the king ordered Ashpenaz, his highest palace official, to choose some young men from the royal family of Judah and from other leading Jewish families. 4The king said, “They must be healthy, handsome, smart, wise, educated, and fit to serve in the royal palace. Teach them how to speak and write our language 5and give them the same food and wine that I am served. Train them for three years, and then they can become court officials.”
6Four of the young Jews chosen were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, all from the tribe of Judah. 7But the king's chief official gave them Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abednego.
8Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace. 9God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel. 10But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”
11The king's official had put a guard in charge of Daniel and his three friends. So Daniel said to the guard, 12“For the next ten days, let us have only vegetables and water at mealtime. 13When the ten days are up, compare how we look with the other young men, and decide what to do with us.” 14The guard agreed to do what Daniel had asked.
15Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace. 16After this, the guard let them eat vegetables instead of the rich food and wine.
17God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
18At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him. 19The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court. 20From then on, whenever the king asked for advice, he found their wisdom was ten times better than that of any of his other advisors and magicians. 21Daniel served there until the first year of King Cyrus.
translation_text:
Danyeli de o badwonna bam taane
Danyeli na ke tei Babilon teo ne to
1Judah teo Pɛ Jehoyakim paare dim bena yatɔ bene dem ne mo Babilon teo Pɛ Nebukadeneza vei Jerusalem se o ke jara de-ba, ye o kaare teo kom maama o pu. 2Baŋa Wɛ déem ma yage chwoŋa se o di Pɛ Jehoyakim. Pɛ Nebukadeneza ma pɛ Wɛ diga kam zela yadwonna o ja o viiri. O na jwoori o tete teo Babilon to mo o jaane Wɛ diga zela yam o zo o teo jwoni zula diga kam o tiŋi da.
3Pɛ Nebukadeneza déem jege nɔɔno dedoa na nii o nakwa maama baŋa ne. O yere maa ye Asepenaza. Pɛ wom ma pa‑o ni se o beeri Isarele tiina bam tetare ne balo ya na nwoŋi Judah teo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne, naa Judah tiina naduna badwonna wone to o pa‑o. 4Banto jege se ba taa ye nɔn-donno telo na lana fase ye gɛɛ tera ba yera ne to. Ba maa wó taa ye yi-pore-nyena balo boboŋa na dana se ba wane wonnu ba zamese to. Ba maa jege se ba taa ye balo na maŋe se ba toŋe Pɛ sɔŋɔ totoŋa to mo. Asepenaza nam mo wó zamese-ba se ba lɔre Babilon tiina taane dem se ba daare ba taa gare ba twanno. 5Pɛ wom ma pa ni se dɛ maama wone, ba pa nɔɔna bam konto wodiu kolo wonto tete de o sɔŋɔ tiina na wó di to. Nɔn-donno tem nam jege se ba kwei bena yatɔ mo ba zamese lanyerane, se ba zamesem dem kwaga ne ba taa toŋe ba pae pɛ wom o sɔŋɔ kom ne.
6Judah teo nɔɔna balo ba déem na kuri to badwonna mo tento: Danyeli, de Hanania, de Misayeli, de Azaria. 7Nebukadeneza nakwa yiga tu wom déem ma jwoori o pa-ba yere-doora. O déem page Danyeli yere we, Bɛletesaza. Hanania yere maa ye Saderake. Misayeli maa ye Mesake, ye Azaria yere leiri de ji Abedenego.
8Danyeli ma ke o boboŋa ne se o yé biini o tete de pɛ wom wodi-laaro telo ba na pɛ‑o se o taa di to. O ma lwoori chwoŋa Pɛ nakwa yiga tu wom tei ne se o taa di wodi-gaa. 9Wɛ déem ma pa Asepenaza lage Danyeli ni taane pa se o duri o ŋwaŋa. 10De konto maama de, nɔɔno wom ta kɔre foone de pɛ wom mo. O ma ta de Danyeli we, “Amo tu Pɛ wom mo pɛ ni abam na wó ta‑á di wodiiru telo, de á na wó ta‑á nyɔ sana balo to. Abam ná lage á ta‑á di wodiiru tedwonna, ye ba ba ba maane we á yera ba zura ne á yuudwonna bam, Pɛ wom wó wane o chigili amo ba o de tega ne ko ŋwaane.”
11Asepenaza nam ya le nɔɔno mo se o taa nii Danyeli, de Hanania, de Misayeli, de Azaria baŋa ne. Danyeli ma yi o tei o ta ded‑o o we, 12“Pa se dé maane dé nii da fuga laŋa ne se n ta‑n pae debam dwo-vɔɔro yerane se dé taa di, de na-gaa se dé taa nyɔa. 13Da fuga ná yia, se n pa dé nwoŋi dé zege. Nmo ma‑n wó kwei debam ya-tega kam n maŋe de nɔn-donno telo tem na di pɛ wom wodi-laaro to ya-tega. Nmo yi laam ná nɛ kolo, se n ke dedaane debam ne ko na maŋe tei to.” 14Nɔɔno wom ma sɛ se o maane-ba da fuga baŋa ne o nii.
15Da fuga kam na yi to, ba ma nii ba na we Danyeli de o yuudwonna bam déem mo nugi lanyerane ye ba jege lam ba dwoi nɔn-donno telo na di pɛ wom wodiiru tem to. 16Wolo na nii ba baŋa ne to daa maa wo fe-ba se ba di pɛ wom wodi-laaro tem se ba daare ba nyɔ o sana bam. Dwo-vɔɔro yerane mo ba déem laam jege ba di.
17Wɛ déem ma pa nɔn-donno tena tento yi-poro de yeino, se ba wane ba zamese twanno de swa dwi maama. Ko woli da, Wɛ déem pɛ Danyeli boboŋa mo se o taa wae o maŋe veera de dendwa kuri chekke.
18Bena yatɔ yalo Pɛ Nebukadeneza na pɛ se ba ma ba bere nɔn-donno tem to ma yi. Asepenaza ma ja ba maama o ja o jeeri Pɛ wom yiga ne. 19Pɛ wom ma ŋɔɔne de-ba dedoa dedoa, ye o daare o bwei-ba bwia. O ma maane we nɔn-donno tem maama wone, Danyeli, de Hanania, de Misayeli, dedaane Azaria mo ke lanyerane ba dwoni wuu. O ma pa ni se ba taa bwola ded‑o ba taa toŋe ba pa‑o. 20Ba déem na wora to, pɛ wom ná lage se ba woli‑o de swa, o yeini o maane we nɔn-donno tem konto swa de ba yiyiu kɛ o yi-nara bam de o liri-keira bam maama swa mo kuni fuga laŋa ne. 21Danyeli déem maŋe pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne mo o toŋe taa se ko yi maŋa kalo Pɛ Sarusi na bobo o di paare to.

english_text:
Nebuchadnezzar's Dream
1During the second year that Nebuchadnezzar was king, he had such horrible nightmares that he could not sleep. 2So he called in his counselors, advisors, magicians, and wise men, 3and said, “I am disturbed by a dream that I don't understand, and I want you to explain it.”
4They answered in Aramaic, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever! We are your servants. Please tell us your dream, and we will explain what it means.”
5But the king replied, “No! I have made up my mind. If you don't tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be chopped to pieces and your houses will be torn down. 6However, if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be greatly rewarded and highly honored. Now tell me the dream and explain what it means.”
7“Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
8The king replied, “You're just stalling for time, 9because you know what's going to happen if you don't come up with the answer. You've decided to make up a bunch of lies, hoping I might change my mind. Now tell me the dream, and that will prove that you can interpret it.”
10His advisors explained, “Your Majesty, you are demanding the impossible! No king, not even the most famous and powerful, has ever ordered his advisors, magicians, or wise men to do such a thing. 11It can't be done, except by the gods, and they don't live here on earth.”
12-13This made the king so angry that he gave orders for every wise man in Babylonia to be put to death, including Daniel and his three friends.
God Tells Nebuchadnezzar's Dream to Daniel
14Arioch was the king's official in charge of putting the wise men to death. He was on his way to have it done, when Daniel very wisely went to him 15and asked, “Why did the king give such cruel orders?” After Arioch explained what had happened, 16Daniel rushed off and said to the king, “If you will just give me some time, I'll explain your dream.”
17Daniel returned home and told his three friends. 18Then he said, “Pray that the God who rules from heaven will be merciful and explain this mystery, so that we and the others won't be put to death.” 19In a vision one night, Daniel was shown the dream and its meaning. Then he praised the God who rules from heaven:
20“Our God, your name
will be praised
forever and forever.
You are all-powerful,
and you know everything.
21You control human events—
you give rulers their power
and take it away,
and you are the source
of wisdom and knowledge.
22“You explain deep mysteries,
because even the dark
is light to you.
23You are the God
who was worshiped
by my ancestors.
Now I thank you and praise you
for making me wise
and telling me the king's dream,
together with its meaning.”
Daniel Interprets the Dream
24Daniel went back to Arioch, the official in charge of executing the wise men. Daniel said, “Don't kill those men! Take me to the king, and I will explain the meaning of his dream.”
25Arioch rushed Daniel to the king and announced, “Your Majesty, I have found out that one of the men brought here from Judah can explain your dream.”
26The king asked Daniel, “Can you tell me my dream and what it means?”
27Daniel answered:
Your Majesty, not even the smartest person in all the world can do what you are demanding. 28-29But the God who rules from heaven can explain mysteries. And while you were sleeping, he showed you what will happen in the future. 30However, you must realize that these mysteries weren't explained to me because I am smarter than everyone else. Instead, it was done so that you would understand what you have seen.
31Your Majesty, what you saw standing in front of you was a huge and terrifying statue, shining brightly. 32Its head was made of gold, its chest and arms were silver, and from its waist down to its knees, it was bronze. 33From there to its ankles it was iron, and its feet were a mixture of iron and clay.
34As you watched, a stone was cut from a mountain—but not by human hands. The stone struck the feet, completely shattering the iron and clay. 35Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed and blown away without a trace, like husks of wheat at threshing time. But the stone became a tremendous mountain that covered the entire earth.
36That was the dream, and now I'll tell you what it means. 37Your Majesty, you are the greatest of kings, and God has highly honored you with power 38over all humans, animals, and birds. You are the head of gold. 39After you are gone, another kingdom will rule, but it won't be as strong. Then it will be followed by a kingdom of bronze that will rule the whole world. 40Next, a kingdom of iron will come to power, crushing and shattering everything.
41-42This fourth kingdom will be divided—it will be both strong and brittle, just as you saw that the feet and toes were a mixture of iron and clay. 43This kingdom will be the result of a marriage between kingdoms, but it will crumble, just as iron and clay don't stick together.
44-45During the time of those kings, the God who rules from heaven will set up an eternal kingdom that will never fall. It will be like the stone that was cut from the mountain, but not by human hands—the stone that crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. Your Majesty, in your dream the great God has told you what is going to happen, and you can trust this interpretation.
Daniel Is Promoted
46King Nebuchadnezzar bowed low to the ground and worshiped Daniel. Then he gave orders for incense to be burned and a sacrifice of grain to be offered in honor of Daniel. 47The king said, “Now I know that your God is above all other gods and kings, because he gave you the power to explain this mystery.” 48The king then presented Daniel with a lot of gifts; he promoted him to governor of Babylon Province and put him in charge of the other wise men. 49At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high positions in Babylon Province, and he let Daniel stay on as a palace official.
translation_text:
Nebukadeneza dendwɛ dem taane
1Dɛ dedwe Pɛ Nebukadeneza paare dim bena yalei bene dem wone mo o dwɛ dendwɛ dedwoŋi. Dendwɛ dem ma pa se o boboŋa tiini ya daane‑o, ye o ga se o dɔ de ŋwaane. 2O ma toŋe o bwoŋi o teo kom liri-keira, de ko yi-nara, de ko vora, de yi-pore-nyena, se ba jeeri ba maŋe o dendwɛ dem kuri ba bere‑o. Ba na tu ba zege pɛ wom yiga ne to, 3o ma ta de-ba o we, “Amo dwɛ dendwɛ mo ye de jege-ne de daana. A nam yɔɔre a lage se a lɔre de kuri mo.”
4Yi-nara bam ma leiri pɛ wom de Aram tiina taane ba we, “Pɛ, Wɛ wó pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre. Nam ta n dendwɛ dem n bere debam se dé maŋe de kuri dé bere‑m.” 5Pɛ wom ma leiri o we, “A boboŋa maŋe ya ja mo de taane dento. Abam mo jege se á ta a dendwɛ dem na ye tei to. Ko kwaga ne, á wó maŋe de kuri á bere-ne. Abam ná wo ke konto maama, a lage a pa ba gwoni abam mo muga-muga se á sam dem de ji di-dwonnu. 6Se á ná tage dendwɛ dem na ye tei ye á ta maŋe de kuri á bere-ne, amo wó pa abam ŋweero de pɛɛra dedɛ ko ŋwaane ye a daare a pa á tiini á na zula. Konto ŋwaane nam, yɔɔre á ta dendwɛ dem se á daare á maŋe de kuri á bere-ne.”
7Ba de daa ma leiri‑o ba we, “Pɛ, ko ye nmo ná lwoni n dendwɛ dem n bere debam yerane mo dé laam wó wane dé maŋe de kuri dé bere‑m.” 8Ba taane dem ma pa pɛ wom ta o we, “Amo yɔɔre a lɔre abam boboŋa a ti mo! Á na yei we a yia seene to mo pɛ se á jege maŋa kam á chɔga. 9Abam nam na yei we á ná wo tage dendwɛ dem kuri á bere-ne, á maama wó te to ŋwaane, mo á jege vwa á fɔe se á ma‑á gane-ne. Abam boŋe we a lage a leiri a wo mo na? Ta-na dendwɛ dem á bere-ne, se ko pa a lɔre we á wó wane á maŋe de kuri chekke á bere-ne.” 10Yi-nara bam ma leiri pɛ wom ba we, “Pɛ, nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera tega baŋa ne se kotu wane o ke n na lage se debam ke kolo to. Dé nam ta wo nɛ pɛ wolo na tage o yi-nara, naa o liri-keira, naa o yi-pore-nyena se ba ke nmo na tage tei to, ne o ná maŋe o ye pa-faro tei maama de. 11Pɛ, nmo lage se dé ke kolo na ware to mo. Ko ná dae wa yam yerane, nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane n dendwɛ dem o ta o bere‑m. Wa yam nam ba zoore de nabiina.”
12Ba taane dem déem ma pa pɛ wom bane tiini de zaŋe, ye o pa ni se ba go swa tiina balo maama na zoore Babilon teo ne to. 13Pɛ wom ni dem ŋwaane, ba toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba go swa tiina bam maama mo. Nɔɔna ma vo ba beeri Danyeli de o yuudwonna bam se ba go ba de ba woli da.
14Nebukadeneza babɛ sem yiga tu wom yere mo ye Arioki. O na vei se o go Babilon teo swa tiina bam to mo Danyeli yi o yera o lwoori‑o de swa se o lɔre kolo na ke to. 15O ma bwei Arioki o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye pɛ yɔɔre o pa ni se ba ke keim dem konto?” Arioki de déem ma lwoni kolo maama ya na ke to o bere‑o. 16Danyeli na nigi konto to, mo o yɔɔre pɛ wom tei o vo o lwoori maŋa fenfee se o jwoori o tei o ta dendwɛ dem kuri o bere‑o.
17Danyeli ta ma jwoori sɔŋɔ ye o ta kolo na ke to, o bere Hanania, de Misayeli, de Azaria. 18O déem ma ta de-ba o we, “Pa-na se dé lwoori Telaao Tu Wɛ wom se o duri debam yibwona se o le wo-siseigo konto kuri o bere debam. Konto ná kea, debam bá tɔge de Babilon teo swa tiina badaara bam dé te.” 19Tete dem konto ne mo Wɛ seene o veere wo-siseigo kom de ko kuri dem o bere Danyeli. Danyeli maa tei Telaao Tu Wɛ wom ye o we,
20“Tei-na Wɛ yere dem se ko taa vei wuu!
Kokuri, wonto mo ye yeino tu,
ye o dam gaale.
21Wonto mo pae se wonnu ke te maŋa ne.
O maa pae pwa jei ba di paare,
ye o ta pae ba badwonna ga ba paare dem.
O ye wolo mo na kwei swa o pa swa tiina to,
ye o daare o pa se yeino yi yi-pore-nyena de.
22Wonto mo le wonnu telo kuri nim na chana ye te seigi to.
O maa yei kolo maama na wo lim wone to.
Pwooni de maa kaare o maama de pu.
23Wɛ wolo a nabaara déem na zuli to,
a tei‑m mo ye a ke n lei.
Ko ye nmo mo pɛ-ne swa de dam.
Nmo ma‑n bere-ne kolo dé na lwoori‑m se n le to kuri,
de n na bere debam pɛ wom dendwɛ dem na ye tei to.”
Dendwɛ dem kuri
24Danyeli ma vo Arioki tei. Pɛ Nebukadeneza ya pɛ wonto ni mo se o go Babilon teo swa tiina bam maama. Danyeli ma ta ded‑o o we, “Yé go ba wolowolo. Nam tɔge a yiga se dé vo pɛ wom tei, se a laam maŋe o dendwɛ dem kuri a bere‑o.”
25Arioki de ma seene o ja Danyeli o vo pɛ Nebukadeneza tei, ye o ta de pɛ wom o we, “Nɔɔna balo dé na kale dé ja dé nwoŋi Judah ne dé ba ywo-seeni to wone mo a nɛ nɔɔno dedoa se o wane o ta nmo dendwɛ dem kuri o bere‑m.”
26Pɛ wom ma bwei Danyeli wolo yere dedwoŋi na ye Bɛletesaza to o we, “Ko ye chega mo we nmo wó wane n ta amo na dwɛ dendwɛ delo to se n ta lɔre de kuri n bere-ne na?”
27Danyeli ma leiri‑o o we, “Swa tu tera, naa yi-naro, naa liri-mwa tu, naa yi-pore-nyem tera, se kotu wane o lɔre wo-siseigo kolo nmo na tage to kuri o bere‑m. 28Telaao Tu Wɛ wom nam wora, ye wonto mo wae o kwei wonnu telo na seigi to o bere jaja. O ma kuri se o bere nmo kolo jwa na wó ke to. A laam wó ta n ya na tigi n dɔa ye n dwɛ wonnu telo to, dedaane boboŋa yalo na tu n yuu ne to kuri a bere‑m.
29Pɛ, nmo na tigi n dɔa konto to mo wonnu telo na wó ke jwa seeni to jaane n boboŋa. Wolo wom na veere wonnu telo ya na seigi to mo pɛ se n lɔre kolo na lage ko ke to. 30Nam lɔre lanyerane we a na lɔre n dendwɛ dem ya na seigi to, ko dae we amo jege swa a dwoi nɔɔna maama mo. Pɛ, ko ye Wɛ nam mo lage se n lɔre wonnu telo na kare te beeri n boboŋa ne ye te daane‑m to kuri.
31Pɛ, nmo na dwɛ to, n nii n na nabiinu nyenyego na zege n yiga ne. Nyenyego kom maa tiini ko daga! Ko ta tiini ko nyeena, ye ko laam jege foone dedɛ. 32Ba kwei sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to mo ba ma ba mɔ nyenyego kom yuu. Ko nyɔɔne dem, de ko vɔna maama ye lu-nyenno mo ba mɛ ba ke tento. Ko puga kam de ko chwa yam de ye channa mo ba mɛ ba ke-te. 33Ko nachere sem maama ye luuru mo ba mɛ ba ke-se. Ko napera yam maa ye luuru de dɔgɔ mo ba gwaane daane ba laam ma ba ke-te. 34Nmo na zege n nii nyenyego kom konto to, mo n daa‑n nɛ kandwɛ-zane na fɔge de nwoŋi peo yuu ne, ye nabiinu wo mɛ o jeŋa o sare-de. Kandwɛ dem tete mo tua de mage nyenyego kom ko napera yam seeni de mumugi-ya, luu de dɔgɔ kom maama. 35Ko laam ma pa se nyenyego kom luuru tem, de dɔgɔ kom, de channa kam, de lu-nyenno tem, de sabu-seŋa kam maama mumugi mura-mura bedwe baŋa ne. Vio de ma ba ko kale tento maama ko ja jei ne te ye swanno yerane mo tei, ye kolokolo daa wo daare. Nmo laam ma‑n na we kandwɛ dem na mage nyenyego kom de chɔge to jigi peo-kamunu mo. Peo kom konto laam ma jwoŋi tega kam baŋa jei maama.
36Nmo dendwɛ dem mo konto. A laam nam wó ta de kuri a bere‑m. 37Pɛ, nmo ye pa-faro mo pwa maama wone. Telaao Tu Wɛ wom nam mo kwei dam dedaane nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ o pa‑m, pa se n paare dem gaale. 38Wɛ ma kwei nabiina de vara maama, ko woli de zuna maama o ke nmo dam kuri ne. Nmo laam ma‑n tei tento maama. Nmo mo ye nyenyego kom yuu kom na ye sabu-seŋa kam ba na mɛ ba ke to.
39Nmo paare dem nam wó kɛ, se paare dedwoŋi de leiri. Paare dem konto nam bá taa dana ne nmo paare dem na ye tei to. De de maa wó di de kɛ se paare batɔ tu laam ba. Dento mo wó taa ye channa paare dem. Paare dem konto wó jage de yi tega kam jei maama. 40Paare bana tu daa ta wó saŋe paare dedwoŋi dem kwaga. Dento nam lage de taa dana mo ne luuru na dana tei to. Paare dem konto wó chɔge paara yadwonna yam maama mo, ne luuru na bwori wonnu ye te ta chochoge-te tei to. 41Nmo nam ta n nɛ we napera yam de namimbia bam jei sedwonna ye luuru, ye sesem de maa ye dɔgɔ. Ko bere we paare dem konto lage de pɔɔre belei mo. Daa dedoa wó taa dana ne luuru na dana tei to, ye kakam daa bwona, ne dɔgɔ na ye tei to. 42Paare dem nam lage de gwaane daane mo, mɛ na bwona to de mɛ na dana to maama. 43Nmo na nɛ we luuru tem de dɔgɔ kom gwaane daane to, ko bere we paare dem konto nam wó taa kwaana se ba di da-bukwa, se ko pa ba taa ye bedwe. Ko nam bá toŋe, ko nye de luuru de dɔgɔ na ba jaane daane tei to mo.
44Ko nam na ye tei to, pwa bam konto paare dim ta ba ti, de Telaao Tu Wɛ wom na tu o chwi paare dedwoŋi. Dento paare dem nam lage de taa wora se ko taa vei wuu mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane-de o che. De maa wó chɔge paara yadwonna yam maama pa se ya jei. Paare dem konto tete nam wó taa wora taa wuu. 45Ko nye de nmo na nɛ kandwɛ-zane delo na fɔge de nwoŋi peo yuu ne ye nabiinu wo mɛ o jeŋa o lɔ-de to. N nɛ we kandwɛ dem konto tu de mage nyenyego kom luuru tem, de channa kam, de dɔgɔ kom, de lu-nyenno tem, de sabu-seŋa kam, ye de chɔge-te mura-mura mo. Wɛ-kamunu kom mo lage se o bere‑m kolo na wó ke jwa seeni to. Pɛ, nmo dendwɛ dem wó seene de ji chega, ye amo de na tage tei a bere‑m to ye ko yuu ne mo.”
46Pɛ Nebukadeneza na nigi konto to, o ma vwi o yibia tega ne o jɔɔne Danyeli. O ma pa ni se ba kwei wodiu pɛɛra ba ma ke kaanem ba pa Danyeli, se ba ta zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa ba pa‑o. 47Pɛ wom ma ta de Danyeli o we, “Abam Wɛ dem mo seene de ye Wɛ chekke de dwoi wa yam maama. O ta ye Yuu-tu mo pwa maama yiga ne. O maa ye Wɛ delo na kwei wonnu telo na seigi to mo o le o bere jaja, bɛŋwaane nmo wane n ta amo dendwɛ dento kuri de de ya na seigi to de.”
48Pɛ wom déem ma pa Danyeli na zula lanyerane, ye o daa ta pa‑o pɛɛra dedɛ na tiini ya lamma to. O ta ma kwei Babilon teo maama o ke o jeŋa ne, ye o daare o pa o ji o swa tiina bam maama yiga tu. 49Danyeli ma lwoori chwoŋa Pɛ wom tei ne, ye ba kwei Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego pa se ba nii Babilon laŋa kam ni maama baŋa ne ba pa‑o. Danyeli tete déem ma maŋe pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne.

english_text:
King Nebuchadnezzar's Gold Statue
1 King Nebuchadnezzar ordered a gold statue to be built 27 meters high and nearly 3 meters wide. He had it set up in Dura Valley near the city of Babylon, 2and he commanded his governors, advisors, treasurers, judges, and his other officials to come from everywhere in his kingdom to the dedication of the statue. 3So all of them came and stood in front of it.
4Then an official stood up and announced:
People of every nation and race, now listen to the king's command! 5Trumpets, flutes, harps, and all other kinds of musical instruments will soon start playing. When you hear the music, you must bow down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up. 6Anyone who refuses will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace.
7As soon as the people heard the music, they bowed down and worshiped the gold statue that the king had set up.
8Some Babylonians used this as a chance to accuse the Jews to King Nebuchadnezzar. 9They said, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever! 10You commanded everyone to bow down and worship the gold statue when the music played. 11And you said that anyone who did not bow down and worship it would be thrown into a flaming furnace. 12Sir, you appointed three men to high positions in Babylon Province, but they have disobeyed you. Those Jews, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, refuse to worship your gods and the statue you have set up.”
13King Nebuchadnezzar was furious. So he sent for the three young men and said, 14“I hear that you refuse to worship my gods and the gold statue I have set up. 15Now I am going to give you one more chance. If you bow down and worship the statue when you hear the music, everything will be all right. But if you don't, you will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace. No god can save you from me.”
16The three men replied, “Your Majesty, we don't need to defend ourselves. 17The God we worship can save us from you and your flaming furnace. 18But even if he doesn't, we still won't worship your gods and the gold statue you have set up.”
19Nebuchadnezzar's face twisted with anger at the three men. And he ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than usual. 20Next, he commanded some of his strongest soldiers to tie up the men and throw them into the flaming furnace. 21-23 The king wanted it done at that very moment. So the soldiers tied up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and threw them into the flaming furnace with all of their clothes still on, including their turbans. The fire was so hot that flames leaped out and killed the soldiers.
24Suddenly the king jumped up and shouted, “Weren't only three men tied up and thrown into the fire?”
“Yes, Your Majesty,” his officers answered.
25“But I see four men walking around in the fire,” the king replied. “None of them is tied up or harmed, and the fourth one looks like a god.”
26Nebuchadnezzar went closer to the flaming furnace and said to the three young men, “You servants of the Most High God, come out at once!”
They came out, 27and the king's high officials, governors, and advisors all crowded around them. The men were not burned, their hair wasn't scorched, and their clothes didn't even smell like smoke. 28King Nebuchadnezzar said:
Praise their God for sending an angel to rescue his servants! They trusted their God and refused to obey my commands. Yes, they chose to die rather than to worship or serve any god except their own. 29And I won't allow people of any nation or race to say anything against their God. Anyone who does will be chopped up and their houses will be torn down, because no other god has such great power to save.
30After this happened, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to even higher positions in Babylon Province.
translation_text:
Sabu-seŋa nyenyego de min-vogo kom
1Pɛ Nebukadeneza déem ma pa ba kwei sabu-seŋa ba ma ba mɔ nyenyego ba zege Dura bwolo kom ne. Jei sem konto de déem wo Babilon kateiri dem wone mo. Nyenyego kom dedɔrem baŋa déem ye jatwogo maŋem kuni fuseredo mo. Ko kayɔlɔ baŋa maa ye jatwogo maŋem kuni beredo. 2Pɛ wom ma toŋe o bwoŋi o teo kom dedɛɛra maama, de ko yiga tiina, de balo na ye yuu tiina teo kom kateira yam ne to, de ko nakwa, de ko swa tiina, de yi-pore-nyena bam, ko ta woli de balo na di nɔɔna taane to, dedaane balo maama na nii kateira yam baŋa ne to se ba ba o tei. O déem bwoŋi banto maama se ba ba ba zuli nyenyego kolo o na pɛ ba ke ba pa‑o to mo. 3Nɔn-kamuna bam konto maama de dedɛɛra bam maama laam ma jeeri daane ba zege sabu-seŋa nyenyego kom yiga ne se ba zuli-ko.
4Kwor-tɔɔlo ma bage baŋa baŋa o we, “Abam balo na nwoŋi dwi maama ne, de teo kolo maama ne, ye á ŋɔɔne taane delo maama to, fɔge á cheigi-na ni delo dé pɛ wom na pɛ to! 5Á wó ni nɔɔna na wó wu nabwanno, de wi, de namunnu. Badwonna de maa wó ta kwanno ye badaara de jege gullu ba maga. Abam nam ná nigi sɔɔ konto dwoŋi, se á ke lela á vwi á yibi tega ne á zuli sabu-seŋa nyenyego kom Pɛ Nebukadeneza na chwi to. 6Wolo maama nam ná ve se o tiiri o jɔɔne nyenyego kom, ba wó ja kotu mo ba dole ba de gwoŋo kolo wone min-vogo na di bileim-bileim to ne.”
7Nɔɔna bam na yɔɔre ba ni nabwanno tem, de wi sem, de kwanno tem, de gullu tem, de namunnu tem kwori to mo ba maama vwi ba yibi sem tega ne. Ba maama ma bobo se ba taa jɔɔne nyenyego kom Pɛ Nebukadeneza na ke to. Ba ná maŋe ba ye dwi delo maama tiina mo, naa ba ná ŋɔɔne taane delo maama de, ba maama ke konto mo.
8Babilon teo swa tiina badwonna ma tɔge keim dem baŋa ne ba vo ba ba Juu tiina bam bebara de pɛ Wom. 9Ba déem ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Pɛ, Wɛ wó pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre! 10Nmo pɛ ni n we, ‘Nɔɔno maama ná nigi wi sem wum, de kwanno tem tam, de sɔɔ dwi maama, se ba maama vwi ba yibi tega ne ba jɔɔne sabu-seŋa nyenyego kom. 11N ni dem ta bere we wolo nam ná ve se o tiiri o jɔɔne nyenyego kom, se ba dole kotu ba de min-vogo wone.’ 12Juu tiina badwonna nam ba nege‑m kɔtaa. Banto maa ye balo nmo na kuri ye n pa-ba dam se ba taa nii Babilon teo kateira yam maama baŋa ne to mo. Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego mo konto. Ba ba zuli nmo teo wa yam. Ba ta ba sɛ se ba tiiri ba zuli nyenyego kom n na ke n zege to.”
13Pɛ Nebukadeneza na nigi konto to, o bane ma tiini de zaŋe de nɔɔna batɔ bam konto. O ma pa ni se ba ja-ba ba ba o tei. Ba na jaane-ba ba yi pɛ wom tei to, 14o ma bwei-ba o we, “Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego, abam mo seene á ta we á bá tɔge á zuli amo wa yam, ye á ta bá jɔɔne sabu-seŋa nyenyego kolo a na chwi to na? 15Tɔ! Boŋe-na á nii á na wó ke tei. Abam daa ná nigi wi sem wum, de kwanno tem tam, de sɔɔ dwi maama, se á vwi á yibi tega ne á jɔɔne sabu-seŋa nyenyego kom. Á nam ná yɔɔre á ve se á jɔɔne-ko, ba laam wó dole abam mo ba de min-vogo kom wone. Á boŋe we wɛ dedwoŋi wora o na wó wane o jwoŋi abam amo jeŋa ne o yage na?”
