You must also pray to the Lord God with all your heart and stop being sinful and cruel. Maybe God will change his mind and have mercy on us, so we won't be destroyed.
10When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_text:
Jonah laam sɛ Wɛ ni
1 Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ŋɔɔne de Jonah o ke belei o we, 2“Nam zaŋe n vo Ninevɛ na ye te-fɔrɔ to, se a laam pa‑m a kwora se n tɔɔle-ka n pa ko nɔɔna bam.”
3Jonah ma sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni ye o daare o vo Ninevɛ. Teo kom konto tiini ko yala ye ba kwei da yatɔ mo ba maa kaare ko ni maama. 4Jonah na vei dɛ wone veiŋa teo kom wone to, mo o bobo se o taa tɔɔle taane dem ye o we, “Da finna mo daare se Baŋa Wɛ chɔge Ninevɛ teo kom zɔŋ-zɔŋ!”
5Ninevɛ tiina bam ma sɛ Wɛ kwora kam. Ba ma tɔɔle se nɔɔna maama vɔ ni se ba daare ba zo gare-nyenyaaro, se ko bere ba wo-chechɔgɔ kom. Nɔɔna maama jege se ba ke konto dwoŋi mo, ko ná ye nɔn-kamuna naa nabwona de.
6Ba pɛ wom na nigi kwora kam to, o ma zaŋe o daare o paare yituŋu kom. O ma lɔɔre o paare gwaaro o tiŋi dáa ne ye o lɛ gare-nyenyaaro. O ma daare o vo o jei tentwarem wone. 7O laam ma tɔɔle o bere Ninevɛ tiina we, “Ni dento nwoŋi Pɛ de o nakwa tei ne mo: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege se o di kolokolo. Ko ná ye nabiina, naa naane, naa sɔŋɔ vara dwi maama, ko chula se ba di wodiu naa ba nyɔ na. 8Nabiina wó zo gare-nyenyaaro mo, se ba daare ba kwei gare-nyenyaaro ba vɔ ba vara yera ne. Nɔɔna maama jege se ba seene yia mo ba lwoori Wɛ lanyerane, ye ba ve ba totoŋ-lwanno de ba vuvuga kikia yam. 9Dɛ delo dé ná ke konto, Wɛ wó sɛ se o leiri o boboŋa, se o ban-lom daa yé taa wo dé baŋa ne se dé te.”
10 Baŋa Wɛ déem maane ba kikia yam de ba na yage ba totoŋ-lwanno tem to. O ma seene o duri ba ŋwaŋa ye o wo waare-ba ne o ya na tage we o wó ke tei to.

english_text:
Jonah Gets Angry with the Lord
1Jonah was really upset and angry. 2 So he prayed:
Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
3 Now let me die! I'd be better off dead.
4The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
5Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
6The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine, 7but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up. 8During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
9But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?”
“Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
10But the Lord said:
You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next. 11In that city of Nineveh there are more than 120,000 people who cannot tell right from wrong, and many cattle are also there. Don't you think I should be concerned about that big city?
translation_text:
Jonah bane zaŋe Wɛ yibwona ŋwaane
1Jonah na nɛ konto to, o wo déem ma fuli dedɛ, ye o bane zaŋe. 2O ma ware Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo ya ta na wo a tete teo ne to, a maŋe a lɔre we tento mo wó ke. Konto ŋwaane mo a nam maŋe a kwaane se a duri a vo Tarasisi to. Kokuri to, amo yei nmo na ye swono tu Wɛ, ye n tiini n jege nɔɔna ŋwaŋa tei to. N ma‑n yeini n peene n bane ye n leiri n boboŋa se n yé chɔge nɔɔna. 3Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nam yage se a te, se a toone gare a ŋwea.” 4Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei‑o o we, “Wɔ mo pɛ‑m chwoŋa se n pa n bane zaŋe konto dwoŋi?”
5Jonah na nigi konto to, o ma nwoŋi teo kom wone o vo ko wɛ-puli seeni o tei pwoŋa o jei ka kuri ne. O laam maa jei ka woro ne o cheiga se o nii kolo na wó ke Ninevɛ teo kom to. 6Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se nyambɔle nwoŋi de milimi de kwoli pwoŋa kam maama pa woro wora lanyerane. Ko ma pa Jonah zurim ye o jege wopwolo de nyambɔle dem vɔɔro.
7Tega na yi ye ka jwoori ka poore to, Wɛ ma pa kanzwɛ dedwoŋi ba de done nyambɔle dem pa de kwaare de te maama. 8Wea na bega to, Wɛ ma toŋe vo-loŋo se ko zege wɛ-puli seeni ko ba ko mage Jonah yupare baŋa. O yuu maa wɔe. O déem gɛ fee mo se o beiri, we-dɛa kam ŋwaane. O ma tiini o boŋe o beeri toone, ye o we, “A toone maŋe de gare a ŋwea.”
9Wɛ daa ma bwei‑o o we, “Chwoŋa kɔ mo n jega se n pa n bane zaŋe nyambɔle dem ŋwaane?” Jonah ma leiri o we, “Chwoŋa wora chekke se a bane zaŋe dedɛ. Ko ná maŋe ko ye se a te de, a jege chega.”
10 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ko ná ye nyambɔle dem, tete dedoa ne mo a pɛ de zaŋe de be. A daa ma pa se de jei tete dedwoŋi ne. Nmo wo ke kolokolo n pa-de, se de maa zaŋe de be. Bɛ mo ye n wo chɔge de ŋwaane? 11Ko nam ná ye Ninevɛ teo nɔn-bia bam, a ná duri ba yibwona, ko dae ko chwoŋa ne na? Ko ye te-fɔrɔ kolo nɔɔna na dwoi morro bi de finlei balo na ware ba pɔɔre lam de lwarem daane to mo. Ba vare-kɔgɔ kom de maa tiini ko gaale. Konto, a seene a jege chwoŋa se a taa jege ba ŋwaŋa.”

english_text:
1 I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah.
Judgment on Samaria
2Listen, all of you!
Earth and everything on it,
pay close attention.
The Lord God accuses you
from his holy temple.
3And he will come down
to crush underfoot
every pagan altar.
4Mountains will melt
beneath his feet
like wax beside a fire.
Valleys will vanish like water
rushing down a ravine.
5This will happen because of
the terrible sins of Israel,
the descendants of Jacob.
Samaria has led Israel to sin,
and pagan altars at Jerusalem
have made Judah sin.
6So the Lord will leave Samaria
in ruins—
merely an empty field
where vineyards are planted.
He will scatter its stones
and destroy its foundations.
7Samaria's idols will be smashed,
and the wages
of temple prostitutes
will be destroyed by fire.
Silver and gold from those idols
will then be used by foreigners
as payment for prostitutes.
Judah Is Doomed
8Because of this tragedy,
I go barefoot and naked.
My crying and weeping
sound like howling wolves
or ostriches.
9The nation is fatally wounded.
Judah is doomed.
Jerusalem will fall.
10Don't tell it in Gath!
Don't even cry.
Instead, roll in the dust
at Beth-Leaphrah.
11Depart naked and ashamed,
you people of Shaphir.
The town of Bethezel mourns
because no one from Zaanan
went out to help.
12Everyone in Maroth
hoped for the best,
but the Lord sent disaster
down on Jerusalem.
13Get the war chariots ready,
you people of Lachish.
You led Jerusalem into sin,
just as Israel did.
14Now you will have to give
a going-away gift
to Moresheth.
Israel's kings will discover
that they cannot trust
the town of Achzib.
15People of Mareshah,
the Lord will send someone
to capture your town.
Then Israel's glorious king
will be forced to hide
in Adullam Cave.
16Judah, shave your head
as bald as a vulture
and start mourning.
Your precious children
will be dragged off
to a foreign country.
translation_text:
1 Baŋa Wɛ na ŋɔɔne taane delo o bere Mika, o na nwoŋi Moresɛf teo to mo tento. Ko maa ye maŋa kalo Jotam, de Ahaz, de Hezekia déem na saŋe daane ba ye pwa Judah teo kom ne to. Samaria dedaane Jerusalem nɔɔna bam na toŋe tei to mo Wɛ veere o bere Mika.
Samaria de Jerusalem borem taane
2Abam balo maama na zoore tega baŋa ne to, pore-na á zwa á cheigi taane dento lanyerane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo jei o wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom ne ye o lage o saŋe abam. 3Nii-na! Baŋa Wɛ zege o jeiŋa jei sem ne o tu o beena! O lage o ba o nɔ logo baŋa peero tem yuu ne mo. 4Peero tem tete wó nyeene kalia kalia, ne ba na saŋe nuga mini ne tei to mo. Zwonnu tem de wó jage te jei, nenɛɛne na na chuuri ba kɛ tei to. 5Ko ye Jakob dwi tiina bam na sɛ lwarem totoŋa to ŋwaane mo konto maama wó ke. Chega to, Isarele tiina bam lɔge Wɛ kwaga ne! Bera mo pɛ se ba tusi konto dwoŋi? Ko ye ba te-fɔrɔ Samaria tiina tete ŋwaane mo! Bera mo pɛ se Judah tiina bam zuli jwona? Ko maa ye ba teo kamunu Jerusalem tiina tete ŋwaane!
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
6“Konto ŋwaane amo lage a chɔge Samaria teo kom maama pa se ko ji di-dwonnu nɔɔna na wó che gaare ye ba du Vini teeni da to. A wó pa se na chuuri teo kom kalankula baŋa ne. Na bam wó ja-ya ba jage pa se teo kom de ko kugu maama saare. 7Amo ta wó chochoge ba jwona yam, ye a daare a ma mini a zwɛ pɛɛra yalo maama ba na kwei ba ma zuli-ya to. Chega to, a wó chɔge kamwaro telo maama ba na jege ba kaane to mo. Ba nɛ ba jwona jejegero tem ka-tole totoŋa baŋa ne mo. Konto ŋwaane amo wó pa se ba dona bam jwoŋi-te ba ja vo teo kodwoŋi ba ma ba ŋwe ka-tole dáane.”
Judah bá lu lɛɛro tem wone
8Lɛɛro na wó ba konto to, amo wo chɔge dedɛ ye a keeri ko ŋwaane. Amo laam wó taa vei kalambwolo de a napera yerane mo. A ta wó suuri ne nywoŋ-kura mo tei, ye a chwoosi ne kunkworo na keeri tei to. 9Samaria tiina bam na nɛ zonne delo to ba jege yɔɔrem. Ba jaweo kom lɔgese ko ja Judah tiina bam de, ye ko lage ko yi Jerusalem teo kom, amo chorro tem na zoore mɛ to.
10Yé zaŋe-na á ta taane dento se Gafa tiina bam maane dé cham dem ni ne! Yé keeri-na de fenfee de! Ko daare abam balo na zoore Bɛte-Lafera ne to, kwei-na fwogo á ma á taare á yera á wo-chechɔgɔ kom ŋwaane. 11Ba wó kale abam Safiri tiina bam ba viiri se á nwoŋi á teo kom wone bwori de á chaveera á ta‑á via. Zaanan tiina bam nam ware ba nwoŋi ba teo kom wone. Bɛte-Ezeli tiina bam maa laare dedɛ, ba daa bá wane abam ba woli. 12Marofa tiina bam maama yɔɔre ba wowole mo ba teene verem, Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe lɛɛro ye te ga fee se te yi Jerusalem teo to ŋwaane.
13Abam balo na zoore Lakisi ne to, kwɛ-na á jara-keim torokooro tem se sisein-nɔɔna vaŋe-te ye á duri á kɛ! Ko ye abam mo bobo á tɔge Isarele tiina wɛleera yam dwoŋi, pa se Jerusalem tiina bam de to tusim wone. 14Judah tiina bam, véi-na á ke bana de Moresɛf-Gafa tiina bam. Á daa bá na-ba. Akiziba teo kom nam lage ko lɔ Isarele tiina pwa bam kwaga ne mo. 15Abam balo na zoore Maresa ne to, Baŋa Wɛ lage o pa á dona bam wane á teo kom ba di mo. Wolo na jege yere Isarele tiina bam wone to wó duri o vo o seigi Adulam peo bɔɔne dem wone.
16Judah tiina bam, cheeri-na á yum se á daare á ta‑á laara, ba na lage ba ja á bu-swonnu tem ba kale ba vo sa-teo to ŋwaane. Chega to, tiini á cheeri-na á yum nenɛɛne duura yum na ye tei to.

english_text:
Punishment for Those Who Abuse Their Power
1Doomed! You're doomed!
At night you lie in bed,
making evil plans.
And when morning comes,
you do what you've planned
because you have the power.
2You grab any field or house
that you want;
you cheat families
out of homes and land.
3But here is what the Lord says:
“I am planning trouble for you.
Your necks will be caught
in a noose,
and you will be disgraced
in this time of disaster.”
4When that happens,
this sorrowful song
will be sung about you:
“Ruined! Completely ruined!
The Lord has taken our land
and given it to traitors.”
5And so you will never again
own property
among the Lord's people.
6“Enough of your preaching!”
That's what you tell me.
“We won't be disgraced,
so stop preaching!”
7Descendants of Jacob,
is it right for you to claim
that the Lord did what he did
because he was angry?
Doesn't he always bless
those who do right?
8My people, you have turned against
one another!
You have even stolen
clothes right off the backs
of innocent neighbors
who pass by in peace.
9You take over lovely homes
that belong to the women
of my nation.
Then you cheat their children
out of the inheritance
that comes from the Lord.
10Get out of here, you crooks!
You'll find no rest here.
You're not fit to belong
to the Lord's people,
and you will be destroyed.
11The only prophet you want
is a liar who will say,
“Drink and get drunk!”
A Promise of Hope
12I, the Lord, promise
to bring together
the people of Israel
who have survived.
I will gather them,
just as a shepherd
brings sheep together,
and there will be many.
13I will break down the gate
and lead them out—
then I will be their king.
translation_text:
Balo na bɛɛse nabwona to wó na lɛɛro
1Ko ná ye balo na jege lwarem boboŋa to, lɛɛro wo ba yuu ne! Ba yeini ba peini tete ne ba boŋe boboŋ-balwaaro mo. Tega ná poore, ba wó seene ba ke kolo na su ba yia to, ba na jege ko dam to ŋwaane. 2Ba yeini ba vere kare selo maama ba yia na su to se ba va. Ba ta maa vere sɔŋɔ kolo maama ba na lage to se ba taa zoore ko wone. Ba yeini ba ke konto mo, ye ba ma dam ba jwoŋi nɔɔna jeŋa wonnu maama.
3 Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage kolo to mo tento:
“Amo tete jege boboŋa se a pa cham mo ba abam baŋa ne. Nɔɔno tera á wone o na wó wane o jwoŋi o tete o yage. Maŋa kam konto ne, á wó na lɛɛro pa se á de á kamunni dem maama tega ne. 4Nɔɔna wó taa jege abam ba mɔna ye ba leeni wo-chechɔgɔ leiŋa ba we:
‘Lɛɛro wo dé yum ne!
Ba vere dé tega kam ba daare debam.
Ka laam wo dé dona bam jeŋa ne mo!’ ”
5Konto to, ba ná jwoori ba pɔɔre tega kam ba pa Wɛ kɔgɔ kom nɔɔna bam, abam balo na vere nɔɔna tega to daa bá jwoŋi á nyem á ta‑á tei.
6Nɔɔna bam konto yeini ba pworisi ba ta de amo ba we, “Yé ta‑n pworisi konto dwoŋi! Debam bere dé bá na dé chaveera!”
7Ko wo maŋe se Jakob dwi tiina bam taa ŋɔɔne konto dwoŋi. Á boŋe we Baŋa Wɛ wó peene o bane de abam, se o yé ke abam kolokolo mo na? Ko nam ná ye balo na tɔge chwoŋa to, amo ni taane dem wó fɔge-ba lanyerane.
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
8“Abam na ke tei to, á tiini á pa ko zo amo nɔɔna bam yera, ne á ye a dona mo tei. Á yeini á zi á dwonna balo na nwoŋi jara jei ba jwoori ba sam to, ye á daare á vere ba gwaaro tem. 9Abam mo zeili amo nɔn-kɔgɔ kom kaana bam pa ba nwoŋi sam delo na ye ba kugu jei sem to wone. Ko ta ná ye ba bia bam, á ma vere wo-laaro telo amo na ke ba jeŋa ne se ba taa tei to.
10Zaŋe-na á lage jei! Á daa bá ta‑á zoore jei sem konto ne se á na siu. Abam lwarem totoŋa mo pɛ se teo kom maama chɔge. 11Nɔɔna bam konto wó taa lage sampwora kalo ni na su de vwa taane to mo. Konto tu ná tu o pworisi de-ba o we, ‘Á wó na sa-dɛɛra dedɛ se á ta‑á nyɔ á sui!’, ba wó tɔge o kwaga de wopwolo.
Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam wó na fɔgem
12Jakob dwi tiina bam, amo wó jwoori a la abam a ke daane. Chega to, a wó kale balo maama na daare Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom wone to, ne nayero na kale o pei o pa se jwoori se zo se peiga jei tei to. Konto to, tega kam wó ba ka su de kɔgɔ dedɛ.”
13Wolo na jege dam se o pore chwoŋa o pa-ba to mo wó tɔge ba yiga. Ba wó pi ba nwoŋi teo kolo ba dona bam na peene-ba to wone. Ba Pɛ wom mo wó to ba yiga ne, ye ba da ba nwoŋi. Wonto ye ba Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo.

english_text:
Evil Rulers and Lying Prophets
1Listen to me,
you rulers of Israel!
You know right from wrong,
2but you prefer to do evil
instead of what is right.
You skin my people alive.
You strip off their flesh,
3break their bones,
cook it all in a pot,
and gulp it down.
4Someday you will beg the Lord
to help you,
but he will turn away
because of your sins.
5You lying prophets promise
security for anyone
who gives you food,
but disaster for anyone
who refuses to feed you.
Here is what the Lord says
to you prophets:
6“You will live in the dark,
far from the sight of the sun,
with no message from me.
7You prophets and fortunetellers
will all be disgraced,
with no message from me.”
8But the Lord has filled me
with power and his Spirit.
I have been given the courage
to speak about justice
and to tell you people of Israel
that you have sinned.
9So listen to my message,
you rulers of Israel!
You hate justice
and twist the truth.
10You make cruelty and murder
a way of life in Jerusalem.
11You leaders accept bribes
for dishonest decisions.
You priests and prophets
teach and preach,
but only for money.
Then you say,
“The Lord is on our side.
No harm will come to us.”
12 And so, because of you,
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple now stands.
translation_text:
Isarele yiga tiina na tiini ba chɔge tei to
1Amo déem tage a we:
“Abam balo na ye yiga tiina Jakob dwi tiina bam wone to, cheigi-na taane dento! Abam ye Isarele tiina bam dedɛɛra, ye á kikia maama ya maŋe se ya taa tɔge chega mo. 2Abam nam chuli kolo maama na jege lam to ye á daare á tɔge totoŋ-balwaaro kwaga. Á yeini á ja amo nɔɔna bam á pwoni ba tɔn-zwona kam á daare ba kwi sem yerane. 3A nɔɔna bam laam mo jigi nɔna ba pa abam. Á yeini á cha ba ya-nɔna yam á ke kambi-zaŋa wone se á saŋe, ye á daare á bwori bwori ba kwi de. Á laam wó twori nɔn-saŋa yam wone á di.”
4Maŋa beene, se nɔn-balwaaro tem konto ba ba lwoori zeina Baŋa Wɛ tei ne. O nam bá sɛ ba wɛ-lworo kom. O wó ma o kwaga o ya-ba, ba na toŋe lwarem kikia to ŋwaane.
5 Baŋa Wɛ ni taane dem mo tento:
“A lage a ta woŋo de sampwori selo na gane a nɔɔna bam to. Nɔɔno wolo ná pɛ-ba ba ni-wodiu, ba wó ta de kotu we, ‘Yazura taa wo n tei ne.’ Wolo nam ná wo pɛ-ba kolokolo, ba wó fugi kotu we tigura beene o baŋa. 6Á maŋa kam ti. Lim wó ba de kwoli abam, se á daa yé ta‑á nae kolokolo á tɛ á bere nɔɔna bam. Amo daa bá veere a tete de abam. Wɛ dem wó zo de diga pa se á jeini lim wone. 7Sampwori sem de yi-nara bam maama wó kwoli ba yibia de chaveera. Ba wó pu ba nia, Wɛ na ve se o leiri ba bwia yam to ŋwaane.”
8Ko nam ná ye amo, Baŋa Wɛ mo ke o Jworo kom a bochare ne pa se a jege dam. Konto ŋwaane mo a wane a lɔre chwoŋa kalo na lana to, ye a na baare se a ta chega de Isarele tiina bam se ba lɔre ba na tusi tei to.
9Abam balo na ye yiga tiina Jakob dwi tiina bam wone to, cheigi-na taane dento! Chega to, abam balo na ye Isarele tiina dedɛɛra bam to yeini á chuli chega kam ye á chɔge kolo maama na lana to. 10Á tɔge puseŋa totoŋa de nɔn-gora kikia baŋa ne á fɔge á lɔ á sam Jerusalem ne, ye ko ye Wɛ tete teo mo. 11Teo kom dedɛɛra bam yeini ba jwoŋi dim mo ye ba daare ba bore nɔɔno bora. Kaanem tiina bam de maa jwoŋi ŋweero se ba daare ba bere Wɛ taane dem. Sampwori sem de jwoŋi sabu ba veera yam ŋwaane mo. Konto maama, ba nam ta bere ba tete we ba sale Wɛ mo. Ba maa kare ba tɛ ba we, “Cham bá yi debam, se Baŋa Wɛ wo debam tei ne.” 12Abam kikia yam konto ŋwaane Wɛ tete teo Jerusalem wó to ko saare ko ji di-dwonnu yerane. Nɔɔna wó ba ba va Zion tega kam konto ba tiŋi. Teeni wó li zwoŋo kolo Wɛ diga kam ya na zege da to.

english_text:
Peace and Prosperity
1In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills,
and every nation
will rush to it.
2People of many nations
will come and say,
“Let's go up to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
3 He will settle arguments
between distant
and powerful nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never again make war
or attack one another.
4 Everyone will find rest
beneath their own fig trees
or grape vines,
and they will live in peace.
This is a solemn promise
of the Lord All-Powerful.
5Others may follow their gods,
but we will always follow
the Lord our God.
The Lord Will Lead His People Home
6The Lord said:
At that time
I will gather my people—
the lame and the outcasts,
and all others into whose lives
I have brought sorrow.
7Then the lame and the outcasts
will belong to my people
and become a strong nation.
I, the Lord, will rule them
from Mount Zion forever.
8Mount Zion in Jerusalem,
guardian of my people,
you will rule again.
9Jerusalem, why are you crying?
Don't you have a king?
Have your advisors gone?
Are you suffering
like a woman in childbirth?
10Keep on groaning with pain,
you people of Jerusalem!
If you escape from your city
to the countryside,
you will still be taken
as prisoners to Babylonia.
But later I will rescue you
from your enemies.
11Zion, because of your sins
you are surrounded
by many nations who say,
“We can hardly wait
to see you disgraced.”
12But they don't know
that I, the Lord,
have gathered them here
to grind them like grain.
13Smash them to pieces, Zion!
I'll let you be like a bull
with iron horns
and bronze hoofs.
Crush those nations
and bring their wealth to me,
the Lord of the earth.
translation_text:
Nabiina wó ba ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ
1Maŋa wó ba ye Baŋa Wɛ diga kam na zege peo kolo yuu ne to na yere ko dwoni logo baŋa jei maama. Ko wó taa zege wɛɛne vili-vili se ko dwoni peero tem maama. Dwi dedɛ tiina wó taa nwoŋi ba teene dem ne ba twoŋi daane taa ba yɔɔre da. 2Logo baŋa dwi tiina bam konto maa wó ba da ye ba ta ba bere daane we, “Pa-na dé vo dé di Baŋa Wɛ peo kom yuu se dé zuli Jakob Wɛ wom o diga kam ne. Wonto wó bere debam o chwei sem, se debam de wane dé taa tɔge-se.”
Kokuri to, da yam konto ne Wɛ bera yam wó zege Zion ne mo ya jage jei maama ne. Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam maa wó nwoŋi Jerusalem ne ka yi nɔɔna maama. 3Dwi tiina balo na zoore teene delo maama wone to ná jege daane, Wɛ wó fɔge-ba o ke daane ye o lwɛ ba jara yam, de ba ná maŋe ba jege dam tei de. Ba laam wó kwei ba jara-keim se-zɔɔro tem ba ma lu vaane, se ba chichwoa yam de pipiri ya ji lare ya pa-ba. Teo daa bá kwaare jara de ko dwoŋi. Nɔɔna de daa bá zamese jara keim. 4Nɔɔna bam maama laam wó taa zoore ba sam wone ye lwia tera. Ba wó jeini ba tete teeni dem woro ne ba sii. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o fugi-ba. Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ni taane mo konto.
5 Dwi-gɛ tiina boŋe se ba taa tɔge ba tete wa yam chwei mo. Debam dwi dem nam wó taa tɔge dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom se ko taa vei wuu.
Isarele tiina wó jwoori sɔŋɔ
6 Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
“Da yam konto ne, amo wó la nɔɔna balo a na pɛ ba yaare sa-teo ne to a ke daane. 7Ba na wo yiga yiga de ba tete teo kom to, ba nye de gwane mo. Amo laam wó pa ba ji balo na daare a nɔɔna bam wone ye ba jwoori sɔŋɔ to. Ba teo kom maa wó fɔge ko ke dam. Ko zege da yam konto ne se ko taa vei wuu, amo Baŋa Wɛ wó taa wo Zion peo kom yuu ne ye a nii ba baŋa ne.”
8Jerusalem, nmo wó taa ye teo kolo Wɛ na yere o nɔɔna bam ne nayero tei ko wone to. Nmo ta wó jwoori n ji te-fɔrɔ mɛ pɛ wom na di o paare da to.
9Bɛ mo ke ye á keeri de baare konto? Ko ye á pɛ wom de á nakwa bam ŋwaane mo na? Ba daa ta tera na? Konto ŋwaane mo pɛ á wo zonne wone ne kapua na wowole se o lo tei to na? 10Ɛɛ, Jerusalem tiina bam! Ta‑á suuri-na ye á kona ne kaane na wowole se o lo tei to. Abam laam wó nwoŋi á yage á sam mo se á vo á pu vwoa gaao ne á peini da. Á dona bam maa wó ja abam ba vo Babilon se ba peene abam teo kom konto ne. Baŋa Wɛ nam wó ba o vere abam o yage á dona bam jeŋa ne pa se á jwoori á ta‑á tei á tete.
11Jar-keira mo nwoŋi teene dedɛ wone ba la daane se ba kwaare jara de abam. Ba maa we, “Pa-na dé yɔɔre dé chɔge Jerusalem teo kom zɔŋ-zɔŋ, se dé daare dé pa chaveera ja-ko!” 12Nɔɔna banto nam za wo lɔre Baŋa Wɛ na kwei boboŋe delo de-ba to. Ba daa wo maane we Wɛ mo lage-ba o ke daane se o fere-ba ne nɔɔno na fere mumuna tei to.
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
13“Jerusalem tiina bam, zaŋe-na se á fere á dona bam! Amo wó pa abam dam nenɛɛne nabea na dana ye ka jege nyea yalo na ye luuru to dedaane napɔɔna yalo na ye channa to. Konto to á wó nɔ dwia yalo maama na wó jeeri abam to. Á laam wó kwei jejegero telo maama ba na nɛ ba jara yam baŋa ne to á ke amo Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ne. Amo mo ye logo baŋa teene dem maama Teiru wom.”

english_text:
A Promised Ruler
1Jerusalem, enemy troops
have surrounded you;
they have struck Israel's ruler
in the face with a stick.
2 Bethlehem Ephrath,
you are one of the smallest towns
in the nation of Judah.
But the Lord will choose
one of your people
to rule the nation—
someone whose family
goes back to ancient times.
3The Lord will abandon Israel
only until this ruler is born,
and the rest of his family
returns to Israel.
4Like a shepherd
taking care of his sheep,
this ruler will lead
and care for his people
by the power and glorious name
of the Lord his God.
His people will live securely,
and the whole earth will know
his true greatness,
5because he will bring peace.
Assyria Will Be Defeated
Let Assyria attack our country
and our palaces.
We will counterattack,
led by a number of rulers
6 whose strong army will defeat
the nation of Assyria.
Yes, our leaders will rescue us,
if those Assyrians
dare to invade our land.
The Survivors Will Be Safe
7A few of Jacob's descendants
survived and are scattered
among the nations.
But the Lord will let them
cover the earth like dew and rain
that refreshes the soil.
8At present they are scattered,
but later they will attack,
as though they were fierce lions
pouncing on sheep.
Their enemies will be torn
to shreds,
with no one to save them;
9they will be helpless,
completely destroyed.
Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
10The Lord said:
At that time I will wipe out
your cavalry and chariots,
11as well as your cities
and your fortresses.
12I will stop you
from telling fortunes
and practicing witchcraft.
13You will no longer worship
the idols or stone images
you have made—
I will destroy them,
14together with the sacred poles
and even your towns.
15I will become furious
and take revenge on the nations
that refuse to obey me.
translation_text:
1Jerusalem tiina bam, la-na á jar-keira bam á ke jeiga dedoa. Dé dona bam tu ba gilimi dé teo kom se ba kwaare jara de debam. Ba lage ba ma da-lɔŋɔ ba mage Isarele tiina yuu tu wom.
Yuu tu wodwoŋi wó nwoŋi Bɛtelehem ne
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
2“Ko nam ná ye nmo, Bɛtelehem Eferata, nmo muri Judah dwi tiina sɔ-yuni tem maama wone. De ko de, amo lage a le dedɛɛro abam wone se o taa tei Isarele tiina bam o pa-ne. O wó taa ye wolo dwi dem na zege faŋa faŋa to mo.”
3Wɛ nam wó yage o nɔɔna bam ba yera se ko taa vei maŋa kalo kapua kam na wó ba o lo bu to. Bu wom chorro tem laam wó na chwoŋa se ba nwoŋi sa-teo ba jwoori ba sam ba woli de ba dwonna Isarele tiina bam. 4Dedɛɛro wom wó zaŋe o taa tei o nɔɔna bam ne nayero na nii o pei baŋa ne tei to. Baŋa Wɛ wó pa‑o dam se o ke konto omo Tu Wɛ tete yere-kamunu kom ŋwaane. Logo baŋa jei sem maama wó ni o kamunni dem ŋwa pa se nɔɔna bam taa zoore de yazura. 5Wonto wó ja wo-zuru o ba o pa-ba.
Isarele tiina bam wó taa tei ba tete
Asiria tiina jar-keira bam wó wane ba ba ba nɔ dé tega kam se ba daare ba chɔge dé sɔ-fwaaro tem. Dé nam wó pa se dedɛɛra dedɛ zaŋe dé wone ba zeili-ba. 6Ba wó wane Asiria tiina bam ba ke-ba ba dam kuri ne. Ba ta wó zo Nimrodi teo kom ba di ko nɔn-bia bam. Chega to, Asiria tiina bam ná kwaare jara de debam, dé dedɛɛra bam wó jwoŋi debam ba jeŋa ne ba yage.
7Maŋa kam konto ne, Jakob dwi tiina balo na daare to wó taa zoore dwi-gɛ tiina tetare ne. Baŋa Wɛ nam wó pa ba taa nye de nyɔnɔ de doa kalo na li tega kam pa ka zuri to mo. Ko dae nabiina mo ba daŋe ba teena ba baŋa ne, se ko ye Wɛ yerane mo. 8Nɔɔna balo na daare Jakob dwi tiina bam wone to wó gwaane dedaane dwi-gɛ tiina. Ba na zoore ba teene wone konto to, ba wó taa nye de nywoŋo kolo na beeri gaao wone ko lage ko ni-wodiu to mo. Ba wó di ba dona bam, nenɛɛne nywoŋo na zo pei-kɔgɔ wone ko ja-se ko tore yera yera ko di tei to mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o jwoŋi-ba o yage. 9Isarele tiina bam, á wó wane á dona bam pa se ba saare tega kam baŋa ne!
10 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we:
“Maŋa kam konto ne amo wó chaale á sisein-nɔɔna bam ye a daare a chɔge á jara-keim torokooro tem maama. 11A ta wó chɔge teene delo á na zoore de wone to, de á sɔ-fwaaro tem maama. 12A ta maa wó chɔge á liri-mwa kikia yam, ye yi-nara bam daa bá wane ba taa toŋa ba totoŋa. 13-14Ko ná ye jwona yalo á na mɔɔne to, dedaane kandwa yalo á na chwi ye á zuli-ya to, amo wó chɔge ya maama, ko ta woli de Asera nyenyego dɛ sem. Abam dáa bá kuni dwonna wonnu telo á jea na mɔɔne to yiga ne á zuli-te. Chega to, amo wó chɔge á jwona yam maama.
15Amo wó tɔge a ban-zɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne a waare dwi-gɛ tiina balo na wo sɛ se ba tɔge amo ni to.”

english_text:
The Lord's Challenge to His People
1The Lord said to his people:
Come and present your case
to the hills and mountains.
2Israel, I am bringing charges
against you—
I call upon the mountains
and the earth's firm foundation
to be my witnesses.
3My people, have I wronged you
in any way at all?
Please tell me.
4 I rescued you from Egypt,
where you were slaves.
I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
to be your leaders.
5 Don't forget the evil plans
of King Balak of Moab
or what Balaam son of Beor
said to him.
Remember how I, the Lord,
saved you many times
on your way from Acacia
to Gilgal.
True Obedience
6What offering should I bring
when I bow down to worship
the Lord God Most High?
Should I try to please him
by sacrificing
calves a year old?
7Will thousands of sheep
or rivers of olive oil
make God satisfied with me?
Should I sacrifice to the Lord
my first-born child as payment
for my terrible sins?
8The Lord God has told us
what is right
and what he demands:
“See that justice is done,
let mercy be your first concern,
and humbly obey your God.”
Cheating and Violence
9I am the Lord,
and you are wise to respect
my power to punish.
So listen to my message
for the city of Jerusalem:
10You store up stolen treasures
and use dishonest scales.
11But I, the Lord, will punish you
for cheating with weights
and with measures.
12You rich people are violent,
and everyone tells lies.
13Because of your sins,
I will wound you and leave you
ruined and defenseless.
14You will eat,
but still be hungry;
you will store up goods,
but lose everything—
I, the Lord, will let it all
be captured in war.
15You won't harvest what you plant
or use the oil
from your olive trees
or drink the wine
from grapes you grow.
16 Jerusalem, this will happen
because you followed
the sinful example
of kings Omri and Ahab.
Now I will destroy you
and your property.
Then the people of every nation
will make fun and insult you.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na bwei Isarele tiina bam tei to
1Cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ na lage o ta kolo to:
“Isarele tiina bam, zaŋe-na se á tole á taane dem se peero tem de zwonnu tem maama ni. 2Amo, Baŋa Wɛ mo jege taane se a ja a jeeri abam balo na ye a tete nɔɔna bam to. Logo baŋa peero tem dedaane tega kuri dem maama wó zege amo chega kam kwaga ne.
3A nɔɔna bam, a bere a ke bɛ mo a ma chɔge abam? A bɛɛse abam tetɛ mo? Á jege taane se á ta na? 4Amo nam jaane abam a nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne a ma vere abam á kabɛɛne dem ne a yage. A déem pɛ se Moses de Aron de Miriam mo tɔge abam yiga. 5Yé swei-na Moaba tiina pɛ Balaki déem na boŋe se o ke abam tei to, se á daare á guli Beora bu Balaam na jwoori o ke zaane abam yuu ne tei to. Daa ta á guli-na á na beeri kagoa kam ne ye a nii abam baŋa ne, ko zege Sitim ne se ko vo ko yi Giligal ne tei to. Konto wó pa se á wane á maane amo na seene a ke abam lanyerane tei to.”
Baŋa Wɛ chwei sem tɔgem
6Amo ná tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se a zuli‑o, a nam wó ja pɛɛre dwi dɔ mo a ba a pa‑o, de o na ye wolo na tei wɛyuu maama to? Ko maŋe se a ja na-bale selo na yi bene to a zwɛ a ma ke kaanem a pa‑o na? 7Amo ná jaane pi-bale morro morro a ma ke kaanem a pa‑o, naa a kwei nuga kalo na su kuriwaa morro fuga to a pa‑o, Baŋa Wɛ yi wó su a pɛɛra yam na? Amo ná maŋe a kwei a bu-kwea kam a ke o jeŋa ne, konto wó wane ko ŋwe a wɛleera yam jene na? Amo yera yam wó saare a lwarem kikia na?
8A choro, ko nam na ye tei to, Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o pa se nmo lɔre chwei selo na lana se n ta‑n tɔge to. O na laga se o na kikia yalo n tei ne to mo tento: Nmo jege se n ta‑n tɔge chega n ŋwea maama wone, ye n jege n dwonna swono, se n daare n tu n tete se n ta‑n tɔge nmo Tu Wɛ chwei sem.
Isarele tiina maŋe waarem
9 Baŋa Wɛ ŋɔɔne de teo kom nɔɔna bam. Wolo maama na jege swa chekke to wó taa kɔre‑o mo. O maa we:
“Cheigi-na, abam balo na gilimi daane teo kom ne to de á dwi dem maama. 10Ko ná ye Jejegero telo á na kwaleme á sam ne to mo, á gane nɔɔna mo á jwoŋi-te. Amo chuli lwarem kikia yanto dwoŋi. 11Ko ná ye wolo na kwei bwɛ selo na muri o ma pini o yeilla bam to, a bá yage kotu wɛleera yam a ma chɛ‑o. 12Teo kom naduna bam bɛɛse balo na ye zora to. Abam balo maama na zoore teo kom ne to maa ye vwa-nyena. Á ni taane ba jege chega.
13Á totoŋ-balwaaro tem konto ŋwaane mo a lage a waare abam lela. Á daa bá ta‑á jege dam. 14Chega na ba chuli taane to, abam wó di wodiu ye á bá fɔge á su. Á wó ta‑á wo kana wone mo taa. Wonnu telo maama na wó zo á jea wone to, á bá na chwoŋa se á tiŋi-te jwa ŋwaane. Amo nam wó pa á dona bam ba ba vere á na wó tiŋi fenfee kolo to jara baŋa ne. 15Abam wó du mena ye á bá zage-ya. Á ta wó ŋoke Olivi tio-bia ye á bá ma nuga kam á turi á yera. Á maa wó ŋoke Vini tio-bia ye á bá nyɔ ba sana bam.
16Chega ŋwaane to, abam tɔge chwei selo Pɛ Omiri de o bu Pɛ Ahab de ba dwi dem maama déem na tɔge to mo. Á na lwoni banto totoŋ-balwaaro tem to ŋwaane mo pɛ se á zo cham dento wone. Amo wó chɔge á teo kom maama pa se chaveera di abam fase. Dwi-gɛ tiina wó taa jege abam ba mɔna, ye ba twe abam dedɛ.”

english_text:
Israel Is Corrupt
1I feel so empty inside—
like someone starving
for grapes or figs,
after the vines and trees
have all been picked clean.
2No one is loyal to God;
no one does right.
Everyone is brutal
and eager to deceive
everyone else.
3People cooperate to commit crime.
Judges and leaders demand bribes,
and rulers cheat in court.
4The most honest of them
is worse than a thorn patch.
Your doom has come!
Lookouts sound the warning,
and everyone panics.
5Don't trust anyone,
not even your best friend,
and be careful what you say
to the one you love.
6 Sons refuse to respect
their own fathers,
daughters rebel against
their own mothers,
and daughters-in-law despise
their mothers-in-law.
Your family is now your enemy.
7But I trust the Lord God
to save me,
and I will wait for him
to answer my prayer.
The Nation Turns to God
8My enemies, don't be glad
because of my troubles!
I may have fallen,
but I will get up;
I may be sitting in the dark,
but the Lord is my light.
9I have sinned against the Lord.
And so I must endure his anger,
until he comes to my defense.
But I know that I will see him
making things right for me
and leading me to the light.
10You, my enemies, said,
“The Lord God is helpless.”
Now each of you
will be disgraced
and put to shame.
I will see you trampled
like mud in the street.
A Bright Future
11Towns of Judah, the day is coming
when your walls will be rebuilt,
and your boundaries enlarged.
12People will flock to you
from Assyria and Egypt,
from Babylonia
and everywhere else.
13Those nations will suffer disaster
because of what they did.
Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
14Lead your people, Lord!
Come and be our shepherd.
Grasslands surround us,
but we live in a forest.
So lead us to Bashan and Gilead,
and let us find pasture
as we did long ago.
15I, the Lord, will work miracles
just as I did when I led you
out of Egypt.
16Nations will see this
and be ashamed because
of their helpless armies.
They will be in shock,
unable to speak or hear,
17because of their fear of me,
your Lord and God.
Then they will come trembling,
crawling out of their fortresses
like insects or snakes,
lapping up the dust.
No One Is Like God
The people said:
18Our God, no one is like you.
We are all that is left
of your chosen people,
and you freely forgive
our sin and guilt.
You don't stay angry forever;
you're glad to have pity
19and pleased to be merciful.
You will trample on our sins
and throw them in the sea.
20You will keep your word
and be faithful to Jacob
and to Abraham,
as you promised our ancestors
many years ago.
translation_text:
Isarele tiina lwarem kikia daga
1A wo chɔge dedɛ. Amo gɛa, nenɛɛne nɔɔno wolo na beeri tio-bia se o di ye o ga tei to. Ko nye de mɔɔro telo a fera na zo to daa wo daare kaporro tem yuu ne, ye nɔɔna maŋe ba gwori Vini tio-bia bam maama. 2Nɔɔna daa tera tega kam baŋa ne ba na jege Wɛ chega kam to. Nɔn-laaro wo daare, de dedoa de. Nɔɔna bam maama yɔɔre ba jei ba pɔe mo se ba ná nɛ pwola se ba zi daane ba go. Nɔɔno maama jei de o dwoŋi bane mo, ye ba gwaare gwonnu ba tiŋi da-ŋwaane. 3Ba jagwia de jazem maama yei lwarem keim. Dedɛɛra bam yeini ba jwoŋi dim mo ye ba daare ba bore nɔɔno bora. Naduna de maa pa se nɔɔna ke ba boboŋa na lage tei to. Ba maama sɔge ni mo daane se ba taa toŋe lwarem. 4Ko ná maŋe ko ye ba wone balo na kwaane se ba taa tɔge chwoŋa to, banto de nye de sabare de ga-cheiŋo mo.
Maŋa mo tento se nɔɔna bam na waarem ne Wɛ sampwori sem na taga tei to. Ba boboŋa wó tiini ya vugimi ko ŋwaane. 5Yé pa n dwoŋi chega, ne o ná maŋe o ye n chilwoŋ-zɔŋɔ mo de. Nmo de n kaane wolo na tigi daane to, ta‑n yei n ni lara ded‑o. 6Maŋa kam konto ne, bu-baara bá taa nege ba kwoa, ye bukwa de wó lɔ ba niina kwaga ne. Kaane maa bá sɛ o nege o baro nu. Nmo tete diga tiina mo wó zaŋe ba done‑m.
7Ko nam ná ye amo, amo teena wo Baŋa Wɛ tei ne mo. Amo Tu Wɛ mo ye amo Vereno. Amo wó taa pɔ‑o mo se o ba o zeini-ne, ne amo na lwoori‑o tei to.
Wɛ wó zeiŋi o nɔɔna bam
8A dona bam, yé ta‑á jege-ne á mɔna. Amo na zo yaara yalo wone to, a daa ta wó zaŋe a yage-ya. A jei yibiri wone mo tento. Baŋa Wɛ nam wó zeiŋi o pwooni dem o pa-ne. 9Amo seene a toŋe wɛleere Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Konto ŋwaane ko maŋe se o bane zaŋe amo baŋa ne. O ná waare-ne o ti, o laam wó ba o zege amo kwaga ne se a zege de chega. O ta wó jwoŋi-ne o ja o zo o pwooni dem wone se a taa tɔge o chwoŋa kam. 10A dona bam yeini ba tɛ ba we, “Nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom bɛ?” Ba nam ná nɛ we Baŋa Wɛ jwoŋi-ne, chaveera wó ja-ba dedɛ. Amo yi wó na ba na toa tei to. Nɔɔna wó ba ba nɔ ba baŋa ne, nenɛɛne ba ye chwoŋa ni bworu mo tei.
11Jerusalem tiina bam, maŋa wó ba se á jwoori á lɔ á teo kom kabiri sem. Abam na wó ta‑á tei jei selo maama to wó yale se gaale. 12Maŋa kam konto ne, á nɔɔna balo déem na jage ba vo mɛ maama to wó jwoori ba taa zoore á teo kom ne. Ba badwonna wó nwoŋi Asiria mo ba ba á tei, se badaara de nwoŋi Ejipti seeni dedaane Yuferata buga kam seeni ba ba. Ba daa ta wó nwoŋi naneero tem jei sem, dedaane peero tem laŋa kam maama ba jwoori ba ba abam tei. 13Tega baŋa kalo maama na daare to laam wó ji kafɛ, dwi-gɛ tiina balo na zoore da to totoŋ-balwaaro tem ŋwaane.
Baŋa Wɛ na duri o nɔɔna ŋwaŋa tei to
14 Baŋa Wɛ, ta‑n nii n nɔɔna bam baŋa ne, ne nayero na yere o pei tei to. Ba ye nmo tete nyem ye ba zoore kagoa wone mo ba yerane. Nam kale-ba n vo te-ywoŋa jei selo na gilimi-ba to. Pa-ba chwoŋa se ba vo Basan de Gilead ye ba di ga-lɛɛro ne ko déem na maŋe ko ye tei to. 15Daa ta n toŋe wo-kenkagela n pa debam, ne n déem na toŋe tei n ma n ja debam n nwoŋi Ejipti ne to. 16Dwi-gɛ tiina bam ná nɛ tento, chaveera wó ja-ba de ba na maŋe ba jege dam ye de ti tei to. Ko wó so-ba pa ba ja ba nia ye ba daare ba se ba zwa ko ŋwaane. 17Ba ta wó ma ba pwi ba fɛɛle tega ne ne tega-veila tei, pa se kasolo yerane mo wó taa ye ba ni-wodiu. Ba wó nwoŋi ba gugworru wone ba ba nmo yiga ne ye ba yera sae, ba na kɔre foone de nmo wolo na ye debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane.
18Debam Tu Wɛ, wɛ dedwoŋi daa tera de na maŋe de nmo to. Nmo yerane mo kwei dé wɛleera n ma n chɛ debam. Debam mo ye balo yerane na daare n tete nɔɔna bam wone to. Nmo bane ná zaŋe debam baŋa ne, ko bá dáane ye de jwoori de to, nmo na jege debam swono to ŋwaane. 19Nmo ta wó ba n duri dé yibwona, se n daare n ma n dam dem n saare dé wɛleera yam. Nmo wó kwei-ya n dole n yage pa se ya kɛ naneo kom tega kuri kuri ne. 20Nmo wó zege n chega kam baŋa ne n pa Jakob dwi tiina bam, ye n daare n ta‑n jege Abaraham dwi tiina bam ŋwaŋa. Nmo wó ta‑n swo-ba se ko maŋe de n na pwooli tei dedaane dé nabaara bam faŋa faŋa to.

english_text:
1 I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh.
The Fierce Anger of the Lord
2The Lord God demands loyalty.
In his anger, he takes revenge
on his enemies.
3The Lord is powerful,
yet patient;
he makes sure that the guilty
are always punished.
He can be seen in storms
and in whirlwinds;
clouds are the dust from his feet.
4At the Lord's command,
oceans and rivers dry up.
Bashan, Mount Carmel,
and Lebanon wither,
and their flowers fade.
5At the sight of the Lord,
mountains and hills
tremble and melt;
the earth and its people
shudder and shake.
6Who can stand the heat
of his furious anger?
It flashes out like fire
and shatters stones.
The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
7The Lord is good.
He protects those who trust him
in times of trouble.
8But like a roaring flood,
the Lord chases his enemies
into dark places
and destroys them.
9So don't plot against the Lord!
He wipes out his enemies,
and they never revive.
10They are like drunkards
overcome by wine,
or like twisted thornbushes
burning in a fire.
11Assyria, one of your rulers
has made evil plans
against the Lord.
12But the Lord says, “Assyria,
no matter how strong you are,
you will be cut down!
My people Judah,
I have troubled you before,
but I won't do it again.
13I'll snap your chains
and set you free
from the Assyrians.”
14Assyria, this is what else
the Lord says to you:
“Your name will be forgotten.
I will destroy every idol
in your temple,
and I will send you to the grave,
because you are worthless.”
15 Look toward the mountains,
people of Judah!
Here comes a messenger
with good news of peace.
Celebrate your festivals.
Keep your promises to God.
Your evil enemies are destroyed
and will never again
invade your country.
translation_text:
1Kwora kanto déem mo tua Elikosi tu Nahum tei Ninevɛ tiina bam ŋwaane. Nahum ma popone wonnu telo Wɛ na veere o bere‑o to o tiŋi tɔnɔ ne.
Wɛ bane zaŋe de Ninevɛ tiina
2 Baŋa Wɛ yi page o nɔɔna bam baŋa ne. O wó waare balo na dwoni ded‑o to. O bane wó tiini de zaŋe de balo na ve‑o to. O ta wó jwoori o ŋwe o jene o seba-nyena baŋa ne. Chega to, o bane wó zaŋe o dona baŋa ne ye o bá yage. 3Baŋa Wɛ yeini o peene o bane mo. O dam-fɔrɔ nam gaale pa se o yɔɔre o waare balo na gɛ bora to. Chwei selo maama ne Baŋa Wɛ na wó tɔge da to, vo-dɛɔ mo yeini ko dola. O na wó nɔne mɛ maama to, kunkwonnu de maa jaane kulululu, ne fwogo mo tei. 4Wonto bwɛ naneo kom we ko we, ye ko seene ko we. O ta maa pae se nabare sem kora. Basan laŋa kam de Kamele peo kom gaaro tem maama koga. Lebanon peero baŋa teeni dem maama de ma te. 5Baŋa Wɛ ná bere o dam dem, peero tem wó ziziŋi mo. Zwonnu tem maa wó saare te to buri-buri. Tega kam baŋa maama de wó chɔge, pa se logo baŋa de nabiina maama yera taa sae. 6Baŋa Wɛ bane ná zaŋe, wɔ mo yi se o zege o yiga ne? O bane ná tutugi, wɔ daa mo wó wori? O ná lwogi o bane logo baŋa ne, kandwa tete wó chochoge mo muga-muga. 7Baŋa Wɛ lamma mo. Cham ná yi o nɔɔna bam, o maa ye ba dalem jei. Ko ná ye balo na seigi o woro kom wone to, o maa nii ba baŋa ne. 8Ko nam ná ye balo na dwoni ded‑o to, o lage o chɔge-ba mo lela, ne na-fwaaro na chuuri ba baŋa ne tei to. O ta wó zeili o dona bam pa se lim kwoli-ba.
9Abam jeeli se á ke bɛ mo á ma‑á chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga? Wonto nam wó pa á boboŋa yam konto jei. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá dwoni ded‑o se ko ke belei. 10O dona bam nye de sa-nyɔra mo. Ba ta nye de sabare selo na milimi daane to mo. Mini mo lage de zwɛ-ba nenɛɛne ga-korro na yeini te zwɛ kula tei to.
11Ninevɛ tiina bam, puseŋ-nyeno mo nwoŋi abam wone o jeeli keim-balɔrɔ se o ke o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. 12Baŋa Wɛ kwora mo tento: “Asiria tiina bam ná maŋe ba damma ye ba daga tei de, amo wó pa ba na chɔgem, pa se ba jage da-yiga ne. A nɔɔna bam, amo seene a pa se cham yi abam. A nam daa bá ke konto. 13Leile konto amo lage a pa se Asiria tiina bam dɔne ba jea á baŋa ne, se ba daa yé taa bɛɛse abam.”
14 Baŋa Wɛ ta pɛ ni dento, se de taa wora abam Asiria tiina bam ŋwaane: “Á dwi dem wó jei mo pa se á yera saare. Amo lage a chɔge á jwona yam mo se á daa yé zuli-ya ya di sem ne. A ta maa wó suli abam tega ne, á na ye nɔn-yɔɔro to ŋwaane.”
15Judah tiina bam, nii-na peero tem seeni! Tontoŋeno mo maa beena. O nɛ sem nɔne peero tem yuu ne ye wopwolo de yazura taane wo o ni ne. Konto ŋwaane, ta‑á di-na á kura yam, se á daare á ke kolo á na gwoni ni de Baŋa Wɛ se á ke to. Puseŋ-nyena bam konto daa bá wane ba kwaare jara de abam, Wɛ na wó chɔge-ba o ti to ŋwaane.

english_text:
Nineveh Will Fall
1Nineveh, someone is coming
to attack and scatter you.
Guard your fortresses!
Watch the road! Be brave!
Prepare for battle!
2Judah and Israel are like trees
with branches broken
by their enemies.
But the Lord is going to restore
their power and glory.
* 3Nineveh, on this day of attack,
your enemies' shields are red;
their uniforms are crimson.
4Their horses prance,
and their armored chariots
dart around like lightning
or flaming torches.
5An officer gives a command.
But his soldiers stumble,
as they hasten to build
a shelter to protect themselves
against rocks thrown down
from the city wall.
6The river gates fly open,
and panic floods the palace.
7Nineveh is disgraced.
The queen is dragged off.
Her servant women mourn;
they moan like doves,
and they beat their breasts
in sorrow.
8Nineveh is like a pond
with leaking water.
Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!”
can be heard everywhere.
But everyone is leaving.
9Enemy soldiers shout,
“The city is full of treasure
and all kinds of wealth.
Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
10Nineveh is doomed! Destroyed!
Her people tremble with fear;
their faces turn pale.
11What happened to this city?
They were safer there
than powerful lions in a den,
with no one to disturb them.
12These are the same lions
that ferociously attacked
their victims,
then dragged away the flesh
to feed their young.
13The Lord All-Powerful
is against you, Nineveh.
God will burn your chariots
and send an army to kill
those young lions of yours.
You will never again
make victims of others
or send messengers to threaten
everyone on this earth.
translation_text:
Ninevɛ teo na wó to tei to
1Ninevɛ tiina bam, á dona bam zege á baŋa ne mo se ba jage abam yera yera. Konto to, zaŋe-na wɛɛne, á ke-na á tete á ke daane. Fɔge-na á dam jei sem. Ta‑á yere-na chwoŋa kam. Ke-na dam á ke á tete kuri ne se á ke jara! 2Baŋa Wɛ lage o jwoori o pa Isarele tiina de Judah tiina mo na nenɔŋa ne ka déem na ye tei to, de ba dona bam na maŋe ba chɔge ba tega kam de ba wodiiru tem tei maama to de.
3Jar-keira balo na tu abam baŋa ne to jege nantane de gwaaro telo na seene chwɛ-chwɛ to mo. Ba ti ba yiga se ba ke jara yam! Ba jara-keim torokooro luuru tem pepele yia ne min-vogo mo tei. Ba maa zei ba chichwoa ba yaare wɛɛne. 4Torokooro tem tiini te duri mo pempala yam baŋa ne. Te maa duri te vei yiga dedaane kwaga teo kom pwooni ne. Te pepela jei maama nenɛɛne min-zwonnu mo tei. Te wurigim dem maa nye de doa pepelem dwoŋi tei. 5Ba ma bwoŋi jar-keira dedɛɛra bam se ba ba. Ba na duri ba maa vei to mo ba chɔɔle ba to tega ne. Ba ma vo ba yi teo kom kabira kam yera, ye ba daare ba kwoli ba yum se ba wane ba bwori manchwoŋo ni dem ba zo teo kom. 6Woŋo kolo ya na chege buga kam to mo bwori. Na bam ma chuuri ba yigi pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ba de tega ne. 7Ninevɛ teo nɔn-bia jege se ba viiri de chaveera! Ba lage ba kale-ba mo ba ja ba kɛ. Pɛ sɔŋɔ kaba-kane sem laam ma keeri wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. Ba maa ŋuura nenɛɛne kunkwona na ŋuuri tei to, ye ba daare ba mage ba takeira ŋwaŋa yerane. 8Ninevɛ teo kom nye de buga kalo na na duri ba nwoŋi yɔɔ tei to mo! Ko nɔn-bia bam nwoŋi ba maa kɛa. Ba ma bage-ba ba we, ‘Zege-na! Zege-na!’, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo pipiri o jwoori.
9Vere-na ba lu-nyenno wonnu tem, de ba sabu-seŋa wonnu tem á ja á viiri! Teo kom su mo dedaane wo-laaro. Ba jejegero tem tiini te jege lonne se ko gaale. 10Lɛɛro mo yi teo kom! Ko chɔge mo ko daare di-dwonnu yerane. Ko nɔn-bia bam bochara dia, ye foone zo-ba. Ba yera maa sae pɔm-pɔm, ye ba yibia tiini ya nyɔne lanyerane.
11Bɛ laam mo ke á teo kom? Ko déem nye dedaane nywonnu tiga jei, ye nywon-bia mo nɛ ba wodiu da ba di. Nywon-bɛ de nywon-kane déem tigi da de ba bia ba sii ye foone tera. 12Nywon-bɛ yeini se go ga-vara ye se ja nɔna se pa se bia de se kaana se ba di ba su. Teo kom maama déem su de jejegero dedɛ.
13Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam tage o we, “Amo done abam mo. A lage a zwɛ á jara-keim torokooro tem mo. Á nɔn-donno tem maa wó te jara wone. Jejegero telo á na vere nɔɔna tei ne to daa bá daare. Abam daa bá toŋe á tontoŋena bam se ba ja á kwora ba vo jei jei.”

english_text:
Punishment for Nineveh
The Lord said:
1Doom to the crime capital!
Nineveh, city of murder
and treachery,
2here is your fate—
cracking whips,
churning wheels;
galloping horses,
roaring chariots;
3cavalry attacking,
swords and spears flashing;
soldiers stumbling
over piles of dead bodies.
4You were nothing more
than a prostitute
using your magical charms
and witchcraft
to attract and trap nations.
5But I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am now your enemy.
I will pull up your skirt
and let nations and kingdoms
stare at your nakedness.
6I will cover you with garbage,
treat you like trash,
and rub you in the dirt.
7Everyone who sees you
will turn away and shout,
“Nineveh is done for!
Is anyone willing to mourn
or to give her comfort?”
Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
8Nineveh, do you feel safer
than the city of Thebes?
The Nile River
was its wall of defense.
9Thebes trusted the mighty power
of Ethiopia and Egypt;
the nations of Put and Libya
were her allies.
10But she was captured and taken
to a foreign country.
Her children were murdered
at every street corner.
The members of her royal family
were auctioned off,
and her high officials
were bound in chains.
11Nineveh, now it's your turn!
You will get drunk and try to hide
from your enemy.
12Your fortresses are fig trees
with ripe figs.
Merely shake the trees,
and fruit will fall
into every open mouth.
13Your army is weak.
Fire has destroyed the crossbars
on your city gates;
now they stand wide open
to your enemy.
14Your city is under attack.
Haul in extra water!
Strengthen your defenses!
Start making bricks!
Stir the mortar!
15You will still go up in flames
and be cut down by swords
that will wipe you out like a field
attacked by grasshoppers.
So, go ahead and increase
like a swarm of locusts!
16More merchants are in your city
than there are stars
in the sky—
but they are like locusts
that eat everything,
then fly away.
17Your guards and your officials
are swarms of locusts.
On a chilly day
they settle on a fence,
but when the sun comes out,
they take off
to who-knows-where.
18King of Assyria,
your officials and leaders
are sound asleep,
while your people are scattered
in the mountains.
Yes, your people are sheep
without a shepherd.
19You're fatally wounded.
There's no hope for you.
But everyone claps
when they hear this news,
because your constant cruelty
has caused them pain.
translation_text:
Lɛɛro lage te yi Ninevɛ teo kom
1Lɛɛro lage te yi teo kom, ko na su dedaane vwa-fɔra dedaane nɔn-gora to ŋwaane. Ba jejegero tem daga te dwoi jaanem. 2Ba dona laam tu ba baŋa ne! Banto fene sem ke sɔɔ! Ba jara-keim torokooro tem durim de ba sisein-nɔɔna bam wurigim dem de maa dɔna kiriba-kiriba! 3Sisein-dira bam yera nyaage mo! Ba se-zɔɔro de ba chichwoa laam maa jaane wɛyuu ne ye te pepela! Ba ma puuri puuri twa bam ba dogele daane vili-vili. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa ware ba ni se o ga o ti. Ko laam ma pa jar-keira bam nɔne ba baŋa ne, ye ba chɔɔle ba to tega ne.
4Ko maama kea Ninevɛ teo kom kikia na nye de ka-tola kikia to ŋwaane mo. Teo kom tiini ko jege fera nɔɔna badwonna tei ne, ye ko ta jege liri-mwanno na soge nɔɔna se ba tusi to. Ko yeini ko tɔge ka-tola kikia yanto baŋa mo ko gane teene dedwonna pa se de to. Ko chɔge dwi tiina badaara de ko liri sem.
5Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam tage o we, “Amo done abam mo. A maa wó le á gwaaro tem a daare pa se á zege kalambwolo. Á wó di chaveera dwi tiina badaara yiga ne, de ba na nɛ abam kuri to ŋwaane. 6Amo ta wó lwo weeru á baŋa ne se á lɔre we a yaale abam mo. Nɔɔna de maa wó di tega á yera ne. 7Nɔɔna balo maama na wó nii ba na abam to wó kɔɔre ba tete mo ba jwoori kwaga ye ba we, ‘Ninevɛ teo kom to ko saare! Wɔ mo wora se o keeri ba lua?’ Amo wó na nɔɔna se ba zege á kwaga ne na?”
8Abam teo kom gare Ejipti teo Tebesi na? Ba déem lɔge teo kom konto Naili buga kam ni ne mo. Buga kam ma kaare teo kom maama ka pu nenɛɛne kabira tei, se cham yé wane de yi-ko. 9Tebesi déem nii Kusi de Ejipti maama baŋa ne mo. Teo kom dam dem gaale dedɛ. Puti de Libia tiina maa ye ko fara. 10De konto maama de, ba déem ta jaane Tebesi tiina bam mo ba kale ba nwoŋi ba vo teo yiga yiga. Ba ma yigi ba bu-sese ba de tega ne ba go teo kom chwoŋa yuu maama ne. Ko ná ye teo kom nakwa de dedɛɛra bam, ba dona ma ta jɔrɔ se ba kuri ba wone, ye ba daare ba vɔ-ba dedaane chegero ba ja ba viiri.
11Abam Ninevɛ tiina de nam lage á nyɔ sa-dɛɛra bam konto dwoŋi mo pa se á beiri. Abam de wó kwaane se á duri á lu á dona bam jeŋa ne. 12Á dam jei sem á na lɔge to nye de kaporro telo mɔɔro na dɛ yiga te be te yi to mo. Ba ná sugi kaporro tem, mɔɔro tem wó yɔɔre te to nɔɔna bam nia wone mo. 13Abam jar-keira bam bwona ne kaana dwoŋi mo. Á teo kom de maa zege bwori á dona bam yiga ne. Mini mo lage de zwɛ á teo kom ni-bworru tem. 14Á dona bam lage ba kaare á teo kom ba pu mo. Mo kokuri abam nam jege se á mɔ na á zege, se á ma á ti á yiga. Ta fɔge-na á kwɛ á dam jei sem. Tiini á nɔne-na teero se te be, se á laam ma á mage wara á tiŋi! 15Abam nam ná maŋe á ke tetei maama de, mini wó zwɛ abam kula mo! Á dona bam ta wó go abam jara wone. Ba lage ba ti abam mo nenɛɛne kayere na yeini se deilimi wodiiru tei maama nyɔ to!
Puli-na dedɛ, ne kayere na tiini se yo tei to! 16Á teo kom pipim-piina bam tiini ba daga zanzam, se ko dwoni wɛyuu chalechwe sem kɔgɔ na mae tei to. Leile konto, ba nam daa tera. Ba jei mo, nenɛɛne kayere na di kara wodiu se ti, ye se laam jaane se viiri tei to. 17Abam nakwa de á dedɛɛra bam nye de kayere mo na nwoŋi de kɔgɔ, ye se laam vo se meeli kabira yera ne se waaro yé yi-se tei to mo. Wea laam ma mage, pa se maama jaane se jei, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno yeiri se na vei mɛ to.
18Asiria pɛ, nmo teo yiga tiina bam mo dɔ ba lusi. Naduna bam de maa tigi ba dɔa, ye ba daa bá zaŋe. Nmo nɔn-bia bam maama ma jage ba yi jei maama peero tem baŋa ne, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se o ja-ba o jwoori o ke daane. 19Zonne delo n na nɛ to bá wane de yɔɔre. Nmo fufwollu tem bá jei kɔtaa! Balo maama ná nigi we n teo kom to mo ko saare, banto wó taa chaka mo de wopwolo, ba daare ba taa mage ba jea. Kokuri to, abam ya na tiini á bɛɛse nɔɔna tei to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo lugi abam lwarem kikia wone.

english_text:
1I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me.
Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
2Our Lord, how long must I beg
for your help
before you listen?
How long before you save us
from all this violence?
3Why do you make me watch
such terrible injustice?
Why do you allow violence,
lawlessness, crime, and cruelty
to spread everywhere?
4Laws cannot be enforced;
justice is always the loser;
criminals crowd out honest people
and twist the laws around.
The Lord Answers Habakkuk
5 Look and be amazed
at what's happening
among the nations!
Even if you were told,
you would never believe
what's taking place now.
6 I am sending the Babylonians.
They are fierce and cruel—
marching across the land,
conquering cities and towns.
7How fearsome and frightening.
Their only laws and rules
are the ones they make up.
8Their cavalry troops are faster
than leopards,
more ferocious than wolves
hunting at sunset,
and swifter than hungry eagles
suddenly swooping down.
9They are eager to destroy,
and they gather captives
like handfuls of sand.
10They make fun of rulers
and laugh at fortresses,
while building dirt mounds
so they can capture cities.
11Then suddenly they disappear
like a gust of wind—
those sinful people who worship
their own strength.
Habakkuk Complains Again
12Holy Lord God, mighty rock,
you are eternal,
and we are safe from death.
You are using those Babylonians
to judge and punish others.
13But you can't stand sin or wrong.
So don't sit by in silence
while they gobble up people
who are better than they are.
14The people you put on this earth
are like fish or reptiles
without a leader.
15Then an enemy comes along
and takes them captive
with hooks and nets.
It makes him so happy
16that he offers sacrifices
to his fishing nets,
because they make him rich
and provide choice foods.
17Will he keep hauling in his nets
and destroying nations
without showing mercy?
translation_text:
1Kwora kalo Baŋa Wɛ na kwei o pa o ni-jwoŋinu Habakuki to mo tento:
Habakuki na poone Baŋa Wɛ tei to
2 Baŋa Wɛ! Amo wó lwoori tetɛ mo a jare‑m
se n laam wane n cheigi-ne,
ye n daare n jwoŋi debam n yage vuvuga kanto wone?
3Nmo boŋe we ko lamma se amo taa nae puseŋa kikia
dedaane vwa totoŋa yanto na gilimi-ne to na?
Bɛ mo ye nmo sɛ pa se nankɔɔre dedaane tigura de chɔgem tiini ko wora jei maama ne konto?
4Nɔɔna daa ba tɔge nmo nia yam,
ba kweele-ya mo ba yage tega ne
ye chega kam jei.
Nɔn-balwaaro bere ba che nɔn-ŋona,
pa se ba borem daa ba tɔge chwoŋa.
Baŋa Wɛ na leiri tei to
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
5Nii-na teene delo na gilimi abam to seeni,
se ko wó sɔɔre á yera.
Amo lage a ke woŋo kodwoŋi mo abam da yam wone,
ye ba ná maŋe ba ta ba bere abam ko kuri tei maama de,
á bá sɛ we ko ye chega.
6Amo lage a pa se Babilonia tiina mo zaŋe wɛɛne.
Banto tiini ba ye nankɔ-nyena, ye ba ta jege baare.
Ba lage se ba taa tei teene dem maama.
Ba yɔɔre ba vei yiga mo,
ye ba wane tega baŋa teene delo na dae ba tete teene to.
7Ba tiini ba jege foone mo ba pa nɔɔna,
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa ware-ba o che ba keim-chɛɛre dem ŋwaane.
8Ba sisein-nɔɔna durim dwoi gweeru na duri tei to.
Se maa jege foone
se dwoi ga-vare-balwaaro.
Ba tiini ba diini sisei sem ba nwoŋi jei selo na ba ŋwae to,
ye se napɔɔna guri tega.
Se maa fere daane
nenɛɛne kawula na nɛ chibia ka chaale tei to.
9Ba ná yi mɛ de ba keim-chɛɛre dem,
nɔɔna fona de-ba mo.
Ko maa pae se ba wae ba dona.
Ba na wane nɔɔna balo to kɔgɔ ye nenɛɛne buga ni kasolo na daga tei to.
10Ba ma gwooni pwa ye ba mɔne dedɛɛra.
Ba yi mo nɛ pwa bam di-dedwaaro telo na damma to.
Ba yeini ba lɔ taara mo ba ja ba di di-dedwaaro tem yuu seeni,
ye ba laam wane-ba.
11Ba fere mo ba kɛa ne vio tei.
Ba maa vei yiga ba ke yanto chaveera yam.
Ba jege kamunni mo de ba jwona yam na pa-ba dam to.
Habakuki poone Baŋa Wɛ o ke belei
12Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo ye Wɛ mo boboa ne. N ma‑n ye Wo-pwoŋo Tu se ko taa vei wuu.
Nmo bá pa se dé te. Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo ye wolo na cho debam to mo.
Nmo mo kuri Babilonia tiina bam se ba bore debam bora,
ba daare ba vaŋe dé zwa.
13Nmo na ye Wo-pwoŋo Tu to, n bá‑n wane n sɛ wo-lwanno. Nmo ba lage se nɔɔna tusi chwoŋa. Nmo na ba lage puseŋ-nyena to, bɛ mo ye n yage pa se nɔn-balwaaro tem chɔge debam balo na gare banto to?
14Nmo pɛ se nabiina nye de ywona dedaane wo-korro telo na wo naneo wone ye te ba jege yuu tu to mo. 15Mo kokuri Babilonia tiina bam yeini ba ma gwoli-dole ba ja nɔɔna nenɛɛne ba ye ywona mo tei. Ba jaane nɔɔna mo ba ke ba chworu tem wone ye ba mɔna. 16Ba ke kaanem ba zuli ba chworu tem, bɛŋwaane te pae se ba nae wodi-laaro ba di, ye ba ŋwea ywomma.
17Konto to, nmo nam daa‑n ta wó pa se ba chɔge teene dem maama taa, ye yibwona tera na?

english_text:
The Lord Answers Habakkuk Again
1While standing guard
on the watchtower,
I waited for the Lord's answer,
before explaining the reason
for my complaint.
2Then the Lord told me:
“I will give you my message
in the form of a vision.
Write it clearly enough
to be read at a glance.
3 At the time I have decided,
my words will come true.
You can trust what I say
about the future.
It may take a long time,
but keep on waiting—
it will happen!
4 “I, the Lord, refuse to accept
anyone who is proud.
Only those who live by faith
are acceptable to me.”
Trouble for Evil People
5Wine is treacherous,
and arrogant people
are never satisfied.
They are no less greedy
than death itself—
they open their mouths as wide
as the world of the dead
and swallow everyone.
6But they will be mocked
with these words:
You're doomed!
You stored up stolen goods
and cheated others
of what belonged to them.
7But without warning,
those you owe
will demand payment.
Then you will become
a frightened victim.
8You robbed cities and nations
everywhere on earth
and murdered their people.
Now those who survived
will be as cruel to you.
9You're doomed!
You made your family rich
at the expense of others.
You even said to yourself,
“I'm above the law.”
10But you will bring shame
on your family
and ruin to yourself
for what you did to others.
11The very stones and wood
in your home
will testify against you.
12You're doomed! You built a city
on crime and violence.
13 But the Lord All-Powerful
sends up in flames
what nations and people
work so hard to gain.
14 Just as water fills the sea,
the land will be filled
with people who know
and honor the Lord.
15You're doomed!
You get your friends drunk,
just to see them naked.
16Now you will be disgraced
instead of praised.
The Lord will make you drunk,
and when others see you naked,
you will lose their respect.
17You destroyed trees and animals
on Mount Lebanon;
you were ruthless to towns
and people everywhere.
Now you will be terrorized.
Idolatry Is Foolish
18What is an idol worth?
It's merely a false god.
Why trust a speechless image
made from wood or metal
by human hands?
19What can you learn from idols
covered with silver or gold?
They can't even breathe.
Pity anyone who says to an idol
of wood or stone,
“Get up and do something!”
20Let all the world be silent—
the Lord is present
in his holy temple.
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na leiri o ke belei tei to
1Amo wó zege nayuu kom baŋa ne mo a cheigi se a nii Baŋa Wɛ lage o ta bɛ mo o bere-ne se o leiri a pompona kam. 2Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o ta de amo o we:
“Popone a na le wonnu telo a bere‑m to jaja n ke tɔnɔ wone. Konto wó pa se balo na wó pa taane dem yi nɔɔna to ni ko kuri se ba de lwoni ba bere nɔɔna. 3Maŋa ta wo yi se wonnu telo a na wó le a bere‑m to ji chega. Ko nam bá dáane se maŋa kalo te na wó ji chega to ba ka yi. Ko ná nye de ko wora ko dáane mo de, daa‑n ta peene n cheigi, se ka maŋa kam wó seene ka yi se veera yam ji chega.
4Nii! Bere-n-tete nyena bam mo wó ga ba ŋwea. Wolo maama na jege chega Wɛ tei ne to wó na ŋwea o wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane.
5Jejegero nam gane nɔɔna pa se ba to mo. Siu de maa tera ko pa bere-n-tete nyena bam. Ba jege puseŋa mo ye ba kaŋe ba nia kayɔn-yɔlɔ ne toone de yibeela to. Ba yeini ba le teene dedɛ se ba taa jega, ye ba wane de nɔn-bia bam.
6Dɛ wó ba de yi pa se ba na wane balo to jwoori ba bɛɛse nɔɔna bam konto. Ba wó de dende ba ma mɔne bere-n-tete nyena bam ye ba we, ‘Lɛɛro wo á baŋa ne, abam balo na gane nɔɔna ye á vere-ba se á ma á duni to. Abam wó ke konto taa se á vo á maŋe yei ne mo?’
7Balo á na jene ba tei ne to wó zaŋe lela ba jwoori ba jwoŋi ba wonnu tem. Ba ta wó pa á ŋwe tedwonna de á woli da. Abam dona mo lage ba jwoori ba wane abam, se foone zo abam. 8Abam wane teene dedɛ nɔɔna mo á go-ba ye á vere ba wonnu. De konto maama de, nɔɔna balo na daare to de mo lage ba jwoori ba vere abam de wonnu tem. Kokuri to, á ke tigura mo logo kom baŋa ne ye á go nabiina teene maama wone.
9Lɛɛro wo á baŋa ne, de á na ke dam á ma á vere wonnu zanzam se á ma á ji naduna to. Á ma‑á kwaane se abam sɔŋɔ kom taa zege lanyerane se ko yé chɔge. 10Abam na ke keim-balwaaro ye á chɔge nɔɔna dedɛ konto to, chaveera mo jaane abam dwi dem maama pa se á ga á ŋwea. 11Peero tem ba na mɛ ba ma lɔ á sane dem to, ko woli de bei selo ba na mɛ ba ke nayuni tem to, wonnu tem konto maama mo wó ŋɔɔne te ve abam bora.
12Lɛɛro wo á baŋa ne, dedaane á na go nɔɔna dedɛ, ye á daare á ke keim-balwaaro á ma á lɔ á teo kom á zege to. 13Nii! Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam mo wó pa se teene dem jejegero dwi maama ji kafɛ. Ba na yaare ba lɔ kolo maama ba zege to wó ji tentwarem. 14Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom wó ba ko lɔre jaja, pa logo baŋa su dedaane balo na yei-ko to, ne na na yɔɔre ba su naneo kom wo maama tei to mo.
15Lɛɛro wo abam baŋa ne, dedaane á na pɛ se á dwonna nyɔ sa-dɛɛra ba su, se á laam wane á na ba kuri-nɔrɔ to. 16Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se á zula ji chaveera! O nam wó pa se á tete jwoori á nyɔ sa-dɛɛra bam á bugi, pa se á tiini á na á chaveera. O maa wó kwei na-zoŋa kalo na wo o jazem ne to o pa abam, se á nyɔ ka wone ye á na waarem. 17Abam mo zage Lebanon teeni dem á de tega ne, ye á daare á zeili kago-vara bam maama á go. Wɛ nam wó zage abam o de tega ne! Kago-vara bam wó jwoori ba ja foone ba ba abam baŋa! Kokuri to, abam go nɔɔna dedɛ ye á ma dam á chɔge logo baŋa teene dedaane de nɔn-bia bam maama.
18Jwoni jege bɛ nyɔɔre mo de pae nabiina? De za jege wolim dɔ mo ye nɔɔna maa jege teena de baŋa ne konto to? Jwoni fɔ vwa yerane mo. Nabiinu mo ke-de o zege, ye de nam ware se de puri de ni de ŋɔɔne. 19Lɛɛro wo abam baŋa ne! Abam yeini á kwei daa naa kandwɛ ye á tɛ á we, de zaŋe wɛɛne de jwoŋi abam de yage! Jwoni wae de ŋɔɔne na? Nabiinu mo kwei sabu-seŋa naa lu-nyenno o ma o kwoli de maama, ye de ba ŋwe.”
20 Baŋa Wɛ nam wo o telaao sɔŋɔ kom ne mo. Logo baŋa nɔɔna maama jege se ba taa ye chemm mo o yiga ne.

english_text:
Habakkuk's Prayer
1This is my prayer:
2I know your reputation, Lord,
and I am amazed
at what you have done.
Please turn from your anger
and be merciful;
do for us what you did
for our ancestors.
3You are the same Holy God
who came from Teman
and Paran to help us.
The brightness of your glory
covered the heavens,
and your praises were heard
everywhere on earth.
4Your glory shone like the sun,
and light flashed from your hands,
hiding your mighty power.
5Dreadful diseases and plagues
marched in front
and followed behind.
6When you stopped,
the earth shook;
when you stared,
nations trembled;
when you walked
along your ancient paths,
eternal mountains and hills
crumbled and collapsed.
7The tents of desert tribes
in Cushan and Midian
were ripped apart.
8Our Lord, were you angry
with the monsters
of the deep?
You attacked in your chariot
and wiped them out.
9Your arrows were ready
and obeyed your commands.
You split the earth apart
with rivers and streams;
10mountains trembled
at the sight of you;
rain poured from the clouds;
ocean waves roared and rose.
11The sun and moon stood still,
while your arrows and spears
flashed like lightning.
12In your furious anger,
you trampled on nations
13to rescue your people
and save your chosen one.
You crushed a nation's ruler
and stripped his evil kingdom
of its power.
14His troops had come like a storm,
hoping to scatter us
and glad to gobble us up.
To them we were refugees
in hiding—
but you smashed their heads
with their own weapons.
15Then your chariots churned
the waters of the sea.
Habakkuk's Response to God's Message
16When I heard this message,
I felt weak from fear,
and my lips quivered.
My bones seemed to melt,
and I stumbled around.
But I will patiently wait.
Someday those vicious enemies
will be struck by disaster.
Trust in a Time of Trouble
17Fig trees may no longer bloom,
or vineyards produce grapes;
olive trees may be fruitless,
and harvest time a failure;
sheep pens may be empty,
and cattle stalls vacant—
18but I will still celebrate
because the Lord God
is my Savior.
19 The Lord gives me strength.
He makes my feet as sure
as those of a deer,
and he helps me stand
on the mountains.
To the music director:
Use stringed instruments.
translation_text:
Habakuki wɛ-lworo kom
1Wɛ-lworo konto mo Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu Habakuki déem mɛ o ji leiŋa o leeni o pa Baŋa Wɛ.
2 Baŋa Wɛ, nɔɔna taga ba bere-ne kolo maama nmo na ke to.
Konto ma pa se a kɔre‑m lanyerane.
Nam ta jwoori n ke konto zem dɛ dem ne,
ne nmo déem na maŋe n ke tei to.
Nmo bane ná maŋe de zaŋe de,
daa ta duri dé ŋwaŋa.
3 Baŋa Wɛ zege Teman ne mo o beena.
Wo-pwoŋo Tu Wɛ mo zege Paran peero tem seeni o maa beena.
O nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom ma kwoli wɛyuu kunkwonnu tem maama.
Nabiina maama laam ma pa‑o zula tega baŋa ne.
4O nyeena mo nenɛɛne doa na pepele tei to.
Mini ma pepele de nwoŋi o jeŋa wone,
mɛ seeni o dam dem na seigi to.
5O pae se jaweero da o yiga,
ye toone de maa tɔge o kwaga.
6O na zege mɛ to,
tega kam ziziŋi mo.
O ma nii logo baŋa nɔɔna bam,
ye ba maama yera sae mo vare-vare.
Faŋa faŋa peero tem ma bwori yera yera.
Zwonnu telo o déem na vei te baŋa ne to ma jwoori te palese.
7Amo nɛ we foone mo zo Kusan dwi tiina bam.
Midian dwi tiina bam de yera maa tiini ya sae.
8 Baŋa Wɛ, ko ye bwi sem mo pɛ n bane zaŋe na?
Nmo jege ban-lom naneo kom ŋwaane mo na?
Nmo déem diini sisein-nɔɔna n vo kunkwonnu tem baŋa ne,
ye n dɔge nmo toroko kom baŋa ne.
Ko maa ye se n ja jara n wane n dona bam.
9Nmo ma saŋe n taŋa kam mo
se n ta n chena yam.
Nmo pɛ se doa tiini ka mage tega kam,
pa se nabare laam dura.
10Peero tem na nɛ nmo keim dem to, te ziziŋi mo.
Doa ma nwoŋi wɛyuu ne ka chuura tega ne.
Naneo kom de maa wuura de dam,
ye na bam popɔgele dedɛ.
11Nmo chena yam na vei de fora
ye n chichwei dem de pepele to,
ko ma pa se wea kam dedaane chana kam zege chemm wɛyuu ne.
12Nmo bane dem na zaŋe konto to,
n vei logo baŋa maama wone,
ye n laam nɔne dwi-gɛ tiina bam baŋa ne.
13Nmo na zaŋe n nwoŋi de dam konto to,
ko ye se n jwoŋi balo na ye nmo jeŋa nɔɔna to,
se n daare n vere n dam-fɔrɔ tu wom.
N ma n chɔge nɔn-balwaaro yiga tu wom,
dedaane o kwaga kam maama.
14O na nwoŋi de o jar-keira bam se o jage debam to,
nmo mɛ o tete chichwei mo n ma n zɔ‑o o yuu seeni,
ye ba ya boŋe we ba wó wane debam lela,
nenɛɛne nɔɔna na bɛɛse nɔn-zora tei to.
15Nmo nɔne naneo kom baŋa ne de n sisein-nɔɔna,
pa se na bam popɔgele mo ye ba zaŋe de puŋa.
16Amo nigi tento maama,
ye a yera sae vare-vare.
Foone tiini de zo-ne lanyerane,
pa se a bochare di ye a yera nyɔne.
Amo laam nam wó taa ye chemm mo
ye a cheigi se Wɛ ba o waare balo na bɛɛse debam to.
17-18Teeni dem dedaane kara wodiiru ná maŋe te wo leigi bia de,
amo daa ta wó taa jege wopwolo Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane.
Pei sem maama ná tega de,
ye naane ná tera nabwoo kom wone,
amo daa ta wó taa jege wopwolo,
Baŋa Wɛ na cho amo to ŋwaane.
19Amo Teiru Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na pa-ne dam to.
O ma pa se a nɛ kwaare tega,
nenɛɛne tɔgɔ nɛ na ye tei to mo.
O laam cho-ne se a yé to peero tem yuu ne.
(Lei yiga tu wom: Ta‑n yei we leiŋa kanto ye se ba ma kwanno mo ba ma leeni-ka.)

english_text:
1 I am Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah.
When Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, the Lord gave me this message.
Judgment on Judah
2I, the Lord, now promise
to destroy everything
on this earth—
3people and animals,
birds and fish.
Everyone who is evil
will crash to the ground,
and I will wipe out
the entire human race.
4I will reach out to punish
Judah and Jerusalem—
nothing will remain
of the god Baal;
nothing will be remembered
of his pagan priests.
5Not a trace will be found
of those who worship stars
from their rooftops,
or bow down to the god Milcom,
while claiming loyalty
to me, the Lord.
6Nothing will remain of anyone
who has turned away
and rejected me.
7Be silent! I am the Lord God,
and the time is near.
I am preparing
to sacrifice my people
and to invite my guests.
8On that day I will punish
national leaders
and sons of the king,
along with all who follow
foreign customs.
9I will punish worshipers
of pagan gods
and cruel palace officials
who abuse their power.
10I, the Lord, promise
that on that day
noisy crying will be heard
from Fish Gate, New Town,
and Upper Hills.
11Everyone in Lower Hollow
will mourn loudly,
because merchants
and money changers
will be wiped out.
12I'll search Jerusalem with lamps
and punish those people
who sit there unworried
while thinking,
“The Lord won't do anything,
good or bad.”
13Their possessions will be taken,
their homes left in ruins.
They won't get to live
in the houses they build,
or drink wine from the grapes
in their own vineyards.
A Terrible Day
14The great day of the Lord
is coming soon, very soon.
On that terrible day,
fearsome shouts of warriors
will be heard everywhere.
15It will be a time of anger—
of trouble and torment,
of disaster and destruction,
of darkness and despair,
of storm clouds and shadows,
16of trumpet calls
and battle cries
against fortified cities
and mighty fortresses.
17The Lord warns everyone
who has sinned against him,
“I'll strike you blind!
Then your blood and your insides
will gush out like vomit.
18Not even your silver or gold
can save you on that day
when I, the Lord, am angry.
My anger will flare up
like a furious fire
scorching the earth
and everyone on it.”
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ dɛ dem
1Kwora kalo Baŋa Wɛ na kwei o pa Zefania maŋa kam Amon bu Josia na ye Judah teo pɛ to mo tento. Zefania ye pɛ Hezekia dwi tu wolo de na nwoŋi Amaria, de Gedalia, de Kusi dwia yam wone to mo.
2 Baŋa Wɛ taga o we:
“Amo lage a saare woŋo kolo maama na wo tega baŋa ne to mo.
3Amo wó chɔge nabiina bam, de vara bam,
de zuna bam, de ywona yam maama.
Amo wó pa se puseŋ-nyena bam to tega ne,
ye nɔɔno de dedoa de bá daare.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
4Amo wó zaŋe Jerusalem tiina
de Judah tiina bam maama baŋa ne.
Ko ná ye balo ta na zuli Baal jwona yam to,
amo wó le-ba jei sento wone a yage.
Ba jwona kaanem yiga tiina bam de wó jei,
pa se ba yera saare tega kam baŋa ne.
5Amo ta wó chɔge balo maama na yeini ba diini nayuu
ba jɔɔne wea, de chana, de chalechwe sem to,
ko woli de balo na zuli amo Baŋa Wɛ
ye ba ta du duuri de Moleka jwoni dem to.
6Ko ná ye balo na jwoori amo Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne
ye ba daa ba laga se a taa nii ba baŋa ne to,
amo wó chɔge banto maama de.”
7Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ borem dɛ dem bwola.
Konto ŋwaane ta‑á ye-na chemm o yiga ne.
Baŋa Wɛ wora o ti o yiga se o kwei Judah tiina bam
o ke ba dona jeŋa ne,
ne o na lage o ke kaanem tei to.
8-9 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we:
“Dɛ dem ba na wó ba ba gwoni ba yum konto to,
amo wó waare pɛ wom dedɛɛra bam,
de o bia bam maama.
Banto yeini ba ma dam de kampina mo ba vere nɔɔna wonnu
se ba kwei-te ba tiŋi ba tu wom diga ne ba su.
A ta wó waare balo na jege veira chullu ba tɔga
ye ba zuli jwo-yɔɔro to.
10Dɛ dem konto ná yia,
keira wó zaŋe teo kom Ywona Ni dem ne.
Abam ta wó ni nɔɔna na chwoosa
teo kom jei-doŋa laŋa kam ne.
Sɔɔ-balɔrɔ de maa wó nwoŋi peero telo na gilimi da to.
11Abam balo na zoore teo kom yaga jei sem ne to,
ta‑á keeri-na,
pipim-piina de sabu-leinna bam maama na jei to ŋwaane.
12Kanto maŋa kam ne, amo wó tɔrege min-zwoŋo
a beeri Jerusalem gugworru maama wone.
Ko ná ye balo na boŋe we ba sii mo ba wɛleera wone
ye ba tɛ we,
‘Baŋa Wɛ bá ke debam kolokolo,
ko ná ye chɔgem naa wolim’ to,
amo wó waare-ba.
13Banto tete dona mo lage ba vere ba jejegero tem
ba daare ba chochoge ba sam dem.
Ba wó lɔ sam,
ba nam bá zo de wone.
Ba ta wó jeiri Vini teeni bia,
ba nam bá na de sana ba nyɔ.”
14 Baŋa Wɛ dɛ-kamunu kom konto bwola.
Dɛ dem duri mo lela se de yi.
Baŋa Wɛ dɛ dem wó ja chanɛɛre de ba.
Babɛ maa wó keeri ba wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane.
15 Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom wó tiini de zaŋe dɛ dem konto ne.
De wó ja wo-chechɔgɔ de cham de ba.
Chɔgem de wó tiini de taa wora.
Dento dɛ dem wó taa ye lim yerane mo.
Kunkwonnu tem wó zwori te li tega kam maama biramm.
16Nabwanno wó wu. Tiguri-kaasa de maa wó zaŋe.
Jara yam wó yi teene delo na lɔge de pe to,
dedaane de di-dedwaaro tem.
17 Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
“Amo wó pa se chanɛɛre yi nabiina
se ba taa vei ne lilwoa tei,
ba na ke wɛleere ba chɔge a yiga to ŋwaane.
Ba yera jana wó lwo nenɛɛne na na chuuri tei to,
ye ba ya-nɔna faare tega ya pɔ.”
18 Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom dɛ dem ná yia,
nabiina lu-nyenno de ba sabu-seŋa bá wane te jwoŋi-ba te yage.
O ban-zɔŋɔ kom wó chɔge logo baŋa maama,
ne mini na zwɛ wonnu tei to.
Wɛ wó ke lela o saare nabiina bam,
pa ba maama jei kula!

english_text:
Turn to the Lord
1You disgraceful nation,
gather around,
2before it's too late.
The Lord has set a time
when his fierce anger
will strike like a storm
and sweep you away.
3If you humbly obey the Lord,
then come and worship him.
If you do right and are humble,
perhaps you will be safe
on that day when the Lord
turns loose his anger.
Judgment on Philistia
4 Gaza and Ashkelon
will be deserted
and left in ruins.
Ashdod will be emptied
in broad daylight,
and Ekron uprooted.
5To you people of Philistia
who live along the coast,
the Lord has this to say:
“I am now your enemy,
and I'll wipe you out!”
6Your seacoast will be changed
into pastureland
and sheep pens.
7The Lord God hasn't forgotten
those survivors in Judah,
and he will help them—
his people will take your land
to use for pasture.
And when evening comes,
they will rest
in houses at Ashkelon.
Judgment on Moab and Ammon
* 8 The Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel, said:
I've heard Moab and Ammon
insult my people
and threaten their nation.
9 And so, I swear by my very life
that Moab and Ammon will end up
like Sodom and Gomorrah—
covered with thornbushes
and salt pits forever.
Then my people who survive
will take their land.
10This is how Moab and Ammon
will at last be repaid
for their pride—
and for sneering at the nation
that belongs to me,
the Lord All-Powerful.
11I will fiercely attack.
Then every god on this earth
will shrink to nothing,
and everyone of every nation
will bow down to me,
right where they are.
Judgment on Ethiopia
12 People of Ethiopia,
the sword of the Lord
will slaughter you!
Judgment on Assyria
13 The Lord will reach to the north
to crush Assyria
and overthrow Nineveh.
14Herds of wild animals
will live in its rubble;
all kinds of desert owls
will perch on its stones
and hoot in the windows.
Noisy ravens will be heard
inside its buildings,
stripped bare of cedar.
15This is the glorious city
that felt secure and said,
“I am the only one!”
Now it's merely ruins,
a home for wild animals.
Every passerby simply sneers
and makes vulgar signs.
translation_text:
Nɔɔna bam jege se ba leiri ba wo
1Nam ke-na daane se á tu á tete Wɛ yiga ne,
á na maŋe se chaveera ja abam to ŋwaane.
2Kokuri to, dɛ dem lage de yi lela
se Baŋa Wɛ laam zeili abam o yage,
nenɛɛne vio na fuli poro ko yage tei to.
Dɛ dem konto ne, o ban-lom dem lage de ba de zwɛ abam mo kula,
ne mini na to wonnu wone ko di maama tei to.
3Abam balo na zoore logo kom wone
ye á tu á tete á daare á tɔge Wɛ nia yam to,
kwaane-na se á lɔre Baŋa Wɛ.
Ta‑á ke-na kolo na lana to,
se á daare á tu á tete Wɛ yiga ne.
Dɛ delo Baŋa Wɛ wó kwoli abam
se chɔgem dem yé tɔge de yi abam
o ban-zɔŋɔ dɛ dem ne.
Filisi tiina taane
4Ta‑á yei-na we nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá daare Gaza teo wone.
Asekelon de wó taa ye di-dwonnu yerane.
Ba lage ba zeili Asedodi tiina maama ba yage,
ye wɛ ta wo yi yupare baŋa.
Ba ta wó gɔ Ekoron tiina de ba yage.
5Abam Filisi tiina balo na zoore naneo kom ni ne to,
lɛɛro wo á yuu ne!
Abam Filisi tiina na zoore Kanaan ne to,
Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o di abam taane ye o we,
“Amo nam wó yɔɔre a chɔge abam
ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá lu.”
6Abam teene delo na bwola de naneo kom to
wó ji naane pwola de najere mo.
7Judah dwi tiina balo na daare to mo wó jwoori
ba jwoŋi á tega kam ba taa tei.
Ba vara wó taa beeri ba di jei sem konto ne.
Tega ná yeini ka yi,
nayera bam wó peini Asekelon di-dwonnu ne.
Ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó taa nii ba baŋa ne
pa se ba jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo.
Moaba de Amon tiina taane
8Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to maa we:
“A nigi Moaba tiina de Amon tiina na jege a nɔɔna bam ba twea
ye ba yaale-ba tei to.
Ba maa bere ba tete we
ba wó jwoŋi ba tega kam ba taa tei.
9Ne amo Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to,
ko ye chega mo we,
Moaba de Amon tiina bam wó yɔɔre ba na chɔgem
nenɛɛne ko na ke Sodom de Gomora teene dem tei to.
Ba teene dem wó ji yɛ-bɔɔro de di-dwonnu yerane,
ye ga-cheiŋo lware tega kam maama taa wuu.
A nɔɔna balo na daare to mo lage ba vere ba wonnu
ye ba daare ba jwoŋi ba tega kam.”
10Konto to, Moaba de Amon tiina bam wó na ba nyɔɔre
ba teera yam baŋa ne,
de ba na jege Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam ba twea
ye ba mɔne-ba to ŋwaane.
11 Baŋa Wɛ mo lage o yɔɔre o fugi-ba,
ye o pa se tega baŋa wa yam maama dam ti.
Logo baŋa teene dem maama ná maŋe ba zoore mɛ maama,
ba laam wó ba ba taa zuli wonto Baŋa Wɛ.
Kusi tiina taane
12Ko ta ná ye abam Kusi tiina bam,
Baŋa Wɛ mo lage o pa á te jara wone.
Asiria tiina taane
13 Baŋa Wɛ wó zaŋe teene delo na wo tega-baŋa seeni to baŋa ne.
O lage o yɔɔre o chɔge Asiria de ko teo kamunu Ninevɛ,
pa se tega kam ji te-kora jei
mɛ nɔɔn-nɔɔno na tera to.
14Naane de pei wó taa peini teo kom wone
ko ta woli de ga-vara dwi maama.
Kunkworru de bachangaaro maa wó taa tigi di-dwonnu tem ne te keera.
Te da-ŋonno tem maama wó taa tigi mo ja,
pa se nɔɔna taa tui ba le-te.
15Ninevɛ teo kom ya lana dedɛ.
Nɔɔna balo na zoore ko wone to tiini ba jege kamunni mo
ye kolokolo ba daane-ba.
Ba maa boŋe we banto teo kom mo dwoi
teene dem maama logo baŋa ne.
Teo kom konto nam mo lage ko ji di-dwonnu
se ga-vara dwi maama taa tigi da.
Balo maama na wó tɔge da ba kɛ to
wó yeeri mo ye ba dole ba je.

english_text:
Sinful Jerusalem
1Too bad for that disgusting,
corrupt, and lawless city!
2Forever rebellious
and rejecting correction,
Jerusalem refuses to trust
or obey the Lord God.
