3Its officials are roaring lions,
its judges are wolves;
in the evening they attack,
by morning nothing is left.
4Jerusalem's prophets are proud
and not to be trusted.
The priests have disgraced
the place of worship
and abused God's Law.
5All who do evil are shameless,
but the Lord does right
and is always fair.
With the dawn of each day,
God brings about justice.
6The Lord wiped out nations
and left fortresses
crumbling in the dirt.
Their streets and towns
were reduced to ruins
and emptied of people.
7God felt certain that Jerusalem
would learn to respect
and obey him.
Then he would hold back
from punishing the city
and not wipe it out.
But everyone there was eager
to start sinning again.
Nations Will Turn to the Lord
8The Lord said:
Just wait for the day
when I accuse you nations.
I have decided on a day,
when I will bring together
every nation and kingdom
and punish them all
in my fiery anger.
I will become furious
and destroy the earth.
9I will purify each language
and make those languages
acceptable for praising me.
Then, with hearts united,
everyone will serve
only me, the Lord.
10From across the rivers
of Ethiopia,
my scattered people,
my true worshipers,
will bring offerings to me.
11When that time comes,
you won't rebel against me
and be put to shame.
I'll do away with those
who are proud and arrogant.
Never will any of them
strut around
on my holy mountain.
12But I, the Lord, won't destroy
any of your people
who are truly humble
and turn to me for safety.
13 The people of Israel who survive
will live right
and refuse to tell lies.
They will eat and rest
with nothing to fear.
A Song of Celebration
14Everyone in Jerusalem and Judah,
celebrate and shout
with all your heart!
15Zion, your punishment is over.
The Lord has forced your enemies
to turn and retreat.
Your Lord is King of Israel
and stands at your side;
you don't have to worry
about any more troubles.
16Jerusalem, the time is coming,
when it will be said to you:
“Don't be discouraged
or grow weak from fear!
17The Lord your God
wins victory after victory
and is always with you.
He celebrates and sings
because of you,
and he will refresh your life
with his love.”
The Lord's Promise to His People
18The Lord has promised:
Your sorrow has ended,
and you can celebrate.
19I will punish those
who mistreat you.
I will bring together the lame
and the outcasts,
then they will be praised,
instead of despised,
in every country on earth.
20I will lead you home,
and with your own eyes
you will see me bless you
with all you once owned.
Then you will be famous
everywhere on this earth.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Jerusalem tiina taane
1Lɛɛro wo á teo kom baŋa ne!
Ko nɔn-bia bam maa ye zwabani-nyena,
de puseŋ-nyena, de nɔn-kayɛ yerane mo.
2Ba tiini ba jege yi-dɛɛre
ye ba ve koresem.
Ba wo ke ba wo-dedoa de ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom
naa ba sale o yera ne.
3Teo kom nakwa bam yeini ba fugi nɔɔna
nenɛɛne nywonnu na ŋuuri tei to mo.
Ko dedɛɛra bam jege wo-loŋo
ne wiira na ba di ba daara se tega poore-ko tei to mo.
4Ba sampwori sem maa ye kampin-nyena na jege nia yalei to.
Ba kaanem tiina bam ve Wɛ nia yam
pa se ba chɔge Wɛ diga kam chullu tem.
5 Baŋa Wɛ nam ta wo teo kom wone.
O maa jege chega yerane
ye o ba tusa de fenfee de.
Tega ná yeini ka poore dɛ maama wone o toŋa
se chega kam mo jeini ka pa o nɔɔna,
ye o ba yaga.
Puseŋ-nyena bam nam ta toŋe lwarem mo
ye chaveera ba jege-ba.
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
6“Amo chɔge logo baŋa dwi tiina dedɛ,
pa se ba dam jei sem to buru-tu-tu.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa tera ba teene dem wone.
Nɔɔna maa ba tɔge de chwei sem ba via.
Ba te-fwaaro tem maama tigi mo zɛɛra,
ye nɔɔno de dedoa de wo daare.
7A nam ya boŋe we abam laam wó taa kɔre amo
ye á sɛ a koresem dem.
A nɔɔna bam ya ná ke konto,
ba sam dem ya bá na chɔgem,
ye a waarem dem bá yi-ba.
Ba nam yɔɔre ba kwaane mo ba toŋe lwarem
ba dɛ dɛ totoŋa baŋa ne.”
8 Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we:
“Konto ŋwaane cheigi-na se a laam ba abam tei.
Dɛ dem konto ne amo wó zaŋe a bere we
logo baŋa dwi tiina bam ba jege chega.
Amo boŋe a ja se a la logo baŋa dwi tiina bam
de balo na zoore teene dem maama ne to mo a ke daane,
se a pa ba lɔre a ban-lom na ye tei to.
Amo wó pa se a bane tiini de zaŋe ba baŋa ne
ye logo kom maama wó chɔge zɔŋ-zɔŋ,
ne mini na zwɛ wonnu tei to.
9Amo laam wó leiri nɔɔna bam ni-taana,
pa se ba maama taa lwoori amo Baŋa Wɛ
ne ko na maŋe se ba ke tei to.
Ba maama wó tɔge daane ba zuli-ne de ni dedwe.
10Ko ta ná ye amo nɔɔna balo na jage ba vo ba gaale Kusi bwi sem,
ye ba zoore teo konto yiga yiga wone ba zuli-ne to,
banto wó ja ba pɛɛra ba jwoori ba ba ba pa-ne.
11Kanto maŋa kam ná yia, abam daa bá taa wo chaveera wone
de á na nwoŋi a kwaga ne tei to ŋwaane.
Kokuri to, amo wó le balo maama na bere ba tete kamunim to á wone.
Nɔɔna daa bá taa jege teera
peo kolo amo na zoore da to baŋa ne.
12Ko ná ye nɔɔna balo na wó daare á wone to,
banto wó taa ye nabwona balo na gwooni ba tete to.
Ba ta wó taa sale amo Baŋa Wɛ yera ne.
13Isarele dwi tiina balo ta na daare to bá ke nɔɔn-nɔɔno lwarem.
Ba bá fɔ vwa, ye ba nam bá gane ba dwonna.
Ba wó na peiga jei ye ba sii.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá fugi-ba.”
14Zion tiina bam, ta‑á leeni-na!
Isarele tiina bam maama, ke-na sɔɔ na ywona to!
Jerusalem teo kom tiina, ta‑á jege-na wopwolo
ye á chaka lanyerane!
15Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ lage o le abam á waarem dem maama wone.
O ta wó zeili á dona bam maama o yage.
Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina pɛ to wo abam tei ne.
Foone daa ba jege se ko ja abam daga.
16Dɛ dem konto ná yia,
ba wó ta de Jerusalem tiina bam we:
“Zion tiina bam, yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone.
Nam yé pa-na á vɔna pare.
17Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wo abam tei ne.
O jege dam ne babea tei se o ma o vere abam.
Baŋa Wɛ yiga wó taa wo abam baŋa ne,
ye á jwoori á na dam o swono kom ŋwaane.
O daa ta wó puli seinim lei á ŋwaane,
18nenɛɛne nɔɔna na di kuri ye ba jege wopwolo tei to.”
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
“Amo lage a le lɛɛro telo na wo á baŋa ne to a yage.
Chaveera daa ba jege se ya ja abam.
19Nii-na! Maŋa kam ná yia,
amo wó waare balo na bɛɛse abam to.
A ta wó jwoŋi balo na ye gwaaro to,
a daare a la balo maama na jage to a ke daane.
Amo wó pa se ba chaveera leiri ya ji zula,
pa se ba na yere logo baŋa jei maama ne.
20Maŋa kam konto ne, a lage a la abam a ke daane,
pa se á jwoori sɔŋɔ mo.
A ta wó pa se á na zula ye á yere zaŋe
logo baŋa dwi maama tei ne,
ye á jwoori á ta‑á jege yu-ywoŋo.
Abam yia wó na amo keim dem konto.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_text:
Rebuild the Temple
1 On the first day of the sixth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak his message to the governor of Judah and to the high priest.
So Haggai told Governor Zerubbabel and High Priest Joshua 2-5that the Lord All-Powerful had said to them and to the people:
You say this isn't the right time to build a temple for me. But is it right for you to live in expensive houses, while my temple is a pile of ruins? Just look at what's happening. 6You harvest less than you plant, you never have enough to eat or drink, your clothes don't keep you warm, and your wages are stored in bags full of holes.
7Think about what I have said! 8But first, go to the hills and get wood for my temple, so I can take pride in it and be worshiped there. 9You expected much, but received only a little. And when you brought it home, I made that little disappear. Why have I done this? It's because you hurry off to build your own houses, while my temple is still in ruins. 10That's also why the dew doesn't fall and your harvest fails. 11And so, at my command everything will become barren—your farmland and pastures, your vineyards and olive trees, your animals and you yourselves. All your hard work will be for nothing.
12Zerubbabel and Joshua, together with the others who had returned from exile in Babylonia, obeyed the Lord's message spoken by his prophet Haggai, and they started showing proper respect for the Lord. 13Haggai then told them that the Lord had promised to be with them. 14So the Lord God All-Powerful made everyone eager to work on his temple, especially Zerubbabel and Joshua. 15And the work began on the twenty-fourth day of that same month.
translation_text:
Wɛ diga kam kwɛɛm
1Bene delo Pɛ Darusi na di paare o ke bena yalei to chane seredo boboa dɛ dem ne mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora déem yi o sampwora Hagayi. Kwora kam nam ye se ka pa Selateli bu Zerubabel mo. Wonto déem mo ye Judah teo kom maama yuu tu. Ka ta maa jege se ka yi Jehozadaki bu Josua, o na ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu to.
2Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam tage tento mo o bere Hagayi we, “Nɔɔna bam kare ba tɛ ba we, maŋa ta wo yi se ba fɔge ba lɔ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam.” 3Baŋa Wɛ laam ma pa o sampwora Hagayi kwora se o lwoni o bere nɔɔna bam ye o we:
4“Abam na zoore sɔ-ŋonno telo na fɔge lanyerane wone to, ye amo diga kam laam zege nenɛɛne di-dwoŋo to, ko maŋe na? 5Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ta maa we: Fɔge á maane á ŋwea wone se á nii ko na ye tei to. 6Abam ná yeini á du wo-dwa dedɛ, á wó zage fenfee mo. Abam seene á ba gae se á di. Ko nam na ye tei to, á ba fɔge á di á sui. Á jege na se á nyɔ, ye na-nyɔm ta jege abam. Gwaaro telo á na zoore á yera ne to maa ba kwoli á waaro. Á na toŋe se á jwoŋi ŋweero telo to ba fɔge te woli abam, ko nye de á kwei-te á ke gare-fɛɛla yalo na jege bɔɔna to wone mo.
7Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam we: Fɔge á maane á ŋwea wone se á nii ko na ye tei to. 8Diini-na peero tem yuu ne á beeri da-ŋonno á ja á ba. Laam kwei-na-se á ma á fɔge á lɔ diga kalo amo yi na wo taa sui to, se á daare á ta‑á zuli-ne ka wone. 9Abam ya teene se á zage wodiu dedɛ mo, ye ko ji fenfee ko pa abam. Kolo á na maŋe á ja á zo diga to mo a fuli de vio a yage a daare abam. Bɛ mo ye a ke konto? Ko ye abam yia na seene á tete sam lɔɔm baŋa ne, ye á yage amo diga kam pa se ka ji di-dwoŋo ka zega to ŋwaane mo. 10Konto ŋwaane nam mo pa se nyɔnɔ daa ba toe. Tega kam de maa ware wodiu se ka ke ka pa abam. 11Amo ta ma pa se da-kore zege á tega kam maama baŋa ne. Ko ná ye á kare sem, de peero tem, de mɛ maama wodiiru na lage te ke to, de mena, de Vini teeni, de Olivi nuga teeni na wo mɛ to, tento maama kwaare mo. Ko ma zo abam tete yera dedaane á vara maama yera, ye á totoŋa maama de ji kafɛ.”
12Zerubabel, de Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu Josua, ko woli de balo maama na dɛ ba nwoŋi sa-teene yiga yiga ba jwoori Jerusalem to maama na nigi Wɛ sampwora Hagayi taane dem konto to, ba déem ma sɛ ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam. Ba ma sɛ we Baŋa Wɛ ni dem tɔge Hagayi baŋa ne mo de yi-ba, ye ba bobo se ba taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ de chega.
13 Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Hagayi déem ma kwei Wɛ ni dem o pa nɔɔna bam ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ pwooli we, o wora de abam mo.”
14 Baŋa Wɛ ma ja nɔɔna bam maama boboŋa o ke daane. Ko ná ye Zerubabel na ye Judah teo kom yuu tu to, de Josua na ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu to, de balo maama de na dɛ ba nwoŋi sa-teo yiga yiga ba jwoori to, ba maama ma ba ba gilimi daane, se ba taa toŋe Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye ba Wɛ to diga kam lɔɔm totoŋa. 15Darusi paare dim bena yalei tu bene dem chane seredo sem da finlei-yana dɛ dem ne mo ba déem bobo ba fɔge ba lɔ Wɛ diga kam.

english_text:
The Glorious New Temple
1-2On the twenty-first day of the next month, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak this message to Governor Zerubbabel, High Priest Joshua, and everyone else:
3 Does anyone remember how glorious this temple used to be? Now it looks like nothing. 4But cheer up! Because I, the Lord All-Powerful, will be here to help you with the work, 5 just as I promised your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt. Don't worry. My Spirit is right here with you.
6 Soon I will again shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land. 7I will shake the nations, and their treasures will be brought here. Then the brightness of my glory will fill this temple. 8All silver and gold belong to me, 9and I promise that this new temple will be more glorious than the first one. I will also bless this city with peace.
The Past and the Future
10On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the Lord God All-Powerful told the prophet Haggai 11to ask the priests for their opinion on the following matters:
12Suppose meat ready to be sacrificed to God is being carried in the folds of someone's clothing, and the clothing rubs against some bread or stew or wine or olive oil or any other food. Would those foods that were touched then become acceptable for sacrifice?
“Of course not,” the priests answered.
13 Then Haggai said, “Suppose someone has touched a dead body and is considered unacceptable to worship God. If that person touches these foods, would they become unclean?”
“Of course they would,” the priests answered.
14So the Lord told Haggai to say:
That's how it is with this entire nation. Everything you do and every sacrifice you offer is unacceptable to me. 15But from now on, things will get better. Before you started laying the foundation for the temple, 16you recalled what life was like in the past. When you wanted 200 kilograms of wheat, there were only 10, and when you wanted 50 jars of wine, there were only 20. 17I made all of your hard work useless by sending mildew, mold, and hail—but you still did not return to me, your Lord.
18Today you have completed the foundation for my temple, so listen to what your future will be like. 19Although you have not yet harvested any grain, grapes, figs, pomegranates, or olives, I will richly bless you in the days ahead.
God's Promise to Zerubbabel
20That same day the Lord spoke to Haggai again and said:
21Tell Governor Zerubbabel of Judah that I am going to shake the heavens and the earth 22and wipe out kings and their kingdoms. I will overturn war chariots, and then cavalry troops will start slaughtering each other. 23But tell my servant Zerubbabel that I, the Lord All-Powerful, have chosen him, and he will rule in my name.
translation_text:
Wɛ di-doŋa kam nenɔŋa taane
1Chane serepɛ sem da finlei dedwe dɛ dem ne mo Baŋa Wɛ ŋɔɔne de o sampwora Hagayi. 2O ma ta‑o se o lwoni o kwora kam o bere Selateli bu Zerubabel na ye Judah teo kom yuu tu to, de Jehozadaki bu Josua na ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu to, dedaane nɔɔna balo na dɛ ba nwoŋi sa-teo ba jwoori to maama. Wɛ ma bwei-ba o we:
3“Abam wɔ mo nɛ Wɛ diga kam nenɔŋa déem na ye tei boboa ne to ye n ta wora zem? Á nam ná lage se á kwei ka déem na ye tei se á maŋe de ka zem nenɔŋa kam, ko ye tetɛ mo? Abam wo maane we ka daa ba jege zula se ka yi Wɛ di-dwoŋa kam na? 4Nam yé pa-na se á vɔna pare ko ŋwaane, se amo, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wo abam tei ne. Zerubabel, de Josua, ko ta woli de á kɔgɔ kom maama, ke-na baare á tete ne se á ta‑á toŋa. 5Maŋa kalo á kwoa bam déem na nwoŋi Ejipti ne to mo a yɔɔre a gwoni ni de-ba we, amo wó taa wora de abam. Amo Jworo ta maa wo abam tei ne. Nam yé ta‑á fona.
6Amo, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo we: Ko ná ke fee amo daa ta wó jwoori a pa se wɛyuu kom de tega baŋa maama ziziŋi. A nam ta wó ziziŋi naneero tem de tega kam maama. 7Amo wó pa se tega baŋa teene dem maama ziziŋi pa se de nɔn-bia bam zeŋe ba jejegero ba ba ywo-seeni. Amo diga kam laam wó tiini ka na nenɔŋa ko baŋa ne. 8Amo, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo we: Lu-nyenno tem, dedaane sabu-seŋa maama ye amo mo tei-te. 9Di-doŋa kanto abam na wora á lɔ to wó taa jege nenɔŋa se ko dwoni di-dwoŋa kam. Jei sem konto ne amo wó pa se a nɔɔna maama na yazura de bochare-zuru. Amo, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.”
Hagayi lare dedaane Wɛ kaanem tiina
10Bene delo Pɛ Darusi paare dim na wó ke bena yalei tu to chane nogo kom da finlei-yana dɛ dem ne mo Baŋa Wɛ daa pɛ o kwora yi o sampwora Hagayi. 11O maa we:
“Amo, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo we: Véi a kaanem tiina bam tei n bwei-ba n nii ba boŋe ba ja bɛ mo keim dento baŋa ne: 12Nɔɔno ná kwei nɔne delo ba na pɔɔre-de ba tiŋi Wɛ kaanem ŋwaane, ye o kukuli-de o ke o gɔrɔ wone, o ná tu o kwei gɔrɔ kom konto o dwei wodiu kolo dwi maama, keim dem konto wó wane de pa se wodiu kolo o gɔrɔ kom na dwei to lɛɛre ko taa ye wose na? Ko ná ye bworobworo, naa dwoa, naa sana, naa nuga, naa wodiu kolo dwi maama, ko wó ke konto na?” Kaanem tiina bam ma leiri we, “Aawo.”
13Hagayi daa ma bwei-ba o we, “Se nɔɔno nam ná dwei too yera pa se ko bere we o digiri o tete de chullu tem mo, ye o laam ná tu o dwei wodiiru tento maama, o keim dem konto wó pa se wodiiru tem digiri na?” Kaanem tiina bam ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ɛɛ, te de wó digiri mo.”
14Hagayi laam maa we:
“Baŋa Wɛ nam tage we, o nii teo konto de ko nɔn-bia bam se ko taa ye konto mo. O nɛ we á na ke kikia yalo to, de á na yeini á kwei wonnu telo á ma á ke kaanem o bimbini dem baŋa ne á pa‑o to maama wo maŋe de o chullu tem mo. 15Baŋa Wɛ nam we:
Ko na zege zem se ko taa via, fɔge-na á maane á nii ko na ye tei to. Guli-na abam ya ta na wo beiri amo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam kuri ye á na cham tei to. 16Á ná vei á kare sem wone, á teene se á ja wodiu zwe finlei mo á zo diga ye zwe fuga yerane mo wora. Abam ta ná teena se á ŋoke sana á ke kunkwollu finnu wone, á wó lwo-ba á su kunkwollu finlei yerane mo. 17Ko ye amo mo pɛ se we-chera, de do-kandwa, de wodiiru jaweero ja á jeŋa totoŋa te chɔge. De konto maama nam, abam ta wo jwoori amo tei. 18Ko nam na zege zem dɛ dem na ye chane nogo kom da finlei-yana to, fɔge-na á maane á nii ko na ye tei to. Boŋe-na á nii Wɛ diga kam kuri zem na chwi se ko taa via ye ko ke abam tei to. 19Abam ta jege mena á tuli wone na? Ko ná ye á teeni dem, Vini teeni, de Olivi teeni, de kaporro, de Pomegara teeni, de daa ta wora de leiri bia na? De ko maama de, ko na zege zem se ko taa via, amo mo lage a swɛ abam swolim.”
Baŋa Wɛ gwoni ni o pa Zerubabel
20Dɛ dem konto na ye chana kam da finlei-yana to, mo Baŋa Wɛ daa pɛ Hagayi kwora o ke kuni belei. 21O maa we:
“Zaŋe n vo Judah teo kom yuu tu Zerubabel tei n ta we: Amo lage a pa se wɛyuu kom de tega baŋa maama vuvugi. 22A ta wó ja dwi-gɛ tiina pwa, se ba paare dim dam maama ti. A lage a pipiri jara-keim sisei-torokooro de balo na diini-te to mo a pu tega ne. Jar-keira sisein-nɔɔna bam maa wó to tega ne, ye balo na diini-se to go daane pa se ba maama te.
23Amo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ we: Dɛ dem konto nam ná yia, amo mo lage a le nmo Zerubabel na ye Selateli bu to. Nmo ye a tontoŋeno. A nam wó pa se n kwei amo yere n ma‑n ta‑n tei a nɔɔna bam, nenɛɛne nmo ye jafole na bere amo dam tei to mo. Kokuri to, nmo mo ye wolo a na kuri to.
Amo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.”

english_text:
Turn to the Lord
1 I am the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo.
In the eighth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told me to say:
2-3Israel, I, the Lord All-Powerful, was very angry with your ancestors. But if you people will return to me, I will turn and help you. 4Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. They were warned by the earlier prophets to give up their evil and turn back to me, but they paid no attention.
5Where are your ancestors now? Not even prophets live forever. 6But my warnings and my words spoken by the prophets caught up with your ancestors. So they turned back to me and said, “Lord All-Powerful, you have punished us for our sins, just as you had planned.”
First Vision: Horses and Riders
7-8 On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, which was the eleventh month of that same year, the Lord spoke to me in a vision during the night: In a valley among myrtle trees, I saw someone on a red horse, with riders on red, brown, and white horses behind him. 9An angel was there to explain things to me, and I asked, “Sir, who are these riders?”
“I'll tell you,” the angel answered.
10At once, the man standing among the myrtle trees said, “These are the ones the Lord has sent to find out what's happening on earth.”
11Then the riders spoke to the Lord's angel, who was standing among the myrtle trees, and they said, “We have gone everywhere and have discovered that the whole world is at peace.”
12At this, the angel said, “Lord All-Powerful, for 70 years you have been angry with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. When are you ever going to have mercy on them?”
13The Lord's answer was kind and comforting. 14So the angel told me to announce:
I, the Lord All-Powerful, am very protective of Jerusalem. 15For a while I was angry at the nations, but now I am furious, because they have made things worse for Jerusalem and are not the least bit concerned. 16And so, I will have pity on Jerusalem. The city will be completely rebuilt, and my temple will stand again. 17I also promise that my towns will prosper—Jerusalem will once again be my chosen city, and I will comfort the people of Zion.
Second Vision: Animal Horns
18Next, I saw four animal horns. 19-21The angel who was sent to explain was there, and so I asked, “What do these mean?”
His answer was, “These horns are the nations that scattered the people of Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem, and took away their freedom.”
Then the Lord showed me four blacksmiths, and I asked, “What are they going to do?”
He replied, “They are going to terrify and crush those horns.”
translation_text:
Fɔɔre-na á twɛ Baŋa Wɛ
1Darusi paare dim bena yalei bene dem chane nana chana kam wone mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora déem yi o sampwora Zekaria. Wonto kwo déem ye Ido bu Berekia mo.
2 Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam mo tento:
A bane déem zaŋe de abam kwoa bam. 3Nam ta de nɔɔna bam we: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Jwoori-na á ba amo tei, se amo de pipiri a jeeri abam. 4Abam de yé ta‑á ke ne á nabaara bam déem na ke tei to. Faŋa to, Wɛ sampwori sedwonna déem tage de-ba mo ba we: ‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tage tento mo de abam: Yage-na á totoŋ-balwaaro tem se á pipiri á jwoori amo tei ne.’ Ba nam wo cheigi amo kwora kam.” Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. 5Á nabaara bam konto laam wo yein-seeni mo? Se Wɛ sampwori sem konto de, ba wó taa wora taa wuu na? 6Ko nam ná ye amo nia yam de a bera yam a déem na pɛ a sampwori sem konto to, ya wo seene ya ke ya ja á kwoa bam na? Banto de ma pipiri ba jwoori ba ba amo tei, ye ba we, “Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ seene o waare debam mo dé kikia ŋwaane, se ko maŋe de o boboŋa na maŋe ya ja se o ke tei to.”
Wɛ veere wonnu o bere Zekaria
1. Sisein-dira taane
7Chane fuga-dedoa chana kam da finlei-yana dɛ dem ne, Baŋa Wɛ kwora déem yi o sampwora Zekaria, o kwo na ye Ido bu Berekia to. Sebate chana kam ne mo konto. Ko maa ye Darusi paare dim bena yalei bene dem ne.
8Tete dem ne mo amo Zekaria nii a na nɔɔno na dɔge sisein-nɔɔno baŋa ne, ka na ye nasoŋo. Mɛ seeni o na zega da to ye bwolo mo ye Motele teeni su ko maama. O laam maa wo de tetare ne. A ta ma na we sisein-nɔɔna sedwonna mo zega o kwaga ne, se na ye nasonno, de nason-pupwiu, de napwonnu, ye nɔɔna de dɔge se baŋa ne.
9Wɛ maleka kadwoŋi déem zege da, ka na ŋɔɔne de-ne. A ma bwei‑o a we, “Amo tu, bɛ mo ye banto maama zege da?” O de ma leiri-ne o we, “Amo wó ta ko kuri a bere‑m.”
10Nɔɔno wolo na wo teeni dem tetare ne to laam ma ta o we, “Banto ye balo Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe se ba taa kare logo ni maama se ba lɔre kolo na jege ko ke da to.” 11Balo na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna bam baŋa ne to de maa lwoni ba kwori ba bere Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam na wo teeni dem tetare ne to ba we, “Debam kaare tega baŋa ni maama, ye dé maane we logo kom maama ye ziim mo, ye kolokolo ba dɔna.”
12 Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam laam ma ta ka we, “Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ, bena fuserepɛ mo tento nmo bane na yɔɔre de wo Jerusalem teo kom, de Judah teene dem maama baŋa ne. Maŋa kɔ mo nmo bane dem wó to se n duri ba ŋwaŋa?” 13Baŋa Wɛ ma ŋɔɔne ta-laaro telo na bwona ye te zuri bochara to o ma leiri maleka kalo na zege ka ŋɔɔne de amo to. 14Maleka kam konto ma ta de amo ka we, “Pa kwora kanto zaŋe wɛɛne we, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Amo yi page a tete teo Jerusalem baŋa ne. 15A bane nam tiini de zaŋe de teene dedwonna dem na boŋe we kolokolo bá daane-ba to mo. Kokuri to, a bane ya zaŋe de a nɔɔna bam fenfee yerane mo. Dwi-gɛ tiina bam laam ma yɔɔre ba pa ko zo ba yera se ko dwoni a ya na boŋe se a ke-ba tei to.’ 16Konto ŋwaane, Baŋa Wɛ tage tento mo o we: ‘Amo laam pipiri a jwoori a ba Jerusalem se a duri a nɔɔna bam ŋwaŋa. Amo diga kam wó jwoori ka lɔ ka zege teo kom wone. Ba ta wó kwei lɔra ŋona kam ba maŋe Jerusalem teo kom ni maama se ba fɔge ba lɔ-ko.’ Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
17Nam ta pa se n kwora zaŋe wɛɛne we: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Teene delo a nɔɔna bam na zoore de wone to daa wó na jejegero dedɛ se ko gaale. Amo Baŋa Wɛ daa ta wó pa se Zion nɔn-bia bam bochara zuri. A ta wó jwoori a le Jerusalem se ko taa ye a tete nyem.’ ”
2. Nyea yana de gwaro tena taane
18Amo ma kwoni a yuu wɛɛne a nii a na nyea yana. 19A ma bwei maleka kalo na zege ka ŋɔɔne de amo to a we, “Nyea yanto bere bɛ mo?” O de ma leiri-ne o we, “Nyea yam zege ya pa dwi-gɛ tiina balo na mɛ ba dam ba wane Judah tiina bam, de Isarele tiina bam, de Jerusalem teo nɔɔna bam ba jage jei maama ne to mo.”
20 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma le gwaro tena o bere-ne. 21A ma bwei‑o a we, “Banto beene ywo se ba ke bɛ totoŋe mo?” O ma leiri o we, “Nyea yam ya jage Judah tiina bam mo se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé wane o le o yuu o ke keim. Gwaro tento nam mo lage ba fugi nyea yam, se ba daare ba chochoge ya dam, se teene delo na daane a nɔɔna Judah tiina bam ye ba jage-ba to dam ti.”

english_text:
Third Vision: A Measuring Line
1This time I saw someone holding a measuring line, 2and I asked, “Where are you going?”
“To measure Jerusalem,” was the answer. “To find out how wide and long it is.”
3The angel who had spoken to me came toward me, when another angel came up to him 4and said, “Hurry! Tell that man with the measuring line that Jerusalem won't have any boundaries. It will be too full of people and animals even to have a wall. 5The Lord himself has promised to be a protective wall of fire surrounding Jerusalem, and he will be its shining glory in the heart of the city.”
A Call to Action
6The Lord says to his people, “Run! Escape from the land in the north, where I scattered you to the four winds. 7Leave Babylonia and hurry back to Zion.”
8Then the glorious Lord All-Powerful ordered me to say to the nations that had raided and robbed Zion:
Zion is as precious to the Lord as are his eyes. Whatever you do to Zion, you do to him. 9And so, he will put you in the power of your slaves, and they will raid and rob you. Then you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful.
10City of Zion, sing and celebrate! The Lord has promised to come and live with you. 11When he does, many nations will turn to him and become his people. At that time you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful. 12Then Judah will be his part of the holy land, and Jerusalem will again be his chosen city.
13Everyone, be silent!
The Lord is present
and moving about
in his holy place.
translation_text:
3. Nɔɔno wolo na zei lɔra ŋona o jeŋa ne to taane
1Amo ma kwoni a yuu wɛɛne a nii a na nɔn-doŋo na zege da ye kotu zei lɔra ŋona o jeŋa ne. 2A ma bwei‑o a we, “Nmo ma‑n vei yei ne mo?” O ma leiri o we, “A maa vei se a maŋe Jerusalem teo kom ni mo, se a lɔre ko dedɔrem, de ko kayɔlɔ maŋem na ye tei to.” 3A daa ma na we maleka kalo ya na zege ka ŋɔɔne de amo to fɔɔre ka kɛ dáa, ye maleka kadwoŋi de fɔɔre ka yi kanto de tei. 4Ka maa we: “Ke lela n vo n ta de nɔn-doŋo kom we, ‘Jerusalem wó tiini ko taa yala se ko daa yé taa jege siseini. Ko nɔn-bia de ko vara de nam wó gaale pa ba bá wane ba lɔ kabiri ba che-ko. 5Amo Baŋa Wɛ tete mo wó ji kabira kalo na ye mini yerane to, ye a kaare teo kom maama a pu. A nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom de wó taa wo teo kom tetare ne ko bere a dam jaja. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ”
Balo na wo sa-teo ne to taane
6 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Hei! Duri-na á nwoŋi baŋa seeni teo kolo wone ba na peene abam to! Kokuri to, amo mo ya seene a jage abam a yage logo baŋa sapɛ sena sem maama seeni. 7Abam balo na ye a nɔɔna ye á zoore Babilon teo tiina bam tei ne to, duri-na á lu se á jwoori Zion seeni!” 8Kolo ŋwaane, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ pɛ-ne ni mo se a da o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom ŋwaane a vo a kaane dwi-gɛ tiina balo na bɛɛse abam to, o yi na page abam baŋa ne to ŋwaane. Wolo ná ke abam zonne, ko nye de kotu ke Wɛ tete yi-chele-bu mo zonne. 9Konto ŋwaane, Baŋa Wɛ tɛ dwi-gɛ tiina bam taane o we, “A lage a kwei a dam mo a chochoge-ba, se a daare a pa ba kabɛ selo ya na toŋe se pa-ba to laam zi-ba ba daare ba vere ba wonnu.” Abam laam maa wó lɔre we Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo seene o toŋe-ne.
10Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Zion tiina bam, leeni-na wopwolo lei! Kokuri to, a lage a ba a taa zoore á tetare ne mo. 11Dɛ dem konto ná yia, dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ wó pipiri ba ba ba sɛ amo Baŋa Wɛ ye ba daare ba ji a nɔɔna. A maa wó taa zoore á tetare ne.” Ko ná ke konto, abam de laam wó lɔre we Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo seene o toŋe-ne abam tei ne. 12Baŋa Wɛ wó pɔɔre Judah laŋa kam o tete tega kam maama wone se o taa tei-ka. O daa ta wó le Jerusalem se ko taa ye o tete nyem.
13Nabiina maama nam maŋe se ba taa ye chemm Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne mo! Kokuri to, o dɔne o tete mo o zaŋe wɛɛne o telaao sɔŋɔ kom ne, ye o lage o nwoŋi o taa toŋe totoŋa.

english_text:
Fourth Vision: Joshua and Satan
1 I was given another vision. This time Joshua the high priest was standing in front of the Lord's angel. And there was Satan, standing at Joshua's right side, ready to accuse him. 2 But the Lord said, “Satan, you are wrong. Jerusalem is my chosen city, and this man was rescued like a stick from a flaming fire.”
3Joshua's clothes were filthy. 4So the angel told some of the people to remove Joshua's filthy clothes. Then he said to Joshua, “This means you are forgiven. Now I will dress you in priestly clothes.”
5I spoke up and said, “Also put a clean priestly turban on his head.” Then they dressed him in priestly clothes and put the turban on him, while the Lord's angel stood there watching.
6After this, the angel encouraged Joshua by telling him that the Lord All-Powerful had promised:
7If you truly obey me, I will put you in charge of my temple, including the courtyard around it, and you will be allowed to speak at any time with the angels standing beside me. 8 Listen carefully, High Priest Joshua and all of you other priests. You are a sign of things to come, because I am going to bring my servant, the Chosen King.
9Joshua, I have placed in front of you a stone with seven sides. I will engrave something on that stone, and in a single day I will forgive this guilty country. 10 Then each of you will live at peace and entertain your friends in your own vineyard and under your own fig trees.
translation_text:
4. Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu wom taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ daa ma le woŋo o bere-ne ye a na Josua na ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu to. O déem zege Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam yiga ne mo, ye Setaane de wo o jazem seeni se o ŋɔɔne Josua yera taane o chɔge‑o. 2Baŋa Wɛ ma tɔge o maleka kam baŋa o ta de Setaane o we, “Setaane, Baŋa Wɛ tete mo lage o bwɛ‑m! Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o le Jerusalem se ko taa ye o tete nyem mo, ye wonto mo wó bwɛ‑m! Nɔɔno wonto nye de daa kalo na jaane mini ye ba vaŋe-ka ba le de wone to mo.” 3Josua na zege maleka kam yiga ne konto to, o déem zo gare-digiru mo. 4Maleka kam ma ta de balo na zege ka tei ne to ka we, “Lɔɔre-na gare-digiru tem na wo o yera ne to.” O laam ma daare o ta de Josua o we, “Nii mo. Ko bere we a yage n wɛleera yam mo a ma a chɛ‑m. A laam wó kwei gare-nyenno mo a lɛ‑m.”
5Amo de ma ta a we, “Jan ja! Kwei-na yuu gare-yi delo na lana to á ma á ba o yuu kom.” Ba ma seene ba ke konto ye ba kwei gare-nyenno tem maama ba zo‑o. Ba déem ke konto ye Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam zege ka nia mo.
6 Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam laam ma pa Josua ni dento ye ka we:
7“Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Nmo ná tɔge a chwei sem n ŋwea wone, ye n toŋe n pa-ne ne a nia yam na bere tei to, amo de wó pa‑m chwoŋa se n ta‑n tei a sɔŋɔ kom de ko konkwallo tem maama. A ta maa wó pa n ta‑n jege chwoŋa se n tɔge de malese selo na zege ywo-seeni to n twɛ amo tei maŋa de maŋa.
8Josua, nmo nam na ye a kaanem nakwe tu to, nmo de n dwonna kaanem tiina balo na jeini n tei ne to fɔge-na á cheigi a taane dento. Abam ye memaŋa mo se ko bere wonnu telo na beene jwa seeni to. Nii mo, a lage a pa a tontoŋeno wolo ba na bwoi‑o we ‘Tio-naga’ to zaŋe o ba. 9A kwei kandwɛ dedoa mo a zege Josua yiga ne, ye de jege sɛ serepɛ. A nam lage a sare poponem mo a yage de baŋa ne. Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. A ta wó kwei dɛ dedwe yerane mo se a saare teo konto wɛleera yam maama a yage dáa ne. 10Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia, abam dedoa dedoa wó toŋe o bwoŋi o fara se ba ba ba jeini ded‑o o sɔŋɔ woro ne, se ba di wodiu daane ye lwia tera.
Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_text:
Fifth Vision: A Lampstand and Olive Trees
1The angel who explained the visions woke me from what seemed like sleep. 2Then he asked, “What do you see?”
“A solid gold lampstand with an oil container above it,” I answered. “On the stand are seven lamps, each with seven flames. 3 One olive tree is on the right side and another on the left of the oil container. 4But, sir, what do these mean?”
5Then he asked, “Don't you know?”
“No sir,” I replied.
6 So the angel explained that it was the following message of the Lord to Zerubbabel:
I am the Lord All-Powerful. So don't depend on your own power or strength, but on my Spirit. 7Zerubbabel, that mountain in front of you will be leveled to the ground. Then you will bring out the temple's most important stone and shout, “God has been very kind.”
8The Lord spoke to me again and said:
9Zerubbabel laid the foundation for the temple, and he will complete it. Then everyone will know that you were sent by me, the Lord All-Powerful. 10 Those who have made fun of this day of small beginnings will celebrate when they see Zerubbabel holding this important stone.
Those seven lamps represent my eyes—the eyes of the Lord—and they see everything on this earth.
11 Then I asked the angel, “What about the olive trees on each side of the lampstand? What do they represent? 12And what is the meaning of the two branches from which golden olive oil flows through the two gold pipes?”
13“Don't you know?” he asked.
“No sir, I don't,” was my answer.
14Then he told me, “These branches are the two chosen leaders who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”
translation_text:
5. Sabu-seŋa min-zwon-zego taane
1Maleka kalo ya na ŋɔɔne de amo to ma ba o susugi-ne, nenɛɛne a ya yɔɔre a dɔ mo to. 2O ma bwei-ne o we, “Bɛ mo nmo nɛa?” A ma leiri a we, “A nɛ min-zwon-zego ba na mɛ sabu-seŋa ba mɔ ko maama to mo. Zoŋa mo wo ko yuu kom seeni de ka wo nuga. Min-zwonnu terepɛ maa wo zego kom baŋa ne. Te maama dedoa dedoa maa jege nia yarepɛ. 3A nam ta nɛ Olivi teeni delei, pa dedoa zege zoŋa kam jazem seeni, ye kokom kom de zege ka jagwia seeni.”
4A ma bwei maleka kam na zege ka ŋɔɔne de amo to a we, “Amo tu, wonnu tento kuri ye bɛ mo?” 5Maleka kam de ma jwoori ka bwei-ne ka we, “Nmo yeiri wonnu tento kuri na?” A ma leiri a we, “Aawo.”
6O laam ma ta de amo o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na jege kwora kalo se o pa Zerubabel to mo tento: ‘Ko dae nmo bembɛɛne ŋwaane, naa n dam ŋwaane mo n lage n na yiga-veiŋa, se ko ye amo tete Jworo ŋwaane mo.’ Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
7Peo-zɔŋɔ kom na chege Zerubabel yiga to, n bere we n ye bɛ mo? Zerubabel yiga ne n jege se n palese mo n ji te-kampare. O laam maa wó ja kandwɛ delo na wó guri Wɛ diga kam to o ja o nwoŋi o ke da, se nɔɔna bam maama taa bage ba yaga we, ‘Wɛ zaane dem ŋwaane! Wɛ zaane dem ŋwaane!’ ”
8 Baŋa Wɛ laam ma pa-ne o kwora o we:
9“Zerubabel mo nii pa ba bobo Wɛ diga kanto kuri ba chwi ka biri-beira kam. Wonto nam ta mo wó pa ba lɔ-ka ba guri. Abam laam wó lɔre we ko seene ko ye Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo toŋe-ne abam tei ne. 10Wolo maama ná nɛ Wɛ diga kam lɔɔm na bobo mɛmɛ tei to ye o gwooni totoŋe dem, kotu wó ba o taa chaka de Zerubabel na zei lɔra ŋona ye diga kam lɔɔm kɛ yiga tei to.”
Maleka kam ta ma leiri-ne ka we:
“Min-zwonnu terepɛ tem nam zege te pae Baŋa Wɛ yia yam na dole ya kaare tega baŋa ni maama to mo.”
11Amo daa ma bwei maleka kam a we, “Olivi teeni delei dem na zege min-zwon-zego kom jazem seeni de ko jagwia seeni to kuri ye bɛ mo?” 12A ta ma bwei a we, “Se ko ná ye Olivi teeni nɛ selei sem na wo sabu-seŋa wo-worru telei tem nuga kam na tɔge te wone ka lwoi ka yage to saŋa ne to, se kuri ye bɛ mo?” 13O de ma jwoori o bwei-ne o we, “Nmo yeiri wonnu tento kuri na?” A ma leiri a we, “Aawo.”
14O laam ma ta o we, “Nɛ selei sem konto zege se pae yiga tiina balei balo ba na tiŋi se ba taa toŋe ba pa ba Tu Wɛ wom na tei logo baŋa ni maama to mo.”

english_text:
Sixth Vision: A Flying Scroll
1When I looked the next time, I saw a flying scroll, 2and the angel asked, “What do you see?”
“A flying scroll,” I answered. “About nine meters long and four and a half meters wide.”
3Then he told me:
This scroll puts a curse on everyone in the land who steals or tells lies. The writing on one side tells about the destruction of those who steal, while the writing on the other side tells about the destruction of those who lie.
4The Lord All-Powerful has said, “I am sending this scroll into the house of everyone who is a robber or tells lies in my name, and it will remain there until every piece of wood and stone in that house crumbles.”
Seventh Vision: A Woman in a Basket
5Now the angel who was there to explain the visions came over and said, “Look up and tell me what you see coming.”
6“I don't know what it is,” was my reply.
“It's a big basket,” he said. “And it shows what everyone in the land has in mind.”
7The lead cover of the basket was opened, and in the basket was a woman. 8“This woman represents evil,” the angel explained. Then he threw her back into the basket and slammed the heavy cover down tight.
9Right after this I saw two women coming through the sky with wings outstretched like a stork in the wind. Suddenly they lifted the basket into the air, 10and I asked the angel, “Where are they taking the basket?”
11“To Babylonia,” he answered, “where they will build a house for the basket and set it down inside.”
translation_text:
6. Tɔnɔ kolo na jaane wɛɛne to taane
1Amo daa ta ma kwoni a yuu wɛɛne ye a nii a na tɔnɔ mo na yɔɔre ko jaane wɛɛne ko tete ne.
2Maleka kam ma bwei-ne ka we, “Bɛ mo n nii n na?” Amo de ma leiri a we, “A nɛ tɔnɔ mo na jaane wɛɛne. Ko dedɔrem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finlei. Ko kayɔlɔ maŋem de maa ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni fuga.”
3O laam ma ta de amo o we, “Tɔnɔ konto jege sensɔle-balɔrɔ mo se ko ja vo ko yi tega baŋa ni maama. Tɔnɔ kom saŋa dedoa wone, ba sɔɔle lwarem mo ba yage balo na ŋɔne to yuu ne we, Wɛ wó saare-ba tega kam wone. Saŋa kadwoŋi kam wone, ba sɔɔle lwarem ba yage balo na bore vwa bora ba ma ba vane ba dwonna to yuu ne we, Wɛ wó saare ba de tega kam wone. 4Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na pɛ ni delo to mo tento: Amo wó toŋe tɔnɔ konto se ko zo ŋweeno sɔŋɔ, de wolo na mae amo yere o bore vwa bora to de sɔŋɔ. Ko nam ná yi da, ko wó maŋe kotu sɔŋɔ ne mo ko chɔge wonnu maama, se ko kabiri tete, de ko bei sem de da te chɔge.”
7. Kaane wolo na jei garewaa wone to taane
5Maleka kalo na ŋɔɔne de amo to laam ma fɔɔre ka yi a tei ye ka ta de amo ka we, “Nam daa‑n kwoni n yuu wɛɛne n nii kolo na zege da ko beene to.” 6Amo de ma bwei‑o a we, “Woŋo kom konto nam ye bɛ mo?” Maleka kam ma leiri ka we, “Woŋo kolo na beene to ye garewaa mo.” O daa ta maa we, “Ko zege ko pae tusim kikia yalo nɔɔna na ke tega kam maama wone to mo.”
7A ma nii a na we ba dɔne luu kolo ya na pugi garewaa kam ni to. A laam ma na we kaane mo jei ka wone. 8Maleka kam ma maŋe ko kuri ka bere-ne ka we, “Kaane wonto mo bere puseŋa kikia na ye tei to.” Ka laam ma yigi kaane wom lela ka jwoori ka yage garewaa kam wone, ye ka daare ka kwei ni-pugu kom ka pu ni dem goppe.
9A ta na kwoni a yuu a nii wɛɛne konto to mo a daa nɛ kaana balei na zege wɛyuu kom ne ba jaane ba maa beena. Ba maa yaare ba vɔna vio yiga ne ne buga ni zuna na ke tei to. Ba ma vo ba gɔ garewaa kam wɛɛne ba ja ba di wɛyuu baŋa.
10A ma bwei maleka kam a we, “Ba jege garewaa kam ba maa vei yei ne mo?” 11Ka de ma leiri-ne ka we, “Ba jege-ka ba maa vei Babilonia teo mo. Ba nam ná yi da, ba wó lɔ diga se ba kwei garewaa kam ba zege ka wone, se nɔɔna laam taa zuli-ka.”

english_text:
Eighth Vision: Four Chariots
1Finally, I looked up and saw four chariots coming from between two bronze mountains. 2 The first chariot was pulled by red horses, and the second by black horses; 3 the third chariot was pulled by white horses, and the fourth by spotted gray horses.
4“Sir,” I asked the angel. “What do these stand for?”
5 Then he explained, “These are the four winds of heaven, and now they are going out, after presenting themselves to the Lord of all the earth. 6The chariot with black horses goes toward the north, the chariot with white horses goes toward the west, and the one with spotted horses goes toward the south.”
7The horses came out eager to patrol the earth, and the angel told them, “Start patrolling the earth.”
When they had gone on their way, 8he shouted to me, “Those that have gone to the country in the north will do what the Lord's Spirit wants them to do there.”
The Chosen Leader
9The Lord said to me:
10-11Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah have returned from Babylonia. Collect enough silver and gold from them to make a crown. Then go with them to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah and put the crown on the head of the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak. 12-13 Tell him that I, the Lord All-Powerful, say, “Someone will reach out from here like a branch and build a temple for me. I will name him ‘Branch,’ and he will rule with royal honors. A priest will stand beside his throne, and the two of them will be good friends. 14This crown will be kept in my temple as a reminder and will be taken care of by Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah.”
15When people from distant lands come and help build the temple of the Lord All-Powerful, you will know that the Lord is the one who sent me. And this will happen, if you truly obey the Lord your God.
translation_text:
8. Torokooro tena taane
1Amo daa ma kwoni a yuu wɛɛne a nii a na sisei-torokooro tena na nwoŋi peero telei tetare laŋa ne te maa beena. Peero tem maama yɔɔre te ye channa yerane mo. 2Sisein-nɔɔna balo na vaŋe boboa toroko kom to ye nasonno mo. Sisein-nɔɔna balo de na vaŋe torokooro telei tu wom to maa ye nazwona. 3Selo na vaŋe torokooro tetɔ tu wom to ye napwona, ko daare ye selo na vaŋe torokooro tena tu wom to ye pupweeru. Se maama nam yɔɔre se dana mo chekke. 4A ma bwei maleka kam na zege ka ŋɔɔne de amo to a we, “Amo tu, wonnu tento de kuri nam daa mo ye bɛ?”
5Ka de ma leiri-ne ka we, “Tento lage te jage te yi logo baŋa sapɛ sena sem maama. Te nam yɔɔre te nwoŋi Wɛ wom na tei logo baŋa ni maama to yiga ne mo. 6Sisein-zwonnu tem vaŋe se toroko kom se yɔɔre baŋa seeni laŋa kam mo. Kolo sisein-pwonnu tem na vaŋe to ma yɔɔre wɛ-zoore seeni, ye kolo sisein-pupweeru tem na vaŋe to de ma yɔɔre tega-kuri seeni.”
7Sisein-dɛɛro tem konto na yɔɔre se nwoŋi to, se yera nyaare mo se se vo se kare se beeri logo baŋa jei maama. Maleka kam de ma pa-se ni ka we, “Véi-na tega baŋa jei maama se á nii.” Se ma nwoŋi se vo se kaare tega baŋa ni maama se pu. 8O laam ma tɔɔle o ta de amo o we, “Nii mo. Sisei selo na maa vei baŋa seeni laŋa kam ne to mo pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ bane dem zuri jei sem konto ne.”
Paare yipuga wó pu Josua yuu ne
9 Baŋa Wɛ kwora déem tu ka yi amo we:
10“Helidayi, de Tobija, de Jedaya zege Babilon teo ne ba ba ywo-seeni. Nam véi n jeeri-ba n daare n jwoŋi pɛɛra yalo ba na jaane ba ba to ba tei ne. Dento dɛ dem ne nɔɔ se n kwei ba pɛɛra yam konto n ja n vo Zefania bu Josia sɔŋɔ. 11Nmo laam wó kwei ba lu-nyenno, de ba sabu-seŋa pɛɛra yam n ma n ke paare yipuga, se n kwei-ka n pu Jehozadaki bu Josua na ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu to yuu ne. 12Laam ta ded‑o we, ‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Nii wolo ba na bwoi‑o we “Tio-naga” to. O nam wó zege ywo-seeni mo o puli jei maama ne ye o fɔge o lɔ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam. 13Chega to, wonto mo wó lɔ-ka o zege. Wonto wó taa jege paare nenɔŋa mo ye o jei o paare yituŋu kom baŋa ne o tei o nɔɔna bam. Wɛ kaanem tu mo wó taa wo o yituŋu kom saŋa ne. Banto balei wó taa toŋe daane de ni-mɔrɔ.’ 14Paare yipuga kam wó maŋe Wɛ diga kam ne mo se nɔɔna taa guli Helidai, de Tobija, de Jedaya, de Zefania bu Josia gula.
15Nɔɔna balo na wo sa-teo wone to wó ba ba woli se Baŋa Wɛ diga kam fɔge ka lɔ. Abam laam wó lɔre we ko seene ko ye Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo toŋe-ne abam tei ne. Tento nam wó seene ko ke, ne abam ná yɔɔre á sɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ ni dem chekke.”

english_text:
A Question about Going without Eating
1On the fourth day of Chislev, the ninth month of the fourth year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord again spoke to me. 2-3It happened after the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer with Regem-Melech and his men to ask the priests in the Lord's temple and the prophets to pray for them. So they prayed, “Should we mourn and go without eating during the fifth month, as we have done for many years?”
4-5It was then that the Lord All-Powerful told me to say to everyone in the country, including the priests:
For 70 years you have gone without eating during the fifth and seventh months of the year. But did you really do it for me? 6And when you eat and drink, isn't it for your own enjoyment? 7My message today is the same one I commanded the earlier prophets to speak to Jerusalem and its villages when they were prosperous, and when all of Judah, including the Southern Desert and the hill country, was filled with people.
8-9So once again, I, the Lord All-Powerful, tell you, “See that justice is done and be kind and merciful to one another! 10Don't mistreat widows or orphans or foreigners or anyone who is poor, and stop making plans to hurt each other.”
11-12But everyone who heard those prophets, stubbornly refused to obey. Instead, they turned their backs on everything my Spirit had commanded the earlier prophets to preach. So I, the Lord, became angry 13and said, “You people paid no attention when I called out to you, and now I'll pay no attention when you call out to me.”
14That's why I came with a whirlwind and scattered them among foreign nations, leaving their lovely country empty of people and in ruins.
translation_text:
Ni-vɔɔm taane
1Pɛ Darusi paare bena yana bene dem chane nogo chana kam da yana dɛ dem ne mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora déem tu ka yi Zekaria. Kisilev chana kam ne mo konto. 2Ko na ye tei to, Bɛtel teo tiina ya toŋe Sarezera, de Regem-Mɛlɛka de ba kwaga nɔɔna bam mo se ba vo ba lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o swɛ ba swolim. 3Ba ma vo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ba bwei o kaanem tiina bam, de o sampwori sem ba we, “Ko ye ko chwoŋa ne se dé ta taa vɔ ni wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane chane senu chana kam wone, ne dé na maŋe dé ke tetei bena dedɛ wone to na?”
4Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ma pa-ne o kwora o we, 5“Bwei teo kom nɔɔna bam de ba kaanem tiina bam we, ‘Bena fuserepɛ yam maama wone á na yeini á vɔ ni wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane chane senu chane sem wone, de chane serepɛ chane sem wone to, ko seene ko ye amo ŋwaane mo á vɔ na? 6Ko nam ná yi se á di wodiu, se á daare á nyɔ sana, abam ba ke konto á tete ywoni ŋwaane mo na?’ ” 7O kwora kam konto ta ye ne o déem na pɛ o faŋa faŋa sampwori sem tɔɔle kwora kalo Jerusalem teo ne to mo. Maŋa kam konto ne nɔɔna dedɛ zoore Jerusalem teo de ko nawuura yam wone ye ba na nyɔɔre ba totoŋa baŋa ne. Tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam, de wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem de déem su de nɔɔna mo.
8 Baŋa Wɛ daa ma pa o kwora yi Zekaria we, 9“Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Ta‑á bore-na chega bora á pa daane, se á daare á ta‑á jege-na da-swono ye á duri da-ŋwaŋa. 10Yé bɛɛse-na kadeina, de botara, de veira, de yiniga tiina. Yé jeeli-na lwarem á bochara ne se á ke á ma á chɔge á dwonna.”
11Á nabaara bam nam yɔɔre ba ve mo se ba cheigi Wɛ sampwori sem taane. Ba déem kwei ba kwaga ba ya Baŋa Wɛ ye ba daare ba se ba zwa mo se ba yé taa cheigi‑o. 12Ba pɛ ba wo ke dam mo ko dwoni peo na ye tei to, se ba yé wane ba cheigi Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nia yam de bera yalo o na dɛ o Jworo kom ŋwaane o pa faŋa faŋa sampwori sem to. Konto ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ bane déem yɔɔre de zaŋe ba baŋa ne.
13Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Amo ya na ŋɔne de banto to, ba wo sɛ ba cheigi-ne. Konto ŋwaane, ba de na ŋɔne a yiga ne to, amo de wo cheigi. 14A nam kwei vo-kekara a ma a kale-ba a yage dwi-gɛ tiina maama wone se ba taa ye veira sa-teo ne. Ba na viiri ba daare tega kalo to ma ji di-dwonnu yerane, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tere ka wone. Konto baŋa ne mo ba te-ywoŋa kam déem jigi kagoa.”

english_text:
The Lord's Promises to Zion
1The Lord All-Powerful said to me:
2I love Zion so much that her enemies make me angry. 3I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.
4Very old people with walking sticks will once again sit around in Jerusalem, 5while boys and girls play in the streets. 6This may seem impossible for my people who are left, but it isn't impossible for me, the Lord All-Powerful. 7I will save those who were taken to lands in the east and the west, 8and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.
9I am the Lord All-Powerful! So don't give up. Think about the message my prophets spoke when the foundation of my temple was laid. 10Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
11My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before. 12Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky. 13People of Judah and Israel, you have been a curse to the nations, but I will save you and make you a blessing to them. So don't be afraid or lose courage.
14When your ancestors made me angry, I decided to punish you with disasters, and I didn't hold back. 15Now you no longer need to be afraid. I have decided to treat Jerusalem and Judah with kindness. 16 But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace. 17Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things.
A Time of Celebration
18The Lord All-Powerful told me to say:
19People of Judah, I, the Lord, demand that whenever you go without food as a way of worshiping me, it should become a time of celebration. No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
20I tell you that people will come here from cities everywhere. 21Those of one town will go to another and say, “We're going to ask the Lord All-Powerful to treat us with kindness. Come and join us.”
22Many people from strong nations will come to Jerusalem to worship me and to ask me to treat them with kindness. 23When this happens, ten people from nations with different languages will grab a Jew by his clothes and say, “Let us go with you. We've heard that God is on your side.” I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ o nɔɔna bam swolim
1Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ta ma yi amo we, 2Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo yiga tiini ka wo Zion teo kom wone. A yi na page ba baŋa ne to ŋwaane mo pa se a ban-lom zaŋe de ba dona bam.”
3 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo lage a jwoori a ba Zion teo se a taa zoore Jerusalem teo kom wone. Nɔɔna laam maa wó taa jege Jerusalem teo kom ba bwoi we, ‘Chega tɔgem teo,’ ye ba daare ba bwoi Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ peo kom we, ‘Peo kolo na ye wose to’.”
4Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Baara de kaana na tiini ba kwe ye ba zi nachei mo ba vei to daa wó taa tole Jerusalem teo pempala yam yuu ne falalala, ye ba jei ba lara. 5Teo kom ta wó su de bakeiri de busankane mo na kare ko chwei sem yuu ne ba kwɛɛra.”
6Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Amo nɔɔna balo fenfee ta na daare da yam konto wone to ga wó nii keim dem konto we de wó taa chamma mo de gaale keim. Ko nam ná ye amo, de wó taa chamma de pa-ne se a ke na?” Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
7Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Ko ná ye a nɔɔna balo na jage ba vo ba zoore wɛ-puli jei sem ne, de wɛ-zoore jei sem ne to, amo lage a jwoŋi-ba mo a yage. 8A maa wó ja-ba a jwoori se ba taa zoore Jerusalem teo kom wone. Ba maa wó taa ye amo tete nɔɔna, se amo de taa ye ba Wɛ. Dé ta wó taa jege chega dé pa daane.”
9Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Abam laam nigi taana yalo amo sampwori sem déem na jege ba tɛ maŋa kalo nɔɔna na bobo se ba chwi amo diga kam kuri se ba fɔge ba lɔ-ka to. Nam ke-na dam á ke á tete kuri ne. 10Se ko na lwoori maŋa kam konto to, nabiina de vara ya ba nae ba totoŋa yam nyɔɔre. Nɔɔna nam ware se ba nwoŋi ba vo jei jei ba toŋe totoŋa, ba dona bam ŋwaane. Amo ta mo pɛ se nɔɔna vae daane. 11Ko nam na ye tei to, a daa bá ke de a nɔɔna balo na daare to ne a ya na waare a nɔɔna bam tei faŋa to.” Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
12“Amo nɔɔna balo ta na daare to ná dugi wodiiru telo maama, te wó ke se yazura taa wora. Ba Vini teeni dem maa wó ke bia lanyerane. Tega kam wó taa ke wodiiru, ye wɛyuu nyɔnɔ de taa toe ko pa-ba. 13Judah de Isarele dwi tiina bam, ne dwi-gɛ tiina bam déem na mɛ á yera ba sɔɔle lwarem ba pa daane tei to, konto mo a lage jwoŋi abam a yage se á lɛɛre á ja Wɛ swolim á ba á pa-ba. Konto to, yé ta‑á fona. Nam ke-na dam á ke á tete kuri ne.”
14Kokuri to, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Á kwoa bam déem na chuchugi a bane to, a ke a boboŋa ne se a waare abam mo ye a boboŋa wo leiri. 15Konto dwoŋi mo a nam daa ke a boboŋa ne se a fɔge a ke Jerusalem teo kom de Judah dwi tiina bam lanyerane. Konto ŋwaane, yé ta‑á fona-na. 16Nam ta ta‑á ke-na wonnu tento: Ta‑á tɛ-na chega á bere daane, se á daare á ta‑á bore chega bora taane dim baŋa ne, se yazura taa wora. 17Nam yé jeeli-na lwarem á bochara ne se á ke á ma á chɔge á dwonna. Ta yé du-na duuri vwa chwoŋa ne. Amo yɔɔre a chuli kikia yam konto maama mo.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.
18Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ kwora daa ta ma yi amo we, 19Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Abam déem na vɔge á nia amo ŋwaane chane sena chana kam wone, de chane senu chana kam wone, de chane serepɛ chana kam wone, de chane fuga chana kam wone tei to laam wó ji kura yalo Judah dwi tiina bam maama na wó di ywoni ye ba chaka ya baŋa ne to mo. Nam ta‑á swoi-na se chega de bochare-zuru jeini á tetare ne.”
20Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ jwa wó nwoŋi ba teene dem ne ba ba ywo-seeni. 21Balo na zoore teo dedoa wone to wó vo ba ta de teo kodwoŋi nɔɔna we, ‘Nam pa-na dé tɔge daane dé vo Jerusalem se dé fɔɔre dé yi Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom tei se dé daare dé lwoori‑o se o swɛ debam swolim. Amo boboŋa jaane mo se a vo da.’ 22Konto to, dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ na nwoŋi te-fwaaro to laam wó ba Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tei Jerusalem ne se ba lwoori swolim o tei ne.”
23Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Maŋa kam konto ná yia, dwi-gɛ nɔɔna fuga na ŋɔɔne taane dwi dwi to wó vo ba to ba gorege Juu tu dedoa. Ba maa wó ta ded‑o we, ‘Popo pa debam chwoŋa se dé tɔge‑m dé vo, kokuri to dé nigi we Wɛ mo wo abam tei ne.’ ”

english_text:
Israel's Enemies Will Be Punished
1 This is a message
from the Lord:
His eyes are on everyone,
especially the tribes
of Israel.
So he pronounces judgment
against the cities
of Hadrach and Damascus.
2Judgment will also fall
on the nearby city
of Hamath,
as well as on Tyre and Sidon,
whose people are clever.
3Tyre has built a fortress
and piled up silver and gold,
as though they were dust
or mud from the streets.
4Now the Lord will punish Tyre
with poverty;
he will sink its ships
and send it up in flames.
5 Both Ashkelon and Gaza
will tremble with fear;
Ekron will lose all hope.
Gaza's king will be killed,
and Ashkelon emptied
of its people.
6A mob of half-breeds
will settle in Ashdod,
and the Lord himself
will rob Philistia of pride.
7No longer will the Philistines
eat meat with blood in it
or any unclean food.
They will become part
of the people of our God
from the tribe of Judah.
And God will accept
the people of Ekron,
as he did the Jebusites.
8God says, “I will stand guard
to protect my temple from those
who come to attack.
I know what's happening,
and no one will mistreat
my people ever again.”
The Lord Tells about the Coming King
9 Everyone in Jerusalem,
celebrate and shout!
Your king has won a victory,
and he is coming to you.
He is humble
and rides on a donkey;
he comes on the colt
of a donkey.
10 I, the Lord, will take away
war chariots and horses
from Israel and Jerusalem.
Bows that were made for battle
will be broken.
I will bring peace to nations,
and your king will rule
from sea to sea.
His kingdom will reach
from the Euphrates River
across the earth.
The Lord Promises To Rescue Captives
11 When I made a sacred agreement
with you, my people,
we sealed it with blood.
Now some of you are captives
in waterless pits,
but I will come to your rescue
12and offer you hope.
Return to your fortress,
because today I will reward you
with twice what you had.
13I will use Judah as my bow
and Israel as my arrow.
I will take the people of Zion
as my sword
and attack the Greeks.
The Lord Will Protect His People
14Like a cloud, the Lord God
will appear over his people,
and his arrows will flash
like lightning.
God will sound his trumpet
and attack in a whirlwind
from the south.
15The Lord All-Powerful
will protect his people,
and they will trample down
the sharpshooters
and their slingshots.
They will drink and get rowdy;
they will be as full as a bowl
at the time of sacrifice.
16The Lord God will save them
on that day,
because they are his people,
and they will shine on his land
like jewels in a crown.
17How lovely they will be.
Young people will grow there
like grain in a field
or grapes in a vineyard.
translation_text:
Wɛ wó waare Isarele tiina bam dona
Teene delo na bwola de Isarele to taane
1 Baŋa Wɛ kwora mo tento. Ka nam jege se ka vo Haderake laŋa kam seeni, ko fɔge ko dae Damasika teo kom mo. Isarele dwia yam maama, ko woli de nabiina maama yia page Baŋa Wɛ baŋa ne mo.
2Hamafa teo kolo na bwola da to tiina yia de page o baŋa ne, ko woli de Tura teo tiina, de Sidon teo tiina, de ba yiyiu kom na ye tei to de.
3Tura tiina bam lɔge dam jei mo ba pa ba tete. Ba ma kwaleme lu-nyenno wonnu, pa te daga ne tega kasolo tei to. Ba ta ma la sabu-seŋa jejegero dedɛ ba tiŋi ne te ye chwoŋa yuu weeru mo tei. 4Baŋa Wɛ nam wó vere ba jejegero tem, o daare o dole ba dam maama o de naneo kom wone. Mini mo wó zwɛ teo kom maama.
5Asekelon teo tiina wó na konto ye foone yɔɔre de ja-ba.
Gaza teo tiina de yera maa wó chɛ, ne ba ga virigi puga mo to.
Ekoron teo tiina bam de wó na ko na ke tei, pa se ba teena maama ti.
Gaza teo pɛ wom wó jei, ye Asekelon teo de ji di-dwonnu yerane.
6Nɔn-gongwaaga mo wó jwoŋi Asedodi teo ba taa tei.
Amo Baŋa Wɛ lage a pa Filisi tiina bam kamunim dem ti mo.
7Amo nam wó pa se ba daa bá do nɔna de ya yera jana, se wodi-zɔɔna daa yé taa wo ba nia ne.
Ba nɔɔna balo na daare to wó woli amo tete nɔɔna bam wone mo, pa se ba ji nenɛɛne Judah dwi tiina sɔ-yuu kodwoŋi. Konto to, Ekoron teo tiina wó gwaane de a nɔɔna bam, ne Jebusi tiina bam de déem na ke tei to.
8Ko nam ná ye a tete teo kom, a lage a che-ko mo se ko dona bam daa yé tɔge da ba kɛ. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá na chwoŋa se o bɛɛse a nɔɔna bam. Amo tete yi laam mo wó taa page ba baŋa ne.
Wɛ Dam Tu wom tutuuri dem taane
9Zion tiina bam,
ta‑á di-na ywoni lanyerane!
Jerusalem teo tiina bam,
ta‑á chaka de kwor-dɛa!
Nii-na á pɛ wom na vei o beene á tei!
O ye chega tu mo ye o di wɔnɔ.
O nam tu o tete mo
ye o di bonaga o beene.
Chega to, o dɔge bona-pɔla baŋa ne mo o via.
10Amo wó pa se jara-keim torokooro ti
Efrayim laŋa kam ne,
se jara-keim sisein-nɔɔna de ti
Jerusalem teo ne.
Taŋa kalo maama ba na mae
ba ke jara to de wó bwori.
Pɛ wom wó tɔɔle we,
yazura taa wo dwi tiina maama tei ne falalala.
O paare wó di de zege
naneo dedoa ni ne,
se ko yi kadwoŋi ni.
De ta wó zege Yuferata buga kam ne mo,
se de vo de yi tega baŋa ni maama.
11Ko nam ná ye abam Zion tiina bam, amo na tɔge jana baŋa ne a ke ni-gwonim de abam to ŋwaane mo a lage a liiri balo ba na jaane á wone ba peene to a ja a nwoŋi ba vole-kore dem wone.
12Pipiri á jwoori-na á dalem jei sem ne, abam peena balo teena na daga to. Amo tɛ de abam we, a wó pa á jwoori á na kolo á na gɛ to kuni belei. 13A lage a ke de Judah ne a taŋa mo a saŋe to, se a daare a kwei Efrayim a ke da, ne ko ye a chena mo tei to.
Zion tiina bam, a lage a kwei abam mo a pa á zaŋe á kwaare jara de Girisi tiina bam. Á wó ta‑á nye de jara-keim se-zɔɔ mo a jeŋa ne.
14 Baŋa Wɛ wó pi o nwoŋi o nɔɔna bam baŋa ne se o woli-ba. O taŋa chena yam lage ya taa vei mo de fora ne doa na pepele tei to.
Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wó wu o nabɔnɔ. O maa wó tɔge tega-kuri seeni vo-dɛɔ baŋa ne o vo o zo jara yam wone.
15Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tete wó kwoli o nɔɔna bam. Ba dona bam ná dole-ba de kandwa tei maama, ba wó nɔne-ba ba se tega ne.
Ba maa wó nyɔ sana ye ba bage de dam, ne sa-nyɔra na ke tei to.
Ba wó di ywoni ba su, ne zoŋa na su de jana ye ba kwei-ba ba miisi kaanem bimbini dem yera ne tei to.
16Dɛ dem konto ne mo ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó jwoŋi-ba o yage, ne nayero na nii o pei-kɔgɔ baŋa ne tei to, ba na ye o nɔɔna to ŋwaane.
Ba ná zoore wonto tete tega kam wone, ba wó taa nyeene mo ne kandwa-nyenno na nyeene paare yipuga yera ne tei to.
17Nii ba lam na tiini de jege fera tei! Nɔn-donno, de bukwa wó di tega kam wodiiru mo, ye ba nyɔ ka sa-doora se ba ma na dam.

english_text:
A Bright Future for Judah and Israel
1I, the Lord, am the one
who sends storm clouds
and showers of rain
to make fields produce.
So when the crops need rain,
you should pray to me.
2 You can't believe idols
and fortunetellers,
or depend on the hope
you receive from witchcraft
and interpreters of dreams.
But you have tried all of these,
and now you are like sheep
without a shepherd.
3I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am fiercely angry
with you leaders,
and I will punish you.
I care for my people,
the nation of Judah,
and I will change
this flock of sheep
into charging war horses.
4From this flock will come leaders
who will be strong
like cornerstones and tent pegs
and weapons of war.
5They will join in the fighting,
and together they will trample
their enemies like mud.
They will fight,
because I, the Lord,
will be on their side.
And they will crush
the enemy cavalry.
6I will strengthen
the kingdoms of Judah
and Israel.
And I will show mercy
because I am the Lord,
their God.
I will answer their prayers
and bring them home.
Then it will seem as though
I had never rejected them.
7Israel will be like
a tribe of warriors
celebrating with wine.
When their children see this,
they will also be happy
because of me, the Lord.
8I will give a signal
for them to come together
because I have rescued them.
And there will be as many
as ever before.
9 Although I scattered my people
in distant countries,
they won't forget me.
Once their children are raised,
they will return—
10I will bring them home
from Egypt and Assyria,
then let them settle
as far as Gilead and Lebanon,
until the land overflows
with them.
11My people will go through
an ocean of troubles,
but I will overcome the waves
and dry up the deepest part
of the Nile.
Assyria's great pride
will be put down,
and the power of Egypt
will disappear.
12I'll strengthen my people
because of who I am,
and they will follow me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Baŋa Wɛ na wó fɔge o kwɛ o nɔɔna tei to
1Lwoori-na Baŋa Wɛ se o pa doa ne duum maŋa ne. Wonto mo pae do-vio kale kunkwonnu, ye o ta pae do-na tui se tega kam ke wodiiru lanyerane.
2Jwona yam jege nɔɔna mo ya gana. Vora bam de maa tɔge yi-nɛɛre ŋwaane ba fɔe vwa. Ba yeini ba maŋe dendwa kuri ba bere nɔɔna ye ko dae chega. Ba ta na pa wolim delo to maa ye kafɛ. Konto ŋwaane, nɔɔna bam maa beeri yɔɔ yerane ye ba nae yaara dedɛ, ne pei selo na ba jege nayero se o taa nii-se to.
Baŋa Wɛ maa we:
3“A bane mo yɔɔre de wiira de nayera bam. A maa wó waare dedɛɛra bam. Kokuri to, amo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó taa nii a nɔn-kɔgɔ kom na ye Judah dwi tiina to baŋa ne mo. A laam maa wó pa ba leiri ba taa jege dam nenɛɛne sisein-nɔɔna balo na wurigi ba vei jara wone tei to.
4Judah dwi dem wone mo dedɛɛro wó pi o nwoŋi.
Diga kuri kandwɛ-zane mo wó nwoŋi ba wone.
Paare delo na jaane vwei to de wó nwoŋi ba wone.
Jara-keim taŋa maa wó nwoŋi ba wone.
Chega to, dedɛɛra dwi maama wó nwoŋi ba wone mo.
5Ba maama ná ke daane, ba wó ji babɛ mo ye ba nɔne ba dona bam ba se chwoŋa ni bworu wone. Ba ta wó kwaare jara ba wane ba dona sisein-dira bam ba de tega ne, Baŋa Wɛ na wo ba tei ne to ŋwaane.
6Amo nam wó pa Judah dwi dem taa jege baare, ye a daare a jwoŋi Josɛf dwi tiina bam a yage. A wó pa ba jwoori ba zege ba faŋa zega jei sem ne, a na jege ba ŋwaŋa to ŋwaane. Ko wó taa nye de a ya maŋe a wo ve-ba mo to, kolo ŋwaane amo mo ye ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, ye a nam wó sɛ ba wɛ-lworo kom.
7Efrayim dwi tiina bam wó ji jara-keim bembɛ mo. Ba maa wó taa jege wopwolo lanyerane, ne nɔɔna na nyɔge sana ye ba wo pwoli tei to. Ba bia bam de wó na konto maama pa se ba de taa jege wopwolo. Ba maa wó di ywoni Baŋa Wɛ zeinim ŋwaane.
8Amo wó bwoŋi a nɔɔna bam se ba ba ba jeeri ba ke daane mo. Kokuri, amo lage a vere-ba mo a yage. Ba maa wó puli de kɔgɔ ne ba déem na daga tei to. 9Amo ya seene a jage-ba a yage dwi-gɛ tiina teene ne yiga yiga. De ko de, ba na wo jei selo maama ne to ba bá swei amo swia. Ba de ba bia bam wó wori ye ba laam jwoori ba tete teo kom. 10Amo wó pa ba badwonna zege Ejipti teo ne ba jwoori, ye a daare a la ba badwonna a ke daane se ba zege Asiria ne ba ba. A wó pa ba zege jei sem konto ne ba ba ba jeini Gilead laŋa kam ne, de Lebanon ne. Ba maa wó taa daga ba su ba gaale tega kam. 11A nɔɔna bam wó bɛ naneo kom de ko chanɛɛre dem ba kɛ. Ba wó pa se buga kam na-ŋone sem peini tega ne. Naili buga kam maama de wó we ba ŋwaane. Asiria tiina kamunim dem wó tu tega. Ejipti teo paare dam dem de maa wó ti.
12Amo Baŋa Wɛ wó pa ba fɔge ba zege amo dam dem ŋwaane. Ba maa wó taa kɔre-ne ba kikia maama wone.”
Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_text:
Trouble for Israel's Enemies
1Lebanon, open your gates!
Let the fire come in
to destroy your cedar trees.
2Cry, you cypress trees!
The glorious cedars have fallen
and are rotting.
Cry, you oak trees of Bashan!
The dense forest
has been chopped down.
3Listen! Shepherds are crying.
Their glorious pastures
have been ruined.
Listen! Lions are roaring.
The forests of the Jordan Valley
are no more to be found.
Worthless Shepherds
4The Lord my God said to me:
Tend those sheep doomed for slaughter! 5The people who buy and butcher them go unpunished, while everyone who sells them says, “Praise the Lord! I'm rich.” Not even their shepherds have pity on them.
6Tend those sheep because I, the Lord, will no longer have pity on the people of this earth. I'll turn neighbor against neighbor and make them slaves of a king. They will bring disaster on the earth, and I'll do nothing to rescue any of them.
7So I became a shepherd of those sheep doomed to be slaughtered by the sheep dealers. And I gave names to the two sticks I used for tending the sheep: One of them was named “Mercy” and the other “Unity.” 8In less than a month, I became impatient with three shepherds who didn't like me, and I got rid of them. 9Then I said, “I refuse to be your shepherd. Let the sheep that are going to die, go on and die, and those that are going to be destroyed, go on and be destroyed. Then let the others eat one another alive.”
10On that same day, I broke the stick named “Mercy” to show that the Lord had canceled his agreement with all people. 11The sheep dealers who saw me knew at once that this was a message from the Lord. 12-13 I told them, “Pay me my wages, if you think you should; otherwise, forget it.” So they handed me my wages, a measly 30 pieces of silver.
Then the Lord said, “Throw the money into the treasury.” So I threw the money into the treasury at the Lord's temple. 14Then I broke the stick named “Unity” and canceled the ties between Judah and Israel.
15Next, the Lord said to me, “Act like a shepherd again—this time a worthless shepherd. 16Once more I am going to let a worthless nobody rule the land—one who won't care for the strays or search for the young or heal the sick or feed the healthy. He will just dine on the fattest sheep, leaving nothing but a few bones.”
17You worthless shepherd,
deserting the sheep!
I hope a sword
will cripple your arm
and blind your right eye.
translation_text:
Lɛɛro wó yi Wɛ nɔɔna bam dona
1Lebanon, pore n teo kom ni,
se mini na chwoŋa de zo
de di n Sedare teeni dem.
2Tei-ŋonno de, ta‑á chwoosi-na,
Sedare teeni dem na toa to ŋwaane.
Tei-kamunnu tem maama to te pɔ mo!
Basan tei-lilirru tem,
keeri-na bugi-bugi!
Ko ná ye goa kalo ya na lini
de teeni to,
ba laam gwoni ka teeni dem maama mo ba de tega ne!
3Cheigi-na se á wó ni nayera bam na laare tei to,
ba vara pwoli sem maama laam na chɔge to ŋwaane.
Cheigi-na se á wó ni
nywonnu tem na suura,
Jɔdan buga ni goa kam tete
de na chɔge to ŋwaane.
Nayera balei taane
4Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Fɔge n kɔne pei selo ba na lage ba go to. 5Balo na yeigi pei sem to mo kwei-se ba go, ye ba ba boŋe we ba tusi. Balo na jege pei sem ba yeigi to de maa tɛ ba we, ‘Dé ke-na Baŋa Wɛ lei, se dé nɛ nyɔɔre dedɛ.’ Pei sem nayera tete de yiga tere se wone. 6A nam daa bá duri teo kom konto nɔɔna bam ŋwaŋa.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. “Nii-na. Amo wó kwei nɔɔno maama a ke o dwoŋi jeŋa ne, de o pɛ wom jeŋa ne. Banto laam maa wó chɔge tega kam maama zɔŋ-zɔŋ. A nam bá jwoŋi nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jeŋa ne a yage.”
7Mo kokuri a jege pei selo ba na lage ba go to a kɔna a pa balo na jege-se ba yeigi to. A nam jege gwola yalei mo. A ma pa dedoa yere ye ‘Zaane’. Dedwoŋi dem yere ye ‘Ni-mɔrɔ’. A maa jege-ya a mae a nii a pei sem baŋa ne. 8Chana dedoa wone, a ma zeili nayera batɔ bam, a na wo wane a ja a tete de-ba to ŋwaane. Pipim-piina bam tete de maa vae a ni taane. 9A ma ta a we, “Amo daa bá taa kɔne pei sem a pa abam. Selo na maŋe se se te to wó te, se selo na ye se se jei to de jei. Selo maa na daare to de wó taa di da ya-nɔna.”
10Amo ma ja a gwoli delo yere na ye Zaane to a bwori, se ko bere we a yiri ni delo a ya na gwoni de nɔɔna bam maama to. 11Dɛ dem konto ne nɔɔ mo ni-gwonim dem seene de chɔge. Pipim-piina bam nɛ-ne, ye ba lɔre we kwora kam konto yɔɔre ka nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ tei ne mo.
12A ma ta de-ba a we, “Abam ná nii we ko maŋe, se á pa-ne a ŋweero. Ko nam daa ná dae konto, se á ta‑á jege-te.” Ba ma jeeli a ŋweero, ye ba kwei lu-nyenno sabu-dala fintɔ ba pa-ne.
13 Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we, “Kwei sabia bam n ke sabu tiŋim dakaa kam wone.” Mo banto sabu-yere delo ba na jeeli se ko taa ye amo ŋweero to mo konto. A ma seene a kwei sabia bam konto a ja a vo Wɛ diga kam a dole a de sabu tiŋim dakaa kam wone.
14A laam ma bwori a gwoli dedwoŋi dem, de yere na ye Ni-mɔrɔ to, se ko bere we Judah tiina bam de Isarele tiina bam choro kom chɔge.
15 Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta de amo o we, “Daa ta kwei nayero zela se n ke ne n ye nayere-jworo mo to. 16Nii-na, a lage a pa nayero wodwoŋi mo ba o taa nii tega kam nɔɔna baŋa ne. Wonto yiga bá taa wo pei selo na lage se jei to wone, de pei selo na beeri yɔɔ to wone. O nam bá taa nii selo na nɛ zonne to se o yɔɔre-se, naa se o kɔne pei selo na dana to. O nam wó di pi-bigila yam mo, ye o tore se napɔɔna yam nywa.
17Lɛɛro nam lage te yi
nayere-jworo kom mo,
o na tage pei sem o yage to ŋwaane!
Se-zɔɔ mo lage ko zɔ o vɔŋɔ
de o jazem yi dem!
O vɔŋɔ kom maama jege
se ko kwaare mo,
ye o jazem yi dem de dwei
de daa ta ba nae!”

english_text:
Victory for Jerusalem
1This is a message from the Lord about Israel:
I am the Lord! I stretched out the heavens; I put the earth on its foundations and gave breath to humans. 2I have decided that Jerusalem will become a bowl of wine that makes the neighboring nations drunk. And when Jerusalem is attacked, Judah will also be attacked. 3But I will turn Jerusalem into a heavy stone that crushes anyone who tries to lift it.
When all nations on earth surround Jerusalem, 4I will blind every horse and make them panic, and every rider will be confused. But at the same time, I will watch over Judah. 5Then every clan in Judah will realize that I, the Lord All-Powerful, am their God, and that I am the source of their strength.
6At that time I will let the clans of Judah be like a ball of fire in a wood pile or a fiery torch in a hay stack. Then Judah will send the surrounding nations up in smoke. And once again the city of Jerusalem will be filled with people.
7But I will first give victory to Judah, so the kingdom of David and the city of Jerusalem in all of their glory won't be thought of more highly than Judah itself. 8I, the Lord God, will protect Jerusalem. Even the weakest person there will be as strong as David, and David's kingdom will rule as though my very own angel were its leader. 9I am determined to wipe out every nation that attacks Jerusalem.
Mourning for the One Pierced with a Spear
10 I, the Lord, will make the descendants of David and the people of Jerusalem feel deep sorrow and pray when they see the one they pierced with a spear. They will mourn and weep for him, as parents weep over the death of their only child or their first-born. 11On that day the people of Jerusalem will mourn as much as everyone did for Hadad Rimmon on the flatlands near Megiddo. 12Everyone of each family in the land will mourn, and the men will mourn separately from the women. This includes those from the family of David, and the families of Nathan, 13Levi, Shimei, 14and all other families as well.
translation_text:
Wɛ wó vere Jerusalem tiina bam o yage
1Kwora kalo Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe se ka vo Isarele tiina bam seeni to mo tento: Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na lware wɛyuu kom pa se ko tigi palalala, ye o daare o chwi tega kam kuri to. O ta daare ke jworo o yage nabiina wone. Wonto tage o we:
2“Nii-na! Amo wó pa Jerusalem teo ji nenɛɛne zoŋa de ka wo sana. Dwi-gɛ tiina balo na bwola da to wó nyɔ ka wone ye ba beiri. Ko ta wó ke konto dwoŋi ko pa Judah tiina bam mo de ba na tɔge ba kwaare jara de Jerusalem tei to. 3Maŋa kam konto ne, dwi tiina bam maama ná jeeri se ba ke jara de Jerusalem teo kom, amo wó pa ko ji nenɛɛne kandwɛ-polɔgɔ mo ko pa-ba. Wolo maama ná kwaane se o guri-ko, ko wó tiini ko ke kotu zonne.”
4 Baŋa Wɛ ta na tage kolo to mo tento: “Ka maŋa ne, a lage a pa sisein-nɔɔna bam maama fom mo, se se dira bam maama de yirisi. A laam maa wó taa fɔge a nii Judah tiina bam baŋa ne. Ko nam ná ye dwi-gɛ tiina sisei sem de, a wó pa se yia dwei. 5Judah yiga tiina bam laam wó ta ba tete ne we, ‘Jerusalem teo nɔn-bia bam nɛ dam, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na ye ba Wɛ to ŋwaane.’
6Maŋa kam konto ne, amo wó pa se Judah yiga tiina bam taa nye de min-zoŋa na to dɛ wone tei to mo. Ba ta wó taa ye ne min-vogo na to men-zwaro wone. Konto to, ba wó pa teene delo maama na bwola da to chɔge kula. Ko daare ye Jerusalem teo kom tete taa zege cheppe de ko nɔn-bia bam maama. 7Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam lage a pa Judah jar-keira bam mo da yiga ba na wɔnɔ, se Pɛ David dwi tiina bam de Jerusalem nɔn-bia bam maama yé na zula ba dwoni Judah tiina bam.
8Maŋa kam konto ne, amo Baŋa Wɛ tete mo lage a taa kwoli balo na zoore Jerusalem teo kom wone to. Wolo na ye nabwom ba maama wone to wó jwoŋi dam ne David na dana tei to mo. David dwi tiina bam wó taa nii ba baŋa ne, ne ko ye Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam tete mo wo ba yiga ne. 9Maŋa kam konto ne, amo yia wó seene dwi tiina balo maama na kwaare jara de Jerusalem to baŋa ne, se a yɔɔre a chɔge-ba.”
Ba keeri ba pa wolo nɔɔna na zɔge to
10“Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam lage a kwei teiŋ-jara jworo de ka-duri-nɔɔna-ŋwaŋa mo a ke David dwi dem, de Jerusalem nɔn-bia bam maama wone. Ko maa wó pa se ba kwoni ba nii amo ye ba keeri ba pa wolo wom ba na zɔge to. Ba wó taa tiini ba keeri wonto lua ye ba chwoosa, ne nɔɔna na gɛ ba bu-doa, naa ba bu-kwea tei to mo. 11Maŋa kam konto ne, Jerusalem tiina wó keeri bugi-bugi, ne nɔɔna déem na keeri tei Hadad-Rimon ne, teo kolo na wo Megido te-kampare sem ne to mo. 12Balo na zoore tega kam jei maama ne to wó taa keeri mo bugi-bugi, sɔ-yuu de sɔ-yuu maama, se kaana bam keira taa ye ka yera de baara bam keira. David diga kam wó keeri lua kam ba yerane, ye ba kaana bam de keeri ba yerane. Natan diga kam de wó keeri ba yerane, ye ba kaana bam de keeri ba yerane. 13Levi diga tiina bam, de ba kaana de wó keeri ba yerane. Simeyi diga kam de ba kaana wó da ba keeri ba yerane, 14ko woli de sɔ-yuni telo maama ta na daare to, de ba kaana.

english_text:
Getting Rid of Idols and False Prophets
1In the future there will be a fountain, where David's descendants and the people of Jerusalem can wash away their sin and guilt.
2The Lord All-Powerful says:
When that time comes, I will get rid of every idol in the country, and they will be forgotten forever. I will also do away with their prophets and those evil spirits that control them. 3If any such prophets ever appear again, their own parents must warn them that they will die for telling lies in my name—the name of the Lord. If those prophets don't stop speaking, their parents must then kill them with a sword.
4Those prophets will be ashamed of their so-called visions, and they won't deceive anyone by dressing like a true prophet. 5Instead, they will say, “I'm no prophet. I've been a farmer all my life.”
6And if any of them are asked why they are wounded, they will answer, “It happened at the house of some friends.”
A Wounded Shepherd and Scattered Sheep
7 The Lord All-Powerful said:
My sword, wake up! Attack
my shepherd and friend.
Strike down the shepherd!
Scatter the little sheep,
and I will destroy them.
8Nowhere in the land
will more than a third of them
be left alive.
9Then I will purify them
and put them to the test,
just as gold and silver
are purified and tested.
They will pray in my name,
and I will answer them.
I will say, “You are my people,”
and they will reply,
“You, Lord, are our God!”
translation_text:
1Maŋa kam konto ne amo wó pa se buli-yi puri de taa bura de pa David dwi tiina bam, de Jerusalem nɔn-bia bam, pa se ba wɛleera de ba digiru tem saare te yage.”
Jwona de sampwori taane
2Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Dɛ dem konto ná yia, amo wó pa se jwona yera yam saare tega kam maama ne, se nɔɔna daa yé taa guli ya gula kɔtaa! A nam ta wó zeili sampwori sem de ba chichiri-lwanno tega kam ne. 3Ba wolo ta ná zaŋe o pworisi o bere nɔɔna, o tete tiina balo na loge‑o to mo wó ta ded‑o we, ‘Nmo maŋe se n te mo, de n na mɛ Baŋa Wɛ yere n pworisi vwa to.’ Ba laam wó zɔ‑o ba go, o na pworisi to ŋwaane.
4Dɛ dem konto ná yia, sampwora kalo maama ná lage o pworisi, chaveera wó ja kotu de veera yalo o na nɛ to. O daa bá kwei gare-nyenyaaro telo dwi Wɛ sampwori sem na zoore to o zo, o na lage se o gane nɔɔna to ŋwaane. 5Kotu maa wó ta we, ‘Ko zege a nɔn-donne maŋa ne varem yerane mo ye a totoŋe. Amo dae Wɛ sampwora.’ 6Nɔɔna maa ná bwei‑o we, ‘Bɛ mo ke ye n na fufwollu tento dwoŋi n nyɔɔne ne?’, o ta wó leiri-ba we, ‘A nɛ fufwollu tem a badwoŋi sɔŋɔ ne mo.’ ”
Nayero de pei taane
7Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Se-zɔɔ, zaŋe dɔɔm wone
se n jeeri a nayero wom
na bwola de amo to.
Yɔɔre n mage nayero wom,
se pei sem maama jage se jei.
Amo tete jeŋa nam mo wó zo se bia bam.”
8 Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento:
“Tega kam ni jei maama ne,
nɔɔna bam popɔra betɔ wone,
kuni belei mo lage ba te,
se popɔra dedoa daare ba taa ŋwe.
9Popɔra dedoa kalo na daare to,
a lage a faŋe-ba a nii mo,
se a daare a fɔge a kwɛ-ba.
Ko wó taa nye de nɔɔno na kwei
lu-nyenno naa sabu-seŋa
o de mini wone
se o pa te taa lana fase tei to mo.
Nɔɔna bam konto laam maa wó ma
amo yere dem ba lwoori-ne,
ye amo de leiri-ba.
Amo wó ta ba taane we,
‘Ba ye a nɔɔna mo,’
ye ba de ta we,
‘Baŋa Wɛ mo ye debam Wɛ.’ ”

english_text:
War and Victory
1The Lord will have his day. And when it comes, everything that was ever taken from Jerusalem will be returned and divided among its people. 2But first, he will bring many nations to attack Jerusalem—homes will be robbed, women raped, and half of the population dragged off, though the others will be allowed to remain.
