6Ko nam ná ye nɔn-wo-korro, se á yé gare á bere-ba Wɛ chega kam. Konto nye de nɔɔno ná kwei woŋo kolo na tiini ko jege fera to o de teira yiga ne. Ya ma nɔ-ko de ya nɛ, ye ya daare ya chiŋi kotu.
Wɛ-lworo taane
Luka 11:9-13
7Ta‑á lwoori-na Wɛ, se á wó na kolo á na gɛ to. Beeri-na kolo á na lage to, se á wó na. Ta ta‑á dɔne-na manchwo-peena yam, se ba wó pore ba pa abam. 8Kolo ŋwaane, wolo maama na lwoori Wɛ se o pa‑o woŋo to wó jwoŋi. Wolo maama na beeri woŋo to wó na-ko. Ba wó pore ba pa wolo maama na dɔne manchwo-peena yam to.
9Abam wolo ná jege bu, ye o ná lwoori bworobworo n tei ne, nmo wó sɛ n kwei kandwɛ n pa‑o na? 10O nam ná lwoori‑m se n pa‑o ywoni, n wó sɛ n pa‑o basankwea na? 11Aawo. Abam wo ba lana ye á ta yei se á pae á bia wo-laaro telo ba na lage to. Ko daare á Kwo Wɛ na gare abam to, wonto nam bá kwei wo-laaro dedɛ o pa balo na lwoori‑o to mo na?
12Ta‑á ke-na á dwonna lanyerane, se ko maŋe de á na lage se banto taa ke abam tei to. Konto mo ye chega kalo Moses de faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem twanno tem na maŋe te bere to.
Yezu tɔgena na wó tɔge chwoŋa kalo to
Luka 13:24; 6:43-44; 13:25-27; 6:47-49
13-14Ta‑á cho-na á tete se á wane á tɔge chwo-memena kam á vo á na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne. Nmo nam ná lage n tɔge chwoŋa kalo kweelim jeiga na ye chɔgem to, ka ni yala dedɛ ye ka tɔgem de ye mɔle. Nɔɔna dedɛ mo yeini ba tɔge-ka. Ko daare, ko ná ye chwoŋa kalo nmo na wó tɔge da se n vo n jwoŋi ŋwea Wɛ tei ne to, ka ni ye memena mo ye ka ta peena. Nɔɔna fenfee yerane mo lɔre chwoŋa kam konto ni ne.
15Ta‑á cho-na á tete de balo na bere we ba ye Wɛ sampwori ye ba dae to. Banto nye de wiira mo de ba na lage ba chɔge abam tei to, ye ba laam pa se ba nye de pei abam yiga ne. 16Ba kikia nam mo wó pa se á lɔre ba na seene ba ye tei to. Kokuri, tio tera ko na wó wane ko lei ko dwoŋi bia. N bá‑n na mɔɔro sabara yuu ne. 17Tei-ŋonno mo yeini te leiri bu-ŋona. Tei-jawone mo yeini te leiri bu-kokwaaro. 18Tei-ŋoŋo tera ko na wó lei bu-kokwaaro. Tei-jawona nam tera ko na wó lei bu-ŋona. 19Tio kolo maama na ba leiri bu-ŋona to, nɔɔna wó gwoni-ko mo ba de tega ne ba zwɛ de mini. 20Ko nam wó tɔge konto mo se á seene á lɔre banto na ye balo to de ba na ke kolo to.
21Ko dae we nɔɔno wolo maama na bwoŋi-ne o we, ‘Amo Teiru, amo Teiru’ to mo wó tɔge o woli amo Kwo Wɛ paare dem wone. Ko nam wó taa ye balo na seene ba tɔge amo Kwo Wɛ boboŋa to mo. 22Bora borem dɛ dem ná yia, nɔɔna dedɛ wó ta de amo we, ‘Dé Teiru, dé tɔge nmo yere dem ŋwaane mo dé tɔɔle Wɛ kwora kam. Dé ta mɛ nmo yere dem dé zeili setaana nɔɔna tei ne, ye dé daare dé ma dé ke wo-kenkagela dedɛ.’ 23Amo nam wó ta-ba we, ‘A nam maŋe a wo fɔge a lɔre abam mo de. Á ye wo-lwan-keira mo. Konto to, véi-na dáa a tei ne.’
24Ko na ye konto to, wolo maama ná jwoŋi a taane dem ye o daare o tɔge-de, konto tu nye de boboŋa tu wolo na chwi o sɔŋɔ kuri pelɔrɔ baŋa ne ye o laam lɔ to mo. 25Doa ma ba ka ne pa se bwi su se pɛɛle. Vo-dɛɔ de ma ba ko mage sɔŋɔ kom. Ko maa wo to, ko kuri na chwi pelɔrɔ kom baŋa ne to ŋwaane. 26Ko daare wolo maama nam na jwoŋi amo taane dem ye o ba tɔge-de to nye de nɔn-jworo kolo na pɔpɔ ko lɔ ko sɔŋɔ kasolo baŋa ne to mo. 27Doa ma ba ka ne pa se bwi su se pɛɛle, ye vo-dɛɔ de mage sɔŋɔ kom pa se ko tiini ko to tega ne buri-buri.”
28Yezu déem na tage wonnu tento maama o ti to, nɔn-kɔgɔ kolo na wora to ma tiini ba ye yaau de o berem dem. 29O na bere-ba tei to mo pɛ se ba lɔre we o jege dam ko dwoi ba tete zamesem tiina bam.

english_text:
Jesus Heals a Man
(Mark 1.40-45; Luke 5.12-16)
1As Jesus came down the mountain, he was followed by large crowds. 2Suddenly a man with leprosy came and knelt in front of Jesus. He said, “Lord, you have the power to make me well, if only you wanted to.”
3Jesus put his hand on the man and said, “I want to! Now you are well.” At once the man's leprosy disappeared. 4 Jesus told him, “Don't tell anyone about this, but go and show the priest that you are well. Then take a gift to the temple just as Moses commanded, and everyone will know that you have been healed.”
Jesus Heals an Army Officer's Servant
(Luke 7.1-10; John 4.43-54)
5When Jesus was going into the town of Capernaum, an army officer came up to him and said, 6“Lord, my servant is at home in such terrible pain that he can't even move.”
7“I will go and heal him,” Jesus replied.
8But the officer said, “Lord, I'm not good enough for you to come into my house. Just give the order, and my servant will get well. 9 I have officers who give orders to me, and I have soldiers who take orders from me. I can say to one of them, ‘Go!’ and he goes. I can say to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes. I can say to my servant, ‘Do this!’ and he will do it.”
10When Jesus heard this, he was so surprised that he turned and said to the crowd following him, “I tell you in all of Israel I've never found anyone with this much faith! 11 Many people will come from everywhere to enjoy the feast in the kingdom of heaven with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. 12 But the ones who should have been in the kingdom will be thrown out into the dark. They will cry and grit their teeth in pain.”
13Then Jesus said to the officer, “You may go home now. Your faith has made it happen.”
Right then his servant was healed.
Jesus Heals Many People
(Mark 1.29-34; Luke 4.38-41)
14Jesus went to the home of Peter, where he found that Peter's mother-in-law was sick in bed with fever. 15He took her by the hand, and the fever left her. Then she got up and served Jesus a meal.
16That evening many people with demons in them were brought to Jesus. And with only a word he forced out the evil spirits and healed everyone who was sick. 17 So God's promise came true, just as the prophet Isaiah had said,
“He healed our diseases
and made us well.”
Some Who Wanted To Go with Jesus
(Luke 9.57-62)
18When Jesus saw the crowd, he went across Lake Galilee. 19A teacher of the Law of Moses came up to him and said, “Teacher, I'll go anywhere with you!”
20Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens, and birds have nests. But the Son of Man doesn't have a place to call his own.”
21 Another disciple said to Jesus, “Lord, let me wait till I bury my father.”
22Jesus answered, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their dead.”
A Storm
(Mark 4.35-41; Luke 8.22-25)
23After Jesus left in a boat with his disciples, 24a terrible storm suddenly struck the lake, and waves started splashing into their boat.
Jesus was sound asleep, 25so the disciples went over to him and woke him up. They said, “Lord, wake up! Save us before we drown!”
26But Jesus replied, “Why are you so afraid? You surely don't have much faith.” Then he got up and ordered the wind and the waves to calm down. And everything was calm.
27The men in the boat were amazed and said, “Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him.”
Two Men with Demons in Them
(Mark 5.1-20; Luke 8.26-39)
28After Jesus had crossed the lake, he came to shore near the town of Gadara and started down the road. Two men with demons in them came to him from the tombs. They were so fierce that no one could travel that way. 29Suddenly they shouted, “Jesus, Son of God, what do you want with us? Have you come to punish us before our time?”
30Not far from there a large herd of pigs was feeding. 31So the demons begged Jesus, “If you force us out, please send us into those pigs!” 32Jesus told them to go, and they went out of the men and into the pigs. All at once the pigs rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
33The people taking care of the pigs ran to the town and told everything, especially what had happened to the two men. 34Everyone in town came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged him to leave their part of the country.
translation_text:
Yezu yɔɔre nɔɔna badwonna
Maake 1:40-45; 1:29-34; Luka 5:12-16; 7:1-10; 4:38-41
1Yezu laam ma zaŋe o tu peo kom yuu ne se o kɛ, ye nɔn-fɔrɔ tɔge o kwaga. 2O na maa kɛ to, nayɔŋɔ kodwoŋi ma vo o tei. O ma kuni dwoona o yiga ne ye o lwoori‑o we, “Amo tu, nmo ná laga, n wó wane n pa se a na yazura.” 3Yezu ma seene o sɛ. O ma twe o jeŋa o dwei‑o, ye o we, “A lage konto. Zaŋe de yazura.” O na tage konto bedwe baŋa ne to mo nɔɔno wom yera yam fɔge ya kwɛ fase.
4Yezu laam ma ta ded‑o o we, “Yé zaŋe n ta kolo na ke to n bere nɔɔn-nɔɔno. Nam yɔɔre n vo Wɛ kaanem tu wom tei se n pa o nii n yera yam, se n daare n ja pɛɛra n vo n ke Wɛ jeŋa ne se ko maŋe de Moses nia yam na bere tei to. Konto wó bere nɔɔna we n jaweo kom seene ko jei.”
5Yezu laam ma vo o yi teo kodwoŋi, ko yere mo Kaparenia. Soja yiga tu wodwoŋi déem maa wora. 6O ma vo Yezu tei o lwoori‑o we, “Amo tu, a jege tontoŋeno sɔŋɔ ne ye jaweo tiini ko chana o yera ne. O maa tigi tega ne ye o ware o zaŋe.” 7Yezu ma leiri‑o we, “Amo wó tɔge a vo se a pa o na yazura.” 8Soja yiga tu wom ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, a muri se n ba n zo amo sɔŋɔ. Konto ŋwaane, nam ta‑n ni we a tontoŋeno wom zaŋe, se o laam wó na yazura. 9Amo yei we n jwoŋi dam Wɛ tei ne. Amo de ye nɔɔno wolo nɔɔna badwonna na jege dam amo baŋa ne to, ye amo de daa ta jege dam badaara baŋa ne. Amo ná tage we nɔɔno wolo véi, o jege se o vo mo. A nam daa ná we nɔɔno wolo ba, o de wó ba mo. Ko ta ná ye a tontoŋeno, amo ná we, o ke woŋo kolo, o jege se o ke mo.”
10Yezu na nigi konto to, ko ma tiini ko so‑o. O ma ta de balo na tɔge ba wora to o we, “A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, amo wo nɛ nɔɔn-nɔɔno o na jege wo-dedoa de amo se ko yi nɔɔno wonto na jege tei to, ne ko ná maŋe ko ye Isarele dwi tiina bam wone de. 11Á ta‑á yei we nɔɔna dedɛ wó nwoŋi logo baŋa jei maama ne ba ba ba zo Wɛ woro kom wo. Dáane mo ba laam wó jeini de debam nabaara Abaraham de Izaak de Jakob, ye ba di ywoni daane. 12Ko daare nɔɔna balo Wɛ na tiŋi o paare dem se ba zo to, banto daa bá na chwoŋa se ba zo. Wɛ wó zeili-ba o yage lim jei ne, yaara na wora mɛ to, ye ba wó taa keera ye ba done ba nwa.”
13Yezu laam ma ta de soja yiga tu wom o we, “Nam véi. Nmo na ke n wo-dedoa de amo se a ke kolo to, Wɛ wó pa ko ke.” Ko ma seene ko ke. Maŋa kam konto ne nɔɔ mo tontoŋeno wom nɛ yazura.
14Yezu laam ma vo Piita ba sɔŋɔ. O ma na Piita tenkaane na tiga o weela. Ko ye paa mo jege‑o. 15Yezu ma vo o tei o ja o jeŋa, ye paa kam nwoŋi o yera ne. Kaane wom laam ma zaŋe wɛɛne o ke wodiu o pa‑o.
16Tega na tu ka wora ka yi to, nɔɔna maa jaane setaana na daane balo to dedɛ ba tui Yezu tei. O maa yeini o mae o ni taane o zeili setaana yam, ye o daare o pa jaweena maama na yazura. 17O na ke tei konto to, ko ye se ko pa Wɛ sampwora Izaya na maŋe o ta kolo faŋa faŋa to mo ba ko ji chega, de o na we,
“Wonto mo le jaweero de lwia yalo na jege debam to o yage.”
Balo na lage se ba tɔge Yezu na ke tei to
Luka 9:57-62
18Yezu déem ma lɔre we nɔn-fɔrɔ tiini ko wora o tei ne. O ma pa o kwaga tɔgena bam ni se ba bɛ buga kam bubɛ dedwoŋi dem. 19Ba daa ta na wo kɛ to, Wɛ nia yam zamesem tu wodwoŋi ma vo o tei, ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Berem tu, nmo na lage n vo jei selo maama to, amo wó tɔge a vo.” 20Yezu ma leiri‑o we, “Ko ná ye yira, banto jege bɔɔna ba tigi da. Zuna de jege pworu ba tigi da. Ko daare amo Nabiin-bu wom ba jege jeiga se a peini da a sii.”
21Nɔɔno wodwoŋi de na ye o kwaga tɔgeno to ma ta ded‑o o we, “Amo tu, yage se a ná ke a kwo lua, se a laam ba a tɔge nmo.” 22Yezu ma leiri‑o we, “Ta‑n tɔge-ne, se n yage se balo na ba jege ŋwea Wɛ tei ne to taa ke ba tete lui.”
Yezu jege dam vo-dɛɔ baŋa ne
Maake 4:35-41; Luka 8:22-25
23Yezu laam ma vo o zo nabworo wo, ye o kwaga tɔgena bam tɔge ded‑o ba kɛ. 24Vo-dɛɔ ma pɔpɔ ko zaŋe ko mage nabworo kom pa se ko wora ko liri na se ko tu na bam kuri. Yezu maa tigi o dɔa. 25O kwaga tɔgena bam ma vo ba zaŋe‑o, ye ba we, “Debam tu, jwoŋi debam ŋwea, se dé lage dé te mo.” 26O ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam fona konto wo bɛ mo? Abam boboŋa muri de Wɛ.” O laam ma zaŋe wɛɛne, ye o daare o bage vio kom de na bam, pa se te maŋe da chemm. 27Nɔɔna bam maa tiini ba ye yaau, ye ba tɛ ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto ke tɛ mo o ye konto? O dam dem pae se vio kom de na bam sɛ o ni.”
Yezu zeili setaana nɔɔna balei tei ne
Maake 5:1-20; Luka 8:26-39
28Ba laam ma vo ba bɛ bubɛ dedwoŋi dem mɛ Gadara tiina na zoore to. Nɔɔna balei maa wora setaana na daane-ba. Banto tigi yibeela jei ne mo, ye ba jege foone pa se nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware o tɔge chwoŋa kam konto o kɛ. Ba laam ma nwoŋi ba peiga jei sem ne ba vo ba jeeri Yezu. 29Ba ma laare baŋa baŋa ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ Bu, nmo tu debam tei se n ke bɛ mo? Nmo tu se n waare debam ye Wɛ borem dɛ dem ta wo yi mo na?”
30Jei sem konto ne teira dedɛ ya wora ya beeri ya wodiu se ya di. 31Setaana yam ma gare ya lwoori Yezu ya we, “Nmo ná lage n zeili debam, se n pa dé vo dé taa tɔge teira yanto.” 32O ma ta o we, ya véi. Ya ma seene ya nwoŋi nɔɔna bam tei ne ya vo ya tɔge teira yam. Teira yam maama ma duri ya siseiri ya tu buga kam wo ya nyɔ na ya te.
33Nɔɔna balo ya na nii teira yam baŋa ne to ma duri ba vo teo kom wo. Ba ma ta kolo maama na ke to, de Yezu na zeili setaana yam nɔɔna balei bam tei ne tei to. 34Ko ma pa se teo kom nɔɔna bam maama nwoŋi ba vo se ba jeeri Yezu. Ba na nɛ‑o to, ba ma lwoori‑o se o nwoŋi ba teo kom ne o viiri.

english_text:
Jesus Heals a Man Who Could Not Walk
(Mark 2.1-12; Luke 5.17-26)
1Jesus got into a boat and crossed back over to the town where he lived. 2Some people soon brought to him a man lying on a mat because he could not walk. When Jesus saw how much faith they had, he said to the man, “My friend, don't worry! Your sins are forgiven.”
3Some teachers of the Law of Moses said to themselves, “Jesus must think he is God!”
4But Jesus knew what was in their minds, and he said, “Why are you thinking such evil things? 5Is it easier for me to tell this man his sins are forgiven or to tell him to get up and walk? 6But I will show you that the Son of Man has the right to forgive sins here on earth.” So Jesus said to the man, “Get up! Pick up your mat and go on home.” 7The man got up and went home. 8When the crowds saw this, they were afraid and praised God for giving such authority to people.
Jesus Chooses Matthew
(Mark 2.13-17; Luke 5.27-32)
9As Jesus was leaving, he saw a tax collector named Matthew sitting at the place for paying taxes. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.” Matthew got up and went with him.
10 Later, Jesus and his disciples were having dinner at Matthew's house. Many tax collectors and other sinners were also there. 11Some Pharisees asked Jesus' disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and other sinners?”
12Jesus heard them and answered, “Healthy people don't need a doctor, but sick people do. 13 Go and learn what the Scriptures mean when they say, ‘Instead of offering sacrifices to me, I want you to be merciful to others.’ I didn't come to invite good people to be my followers. I came to invite sinners.”
People Ask about Going without Eating
(Mark 2.18-22; Luke 5.33-39)
14Some followers of John the Baptist came and asked Jesus, “Why do we and the Pharisees often go without eating, while your disciples never do?”
15Jesus answered:
The friends of a bridegroom aren't sad while he is still with them. But the time will come when he will be taken from them. Then they will go without eating.
16No one uses a new piece of cloth to patch old clothes. The patch would shrink and tear a bigger hole.
17No one pours new wine into old wineskins. The wine would swell and burst the old skins. Then the wine would be lost, and the skins would be ruined. New wine must be put into new wineskins. Both the skins and the wine will then be safe.
A Dying Girl and a Sick Woman
(Mark 5.21-43; Luke 8.40-56)
18While Jesus was still speaking, an official came and knelt in front of him. The man said, “My daughter has just now died! Please come and place your hand on her. Then she will live again.”
19Jesus and his disciples got up and went with the man.
20A woman who had been bleeding for twelve years came up behind Jesus and barely touched his clothes. 21She had said to herself, “If I can just touch his clothes, I will be healed.”
22Jesus turned. He saw the woman and said, “Don't worry! You are now healed because of your faith.” At that moment she was healed.
23When Jesus went into the home of the official and saw the musicians and the crowd of mourners, 24he said, “Get out of here! The little girl isn't dead. She is just asleep.” Everyone started laughing at Jesus. 25But after the crowd had been sent out of the house, Jesus went to the girl's bedside. He took her by the hand and helped her up.
26News about this spread all over that part of the country.
Jesus Heals Two Blind Men
27As Jesus was leaving that place, two blind men began following him and shouting, “Son of David, have pity on us!”
28After Jesus had gone indoors, the two blind men came up to him. He asked them, “Do you believe I can make you well?”
“Yes, Lord,” they answered.
29Jesus touched their eyes and said, “Because of your faith, you will be healed.” 30They were able to see, and Jesus strictly warned them not to tell anyone about him. 31But they left and talked about him to everyone in that part of the country.
Jesus Heals a Man Who Could Not Talk
32As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, some people brought to him a man who could not talk because a demon was in him. 33After Jesus had forced the demon out, the man started talking. The crowds were so amazed they began saying, “Nothing like this has ever happened in Israel!”
34 But the Pharisees said, “The leader of the demons gives him the power to force out demons.”
Jesus Has Pity on People
35 Jesus went to every town and village. He taught in their synagogues and preached the good news about God's kingdom. Jesus also healed every kind of disease and sickness. 36 When he saw the crowds, he felt sorry for them. They were confused and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd. 37 He said to his disciples, “A large crop is in the fields, but there are only a few workers. 38Ask the Lord in charge of the harvest to send out workers to bring it in.”
translation_text:
Yezu bere we o jege dam se o saare nɔɔna wɛleera
Maake 2:1-12; Luka 5:17-26
1Yezu laam ma jwoori o vo o zo nabworo kom. O ma bɛ buga kam o vo o yi o tete teo Kaparenia. 2O na wora to, nɔɔna badwonna ma zeŋe gɔrɔ kolo na tigi gungwolo baŋa ne to ba ba o tei. Yezu ma lɔre ba na tiini ba ke ba wo-dedoa ded‑o tei. O ma ta de gɔrɔ kom o we, “A bu, poore n yera, se nmo wɛleera yam saare.”
3Wɛ nia yam zamesem tiina badwonna maa wora, ye ba ŋɔɔne ba tete yera ne ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto ŋɔɔne o twe Wɛ yere mo.” 4Yezu ma lɔre ba na boŋe kolo to. O ma bwei-ba o we, “Bɛ mo ye á jege wo-balwaaro tem konto á boboŋa ne? 5Kɔ mo ye mɔle, a ná tage we gɔrɔ kom wɛleera yam saare, naa a ná tage we o zaŋe o taa via? 6Amo nam wó pa se abam lɔre we amo wolo na ye Nabiin-bu wom to jege dam logo baŋa ne se a yage nɔɔno wɛleera a ma chɛ‑o.” O laam ma ta de gɔrɔ kom o we, “Zaŋe wɛɛne se n kwei n gungwolo kom n ja n vo sɔŋɔ.” 7O na tage konto to, nɔɔno wom ma seene o zaŋe o viiri. 8Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama na nɛ konto to, foone ma zo-ba. Ba ma zuli Wɛ de o na pɛ dam dem konto wo nabiinu jeŋa ne to.
Yezu bwoŋi Matiyu se o taa tɔge‑o
Maake 2:13-17; Luka 5:27-32
9Yezu laam ma kɛ. O na maa vei to, o ma na nɔɔno wodwoŋi, o yere mo Matiyu. O déem jei mɛ seeni o na yeini o jwoŋi lampwoo nɔɔna tei ne to mo. Yezu ma ta ded‑o o we, “Zaŋe n ta‑n tɔge-ne.” O ma seene o zaŋe o tɔge o kwaga.
10Yezu déem ma vo Matiyu sɔŋɔ se o di wodiu. O de o kwaga tɔgena bam na wora to, lampwoo lara de nɔn-chechɔgero dedɛ maa tɔge ba wora ba di wodiu de-ba. 11Farisi tiina de maa tɔge ba wora. Banto na nɛ Yezu na ke tei to, ba ma vo ba bwei o kwaga tɔgena bam ba we, “Bɛ mo kea ye á berem tu wom di wodiu dedaane lampwoo lara de nɔn-chechɔgero tem konto?”
12Yezu ma ni ba na tage kolo to. O laam ma ta o we, “Ko ná ye balo na jege ya-dɛɛra to, banto ba jege se ba vo dɔkta tu tei se o yɔɔre-ba. Ko daare balo na ba jege yazura to mo jege se ba vo se ba yɔɔre ba tete. 13Wɛ tete maŋe o ta we, ‘Nɔɔna ná jege ba dwonna yibwona, konto pwoli amo wo ko dwoni ba ná ke kaanem ba pa-ne.’ Véi-na á zamese taane dem konto kuri chekke. Amo na tu logo baŋa to, ko dae balo na maŋe ba ye nɔn-ŋona to ŋwaane. A nam tu se a bwoŋi nɔn-chechɔgero mo se ba tɔge chwoŋa.”
Yezu berem dem ye berem-doore
Maake 2:18-22; Luka 5:33-39
14Jɔn kwaga tɔgena déem ma vo Yezu tei, ye ba bwei‑o ba we, “Debam de Farisi tiina bam yeini dé vɔ ni maŋa maama. Bɛ mo kea ye nmo kwaga tɔgena bam ba vɔ ni konto?” 15Yezu ma leiri-ba o we, “Nɔɔno ná wora o ke kadiri, ye o dwonna ná wora se ba tɔge ba di, banto wó wane ba nyɔne ba yiga se ba yé di wodiu na? Kan-baro wom ta ná wora, ba bá sɛ ba ke konto. Ko nam wó ba ko yi maŋa kam ba laam na wó ja kan-baro wom ba viiri to. Maŋa kam konto ne mo o badwonna bam laam wó vɔ ni.
16Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá sɛ se o kwei gare-yi-doore o ma feiri gare-dwoŋo kolo na kaare to. O ná ke konto, ko feirim dem laam wó vuuri gɔrɔ kom ko pa ko chɔge dedɛ. 17Ko woli da, nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá sɛ o kwei sa-doora o lwo o ke lɔ-dwoŋa wone. O ná ke konto ye sana bam ná lage ba keeri, lɔa kam wó bage mo. Sana bam maa wó lwo ba yage, ye lɔa kam de chɔge. Nɔɔno nam maŋe se o kwei sa-doora o ke lɔ-doŋa wone, se te maama maŋe daane.”
Yezu yɔɔre nɔɔna badwonna
Maake 5:21-43; Luka 8:40-56
18Yezu déem na wora o ŋɔɔne konto to, Juu tiina nakwe wodwoŋi ma ba o tei. O ma kuni dwoona o yiga ne ye o we, “Amo bukɔ mo tega leile. Nam ba se n ma n jea n zi‑o, se konto wó pa o jwoori o na ŋwea.” 19Yezu ma seene o zaŋe o tɔge‑o, de o kwaga tɔgena bam maama.
20-21Ba na maa kɛ konto to, kaane wodwoŋi ma vo o tei. Kaane wom konto nam tiini o wɔe wo mo taa, bena fuga-yalei. O maa boŋe o wone o we, “Amo ná dwei o gɔrɔ kom yerane, ko wó pa se a na yazura.” O ma tɔge Yezu kwaga ne o dwei o gɔrɔ kom ni. 22O na dwei‑o konto to, Yezu ma pipiri o na‑o ye o we, “Amo bukɔ, poore n yera. Nmo na ke n wo-dedoa de amo to mo pɛ se n na yazura.” Maŋa kam konto ne nɔɔ mo kaane wom seene o na yazura.
23Yezu laam ma vo o zo Juu tiina nakwe wom sɔŋɔ. O ma zo o na balo na tu se ba leeni lua kam lei to, de nɔɔna dedɛ na wora ba fere ba tete to. 24O ma ta de-ba o we, ba zaŋe ba viiri, se bu wom wo tege, se o tigi o dɔ mo. O na tage konto to, nɔɔna bam maa jege‑o ba mɔna. 25Ba na pɛ se kɔgɔ kom maama nwoŋi to, Yezu laam ma vo o zo diga kam bu wom na wora to. O ma ja o jeŋa pa se o zaŋe wɛɛne.
26O keim dem konto ma jage de yi teo kom jei sem maama ne.
27Yezu déem ma zaŋe o maa kɛa. O na maa vei to, lilwoa balei ma zaŋe ba tɔge o kwaga ye ba tɛ baŋa baŋa ba we, “Pɛ David dwi tu! Duri debam yiniga!”
28O ma vo o zo sɔŋɔ kodwoŋi. Lilwoa balei bam ma tɔge ba zo da. O laam ma bwei-ba o we, “Abam sɛ we amo wó wane a ke á na lage kolo to na?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Debam tu, dé sɛ.” 29O laam ma dwei ba yia yam, ye o we, “Abam na ke á wo-dedoa de amo se a ke kolo to, Wɛ wó pa ko ke.” 30O na tage konto to, ba yia yam ma seene ya jwoori ya nae. O ma kaane-ba we, ba yé pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre ko ni ne. 31O na tage-ba konto to, ba ta ma zaŋe ba kare ba tɛ o taane jei sem maama ne.
32Nɔɔna bam konto na maa kɛ to, nɔɔna badwonna ma ja memaa ba ba Yezu tei. Ko maa ye setaane mo tɔge‑o pa se o ware o ŋɔɔne. 33Yezu ma zeili setaane dem o tei ne. Nɔɔno wom laam maa wae o ŋɔɔna. Ko ma so nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama, ye ba tɛ ba we, “Debam wo fɔge dé na wo-kenkagele dento dwoŋi ywo-seeni Isarele teo ne.” 34Farisi tiina bam déem maa wo sɛ ye ba we, “Wonto na wae o zeili setaana to, ko ye setaana pɛ dam ŋwaane mo.”
35Yezu déem maa kare nawuura yam maama wone o tola. O maa yeini o vei Juu tiina jeerim di sem se o taa bere nɔɔna Wɛ chega kam. O maa tɔɔle Wɛ paare dem kwor-ywoŋa kam, ye o kwori o yɔɔre jaweena de jaweo kolo dwi maama na jege-ba to. 36O déem ma na nɔn-kɔgɔ kom yaara yam na ye tei to. Ba ŋwaŋa ma zo‑o lanyerane, de ba na jege lwia ye ba yeiri ba na wó ke tei to. Ba maa nye de pei selo na ba jege nayero se o taa nii se baŋa ne to. 37O laam ma ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam o we, “Ko nye de wodiu faao na ke lanyerane, ye tontoŋena fenfee yerane wora se ba zage tei to mo. 38Nam lwoori-na faao totoŋa yam yuu tu se o toŋe nɔɔna dedɛ se ba vo ba zage faao kom ba pa‑o.”

english_text:
Jesus Chooses His Twelve Apostles
(Mark 3.13-19; Luke 6.12-16)
1Jesus called together his twelve disciples. He gave them the power to force out evil spirits and to heal every kind of disease and sickness. 2The first of the twelve apostles was Simon, better known as Peter. His brother Andrew was an apostle, and so were James and John, the two sons of Zebedee. 3Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew the tax collector, James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus were also apostles. 4The others were Simon, known as the Eager One, and Judas Iscariot, who later betrayed Jesus.
Instructions for the Twelve Apostles
(Mark 6.7-13; Luke 9.1-6)
5Jesus sent out the twelve apostles with these instructions:
Stay away from the Gentiles and don't go to any Samaritan town. 6Go only to the people of Israel, because they are like a flock of lost sheep. 7 As you go, announce that the kingdom of heaven will soon be here. 8Heal the sick, raise the dead to life, heal people who have leprosy, and force out demons. You received without paying, now give without being paid. 9Don't take along any gold, silver, or copper coins. 10 And don't carry a traveling bag or an extra shirt or sandals or a walking stick.
Workers deserve their food. 11So when you go to a town or a village, find someone able and willing to have you as their guest and stay with them until you leave. 12When you go to a home, give it your blessing of peace. 13If the home is deserving, let your blessing remain with them. But if the home doesn't accept you, take back your blessing of peace. 14 If someone won't welcome you or listen to your message, leave their home or town. And shake the dust from your feet at them. 15 I promise you the day of judgment will be easier for the towns of Sodom and Gomorrah than for that town.
Warning about Trouble
(Mark 13.9-13; Luke 21.12-17)
16 I am sending you like lambs into a pack of wolves. So be as wise as snakes and as innocent as doves. 17 Watch out for people who will take you to court and have you beaten in their synagogues. 18Because of me, you will be dragged before rulers and kings to tell them and the Gentiles about your faith. 19But when someone arrests you, don't worry about what you will say or how you will say it. At that time you will be given the words to say. 20But you will not really be the one speaking. The Spirit from your Father will tell you what to say.
21 Brothers and sisters will betray one another and have each other put to death. Parents will betray their own children, and children will turn against their parents and have them killed. 22 Everyone will hate you because of me. But if you remain faithful until the end, you will be saved. 23When people mistreat you in one town, hurry to another one. I promise you before you have gone to all the towns of Israel, the Son of Man will come.
24 Students are not better than their teacher, and slaves are not better than their master. 25 It is enough for students to be like their teacher and for slaves to be like their master. If people call the head of the family Satan, what will they say about the rest of the family?
The One To Fear
(Luke 12.2-7)
26 Don't be afraid of anyone! Everything that is hidden will be found out, and every secret will be known. 27Whatever I say to you in the dark, you must tell in the light. And you must announce from the housetops whatever I have whispered to you. 28 Don't be afraid of people. They can kill you, but they cannot harm your soul. Instead, you should fear God who can destroy both your body and your soul in hell. 29Aren't two sparrows sold for only a penny? But your Father knows when any one of them falls to the ground. 30Even the hairs on your head are counted. 31So don't be afraid! You are worth much more than many sparrows.
Telling Others about Christ
(Luke 12.8,9)
32If you tell others you belong to me, I will tell my Father in heaven you are my followers. 33 But if you reject me, I will tell my Father in heaven you don't belong to me.
Not Peace, but Trouble
(Luke 12.51-53; 14.26,27)
34Don't think I came to bring peace to the earth! I came to bring trouble, not peace. 35 I came to turn sons against their fathers, daughters against their mothers, and daughters-in-law against their mothers-in-law. 36Your worst enemies will be in your own family.
37 If you love your father or mother or even your sons and daughters more than me, you are not fit to be my disciples. 38 And unless you are willing to take up your cross and follow me, you are not fit to be my disciples. 39 If you try to save your life, you will lose it. But if you give it up for me, you will surely find it.
Rewards
(Mark 9.41)
40 Anyone who welcomes you welcomes me. And anyone who welcomes me also welcomes the one who sent me. 41Anyone who welcomes a prophet, just because that person is a prophet, will be given the same reward as a prophet. Anyone who welcomes a good person, just because that person is good, will be given the same reward as a good person. 42And anyone who gives one of my most humble followers a cup of cool water, just because that person is my follower, will be rewarded.
translation_text:
Yezu toŋe o nɔɔna fuga-balei bam
Maake 3:13-19; 6:7-13; Luka 6:12-16; 9:1-6
1Yezu déem ma bwoŋi o nɔɔna fuga-balei bam se ba ba o tei. O ma pa-ba dam se ba wane setaana ba zeili nɔɔna tei ne, se ba daare ba pa nɔɔna na yazura ba jaweero dwi maama wone.
2O totoŋa nakwa fuga-balei bam yera mo tento:
Simon wolo yere dedwoŋi na ye Piita to mo ye boboa tu.
Ko woli de Anduru wolo na ye Simon nyaane to,
de Jemsi, de o nyaane Jɔn, balo na ye Zebedi bia to.
3Filipi de Batoloma.
Tomas de Matiyu wolo na ye lampwoo laro to.
Jemsi wolo na ye Alafayu bu to, de Tadayus.
4Simon wolo na nwoŋi Zɛlota tigisim wone to,
de Judas Yisakara wolo na tu o yeigi Yezu o pa nɔɔna to.
5Yezu laam ma toŋe banto fuga-balei bam se ba nwoŋi ba beeri. Ba na lage ba kɛ konto to, o ma kaane-ba we, ba yé zaŋe ba vo dwi-gɛ tiina na zoore mɛ to, naa ba vo Samaria tiina teo. 6O maa we, “Á nam jege se á vo Isarele dwi tiina bam tei, se banto nye de pei selo na beeri kafɛ to mo. 7Nam véi-na á bere-ba we maŋa kam yia Wɛ telaao paare dem na lage de ba o nɔɔna baŋa to. 8Véi-na á ta‑á yɔɔre jaweena, se á daare á ta‑á bi balo na tege to, se á pa naywanno jwoori te na yazura, se á daare á ta‑á zeili setaana nɔɔna tei ne. Á nam jege se á zeini nɔɔna zɛɛra mo, á na jwoŋi á dam Wɛ tei ne zɛɛra to ŋwaane. 9Á ná maa vei, se á yé zaŋe á kwei sabu-seŋa naa sabu dwi maama á ke ganlɔgere ne á woli da. 10Nam yé kwei-na tampɔgɔ kolo á na wó ta‑á jwoŋi wodiu á ke da to. Á nam yé kwei gwaaro telei telei, naa natera, naa nacheiga á woli da. Kokuri, tontoŋeno maŋe se o taa jwoŋi o ni-wodiu mo.
11Abam nam ná vei á yi teo kolo, se á lage wolo na ye nɔn-ŋom to, se á laam vo o sɔŋɔ á ta‑á wora se ko ba ko yi á viirim. 12Á nam ná vei á zo sɔŋɔ kolo, se á jɔɔne-ba. 13Sɔŋɔ kom tiina nam ná jeeri abam lanyerane, se á lwoori Wɛ se yazura taa wo ba tei ne. Ko daare, ba ná wo ke abam lanyerane, Wɛ wó pa abam mo leiri ba yuu ne á na yazura. 14Abam nam ná vei sɔŋɔ kolo naa teo kolo, ye ba ná wo sɛ se ba jeeri abam naa ba cheigi abam taane, se á yage jei sem konto. Á ná maa viira, se á kokɔge á nɛ fwogo kom á yage da. 15A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, Wɛ borem dɛ dem ná yia, Sodom de Gomora tiina bá tiini ba na lɛɛro se ko maŋe de teo kom konto.
Yaara yalo na wó yi-ba to taane
Maake 13:9-13; 9:41; Luka 21:12-17; 12:2-9, 51-53; 14:26-27
16Nii-na, a na lage a toŋe abam tei to, á wó ta‑á nye de pei na maa vei se se gwaane wiira wone tei to mo. Mo kokuri á jege se á ta‑á yei á tete ne basankwe na jege se tete tei to, se á daare á pa á wo taa lana ne kunkwona na ye tei to. 17Ta‑á cho-na á tete de nɔɔna na lage ba ke abam tei to. Badaara wó ja abam ba vo ba saŋe nakwa tei ne, ye ba daare ba ja abam ba fere ba jeerim di sem wone. 18Abam na tɔge amo to ŋwaane, ba wó ja abam ba vo ba saŋe dedɛɛra de pwa tei ne. Konto mo á wó wane á bere-ba Wɛ chega kam, ye á daare á bere dwi-gɛ tiina de. 19Ba nam ná jaane abam konto, se á yé ta‑á jege lwia de á na wó ta kolo, naa á na wó leiri-ba tei to. Abam na wó ta‑á zege ba yiga ne maŋa kalo to, Wɛ wó pa á lɔre á na wó ta kolo to. 20Ko bá taa ye abam tete taane, se ko ye á Kwo Wɛ Sin-laao kom mo wó tɔge abam baŋa pa se á ŋɔɔne.
21Nɔɔna badwonna wó ja ba tete chorro ba ke nɔɔna jeŋa ne se ba go-ba. Kwoa de wó ke ba bia konto dwoŋi. Bia de wó zaŋe ba tiina baŋa ne ye ba pa ba ja-ba ba go. 22Nɔɔna maama wó taa chuli abam, á na ye amo nyem to ŋwaane. Wolo maama nam ná tiini o jege pu-dɛa se ko vo ko kweeli, Wɛ wó jwoŋi konto tu ŋwea. 23Ba nam ná bɛɛse abam teo kolo ne, se á duri á vo kodwoŋi. A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, abam bá wane á tole teene delo maama na wo Isarele ne to á ti ye amo Nabiin-bu wom daa ta wo jwoori a ba.
24Zenzamso nam tera o na dwoi o berem tu. Kabaa de nam tera ka na dwoi ka tu. 25Zenzamso nam ná tu o yi ne o berem tu wom tei, konto mo lana ko pa‑o. Kabaa de ná tu ka yi ne o tu wom tei, konto mo lana ko pa‑o. Ba ná jege sɔŋɔ tu ba bwoi we, ‘Setaana pɛ Bɛlzabula’, ba nam wó tiini ba twe o sɔŋɔ tiina bam se ko dwoni konto.
26Á nam yé ta‑á fona de nabiina. Woŋo kolo maama na seigi nɔɔna tei ne to laam wó ba ko lɔre jaja. 27Amo na seigi a bere abam chega kalo maama to, á jege se á pa ka nwoŋi pwooni mo se á pa ba di nayuu ba tɔɔle-ka. 28Ko ná ye nabiina, banto wae ba goe á yera ye ba ware á jworru ba go. Konto ŋwaane, á yé ta‑á kɔre foone de-ba. Á jege se á ta‑á kɔre Wɛ mo, kokuri wonto wae o chɔge á yera de á jworru maama te-seŋa ne.
29Ko ná ye zun-kabeili, ba yeini ba yeigi sento mɔle mo. Á Kwo Wɛ nam nii sento baŋa ne, ye se dedoa bá wane ka to tega ne ka te ye o wo sɛ. 30Ko nam ná ye abam, Wɛ maŋe o yei abam yu-ywei sem ni na mae tei to. 31Konto ŋwaane, á yé ta‑á kɔre foone, se abam dedoa dedoa tiini á jege fera á dwoi zun-kabeili dedɛ.
32Nɔɔno wolo maama ná zege nabiina yiga ne o bere jaja we wonto ye amo nyem, amo de nam wó zege konto tu kwaga ne a bere we o ye a nyem a Kwo Wɛ yiga ne. 33Ko daare nɔɔno wolo maama ná ve amo nabiina yiga ne, amo de wó ve konto tu a Kwo Wɛ yiga ne.
34Amo na tu logo baŋa to, á yé ta‑á boŋe we ko ye se a pa nɔɔna mo na ywoni daane. A nam tu se a de jara mo nabiina tetare ne. 35A tu se a pa nɔɔna de ba kwoa mo chɔge daane, se a daare a pa bukwa de ba niina de ke konto, se kaana de ba banna niina de chɔge daane. 36Ko maa wó pa se nɔɔno de o tete sɔŋɔ tiina taa done daane.
37Wolo ná swoi o tete kwo de o nu se ko dwoni amo, konto tu wo yi se o taa ye amo nyem, ko woli de wolo maama na swoi o bia o dwoi amo to. 38Wolo maama ná wo sɛ se o tɔge amo kwaga se o na yaara ne wolo na zeŋe dagara o maa vei o toone tei to, konto tu wo yi se o taa ye amo nyem. 39Wolo nam na kwaane se o taa jege o tete ŋwea to wó ga-ka Wɛ tei ne. Ko daare wolo na gɛ o ŋwea amo ŋwaane to wó na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne.
40Wolo nam ná jeeri abam lanyerane, konto tu jeeri amo mo. Wolo maa ná jeeri amo, konto tu jeeri Baŋa Wɛ wolo na toŋe-ne to mo. 41Nɔɔno wolo maama ná jeeri Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu lanyerane, de Wɛ na toŋe‑o to ŋwaane, Wɛ wó pa konto tu de tɔge o na nyɔɔre ne o ni-jwoŋinu wom tei. Ko woli da, nɔɔno wolo ná jeeri nɔn-ŋom o nɔn-ŋonne dem ŋwaane, Wɛ wó pa konto tu tɔge o na nyɔɔre delo o na wó pa nɔn-ŋom wom to. 42A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, nɔɔno wolo ná nɛ amo nɔn-balaŋa dedoa, ye o ná pɛ‑o na-zura se o nyɔ o na ye amo tɔgeno to ŋwaane, konto tu wó tiini o na nyɔɔre Wɛ tei ne mo.”

english_text:
John the Baptist
(Luke 7.18-35)
1After Jesus had finished instructing his twelve disciples, he left and began teaching and preaching in the towns.
2John was in prison when he heard what Christ was doing. So John sent some of his followers 3to ask Jesus, “Are you the one we should be looking for? Or must we wait for someone else?”
4Jesus answered, “Go and tell John what you have heard and seen. 5 The blind are now able to see, and the lame can walk. People with leprosy are being healed, and the deaf can hear. The dead are raised to life, and the poor are hearing the good news. 6God will bless everyone who doesn't reject me because of what I do.”
7As John's followers were going away, Jesus spoke to the crowds about John:
What sort of person did you go out into the desert to see? Was he like tall grass blown about by the wind? 8What kind of man did you go out to see? Was he someone dressed in fine clothes? People who dress like that live in the king's palace. 9What did you really go out to see? Was he a prophet? He certainly was. I tell you that he was more than a prophet. 10 In the Scriptures God says about him, “I am sending my messenger ahead to get things ready for you.” 11I tell you no one ever born on this earth is greater than John the Baptist. But whoever is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than John.
12 From the time of John the Baptist until now, violent people have been trying to take over the kingdom of heaven by force. 13All the Books of the Prophets and the Law of Moses told what was going to happen up to the time of John. 14 And if you believe them, John is Elijah, the prophet you are waiting for. 15If you have ears, pay attention!
16You people are like children sitting in the market and shouting to each other,
17“We played the flute,
but you would not dance!
We sang a funeral song,
but you would not mourn!”
18John the Baptist did not go around eating and drinking, and you said, “That man has a demon in him!” 19But the Son of Man goes around eating and drinking, and you say, “That man eats and drinks too much! He is even a friend of tax collectors and sinners.” Yet Wisdom is shown to be right by what it does.
The Unbelieving Towns
(Luke 10.13-15)
20In the towns where Jesus had worked most of his miracles, the people refused to turn to God. So Jesus was upset with them and said:
21 You people of Chorazin are in for trouble! You people of Bethsaida are in for trouble too! If the miracles that took place here had happened in Tyre and Sidon, the people there would have turned to God long ago. They would have dressed in sackcloth and put ashes on their heads. 22I tell you on the day of judgment the people of Tyre and Sidon will get off easier than you will.
23 People of Capernaum, do you think you will be honored in heaven? You will go down to hell! If the miracles that took place in your town had happened in Sodom, it would still be standing. 24 So I tell you on the day of judgment the people of Sodom will get off easier than you.
Come to Me and Rest
(Luke 10.21,22)
25At that moment Jesus said:
My Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I am grateful that you hid all this from wise and educated people and showed it to ordinary people. 26Yes, Father, this is what pleased you.
27 My Father has given me everything, and he is the only one who knows the Son. The only one who truly knows the Father is the Son. But the Son wants to tell others about the Father, so they can know him too.
28 If you are tired from carrying heavy burdens, come to me and I will give you rest. 29 Take the yoke I give you. Put it on your shoulders and learn from me. I am gentle and humble, and you will find rest. 30This yoke is easy to bear, and this burden is light.
translation_text:
Jɔn wolo na pae nɔɔna sɛɛm to taane
Luka 7:18-35
1Yezu déem na pɛ o kwaga tɔgena fuga-balei bam o ni dem o ti to, o laam ma kɛ o vo jei sem konto teene dem wone o tola, se o taa bere nɔɔna ye o tɔɔle Wɛ kwora o pa-ba.
2Jɔn wolo na pae nɔɔna sɛɛm Wɛ ŋwaane to déem maa wo peena diga ne. O ma ba o lɔre Wɛ Dam Tu Yezu na ke kikia yalo to. O ma toŋe o kwaga tɔgena badwonna se ba vo ba nii‑o, 3se ba daare ba bwei‑o we, “Nmo mo ye wolo Wɛ na bere debam we o wó ba to na? Naa dé ta wó taa teene nɔɔno wodwoŋi mo?” 4Ba na bwei Yezu konto to, o ma leiri-ba o we, ba véi ba ta de Jɔn kolo maama ba na nɛ ye ba kwori ba ni to. 5“Á ta á bere‑o we, lilwoa jwoori ba nae, gwaaro de wae te via, naywanno yera de maa kwɛ lanyerane, zwa-kwarro de zwa ni, twa de jwoori ba bi. Ko woli da, yiniga tiina de maa ni Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam. 6Wolo maama na ba jwoori Wɛ kwaga ne amo ŋwaane to mo ye yu-ywoŋo tu.”
7Jɔn kwaga tɔgena bam ma zaŋe se ba viiri. Ba na maa kɛ to, Yezu laam ma ta Jɔn taane o bere nɔn-kɔgɔ kom. O ma ta de-ba o we:
“Abam déem na vei Jɔn tei kagoa yuu ne to, á boŋe we á wó na bɛ mo? Á vei se á nii gaaro telo vio na jege ko dole to mo na? 8Aawo. Se bɛ mo? Á vei se á nii nɔn-yero na zo gare-nyenno to mo na? Aawo. Nɔn-yero nam wó taa zoore sɔ-fɔrɔ wone mo, se ko dae kagoa yuu ne. 9Bɛ nam mo ye á vo? Á vei se á na Wɛ sampwora mo na? Ɛɛ, ko ye konto mo. Á nam na nɛ wolo to tiini o dwoi faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem na ye tei to. 10Wɛ tɔnɔ kom nam maŋe ko ta wonto taane ko we,
‘Nii, amo Wɛ lage a toŋe a tontoŋeno mo,
se o da nmo yiga o vo o kwɛ chwoŋa kalo nmo na wó tɔge da to.’
11A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, nabiina balo ba na maŋe ba lo to wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na yi Wɛ tontoŋeno Jɔn na ye tei to. Ko daare leile konto, nɔn-yɔɔ kolo maama na zo Wɛ woro kom wone to laam tu o dwoi Jɔn. 12Ko zege maŋa kalo Jɔn déem na pɛ nɔɔna sɛɛm to, se ko ba ko yi zem to, Wɛ telaao paare dem laam jage de yi yiga de dam. Balo na seene ba yia Wɛ paare dem ŋwaane to laam mo kwaane lanyerane se ba tɔge ba di o paare dem konto. 13Ko ná ye faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem de Moses de déem na bere kolo to, ba maŋe ba bere Wɛ paare dem chega kam se ko ba ko yi maŋa kalo Jɔn laam na tu to. 14Abam ná sɛ á jwoŋi ba na bere chega kalo to, á wó lɔre we Jɔn na tu o wora to, wonto mo ye Elija wolo ba déem na ŋɔɔne o taane we o wó ba to.
15Abam nam fɔge á cheigi amo taane dem. 16Amo nam wó ke tɛ mo a maŋe zem nɔɔna bam kikia na ye tei to? Ba nye de bia na jei yaga kaporo ne ba kwɛɛra to mo. Ba maa tɛ de ba yuudwonna ba we:
17‘Dé mage gullu mo se á sa,
ye á wo sage.
Dé ma daare dé leeni luseim dé pa abam,
ye á wo sɛ se á pa á yiga nyɔne.’
18Zem nɔɔna bam de ye konto mo. Jɔn na tu to, o peene o kana mo ye o ba nyɔ sana. Nɔɔna na nɛ‑o to, ba maa jege‑o ba yaala we, ko ye setaane mo tɔge‑o. 19Ko daare amo Nabiin-bu wom nam na tu to, amo wo vɔge ni. Nɔɔna daa ta ma yaale amo de ye ba we, a ye nɔn-kwolo mo, ye a ye sa-nyɔro de. Ba daa ta maa we, a me de lampwoo lara de nɔn-chechɔgero mo. Abam nam wó ba á lɔre swa yalo na ye chekke to de ya na pae se nɔɔna tɔge kikia yalo to.”
Lɛɛro wó yi balo na ve Yezu to
Luka 10:13-15
20Yezu na tage konto o ti to, o laam maa jege balo na nɛ o wo-kenkagela yam ye ba ta wo sɛ se ba leiri ba wo to taane o ŋɔɔna. O ma kaane balo na zoore teene delo o na ke wo-kenkagela dedɛ da to, ye o we, 21“Abam Chorazin tiina, lɛɛro yi abam! Ko woli de abam Bɛtasida tiina, lɛɛro yi abam! Kokuri, wo-kenkagela yalo maama amo na ke abam tei ne to, ya dwoŋi ya ná kea Tura de Sidon tiina tei ne, banto ya wó ke lela ba leiri ba wo Wɛ ŋwaane. Ba maa wó zo gare-nyenyaaro ye ba jei tentwarem wone ba wo-chechɔgɔ kom ŋwaane. 22Ta‑á yei-na we, Wɛ borem dɛ dem ná yia, Tura de Sidon tiina bá tiini ba na lɛɛro se ko maŋe de abam.
23Ko nam ná ye abam Kaparenia tiina, á ga boŋe we Wɛ lage o zeiŋi abam wɛyuu ne mo na? Aawo. Abam nam wó to á zo tega kuri kuri ne mo. Kokuri, wo-kenkagela yalo maama amo na ke abam tei ne to, ya dwoŋi ya ná kea Sodom tiina tei ne, ba ya wó leiri ba wo pa se Wɛ ya bá chɔge ba teo kom. 24Á ta‑á yei we, Wɛ borem dɛ dem ná yia, Sodom teo kom bá tiini ko na lɛɛro se ko maŋe de abam.”
Yezu wó pa nɔɔna na siu de ba cham
Luka 10:21-22
25Maŋa kam Yezu na ŋɔɔne konto o ti to, o déem ma ke o Kwo Baŋa Wɛ lei ye o we, “A Kwo, nmo mo ye wolo na tei wɛyuu de tega baŋa maama. Nmo nam pɛ se n chega kam seigi swa tiina de yi-pore-nyena tei ne, ye n daare n pa se balo boboŋa ta na wo bege to lɔre ka kuri. 26A Kwo, a ke nmo lei. Nmo na ke konto to, ko ye n boboŋa na lage kolo to ŋwaane.
27A Kwo Wɛ mo kwei wonnu maama o ke a jeŋa ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o lɔre Wɛ Bu wom o ti, ko ná dae o Kwo yerane. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa ta bá lɔre a Kwo Wɛ, ko ná dae amo wolo na ye o Bu wom to yerane, ko woli de amo na boŋe se a pa nɔɔno wolo maama lɔre o na ye tei to.
28Abam balo na wo cham dedɛ wone, ye á yera chɛ de totoŋa pa se á laam bugi to, se á maama ba amo tei se a pa á na siu. 29Ba-na á sale amo yera ne, nenɛɛne nabɛ na sale daane se vare tei to. Kokuri a ye nɔn-mɔlɔ mo ye a gwooni a tete. A maa wó pa á boboŋa taa tigi jeiga dedoa. 30Á ná sale amo yera ne, a bá taa chana á baŋa ne, ye ko wó taa lana ko pa abam.”

english_text:
A Question about the Sabbath
(Mark 2.23-28; Luke 6.1-5)
1 One Sabbath, Jesus and his disciples were walking through some wheat fields. His disciples were hungry and began picking and eating grains of wheat. 2Some Pharisees noticed this and said to Jesus, “Why are your disciples picking grain on the Sabbath? They are not supposed to do this!”
3 Jesus answered:
You surely must have read what David did when he and his followers were hungry. 4 He went into the house of God, and then they ate the sacred loaves of bread that only priests are supposed to eat. 5 Haven't you read in the Law of Moses that the priests are allowed to work in the temple on the Sabbath? But no one says they are guilty of breaking the law of the Sabbath. 6I tell you there is something here greater than the temple. 7 Don't you know what the Scriptures mean when they say, “Instead of offering sacrifices to me, I want you to be merciful to others?” If you knew what this means, you would not condemn these innocent disciples of mine. 8So the Son of Man is Lord over the Sabbath.
A Man with a Paralyzed Hand
(Mark 3.1-6; Luke 6.6-11)
9Jesus left and went into one of their synagogues, 10where there was a man whose hand was paralyzed. Some Pharisees wanted to accuse Jesus of doing something wrong, so they asked him, “Is it right to heal someone on the Sabbath?”
11 Jesus answered, “If one of your sheep fell into a ditch on the Sabbath, wouldn't you lift it out? 12People are worth much more than sheep, and so it is right to do good on the Sabbath.” 13Then Jesus told the man, “Hold out your hand.” The man did, and it became as healthy as the other one.
14The Pharisees left and started making plans to kill Jesus.
God's Chosen Servant
15When Jesus found out what was happening, he left there and large crowds followed him. He healed all of their sick, 16but warned them not to tell anyone about him. 17So God's promise came true, just as Isaiah the prophet had said,
18 “Here is my chosen servant!
I love him,
and he pleases me.
I will give him my Spirit,
and he will bring justice
to the nations.
19He won't shout or yell
or call out in the streets.
20He won't break off a bent reed
or put out a dying flame,
but he will make sure
that justice is done.
21All nations will place
their hope in him.”
Jesus and the Ruler of the Demons
(Mark 3.20-30; Luke 11.14-23; 12.10)
22Some people brought to Jesus a man who was blind and could not talk because he had a demon in him. Jesus healed the man, and then he was able to talk and see. 23The crowds were so amazed they asked, “Could Jesus be the Son of David?”
24 When the Pharisees heard this, they said, “He forces out demons by the power of Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons!”
25Jesus knew what they were thinking, so he said to them:
Any kingdom where people fight each other will end up ruined. And a town or family that fights will soon destroy itself. 26So if Satan fights against himself, how can his kingdom last? 27If I use the power of Beelzebul to force out demons, whose power do your own followers use to force them out? Your followers are the ones who will judge you. 28But when I force out demons by the power of God's Spirit, it proves that God's kingdom has already come to you. 29 How can anyone break into a strong man's house and steal his things, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can take everything.
30 If you are not on my side, you are against me. If you don't gather in the harvest with me, you scatter it. 31-32 I tell you any sinful thing you do or say can be forgiven. Even if you speak against the Son of Man, you can be forgiven. But if you speak against the Holy Spirit, you can never be forgiven, either in this life or in the life to come.
A Tree and Its Fruit
(Luke 6.43-45)
33 A good tree produces good fruit, and a bad tree produces bad fruit. You can tell what a tree is like by the fruit it produces. 34 You are a bunch of evil snakes, so how can you say anything good? Your words show what is in your hearts. 35Good people bring good things out of their hearts, but evil people bring evil things out of their hearts. 36I promise you on the day of judgment, everyone will have to account for every careless word they have spoken. 37On that day they will be told they are either innocent or guilty because of the things they have said.
A Sign from Heaven
(Mark 8.11,12; Luke 11.29-32)
38 Some Pharisees and teachers of the Law of Moses said, “Teacher, we want you to show us a sign from heaven.”
39 But Jesus replied:
You want a sign because you are evil and won't believe! But the only sign you will get is the sign of the prophet Jonah. 40 He was in the stomach of a big fish for three days and nights, just as the Son of Man will be deep in the earth for three days and nights. 41 On the day of judgment the people of Nineveh will stand there with you and condemn you. They turned to God when Jonah preached, and yet here is something far greater than Jonah. 42 The Queen of the South will also stand there with you and condemn you. She traveled a long way to hear Solomon's wisdom, and yet here is something much greater than Solomon.
Return of an Evil Spirit
(Luke 11.24-26)
43When an evil spirit leaves a person, it travels through the desert, looking for a place to rest. But when the demon doesn't find a place, 44it says, “I will go back to the home I left.” When it gets there and finds the place empty, clean, and neat, 45it goes off and finds seven other evil spirits even worse than itself. They all come and make their home there, and the person ends up in worse shape than before. That's how it will be with you evil people of today.
Jesus' Mother and Brothers
(Mark 3.31-35; Luke 8.19-21)
46While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers came and stood outside because they wanted to talk with him. 47Someone told Jesus, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside and want to talk with you.”
48Jesus answered, “Who is my mother and who are my brothers?” 49Then he pointed to his disciples and said, “These are my mother and my brothers! 50Anyone who obeys my Father in heaven is my brother or sister or mother.”
translation_text:
Siu dɛ chullu
Maake 2:23-28; 3:1-6; Luka 6:1-11
1Da yam konto ni ne Yezu déem ma tɔge kara wo o maa kɛa. Ko déem maa ye Juu tiina siu dɛ dem ne mo konto. O kwaga tɔgena bam de maa tɔge ba wora, ye kana jege-ba. Ba ma bobo se ba taa bwori mena ba yui ba dona. 2Farisi tiina na tɔge ba wora to ma na ba na ke kolo to. Ba laam ma ta de Yezu ba we, “Nii nmo kwaga tɔgena bam na ke kolo. Ko ye totoŋe delo na chɔge Wɛ siu dɛ chullu tem to mo.” 3Yezu ma leiri-ba o we, “Nam guli-na Wɛ tɔnɔ kom na bere Pɛ David taane tei to. Kana déem mo jege wonto de o nɔɔna. 4O ma vo o zo Wɛ diga kam o kwei bworobworo kolo na tigi da Wɛ ŋwaane to pa se o de o tɔgena bam di. Ko nam chula se banto ya di bworobworo kom, se ko ye Wɛ kaanem tiina yerane mo jege chwoŋa se ba di-ko. 5Ko ta woli da, Wɛ tɔn-dwoŋo kom bere we Wɛ kaanem tiina yeini ba toŋe o diga kam totoŋa siu dɛ maama wone mo. Ba maa yeini ba toŋe konto ye ba ta jege bora ko wone. Ko bere we Wɛ diga kam fɔgem dwoi siu dɛ chullu tem. 6Ko daare leile konto, Nabiin-bu wom tu logo baŋa ye wonto dwoi Wɛ diga kam. 7Wɛ tage o we, ‘Nɔɔna ná jege ba dwonna yibwona, konto pwoli amo wo ko dwoni ba ná ke kaanem ba pa-ne.’ Abam ya ná lɔre taane dento kuri, á ya bá yaale balo na jege bora to. 8Kokuri Nabiin-bu wom jege dam siu dɛ chullu tem baŋa ne.”
9Yezu laam ma vo o kɛ. O ma vo o zo Juu tiina jeerim diga kadwoŋi jei sem konto ne. 10Nɔɔno maa wora o jeŋa dedoa na tega. Nɔɔna badwonna de maa wora ba na lage chwoŋa se ba bere we Yezu ke o tusi. Ba ma bwei‑o ba we, “Nɔɔno jege chwoŋa se o yɔɔre o dwoŋi siu dɛ dem ne na?” 11Yezu ma leiri-ba o we, “Abam wolo ná jege pia, ye ka ná to gwoŋo wone siu dɛ dem ne, á bá nii ka baŋa ne se á le-ka na? 12Nabiinu nam tiini o jege kuri o dwoi pia. Konto bere we nɔɔno jege chwoŋa se o ke o dwoŋi lanyerane siu dɛ dem ne.” 13O na tage konto to, o laam ma ta de nɔɔno wolo jeŋa kam na tege to o we, “Twe n jeŋa kam.” Nɔɔno wom ma seene o ke konto, dedaane o jeŋa kam jwoori ka ke lanyerane, ne o je-ŋoŋa kam tei. 14Farisi tiina bam na nɛ konto to, ba ma nwoŋi ba vo ba ŋɔɔne daane ye ba lage chwoŋa se ba go Yezu.
15Yezu déem ma lɔre ba na lage se ba chɔge‑o tei to. O ma yage jei sem konto o kɛ ye nɔn-kɔgɔ dedɛ déem tɔge‑o. O ma yɔɔre ba maama jaweero tem, 16ye o kaane-ba o we, ba yé zaŋe ba pa nɔɔna lɔre o ni ne. 17Yezu na ke tei konto to, ko ye se ko pa Wɛ sampwora Izaya na maŋe o ta Wɛ kwora kalo faŋa faŋa to mo ba ka ji chega, de o na we:
18“Nii-na, amo tontoŋeno wolo a na kuri to mo tento.
Wonto mo amo swoi ye o kikia su amo yi.
Amo wó kwei a Jworo mo a ke o wone.
O maa wó pa se dwi maama tiina ba ba lɔre
amo na toŋe chega a pa-ba tei to.
19O bá mage ni-kantɔgɔ naa o dɔne o kwora se o ke sɔɔ.
O nam bá taa pae o kwora zaŋa teo pwooni ne.
20Ko ná ye nanchan-gaa kalo na bwona to,
o bere o bá bwori-ka.
O nam bá ja min-zwoŋo kolo nuga na ti to mini
o dwei o yage.
O maa wó taa ye konto mo taa
se o laam pa Wɛ chega kam ba ka yi nɔɔna maama.
21Wonto yere ŋwaane mo
dwi maama tiina wó taa jege teena Wɛ tei ne.”
Wɔ dam mo Yezu mae o zeili setaana?
Maake 3:20-30; Luka 11:14-23; 12:10; 6:43-45
22Nɔɔna badwonna déem ma ja lilwei wolo ta na ware o ŋɔɔne to ba ba Yezu tei. Ko maa ye setaane mo daane‑o konto dwoŋi. Yezu ma yɔɔre nɔɔno wom pa se o yia jwoori ya nae ye o daare o wae o ŋɔɔne de. 23Ko ma so nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama, ye ba tɛ ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto mo wó taa ye Pɛ David dwi tu wolo Wɛ na lage o toŋe to na?”
24Farisi tiina bam na nigi konto to, ba ma ta ba we, “Wonto na wae o zeili setaana to, ko ye o tɔge setaana pɛ Bɛlzabula dam ŋwaane mo o ke konto.” 25Yezu ma lɔre ba boboŋa na ye tei to. O ma ta de-ba o we, “Teo kolo paare ná pɔɔre kuni belei pa ba jege daane, ko bá dáane ko chɔge. Teo kolo maama naa sɔŋɔ kolo maama ná pɔɔre ko tete wone, konto wó to lela mo. 26Ko ná seene ko ye chega we amo mae setaana pɛ dam mo a zeili setaana, konto wó bere we setaana pɛ dam dem pɔɔre belei mo ye o paare dem bá dáane de chɔge. 27Ko ná seene ko ye amo tɔge Bɛlzabula dam ŋwaane mo a ma a zeili setaana, abam nɔɔna bam de nam mae dam dem konto mo ba maa zeili-ya na? Á nam wó sɛ we ko ye konto na? Abam tete nɔɔna bam na ke tei to mo bere we chega tera á tei ne. 28Ko nam na ye tei to, ko ye Wɛ Sin-laao kom dam ŋwaane mo pa se a wae setaana a zeila, ye konto maa bere we Wɛ maŋe o ba se o di paare abam yuu ne.
29Setaana pɛ nam nye de nɔn-babea na nii o sɔŋɔ tei to mo. Nɔɔno ná lage se o vo nɔn-babea sɔŋɔ o ŋɔ, o jege se o bobo o ja nɔn-babea kam mo o vɔ. O ná ke konto dwoŋi mo o laam wó wane wonnu tem o kwaleme.
30Nɔɔno wolo maama nam na ba zege amo kwaga ne to ye amo dono mo. Nɔɔno wolo maama na ba tɔge o lae amo wonnu o pa-ne to boŋe se o jage-te mo. 31Á ta‑á yei we, keim-balwaaro telo maama nɔɔna na ke to, naa ta-balwaaro telo ba na ŋɔɔne to, Wɛ wae o yage-te o ma chɛ-ba. Ko daare nɔɔno wolo nam ná ŋɔɔne ta-balɔrɔ o pa Wɛ Sin-laao kom, Wɛ bá sɛ se o ma chɛ konto tu. 32Nɔɔno wolo nam ná ŋɔɔne wo-balwaaro o pa Nabiin-bu wom, Wɛ wó sɛ se o ma chɛ konto tu. Nɔɔno wolo nam ná pɛ se Wɛ Sin-laao kom dam ye setaane nyem, Wɛ bá sɛ se o ma chɛ konto tu maŋa de maŋa se ko taa vei wuu.
33Abam ná sɛ we amo kikia yam lana, á jege se á sɛ we amo dam dem nwoŋi Wɛ Sin-laao kom tei ne mo. Ko nye de tei-ŋoŋo na jege se ko taa leiri bu-ŋona tei to mo. Tei-jawona nam wó taa leiri bu-chechɔgero mo. Abam ná lage se á lɔre tio ná ye tei-ŋoŋo, á wó ma ko bia mo á lɔre.
34Abam nye de basankwe mo. Á na ye nɔn-balwaaro to, á bá wane wo-laaro á ŋɔɔne. Nɔɔno na jege kolo maama o boboŋa ne to mo wó siiri o ni taane wone. 35Nɔn-ŋom wó taa jege wo-laaro mo o boboŋa ne pa se o jege-te o ŋɔɔna. Ko daare nɔn-balɔrɔ wó taa jege wo-balwaaro mo o boboŋa ne pa se o jege tento o ŋɔɔna. 36Ta‑á yei-na we, Wɛ borem dɛ dem ne nɔɔno maama jege se o ta o ni mo o jwoŋi o tete de wo-yɔɔro telo maama o na tage to mo. 37Ko wó taa ye abam tete ni taane mo wó bere we á jege bora naa á ba jega.”
Balo na ve Wɛ chega kam to wó na bora na?
Maake 8:11-12; Luka 11:29-32; 11:24-26
38Wɛ nia zamesem tiina badwonna de Farisi tiina badwonna déem ma zaŋe ba ta de Yezu ba we, “Berem tu, debam lage se n ke wo-kenkagele mo se ko taa ye maana ko pa debam.” 39O ma leiri-ba o we, “Zem nɔɔna ye wo-lwan-keira mo ye ba yiga tera de Wɛ. Mo kokuri ba lage se a ke wo-kenkagele a bere-ba. Ba maa bá na, ko ná dae wo-kenkagele delo na maŋe de ke Wɛ sampwora Jonah baŋa ne faŋa faŋa to. 40Wonto déem ke da yatɔ wea de tete maama mo ywon-kamunu kana ne. Ko nam jege se ko ke amo Nabiin-bu konto dwoŋi mo, de amo na wó ke da yatɔ wea de tete maama tega kuri ne to. 41Jonah déem na vei Ninevɛ tiina tei o bere-ba Wɛ chega kam to, banto leiri ba wo. Wolo na dwoi Jonah to nam wora abam tei ne ye á wo sɛ konto tu. Mo kokuri Wɛ borem dɛ dem ná yia, Ninevɛ tiina laam wó zaŋe ba bere we abam ba jege chega. 42Ko woli da, ka-pɛ wolo déem na tei Sebaa faŋa faŋa to de wó zaŋe o bere konto. Wonto déem zaŋe o tete teo kolo na tiini ko ye yiga yiga to ne o ba Pɛ Solomon tei se o cheigi o swa yam na ye tei to. Wolo nam na dwoi Solomon to wora abam tei ne ye á yiga tera ded‑o.
43Ba ná zeili setaane se o yage nɔɔno, o laam wó vo o beeri laŋa tetare ne mo na na tera mɛ to se o lage jei o sii da. O ma beeri o ga. 44O laam maa we, ‘A jege se a jwoori a vo a na nwoŋi mɛ to mo a taa wora.’ O ma jwoori o vo nɔɔno wom tei, ye o lɔre we o jei sem fɔge se kwɛ lanyerane ye kolokolo wo leiri ko zo da. 45O laam ma jwoori o vo o lage o dwonna barepɛ balo na maŋe ba ye balwaaro ba dwoi o tete to. Ba ma tɔge ded‑o ba vo ba zoore da. Ko maama laam na kweeli tei to ye lɛɛro mo wó taa jege nɔɔno wom konto se ko dwoni o boboa kam na maŋe ka ye tei to. Konto dwoŋi mo lage ko ke zem nɔn-balwaaro tem.”
Yezu nu de o nyaana na ye balo to
Maake 3:31-35; Luka 8:19-21
46Yezu déem ta na wora o ŋɔɔne de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom konto to, o nu de o nyaana ma ba ba zege sɔŋɔ kom pwooni ne, ye ba lage se ba ŋɔɔne ded‑o. 47Nɔɔno wodwoŋi ma ta de Yezu o we, “N nu de n nyaana tua, ye ba lage se ba na nmo.” 48Yezu ma ta de nɔɔno wom o we, “Banto yerane mo ye a nu de a nyaana na?” 49O laam ma nii o kwaga tɔgena bam seeni ye o we, “Amo nu de a nyaana mo tento. 50Kokuri wolo maama na ke a Kwo Wɛ boboŋa na lage tei to mo ye a nyaane, de a nakɔ, de a nu.”

english_text:
A Story about a Farmer
(Mark 4.1-9; Luke 8.4-8)
1That same day Jesus left the house and went out beside Lake Galilee, where he sat down to teach. 2 Such large crowds gathered around him that he had to sit in a boat, while the people stood on the shore. 3Then he taught them many things by using stories. He said:
A farmer went out to scatter seed in a field. 4While the farmer was scattering the seed, some of it fell along the road and was eaten by birds. 5Other seeds fell on thin, rocky ground and quickly started growing because the soil wasn't very deep. 6But when the sun came up, the plants were scorched and dried up, because they did not have deep roots. 7Some other seeds fell where thornbushes grew up and choked the plants. 8But a few seeds did fall on good ground where the plants produced 100 or 60 or 30 times as much as was scattered. 9If you have ears, pay attention!
Why Jesus Used Stories
(Mark 4.10-12; Luke 8.9,10)
10Jesus' disciples came to him and asked, “Why do you use stories to speak to the people?”
11Jesus answered:
I have explained the secrets about the kingdom of heaven to you, but not to others. 12 Everyone who has something will be given more. But people who don't have anything will lose even what little they have. 13I use stories when I speak to them because when they look, they cannot see, and when they listen, they cannot hear or understand. 14 So God's promise came true, just as the prophet Isaiah had said,
“These people will listen
and listen,
but never understand.
They will look and look,
but never see.
15All of them have
stubborn minds!
They refuse to listen;
they cover their eyes.
They cannot see or hear
or understand.
If they could,
they would turn to me,
and I would heal them.”
16 But God has blessed you, because your eyes can see and your ears can hear! 17Many prophets and good people were eager to see what you see and to hear what you hear. But I tell you they did not see or hear.
Jesus Explains the Story about the Farmer
(Mark 4.13-20; Luke 8.11-15)
18Now listen to the meaning of the story about the farmer:
19The seeds that fell along the road are the people who hear the message about the kingdom, but don't understand it. Then the evil one comes and snatches the message from their hearts. 20The seeds that fell on rocky ground are the people who gladly hear the message and accept it at once. 21But they don't have deep roots, and they don't last very long. As soon as life gets hard or the message gets them in trouble, they give up.
22The seeds that fell among the thornbushes are also people who hear the message. But they start worrying about the needs of this life and are fooled by the desire to get rich. So the message gets choked out, and they never produce anything. 23The seeds that fell on good ground are the people who hear and understand the message. They produce as much as 100 or 60 or 30 times what was planted.
Weeds among the Wheat
24Jesus then told them this story:
The kingdom of heaven is like what happened when a farmer scattered good seed in a field. 25But while everyone was sleeping, an enemy came and scattered weed seeds in the field and then left.
26When the plants came up and began to mature, the farmer's servants could see the weeds. 27The servants came and asked, “Sir, didn't you scatter good seed in your field? Where did these weeds come from?”
28“An enemy did this,” he replied.
His servants then asked, “Do you want us to go out and pull up the weeds?”
29“No!” he answered. “You might also pull up the wheat. 30Leave the weeds alone until harvest time. Then I'll tell my workers to gather the weeds and tie them up and burn them. But I'll order them to store the wheat in my barn.”
Stories about a Mustard Seed and Yeast
(Mark 4.30-32; Luke 13.18-21)
31Jesus told them another story:
The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when a farmer plants a mustard seed in a field. 32Although it is the smallest of all seeds, it grows larger than any garden plant and becomes a tree. Birds even come and nest on its branches.
33Jesus also said:
The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when a woman mixes a little yeast into three big batches of flour. Finally, all the dough rises.
The Reason for Teaching with Stories
(Mark 4.33,34)
34Jesus used stories when he spoke to the people. In fact, he did not tell them anything without using stories. 35 So God's promise came true, just as the prophet had said,
“I will use stories
to speak my message
and to explain things hidden
since the creation
of the world.”
Jesus Explains the Story about the Weeds
36After Jesus left the crowd and went inside, his disciples came to him and said, “Explain to us the story about the weeds in the wheat field.”
37Jesus answered:
The one who scattered the good seed is the Son of Man. 38The field is the world, and the good seeds are the people who belong to the kingdom. The weeds are those who belong to the evil one, 39and the one who scattered them is the devil. The harvest is the end of time, and angels are the ones who bring in the harvest.
40Weeds are gathered and burned. That's how it will be at the end of time. 41The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather from his kingdom everyone who does wrong or causes others to sin. 42Then he will throw them into a flaming furnace, where people will cry and grit their teeth in pain. 43 But everyone who has done right will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom. If you have ears, pay attention!
A Hidden Treasure
44The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when someone finds a treasure hidden in a field and buries it again. Such a person is happy and goes and sells everything in order to buy that field.
A Valuable Pearl
45The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when a shop owner is looking for fine pearls. 46After finding a very valuable one, the owner goes and sells everything in order to buy that pearl.
A Fish Net
47The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when a net is thrown into a lake and catches all kinds of fish. 48When the net is full, it is dragged to the shore, and the fishermen sit down to separate the fish. They keep the good ones, but throw the bad ones away. 49That's how it will be at the end of time. Angels will come and separate the evil people from the ones who have done right. 50Then those evil people will be thrown into a flaming furnace, where they will cry and grit their teeth in pain.
New and Old Treasures
51Jesus asked his disciples if they understood all these things. They said, “Yes, we do.”
52So he told them, “Every student of the Scriptures who becomes a disciple in the kingdom of heaven is like someone who brings out new and old treasures from the storeroom.”
The People of Nazareth Turn against Jesus
(Mark 6.1-6; Luke 4.16-30)
53When Jesus had finished telling these stories, he left 54and went to his hometown. He taught in their synagogue, and the people were so amazed that they asked, “Where does he get all this wisdom and the power to work these miracles? 55Isn't he the son of the carpenter? Isn't Mary his mother, and aren't James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas his brothers? 56Don't his sisters still live here in our town? How can he do all this?” 57 So the people were upset because of what he was doing.
But Jesus said, “Prophets are honored by everyone, except the people of their hometown and their own family.” 58And because the people did not have any faith, Jesus did not work many miracles there.
translation_text:
Yezu maŋe memaŋa o bere nɔɔna
Maake 4:1-20; Luka 8:4-15; 10:23-24
1Dɛ dem konto ne nɔɔ Yezu déem ma yage sɔŋɔ kom o vo naneo kom ni. O ma jeini tega ne se o bere nɔɔna. 2O na wora konto to, nɔn-kɔgɔ ma ba ko gilimi‑o. Konto ma pa se o zaŋe o vo o zo nabworo wo o jei da, ye kɔgɔ kom laam zege na bam ni ne se ba taa cheigi‑o. 3O maa mae memaŋa o bere-ba wonnu dedɛ. O déem ma maŋe o we:
“Valo déem mo wora. O ma zaŋe o vo o kara se o du. 4O ma kare o dole o wo-dwa yam. Yadwonna ma to chwoŋa ni ne. Zuna ma ba ba twɛ-ya ba di. 5Yadwonna ma to kandwa yuu ne mɛ teero na ba daga to. Teero na ba lira jei sem ne to, ya maa wo dáane ya puli. 6Wea ma ba ka baane ya maama. Ya bonno na wo zo tega to, ya ma te lela. 7Ko daare wo-dwa yadwonna ma to sabare wone. Ya na puli to, sabare sem laam ma zaŋe se che ya jira. 8Ko daare yadwonna ma to te-ŋoŋa baŋa ne, ye yanto maama nwoŋi ya ke bia lanyerane. Yadaara ke nenɛɛne bia bi bi. Yadaara ke nenɛɛne bia fuseredo fuseredo. Yadaara de maa jege nenɛɛne bia fintɔ fintɔ.
9Á nam fɔge á cheigi a taane dem lanyerane.”
10Yezu na maŋe memaŋe dem konto o ti to, o kwaga tɔgena bam laam ma vo ba yi o tei, ye ba bwei‑o ba we, “Bɛ mo ye n yeini n maŋe memaŋa n bere nɔɔna bam?” 11O ma leiri-ba o we, “Ko ná ye abam, Wɛ maŋe o pa se á lɔre o telaao paare dem kuri na ye tei to, ye chega kam konto ya maŋe ka seigi mo. Ko daare nɔɔna badaara bam, Wɛ wo pɛ-ba chwoŋa se ba lɔre o chega kam konto. 12Memaŋa yam na jege se ya zeini nɔɔna boboŋa tei to nye de nɔɔno ná maŋe o jege woŋo, o ta wó jwoŋi kodwoŋi o woli da se ko tiini ko gaale. Nɔɔno wolo nam na maŋe o ba jege kolokolo to laam wó ba o ga kolo fenfee o ya na jege to mo. 13Amo na maŋe memaŋa a bere-ba kolo ŋwaane to mo ye banto yia mo nae amo na ke wonnu telo to, ye te ba pae ba maana. Ba ta maa ni amo berem dem, ye ba ba lɔre de kuri. 14Banto na ye tei to mo bere we Wɛ sampwora Izaya na tage kolo faŋa faŋa to tu ko ji chega, de o na we:
‘Abam wó fɔge á ta‑á cheigi Wɛ taane dem,
ye á bá ni de kuri.
Abam yia nam wó kwaane ya nii
ye á na nɛ kolo to bá zo á yuu.
15Kokuri nɔɔna bam konto boboŋa seene ya te mo.
Ba zwa de ma kwareme,
ye ba daare ba pu ba yia.
Ko ná dae konto, ba yia na nɛ kolo to
jege se ko zo ba yuu mo.
Ba zwa de ya jege se ya ni Wɛ taane dem,
ye ba boboŋa de wó lɔre de kuri.
Ba ya ná ke konto,
ba ya wó pipiri ba sɛ amo Wɛ
se a pa ba na fɔgem.’ ”
16Yezu ta ma ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam o we, “Ko nam ná ye abam, á yia na nae tei to ye á zwa de ni tei to mo pae se á jege yu-ywoŋo Wɛ tei ne. 17Chega ŋwaane to, faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem dedɛ de nɔn-laaro dedɛ déem jege teena se ba na kolo abam na nɛ to, ye ba wo wane ba na. Ba ta maa kwori ba jege teena se ba ni Wɛ taane delo abam na nigi to, ye ba wo nɛ chwoŋa se ba ni-de.
18Nam cheigi-na se a maŋe valo wom memaŋe dem kuri a bere abam. 19Wo-dwa yalo na to chwoŋa kam ni ne to mo bere nɔɔna badwonna na ye tei to. Banto mo nigi Wɛ paare dem taane, ye ba wo lɔre de kuri. Wo-lwanno tu setaane laam ma ba o chaale-de pa de wo zo ba boboŋa. 20Wo-dwa yalo na to kandwa yuu ne to de maa bere nɔɔna badwonna na ye tei to. Banto yeini ba ni Wɛ taane dem ye ba jwoŋi-de lela de wopwolo. 21Taane dem maa wo tiini de zo ba boboŋa, pa se ba yage-de lela. Yaara na tu ya bɛɛse-ba Wɛ chega kam ŋwaane to, ba ma yage-ka lela. 22Wo-dwa yalo na to sabare sem wone to maa bere nɔɔna badwonna de na ye tei to. Banto ye balo na nigi Wɛ taane dem ye ba ta jege lwia de logo baŋa wonnu to. Sabu-laga ma chɔge ba boboŋa pa se ba kwei Wɛ taane dem ba yage, ye de wo jaane kuri de pa-ba. 23Ko daare wo-dwa yalo na to te-ŋoŋa jei sem ne to maa bere balo na nigi Wɛ taane dem ye ba pa de tiini de zo ba boboŋa to. Konto ma pa se Wɛ taane dem ja kuri de pa-ba, nenɛɛne mena na ke bia lanyerane se ko maŋe de bia bi bi, ye yadaara de ke bia fuseredo fuseredo, ye yadaara de ke bia fintɔ fintɔ to.”
Men-ŋona de men-kayale memaŋe
24Yezu déem ma maŋe memaŋe dedwoŋi o bere-ba o we, “Amo lage a bere abam Wɛ telaao paare dem na wó ba de taa wo nɔɔna baŋa ne tei to mo. Valo wodwoŋi mo kwei men-ŋona o ja vo o kara o du. 25O na dugi-ya konto to, o dono ma zaŋe pein-dɔa maŋa ne o ja kayale bia o vo o du o gwaane valo wom kara men-ŋona yam wone, ye o daare o jwoori sɔŋɔ. 26Men-ŋona yam ma nwoŋi ya ji men-kweero. O dono wom na dugi yalo to ma nwoŋi ya ji men-kayale. 27Sɔŋɔ tu wom tontoŋena laam ma vo ba ta ded‑o ba we, ‘Debam tu, nmo na dugi n kara kam to, ko dae men-ŋona yerane mo n dugi na? Bɛ mo ye kayale laam zaŋe se gwaane da?’ 28O ma leiri-ba o we, ‘Ko ye amo dono mo ke konto.’ Ba laam ma bwei‑o ba we, ‘Dé nam véi dé gɔ kayale sem dé yage na?’ 29O maa wo sɛ, ye o ta de-ba o we, ‘Abam ná ke konto, á wó kɛ á gɔ men-ŋona yam de mo á woli da. 30Nam yage-na se ya maama taa wora se ko ba ko yi zagem maŋa. Kanto maŋa kam ne amo laam wó ta de men-zagena bam se ba pɔɔre kayale sem ba gɔ ba tiŋi dáa ne, se ba laam pɛ ba zwɛ. Ba ná ke konto, se ba daare ba zage mena yam ba pɛ ba ke amo tuli ne.’ ”
Tio-bu-memeeno memaŋe
Maake 4:30-32; Luka 13:18-19
31Yezu daa ta ma maŋe memaŋe dedwoŋi o bere-ba o we, “Wɛ telaao paare dem nye de nɔɔno na kwei tio-bu-memeeno o vo o du o kara ne tei to mo. 32Tio-bu wom konto mo tiini o muri wo-bia maama wone. O ma nwoŋi, ye o ba o tiini o ji kamunu se ko dwoni dwo-vɔɔro telo maama na wo o kara kam ne to. Ko laam maa ye kamunu dedɛ ye zuna tui ba sɔ ba pworu ko yuu ne.”
Bworobworo sabɔle memaŋe
Luka 13:20-21
33Yezu daa ta ma maŋe memaŋe dedwoŋi o bere-ba o we, “Wɛ telaao paare dem nye de kaane wodwoŋi na kwei sabɔle fenfee o gwaane de bworobworo mun-fɔrɔ tei to mo. De laam ma pa se bworobworo muni dem maama fole.”
34Wonnu tem konto maama Yezu déem na bere nɔn-kɔgɔ kom to ye memaŋa yerane mo o ma o bere-ba. O wo tage kolokolo de-ba ye ko dae memaŋe. 35O nam ke konto se ko pa Wɛ sampwora kadwoŋi taane mo ji chega, de o na we,
“Amo wó puri a ni
a ŋɔɔne botare-dende mo a bere-ba.
Amo wó pa ba lɔre wonnu telo na seigi
ko zege logo baŋa boboa ne ko ba ko yi zem to.”
Men-kayale memaŋe dem kuri na ye tei to
36Yezu déem ma zaŋe o yage nɔn-kɔgɔ kom, ye o daare o jwoori sɔŋɔ kom. O kwaga tɔgena bam ma ba o tei ye ba we, “Ko ná ye men-kayale memaŋe dem, se n ta de kuri n bere debam.” 37O ma leiri-ba o we, “Sɔŋɔ tu wolo na dugi men-ŋona yam to mo bere Nabiin-bu wom na ke tei to. 38O kara kam maa nye de logo baŋa. Men-ŋona yam maa nye de Wɛ paare dem nɔɔna bam. Ko daare men-kayale sem maa nye de balo na ye wo-lwanno tu setaane nyem to, 39ye dono wolo na dugi-se to maa nye de setaana pɛ wom tete. Zagem maŋa kam mo bere logo baŋa na wó ba ko kweeli tei to. Men-zagena bam maa nye de Wɛ malese sem. 40Men-zagena bam na gɔge men-kayale sem ba pɛ ba zwɛ to, konto dwoŋi mo wó ke logo baŋa kweelim maŋa kam ne. 41Amo Nabiin-bu wom wó toŋe a malese sem se ba vo ba le kolo maama na pae se tusim wora to, de balo na ye wo-lwan-keira to, se ba daa yé taa tɔge ba wora Wɛ paare dem wone. 42Ba laam maa wó zeili-ba ba yage min-lɔŋɔ jei ne se de di-ba. Dáane mo ba laam wó taa wora ba keera ye ba done ba nwa. 43Ko daare balo na jege chega Wɛ tei ne to laam wó pa pwooni tiini de taa wora ba Kwo Wɛ paare dem wone, ne wea na nye tei to.
Á nam fɔge á cheigi amo taane dem lanyerane.
Wo-ŋonno telo na suli tega ne to memaŋe
44Wɛ telaao paare dem daa ta nye de wo-ŋonno telo na ye lonne nyem ye te suli tega ne to mo. Nɔɔno wodwoŋi laam ma pɔpɔ o na-te. O ma jwoori o kwoli-te. O wo na tiini ko pwoli to, o ma vo o kwei o wonnu maama o yeigi sabu, ye o laam daare o yeigi tega kam konto se wo-ŋonno tem maama ji o nyem.
Kandwɛ-ŋone memaŋe
45Wɛ telaao paare dem daa ta maa nye de pipim-piinu na kare o lage kandwa-nyenno se o yeigi to mo. 46O ma ba o na kandwɛ delo na tiini de jege lam o tei ne to. O laam ma jwoori o vo o kwei o wonnu maama o yeigi, ye o daare o yeigi kandwɛ dem konto yerane se de taa ye o nyem.
Ywon-jara de ba chwogo memaŋe
47Wɛ telaao paare dem na wó ba de taa wo nɔɔna baŋa ne tei to nye de chwogo ywon-jara na kwei ba de buga ne se ba ma ja ywona to mo. Ba na de-ko da to, ba ma ja ywona dwi maama. 48Chwogo kom ma ba ko su lanyerane. Nɔɔna bam laam ma vaŋe-ko ba tuuri ba ja bɛ. Ba laam ma jeini tega ne se ba kuri ywon-ŋona yam ba ke ba lɔɔro wone. Ba ma daare ba kwei ywon-yɔɔro tem ba dole ba yage. 49Ko nam wó ba ko taa ye konto mo logo baŋa kweelim maŋa kam ne. Wɛ malese wó nwoŋi se ba se se pɔɔre nɔn-balwaaro ye se le-ba balo na jege chega Wɛ tei ne to wone. 50Se laam wó daare se zeili-ba se yage min-lɔŋɔ jei ne se de di-ba. Dáane mo ba laam wó taa wora ba keera ye ba done ba nwa.”
Yezu berem dem ye berem-doore
51Yezu na ŋɔɔne o ti to, o laam ma bwei o kwaga tɔgena bam o we, ba nigi wonnu tem maama kuri na? Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, ɛɛ. 52O ma ta de-ba o we, “Tɔ. Wɛ nia yam zamesem tu wolo maama laam na tu o zamese Wɛ telaao paare dem chega kam to nye de sɔŋɔ tu wolo na nii Wɛ nɔɔna baŋa ne ye o le wo-laaro o jejegero tem wone o pa-ba to. Konto tu laam wae o le berem-doore o woli de berem-dwoori dem se o ma o bere o nɔɔna bam.”
Yezu tete teo kom tiina na ve‑o tei to
Maake 6:1-6; Luka 4:16-30
53Yezu déem na maŋe memaŋa yam konto o ti to, o laam ma yage jei sem konto. 54O ma jwoori o vo o tete teo. O na wora to, o ma zo Juu tiina jeerim diga kam se o bere-ba. O na bere-ba tei to, ko déem so-ba lanyerane, pa ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto ke tɛ mo o jege swa yam konto dwoŋi? O nam ke tɛ mo o na dam pa o ma o ke wo-kenkagela yanto dwoŋi? 55Wonto mo dae gɔgɔ kom bu wom na? O nu maa ye Mary. O nyaana maa ye Jemsi, de Josef, de Simon, de Judas. 56O nakɔa maama de ta wora debam tei ne mo. Wonto nam nɛ dam dem konto maama yei ne mo?”
57Konto mo ba boboŋa déem chɔge o ŋwaane. Yezu ma ta de-ba o we, “Nɔɔno ná ye Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu, nɔɔna yeini ba pa‑o zula lanyerane, ko daare o tete teo tiina de o sɔŋɔ tiina nam bá nege‑o.” 58Ba déem na wo ke ba wo-dedoa se ba sɛ‑o to, o maa wo tiini o ke wo-kenkagela dedɛ ba tei ne.

english_text:
The Death of John the Baptist
(Mark 6.14-29; Luke 9.7-9)
1About this time Herod the ruler heard the news about Jesus 2and told his officials, “This is John the Baptist! He has come back from death, and that's why he has the power to work these miracles.”
3-4 Herod had earlier arrested John and had him chained and put in prison. He did this because John had told him, “It isn't right for you to take Herodias, the wife of your brother Philip.” 5Herod wanted to kill John. But the people thought John was a prophet, and Herod was afraid of what they might do.
6When Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced for the guests. She pleased Herod 7so much he swore to give her whatever she wanted. 8But the girl's mother told her to say, “Here on a serving plate I want the head of John the Baptist!”
9Herod was sorry for what he had said. But he did not want to break the promise he had made in front of his guests. So he ordered a guard 10to go to the prison and cut off John's head. 11It was taken on a serving plate to the girl, and she gave it to her mother. 12John's followers took his body and buried it. Then they told Jesus what had happened.
Jesus Feeds Five Thousand
(Mark 6.30-44; Luke 9.10-17; John 6.1-14)
13After Jesus heard about John, he crossed Lake Galilee to go to some place where he could be alone. But the crowds found out and followed him on foot from the towns. 14When Jesus got out of the boat, he saw the large crowd. He felt sorry for them and healed everyone who was sick.
15That evening the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This place is like a desert, and it's already late. Let the crowds leave, so they can go to the villages and buy some food.”
16Jesus replied, “They don't have to leave. Why don't you give them something to eat?”
17But they said, “We have only five small loaves of bread and two fish.” 18Jesus asked his disciples to bring the food to him, 19and he told the crowd to sit down on the grass. Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish. He looked up toward heaven and blessed the food. Then he broke the bread and handed it to his disciples, and they gave it to the people.
20After everyone had eaten all they wanted, Jesus' disciples picked up twelve large baskets of leftovers.
21There were about 5,000 men who ate, not counting the women and children.
Jesus Walks on the Water
(Mark 6.45-52; John 6.15-21)
22At once, Jesus made his disciples get into a boat and start back across the lake. But he stayed until he had sent the crowds away. 23Then he went up on a mountain where he could be alone and pray. Later in the evening, he was still there.
24By this time the boat was a long way from the shore. It was going against the wind and was being tossed around by the waves. 25A little while before morning, Jesus came walking on the water toward his disciples. 26When they saw him, they thought he was a ghost. They were terrified and started screaming.
27At once, Jesus said to them, “Don't worry! I am Jesus. Don't be afraid.”
28Peter replied, “Lord, if it really is you, tell me to come to you on the water.”
29“Come on!” Jesus said. Peter then got out of the boat and started walking on the water toward him.
30But when Peter saw how strong the wind was, he was afraid and started sinking. “Save me, Lord!” he shouted.
31At once, Jesus reached out his hand. He helped Peter up and said, “You surely don't have much faith. Why do you doubt?”
32When Jesus and Peter got into the boat, the wind died down. 33The men in the boat worshiped Jesus and said, “You really are the Son of God!”
Jesus Heals Sick People in Gennesaret
(Mark 6.53-56)
34Jesus and his disciples crossed the lake and came to shore near the town of Gennesaret. 35The people found out he was there, and they sent word to everyone who lived in this part of the country. So they brought all the sick people to Jesus. 36They begged him just to let them touch his clothes, and everyone who did was healed.
translation_text:
Pɛ Herodi na go Jɔn tei to
Maake 6:14-29; Luka 9:7-9
