1The Sabbath was over, and it was almost daybreak on Sunday when Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to see the tomb. 2Suddenly a strong earthquake struck, and the Lord's angel came down from heaven. He rolled away the stone and sat on it. 3The angel looked as bright as lightning, and his clothes were white as snow. 4The guards shook from fear and fell down, as though they were dead.
5The angel said to the women, “Don't be afraid! I know you are looking for Jesus, who was nailed to a cross. 6He isn't here! God has raised him to life, just as Jesus said he would. Come, see the place where his body was lying. 7Now hurry! Tell his disciples he has been raised to life and is on his way to Galilee. Go there, and you will see him. This is what I came to tell you.”
8The women were frightened and yet very happy, as they hurried from the tomb and ran to tell his disciples. 9Suddenly Jesus met them and greeted them. They went near him, held on to his feet, and worshiped him. 10Then Jesus said, “Don't be afraid! Tell my followers to go to Galilee. They will see me there.”
Report of the Guard
11While the women were on their way, some soldiers who had been guarding the tomb went into the city. They told the chief priests everything that had happened. 12So the chief priests met with the leaders and decided to bribe the soldiers with a lot of money. 13They said to the soldiers, “Tell everyone that Jesus' disciples came during the night and stole his body while you were asleep. 14If the governor hears about this, we will talk to him. You won't have anything to worry about.” 15The soldiers took the money and did what they were told. The people of Judea still tell each other this story.
What Jesus' Followers Must Do
(Mark 16.14-18; Luke 24.36-49; John 20.19-23; Acts 1.6-8)
16 Jesus' eleven disciples went to a mountain in Galilee, where Jesus had told them to meet him. 17They saw him and worshiped him, but some of them doubted.
18Jesus came to them and said:
I have been given all authority in heaven and on earth! 19 Go to the people of all nations and make them my disciples. Baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, 20and teach them to do everything I have told you. I will be with you always, even until the end of the world.
translation_text:
Yezu bi toone wone
Maake 16:1-8; Luka 24:1-12; Jɔn 20:1-10
1Ba siu dɛ dem na kɛ to, te-pora ni ne mo Mary Magadala de Mary wodwoŋi wom zaŋe ba vo yibeeli dem ne se ba nii. 2Tega ma pɔpɔ ka ziziŋi dedɛ. Baŋa Wɛ maleka ma nwoŋi telaao ne ka ba ka bibili kandwɛ-kamunu kom ka yage dáa ne, ye ka daare ka jeini ko baŋa ne. 3Ka yibia maa tiini ya pepela, ye ka gwaaro tem de tiini te peere cha. 4Nɔɔna balo na wora ba yere yibeeli dem to ma beiri de foone nenɛɛne ba tege tei.
5Maleka kam laam ma ta de kaana bam ka we, “Yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. A lɔre we abam lage se á na Yezu wolo ba na jaane ba pa dagara kam yuu ne ba go to mo. 6O nam tere ywo. Ko seene ko ke nenɛɛne o na wuuri o ta kolo we, Wɛ wó bi‑o to mo. Nam ba-na á nii o yera yam ya na tigi mɛ. 7Abam nam ke lela á vo á ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam we, Wɛ seene o bi‑o toone wone, ye o laam wó tɔge yiga o vo Galili se á vo á na‑o dáane. Mo kolo a na lage a ta a bere abam to.”
8Maleka kam na tage konto to, kaana bam ma ke lela ba yage yibeeli dem ye ba kɛ de foone delo na jege-ba ye ba ta jege ywoni dedɛ to. Ba ma duri ba vo se ba ta de Yezu kwaga tɔgena bam kolo na ke to.
9Ba na maa kɛ to, Yezu ma pɔpɔ o jeeri-ba, ye o ke ba lei. Ba ma vo ba yi o tei ba kuni dwoona ba ja o nɛ ye ba zuli‑o. 10Yezu ma ta de-ba o we, “Yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. Véi-na amo nu-bia bam tei se á ta de-ba we, ba zaŋe ba vo Galili, se dáane mo ba wó na amo.”
11Kaana bam na yage yibeeli dem jei sem konto to, soja tiina balo na wora ba nii-de to badaara ma zaŋe ba jwoori teo kom wo, ye ba ta kolo maama na ke to ba bere Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam. 12Kaanem yiga tiina bam laam ma vo ba ŋɔɔne de teo kom nakwa bam. Ba ma ke ni daane se ba kwei sabu-fɔrɔ ba pa soja tiina bam, 13ye ba we, “Abam jege se á ta we, Yezu kwaga tɔgena bam mo tu tete ne ba ŋɔ‑o ba ja viiri, de abam ta tigi á dɔa. 14Gɔmena tu wom nam ná tu o lɔre ko ni ne ye ko ke taane, debam wó ŋɔɔne dé jwoŋi abam dé yage se lwia yé taa wora á baŋa ne.”
15Soja tiina bam ma jwoŋi sabu kom ye ba seene ba ke kolo ba na tage-ba se ba ke to. Mo konto mo Juu tiina bam jege ba tɛa de zem maama.
Yezu na ŋɔɔne kolo de o kwaga tɔgena o kweeli to
Maake 16:14-18; Luka 24:36-49; Jɔn 20:19-23; Kikia 1:6-8
16Yezu tɔgena fuga-dedoa bam laam ma zaŋe ba vo Galili peo kolo seeni o na maŋe o ta-ba se ba vo to. 17Ba ma seene ba vo ba na‑o, ye ba kuni dwoona ba zuli‑o. Badaara maa jege boboŋa yalei ded‑o. 18Yezu laam ma fɔɔre o yi ba tei, ye o ta de-ba o we, “Wɛ laam pɛ-ne dam se a taa tei telaao de tega baŋa maama. 19Konto ŋwaane nam véi-na logo baŋa dwi maama tei, se á pa ba ji amo tɔgena, se á daare á pa ba jwoŋi sɛɛm amo Kwo Wɛ yere ŋwaane, ko woli de o Bu wom de o Sin-laao kom yere ŋwaane. 20Ta‑á bere-ba se ba sɛ ba tɔge kolo maama amo na pɛ abam ni se á ke to. Nam ta‑á yei-na we, amo wó taa wora abam tei ne maŋa maama, se ko vo ko yi logo baŋa kweelim maŋa kam.”

english_text:
The Preaching of John the Baptist
(Matthew 3.1-12; Luke 3.1-18; John 1.19-28)
1This is the good news about Jesus Christ, the Son of God. 2 It began just as God had said in the book written by Isaiah the prophet,
“I am sending my messenger
to get the way ready
for you.
3 In the desert
someone is shouting,
‘Get the road ready
for the Lord!
Make a straight path
for him.’ ”
4So John the Baptist showed up in the desert and told everyone, “Turn back to God and be baptized! Then your sins will be forgiven.”
5From all Judea and Jerusalem crowds of people went to John. They told how sorry they were for their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River.
6 John wore clothes made of camel's hair. He had a leather strap around his waist and ate grasshoppers and wild honey.
7John also told the people, “Someone more powerful is going to come. And I am not good enough even to stoop down and untie his sandals. 8I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit!”
The Baptism of Jesus
(Matthew 3.13-17; Luke 3.21,22)
9About that time Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee, and John baptized him in the Jordan River. 10As soon as Jesus came out of the water, he saw the sky open and the Holy Spirit coming down to him like a dove. 11 A voice from heaven said, “You are my own dear Son, and I am pleased with you.”
Jesus and Satan
(Matthew 4.1-11; Luke 4.1-13)
12At once God's Spirit made Jesus go into the desert. 13He stayed there for 40 days while Satan tested him. Jesus was with the wild animals, but angels took care of him.
Jesus Begins His Work
(Matthew 4.12-17; Luke 4.14,15)
14After John was arrested, Jesus went to Galilee and told the good news that comes from God. 15 He said, “The time has come! God's kingdom will soon be here. Turn back to God and believe the good news!”
Jesus Chooses Four Fishermen
(Matthew 4.18-22; Luke 5.1-11)
16As Jesus was walking along the shore of Lake Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew. They were fishermen and were casting their nets into the lake. 17Jesus said to them, “Follow me! I will teach you how to bring in people instead of fish.” 18Right then the two brothers dropped their nets and went with him.
19Jesus walked on and soon saw James and John, the sons of Zebedee. They were in a boat, mending their nets. 20At once Jesus asked them to come with him. They left their father in the boat with the hired workers and went with him.
A Man with an Evil Spirit
(Luke 4.31-37)
21Jesus and his disciples went to the town of Capernaum. Then on the next Sabbath he went into the synagogue and started teaching. 22 Everyone was amazed at his teaching. He taught with authority, and not like the teachers of the Law of Moses. 23Suddenly a man with an evil spirit in him entered the synagogue and yelled, 24“Jesus from Nazareth, what do you want with us? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are! You are God's Holy One.”
25Jesus told the evil spirit, “Be quiet and come out of the man!” 26The spirit shook him. Then it gave a loud shout and left.
27Everyone was completely surprised and kept saying to each other, “What is this? It must be some new kind of powerful teaching! Even the evil spirits obey him.” 28News about Jesus quickly spread all over Galilee.
Jesus Heals Many People
(Matthew 8.14-17; Luke 4.38-41)
29As soon as Jesus left the synagogue with James and John, they went home with Simon and Andrew. 30When they got there, Jesus was told that Simon's mother-in-law was sick in bed with fever. 31Jesus went to her. He took hold of her hand and helped her up. The fever left her, and she served them a meal.
32That evening after sunset, all who were sick or had demons in them were brought to Jesus. 33In fact, the whole town gathered around the door of the house. 34Jesus healed all kinds of terrible diseases and forced out a lot of demons. But the demons knew who he was, and he did not let them speak.
35Very early the next morning before daylight, Jesus got up and went to a place where he could be alone and pray. 36Simon and the others started looking for him. 37And when they found him, they said, “Everyone is looking for you!”
38Jesus replied, “We must go to the nearby towns, so that I can tell the good news to those people. This is why I have come.” 39 Then Jesus went to their synagogues everywhere in Galilee, where he preached and forced out demons.
Jesus Heals a Man
(Matthew 8.1-4; Luke 5.12-16)
40A man with leprosy came to Jesus and knelt down. He begged, “You have the power to make me well, if only you wanted to.”
41Jesus felt sorry for the man. So he put his hand on him and said, “I want to! Now you are well.” 42At once the man's leprosy disappeared, and he was well.
43After Jesus strictly warned the man, he sent him on his way. 44 He said, “Don't tell anyone about this. Just go and show the priest that you are well. Then take a gift to the temple as Moses commanded, and everyone will know that you have been healed.”
45The man talked about it so much and told so many people, that Jesus could no longer go openly into a town. He had to stay away from the towns, but people still came to him from everywhere.
translation_text:
Jɔn pɛ nɔɔna sɛɛm ye o bere-ba
Matiyu 3:1-12; Luka 3:1-17; Jɔn 1:19-28
1Kwor-ywoŋa kalo na vei Wɛ Bu Yezu Krista seeni to mo tento. 2Ko na puli tei to tɔge Wɛ sampwora Izaya na maŋe o popone kolo faŋa faŋa ye o tɔɔle Wɛ kwora o we:
“Nii, amo Wɛ lage a toŋe a tontoŋeno mo,
se o da nmo yiga o vo o kwɛ
chwoŋa kalo nmo na wó tɔge da to.”
3“Nɔɔno mo wo kagoa yuu ne
o kaase o kwora ye o we,
‘Zaŋe-na á fɔge á kwɛ dé Teiru wom chwoŋa kam
o na lage o ba o tɔge da to.
Pa-na se chwei selo o na lage o tɔge to fɔge se yɔɔre lanyerane.’ ”
4Ko déem seene ko ke konto dwoŋi mo. Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Jɔn. O maa wo kagoa ne ye o pa nɔɔna sɛɛm Wɛ ŋwaane. O maa yeini o tɔɔle Wɛ kwora o bere nɔɔna we, ba jege se ba leiri ba wo Wɛ ŋwaane se ba daare ba jwoŋi sɛɛm, se Wɛ laam wó yage ba wɛleera o ma chɛ-ba. 5Nɔɔna dedɛ maa yeini ba nwoŋi Judea nawuura yam maama de Jerusalem ba vei o tei. Ba na tui o tei to, ba maa tɛ jaja ba na ke ba tusi tei to. O laam maa pae se ba zoore Jɔdan buga kam wone ye ba jwoŋi sɛɛm Wɛ ŋwaane.
6Jɔn déem maa zoore gɔrɔ kolo ba na sɔge de kone koro to mo. O maa mae tankila o ja o teiŋa. O wodiu mo ye kayere de tooro. 7O maa tɔɔle o bere nɔɔna o we, “Nɔɔno wodwoŋi wó saŋe amo kwaga o ba, ye wonto tiini o dwoi amo. Amo wo maŋe se a tiiri a le o nɛ natera a pa‑o. 8Amo ná yeini a pa abam sɛɛm, ko ye na mo a mae a ke. Wonto nam ná lage o pa abam jwoŋi sɛɛm, ko wó taa ye Wɛ Sin-laao kom mo o wó pa á jwoŋi.”
Yezu Krista jwoŋi sɛɛm
Matiyu 3:13–4:11; Luka 3:21-22; 4:1-13
9Maŋa kam konto ne, Yezu déem ma zaŋe Galili teo kodwoŋi ne, ko yere mo Nazarete. O ma vo o yi Jɔn tei. Jɔn ma pa o zo Jɔdan buga kam wo ye o daare o pa‑o sɛɛm. 10Yezu na maa nwoŋi na bam wone to, o ma na wɛyuu na pɔɔre belei, ye o na Wɛ Sin-laao kom na nwoŋi da ko maa beene o baŋa, ko na nye de kunkwoŋa tei. 11O ma ni Wɛ kwora na ŋɔɔne telaao ne ka we:
“Nmo mo ye amo bu-doa a na jege n swono to.
N kikia su amo yi.”
12Konto na ke bedwe baŋa ne to, Wɛ Sin-laao kom ma ja‑o ko zo kagoa yuu ne. 13O maa wo kagoa kam wone taa, da finna. O na wora to, setaana pɛ maa kwaane o maŋe‑o o nii. O maa zoore de kago-vara, ye Wɛ malese de tui o tei se zeini‑o.
Yezu bwoŋi nɔɔna bana se ba taa tɔge‑o
Matiyu 4:12-22; Luka 4:14-15; 5:1-11
14Ba déem ma ja Jɔn ba ke peena diga ne. Konto kwaga ne, Yezu ma jwoori o vo Galili. O maa wora o tɔɔle Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam o bere nɔɔna, 15ye o we, “Maŋa kam laam yia Wɛ paare dem na lage de ba o nɔɔna baŋa ne to. Konto ŋwaane, leiri-na á wo de á wɛleera yam se á daare á sɛ Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam.”
16Yezu déem maa wo Galili naneo kom ni ne o via. O ma na nɔɔna balei, ba na ye chorro to. Ba dedoa yere mo Simon. O nyaane yere mo Anduru. Ba ye ywon-jara mo. Ba maa wo na bam wone ba dole chworu se ba ja ywona. 17Yezu ma ta de-ba o we, “Zaŋe-na á ba á ta‑á tɔge amo. Amo wó pa se á ta‑á lage nɔɔna mo se ba ba ba da amo kwaga, se ko taa nye de á zem na jaane ywona tei to.” 18O na tage konto to, ba ma zaŋe lela ba yage ba chworu tem ye ba vo ba tɔge o kwaga.
19O ma vo yiga fee. O daa ma na nɔɔna balei. Ba dedoa yere mo Jemsi. O nyaane de maa wora, o yere mo Jɔn. Ba kwo yere mo Zebedi. Ba maa wo nabworo wone ba kwɛ ba chworu se ba ma ja ywona. 20O laam ma yɔɔre o bwoŋi-ba. O na bwoŋi-ba konto to, ba ma zaŋe ba yage ba kwo wom de o tontoŋena bam nabworo kom wone ye ba vo ba tɔge‑o.
Yezu zeili chichira nɔɔno tei ne
Matiyu 8:14-17; Luka 4:31-44
21Ba ma tɔge daane ba vo ba zo teo kodwoŋi wo, ko yere mo Kaparenia. Juu tiina siu dɛ dedoa na yi to, Yezu ma vo o zo ba jeerim diga kam se o bere-ba. 22O na bere-ba tei to, nɔɔna balo na wora to maa tiini ba ye yaau de o berem dem. Ko pɛ se ba lɔre we, o jege dam ko dwoi ba tete zamesem tiina bam.
23Nɔɔno déem maa wo ba jeerim diga kam ne ye chichira daane‑o. O ma zaŋe lela ye o kaase o we, 24“Yezu, Nazarete tu, bɛ mo n lage debam tei ne? Nmo tu se n chɔge debam dwi mo na? A yei nmo na ye wolo. Nmo ye Wo-pwoŋo Tu wolo Wɛ na toŋe to mo.” 25Yezu ma bwɛ chichira kam o we, “Cheigi sɔɔ, se n yage o yera se n viiri.” 26O na tage konto to, chichira kam ma tiini ka ja nɔɔno wom ka su ye ka kaase de kwor-dɛa. Ka laam ma yage nɔɔno wom yera ka daare‑o.
27Nɔɔna bam na nɛ konto to, ko ma so ba maama lanyerane ye ba bwei daane ba we, “Bɛ mo konto? O bere che-doŋa mo ye o berem dem jege dam chekke. Nii o na tɛ chichiri we se viiri, ye se sɛ o ni.”
28Nɔɔna balo maama na zoore Galili jei sem ne to déem ma ni Yezu ŋwa lela.
29Yezu de o nɔɔna bam ma nwoŋi jeerim diga kam ne ba kɛ. Ba tɔge de Jemsi de Jɔn ba vo ba yi Simon de Anduru ba sɔŋɔ. 30Simon tenkaane maa tigi tega ne ye paa jege‑o. Ba ma ta ba bere Yezu ko na ke‑o tei to. 31O ma vo kaane wom tei o ja o jeŋa pa se o zaŋe o jeini. Paa kam ma yage‑o. O ma zaŋe o ke wodiu o pa-ba.
32Wɛ na zo ye tega daare se ka yi to, nɔɔna maa jaane balo maama na ye jaweena to de setaana na daane balo maama to ba tui Yezu tei. 33Teo kom nɔɔna bam maama ma vo ba tigisi Simon ba sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo ni ne. 34Yezu ma yɔɔre nɔɔna dedɛ de ba jaweero dwi dwi, ye o daare o zeili setaana dedɛ nɔɔna tei ne. O maa wo sɛ se setaana yam ŋɔɔne kolokolo, ya na maŋe ya yei o na ye wolo to ŋwaane.
35Tega na poore tetete ye wɛ daa ta wo puli to, Yezu ma zaŋe o nwoŋi o vo jei selo nɔɔn-nɔɔno na tera to. O ma vo o ware Wɛ o yera ne. 36Simon de o yuudwonna bam laam ma zaŋe ba nwoŋi se ba lage o jei. 37Ba na nɛ‑o to, ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Nɔɔna bam maama beeri nmo jei.” 38Yezu ma leiri-ba o we, “Zaŋe-na se dé kɛ dé vo jei sedwonna. Amo jege se a vo te-balwa balo na wo ywoba seeni to se a tɔɔle Wɛ kwora kam. Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo a nwoŋi se a taa toŋa.”
39O laam ma beeri o tɔge Galili wo maama. O maa yeini o zoore Juu tiina jeerim di sem. O maa bere nɔɔna Wɛ chega kam ye o zeili setaana nɔɔna tei ne.
Yezu yɔɔre nayɔŋɔ
Matiyu 8:1-4; Luka 5:12-16
40Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o na ye nayɔŋɔ. O ma zaŋe o vo Yezu tei o kuni dwoona o yiga ne o lwoori‑o o we, “Nmo ná laga, n wó wane n pa se a na yazura.” 41O ŋwaŋa ma zo Yezu. Yezu de ma twe o jeŋa o dwei‑o, ye o we, “A lage konto. Zaŋe de yazura.” 42O na tage konto bedwe baŋa ne to mo jaweo kom yage nɔɔno wom ye o yera yam kwɛ fase.
43Yezu ma ta‑o se o viiri lela ye o daare o kaane‑o o we, 44“Yé zaŋe n ta kolo na ke to n bere nɔɔn-nɔɔno. Nam yɔɔre n vo Wɛ kaanem tu wom tei se n pa o nii n yera yam, se n daare n kwei wonnu telo Moses nia yam na bere we te maŋe to n ma n kaane Wɛ. Konto wó bere nɔɔna we n jaweo kom seene ko jei.” 45Yezu na tage konto to, nɔɔno wom ma nwoŋi o kare o ŋɔɔne kolo na ke to, pa se nɔɔna maama lɔre ko ni ne. Konto ŋwaane Yezu daa ware o zo teo de teo wo ye o wo seigi o tete. O ma lɛɛre o maŋe gaao wone nɔɔna na tera mɛ to. Nɔɔna maa yeini ba nwoŋa jei maama ba vei o tei.

english_text:
Jesus Heals a Man Who Could Not Walk
(Matthew 9.1-8; Luke 5.17-26)
1Jesus went back to Capernaum, and a few days later people heard that he was at home. 2Then so many of them came to the house that there wasn't even standing room left in front of the door.
Jesus was still teaching 3when four people came up, carrying a man on a mat because he could not walk. 4But because of the crowd, they could not get him to Jesus. So they made a hole in the roof above him and let the man down in front of everyone.
5When Jesus saw how much faith they had, he said to the man, “My friend, your sins are forgiven.”
6Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were sitting there. They started wondering, 7“Why would he say such a thing? He must think he is God! Only God can forgive sins.”
8At once, Jesus knew what they were thinking, and he said, “Why are you thinking such things? 9Is it easier for me to tell this man his sins are forgiven or to tell him to get up and pick up his mat and go on home? 10I will show you that the Son of Man has the right to forgive sins here on earth.” So Jesus said to the man, 11“Get up! Pick up your mat and go on home.”
12The man got right up. He picked up his mat and went out while everyone watched in amazement. They praised God and said, “We have never seen anything like this!”
Jesus Chooses Levi
(Matthew 9.9-13; Luke 5.27-32)
13Once again, Jesus went to the shore of Lake Galilee. A large crowd gathered around him, and he taught them. 14As he walked along, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus. Levi was sitting at the place for paying taxes, and Jesus said to him, “Follow me!” So he got up and went with Jesus.
15Later, Jesus and his disciples were having dinner at Levi's house. Many tax collectors and other sinners had become followers of Jesus, and they were also guests at the dinner.
16Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees, and they saw Jesus eating with sinners and tax collectors. So they asked his disciples, “Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
17Jesus heard them and answered, “Healthy people don't need a doctor, but sick people do. I didn't come to invite good people to be my followers. I came to invite sinners.”
People Ask about Going without Eating
(Matthew 9.14-17; Luke 5.33-39)
18The followers of John the Baptist and the Pharisees often went without eating. Some people came and asked Jesus, “Why do the followers of John and those of the Pharisees often go without eating, while your disciples never do?”
19Jesus answered:
The friends of a bridegroom don't go without eating while he is still with them. 20But the time will come when he will be taken from them. Then they will go without eating.
21No one patches old clothes by sewing on a piece of new cloth. The new piece would shrink and tear a bigger hole.
22No one pours new wine into old wineskins. The wine would swell and burst the old skins. Then the wine would be lost, and the skins would be ruined. New wine must be put into new wineskins.
A Question about the Sabbath
(Matthew 12.1-8; Luke 6.1-5)
23 One Sabbath Jesus and his disciples were walking through some wheat fields. His disciples were picking grains of wheat as they went along. 24Some Pharisees asked Jesus, “Why are your disciples picking grain on the Sabbath? They are not supposed to do that!”
25 Jesus answered, “Haven't you read what David did when he and his followers were hungry and in need? 26 It was during the time of Abiathar the high priest. David went into the house of God and ate the sacred loaves of bread that only priests are allowed to eat. He also gave some to his followers.”
27Jesus finished by saying, “People were not made for the good of the Sabbath. The Sabbath was made for the good of people. 28So the Son of Man is Lord over the Sabbath.”
translation_text:
Yezu jege dam se o saare nɔɔna wɛleera
Matiyu 9:1-8; Luka 5:17-26
1Da fenfee na kɛ to, Yezu ma jwoori o vo o zo Kaparenia. Teo kom nɔɔna bam ma lɔre we o tu sɔŋɔ. 2Ba dedɛ ma ba ba tigisi sɔŋɔ kom ne pa se pwola daa tera ko ni ne de fenfee de. O maa wora o tɛ Wɛ kwora kam o bere-ba. 3O na wora o bere-ba konto to mo nɔɔna bana ya zeŋe gɔrɔ ba jege ba beene o tei. 4Ba na yi jei sem to, ba ma ware ba ja‑o ba yi Yezu tei, kɔgɔ kom na daga to ŋwaane. Ba ma ja‑o ba di sɔŋɔ kom nayuu ye ba daare ba zage-ko ba puri bɔɔne ba maŋe de Yezu na wo mɛ to. Ba ma pa se gungwolo kolo gɔrɔ kom na tigi ka baŋa ne to tɔge da ka tu diga kam wo. 5Yezu ma lɔre we ba ke ba wo-dedoa ded‑o. O ma ta de gɔrɔ kom o we, “A bu, nmo wɛleera yam saare.”
6Wɛ nia zamesem tiina badaara ya wora. Ba maa jei ba bwɛ ba wone ba we, 7“Bɛ mo ye o na chwoŋa se o ŋɔɔne konto dwoŋi? O pae se o de Wɛ ye bedwe mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege chwoŋa se o yage nɔɔno wɛleera o ma chɛ‑o, ko ná dae Wɛ yerane.”
8Yezu ma lɔre ba na jege boboŋa yalo ba wone to. O ma ta de-ba o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo á boŋe konto dwoŋi? 9Kɔ mo ye mɔle, amo ná tage de gɔrɔ kom we o wɛleera yam saare, naa a ná tage ded‑o we o zaŋe wɛɛne o kwei o gungwolo kom o taa via? 10Amo nam wó pa se abam lɔre we amo wolo na ye Nabiin-bu wom to jege dam logo baŋa ne se a yage nɔɔno wɛleera a ma chɛ‑o.” O laam ma ta de gɔrɔ kom o we, 11“A tɛ nmo, zaŋe wɛɛne n kwei n gungwolo kom n ja n vo sɔŋɔ.” 12Yezu na tage konto to, nɔɔno wom ma seene o zaŋe ba maama yiga ne o kwei o gungwolo kom o nwoŋi o viiri. Ba na nɛ konto to, ko ma ke ba maama yaau. Ba ma tei Wɛ ye ba we, “Dé daa ta wo fɔge dé na keim dento dwoŋi.”
Yezu bwoŋi Levi se o taa tɔge‑o
Matiyu 9:9-13; Luka 5:27-32
13Yezu daa ma nwoŋi o vo o wo naneo ni ne. Kɔgɔ dedɛ ma ba o tei ko gilimi‑o. O maa wora o bere-ba Wɛ chega kam. 14O daa ma zaŋe o maa kɛa. O na maa vei to, o ma na nɔɔno wodwoŋi, o yere mo Levi. O kwo yere mo Alafayu. O déem jei mɛ seeni o na yeini o jwoŋi lampwoo nɔɔna tei ne to mo. Yezu ma ta ded‑o o we, “Zaŋe n ta‑n tɔge-ne.” O ma seene o zaŋe o tɔge o kwaga.
15Yezu déem ma vo Levi sɔŋɔ se o di wodiu. O de o kwaga tɔgena bam na wora to, lampwoo lara de nɔn-chechɔgero dedɛ maa tɔge ba wora ba di wodiu de-ba, kolo ŋwaane balo na tɔge‑o to daga. 16Wɛ nia zamesem tiina badaara na nwoŋi Farisi tiina kɔgɔ kom wone to maa tɔge ba wora. Ba na nɛ Yezu na jei o di wodiu de nɔn-chechɔgero de lampwoo lara konto to, ba ma bwei o kwaga tɔgena bam ba we, “Bɛ mo ke ye o di wodiu dedaane lampwoo lara de nɔn-chechɔgero tem konto?”
17Yezu ma ni ba na tage kolo to. O laam ma ta de-ba o we, “Ko ná ye balo na jege ya-dɛɛra to, banto ba jege se ba vo dɔkta tu tei se o yɔɔre-ba. Ko daare balo na ba jege yazura to mo jege se ba vo se ba na yɔɔrem. Amo na tu logo baŋa to, ko dae balo na maŋe ba ye nɔn-ŋona to ŋwaane, se a nam tu se a pa nɔn-chechɔgero mo tɔge chwoŋa.”
Yezu berem dem ye berem-doore
Matiyu 9:14-17; Luka 5:33-39
18Jɔn kwaga tɔgena bam de Farisi tiina bam déem yeini ba vɔ ni. Nɔɔna badwonna ma vo Yezu tei ba bwei‑o ba we, “Bɛŋwaane mo Jɔn kwaga tɔgena bam de Farisi tiina tɔgena bam yeini ba vɔ ni ye nmo kwaga tɔgena bam ba vɔa?” 19Yezu ma leiri-ba o we, “Nɔɔno ná wora o ke kadiri, ye o dwonna ná wora se ba tɔge ba di, banto wó wane ba vɔ ni na? Kan-baro wom ta ná wo ba tei ne, ba bá sɛ ba vɔ ni. 20Ko nam wó ba ko yi maŋa kam ba na wó ja kan-baro wom ba viiri to. Dɛ dem konto ne ye o daa tera ba tei ne to mo ba laam wó vɔ ni wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane.
21Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá sɛ o kwei gare-yi-doore o ma feiri gare-dwoŋo kolo na kaare to. O nam ná ke konto, gare-doŋo kom laam wó vuuri gare-dwoŋo kom pa se ko tiini ko chɔge dedɛ. 22Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ta bá sɛ o kwei sa-doora o lwo o ke lɔ-dwoŋa wone. O ná ke konto, ye sana bam ná keeri, ba wó pa se lɔa kam bage mo. Lɔa kam wó chɔge ye sana bam de lwo ba yage. Konto ŋwaane nɔɔno maŋe se o kwei sa-doora o ke lɔ-doŋa wone mo.”
Yezu Krista dwoi siu dɛ chullu tem
Matiyu 12:1-8; Luka 6:1-5
23Juu tiina siu dɛ dedwoŋi na yi to, Yezu déem ma tɔge kara wo o maa kɛa. O kwaga tɔgena bam de maa tɔge ba via. Ba ma bobo se ba taa bwori mena ba yu ba dona. 24Farisi tiina balo na tɔge ba wora to ma ta de Yezu ba we, “Nii ba na ke tei to! Bɛ mo ye ba ke totoŋe delo na chɔge dé siu dɛ chullu tem to?” 25Yezu ma leiri-ba o we, “Abam ta wo fɔge á ga Wɛ tɔnɔ kom na bere Pɛ David taane tei to na? Ko bere we kana déem jege wonto de o nɔɔna bam ye ba lage wodiu se ba di. 26O ma vo o zo diga kalo na ye Wɛ nyem to, ye o kwei bworobworo kolo na tigi da Wɛ ŋwaane to o di. Bworobworo kom konto chula se nɔn-gaa di-ko, ko ná dae Wɛ kaanem tiina bam yerane. David déem di bworobworo kom ye o daare o pa o nɔɔna bam de tɔge ba di. Keim dem konto ke maŋa kalo Abiatara déem na ye Wɛ kaanem yuu tu to mo.”
27O daa ma ta de-ba o we, “Wɛ na ke nabiina o yage logo baŋa ne to, o tiŋi siu dɛ bakwɛ maama wone se ko taa jege wolim mo ko pa-ba mo. Ko nam dae we Wɛ ke nabiina siu dɛ chullu tɔgem ŋwaane mo. 28Konto ŋwaane Nabiin-bu wom ta jege dam siu dɛ chullu tem baŋa ne.”

english_text:
A Man with a Paralyzed Hand
(Matthew 12.9-14; Luke 6.6-11)
1The next time Jesus went into the synagogue, a man with a paralyzed hand was there. 2The Pharisees wanted to accuse Jesus of doing something wrong, and they kept watching to see if Jesus would heal him on the Sabbath.
3Jesus told the man to stand up where everyone could see him. 4Then he asked, “On the Sabbath should we do good deeds or evil deeds? Should we save someone's life or destroy it?” But no one said a word.
5Jesus was angry as he looked around at the people. Yet he felt sorry for them because they were so stubborn. Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his bad hand was healed.
6The Pharisees left. And at once they started making plans with Herod's followers to kill Jesus.
Large Crowds Come to Jesus
7Jesus led his disciples down to the shore of the lake. Large crowds followed him from Galilee, Judea, 8and Jerusalem. People came from Idumea, as well as other places east of the Jordan River. They also came from the region around the towns of Tyre and Sidon. All of these crowds came because they had heard what Jesus was doing. 9 He even had to tell his disciples to get a boat ready to keep him from being crushed by the crowds.
10After Jesus had healed many people, the other sick people begged him to let them touch him. 11And whenever any evil spirits saw Jesus, they would fall to the ground and shout, “You are the Son of God!” 12But Jesus warned the spirits not to tell who he was.
Jesus Chooses His Twelve Apostles
(Matthew 10.1-4; Luke 6.12-16)
13Jesus decided to ask some of his disciples to go up on a mountain with him, and they went. 14Then he chose twelve of them to be his apostles, so they could be with him. He also wanted to send them out to preach 15and to force out demons. 16Simon was one of the twelve, and Jesus named him Peter. 17There were also James and John, the two sons of Zebedee. Jesus called them Boanerges, which means “Thunderbolts.” 18Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus were also apostles. The others were Simon, known as the Eager One, 19and Judas Iscariot, who later betrayed Jesus.
Jesus and the Ruler of Demons
(Matthew 12.22-32; Luke 11.14-23; 12.10)
20Jesus went back home, and once again such a large crowd gathered that there was no chance even to eat. 21When Jesus' family heard what he was doing, they thought he was crazy and went to get him under control.
22 Some teachers of the Law of Moses came from Jerusalem and said, “This man is under the power of Beelzebul, the ruler of demons! He is even forcing out demons with the help of Beelzebul.”
23Jesus told the people to gather around him. Then he spoke to them in riddles and said:
How can Satan force himself out? 24A nation whose people fight each other won't last very long. 25And a family that fights won't last long either. 26So if Satan fights against himself, that will be the end of him.
27How can anyone break into the house of a strong man and steal his things, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can take everything.
28I promise you that any of the sinful things you say or do can be forgiven, no matter how terrible those things are. 29 But if you speak against the Holy Spirit, you can never be forgiven. That sin will be held against you forever.
30Jesus said this because the people were saying that he had an evil spirit in him.
Jesus' Mother and Brothers
(Matthew 12.46-50; Luke 8.19-21)
31Jesus' mother and brothers came and stood outside. Then they sent someone with a message for him to come out to them. 32The crowd sitting around Jesus told him, “Your mother and your brothers and sisters are outside and want to see you.”
33Jesus asked, “Who is my mother and who are my brothers?” 34Then he looked at the people sitting around him and said, “Here are my mother and my brothers. 35Anyone who obeys God is my brother or sister or mother.”
translation_text:
Yezu yɔɔre nɔɔno siu dɛ ne
Matiyu 12:9-14; Luka 6:6-11
1Yezu daa ma jwoori o vo o zo ba jeerim diga kam. Nɔɔno maa wora o jeŋa dedoa na tega. 2Nɔɔna balo na wora to badwonna maa lage chwoŋa se ba bere we Yezu ke o tusi. Konto ŋwaane ba jei ba yere Yezu se ba nii, o wó sɛ o yɔɔre nɔɔno wom siu dɛ ne naa o bá sɛ. 3Yezu ma ta de nɔɔno wom o we, “Zaŋe n zege nɔɔna maama tetare ne.”
4O laam ma bwei ba maama o we, “Dé chullu tem bere bɛ mo? Kɔ mo tɔge chwoŋa, nɔɔno ná ke o dwoŋi lanyerane siu dɛ dem ne, naa o ná ke‑o lwarem? Kɔ mo lamma, nɔɔno ná vere o dwoŋi ŋwea siu dɛ dem ne, naa o ná go‑o?” O na bwei-ba konto to, ba ma chem. 5O ma nii ba maama ye o bane zaŋe. O wo ma chɔge dedɛ de ba na jege yi-dɛɛre tei to. O laam ma ta de nɔɔno wom o we, “Twe n jeŋa kam.” O ma seene o twe-ka, ye ka jwoori ka ke lanyerane. 6Farisi tiina bam na nɛ o na ke tei to, ba ma nwoŋi ba vo ba ŋɔɔne de Pɛ Herodi kwaga nɔɔna se ba beeri chwoŋa ba go Yezu.
7Yezu de o kwaga tɔgena bam ma zaŋe ba kɛ. Ba ma vo ba yi naneo kom ni. Kɔgɔ dedɛ ma nwoŋi Galili de Judea jei sem maama ne ba tɔge o kwaga. 8Nɔɔna badwonna de ma nwoŋi Jerusalem, de Judea maama, de Yidumia jei sem ne. Badaara de ma nwoŋi jei selo na wo Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ dedwoŋi dem ne to, de Tura de Sidon nawuura yam maama wone. Nɔn-fɔrɔ dedɛ ma vo Yezu tei, ba na lɔre o na ke kikia yalo maama to ŋwaane. 9Ba kɔgɔ kom na daga ye ba kwaane ba peene‑o dedɛ to, o ma ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam se ba ja nabworo ba ba ba zege da se o wane o zo ko wo. 10O na maŋe o yɔɔre nɔɔna dedɛ to ma pa se jaweena maama ma yigi ba peene‑o, ye ba kwaane se ba dwei o yera yam. 11Maŋa maama chichiri sem ná yeini se na‑o, se wó to o yiga ne ye se kaase se we, “Nmo mo ye Wɛ Bu wom.” 12Chichiri sem ná yeini se tɛ konto dwoŋi, o yeini o kaane-se mo se se yé pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre o na ye wolo to.
Yezu le o totoŋa nakwa
Matiyu 10:1-4; Luka 6:12-16
13Yezu laam ma zaŋe o vo o di peo kodwoŋi yuu. O ma bwoŋi balo o na lage o kuri to pa se ba ba o tei. Ba na tu to, 14o ma le nɔɔna fuga-balei ye o tiŋi-ba se ba taa ye o totoŋa nakwa bam. O na kuri-ba to, ko ye se ba taa sale‑o mo, se o wane o toŋe-ba nɔɔna tei ne se ba tɔɔle Wɛ kwora kam. 15O ta ma pa-ba dam se ba wane setaana ba zeili.
16Nɔɔna fuga-balei bam o na le to yera mo tento:
Simon wolo Yezu na pɛ o yere we Piita to.
17Jemsi wolo na ye Zebedi bu to, de o nyaane Jɔn. Yezu ma pa banto yere we Boanerega, ko kuri mo ‘Doa bagem nyena’.
18Anduru, de Filipi, de Batoloma, de Matiyu, de Tomas, dedaane Jemsi wolo na ye Alafayu bu to, de Tadayus, de Simon wolo na nwoŋi Zɛlota tigisim wone to, 19dedaane Judas Yisakara wolo na tu o yeigi Yezu o pa nɔɔna to.
Wɔ dam mo Yezu mae o zeili setaana?
Matiyu 12:22-32; Luka 11:14-23; 12:10
20Yezu ma jwoori o vo sɔŋɔ. Nɔn-kɔgɔ dedɛ daa ta ma ba ba gilimi sɔŋɔ kom ni dem. Ko ma pa se Yezu de o kwaga tɔgena bam daa ware ba na laŋa se ba di wodiu de. 21O sɔŋɔ tiina ma lɔre ko na ke‑o tei to. Ba ma zaŋe ba nwoŋi se ba vo ba ja‑o ba ke diga ne, kolo ŋwaane nɔɔna tɛ ba we o chwo mo.
22Wɛ nia zamesem tiina ya nwoŋi Jerusalem mo ba ba se ba nii. Ba maa tɛ ba we, “Setaana pɛ Bɛlzabula mo tei‑o. Ko ye wonto dam ŋwaane mo o wae setaana o zeila.”
23Yezu laam ma bwoŋi-ba se ba ba o tei ye o daare o maŋe memaŋa o bere-ba o we, “Nɔɔno wó wane o ma setaana pɛ dam o ma zeili setaana na? 24Teo kolo paare ná pɔɔre kuni belei pa ba jege daane, ko jege se ko to mo. 25Sɔŋɔ kolo maama ná pɔɔre ko tete wone, ko de jege se ko to mo. 26Setaana pɛ ná jwoori o jege de o tete, ko bere we o kɔgɔ kom pɔɔre belei mo ye o dam ti. O jege se o to mo. 27Ko nam na ye tei to, setaana pɛ nye de nɔn-babea na nii o sɔŋɔ tei to mo. Venvereno ná lage se o zo nɔn-babea sɔŋɔ o ŋɔ, o jege se o bobo o ja nɔn-babea kam mo o vɔ. O ná ke konto yiga, o laam wó wane o kwaleme o jejegero tem o ja viiri.
28A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, keim-balwaaro telo maama nɔɔna na ke to, naa ta-balwaaro telo ba na ŋɔɔne to, Wɛ wae o yage-te o ma chɛ-ba. 29Ko daare wolo maama nam ná ŋɔɔne o yaale Wɛ Sin-laao kom, Wɛ bá sɛ o ma chɛ konto tu. O keim-balɔrɔ kom konto wó taa wo o yuu ne mo taa wuu, ye o bere o bá na bora kɔtaa.” 30Ba daa ta maa tɛ ba we chichira mo daane‑o. Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo o tage de-ba konto dwoŋi.
Yezu nu de o nyaana na ye balo to chekke
Matiyu 12:46-50; Luka 8:19-21
31Yezu nu de o nyaana ma ba o na wo mɛ to. Ba ma vo ba zege sɔŋɔ kom pwooni ne, ye ba pa ni se ba bwoŋi‑o. 32Kɔgɔ dedɛ maa jei ba gilimi Yezu. Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “N nu de n nyaana tua, ye ba lage nmo.” 33O ma leiri-ba o we, “Banto yerane mo ye a nu de a nyaana na?” 34O laam ma nii balo na jei ba gilimi‑o to seeni ye o we, “Amo nu de a nyaana chekke mo tento. 35Wolo maama na ke Wɛ boboŋa na lage tei to mo ye a nyaane, de a nakɔ, de a nu.”

english_text:
A Story about a Farmer
(Matthew 13.1-9; Luke 8.4-8)
1 The next time Jesus taught beside Lake Galilee, a big crowd gathered. It was so large that he had to sit in a boat out on the lake, while the people stood on the shore. 2He used stories to teach them many things, and this is part of what he taught:
3Now listen! A farmer went out to scatter seed in a field. 4While the farmer was scattering the seed, some of it fell along the road and was eaten by birds. 5Other seeds fell on thin, rocky ground and quickly started growing because the soil wasn't very deep. 6But when the sun came up, the plants were scorched and dried up, because they did not have deep roots. 7Some other seeds fell where thornbushes grew up and choked out the plants. So they did not produce any grain. 8But a few seeds did fall on good ground where the plants grew and produced 30 or 60 or even 100 times as much as was scattered.
9Then Jesus said, “If you have ears, pay attention.”
Why Jesus Used Stories
(Matthew 13.10-17; Luke 8.9,10)
10When Jesus was alone with the twelve apostles and some others, they asked him about these stories. 11He answered:
I have explained the secret about God's kingdom to you, but for others I can use only stories. 12 The reason is,
“These people will look
and look, but never see.
They will listen and listen,
but never understand.
If they did,
they would turn to God
and be forgiven.”
Jesus Explains the Story about the Farmer
(Matthew 13.18-23; Luke 8.11-15)
13Jesus then told them:
If you don't understand this story, you won't understand any others. 14What the farmer is spreading is really the message about the kingdom. 15The seeds that fell along the road are the people who hear the message. But Satan soon comes and snatches it away from them. 16The seeds that fell on rocky ground are the people who gladly hear the message and accept it at once. 17But they don't have roots, and they don't last very long. As soon as life gets hard or the message gets them in trouble, they give up.
18The seeds that fell among the thornbushes are also people who hear the message. 19But they start worrying about the needs of this life. They are fooled by the desire to get rich and to have all kinds of other things. So the message gets choked out, and they never produce anything. 20The seeds that fell on good ground are the people who hear and welcome the message. They produce 30 or 60 or even 100 times as much as was planted.
Light
(Luke 8.16-18)
21 Jesus also said:
You don't light a lamp and put it under a clay pot or under a bed. Don't you put a lamp on a lampstand? 22 There is nothing hidden that will not be made public. There is no secret that will not be well known. 23If you have ears, pay attention!
24 Listen carefully to what you hear! The way you treat others will be the way you will be treated—and even worse. 25 Everyone who has something will be given more. But people who don't have anything will lose what little they have.
Another Story about Seeds
26Again Jesus said:
God's kingdom is like what happens when a farmer scatters seed in a field. 27The farmer sleeps at night and is up and around during the day. Yet the seeds keep sprouting and growing, and he doesn't understand how. 28It is the ground that makes the seeds sprout and grow into plants that produce grain. 29 Then when harvest season comes and the grain is ripe, the farmer cuts it with a sickle.
A Mustard Seed
(Matthew 13.31,32; Luke 13.18,19)
30Finally, Jesus said:
What is God's kingdom like? What story can I use to explain it? 31It is like what happens when a mustard seed is planted in the ground. It is the smallest seed in all the world. 32But once it is planted, it grows larger than any garden plant. It even puts out branches that are big enough for birds to nest in its shade.
The Reason for Teaching with Stories
(Matthew 13.34,35)
33Jesus used many other stories when he spoke to the people, and he taught them as much as they could understand. 34He did not tell them anything without using stories. But when he was alone with his disciples, he explained everything to them.
A Storm
(Matthew 8.23-27; Luke 8.22-25)
35That evening, Jesus said to his disciples, “Let's cross to the east side.” 36So they left the crowd, and his disciples started across the lake with him in the boat. Some other boats followed along. 37Suddenly a storm struck the lake. Waves started splashing into the boat, and it was about to sink.
38Jesus was in the back of the boat with his head on a pillow, and he was asleep. His disciples woke him and said, “Teacher, don't you care that we're about to drown?”
39Jesus got up and ordered the wind and the waves to be quiet. The wind stopped, and everything was calm.
40Jesus asked his disciples, “Why were you afraid? Don't you have any faith?”
41Now they were more afraid than ever and said to each other, “Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!”
translation_text:
Yezu maŋe memaŋa o bere nɔɔna
Matiyu 13:1-23; Luka 8:4-15
1Yezu déem maa wo naneo kom ni ne ye o bere nɔɔna. Nɔɔna dedɛ ma ba ba gilimi‑o. Ba kɔgɔ kom na daga to, o ma zaŋe o zo nabworo na zege na bam wone to, ye o jeini da se o bere-ba. Nɔɔna bam maama ma maŋe na bam ni ne se ba taa cheigi o taane dem. 2O maa mae memaŋa o bere-ba wonnu dedɛ. O déem ma maŋe o bere-ba o we:
3“Cheigi-na. Valo déem mo wora. O ma zaŋe o vo o kara se o du. 4O ma kare o dole o men-dwa yam. Yadwonna ma to chwoŋa ni ne. Zuna ma ba ba twɛ-ya ba di. 5Yadwonna ma to kandwa yuu ne teero na ba daga mɛ to. Teero na ba lira jei sem ne to, ya maa wo dáane ya puli. 6Wea ma ba ka baane ya maama. Ya bonno na wo zo tega to, ya laam ma te lela. 7Ko daare men-dwa yadwonna ma to sabare wone. Ya na puli to, sabare sem laam ma zaŋe se jujugi-ya, pa se ya daa wo ke bia. 8Ko daare yadwonna ma to te-ŋoŋa baŋa ne, ye yanto maama puli ya nwoŋi ya ke bia lanyerane. Yadaara ke nenɛɛne bia fintɔ fintɔ. Yadaara ke nenɛɛne bia fuseredo fuseredo. Yadaara de maa ke nenɛɛne bia bi bi.”
9Yezu ta ma ta o we, “Á nam fɔge á cheigi a taane dem lanyerane.”
10Kɔgɔ kom na viiri ba daare Yezu o yerane to, nɔɔna balo ya na wo o tei ne to badaara ma tɔge de o nɔɔna fuga-balei bam ba vo ba bwei‑o memaŋa yam kuri. 11O ma leiri-ba o we, “Ko ná ye abam, Wɛ maŋe o pa se á lɔre o paare dem kuri na ye tei to, ye chega kam konto ya maŋe ka seigi mo. Ko daare balo na dae amo kɔgɔ kom wo nɔɔna to, amo mae memaŋa yerane mo a bere-ba Wɛ chega kam. 12Amo yeini a bere-ba konto dwoŋi pa se
‘Ba yia yam wó kwaane ya nii,
ye ba na nɛ kolo to bá zo ba yuu.
Ba ta wó fɔge ba ta cheigi Wɛ taane dem,
ye ba bá ni de kuri.
Ko ná dae konto, ba ya wó wane ba pipiri ba sɛ Wɛ,
pa se o yage ba wɛleera o ma chɛ-ba.’ ”
13Yezu laam ma bwei-ba o we, “Á wo nigi memaŋe dento kuri na? Konto to, á wó wane á ni memaŋa yadwonna kuri na? 14Memaŋe dem kuri mo tento:
Men-dwa yalo valo wom na jege o du to mo bere Wɛ taane dem na ye tei to. 15Nɔɔna badwonna nye de men-dwa yalo na to chwoŋa kam ni ne to mo. Banto na nigi Wɛ taane dem to, setaana pɛ laam ma ba o chaale-de o le ba wone. 16Nɔɔna badwonna de maa nye de mena yalo na to kandwa yuu ne to. Banto ma ni Wɛ taane dem ye ba jwoŋi-de lela de wopwolo. 17Taane dem maa wo tiini de zo ba boboŋa, pa se ba yage-de lela. Yaara ná tu ba baŋa ye nɔɔna bɛɛse-ba Wɛ chega kam ŋwaane, ba laam wó kwei-ka ba yage lela. 18Nɔɔna badaara maa nye de mena yalo na to sabare sem wone to. Banto ye balo na nigi Wɛ taane dem 19ye ba ta jege lwia de logo baŋa wonnu to mo. Sabu-laga ma chɔge ba boboŋa ye wo-yɔɔro fera jege-ba pa se ba kwei Wɛ taane dem ba yage, ye de ta wo jaane kuri de pa-ba. 20Ko daare nɔɔna badaara nye de mena yalo na to te-ŋoŋa jei sem ne to mo. Banto mo ye balo na nigi Wɛ taane dem ye ba sɛ-de lanyerane to. Konto ma pa se Wɛ taane dem ja kuri de pa-ba, nenɛɛne mena na ke bia lanyerane se ko maŋe de bia fintɔ fintɔ, ye yadaara de ke bia fuseredo fuseredo, ye yadaara de ke bia bi bi to.”
Memaŋa yadwonna
Matiyu 13:31-32; Luka 8:16-18; 13:18-19
21Yezu daa ma maŋe o bere-ba o we, “Nɔɔno ná jege kanea, o bá sɛ o kwei-ka o pu zoŋa kuri ne, naa o zege-ka gadwogo kuri ne. O wó kwei-ka o pale wɛɛne mo. 22Wɛ chega kalo maama zem na seigi nɔɔna tei ne to jege se ka ba ka lɔre ja mo. Kolo maama zem na kwoli nɔɔna yibia ne to jege se ko puri mo jase se nɔɔna maama lɔre-ko. 23Á nam fɔge á cheigi a taane dem lanyerane.”
24O daa ma ta o we, “Kwaane-na á pa se á na nigi kolo to zo á boboŋa. Abam na ke á dwonna tei to, Wɛ wó ke abam de konto mo se ko taa mae daane, ye o ta ke o woli da. 25Nɔɔno wolo ná maŋe o jege woŋo, kotu ta wó jwoŋi kodwoŋi o woli da, ye nɔɔno wolo nam na maŋe o ba jege kolokolo to wó ba o ga kolo fenfee o ya na jege to de.”
26O daa ta ma ta o bere-ba we, “Wɛ paare dem na wó ba de taa wo nɔɔna baŋa ne tei to mo tento: Valo wodwoŋi mo kwei men-dwa o dole tega ne. 27Dɛ maama tete ne o maa tigi o dɔa ye te-pora ne o yeini o zaŋe. Maŋa maama wea de tete mena yam maa pula ye ya bera, ye valo wom ta yeiri ya na ke tei ya puli. 28Tega kam tete mo pae mena yam jiri konto. Ya yeini ya puli ya nwoŋi mo yiga. Ya laam ma ke men-kweero, ye ya daare ya ke bia. 29Mena yam ná bege ya ti, valo wom laam wó kwei o seo o vo o zage-ya, faao maŋa kam na yi to ŋwaane.”
30O daa ta ma ta o we, “Amo wó ke tɛ mo a bere abam Wɛ paare dem na ye tei to? Amo wó ma memaŋe mo a bere abam se á lɔre lanyerane. 31Wɛ paare dem nye de nɔɔno na kwei tio-bu-memeeno o du tega ne, ye tio-bu wom konto tiini o muri wo-bia maama wone. 32Nɔɔno wom nam na dugi‑o to, o laam ma nwoŋi o ji kamunu se ko dwoni dwo-vɔɔro telo maama na wo o kara kam ne to. Tio kom ma ta nɛ kamuna kamuna pa se zuna tui ba sɔ ba pworu ko woro ne.”
33Yezu maa mae memaŋa yanto dwoŋi dedɛ mo o tɛ Wɛ chega kam o bere nɔɔna bam. O maa yeini o bere-ba nenɛɛne ba na wó wane ba ni ko kuri tei to. 34O mɛ memaŋa yerane mo o bere nɔɔna bam. Ko nam ná daare wonto de o kwaga tɔgena bam yerane, o maa tɛ wonnu maama kuri jaja o bere-ba.
Yezu wane vo-fɔrɔ
Matiyu 8:23-27; Luka 8:22-25
35Dɛ dem konto wɛ-zoore maŋa ne to, Yezu ma ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam o we, “Pa-na dé kwei nabworo dé vo dé bɛ bubɛ dedwoŋi dem.” 36O na jei nabworo kom wone konto to, ba ma kwei‑o ba ja viiri ye ba daare kɔgɔ kom. Nabwooru tedwonna de maa tɔge-ba te via. 37Vo-fɔrɔ laam ma zaŋe ko mage bworo kom lanyerane. Na bam ma pɔgele dedɛ pa se bworo kom wora ko liri na ye ko lage ko tu na bam kuri. 38Yezu maa wo nabworo kom kwaga kam seeni o tigi pulu baŋa ne o dɔa. O kwaga tɔgena bam ma vo ba zaŋe‑o. Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Berem tu, dé lage dé te mo ye n yiga tera.”
39O laam ma zaŋe wɛɛne ye o daare o bage vo-fɔrɔ kom we, ko kwori! O ma ta de na bam we, ba yage! O na tage konto to, vio kom ma seene ko yage ye na bam de maŋe da chemm. 40O ma ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam o we, “Bɛ mo ye á fomma konto? Abam ta wo ke á wo-dedoa de amo na?”
41Foone ma tiini de ja-ba. Ba ma bwei daane ba we, “Wonto nam ye wɔ mo? O dam dem pae se vio kom de na bam sɛ o ni.”

english_text:
A Man with Evil Spirits
(Matthew 8.28-34; Luke 8.26-39)
1Jesus and his disciples crossed Lake Galilee and came to shore near the town of Gerasa. 2When he was getting out of the boat, a man with an evil spirit quickly ran to him 3from the graveyard where he had been living. No one was able to tie the man up anymore, not even with a chain. 4He had often been put in chains and leg irons, but he broke the chains and smashed the leg irons. No one could control him. 5Night and day he was in the graveyard or on the hills, yelling and cutting himself with stones.
6When the man saw Jesus in the distance, he ran up to him and knelt down. 7He shouted, “Jesus, Son of God in heaven, what do you want with me? Promise me in God's name that you won't torture me!” 8The man said this because Jesus had already told the evil spirit to come out of him.
9Jesus asked, “What is your name?”
The man answered, “My name is Lots, because I have ‘lots’ of evil spirits.” 10He then begged Jesus not to send them away.
11Over on the hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding. 12So the evil spirits begged Jesus, “Send us into those pigs! Let us go into them.” 13Jesus let them go, and they went out of the man and into the pigs. The whole herd of about 2,000 pigs rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
14The men taking care of the pigs ran to the town and the farms to spread the news. Then the people came out to see what had happened. 15When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had once been full of demons. He was sitting there with his clothes on and in his right mind, and they were terrified.
16Everyone who had seen what had happened told about the man and the pigs. 17Then the people started begging Jesus to leave their part of the country.
18When Jesus was getting into the boat, the man begged to go with him. 19But Jesus would not let him. Instead, he said, “Go home to your family and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how good he has been to you.”
20The man went away into the region near the ten cities known as Decapolis and began telling everyone how much Jesus had done for him. Everyone who heard what had happened was amazed.
A Dying Girl and a Sick Woman
(Matthew 9.18-26; Luke 8.40-56)
21Once again Jesus got into the boat and crossed Lake Galilee. Then as he stood on the shore, a large crowd gathered around him. 22The person in charge of the synagogue was also there. His name was Jairus, and when he saw Jesus, he went over to him. He knelt at Jesus' feet 23and started begging him for help. He said, “My little daughter is about to die! Please come and touch her, so she will get well and live.” 24Jesus went with Jairus. Many people followed along and kept crowding around.
25In the crowd was a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years. 26 She had gone to many doctors, and they had not done anything except cause her a lot of pain. She had paid them all the money she had. But instead of getting better, she only got worse.
27The woman had heard about Jesus, so she came up behind him in the crowd and barely touched his clothes. 28She had said to herself, “If I can just touch his clothes, I will be healed.” 29As soon as she touched them, her bleeding stopped, and she knew she was healed.
30At that moment Jesus felt power go out from him. He turned to the crowd and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
31His disciples said to him, “Look at all these people crowding around you! How can you ask who touched you?” 32But Jesus turned to see who had touched him.
33The woman knew what had happened to her. So she came trembling with fear and knelt down in front of Jesus. Then she told him the whole story.
34Jesus said to the woman, “You are now well because of your faith. May God give you peace! You are healed, and you will no longer be in pain.”
35While Jesus was still speaking, some people came from Jairus' home and said, “Your daughter has died! Why bother the teacher anymore?”
36Jesus heard what they said, and he said to Jairus, “Don't worry. Just have faith!”
37Jesus did not let anyone go with him except Peter and the two brothers, James and John. 38They went home with Jairus and saw the people crying and making a lot of noise. 39Then Jesus went inside and said to them, “Why are you crying and carrying on like this? The child isn't dead. She is just asleep.” 40But the people laughed at him.
After Jesus had sent them all out of the house, he took the girl's father and mother and his three disciples and went to where she was. 41-42He took the twelve-year-old girl by the hand and said, “Talitha, koum!” which means, “Little girl, get up!” The girl got right up and started walking around.
Everyone was greatly surprised. 43But Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened. Then he said, “Give her something to eat.”
translation_text:
Yezu zeili setaana nɔɔno tei ne
Matiyu 8:28-34; Luka 8:26-39
1Ba ma vo ba bɛ naneo kom bubɛ dedwoŋi dem Gerasa tiina na zoore mɛ to. 2Yezu ma nwoŋi nabworo kom wone. Nɔɔno wodwoŋi maa wora chichira na jege‑o ka yaara. 3-4O déem tigi yibeela jei ne mo. Kuni dedɛ ba yeini ba kwei chaponno ba ma vɔ o jea de o nɛ, ye o damma o dwoi-te. O maa yeini o vaŋe chaponno telo na wo o jea ne to o kɔ. O ma daare o mage luuru telo ba na ke o nɛ sem ne to o chɔge. O na tiini o damma to, nɔɔna daa ware ba ja‑o ba vɔ, naa ba pa o wo zuri. 5Maŋa maama wea de tete o beeri yibeela jei sem ne de peero yuu ne ye o kaasa. O maa yeini o kwei kandwa o ma kaare o tete.
6O na zege yiga yiga o tole o na Yezu to, o ma duri o vo o jeeri‑o. O na yi o tei to, o ma kuni dwoona o yiga ne, 7ye o kaase de kwor-dɛa o we, “Yezu, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom Bu, n tu amo tei se n ke bɛ mo? Nam du de Wɛ we n bá‑n waare-ne.” 8O tage konto kolo ŋwaane Yezu maŋe o wora o tɛ de chichira kam se ka yage o yera.
9Yezu laam ma bwei‑o o we, “N yere mo bɛ?” O ma leiri o we, “A yere mo Akɔgɔ, kokuri mo debam daga dedɛ.” 10Nɔɔno wom ma kwaane o lwoori Yezu kuni dedɛ we, o yé pa se chichiri sem nwoŋi jei sento ne se viiri.
11Teira dedɛ déem maa bwola. Ya kɔgɔ kom ye nenɛɛne morro telei (2,000) mo ye ya wora ya beeri ya wodiu peo kom teiŋa ne ya di. 12Konto ŋwaane setaana yam ma lwoori Yezu ya we, “Popo, pa dé vo teira yam wo dé taa tɔge-ya.” 13O ma pa setaana yam chwoŋa pa ya yage nɔɔno wom ye ya vo ya tɔge teira yam. Teira yam kɔgɔ kom maama laam ma duri ya siseiri ya tu buga kam wo ya nyɔ na ya te.
14Nɔɔna balo ya na nii teira yam baŋa ne to ma duri ba vo ba ta kolo na ke to ba bere teo kom nɔɔna bam de balo na wo ba kare ne ba toŋe to. Nɔɔna bam ma nwoŋi ba vo se ba nii ko na ke tei. 15Ba ma vo ba yi Yezu tei. Ba ma na nɔɔno wolo setaana kɔgɔ kom ya na daane‑o to. O maa jei da dedaane o boboŋa jwoori ya jeini ye o zo gwaaro. Ba na nɛ‑o konto to, foone ma zo-ba. 16Balo yi na nɛ ko maama to ma ta ba bere nɔɔna bam ko na ke nɔɔno wom tei to, de kolo na ke teira yam to de. 17Teo kom nɔɔna bam laam ma kwaane ba lwoori Yezu se o nwoŋi ba teo kom ne o viiri.
18Yezu ma vo se o jwoori o zo nabworo kom wo. Nɔɔno wolo setaana yam ya na jege‑o ya daane to ma lwoori‑o o we, “Popo, pa se a da a vo.” 19O maa wo sɛ ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Véi sɔŋɔ se n ta de n sɔŋɔ tiina Baŋa Wɛ na ke‑m lanyerane ye o duri nmo ŋwaŋa tei to.” 20Nɔɔno wom laam ma kɛ jei selo ba na bwoŋi we ‘Teene Fuga’ to ye o wora o tɛ nɔɔna bam Yezu na ke kolo o pa‑o to. Balo maama na nigi o taane dem to maa ye yaau.
Yezu yɔɔre nɔɔna badwonna
Matiyu 9:18-26; Luka 8:40-56
21Yezu déem ma jwoori o tɔge naneo kom wo o vo o bɛ bubɛ dedwoŋi dem. O na zege naneo kom ni ne to, nɔn-kɔgɔ ma ba o tei ba gilimi‑o. 22Nɔɔno wodwoŋi maa tɔge o wora, o yere mo Jarusi. Wonto ye Juu tiina jeerim diga kam yiga tu mo. O na tu o na Yezu to, o ma tiiri tega ne o yiga ne. 23O ma tiini o lwoori‑o o we, “Amo bukɔ-balaŋa mo lage o te. Popo, a lwoori‑m se n ba n zi n jea o baŋa ne, se konto wó pa o jaweo kom jei ye o jwoori o na ŋwea.” 24Yezu ma sɛ ye o tɔge ded‑o o vo. Kɔ-fɔrɔ de maa tɔge ba via ye ba jege‑o ba peene dedɛ.
25Kaane wodwoŋi maa tɔge o wora, o na tiini o wɔe wo taa, bena fuga-yalei. 26O déem yeini o vei dɔkta tiina dedɛ tei ye ba yaare‑o lanyerane. O ya chɔge o sabu maama ba baŋa ne ye ko ta ba gare ko pa‑o, ko fɔge ko jiri lɛɛro mo o yera ne. 27O laam na nigi Yezu ŋwa to, o ma tɔge kɔgɔ kom wo o kɛ o kwaga o vo o dwei o gɔrɔ kom. 28O maa boŋe we, “Amo ná maŋe a dwei o gɔrɔ yerane, amo wó na yazura.”
29O na dwei Yezu konto to, jana bam ma kɔ. O ma lɔre we o jaweo kom seene ko jei o yera ne. 30Bedwe baŋa ne mo Yezu maane we dam nwoŋi o yera ne. O ma zege kɔgɔ kom wone o pipiri o nii ye o bwei we, “Wɔ mo dwei a gɔrɔ?” 31O kwaga tɔgena bam ma ta ded‑o ba we, “N wo nɛ nɔɔna bam maama na yigi ba peene nmo tei to na? Bɛ mo ye n bwei we, wɔ mo dwei‑m?” 32O daa ta ma fɔge o nii kɔgɔ kom wone se o lɔre wolo na dwei‑o to. 33Kaane wom na lɔre kolo na ke‑o ye o na yazura to, foone maa jege‑o ye o yera sae. O ma vo Yezu tei o kuni dwoona o yiga ne ye o ta o chega maama o bere‑o. 34Yezu ma ta ded‑o o we, “A bukɔ, nmo na ke n wo-dedoa de amo tei to mo pɛ se n na yazura. Wɛ wó woli‑m se n sii de n jaweo kom.”
35Yezu ta na wora o ŋɔɔne konto to, nɔɔna badwonna ma ba ba yi o tei. Ba ya nwoŋi Jarusi sɔŋɔ mo ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “N bukɔ wom tega. Daa‑n yé ta‑n jege berem tu wom n daana.” 36Yezu ma chem, ye o ta de Jarusi o we, “Yé ta‑n fona. Nam yɔɔre n ke n wo-dedoa de Wɛ.”
37Yezu maa wo sɛ se nɔɔna tɔge ded‑o ba vo Jarusi sɔŋɔ kom, ko ná dae Piita, de Jemsi, de o nyaane Jɔn yerane. 38Ba ma vo ba yi sɔŋɔ kom. Yezu ma maane we sɔɔ yerane mo wora bɔge-bɔge, ye nɔɔna keera ye ba chwoosa. 39O ma zo sɔŋɔ kom o ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo á wora á ke sɔɔ ye á keera? Bu wom wo tege, o dɔ mo.” 40O na tage konto to, ba ma mɔne‑o.
O ma zeili ba maama pa ba nwoŋi. O ma daare o ja bu wom kwo, de o nu, de o tete kwaga tɔgena batɔ na wo o tei ne to o vo o zo diga kalo bu wom na tigi da to. 41O ma ja bu wom jeŋa ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Talita, koum.” Taane dento kuri mo ye “Busankana balaŋa, a tɛ nmo, zaŋe wɛɛne.” 42O na tage konto to, busankana kam ma zaŋe wɛɛne ka via. O bena déem ye fuga-yalei mo. Ko na ke‑o konto to, ko ma so-ba lanyerane. 43Yezu laam ma kaane-ba o we, ba yé zaŋe ba pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre kolo na ke to. O ma daare o ta o we, ba ke wodiu ba pa bu wom se o di.

english_text:
The People of Nazareth Turn against Jesus
(Matthew 13.53-58; Luke 4.16-30)
1Jesus left and returned to his hometown with his disciples. 2The next Sabbath he taught in the synagogue. Many of the people who heard him were amazed and asked, “How can he do all this? Where did he get such wisdom and the power to work these miracles? 3Isn't he the carpenter, the son of Mary? Aren't James, Joseph, Judas, and Simon his brothers? Don't his sisters still live here in our town?” The people were upset because of what he was doing.
4 But Jesus said, “Prophets are honored by everyone, except the people of their hometown and their relatives and their own family.” 5Jesus could not work any miracles there, except to heal a few sick people by placing his hands on them. 6He was surprised that the people did not have any faith.
Instructions for the Twelve Apostles
(Matthew 10.5-15; Luke 9.1-6)
Jesus taught in all the neighboring villages. 7Then he called together his twelve apostles and sent them out two by two with power over evil spirits. 8 He told them, “You may take along a walking stick. But don't carry food or a traveling bag or any money. 9It's all right to wear sandals, but don't take along a change of clothes. 10When you are welcomed into a home, stay there until you leave that town. 11 If any place won't welcome you or listen to your message, leave and shake the dust from your feet as a warning to them.”
12The apostles left and started telling everyone to turn to God. 13 They forced out many demons and healed a lot of sick people by putting olive oil on them.
The Death of John the Baptist
(Matthew 14.1-12; Luke 9.7-9)
14 Jesus became so well-known that Herod the ruler heard about him. Some people thought he was John the Baptist, who had come back to life with the power to work miracles. 15Others thought he was Elijah or some other prophet who had lived long ago. 16But when Herod heard about Jesus, he said, “This must be John! I had his head cut off, and now he has come back to life.”
17-18 Herod had earlier married Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip. But John had told him, “It isn't right for you to take your brother's wife!” So, in order to please Herodias, Herod arrested John and put him in prison.
19Herodias had a grudge against John and wanted to kill him. But she could not do it 20because Herod was afraid of John and protected him. He knew that John was a good and holy man. Even though Herod was confused by what John said, he was glad to listen to him. And he often did.
21Finally, Herodias got her chance when Herod gave a great birthday celebration for himself and invited his officials, his army officers, and the leaders of Galilee. 22The daughter of Herodias came in and danced for Herod and his guests. She pleased them so much that Herod said, “Ask for anything, and it's yours! 23I swear that I will give you as much as half of my kingdom, if you want it.”
24The girl left and asked her mother, “What do you think I should ask for?”
Her mother answered, “The head of John the Baptist!”
25The girl hurried back and told Herod, “Here and now on a serving plate I want the head of John the Baptist!”
26Herod was very sorry for what he had said. But he did not want to break the promise he had made in front of his guests. 27At once he ordered a guard to cut off John's head there in prison. 28The guard put the head on a serving plate and took it to the girl. Then she gave it to her mother.
29When John's followers learned that he had been killed, they took his body and put it in a tomb.
Jesus Feeds Five Thousand
(Matthew 14.13-21; Luke 9.10-17; John 6.1-14)
30After the apostles returned to Jesus, they told him everything they had done and taught. 31But so many people were coming and going that Jesus and the apostles did not even have a chance to eat. Then Jesus said, “Let's go to a place where we can be alone and get some rest.” 32They left in a boat for a place where they could be alone. 33But many people saw them leave and figured out where they were going. So people from every town ran on ahead and got there first.
34 When Jesus got out of the boat, he saw the large crowd that was like sheep without a shepherd. He felt sorry for the people and started teaching them many things.
35That evening the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This place is like a desert, and it's already late. 36Let the crowds leave, so they can go to the farms and villages near here and buy something to eat.”
37Jesus replied, “You give them something to eat.”
But they asked him, “Don't you know it would take almost a year's wages to buy all of these people something to eat?”
38Then Jesus said, “How much bread do you have? Go and see!”
They found out and answered, “We have five small loaves of bread and two fish.” 39Jesus told his disciples to tell the people to sit down on the green grass. 40They sat down in groups of 100 and groups of 50.
41Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish. He looked up toward heaven and blessed the food. Then he broke the bread and handed it to his disciples to give to the people. He also divided the two fish, so everyone could have some.
42After everyone had eaten all they wanted, 43Jesus' disciples picked up twelve large baskets of leftover bread and fish.
44There were 5,000 men who ate the food.
Jesus Walks on the Water
(Matthew 14.22-33; John 6.15-21)
45At once, Jesus made his disciples get into the boat and start back across to Bethsaida. But he stayed until he had sent the crowds away. 46Then he told them goodbye and went up on the side of a mountain to pray.
47Later in the evening he was still there by himself, and the boat was somewhere in the middle of the lake. 48He could see that the disciples were struggling hard, because they were rowing against the wind. Not long before morning, Jesus came toward them. He was walking on the water and was about to pass the boat.
49When the disciples saw Jesus walking on the water, they thought he was a ghost, and they started screaming. 50All of them saw him and were terrified. But at this same time he said, “Don't worry! I am Jesus. Don't be afraid.” 51He then got into the boat with them, and the wind died down. The disciples were completely confused. 52Their minds were closed, and they could not understand the true meaning of the loaves of bread.
Jesus Heals Sick People in Gennesaret
(Matthew 14.34-36)
53Jesus and his disciples crossed the lake and brought the boat to shore near the town of Gennesaret. 54As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus. 55So they ran all over that part of the country to bring their sick people to him on mats. They brought them each time they heard where he was. 56In every village or farm or marketplace where Jesus went, the people brought their sick to him. They begged him to let them just touch his clothes, and everyone who did was healed.
translation_text:
Yezu tete teo kom tiina ve‑o
Matiyu 13:53-58; Luka 4:16-30
1Yezu déem ma yage jei sem konto ye o jwoori o vo o tete teo. O kwaga tɔgena bam de tɔge‑o ba vo. 2Juu tiina siu dɛ na yi to, o ma vo o zo ba jeerim diga kam ye o bobo se o bere-ba Wɛ taane. Nɔɔna dedɛ maa wora ye ba cheigi o berem dem. Ba na nigi to, ko so-ba lanyerane. Ba ma ta ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto ke tɛ mo o lɔre wonnu tento dwoŋi? O jege swa ye o wae wo-kenkagela o ke. Ko nam ke tɛ mo? 3O ye debam teo kom nɔɔno, kapenta tu. O nu maa ye Mary. Jemsi, de Josef, de Judas, de Simon ye o nyaana mo. O nakɔa de ta wora debam tei ne. Ko dae konto na?”
Konto mo ba boboŋa déem chɔge o ni taane baŋa ne. 4O laam ma ta de-ba o we, “Nɔɔno ná ye Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu, nɔɔna yeini ba pa‑o zula lanyerane, se o tete teo tiina de o sɔŋɔ tiina de o chorro nam maŋe ba ba nege‑o.”
5O déem ware o ke wo-kenkagela ba tei ne, ko ná dae o na kwei o jeŋa o daŋe jaweena fenfee yerane baŋa ne o pa ba na yazura to. 6Ko ma ke Yezu yaau de ba na wo ke ba wo-dedoa ded‑o to.
Yezu toŋe o nɔɔna fuga-balei bam
Matiyu 10:5-15; Luka 9:1-6
Yezu déem ma tole te-balwa bam o kare o bere nɔɔna Wɛ chega kam. 7O laam ma bwoŋi o nɔɔna fuga-balei bam se ba ba o tei. O ma le-ba balei balei se o toŋe-ba, ye o pa-ba dam se ba wane ba zeili chichiri-lwanno nɔɔna tei ne. 8O ma pa-ba ni o we, “Á ná maa via, se á yé zaŋe á kwei kolokolo á woli da, ko ná dae nacheiga yerane. Á nam yé kwei wodiu, naa tampɔgɔ se á lwoori wodiu á ke da. Á yé kwei sabu á ke ganlɔgere ne á woli da. 9Zo-na natera, se á yé kwei gwaaro telei telei. 10Á ná vei á zo sɔŋɔ kolo á peini da, se á ta‑á wora se ko ba ko yi á viirim maŋa. 11Ko daare á ná yi teo kolo, ye ba ná wo sɛ se ba jeeri abam naa ba cheigi abam taane, se á yage jei sem konto. Á ná maa viira, se á kokɔge á nɛ fwogo kom á yage da, se ko pa nɔɔna bam lɔre we ba wo ke lanyerane.”
12O na tage konto de ba o ti to, ba laam ma nwoŋi ba vo ba tɔɔle Wɛ kwora ba bere nɔɔna we ba jege se ba leiri ba wo de ba keim-balwaaro tem. 13Ba ma zeili setaana dedɛ nɔɔna tei ne. Ba ma kwori ba kwei nuga ba laŋe jaweena dedɛ yuni ne pa ba na yazura.
Pɛ Herodi na go Jɔn tei to
Matiyu 14:1-12; Luka 9:7-9
14Pɛ wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Herodi. O ma ba o ni Yezu ŋwa, nɔɔna dedɛ na jege o taane ba ŋɔɔne to ŋwaane. Nɔɔna badwonna maa tɛ ba we, “Ko ye Jɔn wolo na ye sɛɛm tu to mo jwoori o bi toone wone. Mo kokuri o jege dam pa o wae wo-kenkagela dedɛ o ke.” 15Nɔɔna badaara maa we, “Ko ye Elija mo tua.” Badaara de ta maa we, “O ye Wɛ sampwora mo, nenɛɛne balo na tɔɔle Wɛ kwora faŋa faŋa to.” 16Ko daare Pɛ Herodi na nigi Yezu ŋwa to, o ma ta o we, “Ko wó taa ye Jɔn wolo amo na pɛ ba gwoni o yuu to mo jwoori o bi o na ŋwea.”
17O déem tage konto bɛŋwaane o ya wo ke Jɔn lanyerane ye o pa ba ja‑o ba vɔ ba ke peena diga ne. Ko déem ke tento dwoŋi mo: Herodi ya di kaane wodwoŋi, o yere mo Herodisa. Kaane wom déem ye o zembaaro Filipi nyem mo. 18Jɔn ma zaŋe o ta ded‑o we, ko chula se o di o zembaaro kaane. 19Konto ŋwaane mo Herodisa chuli Jɔn. O maa lage se ba go‑o. O nam wo nɛ chwoŋa, 20kolo ŋwaane Herodi kɔre Jɔn. O maa yei we o ye wo-pwoŋo tu na kɔre Wɛ to. Konto ŋwaane o jege‑o o choa se kolokolo yé ke‑o. O maa yeini o cheigi o taane de wopwolo, ye ko pa o boboŋa vugimi.
21Ko maa wora ko wora ye Herodisa laam na chwoŋa se o chɔge Jɔn ŋwea. Pɛ Herodi lora maŋa ma ba ka yi. O ma ke kuri ye o bwoŋi teo kom dedɛɛra bam, de soja yiga tiina, de naduna balo na zoore Galili ne to se ba tɔge ba di kuri dem. 22Herodisa bukɔ wom ma zo o sa veira bam tetare ne. Ko ma pa pɛ wom de o veira bam wo pwoli lanyerane. Pɛ wom ma ta de bukɔ wom o we, “Woŋo kolo maama nmo na lage to, amo wó pa‑m.” 23O ta ma ta o du o we, omo wó pa‑o woŋo kolo maama o na wó lwoori o tei ne to, ko ná maŋe ko ye o paare jejegero tem chichworo de. 24Bukɔ wom na nigi konto to, o ma nwoŋi o vo o nu tei o bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ ŋo mo amo wó lwoori se a jwoŋi?” O ma leiri o we, “Véi n ta we n lage Jɔn yuu mo se o gwoni o pa‑m.”
25Bukɔ wom ma ke lela o jwoori o zo pɛ tei, ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Amo na lage kolo to mo ye se n gwoni Jɔn yuu n ke-ko zon-tanlaŋa wone n ja n ba n pa-ne leile.” 26Pɛ Herodi na nigi konto to, o wo ma chɔge dedɛ. O nam na dugi ye o veira bam ni to, o maa ba lage se o ve‑o. 27O ma ke lela o toŋe o nɔn-babea dedoa se o vo o gwoni Jɔn yuu kom o ja ba. Nɔɔno wom ma seene o vo peena diga kam o gwoni Jɔn yuu kom. 28O ma kwei-ko o ke zon-tanlaŋa wone o ja ba o pa bukɔ wom. Wonto ma jwoŋi o ja nwoŋi o vo o pa o nu.
29Jɔn kwaga tɔgena bam na lɔre kolo na ke to, ba ma zaŋe ba vo ba kwei o yera yam ba ja vo ba ke yibeeli wone.
Yezu pɛ nɔɔna 5,000 wodiu se ba di
Matiyu 14:13-21; Luka 9:10-17; Jɔn 6:1-14
30Yezu totoŋa nakwa fuga-balei bam ma jwoori ba vo o tei. Ba ma ta ba bere‑o kolo maama ba na ke de ba na bere nɔɔna Wɛ chega kam tei to. 31Nɔɔna dedɛ maa yeini ba tui Yezu tei ye ba jwoori ba viira. Ba na daga konto to, Yezu de o nɔɔna bam daa ware ba na laŋa se ba di wodiu de. Konto ŋwaane o ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam nam ba á yerane se dé vo gaao wo se á wane á sii fenfee.”
32Ba ma pwɛ ba tete ba vo ba zo nabworo se ba vo jei selo na ye gaao wo to ba yerane. 33Ba na maa kɛ to, nɔɔna dedɛ ma na-ba. Ba ma lɔre-ba. Ba ma zaŋe ba nwoŋi ba teene dem maama ne, ye ba vo tega ne ba duri ba vo ba yi jei sem ye banto ta wo yi da. 34Yezu ma nwoŋi nabworo kom wone. O laam ma na nɔn-kɔgɔ kom na tu ko wora. O maa jege nɔɔna bam ŋwaŋa lanyerane, de ba na nye de pei selo na ba jege nayero se o taa nii se baŋa ne to. O laam ma bobo se o taa bere-ba wonnu dedɛ.
35Wɛ na wora de zoore to, o kwaga tɔgena bam ma vo ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Maŋa kam wora ka kɛa ye wodiu tera ywo-seeni se ba yeigi ba di. 36Konto ŋwaane, pa se nɔɔna bam vo sam wone ba yeigi wodiu ba di.” 37O ma leiri-ba o we, “Abam tete mo wó pa-ba wodiu se ba di.” Ba ma ta ba we, “Dé ná lage dé yeigi bworobworo dé pa ba maama se ba di, ko ya wó chɔge sabu dedɛ, nenɛɛne lu-nyenno sabu-dala bia yalei (200) mo. Dé vei dé yeigi konto mo na?”
38O ma bwei-ba o we, “Abam jege bworobworo ko mae tetɛ mo? Véi-na á nii.” Ba na vei ba na to, ba ma jwoori ye ba ta ba we, “Te ye tenu yerane mo, de ywona yalei.”
39Yezu laam ma pa-ba ni se ba pa nɔɔna bam pɔɔre kɔgɔ kɔgɔ ba jeini tega ne. 40Ba maama ma pɔɔre ye ba jeini, badaara kɔgɔ bi bi, badaara kɔgɔ finnu finnu. 41O ma kwei bworobwooru tenu tem de ywona yalei yam, ye o kwoni o yuu wɛɛne o ke Wɛ lei te ŋwaane. O ma fɔ fɔ bworobwooru tem o pa o kwaga tɔgena bam se ba laam jwoŋi-te ba ja vo ba maŋe ba pa nɔɔna bam. O ma daare o maŋe ywona yalei yam o pa ba maama se ba di. 42Nɔɔna bam maama ma di ba su ba daare. 43Ba na di ba daare konto to, Yezu kwaga tɔgena bam ma pɛ bworobworo de ywona chichwooru telo na daare to ba su kayɛ fuga-selei. 44Nɔɔna balo déem na di konto to ye baara morro tenu (5,000) mo, ko woli de kaana de bia de.
Yezu vei na baŋa ne
Matiyu 14:22-36; Jɔn 6:16-21
45Konto baŋa ne Yezu ma pa o kwaga tɔgena bam vo ba zo nabworo kom se ba da yiga ba bɛ naneo kom ba vo ba yi Bɛtasida. Ba na maa kɛ to, o ma pa kɔgɔ kom viiri. 46O na yage-ba konto to, o ma vo o di peero tem baŋa se o ware Wɛ.
47Tega ma ba ka yi. Nabworo kom maa wo naneo kom tetare ne, ye Yezu ta wo buburu kom ne o yerane. 48O ma tole o na o nɔɔna bam na tiini ba kwaane se ba yɛ ye ko chɛ ba yera ne, vo-fɔrɔ na zaŋe ko jeeri-ba to ŋwaane. Tega na wora ka poore to, Yezu ma zaŋe o nɔne na bam baŋa ne o maa vei ba tei. O maa via ye o lage o gaale-ba o kɛ. 49Ba nam na nɛ‑o o na vei na bam baŋa ne to, ba ya boŋe we ko wó taa ye chiru mo. Ba ma laare baŋa baŋa, 50ba maama na nɛ‑o ye foone zo-ba dedɛ to ŋwaane.
Yezu laam ma ŋɔɔne de-ba o we, “Pa-na á bochara ke dam, se ko ye amo mo. Á yé pa foone taa jege abam.”
51O laam ma vo o zo nabworo kom wo. O na yi ba tei konto to, vio kom ma kwori lela. Ko ma tiini ko ke-ba yaau, 52kolo ŋwaane Yezu na maŋe bworobworo kom o pa nɔn-kɔgɔ kom pa ba di to, ba wo nigi keim dem konto kuri. Ba boboŋa muri se Yezu chega kam zo ba wo lanyerane.
53Ba ma vo ba bɛ bubɛ dedem dem. Ba ma ja nabworo kom ba nwoŋi ba tiŋi da. Ba na yi jei selo to yere mo Gɛnesara. 54Ba na nwoŋi nabworo kom wone to, nɔɔna ma ba ba lɔre Yezu. 55Ba laam ma duri jei sem konto maama ne pa nɔɔna lɔre. Ba ma kwei balo na ba jege yazura to ba zeŋe ba ja vo o tei, mɛ maama ba na lɔre we o tu da to. 56O na yeini o vei jei selo maama to, ko ná ye teo balaŋa, naa teo kamunu, naa kara, nɔɔna yeini ba ja jaweena mo ba vo ba tiŋi yaga ni ne. Ba ma lwoori‑o se o pa-ba chwoŋa se ba dwei o gɔrɔ kom ni yerane. Balo maama na dwei o gɔrɔ kom konto to déem nɛ yazura.

english_text:
The Teaching of the Ancestors
(Matthew 15.1-9)
1Some Pharisees and several teachers of the Law of Moses from Jerusalem came and gathered around Jesus. 2They noticed that some of his disciples ate without first washing their hands.
3The Pharisees and many others obey the teachings of their ancestors. They always wash their hands in the proper way before eating. 4None of them will eat anything they buy in the market until it is washed. They also follow a lot of other teachings, such as washing cups, pitchers, and bowls.
5The Pharisees and teachers asked Jesus, “Why don't your disciples obey what our ancestors taught us to do? Why do they eat without washing their hands?”
6 Jesus replied:
You are nothing but show-offs! The prophet Isaiah was right when he wrote that God had said,
“All of you praise me
with your words,
but you never really
think about me.
7It is useless for you
to worship me,
when you teach rules
made up by humans.”
8You disobey God's commands in order to obey what humans have taught. 9You are good at rejecting God's commands so that you can follow your own teachings! 10 Didn't Moses command you to respect your father and mother? Didn't he tell you to put to death all who curse their parents? 11But you let people get by without helping their parents when they should. You let them say that what they own has been offered to God. 12You won't let those people help their parents. 13And you ignore God's commands in order to follow your own teaching. You do a lot of other things just as bad.
What Really Makes People Unclean
(Matthew 15.10-20)
14Jesus called the crowd together again and said, “Pay attention and try to understand what I mean. 15-16The food that you put into your mouth doesn't make you unclean and unfit to worship God. The bad words that come out of your mouth are what make you unclean.”
17After Jesus and his disciples had left the crowd and gone into the house, they asked him what these sayings meant. 18He answered, “Don't you know what I am talking about by now? You surely know that the food you put into your mouth cannot make you unclean. 19It doesn't go into your heart, but into your stomach, and then out of your body.” By saying this, Jesus meant that all foods were fit to eat.
20Then Jesus said:
What comes from your heart is what makes you unclean. 21Out of your heart come evil thoughts, vulgar deeds, stealing, murder, 22unfaithfulness in marriage, greed, meanness, deceit, indecency, envy, insults, pride, and foolishness. 23All of these come from your heart, and they are what make you unfit to worship God.
A Woman's Faith
(Matthew 15.21-28)
24Jesus left and went to the region near the town of Tyre, where he stayed in someone's home. He did not want people to know he was there, but they found out anyway. 25A woman whose daughter had an evil spirit in her heard where Jesus was. And at once she came and knelt down at his feet. 26The woman was Greek and had been born in the part of Syria known as Phoenicia. She begged Jesus to force the demon out of her daughter. 27But Jesus said, “The children must first be fed! It isn't right to take away their food and feed it to dogs.”
28The woman replied, “Lord, even puppies eat the crumbs that children drop from the table.”
29Jesus answered, “That's true! You may go now. The demon has left your daughter.” 30When the woman got back home, she found her child lying on the bed. The demon had gone.
Jesus Heals a Man Who Was Deaf and Could Hardly Talk
31Jesus left the region around Tyre and went by way of Sidon toward Lake Galilee. He went through the land near the ten cities known as Decapolis. 32Some people brought to him a man who was deaf and could hardly talk. They begged Jesus just to touch him.
33After Jesus had taken him aside from the crowd, he stuck his fingers in the man's ears. Then he spit and put it on the man's tongue. 34Jesus looked up toward heaven, and with a groan he said, “Effatha!” which means “Open up!” 35At once the man could hear, and he had no more trouble talking clearly.
36Jesus told the people not to say anything about what he had done. But the more he told them, the more they talked about it. 37They were completely amazed and said, “Everything he does is good! He even heals people who cannot hear or talk.”
translation_text:
Wo-digiru telo na chɔge nɔɔna to
Matiyu 15:1-20
1 Farisi tiina badaara de Wɛ nia zamesem tiina badaara déem ya nwoŋi Jerusalem ne, ye ba laam vo ba gilimi Yezu tei ne. 2Ba ma na o kwaga tɔgena badwonna na jei ba di wodiu ye ba wo sane ba jea se ko tɔge banto chullu tem chwoŋa. 3Ko na ye tei to, Juu tiina bam maama, ko fɔge ko dae Farisi tiina bam, yeini ba fɔge ba sane ba jea mo ye ba daare ba di wodiu. Ba tɔge chullu telo ba nabaara bam na pɛ-ba to mo konto. 4Ba ná yeigi wodiu yaga ne, ba wó sane ba jea mo ye ba laam daare ba di. Ba ta jege chullu dedɛ ba woli da ye ba tɔge-te. Ba yeini ba fɔge ba se ba zwe, de ba kɔɔra, de ba luu-kambi ye ba daare ba ke wodiu da.
5Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo Farisi tiina bam de Wɛ nia zamesem tiina bam déem bwei Yezu ba we, “Bɛ mo ye n tɔgena bam yeini ba di wodiu ye ba wo sane ba jea, ne dé nabaara bam na pɛ debam chullu telo to?” 6O ma leiri-ba o we, “Abam na ye pipiri-nyena to, Izaya déem jege chega de o na wuuri o ta abam taane faŋa faŋa tei to. Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
‘Nɔɔna banto zuli amo de ba ni mo,
ye ba boboŋa tera amo tei ne.
7Ba na pae amo zula tei to maama ye kafɛ mo.
Ba bera yam tɔge nabiina boboŋa chullu mo,
ye ba pae se te ye amo nyem.’
8Chega to, abam mo kwei Wɛ nia yam na bere tei to á yage, ye á daare á tɔge nabiina chullu.”
9O daa ta ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam yeini á ve Wɛ nia yam ye á daare á jege á tete boboŋa chullu mo á tɔga. Konto jege swa na? 10Faŋa faŋa to Moses déem bere Wɛ ni dem o we, nɔɔno jege se o taa zuli o kwo de o nu. O daa ta bere we, nɔɔno ná ŋɔɔne ta-balɔrɔ o pa o nu naa o kwo, konto tu jege se o te mo. 11Ko daare abam nam yeini á ja Wɛ taane dem á pipiri ye á we, nɔɔno ná jege woŋo kolo o ya na wó ma woli o kwo de o nu, ye o ná we, woŋo kom konto ye ‘Kɔban’ mo (ko kuri mo ko maŋe ko ye Wɛ nyem), 12ko bere we wonto daa ba jege se o kwei woŋo kom o ma zeini o kwo de o nu. 13Á na ke tei ye á bere nɔɔna se ba taa tɔge á tete chullu to pae se Wɛ ni dem daa ba jege kuri abam tei ne. Abam yeini á tɔge keim-balwaaro tento dwoŋi dedɛ.”
14Yezu daa ta ma bwoŋi nɔn-kɔgɔ kom pa se ba ba o tei, ye o ta de-ba o we, “Abam maama cheigi lanyerane se á ni amo taane dem kuri. 15Woŋo kolo maama nɔɔno na wó kwei o pa se ko zo o wo to bá wane ko pa o digiri o tete. Ko nam ye kolo na maŋe ko wo nɔɔno wone ye ko laam nwoŋi to mo wó pa o digiri. [16Á nam fɔge á cheigi a taane dem lanyerane.]”
17O laam ma vo o zo sɔŋɔ o daare nɔn-kɔgɔ kom pwooni ne. O kwaga tɔgena bam ma ba o tei ba bwei‑o taane dem kuri. 18O ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam de swa ta muri mo na? Á jege se á ta‑á yei we, woŋo kolo maama nɔɔno na wó kwei o pa se ko zo o wo to bá wane ko pa o digiri. 19Kolo ŋwaane ko bá wane ko chɔge o bochare. Ko nam wó tu o kana yerane mo, ye o laam daare o tɔ-ko o yage.” Yezu déem na tage chega kam konto to, o bere we wodiiru maama maŋe de dim.
20O daa ta ma ta o we, “Ko ye kolo na maŋe ko wo nɔɔno wone ye ko laam nwoŋi to mo wó pa o digiri o tete. 21Kolo ŋwaane ko ye nɔɔno bochare boboŋa mo pae se o lage wo-lwanno tɔgem. Ya maa wae ya pae o tɔge bwoŋa keim de ka-laga wo-zɔɔna maama. Ya maa wae ya pae o ŋɔna, naa o go nɔɔna. 22Ya maa wae ya pae o yi zoore wonnu dedɛ, naa o yaale nɔɔna, naa o gane nɔɔna. Ya ta maa wae ya pae o tɔge ka-laga wo-digiru kikia, naa o jege puseŋa, naa o ŋɔɔne o chɔge o dwoŋi yere, naa o bere o tete kamunim, naa o tɔge jworim kikia. 23Wo-balwaaro tento maama nwoŋi nɔɔno wone mo ye te pa o digiri.”
Kaane wodwoŋi ke o wo-dedoa de Yezu
Matiyu 15:21-28
24Yezu déem ma zaŋe o yage jei sem konto ye o daare o vo Tura nawuura yam seeni. O ma vo o zo sɔŋɔ kodwoŋi o maŋe da. O maa ba lage se nɔɔna lɔre o na wo mɛ to. O nam ware o seigi o tete nɔɔna tei ne. 25-26Kaane wodwoŋi maa wora, o na ye dwi-gɛ tu. Ba ya loge‑o Siria ne mo, jei selo ba na bwoi we Fonikia to. Chichira maa jege o bukɔ ka daana. Konto ŋwaane, o na tu o ni Yezu ŋwa to, o ma ke lela o vo o tei ye o tiiri tega ne o yiga ne. O ma lwoori‑o se o zeili setaane dem pa de yage o bukɔ wom yera. 27O na lwoori konto to, Yezu ma ta ded‑o o we, “Bia bam mo jege chwoŋa se ba da yiga ba di ba daare. Ko wo maŋe se nɔɔno jwoŋi o bia wodiu o dole o pa kukuri.”
28Kaane wom maa we, “Amo tu, n tage chega. Kukuri selo na tigi tabolo kuri ne to nam jege chwoŋa se se twɛ wodiu kolo bia bam na di ye ko siiri tega ne to mo se di.” 29O laam ma ta de kaane wom o we, “Nmo na leiri lanyerane konto to, amo sɛ n lworo kom. Jwoori n vo sɔŋɔ. Setaane dem maŋe de yage n bukɔ wom yera.”
30Kaane wom ma seene o vo sɔŋɔ. O ma na o bukɔ wom o tigi chemm, de setaane dem nwoŋi de daare‑o.
31Yezu laam ma zaŋe o yage Tura nawuura yam seeni ye o daare o da Sidon o kɛ.
