O laam ma tɔge jei selo ba na bwoi we ‘Teene Fuga’ to o vo o yi Galili naneo kom jei sem. 32Nɔɔno mo wora o na ye zɔ-kɔgɔ ye o wae o ŋɔɔne fenfee yerane. Nɔɔna ma ja‑o ba vo Yezu tei. Ba ma lwoori‑o se o kwei o jeŋa o daŋe nɔɔno wom baŋa ne se o yɔɔre‑o. 33Yezu ma ja‑o o vo dáa o yerane o daare kɔgɔ kom. O ma kwei o noa o turi nɔɔno wom zwa ne ye o daare o twe lileeru o ke o noa ne o ma dwei o dindeilimi. 34O ma kwoni o yuu wɛɛne o nii ye o suuri. O ma ta de nɔɔno wom o we, “Effata”, ko kuri mo “Pore!” 35O na tage konto to, o zwa yam seene ya pore ye o dindeilimi de wae de pipira. O maa wae o ŋɔɔne lanyerane.
36Yezu ma kaane nɔɔna bam maama se ba yé ta kolo na ke to ba bere nɔɔn-nɔɔno. O na tiini o kaane-ba o woli da to, ba ma tiini ba ŋɔɔne ko taane ko ja gaale. 37Balo maama na nigi to tiini ba ye yaau. Ba maa we, “Woŋo kolo maama o na ke to ye lanyerane. O maŋe o pae zɔ-kɔro jwoori te ni, ye memaaro de wae te ŋɔɔna.”

english_text:
Jesus Feeds Four Thousand
(Matthew 15.32-39)
1One day another large crowd gathered around Jesus. They had not brought along anything to eat. So Jesus called his disciples together and said, 2“I feel sorry for these people. They have been with me for three days, and they don't have anything to eat. 3Some of them live a long way from here. If I send them away hungry, they might faint on their way home.”
4The disciples said, “This place is like a desert. Where can we find enough food to feed such a crowd?”
5Jesus asked them how much food they had. They replied, “Seven small loaves of bread.”
6After Jesus told the crowd to sit down, he took the seven loaves and gave thanks. He then broke the loaves and handed them to his disciples, who passed them out to the crowd. 7They also had a few little fish, and after Jesus had blessed these, he told the disciples to pass them around.
8-9The crowd of about 4,000 people ate all they wanted, and the leftovers filled seven large baskets.
As soon as Jesus had sent the people away, 10he got into the boat with the disciples and crossed to the territory near Dalmanutha.
A Sign from Heaven
(Matthew 16.1-4)
11 The Pharisees came out and started an argument with Jesus. They wanted to test him by asking for a sign from heaven. 12 Jesus groaned and said, “Why are you always looking for a sign? I can promise you that you will not be given one!” 13Then he left them. He again got into a boat and crossed over to the other side of the lake.
The Yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod
(Matthew 16.5-12)
14The disciples had forgotten to bring any bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat. 15 Jesus warned them, “Watch out! Guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod.”
16The disciples talked this over and said to each other, “He must be saying this because we don't have any bread.”
17Jesus knew what they were thinking and asked, “Why are you talking about not having any bread? Don't you understand? Are your minds still closed? 18 Are your eyes blind and your ears deaf? Don't you remember 19how many baskets of leftovers you picked up when I fed those 5,000 people with only five small loaves of bread?”
“Yes,” the disciples answered. “There were twelve baskets.”
20Jesus then asked, “And how many baskets of leftovers did you pick up when I broke seven small loaves of bread for those 4,000 people?”
“Seven,” they answered.
21“Don't you know what I am talking about by now?” Jesus asked.
Jesus Heals a Blind Man at Bethsaida
22As Jesus and his disciples were going into Bethsaida, some people brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch the man. 23Jesus took him by the hand and led him out of the village, where he spit into the man's eyes. He placed his hands on the blind man and asked him if he could see anything. 24The man looked up and said, “I see people, but they look like trees walking around.”
25Once again Jesus placed his hands on the man's eyes, and this time the man stared. His eyes were healed, and he saw everything clearly. 26Jesus said to him, “You may return home now, but don't go into the village.”
Who Is Jesus?
(Matthew 16.13-20; Luke 9.18-21)
27Jesus and his disciples went to the villages near the town of Caesarea Philippi. As they were walking along, he asked them, “What do people say about me?”
28 The disciples answered, “Some say you are John the Baptist or maybe Elijah. Others say you are one of the prophets.”
29 Then Jesus asked, “But who do you say I am?”
“You are the Messiah!” Peter replied.
30Jesus warned the disciples not to tell anyone about him.
Jesus Speaks about His Suffering and Death
(Matthew 16.21-28; Luke 9.22-27)
31Jesus began telling his disciples what would happen to him. He said, “The nation's leaders, the chief priests, and the teachers of the Law of Moses will make the Son of Man suffer terribly. He will be rejected and killed, but three days later he will rise to life.” 32Then Jesus explained clearly what he meant.
Peter took Jesus aside and told him to stop talking like that. 33But when Jesus turned and saw the disciples, he corrected Peter. He said to him, “Satan, get away from me! You are thinking like everyone else and not like God.”
34 Jesus then told the crowd and the disciples to come closer, and he said:
If any of you want to be my followers, you must forget about yourself. You must take up your cross and follow me. 35 If you want to save your life, you will destroy it. But if you give up your life for me and for the good news, you will save it. 36What will you gain, if you own the whole world but destroy yourself? 37What could you give to get back your soul?
38Don't be ashamed of me and my message among these unfaithful and sinful people! If you are, the Son of Man will be ashamed of you when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
translation_text:
Yezu pɛ nɔɔna 4,000 wodiu se ba di
Matiyu 15:32-39
1Kanto maŋa kam ne, kɔgɔ dedɛ daa ma jwoori ko gilimi daane Yezu tei ne. Ba maa ba jege kolokolo se ba di. Konto ŋwaane Yezu ma bwoŋi o kwaga tɔgena bam se ba ba o tei. O ma ta de-ba o we, 2“Amo jege nɔɔna banto ŋwaŋa de ba na tu ba wo amo tei ne da yatɔ, ye ba laam daa ba jege wodiu se ba di. 3Amo ná pɛ ba viiri ye ba wo di kolokolo, kana wó pa ba beiri chwoŋa ne, kolo ŋwaane ba badaara ya nwoŋi yiga yiga mo ba ba amo tei.” 4O kwaga tɔgena bam ma leiri‑o ba we, “Dé nam wó ke tɛ mo dé na wodiu kagoa kanto yuu ne se ko yi ba maama dim?” 5O ma bwei-ba o we, “Abam jege bworobworo ko mae tetɛ mo?” Ba ma leiri ba we, “Te ye terepɛ mo.”
6Yezu laam ma ta de kɔgɔ kom se ba maama jeini tega ne. O ma kwei bworobwooru terepɛ tem ye o ke Wɛ lei te ŋwaane. O ma ja-te o fɔ fɔ o pa o kwaga tɔgena bam ye banto de laam kwei ba ja vo ba pa nɔɔna bam. 7Ba déem jege ywona fenfee ba woli da. Yezu ma kwei-ya o ke Wɛ lei ye o daare o ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam se ba kwei yanto de ba maŋe ba pa nɔɔna bam maama. 8Ba maama ma di ba su ba daare. Yezu kwaga tɔgena bam laam ma twɛ chichwooru telo na daare to ba su kayɛ serepɛ. 9Balo na wora to déem maŋe de baara morro tena (4,000) mo, ko woli de kaana de bia de.
Yezu laam ma pa se kɔgɔ kom viiri. 10O ma daare o vo o zo nabworo kom de o kwaga tɔgena bam. Ba ma vo ba yi jei sedwoŋi yere na ye Dalemanuta to.
Farisi tiina taane
Matiyu 16:1-12; Luka 12:54-56
11Farisi tiina badwonna déem ma vo Yezu tei se ba ŋɔɔne ded‑o, ye ba nam lage ba maŋe‑o mo ba nii. Ba ma lwoori‑o se o ke wo-kenkagele delo na wó bere-ba we o dam seene de ye Wɛ nyem to. 12O ma tiini o suuri o wone ye o ta o we, “Bɛ mo ye zem nɔɔna bam lage se a ke wo-kenkagele a bere-ba? A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, a bá ke maana a pa-ba.”
13O na tage konto to, o ma yage ba tei ye o jwoori o vo o zo nabworo kom se ba vo ba bɛ bubɛ dedem dem.
14Ba déem na wo nabworo kom wone ba maa vei ba bɛ to, Yezu kwaga tɔgena bam ma maane we ba ya swei se ba ja bworobworo ba woli da, ye dedoa yerane mo ba jega. 15Yezu ma ta de-ba o we, “Ta‑á yei-na se á yé pa Farisi tiina bam de abam sabɔle, de Pɛ Herodi de.” 16O na tage de-ba konto to, ba ma ŋɔɔne daane ba we, “Ko ye bworobworo taane mo o tɛa, dé na ba jege to ŋwaane.”
17Yezu ma maane ba na tɛ kolo to, ye o we, “Bɛ mo ye á pa lwia jege abam de bworobworo na tera to ŋwaane? Abam ta wo lɔre Wɛ na jege dam tei to na? Á boboŋa muri mo. 18Á jege yia ye ya ba nae Wɛ chega kam. Á jege zwa ye á ba ni Wɛ taane dem kuri. 19Á maŋe á swei amo na kwei bworobwooru tenu mo a fɔ fɔ a pa nɔɔna morro tenu tem pa ba di. Ba na di ba ti to, abam twɛ chichwooru tem á su kayɛ segera mo?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Kayɛ fuga-selei mo.”
20O daa ma bwei-ba o we, “Amo daa ta na kwei bworobwooru terepɛ tem a fɔ fɔ a pa nɔɔna morro tena tem to, á twɛ chichwooru tem á su kayɛ segera mo?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Kayɛ serepɛ mo.” 21O laam ma ta de-ba o we, “Tɔ. Abam daa ta ba ni ko kuri mo na?”
Yezu yɔɔre lilwei
22Ba déem ma vo ba yi Bɛtasida. Nɔɔna badwonna ma ja lilwei ba ja vo Yezu tei ye ba lwoori‑o se o kwei o jeŋa o dwei‑o. 23O ma ja lilwei wom jeŋa o vaŋe o ja nwoŋi teo kom dáa. O ma twe lileeru o ke o yia ne. O ma daare o kwei o jea o zi o baŋa ne. O laam ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo nae woŋo mo na?” 24Lilwei wom ma zeiŋi o yuu o nii, ye o we, “Amo wae a nae nɔɔna na via. Ba nam nye de teeni mo ye ba via.”
25Yezu daa ma kwei o jea o daŋe nɔɔno wom yia ne. O laam ma fi o yia yam, ye ya jwoori ya nae. O maa wae o nae woŋo maama lanyerane. 26Yezu laam ma ta ded‑o we, o yɔɔre o vo sɔŋɔ, se o daa yé jwoori o zo teo kom wo.
Piita tage Yezu chega kam
Matiyu 16:13-20; Luka 9:18-21
27Yezu de o kwaga tɔgena bam daa ma kɛ ba vo ba yi Kazaria Filipi nawuura yam. Ba na maa vei to, o ma bwei-ba o we, “Nɔɔna yeini ba tɛ ba we amo ye wɔ mo?” 28Ba ma leiri ba we, “Badaara tɛ ba we, nmo ye Jɔn wolo na ye sɛɛm tu to mo. Badaara de maa tɛ ba we, nmo ye Elija mo. Badaara de maa tɛ ba we, nmo ye faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem dedoa mo.”
29O laam ma bwei-ba o we, “Ko nam ná ye abam, á boŋe se amo ye wɔ mo?” Piita ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo ye Wɛ Dam Tu Krista mo.”
30Yezu laam ma ta-ba we, ba yé ta o chega kam konto ba bere nɔɔn-nɔɔno.
Yezu bere o toone na wó taa ye tei to
Matiyu 16:21-28; Luka 9:22-27
31Ko zege kanto maŋa kam ne Yezu ma ŋɔɔne o bere-ba we omo Nabiin-bu wom maŋe se o na yaara dedɛ. O maa we, “Juu tiina nakwa bam, de ba kaanem yiga tiina bam, de ba zamesem tiina bam mo wó chuli amo. Ba maa wó ja amo ba go, se a laam jwoori a bi da yatɔ dɛ ne.” 32O maa ŋɔɔne konto ja o bere-ba. Piita ma ja‑o o vo dáa, ye o bwɛ‑o o we o yé taa ŋɔɔne konto dwoŋi. 33Yezu ma guni o nii o kwaga tɔgena bam seeni, ye o leiri o bwɛ Piita o we, “Setaana pɛ, véi dáa a tei ne! Nmo boboŋa yam ye nabiina nyem mo ye ya ba tɔge Wɛ na lage tei to.”
34O laam ma bwoŋi nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama de o kwaga tɔgena bam se ba ba o tei. O ma ta de-ba o we, “Nɔɔno wolo maama ná lage se o taa tɔge amo kwaga, konto tu jege se o ve o tete boboŋa ye o sɛ yaara, ne wolo na zeŋe dagara o maa vei o toone jei tei to, se o laam ba o taa tɔge-ne. 35Wolo maama nam ná lage se o jwoŋi o tete ŋwea, konto tu wó ga-ka mo. Ko daare wolo maama ná sɛ se o ga o ŋwea amo ŋwaane de Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam ŋwaane, konto tu wó jwoŋi ŋwea Wɛ tei ne. 36Nɔɔno nam ná kwaane o jwoŋi logo baŋa wonnu tem maama, ye o laam ná gɛ ŋwea Wɛ tei ne, bɛ nyɔɔre mo o nɛa? 37Kolokolo nam tera nɔɔno na wó wane o kwei o ma jwoŋi o ŋwea Wɛ tei ne. 38Zem nɔɔna bam yiga tera de Wɛ ye ba ke ba tusi dedɛ. Konto to, wolo maama ná kɔre chaveera amo ŋwaane de a taane dem ŋwaane, amo Nabiin-bu wom de wó taa jege chaveera konto tu ŋwaane dɛ dem amo na wó jwoori a ba de nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ ne a Kwo Wɛ na jege tei to, ye Wɛ malese de wó tɔge-ne.”

english_text:
1I can assure you that some of the people standing here will not die before they see God's kingdom come with power.
The True Glory of Jesus
(Matthew 17.1-13; Luke 9.28-36)
2 Six days later Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him. They went up on a high mountain, where they could be alone. There in front of the disciples, Jesus was completely changed. 3And his clothes became much whiter than any bleach on earth could make them. 4Then Elijah and Moses appeared and were talking with Jesus.
5Peter said to Jesus, “Teacher, it is good for us to be here! Let us make three shelters, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” 6But Peter and the others were terribly frightened, and he did not know what he was talking about.
7 The shadow of a cloud passed over and covered them. From the cloud a voice said, “This is my Son, and I love him. Listen to what he says!” 8At once the disciples looked around, but they saw only Jesus.
9As Jesus and his disciples were coming down the mountain, he told them not to say a word about what they had seen, until the Son of Man had been raised from death. 10So they kept it to themselves. But they wondered what he meant by the words “raised from death.”
11 The disciples asked Jesus, “Don't the teachers of the Law of Moses say that Elijah must come before the Messiah does?”
12 Jesus answered:
Elijah certainly will come to get everything ready. But don't the Scriptures also say that the Son of Man must suffer terribly and be rejected? 13I can assure you that Elijah has already come. And people treated him just as they wanted to, as the Scriptures say they would.
Jesus Heals a Boy
(Matthew 17.14-20; Luke 9.37-43a)
14When Jesus and his three disciples came back down, they saw a large crowd around the other disciples. The teachers of the Law of Moses were arguing with them.
15The crowd was really surprised to see Jesus, and everyone hurried over to greet him.
16Jesus asked, “What are you arguing about?”
17Someone from the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought my son to you. A demon keeps him from talking. 18Whenever the demon attacks my son, it throws him to the ground and makes him foam at the mouth and grit his teeth in pain. Then he becomes stiff. I asked your disciples to force out the demon, but they couldn't do it.”
19Jesus said, “You people don't have any faith! How much longer must I be with you? Why do I have to put up with you? Bring the boy to me.”
20They brought the boy, and as soon as the demon saw Jesus, it made the boy shake all over. He fell down and began rolling on the ground and foaming at the mouth.
21Jesus asked the boy's father, “How long has he been like this?”
The man answered, “Ever since he was a child. 22The demon has often tried to kill him by throwing him into a fire or into water. Please have pity and help us if you can!”
23Jesus replied, “Why do you say ‘if you can’? Anything is possible for someone who has faith!”
24At once the boy's father shouted, “I do have faith! Please help me to have even more.”
25When Jesus saw that a crowd was gathering fast, he spoke sternly to the evil spirit that had kept the boy from speaking or hearing. He said, “I order you to come out of the boy! Don't ever bother him again.”
26The spirit screamed and made the boy shake all over. Then it went out of him. The boy looked dead, and almost everyone said he was. 27But Jesus took hold of his hand and helped him stand up.
28After Jesus and the disciples had gone back home and were alone, they asked him, “Why couldn't we force out that demon?”
29Jesus answered, “Only prayer can force out this kind of demon.”
Jesus Again Speaks about His Death
(Matthew 17.22,23; Luke 9.43b-45)
30Jesus left with his disciples and started through Galilee. He did not want anyone to know about it, 31because he was teaching the disciples that the Son of Man would be handed over to people who would kill him. But three days later he would rise to life. 32The disciples did not understand what Jesus meant, and they were afraid to ask.
Who Is the Greatest?
(Matthew 18.1-5; Luke 9.46-48)
33Jesus and his disciples went to his home in Capernaum. After they were inside the house, Jesus asked them, “What were you arguing about along the way?” 34 They had been arguing about which one of them was the greatest, and so they did not answer.
35 After Jesus sat down and told the twelve disciples to gather around him, he said, “If you want the place of honor, you must become a slave and serve others!”
36Then Jesus asked a child to stand near him. He put his arm around the child and said, 37 “When you welcome even a child because of me, you welcome me. And when you welcome me, you welcome the one who sent me.”
For or against Jesus
(Luke 9.49,50)
38John said, “Teacher, we saw a man using your name to force demons out of people. But he wasn't one of us, and we told him to stop.”
39Jesus said to his disciples:
Don't stop him! No one who works miracles in my name will soon turn and say something bad about me. 40 Anyone who isn't against us is for us. 41 And anyone who gives you a cup of water in my name, just because you belong to me, will surely be rewarded.
Temptations To Sin
(Matthew 18.6-9; Luke 17.1,2)
42It will be terrible for people who cause even one of my little followers to sin. Those people would be better off thrown into the ocean with a heavy stone tied around their necks. 43-44 So if your hand causes you to sin, cut it off! You would be better off to go into life paralyzed than to have two hands and be thrown into the fires of hell that never go out. 45-46If your foot causes you to sin, chop it off. You would be better off to go into life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into hell. 47 If your eye causes you to sin, get rid of it. You would be better off to go into God's kingdom with only one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell. 48 The worms there never die, and the fire never stops burning.
49Everyone must be salted with fire.
50 Salt is good. But if it no longer tastes like salt, how can it be made salty again? Have salt among you and live at peace with each other.
translation_text:
1O daa ta ma ta de-ba o we, “A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, nɔɔna balo zem na wo ywo-seeni to badaara bá te ye ba ta wo nɛ Wɛ paare dem na tu nɔɔna baŋa ne de dam to.”
Yezu yibia na leiri tei to
Matiyu 17:1-13; Luka 9:28-36
2Da yaredo déem ma ba ya kɛ. Yezu laam ma ja Piita ko woli de Jemsi de Jɔn pa ba tɔge daane ba vo ba di peo-kamunu yuu. Ba maa wora ba yerane mo. Ba na wora konto to, Yezu yibia ma leiri ba yiga ne. 3O gwaaro tem ma tiini te peere cha ye te nyeena. Te peere te gaale nabiinu na bá wane o zare o gwaaro pa te peere tei to. 4Elija de Moses ma pɔpɔ ba nwoŋi ba yiga ne, ye ba ŋɔɔne de Yezu.
5Piita laam ma ta de Yezu o we, “Berem tu, dé na wo ywo-seeni to, ko tiini ko lana ko pa debam. Nam pa dé pu vwoa yatɔ ywo-seeni, se nmo, de Moses, de Elija taa zoore da.” 6Foone déem zo-ba dedɛ. Konto ŋwaane mo o gare o ŋɔɔne konto dwoŋi.
7Kunkwoŋo laam ma ba ko li-ba. Ba ma ni kwora na ŋɔɔne ko wone ka we, “Amo bu-doa mo tento ye a swoi‑o lanyerane. Nam ta‑á cheigi-na o ni taane lanyerane.”
8Ba ma kwaane ba nii lela, ye ba daa wo nɛ nɔɔn-nɔɔno jei sem ne, ko ná dae Yezu yerane. 9Ba ma zaŋe peo kom yuu ne ba maa tua. Yezu laam ma kaane-ba we, ba yé ta kolo ba na nɛ to ba bere nɔɔn-nɔɔno, se ko taa nii maŋa kalo omo Nabiin-bu wom na wó bi toone wone to. 10Ba ma sɛ ye ba ŋɔɔne ba yerane ba bwɛ ba nii, ka-bi-toone-wone taane dem kuri mo bɛ.
11Ba laam ma bwei‑o ba we, “Wɛ nia zamesem tiina bam yeini ba tɛ ba we, Elija mo jege se o ba yiga, se Wɛ Dam Tu wom laam da kwaga. Ko ye chega mo naa vwa mo?” 12Yezu ma leiri-ba o we, “Ko ye chega mo. Elija jege se o da yiga o ba o kwɛ woŋo maama se Wɛ Dam Tu wom laam ba. Bɛ nam mo ye ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we, Nabiin-bu wom jege se o yaare dedɛ ye nɔɔna chuli‑o? 13Nam ta‑á yei-na we, Elija maŋe o ba, ye nɔɔna tiini ba bɛɛse‑o se ko yi ba boboŋa na lage tei to, ne ko na maŋe ko popone o ŋwaane Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne tei to.”
Yezu yɔɔre bu wodwoŋi
Matiyu 17:14-23; Luka 9:37-45
14Yezu de o nɔɔna batɔ bam laam ma jwoori ba vo ba yi o kwaga tɔgena babam tei. Ba ma na kɔgɔ dedɛ na gilimi-ba. Wɛ nia zamesem tiina badwonna maa wora ba mage ni-kantɔgɔ dedaane-ba. 15Nɔɔna bam maama na nɛ Yezu to, ko ke-ba yaau lanyerane. Ba ma duri ba vo o tei ba jɔɔne‑o. 16O ma bwei-ba o we, “Á wora á mage ni-kantɔgɔ bɛ baŋa ne mo?”
17Nɔɔno wodwoŋi maa wo kɔgɔ kom wone ye o leiri‑o o we, “Berem tu, a ya jaane a bu mo a ba nmo tei se n yɔɔre‑o. Chichira mo jege‑o ka daana pa o ware o ŋɔɔne. 18Maŋa maama, ka ná jaane‑o, ka yeini ka yigi‑o ka de tega ne mo. Lilei-puŋa nwoŋi o ni ne ye o done o yeila. O yera yam maama maa yeini ya ko. Tɔ. A ma lwoori nmo kwaga tɔgena bam se ba zeili chichira kam se ka yage‑o ye ba ware.”
19Yezu na nigi konto to, o ma ta o we, “Abam zem nɔɔna bam bere á ba jege wo-dedoa de amo. A nam wó tiini a dáane abam tei ne se ko vo ko maŋe yei ne mo? A nam wó ke tɛ mo a zuri a bochare de abam? Ja-na bu wom á ba.” 20Ba ma ja‑o ba vo o tei. Chichira kam na nɛ Yezu to, ka ma su bu wom pa o sa kɔɔro. O ma to tega ne ye o bibila. Lilei-puŋa ma nwoŋi o ni ne.
21Yezu ma bwei bu wom kwo o we, “Maŋa kɔ mo ka bobo ka ja‑o?” O ma leiri‑o we, “O biini ne mo. 22Kuni dedɛ chichira kam jaane‑o ka de mini wone, de na wone se ka chɔge‑o. Nmo ná wó wane n ke kolo na wó woli debam to, popo se n kwaane n duri debam yiniga.” 23Yezu ma ta‑o o we, “Nmo tage n we, amo ná wó wane. Wolo maama nam ná jege wo-dedoa de amo, kolokolo tera Wɛ na bá wane o ke o pa konto tu.” 24Bu wom kwo laam ma laare o we, “Amo seene a jege wo-dedoa de nmo. Nam woli-ne se a taa fɔge a jega.”
25Yezu ma na nɔn-kɔgɔ dedɛ na dura ko maa beene ba tei. O laam ma bage chichira kam ye o ta de-ka we, “Nmo wolo na pae nɔɔna jiri memaaro de zɔ-kɔro to, a ta de nmo se n yage bu wom yera n viiri, se n daa‑n yé jwoori n yaare‑o.” 26Yezu na tage konto to, chichira kam ma chwoosi ye ka tiini ka su bu wom pa o sa kɔɔro. Ka ma daare ka yage‑o. Ka na yage‑o to, bu wom laam nye de too mo. Nɔɔna dedɛ maa we, “O tege mo.” 27Yezu laam ma ja o jeŋa o pa o zaŋe wɛɛne ye o zega.
28Yezu ma jwoori o vo sɔŋɔ. O na zo to, o kwaga tɔgena bam ma vo o tei ba yerane ye ba bwei‑o ba we, “Bɛŋwaane mo debam ware dé zeili chichira kam?” 29O ma leiri-ba o we, “Chichira kanto dwoŋi zeilim chamma. Ko ná dae we á seene á yia á lwoori Wɛ, ko ya bá wane.”
30Ba déem ma yage jei sem konto ye ba vo ba tɔge Galili wo ba kɛ. Yezu maa ba lage se nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre ba jei, 31o na jege o kwaga tɔgena bam o tei ne ye o bere-ba to ŋwaane. O maa bere-ba o we, “Leile konto ba lage ba ja Nabiin-bu wom ba ke nɔɔna jeŋa ne, ye ba laam wó go‑o. Da yatɔ dɛ ne o maa wó jwoori o bi.” 32O kwaga tɔgena bam maa wo nigi o taane dem kuri, ye ba kɔre se ba bwei‑o ba nii.
Wɔ mo ye nɔn-kamunu Wɛ tei ne?
Matiyu 18:1-9; Luka 9:46-50; 17:1-2
33Ba ma vo ba yi Kaparenia. Ba ma vo sɔŋɔ. Ba na zo to, Yezu ma bwei o kwaga tɔgena bam o we, “Dé na wo chwoŋa ne dé maa beene to, á ya wora á mage ni-kantɔgɔ daane. Ko ye bɛ ŋo ŋwaane mo?” 34Ba ma chem. Ba ya na maa beene to, ba mage kantɔgɔ daane se ba nii, banto wone wɔ mo ye kamunu o dwoi maama. 35Yezu ma jeini tega ne. O ma bwoŋi o nɔɔna fuga-balei bam se ba ba o tei. O ma ta de-ba o we, “Wolo ná lage se o taa ye nɔɔna yiga tu, konto tu maŋe se o ji ba maama kwaga tu, se o taa toŋe o pa ba maama mo.”
36O ma ja bu-balaŋa o pa o zege ba maama tetare ne. O ma kwei‑o o ke o ja-kukworo ne. O ma ta de-ba o we, 37“Wolo maama na wó zuli bu-balwa banto dwoŋi dedoa lanyerane amo yere ŋwaane to zuli amo mo. Wolo nam ná zuli amo, ko dae amo yerane mo o ke konto, se ko ye o zuli Baŋa Wɛ wolo na toŋe-ne to de mo.”
38Jɔn ma ta de Yezu o we, “Berem tu, dé ya nɛ nɔɔno wodwoŋi o na tɔge nmo yere ŋwaane o zeili setaana nɔɔna tei ne. O nam na dae debam kɔgɔ kom nyem to, de ma ta ded‑o we, o yage, o daa yé taa ke konto.” 39Yezu ma leiri o we, “Á ya ba jege se á che‑o. Nɔɔno wolo maama na tɔge amo yere ŋwaane o ke wo-kenkagele to bá wane o pipiri lela o ŋɔɔne ta-balɔrɔ o pa-ne. 40Kolo ŋwaane wolo maama na ba chuli debam to ye debam nɔɔno mo. 41A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, nɔɔno wolo ná nɛ abam, ye o ná dɛ amo yere ŋwaane o pa abam na se á nyɔ, á na ye amo Yezu Krista nyem to ŋwaane, konto tu wó tiini o na nyɔɔre Wɛ tei ne mo.
42Ko ná ye balo na ke ba wo-dedoa de amo, ye ba ná maŋe ba muri ne bu-balwa tei, nɔɔno wolo ná pɛ ba dedoa tusi Wɛ chwoŋa wone, konto tu tiini o chɔge mo dedɛ. Ba ná jaane nɔɔno wom konto ba daare ba lei kandwɛ-kamunu o ba ne, ye ba ná de‑o naneo kom wone se o te, konto gare waarem delo kotu na jege se o na Wɛ tei ne to. 43Nmo jeŋa ná pae n tusa, se n gwoni-ka n yage. Nmo ná gɛ n jeŋa, ye n daare n na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne, konto gare nmo ta ná jege n jea maama ye n vo te-seŋa, mɛ na ye mini delo na bá fɔge de dwei to. [44Jei sem konto ne,
‘Toa wó taa mu ba yera ye ka fɔge ka bá te.
Mini wó taa di-ba ye de fɔge de bá dwei.’]
45Ko woli da, nmo naga ná pae n tusa, se n gwoni-ka n yage. Nmo ná ye gwana ye n na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne, konto gare nmo ta ná jege n nɛ sem maama ye ba laam de‑m ba yage te-seŋa ne. [46Jei sem konto ne,
‘Toa wó taa mu ba yera ye ka fɔge ka bá te.
Mini wó taa di-ba ye de fɔge de bá dwei.’]
47Nmo yi nam ná pae n tusa, se n guri-de n yage. Nmo ná ye yi-doa tu ye n vo n woli Wɛ paare dem wone, konto gare nmo ta ná jege yia yalei ye ba laam de‑m ba yage te-seŋa ne. 48Jei sem konto ne,
‘Toa wó taa mu ba yera ye ka fɔge ka bá te.
Mini wó taa di-ba ye de fɔge de bá dwei.’
49Nɔɔno maama jege se Wɛ kwei mini mo o ma faŋe‑o o nii, se o pa o bochare fɔge de kwɛ. 50Yɛ de lamma ye de wae de kwɛ wodiu. Yɛ ni nam ná ti, n daa‑n bá‑n wane n pa de jwoori de ja ni. Pa-na á wo taa ywomma da-ŋwaane, ne yɛ na pae wodiu ywomma tei to.”

english_text:
Teaching about Divorce
(Matthew 19.1-12; Luke 16.18)
1After Jesus left, he went to Judea and then on to the other side of the Jordan River. Once again large crowds came to him, and as usual, he taught them.
2Some Pharisees wanted to test Jesus. So they came up to him and asked if it was right for a man to divorce his wife. 3Jesus asked them, “What does the Law of Moses say about this?”
4 They answered, “Moses allows a man to write out divorce papers and send his wife away.”
5Jesus replied, “Moses gave you this law because you are so heartless. 6 But in the beginning God made a man and a woman. 7 That's why a man leaves his father and mother and gets married. 8He becomes like one person with his wife. Then they are no longer two people, but one. 9And no one should separate a couple that God has joined together.”
10When Jesus and his disciples were back in the house, they asked him about what he had said. 11 He told them, “A man who divorces his wife and marries someone else is unfaithful to his wife. 12A woman who divorces her husband and marries again is also unfaithful.”
Jesus Blesses Little Children
(Matthew 19.13-15; Luke 18.15-17)
13Some people brought their children to Jesus so he could bless them by placing his hands on them. But his disciples told the people to stop bothering him.
14When Jesus saw this, he became angry and said, “Let the children come to me! Don't try to stop them. People who are like these little children belong to the kingdom of God. 15 I promise you that you cannot get into God's kingdom, unless you accept it the way a child does.” 16Then Jesus took the children in his arms and blessed them by placing his hands on them.
A Rich Man
(Matthew 19.16-30; Luke 18.18-30)
17As Jesus was walking down a road, a man ran up to him. He knelt down, and asked, “Good teacher, what can I do to have eternal life?”
18Jesus replied, “Why do you call me good? Only God is good. 19 You know the commandments. ‘Do not murder. Be faithful in marriage. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about others. Do not cheat. Respect your father and mother.’ ”
20The man answered, “Teacher, I have obeyed all these commandments since I was a young man.”
21Jesus looked closely at the man. He liked him and said, “There's one thing you still need to do. Go sell everything you own. Give the money to the poor, and you will have riches in heaven. Then come with me.”
22When the man heard Jesus say this, he went away gloomy and sad because he was very rich.
23Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, “It's hard for rich people to get into God's kingdom!” 24The disciples were shocked to hear this. So Jesus told them again, “It's terribly hard to get into God's kingdom! 25In fact, it's easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to get into God's kingdom.”
26Jesus' disciples were even more amazed. They asked each other, “How can anyone ever be saved?”
27Jesus looked at them and said, “There are some things that people cannot do, but God can do anything.”
28Peter replied, “Remember, we left everything to be your followers!”
29Jesus told him:
You can be sure that anyone who gives up home or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or land for me and for the good news 30will be rewarded. In this world they will be given 100 times as many houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and pieces of land, though they will also be mistreated. And in the world to come, they will have eternal life. 31 But many who are now first will be last, and many who are now last will be first.
Jesus Again Tells about His Death
(Matthew 20.17-19; Luke 18.31-34)
32The disciples were confused as Jesus led them toward Jerusalem, and his other followers were afraid. Once again, Jesus took the twelve disciples aside and told them what was going to happen to him. He said:
33We are now on our way to Jerusalem where the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses. They will sentence him to death and hand him over to foreigners, 34who will make fun of him and spit on him. They will beat him and kill him. But three days later he will rise to life.
The Request of James and John
(Matthew 20.20-28)
35James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to Jesus and asked, “Teacher, will you do us a favor?”
36Jesus asked them what they wanted, 37and they answered, “When you come into your glory, please let one of us sit at your right side and the other at your left.”
38 Jesus told them, “You don't really know what you're asking! Are you able to drink from the cup that I must soon drink from or be baptized as I must be baptized?”
39“Yes, we are!” James and John answered.
Then Jesus replied, “You certainly will drink from the cup from which I must drink. And you will be baptized just as I must! 40But it isn't for me to say who will sit at my right side and at my left. This is for God to decide.”
41When the ten other disciples heard this, they were angry with James and John. 42 But Jesus called the disciples together and said:
You know that those foreigners who call themselves kings like to order their people around. And their great leaders have full power over the people they rule. 43 But don't act like them. If you want to be great, you must be the servant of all the others. 44And if you want to be first, you must be everyone's slave. 45 The Son of Man did not come to be a slave master, but a slave who will give his life to rescue many people.
Jesus Heals Blind Bartimaeus
(Matthew 20.29-34; Luke 18.35-43)
46Jesus and his disciples went to Jericho. And as they were leaving, they were followed by a large crowd. A blind beggar by the name of Bartimaeus son of Timaeus was sitting beside the road. 47When he heard that it was Jesus from Nazareth, he shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have pity on me!” 48Many people told the man to stop, but he shouted even louder, “Son of David, have pity on me!”
49Jesus stopped and said, “Call him over!”
They called out to the blind man and said, “Don't be afraid! Come on! He is calling for you.” 50The man threw off his coat as he jumped up and ran to Jesus.
51Jesus asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
The blind man answered, “Master, I want to see!”
52Jesus told him, “You may go. Your eyes are healed because of your faith.”
At once the man could see, and he went down the road with Jesus.
translation_text:
Kaane yagem
Matiyu 19:1-12; Luka 16:18
1Yezu laam ma zaŋe o yage jei sem konto ye o vo o yi Judea laŋa kadwoŋi. O ma vo o bɛ Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ dedwoŋi dem. Nɔn-kɔgɔ dedɛ daa ma ba ba gilimi‑o. O daa ma bere-ba Wɛ chega kam, ne o na yeini o ke tei to.
2 Farisi tiina badaara déem ma zaŋe ba vo o tei se ba maŋe o boboŋa ba nii. Ba ma bwei‑o ba we, “Nɔɔno jege chwoŋa se o yage o kaane na?” 3O ma jwoori o bwei-ba o we, “Moses déem pɛ abam ni se á ke tɛ mo?” 4Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Moses pɛ ni we nɔɔno jege chwoŋa se o popone tɔnɔ o pa o kaane se ko bere we o yage‑o.”
5Yezu ma ta-ba o we, “Moses nam popone konto o pa abam, á boboŋa na lira de o berem dem to ŋwaane mo. 6Boboa ne Wɛ na naane woŋo maama to, o ke nabiina se ba taa ye baara de kaana mo. 7Wɛ na ke-ba se ba taa ye konto dwoŋi to, nɔɔno ná di kaane, o jege se o pwɛ o tete o kwo de o nu tei ne, se o daare o ba o pa se o de o kaane wom tane daane. 8Konto wó pa ba laam ji nɔɔno dedoa. Ba daa maa dae nɔɔna balei, se ba ye ŋo dedoa mo. 9Wɛ na pɛ se ba kwaare daane to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa ba jege se o pɔɔre-ba daane.”
10Yezu de o kwaga tɔgena bam laam ma jwoori ba zo sɔŋɔ. Ba na zo to, ba ma bwei‑o o taane dem bwia. 11O ma ta de-ba o we, “Nɔɔno ná yage o kaane ye o daare o di kaane wodwoŋi, konto tu chɔge o kaane mo ye o keim dem de kabwoŋa ye bedwe. 12Kaane de ná ve o baro ye o vo o zo baro wodwoŋi, o de keim dem de bwoŋa ye bedwe mo.”
Bu-balwa maŋe de Wɛ paare dem
Matiyu 19:13-15; Luka 18:15-17
13Nɔɔna badwonna maa jaane bia ba tui Yezu tei se o daŋe o jea ba baŋa ne. O kwaga tɔgena bam ma zaŋe ba bwɛ-ba se ba yé taa ke konto. 14Yezu ma na ba na ke tei to. O bane ma zaŋe ye o ta de-ba o we, “Yage-na se bia bam taa tui a tei, se á yé zaŋe á che-ba. Kokuri Wɛ paare dem ye banto dwi nyem mo. 15Chega ŋwaane to, nɔɔno ná wo sɛ se Wɛ taa tei‑o ne bu-balaŋa tei, o bá na chwoŋa se o zo Wɛ woro kom wone.”
16Yezu na tage konto to, o laam ma kwei bia bam o ke o ja-kukworo ne. O ma daŋe o jea ba baŋa ne ye o daare o swɛ ba swolim.
Naduna wó wane ba na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne na?
Matiyu 19:16-30; Luka 18:18-30
17Yezu ma zaŋe o maa kɛa. Nɔɔno wodwoŋi ma duri o vo o yi o tei. O ma kuni dwoona o yiga ne ye o we, “Berem tu, n ye nɔn-ŋom. Nam bere-ne kolo amo na wó ke se a wane a na ŋwea kalo na ba jege kweelim Wɛ tei ne to.” 18Yezu ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo n tage we, a ye nɔn-ŋom? Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na ye nɔn-ŋom, ko ná dae Wɛ yerane. 19Nmo maŋe n yei Wɛ nia yam na bere kolo to. Yé go nɔɔn-nɔɔno. Yé zaŋe n ke bwoŋa. Yé zaŋe n ŋɔ. Yé fɔ vwa n pa n dwoŋi. Yé pini n dwoŋi. Ta‑n zuli n kwo de n nu.” 20Nɔɔno wom ma ta ded‑o o we, “Berem tu, ko zege amo biini ne mo amo maŋe a tɔge nia yanto maama.”
21Yezu ma nii‑o ye o jege o swono. O ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ko nam ta gɛ ŋo dedoa se n ke. Jwoori sɔŋɔ n kwei woŋo kolo maama n na jege to n yeigi, se n laam kwei sabu kom n ma n woli yiniga tiina. Konto wó pa se n jejegero tiini te puli Wɛ telaao ne. Nmo ná ke konto, se n laam ba n ta‑n tɔge-ne.” 22Nɔɔno wom na nigi konto to, o yiga ma nyɔne. O wo ma chɔge dedɛ, o jejegero tem na tiini te daga to ŋwaane. O ma yage Yezu tei ye o viiri.
23Yezu laam ma pipiri o nii o kwaga tɔgena bam seeni ye o ta de-ba o we, “Naduna ná lage ba zo Wɛ paare dem wone, ko wó taa tiini ko chana ko pa-ba.” 24O kwaga tɔgena bam na nigi konto to, ko ma so-ba. Yezu daa ta ma ta de-ba o we, “A bia bam, nɔɔno ná lage o zo Wɛ paare dem wone, ko wó taa tiini ko chana ko pa kotu. 25Nadum ná lage se o zo Wɛ woro kom wone, ko wó taa chana ko dwoi kone ná lage se de da gare-lwei bɔɔne de nwoŋi.”
26Yezu na tage konto to, ko ma tiini ko so o kwaga tɔgena bam dedɛ, ye ba tɛ daane ba we, “Ko ná ye konto, nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne.” 27Yezu ma nii-ba ye o we, “Nabiina tei ne mo ko bá wane ko ke. Wɛ nam wó pa ko ke. Wɛ wae ŋo maama o ke.”
28Piita laam ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nii. Debam yage dé woŋo maama mo ye dé daare dé tɔge nmo.” 29Yezu ma ta de ba maama o we, “A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, nɔɔno wolo maama ná tɔge amo ŋwaane de Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam ŋwaane o yage o sɔŋɔ, de o nu-bia, de o nu, de o kwo, de o bia, ko woli de o kare de, 30konto tu wó jwoori o jwoŋi kolo maama o na yage to se ko maŋe de kuni bi mo Wɛ tei ne. Zem da yam ne mo o wó jwoŋi sam, de nu-bia, de niina, de kare, ye o tɔge o na yaara o woli da. Ko daare maŋa kalo na wó ba to, konto tu wó na ŋwea kalo na ba jege kweelim Wɛ tei ne to. 31Ko daare balo na maŋe ba ye yiga tiina to dedɛ wó jwoori ba ji kwaga tiina. Balo de na maŋe ba ye kwaga tiina to wó ba ba ji yiga tiina Wɛ paare dem seeni.”
Yezu daa ŋɔɔne o toone taane
Matiyu 20:17-19; Luka 18:31-34
32Yezu de o nɔɔna bam maa wo chwoŋa ne ba maa vei Jerusalem. Yezu maa wo ba yiga ne o via. O kwaga tɔgena bam maa ye yaau. Nɔɔna balo de na tɔge ba kwaga to maa fomma. Yezu ma pɔɔre o nɔɔna fuga-balei bam kɔgɔ kom wone ye o ta o bere-ba kolo na lage ko ke‑o Jerusalem ne to. 33O maa we, “Ta‑á yei-na, dé na maa vei Jerusalem to, dáane mo ba laam wó ja amo Nabiin-bu wom ba ke Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam de ba zamesem tiina bam jeŋa ne. Nɔɔna bam konto maa wó di a taane se ko bere we a maŋe se a te mo. Ba laam wó kwei-ne ba ke dwi-gɛ tiina jeŋa ne. 34Banto wó ke amo ba mɔne, ye ba twe lileeru ba yage a yera ne. Ba maa wó kwei kaasa ba ma fere-ne, ye ba laam daare ba go-ne. Da yatɔ dɛ ne a maa wó jwoori a bi toone wone.”
Yezu chwoŋa kam tɔge yaara ŋwaane
Matiyu 20:20-28
35Jemsi de Jɔn na ye Zebedi bia bam to déem ma vo Yezu tei. Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Berem tu, dé tu nmo tei mo. Popo, ke woŋo kolo dé na lage to.” 36Yezu ma bwei-ba o we, “Á lage se a ke bɛ mo a pa abam?” 37Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Nmo ná tu n ba n di paare, se n pa debam balei jeini nmo tei ne, n jazem ne de n jagwia ne.”
38O ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam tete yeiri á na maŋe á lwoori kolo to. Abam wó wane á tɔge á zo yaara wo, ne amo na lage a ba a na yaara yalo to na? Á wó wane á te ne amo na lage a na toone delo to na?” 39Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ɛɛ, dé wó wane.”
Yezu laam ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam nam wó seene á tɔge á yaare amo yaara yam dwoŋi. 40Ko daare ko ná ye jeiŋa jei amo paare dem ne, amo ba jege chwoŋa se a kuri nɔɔna se ba jeini da. Wɛ nam maŋe o tiŋi jei sem konto se o pa balo na wó jeini da to.”
41O nɔɔna fuga bam na tu ba lɔre ba dwonna balei bam na lwoori kolo Yezu tei ne to, ba bane ma tiini de zaŋe de Jemsi de Jɔn. 42Yezu laam ma bwoŋi ba maama, ye o ta de-ba o we, “Abam maŋe á yei ko na ke tei de balo dwi-gɛ tiina na pae ba ye ba pwa to. Banto yeini ba jege ba nɔɔna ba bɛɛse mo, ye ba dedɛɛra di dam ba baŋa ne. 43Ko nam ná ye abam, ko ba jege se ko taa ye konto á tei ne. Kokuri abam wolo ná boŋe se o ji nɔn-kamunu á wone, konto tu mo jege se o ji tontoŋeno o pa abam. 44Wolo ná boŋe se o ji abam yiga tu, konto tu mo jege se o ji abam maama kabaa. 45Ko ná maŋe ko ye Nabiin-bu wom, amo wo tu se nɔɔna toŋe ba pa-ne. Amo nam tu se a toŋe a pa nabiina, se a daare a kwei a ŋwea a ma leini nɔɔna dedɛ ŋwea Wɛ tei ne.”
Yezu yɔɔre lilwei
Matiyu 20:29-34; Luka 18:35-43
46Yezu de o kwaga tɔgena bam ma vo ba yi teo kodwoŋi, ko yere mo Jeriko. Ba ma tɔge da ba nwoŋi ba maa kɛa. Ba na maa kɛ to, nɔn-kɔgɔ maa tɔge-ba. Nɔɔno wodwoŋi maa wora o na ye lilwei. O yere mo Batimayu, ko kuri mo Timayu bu. O maa jei chwoŋa kam ni ne o lwoora. 47O ma lɔre we ko ye Nazarete tu Yezu mo tɔge dáane o maa kɛa. O laam ma bobo se o laare baŋa baŋa o we, “Yezu, Pɛ David dwi tu, duri amo yiniga!” 48Nɔɔna dedɛ ma bwɛ‑o se o pu o ni. O laam ma tiini o laare dedɛ ye o we, “Pɛ David dwi tu, duri amo yiniga!”
49Yezu laam ma zege ye o ta we, ba bwoŋi‑o se o ba. Ba ma bwoŋi‑o ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Zuri n yera se n zaŋe wɛɛne. O bwoi‑m se n ba.”
50Lilwei wom ma le o gare-bwora o faŋe wɛɛne o vo o yi Yezu tei. 51Yezu ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo lage se a ke bɛ mo a pa nmo?” O ma leiri o we, “Berem tu, amo lage se a jwoori a taa nae mo.” 52Yezu ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nmo na ke n wo-dedoa de amo tei to mo pɛ se n na yazura. Nam vei sɔŋɔ.”
Yezu na tage konto bedwe baŋa ne to mo lilwei wom yia jwoori ya nae. O maa tɔge Yezu kwaga chwoŋa kam ne.

english_text:
Jesus Enters Jerusalem
(Matthew 21.1-11; Luke 19.28-40; John 12.12-19)
1Jesus and his disciples reached Bethphage and Bethany near the Mount of Olives. When they were getting close to Jerusalem, Jesus sent two of them on ahead. 2He told them, “Go into the next village. As soon as you enter it, you will find a young donkey that has never been ridden. Untie the donkey and bring it here. 3If anyone asks why you are doing this, say, ‘The Lord needs it and will soon bring it back.’ ”
4The disciples left and found the donkey tied near a door that faced the street. While they were untying it, 5some of the people standing there asked, “Why are you untying the donkey?” 6They told them what Jesus had said, and the people let them take it.
7The disciples led the donkey to Jesus. They put some of their clothes on its back, and Jesus got on. 8Many people spread clothes on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields.
9 In front of Jesus and behind him, people went along shouting,
“Hooray!
God bless the one who comes
in the name of the Lord!
10God bless the coming kingdom
of our ancestor David.
Hooray for God
in heaven above!”
11After Jesus had gone to Jerusalem, he went into the temple and looked around at everything. But since it was already late in the day, he went back to Bethany with the twelve disciples.
Jesus Puts a Curse on a Fig Tree
(Matthew 21.18,19)
12When Jesus and his disciples left Bethany the next morning, he was hungry. 13From a distance Jesus saw a fig tree covered with leaves, and he went to see if there were any figs on the tree. But there were none, because it wasn't the season for figs. 14So Jesus said to the tree, “Never again will anyone eat fruit from this tree!” The disciples heard him say this.
Jesus in the Temple
(Matthew 21.12-17; Luke 19.45-48; John 2.13-22)
15After Jesus and his disciples reached Jerusalem, he went into the temple and began chasing out everyone who was selling and buying. He turned over the tables of the moneychangers and the benches of those who were selling doves. 16Jesus would not let anyone carry things through the temple. 17 Then he taught the people and said, “The Scriptures say, ‘My house should be called a place of worship for all nations.’ But you have made it a place where robbers hide!”
18The chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses heard what Jesus said, and they started looking for a way to kill him. They were afraid of him, because the crowds were completely amazed at his teaching.
19That evening, Jesus and the disciples went outside the city.
A Lesson from the Fig Tree
(Matthew 21.20-22)
20As the disciples walked past the fig tree the next morning, they noticed that it was completely dried up, roots and all. 21Peter remembered what Jesus had said to the tree. Then Peter said, “Teacher, look! The tree you put a curse on has dried up.”
22Jesus told his disciples:
Have faith in God! 23 If you have faith in God and don't doubt, you can tell this mountain to get up and jump into the sea, and it will. 24Everything you ask for in prayer will be yours, if you only have faith.
25-26 Whenever you stand up to pray, you must forgive what others have done to you. Then your Father in heaven will forgive your sins.
A Question about Jesus' Authority
(Matthew 21.23-27; Luke 20.1-8)
27Jesus and his disciples returned to Jerusalem. And as he was walking through the temple, the chief priests, the nation's leaders, and the teachers of the Law of Moses came over to him. 28They asked, “What right do you have to do these things? Who gave you this authority?”
29Jesus answered, “I have just one question to ask you. If you answer it, I will tell you where I got the right to do these things. 30Who gave John the right to baptize? Was it God in heaven or merely some human being?”
31They thought it over and said to each other, “We can't say that God gave John this right. Jesus will ask us why we didn't believe John. 32On the other hand, these people think that John was a prophet. So we can't say it was merely some human who gave John the right to baptize.”
They were afraid of the crowd 33and told Jesus, “We don't know.”
Jesus replied, “Then I won't tell you who gave me the right to do what I do.”
translation_text:
Yezu zo Jerusalem teo wo
Matiyu 21:1-22; Luka 19:28-40, 45-48; Jɔn 12:12-19
1Yezu de o nɔɔna bam déem ma vo ba twɛ Jerusalem. Ba ma vo ba yi te-balwa balei, ba yera mo Bɛtefage de Bɛtania. Jei sem konto wo Olivi peo kom saŋa ne mo. Yezu ma le nɔɔna balei o kwaga tɔgena bam wone, 2ye o ta de-ba o we, “Véi-na á zo teo kolo na wo abam yiga ne to. Á ná zo teo kom wo, á wó na bona-pɔla na leigi da ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa ta wo diini ka baŋa. Véi-na á bwoli-ka á ja ba á pa-ne. 3Nɔɔno ná bwei abam we, ‘Bɛ mo ye á wora á ke konto?’ se á ta ded‑o we, ‘Ko ye dé Teiru wom mo lage-ka. O bá dáane ye o pa ka jwoori ka ba.’ ”
4Ba ma zaŋe ba vo se ba nii. Ba na yi teo kom to, ba ma seene ba na bona-pɔla chwoŋa kam ni ne. Ka leigi mo diga kadwoŋi ni ne. Ba ma vo ba bwoli-ka. 5Nɔɔna badwonna maa zege da. Ba ma ta de Yezu nɔɔna bam ba we, “Bɛ mo ye á lage á bwoli bona-pɔla kam?” 6Ba ma leiri-ba ne Yezu na maŋe o ta tei to. Nɔɔna bam ma sɛ.
7Ba ma kwei bona-pɔla kam ba ja vo ba yi Yezu tei. Ba laam ma le ba gwaaro ba daŋe ka baŋa ne. Yezu ma di ka baŋa, ye ba vei ba maa kɛa. 8Ba na maa kɛ to, nɔɔna dedɛ ma le ba gwaaro ba lware chwoŋa kam ni ne se Yezu tɔge te baŋa o kɛ. Nɔɔna badaara ma vo ba gwoni teeni nɛ de vɔɔro ba de chwoŋa kam ni ne se o tɔge te baŋa o kɛ. 9Nɔɔna balo na wo o yiga ne de o kwaga ne ba vei to maa laare ba tɛ ba we:
“Hozaana! Zula taa wo Wɛ tei ne!
Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ wolo na tu o yere ŋwaane to swolim.
10Wonto wó taa tei o nɔɔna,
nenɛɛne dé kwo David déem na jege paare tei to mo.
Wɛ wó swɛ o swolim.
Hozaana! Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de tia wɛyuu ne!”
11Yezu ma vo o zo Jerusalem teo kom wo. O ma vo o yi Wɛ diga kam o zo ka wo. O ma kare o nii woŋo maama na ye tei. Wɛ na lage de zo to, o ma jwoori o nwoŋi teo kom ne. O ma tɔge de o nɔɔna fuga-balei bam o vo Bɛtania.
12Tega na poore to, ba ma zaŋe Bɛtania ne se ba jwoori Jerusalem. Yezu kana maa wɔe. 13Ba na maa vei to, o ma tole o na kaporo na zege yiga yiga. Ko déem maŋe ko li de vɔɔro. O ma vo se o nii mɔɔro wora se o di na. O na yi to, o maa wo nɛ kolokolo se vɔɔro yerane, ko na wo yi ko leirim maŋa to ŋwaane. 14O laam ma ta de kaporo kom o we, “Wɛ wó pa se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa yé na mɔɔro nmo yuu ne o di.” O kwaga tɔgena bam ma ni o na tage kolo to.
15Ba ma vo ba yi Jerusalem. Yezu ma vo o zo Wɛ diga kam wo. O ma na nɔɔna na wora ka konkɔlɔ kom ne ba ke pipiu. O ma bobo se o zeili-ba se ba nwoŋi. O ma ja sabu-leinna bam tabollo tem o pipiri o pu tega ne pa se ba sabia bam jage. O ma daare o yigi yitunnu telo nɔɔna badwonna na jei da ba yeigi kunkwon-puura to o de tega ne. 16O maa wo sɛ se pipim-piina taa zeŋe ba zela ba tɔge konkɔlɔ kom wo ba kɛa. 17O ma bere nɔɔna bam o we, “Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we, ‘Ba wó taa bwoi amo sɔŋɔ kom we, wara-jei mo na zege dwi maama ŋwaane.’ Abam nam pɛ se ko ji ŋweena tigisim jei.”
18Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam de ba zamesem tiina bam ma ni Yezu na tage kolo to. Ba laam ma kare ba lage chwoŋa se ba wane ba go‑o. Ba ma kɔre foone ded‑o, nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama na ye yaau de o berem dem to ŋwaane.
19Tega na lage ka yi to, Yezu de o nɔɔna bam ma nwoŋi teo kom ne.
20Tega na poore to, ba maa vei ba maa kɛa. Ba ma na kaporo kom na koga, de ko bonno maama. 21Piita ma guli Yezu ya na tage tei to. O ma ta de Yezu o we, “Berem tu, nii kaporo kom nmo diim na sɔɔle n chɔge-ko to. Ko laam koga.” 22Yezu ma ta de-ba o we, “Fɔge-na á ke á wo-dedoa de Wɛ. 23Chega ŋwaane to, nmo ná tage de peo-kamunu konto we, ko gɔ ko vo ko to naneo kom wone, Wɛ wó pa ko ke. Nmo ná jege boŋem-dɛɔ we nmo na tage kolo to wó seene ko ke, ye n ba jege bobwea, Wɛ wó ke o pa‑m. 24Mo kokuri, ta‑á yei-na we, woŋo kolo maama á na wó lwoori Wɛ tei ne to, se á ta‑á jege boŋem-dɛɔ we á wó seene á na-ko. Konto to, Wɛ wó pa á jwoŋi-ko. 25Maŋa maama abam ná zega á ware Wɛ, ye taane ná wora abam de nɔɔno wodwoŋi laŋa ne, se á kwei á ma chɛ‑o. Á Kwo Wɛ laam wó wane o yage á wɛleera o ma chɛ abam. [ 26Ko daare abam ná wo sɛ se á yage nɔɔna wɛleera á ma chɛ-ba, á Kwo Wɛ de bá ke abam konto.]”
Yezu dam dem nwoŋi yei ne mo?
Matiyu 21:23-27; Luka 20:1-8
27Ba daa ma vo ba yi Jerusalem. Yezu ma vo o zo Wɛ diga kam wo. O maa kare ka wone o beera. Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam, de ba zamesem tiina bam, de ba nakwa bam ma vo o tei. 28Ba ma bwei‑o ba we, “Wɔ mo pɛ nmo chwoŋa se n ke wonnu telo maama n na ke to?” 29O ma leiri-ba o we, “Yage-na se a bwei abam taane dedwe se, á ná leiri-de á pa-ne, se a laam bere abam a na ke tei a jege chwoŋa to. 30A lage a bwei abam a nii, Jɔn na pɛ nɔɔna sɛɛm to, ko ye Wɛ mo pɛ‑o chwoŋa naa nabiina mo?”
31O na bwei-ba konto to, ba maa wora ba bane daane se ba nii ba na wó ta kolo to, ye ba we, “Debam ná leiri dé we, ko ye Wɛ mo, o laam wó bwei debam we, bɛ mo ye dé nam wo sɛ Jɔn taane dem? 32Ko daare, dé bá wane dé ta we ko ye nabiina mo pɛ‑o chwoŋa.” Ba tage konto kolo ŋwaane ba kɔre foone de nɔɔna bam, de ba maama na sɛ we Jɔn seene o ye Wɛ sampwora to. 33Konto ŋwaane ba ma leiri Yezu ba we, “Dé yeiri kotu.” Yezu laam ma ta de-ba o we, “Ko na ye konto to, amo de nam bá ta wolo na pɛ-ne chwoŋa se a taa toŋe to.”

english_text:
Renters of a Vineyard
(Matthew 21.33-46; Luke 20.9-19)
1 Jesus then told them this story:
A farmer once planted a vineyard. He built a wall around it and dug a pit to crush the grapes in. He also built a lookout tower. Then he rented out his vineyard and left the country.
2When it was harvest time, he sent a servant to get his share of the grapes. 3The renters grabbed the servant, beat him up, and sent him away without a thing.
4The owner sent another servant, but the renters beat him on the head and insulted him terribly. 5Then the man sent another servant, and they killed him. He kept sending servant after servant. They beat some of them and killed some.
6The owner had a son he loved very much. Finally, he sent his son to the renters because he thought they would respect him. 7But they said to themselves, “Someday he will own this vineyard. Let's kill him! That way we can have it all for ourselves.” 8So they grabbed the owner's son, killed him, and threw his body out of the vineyard.
9Jesus asked, “What do you think the owner of the vineyard will do? He will come and kill those renters and let someone else have his vineyard. 10 You surely know that the Scriptures say,
‘The stone the builders
tossed aside
is now the most important
stone of all.
11This is something
the Lord has done,
and it is amazing to us.’ ”
12The leaders knew that Jesus was really talking about them, and they wanted to arrest him. But because they were afraid of the crowd, they let him alone and left.
Paying Taxes
(Matthew 22.15-22; Luke 20.20-26)
13The Pharisees got together with Herod's followers. Then they sent some men to trick Jesus into saying something wrong. 14They went to him and said, “Teacher, we know that you are honest. You treat everyone with the same respect, no matter who they are. And you teach the truth about what God wants people to do. Tell us, should we pay taxes to the Emperor or not?”
15Jesus knew what they were up to, and he said, “Why are you trying to test me? Show me a coin!”
16They brought him a silver coin, and he asked, “Whose picture and name are on it?”
“The Emperor's,” they answered.
17Then Jesus told them, “Give the Emperor what belongs to him and give God what belongs to God.” The men were amazed at Jesus.
Life in the Future World
(Matthew 22.23-33; Luke 20.27-40)
18 The Sadducees did not believe that people would rise to life after death. So some of them came to Jesus and said:
19 Teacher, Moses wrote that if a married man dies and has no children, his brother should marry the widow. Their first son would then be thought of as the son of the dead brother. 20There were once seven brothers. The first one married, but died without having any children. 21The second brother married his brother's widow, and he also died without having children. The same thing happened to the third brother, 22and finally to all seven brothers. At last the woman died. 23When God raises people from death, whose wife will this woman be? After all, she had been married to all seven brothers.
24Jesus answered:
You are completely wrong! You don't know what the Scriptures teach. And you don't know anything about the power of God. 25When God raises people to life, they won't marry. They will be like the angels in heaven. 26 You surely know about people being raised to life. You know that in the story about Moses and the burning bush, God said, “I am the God worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” 27He isn't the God of the dead, but of the living. You Sadducees are all wrong.
The Most Important Commandment
(Matthew 22.34-40; Luke 10.25-28)
28 One of the teachers of the Law of Moses came up while Jesus and the Sadducees were arguing. When he heard Jesus give a good answer, he asked him, “What is the most important commandment?”
29 Jesus answered, “The most important one says: ‘People of Israel, you have only one Lord and God. 30You must love him with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength.’ 31 The second most important commandment says: ‘Love others as much as you love yourself.’ No other commandment is more important than these.”
32 The man replied, “Teacher, you are certainly right to say there is only one God. 33 It is also true that we must love God with all our heart, mind, and strength, and that we must love others as much as we love ourselves. These commandments are more important than all the sacrifices and offerings that we could possibly make.”
34When Jesus saw that the man had given a sensible answer, he told him, “You are not far from God's kingdom.” After this, no one dared ask Jesus any more questions.
About David's Son
(Matthew 22.41-46; Luke 20.41-44)
35As Jesus was teaching in the temple, he said, “How can the teachers of the Law of Moses say the Messiah will come from the family of King David? 36 The Holy Spirit led David to say,
‘The Lord said to my Lord:
Sit at my right side
until I make your enemies
into a footstool for you.’
37If David called the Messiah his Lord, how can the Messiah be his son?”
The large crowd enjoyed listening to Jesus teach.
Jesus Condemns the Pharisees and the Teachers of the Law of Moses
(Matthew 23.1-36; Luke 20.45-47)
38As Jesus was teaching, he said:
Guard against the teachers of the Law of Moses! They love to walk around in long robes and be greeted in the market. 39They like the front seats in the synagogues and the best seats at banquets. 40But they cheat widows out of their homes and pray long prayers just to show off. They will be punished most of all.
A Widow's Offering
(Luke 21.1-4)
41Jesus was sitting in the temple near the offering box and watching people put in their gifts. He noticed that many rich people were giving a lot of money. 42Finally, a poor widow came up and put in two coins worth only a few pennies. 43Jesus told his disciples to gather around him. Then he said:
I tell you that this poor widow has put in more than all the others. 44Everyone else gave what they didn't need. But she is very poor and gave everything she had. Now she doesn't have a cent to live on.
translation_text:
Nɔɔno de o gaare memaŋe
Matiyu 21:33-46; Luka 20:9-19
1Yezu daa ta ma maŋe memaŋe de-ba o we, “Nɔɔno wodwoŋi mo wora. O ma zaŋe o che gaare, ye o daare o jeiri Vini teeni de wone. O ma daare o ko gwoŋo te-dɛa jei ne se o ná gwori teeni bia bam, se o ke da o nɔ o ŋoke te nyoa bam. O ma daare o chwi da-pala se nɔɔno taa jei da o yere gaare dem. O na fɔge o che-de konto to, o laam ma kwei nɔɔna o yage da se ba taa toŋa, ye o daare o beeri o vo teo kodwoŋi. 2Tio-bia bam gworim maŋa ma yi. O ma toŋe o tontoŋeno se o vo vala bam tei se ba pɔɔre tio-bia bam ba pa‑o. 3Tontoŋeno wom na yi ba tei to, ba ma zi‑o ba mage. Ba ma daare ba pa o viiri de je-yaara. 4Nɔɔno wom daa ma toŋe o tontoŋeno wodwoŋi. O na yi ba tei to, ba ma mage o yuu ba kaare ye ba twe‑o dedɛ. 5O daa ta ma toŋe o tontoŋeno wodwoŋi o woli da. Wonto na yi ba tei to, ba ma mage‑o ba go. Nɔɔno wom ma jwoori o toŋe o nɔɔna dedɛ. Vala bam ma mage ba badwonna. Ba ma go badwonna.
6Ko na ti to, ko daare nɔɔno dedoa yerane mo. Wonto ye o bu mo. O maa jege o swono dedɛ. O ma toŋe‑o ba tei ne o kweeli, ye o boŋe we, ba wó nege wonto. 7Vala bam nam na nɛ‑o to, ba ma bane daane ba we, ‘Mo gaare dem tu bu-kwea kam, ye wonto mo lage o ba o taa tei o kwo wom wonnu. Nam pa-na se dé go‑o, se dé daare dé taa tei o wonnu tem.’ 8Ba laam ma ja‑o ba go, ye ba vaŋe‑o ba ja nwoŋi gaare dem ne ba yage.
9Tɔ. Gaare dem tu wom laam wó ke vala bam konto bɛ mo? O jege se o ba o go-ba, se o daare gaare dem o kwei o pa nɔɔna badwonna se ba taa nii-de. 10Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
‘Kandwɛ delo lɔra na ve to
laam mo jwoori de ba de ji kandwɛ delo na pae diga kam dana to.
11Konto ye Baŋa Wɛ keim mo.
Ko maa ye wo-kenkagele ko pa debam.’
Abam nam maŋe á wo gage konto na?”
12Juu tiina yiga tiina bam na nigi konto to, ba ma lɔre we o maŋe memaŋe dem banto ŋwaane mo. Konto to, ba ma kwaane ba lage chwoŋa se ba ja‑o. Ba ma ware, ba na kɔre foone de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom to ŋwaane. Ba ma yage‑o ye ba daare ba viiri.
Lampwoo ŋweem
Matiyu 22:15-22; Luka 20:20-26
13Juu tiina bam déem ma le Farisi tiina badwonna de Pɛ Herodi kwaga nɔɔna badwonna se ba vo Yezu tei. Ba maa lage se ba pa o ŋɔɔne o tusi se ba wane ba ja‑o. 14Ba ma yi o tei ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Berem tu, dé yei we nmo ye chega tu mo. Nmo yiga tera de nɔɔna na boŋe kolo ba pa nmo to, ye n ta ba pɔɔre nɔɔna daane de n na ke-ba tei to. Nmo nam yeini n bere nɔɔna Wɛ chwoŋa chekke. Dé lage dé bwei dé nii, debam Juu tiina ná ŋwe lampwoo dé pa logo kom Pa-faro wom, ko chɔge debam chullu na? Dé wó ŋwe naa dé bá ŋwe?”
15Yezu maŋe o yei ba na ye pipiri-nyena tei to. O ma ta de-ba o we, “Bɛ nam mo ye á lage se á ja-ne? Nam bere-ne sabu-dale se a nii.” 16Ba ma le sabu-dale dem ba bere‑o. O ma nii ye o bwei-ba o we, “Wɔ nyenyego de o yere mo ba sare ba yage de baŋa ne?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ko ye Pa-faro wom mo.” 17Yezu laam ma ta de-ba o we, “Ko lamma. Á nam ta‑á ŋwe kolo na ye Pa-faro wom nyem to á pa‑o, se á daare á ta‑á pae Wɛ kolo de na ye o nyem to.”
O na leiri-ba konto to, ko ma so-ba dedɛ.
Wɛ telaao ŋwea na wó taa ye tei to
Matiyu 22:23-33; Luka 20:27-40
18Saduka tiina badwonna déem ma zaŋe ba vo Yezu tei. Banto mo bere we, nɔɔno ná tega, o daa bá jwoori o bi. 19Ba ma vo ba ta de Yezu ba we, “Berem tu, Moses déem na popone kolo o tiŋi o pa debam to, o bere we, nɔɔno zembaaro ná tega ye o daare kaane, ba ná wo loge bia, too wom nyaane mo jege se o di kaane wom se ba wane ba lo bia zembaaro wom ŋwaane. 20Tɔ. Nu-bia barepɛ ya mo wora. Ba nakwe wom ma di kaane. Kaane wom ma te o daare‑o ye o wo loge bu. 21Wolo na saŋe to laam ma di kadeim dem. O de ma te o daare kaane wom ye bu tera. Ko ma ke batɔ tu wom bedwe mo. 22Ba maama barepɛ di kaane wom, ye ba wo loge bia. Ba maama na tege to, kaane wom de laam ma te. 23Ba maama barepɛ na di kaane wom to, ba laam ná tu ba bi toone wone, banto wɔ mo wó taa tei kaane wom?”
24Yezu ma leiri-ba o we, “Abam tiini á tusi mo. Abam maŋe á wo lɔre Wɛ tɔn-dwoŋo kom berem dem, ye á ta yeiri Wɛ dam dem na ye tei to. Ko dae konto na? 25Nɔɔna ná tu ba bi toone wone, banto lage ba taa nye de Wɛ malese sem na ye tei to mo, ye ba ba di kaana, naa ba zo banna de. 26Ko nam ná ye twa na wó bi toone wone tei to, Moses na popone kolo o tiŋi to bere we nɔɔna wó seene ba bi. Abam maŋe á wo gage kolo Wɛ na tage de Moses o na veere o tete sabare wone maŋa kalo to na? Wɛ déem tage de Moses o we, ‘Amo ye Abaraham Wɛ, de Izaak Wɛ, de Jakob Wɛ mo.’ 27Ko bere we banto daa ta jege ŋwea mo o tei ne, kolo ŋwaane Baŋa Wɛ ye ŋwea tiina nyem mo se o dae twa nyem. Mo kokuri, á tiini á tusi de á na boŋe tei to.”
Wɛ nia yam wone dɔ mo dana de dwoi maama?
Matiyu 22:34-40
28Ba na wora ba ŋɔɔne daane konto to, Wɛ nia yam zamesem tu wodwoŋi ma ba ba tei. O ma ni ba taane dem. O ma lɔre we Yezu tiini o kwaane de o na leiri Saduka tiina bam tei to. O laam ma bwei Yezu o we, “Wɛ nia yam maama wone dɔ mo dana de dwoi?” 29Yezu ma leiri‑o o we, “Wɛ ni delo na ye wo-chɛɔ de dwoi maama to mo tento: ‘Isarele tiina bam, cheigi-na. Dé Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ ye debam Teiru, ko ye wonto yerane. 30Ta‑n swoi n tu Baŋa Wɛ wom de n bochare maama, de n wo maama, de n boboŋa maama, de n dam maama.’ 31Wɛ ni delo na saŋe to mo tento: ‘Ta‑n swoi n dwoŋi se ko maŋe de n na swoi n tete tei to.’ Wɛ ni dedwoŋi daa tera de na dana de dwoi nia yalei yam konto.”
32Wɛ nia yam zamesem tu wom ma ta de Yezu o we, “Berem tu, n tage chega. Nmo na tage we Wɛ dedoa yerane mo wora ye o dwoŋi tera to, ko ye chega mo. 33Ko maŋe se dé taa swoi‑o de dé wo maama, de dé boboŋa maama, de dé dam maama, ye dé daare dé taa swoi dé dwonna se ko maŋe de dé tete. Dé ná ke konto, ko bere we dé ke lanyerane ko dwoni dé ná ke zwɛɛm kaanem naa kaanem dwi delo maama dé pa Wɛ.”
34Yezu ma lɔre we o leiri taane dem de boboŋ-dɛɛra. O laam ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ko daare fenfee yerane se n zo Wɛ paare dem wone.”
Ko maa zege maŋa kam konto ne nɔɔna maama maa kɔre se ba daa bwei‑o taane.
Yezu bere nɔɔna Wɛ diga kam wone
Matiyu 22:4-46; 23:1-36; Luka 20:41-47; 21:1-4
35Yezu déem maa wo Wɛ diga kam konkɔlɔ kom ne o bere nɔɔna, ye o ta o we, “Wɛ ni-dwoora zamesem tiina bam yeini ba bere we, Wɛ Dam Tu Krista ye Pɛ David dwi tu mo. Ko nam wó wane ko taa ye konto na? 36Wɛ Sin-laao kom nam pɛ se David tete ta o we,
‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ tage de amo Teiru wom o we:
Ba n jeini amo jazem seeni
se a laam wane nmo dona bam maama
a ke nmo dam kuri ne se n ta‑n tei-ba.’
37David tete na seene o bwoŋi Wɛ Dam Tu wom we, o Teiru to, dé nam wó ke tɛ mo ye dé daa ta bwoi‑o we David dwi tu?”
Yezu na bere Wɛ chega kam tei to ma pa se nɔn-kɔgɔ kolo na jei ba cheigi to wo pwoli dedɛ.
38O daa ta ma bere-ba o we, “Ta‑á cho-na á tete de Wɛ nia zamesem tiina bam. Banto swoi se ba zo gare-dedwaaro se ba taa beera ye nɔɔna nii-ba. Ba ná vei yaga, ba lage se nɔɔna maama taa tui ba zuli-ba. 39Ba ná yeini ba zo ba jeerim di sem, ba wó taa lage jei-kamunu mo se ba jeini yiga ne. Ba ná vei nɔɔno sɔŋɔ se ba di kuri, ko ye jei-laao jeiga ne mo ba lage se ba jeini da. 40Ba maa yeini ba gane kadeina ba jwoŋi wonnu ba tei ne. Ba maa bere ba tete de ba na tiini ba ware Wɛ tei to. Konto ŋwaane Wɛ wó tiini o waare-ba dedɛ.”
41Yezu ma vo o jeini tega ne Wɛ diga kam wone, jeiga kalo Wɛ pɛɛra dakaa kam na wora to. O maa jei o nii nɔɔna bam na vei ba de ba sabia ka wone tei to. Naduna dedɛ ma ba ba de sabu-fɔrɔ ba yage da. 42Kadeim wodwoŋi laam ma tɔge da, o na ye yiniga tu. O ma ja sabu-dala-balɛ selei o vo o de da. Ko maa ye sabu fenfee yerane mo. 43Yezu na nɛ to, o ma bwoŋi o kwaga tɔgena bam se ba ba o tei, ye o ta o we, “A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, kadeim wonto de sabu ko dwoi nɔɔna balo maama na de da to. 44Banto maama le ba sabu-daara wone mo ba pa Wɛ. Kadeim wom nam na ye yiniga tu to, o ma kwei woŋo kolo maama o na jege se o ma yeigi o ni-wodiu to o de da.”

english_text:
The Temple Will Be Destroyed
(Matthew 24.1,2; Luke 21.5,6)
1As Jesus was leaving the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, look at these beautiful stones and wonderful buildings!”
2Jesus replied, “Do you see these huge buildings? They will certainly be torn down! Not one stone will be left in place.”
Warning about Trouble
(Matthew 24.3-14; Luke 21.7-19)
3Later, as Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives across from the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew came to him in private. 4 They asked, “When will these things happen? What will be the sign that they are about to take place?”
5Jesus answered:
Watch out and don't let anyone fool you! 6Many will come and claim to be me. They will use my name and fool many people.
7When you hear about wars and threats of wars, don't be afraid. These things will have to happen first, but that isn't the end. 8Nations and kingdoms will go to war against each other. There will be earthquakes in many places, and people will starve to death. But this is just the beginning of troubles.
9 Be on your guard! You will be taken to courts and beaten with whips in their synagogues. And because of me, you will have to stand before rulers and kings to tell about your faith. 10But before the end comes, the good news must be preached to all nations.
11When you are arrested, don't worry about what you will say. You will be given the right words when the time comes. But you will not really be the ones speaking. Your words will come from the Holy Spirit.
12Brothers and sisters will betray each other and have each other put to death. Parents will betray their own children, and children will turn against their parents and have them killed. 13 Everyone will hate you because of me. But if you keep on being faithful right to the end, you will be saved.
The Horrible Thing
(Matthew 24.15-21; Luke 21.20-24)
14 Someday you will see that “Horrible Thing” where it should not be. Everyone who reads this must try to understand! If you are living in Judea at that time, run to the mountains. 15 If you are on the roof of your house, don't go inside to get anything. 16If you are out in the field, don't go back for your coat. 17It will be an awful time for women who are expecting babies or nursing young children. 18Pray that it won't happen in winter. 19 This will be the worst time of suffering since God created the world, and nothing this terrible will ever happen again. 20If the Lord doesn't make the time shorter, no one will be left alive. But because of his chosen and special ones, he will make the time shorter.
21If someone should say, “Here is the Messiah!” or “There he is!” don't believe it. 22False messiahs and false prophets will come and work miracles and signs. They will even try to fool God's chosen ones. 23But be on your guard! That's why I am telling you these things now.
When the Son of Man Appears
(Matthew 24.29-31; Luke 21.25-28)
24 In those days, right after this time of suffering,
“The sun will become dark,
and the moon
will no longer shine.
25 The stars will fall,
and the powers in the sky
will be shaken.”
26 Then the Son of Man will be seen coming in the clouds with great power and glory. 27He will send his angels to gather his chosen ones from all over the earth.
A Lesson from a Fig Tree
(Matthew 24.32-35; Luke 21.29-33)
28Learn a lesson from a fig tree. When its branches sprout and start putting out leaves, you know summer is near. 29So when you see all these things happening, you will know that the time has almost come. 30You can be sure that some of the people of this generation will still be alive when all this happens. 31The sky and the earth will not last forever, but my words will.
No One Knows the Day or Time
(Matthew 24.36-44)
32 No one knows the day or the time. The angels in heaven don't know, and the Son himself doesn't know. Only the Father knows. 33So watch out and be ready! You don't know when the time will come. 34 It is like what happens when a man goes away for a while and places his servants in charge of everything. He tells each of them what to do, and he orders the guard to keep alert. 35So be alert! You don't know when the master of the house will come back. It could be in the evening or at midnight or before dawn or in the morning. 36But if he comes suddenly, don't let him find you asleep. 37I tell everyone just what I have told you. Be alert!
translation_text:
Lɛɛro telo na wó ba logo baŋa to
Matiyu 24:1-28; Luka 21:5-24
1Yezu laam ma zaŋe se o nwoŋi Wɛ diga kam wone. O na maa kɛ to, o kwaga tɔgena bam dedoa ma ta ded‑o o we, “Berem tu, nii kandwa yanto ba na mɛ ba lɔ diga kam to na lana tei. Nii ka lɔɔm dem na dana tei to.” 2Yezu ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo seene n nae diga kam na daga tei to na? Ka maama nam wó ba ka to ka saare tega ne. Kandwɛ daa bá daare de dwoŋi baŋa ne.”
3Yezu déem ma vo o jeini Olivi peo kom yuu ne. Wɛ diga kam maa wo o yiga ne yiga yiga. O na jei konto to, Piita de Jemsi de Jɔn de Anduru yerane ma vo o tei, ye ba bwei‑o ba we, 4“Maŋa kɔ mo wonnu tento lage te ke ye Wɛ diga kam chɔge konto? Bɛ mo lage ko ke maana ko pa debam se dé lɔre we wonnu tento maama lage te ji chega?”
5Yezu ma leiri-ba o we, “Fɔge-na á che á tete, se á yé pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno gane abam. 6Nɔɔna dedɛ wó ba abam tei ba ma amo yere ba ta de abam we, banto dedoa dedoa mo ye amo, Wɛ Dam Tu wom. Konto dwoŋi mo ba wó gane nɔɔna dedɛ. 7Á wó ba á na tigura na wora abam jei sem ne, ye á kwori á ni ka ŋwa teene dedwonna ne. Á nam ná lɔre konto, se á yé pa lwia taa jege abam. Wonnu tem konto jege se te ke mo, se ko dae we ko yi logo tiim mo. 8Logo baŋa dwi tiina wó zaŋe ba ke jara de ba dwonna dwi-gɛ tiina, ye teo de ko dwoŋi teo wó zaŋe te mage jara. Tega maa wó ziziŋi jei sedwonna ne, ye kana de wó ba ka taa wora jei dedɛ ne. Yaara yam konto maama nam nye de kaane na bobo se o taa wɔe puga, ye cham daa ta wo kwaga ne to mo.
9Á fɔge á che á tete. Nɔɔna wó ja abam ba vo ba saŋe nakwa tei ne. Ba ta wó ja abam ba fere ba jeerim di sem wone. Abam nam na tɔge amo to, ba wó ja abam ba vo ba saŋe dedɛɛra de pwa tei ne. Konto mo á wó na chwoŋa se á bere-ba Wɛ chega kam. 10Ko nam fe mo se ba da yiga ba tɔɔle Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam ba bere logo baŋa dwi tiina maama, se ko lwoori wonnu maama kweelim. 11Maŋa maama ba ná jaane abam ba vo ba saŋe ba nakwa yiga ne, á yé ta‑á jege lwia de á na wó ta kolo to. Abam na wó ba á zege ba yiga ne maŋa kalo to, se á laam ŋɔɔne botare selo Wɛ na wó pa abam to. Ko bá taa ye abam tete taane, se ko ye Wɛ Sin-laao kom mo wó pa á ŋɔɔne. 12Nɔɔna badwonna wó ja ba tete chorro ba ke nɔɔna jeŋa ne se ba go-ba. Kwoa de wó ke ba bia konto dwoŋi. Bia de wó zaŋe ba tiina baŋa ne ye ba pa ba ja-ba ba go. 13Nɔɔna maama wó taa chuli abam, á na ye amo nyem to ŋwaane. Wolo maama nam ná tiini o jege pu-dɛa se ko vo ko kweeli, Wɛ wó jwoŋi konto tu ŋwea.
14Abam nam wó ba á na wo-zɔɔne delo na chɔge Wɛ yere to na wó ba ko zege jei selo na wo maŋe se ko taa wora to ne.” A tɛ abam wolo ná gaga, se n kwaane n ni ko kuri lanyerane.
“Abam ná nɛ wo-lɔŋɔ kom konto, se abam balo na zoore Judea ne to ke lela á nwoŋi á duri á vo peero jei á seigi da. 15Nɔɔno nam ná wo nayuu ne, se o yé tu o zo diga wo se o kwaleme o zela o ja nwoŋi. 16Nɔɔno wolo nam ná wo kara ne, se o daa yé jwoori sɔŋɔ se o kwei o gare-laao o zo. 17Kanto maŋa kam ne ko wó tiini ko taa ye lɛɛro kaana balo na jege pwi to tei ne, de balo na jege bia ye ba ŋɔge yele to tei ne. 18Nam ta‑á lwoori-na Wɛ se cham dem konto yé ba doa nenem maŋa ne. 19Kokuri yaara yalo na lage ya ba da yanto ni ne to wó taa tiini ya chamma ya dwoi yalo na maŋe ya ke boboa ne ye Wɛ ke logo se ko ba ko yi zem to. Yanto nam ná kea, ya dwoŋi daa tera ya na wó ba konto dwoŋi. 20Baŋa Wɛ ya ná wo pɛ se yaara yam da yam tiri, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ya bá wori. Ko nam ye Wɛ tete nɔɔna balo o na kuri to ŋwaane mo o lage o pa se yaara yam da yam tiri.
21Kanto maŋa kam ne, nɔɔno wolo maama ná tage de abam o we, ‘Nii Wɛ Dam Tu Krista wom, o wo ywo-seeni’, se á yé sɛ konto tu. 22Nɔɔna badaara wó zaŋe ba bere we ba ye Wɛ Dam Tu Krista wom ye ba dae, ye badwonna de bere we banto mo ye Wɛ sampwori ye ba dae. Ba maa wó ke wo-kenkagela de maana, ye chwoŋa ya ná wora, yanto ya wó wane ya soge Wɛ tete nɔɔna balo o na kuri to. 23Ta‑á cho-na á tete. Amo wuuri a ta a bere abam wonnu tem maama mo ye te maŋa kam ta wo yi.
Nabiin-bu wom wó pɔpɔ o ba logo baŋa
Matiyu 24:29-44; Luka 21:25-36
24Yaara yam konto ná ke ya ti da yanto wone,
‘Wea kam laam wó ji nazwono tim-tim.
Chana kam de daa bá fuŋi pwooni.
25Chalechwe sem de wó kwori wɛyuu ne se to,
ye wɛ-baŋa de wó ziziŋi pa se ko wonnu maama leiri.’
26Maŋa kam konto ne nɔɔna wó na Nabiin-bu wom na maa beene logo baŋa to. O wó taa wo kunkwonnu baŋa ne o beena de dam, ye nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ tiini ko wo o tei ne. 27O laam wó pa se o malese sem nwoŋi se ba se zege logo baŋa dɛ sena sem ne se la o nɔɔna balo Wɛ na kuri tega baŋa de wɛyuu jei maama ne to se ke daane.
28Nam maane-na á nii kaporo na ye tei to. Konto ná yeini ko wora ko kwi vɔɔro, á yeini á lɔre we ko twɛ yadɛ maŋa mo. 29Ko maa ye bedwe mo de á ná nɛ wonnu telo amo na tage a bere abam to ná wora te ke, se á lɔre we maŋa kam laam twɛ ka ti mo. 30A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, wonnu tem konto maama wó ba te ke ye abam dwi dem ta wo ti. 31Wɛyuu de tega baŋa maama wó ba te jei, ye amo taane dem ta wó taa jege chega se ko taa vei wuu.
32Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam yeiri dɛ delo Nabiin-bu wom na lage o jwoori o ba to, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno yeiri dɛ dem wone maŋa kam o na wó ba to, ko ná maŋe ko ye Wɛ malese sem naa o Bu wom tete de. Ko nam ye amo Kwo Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo yei. 33Á ta‑á fɔge á cho á tete, se á yeiri maŋa kam ko na wó ke to. 34Ko na wó taa ye tei to, ko nye de sɔŋɔ tu na nwoŋi se o beeri o vo yiga yiga tei to. O ma pa o tontoŋena bam ni se ba taa nii o sɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne. O ma pa ba maama dedoa dedoa ba totoŋe. O ma ta de ba dedoa se o taa wo manchwoŋo ni ne o fɔge o nia. 35Abam de jege se á fɔge á ta‑á nii konto dwoŋi mo. Á yeiri maŋa kalo sɔŋɔ tu wom na wó jwoori o ba to. O nam wó wane o ba dedaan-ni ne, naa tete kokoro ne, naa te-pora ni ne, naa wɛ-puli maŋa ne. 36Konto to, o ná pɔpɔ o ba lela, á yé pa se o ba o peere abam de á tigi á dɔa. 37Amo tɛ de abam de nɔɔna maama we, á jege se á ta‑á cho á tete mo.”

english_text:
A Plot To Kill Jesus
(Matthew 26.1-5; Luke 22.1,2; John 11.45-53)
1 It was now two days before Passover and the Festival of Thin Bread. The chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses were planning how they could sneak around and have Jesus arrested and put to death. 2They were saying, “We must not do it during the festival, because the people will riot.”
At Bethany
(Matthew 26.6-13; John 12.1-8)
3 Jesus was eating in Bethany at the home of Simon, who once had leprosy, when a woman came in with a very expensive bottle of sweet-smelling perfume. After breaking it open, she poured the perfume on Jesus' head. 4This made some of the guests angry, and they complained, “Why such a waste? 5We could have sold this perfume for more than 300 silver coins and given the money to the poor!” So they started saying cruel things to the woman.
6But Jesus said:
Leave her alone! Why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful thing for me. 7 You will always have the poor with you. And whenever you want to, you can give to them. But you won't always have me here with you. 8She has done all she could by pouring perfume on my body to prepare it for burial. 9You may be sure that wherever the good news is told all over the world, people will remember what she has done. And they will tell others.
Judas and the Chief Priests
(Matthew 26.14-16; Luke 22.3-6)
10Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve disciples. He went to the chief priests and offered to help them arrest Jesus. 11They were glad to hear this, and they promised to pay him. So Judas started looking for a good chance to betray Jesus.
Jesus Eats with His Disciples
(Matthew 26.17-25; Luke 22.7-14,21-23; John 13.21-30)
12It was the first day of the Festival of Thin Bread, and the Passover lambs were being killed. Jesus' disciples asked him, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal?”
13Jesus said to two of the disciples, “Go into the city, where you will meet a man carrying a jar of water. Follow him, 14and when he goes into a house, say to the owner, ‘Our teacher wants to know if you have a room where he can eat the Passover meal with his disciples.’ 15The owner will take you upstairs and show you a large room furnished and ready for you to use. Prepare the meal there.”
16The two disciples went into the city and found everything just as Jesus had told them. So they prepared the Passover meal.
17-18 While Jesus and the twelve disciples were eating together that evening, he said, “The one who will betray me is now eating with me.”
19This made the disciples sad, and one after another they said to Jesus, “You surely don't mean me!”
20He answered, “It is one of you twelve men who is eating from this dish with me. 21The Son of Man will die, just as the Scriptures say. But it is going to be terrible for the one who betrays me. That man would be better off if he had never been born.”
The Lord's Supper
(Matthew 26.26-30; Luke 22.14-23; 1 Corinthians 11.23-25)
22During the meal Jesus took some bread in his hands. He blessed the bread and broke it. Then he gave it to his disciples and said, “Take this. It is my body.”
23Jesus picked up a cup of wine and gave thanks to God. He gave it to his disciples, and they all drank some. 24 Then he said, “This is my blood, which is poured out for many people, and with it God makes his agreement. 25From now on I will not drink any wine, until I drink new wine in God's kingdom.” 26Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.
Peter's Promise
(Matthew 26.31-35; Luke 22.31-34; John 13.36-38)
27 Jesus said to his disciples, “All of you will reject me, as the Scriptures say,
‘I will strike down
the shepherd,
and the sheep
will be scattered.’
28 But after I am raised to life, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
29Peter spoke up, “Even if all the others reject you, I never will!”
30Jesus replied, “This very night before a rooster crows twice, you will say three times that you don't know me.”
31But Peter was so sure of himself that he said, “Even if I have to die with you, I will never say I don't know you!”
All the others said the same thing.
Jesus Prays
(Matthew 26.36-46; Luke 22.39-46)
32Jesus went with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and he told them, “Sit here while I pray.”
33Jesus took along Peter, James, and John. He was sad and troubled and 34told them, “I am so sad that I feel as if I am dying. Stay here and keep awake with me.”
35-36Jesus walked on a little way. Then he knelt down on the ground and prayed, “Father, if it is possible, don't let this happen to me! Father, you can do anything. Don't make me suffer by drinking from this cup. But do what you want, and not what I want.”
37When Jesus came back and found the disciples sleeping, he said to Simon Peter, “Are you asleep? Can't you stay awake for just one hour? 38Stay awake and pray that you won't be tested. You want to do what is right, but you are weak.”
39Jesus went back and prayed the same prayer. 40But when he returned to the disciples, he found them sleeping again. They simply could not keep their eyes open, and they did not know what to say.
41When Jesus returned to the disciples the third time, he said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough of this! The time has come for the Son of Man to be handed over to sinners. 42Get up! Let's go. The one who will betray me is already here.”
Jesus Is Arrested
(Matthew 26.47-56; Luke 22.47-53; John 18.3-12)
43Jesus was still speaking, when Judas the betrayer came up. He was one of the twelve disciples, and a mob of men armed with swords and clubs were with him. They had been sent by the chief priests, the nation's leaders, and the teachers of the Law of Moses. 44Judas had told them ahead of time, “Arrest the man I greet with a kiss. Tie him up tight and lead him away.”
45Judas walked right up to Jesus and said, “Teacher!” Then Judas kissed him, 46and the men grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
47Someone standing there pulled out a sword. He struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
48Jesus said to the mob, “Why do you come with swords and clubs to arrest me like a criminal? 49 Day after day I was with you and taught in the temple, and you didn't arrest me. But what the Scriptures say must come true.”
50All of Jesus' disciples ran off and left him. 51One of them was a young man who was wearing only a linen cloth. And when the men grabbed him, 52he left the cloth behind and ran away naked.
Jesus Is Questioned by the Council
(Matthew 26.57-68; Luke 22.54,55,63-71; John 18.13,14,19-24)
53Jesus was led off to the high priest. Then the chief priests, the nation's leaders, and the teachers of the Law of Moses all met together. 54Peter had followed at a distance, and when he reached the courtyard of the high priest's house, he sat down with the guards to warm himself beside a fire.
55The chief priests and the whole council tried to find someone to accuse Jesus of a crime, so they could put him to death.
