And you can be sure that God's kingdom will soon be here!” 12 I tell you that on the day of judgment the people of Sodom will get off easier than the people of that town!
The Unbelieving Towns
(Matthew 11.20-24)
13 You people of Chorazin are in for trouble! You people of Bethsaida are also in for trouble! If the miracles that took place in your towns had happened in Tyre and Sidon, the people there would have turned to God long ago. They would have dressed in sackcloth and put ashes on their heads. 14On the day of judgment the people of Tyre and Sidon will get off easier than you will. 15 People of Capernaum, do you think you will be honored in heaven? Well, you will go down to hell!
16 My followers, whoever listens to you is listening to me. Anyone who says “No” to you is saying “No” to me. And anyone who says “No” to me is really saying “No” to the one who sent me.
The Return of the Seventy-Two
17When the 72 followers returned, they were excited and said, “Lord, even the demons obeyed when we spoke in your name!”
18Jesus told them:
I saw Satan fall from heaven like a flash of lightning. 19 I have given you the power to trample on snakes and scorpions and to defeat the power of your enemy Satan. Nothing can harm you. 20But don't be happy because evil spirits obey you. Be happy that your names are written in heaven!
Jesus Thanks His Father
(Matthew 11.25-27; 13.16,17)
21At that same time, Jesus felt the joy that comes from the Holy Spirit, and he said:
My Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I am grateful that you hid all this from wise and educated people and showed it to ordinary people. Yes, Father, this is what pleased you.
22 My Father has given me everything, and he is the only one who knows the Son. The only one who really knows the Father is the Son. But the Son wants to tell others about the Father, so they can know him too.
23Jesus then turned to his disciples and said to them in private, “You are really blessed to see what you see! 24Many prophets and kings were eager to see what you see and to hear what you hear. But I tell you they did not see or hear.”
The Good Samaritan
25 An expert in the Law of Moses stood up and asked Jesus a question to see what he would say. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to have eternal life?”
26Jesus answered, “What is written in the Scriptures? How do you understand them?”
27 The man replied, “The Scriptures say, ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind.’ They also say, ‘Love your neighbors as much as you love yourself.’ ”
28 Jesus said, “You have given the right answer. If you do this, you will have eternal life.”
29But the man wanted to show that he knew what he was talking about. So he asked Jesus, “Who are my neighbors?”
30Jesus replied:
As a man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, robbers attacked him and grabbed everything he had. They beat him up and ran off, leaving him half dead.
31A priest happened to be going down the same road. But when he saw the man, he walked by on the other side. 32Later a temple helper came to the same place. But when he saw the man who had been beaten up, he also went by on the other side.
33 A man from Samaria then came traveling along that road. When he saw the man, he felt sorry for him 34and went over to him. He treated his wounds with olive oil and wine and bandaged them. Then he put him on his own donkey and took him to an inn, where he took care of him. 35The next morning he gave the innkeeper two silver coins and said, “Please take care of the man. If you spend more than this on him, I will pay you when I return.”
36Then Jesus asked, “Which one of these three people was a real neighbor to the man who was beaten up by robbers?”
37The expert in the Law of Moses answered, “The one who showed pity.”
Jesus said, “Go and do the same!”
Martha and Mary
38 The Lord and his disciples were traveling along and came to a village. When they got there, a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home. 39She had a sister named Mary, who sat down in front of the Lord and was listening to what he said. 40Martha was worried about all that had to be done. Finally, she went to Jesus and said, “Lord, doesn't it bother you that my sister has left me to do all the work by myself? Tell her to come and help me!”
41The Lord answered, “Martha, Martha! You are worried and upset about so many things, 42but only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen what is best, and it will not be taken away from her.”
translation_text:
Yezu toŋe o nɔɔna fuserepɛ-balei
Matiyu 11:20-27; 13:16-17
1Ko kwaga ne, dé Teiru Yezu daa ta ma le nɔɔna fuserepɛ-balei (72), se o toŋe-ba balei balei se ba da yiga ba vo mɛ maama o na lage o vo to. 2O na lage o toŋe-ba konto to, mo o tage de-ba o we, “Ko nye de wodiu faao mo ke lanyerane, ye tontoŋena fenfee yerane mo wora se ba zage. Nam lwoori-na faao totoŋa yam yuu tu wom se o toŋe nɔɔna dedɛ se ba vo ba zage faao kom ba pa‑o.”
3O ma daare o we, “Amo na lage a toŋe abam jei sem konto ne to, á wó taa nye de pipeili na maa vei se se gwaane wiira wone tei to. 4Á ná maa via, á yé kwei sabia ganlɔgere, naa á kwei tampɔgɔ, naa á ta‑á jege natera á woli da. Yé zege-na chwoŋa ne á daane nɔɔn-nɔɔno peiga. 5Á nam ná yi sɔŋɔ kolo maama á na lage á zo to, se á ta de sɔŋɔ kom tiina we, ‘Wɛ wó pa abam zaane.’ 6Wɛ zaane nyem ná wora, wonto wó seene o na zaane ne á na tage tei to. Wɛ zaane nyem nam ná tera, abam tete mo wó jwoori á jwoŋi. 7Ta‑á zoore-na sɔŋɔ kom konto wone, se ko taa vei maŋa kam á na wó viiri to. Wodiu kolo maama ba ná ke ba pa abam, se á ta‑á di konto. Tontoŋeno maŋe se o taa jwoŋi o ŋweero mo. Á yé zaŋe á vo sɔŋɔ kodwoŋi á ta‑á zoore da. 8Á ná zo teo kolo maama ye ba ná jeeri abam lanyerane, se á ta‑á di wodiu kolo maama ba na ke ba pa abam to. 9Á ná wora, yɔɔre-na balo na ba jege yazura, ye á daare á ta-ba we, Wɛ tete fɔɔre o twɛ ba tei se o di paare ba baŋa ne. 10Ko daare, á ná zo teo kolo maama ye ba ná wo sɛ se ba jeeri abam, se á nwoŋi teo kom pwooni ye á ta-ba we, 11‘Abam teo fwogo kom na taare debam nɛ sem to, nii-na dé kokɔge-ko dé yage da, se ko bere we abam wo ke lanyerane. Nam ta‑á yei-na we, Wɛ tete fɔɔre o twɛ se o di paare o nɔɔna baŋa ne.’ 12Amo nam tɛ abam we, Wɛ borem dɛ dem ná yia, Sodom tiina bá tiini ba na lɛɛro se ko maŋe de teo kom konto.
13Abam Chorazin tiina, lɛɛro yi abam! Ko woli de abam Bɛtasida tiina, lɛɛro yi abam! Kokuri, wo-kenkagela yalo maama amo na ke abam tetare ne to, ya dwonna ya ná ke Tura de Sidon tiina tei ne, banto ya wó ke lela ba leiri ba wo Wɛ ŋwaane. Ba maa wó zo gare-nyenyaaro ye ba jei tentwarem wone ba wo-chechɔgɔ kom ŋwaane. 14Wɛ borem dɛ dem ná yia, Tura de Sidon tiina bá tiini ba na lɛɛro se ko maŋe de abam. 15Ko nam ná ye abam Kaparenia tiina, á ga boŋe we Wɛ lage o zeiŋi abam wɛyuu ne mo na? Aawo. Abam nam wó to á zo tega kuri kuri ne mo.”
16Yezu daa ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Wolo maama ná jwoŋi abam taane, konto tu jwoŋi amo taane mo. Wolo maama nam ná tɔne de abam, kotu tɔne de amo mo. Wolo maama na tɔne de amo to tɔne de Baŋa Wɛ wolo na toŋe-ne to mo.”
17Ko na ke fee to, nɔɔna fuserepɛ-balei bam déem ma jwoori Yezu tei de wopwolo. Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Debam Teiru, setaana tete dɛ nmo yere kɔrɔ ŋwaane ya sɛ ya pa debam.” 18O ma leiri-ba o we, “Amo nɛ setaana pɛ na kwori wɛyuu ne o to tega ne, ne doa na pepela ka baga ka tu ka kwaare tega tei to. 19Nii-na, a pɛ abam dam se á wane basankwe á taa nɔna, de nwanno, se á wane setaana pɛ de o dam maama, ye te kolokolo bá wane te ke abam woŋo. 20Á na jege dam dem konto to, á nam yé ta‑á jege wopwolo de chichiri na kɔre abam to ŋwaane. Nam ta‑á jege-na wopwolo dedɛ de á yera na popone Wɛ telaao ŋwe-doŋa tɔnɔ kom wone to.”
21Maŋa kam konto ne, Wɛ Sin-laao kom déem pɛ Yezu di ywoni lanyerane. O laam ma ke o Kwo Baŋa Wɛ lei ye o we, “A Kwo, nmo ye wolo na tei wɛyuu de tega baŋa maama. Nmo nam pɛ se n chega kam seigi swa tiina de yi-pore-nyena tei ne, ye n daare n pa se balo boboŋa ta na wo bege to lɔre ka kuri. A Kwo, a ke nmo lei. Nmo na ke konto to, ko ye n boboŋa na lage kolo to ŋwaane.
22A Kwo mo kwei wonnu maama o ke a jeŋa ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o lɔre Wɛ Bu wom na ye tei, ko ná dae o Kwo yerane. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa ta bá lɔre a Kwo Wɛ na ye tei, ko ná dae amo wolo na ye o Bu wom to yerane, ko woli de amo na boŋe se a pa nɔɔno wolo maama lɔre o na ye tei to.”
23Yezu laam ma pipiri o nii o kwaga tɔgena bam seeni, ye o ŋɔɔne de banto ba yerane o we, “Á jege yu-ywoŋo de á yi na nae wo-kamunnu telo to. 24Lɔre-na we, faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori dedɛ, de pwa dedɛ déem jege teena se ba na kolo maama abam na nae leile to, ye ba wo wane ba na. Ba maa jege teena se ba ni Wɛ taane delo abam na nigi to, ye ba wo wane ba ni-de.”
‘Wɔ mo ye a dwoŋi?’ memaŋe
25Wɛ nia yam zamesem tu dedoa déem zaŋe Yezu tei ne se o maŋe‑o o nii o swa na ye tei. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Berem tu, amo nam wó ke tɛ mo se a jwoŋi ŋwea kalo na ba jege kweelim Wɛ tei ne to?”
26Yezu ma ta ded‑o o we, “Bɛ mo popone Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom wone? Bɛ mo n yeini n gare da?” 27Nɔɔno wom ma leiri o we, “Ko popone we, ta‑n swoi n Tu Baŋa Wɛ de n bochare maama, de n wo maama, de n dam maama, de n boboŋa maama, se n kwori n ta‑n swoi n dwoŋi se ko maŋe de n tete.”
28Yezu ma leiri o we, “N pɔɔre chega. Nam ta‑n ke konto, se n wó na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne.”
29Nɔɔno wom maa lage se o taa jege bora. O ma pipiri o taane dem, ye o bwei Yezu o we, “Amo dwoŋi mo wɔ?” 30Yezu déem ma maŋe memaŋe o ma leiri‑o tento:
“Nɔɔno wodwoŋi mo zege Jerusalem teo ne o nwoŋi o maa vei Jeriko. O ma vo o maŋe de venverena. Venverena bam ma zi‑o ba vere o gwaaro de o wonnu maama. Ba ma mage‑o lanyerane pa se o da toone tei o kɛ, ye ba daare ba duri ba viiri. 31O na tigi da konto to, Wɛ kaanem tu dedoa de ya wo chwoŋa kam konto ne o maa via. O na maa vei to, o ma na nɔɔno wom na tigi o yiga ne. O ma lɛɛne o tɔge dáa o kɛ. 32Wɛ diga tontoŋeno wolo na ye Levi dwi tu to de maa tɔge da o maa kɛa. O na yi jei sem to, o ma na nɔɔno wom na tiga. O de daa ma lɛɛne o tɔge dáa o kɛ. 33Samaria tu wodwoŋi de déem maa wo beira ne. O ma vo o yi nɔɔno wom na tigi mɛ to. O na nɛ‑o to, o ma duri o ŋwaŋa. 34O ma vo o tei. O ma kwei nuga de sana o ma zare o fufwollu tem, ye o daare o vɔ-te. O laam ma kwei‑o o daŋe o tete bonaga baŋa ne o ja vo nɔɔno wodwoŋi veira diga. Ba na yi da to, o maa jege‑o o nii lanyerane. 35Tega na poore to, Samaria tu wom ma zaŋe se o kɛ. O ma le lu-nyenno sabu-dala yalei o pa wolo na tei veira diga kam to. O ma ta ded‑o o we, ‘Ta‑n nii nɔɔno wom baŋa ne n pa-ne. Sabu kom ná wo yi, maŋa kalo amo na wó jwoori to a nam wó ŋwe kolo maama n na wó ke n woli da to.’
36Tɔ. Nam ta n bere-ne, nɔɔna batɔ bam wone wɔ mo bere we o ye wolo venverena bam na vere to dwoŋi chekke?” 37Zamesem tu wom maa we, “Wolo wom na jege o ŋwaŋa to.”
Yezu laam ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nam véi n lwoni n ta‑n ke konto dwoŋi.”
Marita de Mary taane
38Yezu de o kwaga tɔgena bam daa maa wo chwoŋa ne ba via. O ma vo o yi teo kodwoŋi. Kaane wodwoŋi maa wora, o yere mo Marita. O ma jeeri Yezu lanyerane ba sɔŋɔ ne. 39Marita nyaane de maa wora, o yere mo Mary. O ma jeini tega ne Yezu tei ne, ye o cheigi o taane dem maama. 40Mary na jei konto to, Marita déem tiini o chɛ totoŋa ne mo de boboŋ-fara. O ma vo Yezu tei ye o we, “Amo tu, nii amo na zege a toŋa dedɛ a yerane, ye a nyaane wom chem. Nmo yiga tera na? Ta n bere‑o se o zaŋe o woli-ne.” 41Dé Teiru Yezu ma leiri‑o o we, “Marita, n boboŋa dedɛ yam mo jege‑m ya daana. 42Woŋo kodwoŋi yerane mo daare. Mary mo le kolo na lana to se o ke, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o che-ko.”

english_text:
Prayer
(Matthew 6.9-13; 7.7-11)
1When Jesus had finished praying, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his followers to pray.”
2So Jesus told them, “Pray in this way:
‘Father, help us
to honor your name.
Come and set up
your kingdom.
3Give us each day
the food we need.
4Forgive our sins,
as we forgive everyone
who has done wrong to us.
And keep us
from being tempted.’ ”
5Then Jesus went on to say:
Suppose one of you goes to a friend in the middle of the night and says, “Let me borrow three loaves of bread. 6A friend of mine has dropped in, and I don't have a thing for him to eat.” 7And suppose your friend answers, “Don't bother me! The door is bolted, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you something.”
8He may not get up and give you the bread, just because you are his friend. But he will get up and give you as much as you need, simply because you are not ashamed to keep on asking.
9So I tell you to ask and you will receive, search and you will find, knock and the door will be opened for you. 10Everyone who asks will receive, everyone who searches will find, and the door will be opened for everyone who knocks. 11Which one of you fathers would give your hungry child a snake if the child asked for a fish? 12Which one of you would give your child a scorpion if the child asked for an egg? 13As bad as you are, you still know how to give good gifts to your children. But your heavenly Father is even more ready to give the Holy Spirit to anyone who asks.
Jesus and the Ruler of Demons
(Matthew 12.22-30; Mark 3.20-27)
14Jesus forced a demon out of a man who could not talk. And after the demon had gone out, the man started speaking, and the crowds were amazed. 15 But some people said, “He forces out demons by the power of Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons!”
16 Others wanted to put Jesus to the test. So they asked him to show them a sign from God. 17Jesus knew what they were thinking, and he said:
A kingdom where people fight each other will end up in ruin. And a family that fights will break up. 18If Satan fights against himself, how can his kingdom last? Yet you say that I force out demons by the power of Beelzebul. 19If I use his power to force out demons, whose power do your own followers use to force them out? They are the ones who will judge you. 20But if I use God's power to force out demons, it proves that God's kingdom has already come to you.
21When a strong man arms himself and guards his home, everything he owns is safe. 22But if a stronger man comes and defeats him, he will carry off the weapons in which the strong man trusted. Then he will divide with others what he has taken. 23 If you are not on my side, you are against me. If you don't gather in the crop with me, you scatter it.
Return of an Evil Spirit
(Matthew 12.43-45)
24When an evil spirit leaves a person, it travels through the desert, looking for a place to rest. But when it doesn't find a place, it says, “I will go back to the home I left.” 25When it gets there and finds the place clean and fixed up, 26it goes off and finds seven other evil spirits even worse than itself. They all come and make their home there, and that person ends up in worse shape than before.
Being Really Blessed
27While Jesus was still talking, a woman in the crowd spoke up, “The woman who gave birth to you and nursed you is blessed!”
28Jesus replied, “That's true, but the people who are really blessed are the ones who hear and obey God's message!”
A Sign from God
(Matthew 12.38-42; Mark 8.12)
29 As crowds were gathering around Jesus, he said:
You people of today are evil! You keep looking for a sign from God. But what happened to Jonah is the only sign you will be given. 30 Just as Jonah was a sign to the people of Nineveh, the Son of Man will be a sign to the people of today. 31 When the judgment comes, the Queen of the South will stand there with you and condemn you. She traveled a long way to hear Solomon's wisdom, and yet here is something far greater than Solomon. 32 The people of Nineveh will also stand there with you and condemn you. They turned to God when Jonah preached, and yet here is something far greater than Jonah.
Light
(Matthew 5.15; 6.22,23)
33 No one lights a lamp and then hides it or puts it under a clay pot. A lamp is put on a lampstand, so everyone who comes into the house can see the light. 34Your eyes are the lamp for your body. When your eyes are good, you have all the light you need. But when your eyes are bad, everything is dark. 35So be sure your light isn't darkness. 36If you have light, and nothing is dark, then light will be everywhere, as when a lamp shines brightly on you.
Jesus Condemns the Pharisees and Teachers of the Law of Moses
(Matthew 23.1-36; Mark 12.38-40; Luke 20.45-47)
37When Jesus finished speaking, a Pharisee invited him home for a meal. Jesus went and sat down to eat. 38The Pharisee was surprised that he did not wash his hands before eating. 39So the Lord said to him:
You Pharisees clean the outside of cups and dishes, but on the inside you are greedy and evil. 40You fools! Didn't God make both the outside and the inside? 41If you would only give what you have to the poor, everything you do would please God.
42 You Pharisees are in for trouble! You give God a tenth of the spices from your gardens, such as mint and rue. But you cheat people, and you don't love God. You should be fair and kind to others and still give a tenth to God.
43You Pharisees are in for trouble! You love the front seats in the synagogues, and you like to be greeted with honor in the market. 44But you are in for trouble! You are like unmarked graves that people walk on without even knowing it.
45A teacher of the Law of Moses spoke up, “Teacher, you said cruel things about us.”
46Jesus replied:
You teachers are also in for trouble! You load people down with heavy burdens, but you won't lift a finger to help them carry the loads. 47Yes, you are really in for trouble. You build monuments to honor the prophets your own people murdered long ago. 48You must think that was the right thing for your people to do, or else you would not have built monuments for the prophets they murdered.
49Because of your evil deeds, the Wisdom of God said, “I will send prophets and apostles to you. But you will murder some and mistreat others.” 50You people living today will be punished for all the prophets who have been murdered since the beginning of the world. 51 This includes every prophet from the time of Abel to the time of Zechariah, who was murdered between the altar and the temple. You people will certainly be punished for all of this.
52You teachers of the Law of Moses are really in for trouble! You carry the keys to the door of knowledge about God. But you never go in, and you keep others from going in.
53Jesus was about to leave, but the teachers and the Pharisees wanted to get even with him. They tried to make him say what he thought about other things, 54so they could catch him saying something wrong.
translation_text:
Wɛ-lworo taane
Matiyu 6:9-15; 7:7-11
1Dɛ dedwe mo Yezu déem vei jei sedwoŋi se o ware Wɛ. O na ware Wɛ o ti to, o kwaga tɔgena bam dedoa ma ta ded‑o o we, “Debam Teiru, bere debam dé na wó ke tei se dé taa ware Wɛ, ne Jɔn de na bere o tɔgena bam se ba taa ke tei to.”
2Yezu ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam ná lage á ware Wɛ, se á ta tento dwoŋi:
‘Debam Kwo,
nmo yere dem maŋe de tia mo.
Nmo paare dem de ma maŋe
se de ba de jeini de dam.
3Ta‑n pae debam wodiiru dɛ dɛ se te maŋe debam.
4Yage dé wɛleera n ma n chɛ debam,
se debam de yeini dé ma chɛ wolo maama
na ke o chɔge debam yiga to mo.
Yé pa se dé na cham delo na wó maŋe dé boboŋa to.’ ”
5Yezu daa ma ta de o tɔgena bam o we, “Wɛ-lworo nye de nmo na jege n badwoŋi n ke tei. Nmo ma‑n zaŋe tete kokoro ne n vo o tei n ta ded‑o we, ‘A badwoŋi, popo a lwoori‑m se n pa-ne bworobwooru tetɔ, 6se veiru mo nwoŋi yiga yiga o ba amo tei, ye a ba jege kolokolo se a pa‑o se o di.’ 7Nmo badwoŋi wom maa zege diga kam wone o ta de nmo o we, ‘Yé ta‑n jege-ne n daana, se manchwo-peena yam pe ye amo de a bia maama tigi dé dɔa. Amo bá wane a zaŋe a woli‑m.’
8Tɔ. N badwoŋi wom wó wane o ta konto dwoŋi na? Dɛ delo á badwoŋo kom bá pa o sɛ o zaŋe o pa nmo wodiu kom. Nmo nam ná zege da taa n lwoori‑o de baare, o laam wó sɛ o zaŋe o pa nmo kolo maama n na lage to.
9Mo kokuri, ta‑á lwoori-na Wɛ, se á wó na kolo á na lage to. Beeri-na kolo á na lage to, se á wó na. Ta ta‑á dɔne-na manchwo-peena yam, se ba wó pore ba pa abam. 10Kolo ŋwaane, wolo maama na lwoori Wɛ se o pa‑o woŋo to wó jwoŋi. Wolo maama na beeri woŋo to wó na-ko. Ba wó pore ba pa wolo maama na dɔne manchwo-peena yam to.
11Abam wolo ná jege bu, ye o ná lwoori‑m se n pa‑o ywoni, nmo wó sɛ n pa‑o basankwea na? 12O ná lwoori chechare nmo tei ne, nmo wó sɛ n kwei nɔŋɔ n pa‑o na? 13Aawo. Abam wo ba lana ye á ta yei se á ta‑á pae á bia wo-laaro telo ba na lage to. Ko daare á Kwo Wɛ na gare abam to, wonto nam bá kwei o Sin-laao kom o pa balo na lwoori‑o to mo na?”
Wɔ dam mo Yezu mae o zeili setaana?
Matiyu 12:22-30, 43-45; Maake 3:20-27
14Dɛ dedoa mo Yezu déem zeili setaane nɔɔno wodwoŋi tei ne. Setaane dem ya pɛ se nɔɔno wom ji memaa mo. De na yage o yera to, o laam maa ŋɔɔna. Ko ma so nɔn-kɔgɔ kom lanyerane. 15Nɔɔna badaara nam na nɛ to, ba maa we, “O na wae o zeili setaana to, ko ye setaana pɛ Bɛlzabula dam ŋwaane mo.” 16Ba badaara maa kwaane ba maŋe o dam ba nii, ye ba we o jege se o ke wo-kenkagele delo na wó bere-ba we o seene o nwoŋi Wɛ tei to mo.
17Yezu ma lɔre ba boboŋa na ye tei to. O ma ta de-ba o we, “Teo kolo maama paare ná pɔɔre belei pa ba jege daane, ko bá dáane ye ko chɔge. Sɔŋɔ kolo maama ná pɔɔre ko tete wone, ko jege se ko to mo. 18Setaana pɛ dam dem ná seene de pɔɔre belei, o paare dem bá dáane ye de chɔge. Abam na tɛ we ko ye Bɛlzabula dam ŋwaane mo a wae a zeili setaana to mo pɛ a ta konto dwoŋi. 19Ko ná seene ko ye amo tɔge Bɛlzabula dam ŋwaane mo a maa zeili setaana, abam nɔɔna bam de nam mae dam dem konto mo ba maa zeili-ya na? Abam tete nɔɔna bam na ke tei to mo bere we chega tera á tei ne. 20Ko nam na ye tei to, ko ye Wɛ tete dam ŋwaane mo a wae setaana a zeila. Konto maa bere we Wɛ maŋe o ba abam tei se o di paare o nɔɔna baŋa ne.
21Setaana pɛ nam nye de nɔn-babea na jege taŋa de chena o maa nii o sɔŋɔ tei to. O ta ná zege da konto, o jejegero tem bá jei. 22Nɔɔno wodwoŋi nam ná tua, ye o dam ná dwoi nɔn-babea kam, konto tu wó ja nɔn-babea kam o mage‑o o wane. O laam wó vere o jara zela yam, o ya na daŋe o teena ya baŋa ne to. O laam wó wane o wonnu tem maama o kwaleme ye o maŋe-te o pa nɔɔna.
23Nɔɔno wolo maama nam na ba zege amo kwaga ne to ye amo dono mo. Nɔɔno wolo maama nam na ba tɔge o lae amo wonnu o pa-ne to boŋe se o jage-te o yage mo.
24Setaane ná nwoŋi nɔɔno tei ne, o laam wó vo o beeri mɛ seeni na ye te-kora to se o lage jei o sii da. O ma beeri o ga. O laam maa we, ‘A jege se a jwoori a vo a na nwoŋi mɛ to mo a taa wora.’ 25O ma jwoori o vo nɔɔno wom tei, ye o lɔre we o jei sem fɔge se kwɛ lanyerane. 26O laam ma jwoori o vo o lage o dwonna barepɛ balo na maŋe ba ye puseŋ-nyena ba dwoi o tete to. Ba ma tɔge daane ba vo ba zoore da. Ko maama laam na kweeli tei to ye lɛɛro mo wó taa jege nɔɔno wom konto se ko dwoni o boboa kam na maŋe ka ye tei to.”
27Yezu na zege o ŋɔɔne konto to, kaane wodwoŋi na tɔge o wo kɔgɔ kom wone to ma ta baŋa baŋa o we, “Kaane wolo na loge‑m ye n ŋɔge o yele to mo ye yu-ywoŋo tu.” 28Yezu ma leiri o we, “Se balo na ni Wɛ kwora kam ye ba sɛ o ni to mo jege yu-ywoŋo ko ja gaale.”
Balo na ve Wɛ chega kam to wó na bora na?
Matiyu 12:38-42; Maake 8:12
29Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom ma tiini ko peene daane. Yezu daa ma ta o we, “Zem nɔɔna ye nɔn-balwaaro mo. Ba lage se a ke wo-kenkagele mo a bere-ba se ko taa ye maana ko pa-ba. Ba nam bá na, ko ná dae wo-kenkagele delo na maŋe de ke Jonah baŋa ne faŋa faŋa to. 30Wonto déem bere Wɛ dam Ninevɛ tiina tei ne se ko taa ye maana ko pa-ba. Amo wolo na ye Nabiin-bu wom to de wó ji maanem zem nɔɔna bam tei ne, ne ko déem na ke Jonah tei to. 31Wɛ borem dɛ dem ná yia, ka-pɛ wolo déem na tei Seba faŋa faŋa to wó zaŋe o bere we abam ba jege chega. Wonto déem zaŋe o tete teo kolo na tiini ko ye yiga yiga to ne o ba Pɛ Solomon tei se o cheigi o swa yam na ye tei to. Wolo nam na dwoi Solomon to wo abam tei ne ye á yiga tera ded‑o. 32Ninevɛ tiina de wó zaŋe dɛ dem konto ne ba bere we abam ba jege chega, kolo ŋwaane Jonah na vei ba tei o bere-ba Wɛ chega kam to, ba leiri ba wo. Wolo na dwoi Jonah to nam wo abam tei ne ye á wo sɛ konto tu.
Wɛ chega kam pae debam pwooni
Matiyu 5:15; 6:22-23
33Nɔɔno ná jege kanea, o bá sɛ o tɔre-ka o zege gugworo wone, naa o pu-ka zoŋa kuri ne. O nam wó kwei-ka o pale wɛɛne mo, se balo na zo diga kam wo to taa nae pwooni dem. 34Nmo yia mo pae se n yera jege pwooni. Konto to, nmo yia ná lana, ko pae se n ŋwea maama taa tɔge pwooni mo. Ya nam ná ba lae, ko pae se n ŋwea maama wo lim wone. 35Konto ŋwaane ta‑n yei n tete, se n pa pwooni dem seene de taa wo n tei ne, ye ko dae lim yerane. 36Konto to, pwooni yerane ná wo n tei ne, ye lim tera de fenfee de, nmo ŋwea maama wó taa jege pwooni chekke, ko maŋe de kanea na pae se pwooni wo n tei ne tei to.”
Lɛɛro wó yi Farisi tiina de ba dwonna
Matiyu 23:1-36; Maake 12:38-40; Luka 20:45-47
37Yezu déem na ŋɔɔne wonnu tem konto o ti to, Farisi tu dedoa ma bwoŋi‑o se o da o vo o sɔŋɔ o di wodiu. O ma vo o zo sɔŋɔ kom o jeini se o di. 38Farisi tu wom ma na we Yezu wo sane o jea se ko tɔge ba chullu tem chwoŋa. Ko ma so‑o. 39Dé Teiru Yezu ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nii mo! Abam Farisi tiina ná lage á di wodiu, á yeini á tɔge á chullu tem á fɔge á se á zwe de á kabeili, ko ná maŋe ko ye se kwɛ sem de. Ko daare abam tete nam su de digiru. Á ye kampin-nyena ye á tɔge wo-zɔɔna kikia. 40Abam ye jworru mo. Wɛ nam wo ke woŋo maama kwaga de ko yiga na? 41Á nam jege se á kwei wodiiru telo á na jege á zwe sem wone to á maŋe á pa yiniga tiina. Á ná ke konto, á woŋo maama bá taa jege digiru.
42Abam Farisi tiina bam, lɛɛro yi abam. Ko ná ye dwoa wo-sworru dwi maama, te ná maŋe te ye memeeno tei, á yeini á pɔɔre Wɛ-teiri á le á pa‑o. Ko lana. Ko daare abam yiga tera de chega tɔgem de Wɛ swono. Ko ya maŋe se á ta‑á tɔge keim-laaro tem konto maama, se á yé yage tedaara.
43Abam Farisi tiina bam, lɛɛro yi abam. Á ná zo á jeerim di sem, á lage jei-kamunnu mo se á jeini yiga ne. Á ná vei yaga, á lage se nɔɔna maama taa tui ba zuli abam.
44Lɛɛro yi abam! Á nye de yibeela yalo na saare ya daare tega, pa se nɔɔna tɔge ya baŋa ba kɛ ye ba ta yeiri ya ni ne to mo.”
45Wɛ nia yam zamesem tu dedoa laam ma zaŋe o ta de Yezu o we, “Berem tu, nmo na jege wonnu telo n ŋɔɔne to pa se n twe debam de mo.” 46Yezu ma leiri o we, “Abam balo na ye Wɛ nia yam zamesem tiina to, lɛɛro yi abam. Abam yeini á daane nɔɔna de wo-chɛɛro se ba taa tɔga. Ko maa nye de á na pa ba zeŋe zela yalo dum na dwoi ba zeŋem to, ye abam tete ba sɛ se á twori zela yam fenfee de á zeiŋi.
47Lɛɛro yi abam! Abam yeini á fɔge á ke faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem yibeela. Ko nam ye á nabaara mo go-ba. 48Á kikia yam bere we á sɛ keim-lwanno telo á nabaara bam na ke to. Banto déem go Wɛ sampwori sem, ye abam tete laam fɔge á kwɛ ba yibeela yam. 49Abam na tɔge á kwoa kikia konto to, Wɛ dɛ o swa ŋwaane ye o we, ‘Amo wó toŋe a sampwori de a tontoŋena ba tei ne. Ba maa wó ja ba badaara ba go, ye ba pa ba badaara na yaara.’ 50Konto ŋwaane Wɛ waarem dem wó ba á baŋa, ne ko ye abam tete mo go Wɛ sampwori selo maama ba na go boboa ne se ko ba ko yi zem to. 51Konto maa zege Abel ne, se ko ba ko woli de Zekaria wolo ba na go Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem de o tete diga kam tetare laŋa ne to. A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, keim-lwanno tem konto maama wó taa wo zem nɔɔna bam yuu ne.
52Wɛ nia yam zamesem tiina bam, lɛɛro yi abam. Á yeini á che nɔɔna se ba yé jwoŋi yeino chekke. Abam tete wo sɛ se á jwoŋi-ko, ye á daare á wo pɛ balo na lage ba jwoŋi-ko to chwoŋa se ba jwoŋi.”
53Yezu laam ma yage jei sem konto ye o viiri. Wɛ nia zamesem tiina bam de Farisi tiina bam maa ba lage o ni taane kɔtaa. Ba maa daane‑o ye ba bwei‑o wonnu dedɛ. 54Ba maa lage se ba pa o ŋɔɔne o tusi se ba wane ba da ko ŋwaane ba ja‑o.

english_text:
Warnings
1 As thousands of people crowded around Jesus and were stepping on each other, he told his disciples:
Be sure to guard against the dishonest teaching of the Pharisees! It is their way of fooling people. 2 Everything that is hidden will be found out, and every secret will be known. 3Whatever you say in the dark will be heard when it is day. Whatever you whisper in a closed room will be shouted from the housetops.
The One To Fear
(Matthew 10.28-31)
4 My friends, don't be afraid of people. They can kill you, but after that, there is nothing else they can do. 5God is the one you must fear. Not only can he take your life, but he can throw you into hell. God is certainly the one you should fear!
6Five sparrows are sold for only a few cents, but God doesn't forget a single one of them. 7Even the hairs on your head are counted. So don't be afraid! You are worth much more than many sparrows.
Telling Others about Christ
(Matthew 10.32,33; 12.32; 10.19,20)
8If you tell others that you belong to me, the Son of Man will tell God's angels that you are my followers. 9But if you reject me, you will be rejected in front of them. 10 If you speak against the Son of Man, you can be forgiven, but if you speak against the Holy Spirit, you cannot be forgiven.
11 When you are brought to trial in the synagogues or before rulers or officials, don't worry about how you will defend yourselves or what you will say. 12At that time the Holy Spirit will tell you what to say.
A Rich Fool
13A man in a crowd said to Jesus, “Teacher, tell my brother to give me my share of what our father left us when he died.”
14Jesus answered, “Who gave me the right to settle arguments between you and your brother?”
15Then he said to the crowd, “Don't be greedy! Owning a lot of things won't make your life safe.”
16So Jesus told them this story:
A rich man's farm produced a big crop, 17and he said to himself, “What can I do? I don't have a place large enough to store everything.”
18Later, he said, “Now I know what I'll do. I'll tear down my barns and build bigger ones, where I can store all my grain and other goods. 19 Then I'll say to myself, ‘You have stored up enough good things to last for years to come. Live it up! Eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.’ ”
20But God said to him, “You fool! Tonight you will die. Then who will get what you have stored up?”
21“This is what happens to people who store up everything for themselves, but are poor in the sight of God.”
Worry
(Matthew 6.25-34)
22Jesus said to his disciples:
I tell you not to worry about your life! Don't worry about having something to eat or wear. 23Life is more than food or clothing. 24Look at the crows! They don't plant or harvest, and they don't have storehouses or barns. But God takes care of them. You are much more important than any birds. 25Can worry make you live longer? 26If you don't have power over small things, why worry about everything else?
27 Look how the wild flowers grow! They don't work hard to make their clothes. But I tell you Solomon with all his wealth wasn't as well clothed as one of these flowers. 28God gives such beauty to everything that grows in the fields, even though it is here today and thrown into a fire tomorrow. Won't he do even more for you? You have such little faith!
29Don't keep worrying about having something to eat or drink. 30Only people who don't know God are always worrying about such things. Your Father knows what you need. 31But put God's work first, and these things will be yours as well.
Treasures in Heaven
(Matthew 6.19-21)
32My little group of disciples, don't be afraid! Your Father wants to give you the kingdom. 33Sell what you have and give the money to the poor. Make yourselves moneybags that never wear out. Make sure your treasure is safe in heaven, where thieves cannot steal it and moths cannot destroy it. 34Your heart will always be where your treasure is.
Faithful and Unfaithful Servants
(Matthew 24.45-51)
35 Be ready and keep your lamps burning 36 just like those servants who wait up for their master to return from a wedding feast. As soon as he comes and knocks, they open the door for him. 37Servants are fortunate if their master finds them awake and ready when he comes! I promise you he will get ready and let his servants sit down so he can serve them. 38Those servants are really fortunate if their master finds them ready, even though he comes late at night or early in the morning. 39 You would surely not let a thief break into your home, if you knew when the thief was coming. 40So always be ready! You don't know when the Son of Man will come.
41Peter asked Jesus, “Did you say this just for us or for everyone?”
42The Lord answered:
Who are faithful and wise servants? Who are the ones the master will put in charge of giving the other servants their food supplies at the proper time? 43Servants are fortunate if their master comes and finds them doing their job. 44A servant who is always faithful will surely be put in charge of everything the master owns.
45But suppose one of the servants thinks that the master won't return until late. Suppose that servant starts beating all the other servants and eats and drinks and gets drunk. 46If that happens, the master will come on a day and at a time when the servant least expects him. That servant will then be punished and thrown out with the servants who cannot be trusted.
47If servants are not ready or willing to do what their master wants them to do, they will be beaten hard. 48But servants who don't know what their master wants them to do will not be beaten so hard for doing wrong. If God has been generous with you, he will expect you to serve him well. But if he has been more than generous, he will expect you to serve him even better.
Not Peace, but Trouble
(Matthew 10.34-36)
49I came to set fire to the earth, and I wish it were already on fire! 50 I am going to be put to a hard test. And I will have to suffer a lot of pain until it is over. 51Do you think that I came to bring peace to earth? No indeed! I came to make people choose sides. 52A family of five will be divided, with two of them against the other three. 53 Fathers and sons will turn against one another, and mothers and daughters will do the same. Mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law will also turn against each other.
Knowing What To Do
(Matthew 16.2,3; 5.25,26)
54Jesus said to all the people:
As soon as you see a cloud coming up in the west, you say, “It's going to rain,” and it does. 55When the south wind blows, you say, “It's going to get hot,” and it does. 56Are you trying to fool someone? You can predict the weather by looking at the earth and sky, but you don't really know what's going on right now. 57Why don't you understand the right thing to do? 58When someone accuses you of something, try to settle things before you are taken to court. If you don't, you will be dragged before the judge. Then the judge will hand you over to the jailer, and you will be locked up. 59You won't get out until you have paid the last cent you owe.
translation_text:
Dé na wó taa jege dé tete tei to
Matiyu 10:26-33
1Maŋa kam konto ne, kɔ-fɔrɔ dedɛ ya lage daane Yezu tei ne. Ba déem yi nenɛɛne morro dedɛ ye ba peene daane pa se ba wora ba nɔne daane. Yezu ma bobo o ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam o we, “Fɔge-na á che á tete se á yé pa Farisi tiina bam de abam sabɔle, de ba na ye pipiri-nyena ye ba seigi ba ke wo-lwanno tei to. 2Woŋo kolo maama na seigi nɔɔna tei ne to laam wó ba ko lɔre jaja. 3Konto to, abam na seigi á ta kolo maama to jege se ko nwoŋi pwooni mo, se nɔɔna di nayuu ba tɔɔle-ko.
4A badwonna bam, a tɛ abam se á yé ta‑á kɔre foone de nabiina. Ba wae ba goe á yera yam ye ko kwaga seeni ba daa ware ba ke abam kolokolo. 5Amo nam wó bere abam á na wó ta‑á kɔre wolo to. Á jege se á ta‑á kɔre Wɛ mo. Kokuri, ba ná go abam ba daare, wonto jege dam se o dole abam o yage te-seŋa jei ne. A tɛ abam we, á jege se á ta‑á kɔre foone de wonto mo.
6Ko ná ye zun-kabeili, ba yeini ba yeigi sento mɔle mo. Wɛ nam ba swei se maama ni ne, de se dedoa de. 7Wɛ maŋe o yei abam tete yu-ywei sem ni na mae tei to. Á yé ta‑á kɔre foone, se abam dedoa dedoa tiini á jege fera á dwoi zun-kabeili dedɛ.
8A tɛ abam we, nɔɔno wolo maama ná zege nabiina yiga ne o bere jaja we o ye amo nyem, amo Nabiin-bu wom de wó zege konto tu kwaga ne a bere we o ye a nyem Wɛ malese sem yiga ne. 9Ko daare wolo maama ná ve amo nabiina yiga ne, amo de wó ve konto tu Wɛ malese sem yiga ne. 10Wolo maama ná ŋɔɔne wo-balwaaro o pa Nabiin-bu wom, Wɛ wó sɛ se o yage o ma chɛ konto tu. Wolo nam ná ŋɔɔne o yaale Wɛ Sin-laao kom, Wɛ bá sɛ se o ma chɛ konto tu.
11Nɔɔna wó ja abam ba vo ba saŋe Juu tiina nakwa tei ne, de teo kom yiga tiina de dedɛɛra tei ne. Ba ná ke abam konto, se á yé ta‑á jege lwia de á na wó ŋɔɔne kolo se á ma á jwoŋi á tete, de á na wó tole taane dem tei to. 12Kanto maŋa kam ne Wɛ Sin-laao kom wó pa á lɔre á na jege se á ta kolo to.”
Jejegero memaŋe
13Nɔɔno dedoa na tɔge o wo kɔgɔ kom wone to ma ta de Yezu o we, “Berem tu, popo se n ta a zembaaro wom se o kwei wonnu telo debam kwo na tege o daare to o pɔɔre amo nyem o pa-ne.” 14Yezu ma leiri‑o o we, “A nɔɔno, amo jege chwoŋa se a bore abam taane na?”
15O laam ma ta de ba maama o we, “Ta‑á yei-na á tete se á yé pa á yi taa sui wonnu dedɛ. Nɔɔno jejegero tem ná daga tei, te bá wane o ŋwea te ke, o ná maŋe o ye nadum tei maama.”
16Yezu laam ma maŋe memaŋe o bere-ba o we: “Nadum mo wora. O kare sem ma ke wodiiru dedɛ se pa‑o. 17O ma boŋe o we, ‘Amo nam wó ke tɛ mo? Jei daa tera se a ke a wodiiru tem maama da. 18A wó yigi a tuli sem maama mo a de tega ne, se a daare a lɔ tuli-zɛ se a wane a pɛ a wodiiru tem de a wonnu maama a ke da. 19A laam wó ta de a tete we, a ye yu-ywoŋo tu mo. A jege wonnu telo maama a na lage to se ko maŋe de bena kɔgɔ kɔgɔ. Lwia daa bá ja-ne. Amo wó taa ke a boboŋa na lage tei, ye a di a ni ye a kwɛɛra.’ 20Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, ‘Nmo ye nɔn-jworo mo. Tete dento wone n ŋwea jege se ka ti. Konto to, nmo tete wó wane n di wonnu tento maama n na ke n pa n tete to na?’ 21Tɔ. Wolo maama ná tiŋi jejegero dedɛ o tete tei ne ye o ba jege kolokolo Wɛ tei ne, ko wó ke kotu konto dwoŋi mo.”
Wɛ na wó taa jege de teena tei to
Matiyu 6:25-34
22Yezu daa ta ma ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam o we: “Konto ŋwaane mo a tɛ abam se á yé ta‑á jege-na lwia de logo baŋa kolokolo, ko ná ye á ni-wodiu, naa á na wó zo gwaaro telo to de. 23Kokuri á ŋwea gare wodiiru. Yera yalo Wɛ na pɛ abam to de ma gare gwaaro. 24Nam maane-na á nii bachangaaro na ye tei to. Te ba dua, ye te ta ba zage mena. Te ba jege tuli de tikeiri se te ke wodiiru da. Ko nam ye Wɛ mo nii te baŋa ne de te ni-wodiu. Abam nam tiini á jege kuri á dwoi zuna bam. 25Abam wolowolo bá wane o twoŋi o ŋwea de fenfee de, o na maŋe o jege ka lwia tei de. 26Abam na ware konto fenfee á ke to, bɛ mo ye á jege lwia de wonnu telo maama na daare to?
27Maane-na á nii gaao punnu tem na ye tei to. Tento nam ba ke totoŋa ye te ba sɔ gwaaro. Nam ta‑á yei-na we, tento jege lam te dwoi Pɛ Solomon déem na maŋe o zoore gare-nyenno telo to. 28Ko nam ná ye gaaro tem konto, tento ba jege dɛ ye nɔɔna yeini ba zwɛ-te. De konto de Wɛ ta mo pae te jege lam konto dwoŋi. Konto ŋwaane ko ná ye abam, Wɛ wó tiini o nii abam baŋa ne. Abam boboŋa muri de Wɛ.
29Yé ta‑á jege-na boboŋ-fara de á na wó ke tei se á na wodiu á di to. Á yé ta‑á jege lwia konto seeni. 30Logo baŋa dwi tiina balo na yeiri Wɛ to mo tiini ba boŋe wonnu tem konto maama boboŋa. Abam Kwo Wɛ nam maŋe o yei á na lage-te tei to. 31Abam jege se á pa á boboŋa taa tɔge Wɛ paare dem mo. Á ná ke konto, Wɛ laam wó woli abam de á logo baŋa wonnu tem.
32Amo kɔgɔ fenfee, yé pa-na foone taa jege abam. Abam Kwo Wɛ boboŋa mo lage se o pa abam tɔge á di o paare dem. 33Kwei-na á jejegero tem á yeigi se á daare á maŋe te sabu kom á ma á woli yiniga tiina. Konto mo á wó kwei á jejegero á tiŋi Wɛ telaao ne, sabia ganlɔgera na bá chɔge mɛ to. Á ná tiŋi wo-laaro Wɛ tei ne, te daa bá ba te muri. Ŋweena daa bá wane ba ŋɔ-te. Kolokolo bá wane ko mu-te ko chɔge. 34Ta‑á ke-na konto bɛŋwaane á wonnu tem na wo mɛ maama, á boboŋa wó tiini ya taa tigi dáane mo.”
Dé Teiru wom tutuuri dem memaŋa
Matiyu 24:42-51; 10:34-36; 16:2-3
35-36Yezu ta ma ta o we, “Ta‑á fɔge-na á cho á tete, ne nɔɔna balo tu wom na nwoŋi o vo se o di kadiri ye ba jege o teena se o jwoori o ba to. Ba ma fɔge ba vɔ ba gwaaro lanyerane, ye ba tɔre ba min-zwonnu ba zege ba tei ne. Ba tu wom ná tu o yi manchwo-peena, ba laam wó wane ba zaŋe lela ba pore ba pa‑o. 37Sɔŋɔ tu wom ná jwoori o ba, ye o tontoŋena ta ná jege ba tete ba nia, wopwolo wó taa wo ba tei ne. A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, sɔŋɔ tu wom laam wó pa ba jeini se ba di wodiu. O maa wó kwɛ o tete se o kwei wodiu kom o vo o tiŋi pa ba di. 38O nam ná jwoori o ba tete kokoro ne de, ye o sɔŋɔ tontoŋena bam ta ná jege ba tete ye ba ba dɔa, wopwolo wó taa wo ba tei ne.
39Ta‑á yei-na we, sɔŋɔ tu wom ya ná lɔre maŋa kalo ŋweeno na lage o ba to, o ya bá pa ŋweeno wom na chwoŋa o zo o ŋɔ. 40Konto ŋwaane abam jege se á che á tete mo, se Nabiin-bu wom lage o ba maŋa kam á na ba jege o teena to mo.”
41Piita ma bwei Yezu o we, “Dé Teiru, nmo na maŋe memaŋe dem to, ko ye debam ŋwaane mo naa nɔɔna maama ŋwaane mo?”
42Dé Teiru Yezu ma leiri o we, “Abam jege se á ta‑á tɔge chega de á boboŋ-dɛɛra, nenɛɛne sɔŋɔ tontoŋeno wolo yuu tu na yage o totoŋa o pa‑o, ye o daare o nwoŋi se o beeri to. O tu wom ma le‑o se o taa nii o dwonna tontoŋena bam baŋa ne se o daare o taa pa-ba ba ni-wodiu dɛ maama wone. 43O sɔŋɔ tu wom ná jwoori o ba, ye o ke kolo maama o na pɛ‑o se o ke to, wopwolo laam wó taa wo tontoŋeno wom konto tei ne. 44A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, o tu wom laam wó pa se o taa nii o jejegero maama baŋa ne mo.
45Tontoŋeno wom nam ná boŋe we, omo tu wom dáane dedɛ ye o ta wo tu, ko wó ke‑o tɛ mo? O maa wó taa jege o dwonna tontoŋena bam mo o maga, baara bam de kaana bam de. O maa di wodiiru o chɔga, ye o nyɔ sana o sui. 46Tontoŋeno wom konto tu wom laam wó jwoori o ba dɛ dem tontoŋeno wom na ba jege o teena de maŋa kalo o na wó ba o zo to. O tu wom nam ná tu o peere‑o konto, o laam wó zeili‑o o sɔŋɔ kom wone, ye o daare o pa se kotu tɔge de balo na ve Wɛ chega kam to o na waarem.
47Tontoŋeno wolo maama ná lɔre o tu wom boboŋa na lage se o ke kolo to, ye o ná wo sɛ se o ja o tete o ke konto, konto tu wó na waarem dedɛ. 48Ko daare wolo ná yeiri o tu wom na lage se o ke kolo to, ye o ná ke kolo na maŋe se o na waarem to, konto tu wó na waarem fenfee yerane mo. Wolo maama ná jege Wɛ yeino dedɛ, Wɛ wó jeeli se o na wo-laaro dedɛ konto tu tei ne. Nɔɔno wolo ná jwoŋi wonnu dedɛ se o taa nii te baŋa ne, Wɛ wó jeeli se o jwoŋi dedɛ wonto tei ne ko ja gaale.”
49Yezu daa ta ma ta o we, “Amo na tu logo baŋa to, ko ye se a tɔre mini a ma zwɛ-ko mo. Mini dem ya ná maŋe de tɔre, ko ya jege a wopwolo mo. 50Amo nam jege se a zo yaara wo. Ko maa pae se a boboŋa chɔge se ko taa nii maŋa kam ko na wó ke ko kɛ to. 51Amo na tu logo baŋa to, á boŋe we ko ye se a pa nɔɔna fɔge daane mo na? Aawo. A tu se a pa nɔɔna pɔɔre daane mo. 52Ko zege zem ko taa via, sɔŋɔ dedoa wone nɔɔna banu wó pɔɔre mo, batɔ de balei. 53Kwo de o bu wó chɔge daane. Nu de o bukɔ de wó chɔge daane. Kaane de o baro nu de maa wó chɔge daane.”
54Yezu laam ma ta de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom o we, “Abam yeini á wae á nii wɛyuu de tega baŋa á ma lɔre tega kam yibia na wó taa ye tei to. Á ná nɛ kunkwonnu na wora te zaŋa mɛ seeni doa na zege da ka nene to, á yeini á ta lela we, doa lage ka ne, ye ka wó seene ka ne. 55Ko daare gungun-koro vio ná wora ko maga, á yeini á we, lon-wea maa beena, ye ko seene ko ke konto. 56Abam ye pipiri-nyena mo! Abam wae á nii wɛyuu de tega baŋa ye á lɔre te na bere tei to chekke. Bɛ nam mo ye á ware á lɔre wonnu telo na wora te ke leile to kuri?
57Bɛŋwaane mo abam ba sɛ se á pɔɔre kolo na lana se á ta‑á ke to? 58Ko nye de nɔɔno ná jaane‑m o vo o saŋe kɔɔte ne. Abam ta ná wo chwoŋa ne á via, se n kwaane n pa á fɔge daane. Ko ná dae konto, o laam wó ja nmo o ke dedɛɛro wom jeŋa ne se o waare‑m. Wonto de laam maa wó ke nmo o tontoŋeno jeŋa ne, se o ke nmo peena diga ne. 59A tɛ nmo, nmo wó ta‑n wora taa. Nmo ná wo ŋwe jene dem maama ye bi wo daare, ba bá yage‑m.”

english_text:
Turn Back to God
1About this same time Jesus was told that Pilate had given orders for some people from Galilee to be killed while they were offering sacrifices. 2Jesus replied:
Do you think that these people were worse sinners than everyone else in Galilee just because of what happened to them? 3Not at all! But you can be sure that if you don't turn back to God, every one of you will also be killed. 4What about those 18 people who died when the tower in Siloam fell on them? Do you think they were worse than everyone else in Jerusalem? 5Not at all! But you can be sure that if you don't turn back to God, every one of you will also die.
A Story about a Fig Tree
6Jesus then told them this story:
A man had a fig tree growing in his vineyard. One day he went out to pick some figs, but he didn't find any. 7So he said to the gardener, “For three years I have come looking for figs on this tree, and I haven't found any yet. Chop it down! Why should it take up space?”
8The gardener answered, “Master, leave it for another year. I'll dig around it and put some manure on it to make it grow. 9Maybe it will have figs on it next year. If it doesn't, you can have it cut down.”
Healing a Woman on the Sabbath
10One Sabbath, Jesus was teaching in a synagogue, 11and a woman was there who had been crippled by an evil spirit for 18 years. She was completely bent over and could not straighten up. 12When Jesus saw the woman, he called her over and said, “You are now well.” 13He placed his hands on her, and at once she stood up straight and praised God.
14 The man in charge of the synagogue was angry because Jesus had healed someone on the Sabbath. So he said to the people, “Each week has six days when we can work. Come and be healed on one of those days, but not on the Sabbath.”
15The Lord replied, “Are you trying to fool someone? Won't any one of you untie your ox or donkey and lead it out to drink on a Sabbath? 16This woman belongs to the family of Abraham, but Satan has kept her bound for 18 years. Isn't it right to set her free on the Sabbath?” 17Jesus' words made his enemies ashamed. But everyone else in the crowd was happy about the wonderful things he was doing.
A Mustard Seed and Yeast
(Matthew 13.31-33; Mark 4.30-32)
18Jesus said, “What is God's kingdom like? What can I compare it with? 19It is like what happens when someone plants a mustard seed in a garden. The seed grows as big as a tree, and birds nest in its branches.”
20Then Jesus said, “What can I compare God's kingdom with? 21It is like what happens when a woman mixes yeast into three batches of flour. Finally, all the dough rises.”
The Narrow Door
(Matthew 7.13,14,21-23)
22As Jesus was on his way to Jerusalem, he taught the people in the towns and villages. 23Someone asked him, “Lord, are only a few people going to be saved?”
Jesus answered:
24Do all you can to go in by the narrow door! A lot of people will try to get in, but will not be able to. 25Once the owner of the house gets up and locks the door, you will be left standing outside. You will knock on the door and say, “Sir, open the door for us!”
But the owner will answer, “I don't know a thing about you!”
26Then you will start saying, “We dined with you, and you taught in our streets.”
27 But he will say, “I really don't know who you are! Get away from me, you evil people!”
28 Then when you have been thrown outside, you will weep and grit your teeth because you will see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God's kingdom. 29People will come from all directions and sit down to feast in God's kingdom. 30 There the ones who are now least important will be the most important, and those who are now most important will be least important.
Jesus and Herod
31At that time some Pharisees came to Jesus and said, “You had better get away from here, because Herod wants to kill you!”
32Jesus said to them:
Go tell that fox, “I am going to force out demons and heal people today and tomorrow, and three days later I'll be through.” 33But I am going on my way today and tomorrow and the next day. After all, Jerusalem is the place where prophets are killed.
Jesus Loves Jerusalem
(Matthew 23.37-39)
34 Jerusalem, Jerusalem! Your people have killed the prophets and have stoned the messengers who were sent to you. I have often wanted to gather your people, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. But you wouldn't let me. 35 Now your temple will be deserted. You won't see me again until the time when you say,
“Blessed is the one who comes
in the name of the Lord.”
translation_text:
Dé ná wo leiri dé wo, dé wó na chɔgem
1Kanto maŋa kam ne nɔɔna badwonna maa wora ye ba vo ba ta Galili tiina badwonna taane ba bere Yezu. Gɔmena tu Pilata ya jaane banto o go maŋa kalo ba na wora ba kaane Wɛ to, pa se ba jana bam nwoŋi ba gwaane de vara jana. 2Yezu ma leiri nɔɔna bam o we, “Galili tiina banto bam na tiini ba na cham konto dwoŋi to, á boŋe we ko ye ba na tiini ba ye nɔn-chechɔgero ba dwoi ba dwonna bam to ŋwaane mo na? 3Aawo, ko dae konto. Abam tete de ná wo leiri á wo de á keim-balwaaro tem, abam maama de wó na chɔgem. 4Ko ta ná ye nɔɔna fuga-nana balo ya na tege Siloam ne maŋa kam wɛyuu diga na to ba baŋa ne to, á boŋe we ko ye ba na maŋe de chɔgem se ko dwoni ba dwonna Jerusalem tiina to ŋwaane mo na? 5Aawo, ko dae konto. Abam tete ná wo leiri á wo Wɛ ŋwaane, abam maama de wó na chɔgem.”
6Yezu laam ma maŋe memaŋe o bere-ba o we, “Nɔɔno mo wora. O maa jege kaporo o gaare wone. O ma vo se o nii, o wó na ko bia o gwori na. O maa wo nɛ. 7Ko na ba leiri bia to, o ma ta de o gaare tontoŋeno wom o we, ‘Dɔɔm jege bena yatɔ mo amo na tui a lage ko bia ye a ba nae kolokolo. Nam gwoni-ko n de tega ne. Ko zege da kafɛ mo.’ 8Tontoŋeno wom ma leiri‑o o we, ‘Amo tu, yage se ko daa ke bene dedoa. Amo wó ko gwoŋo a gilimi ko maama ye a ke popɔnɔ da. 9Ko ná yi bene dedoa ye ko ná leigi bia, ko wó taa lana. Ko nam ta ná wo leigi, de laam wó gwoni-ko de de tega ne.’ ”
Yezu yɔɔre kaane wodwoŋi siu dɛ ne
10Juu tiina siu dɛ dedwoŋi déem ma yi. Yezu maa wo ba jeerim diga kam ne o bere-ba Wɛ taane. 11Kaane wodwoŋi maa tɔge o wora, chichira na jege‑o ka daana taa, bena fuga-nana, pa se o ye gɔrɔ. Kaane wom maa tiiri tega ne ye o daa ware o kwoni o tete. 12Yezu na nɛ‑o to, o ma ta ded‑o se o ba o tei. O laam ma ta ded‑o o we, “A nakɔ, Wɛ wó pa n sii de n yaara yam.” 13O na tage konto to, o ma daŋe o jea o baŋa ne. Bedwe baŋa ne mo kaane wom kwoni wɛɛne. O laam na dana to, o ma tei Wɛ.
14Jeerim diga kam yuu tu wom na nɛ Yezu na ke tei ba siu dɛ dem ne ye o yɔɔre kaane wom to, o bane ma zaŋe. O ma ta de nɔɔna balo na wo diga kam wone to o we, “Wɛ pɛ debam da yaredo mo se dé taa maa toŋe totoŋa. Konto to, á jege se á ta‑á tui da yam konto ne mo se á na yɔɔrem, se ko dae siu dɛ dem ne.”
15Dé Teiru Yezu ma leiri‑o o we, “Abam ye pipiri-nyena mo! Abam wolo ná jege nabea naa bonaga, n bá‑n sɛ n bwoli-ka n ja n vo buga se ka nyɔ na á siu dɛ dem ne na? 16Konto to, ko chula se a pa kaane wonto sii de o yaara yam siu dɛ dem ne na? Wonto maa ye Abaraham dwi tu ye setaana pɛ ya jege‑o o peene taa, bena fuga-nana. Ko ya chula se a bwoli‑o a yage na?”
17O na tage konto to, ko ma pa balo na ve‑o to na ba chaveera. Ko daare nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maa jege wopwolo dedɛ de wo-kenkagela yalo maama o na ke to.
Wɛ paare dem taane
Matiyu 13:31-33; 7:13-14, 21-23; Maake 4:30-32
18Yezu daa ma ta o we, “Wɛ paare dem ye tetɛ mo? Amo wó ke tɛ mo a maŋe de na ye tei to a bere abam? 19Wɛ paare dem nye de nɔɔno na kwei tio-bu-memeeno o vo o du o kara ne. Tio-bu wom konto ma nwoŋi, ye tio kom tiini ko ji kamunu. Zuna laam ma ba ba sɔ ba pworu da.”
20Yezu daa ta ma ta o we, “Amo ta wó ke tɛ mo a maŋe Wɛ paare dem na ye tei to a bere abam? 21De nye de kaane wodwoŋi na kwei sabɔle o gwaane de bworobworo muni dedɛ tei to. De laam ma pa se bworobworo muni dem maama fole.”
22Yezu déem wo chwoŋa ne o maa vei Jerusalem. O na maa vei to, o tole teene dem maama ye o bere Wɛ taane. 23Nɔɔno wodwoŋi ma bwei‑o o we, “Amo tu, nɔɔna fenfee yerane mo wó na verem na?”
Yezu ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, 24“Ta‑á cho-na á tete se á kwaane á da ni delo na peene to á zo Wɛ woro kom wo. A tɛ abam, nɔɔna dedɛ wó kwaane se ba zo, ye ba bá wane ba na chwoŋa. 25Maŋa kam wó yi, ye sɔŋɔ tu wom zaŋe o pe manchwoŋo kom. Abam laam wó ba á zege pwooni ne á dɔne dɛ sem ye á lwoori‑o á we, ‘Debam tu, popo, pore n pa debam.’ O laam wó leiri o we, ‘Amo nam yeiri abam kɔtaa.’ 26Abam maa wó ta we, ‘Debam ya tɔge de nmo dé jeini dé di wodiu ye dé nyɔa. Ko ye debam teo kom pwooni mo n zege da n bere Wɛ taane.’ 27O nam ta wó leiri abam o we, ‘Amo nam yeiri abam kɔtaa. Lage-na jei! Abam maama ye wo-lwan-keira mo.’
28Ko ná ke abam konto, á wó na Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob na jeini Wɛ woro kom wone, ko woli de faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem maama. Abam tete nam bá na chwoŋa se á zo. Abam wó maŋe dáa ne, yaara na wora pa se nɔɔna keera ye ba done ba nwa mɛ to. 29Nɔɔna wó nwoŋi logo baŋa jei maama ne ba ba ba zo Wɛ woro kom wo, ye ba jeini ba di ywoni daane. 30Nam ta‑á yei-na we, nɔɔna badaara zem na ye kwaga tiina to wó ba ba ji yiga tiina. Badaara de na maŋe ba ye yiga tiina to wó jwoori ba ji kwaga tiina.”
Yezu wo chɔge Jerusalem tiina ŋwaane
Matiyu 23:37-39
31Maŋa kam konto ne Farisi tiina badwonna ma vo Yezu tei ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Yage ywo-seeni se n vo jei sedwoŋi. Pɛ Herodi lage se o pa ba go nmo mo.”
32O ma leiri-ba o we, “Wonto ye nasea mo! Véi-na á ta á bere‑o we, zem da yanto ne amo jege se a taa zeili setaana ye a kwori a yɔɔre nɔɔna jaweero. Da yatɔ ná kɛ, amo laam wó yi a kweelim jeiga. 33Amo nam jege se a daa kwei a chwoŋa a taa kɛa se ko ke da yatɔ, kolo ŋwaane ko bá wane se wolo na ye Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu to ga o ŋwea ye ko dae Jerusalem ne.
34Ei! Jerusalem tiina bam, á yeini á go Wɛ sampwori selo o na toŋe abam tei ne to, ye á dole-ba de kandwa. Kuni dedɛ mo a ya lage se a la abam nɔn-bia a ke daane se a taa nii á baŋa ne, nenɛɛne chworo na kukwori ko bia ko ke ko vɔna kuri ne tei to. Abam maa ba sɛa. 35Wɛ nam wó dɔne o jea abam teo kom baŋa ne se ko ji di-dwonnu. Á ta‑á yei we, á daa bá na-ne se ko taa vei maŋa kalo á na wó ta we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ wolo na tu o yere ŋwaane to swolim.’ ”

english_text:
Jesus Heals a Sick Man
1One Sabbath, Jesus was having dinner in the home of an important Pharisee, and everyone was carefully watching Jesus. 2All of a sudden a man with swollen legs stood up in front of him. 3Jesus turned and asked the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law of Moses, “Is it right to heal on the Sabbath?” 4But they did not say a word.
Jesus took hold of the man. Then he healed him and sent him away. 5 Afterwards, Jesus asked the people, “If your son or ox falls into a well, wouldn't you pull him out at once, even on the Sabbath?” 6There was nothing they could say.
How To Be a Guest
7Jesus saw how the guests had tried to take the best seats. So he told them:
8 When you are invited to a wedding feast, don't sit in the best place. Someone more important may have been invited. 9Then the one who invited you will come and say, “Give your place to this other guest!” You will be embarrassed and will have to sit in the worst place.
10When you are invited to be a guest, go and sit in the worst place. Then the one who invited you may come and say, “My friend, take a better seat!” You will then be honored in front of all the other guests. 11 If you put yourself above others, you will be put down. But if you humble yourself, you will be honored.
12Then Jesus said to the man who had invited him:
When you give a dinner or a banquet, don't invite your friends and family and relatives and rich neighbors. If you do, they will invite you in return, and you will be paid back. 13When you give a feast, invite the poor, the paralyzed, the lame, and the blind. 14They cannot pay you back. But God will bless you and reward you when his people rise from death.
The Great Banquet
(Matthew 22.1-10)
15After Jesus had finished speaking, one of the guests said, “The greatest blessing of all is to be at the banquet in God's kingdom!”
16Jesus told him:
A man once gave a great banquet and invited a lot of guests. 17When the banquet was ready, he sent a servant to tell the guests, “Everything is ready! Please come.”
18One guest after another started making excuses. The first one said, “I bought some land, and I've got to look it over. Please excuse me.”
19Another guest said, “I bought five teams of oxen, and I need to try them out. Please excuse me.”
20Still another guest said, “I've just now married, and I can't be there.”
21The servant told his master what happened, and the master became so angry he said, “Go as fast as you can to every street and alley in town! Bring in everyone who is poor or paralyzed or blind or lame.”
22When the servant returned, he said, “Master, I've done what you told me, and there is still plenty of room for more people.”
23His master then told him, “Go out along the back roads and make people come in, so my house will be full. 24Not one of the guests I first invited will get even a bite of my food!”
Being a Disciple
(Matthew 10.37,38)
25Large crowds were walking along with Jesus, when he turned and said:
26 You cannot be my disciple, unless you love me more than you love your father and mother, your wife and children, and your brothers and sisters. You cannot follow me unless you love me more than you love your own life.
27 You cannot be my disciple unless you carry your own cross and follow me.
28Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. What is the first thing you will do? Won't you sit down and figure out how much it will cost and if you have enough money to pay for it? 29Otherwise, you will start building the tower, but not be able to finish. Then everyone who sees what is happening will laugh at you. 30They will say, “You started building, but could not finish the job.”
31What will a king do if he has only 10,000 soldiers to defend himself against a king who is about to attack him with 20,000 soldiers? Before he goes out to battle, won't he first sit down and decide if he can win? 32If he thinks he won't be able to defend himself, he will send messengers and ask for peace while the other king is still a long way off. 33So then, you cannot be my disciple unless you give away everything you own.
Salt and Light
(Matthew 5.13; Mark 9.50)
34Salt is good, but if it no longer tastes like salt, how can it be made to taste salty again? 35It is no longer good for the soil or even for the manure pile. People simply throw it out. If you have ears, pay attention!
translation_text:
Yezu vei Farisi tu sɔŋɔ
1Siu dɛ dedwoŋi déem ma yi. Yezu ma vo Farisi tiina nadum sɔŋɔ o zo se o di wodiu. O na wora to, nɔɔna maa kwaane ba yere‑o se ba nii o na wó ke tei to. 2Na-dea tu maa tɔge o jei da. 3Yezu na nɛ‑o to, o ma bwei Wɛ nia zamesem tiina bam de Farisi tiina bam o we, “Nɔɔno jege chwoŋa se o yɔɔre o dwoŋi siu dɛ dem ne naa ko chula?” 4Ba ma chem. O laam ma ja nɔɔno wom o pa o na yazura ye o yage‑o se o viiri.
5O laam ma bwei-ba o we, “Abam wolo bu ná to vole wone siu dɛ dem ne, n bá‑n ke lela n vo n vaŋe‑o n le na? Ko ná ye n nabea de, n bá‑n ke konto na?” 6Ba maa ware ba leiri‑o kolokolo.
7Nɔɔna balo na tu se ba tɔge ba di wodiu Farisi tu wom sɔŋɔ ne to ma zo ba lage jeiŋa jei. Yezu ma na we ko ye jei-laao jei ne mo ba lage se ba jeini da. O na nɛ konto to, o ma maŋe memaŋe o bere-ba o we: 8“Nɔɔno ná ke kadiri ye o bwoŋi‑m se n ba n di, yé kwaane n jeini nɔn-kamuna jeiŋa jei ne. Nmo ná ke konto, ye nɔn-yero ná tua, 9ko laam wó pa se n na n chaveera mo. Sɔŋɔ tu wolo na bwoŋi abam maama to wó ba o ta de nmo o we, ‘Zaŋe se n daare jei n pa nɔn-yero konto.’ Nmo laam wó nwoŋi n vo n jeini kwaga kwaga de n chaveera yam.
10Ko daare, ba ná bwoŋi‑m se n vo n di, vei n jeini kwaga kwaga. Nmo ná ke konto, ye sɔŋɔ tu wom ná tu o na‑m, o laam wó ta we, ‘A badwoŋi, zaŋe n ba yiga n jeini.’ Konto wó pa se n na zula nɔɔna bam maama yiga ne. 11Kolo ŋwaane, wolo ná bere o tete kamunim, konto tu wó ba o ji nɔn-balaŋa mo. Wolo nam ná gwooni o tete, Wɛ wó zeiŋi konto tu nɔɔna yiga ne.”
12Yezu laam ma ta de sɔŋɔ tu wom o we, “Nmo ná lage n ke wodi-fɔrɔ n pa nɔɔna, se n yé bwoŋi n badwonna bam, de n chorro tem, de n dwonna naduna bam se ba ba ba di. Nmo ná ke konto, banto wó wane ba jwoori ba ke‑m konto dwoŋi ba ŋwe jene dem. 13Nmo nam ná lage n ke kuri, se n bwoŋi balo na ye yiniga tiina, de gwaaro, de gwane, de lilwoa, se ba ba ba di. 14Nmo ná ke konto, nmo wó ta‑n jege yu-ywoŋo. Nɔɔna banto dwoŋi bá wane ba jwoori ba ŋwe nmo jene dem. Maŋa kam Wɛ na wó pa nɔn-ŋona bi toone wone to, nmo nam wó jwoŋi n keim dem kwora.”
15Nɔɔno wodwoŋi na tɔge o jei Yezu tei ne o di to ma ni o na tage kolo to. O ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nɔɔno wolo maama na zo Wɛ woro kom wo o jeini o di ywoni dáane to mo ye yu-ywoŋo tu.”
16Yezu ma ma memaŋe o leiri o we: “Nɔɔno wodwoŋi ya wora o na lage o ke wodi-fɔrɔ o pa o dwonna. O ma bwoŋi nɔɔna dedɛ se ba ba ba di. 17Kuri dem maŋa na yi to, o ma toŋe o tontoŋeno se o vo o ta de balo o na bwoŋi to o we, woŋo maama ti ko yiga se ba laam ba. 18Nɔɔna bam na nigi konto to, ba maama maa wora ba lwoori chwoŋa o tei ne. Ba dedoa maa we, ‘Leile konto a nɛ kara mo se a va. Amo jege se a vo dáane mo. Popo, pa-ne chwoŋa.’ 19Nɔɔno wodwoŋi de maa we, ‘Leile konto a yeigi nabɛ fuga mo se a ma va. Amo wo chwoŋa ne mo se a vo a ke a nii. Popo, pa-ne chwoŋa.’ 20Nɔɔno wodwoŋi de ma ta o we, ‘Leile konto a di kaane mo. Amo daa bá wane a ba.’
21Tontoŋeno wom laam ma jwoori sɔŋɔ o vo o ta de o tu wom ko na ke tei to. Sɔŋɔ tu wom na nigi to, o bane ma zaŋe. O ma ta de o tontoŋeno wom o we, o nwoŋi lela o vo teo kom pwooni jei maama o la yiniga tiina, de gwaaro, de lilwoa, de gwane o pa ba ba ba di. 22Tontoŋeno wom na ke konto to, o ma ta o we, ‘Amo tu, a ke kolo maama nmo na tage to, ye laŋa daa ta daare se nɔɔna jeini da.’
23Sɔŋɔ tu wom daa ma ta ded‑o o we, ‘Nwoŋi teo kom wo n vo n beeri kare sem wone, de gaao chwei sem maama ni ne, se n pa balo na wora to ba ba zo a sɔŋɔ kom se laŋa daa yé daare. 24Amo tɛ abam we, ko ná ye nɔɔna balo a ya na bwoŋi ye ba ve to, banto wolowolo bá na jeiga amo sɔŋɔ ne se ba tɔge ba di.’ ”
Dé wó seene dé yia dé taa tɔge Yezu
Matiyu 10:37-38
25Yezu na wo chwoŋa ne o maa vei to, nɔn-kɔgɔ dedɛ maa tɔge o kwaga. O ma pipiri o nii ba seeni ye o we, 26“Nɔɔno wolo ná tu amo tei, ye o ná wo ve o kwo, de o nu, de o kaane, de o bia, de o zembaara, de o nyaana, de o nakwa, ye o ná wo ve o tete boboŋa de, konto tu bá wane o ji amo kwaga tɔgeno. 27Wolo maama ná tɔge amo kwaga ye o ná wo sɛ se o na yaara, ne wolo na zeŋe dagara o maa vei o toone tei to, konto tu bá wane o ji amo kwaga tɔgeno.
28Abam wolo ná boŋe se o lɔ wɛyuu di-dedɔrɔ, nmo laam wó bobo n jeini n jeeli n nii, sabu kom wó wane diga kam ko lɔ ko ti naa ko bá wane. Ko dae konto na? 29N ná wo ke konto, ye n ná chwi diga kam kuri ye ka lɔɔm daa ware ko guri, balo maama na lɔre to wó taa mɔne‑m, 30ye ba we, ‘Nɔɔno wonto bobo diga lɔɔm ye o ware o guri-ka.’
31Ko woli da, pɛ ná lage o ke jara de pɛ wodwoŋi, o laam wó bobo o jeini o bwɛ o nii, nɔɔna morro fuga (10,000) balo na wo o kwaga ne to wó wane ba jeeri nɔɔna morro finlei (20,000) balo na wo pɛ wodwoŋi wom kwaga ne to naa ba bá wane. Ko dae chega na? 32O nam ná bá wane, pɛ wodwoŋi wom ta ná wo yiga yiga o beena, o wó toŋe tontoŋena o tei ne se ba kwoori‑o se o yage jara yam. 33Tɔ. Ko ye bedwe mo de abam wolo maama ná wo kwei o woŋo maama o yage dáa ne, kotu bá wane o ji amo kwaga tɔgeno.
34Yɛ lamma ye de wae de kwɛ wodiu. Yɛ ni nam ná ti, n daa‑n bá‑n wane n pa de jwoori de ja ni. 35Dento daa ba jege kuri. N bá‑n wane n ke-de n kaduga ne, naa n ma n ke popɔnɔ. Nmo jege se n lwo-de n yage mo.
Abam nam fɔge á cheigi amo taane dem.”

english_text:
One Sheep
(Matthew 18.12-14)
1 Tax collectors and sinners were all crowding around to listen to Jesus. 2So the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law of Moses started grumbling, “This man is friendly with sinners. He even eats with them.”
3Then Jesus told them this story:
4If any of you has 100 sheep, and one of them gets lost, what will you do? Won't you leave the 99 in the field and go look for the lost sheep until you find it? 5And when you find it, you will be so glad that you will put it on your shoulder 6and carry it home. Then you will call in your friends and neighbors and say, “Let's celebrate! I've found my lost sheep.”
7Jesus said, “In the same way there is more happiness in heaven because of one sinner who turns to God than over 99 good people who don't need to.”
One Coin
8Jesus told the people another story:
What will a woman do if she has ten silver coins and loses one of them? Won't she light a lamp, sweep the floor, and look carefully until she finds it? 9Then she will call in her friends and neighbors and say, “Let's celebrate! I've found the coin I lost.”
10Jesus said, “In the same way God's angels are happy when even one person turns to him.”
Two Sons
11Jesus told them yet another story:
Once a man had two sons. 12The younger son said to his father, “Give me my share of the property.” So the father divided his property between his two sons.
13Not long after that, the younger son packed up everything he owned and left for a foreign country, where he wasted all his money in wild living. 14He had spent everything, when a bad famine spread through that whole land. Soon he had nothing to eat.
15He went to work for a man in that country, and the man sent him out to take care of his pigs. 16He would have been glad to eat what the pigs were eating, but no one gave him a thing.
17Finally, he came to his senses and said, “My father's workers have plenty to eat, and here I am, starving to death! 18I will go to my father and say to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against God in heaven and against you. 19I am no longer good enough to be called your son. Treat me like one of your workers.’ ”
20The younger son got up and started back to his father. But when he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt sorry for him. He ran to his son and hugged and kissed him.
21The son said, “Father, I have sinned against God in heaven and against you. I am no longer good enough to be called your son.”
22But his father said to the servants, “Hurry and bring the best clothes and put them on him. Give him a ring for his finger and sandals for his feet. 23Get the best calf and prepare it, so we can eat and celebrate. 24This son of mine was dead, but has now come back to life. He was lost and has now been found.” And they began to celebrate.
25The older son had been out in the field. But when he came near the house, he heard the music and dancing. 26So he called one of the servants over and asked, “What's going on here?”
27The servant answered, “Your brother has come home safe and sound, and your father ordered us to kill the best calf.” 28The older brother got so angry that he would not even go into the house.
His father came out and begged him to go in. 29But he said to his father, “For years I have worked for you like a slave and have always obeyed you. But you have never even given me a little goat, so that I could give a dinner for my friends. 30This other son of yours wasted your money on prostitutes. And now that he has come home, you ordered the best calf to be killed for a feast.”
31His father replied, “My son, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours. 32But we should be glad and celebrate! Your brother was dead, but he is now alive. He was lost and has now been found.”
translation_text:
Pi-jia kam memaŋe
Matiyu 18:12-14
1Dɛ dedwe lampwoo lara de nɔn-chechɔgero dedɛ ma fɔɔre ba yi Yezu tei se ba cheigi o kwora. 2Farisi tiina de Wɛ nia zamesem tiina na nɛ konto to, ba maa poona ba we, “Ta‑á nii nɔɔno wonto na yeini o jeeri nɔn-chechɔgero lanyerane, ye o ta kwori o di wodiu de-ba.”
3Yezu laam ma maŋe memaŋe o bere-ba o we: 4“Abam wolo ná jege pei bi (100), ye se dedoa ná jei, o bá yage pei funogo-nogo sem (99) gaao ne, ye o daare o vo o beeri pi-jia kam na? 5O nam ná beeri o na-ka, o laam wó kwei-ka o daŋe o bakala baŋa ne de wopwolo 6o ja vo sɔŋɔ. O ná tu o yi sɔŋɔ, o wó bwoŋi o badwonna de o sɔŋɔ tiina maama ye o ta de-ba o we, ‘Á pa se dé di ywoni daane, amo na nɛ a pia kalo ya na jei to ŋwaane.’
7Tɔ. A tɛ abam we, ko ye bedwe mo de nɔn-chechɔgɔ dedoa ná leiri o wo Wɛ ŋwaane, ko wó pa se ywoni taa daga Wɛ telaao ne. Ba wó taa jege wopwolo dedɛ ded‑o se ko dwoni nɔn-laaro funogo-nogo (99) na ba boŋe se ba leiri ba wo Wɛ ŋwaane to.
Sabu-jiu kom memaŋe
8Ko woli da, kaane ná jege sabu-dala fuga, ye dedoa ná jei, o bá tɔre kanea ye o zuri o yera o zɔre sɔŋɔ kom wo maama se o nii, o wó na-de na? 9O nam ná nɛ-de, o laam wó bwoŋi o badwonna de o sɔŋɔ tiina maama, ye o ta de-ba o we, ‘Á pa se dé di ywoni daane, amo na nɛ sabu-dale delo ya na jei to ŋwaane.’
10Tɔ. A tɛ abam chega ŋwaane to, nɔn-chechɔgɔ dedoa ná leiri o wo Wɛ ŋwaane, ko pa se wopwolo dedɛ wora Wɛ malese sem tei ne.”
Bu-jiu kom memaŋe
11Yezu daa ta ma ta o we: “Nɔɔno mo wora o na jege bakeiri selei. 12Dɛ dedwe nyaane wom ma zaŋe o ta de o kwo o we, ‘Amo kwo, a lwoori‑m se n pɔɔre amo teiri nmo wonnu tem wone n pa-ne leile konto.’ O kwo ma sɛ. O ma pɔɔre o jejegero tem o pa o bia balei bam.
13Ko na ke da yalei to, nyaane wom ma zaŋe o kwaleme o wonnu maama o ja nwoŋi o vo sa-teo yiga yiga. O maa zoore da ye o ke poweeni yerane. O maa jege o wonnu tem o chɔge yɔɔ yɔɔ. 14O wonnu tem laam ma ba te chɔge te ti maama. Kana ma tiini ka zo teo kom ye o daa ba jege kolokolo. 15O ma vo teo kom nɔɔno dedoa tei o lwoori‑o wolim. Nɔɔno wom ma pa se o vo o tɔge o teira gaao ne. 16Kana na tiini ka chɛ o yera ne to, o ma boŋe se o tɔge o di teira yam so-porro tem. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa ba pa‑o kolokolo se o di. 17O boboŋa laam ma jwoori. O ma bwɛ o tete ne o we, ‘Amo kwo yeini o pae o tontoŋena bam maama wodiiru dedɛ pa se ba di ba daara. Ko daare amo wo ywo-seeni ye kana wora ka go-ne. 18Amo jege se a zaŋe a jwoori a vo a kwo tei ye a ta ded‑o we, “Amo kwo, a tusi a chɔge Wɛ yiga, ye a ta ke a chɔge nmo wo. 19Konto to, amo daa ba jege kuri se n ke-ne ne nmo bu tei. Nam pa se a taa tɔge a ye nmo tontoŋena bam dedoa.” ’
20O na boŋe konto to, o laam ma zaŋe o maa vei o kwo tei. O ta na wo yiga yiga to mo o kwo wom nɛ‑o. O na nɛ‑o to, o bu wom ŋwaŋa ma zo‑o lanyerane. O ma zaŋe o duri o vo o jeeri o bu wom o kukwori‑o de wopwolo dedɛ. 21Bu wom laam ma ta ded‑o o we, ‘Amo kwo, a tusi a chɔge Wɛ yiga, ye a ta ke a chɔge nmo wo. Konto to, amo daa ba jege kuri se n ke-ne ne nmo bu tei.’ 22O kwo wom ma ta de o sɔŋɔ tontoŋena bam o we, ‘Á ke lela á zo á kwei gare-dedɔrɔ kolo na tiini ko lana to á ja ba á zo‑o. Kwei-na jafolo á ke o jeŋa ne, se á kwei natera de á pa o zo. 23Véi-na á ja na-paale kamunu kom á ja ba á go, se dé ma ke wodi-fɔrɔ dé di se dé daare dé kwɛɛre o ŋwaane. 24Kolo ŋwaane amo bu wonto ya tege mo ye o laam jwoori o bi. O ya jei mo ye a laam na‑o.’ Ba ma bobo wodiiru tem dim ye ba kwɛɛra.
25Maŋa kalo nyaane wom na tu o yi sɔŋɔ konto to, o zembaaro wom ya wo kara ne mo o vara. O na nwoŋi kara kam ne o maa beene sɔŋɔ to mo o nigi ba na mage wonnu ye ba sae. 26O ma bwoŋi o kwo tontoŋena bam dedoa o bwei‑o woŋo kolo na ke ye ba kwɛɛre to. 27Tontoŋeno wom ma leiri‑o o we, ‘Nmo nyaane wom mo tua. Nmo kwo ma ja na-paale kamunu kom o go se ba di, o na nɛ‑o ye o ŋwe de yazura to ŋwaane.’
28Bu-kwea kam na nigi konto to, o bane ma zaŋe. O maa ba lage se o zo diga. O kwo wom ma nwoŋi o vo o kwoori‑o se o zo. 29O ma ta de o kwo wom o we, ‘Ta‑n nii, bena yanto maama amo tiini a toŋe dedɛ a pa nmo. Amo yeini a sɛ nmo ni maŋa maama. Nmo nam wo pɛ-ne varem se a go, se amo de a badwonna ma di ywoni daane, de bo-bala de. 30Ko daare nmo bu wonto na tu to, n jaane na-paale kamunu kom n go n pa‑o, ye o ye wolo na kwei nmo wonnu tem o vo o chɔge ka-bworru baŋa ne ye o laam jwoori o ba to.’
31O kwo wom ma leiri‑o o we, ‘Amo bu, nmo maŋe n wo amo tei ne maŋa maama. Wonnu telo maama amo na jege to ye nmo nyem. 32Dé zem nam jege se dé di ywoni ye dé kwɛɛre, kolo ŋwaane nmo nyaane wom ya tege mo ye o jwoori o bi. O ya jei mo ye dé daa na‑o.’ ”

english_text:
A Dishonest Manager
1Jesus said to his disciples:
A rich man once had a manager to take care of his business. But he was told that his manager was wasting money. 2So the rich man called him in and said, “What is this I hear about you? Tell me what you have done! You are no longer going to work for me.”
3The manager said to himself, “What shall I do now that my master is going to fire me? I can't dig ditches, and I'm ashamed to beg. 4I know what I'll do, so that people will welcome me into their homes after I've lost my job.”
5Then one by one he called in the people who were in debt to his master. He asked the first one, “How much do you owe my master?”
6“A hundred barrels of olive oil,” the man answered.
So the manager said, “Take your bill and sit down and quickly write ‘50.’ ”
7The manager asked someone else who was in debt to his master, “How much do you owe?”
“A thousand sacks of wheat,” the man replied.
The manager said, “Take your bill and write ‘800.’ ”
8The master praised his dishonest manager for looking out for himself so well. That's how it is! The people of this world look out for themselves better than the people who belong to the light.
9 My disciples, I tell you to use wicked wealth to make friends for yourselves. Then when it is gone, you will be welcomed into an eternal home. 10Anyone who can be trusted in little matters can also be trusted in important matters. But anyone who is dishonest in little matters will be dishonest in important matters. 11If you cannot be trusted with this wicked wealth, who will trust you with true wealth? 12And if you cannot be trusted with what belongs to someone else, who will give you something that will be your own? 13 You cannot be the slave of two masters. You will like one more than the other or be more loyal to one than to the other. You cannot serve God and money.
Some Sayings of Jesus
(Matthew 11.12,13; 5.31,32; Mark 10.11,12)
14The Pharisees really loved money. So when they heard what Jesus said, they made fun of him. 15But Jesus told them:
You are always making yourselves look good, but God sees what is in your heart. The things that most people think are important are worthless as far as God is concerned.
16 Until the time of John the Baptist, people had to obey the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets. But since God's kingdom has been preached, everyone is trying hard to get in. 17 Heaven and earth will disappear before the smallest letter of the Law does.
18 It is a terrible sin for a man to divorce his wife and marry another woman. It is also a terrible sin for a man to marry a divorced woman.
Lazarus and the Rich Man
19There was once a rich man who wore expensive clothes and every day ate the best food. 20But a poor beggar named Lazarus was brought to the gate of the rich man's house. 21He was happy just to eat the scraps that fell from the rich man's table. His body was covered with sores, and dogs kept coming up to lick them. 22 The poor man died, and angels took him to the place of honor next to Abraham.
The rich man also died and was buried. 23 He went to hell and was suffering terribly. When he looked up and saw Abraham far off and Lazarus at his side, 24he said to Abraham, “Have pity on me! Send Lazarus to dip his finger in water and touch my tongue. I'm suffering terribly in this fire.”
25Abraham answered, “My friend, remember that while you lived, you had everything good, and Lazarus had everything bad. Now he is happy, and you are in pain. 26And besides, there is a deep ditch between us, and no one from either side can cross over.”
27But the rich man said, “Abraham, then please send Lazarus to my father's home. 28Let him warn my five brothers, so they won't come to this horrible place.”
29Abraham answered, “Your brothers can read what Moses and the prophets wrote. They should pay attention to that.”
30Then the rich man said, “No, that's not enough! If only someone from the dead would go to them, they would listen and turn to God.”
31So Abraham said, “If they won't pay attention to Moses and the prophets, they won't listen even to someone who comes back from the dead.”
translation_text:
Tontoŋeno de o jene memaŋe
1Yezu daa ta ma ta de o kwaga tɔgena bam o we: “Nadum mo wora o na jege o tontoŋeno. O tontoŋeno wom mo nii o wonnu maama baŋa ne. Nɔɔna badwonna ma vo ba ta de nadum wom ba we, o tontoŋeno wom jege o wonnu tem o chɔga. 2O ma bwoŋi o tontoŋeno wom ye o ta ded‑o o we, ‘Amo nigi nmo na ke tei to. Nmo nam wó ta bɛ mo? Nam véi n jeeli nmo na ke tei de a wonnu tem se n laam ba n bere-ne. Nmo daa‑n bá‑n wane n ta‑n ye amo tontoŋeno.’
3Tontoŋeno wom ma bwɛ o tete ne o we, ‘Amo nam wó ke tɛ mo? Amo tu wom lage o le-ne o totoŋa yam ne. Amo ba dana se a wane a va. Chaveera maa jege-ne se a taa kare a lwoora. 4Amo nam yei a na wó ke tei se, o ná le-ne a totoŋe dem ne, se nɔɔna taa jeeri-ne lanyerane ba sam ne to.’
5O na boŋe konto to, o ma bwoŋi balo na jege o tu wom jene to dedoa dedoa pa se ba ba o tei. O ma bwei boboa nɔɔno wom o we, ‘Nmo jege amo tu wom jene ko maŋe tɛ ta mo?’ 6Nɔɔno wom ma leiri o we, ‘Ko ye nuga garewɛ bi (100) mo.’ Tontoŋeno wom ma ta‑o we, ‘Nii tɔnɔ kolo nmo jene dem na popone da to. Nam kwei n ja n vo n jeini n popone we, garewɛ finnu (50).’
7O daa ta ma bwei nɔɔno wodwoŋi o we, ‘Nmo jege amo tu wom jene ko maŋe tɛ ta mo?’ O ma leiri o we, ‘Ko ye mena ywollu bi (100) mo.’ Tontoŋeno wom ma ta‑o we, ‘Kwei tɔnɔ kom n popone we, ywollu funɔnɔ (80).’
8Nadum wom na lɔre o tontoŋeno-balɔrɔ kom na ke tei to, o maa we o tiini o kwaane dedɛ de o na mɛ o swa o lɔre o na wó ke tei to. Kokuri mo, balo na jege kugu jei logo baŋa ne to yeini ba ma swa mo de ba na ke ba dwonna tei to, se ko dwoni balo na ye Wɛ pwooni dem nyem to na ke tei.
9Amo nam tɛ abam we, á jege se á kwei logo baŋa sabu á ma á woli nɔɔna se ko pa á di badwoŋo daane. Á ná ke konto, ye á sabu kom ta ná ba jege kuri ko pa abam, ba laam wó jeeri abam lanyerane Wɛ sɔŋɔ ne se á ta‑á wora taa wuu. 10Nɔɔno wolo na tɔge chega de woŋo fenfee to wó taa tɔge chega de wo-kamunnu mo. Ko daare wolo na ba tɔge chega de woŋo fenfee to bá taa tɔge chega de wo-kamunnu. 11Konto to, abam ná ware á tɔge chega de logo baŋa sabu, Wɛ bá sɛ se o kwei jejegero telo na ye chekke to o ke abam jeŋa ne. 12Abam ná ware á tɔge chega de wonnu telo ba na kwei ba ke abam jeŋa ne se á nii te baŋa ne to, Wɛ bá sɛ se o pa abam wonnu telo na wó taa ye abam tete nyem to.
13Sɔŋɔ tontoŋeno bá wane o kwei boboŋe dedwe se o ma toŋe o pa o yuu tiina balei. O wó taa chuli dedoa kam ye o daare o swoi wodwoŋi wom, naa o wó taa nege dedoa kam ye o daare o gwooni wodwoŋi wom. Konto ŋwaane, abam bá wane á pa se Wɛ taa ye á tu, ye á daare á tɔge sabu-laga de.”
14 Farisi tiina na wora to ma ni Yezu na tage kolo maama to. Ba na ye sabu-lagena to, ba maa jege‑o ba mɔna. 15O ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam mo lage se á bere á tete nɔɔna yiga ne we á jege chega. Wɛ nam yei á bochara na ye tei to. Woŋo kolo nɔɔna na pae ko ye wo-kamunu to mo ye wo-zɔɔne Wɛ tei ne.
16Wɛ sɛɛm tu Jɔn ta na wo tu to, nɔɔna déem jege Moses nia yam de faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem na bere kolo to mo ba tɔga. Ko zege maŋa kalo Jɔn na tu to, ko ye Wɛ paare dem kwor-ywoŋa kam mo wora se nɔɔna sɛ-ka. Nɔɔna maama tiini ba kwaane se ba tɔge ba zo Wɛ woro kom wo.
17Wɛyuu de tega baŋa ná lage te jei, konto wó taa ye mɔle ko dwoi woŋo fenfee ná lage ko le Wɛ nia yam wone.
18Nɔɔno wolo ná yage o kaane ye o daare o di kaane wodwoŋi, konto tu keim dem de kabwoŋa ye bedwe mo. Nɔɔno wolo ná zaŋe o di kaane wolo o tete baro na yage‑o to, konto tu keim dem de bwoŋa de ye bedwe mo.”
Nadum de yiniga tu memaŋe
19Yezu ta ma ta o we, “Nadum mo wora. O ma yeini o zo gare-nyenno telo na tiini te lana to. Dɛ maama mo o nae ywoni ye o di o ni. 20Yiniga tu de maa wora, o yere mo Lazaru. O yera yam maama jege ŋɔna. Nɔɔna ma yeini ba ja‑o ba vo ba tiŋi nadum wom sɔŋɔ woro ne se o taa lwoora. 21O maa lage se o taa di wodiu kolo nadum wom na di ye ko siiri tega ne to mo. Kukuri de maa tui se deilimi o ŋɔna yam.
