O ma kwoni o yuu wɛɛne o yɔɔre o nii Wɛ telaao seeni o na Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ na daga tei to. O ma daare o nii o na Yezu na zege Baŋa Wɛ jazem seeni tei to. 56O laam ma ta o we, “Nii-na! Amo nɛ Wɛ telaao ni na pore, ye Nabiin-bu wom zege Wɛ jazem seeni.”
57Nɔɔna bam na nigi konto to, ba ma laare baŋa baŋa de kwor-dɛa, ye ba pu ba zwa se ba daa yé taa ni o taane dem. Ba maama ma duri bedwe baŋa ne ba vo ba zi‑o. 58Ba ma zeili-o pa o nwoŋi da teo kom wone. Ba laam ma daare ba jege‑o ba dola de kandwa se ba go. Balo na wora to ma le ba gwaaro ba pa nɔn-doŋo kodwoŋi se o taa nia. Nɔɔno wom yere mo Sɔɔl. 59Ba na jege Stiiven ba dola konto to, o ma lwoori Wɛ o we, “Amo Teiru Yezu, jwoŋi amo jworo.”
60O laam ma kuni dwoona tega ne o laare de kwor-dɛa o we, “Amo Teiru, nam yé kwei banto keim-lwanno tem n ke n boboŋa ne.” O déem tage konto mo ye o daare o te.

english_text:
1-2Saul approved the stoning of Stephen. Some faithful followers of the Lord buried Stephen and mourned very much for him.
Saul Makes Trouble for the Church
At that time the church in Jerusalem suffered terribly. All of the Lord's followers, except the apostles, were scattered everywhere in Judea and Samaria. 3 Saul started making a lot of trouble for the church. He went from house to house, arresting men and women and putting them in jail.
The Good News Is Preached in Samaria
4The Lord's followers who had been scattered went from place to place, telling the good news. 5Philip went to the city of Samaria and told the people about Christ. 6They crowded around Philip because they were eager to hear what he was saying and to see him work miracles. 7Many people with evil spirits were healed, and the spirits went out of them with a shout. A lot of paralyzed and lame people were also healed. 8Everyone in that city was very glad because of what was happening.
9For some time a man named Simon had lived there and had amazed the people of Samaria. He practiced witchcraft and claimed to be somebody great. 10Everyone, rich and poor, crowded around him. They said, “This man is the power of God called ‘The Great Power.’ ”
11For a long time, Simon had used witchcraft to amaze the people, and they kept crowding around him. 12But when they believed what Philip was saying about God's kingdom and about the name of Jesus Christ, they were all baptized. 13Even Simon believed and was baptized. He stayed close to Philip, because he marveled at all the miracles and wonders.
14The apostles in Jerusalem heard that some people in Samaria had accepted God's message, and they sent Peter and John. 15When the two apostles arrived, they prayed that these people would be given the Holy Spirit. 16Before this, the Holy Spirit had not been given to any of them, though some of them had been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. 17Peter and John then placed their hands on everyone who had faith in the Lord, and they were given the Holy Spirit.
18Simon noticed that the Spirit was given only when the apostles placed their hands on the people. So he brought money 19and said to Peter and John, “Let me have this power too! Then anyone I place my hands on will also be given the Holy Spirit.”
20Peter said to him, “You and your money will both end up in hell if you think you can buy God's gift! 21You don't have any part in this, and God sees that your heart isn't right. 22Get rid of these evil thoughts and ask God to forgive you. 23I can see that you are jealous and bound by your evil ways.”
24Simon said, “Please pray to the Lord, so that what you said won't happen to me.”
25After Peter and John had preached about the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem. On their way they told the good news in many villages of Samaria.
Philip and an Ethiopian Official
26The Lord's angel said to Philip, “Go south along the desert road that leads from Jerusalem to Gaza.” 27So Philip left.
An important Ethiopian official happened to be going along that road in his chariot. He was the chief treasurer for Candace, the Queen of Ethiopia. The official had gone to Jerusalem to worship 28and was now on his way home. He was sitting in his chariot, reading the book of the prophet Isaiah.
29The Spirit told Philip to catch up with the chariot. 30Philip ran up close and heard the man reading aloud from the book of Isaiah. Philip asked him, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
31The official answered, “How can I understand unless someone helps me?” He then invited Philip to come up and sit beside him.
32 The man was reading the passage that said,
“He was led like a sheep
on its way to be killed.
He was silent as a lamb
whose wool
is being cut off,
and he did not say
a word.
33He was treated like a nobody
and did not receive
a fair trial.
How can he have children,
if his life
is snatched away?”
34The official said to Philip, “Tell me, was the prophet talking about himself or about someone else?” 35So Philip began at this place in the Scriptures and explained the good news about Jesus.
36-37As they were going along the road, they came to a place where there was some water. The official said, “Look! Here is some water. Why can't I be baptized?” 38He ordered the chariot to stop. Then they both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
39After they had come out of the water, the Lord's Spirit took Philip away. The official never saw him again, but he was very happy as he went on his way.
40Philip later appeared in Azotus. He went from town to town, all the way to Caesarea, telling people about Jesus.
translation_text:
1Sɔɔl déem ma na ba na ke tei ba go Stiiven to, ye o sɛ ba keim dem.
Yezu nɔɔna bam nɛ yaara
Dɛ dem konto ne Yezu kɔgɔ kom nɔɔna balo na wo Jerusalem ne to laam ma bobo se ba na yaara dedɛ nɔɔna tei ne. Ba maama ma jage ba duri ba zo teene delo maama na wo Judea de Samaria ne to wone. Ko daare Yezu totoŋa nakwa bam yerane mo wo tɔge ba duri. 2Nɔɔna badwonna na kɔre Wɛ to ma kwei Stiiven yera yam ba suli, ye ba daare ba keeri‑o lanyerane. 3Sɔɔl ma kwaane se o chɔge Yezu kɔgɔ kom maama. O maa yeini o tole sam dem wone o jaane balo na tɔge Yezu to o vei o ke peena diga ne, baara de kaana maama.
Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam jage
4Yezu nɔɔna balo na duri ba jage to maa yeini ba vei jei maama ba tɔɔle Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam. 5Filipi ma zaŋe o vo Samaria teo kodwoŋi o ta Wɛ Dam Tu Krista taane o bere nɔɔna bam. 6Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom ma seene ba yia ba cheigi Filipi na ŋɔɔne kolo to. Ba maama déem cheigi o taane dem ye ba kwori ba na wo-kenkagela yalo o na ke to. 7Ba ma na chichiri na yage nɔɔna dedɛ ye se chwoosi baŋa baŋa. Gwaaro dedɛ, de gwane de ma na yazura. 8Konto ŋwaane wopwolo déem maa tiini ko wora Samaria tiina bam tei ne.
9Teo kom konto ne nɔɔno déem ya wora, o yere mo Simon. O maa pae se Samaria tiina bam ye yaau o liri kikia baŋa ne. O déem bere o tete we o ye nɔn-kamunu mo. 10Teo kom nɔɔna maama ma kwaane ba cheigi‑o lanyerane, dedɛɛra de nabwona maama. Ba maa pae se Wɛ dam mo wo o tei ne, ye ba jege‑o ba bwoi we ‘Dam-fɔrɔ tu’. 11O déem ya pɛ se ba ye yaau de o liri sem taa, se ko dáane dedɛ. Konto ŋwaane mo ba déem seene ba yia ba cheigi‑o lanyerane.
12Filipi laam ma ba o da Yezu Krista yere dem ŋwaane o tɔɔle Wɛ paare dem kwor-ywoŋa kam. Nɔɔna bam ma sɛ o taane dem. Ba ma jwoŋi sɛɛm Yezu ŋwaane, baara de kaana de. 13Simon tete de ma sɛ ye o daare o jwoŋi sɛɛm. O ma tɔge dedaane Filipi ye o na wo-kenkagela de maana yalo o na ke ye ya bere Wɛ dam to. O na nɛ-ya to, ko ma ke‑o yaau.
14Yezu totoŋa nakwa bam na wo Jerusalem ne to ma ni we Samaria tiina bam tu ba sɛ Wɛ taane dem. Ba ma toŋe Piita de Jɔn se ba vo ba nii. 15Ba na vei ba yi da to, ba ma lwoori Wɛ ba pa balo na sɛ Yezu to, se ba wane ba jwoŋi Wɛ Sin-laao kom. 16Kolo ŋwaane Wɛ Sin-laao kom daa ta wo tu banto wolowolo tei. Ba na jwoŋi sɛɛm to déem ye dé Teiru Yezu yere ŋwaane yerane mo. 17Piita de Jɔn laam ma daŋe ba jea ba baŋa ne pa ba jwoŋi Wɛ Sin-laao kom ba bochara ne.
18Yezu totoŋa nakwa bam na daŋe ba jea nɔɔna bam baŋa ne pa ba jwoŋi Wɛ Sin-laao kom konto to, Simon ma na ko na ke tei to. O ma kwei sabu o ma lwoori Piita de Jɔn o we, 19“Amo lage se á pa amo de taa jege dam dento dwoŋi se, amo ná kwei a je a daŋe nɔɔno wolo baŋa ne, se konto tu jwoŋi Wɛ Sin-laao kom.” 20Piita ma leiri‑o o we, “Wɛ wó chɔge nmo, de n sabu kom maama, nmo na boŋe we n wó wane n ma n sabu n yeigi Wɛ pɛɛre to ŋwaane. 21Nmo bochare ba tɔge chega Wɛ yiga ne. Konto to, n bá‑n na chwoŋa se n tɔge de debam n toŋe Wɛ totoŋa yam. 22Nam leiri n wo se n yage wo-lwanno telo nmo na boŋe se n ke to, se n daare n lwoori dé Teiru Wɛ we, o ná sɛ, se o yage-te o ma chɛ‑m. 23Kokuri amo nɛ we n jege puseŋa dedɛ, ye wɛleera jege‑m ya dam kuri ne.” 24Simon ma leiri o we, “Nam lwoori-na Wɛ á pa-ne se wonnu telo maama á na tage amo baŋa ne to yé ba te chɔge-ne.”
25Piita de Jɔn déem ma ta Yezu chega kam ba bere nɔɔna bam ye ba kwori ba ŋɔɔne Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam. Ba laam ma jwoori ba maa vei Jerusalem. Ba na maa jwoori to, ba ma tole Samaria te-nia yam wone ba tɔɔle Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam.
Filipi pɛ dedɛɛro ni Wɛ taane kuri
26Baŋa Wɛ maleka laam ma ba Filipi tei ka ta ded‑o ka we, “Zaŋe wea tetare ne n vo n tɔge chwoŋa kalo na zege Jerusalem ne ka vei Gaza to.” Chwoŋa kam konto tɔge kagoa wo mo ka via.
27Filipi ma zaŋe o kɛ. Etiopia tu de déem maa wo chwoŋa kam ne o maa vei sɔŋɔ. Wonto mo ye dedɛɛro ye o toŋe o pae o teo kom ka-pɛ wom ba na bwoi we ‘Kandake’ to. O maa nii o jejegero tem maama baŋa ne. O déem ya vei Jerusalem mo se o ware Wɛ, 28ye o laam maa jwoori o vei sɔŋɔ de toroko kolo siseiŋa na vaŋe to. O toroko kom na maa dura konto to, o maa jei o gare tɔnɔ kolo Wɛ sampwora Izaya na popone faŋa faŋa to. 29Wɛ Sin-laao kom ma bere Filipi ko we, “Véi n ta‑n tɔge toroko kom.” 30O ma duri o vo o yi nɔɔno wom tei. O ma ni nɔɔno wom na jege Wɛ sampwora Izaya tɔnɔ kom o gara. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo wó wane n ni n na jege kolo n gare to kuri na?” 31O ma leiri o we, “Amo nam wó ke tɛ mo a lɔre ko kuri ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo maŋe-ko o bere ne?” O laam ma pa se Filipi di toroko kom baŋa o jeini o tei ne. 32O na wora o gare wonnu telo tɔnɔ kom wone to mo tento:
“Wonto déem mo nye de pia ba na vaŋe ba ja ba vo se ba go to.
O ta nye de pipeila kalo ba na fane ka koro ye ka wo ke sɔɔ to.
Konto dwoŋi mo o wo puri o ni o ta kolokolo.
33Nɔɔna maa jege‑o ba gwoona.
Ba wo mɛ chega ba di o taane.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa tera o na wó ŋɔɔne o dwi dem taane,
kolo ŋwaane o dwi ti logo baŋa ne.”
34Dedɛɛro wom ma ta de Filipi o we, “A lage a bwei a nii, wɔ taane mo Wɛ sampwora kam tɛa, o tete mo o tɛ naa nɔɔno wodwoŋi mo?” 35Filipi ma jwoori o bobo nɔɔno wom na gage mɛ to o bere‑o ko kuri, ye o daare o ta Yezu kwor-ywoŋa kam maama o bere‑o. 36Ba na tɔge chwoŋa kam ba maa vei konto to, ba ma vo ba yi buga. Dedɛɛro wom ma ta o we, “Nii, na wora ywo-seeni. Amo bá wane a jwoŋi sɛɛm na?” [37Filipi ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo ná sɛ Wɛ chega kam de n wo maama, nmo wó wane n jwoŋi sɛɛm.”]
38Dedɛɛro wom laam ma pa se toroko kom zege. Ba maama ma tu tega ba vo ba zo na bam wo. Filipi ma pa‑o sɛɛm Yezu ŋwaane. 39Ba ma nwoŋi na bam wone. Ba na nwoŋi to, dé Teiru wom Sin-laao kom ma chaale Filipi ko ja viiri. Dedɛɛro wom ma daa wo nɛ‑o. O ma jwoori o kwei chwoŋa o maa kɛa, ye o tiini o jege wopwolo dedɛ. 40Filipi ma na we o tu o wo Azota ne mo. O ma tole teene maama o tɔɔle Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam taa, o vo o yi Kazaria.

english_text:
Saul Becomes a Follower of the Lord
(Acts 22.6-16; 26.12-18)
1Saul kept on threatening to kill the Lord's followers. He even went to the high priest 2and asked for letters to the leaders of the synagogues in Damascus. He did this because he wanted to arrest and take to Jerusalem any man or woman who had accepted the Lord's Way. 3When Saul had almost reached Damascus, a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around him. 4He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying, “Saul! Saul! Why are you so cruel to me?”
5“Who are you?” Saul asked.
“I am Jesus,” the Lord answered. “I am the one you are so cruel to. 6Now get up and go into the city, where you will be told what to do.”
7 The men with Saul stood there speechless. They had heard the voice, but they had not seen anyone. 8Saul got up from the ground, and when he opened his eyes, he could not see a thing. Someone then led him by the hand to Damascus, 9and for three days he was blind and did not eat or drink.
10A follower named Ananias lived in Damascus, and the Lord spoke to him in a vision. Ananias answered, “Lord, here I am.”
11The Lord said to him, “Get up and go to the house of Judas on Straight Street. When you get there, you will find a man named Saul from the city of Tarsus. Saul is praying, 12and he has seen a vision. He saw a man named Ananias coming to him and putting his hands on him, so he could see again.”
13Ananias replied, “Lord, a lot of people have told me about the terrible things this man has done to your followers in Jerusalem. 14Now the chief priests have given him the power to come here and arrest anyone who worships in your name.”
15The Lord said to Ananias, “Go! I have chosen him to tell foreigners, kings, and the people of Israel about me. 16I will show him how much he must suffer for worshiping in my name.”
17Ananias left and went into the house where Saul was staying. Ananias placed his hands on him and said, “Saul, the Lord Jesus has sent me. He is the same one who appeared to you along the road. He wants you to be able to see and to be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
18 Suddenly something like fish scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see. He got up and was baptized. 19Then he ate and felt much better.
Saul Preaches in Damascus
For several days Saul stayed with the Lord's followers in Damascus. 20Soon he went to the synagogues and started telling people that Jesus is the Son of God. 21Everyone who heard Saul was amazed and said, “Isn't this the man who caused so much trouble for those people in Jerusalem who worship in the name of Jesus? Didn't he come here to arrest them and take them to the chief priests?”
22Saul preached with such power that he completely confused the Jewish people in Damascus, as he tried to show them that Jesus is the Messiah.
23 Later some of them made plans to kill Saul, 24but he found out about it. He learned that they were guarding the gates of the city day and night in order to kill him. 25Then one night his followers let him down over the city wall in a large basket.
Saul in Jerusalem
26When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the followers. But they were all afraid of him, because they did not believe he was a true follower. 27Then Barnabas helped him by taking him to the apostles. He explained how Saul had seen the Lord and how the Lord had spoken to him. Barnabas also said when Saul was in Damascus, he had spoken bravely in the name of Jesus.
28Saul moved about freely with the followers in Jerusalem and told everyone about the Lord. 29He was always arguing with the Jews who spoke Greek, and so they tried to kill him. 30But the followers found out about this and took Saul to Caesarea. From there they sent him to the city of Tarsus.
31The church in Judea, Galilee, and Samaria now had a time of peace and kept on worshiping the Lord. The church became stronger, as the Holy Spirit encouraged it and helped it grow.
Peter Heals Aeneas
32While Peter was traveling from place to place, he visited the Lord's followers who lived in the town of Lydda. 33There he met a man named Aeneas, who for eight years had been sick in bed and could not move. 34Peter said to Aeneas, “Jesus Christ has healed you! Get up and make up your bed.” At once he stood up.
35Many people in the towns of Lydda and Sharon saw Aeneas and became followers of the Lord.
Peter Brings Dorcas Back to Life
36In Joppa there was a follower named Tabitha. Her Greek name was Dorcas, which means “deer.” She was always doing good things for people and had given much to the poor. 37But she got sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upstairs room. 38Joppa wasn't far from Lydda, and the followers heard that Peter was there. They sent two men to say to him, “Please come with us as quickly as you can!” 39At once, Peter went with them.
The men took Peter upstairs into the room. Many widows were there crying. They showed him the coats and clothes that Dorcas had made while she was still alive.
40After Peter had sent everyone out of the room, he knelt down and prayed. Then he turned to the body of Dorcas and said, “Tabitha, get up!” The woman opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up. 41He took her by the hand and helped her to her feet.
Peter called in the widows and the other followers and showed them that Dorcas had been raised from death. 42Everyone in Joppa heard what had happened, and many of them put their faith in the Lord. 43Peter stayed on for a while in Joppa in the house of a man named Simon, who made leather.
translation_text:
Pɔɔl pipiri o ba o sɛ Yezu
Kikia 22:4-16; 26:9-18
1Sɔɔl déem ta yɔɔre o fugi dé Teiru Yezu tɔgena, ye o kwaane o lage chwoŋa se o go-ba. Konto ŋwaane o ma zaŋe o vo Juu tiina kaanem yuu tu wom tei. 2O ma vo o lwoori‑o se o pa‑o tɔnɔ kolo o na wó kwei o bere Juu tiina balo na nii ba jeerim di sem Damasika ne to, se ko pa ba jeeri‑o lanyerane. O déem lage chwoŋa se, o ná nɛ balo na tɔge Wɛ chwo-doŋa kam to mo, se o wane o ja-ba o jwoori o vo Jerusalem o ke-ba peena diga ne, baara de kaana maama. 3O na nɛ tɔnɔ kom to, o ma zaŋe o maa vei Damasika. O na twɛ teo kom to, pwooni ma pɔpɔ de nwoŋi wɛyuu de pepele de gilimi‑o. 4O ma to tega ne ye o ni kwora na bwoŋi o yere ka we, “Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, bɛŋwaane mo nmo jege-ne n bɛɛsa konto?” 5O de ma bwei o we, “Amo tu, nmo nam ye wɔ mo?” Kwora kam ma ta ka we, “Amo ye Yezu mo, nmo na jege n bɛɛse to. 6Nam zaŋe n zo teo kom wo. Nmo ná yi da, ba laam wó ta kolo nmo na jege se n ke to.”
7Nɔɔna balo na tɔge de Sɔɔl to maa yɔɔre ba zega ye ba ware kolokolo se ba ta. Ba déem nigi kwora kam ye ba nam wo nɛ nɔɔn-nɔɔno. 8Sɔɔl ma zaŋe wɛɛne o puri o yia ye o ware se o na kolokolo. Ba ma ja o jeŋa ba vaŋe‑o ba ja zo Damasika teo wone. 9O déem jege da yatɔ mo o yia na dwei. Maŋa kam konto ne o ba di kolokolo ye o ta ba nyɔa.
10Yezu tɔgeno wodwoŋi déem maa wo Damasika ne, o yere mo Anania. O ma dwɛ o na dé Teiru wom na ŋɔɔne ded‑o. O ma bwoŋi o yere o we, “Anania!” O ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, nii-ne.”
11Dé Teiru wom ma ta ded‑o o we, “Zaŋe n vo Judas sɔŋɔ, ko na zege chwoŋa kalo ba na bwoi we ‘Chwo-yɔɔro’ to ni ne. Nmo ná yi da, se n bwei nɔɔno wolo yere na ye Sɔɔl to bwia. O ye Tasusi tu mo. Nmo wó na o na wora o ware Wɛ. 12O ya dwɛ mo o na nɔɔno, o yere mo Anania. O ma na‑o ye o ba o daŋe o jea o yuu ne, se o yia yam jwoori ya taa nae.”
13Anania na nigi konto to, o ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, nɔɔna dedɛ maŋe ba ta nɔɔno wom konto taane ba bere amo de o na ke wo-balwaaro telo maama o ma chɔge nmo nɔɔna balo na wo Jerusalem ne to. 14O laam tu ywo Damasika ne mo de o na jwoŋi chwoŋa Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam tei ne se o ja balo maama na tɔge nmo yere ŋwaane ba zuli Wɛ to.” 15Dé Teiru wom ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nam véi, kolo ŋwaane wonto mo ye wolo amo na kuri se o taa toŋe o pa-ne, se o daare o zeiŋi amo yere Isarele dwi tiina bam tei ne, dedaane dwi-gɛ tiina de ba pwa de tei ne. 16Amo tete nam wó bere‑o yaara yalo maama o na jege se o na amo yere ŋwaane to.”
17Anania laam ma zaŋe o vo o yi sɔŋɔ kom o zo. O ma na Sɔɔl o daare o vo o daŋe o jea o baŋa ne ye o we, “Amo nu-bu Sɔɔl, dé Teiru Yezu tete mo toŋe amo nmo tei ne. Wonto ya mo veere o tete nmo yiga ne, n ya na wo chwoŋa ne n ma‑n beene to. O toŋe-ne se a ba a pa n jwoori n ta‑n nae mo, se n daare n jwoŋi Wɛ Sin-laao kom de ko dam maama.” 18Anania na tage konto to, bedwe baŋa ne mo wonnu kore te nwoŋi Sɔɔl yia yam ne, ne ywon-porro tei, ye o laam daare o jwoori o nae lanyerane. O ma zaŋe o zege wɛɛne. O ma jwoŋi sɛɛm Yezu ŋwaane. 19O laam ma di wodiu pa se o jwoori o na dam. O ma maŋe Damasika ne da fenfee o woli Yezu tɔgena bam wone.
20Sɔɔl déem na wo Damasika ne konto to, o ma yeini o vo Juu tiina jeerim di sem o bere-ba Yezu taane. O maa tɛ o we, Yezu ye Wɛ Bu mo. 21Nɔɔna balo maama na nigi o berem dem to maa ye yaau ded‑o. Ba ma bwei daane ba we, “Ko dae nɔɔno wonto déem mo wo Jerusalem ne o kwaane o chɔge balo na tɔge yere dento ŋwaane ba zuli Wɛ to na? Ko nam dae konto ŋwaane mo o tu ywo-seeni se o taa jaane Yezu tɔgena o vei o ke Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam jeŋa ne na?”
22Sɔɔl déem nam mo tu o na baare dedɛ de o na bere nɔɔna tei to. O maa bere nɔɔna we, Yezu seene o ye Wɛ Dam Tu wom mo. Ko ma pa se Juu tiina balo na zoore Damasika ne to daa ware se ba leiri o ni taane.
23Da kɔgɔ kɔgɔ na kɛ to, Juu tiina bam ma ke ni daane se ba go Sɔɔl. 24O ma lɔre ba na boŋe se ba ke‑o kolo to. Dɛ maama wea de tete ba zege ba nii teo kom nia yam se ba nii, Sɔɔl wó tɔge da se ba laam go‑o na. 25Dɛ dedwe tete ne o nɔɔna bam ma pa se o zo tetɔ-kamunu wo, ye ba lei ŋona ko ni ne ba pa o tɔge takworo o nwoŋi o chu tega ne ye o lu.
26Sɔɔl laam ma zaŋe o vo Jerusalem. O maa kwaane se o tɔge o woli Yezu tɔgena bam wone. Ba maama maa fona ded‑o, ye ba wo sɛ we o seene o ji Yezu tɔgeno. 27Banabas ma vo o tei se o woli‑o. O ma ja‑o o vo Yezu totoŋa nakwa bam tei. O ma ta o bere-ba Sɔɔl na wo chwoŋa ne o via ye o na dé Teiru wom na ŋɔɔne ded‑o tei to. O ta ma ta o bere-ba Sɔɔl na yɔɔre o ŋɔɔne de baare Yezu yere ŋwaane tei to, pa se balo na wo Damasika ne to lɔre Wɛ chega kam. 28Sɔɔl ma maŋe Yezu tɔgena bam tei ne ye o tole Jerusalem ni maama o bere nɔɔna Wɛ chega kam dé Teiru wom yere ŋwaane. 29O maa yeini o ŋɔɔne de Juu tiina balo na ŋɔɔne Girisi tiina taane to ye o mage ni-kantɔgɔ de-ba. Ba laam ma kwaane se ba go‑o. 30O dwonna bam na lɔre konto to, ba ma ja‑o ba ja vo Kazaria. Ba laam ma pa se o kɛ o vo Tasusi.
31Yezu kɔgɔ kom nɔɔna balo maama na wo Judea, de Galili, de Samaria jei sem ne to déem ma na siu ba yaara yam wone. Ba kɔgɔ kom ma fɔge de dam ye ko puli lanyerane, Wɛ Sin-laao kom na zeini-ba to ŋwaane. Ba maa kɔre dé Teiru wom ba ŋwea maama wone.
Piita na toŋe Wɛ totoŋa tei to
32Piita déem yeini o beeri o tole jei maama mo. Dɛ dedwe o daa ma zaŋe o vo se o nii Wɛ nɔɔna balo na zoore Lida ne to. 33O na yi da to, o ma na nɔɔno, o yere mo Ayinea. O déem ye gɔrɔ mo, ye o tigi o sara ne taa, bena nana, o ware o zaŋe wɛɛne. 34Piita na nɛ‑o to, o ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ayinea, Yezu Krista wó pa n na yazura. Nam zaŋe wɛɛne se n fɔge n piri n sara kam n tiŋi.” O na tage konto to, bedwe baŋa ne mo Ayinea ma zaŋe wɛɛne. 35Nɔɔna balo maama na zoore Lida ne de Sarɔn jei sem maama ne to ma na‑o. Ba laam ma ba ba sɛ dé Teiru Yezu.
36Kaane wodwoŋi déem mo wo Jopa ne, o yere mo Tabita. (O yere dedaane Girisi tiina taane mo ye Dɔkase.) O maa ye Yezu tɔgeno. O maa chɛ de keim-laaro ye o woli yiniga tiina dedɛ. 37Maŋa kam konto ne o ma ba o weele o te. Nɔɔna ma kwei o yera yam ba swɛ, ye ba ja‑o ba di wɛyuu diga ba tiŋi da. 38Jopa maa bwola dedaane Lida. Konto to, Yezu tɔgena balo na wo Jopa ne to ma lɔre we Piita tu Lida o wora. Ba ma toŋe nɔɔna balei o tei ne. Ba ma vo ba lwoori‑o ba we, “Popo, ke lela n ba debam teo kom.”
39Piita ma zaŋe o tɔge de-ba o kɛ. O na yi Jopa to, ba ma ja‑o ba di wɛyuu diga kam. Kadeina bam maama maa zege ba gilimi‑o ye ba keera. Ba ma bere‑o gwaaro telo maama Dɔkase ya na ŋwe ye o sɔ to. 40Piita laam ma pa se ba maama nwoŋi diga kam wone ba daare‑o. O ma daare o kuni dwoona tega ne o ware Wɛ. O laam ma pipiri o nii too wom ye o we, “Tabita, zaŋe wɛɛne.” O ma puri o yia o na Piita na wora. O ma zaŋe o jei. 41Piita ma tei o jeŋa o woli‑o pa se o zaŋe wɛɛne o zega. O laam ma bwoŋi kadeina bam de Yezu tɔgena bam maama. O ma pa Tabita zege ba yiga ne ye o ŋwe.
42Keim dem konto taane ma jage de yi Jopa jei sem maama. Ko ma pa se nɔɔna dedɛ ke ba wo-dedoa de dé Teiru Yezu. 43Piita ma maŋe Jopa ne taa, da kɔgɔ kɔgɔ. O déem zoore gɔgɔ kodwoŋi tei ne mo, o yere mo Simon.

english_text:
Peter and Cornelius
1In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, who was the captain of a group of soldiers called “The Italian Unit.” 2Cornelius was a very religious man. He worshiped God, and so did everyone else who lived in his house. He had given a lot of money to the poor and was always praying to God.
3One afternoon at about three o'clock, Cornelius had a vision. He saw an angel from God coming to him and calling him by name. 4Cornelius was surprised and stared at the angel. Then he asked, “What is this all about?”
The angel answered, “God has heard your prayers and knows about your gifts to the poor. 5Now send some men to Joppa for a man named Simon Peter. 6He is staying with Simon the leather maker, who lives in a house near the sea.” 7After saying this, the angel left.
Cornelius called in two of his servants and one of his soldiers who worshiped God. 8He explained everything to them and sent them off to Joppa.
9 The next day about noon these men were coming near Joppa. Peter went up on the roof of the house to pray 10and became very hungry. While the food was being prepared, he fell sound asleep and had a vision. 11He saw heaven open, and something came down like a huge sheet held up by its four corners. 12In it were all kinds of animals, reptiles, and birds. 13A voice said to him, “Peter, get up! Kill these and eat them.”
14 But Peter said, “Lord, I can't do that! I've never eaten anything that is unclean and not fit to eat.”
15The voice spoke to him again, “When God says that something can be used for food, don't say it isn't fit to eat.”
16This happened three times before the sheet was suddenly taken back to heaven.
17Peter was still wondering what all this meant, when the men sent by Cornelius came and stood at the gate. They had found their way to Simon's house 18and were asking if Simon Peter was staying there.
19While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Holy Spirit said to him, “Three men are here looking for you. 20Hurry down and go with them. Don't worry, I sent them.”
21Peter went down and said to the men, “I am the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”
22They answered, “Captain Cornelius sent us. He is a good man who worships God and is liked by the Jewish people. One of God's holy angels told Cornelius to send for you, so he could hear what you have to say.” 23Peter invited them to spend the night.
The next morning, Peter and some of the Lord's followers in Joppa left with the men who had come from Cornelius. 24The next day they arrived in Caesarea where Cornelius was waiting for them. He had also invited his relatives and close friends.
25When Peter arrived, Cornelius greeted him. Then he knelt at Peter's feet and started worshiping him. 26But Peter took hold of him and said, “Stand up! I am nothing more than a human.”
27As Peter entered the house, he was still talking with Cornelius. Many people were there, 28and Peter said to them, “You know that we Jews are not allowed to have anything to do with other people. But God has shown me that he doesn't think anyone is unclean or unfit. 29I agreed to come here, but I want to know why you sent for me.”
30Cornelius answered:
Four days ago at about three o'clock in the afternoon I was praying at home. Suddenly a man in bright clothes stood in front of me. 31He said, “Cornelius, God has heard your prayers, and he knows about your gifts to the poor. 32Now send to Joppa for Simon Peter. He is visiting in the home of Simon the leather maker, who lives near the sea.”
33I sent for you at once, and you have been good enough to come. All of us are here in the presence of the Lord God, so that we can hear what he has to say.
34 Peter then said:
Now I am certain that God treats all people alike. 35God is pleased with everyone who worships him and does right, no matter what nation they come from. 36This is the same message that God gave to the people of Israel, when he sent Jesus Christ, the Lord of all, to offer peace to them.
37You surely know what happened everywhere in Judea. It all began in Galilee after John had told everyone to be baptized. 38God gave the Holy Spirit and power to Jesus from Nazareth. He was with Jesus, as he went around doing good and healing everyone who was under the power of the devil. 39We all saw what Jesus did both in Israel and in the city of Jerusalem.
Jesus was put to death on a cross. 40But three days later, God raised him to life and let him be seen. 41Not everyone saw him. He was seen only by us, who ate and drank with him after he was raised from death. We were the ones God chose to tell others about him.
42God told us to announce clearly to the people that Jesus is the one he has chosen to judge the living and the dead. 43Every one of the prophets has said that all who have faith in Jesus will have their sins forgiven in his name.
44While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit took control of everyone who was listening. 45Some Jewish followers of the Lord had come with Peter, and they were surprised that the Holy Spirit had been given to Gentiles. 46Now they were hearing Gentiles speaking unknown languages and praising God.
Peter said, 47“These Gentiles have been given the Holy Spirit, just as we have! I am certain that no one would dare stop us from baptizing them.” 48Peter ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, and they asked him to stay on for a few days.
translation_text:
Dwi-gɛ tu lɔre Wɛ chega kam
1Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Kɔnilusi. O maa zoore Kazaria ne. O déem ye Rom soja tiina dedɛɛro mo. Soja tiina kɔgɔ kolo o na tɔge o wo ko wone to yere mo ‘Yitalia tiina kɔgɔ’. 2O déem kɔre Wɛ mo. O de o sɔŋɔ tiina maama maa zuli Wɛ lanyerane. O maa woli Juu tiina balo yiniga na jege-ba to. O maa yeini o ware Wɛ maŋa maama. 3Dɛ dedwe wɛ na guni maŋa kalo to, o ma dwɛ o na wo-kenkagele. O ma yɔɔre o na Wɛ maleka na tu ka bwoŋi o yere ka we, “Kɔnilusi!” 4O ma fi o yia o nii maleka kam seeni ye foone jege‑o. O ma ta o we, “Amo tu, n tu amo tei mo na?” Maleka kam ma leiri‑o ka we, “Nmo na yeini n ware Wɛ ye n kwori n woli yiniga tiina to mo pɛ se n kikia yam konto su Wɛ yi. O nam guli nmo gula mo. 5Leile konto nmo jege se n toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo Jopa ba bwoŋi nɔɔno wodwoŋi, o yere mo Simon Piita. 6O ye veiru mo gɔgɔ kodwoŋi sɔŋɔ ne. Gɔgɔ kom yere mo Simon. O sɔŋɔ kom maa wo naneo kom ni ne.”
7Maleka kam na tage konto ka ti to, ka ma viiri. Kɔnilusi ma bwoŋi o sɔŋɔ kom tontoŋena balei, de soja tu dedoa wolo na toŋe o pa‑o ye o de kɔre Wɛ to. 8O ma ta kolo maama na ke to o bere-ba ye o daare o toŋe-ba se ba vo Jopa.
9Tega na poore to, nɔɔna bam ma daare fenfee se ba yi Jopa. Piita déem diini sɔŋɔ kom nayuu se o ware Wɛ. Ko ye wea tetare ne mo. 10Kana laam maa jege‑o ye o lage wodiu se o di. Ba na wora ba ke wodiu kom to, Wɛ ma pa se o na wo-kenkagele ne dendwɛ mo tei. 11O nɛ wɛyuu na pore o baŋa ne ye woŋo nwoŋi da ko maa tu tega. Woŋo kom nye de gɔr-kamunu mo ye ba zei ko nia yana pa se ko maa tu tega. 12Vara dwi maama mo tigi ko wone, dedaane tega-veila, de zuna. 13O na nɛ to, o ma ni kwora na ŋɔɔne ded‑o ka we, “Piita, zaŋe n go wonnu tem n di.” 14Piita ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, a bá sɛ. Amo wo fɔge a di woŋo kolo na ba lana ye ko wo maŋe de dim to.” 15O daa ma jwoori o ni kwora kam na we, “Yé zaŋe n chuli woŋo kolo Wɛ na pɛ se ko maŋe de dim to.” 16Ko ke konto mo kuni betɔ. Wonnu tem laam ma jwoori te vaŋe te di wɛyuu.
17Piita maa bwɛa wo-kenkagele dem o na nɛ to kuri. O na wora konto to, mo nɔɔna balo Kɔnilusi na toŋe o tei ne to maŋe ba lɔre Simon sɔŋɔ kom jei. Ba laam ma vo ba yi manchwoŋo kom ba zega. 18Ba ma bwoŋi ba bwei ba we, “Nɔɔno zoore ywo, o yere mo Simon Piita na?”
19Piita daa ta maa kwaane se o lɔre wo-kenkagele dem o na nɛ to kuri. Wɛ Sin-laao kom ma ta ded‑o ko we, “Nii! Nɔɔna batɔ mo tu ywo ba lage nmo. 20Zaŋe n tu tega. Yé ta‑n jege boboŋa yalei se n tɔge de-ba n kɛ, kolo ŋwaane amo mo toŋe-ba.” 21Piita ma tu tega ye o ta de-ba o we, “Amo mo ye wolo abam na lage to. Bɛŋwaane mo ye á ba?” 22Ba ma leiri ba we, “Soja tiina dedɛɛro Kɔnilusi mo toŋe debam. O ye nɔn-ŋom mo ye o kɔre Wɛ lanyerane. Juu tiina bam maama maa pa‑o zula. Wɛ maleka mo tage ded‑o se o bwoŋi nmo o sɔŋɔ ne se o wane o ni kolo nmo na lage n ta to.” 23Piita ma pa se ba zo sɔŋɔ kom ba peini.
Tega na poore to, o ma zaŋe o tɔge de-ba o kɛ. Yezu nɔɔna badaara de ma zaŋe Jopa ne ba tɔge ded‑o ba kɛ. 24Tega daa na poore to mo o yi Kazaria. O yi da dedaane Kɔnilusi, de o sɔŋɔ tiina, de o badwonna o na bwoŋi to maŋe ba jei ba cheigi‑o. 25Piita na yi sɔŋɔ kom to, o maa boŋe se o zo. Kɔnilusi ma zaŋe o nwoŋi o jeeri‑o, ye o daare o to o yiga ne o jɔɔne‑o. 26Piita ma pa se o zaŋe wɛɛne o zege, ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Amo tete ye nabiinu mo.” 27O daa ta maa ŋɔɔne ded‑o ye ba maa zoore sɔŋɔ kom. O ma na nɔn-kɔgɔ na gilimi da ba jei. 28O ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam maŋe á yei we ko chula se Juu tu taa zoore dedaane dwi-gɛ tiina, naa o taa tɔge de-ba. Wɛ nam mo bere amo we, ko wo maŋe se a taa chuli nɔɔn-nɔɔno, naa a pae o taa ye nɔn-diku. 29Konto ŋwaane, abam na toŋe á bwoŋi-ne to, a wo ve ye a ba. Amo nam lage a bwei a nii, bɛ mo ye á toŋe á bwoŋi-ne?”
30Kɔnilusi ma ta o we, “Zem mo jege da yana, ko maŋe de maŋa kanto ne, wɛ na guni to, ye a wora a ware Wɛ sɔŋɔ ne. Nɔɔno ma pɔpɔ o ba o zege amo yiga ne. O maa zo gare-nyenno. 31O ma ta de amo o we, ‘Kɔnilusi, Wɛ mo jwoŋi nmo wara yam. Nmo na woli yiniga tiina to ŋwaane mo o guli nmo gula. 32Nam toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo Jopa ba bwoŋi nɔɔno wodwoŋi, o yere mo Simon Piita. O ye veiru mo Simon wolo na ye gɔgɔ to sɔŋɔ ne. O maa zoore naneo kom ni ne.’ 33O na tage konto to, a ma toŋe nɔɔna lela se ba vo ba bwoŋi‑m se n ba. A ke nmo lei de nmo na tu to. Debam maama nam zege Wɛ yiga ne mo dé cheigi se dé ni kolo maama dé Teiru wom na pɛ‑m se n ta to.”
34Piita laam ma zaŋe o ta o we, “Amo zem lɔre we ko ye chega mo we Wɛ ba kuri nɔɔna daane. 35Wɛ jwoŋi nɔɔno wolo maama na kɔre‑o ye o daare o ke kolo na tɔge chwoŋa to mo, ko ná ye Juu tu naa dwi tu wolo de. 36Abam maŋe á yei Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam o na toŋe Isarele dwi tiina bam tei ne we Yezu Krista mo wae o jwoŋi nɔɔna o fɔge ba de Wɛ daane tei to. Wonto mo ye nabiina maama Teiru. 37Abam ta yei wo-kamunnu telo maama na ke Judea ne to. Ko déem bobo Galili ne mo, maŋa kam Jɔn na bere nɔɔna se ba jwoŋi sɛɛm Wɛ ŋwaane ye ko kɛ to. 38Abam lɔre Nazarete tu Yezu yera seina na ye tei to. Wɛ déem lwogi o Sin-laao kom o yera ne ye o kwori o pa‑o dam. Wɛ na wo o tei ne konto to, o maa yeini o vei jei maama o zeini nɔɔna lanyerane, ye o kwori o jwoŋi balo na wo setaana pɛ jeŋa ne to o yaga. 39Debam nam mo nɛ wonnu telo maama o na ke Jerusalem ne de Juu tiina teene dem maama ne to ye dé zege te chega kam kwaga ne. Ba laam jaane‑o mo ba pa dagara yuu ne ba go. 40Wɛ ma pa se o jwoori o bi toone wone da yatɔ dɛ ne. O ma pa se o veere o tete nɔɔna yiga ne pa ba na‑o. 41Ko nam dae we nɔɔna maama mo nɛ‑o, ko ye balo yerane Wɛ na maŋe o kuri se ba taa zege o kwaga ne to mo. Debam mo konto. Yezu na bi toone wone to, debam tɔge ded‑o dé di wodiu ye dé nyɔ na. 42O ma pa debam ni se dé tɔɔle Wɛ kwora kam dé bere nɔɔna se dé daare dé pa ba lɔre we, omo ye wolo Wɛ na tiŋi se o bore nɔn-ŋwena de twa taane to. 43Faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem maama déem tage wonto taane ye ba ta ba we, nɔɔno wolo maama ná ke o wo-dedoa ded‑o, Wɛ wó yage konto tu wɛleera o ma chɛ‑o wonto yere ŋwaane.”
44Piita ta na wora o ŋɔɔne konto to, Wɛ Sin-laao kom ma tu ko ba balo maama na jei ba cheigi o taane dem to tei. 45Juu tiina balo na maŋe ba sɛ Yezu ye ba tɔge de Piita ba ba to maa ye yaau de Wɛ na lwogi o Sin-laao kom o pa dwi-gɛ tiina o woli da to. 46Kolo ŋwaane ba nigi ba na ŋɔɔne ta-gɛ mo ye ba kwori ba zuli Wɛ.
47Piita laam ma ta o we, “Nɔɔna banto seene ba jwoŋi Wɛ Sin-laao kom ne debam de na jwoŋi tei to mo. Konto to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o ve se dé kwei na dé pa ba jwoŋi sɛɛm.” 48O ma daare o ta se ba pa-ba sɛɛm Yezu Krista yere ŋwaane. Ba laam ma lwoori‑o se o maŋe ba tei ne da fenfee.

english_text:
Peter Reports to the Church in Jerusalem
1The apostles and the followers in Judea heard that Gentiles had accepted God's message. 2So when Peter came to Jerusalem, some of the Jewish followers started arguing with him. They wanted Gentile followers to be circumcised, and 3they said, “You stayed in the homes of Gentiles, and you even ate with them!”
4Then Peter told them exactly what had happened:
5I was in the town of Joppa and was praying when I fell sound asleep and had a vision. I saw heaven open, and something like a huge sheet held by its four corners came down to me. 6When I looked in it, I saw animals, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds. 7I heard a voice saying to me, “Peter, get up! Kill these and eat them.”
8But I said, “Lord, I can't do that! I've never taken a bite of anything that is unclean and not fit to eat.”
9The voice from heaven spoke to me again, “When God says that something can be used for food, don't say it isn't fit to eat.” 10This happened three times before it was all taken back into heaven.
11Suddenly three men from Caesarea stood in front of the house where I was staying. 12The Holy Spirit told me to go with them and not to worry. Then six of the Lord's followers went with me to the home of a man 13who told us that an angel had appeared to him. The angel had ordered him to send to Joppa for someone named Simon Peter. 14Then Peter would tell him how he and everyone in his house could be saved.
15After I started speaking, the Holy Spirit was given to them, just as the Spirit had been given to us at the beginning. 16 I remembered that the Lord had said, “John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.” 17God gave those Gentiles the same gift that he gave us when we put our faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. So how could I have gone against God?
18When they heard Peter say this, they stopped arguing and started praising God. They said, “God has now let Gentiles turn to him, and he has given life to them!”
The Church in Antioch
19 Some of the Lord's followers had been scattered because of the terrible trouble that started when Stephen was killed. They went as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, but they told the message only to the Jews.
20Some of the followers from Cyprus and Cyrene went to Antioch and started telling Gentiles the good news about the Lord Jesus. 21The Lord's power was with them, and many people turned to the Lord and put their faith in him. 22News of what was happening reached the church in Jerusalem. Then they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
23When Barnabas got there and saw how God had blessed them with undeserved grace, he was very glad. So he begged them to remain faithful to the Lord with all their hearts. 24Barnabas was a good man of great faith, and he was filled with the Holy Spirit. Many more people turned to the Lord.
25Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul. 26He found Saul and brought him to Antioch, where they met with the church for a whole year and taught many of its people. There in Antioch the Lord's followers were first called Christians.
27During this time some prophets from Jerusalem came to Antioch. 28 One of them was Agabus. Then with the help of the Spirit, he told that there would be a terrible famine everywhere in the world. And it happened when Claudius was Emperor. 29The followers in Antioch decided to send whatever help they could to the followers in Judea. 30So they appointed Barnabas and Saul to take their gifts to the church leaders in Jerusalem.
translation_text:
Piita tole ko na ke tei to
1Yezu totoŋa nakwa bam de o tɔgena balo na zoore Judea teene dem maama wone to ma ni we dwi-gɛ tiina de laam tu ba sɛ Wɛ kwora kam. 2Piita déem ma zaŋe o vo Jerusalem. O na yi da to, Juu tiina balo na tu ba sɛ Yezu to ma bwɛ‑o. 3Ba ma bwei‑o ba we, “Bɛ mo ye n vo n wo dwi-gɛ tiina sɔŋɔ ne ye ba ye balo na wo gwoni ba peina to? Bɛ mo ye n di wodiu de-ba?”
4Piita ma zaŋe o tole kolo maama na ke to o bere-ba ye o we:
5“Amo ya wo Jopa ne ye a wora a ware Wɛ. Wɛ ma pa a na wo-kenkagele. Amo dwɛ a na wo-kamunu na nwoŋi wɛyuu ko maa tu tega. Ko nye de gɔr-kamunu mo ye ba zei ko nyea yana pa se ko maa tu tega. Ko ma ba ko zege amo yiga ne. 6A ma nii ko wone ye a na vara na wora, ga-vara, de sɔŋɔ vara, de tega-veila, de zuna. 7A laam ma ni kwora ye ka ŋɔɔne de amo ka we, ‘Piita, zaŋe n go n di.’ 8Amo ma leiri a we, ‘Amo tu, a bá sɛ. Amo wo fɔge a di woŋo kolo na ba lana ye ko wo maŋe de dim to.’ 9Kwora kam daa ta ma jwoori ka zege wɛyuu ne ka ŋɔɔne ka we, ‘Yé zaŋe n chuli woŋo kolo Wɛ na pɛ se ko maŋe de dim to.’ 10Ko ke konto mo taa, kuni betɔ, ye wonnu tem maama jwoori te vaŋe te di wɛyuu.
11Amo laam ma nii a na nɔɔna batɔ ba tu ba zege sɔŋɔ kolo a na zoore to ni ne. Ba ya toŋe-ba Kazaria ne mo pa ba ba. 12Wɛ Sin-laao kom ma ta ko bere-ne we, a yé taa jege boboŋa yalei se a tɔge de-ba a kɛ. Dé nu-bia banto baredo de ma da amo ba vo. Dé maama ma vo dé yi Kazaria, ye dé vo dé zo Kɔnilusi sɔŋɔ kom. 13O ma ta o bere debam we o nɛ Wɛ maleka na tu o sɔŋɔ ka zega ye ka ta ded‑o we, ‘Toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo Jopa ba bwoŋi nɔɔno wodwoŋi o yere na ye Simon Piita to se o ba. 14Wonto ná tua, o laam wó ŋɔɔne taane de nmo se ko pa nmo de n sɔŋɔ tiina bam maama na verem.’
15Tɔ. Amo laam ma bobo se a ŋɔɔne de-ba. A na wora a ŋɔɔne konto to, Wɛ Sin-laao kom ma tu ko ba ba tei, nenɛɛne ko na bobo ko ba debam tei tei to. 16Amo laam ma guli dé Teiru wom déem na tage tei we, ‘Jɔn déem kwei na mo o ma pa nɔɔna sɛɛm. Ko nam ná ye abam, Wɛ wó tɔge o Sin-laao kom ŋwaane mo o pa abam sɛɛm.’ 17Ko seene ko ye chega mo we, Wɛ pɛ dwi-gɛ tiina banto o pɛɛre dem ne o na maŋe o pa debam de maŋa kalo dé na ke dé wo-dedoa dé sɛ dé Teiru Yezu Krista to. Ko maama ye bedwe mo. Konto to, amo ya wó kwaane se a cheiŋi Wɛ na?”
18Piita na tage konto ye ba ni to, ba ma yage taane dem ye ba daare ba tei Wɛ. Ba maa we, “Wɛ seene o pa dwi-gɛ tiina bam de chwoŋa se ba leiri ba wo ye ba daare ba na o ŋwe-doŋa kam.”
Yezu kɔgɔ kolo na wo Antioka ne to taane
19Maŋa kam ba déem na go Stiiven to, Yezu tɔgena bam nɛ yaara nɔɔna tei ne pa se ba jage da yiga ne. Balo na jage to badwonna ma vo ba yi Fonikia, de Kupirus, de Antioka. Ba na beeri konto to, ba yeini ba tɛ Wɛ kwora kam ba bere Juu tiina yerane. 20Ko daare Yezu tɔgena badaara na nwoŋi Kupirus de Kurene to ma zaŋe ba vo Antioka ba ta dé Teiru Yezu kwor-ywoŋa kam ba bere dwi-gɛ tiina de. 21Baŋa Wɛ dam maa wo ba tei ne. Nɔɔna dedɛ ma ke ba wo-dedoa ba sɛ dé Teiru wom ye ba daare ba tɔge‑o.
22Yezu kɔgɔ kolo na wo Jerusalem ne to ma ni kolo na ke to. Ba ma toŋe Banabas se o vo Antioka o nii. 23O na vei o yi da to, o ma na Wɛ na seene o ke nɔɔna bam zaane tei to. O maa jege wopwolo lanyerane. O ma kwoori ba maama se ba taa tɔge dé Teiru wom de ba wo maama se ba yé zaŋe ba yage.
24Banabas maa ye nɔn-ŋom. O maa tiini o jege wo-dedoa de Yezu, ye Wɛ Sin-laao kom wo o tei ne de dam. Nɔɔna dedɛ déem ma ba ba sɛ dé Teiru wom ye ba woli o kɔgɔ kom wone.
25Banabas laam ma zaŋe o vo Tasusi se o beeri Sɔɔl jei. 26O na vei o na‑o to, o ma ja‑o o jwoori Antioka. Ba na wora to, ba maa yeini ba woli daane ba bere Yezu kɔgɔ kom. Ba ke konto taa se ko yi bene, ye nɔɔna balo ba na bere to daga dedɛ. Ko ye Antioka ne mo ba bobo se ba bwoŋi Yezu tɔgena bam we Krista bia.
27Da yam konto ne Wɛ ni-jwoŋina badwonna na tɔɔle o kwora to ma zege Jerusalem ne ba vo Antioka. 28Ba dedoa yere mo Agabu. Wɛ Sin-laao kom ma pa se o ta Wɛ kwora kam we, kana lage ka ba ka zo logo baŋa maama. Ko déem seene ko ke konto mo maŋa kalo Kaludu na di paare to. 29Yezu tɔgena bam na nigi konto to, ba boboŋa ma ja se ba la sabu ba ma woli ba nu-bia balo na zoore Judea ne to. Ba dedoa dedoa ma sɛ se o pa ne o na wó wane tei to. 30Ba ma seene ba ke konto. Sabu kolo ba na lage to mo ba ke Banabas de Sɔɔl jeŋa ne se ba kwei ba ja vo Jerusalem ba pa Yezu kɔgɔ kom nakwa bam.

english_text:
Herod Causes Trouble for the Church
1At that time King Herod caused terrible suffering for some members of the church. 2He ordered soldiers to cut off the head of James, the brother of John. 3 When Herod saw that this pleased the Jewish people, he had Peter arrested during the Festival of Thin Bread. 4He put Peter in jail and ordered four squads of soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to put him on trial in public after the festival.
5While Peter was being kept in jail, the church never stopped praying to God for him.
Peter Is Rescued
6The night before Peter was to be put on trial, he was asleep and bound by two chains. A soldier was guarding him on each side, and two other soldiers were guarding the entrance to the jail. 7Suddenly an angel from the Lord appeared, and light flashed around in the cell. The angel poked Peter in the side and woke him up. Then he said, “Quick! Get up!”
The chains fell off his hands, 8and the angel said, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” Peter did what he was told. Then the angel said, “Now put on your coat and follow me.” 9Peter left with the angel, but he thought everything was only a dream. 10They went past the two groups of soldiers, and when they came to the iron gate to the city, it opened by itself. They went out and were going along the street, when all at once the angel disappeared.
11Peter now realized what had happened, and he said, “I am certain that the Lord sent his angel to rescue me from Herod and from everything the Jewish leaders planned to do to me.” 12Then Peter went to the house of Mary the mother of John whose other name was Mark. Many of the Lord's followers had come together there and were praying.
13Peter knocked on the gate, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer. 14When she heard Peter's voice, she was too excited to open the gate. She ran back into the house and said Peter was standing there.
15“You are crazy!” everyone told her. But she kept saying it was Peter. Then they said, “It must be his angel.” 16But Peter kept on knocking, until finally they opened the gate. They saw him and were completely amazed.
17Peter motioned for them to keep quiet. Then he told how the Lord had led him out of jail. He also said, “Tell James and the others what has happened.” After that, he left and went somewhere else.
18The next morning the soldiers who had been on guard were terribly worried and wondered what had happened to Peter. 19Herod ordered his own soldiers to search for him, but they could not find him. Then he questioned the guards and had them put to death. After this, Herod left Judea to stay in Caesarea for a while.
Herod Dies
20 Herod and the people of Tyre and Sidon were very angry with each other. But their country got its food supply from the region that he ruled. So a group of them went to see Blastus, who was one of Herod's high officials. They convinced Blastus that they wanted to make peace between their cities and Herod, 21and a day was set for them to meet with him.
Herod came dressed in his royal robes. He sat down on his throne and made a speech. 22The people shouted, “You speak more like a god than a man!” 23At once an angel from the Lord struck him down because he took the honor that belonged to God. Later, Herod was eaten by worms and died.
24God's message kept spreading. 25And after Barnabas and Saul had done the work they were sent to do, they went back to Jerusalem with John, whose other name was Mark.
translation_text:
Wɛ maleka vere Piita Herodi jeŋa ne
1Maŋa kam konto ne Pɛ Herodi ma zaŋe o ja Yezu kɔgɔ kom nɔɔna badwonna se o pa ba na yaara. 2O ma ja Jemsi wolo na ye Jɔn zembaaro to o pa ba go‑o de se-zɔɔ. 3O na ke konto to, o ma lɔre we ko pwoli Juu tiina bam wo lanyerane. O ta ma fɔge o zege ye o ja Piita. Ko maa ye Bworobworo-memene kuri dim maŋa ne mo, ba na yeini ba di bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle to. 4O na jaane Piita konto to, o ma ke‑o peena diga ne, ye o pa se soja tiina bana bana kuri bena yere‑o ba leini daane. Herodi déem maa lage se Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem ná kɛ de daare, se o laam pa ba ja Piita ba nwoŋi se o di o taane nɔɔna maama yiga ne. 5Konto ŋwaane Piita maa wo peena diga kam ne taa, ye Yezu kɔgɔ kom nɔɔna bam maa tiini ba lwoori Wɛ ba pa‑o.
6Ko déem ma yi tete delo tega na wó poore se Herodi pa Piita nwoŋi pwooni se o di o taane to. Piita maa tigi soja tiina balei tetare ne o dɔa. Ba ya vɔge‑o de chaponno telei mo, jazem de jagwia. Soja tiina badwonna de wo peena diga kam ni ne ba yera. 7Baŋa Wɛ maleka laam ma pɔpɔ ka ba ka zege da. Pwooni ma su diga kam. Maleka kam ma pepage Piita yera ka pa o zaŋe ye ka ta ka we, “Ke lela n zaŋe wɛɛne!”
Chaponno tem ma kɔ Piita jea ne te to tega ne. 8Maleka kam ma ta‑o ka we, “Faŋe n zo n gɔrɔ kom de n natera yam.” O ma seene o ke konto. Ka daa ma ta ka we, “Vɔ n gɔrɔ kom se n daare n ta‑n tɔge-ne.”
9Piita ma tɔge o kwaga o nwoŋi peena diga kam wone. O maa yeiri maleka kam na ke kolo to ye chega mo naa vwa mo. O maa boŋe we o dwɛ mo. 10Ba ma vo ba tɔge jei selo soja tiina bam na wora ba yere to. Ba ma da yiga de kwaga jei sem ba kɛ. Ba ma daare ba vo ba yi luu-bworo kolo na pore ko vei teo kom wo to. Bworo kom tete ma pore ye ba kɛ ba nwoŋi. Ba ma kwei chwoŋa ba vei ba maa kɛa. Maleka kam laam ma pɔpɔ ka viiri ka daare Piita.
11Piita boboŋa laam ma jwoori. O ma ta o we, “Amo laam lɔre we konto ye chega mo. Wɛ seene o toŋe o maleka mo ye o daare o jwoŋi-ne Herodi jeŋa ne o yage, se Juu tiina bam daa yé wane ba ke amo ne ba na boŋe tei to.”
12Piita na maane ko na ye tei to, o ma vo Mary ba sɔŋɔ. Wonto maa ye Jɔn Maake nu. Nɔɔna dedɛ déem mo tigisi daane sɔŋɔ kom ne ba wora ba ware Wɛ. 13O ma vo o yi pwooni yiga bworo kom o mage. Ka-nyaane maa wo sɔŋɔ kom ne, o yere mo Roda. O ma vo se o nii wɔ mo maga. 14O na vei to, o ma lɔre Piita kwora kam. O maa tiini o jege wopwolo lanyerane pa se o duri o jwoori ye o wo pore bworo kom. O ma vo o ta de nɔɔna bam we Piita mo zege manchwoŋo ne. 15Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, o chwo mo. O ma chem ye o ta o we, ko seene ko ye chega mo. Ba daa ma leiri ba we, ko wó taa ye o tete maleka mo.
16Ko na wora ko ke konto to, Piita maa mage bworo kom taa. Ba laam ma ba ba pore. Ba na nɛ‑o to, ko ma tiini ko ke-ba yaau. 17O ma zeiŋi o jea se ba cheigi sɔɔ. O ma daare o maŋe dé Teiru wom na ke tei o ja‑o o nwoŋi peena diga kam ne tei to. O daa ma ta-ba o we, ba véi ba ta kolo na ke to ba bere Jemsi de ba nu-bia bam maama. O laam ma yage-ba ye o vo jei sedwoŋi.
18Tega na poore tetete to, soja tiina balo ya na jege Piita ba yere to ma kɔre foone dedɛ ye ba boboŋa vugimi. Ba ma bwei daane ba we, “Bɛ mo ke ye Piita tera?” 19Herodi ma yage ni se ba kwaane ba beeri o jei. Ba ma beeri taa ba ga. Herodi ma bwei soja tiina bam taane o nii, ye o daare o pa se ba go-ba.
Konto na ke ko kɛ to, Herodi ma zaŋe Judea ne o vo Kazaria o zoore da.
Ko na ke tei ye Herodi te to
20Herodi bane déem tiini de zaŋe Tura de Sidon tiina baŋa ne. Jei sem nɔɔna bam ma zaŋe ba la kɔgɔ se ba vo ba kwoori Herodi se o yage. Herodi déem jege dedɛɛro wolo na nii o sɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne, o yere mo Bilasitu. Nɔɔna bam ma bobo ba di badwoŋo dedaane wonto, ye ba daare ba vo Herodi tei ba ŋɔɔne ded‑o se o yage o ban-zɔŋɔ kom. Ba déem lage ni-sɛɛm ba tete teo kom na yeini ko jwoŋi ko wodiiru pɛ wom teo kom ne to ŋwaane. 21Ba ma tiŋi dɛ se ba jeini daane ba ŋɔɔne taane dem.
Dɛ dem na yi to, Herodi ma kwei o paare zela yam o zo. O laam ma jeini o paare yituŋu kom baŋa ne se o ŋɔɔne de nɔɔna bam. 22O kwora na zaŋe ye o ŋɔɔne de-ba konto to, nɔɔna bam ma ta baŋa baŋa ba we, “Ko ye wɛ dedwoŋi mo ŋɔɔna, se ko dae nabiinu yerane.” 23Herodi na sɛ ba zula yam ye o wo pɛ se ba zuli Wɛ chekke to, Baŋa Wɛ maleka ma pa se jaweo ja‑o lela. Kanzwa ma zo o wo ya di‑o ya go.
24Wɛ kwora kam déem ma jage jei maama ye nɔɔna dedɛ sɛ-ka. 25Banabas de Sɔɔl ma ti totoŋe delo ba na vei Jerusalem se ba ke to. Ba laam ma ja Jɔn Maake ba woli ba tete ne ye ba nwoŋi Jerusalem ba jwoori ba vo Antioka.

english_text:
Barnabas and Saul Are Chosen and Sent
1The church at Antioch had several prophets and teachers. They were Barnabas, Simeon, also called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen, who was Herod's close friend, and Saul. 2While they were worshiping the Lord and going without eating, the Holy Spirit told them, “Appoint Barnabas and Saul to do the work for which I have chosen them.” 3Everyone prayed and went without eating for a while longer. Next, they placed their hands on Barnabas and Saul to show that they had been appointed to do this work. Then everyone sent them on their way.
Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus
4After Barnabas and Saul had been sent by the Holy Spirit, they went to Seleucia. From there they sailed to the island of Cyprus. 5They arrived at Salamis and began to preach God's message in the synagogues. They also had John as a helper.
6Barnabas and Saul went all the way to the city of Paphos on the other end of the island, where they met a Jewish man named Bar-Jesus. He practiced witchcraft and was a false prophet. 7He also worked for Sergius Paulus, who was very smart and was the governor of the island. Sergius Paulus wanted to hear God's message, and he sent for Barnabas and Saul. 8But Bar-Jesus, whose other name was Elymas, was against them. He even tried to keep the governor from having faith in the Lord.
9Then Saul, better known as Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas 10and said, “You son of the devil! You are a liar, a crook, and an enemy of everything that is right. When will you stop speaking against the true ways of the Lord? 11The Lord is going to punish you by making you completely blind for a while.”
Suddenly the man's eyes were covered by a dark mist, and he went around trying to get someone to lead him by the hand. 12When the governor saw what had happened, he was amazed at this teaching about the Lord. So he put his faith in the Lord.
Paul and Barnabas in Antioch of Pisidia
13Paul and the others left Paphos and sailed to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them and went back to Jerusalem. 14The rest of them went on from Perga to Antioch in Pisidia. Then on the Sabbath they went to the synagogue and sat down.
15After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the leaders sent someone over to tell Paul and Barnabas, “Friends, if you have anything to say that will help the people, please say it.”
16Paul got up. He motioned with his hand and said:
People of Israel, and everyone else who worships God, listen! 17 The God of Israel chose our ancestors, and he let our people prosper while they were living in Egypt. Then with his mighty power he led them out, 18 and for about 40 years he took care of them in the desert. 19 He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave their land to our people. 20 All this happened in about 450 years.
Then God gave our people judges until the time of the prophet Samuel, 21 but the people demanded a king. So for 40 years God gave them King Saul, the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin. 22 Later, God removed Saul and let David rule in his place. God said about him, “David the son of Jesse is the kind of person who pleases me most! He does everything I want him to do.”
23God promised that someone from David's family would come to save the people of Israel, and this one is Jesus. 24 But before Jesus came, John was telling everyone in Israel to turn back to God and be baptized. 25 Then, when John's work was almost done, he said, “Who do you people think I am? Do you think I am the Promised One? He will come later, and I am not good enough to untie his sandals.”
26Now listen, you descendants of Abraham! Pay attention, all of you Gentiles who are here to worship God! Listen to this message about how to be saved, because it is for everyone. 27The people of Jerusalem and their leaders didn't realize who Jesus was. And they didn't understand the words of the prophets they read each Sabbath. So they condemned Jesus just as the prophets had said.
28-29 They did exactly what the Scriptures said they would. Even though they couldn't find any reason to put Jesus to death, they still asked Pilate to have him killed.
After Jesus had been put to death, he was taken down from the cross and placed in a tomb. 30But God raised him from death! 31 Then for many days Jesus appeared to his followers who had gone with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Now they are telling our people about him.
32God made a promise to our ancestors. And we are here to tell you the good news 33 that he has kept this promise to us. It is just as the second Psalm says about Jesus,
“You are my son because today
I have become your Father.”
34 God raised Jesus from death and will never let his body decay. It is just as God said,
“I will make to you
the same holy promises
that I made to David.”
35 And in another psalm it says, “God will never let the body of his Holy One decay.”
36When David was alive, he obeyed God. Then after he died, he was buried in the family grave, and his body decayed. 37But God raised Jesus from death, and his body did not decay.
38My friends, the message is that Jesus can forgive your sins! The Law of Moses could not set you free from all your sins. 39But everyone who has faith in Jesus is set free. 40Make sure what the prophets have said doesn't happen to you. They said,
41 “Look, you people
who make fun of God!
Be amazed
and disappear.
I will do something today
that you won't believe,
even if someone
tells you about it!”
42As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to say more about these same things on the next Sabbath. 43After the service, many Jews and a lot of Gentiles who worshiped God went with them. Paul and Barnabas begged them all to remain faithful to God, who had treated them with undeserved grace.
44The next Sabbath almost everyone in town came to hear the message about the Lord. 45When the Jewish people saw the crowds, they were very jealous. They insulted Paul and spoke against everything he said.
46But Paul and Barnabas bravely said:
We had to tell God's message to you before we told it to anyone else. But you rejected the message! This proves that you don't deserve eternal life. Now we are going to the Gentiles. 47 The Lord has given us this command,
“I have placed you here
as a light
for the Gentiles.
You are to take
the saving power of God
to people everywhere on earth.”
48This message made the Gentiles glad, and they praised what they had heard about the Lord. Everyone who had been chosen for eternal life then put their faith in the Lord.
49The message about the Lord spread all over this region. 50But the Jewish leaders went to some of the important men in the town and to some respected women who were religious. They turned them against Paul and Barnabas and started making trouble for them. They even chased them out of this part of the country.
51 Paul and Barnabas shook the dust from that place off their feet and went on to the city of Iconium.
52But the Lord's followers in Antioch were very happy and were filled with the Holy Spirit.
translation_text:
Yezu kɔgɔ kom le Banabas de Sɔɔl
1Yezu kɔgɔ kolo déem na wo Antioka ne to maa jege Wɛ ni-jwoŋina balo na wae ba tɔɔle Wɛ kwora ye ba bere o chega kam to ba wone. Banto mo ye Banabas, de Simeon wolo ba na bwoi we nazwono to, de Kurene tu Lukius, de Manayan wolo déem na ye yuudwoŋo dedaane gɔmena tu Pɛ Herodi to, dedaane Sɔɔl. 2Dɛ dedwe ba maa wora ba ke kolo na wó pa Baŋa Wɛ zula to, ye ba ta kwori ba vɔ ba nia Wɛ ŋwaane. Wɛ Sin-laao kom laam ma ta ko bere-ba we, “Abam jege se á le Banabas de Sɔɔl amo ŋwaane se ba taa ke totoŋe delo amo na maŋe a kuri-ba se ba ke to.”
3Yezu nɔɔna bam na nigi konto to, ba daa ta ma vɔ ba nia ye ba lwoori Wɛ ba pa-ba. Ba ma daare ba daŋe ba jea ba baŋa ne, ye ba laam bane-ba pa ba viiri.
4Wɛ Sin-laao kom déem na pɛ Banabas de Sɔɔl zaŋe ba kɛ konto to, ba ma vo ba yi Selukia. Ba ma zo nabworo ba tɔge naneo kom wo ba vo ba bɛ ba yi Kupirus. 5Ba ma vo ba zo Kupirus teo kodwoŋi, ko yere mo Salamis. Ba na wora to, ba maa zoore Juu tiina jeerim di sem ba bere Wɛ taane. Jɔn Maake maa wo ba tei ne o woli-ba.
6Ba ma zaŋe Salamis ne ba tole jei sem maama ba kɛ. Ba ma vo ba yi Pafos. Ba ma jeeri liri tu wodwoŋi dáane, o yere mo Ba-yezu, ye o ye Juu tu. O déem pɛ se o ye Wɛ sampwora mo ye o dae. 7O maa ye gɔmena tu Sɛgiu Pɔɔla kwaga nɔɔno mo. Gɔmena tu wom maa ye yi-pore-nyem. O ma bwoŋi Banabas de Sɔɔl se ba ba o tei. O maa lage se o ni Wɛ kwora kam. 8Liri tu wom ma zaŋe o wora o tɔne ba berem dem. O maa kwaane se o che gɔmena tu wom se o yé sɛ Wɛ chega kam. Liri tu wom yere dedwoŋi mo ye Elumas de Girisi tiina taane dem. 9Sɔɔl yere dedwoŋi daa ta maa ye Pɔɔl. Wɛ Sin-laao kom maa wo o tei ne ye ko dam su‑o lanyerane. O ma yɔɔre o nii liri tu wom ye o we, 10“Nmo ye setaana pɛ jeŋa nɔɔno mo. Nmo chuli wonnu telo maama na lana to. Nmo kwaane se n ma n swa n gane nɔɔna mo. Nmo yeini n kwaane se n pipiri dé Teiru wom chega kam se ko taa ye vwa. 11Nii, Baŋa Wɛ wó ba o waare nmo de o je-dɛa leile konto. Nmo wó ba n ji lilwei ye n daa‑n bá‑n na wea pwooni se ko taa vei maŋa kalo Wɛ na lage to.”
O na tage konto to, bedwe baŋa ne mo Yɛlumas yia yam dwei ya ji lim yerane. O maa kare o kekara ye o lage vaŋeno se o ja o jeŋa. 12Gɔmena tu wom ma na kolo na ke to. O laam ma ba o ke o wo-dedoa de Yezu. Dé Teiru wom chega kam ba na bere‑o to ma kagele‑o.
13Pɔɔl de o badwonna bam laam ma zaŋe Pafos ne ba zo nabworo ba vo ba yi Panfilia teo kodwoŋi, ko yere mo Pɛɛga. Jɔn Maake ma yage-ba dáane ye o daare o jwoori Jerusalem. 14Ba daa maa zege Pɛɛga ne ba vo Antioka kolo na wo Pisidia ne to. Juu tiina siu dɛ dem na yi to, ba ma vo ba zo ba jeerim diga kam wo ba jei da. 15Nɔɔna ma zaŋe ba ga Moses de faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem twanno tem wone. Ba na gage ba ti to, ba yiga tiina bam ma toŋe ni ba pa Pɔɔl ba ye ba we, “Dé nu-bia bam, abam ná jege taane delo na wó fɔge nɔɔna bam to, se á zaŋe á ta.” 16Pɔɔl ma zaŋe wɛɛne o zeiŋi o jeŋa ba baŋa ne, ye o laam daare o ta o we:
“Amo dwonna Isarele dwi tiina bam dedaane dwi-gɛ tiina balo na tu á sɛ Wɛ to, cheigi-na amo. 17Isarele tiina bam Wɛ wom déem le dé nabaara bam se ba taa ye o nyem. Maŋa kam ba déem na ye veira Ejipti ne to mo Wɛ pɛ se ba puli lanyerane. O ma daare o ma o tete je-dɛa kam o le-ba pa ba nwoŋi teo kom konto ne. 18Ba na beeri kagoa yuu ne taa, bena finna to, o ma peene o bane de-ba. 19Ba na zo Kanaan to, o ma pa se logo kom dwia yera yera kuni berepɛ na chɔgem, ye o daare o pa se o tete nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam taa tei tega kam konto. 20Konto keim dem maama ye nenɛɛne bena bia yana de finnu (450) mo.
Konto kwaga ne, Wɛ laam ma kuri dedɛɛra o pa-ba ye banto tei-ba taa, se ko yi maŋa kam o sampwora Samuwel na tu o ba o tei-ba to. 21Nɔɔna bam laam ma lwoori Samuwel se o tiŋi pɛ o pa-ba. Wɛ ma tiŋi Benjamin dwi tu dedoa o pa-ba, o yere mo Sɔɔl. O maa ye Kisi bu. O ma di paare bena finna. 22Wɛ déem ma ba o le Sɔɔl paare dem wone, ye o daare o pa se David ji ba pɛ. Wɛ déem tage wonto taane o we, ‘Ko ná ye Jesse bu David, o ye nɔɔno wolo kikia na dɛ amo wo to. Wonto wó ke kolo maama a boboŋa na lage to.’
23Ko maa ye wonto dwi dem wone mo Wɛ pɛ Yezu zaŋe o ba. Wɛ ma tɔge ni delo o na tiŋi o pa o nɔɔna bam to o pa Yezu ba o ji debam Isarele tiina bam Vereno. 24Maŋa kam Yezu ta na wo bobo o totoŋa yam to, Jɔn déem mo bere Isarele tiina bam maama o we, ba leiri ba wo de ba wɛleera yam, se ba daare ba jwoŋi sɛɛm Wɛ ŋwaane. 25Ko ta na daare fenfee se Jɔn ti o totoŋa yam to, o ma bwei nɔɔna bam o we, ‘Abam boŋe we amo ye wɔ mo? Amo dae wolo wom á na jege o teena to. Wonto nam lage o saŋe amo kwaga o ba, ye amo wo maŋe se a bwoli o nɛ natera de.’
26Amo nu-bia bam, Abaraham dwi tiina, de dwi-gɛ tiina balo na tu á kɔre Wɛ to, ko ye debam mo Wɛ pɛ se dé ni o taane dem konto se dé wane dé lɔre o na lage o jwoŋi debam o yage tei to. 27Jerusalem tiina bam de ba yiga tiina bam nam wo lɔre Yezu na ye wolo to. Ko daa ta ná ye wonnu telo Wɛ sampwori sem na popone ba tiŋi ye nɔɔna yeini ba gare-te ba siu da yam maama ne to, ba ba ni wonnu tento kuri de. Ba nam na pɛ se Yezu na chɔgem to, ko pɛ se Wɛ sampwori sem na popone kolo to seene ko ji chega. 28Ba maa wo nɛ taane delo na wó pa se ba go‑o to. De konto de, ba ta ma lwoori Pilata se o pa o te. 29Ba ma ke kolo maama na maŋe ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne ye ko ta o taane to ba ti. O na tege to, ba laam ma pare‑o dagara kam yuu ne ba daare ba ke‑o yibeeli wone. 30Wɛ laam ma pa o bi toone wone. 31O maa wora da kɔgɔ kɔgɔ. O na wora to, kuni dedɛ mo o veere o tete o tɔgena bam yia ne. Balo ya na tɔge ded‑o Galili ne ba beeri ba vo Jerusalem to mo konto. Banto laam zege o chega kam kwaga ne ba pa debam Isarele tiina bam.
32Debam laam tu abam tei se dé ta Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam dé bere abam. Ko maa ye we, Wɛ déem na pwooli de dé nabaara bam we o wó ke kolo to mo 33o laam seene o ke o pa debam balo na ye ba naaro to. Ko ye o bi Yezu toone wone mo konto. Ko ta ye nenɛɛne ko na maŋe ko popone Wɛ Seinim Lei tɔnɔ belei tu wone to ye ko we:
‘Nmo mo ye amo Bu,
ye zem amo de ji nmo Kwo.’
34Wɛ tɔnɔ kom daa ta bere Wɛ na wó bi‑o toone wone pa se o yera daa bá pɔ to. Ko maa we:
‘Amo wó pa se n na wo-laaro telo na ye chekke
ye a maŋe a tiŋi ni se a pa David na-te to.’
35Wɛ tɔnɔ kom jei sedwoŋi ne ko popone we:
‘Nmo bá‑n sɛ se n tete Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom yera pɔ.’
36Ko nam ná ye David tete, wonto déem toŋe Wɛ totoŋa yam maŋa kalo o na ŋwe to ye o laam ba o te. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o nabaara bam tei ne. O yera ma seene ya pɔ. 37Ko daare wolo wom Wɛ na pɛ o bi toone wone to, wonto yera nam wo pɔge kɔtaa.
38A nu-bia bam, abam jege se á lɔre we ko ye Yezu ŋwaane mo dé jege chwoŋa se dé bere abam we, Wɛ wó wane o yage á wɛleera o ma chɛ abam. 39Wɛ nia yalo o na ke Moses jeŋa ne to ware ya pa á wɛleera yam saare. Ko daare wolo maama na ke o wo-dedoa de Yezu to wó na bora Wɛ tei ne, de o wɛleera yam maama na saare wonto ŋwaane to. 40Nam ta‑á yei-na á tete ni ne, se lɛɛro telo Wɛ sampwori sem na popone te taane to yé seene te ke abam baŋa ne. 41Ba déem we:
‘Nii-na, wɛ-lwɛɛna bam,
abam yera wó sɔɔre ye á daare á te.
Kolo ŋwaane amo lage a ke woŋo abam da yam wone,
ye nɔɔno ná maŋe o bere abam ko kuri tei maama de,
á bá sɛ we ko ye chega’ ”
42Pɔɔl na tage konto o ti to, o de Banabas ma zaŋe se ba nwoŋi jeerim diga kam wone. Ba na lage ba viiri to, nɔɔna bam ma ta de-ba se ba jwoori ba siu dɛ dedwoŋi dem ne, se ba daa ta wonnu tem konto taane. 43Nɔɔna bam ma zaŋe ba jage se ba vo sam. Ba dedɛ ma tɔge Pɔɔl de Banabas, Juu tiina de dwi-gɛ tiina balo na tu ba sɛ Wɛ to de. Pɔɔl de Banabas maa tɛ de nɔɔna bam se ba taa kwaane ba dale Wɛ, de zaane delo o na ke ba yuu ne to.
44Ba siu dɛ dem ma jwoori de yi. Nɔɔna dedɛ ma la daane se ba cheigi Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam. Ko déem nye de ko ye teo kom nɔɔna maama mo jeeri da. 45Juu tiina bam na nɛ kɔgɔ kom na su jei sem maama to, ba maa tiini ba jege puseŋa de-ba. Ba ma yaale Pɔɔl na tɛ kolo to ye ba kwori ba twe‑o. 46Pɔɔl de Banabas laam fɔge ba ŋɔɔne de baare ye ba we, “Dé ya jege se dé bobo abam tei ne mo dé ŋɔɔne Wɛ kwora kam. Abam nam na maŋe á wo sɛ-ka to, ko bere we á ba boŋe se á maŋe de Wɛ ŋwe-doŋa kam. Konto ŋwaane mo dé laam wó vo dwi-gɛ tiina bam tei dé daare abam. 47Dé Teiru Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ debam o ni tei to mo tento:
‘Amo tiŋi nmo se n ji pwooni
n nye dwi-gɛ tiina bam baŋa ne,
se n wane n pa nabiina na verem
logo baŋa jei maama ne.’ ”
48 Dwi-gɛ tiina balo na wora to na nigi konto to, ba maa jege wopwolo ye ba pa se Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam jege dam. Balo maama Wɛ na kuri se ba na o ŋwe-doŋa kam to mo seene ba ke ba wo-dedoa de Yezu.
49Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam ma jage laŋa kam konto maama wone. 50Ko daare Juu tiina bam ma kwaane ba pa se nɔɔna bane zaŋe de Pɔɔl de Banabas. Ko ná ye kaana balo jeŋa na gare ye ba kɔre Wɛ to, de teo kom dedɛɛra bam, ba déem pɛ se ba yaare Pɔɔl de Banabas, ye ba daare ba zeili-ba pa ba nwoŋi ba teo kom ne. 51Ko na ke-ba konto to, Pɔɔl de Banabas ma kokɔge ba nɛ fwogo kom ba yage da se ba kaane nɔɔna bam. Ba laam ma daare ba vo Ikonium. 52Yezu tɔgena bam déem tiini ba di ywoni. Wɛ Sin-laao kom maa wo ba tei ne ko su-ba lanyerane.

english_text:
Paul and Barnabas in Iconium
1Paul and Barnabas spoke in the synagogue in Iconium, just as they had done at Antioch, and many Jews and Gentiles put their faith in the Lord. 2But the Jews who did not have faith in him made the other Gentiles angry and turned them against the Lord's followers.
3Paul and Barnabas stayed there for a while, having faith in the Lord and bravely speaking his message. The Lord gave them the power to work miracles and wonders, and he showed that their message about his gift of undeserved grace was true.
4The people of Iconium did not know what to think. Some of them believed the Jewish group, and others believed the apostles. 5Finally, some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, decided to make trouble for Paul and Barnabas and to stone them to death.
6-7But when the two apostles found out what was happening, they escaped to the region of Lycaonia. They preached the good news there in the towns of Lystra and Derbe and in the nearby countryside.
Paul and Barnabas in Lystra
8In Lystra there was a man who had been born with paralyzed feet and had never been able to walk. 9The man was listening to Paul speak, when Paul saw that he had faith in Jesus and could be healed. So he looked straight at the man 10and shouted, “Stand up!” The man jumped up and started walking around.
11When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they yelled out in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have turned into humans and have come down to us!” 12The people then gave Barnabas the name Zeus, and they gave Paul the name Hermes, because he did the talking.
13The temple of Zeus was near the entrance to the city. Its priest and the crowds wanted to offer a sacrifice to Barnabas and Paul. So the priest brought some bulls and flowers to the city gates. 14When the two apostles found out about this, they tore their clothes in horror and ran to the crowd, shouting:
15 Why are you doing this? We are humans just like you. Please give up all this foolishness. Turn to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them. 16In times past, God let each nation go its own way. 17But he showed he was there by the good things he did. God sends rain from heaven and makes your crops grow. He gives food to you and makes your hearts glad.
18Even after Paul and Barnabas had said all this, they could hardly keep the people from offering a sacrifice to them.
19Some Jewish leaders from Antioch and Iconium came and turned the crowds against Paul. They hit him with stones and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead. 20But when the Lord's followers gathered around Paul, he stood up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas went to Derbe.
Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch in Syria
21Paul and Barnabas preached the good news in Derbe and won some people to the Lord. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch in Pisidia. 22They encouraged the followers and begged them to remain faithful. They told them, “We have to suffer a lot before we can get into God's kingdom.” 23Paul and Barnabas chose some leaders for each of the churches. Then they went without eating and prayed that the Lord would take good care of these leaders who had trusted in the Lord.
24Paul and Barnabas went on through Pisidia to Pamphylia, 25where they preached in the town of Perga. Then they went down to Attalia 26and sailed to Antioch in Syria. It was there that they had been placed in God's care for the work they had now completed.
27After arriving in Antioch, they called the church together. They told the people what God had helped them do and how he had made it possible for the Gentiles to believe. 28Then they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
translation_text:
Ko na ke tei Ikonium ne
1Pɔɔl de Banabas déem ma vo ba yi Ikonium. Ba na wora to, ba yeini ba vei Juu tiina jeerim diga kam, ye ko ke-ba ne ko na maŋe ko ke tei to. Ba déem ŋɔɔne Wɛ taane dem ba bere nɔɔna bam pa se ba dedɛ ke ba wo-dedoa de Yezu, Juu tiina de dwi-gɛ tiina de. 2Ko daare Juu tiina badwonna ve Wɛ taane dem. Banto ma zaŋe ba vugimi dwi-gɛ tiina bam boboŋa pa se ba wo chɔge de Yezu nɔɔna bam. 3Pɔɔl de Banabas maa zoore da taa se ko dáane. Ba na wora konto to, ba maa ŋɔɔne dé Teiru wom taane de baare. Ba maa tɛ dé Teiru wom na ke nɔɔna zaane tei to, ye o zege ba taane dem kwaga ne de o na pɛ-ba dam se ba taa ke wo-kenkagela de maana tei to. 4Teo kom nɔɔna bam maama déem pɔɔre belei mo. Ba badaara tɔge Juu tiina bam mo, ye badaara bam de maa tɔge Yezu totoŋa nakwa bam.
5 Dwi-gɛ tiina de Juu tiina badwonna boboŋa laam ma ja se ba tɔge dedaane ba yiga tiina bam ba ke lwarem ba pa Yezu tontoŋena bam, se ba dole-ba de kandwa ba go. 6Ba na lɔre ko ni ne to, ba ma duri ba vo Lukayonia teene Lustera de Dɛɛbe, de de nawuura yam. 7Ba na wora to, ba ma yɔɔre ba tɔɔle Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam.
Ko na ke tei Lustera ne
8Nɔɔno déem mo wo Lustera ne ye o nɛ sem gwarege. Ko zege o lora maŋa ne o maŋe o ye gɔrɔ mo, o ware o vo. 9O déem maa tɔge o jei o cheigi Pɔɔl na ŋɔɔne taane delo to. Pɔɔl ma yɔɔre o nii‑o ye o lɔre we o jege wo-dedoa de Yezu se o wane o na yazura. 10O laam ma ta de kwor-dɛa o we, “Zaŋe wɛɛne n zege n nɛ sem baŋa ne yɔm!” O na tage konto to, gɔrɔ kom ma zaŋe wɛɛne o faŋe o chu ye o bobo veiŋa. 11Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom na nɛ kolo Pɔɔl na ke to, ba ma tiini ba ŋɔɔne baŋa baŋa de ba tete teo kom taane dem ba we, “Ko ye debam wa yam mo jigi nabiina ya tu ya ba debam tei.” 12Ba ma pa Banabas yere we Zeusa. Pɔɔl de yere maa ye Hɛmesi, kolo ŋwaane ko ye wonto ya mo ŋɔɔne taane dem.
13Ba déem maa jege diga ba teo kom manchwoŋo ni ne ba na yeini ba kaane ba wɛ Zeusa da to. Ba kaanem yuu tu wom ma zaŋe o ja nabɛ de teeni punnu telo ba na sɔge to o ba o zege teo kom ni dem ne. Wonto dedaane nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama déem maa lage se ba go nabɛ sem ba ma kaane Yezu nɔɔna bam. 14Yezu totoŋa nakwa Banabas de Pɔɔl ma lɔre ba na boŋe se ba ke tei to. Ba wo ma chɔge dedɛ. Ba ma ja ba tete gwaaro tem ba kaare kaare, ye ba daare ba duri lela ba zo nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wo. Ba maa tɛ baŋa baŋa ba we, 15“Nɔɔna bam, bɛ mo ye abam lage á ke konto? Debam ye nabiina mo, ne abam tete tei. Debam nam tu ywoba seeni se dé tɔɔle Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam mo dé bere abam, se ko pa á yage jwona kaanem, se á daare á ta‑á tɔge ŋwea tu Baŋa Wɛ. Wonto mo ke wɛyuu, de tega baŋa, de naneo kom, de wonnu telo maama na wo te wone to. 16Faŋa to Wɛ déem yage chwoŋa o pa logo baŋa dwi maama tiina se ba taa tɔge chwei selo ba na lage to. 17De konto de o ta yeini o ke abam lanyerane se ko pa á lɔre we o ye Wɛ chekke. O yeini o pa se doa nena ye wodiiru ke te maŋa ne. O maa pae abam wodiu ye á di, ye o pa se á na ywoni á bochara ne lanyerane.”
18Pɔɔl na tage konto to, ko ya gɛ fenfee mo se nɔɔna bam kwei wonnu tem ba ma kaane-ba, ye ba laam yage.
19Juu tiina badwonna ya nwoŋi Pisidia teo Antioka mo ba ba. Badaara de ma nwoŋi Ikonium ba ba. Banto ma pa se kɔgɔ kom maama boboŋa leiri de Pɔɔl. Ba laam ma dole‑o de kandwa ye ba daare ba tuuri‑o ba ja nwoŋi teo kom wone. Ba ya boŋe we o tege mo. 20Yezu tɔgena bam laam ma vo ba gilimi‑o. O ma zaŋe ba tetare ne o jwoori o zo teo kom wo. Tega na poore to, o ma tɔge dedaane Banabas ye ba vo Dɛɛbe.
Ba jwoori ba vo Antioka
21Pɔɔl de Banabas na wo Dɛɛbe ne to, ba ma tɔɔle Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam ba bere nɔɔna pa se ba dedɛ ji Yezu tɔgena. Ba daa ma jwoori ba vo Lustera de Ikonium, ye ba daare ba kɛ ba yi Antioka kolo na wo Pisidia wone to. 22Ba na maa vei konto to, ba ma pa se balo maama na ye Yezu tɔgena to boboŋa su de baare, ye ba kwoori-ba se ba fɔge ba taa tɔge Wɛ chega kam, se ba yé yage-ka. Ba ta ma bere-ba we, “Debam balo maama na sɛ Yezu to jege se dé na yaara dedɛ mo se dé daare dé zo Wɛ woro kom wo.”
23Jei selo maama ba na vei to, ba déem le nakwa Yezu kɔgɔ kom wone se ba taa nii-ba. Ba ma yeini ba lwoori Wɛ ba pa nakwa bam ye ba vɔ ba nia Wɛ ŋwaane. Ba tɔge konto dwoŋi mo ba fɔge ba ke nakwa bam dé Teiru wom jeŋa ne, o na ye wolo ba na ke ba wo-dedoa ded‑o to ŋwaane.
24Ba déem ma da Pisidia ni maama ba kɛ. Ba ma vo ba yi Panfilia jei sem. 25Ba na wora to, ba ma vo Pɛɛga ba bere Wɛ kwora kam da, ye ba daare ba vo Atalia. 26Ba laam ma zege dáane ba zo nabworo ba jwoori ba vo Antioka kolo na wo Siria wone to. Ko déem ye konto jei sem ne mo Yezu kɔgɔ kom nɔɔna bam ya kwei-ba ba ke Wɛ jeŋa ne se o ke-ba zaane se ba wane ba vo ba beeri ba toŋe kolo ba laam na tu ba ke ba ti to. 27Ba na yi Antioka to, ba ma pa se Yezu kɔgɔ kom la daane, ye ba laam tole ba bere-ba kolo maama Wɛ na tɔge ba ŋwaane o ke to, de o na pore chwoŋa o pa dwi-gɛ tiina se ba wane ba ke ba wo-dedoa de Yezu to. 28Ba maa zoore Yezu tɔgena bam tei ne taa.

english_text:
1 Some people came from Judea and started teaching the Lord's followers that they could not be saved, unless they were circumcised as Moses had taught. 2This caused trouble, and Paul and Barnabas argued with them about this teaching. So it was decided to send Paul and Barnabas and a few others to Jerusalem to discuss this problem with the apostles and the church leaders.
The Church Leaders Meet in Jerusalem
3The men who were sent by the church went through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling how the Gentiles had turned to God. This news made the Lord's followers very happy. 4When the men arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, including the apostles and the leaders. They told them everything God had helped them do. 5But some Pharisees had become followers of the Lord. They stood up and said, “Gentiles who have faith in the Lord must be circumcised and told to obey the Law of Moses.”
6The apostles and church leaders met to discuss this problem about Gentiles. 7 They had talked it over for a long time, when Peter got up and said:
My friends, you know that God decided long ago to let me be the one from your group to preach the good news to the Gentiles. God did this so they would hear and obey him. 8 He knows what is in everyone's heart. And he showed he had chosen the Gentiles, when he gave them the Holy Spirit, just as he had given his Spirit to us. 9God treated them in the same way that he treated us. They put their faith in him, and he made their hearts pure.
10Now why are you trying to make God angry by placing a heavy burden on these followers? This burden was too heavy for us or our ancestors. 11But we believe that we will be saved by the gift of undeserved grace from our Lord Jesus Christ, just as the Gentiles are.
12Everyone kept quiet and listened as Barnabas and Paul told how God had given them the power to work a lot of miracles and wonders for the Gentiles.
13After they had finished speaking, James said:
My friends, listen to me! 14Simon Peter has told how God first came to the Gentiles and made some of them his own people. 15This agrees with what the prophets wrote,
16 “I, the Lord, will return
and rebuild
David's fallen house.
I will build it from its ruins
and set it up again.
17Then other nations
will turn to me
and be my chosen ones.
I, the Lord, say this.
18I promised it long ago.”
19And so, my friends, I don't think we should place burdens on the Gentiles who are turning to God. 20 We should simply write and tell them not to eat anything that has been offered to idols. They should be told not to eat the meat of any animal that has been strangled or that still has blood in it. They must also not commit any terrible sexual sins.
21We must remember that the Law of Moses has been preached in city after city for many years, and every Sabbath it is read in our synagogues.
A Letter to Gentiles Who Had Faith in the Lord
22The apostles, the leaders, and all the church members decided to send some men to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Silas and Judas Barsabbas, who were two leaders of the Lord's followers. 23They wrote a letter that said:
We apostles and leaders send friendly greetings to all of you Gentiles who are followers of the Lord in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
24We have heard that some people from here have terribly upset you by what they said. But we did not send them! 25So we met together and decided to choose some men and to send them to you along with our good friends Barnabas and Paul. 26These men have risked their lives for our Lord Jesus Christ. 27We are also sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things that we are writing.
