Ko daare balo Wɛ nia yam na tei-ba to ná ke ba tusi, Wɛ wó tɔge o nia yam konto baŋa ne mo o chɔge-ba. 13Kokuri, nɔɔna bá na chega de Wɛ ba na nigi o nia yam to ŋwaane. Ba nam ná seene ba tɔge Wɛ nia yam na bere tei to, ba laam wó na chega o tei ne. 14Dwi-gɛ tiina bam nam yeiri Wɛ nia yam se ba taa tɔge-ya. Ba tete boboŋa nam wae ya pae se ba tɔge chega kalo Wɛ nia yam na bere to. Ko maa bere we, ba maŋe ba yei kolo na maŋe se ba taa ke to, ye Wɛ nia yam ta tera ba tei ne. 15Ba kikia yam bere we chega kalo Wɛ nia yam na bere to tigi ba bochara ne. Ba boboŋa na pae ba tɔge chwoŋa kalo to de bere we konto ye chega, kolo ŋwaane ba boboŋa wae ya bere-ba we ba ke ba chɔge, naa ya ga bere-ba we ba jege chega. 16Ko wó taa ye konto mo Wɛ borem dɛ dem ne. Baŋa Wɛ wó da Yezu Krista ŋwaane o bore nɔɔna maama boboŋa yalo na seigi to. Mo amo na yeini a bere Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam tei to.
Wɔ mo ye Juu tu chekke?
17Nmo wolo na bere n tete we n ye Juu tu to, ko wó ke‑m tetɛ mo? Nmo dale Wɛ nia yam mo, ye n jege teera de n na tɔge Wɛ tei to. 18Nmo maŋe n yei Wɛ boboŋa na lage se n ke tei to. Nmo na zamese Wɛ nia yam to mo pɛ se n lɔre woŋo kolo na ye chega to. 19Nmo boŋe we n jege Wɛ pwooni n pae balo ta na wo lim wone to, ye n nye de lilwei vaŋeno se n pa nɔɔna tɔge Wɛ chwoŋa. 20Nmo ma‑n boŋe we n jege chwoŋa se n bere nayeiri-nyena, ye n daare n zamese balo boboŋa ta na wo kweere to. Wɛ nia yam na tiini ya bere yeino de chega kam maama to mo pae n boŋe konto. 21Nmo nam na bere n tete konto to, ko lana na? N yeini n jege n dwonna n bera. Bɛŋwaane mo ye n tete ba jwoŋi bera? N bere nɔɔna we, ba yé taa ŋɔna. Nmo tete ba ŋɔne na? 22N tɛ we, ba yé ke kabwoŋa kikia. Nmo tete ba ke kabwoŋa na? N chuli jwona. Nmo tete nam ba ŋɔne wonnu jwona yam di sem ne na? 23Nmo jege teera de Wɛ na ke o nia yam n jeŋa ne to. Nmo nam ba chɔge Wɛ yere dem mo, de n na jege o nia yam n chɔge tei to na? 24Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we, “Ko ye abam Juu tiina kikia ŋwaane mo pae se dwi-gɛ tiina jege Wɛ yere dem ba yaala.”
25Abam yeini á gwoni á peina se ko bere we á ye Wɛ nɔɔna mo. Á ná kwaane á tɔge Wɛ nia yam, á peina gwonim jege kuri á tei ne. Ko daare, á ná chɔge Wɛ nia yam, á peina gwonim dem ye kafɛ mo. 26Dwi-gɛ tiina nam ba yeini ba gwoni ba peina. Ba wone dedoa nam ná tɔge chega kalo Wɛ nia yam na bere to, konto tu wó taa ye bedwe de Juu tu wolo na gwoni o peini se ko bere we o ye Wɛ nyem to. 27Dwi-gɛ tiina wó bere we abam Juu tiina ba jege chega. Á jege Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom á tei ne, ye á gwoni á peina. De ko de, á ta yeini á chɔge Wɛ nia yam mo. Banto peina nam wo gwoni ye ba nam tɔge Wɛ nia yam mo.
28Ko dae wolo na bere o tete we o ye Juu tu to mo seene o ye Juu tu chekke Wɛ yiga ne. Ko nam ta dae we wolo yera na jege gwonim to mo seene o ye Wɛ nyem. 29Wɛ yiga ne, Juu tu chekke ye wolo bochare na pae o ye Wɛ nyem to mo. Wonto bochare na fɔge de kwɛ tei to mo nye de o peini dem gwonim chekke. Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom bá wane ko fɔge nɔɔno bochare. Ko maa ye Wɛ Sin-laao kom keim mo. Nɔɔno wom konto dwoŋi nae zula Wɛ tei ne mo, se ko dae nabiina tei ne.

english_text:
1What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised? 2It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews. 3It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith? 4 No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God,
“Your words
will be proven true,
and in court
you will win your case.”
5If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask. 6But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world? 7Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner. 8You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well.
No One Is Good
9What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said. 10 The Scriptures tell us,
“No one is acceptable to God!
11Not one of them understands
or even searches for God.
12They have all turned away
and are worthless.
There isn't one person
who does right.
13 Their words are like
an open pit,
and their tongues are good
only for telling lies.
Each word is as deadly
as the fangs of a snake,
14 and they say nothing
but bitter curses.
15 These people quickly
become violent.
16Wherever they go,
they leave ruin
and destruction.
17They don't know how
to live in peace.
18 They don't even fear God.”
19We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty. 20 God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin.
God's Way of Accepting People
21Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses. 22 God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ. 23All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory. 24But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins. 25-26 God sent Christ to be our sacrifice. Christ offered his life's blood, so by faith in him we could come to God. And God did this to show that in the past he was right to be patient and forgive sinners. This also shows that God is right when he accepts people who have faith in Jesus.
27What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith. 28We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law. 29Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is! 30 There is only one God, and he accepts Gentiles as well as Jews, simply because of their faith. 31Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_text:
Juu tu dwoi dwi-gɛ tu na?
1Juu tu nam nɛ nyɔɔre se ko dwoni dwi-gɛ tu na? Ba ná gwoni Juu tu peini, ko jege wolim ko pa‑o na? 2Ɛɛ, ko tiini ko jege kuri. Yiga to, Juu tiina bam mo ye balo Wɛ na kwei o ni-botare sem o ke ba jeŋa ne to. 3Ba badaara nam wo ke ba wo-dedoa de Wɛ. Konto nam bá wane ko pa Wɛ taa ye wolo na nwoŋi o chega kam kwaga ne to. 4Kɔtaa. Nɔɔna maama ná maŋe ba ye vwa-nyena, Wɛ jege se o ta taa ye chega tu mo. Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
“Nmo jege chega de nmo na ŋɔɔne taane delo to.
Nmo ná bore nɔɔna taane,
n ta jege chega mo.”
5Konto ŋwaane, dé ná maŋe dé tɔge tusim kikia, ko ta bere jaja we Wɛ tiini o jege chega. Konto maa pae se nɔɔna wae ba tɛ we, Wɛ ná waare-ba ba tusim kikia ŋwaane, o wo ke lanyerane. 6Konto nam ba jege kuri. Wɛ ya ná ba jege chega, o ya bá wane o di nabiina bora. 7Nɔɔna ta wae ba tɛ we, “Amo ná yeini a fɔ vwa, konto wae ko pa nɔɔna lɔre jaja we Wɛ tiini o ye chega tu mo, pa se o jwoŋi yere lanyerane. Ko na ye konto to, bɛ mo ye a jege se a na chɔgem a keim-balwaaro ŋwaane?” 8Konto ya ná ye chega, dé ya wó wane dé ta we, “Pa-na se dé taa toŋe lwarem, se ko wane ko ja lanyerane ko ba.” Nɔɔna badwonna bere we amo yeini a tɛ konto dwoŋi. Ba nam lage se ba chɔge amo yere mo. Ba tete wó na chɔgem se ko maŋe de ba kikia.
Wɔ mo jege chega Wɛ yiga ne?
9Ko bere we debam Juu tiina bam gare dwi-gɛ tiina bam na? Aawo, kɔtaa. Amo ya maŋe a ta jaja we nɔɔna maama wo wɛleera jeŋa ne mo, ko ná ye Juu tiina naa dwi-gɛ tiina bam de. 10Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
“Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na jege chega Wɛ tei ne,
de nɔɔno dedoa de.
11Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na lɔre swa chekke.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na lage Wɛ se o zuli‑o.
12Nɔɔna maama mɛ ba kwaga ba ya Wɛ,
ye ba maama tusi.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na ke lanyerane,
de nɔɔno dedoa de.
13Ba nia maa ŋɔɔre,
ne yibeeli na puri to.
Ba maa mae ba dindeilima
ba gane nɔɔna.
Ba ni taane goe nɔɔna,
ne kapaa vea na ke tei to.
14Ba maa sɔɔle wo-balwaaro ba pa nɔɔna.
15Ba tiini ba lage lela de nɔɔna gom.
16Ba yeini ba chɔge nɔɔna pa ba na yaara dedɛ.
17Ba maa yeiri ywoni chwoŋa se ba tɔge-ka.
18Ba maa bere ba ba kɔre Wɛ.”
19Dé yei we kolo maama Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom na bere to, ko popone ko pa balo ni-kaana yam na tei-ba to mo. Konto ŋwaane, nabiina maama wó ba ba zege Wɛ yiga ne se o bwei-ba, ye ba wolowolo bá wane o pore o ni se o jwoŋi o tete. 20Wɛ ni-kaana yam pae se nabiina lɔre we ba ke ba tusi. Nɔɔno ná maŋe o yɔɔre o tɔge-ya tei, konto bá wane ko pa o na chega Wɛ yiga ne.
Dé na wó na chega Wɛ tei ne tei to
21Leile konto dé laam lɔre Wɛ na tɔge chwoŋa kalo o pae se nɔɔna jege chega o tei ne to, ye ko ba zege o nia yam tɔgem baŋa ne. Moses de Wɛ sampwori sem de na bere tei faŋa faŋa to nam maŋe ko bere ko na wó taa ye tei to. 22Ko nam ye nɔɔna na ke ba wo-dedoa de Yezu Krista tei to ŋwaane mo Wɛ pae ba jege chega o tei ne. Balo maama na ke ba wo-dedoa ba sɛ Yezu Krista to wó na chega Wɛ yiga ne, kolo ŋwaane nɔɔna maama ye bedwe mo o tei ne. 23Nabiina maama tusi ye ba ware ba maŋe de Wɛ paare dem. 24Wɛ nam tɔge o zaane dem baŋa ne mo o pae se nɔɔna na chega o tei ne, Yezu Krista na ŋwe ba wɛleera jene o ma jwoŋi-ba to ŋwaane. Wɛ pae nɔɔna o zaane dem zɛɛra mo. 25O ma pa se Yezu ba o ji kaanem. O jana bam na nwoŋi konto to, o wane o saare nɔɔna wɛleera Wɛ yiga ne, ba na jege wo-dedoa ded‑o to ŋwaane. Wɛ ke konto mo se ko bere we o ye chega tu. Faŋa faŋa to o déem jege o tete mo ye o ba ke nɔɔna wɛleera o boboŋa ne se o chɔge-ba ya ŋwaane. 26Ko daare leile konto mo Wɛ bere we o ye chega tu de o na jwoŋi nɔɔna ba wɛleera wone ye o pa ba na chega o tei ne to. Konto maa bere we Wɛ jege chega ye o ta pae se balo maama na ke ba wo-dedoa de Yezu to de jege chega o tei ne.
27Ko na ye konto to, dé wó wane dé mage dé nyɔɔna bɛ baŋa ne mo? Kolokolo tera. Kolo ŋwaane ko dae dé na tɔge Wɛ ni-kaana yam to mo wó pa dé na chega. Ko nam ye dé na jege wo-dedoa to ŋwaane mo. 28Kokuri dé yei we nɔɔna wó na chega Wɛ tei ne ba wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane mo, ye ko dae ni-kaana yam tɔgem ŋwaane. 29Wɛ yiga wo Juu tiina bam yerane wone mo na? O yiga tera de dwi-gɛ tiina na? Aawo. O nii nabiina maama baŋa ne mo. 30Wɛ ye dedoa mo. Juu tiina ná ke ba wo-dedoa ded‑o, o wó pa ba na chega o yiga ne. Dwi-gɛ tiina de ná ke konto, o wó ke-ba bedwe mo. 31Konto nam ba bere we Wɛ ni-kaana yam daa ba jege kuri. Dé wo-dedoa kam bá wane ka leiri Wɛ ni-kaana yam yuu ne. Dé nam na jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ tei to pae se o nia yam tiini ya jege kuri mo.

english_text:
The Example of Abraham
1Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham? 2If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God. 3 The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
4Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working. 5But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him. 6In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
7-8 “What a blessing
when God forgives our sins
and our evil deeds.
What a blessing
when the Lord erases our sins
from his book.”
9Are these blessings meant for circumcised people or for those who are not circumcised? Well, the Scriptures say that God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him. 10But when did this happen? Was it before or after Abraham was circumcised? Of course, it was before.
11 Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised. 12This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised.
The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
13 God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable. 14 If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
15God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken. 16 Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all. 17 The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
18 God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations. 19 Abraham's faith never became weak, not even when he was nearly 100 years old. He knew he was almost dead and that his wife Sarah could not have children. 20But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
21Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised. 22So God accepted him, 23just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham. 24They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life. 25 God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
translation_text:
Abaraham na nɛ chega tei to
1Á pa dé nii dé nabaaro Abaraham déem na ye tei ye o jege chega Wɛ tei ne to. Dé wó ta we o nɛ kɔ mo? 2Wɛ ya ná pɛ‑o chega o na ke keim-laaro to ŋwaane, o ya wó taa jege woŋo se o mage o nyɔɔne ko baŋa ne, se ko dae Wɛ yiga ne mo o wae o ke konto. 3Wɛ tɔnɔ kom nam bere debam we, “Abaraham sɛ Wɛ de wo-dedoa, ye Wɛ pa o na chega ko ŋwaane.” 4Ko nam ná ye nɔɔno ná toŋe totoŋa, o wó jwoŋi o ŋweero o totoŋa yam baŋa ne, ye ko dae pɛɛre mo o jwoŋi. 5Ko daare nɔɔno wolo ná maŋe o ba tɔge keim-laaro ŋwaane se o na chega Wɛ tei ne, ye o ta ke o wo-dedoa de Wɛ, Wɛ wó pa konto tu na chega o wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane. Wɛ mo ye wolo na pae se wɛ-lwɛɛna na chega o yiga ne. 6Pɛ David de maŋe o ŋɔɔne taane dento dwoŋi. O déem tage we, nɔɔno wolo Wɛ na pɛ se o na chega ye ko dae o keim-laaro ŋwaane to ye wopwolo tu mo. 7David maa we:
“Balo Wɛ na yage ba wo-balwaaro tem o ma chɛ-ba to jege yu-ywoŋo,
o na saare ba wɛleera to ŋwaane.
8Nɔɔno wolo na jege wɛleera
ye Wɛ ba ke-ya o bochare ne to jege yu-ywoŋo.”
9David na ŋɔɔne wopwolo kom taane to, o ŋɔɔne o pa balo peina na gwoni to yerane mo na? O nam ŋɔɔne o pa balo peina na wo gwoni to de mo. Dé maŋe dé lɔre we, “Abaraham ke o wo-dedoa o sɛ Wɛ, ye Wɛ pa o na chega ko ŋwaane.” 10Wɛ na pɛ o jege chega o tei ne konto to, ko ye o peini na maŋe de gwoni to mo na? Aawo, o peini ya ta wo gwoni mo. 11Ko ye ko kwaga ne mo ba gwoni o peini se ko taa ye maana we Wɛ maŋe o pa o jege chega o wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane ye ba ta wo gwoni o peini. Konto to, balo maama peina na wo gwoni ye ba ke ba wo-dedoa de Wɛ pa se ba na chega o tei ne to ye Abaraham dwi tiina chekke mo. 12Balo maama na ke ba wo-dedoa de Wɛ ye ba maŋe ba gwoni ba peina to de ye Abaraham dwi tiina mo, de ba na tɔge Abaraham déem na jege wo-dedoa ye ba ta wo gwoni o peini tei to.
13Ko dae Abaraham na tɔge Wɛ ni-kaana yam tei to ŋwaane mo pɛ se Wɛ pwooli se o zeini Abaraham de o dwi tiina bam. Ko nam ye Abaraham na jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ ye o na chega o tei ne to ŋwaane mo pɛ Wɛ pwooli we, o wó pa o ba o taa tei logo kom. 14Ko ya ná ye balo na boŋe se ba na chega Wɛ tei ne de ba ni-kaana tɔgem to mo wó ba ba taa tei logo kom, ko ya wó pa se wo-dedoa tɔgem daa ta ba jege kuri, ye Wɛ kampwola kam de wó ji kafɛ mo. 15Wɛ ni-kaana yam mo pae o bane zaŋe de nɔɔna de ba na chɔge-ya to ŋwaane. Ni-kaana nam ná tera, nɔɔna bá wane ba lɔre we ba chɔge-ya.
16Dé lɔre we ko ye Abaraham wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane mo pɛ se Wɛ pwooli kampwola ded‑o, se o wane o pa-ka zɛɛra. Konto to, Abaraham dwi tiina bam maama wó seene ba na wo-laaro telo Wɛ na tiŋi o ni se o pa-ba to. Ko dae balo na jege Wɛ ni-kaana yam ba tɔge to yerane mo wó na-te, se ko ye balo de na jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ ne Abaraham de na jege tei to mo. Konto ŋwaane, debam maama wó wane dé bwoŋi Abaraham we dé nabaaro. 17Wɛ déem tage de Abaraham o we, “Amo gwoni a ni se a pa n ji dwi tiina dedɛ nabaaro.” Abaraham na ke o wo-dedoa de Wɛ to, o seene o ye dé nabaaro Wɛ yiga ne. Wɛ nam mo bi nɔɔna toone wone o pa-ba ŋwea, ye o ŋɔɔne wonnu telo ta na tera to, ne te na maŋe te wora tei to. 18Wɛ déem na tage de Abaraham we, o dwi tiina wó puli to, Abaraham maa yeiri Wɛ na wó ke tei o ke konto. De konto de, o jege teena lanyerane, ye o ke o wo-dedoa o sɛ Wɛ ni dem. Konto ma pa se o seene o ji dwi tiina dedɛ nabaaro, nenɛɛne Wɛ na tage we o dwi dem wó puli tei to. 19Abaraham déem na yi bena bi to, o ma na we o yera tiini ya bugi ye o ga fee se o te. O ma daare o na o kaane Sara de na kwe dedɛ ye o kɛ lora to. De konto maama o déem wo pɛ se o wo-dedoa kam chɔge. 20O maa ba jege boboŋa yalei de Wɛ na pwooli se o pa‑o kolo to. O nam tiini o zege lanyerane de o wo-dedoa kam mo, ye o zeiŋi Wɛ yere. 21O maa seene o yei lanyerane we, Wɛ wó wane o ke kolo o na pwooli se o ke to. 22Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo ko popone we, “Wɛ ma pa o na chega o wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane.” 23Ko nam na popone we, “Wɛ ma pa o na chega” to, ko dae Abaraham yerane ŋwaane mo ko popone konto. 24Ko nam popone debam de ŋwaane mo. Kokuri, Wɛ wó pa debam de na chega o tei ne, dé na ye balo na ke dé wo-dedoa dé sɛ‑o to ŋwaane. Wonto nam mo ye wolo na bi dé Teiru Yezu toone wone to. 25Wɛ nam mo ke Yezu nabiina jeŋa ne pa se o te debam wɛleera ŋwaane. O ma daare o bi‑o toone wone pa se o jwoori o na ŋwea, se ko pa dé na chega o tei ne.

english_text:
What It Means To Be Acceptable to God
1By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God. 2Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God. 3But that's not all! We gladly suffer, because we know that suffering helps us to endure. 4And endurance builds character, which gives us a hope 5that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
6Christ died for us at a time when we were helpless and sinful. 7No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person. 8But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
9But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger. 10Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son. 11And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us.
Adam and Christ
12 Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die. 13Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law. 14Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did.
In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later. 15But the gift of God's undeserved grace was very different from Adam's sin. That one sin brought death to many others. Yet in an even greater way, Jesus Christ alone brought God's gift of undeserved grace to many people.
16There is a lot of difference between Adam's sin and God's gift. That one sin led to punishment. But God's gift made it possible for us to be acceptable to him, even though we have sinned many times. 17Death ruled like a king because Adam had sinned. But that cannot compare with what Jesus Christ has done. God has treated us with undeserved grace, and he has accepted us because of Jesus. And so we will live and rule like kings.
18 Everyone was going to be punished because Adam sinned. But because of the good thing that Christ has done, God accepts us and gives us the gift of life. 19Adam disobeyed God and caused many others to be sinners. But Jesus obeyed him and will make many people acceptable to God.
20The Law came, so that the full power of sin could be seen. Yet where sin was powerful, God's gift of undeserved grace was even more powerful. 21Sin ruled by means of death. But God's gift of grace now rules, and God has accepted us because of Jesus Christ our Lord. This means that we will have eternal life.
translation_text:
Debam de Wɛ na fɔge daane tei to
1Dé na ke dé wo-dedoa de Wɛ to mo pae dé jege chega o yiga ne. Konto ŋwaane, dé na me de dé Teiru Yezu Krista to mo pae debam de Wɛ fɔge daane. 2Yezu mo jaane debam o vo o zege Wɛ yiga ne, ye Wɛ ke debam zaane dé wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane. Konto to, dé jege teena we dé wó na paare Wɛ tei ne, ye ko pae debam wo pwoli lanyerane. 3Dé nam ta jege wopwolo dé yaara yam baŋa ne, kolo ŋwaane dé yei we yaara wae ya pae se dé fɔge dé zege mo de pu-dɛa. 4Dé pu-dɛa kam laam maa pae dé jege boboŋ-dɛɛra de Wɛ. Dé boboŋ-dɛɛra yam ta mo pae dé jege teena Wɛ tei ne. 5Dé na jege teena konto to bá pa dé na dé chaveera, kolo ŋwaane Wɛ tiini o ke o swono debam bochara ne, de o na pɛ o Sin-laao kom ta wo debam tei ne to.
6Debam ta na bwona ye dé ware dé jwoŋi de tete to, Yezu Krista tega maŋa kalo Wɛ boboŋa na kuri se o ma o jwoŋi wɛ-lwɛɛna ba wɛleera wone o yage to mo. 7Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá sɛ se o zaza o te o dwoŋi ŋwaane, de o dwoŋi wom na ye chega tu tei to de. Dɛ delo nɔɔno bá kɔre foone se o te o dwoŋi nɔn-ŋom ŋwaane. 8Ko nam ná ye Baŋa Wɛ, wonto bere debam o na tiini o jege debam swono tei to de o na pɛ se Yezu Krista ba o te debam ŋwaane ye dé daa ta tɔge wɛleera chwoŋa to. 9Yezu na tega ye o jana bam nwoŋi to mo pɛ dé na chega Wɛ yiga ne. Konto to, ko tiini ko ye chega we, o laam wó jwoŋi debam Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ kom wone. 10Debam ya ye Wɛ dona mo. O Bu wom toone dem nam mo pɛ se debam de Wɛ fɔge daane. Debam laam na ye Wɛ nɔɔna to, ko tiini ko ye chega we, Wɛ wó da o Bu wom ŋwea ŋwaane o jwoŋi debam ŋwea. 11Ko ta woli da, dé jege wopwolo lanyerane de Wɛ na zeini debam dé Teiru Yezu Krista ŋwaane to. Wonto mo pore chwoŋa se debam de Wɛ ba dé fɔge daane.
Adam de Yezu Krista memaŋe
12Nabiinu dedoa ŋwaane mo pɛ se wɛleera ba logo baŋa, ye wɛleera de ja toone ya woli da ya ba. Konto to, nabiina maama jege se ba te, ba maama na ke wɛleera to ŋwaane. 13Wɛ déem ta na wo ke o ni-kaana yam o nɔɔna jeŋa ne to, de wɛleera maŋe ya wora mo logo baŋa ne. Ni-kaana nam na tera to, Wɛ ba ke nɔɔna wɛleera o boboŋa ne. 14Maŋa kam konto ne, ko zege Adam maŋa kam ne se ko vo ko yi Moses maŋa kam, toone nam maŋe de wae nabiina pa se ba maama toa. Toone maa wae balo de na ke ba tusi, ye ko dae nenɛɛne Adam déem na ke tei ye o chɔge Wɛ ni dem to.
Adam nam bere debam Yezu ya na lage o ba se ko taa ye tei to. Ba nam dae bedwe. 15Adam déem na ke o tusi tei to dae bedwe de Wɛ na ke tei o zeini debam zɛɛra to. Nabiinu dedoa kam konto tusim dem mo pɛ se nɔɔna dedɛ tɔge ba te. Wɛ zaane dem nam dwoi konto ye o toŋe nabiinu dedoa Yezu Krista o pa nɔɔna zɛɛra se wonto ke zaane o ke ba yuu ne. 16Wɛ na kwei pɛɛre dem o pa nɔɔna zɛɛra konto to dae bedwe de nabiinu dedoa kam na ke o tusi tei to. Wonto na ke o tusi bedwe to mo pɛ se Wɛ bore nɔɔna o chɔge. Ko daare nɔɔna dedɛ na ke ba tusi to, Wɛ zeinim dem nam pɛ se ba wɛleera dedɛ saare ye ba na chega o tei ne. 17Nabiinu dedoa kam tusim dem mo pɛ se toone tɔge wonto ŋwaane de ba, ye de ta wae nɔɔna de dam. Ko nam tiini ko ye chega mo we, nabiinu dedoa Yezu Krista mo pɛ nɔɔna chwoŋa se ba taa jege Wɛ ŋwe-doŋa kam de dam. Balo maama Wɛ na yɔɔre o ke zaane ba yuu ne pa se ba jege chega o yiga ne to mo wó na o ŋwe-doŋa kam konto Yezu Krista ŋwaane.
18Dé nam lɔre we Adam na ke o tusi bedwe to mo pɛ se nabiina maama na chɔgem Wɛ tei ne. Yezu Krista keim-laao dedoa kam nam mo pɛ se nɔɔna maama na chega Wɛ tei ne, ye ba jege Wɛ ŋwe-doŋa kam. 19Nabiinu dedoa kam na ve Wɛ ni dem to mo pɛ se nɔɔna dedɛ tɔge o ŋwaane ba taa ye nɔn-chechɔgero. Nɔɔno dedoa kam nam na sɛ Wɛ ni to de wó pa se nɔɔna dedɛ taa jege chega Wɛ yiga ne.
20Wɛ déem ke o ni-kaana yam nɔɔna jeŋa ne se ko pa tusim mo fɔge de puli jaja. Wɛleera nam na puli konto to, Wɛ na ke nɔɔna zaane tei to mo tiini ko puli dedɛ. 21Konto to, wɛleera tɔge toone ŋwaane mo ya maa tei nɔɔna. Wɛ zaane dem nam tɔge o na pae nɔɔna chega tei to baŋa ne de maa zeini nɔɔna lanyerane se ba taa jege ŋwea kalo na ba jege kweelim Wɛ tei ne to dé Teiru Yezu Krista ŋwaane.

english_text:
Dead to Sin but Alive because of Christ
1What should we say? Should we keep on sinning, so that God's gift of undeserved grace will show up even better? 2No, we should not! If we are dead to sin, how can we go on sinning? 3Don't you know that all who share in Christ Jesus by being baptized also share in his death? 4 When we were baptized, we died and were buried with Christ. We were baptized, so we would live a new life, as Christ was raised to life by the glory of God the Father.
5If we shared in Jesus' death by being baptized, we will be raised to life with him. 6We know that the persons we used to be were nailed to the cross with Jesus. This was done, so our sinful bodies would no longer be the slaves of sin. 7We know sin doesn't have power over dead people.
8As surely as we died with Christ, we believe we will also live with him. 9We know that death no longer has any power over Christ. He died and was raised to life, never again to die. 10When Christ died, he died for sin once and for all. But now he is alive, and he lives only for God. 11In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to the power of sin. But Christ Jesus has given life to you, and you live for God.
12Don't let sin rule your body. After all, your body is bound to die, so don't obey its desires 13or let any part of it become a slave of evil. Give yourselves to God, as people who have been raised from death to life. Make every part of your body a slave that pleases God. 14Don't let sin keep ruling your lives. You are ruled by God's undeserved grace and not by the Law.
Slaves Who Do What Pleases God
15What does all this mean? Does it mean we are free to sin, because we are ruled by God's gift of undeserved grace and not by the Law? Certainly not! 16Don't you know that you are slaves of anyone you obey? You can be slaves of sin and die, or you can be obedient slaves of God and be acceptable to him. 17You used to be slaves of sin. But I thank God that with all your heart you followed the example set forth in the teaching you received. 18Now you are set free from sin and are slaves who please God.
19I am using these everyday examples, because in some ways you are still weak. You used to let the different parts of your body be slaves of your evil thoughts. But now you must make every part of your body serve God, so that you will belong completely to him.
20When you were slaves of sin, you didn't have to please God. 21But what good did you receive from the things you did? All you have to show for them is your shame, and they lead to death. 22Now you have been set free from sin, and you are God's slaves. This will make you holy and will lead you to eternal life. 23Sin pays off with death. But God's gift is eternal life given by Jesus Christ our Lord.
translation_text:
Wɛ ŋwe-doŋa kam taane
1Wɛ zaane dem na daga to, dé nam wó ta bɛ mo? Dé wó wane dé ta we, dé jege chwoŋa se dé taa ke wɛleera se ko wane ko pa Wɛ zaane dem tiini de puli dé tei ne mo na? 2Aawo, dé bá ta konto dwoŋi. Wɛleera seeni debam nye de twa mo. Konto to, dé ba jege chwoŋa se dé taa ke wɛleera dé ŋwea wone. 3Debam balo maama na jwoŋi sɛɛm se dé taa ye Yezu Krista nyem to, ko bere we dé tɔge dé sɛ o toone dem mo. Abam yeiri konto na? 4Konto ŋwaane, dé na jwoŋi sɛɛm to, ko nye de ba suli debam de Yezu daane mo, se ko bere we dé tɔge ded‑o de te. Konto ma pa dé tɔge de Yezu Krista dé na Wɛ ŋwe-doŋa kam, ne dé Kwo Wɛ na mɛ o paare dem dam o bi Yezu toone wone o pa o na ŋwea tei to.
5Debam na me de Yezu to mo pɛ dé tɔge ded‑o dé te wɛleera seeni. Konto ŋwaane, dé daa ta wó tɔge ded‑o dé bi toone wone. 6Dé yei we, ba na page Yezu dagara kam yuu ne ba go to, dé ŋwe-dwoŋa kam de tɔge da ka te mo, pa se wɛleera daa yé taa wae dé yera yam. Konto to, dé laam tei dé tete mo wɛleera jeŋa ne, 7kokuri to wɛleera daa bá wane ya taa tei wolo na maŋe o tɔge de Yezu o te to.
8Dé na tɔge de Yezu Krista dé te to, dé jege teena we dé wó tɔge dé na ŋwea o tei ne. 9Kokuri dé yei we Yezu Krista bi toone wone ye o daa bá jwoori o te. Konto ŋwaane, toone daa bá wane‑o de taa tei. 10Yezu na tege konto to, ko ye se o che wɛleera dam mo. O tege bedwe yerane mo o ma kweeli. O laam na jege ŋwea tei to mo o ŋwe o pa Wɛ. 11Ko ta ye konto mo abam de tei ne. Ko ná ye wɛleera seeni, se á maane we á nye de twa mo. Ko nam ná ye ŋwea kalo á na jege to, á ŋwe á pa Wɛ mo, á na me de Yezu Krista to ŋwaane.
12Konto ŋwaane abam daa yé pa se wɛleera di dam á yera yam na wó te to baŋa ne. Á nam yé sɛ á pa wo-zɔɔna yalo á fera na zoore to. 13Yé sɛ-na á kwei á yera yam á ke wɛleera dam jeŋa ne, se ko pa á ta‑á ke keim-balwaaro. Nam kwei-na á tete á ke Wɛ jeŋa ne, á na ye balo Wɛ na jwoŋi toone wone ye á jege ŋwea o tei ne to ŋwaane. Kwei-na á maama á pa Wɛ se o wane o ma o toŋe kolo na ye chega to. 14Wɛleera daa ba jege se ya taa tei abam, kokuri to, á na jege ŋwea Wɛ tei ne to dae o nia yam ŋwaane, ko nam ye o zaane dem ŋwaane mo.
Wɛ vere debam wɛleera jeŋa ne
15Ko nam bere debam we bɛ mo? Dé na jege ŋwea Wɛ tei ne o zaane dem ŋwaane ye ko dae o nia yam ŋwaane to bere we dé jege chwoŋa se dé taa ke wɛleera na? Aawo, dé bá sɛ konto. 16Á yei we, á ná kwei á tete á ke nɔɔno jeŋa ne se á ta‑á ye o kabɛ ye á sɛ o ni, á seene á ye á na sɛ á pa wolo to kabɛ mo. Konto to, á wae á ye wɛleera kabɛ se toone laam ba de ja abam, naa á wae á ye kabɛ selo na toŋe á tɔge Wɛ ni to se á daare á na chega o tei ne. 17Amo nam ke Wɛ lei de abam déem na ye kabɛ wɛleera jeŋa ne, ye á laam ke á tete Wɛ chega kam jeŋa ne se á ta‑á tɔge-ka de á bochara maama. 18Wɛ mo vere abam wɛleera jeŋa ne, ye á laam ba á ji kabɛ o chega kam tei ne.
19Abam nam na ba jege boboŋ-dɛɛra to mo pae se amo maŋe nabiina memaŋa a ma bere abam konto dwoŋi. Abam déem kwei á maama á sɛ wo-digiru de lwarem kikia se á ta‑á ye kabɛ ya tei ne, ye á toŋe wo-lwanno ko ja gaale. Abam laam nam jege se á kwei á maama mo á sɛ Wɛ chega kam, se á ta‑á ye ka kabɛ ye á bochara ba ya kwɛ fase. 20Abam déem na ye wɛleera kabɛ to, á tei á tete mo Wɛ chega kam jeŋa ne. 21Abam na ke wo-yɔɔro telo to déem jege bɛ nyɔɔre mo te pa abam? Chaveera laam jege abam te baŋa ne. Wonnu tento kweelim jei nam pae toone mo. 22Ko daare leile konto, Wɛ vere abam wɛleera jeŋa ne ye á laam ye o kabɛ mo. Konto ŋwaane, á jege nyɔɔre de á bochara na fɔge ya kwɛ tei to, ye ko kweelim jei mo wó pa á na ŋwea kalo na ba jege kweelim Wɛ tei ne to. 23Ŋweero telo dé na jwoŋi wɛleera baŋa ne to mo ye toone. Ko daare Wɛ pɛɛre delo o na pae debam zɛɛra to nam mo ye ŋwea kalo na ba jege kweelim o tei ne to, dé na me de dé Teiru Yezu Krista to ŋwaane.

english_text:
An Example from Marriage
1My friends, you surely understand enough about law to know that laws only have power over people who are alive. 2For example, the Law says that a man's wife must remain his wife as long as he lives. But once her husband is dead, she is free 3to marry someone else. However, if she goes off with another man while her husband is still alive, she is said to be unfaithful.
4That is how it is with you, my friends. You are now part of the body of Christ and are dead to the power of the Law. You are free to belong to Christ, who was raised to life so we could serve God. 5When we thought only of ourselves, the Law made us have sinful desires. It made every part of our bodies into slaves who are doomed to die. 6But the Law no longer rules over us. We are like dead people, and it cannot have any power over us. Now we can serve God in a new way by obeying his Spirit, and not in the old way by obeying the written Law.
The Battle with Sin
7 Does this mean that the Law is sinful? Certainly not! But if it had not been for the Law, I would not have known what sin is really like. For example, I would not have known what it means to want something that belongs to someone else, unless the Law had told me not to do this. 8It was sin that used this command as a way of making me have all kinds of desires. But without the Law, sin is dead.
9Before I knew about the Law, I was alive. But as soon as I heard that command, sin came to life, 10and I died. The very command that was supposed to bring life to me, instead brought death. 11 Sin used this command to trick me, and because of it I died. 12Still, the Law and its commands are holy and correct and good.
13Am I saying something good caused my death? Certainly not! It was sin that killed me by using something good. Now we can see how terrible and evil sin really is. 14We know that the Law is spiritual. But I am merely a human, and I have been sold as a slave to sin. 15 In fact, I don't understand why I act the way I do. I don't do what I know is right. I do the things I hate. 16Although I don't do what I know is right, I agree that the Law is good. 17So I am not the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
18I know that my selfish desires won't let me do anything that is good. Even when I want to do right, I cannot. 19Instead of doing what I know is right, I do wrong. 20And so, if I don't do what I know is right, I am no longer the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
21The Law has shown me that something in me keeps me from doing what I know is right. 22With my whole heart I agree with the Law of God. 23But in every part of me I discover something fighting against my mind, and it makes me a prisoner of sin that controls everything I do. 24What a miserable person I am. Who will rescue me from this body that is doomed to die? 25Thank God! Jesus Christ will rescue me.
So with my mind I serve the Law of God, although my selfish desires make me serve the law of sin.
translation_text:
Ban-zore memaŋe
1A nu-bia bam, á maama yei ni-kaana na ye tei to. Konto ŋwaane á yei we ni-kaana yam wó taa tei nɔɔno se ko taa vei o toone. O ná tega, ya daa ba tei‑o. 2A lage a bere abam ko na ye tei to. Kaane ná zo baro, Wɛ ni dem bere we o baro wom ta ná ŋwe, o ba jege chwoŋa se o yage o baro wom. O baro wom nam ná tega, o yiga le Wɛ ni dem konto ne. 3Konto ŋwaane, o baro wom ta ná ŋwe, ye o ná vei o zo baro wodwoŋi, Wɛ ni dem bere we o ke wɛleere mo. O baro wom nam ná tega, o yiga le ni dem konto ne. O laam ná zo baro wodwoŋi, ko ba bere we o chɔge Wɛ ni dem konto.
4A nu-bia bam, ko ye konto mo de abam de. Wɛ ni-kaana yam seeni ko nye de debam maama tege mo, dé yera yam na gwaane de Yezu Krista yera yam na tege to ŋwaane. Konto ma pa dé yiga le ni-kaana yam wone, ye dé jege chwoŋa se dé ke dé tete nɔɔno wodwoŋi jeŋa ne. Wonto ye wolo na bi toone wone to mo. Ko maa pae se dé jege nyɔɔre dé pa Wɛ. 5Dé déem na ke dé boboŋ-yɔɔro na lage kolo to, ko ye Wɛ ni-kaana yam mo pa se dé fera zoore keim-lwanno ye dé tɔge-te. Ko déem ma pa se dé jege nyɔɔre dé pa toone yerane. 6Ni-kaana yam déem peene debam de dam. Leile konto dé yiga laam le ya wone, dé na tɔge de Yezu dé te to ŋwaane. Konto to, dé na toŋe dé pwoli Wɛ wo tei to tɔge o Sin-laao kom na wo dé bochara ne to ŋwaane mo. Dé tɔge chwo-doŋa kam konto, ye ko dae chwo-dwoŋa kalo na zege ni-kaana yalo na popone tɔnɔ ne to ŋwaane.
Ni-kaana na ye tei to
7Bɛ mo dé nam wó ta Wɛ ni-kaana yam seeni? Ya tete jege tusim mo na? Aawo, ko dae konto. Wɛ ni-kaana yam nam mo pɛ se amo lɔre tusim na ye tei to. Wɛ ni-kaana yam ya ná wo bere-ne we, “Yé pa n yi taa sui n dwonna wonnu”, a ya bá taa yei we yi sum n dwonna wonnu ye wɛleere mo. 8Wɛ ni dem konto nam mo pɛ tusim na chwoŋa de zo a boboŋa pa a yi taa sui wonnu dedɛ. Ni-kaana nam ná tera, tusim bá taa jege dam. 9Amo tei ne, a déem ya yeiri Wɛ nia yam ye a ta jege ŋwea. Amo laam ma ba a lɔre Wɛ ni dem na bere kolo to. Tusim ma na dam se de ja-ne, 10ye a lɔre we a seene a ga a ŋwea Wɛ tei ne. Konto ŋwaane, Wɛ ni delo na jege se de pa nɔɔna ŋwea to laam ma pa se toone ja amo. 11Wɛ ni dem mo pɛ se tusim na chwoŋa se de gane amo. Tusim ma tɔge Wɛ ni dem baŋa ne mo de pa toone ja-ne. 12Wɛ ni-kaana yam tete nam ba jege tusim. Nia yalo maama Wɛ na pɛ debam to ba jege tusim. Ya nam lana dedɛ ye ya jege chega.
13Konto nam bere we Wɛ nia yalo na lana to mo jaane toone ya ba amo baŋa na? Aawo. Ko nam ye tusim mo tɔge Wɛ nia yalo na lana to baŋa ne de pa toone ja amo. Konto ke se nɔɔna wane ba lɔre tusim na seene de ye tei to mo. Wɛ nia yam ma pa se tusim tiini de yiriga.
14Dé yei we Wɛ ni-kaana yam tɔge o boboŋa na lage tei to mo. Amo nam ye logo baŋa nabiinu mo ye a ye kabaa wɛleera tei ne. 15Amo ta yeiri a kikia yam kuri. A ba yeini a ke kolo a na lage se a ke to, ye a daare a ke kolo a na chuli to. 16Amo ná yeini a ke kolo a na ba lage se a ke to, ko bere we a sɛ we Wɛ ni-kaana yam jege chega mo. 17Ko na ye konto to, ko dae we amo tete mo seene a ke wonnu tem konto, ko nam ye tusim delo na wo a bochare ne to mo ke-te. 18Amo nam yei we lam tera a tei ne, de a na ye nabiinu ye a fera zoore logo baŋa wonnu to. Kokuri, amo ná yeini a jege boboŋa se a ke lanyerane, a ta ware lanyerane a ke. 19Amo ba yeini a ke lanyerane ne a boboŋa na lage tei to. A maa yeini a ke wo-balwaaro telo a na ba lage se a ke to. 20Amo ná yeini a ke kolo a boboŋa na ba lage se a ke to, ko bere we ko dae a tete mo seene a ke wonnu tem konto, ko ye tusim delo na wo a bochare ne to mo ke-te.
21Amo lɔre ko na yeini ko ke amo tei to. Amo ná yeini a boŋe se a ke kolo na lana to, lwarem yerane mo tui. 22Amo bochare ne a tiini a jege wopwolo de Wɛ ni-kaana yam. 23Amo nam lɔre we a yera yam mo lage se ya taa tɔge chwoŋa kadwoŋi. Amo yera yam na ke tei to mo lage ko chɔge amo boboŋa yam na lage chwoŋa kalo to. Konto maa peene amo, ye a yera yam jege se ya taa tɔge tusim. 24Lɛɛro jege-ne. Amo yera yam lage se ya pa toone ja-ne. Wɔ mo wó wane o vere-ne ya jeŋa ne? 25Amo ke Wɛ lei dé Teiru Yezu Krista ŋwaane. Wonto mo wó jwoŋi-ne.
Ko na ye konto amo tei ne to, amo boboŋa yam mo pae se a sɛ Wɛ ni-kaana yam. A nam na ye logo baŋa nabiinu to mo pae se a tɔge tusim.

english_text:
Living by the Power of God's Spirit
1If you belong to Christ Jesus, you won't be punished. 2The Holy Spirit will give you life that comes from Christ Jesus and will set you free from sin and death. 3The Law of Moses cannot do this, because our selfish desires make the Law weak. But God set you free when he sent his own Son to be like us sinners and to be a sacrifice for our sin. God used Christ's body to condemn sin. 4He did this, so that we would do what the Law commands by obeying the Spirit instead of our own desires.
5People who are ruled by their desires think only of themselves. Everyone who is ruled by the Holy Spirit thinks about spiritual things. 6If our minds are ruled by our desires, we will die. But if our minds are ruled by the Spirit, we will have life and peace. 7Our desires fight against God, because they do not and cannot obey God's laws. 8If we follow our desires, we cannot please God.
9You are no longer ruled by your desires, but by God's Spirit, who lives in you. People who don't have the Spirit of Christ in them don't belong to him. 10But Christ lives in you. So you are alive because God has accepted you, even though your bodies must die because of your sins. 11 Yet God raised Jesus to life! God's Spirit now lives in you, and he will raise you to life by his Spirit.
12My dear friends, we must not live to satisfy our desires. 13If you do, you will die. But you will live, if by the help of God's Spirit you say “No” to your desires. 14Only those people who are led by God's Spirit are his children. 15 God's Spirit doesn't make us slaves who are afraid of him. Instead, we become his children and call him our Father. 16God's Spirit makes us sure that we are his children. 17His Spirit lets us know that together with Christ we will be given what God has promised. We will also share in the glory of Christ, because we have suffered with him.
A Wonderful Future for God's People
18 I am sure what we are suffering now cannot compare with the glory that will be shown to us. 19In fact, all creation is eagerly waiting for God to show who his children are. 20 Meanwhile, creation is confused, but not because it wants to be confused. God made it this way in the hope 21that creation would be set free from decay and would share in the glorious freedom of his children. 22We know that all creation is still groaning and is in pain, like a woman about to give birth.
23 The Spirit makes us sure about what we will be in the future. But now we groan silently, while we wait for God to show that we are his children. This means that our bodies will also be set free. 24And this hope is what saves us. But if we already have what we hope for, there is no need to keep on hoping. 25However, we hope for something we have not yet seen, and we patiently wait for it.
26In certain ways we are weak, but the Spirit is here to help us. For example, when we don't know what to pray for, the Spirit prays for us in ways that cannot be put into words. 27 All of our thoughts are known to God. He can understand what is in the mind of the Spirit, as the Spirit prays for God's people. 28We know that God is always at work for the good of everyone who loves him. They are the ones God has chosen for his purpose, 29and he has always known who his chosen ones would be. He had decided to let them become like his own Son, so his Son would be the first of many children. 30God then accepted the people he had already decided to choose, and he has shared his glory with them.
God's Love
31What can we say about all this? If God is on our side, can anyone be against us? 32God did not keep back his own Son, but he gave him for us. If God did this, won't he freely give us everything else? 33If God says his chosen ones are acceptable to him, can anyone bring charges against them? 34Or can anyone condemn them? No indeed! Christ died and was raised to life, and now he is at God's right side, speaking to him for us. 35Can anything separate us from the love of Christ? Can trouble, suffering, and hard times, or hunger and nakedness, or danger and death? 36 It is exactly as the Scriptures say,
“For you we face death
all day long.
We are like sheep
on their way
to be butchered.”
37In everything we have won more than a victory because of Christ who loves us. 38I am sure that nothing can separate us from God's love—not life or death, not angels or spirits, not the present or the future, 39and not powers above or powers below. Nothing in all creation can separate us from God's love for us in Christ Jesus our Lord!
translation_text:
Wɛ Sin-laao kom na pae dé ke kikia yalo to
1Konto to, balo na me de Yezu Krista to daa bá ga bora Wɛ tei ne. 2Wɛ Sin-laao kom mo pae dé jege ŋwea Wɛ tei ne Yezu Krista ŋwaane. Konto dam dem mo pɛ dé na verem tusim dedaane toone jeŋa ne. 3Debam na ye nabiina ye dé bwona to mo pae se dé ware Wɛ nia yam dé taa tɔga. Konto ŋwaane dé daa bá wane dé na chega Wɛ tei ne o nia yam tɔgem ŋwaane. Mo kokuri pa se Wɛ déem toŋe o tete Bu se o ba o ji nabiinu, ye o nye de nabiina balo tusim na wae-ba to. O ma ba o te nabiina wɛleera saarem ŋwaane, se o ma chɔge tusim na jege dam delo nabiina baŋa ne to. 4Wɛ ke konto se ko pa dé na chega o tei ne, nenɛɛne o nia yam na bere we dé jege se dé taa ye tei to maama. Kolo ŋwaane debam ye balo na tɔge Wɛ Sin-laao kom chwoŋa kam ye dé ba sɛ wo-yɔɔro telo nabiina fera na zoore to. 5Balo nam na tɔge wo-yɔɔro konto dwoŋi to tiini ba kwei ba boboŋa ba tiŋi wonnu telo nabiina boboŋa na lage to baŋa ne mo. Ko daare balo na tɔge Wɛ Sin-laao kom chwoŋa to mo kwei ba boboŋa ba tiŋi wo-laaro telo Sin-laao kom boboŋa na lage to baŋa ne. 6Nɔɔno boboŋa ná tɔge wo-yɔɔro telo nabiina fera na zoore to, toone wó ja konto tu Wɛ yiga ne. Wolo boboŋa nam na tɔge Wɛ Sin-laao kom chwoŋa to wó na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne de bochare-zuru. 7Kokuri, nɔɔno ná tɔge nabiina boboŋ-yɔɔro tem, kotu ye Wɛ dono mo, o na ba sɛ o tɔge Wɛ nia yam ye o ware-ya o ke to ŋwaane. 8Balo maama na tɔge wo-yɔɔro telo nabiina boboŋa na lage to nam bá wane ba pwoli Wɛ wo.
9Abam nam ba tɔge nabiina boboŋ-yɔɔro na lage kolo to. Ko ná ye chega we Wɛ Sin-laao kom wo á bochara ne, á wó ta‑á tɔge ko na bere abam chwoŋa kalo to mo. Yezu Krista Sin-laao kom nam na tere nɔɔno wolo tei ne to seene o dae Yezu nyem. 10Yezu Krista nam na wo abam tei ne to, á jworru tem mo jege ŋwea Wɛ yiga ne, á na jege chega o tei ne to ŋwaane. Á yera yam nam jege se ya te, tusim na tei-ya to ŋwaane. 11Wɛ mo bi Yezu toone wone. Konto ŋwaane, o Sin-laao kom ná wo á bochara ne, Wɛ wó pa se abam yera yalo na jege se ya te to jwoori ya na ŋwea, o Sin-laao kom na wo á bochara ne to ŋwaane.
12A nu-bia bam, ko bere we dé laam jege zele mo dé zeŋa. Ko nam dae se dé taa tɔge wo-yɔɔro telo nabiina boboŋa na lage to. 13Kolo ŋwaane, á ná tɔge nabiina boboŋa na lage kolo to, toone wó ja abam Wɛ yiga ne. Ko daare, á nam ná tɔge Sin-laao kom dam ŋwaane á che á tete de keim-lwanno telo á yera yam na lage to, á wó na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne. 14Balo maama na pae se Wɛ Sin-laao kom taa tei-ba to mo ye Wɛ bia. 15Jworo kolo Wɛ na ke á bochara ne to ba pae se foone jwoori de taa jege abam ne kabɛ mo tei. Wɛ Sin-laao kom nam pae se á ye Wɛ bia mo. Ko maa pae dé jege chwoŋa se dé bwoŋi Wɛ we, “Dé Kwo, Baba.” 16Wɛ Sin-laao kom nam gwaane dedaane debam dedoa dedoa jworo kom, ye ko pae dé yei we dé seene dé ye Wɛ bia. 17Dé na ye Wɛ bia to, dé wó ba dé taa tei wo-laaro telo maama o na tiŋi se o pa o bia bam to. Dé wó tɔge de o Bu Yezu Krista dé jwoŋi kolo maama Wɛ na tiŋi se o pa‑o to. Dé ná sɛ se dé tɔge dé na Yezu yaara yam dwoŋi, dé laam wó tɔge dé na o paare dem dwoŋi.
Dé jege teena we dé wó di paare Wɛ tei ne
18Amo boŋe we, dé na yeini dé na yaara yalo leile to bá wane ya taa mae de paare delo Wɛ na wó pa dé na o tei ne to. 19Wɛ na naane wonnu telo maama to tiini te jege teena se te na dɛ dem Wɛ na wó pa o bia bam lɔre jaja to. 20Wonnu telo Wɛ na naane to nam tu te ji wo-yɔɔro. Te na jigi wo-yɔɔro konto to, ko ye Wɛ boboŋa ŋwaane mo, ye ko dae wonnu tem tete na lage tei to. Wɛ mo pɛ te ji wo-yɔɔro ye o nam ta pa dé jege teena we, 21wonnu telo maama o na naane to wó ba te na verem, se te daa yé taa chɔga ne te zem na yeini te chɔge tei to. Wɛ wó fɔge o kwɛ-te se te laam ba te na nenɔŋa o tei ne, se ko maŋe de Wɛ bia bam tete na wó na paare delo to.
22Dé yei we wonnu maama tɔge daane te nae cham de zem maama. Te maa cheigi maŋa kalo Wɛ na wó fɔge-te to, ne kaane puga na virigi ye o kone tei to. 23Ko nam dae wonnu tem konto yerane, se ko ye debam balo Wɛ na ke o Sin-laao kom dé bochara ne to de mo. Konto maa ye Wɛ da-yiga pɛɛre delo na bere we, dé wó daare dé na o wo-laaro tem maama dé woli da. Debam de nam kone mo ye dé jege teena dé cheigi maŋa kam Wɛ na wó pa se dé ji o tete sɔŋɔ bia ye o vere debam o pa dé yera yam fɔge ya kwɛ. 24Wɛ na jwoŋi debam to, ko pae dé jege teena o tei ne. Dé nam ná maŋe dé na kolo dé ya na jege teena ko ŋwaane to, dé daa bá taa jege ko teena. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba teena kolo o na maŋe o na to. 25Dé nam ta wo nɛ Wɛ wo-laaro tem maama, ye dé jege teena se dé na-te. Konto ŋwaane, dé zuri dé yera dé cheigi se te maŋa kam laam yi.
26Wɛ Sin-laao kom de nam woli debam, dé na bwona to ŋwaane. Debam yeiri dé na wó lwoori Wɛ se ko maŋe tei to. O Sin-laao kom nam lwoori‑o o pa debam. Ko vuvuna mo dé tei ne ye botare-bia tera de wone. 27Wɛ nam yeini o buŋi dé bochara wone ye o lɔre dé boboŋa na ye tei to. O ta kwori o yei o Sin-laao kom boboŋa yam, kolo ŋwaane Sin-laao kom tɔge Wɛ boboŋa na lage tei to, ye o lwoori Wɛ o pa debam balo na ye o nɔɔna to.
28Ko ná ye balo na swoi Wɛ to, dé yei we Wɛ yeini o toŋe o woli-ba wonnu maama baŋa ne se lanyerane taa tui. Wɛ ke konto o pa balo o na maŋe o jege ba boboŋa ye o bwoŋi-ba se ba taa tɔge‑o to. 29Wɛ déem maŋe o jege banto boboŋa o bochare ne faŋa faŋa, ye o daare o kuri-ba se ba laam ba ba taa nye de o Bu wom na ye tei to. Konto maa wó pa Wɛ Bu Yezu na nyaana dedɛ, balo de na ye Wɛ bia ye ba saŋe o kwaga to. 30Wɛ nam na maŋe o kuri balo to mo o bwoŋi se ba taa ye o nyem. O na bwoŋi balo konto to, o ma pa ba na chega o yiga ne. Balo o na pɛ ba jege chega konto to mo o pɛ ba na paare o tei ne.
Wɛ zeini debam balo na ye o bia to
31Ko na ye konto to, dé nam wó ta bɛ mo? Wɛ ná zege debam kwaga ne, nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o chɔge debam. 32Wɛ wo cheiŋi o tete Bu wom de yaara, ye o nam sɛ o ke‑o nabiina jeŋa ne se o te debam maama ŋwaane. Wɛ na zeini debam konto to, o ta wó kwei wo-laaro maama o pa debam zɛɛra o woli de o Bu wom. 33Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o ŋɔɔne taane o chɔge debam balo Wɛ na kuri to. Ko ye Wɛ tete mo pae dé jege chega. 34Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o pa se dé ga bora Wɛ tei ne. Ko ye Yezu Krista tete mo tega debam ŋwaane, ye o ta jwoori o bi toone wone pa se o na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne. O laam maa jege paare Wɛ jazem seeni ye o lwoori Wɛ o pa debam. 35Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o chɔge debam de Yezu Krista swono kom daane. Yaara wó wane ya chɔge debam konto na? Naa cham mo, naa nabiina bɛɛsem, naa kana, naa yiniga, naa keim-chɛɛre, naa tigura mo? Aawo, ya bá wane. 36Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
“Debam na ye Wɛ nɔɔna to mo pae
dé da toone tei dé kɛ dɛ maama wone.
Ba kwei debam ba ma ji pei selo ba na lage ba go to mo.”
37Wɛ nam na maŋe o jege debam swono to, wo-chɛɛro tento kolokolo bá wane debam te chɔge, ye dé wae dé di dam te maama baŋa ne. 38Amo yei lanyerane we kolokolo tera ko na wó wane ko chɔge debam de Wɛ swono kom daane. Ko ná ye toone naa ŋwea mo, naa ko ná ye malese naa wɛ-baŋa dedɛɛra maama mo, naa ko ná ye zem wonnu naa jwa wonnu mo, naa ko ná ye wonnu telo maama na jege dam to, 39naa ko ná ye wɛyuu wonnu dam naa tega kuri wonnu dam mo, naa ko ná ye wonnu telo maama Wɛ na ke to, tento maama kolokolo bá wane ko chɔge debam de Wɛ swono kom daane, ko na ye swono kolo o na tɔge dé Teiru Yezu Krista baŋa ne o jege de debam to ŋwaane.

english_text:
God's Choice of Israel
1I am a follower of Christ, and the Holy Spirit is a witness to my conscience. So I tell the truth and I am not lying when I say 2my heart is broken and I am in great sorrow. 3I would gladly be placed under God's curse and be separated from Christ for the good of my own people. 4 They are the descendants of Israel, and they are also God's chosen people. God showed them his glory. He made agreements with them and gave them his Law. The temple is theirs and so are the promises that God made to them. 5They have those famous ancestors, who were also the ancestors of the Christ. I pray that God, who rules over all, will be praised forever! Amen.
6It cannot be said that God broke his promise. After all, not all of the people of Israel are the true people of God. 7-8 In fact, when God made the promise to Abraham, he meant only Abraham's descendants by his son Isaac. God was talking only about Isaac when he promised 9 Sarah, “At this time next year I will return, and you will already have a son.”
10Don't forget what happened to the twin sons of Isaac and Rebekah. 11-12 Even before they were born or had done anything good or bad, the Lord told Rebekah that her older son would serve the younger one. The Lord said this to show he makes his own choices and it wasn't because of anything either of them had done. 13 That's why the Scriptures say that the Lord liked Jacob more than Esau.
14Are we saying God is unfair? Certainly not! 15 The Lord told Moses that he has pity and mercy on anyone he wants to. 16Everything then depends on God's mercy and not on what people want or do. 17 In the Scriptures the Lord says to the king of Egypt, “I let you become king, so that I could show you my power and be praised by all people on earth.” 18Everything depends on what God decides to do, and he can either have pity on people or make them stubborn.
God's Anger and Mercy
19Someone may ask, “How can God blame us, if he makes us behave in the way he wants us to?” 20 But, my friend, I ask, “Who do you think you are to question God? Does the clay have the right to ask the potter why he shaped it the way he did? 21 Doesn't a potter have the right to make a fancy bowl and a plain bowl out of the same lump of clay?”
22 God wanted to show his anger and reveal his power against everyone who deserved to be destroyed. But instead, he patiently put up with them. 23He did this by showing how glorious he is when he has pity on the people he has chosen to share in his glory. 24Whether Jews or Gentiles, we are those chosen ones, 25 just as the Lord says in the book of Hosea,
“Although they are not
my people,
I will make them my people.
I will treat with love
those nations
that have never been loved.
26 “Once they were told,
‘You are not my people.’
But in that very place
they will be called
children of the living God.”
27 And this is what the prophet Isaiah said about the people of Israel,
“The people of Israel
are as many
as the grains of sand
along the beach.
But only a few who are left
will be saved.
28The Lord will be quick
and sure to do on earth
what he has warned
he will do.”
29 Isaiah also said,
“If the Lord All-Powerful
had not spared some
of our descendants,
we would have been destroyed
like the cities of Sodom
and Gomorrah.”
Israel and the Good News
30What does all of this mean? It means that the Gentiles were not trying to be acceptable to God, but they found that he would accept them if they had faith. 31-32It also means that the people of Israel were not acceptable to God. And why not? It was because they were trying to be acceptable by obeying the Law instead of by having faith in God. The people of Israel fell over the stone that makes people stumble, 33 just as God says in the Scriptures,
“Look! I am placing in Zion
a stone to make people
stumble and fall.
But those who have faith
in that one will never
be disappointed.”
translation_text:
Wɛ na kuri nɔɔna balo se ba taa ye o nyem to
1Amo na ye Yezu Krista nyem to, a ŋɔɔne chega mo ye ko dae vwa. Wɛ Sin-laao kom na wo a bochare ne to mo pae a yɔɔre a yei we, 2a wo mo tiini ko chɔge amo tete dwi tiina bam ŋwaane de ba na wo sɛ Yezu Krista to. Lwia maa tiini ya jege-ne ba ŋwaane. 3Amo ya wó taa lage se a le a tete Wɛ yiga ne a yage se ko pa amo pwɛ Yezu Krista tei ne, nenɛɛne ko ya ná wó wane ko woli amo nu-bia bam. Banto ye amo tete dwi tiina. 4Ba ye Isarele dwi tiina mo. Ko ye banto mo Wɛ déem pɛ ba ji o bia, ye o bere-ba o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom. O ma gwoni ni o pa-ba, ye o daare o ke o nia yam ba jeŋa ne. O ma bere-ba ba na jege se ba taa zuli‑o tei to. O ma pwooli se o taa nii ba baŋa ne. 5Ba kuri nwoŋi debam nabaaro Isarele bia fuga-balei bam wone mo. Ba na loge Yezu Krista logo baŋa ne to, ko ye banto dwi tiina wone mo o nwoŋi. Wonto mo ye wonnu maama Tu Wɛ wom na maŋe se o taa jwoŋi teem taa wuu to. Ameena.
6Isarele dwi tiina bam na ve Wɛ to nam ba bere we Wɛ na gwoni o ni se o ke kolo to jigi kafɛ. Kokuri to, ko dae we Isarele dwi tiina bam maama mo seene ba ye Isarele tiina chekke Wɛ yiga ne. 7Abaraham dwi tiina bam maama nam dae o bia chekke Wɛ yiga ne. Wɛ déem tage de Abaraham o we, “Amo tei ne, n bu Izaak dwi dem yerane mo wó taa ye n dwi tiina chekke.” 8Ko bere we, ko dae bia balo maama ba na loge to mo ye Wɛ bia chekke. Ko nam ye bia balo Wɛ na pwooli kampwola kam ba ŋwaane ye ba laam lo-ba to mo seene ba ye Abaraham dwi tiina chekke. 9Kolo ŋwaane Wɛ déem pwooli we, “Maŋa kam ná yia, amo wó jwoori a ba, dedaane Sara laam jege bakeira o jeŋa ne.”
10Kolo na woli da to mo ye Izaak kaane Rabɛka déem loge bia balei ye ba ye kwo dedoa. Wonto maa ye debam nabaaro Izaak. 11-12Maŋa kam Rabɛka ta na wo loge o bia balei bam, ye ba daa ta wo maŋe se ba ke keim-laaro naa keim-balwaaro to, Wɛ déem tage ded‑o o we, “Zembaaro wom mo wó taa toŋe o pa o nyaane wom.” Ko ke konto se Wɛ na kuri-ba daane tei to mo tɔge o boboŋa na maŋe ya ja tei to. Ko bere we Wɛ kurim dem tɔge o na bwoŋi wolo wom se o taa ye o nyem to mo, ye ko dae nɔɔno wom kikia ŋwaane. 13Wɛ na tage kolo to popone o tɔnɔ kom ne we, “Amo jege Jakob swono, ye a chuli Esawu ni taane.”
14Dé nam wó ta bɛ mo? Dé bá wane dé ta we Wɛ ba jege chega de o na pɔɔre nɔɔna daane tei to. Kɔtaa! 15Ko nam na ye tei to, Wɛ déem tage de Moses o we:
“Amo wó duri wolo maama a na kuri to yibwona,
ye a ke zaane kotu yuu ne.”
16Ko bere we ko maama tɔge Wɛ na jege nɔɔna ŋwaŋa tei to mo, ye ko dae nabiina boboŋa na lage kolo to, naa ba kikia na ye tei to. 17Wɛ déem na tage kolo de Ejipti Pa-faro wom to popone o tɔnɔ kom ne we, “Woŋo kolo ŋwaane amo na pɛ chwoŋa se n yere zaŋe to mo ye se a wane a tɔge nmo ŋwaane a bere nɔɔna amo dam dem na mae tei to, ye a daare a jwoŋi yere logo baŋa jei maama ne.” 18Ko bere we Wɛ duri balo ŋwaŋa nenɛɛne o na boŋe tei to mo, ye o daare o pa badwonna taa jege yi-dɛɛre nenɛɛne o na boŋe tei to.
19Abam dedoa wae o bwei amo we, “Bɛŋwaane mo Wɛ nam yaale nɔɔna de ba kikia? Dé bá wane dé ve keim delo Wɛ na jaane boboŋa se dé ke to.” 20Nmo nam na ye nabiinu to, n ye wɔ mo se n jwoori n bwei Wɛ? Ko ná ye kamɔgɔ, ko bá wane ko bwei ko mɔro wom we, “Bɛ mo ye n ke-ne tento dwoŋi?” 21Kamɔ-mɔro wom nam jege chwoŋa se o kwei dɔgɔ o chɛ o ma mɔ kamwaro telei, ne o boboŋa na jaane se o ke tei to. O wae o mɔɔne dedoa se ka taa ye lonne nyem, ye o daare o mɔ kadwoŋi se ka taa ye woŋo maama nyem.
22Ko ta ye konto mo de Wɛ. O ná lage se o bere nɔɔna o ban-zɔŋɔ kom de o dam dem na mae tei to, o jege chwoŋa se o peene o bane mo de balo na chuchugi o bane ye ba maŋe de chɔgem to. 23O jege chwoŋa se o peene o bane konto dwoŋi se ko wane ko woli balo na daare ye o jege ba ŋwaŋa to, se ba lɔre o paare dem na tiini de jege nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ tei to. Banto maa ye balo o na maŋe o tiŋi se ba zo o paare dem wo to. 24Debam mo konto. Dé maa ye balo o na kuri nabiina dwi maama wone, ye ko dae Juu tiina dwi dem yerane wone to.
25Wɛ maŋe o tɔge Hosea baŋa ne o we:
“Nɔɔna balo ya na dae amo nyem to mo
a laam wó bwoŋi-ba we, amo nɔɔna bam.
Dwi tiina balo amo ya na ba jege ba swono to mo
a laam wó bwoŋi-ba we, amo nɔn-swonnu tem.
26Jeiga kalo Wɛ ya na tage de-ba we,
ba dae o nɔɔna to,
jeiga kam konto ne nɔɔ mo ba laam wó bwoŋi-ba we,
Ŋwea Tu Wɛ wom bia bam.”
27Izaya de déem ŋɔɔne Isarele tiina bam taane o we:
“Isarele tiina bam ná maŋe ba daga,
ne naneo ni kasolo bia na ye tei,
ba fenfee yerane mo wó na verem.
28Kolo ŋwaane Baŋa Wɛ wó ke lela mo
o pa se nabiina maama lɔre o boboŋa na jaane
se o waare-ba tei to ye taane daa tera.”
29Ko ta ye nenɛɛne Izaya na maŋe o ta tei o we:
“Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ya ná wo daare debam badaara
o yage dé dwi dem ne,
dé dwi dem ya ti mo,
ne ko déem na ke Sodom teo tiina tei to.
Dé ya wó ji ne Gomora teo déem na ye tei to.”
30Dé nam wó ta bɛ mo? Dé lɔre we dwi-gɛ tiina balo ya na ba kwaane ba nii se ba na chega Wɛ tei ne to laam seene ba jege chega Wɛ tei ne. Ko ye ba na ke ba wo-dedoa de Wɛ to ŋwaane mo ba nɛ chega kam konto. 31Ko daare Isarele dwi tiina bam mo tiini ba kwaane se ba na chega Wɛ tei ne de ba na tɔge o nia yam tei to ye ba ga. 32Bɛ mo ye ba nam ga? Kolo ŋwaane banto boŋe se ba na chega mo ba keim-laaro ŋwaane ye ko dae ba na jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ tei to. Ba na ve Wɛ konto to nye de ba mage ba naga de kandwɛ delo na pae nɔɔna chɔɔle ba toe to ye ba seene ba to tega ne. 33Ko maŋe ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
“Nii-na! Amo lage a chwi kandwɛ mo Zion ne.
De maa ye pelɔrɔ kolo na cheili
pa nɔɔna gare-ko ba to tega ne to mo.
Ko daare nɔɔno ná ke o wo-dedoa
de wolo na ye kandwɛ dem to,
chaveera bá fɔge ya ja kotu.”

english_text:
1Dear friends, my greatest wish and my prayer to God is for the people of Israel to be saved. 2I know they love God, but they don't understand 3what makes people acceptable to him. So they refuse to trust God, and they try to be acceptable by obeying the Law. 4But Christ makes the Law no longer necessary for those who become acceptable to God by faith.
Anyone Can Be Saved
5 Moses said a person could become acceptable to God by obeying the Law. He did this when he wrote, “If you want to live, you must do all the Law commands.”
6 But people whose faith makes them acceptable to God will never ask, “Who will go up to heaven to bring Christ down?” 7Neither will they ask, “Who will go down into the world of the dead to raise him to life?”
8All who are acceptable because of their faith simply say, “The message is as near as your mouth or your heart.” And this is the same message we preach about faith. 9So you will be saved, if you honestly say, “Jesus is Lord,” and if you believe with all your heart that God raised him from death. 10God will accept you and save you, if you truly believe this and tell it to others.
11 The Scriptures say no one who has faith will be disappointed, 12no matter if that person is a Jew or a Gentile. There is only one Lord, and he is generous to everyone who asks for his help. 13 All who call out to the Lord will be saved.
14How can people have faith in the Lord and ask him to save them, if they have never heard about him? And how can they hear, unless someone tells them? 15 And how can anyone tell them without being sent by the Lord? The Scriptures say it is a beautiful sight to see even the feet of someone coming to preach the good news. 16 Yet not everyone has believed the message. For example, the prophet Isaiah asked, “Lord, has anyone believed what we said?”
17No one can have faith without hearing the message about Christ. 18 But am I saying that the people of Israel did not hear? No, I am not! The Scriptures say,
“The message was told
everywhere on earth.
It was announced
all over the world.”
19 Did the people of Israel understand or not? Moses answered this question when he told that the Lord had said,
“I will make Israel jealous
of people
who are a nation
of nobodies.
I will make them angry
with people
who don't understand
a thing.”
20 Isaiah was fearless enough to tell that the Lord had said,
“I was found by people
who were not looking
for me.
I appeared to the ones
who were not asking
about me.”
21 And Isaiah said about the people of Israel,
“All day long the Lord
has reached out
to people who are stubborn
and refuse to obey.”
translation_text:
Isarele dwi tiina boboŋa muri Wɛ tei ne
1A nu-bia bam, amo tiini a jege teena a bochare ne we Isarele dwi tiina wó na verem, ye a yeini a lwoori Wɛ a pa-ba ko ŋwaane. 2Amo nam wó zege ba kwaga ne we, ba tiini ba lage se ba tɔge Wɛ boboŋa ye ba yeiri chwoŋa kalo ba na jege se ba tɔge to. 3Ba maa yeiri chwoŋa kalo Wɛ na tɔge o maa pae se nabiina na chega o tei ne to. Ba maa boŋe se ba tiŋi ba tete chwoŋa se ba maa na chega Wɛ tei ne, ye ba ba sɛ se ba taa tɔge chwoŋa kalo Wɛ na tiŋi to. 4Yezu Krista mo pɛ se Wɛ nia yam tɔgem chwoŋa kam laam ba ka kweeli, pa se balo maama na ke ba wo-dedoa de Wɛ to laam na chega o tei ne.
5Moses déem popone ko na ye tei ye nɔɔna wae ba na chega Wɛ tei ne o nia yam tɔgem ŋwaane. Moses popone we, “Wolo kikia na tɔge Wɛ nia yam to wó na ŋwea ya baŋa ne.” 6Ko nam ná ye nɔɔna na ke tei ba jege chega Wɛ tei ne ba wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane to, ko bá taa dana. Ko popone we, “Yé bwei n tete ne nenɛɛne, wɔ mo wó wane o di telaao?” Dé ba jege se dé vo dáane dé pa Yezu Krista tu o ba se o zeini debam. 7“Daa‑n yé bwei nenɛɛne, wɔ mo wó wane o zo tega kuri ne?” Dé ba jege se dé vo dáane dé pa Yezu bi toone wone o ba. 8Ko nam popone we, “Ko ba dana se n wane n lɔre Wɛ kwora kam. Ka maŋe ka wo nmo tei ne, de nmo ni ne, de nmo bochare ne.” Kwora kam konto zege wo-dedoa yera ne mo, ye kanto mo dé jege dé bere nɔɔna. 9Ka maa we, nmo ná tɛ jaja we Yezu mo ye Teiru wom, ye nmo ná sɛ de n bochare maama we Wɛ seene o bi‑o toone wone, Wɛ wó jwoŋi nmo ŋwea. 10Kolo ŋwaane ko ye nmo bochare ne mo nmo wó sɛ de n wo-dedoa ye n na chega Wɛ tei ne. Ko daare ko ye nmo ni ne mo nmo wó ta jaja we, n sɛ Yezu pa n na verem. 11Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we, “Wolo maama ná ke o wo-dedoa de Wɛ Dam Tu wom, chaveera bá ja kotu.” 12Ko ye bedwe mo nɔɔna maama tei ne, Juu tiina bam de dwi-gɛ tiina bam de. Ba maama Teiru ye dedoa mo, ye o yeini o swɛ balo maama na lwoori zeinim o tei ne to swolim. 13Kolo ŋwaane, “Wolo maama ná bwoŋi dé Teiru wom yere o ma lwoori zeinim, kotu wó na verem.”
14Ko nam na ye konto to, nɔɔna ná wo ke ba wo-dedoa de Yezu Krista, ba wó ke tɛ mo ba lwoori zeinim o tei ne? Ba ta wó wane ba ke ba wo-dedoa ded‑o ye ba wo nigi o kwora na? Ba nam wó wane ba ni o kwora ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo tɔɔle-ka o bere-ba na? 15Nɔɔno nam wó ke tɛ mo o vo o tɔɔle Wɛ kwora kam o bere-ba ye Wɛ wo toŋe‑o? Ko nam popone we, “Balo na jege kwor-ywoŋa ba beeri ba bwooli to veiŋa jege ywoni mo.”
16Ko nam dae we nɔɔna maama mo sɛ Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam. Izaya déem tage o we, “Dé Teiru Wɛ, debam na tɔɔle kwora kalo to, wɔ mo sɛ we ka ye chega?” 17Ko maama bere we nɔɔna zwa na ni kolo to mo pa-ba chwoŋa se ba ke ba wo-dedoa de Wɛ. Kwora kalo ba na jege se ba ni to mo ye Yezu Krista yera taane.
18Amo lage a bwei a nii, Isarele tiina bam wo nigi Wɛ ni taane dem mo na? Ba seene ba ni-de. Ko ye chega mo Wɛ tontoŋena bam seeni we:
“Ba kwora kam yi logo baŋa jei maama mo.
Ba ni taane jage de yi dɔŋɔ ni maama.”
19Amo ta lage a bwei a nii, Isarele tiina bam wo lɔre taane dem kuri na? Ba nam lɔre. Da-yiga to, Wɛ déem tɔge Moses ŋwaane o ta de-ba o we,
“Amo wó tɔge dwi-gɛ tiina balo na ye nɔn-yɔɔro to baŋa ne
a ma pa se abam taa jege kazwe á zwe de-ba,
ye á bane zaŋe ba ŋwaane.”
20Ko woli da, Izaya de déem jege baare ye o ta Wɛ taane o we:
“Ko ná ye balo na wo beeri a jei se ba lɔre-ne to,
banto mo tu ba lɔre amo.
A ta ma le a tete
a bere balo na wo bwei amo bwia to.”
21Ko nam ná ye Isarele tiina bam, Wɛ maa we,
“Dɛ wone maama amo tei a jeŋa se a zaane a nɔɔna bam,
de ba na maŋe ba ye zwabani-nyena tei to de.”

english_text:
God Has Not Rejected His People
1 Am I saying that God has turned his back on his people? Certainly not! I am one of the people of Israel, and I myself am a descendant of Abraham from the tribe of Benjamin. 2God did not turn his back on his chosen people. Don't you remember reading in the Scriptures how Elijah complained to God about the people of Israel? 3 He said, “Lord, they killed your prophets and destroyed your altars. I am the only one left, and now they want to kill me.”
4 But the Lord told Elijah, “I still have 7,000 followers who have not worshiped Baal.” 5It is the same way now. God treated the people of Israel with undeserved grace, and so a few of them are still his followers. 6This happened because of God's undeserved kindness and not because of anything they have done. It could not have happened except for God's gift of undeserved grace.
7This means that only a chosen few of the people of Israel found what all of them were searching for. And the rest of them were stubborn, 8 just as the Scriptures say,
“God made them so stupid
that their eyes are blind,
and their ears
are still deaf.”
9 Then David said,
“Turn their meals
into bait for a trap,
so that they will stumble
and be given
what they deserve.
10Blindfold their eyes!
Don't let them see.
Bend their backs
beneath a burden
that will never be lifted.”
Gentiles Will Be Saved
11Do I mean that the people of Israel fell, never to get up again? Certainly not! Their failure made it possible for the Gentiles to be saved, and this will make the people of Israel jealous. 12But if the rest of the world's people were helped so much by their sin and loss, they will be helped even more by their full return.
13I am now speaking to you Gentiles, and as long as I am an apostle to you, I will take pride in my work. 14I hope in this way to make some of my own people jealous enough to be saved. 15When Israel rejected God, the rest of the people in the world were able to turn to him. So when God makes friends with Israel, it will be like bringing the dead back to life. 16If part of a batch of dough is made holy by being offered to God, then all of the dough is holy. If the roots of a tree are holy, the rest of the tree is holy too.
17You Gentiles are like branches of a wild olive tree made to be part of a cultivated olive tree. You have taken the place of some branches that were cut away from it. And because of this, you enjoy the blessings that come from being part of that cultivated tree. 18But don't think you are better than the branches that were cut away. Just remember you are not supporting the roots of this tree. Its roots are supporting you.
19Maybe you think those branches were cut away, so you could be put in their place. 20That's true enough. But they were cut away because they did not have faith, and you are where you are because you do have faith. So don't be proud, but be afraid. 21If God cut away those natural branches, couldn't he do the same to you?
22Now you see both how kind and how hard God can be. He was hard on those who fell, but he was kind to you. And he will keep on being kind to you, if you keep on trusting in his kindness. Otherwise, you will be cut away too.
23If those other branches will start having faith, they will be made a part of that tree again. God has the power to put them back. 24After all, it wasn't natural for branches to be cut from a wild olive tree and to be made part of a cultivated olive tree. So it is much more likely that God will join the natural branches back to the cultivated olive tree.
The People of Israel Will Be Brought Back
25My friends, I don't want you Gentiles to be too proud of yourselves. So I will explain the mystery of what has happened to the people of Israel. Some of them have become stubborn, and they will stay like that until the complete number of you Gentiles has come in. 26 In this way all of Israel will be saved, as the Scriptures say,
“From Zion someone will come
to rescue us.
Then Jacob's descendants
will stop being evil.
27 This is what the Lord
has promised to do
when he forgives their sins.”
28The people of Israel are treated as God's enemies, so the good news can come to you Gentiles. But they are still the chosen ones, and God loves them because of their famous ancestors. 29God doesn't take back the gifts he has given or disown the people he has chosen.
30At one time you Gentiles rejected God. But now Israel has rejected God, and you have been shown mercy. 31And because of the mercy shown to you, they will also be shown mercy. 32All people have disobeyed God, and that's why he treats them as prisoners. But he does this, so that he can have mercy on all of them.
33 Who can measure the wealth and wisdom and knowledge of God? Who can understand his decisions or explain what he does?
34 “Has anyone known
the thoughts of the Lord
or given him advice?
35 Has anyone loaned
something to the Lord
that must be repaid?”
36 Everything comes from the Lord. All things were made because of him and will return to him. Praise the Lord forever! Amen.
translation_text:
Wɛ na kuri nɔɔna balo to
1Amo ta lage a bwei a nii, ko bere we Wɛ ve o tete nɔɔna bam maama o yage mo na? Kɔtaa! Nii-na, amo tete mo ye Isarele dwi tu. Abaraham mo ye a nabaaro, ye a nwoŋi Benjamin dwi dem wone. 2Wɛ seene o wo ve o nɔɔna balo o na maŋe o jege ba boboŋa boboa ne to. Abam maŋe á yei Wɛ tɔnɔ kom na bere Elija taane tei to. O déem lwoori Wɛ se o waare Isarele tiina bam, 3ye o we, “Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, ba go nmo sampwori sem, ye ba daare ba chochoge nmo kaanem bimbina yam. Ko laam ta daare amo yerane mo ye ba kwaane se ba go-ne.”
4Wɛ nam leiri‑o o we bɛ mo? O we, “Amo nam le nɔɔna morro terepɛ (7,000) mo se ba taa ye amo tete nyem. Banto wo fɔge ba kuni dwoona ba zuli Baal jwoni dem.” 5Ko ta ye bedwe mo de zem maama. Kɔgɔ fenfee ta mo daare, Wɛ na tɔge o zaane dem ŋwaane o kuri balo to. 6Wɛ nam na dɛ o zaane dem baŋa ne o kuri-ba to, ko bere we ko dae ba kikia ŋwaane. Ko ya ná ye ba kikia ŋwaane mo o kuri-ba, ko bá taa ye o zaane dem mo o pɛ-ba zɛɛra.
7Ko bere we Isarele tiina bam wo nɛ chega kalo ba na seene ba yia se ba na Wɛ tei ne to. Kɔgɔ kolo Wɛ na kuri to nam mo nɛ-ka. Balo na daare to nam maa jege yi-dɛɛre. 8Ko ke-ba ne ko na popone tei Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
“Wɛ mo pɛ se ba tiini ba dɔ ba kɛ.
De zem maama, ba yia ta ba nae,
ye ba zwa de kwareme Wɛ chega kam seeni.”
9David de déem tage ba taane o we,
“Wɛ wó pa se ba kuri wodi-fɔrɔ kom
jwoori ko ja chɔgem ko ba ba baŋa ne,
ne kalanchogo na jaane-ba
ye ba to tega ne tei to,
10Wɛ wó pa se ba yia dwei ye ba daa ware ba nae.
Wɛ wó pa se ba yera chɛ de yaara taa wuu.”
11Amo ta lage a bwei a nii, Isarele tiina bam na chɔɔle ba to konto to, ko bere we ba daa bá na chwoŋa se ba jwoori ba zaŋe mo na? Kɔtaa! Banto na chɔge Wɛ chega kam tei to mo pɛ se dwi-gɛ tiina na chwoŋa se Wɛ jwoŋi-ba. Wɛ ke konto se ko pa Isarele tiina bam taa jege kazwe ba ŋwaane. 12Banto na ke ba chɔge tei to mo pɛ se nabiina maama wane ba na Wɛ zeinim lanyerane. Ba na muri Wɛ tei ne to mo pɛ se dwi-gɛ tiina na chwoŋa se ba jwoŋi Wɛ zeinim dem. Ko bere we Isarele dwi tiina kɔgɔ kolo na tɔge Wɛ to ná puli ko ti, ko wó pa se nɔɔna tiini ba na Wɛ zeinim ko ja gaale.
13Ko ye abam dwi-gɛ tiina bam mo a tɛ taane dento. Amo na ye Yezu totoŋa nakwe se a ta o taane a bere dwi-gɛ tiina bam to tiini ko ye totoŋ-kamunu amo tei ne. 14Amo kwaane a toŋe se ko wane ko pa amo dwonna Isarele tiina bam taa jege puseŋa, se a laam jwoŋi ba badwonna a ke Wɛ jeŋa ne. 15Wɛ na ve banto o yage to, ko pɛ se logo baŋa dwi tiina laam ba ba fɔge de Wɛ. Ko daare maŋa kalo Wɛ na wó jwoŋi-ba to, ko wó taa nye de twa na jwoori ba na ŋwea tei to mo.
16Dé yei we, nmo ná dɛ yiga n fɔ bworobworo n tiŋi n pa Wɛ, ko chichworo kom na daare to daa ta ye o nyem. Ko woli da, tio kuu ná ye Wɛ nyem, ko nɛ sem maama de ye o nyem mo. 17Isarele tiina bam nye de Olivi tio ba na jeiri gaare wone to. Ko ye nenɛɛne Wɛ bwori tio kom konto nɛ sedaara o yage, ye o daare o kwei Olivi tio kolo na wo gaao wone to naga kadwoŋi o twoŋi o gwaane nɛ sedwonna sem wone. Nmo wolo na ye dwi-gɛ tu to nye de naga kam konto mo. Nmo laam wori ye n tɔge n nae tio kom kugu kom nyoa kam. 18Nmo nam yé ta‑n gwooni nɛ selo na bwori se yage to. Nmo ná boŋe se n bere n tete konto, se n ta‑n yei we, ko dae nmo mo pae tio kom kugu kom wori ye ko zega. Ko ye kugu kom mo jege nmo ko teila. 19Nmo nam wó wane n ta we, “Wɛ bwori nɛ sedaara sem o yage tega ne se ko pa amo mo na laŋa a twoŋi da.” 20Ko seene ko ke konto mo. Wɛ nam bwori nɛ sem konto o yage ba na wo sɛ‑o to ŋwaane. Nmo nam na nɛ jeiga to tɔge n wo-dedoa kam yerane ŋwaane mo. Nam yé ta‑n boŋe kamunim n pa n tete, se n daare n kɔre Wɛ de foone. 21Kolo ŋwaane Wɛ wo sɛ se o yage tio kom tete nɛ sem se jei ne. Nmo ná ba jege wo-dedoa ded‑o, o bá yage nmo de.
22Ko maama bere Wɛ na jege nɔɔna ŋwaŋa tei, de o na daare o vaŋe nɔɔna zwa tei to mo. Ko ná ye balo na ke ba chɔge to, o vaŋe ba zwa mo. Ko daare nmo, n ná tɔge o ŋwaŋa kam na ye tei to, o wó taa jege nmo ŋwaŋa. Nmo nam ná yage Wɛ ŋwaŋa kam, o laam wó bwori nmo de o yage tega ne. 23Isarele tiina bam nam ná jwoori ba ke ba wo-dedoa ba sɛ Wɛ, ba laam wó jwoori ba na ba jeiga. Wɛ wó wane o jwoori o twoŋi-ba da. 24Nmo wolo na ye dwi-gɛ tu to nye de naga kalo Wɛ na gwoni Olivi tio kolo na wo gaao ne to yera ne. O ma kwei nmo o twoŋi Olivi tio kolo na jeiri gaare ne to yera ne ye ko dae nmo tete kuu jei. Konto ŋwaane ko bá taa chana Wɛ tei ne se o jwoori o twoŋi nɛ selo o ya na bwori to se tete kuu kom jei ne.
25A nu-bia bam, amo lage se á lɔre Wɛ chega kalo déem na seigi to mo. Abam ná seene á lɔre konto, á daa bá ta‑á boŋe kamunim á pa á tete. Ko na ye tei to, leile konto Isarele tiina badaara jege yi-dɛɛre mo, ye ko bá taa ye konto taa taa. Ko nam wó taa ye konto se ko vo ko yi maŋa kam dwi-gɛ tiina balo na sɛ Wɛ to kɔgɔ kom ná puli ko ti. 26Ko ná ke konto dwoŋi, Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama laam wó na verem, ne ko na popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
“Vereno wom wó zaŋe Zion ne o ba.
O maa wó pa se Jakob dwi tiina bam yage ba wɛleera kikia yam.
27Amo Wɛ wó ke ni-gwonim dento a pa-ba we,
amo wó saare ba wɛleera yam a yage.”
28Isarele tiina bam na ve Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam to, ba ye Wɛ dona mo, ye konto laam pa se abam dwi-gɛ tiina bam na wolim. Ko daare Wɛ na kuri nɔɔna se ba taa ye o nyem tei to seeni, o jege Isarele tiina bam swono, o déem na gwoni ni de ba nabaara bam to ŋwaane. 29Wɛ nam ba zae o boboŋa de o na kuri nɔɔna ye o ke-ba lanyerane tei to. 30Abam dwi-gɛ tiina bam déem ya ve Wɛ ye á laam ba á jwoŋi o zeinim dem, Isarele tiina bam na ve Wɛ to ŋwaane. 31Banto de laam tu ba ve Wɛ ni. Ko maa ye se ba wane ba tɔge abam na jwoŋi Wɛ zeinim dem tei to baŋa ne, ye ba de laam ba ba jwoŋi o zeinim dem. 32Wɛ nam pɛ se nɔɔna maama wo yi-dɛɛre jeŋa ne mo, se o laam wane o taa jege ba maama ŋwaŋa.
33Maane-na á nii Wɛ zaane dem na tiini de daga tei!
O boboŋa maa tiini ya lira, de o yeino kom de.
Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o lɔre o boboŋa na jaane tei to
naa o lɔre chwei selo o na tɔge to.
34“Wɔ mo yi se o wane o lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa,
naa o bere‑o o na wó ke tei?
35Wɔ mo wó wane o kwei o woŋo o ma jene Wɛ,
se Wɛ ŋwe o pa kotu?”
36Wonnu maama nwoŋi Wɛ tei mo,
ye o jege te maama o nia.
Te maama maa jege kuri te pa‑o.
Wɛ maŋe de zula se ko taa vei wuu. Ameena.

english_text:
Christ Brings New Life
1Dear friends, God is good. So I beg you to offer your bodies to him as a living sacrifice, pure and pleasing. That's the most sensible way to serve God. 2Don't be like the people of this world, but let God change the way you think. Then you will know how to do everything that is good and pleasing to him.
3I realize God has treated me with undeserved grace, and so I tell each of you not to think you are better than you really are. Use good sense and measure yourself by the amount of faith that God has given you. 4 A body is made up of many parts, and each of them has its own use. 5That's how it is with us. There are many of us, but we each are part of the body of Christ, as well as part of one another.
6 God has also given each of us different gifts to use. If we can prophesy, we should do it according to the amount of faith we have. 7If we can serve others, we should serve. If we can teach, we should teach. 8If we can encourage others, we should encourage them. If we can give, we should be generous. If we are leaders, we should do our best. If we are good to others, we should do it cheerfully.
Rules for Christian Living
9Be sincere in your love for others. Hate everything that is evil and hold tight to everything that is good. 10Love each other as brothers and sisters and honor others more than you do yourself. 11Never give up. Eagerly follow the Holy Spirit and serve the Lord. 12Let your hope make you glad. Be patient in time of trouble and never stop praying. 13Take care of God's needy people and welcome strangers into your home.
14 Ask God to bless everyone who mistreats you. Ask him to bless them and not to curse them. 15 When others are happy, be happy with them, and when they are sad, be sad. 16 Be friendly with everyone. Don't be proud and feel that you know more than others. Make friends with ordinary people. 17Don't mistreat someone who has mistreated you. But try to earn the respect of others, 18and do your best to live at peace with everyone.
