I encourage God's own people to have more faith and to understand the truth about religion. 2Then they will have the hope of eternal life God promised long ago. And God never tells a lie! 3So, at the proper time, God our Savior gave this message and told me to announce what he had said.
4 Titus, because of our faith, you are like a son to me. I pray that God our Father and Christ Jesus our Savior will be kind to you and will bless you with peace!
What Titus Was To Do in Crete
5I left you in Crete to do what had been left undone and to appoint leaders for the churches in each town. As I told you, 6 they must have a good reputation and be faithful in marriage. Their children must be followers of the Lord and not have a reputation for being wild and disobedient.
7Church officials are in charge of God's work, and so they must also have a good reputation. They must not be bossy, quick-tempered, heavy drinkers, bullies, or dishonest in business. 8Instead, they must be friendly to strangers and enjoy doing good things. They must also be sensible, fair, pure, and self-controlled. 9They must stick to the true message they were taught, so their good teaching can help others and correct everyone who opposes it.
10There are many who don't respect authority, and they fool others by talking nonsense. This is especially true of some Jewish followers. 11But you must make them be quiet. They are after money, and they upset whole families by teaching what they should not. 12It is like one of their own prophets once said,
“The people of Crete
always tell lies.
They are greedy and lazy
like wild animals.”
13This surely is a true saying. And you should be hard on such people, so you can help them grow stronger in their faith. 14Don't pay any attention to any of those senseless Jewish stories and human commands. These are made up by people who won't obey the truth.
15Everything is pure for someone whose heart is pure. But nothing is pure for an unbeliever with a dirty mind. That person's mind and conscience are destroyed. 16Such people claim to know God, but their actions prove they really don't. They are disgusting. They won't obey God, and they are too worthless to do anything good.
translation_text:
1Amo Pɔɔl wolo na ye Wɛ kabaa de Yezu Krista totoŋa nakwe to mo popone tɔnɔ konto se a pa nmo Titusi. Wɛ pɛ-ne chwoŋa se a pa balo o na kuri se ba taa ye o nyem to taa jege wo-dedoa ded‑o, se ba kwori ba taa yei o chega kam. Chega kam konto nam mo pae se nɔɔna kɔre Wɛ lanyerane, 2kolo ŋwaane ba jege teena we, ba wó na ŋwea kalo na ba jege kweelim o tei ne to. Faŋa faŋa to, ko zege logo baŋa boboa ne, Wɛ déem tiŋi o ni ŋwea kam konto baŋa ne mo, ye o ware o ni o kwane. 3Ko daare ka maŋa kam na yi to, debam ma ba dé lɔre o ni-gwonim dem konto jaja. Ko maa ye kwora kam konto mo dé Vereno Wɛ pɛ amo ni se a taa tɔɔle a bere nɔɔna.
4Nmo Titusi ye nenɛɛne amo bu chekke mo dedaane dé na tɔge daane dé jege wo-dedoa de Yezu tei to.
Dé Kwo Wɛ, de dé Vereno Yezu Krista wó pa nmo zaane de yazura.
Yezu kɔgɔ kom nakwa taane
5Amo bu, a déem na yage nmo Kiriti ne to, ko ye se n kwaane n ke wonnu telo ta na daare se n ke to mo. Yezu nɔɔna bam na wo teo kolo maama ne to, se n kuri nakwa da, nenɛɛne amo na maŋe a ta de nmo se n ke tei to. 6Nmo ná kuri wolo, o jege se o taa ye wolo nɔɔna na bá taa jege o yera taane to mo. O nam maŋe se o taa jege kaane dedoa yerane mo. Ko maŋe se o bia de taa jege wo-dedoa de Yezu, se nɔɔna yé pa ba ye nɔn-wo-korro de zwabani-nyena. 7Kokuri, ko maŋe se wolo na jege Yezu nɔɔna bam o nii to taa ye wolo nɔɔna na bá taa jege o yera taane to mo, Wɛ na ke o nɔɔna bam wonto jeŋa ne se o taa nii-ba to ŋwaane. O yé taa ye boyere-nyem, naa ban-lom tu, naa sa-nyɔro, naa jar-keiru, naa nɔn-kwolo, naa kampin-nyeno. 8Ko nam maŋe se o taa ye nɔn-ŋom na jeeri veira o sɔŋɔ ne to. O jege se o taa ye jawale-nyem wolo na tɔge Wɛ ni de chega, ye o wae o tete o jaana to. 9Ko ta woli da, o jege se o yɔɔre o taa tɔge taane delo debam na maŋe de bere abam to. Dento mo jege kuri lanyerane se nɔɔna sɛ-de. Konto to, o wó wane o pa se nɔɔna taa jege boboŋ-dɛɛra de ba Wɛ chega kam tɔgem. O ta wó wane o bere nɔɔna Wɛ taane dem chekke, ye o kwori o pa se balo na ve Wɛ chega kam to lɔre we ba tusi.
10Nam tiŋi yiga tiina konto dwoŋi, kolo ŋwaane zwabani-nyena dedɛ wora abam tei ne. Banto yeini ba gane nɔɔna mo ye ba bere-ba wo-yɔɔro. Ba dedɛ mo ye balo na tiini ba sɛ Juu tiina chullu tem to. 11Abam nam jege se á che banto ni taane dem mo, kolo ŋwaane ba berem dem yeini de chɔge nɔɔno de o sɔŋɔ tiina mo daane. Ba yeini ba bere kolo na wo maŋe se ba bere nɔɔna to mo, se ba gane-ba ba ma na sabu. 12Kiriti tiina bam tete sampwora déem mo wora, ye o ta o we, “Kiriti tiina yeini ba fɔ vwa mo maŋa maama. Ba maa nye de vare-balwaaro tei, ye ba ta ye jawɔre-nyena de nɔn-kwollu de.”
13O nam na tage konto to, ko ye chega mo o taga. Mo kokuri nmo nam jege se n tiini n kaane Kiriti tiina bam lanyerane se ko pa ba yɔɔre ba taa tɔge Wɛ chega kam chekke, 14se ba daa yé sɛ Juu tiina sensɔle selo na dae chega to, naa se ba sɛ chullu telo nɔɔna na ve Wɛ chega kam ye ba jege ba bere-ba to. 15Wolo maama na jege wo-pwoŋo to, kolokolo ba jege digiru wonto tei ne. Ko daare wolo na ve Wɛ ye o bochare ta jege digiru to, kolokolo tera ko na lana wonto tei ne. Konto tu boboŋa chɔge mo ye o yu-punnu vugimi. 16Nɔɔna bam konto dwoŋi nam tɛ ba we ba me de Wɛ, ye ba nam yeiri‑o. Ba kikia nam mo bere konto. Ba jege yi-dɛɛre, ye ba ke wo-zɔɔna Wɛ yiga ne. Ba ma bere ba wo maŋe de kolo maama na lana to keim.

english_text:
Instructions for Different Groups of People
1Titus, you must teach only what is correct. 2Tell the older men to have self-control and to be serious and sensible. Their faith, love, and patience must never fail.
3Tell the older women to behave as those who love the Lord should. They must not gossip about others or be slaves of wine. They must teach what is proper, 4so the younger women will be loving wives and mothers. 5Each of the younger women must be sensible and kind, as well as a good homemaker, who puts her own husband first. Then no one can say insulting things about God's message.
6Tell the young men to have self-control in everything.
7Always set a good example for others. Be sincere and serious when you teach. 8Use clean language that no one can criticize. Do this, and your enemies will be too ashamed to say anything against you.
9Tell slaves always to please their owners by obeying them in everything. Slaves must not talk back to their owners 10or steal from them. They must be completely honest and trustworthy. Then everyone will show great respect for what is taught about God our Savior.
God's Kindness and the New Life
11God has shown us undeserved grace by coming to save all people. 12He taught us to give up our wicked ways and our worldly desires and to live decent and honest lives in this world. 13We are filled with hope, as we wait for the glorious return of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ. 14 He gave himself to rescue us from everything evil and to make our hearts pure. He wanted us to be his own people and to be eager to do right.
15Teach these things, as you use your full authority to encourage and correct people. Make sure you earn everyone's respect.
translation_text:
Berem delo na wae de woli nɔɔna to
1Ko nam ná ye nmo Titusi, se n ta‑n bere nɔɔna ba na wó ke tei se ba taa tɔge berem chekke dem to. 2Nmo jege se n bere nɔn-kweero se ba taa nege ba tete mo, se ba kwori ba taa ye jawale-nyena, se ba yɔɔre ba sɛ Yezu de wo-dedoa, de swono, de pu-dɛa.
3Ko ná ye kazena, se n pa ba taa jege ba tete se ko pa Wɛ taa nae zula ba tei ne. Ba nam yé taa ye bebare-nyena, naa ba taa pae sana nyɔɔm wae-ba. Ba nam jege se ba taa bere nɔɔna chwo-laao tɔgem na ye tei to. 4Konto mo ba wae ba pa se ka-bwona zamese ba na wó taa jege ba banna swono, de ba bia swono tei. 5Ko maŋe se ka-bwona bam taa ye jawale-nyena balo na cho ba tete de digiru to, se ba kwori ba taa ye ka-yerro telo na toŋe sɔŋɔ totoŋa lanyerane ye ba sɛ ba pa ba banna to. Konto to, nɔɔna daa bá na chwoŋa se ba yaale Wɛ taane dem, kaana banto kikia yam ŋwaane.
6Ko ta ná ye nɔn-donno, se n kwoori-ba se ba de taa ye jawale-nyena wonnu maama baŋa ne.
7Ko nam ná ye nmo tete, ko maŋe se n kikia yam bere nɔɔna ba na wó ke tei ba tɔge chwoŋa lanyerane to. Nmo na bere-ba Wɛ chega kam tei to, se n seene n yia n bere-ba lanyerane. 8Pa se n ni taane taa jege chega, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé zaŋe o yaale-de. Konto to, wolo maama na done debam to wó na o chaveera de woŋo na tera se o maa ŋɔɔne o chɔge debam yiga to.
9Ko daare ko ná ye kabɛ, ko maŋe se ba sɛ ba pa ba tiina wonnu maama wone, se ko pa ba tiina bam wo pwoli. Ba yé ve ba tiina bam ni, 10naa ba ŋɔ-ba. Ba nam pa se nɔɔna taa yei ba wo lanyerane de wonnu maama, se ko pa nɔɔna lɔre we, berem delo na vei dé Vereno Wɛ chega kam seeni to jege kuri lanyerane.
11Kokuri to, Wɛ pɛ se nɔɔna lɔre o zaane dem na ye tei, se ko pa ba maama na verem o tei ne. 12Wɛ tɔge o zaane dem konto ŋwaane o korese debam se dé lɔre we, ko maŋe se dé yage wɛleera kikia maama, de wo-yɔɔro telo dé fera na zoore to, se dé daare dé taa ye jawale-nyena logo baŋa ne, ye dé tɔge chwoŋa lanyerane dedaane Wɛ kɔrɔ. 13Ko maŋe se dé taa ye konto mo ye dé jege teena se dé pɔ Yezu Krista de wopwolo, se o jwoori o ba o veere o tete nabiina yiga ne. Wonto mo ye debam Wɛ-kamunu ye o ta ye dé Vereno. 14O ma kwei o tete o ke nabiina jeŋa ne, ye o sɛ se o te se o ma ŋwe debam wɛleera jene, se o daare o fɔge o kwɛ dé bochara se dé taa ye o tete nɔɔna, ye dé tiini dé seene dé yia wo-laaro kikia baŋa ne.
15Nam ta‑n bere nɔɔna wonnu tem konto se ba taa tɔge-te, se n daare n kwoori-ba ye n kwori n bwɛ-ba, se ko maŋe de nmo na jwoŋi dam se n ke tei to. Nam yé sɛ se nɔɔn-nɔɔno gwooni nmo.

english_text:
Doing Helpful Things
1Remind your people to obey the rulers and authorities and not to be rebellious. They must always be ready to do something helpful 2and not say cruel things or argue. They should be gentle and kind to everyone. 3We used to be stupid, disobedient, and foolish, as well as slaves of all sorts of desires and pleasures. We were evil and jealous. Everyone hated us, and we hated everyone.
4God our Savior showed us
how good and kind he is.
5He saved us because
of his mercy,
and not because
of any good things
we have done.
God washed us by the power
of the Holy Spirit.
He gave us new birth
and a fresh beginning.
6God sent Jesus Christ
our Savior
to give us his Spirit.
7Jesus treated us much better
than we deserve.
He made us acceptable to God
and gave us the hope
of eternal life.
8This message is certainly true.
These teachings are useful and helpful for everyone. I want you to insist that the people follow them, so that all who have faith in God will be sure to do good deeds. 9But don't have anything to do with stupid arguments about ancestors. And stay away from disagreements and quarrels about the Law of Moses. Such arguments are useless and senseless.
10Warn troublemakers once or twice. Then don't have anything else to do with them. 11You know their minds are twisted, and their own sins show how guilty they are.
Personal Instructions and Greetings
12 I plan to send Artemas or Tychicus to you. After he arrives, please try your best to meet me at Nicopolis. I have decided to spend the winter there.
13 When Zenas the lawyer and Apollos get ready to leave, help them as much as you can, so they won't have need of anything.
14Our people should learn to spend their time doing something useful and worthwhile.
15Greetings to you from everyone here. Greet all of our friends who share in our faith.
I pray that the Lord will be kind to all of you!
translation_text:
Keim-laaro tɔgem na ye tei to
1Guli n bere nɔɔna bam se ba taa nege ba yiga tiina de balo na ye dedɛɛra to, se ba taa sɛ ba ni. Ba nam taa yei se ba ke wo-laaro dwi maama. 2Ba nam yé zaŋe ba yaale nɔɔn-nɔɔno yuu, naa ba mage ni-kantɔgɔ. Ko nam maŋe se ba taa zuli nɔɔna, ye ba gwooni ba tete nɔɔna maama yiga ne.
3Kokuri debam maama déem ye bedwe mo. Debam yi déem wo poore. Dé maa jege yi-dɛɛre ye dé kwori dé tusi. Dé déem wo wo-yɔɔro jeŋa ne mo ye dé tɔge kolo maama dé boboŋa na lage to. Dé maa yeini dé ke lwarem de puseŋa, ye dé chuli daane. 4De ko de, debam Vereno Wɛ wom laam bere jaja we, o jege nabiina swono lanyerane, 5ye o vere debam wɛleera jeŋa ne o yage. O na jwoŋi debam o yage to, ko ye o na ye ŋwaŋa tu to ŋwaane mo, ye ko dae debam na ke keim-laaro telo to ŋwaane. O ma tɔge o Sin-laao kom ŋwaane mo o saare wo-digiru dé bochara wone, pa se dé pipiri dé taa jege boboŋ-doora, ye dé na ŋwe-doŋa o tei ne. 6Ko maa ye debam Vereno Yezu Krista ŋwaane mo Wɛ toŋe o Sin-laao kom o pa debam zɛɛra, 7se dé wane dé na chega o tei ne o zaane dem ŋwaane. Ko maa pae dé ye o bia balo na wó taa tei o wo-laaro tem to. Dé maa jege teena we, dé wó na ŋwea kalo na ba jege kweelim o tei ne to.
8Amo na tɛ taane delo to ye berem chekke mo. Konto ŋwaane, a lage se n kwaane n zege wonnu tem konto chega kam kwaga ne, se ko pa balo na sɛ Wɛ to seene ba yia ba taa tɔge keim-laaro. Dento berem dem lana, ye de jege nyɔɔre de pae nɔɔna maama. 9Ko daare ko ná ye ta-yɔɔro, naa dé kwoa kwoa yera natɔga taane, naa ni-kantɔgɔ Juu tiina chullu tem baŋa ne, se n che n tete de tento maama. Te nam ba jege nyɔɔre ye te ye kafɛ mo. 10Nɔɔno wolo ná boŋe se o ke nɔɔna daane se ba yé taa jege ni dedwe, se n kaane konto tu nenɛɛne kuni belei tei. O ta ná wo sɛ nmo taane dem, se n ja n tete ded‑o. 11Kokuri, nɔɔno ná ye konto dwoŋi, n yei we o daa ba lage se o tɔge chwoŋa. O na maŋe o tusi tei to mo bere we, o bá na bora Wɛ tei ne.
12Amo lage a toŋe Atimasa naa Tichika nmo tei ne. Ba wolo ná yi nmo tei, se n kwaane n ba lela n na amo Nikopola ne, kokuri amo boŋe se yadɛ dem ti amo dáane mo. 13Nmo nam kwaane se n woli Apolo, de Zenase wolo na ye lɔya tu to, se ba zaŋe ba bobo ba chwoŋa kam veiŋa, se n daare n pa-ba kolo maama ba na lage to. 14Pa se dé nu-bia bam taa yei se ba seene ba yia ba taa ke keim-laaro telo na wó woli nɔɔna ba gɛɛre wone. Konto mo wó pa ba ŋwea taa jege nyɔɔre nɔɔna tei ne.
15Dé nu-bia balo na wo amo tei ne to maama jɔɔne nmo. Jɔɔne balo na sɛ Yezu ye ba jege debam swono to.
Wɛ zaane dem taa wo abam maama tei ne.

english_text:
1From Paul, who is in jail for serving Christ Jesus, and from Timothy, who is like a brother because of our faith.
Philemon, you work with us and are very dear to us. This letter is to you 2 and to the church that meets in your home. It is also to our dear friend Apphia and to Archippus, who serves the Lord as we do.
3I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace!
Philemon's Love and Faith
4Philemon, each time I mention you in my prayers, I thank God. 5I hear about your faith in our Lord Jesus and about your love for all God's people. 6As you share your faith with others, I pray they may come to know all the blessings Christ has given us. 7My friend, your love has made me happy and has greatly encouraged me. It has also cheered the hearts of God's people.
Paul Speaks to Philemon about Onesimus
8Christ gives me the courage to tell you what to do. 9But I would rather ask you to do it simply because of love. Yes, as someone in jail for Christ, 10 I beg you to help Onesimus! He is like a son to me because I led him to Christ here in jail. 11Before this, he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
12Sending Onesimus back to you makes me very sad. 13I would like to keep him here with me, where he could take your place in helping me while I am here in prison for preaching the good news. 14But I won't do anything unless you agree to it first. I want your act of kindness to come from your heart, and not be something you feel forced to do.
15Perhaps Onesimus was taken from you for a little while so you could have him back for good, 16but not as a slave. Onesimus is much more than a slave. To me he is a dear friend, but to you he is even more, both as a person and as a follower of the Lord.
17If you consider me a friend because of Christ, then welcome Onesimus as you would welcome me. 18If he has cheated you or owes you anything, charge it to my account. 19With my own hand I write: I, PAUL, WILL PAY YOU BACK. But don't forget you owe me your life. 20My dear friend and follower of Christ our Lord, please cheer me up by doing this for me.
21I am sure you will do all I have asked, and even more. 22Please get a room ready for me. I hope your prayers will be answered, and I can visit you.
23 Epaphras is also here in jail for being a follower of Christ Jesus. He sends his greetings, 24 and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, who work together with me.
25I pray that the Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you!
translation_text:
1Amo Pɔɔl wolo na ye Yezu Krista nyem ye ba ja-ne ba ke peena diga ne o chega kam ŋwaane to mo popone tɔnɔ konto, ye dé nu-bu Timoti wo amo tei ne. Dé popone dé pa nmo Filimon, nmo na ye debam badwoŋ-swono ye n tɔge de debam n toŋe Wɛ totoŋa to. 2Dé jɔɔne nmo, ye dé daare dé jɔɔne dé nakɔ Afia, de Achipu wolo de na chana Wɛ totoŋa baŋa ne to. Dé daare dé jɔɔne Yezu kɔgɔ kolo na yeini ko tigisi daane nmo sɔŋɔ ne to maama.
3Dé Kwo Wɛ, de dé Teiru Yezu Krista wó pa abam zaane de yazura.
4Maŋa maama amo ná yeini a lwoori Wɛ, a guli nmo gula o yiga ne ye a ke‑o lei nmo ŋwaane. 5Kolo ŋwaane a lɔre we, n jege Wɛ nɔɔna bam maama swono lanyerane, ye n ta kwori n ke n wo-dedoa de dé Teiru Yezu. 6Wɛ wó pa‑m chwoŋa se n wane n woli n dwonna de nmo na jege wo-dedoa de Yezu Krista tei to, pa se n totoŋa yam ja kuri lanyerane, ye n wane n lɔre wo-laaro telo maama Wɛ na ke o pa debam Yezu ŋwaane to. 7Nmo na jege n dwonna swono tei to mo pae se amo wo pwoli dedɛ, ye ko fɔge amo de baare, nmo na woli Wɛ nɔɔna bam se ba na ywoni ba bochara ne to ŋwaane.
8Mo kokuri, amo lage a lwoori nmo se n ke kolo na maŋe se n ke to. Amo ya wó taa jege chwoŋa se a da Yezu Krista ŋwaane a ma dam a bere‑m nmo na wó ke kolo to. 9Amo nam wó tɔge swono ŋwaane mo a lwoori‑m. Amo Pɔɔl wolo na ye nɔn-kwea ye ba ke-ne peena diga ne leile konto Yezu Krista chega kam ŋwaane to, 10a lage a lwoori‑m nmo kabaa Onesima ŋwaane. Wonto nye de a tete bu mo. Amo na wo peena diga ne to mo a jigi o kwo Wɛ chwoŋa seeni. 11O déem na toŋe o pa nmo to, o wo pɛ se n na nyɔɔre. Ko daare leile konto o jege nyɔɔre o pa nmo de amo maama.
12Amo lage a toŋe‑o se o jwoori o ba nmo tei, ye a ta jege o swono a bochare ne. 13Amo na wo peena diga ne Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam berem ŋwaane to, a ya wó taa lage se o maŋe a tei ne, se o wane o leiri nmo yuu ne o taa toŋa o pa-ne. 14Amo nam ba lage se a ke kolokolo ye nmo yeiri ko ni ne. Ko wó taa ye nmo ná sɛ se n woli-ne, ye ko bá taa ye fefeo ŋwaane.
15Onesima na duri o yage nmo to, o pɔɔre nmo tei ne maŋa fenfee wone. Ko nam wó wane ko pa se o laam jwoori o ba o taa wo nmo tei ne taa wuu. 16O na duri o yage nmo to, o déem ye kabaa mo. O ná jwoori, o laam wó taa dwoi kabaa na ye tei to, de o na jigi nmo nu-bu dé Teiru wom ŋwaane to. Amo tiini a jege o swono. Nmo nam wó tiini n ta‑n swoi‑o se ko gaale, o na ye n kabaa ye o kwori o ye n nu-bu to ŋwaane.
17Nmo ná sɛ we debam seene dé me daane Wɛ ŋwaane, se n kwaane n jeeri Onesima lanyerane ne amo mo tei. 18O déem ná maŋe o ke o chɔge nmo yuu, naa o ná jege nmo jene, se n kwei ko maama n pa amo. 19Nii, amo Pɔɔl tete mo mɛ a jeŋa a popone tento we, Amo wó ŋwe jene dem. Ko daare nmo wó wane n guli we, n maŋe n jege amo jene dedɛ, de nmo na nɛ ŋwea Wɛ tei ne amo ŋwaane to. 20A nu-bu, ko ye chega mo we, amo laam lage se a na nyɔɔre nmo baŋa ne, nmo na ye dé Teiru wom nyem to ŋwaane. Pa se ywoni taa wo amo bochare ne Yezu Krista ŋwaane. 21Amo na popone tɔnɔ konto a pa nmo to, a yei lanyerane we, nmo wó sɛ a boboŋa yam. Amo ta yei we, nmo wó ke keim delo na wó dwoni amo na lwoori kolo to.
22Ko ta woli da, a lwoori‑m se n kwaane n lage diga se a peini da. Kolo ŋwaane amo jege teena we, Wɛ wó sɛ abam na lwoori‑o á pa-ne tei to ye o pore chwoŋa se a jwoori a ba abam tei.
23Epafera mo jɔɔne‑m. Wonto dedaane amo mo wo peena diga ne Yezu Krista chega kam ŋwaane. 24Maake, de Arisaka, de Demas, de Luka maama de jɔɔne‑m. Banto de amo tɔge daane dé toŋa dé pa Wɛ.
25Dé Teiru Yezu Krista zaane dem taa wo abam bochara ne.

english_text:
1Long ago in many ways and at many times God's prophets spoke his message to our ancestors. 2 But now at last, God sent his Son to bring his message to us. God created the universe by his Son, and everything will someday belong to the Son. 3 God's Son has all the brightness of God's own glory and is like him in every way. By his own mighty word, he holds the universe together.
After the Son had washed away our sins, he sat down at the right side of the glorious God in heaven. 4He had become much greater than the angels, and the name he was given is far greater than any of theirs.
God's Son Is Greater than Angels
5 God has never said
to any of the angels,
“You are my Son, because today
I have become your Father!”
Neither has God said
to any of them,
“I will be his Father,
and he will be my Son!”
6 When God brings his first-born Son into the world, he commands all of his angels to worship him.
7 And when God speaks about the angels, he says,
“I change my angels into wind
and my servants
into flaming fire.”
8 But God says about his Son,
“You are God,
and you will rule
as King forever!
Your royal power
brings about justice.
9You loved justice
and hated evil,
and so I, your God,
have chosen you.
I appointed you
and made you happier
than any of your friends.”
10 The Scriptures also say,
“In the beginning, Lord,
you were the one
who laid the foundation
of the earth
and created the heavens.
11They will all disappear
and wear out like clothes,
but you will last forever.
12You will roll them up
like a robe
and change them
like a garment.
But you are always the same,
and you will live forever.”
13 God never said to any
of the angels,
“Sit at my right side
until I make your enemies
into a footstool for you!”
14 Angels are merely spirits sent to serve people who are going to be saved.
translation_text:
Yezu Krista bere debam Wɛ chega kam chekke
1Faŋa faŋa to, Wɛ déem tɔge o sampwori sem baŋa ne mo o ŋɔɔne dedaane dé nabaara bam. O déem yeini o da chwei dwi dwi mo o ŋɔɔne de-ba kuni dedɛ. 2Ko daare leile konto, logo baŋa kweelim da yam na daare fee maŋa kalo to, Wɛ laam ma pa se o Bu mo ba o ŋɔɔne o taane de debam. Wɛ dɛ wonto ŋwaane mo o ke logo baŋa de wɛyuu wonnu maama, ye o tiŋi‑o se o ba o taa tei wonnu telo maama na wora to. 3Wɛ Bu wom maa jege pwooni delo na bere Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom na ye tei to. O maa jege o Kwo Wɛ nyenyego chekke, pa se dé lɔre Wɛ na ye tei to ja. O ni taane maa jege dam ye de pae se wonnu maama taa fɔge te wora taa taa.
O ma ba o saare nɔɔna wɛleera pa ba bochara fɔge ya kwɛ, ye o laam daare o jwoori o di wɛyuu o vo o jeini Baŋa Wɛ jazem seeni. 4Konto to, o tu o dwoni Wɛ malese sem, de Wɛ na pɛ o jege yere delo na daga de dwoi sento na jege yere tei to.
5Ko ná ye malese sem, Wɛ wo fɔge o ta de se wolowolo o we:
“Nmo mo ye amo Bu,
ye zem amo de ji nmo Kwo.”
Wɛ daa ta wo tage o maleka tu wolowolo taane o we:
“Amo wó taa ye o Kwo,
se o de taa ye amo bu.”
6Ko daare maŋa kalo Wɛ na boŋe se o toŋe o Bu-doa kam se o ba logo baŋa to, o tage o we,
“Wɛ malese sem maama jege se se zuli‑o mo.”
7Ko nam ná ye malese sem tete, Wɛ tage se taane o we,
se ye omo tontoŋena mo,
ye se toŋe ne vio mo tei.
O ta pae se ji ne min-vogo mo tei,
se se taa toŋa se pa‑o.
8Ko daare ko ná ye Wɛ Bu wom, Wɛ tage o taane o we:
“Wɛ, nmo paare dem wó taa wora taa,
se ko taa vei wuu.
Nmo wó ta‑n tei n nɔɔna se ko tɔge chwoŋa chekke.
9Nmo swoi chega tɔgem, ye n daare n chuli lwarem kikia.
Konto ŋwaane mo, n Tu Wɛ wom kuri nmo,
ye o lwo o swolim nuga kam n yuu ne
pa se n di ywoni n dwoni n dwonna bam maama.”
10Wɛ ta tage dé Teiru wom taane o we:
“Boboa ne to, nmo déem mo chwi tega kam kuri,
ye n ta kwori n ma n jea n naane wɛyuu wonnu maama.
11Wonnu tem konto maama wó ba te chɔge,
ko daare nmo ta wó ta‑n wora taa.
Wonnu tem konto maama wó ba te zareme
ne gɔrɔ na yeini ko zareme tei to.
12Te wó ba te leiri, ye n kukuli-te n tiŋi,
ne nmo na kukuli gare-dwoŋo n tiŋi
ye n daare n kwei gare-doŋo n zo tei to.
Nmo nam ta wó ta‑n ye ne n na maŋe n ye tei to mo.
N bena yam bá fɔge ya ti.”
13Wɛ déem wo fɔge o ta de o malese sem wolowolo o we:
“Ba n jeini amo jazem seeni,
se a daare a wane n dona bam
a ke n dam kuri ne se n ta‑n tei-ba.”
14Wɛ malese sem nam na ye tei to, se maama ye balo na toŋe ba pa Wɛ to mo. Wɛ maa yeini o toŋe-se se se vo se woli balo o na tiŋi o ni we, omo wó jwoŋi-ba o yage to.

english_text:
This Great Way of Being Saved
1We must give our full attention to what we were told, so we won't drift away. 2The message spoken by angels proved to be true, and all who disobeyed or rejected it were punished as they deserved. 3So if we refuse this great way of being saved, how can we hope to escape? The Lord himself was the first to tell about it, and people who heard the message proved to us that it was true. 4God himself showed that his message was true by working all kinds of powerful miracles and wonders. He also gave his Holy Spirit to anyone he chose to.
The One Who Leads Us To Be Saved
5We know that God did not put the future world under the power of angels. 6 Somewhere in the Scriptures someone says to God,
“What makes you care
about us humans?
Why are you concerned
for weaklings such as we?
7You made us lower
than the angels
for a while.
Yet you have crowned us
with glory and honor.
8And you have put everything
under our power!”
God has put everything under our power and has not left anything out of our power. But we still don't see it all under our control. 9What we do see is Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels. Because of God's gift of undeserved grace, Jesus died for everyone. And now that Jesus has suffered and died, he is crowned with glory and honor!
10Everything belongs to God, and all things were created by his power. So God did the right thing when he made Jesus perfect by suffering, as Jesus led many of God's children to be saved and to share in his glory. 11Jesus and the people he makes holy all belong to the same family. This is why he isn't ashamed to call them his brothers and sisters. 12 He even said to God,
“I will tell them your name
and sing your praises
when they come together
to worship.”
13 He also said,
“I will trust God.”
Then he said,
“Here I am with the children
God has given me.”
14We are people of flesh and blood. This is why Jesus became one of us. He died to destroy the devil, who had power over death. 15But he also died to rescue all of us who live each day in fear of dying. 16 Jesus clearly did not come to help angels, but he did come to help Abraham's descendants. 17He had to be one of us, so he could serve God as our merciful and faithful high priest and sacrifice himself for the forgiveness of our sins. 18And now that Jesus has suffered and was tempted, he can help anyone else who is tempted.
translation_text:
Dé wó taa seene dé yia se Wɛ jwoŋi debam
1Konto ŋwaane mo ko fe se dé kwaane dé taa jege Wɛ kwora kalo dé na nigi to se ko gaale, se dé yé tutwoni dé nwoŋi o chega kam wone. 2Kokuri Wɛ déem ya pɛ se o kwora kam tɔge o malese jeŋa mo ka ba dé nabaara bam tei, ye o taane dem konto maŋe de jege kuri lanyerane. Nɔɔno ná wo sɛ-de ye o ná chɔge de nia yam, konto tu jege se o na waarem ne ko na maŋe se o na tei to. 3Ko nam ná ye debam balo Wɛ na dɛ o Bu wom ŋwaane o pa dé lɔre o kwora kam to, dé yiga ná tera o verem dem wone, dé wó wane dé lu na? Dé Teiru Yezu mo dɛ yiga o ŋɔɔne Wɛ verem dem konto taane o bere nɔɔna. Balo na nigi-de to laam ma daare ba ta ba bere debam we ko ye chega mo. 4Ko woli da, Wɛ tete mo zege ba kwaga ne de o na pɛ ba ke maana de wo-kenkagela dwi dwi na bere o dam to. O ma daare o woli ba maama de o Sin-laao kom dam, nenɛɛne o na boŋe se o ke o pa ba dedoa dedoa tei to.
Yezu tu o ji nabiinu se o jwoŋi debam
5Wɛ wo pɛ o malese sem di dam logo kolo na lage ko ba ko taa wora to baŋa ne. Ko ye lo-doŋo kom konto taane mo dé tɛa. 6Wɛ tɔnɔ kom nam bere David na ŋɔɔne de Wɛ o we:
“Amo Tu Wɛ, ko ná ye nabiina,
bɛ mo ye n jege ba boboŋa?
Bɛ mo ke ye n yiga wo nabiin-bia wone konto?
7Nmo nam pɛ se nabiina tiini ba jege paare,
ye n ta pa-ba zula,
ye ba laam daare fee se ba taa mae de malese sem.
8N ma‑n daare n ke wonnu maama
ba dam kuri ne.”
Ko bere debam we, Wɛ ke wonnu maama nabiina dam kuri ne mo. Kokuri mo kolokolo tera Wɛ na wo ke-ko ba dam kuri ne. Ko nam ye chega mo we, leile konto dé ta wo nɛ we, wonnu maama wo nabiina dam kuri ne. 9Dé na nɛ kolo to mo ye Yezu de o dam-fɔrɔ kom. Wonto déem jigi nabiinu mo ye o daare fee se o taa mae de malese sem. O ma tu o tete ye o yaare o te. Konto ŋwaane Wɛ laam ma pa se o tiini o na paare de zula telaao ne. Konto baŋa ne mo Wɛ tɔge o zaane dem ŋwaane o pa se Yezu wane o leiri nabiina maama yuu ne o te ba zeinim ŋwaane.
10Wɛ mo ye wolo na tɔge o tete ŋwaane o ke wonnu maama to. O boboŋa déem ma ja se o pa nabiina dedɛ ji o bia, se ba daare ba taa jege paare o tei ne. Mo kokuri ko maŋe se Wɛ pa o Bu Yezu tɔge yaara ŋwaane o vo o yi o jeiŋa jei o ti. Wonto mo jwoŋi Wɛ bia bam ba wɛleera wone, ye o tɔge ba yiga o jaane-ba o vei Wɛ tei.
11Yezu mo ye wolo na pae nabiina ye wose Wɛ yiga ne to. Wonto de balo o na pɛ ba ji wose to ye nɔn-doa bia mo. Konto ŋwaane mo o bwoi-ba we o nu-bia, ye ko ba jege chaveera o tei ne. 12Mo kokuri o tage de Wɛ o we:
“Amo wó pa nmo yere zaŋe a nu-bia bam yiga ne.
A maa wó zege ba nɔn-kɔgɔ kom tetare ne
a leeni a seini nmo yere dem.”
13O daa ta maa we:
“Amo tete wó kwei a teena maama a pa Wɛ.”
O daa ta we:
“Nii-na amo de bia balo Wɛ na ke amo jeŋa ne to mo tento dé zega.”
14Chega ŋwaane to, balo na ye Wɛ bia to ye nabiina mo, ye ba jege yera de jana. Konto ŋwaane mo Yezu de déem tɔge o ji nabiinu, se o wane o tɔge o toone dem ŋwaane o chɔge wolo na jege toone dam to. Wonto mo ye setaana pɛ. 15Yezu na wane toone konto to, ko pɛ se o wane o jwoŋi balo na fona de toone to o yage. Banto de ba ŋwea maama ya fona ba pa toone ne kabɛ tei, ye Yezu laam jwoŋi-ba. 16Dé lɔre we, ko dae malese sem mo o tu se o zeini. O nam tu se o zeini Abaraham dwi tiina mo. 17Mo kokuri ko maŋe se o ji nabiinu pa se o seene o nye de o nu-bia bam chekke. Konto mo pɛ‑o chwoŋa se o taa ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu wolo na jege o nu-bia bam ŋwaŋa lanyerane, ye o toŋe Wɛ yiga ne de jawala o pa-ba. O keim dem konto mo pɛ o wae o saare ba wɛleera ye o pa ba fɔge de Wɛ. 18Kokuri Yezu na nɛ yaara ye o wo sɛ se ya soge‑o to, o laam wae o zeini balo yaara na wora ya faŋe-ba to se ba de taa jege pu-dɛa.

english_text:
Jesus Is Greater than Moses
1My friends, God has chosen you to be his holy people. So think about Jesus, the one we call our apostle and high priest! 2 Jesus was faithful to God, who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in serving all God's people. 3But Jesus deserves more honor than Moses, just as the builder of a house deserves more honor than the house. 4Of course, every house is built by someone, and God is really the one who built everything.
5Moses was a faithful servant and told God's people what would be said in the future. 6But Christ is the Son in charge of God's people. And we are those people, if we keep on being brave and don't lose hope.
A Rest for God's People
7 It is just as the Holy Spirit says,
“If you hear God's voice today,
8don't be stubborn!
Don't rebel like those people
who were tested
in the desert.
* 9 For forty years your ancestors
tested God and saw
the things he did.
10“Then God got tired of them
and said,
‘You people never
show good sense,
and you don't understand
what I want you to do.’
11God became angry
and told the people,
‘You will never enter
my place of rest!’ ”
12My friends, watch out! Don't let evil thoughts or doubts make any of you turn from the living God. 13You must encourage one another each day. And you must keep on while there is still a time that can be called “today.” If you don't, then sin may fool some of you and make you stubborn. 14We were sure about Christ when we first became his people. So let's hold tightly to our faith until the end. 15 The Scriptures say,
“If you hear his voice today,
don't be stubborn
like those who rebelled.”
16 Who were those people that heard God's voice and rebelled? Weren't they the same ones that came out of Egypt with Moses? 17Who were the people that made God angry for 40 years? Weren't they the ones that sinned and died in the desert? 18And who did God say would never enter his place of rest? Weren't they the ones that disobeyed him? 19We see that those people did not enter the place of rest because they did not have faith.
translation_text:
Wɛ Bu Yezu tiini o dwoi Moses
1A nu-bia balo na ye Wɛ nyem to, Wɛ bwoŋi abam se á tɔge á na ywoni telaao ne. Nam boŋe-na á nii Yezu na ye tei to. Wonto mo ye Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋ-kweo de Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu wolo dé na jege o chega to. 2Wɛ mo tiŋi‑o se o taa ye konto, ye o toŋa o pa Wɛ de jawala. Ko nam ye bedwe mo de Moses déem na jege jawala o nii Wɛ nɔɔna bam o pa‑o tei to. 3Yezu nam seene o maŋe se o na zula ko dwoni Moses, kokuri nɔɔno ná bobo sɔŋɔ kuri, wonto jege se o na zula se ko dwoi sɔŋɔ kom tete. 4Sɔŋɔ nam tera ye ko dae nɔɔno mo bobo ko kuri. Wɛ nam mo ye wolo na bobo wonnu maama kuri. 5Moses déem nye de tontoŋeno mo Wɛ sɔŋɔ wone, de o na toŋe de jawala o pa Wɛ nɔɔna tei to. O ma yeini o wuuri o bere-ba Wɛ chega kalo na wó ba ka lɔre ja to. 6Ko daare Yezu Krista mo ye sɔŋɔ kom tete bu chekke, ye o tei Wɛ sɔŋɔ kom. Debam maa ye o sɔŋɔ kom tiina, ne dé ná maŋe dé jege pu-dɛa ye dé ta bere we, dé jege teena o tei ne to.
Dé yé taa jege yi-dɛɛre dé pa Wɛ
7Ko maa nye de Wɛ Sin-laao kom na bere debam tei ko we:
“Abam zem ná nigi Wɛ kwora,
8se á yé pa á wo ke dam,
ne á nabaara déem na jege yi-dɛɛre
ye ba kwaane se ba maŋe Wɛ ba nii
maŋa kalo ba na wo kagoa kam yuu ne to.”
9Wɛ maa we:
“Abam nabaara bam déem nɛ amo na ke-ba tei taa, bena finna to,
ye ba ta kwaane se ba maŋe amo ba nii.
10Konto ŋwaane mo amo bane zaŋe de á nabaara bam konto,
ye a ta a we, ‘Ba yeini ba paale ba tusi mo maŋa maama.
Ba maa ba sɛa se ba tɔge amo chwei sem.’
11Mo kokuri amo tɔge a ban-zɔŋɔ kom baŋa a ma du duuri a pa-ba a we,
amo bere a bá pa-ba chwoŋa se ba zo amo woro kom wone ba sii.”
12A nu-bia bam, ta‑á yei-na se abam wolowolo yé taa jege boboŋ-lwanno o bochare ne se ko pa o ve Ŋwea Tu Wɛ ni ye o daare o ywori o kwaga ne. 13Nam ta‑á woli-na daane maŋa maama, se ko pa á ta‑á jege pu-dɛa. Ko ta ná ye zem da yam ye á ni Wɛ kwora kam, se abam wolowolo yé pa lwarem gane‑o pa se o ke yi-dɛɛre o pa Wɛ. 14Debam nam tu dé tɔge de Yezu Krista dé ye Wɛ bia mo, ne dé ta ná jege teena de Wɛ, nenɛɛne dé na maŋe dé jege tei boboa ne to, se ko vo ko yi dé ŋwea kweelim.
15Dé maŋe dé lɔre Wɛ tɔnɔ kom na bere tei ko we:
“Abam zem ná nigi Wɛ kwora,
se á yé pa á wo ke dam,
ne á nabaara bam déem na jege yi-dɛɛre de Wɛ tei to.”
16Ko ná ye balo déem na nigi Wɛ kwora kam ye ba daare ba jege yi-dɛɛre to, banto ye bera mo? Ba ye balo maama Moses na tɔge ba yiga o ja o nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom wone to mo. 17Ko ná ye balo Wɛ bane na zaŋe de-ba taa se ko vo ko yi bena finna to, ba ye bera mo? Ba ye nɔɔna balo na ke ba tusi kagoa kam wone ye Wɛ pa se ba te da to mo. 18Wɛ na dugi o we, omo bere o bá pa-ba chwoŋa se ba zo o woro kom wo ba sii to, ko ye balo na ve o ni to taane mo. Ko dae konto na?
19Ko ma pa dé lɔre we, Wɛ na wo pɛ-ba chwoŋa se ba zo o woro kom wo to, ko ye ba na wo ke ba wo-dedoa ded‑o to ŋwaane mo.

english_text:
1The promise to enter the place of rest is still good, and we must take care that none of you miss out. 2We have heard the message, just as they did. But they failed to believe what they heard, and the message did not do them any good. 3 Only people who have faith will enter the place of rest. It is just as the Scriptures say,
“God became angry
and told the people,
‘You will never enter
my place of rest!’ ”
God said this, even though everything has been ready from the time of creation. 4 In fact, somewhere the Scriptures say that by the seventh day, God had finished his work, and so he rested. 5 We also read that he later said, “You people will never enter my place of rest!” 6This means that the promise to enter is still good, because those who first heard about it disobeyed and did not enter. 7 Much later God told David to make the promise again, just as I have already said,
“If you hear his voice today,
don't be stubborn!”
8 If Joshua had really given the people rest, there would not be any need for God to talk about another day of rest. 9But God has promised us a Sabbath when we will rest, even though it has not yet come. 10 On that day God's people will rest from their work, just as God rested from his work.
11We should do our best to enter the place of rest, so none of us will disobey and miss going there, as they did. 12God's word is alive and powerful! It is sharper than any double-edged sword. His word can cut through our spirits and souls and through our joints and marrow, until it discovers the desires and thoughts of our hearts. 13 Nothing is hidden from God! He sees through everything, and we will have to tell him the truth.
Jesus Is the Great High Priest
14We have a great high priest, who has gone into heaven, and he is Jesus the Son of God. This is why we must hold on to what we have said about him. 15Jesus understands every weakness of ours, because he was tempted in every way that we are. But he did not sin! 16So whenever we are in need, we should come bravely before the throne of our merciful God. There we will be treated with undeserved grace, and we will find help.
translation_text:
Dé wó kwaane se dé zo Wɛ woro kom wo dé sii
1Wɛ na pwooli kampwola se o pa nɔɔna chwoŋa se ba zo o woro kom wo ba sii to ta fɔge ka wora mo. Debam nam wó taa yei dé tete mo se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé sa chwoŋa ye o ta wo yi Wɛ woro kom se o sii. 2Debam maŋe dé ni Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam, nenɛɛne dé nabaara bam de na nigi-ka tei to. Banto nam na nigi-ka to, ba wo nɛ nyɔɔre ka baŋa ne, kolo ŋwaane ba wo ke ba wo-dedoa se ba tɔge Wɛ na tage kolo to. 3Debam balo na ke dé wo-dedoa de Wɛ to mo wó ba dé sii o woro kom wone. Wɛ nam tage nɔɔna banto taane o we:
“Amo tɔge a ban-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane
a du duuri a pa-ba a we,
amo bere a bá pa-ba chwoŋa se ba zo amo woro kom wo ba sii.”
Wɛ na tage konto to, ko nam dae we o ba jege woro mo se ba zo da ba sii. Ko zege maŋa kalo o na naane logo baŋa to mo o totoŋa yam ti ye o daare o sii. 4Wɛ tɔnɔ kom tage Wɛ totoŋa da yarepɛ siu dɛ dem taane ko we,
“Da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne mo Wɛ laam jeini o sii
o totoŋa yam maama wone.”
5Wɛ daa ta tage o siu kom taane o we,
“Amo bere a bá pa-ba chwoŋa se ba zo amo woro kom wo ba sii.”
6Ko na ye konto to, dé nabaara balo na dɛ yiga ba ni Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam to wo wane ba zo o woro kom wo ba sii, ba na ve o ni to ŋwaane. Konto ŋwaane ko laam daare se nɔɔna badaara mo na chwoŋa se ba zo. 7Mo kokuri Wɛ daa ta tiŋi dɛ dedwoŋi se nɔɔna wane ba sɛ o ni, ye ba daare ba zo o woro kom wo ba sii. Dé nabaara bam na wo wane ba zo ye bena dedɛ kɛ to, Wɛ daa ta bere o ni dem de nɔɔna badaara, ye David ta de taane o we:
“Abam zem ná nigi Wɛ kwora,
se á yé pa á wo ke dam.”
8Josua déem tɔge Wɛ nɔɔna bam yiga o pa ba vo ba zoore te-ywoŋa jei ne. Ko nam dae Wɛ woro kom mo ba zo se ba sii. Ba ya ná seene ba na siu, Wɛ ya daa bá tiŋi dɛ dedwoŋi se nɔɔna na siu de wone. 9Konto mo dé yei we, chwoŋa ta wora zem se Wɛ nɔɔna bam na siu o tei ne. 10Wolo maama ná zo Wɛ woro kom wo se o sii, wonto wó seene o na siu o totoŋa yam wone, ne Wɛ de déem na sii de o totoŋa yam da yarepɛ dɛ ne tei to. 11Konto ŋwaane pa-na dé kwaane se dé zo Wɛ woro kom wo dé sii. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé zaŋe o ve Wɛ ni se o jwoori Wɛ kwaga ne, ne dé nabaara bam déem na ke tei to.
12Wɛ kwora kam jege ŋwea ye ka dana lanyerane. Ka nye de se-zɔɔ kolo na jege nia yalei to mo. Ka maa wae ka zoore nɔɔno wo ka pɔɔre o jworo de o bochare wonnu maama, ye ka daare ka lɔre o swa de o boboŋa maama na ye tei to. 13Kolokolo bá wane ko seigi Wɛ yiga ne. Woŋo kolo maama na wora to, o maŋe o yei ko na ye tei to chekke. Ko maa ye wonto mo dé jege se dé ja dé tete dé ba dé pa‑o, se o bwei debam o nii.
Yezu zo Wɛ tei debam ŋwaane
14Debam nam jege wolo na nɛ chwoŋa se o zo Wɛ tei telaao ne, o na ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu debam ŋwaane to. Wonto mo ye Wɛ Bu Yezu, ye o dwoi logo baŋa kaanem yiga tiina bam maama. Konto ŋwaane pa-na se dé tiini dé sɛ Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem lanyerane. 15Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu wom konto nam dae wolo na bá wane o taa jege debam ŋwaŋa. O nam yei debam na bwona tei to, ye o na yaara yalo na faŋe‑o to, ne yaara yalo maama dwoŋi debam na nɛ to. De konto de, o ta wo sɛ o tusi. 16Konto ŋwaane, pa-na se dé taa jege baare ye dé vo dé yi Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom jeiŋa jei, se dé jwoŋi zaane o tei ne. Konto mo Wɛ wó duri dé ŋwaŋa ye o pa debam zaane se ko wane ko zeini debam maŋa kalo dé na lage wolim to.

english_text:
1Every high priest is appointed to help others by offering gifts and sacrifices to God because of their sins. 2A high priest has weaknesses of his own, and he feels sorry for foolish and sinful people. 3 This is why he must offer sacrifices for his own sins and for the sins of others. 4 But no one can have the honor of being a high priest simply by wanting to be one. Only God can choose a priest, and God is the one who chose Aaron.
5 This is how it was with Christ. He became a high priest, but not just because he wanted the honor of being one. It was God who told him,
“You are my Son, because today
I have become your Father!”
6 In another place, God says,
“You are a priest forever
just like Melchizedek.”
7 God had the power to save Jesus from death. And while Jesus was on earth, he begged God with loud crying and tears to save him. He truly worshiped God, and God listened to his prayers. 8Jesus is God's own Son, but still he had to suffer before he could learn what it really means to obey God. 9Suffering made Jesus perfect, and now he can save forever all who obey him. 10This is because God chose him to be a high priest like Melchizedek.
Warning against Turning Away
11Much more could be said about this subject. But it is hard to explain, and all of you are slow to understand. 12 By now you should have been teachers, but once again you need to be taught the simplest things about what God has said. You need milk instead of solid food. 13People who live on milk are like babies who don't really know what is right. 14Solid food is for mature people who have been trained to know right from wrong.
translation_text:
1Ko ná ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu maama, ba yeini ba le‑o o dwonna nabiina wone mo se o taa toŋe o pa-ba Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem seeni. Wonto jege se o taa kaane Wɛ ba maama wɛleera saarem ŋwaane mo. 2O tete nam na bwona ye o yeini o tusi to, o wae o jaane o bochare de balo na yeiri Wɛ chega kam lanyerane ye ba tusi to. 3O na bwona konto to, ko fe mo se o kaane Wɛ o tete wɛleera saarem ŋwaane, se ko woli de balo o na toŋe o pa-ba to de wɛleera ŋwaane.
4Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam bá wane o le o tete se o ji Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu. Ko ye Wɛ mo wó kuri‑o se o taa ye konto, nenɛɛne o déem na bobo o kuri Aron tei to.
5Ko ta ye bedwe mo de Yezu Krista na jigi Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu to. O wo boŋe kamunim o pa o tete se o taa ye konto. Wɛ nam mo tage ded‑o o we:
“Nmo mo ye amo Bu,
ye zem amo de ji nmo Kwo.”
6Wɛ daa ta tage o tɔnɔ kom jei sedwoŋi ne we:
“Nmo wó ta‑n ye amo kaanem tu taa wuu,
ne Melkizedeka na ye tei faŋa faŋa to.”
7Yezu na wo logo baŋa ne maŋa kalo to, o yeini o tiini o ware Wɛ, ye o ka yi-na o kaase o ma lwoori‑o, o na yei we Wɛ wó wane o jwoŋi‑o toone wone to ŋwaane. Wɛ ma sɛ o wɛ-lworo kom, o na tu o tete ye o zuli‑o lanyerane to ŋwaane. 8O maŋe o ye Wɛ Bu mo. De konto de, o na yaare tei to mo pɛ o lɔre o na wó ke tei o tɔge Wɛ ni to. 9O laam ma ji wolo na jege chega chekke ye o wae o jwoŋi balo maama na sɛ o ni to o pa ba na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne. 10Wɛ ma le‑o se o taa ye o kaanem nakwe tu, ne Melkizedeka faŋa faŋa na ye tei to.
Dé yé ywori Wɛ chwoŋa wone
11Amo ya jege taane dedɛ se a ta a bere abam konto baŋa ne, ye ko nam tiini ko chana se a pa á ni ko kuri, kolo ŋwaane abam laam jege jawɔrɔ á boboŋa ne. 12Ko ná dae konto ŋwaane, tento wɛɛne abam ya wó ta‑á ye balo na maŋe se á ta‑á jege Wɛ nɔɔna á zamese to mo. Ko na ye chega to, ko maŋe se nɔɔna jwoori ba zamese abam Wɛ taane wo-mwaalo tem mo. Abam nye de bia balo ta na wo yi wodiu dim, ye á jege se á ta‑á ŋɔge yela mo ne bu-balɛ tei to. 13Balo na jege bu-balɛ boboŋa konto to bere we, ba ta wo lɔre Wɛ kwora kalo na bere o chega kam to chekke. 14Ko daare balo boboŋa na kweere Wɛ chega kam seeni to mo laam yi se ba di wodiu kolo na duna to. Banto mo yeini ba tɔge Wɛ chega kam de jawala, pa se ba wae ba pɔɔre lam de lwarem daane.

english_text:
1We must try to become mature and start thinking about more than just the basic things we were taught about Christ. We shouldn't need to keep talking about why we ought to turn from deeds that bring death and why we ought to have faith in God. 2And we shouldn't need to keep teaching about baptisms or about the laying on of hands or about people being raised from death and the future judgment. 3Let's grow up, if God is willing.
4-6But what about people who turn away after they have already seen the light and have received the gift from heaven and have shared in the Holy Spirit? What about those who turn away after they have received the good message of God and the powers of the future world? There is no way to bring them back. What they are doing is the same as nailing the Son of God to a cross and insulting him in public!
7A field is useful to farmers, if there is enough rain to make good crops grow. In fact, God will bless such a field. 8 But land that produces only thornbushes is worthless. It is likely to fall under God's curse, and in the end it will be set on fire.
9My friends, we are talking this way. But we are sure that you are doing those really good things people do when they are being saved. 10God is always fair. He will remember how you helped his people in the past and how you are still helping them. You belong to God, and he won't forget the love you have shown his people. 11We wish each of you would always be eager to show how strong and lasting your hope really is. 12Then you would never be lazy. You would be following the example of those who had faith and were patient until God kept his promise to them.
God's Promise Is Sure
13No one is greater than God. So he made a promise in his own name when he said to Abraham, 14 “I, the Lord, will bless you with many descendants!” 15Then after Abraham had been very patient, he was given what God had promised. 16When anyone wants to settle an argument, they make a vow by using the name of someone or something greater than themselves. 17So when God wanted to prove for certain his promise to his people could not be broken, he made a vow. 18God cannot tell lies! And so his promises and vows are two things that can never be changed.
We have run to God for safety. Now his promises should greatly encourage us to take hold of the hope that is right in front of us. 19 This hope is like a firm and steady anchor for our souls. In fact, hope reaches behind the curtain and into the most holy place. 20 Jesus has gone there ahead of us, and he is our high priest forever, just like Melchizedek.
translation_text:
1Konto ŋwaane pa-na se dé yage Yezu Krista taane wo-mwaalo tem, se dé laam pa dé boboŋa kweere Wɛ chega kam seeni. Abam daa ba jege se á jwoori á bobo Wɛ taane dem zamesem, bɛŋwaane á maŋe á lɔre á na wó yage wo-yɔɔro kikia tei to, de á na wó ke á wo-dedoa de Wɛ tei to. 2Á maŋe á zamese nɔɔna na wó zare ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane tei to, ko woli de nakwa na wó kwei ba je ba daŋe nɔɔna yuu ne se Wɛ zeini-ba tei to, ye á kwori á zamese twa na wó bi tei to, ko woli de Wɛ na wó ba o di nabiina bora tei to. 3Pa-na dé yage wonnu tem konto zamesem se dé daare dé kwaane dé kɛ yiga. Wɛ ná sɛ, dé wó wane dé ke konto.
4Ko ná ye balo na maŋe ba sɛ Wɛ chega kam to, ba laam ná paale ba ywori o tei ne, nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá wane o jwoori o de-ba Wɛ chwoŋa wone. Banto mo maŋe ba ye balo yi na poore de Wɛ chega kam ye ba daare ba lɔre Wɛ ŋwe-doŋa kam na ye tei to. Ba de Wɛ Sin-laao kom maa me daane. 5Ba maŋe ba lɔre Wɛ ni taane dem na ywomma tei to, ye ba na Wɛ totoŋ-kamunnu telo na maŋe de Wɛ paare delo na lage de ba to mo. 6Nɔɔna banto dwi ná ywori Wɛ chwoŋa wone, nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá wane o pa ba leiri ba wo se ba daa taa tɔge Wɛ, kolo ŋwaane ba yeini ba pa Wɛ Bu Yezu na chaveera nɔɔna yiga ne, nenɛɛne ba tete na jwoori ba ke‑o dagara kam yuu ne ba go tei to.
7Ko nye de doa ná wora ka nena lanyerane nɔɔno kara ne. Tega kam ná nyɔge doa na bam, ye ka daare ka ke wodiiru lanyerane ka pa balo na dugi ka baŋa ne to, Wɛ wó swɛ tega kam konto swolim. 8Ko daare tega kam ná ke sabare de wo-korro yerane, ko bere we ka ye kafɛ mo ye ka maŋe se Wɛ mo sɔɔle-ka o yage. Ko kweelim nam ye se ba ma mini mo ba zwɛ-ka ba chɔge.
9De konto de, a badwoŋ-swonnu bam, abam wó taa gara. Amo yei we abam ta wo Wɛ chwoŋa wone á maa vei o tei se o jwoŋi abam. 10Wɛ ye chega tu mo. O nam bá swei á na maŋe á tɔge keim-laaro tei to. O ta bá swei á na jege o swono lanyerane, ye á toŋe á woli o nɔɔna bam ko ba ko yi zem maama to. 11Amo nam na tiini a lage kolo to mo ye se abam maama ta‑á yei á tete lanyerane de á na tɔge Wɛ tei to, se á laam vo á yi o tei ye á seene á na wo-laaro telo á na jege teena se á na to. 12Á yé pa se jawɔrɔ zo abam. Nam lwoni-na balo na fɔge ba zege de pu-dɛa ye ba jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ to. Banto laam wó ba ba jwoŋi wonnu telo Wɛ na pwooli we, o wó pa-ba to.
Wɛ kampwola bá fɔge ka leiri
13Faŋa faŋa to, Wɛ déem pwooli de Abaraham o we, omo wó fɔge‑o lanyerane. Wɛ na tiŋi o ni dem ded‑o konto to, o dugi de o tete mo, kolo ŋwaane woŋo tera ko na dwoi‑o se o ma du de-ko. 14Wɛ gwoni o ni dem ded‑o o we:
“Amo wó swɛ nmo swolim lanyerane
ye a pa se n dwi dem puli dedɛ.”
15Wɛ na dugi konto to, Abaraham déem ma vɔ pu-dɛa taa, ye o laam ba o na Wɛ na pwooli se o pa‑o kolo to.
16Ko ná ye nabiina ná yeini ba du duuri, ba wó ma wolo na dwoi ba tete to yere mo ba du, se ko bere we ba taane dem ye chega, se bwɛa daa ta tera. 17Ko ná ye Wɛ na pwooli kampwola de balo to, o lage se ba lɔre lanyerane we, o bá fɔge o yiri o ni dem. Konto ŋwaane mo o dugi duuri o woli de o kampwola kam. 18Kikia yanto yalei bá wane ya leiri ya ji vwa, ko na ye Wɛ tete kikia to ŋwaane. Konto ŋwaane mo debam balo na ke dé tete Wɛ jeŋa ne to wó tiini dé ke pu-dɛa ye dé ta jege teena ded‑o we, dé wó na wonnu telo o na tiŋi o pa debam to. 19Teena yam dé na jege Wɛ tei ne konto to tiini ya dana ye ya bá wane ya chɔge. Ya maa pae se dé boboŋa tigi jeiga dedoa, ye ya zo Wɛ tete jeiŋa jei mɛ na chege de gare-jale se nabiina yé zo to. 20Yezu nam maŋe o da yiga o zo jei sem konto se o pore chwoŋa mo o pa debam. Wonto mo jigi Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu se ko taa vei wuu, ne Melkizedeka déem na ye tei to.

english_text:
The Priestly Family of Melchizedek
1 Melchizedek was both king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He was the one who went out and gave Abraham his blessing, when Abraham returned from killing the kings. 2Then Abraham gave him a tenth of everything he had.
The meaning of the name Melchizedek is “King of Justice.” But since Salem means “peace,” he is also “King of Peace.” 3We are not told he had a father or mother or ancestors or beginning or end. He is like the Son of God and will be a priest forever.
4Notice how great Melchizedek was! Our famous ancestor Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had taken from his enemies. 5 The Law teaches that even Abraham's descendants must give a tenth of what they possess. And they are to give this to their own relatives, who are the descendants of Levi and are priests. 6Although Melchizedek wasn't a descendant of Levi, Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had. Then Melchizedek blessed Abraham, who had been given God's promise. 7Everyone agrees a person who gives a blessing is greater than the one who receives the blessing.
8Priests are given a tenth of what people earn. But all priests die, except Melchizedek, and the Scriptures teach that he is alive. 9Levi's descendants are now the ones who receive a tenth from people. We could even say that when Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth, Levi also gave him a tenth. 10This is because Levi was born later into the family of Abraham, who gave a tenth to Melchizedek.
11Even though the Law of Moses says the priests must be descendants of Levi, those priests cannot make anyone perfect. So there needs to be a priest like Melchizedek, rather than one from the priestly family of Aaron. 12And when the rules for selecting a priest are changed, the Law must also be changed.
13The person we are talking about is our Lord, who came from a tribe that had never had anyone to serve as a priest at the altar. 14Everyone knows he came from the tribe of Judah, and Moses never said priests would come from that tribe.
15All of this becomes clearer, when someone who is like Melchizedek is appointed to be a priest. 16That person wasn't appointed because of his ancestors, but because his life can never end. 17 The Scriptures say about him,
“You are a priest forever,
just like Melchizedek.”
18In this way a weak and useless command was put aside, 19because the Law cannot make anything perfect. At the same time, we are given a much better hope, and it can bring us close to God.
20-21 God himself made a promise when this priest was appointed. But he did not make a promise like this when the other priests were appointed. The promise he made is,
“I, the Lord, promise that you
will be a priest forever!
And I will never
change my mind!”
22This means that Jesus guarantees us a better agreement with God. 23There have been a lot of other priests, and all of them have died. 24But Jesus will never die, and so he will be a priest forever! 25He is forever able to save the people he leads to God, because he always lives to speak to God for them.
26Jesus is the high priest we need. He is holy and innocent and faultless, and not at all like us sinners. Jesus is honored above all beings in heaven, 27 and he is better than any other high priest. Jesus doesn't need to offer sacrifices each day for his own sins and then for the sins of the people. He offered a sacrifice once for all, when he gave himself. 28The Law appoints priests who have weaknesses. But God's promise, which came later than the Law, appoints his Son. And he is the perfect high priest forever.
translation_text:
Melkizedeka de Yezu memaŋa
1A laam lage a ta Melkizedeka taane dem a bere abam. Wonto déem ye Salem tiina pɛ mo ye o kwori o ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tu. Abaraham na wane pwa badwonna jara wone ye o laam jwoori maŋa kalo to mo Melkizedeka jeeri‑o chwoŋa ne o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o ke o yuu ne. 2Abaraham laam ma kwei nyɔɔre delo o na nɛ jara yam baŋa ne to o pɔɔre teiri delo na ye Melkizedeka nyem to o pa‑o. Melkizedeka yere dem kuri mo ye ‘Chega tu’. Ko woli da, o na ye Salem pɛ to, ko ta bere we o ye ‘Yazura pɛ’ mo. 3Debam nam wo nigi Melkizedeka kwo de o nu ŋwa, ye dé yeiri o kuri na bobo mɛ to. Dé maa yeiri o lora dɛ de o toone maŋa. Konto pa se o nye de Wɛ Bu wom, ye o ye Wɛ kaanem tu taa wuu.
4Boŋe-na á nii Melkizedeka déem na jege kamunim tei to. Konto ŋwaane mo debam nabaaro Abaraham déem le o nyɔɔre dem o na nɛ jara yam baŋa ne to o pa‑o. 5Ko ná ye balo na nwoŋi Levi dwi tiina wone ye ba kaane ba pa Wɛ to, Wɛ ni dem pɛ-ba chwoŋa se ba jwoŋi ba teiri wonnu ba dwonna Isarele tiina bam tei ne, ye ba maama maŋe ba ye Abaraham dwi tiina mo. 6Melkizedeka nam wo nwoŋi Levi dwi dem wone. De konto de, o jwoŋi o teiri wonnu Abaraham tete tei ne. O ma daare o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage Abaraham yuu ne, ye Abaraham nam ya mo ye wolo Wɛ na pwooli kampwola ded‑o to. 7Ko nam ba jege bobwea we, nɔɔno ná sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o pa o dwoŋi, wonto mo ye nɔn-kamunu o dwoi wodwoŋi wom.
8Levi dwi tiina bam déem yeini ba jwoŋi ba teiri wonnu mo, ye banto mo ye balo na bá lu toone jeŋa ne to. Wɛ tɔnɔ kom nam bere we, Melkizedeka ye wolo na ŋwe to mo ye o jwoŋi o teiri wonnu. 9-10Abaraham na pɔɔre Melkizedeka wonnu o pa‑o maŋa kalo to, ba ta wo loge Levi ye o nam wo o nabaaro Abaraham jana wone. Levi nam ye wolo dwi tiina na jege chwoŋa se ba jwoŋi ba teiri wonnu ba dwonna tei ne to mo. De konto de, ko nye de Levi tɔge Abaraham ŋwaane mo o pa Melkizedeka jwoŋi o teiri wonnu.
11Wɛ na tɔge Moses jeŋa o pa o nia yam Isarele tiina bam to, o nia yam konto de Levi dwi tiina kaanem dem tɔge ya woli daane mo. Dé yei we banto na yeini ba ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ tei to wo wane ko yi chega kam chekke. Ko ya ná seene ko ye chega, Wɛ ya bá kuri kaanem tu wodwoŋi wolo na dae Levi dwi tu to. Wɛ nam kuri wolo na ye kaanem tu ne Melkizedeka déem na ye tei, ye o wo nwoŋi Aron dwi dem wone. 12Wɛ na leiri o kaanem tu dwi konto to, ko jege se o nia yam de tɔge ya leiri mo. 13-14Memaŋa yanto maama nam tɛ dé Teiru Yezu taane mo. Dé yei we ba loge wonto Judah dwi tiina wone mo, ye o dae Levi dwi tu. O dwi dento wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo fɔge o ji Wɛ kaanem tu. Ko ná ye Wɛ nia yalo o na ke Moses jeŋa ne to, ya wo pɛ Judah dwi tiina chwoŋa se ba ji Wɛ kaanem tiina kɔtaa.
15Dé nam seene dé lɔre Wɛ na tiŋi chwo-doŋa tei to. Ko maa ye o kaanem tu Yezu laam na nwoŋi dwi-gaa wone, ye o nye de Melkizedeka déem na ye tei to. 16Yezu na jigi Wɛ kaanem tu tei to wo tɔge nabiina chullu ŋwaane, se ko tɔge o ŋwea kalo toone na ba jege dam ka baŋa ne to ŋwaane mo. 17Wɛ nam tage o taane o we:
“Nmo mo wó ta‑n ye amo kaanem tu taa wuu,
ne Melkizedeka faŋa faŋa na ye tei to.”
18-19Ko maa bere we, chwo-dwoŋa kam mo gwoni ka yage, bɛŋwaane nia yalo Wɛ na ke Moses jeŋa ne to ware ya pa kolokolo taa ye chega chekke. Ya maa ba jege dam se ya woli nɔɔna. Ko daare leile konto dé laam jege teena lanyerane de Wɛ na tiŋi chwo-laao kolo o pa debam, se dé ma wane dé tɔge-ka dé vo dé yi o tei.
20Wɛ nam dugi duuri o woli da. Levi dwi tiina nam na jigi o kaanem tiina to, o wo dugi duuri dem konto dwoŋi. 21Ko daare Yezu na jigi Wɛ kaanem tu to, Wɛ dugi duuri o ŋwaane, ye o ta ded‑o o we:
“Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo dugi a duuri
ye a bá fɔge a za a ni.
Nmo wó ta‑n ye amo kaanem tu taa wuu.”
22Wɛ na dugi duuri o pa Yezu konto to, ko bere we, o na ke ni-gwonim delo o pa debam to tiini de lana de dwoi o ni-dwoori dem, Yezu na zege dé kwaga ne to ŋwaane.
23Ko ná ye Levi dwi tiina bam, ba dedɛ déem yeini ba jiri Wɛ kaanem tiina. Toone nam na yeini de jaane-ba to, ko pɛ se ba daa ware ba toŋe Wɛ kaanem totoŋa yam. 24Ko daare Yezu mo jege ŋwea taa wuu, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa ba jege se o leiri o yuu ne o ji Wɛ kaanem tu. 25Konto to, o wae o jwoŋi balo na tɔge o ŋwaane ba vei Wɛ tei to o yaga, se kolokolo daa yé chɔge-ba, o na jege ŋwea maŋa maama ye o lwoori Wɛ o pa-ba to ŋwaane.
26Yezu na ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu tei to maŋe de debam boboŋa. O jege wo-pwoŋo de chega Wɛ yiga ne, ye tusim tera o tei ne. Wɛ ma pwɛ‑o nɔn-chechɔgero tei ne, ye o daare o zeiŋi‑o pa o zo o tei wɛyuu baŋa seeni. 27Ko ná ye Wɛ kaanem yiga tiina déem na ye tei to, dɛ maama ba yeini ba da yiga ba kaane Wɛ ba ma saare ba tete wɛleera, ye ba laam daare ba kaane Wɛ ba dwonna bam wɛleera ŋwaane. Yezu nam ba jege se o ke konto dwoŋi. Wonto kwei o tete mo o ma kaane Wɛ kuni bedwe yerane, ye konto jege kuri se ko taa vei wuu. 28Nia yalo Wɛ na ke Moses jeŋa ne to pae se nabiina mo taa jiri Wɛ kaanem yiga tiina ye ba bwona. Ko nam ná ye Wɛ ni-gwonim delo o na dugi duuri de ŋwaane to, dento laam mo leiri Moses nia yam yuu ne, ye de pa se Wɛ tete Bu wom ji o kaanem nakwe tu wolo na jege chega chekke se ko taa vei wuu to.

english_text:
A Better Promise
1 What I mean is we have a high priest who sits at the right side of God's great throne in heaven. 2He also serves as the priest in the most holy place inside the real tent there in heaven. This tent of worship was set up by the Lord, not by humans.
3Since all priests must offer gifts and sacrifices, Christ also needed to have something to offer. 4If he were here on earth, he would not be a priest at all, because here the Law appoints other priests to offer sacrifices. 5 But the tent where they serve is just a copy and a shadow of the real one in heaven. Before Moses made the tent, he was told, “Be sure to make it exactly like the pattern you were shown on the mountain!” 6Now Christ has been appointed to serve as a priest in a much better way, and he has given us much assurance of a better agreement.
7If the first agreement with God had been all right, there would not have been any need for another one. 8 But the Lord found fault with it and said,
“I tell you the time will come,
when I will make
a new agreement
with the people of Israel
and the people of Judah.
9It won't be like the agreement
that I made
with their ancestors,
when I took them by the hand
and led them out of Egypt.
They broke their agreement
with me,
and I stopped caring
about them!
10“But now I tell the people
of Israel
this is my new agreement:
‘The time will come
when I, the Lord,
will write my laws
on their minds and hearts.
I will be their God,
and they will be
my people.
11Not one of them
will have to teach another
to know me, their Lord.’
“All of them will know me,
no matter who they are.
12I will treat them with kindness,
even though they are wicked.
I will forget their sins.”
13When the Lord talks about a new agreement, he means that the first one is out of date. And anything that is old and useless will soon disappear.
translation_text:
Yezu tiini o zeini debam Wɛ ni-doore dem ŋwaane
1Taane dem maama wone de jei sento mo bere we, dé seene dé jege Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu wom konto dwoŋi. O ma na jeiŋa jei telaao ne Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ paare yituŋu kom jazem seeni. 2O maa wo Wɛ wara-jei sem ne mo o toŋa o pa‑o. Jei sem konto ye Baŋa Wɛ tete nyem chekke mo, ye ko dae logo baŋa vwei delo nabiina na pugi se ba taa zuli‑o da to.
3Wolo maama na ye Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu to mae vara de pɛɛra dwi dwi mo o kaane Wɛ. Debam Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu Yezu de nam maŋe se o taa jege kolo o na wó kwei o ke Wɛ jeŋa ne to mo. 4O nam ba jege se o taa wo logo baŋa ne se o kwei woŋo o ma kaane Wɛ. Wɛ kaanem tiina maŋe ba wo logo baŋa ne, ye ba kwei pɛɛra ba ke Wɛ jeŋa ne, se ko maŋe de Moses nia yam na bere tei to. 5Banto na yeini ba toŋe ba pa Wɛ tei to ye ba lwoni totoŋa yalo na ye chekke to mo. Ba na toŋe mɛ to ye lunluŋu mo ko bere kolo na wo telaao ne ye ko ye chekke to na ye tei. Konto to, Moses déem na lage o pu Wɛ wara-vwei dem to, Wɛ déem bere‑o o na wó ke tei ye o we, “Kwaane n ke wonnu tem maama se te lwoni amo na maŋe a bere‑m peo kom yuu ne tei to.”
6Ko daare leile konto, Yezu na toŋe o pa Wɛ tei to tiini ko jege kuri lanyerane ko dwoi kaanem tiina bam totoŋa maama. Ko nam ye bedwe mo de ni-gwonim delo Wɛ na tɔge Yezu ŋwaane o ke o pa debam to na dwoi da-yiga ni-gwonim dem na ye tei to, de na tɔge o kampwola kam na tiini ka lana to ŋwaane mo. 7Da-yiga ni-gwonim delo Wɛ na ke o pa o nɔɔna to ya ná ba jege gɛɛre, ni dedwoŋi ya daa bá wane de leiri dento yuu ne. 8Ko nam na ye tei to, Wɛ déem bere we gɛɛre wora, ye o ta de o nɔɔna o we:
“Maŋa lage ka yi se amo jwoori a gwoni ni
de Isarele dwi tiina bam de Judah dwi tiina bam,
se ko taa ye amo ni-doore.
9Dento nam bá taa ye bedwe de ni delo a déem na gwoni de ba nabaara bam
maŋa kam a na mɛ a jeŋa a ja-ba a nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom wone to.
Banto déem wo sɛ ba tɔge amo ni-gwonim dem konto.
Ko ma pa a yiga daa tere ba wone.
10Maŋa kam ná yia, ni delo amo na wó gwoni de Isarele dwi tiina bam to mo tento:
Amo wó kwei a nia yam a tiŋi ba boboŋa ne mo,
ye a daare a popone-ya a yage ba bochara wone.
Amo maa wó taa ye ba Tu Wɛ wom,
se ba de taa ye amo nɔɔna.
11Ba wolowolo daa ba jege se o bere o dwonna,
naa se o ta de o chorro we, ba lɔre Baŋa Wɛ.
Kolo ŋwaane ba maama wó taa yei amo, ko ná maŋe ko ye nabwona de dedɛɛra de.
12Maŋa kam konto ne amo wó duri ba ŋwaŋa
de ba keim-lwanno tem.
A daa bá guli ba wɛleera yam gula.”
Mo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei.
13Wɛ na ŋɔɔne o ni-doore dem taane konto dwoŋi to, ko bere we o da-yiga ni dem laam jigi ni-dwoori mo. Ko maa bere we dento daa ba jege kuri, ye de da yam lage ya kɛ.

english_text:
The Tent in Heaven
1The first promise included rules for worship and a tent for worship here on earth. 2 The first part of the tent was called the holy place, and a lampstand, a table, and the sacred loaves of bread were kept there.
3 Behind the curtain was the most holy place. 4 The gold altar for burning incense was in this holy place. The gold-covered sacred chest was also there, and inside it were three things. First, there was a gold jar filled with manna. Then there was Aaron's walking stick that sprouted. Finally, there were the flat stones with the Ten Commandments written on them. 5 On top of the chest were the glorious creatures with wings opened out above the place of mercy.
Now isn't the time to go into detail about these things. 6 But this is how everything was when the priests went each day into the first part of the tent to do their duties. 7 However, only the high priest could go into the second part of the tent, and he went in only once a year. Each time he carried blood to offer for his sins and for any sins that the people had committed without meaning to.
8All of this is the Holy Spirit's way of saying no one could enter the most holy place while the tent was still the place of worship. 9This also has a meaning for today. It shows we cannot make our consciences clear by offering gifts and sacrifices. 10These rules are merely about such things as eating and drinking and ceremonies for washing ourselves. And rules about physical things will last only until the time comes to change them for something better.
11 Christ came as the high priest of the good things that are now here. He also went into a much better tent that wasn't made by humans and that doesn't belong to this world. 12Then Christ went once for all into the most holy place and freed us from sin forever. He did this by offering his own blood instead of the blood of goats and bulls.
13 According to the Law of Moses, those people who become unclean are not fit to worship God. Yet they will be considered clean, if they are sprinkled with the blood of goats and bulls and with the ashes of a sacrificed calf. 14But Christ was sinless, and he offered himself as an eternal and spiritual sacrifice to God. This is why his blood is much more powerful and makes our consciences clear. Now we can serve the living God and no longer do things that lead to death.
15Christ died to rescue those who had sinned and broken the old agreement. Now he brings his chosen ones a new agreement with its guarantee of God's eternal blessings! 16In fact, making an agreement of this kind is like writing a will. This is because the one who makes the will must die before it is of any use. 17In other words, a will doesn't go into effect as long as the one who made it is still alive.
18Blood was also used to put the first agreement into effect. 19 Moses told the people all the Law said they must do. Then he used red wool and a hyssop plant to sprinkle the people and the book of the Law with the blood of bulls and goats and with water. 20He told the people, “With this blood God makes his agreement with you.” 21 Moses also sprinkled blood on the tent and on everything else used in worship. 22 The Law says that almost everything must be sprinkled with blood, and no sins can be forgiven unless blood is offered.
Christ's Great Sacrifice
23These things are only copies of what is in heaven, and so they had to be made holy by these ceremonies. But the real things in heaven must be made holy by something better. 24This is why Christ did not go into a tent made by humans and was only a copy of the real one. Instead, he went into heaven and is now there with God to help us.
25Christ did not have to offer himself many times. He wasn't like a high priest who goes into the most holy place each year to offer the blood of an animal. 26If he had offered himself every year, he would have suffered many times since the creation of the world. But instead, near the end of time he offered himself once and for all, so he could be a sacrifice that does away with sin.
27We die only once, and then we are judged. 28 So Christ died only once to take away the sins of many people. But when he comes again, it will not be to take away sin. He will come to save everyone who is waiting for him.
translation_text:
Logo baŋa wara-vwei dem taane
1A lage a ta da-yiga ni-gwonim dem taane mo. De déem jege chullu telo na bere nɔɔna ba na wó taa zuli Wɛ tei o wara-jei selo na wo logo baŋa ne to wone mo. 2Wɛ wara-vwei dem konto wo nam pɔɔre di selei mo. De kwaga diga kam yere mo ‘Wɛ di-yuu kom’, ye ka jege min-zwon-zego kom. Tabolo de maa wora ye bworobwooru telo na ye Wɛ nyem to maa tigi ko baŋa ne. 3Di-yun-gala de maa wora, ka na tiini ka ye wose Wɛ ŋwaane to mo, ye gare-jale pale de gare de che-ka. 4Sabu-seŋa Wɛ kaanem dakaa maa zege da, ba na zwɛ wonnu telo lwom na ywomma to ka baŋa ne ba pa‑o. Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam de maa wora ba na mɛ sabu-seŋa ba ma kwoli-ka. Ka wo kom maa jege sabu-seŋa zoŋa kalo de wo na jege wodiu kolo yere na ye ‘Manna’ to. Nacheiga kalo na ye Aron nyem ye ka déem puli vɔɔro to de maa wora Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam wone, ko woli de kandwa-pelɛ selei Wɛ nia fuga kam na popone se baŋa ne to. 5Dakaa kam baŋa maa ye jeiga kalo Wɛ na saare nabiina wɛleera mɛ to. Ba déem ma ke cherubi selei nyenyero ba zege da. Se maa bere Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom ye se vɔna yam kwoli dakaa kam baŋa.
Ko nam daa dae se dé ŋɔɔne wonnu tem konto taane dedɛ.
6Wara-vwei dem de de wonnu tem na wora konto to, Wɛ kaanem tiina bam yeini ba zo de kwaga diga kam dɛ maama mo se ba toŋe ba totoŋa yalo na pae Wɛ jege zula to. 7Ko nam ná ye di-yun-gala kam, Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu wom yerane mo jege chwoŋa se o zo ka wo bedwe bene maama wone. Wonto nam ná lage o zo, o wó kwei vara jana mo o ja zo se o ma kaane Wɛ, se ko saare o tete wɛleera, se ko daare ko saare tusim kikia yalo o dwonna nabiina na ke ye ba yeiri ya ni ne to.
8Wɛ Sin-laao kom laam mae kikia yam konto maama na ye tei to mo ko bere debam we, chwoŋa déem ya tera se nɔɔna wane ba zo Wɛ di-yun-gala kam. Vwei dem dedaane de kwaga diga kam maama ta na zege to bere we di-yun-gala kam ni ta wo pore mo. 9Ko maa ye maana mo ko bere debam zem se dé lɔre Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem na ye tei to. Ko bere we vara de pɛɛra yalo maama nabiina na kwei ba ma kaane Wɛ to bá wane ya zeini wolo na kwei-ya o ma zuli Wɛ to se ya pa o bochare kwɛ fase Wɛ seeni. 10Kaanem kikia yanto dwoŋi jege kuri logo baŋa seeni yerane mo, ko ná ye wodiu dim, naa bochare digiru zarem ŋwaane. Ya maama tɔge nabiina chullu mo, ye ya jege kuri se ko taa vei maŋa kam Wɛ na wó fɔge o tiŋi o chwo-doŋa kam to.
Yezu Krista jana bam taane
11Wɛ laam tiŋi o chwo-doŋa kam mo de Yezu Krista na tu o ba o ji o kaanem nakwe tu debam ŋwaane to. Ko ma pa dé jwoŋi o ŋwe-doŋa wo-laaro telo na maŋe te wora to. Yezu na zo Wɛ tei debam ŋwaane to, ko ye Wɛ sɔŋɔ chekke mo o zoa, ye konto tiini ko lana ko dwoi logo baŋa vwei dem. O na zo mɛ to dae vwei delo nabiina na pugi to. 12O ma vo o zo Wɛ tete di-yun-gala kam. Ko ye bedwe yerane mo o zoa, ye o laam wora taa wuu. O nam wo kwei bone naa na-bale jana o ja zo se o ma kaane Wɛ. Ko maa ye o tete jana mo o mɛ o ŋwe debam wɛleera jene, ye o jwoŋi debam o ke Wɛ jeŋa ne se ko taa vei wuu. 13Wɛ ni-dwoori dem bere we, nɔɔno wolo bochare ná jege digiru, ba jege se ba kwei bone jana naa na-bale jana ba gwaane de na-chwɛ delo ba na zwɛ to tentwarem mo ba ma mi nɔɔno wom yera. Keim dem konto mo yeini de zare o yera digiru tem ye de daare de fɔge‑o Wɛ chwoŋa wone. 14Ko na ye konto to, Yezu na tega ye o jana nwoŋi to, ko bá tiini ko fɔge nɔɔna bochara mo na? O ma tɔge Wɛ Jworo kom na wo o tei ne taa wuu to baŋa o ji kaanem delo na lana fase to o ke o pa Wɛ. O na kaane Wɛ debam ŋwaane konto to, ko wae ko pae dé bochara taa lana fase, pa se dé boboŋa daa yé zo wo-yɔɔro kikia, ye dé daare dé zuli Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ.
15Konto ŋwaane Yezu mo ye wolo Wɛ na dɛ o ŋwaane o gwoni ni-doore de o nɔɔna bam to. O na mɛ o toone o ŋwe nabiina wɛleera jene to, o wae o jwoŋi-ba de ba na ke kolo ba chɔge Wɛ da-yiga ni-gwonim dem to. Konto ŋwaane balo maama Wɛ na kuri se ba taa ye o bia to wae ba jwoŋi o ŋwe-doŋa kam de ka wo-laaro tem maama, ne o na pwooli se o pa-ba tei to.
16-17Ko nye de nɔɔno na gwoni o ni o bere se, o ná tega o daare, ba na wó pɔɔre o wonnu tei to. O ta ná ŋwe, o ni dem konto ba jege bu. Nɔɔna nam ná lɔre we o tega, ba laam wó pɔɔre o wonnu tem se ko maŋe de o ni dem na tage tei to. 18Konto ŋwaane mo, Wɛ na ke da-yiga ni-gwonim dem o pa o nɔɔna to, ba kwei varem jana mo ba ma bere we, o ni dem jege bu. 19Ko déem na ke to, Moses bobo o tɔɔle Wɛ nia yam maama o bere Isarele tiina bam maama. O laam ma kwei na-bale de bone delo ba na go to jana o gwaane de na, ye o daare o ma o mi tɔnɔ kolo Wɛ nia yam na popone da to. O laam ma mi Isarele tiina bam maama yera ne. O kwei Husopa tio daa, ye o vɔ gare-ŋon-seŋa ka yuu ne o lu jana bam wone o ma mi wonnu tem, de nɔɔna bam maama. 20O déem na yeini o ke konto dwoŋi to mo o tage we, “Jana banto bere we Wɛ ni-gwonim dem jege bu, o na tage abam se á tɔge-de to.”
21Moses daa ta ma kwei jana bam o ke konto dwoŋi o ma mi vwei dem de wonnu telo maama na wora Wɛ zula ŋwaane to. 22Ko ye chega mo we, Wɛ nia yalo o na ke Moses jeŋa ne to bere we nɔɔna jege se ba kwei varem jana mo ba ma zare ba wonnu Wɛ ŋwaane. Ko ye nenɛɛne wonnu maama jege se te zare konto mo. Ko ta woli da, toone jana ná tera, Wɛ bá yage nɔɔna wɛleera o ma chɛ-ba.
23Logo baŋa vwei dem wonnu telo na wora ye te lwoni Wɛ telaao wonnu chekke na ye tei to jege se te zare de vara jana mo konto dwoŋi. Ko daare Wɛ telaao wonnu tem tete na wó fɔge te kwɛ tei to, ko fe mo se ba kaane Wɛ se ko taa dwoi faŋa kaanem dem na ye tei to. 24Yezu Krista nam na zo Wɛ tei to, ko dae wara-vwei delo nabiina na pugi ye de lwoni Wɛ sɔŋɔ chekke to mo o zoa. O nam seene o zo Wɛ tei telaao ne mo chekke. O maa wo dáane o zege Wɛ yiga ne debam zeinim ŋwaane. 25O na zo Wɛ tei chekke konto to, o zo kuni bedwe mo, ko dae bene maama wone, nenɛɛne Wɛ kaanem yiga tiina déem na ke tei to. Banto yeini ba kwei vara jana mo ba ja zo Wɛ di-yun-gala kam, ko dae ba tete jana. 26Yezu ya ná jege se o kwei o tete o ma kaane Wɛ bene maama wone, o ya wó yaare o te kuni dedɛ, ko zege logo baŋa boboa ne ko ba ko yi zem. Ko nam na ye tei to, o laam tu o veere o tete nabiina tetare ne mo logo baŋa kweelim da yam ne. O tu bedwe mo ye o ba o te o kaane Wɛ se ko pa nabiina wɛleera saare se ko taa vei wuu. 27Ko nye de nɔɔno maama na jege se o te bedwe tei to, se o laam vo Wɛ tei ye o di o taane. 28Yezu Krista de nam tu o te o ma kaane Wɛ bedwe mo, se o wane o le nɔɔna dedɛ wɛleera o yage. O nam ta wó jwoori o ba logo baŋa, ye ko bá taa ye nɔɔna wɛleera saarem ŋwaane. Ko ye se o jwoŋi balo na jege o teena se o ba to o yage mo.

english_text:
1The Law of Moses is like a shadow of the good things to come. This shadow isn't the good things themselves, because it cannot free people from sin by the sacrifices offered year after year. 2If there were worshipers who already have their sins washed away and their consciences made clear, there would not be any need to go on offering sacrifices. 3-4But the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins. It only reminds people of their sins from one year to the next.
5 When Christ came into the world, he said to God,
“Sacrifices and offerings
are not what you want,
but you have given me
my body.
6No, you are not pleased
with animal sacrifices
and offerings for sin.”
7Then Christ said,
“And so, my God,
I have come to do
what you want,
as the Scriptures say.”
8The Law teaches that offerings and sacrifices must be made because of sin. But why did Christ mention these things and say that God did not want them? 9Well, it was to do away with offerings and sacrifices and to replace them. This is what he meant by saying to God, “I have come to do what you want.” 10So we are made holy because Christ obeyed God and offered himself once for all.
11 The priests do their work each day, and they keep on offering sacrifices that can never take away sins. 12 But Christ offered himself as a sacrifice that is good forever. Now he is sitting at God's right side, 13and he will stay there until his enemies are put under his power. 14By his one sacrifice he has forever set free from sin the people he brings to God.
15The Holy Spirit also speaks of this by telling us that the Lord said,
16 “When the time comes,
I will make an agreement
with them.
I will write my laws
on their minds and hearts.
17 Then I will forget
about their sins
and no longer remember
their evil deeds.”
18When sins are forgiven, there is no more need to offer sacrifices.
Encouragement and Warning
19My friends, the blood of Jesus gives us courage to enter the most holy place 20by a new way that leads to life! And this way takes us through the curtain that is Christ himself.
21We have a great high priest who is in charge of God's house. 22 So let's come near God with pure hearts and a confidence that comes from having faith. Let's keep our hearts pure, our consciences free from evil, and our bodies washed with clean water. 23We must hold tightly to the hope we say is ours. After all, we can trust the one who made the agreement with us. 24We should keep on encouraging each other to be thoughtful and to do helpful things. 25Some people have given up the habit of meeting for worship, but we must not do that. We should keep on encouraging each other, especially since you know that the day of the Lord's coming is getting closer.
26No sacrifices can be made for people who decide to sin after they find out about the truth. 27 They are God's enemies, and all they can look forward to is a terrible judgment and a furious fire. 28 If two or more witnesses accused someone of breaking the Law of Moses, that person could be put to death. 29 But it is much worse to dishonor God's Son and to disgrace the blood of the promise that made us holy. And it is just as bad to insult the Holy Spirit, who shows us mercy. 30 We know that God has said he will punish and take revenge. We also know that the Scriptures say the Lord will judge his people. 31It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
32Don't forget all the hard times you went through when you first received the light. 33Sometimes you were abused and mistreated in public, and at other times you shared in the sufferings of others. 34You were kind to people in jail. And you gladly let your possessions be taken away, because you knew you had something better, something that would last forever.
35Keep on being brave! It will bring you great rewards. 36Learn to be patient, so you will please God and be given what he has promised. 37 As the Scriptures say,
“God is coming soon!
It won't be very long.
38The people God accepts
will live because
of their faith.
But he isn't pleased
with anyone
who turns back.”
39We are not like those people who turn back and get destroyed. We will keep on having faith until we are saved.
translation_text:
Yezu kaanem dem jege kuri taa wuu
1Ko ná ye Wɛ nia yalo o na ke Moses jeŋa ne to, ya lage ya bere wo-laaro tem de na wó jwoŋi Wɛ tei ne to na ye tei to mo. Ya nam ye lunluŋu yerane mo, ye ya dae bedwe de Wɛ telaao wonnu tem tete. Ya pae se nɔɔna jwoori ba kaane Wɛ bene maama wone se ko taa vei wuu. Konto ŋwaane, ya bá wane ya pa se balo na tɔge ya ŋwaane ba zuli Wɛ to bochara taa jege chega chekke. 2Wɛ nia yam ya ná wae ya pae balo na zuli‑o to wɛleera saare ya tia, ba ya daa bá lɔre we ba wɛleera ta wo ba yuu ne, ye ba ya bá boŋe se ba jwoori ba daa kaane Wɛ konto dwoŋi. 3Ba nam na jege se ba daa kaane Wɛ bene maama wone to pae se ba jwoori ba guli we ba wɛleera yam ta wo ba yuu ne mo. 4Kokuri nabiina wɛleera bá wane ya saare de na-bale de bone jana kɔtaa.
5Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo Yezu déem na lage o ba logo baŋa maŋa kalo to, o tage de o Kwo Wɛ o we:
