“Nmo yiga tera de nabiina na yeini ba kwei vara de wodiiru
ba ma ke kaanem ba pa‑m tei to.
Nmo nam ke nabiinu yera mo n pa-ne.
6Ko ná ye vara zwɛɛm kaanem de wɛleera saarem kaanem,
ba kikia yam konto maama wo su nmo yi.
7Amo maa we,
‘Amo Kwo Wɛ, nii-ne da!
Amo tu se a toŋe nmo boboŋa na lage tei to,
ne ko na maŋe ko popone amo taane
nmo faŋa faŋa tɔnɔ kom ne tei to.’ ”
8Yezu maŋe o da yiga o ta de o Kwo Wɛ o we, “Nmo yiga tera de nɔɔna na yeini ba kwei wonnu ba ma kaane‑m tei to maama, nenɛɛne ko ná ye vara zwɛɛm kaanem naa wɛleera saarem kaanem. Kaanem dwi dem konto wo su nmo yi.” De konto de, nɔɔna na kaane Wɛ konto to maama tɔge o ni-dwoora yam na bere tei to mo. 9O laam ma daare o ta o we, “Amo Kwo Wɛ, nii-ne da! Amo tu se a ke nmo boboŋa na lage tei to.” Konto bere we Wɛ saare o da-yiga vara kaanem ni dem o yage, ye o daare o tiŋi chwo-doŋa se nɔɔna tɔge-ka. 10Chwo-doŋa kam nam tɔge Yezu Krista na ke o Kwo Wɛ boboŋa yam maama ye o kwei o tete yera o ma kaane‑o to mo. O ke konto bedwe yerane, ye ko jege kuri taa wuu, se ko pa dé taa ye wose mo Wɛ yiga ne.
11Logo baŋa kaanem tiina maama yeini ba jege se ba taa vei Wɛ yiga maŋa maama ba goe vara ba maa kaane‑o. Ba maa yeini ba ke konto dwoŋi dɛ maama ka, ye ba kikia yam konto ware ya saare wɛleera kɔtaa. 12Ko nam ná ye Yezu, wonto kwei o tete o ma kaane Wɛ bedwe yerane mo, ye ko jege kuri taa wuu se ko jwoŋi nɔɔna ba wɛleera wone. O na ke konto o ti to, o laam ma vo o jeini Baŋa Wɛ jazem seeni, 13ye o ta wora o cheigi maŋa kalo Wɛ na wó wane o dona maama o ke o dam kuri ne to. 14Kolo ŋwaane o kaane Wɛ kuni bedwe se ko pa nɔɔna balo o na wora o kwɛ ba bochara to taa ye wose se ko taa vei wuu.
15Ko woli da, Wɛ Sin-laao kom de zege wonnu tem konto chega kam kwaga ne o bere debam. Baŋa Wɛ déem dɛ ko baŋa o we:
16“Maŋa kam ná yia, ni delo amo na wó gwoni de a nɔɔna bam to mo tento:
Amo wó kwei a nia yam a tiŋi ba bochara ne mo,
ye a daare a popone-ya a yage ba boboŋa ne.”
17Wɛ ma daare o ta o we,
“Amo daa bá guli ba wɛleera de ba tusim kikia yam gula kɔtaa.”
18Wɛ na dɛ chwoŋa kam konto o yage dé keim-balwaaro tem o ma chɛ debam to, ko daa ba jege kuri se nabiina go vara ba ma kaane‑o ba wɛleera saarem ŋwaane.
Dé wó taa jege baare de Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem
19A nu-bia bam, dé laam nɛ baare se dé zo Wɛ di-yun-gala kam na ye o swono jeiga to, Yezu Krista toone jana bam ŋwaane. 20Wonto nam pore chwo-doŋa o pa debam, ye kanto mo pae ŋwea. Ka maa tɔge gare-jale dem laŋa ka zoore Wɛ tei chekke. Kokuri mo ka tɔge Yezu yera yam ŋwaane, de o na kwei-ya o ma kaane Wɛ tei to mo. 21Konto to, debam jege wolo na seene o ye Wɛ kaanem tu chekke ye o nii Wɛ tete sɔŋɔ tiina baŋa ne to. 22Konto ŋwaane, pa-na se dé fofɔ de yi Wɛ tei de boboŋ-ŋona, de baare delo na bere we dé jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ to. Wɛ fɔge dé bochara pa se dé daa ba boŋa we, dé wɛleera ta wo dé yuu ne, ye dé yera na zarem de na-ŋona. Konto ŋwaane mo dé jege baare se dé zo Wɛ tei. 23Pa-na se dé bere we, dé jege teena Wɛ tei ne ye bobwea tera. O nam tiŋi o ni o pa debam, ye o bá fɔge o kwane-de. 24Pa-na se dé taa yei da-ni ne, se dé taa zeini daane, ye dé jege da-swono, ye dé ke keim-laaro. 25Á yé pa se dé yage ka-taa-gilimi-daane Wɛ zula ŋwaane, ne badaara na ke tei to. Nam kwaane-na se á woli daane se ko pa á yera poore. Á na lɔre we dé Teiru wom dɛ dem lage de yi to, se á tiini á ta‑á ke konto.
26Nɔɔno ná lɔre Wɛ chega kam ye o ke-ka o boboŋa ne, ye o ta ná yeini o paale o ke o tusa, kaanem daa bá taa wora de na wó pa kotu wɛleera yam saare. 27Ko laam daare se foone mo taa jege‑o de Wɛ na lage o ke‑o tei to. Wɛ ná di o taane, o laam wó na chɔgem ye o zo min-fɔrɔ kolo na wó chɔge balo maama na done Wɛ to. 28Ko ná ye Wɛ nia yalo o na ke Moses jeŋa ne to, nɔɔno wolo ná yaale-ya, ye nɔɔna balei naa batɔ ná lɔge o kwaga ne, ba wó go konto tu ye ŋwaŋa bá taa wora. 29Ko daare nɔɔno ná yaale Wɛ tete Bu wom, konto tu chɔgem dem bá tiini de gaale na? Konto tu pae se Yezu jana balo Wɛ na dɛ ba ŋwaane o gwoni o ni dem to ye wo-yɔɔ mo. Ko nam ye jana bam konto mo Wɛ mɛ o le tusim kotu bochare ne. Ko woli da, konto tu ta twe Wɛ Sin-laao kom na jege Wɛ zaane ko pae nɔɔna tei to mo. Konto to, o bá tiini o na waarem na? 30Kokuri debam maŋe dé yei wolo wom na tage o we:
“Amo mo wó jwoori a ŋwe ba keim-balwaaro jene,
se ba na kolo na maŋe de-ba to.”
Ko ta popone we:
“Baŋa Wɛ wó di o nɔɔna bam bora.”
31Nɔɔno ná ke o tusi, ye Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ná zo‑o, ko wó tiini ko taa ye lɛɛro ko pa‑o.
32Nam guli-na á yia déem na tu ya poore de Wɛ chega kam ye kolo ke abam to. Á déem yaare dedɛ, ye cham dem wo wane abam, á na vɔge pu-dɛa to ŋwaane. 33Maŋa kadwoŋi ne ba yeini ba twe abam nɔɔna yiga ne, ye ba bɛɛse abam. Maŋa kadwoŋi ne de, á yeini á sɛ se á tɔge á woli balo de na nɛ yaara konto dwoŋi to. 34Kokuri á tɔge á na yaara de balo na wo peena diga ne to. Nɔɔna maa yeini ba vere abam wonnu ye á sɛ de wopwolo, kolo ŋwaane á yei we, á maŋe á jege kolo na tiini ko lana ye ko wó taa ye abam nyem taa wuu to.
35Á nam yé yage á na jege baare tei to. Kokuri de lage de pa á na nyɔɔre dedɛ Wɛ tei ne. 36Á jege se á zege lanyerane de pu-dɛa, se á wane á ke Wɛ boboŋa na lage tei to, se á daare á jwoŋi wo-laaro telo o na pwooli se o pa abam to. 37Wɛ kwora mo ye:
“Ko laam daare fee
se wolo na lage o ba to laam ba.
O nam bá dáane.
38Wolo nam na jege chega amo tei ne to
wó na ŋwea o wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane.
Konto tu nam ná kɔre foone ye o jwoori o kwaga,
o kikia bá su amo yi.”
39Debam nam tɔge dé dae balo na jwoori ba kwaga pa se ba na chɔgem to. Dé tɔge dé wo balo na ke ba wo-dedoa de Wɛ pa se ba jwoŋi ba ŋwea to wone mo.

english_text:
The Great Faith of God's People
1Faith makes us sure of what we hope for and gives us proof of what we cannot see. 2 It was their faith that made our ancestors pleasing to God.
3 Because of our faith, we know that the world was made at God's command. We also know that what can be seen was made out of what cannot be seen.
4 Because Abel had faith, he offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. God was pleased with him and his gift, and even though Abel is now dead, his faith still speaks for him.
5 Enoch had faith and did not die. He pleased God, and God took him up to heaven. This is why his body was never found. 6But without faith no one can please God. We must believe that God is real and rewards everyone who searches for him.
7 Because Noah had faith, he was warned about something that had not yet happened. He obeyed and built a boat that saved him and his family. In this way the people of the world were judged, and Noah was given the blessings that come to everyone who pleases God.
8 Abraham had faith and obeyed God. He was told to go to the land that God had said would be his, and he left for a country he had never seen. 9 Because Abraham had faith, he lived as a stranger in the promised land. He lived there in a tent, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who were later given the same promise. 10Abraham did this, because he was waiting for the eternal city God had planned and built.
11 Even when Sarah was too old to have children, she had faith that God would do what he had promised, and she had a son. 12 Her husband Abraham was almost dead, but he became the ancestor of many people. In fact, there are as many of them as there are stars in the sky or grains of sand along the seashore.
13 Every one of those people died. But they still had faith, even though they had not received what they had been promised. They were glad just to see these things from far away, and they agreed that they were only strangers and foreigners on this earth. 14When people talk this way, it is clear they are looking for a place to call their own. 15If they had been talking about the land where they had once lived, they could have gone back at any time. 16But they were looking forward to a better home in heaven. This is why God wasn't ashamed for them to call him their God. He even built a city for them.
17-18 Abraham had been promised that Isaac, his only son, would continue his family. But when Abraham was tested, he had faith and was willing to sacrifice Isaac, 19because he was sure that God could raise people to life. This was just like getting Isaac back from death.
20 Isaac had faith, and he promised blessings to Jacob and Esau. 21 Later, when Jacob was about to die, he leaned on his walking stick and worshiped. Then because of his faith he blessed each of Joseph's sons. 22 And right before Joseph died, he had faith that God would lead the people of Israel out of Egypt. So he told them to take his bones with them.
23 Because Moses' parents had faith, they kept him hidden until he was three months old. They saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid to disobey the king's orders. 24 Then after Moses grew up, his faith made him refuse to be called the king's grandson. 25 He chose to be mistreated with God's people instead of having the good time that sin could bring for a little while. 26Moses knew that the treasures of Egypt were not as wonderful as what he would receive from suffering for the Messiah, and he looked forward to his reward.
27Because of his faith, Moses left Egypt. Moses had seen the invisible God and wasn't afraid of the king's anger. 28 His faith also made him celebrate Passover. He sprinkled the blood of animals on the doorposts, so that the first-born sons of the people of Israel would not be killed by the destroying angel.
29 Because of their faith, the people walked through the Red Sea on dry land. But when the Egyptians tried to do it, they were drowned.
30 God's people had faith, and when they had walked around the city of Jericho for seven days, its walls fell down.
31 Rahab had been a prostitute, but she had faith and welcomed the spies. So she wasn't killed with the people who disobeyed.
32 What else can I say? There isn't enough time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets. 33 Their faith helped them conquer kingdoms, and because they did right, God made promises to them. They closed the jaws of lions 34 and put out raging fires and escaped from the swords of their enemies. Although they were weak, they were given the strength and power to chase foreign armies away.
35 Some women received their loved ones back from death. Many of these people were tortured, but they refused to be released. They were sure they would get a better reward when the dead are raised to life. 36 Others were made fun of and beaten with whips, and some were chained in jail. 37 Still others were stoned to death or sawed in two or killed with swords. Some had nothing but sheep skins or goat skins to wear. They were poor, mistreated, and tortured. 38The world did not deserve these good people, who had to wander in deserts and on mountains and had to live in caves and holes in the ground.
39All of them pleased God because of their faith! But still they died without being given what had been promised. 40This was because God had something better in store for us. And he did not want them to reach the goal of their faith without us.
translation_text:
Wo-dedoa de Wɛ na pae nɔɔna ye tei to
1Nmo ná jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ, kokuri mo n yei lanyerane we, nmo wó seene n na wonnu telo n teena na tɔge to. Ko maa wó pa se n lɔre we, wonnu telo n na ba nae de n yia to seene te wora. 2Ko ná ye balo na maŋe ba da Wɛ chwoŋa faŋa faŋa to, ko ye ba na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se ba yere zaŋe.
3Ko ye debam de na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pae dé lɔre we, Wɛ mɛ o ni taane mo o ke logo baŋa de wɛyuu maama. Konto mo dé sɛ we Wɛ kwei wonnu telo na ba nae de yia to o ma ke telo na wora ye dé wae dé nae de yia to.
Abel
4Faŋa faŋa to ko ye Abel na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se o na kwei kolo o ma kaane Wɛ to dwoni Kain na kaane Wɛ tei to. O wo-dedoa kam mo pɛ se o yere zaŋe de o na ye chega tu Wɛ tei ne to, o pɛɛra yam na su Wɛ yi to ŋwaane. O daa tera, ye o wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane nam pae se o taane ta wora.
Enoki
5Enoki de na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se Wɛ le‑o logo baŋa ne ye toone wo jaane‑o. Wɛ na le‑o konto to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa wo nɛ o jei. Konto ta na wo ke to, o maŋe o jege yere de o na pwoli Wɛ wo tei to. 6Kokuri nɔɔno ná ba jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ, o bá wane o pa se Wɛ wo pwoli. Wolo maama na boŋe se o ke o tete Wɛ jeŋa ne to, ko fe mo se konto tu taa jege wo-dedoa o sɛ we, Wɛ seene o wora ye o zeini balo na lage se ba lɔre‑o to.
Noah
7Noah de déem na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se o sɛ Wɛ ni delo o na tage ded‑o to. Wɛ déem kaane‑o de kolo na lage ko ba ko ke ye nabiina yia ta wo nɛ-ko to. O na kɔre Wɛ to, o ma sɛ o kwaare nabwor-kamunu se o ma jwoŋi o sɔŋɔ tiina ŋwea. O keim dem konto ma bere we, nabiina balo na wo sɛ Wɛ ni to ba jege bora. Wonto tete nam nɛ chega Wɛ tei ne, ne Wɛ na yeini o ke o pa balo na sɛ‑o de ba wo-dedoa to tei.
Abaraham
8Abaraham déem na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se o nwoŋi o tete teo kom ne o vo jeiga kalo Wɛ na pwooli we, o wó pa‑o se o dwi tiina taa tei taa to. Wɛ na bwoŋi‑o we o nwoŋi konto to, o ma seene o sɛ se o vo, ye o ta yeiri jei sem o na lage o vo to. 9O wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane mo pɛ se o vo o zoore jei sem konto ne, ne o ye veiru mo tei. O déem zoore vwei wone mo. Izaak de Jakob de maa tɔge ba zoore da konto dwoŋi, ye Wɛ ya pwooli kampwola o pa banto de. 10Ko bere we, Abaraham déem pɔe se o zo Wɛ tete teo kolo kuri na fɔge ko chwi lanyerane to mo. Ko ye Wɛ tete mo tei teo kom konto lɔɔm maama.
11Abaraham kaane Sara déem ye kadega mo ye o kɛ lora. De konto de, o na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se o sɛ we, Wɛ bá kwane o ni dem o na tiŋi to ye o wane o lo bu. 12Konto ŋwaane, ko zege nɔn-doa wolo na ye Abaraham ye o tiini o kwe to yera ne mo Wɛ pɛ o jege dwi kɔgɔ kɔgɔ. Nmo bá‑n wane n lɔre ba ni, ne chalechwe na daga wɛyuu ne de kasolo bia na wo naneo ni ne tei to.
13Nɔɔna bam konto maama nam tega, ye ba ta jege ba wo-dedoa. Ba nam wo nɛ wonnu telo Wɛ na pwooli se o pa-ba to. Ba déem maane we, wonnu tem dɛ wó dáane ye te laam ba, ye ba wo pwoli ko ŋwaane. Ba nam seene ba sɛ mo ja we, ba ye veira balo na ba jege kugu jei logo baŋa ne to mo. 14Balo na yeini ba tɛ konto dwoŋi to bere we, ba daa ta jege teena se ba na teo kolo na wó taa ye ba kugu jei to mo. 15Ba daa ba jege teo kolo ba na nwoŋi ko wone to boboŋa ba yuu ne. Ba ya ná jege boboŋa konto dwoŋi, ba ya wó wane ba na chwoŋa se ba jwoori. 16Ko nam na ye tei to, ba boboŋa tiini ya zo teo kolo na tiini ko lana ko gaale to. Konto mo ye Wɛ tete telaao kom. Konto ŋwaane, chaveera ba jege Wɛ de ba na bwoi‑o we ba Wɛ to. O nam maŋe o jege teo kolo o na wó pa-ba to.
Abaraham de o dwi tiina
17-18Ko ta woli da, maŋa kalo Wɛ na faŋe Abaraham se o nii to, Abaraham wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane mo pɛ se o ya lage o ma o bu Izaak o kaane Wɛ. Wɛ nam maŋe o pwooli ded‑o we, “Ko zege Izaak yera ne mo n dwi tiina wó puli.” De konto de, Abaraham déem ta boŋe se o ma o bu-doa kam o kaane Wɛ, ne Wɛ na bere‑o tei to. 19O boboŋa nam maŋe ya ja we, Wɛ wó wane o bi Izaak toone wone. Ko laam na seene ko ke tei to nye de o jwoŋi‑o toone wone mo.
20Izaak tete de na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage o bia Jakob de Esawu yuu ne se ko vo wonnu telo na lage te ke to seeni.
21Jakob de na daare fee se o te to, o wo-dedoa kam mo pɛ se o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage o bu Josɛf bia bam maama yuu ne. O déem ma chwi o nacheiga o tiiri ka baŋa ne ye o zuli Wɛ.
22Josɛf de maŋa na twɛ se o te to, o na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se o ta de Isarele tiina bam we, ba wó nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne. O ma pa-ba ni we, ba ná nwoŋi, ba jege se ba guri o kwi sem mo Ejipti ne ba ja vo ba tete teo.
Moses
23Ko woli da, Moses tiina déem na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se ba kwei‑o ba seigi chane setɔ ba na loge‑o maŋa kalo to. Ba ma lɔre we, bu wom ye bu-laao, ye ba wo kɔre foone se ba ve Pa-faro wom ni dem.
24Moses déem na ke nɔɔno to, ko ye o wo-dedoa ŋwaane mo pɛ o wo sɛ se ba taa bwoi‑o we, Pa-faro wom bukɔ bu. 25O déem maa boŋe we, o ná tɔge de Wɛ nɔɔna bam o na yaara, ko wó taa gare o ná yage Wɛ chwoŋa ye o daare o di ywoni delo na bá dáane to. 26O nam boŋe o ja se nɔɔna taa yaale‑o Wɛ Dam Tu Krista ŋwaane, ye ko gare o ná nɛ jejegero dedɛ Ejipti ne, kokuri o boboŋa yeini ya tɔge nyɔɔre delo o na wó jwoŋi Wɛ tei ne to mo.
27Moses wo-dedoa kam ŋwaane mo pɛ se o nwoŋi Ejipti ne, ye o wo kɔre Pa-faro wom ban-zɔŋɔ kom. O maa jege baare, ye o wo sɛ se o jwoori o kwaga, kokuri o yei we, Wɛ wolo na ba nae de yia to wo o yiga ne. 28O na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se o sɛ Wɛ ni, ye o pa Isarele tiina bam maama ke Atɔgebabaŋa wodiu ba sam ne ba di. O ma pa ba kwei jana ba ma mi ba sam nia ne, se toone maleka kalo na tu se ka go bakeiri-kwe sem maama to daa yé ke ba tete bia bam kolokolo.
Isarele tiina bam
29Isarele tiina bam na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se ba wane ba bɛ Nane-soŋo kom. Wɛ ma pa se na bam pɔɔre belei ba daare te-kora ye Isarele tiina bam tɔge da ba bɛ. Ejipti tiina bam na kwaane se ba tɔge ba kwaga ba bɛ to, na bam ma jwoori ba ke daane pa se ba maama nyɔ na bam ba te.
30Wɛ nɔɔna bam na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ ba vo ba kaage Jeriko teo kom da yarepɛ, ye ko kabiri sem laam to tega ne. 31Ko daa ta ná ye Rahaba wolo na ye ka-tola ye o zoore Jeriko ne to, o na jege wo-dedoa tei to mo pɛ se o jeeri Wɛ nɔɔna balo na kare ba yere teo kom to lanyerane. Konto ŋwaane mo ba wo go‑o ba woli de balo na ve Wɛ to.
Faŋa faŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam
32Amo ya jege taane dedɛ se a ta a woli da, ye laŋa daa tera se a ŋɔɔne nɔɔna badaara taane a woli da. Amo ya wó ta Gideon, de Baraka, de Samson, de Jefeta, de David, de Samuwel, de faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem maama taane mo. 33Banto bam maama jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ, ye ba mage jara ba wane teene kamunnu dedɛ. Ba ma kwori ba pa se nɔɔna taa tɔge chega chwoŋa. Ba ma daare ba na wolim delo Wɛ na pwooli se o pa-ba to. Nywonnu déem ma lage te chɔge-ba, ye ba wane ba che te chwoŋa. 34Ba ta ma wane min-lwanno telo na lage te chɔge-ba to ye te wo di-ba. Ba ma wane ba lu nɔɔna jeŋa ne pa se ba wo go-ba. Ba ya maa bwomma ye ba jwoori ba na dam. Ba ma tiini ba na baare se ba mage jara, ye ba wane ba zeili dwi-gɛ tiina balo na ye ba dona to pa se ba jwoori ba viiri. 35Kaana de jwoori ba jwoŋi ba nɔɔna balo ya na tega ye ba jwoori ba bi to.
Nɔɔna badwonna maa wo sɛ se ba jwoŋi ba tete balo na jege ba yera ba maga se ba go-ba to tei ne. Ba ma sɛ se ba te se ba wane ba jwoori ba bi ba na ŋwea Wɛ tei ne. 36Nɔɔna badaara yuu yaale de nɔɔna na mɔne-ba, ye ba daare ba fere-ba tei to. Ba ma vɔ nɔɔna badwonna, ye ba daare ba ke-ba peena diga ne. 37Ba ma kwei kandwa ba ma dole ba badwonna ba go. Ba ma gwoni badwonna yera yam kuni belei. Ba ma kwei se-zɔɔro ba ma go ba badwonna. Wɛ nɔɔna badwonna maa kare ba beera, ye ba zo pei de bone tankwallo yerane. Yiniga de cham ma ja-ba, ye nɔɔna de bɛɛse-ba. 38Nɔɔna balo na jege kugu jei logo baŋa ne to nam wo yi se ba de nɔɔna bam konto taa wora daane. Wɛ nɔɔna bam déem beeri kagoa yuu ne, de zwonnu jei ne. Ba maa zoore peero gugworru wone, de bɔɔna wone, ba na ba jege kugu jei to ŋwaane.
39Nɔɔna bam konto maama yere zaŋe de ba na jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ tei to. De konto de, ba nam wo nɛ kolo Wɛ ya na pwooli se o pa o nɔɔna to ba ti. 40Kokuri Wɛ boboŋa déem jaane se o ke kolo na tiini ko lana to debam ŋwaane. Konto ŋwaane, faŋa faŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam déem wo nɛ chwoŋa se ba yi Wɛ wo-laaro tem ba ti ye debam ta wo woli ba wone.

english_text:
A Large Crowd of Witnesses
1 Such a large crowd of witnesses is all around us! So we must get rid of everything that slows us down, especially the sin that just won't let go. And we must be determined to run the race that is ahead of us. 2 We must keep our eyes on Jesus, who leads us and makes our faith complete. He endured the shame of being nailed to a cross, because he knew later on he would be glad he did. Now he is seated at the right side of God's throne! 3So keep your mind on Jesus, who put up with many insults from sinners. Then you won't get discouraged and give up.
4None of you have yet been hurt in your battle against sin. 5 But you have forgotten that the Scriptures say to God's children,
“When the Lord punishes you,
don't make light of it,
and when he corrects you,
don't be discouraged.
6The Lord corrects the people
he loves
and disciplines those
he calls his own.”
7Be patient when you are being corrected! This is how God treats his children. Don't all parents correct their children? 8God corrects all his children, and if he doesn't correct you, then you don't really belong to him. 9Our earthly fathers correct us, and we still respect them. Isn't it even better to be given true life by letting our spiritual Father correct us?
10Our human fathers correct us for a short time, and they do it as they think best. But God corrects us for our own good, because he wants us to be holy, as he is. 11It is never fun to be corrected. In fact, at the time it is always painful. But if we learn to obey by being corrected, we will do right and live at peace.
12 Now stand up straight! Stop your knees from shaking 13 and walk a straight path. Then lame people will be healed, instead of getting worse.
Warning against Turning from God
14Try to live at peace with everyone! Live a clean life. If you don't, you will never see the Lord. 15 Make sure no one misses out on God's wonderful kindness. Don't let anyone become bitter and cause trouble for the rest of you. 16 Watch out for immoral and ungodly people like Esau, who sold his future blessing for only one meal. 17 You know how he later wanted it back. But there was nothing he could do to change things, even though he begged his father and cried.
18 You have not come to a place like Mount Sinai that can be seen and touched. There is no flaming fire or dark cloud or storm 19or trumpet sound. The people of Israel heard a voice speak. But they begged it to stop, 20 because they could not obey its commands. They were even told to kill any animal that touched the mountain. 21The sight was so frightening that Moses said he shook with fear.
22You have now come to Mount Zion and to the heavenly Jerusalem. This is the city of the living God, where thousands and thousands of angels have come to celebrate. 23Here you will find all of God's dearest children, whose names are written in heaven. And you will find God himself, who judges everyone. Here also are the spirits of those good people who have been made perfect. 24 And Jesus is here! He is the one who makes God's new agreement with us, and his sprinkled blood says much better things than the blood of Abel.
25 Make sure you obey the one who speaks to you. The people did not escape, when they refused to obey the one who spoke to them at Mount Sinai. Do you think you can possibly escape, if you refuse to obey the one who speaks to you from heaven? 26 When God spoke the first time, his voice shook only the earth. This time he has promised to shake the earth once again, and heaven too.
27The words “once again” mean that these created things will someday be shaken and removed. Then what cannot be shaken will last. 28We should be grateful we were given a kingdom that cannot be shaken. And in this kingdom we please God by worshiping him and by showing him great honor and respect. 29 Our God is like a destructive fire!
translation_text:
Wɛ na jege o bia o koresa tei to
1Debam laam lɔre faŋa faŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam na ye kɔgɔ kɔgɔ ye ba gilimi debam ba nii tei to. Ba chega kam maa bere debam Wɛ na woli-ba tei, ba na jege wo-dedoa ded‑o to ŋwaane. Konto ŋwaane, pa-na se dé yage wo-yɔɔro telo maama na daane debam pa se dé ware dé tɔge Wɛ lanyerane to. Pa-na dé le wo-lwanno telo na ye wɛleera ye te jege dé yera to dé yage, se dé daare dé vɔ pu-dɛa dé kwaane dé duri dé tɔge chwoŋa kalo Wɛ na tiŋi o pa debam to. 2Pa-na se dé yɔɔre dé taa nii Yezu seeni. Wonto nam mo bere debam dé na wó taa jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ tei to, ye o pa se dé taa jege wo-dedoa taa, se dé ja dé vo dé kweeli. O déem vɔge pu-dɛa mo ye o yaare o te dagara kam yuu ne. O wo pɛ se chaveera ja‑o ko ŋwaane, kolo ŋwaane o nɛ we Wɛ tiŋi ywoni mo se o pa‑o. O laam ma daare o vo o jeini Baŋa Wɛ paare yituŋu kom jazem seeni.
3Boŋe-na á nii Yezu na tiini o vɔ pu-dɛa de nɔn-chechɔgero na jege‑o ba yaale tei to. Á yé pa se jawɔrɔ zo abam se á yage Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem. 4Abam na yeini á kwaane se á chɔge wo-balwaaro dam tei to daa ta wo yi se á na toone nɔɔna tei ne. 5Wɛ tɔnɔ kom nam jege taane delo na wó wane ko pa abam yera poore lanyerane, á na ye Wɛ bia to ŋwaane. Nam guli-na ko na bere abam tei ko we:
“Amo bu, Baŋa Wɛ ná jege‑m o koresa,
se n sɛ koresem.
O maa ná bwɛ nmo,
se n yé pa n nagwola te.
6Kokuri Baŋa Wɛ yeini o korese
o na swoi balo to mo.
Wɛ ná jwoŋi wolo maama se o taa ye o bu,
o yeini o pa se konto tu yera chɛ mo.”
7Abam ná nɛ yaara, se á pa ko taa ye á Kwo Wɛ mo korese abam o de chwoŋa ne. Á na ye Wɛ bia to mo pae o ke abam konto dwoŋi. Bu tera ye o kwo bá vaŋe o zwɛ se o pa o korese. 8Wɛ nam ná wo korese abam ne o na ke o bia bam maama tei to, ko bere we abam dae o bia chekke, á ye tampira mo. 9Dé logo baŋa kwoa bam na yeini ba vaŋe dé zwa tei to mo pae se dé nege-ba. Ko nam ná ye dé Kwo wolo na tei dé jworru to, ko maŋe se dé taa sɛ o ni se dé laam na ŋwea o tei ne. 10Dé logo baŋa kwoa bam yeini ba vaŋe dé zwa bena fenfee yerane mo se ko maŋe de ba boboŋa na lage tei to. Dé Kwo Wɛ nam ke konto se ko woli debam mo, se dé wane dé tɔge dé taa ye wose, ne wonto na ye tei to. 11Ko ná ye á koresem maŋa kam ne, ko yeini ko pa á wo chɔge mo ye á ba jege wopwolo. Ko kwaga ne, zwɛ vaŋem dem wó zeini balo de na pɛ ba korese to pa se ba na nyɔɔre, de ba ŋwea na jege chega de bochare-zuru tei to.
12Konto ŋwaane, á vɔna ná bugi, naa á nagwola ná tega, kwaane-na se á ta‑á tɔge Wɛ chwoŋa de pu-dɛa. 13Fɔge-na á kwɛ chwoŋa kalo á na wó tɔge to se balo de na tɔge-ka ye ba ye gwane to yé to ba ŋoleme ba nɛ sem, se ko nam pa ba na yɔɔrem.
Dé yé ve Wɛ zaane dem
14Kwaane-na se á ta‑á zoore dedaane nɔɔno maama de ywoni, se á kwori á ta‑á jege wo-pwoŋo Wɛ yiga ne, kolo ŋwaane, nɔɔno ná ba jege wo-pwoŋo, o bá wane o na dé Teiru Wɛ. 15Fɔge-na á che á tete se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé ga Wɛ zaane dem. Yé yage-na chwoŋa se nɔɔno wolo wo na ba lana to zaŋe á wone ye o daane abam pa se abam dedɛ na chɔgem Wɛ yiga ne. 16Á yé pa se á wolowolo taa ye ka-lageno, naa Wɛ-lwɛɛno ne Esawu déem na ye tei to. Wonto yiga tera de o na ye o kwo bu-kwea to. O kana maa wɔe, ye o kwei o nakwe nyɔɔre dem o ma leini o nyaane wom zoŋ-dia wodiu o di. 17Abam maŋe á yei kolo na ke‑o kwaga seeni to. O ma jwoori o lage se o kwo sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o pa‑o, se ko maŋe de o na ye o bu-kwea to ŋwaane. O ma kwaane o lwoori chwoŋa o kwo tei ne taa, ye o ka yi-na. O maa wo nɛ chwoŋa, kolo ŋwaane o daa ware o jwoori o fɔge o keim dem.
18Abam nam tu á twɛ Wɛ, ye ko dae nenɛɛne ko déem na ke tei de Isarele tiina bam to. Banto déem tu peo kolo ba yi na nɛ ye ba wae ba dwei de jea to. Maŋa kalo Wɛ na kwei o nia yam o ke Moses jeŋa ne o pa-ba to, min-fɔrɔ, de lim, de doa mumunim wora, 19ko woli de nabɔnɔ wum, de kwora na ŋɔɔne. Balo na nigi Wɛ kwora kam konto to ma lwoori‑o se o daa yé jwoori o ta taane o woli da, 20kolo ŋwaane o na maŋe o kaane-ba tei to tiini ko dana ko pa-ba, de o na tage de-ba o we, “Kolo maama ná nɔne peo kom baŋa ne, ko ná ye varem mo de, se á dole-ko á go.” 21Wɛ na bere o dam dem ja konto to ma pa se Moses tete ta o we, “Foone tiini de zo-ne ye a yera sae.”
22Ko nam dae konto abam tei ne. Abam nam tu á yi peo kolo yere na ye Zion to mo. Ko maa ye Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ teo Jerusalem kolo na wo telaao ne to. Á na tu da to, Wɛ malese morro kɔgɔ kɔgɔ ma tigisi daane ye se wora se di ywoni. 23Abam tu á woli Wɛ kɔgɔ kom wone. Ko maa ye o bu-kwe sem kɔgɔ kom, ba yera na popone ya tiŋi Wɛ telaao tɔnɔ kom ne to. Ko ye Wɛ wolo na wó di nabiina maama taane to tei mo á tu á yi da. Balo na jege chega o yiga ne ye o laam pa se ba bochara kwɛ ya ti fase to jworru maa wo o tei ne. 24Á nam ta tu Yezu tei, wolo Wɛ na dɛ o ŋwaane o gwoni o ni-doore dem to. Ko ye Yezu jana bam ŋwaane mo pɛ á fɔge de Wɛ, ye ba dae nenɛɛne Abel jana bam na bere Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ kom tei to.
25Ta‑á yei-na se á yé zaŋe á ve wolo wom na ŋɔɔne to taane. Isarele tiina bam déem ve wolo na bere-ba Wɛ kwora logo baŋa ne to, ye ba wo wane ba lu Wɛ jeŋa ne. Debam nam ná ve wolo na wo telaao ne ye o ŋɔɔne de debam to, dé wó wane dé lu na? 26Faŋa faŋa to Wɛ kwora kam déem pɛ se tega baŋa maama ziziŋi. O laam nam pwooli we:
“Amo daa ta wó jwoori a pa tega kam ziziŋi bedwe,
ye ko dae kanto yerane,
ko laam wó woli de wɛyuu kom maama mo.”
27Wɛ na tage o we, o ta wó jwoori o ke konto dwoŋi bedwe to bere we, wonnu telo o na naane to mo o laam lage o ziziŋi o le te zega jei ne, pa se te daa yé taa wora. Wonnu telo na bá wane te ziziŋi to yerane laam wó daare.
28Wɛ nam pɛ se dé tɔge dé di paare delo na bá wane de ziziŋi to mo. Konto ŋwaane dé wó ke‑o lei. Dé maa wó pa‑o zula yalo na tɔge o boboŋa to, ye dé taa kɔre‑o lanyerane, 29kolo ŋwaane debam Tu Wɛ nye de min-fɔrɔ kolo na di wo-yɔɔro maama to mo.

english_text:
Service That Pleases God
1Keep being concerned about each other as the Lord's followers should.
2 Be sure to welcome strangers into your home. By doing this, some people have welcomed angels as guests, without even knowing it.
3Remember the Lord's people who are in jail and be concerned for them. Don't forget those who are suffering, but imagine you are there with them.
4 Have respect for marriage. Always be faithful to your partner, because God will punish anyone who is immoral or unfaithful in marriage.
5 Don't fall in love with money. Be satisfied with what you have. The Lord has promised that he will not leave us or desert us. 6 This should make you feel like saying,
“The Lord helps me!
Why should I be afraid
of what people
can do to me?”
7Don't forget about your leaders who taught you God's message. Remember what kind of lives they lived and try to have faith like theirs.
8Jesus Christ never changes! He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. 9Don't be fooled by any kind of strange teachings. It is better to receive strength from God's gift of undeserved grace than to depend on certain foods. After all, these foods don't really help the people who eat them. 10But we have an altar where even the priests who serve in the place of worship have no right to eat.
11 After the high priest offers the blood of animals as a sin offering, the bodies of those animals are burned outside the camp. 12Jesus himself suffered outside the city gate, so his blood would make people holy. 13This is why we should go outside the camp to Jesus and share in his disgrace. 14On this earth we don't have a city that lasts forever, but we are waiting for such a city.
15Our sacrifice is to keep offering praise to God in the name of Jesus. 16But don't forget to help others and to share your possessions with them. This too is like offering a sacrifice that pleases God.
17Obey your leaders and do what they say. They are watching over you, and they must answer to God. So don't make them sad as they do their work. Make them happy. Otherwise, they won't be able to help you at all.
18Pray for us. Our consciences are clear, and we always try to live right. 19I especially want you to pray that I can visit you again soon.
Final Prayers and Greetings
20God gives peace, and he raised our Lord Jesus Christ from death. Now Jesus is like a Great Shepherd whose blood was used to make God's eternal agreement with his flock. 21 I pray God will make you ready to obey him and that you will always be eager to do right. May Jesus help you do what pleases God. To Jesus Christ be glory forever and ever! Amen.
22My friends, I have written only a short letter to encourage you, and I beg you to pay close attention to what I have said.
23By now you surely must know that our friend Timothy is out of jail. If he gets here in time, I will bring him with me when I come to visit you.
24Please give my greetings to your leaders and to the rest of the Lord's people.
His followers from Italy send you their greetings.
25I pray that God will be kind to all of you!
translation_text:
1Ta‑á jege-na da-swono se á yé yage, á na ye nu-bia daane to ŋwaane. 2Ta‑á yei-na se á ta‑á jeeri veira á sam ne lanyerane. Nɔɔna badwonna déem na ke konto dwoŋi to, ko ye Wɛ malese mo ba jeeri ye ba yeiri ba na ye balo to. 3Ta‑á jege-na balo na wo peena diga ne to boboŋa, nenɛɛne abam de tɔge á wo peena diga ne mo tei, ye á zeini-ba. Ko ta ná ye balo nɔɔna na bɛɛse-ba to, se á ta‑á jege ba boboŋa nenɛɛne abam de tɔge á yaare mo tei.
4Baaro de kaane maama jege se ba taa zoore daane mo de swono de zula. Baro wom de kaane wom maama jege se ba taa tɔge chega mo da-tei ne. Wɛ nam wó waare balo na ke kabwoŋa, de balo maama na tɔge ka-laga wo-zɔɔna kikia to.
5Á yé pa se á ŋwea taa tɔge sabu-laga. Kolo maama á na jege to, se á pa ko maŋe abam ye á ba gwooni-ko. Kokuri Wɛ maŋe o ta o we, “Amo bá fɔge a yage abam kɔtaa.”
6Konto ŋwaane debam wó taa jege baare se dé ta we:
“Baŋa Wɛ mo ye amo zeinnu.
A daa bá taa kɔre foone.
Nabiina lage ba ke amo bɛ mo?”
7Ta‑á guli-na nɔɔna balo na ye á yiga tiina ye ba déem ŋɔɔne Wɛ kwora kam ba bere abam to gula. Maane-na á nii ba ŋwea na ye tei se ko vo ko yi ba toone to, se á daare á lwoni ba na jege wo-dedoa de Yezu Krista tei to. 8Maŋa maama Yezu Krista ye nenɛɛne o na maŋe o ye tei to mo, diim de zem maama, se ko taa vei wuu. 9Yé pa-na se nɔɔna taa mae berem-gɛ ba gane abam de wonnu dwi dwi se ko pa á ywori Wɛ tei ne. Nmo ná lage se n bochare ke dam de Wɛ, ko ye Wɛ zaane dem mo wó pa konto, ye ko bá taa ye wodiiru tedwonna dim ŋwaane. Balo na tɔge wodiiru dim chwoŋa to nam wo nɛ nyɔɔre ko baŋa ne.
10Yezu Krista na kwei o tete o ma kaane Wɛ debam ŋwaane tei to dae kaanem delo dwoŋi nɔɔna na wó di de nɔna yam to. Balo na toŋe Wɛ vwei dem wone ba pa‑o to ba jege chwoŋa se ba twori kaanem dento wone ba di. 11Ko na ke tei to, Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu wom yeini o go vara mo o kwei ba jana bam o ja zo Wɛ di-yun-gala kam se o ma saare nɔɔna bam wɛleera. Ko daare vara bam yera yam tete mo, ba laam wó kwei-ya ba ja nwoŋi dáa ba zwɛ maama. 12Yezu toone dem de tɔge konto dwoŋi mo. O ma yaare o te teo kom dáa ne, se o wane o ma o tete jana bam o saare Wɛ nɔɔna bam wɛleera se ba taa ye wose Wɛ yiga ne.
13Konto ŋwaane, pa-na se dé nwoŋi dé vo o tei teo kom dáa ne, se dé tɔge dé na o chaveera yam dwoŋi. 14Kokuri logo baŋa ywo-seeni debam ba jege teo kolo na wó taa ye dé kugu jei taa to, ye dé nam jege teena se dé na teo kolo na lage ko ba to mo.
15Pa-na se dé tɔge Yezu ŋwaane dé taa zuli Wɛ maŋa maama. Konto mo ye keim delo dé na wó kwei dé ma ke kaanem dé pa‑o to. Dé ni taane na zeiŋi Wɛ yere tei to mo ye dé pɛɛra yalo dé na wó ke o jeŋa ne to. 16Á yé swei se á ta‑á ke keim-laaro, se á daare á ta‑á woli daane. Dé ná yeini dé kwei kikia yanto dwoŋi dé ma kaane Wɛ, konto mo pa‑o wopwolo.
17Ta‑á nege-na á yiga tiina, se á daare á ta‑á sɛ ba ni. Banto kwaane ba nii abam ŋwea baŋa ne mo, ye ba yei we ba laam wó ba ba zege Wɛ yiga se o bwei-ba ba totoŋa yam ŋwaane. Nam ta‑á nege-ba se ba wane ba toŋe de wopwolo. Ko ná dae konto, ko wó pa ba wo chɔge, ye ko daa bá taa jege wolim ko pa abam.
18Ta‑á lwoori-na Wɛ á pa debam. Dé yeini dé kwaane se dé da chega chwoŋa mo maŋa maama, ye chaveera tera dé tei ne. 19Amo nam lage a kwoori abam se á ta‑á lwoori Wɛ á pa-ne, se ko pa a na chwoŋa a jwoori abam tei leile.
20Bochare-zuru Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó zeini abam. Wonto mo bi de Teiru Yezu toone wone de o na dɛ o jana bam ŋwaane o gwoni ni delo na wó taa wora taa wuu to. O laam ma pa o ye nayero chekke ye o wae o nii debam balo na nye de o pei sem to lanyerane. 21Wɛ wó zeini abam de wo-laaro telo maama na maŋe se á wane á ta‑á tɔge o boboŋa to, ye o tɔge Yezu Krista ŋwaane o fɔge abam, ne ko na wó pwoli o wo tei to.
Yezu maŋe de zula se ko taa vei wuu. Ameena.
22A nu-bia bam, a lwoori abam se á zuri á yera á cheigi amo na popone kolo a ma kwoori abam to. Amo na popone taane delo to nam ba dɔra.
23A lage se abam ta‑á yei we, ba yage dé nu-bu Timoti se o nwoŋi peena diga ne. O ná tu amo tei lela, a laam wó pa dé tɔge daane dé ba dé na abam.
24Jɔɔne-na á yiga tiina bam, de Wɛ nɔɔna bam maama á pa debam. Dé nu-bia balo na nwoŋi Yitalia to de jɔɔne abam.
25Wɛ zaane dem taa wo abam maama tei ne.

english_text:
1 From James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Greetings to the twelve tribes scattered all over the world.
Faith and Wisdom
2 My friends, be glad, even if you have a lot of trouble. 3You know you learn to endure by having your faith tested. 4But you must learn to endure everything, so you will be completely mature and not lacking in anything.
5 If any of you need wisdom, you should ask God, and it will be given to you. God is generous and won't correct you for asking. 6But when you ask for something, you must have faith and not doubt. Anyone who doubts is like an ocean wave tossed around in a storm. 7-8If you are that kind of person, you can't make up your mind, and you surely can't be trusted. So don't expect the Lord to give you anything at all.
Poor People and Rich People
9Any of God's people who are poor should be glad he thinks so highly of them. 10 But any who are rich should be glad when God makes them humble. Rich people will disappear like wild flowers 11scorched by the burning heat of the sun. The flowers lose their blossoms, and their beauty is destroyed. This is how the rich will disappear, as they go about their business.
Trials and Temptations
12 God will bless you, if you don't give up when your faith is being tested. He will reward you with a glorious life, just as he rewards everyone who loves him.
13 Don't blame God when you are tempted! God cannot be tempted by evil, and he doesn't use evil to tempt others. 14We are tempted by our own desires that drag us off and trap us. 15Our desires make us sin, and when sin is finished with us, it leaves us dead.
16Don't be fooled, my dear friends. 17Every good and perfect gift comes down from the Father who created all the lights in the heavens. He is always the same and never makes dark shadows by changing. 18He wanted us to be his own special people, and so he sent the true message to give us new birth.
Hearing and Obeying
19 My dear friends, you should be quick to listen and slow to speak or to get angry. 20If you are angry, you cannot do any of the good things God wants done. 21You must stop doing anything immoral or evil. Instead be humble and accept the message planted in you to save you.
22Obey God's message! Don't fool yourselves by just listening to it. 23If you hear the message and don't obey it, you are like people who stare at themselves in a mirror 24and forget what they look like as soon as they leave. 25But you must never stop looking at the perfect law that sets you free. God will bless you in everything you do, if you listen and obey, and don't just hear and forget.
26If you think you are being religious, but can't control your tongue, you are fooling yourself, and your religion is useless. 27Religion that pleases God the Father must be pure and spotless. You must help needy orphans and widows and not let this world make you evil.
translation_text:
1Amo Jemsi wolo na ye Wɛ kabaa de debam Teiru Yezu Krista kabaa to mo popone tɔnɔ konto. A jɔɔne abam dwi kuni fuga-balei bam na ye Wɛ nɔɔna ye á jage á yi logo baŋa jei maama to.
Wɛ zeini nɔɔna lanyerane
2A nu-bia bam, maŋa kalo maama cham ná tu abam baŋa, se á ta‑á jege wopwolo lanyerane, kolo ŋwaane á yei we yaara dwi dwi ná tui abam tei, 3ko ye se ya maŋe abam mo ya nii á na ke á wo-dedoa de Wɛ tei to. Ko kwaga ne ko laam wó pa se á ta‑á jege pu-dɛa lanyerane á woli da. 4Kwaane-na se á ta‑á zege lanyerane de pu-dɛa se á yé jwoori kwaga. Keim dem konto wó fɔge abam fase, pa se á boboŋa kweere de Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem, se á yé wane á ga kolokolo.
5Abam wolo maama nam ná yeiri kolo na lana se o ke to, konto tu jege se o lwoori swa mo Wɛ tei ne. Wɛ yeini o woli nɔɔna maama lanyerane mo, ye o ba ŋwaana. Nmo ná lwoori swa o tei ne, o wó ke konto mo o pa‑m. 6Nmo nam ná lwoori woŋo Wɛ tei ne, se n ta‑n jege boŋem-dɛɔ we, n wó seene n na. Yé ta‑n jege bobwea ko baŋa ne, kokuri bobwea tu nye ne vio na dole na-ŋone, pa se vei yiga de kwaga tei to mo. 7-8Konto tu bere o wo ke o wo-dedoa de Wɛ, ye o yeini o za o boboŋa de kolo maama o na boŋe se o ke to. Nɔɔno wom konto dwoŋi yé taa boŋe we, o wó na woŋo dé Teiru wom tei ne.
9Nmo wolo na tɔge Yezu ye yiniga jege‑m to, se n ta‑n jege wopwolo de Wɛ na pɛ n jege yere o tei ne to ŋwaane. 10Nmo wolo nam na ye nadum to, se n de ta‑n jege wopwolo de Wɛ na pɛ se n gwooni n tete o tei ne to ŋwaane. Nabiina ba dáana ye ba toa, ba ná maŋe ba ye naduna tei de. Ko nye ne gaaro na ke punnu ye te jege lam tei to mo. 11Wea nam ná bega, ka wó baane-te mo pa te kwaare. Punnu tem ma siiri ye te daa ba jege lam. Ko nam ye bedwe mo de naduna na wó ba ba te ba jejegero tem lagem wone tei to.
12Nɔɔno wolo ná wo cham wone ye o ná zege lanyerane de pu-dɛa, konto tu jege yu-ywoŋo mo. O yaara yam ná faŋe‑o ya ti, ye o ta ná zege lanyerane, o laam wó na Wɛ pɛɛre delo na ye ŋwea chekke to. Wɛ pwooli se o pa ŋwea kam konto mo balo maama na swoi‑o to.
13Nɔɔno ná nɛ maŋem, o yé zaŋe o kwei o ma gwori Wɛ. O yé zaŋe o ta nenɛɛne, ko ye Wɛ mo soge‑o se o ke wo-lɔŋɔ. Kolokolo tera ko na wó wane ko soge Wɛ se o tusi, ye Wɛ tete bá sɛ se o soge nɔɔno se o tusi. 14Woŋo kolo nam na yeini ko soge‑m to ye n tete boboŋa mo. Ya maa pae n fera zoore wo-zɔɔna, ye ya gane‑m se n vo n to gwoŋo ne. 15Nmo ná sɛ n tɔge n boboŋ-balwaaro tem, ya laam pa se n ke wo-lwanno mo. Wo-lwanno tem laam wó puli te taa daga nmo baŋa ne, ye ko laam daare toone yerane mo.
16A nu-bi-swonnu bam, ta‑á yei-na á tete. 17Pɛɛre delo maama na lana ye de jege chega to mo dé yeini dé jwoŋi Wɛ tei ne. Wonto mo ke wonnu telo maama na wo wɛyuu ne ye te pae pwooni to. Wonnu tem konto mo yeini te wae te pipira wea de tete. Wɛ nam ba leira ne tento wonnu tem tei. 18O boboŋa jaane mo se o tɔge o chega taane dem ŋwaane o pa dé na o ŋwe-doŋa kam. Ko nye nenɛɛne o le debam mo o ke nɔɔna maama yiga ne se dé taa ye o bia.
Kikia yalo na maŋe de Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem to
19A nu-bi-swonnu bam, ta‑á yei-na we, nɔɔno maama jege se o zuri o yera mo o taa cheigi o dwoŋi taane, se o yé gare o ŋɔɔne. O jege se o ja o bane mo. 20Kolo ŋwaane n bá‑n wane n tɔge ban-zɔŋɔ ŋwaane n ke wo-laaro ne Wɛ boboŋa na lage tei to mo.
21Konto ŋwaane, le-na wo-zɔɔna yalo maama na wo á wone to á yage, se á daare á che á tete de wo-lwanno telo na lage te chɔge abam to. Wɛ maŋe o kwei o taane dem o ke abam bochara ne. Nam gwooni-na á tete á sɛ-de lanyerane, de na wó wane de jwoŋi abam de yage to ŋwaane.
22Nam ta‑á yei-na se á ta‑á tɔge Wɛ kwora kam, se ko dae we á ta‑á cheigi o taane dem yerane. 23Nɔɔno wolo ná cheigi Wɛ taane ye o ba tɔge de na bere tei to, kotu gane o tete mo. O nye nenɛɛne nɔɔno mo kwei niu se o ma o nii o tete. 24O ma nii o na o yibia na ye tei to, ye o laam pipiri o kɛ o daare niu kom. Ko wo dáane de o na swei o yibia kam na ye tei to. 25Ko nam ná ye Wɛ ni taane dem, dento lana fase ye de wae de jwoŋi nɔɔna pa ba na ba tete. Nɔɔno ná nii-de ye o jege-de o yuu ne maŋa maama, konto tu bá taa nye de wolo na gare o swei chega kalo o na lɔre to. O maa ye wolo na seene o tɔge chega kam to mo. Wonto wó na wopwolo lanyerane o kikia maama baŋa ne.
26Abam wolo ná boŋe we o kɔre Wɛ, ye o ná ware o ni taane o ja, wonto gane o tete mo. O Wɛ kɔrɔ kom maa ye kafɛ mo. 27Dé Kwo Wɛ nam na lage se dé sɛ‑o tei to mo ye se dé taa zeini botara de kadeina balo na yaare to, ye dé kwaane dé che dé tete de logo baŋa wo-zɔɔna yam. Wɛ kɔrɔ konto dwoŋi mo su Wɛ yi, ye tusim tere ko wone.

english_text:
Warning against Having Favorites
1My friends, if you have faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, you won't treat some people better than others. 2Suppose a rich person wearing fancy clothes and a gold ring comes to one of your meetings. And suppose a poor person dressed in worn-out clothes also comes. 3You must not give the best seat to the one in fancy clothes and tell the one who is poor to stand at the side or sit on the floor. 4This is the same as saying that some people are better than others, and you would be acting like a crooked judge.
5My dear friends, pay attention. God has given a lot of faith to the poor people in this world. God has also promised them a share in his kingdom that he will give to everyone who loves him. 6You mistreat the poor. But isn't it the rich who boss you around and drag you off to court? 7Aren't they the ones who make fun of your Lord?
8 You will do all right, if you obey the most important law in the Scriptures. It is the law that commands us to love others as much as we love ourselves. 9But if you treat some people better than others, you have done wrong, and the Scriptures teach that you have sinned.
10 If you obey every law except one, you are still guilty of breaking them all. 11 The same God who told us to be faithful in marriage also told us not to murder. So even if you are faithful in marriage, but murder someone, you still have broken God's Law.
12Speak and act like people who will be judged by the law that sets us free. 13Do this, because on the day of judgment there will be no pity for those who have not had pity on others. But even in judgment, God is merciful!
Faith and Works
14My friends, what good is it to say you have faith, when you don't do anything to show you really do have faith? Can this kind of faith save you? 15If you know someone who doesn't have any clothes or food, 16you shouldn't just say, “I hope all goes well for you. I hope you will be warm and have plenty to eat.” What good is it to say this, unless you do something to help? 17Faith that doesn't lead us to do good deeds is all alone and dead!
18Suppose someone disagrees and says, “It is possible to have faith without doing kind deeds.”
I would answer, “Prove that you have faith without doing kind deeds, and I will prove that I have faith by doing them.” 19You surely believe there is only one God. That's fine. Even demons believe this, and it makes them shake with fear.
20Does some stupid person want proof that faith without deeds is useless? 21 Well, our ancestor Abraham pleased God by putting his son Isaac on the altar to sacrifice him. 22Now you see how Abraham's faith and deeds worked together. He proved his faith was real by what he did. 23 This is what the Scriptures mean by saying, “Abraham had faith in God, and God accepted him.” That's how Abraham became God's friend.
24You can now see that we please God by what we do and not only by what we believe. 25 For example, Rahab had been a prostitute. But she pleased God when she welcomed the spies and sent them home by another way.
26Anyone who doesn't breathe is dead, and faith that doesn't do anything is just as dead!
translation_text:
Dé yé taa kuri nɔɔna daane
1A nu-bia bam, abam ye balo na seene á sɛ dé Teiru Yezu Krista wolo na di paare telaao ne to mo. Konto ŋwaane, ko wo maŋe se á ta‑á kuri nɔɔna daane de á na zuli-ba tei to. 2Abam ná tigisi daane se á ware Wɛ, dɛ delo nɔɔna balei ma ba á tei. Dedoa maa ye nadum. O ma zo gare-nyenno ye o ke sabu-seŋa jafolo o jeŋa ne. O dwoŋi wom maa ye yiniga tu, ye o zo gare-zenzwanno. 3Dɛ delo á wó jeeri nadum wom lanyerane, ye á pa o na jeiŋa jei, á daare á ta de yiniga tu wom we, o zege dáa ne, naa o jeini tega ne á nɛ ni ne. 4Á ná pɔɔre-ba daane konto dwoŋi, ko bere we á pae se nɔɔna ba mae daane mo. Ko nam ye boboŋ-lwanno mo pae á kuri nɔɔna daane konto.
5A nu-bi-swonnu bam, cheigi-na amo. Wɛ mo seene o kuri balo na ye yiniga tiina nɔɔna tei ne to, se ba taa ye naduna o tei ne, de ba na ke ba wo-dedoa de Yezu tei to. O wó pa ba woli o paare dem wone, ne o na maŋe o pwooli se o ke o pa balo na swoi‑o to. 6Ko nam na ye konto to, bɛ mo kea ye á jege yiniga tiina á twea? Bera mo jege abam ba bɛɛsa? Ko dae naduna bam mo na? Banto mo yeini ba ja abam de dam ba ja vo ba saŋe kɔɔte ne. 7Ba maa jege Yezu yere-ŋom dem ba twea, ye abam mo ye o bia.
8Wɛ ni delo na bere o paare dem to popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we, “Ta‑n swoi n dwoŋi se ko maŋe de n na swoi n tete tei to.” Abam ná sɛ á tɔge ni dem konto, ko lana. 9Ko daare á ná pɔɔre nɔɔno de nɔɔno daane de á na zuli-ba tei to, ko bere we á ke wɛleere mo. Wɛ ni dem bere we á ke á tusi mo. 10Nɔɔno ná tɔge Wɛ nia yam maama ye o ná chɔge ya woŋo dedoa yerane, ko bere we o chɔge ya maama mo. 11Wɛ mo pɛ o ni we, dé yé zaŋe dé ke kabwoŋa. Wonto nam ta mo we, dé yé go nɔɔno. Mo kokuri, n ná maŋe n wo ke kabwoŋa, ye n ná go nɔɔno, ko bere we, n ta chɔge Wɛ ni mo.
12Ta‑á pa-na á ni taane de á kikia maama taa tɔge Wɛ ni delo na wae de jwoŋi nɔɔna pa ba na ba tete to, se Wɛ wó tɔge o ni dem konto baŋa ne mo o ma di debam taane. 13Kolo ŋwaane, Wɛ ná di wolo na ba jege o dwonna ŋwaŋa to taane, o bá duri konto tu de ŋwaŋa. Wolo nam na jege o dwonna ŋwaŋa to wó lɔre we, Wɛ duri nɔɔna ŋwaŋa se ba yé na waarem mo.
Wo-dedoa keim de keim-laaro taane
14A nu-bia bam, nɔɔno ná tɛ o we, omo ke o wo-dedoa de Wɛ, ye o laam ba tɔge kikia yalo na maŋe to, ko jege kuri na? O Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem dem konto wó wane de jwoŋi‑o de yage na? 15Dɛ delo n nu-bu dedoa wó ba nmo tei ye o ba jege gɔrɔ se o zo, de o ni-wodiu se o di. 16Nmo laam ná tage ded‑o n we, o véi, se Wɛ wó zeini‑o pa o na gɔrɔ de o ni-wodiu, ye n ná wo pɛ‑o wonnu telo o na lage to, ko jege kuri na? 17Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem de ye konto mo. Nmo ná tɛ we, n ke n wo-dedoa de Wɛ, ye n laam daare n ba ke keim-laaro, ko bere we n Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem dem ye kafɛ mo.
18Nɔɔno wae o tɛ we, omo ke o wo-dedoa de Wɛ. Amo nam ke keim-laaro mo. Nmo na ba ke keim-laaro to, nmo nam wó ke tɛ mo n bere-ne we n seene n ke n wo-dedoa de Wɛ? Ko nam ná ye amo, amo wó kwei a keim-laaro tem a ma bere‑m we a sɛ Wɛ de wo-dedoa.
19N sɛ we Wɛ ye dedoa yerane mo na? N ná sɛ konto, ko lana. Setaana tete de maŋe ya sɛ konto mo, ye ko pae ya yera sae. 20N ba jege boboŋa mo na? N yeiri we Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem delo na ba tɔge de keim-laaro to ye kafɛ mo na? 21Boŋe n nii debam nabaaro Abaraham kikia déem na ye tei to. Ko ke tɛ mo ye Wɛ pa se o jege chega o tei ne? Ko ye o kikia yam ŋwaane mo, de o na kwei o bu Izaak se o go o ma ke kaanem. 22Ko bere we o Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem dem dedaane o keim-laaro maama tɔge daane mo. O keim-laaro tem déem mo pɛ se o Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem dem ji chega. 23Konto mo, kolo na popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne to jigi chega ye ko we, “Abaraham ke o wo-dedoa de Wɛ, ye Wɛ pa o na chega ko ŋwaane.” Nɔɔna déem maa bwoi‑o we “Wɛ badwoŋi”.
24Konto wó pa á lɔre we, ko ye nɔɔno kikia mo pae o na chega Wɛ tei ne, se ko dae o na ke o wo-dedoa de Wɛ to yerane ŋwaane. 25Ko woli da, ko ná ye ka-tola kalo yere na ye Rahaba to, wonto kikia de bere konto mo. Isarele tiina tontoŋena bam déem na tu o tei to, o ke-ba lanyerane ye o bere-ba chwoŋa se ba tɔge da ba ma lu ba dona jeŋa ne. O kikia yam konto mo pɛ se o na chega Wɛ tei ne.
26Konto maama bere we, nɔɔno Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem ná ba jege keim-laaro, ko ye kafɛ mo. Ko ye bedwe mo de nɔɔno yera ná ba jege jworo, wonto ye too mo.

english_text:
The Tongue
1My friends, we should not all try to become teachers. In fact, teachers will be judged more strictly than others. 2 All of us do many wrong things. But if you can control your tongue, you are mature and able to control your whole body.
3By putting a bit into the mouth of a horse, we can turn the horse in different directions. 4It takes strong winds to move a large sailing ship, but the captain uses only a small rudder to make it go in any direction. 5Our tongues are small too, and yet they brag about big things.
It takes only a spark to start a forest fire! 6 The tongue is like a spark. It is an evil power that dirties the rest of the body and sets a person's entire life on fire with flames that come from hell itself. 7All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures can be tamed and have been tamed. 8But our tongues get out of control. They are restless and evil, and always spreading deadly poison.
9-10 My dear friends, with our tongues we speak both praises and curses. We praise our Lord and Father, and we curse people who were created to be like God, and this isn't right. 11Can clean water and dirty water both flow from the same spring? 12Can a fig tree produce olives or a grapevine produce figs? Does fresh water come from a well full of salt water?
Wisdom from Above
13 Are any of you wise or sensible? Then show it by living right and by being humble and wise in everything you do. 14But if your heart is full of bitter jealousy and selfishness, don't brag or lie to cover up the truth. 15This kind of wisdom doesn't come from above. It is earthly and selfish and comes from the devil himself. 16Whenever people are jealous or selfish, they cause trouble and do all sorts of cruel things. 17But the wisdom that comes from above leads us to be pure, friendly, gentle, sensible, kind, helpful, genuine, and sincere. 18When peacemakers plant seeds of peace, they will harvest justice.
translation_text:
Ni taane wae de chɔge debam
1A nu-bia bam, abam dedɛ yé ta‑á kwaana se á ta‑á ye Wɛ kwora kam berena. Kolo ŋwaane á yei we, Wɛ borem dɛ dem ne ko wó taa tiini ko chana ko pa debam berena bam ko dwoi nɔɔna badaara. 2Debam maama yeini dé ke dé tusa. Nɔɔno wolo nam na ba ke o tusa o ni taane wone to yɔɔre o ye nɔn-ŋom mo, ye o wae o tete o jaane lanyerane.
3Nɔɔno ná yeini o lage o di siseiŋa, o wó kwei gara mo o ke ka ni ne se o wane o pa ka vo mɛ de mɛ o na lage to. 4Nam boŋe-na á nii nabworo na ye kamunu tei, ye vo-dɛɔ taa jege-ko ko maga. Ko tu wom nam ta wae o ma nayuŋ-balaŋa o pa ko vei o na lage mɛ to. 5Ko nam ta ye bedwe mo de nɔɔno dindeilimi na ye balaŋ-laŋa tei, ye de wae de tɛ wo-kamunnu de pae de tu wom to.
Nam ta‑á boŋe-na á nii kagoa na mae tei ye min-cheŋo ná to ka wone, ko wó di ka maama mo. 6Nɔɔno dindeilimi de nam ye mini mo, ye logo baŋa wo-lwanno maama wo de tei ne. De maa ye yera yam daa dedoa mo, ye de wo-lwanno tem laam wae te lɔgese yera yam maama. Dindeilimi jege mini mo de maa zwɛ nɔɔno ŋwea maama pa ka chɔge, ye mini dem konto nwoŋi te-seŋa ne mo.
7Nabiinu wae o tulimi wonnu dwi maama. O tulimi ga-vara, de zuna, de tega-veila, de ywona. 8Ko nam ná ye dindeilimi, nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na wae o tulimi-de. De maa ye wo-lɔŋɔ kolo na ware ko che to mo, ye de kwori de jege chɔŋɔ kolo na goe nɔɔna to. 9Dé yeini dé ma dento mo dé maa tei Wɛ wom na ye dé Teiru dedaane dé Kwo to, ye dento mo dé ta maa sɔɔle lwarem dé yage dé dwonna yuu ne. Wɛ nam ke banto pa ba jege o nyenyego. 10Konto to, teem de chɔgem maama nwoŋi ni dem konto dedoa wone mo. A nu-bia bam, ko wo maŋe se ko taa ye konto. 11Ko ná ye buli-yi, na-ŋona de na-chɛɔ maama bá wane ba taa buri de wone. 12A nu-bia bam, kaporo bá wane ko lei swa. Kansɔlɔ de nam bá wane ko lei mɔɔro. Ko ye bedwe mo de n na bá wane n mɔ na-ŋona bworu jei ne tei to.
Wɛ na pae swa yalo to
13A lage a ta woŋo de abam wolo maama na boŋe we o jege swa de yi-poro lanyerane to. Konto tu jege se o taa tɔge chwo-laao mo, ye o gwooni o tete o ke keim-laaro, ne ko na maŋe de o swa yam tei to. 14Nmo nam ná jege wo-goo de puseŋa, ye n lage n yerane wonnu, se n yé zaŋe n mage n nyɔɔne n ta we, n jege swa. N fɔ vwa n ma n kweele chega kam mo konto. 15Swa yam konto dwoŋi dae swa yalo na nwoŋi Wɛ tei to. Yanto ye logo baŋa nyem mo. Ya maa ye nabiina swa yalo na nwoŋi setaana tei to. 16Mɛ maama nɔɔna na lage ba yerane wonnu ye ba jege puseŋa de ba dwonna to, dáane mo kantɔgɔ de keim-lwanno dwi maama wora.
17Ko nam ná ye swa yalo na seene ya nwoŋi Wɛ tei to, yanto mo tiini ya lana fase. Ya maa swoi se ywoni taa wora, ye ya tu ye nɔn-pwoŋo wolo na nege nɔɔna to. O maa jege o dwonna ŋwaŋa lanyerane, ye o ta ke keim-laaro de o woli da. O ba kuri nɔɔna daane de o na ke-ba tei to, ye nɔɔna yei o wo lanyerane. 18Balo na swoi ywoni to wae ba woli ba dwonna se ywoni taa wo ba tetare ne. Nyɔɔre delo ba na wó na ba kikia yam baŋa ne to ye se chega mo taa toŋa.

english_text:
Friendship with the World
1Why do you fight and argue with each other? Isn't it because you are full of selfish desires that fight to control your body? 2You want something you don't have, and you will do anything to get it. You will even kill! But you still cannot get what you want, and you won't get it by fighting and arguing. You should pray for it. 3Yet even when you do pray, your prayers are not answered, because you pray just for selfish reasons.
4You people aren't faithful to God! Don't you know if you love the world, you are God's enemies? And if you decide to be a friend of the world, you make yourself an enemy of God. 5Do you doubt the Scriptures that say, “God truly cares about the Spirit he has put in us”? 6 In fact, God treats us with even greater kindness, just as the Scriptures say,
“God opposes everyone
who is proud,
but he blesses all who are humble
with undeserved grace.”
7Surrender to God! Resist the devil, and he will run from you. 8Come near to God, and he will come near to you. Clean up your lives, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you people who can't make up your mind. 9Be sad and sorry and weep. Stop laughing and start crying. Be gloomy instead of glad. 10Be humble in the Lord's presence, and he will honor you.
Saying Cruel Things about Others
11My friends, don't say cruel things about others! If you do, or if you condemn others, you are condemning God's Law. And if you condemn the Law, you put yourself above the Law and refuse to obey either it 12or God who gave it. God is our judge, and he can save or destroy us. What right do you have to condemn anyone?
Warning against Bragging
13 You should know better than to say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to the city. We will do business there for a year and make a lot of money!” 14What do you know about tomorrow? How can you be so sure about your life? It is nothing more than mist that appears for only a little while before it disappears. 15You should say, “If the Lord lets us live, we will do these things.” 16Yet you are stupid enough to brag, and it is wrong to be so proud. 17If you don't do what you know is right, you have sinned.
translation_text:
Dé jege se dé tu dé tete Wɛ yiga ne
1Jara dedaane ni-kantɔgɔ yeini ya wora abam tei ne. Bɛ nam mo pae ya tui? Á na lage á boboŋa wonnu tei to mo tei á bochara jege daanem, pa se jara wo á wone. 2Ko na ye tei to, á fera zoore wonnu ye á nam ba na-te. Ko maa pae á lage se á go nɔɔna. Á yi tiini de su wonnu dedɛ ye á ware-te á na. Konto mo pae kantɔgɔ de jara tui á tetare ne. Á ba jege wonnu telo á na lage to kolo ŋwaane á wo lwoori Wɛ te ŋwaane se o pa abam. 3Abam nam ná maŋe á lwoori wonnu Wɛ tei ne, á yeini á ba na-te, á na mae boboŋ-lwanno mo á lwoora to ŋwaane. Á lwoori se á ta‑á ma-te á ke á tete yerane boboŋa mo.
4Á nwoŋi Wɛ kwaga ne mo na? Á nam yeiri we, á ná me de logo baŋa wonnu, á ye Wɛ dona mo na? Wolo maama na lage se o me de logo baŋa wonnu tem to wó ji Wɛ dono mo. 5Á yé ta‑á boŋe we kolo na popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom wone to ba jege kuri, de ko na we, “Jworo kolo Wɛ na ke dé bochara ne to lage se ko yerane mo taa tei debam.” 6Wɛ nam mo ke debam zaane se ko gaale. Ko ta popone we:
“Wɛ ve balo na bere ba tete kamunim to,
ye o daare o ke zaane balo na tu ba tete to yuu ne.”
7Ko nam na ye konto to, kwei-na á tete á ke Wɛ jeŋa ne, se á daare á ve setaana pɛ wom, se wonto wó duri o viiri á tei ne. 8Fofɔ-na á twɛ Wɛ tei, se o de wó taa bwola de abam. Sane-na á je á yage á wo-lwanno kikia yam. Kwɛ-na á bochara se á daa yé ta‑á jege woro telei. 9Nyɔne-na á yiga á ta‑á kona ye á keera. Pa-na á mwanno tem leiri te ji keira, se á wopwolo kom leiri ko ji wo-chechɔgɔ. 10Tu-na á tete dé Teiru wom yiga ne, se o laam wó ja abam o pa á zaŋe.
11A nu-bia bam, yé ta‑á ŋɔɔne-na ta-balwaaro á pa daane. Wolo maama ná ŋɔɔne ta-balɔrɔ o pa o nu-bu, naa o yaale o yuu, konto tu ŋɔɔne o chɔge Wɛ nia yam mo ye o yaale-ya. Nmo nam ná yaale Wɛ nia yam, ko bere we n daa‑n ba tɔge-ya mo, ye n jege dam ya baŋa ne. 12Wɛ yerane mo tei o nia yam ye o tɔge-ya o ma bore nɔɔna bora. Wonto yerane mo wae o jwoŋi nɔɔna o yaga, naa o chɔge-ba. Nmo nam boŋe we n ye wɔ mo se n di n dwoŋi taane?
13Fɔge á cheigi-na, abam balo na yeini á tɛ we, “Zem naa jwa ne dé wó vo teo kodwoŋi dé ke pipiu da bene dé na sabu” to. 14Á tɛ konto dwoŋi ye á yeiri tega na wó poore se á ŋwea taa ye tei. Á ŋwea nam nye de kunu mo. Ko wó li ye ko bá dáane ye ko jei. 15Ko ya maŋe se á ta‑á tɛ we, “Wɛ ná sɛ pa dé jwa ŋwe, dé wó ke kolo dé na boŋe to.” 16Ko nam na ye tei to, á pa á tete kamunni mo de á na wó ke wonnu telo to. Kamunni dem konto nam ba lana.
17Konto to, nɔɔno wolo ná yei kolo na lana se o ke to, ye o ná wo ke, kotu ke wɛleere mo.

english_text:
Warning to the Rich
1You rich people should cry and weep! Terrible things are going to happen to you. 2 Your treasures have already rotted, and moths have eaten your clothes. 3 Your money has rusted, and the rust will be evidence against you, as it burns your body like fire. Yet you keep on storing up wealth in these last days. 4 You refused to pay the people who worked in your fields, and now their unpaid wages are shouting out against you. The Lord All-Powerful has surely heard the cries of the workers who harvested your crops.
5While here on earth, you have thought only of filling your own stomachs and having a good time. But now you are like fat cattle on their way to be butchered. 6 You have condemned and murdered innocent people, who couldn't even fight back.
Be Patient and Kind
7My friends, be patient until the Lord returns. Think of farmers who wait patiently for the autumn and spring rains to make their valuable crops grow. 8Be patient like those farmers and don't give up. The Lord will soon be here! 9Don't grumble about each other or you will be judged, and the judge is right outside the door.
10My friends, follow the example of the prophets who spoke for the Lord. They were patient, even when they had to suffer. 11 In fact, we praise the ones who endured the most. You remember how patient Job was and how the Lord finally helped him. The Lord did this because he is so merciful and kind.
12 My friends, above all else, don't take an oath. You must not swear by heaven or by earth or by anything else. “Yes” or “No” is all you need to say. If you say anything more, you will be condemned.
13If you are having trouble, you should pray. And if you are feeling good, you should sing praises. 14 If you are sick, ask the church leaders to come and pray for you. Ask them to put olive oil on you in the name of the Lord. 15If you have faith when you pray for sick people, they will get well. The Lord will heal them, and if they have sinned, he will forgive them.
16 If you have sinned, you should tell each other what you have done. Then you can pray for one another and be healed. The prayer of an innocent person is powerful, and it can help a lot. 17 Elijah was just as human as we are, and for three and a half years his prayers kept the rain from falling. 18 But when he did pray for rain, it fell from the skies and made the crops grow.
19My friends, if any followers have wandered away from the truth, you should try to lead them back. 20 If you turn sinners from the wrong way, you will save them from death, and many of their sins will be forgiven.
translation_text:
Naduna na bɛɛse nɔɔna tei to
1Ko daare abam balo na ye naduna to, fɔge á cheigi-na. Ta‑á keeri-na se á ta‑á chwoosa de lɛɛro telo na lage te ba abam baŋa to. 2Abam jejegero tem maama pɔga, ye charebombore de di á gwaaro tem. 3Abam sabu-seŋa kam de á sabia maama maa soŋe. Bora borem dɛ dem ne te soŋem dem konto mo wó bere we á ke á tusi, ye dento ta wó di abam yera yam ne mini tei. Logo baŋa kweelim da yam nam twɛ, ye abam ta fɔge á la á jejegero tem á tiŋi. 4Ko ta woli da, á ba sɛ se á ta‑á ŋwe balo na toŋe ba pa abam to. Cheigi-na á nii ba na poona de á na pini-ba tei to. Balo na ke abam wodiiru tem ba ke diga ne to keira kam to Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ zwɛ ne. 5Á logo baŋa ŋwea kam ye paare yerane mo, ye á ke á boboŋa na lage tei. Á di á nu, ne ba na kɔne varem se ba go tei to. 6Á ta kwori á pae balo na jege chega to ga bora, á daare á go-ba, ye ba ware á yiga se ba che.
Dé wó pa se Wɛ taa jege dé teena
7A nu-bia bam, zuri-na á bochara á ta‑á maa nii maŋa kam dé Teiru wom na wó jwoori o ba to. Ta‑á nii-na valo na yeini o zuri o yera tei o maa cheigi maŋa kam o wodiiru tem na wó be to. O yeini o zuri o yera o maa cheigi duum doa, de faao-ni doa. 8Konto ŋwaane, ko maŋe se abam de zuri á bochara mo ye á vɔ á wo lanyerane, se dé Teiru wom bá dáane ye o ba.
9A nu-bia bam, yé ta‑á poone daane, se ko wó pa á ga bora Wɛ tei ne. Nii-na, ko twɛ ko ti se Wɛ di debam taane. 10A nu-bia bam, guli-na Baŋa Wɛ sampwori selo déem na tɔɔle o kwora kam to gula. Ba déem nɛ yaara dedɛ ye ba vɔ ba wo ba fɔge ba zege ka baŋa ne lanyerane. Konto to, ko maŋe se abam de lwoni banto kikia yam mo. 11Ko ná ye balo na jege pu-dɛa kanto dwoŋi to, dé yei we ba nɛ wopwolo Wɛ tei ne. Abam maŋe á yei Job déem na ke pu-dɛa o yaara yam wone tei, ye á kwori á yei Wɛ na pɛ o kweeli ya wone tei to. Chega ŋwaane to, Baŋa Wɛ tiini o jege debam ŋwaŋa ye o duri debam yibwona lanyerane.
12A nu-bia bam, konto maama baŋa ne, ta‑á yei-na se, á ná lage á gwoni ni, se á yé zaŋe á du duuri á woli da. Yé du-na de Wɛ, naa tega, naa de kolokolo de. Á nam wó ta we, “ɛɛ” naa “aawo”, se á yé du duuri á woli da. Ko ná dae konto, á wó ga bora Wɛ tei ne.
13Abam wolo ná wo cham wone, se kotu lwoori Wɛ. Abam wolo nam ná jege wopwolo, se kotu taa leeni o seini Wɛ. 14Abam wolo nam ná ba jege yazura, se o bwoŋi Yezu kɔgɔ kom nakwa bam se ba ba ba lwoori Wɛ ba pa‑o, se ba daare ba kwei nuga ba ke o yuu ne dé Teiru Yezu yere ŋwaane. 15Ba ná ke ba wo-dedoa ba lwoori Wɛ konto dwoŋi, jaweeno wom wó seene o na yazura mo. Dé Teiru wom wó pa o wori, ye wɛleera yalo maama o na ke to Wɛ wó yage o ma chɛ‑o. 16Konto ŋwaane, ko maŋe se á ta‑á tɛ á wɛleera taane jaja mo á bere daane, se á daare á ta‑á lwoori Wɛ á pa daane, se Wɛ wó pa á na yazura. Nɔn-ŋom wɛ-lworo tiini ko dana lanyerane ko wae ko pae wonnu ke. 17Guli-na Elija déem na ke tei to. O ye nabiinu ne debam na ye tei to mo, ye o seene o yia o lwoori Wɛ se doa daa yé taa nena. Ka ma seene ka wo nege bena yatɔ de chane seredo. 18O daa ma jwoori o lwoori Wɛ. Ka daa ma seene ka ne, ye tega baŋa wonnu maama jwoori te puli te nwoŋi te ke wodiiru.
19A nu-bia bam, abam wolo ná ywori chega chwoŋa kam wone, ye o dwoŋi ná wane o pa o jwoori o to ka wone, ko lana. 20Á nam ta‑á yei we, wolo maama ná wane o che wɛle-keiru pa o yage o tusim dem, kotu wó wane o vere nɔɔno wom toone jeŋa ne, ye o wɛleera maama de wó saare.

english_text:
1From Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ.
To God's people who are scattered like foreigners in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
2God the Father decided to choose you as his people, and his Spirit has made you holy. You have obeyed Jesus Christ and are sprinkled with his blood.
I pray that God will be kind to you and will keep on giving you peace!
A Real Reason for Hope
3Praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. God is so good, and by raising Jesus from death, he has given us new life and a hope that lives on. 4 God has something stored up for you in heaven, where it will never decay or be ruined or disappear.
5You have faith in God, whose power will protect you until the last day. Then he will save you, just as he has always planned to do. 6On that day you will be glad, even if you have to go through many hard trials for a while. 7 Your faith will be like gold that has been tested in a fire. And these trials will prove that your faith is worth much more than gold that can be destroyed. They will show that you will be given praise and honor and glory when Jesus Christ returns.
8You have never seen Jesus, and you don't see him now. But still you love him and have faith in him, and no words can tell how glad and happy 9you are to be saved. This is why you have faith.
10Some prophets told how God would treat you with undeserved grace, and they searched hard to find out more about the way you would be saved. 11The Spirit of Christ was in them and was telling them how Christ would suffer and would then be given great honor. So they searched to find out exactly who Christ would be and when this would happen. 12But they were told that they were serving you and not themselves. They preached to you by the power of the Holy Spirit, who was sent from heaven. And their message was only for you, even though angels would like to know more about it.
Chosen To Live a Holy Life
13Be alert and think straight. Put all your hope in how God will treat you with undeserved grace when Jesus Christ appears. 14Behave like obedient children. Don't let your lives be controlled by your desires, as they used to be. 15Always live as God's holy people should, because God is the one who chose you, and he is holy. 16 That's why the Scriptures say, “I am the holy God, and you must be holy too.”
17You say that God is your Father, but God doesn't have favorites! He judges all people by what they do. So you must honor God while you live as strangers here on earth. 18You were rescued from the useless way of life you learned from your ancestors. But you know you were not rescued by such things as silver or gold that don't last forever. 19 You were rescued by the precious blood of Christ, that spotless and innocent lamb. 20Christ was chosen even before the world was created, but because of you, he did not come until these last days. 21And when he did come, it was to lead you to have faith in God, who raised him from death and honored him in a glorious way. This is why you have put your faith and hope in God.
22You obeyed the truth, and your souls were made pure. Now you sincerely love each other. But you must keep on loving with all your heart. 23Do this because God has given you new birth by his message that lives on forever. 24 The Scriptures say,
“Humans wither like grass,
and their glory fades
like wild flowers.
Grass dries up,
and flowers fall
to the ground.
25But what the Lord has said
will stand forever.”
Our good news to you is what the Lord has said.
translation_text:
1Amo Piita wolo na ye Yezu Krista totoŋa nakwe to mo popone tɔnɔ konto se a pa abam balo Wɛ na kuri se á ta‑á ye o nyem ye á ba jege kugu jei logo baŋa ne to. Abam ma jage á vo á zoore Pontusi, de Galatia, de Kapadokia, de Asia, de Bitunia kateira yam teene wone. 2Dé Kwo Wɛ ma wuuri o ke o boboŋa ne se o kuri abam konto, ye o tɔge o Sin-laao kom ŋwaane mo o pa se á ji o nyem. Wɛ nam ke konto se ko pa á ta‑á sɛ á pa Yezu Krista, ye á bochare fɔge ya kwɛ o toone jana bam ŋwaane.
Wɛ wó pa abam zaane de yazura se ko gaale.
Dé na jege teena Wɛ tei ne tei to
3Baŋa Wɛ wolo na ye dé Teiru Yezu Krista Kwo to maŋe de teem. Wonto na tiini o ye ŋwaŋa tu to, o ma pa se dé jege ŋwe-doŋa, ye dé ta jege teena o tei ne maŋa maama, o na pɛ se Yezu Krista bi toone wone to ŋwaane. 4Konto mo dé yei we, dé wó ba dé jwoŋi wo-laaro telo Wɛ na tiŋi se o pa o nɔɔna to. Wonnu tem konto nam ba pɔe, ye te ba chɔga, te nam ba leere de. Wɛ tiŋi tento mo telaao ne se o pa abam. 5Á na sɛ‑o de wo-dedoa to, o maa mae o dam dem o cho abam se ko vo ko yi logo baŋa kweelim da yam, se o laam fɔge o jwoŋi abam fase, ne o boboŋa na jaane se o ke tei nɔɔna maama yiga ne to.
6Konto maa pae á jege wopwolo lanyerane. Ko daare leile konto, cham dwi dwi wae ya tui ya maŋe abam maŋa fenfee yerane, ye ko pa se á wo chɔge. 7Ko ná ye cham dem konto, de ye se de maŋe abam de nii á na jege wo-dedoa de Wɛ tei to mo. Abam wo-dedoa kam á na jege to tiini ka dwoi sabu-seŋa na lana tei to. Sabu-seŋa nam wae ka chɔga, ye ba mae mini mo ba ma maŋe-ka se ba lɔre ka na lana tei to. Konto to, cham ná maŋe á wo-dedoa kam, ye ka ta ná lana, ko wó pa se á na zula de teem Wɛ tei ne, maŋa kalo Yezu Krista na wó jwoori o ba se o veere o tete nabiina yiga ne to. 8Abam yi nam ta wo nɛ‑o, ye á ta jege o swono. Á ta maa ba na‑o, ye á ke á wo-dedoa ded‑o, pa se á tiini á jege ywoni de wopwolo kolo na ye wo-kenkagele ye ko taane bá wane ko ta to. 9Abam jege wopwolo konto dwoŋi kolo ŋwaane á wora á nae nyɔɔre á wo-dedoa kam baŋa ne, de Wɛ na wora o jwoŋi abam ŋwea tei to.
10Faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem déem kwaane ba tɔge ko nɛ lanyerane se ba lɔre Wɛ na wó jwoŋi o nɔɔna ŋwea tei to. Ba déem maŋe ba wuuri ba ta Wɛ na wó ke abam zaane tei to. 11Yezu Krista Sin-laao kom maa wo ba tei ne ye ko pa ba wuuri ba lɔre we, Yezu wó ba o na yaara se o laam daare o na paare Wɛ tei ne. Ba maa tiini ba kwaane se ba lɔre maŋa kam konto, de ko na wó ke tei to. 12Wɛ ma guri o chega kam o pa o sampwori sem konto lɔre we, ko dae ba tete ŋwaane mo ba toŋa, se ko ye abam ŋwaane mo. Ba déem na bere chega kalo to ye bedwe mo de kwor-ywoŋa kalo Wɛ tontoŋena badwonna zem na tɔɔle ba bere abam to. Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ se o Sin-laao kom nwoŋi telaao ne ko ba banto tei, ye ba wane ba bere abam o kwora kam konto. Wɛ malese sem tete maŋe se lage se se lɔre chega kam konto kuri na ye tei to.
Wɛ lage se dé taa jege wo-pwoŋo
13Abam nam fɔge á ja á tete de boboŋ-dɛɛra. Peene-na á tete se á tiini á ta‑á jege teena de Wɛ na wó ke zaane delo abam yuu ne maŋa kalo Yezu Krista na wó jwoori o ba se o veere o tete nabiina yiga ne to. 14Ta‑á sɛ-na á Kwo Wɛ ni. Ko nam ná ye á déem ta na wo lɔre Wɛ chega kam ye á fera zo wo-yɔɔro telo to, se á daa yé pa te taa tei á boboŋa. 15Wɛ nam mo bwoŋi abam se á ta‑á ye o nyem, ye wonto yɔɔre o ye wo-pwoŋo tu. Mo kokuri á jege se á ta‑á jege wo-pwoŋo á ŋwea maama wone. 16Ko nam maŋe ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne ko we,
“Pɔɔre-na á tete se á ta‑á ye wose,
se amo mo ye wose.”
17Abam na lwoori Wɛ tei to, á yeini á bwoi‑o we á Kwo, ye o nam mo ye wolo na wó di nabiina maama taane to. O maa yeini o tɔge nɔɔna maama kikia na ye tei to o ma di ba taane, ye o ba kuri nɔɔna daane de o na ke-ba tei to. Konto to, á ta ná zoore logo baŋa ne, se á ta‑á kɔre Wɛ de á na tɔge chwei selo to. 18Kokuri á yei we, Wɛ jwoŋi abam se á daa yé ta‑á tɔge chullu telo na nwoŋi á nabaara jeŋa ne to. Wɛ na le abam wo-yɔɔro tem konto wone to, ko dae logo baŋa sabu kolo na wae ko chɔge to mo o mɛ o ŋwe o jwoŋi abam o yage. 19O nam mɛ Yezu Krista toone jana bam mo o ma jwoŋi abam, ye banto tiini ba ye lonne nyem. Yezu na jigi wo-kaanem konto to, o maa nye de pipeila kalo na tiini ka lana fase ye kolokolo wo taŋe ka yera ne to mo. 20Boboa ne ye logo baŋa ta tera to, Wɛ maŋe o kuri wonto mo se o ma jwoŋi o nɔɔna ba wɛleera wone. Ko daare logo baŋa kweelim maŋa kam laam yia, ye Wɛ le‑o o bere nabiina abam zeinim ŋwaane mo. 21Á nam dɛ Yezu ŋwaane mo á ke á wo-dedoa de Wɛ. Ko maa ye Wɛ mo bi wonto toone wone, ye o daare o pa o di paare Wɛ telaao ne. Konto ma pa á seene á jege wo-dedoa de teena Wɛ tei ne.
22Abam laam na sɛ Wɛ chega kam to mo pɛ á bochara fɔge ya kwɛ, pa se á jege swono chekke de á nu-bia balo de na ye Wɛ nyem to. Konto to, yɔɔre á ta‑á jege da-swono de á bochara maama. 23Abam na jege Wɛ ŋwe-doŋa kam to, ka kuri wo nwoŋi nabiina dwi wone, balo toone na wae-ba to. Ka nwoŋi Wɛ tei mo ye ka ba chɔga. Á tɔge Wɛ kwora kalo na jege ŋwea ye ka wora taa taa to baŋa ne mo á na o ŋwe-doŋa kam konto. 24Ko nam popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
“Ko ná ye nabiina,
ba maama nye de gaaro mo.
Ba nenɔŋa maa nye de gaao wo punnu.
Ba ba dáana ye ba toa.
Gaao kom maa yeini ko kwaare,
ye ko punnu tem de siiri.
25Ko nam ná ye Wɛ kwora kam,
kanto wó taa wora mo taa wuu.”
Kwora kam konto mo ye kwor-ywoŋa kalo ba na tɔɔle ba bere abam to.

english_text:
A Living Stone and a Holy Nation
1Stop being hateful! Quit trying to fool people, and start being sincere. Don't be jealous or say cruel things about others. 2Be like newborn babies who are thirsty for the pure spiritual milk that will help you grow and be saved. 3 You have already found out how good the Lord really is.
4Come to Jesus Christ. He is the living stone people have rejected, but which God has chosen and highly honored. 5And now you are living stones being used to build a spiritual house. You are also a group of holy priests, and with the help of Jesus Christ you will offer sacrifices that please God. 6 It is just as God says in the Scriptures,
“Look! I am placing in Zion
a choice and precious
cornerstone.
No one who has faith
in this one
will be disappointed.”
7 You are followers of the Lord, and this stone is precious to you. But it isn't precious to those who refuse to follow him. They are the builders who tossed aside the stone that turned out to be the most important one of all. 8 They disobeyed the message and stumbled and fell over this stone, because they were doomed.
9 But you are God's chosen and special people. You are a group of royal priests and a holy nation. God has brought you out of darkness into his marvelous light. Now you must tell all the wonderful things he has done. The Scriptures say,
10 “Once you were nobody.
Now you are God's people.
At one time no one
had mercy on you.
Now God has treated you
with kindness.”
Live as God's Servants Should
11Dear friends, you are foreigners and strangers on this earth. So I beg you not to surrender to those desires that fight against you. 12Always let others see you behaving properly, even though they may still accuse you of doing wrong. Then on the day of judgment, they will honor God by telling the good things they saw you do.
13The Lord wants you to obey all human authorities, especially the Emperor, who rules over everyone. 14You must also obey governors, because they are sent by the Emperor to punish criminals and to praise good citizens. 15God wants you to silence stupid and ignorant people by doing right. 16You are free, but still you are God's servants, and you must not use your freedom as an excuse for doing wrong. 17Respect everyone and show special love for God's people. Honor God and respect the Emperor.
The Example of Christ's Suffering
18Servants, you must obey your masters and always show respect to them. Do this, not only to those who are kind and thoughtful, but also to those who are cruel. 19God will bless you, even if others treat you unfairly for being loyal to him. 20You don't gain anything by being punished for some wrong you have done. But God will bless you, if you have to suffer for doing something good. 21After all, God chose you to suffer as you follow in the footsteps of Christ, who set an example by suffering for you.
22 Christ did not sin
or ever tell a lie.
23 Although he was abused,
he never tried to get even.
And when he suffered,
he made no threats.
Instead, he had faith in God,
who judges fairly.
24 Christ carried the burden
of our sins.
He was nailed to the cross,
so we would stop sinning
and start living right.
By his cuts and bruises
you are healed.
25You had wandered away
like sheep.
Now you have returned
to the one
who is your shepherd
and protector.
translation_text:
Debam tɔge de Yezu dé ye Wɛ bia
1Mo kokuri, ja-na á tete de lwarem kikia dwi maama. Á daa yé ta‑á gane á dwonna, naa á jege ni-zɛ ni-zɛ, naa wo-goo. Yé ta‑á twe-na daane. 2Pa-na se á fera taa zoore Wɛ chega kam se ka taa fɔge á boboŋa lanyerane, ne bu-seseŋa fera na zoore o nu yele tei to. Konto mo wó pa á boboŋa ba ya kweere Wɛ chega kam seeni, se o laam fɔge o jwoŋi abam fase. 3Abam nam maŋe á maane á nii dé Teiru wom na tiini o lana tei to.
4Dé Teiru Yezu maa ye wolo nabiina na ve, ye o ta ye ŋwea tu to mo. Wɛ nam maŋe o tiŋi wonto se o tiini o taa jege fera o pa‑o, ne o ye kandwɛ delo o na lage o ma-de o lɔ o sɔŋɔ kom to. 5Á na ke á tete Yezu jeŋa ne to maa pae se abam de tɔge á ji ne kandwa yalo Wɛ na jege-ya o maa lɔ o sɔŋɔ kom to, ye á ye balo na jege o ŋwe-doŋa kam to. Ko ta maa pae se á ji Wɛ tete nɔɔna balo na ke kaanem ba pa‑o to, ye pɛɛra yalo á na ma á kaane‑o to ye wo-laaro telo o Sin-laao kom na ke á bochara ne to. Á pɛɛra yam konto su Wɛ yi, á na me de Yezu Krista to ŋwaane.
6Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne we:
“Nii-na amo Wɛ na lage a chwi kandwɛ delo na tiini de lana to,
se a ma lɔ sɔŋɔ Zion ne.
Amo kuri kandwɛ-zane dem konto
se de taa ye kandwɛ delo na pae diga kam zega lana to mo.
Wolo nam ná sale wonto yera ne,
chaveera bá fɔge ya ja konto tu.”
7Ko ná ye abam balo na jege wo-dedoa ded‑o to, o jege lonne mo á tei ne. Ko daare, ko ná ye balo bam na ve‑o to,
“O maa nye de kandwɛ delo lɔra bam na ve,
